They started to cry. They had ruined their toys and their fun. They wished they had been nicer and played better. But it was too late. The doll was gone and the tray was forgotten. They had a bad ending.

The sun was shining brightly on the stream. Frogs were hopping happily around as bugs flew by. Sammy was sitting by the stream, his hands were busy building a castle in the sand. He didn't notice his big brother Joe coming up behind him until he heard Joe's voice.

"Whoa there Sammy! What are you doing?" asked Joe.

Sammy was surprised but he answered "Making a castle."

"Is the stream trust to play in?" asked Joe.

Sammy thought for a moment, then smiled and said "Yes, I trust it."

So Joe and Sammy played in the stream. Sammy was really busy, catching frogs and making little boats to float downstream. Joe showed him how to make bridges with twigs and rocks.

When it was time to go home, Sammy was sad but Joe told him "Don't worry, I'll come back soon and we can play in the stream again." Sammy smiled, he knew he could trust Joe to keep his promise.

Ben and Sam were brothers. They liked to play with their toys in their room. One day, they saw a big dish on the table. It was shiny and round. They wanted to touch it.

"Look, Ben, a dish!" Sam said. "Can we play with it?"

"I don't know, Sam. Mom said it is her dish. She said it is very old and hard to find. She said we should not touch it." Ben said.

"But it is so pretty, Ben. I want to see it. Maybe it is magic. Maybe it can make wishes come true." Sam said. He did not listen to Ben. He ran to the table and grabbed the dish.

"Sam, no! Put it back! Mom will be mad!" Ben said. He followed Sam and tried to take the dish from him.

But Sam did not want to give the dish to Ben. He held it tight and pulled it away. He believed the dish was his. He believed the dish was magic.

They fought over the dish. They pushed and pulled and shouted. They did not see the edge of the table. They did not see the dish slip from their hands. They did not see the dish fall to the floor.

CRASH!

The dish broke into many pieces. It was not magic. It was not hard. It was fragile and old. It was Mom's dish.

Mom heard the noise. She came to the room. She saw the dish on the floor. She saw Ben and Sam with guilty faces. She was very angry. She was very sad.

"Ben! Sam! What have you done? That was my dish! That was my grandmother's dish! That was the only thing I had from her! How could you be so careless? How could you be so selfish?" Mom said. She did not hug them. She did not kiss them. She did not forgive them.

She sent them to their room. She did not talk to them. She did not play with them. She did not love them.

Ben and Sam felt bad. They felt sorry. They felt lonely. They wished they had listened to Ben. They wished they had not touched the dish. They wished they had not broken the dish. They wished they had not broken Mom's heart.

But it was too late. The dish was gone. The magic was gone. The love was gone.

The end.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Jake and Sue, who lived in a tiny universe. One day, Jake thought it would be fun to test their universe. He picked a sour apple and asked Sue to take a bite. As Sue bit into it, something magical happened. The universe changed! Suddenly, there was a huge playground with lots of fun. Jake and Sue explored the playground, trying out different rides and having so much fun. After a while, Jake and Sue knew the test was a success and the playground was their own special universe. They had lots of fun that day and now whenever they want, they can test their universe by picking a sour apple.

Once upon a time, there lived a cow called Moo. Moo was a selfish cow and did not care about anyone else around her. She would only look out for herself.

One day, right at noon, Moo decided to strike. She lifted her hooves and pawed at the ground, making a big fuss. All the other animals gathered around her, curious to find out what was going on.

Moo spoke up and said, "I am striking because I want more food and hay, so that I can be happy and content!"

The other animals were unimpressed and scoffed at her. "You are so selfish," said one of the other cows. "Don't you care about anyone else around you? We all want more, too!"

Moo realized she was being selfish and decided to drop her strike. Together with the other animals, they all worked together to find a solution. 

In the end, they could all be happy and content.

Jane was a very curious 3 year old. Whenever she visited the park, she would always examine the funny animals.

Today, she saw a chicken in the farmer's barn. She was so interested in it! She wanted to see if it was fit.

"Can I please examine the chicken?" she asked the farmer.

The farmer said, "Yes, but be careful. Don't get too close to it."

Jane nodded and examined the chicken up close. She saw it was very fit but didn't want to touch it.

Just then, the chicken became startled and started to run around in the barn! Jane quickly stepped back and watched it. She learned that although it's important to examine things, it's best to observe them from a distance.

Moral of the story: Don't get too close to something you don't know. It's important to be careful and observe things from a distance.

Tom and Lily were friends who liked to play together. One day, they found a newspaper in the park. They looked at the pictures and the words. They saw a picture of a man and a woman in nice clothes. They had rings on their fingers and flowers in their hands.

"What are they doing?" Lily asked.

"They are marrying," Tom said. "They love each other and want to be together."

"I want to marry you, Tom," Lily said. "You are my best friend and I love you."

"OK, Lily, let's marry," Tom said. "We can use this newspaper as a dress and a hat."

They tore the newspaper and wrapped it around themselves. They held hands and pretended to say vows. They kissed each other on the cheek.

Some older kids saw them and laughed. They pointed and said mean words. They said Tom and Lily were silly and stupid. They said they were too young to marry. They said they looked funny in the newspaper clothes.

Tom and Lily felt embarrassed. They felt sad and hurt. They ran away from the older kids. They cried and hugged each other.

A nice lady saw them and came to help. She asked them what happened. They told her about the newspaper and the older kids. She smiled and said, "Don't worry, Tom and Lily. You are not silly or stupid. You are sweet and brave. You have a lot of imagination and love. You can pretend to marry if you want. It's a fun game. But you don't have to marry for real. You are too young for that. You have a lot of time to grow and learn and make friends. You can marry when you are older and ready. And you can choose whoever you want. But for now, you can be happy as friends."

Tom and Lily nodded and thanked the lady. They felt better and smiled. They decided to keep the newspaper as a souvenir. They said they would always be friends and maybe marry someday. They went back to play and have fun.

The moral of the story is: Don't let others make fun of you or your dreams. Be yourself and be kind. Friendship is a precious gift. Marriage is a serious commitment. Enjoy your childhood and respect others.

Lily had a yellow diary that she liked to write in every day. She wrote about her friends, her toys, her dreams and her feelings. She did not want anyone to read her diary, because it was her secret.

One day, she left her diary on her bed when she went to play outside. Her brother Max saw the diary and was curious. He opened it and started to read. He saw that Lily wrote that he was mean and annoying. He got angry and tore some pages from the diary.

When Lily came back, she saw her diary on the floor and some pages missing. She was very sad and mad. She picked up her diary and ran to Max. She yelled at him, "You are a bad brother! You ruined my diary! Give me back my pages!"

Max yelled back, "You are a bad sister! You wrote mean things about me! I don't have your pages!"

They yelled and yelled until their mom came and stopped them. She asked them what happened and they told her. She was not happy. She said, "You both did wrong. Lily, you should not write mean things about your brother. Max, you should not read and tear your sister's diary. You should say sorry to each other and share your feelings nicely."

Lily and Max felt sorry and hugged each other. They said sorry and promised to be nicer. They also helped each other to fix the diary with some tape and stickers. Lily let Max write something nice in her diary and Max let Lily play with his car. They learned to respect each other's things and feelings.

Once upon a time there was a graceful princess who was walking in her garden. She came to a special point in the garden and while standing there she saw something special. She received a beautiful necklace with a magical gem. She was so happy and sang and danced with joy.

Then the princess saw a fairy appear in the sky. The fairy told her that the gem was a special present. It would bring her courage, strength and love. She thanked the fairy and held the gem close to her heart.

The princess kept the gem with her, always wearing it and cherishing it. Whenever she was feeling scared or sad, she would look at the gem and be filled with courage and love.

The princess was very grateful and would often talk to the gem, asking for help and guidance. The princess was so graceful and the gem was so special, it was a beautiful sight for everyone who saw them.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play in their room. They have a big bed with a blue sheet. The sheet is soft and delicate.

One day, they have a new game. They take the sheet off the bed and make a tent. They use chairs and pillows to hold the sheet. They crawl inside the tent and pretend they are in a castle.

"Look, Anna, we have a secret place!" Ben says. "No one can find us here!"

"Yes, Ben, we are the king and the queen!" Anna says. "We have a lot of fun!"

They laugh and sing and tell stories. They forget about the time. They do not hear their mom calling them for lunch.

Suddenly, they hear a loud noise. They look outside the tent and see their dog, Rex. Rex is big and furry. He likes to play too. He sees the sheet and thinks it is a toy. He jumps on the sheet and pulls it with his teeth.

"Rex, no!" Anna and Ben shout. "That is our tent! Leave it alone!"

But Rex does not listen. He is too excited. He shakes the sheet and tears it apart. He makes a big hole in the sheet. He also knocks down the chairs and the pillows. He makes a big mess in the room.

Anna and Ben are sad and angry. They love their sheet. They worked hard to make their tent. Now their sheet is ruined and their game is over.

They cry and yell at Rex. Rex does not understand. He thinks they are still playing. He wags his tail and barks.

Their mom hears the noise and comes to the room. She sees the sheet, the chairs, the pillows and the dog. She sees Anna and Ben crying and yelling.

She is not happy. She scolds Rex and puts him outside. She scolds Anna and Ben and tells them to clean up the room. She tells them they are in trouble. She tells them they cannot play with the sheet anymore.

Anna and Ben are sorry. They say they are sorry to their mom and to each other. They say they are sorry to the sheet. They hug the sheet and try to fix it. But the sheet is too delicate. It cannot be fixed.

They have to throw away the sheet. They have no more tent. They have no more fun.

The end.

Jenny was a bossy girl who liked to tell everyone what to do. She wanted to have a tea party with her dolls and invite her friends, but she did not want to share her pastry. She had a big, yummy pastry that her mom gave her for being good. She hid it under a napkin and hoped no one would see it.

She called her friends, Sam and Lily, and told them to come to her house. She said they could play with her dolls and have tea, but they had to do everything she said. Sam and Lily liked Jenny, but they did not like how she was bossy. They decided to go anyway, because they wanted to have fun.

When they got to Jenny's house, they saw her tea set and her dolls. They also saw the napkin on the plate, but they did not know what was under it. Jenny said, "Welcome to my tea party! You can sit here and here, and I will sit here. You can have this tea and this cookie, and I will have this tea and this napkin." She smiled and lifted the napkin, revealing her pastry.

Sam and Lily gasped. They thought the pastry looked delicious and they wanted a bite. They asked Jenny, "Can we have some of your pastry, please? It looks so good!"

Jenny shook her head. She said, "No, this is my pastry. I got it for being good. You can't have any. It's mine, mine, mine!" She took a big bite and made a loud noise.

Sam and Lily felt sad and angry. They thought Jenny was being mean and selfish. They did not want to play with her anymore. They said, "We don't like your tea party. You are not a good friend. You don't share. We are going home." They got up and left, leaving Jenny alone with her pastry.

Jenny felt surprised and lonely. She did not understand why her friends left. She looked at her pastry and realized it was not as yummy as she thought. She wished she had shared it with Sam and Lily. She wished they were still there. She wished she was not so bossy. She learned a lesson that day: it is better to be kind and generous than to be greedy and rude.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tom. One day, Tom lost his key. He looked everywhere, but he could not find it. He was very sad and embarrassed because he knew he should have taken better care of it.

Tom's mom saw him looking sad and asked what was wrong. Tom told her about the lost key. His mom said, "Sometimes, when we need help, we can pray and ask for it." So, Tom closed his eyes and prayed for help to find his key.

The next day, Tom found his key under his bed. He was so happy! He thanked his mom for teaching him to pray. From that day on, Tom always prayed when he needed help and took better care of his things.

Once there was a proud boat. It was made of velvet, and it was very nice. One day, the boat wanted to sail. It sailed off into the seas and went on a grand adventure. It saw lots of different creatures, and went through stormy weather. It was strong, and nothing could stop it. Finally, the proud boat finished its voyage and returned to where it began, safe and sound.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Lucy who was very healthy. Every morning Lucy would go to a big, green field with her friend Ben. In the field, Lucy liked to guess how far she could throw her ball. 

Ben would measure the "pitch", which was how far Lucy could throw her ball. The longest Lucy had ever thrown it was eight meters. 

One day, Lucy had a special ball. She threw it with all her might and with a huge grin on her face. She couldn't believe it when Ben said she had thrown it ten meters! 

It was her new personal best and she was very proud. From that day on, Lucy kept guessing how far she could throw the ball, always aiming to beat her previous high score. 

The end!

Once upon a time, there was a little seed. The seed wanted to grow big and strong, but it needed help. The sun and the rain were gentle and kind, and they allowed the seed to grow. 

The seed sent out a tiny root, searching for water and food. It dug deep into the ground, and the earth was soft and welcoming. The root found what it needed, and the seed grew taller and taller. 

Soon, the little seed became a big, beautiful flower. It was so happy to be alive and to have grown so strong. The sun and the rain continued to be gentle, and they allowed the flower to bloom. The flower was grateful for their help, and it smiled and danced in the breeze.

Once upon a time, there was a poor barber who had no money. He was very sad and wanted to make some money, but he was too scared to ask people for help.

One day, he had an idea. He decided to push his barber chair out of his house and into the street. He said to everyone he saw, "Do you need a haircut? I'm a barber and can give you a nice one."

People started coming to him! They liked his haircuts, so they brought him money. Soon, the poor barber had enough money to buy food and new clothes. He was so happy!

Everyday, the poor barber would push his barber chair into the street to find customers. He worked very hard and soon became very rich.

The poor barber never forgot to say thank you to those who pushed him out the door. He was very grateful for all their help.

One sunny day, a little girl named Lily went to the park with her mommy. They walked around and saw a big pond with swans swimming in it. Lily pointed and said, "Look mommy, pretty birdies!" Her mommy said, "Those are called swans, Lily. They are very graceful." 

Lily wanted to get closer to the swans, so they walked over to a little fair that was set up nearby. They went on the merry-go-round and ate cotton candy. When they were done, they saw a man selling bread to feed the swans. They bought some and walked back to the pond. 

Lily threw the bread into the water and watched the swans swim over to eat it. She said, "Mommy, I enjoy watching the swans. They are so pretty and nice." Her mommy smiled and said, "I'm glad you like them, Lily. They are one of my favorite animals too."

Once upon a time, there was a big box in the park. A little boy named Tim saw it and wanted to open it. He thought there might be something impressive inside. 

Tim asked his friend, Jane, "Do you want to help me open the box?" Jane said, "Yes! Let's open it together!" So, they both pushed and pulled the box to open it. 

When the box was open, they found a lot of colorful balloons inside. They were so happy with the result! Tim and Jane played with the balloons all day and shared them with their friends. Everyone had a great time.

Once upon a time, there was a little fox. He had a special twig he liked to carry. The twig made him feel safe and happy.

One day, the fox was walking through the forest and found his twig missing! He started to worry. Where had his twig gone? He searched through the tall grass but still couldn't find it.

He felt so sleepy and sad. With a heavy heart, he curled up under a tree and fell asleep.

When he awoke, he noticed a twig in front of him! He was so excited, he picked it up and ran home.

The fox was so happy he had his twig back that he never worried again. He kept his twig safe, happy and never felt sleepy.

Ben and Lily are twins. They like to play with their toys. They have many toys, but their favorite is a big red car. The car can make noises and move by itself. Ben and Lily take turns to drive the car.

One day, the car stops working. Ben and Lily are sad. They try to push the car, but it does not move. They look at the car and see a number on it. The number is zero.

"What does zero mean?" Ben asks.

"I don't know," Lily says. "Maybe it means the car has no power."

They look for their mom. They hope she can fix the car. They find her in the kitchen. She is making cookies.

"Mom, mom, our car is broken!" Ben and Lily say.

"Oh, no, what happened?" Mom says.

She follows them to their room. She sees the car and the zero.

"Zero means the car needs new batteries," Mom says. "Batteries are things that make the car go. I have some in the drawer. Let me get them for you."

Mom opens the drawer and takes out two batteries. She opens the car and puts the batteries inside. She closes the car and turns it on. The car makes noises and moves by itself.

"Yay, the car is working!" Ben and Lily say.

They hug their mom and thank her.

"You're welcome, my sweeties," Mom says. "You are very helpful for showing me the problem. Now you can play with your car again. But don't forget to share and be nice to each other."

Ben and Lily nod. They are happy. They drive the car together. They share and are nice to each other. They hope Mom will give them some cookies later.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Anna. She was three years old and very curious. She wanted to explore the world around her.

One day, Anna was walking through the forest when she came across an old oak tree. She stopped to look at it and noticed that the base of the tree was empty. Anna decided to take a closer look and curiously stepped inside.

She was amazed to discover that the hollow tree was filled with twinkling lights which displayed colourful images. She gasped in delight and called out to her mum, who had been walking just behind Anna.

"Mummy! Come and look!" Anna exclaimed, stretching her arm out to point to the beautiful display. 

Mummy smiled, "Oh Anna, you have found a magical tree!"

Once there was a boy who loved to whistle. Every day he would go to the village and practice whistling. One day, he was walking in the village and noticed something fragile. He decided to be extra careful when he got close. When he finally got closer to it, he saw that it was made out of wood. He started to whistle and it sounded so beautiful. He whistled so loudly that everyone in the village heard him. He was so happy and continued to whistle until it was time for him to go home. The village was filled with happy whistling every day!

Lily was a big girl. She had four teeth in her mouth. She liked to show them to everyone. She said, "Look at my teeth! They are shiny and strong!"

One day, she saw a boy in the park. He had no teeth. He was smaller than Lily. Lily ran to him and said, "Where are your teeth? You have no teeth! You are a baby!"

The boy felt sad. He said, "I am not a baby. I am Sam. My teeth are growing. They are inside my gums. They will come out soon."

Lily did not believe him. She said, "That is silly. Teeth do not grow. They are always there. You are ignorant. You do not know anything."

Sam was angry. He said, "You are ignorant. You do not know everything. Teeth do grow. My mom told me. She knows a lot. She is a dentist."

Lily was confused. She said, "What is a dentist?"

Sam said, "A dentist is a person who helps people with their teeth. She looks at them and cleans them and fixes them. She has a big chair and a bright light and many tools."

Lily was curious. She said, "Can I see your mom? Can I see her chair and her light and her tools?"

Sam said, "Yes, you can. But you have to be nice to me. And you have to say sorry for calling me a baby and ignorant."

Lily thought for a moment. She said, "Okay, I am sorry. You are not a baby and ignorant. You are Sam and smart. Can we be friends?"

Sam smiled. He said, "Yes, we can be friends. Come on, let's go see my mom. Maybe she can show you how your teeth are growing too."

Lily liked to play with her dolls. She had many dolls on her shelf. She gave them names and clothes and stories. She did not like to share her dolls with anyone.

One day, her cousin Ben came to visit. Ben was older and bigger than Lily. He liked to play with cars and trucks. He did not like dolls. He saw Lily's shelf and said, "What are these? They are silly and boring. Let me show you my cars. They are fast and loud and fun."

Lily did not want to play with Ben's cars. She wanted to play with her dolls. She said, "No, thank you. I like my dolls. They are pretty and nice and fun. You can play with your cars by yourself."

Ben did not like Lily's answer. He got angry and said, "Fine. If you don't want to play with me, I will play with your dolls. I will make them race and crash and fly. I will show you how to have fun."

Lily did not want Ben to touch her dolls. She said, "No, stop. Those are my dolls. You will break them. You will hurt them. Leave them alone."

But Ben did not listen. He ignored Lily and grabbed her dolls. He threw them on the floor and smashed them with his cars. He made fierce noises and laughed. He did not care that Lily was crying and screaming.

Lily ran to her mom and told her what Ben was doing. Her mom was very angry and said, "Ben, how dare you? You are being very rude and mean. You have to apologize to Lily and help her fix her dolls. You have to share and be nice. Or you will have to go home."

Ben did not want to apologize or help. He did not want to share or be nice. He wanted to play with his cars. He said, "No, I don't. I don't care. I don't like dolls. I like cars. They are better."

But his mom heard him and said, "That's enough. You are being very naughty and selfish. You have to go home now. You are not welcome here until you learn to be respectful and kind."

She took Ben by the hand and led him to the door. Ben was crying and kicking. He did not want to go home. He wanted to play with his cars. But he had to go. He had learned a hard lesson. He had lost his cousin and his fun. He had made a big mistake.

Sara and Tom are twins. They like to play with their toys and books. One day, their mom says they can go on a big plane and fly to see their grandma. Sara and Tom are very happy. They pack their bags and go to the airport.

At the airport, they see many people and planes. Mom gives them each a ticket. The ticket has their name and a picture of a plane. Sara and Tom hold their tickets and follow mom to the gate. They wait for their plane to come.

But then, Tom drops his ticket. A big wind blows it away. Tom runs after it, but he can't catch it. He starts to cry. He thinks he can't fly without his ticket.

Sara sees Tom crying. She feels sorry for him. She has an idea. She goes to Tom and says, "Don't cry, Tom. I have a ticket for you. You can have mine. I don't need it. I can fly with my soft bear. He has wings. See?"

Tom looks at Sara. He sees her ticket and her soft bear. He smiles. He says, "Thank you, Sara. You are very nice. I will share my snacks with you on the plane. Can I hold your soft bear too?"

Sara nods. She gives Tom her ticket and her soft bear. They hug. Mom sees them and smiles. She says, "You are very good twins. I'm proud of you. Come on, let's go. Our plane is here. We can fly now."

Sara and Tom hold hands and follow mom to the plane. They are excited to fly and see their grandma. They are happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily's mommy said they were going to visit grandma. Lily was very excited to see grandma because she always gave her candy. 

When they got to grandma's house, Lily saw that it was very messy. Her mommy said they needed to clean up before they could play. Lily helped by picking up her toys and putting them away. She was very good at cleaning!

After they finished cleaning, Lily played with grandma and ate candy. But soon, Lily started to feel tired. She asked her mommy if they could go home and take a nap. Her mommy said yes and they went home to rest. The end.

Once upon a time, in a small village, there was a boy named Tim. Tim had a toy whip. He liked to play with his whip every day. But sometimes, he felt helpless because he did not know how to use it well.

One day, Tim met a kind man. The man saw Tim with his whip and wanted to help him. He said, "I can teach you how to improve and use your whip better." Tim was happy and said, "Yes, please!"

The kind man showed Tim how to hold the whip and move it. Tim practiced and practiced. Soon, he was not helpless anymore. He knew how to use his whip very well. Tim was happy and thanked the kind man. And from that day on, Tim played with his whip and had lots of fun.

Once upon a time there was a happy little girl called Ami. She loved to dance around her house and make funny faces with her family.

One day, Ami's mommy gave her a pretty mask to wear. Ami was so excited and she put it on straight away. She felt a bit silly wearing it, but she loved its bright colors.

Ami started to dance around the room with her mask on. She twirled and hopped and jumped. She felt so free and happy.

But then she heard a loud noise outside and Ami felt a bit nervous. She wanted to keep dancing but she was too scared. So she took off her mask and ran to find her mommy.

Mommy hugged Ami and told her not to be scared. She said that with her mask on, she could be brave and keep on dancing. So Ami put her mask back on and started dancing around the room again.

Ami was so brave, and she danced with a happy smile on her face. She forgot all about the noise outside, because dancing made her feel so free and happy.

Once upon a time, there was a big bear. The big bear lived in a big forest. One day, the big bear found a nail on the ground. The big bear picked up the nail and looked at it. The nail was very sharp. The big bear decided to fold the nail in half so it wouldn't hurt anyone. The big bear was very happy that he could help keep his friends safe.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, her mommy asked her to come to the grocery store with her. Lily was very happy and excited to go. When they got there, they saw a big mess on the floor. Lily's mommy said, "Oh no, this is messy. We need to be careful not to slip and fall."

Lily said, "I can help clean it up!" But her mommy said, "No, it's not safe for you. I'll take care of it." As they were walking down the aisle, Lily saw a toy she really wanted. She asked her mommy if they could buy it, but her mommy said they didn't have enough money for it.

Lily was sad and started crying. Her mommy hugged her and said, "Don't worry, we can save up for it next time." Lily felt better and they continued shopping. When they got home, Lily helped her mommy put away the groceries. She felt happy that she could help and that they had a nice time together.

Sam and Mia are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big sign. The sign says: "East Fair. Fun and games for all!"

"Let's go to the fair!" Sam says. "Maybe we can ride the horses or eat some candy."

"OK!" Mia says. "But we have to ask our moms first."

They run to their moms, who are sitting on a bench. They ask if they can go to the fair. Their moms say yes, but they have to stay together and be careful.

Sam and Mia are happy. They hold hands and walk to the fair. They see many people and colors and sounds. They smell popcorn and cotton candy. They hear music and laughter.

They go to a booth that sells lemonade. They are thirsty. They each get a cup and drink. But the lemonade is not sweet. It is bitter. They make a face and spit it out.

"Yuck!" Sam says. "This lemonade is bad. It tastes like soap."

"I don't like it either," Mia says. "It hurts my tongue."

They throw away their cups and look for something else to drink. They see a man with a big jug. He says he has apple juice. They think apple juice is good. They ask for some.

The man smiles and pours them some juice. They take a sip. But the juice is not good. It is bitter too. They make another face and spit it out.

"Yuck!" Mia says. "This juice is worse than the lemonade. It tastes like dirt."

"I agree," Sam says. "It is awful. Why is everything so bitter here?"

They look at the man. He is not smiling anymore. He is angry. He says: "You are rude kids. You don't appreciate my drinks. They are not bitter. They are sour. Sour is good. Sour is east. East is the best. You are west. West is the worst."

Sam and Mia are confused. They don't understand what the man is saying. They don't know what east and west are. They only know that they don't like his drinks. They are scared of him. They run away from him.

They find their moms and tell them what happened. Their moms hug them and say they are sorry. They say they will take them to another fair. A fair that has sweet drinks and nice people. A fair that is not east or west. A fair that is just fun.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved to draw. She had a big pencil that she used to make her art. One day when she was playing, she was very clumsy and accidentally knocked the pencil off the table.

The pencil rolled across the floor and split into two pieces. The little girl was so upset to see her pencil separate. She wanted to put it back together but she had no idea how.

Luckily for the little girl, her mom had a great idea. She gave the little girl some tape and helped her to fix the pencil. With the tape, the little girl was able to make the pencil one piece again.

The little girl was so happy that she was able to fix her pencil with the help of her mom. From that day on, she was extra careful not to be clumsy.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named John. He was only three years old and loved to explore the world. One day he decided to visit the park. As he reached the park, he saw a bowl on the ground. He could not take his eyes off it. He picked it up and felt incredible!

John asked his dad, "What is this, daddy?"

His dad smiled and said, "That's a magical bowl! You can make a wish and it will come true. But you have to be careful. Don't make mistakes!"

John was filled with excitement. He sat and thought carefully about what to wish for. Suddenly, he realized he knew exactly what to wish for!

He closed his eyes and made a wish and then held the bowl in his hands. After a few minutes, something incredible happened. John saw sparkles coming out of the magical bowl! His wish had come true! 

John had realized that with a little bit of magic, anything was possible!

The bird was calm in the sky. It was so high, it almost looked like it was touching the sun. The bird spread its wings and flew through the clouds. It sent a message to all the other birds. The birds in the sky began to increase in number. Soon there were so many birds in the sky, the sun started to disappear. The air was filled with happy chirps and the sky was full of wings. All the birds flew in circles, higher and higher into the sky. They flew together, sending a message of peace. The birds stayed in the sky until the sun set, then they flew back home. The birds flew happily and they increased in numbers each day. They kept sending their message of peace until finally, the whole world was calm.

One day, a little boy was walking in the park. Suddenly he heard something that sounded like a loud roar. But it didn't sound like a lion! It was coming from the mailbox. The little boy was so surprised that he ran over to it.

When he got there, he saw that it was an angry cat. The cat was roaring and hissing at the little boy. Suddenly the cat jumped out of the mailbox, and the little boy ran away, scared.

The little boy was very happy to get home. He told everyone about the angry cat roaring in the mailbox. Everyone thought it was funny, but he was still a little scared!

One day, a tiny mouse was scurrying around looking for food. Suddenly, he saw an enormous leak coming from a nearby bush. He excitedly scurried over to the leak to have a drink. However, as he was about to take a sip, a big hand came out from the bush and slapped the mouse away!

The mouse was so scared that he ran and hid under a log. But there, he noticed an enormous ant carrying an enormous leaf. He was so impressed that he decided to follow the ant. As they marched back to his ant colony, the mouse noticed even more enormous leaks on the ground. He cautiously took a sip and tasted the sweetest water he had ever had! 

Happy and quenched, the mouse bid goodbye to the huge ant and thanked him for showing him the enormous leak. From then on, he would return every day for a sip of the sweetest water.

Samuel was walking in the park one day when he discovered something special. He saw a reindeer with a big red nose! Samuel thought it was so cool. He got closer and asked the reindeer for its name. 

"My name is Barry," the reindeer said. "I'm a very smart reindeer."

Samuel was so impressed with Barry. He asked him many questions about his life. Barry told him that he was the leader of a team of reindeer and they visited everywhere, even the North Pole!

Samuel was amazed. He wanted to be part of Barry's team. Barry was happy and said Samuel could join them. 

Samuel and Barry went off together, looking for the other reindeer. When they found them, Samuel was so excited. He discovered he could fly with the other reindeer. 

Samuel flew up in the sky with Barry and the other smart reindeer. He felt so happy and free! He had discovered a new and exciting adventure. 

At the end of the day, Samuel thanked Barry for his newfound friendship and all the fun they had. They hugged, said goodbye and went their separate ways.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. Her name was Mia. One day, Mia wanted to explore the world, but her mom would not encourage her. Mia thought that was very mysterious. 

Then one day, there was an emergency. The family had to leave the house to find safety. Mia begged her mom to explore, but her mom did not want to. Eventually, her mom encouraged her to explore the area and find a place to be safe.

Mia and her family explored the area until they were sure it was safe. Mia was so excited to explore and discover new places. She found a mysterious cave and thought it was the most magical thing she had ever seen. 

Mia explored the cave and found many different colorful rocks and other magical items. In the end, Mia's mom was very proud of her for being brave and exploring. 

The moral of the story is to always be brave and explore, even when faced with an emergency. You never know what amazing mysteries you may find!

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tweety. Tweety loved to sing and fly high in the sky. One day, Tweety met a friendly cat named Whiskers. Whiskers asked Tweety, "Where are you going?"

"I'm going to find a safe place to build my nest," replied Tweety.

Whiskers said, "I know a safe place. Follow me." Tweety followed Whiskers to a big tree. "This is a good place for your nest," said Whiskers.

Tweety thanked Whiskers and sang a happy song. But one day, a big storm came and destroyed Tweety's nest. Tweety was very sad and didn't know where to go. Whiskers came to help but it was too late. Tweety was gone. Whiskers felt very sorry and said, "I wish I could have done more to keep Tweety safe. I will always remember Tweety's tasty singing."

Timmy was out playing in the park. He was feeling incredible and having so much fun. Suddenly, a boy next him said, "Hey Timmy, want some beef?"

Timmy hesitated for a moment. He wasn't sure if he wanted beef or not. He wanted to try it, but he was a bit scared. Finally, he said, "Yes please."

The boy gave Timmy a big piece of beef. Timmy took a bite and it tasted absolutely delicious. But, he started to feel a bit funny afterwards. His stomach started to feel a bit weird.

Timmy felt regret for trying the beef. He ran to his mom and told her what happened. His mom said, "It's alright Timmy. Next time, just wait a while before you try something new."

Timmy nodded and promised he would never eat anything too quickly again. From then on, he was always very careful with anything that he tried.

Once upon a time, there was a princess named Lily. She lived in a big castle with her mommy and daddy, the king and queen. One day, the king and queen told Lily that she would marry a prince named Jack. Lily was happy because she always wanted to marry a prince.

But when Lily met Jack, she felt frustrated. He was not very nice to her and always made fun of her. Lily thought that maybe she didn't want to marry Jack after all. 

One day, while Lily was walking in the garden, she met a kind prince named Max. Max was very nice to Lily and they became friends. Lily realized that she wanted to marry Max instead of Jack. 

So, Lily went to her mommy and daddy and told them that she wanted to marry Max instead. The king and queen were happy because they could see that Lily was happy with Max. And so, Lily and Max got married and lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who was very adventurous. One day, she set off to explore the woods. Everything was going great, until she stumbled on a stone. She fell to the ground with a thump. She started to cry, but then remembered how brave she was. She got up and continued exploring the woods, being even more adventurous than before. 

She went really far and the trees got really tall. She had a little snack, to keep her energy up, and then continued her journey. She stumbled over a few more stones, and each time got back up again. 

After a while she reached the edge of the woods and she was so happy. As a reward for being so brave and adventurous, she brought home a big stone, as a reminder of her adventures in the woods.

Lily and Tom were hungry. They wanted to eat soup for lunch. Mom said she would make soup for them. She went to the kitchen and put a pot on the stove.

Lily and Tom followed Mom to the kitchen. They saw a big spoon on the counter. It was shiny and silver. Lily liked shiny things. She wanted to play with the spoon.

"Can I have the spoon, Mom?" Lily asked.

"No, Lily, that spoon is for the soup. You can have another spoon to play with," Mom said.

But Lily did not listen. She reached for the shiny spoon when Mom was not looking. She grabbed it and ran away.

Tom saw Lily run away with the spoon. He was confused. Why did Lily take the spoon? He wanted to help Mom with the soup. He ran after Lily.

"Lily, give back the spoon! Mom needs it for the soup!" Tom shouted.

Lily did not want to give back the spoon. She liked the shiny spoon. She ran to her room and hid under the bed.

Tom followed Lily to her room. He looked under the bed. He saw Lily and the spoon.

"Lily, please give back the spoon. The soup will be ready soon. We can share the soup and eat it with our own spoons," Tom said.

Lily looked at Tom. She saw that he was sad. She felt sorry for Tom. She did not want to make him sad. She decided to give back the spoon.

"Okay, Tom, I will give back the spoon. I'm sorry I took it. I just liked the shiny spoon," Lily said.

She gave the spoon to Tom. Tom smiled and thanked her. He took the spoon to the kitchen and gave it to Mom.

Mom was happy to see the spoon. She stirred the soup with the spoon. She smelled the soup. It was hot and yummy.

"Soup is ready, Lily and Tom! Come and eat!" Mom called.

Lily and Tom ran to the kitchen. They sat at the table and waited for Mom to serve them soup. They each got a bowl of soup and a spoon. They ate the soup and enjoyed it.

They were not hungry anymore. They were happy. They liked soup. They liked Mom. They liked each other. They learned to share. They learned to listen. They learned to say sorry. They learned to shine.

Once upon a time there was a cat and a mouse. They lived in the same house and although they had very different personalities, they were friends. 

One day, the cat had a brilliant idea - he wanted to unite them even more. He wanted to create a special trap that they could share and use together. The mouse thought it was a wonderful plan, and they began to build their special trap.

At first, they worked together, but then the mouse got stuck in the trap and it hurt him. He was very scared, but the cat said he had a plan. He took a piece of yarn he found nearby and used it to unite the mouse with the trap. 

The mouse was very thankful to the cat for not only giving him a way out, but also for uniting them even more closely. From that day on, the mouse and the cat were even better friends.

The End.

Ben and Lily were twins who liked to play with their toys. They had many toys, but they did not like to share them. They always fought over who got to play with what, and they made a lot of noise and mess.

One day, their mom said, "We are going to the store to buy a new rug for the living room. You can come with me, or you can stay home with dad. But you have to clean up your toys first."

Ben and Lily did not want to clean up their toys. They wanted to keep playing. They said, "No, we don't want to go to the store. We want to stay home with dad."

Their mom said, "Okay, but you have to promise to clean up your toys before I come back. And don't fight, or dad will be grumpy."

Ben and Lily said, "Okay, okay, we promise." But they did not mean it. As soon as their mom left, they started to play again. They did not clean up their toys. They did not share. They did not listen to their dad. They made him very grumpy.

When their mom came back, she saw the mess and the noise. She was very angry. She said, "Ben and Lily, you did not keep your promise. You did not clean up your toys. You did not behave. You made dad grumpy. You are not nice."

She took away their toys and put them in a box. She said, "You cannot play with your toys until you learn to share and be nice. And you have to help me put the new rug in the living room."

Ben and Lily felt very sad. They realized they had been selfish and naughty. They said, "We are sorry, mom. We are sorry, dad. We want to be nice. We want to share. We want to help."

They helped their mom put the new rug in the living room. It was a soft and colorful rug. They liked it very much. They said, "Wow, mom, this is a nice rug. Can we play on it?"

Their mom said, "Yes, you can play on it, but only if you share and be nice. And you have to clean up your toys after you play."

Ben and Lily agreed. They said, "Okay, mom, we will share and be nice. And we will clean up our toys. Thank you for the nice rug."

They hugged their mom and dad. They were not grumpy anymore. They were happy. They learned that sharing and being nice is better than fighting and being naughty. They played on the new rug with their toys, and they had a lot of fun.

Once upon a time there was a little bunny. His name was Hop. He liked to hop all around the meadow. He hopped and hopped all day long.

One morning, Hop heard a loud honking. He hopped over to see what was going on. It was a big yellow horn. Hop hopped up close and took a look. He saw a big truck coming down the road. It was a miserable sight.

Hop hopped away to safety, but he kept looking back at the truck. He wished he could get away from that terrible horn. Then, it happened. He hopped onto a tree branch and flew away. He flew all day, out of sight of the miserable truck.

He finally flew away to a new and happy home. He was so happy that he hopped around for joy! He no longer heard the miserable horn, and he was rid of the truck. He was so happy that he kept hopping and hopping. And he never had to worry about the truck again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to play outside in the garden. One day, while she was digging in the dirt, she found a little worm. The worm was wiggly and squiggly and Lily thought it was very funny.

Lily showed the worm to her friend, Timmy. Timmy thought the worm was cool too. Soon, all the kids in the neighborhood wanted to see the worm. The worm became very popular.

One day, while Lily was playing with the worm, she accidentally dropped it. The worm fell into a hole and disappeared. Lily started to panic. She didn't want to lose her new friend. She called out to Timmy for help.

"Don't worry," said Timmy. "We'll find your worm. Let's look together!"

Lily felt better knowing that she had a friend who could help her. They searched and searched until they found the worm again. Lily was so happy to see her wiggly, squiggly friend again. She thanked Timmy for his help and they all played together in the garden.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play dress-up and wear pretty clothes. Her mommy had a big box of clothes that Lily could use to make different outfits. One day, Lily found a sparkly dress that was very fashionable. It had lots of glitter and was pink and purple. She put it on and twirled around, feeling like a princess.

Lily wanted to show her friends her modern dress, so she went outside to play. Her friends were impressed and said she looked very pretty. They asked if they could use the dress too, but it was too small for them. Lily was happy that her dress was special and just for her. She danced and played all day in her fashionable dress, feeling very happy. When it was time for bed, she took off her dress and put it back in the box, ready to use again another day.

Once upon a time, there was a black cow who lived in a meadow. She was a very happy cow who loved to dance and run around. 
One day, while the cow was peacefully eating the grass in the meadow, a big monster came and tried to destroy her. The monster had big red eyes and sharp claws.
The cow ran quickly, but the monster chased after her. It was very scary! Fortunately, a brave old farmer saw what happened and tried to help the cow. 
He waved his hat at the monster and yelled, making it very scared. It ran away, leaving the cow alone in the meadow. 
The farmer smiled and the black cow thanked him with a big, happy moo. Then, the cow was safe and she lived happily ever after!

Once there was a boy who loved to talk. He talked all the time and his family called him chatty. One day he went to the store to buy a crayon. He was really busy running around the store, looking for just the right one. He picked up a bright red crayon and was so excited that he immediately started to talk about it. He talked about how pretty the color was, and what he was going to draw with it. 

When he got home he set up his paper and crayon. He drew a picture of his house but it was a bit wobbly. He showed his Mom and she said that was ok. She was proud of him for being so creative with just a crayon. He smiled because he was proud of himself too. 

He used the crayon to make more pictures. Sometimes he used other colors too. But he always loved the bright red one because it always made him feel so happy and talkative.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Mary. Mary loved to ride her tricycle. She would ride it all around her neighborhood, around the block and down the street. 

One day, Mary saw something strange. It was a big green caterpillar! It was crawling around on the sidewalk. Mary thought it was the most wonderful thing she had ever seen. 

"Do you want to come for a ride on my tricycle, caterpillar?" said Mary with a smile. 

The caterpillar paused for a moment, then shook its head with a harsh squeal. "No way!" it squeaked. "I'm much too big to fit!"

Mary thought for a moment. "Ok," she said, "I know what we could do." Mary ran to the garden and picked some long grass. Carefully, she woven the grass into a small caterpillar-sized hammock. 

"Now you can come on my tricycle," said Mary. The caterpillar smiled and climbed onto the hammock. Mary held onto him tightly as she peddled the tricycle around the block. 

The caterpillar loved the ride, and began to laugh heartily. Mary and the caterpillar became very good friends, and they still ride together sometimes.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. Her name was Sophie. Sophie was very kind. She always tried to be nice to everyone. 

One day, whilst at the playground, Sophie was playing with her friends. Suddenly, a naughty boy came to the playground. He started to behave rudely. He didn't listen to anyone. 

Sophie tried to tell the naughty boy to be kind, but he didn't listen. As a result, he started to misbehave even more. Sophie was very frustrated.
 
Suddenly, Sophie's mom came to the playground. She saw what was happening. She kindly said to the naughty boy, "Please behave how Sophie does, she is a very kind girl". 

The naughty boy realized his mistake and he started to behave better. Sophie was relieved and thanked her mom. They both knew that the best way to behave was to be kind to everyone. 

The End

One day, a boy found a path and walked down it. As he walked, he met a cat. The cat was very friendly and welcomed him. The boy smiled, happy to have a new friend.

He followed the path for a little while and met someone else. It was a girl, who was carrying a very expensive hat. The boy had never seen a hat like it before. He asked the girl what made it so special.

The girl said that the hat was very special because it was made from the finest materials, and that made it expensive. The boy thought the hat was very pretty and asked the girl if he could try it on. She said yes, and the boy put on the hat with a huge smile on his face.

The boy walked with the girl for a while, until they came to the end of the path. They said their goodbyes and went their separate ways. The boy was so happy to have met the girl and found a new friend. He also loved his special hat and wore it proudly.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She loved playing in the park but today there was something special; something new. She walked over to take a look and there, in the middle of the playground, was a giant broccoli! The little girl couldn't believe it - she had never seen a broccoli so big before.

She decided to sit down next to it. She watched as the other children ran around, laughing and playing. When they saw the broccoli they stopped and stared. Even the adults stopped to take a look.

The little girl asked one of the moms, "What happens when you eat broccoli?" The woman smiled and said, "It's supposed to be very good for you - it's available in all kinds of shapes and colors."

The little girl was so excited to learn this new information. She thanked the mom and then ran off to tell all of her friends. Everyone wanted to try the broccoli and they were all amazed at how delicious it was! From then on, they were all searching the playground for more available broccoli!

Once upon a time there was a unique little mushroom. The mushroom liked to explore the garden and one day it stumbled across a puddle. The mushroom stepped into the puddle and everything went hot. The mushroom began to melt!

The mushroom shouted for help but no one was nearby. The mushroom felt more and more energy go out of it until it was completely melted away.

Suddenly, a friendly caterpillar came along. The caterpillar asked, "What happened to you?" 

The mushroom replied, "I stepped into the puddle and it melted my body away." 

The caterpillar wished it could help but it was too late. The mushroom was gone, never to be seen again. 

The caterpillar thought sadly of its unique friend as it went on its way.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Jack and Jill. One day, Jack decided to share his ancient treasure.

"Jill, come over here! I want to share something special with you!" shouted Jack.

Jill came running over and said, "What is it Jack?"

"Look!" said Jack, opening the box to reveal an ancient treasure.

"Wow!" shouted Jill excitedly. "What is it?"

"It's an ancient treasure," said Jack proudly. "I want to share it with you."

"Thank you, Jack! This is the best treasure ever," said Jill with a big smile.

The two friends shared the treasure and promised to keep it safe forever. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Joe who lived on a farm. Joe's farm was full of animals, like cows and chickens, and he even had a horse. One day, Joe went outside to the barn to gather some hay for the animals. As soon as he entered, Joe found that the hay was piled up very deep in the barn. So Joe decided to behave and get to work.

He started picking up the hay and placing it into a pile. It was hard work, but Joe behaved and kept working. Once the hay was all in a neat pile, Joe was very proud of himself. He patted the hay and thanked it for being so helpful. 

The next day, Joe went back to the barn and found that all of his hard work was still there. Joe was amazed at how deep the hay was and realized that behaving was the right thing to do. From then on, Joe was sure to always behave. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Daisy. Daisy wanted a new toy, so she went to the toy shop. In the shop, she saw a big bow. She wanted it very much and asked her Dad if she could have it. Her dad said yes, so Daisy was very happy.

Daisy dad paid for the bow, and before they left the shop, Daisy hugged it and thanked him for buying it. He smiled as he watched her.

Back at home, Daisy played with the bow every day. She loved it and it was very reliable. She could always depend on it to make her smile.

Daisy was very glad that her dad had paid for the bow. She would never forget his kindness.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She was very excited about going to camp for the first time. She was also a little bit anxious. 

The little girl grabbed her bag and ran out the door with a big grin on her face. 

When she arrived at the camp, she was greeted by the camp director. He said, â€œHello, welcome to camp! Are you ready to have some fun?â€

The little girl nodded and smiled. The camp director said, â€œFirst, letâ€™s go down to the lake and take a bath.â€ 

The little girl followed the camp director down to the lake. She was nervous but excited to take her first bath outside. The camp director helped her take off her clothes and get into the lake. 

The little girl squealed with delight and splashed around in the cool water. She had so much fun that she didn't want to get back out! The camp director reassured her that there would be plenty of time for camping fun later and that it was now time to get out and dry off. 

The little girl was relieved to have taken her first lake bath. She knew that she was ready for all the activities that camp had to offer.

Once there was a man who had a dependable bicycle. He liked to take it out and ride it all the time. He took it to the park and went around in circles, spinning his bike wheels. He found it was so much fun to cycle around and around, and the bicycle felt fast.

One day a 3 year old kid asked the man if he could try it out. The man said yes, and the 3 year old hopped onto the bicycle. The man helped the little boy to spin the bike around, and the kid giggled with delight. He had never rode a bike before and he felt very brave.

The man stayed by the kid's side, helping him go around and around. After several spins, the kid fell off the bike and started to cry. The man told him it was okay and the 3 year old realized the bike was nice and dependable. He hopped back on and the man held onto him. Together they rode around the park, spinning together. It was the best day ever!

Once upon a time there was a little girl who loved to do things. One day she had an idea. She decided to find a horn! She found one that was very shiny and she was so excited.

Next she found a person with a big truck. She asked the person if she could do something with the horn. The person was very polite and said yes. So she put the horn in her pocket and ran off.

She went to a playground where some children were playing. She saw a swing in the playground so she went over to it. She pulled the horn out of her pocket and blew it! The children stopped and stared at her in surprise!

The little girl smiled and said, "Let's all swing together!" Everyone was very polite and thanked her for making it so much fun. Together they all swung higher and higher until it was time to go home.

The little girl was very happy she had done something special with the horn and the children. She put the horn away and went off to bed, dreaming of the adventure she had.

Jake was an organized infant. Every day he liked to mix things up in his room. One day he decided to mix up all of his toys. First he mixed all of the blocks together and then he mixed the dolls together. After that, he mixed all of the books one by one. Jake loved mixing because it made him feel excited and happy. When he was done, his room was so organized. He looked around, smiled and said "this is perfect!".

Once upon a time there lived a little boy. He had a motor. He loved riding it around the house. Every day, he would play pretend with his motor.

One day, he felt hungry so he asked his mom for something to eat. She said she had a special treat for him. She gave him a big bowl with a lot of delicious fruits in it.

The little boy was so excited. He grabbed a strawberry and taste it. It was so sweet! He also ate a banana, it was yummy too. Then he ate a raspberry and it was very sour. He made a funny face.

After he ate the fruits, the little boy was full. He thanked his mom and went back to playing with his motor. He had lots of fun that day.

Tom was a bird who lived in a big cage. He had no friends to play with. He was very lonely. He wished he could fly in the sky and see other birds.

One day, a girl came to the cage. She had a feather in her hand. She said, "Hello, bird. Do you want this feather? It is very pretty and soft. You can have it if you sing for me."

Tom was happy. He wanted the feather. He thought maybe he could use it to make a friend. He opened his mouth and sang a song. The girl smiled and gave him the feather.

Tom took the feather and put it in his nest. He felt the feather with his beak. It was very pretty and soft. He said, "Thank you, girl. You are very nice. Maybe you can be my friend."

The girl said, "You're welcome, bird. But I have to go now. Bye-bye." She left the cage and closed the door.

Tom was sad. He wanted the girl to stay. He wanted to talk to her more. He looked at the feather and hoped she would come back.

But she did not come back. The next day, Tom saw a big cat outside the cage. The cat saw Tom and his feather. The cat wanted to eat Tom and his feather. The cat jumped on the cage and shook it hard. The cage fell to the floor and broke. The cat grabbed Tom and his feather and ran away.

Tom was scared. He tried to fly away, but he could not. The cat was too fast and strong. Tom felt the cat's teeth and claws. He felt pain and fear. He cried for help, but no one heard him.

Tom was gone. He never saw the sky or other birds. He never saw the girl or his feather again. He was very lonely. He was very sad. He was very dead.

Once upon a time, there was a bright and attractive blueberry. It was very special because it had never been picked before. The blueberry tried its best to grow all summer, but no one noticed it. One day, however, a little boy was out walking in the field. His name was John, and he was just 3 years old. 

John noticed the beautiful blueberry and decided to pick it for a special treat. He ran back to his house and put it in a pot. Then, he mixed together some butter and sugar, and stirred it all together. After a few minutes of stirring, he opened the pot and the kitchen filled with a wonderful smell.

John smiled and took out the warm blueberry pie. He quickly put it on a plate and took a bite. It was delicious! He smiled and thanked his mum for the special treat. From that day forward, John always looked out for attractive blueberries in the field, so he could make special treats whenever he wanted.

Once upon a time, there was a friendly girl named Lucy. She was very curious and loved learning new things. One day, Lucy went to the park by herself. As she ran around, she stumbled upon a wise owl. The owl asked Lucy, "Do you want to learn a lesson?" Lucy nodded her head happily and the owl began to speak.

"If you're ever feeling lost, remember that wisdom will always be there for you. Just be reliable and never give up. Even if you lose something, you can always find it again if you try hard enough."

Lucy thought about the owl's words for a moment and smiled. She thanked the owl for the wise advice. From that day forward, she always kept the owl's words in mind. Whenever Lucy lost something, she remembered the owl's message and searched until she found it.

The wise owl smiled and flew away, leaving Lucy with a valuable lesson that she would never forget.

One day, something special happened. A girl saw a sport like she had never seen before. She watched it and she felt dizzy. She liked it very much, and wanted to try it.

The girl asked her parents and they said she could try it. So, the very next day, she went to the sport with her parents. Everyone was really friendly, and the girl had so much fun.

She learned to jump and spin around and she wasn't dizzy anymore. She was so happy to be part of the sport. After that day, she went back to the sport every day, and she got better and better.

The girl's parents were happy too, because she made a lot of friends and she was so happy. With lots of practice, the girl soon became an expert of the sport, and she was the happiest she'd ever been.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside with her friends. One day, they went on a walk and found a big cross in the park. It was very impressive! They decided to climb on it and take a picture.

But when they got home, Lily realized she forgot her favorite toy at the park. She was very sad. Her mom asked her what was wrong and Lily told her about her toy. Her mom said they could go back and look for it.

When they got to the park, they found Lily's toy right next to the cross! Lily was so happy and impressed that she found her toy. She gave her mom a big hug and said, "Thank you for helping me not forget my toy!"

Once upon a time there was a messy room. Toys were all over the floor and the bed was a mess.

A young boy named Timmy wanted to tidy up the room. He began to pick up the toys and put them on the shelves. He took all the pillows off the bed and made it look neat and tidy.

When he was finished, a feeling of peace came into the room. Timmy smiled and laid down on the bed. He was so happy to have finished tidying the room.

Then Timmy's mom came in and praised him for making his room look so neat and clean. Timmy smiled even wider. He was sure glad to have finished tidying up his messy room.

Once upon a time there was a girl called Sue. She was only 3 and liked exploring outside.

One day Sue was playing in her garden when she saw something wet and unusual. She came closer and leaned down to take a look. Suddenly she heard a whisper! She felt scared but called out bravely 'Who's there?'.

From the wet and unusual thing stepped out a friendly frog. His voice was soft and kind as he said 'Hello Sue, I'm Henry.' Sue was so happy to meet someone new and laughed as the frog hopped away.

The next day Sue and Henry became best friends. They played in the garden and went for adventures. Every time they went out Henry would whisper 'Let's explore!'. Sue couldn't believe that she had found such an unusual new friend.

Once upon a time, there were two friends, a boy and a girl. The girl had a spade, and she liked using it to dig in the ground. 

One day, the boy said to the girl, â€œLetâ€™s make a hole together!â€ He had a spade too, and he held it in his hands. Together, they used their spades to dig into the ground.

But soon the ground became very dirty, so filthy that the friends couldnâ€™t see. So the girl said, â€œLetâ€™s join our hands to make a big circle.â€ And when they did that, the dirt moved away and the ground was clean.

The friends were so happy that they had been able to unite and make the ground clean again. They hugged each other and laughed. And from then on, whenever they had a problem, they would unite to solve it.

Sara and Ben were twins who liked to play in the garden. One day, they found a big hole in the ground. They wondered what was inside.

"Let's dig and see," Ben said. He took a shovel and started to scoop out dirt.

"Wait, Ben," Sara said. "Maybe there is something bad in there. Maybe it is a trap or a monster. Please be careful."

Ben did not listen. He thought Sara was foolish and scared. He wanted to find a treasure or a secret. He dug faster and faster.

Suddenly, he felt something hard and shiny. He pulled it out of the hole. It was a metal ball with buttons and lights. He was very happy.

"Look, Sara, look what I found!" he shouted. "It is a toy or a machine. Maybe it can fly or talk or make magic. Let's play with it."

He pressed one of the buttons. The ball made a loud noise and started to shake. Sara was afraid. She ran to Ben and tried to take the ball from him.

"Ben, stop, stop!" she cried. "That is not a toy or a machine. That is a bomb. It will explode and hurt us and the earth. Please give it to me. We have to throw it away."

But Ben did not listen. He thought Sara was foolish and silly. He wanted to keep the ball and see what it could do. He pressed another button. The ball flashed and beeped. It was ready to explode.

Marlon was only three years old but he already knew that he wanted to be an astronaut one day. Every night he would look up at the stars and dream about floating around in the sky. He decided to make a spaceship out of cardboard.

Marlon was so excited. He chose a nice spot in the garden to launch his spaceship and asked his mum to push him up in it. His mum laughed and was happy to help him.

When they got to the top, Marlon didn't know what to do. He was scared and wished he had asked his mum for a few tips. He started flapping his arms up and down quickly and was surprised to see that he hadn't moved an inch!

Suddenly, Marlon realised that he was missing something very important - oxygen. He had been so excited about taking off that he had forgotten this essential item! He looked down at his mum and felt a wave of regret as he watched her shaking her head in disappointment.

Marlon's mum hugged him tightly and said, "Don't worry, Marlon. You'll be a great astronaut one day!" Marlon smiled and hugged her back. He now knew that he needed to remember the right things when making his spaceship!

Once upon a time there was a big tree. It had lots of leaves and a big branch. Every day the wind blew and the leaves would dance around the big branch.

One day, a little bird came and landed on the big branch. He was very excited and asked if he could play. The tree was happy and said yes. The bird held onto the branch with its claws and started to move up and down.

The bird had a plan. He wanted the branch to get bigger and stronger. So, he started to chirp and sing. His happy singing made the branch grow bigger and stronger. It was now beautiful!

The bird continued to sing and the branch kept getting bigger and stronger. Pretty soon, it was the biggest, strongest and most beautiful branch in the whole world. Every day, the little bird flew around, singing happy songs and helping make the branch bigger and better.

The little bird had improved the branch and the tree was very happy. From then on, the branch was known as the most beautiful branch in the world.

Joey was so excited when he saw the horse. It was pink and he thought it was so pretty. He wanted to get close to it to see it better. He reached out and touched the horse's pink fur. It felt so soft and smooth. 

The horse nickered softly and made Joey feel happy. He thought it was so nice to pet the pink horse. Joey wished he could take it home but he knew that wasn't possible. 

Joey gave the horse one more pat before saying goodbye. He hoped to see the pink horse someday again. He smiled and waved as it trotted away and he walked back home, feeling happy.

Once upon a time there was a special wish. It lived in a big, friendly tree. The wish liked to be snuggled and cuddled. It also liked to watch the animals play in the meadow below.

One day, a dragon came and wanted to take the wish away. The dragon was very mean and it wanted to keep the wish all to itself.

Because the wish was so small and delicate, the animals decided to protect it. They made a big circle around the wish and they all huddled close together. 

The dragon was so surprised that it decided to leave. It flew away, and it never came back. The animals felt so happy they hugged the wish and sang a special song.

The animals made sure the wish was safe and protected. They would always be friends and look after the wish. They knew it would always be safe in their big, friendly tree.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat sausages for breakfast. One day, Lily woke up and couldn't find her sausage. She searched everywhere in the kitchen but couldn't find it.

Lily's mom asked her, "What are you looking for, Lily?"

"I'm searching for my sausage. It's missing," replied Lily.

Lily's mom smiled and said, "Don't worry, Lily. I found your sausage. It was hiding behind the milk carton. Now you can have a happy breakfast!"

Lily was so happy and thanked her mom. She ate her sausage and had a happy day. The end.

Once there was a big, impressive mountain. It was so big that it looked like it could touch the clouds. Everyone admired it.

One day, a small child named Ted wanted to explore the mountain. His parents said no, it was too dangerous. But Ted was brave and he still wanted to explore.

He started to climb the mountain on his own. He was very brave and he felt safe and confident as he climbed. The climb was tiring, but Ted was determined to reach the top.

But then, an avalanche of snow came down from the mountain's peak. Ted tried to find a safe place, but he couldn't find one in time. The avalanche was too powerful and he got buried in the snow.

The villagers admired Ted for being so brave, but it was a sad ending. He never made it to the top of the impressive mountain.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. He was three years old. Tim really loved whales.

One day, Tim went to the beach with his mom. He saw a whale in the water. He ran to the edge of the water and shouted, "Mommy, look! A whale!"

Tim's mom smiled. She said, "Yes, that's a whale. Would you like to try to match it?"

Tim was excited. "Yes!" he said.

Tim and his mom ran up and down the beach. They looked for something that matched the whale. Finally, they found some blue and white beach towels. They put them together and matched the whale's colors!

Tim and his mom had lots of fun. Matching the whale was so easy - it was a great day at the beach.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved playing with her toys and her favorite toy was a rubber duck. One day, Lily was taking a bath with her rubber duck when she noticed that the water was leaking from the bathtub. She quickly called out to her mommy and said, "Mommy, the water is leaking!" 

Her mommy came running and saw that the water was indeed leaking. She told Lily to quickly get out of the bathtub so that she could save the water from going to waste. Lily got out of the bathtub and watched as her mommy quickly fixed the leak. 

After the leak was fixed, Lily's mommy turned to her and said, "Lily, you were so brave to tell me about the leak. You saved a lot of water from going to waste." Lily smiled and felt proud of herself. She looked at her rubber duck and noticed that it was pale from being in the water for too long. She quickly took it out of the bathtub and said, "Don't worry rubber duck, I saved you too!"

Once upon a time, there was a lucky girl named Susan. She loved baking, and she could make the most delicious treats! One day Susan thought of a wonderful idea. She would bake a cake and put a print on it.

Susan got to work. She found the most delicious ingredients and gathered them all together. She made the batter and put it in the oven. She was careful to not let it bake too long, and when it finished, the cake was perfect!

Susan was so excited! She took the cake out of the oven and carefully spread the print on it. She stepped back to admire her handiwork.

Just then, Susan's mom poked her head in. "What a lucky girl you are, Susan," she said. "This cake looks so yummy!" Susan smiled and then, with a wink, she said proudly, "I know, isn't it great? I got the idea myself!"

Lily was a wise girl who liked to help her mom in the kitchen. She knew how to wash the fruits, stir the soup and set the table. One day, her mom let her make a salad for lunch. Lily was very happy and proud.

She took a big plate and put some lettuce, tomatoes, carrots and cheese on it. She added some salt, pepper and oil and mixed everything with a spoon. She tasted a bite and smiled. It was yummy and healthy. She carried the plate to the table and put it in the middle.

"Look, mom, I made a salad!" she said.

"Wow, Lily, you did a great job!" her mom said. "You are a very wise and helpful girl. Thank you for making lunch for us."

Lily's mom gave her a hug and a kiss. They sat down and enjoyed the salad together. Lily felt very happy and proud. She liked to help her mom in the kitchen.

Lily was an adventurous girl. She liked to explore new places and find new things. One day, she went to the park with her mom and dad. She saw a big green slide and wanted to try it.

She ran to the slide and climbed up the ladder. She looked down and saw how high it was. She felt a little scared, but also excited. She slid down very fast and laughed. She liked the slide a lot. She wanted to do it again and again.

She forgot about her mom and dad. She forgot that they told her to stay close to them. She forgot that there were other people in the park. She only thought about the slide.

She did not see that her mom and dad were looking for her. They were worried and scared. They called her name and searched everywhere. They did not see her on the slide.

Lily did not hear them. She was having too much fun. She did not notice that the sun was going down and it was getting dark. She did not notice that the park was empty and quiet.

She slid down one more time and then she saw. She saw that she was alone. She saw that she was lost. She felt a big fear in her chest. She cried and cried. She wanted her mom and dad.

She heard a voice. It was her dad. He found her and hugged her. He was happy and angry. He told her that she was very naughty and that she should never forget them. He told her that he loved her and that he was sorry.

She hugged him back and said sorry too. She said that she loved him and that she was sorry. She said that she was adventurous but not smart. She said that she would never forget them again.

They walked to her mom and hugged her too. She was happy and sad. She told her that she was very brave and that she should always be careful. She told her that she loved her and that she was sorry.

They all hugged and kissed and said sorry and love. They left the park and went home. Lily learned a lesson. She learned that being adventurous is good, but being safe is better. She learned that forgetting her mom and dad is bad, but remembering them is good. She learned that she had the best mom and dad in the world.

Once upon a time, there was a happy little girl called Ella. Ella had a friendly pet rabbit called Toby. One day, Ella wanted to give Toby a nice trim. She asked her mother for a razor to lend her. 

Her mother said, "That's a great idea! But why do you need a razor?" 

Ella replied, "Toby has been shedding so much fur and it's getting messy! I wanted to lend him a razor to help make him neater." 

Her mother said, "Ah, I understand. Now that's a kind thing to do. Here, you can lend this razor to Toby. Make sure you're careful with it." 

Ella said "Thank you, Mum! I will be careful!" She took the razor and lent it to Toby. It was the perfect size for him and he looked so neat afterwards. Toby was so happy and Ella was too. 

The end.

One day, Jack and his mom decided to visit a big park. The park was enormous, with lots of tall trees and lots of other children running around to play.

Jack's mom said, "Look at how big this park is, Jack! Shall we explore?"

Jack said, "Yes please!"

So they started walking through the park. After a while, they came to a big cross. It was made of wood and it was enormous.

Jack said, "Mommy, what's that big cross?"

Mom said, "That's a cross. It is a sign for people to remember that Jesus died for us and loves us very much."

Jack was very surprised. He said, "That's amazing! Thank you for showing me this."
