Once upon a time there was a sister and her brother. They were the best of friends and did everything together. Every morning they went to the park to play in the sunshine. 

One day the brother read a book about a wise old owl. When he finished, he looked up and shared his thoughts with his sister. "I think it was so wise for the owl to know so much," he said.

The sister thought for a moment and said, "You know what!? You can be like the wise owl, too! Maybe you can read more books and learn lots of wise things. Then you can share it with me and others."

The brother smiled and replied, "Yes! That's a good idea. Then we can be just like the wise owl, together!" 

The sister and her brother went on to have many other adventures in the park and learn a lot of wise things by reading books.

One day, a fish was swimming in the deep sea. He liked to look at the bright colors of the coral and the plants. He was happy and curious.

He saw a big shadow above him. He swam up to meet it. He thought it was a friend. But it was a shark! The shark had sharp teeth and a hungry look. The fish was scared and tried to swim away.

But the shark was faster and chased him. The fish saw a small hole in a rock. He swam inside and hid. The shark could not fit in the hole. He was angry and went away.

The fish was safe, but he learned a lesson. He learned that not everyone he meets is a friend. He learned that he should be careful and not go too close to strangers. He learned that the deep sea can be dangerous. He was glad that he had a safe home in the rock. He thanked the rock for saving him.

It was time to celebrate! Mommy and Daddy said they had something special to do.

They took their daughter to the attic. She was a bit fearful. She held Daddy's hand tightly.

When they got to the top of the attic, there was a huge surprise - balloons, cake, and lots of presents! She couldn't believe it.

Mommy and Daddy said it was time for her birthday party! She was so excited. She got to play games and blow out all the candles on her cake.

It was a fun day of celebrating in the attic. Then they went home with lots of goodies and memories.

Gina was a little girl. She had a file that was filled with fun things. She loved it. 

One day, the file went missing. Gina looked everywhere but couldn't find it. She was very sad.

Gina's mommy asked her what was wrong. She said she missed her file. Mommy said she would help find it.

They looked everywhere together. Finally, they found it in a bad place. It was not safe. 

Mommy said it was okay. She hugged Gina and told her that the file was safe now. Gina smiled and said she was very happy.

One day, two pals; a giraffe and a hippo decided to join the friend party. The party was held in the living room and everyone was invited!

The hippo was so excited. He gathered a thick pillow and hopped to the living room. The giraffe shyly joined him.

As they arrived at the living room, the party was already started! There were other friends like the lion and the monkey. Everyone was having so much fun.

Suddenly, the friends noticed the giraffe and hippo! They waved and smiled at them. The giraffe was so happy, he grabbed a thick pillow and snuggled with the hippo; they became fast friends!

The party continued as all the friends joined in the fun, playing and laughing until the end of the day. That was the best friend party ever!

One day, there was a panda who was very organized. All of the panda's days were spent in a very structured and planned way. 

One morning, the panda was walking along and saw a little bird. The bird was about to strike its beak against a rock. The panda said to the bird, "Hey! What are you doing?"

The bird answered, "I'm trying to crack open this rock!" 

The panda was surprised and said, "That's really brave! But don't you know how organized I am? You should come and help me with my routine!" 

The bird thought about it for a moment and decided that it would join the organized panda in his schedule. The two of them went about their days and had lots of fun playing together.

John was a three-year-old who loved playing and running around in his backyard. Every morning he was so excited to go outside and explore. One day as he tried to rush outside, he saw that his door was locked. He pulled and pulled on the door knob, but it wouldn't open.

"Daddy, why can't I go outside?" he asked, feeling frustrated.

"I locked the door so nothing gets into our yard," his father replied. 

John wanted to have fun in the backyard. He tried to shoulder the door open but it wouldn't budge. He figured out that it was his dad who had the key.

John tapped on his dad's shoulder, "Please open the door, Daddy!" he pleaded. 

His dad smiled and got the key. He opened the door and John rushed out into the backyard. He was so happy to play outside with all the toys, that he laughed and danced with joy. 

John's dad smiled at how excited his son was. He looked so happy and content having fun in the backyard.

Once upon a time there was a little girl and she wanted a puppy. She asked her mom for one and the mom said yes! The girl was so happy! She went outside to find her puppy and went for a walk in the icy cold winter air.

Suddenly, she noticed a puppy! It was a brown and white puppy and it was shaking because it was so cold. She quickly joined the puppy and they ran back home. When they got back, the girl's mom gave the puppy a big hug to keep it warm. The puppy was so happy and they snuggled on the couch together.

The mom made a warm blanket for the puppy and the girl made a special bed for her puppy in her bedroom. They ate some food and the puppy even drank some milk.

The girl and the puppy became best friends. Everywhere the girl went, the puppy joined her. Even in the snow, the puppy and girl had fun together. The puppy was so happy to have a new home and be with the girl. They were an icy cold winter team!

Tom and Sue are friends. They like to play in the park. They have a rag. The rag is old and dirty, but they love it. They pretend the rag is a cape, a flag, or a blanket.

One day, they are playing with the rag in the park. They see a big dog. The dog is hungry. He smells the rag. He thinks the rag is food. He runs to Tom and Sue and tries to take the rag.

"Hey, that is our rag!" Tom says. He pulls the rag from the dog.

"Go away, dog!" Sue says. She waves a stick at the dog.

The dog is angry. He barks and growls. He wants the rag. He jumps at Tom and Sue.

Tom and Sue are scared. They run away from the dog. They hold the rag tight. They look for a safe place.

They see a bench. They run to the bench. They climb on the bench. They hug the rag.

The dog can not reach them. He is sad. He walks away.

Tom and Sue are happy. They have their rag. They are safe.

They say to the rag, "We love you, rag. You are our friend."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and jump on her bed. One day, her mom bought some new furniture for their house. Lily thought it was incredible! She loved the new couch and the pretty table.

But then it started to rain. Lily's mom told her to stay inside, but Lily wanted to play outside in the rain. She ran outside and jumped in puddles. But then, she slipped on the wet grass and hurt herself really badly.

Lily learned that sometimes it's important to listen to your mom and stay safe inside. She also learned to be careful around wet furniture, so it doesn't get ruined. Even though she got hurt, she was glad she learned an important lesson.

Once, there was a lively fox. He loved to explore and often went for walks around his home. One day, he came to a big lake and saw a flame in the middle! He wondered why it was there and decided he wanted it for himself. So the fox reached out and stole the flame. He was so proud of his new flame and couldn't wait to show it to his family!

He ran back home and proudly showed his family. All of his friends and family admired the flame and thought it was amazing. They also gave the fox lots of praise and congratulated him. The fox was so proud and happy he'd been able to steal the flame! He was so glad he had such an adventure. 

The fox and his family continued to admire the flame. They watched it flicker and light up the room with its lively colors. The fox never forgot how brave he was to steal the flame and always had fond memories of his exploration.

Once there was a boy named Jack who loved to whistle. Whenever he was feeling glad, he would whistle a happy tune. One day Jack was walking through the woods and he saw a leak. He wondered where it came from and decided to investigate. As he got closer he heard someone whistling. He walked over to the source of the whistle and saw a small beautiful stream. He was so glad to have found a stream that he started to whistle along.

Jack asked, â€œWho are you?â€ 

The stream replied, â€œI am a stream, and I make music by whistling. I make music with the leak that you found.â€

Jack was so happy he started to whistle with the stream. They whistled together for what seemed like forever and it was the most beautiful music that Jack had ever heard. They were so glad to be able to make music together!

Lily and Ben were bored. They wanted to play outside, but it was raining. They looked around the house for something fun to do. They saw a big box in the corner. It had a picture of a castle on it.

"Let's build the castle!" Lily said.

"OK!" Ben said.

They opened the box and took out the pieces. They were very cheap. They broke easily and did not fit well. Lily and Ben tried to make the castle, but it kept falling apart.

"This is no fun!" Lily said.

"Let's pretend we are in the castle!" Ben said.

They crawled inside the box and closed the flaps. They imagined they were a king and a queen. They had a crown and a dress and a sword. They had a lot of fun.

Suddenly, they heard a loud noise. It was their dog, Rex. He smelled them in the box. He wanted to play with them. He ran to the box and jumped on it. He ripped the flaps and bit the pieces. He barked and wagged his tail.

"Rex, no!" Lily and Ben shouted.

They tried to escape, but it was too late. Rex had made a big mess. He had torn the box and the pieces. He had scratched Lily and Ben. They had cuts and bruises. They cried and ran to their mom.

Mom was very angry. She saw the mess and the blood. She scolded Lily and Ben and Rex. She threw away the box and the pieces. She cleaned their wounds and gave them a hug.

She said, "You should not play with cheap toys. They are not safe. And you should not hide in a box. Rex did not know you were there. He thought it was a game. You are lucky he did not hurt you more. Next time, be more careful."

Lily and Ben felt sorry. They said, "We are sorry, Mom. We were bored. We wanted to have fun."

Mom said, "I know, but you have to be smart. You have other toys to play with. And you can read a book or draw a picture or sing a song. There are many ways to have fun inside. And when it stops raining, you can play outside. But no more cheap castles, OK?"

Lily and Ben said, "OK, Mom. We love you."

They hugged Mom and Rex. They learned their lesson. They never played with cheap castles again.

Once upon a time, there was a grumpy old man who lived in a house. He had a pipe that he loved to smoke. One day, a little bird flew into his house and started to sing. The grumpy old man did not like the singing and yelled at the bird to leave. But the bird did not listen and continued to sing.

The grumpy old man got angrier and angrier and yelled louder and louder. Suddenly, the pipe fell out of his mouth and broke into pieces. The grumpy old man was so upset that he started to cry. The little bird saw the grumpy old man crying and felt bad. So, the bird flew over to the man and started to sing a lullaby. The grumpy old man listened to the beautiful singing and felt better. From that day on, the grumpy old man and the little bird became friends and the man never yelled again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She was walking in the woods when she saw something in the trees. It was a twig that appeared clear as ice.

The little girl was curious, so she asked her mom, "What is that twig?".

Her mom smiled and said, "That's a magical twig. It is clear and sparkly, and it makes wishes come true!" 

The little girl was so excited! She wanted a wish to come true. She reached for the twig, but it disappeared. 

The mom smiled and said, "The twig is magical. It only appears when it's ready to give a wish." 

The little girl was happy to know that, so she waited. She believed that soon the twig would appear, and her wish would come true.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the sunshine. One day, Lily saw a big, beautiful rainbow in the sky. She ran to her mom and said, "Look, Mommy! A pretty rainbow!"

Her mom said, "Yes, Lily, it's very pretty. But we have to leave soon to go to the store."

Lily was sad to leave the rainbow, but she knew she could come back and see it another time. As they walked to the store, Lily saw some kids playing in the rain. She wanted to play too, but her mom said no. Lily felt ashamed that she couldn't play in the rain like the other kids.

When they got home, Lily's mom surprised her with a rainbow sticker. Lily was so happy and put it on her favorite toy. She said, "Thank you, Mommy! Even though we had to leave the rainbow, I have a little rainbow with me now."

Tim and Sue wanted to play in the sand. They took their spades and buckets and ran to the big hill. The hill had a lot of sand and rocks. It looked like fun.

"Let's climb the hill and make a castle!" Tim said.

"OK!" Sue said. They started to climb the hill with their spades and buckets. They dug some sand and put it in their buckets.

But the hill was very steep and slippery. Tim and Sue had to be careful not to fall. They held on to their spades and buckets.

Suddenly, Tim saw a shiny rock. He wanted to have it. He let go of his spade and reached for the rock.

"Tim, don't!" Sue shouted. "You will fall!"

But Tim did not listen. He grabbed the rock and smiled. He thought he was clever.

But then he lost his balance. He slipped and rolled down the hill. He dropped his rock and his bucket. He got sand in his eyes and mouth. He cried.

Sue watched him and shook her head. She thought he was foolish. She climbed down the hill and helped him. She gave him some water and a hug.

"Tim, you should not let go of your spade. You could have hurt yourself. And the rock was not worth it. It was just a rock." Sue said.

"I'm sorry, Sue. You are right. I was foolish. I should have listened to you. Can we still play?" Tim said.

"Of course we can. But let's play on the flat ground. It is safer and easier. And we can still make a castle." Sue said.

They took their spades and buckets and went to the flat ground. They dug some sand and made a castle. They had fun. They learned their lesson. They were happy.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to play outside. She especially liked to play in her garden.

One day, while she was playing in the garden, Lily found a bracelet lying on the ground. It was a pretty bracelet with silver and pink stones. Lily stopped to look at it. She paused for a moment and then picked it up.

Lily ran to show the bracelet to her mama. Mama was very happy and told Lily she could keep it forever. "It's so lovely!", said Mama.

Lily started wearing the bracelet all the time. Whenever she felt sad or lonely, she would take a look at the bracelet and feel peaceful.

From then on, the bracelet was very special to Lily. Whenever she wore it, it made her feel brave and happy.

Once upon a time there was a boy. He liked to wander around in the woods. He found a skull there. It was very big and tough. He decided to wander with it in his hands. He explored the sunny forest with the skull.

The boy made a friend with the skull, and he would even talk to it. He told it about all his adventures and he asked it questions, too. He found some fruits to eat and some tiny animals to play with. The boy wandered happily in the woods all day long.

When it was dusk, the boy finally went home with the skull. He wanted to keep it as a friend. But it was getting a bit too dark to wander around and he had to go home. He promised his new skull friend that he'd come back soon and wander in the woods with him again.

Sara and Ben are happy. They like to play in the park with their ball. They run and kick and laugh. They see a big lake with ducks and fish. They want to see the lake.

They hold hands and walk to the lake. They see the water is blue and shiny. They see the ducks are white and brown. They see the fish are orange and green. They say hello to the ducks and the fish.

They throw their ball to each other near the lake. They are careful not to drop the ball in the water. They have fun with their ball. But then, something bad happens. Ben throws the ball too hard and it goes over Sara's head. The ball falls into the lake. Sara and Ben are sad.

They run to the edge of the lake. They look for their ball. They cannot see their ball. The ball has disappeared. They do not know what to do. They cry and hug each other.

Then, they hear a splash. They look up and see a duck. The duck has their ball in its mouth. The duck swims to them and gives them their ball. Sara and Ben are happy again. They say thank you to the duck. The duck quacks and swims away. Sara and Ben smile and play with their ball again. They are careful not to throw it in the lake. They are happy.

Once there was a bunny who lived in the forest. He was always very happy, hopping around and making new friends. Every day he hopped around the forest meeting new animals. 

One day, he was hopping near a stream and heard a funny noise. He stopped and looked to see what it was. Suddenly he saw a big snake! He was very anxious but he bravely hopped closer. The snake was friendly and they talked for a while. They even played tag, hopping around the stream. 

The bunny and the snake became best friends. Every day they would hop around the forest, having a lot of fun. They were always very happy together. It made the bunny less anxious. 

The bunny and the snake would hop all around the forest, exploring new lands and having adventures. They were the best of friends and the forest was a much happier place with them hopping around.

Lila and Ben were best friends. They liked to play in the park with their toys. Lila had a doll and Ben had a car. They shared their snacks and had fun.

One day, they saw a big orange cat in the park. It was sitting on a bench, licking its paw. Lila and Ben wanted to pet the cat. They walked slowly towards it.

"Meow," the cat said. It looked at them with green eyes.

"Hello, cat," Lila said. "You are very pretty. Can we pet you?"

The cat did not answer. It arched its back and hissed.

"Be careful," Ben said. "The cat does not like us. It might scratch us."

Lila did not listen to Ben. She reached out her hand to touch the cat. The cat swiped at her with its claws.

"Ow!" Lila cried. She pulled back her hand. It had a red mark on it. It hurt a lot.

"I told you to be careful," Ben said. He was a reliable friend. He always warned Lila when something was dangerous. He took out a tissue from his pocket and wrapped it around Lila's hand.

"Thank you, Ben," Lila said. She was sorry she did not listen to him. She hugged him.

The cat jumped off the bench and ran away. Lila and Ben decided to leave the cat alone. They went back to their toys and played some more. They were happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She loved animals and wanted to go to the park to see them.

So she asked her mom if she could go. Mom said yes, but to be careful. 

So off she went to the park. There were so many animals to see! She saw birds in the sky, ducks swimming in the pond, and lots of squirrels running around. 

She was so excited and wanted to tell someone. So she ran to get her mom and said, "Mom! Come see all the animals!"

Mom smiled and said, "Wow! Aren't they lovely? That's why it's important to stay careful around them." 

So the little girl stayed safe and had lots of fun looking and learning about all the animals.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in her backyard. One day, her parents put up a big tent for her to play in. The tent was colorful and had lots of toys inside.

Lily was playing in the tent when she slipped on a toy and fell down. She wasn't hurt, but she was a little scared. However, Lily was a stubborn girl and didn't want to leave the tent. She got back up and kept playing.

As the sun started to set, Lily's parents called her inside for dinner. Lily didn't want to leave the tent, but her parents promised she could play in it again tomorrow. So, she reluctantly left the tent and went inside for dinner. From that day on, Lily loved playing in her tent and never slipped again.

Once upon a time there was a mill. It was an old and organized mill. Inside the mill you could find a lot of things that belonged to the mill. Every day people went to the mill to help organize and take care of the things that belonged to the mill.

One day a little boy came to the mill. He asked the people at the mill where he belonged. The nice people smiled and told him that he belonged at the mill too.

The little boy started to help the people at the mill. They showed him how to organize the things that belonged to the mill. He quickly learned how to do it and soon he was helping the people organize the mill better than ever before.

The little boy was so happy that he now belonged at the mill. He was proud to call the mill his home. He continued to help the people at the mill for many years, and everyone was thankful for all his hard work. The mill was organized better than ever before and the little boy finally had a place to belong.

Once upon a time, there was a cow. She liked to come to the farm every day. But one day, a big storm came. It was not safe. The cow was scared, but it still wanted to come to farm.

But the wind and rain were so strong that the cow was afraid to come. Then a little boy came to the farm. He wanted to help the cow feel safe. He said â€œCome cow and I'll take care of you.â€

The little boy put his hand on the cow's back. He took her to the barn. The cow felt safe there. The little boy gave the cow some food and water. And he even let the cow sleep in his bed!

The storm was gone the next day, but the cow still stayed. She and the little boy were best friends. From then on, whenever the cow wanted to come to the farm, she knew she would be safe.

Once upon a time there lived a brave leopard in a deep, dark forest. All day long the leopard looked for food, playing and exploring all the nooks and crannies of the forest. One day, the leopard came across another animal, who had become tired and weak. The leopard decided to encourage the animal to persevere and keep going. The animal moved a little but was too weak to get up. The leopard kept encouraging the animal until finally it said, "Thank you. I'm just too tired to continue". Suddenly, a hunter appeared and the leopard was too scared to help the animal anymore. The hunter shot the animal and the leopard fled from the forest never to be seen again.

Once upon a time there was a wizard. He liked to create things. One day he decided he wanted to make something special. He wanted to create a new kind of medicine. So he set to work to make the best medicine he could. 

He worked very hard and was very careful with his work. Finally, he had finished and it was time to test it out. He took some of the medicine and drank it. He felt strange and started to feel better.

The wizard was so happy he decided to share his medicine with his friends. So he loaded up his cart and went to see them. On the way, he noticed it was getting very noisy. Everyone was very excited to get the medicine. 

Once his friends had taken the medicine, the wizard asked if it helped. They said yes and thanked him for the wonderful medicine. Everyone was very happy and the wizard smiled. He was glad that he had been able to create medicine that others could use.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who lived in a big house with her mommy and daddy. One day, while playing outside, she saw a bird flying in the sky. She got very excited and wanted to catch it.

Lily went inside and asked her mommy if they could get a birdcage to keep the bird in. Her mommy said they could plan a trip to the pet store to get one. Lily was very excited about the plan.

The next day, Lily and her mommy went to the pet store and bought a beautiful birdcage. They brought it home and set it up in the backyard. Lily waited patiently for the bird to come back.

Finally, the bird came back and landed in the backyard. Lily quickly caught it and put it in the birdcage. She was very happy and excited to have a new pet. From that day on, Lily took good care of her bird and they became best friends.

Once upon a time, there was a happy boy named Tim. Tim loved to play with his toys and his friends. One day, Tim went to the beach with his family. They saw a big island far away. The island looked different than the other islands they had seen before.

Tim wanted to go to the island and see what was there. His family said they could not swim that far. But Tim had an idea. He asked his friends if they wanted to join him on an adventure. They all said yes! So, Tim and his friends got into a boat and rowed to the island. 

When they got there, they found many new things they had never seen before. There were big trees, colorful birds, and even a hidden cave. Tim and his friends were so happy they decided to stay on the island for a while. They played and explored until it was time to go back home. Tim knew he would always remember their fun adventure to the different island.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Sarah. She was very excited because it was time to go for a bike ride with her dad.

Sarah put on her gear, which included a helmet and some sneakers. She hopped on her bike and was ready to go!

But as Sarah and her dad started to ride, Sarah noticed something was wrong. Her dad had forgotten to fasten his safety gear! 

The dad heard Sarah shouting about it and he realized his mistake. He quickly fixed his gear and firmly told Sarah to never be careless when it comes to safety.

Sarah nodded and the two of them set off again, this time with the right safety gear. They both had a great time on their bike ride, shouting with glee all the way!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she went to the bakery with her mommy. Lily wanted to eat a yummy pastry, but her mommy said she had to wait until they got home. Lily was sad, but she didn't cry.

Suddenly, it started to rain outside. Lily's mommy said, "Oh no, our car seat is going to get wet!" Lily said, "Mommy, can we sit in the bakery and eat my pastry while we wait for the rain to stop?" Her mommy thought it was a good idea, so they went inside.

Lily was so happy to eat her pastry. She said, "Mmm, this is so yummy!" Her mommy said, "I'm glad you like it, Lily." Then, the rain stopped and they went back to their car. Lily's mommy said, "Good thing we didn't have to sit on a wet seat!" Lily giggled and said, "Yeah, that would be silly!"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was very hungry and wanted to eat something yummy. So, she went to her mom and said, "Mommy, I am hungry. Can I have some cookies, please?"

Her mom said, "Sure, Lily. But first, let's watch the structure we built yesterday." They went outside and looked at the tall tower they had made with blocks. Lily said, "Wow, Mommy! It's so big and strong!"

After watching the structure, they went back inside and Lily's mom gave her some cookies. Lily was very happy and said, "These cookies are delicious! Thank you, Mommy." And her mom replied, "You're welcome, sweetie. I'm glad you like them."

Lily and Ben love to watch the parade. They see big balloons, loud drums, and funny clowns. They wave and cheer with their mom and dad.

But Lily wants to see more. She sees a big red fire truck at the end of the parade. She likes fire trucks. They are shiny and fast and reliable. They help people when there is a fire.

She tugs on her mom's hand and says, "Mom, can we go closer to the fire truck? Please, please, please?"

Her mom smiles and says, "Okay, Lily, we can go closer. But we have to be careful and stay with dad and Ben. The fire truck is very big and loud. It might scare you."

Lily nods and says, "I'm not scared, mom. I'm brave. Thank you, mom."

They walk to the end of the parade, where the fire truck is parked. Lily sees a friendly fireman sitting on the truck. He waves and says, "Hello, little girl. Do you like the fire truck?"

Lily nods and says, "Yes, I do. It's very pretty and strong. Can I see it closer?"

The fireman smiles and says, "Sure, you can. But you have to ask your mom and dad first. They have to say yes."

Lily looks at her mom and dad and says, "Mom, dad, can I see the fire truck closer? Please, please, please?"

Her mom and dad look at each other and say, "Okay, Lily, you can. But you have to be careful and listen to the fireman. He knows how to keep you safe."

Lily says, "Thank you, mom. Thank you, dad."

The fireman helps Lily climb on the fire truck. He shows her the hose, the ladder, and the siren. He lets her wear his helmet and jacket. He tells her stories about his job and his friends.

Lily is very happy. She thinks the fire truck is the best thing in the parade. She thanks the fireman and gives him a hug. She says, "You are very nice and reliable. You are my hero."

The fireman says, "You are very welcome and brave. You are my friend."

Once upon a time, there was a smart little girl named Lily. She loved going to school and learning new things. Every day, she would skip happily to her classroom and sit in front of the blackboard.

One day, Lily's teacher asked her to come up to the blackboard and write her name. Lily was so excited! She skipped up to the blackboard and wrote her name in big letters.

After that, Lily skipped back to her seat and smiled with pride. She felt very smart and happy that she could write her name all by herself. From that day on, she loved going to school even more and skipping to her classroom every morning. The end.

Once upon a time there was a grumpy bear who lived in a big forest. He loved to play with blocks, but he never shared them with anyone.

One day, the grumpy bear found a magic spinning top. He was so excited that he started to spin it around and around. Round and round it went until it made a big whirling circle.

The bear was so happy he couldnâ€™t help but run around the circle. The spinning top was making the blocks fly upwards and then float gently back down. The grumpy bear smiled and started to play with the blocks as they floated down.

The spinning top made the grumpy bear very happy. He played with the blocks until the sun went down and the night came. The grumpy bear was so happy that he even shared his blocks with his forest friends.

Once upon a time, there was a fish named Tom. Tom was a very helpful fish. Every day he would peek out of the water and look for ways to help other fish.

One day, Tom noticed a small fish swimming around by itself. It looked very scared and alone, so Tom swam to it and asked if it needed help. The little fish nodded its head and thanked Tom for being so kind.

Tom decided to take the little fish with him to show it the best fishing spots in the sea. The little fish was so excited to follow Tom around and learn new things. Together, they swam around and caught lots of yummy fish.

At the end of the day, they hugged goodbye and the little fish thanked Tom for all his help. Tom waved goodbye as the little fish left and felt very happy that he had been so helpful.

Once upon a time, there was a big ladder. Joe was ready to use it to go up to the top of his house. He wanted to paint the house. Joe started to pour the paint onto the ladder. He was so excited to start painting.

Suddenly the ladder started to move. Joe felt scared and held on tight. But the ladder was too slippery. Joe started to fall. He screamed and screamed but no one heard him.

He fell from the ladder and landed on the ground. It really hurt; Joe couldn't get up. His mom and dad ran outside. They were sad to see Joe on the floor. They took him to the hospital.

At the hospital, the doctor said Joe was not ready for a big ladder. Joe had to stay in bed for a long time. Even now, he still gets scared when he sees a ladder.

Tom and Lily are friends. They like to play outside. One day, they see a big kite in the sky. It is red and yellow and has a long tail.

"Wow, look at the kite!" Tom says. "It is so high and fast. I want to fly a kite too."

"Me too," Lily says. "Let's go and find one."

They run to the shed. They see a small kite. It is blue and green and has a star on it. They take the kite and a string. They go to the field.

They try to fly the kite. They run and run. But the kite does not go up. It falls to the ground.

"Why does it not fly?" Tom asks. "The wind is strong. It should fly."

"Maybe the string is too short," Lily says. "Or maybe the kite is too heavy."

They look at the kite. They see a problem. The kite has a hole in it. The wind goes through the hole. The kite does not hang in the air.

"Oh no, the kite is broken," Tom says. "How can we fix it?"

"Maybe we can use a patch," Lily says. "Or some tape. Or some glue."

They look for something to fix the kite. They see a big leaf. It is brown and dry. They think it can cover the hole.

They take the leaf. They put it on the hole. They use some grass to tie it. They hope it will work.

They try to fly the kite again. They run and run. The kite goes up. It hangs in the air. It moves with the wind. It looks like a bird.

"Yay, we did it!" Tom says. "The kite is flying. It is so pretty."

"Yay, we are so smart!" Lily says. "The leaf is a good patch. It is like a wing."

They laugh and clap. They watch the kite. They are happy.

But then, something bad happens. The wind gets stronger. It blows harder. It pulls the kite. The string breaks. The kite flies away.

"Uh oh, the kite is gone," Tom says. "The wind took it. We can't get it back."

"Uh oh, that is sad," Lily says. "The kite was ours. We liked it."

They are scared. They cry. They hug each other.

They see a man. He is walking in the field. He has a hat and a coat. He sees the kite. He catches it. He brings it to them.

"Hello, kids," he says. "Is this your kite? I saw it flying in the sky. It is a nice kite. But it has a hole in it. And a leaf on it. Did you do that?"

"Yes, sir," Tom says. "The kite was broken. We tried to fix it. But the wind was too strong. It broke the string. It flew away."

"Yes, sir," Lily says. "We were scared. We thought we lost it. We were sad. Thank you for finding it."

"You're welcome, kids," he says. "You are very clever. You used a leaf to patch the hole. That is a good idea. But you need a stronger string. And a smaller hole. Do you want me to help you?"

"Yes, please," Tom and Lily say. "We want to fly the kite again. We want to have fun."

"Okay, then," he says. "Let's go to my house. I have some tools and materials. We can fix the kite together. And then we can fly it again. How does that sound?"

"Good, good," Tom and Lily say. "Thank you, thank you."

They go with the man. They fix the kite. They fly it again. They are happy. The end.

Lily and Ben were playing pirates in the backyard. They had a big cardboard box that they pretended was a ship. They wore hats and eye patches and had wooden swords. They also had a hook that they took from the kitchen.

"Arrr, matey, I'm the captain of this ship!" Ben said, holding the hook in his hand.

"No, I'm the captain, you're the first mate!" Lily said, pointing her sword at him.

They started to argue and shout, but then they heard a loud roar from behind the fence. They stopped and looked at each other, scared.

"What was that?" Ben whispered.

"I don't know, maybe a lion or a bear!" Lily whispered back.

They grabbed their swords and hook and tiptoed to the fence. They peeked over and saw a big, colorful dragon. It had scales of red, green, blue and yellow. It had horns, wings and a long tail. It was breathing fire and smoke.

"Wow, look at that!" Ben said, amazed.

"It's so pretty!" Lily said, smiling.

The dragon saw them and roared again, but this time it sounded friendly. It wagged its tail and flapped its wings.

"Hello, little pirates!" the dragon said. "Do you want to play with me?"

Lily and Ben nodded, excited. They climbed over the fence and ran to the dragon. They touched its scales and rode on its back. They had fun with the dragon and forgot about their pirate game.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a silly queen. She lived in a big castle with lots of people around her. Every day, she had to move around the castle and she loved it!

One day, she decided to move outside the castle walls. She walked and walked until she reached a special garden. There, she saw many beautiful flowers and strange animals. Everything was so amazing!

The queen kept moving, and soon she reached a big lake. She sat by the lake and watched the birds fly around. It was so peaceful and quiet.

Suddenly the queen heard a noise. She looked up and saw a squirrel running right in front of her. It was so silly! The queen laughed and laughed until her stomach ached. Then she stood up and moved back to the castle. She knew she would remember this day forever.

John was playing hide and seek with his mom. He closed his eyes and counted to three. When he opened them, he saw his mom standing behind a soft curtain. He smiled and ran to find his own hiding spot. John looked around the room and noticed a soft curtain. He snuck behind it so his mom couldn't see him. As the curtain was so soft, John felt so cosy. He stayed very quiet, but then he heard his mom calling him. He giggled and ran out to give her a big surprise. His mom was so happy to see him and they both hugged!

Lily and Ben are twins. They like to play in the living room. There is a big armchair in the living room. It is soft and cozy. Lily and Ben both want to sit on the armchair.

"Me first!" Lily says. She runs to the armchair and jumps on it.

"No, me first!" Ben says. He runs after Lily and tries to push her off.

"Stop it!" Lily says. She holds on to the armchair.

"Move!" Ben says. He pulls Lily's hair.

"Ow!" Lily says. She kicks Ben's leg.

They make a lot of noise. They yell and cry and fight. They do not share the armchair.

Mom hears the noise. She comes to the living room. She sees Lily and Ben on the armchair. She is not happy.

"What are you doing?" Mom asks. She looks at Lily and Ben.

They stop fighting. They look at Mom. They are quiet.

"We want to sit on the armchair," Lily says.

"But there is only one armchair," Mom says.

Lily and Ben look at the armchair. They look at each other. They have to decide.

"Can we take turns?" Lily asks.

"OK," Ben says.

They nod. They smile. They hug.

Mom smiles too. She is happy.

"Good job," Mom says. She claps her hands.

Lily and Ben take turns. They sit on the armchair. They read a book. They sing a song. They are not noisy. They are nice. They share the armchair.

Once upon a time, there was a big, big, enormous circle. It was round and yellow like the sun. The circle was all alone and wanted friends to join in. 

One day, a little bird saw the enormous circle and flew over to join in. The bird hopped around the circle and sang a happy song. 

Soon, more friends came to join in. A friendly cat, a happy dog, and even a bouncy bunny. They all played together in the enormous circle, running around and having fun. 

The circle was no longer alone and was very happy to have so many friends to play with. They all agreed to come back and join in the fun every day. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a smelly old tree. By the tree, there was a big hole. In the hole, there was a shiny coin. A boy named Tim saw the coin and wanted it.

Tim said to his friend, "I want that coin, but the tree is smelly and rot." His friend said, "Be brave, Tim! You can get the coin." So, Tim went to the smelly tree and tried to get the coin from the hole.

As Tim got closer to the hole, he saw a little mouse. The mouse said, "I will help you get the coin, but you must help me too." Tim agreed, and they got the coin together. Tim was happy, and the mouse was happy too. And they both learned that even in smelly places, good things can happen.

Sara and Tom are twins. They like to visit their grandpa. He is a great man. He has a big house with a garden. He tells them stories and plays with them.

One day, they go to visit grandpa with their mom. They knock on the door. Grandpa opens it and smiles. He hugs them and says, "Hello, my little ones. I'm so happy to see you. Come in, come in."

They go inside and see a big cake on the table. It has candles and frosting. Grandpa says, "It's my birthday today. I made a cake for us. Do you want some?"

Sara and Tom clap their hands and say, "Yes, please. Happy birthday, grandpa. We love you."

They sit down and eat the cake. It is yummy. They sing a song for grandpa. He blows out the candles and makes a wish. He says, "My wish is to have more days like this. You are the best gift I ever had."

Sara and Tom hug him and say, "You are the best grandpa ever. We are glad you are our grandpa."

They spend the afternoon playing and talking. They have a lot of fun. They are happy to visit their grandpa. He is a great man.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She went to the shop with her mommy. They walked and walked until they found a big shop with lots of toys.

Lily noticed a white teddy bear on the shelf. It was so fluffy and cute! She wanted it so much. But her mommy said she could only get one toy.

Lily thought and thought until she saw a pretty pink doll. It was just as nice as the teddy bear. She decided to get the doll instead. She was happy and hugged her new toy all the way home.

One day, Mary was walking down the hall. She saw a door and knocked on it.

A tall lady opened the door and asked, "Can I help you, Mary?"

Mary answered, "Yes, please. I'm looking for my toy."

The lady smiled and said, "You have to be careful. Follow me and try not to get lost."

The lady led Mary down the hall until they reached a room full of toys. Mary saw her toy and picked it up. She thanked the lady and waved goodbye.

Mary walked back down the hall carefully, clutching her toy. She smiled as she remembered the friendly lady who had helped her.

Once upon a time, there was a dog named Max. Max loved to play outside and run around. One day, Max saw a big, dirty puddle. He ran towards it and jumped in, getting all dirty. 

Max's owner, Sarah, saw him and said, "Max, stand still!" Max stopped moving and stood there. Sarah got a hose and sprayed water on Max to clean him up. 

After Max was clean, Sarah said, "Let's go inside and take a break." They went inside and Sarah paused the TV so they could have a snack. Max was happy and wagged his tail. The end.

There were two children named Sammy and Sarah. They loved to play together. 

One day, Sammy said to Sarah, "Let's pretend to be dancers!" Sarah was so excited. 

They both grabbed their staffs, which were like sticks. Sammy put on some soft music as Sarah got ready to dance. 

Sarah was very graceful. She moved her staff around elegantly, swirling and twirling in the air. Sammy copied Sarah, trying to be graceful like her. 

They both laughed and smiled as they pretended to be dancers. They had so much fun together!

Once upon a time, a family went searching in the deep forest. The trees were tall and the sky was blue. Suddenly, they found a delicate sheet lying on the ground. The sheet was made from a very soft material.

The family did not know what to do with the sheet. So, they decided to take it with them and search for something else. They searched for some time but did not find anything else. Finally, they took the sheet home with them.

When they got home, the family laid out the sheet in the middle of the room. All of a sudden, the sheet started to move. Something was inside it! Slowly, the sheet opened and out came a tiny dragon. 

The family was shocked! It seemed like the delicate sheet was the perfect hiding place for the dragon. It had been sleeping inside the sheet warm and safe. The family was so happy to give the dragon a home. 

They all lived happily ever after!

Once upon a time, there was a small bald panda. He lived in the forest with his friends and they would play together in the sunshine.

One day, the bald panda went out to find some food. He looked and looked, but he couldn't find anything. He was so hungry!

As he looked, he got more and more lost. He went deeper and deeper into the forest and soon he couldn't remember how to get home.

The bald panda was feeling sad. He wanted to be home with his friends again. But he just couldn't find a way out.

Then, suddenly, he saw a big tree. He climbed up and looked around. There, in the distance, he could see his home!

He was so happy that he didn't lose the way home. Now he could have some dinner with his friends!

Once upon a time, there was a white duck named Lily. Lily lived near a pond. She liked to swim and play with her friends in the water.

One day, Lily saw a big white frog named Fred. He was sitting by the pond. Lily said, "Hi, Fred! Do you want to swim with me?" Fred said, "Yes, Lily! I like to swim too!"

As they went to the pond, Lily slipped on a wet rock. "Oh no!" she cried. Fred helped her up and said, "Be careful, Lily. The rocks are slippery." Then, they swam and played in the pond. They had a fun day together.

Once upon a time there was a modest thing. It was small, but it was always getting bigger.

The thing started by being small and very quiet. But it always wanted more. So one day it decided to start getting bigger.

First it started to get higher. Then it started to get wider. Soon, it was as tall and wide as a big tree.

Next, it started to get stronger. It started to shine brightly and look more important. Finally, it started to make noise. Suddenly it was loud and happy.

The thing had started as small and modest. But now it was huge and strong.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a clock in her room that tick-tocked all day long. One night, Lily couldn't sleep because the clock was too loud and uncomfortable. She wondered why the clock had to make so much noise. 

The next morning, Lily asked her mom if they could move the clock to a different room. Her mom said yes and they moved the clock to the living room. Lily felt much better and could sleep peacefully again. She wondered why she didn't think of moving the clock sooner. 

From that day on, Lily learned that sometimes things can be uncomfortable, but there's always a solution. She was happy that she could sleep well again and wondered what other problems she could solve.

Ben and Lily were brother and sister. They liked to play in the backyard with their toys. But they did not like to share. They always fought over who got the best toy.

One day, Ben found a big red truck in the backyard. He wanted to play with it. He grabbed it and ran away from Lily. Lily saw him and got mad. She wanted the truck too. She ran after him and shouted.

"Give me the truck, Ben! It is my turn!" Lily said.

"No, it is mine! I found it first!" Ben said.

They both pulled the truck hard. They were stubborn. They did not listen to each other. They did not see the big hole in the backyard. They fell into the hole with the truck. They got hurt and dirty. They cried and screamed.

Mom and Dad heard them and came to the backyard. They saw Ben and Lily in the hole with the truck. They were angry and sad. They helped them out of the hole and took them inside. They cleaned their wounds and clothes. They took away the truck and put it in the closet. They said Ben and Lily could not play with it anymore. They said they had to learn to share and be nice.

Ben and Lily hated the hole. They hated the truck. They hated each other. They had a bad day. They wished they had shared and been nice.

Once upon a time there was a silly stone. It liked to roll around and explore. It had lots of fun zig-zagging across the ground.

One day, it met a special friend who wanted to own it. The little stone said it wouldn't go too far away, so the friend agreed and put it in her pocket.

The partner went about their day, playing, fishing and running around in circles. Whenever they needed cheering up, they'd take the silly stone out of the pocket and give it a cuddle. The stone felt lucky to be cared for by such a great friend.

They were always together, until the time came when it was time to say goodbye. The stone's friend knew they couldn't take it with them and so they said one last farewell, promising to keep it in their heart.

And so, the silly stone stayed there, rolling around, thinking of the kind friend who once owned it.

There was once a tall robot. It had a belt around its middle. Every day, the robot went for a walk. But, one day, the robot had an idea. It decided to reverse its belt! The robot put the belt on the wrong way around. It was so excited to try out its new look.

The next day, the robot went for a walk again. It seemed to take much longer than before, because it was walking backwards! People passing by laughed and pointed at the tall robot's new look.

The robot liked going for walks backwards. But one day, the belt became too tight. The robot decided to reverse the belt back to its original position, because it felt much better with the belt the right way around.

From then on, the robot always made sure to wear the belt the right way around. It was much more comfortable that way - but every now and then, the robot still had fun going for walks backwards!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He loved playing soccer and would always kick the ball around in his backyard. One day, Timmy's dad took him to a big stadium to watch a soccer game. Timmy was so excited to see all the players and hear the crowd cheering.

As they were walking to their seats, Timmy's dad said, "Be careful not to run too fast or you might trip and fall." Timmy listened and walked slowly to his seat. 

During the game, Timmy saw one player who was very good. He scored many goals and the crowd cheered loudly for him. Timmy thought, "I want to be like him when I grow up." 

After the game, as they were leaving the stadium, Timmy's dad said, "Remember, it's important to be humble even if you're really good at something." Timmy nodded and said, "I will remember." He also remembered to stop and look both ways before crossing the street.

Bobbie watched her body as it splashed into the water. As she swam, she saw a big rock. She climbed it and looked around. Suddenly she spotted a large creature. Bobbie was scared, but she was curious. She watched as it swam towards her. Bobbie's Grandpa had told her that if you stay still and are reliable, animals will usually leave you alone. Bobbie stays still and watched the creature. Just then the creature stopped and went away. Bobbie was relieved. She got off the rock and was careful as she swam back. She was happy to be back on shore and hugged her reliable Grandpa. He was so proud that Bobbie was brave and watched her body.

John was a little boy. He loved to go outside to play with the birds and trees. One day, he went out to the park. The sun was shining and the trees were blowing in the wind. 

John felt so powerful. He felt like he could fly. He started to run and jump around and feel graceful like a bird. 

Suddenly, John fell to the ground. He cried out for help. A man came running to help him. 

The man spoke, â€œYou were being too brave and over confident. You cannot use your power like that.â€ 

John felt sad. He learned a lesson he would never forget. He knew he had to be more careful. 

John never went outside to play again. He was too scared to feel the powerful, graceful energy again.

Once upon a time, there was a young girl named Lucy. She had a big stack of books in her bedroom. Every day, she and her mom would promise each other to read some of them.

One morning, Lucy and her mom woke up to find a very mild sun outside. It made Lucy feel happy and excited. She asked her mom if they could start reading one of the books in their stack.

Her mom said that she had to do some chores first, but promised Lucy that then they would read one. Lucy was happy with this.

So she went outside to play and after she was done with her chores, she went back to her room. Her mom was already there and they started reading one of the books in the stack.

Together they read the entire story and Lucy was so excited that she wanted to read the next one. Her mom promised they would read the next story, too. Lucy was so content and couldn't wait to start reading again.

Ben likes to learn new things. He has a tutor who comes to his house and teaches him letters and numbers. His tutor is nice and patient. She gives him stickers and candy when he does well.

One day, Ben's tutor brings a big box of crayons. She says they will draw pictures with them. Ben is happy. He loves to draw. He picks a blue crayon and starts to draw a sky. He fills the whole paper with blue.

"Good job, Ben!" his tutor says. "Now, can you draw something else on the sky? Maybe a sun, or a bird, or a cloud?"

Ben thinks for a moment. He wants to draw a cloud. He looks for a white crayon. But he can't find one. All the crayons are bright colors. There is no white.

Ben feels sad. He likes white. He wants to draw a cloud. He looks at his tutor. She is busy with her phone. She does not see him.

Ben has an idea. He sees a white pillow on the couch. He takes the pillow and rips it open. White feathers fly out of the pillow. Ben grabs a handful of feathers and sticks them on his paper. He fills the sky with white feathers. He smiles. He has a cloud.

"Ben, what are you doing?" his tutor says. She looks up from her phone and sees the mess. She sees the feathers on the paper and on the floor. She sees the ripped pillow. She is angry. She is grumpy.

"Ben, you made a big mess! You ruined the pillow! You wasted the feathers! You can't do that!" she scolds him.

Ben feels scared. He does not like to be yelled at. He does not understand why his tutor is grumpy. He just wanted to draw a cloud. He starts to cry.

"I'm sorry, I'm sorry, I'm sorry!" he says. He hugs his paper. He likes his cloud. He thinks it is pretty. He wishes his tutor would like it too.

Lila and Ben are friends. They like to play at the beach. They see big waves and surf boards. They want to try to surf.

"Can we surf, please?" Lila asks her mom.

"Surfing is hard, Lila. You need to be careful and listen to the teacher," her mom says.

"OK, mom. We will be good," Lila says.

Lila and Ben follow the teacher to the water. He gives them small surf boards and shows them how to stand on them. He tells them to wait for the right wave and push with their feet.

Lila and Ben try to surf. They fall off many times, but they laugh and try again. They have fun.

Suddenly, they see something furry in the water. It is a seal. The seal swims near them and makes a noise.

"Hello, seal!" Lila says.

"Hello, kids!" the seal says.

Lila and Ben are surprised. They did not know seals can talk.

"Can you surf, seal?" Ben asks.

"Sure, I can surf. Watch me!" the seal says.

The seal jumps on a big wave and rides it with his flippers. He looks happy.

Lila and Ben clap and cheer. They think the seal is amazing.

"Wow, you are a great surfer, seal!" Lila says.

"Thank you, Lila. You and Ben are good surfers too. Do you want to surf with me?" the seal asks.

"Yes, please!" Lila and Ben say.

The seal helps them catch a big wave and surf with him. They feel the wind and the spray. They smile and shout.

Lila and Ben have the best day ever. They make a new furry friend. They love to surf.

Once upon a time, there was a blue bird who was very intelligent. He lived in a tree and loved to sing songs. One day, he decided to visit his friend, a little mouse who lived in a hole in the ground.

"Hello, little mouse!" said the blue bird. "I came to visit you today."

"Welcome, blue bird!" replied the little mouse. "I'm so happy to see you."

They chatted and played together, but suddenly a big cat appeared. The cat wanted to eat the little mouse.

"Run, little mouse, run!" shouted the blue bird.

The little mouse tried to run, but the cat was too fast. Sadly, the blue bird had to watch as his friend was eaten by the cat. From that day on, the blue bird never visited anyone again.

Lila and her mom were in the car. They wanted to go to the zoo. Lila loved the zoo. She wanted to see the wild animals. She hoped to see the lions and the monkeys and the giraffes.

But the car was not moving. There were many cars in front of them and behind them. They were stuck in traffic. Lila was sad. She looked out the window and saw the red lights and the honking horns.

"Mom, why are we not moving?" she asked.

"Because there is too much traffic, honey. Sometimes there are too many cars on the road and they make a big jam. We have to wait until the jam clears," mom said.

"How long do we have to wait?" Lila asked.

"I don't know, honey. Maybe a few minutes, maybe a long time. It depends on how fast the cars can move," mom said.

Lila sighed. She did not like waiting. She wanted to go to the zoo. She hoped the traffic would go away soon. She hoped the zoo would not close before they got there. She hoped the wild animals would not be too tired or too hungry to play with her. She hoped they would have fun at the zoo. She hoped, she hoped, she hoped.

One day, the little girl was feeling very miserable. She walked outside and noticed that the wind had taken her towel! She began to look around, but she couldn't find it. She was starting to become more and more sad.

Then, suddenly, she heard something. She looked around and saw a small bird holding her towel! It had flown away with it when the wind blew it away.

The little girl was so happy! She thanked the bird and it flew away. She took the towel and returned to her house, feeling much better.

When she got to her house, her mom hugged her and gave her a big kiss. The little girl was so happy to have her towel back again. She learned that day that when something is lost, it can sometimes return.

Once there was a little girl called Daisy. She was three years old. Daisy was playing in her garden when she saw something sparkly in the dirt. She carefully pulled it out and noticed it was a beautiful medal. Daisy held it up to the sun and saw it was broken in two pieces.

But she wasn't sad. Daisy smiled, because she saw a tiny flower growing up through the dirt near the medal. It was already starting to bloom. Daisy smiled even wider when she realized the flower was growing right between the broken pieces of the medal.

Daisy knew she had to show her Mom and Dad the special flower with the medal inside. She carefully pulled the flower up, medal and all, and carefully put it in a cup with some water.

Daisy loved her little flower with the broken medal. It would bloom even more when the sun shone and that made Daisy happy.

Once upon a time, there was a bunny named Benny. Benny was a happy bunny who loved to play in the spring. One day, Benny found some carrots and wanted to eat them. But he needed to add some salt to make them taste good. 

Benny hopped around looking for some salt, but he couldn't find any. He asked his friend, a bird, if he knew where to find salt. The bird told Benny that he could find some at the farmer's house. 

So, Benny hopped over to the farmer's house and found some salt. He added it to his carrots and they tasted so yummy! Benny was so happy that he could enjoy his snack in the beautiful spring weather. The end.

Once upon a time there was an old man who loved to sing. Every day he went out to a big pool to sing and the animals in the area always gathered to listen.

One day, a little 3-year-old girl was nearby. When the old man began to sing, the girl was so charmed that she started to clap her hands and smiled.

The old man, who saw this, stopped singing and said, "Little one, why don't you come join me and sing along?" 

The little girl was so excited and hesitantly, she started singing. "Row, row, row your boat, gently down the stream..."

The old man was delighted and took the little girl by the hand and they both sang together. All the animals in the area gathered around and sang too. 

When the song was finished, the girl thanked the old man very much, and they promised to see each other again the next day. From that day onward, the little girl and the old man sang together every day at the pool.

Once upon a time there was a smart little navy dog. His name was Count and he loved to play.

One day Count saw three little ducks by the river. He wanted to play with them so he yapped and barked at them. 

The three ducks quacked back at him. "What do you want?" they said.

Count wagged his tail and said, "Let's play!" 

The ducks thought this was a good idea and they agreed. So they swam around and around and Count danced around them barking and having a lot of fun. 

When it was time to go, the three little ducks said goodbye to Count and waved at him. Count waved back and the ducks flew away. 

Count was happy and ran home to tell his friends about his fun day.

Bob was a 3-year-old boy who loved to play. He ran around the park and looked for many things to do. One day, he spotted something that he had never seen before. It was a luxury car! He noticed the car's shiny exterior, big wheels, and comfortable looking seats. 

Bob was eager to try it out and see what the car was like. He excitedly opened the door and sat in the driver's seat. He loved the soft feeling of the leather and the smoothness of the steering wheel. Bob heard someone coming, so he quickly put the car into drive and started to move it forward. 

The car's owner, an angry-looking man, ran towards them and shouted out, "Hey! What do you think you're doing?! That's my car! Get out of it right now!"
