Mom smiled and put down her book. She came to the kitchen and saw the sauce bottle. She took it and opened it easily.

"Here you go," she said. "Be careful, the sauce is spicy. Do you want some water too?"

Lily and Tom thanked Mom and poured some sauce on their cheese and bread. They put them in the toaster and waited. Soon, they smelled something delicious.

"Yay, cheese toasties are ready!" Lily said. She and Tom took them out and cut them in half. They blew on them to cool them down and took a bite.

"Mmm, so good!" Tom said. He liked the cheese and the sauce. They were warm and gooey.

Lily agreed. She liked them too. They were crunchy and tasty. She and Tom ate their cheese toasties and drank some water. They were happy and full.

One day, a little bird named Tim wanted to rise high in the sky. He wanted to see how high he could go. So, he flapped his wings and began to rise up, up, up.

As Tim rose higher, he met a big, comfortable cloud named Fluffy. Fluffy was soft and white. "Hello, little bird," Fluffy said. "Do you want to rest on me?" Tim was tired, so he said, "Yes, thank you!" Tim landed on Fluffy and felt very comfortable.

After resting, Tim was ready to rise again. He said goodbye to Fluffy and flew higher in the sky. Tim was so happy to rise and see the world below him. And he knew that whenever he needed a rest, his friend Fluffy would be there to help him.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy who played tag. He ran and ran, but he never seemed to be able to catch his friends. He felt sad, so he sat down on the ground and began to cry.

Suddenly, a ship appeared in the sky. It was long and magical and it shined brightly in the sky. The boy jumped up and ran to it. He wanted to touch it and ride it all around the world.

But when the boy kicked the ship with his foot, it flew away and disappeared. He was so sad and disappointed.

The boy learned a valuable lesson that day. He learned that if he wants something to last, he must be gentle and kind with it. He must treat it with care, instead of kicking it away.

Once, there was a little girl called Ruby. She was three years old and was always so curious and full of energy! She was very generous, and always wanted to help everyone.

One day, she went out to play in the park. She was wearing her favourite red coat, but it wasn't very warm and she was starting to feel cold. Then she saw a gentleman walking towards her. He smiled, and said "Hello. I'm feeling very generous today - would you like my coat?"

Feeling a bit shy, she nodded and he helped her put it on. It was so warm and cosy!

Ruby tried out the coat for the whole day, running around and playing with her friends. She wanted to say thank you to the kind gentleman, but he had gone. So, she decided to use her generous spirit and try to find him. She kept looking around the park until finally, there he was!

Ruby was so happy that she helped find him so that she could say thank you. He thanked her back and they both smiled. Ruby was thankful for his generous act and knew that she'd always remember this special moment.

Once upon a time, there was an eraser that wanted to bake something delicious. It asked all of its friends if they wanted to help make something. Everyone said yes and they all hopped in a big oven. 

The eraser put everything in the oven and started to bake. After a while, the oven was hot and smelt so yummy. Everyone was so excited. Then the oven door opened and out jumped the eraser, but it was all black and dead. 

All of the eraser's friends were sad, but then one of the friends had an idea. The friend took a big drink of water and splashed it on the eraser. The eraser started to come back to life and everyone laughed and cheered. 

The eraser was saved and everyone enjoyed their delicious treats!

Once upon a time there was a very serious mailman. Every day he spread mail around to all the people in the town. One special day, the mailman took out a really special envelope. He spread it through the town and soon everyone had the special mail. 

When everyone opened the mail they were so amazed! It was a big party invitation. The town was so excited they were going to have a surprise party. 

Everyone was so busy getting ready for the party. They made decorations, cooked food and spread the news to everyone in the town. 

When the day of the party arrived, the whole town was there! It was the best party ever! They ate cake, listened to music and danced all night. Everyone had the best time and was happy the mailman spread the special mail!

Mama was walking through the park when she heard a loud scream. She looked up into the sky and saw a beautiful, green parrot. It was flying in circles and screeching so loudly, it made Mama's ears hurt.

Mama decided to try and catch the parrot. She reached up with her hands and tried to grab it, but it flew away each time. Finally, Mama decided to try something else. She grabbed some peanuts from her bag and threw them on the ground. Then, she stood back and watched.

Sure enough, the parrot flew down and started picking up the peanuts. Mama crept closer and closer, until, with one swoop of her hand, she had captured the parrot!

Mama laughed and hugged the parrot tightly, making sure it was warm. She took it home and put it in her bedroom. From that day forward, Mama and the parrot were best friends. They did everything together. Mama even took the parrot with her when she went for ice cream!

One day, a little girl named Lucy was playing in her backyard. She was having lots of fun in the dirt. Lucy saw a bug, so she bent down and picked up some soil. She threw it in the air and then she kicked it. It flew really high! She laughed and laughed.

The noise was very loud, and her mom came to the door to see what was going on. She saw Lucy kicking the soil and said, "No, Lucy! Don't kick the soil!" 

Lucy stopped. She looked at the soil and then at her mom. She said "OK" and put the soil back on the ground. She promised her mom that she would not kick it again.

Then, she started playing with some toys. She was having lots of fun! Lucy forgot all about the soil, but she always remembered to be careful with it - and not to kick it again.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She had a pretty dress that she loved to wear. One day, while she was playing outside, she heard a loud snap. She looked around and saw that a branch had snapped off a tree. 

Lily picked up the branch and started to play with it. She pretended it was a wand and she was a fairy princess. But then, she accidentally snapped the branch in two. She felt sad because she had broken it. 

Later that day, Lily's mom made her a rare treat for dessert. It was a chocolate cake with sprinkles on top. Lily was so happy and excited to eat it. She felt like a princess in her pretty dress, eating her special treat. She knew she had to be careful not to snap the fork while eating her cake.

One cold winter day, Tilly was outside helping in the garden. She grabbed a rake and started cleaning up the leaves on the ground. She held the rake in front of her and carefully balanced the leaves. The ground was icy so Tilly took some small steps to steady herself.

Tilly carefully moved the rake back and forth against the ground, pushing the leaves into a pile. She smiled as the pile grew bigger. She even found some shiny objects under the leaves.

When she was finished, Tilly stood back and admired her work. The ground was so clean and tidy. Tilly was so proud of herself. She gave herself a big hug to celebrate. 

Tilly grabbed her rake, feeling warm and happy inside. She had done an amazing job with the rake and was super proud of herself.

Once upon a time, there lived a girl called Ellie. Ellie was only three years old and loved to play with her friends all day. 

One day, Ellie wanted to make her dolls' house even better. She asked her mom, "Mom can I make my dolls' house lovely?" Her mom nodded and said, "Yes, you can. If you work hard, you will improve it."

So Ellie worked hard. She added windows to the house and made a tiny garden. After an hour of hard work, the dolls' house was finished. It looked even better than before.

Ellie smiled and said to her mom, "Mom, look! I improved the dolls' house. Don't you think it's lovely?" Ellie's mom laughed and said, "Indeed it is! You worked really hard and you've done a great job." 

Ellie was so happy. She got a hug from her mom and thanked her for her help. 

From that day forward, Ellie knew that if she worked hard she could achieve anything.

Ben and Mia are friends. They like to play in the park. They have a watch. The watch can tell time. The watch is reliable. It always works.

One day, they want to go on the slide. But there is a line. Many kids are waiting. Ben and Mia look at the watch. They have to go home soon. They are sad.

"Can we use the watch to skip the line?" Ben asks Mia.

"How?" Mia says.

"Maybe we can tell the other kids that the watch is magic. And it can make them fly. And we can trade the watch for a turn on the slide." Ben says.

Mia thinks. She likes the watch. She does not want to lose it. But she also wants to go on the slide. She nods.

"OK. Let's try." Mia says.

They go to the front of the line. They show the watch to the other kids. They say it is magic. They say it can make them fly. They ask if anyone wants to trade.

Some kids laugh. They do not believe them. They say the watch is not magic. They say it is just a watch. They say no.

But one kid is curious. He has never seen a watch like that. He wants to try. He says yes.

Ben and Mia give him the watch. He gives them his turn on the slide. They are happy. They run to the slide. They slide down. They have fun.

The kid looks at the watch. He tries to make it fly. He shakes it. He presses it. He talks to it. Nothing happens. He is confused. He is angry. He wants his turn back.

He runs after Ben and Mia. He yells at them. He says they lied. He says the watch is not magic. He says he wants his turn back.

But Ben and Mia are gone. They have left the park. They have gone home. They have taken another watch. The watch is not theirs. The watch is their mom's. They have borrowed it. They have not asked. They are in trouble.

Once upon a time there was a small bear named Stewy. Stewy was an incredible bear with twinkly eyes and soft, furry ears. One day, Stewy decided to go to the bakery next door to buy some cookies. But before he could even leave the house, he heard a voice saying: "Wait, Stewy! You need to be weighed before you go!". Stewy looked up and he saw his mom standing near the scales.

Stewy nervously stepped onto the scales and he asked his mom: "Why do I need to be weighed?". His mom smiled and said: "Because I want to make sure you have the energy to get all the way to the bakery and buy the cookies you want!".

Stewy stepped off the scales, looking very relieved. His mom smiled and said: "You've done an incredible job, Stewy! You've gained some weight, so you'll have enough energy to get to the bakery!" Then she hugged him and said: "Now go and have fun!" 

Stewy was so excited, he put on his fluffy hat, grabbed his basket and off he went to the bakery with his twinkly eyes and soft, furry ears!

Once there was a little girl called Lucy. She was only three years old and very excited. She went to her bedroom to sort her toys. She found all kinds of fun things, including a pink poem. Lucy was so happy to have this poem and read it out loud.

"This poem has the power to make me happy!" she exclaimed.

But suddenly, a large monster came in and snatched the poem away from her. He wouldn't give it back and roared in a very deep voice.

"Give it back!" shouted Lucy.

But the monster refused and ran away with the poem. Lucy was devastated and started crying. There was nothing else she could do. She had lost her pink poem and would never have it again.

Once upon a time there was a nice red couch. On the couch sat a boy. His nose started to tickle and he had to sneeze! He put his hand to his face and said, "Ah-choo!" All around him, everyone laughed. It was fun to sneeze!

The boy liked the red couch. He liked to sit on it and look around the room. He noticed a plush toy on the couch and picked it up. He hugged it and grinned. Then, he sneezed again! "Ah-choo!" He laughed and put the toy down.

The boy kept looking around the room. Everything was so nice and colourful. Then, he sneezed one more time, saying, "Ah-choo!" He looked around and laughed again. It was funny to sneeze! He loved his red couch and the funny feeling that came with it when he sneezed.

Sara and Ben were twins who liked to play in the old house near their home. The old house had many rooms with old things and cobwebs. Cobwebs were like thin strings that spiders made. Sara and Ben thought they were fun to touch and look at.

One day, they found a big chest in a dark room. They opened it and saw many shiny things inside. They were jewels and coins and rings. Sara and Ben wanted to take some of them and keep them for themselves.

"Look, Ben, these are so pretty and rare! Let's take some and hide them in our pockets!" Sara said.

"No, Sara, we should not do that. These are not ours. They belong to someone else. Maybe they are very important to them. We should leave them alone." Ben said.

"But, Ben, no one lives here. No one will know. We can gain a lot of things from this chest. We can buy toys and candy and books. Don't you want that?" Sara said.

Ben shook his head. He did not want to take things that were not his. He knew that was wrong. He tried to make Sara understand.

"Sara, think about how you would feel if someone took your things. Would you be happy or sad? Would you like them or not? Taking things that are not yours is not nice. It is not fair. It is not good. We should be honest and kind. That is how we gain friends and respect. Not by taking things that are not ours." Ben said.

Sara thought about what Ben said. She remembered how she felt when someone took her favorite doll. She felt sad and angry. She did not like that person. She realized that Ben was right. Taking things that were not hers was not nice. It was not fair. It was not good. She did not want to do that.

"Ben, you are right. I am sorry. I do not want to take these things. I want to be honest and kind. I want to gain friends and respect. Not by taking things that are not mine." Sara said.

Sara and Ben hugged each other. They closed the chest and left the room. They decided to play with the cobwebs instead. They had fun and felt good. They learned that being honest and kind is better than being greedy and selfish. That is the moral of the story.

Sam was a boy who liked to play with his toys. He had a lot of cars, trucks, and trains that he could make noises with. He also had a teddy bear that he hugged when he was sad or sleepy.

One day, his mom came into his room with a big smile. She said, "Sam, I have some news for you. You are going to have a baby sister soon. Isn't that exciting?"

Sam did not think it was exciting. He thought it was bad. He did not want a baby sister. He wanted to be the only child. He thought a baby sister would cry a lot, take his toys, and make his mom and dad busy. He said, "No, I don't want a baby sister. Go away!"

His mom looked sad. She said, "Sam, don't be angry. A baby sister is a gift. You will love her and she will love you. You will have a lot of fun together. You will be a big brother and help her learn and grow."

Sam did not listen. He turned away and buried his face in his teddy bear. He started to weep. He wept so loud that his dad heard him and came into his room. He asked, "What's wrong, Sam? Why are you weeping?"

Sam said, "Mom told me I will have a baby sister. I don't want a baby sister. I want to be alone. I want everything to be ordinary."

His dad hugged him and said, "Sam, I understand how you feel. I felt the same way when I was a boy and my mom told me I would have a baby brother. I was scared and angry. But you know what? When my baby brother was born, I changed my mind. I saw how cute and sweet he was. I liked to hold him and play with him. He became my best friend. I was glad I had a baby brother."

Sam looked at his dad and said, "Really? You were glad?"

His dad nodded and said, "Really. And I think you will be glad too, when you see your baby sister. She will be cute and sweet too. She will look up to you and follow you. She will laugh at your jokes and share your toys. She will be your best friend too. Trust me, Sam. Having a baby sister is not bad. It's good."

Sam thought about what his dad said. He felt a little better. He said, "Maybe you are right, dad. Maybe having a baby sister is good. But can I still hug my teddy bear?"

His dad smiled and said, "Of course, Sam. You can hug your teddy bear as much as you want. And you can hug your baby sister too, when she comes. She will love your teddy bear too."

Sam smiled and said, "OK, dad. I will hug my baby sister too. And I will be a good big brother. But can you tell mom to not smile so big? It makes me nervous."

His dad laughed and said, "OK, Sam. I will tell mom to not smile so big. But she is very happy, Sam. And so am I. And so will you be, soon. You will see."

Sam nodded and said, "OK, dad. I will see. I will try to be happy too. But can you stay with me for a while?"

His dad said, "Sure, Sam. I will stay with you for a while. We can play with your toys and talk about your baby sister. How about that?"

Sam said, "That sounds good, dad. That sounds very good."

Tom and Anna liked to pretend they were wealthy scientists. They had a lab in the basement, where they mixed water and food coloring in bottles. They wore white coats and glasses and talked in big words.

One day, Tom found a shiny coin on the street. He was very happy and ran to show Anna. "Look, Anna, I found money! Now we can buy more things for our lab!" he said.

Anna was jealous. She wanted the coin for herself. She thought of a plan. "That's great, Tom! But you know what? I heard there is a treasure in the park. Maybe we can find more money there. Let's go and see!" she said.

Tom agreed. He put the coin in his pocket and followed Anna. They walked to the park, where Anna pointed to a big hole. "There it is, Tom! The treasure is in there! You go first and I'll wait here," she said.

Tom was excited. He climbed into the hole, hoping to find more coins. But as soon as he was inside, Anna pushed a big rock over the hole. She laughed and ran away with Tom's coin. "Ha ha, Tom! I tricked you! Now the coin is mine and you are stuck in there!" she said.

Tom was scared and sad. He tried to push the rock, but it was too heavy. He shouted for help, but no one heard him. He wished he never pretended to be a wealthy scientist. He wished he never met Anna. He wished he could go back to his lab. But it was too late.

Once upon a time there was a little boy who wanted to make a noise. He had an object that he could clap. Every time the little boy clapped it, it made a noise. He was so happy and clapped it as loud as he could. He clapped it so many times that even his mom heard it. She came to the room and asked what he was doing. He proudly showed her the object and told her that he was making noises by clapping it. She was so pleased with what he was doing, she said he could play with it as much as he wanted. The little boy was so excited and kept clapping the object whenever he felt like making some noise.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside with her friends. One day, Lily and her friends were playing near a big field. Suddenly, they heard a loud horn sound.

Lily asked her friend, "What's that loud noise?"

Her friend replied, "It's a truck. The driver is letting us know he's coming."

Lily thought the sound was scary, but her friend said, "Don't worry, the driver is dependable. He always drives safely."

Lily felt better and continued playing with her friends. They had so much fun that they forgot about the loud horn sound. From that day on, Lily knew that she could always ask her friend for help when she felt scared.

Tim went to the park. He saw a big slide. He wanted to go down it. He set his toy on the ground. It was very dirty.

Tim ran up to the slide and put his hands on the sides. He looked down and saw it was very high. He was scared.

Then he took a deep breath. He stepped up onto the slide and set off. He felt very brave. He went down with a "whoo!" 

He reached the bottom and felt a big smile on his face. It was so much fun. He looked back up and saw the slide was now very dirty. He couldn't believe how quickly he'd made it so dirty. 

He thought he would try again and set off once more. He went down the slippery slide over and over, giggling each time. He felt like the slide was his best friend. 

Finally, he was too tired to go down the slide again. He waved goodbye and said "Bye! See you soon!" He picked up his dirty toy and walked away.

Once upon a time there was a little girl, who was very excited. She loved playing outside, especially in her garden. One day, when she was playing in the garden, she spotted something unusual. She saw a vine had started growing up one of the walls near her window. 

"Wow, that's so cool!" the little girl exclaimed.

The vine kept growing and when the little girl returned to the garden, the vine had changed - it had now covered the entire wall!

The little girl was so excited that she ran inside to get some help. She quickly found her mommy and told her about the vine.

"Mommy, I want to climb the vine!" the little girl said, hopping from one foot to the other.

Her mommy smiled and said, "Okay, but be careful!"

The little girl carefully climbed the vine to the top of the wall, and she was so proud of herself. She was excited to have done something so special and was looking forward to doing it again!

Once upon a time, there was a big, broken castle. A little girl named Lily lived in the castle with her friend, a small dog named Max. One day, they found a big, red ball in the castle.

"Max, let's play with the ball!" said Lily. But Max didn't want to play. He barked and ran away. Lily felt sad and didn't know why Max ignored her. She went to look for him in the castle.

Lily found Max in a small room. He was looking at a broken toy. Lily understood that Max was sad too. She said, "Max, I'm sorry I ignored your feelings. Let's fix the toy together." They worked together and fixed the broken toy.

After fixing the toy, they played with the big, red ball. They learned that they should not ignore each other's feelings. And they lived happily in the big, broken castle.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play with their phones. They have a network of other friends who play with them. They send messages and pictures to each other.

One day, Anna sees a famous star on TV. She likes the star very much. She wants to send a message to the star. She thinks the star will be happy to hear from her.

She writes: "Hi, I am Anna. I like you. You are very pretty and funny. Can you be my friend?"

She sends the message to the star's phone number. She waits for a reply.

But Ben sees what Anna does. He is angry. He likes Anna. He does not want her to like the star. He thinks the star is silly and boring. He wants to stop Anna from sending messages to the star.

He takes Anna's phone when she is not looking. He deletes the message to the star. He writes a new message: "Hi, I am Anna. I don't like you. You are very ugly and mean. Go away!"

He sends the message to the star's phone number. He thinks he has done a good thing.

But Anna sees what Ben does. She is sad. She cries. She does not understand why Ben is so mean. She wants to say sorry to the star. She wants to be friends with the star and with Ben.

She takes her phone back from Ben. She writes: "Hi, I am Anna. I am sorry for the bad message. It was not me. It was Ben. He is my friend, but he is jealous. He does not like you. But I do. Please don't be mad at me."

She sends the message to the star's phone number. She hopes the star will forgive her.

The star sees the messages from Anna. He is confused. He does not know who Anna is. He does not know why she likes him or why Ben hates him. He does not know what to do.

He writes: "Hi, I am the star. Who are you? Why are you sending me messages? Do you know me? Do you watch me on TV? Are you a fan?"

He sends the message to Anna's phone number. He waits for an answer.

Once upon a time, there was a brilliant parrot. He served his family faithfully everyday. He cracked open their nuts for breakfast and sang sweet songs for them in the evening.

One day, the parrot saw a brilliant butterfly. He wanted to show off his brilliance and serve the butterfly too. So he hopped up really high, trying to catch it. But the butterfly was too quick and flew away.

The parrot's family was sad that he didn't catch the butterfly. They found him a delicious seed to eat, to make him feel better. The parrot was so happy to be served and thanked his family with a very catchy song. 

The parrot made sure to keep practicing his flying and singing. He wanted to be able to serve even more people and make them happy too.

Claire had a mild day. She was out in her backyard playing. She found a puddle and decided to splash around in it. She jumped and twirled around, feeling so happy to belong in her backyard. 

Claire's mom noticed her daughter in the puddle. "There you are Claire! Come out of there and dry off," she said. Claire stopped to listen, and then walked over to her mom. She grabbed hold of her mom's hand and felt like she belonged there.

Claire's mom was so happy to see her daughter playing and having fun. She smiled and said, "Let's inside to get you warm and dry." The mother and daughter went inside and had a fun day. Claire felt like she belonged there too.

Maggie was so excited when she saw the big green package on the table. She ran up to it and started to tear away at the wrapping paper. Bits and pieces of the paper flew in the air as Maggie tore away, faster and faster.

Eventually the package was open and Maggie gasped at what she saw. Inside was a bright, shiny, green bike! She couldn't believe her eyes and, squealing with delight, she jumped on the bike and started to pedal away.

Maggie rode the bike around and around the garden, taking in all the sights. Soon her mom called her inside for dinner, but Maggie didn't want to leave. She'll just play with her green bike tomorrow, she thought!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named John. He was very curious about the world around him. 

One day, John went to a park to play. He saw a strange box full of junk. It was a big box of old items, like toys and blankets. 

John loved to poke things, so he started poking the box with his finger. Inside, he saw something funny. It was a stuffed toy! It was a bit silly looking, so John thought it was stupid.

He started poking the toy with his finger and it made a funny sound. He laughed and poked it again. Suddenly, the toy started moving and talking! John was so surprised and he jumped back.

The toy said, â€œHi John! My name is Pat. I am a talking toy. Want to be friends?â€ 

John was so happy he had a new friend! He nodded and hugged Pat. They were best friends, and every day John would go to the park to play with Pat and poke the junk in the box.

Anna and Ben were at the park with their mom. They liked to play on the swings, the slide and the sandbox. They saw many other kids and some dogs too. They waved to their friends and said hello.

"Mom, can we have ice-cream?" Anna asked. She loved ice-cream, especially chocolate and vanilla. Ben nodded. He liked ice-cream too, but he preferred strawberry and banana.

"Sure, sweeties. Let's go to the ice-cream truck," mom said. She took their hands and walked with them to the truck. There were many flavors and colors of ice-cream. Anna and Ben chose their favorites and mom paid the man.

"Thank you, mom!" Anna and Ben said. They licked their ice-creams and smiled. They were very yummy and cold.

As they were eating their ice-creams, they saw a little girl with a big hat and a pink dress. She was holding a balloon and a teddy bear. She looked very adorable. She waved to Anna and Ben and came closer.

"Hi, I'm Lily. Do you want to play with me?" she asked. She had a friendly voice and a cute smile.

"Hi, I'm Anna and this is Ben. We would love to play with you," Anna said. She liked Lily's hat and balloon. Ben liked her teddy bear.

"Great! Let's go to the sandbox. I have some toys there," Lily said. She led them to the sandbox and they started to make sandcastles, bridges and tunnels. They had a lot of fun and shared their toys and ice-creams.

Anna, Ben and Lily became good friends. They played until it was time to go home. They hugged and waved goodbye. They promised to see each other again soon. They were very happy.

Once there was a little girl called Emma. She was three years old and very curious. One day she went outside and discovered a parrot in the garden. The parrot was very pretty and had bright colours.

Emma was so happy to make a new friend. She asked him his name and he told her it was Fred. Emma and Fred played games and sang songs together all day long. 

And then, when the sun was setting, the parrot showed Emma a secret spot in the garden. It was the most beautiful place ever! There were colourful flowers, butterflies and birds. Emma was so happy that she wanted to stay there forever.

Emma and Fred promised to come back and discover new things together every day. And they did, for many years!

Once there was a kangaroo who was very popular. Everyone in the bush loved him. He was always very happy and wore a big smile on his face. 

One day, the kangaroo decided he wanted to dress up. He put on bright colors and cool patterns. Everyone thought he looked stunning! 

The kangaroo strutted around the bush and all his friends and family admired his outfit. Everyone wanted to look like him, including the other kangaroos. 

The popular kangaroo was the happiest ever and he wore his bright clothes proudly. He loved his new outfit and it made him feel special. 

The other kangaroos also wore colorful clothes now and everyone in the bush had a lot of fun. Even the kangaroo felt very cool and popular.

Once upon a time, there was a big safari with lots of animals like lions, zebras, and monkeys. A little boy named Timmy went on the safari with his mommy and daddy. They rode in a bumpy truck and saw all the animals up close. Timmy was very happy and excited.

Suddenly, they saw a big surprise! A giraffe was eating leaves from a tall tree. Timmy had never seen a giraffe before and it made him very happy. He pointed and said "Look mommy, a giraffe!"

After a while, the truck drove on a tight road and bumped a lot. Timmy held onto his mommy tight so he wouldn't fall. But he still had fun and saw lots of animals. When they got back to their hotel, Timmy was tired but happy. He told his mommy and daddy all about the safari and how he saw a big surprise.

The sun was shining brightly one day. A small girl went outside and saw something sparkly in the grass. She bent down and picked it up. It was a skull! She held it up to the sun and noticed it shone with a soft, mild light. 

She was so excited! She wanted to make it special, so she took it inside and spent the day painting it with sparkles and glitter. She even put a ribbon around it. 

When she was done, she went back outside and held the skull up to the sun once more. It shone even more brightly now. She smiled and hugged it close, feeling a warm, mild light fill her up inside too.

Once upon a time, there was a girl called Lucy. Every day, Lucy would worry about something. She worried about going to school, or not having enough sweets, or if everyone would like her. 

One day, Lucy's dad gave her a special symbol to wear around her neck. It was in the shape of a heart and it was pink. Lucy was very grateful for the symbol, as it made her feel safe and calm.

Whenever Lucy started to worry again, she'd take out the symbol and look at it. It made her feel better and she felt safe and comforted. 

From then on, whenever Lucy felt scared or worried, she'd just touch her symbol and she knew she was alright. This made Lucy very happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Jimmy. He lived in a small village with his mama. Every day he would explore and have lots of fun.

One day, Jimmy found a broken toy on the ground. He was so excited! He knew his mama could repair it.

Jimmy quickly ran back home and asked his mama if she could repair the toy. But his mama said she was very busy and had lots of work to do. Jimmy was disappointed and walked away sadly. 

The next day Jimmy asked his mama again, but she was still too busy. Jimmy was sad, but he thought of an idea. He searched the village and asked all his friends if any of them could repair the toy. 

Finally, Jimmy found his best friend, Ben. Ben said he could do the repair. Jimmy was so excited! They worked together to repair the toy.

When they were finished, the toy was like new and looked so cool! Jimmy was so happy. He thanked Ben for the repair. Jimmy and Ben had lots of fun playing with the toy. 

Jimmy was so glad he had thought of the idea to ask his friends for help. He promised himself to always be brave and never give up.

One day, a little girl called Jo was playing in her garden. She was very careful and she didn't want to make a mess. Suddenly, she found some sugar on the ground. "Oh, sugar!", she thought. Jo wanted to make something special with the sugar, so she started to throw it up into the air. The sugar spun around as it flew and when it came back down, it sparkled like stars. Jo was very happy and she laughed and smiled. But she needed to be careful with the sugar, so she put it back on the ground, and ran off to find something else to play with.

Patty was a creative 3 year old girl who loved to explore and play. Every morning, she would wake up, have a glass of milk, and go out to the garden.

One morning, however, her usual routine was interrupted. As Patty was drinking her milk she heard a loud noise coming from the garden. She put down her glass and went outside to investigate. 

To her surprise, Patty found a group of magical creatures in the garden. They asked her to come with them on an adventure. Patty was hesitant at first, but she was excited to explore and see what surprises the journey had in store.

The group of curious creatures led Patty to the center of the garden, where they performed a very special ceremony. With a wave of their wands, they changed the grass into a carpet of stars. 

Patty was amazed by the sight of the night sky painted on the ground. She had never seen anything like it before. She could feel the creative energy swirling around her. From that moment on, her life would never be the same again.

Sara and Sam are twins. They like to play in the park. They have a red ball and a blue ball. They throw the balls to each other and catch them.

One day, a big dog comes to the park. The dog is fast and likes to chase balls. The dog sees Sara and Sam's balls and runs after them. Sara and Sam are scared of the dog. They drop their balls and run to their mom.

"Mom, mom, help!" Sara and Sam cry. "The dog wants our balls!"

Mom sees the dog and the balls. She is not scared of the dog. She knows the dog is friendly and just wants to play. She kneels down and calls the dog.

"Come here, boy. Good dog. Sit. Stay." Mom says. The dog listens to mom and sits. Mom picks up the balls and gives them to Sara and Sam.

"See, the dog is nice. He just likes balls. You can play with him if you want." Mom says. "But you have to ask his owner first. He is over there."

Sara and Sam look at the dog. The dog wags his tail and licks his lips. He looks happy and cute. Sara and Sam smile and nod.

"OK, mom. We want to play with the dog." Sara and Sam say. They go to the dog's owner and ask him.

"Can we play with your dog, please? He likes our balls." Sara and Sam say.

"Sure, you can. His name is Spot. He loves to play with kids and balls." The dog's owner says. He smiles and nods.

Sara and Sam thank the dog's owner and go back to mom and Spot. They throw the balls and Spot chases them. They catch the balls and Spot brings them back. They laugh and have fun. They make a new friend.

Once upon a time, there was an ancient vegetable garden. In the garden there grew lots of juicy and delicious vegetables.

One day a little girl named Anna came to the garden. She was wearing a yellow dress and had a big smile on her face. She was so excited because she had never seen such a beautiful vegetable garden before.

Anna started picking some of the juiciest vegetables she could find. But then suddenly, she heard an ear-piercing scream coming from the garden. Startled, she dropped her basket of veggies and quickly looked around to see what was happening.

Just a few feet away were two little boys who were screaming with excitement. They had seen the biggest carrot they had ever seen in their lives! Anna couldn't help but smile as the two boys happily ran towards the ancient carrot.

And that's how Anna discovered the wonderful ancient vegetable garden.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. He had a message for his friend, but he didn't know how to send it. He decided to write it on a piece of paper and put it in a bow. 

Timmy walked to his friend's house and left the bow with the message on the doorstep. He waited for his friend to read it and come outside to play. 

But his friend never came outside. Timmy went back to his house feeling sad and stupid for not knowing how to send the message properly. 

Days went by and Timmy's friend never came to play. Timmy found out that his friend had moved away and never got the message. Timmy felt even more stupid and wished he had done things differently.

Once upon a time there was a green frog. The frog wanted to win a prize but did not know how. One day, he saw a man spraying something in his garden.

Frog hopped over and said, "What are you doing?"

The man said, "I'm spraying a special chemical to help my plants grow."

Frog said, "Can you spray something to help me win a prize?"

The man smiled and said, "Well, no, unfortunately I can't. But I can give you some advice. Work hard and never give up and you'll have a fighting chance at winning a prize."

Frog was so thankful for the advice. So he hopped away and worked hard every day. After a while, Frog finally did win a prize and was so happy. He danced around, celebrating his success and thanked the man who gave him the advice.

Jill and her dad were walking in the park. It was cold outside.

"Dad, let's bury the bottle of shampoo!" Jill said.

Jill's dad smiled.

"That is a good idea, Jill." He said.

Jill and her dad dug a hole and buried the shampoo. Then they covered the shampoo with dirt.

"Now the shampoo is buried," said Jill's dad.

"Yes, now it's safe," said Jill.

They both smiled and then walked home.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who went to the park. When she got there, it was an icy day. She felt very cold and wanted to go home. But then she saw a parade in the park. 

The girl was very excited and ran towards it. There were lots of colorful balloons and people dancing. She couldn't believe it! She suddenly realized that she was having lots of fun.

The parade was so different from her cold, icy park. She laughed and enjoyed it. She even sang along with the music. 

The parade seemed to last forever and the girl was filled with joy. When it was finally over, she was sad but also thankful. The girl then went home with a smile on her face.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Kaylee. She was only three years old and she loved to explore.

One day, her mommy gave her a soft blue ribbon and asked her to tie it to her hair. Kaylee happily accepted the ribbon and started to tie it to her hair. She was so happy that she skipped down the street.

As Kaylee walked, the street became a little busier. She stopped to look at all the cars and the bright lights. Suddenly, she smelled something funny. It was a strong, strange smell.

"Mommy, what's that smell?" Kaylee asked.

Her mommy replied, "that smell is gas. It's what the cars use to make them move."

Kaylee nodded her head and continued exploring. She couldn't believe how wonderful the world was - but she was glad to be safe and sound with her mommy.

Once upon a time, there was a little lizard. The lizard was very fierce. He liked to play in the sun all day. One day, he met a big lion.

The lion said, "Why are you so fierce, little lizard?"

The lizard said, "I feel fierce because I am strong and brave."

The lion smiled and said, "You are very brave, little lizard. Let's be friends and play together."

So, the fierce lizard and the big lion played together. They had lots of fun and became best friends.

Once upon a time, there was a happy island with lots of animals who lived there. Every morning the animals would wake up and smile at each other. They were so happy!

One day, a graceful swan flew onto the island. The animals were so excited to meet her. She had beautiful feathers and they all wanted to give her a big hug.

The swan was so happy on the island. Every day she would smile and make new friends. She liked to play in the ocean and the animals would laugh and smile when she swam around gracefully.

The animals were so happy when the swan stayed with them. They were sad when she flew away, but they still smiled and waved goodbye. They were thankful for the time they had together and they would always remember their happy island.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she was playing hide-and-seek with her friends. She found a hidden spot behind a big tree and waited to be found. But nobody came to look for her.

After a while, Lily got hungry and remembered she had a meal in her backpack. She opened it and started to eat. Suddenly, she heard a noise. It was her friend, Emma. "I found you, Lily!" she said.

Lily was happy to be found, but she noticed that her meal was gone. She asked Emma if she had taken it. Emma said no. Lily then examined the area around the tree and found some crumbs. She realized that a little mouse had taken her meal.

From that day on, Lily made sure to keep her meals in a safe place where no little animals could find them. And she and Emma continued to play hide-and-seek, always checking for hidden spots and making sure to keep their snacks safe.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She lived in a village with her family. One day, Lily went outside to play. It was very cold outside, and she felt chilly.

Lily saw an old man walking by, and she said, "Hello, sir! It's very cold today, isn't it?"

The old man replied, "Yes, it is. But I have to go to the village to speak with the mayor."

Lily felt sorry for the old man, so she offered him her scarf to keep him warm. The old man was very grateful and thanked Lily. 

Later that day, Lily's mother told her that it's always nice to help others, even if it's just a simple gesture. Lily remembered what she did for the old man, and she felt happy knowing that she helped someone in need.

Once there was a girl named Lily. She was very curious and loved looking at animals. Lily loved going to the park and examining the animals that lived there.

One day, Lily saw an owl sitting on a tree. She was so excited. The owl was so pretty! With its white feathers, round eyes and pointy ears. She wanted to get closer to get a better look.

Lily slowly tiptoed towards the tree where the owl was perched on. The owl looked down at her but did not move. Lily was so close that she could even touch the owl. She looked carefully at all its features and examined every detail.

The owl was sitting so still and seemed happy that Lily was there. Lily smiled at it and said 'hello'. The owl didn't say anything. Lily said goodbye and thanked the owl for letting her examine it.

Lily left feeling very happy. She had seen a pretty owl and been able to get so close!

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny named Hopper. Hopper loved to hop around all day long. One day, Hopper went to visit his friend, Teddy Bear. Teddy Bear was sleeping on a delicate mattress. 

Hopper said, "Hi Teddy Bear! Can I hop on your bed?" 

Teddy Bear replied, "No, Hopper. My mattress is delicate. If you hop on it, you might break it." 

Hopper felt sad. He didn't want to break his friend's bed. So, he decided to hop around the room instead. 

Teddy Bear woke up and saw Hopper hopping around. He said, "Wow, Hopper! You're such a good hopper. Maybe we can play hopscotch together." 

Hopper felt happy again. He loved to hop and now he had a new game to play with his friend. They played hopscotch all day long and had so much fun together.

One day, a little girl named Emily was playing in her garden. Suddenly, she heard a noise coming from her pond. She looked in and saw a small frog swimming around. She lifted it out of the water and it hopped away. 

Emily felt sad that the frog had to leave, so she started to fill the pond with water. She filled it until the pond was full. After that, she planted some flowers around it, so that the frog could come back and find a nice place to stay. 

Every year, Emily made sure the pond was full and that the flowers were alive and healthy. Then, one year, Emily noticed that the pond was empty and the flowers were dead. She was very sad and sat in her garden for a long time. 

Finally, Emily decided she was going to do something. She filled the pond with water and planted new flowers. Then, she waited, and soon enough, a frog appeared. Emily was so happy that she jumped up and down and clapped her hands. 

The little frog seemed to be happy too. Emily liked to watch it swim and play in the pond. She knew she had done the right thing, and she was proud of herself. From that day on, Emily made sure the pond was full and the flowers were alive, so that the little frog was happy and safe.

Once upon a time there was a bright little bird. She had two small legs and she was very happy. She wanted to know more about the world, so she spread her wings and flew to the sky.

As she flew she looked down on the flowers and trees below. She noticed the sun was shining so she flew higher and higher to find out what it was like. She flapped her wings fast and flew until the sun was brighter and brighter.

The bright sun warmed her wings and she felt so happy. She flew lower and lower until she could see the people and animals below. From up there she knew she was part of the world and she was glad. 

The little bird flew back to her nest, feeling very content. She knew how lucky she was to be able to fly and explore the world. Now she knew it was a big and beautiful place.

Once upon a time there were two mice that lived in a farm. Their names were Daisy and Tom. Tom was very brave but Daisy was a bit fearful.
One day, Tom sailed away in a cage. Daisy was very sad and cried for many hours. She was so fearful that something bad may have happened to him. 
Suddenly, Daisy heard a voice. It was Tom! Tom explained that he had floated away in his cage and the wind had brought him back to the farm. He had learnt an important lesson - that the greatest adventures are close to home.

So, Tom and Daisy stayed home, but still often went exploring together. They were no longer fearful, as they knew that even the most amazing adventures were right in their backyard. In the end, they both learnt an important life lesson â€“ that home is a safe and special place.

Once upon a time there was a grumpy bear. The bear lived alone in a little cave deep in the woods. Every morning he would wake up and be so grumpy that he would stomp around and moan. 

One day, the bear heard music and singing coming from the nearby village. He peeked out of his cave and saw everyone was dancing. He wanted to join in, so he decided to go out and join them. 

The bear was amazed. He had never seen so many people dancing. He tried to dance too, but he was so grumpy that he was too clumsy. Everyone laughed at the clumsy bear and soon he gave up and quit. 

He returned to his cave, feeling sad. But then he changed his mind and decided he was not too grumpy for a dance. In the morning he went out and joined the dancing again. And this time he did it with a big smile.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy who loved to play with his boat in the pond. One day, Timmy's boat floated away from him and he couldn't reach it. He was sad and started to cry.

Just then, Timmy's friend Billy came along and asked him why he was crying. Timmy explained what happened and Billy said, "Don't worry, I'll help you get your boat back."

Billy jumped into the pond and swam to the boat. He brought it back to Timmy and they both smiled happily. But then, Timmy noticed that the water tasted bitter. "Yuck!" he said. "This water is bitter."

Billy explained that sometimes the water can taste bitter when the weather is bad. Timmy thanked Billy for helping him return his boat and they both went home, happy and dry.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to dream about silly things like flying unicorns and talking animals. One day, she was playing outside when she saw a butterfly. "Hello butterfly! Can I touch you?" she asked. "Yes, you can touch me," the butterfly replied.

Lily gently touched the butterfly's wings and it flew away. She continued to play outside until it was time for bed. That night, she had a dream about the butterfly she had touched. In her dream, the butterfly talked to her and they went on a magical adventure together.

The next morning, Lily woke up feeling happy and excited about her dream. She ran to her mom and said, "Mommy, I had a silly dream about a butterfly I touched!" Her mom smiled and said, "That sounds like a wonderful dream. I'm glad you had fun." From that day on, Lily always looked forward to dreaming about silly things and touching new creatures she met outside.

One day, May and her mom went to the store. May was excited to explore the shelves. She saw the price tags and was confused. She didn't understand why some of the things cost money.

Her mom saw her confusion and smiled. She picked up a small toy and said "This toy is a good price". She handed the toy to May, and May was not confused anymore. 

May was so happy with her new toy. She ran around the store with it, scattering the pieces of the toy around the aisles. Mum laughed and helped May pick them all up. 

When they arrived home, May was tired and happy with her favorite toy. She hugged her mom, thankful for taking her to the store.

Once upon a time, there was a big clock in a famous tower. The clock had big hands that moved all day long. People came from far away just to see the famous clock.

One day, a little girl went to see the clock. She looked up and saw that the clock was frowning. She didn't know why the clock was sad, so she asked her mommy. Her mommy said that sometimes things get tired, just like people do.

The little girl felt sad for the clock, so she decided to draw a picture of the clock smiling. She showed the picture to the clock and the clock smiled back. From that day on, the clock was no longer frowning and the little girl felt happy that she had made the clock feel better.

Once upon a time there was a hunter who was looking for something to hunt. Everywhere that the hunter looked, he could not find any prey. But then suddenly he saw a lively fox jumping around in a meadow. The hunter was eager to catch the fox, but the fox was even more eager to escape.

The hunter yelled, "Hey fox, stop running around and be my prey!" But the fox didn't listen and kept running. He shouted louder and louder, but the fox kept on.

The fox exclaimed, "No way! I will resist you and keep running!" With that, the fox hopped and skipped around the meadow, dodging the hunter as best as he could.

The hunter was frustrated and angry. He tried to come up with different plans to catch the fox, but nothing worked. The fox was too lively! So the hunter gave up and went home without any prey that day.

John was out at the park with his family. He wanted to act brave, so he ran and jumped across the wooden bridge. But when he reached the other side, he felt a bit dizzy. He decided to sit and watch his brothers and sisters play. He heard his dad say something about a surprise. 

Mom asked, "What surprise, dad?" 

Dad replied, "We'll give John a special pass that he can use to go on all the rides at the fair!" 

John was so excited that he jumped off the bridge and ran over to his dad. "Can I go on the rides?" he squealed. 

Dad smiled and said, "All in good time my son. You'll have to wait and see!" 

All the way home, John wondered what it would be like to be able to go on all the rides. When they arrived home, he was so eager to find out that he ran inside and grabbed the pass. But as he looked at it, he felt a bit dizzy. It was only then that he realized it had to be a special day to use the pass. Now he was more excited than ever to find out what it was!

Once there was a girl called Margie and she really loved to write. She had a favourite pen, and every morning before school she would write in her special notebook. Margie was very creative and loved to make stories.

One day she was in her garden and noticed something furry. She got closer and realised it was a sheep! Its wool was soft and hairy, and so Margie decided she wanted to write about it.

So she went inside and got her notebook and pen. She wrote a fantastic story about the sheep and all the things she liked about it. She wrote and wrote until she'd finished the whole story.

When she was done, she was very proud of what she had written. From then on, every time she saw a sheep, she'd remember that story she'd written.

Once upon a time, there was a big, hairy bear named Bubba. Bubba loved to play in the forest and eat honey from the trees. One day, Bubba was walking through the forest when he saw a shiny steel trap on the ground. 

"What's this?" Bubba asked himself. "It looks like a toy."

Bubba went to investigate the trap and accidentally stepped on it. The trap closed around Bubba's paw and he couldn't get free. 

"Help!" Bubba cried out. "Somebody help me!"

But no one heard Bubba's cries for help. He was stuck in the trap for days until he finally passed away. The forest animals mourned the loss of their friend, Bubba the bear.

Once upon a time, there was a light that shone in the darkness. One night, something very sad happened. The light became miserable and wasn't so bright any more.

The world around it seemed to get darker and darker. Soon, everything was so dark, the sad light couldn't be seen at all. Everyone was sad about what had happened.

But suddenly, something amazing happened. The light started to shine again! The darkness disappeared, and the light was happy and bright.

Everyone cheered and were so glad that the light was back. Now they could all feel safe and warm again. From then on, the light kept shining brightly, and the world was a happy place once more.

Once upon a time, there was a small girl named Jenny. She was three years old. One day, Jenny found an interesting tube of toys. She was so excited! 

She grabbed the tube and opened it. Inside, she could see lots of colourful shapes. There were stars, circles, squares and more. She was awe-struck! 

Jenny said, "What shall I do?"

Her mommy smiled and said, "Let's count them, Jenny!"

So, Jenny and her mommy counted together. When they finished, they had counted 32 shapes. 

Jenny was very happy. She smiled and said, "This is so interesting!" 

Then, they put the toys back in the tube and put it away. Jenny and her mommy had a great time counting together.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tweety. Tweety was very happy because she lived in a beautiful garden with lots of flowers and fruits to eat. One day, Tweety saw a big cat coming towards her. The cat wanted to catch Tweety and eat her. Tweety was scared and needed to escape.

Tweety flew as fast as she could and landed on a tree branch. The cat couldn't reach her there. Tweety said, "Thank you for not eating me, Mr. Cat. I need to go now. Bye-bye!" The cat replied, "You're welcome, Tweety. Have a good time in your beautiful garden."

Tweety felt relieved and happy. She realized that it was important to be careful and always have a plan to escape from danger. She flew back to her garden and enjoyed the beautiful flowers and fruits with her bird friends. From that day on, Tweety knew that she could always escape from danger and have a good time in her beautiful garden.

Once upon a time, a little bunny named Floppy went for a walk in the forest. Floppy loved to play and hop around. Suddenly, he saw a big hole in the ground. He thought it would be fun to bury himself in it, so he hopped inside.

But then, Floppy realized he couldn't see anything. The hole was too deep and dark. He got scared and wanted to get out, but he couldn't find the way. Then, he heard a sound. It was a fox! The fox saw Floppy and wanted to eat him. 

Floppy tried to run away, but he was trapped. The fox caught him and hurt him. Poor Floppy! He should have never buried himself in that hole. From that day on, he knew to always be careful and never go out of sight.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Mandy. Mandy loved to create, and she loved to explore. Whenever she explored, Mandy would find cool things, like a rare symbol that she had never seen before.

Mandy asked her mom what the symbol meant. Her mom said, â€œItâ€™s a special symbol Mandy. This symbol is rare and special. Itâ€™s a symbol for everyone to use to create something together.â€

Mandy was so excited! She wanted to create something special with her friends. Together, they made a big picture using the rare symbol. It was colorful and had lots of different shapes.

When they finished, Mandy smiled and said, â€œWe created something special!â€ Her friends agreed, and they all knew they had created something amazing.

Once upon a time there was a very special elderly lady. Her name was Mrs Jones. She liked to write letters. Every day she would pick up a pen and start writing.

One day when Mrs Jones was writing her letters she had an idea. She decided to print her name on her letters. She sat down at her computer and opened the printer. She pressed all the buttons and soon her name was printed on the paper. 

Mrs Jones was so happy with her name. She put the paper in an envelope and sent it off. 

The days went by and Mrs Jones received a letter back in the mail. It was from a 3 year old girl and it said, "Dear Mrs Jones, thank you for writing me and for printing your name on your letter. From, Lily."

Mrs Jones smiled wide and was so happy. She had a new friend in Lily. Mrs Jones planned to write to Lily often and always print her name on the envelopes.

Once upon a time there lived an adorable bunny called Binky. Binky lived in a big garden and loved hopping around. He never felt scared, not even when the sun went down. Until one night.

Binky was hopping around, when something big and dark flew past his ears! He was so scared that he hopped really quick away. He stopped under a bush and he could feel his heart going very fast.

Binky knew he couldn't be scared forever, so he closed his eyes and was brave. Slowly, he hopped out from under the bush and looked around the garden. To his surprise, he saw a big owl perched on a branch nearby, who was looking at him with big eyes.

It was the owl that had scared him! Binky was so relieved, he eventually worked up the courage to hop closer to the owl. He was so friendly that the owl flew down and perched on Binkyâ€™s back. From that day forward, Binky and the owl were the best of friends. No matter what time of day, they were always hopping, flapping and playing together in the garden.

Lily and Ben were going to the park with Mom and Dad. They had to prepare for the trip. They packed their snacks, water, hats and toys in a big bag. They also put on sunscreen and shoes. Mom and Dad prepared the van. They checked the gas, the tires and the map. They put the bag and a blanket in the back of the van.

The van was very original. It was old and colorful. It had many stickers and drawings on it. Lily and Ben liked the van. They thought it was fun and cool. They climbed in the van and buckled their seat belts. They waved to their neighbors and said goodbye.

The park was not far away. They drove for a little while and saw many things. They saw cars, trucks, buses, bikes and people. They saw trees, flowers, birds and squirrels. They saw a big sign that said "Welcome to the park". They were very excited.

They parked the van in a shady spot. They got out of the van and took the bag and the blanket. They found a nice place to sit on the grass. They spread the blanket and put the bag on it. They ate their snacks and drank their water. They felt happy and full.

They played in the park for a long time. They ran, jumped, swung, slid and climbed. They made new friends and shared their toys. They laughed and had fun. They saw more animals and plants. They learned new things. They had a great day.

Lily was a shy girl. She liked to play with her dolls and books, but she did not like to talk to other kids. She was afraid they would laugh at her or be mean to her.

One day, her mom told her that they were going to a birthday party. It was for Anna, a girl from her preschool. Lily did not know Anna very well, but she knew she liked princesses. Lily liked princesses too, but she did not have a princess dress.

"Don't worry, sweetie," her mom said. "You can wear your pink skirt and your white shirt. You look very pretty. And maybe you can make a new friend at the party."

Lily nodded, but she felt nervous. She did not want to go to the party. She wanted to stay home and play with her dolls.

When they got to the party, Lily saw a lot of kids. They were running and jumping and laughing. They had balloons and hats and cake. Lily felt scared. She held her mom's hand and hid behind her.

"Look, there's Anna!" her mom said. "Let's go say hello."

Lily saw Anna. She was wearing a beautiful princess dress. It was purple and sparkly and had a big bow. She had a crown on her head and a wand in her hand. She looked very happy.

"Hi, Lily!" Anna said. "I'm so glad you came to my party. Do you like princesses?"

Lily nodded, but she did not say anything. She looked at the ground.

"Me too!" Anna said. "Do you want to play with me? I have a lot of princess toys. We can pretend to be princesses and have a tea party. Come on, I'll show you."

Anna took Lily's hand and led her to a corner of the room. There was a table with cups and plates and a teapot. There were also dolls and stuffed animals dressed as princesses and princes.

"Look, this is my favorite princess," Anna said. "Her name is Elsa. She has ice powers. And this is my favorite prince. His name is Jack. He likes to make snowmen. Who is your favorite princess?"

Lily looked at the toys. She saw a princess she liked. She had long blonde hair and a pink dress. She had a necklace with a heart.

"I like her," Lily said softly. "She is pretty."

Anna smiled. "She is pretty. Her name is Rapunzel. She has magic hair. Do you want to play with her?"

Lily nodded. She took the doll and held it gently.

"Great!" Anna said. "You can be Rapunzel and I'll be Elsa. And we can invite the other princesses and princes to our tea party. Do you want to do that?"

Lily nodded again. She felt a little less shy. She liked Anna. She liked playing with her. She liked being a princess.

"Okay, let's do it!" Anna said. "We are the best princess friends ever!"

Lily smiled. She agreed. She was happy. She was glad she came to the party.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved going to the library with his mom. They would read books and play games together. One day, Timmy saw a fragile vase on a shelf. He wanted to touch it, but his mom said "No, it's fragile. It could break." 

Timmy felt sad, but he listened to his mom. They went to the desk to check out their books. Suddenly, Timmy saw a zipper on the librarian's jacket. He asked "Can you zip and unzip that?" The librarian smiled and said "Yes, I can." 

As they were leaving the library, Timmy accidentally knocked over the fragile vase. It broke into a million pieces. His mom was very upset and the librarian said "That was very careless, Timmy." Timmy felt bad and said "I'm sorry."

One day, Jane was walking through the woods searching for a place to take a nap. She had been walking for hours and was feeling very tired. All of a sudden, she spotted a tunnel. Everything was peaceful until she heard a loud voice. 

"You can't take a nap here!", yelled a voice.

Jane was feeling frustrated but knew that the squirrel was right. She slowly began to stand up and as she stepped out of the tunnel, she thanked him for reminding her that she needed to find a better place to take her nap. 

The next day, Jane returned to the woods feeling determined to find the perfect place to take a nap. After a while, she noticed a small clearing in a nearby park. Ben is not happy. He does not want to share the teddy bear. He wants a car or a truck. He thinks Mommy does not know what he likes. He pouts and crosses his arms.

"Come on, Ben," Anna says. "The teddy bear is nice. You can play with it too. We can take turns."

Ben shakes his head. He does not want to play with the teddy bear. He thinks it is boring. He walks away from the box. He goes to his room. He finds his old car. It is blue and shiny and has four wheels. He likes his car. He plays with it on the floor.

"Ben, can I come in?" she asks.

Ben does not answer. He pretends he does not hear her. He keeps playing with his car.

"Ben, look what I have," she says. She holds the teddy bear. "It is not just a teddy bear. It is a driver. He can drive your car. He can go fast and make noises. Vroom, vroom!"

Ben looks up. He sees the teddy bear. He sees Anna's smile. He feels curious. He wonders how the teddy bear can drive his car.

"Really?" he asks.

"Really," Anna says. She puts the teddy bear in the car. She pushes the car. The car and the teddy bear move on the floor. They make noises. Vroom, vroom!

Ben laughs. He thinks it is funny. He thinks it is cool. He reaches for the car. He wants to try it too.

"Can I play with you?" he asks.

"Of course," Anna says. She gives him the car. She gives him the teddy bear. "You can play with them. We can share."

Ben smiles. He thanks Anna. He hugs the teddy bear. He hugs his sister. He thinks she is nice. He thinks she is smart. He thinks they are twins. They are the same.

Tommy was walking outside. The cold wind was blowing and Tommy felt chilly. Suddenly, Tommy heard a loud noise and saw that the window had split open. Looking in the window, Tommy saw something amazing! A Promise Bird was singing a lovely song.

Tommy felt so happy that he wanted to make the Promise Bird his friend. He made a big promise to the bird that they would be friends forever and ever.

One day, the cold wind was blowing even harder than before. Tommy was worried that the Promise Bird wouldn't stay warm enough and he might get hurt.

So Tommy got his warmest coat and covered the bird with it. The bird was so happy and thanked him. From that day on, the bird stayed with Tommy and they kept the promise they made to stay together forever and ever.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved playing with his toys and going to the park. One day, Timmy's mom told him they needed to clean his room. Timmy didn't want to clean his room because he wanted to play with his toys. But his mom said it was important to keep things in order.

One day there was a carrot. She was very competitive. She wanted to win a race. So she asked all the other carrots to race her. Every carrot wanted to win.

The race began and the carrots hopped as fast as they could. The carrot was trying her best. She was faster than the others. The carrot hopped and hopped until she reached the finish line.

Once upon a time, there was a grumpy old coat. Nobody wanted to wear him because he was so heavy. So he stayed in the closet all alone. Every morning, he would peek out to see if anyone was coming to get him. But no one ever did.

One day, a little 3-year-old girl opened the closet door. She saw the grumpy old coat and smiled. "This is just perfect for me!" she said. She weighed it in her hands and found it was very light. Then she put it on and felt wonderful.

From then on, she wore the grumpy old coat all the time. Whenever she went outside, she stayed warm and cozy. Even when she was grumpy, the coat made her happy. And now, the grumpy old coat is always in the three-year-old girl's closet, waiting for her to wear it.

Once upon a time there was a very intelligent penny. He could do tricks like no other penny around. He loved to wrap himself in paper and make shapes out of it.

One day the penny was wrapping himself when it heard a sound. It was a hungry fox who had been watching him. The intelligent penny knew he needed to get away quickly. He ran as fast as he could but the fox was faster.

Before he knew it, the fox had caught the penny in its mouth. The intelligent penny had no way to escape. The fox wrapped the penny up in its mouth and ate it in one big bite.

Once upon a time there was a stubborn faucet that was leaking everywhere. A brave 3 year old, Joe, was determined to solve the problem.

Joe's mom asked him, "Can you please help me with this leaking faucet? It's making a mess!" Joe said, "Yes, I will help you. I will solve the problem!"

Joe got to work. He tried turning the faucet handle. He tried tightening the pipes. He tried making adjustments of all kinds. But every time he thought he had solved the problem, the faucet leaks kept coming. 

Joe kept on working and he kept on trying. But the faucet was stubborn and nothing seemed to work.

Luckily, Joe's mom came to the rescue. She said, "Joe, sweetheart, how about we call the plumber? They will know how to solve this problem."

Joe and his mom called the plumber who quickly fixed the leaky faucet. Joe was happy and proud of himself for helping to solve the problem. 

And Joe and his mom lived happily ever after!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to play with her toys on the floor. One day, she found a secret door on the floor. She opened it and found a treasure chest inside. She was so happy and excited to reveal the treasure to her family.

But then, a big, scary monster came out of the treasure chest. Lily was helpless and didn't know what to do. The monster started to chase her around the room. Lily tried to hide, but the monster found her.

Once upon a time, there was a fat horse living in a stable. He was very sad, because he wanted to escape! One day, he saw an opportunity. He saw that the door of the stable was open just a little bit. So he ran fast and he squeezed through the small opening. He was free!

The horse was so happy! He ran and ran until he couldn't run anymore. He looked around and he was in a beautiful field full of grass and flowers. He ate the grass until his tummy was full. He was so happy to escape the stable and enjoy the fresh air.

He stayed in the field for a long time, until it was time to go back home. He slowly made his way back to the stable and found the door open. He stepped back inside and was ready to go to sleep.

The fat horse was very happy that he was brave enough to escape the stable. He was so glad to be back home. And he never tried to escape again!

Lily and Tom love to ride their bikes. They have red bikes with big wheels and bells. They like to ride fast and ring their bells loud. Sometimes they race each other and laugh.

Lily gets angry. She does not want to play with Tim anymore. She takes her doll and runs away.

"Lily, wait. I am sorry. I was just joking. I do not mean to be mean. I like you. You are my friend. Please, come back and play with me," Tim says.

Will Lily forgive Tim? Will they play with their dolls again? What do you think?

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in her backyard with her favorite toy, a stuffed bunny named Binky. One day, while playing, Binky accidentally fell over the fence and into the neighbor's yard.

Lily was sad and didn't know what to do. Suddenly, she saw an adorable puppy named Max marching towards her. Max asked, "What's wrong, Lily?"

Lily was so happy and thanked Max for his help. From then on, Max and Lily became the best of friends and played together every day in the backyard.

Once upon a time, there was a small girl named May who had a pet rabbit. May loved her rabbit and enjoyed playing with her every day.

One day, the rabbit spotted something new in the backyard. She dug a dry hole in the ground with her paws and found something shiny. May ran over to the rabbit, looked in the hole, and saw it was full of carrots! 

May was so excited that she asked the rabbit, "do you want to share the carrots?" But the rabbit shook her head and said, "No! I hate carrots, they're yucky!"

May laughed and said, "Well, if you don't want the carrots, can I have them?" But the rabbit said, "No, I don't want them either. The hole is mine and I found it first!"

May huffed and puffed but knew the rabbit had found the hole and it was only fair. So she said, "OK, we will both keep the hole and you can do whatever you want with it."

The rabbit proudly hopped away, knowing her hole was safe, and May and her rabbit played happily the rest of the day.

One day little Jimmy went for a drive with his mom. It was very icy outside, so the driver had to be careful. Suddenly, the car started to slide. The driver tried to steer it back on the road, but it was too late. The car went off the side of the road and got stuck in a ditch.

Jimmy's mom was very scared, but she knew that everything was going to be alright. She told Jimmy to stay inside the car, and stepped outside to look for help. Jimmy watched from the window as his mom waved her arms to get someone's attention.

Finally, a truck driver stopped. He got out and pulled the car out of the ditch with a rope. Jimmy was so excited that he wanted to thank the driver. So he hugged the driver and jumped up and down. The driver laughed and said "I'm glad I could help." 

Then they all went home. Jimmy hung his hat on the hook by the door and he couldn't stop talking about the icy adventure he had been on. His mom smiled and said, "Let's never do that again!"

Once upon a time, there was a polite tiger. He lived in a big forest with lots of trees and animals. One day, the tiger got very dirty from playing in the mud. He decided to clean himself in the river. He splashed and played in the water until he was clean again. After that, he went back to his home in the forest feeling happy and fresh. The other animals were amazed to see how clean and shiny the tiger looked. From that day on, the tiger made sure to stay clean and tidy.

Once upon a time, there was a long giant. Everywhere it went, it liked to collect things. It had a big bag and it filled it up with all sorts of interesting things! It collected leaves, rocks, feathers and even sticks. 

One day it was running low on things to collect and it started to worry. But then it noticed a big hill and it had an idea. It picked up the hill and put it in its bag!

The long giant was so happy with its collection. It carried the hill wherever it went and it was always busy collecting more and more things. 

The end.

One day, a cat named Tom was playing outside. It started to rain, and Tom got very wet. He did not like being wet, so he tried to find a dry place to hide.

Tom saw a big wall and thought it would be a good place to hide from the rain. But the wall was very tall, and Tom was small. He started to climb the wall, but it was hard. Tom began to struggle as he tried to climb the wet wall.

A dog named Sam saw Tom and said, "Do you need help, Tom?" Tom said, "Yes, please. The wall is too tall, and I am wet." Sam helped Tom climb the wall, and they both found a dry place to hide from the rain. They were happy to be dry and safe together.

Mum and Dad had an exciting surprise for Sarah and her brother, Ben.
Dad said, "Come and look what I've got!" 
He lifted up a box, and there was a new light bulb inside. Sarah and Ben each held one end and lifted it together. Then Dad said, "This light bulb will make your room nice and clean."

Sarah and Ben both nodded enthusiastically. Then they switched on the light and the room filled with a warm, inviting glow.

Once upon a time, there were two friends â€“ Moo and Pete. Moo was a cow and Pete was a pig. One day, they were walking along the farm together. Moo said to Pete, â€œLetâ€™s play with my new bucket!â€
