On his hopping adventures he came across some really cool stuff. First, he found a big juicy carrot, then some sweet honey, and even some spicy peppers! He collected all this stuff in his big floppy ears.

The bunny kept hopping and when he came to a big pond, he stopped to take a rest. But just then, he heard a voice. â€œHey!â€

He looked and there was a frog standing on the edge of the pond. â€œDo you want some of my stuff?â€ the frog asked.

The bunny hopped over to the frog, and saw that the frog had some wonderful stuff. There were lots of tasty bugs, a variety of smooth stones, and a few spicy peppers. The bunny was so excited! He hopped around in circles, stuffing his ears with the frog's stuff.

The frog smiled and said, â€œI'm glad you like my stuff. Now you can go on your hopping-adventures with something yummy and spicy!â€

The bunny thanked the frog, and he hopped away, with the most wonderful stuff ever.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a toy that she loved to play with every day. One day, the toy stopped working. Lily tried to play with it, but it wouldn't turn on. She looked at the toy and saw that the switch was broken. 

Lily was sad because she couldn't play with her toy anymore. She decided to rest and think about what she could do to fix it. After a while, she got an idea. She went to her dad and asked him to help her fix the switch. 

Her dad looked at the toy and saw that it was an easy fix. He got a new switch and replaced the broken one. Lily was so happy that her toy was working again! She played with it all day and when she was tired, she put it away and went to rest.

Once upon a time there was a horse. He was very furry. His name was Bob. Bob wanted a friend so he went on a journey. Along the way he met a little boy. His name was Jack. Jack thought Bob was very special so he decided to introduce him to his family. 

He took Bob home and everyone was very excited to meet him. They petted him and fed him carrots. Jacks parents were very happy. They thought Bob was a friendly and gentle horse. He was the perfect addition to their family. 

Jack and Bob became the best of friends. They went on long walks and raced each other in the fields. Jack would always give Bob a big hug at the end of the day. 

Bob and Jack would spend all of their days together and Bob was always happy. They were a great team.

Tom and Lily were playing with their toys in the living room. They had many toys, like cars, dolls, blocks and books. They liked to make noise and have fun.

But their mom was very tired. She had a hard day at work. She wanted to relax and watch TV. She did not like the noise and the mess. She said in a harsh voice, "Tom and Lily, stop playing now! It is time to clean up and go to bed. I need some quiet and peace."

Tom and Lily did not want to stop playing. They liked their toys and they were not sleepy. They said, "But mom, we are having fun. We want to play more. Can we watch TV with you?"

Their mom said, "No, you cannot watch TV with me. TV is not for little kids. It is for grown-ups. You need to sleep and rest. Now go to your room and brush your teeth. I will come and tuck you in."

Tom and Lily were sad and angry. They did not like their mom's harsh voice. They did not like to clean up and go to bed. They did not like to miss TV. They thought their mom was mean and unfair.

But they knew they had to obey their mom. They put their toys away and went to their room. They brushed their teeth and put on their pajamas. They waited for their mom to come and tuck them in.

Their mom came after a while. She looked calmer and softer. She said, "I'm sorry, Tom and Lily. I did not mean to be harsh. I love you very much. I just had a bad day and I needed to relax and watch TV. But I know you are good kids and you deserve some fun too. How about we watch some TV together tomorrow? We can watch your favorite show and have some snacks. Would you like that?"

Tom and Lily smiled and nodded. They felt better and happier. They said, "Yes, mom, we would like that. We love you too. We are sorry for making noise and mess. We hope you have a good night and a better day tomorrow."

Their mom hugged them and kissed them. She said, "Thank you, Tom and Lily. You are very sweet and thoughtful. You make me proud and happy. Have a good night and sweet dreams."

She turned off the light and left the room. Tom and Lily snuggled in their beds and closed their eyes. They felt warm and cozy. They relaxed and fell asleep.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sue. She had a big, hairy dog named Max. They loved to play together in the park. One day, while they were playing, Sue lost her mom's phone. She was very sad and worried.

Sue and Max started to look for the phone. They looked under the trees, behind the bushes, and on the slides. Max used his nose to help find the phone. Finally, Max found the phone near the swings. Sue was very happy and hugged her hairy friend.

Sue learned that it is important to take care of things that belong to others. She promised to be more careful with her mom's phone. Sue and Max went home, happy that they could find the phone. The moral of the story is to always be responsible and take care of other people's things.

Once upon a time, there was a girl called Sarah. She was very organised and liked to keep her home neat and tidy. She had a big, comfortable bed and lots of toys. She also had a special phone, which was pink and sparkly.

Every day she would use her phone to organise her day. She wrote down what she wanted to do and ticked it off when she was done. This made Sarah feel very comfortable and proud of herself.

Sarah organised things for her friends too. She would make time to play games with them and call them on the phone. She organised playdates and tea parties and made sure to tell her friends when and where.

One day, when Sarah was feeling particularly organised, she decided to organise a surprise picnic for all her friends. She quickly got her phone and sent out some invites. Everyone was surprised and excited when they found out.

Sarah was so proud of herself and knew that she had done a great job. She felt so comfortable and happy - knowing that she could organise anything she wanted. In the end, Sarah enjoyed her special picnic and had a lot of fun with her friends.

Once upon a time, there were two best friends, a boy and a girl. Their names were Joe and Sarah. They both liked to play together and always made each other laugh.

One day, Sarah asked Joe to marry her. Joe was so happy, he said yes right away. They were both so excited, they decided to throw a big party.

Everyone was having a great time until a mysterious cage appeared. Nobody knew where it came from. Joe and Sarah were scared, but they were brave. They decided to open the cage and see what was inside.

Inside, they found two birds. Joe and Sarah explained to the birds that they wanted to get married someday, and said that the birds could come with them if they wanted. And so, the birds flew around Joe and Sarah as they said â€˜I doâ€™.

Everyone cheered and clapped. Joe and Sarah were now married. From that day on, the birds always stayed close by Joe and Sarah, remembering the special day when their new friends got married.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Sarah. She loved to explore and play. One day, Sarah went on an adventure. While exploring, she spotted an old vase in the grass. She carefully picked it up. When Sarah saw the vase, she was amazed! It glowed with a unique light. 

Sarah looked at the vase in wonder. The vase felt warm in her hands. She touched it gently and watched as the glowing light changed color. Sarah had never seen anything like this before! 

Before long, it started to get dark, so Sarah took the vase home with her. The light from the vase lit up her room as she placed it on her shelf. The unique glow of the vase made Sarah feel very special. 

 Sarah went to bed that night dreaming of the mysterious vase. She loved it so much and knew it would always be a special part of her home.

Once upon a time there was a bear who loved to climb. Every day he would climb up the tallest trees, over the highest hills, and onto the highest mountains. He loved the feeling of being so high up and looking out over the world.

One day, the bear wanted to do something extra special. So, he decided to climb the highest peak in the world. It was so cold and the wind was so strong that he thought he'd never make it to the top. But the bear kept going and plodded on until he finally reached the top.

And there, at the very highest peak, the bear found a medal. He gave it a big hug and was so happy to have it!

The bear kept the medal forever and cherished it. He thought of all the brave things he had done to reach the top and be rewarded with such a special medal. 

The bear was very proud and never forgot how happy he was that day. He often thought back to all the amazing climbs he had done and how, when he was brave enough, he achieved the highest peak and was rewarded with a cold, shimmering medal.

Sam was a bald man. Every day he would put on his special jacket. The jacket was very important to Sam. It had lots of pockets, and in them was all the things he needed to record the day. He had a very special recording device that would help him remember everything he had seen and done during the day. 

Sam liked to take walks and look at the things around him. He would record the colors of the trees, the shapes of the clouds, the sound of the birds, and all sorts of other things. He was very curious and enjoyed recording the world.

Today, he went to the park to record things he hadn't seen before. He recorded the colors of the flowers, the speed of a squirrel running across the grass, and the sound of children playing. 

At the end of the day, Sam took off his special jacket and carefully put away his recording device. He smiled, happy to remember the things he had seen and heard. From now on, he would keep the recording in his memory and enjoy the world around him.

Once there was a little girl named Daisy. She was three years old and very curious.

One day, Daisy asked her mom, "Can I bathe in the spring?" Her mom said, "Sure, it will be fun!"

So Daisy and her mom went to the nearby spring. The water was cool and clear. Daisy jumped in and started playing.

Suddenly Daisy tasted something sour! She found a small sour apple that was floating in the spring. She took a bite and made a sour face.

Seeing Daisy's reaction, her mom smiled and said, "Come on Daisy, you need to wash off all that sourness!" So Daisy and her mom splashed around and bathed in the spring until the sourness was washed away.

At the end of the day Daisy was a happy, clean girl. She said goodbye to the spring and together she and her mom went home.

A boy and his mom went to the park. The boy liked to play on the swings and the slide. He saw a big dog with a ball in his mouth. The boy wanted to play with the dog and the ball. He ran to the dog and tried to take the ball.

"Stop, boy, stop!" his mom shouted. "The dog is not yours. He may bite you!"

But the boy did not listen. He grabbed the ball from the dog's mouth. The dog did not like that. He growled and barked. He jumped on the boy and bit his arm. The boy dropped the ball and cried.

"Help, help!" his mom screamed. She ran to the boy and the dog. She tried to pull the dog away. But the dog was too strong. He bit the mom's leg. She fell to the ground and cried.

A man came to help. He was the dog's owner. He was wise. He knew how to calm the dog. He called the dog's name and gave him a treat. The dog let go of the mom and the boy. He wagged his tail and ate the treat.

"I'm so sorry," the man said. "My dog is not bad. He just loves his ball. He thought you wanted to take it away from him."

The mom and the boy were hurt. They had blood on their clothes. They needed a doctor. The man said he would pay for the doctor. He said he was sorry again.

But the mom and the boy were not happy. They were scared and sad. They did not want to play with the dog or the ball. They did not want to go to the park. They wanted to go home. They cried.

Once upon a time there was a little boy called Jack who lived with his Mommy and Daddy. He was very happy but he sometimes worried about things. 

One day, Jack was watching TV when Daddy suddenly said: "Hey Jack! Can you help me make breakfast?" Jack was so excited. He loved helping Daddy do things.

 Daddy showed Jack six boxes of cereal. He asked Jack which one should they have for breakfast. Jack looked at all the cereals and thought really hard about it. But then he noticed one box which looked really brilliant. He knew this must be the one.

So Jack said "this one is brilliant!". Daddy smiled and said: "You're right Jack! That's the one I was going to pick too!". 

Jack was so proud of himself. He had made the right choice and he knew it. Daddy gave him a big hug and they had a wonderful breakfast together. From then on, Jack never worried about making decisions - he knew he was brilliant!

Lila was very happy. She had a new toy. It was a big red car. She wanted to test it. She put it on the floor and pushed a button. The car made a loud noise and moved fast.

"Wow!" Lila said. "This is fun!"

She ran after the car and tried to catch it. But the car was too fast. It bumped into the wall and fell down. Lila picked it up and looked at it. The car had a scratch on its side.

"Oh no!" Lila said. "My new toy is broken!"

She felt sad and started to cry. Her mom heard her and came to see what was wrong.

"What happened, Lila?" her mom asked.

"My new car is broken!" Lila said, showing her mom the scratch.

Her mom hugged her and took the car in her hand. She looked at it and smiled.

"It's not broken, Lila. It's just a little scratch. It's still a good car. It can still make noise and move fast. Do you want to test it again?"

Lila nodded and wiped her tears. She took the car from her mom and pushed the button again. The car made a loud noise and moved fast.

"Yay!" Lila said. "It still works!"

She smiled and ran after the car. Her mom watched her and smiled too. She was glad that Lila was happy with her new toy.

Once upon a time, there was a lazy cat named Tom. Tom had soft, pretty skin. He liked to sleep all day and play all night.

One day, Tom saw a big ball of yarn. He wanted to play with it, but it was stuck on a high shelf. Tom tried to jump, but he could not reach it. He started to struggle, jumping again and again. "I want that yarn!" Tom meowed.

Tom's friend, a little girl named Sue, heard him. She came into the room and saw Tom trying to get the yarn. "Don't worry, Tom. I will help you," Sue said. She got a chair and climbed up. She reached the yarn and gave it to Tom. They both played with the yarn all day long, and Tom was very happy.

Tim and Sam were brothers. They liked to play with their toys in the bathroom. They had cars, trucks, trains and planes. They made loud noises and pretended to crash and destroy things.

One day, Mom said, "Boys, you have to clean up the bathroom. It is very messy. You have to put your toys away and throw away the trash." She gave them a big, heavy bag to use.

Tim and Sam did not want to clean up. They wanted to keep playing. They said, "No, Mom, we are having fun. We will do it later." Mom said, "No, you have to do it now. I will be back in five minutes. If you don't do it, you will be in trouble."

Mom left the bathroom. Tim and Sam looked at each other. They had an idea. They said, "Let's put all our toys and trash in the bag. Then we can hide it under the sink. Mom will not see it. We can play more later."

They started to fill the bag with their toys and trash. They did not know that the bag had a hole in it. They did not see that some of their toys and trash fell out of the bag and onto the floor. They did not hear that Mom was coming back.

Mom opened the door and saw the bathroom. She saw the toys and trash everywhere. She saw the bag under the sink. She saw the hole in the bag. She was very angry. She said, "Boys, what did you do? You did not clean up. You made a bigger mess. You lied to me. You destroyed the bathroom. You are in big trouble."

Tim and Sam looked at Mom. They looked at the bathroom. They looked at the bag. They felt very bad. They said, "We are sorry, Mom. We were trying to be smart. We did not mean to destroy the bathroom. We will clean up now. Please don't be mad at us."

Mom said, "You have to learn to be responsible. You have to do what I tell you. You have to respect the bathroom. It is not a place to play and destroy. It is a place to be clean and safe. You have to help me fix the bathroom. And you have to say sorry to each other. You are brothers. You have to be kind and honest to each other."

Tim and Sam said, "We are sorry, Mom. We are sorry to each other. We will help you fix the bathroom. We will be good boys. We will not play and destroy in the bathroom again."

Mom said, "Thank you, boys. I love you. But you still have to go to your room and think about what you did. And you have to give me some of your toys. You have too many. You have to share them with other kids who don't have any."

Tim and Sam said, "OK, Mom. We understand. We love you too." They hugged Mom and went to their room. They gave Mom some of their toys. They learned their lesson. They never played and destroyed in the bathroom again.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to run fast and play outside. One day, Timmy saw his big brother practicing for a race. Timmy wanted to race too, but he didn't know how.

"Can you teach me how to race like you?" Timmy asked his brother.

"Sure, little brother. First, you need to run as fast as you can," his brother replied.

Timmy tried his best to run fast, but he kept falling down. His brother helped him up and said, "Don't worry, I'm glad you're trying. Keep practicing and you'll get better." 

From that day on, Timmy practiced every day with his brother. He ran faster and faster until one day, he won his very first race. Timmy was so glad that he learned how to race and he thanked his brother for teaching him.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play in her yard. She had an ordinary day, playing with her toys and chasing butterflies. Suddenly, she saw a bird with a broken wing. 

Lily went to her mom and said, "Mommy, I want to help the bird. Can we tie a bandage on its wing?" Her mom smiled and said, "Yes, we can help the bird. Let's go get a bandage."

Lily and her mom carefully tied the bandage on the bird's wing. The bird flew away, happy and healthy. Lily felt proud that she helped the bird. Her mom said, "Lily, it's important to help others when we can. It makes us feel good inside." 

From that day on, Lily always looked for ways to help others. She knew that even an ordinary day could turn into something special if she helped someone in need.

Mia and Ben were playing in the living room. They had many toys and books and cushions to have fun with. They liked to build forts and pretend they were in a castle or a spaceship.

One day, they had a big fight. Mia wanted to use the blue cushion for her fort, but Ben wanted it too. He said it was his cushion and he grabbed it from Mia. Mia got angry and tried to pull it back. They both tugged and tugged until the cushion ripped and the white fluff inside came out.

"Oh no!" Mia and Ben said. They looked at the mess they made. The fluff was everywhere. It scattered on the floor, on the couch, on the table, and on their toys. It looked like snow.

Just then, their mom came in. She saw the ripped cushion and the fluff. She was not happy. She asked Mia and Ben what happened. They both pointed at each other and said it was their fault.

Mom sighed. She told them to stop fighting and to help her clean up. She said they had to be patient and share their things. She said they could fix the cushion later. She gave them a big bag and a broom.

Mia and Ben felt sorry. They said they were sorry to mom and to each other. They hugged and said they were still friends. They worked together to pick up the fluff and put it in the bag. They also put their toys and books back in their places. They learned their lesson. They decided to play nicely and to use the other cushions for their forts. They had fun again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved going on tours with her family. One day, they went on a tour to a beautiful beach. Lily was so excited to play in the sand and swim in the water.

But when they arrived, Lily saw that the beach was very dirty. There was trash everywhere! Lily felt sad and didn't know what to do. Then, her mom told her that they could help clean up the beach. So, Lily and her family picked up all the trash and made the beach clean again.

After they finished, Lily felt happy and relaxed. She learned that it's important to take care of the environment and keep it clean. From that day on, whenever she went on a tour, she made sure to leave the place better than she found it.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named John. He had an old belt which he liked to wear. One day, he noticed the buckle had become very dull. He asked his mom to help him improve the buckle.

"Mom, can you help me to make the buckle shine?" John said.
"Hmmmâ€¦ That's a good idea!" she replied.

So, John and his mom went to the store to get a mild cleaner for the belt buckle. They bought it and went back home.

John was very excited. He carefully followed the instructions to make the buckle shine. He put the cleaner on the buckle and waited for a few minutes. After that, he rubbed off the cleaner and saw his buckle shining brightly.

John was so delighted to see the improvement. He thanked his mom for helping him.

"You're welcome, John. I'm glad it improved the buckle," she said with a smile.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Max and Tom. Max was the more adventurous one, so he would always lead Tom on exciting adventures. 

Today they were going to explore the nearby forest and see what they could find. Max was confident they would have a lot of fun.

As they walked through the forest, Max spotted something in the distance. "Look, Tom! What's that?" Max pointed to a little hut in a clearing.

Tom's eyes lit up. "Let's go take a look!" 

Max approached the hut carefully and he felt curious. What was it? He peaked inside the little window of the hut and saw a table with some fun-looking toys. "This looks like fun," Max said.

Tom walked over to the hut and they both went inside. Max and Tom jumped on the toys and had a lot of fun. 

Max and Tom spend the rest of the day playing in the hut in the clearing. They had an awesome adventure and vowed to come back to the hut the next time they went to explore.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play in the snow. They make a big igloo with snow blocks. They go inside the igloo and pretend they are Eskimos.

"Look, we have a cozy home!" Anna says.

"Yes, and we have a fire and a fish!" Ben says. He points to a red sock and a toy fish.

They laugh and hug. They are happy.

But then they hear a loud noise. It is a snow plow. It is clearing the road. It is coming closer to their igloo.

"Oh no, it will break our igloo!" Anna says. She is scared.

"Quick, let's get out!" Ben says. He is brave.

They crawl out of the igloo and run to the sidewalk. They watch as the snow plow pushes the snow and their igloo away.

They are sad. They cry.

"Hey, don't cry!" a voice says. It is their mom. She is walking to them. She is calm.

"Mom, our igloo is gone!" Anna says.

"I know, honey, I'm sorry. But you can make another one tomorrow. Come on, let's go home. It's cold and dark." Mom says.

She hugs them and takes their hands. They walk home.

"Can we have hot chocolate?" Ben asks.

"Of course, you can. And maybe a cookie too." Mom says.

They smile. They are warm and safe. They love their mom.

Once there was a strong stone. It wanted to stay by itself so it could be alone. But that was hard to do in the forest. Every day an animal would come by and try to move the stone. But the stone was strong and wouldn't budge.

Then one day, a butterfly flew by and asked the stone why it wanted to stay by itself. The butterfly said it would like to be friends with the stone. The stone was very happy.

The butterfly and the stone became great friends. Every day, the butterfly would come to visit and stay with the stone. The stone was so glad that it didn't have to be alone any more. It was strong and would stay with its friend forever.

Once upon a time, there was an intelligent thing that zoomed around. Every day it zipped and sped and raced with joy!

The thing would fly this way and that, above the clouds and over the trees. It loved to explore the world and have fun.

One day, it saw something it hadn't seen before. It was one of the most beautiful and amazing things ever! So the thing zoomed closer and found out it was a small, fluffy puppy.

The intelligent thing was so excited. It zoomed and zoomed around the puppy, who just sat there and watched. Then, it and the puppy started to play and have a wonderful time together!

The thing and the puppy zoomed around the park and laughed and played until the sun set. Then, they both said goodbye until they could meet again.

Once upon a time there was a very curious little girl. She was tiny but her ideas were grand. She wanted to explore the world around her to see if she could discover what made everything so special. 

One day, the little girl got a special present from her parents; a microscope! She was so excited that she shouted: "Look Mom and Dad, now I can look at everything up close!"

The little girl took the microscope outside and looked at all kinds of things; leaves, rocks, dirt and even bugs! Everything was so fascinating.

But then suddenly, the little girl noticed something sparkle in the dirt. She looked closer by using the microscope and she was amazed to find a big diamond!

The little girl shouted: "Mom, Dad! Come here, I found a diamond!" But before she could pick it up, everything around her started to freeze. 

Mom smiled and said: "That diamond must be magic. We better leave it here and keep it safe, otherwise it might freeze everything clean!" 

The little girl nodded and put the diamond back down. She was so happy to have found such an exciting surprise, but she was also glad that the diamond was safe and the world could stay beautiful and clean.

Once upon a time there was a nice mummy bear who had a big jar of jam. One day, she wanted to examine the jam to see if it was nice. So she took the lid off the jar, and had a close look. The jam was sparkling in the morning sun. Mummy bear smiled to herself. She thought that the jam was looking very nice.

Next, mummy bear dipped her paw into the jar and felt the smooth, sticky jam gloop between her furry fingers. She licked her paw, and the jam was delicious! She knew it was nice and that she did not need to examine it any more.

Mummy bear was very happy that her jam was nice. She put the lid back on the jar and went off to play in the sunshine.

The end.

John was a 3 year old. He had a dream to be successful, but he was not sure how to do it. One day, he saw a rainbow in the sky. It seemed to lead him somewhere. So, John followed it. He walked and walked until he reached a rainbow bridge. It was very pretty, but he was a little scared. He looked back, but the rainbow was gone. He decided to go over the bridge anyway. 

On the other side, he found a big castle with a golden door. He opened it up and went inside. Inside he saw a giant staircase and he started to climb it. As he climbed, the stairs lead him to a big room at the top. In the room, there was a shiny star on the floor pointing to a door. John opened the door and he saw a giant golden chest. He opened the chest and inside was a book. He opened the book and it was full of words of wisdom. 

John read the book and he learned how he could be successful. He followed the advice and this lead him to his dream of being successful. John was so happy and he thanked the rainbow for leading him to his dream.

Once upon a time, there was a little car named Beep. Beep loved to spend time with his friends. They would play and laugh all day long. Beep was very happy.

One day, Beep needed oil. He asked his friends where he could find oil. They told him that there was oil in a distant place. Beep was a little scared, but he wanted to be strong for his friends.

Beep went on a long trip to find the oil. He saw many new things along the way. When he finally found the oil, he was very happy. Beep went back home to his friends and they all played together again. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a dependable bug. He liked to scatter around the garden, looking for tasty treats. One day, the bug came across a small boy. The boy was so excited to see the bug, and he began to giggle. The bug was happy to have made a friend.

The bug and the boy would explore the garden every day. The bug showed the boy all the secret places that he liked to hide and scatter in. He was a great tour guide! The boy was happy to have such a dependable friend.

One day, it started to rain. The bug scattered away from the rain drops, but the boy didn't know what to do. He was scared. But then he noticed the bug, waiting for him under a big leaf. The bug had found a safe place to keep them both dry. The boy was so happy.

From then on, the bug stayed close to the boy. Wherever the boy went, the bug was right by his side. They were dependable friends.

Once upon a time, there was a driver who drove a big truck. One day, as the driver drove, he saw two children playing in a dark alley. The driver smiled, and then he started to tease the two children.

The two children just laughed and had fun. They were happy to see the driver. The driver waved and honked his big horn. Then, he drove away into the dark night.

The children continued to play in the dark alley. But they still thought of the driver and they smiled. After a while, they went to sleep happy and warm. The driver had made their day special!

One day, a young girl named Lucy went outside to play. She saw something mysterious that made her stop in her tracks. It was a nail. It seemed like it had fallen from the sky.

Lucy looked around but didn't see anyone else. She picked up the nail and held it in her hand. It felt strange and she was very curious.

Lucy decided to take the nail and dig a hole in her backyard. Maybe she could find more of them. She started digging and soon found another nail.

Lucy was so excited. It seemed like something special was hidden underground and she wanted to find out more. She kept digging, looking for more mysterious nails. 

After a while, she had a whole pile of the nails. Lucy decided to keep the nails in her room. It was a big mystery what the nails were for, but she was glad to have them.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to wear pretty dresses. One day, she saw a new dress in the store. It was so pretty and pink. She wanted it so much.

Lily asked her mom, "Can we get that dress, please?" Her mom replied, "We can't buy it now, but if you save your money, you can gain enough to buy it later."

Lily thought about it and decided to save her money. She did chores around the house and earned some money. After a few weeks, she had enough to buy the dress. She was so happy and couldn't wait to wear it. When she tried it on, she felt so pretty and the dress was so tasty.

There was a little girl called Daisy. She loved to march. One day, her mommy took her to the store. 

"Can I have a radish, please Mommy?" asked Daisy.

Mommy nodded and gave her a regular radish. Daisy was so excited that she started to march around the store. 

All the people in the store stopped and watched Daisy. They smiled and clapped their hands as Daisy marched with her radish. She looked so proud and happy. 

Finally, Daisy and Mommy went home. Daisy kept the radish in her pocket and kept marching. She was so proud of her radish that she marched all the way home. 

The end.

Anna loved to bounce on her bed. She liked how it made her feel high and happy. She bounced every morning and every night, even when her mom told her to stop.

One day, she bounced too hard and too fast. She flew off her bed and hit her head on the wardrobe. It hurt a lot and made a loud noise. She started to cry and hold her head.

Her mom heard the noise and ran to her room. She saw Anna on the floor and the wardrobe with a dent. She was angry and scared. She said in a harsh voice, "Anna, what did you do? You could have hurt yourself badly. How many times have I told you not to bounce on your bed?"

Anna felt sorry and scared. She said in a small voice, "I'm sorry, mom. I just wanted to have fun. I didn't mean to break the wardrobe or hurt my head."

Her mom sighed and hugged her. She said in a softer voice, "I know, honey. But you have to be careful and listen to me. Bouncing on your bed is not safe or good for your bed or your wardrobe. Why don't you bounce on this ball instead? It's much more fun and less dangerous."

She gave Anna a big, colorful ball that she had bought for her birthday. Anna smiled and thanked her mom. She liked the ball and how it bounced. She decided to bounce on the ball from now on and not on her bed. She learned her lesson and was happy.

Lila and Ben went to the zoo with Mom and Dad. They saw many animals, like lions, monkeys, and birds. They liked the animals, but they wanted to see the seals. They liked how the seals jumped and played in the water.

They came to the seal pool and saw a big seal with a ball on its nose. The seal was very good at balancing the ball. Lila and Ben clapped and laughed. They wanted to play with the seal too. They saw a man with a bucket of fish. He was the seal's friend. He gave the seal a fish when it did a trick.

Lila and Ben had some crackers in their pockets. They thought the seal might like some crackers too. They went closer to the pool and offered the seal a cracker. The seal saw the cracker and opened its mouth. But it did not want the cracker. It wanted the fish. It was angry that Lila and Ben gave it a dry cracker instead of a wet fish.

The seal bit Lila's hand and took the cracker. Lila screamed and cried. She dropped the rest of the crackers in the pool. The seal ate them all. Ben was scared and ran away. Mom and Dad came and took Lila to the nurse. The nurse put a bandage on Lila's hand and gave her a hug. Lila was very sad and hurt. She did not like the seal anymore. She wished she never offered it a cracker.

Once upon a time, there was a rich man. He had many toys and candies. He lived in a big house. One day, he saw a little girl. The girl had no toys. The rich man wanted to help her.

He decided to send her a gift. He put a toy and some candies in a box. The box had a handle. The little girl could carry the box with the handle.

The little girl got the box. She was very happy. She played with the toy and ate the candies. The rich man felt good. He was happy to help the little girl. They both had a great day.

Once upon a time there was a bird who wanted to go to a meeting. He put on his delicate coat and flew to the place. He tapped the door with his beak and asked to enter.

"Come in," said a voice.

Inside there were many birds, all of them wearing their delicate coats. The bird said hello to everyone and they all nodded back. 

"Welcome," said an owl. "This is an important meeting. We are discussing how to make the pond a better place!"

The bird was excited, so he nodded his head. They all began to talk about what they could do to help, and it was clear everyone wanted to make a difference.

Then everyone agreed there should be a big clean-up in the pond. They all nodded together.

After the meeting was over, the bird flew away with a happy heart. He knew he had been part of something special and he was proud of the delicate work his friends had all done.

Once upon a time, there was a caterpillar called Bill. He had 8 small legs and loved exploring in the garden.

One day, Bill was walking around when he heard a noise in the bushes. Curious, he crept closer to take a look.

Suddenly, a big, tough frog jumped out from the bushes. Bill was so scared, he blinked his eyes and scurried away.

The frog bellowed "Where are you going? Don't be a scaredy-cat!"

It made Bill feel better as he stopped and said shyly, "I'm sorry, I thought you were scary."

The frog smiled and said, "There's nothing wrong with being scared, just always be brave and face your fear. Everyone gets scared sometimes."

Bill smiled back, thanked the frog, and continued his adventure. He soon realized that sometimes, being brave and facing tough things can be quiet rewarding.

From that day forth, Bill always remembered the frog's advice and faced his fear, no matter how tough it seemed.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named George. He was very excited to be playing in the park. He had promised his mum that he would stay on the swing, so he started to tie the swing to the tree.

George was so excited that he wanted to keep playing. He decided that if he could tie the swing very tightly, he would get a prize. He worked very hard and managed to tie the swing to the tree so it wouldn't move.

When his mum saw his work, she was very proud and gave him a prize. At first George was very happy but then he tasted it, and it was very bitter. He didn't like it and he was sad.

George's mum smiled and said â€œAlways remember that things that come too easily don't always have the same value as things which we have to work hard for.â€

From that day, George learned that it is much better to work hard and earn something, rather than taking shortcuts.

Once upon a time there was a pretty barn. It was lovely and always made the animals around it happy. One day, an animal inside the barn began to spin.

The spinning animal was a pig. He was spinning around and around in circles, showing off his silly moves. The other animals in the barn watched in awe and laughed.

Soon, all the animals in the barn joined in too. They jumped and spun with the pig, until the sun began to set. Each animal was having so much fun.

When the barn had grown dark and all the animals were exhausted, they said goodbye and went to bed. But at this barn there was always a lot of love, thanks to the pretty barn and the animals who spun together inside it. 
The end.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who loved figuring out things. She was very creative. Her parents saw all the happy things she was doing and wanted to give her a special treat. So one day they decided to give her a present.

The present was a big box, with a padlock on it. The little girl was so excited! She quickly asked her parents what was inside. But they just smiled and said she had to unlock it to find out.

The little girl thought and thought about how to unlock the box. She tried many different things but nothing would work. After awhile her parents helped her to solve the puzzle. They showed her how to turn the key and twist it until the padlock clicked open.

When she opened the box, the little girl was so happy! Inside was a brand new toy that she could play with. She was so thankful to her parents for giving her such a creative and special gift.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a big wish to go to the park and play on the swings. Her mommy said they could go, but only if Lily ate all her vegetables. Lily didn't like vegetables, but she wanted to go to the park so she ate them all.

When they got to the park, Lily was so happy. She went straight to the swings and started to swing higher and higher. But then, a big boy came and pushed her off the swing. Lily was upset and started to cry. Her mommy came over and hugged her, but Lily still felt sad.

Suddenly, a bee came and stung Lily on the arm. She cried even more and her mommy took her home. Lily's arm got very swollen and she had to go to the hospital. The doctor gave her medicine, but it didn't help. Lily's wish to play on the swings was ruined and she was very upset.

Once upon a time, there was a jolly crab named Crusty who lived in the ocean. One day, Crusty saw a shiny oyster and wanted to eat it. But the oyster was closed tight and Crusty couldn't open it. He asked his friend, a fish named Finny, "Can you help me snap this oyster open?"

Finny said, "Sure, let me try." Finny tried to snap the oyster open with his teeth, but it was too hard. Just then, a big wave came and pushed the oyster onto a rock. The oyster snapped open by itself! Crusty was so happy and thanked Finny for trying to help. They both ate the oyster together and it was delicious. From that day on, Crusty and Finny were the best of friends.

Lily and Ben like to bake with Mom. They help Mom put flour, eggs, sugar, and butter in a big bowl. They mix and mix with a spoon. Mom says they are good helpers.

Mom gives Lily and Ben some dough to make cookies. They roll the dough with a rolling pin. They cut out shapes with cookie cutters. They make stars, hearts, circles, and animals. Lily makes a hairy lion with raisins for eyes and a nose. Ben makes a palm tree with green sprinkles for leaves and chocolate chips for coconuts.

They put the cookies on a tray and Mom puts the tray in the oven. They wait and wait. They smell something yummy. Mom says the cookies are ready. She takes the tray out of the oven and puts it on the table. She lets the cookies cool down a little.

Lily and Ben are happy. They pick their favorite cookies and eat them. They say the cookies are delicious. Mom smiles and hugs them. She says they are the best bakers. They say they love Mom and they love baking.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in her backyard, where there was a big palm tree. She liked to climb it and pretend she was a monkey.

One day, Lily's mom asked her to help tidy up the garden. Lily didn't want to, but her mom promised her a surprise if she did. So, Lily started picking up toys and putting them away.

As she was cleaning, Lily noticed a small hole in the ground. She wondered what could be buried there. She asked her mom, but she didn't know. Lily decided to investigate.

She grabbed a small shovel and started digging. After a few minutes, she found a small treasure chest buried in the ground! She was so happy and excited. She showed her mom and they opened it together. Inside, there was a beautiful necklace with a palm tree pendant. Lily wore it proudly and promised to always keep the garden tidy so she could find more treasures.

Once there was a girl named Lucy. She was only 3 years old but already an expert at playing in the park. Today, she was playing hide-and-seek with her friends.

Lucy was looking for a great place to hide. She found a tall tree and knelt down behind it so no one would find her. She looked around and smiled because she knew she was safe.

Suddenly, she noticed a clear glove lying on the ground. She reached down and picked it up. It was very shiny, so Lucy decided to wear it and pretend to be like her Mommy.

She put on the glove and started to play with her friends. Every time she found someone, she waved hello with the glove. Everyone thought it was so funny that she had a glove on!

At the end of the day, Lucy thanked her friends for playing with her and took off her glove. She knelt down and said a few words of thanks to the tree for helping her hide so well.

Then she walked home with a big smile on her face, holding the clear glove in her hand.

Once there was a girl named Jane who was three years old. She asked her mom a question, "Mom, where do prunes come from?" Her mom answered her, "Prunes come from a tree." 

But Jane wanted more information and asked, "How do they get prunes off of the tree?" Her mom replied, "Well they have to pick them." 

Jane became more curious and asked, "But how do they pick the prunes?" Her mom explained, "They use a ladder to climb the tree and a big basket to gather the prunes. Then they put the prunes in the basket and bring them down." 

"That's so cool!" Jane said. But when Jane's brother heard her, he was very rude and said, "That's is not cool. That's boring." Jane was sad, but her mom said, "You don't have to listen to your brother. Don't worry, everything is okay."

Jane was happy that her mom was there to answer her questions and make her feel better.

Once upon a time there was a puppy who loved swimming in the sea. Every day the puppy would take a run to the shore and go for a swim.

One day when the puppy was at the shore, a big wave took him away. He was so scared and tried to get back, but he couldn't find a way. He swam and swam and swam, but he couldn't get back to the shore.

The puppy became so frustrated, but he didn't give up. He kept swimming and eventually, he saw the shore in the distance. He paddled and paddled until he made it back to the shore. He was so happy to be back on land and never wanted to leave again. 

The puppy was so pleased to be safe and sound at the shore, that every day he ran to the shore for a swim, but he never forgot his scary adventure.

Once there was a girl who was very uncomfortable. She didn't feel right in her own skin and wanted to go play. But one day, a strange creature appeared with an axe. It made her very scared and she began to weep.

The creature was big and it was coming closer to her. She was too scared to move and just sat there, crying. But suddenly, something happened. A bright light shone from the sky and surrounded the creature. It stopped what it was doing and flew away.

The girl was so relieved! Seeing the creature leave made her happy, and she stopped weeping. She felt safe now, but the axe was still there. She didn't know what it was for and she felt uncomfortable.

The girl picked up the axe carefully and took it home. She showed it to her mom and dad, and they explained that it was a tool to help them cut wood. The girl smiled and was no longer uncomfortable. From then on, she happily played with the axe whenever she went outside.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a favorite dress that was made of soft velvet. She loved to twirl around in it and feel the fabric brush against her skin.

One day, Lily's little brother, Max, accidentally spilled grape juice on her dress. Lily was very frustrated because she loved her dress so much and didn't want it to be ruined.

Max tried to apologize, but Lily didn't want to hear it. She whispered to herself about how upset she was and didn't want to talk to anyone.

But then, their mom came in and helped clean up the stain. Lily realized that accidents happen and forgave her brother. She even whispered to him that it was okay and they hugged it out. From then on, Lily made sure to keep her dress extra safe.

Once upon a time, there was a boy. He wanted to have fun so he went outside. He saw mud and was very excited. He wanted to make things with the mud. He used his hands to make a big yellow ball.

He was so proud of his yellow ball. He started to laugh and he felt happy. He wanted to finish it off with a smiley face on top. He took some of the mud and made two eyes and a smile. It was perfect!

The boy rolled the yellow ball around in the mud. He giggled and was having so much fun. He was happy that he finished his special yellow ball. 

He gave it one last hug and then the boy went inside to get a drink of juice. He was still smiling because he had made the perfect yellow mud ball.

Bobby was running through the garden, looking for something fun to do. He suddenly saw a post that looked very interesting. He slowly walked over to it and was surprised to find a big, yellow blanket covering the post. He immediately wanted to see what was underneath, so he quietly lifted up a corner of the blanket. Underneath, he found a smiling caterpillar for him to play with! Bobby was so excited, he held the caterpillar close to his chest and ran back to the house to show his mom. She smiled at Bobby, and thanked him for finding the caterpillar. Bobby thanked the post for being so quiet and keeping the caterpillar hidden until he could find it.

Danny was in a hurry. He wanted to get to the park quickly and he ran as fast as he could. His mama said they would be late if he didn't hurry up.

When they got to the park, Danny was eager to run and play. He didn't want to wait any longer. But his mama said he had to be patient. She told him that his friends were coming soon.

So Danny sat down on the bench to wait. He was patient, but it was hard. All he wanted was to play with his friends. He wished for them to hurry.

Suddenly Danny saw them running down the street. They were hurrying just like him. He couldn't wait any longer and ran to meet them. He was so eager to start playing with them.

Danny's mama smiled. She was glad that Danny had been so patient. Finally he could have fun with his friends.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who loved jugs. She had one big jug and one small jug. One day she went to the river and found a jug. It was made of clay and it was colourful. She decided to take it home.

When she arrived home, she opened the jug. Inside it was sour juice. She didn't like the taste, but she thought that maybe she could use the jug for something else. She thought about keeping it as a toy.

But the little girl's brother wanted the jug too. He grabbed it and wouldn't let her have it. She got mad and tried to take it away from him. They fought and fought until finally the jug broke. The jugs fell on the floor and the sour juice splashed everywhere.

The little girl was sad and started to cry. She had lost her special jug and it was all her brother's fault. He got in trouble, but she was still very sad. She would never get to play with her jug again and nothing could help her feel better. She wished she hadn't opened the jug at all.

Once upon a time, there was a brave boy called Bill. He wanted to help the people in his village and was determined to do this. Every day, he would try something new.

One day Bill had an exam. He was feeling very mysterious because he didn't know what this exam was or what to expect. Bill tried his best and hoped he would do well. 

When Bill got his results, he realised that this exam had been to reach out to the people in his village and help them in any way that he could. Bill was so happy and excited to be able to help the people he loved. 

Bill spread the word and soon everyone in the village was doing their bit to help each other. Everyone was smiling and happy because their lives were getting easier.

Moral of the story: Bill taught us that everyone can help others, no matter how small. Help make the world a better place!

John was a three year old boy. He was playing outside in his yard when he saw a farmer. The farmer was standing in the middle of the field, pointing one way and then another.

John asked the farmer, "What are you doing?"

The farmer replied, "I'm looking for my sheep. They have gone off into the rough parts of the field."

John asked if he could help, and the farmer said yes. They began walking around the field, pointing and looking for the sheep. After a while, John and the farmer spotted the sheep in the distance. The farmer was so happy and thanked John for helping. 

John was proud of himself. He had helped the farmer find his sheep.

It was spring time and the trees were full of life. A little girl was playing in the park when she noticed a bird on a branch. She wanted to try to fly like the bird, so she jumped up and down with all her energy. But no matter how hard she tried, she just couldnâ€™t make it to the branch. 

Her parent saw her and knew she was frustrated. So they asked her what she was trying to do. She said she wanted to fly like the bird, but she just couldnâ€™t reach it. Her parent looked up at the branch and smiled. 

They said, "Let's try something else. Why don't you try jumping on my back?". The little girl was confused at first, but then she smiled and jumped on her parentâ€™s back. With a boost from her parent, she was able to spring up and reach the branch. She was so excited, she couldnâ€™t believe she was so close to a real bird!

Joey was playing in the garden one day, when he noticed something strange. His neighbour, Maggie, had a special box. It was shaking and rattling, as if it had something inside.

Joey approached Maggie and asked, "What's inside the box, Maggie?".

Maggie smiled, and said, "It's a secret, Joey! I'm not allowed to tell anyone".

Joey was feeling a bit stubborn, so he followed Maggie around, asking her over and over again to tell him the secret.

Finally, Maggie had had enough. She opened the box, and said, "Look inside, Joey, it's a beehive! They sting, so you mustn't go near them!"

Joey was amazed. He watched the bees buzzing around in the box and thanked Maggie for letting him see her secret.

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play together. They had many toys, but their favorite was a big teddy bear. They called him Mr. Fluffy and gave him many hugs every day.

One day, their mom took them to the doctor for a check-up. The doctor was a nice lady who smiled and talked to them. She looked at their eyes, ears, and mouth, and listened to their heart and lungs. She said they were very healthy and brave.

But then, she took out a needle and said they needed a shot. Lily and Ben did not like needles. They were scared and cried. They did not want a shot. They wanted to hug Mr. Fluffy.

"Please, don't cry," the doctor said. "The shot will only hurt a little bit, and then it will be over. It will help you stay healthy and strong. You can hug Mr. Fluffy after the shot, okay?"

But Lily and Ben did not listen. They ran away from the doctor and hid under a table. They hugged Mr. Fluffy and said they did not want a shot. They were very grumpy and did not listen to their mom or the doctor.

The doctor and their mom tried to find them and calm them down, but they could not. They were too fast and too loud. They knocked over a lamp and a chair and made a big mess. They made the doctor and their mom very angry and sad.

They did not get their shot, but they also did not get to go home. They had to stay in the doctor's office until they said sorry and behaved. They missed their lunch and their nap. They were hungry and tired and still scared. They wished they had listened to the doctor and their mom. They wished they had been brave and not grumpy. They wished they had a better day.

Harvey was a young boy who wanted to fly like a bird. He wanted so badly to be able to soar over the clouds. So one day, after school, he went to his parents and asked them if they could get him a red jacket with wings. 

At first, his parents were taken aback. Harveys dad shook his head, but his mom smiled and said, "Let's see if we can find anything like that, Harvey." 

So Harvey and his mom drove to the store. When they got there, his mom found him a nice red jacket with special wings sewn onto it! "Here you go," she said.

But when he put the jacket on, he frowned. Nothing was happening! He had expected to be able to fly. 

His mom saw Harvey's disappointment and said, "Come here, honey. Let me tell you something. Have faith that if you truly want something, you can get it. Just focus on it and keep working hard, you'll get there. We'll always be here to encourage you, no matter what." 

Harvey saw the look of love in his mom's eyes. He smiled and said, "Thanks, mom!" 

With new courage, he spread his arms out wide and imagined himself flying. He was ready to take on the challenge.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lucy. She had a special journal that she liked to take with her everywhere. One day, an awful storm came. It was so terrible! Lucy was scared, so she took her journal and hugged it really tight.

The storm was really wild, with lots of roaring and booming. But Lucy felt safe, because she had her journal with her. She looked outside and saw the rain coming down. Lightning lit up the sky!

Soon the storm was over, and Lucy was so happy. She opened her journal and drew a picture of what she had seen. Then she wrote about the storm in her journal. She couldn't believe how terrible it had been, but she was so glad she had her journal with her.

Once upon a time, there was a rare bird with a special style. The bird had pretty colors and could sing beautiful songs. Everyone loved to watch and listen to the bird.

One day, the bird was flying high in the sky when it saw a little cat stuck in a tree. The bird wanted to help the cat. So, the bird flew down to save the cat.

The bird sang a soft song to make the cat feel better. Then, the bird gently picked up the cat with its strong feet. The bird flew down and put the cat safely on the ground. The cat was so happy to be saved by the rare bird with a special style. They became best friends and played together every day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the park with her friends. One evening, she went to the park with her mom.

Lily's mom bought her a sweet ice cream cone. Lily loved it so much that she didn't want to share it with anyone. Her friend, Timmy, asked her if he could have a lick. Lily didn't want to lie to him, so she told him the truth. She said, "I don't want to share my ice cream."

Timmy was sad, but he understood. He said, "That's okay, Lily. Maybe next time you can share with me." Lily felt bad for not sharing her ice cream, so she decided to give Timmy a little bit. Timmy was happy and they played together until it was time to go home. The end.

Tom is sick. He has a fever and a cough. He lies in a bed in a big room with other sick kids. A nurse comes to see him. She wears a white dress and a black hat. She has a kind face and a soft voice.

The nurse gives Tom some medicine and a glass of water. She checks his temperature and listens to his chest. She says he will get better soon. She smiles and tells him a story about a brave lion and a clever mouse.

Tom likes the story. He feels a little better. He asks the nurse if he can do something. She says he can fold some paper. She gives him some colorful paper and shows him how to make a bird, a flower, and a boat. Tom tries to fold the paper like the nurse. He makes a bird, a flower, and a boat. He is proud of his work.

The nurse praises Tom for his folding. She says he is very smart and creative. She puts his paper bird, flower, and boat on his bedside table. She says they will make him happy and remind him of the story. She says she has to go and see other sick kids, but she will come back later. She kisses Tom on the forehead and says goodbye.

Tom waves to the nurse. He likes her. He thinks she is very nice and helpful. He looks at his paper bird, flower, and boat. He feels happy and hopeful. He thinks he will get better soon. He closes his eyes and falls asleep.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She went to the movies with her mom and dad. They sat in the back row of seats. Lily loved sitting in the back row because she could see everything!

During the movie, Lily spilled her popcorn all over the floor. Her mom said, "Oh no, Lily! That's a terrible mess!" Lily felt sad, but her dad said, "Don't worry, we'll clean it up after the movie."

After the movie, Lily and her family went to the front row to ask the movie theater worker for a broom. The worker said, "Sure, I'll get you one." Lily said, "Thank you!" and her mom said, "That was very kind of you." They cleaned up the popcorn and went home happy.

Once upon a time there was a little lion. Everywhere the lion went, he roared. He roared when he was happy, he roared when he was sad, he even roared when he was mad! 
The little lion loved the evening the most. He loved the way the sun sparkled in the sky. He loved the birds singing and the wind blowing. But most of all, he loved how a little quieter it got when the sun went down.

But one night, something was different. Instead of being quiet, the night was noisy and busy. Everywhere the lion looked he could see people walking around. 

The little lion was confused. Then, he heard a familiar sound - it was a big lion roaring! 

The little lion was so excited and he ran to find the big lion. When he found the big lion, he saw it was the king of the jungle! 

The little lion was nervous, but he roared back. The king of the jungle smiled and roared back. 

The little lion was so happy to have found the king of the jungle. They roared back and forth until the sun came up again. From then on, the little lion never missed an evening in the jungle!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to draw and write in her journal. One day, Lily's mom asked her to pour some milk into her cereal bowl. But Lily was careless and spilled the milk all over the table.

"Oh no, Lily! You need to be more careful when you pour the milk," said her mom.

"I'm sorry, Mommy," said Lily. "I'll clean it up."

Lily grabbed a towel and wiped up the milk. Then, she went back to writing in her journal. She wrote about the milk spill and how she learned to be more careful. From that day on, Lily was very careful when she poured things.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who liked to play pretend. One day she found a funny jellyfish in the ocean. She thought it was so funny that she wanted to keep it and take it home with her.

But the jellyfish didn't want to leave its home in the ocean. It swam away when the little girl tried to catch it. She had to try again and again but the jellyfish kept swimming away!

The little girl got sad. She wanted the jellyfish to be her pretend friend. But it seemed as though the jellyfish did not want to be her friend. 

The little girl thought and thought. Then she had an idea! She filled up her pool with some water from the ocean. The jellyfish was so happy to see its home again that it swam into the pool!

The little girl and the jellyfish became the best of friends. They played pretend all day long. The little girl was so happy that she had her funny jellyfish friend!

Once upon a time, there was a rabbit who needed some food. He searched around for something to eat but he couldn't find anything. He was getting very hungry and started to feel sad.

Suddenly, he saw a zipper on the ground! He hopped over and opened it with his fuzzy little paws. Inside the zipper was lots of yummy food!

The rabbit was very excited! He gobbled up the food and the zipper stretched and stretched as he ate. It was very flexible!

The rabbit was full. He thanked the zipper and scurried away. The zipper lay there on the ground, happy to have fed the rabbit.

Once upon a time, there was a big engine. It was very loud and impressive! One day, a clever boy wanted to learn about the engine. He asked his mom for help.

His mom said "today, we will read about the engine". The boy found it very exciting. He sat on his chair and started to listen. His mom read to him about the engine. It was a very noisy machine that could do lots of amazing things. 

The boy thought it was amazing. He asked lots of questions and wanted to learn more. His mom smiled and kept reading. He asked so many questions that soon they had read all day! 

When it was time to go to bed, the boy said. "Mom, the engine was very impressive". His mom smiled and said, "Yes, the engine was very impressive - and so are you".

Ben and Mia were playing with clay. They liked to make shapes and animals with the clay. They had a big box of clay and many tools to cut and roll and squeeze the clay.

"Look, I made a snake!" Mia said, holding a long green clay snake. "It can bite you!"

"No, it can't!" Ben said, laughing. "It's just clay. I made a lion. It can roar and eat your snake!"

He showed Mia his clay lion, which had a big mouth and a mane. He made it roar and moved it towards Mia's snake.

Mia was scared. She did not like Ben's lion. She did not want it to eat her snake. She grabbed a tool that looked like a measure. It had numbers and a pointy end. She wanted to poke Ben's lion and make it go away.

"Stop it, Mia!" Ben said, seeing what she was doing. "That's not a toy, that's a measure. You can hurt me or the lion with that!"

But Mia did not listen. She was angry and afraid. She poked Ben's lion with the measure. The measure went through the clay and hit Ben's hand. Ben screamed. It hurt a lot. Blood came out of his hand.

Mia dropped the measure. She saw what she had done. She felt sorry and scared. She started to cry.

Ben's mom heard the scream and the cry. She ran to the room. She saw Ben's hand and the measure and the clay. She was very angry and sad. She picked up Ben and took him to the bathroom. She wrapped his hand with a cloth. She called the doctor.

She looked at Mia with a harsh face. She said, "Mia, you did a very bad thing. You hurt Ben with the measure. You could have hurt him more. You are not allowed to play with clay or tools anymore. You have to go home now. I will tell your mom what you did."

Mia felt very bad. She wanted to say sorry to Ben and his mom. But they did not want to talk to her. She had to go home with her mom. She did not have any friends to play with. She did not have any clay to make shapes and animals. She was very sad and lonely. She wished she had not poked Ben's lion with the measure.

Once upon a time, there was a frog named Fred. Fred was very adventurous and loved to hop around in the forest. One day, Fred saw a big juicy fly on the other side of the pond. He wanted to eat it, but he didn't want to get wet. So, he had an idea. He saw a big leaf and decided to use it as a boat to get across the pond.

But as he was speeding across the pond, a mean snake named Sam saw him and wanted to eat him for dinner. Sam started chasing Fred, but Fred was too fast for him. Fred made it safely to the other side and ate the big juicy fly. He was very happy that he was able to be both adventurous and smart to avoid the mean snake. From that day on, Fred was known as the bravest frog in the forest.

Once upon a time, there was a pumpkin who wanted to have some fun. He hopped to the middle of the field and shouted, "Who wants to play?"

A bird in a tall tree overhead chirped, "I do!" So the pumpkin invited the bird to play a game.

The pumpkin said, "Let's clap together, 1,2,3!" So they both clapped and laughed.

The bird said, "My wings are too small, but my beak is long. I'll use it to roll the pumpkin!"

So the bird used his beak and the pumpkin rolled across the grass. They laughed and played all afternoon. 

At night, the bird said goodbye and flew away. The pumpkin waved and said, "Come back soon!" He watched until the bird was gone, then said, "That was fun!" He said it again, louder this time. "That was fun!" 

The pumpkin clapped his hands together, feeling happy and content. And he stayed there in the field, still clapping long after the bird had gone.

Once upon a time there was an adorable little girl. She loved to go for walks in her garden. One day, when she was walking, she heard a loud noise. She looked around and saw a flying bird. She felt so excited and she wanted to shoot it.

So she picked up her toy gun and pointed it at the bird. But when she shot something else flew out of the gun. It was a lemon!

She was surprised but she didn't mind. She picked up the lemon and ran back inside and showed it to her mum. Her mum was so happy, and cut the lemon into slices. Then she gave a slice to the little girl.

The little girl took a bite and was surprised. It was so yummy! She remembered that day and loved lemons ever since.

Once upon a time, there was a little mouse. He was so small and smooth. He always loved to explore and create things.

One day, the mouse decided to build something special. He gathered some wood and started putting it together. He worked so hard, and when he was finished, he was so proud of himself! 

He had made a little boat. With a smile on his face, he hopped in and began to sail the boat. He splashed around in the water, having the time of his life.

Just then, he heard a voice calling from the edge of the pond.

â€œOh, mouse! Youâ€™ve done a great job creating that boat. You must be so proud of yourself!â€
