John watched a bug crawl across the grass. He was careful not to hurt it. His mom smiled as she watched him.

Mom picked up the little bug and put it inside her case. She explained that it would be safer inside.

John was upset. He wanted the bug to stay outside and play. He began to cry.

Mom gave John a hug, and she sighed. She said that she was sorry, but it was safer inside the case.

John smiled. He still missed the little bug, but he understood why mom was being so careful.

John and mom hugged again. Mom thanked John for understanding, and they went on to play some more.

Once there was a little girl named Joy. She was three years old and she loved to play. One day she decided to go to a yoga class with her mom.

When they arrived, everyone spread out their mats and got ready to do yoga. Joy watched intently as the teacher talked. He told them to be gentle and to not move too fast.

Joy did her best to follow the instructions. She found the poses heavy, but they made her smile because she was trying to do them just like the others.

After the class was finished, Joy and her mother talked. Joy said, "I really like yoga, Mom! It was so much fun!"

Joy's mom smiled and said, "That's great, Joy. I'm glad you enjoyed it!" 

They both continued to talk and then headed home. Joy felt happy, strong and ready for her next yoga class!

Once upon a time, there was a very cheerful little sock. Every day, he would race around the house, bringing smiles and laughter with him wherever he went!

One day, he decided to go outside and play. He quickly skipped and jumped around the garden. But then his foot got very dirty, making the once happy and cheerful sock look sad.

Not wanting to stay dirty for long, the sock quickly ran back inside. There, he saw a big, soft cloth lying by the door. The sock smiled. He knew what to do!

So the sock grabbed the cloth and began to wipe his foot. The soft cloth's touch was just like magic; it made the sock's foot clean again!

Happy and cheerful once more, the sock thanked the cloth and went on his merry way, ready to bring smiles and laughter once again!

Once upon a time there was a special stick. It was lucky, because it had special power. One day, some friends were playing together when they found the stick. They were so excited and they each held it. 

Suddenly, an old man appeared. He said that the stick was magical and that it would reveal the answer to one lucky person. He asked the friends to close their eyes, and to each make a wish.

The old man told them to open their eyes. One of the friends was lucky - the stick had revealed that their wish had come true! Everyone was so excited. The old man said goodbye and vanished.

The friends all kept playing with their new lucky stick. They were so happy that the stick had revealed the lucky person's wish!

Jack woke up feeling very restless. He was itching to go outside and explore. He pulled on his coat and ran to the door. Suddenly he saw something glowing on the ground - it was a pin! He picked it up, and it seemed to be ringing. Jack was so excited - he had never seen a ringing pin before. He held it up to his ear and heard a cheerful tune jingling from it. He shook it and he danced around the room to the music. 

Soon, Jack's mom came home and saw him dancing with the pin in his hand. She laughed and said, "That pin is magical! Wherever you go, it will always ring for you." Jack thanked her with a big smile and ran off to explore the world outside. Wherever he went, Jack always had his magical ringing pin with him.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to ride her tricycle every day. One day, she went for a ride and noticed her pedals were shaking. She stopped and looked down. 

Lily said, "Mommy, my pedals are shaking. It feels uncomfortable." 

Her mommy said, "Let me take a look." She saw that one of the pedals was loose. She tightened it and said, "Try it now." 

Lily got back on her tricycle and pedaled away. She smiled and said, "Thank you, Mommy. It feels much better now."

Once upon a time there were two friends, Jack and Jill. Jack and Jill went up the hill to play a game. The game was silly. Jack and Jill took turns pushing a big button. Every time they pushed the button they would separate.

Jack shouted: "Let's try again!" So they took turns pushing the button again. This time the button spun them around and around until they were dizzy.

Jill giggled and said: "That was so silly!" 

Jack laughed and said: "Let's try the button one more time!" So they pressed the button again and this time it sent them soaring high into the sky!

Jack and Jill flew around, but eventually the button sent them back down to the ground. They were safe and sound, but something was different this time.

Jack and Jill were no longer together. The button had separated them! But it was all worth it in the end, because a silly game can bring people together in the most unexpected of ways.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. Her name was Jane. She liked to draw with her pen. One day, the pen became dull. She was sad and crossed her arms.

Mommy noticed and said, "Don't be sad, Jane. Maybe I can help with your pen." Jane smiled and nodded.

Mommy told her to wait and came back with a brand new pen. Jane was so excited that she almost forgot it was dull.

Mommy said, "Let's draw together. It will be more fun that way." Jane smiled and hugged her mommy.

Together, they drew a beautiful picture. Mommy said, "See Jane, I told you that your new pen would come in handy."

Lily and Ben were friends who liked to play in the garden. One day, they saw a big red strawberry on a green plant. They wanted to eat it, but it was too high for them to reach.

"Let's use a stick to get it," Ben said. He found a long stick and tried to poke the strawberry. But the stick was too heavy and he dropped it.

"Let's use a chair to climb up," Lily said. She dragged a small chair from the porch and put it near the plant. She climbed on the chair and reached for the strawberry. But the chair was too wobbly and she fell down.

"Are you okay?" Ben asked. He helped Lily get up and dusted off her dress.

"I'm okay, but I still want the strawberry," Lily said. She looked around and saw a butterfly. It was yellow and black and very graceful. It flew over the plant and landed on the strawberry.

"Look, a butterfly!" Lily said. She pointed at the butterfly and smiled.

"Maybe the butterfly can help us," Ben said. He had an idea. He whispered to Lily and they nodded.

They went to the butterfly and said, "Hello, butterfly. You are very pretty and graceful. We like you very much. Can you please share the strawberry with us? We are very hungry and we have no other fruit."

The butterfly looked at them and fluttered its wings. It was very kind and generous. It said, "Hello, children. You are very polite and friendly. I like you very much too. Of course I can share the strawberry with you. There is enough for all of us."

The butterfly moved aside and let Lily and Ben pick the strawberry. They thanked the butterfly and broke the strawberry in three pieces. They each ate a piece and gave the last piece to the butterfly. It was very sweet and juicy.

They all enjoyed the strawberry and became good friends. They played in the garden until the sun went down. They said goodbye to the butterfly and went home. They were very happy and grateful.

Once there was a grumpy monster. Every night he would climb up to the ceiling, looking for something to protect. He watched over the house while everybody was sleeping.

One night, a little girl was playing in her room. She was having so much fun, she didn't see the grumpy monster on the ceiling. The monster saw the little girl and knew he had to protect her. He jumped down and flew over to her.

The little girl was scared at first. But the monster spoke in a gentle voice,
"Don't be scared. I'm here to protect you."

The little girl smiled and thanked the monster for looking after her. From then on, the grumpy monster and the little girl were friends. He would always watch over her so she could play without worry. The grumpy monster had finally found something to protect.

Once upon a time, there lived a little girl. She loved going outside to play in the sun. One day, the sun was shining so brightly and everything was so warm.

The little girl excitedly started to run around. She ran so fast she got dizzy, then fell to the ground.

But then, to her surprise, she felt something cold. She looked down and saw the ground was covered in snow. The little girl gasped.

She quickly ran to her mom and said, "Mommy, there's snow outside! Can we go play?"

Her mom chuckled and said, "Yes, but we have to grab a sack first."

So they went outside and gathered up the snow in a sack. The little girl was so excited that she twirled around and around, making a mini snow storm. 

They took the sack home and put it near the fireplace. The little girl wanted to play with the snow all day, and her mom said she could do just that.

So the little girl spent the day playing with the snow until the sack was empty. It was cold but still so much fun!

Once upon a time, there was a polite crab. The crab lived in the sea. The crab had many friends.

One day, the crab met a new friend. The new friend did not know how to play. The crab wanted to help the new friend.

The polite crab showed the new friend how to play. They played all day. They had lots of fun. The new friend was happy. The polite crab was happy too. They were best friends forever.

Once upon a time, there was a big factory. In the factory, there were many people working. They made toys for kids to play with.

One day, a bossy man came to the factory. He demanded, "Make more toys now!" The workers were sad because they were tired. But they did not want the bossy man to be mad, so they worked harder.

A kind worker saw that everyone was sad. She said, "Let's take a break and be happy." The workers took a break and played with the toys. They laughed and had fun. The bossy man saw this and realized he was wrong. He said, "I am sorry. Let's all be happy and work together."

From that day on, everyone in the factory was happy. They made toys and had fun. The moral of the story is that being kind and working together makes everyone happy.

Tom was sad. He did not like school. He missed his mom and dad. He did not have any friends. He sat alone in the corner with his folder. His folder had pictures of his family and his dog. He looked at them and felt a little better.

But then a loud noise made him jump. It was a big boy who kicked a ball. The ball hit Tom's folder and made it fly away. The big boy laughed and ran away. Tom felt angry and scared. He wanted his folder back. He cried and cried.

Lily saw Tom crying. She felt sorry for him. She was a kind girl. She liked to help others. She went to Tom and said, "Don't cry. I will help you find your folder. Come with me." She took Tom's hand and led him to the ball. She picked up the ball and threw it back to the big boy. She said, "That was not nice. You should say sorry to Tom. He is sad because you took his folder." The big boy looked ashamed. He said, "Sorry, Tom. I did not mean to hurt you. Here is your folder. I hope you are okay." He gave Tom his folder and walked away.

Tom smiled and hugged his folder. He said, "Thank you, Lily. You are very nice. You comforted me. You are my friend." Lily smiled and hugged Tom. She said, "You are welcome, Tom. You are very brave. You are my friend too. Let's play together." They went to the playground and played happily.

The moral of the story is: Be kind to others and they will be kind to you. Don't be mean or hurtful. Comfort those who are sad and lonely. Friendship is a precious gift.

John had a big day planned for today. His mom said he was going to a park. He put on his shoes and ran to the door.

John's mom said. "We have to Catch an ambulance!"
John said, "Ambulance? For the park?"

His mom smiled and said, "No, for a special surprise. We're going to a very Rich place where we'll have lots of fun!" 

John was excited. The ambulance drove for a long time, and when it stopped John saw a beautiful castle! John said, "This is a Rich place!"

John and his mom had a great time. They played games, went on rides, and saw lots of amazing things.

By the end of the day, John was tired but happy. He thanked his mom for taking him to a Rich place. His mom smiled and said, "Let's Catch the ambulance and go home."

Once upon a time, there was a bear. He was very tough and he liked to protect his meals. One day, he was eating his dinner in the woods, when a little bunny hopped up to him. The bunny said "Hello! Can I have a bite of your dinner?". The bear shook his head and said firmly "No, this is my meal and I want to protect it". The bunny said "But I'm so hungry!". 

The bear thought for a moment and then he said "I'll tell you what. I'll give you half my dinner. If you promise to leave the other half for me". The bunny thanked the bear and said "Ok, I promise". The bear gave the bunny half the meal and the bunny enjoyed it a lot. 

The bear said "I'm glad I protected my dinner and I'm happy that I shared with you". The bunny said "Me too, thank you for being so tough but kind". Then they both hopped off into the sunset.

Once upon a time, there was a brave rabbit. He had a nice, warm mitten to keep his hand nice and toasty. One day, he dared to go outside on a cold day. He shivered as the cold wind blew against his mitten. He hopped around through the cold snow.

Then, he saw a scary bear. The bear was huge and had big claws! The brave rabbit was scared, so he just stood still. He wanted to run away, but he was too scared. Suddenly, he had an idea. He opened his mitten and waved it in the air.

The brave rabbit shouted, â€œGo away, bear!â€ The bear was confused and ran away! The brave rabbit cheered, feeling very proud. His mitten was a big help! He hopped home to his warm burrow, never to forget his big dare on a cold day.

Once upon a time, there lived a boy called Joey. He was three years old and lived in a small house with his mom and dad. 

One day, Joey's mom said "It's time to get ready to go, Joey!"

Joey replied, "I don't want to dress!" 

His mom said, "Don't make me shut the door! You need to put on your dress. It will only take a few moments."

Joey still didn't want to get dressed, so his mom said, "Listen here, young man. I'm being very persistent about this. You need to put on your dress now!"

Finally, Joey relented and put on his dress. His mom smiled and gave him a hug.

The End.

Once upon a time there was a modern pit. All the animals hated it. One day a rabbit said to a fox, â€œWe should do something about this awful pit.â€

The fox replied, â€œWhat can we do? Weâ€™re too little and the pit is too big.â€

The rabbit thought for a moment. Then he said, â€œLetâ€™s get the other animals together and see if we can push it away.â€

The fox smiled. â€œI like that idea. Iâ€™ll get everyone together.â€

The fox ran to the other animals and told them the plan. They were all excited to help out. So they all pushed on the pit. After a lot of hard work, they moved the modern pit away from their home.

Everyone cheered. The animals were so happy they never had to see that pit again. They all lived happily ever after. The End.

Once upon a time, in a big forest, there lived a gentle crane. The crane had many friends. One day, the crane's best friend, a tiny mouse, came running to him. The mouse was sad.

"Help me, crane!" said the mouse. "A big cat took my food. I have nothing to eat and I am hungry."

The gentle crane wanted to help his friend. So, he went to the big cat and asked, "Please give the food back to the mouse. He is very hungry."

The big cat laughed and said, "No, I will not give it back. I will eat it all."

The gentle crane had an idea. He told the big cat, "If you give the food back, we will celebrate with you. We will have a big party!"

The big cat liked the idea of a party. So, he gave the food back to the mouse. They all had a big party together and celebrated. The mouse was happy, and they all became friends.

Tom and Anna are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big tree with many red apples. They want to pick some apples to eat.

"Let's count how many apples we can pick," Tom says.

"OK," Anna says. "You pick from this side, and I pick from that side. Then we count together."

They start to pick apples. Tom picks one, two, three, four, five apples. Anna picks one, two, three, four apples. But then she sees a little bird on a branch. The bird is hurt. It cannot fly.

"Tom, look!" Anna says. "There is a little bird. It needs help."

Tom looks at the bird. He sees that it is hurt. But he also sees more apples.

"Let's pick more apples first," Tom says. "Then we can help the bird."

"No, Tom," Anna says. "The bird is more important than the apples. We have enough apples. We should help the bird now."

Anna puts down her apples. She climbs up the tree. She gently takes the bird in her hands. She brings it down. She finds some water and some seeds. She gives them to the bird.

The bird drinks the water and eats the seeds. It feels better. It chirps happily. It thanks Anna. It flies away.

Anna smiles. She is happy. She helped the bird.

Tom looks at his apples. He feels bad. He was greedy. He did not help the bird.

"I'm sorry, Anna," Tom says. "You were right. The bird is more important than the apples. You are a good friend."

Anna hugs Tom. She forgives him. She says, "It's OK, Tom. You can still be a good friend. Next time, let's help others before we pick apples."

They share their apples. They eat them together. They are happy. They learned a lesson. They learned to be kind and generous.

Once upon a time, there was a group of animals who lived in the forest. They were all friends and liked to play together. They loved to run and jump and climb trees. One day, they heard about a big party that was going to happen in the forest. The party was going to be very popular and many animals were going to attend.

The animals wanted to go to the party too, but they didn't know how to get there. They decided to ask the wise old owl for help. The owl told them that they needed to follow the river and then turn left at the big rock. The animals listened carefully and thanked the owl for his advice.

The day of the party arrived and the animals all dressed up in their best clothes. They followed the owl's directions and finally arrived at the party. There were lots of animals there, dancing and singing. The animals were having so much fun that they didn't even notice when a big storm came. Suddenly, the wind started to blow and the trees began to bow. The animals were scared, but they remembered what the owl had told them. They all huddled together and waited for the storm to pass. When it was over, they realized that they had become even closer friends. From that day on, they knew that they could always count on each other, no matter what happened.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she went to the park with her mom. She was very hungry and her mom gave her a yummy sandwich to eat. But Lily saw a bird and wanted to share her sandwich with it. 

Her mom said, "No, Lily. The bird can't eat your sandwich. It's not good for them." 

Lily didn't listen and threw some bread to the bird. Suddenly, a bigger bird came and snatched the sandwich from Lily's hand. 

Lily was sad and her mom said, "That's why we should never waste our food or give it to animals. They have their own food to eat." 

Lily learned her lesson and promised to never waste her food again. She also learned that sometimes when we do something wrong, bad things can happen, like when the bigger bird shot away with her sandwich.

Once upon a time there was a field. It was green and very big. In the middle of the field was a surprise. It was a flower! It was so pretty and it was the biggest flower anyone had ever seen. It was very impressive. 

As the flower stood in the field, it started to grow bigger and bigger. It's petals got wider and it's stem got longer. But suddenly the flower started to shrink. It got smaller and smaller until it was the size of a tiny baby flower. 

Everyone gathered around the flower to see what had happened. The flower was shrinking even smaller as they watched. Suddenly, the flower disappeared! It was gone. Everyone was so amazed. They had never seen anything like it. 

And that is the story of the impressive shrinking flower in the big green field.

Mum and Tommy were in Tommyâ€™s bedroom. Tommy was looking for an elephant toy. He saw the elephant on the shelf. It was big and wide. It had a pink trunk and two big ears. Tommy asked his mum: â€œCan I decorate the elephant?â€ 

Mum said: â€œYes, you can.â€ 

Tommy took paints and crayons. He painted the elephant's body green and yellow. He added some orange spots. He drew a big smiling face on the head. Mum said â€œThat looks very nice, Tommy!â€

Tommy said: â€œI love my elephant!â€ 

Mum hugged Tommy and said: â€œI love you too.â€

Once upon a time, in a modern house, lived a boy named Tom. He had a wild dog named Spot. They loved to play outside in the sun.

One day, Tom and Spot went to the park. They saw a big tree. Tom wanted to climb the tree, but Spot wanted to play with a ball. So, Tom threw the ball for Spot to catch.

When Spot ran to get the ball, he saw a wild cat. Spot wanted to play with the cat, but the cat didn't want to play. The cat was scared, and it bit Spot. Spot cried, and Tom ran to help him. They went home, but Spot was hurt and sad. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a kind fox who loved to go on adventures. One day, he met a little rabbit on the trail. "Hello there! What are you doing?" asked the fox. "I'm trying to find my way home. I'm lost," replied the rabbit. "Don't worry, I'll help you," said the fox.

So, the fox and the rabbit walked together on the trail. Suddenly, the rabbit saw a beautiful flower and wanted to pick it. "Wait, don't pick that! It's better to leave it there and let it lay," said the fox. "Why?" asked the rabbit. "Because if you pick it, it won't be able to grow anymore," replied the fox.

Finally, after a long walk, they found the rabbit's home. "Thank you so much for your help," said the rabbit. "No problem, it was my pleasure," said the fox. And from that day on, they became good friends and went on many more adventures together.

Once upon a time there was a little boy called Charlie. Charlie was three years old, and he loved to imagine the coolest things.

One day, Charlie was in the kitchen with his mom. He saw one of the cabinets open, and he gasped with excitement. Inside was a mixer! 

Charlie said, "Mom, what is a mixer?" 

His mother replied, "It's a special machine that helps mix things together. What would you like to make with it?" 

Charlie thought for a few moments and then said, "Let's make something spicy!" 

His mother smiled and carefully opened a cupboard. She pulled out some onions, peppers, and some spices. Charlie imagined how delicious it would taste.

His mother helped him put the ingredients into the mixer, and she pressed the button. The mixer began to whir and the ingredients all blended together. 

When the mixture was done, it looked and smelled great. Charlie and his mom tasted it, and it was the most delicious and spicy thing they'd ever eaten!

Once upon a time there was a big fire in a town. Everyone was really scared. They didn't know what to do.

Suddenly, a brave fireman came and saved the town. He sprayed water on the flames, and the town was saved.

That night, there was a big wake to celebrate the brave fireman. Everyone ate foods that were spicy and thanked the fireman for saving their town.

The next day, all the children were so excited to thank the fireman. Everyone was so happy that the town was safe.

The fireman smiled and thanked everyone for their kind words. He said he was happy that he was able to save the day. Everyone cheered and thanked the brave fireman again!

Once upon a time there were two friends, Joey and Tiny. They liked to skip together every day. One day, Joey wanted to go to the opera but Tiny selfishly said no. Feeling sad, Joey decided to go to the opera by himself and skip all the way there.

When Joey arrived, the opera was just beginning. He was so excited! He skipped up the stairs and into the theater. Inside, it was beautiful.

Joey skipped all the way to his seat and watched the opera. He clapped and cheered in excitement. As the night went on, Joey forgot all about his selfish friend.

The opera was so much fun that Joey stayed late, skipping all the way home afterwards. He couldn't wait to come back and be amazed by the opera once again.

The end!

Once upon a time, there was a boy who was very hungry. Everywhere he looked, people had food and he did not. He asked his mommy and daddy what he could do, but they told him he had to wait. He was sad, but he understood.

One day, his mom and dad took him to a farm. He saw a lot of wheat growing in the fields and he was amazed. He saw a machine that was harvesting the wheat and knew what he had to do. He asked his mom and dad if he could go get some wheat. They said yes and he ran to the wheat field.

He started to pick the wheat and put it in a bag. As he filled the bag up, he felt more and more happy inside. After he finished collecting the wheat, he took it home. He, his mom and dad made bread with all the wheat.

When he tasted the bread, his hunger was gone and he felt good. He smiled and thanked his mommy and daddy for helping him find the wheat. From that day, he knew that when he felt hungry, he could find a way to increase his food!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily was very tired and needed a nap. She asked her mommy if she could nap under the big tree in the park. Her mommy said yes and told her to be careful.

Lily fell asleep and had a dream about a friendly bunny. The bunny was very compassionate and helped her find her way back home. When she woke up, she saw that her mommy was gone. She looked around and saw a scary man. The man was not compassionate and took her away.

Lily was very scared and cried for her mommy. She wished she had never taken a nap under the big tree.

John was running in the park with his mom. He saw a huge plate. He thought it was very strange. He wondered why there was a plate in the park. 

John's mom asked him, "Do you want to touch it?" He shook his head yes and ran over to the plate.

John touched the plate and it made a loud noise. It scared him and he ran back to his mom. His mom laughed and said, "Let's see if something else happened." 

John and his mom ran back over to the plate and saw that there was now a big pile of cookies. 

John was very excited! He ran over to the plate, and starting eating the cookies. He was so happy he had found such a huge plate of cookies.

Once upon a time, there was a caterpillar. The caterpillar was very hungry and wanted to eat a lot. One day, he found a big green leaf and started eating it. The caterpillar ate and ate until he was very full. 

After he ate, the caterpillar started to feel very cool. He began to wiggle and move around in a funny way. His friends saw him and thought he was behaving very silly. 

But the caterpillar didn't care, he was just happy to be full and feeling cool. He continued to wiggle and move around until he was tired and fell asleep. The end.

Once upon a time there was a family. They wanted to have dinner so they looked at the menu. It had lots of different kinds of food. The mom wanted to try something new, so she chose one of the special things on the menu. The dad wanted something normal so he chose something he could recognize.

When their meals arrived, the mom and dad were excited to eat. But when they tasted their food, they were even more excited. It was delicious! They were able to complete their meal and were really happy they tried something new. 

After they finished their meals, they decided to get something else on the menu. The mom went with something special again and the dad chose something normal. They were both happy with their choices and completed their meal with a smile. 

The family was so glad they looked at the menu. They had a wonderful dinner and were full and happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to play with his toys at home. He had a very strong toy, a big red ball. Tim liked to play with the ball every day.

One sunny day, Tim went outside to play with his big red ball. He bounced it high in the sky and kicked it far. He ran, jumped, and laughed as he played with his strong ball.

After a long day of play, Tim went back home. He was tired but happy. He knew that tomorrow, he would play with his big red ball again. And every day, Tim and his strong ball had lots of fun together.

Once upon a time there was a hairy monster who lived under a mountain. The monster was so naughty that the other animals were scared of him. One day, the monster wanted to escape from the mountain, so he bit through the stone walls. Suddenly, a jail appeared in front of him. The monster was so scared that he forgot about freedom and ran back inside the mountain.

The next day, the monster saw a mouse walking by. The monster jumped out and said, "Please, mouse, will you help me escape this jail?" 

The mouse replied, "If you promise not to bite me, I will try to help you."

The monster agreed and the mouse guided him out of the jail and back to the mountain. From then on, the monster was careful not to bite anyone anymore.

Tom and Lily are friends. They like to play with their scooters in the park. One day, it is very cloudy and windy. Tom and Lily do not care. They put on their coats and hats and go to the park.

They ride their scooters on the path. They go fast and slow. They make turns and jumps. They have fun. They see a big puddle. It is wet and shiny. Tom has an idea.

"Let's go through the puddle!" he says to Lily. "It will be fun!"

Lily is not sure. She thinks the puddle is too big and too wet. She does not want to get dirty and cold.

"I don't know, Tom," she says. "The puddle is very wet. Maybe we should go around it."

Tom laughs. He is not afraid of the puddle. He wants to try something new.

"Come on, Lily," he says. "Don't be scared. It will be fun. I will go first. You can watch me. Then you can guess how wet I will be."

Tom rides his scooter to the puddle. He goes very fast. He splashes into the puddle. The water goes up and down. It covers Tom and his scooter. He comes out of the puddle. He is very wet. He smiles.

"Wow, that was fun!" he says. "Look at me, Lily. I am very wet. Can you guess how wet I am?"

Lily looks at Tom. She sees the water on his coat, his hat, his face, his hair, his shoes, his socks, his scooter. She shakes her head.

"I can't guess, Tom," she says. "You are too wet. You are the wettest thing I ever saw. You need a towel."

Tom laughs. He does not mind being wet. He likes the puddle. He wants to go again.

"Come on, Lily," he says. "It is your turn. Don't you want to try? It is fun. You will like it."

Lily thinks. She looks at the puddle. She looks at Tom. She looks at her scooter. She makes a decision.

"OK, Tom," she says. "I will try. But only once. And then we go home. And we get dry. And we have hot chocolate."

Tom claps. He is happy. He likes to share his fun with Lily. He waits for Lily. Lily rides her scooter to the puddle. She goes slower than Tom. She splashes into the puddle. The water goes up and down. It covers Lily and her scooter. She comes out of the puddle. She is wet. She smiles.

"That was fun, Tom," she says. "You were right. I liked it. But I am wet. Can you guess how wet I am?"

Tom looks at Lily. He sees the water on her coat, her hat, her face, her hair, her shoes, her socks, her scooter. He nods.

"I can guess, Lily," he says. "You are wet. But not as wet as me. You are a little wet. You need a towel, too."

Lily laughs. She agrees with Tom. She is wet, but not as wet as him. She likes the puddle, but not as much as him. She is glad they are friends. They ride their scooters to their homes. They get towels. They get dry. They have hot chocolate. They are happy.

Lily and Max are furry cats who live in a big house with a nice lady. They like to play and nap and drink milk from a bowl. Sometimes they chase mice or birds in the garden, but they are careful not to hurt them.

One day, Lily and Max hear a loud noise from the kitchen. They run to see what it is. They find a big dog who has knocked over the trash can and is eating the scraps. The dog is not furry, he is hairy and smelly. He growls at them and shows his teeth.

"Go away, dog!" Lily says. "This is our house, not yours!"

"Meow!" Max agrees. He puffs up his tail and hisses.

The dog does not listen. He keeps eating and making a mess. Lily and Max are scared and angry. They want to drink their milk, but they are afraid of the dog.

They see the nice lady coming down the stairs. She sees the dog and the trash and shouts.

"Bad dog! Get out of here!" She grabs a broom and chases the dog out of the door. She closes it and locks it.

She turns to Lily and Max and smiles. She picks them up and hugs them.

"Good cats! You are so brave and smart!" She says. "I'm sorry the dog scared you. He was a stray, he must have been hungry. But he can't come in here and make trouble. This is your home, and you are my pets."

She puts them down and fills their bowl with fresh milk. She strokes their fur and says.

"Here you go, my furry friends. Drink your milk and be happy. I love you very much."

Lily and Max purr and lick her hand. They drink their milk and feel safe and warm. They are glad the dog is gone and the nice lady is here. They are quiet and calm. They snuggle up together and take a nap.

Jonny was a 3 year old who loved going to the park. Today Jonny was so excited to go to the park and play with his friends. He hopped out of the car and ran to the playground. Jonny found a big brown dull slide and went down it.

Next, Jonny spotted a bright yellow swing set. He jumped onto the swing and had so much fun going up and down. Suddenly he saw something on the ground. It was a big spoon filled with butter! Jonny put some of the butter on his finger and licked it. It was so yummy!

Then Jonny ran around the park with his friends. He went on the slide, the swings and the monkey bars. Finally Jonny said goodbye to his friends and went home. He couldn't wait to come back to the park again.

There was a happy family of polar bears. One day the parents saw a big igloo. They thought it would be the perfect home for their little family so they moved in.

One day, it snowed outside and the family was warm and cozy in their igloo. The mom and dad were both very dependable. They were thankful for their new home.

The little bear was excited to have an igloo to play in. He played in the snow and thanked his parents for his home.

The family was so thankful for their warm, dependable igloo. They were happy and stayed in their igloo for a very long time!

Mina and Thomas were best friends. They lived in the same town and went everywhere together. One day, Mina had an idea. She wanted to explore the mysterious hills near their home.

"Thomas, do you want to come with me? I hear there are secret advetures," said Mina.

"Yes! That sounds exciting," Thomas replied.

So the two of them packed a picnic and decided to go to the hills. They were so beautiful. Mina and Thomas hiked along the terrain and collected rocks and leaves. They even found a cave.

When they returned, they told everyone about their journey. Each one had a different opinion, but they all agreed that it was a mysterious place. From then on, when Mina and Thomas asked to explore the hills, their parents just smiled.

Dave was an eager dancer. He loved to move around and do flips. Every day he practiced his moves. One day, he decided to try something new. He tasted a strange looking fruit. It had an odd taste, but he liked it. Suddenly, Dave felt sick. His head spun, and he dropped to the ground. The fruit was poisonous, and Dave couldn't get the help he needed. He lost feeling in his body and died shortly after. Dave's eager dancing came to a sad end.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Kim. She was three years old and had bright, twinkling eyes.

Kim wanted to explore the world, so she started walking down a path. It felt like a distant journey already!

Suddenly, she saw a cell. It was small, with tiny little doors on it. Kim's eyes twinkled even brighter as she ran towards it.

"What's this?" Kim asked.

A voice from inside the cell replied, "I'm a rabbit! Can you please squeeze my door open?"

Kim used all her little fingers to try and squeeze the door open. After a few tries, she finally did it and the rabbit ran away to freedom.

Kim laughed with joy and gave one last tiny squeeze to the door before going back on her distant journey.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to explore the park and play with her toys. One day, she saw a stranger sitting on a bench. The stranger looked kind and smiled at her. Lily felt a little scared but also curious. 

She decided to approach the stranger and say hello. The stranger introduced himself as Mr. Smith and offered her a cookie. Lily was hesitant at first, but the cookie smelled so tasty that she couldn't resist. Mr. Smith admired her bravery for talking to a stranger and they chatted for a while. 

As Lily was about to leave, Mr. Smith told her a secret. He said that there was a hidden treasure in the park and only the bravest and kindest children could find it. Lily was excited and went on a treasure hunt. She searched high and low until she found a shiny box. Inside, there was a note that said, "Congratulations, you are the bravest and kindest child in the park. You have earned my admiration." Lily smiled and felt proud of herself. She realized that sometimes, talking to strangers can lead to amazing adventures.

The sun rose in the sky. Jack was so excited to see it. His mommy told him that they were going on an adventure. Jack saw a thick automobile outside his house. He ran outside with a big smile on his face.

Jack sat in the automobile and it started moving. He looked out the window and saw a lot of things. Jack was very happy, he was so curious. Everything felt new and exciting.

After a while, Jack started to feel tired. He felt his mouth open wide, then he heard a loud yawn. Jack was tired but he didn't want to miss anything. He looked out the window and stayed up for a little longer. 

Finally, Jack curled up and closed his eyes. He was so warm in the thick automobile that he fell asleep almost instantly. 

The next morning, Jack woke up and opened his eyes. They were back at home and the adventure was over. Jack smiled, feeling refreshed and ready for his next adventure.

One day, Tim went to the park with his mom. They took a cooler with yummy food inside. Tim was happy to play and eat at the park.

While playing, Tim saw a big, scary dog. He did not know what to do. Tim started to panic. He ran to his mom for help.

Mom told Tim not to worry. She said the dog was nice and not scary. They opened the cooler and gave the dog a treat. Tim and the dog became friends and played together.

Tim and Kim were twins who liked to play with their toys. One day, they found a big jar of beans in the kitchen. They wanted to use the beans to make a picture on the floor.

"Look, I can make a sun with yellow beans!" Tim said.

"I can make a flower with red beans!" Kim said.

They had fun with the beans until Mom came in. She saw the mess on the floor and was not happy.

"Tim and Kim, what are you doing?" Mom asked. "You need to remove the beans from the floor right now. They are not toys. They are food."

Tim and Kim did not want to remove the beans. They liked their picture. They said, "No, Mom, we want to play with the beans. They are pretty."

Mom was not glad. She said, "No, you have to listen to me. The beans are for dinner. If you don't remove them, you will not get any dessert."

Tim and Kim did not like that. They loved dessert. They looked at each other and decided to remove the beans. They picked up the beans and put them back in the jar. They said, "Sorry, Mom, we will not play with the beans again."

Mom was glad. She said, "Thank you, Tim and Kim, for removing the beans. You are good children. Now you can have some dessert."

Tim and Kim were glad too. They hugged Mom and said, "Thank you, Mom, for the dessert. We love you."

They ate their dessert and then played with their toys. They did not touch the beans again. They learned their lesson.

Once upon a time there was a car. The car was slow and it made the driver feel sad. The driver said, "I wish I could make my car go faster."

The driver's friend said, "I have an idea, let's try to improve your car!"

The driver was so happy. The friend and the driver began to work on the car. First, they made sure the wheels were tight. Then, they put some new oil in the engine so it would run better.

When they finished, the driver started the car to see how it ran. The car roared to life and drove faster than before. The driver and his friend were so happy!

The driver said, "I knew we could improve my car!" They were both so proud of their work. Now the driver can get where he needs to go faster.

Once upon a time there was a girl who loved ice-cream. Her favorite flavor was chocolate. She always had the best scoop of ice-cream in her hand. One day, the girl went outside to play. It was a sunny day, so she decided to play with the sand. She built a beautiful sandcastle. As she was playing, a big wave came and destroyed her sandcastle. She was very sad.

The girl's dad saw that she was sad and he bought her an ice-cream cone to make her happy. She ate it with a big smile. The girl felt much better after eating her ice-cream cone.

The girl decided that she wanted to do something useful with her ice-cream. She thought of a great idea! She gathered all the neighborhood kids and asked them for their sand toys. She then used the ice-cream to fill in the sandcastle.

The kids were so excited to see their sandcastle filled with ice-cream. They had lots of fun playing in it and eating the ice-cream. The sandcastle was just as beautiful as before, full of tasty, useful ice-cream.

Ben and Mia are playing in the backyard. They have a small table and some cups and plates. They pretend they are having a tea party.

"Would you like some more tea, Mia?" Ben asks, holding a cup.

"Yes, please, Ben. You are a good server," Mia says, smiling.

They sip their pretend tea and chat about their toys and pets. They hear a noise at the gate. It is the mailman. He has a big bag of mail.

"Hello, Ben and Mia. I have some mail for you," the mailman says, waving.

"Mail for us? Wow!" Ben and Mia say, running to the gate.

The mailman gives them each a colorful envelope. They have stickers and drawings on them.

"Who are they from?" Ben asks, curious.

"They are from your grandma and grandpa. They live far away, but they love you very much. They wrote you some letters and sent you some pictures," the mailman explains.

"Thank you, mailman. You are very nice," Mia says, grateful.

"You're welcome, kids. Have fun reading your mail. And be careful with the scissors," the mailman says, leaving.

Ben and Mia run back to their table. They open their envelopes with scissors. They find letters and pictures inside. They see their grandma and grandpa smiling and waving. They read their letters out loud. They say they miss them and they are proud of them. They also send them some jokes and riddles.

"Grandma and grandpa are very funny," Ben says, laughing.

"They are also very serious. They say we have to be good and listen to our mom and dad," Mia says, nodding.

"We will, grandma and grandpa. We love you too," Ben and Mia say, looking at the pictures.

They put their letters and pictures on their table. They finish their tea party. They hug each other. They are happy. They have mail.

Tom and Sam are brothers. They like to play outside in the sun. The sun is bright and warm. It shines on their faces and makes them happy.

One day, they see a big cow in the field. The cow is brown and has spots. It is eating grass. Tom and Sam want to pet the cow. They run to the fence and call the cow.

"Hello, cow! Come here, cow! We want to say hi!" they shout.

But the cow does not come. It is too lazy. It keeps eating grass and does not look at them. Tom and Sam are sad. They think the cow is rude.

"Maybe the cow is hungry," Tom says. "Maybe it wants some beef."

Sam thinks that is a silly idea. He knows that cows do not eat beef. Beef is meat. Cows are meat. Cows do not eat themselves.

"No, Tom. Cows do not eat beef. That is yucky. Cows eat grass. That is what they like," Sam says.

Tom does not believe him. He thinks that beef is yummy. He likes to eat beef with his mom and dad. He thinks that the cow would like it too.

He has an idea. He runs to the house and gets a piece of beef from the fridge. He brings it back to the fence. He holds it out to the cow.

"Look, cow! I have beef for you. It is tasty. Try it, cow. You will like it," he says.

But the cow does not try it. It does not like it. It sniffs the beef and makes a loud noise. It sounds like "Moo!" It sounds like "No!"

The cow turns away from Tom and walks to the other side of the field. It does not want to be near him. It does not want his beef.

Tom is confused. He does not understand why the cow does not like his beef. He thinks that the cow is weird.

Sam laughs. He thinks that Tom is funny. He knows that the cow is smart. He knows that the cow knows what is good for it.

He hugs Tom and says, "Don't worry, Tom. The cow is not mad at you. The cow is just different from you. The cow likes grass. You like beef. That is okay. We can still be friends with the cow."

Tom smiles. He thinks that Sam is right. He thinks that the cow is not so bad. He thinks that the cow is just lazy.

He says, "Okay, Sam. I understand. The cow is lazy. But it is still cute. Maybe next time, we can bring it some grass. Maybe then, it will come and say hi."

Sam nods. He thinks that is a good idea. He thinks that the cow will like that. He thinks that the sun will shine on them and make them happy.

Once there was a little pig called Curly. He was so excited as today he had been invited to the amazing slide. All he wanted to do was just slide and slide! He was so happy.

On the way to the slide Curly noticed a large plate of meat. He asked his mum, "Can I have some of that delicious meat?". His mum said no and explained if he had some he wouldn't be able to enjoy the slide. 

So, Curly kept walking and reached the slide. He looked up, saw the amazing slide and quickly hopped on. He just wanted to slide and slide! 

Curly was having so much fun on the slide, he didn't notice the plate of meat sitting next to the slide. He spent lots of time having the time of his life sliding up and down. The hours passed and Curly suddenly noticed it was dark outside. He suddenly remembered he hadn't had dinner yet. He was so hungry.

But sadly, it was too late. Curly had spent all day on the slide and his mum had already gone home. He would have to wait until morning to have dinner.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lizzie. She was only three years old, but she loved to explore.

One day, Lizzie was in her backyard when she came across a small, fragile island. It was perfect for exploring! She quickly scampered onto the island and began to explore.

Suddenly, Lizzie noticed that the island was starting to move! She was so surprised and asked, "What is happening?"

Her dad was watching her from the backyard and said, "It looks like you found a magical island, Lizzie! You can slide it!" 

Lizzie smiled and said, "Really? Cool!" She then grabbed the island and happily slide it across the grass. She had so much fun exploring her own little island. 

The end!

Once upon a time, there was a little child. She was happy and carefree and loved playing with her toys. One day, she heard a strange sound coming from outside her home. The child rushed out to investigate and, to her surprise, saw a dead bird on the ground. She was scared and her heart began to beat fast. 

Suddenly, a big splash of water appeared and a lot of green leaves floated around her. It was the river and it seemed like it was rushing quickly. The child was too scared to move, but then she saw another child coming from the other side of the river. The other child ran to her and with a big smile, said "Don't be scared, it's just the river." 

The two children started playing with the leaves and soon they were laughing and splashing in the river. The little child was no longer scared. From then on, the two of them were best friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toy tank in the sandbox. One day, Timmy's mom told him it was time to go inside for lunch. Timmy was sad because he wanted to keep playing. 

As they walked inside, Timmy's mom said, "Don't worry, Timmy. We can come back and play later. But we have to close the sandbox so the sand doesn't blow away." 

After lunch, Timmy was patient and waited for his mom to finish her work. Finally, they went back outside to play. But when they got to the sandbox, they saw that it was already closed. Timmy was sad again. 

But then, his mom opened the sandbox and revealed a surprise. She had filled it with even more sand and some new toys for Timmy to play with. Timmy was so happy and thanked his mom for being so kind and patient with him.

Once there was a little boy named Joe. He loved to play with his toy box. He had all sorts of fun stuff inside. One day, Joe wanted to hide something in the box. He really wanted to keep it secret. 

So Joe put his orange victory flag inside the box. Then he closed the flaps and smiled.

Suddenly, he heard his mom's voice calling him. 
"Joe! Come find me!" she said.

Joe smiled, his secret was safe. He ran off to find his mom and show her something else. But little did he know, his mom had already found the victory flag. 

When Joe came back, his mom was holding the flag. She said "I found your victory flag! It looks like you were trying to hide it. Why Joe? 

Joe just smiled and shrugged his shoulders. He was happy that his mom knew about his victory flag, and was even more happy that he was able to keep it a secret.

Once there was a boy called Jack. He was only three years old. One day Jack went for a walk with his mom. They walked and walked until they came to a tall tree. Jack was happy because the tall tree was his favorite. 

Suddenly, Jack realized he couldn't hear anything. He looked around and saw that everything was silent and still. He felt strong and happy in the silence.

"Mommy," he said, "it's so quiet here." His mom smiled and said, "That's why it's so special." Jack understood and enjoyed the silence for many minutes.

When it was time to go, Jack was sad. But he knew he'd come back one day and realize the silence again.

Once there was a boy who was very eager to go outside. He looked out the window and saw that the sun was shining. He quickly put on his bathrobe and ran outside. He saw a butterfly and he followed it as it flew away. The butterfly fluttered around the garden, stopping at strange flowers. The boy followed as it flew up high and around. The boy followed the butterfly until it flew out of sight. He had a lot of fun and was very happy. He went inside, took off his bathrobe, and went to bed with a big smile on his face.

Emmy was a 3 year old girl who had a secret. She kept it hidden in a special place. She wanted to keep it safe and no one else knew about it.

One day, Emmy was sitting in her room and trying to work out a way to make her secret even more hidden. As she thought, her lip started to twitch. She had an idea!

Emmy got up and grabbed a special box. She took off the lid and put her secret inside. She used her imagination to decorate it and make it even more hidden.

When she finished, Emmy looked at her secret box with a smile on her face. Even if someone found it, they would have to really work to uncover her secret.

Once upon a time, there was a silly little alien who lived on a planet far, far away. The alien loved to sleep all day and all night. One day, the alien decided to go on an adventure to explore the other planets in the galaxy. 

The alien traveled through space and visited many planets. On one planet, the alien met a friendly creature who liked to dance. On another planet, the alien saw a giant volcano that erupted with fire and smoke. 

But after many adventures, the silly little alien started to feel homesick. The alien missed their cozy little bed and decided to go back home to their planet to sleep. And so, the alien traveled back through space to their planet and slept happily ever after.

Lila and her mom went to visit Auntie Rose, who lived in a big house with many rooms and things. Auntie Rose was wealthy, which meant she had a lot of money and could buy whatever she wanted. Lila liked Auntie Rose, but she did not like her house. It was too quiet and cold and boring.

"Can I play with your toys?" Lila asked Auntie Rose.

"Of course, dear. They are in the guest room upstairs. You can take whatever you like," Auntie Rose said. She smiled and sipped her coffee, which was a hot drink that grown-ups liked.

Lila ran upstairs and found the guest room. There were many toys on the shelves and in the boxes, but they were all old and dusty and not fun. Lila looked for something that she could play with, but she did not see anything that she liked. She felt sad and lonely.

She saw a big ball on the floor. It was red and shiny and looked new. Lila picked it up and bounced it on the carpet. It made a soft sound that Lila liked. She bounced it harder and harder, until it flew up in the air and hit the ceiling. It came down and hit a lamp, which fell over and broke. Lila gasped and dropped the ball.

She heard footsteps on the stairs. It was Auntie Rose, who had heard the noise. She came into the room and saw the broken lamp and the ball. She frowned and looked at Lila.

"What have you done, Lila?" she asked. She sounded angry and scared.

Lila felt sorry and scared too. She did not mean to break the lamp. She wanted to say sorry, but she could not find the words. She started to cry.

Auntie Rose put down her coffee and hugged Lila. She said, "It's okay, Lila. It was an accident. I'm not mad at you. I'm sorry I left you alone. Do you want to come downstairs and have some cookies with me and your mom?"

Lila nodded and wiped her tears. She said, "Yes, please. I'm sorry, Auntie Rose. I love you."

Auntie Rose smiled and said, "I love you too, Lila. Come on, let's go." She took Lila's hand and led her downstairs. Lila felt better and hoped that Auntie Rose would still like her. She decided that she did not like the big house, but she liked Auntie Rose. She liked cookies too.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She loved to collect things. Her favorite thing to collect was pinecones. Every time the girl went outside, she would look for brown pinecones and put them in her pocket.

One day, the girl went to a park. She looked and looked, but she couldn't find any pinecones. Suddenly, she saw something in the distance. What was it? It was a big pine tree. The girl squealed and ran to the pine tree. She was so excited!

The girl looked up at the pine tree. It had so many brown pinecones! She couldn't believe her eyes. She quickly began picking and collecting the pinecones. She put as many as she could into her pocket.

The girl finished collecting the pinecones and ran home to show her mom. She was so happy with her new collection. She couldn't wait to go back to the park and find the next set of brown pinecones!

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play in the kitchen. They see a big sink with water and soap. They want to make bubbles.

They climb on a chair and reach for the sink. They turn on the tap and see the water come out. They put their hands in the water and feel the soap. They laugh and splash each other.

But the chair is weak. It breaks under their weight. They fall to the floor with a loud bang. They hit their heads and cry. They are hurt and scared.

Mom hears the noise and runs to the kitchen. She sees Anna and Ben on the floor. She sees the water and the soap. She sees the broken chair. She is angry and sad.

She picks up Anna and Ben and hugs them. She says, "You are naughty. You should not play with the sink. You could have drowned. You could have died. You made a big mess. You are in trouble."

She takes them to their room and puts them in their beds. She says, "You have to stay here until I say so. You have to think about what you did. You have to say sorry."

She leaves them alone and closes the door. Anna and Ben are still crying. They hug each other and say, "We are sorry. We did not mean to be bad. We just wanted to have fun. We love you, Mom."

But Mom does not hear them. She is busy cleaning the kitchen. She is too upset to talk to them. She does not hug them back. The end.

Lily liked to play with her blocks. She had many blocks of different colors and shapes. She could make towers, houses, trains and more. She liked to make patterns with her blocks. She put red, blue, red, blue, or circle, square, circle, square.

One day, she was playing with her blocks in her room. She made a long pattern with her blocks on the floor. She was very proud of her pattern. She wanted to show it to her mom. She ran to the door and yelled, "Mom, come see my pattern!"

But when she came back, she saw that her pattern was gone. Her little brother, Ben, had come into her room. He had knocked down her blocks and scattered them everywhere. He was laughing and clapping his hands. He liked to make noise with the blocks.

Lily was very angry. She yelled, "Ben, you ruined my pattern! Go away!" She pushed him away from her blocks. She tried to fix her pattern, but she could not remember how it was. She felt sad and frustrated.

Mom heard Lily and Ben yelling. She came into the room. She saw the mess of blocks and the tears on Lily's face. She hugged Lily and said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I know you worked hard on your pattern. It's not nice of Ben to destroy it. He is too little to understand. He just wanted to play with you."

She picked up Ben and said, "Ben, say sorry to Lily. You can't take her blocks without asking. You can play with your own toys." She gave him a kiss and took him to his room.

She helped Lily to pick up her blocks. She said, "Lily, why don't you make a new pattern with me? We can use different colors and shapes. We can make it deep and high. It will be fun." She smiled and gave her a kiss.

Lily nodded and smiled. She said, "OK, Mom. I love you. Thank you for helping me." She took some blocks and started to make a new pattern with Mom. She forgot about her old pattern. She was happy again.

Once there was a cool mine. It was filled with glittering treasures. One day, three little birds flew in. They loved the mine so much! They started to sing. Their sweet songs echoed through the tunnels. Everyone in the mine could hear them.

The birds sang louder and louder, filling the air with their happy sounds. Everyone in the mine was so glad to have them. They loved the birds and their singing.

Everyone worked together to make the mine even cooler. They used the treasures they found to build staircases and bridges. Everyone had laughter and fun in the mine.

The three little birds were happy too. They flew around the mine, singing proudly. They were so thrilled that the treasures were now part of their home.

And from then on, the birds could sing and the mine stayed cool.

Once upon a time there was a famous van. It was special because it could take people all around the world. One day, a little 3 year old boy saw the van and was so excited that he ran up to it. He put his hand on the warm side of the van and it trembled beneath his touch. The boy couldn't believe the van was real. He thought it was magical and he wanted to go for a ride! So the boy asked his mom to help him get inside. She smiled and opened a door for him. The boy couldn't believe his luck and hopped right in. His mom said goodbye and off he went, traveling around the world in the famous van. The little boy had the best adventure of his life!

The big blue sky was shining high up above. The sun was high and strong. 

Lily was sitting in her chair in her garden when she noticed that a bird was caught in the branches of the big tree. She went to help him. With both hands, she lifted the heavy branches and the bird flew out, chirping and singing.

Lily then went to the garden shed. She opened the door and there saw a lollipop. She quickly picked it up and put it in her pocket.

On the way back, it started to rain. The rain made Lily's hair and clothes wet.

Lily called out loudly "Mom! I'm wet!" Her mom came out and said: "Here, you can have this umbrella. Now, you won't get wet!"

Lily smiled. She put the lollipop in her mouth and lifted the umbrella. She laughed and started to run around in the rain.

Sara and Ben are twins. They like to play in the park. They like to swing, slide and run. They have fun with their friends.

One day, they go to the park with their mom. The sun is bright and warm. They see some flowers. They are yellow and pink and purple. They smell good. Sara and Ben want to pick some flowers for their mom.

They run to the flowers. They see a big bee. It is black and yellow. It buzzes loud. It looks angry. Sara and Ben are scared. They do not like bees. They think bees can hurt them.

The bee flies to Sara. Sara screams. She springs away from the bee. She runs to her mom. The bee follows her. Ben sees the bee. He wants to help Sara. He picks up a stick. He swings the stick at the bee. He misses. The bee flies to Ben. Ben screams. He springs away from the bee. He runs to his mom. The bee follows him.

Sara and Ben reach their mom. They hug her. They cry. They tell her about the bee. Their mom is kind. She hugs them. She tells them not to be afraid. She tells them the bee is gone. She tells them the bee was not mean. She tells them the bee was just doing its job. She tells them the bee makes honey. She tells them honey is sweet and good.

Sara and Ben stop crying. They look at the flowers. They are still pretty. They ask their mom if they can pick some flowers. Their mom says yes. She says they can pick some flowers, but they have to be careful. She says they have to watch out for bees. She says they have to respect the bees. She says the bees are not their enemies. She says the bees are their friends.

Sara and Ben nod. They understand. They say sorry to the bee. They say thank you to the bee. They pick some flowers. They give them to their mom. Their mom smiles. She says they are beautiful. She says she loves them. She says they are brave. She says they are smart.

Sara and Ben smile. They feel happy. They feel proud. They go back to play. They have fun. They do not see the bee again. They do not mind. They know the bee is busy. They know the bee is happy. They know the bee is their friend.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird. The bird lived in a cage with bars. The cage was in a room with a window. The bird liked to stare out the window. It was easy for the bird to see the trees and the sky. 

One day, a little girl came into the room. She saw the bird in the cage and felt sad. She wanted the bird to be free. The girl opened the cage and the bird flew out the window. The bird was happy to be free and the girl was happy too. They both stared at each other for a moment before the bird flew away.

Sophia and her mom were looking for their house when they noticed a wolf nearby. As Sophia looked on with wide eyes, her mom explained, "That wolf is impressive Sophia; it must have been wandering around here for a while".

At that moment, the wolf ran up to them and sat down in front of Sophia and her mom. Sophia couldn't believe her eyes and whispered, "Mommy, what does it want?". Her mom smiled and explained, "Maybe it just wanted us to admire how impressive it is".

Sophia was amazed and cautiously reached out to pet the wolf. After a few moments, the wolf nuzzled her hand, then trotted away. 

Sophia's mom told her what a special moment it was they had just shared, and the two of them continued their journey home.

Lily and Ben were friends who liked to play together. They had many toys, but Lily's favorite was a big doll with long hair and a pink dress. Ben liked the doll too, but he had a car that made noises and lights.

One day, Lily's mom made rice for lunch. She gave Lily and Ben each a bowl and a spoon. "Eat well, children," she said. "Rice is good for you."

Lily and Ben started to eat, but Ben was not very hungry. He looked at Lily's doll and wanted to play with it. He put his spoon down and reached for the doll. "Can I have your doll, Lily?" he asked.

Lily was not happy. She loved her doll and did not want to share it. She held the doll tightly and said, "No, Ben. This is my doll. You have your car."

Ben felt jealous. He thought Lily's doll was better than his car. He tried to grab the doll from Lily, but Lily pulled it back. They started to fight over the doll. They did not hear Lily's mom coming back to the kitchen.

Lily's mom saw them fighting and was angry. She recognized the doll as a gift from Lily's grandma. She took the doll from them and said, "Stop it, both of you. Fighting is not nice. You should share your toys and be kind to each other."

Lily and Ben felt sorry. They did not want to make Lily's mom angry. They said, "We're sorry, mom. We won't fight again."

Lily's mom smiled and said, "That's good. Now finish your rice and then you can play nicely. And remember, the doll and the car are both special. You can take turns and enjoy them together."

Lily and Ben nodded and ate their rice. They learned their lesson and decided to be better friends. They played with the doll and the car and had fun. They were not jealous anymore.

Once there was a little girl who loved to play. She was so happy! One day she was playing with her hands in the garden. Suddenly, she saw a sweet butterfly fly by. She wanted to catch the butterfly, so she reached out with her hands. But, just as she was about to touch it, the butterfly disappeared. She looked everywhere for it, but it was gone. She couldn't believe it had disappeared so quickly. She sat down, feeling so sad that the butterfly had gone away. Suddenly, she heard a tiny voice whisper in her ear, "Don't worry. I'll be back soon." The little girl looked around and smiled, feeling happy again. Sure enough, when she looked up, the sweet butterfly had returned!

Once upon a time, there were two friends Ben and Joe. They were the best of pals, always playing and having fun together. One day, they had a big fight! Ben wanted to paint the wall with his finger but Joe wanted to do it his way.

Joe said, "No Ben, I don't like your idea. My way is better!"

Ben plopped down in a huff, "No it's not. My way is more creative!" The two friends were determined to prove that their way was best.

They argued and argued, until finally they decided to have a finger painting contest! They each took a big piece of paper, some paints and brushes, and started to draw.

After they were both done, they stepped back and admired each other's work. Ben's was a big yellow sun and Joe's was a bright rainbow. They both laughed and agreed that their idea was the best after all. They were so glad that instead of fighting, they found a creative way to solve their problem.

Once there was a little girl named Lily. She was three years old. One day Lily was playing outside. She saw a long thread on the ground. She picked it up and started running with it. She ran very fast with the thread across the field.

Suddenly, she ran into her friend, Katie. Lily was very sorry. She said sorry to Katie. Katie said it was ok. Then they both started running again with the thread. They ran in a circle so it made a pretty circle on the grass.

Then they said bye to each other and went their own way. Lily was happy that she made a new friend and had lots of fun playing with the thread.

Once upon a time, there was a train station. At the station, there were many trains. One train was regular. It came every day. The other trains were not regular. They came sometimes.

One day, a little girl named Amy went to the station with her mom. Amy wanted to ride the regular train. Her mom said, "You can trust this train. It comes every day." Amy was very happy.

Amy and her mom got on the regular train. They went to a fun park. They played all day. When it was time to go home, they went back to the station. They trusted the regular train to take them home. They had a great day.

One day, Mommy put on her wide cloth and took Timmy to the park. He was so excited! When they got there, Timmy saw lots of kids playing. He ran over to a group of kids playing tag. He laughed and ran with them. 

Timmy also saw some big trees. He wanted to climb one and Mommy said it was ok. Timmy scrambled up the tree. He could see so far from up there. He could see all of the park. 

He stayed in the tree for awhile, but then it got dark. Mommy said it was time to go home. Timmy said goodbye to his friends and they waved. Then, he hopped down from the tree and ran over to Mommy. They held hands and walked home.

Once upon a time, there was a dragon who was very shy. He lived in a deep dark cave, far away from the rest of the world. He did not like it when people came too close, so he hid away in his cave. 

One day, the dragon heard something from outside. It was the sound of counting. He poked his head out of the cave to see what was happening. There was a little girl counting numbers 1, 2, 3, 4 and so on! 

The dragon liked the sound of the numbers, so he grew a bit braver and slowly crept out of his cave, step by step. He saw the girl and went closer. The little girl was so happy to meet the dragon, but he was still very shy. 

But the dragon eventually got used to the little girl, and they became friends. Every day, the little girl would come to the cave and they would play counting numbers together. The dragon was no longer shy, and they were happy friends. 

The End

One day, the sun was shining brilliantly in the sky and the birds were chirping. All the trees and flowers were colorful and the squirrels were happy.

Daisy, who is 3 years old, decided to go outside and watch the beautiful day. She slowly walked out of her house and uuuh-ohed when she saw the brilliant blue sky and bright green grass. Everywhere she looked, Daisy saw amazing things.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Jane. Jane was very sad. She didn't know why but it made her feel very heavy in her heart. She wanted the sad feeling to go away.

The little girl smiled, wiped away her tears and took Janeâ€™s hand. Together they walked away from the park. Soon the animalâ€™s stopped scattering and the sun was shining brighter than ever. Once upon a time there were two friends who were both very brave. Their names were Lucy and Tommy. Tommy wanted to explore the mysterious underground, so they both went together.

When they got closer, they started to feel a little bit nervous. It was dark and unknown down there. They could see lots of rocks and had to be careful not to slip.

Tommy turned to Lucy and said: â€œLetâ€™s keep going, we can do it!â€

Once upon a time, there was a little bird. The bird loved to soar high in the sky. One day, the bird saw a vehicle on the ground. The vehicle was very big and made a loud noise. The bird was scared of the vehicle and didn't want to fly near it.

But one day, the bird saw a little mouse who was stuck in a trap near the vehicle. The bird knew it had to help the mouse. So, the bird flew down to the ground and helped the mouse escape. The mouse was very grateful to the bird.

The moral of the story is that even though something might seem scary, we should always try to help others who need us. And sometimes, even the most mild and gentle creatures can be the bravest.

Once upon a time, there was a happy little bird. The bird liked to pick berries from the bushes. One day, the bird saw a printer and wanted to print out pictures of the berries. 

The bird flew to the printer and tried to pick it up. But the printer was too heavy. The bird tried and tried, but it couldn't pick up the printer. 

Suddenly, the printer fell on the bird and hurt it very badly. The bird was no longer happy and couldn't fly anymore. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She loved shiny things and wanted a diamond. She asked her mom, "Can I have a diamond please?" Her mom said, "No, it's too expensive."

Lily thought it would be easy to get a diamond. She went to the store and saw a shiny diamond. She took it and ran away. But the store owner saw her and called the police. The police came and took Lily to jail.

Lily was sad because she didn't listen to her mom and got in trouble. She realized that it's not easy to get what you want and it's important to always ask nicely.

Bob was a happy kid and every day he would go to the park to play. One day he went to the park and saw a large dish of sauce on a table. Bob was excited and he immediately went to the sauce and grabbed some in his hands. Unfortunately, he slipped and some of the sauce spilled on the ground. Bob felt very sad and he started to cry. His mom noticed him and she quickly ran to him. She wiped away his tears and said, "It's ok, Bob! Don't worry, we can clean it up!" Bob's mom and Bob quickly cleaned up the spilled sauce.
