Molly felt hurt inside because she wanted to help, but she didn't know what else to do. But then Mom smiled, and showed her how to tie the laundry to the line with a knot. Molly worked hard, and soon all the laundry was tied up safely on the line. 

Molly felt proud as she watched Mom fluff up the laundry on the line. Now it was ready for the wind to make it nice and clean.

John was walking in the park when he heard a rustling in the bushes. He stopped to be alert and saw a melon rolling out! When he walked closer he saw a puppy playing with it. He heard the puppy bark and he couldn't help but laugh. The puppy looked so happy and he wanted to play too.

John reached out to the puppy and the puppy wagged its tail. He then picked up the melon and gave it to the puppy. He heard the puppy yip with excitement and he rolled it away. John watched as the puppy chased the melon around and around the park.

John was glad that he was able to make the puppy happy. He had a great time watching the puppy play and he walked away with a smile on his face.

Once there was a little fish named Fred. He lived in a big reef in the sea. Every day he saw all the other fishes swimming around and having fun.

But Fred was anxious. He wanted something special to show off to the others. So he decided to print a picture of himself.

One day, Fred swam up to the surface and printed an amazing picture of himself! It was bright and colourful and all the other fishes were amazed.

They loved his picture so much, that they all copied him. Soon the reef was filled with lots of pictures of little fishes!

Fred was so happy that he ran around, shouting with joy! He was so excited to show off his new picture to all his friends!

Once there was a girl. She was very hungry. She saw a piece on the ground and she decided to eat it. It was very spicy. The girl started to feel sick. The feeling got worse and worse. She couldn't stop eating that spicy piece. Soon, the girl was very sick and she had to go to bed. Sadly, she could not go back to playing and having fun with her friends. The bad piece made her very sick.

Tom and Anna are playing in the sand. They have a big bucket and a small shovel. They want to make a sand castle.

"Look, Anna, I made a tower!" Tom says. He puts some sand in the bucket and flips it over. A sand tower comes out.

"Wow, Tom, that's a nice tower!" Anna says. She makes another tower next to Tom's. They make four towers in a row.

"Let's make a wall around our castle!" Tom says. He digs a trench with his shovel and piles up the sand.

"OK, Tom, let's do that!" Anna says. She helps him with the wall. They make it high and strong.

They are happy with their castle. They sit inside and pretend to be a king and a queen.

"Tom, I have an idea!" Anna says. "Let's bury something in the sand and see if we can find it later!"

"That sounds interesting, Anna!" Tom says. "What should we bury?"

"How about this shell?" Anna says. She picks up a shiny shell from the sand. "It's pretty and smooth."

"OK, Anna, let's bury the shell!" Tom says. He digs a hole with his shovel and puts the shell inside. He covers it with sand and smooths it over.

"Can you remember where we buried it, Tom?" Anna says.

"Yes, Anna, I can!" Tom says. He points to the spot. "It's right here, next to the wall!"

"Good, Tom, let's go play something else and come back later!" Anna says.

They leave their castle and their shell and go to play with a ball. They have fun in the sun. They forget about the shell for a while.

Lila and Ben are playing with bricks. They like to build towers and houses with the bricks. The bricks are colorful. Some are red, some are blue, some are yellow, and some are green.

Lila wants to make a big tower with all the bricks. She says to Ben, "Let's make a big tower with all the bricks. It will be fun!"

But Ben does not want to make a big tower. He wants to make a small house with some of the bricks. He says to Lila, "No, I don't want to make a big tower. I want to make a small house with some of the bricks. It will be cozy!"

Lila and Ben start to argue. Lila says, "You have to share the bricks with me. We have to make a big tower together." Ben says, "No, I don't have to share the bricks with you. I can make a small house by myself."

Lila and Ben refuse to play with each other. They are angry and sad. They each take some of the bricks and go to different corners of the room. They start to build their own things. But they are not happy.

Then, they hear a knock on the door. It is their friend Mia. Mia comes in and sees the bricks. She says, "Wow, you have so many colorful bricks. Can I play with you?"

Lila and Ben look at each other. They remember that they are friends. They feel sorry for arguing. They say to Mia, "Yes, you can play with us. We have enough bricks for everyone. We can make a big tower and a small house and anything else we want."

Lila and Ben smile and hug each other. They share the bricks with Mia. They have fun playing with the bricks. They are happy.

One day, a little girl named Lily went to the park. She saw her friend Tom playing with a hoop. Lily wanted to play with the hoop too. She asked Tom, "Can you give me the hoop, please?" Tom said, "No, I am playing with it now."

Lily was sad, but she tried to stay calm. She waited for a while and asked again, "Can I play with the hoop now?" Tom looked at Lily and saw that she was calm and kind. He decided to share the hoop with her.

They took turns playing with the hoop. They both had a lot of fun. The hoop made them very happy. In the end, they learned that sharing and being calm can make everyone happy.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play with cars and animals. One day, they find a big green toy crocodile in the park. They think it is pretty and funny.

"Can we drive the crocodile?" Anna asks Ben.

"Yes, let's drive the crocodile!" Ben says. They sit on the crocodile and pretend it is a car. They make noises like vroom and beep.

They drive the crocodile around the park. They see a pond with ducks and fish. They drive the crocodile to the pond.

"Hello, ducks and fish!" Anna says. "We have a crocodile. Do you want to play with us?"

The ducks and fish are scared of the crocodile. They swim away and hide. They think the crocodile is real and mean.

"Oops, I think they don't like the crocodile," Ben says.

"Maybe they think it is not a toy," Anna says.

They feel sorry for the ducks and fish. They decide to drive the crocodile away from the pond.

"Bye, ducks and fish!" Anna says. "We are sorry we scared you. The crocodile is not real. It is just a toy. We are nice and friendly."

They drive the crocodile to another place in the park. They see a slide and a swing. They drive the crocodile to the slide and the swing.

"Can we slide and swing with the crocodile?" Anna asks Ben.

"Yes, let's slide and swing with the crocodile!" Ben says. They have fun with the crocodile. They slide and swing and laugh.

They are happy. They like the crocodile. They think it is pretty and funny. They are friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the sun. One day, she went to the park with her mom. There was a big pool of water there, and Lily wanted to play in it. 

But the water was moving very fast, and Lily's mom said it was too dangerous. So, they decided to sort some pretty flowers instead. They picked pink and yellow flowers and put them in a basket. 

Lily was sad she couldn't play in the water, but she was happy to have a basket of pretty flowers. She showed it to her dad when he came home from work, and he smiled and said it was beautiful. From that day on, Lily loved to sort things, and she always remembered the day she picked flowers with her mom.

Martha was excited to go to school. It was the first day of school and she wanted to try lots of new things. She had a big smile on her face when she entered the classroom. 

The teacher said that the first activity of the day would be to do some clapping. Martha clapped with the class, the sound was loud and clear. They played some fun clapping games and Martha really enjoyed it. 

After a few minutes, the teacher said it was time for recess. Martha ran out of the classroom with her friends and went to play tag. For the rest of the day, Martha was happy and having lots of fun. 

In the afternoon, the teacher told Martha and her friends to clap one more time. They all held hands and clapped while they sang a song. It was a wonderful way to end a great first day of school.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Sam. She had a toy tire in her garden. Every day it sparkled in the bright sunshine. Sam loved the tire and laughed whenever she saw it.

One day, Sam was playing in her garden with the tire. She ran around it and clapped her hands with joy. Then she stopped and said, â€œI wish this tire was colorful like a rainbow!â€

Suddenly, there was a loud noise in the garden. Sam looked up and saw a bright rainbow appear above her. The tire was now colored in all the colors of the rainbow. Sam was so happy she clapped and yelled, â€œYay!â€

The tire looked so beautiful in its colorful rainbow colors. Sam kept playing with it and clapping her hands. She vowed to play with her colorful tire every day and never be bored.

Mama was baking a cake. She stirred and mixed together the ingredients in the big bowl. She hummed a happy tune as she worked.

Mama placed the bowl in the oven and turned on the heat. She grabbed a screw to tighten the knob. Then, she looked at little Joe.

"Let's check on the cake," mama said with a smile.

Joe and mama went to the oven, opened the door and looked inside. It smelled delicious! Mama pointed to some yummy looking chocolate chips.

"Look Joe! It smells so good!"

Joe smiled proudly. He jumped up and down and clapped his hands.

"Yay! Cake!" he shouted.

Mama reached inside the oven and pulled out the cake. Joe licked his lips.

They waited impatiently for the cake to cool down. Finally, it was time for Joe to have his first bite.

Mama carefully cut the cake and placed a big slice in a plate for him. Joe grabbed the plate with both hands and smiled.

"Yummy!" he said with a big smile. Mama smiled too. She was so proud of her little one.

Andy was ready. He had his trumpet. He couldn't wait to set off and play. He marched off down the street, marching to the beat of his trumpet. He stopped outside the park. He set up his music stand and then set his trumpet down onto it. Then he closed his eyes and began to play. Everywhere he went people smiled. The music was so loud, it sounded like coming from a trumpet! 

When he finished, the people around him clapped so loudly. He smiled and thanked them. Then he set off to the next place. As he set off, he knew that he was ready. Ready to bring joy to more people with his trumpet.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sue. She loved to run fast. One day, her friend Tom asked her to join a race. The race was at the big park. Sue was very excited.

Before the race, Sue's mom told her to clean her shoes. Sue wanted to look attractive for the race. She cleaned her shoes until they were shiny. She put on her favorite dress too. 

The day of the race came, and Sue was ready. She ran as fast as she could. All her friends cheered for her. Sue won the race and got a big prize. She was so happy that she cleaned her shoes and looked attractive.

Johnny needed a hoop. He looked all around his house but couldn't find one. He went to the store to look for one and he saw a big hoop. He asked his mom if he could buy the big hoop and his mom said okay.

Johnny held the hoop in his hand and couldn't wait to play with it. He ran out of the store and went to the park. He was so happy he was singing and skipping.

At the park, he found a lot of kids playing with hooped. Some were playing with a medium hoop and some with a big hoop. Johnny asked the kids if he could join them and they said yes.

Johnny tried to throw the hoop but it was difficult because the hoop was too big and heavy. He asked the kids how they were doing it and they said they were using a mild hoop.

Johnny said, "I need a mild hoop! Do you know where I can get one?"

The other kids said, "Yes, at the store around the corner. They have lots of mild hoops there."

Johnny thanked them and ran off to the store. He found the perfect mild hoop and couldn't wait to start playing with it. He said goodbye to his new friends and thanked them for their help. With his new hoop, Johnny was ready for hours of fun!

Once upon a time, there was an ancient man. He would come down to the river to bring bananas for his family.

One day, as he was picking up some bananas, he heard a little voice.

"Can you bring me a banana too?" asked the little voice.

The old man looked around and, to his surprise, he saw a small child. He was three years old and was looking up at the ancient man with big bright eyes.

The old man kindly smiled and said, "Yes, I can bring you a banana."

The old man brought some bananas home to his family and he also shared one with the young child.

The old man taught the young child that it was important to be kind and generous to everyone, no matter how big or small they are.

The moral of the story is to remember to be kind and generous to everyone.

Once upon a time, Mama and DiDi were sitting in their garden. DiDi was having a drink of apple juice and Mama was reading a book. Suddenly, DiDi jumped up and said, "Mama, let's discover something! I want to find something fun to do." Mama smiled and said, "Letâ€™s go to the park and see what we can find."

When they got to the park, DiDi and Mama were very surprised. They discovered a big club! It was white and there were swings, slides and climbing frames. DiDi was so excited! He screamed out, "Mama, can I play here?" Mama replied, "Yes! Have fun, DiDi!"

DiDi ran over to the club and started exploring. He found some sand and started to dig. Suddenly, he discovered a big red ball! He grabbed it and ran back to Mama. He said, "Look what I found!" Mama was so proud of him. She said, "Well done, DiDi!"

DiDi and Mama had a lot of fun exploring the park that day. DiDi was even more excited to discover the big club and the big red ball. It was a day that he would always remember.

Once upon a time, there was a small, pink rabbit named Peter. Peter spent all his time hopping around his favorite meadow. Every day, he would gather different types of flowers.

One day, Peter noticed a large stage in the middle of the meadow. He had never seen it before and wondered what it was. He hopped over to get a closer look.

When he arrived, he saw the stage was filled with gorgeous, pink flowers, just like the ones he had been gathering. Peter had never seen so many pretty, pink petals in one place before. He had a feeling that something special was about to happen.

Sure enough, the next morning, the meadow was full of creatures and friends. They had come together for a special celebration. It was all because of the stage filled with lovely, pink flowers. In no time, the meadow was filled with laughter and music.

Peter was amazed. His little gathering had turned into a wonderful celebration. He realized that special moments can come from the smallest of beginnings.

Once upon a time there was a little fox. The fox was very hairy, with a patch of white on his tail. The fox liked to explore and go on adventures. One day he went on a big adventure and decided to explore the forest.

He ran and ran through the trees until he found a big patch of green grass. He rolled around in the grass and it tickled his back. He wanted to stay in the grass all day, but then he heard a big noise.

He jumped up and tried to find the noise. He ran around and found a lake with some fish in it. He watched the fish swim around until the sun started to set. He knew it was time to go home and he ran off. 

When he arrived at his den, he was so tired he fell asleep fast. He had a wonderful dream about his adventure. When he woke up in the morning, he knew he would go back to the patch of grass again. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Clara. She loved to play in the dark and always used her flashlight to explore different places.

One day, Clara found a big door with a big silver keyhole. She was so curious to see what was behind the door, so she found a way to unlock it.

Clara got her flashlight and shone it on the lock. She saw a delicious and shiny apple inside, so she opened the door and grabbed it.

"Yummy! It's so tasty!" said Clara. 

Suddenly, Clara heard a voice. It was coming from the darkness. "Be careful. Guard the apple with your flashlight, or you'll never know what else is hidden in the darkness," the voice said.

Clara was scared, but she was brave. She held on tight to the apple and shined her flashlight onto the darkness. She saw many other delicious things and Clara was so excited to explore more. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Lucy. She was three years old and she loved to explore her backyard. One day, Lucy decided to go in search of a new adventure. She had a cane in her hand and was excited to go on an adventure.

Suddenly, Lucy heard a noise coming from the dirt. She got closer to the spot and saw some dirt moving. She used her cane to shovel away the dirt. After a few minutes, Lucy uncovered a small box buried in the dirt.

Lucy was very excited, she opened the box and saw a small puppy. He looked up at Lucy with sad eyes. He was hurt and his leg was broken. Lucy knew she had to help the puppy, so she carefully picked him up and carried him to her house.

Lucy's mom was surprised to see the puppy and asked Lucy how she found him. Lucy told the story of how she found the puppy buried in the dirt.

Lucy and her mom took the puppy to the vet. After a few days of rest, the puppy was feeling much better. Lucy and her mom decided to keep the puppy and they named him Oreo.

Lucy was so proud of herself for finding the puppy and taking care of him. She always remembers that special day when she buried the cane in the dirt and found Oreo.

Once upon a time, there was a jolly boy named Tim. He loved to read books. One day, he went to the library to find a new book. The library was big and full of books. Tim was very happy.

In the library, Tim met a girl named Sue. Sue did not like the library. She would complain about the books. She said they were boring. Tim wanted to help Sue. He showed her fun books to read. But Sue did not want to try.

One day, a big storm came. The wind blew and the rain fell. The library started to flood. Tim knew what to do. He put the books up high so they would not get wet. Sue did not help. She just complained.

The library was saved, but Sue's house was not. All her things got wet and ruined. She was sad. Tim tried to help, but it was too late. The moral of the story is to not complain and try to help others.

Sam was a very powerful 3-year-old. He liked to sort things. On this particular day, he was sorting a pile of toys. 

His mom came in and said, "What are you doing, Sam?"

Sam replied, "Sorting my toys!"

His mom smiled and said, "That's nice. Now, can you sort the paper on the screen into two piles?"

Sam thought for a moment, then nodded. He got to work, sorting the papers into two piles.

When he was done, his mom said, "Amazing! You're so powerful."

Sam smiled proudly. He just loved sorting things!

Once upon a time, there were two friends - one named Jack and one named Jill. They were playing in the garden when they stumbled upon a wide, shiny shell.

Jack looked at the shell and said to Jill, "It's beautiful! What should we name it?"

Jill smiled and said, "Let's name it Shellie!"

Jack and Jill agreed that Shellie was the perfect name for the shell and they decided to take it with them on their adventure.

The two friends explored the garden all day, and they kept Shellie close by. They played and laughed, even picked some flowers, too. 

At the end of their day, the two friends returned home with Shellie, the wide, shiny shell. They said goodbye to Shellie, looking forward to their next fun adventure together.

Once upon a time, there was a playful little bell. Every day, it would ring and make a lovely sound. One day, the bell got a surprise - a shiny trophy! The bell was so happy that it rang even more.

The bell's friends, a sunflower and a bumblebee, heard the trophy ringing and came to take a look. What a surprise! They thought the bell was amazing and asked to borrow the trophy.

The bell said yes and its friends went to show the trophy off to all their other friends - a butterfly, a rose and a squirrel. They were all so amazed and delighted, they decided to give the bell something special in return.

They gave the bell a big hug and sang a special song. The bell was so happy, it sang and rang along with them. Everyone had so much fun, they decided to do it again the next day. And they all lived happily ever after!

Sara liked to play with her dolls in the park. She had many dolls and she gave them names and clothes. She was happy when she played with her dolls.

One day, a boy came to the park. He had a big truck and he made loud noises. He said, "Vroom, vroom, crash, bang!" He drove his truck near Sara and her dolls. He did not see them and he hit them with his truck. Sara's dolls fell down and some of their clothes came off.

Sara was sad and angry. She said, "Hey, you are bad! You hurt my dolls! Go away!" The boy stopped his truck and looked at Sara. He said, "Sorry, I did not see your dolls. I like to play with my truck. It is fun and loud."

Sara said, "But your truck is not fun for me. It is loud and scary. It makes me and my dolls unhappy. You should play somewhere else." The boy said, "But I like this park. It has grass and trees and flowers. And I want to play with you. You have many dolls. They are pretty and soft. Can I play with you and your dolls?"

Sara thought for a moment. She did not like the boy's truck, but she liked the park too. And she liked to play with other children. She said, "OK, you can play with me and my dolls. But you have to be careful and gentle. And you have to be quiet. No more loud noises. Do you understand?" The boy nodded and smiled. He said, "OK, I understand. I will be careful and gentle and quiet. Thank you for letting me play with you and your dolls."

Sara and the boy played together in the park. They shared their toys and they talked and laughed. They became friends and they had fun. They learned to respect each other's feelings and preferences. They learned that playing together is better than playing alone.

Lily and Ben were playing in the garden. They saw a big tree with many branches. Lily wanted to climb the tree and see the birds. Ben was scared of heights and said no.

"Come on, Ben, it will be fun!" Lily said. "The tree is smooth and easy to climb. You can hold on to the hose that hangs from the branch. I will go first and show you."

Lily climbed the tree with the help of the hose. She reached the top and saw a nest with three eggs. She was happy and called Ben to join her.

Ben was still afraid, but he did not want to disappoint Lily. He tried to climb the tree, but he slipped and fell. He hurt his knee and cried.

Lily heard Ben's cry and climbed down quickly. She ran to him and hugged him. She said she was sorry and that she should not have pushed him.

Ben stopped crying and hugged her back. He said he was sorry too and that he should have told her how he felt.

They learned that they should respect each other's feelings and not force each other to do things they don't like. They decided to play something else that they both enjoyed. They were happy and stayed friends.

Once upon a time, there was a big bird. It had two big wings that it used to fly. One day, the bird had a smelly surprise. It wanted to try the yucky smell, but it refused. The bird didn't want to try the smelly thing. It wanted to fly away as fast as it could. So it flapped its wings and flew away. 

When the bird was high in the sky, it looked down at the smelly thing on the ground. It was happy it had refused to try it. The bird stayed away and kept flying, never stopping until it got to a new place filled with fresh, clean smells. The bird was so happy it had refused and kept flying. 

The End.

Lily and Tom liked to play in the attic. They found many old things there, like books, hats, and toys. One day, they saw a big box with a picture of a boat on it. They opened the box and found a cute wooden sailboat inside.

"Wow, look at this!" Tom said. "It has a white sail and a red flag. Can we play with it?"

"Yes, let's!" Lily said. "But where can we sail it? There is no water in the attic."

Tom thought for a moment. Then he had an idea. He pointed to the window. "Look, there is a pond outside. We can sail it there!"

Lily and Tom carried the sailboat down the stairs and ran to the pond. They put the sailboat on the water and watched it glide. The wind made the sail flap and the flag wave. The sailboat looked like it was having fun.

"Look, it's sailing!" Lily said. "It's so fast and pretty!"

Tom nodded. He smiled and said, "It's the best toy ever. I'm glad we found it in the attic."

Once upon a time, there was a big cow named Betsy. Betsy was always sleepy, and she would often lay down in the grass to take a nap. One day, a little girl named Lily came to visit Betsy in the field where she lived.

"Hi Betsy!" said Lily. "Do you want to play with me?"

Betsy opened her eyes and looked at Lily. "I'm too sleepy to play," she said.

"Oh, okay," said Lily. "Well, I'm going to run around and have fun. Maybe you can play with me later when you're not so sleepy."

Betsy watched as Lily ran around the field, laughing and playing. She felt a little bit sad that she couldn't join in on the fun. But soon enough, Lily came back to sit with Betsy.

"I'm tired now," said Lily. "Can we take a nap together?"

Betsy smiled and nodded her head. "Yes, let's take a nap," she said.

And so, Lily and Betsy both laid down in the grass and fell asleep, feeling happy and content.

Sara and Ben liked to play in the park. They liked to swing, slide and run. One day, they saw a big, old house near the park. It looked ancient and scary.

"Let's go and see the house," Ben said. He was brave and curious.

"No, no, no," Sara said. She was scared and careful. "It might be dangerous. Mom and Dad said not to go near it."

But Ben did not listen. He ran to the house and opened the door. Sara followed him, but she was very nervous.

Inside the house, it was dark and dusty. There were many things that Sara and Ben did not know. There were books, paintings, clocks and statues. Ben wanted to touch everything.

"Look at this," he said, and picked up a shiny ball. It had wires and lights on it. He pressed a button and the ball made a loud noise.

"Zap!"

The ball gave Ben a shock. He dropped it and screamed. Sara screamed too. They were both very scared.

They ran out of the house and back to the park. They did not want to play anymore. They wanted to go home and hug Mom and Dad.

They learned a lesson. They should not go to places that are ancient and scary. They should listen to Mom and Dad. They should be careful and safe.

Once upon a time, there was a boy called Tom. Tom was three years old and he was very interested in learning new things. One day, Tom's mum brought home an attractive dictionary. Tom was so excited! He wanted to release the dictionary from its cover and find out what wonderful words and pictures it held inside.

Tom opened the dictionary and looked through its pages. He couldn't believe his eyes. It was full of colourful pictures and lots of new words. Tom was so happy he ran around the house.

Tom's mum smiled. She gave him a hug and helped him to use the dictionary. Together they read some words and looked at lots of pictures.

Tom was very pleased with his new dictionary. From then on he was always keen to release it and learn new things.

Once upon a time, there were two best friends, Joe and Grace. They were always playing together and having so much fun. One day, Joe and Grace decided to go to the town's marketplace.

When they got there, they saw a vendor with lots of colorful balloons. Joe wanted one so badly, but he didn't have enough money. Grace saw how sad Joe was and wanted to help. She asked her mom to bring some money so Joe could buy a balloon.

When Grace's mom arrived she saw that Joe wanted a deep red balloon. Joe was so relieved to be able to buy it after his friend helped him. Grace said to Joe, "Remember, if you help a friend in need, you will always be rewarded!"

Joe and Grace smiled and hugged each other, walked away with the deep red balloon, proud of the lesson they had learnt.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sue. Sue loved to learn new things. One day, she saw her friend, Tim, playing with a big, red ball. Sue wanted to play with the ball too. She went to Tim and asked, "Can I borrow your ball, please?" Tim said, "Yes, you can. But you have to be honest and give it back when you are done."

Sue was very happy. She played with the ball all day. She bounced it high and low. She even tried to teach her dog, Spot, to play with the ball. Spot liked the ball too. He jumped and barked, trying to catch the ball in his mouth.

At the end of the day, Sue remembered that she had to give the ball back to Tim. She was an honest girl. She took the ball to Tim's house and said, "Thank you for letting me borrow your ball. I had a lot of fun today!" Tim smiled and said, "You're welcome, Sue. I'm glad you had fun." And from that day on, Sue and Tim were the best of friends.

Once there was a little boy named Henry. He wanted to have some fun. So he asked his dad to supply some toys.

His dad brought out a big box of strips. Henry opened up the box and saw lots of colourful strips in there. He took out some of them and started to make a funny figure. He kept on putting different strips on it, trying to make it look even funnier. 

When he was done Henry was so happy. He proudly showed his dad his funny figure. His dad was very pleased and gave him some more strips to play with. 

Henry had so much fun playing with the strips. He continued to make different figures, always trying to make them look more and more funny. And to this day he's still playing with the strips his dad supplied him.

Lily and Tom were friends. They liked to play outside. One day, they saw a big hill. They wanted to climb it. They walked and walked until they reached the top.

At the top, they saw a cliff. A cliff is a place where the ground stops and there is a big drop. Lily and Tom were curious. They wanted to see what was on the other side. They walked closer and closer to the edge.

But then, they heard a loud noise. It was a bird. A big bird with a long beak and sharp claws. It was angry. It did not like Lily and Tom near its nest. It flew towards them and tried to peck them.

Lily and Tom were scared. They ran away from the cliff. They ran back to the hill. They ran down the hill. They ran all the way to their home.

They were safe. They hugged each other. They were happy to return to their normal place. They decided not to go near the cliff again. They learned that some places are not for playing. They played with their toys instead. They were still friends.

Once upon a time there was a brave little sailor. He was on a big boat in the sea and wanted to explore faraway places. Suddenly, he noticed that the boat was not moving! It had become frozen in place. 

He looked around and spotted an anchor on the shore. It looked so big and strongâ€”so the sailor grabbed it and threw it into the water. The anchor sank down and soon the boat was no longer frozen.

The sailor was so happy that he decided to follow his dream of going on an adventure. He paddled and paddled until he could no longer see the shore.

Once there was a little girl called Lilly. Lilly was three years old and loved adventures. But one night Lilly had a nightmare. She was scared and started to cry. She ran to her parents and knelt down beside her mum and dad.

Her mum said, "Don't worry Lilly, we're here to look after you."

Lilly felt much better but she was still scared of the nightmare. So she decided to take matters into her own hands. She ran to her dad and said, "Let's make a nightmare catcher!â€ 

Her dad got some thin sticks and bent them into an arch. Then he tied them together with some string. He said, â€œThis will catch any nightmares that come too close to you.â€

Together they hung the nightmare catcher over Lilly's bed and with a smile she said, "Goodnight."

Lilly felt much better and brave enough to go to sleep. She fell asleep safe in the knowledge that any nightmare that tried to enter her room would be caught up in the nightmare catcher.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play basketball. He had a big basketball that he liked to throw high in the air. One day, Timmy wanted to play basketball with his friends. But when he tried to put the basketball in his backpack, it didn't fit. 

Timmy was sad because he wanted to play with his friends. But then he had an idea! He put the basketball in a big basket and carried it to the park. When he got there, he threw the basketball high into the air and caught it. His friends were impressed and they all played basketball together. 

Timmy was happy because he found a way to fit the basketball in the basket and still play with his friends. From that day on, he always brought the basket with him when he wanted to play basketball.

Once upon a time, there was a poor girl. She looked at her medals every day, but they were so dirty. She wished she could wash them, but she had no water.

One day, the girl found a big puddle. She thought it would be perfect for washing her medals! She got down on her knees and started washing them. She was very careful and scrubbed each one until it was clean.

When she was finished, the poor girl's medals had a brand new shine. She felt so proud of them. She ran to show her mommy, and they both smiled at how nice the medals looked.

The poor girl was so happy that she could wash her medals. From then on, she kept them clean and sparkly every single day.

Larry was a chubby little boy who loved food. He and his family were out for a drive and he was starting to get tired. He yawned and his mom grabbed a snack for him, it was cheese and crackers. He munched happily as they drove.

Soon he was feeling full and sleepy. He yawned again, this time much bigger. His mom smiled as she looked back at him from the front seat. She saw that he was getting heavy eyed and said it was time to go home for a nap.

Larry nodded and yawned again. He was so sleepy he almost forgot about the food! They drove home and Larry got out of the car, still yawning. When he got to his bedroom, he quickly crawled up into bed and before he knew it he was fast asleep.

Sam and Lily were playing in the kitchen. They liked to pretend they were chefs and make food for their toys. Sam found a big tray in the cupboard and put some plastic fruits and vegetables on it. He said, "Look, Lily, I made a salad for our guests. Do you want to help me carry it to the table?"

Lily nodded and grabbed one end of the tray. But the tray was heavy and slippery, and Lily was not very careful. She bumped into the chair and the tray wobbled. Some of the fruits and vegetables fell off and rolled on the floor.

"Oops!" Lily said. "Sorry, Sam. I didn't mean to drop them."

Sam was not happy. He had worked hard to make the salad. He said, "Lily, you have to be more careful. You could have broken the tray or hurt yourself. Mommy always warns us not to play with the big tray. It is not a toy. It is for grown-ups only."

Lily felt bad. She knew Sam was right. She said, "I'm sorry, Sam. I didn't listen to Mommy. I wanted to play with you and have fun. But I should have used a smaller tray or a plate. Can we still be friends?"

Sam smiled. He was not angry anymore. He said, "Of course we can still be friends. You are my sister and I love you. But next time, let's use something else to make our food. Something more normal and safe. OK?"

Lily nodded. She said, "OK, Sam. Thank you for being nice to me. Let's pick up the fruits and vegetables and put them back in the basket. Then we can make something else for our guests. Maybe some cookies or sandwiches. What do you think?"

Sam agreed. He said, "That sounds good, Lily. Let's do that. But first, let's clean up the mess. We don't want Mommy to see it and get mad at us."

They hugged and went to work. They were happy to play together and to learn from their mistakes. They were good children and good chefs.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who wanted to observe what was going on near her. She saw a thermometer and thought it was very interesting. She got closer to get a much better look.

Suddenly a rude man appeared and began to shout at her. The little girl was very scared and started to cry. She ran away quickly. 

The little girl was sad, because she couldn't observe the thermometer anymore. She wanted to know more about it and find out why the rude man didn't want her to look at it.

The little girl decided that one day she would go back to observe the thermometer and find out why the rude man had been so mean. She was determined to get the answer!

Once upon a time there was a boy called Tom. He was a very kind and gentle boy. He felt sad every day because sometimes it felt like the world was too rough and unkind.

One day Tom spoke to his mom and said, "Mom, I don't like that the world is so rough." His mom paused and thought for a moment, then said, "I know what you can do to help make the world nicer, Tom."

Tom waited eagerly as his mom explained. "You can use your kind heart to heal the world. You can be kind and gentle like you always are and that will help the world feel better." Tom's eyes lit up and he wondered if he could really do it.

The next day, Tom went outside and smiled at everyone he saw. He said hello and wished them a good day. Little by little, he felt more and more joy in his heart. He knew he was helping to heal the world and that made him smile.

The world always needs a little bit of love, and with help from Tom, it was slowly beginning to heal.

Once there was a girl called Annie. One day, she wanted to make something special.

She went to the shop to buy some thread but the thread was so tangled. Annie tried to untangle it but it was too hard.

So she asked her mom for help. Together, they cleaned the thread. Then she made a beautiful dress with the thread.

She also added some spicy-smelling flowers to her dress, to make it even more special. Everyone was so surprised with her new dress!

Annie was very happy and she wore it everywhere she went!

Tommy loves Sunday. On Sunday, he can play with his toys, watch his favorite show, and eat pancakes. He does not have to go to school or do homework. He is very happy on Sunday.

But this Sunday is different. Tommy wakes up and sees that his mom and dad are not in their bed. He hears a loud noise from the kitchen. He runs to see what is happening. He sees his mom and dad holding a big cake with candles. They smile and say, "Surprise! Happy birthday, Tommy!"

Tommy is shocked. He forgot that today is his birthday. He feels silly and happy at the same time. He realizes that his mom and dad planned a special day for him. He hugs them and says, "Thank you! I love you!"

They bring the cake to the living room, where Tommy sees more surprises. There are balloons, streamers, and presents. There are also his friends from school and his grandma and grandpa. They all sing "Happy Birthday" to Tommy and clap. Tommy feels very special and loved.

He opens his presents and finds many things he likes. He gets a new bike, a book, a puzzle, and a teddy bear. He thanks everyone for the gifts and shares them with his friends. They play games, eat cake, and have fun. Tommy's mom and dad are gentle and kind. They help him with everything and make sure he is happy.

Tommy thinks that this is the best Sunday ever. He realizes that he is very lucky to have such a wonderful family and friends. He wishes that every day could be like this. He smiles and says, "This is the best birthday ever!"

Tom and Mia were best friends. They liked to play with blocks and make castles. One day, they made a big castle with many rooms and towers. They were very proud of their original castle.

But then, a mean boy came and kicked their castle. He laughed and ran away. Tom and Mia were very sad and angry. Their castle was broken and their blocks were everywhere.

Mia started to cry. Tom hugged her and said, "Don't cry, Mia. We can make another castle. We have many blocks. We can make it even better than before."

Mia sniffed and nodded. She wiped her tears and smiled. "You are right, Tom. You are a good friend. Thank you for comforting me."

They picked up their blocks and started to build again. They did not let the mean boy ruin their fun. They made a new castle, bigger and stronger than before. They were happy and proud again.

Once upon a time, there was a fancy goose. She had a big, pretty hat. She liked to walk by the pond.

One day, the fancy goose saw a little duck stuck in the mud. The duck was sad and scared. The fancy goose wanted to help.

The fancy goose went into the mud. She used her strong wings to rescue the little duck. They both got out of the mud and were happy. The fancy goose and the little duck became best friends. They played together by the pond every day.

"Mummy," said the little girl, "what's that green thing?" The mother looked over and saw a broccoli in the vegetable aisle. She smiled and said, "That's broccoli, sweetheart!"

The little girl stared at the broccoli, her eyes wide with curiosity. She touched it and said, "It's so pale." Her mum smiled and said, "Yes, but it's very yummy!"

The little girl thought for a moment and then said, "Can I have some, please?" Her mummy urged her to try it. The little girl picked up the broccoli and put it in her basket.

When they got home, the little girl's mummy cooked the broccoli and served it up on a plate. She watched as the little girl hesitantly took a bit of the broccoli and tried it. Suddenly, the little girl's eyes lit up. "Wow, it's delicious!" she said.

The little girl's mummy smiled. "I told you it was yummy!" she said. From that day on, the little girl always asked for more broccoli.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sarah. She was adorable and liked to do lots of things, like play with her dolls and color with markers. One day, Sarah's mom said, "Hurry up, Sarah. We're almost late to your music lesson!" Sarah was so excited. She was learning to play the guitar! She grabbed her guitar and hurried out the door.

When they arrived at the music school, Sarah ran inside to find her teacher. He welcomed her with a smile and said, "Let's get started!" Sarah was a quick learner. After a few lessons, she was able to play her favorite song. She was very proud of herself!

On the way back home, Sarah and her mom stopped for ice cream. Sarah said, "Thanks, Mom! Today was so fun!" Sarah strummed her guitar as they walked back home in the sunshine. She was so excited to show off her skills at her next music lesson!

Lily and Tom are friends. They like to play with toys and draw pictures. One day, Lily visits Tom at his house. She sees a big picture on the wall. It is a picture of Tom and his family. Lily thinks the picture is pretty. She wants to touch it.

"Can I touch the picture?" Lily asks Tom.

"No, you can't," Tom says. "Mommy says the picture is special. She says we have to be careful with it. It can break."

Lily nods. She knows she has to listen to Mommy. But she is curious. She wants to see the picture closer. She waits until Tom is busy with his blocks. Then she sneaks to the wall. She reaches for the picture.

But the picture is too high. Lily can't reach it. She jumps and stretches. She tries to grab the picture. But she misses. She bumps the picture. The picture falls off the wall. It makes a loud noise. It breaks.

Lily is scared. She hears Tom cry. She hears Mommy come. She feels guilty. She knows she did a bad thing. She wants to say sorry. But she can't find the words.

Mommy sees the broken picture. She sees Lily and Tom. She is angry. She is sad. She asks them what happened.

Tom points at Lily. He says, "She did it. She touched the picture. She broke it."

Lily feels worse. She looks at Mommy. She looks at Tom. She looks at the broken picture. She wishes she didn't touch it. She wishes she could fix it. She wishes she could make Mommy and Tom happy again.

Ben and Lily were playing in the park. They liked to slide, swing and run. They saw a big hill with a zip line. They wanted to try it.

"Can we go on the zip line, Mom?" Ben asked.

"Sure, but be careful. Hold on tight and don't let go," Mom said.

Ben and Lily climbed the hill. They took turns on the zip line. They felt the wind in their hair and the sun on their faces. They had great fun.

Then, Lily saw a shiny thing on the ground. She picked it up. It was a fork.

"Look, Ben, I found a fork!" Lily said.

"What are you going to do with it?" Ben asked.

"I don't know. Maybe I can use it to zip faster," Lily said.

She put the fork in her pocket and went on the zip line again. But the fork was sharp. It poked a hole in her pocket and fell out. It landed on the zip line wire.

Ben did not see the fork. He went on the zip line after Lily. But when he reached the fork, it cut the wire. Ben fell down. He hit his head on a rock. He cried out loud.

Mom heard Ben's cry. She ran to him. She saw the blood on his head. She was scared.

"Oh no, Ben, what happened?" Mom asked.

"Lily's fork cut the wire. It hurt me," Ben said.

Mom hugged Ben. She called for help. She was angry with Lily.

"Lily, why did you bring a fork to the park? You could have killed your brother!" Mom said.

Lily felt bad. She did not mean to hurt Ben. She was sorry.

"I'm sorry, Mom. I'm sorry, Ben. I just wanted to have fun," Lily said.

But it was too late. Ben had to go to the hospital. He had a big wound on his head. He needed stitches. He was in pain.

Lily learned a hard lesson. She never played with forks again. She wished she could zip back in time and change what she did. But she could not. She was sad.

Lily and Tom were friends who liked to play outside. One day, they saw a large van parked near their house. It had many colors and pictures on it. They wanted to see what was inside.

"Let's go test the van," Tom said. "Maybe it has toys or candy."

Lily was not sure. She felt scared. "But what if someone is in there?" she asked. "What if they get angry?"

Tom laughed. "Don't be silly," he said. "There is no one in there. Come on, it will be fun."

He took Lily's hand and pulled her to the van. He opened the door and climbed in. Lily followed him. The van was dark and messy. There were wires and boxes and bottles. They did not see any toys or candy.

"Tom, I don't like this," Lily said. "Let's go back."

But before they could go back, the door slammed shut. They heard a loud noise and felt the van move. Someone was driving the van away.

"Help! Help!" Lily and Tom cried. "Let us out!"

But no one heard them. The van drove faster and faster. Lily and Tom did not know where they were going. They were trapped in the large van. They wished they had never tested it. They were very sorry.

Once there was a truck that wanted to go for a drive. It rolled onto the street and started its journey. It drove around the corner, past the park and over the bridge. Along the way it saw lots of funny things. It saw a dog dressed in a raincoat, a squirrel eating a ice cream cone, and a group of cats playing music. 

The truck continued driving until it reached the beach. It was a beautiful day outside and the truck was excited to play in the sun. It spent the whole day playing with the children and going for rides in the sand. It was so much fun!

At the end of the day, the truck drove home tired but happy. It had had a really funny and exciting day.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. He was an obedient child who always listened to his mom and dad. One day, his mom asked him to help her in the kitchen. She wanted to make rice for dinner.

"Tim, can you please repeat after me? First, wash the rice. Then, put it in the pot with water. Lastly, turn on the stove," said his mom. Tim listened carefully and repeated, "Wash rice, put in pot with water, turn on stove."

Tim did as his mom told him. He washed the rice, put it in the pot with water, and turned on the stove. The rice began to cook. The smell of the rice filled the kitchen, making Tim and his mom very hungry.

Soon, the rice was ready. Tim and his mom put the rice on their plates and sat down to eat. They both enjoyed the delicious rice that Tim had helped to make. Tim felt proud that he was able to help his mom in the kitchen and be an obedient child.

Once upon a time there was a brave boy. One day he found a raft in the sea. He got on the raft and went on an adventure! The sun was bright and it was hot.

As he headed off, along the way he saw a fire. He got close and called out "Hello, who's there?".

A gruff voice answered "I'm a dragon and I want to burn."

The brave boy became scared. He said "No, please don't. I'm on my big raft, please don't".

But the dragon said "I must, you must go back."

The brave boy had a thought. He said "Please don't burn my raft. I can help you. I'll be your friend".

The dragon paused. He had not had a friend before. After a moment he said "OK, I won't burn. We can be friends".

The brave boy was relieved. He said "Thanks for being so nice". The dragon looked happy and the day was saved!

Once there was a nosy little girl named Jane. Jane always wanted to know what was happening around her.

One day, she found a jar on the floor. Jane was very excited. She picked up the jar and opened it. Inside, she discovered a sparkly pink butterfly!

The butterfly was so beautiful that Jane wanted to keep it. She closed the jar and put it on the windowsill in her bedroom.

Every day, Jane would open the jar and look at the butterfly. Then the butterfly would flutter around Janeâ€™s room, full of life and energy.

One day, something strange happened. The butterfly began to change and slowly it became a fairy! Jane couldnâ€™t believe her eyes. The fairy gave Jane a magical necklace and flew away, waving goodbye.

Jane was so excited by her new magical friend. She never stopped being nosy, but she always remembered the magical day the butterfly became a fairy.

Anna and Ben are friends who live in a village near a big river. They like to play near the water and splash each other. One day, they see a man who is very thirsty. He has a bottle, but it is empty. He asks them if they can share some water with him.

"Please, can I have some water?" he says. "I have walked a long way and I have no water left."

Anna and Ben look at each other. They have a bucket of water that they filled from the river. They can give some to the man, but then they will have less to play with.

"Why do you need water?" Anna asks. "Water is for fun, not for drinking."

The man smiles and says, "Water is for many things, my dear. Water is for drinking, for washing, for cooking, for growing plants, for making rainbows. Water is a gift from God, and we should value it and use it wisely."

Anna and Ben think about what the man says. They realize that water is not only for fun, but also for life. They feel sorry for the man, who has no water. They decide to share their water with him.

"Here, you can have some of our water," Ben says. "We have plenty, and you need it more than we do."

The man thanks them and drinks some water. He feels better and says, "You are very kind and generous, children. You have humble hearts and you know how to share. May God bless you and your water."

Anna and Ben smile and say, "You are welcome, sir. Thank you for teaching us about water. We will value it and use it wisely."

The man leaves and Anna and Ben go back to playing near the water. They splash each other, but they also drink some water and thank God for it. They are happy and grateful. They have learned a valuable lesson.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim was very nervous. He had lost his toy razor. He loved to pretend to shave like his dad. Every day, he would play with his toy razor. But now, it was gone.

One day, Tim went to the park with his mom. He thought maybe he left his toy razor there. He looked and looked, but he could not find it. Tim was very sad. He missed his toy razor so much. He wanted to find it and play with it again.

Then, Tim saw a girl playing with a toy. He looked closer and recognized it. It was his toy razor! Tim was so happy. He went to the girl and told her that it was his toy. The girl was nice and gave it back to him. After that, Tim was not nervous anymore. He had his toy razor back and could play with it again. And they all lived happily ever after.

One day, a brave little girl named Emmy was walking in the forest. She looked around, admiring the tall trees, furry animals and tall grass.

Suddenly, she noticed a scary smell. It was getting stronger and stronger. Emmy looked around, wondering where it was coming from. Suddenly, she saw smoke coming from a nearby hill.

Emmy was very worried. She ran to find her mom, who was sitting at the edge of the forest. Emmy's mom was surprised to see her daughter so scared.

"Mom," she said, "I saw smoke. Something is burning!"

Emmy's mom became very worried. She grabbed Emmy's hand and said, "Let's go investigate."

They ran to the top of the hill and found a big fire. Emmy was terrified of the flames, but her mom was brave. She ran to get help and put out the fire.

Luckily, they managed to save the forest. Emmy and her mom had saved the day!

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy who loved to play with his toys. He had a big collection of cars, trucks and robots. Timmy's favorite toy was a red car that he liked to drive around his room.

One day, Timmy's friend Tommy came over to play. Tommy brought his own toys, but Timmy didn't like them very much. He didn't want to play with them, but he didn't want to hurt Tommy's feelings either. Timmy started to frown, feeling unsure of what to do.

Suddenly, Timmy remembered something his mom had told him. She said that it's important to always be true to yourself and do what makes you happy. So, Timmy politely told Tommy that he wanted to play with his own toys instead. Tommy was a little sad at first, but then he saw how happy Timmy was playing with his popular red car. They both had fun playing together and being true to themselves. The end.

Once upon a time there was a young girl named Hilda. She was a very brave and bold girl who loved to explore new places.

One day she decided to take a walk in the hot summer sun. She saw an old barn and decided to take a closer look. Unbeknownst to her, the barn was a secret hideout for a group of rough youth who had recently moved into town.

When Hilda opened the door of the barn, she was instantly surrounded by the group of boys. She tried to run away, but just couldn't manage it.

The boys started to laugh at her and made cruel jokes. Suddenly, one of them came closer and said:

"You want to be brave? Let's see how brave you can be!"

Hilda was scared and tried to talk her way out but it was too late. The boys dragged her into the barn and tied her up.

Afterwards, the boys ran away and left Hilda tied up in the hot barn. Eventually, a few hours later, a farmer came to the barn and found her. Poor Hilda never managed to get herself out of this terrifying situation.

Once upon a time, there was a round ball. It was yellow and all the children liked it very much. They would gather around it and bounce it up and down. They were all so happy and grateful!

The ball was bouncy and fast. It could go all around the room in a circle. The children were so excited; they laughed and cheered. They were very happy to play with the round ball.

After awhile, the children got tired from bouncing it around the room. One of the children was exhausted, so the other children gave her a special place for her to rest. They were so kind and she was so grateful.

After she had a nice rest, it was time for the ball to be bounced again around the circle. Everyone shouted and cheered and it made them all laugh. Bouncing the round ball was their favorite thing to do.

In the end the children were all happy and grateful. They said goodbye to the yellow bouncy ball, until they could play with it again.

Once upon a time, there lived a smart mouse. He loved to explore and find new things. One day, he was exploring in the forest when he spotted an arrow. He went up to take a closer look and the arrow flew away! The mouse used his smarts and chased after the arrow. He followed the arrow deep into the woods, but the arrow was too fast and the mouse couldn't catch up. 

He stopped to catch his breath and suddenly he heard a voice.
"Why are you chasing me?" it said. The mouse was shocked and he quickly looked around. He saw a little girl standing there with the arrow in her hand. She was very brave and the mouse liked that.

The mouse finally replied, "I'm trying to escape the arrow!" The girl smiled and said, "Come and join me on my adventures. I could use a smart mouse like you by my side." The mouse agreed and together the two friends took off in search of new and exciting places.

Once upon a time, there was a clumsy bear. He lived in a big city with lots of people and cars. One day, the bear was walking down the street when he tripped and fell. He hurt his paw and started to cry.

Luckily, a kind little girl saw the bear and ran to comfort him. She gave him a hug and told him everything would be okay. The bear stopped crying and felt much better.

But then, a loud noise scared the bear and he ran away from the little girl. He didn't look where he was going and accidentally ran into a big truck. The bear was badly hurt and couldn't get up.

The little girl called for help, but it was too late. The bear had died from his injuries. The city was sad to lose such a clumsy but lovable bear.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Mia. She loved to laugh and joke around with her friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the grass and pick flowers. One day, she saw a little bunny hopping around. The bunny looked scared and lost.

Lily said, "Hi bunny, what's wrong?"

The bunny replied, "I lost my basket and I need to hurry and find it before it gets dark."

Lily said, "Don't worry, I'll help you find it. Let's look in the wildflowers."

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Lucy. She was three years old, and she loved going to the river. Every day she would put on her red dress and skip along to find her friends.

When she got to the river there was a beautiful big tree with brilliant leaves. She loved to sit beneath it and watch the river flow. Every day she would explore the riverbank, looking for treasures and picking flowers.

One day she found a brilliant purple flower and she decided to pick it. She wanted to bring it back and show her friends, but then she heard someone calling her name. It was her friends, telling her they had something special to show her!

She ran over to them and they gave Lucy a present. It was a lovely bracelet that belonged to them all. It was a special symbol of friendship, and they all decided to wear it together.

Now every day they go to the river and they wear their friendship bracelet. They have lots of fun exploring and picking flowers, and they belong to each other like the river belongs to the tree.

One day, a little girl named Daisy was washing her hands. She was getting ready to help her mom make dinner. Mom was making something special - cheese! 

Daisy was so excited. She'd never tried cheese before, only heard about it from her friends. 

When the cheese was ready, Daisy's mom let her smell it. When Daisy smelled the cheese, she said it was incredible! Then Daisy and her mom tried a little piece. 

It tasted just like what Daisy had heard about. She said it was incredible! She asked for more and more until she was full. 

Daisy had the most incredible meal ever that day. She and her mom enjoyed it so much!

Lila and Ben were friends who liked to play in the park. They had a plan to make a path with stones and sticks. They wanted to make the path go from the slide to the swings. They thought it would be fun to walk on the path and pretend they were on an adventure.

They started to look for stones and sticks on the ground. They found some big ones and some small ones. They put them in a pile near the slide. Then they began to lay them on the grass, making a line. They were happy with their plan.

But then they saw a big dog running towards them. The dog was barking and wagging its tail. It looked friendly, but Lila and Ben were scared. They did not know the dog. They did not know if it was nice or mean. They ran away from the slide and the path. They hid behind a bench.

"Go away, dog!" Lila shouted. "This is our path! You can't ruin it!"

The dog did not listen. It jumped on the slide and slid down. It landed on the path and knocked over some stones and sticks. It ran around the path, making a mess. It thought it was a game.

Lila and Ben were troubled. They did not like the dog. They did not like what it did to their path. They wanted it to leave. They looked for someone who could help them. They saw a lady walking with a leash. She was the dog's owner.

"Miss, miss!" Ben called. "Please get your dog! It is ruining our path!"

The lady heard Ben and saw the dog. She was sorry. She ran to the dog and put the leash on it. She apologized to Lila and Ben.

"I'm so sorry, kids. I didn't see you there. My dog is very playful, but he doesn't mean any harm. He just likes to have fun. I hope he didn't hurt your path too much."

Lila and Ben looked at their path. It was not as nice as before. Some stones and sticks were out of place. Some were broken. They were sad.

"It's okay, miss," Lila said. "We can fix it. We can make it better. We still have our plan."

The lady smiled and thanked them. She walked away with the dog. Lila and Ben went back to the slide and the path. They picked up the stones and sticks. They rearranged them on the grass. They made the path go from the slide to the swings. They were happy with their plan. They walked on the path and pretended they were on an adventure.

Tom and Anna are going to visit Grandma and Grandpa. They are very happy because they love Grandma and Grandpa. They also love their big house and their big lawn. They can play with their dog, Spot, and their toys.

Mom tells them to pack their bags. She says they need to bring clothes, pajamas, toothbrushes, and books. Tom and Anna run to their rooms and pack their bags. They put everything they need in their bags. They also put some things they want, like their favorite teddy bears and cars.

Mom checks their bags and smiles. She says they did a good job. She tells them to put their bags in the car. She says they need to hurry because Grandma and Grandpa are waiting for them. Tom and Anna run to the car and put their bags in the trunk. They are very excited.

Dad comes out of the house. He looks at the lawn and frowns. He says the lawn is very messy. He says there are leaves and sticks and rocks everywhere. He says he needs to clean the lawn before they go. He says he will be quick.

Tom and Anna look at the lawn and feel sorry. They say they want to help Dad. They say they can pick up the leaves and sticks and rocks. They say they can make the lawn nice and clean. Dad smiles and says thank you. He says they are very kind and helpful. He gives them a rake and a bucket. He says they can work together.

Tom and Anna work with Dad. They rake the leaves and put them in the bucket. They pick up the sticks and rocks and put them in the bucket. They make the lawn nice and clean. They have fun and talk and laugh. Mom comes out of the house and sees them. She says they did a great job. She says the lawn looks beautiful. She says they are ready to go.

Tom and Anna hug Dad and Mom. They say they love them. They say they are happy to go to Grandma and Grandpa. They say they are happy to help Dad. They get in the car and buckle their seatbelts. Dad and Mom get in the car and start the engine. They wave goodbye to the house and the lawn. They drive to Grandma and Grandpa. They have a wonderful time.

Once there was a little boy named Joe who loved balloons. Every day, Joe would go out and blow up balloons in many shapes and colors. One day, Joe was having a lot of fun blowing up a balloon when his Mom warned him, "Joe, remember to stay organized and not make too much mess!" Joe quickly grabbed the balloon and said, "Okay Mom, I'll be careful with the balloon!" His Mom gave him a smile, and Joe went back to his play.

Joe then went outside and started to have fun with his balloon. He ran around the yard, laughing and playing. A sudden gust of wind blew by and Joe's balloon flew up in the air! Joe gasped and ran after it, but it floated away faster than he could run. He yelled, "My balloon!" But it was too far.

Joe was sad. His Mom then came and hugged him. She said, "Joe, I warned you to stay organized and not make too much mess. Let this be a lesson to you about always being careful with things." Joe nodded his head and promised to be careful with his balloons from then on.

Once upon a time there was a boy who had a very bad day. He was sad because he had lost his toy. No matter how hard he looked, he couldn't find it. He was so upset that he started to cry. 

Suddenly, he saw a hand reach out to him. He looked up and saw his friend. She smiled and said, "Don't worry. I'll rescue you!" She grabbed his hand and together they looked for the toy. 

They searched everywhere, but they still couldn't find it. He started to cry, again. But then his friend said, "I know how to make you feel better. Come with me!"

She took him to her house and gave him a new toy. He was so happy and hugged his friend. She smiled and said, "I'm glad I could rescue you!" 

From that day forward, the boy knew he had a true friend who would help him when things got bad. He was never scared to ask her for help because he knew she was always there to rescue him.

Lila and Ben are twins. They like to play in the garden. One day, they see a big bird with red and blue feathers. The bird has a nest in a tree. The nest has four eggs.

"Look, Ben, eggs!" Lila says. "Let's take one and see what is inside."

"No, Lila, we can't do that," Ben says. "The eggs are not ours. They are the bird's. The bird values the eggs. They are her babies."

"But I want to see," Lila says. She tries to climb the tree.

The bird sees Lila and makes a loud noise. She flies to the nest and pecks at Lila's hand. Lila cries and falls down.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Lila says. "The bird hurts me!"

Ben runs to Lila and hugs her. He says, "I'm sorry, Lila. The bird is alert. She protects the eggs. She thinks you are a bad animal who wants to eat them."

Lila sniffles and says, "I'm sorry, too, Ben. I was wrong. I should not touch the eggs. They are not toys. They are the bird's babies."

Ben and Lila go back to the house. They tell their mom what happened. Mom gives them a band-aid and a cookie. She says, "I'm glad you learned your lesson. The bird values the eggs. We should respect the bird and the eggs. They are part of nature. Nature is beautiful and wonderful, but we have to be careful and kind."

Lily and Sam went to the beach with Mom and Dad. They liked to play in the sand and look at the sea. The sea was big and blue and made a loud sound.

"Can we go in the water, Mom?" Lily asked.

"Not now, Lily. The sea is too cold and too rough today. Maybe later, when it is calm and warm," Mom said.

Lily and Sam felt sad. They wanted to swim and splash in the sea. They saw some other kids with buckets and shovels. They asked Mom and Dad if they could have some too.

"Sure, you can have some buckets and shovels. Let's go to the shop and see what they have," Dad said.

They walked to the shop near the beach. It had many things for the beach, like hats, sunglasses, towels, and toys. Lily and Sam looked at the buckets and shovels. They saw different colors and shapes. They wanted to order the ones they liked.

"I want the red bucket and the yellow shovel, please," Lily said.

"I want the blue bucket and the green shovel, please," Sam said.

The shopkeeper smiled and gave them the buckets and shovels they ordered. He said they were available and not too expensive.

"Thank you, shopkeeper," Lily and Sam said.

"You're welcome, kids. Have fun at the beach," the shopkeeper said.

Lily and Sam ran back to the sand with their buckets and shovels. They started to make castles and holes and bridges. They had fun at the beach, even if they could not go in the sea. They hoped the sea would be calm and warm tomorrow.

Sara and Ben were playing in their room. They liked to pretend they were spies and look for clues. Sara had a flashlight and Ben had a magnifying glass.

"Let's enter the closet and see what's inside," Sara said. "Maybe we can find a secret passage or a treasure."

"OK, but be careful. It's dark and there might be monsters," Ben said.

They opened the closet door and crawled inside. They saw clothes, shoes, toys and books. Sara shone the flashlight around and Ben looked closely with the magnifying glass.

"Look, there's a hole in the wall behind the coats," Sara said. "Maybe it leads to another room."

"Let's go and check it out," Ben said. "But we have to be flexible and squeeze through the hole."

They pushed the coats aside and saw the hole. It was small and round, like a mouse hole. Sara and Ben were not afraid. They were curious and brave. They took their flashlight and magnifying glass and entered the hole.

They crawled through the hole for a while. It was dark and narrow, but they could see some light at the end. They reached the end and saw another closet. It was full of old and dusty things. They saw a trunk, a hat, a doll and a map.

"Wow, this is amazing," Sara said. "Maybe this is the treasure we were looking for."

"Maybe, but we have to be careful. There might be traps or guards," Ben said.

They opened the trunk and saw a lot of shiny and colorful things. They saw coins, jewels, medals and keys. They picked some of them and put them in their pockets.

"We're rich, we're rich," Sara said. "We found the treasure."

"Shh, be quiet. Someone might hear us," Ben said.

They heard a noise outside the closet. It sounded like footsteps and a voice.

"Who's there? Who's in the closet?" the voice said.

Sara and Ben were scared. They quickly closed the trunk and hid behind the coats. They hoped the voice would go away.

The end.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Mia. Every day Mia would go to the museum with her mommy and daddy. She was always very excited to go because it was one of her favorite places. 

One day when they were at the museum Mia asked her mommy, "What are those pictures on the wall?" Her mommy smiled and said, "Those are called paintings. They are done by an artist with special brushes and paints." Mia looked at the pictures in amazement and asked, "Can I do that too?" 

Her daddy said, "Of course you can, but first you have to learn how." He brought over some paper, paints and brushes and began to show Mia how to use them. At first she was a little confused but with some practice and guidance from her mom and dad she soon became an enthusiastic painter. 

Mia and her mom and dad took turns talking about her paintings and how she did them. She was so proud of her accomplishments, and each time she showed them a new painting, they were amazed. 

The end.

Tim was with his family at the beach. He was feeling anxious, but it was so much fun. The sun was shining and the water was warm.

Tim's dad said, "Let's go for a swim!" Tim got excited and said, "Yes!"

His mom said, "Listen closely. You need to hear us so you stay safe in the water. Can you do that?" Tim nodded his head yes.

Tim heard his parents tell him what to do. He hopped into the water with them. He was a bit anxious, but his dad held him tight.

After a few minutes, Tim heard his dad whisper, "I will always keep you safe." Tim felt better and smiled. He was having so much fun!

Once upon a time there was a bunny who wanted to be a guitar player. He studied very hard and practiced every day.

One day, his mother took him out to see a guitar shop. The bunny gazed at all the shiny, colourful guitars and explained to his mother that he had to have one. His mother smiled and asked, "Do you think you can be obedient enough?" The bunny pondered for a moment and then replied, "Yes, I can be obedient if I can have a guitar."

So, the mother bought the bunny a guitar. She created a special practice spot for him and reminded him of the importance of obedience. The bunny practiced every day, and soon he was a talented guitar player.

The moral of the story is that obedience is important if you want to achieve something. For if you are obedient, you will discover all kinds of things you need and enjoy.

Robbie was a little bunny. He was feeling hungry so he hopped through the garden, looking for something to eat. He found a sweet carrot! He hopped closer and sniffed it. It smelled so good.

Robbie asked the carrot, "Are you yummy?"

The carrot didn't answer but Robbie was sure it was yummy. He nibbled a tiny bit. It tasted so sweet that Robbie wanted to eat the whole thing. He asked the carrot, "Can I eat the whole thing?"

The carrot was silent, so Robbie decided to eat it. He ate the whole carrot and felt very satisfied. He hopped away, feeling happy he had asked the carrot his question so he could enjoy a sweet snack.

Molly and her Mommy were getting ready for their visit. Molly was very excited to see the farm animals. 

First, they took the bus. It was a long and bumpy ride, but Molly loved it. She watched the trees go by out the window.

When they got to the farm, they saw so many animals. Molly smiled at all of the cows, sheep, and chickens. She could even see a horse in the distance. 

But the best part was the hayride. Molly and her Mommy snuggled up in a big haystack, and the kind farmer filled it with blankets to keep them warm. The ride was so mild and slow, it lulled Molly to sleep. 

When Molly awoke, all the animals were looking at her. She smiled, and wished she could visit the farm every day.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy wanted to put his picture on the fridge, but it was too high for him to reach. He tried to jump, but it was too hard. 

Timmy's mom saw him struggling and said, "What's wrong, Timmy? Can I help you?" 

Timmy replied, "I want to put my picture on the fridge, but it's too high." 

Mom said, "Don't worry, it's easy. I'll attach a magnet to the back of your picture and then you can put it on the fridge." 

Timmy was happy and said, "Thank you, Mommy! Now I can see my picture every day!" 

From that day on, Timmy learned that if he ever needed help, he could always ask his mom. And attaching things to the fridge was easy with a magnet. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a fancy dress that she loved to wear. One day, she spilled oil on her pretty dress and it made her very sad.

Lily's mom saw her crying and asked, "What happened, sweetie?"

"Don't worry, we can wash it," her mom said. "But first, let's reach for some paper towels to clean it up."

Lily and her mom cleaned the oil off the dress and it looked as good as new. Lily was so happy that she hugged her mom and said, "Thank you for helping me."

The plane was flying high in the sky. Mommy and Daddy were in the plane, too. Daddy was teaching Mommy how to fly the plane. Mommy had never flown a plane before!

Mommy was doing very well. Daddy showed Mommy all the useful parts of the plane. He taught Mommy how to turn the plane and make it go up and down. Mommy was very happy to learn.

When the plane landed, Mommy was so proud. She had learned something new and it was very useful. Daddy was very proud of Mommy, too. They hugged each other and couldn't stop smiling!
