One day, Nicky was looking out the window and saw some birds. They chirped and flew around in the sky. Nicky liked to watch them, it was very peaceful. 

Suddenly it was time to stop. Nicky didn't want to stop watching the birds, but it was almost dinner time. So Nicky said goodbye to the birds and went to the dinner table. 

After dinner, Nicky went back to the window and looked out again. The birds were gone and the sky was dark, but Nicky still found the view peaceful. 

Nicky stayed at the window until it was time for bed. Then he put on his pajamas and said goodnight to the night sky. He knew that tomorrow he could watch the birds again.

One day, a vendor went to the store to buy things. The store had different types of things inside, such as candy, toys, and books. The vendor was very excited to find something special. 
But, when the vendor went to the checkout line, they realized they didn't have enough money to pay for the things they wanted.

The vendor became very sad and decided to leave the store. On the way back, they passed by the park. There they saw many people playing, enjoying the sunshine. The vendor suddenly had an idea. 

They decided to pack up some of the things they had and sold them at the park. Everyone loved the different items, and the vendor soon made enough money to buy all they wanted from the store.

The moral of the story is that you don't need money to make money. Just be creative and resourceful, and you can find all sorts of different ways to make your dreams come true.

Once upon a time there was an old man. He was so old he had a white beard. Every day he sat in his chair, waiting. He waited for his dinner. His dinner was plain, but he liked it.

One day, he had a surprise. A little baby rabbit hopped up to him. The little rabbit had a carrot in its mouth. It hopped up to the old man and gave him the carrot.

The old man was so excited. He started to chew the carrot, chomping and munching. The little rabbit watched him. It was so happy to have made the old man so happy.

The old man and the rabbit became friends. The old man waited for the baby rabbit each day, and the rabbit came with a carrot every time. The old man would chew the carrot and smile, and the rabbit gave a big hopped and cheered when he was finished.

Once upon a time there was a big, yellow bird. Every day the bird would go out and bring a little bit of fur home. All of the other animals in the forest were excited to see what the yellow bird had brought that day.

One day, the yellow bird brought a special something! It was a fur ball, yellow and soft. He shined and sparkled in the sun.

The little fox couldn't contain its excitement. "What is it?" he asked.

The yellow bird smiled and replied, "It's a special gift for you. I thought you'd like it!" 

The fox smiled and gave the yellow bird a great big hug. From that day on, the yellow bird and the fox were great friends. They were each other's best friends, and they shared the yellow fur ball every day!

Tom and Lily wanted to measure how far they could walk. They took a long rope and tied one end to a tree. Then they walked and walked, holding the other end of the rope. They wanted to see who could walk farther.

"I can walk more than you," Tom said. "I am healthy and strong."

"No, I can walk more than you," Lily said. "I am healthy and smart."

They walked and walked, until they reached a big pond. They could not walk any more, because the water was deep and cold. They looked at the rope and saw that it was very short.

"Who won?" Tom asked.

"I don't know," Lily said. "The rope is too short to measure."

They were sad and angry. They wanted to know who could walk more. They started to argue and pull the rope.

"Let go of the rope!" Tom said.

"No, you let go of the rope!" Lily said.

They pulled and pulled, until the rope broke. The rope flew into the pond and sank. Tom and Lily fell down and got dirty.

They looked at each other and felt silly. They had lost the rope and their game. They had no way to measure how far they could walk.

They decided to stop arguing and be friends. They walked back to the tree and hugged. They learned that it was not important to measure how far they could walk, but to have fun and be healthy.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside in the wind. He loved to feel the wind blow through his hair and make his kite fly high in the sky. 

One day, Timmy's mom asked him to clean up his room. But Timmy didn't want to clean his room. His room was very messy and filthy. 

Timmy's mom mentioned that if he cleaned his room, they could go outside and play in the wind. Timmy was so excited to play in the wind that he quickly cleaned his room. When they went outside, the wind was blowing so strong that it made Timmy's kite fly higher than ever before. 

From that day on, Timmy learned that cleaning his room was important so he could go outside and play in the wind.

Once upon a time there was an opera singer who lived in a purple house. Her name was Mrs Mailer. Mrs Mailer loved to sing opera in the garden. Every day she called out to the birds, singing beautiful tunes.

One day Mrs Mailer wanted to send a letter to a friend, so she went to the purple post box. She took out a piece of paper and a purple pen and wrote a long letter. She put the letter in an envelope and stamped it purple. Then she put it in the post box and sent it away.

That evening, Mrs Mailer opened her mailbox. Inside was a letter for her from her friend! She was so happy that she had been able to mail her letter. From then on, every day she wrote a letter, stamped it purple and posted it in the post box. 

Mrs Mailer always said that nothing beats the magic of mail.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy was very nice and loved to eat popcorn. One day, Timmy went to the park to play with his friends. They decided to catch butterflies, but Timmy didn't like that. He wanted to catch popcorn instead. So, they went to the popcorn stand and bought a big bag of popcorn. They threw the popcorn in the air and tried to catch it with their mouths. Timmy caught the most popcorn and everyone thought he was very good at it. They all had a nice time playing together and eating popcorn. The end.

Once upon a time there was a puppy. He was small and brown, and loved to play. Every day, he would go out on fun adventures with his dad. 

But one day, something wonderful happened! His dad decided that he was an obedient dog, so he was going to become a model! That meant he had to listen even more closely to his dad, so he did his best. 

The puppy was so excited to model for all the people he met. He loved meeting new people and showing off how obedient he could be. People would say, "What a nice puppy!"

The puppy soon became famous! He was very popular, and his dad was so proud of him. The puppy had become a very famous model!

The puppy and his dad had lots of fun after that. The puppy was always very obedient, which made his dad very happy. They would go on all kinds of adventures and the puppy was always the star!

Once upon a time, a little cat named Luna was very hungry. She went outside to find some food. Luna saw a big tree with a lot of birds. She thought, "I will catch a bird to eat." Luna was ready to climb the tree.

Then, a thick mist arrived. Luna could not see the tree or the birds. She was sad and still hungry. She went back home and waited for the mist to go away. Luna knew something good would come after the mist.

When the mist was gone, Luna saw a big surprise. In her yard, there was a big, yummy fish. The fish arrived when the mist went away. Luna was so happy! She ate the fish and was not hungry anymore.

Ben and Lily were twins who liked to play pretend. One day, they found a big box of costumes in the attic. They tried on different hats, coats, and shoes. Ben found a fake mustache and stuck it on his face. He pretended to be a detective and said, "I am looking for clues. Lily, you are my helper. Behave and follow me."

Lily nodded and put on a scarf and a pair of glasses. She pretended to be a reporter and said, "I am looking for a story. Ben, you are my partner. Behave and listen to me."

They went downstairs and looked around the living room. They saw a vase with flowers, a book with pictures, and a cookie jar with a lid. Ben said, "Maybe there is a clue in the vase. Let me check." He lifted the vase and peeked inside. He saw nothing but water and stems. He put the vase back on the table.

Lily said, "Maybe there is a story in the book. Let me see." She opened the book and flipped through the pages. She saw nothing but words and drawings. She closed the book and put it back on the shelf.

They both said, "Maybe there is a treat in the cookie jar. Let us look." They tiptoed to the cookie jar and lifted the lid. They saw nothing but crumbs and dust. They frowned and put the lid back on the jar.

They heard a voice behind them. It was their mom. She said, "What are you two doing? You know you are not supposed to touch the vase, the book, or the cookie jar. They are not toys. They are not yours. They are mine."

Ben and Lily turned around and saw their mom. She was wearing a big hat, a long coat, and a fake mustache. She pretended to be a thief and said, "I am looking for treasure. Ben and Lily, you are my victims. Behave and give me your costumes."

Ben and Lily gasped and laughed. They realized their mom was playing along. They said, "Mom, you are so funny. You are not a thief. You are our mom. We love you and your mustache."

They hugged their mom and gave her their costumes. They said, "We are sorry we touched your things. We were just playing pretend. We are glad you joined us."

Their mom smiled and said, "I am sorry I scared you. I was just playing pretend too. I am glad you had fun. But next time, ask me before you use my things. And don't forget to clean up your mess."

They nodded and said, "Okay, mom. We will." They helped their mom put the costumes back in the box and the box back in the attic. They said, "Thank you, mom, for the best game ever."

Their mom said, "You are welcome, Ben and Lily, for the best twins ever."

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Jilly. Jilly was three years old and very competitive. She loved playing games with her friends.

One day, Jilly was playing a game of 'name that smell'. Her friend held up a little bag of mint, and Jilly recognized it right away. She had smelled that smell many times before.

Jilly shouted out, "It's mint!" Everyone was so impressed. They cheered and cheered! Jilly had won the game.

From then on, whenever someone heard the smell of mint, they thought of Jilly! They remembered her competitive nature and how she was the first to recognize the smell.

Lily and Ben were playing in the garden. They liked to smell the roses and look for bugs. Lily saw a big rose with many petals. She wanted to pick it and give it to her mom.

"Look, Ben, a pretty rose!" she said. "I will take it to mom. She will be happy."

Ben shook his head. "No, Lily, don't do that. That rose is not ours. It belongs to the old lady next door. She is very mean. She will be angry if you take her rose. She will yell at us and maybe hurt us."

Lily did not listen to Ben. She thought he was just scared. She reached for the rose and pulled it hard. But the rose had many thorns. They pricked Lily's hand and made it bleed. Lily cried out in pain.

The old lady next door heard Lily's cry. She came out of her house and saw Lily holding her rose. She was very angry. She had an unknown thing in her hand. It looked like a stick with a sharp end. She pointed it at Lily and Ben.

"Who are you? What are you doing in my garden? How dare you steal my rose? You are bad children. I will teach you a lesson. Come here!" she shouted.

Lily and Ben were very scared. They dropped the rose and ran away. But the old lady was faster. She caught them and hit them with the unknown thing. It hurt a lot. Lily and Ben screamed and cried. They wished they had listened to Ben. They wished they had not taken the rose. They wished they had not made the old lady angry. They worried that they would never see their mom again.

Sara and Ben were twins who liked to play with their toys. They had many toys, but their favorite was a big velvet bear. The bear was soft and cuddly, and they named him Ted.

One day, Sara and Ben had a fight. Sara wanted to play with Ted, but Ben wanted to play with him too. They both pulled on Ted's arms, trying to take him away from each other.

"Let go of Ted! He is mine!" Sara shouted.

"No, he is mine! I found him first!" Ben yelled.

They pulled and pulled, until Ted's arms ripped off. Sara and Ben gasped. They looked at Ted, who had no arms left. They felt very sad and sorry.

They looked at each other, and saw tears in their eyes. They realized they had been very mean and selfish. They hugged each other and said, "I'm sorry, I love you."

They decided to unite Ted's arms with some thread and a needle. They worked together, and soon Ted had his arms back. They hugged Ted and said, "We're sorry, we love you too."

They learned to share and care for their toys and each other. They never fought over Ted again. They played with him every day, and he was happy. They were happy too. They thought Ted was the best toy ever, and not boring at all.

Once there was a little boy named Jack. He was the youngest sibling and often got jealous when his sister and brother were given special opportunities.

One day, Jack's mom said that if he wanted to join in on the fun they were having, he had to help clean up the park. Jack agreed that it would be fun and put on his cleaning gloves.

Jack started to clean but it was taking too long. He watched as his siblings finished quickly and started to play. Jack became jealous. He wanted to join in but he still had so much to do.

Then suddenly, Jack's mom told them about a shortcut. She said that if he cut the grass at the park, he could clean faster. Jack couldn't believe his ears! He quickly grabbed the scissors and started to cut the grass super fast.

Before he knew it, Jack had finished cleaning the park. He ran to where his siblings were playing and finally got to have some fun. He was so happy that he found the shortcut.

Once there was a little girl who was very poor. Every day she wished for something special. One day, she saw a shiny jewel lying in the dirt. She tried to pick it up, but it was so hard that she could not move it.

The little girl decided to tell her story to a kind old man who lived in the village. He listened carefully and decided he wanted to help her. So he asked the little girl to come back the next day.

True to his word, the old man brought the little girl a spade. Together they dug in the dirt until they uncovered the jewel. It was so beautiful!

The old man told the little girl that although it was hard to get something that we want, with patience and hard work, anything is possible.

The little girl was so happy and she thanked the old man for teaching her this valuable lesson. From then on, she never hesitated to put in the effort to achieve her goals.

Ben and Lily liked to play in the park. They liked to run, slide, swing and climb. They had a lot of fun with their friends. But they also had to listen to their mom and dad. They told them to stay in the park and not to go near the road.

One day, Ben saw a big truck on the road. It had many colors and pictures on it. It looked like a toy. Ben wanted to see it better. He ran out of the park and followed the truck. He did not hear his mom calling him.

Lily saw Ben running after the truck. She was scared. She knew the road was dangerous. She ran after Ben and shouted, "Ben, stop! Come back! The road is not for playing!"

The truck driver saw Ben and Lily on the road. He was tired. He had been driving for a long time. He tried to stop the truck, but it was too heavy and fast. He honked his horn, but Ben and Lily did not hear him.

The truck driver was very scared. He thought he would hit Ben and Lily. He swerved the truck to the side, but he lost control. The truck crashed into a tree. The driver was hurt. Ben and Lily were very lucky. They were not hurt, but they were very close to the truck.

Ben and Lily cried. They were sorry for what they did. They ran back to their mom and dad. They hugged them and said, "We are sorry. We were bad. We followed the truck. We did not listen to you."

Their mom and dad were angry, but they were also happy. They were happy that Ben and Lily were safe. They said, "We are glad you are okay. But you must never do that again. You must never follow a truck or any other car on the road. You must always stay in the park and listen to us. The road is not for playing. The road is for drivers. And drivers can be tired and make mistakes. You could have been hurt or worse. Do you understand?"

Ben and Lily nodded. They said, "We understand. We are sorry. We will never follow a truck again. We will always stay in the park and listen to you."

Their mom and dad hugged them and said, "We love you. We want you to be safe and happy. We want you to have fun, but also to be careful. That is the moral of the story."

Tom and Lily are friends. They like to play in the park. They have a red bike and a blue bike. They take turns to ride the bikes.

One day, Tom wants to ride the red bike. He says to Lily, "I want the red bike. It is faster than the blue bike. I can speed on the red bike."

Lily says, "No, Tom. It is my turn to ride the red bike. You had it yesterday. You can have the blue bike. It is nice too."

Tom is angry. He does not want the blue bike. He pushes Lily and takes the red bike. He rides away very fast. He does not look where he is going.

Lily is sad. She cries. She has a scratch on her face. She picks up the blue bike and walks to the bench. She sits down and waits for Tom.

Tom speeds on the red bike. He feels happy. He thinks he is the best rider. He does not see the big rock on the path. He hits the rock and falls off the bike. He hurts his knee and his elbow. He also has a scratch on his face. He cries too.

He sees Lily on the bench. He feels sorry. He walks to her with the red bike. He says, "I am sorry, Lily. I was mean to you. I should have shared the red bike with you. Are you okay?"

Lily looks at Tom. She sees his scratch and his tears. She says, "I am okay, Tom. I am sorry you got hurt. I should have let you ride the red bike for a while. Are you okay?"

Tom and Lily hug. They are friends again. They decide to ride the bikes together. They take turns to speed on the red and the blue bike. They have fun. They are nice to each other.

Once upon a time, there was a hairy bear who lived in the woods. He liked to sing and play all day long. One day, he heard the police coming and he got very scared.

The bear said to the police, â€œLet me go! I donâ€™t want to get into any trouble!â€ The police said, â€œWe just want to help. We will take care of you.â€

The police took the bear to the doctorâ€™s office. The doctor gave the bear a checkup and made sure he was safe. 

Then, the police drove the bear back to his home in the woods. Before they said goodbye, the police said, â€œStay out of trouble and be happy!â€

The bear was so happy that he started singing and dancing. He thanked the police for their help and ran off into the woods. From that day on, he always stayed out of trouble and was never scared of the police again.

One day, a mommy warned her three-year-old about an old fan. She said, "It's very old and could be dangerous."

The mommy was fearful that it could hurt her little one. So she asked him to stay far away from it.

The three-year-old was a curious boy, and he wanted to see what it looked like. So he quietly tiptoed over to take a peek.

But then he heard his mommy's voice again. She warned him to come back, in a voice that sounded stern. He knew that he shouldn't ignore her warning, so he ran back to the safety of his mommy's arms. 

The three-year-old was glad he had listened to his mommy. He would never forget her warning about the old fan.

One day, Jack and his dad went for a walk in the woods. Jack saw a big tree and decided to climb it. He got to the top and he could see everywhere. He saw a really cool animal. It was a deer! Jack thought it was so cool, so he got his dad's spear and he decided to try to catch the deer.

But the deer was very fast and it ran away. Jack's dad laughed and said it was crazy to try and catch the deer. Jack's dad was sad because Jack was too little. He was only 3 years old.

Jack started to feel sad too, but then he realized something. He'd had so much fun trying to catch the deer. His dad was right, it had been a crazy idea! But it didn't matter. Jack had still had a great time and he smiled.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim and his mom went to the store. They wanted to buy a toy. Tim saw a toy car. It was blue and icy. Tim liked the icy toy car. He asked his mom, "Can I have the car?" His mom looked at the price. The price was low. She said, "Yes, you can have the car."

When they got home, Tim was very happy. He wanted to play with his new toy car. He asked his mom, "Can I unpack the car now?" His mom said, "Yes, you can unpack the car." Tim unpacked the car. He played with it all day.

At night, Tim put his icy toy car next to his bed. He said goodnight to his mom. He was very happy with his new toy. Tim went to sleep with a big smile on his face.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Pete. He was very little, only three years old! While playing outside, Pete got very sleepy. So, he settled in the grass and decided to take a nap. While Pete was napping, a rude boy came and tried to wake him up. But Pete's body was too heavy and the rude boy couldn't wake him.

Eventually, Pete woke up. He smiled and rubbed his eyes, then he sat up and asked the rude boy why he was trying to wake him. The boy said he just wanted to play. Pete smiled, said he was tired and suggested the boy take a nap too!

The two boys cuddled up together and took a nap in the sun. When they woke up, Pete and the rude boy were best friends. From then on, the two boys would always take a nap together after they played!

Once upon a time there was a miserable little pig. He wanted to print a picture of a palace. He looked everywhere for one, but he couldn't find one. Everywhere he looked he saw rivers, trees and houses.

Finally, he saw something up in the sky. It was a palace! He was so excited he wanted to print it right away. He found some paper and a printer and put them together. 

The pig pressed the button on the printer and a beautiful picture of the palace printed out. He was so happy that he did a little dance. Now, he could always look at the palace whenever he wanted.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to jog with his dog, Spot. They would jog every day in the park. Tim and Spot were very happy when they jogged.

One day, a big angry dog came to the park. The angry dog did not behave. It barked and growled at Tim and Spot. Tim and Spot were scared and stopped jogging.

Tim's mom saw the angry dog and said, "You must behave!" The angry dog listened to Tim's mom and stopped being mean. Tim and Spot were happy again. They went back to their jog and had a fun day in the park.

Once upon a time, there was a princess. She had lots of things to do, but she was bored. She wanted to do something different. 
The princess thought of a great idea. She decided to make an unusual thing. She gathered lots of things and started to make her unusual thing. She mixed and stirred, and put together lots of pieces. 
After a while, the princess finished making her unusual thing. She was very proud of what she had made. She showed everyone her unusual thing. 
The princess and everyone else were so happy! They were amazed at what the princess had made. 
From that day on, the princess made lots of unusual things. Everytime she made something she felt very proud and happy.

John and his mom were in the car, ready to travel to the beach. 

John: â€œMom, can I bring my bug with me?"

Mom: â€œSure, sweetheart! Just make sure you donâ€™t let it go!â€

John and his mom drove for a long time until they arrived at the beach. After spending the day in the sun, John saw something on the ground - it was a bug!

John: â€œMom, look â€“ itâ€™s a bug!"

Mom: â€œOh no! You must have let your bug go, John. You feel guilty now that itâ€™s lost.â€

John felt sad and guilty at the same time. He wished he had been careful with his bug. Together, John and his mom looked around until they finally found it and were able to bring it home safe and sound.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she found some paper in her room. The paper was very interesting because it had lots of colors on it.

Lily wanted to make something with the paper. She got some glue and started to mix it with the paper. She folded the paper and cut it into shapes. 

After a while, Lily had made a beautiful paper butterfly. She was very happy and showed it to her mom. Her mom said it was very pretty and interesting too. Lily was so proud of her creation and decided to make more things with paper.

Once upon a time there was a fierce hut that lived on the edge of a big forest. The hut was made of sticks and was so fierce that it scared away the animals.

One evening when the sun was about to set, a brave little girl remembered where she had seen the hut before. She took a deep breath and started walking towards it. The little girl wasn't scared.

When she finally reached the hut, the little girl looked inside. Although the hut was small, it was filled with lots of warm blankets and food.

The little girl brought her friends to the hut the next day and they all laughed and played there. They decided to make it their secret club house and the fierce hut became their happy hideaway.

From then on the brave little girl remembered how she had found the hut and the adventures she and her friends had there. The little girl had made a true friend in the fierce hut.

Once upon a time, there was a girl who loved to count. She counted everything she couldâ€”tiny stones on the ground, fluffy clouds in the sky, and small leaves floating in the wind.

One day, the girl decided to count birds. She saw a small flock of birds on the ground and decided to count them. She carefully started to count-one, two, three-but she was too slow. The birds flew away before she could finish.

The girl kept trying to count the birds, but it was too hard. The ground was too soft and flexible and the birds were too fast. The girl was feeling sad when she heard a tiny voice say, â€œI can help.â€

It was a tiny butterfly. It said, â€œI can help you count if you are careful. Butterflies are fragile like glass and can be easily frighted away. But I will help you if you are gentle.â€

So the girl and the butterfly started counting. Slowly and carefully, the girl and the butterfly counted the birds until all of them were counted. The girl was so happy. She thanked the butterfly for helping her and together they watched the birds fly away in the sky.

Once upon a time there was a pot. The pot was jolly and it could zoom. The pot zipped around town, zooming faster than a bee.

One afternoon, the pot met a kitten. They both meowed at each other and the pot asked, "Can I join you?" The kitten said, "Yes! Come on, let's play!"

The kitten and the pot zoomed around town together. They ran past trees, hopped over a river, and dashed through the park. The pot was so happy that it could hardly keep up with the kitten.

Finally, the duo stopped at a big tree. They turned to each other and said, "That was fun! Let's do it again soon!" The pot smiled and said, "Yes, let's zoom again soon!" 

And that's what they did. The pot and kitten would zoom around town every day, enjoying their jolly adventures.

Once upon a time, there was a graceful pumpkin. He was so happy, he wanted to explore the world. One day, he dared to leave his patch. He rolled and rolled, until he came to a big green field.

The pumpkin saw a lot of new things. He saw tall trees, flying birds, and a small pond. He sat by the pond and watched the ripples. They were so peaceful. 

But then, he saw something he had never seen before. It was a big, orange cat with long ears. The cat was so graceful, it almost looked like the pumpkin. The pumpkin was scared, but decided to dare and say hello anyway. 

The cat was very friendly. The cat told the pumpkin about all the new things he could see and explore. The pumpkin was so excited, he asked the cat to be his friend and explore the world together. 

And so, the graceful pumpkin and the big orange cat went off to explore the world together. What fun!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy who loved to play with his toys. One day, he found a big cabinet in his house. He opened it and saw a lot of colorful jars inside. Timmy wanted to touch them, but his mom told him to be careful.

Timmy tried to be careful, but he accidentally knocked over one of the jars. It made a loud sound and his mom came running. She was very angry and told Timmy to go to his room. Timmy felt sad and wished he had been more careful.

The lesson Timmy learned was to always listen to his mom and be careful. He promised to be more careful in the future. From that day on, Timmy would clap his hands whenever he remembered to be careful.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to paint and would spend hours making pictures with his colors. One day, Timmy's friend Billy came over to play. Billy wanted to play with Timmy's drum, but Timmy didn't want to share. Billy got mad and started to cry.

Timmy felt bad and wanted to make Billy happy again. He had a smart idea! He decided to paint a picture of Billy playing the drum. Timmy worked hard on the painting and when he was finished, he showed it to Billy. Billy was so happy and stopped crying. He loved the painting and felt better about not being able to play with the drum.

From then on, Timmy and Billy played together happily. Timmy learned that sharing is important and that he could use his painting skills to make others happy. And Billy learned that there are other ways to enjoy playing besides just playing with a drum.

Once upon a time, there was a shy cat named Kitty. She lived in a small house with a porch. Kitty loved to rub her soft fur on the porch steps.

One sunny day, Kitty saw a little boy named Timmy walking by. Timmy saw Kitty on the porch and said, "Hi, Kitty! Can I play with you?" Kitty felt shy, but she wanted to play with Timmy too.

So, Kitty let Timmy rub her soft fur gently. They played together on the porch and became good friends. From that day on, Kitty was not shy anymore, and she loved playing with Timmy every day.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Lila. She was only three years old but she loved to play all the time. 

One day, Lila's mommy told her, "Lila, it's time to behave. I have to go to work, so you need to be good."

Lila said, "Okay!", and she put on her top. Then she grabbed her toys and went outside to play in the garden.

She ran around, exploring the garden and having fun. Then, out of nowhere, a big angry dog came running towards Lila. She was so scared!

Lila shouted, "Help! That dog looks terrible!"

But luckily her dad was nearby and he heard her. He ran over and saved her.

He said, "Lila, it's important to always behave or else things like this can happen."

Lila smiled and said, "Yes, Daddy. I'll be good from now on." And she hugged him tight.

Once upon a time, in a fair land, there was a pretty lily. The lily lived in a big garden with many friends. They all played and laughed together every day.

One day, a new friend came to the garden. His name was Spike, and he was a sharp cactus. Spike wanted to play with Lily and her friends, but they were scared of his sharp parts. "I don't want to get hurt," said one of the flowers.

Spike felt sad, but Lily had an idea. "Let's play a game where we don't need to touch," said Lily. So, they all played a fun game of hide and seek. Spike was very good at hiding, but Lily was the best at finding her friends.

From that day on, Lily, Spike, and all their friends played together every day. They learned that even if someone looks different, they can still be a good friend. And they all lived happily ever after in their fair garden.

Once upon a time, there was a kind little boy called Adam. He wanted to share his things with other people. So he went to his room and took out his dictionary. Adam was very proud of it, because it was nice and tight.

He went outside and saw his friend Ben. Adam called him and showed him the dictionary. Ben was very excited and he asked for a turn. So Adam let him hold the dictionary, and Ben was so happy! Adam felt good inside.

Adam shorted the dictionary to his next friend, Jemima. She liked it too. She hugged Adam and thanked him for sharing. Adam smiled and they went off to play.

Adam continued to share his dictionary with others. He wasn't afraid to give it away. He found that when he shared things with his friends, they all felt happy. Adam was very proud of himself!

Lily and Ben went to the park with Mom. They saw a pond with many ducks. Lily and Ben liked ducks. They wanted to feed them bread.

"Can we feed the ducks, Mom?" Lily asked.

"Sure, but be careful and gentle. Don't scare them or chase them," Mom said.

Lily and Ben took some bread from Mom and walked to the pond. They saw a big duck with a green head and a yellow beak. He looked very hungry.

"Hello, duck. We have some bread for you. Do you want some?" Lily said.

The duck nodded and quacked. He swam to Lily and Ben. They threw some bread to him. He ate it very fast.

"Wow, you are a hungry duck. What is your name?" Ben asked.

The duck did not answer. He just quacked louder and louder. He wanted more bread.

"Hey, that's rude. You should say your name and thank us for the bread," Ben said.

The duck did not care. He bit Ben's finger and took the bread from his hand. He swam away.

"Ow, that hurts. He bit me. He is a mean duck," Ben cried.

Mom came and hugged Ben. She put a band-aid on his finger.

"I'm sorry, Ben. That was a very rude duck. He did not introduce himself or say thank you. He was not nice at all," Mom said.

Lily and Ben did not like the rude duck. They looked for another duck to feed. They saw a small duck with a brown head and a white neck. She looked very friendly.

"Hello, duck. We have some bread for you. Do you want some?" Lily said.

The duck nodded and quacked. She swam to Lily and Ben. They threw some bread to her. She ate it very slowly.

"Thank you for the bread. You are very kind. My name is Daisy. What are your names?" the duck said.

Lily and Ben smiled. They liked Daisy. She was a polite duck. She introduced herself and said thank you. She was very nice.

"I'm Lily and this is my brother Ben. We like ducks. You are a very nice duck, Daisy," Lily said.

"Thank you, Lily and Ben. You are very nice too. Do you want to be my friends?" Daisy asked.

Lily and Ben nodded and quacked. They wanted to be Daisy's friends. They fed her more bread and played with her. They had fun.

Mom watched them and smiled. She was happy that Lily and Ben found a nice duck to feed. She was proud that they were polite and gentle. She hoped that the rude duck would learn to be nicer too.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She was very silly and liked to do funny things.

One day, the little girl had an idea. She wanted to have her own license! So, she grabbed a piece of paper and a pen and started to draw. 

But then the silly little girl started to tear the paper into little pieces. She was very sad and started to cry.

Luckily, her mom noticed what happened. She gave the little girl a hug and took her to the store. In the store, they got a special license for the little girl.

The little girl was very happy! She couldn't wait to show her new license to all her friends. From then on, she was always very careful with her new license.

Sara and Tom were playing in the park. They liked to run and jump and slide. They saw their shadows on the ground. They made funny shapes with their bodies.

"Look, I can make a bird!" Sara said.

"I can make a dog!" Tom said.

They laughed and had fun.

But then a big cloud came and covered the sun. Their shadows disappeared. They could not see them anymore.

"Where did they go?" Sara asked.

"I don't know. Maybe they are hiding." Tom said.

They looked around, but they could not find their shadows. They felt sad and scared.

They wanted to go home, but they did not know the way. They had run too far from their mom and dad. They had not listened when they said to stay close.

They saw a man walking by. He had a dirty coat and a dirty hat. He had a dirty bag in his hand.

"Excuse me, sir. Can you help us?" Sara said.

The man stopped and looked at them. He smiled a bad smile.

"Sure, I can help you. Come with me. I know where your shadows are." He said.

He took their hands and led them away. He did not take them to their shadows. He took them to a dirty place. He locked them in a dirty room. He said he would not let them go.

Sara and Tom cried and cried. They wished they had never left their mom and dad. They wished they had never played with their shadows. They wished they could improve their situation. But they could not. They were stuck in the dirty place with the bad man. They did not know what he would do to them. They were very afraid.

Once upon a time there was a mom and a baby. The baby was very tired and wanted to lay down. Mom helped the baby to lay on the bed. She gave the baby a soft shirt to wear and tucked her in.

The baby yawned and smiled as she snuggled into the shirt. The shirt was so warm and cosy. The baby's eyes drooped and soon she was fast asleep.

Mom kissed the baby's forehead, happy that the baby was getting the rest she needed. Mom stood up, feeling very tired herself. With a big stretch, she sighed and decided to lay down for a nap too.

Once there was a black cat called Mimi. Mimi didn't have a home and she hadn't had anything to eat for a long time. She was very worry and she was getting weak.

Mimi decided to make a journey across the meadow to the farm. When she got there, she saw a nice big barn with lots of food inside.

Mimi was very brave and she walked right up to the front door. She demanded that the farmer let her in to get some food. The farmer was surprised but he agreed.

Mimi was very relieved and happy when she left the barn with a full stomach. She never forgot how brave she was and she never went hungry again.

Once upon a time there was a bridge. It was very smooth. All the animals wanted to walk on top of it.

One day a little mouse was walking across the bridge. He saw a big dog on the other side and the little mouse wanted to show the dog how brave he was. He bowed to the big dog and kept walking.

The big dog didn't like the little mouse and he chased him to the other side. The little mouse was so scared and screamed for help. Unfortunately no-one was around to help him.

The big dog finally caught up with the little mouse and he was so angry. He barked very loudly and the little mouse screamed and ran away as fast as he could.

But it was too late. The big dog had been too fast and the little mouse was never seen again.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Lucy. She was only three years old and she always wanted to play. 

One day Lucy was playing hide and seek with her teddy bear. She knew the perfect hiding spot, under a soft palm tree. She ran and hid behind the tree, and the teddy bear had to try and find her! 

Lucy was giggling and peeking out from behind the palm tree, but the teddy bear didn't see her. He searched and searched, but he couldn't find Lucy. 

But then, Lucy jumped out from behind the tree and she shouted, "Here I am!" 

The teddy bear laughed and hugged Lucy, and they played hide and seek together all day!

Once upon a time, there was a boy who had a round, soft rug. He loved to play on it. One day he wanted to do something different. He decided to number the rug. So, the boy got his markers and carefully he started to number each side of the rug. The boy was slow and precise. He must make sure that the numbers were neat and even. Finally, the number rug was complete and the boy was very happy. Every day he wakes up, jumps onto the rug and counts the numbers. It was so much fun to sit and relax on his special number rug!

Once upon a time, there was a big, furry bear named Bobo. Bobo was a very nice bear who lived in the woods. One day, he looked up at the sky and saw the big, round moon. Bobo thought the moon was very pretty.

Bobo wanted to show his friend, Bunny, the moon. He went to Bunny's house and said, "Bunny, come see the big moon!" Bunny hopped outside and looked at the moon. Bunny said, "Wow, Bobo! The moon is so pretty!"

But then, Bobo did something silly. He tried to jump up and touch the moon. He jumped and jumped, but he couldn't reach it. Bunny laughed and said, "Silly Bobo, you can't touch the moon!" Bobo felt embarrass, but he laughed too. They both had fun looking at the moon together.

Once upon a time, there was a small elf named Pixie. She was very good at solving problems. One day, Pixie saw something strange in the sky. She had never seen anything like it before.

Pixie looked closer and saw something moving in the light. "What is this?" she said out loud. She tried to make out what it was.

Suddenly, Pixie remembered that her friends had told her about something called motion. That was when things moved by themselves.

So Pixie decided to solve the mystery. She took out a magnifying glass and looked very carefully. After a long time of looking, Pixie finally saw what it was - a beautiful butterfly!

Pixie was so happy to have solved the mystery. She waved goodbye to the butterfly as it flew away, and smiled to herself.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to help her mommy cook in the kitchen. One day, her mommy asked her to put on her apron so she wouldn't get her dress dirty. Lily put on her apron and felt very grown up.

Mommy asked Lily to stir a pot on the stove. Lily stirred and stirred until her arm got tired. Mommy thanked her for helping and gave her a big hug. 

After they finished cooking, they sat down to eat. Mommy made a mild soup that was not too spicy for little Lily. Lily loved it and said "yum!" Mommy smiled and thanked her for being such a good helper in the kitchen.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys all day long. One day, her mom came into her room and saw that Lily was feeling restless.

Mom: "Lily, why are you feeling restless?"

Lily: "I don't know, Mommy. I just want to play with my toys."

Mom: "I understand, but it's important to rest your mind and body too. Let me teach you about gears."

Lily: "What are gears, Mommy?"

Mom: "Gears are like little machines that help things move. Just like how we need to rest to keep our bodies moving properly, gears need to rest too. If they don't rest, they can break and stop working."

Lily understood what her mom was saying and decided to take a break from playing with her toys. She learned that it's important to rest and take care of yourself, just like how gears need to rest to keep working properly.

Once upon a time, there was an ant who loved to climb. He loved to climb so much that he decided to build a tall tower. He asked his friends to help him, so they all started to build. They found a long string, and they worked hard to wrap it around the tower.

The ant climbed inside and up he went! He climbed the string to the very top and then he shouted with joy! He could see for miles and miles, it was so much fun!

But then the ant noticed something spicy on the string and he froze. He had found a chili pepper! He was so scared that he quickly came down the string. But then he realized that it tasted really good!

He had so much fun climbing the string and tasting the spicy chili pepper that he decided to climb the string again, this time to share it with all his friends. From then on, they would always climb the tower and taste the spicy chili pepper.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. One night Lucy was very sleepy, so she lay down in her crib. She wanted to go to sleep, but she was cold. 

Suddenly, Lucy saw something in her crib. It was a fake blanket! It looked like a real one, but it was made out of cloth. 

Lucy wrapped the fake blanket around her and got very warm. She lay in her crib and smiled with happiness. She soon fell asleep and had a wonderful dream. 

The next morning, Lucy woke up and put the fake blanket away. Then she lay back down in her crib and had a nice warm nap. 

The end!

Lily and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to make houses with twigs and leaves. They found a long twig that was good for the roof. Lily said, "This is mine. I found it first." Ben said, "No, it is mine. I saw it first." They both pulled the long twig and it broke in half.

Lily and Ben were sad and angry. They did not want to share the long twig. They did not want to play together anymore. They sat on the grass and looked away from each other.

A squirrel came by and saw the broken twig. He needed a twig for his nest. He picked up one half and ran away. Lily and Ben did not notice. Then a bird came by and saw the other half. He needed a twig for his nest too. He picked up the other half and flew away. Lily and Ben did not notice.

Lily and Ben looked up and saw that the long twig was gone. They looked around and saw the squirrel and the bird with their halves. They realized that they had been selfish and silly. They said, "We are sorry. We should have shared the long twig. We should have played nicely together." They hugged and said, "Let's find another twig and replace the roof. Let's make a bigger house and invite the squirrel and the bird to join us."

Lily and Ben learned that sharing is caring and that friends are more important than things. They had fun playing with the twigs and the animals. They were happy and proud of their house.

Mum and Dad were busy packing for their holiday.

"Look at all these things!" shouted Dad.

Mum smiled at him. "We have to stay here until it's all ready," she reminded him.

Dad nodded. He went over to their little girl and asked, "Can you help us? We need to stay focused and get it all done."

The little girl smiled and nodded. She started looking around the room, trying to work out the best way to help. Suddenly she spotted her favourite teddy bear.

"Teddy can stay here with me!" she said happily.

Mum and Dad smiled at each other. "Yes, that's a good idea," said Mum. "You can stay here with Teddy and look after him, while we get ready for the holiday."

The little girl hugged Teddy close and nodded. She watched happily as Dad and Mum continued their busy packing.

Henry was a naughty boy. He was always in trouble with his mum. One day, Henry got a new razor. He was excited so he decided to see what it could do. He ran to the living room but Mum saw him.

"Henry! What are you doing?" Mum asked.

Henry was scared. He knew he had done something wrong.

"I wanted to try my new razor," he said, feeling guilty.

Mum knew he was up to no good. She grabbed the razor and put it in a sack.

"No more razors for you, young man," she said.

Henry felt sad. He knew he had done something wrong again. He hung his head in shame. 

Mum shook her head. She was disappointed. But she gave Henry a hug and said, "I still love you, even if you make mistakes."

Henry felt better. He knew that his mum would always love him. He hugged her back and promised to try his best to be a good boy. 

Mum smiled. She knew that Henry was as naughty as ever but he had a very big heart.

Tim and Sue are twins. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big slide. Tim wants to go first. He runs to the slide and climbs up the ladder. Sue follows him.

"Wait for me, Tim!" Sue says. "We can slide together!"

But Tim does not wait. He slides down very fast. He likes the speed. He laughs and runs to the slide again.

Sue is sad. She wants to slide with Tim. She crawls to the slide and tries to climb up the ladder. But it is too high for her. She cannot reach the top.

"Help me, Tim!" Sue says. "Please!"

Tim hears Sue. He looks at her. He sees that she is stuck. He feels sorry for her. He is a generous brother. He slides down and runs to Sue. He helps her up the ladder. He holds her hand.

"Sorry, Sue," Tim says. "I was too fast. Let's slide together."

Sue smiles. She is happy. She hugs Tim. They slide down together. They have fun. They are good twins.

Once there was a wealthy girl called Anna. She loved to go out to dinner with her family. One day, they went to a special restaurant that had an amazing garden. The sun was shining, and it was very hot. 

Anna went to the garden and looked around. Suddenly, she heard a noise. 

"Splash!"

She looked and saw a boy standing in a big pool of water.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy who loved to go on adventures. He lived in the east, and one day he decided to go to the west. As he started off on his journey, he noticed a fragile flower. The flower was so beautiful, he decided to pinch it and take it with him.

The delicate flower continues to live on to this day, serving as a reminder to the little boy of his beginnings and the adventure he went on.

Lily and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toys in the living room. One day, they see a big jar of sugar on the kitchen table. They want to taste it.

"Let's get some sugar," Lily says. "It is sweet and yummy."

Lily has an idea. She gets a chair and puts it near the table. She climbs on the chair and tries to grab the jar. She stretches her arm as far as she can, but she still cannot touch it.

"Help me, Ben," she says. "Push the chair closer."

Ben pushes the chair a little bit, but he is not strong enough. The chair does not move much. Lily stretches more and more, but she still cannot get the sugar.

Suddenly, they hear a loud noise. It is their mom. She is coming back from the store. She has a big bag of groceries. She sees Lily and Ben on the chair and the table.

"What are you doing?" she asks. "You are not supposed to touch the sugar. It is not good for you."

She takes Lily and Ben down from the chair and the table. She hugs them and kisses them.

"I'm sorry, mom," Lily says. "We just wanted to try some sugar."

"I know, sweetie," mom says. "But sugar is not a toy. It is for baking and cooking. Too much sugar can make you sick and give you cavities."

She opens the bag and shows them what she bought. There are some apples, bananas, carrots, cheese, and bread. There is also a blue box with a picture of a cake on it.

"Look, I have a surprise for you," mom says. "We are going to make a cake together. It will have some sugar, but not too much. And it will have other good things, like eggs and milk and flour. Do you want to help me?"

Lily and Ben nod and smile. They forget about the jar of sugar. They follow mom to the kitchen. They wash their hands and put on aprons. They help mom measure, mix, pour, and bake. They have fun making the cake. They wait for it to cool down. Then they decorate it with frosting and sprinkles. They cut a big slice for each of them. They eat the cake and enjoy it. It is sweet and yummy.

They thank mom for the cake and the surprise. They hug her and kiss her.

"We love you, mom," they say.

"I love you, too," mom says. "You are my sweeties."
