Tom and Sam are friends. They like to play with toys and eat snacks. One day, they find a big yellow banana in the kitchen. They want to share it, but it is too big for them.

"Let's talk to Mom," Tom says. "Maybe she can cut the banana for us."

They go to the living room, where Mom is reading a book. They show her the banana and ask her to help them.

"Sure, I can help you," Mom says. "But first, you have to do something for me. You have to show me how fit you are. Can you do some jumps, some runs, and some claps?"

Tom and Sam nod. They like to move and have fun. They do some jumps, some runs, and some claps. Mom watches and smiles. She is proud of them.

"Good job, Tom and Sam," Mom says. "You are very fit and strong. Now, I will cut the banana for you. You can have half each."

She takes the banana and a knife. She cuts the banana in two. She gives one half to Tom and one half to Sam. They say thank you and take a big bite. The banana is sweet and yummy. They are happy and full. They hug Mom and go back to play with their toys.

One day, Jane wanted to take a walk in the park. It was a high day, so the sun was bright and warm. On the way, she felt an itch in her shoe. She took it off and saw a big bug! She jumped back and took a closer look. The bug had lots of little legs and was moving around quickly. Suddenly, it flew off and she took a deep breath. Relief! Jane continued her walk, enjoying the sunshine and the fresh air. She looked high into the sky at the birds flitting around above her. She made it to the park and took a seat on a bench. She watched the kids playing in the sand, then decided to take a nap in the sunshine. She fell asleep with a smile on her face.

Tom and Lily were friends who liked to play in the garden. They liked to smell the herbs that grew there, like mint and rosemary. They liked to see the sun shine on the flowers and the bees. They liked to hear the birds sing and the wind blow.

One day, Tom and Lily saw a new herb in the garden. It was tall and green, with purple flowers. It smelled sweet and spicy. They wanted to touch it and taste it, but they did not know what it was.

"Let's ask Mom," Tom said.

"No, let's try it ourselves," Lily said. "It looks yummy."

Lily picked a leaf and put it in her mouth. She made a face and spat it out. "Yuck! It's bitter and hot!"

Tom laughed. "You're silly, Lily. You should not eat things you don't know."

Lily felt angry and sad. She wanted to make Tom feel bad too. She saw a shiny red berry on the herb. She picked it and gave it to Tom. "Here, try this. It's sweet and juicy."

Tom trusted Lily. He took the berry and bit it. He felt a pain in his mouth and his throat. He dropped the berry and cried. "Ow! Ow! It hurts! It burns!"

Lily saw Tom cry and felt scared. She did not mean to hurt him. She wanted to help him, but she did not know how. She ran to the house and called Mom.

Mom came and saw Tom. She saw the herb and the berry. She knew what they were. They were poison. She was very angry and very worried. She took Tom to the car and drove to the hospital.

Lily stayed in the garden. She felt lonely and sorry. She wished she had not given Tom the berry. She wished she had listened to him. She wished they were still friends. She cried and cried. The sun did not shine for her anymore.

Once upon a time there was a smelly crab. He lived in a big sandy beach by the sea. The crab was always snapping at the fish that swam by. Every day his sharp claws snapped in the water.

One day the crab saw something shiny and bright. He crawled over to take a closer look and he saw that it was a gold coin. He quickly grabbed the coin with his claws and snapped it up.

The crab was so excited with his new treasure that he started to sing a happy song. Suddenly the crab heard a voice from the bushes. "Hey, that's my gold coin!" said the voice.

It was a little girl who was looking for her gold coin. She had dropped it while digging in the sand and and the crab had found it. The crab wanted to keep it but the little girl talked nicely and asked nicely so he agreed to give it back.

The little girl thanked the crab and gave him a big hug before she left with her gold coin. The crab stood there with a big smile on his face and snapped his claws a happy song.

One day, a little girl named Lucy wanted to bake a big stack of cookies. She was very anxious because she had never baked cookies before. She asked her mom, "Can you help me bake cookies, please?" Her mom said, "Of course, let's bake together!"

In the kitchen, they mixed flour, sugar, and butter. They made little balls of dough and put them on a tray. Lucy and her mom put the tray in the oven. They waited and watched as the cookies baked. The smell of cookies filled the air.

When the cookies were ready, they took them out of the oven. Lucy and her mom made a big stack of cookies on a plate. They were so proud of their work. Lucy shared the cookies with her family and friends. Everyone loved the cookies and they all had a great time.

Once, there was a little girl named Lucy. She loved playing in the rain. One day, when it was raining, Lucy went outside and spun around in the rain. The cool water soaked her and she laughed and twirled around.

But later, the rain stopped and it made Lucy sad. She wanted to keep playing in the rain. So Lucy stomped her feet and said, "Where is the rain?"

Then, Lucy heard a voice speaking. It said, "It's the season for rain, but now it's dull outside. Don't worry, the rains will come again soon."

Lucy smiled and waited for rain. When the rain did come again, she ran outside and spun around again in the rain. She felt so happy when she was soaked in the rain!

One day, a girl named Sue went to her mom's kitchen. She saw her mom kneel down to get a cup. The cup was for coffee. Sue thought coffee was dull. She liked juice better.

Sue's mom said, "Sue, I have a surprise for you later." Sue was excited. She thought about the surprise all day.

In the afternoon, Sue's mom called her to the kitchen. There was a big, bright cup with a straw. Sue's mom said, "Here is your surprise, Sue! It's a new cup for your juice!" Sue was so happy. She knew her mom's coffee cup was dull, but her juice cup was the best.

Sam had a plan to be successful. He decided to leave his house and find a maze. He thought that if he could find the maze, he could be successful. So, he packed his bag and set out on his adventure.

Sam searched and searched, but he couldn't find the maze. He was so tired from searching that he eventually lay down and rested. He wanted the maze to be close, but he couldn't find it.

Finally, he tried one last time and found the entrance to the maze. He started to walk through it, but the maze was too tricky and he got lost. He didn't know what to do and eventually gave up.

Sam sadly returned home without finding the maze. He wasn't successful because he couldn't find it. He was disappointed, but he still had his plan to try again and be successful.

Once there was a girl called Chloe. She was a happy and popular girl who loved lollipops. One day, her mum showed her an extra-big lollipop which she had bought especially for Chloe. Chloe was so excited!

She showed it to all of her friends and they were very jealous. Everyone wanted to try it, but Chloe wouldn't share it. She wanted to keep it all for herself.

So, Chloe and her mum went to the park and sat on the swings. Chloe enjoyed her lollipop until there was nothing left. When she was finishing it, she showed it to all of the children who had been watching her, and they all cheered.

Chloe had the most popular lollipop in the park!

Jenny and Ben were twins who liked to play together. They had a big calendar on the wall with pictures of animals and numbers. They used stickers to mark the days when they did something fun or good.

One day, Jenny saw that Ben had more stickers than her on the calendar. She felt angry and sad. She wanted to have more stickers too. She thought of a plan to get more stickers.

She went to the kitchen and found a lemon. She cut it in half and squeezed some juice into a cup. She added some water and sugar and stirred it. She made lemonade. She smiled and thought, "This will be a good way to get more stickers. I will share my lemonade with Ben and he will give me some of his stickers."

She took the cup and went to find Ben. He was playing with his toy cars in the living room. She said, "Hi, Ben. I made some lemonade for you. Do you want to try some?"

Ben looked at the cup and said, "Sure, thank you, Jenny. You are very nice. I like lemonade." He took the cup and drank some. He made a face and spit it out. He said, "Yuck! This lemonade is sour. It tastes bad. Why did you give me this?"

Jenny said, "I'm sorry, Ben. I thought you would like it. I recommend you drink some more. It is good for you. And maybe you can give me some of your stickers for making you lemonade."

Ben said, "No, Jenny. I don't like your lemonade. And I don't want to give you my stickers. You are not nice. You are mean. You tried to trick me. Go away."

Jenny felt sorry and ashamed. She realized that her plan was wrong. She said, "I'm sorry, Ben. I was jealous of your stickers. I wanted to have more too. But I should not have done that. I love you, Ben. Can you forgive me?"

Ben looked at Jenny and saw that she was crying. He felt sorry too. He said, "I love you too, Jenny. I forgive you. But don't do that again. And don't be jealous of my stickers. We can share them. We are twins. We are a team."

Jenny smiled and hugged Ben. She said, "Thank you, Ben. You are very kind. We are a team. And we can share our lemonade too. But next time, I will make it better. I will add more sugar and less lemon."

Ben smiled and said, "OK, Jenny. That sounds good. Let's go and get some more stickers. And maybe some cookies too."

They went to the kitchen and made some more lemonade and got some cookies. They shared them and put some stickers on the calendar. They were happy and proud. They learned a lesson. They learned to be honest and generous and not to be jealous. They learned to love each other.

Once upon a time, there was a deaf youth by the name of Joe. He was always very sad, because he couldn't hear like other kids his age. One night, his grandma came to visit him. She took him to an ancient forest nearby and said, "Come, young Joe, I will show you something special!"

Joe followed his grandma into the forest and soon they came upon a strange tree. Grandma said, "Close your eyes, Joe, and make a wish. Whatever you wish for will come true."

Joe closed his eyes tight and wished he could get his hearing back. When he opened his eyes, he gasped in surprise. His wish had come true! He could now hear everything around him! He was so happy that he ran back home to tell everyone the news.

From that day on, Joe was no longer a deaf youth. He could now hear birds chirping, people talking and even the wind rustling through the trees. Everyone was so happy for Joe!

One day, a girl named Lily went to the park. She was a little careless and dropped her toy. A boy named Tom saw the toy and picked it up. He wanted to show it to his new friend, Lily.

"Hi, I am Tom. I found your toy," said Tom. "Oh, thank you! I am Lily. You are very nice," said Lily. They both smiled and started to play together.

They played with the toy and had lots of fun. They were careful not to drop it again. Lily and Tom became good friends. They learned that being careful is important and that it is nice to help each other.

Lily and Ben were playing with their toy vehicles in the garden. They had cars, trucks, buses and bikes. They liked to make noises and pretend they were driving.

"Look, Lily, I have a big truck. It can carry many things. Vroom, vroom!" Ben said.

"I have a bus. It can take many people. Beep, beep!" Lily said.

They had fun moving their vehicles around the grass and the dirt. They made a road with some stones and a bridge with some sticks.

Then they saw something unusual in the sky. It was a big, shiny vehicle with wings and a tail. It made a loud noise. Whoosh, whoosh!

"What is that, Ben?" Lily asked.

"I don't know, Lily. It looks like a bird, but bigger and faster. And it has no feathers. Maybe it is a special vehicle. A flying vehicle!" Ben said.

They watched the flying vehicle as it moved across the sky. It looked like it was going far away. They wanted to see it better.

"Let's increase our eyes, Lily. Maybe we can see it more clearly." Ben said.

"How do we increase our eyes, Ben?" Lily asked.

"Like this. We make our hands into circles and put them around our eyes. Then we look through them. They are like glasses. They make things bigger." Ben said.

He showed Lily how to do it. They both put their hands around their eyes and looked at the sky. The flying vehicle looked bigger and closer. They could see more details. It had windows and doors and wheels.

"Wow, Ben, you are right. It is a special vehicle. A flying vehicle. It is amazing. I wonder where it is going and who is inside." Lily said.

"Me too, Lily. Maybe it is going to another place. A place we don't know. Maybe there are other people there. People who like flying vehicles." Ben said.

They kept looking at the flying vehicle until it disappeared behind some clouds. They felt curious and excited. They wanted to learn more about it.

"Maybe one day we can go in a flying vehicle, Lily. Maybe we can see other places and people. That would be fun." Ben said.

"Yes, Ben, that would be fun. But for now, let's play with our toy vehicles. They are fun too. And we have each other." Lily said.

They smiled and hugged. Then they went back to playing with their cars, trucks, buses and bikes. They were happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved to build. She would build every day with rocks, sticks, and leaves. She was very proud of her work, and she wanted to show it to her friend.

One day, she took her friend to the park, and they played together for a long time. They built towers, bridges and even a little pond in the ground. But when that pond was filled with water, it was very noisy.

The little girl's friend said, "Let's stop playing, it's too noisy here." The girl didn't understand. She said, "But why don't we just move away from the water?"

Her friend kindly replied, "No, we don't need to move away. We can keep playing, just not too loud, so that everyone can enjoy the park."

The little girl realized that her friend was right. To her, building was about more just making something nice. It was also about being kind and considerate to others in the area. From that day on, she made sure to always play and build without making too much noise. And that, is the moral of our story.

Sammy was a little bear with bright eyes. He was a very clumsy bear, but he was brave. He wanted to try and climb the tall tree in his garden. He tried to find something to help him climb, but he couldn't see anything he could use.

Then he saw his friend Annie. Annie had some glue with her. Sammy asked her if he could borrow some to use. Annie gave him a big smile and gave him some glue.

Sammy took the glue and started to stick it onto the tree. He stuck it on really carefully and made sure it was really secure. Then he started to climb the tree. He wobbled and wobbled as he went up, but he kept going and going until he reached the top.

He was very proud of himself. He had done it, he had climbed the tall tree! He shouted out with joy, for he had achieved the impossible.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there lived a famous dog named Max. Max was famous because he could find anything with his nose. People would ask him to find lost toys, food, and even mints.

One day, a big cat named Tom came to town. Tom liked to fight and cause trouble. He saw Max and wanted to fight him too. Max did not want to fight, but he wanted to keep the town safe and happy.

Max had an idea. He found a mint and gave it to Tom. Tom liked the mint very much. He did not want to fight Max anymore. They became friends and played together. The town was safe and happy again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Beth. She loved to explore and find interesting things. One sunny afternoon, Beth went into the forest to explore. 

Suddenly, Beth saw a big, scary witch sitting near a tree. The witch had a big, pointy hat and long, grey hair. Beth was scared and wanted to leave, so she stayed very still. 

The witch asked Beth if she wanted a delicious apple. Beth was very hungry and she said yes. She slowly walked towards the witch and took the apple. 

Suddenly, the witch said, "Stay right there! You must pay me with a hug if you want to leave." Beth was so scared that she couldn't move. She slowly hugged the witch, while the witch cackled with laughter. 

Beth was so scared that she ran away as soon as the hug was finished. Unfortunately, Beth had forgotten the apple and she was sad. She couldn't stay in the forest forever, so she eventually went home without the delicious apple.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She had a black candle in her hand. She said, "Let's go and rest!" The little girl set her black candle down and flopped on the bed. When she closed her eyes, she heard a voice. The voice said, "Don't forget me!" The little girl opened her eyes and picked up the black candle. She said, "Let's go and rest together!" So, the little girl and the black candle went outside and found a nice spot to sit and rest. 

The little girl held the black candle close and said, "Thank you for coming with me to rest." The black candle glowed and replied, "You're welcome, my friend." Then the sun began to set, and the little girl and the black candle watched the sky turn from blue to black. They rested for a few more minutes before the little girl stood up, blew out the black candle, and said, "Let's go home now." 

And so, the little girl and the black candle went home together and had a good night's rest.

Once upon a time, there was a little car named Red. Red loved to drive around and explore the world. One day, Red drove into a cold and dark cave. Suddenly, Red heard a loud noise and felt something strike the car. 

Red was scared and didn't know what to do. But then, Red saw a little bat hanging upside down. The bat had accidentally hit Red while flying around. Red realized that the bat was not trying to hurt the car. 

Red thought the bat was cute and wanted to be friends. So, Red asked the bat to come along for a ride. The bat agreed and they drove off into the night, with the cold air blowing through the car's windows. From that day on, Red and the bat were the best of friends and went on many adventures together.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird. The bird was very small and weak. It could not fly very high. One day, the bird saw its mother flying high in the sky. The bird wanted to fly like its mother.

"Mother, how can I soar like you?" asked the little bird.

"You must flap your wings and believe in yourself," replied the mother bird.

The little bird flapped its wings and tried to fly. It flew higher and higher until it was soaring just like its mother. The little bird was very happy and proud of itself. It thanked its mother for teaching it how to soar.

Once there was a little girl called Mandy. She had a wonderful model plane. Every day after school, she would take it out and throw it high into the sky. She loved to watch it soar up high, faster and faster. 

One day, Mandy was practising throwing her model plane, when suddenly she saw an eagle soaring in the sky. It was so beautiful, she decided she wanted to throw her plane higher so she could be like the eagle. 

But this time, her plane flew too high and too far away. Mandy began to worry. She searched everywhere, but the plane was gone. She was sad and upset. 

Suddenly, she heard a rustling sound in the nearby bushes. She looked over and saw her plane was safely perched on a branch. She was so relieved and quickly ran over to retrieve it. 

From then on, Mandy was very careful when throwing her model plane. She wanted to make sure it was safe and she never wanted to lose it again.

One day, Mommy and Baby were walking in the park. Baby saw a cat with a soft, velvet fur and said "Mommy, I like it!" Mommy said, "It sure is soft!" Baby said, "It's weird too!" 

Mommy smiled and said, "Yes, it's a bit weird. But God made it and we can thank him for it." Baby said, "Thank God for weird velvet cats!" 

Just then, a dog ran up to the cat and started barking. Baby got scared, but the cat seemed happy. He purred and rubbed against the dog. Baby said, "Mommy, that's weird!" 

Mommy smiled again and said, "Yes, that's a bit strange. They look like they're friends. It's nice that they can be so kind to each other. Let's thank God for that." 

Baby smiled and said, "Thank you God for weird velvet cats and kind dogs!"

One day, a thoughtful cat named Sam went for a walk. He saw the big, round moon in the sky. The moon was so pretty! Sam wanted to act like the moon.

Sam acted like the moon by walking slowly and being very quiet. He looked up at the sky and tried to be round like the moon. His friends, a dog and a bird, saw Sam acting like the moon. They laughed and wanted to act like the moon too.

The dog and the bird joined Sam in his moon walk. They all acted like the moon together, being quiet and round. They had a lot of fun under the big, round moon. Sam was happy that he could share his thoughtful moon walk with his friends.

Once there was a brave jeep. He was an old jeep and had been around for many years. One day he decided he wanted to have an adventure! He drove off into the night. 

Everywhere he looked, he could see animals and stars in the sky. After a while he came across a big hill. He wanted to climb the hill but it was too steep. He tried and tried but he couldn't make it to the top. 

Suddenly, he heard a loud noise. It was a group of brave soldiers in a jeep coming up the hill! The jeep was very strong and brave. He knew he would never be able to beat the jeep. So, he decided to surrender and let them drive up the hill.

The jeep and the soldiers climbed to the top of the hill. The jeep was very proud. He was no match for the brave jeep and the soldiers. He had surrendered but he learned what it meant to be brave.

Tom and Mia are friends. They like to play outside. But today, it is rain. Rain is wet and cold. They cannot go out.

"Rain, rain, go away. Come again another day," Tom sings. He looks out the window. He sees a big puddle. He wants to jump in it.

"Mia, look! A puddle! Let's go out and splash!" Tom says.

"No, Tom. We cannot go out. Mom said so. We will get sick," Mia says. She has a book. She likes to read.

"Books are boring. Puddles are fun. Come on, Mia. Please," Tom begs.

"No, Tom. I like books. Books are quiet. Puddles are loud. And wet. And cold. No, thank you," Mia says.

Tom is sad. He does not want to read. He wants to play. He thinks of a plan. He gets a towel. He rubs it on his hair. He rubs it on his arms. He rubs it on his legs. He rubs it on his feet. He is dry.

"Look, Mia. I am dry. I can go out. I will not get sick," Tom says.

He opens the door. He runs to the puddle. He jumps in it. He splashes. He laughs.

"Tom, come back! You are wet! You will get sick!" Mia shouts.

She drops her book. She runs to the door. She sees Tom. He is wet. He is cold. He is not laughing. He is sneezing.

"Tom, I told you so. You are sick. You need to come in. You need to get warm. You need to rest," Mia says.

She gets another towel. She wraps it around Tom. She rubs his hair. She rubs his arms. She rubs his legs. She rubs his feet. She is a good friend.

"Sorry, Mia. You were right. Books are better. Puddles are bad. Can you read to me?" Tom says.

"Sure, Tom. I will read to you. But next time, listen to me. And to Mom. Rain is not for playing. Rain is for staying in," Mia says.

They go inside. They sit on the couch. Mia reads to Tom. Tom listens. They are quiet. They are happy. The rain goes on.

Tim and Lily were playing in the park with their ball. They liked to kick the ball to each other and run after it. Sometimes they missed the ball and it rolled away. They had to be careful not to lose the ball or hit someone with it.

One time, the ball went too far and landed near a lady who was sitting on a bench. She had a big hat and a book. She looked up and saw the ball. She smiled and picked it up.

"Hello, children," she said. "Is this your ball?"

"Yes, it is," Tim said. "We are sorry. We did not mean to bother you."

"That's all right," the lady said. "You can have your ball back. But please be careful where you kick it. There are other people and animals in the park. You don't want to hurt them or make them angry."

"OK, we will," Lily said. "Thank you, lady."

The lady gave them the ball and they said goodbye. They ran back to their spot and decided to play a different game. They agreed to settle for catch instead of kick. They threw the ball to each other and caught it with their hands. They had fun and were careful not to let the ball go too far again. They liked the lady and hoped to see her again.

Once there was a bear named Brown. One day Brown decided to go on a walk. He did not know where the trail would lead him, but he was so very excited. He walked for a long time and started to hum a happy song.

Finally he arrived at a dark forest. He was scared but he bravely marched forward. Then he heard a noise! He looked around, peeking through the trees. He noticed something shiny in the distance.

It was a crowd of animals! They shouted and clapped their hands. Brown was so excited and joined in the applause. He waved his arms in the air and laughed and shouted.

The other animals soon joined in the fun and a great party began. Brown followed the trail back home, feeling very content. He had a great adventure and he was very proud of himself.

Tom and Lily love to perform for their family. They like to sing, dance and tell jokes. They make everyone laugh and clap.

One day, they decide to perform outside in nature. They find a big tree and use it as a stage. They pick some flowers and leaves and make costumes. They invite their mom, dad and dog to watch.

Tom sings a song about a funny frog. He hops and croaks and sticks out his tongue. Lily dances a dance about a funny bird. She flaps and chirps and spins around. They both tell jokes about funny animals. They make their family laugh and clap.

They have so much fun performing in nature. They hug their mom, dad and dog and say thank you. They are happy and proud. They love to perform.

Once upon a time, there was a model who lived in a big house. One day, when the model was doing her laundry, a thief sneaked into her house. The thief had a plan to steal something. She quickly crept around the house, looking for something to take.

The model came back into the house to find the thief. She saw the thief with a big bag and she was very confused. The model asked the thief what was in the bag, but the thief didn't say anything.

The model was even more confused. She shouted at the thief, but the thief ran off with the bag full of things. The model knew that the thief had tried to steal something from her house. She looked around, trying to work out what it was.

After a while, the model realised that the thief had stolen her favourite model. She was so confused and sad, but at least she knew what the thief had taken. She decided to call the police to help her get her model back.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Martha and a boy named Bob. They were best friends and loved to play together. One day they decided to have lots of fun, so Martha suggested they explore a tunnel. 

They raced to the tunnel, laughing and squealing with joy. They squeezed through the tiny entrance and soon enough they were in a dark, long tunnel. 

Martha and Bob were so excited! They ran down the dark tunnel, taking turns to lead the way. Suddenly, they came to a door at the end of the tunnel and Bob decided to open it. 

When the door opened they found themselves in a big room, but there was something strange in the room. On one side there was a big red seat, with two big chocolate cakes on it. 

Martha and Bob felt guilty. They knew this was not their cake and so they quickly stepped away from the seat and ran out of the room. 

As quickly as they had come, Martha and Bob ran out of the tunnel and raced home. They never ran back to the tunnel, because they felt so guilty.

Once upon a time, a little girl was playing with her doll outside. She loved to make the doll do all kind of things. One day she decided to give her doll a new house. She took a big box and looked for something to use to build a house.

Suddenly, she saw a big nail. She picked it up and knew just what to do. She pushed the nail in the box and nailed it in to make the walls. The little girl was so proud of what she had done.

Her mommy came out and saw the house. She said, "Wow, sweetheart, you did a great job! That house looks peaceful and pretty." The little girl was happy to hear her mom say that and smiled.

The little girl had made a beautiful house and was proud she did it all by herself. She now knew how to nail things together and was happy her house was peaceful and pretty.

Ben and Lily were playing soldiers in the garden. They had sticks for guns and hats for helmets. They ran and hid behind the trees and bushes, pretending to shoot at each other.

"Bang, bang, you're dead!" Ben shouted, pointing his stick at Lily.

"No, I'm not, you missed!" Lily said, dodging behind a flower.

"Yes, you are, I saw you fall!" Ben insisted, running after her.

They chased each other around the garden, making loud noises and laughing. Then they saw Mom standing by the door, holding a tray of cookies and milk.

"Time for a snack, kids!" Mom called. "Come inside and wash your hands."

Ben and Lily stopped playing and ran to the door. They were hungry and thirsty, and the cookies looked yummy.

"Mom, we were playing soldiers!" Ben said. "I was the good guy and Lily was the bad guy."

"Really? And who won?" Mom asked.

Ben looked at Lily and smiled. He knew she was his sister and he loved her, even if they played different sides.

"We both won, Mom," he said. "We decided to surrender and share the cookies."

Mom smiled and hugged them. She was proud of her kids for being kind and fair.

"Good job, soldiers," she said. "Now, line up and follow me to the kitchen. There's an open seat for each of you at the table."

Once upon a time there was a good angel who loved to care for people. She was always there when somebody needed help. 

One day, a small child named Joe was walking in the park. He was only three years old and seemed a bit lost. He was looking around and seemed worried. 

The angel noticed Joe and flew down to talk to him. She said with a gentle voice, "Hello Joe! Are you okay?"

Joe looked up at the angel with surprise. "I'm lost," he said sadly. 

The angel smiled kindly and said, "Don't worry Joe. I will help you. I will take care of you and show you the way home." 

Joe smiled back, feeling relieved. Together, the good angel and Joe found his way back home. 

The end!

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to watch cartoons on TV. Sometimes they fight over which cartoon to watch. Mom says they have to share and take turns.

One day, Anna and Ben find a hidden remote under the sofa. They are very happy. They think they can watch any cartoon they want. They sneak to the TV room when Mom is busy.

Anna wants to watch the cartoon with the princess and the dragon. Ben wants to watch the cartoon with the cars and the robots. They both press the buttons on the remote. The TV screen changes very fast. Anna and Ben stare at the TV. They are confused.

"What is happening?" Anna asks.

"I don't know. It's not working." Ben says.

They hear Mom coming. They are scared. They hide the remote under a pillow. Mom enters the TV room. She sees the TV screen. She is angry.

"Anna and Ben, what are you doing? You know you are not allowed to touch the remote. You have to ask me first. And why are you watching this strange cartoon? It is not for kids. It is for grown-ups. Turn it off right now!"

Anna and Ben feel sorry. They say sorry to Mom. They turn off the TV. They hug Mom. Mom hugs them back. She says they can watch a nice cartoon later, but only one. They have to agree on which one. Anna and Ben nod. They say they will share and take turns. They love Mom. Mom loves them.

Tom and Mia went to the big water park with their mom and dad. They saw many slides and pools and fountains. They wanted to have fun and get wet.

They saw a big pool with a sign that said "Dolphin Show". They asked their mom and dad if they could watch. Their mom and dad said yes and took them to the seats. They waited for the show to start.

Soon, they heard some music and saw some people in blue suits. They were the dolphin trainers. They had whistles and fish. They called the dolphins and the dolphins came out of the water. They were big and gray and had smiles.

The dolphins did many tricks. They jumped and spun and flipped. They made noises and waved their tails. They splashed the water and sprayed the people. Tom and Mia laughed and clapped. They liked the dolphins.

One of the dolphins came close to Tom and Mia. It looked at them and made a sound. It seemed to say hello. Tom and Mia said hello back. They reached out their hands and touched the dolphin. It felt smooth and wet. The dolphin sprayed them with water. Tom and Mia giggled. They said thank you to the dolphin. The dolphin nodded and swam away.

The show was over. The people in blue suits thanked the dolphins and the audience. They said the dolphins were very smart and fair. They said the dolphins liked to play and make friends. They said the dolphins needed clean water and good food. They asked the people to help protect the dolphins and the ocean.

Tom and Mia learned a lot from the show. They loved the dolphins. They wanted to see them again. They told their mom and dad that the dolphins were the best part of the water park. Their mom and dad agreed and hugged them. They said they were proud of them for being kind and curious. They said they had a great day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sue. Sue had a big, purple towel that she loved very much. She took her purple towel with her everywhere she went.

One sunny day, Sue and her friends went to the park to play hide and seek. Sue had a great idea. She would use her purple towel to help her hide. Sue found a big tree with lots of leaves and wrapped her purple towel around her.

Sue's friends looked and looked, but they could not find her. Sue was so good at hiding with her purple towel. After a while, Sue came out from behind the tree and waved her purple towel. Her friends laughed and said, "Sue, you are the best at hiding!"

From that day on, Sue always used her purple towel when she played hide and seek. She and her friends had lots of fun playing together at the park.

One day, a boy named Tim went to the store with his mom. He saw a green fruit called an avocado. Tim's tummy was hurt, so he asked his mom, "Can I eat this?"

His mom said, "I recommend you try it. It might help your hurt tummy feel better."

At home, Tim's sister, Sue, wanted the avocado too. They both wanted to eat it, but there was only one. Tim said, "My tummy hurts, so I should eat it." Sue said, "But I want it too!"

Mom came in and said, "I will buy more avocados tomorrow. You can share this one today." Tim and Sue shared the avocado, and Tim's hurt tummy felt better. They were happy to share and play together.

Once, there was a brave elephant. He wanted to go on an adventure. So he set off, walking very far.

He soon reached a tall mountain. He was scared to climb it, so he asked a friendly bird for help. "Will you answer me one thing?" he asked.

The bird agreed and the brave elephant asked, "How do I get over this tall mountain?"

The bird answered, "Climb up on my back and I will take you over it".

So the elephant climbed up onto the bird's back and the bird flew him over the tall mountain. When the elephant safely reached the other side, he thanked the bird for the help.

The brave elephant was so proud of himself for having the courage to go on an adventure. He had answered the mountain's challenge and now he was ready for more!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily was very chubby and loved to play dress up. She had a big box full of pretty dresses and would wear them all the time. 

One day, Lily wanted to make a special craft. She got some glue and some paper and started to make a pretty picture. She put glue on the paper and stuck on some sparkly stars. 

After Lily finished her craft, she went back to playing dress up. She put on a beautiful pink dress and twirled around. Lily was very happy and loved to play with her dresses and make crafts with glue.

Once upon a time there was a young boy called Tom. One day Tom wanted to go on a special adventure. He decided to enter a nearby forest with his kayak.
Tom was so excited as he paddled through the forest. Everything was so quiet! Suddenly he spotted something very unique. It was a shiny beetle with blue wings. Tom was mesmerized by the beauty of the beetle. 
He wanted to take the beetle back home with him. He carefully picked it up with his hands and put it in his kayak. Then Tom paddled away and went back to his house.
The end.

Once upon a time there was a jolly little girl called Sarah. She loved to pack her things up in a box so she could take them to new places.

One day she went to the park with her mommy and she saw a big pit in the ground. Sarah asked her mommy what it was - "I think it's a sandbox, my darling," said her mommy.

Sarah was so excited. She ran over to the pit, grabbed her box and started to pack it full of sand.

Mommy watched Sarah and said, "What are you doing?" Sarah said, "I'm packing a sandbox, Mommy!" 

Mommy smiled and said, "That's great! You're packing a jolly sandbox!" 

Sarah smiled back and said, "Yes, I am!" And she continued to pack until the pit was full of sand.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play dress-up and wear costumes. One day, she found a brilliant mask in her toy box. It was shiny and sparkly, and she loved it so much.

Lily's mom saw her wearing the mask and said, "Wow, that's a beautiful mask! How many masks do you have?" 

Lily replied, "I have a number of masks, but this one is my favorite because it's so pretty."

Later that day, Lily's friend came over to play. When she saw Lily wearing the mask, she said, "That mask is so cool! Can I wear it too?" 

Lily said, "Sure! Let's play a game where we both wear masks and pretend we're superheroes." 

So, Lily and her friend wore their masks and pretended to save the world from bad guys. It was so much fun! And Lily was happy to share her brilliant mask with her friend.

Once upon a time there was a little red rag. One day it decided to go on an adventure. It flew high up in the sky and ended up on the back of a big, white cloud. 

The rag thought that the cloud looked like a chair. So, it wriggled and squeezed, until it made a comfortable seat. From its new seat, the rag could see the entire world. 

The rag watched a farmer plant his fields. It saw a boat sail out into a sparkling sea. It watched two birds chase each other around the sky. The rag had the best seat in the house!

When the sun began to set, the rag decided it was time to head back home. It swooped down from the sky and landed softly in a meadow. 

The rag had had an amazing day and couldn't wait to tell everyone about its adventure!

Tim and Sam were brothers who liked to play outside. One day, they saw a big fire in the woods. They ran to see what was happening. They saw many trees and animals burning. They felt scared and sad.

"Look, Sam, there is a lot of ash on the ground. It is black and dirty. Do you think we can touch it?" Tim asked.

"No, Tim, we should not touch it. It is hot and bad. It can hurt us and make us sick. We should go back home and tell mom and dad," Sam said.

But Tim was curious and did not listen to Sam. He picked up a handful of ash and threw it in the air. He laughed and said, "Look, Sam, it is like snow. It is fun and pretty."

Sam shook his head and said, "No, Tim, it is not like snow. It is not fun and pretty. It is dangerous and ugly. You are being silly and naughty. Come on, let's go home."

But Tim did not listen to Sam. He ran to a big pile of ash and jumped on it. He said, "Look, Sam, it is like a hill. It is soft and high. I can see everything from here."

Sam sighed and said, "No, Tim, it is not like a hill. It is not soft and high. It is hard and low. You cannot see anything from there. You are being foolish and rude. Come on, let's go home."

But Tim did not listen to Sam. He sat on the pile of ash and said, "Look, Sam, it is like a chair. It is cozy and warm. I can sit here all day."

Sam cried and said, "No, Tim, it is not like a chair. It is not cozy and warm. It is cold and harsh. You cannot sit here all day. You are being stubborn and mean. Come on, let's go home."

But Tim did not listen to Sam. He sat on the pile of ash and did not move. He said, "No, Sam, I will not go home. I like it here. You are being boring and bossy. Go away and leave me alone."

Sam felt hurt and angry. He said, "Fine, Tim, I will go home. But you will be sorry. You will be lonely and dirty. You will be hungry and thirsty. You will be sorry."

Sam ran back home and told mom and dad what happened. They were shocked and worried. They went to the woods to find Tim. But they could not find him. They only saw a lot of ash and smoke. They called his name, but he did not answer. They looked for him, but he did not show. They searched for him, but he did not come.

They were sad and scared. They thought they lost him. They cried and prayed. They hoped he was safe.

But Tim was not safe. He was still sitting on the pile of ash. He was not happy. He was lonely and dirty. He was hungry and thirsty. He was sorry.

He wished he listened to Sam. He wished he went back home. He wished he was not silly and naughty. He wished he was not foolish and rude. He wished he was not stubborn and mean. He wished he was not sitting on the pile of ash.

He learned a lesson. He learned that fire is bad and ash is worse. He learned that curiosity is good but obedience is better. He learned that playing is fun but listening is important. He learned that he loved his brother and his family. He learned that he was sorry.

He hoped they would find him. He hoped they would forgive him. He hoped they would love him. He hoped he would not sit on the pile of ash.

Charlie the cat was feeling very sleepy. He needed to get some exercise, so he put on his trainers and decided to go for a jog. He jogged down the street, feeling the sunshine on his fur. He then spotted a big puddle, but he wanted to stay dry. So he hopped and skipped over it, and continued his jog.

Next, Charlie decided to visit his friend, the vet. He pushed open the door and saw all sorts of animals. He was curious to know what was going on, so he stood still and watched. One of the cats was having an x-ray. The vet was very quiet as he examined the x-ray.

Charlie continued his jog, feeling refreshed and energetic after his visit. He ran down his street and waved to all his neighbours. He eventually made it back home and hopped into bed. He was tired after his special jog, so he went to sleep with a smile on his face.

One day, there was a little boy who was playing in his tidy bedroom. He could hear the sound of a vehicle outside. Suddenly, he noticed that the window was open and the vehicle was still running! 

He ran to his mom and said "Mom, come quick! Someone left a vehicle running outside." Mom was very impressed by the boy's observant nature and how he was thinking of the safety of everyone around him.

Mom said, "Thankyou for telling me, son. It's very important to be aware of our surroundings and to look out for the people around us."

The boy nodded and said, "Yes, Mommy. We should always be aware when we're outside and look out for each other."

Mom and the boy smiled at each other and the boy went back to playing in his tidy bedroom. He had learnt a very important lesson that day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily was eating her breakfast when she accidentally dropped her spoon on the floor. The spoon was delicate and broke into many pieces.

Lily's mom came to see what happened and asked, "What happened, Lily?"

Lily replied, "I dropped my spoon and it broke. I didn't understand why it was so delicate."

Mom said, "It's okay, Lily. We can get you a new spoon. Just be more careful next time."

Lily liked to play with her truck. It was big and red and had four wheels. She liked to fill it with rocks and dirt and drive it around the yard. She was very happy with her truck.

One day, a new boy moved in next door. His name was Max. He saw Lily playing with her truck and he wanted it. He asked Lily if he could play with it, but Lily said no. It was her truck and she did not want to share it. Max was angry and he went away.

The next day, Lily was playing with her truck again. She saw Max watching her from his window. He had a mean look on his face. Lily did not care. She drove her truck to the other side of the yard, where there was a big hole. She wanted to dump her rocks and dirt into the hole.

But when she got there, she saw something scary. A big snake was in the hole. It had black and yellow stripes and a sharp tongue. It hissed at Lily and showed its teeth. Lily was very afraid and she dropped her truck. She ran away as fast as she could.

Max saw what happened and he smiled. He waited until Lily was gone and then he ran to the hole. He grabbed the truck and ran back to his house. He was very happy. He had the truck and Lily did not.

But when he got to his house, he saw something bad. The truck was open and the snake was inside. It had crawled out of the hole and into the truck. It was angry and it bit Max on the hand. Max screamed and dropped the truck. He ran to his mom and cried. He had a big bump on his hand and it hurt a lot.

Lily heard Max scream and she came back. She saw the truck and the snake and she felt sorry for Max. She went to him and said she was sorry. She said they could share the truck if he wanted. Max said he was sorry too. He said he was wrong to take the truck. He said he did not want the truck anymore. He said he wanted to be friends with Lily.

The snake slithered away and disappeared. Lily and Max hugged and said they were friends. They learned a lesson. They learned that being greedy and mean is bad. They learned that being kind and sharing is good. They learned that snakes are scary and they should stay away from them.

Jane had a kitten and she loved it very much. Everyday, she would play with it and cuddle it. One day, Jane took the kitten to play a game with her friends. The game was to see who could win. Jane and the kitten tried their best, and they were winning! Finally, Jane and her kitten won the game! However, they were both very disgusted with the prize they had won. It was an ugly toy that no one wanted. But, Jane loved her kitty so much that she kept the disgusting toy anyway. Jane and her kitten were so happy to have won together.

Lily and Max were hungry. They wanted to eat some soup. Mommy made them yummy soup with carrots and noodles. She put the soup in two bowls and said, "Be careful, it's hot."

Lily and Max sat at the table and waited for the soup to cool down. They smelled the soup and said, "Mmm, it smells good." They took their spoons and started to eat.

But then, something strange happened. Lily's spoon disappeared! She looked at her hand and saw nothing. She looked at her bowl and saw nothing. She looked at Max and said, "Max, where is my spoon?"

Max looked at Lily and saw her empty hand. He looked at her bowl and saw her soup. He looked at his spoon and said, "I don't know, Lily. Maybe it's magic."

Lily and Max were puzzled. They wondered how the spoon could disappear. They looked around the room and saw nothing. They looked under the table and saw nothing. They looked at Mommy and said, "Mommy, Lily's spoon disappeared!"

Mommy looked at Lily and Max and smiled. She said, "Don't worry, my little ones. It's not magic. It's a trick. I have a magnet in my pocket. I can make the spoon stick to it. See?" She pulled out the magnet and showed them the spoon.

Lily and Max were amazed. They said, "Wow, Mommy, that's cool. How did you do that?"

Mommy said, "It's a secret. But I'll tell you later. Now, finish your soup. It's yummy and good for you."

Lily and Max nodded. They took their spoons and ate their soup. They said, "Thank you, Mommy, for the soup and the trick. We love you."

Mommy said, "I love you too, my little ones. You're very smart and curious. And you're very good at eating your soup."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play hide and seek with her friends. One day, she was playing in her room when she heard a noise. She peeked under her bed and saw her cat, Mittens, hiding there.

"Hi, Mittens! What are you doing under there?" Lily asked.

Mittens meowed and Lily giggled. She decided it was time to tidy up her room so she could play with her toys. She put her dolls in their box and her blocks in a pile. 

After she finished, Lily sat on her bed and looked around. "My room looks so tidy now," she said to Mittens. "Let's play peek-a-boo!"

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play and share. One day, they go to the market with Mom. Mom gives them some money to buy something they want.

Anna sees a big, red apple. She loves apples. She gives the money to the man and takes the apple. She is happy.

Ben sees a small, yellow toy car. He loves cars. He gives the money to the woman and takes the car. He is happy.

They go back to Mom. Mom smiles and says, "What did you buy?"

Anna shows her apple and says, "I bought an amazing apple. It is big and red and sweet. Do you want some?"

Ben shows his car and says, "I bought an amazing car. It is small and yellow and fast. Do you want to play?"

Anna and Ben look at each other. They both want to try the other's thing. They decide to share. Anna gives Ben a bite of her apple. Ben gives Anna a turn with his car. They both say, "Thank you!"

Mom hugs them and says, "You are amazing twins. You are kind and generous. Sharing is caring. I am proud of you."

Anna and Ben smile and hug Mom. They are happy. They learned a good lesson. They enjoy their apple and car together. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside. One day, he went outside and saw lots of acorns on the ground. He wanted to gather them all up in his little bucket.

Timmy ran back inside to get his bucket. He found his cap on the floor and put it on his head. Then, he went back outside and started to gather all of the acorns. He was so happy to see how many he could collect.

When Timmy was finished, he went back inside and put his bucket on the table. He opened it up and counted all of the acorns. He had gathered so many! Timmy was very proud of himself and couldn't wait to show his mommy and daddy.

Once upon a time there was a crab. The crab wanted to have a clean house. It would do many things to make it clean. The crab found some water and got its shell wet. Then it scrubbed and scrubbed until it sparkled. It also found some sand and dusted the floor of its house. Lastly, it found some leaves and put them on the floor.

The crab looked around and saw how clean its house had become. It smiled happily and said to itself, "My house is so clean!" Then it snuggled into a corner and went to sleep.

The end.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who loved to run. Everywhere she would go she'd run and run, so fast that she couldn't be stopped.

One day, she ran up to a big house. She ran all the way to the fireplace and stopped. It was so big and made her feel small.

The fireplace was on and it was hot. But, when she looked closely, she saw it was very harsh. Even though it made her feel scared, she reached out and touched it. She burned her hand and started to cry. 

The little girl slowly backed away from the fireplace and ran in the opposite direction. She was scared, but she was glad she learned her lesson.

The little girl never ran too close to a fireplace again!

Once upon a time there was a big, mighty bow. It was so big, it looked like it was made for giants! One day, a girl named Lucy saw the bow and decided to paint it. She got out her paint set and gave it a good look.

Lucy started painting with bright and colorful colors. She painted big, green leaves on one part of the bow and orange and yellow shapes on the other. She was so happy when she finished! Lucy beamed at her work and couldn't wait to show it to her friends.

The next day, Lucy's friends came over to look at the bow. Everyone was so amazed and impressed with Lucy's painting - they said it looked like a masterpiece! From then on, the bow was known as Lucy's mighty bow.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a big smile and rosy cheeks, but she felt lonely because she had no friends to play with. One day, she went to the park and saw a little boy sitting on a bench, looking sad.

Lily went to the boy and asked, "Why are you sad?" The boy replied, "I lost my toy car and I can't find it." Lily said, "I understand how you feel. I lost my favorite doll once."

The boy looked at Lily's lip and said, "You have a pretty lip." Lily smiled and said, "Thank you. Do you want to play with me? We can look for your toy car together." The boy's face lit up and he said, "Yes, please!"

Lily and the boy had so much fun playing together and they found the toy car too. From that day on, they became best friends and never felt lonely again.

Lily and Tom were bored. They wanted to play, but it was raining outside. They asked their mom if they could go to the attic. Mom said no. She said the attic was dark and dusty and had many things that could hurt them. She said they could play with their toys in their room.

But Lily and Tom did not listen. They waited until mom was busy in the kitchen. Then they sneaked up the stairs to the attic. They opened the door and saw a big pile of boxes and bags. They thought it looked like fun. They started to dig and pull and throw things around.

They found old clothes and hats and books and toys. They tried them on and made funny noises. They did not hear mom calling them from downstairs. They did not hear the thunder and lightning outside. They did not hear the roof leaking and dripping water on the floor.

They only heard a loud crash when they knocked over a big lamp. The lamp broke and made sparks and smoke. Lily and Tom screamed and ran to the door. But the door was stuck. They pushed and pulled, but it did not open. They were scared and cried for help.

Mom heard them and ran up the stairs. She saw the smoke and smelled the fire. She grabbed a hammer and broke the door. She pulled Lily and Tom out of the attic. She hugged them and said they were safe. But she was also angry and sad. She said they were very naughty and did not listen. She said they could have been hurt or burned. She said they ruined many things that belonged to grandma and grandpa. She said they would regret what they did.

Lily and Tom felt sorry and ashamed. They said they were sorry and did not mean to cause trouble. They said they just wanted to have fun. They said they loved mom and grandma and grandpa. Mom said she loved them too, but they had to learn to obey and be careful. She said they had to help clean up the mess and fix what they could. She said they had to say sorry to grandma and grandpa too.

Lily and Tom nodded and hugged mom. They followed her downstairs. They saw the firemen and the police and the neighbors outside. They saw the hole in the roof and the water on the floor. They saw the broken lamp and the burned boxes and bags. They wished they had never gone to the attic. They wished they had listened to mom. They wished they could go back in time and do things differently. They regretted what they did.

Once upon a time, there was a girl called Ruby. Ruby was very happy because today was a special day.

Ruby went to the park with her mummy and daddy. As they walked, Ruby saw some weird birds in the blue sky.

Suddenly, Daddy said: "Oh look! An old notebook has fallen from the sky!"
Ruby and Mummy ran to pick it up.

It was a very special notebook - the pages were filled with strange symbols. Ruby and Mummy and Daddy looked at each other. They were all so excited!

Mummy said: "Let's take this notebook home, let's see what it has to say!"

So, they took the notebook home. When they opened it, they discovered that the symbols were actually a secret message! It was a message just for Ruby.

Ruby was so surprised and happy. What a weird and wonderful day!

Once upon a time, there was a delicate band. It was very special and everyone wanted it. 

One day, the band started to glitter and shine very brightly. Suddenly, it vanished! Everyone was sad and looked everywhere for it.

The next morning, a bright ray of sunshine lit up the town. People opened their windows and looked around. What they saw made them smile - the delicate band was back! It was resting in the sun and letting everyone admire it. 

Everyone was so happy to have their special band back that they all danced around it. They thanked the sun for bringing it back and vowed to keep it safe forever.

Lily and Tom were playing with their toy cars. They liked to match the cars by their colors. Lily had a red car and a blue car. Tom had a yellow car and a green car. They put the cars in pairs on the floor.

"Look, we have a red pair and a blue pair and a yellow pair and a green pair," Lily said.

"Yes, we do. But we don't have an orange pair or a purple pair," Tom said.

"Maybe we can make them," Lily said. She looked around the room for something orange or purple.

She saw a bowl of salad on the table. The salad had carrots and lettuce and tomatoes and cheese. Lily had an idea.

"Tom, come here. I found something orange and something purple," she said.

She ran to the table and grabbed a carrot and a piece of cheese. She broke the carrot in half and gave one half to Tom. She broke the cheese in half and kept one half for herself.

"Look, we have orange cars now," she said. She put the carrot and the cheese on the floor next to her yellow car.

Tom did the same. He put the carrot and the cheese next to his green car.

"Wow, you're right. We have orange cars now," he said.

They looked for something purple. They saw a grape on the salad. Lily picked it up and broke it in half. She gave one half to Tom and kept one half for herself.

"Look, we have purple cars now," she said. She put the grape next to her blue car.

Tom did the same. He put the grape next to his red car.

"Wow, you're right. We have purple cars now," he said.

They were very happy. They had matched all the colors. They smiled at each other.

But then they heard a loud voice.

"Hey, what are you doing with my salad?" It was Mom. She was not happy. She saw the broken carrot and cheese and grape on the floor. She saw the toy cars next to them.

She was very angry. She picked up the salad and the toy cars. She took them away from Lily and Tom.

"No more playing with food. No more playing with cars. Go to your room. Now," she said.

Lily and Tom were very sad. They had to go to their room. They had no more salad. They had no more cars. They had no more colors. They had no more fun.

Once upon a time, there was a small walk. It was so small it could only fit one person. Every day, someone would come and take the walk, enjoying the warm sunshine and fresh air. 

One day, the person who came was feeling a little lonely, so they decided to surrender to the walk and make it a bit longer. As the person wandered along, something small appeared ahead. When the person got closer, they realized it was a tiny puppy. 

The person was so happy and excited to see the new friend, but the puppy was scared and ran away. The person followed and followed, but the puppy ran faster and soon disappeared from sight.

The person felt a bit sad from losing the puppy, but also happy that the puppy was able to surrender to the freedom of running in the woods. And so, the person decided to use the same power of surrender and have a peaceful, longer walk. 

And so the person continued with their special walk, never forgetting the small puppy they had seen.

Once upon a time there was a jolly shape. He lived high above the clouds in a magical land. One day he decided he wanted to meet someone new. So he waved his magical wand and flew down to earth.

He landed in a big, green field. There he saw a young girl. She was playing in the grass and laughing. The shape called out to her and said "Hi there! Who are you?"

The girl looked up, smiled and said "I'm Sally. What's your name?"

The shape laughed and said "I'm Shapey. It's nice to meet you, Sally!"

Sally laughed too and said "It's nice to meet you too, Shapey!"

The two talked and laughed and played together. They had so much fun meeting new friends and exploring the world around them. From then on, they were the best of friends!

Tim and Sam were friends who liked to play in the park. They had a ball, a whistle and a stick. They took turns to kick the ball, blow the whistle and point with the stick.

One day, they saw a big dog in the park. It was brown and furry and had a long tail. Tim and Sam wanted to pet the dog, but they did not know if it was friendly or not.

"Look, a dog!" Tim said, pointing with his stick.

"Let's go and say hi!" Sam said, blowing his whistle.

The dog heard the whistle and looked at them. It wagged its tail and ran towards them. Tim and Sam were happy and ran to meet the dog.

But the dog did not want to play. It did not like the whistle and the stick. It thought they were loud and sharp. It barked and growled and showed its teeth.

Tim and Sam were scared and stopped. They dropped the ball, the whistle and the stick. They did not know what to do.

"Go away, dog!" Tim said, in a small voice.

"Leave us alone!" Sam said, in a small voice.

The dog did not listen. It came closer and closer. Tim and Sam backed away and looked for help.

They saw a man in the park. He was wearing a dull hat and a dull coat. He had a leash in his hand. He was the dog's owner.

"Hey, stop that!" the man said, in a loud voice. He ran to the dog and grabbed its collar. He pulled the dog away from Tim and Sam.

"I'm sorry, boys. He's not a bad dog, he's just scared of noises. He doesn't like whistles and sticks. He likes balls and treats. Here, you can have your things back." the man said, in a kind voice. He gave them the ball, the whistle and the stick.

"Thank you, sir." Tim said, in a polite voice.

"Thank you, sir." Sam said, in a polite voice.

They took their things and smiled. They were not scared anymore.

The man smiled too. He gave the dog a treat and a pat. He put the leash on the dog and walked away.

"Bye, dog!" Tim said, waving his stick.

"Bye, dog!" Sam said, waving his whistle.

They watched the dog go. Then they looked at each other and laughed.

They were still friends who liked to play in the park. They had a ball, a whistle and a stick. They took turns to kick the ball, blow the whistle and point with the stick.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny named Benny. Benny loved to wander around the forest and play with his friends. One day, Benny saw a big root sticking out of the ground. He thought it looked dull, but he decided to play around it anyways.

As Benny was hopping around the root, he heard a loud noise. Suddenly, a big storm came and the wind started to blow very hard. Benny got scared and tried to run away, but he tripped on the root and hurt his leg. 

Benny's friends tried to help him, but his leg was too hurt. They had to leave him behind and go find help. Benny was all alone in the forest, unable to move. As the night fell, Benny started to feel very cold and scared. He wished he had never wandered around the root. 

Sadly, Benny never saw his friends again. He was never found and had to spend the rest of his life alone in the forest. The end.

Lily loved her bear very much. She hugged him every night and took him everywhere. She named him Brownie, because he was brown and soft.

One day, Lily went to the park with her mom and Brownie. She saw some other kids playing with a ball. She wanted to join them, but she was shy. She held Brownie tight and stayed near her mom.

"Hi, can I play with you?" a boy asked her. He had a big smile and a red cap. He pointed at Brownie. "He is cute. What is his name?"

Lily felt nervous. She did not know the boy. She did not want to share Brownie. She shook her head and said, "No, he is mine. His name is Brownie. Go away."

The boy looked sad. He said, "Okay, sorry. I just wanted to be your friend." He walked away and joined the other kids.

Lily's mom heard what happened. She was not happy. She said to Lily, "That was not nice, Lily. You should not be rude to other kids. They might want to play with you and your bear. You should not spoil your fun and theirs. Sharing is good. It makes you and others happy."

Lily felt sorry. She realized she was wrong. She said to her mom, "I'm sorry, mom. I was scared. I like Brownie too much. I don't want to lose him."

Her mom hugged her and said, "I understand, Lily. But you don't have to worry. Brownie will always be yours. He loves you too. But he also likes to make new friends. He is not shy like you. He wants to play with other kids and their toys. He wants to have fun. And so do you. Why don't you try to say hello to the boy and ask him if he wants to play with you and Brownie?"

Lily thought about it. She looked at Brownie. He seemed to nod and smile. She felt brave. She said to her mom, "Okay, mom. I will try. Thank you."

She took Brownie and ran to the boy. She said, "Hi, I'm sorry I was mean. My name is Lily. This is Brownie. Do you want to play with us?"

The boy smiled and said, "Sure, I would love to. My name is Tom. This is my ball. Do you want to catch it?"

Lily smiled and said, "Yes, please. That sounds fun."

They played together with the ball and Brownie. They laughed and had a good time. They became friends. Lily was not shy anymore. She learned to share and enjoy. She and Brownie were happy.

Once upon a time there was a poor little boy who was playing in the park. He was running and jumping around, when he stumbled upon the patch of grass. He tried to get up but fell again.

Suddenly a kind woman wearing a towel on her head, came over to help him. With her gentle hands, she helped the little boy stand up. 

"Are you OK? said the kind woman

The little boy nodded, smiled, and thanked the woman for helping him.

The kind woman was very happy to help the little boy. She patted him on the head with her towel, and then she went on her way. 

The little boy was very thankful to the kind woman for helping him up. He will never forget the warm feeling he felt when she patted him on the head with her towel. He was so happy. 

The end.

Once, there was a girl called Emily. She was three years old and loved to explore. One day, she spotted a cave in the woods and went inside. As she crawled into the small and uncomfortable cave, she found that there were lots of animals inside. 

She wanted to take them home, so she put them all in a bag. After she had filled the bag, she went outside the cave. 

Suddenly, she heard a loud voice: "What have you got there?" It was the owner of the cave, an old man. He shouted, "You are not allowed to take my animals away!"

Emily was frightened, but she pleaded with the old man, "Please, let me keep them! I promise I will take good care of them."
The old man refused, and Emily had to leave the bag of animals. 

Sad and upset, Emily had to go home empty-handed and received nothing for her efforts.

It was Mommy's special day. She was getting a new faucet for the kitchen sink. She was so excited, she couldn't wait to see it fit in the tight space.

The little 3 year old boy watched Mommy as she took out all the tools she needed for the big job. He wanted to help too.

Mommy smiled when she saw the boy's eager face.

"Okay, you can help!" she said.

The little boy helped Mommy hold the faucet in place. He watched as she carefully worked, making sure it would fit just right.

At last, the faucet fit tight against the sink. Mommy smiled and said, "We did it! What a great job!"

The little boy was so proud of himself. He had helped Mommy make the faucet fit, and now it was perfect. They both stood there, admiring their work. Of course, Mommy had done the hard part, but the little boy felt like he had done his part, too. 

"We make a great team," Mommy said with a big smile.

The little boy smiled back, and he knew she was right.

Once there was a generous woman called Mrs. Milly. She loved helping people, so she decided to give away all her possessions. One day she saw a little boy who looked lost and sad. Mrs. Milly was filled with compassion for him and she asked him what was wrong.

The little boy told Mrs. Milly that he had lost his favourite toy. He was so sad that he had not been able to find it. Mrs. Milly was very kind and she wanted to help the little boy. She smiled and said: "Don't worry, I will replace your toy".

Mrs. Milly then went to the toy shop and bought the little boy a new toy. When she returned, the little boy was so happy and excited to have a new toy. He gave Mrs. Milly a big hug and thanked her for being so kind.

Mrs. Milly saw the little boy's tears turn into smiles and her heart was filled with joy. Even though she no longer had any possessions, she was glad she could bring happiness to the little boy.

The mist of tears had been replaced by the warmth of compassion. Mrs. Milly saw the power of kindness and how it can bring joy to people.

Once upon a time, in a big garden, there was a little flower. The flower was very sad. It wanted to bloom and become a pretty thing, like all the other flowers in the garden. But it was too small and felt ashamed.

One day, a nice bee came to the flower. The bee saw the sad flower and wanted to help. The bee said, "Don't be ashamed, little flower. I will help you bloom and become a pretty thing too."

The bee went to find water and food for the little flower. The flower drank the water and ate the food. Soon, the little flower started to grow. And one bright morning, the little flower bloomed into a beautiful thing. The flower was so happy and not ashamed anymore. The bee and the flower became best friends, and they lived happily in the big garden together.

Once upon a time, there was a nosy cat named Tom. Tom liked to look at everything and everyone. He would look at his friends, the birds, and the fish in the pond.

One day, Tom saw a dish with yummy food. He wanted to eat the food, but it was not his dish. Tom did not care, he was too nosy. He went to the dish and started to eat the food.

Suddenly, a big dog named Max came. Max saw Tom eating from the dish. Max did not like that. Max walked up to Tom and gave him a big slap. Tom learned his lesson and never ate from someone else's dish again.

Mummy was with her little girl in the park. The little girl loved to play on the swings and they had been there a long time. 
Mummy said, "We should go soon. It's getting dark."
But the little girl protested, "No, I want to stay here!" She was having so much fun. 
Mummy sighed. She urged the little girl to leave, but the little girl's feelings were too strong.

Mummy was starting to worry. She was worried about the darkness, and that the little girl might get tired and weak. She said, "Come on sweetheart, we must go now."
The little girl felt a bit weak, so finally she agreed to go. Mummy was happy, because she was no longer worried.

Charlie was playing in the gym. He liked going there because he liked being active. He loved tossing around the balls and running around. He was having lots of fun!

But then it got too loud. Too many people were in the gym shouting and laughing. Charlie didn't like it when it was too noisy. He needed to find somewhere quieter to play.

He looked around the gym and he saw an empty corner. He ran over to the corner and started to sort out the toys that were lying around so he could play. He knew that would make it nice and peaceful.

He put all the balls in one pile and then he made another pile for the blocks. When he was done sorting, he had a nice, quiet spot all to himself. 

He could play there until it was time to go home. The quiet corner was just perfect for him!

Sam loved to play with his toy plane. He made it zoom and fly in the air, and he pretended he was the pilot. He liked to make loud noises like the plane's engine and the wind.

One day, he was playing with his plane in the living room, when his mom called him for lunch. He did not want to stop playing, so he ignored her. He kept flying his plane around the sofa and the table, and he did not hear his mom calling him again and again.

Then, he heard a loud crash. He turned around and saw that his plane had hit a vase on the shelf. The vase fell and broke into many pieces on the floor. Sam was scared and sad. He had broken his mom's favorite vase. He knew he was in trouble.

He paused and thought about what he had done. He realized he had been very rude and careless. He should have listened to his mom and put away his plane. He felt sorry and ashamed.

He ran to his mom and hugged her. He said he was sorry for breaking the vase and for not listening to her. He said he loved her and he would be more careful and respectful. His mom was angry, but she also loved him. She hugged him back and said she forgave him, but he had to help her clean up the mess and learn from his mistake.

Sam learned that playing is fun, but he also had to follow the rules and be polite. He learned that being a pilot is not only about flying smooth, but also about being responsible and safe. He learned that saying sorry is important, but so is changing his behavior. He learned a valuable lesson that day.

Once upon a time, there was a bad man. He liked to eat meat. Every day he would include more and more of it in his meals. He never wanted to eat anything else! 
One day, a little girl who was only three years old saw the bad man eating. She asked him why he was only eating meat. The man just smiled and kept eating. 
The little girl kept asking questions. She wondered why the man was so bad and why he only ate meat. Suddenly, the man stopped eating and looked at the girl. 
He explained that he only ate meat because it made him feel strong and healthy. The little girl smiled and nodded her head. She understood why the man liked to eat meat. 
The bad man and the little girl became friends that day. The bad man still included plenty of meat in his meals, but he also started to try different foods. The little girl was proud of her new friend.

Once upon a time, there was a friendly dog named Spot. Spot loved to play with his friends in the park. One day, while playing, Spot saw a cable on the ground.

A big bird came and tried to steal the cable. Spot barked, "No, bird! Don't steal!" The bird looked at Spot and said, "I'm sorry, I didn't know it was yours."

Spot and the bird became friends, and they played together in the park. They shared the cable and had lots of fun. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once there was a famous kite that liked to speak with the birds in the sky. Every day it would fly around and talk with them about the clouds and the wind. One day, a little girl spotted the kite and decided to fly it. She ran to the park with it under her arm and couldn't wait to get it in the air.

Once the kite was let go, it flew higher and higher and seemed to talk to the birds more excitedly than ever before. The girl watched in wonder and tried to call out to the kite, but it only spoke with the birds.

She asked one of the birds what the kite was saying. The bird responded with a cheerful chirp, "The kite says it's happy to be here with you today! It loves its new home in the sky and wants to come back and see you again soon."

The girl smiled in delight and thanked the bird before running home with the famous kite still in her heart.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and her friends. One day, Lily heard about a club where all the cool kids went to play. She wanted to join the club so badly, but she didn't know how.

Lily asked her friends how to join the club, but they didn't know either. Then, she saw a fierce-looking boy who was in the club. She thought he must know how to join. So, she went up to him and asked him how to join. The boy said she had to do something really mean to someone else to join.

Lily didn't want to do something mean, but she really wanted to join the club. So, she did something mean to her little brother. She thought she would finally be able to join the club, but when she went back to the boy, he told her that the club was only for mean kids. Lily realized that being mean was not worth it and she felt very sad. The moral of the story is that it's better to be kind than to be in a club that makes you do mean things.

Once upon a time there were two friends. They were animals, a lion and a tiger. They were very wild. The lion liked to roar and the tiger liked to stamp her feet. 
One day, the two friends wanted to have some fun. They decided to fight. The lion roared and the tiger stamped her feet. They growled and chased each other around. 
Before long, they both got tired from all their wild fighting. The lion lay down in the sun and the tiger curled up in the shade. They were happy and best of friends.

Once there was a brave little girl. She loved exploring the world around her.

One day, she went on a walk in the woods. She found an apple tree and decided to pick one of the big apples for her snack. As she was enjoying the sweet apple, she grew tired. She decided to have a nap under the apple tree.

The sun was warm and the breeze was gentle, so she curled up and fell fast asleep. She dreamed of all the brave adventures she would have in the future.

When she woke up, she felt refreshed. She climbed down from the apple tree and went off to explore new paths. She was ready for more brave adventures!

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She had a pretty dress that she loved to wear. One day, she was walking in the park with her friend, Timmy. Suddenly, she slipped on a banana peel and fell down. Her dress got dirty and she felt sad.

Timmy said, "Don't be sad, Lily. Your dress is still pretty, even if it's a little dirty. Let's go to my house and we can wash it together."

Lily smiled and agreed. When they got to Timmy's house, they washed the dress in the sink. It was a modest dress, not too fancy, but still pretty. After they washed it, they hung it up to dry.
