She asked her mom why the zebra had to leave. Mom said the zebra was going to a new home, so it could make more friends. Jane felt better knowing the zebra was just going away for a little while. She said goodbye to the zebra, and wished it a safe trip. 

Now, Jane remembers the zebra with fondness. She knows that it has found new friends, and is happy in its new home.

Sara and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to catch bugs and put them in a jar. They wanted to see how the bugs lived and what they did. They thought bugs were a wonder.

"Look, Sara, I caught a big beetle!" Ben said, holding up his jar. "It has shiny wings and long legs. Do you think it can fly?"

"Wow, Ben, that is a nice bug!" Sara said, admiring the beetle. "But be careful, don't shake the jar too much. You might hurt it."

Sara and Ben found a shady spot under a tree and sat down with their jars. They watched the bugs crawl and wiggle inside. They tried to guess what the bugs were thinking and feeling.

Suddenly, they heard a loud bark. A big dog ran towards them, wagging its tail. It was Max, the spoiled dog from next door. Max liked to chase and bite everything he saw. He did not listen to anyone.

"Uh-oh, it's Max!" Sara said, grabbing her jar. "He will try to get our bugs! Run, Ben, run!"

Sara and Ben ran as fast as they could, but Max was faster. He jumped on them and knocked them down. He grabbed Ben's jar with his mouth and shook it hard. The jar broke and the beetle flew away.

"Max, no!" Ben cried, trying to get his jar back. "Bad dog, bad dog! You spoiled my bug!"

Max did not care. He licked Ben's face and wagged his tail. He thought he was playing a fun game. He did not understand why Ben was sad and angry.

Sara hugged Ben and tried to make him feel better. She said, "I'm sorry, Ben. Max is a mean dog. He does not know how to share. But don't worry, we can catch another bug. Maybe we can find a butterfly or a ladybug. They are pretty and gentle. Do you want to try?"

Ben nodded and wiped his tears. He said, "OK, Sara. Thank you. You are a good friend. Let's go catch another bug. Maybe we can find a wonder."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to play outside and her favorite thing to do was to point at the birds in the sky. One day, while she was playing in the park, she saw a colorful glove on the ground. She picked it up and asked her mom, "Can I keep this pretty glove?"

Her mom said, "Yes, but be careful. It might belong to someone." Lily put the glove in her pocket and continued playing. Later that day, she saw a sad boy looking for something. She asked him what he was looking for and he said, "I lost my favorite colorful glove. It means a lot to me."

Lily remembered the glove in her pocket and gave it to the boy. He was so happy and thanked her. From that day on, they became good friends and played together every day. Lily learned that doing the right thing can bring happiness and new friendships.

Once upon a time there lived a very kind and compassionate giant. Every day he would take care of animals in the forest by feeding them. He had two very special friends, a rabbit and a peacock.

Every day the giant would bring them yummy food in his big hands. The rabbit and peacock both knew that he was very kind and would always feed them until they were full.

One day, the giant saw a small squirrel in the forest who didn't look very happy. When he went to feed the squirrel some nuts, he saw that it was hurt. The giant knew he couldn't leave the squirrel when it was so scared, so he scooped it up and held it in the palm of his hand.

The giant was so compassionate and caring. He spent the day cuddling the squirrel and comforting it. He fed it some nuts and made sure it was safe and warm. Eventually, the squirrel felt better and hopped away. 

The giant was happy that he was able to help the poor squirrel and was glad that he could show compassion. He continued to take care of all the animals in the forest by feeding them every day.

Once there was a little girl who was curious. Whenever she saw something new, she wanted to try it. One day, she found a furry thing on the floor. She thought it was very interesting. She picked it up and said to herself, â€œWhat is this?â€

Just then, her mom came up to her. She saw the small, furry object and said, â€œThatâ€™s a match.â€ The little girl looked confused. â€œWhat does it do?â€ she asked.

â€œWell, itâ€™s used to make a fire in a sinkâ€, her mom replied. The little girl thought for a moment before she said, â€œOh. Like when we cook food?â€

Her mom smiled. â€œYes, exactly.â€ She took the match from the little one and lit it with her thumb. â€œSee, now it will help us cook.â€ 

The little girl liked playing with the furry match. She watched as her mom used it to light the fire in the sink. She clapped happily, excited to learn something new.

One day, Ben and Lily went to the park with their mom. They saw many trees with green and yellow leaves. Ben and Lily liked to pick up the leaves and look at them.

"Look, mom, this leaf is big and shiny!" Ben said, holding a yellow leaf.

"That's a nice leaf, Ben. Do you want to pass it to Lily so she can see it too?" mom asked.

Ben nodded and walked towards Lily. But on his way, a big boy ran into him and knocked the leaf out of his hand. The big boy did not say sorry. He was rude.

"Hey, that's my leaf!" Ben shouted.

The big boy laughed and picked up the leaf. He said, "No, it's mine now. Find your own leaf, baby."

Lily saw what happened and ran to help Ben. She said, "Give it back, you meanie. That's Ben's leaf. You are rude."

The big boy stuck out his tongue and ran away with the leaf. Ben and Lily felt sad and angry. They wanted their leaf back.

Mom saw what happened and hugged Ben and Lily. She said, "I'm sorry, my loves. That big boy was very rude. He should not have taken your leaf. But don't worry, there are many more leaves in the park. Let's go and find some more together."

Ben and Lily nodded and smiled. They followed mom and looked for more leaves. They found red and orange and brown leaves. They made a pile of leaves and jumped in it. They had fun. They forgot about the rude big boy and the yellow leaf. They were happy.

Once upon a time, two towns were fighting a fierce war. Everyone in both towns were scared and the noise of battle was very loud. One day, a small bird flew high in the sky and noticed the towns were causing a huge disturb.

The small bird flapped her wings and flew down to the fight. When she got to the ground, she said to the towns, â€œWhy are you fighting? When you fight, you disturb the peace.â€

The towns listened and stopped fighting. The air filled with peace and the birds sang happily. The towns hugged and became friends, never wanting to have a fierce war again.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to eat pastries. One day, he went to the bakery to buy an ordinary pastry. 

As he was walking home, he saw his friend, Sally. Sally asked him, "What did you buy at the bakery, Timmy?" 

"I bought an ordinary pastry," he replied. 

Sally said, "Let's speed up and go eat it together!" 

So, they ran to Timmy's house and ate the pastry together. It was delicious! They both smiled and said, "Yum!"

Once upon a time there was a girl called Sara. She was so excited because she had a package. She could not wait to open it and when the package arrived, she was ready. As soon as she opened the package, she screamed with joy. Inside there were lots of toys - dolls, trucks and puzzles - everything she wanted! She was so happy that she started to run around the room and jumped with joy, screaming. Sara had so much fun playing with her new toys. She smiled and laughed all day long.

Once there was a girl named Lucy. She was three years old and she loved gum. She had lots of different flavours and she ate it every day.

One day Lucy thought it would be fun to try extra big bubblegum. She put it in her mouth and blew a huge bubble. Suddenly, the bubble popped and tickled her nose. She started to sneeze and sneeze. 

Lucy looked down and saw her shirt was covered in gum. She was so ashamed. She wanted to hide but couldn't. 

So she asked for help from her parents. They showed her how to use a wet cloth to wipe the gum away. She smiled with relief and promised never to try big bubblegum again.

Once, there was a slow gorilla. He sat in his cage all day, looking at the other animals in the zoo. He felt very sad and lonely. One day, a little girl came to look at him. She saw how sad he looked and her heart started to ache. She asked the zookeeper why he was so sad and he told her that gorillas were meant to live in groups with their family and friends.

The little girl felt so sorry for theSlow Gorilla that she started to cry. His heart filled with happiness when he saw her crying for him. He put his hands on the bars of his cage and made a soft, mournful sound. He wanted to thank her for understanding how lonely he felt. 

The little girl wiped away her tears and looked at the gorilla with a smile. She felt as though they had shared a special moment. As she walked away, theSlow Gorilla watched her until he could no longer see her. He knew he would always remember the kind girl who had come to visit him and had taken the time to cry for him.

Tommy was sick. He had a bad cough and a hot head. He did not want to play or eat. His mom took him to the doctor. The doctor was nice. He looked at Tommy's ears, nose and throat. He gave him some medicine.

"Tommy, you need to take this medicine every day. It will help you feel better," the doctor said.

"OK, doctor. Thank you," Tommy said.

The doctor smiled. He gave Tommy a sticker. It had a picture of a lion. Tommy liked lions. He put the sticker on his shirt.

"Good boy, Tommy. Now, follow the nurse. She will lead you to the exit," the doctor said.

The nurse was kind. She held Tommy's hand. She walked with him and his mom to the door.

"Bye, Tommy. I hope you get well soon," the nurse said.

"Bye, nurse. You are good," Tommy said.

Tommy and his mom went home. Tommy took his medicine. He drank some water. He rested on the couch. He felt a little better. He looked at his sticker. He smiled. He was brave like a lion.

Once upon a time, there was a little fish named Nemo. Nemo lived in a big ocean with his friends. One day, Nemo and his friends went to explore a reef. The reef was very pretty and colorful. Nemo was very excited to see all the different kinds of fish swimming around.

Suddenly, the water started to tremble. Nemo and his friends were scared and didn't know what was happening. They heard a big voice say, "I am a big and flexible octopus, and I am going to eat you all!" Nemo and his friends tried to swim away, but the octopus was too fast. He caught them all and ate them for dinner.

The end.

Lily was shy. She did not like to talk to new people. She liked to play with her dolls and make things with yarn. She had a big box of yarn in many colors.

One day, she saw a new girl in her class. Her name was Anna. Anna had a big smile and long brown hair. She wore a pretty sweater with flowers on it. Lily liked her sweater, but she was too shy to say hello.

At recess, Lily sat on a bench and took out some yarn. She wanted to make a sweater for her doll. She knew how to make loops and knots with the yarn. She liked to see the sweater grow.

Anna saw Lily and walked over to her. She said, "Hi, I'm Anna. What are you making?"

Lily looked up and felt scared. She did not know what to say. She held her yarn and her doll.

Anna smiled and said, "Is that a sweater for your doll? It's very nice. I like to make things with yarn, too. Can I sit with you and make something?"

Lily nodded and moved over a little. She felt a bit less shy. She said, "I'm Lily. This is my doll, Rose. What do you want to make?"

Anna said, "Maybe I can make a hat for my doll, Daisy. She has a blue dress. What color do you have?"

Lily said, "I have blue, too. And pink, and yellow, and green. You can use any color you want."

Anna said, "Thank you. You are very kind. Can we be friends?"

Lily smiled and said, "Yes, we can be friends."

They sat together and made things with yarn. They talked and laughed. Lily was not shy anymore. She was happy. She had a new friend.

Tom and Sam are brothers. They like to play with sand in the backyard. They have a big bucket and a small bucket. They fill the buckets with sand and make sand castles.

One day, they see a white cat in the backyard. The cat is rough and dirty. It has no collar and no name. Tom and Sam want to pet the cat, but the cat is scared and runs away.

"Let's catch the cat and make it our friend," Tom says.

"No, let's leave the cat alone. It doesn't want to play with us," Sam says.

Tom and Sam argue. Tom runs after the cat with the big bucket. Sam stays with the small bucket and the sand castles.

Tom chases the cat around the backyard. He tries to throw the big bucket over the cat, but the cat is fast and smart. The cat dodges the bucket and scratches Tom's arm. Tom cries and drops the bucket.

Sam hears Tom's cry and runs to him. He sees the cat run away and the big bucket on the ground. He sees Tom's arm bleeding and his face sad.

"I'm sorry, Tom. Are you okay?" Sam asks.

"It hurts, Sam. The cat was mean to me," Tom says.

Sam hugs Tom and says, "I'm sorry, too. I should have helped you. But the cat was scared, too. It didn't know us and it didn't like the bucket. Maybe we should have been nicer to the cat."

Tom nods and says, "You're right, Sam. We should have been nicer to the cat. Maybe it would have liked us then. Can we still be friends?"

Sam smiles and says, "Of course we can, Tom. You're my brother and I love you. Come on, let's go inside and get a band-aid for your arm. And maybe some cookies, too."

Tom and Sam go inside and hug their mom. They learn that the cat belongs to their neighbor, who is looking for it. They say sorry to their neighbor and promise to be gentle with the cat next time. They also learn that the cat's name is Snowy, because it is white. They think that is a nice name for a cat.

The moral value of the story is: Be kind to animals and respect their feelings. Don't chase or hurt them, or they might chase or hurt you back. If you want to make friends with them, be gentle and patient. And always listen to your brother, he might know better than you.

Once upon a time, in a big forest, there lived a strong kangaroo. His name was Kip. Kip loved to jump and play with his friends. He was very good at helping others.

One day, a little bird came to Kip. The bird was very sad because she lost her way home. Kip wanted to help the bird. He said, "Don't worry, little bird. I will help you find your home." So, Kip and the bird went on a long walk to find the bird's home.

They walked and walked until they saw a big tree. The bird was very happy because that was her home. Kip helped the bird come back to her home. The bird said, "Thank you, Kip, for helping me." Kip was very happy to help his new friend.

Kip and the bird became very good friends. They played together every day. All the animals in the forest saw how Kip helped the bird. They learned that it is good to help others when they need it. And that was the moral of the story: always help your friends when they need you.

Once upon a time, there was a big garden with many flowers. One day, a little flower was sad because it did not bloom like the others. It wanted to be pretty like them. 

An elderly woman came to the garden and saw the sad little flower. She put a collar around it and said, "You are special, just like this collar. You will bloom when it is your time." 

The little flower was happy and waited patiently. But then, a big wind came and blew all the flowers around. The little flower was scared and thought it would never bloom. 

But the collar kept it safe and the little flower finally bloomed. It was the prettiest flower in the garden. The other flowers were happy for the little flower and the elderly woman smiled.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny named Benny. Benny was very eager to go outside and play. He asked his mommy if he could go outside, and she said yes! 

As Benny was hopping around, he saw a hole in the ground. He thought it looked very interesting. Benny wanted to explore the hole, so he asked his mommy if he could. 

His mommy was a little worried, but she knew Benny was very curious. She granted his request and Benny went exploring. He found some bugs and even a little mouse living in the hole! Benny was so happy he got to explore something new.

Once upon a time, there was a very sad alligator. He had no one to care for him. Each day was very bitter and he had no friends.

One day, he saw a little girl playing in the park. He wanted to be friends with her, to have someone to care for him. He slowly crawled up to her and said, "Hello". The little girl was surprised to see an alligator and she slowly backed away. 

The alligator was very sad. He wanted to be friends and show the little girl how much he cared. He backed away slowly, understanding that the little girl was scared.

The next day, the alligator saw the same little girl in the park. He decided to try again. He slowly walked up to her and calmly said, "Please, I just want to be friends". The little girl smiled, understanding that the alligator only wanted to be friends and care for someone.

From then on, the alligator and the little girl were best friends. They played together in the park every day and the little girl cared for the alligator. The alligator was no longer sad or bitter - he was happy and joyful!

Lily was a little girl who liked to draw and paint. She had a tutor who came to her house every week to teach her new things. The tutor was very nice and patient, and Lily enjoyed learning with her.

One day, Lily wanted to show her tutor her new picture. She had drawn a huge flower with many colors and shapes. She was very proud of it and ran to get it from her room. But when she came back, she saw that her baby brother had found her picture and was tearing it into pieces. Lily was very sad and angry. She shouted at her brother and tried to take her picture back.

"Stop it, Max! That's my picture! You are bad!" Lily cried.

"No, no, no! Mine, mine, mine!" Max said, holding the torn pieces tightly.

The tutor heard the noise and came to see what was wrong. She saw Lily and Max fighting over the picture and tried to calm them down.

"Lily, Max, don't fight. It's not nice to tear other people's things. Max, can you say sorry to Lily? Lily, can you forgive Max? He is still very small and doesn't know better." The tutor said.

Max looked at the tutor and then at Lily. He saw that Lily was crying and felt sorry. He gave her the pieces of the picture and said, "Sorry, Lily. Me no tear."

Lily looked at the pieces of the picture and then at Max. She saw that he was sorry and felt better. She gave him a hug and said, "It's okay, Max. Me forgive."

The tutor smiled and said, "That's very good, Lily and Max. You are both very kind. How about we make a new picture together? I have some paper and crayons. We can draw a huge flower again, or anything you like."

Lily and Max nodded and smiled. They followed the tutor to the table and started to draw. They had fun and learned to share. They forgot about the torn picture and made a new one. They were happy.

The little boy was so excited. He was going to get his own dinosaur today!

The dinosaur was bright green and had bright yellow spots. He was so cute that the little boy wanted to hug him. But he didn't - instead he just looked at the dinosaur and smiled.

"What are you going to call him?" his mom asked.

The little boy thought for a minute. Then his face lit up.

"I'm going to call him Chewy!"

His mom smiled.

The little boy and Chewy played all day. They ran and chased each other. They made funny noises and laughed.

But after a while, the little boy started to get tired. He yawned and said, "I'm so tired. I think Chewy needs a nap, too."

So the little boy lay down and Chewy nestled up close. And soon, they were both fast asleep.

Amy was very excited. She was finally going to design her first hoop. She had picked out some really big, colorful pieces of paper. She and her dad sat at the table together and got out some glue and scissor. 

"What kind of hoop do you want to make?" asked her dad.

"Oh, I want it to be big," said Amy.

Her dad smiled. Then he helped her cut the pieces of paper in circles and glue them together until they had a big hoop. 

They hung it on Amy's bedroom door and admired it together. They had designed a beautiful big hoop. Amy was so proud of it. 

"This hoop looks perfect!" said her dad.

Amy smiled. She knew she had designed something special.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play together. They play with dolls, cars, and blocks. Sometimes they play in the park. Sometimes they play in the house.

One day, Anna's mom says, "We have to go to the store. You can play with Ben later." Anna is sad. She wants to play with Ben now. She says, "Mom, can I play with Ben for a little bit? Please?"

Mom says, "Okay, but only for a little bit. Then we have to go. Do you promise to come back when I call you?"

Anna says, "Yes, mom. I promise. I am a dependable girl. I always do what I say."

Mom says, "Good. I trust you. Go and play with Ben. But listen for my voice. I will call you when it is time to go."

Anna runs to Ben's house. She knocks on the door. Ben opens the door. He is happy to see Anna. He says, "Hi, Anna. Do you want to play with me?"

Anna says, "Yes, Ben. I want to play with you. But only for a little bit. I have to go to the store with mom soon. I promised to come back when she calls me."

Ben says, "Okay, Anna. I understand. You are a dependable friend. You always keep your promises. Let's play with the blocks. We can build a castle."

Anna and Ben play with the blocks. They have fun. They make a big castle. They pretend to be a king and a queen. They laugh and talk.

Soon, Anna hears her mom's voice. She says, "Anna, it is time to go. Come back now."

Anna says, "Okay, mom. I am coming. Bye, Ben. Thank you for playing with me. You are a good friend."

Ben says, "Bye, Anna. You are welcome. You are a good friend, too. See you later."

Anna runs back to her mom. She gives her a hug. She says, "Mom, I am sorry. I had fun with Ben. But I kept my promise. I came back when you called me."

Mom says, "I am proud of you, Anna. You are a dependable girl. You did what you said. You are a good friend to Ben. And you are a good daughter to me. I love you."

Anna says, "I love you, too, mom. Can we play with Ben again tomorrow?"

Mom says, "Yes, we can. If he wants to. And if you promise to listen to me again."

Anna says, "I promise, mom. I always listen to you. You are the best mom in the world."

Once upon a time, there was a lazy cat named Tom. Tom liked to sleep all day and play all night. One day, Tom saw a tunnel near his house. He was curious and wanted to explore it.

Tom went inside the tunnel and saw a big room. In the room, there was a big red button. When Tom pressed the button, it started to record his voice. Tom meowed and the button recorded his meow.

Tom had fun with the button and played in the tunnel all day. He forgot to be lazy and enjoyed his new adventure. When it was time to go home, Tom left the tunnel, but he knew he would come back again to play with the button that could record his voice. And from that day on, Tom was not so lazy anymore.

Billy was a three-year old. One day he was playing in the garden with his mom when they heard an eerie sound. They both stopped and looked around.

"What's that noise, mommy?" asked Billy.

His mom shivered and said, "It's a ghost. Let's go inside, quickly!"

Billy was scared, but he stood up courageously and said, "I'm not scared of ghosts. They're stupid!"

His mom smiled and said, "You're strong, Billy!" Then, she took his hand and they ran inside.

They were both relieved to be safe. Billy felt proud for standing up to the ghost.

Once upon a time, there was a little infant named Tim. He liked to play with his toys and watch the birds outside his window. Tim had a big, soft teddy bear that he loved very much.

One day, Tim's teddy bear was sad. Tim did not know why his teddy bear was sad. He tried to make his teddy bear happy by giving it a hug and a kiss.

Tim decided to take his sad teddy bear outside to watch the birds with him. They sat under a big tree and watched the birds sing and fly. Soon, the teddy bear was not sad anymore. Tim and his teddy bear were very happy watching the birds together.

Lily liked to draw pictures with her crayons. She drew flowers, animals, and people. She drew a picture of her best friend, Mia, who lived far away. She wanted to send it to Mia, so she asked her mom for help.

"Mom, can I send this to Mia?" Lily showed her mom the picture.

"Of course, sweetie. That's very nice of you. We need an envelope to put it in." Mom took an envelope from a drawer and wrote Mia's address on it. She helped Lily put the picture inside and seal it. "Now we need a stamp. Do you know what a stamp is?"

Lily nodded. "It's a sticker that you put on the envelope. It tells the mailman where to go."

"That's right. And do you know what the mailman does?"

"He takes the envelope and puts it in his big bag. Then he drives his truck and gives the envelope to Mia."

"Very good. And sometimes, Mia will send you an envelope back. That's called return. She will draw a picture for you and return it to you. Do you like that?"

Lily smiled. "Yes, I like that. Mia is my best friend. She is very popular. Everyone likes her."

Mom hugged Lily. "I'm sure she likes you too. You are very popular too. You are kind, smart, and creative. Now let's go to the mailbox and send your envelope."

Sara and Ben like to watch videos on the big screen. They have many videos of animals, songs and stories. Sometimes they share the videos, and sometimes they want different ones.

One day, Sara wants to watch a video of a princess, but Ben wants to watch a video of a dinosaur. They both grab the same video and pull hard. The video tears in half and makes a loud noise. Sara and Ben start to cry.

Mom hears the noise and comes to see what happened. She sees the broken video and the sad children. She is not happy. She says, "Sara and Ben, you should not tear the video. That is not nice. You should be modest and take turns. Now you cannot watch any video today. Go to your rooms and think about what you did."

Sara and Ben feel sorry. They say, "We are sorry, Mom. We did not mean to tear the video. We just wanted to watch it. Can we say sorry to each other and hug?"

Mom smiles and says, "That is a good idea. You can say sorry and hug, and then you can play with your toys. Maybe tomorrow you can watch a new video, if you are modest and share."

Sara and Ben say sorry and hug. They go to their rooms and play with their toys. They learn to be modest and share. They are happy again.

Once upon a time, there was a mighty cat called Fred. He loved playing in the garden and chasing around the birds. But one day, there was a problem. Fred found himself stuck in a tree and he couldn't find a way out.

Fred was scared and he meowed for help. But alas, nobody was around. He tried jumping but he couldn't reach the ground. He was starting to lose hope.

Just then, a kind man came along. He looked up and saw Fred in the tree. He stretched out his arms and said: "Come on, Fred! Jump, I will catch you". Fred was very brave and he jumped. The kind man caught him safely and Fred was so happy.

The adventure had come to an end and they all went home with a smile. Fred was relieved and promised himself never to get stuck in a tree again. The day was saved, thanks to the kind man and the mighty cat Fred. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time there was a big mark in space. It was a big and bright spot. Everyone thought it was the most special thing in the whole universe. It was an original mark that nobody else had ever seen before.

One day, a small rocket came flying by. It was seen from a very far away place. When it came close, everybody saw that it was an ordinary rocket. But there was something special inside it.

The rocket went around the mark in space and started to make circles. Then it went around the mark one more time and made even more circles. When it was done, the mark in space was filled with lots of small circles. It looked like a big flower.

Everybody thought the rocket had made a very special and original mark in space. They all cheered and celebrated. The new mark in space made the entire universe even more special.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys, especially his toy cars. One day, Timmy's mom told him to clean up his toys before dinner. Timmy didn't want to clean up, so he threw his toys everywhere.

Later that night, Timmy went to bed with his fan on. He loved the sound it made. But Timmy didn't know that his fan was dangerous. The fan was old and broken, and it started to shake. Suddenly, the fan fell off the table and hit Timmy on the head. Timmy was hurt and had to go to the hospital.

Timmy's mom was very sad. She wished Timmy had listened to her and cleaned up his toys. She also wished she had checked the fan before letting Timmy use it. Now, Timmy had to stay in the hospital and relax until he felt better.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird who lived in a tree. The bird was proud of his nest, which he built all by himself. One day, the bird saw some dark clouds in the sky. He knew it was going to rain soon. So, he started to look for a shelter for himself and his nest.

He flew around and finally found a big tree with lots of leaves. The bird spread his wings and flew to the tree. He saw a small hole in the trunk and thought it would be a perfect shelter for him and his nest. He quickly moved his nest to the hole and waited for the rain to come.

Soon, it started to rain heavily. The little bird was happy that he found a safe shelter for himself and his nest. He felt proud of himself for being so clever. The rain continued for a long time, but the little bird and his nest stayed dry and cozy in their new shelter.

Anna and Ben were friends who liked to play in the garden. One day, they saw a big bush with many blueberries on it. They ran to the bush and picked some blueberries to eat.

"These are yummy!" Anna said.

"Yes, they are!" Ben agreed.

But then they saw something strange. Some of the blueberries were glowing. They were bright and shiny, like stars.

"Wow, look at these!" Ben said. He reached for a glowing blueberry.

"Wait, Ben!" Anna said. "Maybe they are not good to eat. Maybe they are hot or bad."

But Ben did not listen. He put the glowing blueberry in his mouth. He felt a sharp pain. He spit out the blueberry and cried.

"Ow, ow, ow! It is hot! It burned my tongue!" Ben said.

Anna felt sorry for Ben. She gave him some water and a hug.

"I'm sorry, Ben. I tried to warn you," Anna said.

"I'm sorry, Anna. I should have listened to you," Ben said.

They learned a lesson that day. They learned to be careful and not to eat things that look strange. They learned to listen to their friends who care for them. They learned that glowing blueberries are not yummy.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play at the beach and build sandcastles. One day, Timmy was playing in the water when a big wave came and knocked him down. Timmy started to panic because he didn't know how to swim. 

Suddenly, a creative idea popped into Timmy's head. He remembered that he had a floaty in his bag. Timmy quickly grabbed the floaty and put it on. He felt safe and happy again. 

But then, another big wave came and this time, it was even bigger than the last one. Timmy tried to hold on to his floaty, but the wave was too strong. The wave took Timmy far away from the shore and he couldn't see his parents anymore. 

Timmy was scared and alone. He started to panic again, but this time, there was no creative idea to save him. Timmy was lost forever in the big ocean. The end.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Daisy. She liked to do yoga. One day, her mom suggested that she take a serious yoga class. So Daisy found a seat in the classroom and listened to the teacher.

The teacher said, "Tonight, we will start with a very serious yoga pose. It's very tricky and it takes lots of practice." Daisy thought it sounded fun, so she eagerly nodded her head.

But then, Daisy started to think: what if she couldn't do this tricky yoga pose? Would she still be able to do yoga? Daisy was getting more and more worried, so she asked her teacher what would happen. 

The teacher replied, "If you don't get this pose right, then you can't do yoga anymore." Daisy was sad and scared, but she tried her best. Unfortunately, Daisy couldn't do the pose and her teacher said she would have to leave the class.

And they all lived sadly ever after.

Once upon a time there was a clever child who loved to play. The child played with a toy train and raced it around the room, making "whoosh" noises all the while.

One day, the child's teacher mentioned something very interesting in class. The teacher said that if the child practiced really hard, he could learn something very special.

The child was curious and decided to practice every day. After a few months, the child was surprised to find that he had learnt this special thing.

He proudly showed his teacher what he had learnt and the teacher was so impressed. He said that the child was really clever for learning so quickly.

The child was thrilled and as he went home he thought to himself that if he kept practicing, he could learn even more special things.

Once there was a little boy who was very happy. He was playing in his backyard when he spotted a wire that had been left behind. He went to take a closer look and noticed that the wire was all tangled up.

He started to play with it and unwind it, being very careful not to break it. He worked and worked and eventually he managed to untangle the wire. He felt so happy that he was able to do it all by himself.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big boot on the grass. It is brown and dirty.

"Who left this boot here?" Lily asks.

Lily laughs. She thinks Ben is funny. She tries to find another boot, but there is only one.

"Can I try the boot?" she asks.

"OK," Ben says. He gives the boot to Lily. She puts it on her head. It is too big for her. It covers her eyes and nose.

"Help, I can't see!" Lily says. She feels anxious. She does not like the boot.

Ben hears Lily. He takes the boot off her head. He hugs her.

"I'm sorry, Lily. I was joking. Are you OK?" he asks.

Lily nods. She is OK. She hugs Ben back.

"Thank you, Ben. You are a good friend," she says.

They smile. They put the boot back on the grass. They go to play on the swings. They are happy.

Tim and Jen are twins. They like to play with cars and trucks. They have many cars and trucks in their room. They make noises like vroom and beep.

One day, mom says, "We are going to the park. Get ready." Tim and Jen are happy. They love the park. They want to bring their cars and trucks. They put some in a bag.

Mom takes them to the car. She says, "I have a surprise for you. We have a new driver today. His name is Bob. He is very nice. Say hello to Bob."

Tim and Jen look at Bob. He is sitting in the front. He has a big nose, a big beard, and a big hat. He smiles at them. He says, "Hello, Tim and Jen. I am Bob. I am your driver today. Are you ready to go to the park?"

Tim and Jen think Bob is ugly. They do not like his nose, his beard, and his hat. They do not say hello. They hide behind mom. They whisper, "Mom, we do not like Bob. He is ugly. Can we have another driver?"

Mom says, "Shh, Tim and Jen. That is not nice. Bob is not ugly. He is different. He is a good driver. He will take us to the park safely. You should be polite and friendly. Say hello to Bob."

Tim and Jen feel bad. They do not want to be rude. They peek at Bob. He still smiles at them. He says, "Do you like cars and trucks? I see you have some in your bag. I like cars and trucks too. I have some in my hat. Do you want to see?"

Tim and Jen are curious. They like cars and trucks. They nod. Bob takes off his hat. He shows them his cars and trucks. They are small and colorful. He says, "These are my cars and trucks. I bring them with me everywhere. They are my friends. Do you want to play with them?"

Tim and Jen are surprised. They think Bob is funny. They like his cars and trucks. They say, "Yes, please. Can we play with them?" They take some from his hat. They make noises like vroom and beep.

Bob says, "Sure, you can play with them. But be careful. Do not lose them. They are very special to me." He puts his hat back on. He says, "Now, let's go to the park. Are you ready?"

Tim and Jen say, "Yes, we are ready. Thank you, Bob. You are a nice driver. And you are not ugly. You are different. And we like different." They smile at Bob. They hold their cars and trucks. They are happy.

Mom says, "That's good, Tim and Jen. I am proud of you. You are learning to be kind and respectful. And you are making a new friend. Bob is a good driver. And he is a good person. And he has a good hat." She smiles at Bob. She says, "Thank you, Bob. You are a great driver. And you have a great hat." She buckles up. She says, "Now, let's go to the park. And have some fun."

Once upon a time, a little girl called Emily was in her classroom. On the wall, there was a big blackboard. Emily wanted to choose a thick chalk to write on the blackboard.

Ben and Lily like to jog in the park. They jog fast and slow, and they jog with their dog Spot. Spot is a big and brown dog. He likes to jog with Ben and Lily.

One day, they see a big square in the park. The square is open and has many colors. Ben and Lily want to see what is inside the square. They jog to the square with Spot.

Lily and Sam love to play theater. They have a big box that they put in the living room. They cut out a hole for the stage. They use their toys and clothes to make the actors and the costumes. They invite their mom and dad to watch their show.

Today, they are doing a show about a princess and a dragon. Lily is the princess and Sam is the dragon. Lily wears a pink dress and a crown. Sam wears a green shirt and a mask. Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she saw a big chocolate in the store. She thought it was so yummy, but also very expensive. She asked her mom if she could buy it, but her mom said no.

Once upon a time, there was a playful bunny named Bob. Bob loved to hop and play in the sunny meadow near his home. One day, while he was playing, he found a big, red radish.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Emma. Outside, the sky was grey and gloomy. Emma was feeling sad.

Emma's dad said, "It sure is nice to see the sun again. I'm so glad it's a beautiful day."

Once there were two friends, Sarah and Tony. They both wanted a shelter. So they worked together to build one.

Tony and Sarah gathered wood and nails. They used a hammer to build the walls and a saw to make the roof. Sarah cut the roof panels and Tony nailed them together.

Once upon a time there was a bald man who wanted to build something special. He worked very hard on it every day and when he was finished, he had built a big medal. He was so proud of his medal and he wanted to show it off!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the lovely sunshine. One day, she saw a butterfly flying in the sky. It was so pretty!

Once upon a time, there was a happy girl named Lily. She loved to eat ice cream cones. One day, she saw a man lying on the ground. She asked him, "Are you okay?"

Billy was walking in the park. He was feeling happy so he started to skip. He looked down and saw a leaf on the ground. It was a regular leaf, not too big and not too small. When he got back to his house, he put the leaf on a shelf to remind him of that happy day in the park.

"Yay! The duck likes olives!" Ben cheered.

Ben and Lily smiled. They sat on the grass and watched the ducks swim and eat olives. They had a lot of fun at the park.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside and explore the world around him. One day, Timmy went on an adventure to find his missing pants. He looked high and low, but he couldn't find them anywhere.

As he continued his search, he saw a dangerous snake slithering towards him. Timmy was scared, but he remembered that his mom had taught him how to record animals with his phone. He quickly took out his phone and recorded the snake.

Timmy's mom found him lying on the ground and rushed him to the hospital. Sadly, Timmy didn't make it. His mom was heartbroken and wished she had never let him go on that dangerous adventure. She watched the video of the snake that Timmy had recorded and cried, knowing that it was the last thing he ever did.

They were amazed to see how brightly they all glowed. Priscilla gave them a final wave and flew off, satisfied that she had shared her magic with the children.

Once there was a famous tie. It was purple and sparkly. Everybody liked it. One day, the tie was torn by accident. Everyone was sad. They tried to fix it but nothing worked. Everyone was sad that it was ruined. Then, something magical happened. A fairy came and flew down from the sky. She waved her wand and it fixed the tie. Everyone was very happy and cheered. Max was a very careless boy. He liked to play all day, but his mum kept telling him to help around the house. One day Max decided he would clean up the garden.

Max had a light bulb moment and quickly put the tip back in the garden. He had been careless to not think about this before. Now he was sure to remember to return things to their rightful owners.

Once upon a time, there was a lovely goat who lived on a farm. Every day, the goat would leave her pen and walk around in the sun.

"Tom, Tom, we have to hide! The police are coming!" he said.

Tom was confused. He did not know what Sam was talking about. He looked at the box and saw a badge, a gun, a hat and a radio. He realized that the box belonged to their dad, who was a police officer.

"Sam, don't worry. This is dad's stuff. He is not home right now. He is working. The police are not coming for us." he said.

He tried to calm Sam down, but it was too late. The phone was still on and the police heard everything. They traced the call and found their address. They thought that someone had stolen their dad's things and was in trouble. They came to their house with sirens and lights.

Tom and Sam heard a loud knock on the door. They were very scared. They hid under the bed and hoped that the police would go away. But they did not. They broke the door and ran upstairs. They found the box and the phone in their room. They saw Tom and Sam under the bed.

"Freeze! Put your hands up!" one of the police officers shouted.

Tom and Sam did not understand. They cried and begged for mercy. They said that they were sorry and that they did not mean to do anything bad. They said that they were just playing with their dad's things.

The police officers did not listen. They thought that Tom and Sam were lying and that they were dangerous. They grabbed them and put them in handcuffs. They took them to their car and drove them to the police station. They locked them in a small cell with no toys, no food and no water. They left them there and forgot about them.

Tom and Sam were very hungry, very thirsty and very sad. They missed their dad and their mom and their toys. They wished that they never opened the box. They wished that they never played with the phone. They wished that they never heard the voice. They wished that they never made the police angry. They wished that they could go home.

But they could not. They were stuck in the cell. They had no one to help them. They had no one to love them. They had no one to applaud them. They had no one to play with. They had no one to hug them. They had no one to tell them a story. They had no one to say good night.

They had nothing.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and collect pretty pebbles. One day, she found a shiny pebble that was stuck tight in the mud. She tried to pull it out, but it wouldn't budge.

Lily decided to search for something to help her get the pebble out. She looked around and found a stick that was just the right size. She used the stick to pry the pebble loose and it finally came free.

Lily learned that sometimes you need to search for a solution to a problem and that with a little effort, you can achieve your goal. She also learned that even something as small as a pebble can be valuable and worth the effort to obtain.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Joe. He was always happy and very healthy. 

One day, Joe saw a lovely bird in the sky. He was so amazed and pointed at it. 

"Look, look!", he said to his mum. 

His mum looked up and smiled. "Joe, don't you realize the sky is filled with so many birds?"

Joe thought for a second, and then his face lit up. He had realized that the sky was full of wonderful birds. 

Mum smiled, proud of her little boy. She was glad to see him realize something so special. Joe was happy too - he had just had a wonderful realization.

Bunny and Fox were friends. They liked to play in the forest. One day, they saw a hunter. He had a big stick that made loud noises. He wanted to catch Bunny and Fox.

"Run, Bunny, run!" Fox said. "The hunter is bad. He will hurt us."

Bunny and Fox ran as fast as they could. They hid behind a big rock. The hunter followed them. He looked for them with his eyes.

"Where are they?" the hunter said. "I want to make a coat from their fur."

Fox had an idea. He was brave and smart. He wanted to protect Bunny. He made a noise like a bird.

"Tweet, tweet!" Fox said.

The hunter heard the noise. He thought it was a bird. He was foolish. He left the rock and walked to the noise.

"Ha, ha!" Fox said. "I tricked the hunter. He is not smart. He is silly."

Bunny and Fox came out from behind the rock. They saw the hunter walking away. They were happy and safe.

"Thank you, Fox," Bunny said. "You are a good friend. You protected me from the hunter."

"You are welcome, Bunny," Fox said. "You are a good friend too. Let's go and play some more."

Bunny and Fox ran away. They played in the forest. They were careful and happy. They never saw the hunter again.

Tommy loved to examine things. He liked to look at them, touch them, smell them, and sometimes taste them. He wanted to know everything about them. He had a big box of things he had examined in his room.

One day, he found a shiny thing in the park. It was round and smooth and had a hole in the middle. He wondered what it was. He put it in his pocket and took it home. He wanted to examine it more.

He took out the shiny thing and put it on his bed. He looked at it with his eyes. He touched it with his fingers. He smelled it with his nose. He did not taste it with his mouth. He thought it was harmless.

But then, he heard a loud noise. It was his mom. She came into his room and saw the shiny thing. She looked scared and angry. She shouted at Tommy. She said the shiny thing was bad. She said it was a memory of a war. She said it could explode and hurt him and her and the house.

She took the shiny thing away from Tommy. She put it in a bag and called someone. She said they would come and take it away. She hugged Tommy and said she was sorry. She said she was glad he was safe. She said he should not examine things he did not know.

Tommy felt sad and confused. He did not understand what a war was. He did not understand what a memory was. He did not understand why the shiny thing was bad. He only wanted to examine it. He liked to examine things. He wondered what else he could not examine. He wondered what else he did not know.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to dance and play in the pool. One day, she went to the pool with her mom and dad. They were having fun splashing and swimming when Lily saw a shiny red ball.

Lily ran to grab the ball, but she slipped and fell into the pool. She couldn't swim, and she started to panic. Her mom and dad quickly jumped in to save her. They were so lucky they got there in time!

After they got out of the pool, Lily's dad said, "Lily, you have to be careful around the pool. It's not safe to run and jump like that." Lily nodded and said, "I just wanted to dance with the ball." Her mom smiled and said, "We can dance with the ball outside of the pool, too." Lily laughed and said, "Okay!" They all danced around the pool, happy and safe. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in her backyard, where she had a sandbox with lots of toys. One day, she found a shiny coin in the sandbox and picked it up. She thought it was very pretty and showed it to her mom.

Her mom said, "That's a lucky coin, Lily. Keep it safe." Lily put the coin in her pocket and went back to playing. Suddenly, she saw a big bird flying overhead. It was carrying a stick in its beak. Lily thought the bird was very smart to know how to carry things like that.

Later that day, Lily and her mom went to the store. Lily saw a toy she really wanted, but her mom said they couldn't buy it right now. As they were leaving the store, Lily saw a man pause outside the window. He was looking at the same toy she wanted. Lily wondered if he was going to buy it. 

The next day, Lily went back to her sandbox to play. She saw something shiny in the sand and realized it was her lucky coin! She was so happy and thought about how lucky she was to find it again. Just then, the big bird flew back and dropped the stick it was carrying. Lily remembered how smart the bird was and thought maybe it was trying to tell her something. She looked at the stick and realized it was shaped like the toy she wanted at the store! Lily knew what she had to do. She ran back to the store and bought the toy with her lucky coin. She was so happy she could barely contain herself!

Lily likes to play with her toy cars. She has many cars of different colors and sizes. Some are big and loud, some are small and fast. She likes to make them race and crash on the floor.

One day, she finds a new car in her toy box. It is shiny and silver, and has a cute face on the front. It looks like a happy car. Lily picks it up and makes it zoom around the room. She pretends it is a friendly robot car that can talk and sing.

But then, she spills some juice on the car. The juice makes the car wet and sticky. Lily feels sad. She does not want her new car to be dirty. She runs to the kitchen and gets a cloth. She wipes the car with the cloth, gently and carefully. She tries to make it shiny and silver again.

The car feels the cloth on its metal body. It thinks Lily is being nice to it. It makes a happy beep and says, "Thank you, Lily. You are a good friend. I like you." Lily hears the car talk and sing. She is surprised and happy. She hugs the car and says, "You are welcome, car. You are a good car. I like you too." They smile at each other and play some more.

Once upon a time there was a young girl named Penny. Penny loved to borrow things from her mom. One day, Penny asked her mom, "Mom, can I borrow the prune?" 

Her mom smiled and said, "What do you need the prune for, Penny?" 

"I want to play with it," Penny replied. Her mom said that she could borrow it if she promised to take good care of it and give it back.

So Penny borrowed the prune and played with it all afternoon. When she was done, the prune felt very dull in her hands. She was worried that she had broken it. 

She took it back to her mom and asked, â€œMom, did I break the prune?â€ 

Her mom said, â€œNo Penny, you didn't break it. But next time you borrow something, remember to take good care of it, okay?â€ 

Penny nodded, relieved. She promised her mom that she would take better care of things when she borrowed them in the future.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He loved to play with his toys all day long. One day, his mom told him that they were going to celebrate his birthday. Timmy was so happy! He couldn't wait to see his friends and eat cake.

On the day of his birthday, Timmy's mom brought out a big cake with candles on top. Timmy blew out the candles and his friends cheered. Then, they all sat down to eat the cake. It was so yummy and easy to eat.

After they finished eating, Timmy's mom gave him a present. He was so excited to open it! Inside, there was a toy car that he had been wanting for a long time. He was so happy that he started to jump up and down. Suddenly, he heard a crack. Oh no! He had accidentally broken his new toy car. But his mom told him not to worry, they could fix it together. And so, they did. Timmy's birthday was the best day ever!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to watch TV. One day, her mom bought her a new TV. "Be careful, Lily. The TV is fragile," said her mom. "Ok, mommy," said Lily.

Lily turned on the TV and started to watch her favorite show. Suddenly, she heard a knock on the door. It was her friend, Timmy. "Hi, Lily! Can I come in and watch TV with you?" asked Timmy. "Sure, Timmy! Come in!" said Lily.

They sat on the couch and watched TV together. Timmy stared at the TV and said, "Wow, this is a big TV!" "Yes, it is!" said Lily. They watched TV for a while, but then Lily accidentally knocked over a vase. "Oh no! The vase is broken!" cried Lily. "It's ok, Lily. It was just a vase. We can clean it up," said Timmy.

Jane and her mommy were outside in the backyard. Jane saw the pool and she asked what it was. Her mommy said it was a pool. Jane was very excited and asked if she could go in it. Her mommy said they had to clean it first.

So they got to work. Jane's mommy put on rubber gloves and started to scrub the sides and the bottom of the pool. Jane loved helping her mom, so she got a small brush and she scrubbed too. After lots of scrubbing and sweeping, the pool was finally clean.

Now Jane could go in it. She sat down on the edge and then she splashed into the water. Jane giggled and laughed as she splashed around the pool. Suddenly, she felt something hurt her foot. She quickly got out and told her mommy about it. Her mommy said there must have been something sharp at the bottom.

So they looked around the pool and sure enough, they found some broken glass. Jane was a bit scared so her mommy told her it was all cleaned up now. She put her hands around Jane and said that nothing would hurt her again. 

Jane was so happy. She splashed around in the clean pool the entire day.

Once there was a bear called Bob. Bob was always very hungry. He wanted to find something to eat.

One day, he heard thunder. He was scared. Suddenly, he saw a tree full of juicy apples. His mouth began to water. He wanted to chew them so badly!

He slowly climbed the tree and carefully chewed on the apples. They were so juicy and delicious. Bob ate every single apple.

Afterwards, Bob was full and happy. The thunder had disappeared and Bob could rest. He had been so hungry and the apples had tasted great.

Tim and Mia like to play with rocks. They have many rocks of different colors and shapes. They make piles of rocks and pretend they are castles or mountains. Sometimes they throw rocks at each other and have a war.

One day, they find a big rock that is open. It has a hole in it. They wonder what is inside. They look at each other and smile. They decide to play a game. They take turns to put their hand in the hole and feel what is there.

Tim goes first. He puts his hand in the hole and says, "I feel something soft and furry. Maybe it is a rabbit or a mouse." He pulls his hand out and shows Mia. He has a tuft of brown fur in his hand.

Mia goes next. She puts her hand in the hole and says, "I feel something hard and shiny. Maybe it is a coin or a ring." She pulls her hand out and shows Tim. She has a small metal button in her hand.

Tim and Mia are happy. They think they have found a treasure. They want to find more. They take turns to put their hand in the hole again and again. They find more fur and more buttons. They laugh and clap.

But they do not know that the hole is not empty. There is something else in the hole. Something that does not like to be disturbed. Something that has teeth and claws. Something that is angry and hungry.

The last time Tim puts his hand in the hole, he does not feel anything soft or hard. He feels something sharp and wet. He feels pain. He screams. He tries to pull his hand out, but he cannot. Something is holding his hand. Something is biting his hand.

Mia hears Tim scream. She sees blood on his hand. She is scared. She runs to help him. She tries to pull his hand out, but she cannot. Something is holding his hand. Something is biting his hand.

Tim and Mia cry. They call for help. But no one hears them. No one comes. They are alone with the rock. The rock that is open. The rock that has a monster. The rock that is their end.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named John. He was very keen to win a prize. One day, he saw a big contest was being held to win a big, shiny prize. He was so excited and he wanted to enter! He started to zip around and around, trying to get to the contest in time. 

But when he reached the contest, he saw it was really dull. All the other entries were plain and boring, and he was the only one who was zipping around. He was disappointed and felt that he didn't stand a chance of winning, but he still decided to compete. 

At the end of the day, John found out he had won the big, shiny prize! Everyone around him was so surprised and happy, because he was the only one who was different. 

This story teaches us that it is important to be unique and not be afraid to stand out. Being different makes you special and it can help you win prizes if you never give up!

Once upon a time, there was a big wide moon in the night sky. One night, a little girl wanted to bake something special. She put on her apron and started mixing together ingredients.

Soon, she was ready to bake. She put the mix in the oven and waited patiently. A few minutes later, the oven made a happy sound. The little girl opened the oven door and saw a beautiful cake inside. She said a big "yay!"

She put the cake on a plate and smiled. Then she looked up at the wide moon in the sky and said, "Happy baking, moon!" Then the little girl ate her delicious cake and smiled. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a nice little girl named Amy. Her mom and dad loved her very much and always wanted to support her. 
One day, Amy's dad told her about the fine prize she could win in the competition she had entered. He said if she worked really hard, she would win the prize. 

Amy was so excited. She put in lots of effort to prepare for the competition, and soon it was time for the big day. The judges were so impressed with Amy and announced that she was the winner! 

Amy's dad hugged her tight and said, "I'm so proud of you! You worked so hard and it paid off. I'm glad I could support you." 

Amy smiled and replied, "Thanks, dad! I'm so happy I won the fine prize!"

Once upon a time, there was a nosy little dog named Spot. Spot loved to play and have fun. One day, he saw a big box in his house. Spot was very curious about the box. He wanted to see what was inside.

Spot's mom came into the room and said, "Let's unpack the box, Spot!" They opened the box together. Inside the box, there were many things to play with. There was a ball, a bat, and a net. Spot's mom said, "These are for a sport called 'catch'."

Spot was very excited to play this new sport. He took the ball and threw it to his mom. She caught it and threw it back to Spot. They played catch all day long. Spot loved the new sport and was so happy they unpacked the box.

Once upon a time, there were two friends who loved to play together. One day, they played a game of hide and seek. After a few minutes, one of them found the other. But when he found his friend, he saw that his friend had an itch. He asked, "What's wrong? Why do you have an itch?" His friend replied, "My shirt is dirty, and it's making me itchy." 

The friend then had a brilliant idea! He said, "Let's share! I have a clean shirt here that I can give you!" His friend was so happy and he agreed to take the shirt. The friends shared the shirt, and the friend with the itch was now feeling much better. 

They both laughed out loud and hugged each other to celebrate their special moment. Then they continued to play until it was time to go home. They were very happy, both with their special moment as well as sharing the shirt â€“ it was a perfect day!

Once upon a time there was a rare animal called an elephant. He was looking for a place to hide. He searched and searched until he saw a big tree. He went inside the tree to hide.

As he was hiding he heard an unfamiliar noise. He looked and saw the tree's owner! The elephant quickly hid behind some leaves.

The tree's owner was looking for something. He looked around but could not see the elephant. Suddenly, the owner spotted something behind the leaves. It was the elephant!

The owner was very happy to see the rare elephant. He called some friends to come and see and they all enjoyed watching the elephant hide.

The elephant stayed in the tree for many days and the owner was very happy. Finally, the elephant decided it was time to leave. He said goodbye to the tree's owner and went off in search of a new home.

Once upon a time there was a boy, who was three years old. He was always looking for fun things to do. One day he decided to go for a walk in the woods. As he was walking he saw something funny. It was a big lion, making a lot of noise! The boy was so surprised and scared that he ran away.

The next day he decided to go back to the same spot and take a closer look. He was very brave and slowly he crept closer to the lion. The lion just sat there, looking happy and a bit crazy. The boy was curious, so he walked even closer and discoverd the lion was not dangerous at all.

The boy wanted to get to know the lion better, so he started talking to it. The lion just sat there and listened. Soon they became friends and the boy started saying hello to the lion every day when he went for a walk. The lion seemed to like the boy a lot too!

The boy and the lion had many fun adventures together and the boy always got home in time for dinner. He would tell his parents the stories about his crazy lion friend. They all had a lot of laughs. 

The boy and the lion were best friends forever.

Once there were two friends: a dog and a cat. They wanted to discover something new, so they decided to take a walk down the road. On their way they saw lots of different things, but none of them seemed interesting. 

Suddenly, the dog noticed something in the distance. He pointed it out to his friend and they ran towards it. As they got closer, they noticed that it was a harmless creature. It was a small, fluffy bunny! 

The two friends were overjoyed and they decided to take the bunny home with them. They brought the bunny back to their house and the friends decided to keep it as a pet. 

The dog and the cat had made a new discovery on their walk down the road, and they both were very happy that they had discovered something harmless and fun. They had a new best friend!

Ben and Lily were playing in the park. They liked to slide, swing and run. But they also liked to search for things. They searched for bugs, flowers and rocks. Sometimes they found something special, like a shiny coin or a feather.

One day, they saw a big hill. They wanted to climb it and see what was on the other side. They asked their mom if they could go. She said yes, but be careful and come back soon. Ben and Lily ran to the hill and started to climb. They used their hands and feet and helped each other.

When they reached the top, they saw a surprise. There was a big lake with ducks and fish. There was also a boat with a sail. It was red and white and looked powerful. Ben and Lily wanted to go on the boat and sail on the lake. They ran to the boat and jumped in.

"Hello, who are you?" a voice said. Ben and Lily looked around and saw a man. He was sitting on the boat and holding a rope. He looked angry. "This is my boat. You can't just come and take it. Get off now!"

Ben and Lily were scared. They did not know the man was there. They did not mean to take his boat. They just wanted to have fun. They said sorry and tried to get off. But the man was still mad. He pulled the rope and made the sail move. The boat started to move fast on the lake. Ben and Lily screamed.

"Help! Help!" they shouted. They wanted their mom. They wanted to go back to the park. They did not like the boat or the lake or the man. They wished they never climbed the hill. They wished they never saw the surprise.

Once upon a time, there was a young girl named Katie. She was very excited to learn how to draw.

So one day she asked her mom, "Can you teach me to draw an image?" Katie's mom smiled and said, "Yes, of course I can! I would love to show you."

Katie was very enthusiastic to learn so she followed her mom to her studio. The studio was filled with paints, markers, and paper.

Katie's mom began to draw an image on a piece of paper. "Look, this is an airplane," she said. Katie watched in awe as the image began to take shape.

"Now it's your turn," said her mom. Katie picked up a blue marker and drew a small circle. She was so proud of her work and smiled happily.

Katie's mom asked, "Do you want to learn more?" Katie's eyes lit up and she nodded eagerly. Her mom's request made her even more excited to learn. Together they created many new images.

Once upon a time, there was an enormous cactus. Its spikes were as sharp as thorns, and it's green body reached far into the sky.

One day, a three year old came across the cactus. She was walking in the desert and noticed how big it was. She got close to the enormous cactus and called out to her mom, asking to pick it.

Her mom quickly told her to keep away. She said, "No no. You can't miss that cactus." 

But the three year old was very stubborn and she ignored her mom and reached out for the cactus. As soon as she touched it, she was hurt by the sharp spikes.

She began to cry loudly and felt a lot of pain. Her mom quickly came to help her. The three year old felt very sad and she had to go to the doctor.

Sadly, the three year old had to miss playing outdoors and visit the doctor often, because of the enormous cactus.

George was feeling adventurous. He wanted to explore the world with his best friend Coco. Coco was a big, brown cocoa-coloured bear with buttons for eyes. He was George's best cuddly buddy. 

One day, George and Coco decided to go for an adventure in the park. They explored all the interesting things around the park. Suddenly, George noticed a big hill at the end of the park. With excitement, he grabbed Coco's hand and started to push him up the hill. But the hill was steep! After pushing and pushing, George and Coco finally managed to get to the top of the hill. The view was amazing! George was so proud of himself and Coco. 

At the end of the day, George and Coco had a great time. Their adventurous adventure was filled with lots of pushing to get to the top of the hill. It was an adventure they would never forget!

Mum and Dad were very proud of their son, Jack. They wanted him to do so many things like all the other children. So, they decided to load Jack's day with all kinds of activities such as painting and playing, but also with a lecture about math. 

Jack didn't want to go to the lecture because he found math to be very difficult. But, his parents insisted, "You have to go to the lecture. It will make us proud of you."

Jack asked his mum and dad, "What if I'm not good at it? I'm only three." 

Mum and Dad looked at each other, they knew Jack was right. They hugged him and said, "Don't worry, Jack. Just do your best".

But when Jack arrived at the lecture, he became so overwhelmed. He was so scared, he couldn't even listen! He didn't understand the math and he was so embarrassed. 

Sadly, Jack had a very bad experience. He felt like he let his parents down. He didn't understand the lecture, and he was certainly not proud of himself.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Lily. She was very excited for Christmas because it was only one day away.

Lily asked her mum, "What will Santa bring me?"

"That's a worry for another day, Lily!" said her mum.

Lily couldn't wait, so the next day she woke up very early. Suddenly, her room started to change. She now saw a Christmas tree with presents underneath it.

"Mummy! Mummy!" she yelled. "Santa came!"

Lily was so excited. She opened all her presents, finding lots of surprises inside.

When she was finished, Lily hugged her mum and said, "My Christmas is changed because of you."

The snail was feeling polite. He was crossing the road and was almost finished when he heard a loud noise. It was a car! The car didn't see the snail and it drove right over him. The snail finished in a shell. The end.

Once there was a little girl called Daisy. One day, Daisy went to the park and saw something very impressive. It was a shiny crystal! She decided to take it and started to play with it in her bedroom.

Suddenly, Daisy heard her mum calling her. She quickly hid the crystal under her bed.

When Daisy went to the living room, her mum said to her, "Why did you take so long?" Daisy started to complain, but her mum just said "Nevermind."

Daisy thought the crystal was very special. She wanted to keep it and show her friends, but she was afraid of getting in trouble from her mum.

The next day, Daisy decided to tell her mum about it. She thought she'd try and ask politely, but then she started to cry. "Please can I keep the crystal, it's so impressive!" 

Her mum, who was very understanding, smiled at Daisy and said warmly, "You can keep it, darling." 

Daisy was so happy! She hugged her mum and together they went to see the crystal in her bedroom and marvel at its beauty.

Anna and Ben were playing in the park with their ball. They liked to pass the ball to each other and catch it. Sometimes they threw the ball very high and watched it fly in the sky.

One day, they saw a giant walking in the park. He was very big and tall, and he had a long beard and a big hat. He looked scary, but he was not mean. He was harmless. He just liked to walk and see the flowers and the trees.

"Hello, little ones," the giant said to Anna and Ben. "Do you want to play with me?"

Anna and Ben were afraid of the giant. They did not know what to do. They held their ball tight and hid behind a bench.

"Don't be scared," the giant said. "I won't hurt you. I just want to have some fun. Can I pass the ball with you?"

Anna and Ben looked at each other. They saw that the giant had a kind smile and a gentle voice. They decided to give him a chance.

"Okay," Anna said. "But you have to be careful. Don't throw the ball too hard or too far."

"Of course," the giant said. "I will be gentle. Thank you for playing with me."

Anna and Ben came out from behind the bench and passed the ball to the giant. The giant passed the ball back to them. They had a lot of fun. They laughed and talked and made a new friend. The giant was not scary at all. He was harmless.

Once upon a time, there was a brave girl who loved exploring. One day, she decided to take a long walk and explore an incredible landscape that she had never seen before. She wanted to soak in all of the beauty, so she started running through the fields, laughing and twirling.

When she noticed she was getting tired, she started hurrying. With every step she took, she couldn't help but admire the incredible beauty of the landscape around her. The sunbeams created patterns in the grass and the colors were so vibrant and beautiful.

Eventually, the brave girl got to a place that she had never seen before. There was a big tree with a tire swing and lots of animals that were so cute! She was so excited and felt like she could stay there forever.

But then she started to hear a sound in the distance. It was getting closer and closer, and she quickly realized that it was time to go. She quickly climbed down from the tire swing, and began to hurry back home.

When she got home, she was happy to see her family who had been so worried about where she had gone. She couldn't wait to tell them all about the incredible landscape she had seen and explored.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Daisy who lived near the beach. She was very independent and always wanted to try new things. So one day, Daisy decided to go kayaking. She had never been kayaking before and was a bit scared. But after a few practice paddles, Daisy started to have fun. 

Suddenly, a big wave came and slapped the side of her kayak. Daisy was taken by surprise and she let out a loud scream. But she didn't give up. She kept paddling and the wave eventually passed. Daisy was feeling more independent and confident. 

She paddled back to the beach and showed all her friends the kayak she had been riding in. Everyone gave her a big round of applause for being so brave and independent. Daisy was so happy and enjoyed telling everyone about her adventure. 

The End.

Anna and Ben were playing with their toys in the park. They saw a big crane lifting heavy things. They wanted to know how it worked.

"Let's go and ask the man who drives the crane," Ben said.

"OK, but be careful," Anna said.

They ran to the crane and saw a man sitting inside. He was wearing a helmet and a vest.

"Hello, sir," Ben said. "Can you tell us how you make the crane move?"

The man smiled and opened the door. He invited them to sit with him.

"Sure, I can tell you," he said. "The crane has a motor and a cable. The motor makes the cable go up and down. The cable has a hook at the end. I use a joystick to control the hook. I can lift and lower things with the hook."

"Wow, that's amazing," Anna said. "You must be very intelligent to do that."

The man laughed and said, "Thank you, but I'm not the only one who is intelligent. The crane is also intelligent. It has sensors and computers that help me. They tell me how much weight I can lift and how far I can move. They also warn me if there is any danger or problem."

"Really? How do they do that?" Ben asked.

The man showed them a screen and some buttons. He explained how the sensors and computers worked. He also told them some rules and safety tips for using the crane.

Anna and Ben learned a lot from the man. They thanked him and said goodbye. They went back to their toys and pretended to be crane drivers.

They had fun and also learned something new. They realized that the crane was not just a big toy, but a useful and intelligent machine. They also realized that the man was not just a driver, but a teacher and a friend. They learned to be curious, respectful, and grateful.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Emily. Emily was a very independent girl and she loved to go outside and do things by herself. One day she was feeling happy and decided to go skipping. She skipped through the long grass and sang a song. Soon she came to a big garden full of different plants and flowers. 

But what caught Emily's eye was the strange little trees growing in the garden. She couldn't believe her eyes! They were broccoli trees! She skipped over to the trees and looked closely at the broccoli. It was so delicious and juicy. 

Emily started picking the broccoli and putting it in the basket she was carrying. Then she skipped off happily to deliver the broccoli to her family. From that day on, Emily was so proud of herself for being so independent and she never forgot her broccoli picking adventures.

Once upon a time there was a popular, stretchy-legged girl named Suzie. She always loved to stretch out her legs and show everyone how long and limber they were. But one day, Suzie was feeling so tired she just couldn't do it. Suzie lifted her head and asked her mom, "Why can't I stretch like I used to?"

Her mom smiled and said, "Suzie, we all need to use our lungs when we stretch. You have to take a deep breath and use your lungs to help you stretch." Then Suzie practiced and she soon saw how deep breaths could help her stretch her legs even further.

From then on, Suzie was the most popular girl in the neighbourhood for her stretching talent. But she never forgot the important lesson that day. Whenever she needed to stretch, Suzie always remembered to breathe and use her lungs.

This important lesson teaches us all that when we work hard and use our lungs, we can use our strength to reach our goals.

Once there was a mommy, a daddy, and a baby. The baby was only three years old. One day, Mommy wanted to take the baby to the park. So she got the baby's coat and put it on him. She was about to do up the buckle, but then she forgot.

The baby was getting crazy. He wanted to go to the park! So he tried to do up the buckle himself, but it was too tricky. Mommy noticed he was having trouble and she remembered the buckle. She did it up for him so he could go.

When the baby was all ready, they went to the park. They had so much fun that Mommy and Daddy almost forgot about the buckle again. But the baby reminded them - he didn't want to forget the buckle again!

One day, a modest rabbit named Bob found a big, red apple. The apple was on the ground under a tree. Bob was very happy. He wanted to eat the apple, but he saw that it was starting to rot. "Oh no," said Bob. "I can't eat this apple now."

Bob had a friend, a bird named Sue. Sue saw Bob looking sad. "What's wrong, Bob?" asked Sue. "I found this big, red apple, but it's starting to rot," said Bob. "I can't eat it."

Sue had a secret. She knew how to make the rot go away. "Bob, I can help you," said Sue. "I know a secret to fix the apple." Sue sang a special song. The rot went away, and the apple was good again. Bob and Sue shared the apple and were very happy.

Mia loved to whistle. She whistled when she woke up, when she ate, when she played, and when she went to bed. She whistled happy songs, sad songs, and silly songs. She whistled so much that her mom and dad sometimes asked her to be quiet.

One day, Mia went to the park with her mom. She saw a charming bird on a tree. It had bright feathers and a long tail. Mia wanted to be friends with the bird. She whistled a song to the bird. The bird looked at her and whistled back. Mia was very happy. She whistled more songs to the bird. The bird whistled more songs to Mia.

But not everyone liked Mia's whistling. A big boy who was playing with a ball heard Mia and the bird. He did not like their noise. He wanted to play with the bird. He threw his ball at the tree. The ball hit the bird and made it fall. Mia saw the bird fall and cried. She ran to the bird and picked it up. The bird was hurt and scared. It did not whistle anymore.
