Mia was very angry at the big boy. She shouted at him. "You are mean! You hurt my friend! You are not nice!" The big boy laughed at Mia. He said, "It is just a bird. It is not your friend. You are silly. You whistle too much. You are annoying!"

Mia's mom heard Mia and the big boy. She came to them and saw the bird in Mia's hands. She saw the ball on the ground. She understood what happened. She scolded the big boy. She said, "You are rude! You hurt the bird! You are not kind! You should say sorry to Mia and the bird!"

The big boy did not want to say sorry. He was stubborn. He said, "No! I will not say sorry. It is my ball. I can do what I want. You are not my mom. You can not tell me what to do!"

Mia's mom was very disappointed in the big boy. She said, "You are wrong. You can not do what you want. You have to respect others. You have to be gentle with animals. You have to apologize when you make a mistake. You have to learn to be a good person."

She took Mia and the bird to a bench. She hugged Mia and comforted her. She checked the bird and saw that it was not badly hurt. She gave the bird some water and some seeds. She said, "Don't worry, Mia. The bird will be okay. It is a brave and charming bird. It will whistle again soon. You are a good and sweet girl. You love to whistle and make friends. You are not silly or annoying. You are wonderful."

Mia smiled and thanked her mom. She held the bird gently and whispered to it. She said, "I am sorry, bird. I hope you feel better. You are my friend. You are beautiful. You are amazing."

The bird heard Mia and felt her warmth. It blinked and opened its beak. It whistled a soft and grateful song to Mia. Mia whistled a happy and loving song to the bird. They whistled together and made a light in their hearts.

Jill was feeling very thoughtful one day. She decided that it was the perfect day to visit her best friend, Hannah. 

When Jill arrived at Hannah's house, she knocked on the door. When Hannah opened the door, she beamed with joy. "Jill!" she said. 

"I brought you a special surprise," said Jill. She handed Hannah a big package. 

Inside of the package was a big, beautiful bow. But when Hannah looked closer, she noticed it was something even better. Inside the bow was a big can of tuna! 

Hannah was so excited that she bowed to thank Jill. She said, "Thank you for being so thoughtful! I love this special surprise." 

Jill smiled. She knew that she made the right decision in bringing a tuna for her best friend.

Once there was a little girl named Daisy. Daisy loved exploring the world around her. Her favorite thing was looking for her special treasures.

One day Daisy found something very special. It was gray, fragile and sparkly. Daisy was so excited to have found her special treasure. She carefully put it in her pocket and ran to show her mom.

When Daisy got home she couldn't find her treasure! She looked in her pocket and it was gone! Daisy was so sad and started to cry. She missed her treasure and was sad that it was gone. 

Daisy's mom smiled when she saw how sad Daisy was. "Don't worry, my sweet," she said. She pulled out a similar gray and fragile treasure and handed it to Daisy. 

Daisy smiled with delight! She hugged her mom and thanked her for her special gift. Daisy never missed her special treasure again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to cook with her mommy in the kitchen. One day, they made yummy cookies together. "These cookies smell so good!" said Lily. "I can't wait to eat them!" 

After they finished cooking, Lily accidentally spilled some crumbs on the rug. "Uh-oh, mommy. I made a mess," said Lily. "That's okay, sweetie. We'll just clean it up," replied her mommy. 

As they cleaned up the crumbs, Lily felt the rug and noticed it was rough. "Mommy, why is the rug so rough?" asked Lily. "It's because it's made of a rough material, like burlap," explained her mommy. 

Lily and her mommy sat down on the rug and enjoyed their cookies together. "These cookies are so yummy and we had fun cooking them together," said Lily. "Yes, we did, sweetie. I love cooking with you," replied her mommy.

Anna and Ben went to the zoo with their mom. They saw many animals. They saw lions, monkeys, elephants and more. Anna liked the lions best. She pointed at them and said, "Look, mom, big cats!"

Ben liked the monkeys best. He pointed at them and said, "Look, mom, funny animals!" He laughed when they jumped and swung on the trees.

Mom took them to the cafeteria for lunch. They had sandwiches, fruit and juice. They were hungry and ate everything. Anna said, "This is delicious, mom!" Ben said, "Me too, mom!"

After lunch, they went to see more animals. They saw giraffes, zebras, penguins and more. They had fun and learned a lot. They thanked mom for taking them to the zoo. Mom said, "You're welcome, my loves. I'm glad you enjoyed it." They hugged mom and went home. They were tired and happy.

Once there was a man and he was tired. His name was Mr. Joseph. One day he decided to gain a new job as a lawyer. He went to a building with a sign that said 'Lawyer', and he went inside.

Inside the building, Mr. Joseph met a nice lady. She asked him for his papers and he gave them to her. She smiled and said he was approved to be the new lawyer.

Mr. Joseph was so happy that he'd gained a job as a lawyer. He thanked the nice lady and left the building. He felt so excited to be a lawyer that he began to jump and dance.

On the way home, Mr. Joseph began to get very tired. He wanted to sleep, but he was so proud that he'd gained a job as a lawyer. So he kept walking.

When he finally reached his home, Mr. Joseph was so tired that he went straight to his bed. He fell asleep and dreamed of all the wonderful things he would do as a lawyer.

Tom is a dog who likes to play with his bone. He has a big bone that he found in the park. He thinks it is the best bone ever. He carries it everywhere and chews on it all day.

One day, Tom sees a new dog in the park. The new dog is big and fluffy and has a shiny collar. Tom thinks the new dog is very pretty. He wants to be friends with her. He runs to her and says, "Hi, I am Tom. Do you want to play with me and my bone?"

The new dog looks at Tom and his bone. She sniffs them and says, "No, thank you. Your bone is old and dirty. And you are small and ordinary. I only play with dogs who have new and shiny bones. And who are big and special. Go away, Tom. You are boring."

Tom feels sad and hurt. He does not understand why the new dog is so mean. He likes his bone and he thinks he is a good dog. He does not want to go away. He wants to play and have fun.

But the new dog ignores him. She turns her back on him and walks away. She does not care about Tom or his feelings. She only cares about herself and her looks.

Tom decides that the new dog is not a nice dog. He does not want to be friends with her anymore. He goes back to his bone and chews on it happily. He thinks his bone is the best bone ever. And he is a good dog. He hopes to find other dogs who are kind and friendly. And who like to play with him and his bone.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a beautiful cake for her birthday. Her mommy made it for her.

Lily's friend, Timmy, came over to play. He saw the cake and said, "Wow, that cake looks yummy. Can I have a piece?"

Lily said, "Sure, but let's stretch it so we both can have some."

They stretched the cake and cut it in half. They both had a piece and it was delicious.

But then, Lily's dog came in and knocked the cake off the table. The cake fell on the floor and broke into many pieces. Lily and Timmy were sad because they couldn't eat the rest of the cake.

Ben and Lily were going to fly in a big plane for the first time. They were very excited, but also a little nervous. They packed their bags and hugged their mom and dad goodbye.

"Have fun, kids! We'll see you soon!" Mom said.

"Be good, and listen to your aunt and uncle!" Dad said.

They got on the plane and found their seats. They buckled their belts and looked out the window. They saw the clouds and the sun and the birds. They heard the pilot say, "Hello, everyone. We are ready to take off. Please stay in your seats and enjoy the flight."

The plane started to move faster and faster. Ben and Lily felt their stomachs go up and down. They held hands and smiled. They liked the feeling of flying.

They watched a movie and ate some snacks. They played with their toys and drew some pictures. They talked to each other and to the nice lady next to them. They had a lot of fun.

After a while, they heard the pilot say, "We are almost there. We are going to land soon. Please put your things away and buckle your belts again."

The plane started to go down and down. Ben and Lily saw the ground and the houses and the cars. They felt the plane shake and bump. They held hands and closed their eyes. They were a little scared.

They heard the pilot say, "We have landed. Welcome to your destination. Thank you for flying with us. Have a nice day."

The plane stopped and the doors opened. Ben and Lily got up and grabbed their bags. They followed the people and got off the plane. They saw their aunt and uncle waiting for them. They ran to them and hugged them.

"Hi, Ben and Lily! We are so happy to see you!" Aunt said.

"Hi, Aunt and Uncle! We are happy to see you too!" Ben and Lily said.

They told them all about their flight and how they felt. They said they liked flying, but they were also glad to be on the land. They said they were ready to have more fun with their aunt and uncle.

They walked to the car and drove away. They looked out the window and saw new things. They were excited, but also a little nervous. They wondered what adventures they would have in this new land.

Once upon a time, there was a loyal bean who lived in the forest. One day, a fierce wind blew through the trees. The loyal bean was scared, so he started to call out to anyone who could help him. 

Suddenly, he heard a booming voice coming from the top of a tall tree. It was a brave bear who said, "I will protect you little bean!"

The bear stretched out her arms and caught the loyal bean in her giant paws. She snuggled him close, and the loyal bean felt safe. 

The brave bear nuzzled the loyal bean and said, "You can count on me to always keep you safe." The loyal bean smiled and thanked the brave bear for protecting him. 

The loyal bean and the brave bear became best friends, and the bear always kept the loyal bean safe from the fierce winds. 

The end.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Emily. She was three years old and loved to explore the world around her.

One day Emily was playing in her room and noticed a modern rug on the floor. She reached down to touch it and said, "What is this?"

Her mom replied, "It's a rug."

Emily asked, "What is a rug?"

Her mom said, "A rug is a special thing that makes your room cozy and warm."

Emily smiled and said, "I know! I can sit on it and be comfy!"

So Emily sat on the rug, feeling very cozy and happy. She didn't know it yet, but she now knew a lot more about rugs and the world around her.

Once upon a time, there was a deep lake. Every morning, a package was allowed to float across the lake. The package made all of the animals smile. One day, a little fish swam up to the package and asked if he could open it. The package agreed and allowed the little fish to open it. Inside was a very special surprise! It was a big, yellow duck. The little fish was so happy to find the duck! He made sure to look after it, swimming around the lake together all day. They had lots of fun until it was time to go home. The package allowed the little fish to keep the duck as a special friend.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tweety. Tweety loved to fly high in the sky and sing songs. One day, Tweety saw a big, scary cliff in front of her. She didn't know how to get past it.

Tweety tried to fly over the cliff, but she was too small and couldn't fit through the gap. She tried to fly around it, but it was too wide. Tweety was scared and didn't know what to do.

Suddenly, Tweety saw a rare butterfly flying nearby. The butterfly had beautiful colors and was very pretty. Tweety asked the butterfly for help. The butterfly said she could help Tweety, but only if Tweety helped her first.

The butterfly had lost her way and needed Tweety to guide her back home. Tweety agreed to help and the butterfly showed her a secret path that went around the cliff. Tweety was so happy and grateful to the butterfly. She sang a song to say thank you and flew away, feeling proud that she had solved her problem.

Once upon a time there was a huge cupboard. Inside it, tucked away in the corner, was a sleepy bear. He was very tired, so he opened his big mouth, and gave such a huge yawn that the cupboard rattled.

The bear was so tired that he hopped right into the cupboard and curled up in the corner. He closed his eyes and dozed off, snoring softly.

Suddenly, something strange happened. The cupboard started growing, getting bigger and bigger, until it was so huge that it filled the entire room. The sleepy bear was so surprised he almost fell out of his cupboard. 

But instead, he just curled up in the corner and gave a big, happy yawn. He knew he was safe and comfy inside his huge cupboard, so he snuggled in and fell fast asleep.

The End.

Once upon a time, in a small village, there was a winter. The snow was everywhere. It was so cold. People stayed in their warm homes. One day, a harmless little rabbit went outside to play.

The rabbit saw a big snowman. The snowman looked sad. The rabbit asked, "Why are you sad, snowman?" The snowman said, "I am cold, and I want to be bigger. If I am bigger, I will be warmer." The rabbit wanted to help the snowman.

The rabbit had an idea. "I will help you increase," the rabbit said. They started to roll the snowman in the snow. The snowman got bigger and bigger. The snowman was so happy. But then, the snowman got too big. The snowman was now too close to the sun.

The snowman started to melt. The rabbit said, "Oh no! We need to fix this!" The rabbit and the snowman rolled back to the village. The villagers helped the rabbit and the snowman. They all worked together to make the snowman smaller and happy again. The snowman was safe from the sun, and the rabbit was happy to have a new friend.

Once upon a time, in a big forest, there was a tiny mushroom. It was all alone. The sun was very harsh, and the mushroom did not like it. It wanted to find a friend to play with and to help it hide from the sun.

One day, a little bunny came hopping by. The mushroom called out, "Hello, bunny! Will you be my friend?" The bunny looked at the mushroom and smiled. "Sure, I will be your friend. Let's play together!" The bunny and the mushroom played all day, and they were very happy.

As they played, the bunny realized that the mushroom needed help to hide from the harsh sun. So, the bunny dug a hole in the ground and put the mushroom inside. Now, the mushroom was safe and cool. The mushroom and the bunny were the best of friends, and they played in the forest every day.

Once upon a time there was a pink bird. Everyday it would open its wings and make a big wave. The wave was so strong, it would travel far away. One day the bird saw a house with a door open. It flew to the door and peeked inside. There was a little girl, with pink hair and a big smile. The bird was so excited, it opened its wings and made a huge wave. The little girl started to laugh, and then she waved back. The pink bird was so happy. Every day the bird would come back, and the little girl would wave to it. They would have parties and dance and play, until they said goodbye. And they lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time there was a little boy named Joe. He had a nice coat that was very warm and cosy. One day Joe asked his dad to lend him his high boots. His dad said yes and Joe was so excited to wear them. 

So Joe put on his coat and the boots and went outside. He felt so tall in his high boots! Joe enjoyed jumping and running around in them. After a while, he decided to lend them to his friend. 

Joe's friend was also excited to wear the boots and he thanked Joe for lending them. Joe was happy that he could share his coat and boots with his friend. He enjoyed being outside with his friends and having lots of fun. 

The end.

Once upon a time, a girl named Lucy found a box. She opened the box and inside was something special - it was jewelry! The jewelry was purple and sparkled in the light. 

Lucy was so excited, she showed it to her mom. She asked what it was and her mom told her that it was jewelry. Her mom said she should examine it closely so she could see it better. So Lucy examined the jewelry, looking closely at all the details.

She saw tiny purple stones glistening and sparkling. She also noticed that the jewelry felt very soft and smooth against her skin.

Lucy was so happy with the jewelry. She had never seen anything so beautiful before. She thanked her mom, who said she had found it while they were out and about. Lucy smiled as she hugged her mom and said, "Thanks for my beautiful purple jewelry!"

Once upon a time there was a girl called Sarah. She loved to imagine things. One day she imagined that she was standing in front of a big plate of spaghetti. She imagined the spaghetti was long and yummy. It was the best spaghetti ever!

Sarah loved the taste of spaghetti. She wanted to eat it, so she grabbed a fork and started eating. It was so delicious that she ate it all. She was full and happy.

But then she started feeling competitive. She wanted to know if she could eat even more spaghetti! So she imagined a big bowl of spaghetti was in front of her. This time it was even bigger than before! It was a big challenge for Sarah.

Sarah had to be brave and eat it all. But she was brave and she ate the whole bowl of spaghetti! She was so proud of herself. She had managed to eat the biggest bowl of spaghetti!

Once upon a time there was a boy named Joe. Joe enjoyed playing in the park everyday. One day, Joe was playing in the park with his friends when he noticed a flower in a patch of grass that he had never seen before.

Joe went up to the flower and asked his friends, "What kind of flower is this?" His friends didn't know, so Joe decided to ask an old lady nearby. 

The old lady said, "This is a special flower. It provides lots of thread. But it's unknown where the thread will go." 

Joe was very curious and wanted to know more. The old lady smiled and said, "If you care for the flower, the thread will go to something special." 

Joe kept caring for the flower. Every day he watered the flower and picked off any dead leaves. He was excited to see what the flower would provide. 

One day, Joe was playing with some of his friends in the park and he noticed something bright and shiny in a tree. He thought it might be what the flower had provided, so he went up to the tree. He found a beautiful kite that he could play with. 

He was very excited and thanked the old lady for her help. The old lady smiled and said, "You are welcome, Joe. I'm glad you took care of the flower and it's special thread."

Once upon a time there was a cat named Zip. He loved to stir up trouble around the house.

One day, he was meowing around the kitchen, getting into all sorts of mischief. He jumped on the stove and accidentally switched it on. He quickly jumped down and scampered away.

But he left the stove on and soon the kitchen began to fill with smoke and smell kind of yucky.

The mom rushed in with a loud, "Zip! You naughty cat!"

Zip said nothing as he tried to hide behind the sofa. He knew he had done something wrong, but was too scared to face the harsh words coming from his mom.

His mom switched off the stove and opened the windows to clear out the smoky air. She looked at Zip with a stern face and said, "No more stirring up trouble, Zip! From now on, you need to be a good cat."

Zip nodded, vowing to be a good cat from now on. He knew his mom was right; stirring up trouble never ends well.

Once there was a bear. He was very, very hungry. He went to find some food. He saw an apple tree and went to get some apples. He waved his hands and the apples fell down from the tree. He was so happy!

The bear picked up the apples and started munching. With a full tummy, the bear felt much better. He decided to look for some paint so he could draw pictures. He found a box of paints in the forest and began to paint.

The bear loved to paint and happily finished three pictures. He made sure to keep them safe. He knew they looked really wonderful. He wanted to make sure they stayed healthy.

He was very happy with his pictures. He decided to show them to his best friend, the rabbit. 

The bear ran to the rabbit and said, â€œLook at these wonderful pictures I made.â€ 

The rabbit carefully looked at the pictures and said, â€œWow! Those are beautiful! To show you how much I like them, Iâ€™ll feed you some delicious carrots!â€ 

The bear happily accepted the carrots and said, â€œThank you for feeding me, Rabbit.â€ They both enjoyed eating the carrots and laughed the whole day.

Billy was three years old and he loved to learn new things. So his dad decided to explain how to use a tool. Billy was very curious and eagerly asked his father to show him the tool.

Dad explained that it was a fast tool, specifically designed to quickly cut things. It was shaped like a small box with a sharp blade at the front. He showed Billy how to carefully press down on the blade and move the tool around an object to cut it.

Billy was fascinated and immediately picked up the tool with both hands. Dad quickly took it away and smiled as he said, "Not so fast, Billy. You need to be very careful when using this tool to make sure you don't get hurt."

Billy nodded and looked carefully as his dad explained how to use the tool. Dad demonstrated how to cut paper and wood with the tool. Soon, Billy was using the tool like a pro! Dad was proud and praised him for his hard work. From then on, Billy was always excited to use the tool any chance he got.

Once there was a girl who was very sad. Everywhere she went she felt lonely. One day, she was feeling especially lonely when she heard an unfamiliar sound. It was a soft, gentle whistle coming from a nearby tree. She curiously looked up and saw a little bird perched on one of the branches. The girl was amazed and smiled.

The bird then hopped to the next branch and whistled again. The girl, feeling encouraged, began to whistle back. The bird flew down and landed on the girl's shoulder. Together they whistled a sweet harmony.
 
The girl's sadness evaporated as she continued to whistle with her new feathered friend. When it was time to go home, she kissed the bird goodbye and thanked him for lifting her mood. She wouldn't forget the day when a little bird taught her to whistle.

One day, a child named Alex was playing with their toy. They wanted to show it to their parents, so they ran to them, saying: "See Mom! See Dad! I have a toy!"

The parents smiled, and revealed a surprise â€“ there was another toy, just like the one Alex had!

"Mom and Dad! How?" Alex asked.

"This one is the original," the parents replied. "We made it for you!"

Alex was so delighted. They hugged their parents and thanked them for making such a wonderful present. The parents smiled and hugged back, happy to share the special moment.

Alex carried the original toy with them everywhere, taking special care to keep it safe and sound. They showed it to all their friends, who thought it was the coolest thing they had ever seen!
 
Alex treasured the original toy - it was a reminder of a special moment spent with their parents, and it revealed a love that could never be broken.

Mummy and daddy said it was time to leave the house. They put a big file into their bags. It was smooth and shiny.

They jumped into the car and drove away. Mummy said she had something very important in that file she was carrying. Then Daddy said he had to take it to a special place.

The car drove for a long time and then, they stopped. Mummy and Daddy got out of the car. They hugged and Mummy said she had to leave the file there. They said goodbye and Daddy put the file into a big box at the special place. 

Then, they drove back home. When they arrived, Mummy said the job was done and she was happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the snow. One day, Lily's mommy gave her a yummy snack to eat. It was a juicy red apple. Lily took a big bite and it was so tasty! But then, she accidentally dropped the apple on the ground and it made a big messy spot. 

Lily didn't want to leave the apple there, so she tried to pick it up. But her hands were so cold from playing in the snow that they started to freeze! She couldn't move her fingers. She felt sad because she wanted to eat the rest of the apple, but she couldn't because her hands were too cold. 

Just then, Lily's mommy came outside and saw what happened. She picked up the apple and told Lily not to worry about the messy spot. Lily's mommy hugged her and took her inside to warm up her hands. They sat by the fire and had hot cocoa together. Lily felt happy again, even though she didn't get to finish her snack.

Lily and Ben were going on vacation with Mom and Dad. They were very happy. They packed their bags and toys and got in the car. Mom said, "We are going to the beach. We will see the sand and the water and the sun. It will be fun."

Lily and Ben liked the beach. They played with their buckets and shovels and made a big castle. They found some shells and stones and put them on the castle. They ran in the water and splashed each other. They laughed and had a good time.

But then, a big wave came and washed away their castle. Lily and Ben were sad. They cried and said, "Our castle is gone. We worked so hard. It was so pretty."

Mom and Dad came and hugged them. Dad said, "I'm sorry, kids. Sometimes the water takes away our things. But we can make another castle. Or we can do something else. We still have time to enjoy our vacation."

Mom said, "That's right. And you know what? You can keep the shells and stones you found. They are your souvenirs. You can take them home and remember your castle and the beach."

Lily and Ben wiped their tears and smiled. They said, "Thank you, Mom and Dad. You are wise. We love you. And we love our vacation." They picked up their shells and stones and put them in their bags. Then they went to look for more fun things to do. They shut their bags and held their hands. They were happy again.

Jenny was an independent otter. She liked to swim and play by herself in the river. She did not need anyone to help her or tell her what to do. She was happy and free.

One day, she saw a big fish in the water. She was hungry and wanted to catch it. She chased the fish with her fast paws and sharp teeth. She was almost there when she heard a voice.

"Stop! That's my fish!" the voice said. It was Tom, another otter. He was bigger and stronger than Jenny. He also liked to swim and play in the river, but he was not independent. He always followed his mother and did what she said.

"Your fish? I saw it first!" Jenny said. She did not want to share or give up. She was brave and proud.

"No, it's mine! My mother served it to me for lunch. She caught it for me because I'm her good son. You are a bad otter. You have no mother. You have no manners. Go away!" Tom said. He was rude and mean. He did not care about Jenny or her feelings.

Jenny felt angry and sad. She did not have a mother, but she had a father. He taught her how to be independent and smart. He loved her very much. He was not there now, but he would come back soon. She did not need Tom or his fish. She said, "I don't want your fish. It's probably old and smelly. I can catch my own fish. I don't need your mother or your manners. I have my father and my freedom. You are a silly otter. You have no fun. Go away!"

She swam away from Tom and his fish. She found another fish, a bigger and fresher one. She caught it and ate it. She was full and happy. She saw her father coming. He smiled and hugged her. He said, "You are my independent otter. You are brave and smart. I'm proud of you. I love you."

Jenny smiled and hugged him back. She said, "I love you too, father. You are my best friend." They swam and played together in the river. They were happy and free.

Once there was a delicate flower in a deep pit. The flower had many petals and it was very small. Its petals were a beautiful white color, and they were so soft that they seemed to twinkle in the sunlight. Every day, the flower would look up to the sky and hope that it would one day be able to bloom and enjoy the sunshine.

One morning, the sun shone brighter than usual and the flower began to feel a warmth it had never felt before. Suddenly, a powerful force reached down from the sky and filled the little flower with energy. The petals began to stretch and open, and the flower bloomed for the very first time.

The flower was overjoyed. It stretched its petals to the sky, soaking up the warm and powerful sunshine. The deep pit was suddenly filled with light and beauty and the flower said, "thank you for this wonderful day and for helping me bloom."

Once there was a naughty little boy. He was always getting into trouble. One day he was out playing in the garden and he decided to crawl. He crawled under the fence and out into the road.

He had no idea it was dangerous because he was so small. Suddenly the sun was starting to set and his mom was calling him home. He was so naughty that he would not listen to her! He just kept crawling until he was too tired.

Finally, he looked up and saw the most beautiful sunset. It was the most gorgeous thing he had ever seen. He sat and watched the colours of the sunset until his mom finally found him and took him home. From then on he was a much better boy, and he never crawled away again.

One day, Jay and his mom went to the park. Jay wanted to make some noise, so he ran around and laughed. His mom saw some kids playing near a cone and had an idea. She said to Jay, â€œLetâ€™s bake a cake in the cone!â€

Jay nodded and they went to the store to buy the ingredients their cake would need.

Back at the park, they created a fire in the cone. Jayâ€™s mom put the cake mix inside, and then Jay took a stick to stir it. As he stirred, the fire started to get bigger and bigger.

Soon, the cake was done. Jay took a bite and was so surprised. It was the most delicious cake heâ€™d ever tasted! The cone had made it even better. 

The park was so noisy with all the laughing, singing, and clapping at the end. Jay knew this was one baking adventure he wouldnâ€™t forget.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Jane was playing in her garden. She wanted to find a rod so she could pretend to be a pirate-captain.

So she stepped across the garden, looking around and trying to find a rod. As she was looking, she saw a jealous frog. He was hopping from rock to rock, Keeping an eye on her.

She stopped and looked at him and said, â€œHi, frog. Do you know where I can find a rod?â€

The frog replied, â€œYes, I do! Itâ€™s over there by the tree.â€ He pointed with his long green arm.

Jane thanked the frog and stepped over to the tree. She found a rod and smiled. Now she was ready to play at being a pirate-captain!

Jim was a chubby boy and he lived with his mom and dad. Every night, he would sit at his desk and see something fun. Last night, he saw a butterfly. It had beautiful wings, and it was so colourful! He was so happy to see it. 

The next day, Jim went to school. He was scared at first, but then he saw his friends. He smiled and waved at them. Then, he saw his teacher. She was holding a book and smiling. He knew he was going to have fun today.

After school was over, Jim ran to his desk and saw a present. He was so excited to open it! It was a toy car â€“ his very own car. He jumped and shouted with joy.

Jim loved having fun at his desk. He felt happy and safe there. He was a chubby boy with a big smile on his face.

Molly and her dad were walking down the street together. Molly was very enthusiastic and she was full of energy.

Molly noticed something up ahead. "Dad, look!" she said, pointing.

There, in the grass, were two baby rabbits. Molly was so excited. She ran over to them, and her dad followed her.

Molly asked her dad if they could give them something to eat. He told her they could. He picked an oat from the ground, and Molly carefully placed it in front of the rabbits.

The baby rabbits sniffed it and then started to eat the oat. They were hungry and they ate it quickly.

Molly talked to the rabbits, in a soft voice. She was so enthusiastic! She thanked the rabbits for eating the oat and told them it was time to go.

Molly and her dad continued on their walk, with a big smile on their faces.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved going on adventures in her backyard. One day, she saw a big, orange pumpkin. It was so tight in the ground that she couldn't pull it out.

Lily's friend, Timmy, came over to play. She showed him the pumpkin and said, "Look, Timmy! I discovered this pumpkin! But it's too tight to get out. Can you help me?"

Timmy tried to pull the pumpkin out, but it wouldn't budge. Suddenly, they heard a voice. It was Lily's mom. She said, "Kids, I have an idea. Let's use a shovel to dig around the pumpkin and loosen the dirt. Then we can pull it out together!"

Lily and Timmy were so happy. They dug and dug until the pumpkin finally came loose. They were so proud of themselves for discovering the pumpkin and working together to get it out. They couldn't wait to show it to Lily's mom and make pumpkin pie!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to draw pictures and show them to her friends. One day, Lily drew a beautiful image of a flower and showed it to her friend, Sarah.

Sarah looked at the picture and said, "Wow, that's so pretty! Can I have it?"

Lily hesitated but then said, "Okay, you can have it."

The next day, Lily saw Sarah using her image to show off to other friends. Lily felt upset that Sarah didn't appreciate the picture and just used it to impress others. 

Lily learned that it's important to value things and not just use them for show. She also learned that it's okay to say no when someone asks for something that is important to her.

Once upon a time, there was a man named Dave. One day while walking in the forest, Dave passed a big tree. He stopped to take a closer look and noticed something strange. 

"What is that?" said Dave as he saw a bright light coming from the tree.

He touched the tree and was immediately sent through a portal! Now Dave was in a strange new universe that he had never seen before. 

The universe was so big and vast. Dave noticed the sun and the stars were a bit different too and he had to learn the new rules of this place.

After a few days, Dave found himself a bit lonely and homesick. That's when he started to feel a little bit bitter. But then, he passed by a small house and stopped. He heard some friendly voices coming from the house and was happy to meet new friends. 

Dave made some new friends, and they all had a lot of fun together. Dave felt that the universe was not so lonely after all and was happy he was able to find new friends. 

The End.

Once there was a farmer. He was very careful. He looked after his animals and his crops.

One day he wanted to cook a nice meal. So he went out to the farm and he picked some fresh crops. He took them home to the kitchen.

He washed the vegetables carefully and chopped them up. He put the food in a pot and added some spices. Then he lit a fire and put the pot on the stove.

He stirred the food until it was cooked. He served the meal to everybody on the farm. Everyone said it was the best meal they ever had!

One day, a little boy named Tim found some clay. It was soft and brown. He wanted to make something with it. He thought hard about what to make. Tim was confused.

Tim asked his mom for help. "Mom, what can I make with this clay?" His mom smiled and said, "You can make anything you want, Tim." She gave him an idea. "Why don't you make a cat?" Tim liked the idea and started to make a cat with the clay.

When he finished, he showed his cat to his mom. She was happy with his work. "Good job, Tim!" she said. Tim felt proud of his clay cat. He put it on a shelf in his room. Every time he looked at it, he remembered how he asked his mom for help and she answered his question.

Once there was a cat who lived in a house with a little girl. The girl was three years old and her name was Lucie. Every morning when Lucie woke up she went to go see the cat. The cat was very soft and she was always happy to see Lucie. 

Lucie would pet the cat and they would play together. They especially enjoyed playing with a ball of yarn. They would roll it around and chase it. After they played, the cat would curl up in the sun and take a nap.

At night, after Lucie had gone to sleep, the cat would come up and sit next to Lucie's bed. Sometimes the cat would purr and sometimes she would meow. No matter what, she always made sure Lucie felt safe and happy.

Lucie would sleep very fine with the cat nearby. For many years the cat and Lucie were the very best of friends. They would play and laugh together, and always look out for one another.

Teddy wanted to play the piano. He was only three years old, but he already loved music. He wanted to sound great just like the grown-ups.

So Teddy went to get the piano and he tried to carry it across the room. But it was too big and too heavy. He struggled to push and pull it, but he couldn't do it.

He asked his mom for help and with her help, Teddy finally managed to get the piano to the other side of the room. Teddy was so happy.

He sat down on the bench and started to play the keys. There were lots of wrong notes, but he didn't give up. He kept trying and eventually he figured out how to play a great melody.

At the end, Teddy and his mom hugged and danced around the room, celebrating Teddy's achievement. He had a big smile on his face and he was so proud of himself. He had done it!

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside in the wild forest near his home. One day, Timmy found a diary in the forest. He was so happy to have found it, and he took it home to show his mom. 

His mom taught him how to write in the diary, and Timmy loved it. He wrote about all his adventures in the wild forest. But one day, Timmy lost the diary while playing outside. He looked everywhere but couldn't find it. 

Days went by, and Timmy started to feel sad. He missed his diary and all the memories he had written down. But one day, he found the diary again! He was so happy and ran home to show his mom. 

But when he got home, he found out that his little brother had drawn all over the pages of the diary. Timmy was so upset that he cried and cried. His mom tried to make him feel better, but it was too late. Timmy's diary was ruined, and he never wrote in it again.

Once upon a time there was a cute little rabbit called Josie. Josie lived in a perfect little burrow in the countryside. 

One day, Josie decided to go for an adventure. She hopped and skipped until she found a big field. Josie thought it was so exciting, so she ran around until she was sweaty and tired. 

Josie suddenly saw a whip in the field! It was just lying there all alone. She went over to take a closer look and saw that it was very special: it was perfect! Josie wanted to take the whip home, so she picked it up and covered it with her hands, then hopped off with the whip back to her burrow. 

When Josie got home, she hugged the whip tight and kept it safe under her bed. She knew she'd never let it go, it was now her perfect whip forever!

Once upon a time, there was a cute little bug named Billy. Billy loved to glow at night. He would fly around and make pretty lights for his friends. All the other bugs loved to see Billy glow.

One night, Billy and his friends were playing in the garden. Billy said, "Why did the bug go to the doctor?" His friends did not know. Billy laughed and said, "Because it had a glow-ache!" All his friends laughed at the joke.

As they played, a big, scary bird came. The bird wanted to eat the bugs. But Billy had an idea. He started to glow very brightly. The bird was scared of the light and flew away. Billy and his friends were safe.

"Thank you, Billy," said his friends. "Your glow saved us."

From that day on, Billy learned that his glow was not just for fun, but it could also help his friends. The moral of the story is that sometimes our talents can be used to help others.

Once upon a time, there were two little girls who liked to race. Their names were Fashion and Graceful. They loved to run fast around the house, laughing and playing tag.

One day, Fashion saw something in the garden. She ran to it and told Graceful. It was a big balloon that was bright and shiny. Fashion and Graceful wanted to race to see who could reach the balloon first.

They got ready to go and then, as fast as two little girls could, they raced to win. In one second, Graceful was ahead, in the next second, it was Fashion. They were both running so fast they could barely keep up.

Finally, with one last burst of speed, Fashion got there first and snatched the balloon. Graceful was so proud of her friend and they jumped up and down, laughing and cheering. They couldn't wait to play with their shiny new balloon.

Once upon a time, there was a big rock. The rock was not pretty or special. It was just a cheap rock. A man found the rock and thought he could deliver it to his friend.

The man put the rock in a bag and started to walk. He walked and walked, but the rock was very heavy. He was tired from carrying the heavy rock. He wanted to give the rock to his friend, but it was too hard.

At last, the man could not walk anymore. He sat down by the road and cried. The rock was too heavy, and he could not deliver it to his friend. The man was very sad because he could not help his friend. The rock stayed by the road, and the man went home. The story has a bad ending.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Mark. Mark had a big, brown patch on his back. He lived in a small, red house with his best friend, a girl named Sue.

One day, Mark and Sue went for a walk in the park. They saw a big, loud bird. The bird was very loud and it scared Mark. Sue hugged Mark and told him, "Don't worry, I am here with you."

Mark and Sue played in the park all day. They ran and jumped and had lots of fun. When it was time to go home, they walked back to their small, red house together. Mark and Sue were very happy to have each other as best friends.

At first, it was sunny outside. Then, the sky became serious and it started to rain. 

Mama and Lily were very sad. They were hoping to go outside and play. But it was too wet and rainy to do that now.

Mama had an idea. She said, "Let's make a special treat inside! We can be serious and do our best."

So that's what they did. They worked together to make a delicious cake. Lily started mixing the ingredients, while Mama put it in the oven. 

When it was done baking, the cake smelled and looked so good! They had fun eating it and even shared some with their neighbors. 

Even though it was raining outside, Lily and Mama had a happy time together inside.

Once upon a time, there was a small boy named Andy. He was only three years old, but he had a big curiosity. One day, he saw a safe with a big, red handle just outside his house. It looked very clear and he wanted to open it. 

Andy tried to open the safe but it was locked. He looked for a key, but there was none. He began to cry and tear. He was very sad he couldnâ€™t open the safe.

Suddenly, Andy heard a voice. He looked up and saw his grandma. She had a big smile on her face and said, â€œDonâ€™t worry, Andy. I have the key to the safe. But it is only for special occasions.â€ She winked at him and then put the key in the handle. 

The safe suddenly opened. The biggest surprise was revealed! Andy started cheering and jumping with joy as he saw his birthday presents inside the safe. He hugged his grandma and thanked her. She just smiled and said, â€œI told you itâ€™s only for special occasions.â€

Andy now knew the secret of the safe and shared the key with his sister and brother. Now all of them could open it whenever they want for special occasions. He was very clear about this and carefully kept the key safe.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Milly. Milly had a shiny, red car and she wanted to keep it that way. Every day Milly would polish her car to make sure it stayed bright and pretty.

One day, Milly was polishing her car when a stranger came up to her. The stranger had a bag full of food. He said it was spicy food and asked if Milly wanted some. 

Milly said yes and the two of them sat in the sunshine and ate the yummy, spicy food.

When they were finished, Milly thanked the kind stranger and then went back to polishing her car. The stranger waved goodbye and walked away.

When she was finished, Milly's car was very shiny. She smiled and went inside her house feeling very happy.

Once upon a time there lived a very stubborn little boy. Every day, he was told to take his pill and they had to keep reminding him because he was very forgetful. But today, he had had enough and he refused to take it. He crossed his arms and shook his head, saying, "No way!"

His mother was very frustrated, but she knew he was just being stubborn. She knelt down and said, "Please, I need you to take your pill. It will make you feel better." 

But the little boy just crossed his arms again, determined not to take it. His mother sighed, and she decided to try something else. She said, "If you take your pill, I will carry you around the garden!"

The little boy hesitated for a moment, but finally he nodded and said, "OK." He was too curious to see how it felt like to be carried around the garden. So, he took the pill, and his mother carried him around on her back.

And ever since that day, the little boy always remembered to take his pill.

Once upon a time, there was a big mill. It was in a small town with lots of trees and flowers. The mill was where people made flour from wheat. Many people worked there, and they were happy.

One sunny day, a little cat came to the big mill. The cat was tired and wanted to find a place to nap. It looked around and found a soft, warm spot near a big window. The cat curled up and closed its eyes.

While the cat took its nap, the people in the big mill kept working. They did not make much noise, so the cat slept very well. When the cat woke up, it felt happy and rested. It stretched, yawned, and went outside to play. The people in the big mill smiled and waved goodbye to the little cat.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was very restless and couldn't sit still for long. One day, her mom told her to go play in the kitchen while she cooked dinner. Lily went to the kitchen and saw lots of pots and pans on the stove. She started playing with them and pretending to cook too. 

Suddenly, her mom called out from the living room, "Lily, come here!" Lily ran to her mom and asked, "What is it?" Her mom smiled and said, "I have a surprise for you!" She then told Lily that they were going to have ice cream for dessert. Lily was so happy and couldn't wait to eat it. 

After dinner, Lily's mom tucked her into bed and kissed her goodnight. Lily was so tired from playing and eating lots of ice cream that she fell asleep right away. As she drifted off to sleep, she thought about how much fun she had in the kitchen and how her mom always tells her the best surprises.

Sara and Ben like to play with cars. They have many cars of different colors and sizes. They make roads and bridges with blocks and books. They pretend to drive their cars to different places.

One day, Sara and Ben want to play with the same car. It is a big red car that makes noise and has lights. Sara says, "I want to play with the red car. It is mine. You play with the blue car." Ben says, "No, I want to play with the red car. It is fun. You play with the yellow car." They both pull the red car and start to cry.

Mom hears them and comes to see what is wrong. She says, "Why are you crying? You have so many cars to play with. Why do you fight over one car?" Sara says, "Because it is the best car. I saw it first. Ben is bossy. He always wants what I have." Ben says, "No, Sara is bossy. She never shares. I like the red car too. It is fair to take turns."

Mom says, "You are both being bossy. You need to learn to share and play nicely. How about this? You can each play with the red car for five minutes. Then you have to switch. And you have to say please and thank you. OK?" Sara and Ben nod. They agree to try Mom's idea.

Mom sets a timer and gives the red car to Sara. She says, "Sara, you can play with the red car for five minutes. Then you have to give it to Ben. Please be careful and have fun." Sara says, "Thank you, Mom. I will play with the red car and drive to the park." She makes the car go vroom vroom and honk honk. She smiles and enjoys the car.

Ben waits patiently and plays with the blue car. He says, "I will play with the blue car and drive to the store. I will buy some gas for the red car." He makes the car go beep beep and zoom zoom. He pretends to fill the car with gas and pay with coins.

The timer rings and Mom says, "Sara, your time is up. You have to give the red car to Ben. Please say thank you and switch." Sara says, "Thank you, red car. You are fun. Here, Ben. You can play with the red car now. Please be gentle and have fun." She gives the red car to Ben and takes the yellow car.

Ben says, "Thank you, Sara. You are nice. I will play with the red car and drive to the zoo. I will see some animals and feed them." He makes the car go roar roar and squeak squeak. He pretends to see lions and monkeys and give them bananas.

Sara and Ben play with the cars for five more minutes. Then they switch again. They say please and thank you and share the red car. They have fun and stop crying. Mom is happy and proud. She says, "You are doing great. You are learning to share and play nicely. You are almost finished. Then we can have a snack and read a book." Sara and Ben say, "OK, Mom. We love you. We love cars. We love snacks and books." They hug Mom and each other and finish playing with the cars.

Once upon a time, there was a goat. The goat was very friendly and liked to play with the children. One day, a little girl came to see the goat. "Can I play with your goat?" she asked the farmer. "Yes, you can," he replied. "Just be careful and don't let him eat too much grass."

The little girl played with the goat for a while. She petted him and let him nibble on her dress. "You're such a friendly goat," she said. "I wish I had a goat like you." The goat bleated happily in response.

After a while, the little girl had to go home. "Goodbye, friendly goat," she said. "I'll come back and play with you again soon." The goat watched her go, then went back to his grazing. He was happy to have made a new friend.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Lily. Lily was three years old, and she loved to explore!

One day, Lily went to story and found all sorts of things. She saw hot bowls, and soft blankets, and a shiny journal.

Lily wanted to take the journal home with her, so she asked her mom. "Mommy, can I store this journal?"

Her mom said, "No, Lily. That one isn't for taking. But you can look at it and write stories in it when we are at the store. Would you like that?"

Lily nodded her head with a big grin. She was so excited to have the journal to write in that she could hardly wait to get it back home!

Sara likes to read books. She has many books in her room. She reads them every day. She reads about animals, and cars, and stars.

One day, Sara finds a new book in her room. It is a big book with a shiny cover. She opens it and sees many pictures. She sees a picture of a chain. A chain is a long thing with many round parts. She reads the words under the picture. The words say: "A chain can be used to pull, to lock, or to make noise."

Sara wants to try the chain. She looks around her room. She sees her toy box. She sees a lock on her toy box. She thinks: "Maybe I can use the chain to open the lock." She takes the chain and puts it around the lock. She pulls the chain hard. The lock does not open. She pulls harder. The lock still does not open. She pulls harder and harder. The chain breaks. The lock falls to the floor. Sara is sad. She says: "Oh no, I broke the chain. Now I can't read the book anymore."

Sara hears a noise. She turns around. She sees her mom. Her mom is smiling. She says: "Sara, what are you doing? I brought you a new book. It is a book about chains. I thought you would like it." Sara is surprised. She says: "Mom, this is the book I was reading. I found it in my room. I tried to use the chain to open the lock, but I broke the chain. I'm sorry, mom." Her mom hugs her. She says: "It's okay, Sara. The chain was old and weak. It was not a good chain. I have a new chain for you. It is a strong chain. You can use it to play, but not to open locks. And you can still read the book. The book is not broken. It is a good book. I love you, Sara." Sara smiles. She says: "I love you too, mom. Thank you for the book and the chain. Can we read the book together?" Her mom says: "Of course, Sara. Let's read the book together. It is a warm day. We can read the book in the garden. Come on, Sara. Let's go." Sara takes the book and the chain. She follows her mom. She is happy. She likes to read books. She likes to learn new things. She likes to be with her mom.

Once there was a fat cat. The cat loved to play. It liked to play with a net. So, one day it grabbed the net with it's paw and kicked it. The net sailed through the air and landed on the ground. 

The cat ran after the net and kicked it playing a game of its own. It swatted it with it's paws and kicked it with it's hind legs.

The cat played and played until it was tired. So, it curled up and fell to sleep with the net in its furry paws. 

The fat cat dreamed of playing with its net that night.

Polly had been playing in the garden all day and it was very late. She was so tired she could barely keep her eyes open. Suddenly she heard a noise and jumped with surprise â€“ it was her granddad! She smiled at him and ran to him with open arms. Granddad was tall and generous, and always brought something for Polly when he visited. 

This time he had a jug of milk in his hands. Polly looked at it hungrily â€“ she had seen milk before but never tasted it. Granddad opened the jug and poured Polly a cup. She held it in both hands and tasted the milk. It was sweet, and delicious. She smiled with delight and thanked granddad.

Afterwards they said goodnight, and granddad gave Polly a big hug. With a wave he disappeared back into the night. Polly was tired, but she felt so happy, and drifted off to sleep with a big smile on her face.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play with her toys. One day, she looked at her toys and saw they were all over the floor. She wanted to play with them, but it was hard to find the one she wanted. So, she decided to organize them. 

Lily picked up each toy and put them in their own special spot. She put the dolls on the bed and the cars in the box. When she was done, she felt happy because she could find her toys easily. 

Later that day, Lily went outside to play with her friends. It was a gloomy day and the sky was gray. Lily didn't mind because she was having fun. Suddenly, her friend fell and hurt her finger. Lily helped her friend and made her feel better. Her friend smiled and said, "Thank you, Lily. You are a good friend."

Once upon a time, there was a clear jar. It was very special, because it was filled with amazing things. A little boy wanted to examine the jar to find out what was inside.

The boy used his fingers to carefully open the lid of the jar. He reached inside and pulled out the things one by one. He found pretty stones, colorful feathers, and interesting leaves.

The boy looked closely at the items he had found. He touched them and smiled. Then, he put the items back into the jar and closed the lid.

The boy liked examining the jar and exploring the things inside. It gave him lots of excitement and fun!

Once there was a family who were very excited. They were going to a new restaurant for dinner. When they arrived, they saw something strange - the restaurant was going in reverse! Everything was going backwards! The family couldn't believe their eyes.

They went inside, and the food was in reverse too! The plates were going upside down and the customers were eating from the bottom! The family laughed at the silly sight. 

They finished dinner and went back outside. Everything was the same - the restaurant was still going in reverse. The family was amazed. They had never seen anything like it before. 

As they drove away, they couldn't stop talking about their unusual dinner in the new reverse restaurant.

Lila and Tom are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big pile of wood. They want to make something with the wood.

They ask their moms if they can use the wood. Their moms say yes, but be careful. Lila and Tom are happy. They start to move the wood. They find some nails and a hammer. They think of what they can make.

They decide to make a house. They use the nails and the hammer to join the wood. They make a floor, a wall, a door, and a roof. They work hard and have fun. They are clever.

When they finish, they show their moms their house. Their moms are proud. They say it is a very good house. They say Lila and Tom are very clever. They say they are also very kind, because they share the wood.

Lila and Tom smile. They are happy. They invite their moms to come inside their house. They say they made the house to unite their families. They say they love their moms. They hug their moms. They are very clever and very kind.

Once upon a time, there was a shark who was very different. He was the only one of his kind, and he felt special because of it. The shark loved exploring the ocean and discovering all the different things it had to offer. 

One day, the shark got a special gift. It was a shiny stone with the word 'value' written on it. The shark didn't understand what it meant, so he asked an old turtle what it meant. 

The turtle told the shark that 'value' meant that he was special, and was worth a lot. He was valuable. The shark was so happy to know that he was valuable, that he swam around the ocean showing everyone this special rock with the word 'value'.

The shark was filled with joy and he spread the love to everyone he met, reminding them that even though we can all be different, we all have something special inside us that has value!

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Mark. Mark was very curious and loved to study. Every day he looked for new things to learn about.

One day, Mark went to the market to study some of the different fruits that were for sale. He was amazed to see the bright colors and shapes of the various fruits. He loved to study them closely!

Afterwards, Mark went to the grocery store. Here, he studied some of the smaller fruits, like lemons and oranges. He liked how clean they looked and thought they must be very juicy. 

Mark enjoyed learning about the fruit and felt happy to have studied them that day.

Lily wanted a pen. She kept asking her mom for one but her mom said she had to wait until she was old enough. So, Lily patiently waited for the day when she could own a pen. 

Finally, her mom said she was old enough and took her to the store to pick out her first pen. Inside the store, Lily saw so many pens. There were big ones, small ones, colorful ones, regular ones, etc. 

But, Lily decided to pick a regular pen. It was gray and just the right size to fit in her hand. She held her new pen in her hands and could not believe that it was her own.

Once upon a time, there was a pretty little girl named Lily. Lily loved to learn new things. One day, her mom took her on a trip to the big city. Lily was very excited to see the tall buildings and the busy streets.

John was walking in the park one day, when he found a blueberry bush. He was so excited, he began to speed towards it. As he arrived, he saw the blueberries were so big and juicy. As they walked, Tommy's mum looked down and said "Thank you for helping me. I am very happy that you are here with me." Tommy was relieved, and smiled very wide. The sun came out from behind the clouds and they enjoyed the bright green trees and flowers in the garden.

Anna was a very intelligent girl. She liked to read books and learn new things. She also liked to help her mom and dad with chores. One day, her mom asked her to put on her jacket and go to the store with her. Anna was happy to go, but she had a problem. Her jacket was too big for her. It was her brother's jacket, and he was much older and taller than her.

"Mom, I can't wear this jacket. It's too big for me. It covers my hands and feet. I can't see or walk well," Anna said.

"I'm sorry, Anna. Your jacket is in the laundry. It got dirty yesterday when you played in the mud. You have to wear this one for now. It's cold outside. You can manage, right?" her mom said.

Anna nodded, but she was not sure. She tried to roll up the sleeves and the hem of the jacket, but it was still too big. She felt like a turtle in a shell. She followed her mom to the store, but she was not happy.

At the store, Anna saw many things that she liked. She saw toys, books, candies, and fruits. She wanted to touch them and look at them, but she couldn't. Her jacket was in the way. She couldn't reach for anything or hold anything. She felt frustrated and sad.

"Mom, can I have this book, please?" Anna asked, pointing to a book with colorful pictures.

"Sure, Anna. You can have the book. You are such an intelligent girl. You love to read. Here, let me get it for you," her mom said.

She reached for the book, but as she did, she bumped into a display of cans. The cans fell down and made a loud noise. Everyone in the store looked at them. Anna and her mom felt embarrassed.

"Oh, I'm so sorry. I didn't mean to do that. It's this jacket. It's too big for me. I can't see or move well," Anna said.

The store clerk came over and helped them pick up the cans. He was very nice and friendly. He smiled at Anna and her mom.

"Don't worry. It's okay. Accidents happen. Here, let me help you with the jacket. It's too big for you. You need a smaller one. I have one in the back. It's my daughter's jacket. She left it here yesterday. She is about your size. You can borrow it if you want," he said.

He went to the back and came back with a jacket. It was pink and had flowers on it. It was very pretty and cozy. He helped Anna take off the big jacket and put on the small one. It fit her perfectly. She felt warm and comfortable. She could see and move well.

"Wow, thank you so much. This jacket is very nice. It fits me well. I like it a lot," Anna said.

"You're welcome. You can keep it. My daughter has many jackets. She won't miss this one. You look very cute and intelligent in it. Enjoy your book," he said.

Anna and her mom thanked him again and paid for the book. They left the store, feeling happy and grateful. Anna hugged her book and her jacket. She felt proud of herself. She managed to overcome her problem and make a new friend. She learned that sometimes, big things can be good, but small things can be better.

Once there was a modest mouse who lived in a chimney. Every night, the mouse would look out into the night sky and thought of all the places he would like to go. One night, he decided it was time to go exploring.

He set off into the night and after a while, he came to a big, old house. There was a crack in the chimney and the mouse crawled inside to stay warm.

Suddenly the mouse heard a voice. It came from inside the house and belonged to a little girl. "Please don't go!" She shouted. 

The mouse was surprised and he said, "Why should I stay?". The little girl said, "Because I am lonely. You can be my friend". 

The mouse knew he could also be brave and explore, so he decided to stay. The mouse found a cozy spot in the chimney and the two friends enjoyed many nights of stories and fun.

Sara looks at Max. She sees that he is sorry. She remembers that she loves Max too. She wipes her tears and smiles.

She hugs Max and gives him a treat. Max wags his tail and barks. He is happy. Sara and Max go to play with the other dogs and people at the park. Mom watches them and smiles. She is proud of Sara and Max. She sends a picture of them to Dad. Dad is at work, but he sees the picture and smiles too. He loves Sara and Max. He can't wait to see them.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim was a restless boy who loved to play all day. One sunny day, Tim found a small teaspoon in his kitchen. He decided to take it outside to play with it.

Lena did not want to stop playing. She said, "No, mom, I want to stay in the tub. I want to play with my toys."

Her mom came to the bathroom and smiled. She said, "Lena, you have played enough. You can play with your toys again tomorrow. But now you need to get out and put on your pajamas. I have a surprise for you."

Lena was curious. She said, "What is the surprise, mom?"

Her mom said, "You will see. Come on, get out of the tub and I will show you."

Lena got out of the tub and wrapped herself in a towel. Her mom dried her hair and helped her put on her pajamas. Then she took her to her room.

There, on her bed, was a new notebook. It had a pink cover and many blank pages. Lena loved to draw and write. She was very happy to see the notebook.

"Wow, mom, thank you! This is a great surprise. Can I use it now?" she asked.

Her mom said, "Yes, you can. But only for a little while. Then you need to brush your teeth and go to sleep. You have school tomorrow."

Lena nodded. She took the notebook and a crayon. She opened the notebook and started to draw. She drew her toys in the tub. She drew the duck, the boat, the frog and the fish. She wrote their names under each picture. She was very organized.

She showed her mom her drawing. Her mom said, "That's very nice, Lena. You are very good at drawing and writing. I'm proud of you."

Lena smiled and hugged her mom. She said, "Thank you, mom. I love you. And I love my new notebook."

Her mom said, "I love you too, Lena. And I'm glad you love your notebook. Now, let's brush your teeth and go to sleep. Good night, sweetie."

Lena brushed her teeth and got into bed. Her mom tucked her in and kissed her forehead. She put the notebook on the nightstand. She said, "Good night, Lena. Have sweet dreams."

Lena said, "Good night, mom. I will dream of my toys in the tub. And of my new notebook."

She closed her eyes and fell asleep. She was very happy.

Once upon a time there was a boy named Jack. He loved things that went fast. One of his favorite things was his motorcycle. He would ride it around the block every day.

One day, Jack was in the kitchen. He smelled something tasty. It was his mom cooking dinner. She asked him, "Jack, what would you like for dinner?"
Jack replied, "I would like something tasty!"

His mom smiled and said, "Let's have some tasty spaghetti!" Jack smiled back and said, "Yes, that sounds great!"

They both ate the delicious dinner. Afterwards Jack went outside with his motorcycle and rode around the block. He was in awe of how fast it went and he said, "Wow! This is the best motorcycle ever!" 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to eat mac and cheese for dinner. But one day, his mom put the mac and cheese in the dishwasher instead of washing it by hand. Timmy didn't like that. 

"Mommy, I disagree!" Timmy said. "The dishwasher doesn't make my mac and cheese clean." 

His mom explained that the dishwasher was clean and would make the dish clean too. But Timmy still didn't like it. 

So, his mom washed the dish by hand just for him. Timmy was happy and ate his mac and cheese with a clean dish. The end.

Once there was a girl called Mary who had a cube. Mary liked to take her cube everywhere. But one day, when Mary was playing with her cube, it suddenly disappeared! Mary began to worry.

She searched high and low, but she couldn't find her cube. Then, all of a sudden, she heard a noise coming from behind the sofa. She rushed to see what it was, and there it was! Her cube was rolling across the floor, very fast.

Mary was so happy! She quickly picked up her cube and held it close. She didn't want it to run away again - so she made sure to put it away in a safe spot. And from then on, she never had to worry about it disappearing again!

Tommy loved going shopping with his aunt. She always made it so much fun! He looked up at her and smiled.

Billy was a young player who loved to play games. One day his dad gave him a new toy called an original player. Billy was so excited to play with it! He put the player on the floor and pushed the big, red button. Sure enough, it made lots of wonderful music. Billy danced along to the music.

Once upon a time, in a small village, there was a lazy cat named Tom. He did not like to work. He just wanted to sleep all day. One day, Tom heard about a big diamond in the forest. He thought, "If I find the diamond, I will be rich and never need to work again."

Tom went to the forest to look for the diamond. He looked under rocks and behind trees. He did not find the diamond. He was very tired, but he did not give up. He knew he needed to work hard to find the diamond.

After many days, Tom found the diamond. He was very happy. He took the diamond back to the village. Tom learned that hard work is important. He was not lazy anymore. The village people were proud of Tom. The moral of the story is that we need to work hard and not be lazy to get what we want.

Tom and Lily wanted to decorate the big tree in the garden. They had many shiny things to hang on the branches. They also had a star for the top.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She was feeling very gloomy. She was missing her mom and dad who were away on a trip.

One day the little girl decided to go for a walk. She walked until she came to a big drain. She looked down into the drain with sadness in her eyes - she was still missing her parents so much. 

Suddenly, the little girl noticed a tiny little fish in the drain. She smiled and felt a little bit happy again. She watched the fish swimming around and felt a bit better. 

The fish said "Follow me, I'll show you something special". The little girl followed the fish into the drain. It was dark and scary, but the fish was brave and the little girl was brave too. 

Soon they came to a big pipe leading out of the drain. Through it, the little girl could hear her mom and dad talking - they were home! She followed the pipe back and ran straight into their arms. She never felt so happy or so warm. She never missed them so much ever again.

Lily and Tom were playing in the park. They saw a giant slide. Lily wanted to go on it, but Tom was scared.

"Come on, Tom, it will be fun!" Lily said.

"No, it is too high and fast. I don't want to go." Tom said.

Lily tried to pull Tom by the hand, but he did not move. He resist her. He was stubborn.

"Please, Tom, don't be ignorant. It is not scary, it is exciting. Look, other kids are going and they are happy." Lily said.

She pointed to the slide, where some children were laughing and sliding down.

Tom looked at the slide, and then at Lily. He saw that she was eager and brave. He did not want to make her sad or angry. He decided to try the slide.

"Okay, Lily, I will go with you. But you have to hold my hand." Tom said.

Lily smiled and hugged Tom. She was proud of him. They held hands and climbed up the stairs. They reached the top of the slide. They looked down and saw the ground far away.

"Are you ready, Tom?" Lily asked.

They let go of the stairs and slid down the slide. They felt the wind in their hair and the thrill in their stomachs. They screamed and laughed. They reached the bottom and got up.

They hugged each other and ran to the slide again. They were happy and brave. They did not resist the slide anymore. They enjoyed it.

Once upon a time, there was a little toy robot called Bob. He was a very nice robot and everyone who met him thought he was really cool.

When Bob got back home, he quickly entered his house and put the battery in the charger. Then he went off to bed, dreaming of the delicious treats he had discovered.

John and his family were very excited because it was the start of summer. Every morning, they would get up early and go outside to create beautiful things. Once there was a bird. The bird was fit and strong. He was always happy to be outside flying in the sky. But one day he found himself in a cage and couldn't fly away. All day long he tried to find a way out but it was too hard.

Then one day a kind man saw the bird and was sad that it was in the cage. He wanted to help. The man opened the cage and went to get something. He came back with a piece of string and tied it to the cage door. He then said to the bird, "You are free now".

The bird was so happy. He arose up into the air and flew off to find a new home. He flew high and he flew far. He was so glad to be released and free. He never forgot how the kind man had helped him and was always thankful to be fit and able to fly.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved ice cream and would always ask his mom for a cone when they went to the park. One day, Timmy's mom promised him a cone if he was quiet during their walk.

Timmy tried his best to be quiet, but he couldn't help but get excited when he saw the ice cream truck. He started jumping up and down and shouting, which made his mom very unhappy.

When they got to the ice cream truck, Timmy's mom told him that he couldn't have a cone because he didn't keep his promise to be quiet. Timmy felt sad and learned that it's important to keep your promises and be quiet when you need to.

Lily liked to play with her mother's telephone. It was fancy and shiny and had many buttons. Sometimes, Lily would pretend to call her friends and tell them stories. She would say hello and bye-bye and make funny noises.

One day, Lily found the telephone on the sofa. She picked it up and pressed a button. She heard a voice say, "Hello, this is the bank. How can I help you?" Lily was surprised. She thought it was a friend. She said, "Hello, I am Lily. I like to play with dolls and cars. Do you like to play?"

The voice said, "I'm sorry, this is not a play call. This is a serious call. Please hang up and don't call again." Lily did not understand. She said, "Why not? You are not nice. I want to tell you more stories. Do you want to hear about my cat?"

The voice said, "No, I don't. Please hang up now or I will call your parents. This is a waste of time and money." Lily felt sad and angry. She said, "You are mean. I don't like you. You are not my friend. Bye-bye." She threw the telephone on the floor and ran away.

Her mother heard the noise and came to see what happened. She saw the telephone on the floor and picked it up. She heard the voice say, "Hello, hello, are you still there? Who is this? Is this a prank call?" Her mother said, "I'm sorry, this is a mistake. My daughter was playing with the telephone. She didn't know what she was doing. I apologize for the trouble." She hung up and looked for Lily.

She found Lily in her room, crying on her bed. She hugged her and said, "What's wrong, sweetie? Why are you crying?" Lily said, "I wanted to talk to a friend on the telephone, but he was not a friend. He was mean and rude and he didn't want to hear my stories. He said he would call you and tell on me. I'm sorry, mommy. I didn't mean to be bad." Her mother said, "It's okay, honey. You are not bad. You are a good girl. But you have to be careful with the telephone. It is not a toy. It is for important calls. You can't call strangers and bother them. They might get angry or scared. Do you understand?" Lily said, "Yes, mommy. I understand. I'm sorry. Can I still play with the telephone?" Her mother said, "No, you can't. The telephone is not for playing. But you can play with your dolls and cars and tell them stories. They will listen and be nice. And you can call your real friends later, with my permission. How does that sound?" Lily said, "That sounds good, mommy. Thank you. I love you." Her mother said, "I love you too, Lily. Now, let's go and have some cookies and milk. And don't worry about the bank. I will explain to them what happened. They will understand. It was just a mistake." Lily said, "Okay, mommy. Let's go." She smiled and hugged her mother. They went to the kitchen and had some cookies and milk. Lily felt better and forgot about the mean voice on the telephone. She was happy to have her mother and her toys and her stories. She was a good girl.

Once upon a time, a little birdie lived in a big tree. The birdie was very wise and knew all the secrets of the forest. One day, the birdie wanted to take a bath and decided to use some shampoo. As the birdie was washing its feathers, it blinked and suddenly a big, mean cat appeared out of nowhere.

The cat tried to catch the birdie, but the birdie was too wise and flew away. However, the birdie accidentally dropped the shampoo and it spilled all over the cat. The cat got very angry and started chasing the birdie. The birdie flew as fast as it could, but the cat was getting closer and closer.

Finally, the birdie got tired and the cat caught it. The birdie was very scared and wished it had never blinked while washing its feathers. The cat ate the birdie and felt very satisfied. From that day on, the cat always looked for birds to eat and never forgot the smell of that shampoo.

Once upon a time there was a mom and a dad who loved each other very much. One day, they started to quarrel, which made them very sad. The dad left the house and went for a long walk.

In the meantime, the mom went to the telephone and called her friend. She told her about the quarrel and asked for advice. The friend gave her good advice about how to make the quarrel perfect.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to play at the park. One sunny day, he saw a big slide. The slide was new and available for all kids to play on. Tim was very excited to start playing on the slide.
