They told their mom about their adventure and asked if they could play again after lunch. Their mom said, "Yes, you can. I am proud of you both!"

Lily and Tom are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big cake on a table. The cake has pink and white frosting and many sprinkles. It looks yummy.

"Wow, look at that cake!" Lily says. "I want to taste it. Do you think it is for us?"

Tom shakes his head. "No, Lily. That cake is not for us. That cake is for someone else. Maybe it is for a birthday. We should not touch it. It is not ours. It is not mine. It is not yours."

But Lily does not listen. She runs to the table and takes a big bite of the cake. She smiles and says, "Mmm, this cake is so good. It is sweet and soft. It is easy to eat. You should try it, Tom."

Tom is scared. He sees a lady coming to the table. She looks angry. She says, "Hey, what are you doing? That is my cake! You are very naughty. You should not eat my cake. That is not nice. That is not fair. That is not easy. You should say sorry."

Lily feels bad. She says, "I'm sorry, lady. I did not know it was your cake. I was hungry and it looked yummy. Please do not be mad at me."

The lady sighs. She says, "It's okay, Lily. I forgive you. But you should not do that again. You should ask before you take something that is not yours. You should share and be polite. Do you understand?"

Lily nods. She says, "Yes, lady. I understand. Thank you for forgiving me. Can I share your cake with Tom? He is my friend. He did not eat your cake. He was good."

The lady smiles. She says, "Sure, Lily. You can share my cake with Tom. But only a little bit. This cake is for my daughter. It is her birthday. She is three years old, like you. Do you want to say happy birthday to her?"

Lily and Tom say, "Yes, lady. We want to say happy birthday to her. What is her name?"

The lady says, "Her name is Rose. She is over there, on the swing. Come on, let's go and say hello. And bring some cake. Maybe she will share with you too."

Lily and Tom follow the lady. They say happy birthday to Rose. They share some cake. They make a new friend. They have fun. They learn a lesson. They are happy. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to draw with her pencil. One day, she wanted to draw a picture for her mom's birthday. 

Lily went to her mom and said, "Mommy, can you help me prepare a special picture for you?" 

Her mom smiled and said, "Of course, Lily! I'm sure whatever you draw will be wonderful. You can always depend on your artistic skills." 

Lily was happy to hear that and got to work. With her mom's help, she drew a beautiful picture of a flower garden. Her mom loved it so much that she hung it up on the wall. 

From that day on, Lily knew that her pencil was a dependable tool for making special gifts. She continued to draw pictures for her loved ones, and they were always amazed by her talent.

Once upon a time, there was a little puppy named Chippy. Chippy was so excited because today was her birthday! All of Chippy's friends were coming over to help her celebrate. She was so excited!

Chippy's mommy got a big pan and made some tasty treats. There was cake, ice cream and even some doggy treats! Now it was time to invite everyone over.

Chippy's mom kept the treats on the kitchen counter. It was a safe place, so the treats wouldn't get spilled. Chippy was so excited and ran around, barking and wagging her tail! 

Once her friends arrived, they all started to enjoy the treats. Everyone was so happy and grateful to be there. Chippy was the happiest little puppy and thanked everyone for coming. 

"I'm so glad you all could come," said Chippy. "It's been a very special day!"

Once upon a time, there was a little boy. His favorite thing to do was to play in the park all day. But one day, a storm came and made it too cold and wet to play.

The little boy was scared when he heard the loud thunder. But soon he noticed the white clouds were moving and the thunder was getting quieter. All the birds were still singing and the sun was shining again.

The little boy felt happy again. He sat in the park and just relaxed while the storm passed. The sun was so warm and the air was so clean.

The little boy knew he had to go home soon, but he didn't want to miss a minute of the beautiful weather. He looked up at the sky and smiled. Relaxing in the park after a storm was the best thing ever.

Once upon a time, there was a furry bear. He had fluffy fur and a long, hairy tail. He was always curious about the world and he wanted to wander.

One day, the bear had an idea. He was going to explore the big, cold freezer. It was a very tall place, filled with strange things! But the bear didn't know what it was.

He was so excited to explore the freezer. He crept inside. Inside it was dark and very cold, but the bear wasn't scared. He felt so brave as he wandered around. He found lots of interesting shapes and colours.

The bear wanted to stay in the freezer forever. He loved discovering all the new things but he knew it was time to leave. He soon stepped out of the freezer and was met with the warm sunshine. He knew he would be back soon to explore the freezer again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the sunshine, but one day she fell into a muddy puddle and got very dirty. Her mom told her it was time to bathe, so Lily took a warm bath with lots of bubbles.

After her bath, Lily's mom read her a story about a silly skeleton who loved to dance. Lily thought the skeleton was funny, but also a little bit scary.

Later that day, Lily helped her mom make some cookies. She tasted the batter and made a sour face because it was bitter. But when the cookies were done baking, they tasted sweet and delicious. Lily was very happy and ate a whole cookie all by herself.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to race her toy car around the house. One day, she accidentally knocked over her juice and it spilled all over the table. 

Her mom quickly grabbed a napkin to clean up the mess. Lily felt angry because she wanted to keep playing with her car. 

"Mommy, I don't want to stop racing," Lily said. 

"I know, sweetie, but we have to clean up first," her mom replied. 

Lily helped her mom clean up the juice with the napkin. After they finished, Lily felt much better and continued to race her car around the house.

Once there was a tired dog. He was tired because he had been pushing a big ball all day. The ball was so big that the dog needed his friend's help. His friend was a rabbit. 

The rabbit had a blue glove. He put the glove on so he could help the dog by pushing the ball with him. Together they pushed the big ball. 

Afterwards, they both felt like they had been pushing the ball forever. The dog was so tired that he just lay down on the grass and shut his eyes. The rabbit took off his glove and put it into his pocket. He looked at the dog and smiled. 

The dog and the rabbit were tired but happy after a long day of pushing the big ball together.

Tim and Liz are brother and sister. They like to play in their room. They have many toys and books. But they do not like the dark. When it is night, they are scared.

One night, Tim hears a noise. He thinks it is a monster. He jumps out of his bed and runs to Liz's bed. He says, "Liz, Liz, there is a monster! Help me!"

Liz wakes up and hugs Tim. She says, "Do not be scared, Tim. There is no monster. It is just the wind. I will protect you. You can sleep with me."

Tim feels better. He says, "Thank you, Liz. You are a good sister. You are brave and kind."

Liz says, "You are welcome, Tim. You are a good brother. You are smart and funny."

They snuggle in Liz's bed. They feel safe and warm. They close their eyes and sleep. It is easy to sleep when they have each other.

Once upon a time there lived a queen. She was known for her kindness and generosity. Every day, she would take creations from the people of her kingdom and make them even better.

One day, the queen heard a knock on the door. She opened the door to find a mysterious box. Inside the box was something unknown. Before the queen had the chance to find out what it was, the box began to shake. Suddenly, it tore open and out flew a beautiful bird.

The queen was delighted and she quickly named the bird Fred. Everyone in the kingdom loved Fred and all the people cheered. As time went on, the unknown bird became a part of the royal family.

It was then that the queen knew that the unknown bird was no ordinary creature. It was a magical bird that the queen had heard stories about from her ancestors. She realized that the bird was sent to her from the heavens above! From then on, the queen and the bird were best friends.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who had a special chest. Inside the chest was a special surprise for her, but she was too young to open it.

The girl's parents always told her not to touch the chest and to ignore it. But one day the girl was feeling very curious, so she couldn't ignore the chest any more. 

The little girl opened the chest and saw something beautiful inside! But when she tried to pick it up, her parents got mad and were very rude to her. 

The little girl was sad and for a long time she ignored the chest. She was scared that her parents would be angry again. 

But one day her parents told her that it was okay to open the chest, and they gave her a hug. From then on the little girl was not scared to look in the chest and she loved the special surprise inside!

Once upon a time, there was a nice house. In the garden was a special fence, the fence glowed at night. One night, a young girl asked her mom, "What makes the fence glow, Mommy?" Her mom said, "It's magic, my love. It always glows at night to make sure things stay safe." The little girl smiled, imagining wonderful things behind the fence. She thought to herself, "I'm so lucky to have this nice fence in my garden". She smiled and went to bed, dreaming of magical things behind the glowing fence.

Krista was so happy when her parents invited her over for a play date with her friend, Abi. It was a pretty Saturday morning and the sun was shining. She quickly put on her pretty dress and ran out to meet Abi. The two of them had so much fun! They laughed and danced together. Both of them were very excited for lunch.

When Abi arrived at Krista's house, her mom had cooked a delicious lunch. Abi sighed with delight as she took a bite. Krista wanted to show Abi something and led her to the backyard. There were two empty boxes filled with dirt. Krista showed Abi the little garden she had made. She had planted some pretty pink roses and watered them every day.

The two of them started playing with the dirt and making mud pies. They had so much fun that they didn't even notice that it was getting dark. By sunset, they had muddy clothes and faces. Krista's mom saw them and smiled. She said, â€œOkay, now itâ€™s time to go inside. Please put all the waste in the bin.â€

Krista and Abi quickly washed their hands and went into the kitchen. Krista's mom had prepared a special treat for them -- a big bowl of ice cream with sprinkles and marshmallows. They both shouted for joy and started eating. It was the best day ever!

Lila liked to play in the garden with her mom. She liked to smell the flowers and watch the bees. One day, she saw a rose that was very unusual. It was not red or pink or yellow like the other roses. It was blue!

"Mom, look at this rose!" Lila said, pointing to the blue flower. "It is so pretty and different!"

Mom came over and smiled. "You are right, Lila. This is a very unusual rose. It is very rare and special. Do you know how it got here?"

Lila shook her head. She did not know.

Mom picked up the rose gently and gave it to Lila. "This rose came from your grandma. She passed it to me before she went to heaven. She loved blue roses very much. She wanted me to have one and to pass it to you when you were old enough. She wanted you to know that she loves you and is always with you."

Lila hugged the rose and felt happy. She smelled its sweet scent and felt its soft petals. She thanked her mom and said, "I love you, mom. And I love grandma. And I love this rose. It is a very special gift."

Once upon a time, there was a wise bear. He had a spear given to him by a great king. The bear was so wise that he used the spear in special ways. He could use the spear to help him find food!

One day, the bear was looking for something special to eat. He found a special fruit. The bear liked it so much he wanted to have it all for himself. But, the fruit was starting to rot and the bear knew he had to share. 

So, he called upon his animal friends. He said, "Come help me! I have found a special fruit, but it is starting to rot. I wish to share it with all of you."

His friends were so very thankful! They ate the fruit and shared stories until it was gone. The bear felt so wise for sharing the fruit, and it made him happy to see his friends happy too.

Once there was a little girl named Lexi. She was very bossy and liked to dance. Every day she would go outside and find a box. She would twirl around and around like a spinning top.

One day, Lexi put on her dancing shoes and took her box outside. She started to jig, hopping and spinning in circles. As she danced around, she saw a big, black cloud in the sky. She was worried, but she still kept dancing.

Suddenly, the rain started to pour. The pitter-patter of the rain made Lexi feel wiggly, so she kept on dancing. She didn't even mind when her shoes got wet. When she was done dancing, she looked around and noticed that the rain had stopped.

When Lexi went back inside, she felt tired but happy. She looked at the box, now filled with water from the rain. She realized that she had danced her way out of the storm. From then on, Lexi was extra bossy when it came to her dancing.

Once there was a boy who was hungry. He asked his mom for something to eat. His mom said, "I will take soup for you!" So she took a soup pot and filled it with warm water.

Next, she took some vegetables and cut them into tiny pieces and put them into the pot. Then she took some spices and stirred them in.

After that, she put the pot on the stove and turned it on. The pot began to sizzle, simmer and boil. The kitchen got busy.

After a while, the soup was ready. The boy was very happy!

His mom poured the soup into a bowl and handed it to the boy. He drank it all up and said, "Yum! Thank you mom!"

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. He liked to play near the old creek. It was fun to throw rocks and watch the water splash.

One day, Tim saw a big, sharp stick near the creek. He wanted to play with it. But his mom said, "No, Tim! That stick is too sharp. It can hurt you."

Tim was sad, but he knew his mom was right. He left the sharp stick and went back to throwing rocks in the creek. And he had lots of fun playing safely by the water.

Once upon a time, there were two friends who loved to play together. One day, they went to the park to run on the track. But then, they started to quarrel because they both wanted to run faster. Their faces looked troubled and sad. 

Suddenly, they saw a bird flying in the sky. They both stopped quarreling and looked up. The bird was so beautiful and they were amazed. They forgot about their argument and started to talk about the bird. They had fun watching it fly around. 

After a while, they realized that they were both feeling happy again. They hugged each other and decided to run together on the track. They ran as fast as they could and laughed together. From then on, they never quarreled again and always found joy in simple things like watching birds.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She had a big white hat and white shoes. She was so happy.

One day she went for a walk in the park and something strange happened. In the lake she saw a monster! It was a big white monster with lots of eyes and teeth.

The little girl was so scared and she wanted to run away, but then she decided to be brave. She stomped her feet and clapped her hands. The monster got scared and it ran away!

The little girl was so happy. She clapped her hands and said, "Yay!" She was so brave.

The End.

Once upon a time, there was a sister and a brother who played together in the garden. The brother found a flower and said to the sister, â€œLook at the flower. It is so pretty!â€

But the sister said, â€œI donâ€™t like it.â€

The brother asked, â€œWhy?â€

The sister replied, â€œIt is my opinion.â€

The brother thought for a moment, then said, â€œThat is okay. Everyone can have their own opinion. We need to be honest and separate our opinions from each other.â€

The sister nodded and they both smiled. They went back to playing together in the garden.

Once upon a time, two friends, Tom and Ben, were planning an outing to the opera that evening. Tom was very excited to go and was hopeful to see all the wonderful things the opera had to offer.

Ben wasn't as optimistic as Tom. He said to Tom, "We don't have enough money for the opera. How can we see the show?"

Tom replied, "Don't worry, I have an idea. I hope we can get into the opera. I have a friend who works there. She is a generous person, I'm sure she will help us."

So, Tom and Ben walked over to the opera. When they arrived, they knocked on the door. To their surprise, the door opened and it was Tom' friend. She smiled and said, "Oh, you two wanted to go to the opera. Come in, I think I can help you."

Tom and Ben were very happy to have been welcomed into the opera. Little did they know, it was about to be one of the most incredible nights of their lives!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to run and play outside. One day, she was running in the park and she saw her friend, Timmy. 

"Hi Timmy!" Lily said. 

"Hi Lily!" Timmy said. 

Lily noticed that Timmy was shivering. "Are you cold?" she asked. 

"Yes," Timmy said. "I forgot my blanket at home." 

Lily had an idea. "I have a comfortable blanket at my house. Let's go get it!" 

So, Lily and Timmy ran to her house and got the blanket. Timmy was so happy and warm under the comfortable blanket. "Thank you, Lily!" he said. 

"You're welcome, Timmy!" Lily said. They both smiled and continued to play outside under the warm sun.

Sara and Ben were friends who liked to paint. They had many colors and brushes to make pictures. One day, they decided to paint a big rainbow on a white paper. They mixed red, orange, yellow, green, blue and purple to make the rainbow. They were very happy with their painting.

But then, Sara saw some scissors on the table. She had an idea. She wanted to cut out the rainbow and make it into a necklace. She thought it would look pretty on her. She did not ask Ben if he wanted to share the rainbow. She just took the scissors and started to cut.

Ben saw what Sara was doing and felt sad. He liked the rainbow too. He wanted to keep it as a painting. He said to Sara, "Sara, why are you cutting the rainbow? I helped you paint it. Can we keep it together?"

Sara did not listen to Ben. She said, "No, Ben, I want the rainbow for myself. It is mine. I can do what I want with it." She finished cutting the rainbow and put it around her neck. She smiled and said, "Look, Ben, I have a rainbow necklace. Isn't it beautiful?"

Ben did not think it was beautiful. He thought it was mean. He said to Sara, "Sara, you are not a good friend. You are not generous. You are selfish. You did not share the rainbow with me. You ruined our painting. I don't want to play with you anymore." He took his colors and brushes and left.

Sara felt sorry for what she did. She looked at the rainbow necklace and realized it was not as pretty as the painting. She wished she had shared the rainbow with Ben. She missed her friend. She wanted to say sorry to him. She took off the necklace and ran after Ben. She hoped he would forgive her.

Once upon a time, there was a big, rich rat who lived in a fancy house. He had lots of cheese and gold coins. One day, a small mouse came to his door and asked if he could lend some cheese. The wealthy rat said no and slammed the door.

The mouse was sad and hungry. He went to ask his friend, a kind rabbit, for help. The rabbit shared his carrots and let the mouse stay with him. The mouse was grateful and happy.

After a few days, the wealthy rat came to the rabbit's house and asked for help. He had lost all his cheese and gold coins and had nowhere to go. The rabbit remembered how the rat had treated his friend and said no. The rat realized he had been selfish and promised to be kind from now on. And they all lived happily ever after.

Geoffrey was measuring his bedroom when something went crazy. He stopped and looked up. An olive was spinning around, faster and faster. He could hear it laughing. 

He looked around his bedroom, but nothing else seemed unusual. He thought it was very strange that an olive would be spinning around like that.

He asked the olive, "What are you doing?"

The olive said, "I'm measuring too! I'm measuring how long I can spin around."

Geoffrey thought for a moment, then he said, "That's crazy! But why are you measuring in my room?"

The olive smiled and said, "Because I like it here. I like to measure in your room."

Mama was tired. She had been washing dishes by hand all day and her hands were getting sore. She wanted to find a better way to do it. Then one day, she saw a big blue box in the store. It was a dishwasher! She bought it and brought it home.

Mama was so excited. She put a bunch of dishes in it, filled it with soapy water, then pushed a button. The dishwasher started to hum and make bubbles. Mama smiled.

When the dishwasher was done, the dishes were very clean and dry. Mama had to put them away. She was so happy. No more washing dishes by hand! From now on, Mama would use the dishwasher to keep her dishes clean and dry.

The sun shone brightly in the sky, making the grass very dry.

Tommy and his dad were outside playing football. Tommy enjoyed playing football with his dad very much.

Suddenly, Tommy started to sneeze. He sneezed so hard that he dropped the football.

His dad said, "Bless you, Tommy. Take a break and have a drink of water."

Tommy sat down and drank his water. After a few sips, he felt much better.

He said to his dad, "Can we play some more football now? It's a lot of fun!"

His dad smiled and said, "Yes, let's go!"

They started playing football again and had a great time. Tommy never wanted the day to end.

Sara and Tom are friends. They like to draw with pastels. Pastels are soft and colorful. They make pretty pictures on paper.

One day, Sara and Tom are drawing in the park. Sara draws a flower. Tom draws a car. They show each other their pictures.

"Wow, your flower is very nice!" Tom says.

"Thank you, your car is very cool!" Sara says.

They smile and keep drawing.

Then, Tom has an idea. He wants to joke with Sara. He takes a thin pastel. It is black. He draws a big spider on Sara's flower. He thinks it is funny.

Sara looks at her flower. She sees the spider. She screams.

"Tom, what did you do?" Sara says. "You ruined my flower!"

Tom laughs. He says, "It is a joke, Sara. It is not a real spider. It is just a pastel."

Sara is not happy. She does not like the joke. She does not like spiders. She is scared and angry.

She takes a thick pastel. It is red. She draws a big X on Tom's car. She says, "This is a joke, too. It is not a real X. It is just a pastel."

Tom looks at his car. He sees the X. He stops laughing. He is sad. He likes his car. He does not like the X.

He says, "Sara, why did you do that? You ruined my car!"

Sara says, "You started it, Tom. You ruined my flower first."

They look at each other. They are both sorry. They do not want to fight. They want to be friends.

They say, "I am sorry" at the same time. They hug and make up.

They take new papers. They draw new pictures. They do not joke with pastels anymore. They joke with words. They have fun. They are happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys all day long. One day, he found a shiny toy car that he really liked. He said, "This car is mine now!" and he played with it all the time. 

Timmy liked to pretend that he was driving the car and going on adventures. He would make vroom vroom noises and imagine that he was driving on a normal road. One day, he pretended that he was driving to the moon! 

Timmy had so much fun pretending with his toy car that he didn't even notice when it was time for dinner. His mom had to come and remind him that it was time to eat. Timmy put his toy car away and went to have a normal dinner with his family.

Paul was feeling very happy. Today he was meeting his old friends from his childhood. Paul was excited to see them again as it had been a long time. When he arrived, he was reminded of all the fun they used to have together. 

Paul said, "Do you remember when we used to play together in this park? It was so much fun!" All of his friends nodded and started laughing. 

His friends suggested they should keep in touch, so they decided to create a network. This way, they could always stay in touch, no matter where they were in the world. They wanted to make sure that their network was reliable so they exchanged emails, telephone numbers and addresses. 

Paul was delighted. "This is a great idea! Now, we always have a way to stay connected". His friends agreed and all of them hugged before saying goodbye. Paul couldn't believe how lucky he was. He was reminded of how wonderful it was to have such reliable friends.

Sara and Ben are playing outside. They see many clouds in the sky. Some are big and white, some are small and gray. Sara likes the big white clouds. She wants to take one home.

"Look, Ben, that cloud is so fluffy and soft. I want to take it home and hug it. Can we take it home, please?" Sara asks.

Ben shakes his head. "No, Sara, we can't take the cloud home. It is too high and too big. How will we take it down? How will we carry it? Where will we put it?" Ben says.

Sara thinks for a moment. She has an idea. She runs to the shed and gets a ladder and a big bag. She puts the ladder under the cloud and climbs up. She tries to catch the cloud in the bag, but the cloud is not solid. It is made of tiny drops of water. The cloud slips through the bag and makes Sara wet and messy.

"Oops, Sara, what are you doing? You can't take the cloud home. It is not a toy. It is part of the sky. It will make you wet and messy. Come down, please." Ben says.

Sara is sad and disappointed. She wanted to take the cloud home, but she can't. She climbs down the ladder and puts the bag and the ladder back in the shed. She is wet and messy. She needs to change her clothes.

"Sorry, Ben, I just wanted to take the cloud home. It looked so fluffy and soft. I thought it would be fun to hug it. But you are right, it is not a toy. It is part of the sky. Maybe we can make our own clouds with cotton and glue. Do you want to try?" Sara says.

Ben smiles and nods. He likes Sara's idea. He thinks it will be fun to make their own clouds. He goes to the house and gets some cotton and glue. He and Sara make their own clouds with cotton and glue. They stick them on the wall and pretend they are in the sky. They are happy and creative. They forget about the wet and messy cloud.

John was in the park with Mommy. He liked going to the park with Mommy and playing with the other children.

John saw another boy and he went over to him. "Hi, what's your name?" asked John.

The boy said, "My name is Ryan. Do you want to play?"

John nodded and pointed to his blue blouse. "Do you like my blouse?"

Ryan smiled and said, "Yes, it's very nice. I like the blue color!"

John and Ryan played together. They ran around the park and had lots of fun.

It was time to go home and Mommy said, "John, it's time to go."

John said goodbye to Ryan and they both hugged. John pointed to Ryan's blue blouse and said, "I like your blouse too!" 

Mommy and John went home. John was very happy and excited to have a new friend.

Once upon a time, there lived a brilliant girl named Ella. She was only three years old, and she was full of energy and creativity. She loved to explore her bedroom and find ways to have fun. 

One day, Ella was walking around her bedroom and she stumbled onto a small box. It was filled with exciting colours and shapes. She opened the box and found a lot of interesting things inside. 

Her mum saw her and noticed the box. She asked Ella: 
"What do you think will happen if you keep taking out other people's belongings without asking them first?" 

Ella thought for a bit and then replied: 
"I think it's not very nice to take things without asking, so I should always ask first." 

Her mum smiled and nodded. From that day onwards, Ella remembered to always be polite and ask before taking things that weren't hers. She respected other people and their belongings, and she kept her bedroom tidy and neat. And everyone lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who wanted to polish something special. So, one day she asked her mom for an egg. Mom gave her a shiny, white egg. 

The little girl was excited and ran to her room to polish the egg. She found a hairy brush and started polishing the egg. She worked hard, and soon the egg was shiny and smooth.

The little girl was very proud of her work and showed her mom her shiny egg. Mom was very proud of her and gave her a hug. Then, they went out to show her friends the special, shiny egg. 

They all loved the egg and said it looked so beautiful. The little girl was very happy and hugged her mom. 

From then on, the little girl always made sure to polish special things.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She liked to go on adventures in the forest near her house. One day, she woke up early and decided to go on a walk. She put on her coat and went outside. 

As she walked, she saw a thin mist in the air. It looked like a cloud that was really close to the ground. Lily thought it was magical. She decided to follow the mist and see where it went. 

The mist led her to a clearing in the forest. In the middle of the clearing was a tree with a swing hanging from one of its branches. Lily was so happy she had followed the mist. She spent the whole morning swinging and having fun. She decided it was the best adventure she had ever been on.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tim. Tim loved to build things with his hammer. He would hammer and hammer until he made something new. 

One day, Tim's friend came over and requested to use Tim's hammer. Tim said yes and gave his friend the hammer. But his friend got angry and broke the hammer. Tim was sad because he loved his hammer so much.

Tim's parents tried to fix the hammer, but it was broken beyond repair. Tim was so upset that he didn't want to build anything anymore. He lost his passion for creating things and never wanted to share his toys again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside, but it was very cold. Her mommy told her to put on her coat so she wouldn't get sick.

Lily tried to put on her coat, but it didn't fit. She was so sad! Her mommy said, "It's okay, we can get you a new coat that fits better."

The next day, they went to the store and found a new coat that fit perfectly. Lily was so happy! She ran outside to play, but she was a little clumsy and fell down. Her mommy came running over and said, "Are you okay?" Lily said, "Yes, I'm okay. I just need to be more careful." 

From then on, Lily was more careful when she played outside and she loved her new coat that fit just right.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play by the sea. He liked to build sandcastles and collect seashells. One day, Timmy's mom bought him a new pair of shoes. They were shiny and red. Timmy was very happy and wanted to wear them to the beach.

When Timmy got to the beach, he ran towards the sea. He was so excited to show his new shoes to his friends. But as he got closer to the water, he slipped on a wet rock and fell down. His new shoes got all wet and sandy. Timmy was sad, but his friends helped him up and they all played together on the beach.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lizzie. She was always very anxious, but she liked to pretend she wasn't. One day, her mom and dad took her to a special place. It was a cave full of gold! Lizzie was very excited to see it, but her anxiousness made it hard to trust the new, strange place. 

Then, her parents showed her something else that made her feel better - they gave her a special necklace with a large golden charm. She had never seen anything so beautiful and shiny before! Her parents told her it was a symbol of their love and she should never forget it. She wrapped it around her neck and instantly felt safe and protected. 

From then on, Lizzie trusted that her parents would keep her safe, no matter what. Whenever she felt anxious about something, she would reach for her necklace and it helped her to remain brave and confident. 

That's how Lizzie learned the power of trusting and the strength of golden symbols.

Once upon a time, there was a little rabbit named Benny. Benny loved to play in the forest and eat carrots. One day, he found a pine cone. It was so pretty and shiny! Benny thought it was very important.

Suddenly, a big, scary wolf appeared! The wolf wanted to take the pine cone from Benny. Benny didn't want to give it up. He ran and ran until he found a hole to bury the pine cone in. The wolf couldn't find it!

Benny felt very proud and happy that he saved his important pine cone. He went back to his burrow and ate a carrot. The end.

Once upon a time there was a girl called Lucy. She was very excited because it was her birthday. It was a sunny day, so she rushed outside to play in the garden.

In the garden, she saw a word. It was a dry word and it was very charming. She liked the way it looked and wanted to take it home. So Lucy put the word carefully in her pocket and brought it inside.

She decided to use the dry word to make a birthday card for herself. She cut a beautiful shape out of a piece of paper and then glued the word on it. It looked perfect!

She put the card on the kitchen table and waited for her parents to come home so they could see it. When they arrived they were so charmed by her card that they gave her a big hug and told her they were very proud of her.

Lucy hugged her parents back and was so happy to have a beautiful, dry word to make her birthday card.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Mia. One day Mia went to the park with her mommy and daddy. Mia saw a little stand with lots of yummy treats. Mia's mommy asked if she wanted one, so Mia pointed to a cookie.

The cookie was really pretty. It looked like it was made with lots of love. Mia was excited when she saw it.

The lady behind the stand said that the cookie was fragile. She said that Mia needed to be extra careful when it was time to eat it. Mia and her mommy agreed and mommy paid for the cookie.

Mia was so excited to eat the cookie but then she saw a dog and gave the cookie to him. The dog ate the cookie in one big bite! Mia's mommy was surprised and said that it was so nice that Mia thought of the dog. 

Mia's mommy said that she would recommend the cookie to her friends. Mia and her mommy went home happy, with the memory of the yummy cookie.

Once upon a time, there was a delicate boat floating in the ocean. It was getting tired so it decided to take a rest. The boat gently floated to a beautiful harbor. The harbor was full of many boats like the delicate one. The delicate boat was happy to be in the harbor. All the boats rested in the harbor together. There was a nice breeze blowing. Everyone was happy and safe in the harbor. The delicate boat went to sleep in the harbor and felt cozy and content. 

The boats stayed in the harbor for a long time to get some rest. After a while, the boats started to wake up and were ready to sail again. The delicate boat was happy to be in the harbor and thanked them all for the peace it had found. 

The delicate boat was so happy that it had found a place to rest in the harbor. It said goodbye to the other boats and started sailing again. The delicate boat went on many adventures, but it would always remember the peaceful moments it had spent in the harbor.

One day, there were two friends named Abigail and Daniel. They decided they would march together in the park. So, they put on their coats and marched off. At first, everything was fun. They sang songs and marched along the sidewalk. 

Suddenly, Abigail felt a sharp pain in her leg. She stopped and cried out. She was so angry. Daniel tried to help her, but she refused. She had to march on her own. 

Abigail marched slowly, trying to ignore the pain. After a few moments, she felt a bit better. She and Daniel continued to march together, happily singing their favorite song. They had made it through their march, despite the pain.

Once there was a little boy named Ben. Ben liked to play with his silver toy cars. One day when Ben was playing outside it began to rain. His toy cars looked so sad and wet! Ben wanted to make them dry. He found some easy steps.

First, Ben got the towel. He decided to dry the cars one by one. Ben wiped each car with the towel, taking care to make sure it was dry. He rubbed hard until each car was completely dry.

After all his cars were dried, Ben was pleased to see them sparkling like new! He put them all away and went inside to eat a snack.

Ben learned that day that if something gets wet, he can make it dry again. And it doesn't need to be hard - just easy!

Once there was an otter who wanted to go exploring. He wanted to go somewhere no one had ever been before and find something special. He took a modest canoe and set off across the big, wide river. 

The otter paddled and paddled and soon he found a few islands. He looked around, but everything seemed ordinary. He was about to turn back when he noticed something sparkling in the sun.

He stopped paddling. "What is that?" He asked himself. He paddled closer, and soon he saw it was a large diamond. He jumped from the canoe and plucked the diamond from the ground.

He was so excited, but his happy moment didn't last. Suddenly, the ground began to shake and the diamond split into two. He was shocked and quickly put the two pieces back together. But no matter how hard he tried, there was no way to fix it. 

But the otter wasn't too upset, he realized it was still a special treasure and decided to keep the broken diamond in two pieces. He put it in his pocket, smiled to himself and paddled away.

Once upon a time, there was a funny dog named Spot. Spot loved to play all day long. In the evening, when the sun went down, Spot would go home to his family.

One day, Spot's mom told him to behave when they went to visit their friends. Spot promised to be a good dog. He wagged his tail and barked happily.

At their friend's house, Spot played with the other dogs. They all had so much fun. Spot remembered to behave and was a good dog. In the end, everyone had a great evening.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She was three years old and her name was Sarah. She was a very happy girl and always enjoyed playing outside near her house. 

One day, Sarah was playing in the garden when she saw a yellow bow on the ground. She bent down to pick it up. As soon as she touched it, she felt a rush of excitement. She knew she wanted to wear it! 

Sarah quickly ran over to her mom and asked if she could put on the bow. Her mom smiled and said yes. Sarah happily placed the bow in her hair and began to rush around the garden. She twirled, spun, and jumped all around. 

Sarah felt so proud wearing her yellow bow. She felt like a pretty princess! She ran to show her mom how beautiful she looked and gave her a big hug. 

Sarah loved her yellow bow and wore it all the time!

Once upon a time there was a dark dessert. It was a special dessert and everyone valued it. Everyone wanted a piece and it was popular among all ages.

The dessert had a secret ingredient. It gave it a unique flavor and one couldn't help but love it. It was always dark and smelt so delicious.

Eventually the creator of the dessert showed everyone the secret. It was the love and care he put into it. Everyone valued the dessert even more after learning the secret.

The dessert would be enjoyed for many years to come and everyone valued it. They looked forward to its sweet dark goodness. It made them so happy. The End.

Once there was a girl named Sarah who loved to play with her stuffed animals. Every day she would take them to the park and play. One day, Sarah was so happy playing in the park that she didn't notice a huge storm rolling in. A tight wind blew and Sarah was scared. She grabbed her stuffed animals and ran home.

When she got home, her Mommy looked at the sky. Mommy saw how dark the clouds were and knew Sarah needed to stay inside. Mommy said, "It's time to go inside and play, Sarah." 

Sarah was sad, but then Mommy had a great idea. She said, "I think I'll recommend a new game for us. Let's play 'Cuddle Bear Race'. We can pretend to race with the stuffed animals and see who wins!"

Sarah was so excited. She got her stuffed animals ready and they started the race. She had so much fun! Afterwards, they hugged the stuffed animals tight to give them a hug of love. 

When the storm was finally over, Sarah and Mommy went back to the park. Sarah was so happy that she could play in the park and that Mommy had recommended such a fun game.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. She loved to go to the beach and play in the waves.

One day, she put on her wetsuit, took her bucket and spade, and ran down to the beach. She laughed and smiled as she watched the waves come in. She splashed and waved her hands in the water. 

Suddenly, the water looked very cold and Lucy started to shiver.

"I'm cold," she said, starting to cry.

Just then, her big sister came over. She said, "Let's go paddling in the sun." 

So they ran over to the warm, shallow water and paddled together. Lucy laughed and smiled at the warm water, and soon she stopped shivering. 

At the end of the day, they both ran back to the beach, wet but happy. 

The End

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sue. Sue had long, blonde hair and she loved to play every day. But one day, when Sue woke up, she was very sad. She looked around her room and started to cry.

Sue's mom heard her and quickly ran to Sue's room. 
"Oh Sweetie! What's wrong?" She asked.

So Sue told her mom the story. 
"There was a fake door in my room last night," she said, "It was pink and I wanted to go play behind it, but it disappeared this morning."

Her mom hugged her and wiped away her tears.

Then, Sue's mom said, "I know it feels bad to have a fake door, but I know a way we can make it better." 

So, her mom opened the door to her room and said, "You see this real door? You can go through it and play anywhere you like." 

Sue smiled and hugged her mom. She was no longer sad. 

And from that day on, every time Sue walked through the door, she was always happy.

Ben likes to draw with his tutor, Miss Lee. She helps him learn new words and colors. Today, they are drawing a big farm with many animals. Ben draws a cow, a pig, a sheep and a hen. He uses brown, pink, white and red crayons.

"Very good, Ben!" Miss Lee says. "You are a great artist. Do you know what sound each animal makes?"

Ben nods and makes the sounds. "Moo, oink, baa, cluck!" he says proudly.

Miss Lee smiles and claps. "That's right, Ben! You are very smart. Now, can you draw a little duck to complete the farm?"

Ben thinks for a moment. He remembers seeing a duck at the park. He picks a yellow crayon and draws a little duck with a round body, a long neck and a flat bill. He adds two black dots for eyes and an orange line for a mouth.

"Quack, quack!" Ben says, showing his drawing to Miss Lee.

Miss Lee hugs him and praises him. "You did it, Ben! You completed the farm. The little duck is very cute. I'm so proud of you!"

Ben beams and hugs her back. He likes his tutor, Miss Lee. She makes him happy and helps him learn. He can't wait to draw more with her.

Tom and Mia were playing in the garden. They had a big hose that could spray water. They liked to spray the flowers and the grass and each other. It was fun and cool.

But then Tom saw something shiny on the table. It was money. Tom wanted to see the money. He ran to the table and picked up the money. He saw different colors and numbers on the paper.

"Look, Mia, money!" he shouted. He waved the money in the air.

Mia came to see the money too. She wanted to touch it. But Tom did not want to share. He held the money tight in his hand.

"Give me some money, Tom!" Mia said. She tried to grab the money from Tom.

"No, it's mine!" Tom said. He pushed Mia away.

Mia was angry. She saw the hose on the ground. She had an idea. She picked up the hose and turned it on. She aimed it at Tom and sprayed him with water.

"Hey, stop it!" Tom cried. He dropped the money. The water soaked the money and made it wet and wrinkled.

Mia laughed. She thought it was funny. She sprayed Tom some more.

Tom was sad. He looked at the money. It was ruined. He liked the money. He wanted to keep it. He felt sorry.

"Sorry, Mia," he said. He picked up the money and gave it to Mia. "Here, you can have some money."

Mia stopped spraying. She looked at the money. It was wet and wrinkled. She did not like it. She felt sorry too.

"Sorry, Tom," she said. She gave the money back to Tom. "I don't want the money. It's bad."

They hugged each other. They were friends again. They did not care about the money. They cared about each other.

They threw the money in the trash. They played with the hose again. They sprayed the flowers and the grass and each other. It was fun and cool.

Once there was an enormous hook. The hook was so big it seemed to reach up to the sky. Every day the hook stayed in the same place. It was very quiet. 
One night, the hook started to move. It began to swing around and around, faster and faster. It moved so quickly it began to glow brightly. 
The hook started to take the shape of an enormous bird. The bird was so big that it filled the sky. It glided slowly over the hills. 
Every day the bird stayed in the same place, soaring in the sky. It was very peaceful. Eventually the bird changed shape and returned to the same spot- an enormous hook.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved playing outside in the grass, but one day he noticed that the grass was troubled. It was all brown and dry, and it didn't look happy.

Timmy decided to help the grass by giving it some water. He paused his playtime and got a watering can. He watered the grass every day, and soon it started to turn green and happy again.

Timmy learned that sometimes things can be troubled, but with a little bit of help and kindness, they can become happy again. And that made Timmy very happy too.

Sam and Lily were twins who liked to play with their toys. They had a big blanket that they used to make forts and tents. One day, they wanted to make a castle with the blanket, but it was too long and dragged on the floor.

"Let's cut the blanket and make it shorter," Sam said. He found some scissors and started to snip the edge of the blanket.

"No, don't cut the blanket!" Lily cried. "Mommy will be mad at us. She gave us the blanket when we were babies. It is special and soft."

But Sam did not listen. He cut and cut until the blanket was in two pieces. He gave one piece to Lily and said, "Here, now we have two blankets. We can make a bigger castle."

Lily was sad and angry. She did not want two blankets. She wanted the whole blanket that Mommy gave them. She threw the piece that Sam gave her on the floor and ran to their room. She hugged the other piece and cried.

Sam felt bad. He did not mean to make Lily cry. He followed her to their room and said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I was wrong to cut the blanket. Can we be friends again?"

Lily looked at Sam and saw that he was sorry. She wiped her tears and said, "It's okay, Sam. I forgive you. But we have to tell Mommy what we did. Maybe she can fix the blanket."

Sam nodded. He took the piece that he cut and held it with Lily's piece. They went to find Mommy and told her the truth. Mommy was not happy, but she was not very mad either. She said, "I'm glad you told me. Cutting things without permission is not nice. But I love you both and I know you love the blanket. I will try to sew it back together."

She took the blanket and the scissors and went to her sewing machine. Sam and Lily watched as she stitched the pieces together. It took a long time, but she made the blanket whole again. It had a line where she sewed it, but it was still special and soft.

"Thank you, Mommy," Sam and Lily said. They hugged Mommy and the blanket. They felt lucky to have a Mommy who could fix things and who loved them. They decided to never cut the blanket again. They went back to their playroom and made a castle with the blanket. They played happily and shared their toys. They were good twins.

Once upon a time, there was a little lizard. The little lizard lived in a tiny house. The house was in a big forest with many trees and flowers. The little lizard loved to play with his friends, the birds and the bugs.

One day, the little lizard saw a big fire in the forest. The fire was very close to his tiny house. The little lizard wanted to prevent the fire from burning his house. He thought very hard about what to do.

The little lizard had an idea. He asked his friends, the birds, to help him. The birds flew to the river and brought water in their beaks. They dropped the water on the fire. The little lizard and his friends worked together to prevent the fire from burning his house. They were all very happy and proud of what they did.

Once upon a time, there were two friends named Joe and Ben. Joe had a birthday coming up, and Ben wanted to make it special. 

He had a great idea! Ben went to the store and bought some decorations.

When he got home, he excitedly showed Joe. Joe was so happy to see the decorations. There was a funny owl to put on the wall and bright streamers to hang from the ceiling.

Joe said: "Wow, Ben! This looks so interesting. You really decorated it up for me. Thank you so much!"

Ben smiled. He liked making friends happy. 

Joe and Ben hung up the decorations together. Joe thought it looked amazing, and he felt so special. 

Then Ben said, "Let's have a party!" They did, and it was a fun and special birthday for Joe.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a clock in her room that she loved to watch tick-tock. One day, Lily's mommy asked her to clean her room. Lily said, "Okay mommy, but it's difficult." Her mommy replied, "I know it's difficult, but you can do it. Don't forget to put your toys away." 

Lily started to clean her room, but she kept getting distracted by her clock. She watched it tick-tock and tick-tock. Suddenly, her mommy came in and saw that Lily hadn't cleaned her room yet. Her mommy said, "Lily, you forgot to clean your room. You need to put your toys away and make your bed." 

Lily felt sad that she forgot to clean her room, but she knew she had to do it. She put her toys away and made her bed. Her mommy was proud of her for doing a good job. Lily looked at her clock and smiled. She knew that she could do difficult things if she tried her best.

Once upon a time, there was a kind bunny named Benny. Benny liked to hop and play in the meadow with his friends. One day, Benny found a shiny red apple on the ground. He picked it up and wanted to eat it, but his friends told him not to. They said it might be bad for him.

But Benny didn't listen. He took a bite of the apple at noon, and it tasted delicious! But soon after, Benny started to feel sick. He realized his friends were right. He shouldn't have accepted the apple from a stranger. Benny learned a valuable lesson that day, and he never forgot it.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved winter because he could play in the snow. One day, Timmy went outside to play, but he saw a fierce snowstorm coming. The snow was blowing everywhere and it was very cold.

Timmy knew he had to act fast. He ran inside and told his mom about the storm. His mom was very proud of him for being responsible and telling her. They stayed inside and watched the storm from the window.

After the storm was over, Timmy and his mom went outside to play in the snow. Timmy learned that it's important to act fast when there is danger, and to always listen to his mom. The moral of the story is to stay safe and have fun in the winter!

Once, there was a hippo who lived in a big lake. He was happy and loved to play with all his friends in the lake.

One day, the hippo decided to race his friends. So, he asked them: "Who wants to race me around the lake?" His friends all wanted to race, so the hippo said, "Let's get ready, set, go!"

The hippo was the fastest of all his friends. He was very happy and it seemed like he would win the race easily.

But then, he felt something he had never felt before. He felt an earth tremor as he raced. Suddenly, the hippo was stuck and he couldn't move! He was stuck in the mud, and it looked like he wouldn't be able to finish the race.

But then, the hippo realized that the mud was actually very useful. He used it to quickly push himself out of the mud. With a few big pushes, he was out!

The hippo raced to the finish line and won the race! Everyone was very happy for him, and the hippo knew that being useful could help him during a race.

Tom and Lily were playing in the park. They liked to swing on the long cord that hung from a big tree. They took turns to push each other and go high in the air.

"Look at me, Lily!" Tom shouted. "I can touch the sky!"

"You are so brave, Tom!" Lily said. "Can I try too?"

"Sure, Lily. But be careful. The cord is very long and you might fall."

Tom helped Lily to sit on the cord and gave her a big push. Lily felt the wind in her hair and the sun on her face. She laughed and waved to Tom.

"Tom, Tom, this is so fun!" Lily cried. "I want to go higher!"

But then, Lily saw something that made her scared. A big dog was running towards them, barking loudly. It looked angry and hungry.

"Tom, Tom, there is a dog!" Lily screamed. "Help me, Tom!"

Tom saw the dog too. He was scared, but he wanted to help Lily. He ran to the tree and grabbed the cord. He pulled hard and tried to make Lily come down.

"Lily, Lily, hold on!" Tom said. "I will get you down!"

But the cord was too long and too strong. Tom could not pull Lily down. He felt the dog getting closer and closer.

"Tom, Tom, I am scared!" Lily sobbed. "What can we do?"

Tom did not know what to do. He wished he had a stick or a stone to scare the dog away. He wished someone would come and help them. He wished they had never played on the long cord.

Then, he remembered something. He remembered what his mom had told him once. He remembered what to do when a dog was angry.

"Tom, Tom, what are you doing?" Lily asked. She saw Tom let go of the cord and stand still. He looked at the dog and said something in a loud voice.

"NO!" Tom said. "BAD DOG! GO AWAY!"

The dog heard Tom's voice and stopped. It looked at Tom and tilted its head. It did not understand why Tom was not afraid. It did not like Tom's voice. It felt confused and bored.

The dog turned around and ran away. It did not want to play with Tom and Lily anymore. It wanted to find something else to chase.

Tom and Lily were happy and relieved. They hugged each other and thanked Tom for being brave and smart. They decided to leave the long cord alone and play something else. They never forgot that day and they always remembered what to do when a dog was angry.

Anna likes to draw with crayons. She has many colors and makes pictures of flowers, animals and people. She draws on paper, but sometimes she also draws on the wall. Mommy does not like that. She says Anna has to wipe the wall with a cloth and soap.

One day, Anna draws a big heart on the wall. Inside the heart, she writes "I love mommy". She thinks mommy will like it. She shows mommy her drawing and smiles. Mommy sees the drawing and smiles too. She hugs Anna and says "I love you too, sweetie. You are very kind and attractive. But you still have to wipe the wall, okay?"

Anna nods and gets a cloth and soap. She wipes the wall with her hand. The crayon comes off and the wall is white again. Mommy helps her and says "Good job, Anna. You are very smart and helpful. Next time, please draw on paper, not on the wall. Okay?"

Anna says "Okay, mommy. I'm sorry. I just wanted to make you happy." Mommy says "You always make me happy, Anna. You are my precious girl. Now, let's go and have some cookies and milk. How does that sound?"

Anna says "Yay! I love cookies and milk. And I love you, mommy." Mommy says "I love you too, Anna." They go to the kitchen and have a nice snack. Anna is happy and mommy is happy. They love each other very much. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily and her best friend, a teddy bear named Teddy, went for a walk in the park. They played on the swings and climbed on the jungle gym. Suddenly, the sky turned dark and it started to rain.

Lily and Teddy ran to a nearby tree to take shelter from the rain. But the tree was rough and scratchy, and it hurt their skin. Lily said, "This tree is too rough. We need to find a better place to hide."

Teddy replied, "I know a place. Let's call my friend, Mr. Rabbit. He has a cozy burrow where we can stay dry."

Lily and Teddy called Mr. Rabbit on the phone and he invited them to his burrow. They went inside and had a warm cup of tea with Mr. Rabbit. They were safe and happy, even though it was dark and stormy outside.

The moral of the story is that when you have a problem, you should call a friend for help. And sometimes, the best solution is not the most obvious one.

Once upon a time, there was a fancy rhinoceros who lived in the forest. All the other animals in the forest thought the rhinoceros was the prettiest of them all. Every day, the rhinoceros would bow to the other animals as it walked around the forest.

The other animals loved this! They asked the rhinoceros if it wanted to join in a dance. "Yes!" said the rhinoceros, and so it joined them. It bow-ed and jumped and had lots of fun!

The other animals smiled and laughed as they watched the fancy rhinoceros bow and dance. It was so much fun! Everyone was clapping, cheering and having a wonderful time, until night-time came and all the animals said their goodbyes, leaving the rhinoceros alone in the forest.

But the next morning, when the rhinoceros looked around the forest, all the animals were there waiting for him, with smiles on their faces. They asked the rhinoceros to bow again, and they all danced and laughed till night-time.

From that day on, the fancy rhinoceros was the most popular animal in the forest, and every day the animals would come and ask it to bow and dance with them. They were all very happy.

Once upon a time, there was a big bus. The bus was very impressive because it was so big and shiny. One day, a little boy saw the bus and he wanted to ride it. But his mommy didn't let him because she was too busy. The little boy was sad.

The next day, the little boy saw the bus again and he really wanted to ride it. He asked his mommy if he could go on the bus, but she said no again. The little boy was very upset.

Finally, one day the little boy snuck away from his mommy and got on the bus by himself. He was so happy to finally ride on the impressive bus. But then, something bad happened. The bus crashed and the little boy got hurt. His mommy was very sad when she found out what happened. She wished she had let the little boy ride the bus with her instead.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a bed that was big and cozy, but she didn't like to sleep in it alone. Every night, she would ask her parents to stay with her until she fell asleep. 

One day, Lily's parents went on a trip and left her alone in the house. At bedtime, Lily climbed into her empty bed and felt scared. She wished her parents were there to keep her company. As she lay there, she started to shiver with fear.

Suddenly, Lily remembered something her parents had told her before they left. They said that she was a brave girl and didn't need anyone to protect her. With that thought, Lily stopped shivering and closed her eyes. She felt safe in her bed and fell asleep peacefully. From that night on, Lily learned that she was strong and brave, even when she was alone.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved playing cowboys and Indians with his friends. One day, Timmy found a toy pistol in his toy box. The pistol was warm because it had been sitting in the sun.

Timmy's friend, Johnny, came over to play. "Wow, Timmy! That's a cool pistol! Can I play with it?" asked Johnny.

Timmy thought for a moment and then said, "Sure, but you have to attach this holster to your belt first." Timmy showed Johnny how to attach the holster to his belt.

Johnny put the pistol in the holster and they played cowboys and Indians for hours. They had so much fun, but they knew they had to be careful with the pistol. They made sure to put it away safely when they were done playing.

Tom and Lily are playing with blocks. They like to build towers and bridges and houses. They have many blocks of different colors and shapes.

"Look, Lily, I made a big tower!" Tom says. He puts another block on top of his tower. "It is very high and strong!"

Lily looks at Tom's tower. She wants to make a bigger tower. She takes some blocks from Tom's pile and adds them to her tower. "My tower is bigger and better!" she says. She puts another block on top of her tower. "It is very fit and tall!"

Tom sees that Lily is taking his blocks. He gets angry. He wants his blocks back. He pushes Lily's tower. "No, Lily, those are my blocks! Give them back!" he says.

Lily's tower falls down. The blocks crash on the floor. Lily is sad and scared. She cries. "Tom, why did you do that? You are mean and bad!" she says.

Tom feels sorry. He did not mean to make Lily cry. He wants to say sorry and share his blocks. But before he can say anything, Mom comes in. She hears Lily crying and sees the mess on the floor. She is very mad.

"Tom, what did you do? You made Lily cry and you broke her tower! You are in big trouble, mister!" Mom says. She takes Tom by the hand and drags him to his room. "You have to stay here for ten minutes and think about what you did. No more blocks for you today!"

Tom is sad and lonely. He wishes he did not push Lily's tower. He wishes he could play with Lily and the blocks again. He looks at the clock. The minute hand moves very slowly. He thinks ten minutes is a very long time. He thinks he is very stupid and bad. He cries. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy liked to play with his toy cars and trucks. One day, he found a long chain in his backyard. Timmy thought the chain was useful and decided to raise it up high. He raised the chain up to the top of a tree and was very proud of himself.

But then, a big gust of wind came and knocked the tree down. The chain fell on top of Timmy and he got hurt. Timmy realized that even though something seems useful, it can still be dangerous. From then on, he made sure to always ask his parents before playing with things he found in the backyard.

There was once a little girl who loved sunflowers. Every day she would walk around her garden, wondering what the world was like. One day, she noticed that one of her sunflowers had started to wilt. She asked her mom why this was the case.

Her mom said, â€œYour sunflower needs water, honey. You must take care of all the things in your garden.â€

The little girl thought about this and decided to try her best to care for her sunflower. She made sure it got enough water every day and soon it became strong and beautiful.

The little girl learnt a valuable lesson. With patience and care, you can make any situation calm and peaceful.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and have tea parties with her friends. One day, she had a tea party with her teddy bear, Mr. Snuggles.

Lily was very excited to share her tea with Mr. Snuggles. But Mr. Snuggles was a bit selfish. He did not want to share the tea with Lily. Lily was sad and did not know what to do.

Then, Lily's mom came into the room and saw what was happening. She mentioned to Lily that sharing is very important. Lily told Mr. Snuggles that sharing is good. Mr. Snuggles listened and decided to share the tea with Lily. They both had a fun tea party and learned to share with each other.

Once upon a time there were two best friends, Mandy and Jojo. They were both three years old.

One day, they were walking together in the park. There were lots of trees, grass and flowers. Mandy stopped and asked Jojo a question.

"Do you like the daisies on this side or the tulips on that side?" said Mandy, pointing to one side with daisies and another side with tulips.

"Both!" said Jojo without hesitation. Mandy was so happy.

The girls smiled at each other and agreed that the view was perfect. They walked hand in hand, enjoying the perfect day.

Clara and Mommy were walking down the street. Clara had her favourite beach ball with her. She held it tight in her hands. Suddenly, she saw a big sign. It was tall and colourful. It said, "Examine this Creative Place". 

Mommy looked at the sign and said, "Let's see what this creative place is." They started walking slowly towards it. 

When they got closer, they saw the creative place was a big park! Clara was so excited. She wanted to explore. 

Mommy and Clara walked towards the park. Mommy told her to examine every corner of it carefully. They saw lots of trees, flowers and a pond. They even saw some groups of children playing games. 

Clara and Mommy had a great time in the park. Clara was very happy to have seen such a creative place.

Amy and Joe were best friends. Every day Amy would bring a lovely pencil to school. Joe always thanked her every morning. Joe was so thankful because Amy always shared her pencils with him. Joe loved to draw and Amy's pencils were the only thing that he had to draw with.

One day Joe had brought a pencil for Amy too. It was a surprise for her. When Amy saw it she said, "Thank you, Joe! It's lovely." 

They both liked to draw so they drew pictures together with the pencils and laughed. Every day they drew pictures and shared their pencils. They were so happy.

Amy and Joe were the best of friends and always thanked each other for their lovely pencils. They were very happy together.

One day, Sam was walking in the park. He saw a wide green field, with a carrot patch surrounded by a fence. He wanted to pick some carrots, so he ran over to the patch. But when he got there, he saw that the fence was too high. He wanted to quit, so he started crying. 

Just then, he heard a voice. He looked around and saw an old man. The man took Sam's hand, and then he walked to the other side of the carrot patch. There was a wide gate, and the old man opened it for Sam.

Sam was so happy; he could finally pick the carrots. He ran into the patch and grabbed his basket. Soon he was picking carrots like crazy. He ate some, too; they were so sweet!

When the basket was full, it was time for Sam to quit. He gave the man a big hug, thanked him, and then walked back home. He had a big basket of carrots and the best adventure ever!

Once upon a time, there was a small post. The post was fragile and needed to be held carefully. One day, a little girl named Jane decided to pick it up. She held it very carefully and walked across the street. 

Once she had the post in her hands, she looked around to see if anyone was watching. Luckily, no one was around. Jane quietly placed the post in the front yard of her house. She smiled, feeling proud of herself.

The following day, Jane got out of bed early. She wanted to make sure no one had moved the post. When she arrived at her house, the post was still there. She was so relieved! She carefully picked up the post and safely put it back in its place. 

From that day, Jane took turns with her friends holding the post until it no longer needed protecting. The fragile post was safe and the children were happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Max. Max loved to play in the park and chase after balls. One day, Max saw a big bone on the other side of the park. He wanted it so badly, but there was a big puddle in the way. Max didn't like getting wet, but he really wanted that bone.

Max tried to jump over the puddle, but he couldn't manage to do it. He was getting tired from all the jumping. Suddenly, another dog came by and saw Max struggling. The other dog had big paws and was able to jump over the puddle easily. The other dog was kind enough to help Max get the bone.

Max was so happy to have the bone and he thanked the other dog for helping him. He learned that sometimes it's okay to ask for help when you can't manage on your own.

Lily was a tall girl who liked to eat toast for breakfast. She liked to put butter and jam on her toast and make it sweet and soft. She also liked to tell stories to her little brother, Ben, who was still in his crib.

One morning, Lily woke up early and went to the kitchen. She saw a big loaf of bread on the counter and decided to make toast for herself and Ben. She took two slices of bread and put them in the toaster. She waited for them to pop up and then took them out. She put butter and jam on them and put them on a plate.

She carried the plate to Ben's room and saw him sleeping. She smiled and said, "Wake up, Ben! I have toast for you!" She put the plate on his nightstand and climbed into his crib. She gave him a hug and a kiss and said, "Good morning, Ben! Do you want to hear a story?"

Ben opened his eyes and saw Lily and the toast. He smiled and said, "Yes, please! I love your stories!" He took a bite of the toast and said, "Mmm, this is yummy! Thank you, Lily!"

Lily said, "You're welcome, Ben! Now, listen to my story. It's about a tall princess who lived in a castle with a dragon. She was brave and smart and kind. Do you want to know what she did?"

Ben nodded and said, "Yes, yes, tell me more!"

Lily smiled and began to tell her story. She used her voice and her hands to make it fun and exciting. Ben listened and laughed and asked questions. They ate their toast and enjoyed their story. They were happy and loved each other very much.

Once upon a time there was a girl called Jane. She was three years old and very curious. She loved to make things so one day she grabbed a big bottle of glue and a big piece of paper. She took them to the table and began to pour the glue onto the paper.

"Wow!" she said. "This glue is so cool, it's famous! I'm so happy I'm going to make something."

Just then the door opened and in walked Jane's mum. She was smiling.

"What are you making dear?" she asked.

"I'm making a big picture!" Jane said proudly.

Mum laughed. "That's so wonderful! I'm sure it will be famous too!" 

Jane smiled and kept pouring the glue onto the paper. She was so excited to see what it would look like at the end. She knew it was going to be something special!

Once upon a time, there was a mommy and a little girl. The mommy and the little girl went to the store. The little girl wanted to buy a reef. The mommy said that was ok and helped her pick out a nice reef. It was a pretty reef with lots of colors.

The mommy paid for the reef and the two of them went home. The little girl was very happy to have her new reef. She put it in her room and it was very normal. Every day, she would look at the reef and smile.

The little girl liked her reef so much. She would play with it, talk to it and bring it when she went to Grandma's house. Her mommy was very happy that the little girl had a reef that she could play with and keep her busy. 

Even as the little girl got older, she still loved to buy reefs. Every time she got a new reef it was a special moment. She would proudly put her new reef in her room and feel special. 

The end.

Jack and Sue were playing in the yard when they spotted a Dinosaur. They both ran up to it to take a closer look. Sue was filled with amazement.

"Wow!", she said awely. "Where did it come from?"

"I don't know", Jack said. But let's hang it up in my room so we can look at it everyday."

The two of them grabbed the dinosaur and filled it up in Jack's room. Jack hung it from a tree branch in one corner of his room and it looked very nice.

Sue watched with a proud smile.

"That makes your room look really humble", she said.

Jack smiled happily.

"Thank you Sue!", he said with a big smile. "Now I can see it every morning when I wake up!"

Once upon a time, there was a helpful girl named Lily. She liked to play with her friends in the park. One day, while she was playing with her friends, a boy came and disturbed them. He took their toys and threw them away.

Lily said, "Hey, that's not nice. You're disturbing us. Please give our toys back." But the boy didn't listen and ran away.

Lily and her friends were sad because they couldn't play without their toys. But then, Lily had an idea. She said, "Let's ask the other kids in the park if they have any extra toys we can borrow."

They asked around and found some helpful kids who gave them toys to play with. The boy who disturbed them saw how happy they were and felt bad. He came back and apologized. From then on, they all played together and had fun.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to draw and write on paper with her crayons. One day, she saw a big black dog in her backyard. The dog was so big that it scared her. But then, she saw that the dog was friendly and wagged its tail. 

Lily wanted to show her mommy the big dog, so she ran inside to get a piece of paper to write a note. She wrote, "Mommy, there is a big black dog outside. He is friendly." She showed the note to her mommy and they both went outside to pet the dog. 

After they pet the dog, Lily's mommy made some lemonade for them to drink. Lily loved the sour taste of the lemonade. She smiled and said, "Mommy, this lemonade is yummy!" They sat outside and enjoyed the sunshine with the big black dog. From that day on, the dog would visit Lily's backyard and they would play together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved to play. She liked games and exploring. One day, the little girl decided to go out and explore the world.

She looked around and saw many beautiful things: a tall tree with shiny leaves, a river with a blue sky. The little girl wanted to see what was around the corner, so she walked and walked.

Just then, she saw her friend. "Hi friend," she said, smiling. Her friend smiled back. "Let's have some fun!" she said. 

The little girl and her friend had so much fun together! They played games, sang songs and laughed a lot. Eventually, it was time to go home.

The little girl said goodbye to her friend, and they hugged. Her friend said goodbye and waved to her. Then the friend said, "I'll send you fun every day."

The little girl smiled, and she knew what her friend meant. She realized that she could remember the good times, and use them to make her own days more fun. She knew that by remembering what was nice, she could make each day more beautiful.

Once upon a time, there was a large puddle on the ground. A tiny frog was in the puddle, and it wanted to find a new home. "Where should I go?" the frog whispered.

Just then, a giant dragonfly flew above the puddle. "I know a place you can go," said the dragonfly. "Follow me!"

The frog hopped out of the puddle and followed the dragonfly. They flew and flew until they came to a large pond. It was full of lily pads and other frogs.

"This is the perfect place for you," the dragonfly said.

The frog hopped into the pond with happiness. He was so excited to have a new home. From then on he lived happily in the large pond.

Once there was a boy called Joe. One day, Joe was walking in the forest. He felt so very hungry. All he could think about was food!
Suddenly, Joe saw a distant village. He decided to take a look and see if he could find something to eat. 
Joe walked through the village. He looked in all the windows and doors, but he could not find anybody and no food. He was so sad. 
But then, Joe heard noise from a house in the corner. He walked closer and knocked on the door. 
"Hello?" said Joe. "Is anybody there?"

A voice answered from inside the house. "Yes, come in!"

Joe was so happy. He opened the door and saw a kindly old man. "I am so hungry," said Joe.

The old man smiled. "Come and have a meal with me," he said. 

Joe was excited, and he passed the old man a big smile. He ate a big dinner with the old man, who told Joe stories of far away lands while they enjoyed their meal. 

When Joe was finished, the old man said, "You are welcome to pass by anytime." Joe thanked the old man, and he left feeling full and happy.

Once upon a time, there was a mountain. It was very big and very high. Every day it sparkled in the sunshine. It was so rare that nobody had ever seen one like it before. Everyone who lived nearby wanted to go and explore the mountain.

One day, three little kids decided to take the adventure. They packed their bags, got some food and water, and set off. They hiked up the mountain and had so much fun!

As they walked, they got to a lake. It was so clear and so blue! The kids were so thirsty, so they stopped to drink from the lake. It was the most delicious water they had ever tasted! They drank and drank until their tummies were full. 

The kids were so glad they explored the rare mountain. They took many more trips together before they grew up, and each time was more magical than the last.

Once there was a modest boy who loved riding his motorcycle. Every day, he rode around his city, zig-zagging through the streets and feeling the wind on his face. 

One day, the boy decided to take his motorcycle to the park and explore some of the trails. He found a beautiful, winding path and thought it was a perfect place to explore. But, just as he was about to begin his journey, he heard a noise coming from the bushes. 

The boy stopped and asked, â€œWhoâ€™s there?â€ 

Suddenly, a voice shouted, â€œYou better not keep going! Iâ€™ll tear your bike apart if you do!â€ 

The boy was scared and quickly turned around. He was about to leave when he saw an old, broken motorcycle nearby. The sight of it made him feel even more scared and he quickly ran away. 

The boy never returned to the park. He could not forget the warning, and he knew that something bad was lurking in the shadows. Foreshadowing the bad things to come, that broken motorcycle had been a warning of what was truly in the bushes.

Once upon a time, there was a fish who lived in the ocean. He was small and independent. Every day, he liked to bathe in the warm tide.
