Once upon a time there was a kid named Todd. He was three years old and loved adventure. One day, he decided to sail out to sea on a homemade raft. 

Todd hoisted up the sail and it bellowed in the wind. He was scared at first but then he smiled with delight. The sun was shining, the water was glimmering, and he felt like he was on top of the world.

He said loudly to the sea, "This is the best day of my life!" 

Suddenly, a giant fish jumped out of the water. "Wow!" Todd called. "It looks like it's trying to play with me."

The fish kept jumping in the air and making loud noises. He jumped and laughed until he was so tired he could barely keep his eyes open. Todd waved goodbye to the giant fish and sailed back to shore. 

He thought to himself, "I can't wait for the next time I can sail."

Tom and Mia are twins. They like to play with their toys in the living room. Sometimes they also play with Mom's phone. Mom says they can only touch the phone when she is there. But Tom and Mia are curious. They want to see what the phone can do.

One day, Mom is busy in the kitchen. She does not see Tom and Mia crawl to the phone on the table. Tom picks up the phone and presses some buttons. He hears a beep and a voice. He puts the phone to his ear and says, "Hello?"

The voice says, "Hello, this is Grandma. Who is this?"

Tom does not know what to say. He does not know Grandma. He only knows Mom and Dad and Mia. He looks at Mia and says, "Phone talks!"

Mia crawls to Tom and takes the phone from him. She puts the phone to her ear and says, "Hi!"

The voice says, "Hi, sweetie. Is this Mia? Where is Mom?"

Mia does not understand the voice. She only knows a few words. She says, "Phone talks!"

The voice says, "Yes, phone talks. But I can't hear you very well. Can you speak louder?"

Mia does not know what louder means. She says, "Phone talks!"

The voice says, "Oh, dear. I think you are too young to use the phone. Can you give the phone to Mom, please?"

Mia does not know what please means. She says, "Phone talks!"

The voice says, "I'm sorry, I can't hear you. I think I'm going deaf. Can you call me back later?"

Mia does not know what deaf means. She says, "Phone talks!"

The voice says, "Goodbye, Mia. I love you."

Mia says, "Bye!"

She hangs up the phone and gives it to Tom. They smile and crawl back to their toys. They think the phone is fun. They do not know they just talked to Grandma. They do not know Mom is coming to the living room. They do not know Mom is going to be mad. They only know the phone talks.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Jack. He loved music, and wanted to learn how to play the violin. Every day, he saw his parents playing their violins. Jack thought it looked like so much fun.

So, one day, Jack asked his parents if he could have a violin of his own. His parents said he could, and they bought him the most wonderful violin.

Jack was so excited! He soon learned how to play it, and practice every day. He enjoyed learning new songs, and he become very good at playing.

But one day, he was so scared that he made a mistake when playing a song. He became fearful, and he stopped playing.

But his parents showed him that it was okay to make mistakes. They hugged him, and told him that mistakes happen, and that learning was part of the fun. They reminded him to value all of his efforts and enjoy the experience of learning. 

Jack smiled, and continued to practice, with a newfound appreciation for the instrument. He valued his violin more than ever, and was no longer fearful. He continued to practice and play for many years!

Sam was sad. He looked up at the sky and saw the beautiful sunset. He sighed because the sunset was so fragile and beautiful.

Then something amazing happened. He heard someone calling his name. He looked up and saw his best friend Richard. Richard smiled at him and reached out his hand.

So Sam smiled back and took Richard's hand. They walked together and talked about the things that were important to them. Sam laughed and felt much better.

As they watched the sunset, they felt happy and understood the fragile beauty of the sunset. Then they hugged and said goodbye until next time.

Once upon a time there was a missile, who wanted to be shiny and new all the time. He asked the moon and the stars how to do it, but they just said he had to work hard. So he looked around and he saw a compassionate lady polishing her shoes. He asked her if she could help him too and she said â€œSure!â€

So every day the lady would come up to the missile and polish him. After a few days of polishing he started to shine so brightly that the stars and moon would twinkle at him.

He was so happy and thanked the lady for her help. From then on, the missile felt new and happy every day, because he knew the lady was always there to Polish him. The End.

Once upon a time a little girl named Lisa was playing in her garden. She saw a snake in her garden and it made her feel afraid. Lisa asked her dad what to do.

Her dad said he would help her. "I will take the snake away," he said. Lisa asked if he could take the snake to the lake.

He agreed. Dad put the snake into a box and drove to the lake. Lisa and her dad put the snake in the lake.

The snake began to swim around in the water. It was so happy to be free. Lisa smiled and felt much better.

The snake swished its tail and said â€œThank you.â€ Lisa felt happy and glad that the snake was no longer miserable.

Once upon a time, there was an ugly sheep. The sheep was feeling very hot. So it decided to jump into the lake. It was so happy when it felt the cool water surrounding it! It soaked in the lake for a long time.

When the sheep got out of the lake, it felt much better and much cooler. The sheep ran around the lake, feeling relieved and refreshed.

Suddenly, a farmer came out of nowhere. He was looking for the ugly sheep but he couldn't find it. He looked from left to right but still, he couldn't find it.

But then, he suddenly heard a sound coming from the lake. It was a splashing noise! When he looked to the right, the ugly sheep was in the lake, soaking.

The farmer was so happy to find the sheep and he quickly took it out of the lake. Then, the farmer took the sheep home and the ugly sheep was safe and happy.

Once there was a smart rabbit named Danny. He was always curious and loved exploring. 

One day Danny wanted to explore the big house he lived in. He hopped from room to room until he came to the bathroom. He had never been in there before and he lay down on the furry rug to take a closer look. 

Danny saw that the bathroom was very sparkly. The floor was made up of shiny little tiles and there was a bright bath in the corner. He hopped closer to take a peek and saw that the bath was filled with warm water and bubbles. 

Danny thought it looked like lots of fun and he wanted to jump in! After a few minutes of bouncing up and down, Danny finally decided to take a bath. He hopped in and lay down in the bubbly water. 

Danny enjoyed the warm water and felt so clean and smart when he got out. From then on, he loved taking baths and he always felt smart when he finished.

Once upon a time there was a small pup named George. He was a curious pup who liked to explore the world. One day, George came across a very strange object. It was a big box with buttons and a digital screen.

George was very confused and didn't know what to do. Then a voice came from inside the box. "Hello George," said the voice. "This is a weigh machine. It can tell you how much you weigh!"

George was still confused, but he was excited too. He stepped onto the machine. The voice spoke again. "You weigh 8 kilos," it said.

George was so surprised. He jumped off the machine with a smile. He didn't understand what had just happened, but he was proud that he had learned something new.

The next day, George went to school. The teacher was talking about the weigh machine and George decided to share his story. When he was done, all his classmates were just as surprised and confused as he had been.

The teacher smiled. "You've completed your lesson today," she said. "Now you all know what a weigh machine is and how it works." 

George was very proud. He felt like he had been much more than just a pupil for that day.

Once upon a time, there was a man called John. John had a job to do every week. He was dependable, so he always got the job done.

John thought about it for a while, but he wasn't sure how to do the job. He decided to ask for help. He called his neighbor, Dan.

John said, "Hi Dan, can you help me? I have this job to do every week, but I can't figure it out."

Dan replied, "Yes, of course I can help you. I will come by in the morning and show you what to do."

John was so happy. He thanked Dan and said goodnight.

The next morning, Dan came over and showed John how to do the job. John watched and listened carefully. Afterward, he thanked Dan again and said goodbye.

John was now able to do the job himself each week. He was so happy to be dependable and to be able to do the job without help.

Ben and Mia love to swim in the sea. They have big masks and tubes to see the fish. One day, they see a big boat near the shore. The boat has many boxes on it.

"Let's go see the boat," Ben says. "Maybe they have something fun."

"OK," Mia says. "But we have to be careful. The boat might be bad."

They swim to the boat and look at the boxes. They see words on them. They do not know what they mean. They see a hole in one box. They peek inside. They see many shiny things.

"Wow," Ben says. "These are pretty. Can we take some?"

"I don't know," Mia says. "Maybe they belong to someone."

They hear a loud voice from the boat. It is a man. He is angry.

"Hey, you kids! Get away from there! That's my supply of jewels! I stole them from the reef! They are very valuable!"

Ben and Mia are scared. They drop the shiny things and swim away. The man tries to catch them, but he is too slow. He is crazy.

Ben and Mia reach the shore. They are safe. They hug each other.

"That was scary," Ben says. "We should not go near the boat again."

"Yes," Mia says. "The boat is bad. The man is bad. The shiny things are bad. They hurt the reef and the fish."

They decide to swim in another place. They find a nice reef with many colors and shapes. They see many friendly fish. They are happy. They forget about the boat and the crazy man. They have fun.

Once in a small village, there was a big purple chair. All the kids loved to sit on it. One day, two friends, Tim and Lily, went to the chair at the same time.

"I want to sit on the purple chair!" said Tim.
"No, I want to sit on it!" said Lily.

They both wanted to sit on the chair, but there was only room for one. They started to get mad at each other. Their friend, Max, saw them fighting and came to help.

"Hey, why don't you both sit on the chair together?" Max suggested. Tim and Lily looked at each other, then looked at the chair. They decided to try it.

Tim and Lily both sat on the purple chair. They smiled and laughed. They were happy to share the chair and have fun together. And they learned that it's better to share than to fight.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He loved to play at the beach and watch the waves. One day, he saw a mighty wave coming towards him. He was scared, but his mom said, "Don't worry, Timmy. The wave won't hurt you."

Timmy asked his mom, "Can I go in the water now?" His mom said, "Yes, but only if you stay close to me." Timmy was happy that his mom allowed him to go in the water.

As Timmy played in the water, he saw a seagull flying above him. He said to the seagull, "Hello, Mr. Seagull! Do you like the beach?" The seagull replied, "Yes, I do. I like to fly over the mighty waves."

Timmy smiled and said, "I like the waves too. They're so big and strong!" His mom said, "Yes, but we have to be careful around them. They can be dangerous." Timmy nodded and said, "Okay, Mom. I'll be careful."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved summer because she could play outside all day long. One day, Lily and her friends went to the park to play. They saw a butterfly and tried to catch it, but it flew away. 

Lily's friend said she didn't believe they would ever catch a butterfly. But Lily believed they could catch one if they were patient. They kept looking and finally found a butterfly sitting on a flower. 

The sky was clear and the sun was shining. Lily felt happy and excited because they caught the butterfly. She showed it to her friends and they all smiled. It was a fun day in the summer sun.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She loved the cold. On a cold day, she went out into the garden. There, she saw a pastel-colored bird. The little girl was so excited! The bird was moving really quickly, it was speeding all around the garden. The little girl had never seen anything move so fast before! She laughed as she watched it speed around the garden. She wished she could move as fast as the bird, but she knew that she could never run that fast. The bird flew away into the sky and the little girl sighed with happiness. She wished the bird a safe journey.

Once upon a time, there was a boy. His name was Timmy. He was only 3-years-old. 

Timmy and his parents were going on a long drive. They were going to take the jeep. 

Timmy's parents were ready to go but Timmy was still getting ready. They said to him, "Timmy, why are you taking so long? Hurry up, let's go."

Timmy was fearful and said, "I'm scared. I don't like the jeep". 

His parents said, "Don't be scared. Everything will be fine."

But Timmy delayed and he was still scared. His parents were getting angry and they told him he had to ride in the jeep or they would go without him.

Timmy was so scared he started to cry. He cried and cried until he was too tired to cry anymore. Finally, he got in the jeep with his parents. 

Timmy wished he hadn't been so scared but it was too late. The jeep drove away and was never seen again.

Once there was a yacht that was ready to sail. It bobbed on the water, waiting to set off to find new lands. The captain was ready, too. He was folding the sails and making sure they were nice and tidy. When he was finished, the yacht was ready to go. 

The captain sent up the sails, and the wind pushed the yacht forward. The sails billowed out, and the captain steered with the wheel. The captain and his crew took the yacht on a big adventure. They sailed to new lands, and had many new experiences. 

Finally, after a long journey, the captain steered the yacht back home. He put the sails away and gave them a good fold. Then the captain and his crew stepped off the yacht and went to their homes, happy and proud of the journey they had taken.

Tim and Lily were twins who liked to play in the living room. They had a big fireplace that made the room warm and cozy. Sometimes, they would sit by the fireplace and read books or draw pictures. But today, they wanted to do something different.

"Let's make a fort with the pillows and blankets," Tim said. "We can pretend we are in a castle or a cave."

"OK, that sounds fun," Lily agreed. They took the pillows and blankets from the couch and the chairs and piled them up in a corner. They made a door and a roof and crawled inside.

"This is our fort," Tim said. "We are the king and the queen of the fort. No one can come in without our permission."

They played for a while, making up stories and rules for their fort. They had a lot of fun. But then, they heard a loud noise from the fireplace. They looked out and saw sparks and smoke coming out of it.

"Oh no, the fireplace is on fire!" Lily cried. "We have to get out of here!"

But Tim was scared. He didn't want to leave the fort. He liked the fort. He thought it was safe.

"No, we can stay here," he said. "The fire can't get us. We are fine."

Lily shook her head. She knew the fire was dangerous. She knew they had to get help.

"Tim, we have to go," she said. "The fire can spread and burn the house. We have to tell Mom and Dad. Come on, please."

She grabbed his hand and tried to pull him out of the fort. But Tim resisted. He held on to the blankets and pillows.

"No, no, no," he said. "I don't want to go. I want to stay here."

They started to argue and tug at each other. They didn't notice that the fire was getting bigger and closer. They didn't notice that the smoke was filling the room. They didn't notice that Mom and Dad were running in with a bucket of water and a fire extinguisher. They only noticed when Mom and Dad lifted them up and carried them out of the living room.

"Tim, Lily, are you OK?" Mom asked. "What were you doing in there? Don't you know the fireplace is not a toy?"

"We were playing in our fort," Tim said. "We didn't mean to start the fire."

"We tried to stop him, but he wouldn't listen," Lily said. "He wanted to stay in the fort."

Mom and Dad hugged them and kissed them. They were glad they were not hurt. They were glad they put out the fire. They were not glad about the mess in the living room.

"Tim, Lily, you have to be more careful," Dad said. "The fireplace is not a place to play. It can be very hot and dangerous. You have to stay away from it when it is on."

"We're sorry, Mom and Dad," Tim and Lily said. "We won't do it again."

They looked at their fort. It was ruined. The pillows and blankets were burned and dirty. The fire had destroyed their fun.

They felt sad. They wished they had listened to Lily. They wished they had left the fort. They wished they had not played with the fireplace. They learned a hard lesson. They learned that fire is not a friend. They learned that fire is not fine.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy was walking in the park with his mommy when he saw a statue. The statue was big and shiny.

Timmy said, "Mommy, look at that statue! It's so big and shiny!"

Mommy said, "Yes, Timmy. It's very pretty."

Suddenly, Timmy saw a bird on the statue's head. Timmy said, "Mommy, that bird is being mean to the statue! We have to shoot it away!"

Mommy said, "No, Timmy. We can't shoot the bird. That's not nice. Let's just leave it alone."

Timmy was sad, but he knew his mommy was smart and always knew what was best. They walked away from the statue and the bird flew away on its own.

Once there was an elephant, who loved to play all day. He was very competitive and wanted to have the most fun. One day he decided to go for a walk. He stumbled his way along, trying to find a new adventure. Suddenly he heard a noise. He turned and saw a small family of tigers. He was so excited that he started running towards them.

The tigers were scared and ran away. The elephant continued to stumble through the jungle, trying to follow them. He stumbled and stumbled all around, until suddenly he stepped into a big muddy puddle. He slipped and fell and all of the mud splashed onto him.
 
He was so embarrassed that he just lay there and didn't move. Eventually he picked himself back up and, feeling a bit more competitive, started to run again. He ran and ran until he found the tigers again. He was so excited to see them, he started to dance! The tigers were so happy that they joined in and the elephant and tigers danced together all night long.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Sally. She liked to go on adventures. One day she decided to go for a walk in the woods.

As Sally walked deeper into the woods, she saw a strange skull in the ground. It was hard and had sharp edges. She looked closer and saw a gemstone in the middle of the skull.

Sally tried to turn the skull over to see what was underneath, but it was too heavy. She pushed and pushed but nothing would budge. 

Then, suddenly, the skull started to move. Sally was so excited! She quickly turned the skull to find something amazing - a secret cave hidden behind it! 

In the cave, there were sparkling gems and treasures of all kinds. Sally was so happy with her discovery. She quickly ran home to show her parents her new treasure. 

And that's how Sally found the secret cave with the hard skull!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside and watch the birds fly in the sky. One day, Timmy's mom told him they were going to a fair. Timmy was so excited!

At the fair, Timmy saw a big ride with swings that went up high in the air. Timmy wanted to go on it so badly, but he was too short. Timmy's mom said they could come back when he was taller.

Later, Timmy saw a group of older kids playing a game. They asked Timmy if he wanted to play too. Timmy was happy to join, but he didn't know the rules. When he made a mistake, the older kids laughed and teased him. Timmy felt embarrassed.

As they were leaving the fair, Timmy saw a butterfly. It reminded him of the birds he loved to watch. He knew he would grow taller one day and be able to ride the swings. And he also knew that it's okay to make mistakes and feel embarrassed sometimes.

Tim and Sam were brothers who liked to play with trains. They had a big train set with many tracks and cars and a toy engine that made noise. They pretended to be drivers and passengers and had fun.

One day, their dad brought home a surprise. He had a big bag of coal for their train. He said coal was what old trains used to make fire and steam. He showed them how to put some coal in the engine and light it with a match. Then the engine started to puff and chug and move on the tracks.

Tim and Sam were very excited. They wanted to try the coal train. They took turns to fill the engine with more coal and watch the smoke come out. They made the train go faster and slower and stop at different stations. They had a lot of fun.

But after a while, they noticed something. The engine was getting very hot and dry. It needed water to make steam. They looked for a water bottle or a cup, but they could not find any. They started to worry. What if the engine stopped working or broke down?

Then Sam had an idea. He ran to the kitchen and got a glass of milk. He came back and said to Tim, "Let's give the engine some milk. Maybe it will like it and keep going."

Tim was not sure. He said, "But milk is not water. Milk is for drinking, not for trains. What if the engine does not like it and gets sick?"

Sam said, "It's worth a try. We have nothing else. Come on, let's do it."

They poured some milk into the engine and waited. The engine made a funny noise and spat out some milk. Then it stopped puffing and chug

Once upon a time there was a boy named Bruce. Bruce was three years old and he loved going to the junkyard to play. Every day after school, Bruce would go to the junkyard to dig around. One day, as he explored the piles of junk, he came across a very mild feeling in the air. It was like the air was tickling him softly. He stopped and thought to himself, "I remember this feeling!"

Bruce smiled to himself and knew exactly what it was. He had felt this soft and gentle feeling before when his Mom used to hold him. He could almost feel her arms around him again and was filled with love and warmth. As he remembered the feeling of his Mom's arms, he realized that this feeling was coming from the junk itself.

Bruce was amazed by how gentle and mild the junk could make him feel. He often visited the junkyard just so he could remember his Mom and the special times they shared. Bruce smiled, thankful for junk that could make him remember his Mom's love.

Once there was a boy called Peter who loved to explore outside. One day, he went exploring in a new place and he saw something unusual. There was a rail, glistening in the sun. He decided to climb on it. He had fun riding on the rail but then the sun got too hot and he started to feel strange.

The rail started to get very hot and Peter realized he had to get off it. But it was too late. The rail had melted and Peter was stuck! He tried and tried to get off the melted rail but he couldn't.

Peter's neighbours heard his cries for help and came to try to rescue him. But it was too late. The rail had melted completely and Peter had disappeared. Everyone was very sad because they would never see him again. It was a very unusual and unfortunate end for Peter.

Tom and Mia are friends. They like to play outside. One day, they go to the creek. The creek is a small river with rocks and fish. Tom and Mia see a smooth stone. It is round and shiny. They want to touch it.

"Look, Mia, a smooth stone!" Tom says.

"Can I hold it?" Mia asks.

"OK, but be careful. It might be slippery," Tom says.

They take turns holding the smooth stone. It feels cold and wet. They hear the water make sounds. Splash, splash, splash. They hear the birds sing. Tweet, tweet, tweet. They hear the wind blow. Whoosh, whoosh, whoosh.

They are happy. They smile and laugh. They play with the smooth stone. They throw it in the water and watch it sink. They find another smooth stone and do it again. They have fun at the creek. They are good friends.

Once upon a time, there was a delicate pig. The pig lived on a farm with many animals. The pig was very small and pretty. All the animals liked the pig.

One day, the pig heard a voice call, "Pig, come here!" The pig looked and saw a big wolf. The wolf said, "Pig, let's play a game." The pig was scared, but the wolf looked friendly.

The pig and the wolf played for a while. But then, the wolf got hungry. The wolf said, "Pig, I am hungry. I want to eat you." The pig tried to run away, but the wolf was too fast. The wolf ate the pig, and the farm was very sad.

Once there was a boy named Tim. He liked to play with his big toy box. One day, Tim opened up his toy box and saw something funny; a metal. It was shiny and smooth, but it was too big to play with.

So Tim had an idea. He grabbed the metal and started to fold it. He folded it a few times this way and that way, until it was as small as a toy car. He smiled, because now he had something fun to play with.

Tim imagined that the folded metal was now a toy car and it could drive around his room. He was so busy playing with his new toy car that he forgot all about the big metal. Tim played until he was very tired and then he put his toy car back into the toy box and went to get a drink of water.

The next day, Tim opened his toy box and was so excited to see the folded metal was still there. He had lots of fun playing with it for the rest of the day. The metal had become his favorite toy!

Suzie was hungry. She looked in the kitchen, but there was nothing to eat. She went outside, and when blinked she saw her neighbor's garage. She walked over and peaked through the window.

Inside, she saw lots of yummy food. Cookies and cakes, breads and apples. She wished it was hers! She wondered how she could get some.

So Suzie blinked again and saw something strange. A little mouse was moving around inside the garage. Suzie thought that the mouse might help her, so she waited and watched for a while.

When the mouse came out, Suzie said, "Hi, Mr Mouse. Could you please help me get some of those yummy things from the garage? I'm very hungry." The mouse smiled and said, "Why of course I can help you, Suzie!" He asked what she wanted, and soon Suzie was enjoying her snack.

It was a happy day for Suzie!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys, especially her favorite doll. One day, her mom took her to the store to buy a new toy. Lily saw a beautiful glass ball and asked her mom to buy it. Her mom told her it was very fragile and she needed to be careful with it.

Lily promised to be careful and her mom bought her the glass ball. On the way home, they got stuck in traffic. Lily got bored and started playing with her new toy. Suddenly, the glass ball slipped from her hand and broke into many pieces. Lily was very sad and her mom was upset too.

Her mom explained to her that sometimes we need to be careful with the things we have and pay attention to our surroundings. Lily learned her lesson and promised to be more careful in the future.

Once there was a boy who wanted to go on an adventure. He looked around and saw a big danger! He was so troubled.

He started to take a step but then he heard a noise. He stopped and he listened. The noise was coming from a little bush. He went closer to investigate.

He peeked behind it and found a little creature! He was so amazed. The little creature asked him if he wanted to come on an adventure. It sounded exciting so the boy said "Yes!"

They started to run together. The boy stopped to listen to the wind and the birds. Finally, they reached a place filled with trees and flowers. The boy was so happy!

The little creature told the boy that he had to stay quiet. He could hear all kinds of things if he kept still and listened. The boy listened closely and heard different animals and stories from the trees. He was so excited that he wanted to stay and listen for days. The little creature was happy too!

In the end, the boy decided it was time to go home. He thanked the little creature for the amazing adventure and promised to listen carefully next time he went on an adventure.

Once there was a poor man who needed help. He wanted to count the stars in the night sky, but he couldn't reach them. He tried and tried but he just couldn't do it.

One day, he had an idea. He decided to put an ashtray on the ground. 

He looked up and started to count the stars one by one. Everytime he counted one, he put a pebble in the ashtray. After counting all the stars, he had a big pile of pebbles in the ashtray.

The poor man was so happy. He had managed to count the stars! Now he could count the stars whenever he wanted.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and pick flowers. One day, Lily's mom asked her to help prepare dinner for their family. 

Lily was excited to help, but didn't know what to do. Her mom explained that they needed to wash the vegetables and cut them into small pieces. Lily was successful at cutting the vegetables with her little knife. 

While they were cooking, Lily's mom asked her how she felt about helping. "I feel happy," Lily said. "I like to help you." 

Her mom smiled and said, "It's important to help others. When we work together, we can be successful and make things easier for everyone." 

From that day on, Lily loved to help her family prepare meals and learned that helping others can make a big difference.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Ria. Ria was so excited to try her first baking experience! She got together the ingredients for her very special recipe.

Ria grabbed a bowl and started mixing things in it. She stirred with a spoon and added some yummy ingredients from the pantry. 

Then, Ria put the mix in an oven and waited patiently while it baked. She could hardly contain her excitement!

Half an hour later, Ria took out her delicious creation. "What will be the result of my baking?" she asked.

Ria's mum smiled and said, "I can't wait to see the performance!"

Ria beamed with joy and waited until the cake cooled down. Finally, her patience was rewarded with a yummy result!

Jenny was out walking with her mom one day. She saw something ahead on the path - it was a big, furry animal! She was so excited! She asked her mom, "What is it?" Her mom said, "It's a bear!" Jenny was scared; she felt a bit fearful. But her mom said, "Don't worry - this bear will not hurt us. We just need to keep away from him. Keep walking on the trail and be careful not to get too close." 

So Jenny and her mom kept walking on the trail. They looked back every now and again to make sure the bear wasn't following them. Soon, the bear disappeared from sight and Jenny was no longer fearful. She felt happy and excited as she continued down the trail with her mom.

Once upon a time, there was a cute little duck named Quackers. Quackers lived in a pond with his family and friends. One day, Quackers saw a big wave coming towards him. He quacked loudly to warn his friends.

"Quack, quack! Big wave coming!" said Quackers.

All the ducks quickly swam to the other side of the pond. When the wave passed, Quackers noticed that his friend, Little Duckling, was missing.

"Oh no, where's Little Duckling?" asked Quackers.

Just then, Little Duckling popped up from behind a rock. She was carrying a basket full of berries.

"I went to fill my basket with berries," said Little Duckling.

Quackers was relieved to see his friend was safe. From then on, Quackers made sure to always keep an eye out for any danger in the pond.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Billy. Billy loved to collect rocks. He would go outside every day and look for new rocks to add to his collection. He was always so glad when he found a new one.

One day, Billy went to the mine to look for rocks. He found a shiny one that he had never seen before. He was so glad and added it to his collection. But when he got home, he realized that the rock was not just any rock. It was a special rock that belonged to the mine.

The next day, the mine owner came to Billy's house and took the rock away. Billy was sad and cried because he didn't know that the rock was not his to collect. He learned that sometimes things are not meant to be collected and kept.

Once upon a time, there was a big, hairy dog named Max. Max lived with his best friend, a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily's mom asked her to help clean the house. Lily didn't want to, but her mom said, "If you help me clean, we can go outside and play later."

Lily and Max started cleaning the living room. Lily dusted the fireplace while Max licked his paws. "Max, can you help me part the curtains?" asked Lily. Max wagged his tail and jumped up to help. They finished cleaning and went outside to play.

While they were playing, Lily saw some smoke coming from a neighbor's house. "Max, we have to go help!" she said. They ran to the house and saw that the fireplace was on fire. Lily called 911 and Max barked to alert the neighbors. The firefighters came and put out the fire. The family was safe, thanks to Lily and Max.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved playing outside in the sunshine, but one day, a big storm came. The storm was very loud and made Lily feel scared. She went inside her house and looked out the window. The storm was so strong that it blew all of the leaves off the trees.

After a while, the storm stopped and Lily went outside to play. She saw that the storm had made a big mess. There were branches and leaves all over the ground. Lily decided to help clean up the mess. She picked up all of the branches and put them in a pile. Then, she picked up all of the leaves and put them in a bag. She felt proud to have completed the task.

But then, Lily saw something disgusting. There was a big pile of mud that the storm had made. It was smelly and gross. Lily didn't know what to do. She didn't want to touch it, but she knew she had to clean it up. She took a deep breath and used a shovel to scoop up the mud. It was hard work, but she finally completed the task. Lily felt happy that she had helped clean up the mess the storm had made.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tip. He had wings that could fly and every morning he would take off and soar over the beautiful countryside. He was reliable and always brought joy to those who saw him.

One morning, Tip decided to fly higher than ever before, he wanted to see more of the world from up above. But when Tip attempted to rise, he found that reaching great heights was harder than he expected. He kept flapping his wings but he just couldn't seem to get enough momentum to reach the top.

"Help!" shouted Tip.

A nearby crow had been watching Tip's efforts and decided to help him out.

"I can help you get higher, just hop on my back" the crow said.

Tip gratefully accepted the offer and hopped onto the crow's back. The crow rose up higher and higher into the sky and Tip felt like he was on top of the world.

At first, all was going well, until suddenly, the crow plummeted back down to earth. Tip was scared and confused, but he held on as tight as he could.

When Tip and the crow eventually landed, Tip was devastated to discover that the crow had tricked him. He had only offered to give Tip a ride because he wanted his feathers to use in his nest. Tip realized that being reliable couldn't always be trusted.

Mama was sad and miserable, she didn't like to leave home. But one day, Papa encouraged her to go with him. He said they would go find a special spear. Mama didn't understand why they needed a spear, but she trusted Papa. 

So they set off. Mama and Papa walked a long way until they got to a big river. On the other side, Papa showed Mama that there was a big tree with a special spear hanging from its branches. Mama was very excited. 

When the two of them crossed the river, Mama was scared, but Papa encouraged her to be brave. Eventually, Mama made it to the other side of the river. Papa handed her the spear, and it was so beautiful. They smiled at each other, and Mama was no longer feeling so miserable.

Once there was an ugly sack. It was a big, brown sack, and it was so old that it was starting to rip. It wanted to be stylish just like all of the other sacks, but it was too ugly.

So, the sack decided to go on an adventure. It traveled all around, trying to find its style. Everywhere it went, it only found more ugly sacks, nothing that could make it look special.

The sack kept going until it arrived at a big river. It stopped to rest in the sun, when it saw the most beautiful sack it had ever seen! This sack was colored with bright oranges, purples, and blues, and it was sparkling in the sunlight.

The ugly sack knew the other sack was its style. So it asked the other sack to teach it how to be beautiful. The other sack said yes and started to teach the ugly sack all its secrets. Soon, the ugly sack was looking just like the other sack, and it felt so wonderful! 

Now the two sacks travel together, and they can be found walking around the big river. They love showing off their new style and always look so amazing!

Ahmed was very worried on Sunday. He wanted to go to the park and play but his mom said he could not. Ahmed felt very sad and he wanted to shout, but he was worried he might get in trouble.

Suddenly, Ahmed heard music in the distance. He couldn't believe it and he started to run in the direction of the music. He was so excited! As Ahmed got closer he could see a big crowd of people. He had a big smile on his face!

Ahmed ran up to his parents, his mom was holding a banner and his dad was holding a microphone in his hand. Ahmed was confused and his parents told him it was his own birthday party! His family and friends were there shouting for him and giving him presents. Ahmed was so happy he shouted with joy!

Once upon a time there was a boy named Jack. He was only three years old. Jack lived in a big, dark house with his mum and dad. Every night it was time for bed but Jack was always scared of the dark.

Mum tried to help by giving Jack a flashlight. She showed him how to switch it on and off. Jack felt much braver with the flashlight in his hand.

One night Jack woke up in the darkness. He was very frightened and held his flashlight tight. Suddenly, he heard a noise outside. He shone the flashlight at the window and caught sight of something.

It was a big, white bear! Jack was so scared he dropped his flashlight. The bear came closer and closer and then it released a loud roar.

Jack was so scared he couldn't move. Luckily, Dad came running out of his bedroom and chased the bear away. Jack was very relieved and glad to have his flashlight back. From that day on he was never frightened of the dark again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Annie who was three years old. One day, she went outside to play, and when she came back in, she saw something very strange on the rug.

When she leaned in to get a better look, she noticed that it was a tiny little mouse, who seemed very weak and scared.

Annie said hello and asked the mouse what his name was, but the little mouse didn't answer. She asked him again and said she just wanted to be his friend. This time, when she asked the question, he slowly looked up and answered "My name is Max".

Annie smiled and asked if he wanted to play. Max started to smile too and said yes. So, Annie and Max had a fun game of tag on her rug - and every time Annie asked Max a question, he would answer.

The two of them ended up having so much fun that they were having a great time playing together. They even forgot all about how weak and scared Max was when they first met.

They had their own special secret, which was that they were the best of friends.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to speak and play with his friends. One day, Tim found a big, pink gum on the ground. It looked amazing. Tim picked it up and put it in his pocket. He thought, "I will show this to my friends later."

Tim went to the park to play with his friends. He saw them playing and running. Tim took the gum out of his pocket and showed it to his friends. They all wanted to see the amazing gum. Tim told them, "I found it on the ground. It looks amazing, right?" His friends nodded and smiled.

Later, Tim and his friends sat under a big tree. They all looked at the gum and talked about how amazing it was. Then, they decided to share the gum. They broke it into small pieces and each took a piece. They chewed the gum and it was very yummy. They all laughed and spoke about how great the gum was. Tim was happy that he found the amazing gum and could share it with his friends.

One day, Bobby and his mom went to the movies. Bobby was very excited. He saw a big screen, and smelled popcorn. As the movie started, Bobby watched intently. Monsters appeared on the screen, and Bobby was frightened. He grabbed his mom and hid under her arm. 

Then, Bobby noticed that the monsters were getting stuck in popcorn. He laughed, and wasn't scared anymore. He watched the monsters having fun trying to get out of the popcorn. Bobby wanted to help, so he grabbed a handful of popcorn and threw it at the screen. 

Bobby's mom giggled and gave him a hug. Bobby kept watching the movie, excitedly throwing popcorn at the screen each time a monster appeared. He had a great time and wasn't frightened anymore.

Lily and Tom were playing near the old mill. They liked to look at the big wheel that turned the water. They also liked to find stones and sticks and make shapes with them.

But today, the mill was very dusty. The wind blew the dust in their eyes and noses. Lily and Tom started to sneeze.

"Achoo! Achoo!" Lily sneezed.

"Achoo! Achoo!" Tom sneezed.

They rubbed their eyes and noses. They did not like the dust.

"Let's go away from the mill," Lily said. "The dust is too rough."

"OK," Tom said. "Let's go to the meadow. The grass is soft and the flowers are pretty."

They ran away from the mill. They stopped sneezing. They found a nice spot in the meadow. They lay down on the grass and looked at the sky.

They saw clouds and birds and a big sun. They smiled and laughed. They were happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and explore the world around her. One day, she went to the park and met a new friend named Sam. 

"Hi, my name is Lily. What's your name?" Lily asked Sam.

"My name is Sam. Nice to meet you," Sam replied.

Lily showed Sam her favorite toy, a magnet. "This is my magnet. It can stick to metal things," she said.

Sam was amazed. "Wow, that's cool! Can you introduce me to your magnet?" he asked.

Lily smiled and said, "Sure! Let's go play with it in the light." They ran over to a sunny spot and played with the magnet together, watching it stick to different objects. From that day on, Lily and Sam were the best of friends, always exploring and discovering new things together.

Nina and Mikey were excited to go to their new tutor. They had seen their friends go to tutors, so they thought it would be fun to go too. They held their mommy's hand and asked her what they would do.

"A tutor will help you learn things that school can't teach," mommy explained. "You'll be safe and I'm sure you'll have lots of fun!"

When they arrived, the tutor said hello and allowed the kids to choose what to learn. Nina picked a coloring book, and Mikey chose a picture of animals. The tutor asked them questions about the pictures, and Nina and Mikey answered as best as they could. They played games and sang songs, and when it was time to go, they said goodbye to their tutor and thanked her for helping them learn.

Now moms and kids alike feel reassured that the tutor is helping them have a fun and safe learning experience while they stay at home.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Ellie who was 3 years old. 
One day, Ellie was feeling chilly and cold so she decided to find something to keep her warm. She searched all around the house but couldn't find anything.

Suddenly Ellie had a super idea. She remembered seeing a blanket in the wardrobe a few days ago, so she opened it and grabbed it. She wrapped the blanket around her and felt its warmth. It was hot!

Ellie had solved her problem and she was very happy. She felt warm and cozy and had a big smile on her face.

The End.

Once upon a time there was a lucky little girl. Her name was Jane and she was three.

One day she went to school and looked around. The teacher said to her, "Oh, Jane, why don't you come sit at this desk?"

Jane looked at the desk and it was bright and red! She was so excited. She sat down and smiled.

The teacher said, "Let's do a fun activity! I have some lucky stickers and we can put them on the desk!"

Jane said, "Yes!"

So the teacher gave her a sticker. She looked closely at it and it had a picture of a rainbow. She carefully placed it on the desk and smiled.

Then she looked up and said, "Thank you! I'm so lucky to have this desk". 

The teacher smiled back and said, "You're right, Jane. You are very lucky".

Once upon a time there was a little girl who wanted to travel. She looked up at the tall vine growing over her head and decided to climb it. She grabbed onto the vine and began to climb. As she got higher and higher, an old man noticed her and called out to her.

"Where are you going, child?" he asked. 

The little girl grinned. "Up!" she said and kept on climbing. 

The old man chuckled. "You can't reach the sky," he said. "But if you keep going, you'll reach the end of the vine."

So the little girl kept climbing and eventually reached the top of the tall vine. As she looked around, she felt so happy and proud of herself. She took in a deep breath of fresh air and said, "I did it! I traveled the tall vine!"

As she looked around, she knew it was time to go home. She carefully made her way back down the vine until she felt safe to jump down.

The old man was waiting for her with a smile on his face. "You travelled the tall vine bravely," he said.

She smiled and said, "Yep, I did it! It was so fun!" 

The old man said, "That's what adventure is all about. Keep exploring and never stop travelling!"

Once upon a time there was a girl called Sally. She was in a hurry! She wanted to get to school before the bell rang. 

Sally was very excited as she ran. She had a special pencil with her and couldn't wait to show it to her friends. It was unusual because it was blue and sparkly. 

Sally kept running, but she was out of breath. Suddenly, she saw a puddle in the road and jumped over it! Her pencil was still in her hand and she was almost at school. 

Sally reached the front door of school and went in. She showed her friends the unusual pencil, and when the bell rang she was ready for class.

Once upon a time, there was a fireman who was so nice and clean. He always wanted to help people. One day, he saw something glow in the night sky. He knew he had to help, so he grabbed his fire gear and ran. When he arrived, he saw the fire and it was big and orange. He began to work quickly and bravely. He put out the fire and sprinked the ground with water to make sure it was clean. The fireman smiled with happiness, for he had saved the town from the fire. He knew he was helping and it made him feel good.

Once upon a time there was a little boy. He was very enthusiastic and he loved to ride. Every day he would take his bike and go for a ride.

One day, he had a special surprise. He got to ride in a car! He was so excited he couldn't believe it. He climbed into the car and off they went.

The car went quite fast and soon they arrived at a place with lots of people. They all gathered together and the little boy found out they were having a quiz! He was very enthusiastic, he wanted to win!

The quiz started and the little boy rode his bike around the room. He was so determined, and he answered lots of questions. In the end, he got the most answers right and he won the quiz!

He was so happy and his friends cheered for him. He thanked them for coming and for being so enthusiastic. After the quiz, they all went for a ride together. The little boy was so proud of himself and he never forgot this special day.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird. The bird wanted to drink water from the stream. The stream was very clear and the bird liked that. The bird leaned down to drink from the stream. Suddenly, a big gust of wind blew and the bird fell into the stream! The bird was scared, but then a kind frog came and helped the bird out of the stream. From then on, the bird and the frog were friends and they always drank from the clear stream together.

One day, a leopard was walking through the forest. He was walking very slow, so he couldn't see where he was going. Suddenly, he stopped to look around. He was a bit worried because he was lost.

He heard a voice. "Hello there!" said the voice. The leopard looked around and saw a little rabbit.

The leopard was happy to see someone. He said, "Do you know where I am?". The rabbit frowned, because he did not know the answer.

The leopard felt sad. He slowly walked away, looking for someone who could help him. Finally, he heard another voice. It was Birdie!

Birdie said, "Hey there, Leopard! I know where you are! Follow me!" The leopard was relieved and quickly followed Birdie.

He noticed that Birdie was hopping very fast, so he had to run to keep up. Soon, he was back at home, safe and sound. He smiled and thanked Birdie for his help.

Once upon a time, there was a messy house. It had books and toys everywhere! Every day, the family in that house would feed the fish in the tank. They also looked at pictures of family and friends. Then, one day, Grandpa visited and wanted to talk. He told stories about when he was a boy. The kids were excited to learn some history. However, the stories were a bit dull! So, the kids decided to go play instead. They had so much fun that they soon forgot about the boring stories! 

The End.

Once upon a time, there was a bee. The bee liked to fly around and collect nectar from flowers. One day, the bee saw a flower that looked very interesting. The bee flew over to the flower and started to collect nectar. 

But then, another bee came along and wanted to collect nectar from the same flower. The two bees started to quarrel and buzzed loudly at each other. They both wanted the nectar from the interesting flower. 

The quarrel between the two bees got louder and louder. Suddenly, a bird swooped down and caught one of the bees in its beak. The other bee flew away quickly, feeling sad and scared. From then on, the bee learned to share the flowers and never quarreled with other bees again.

Once upon a time, there was a very high tree. At the top of the tree was a beautiful flower pot. Inside the pot was a special ink that glowed in the dark. Every night, the ink would twinkle like the stars in the sky.

One day, a little bird flew up to the top of the tree and pecked inside the flower pot. He found some of the glowing ink and used it to make his feathers twinkle. Soon, all of the birds in the sky had glowing feathers!

The people below noticed the glowing birds and were so amazed that they started to use the ink to make all kinds of things twinkle. They used it to make their houses glow, their trees glow and even their clothes. Everything twinkled and it was so beautiful.

The glowing ink made the world a much brighter and happier place. It was like a special magic that made everything around it shimmer and shine with joy.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Mia went for a walk. She saw a shiny copper coin on the ground. Mia thought it was perfect. She grabbed the coin and put it in her pocket.

Mia met her friend Tom. She showed him the perfect copper coin. Tom said, "Wow, that's pretty! Can I hold it?" Mia said, "Sure!" Tom grabbed the coin and looked at it closely.

Mia and Tom played with the copper coin all day. They took turns grabbing it and pretending it was treasure. When the sun went down, they said goodbye and went home. Mia kept the perfect copper coin as a special memory of their fun day.

Once upon a time there was a clumsy girl. One day, she was playing in the snow and wearing some warm mittens. She loved to make snowballs. But when she threw them, she forgot about her mittens and one flew away. She was sad to lose her mitten and didn't know how to find it.

So, she asked her friend to help. Together, they searched for the lost mitten. Finally, they found it in a snow bank! The girl was so happy to get her mitten back. She promised to be more careful next time. 

Then, they went back to playing in the snow. The girl never lost her mitten again!

Once there was a baby bear who was very worried. He was worried because he had heard that two big bears were going to fight. He didn't want them to get hurt. He was so worried that he couldn't even take a nap.

Then suddenly, two kind rabbits hopped over to the bears and talked to them. The rabbits told the bears that they should not fight because it would make them both sad. The bears listened to the rabbits and decided to become friends instead.

The baby bear was so relieved that the fight did not happen. He had been so worried that he could now happily take a nap. He stretched out on a soft bed of leaves and closed his eyes, feeling calm and relaxed. 

The baby bear and the two friendly bears became friends and promised each other that they would never fight with each other again. From then on, they would only be kind and giving. The baby bear smiled and settled down for another nap.

Once upon a time, there was a little bear named Benny. Benny was feeling troubled because he couldn't find his favorite toy. He looked under his bed, in his toy chest, and even in the garden, but he couldn't find it anywhere.

Benny's mom noticed that he was feeling sad and asked him what was wrong. "I can't find my toy," Benny said with a frown. "Don't worry," said his mom, "let's go pick some flowers and that will make you feel better."

So, they went to the garden and picked some pretty flowers. Benny's mom gave him a big hug and said, "I love you, even without your toy." Benny smiled and hugged his mom back, feeling much better. From that day on, Benny learned that sometimes a hug and some flowers can make everything better.

Once there was a boy named Lee. He was very excited because today was his exam. He put on his nice clothes and went to the exam center. When he got there, it was very cold. He hugged his arms around himself and shivered.

Just then, he heard a voice. It was the teacher who was giving him the exam. "Lee," she said, "Today you will put your skills to the test. Are you ready?"

Lee nodded. The teacher smiled and gave him some paper and pencils. Lee looked at them and then began his exam. He worked hard, concentrating on each question and carefully writing down his answers. After a while, the teacher said, "Time's up. You can put your pencils away now."

Lee put the pencils down on the table and the teacher smiled at him. "That was very good," she said.

Lee grinned and thanked the teacher. He had worked hard and passed his exam. Now he could go home, happy and proud.

Once upon a time, there was a clever little dog named Max. Max loved to swing on the big tree in his yard. One day, Max's friend, a cat named Luna, came for a visit. They played together and had lots of fun.

One day, while Max and Luna were swinging, they saw a big bird. The bird wanted to swing too, but it was too big for the tree. Max and Luna felt sad for the bird. They thought of a plan to help the bird swing.

Max and Luna found a bigger tree for the bird to swing on. The bird was so happy and thanked Max and Luna for being so clever. They all played together and had a great time. And from that day on, Max, Luna, and the bird became best friends.

Once upon a time, there was a family of birds. They lived in a tree and had a view of the big, blue sky.

One day, the mama bird said to her four babies, â€œListen carefully! I want you to attach yourselves to the law!â€

The four little birds looked at each other with ignorant eyes, not understanding what she meant.

Mama bird went on, â€œThe law is something that everyone must obey. When you attach yourselves to it, no one will be able to hurt you.â€

The four little birds nodded in unison and chirped, â€œYes, Mama Bird!â€ 

Mama Bird smiled and said, â€œGood! Now you know the law and you can always keep it near your heart.â€

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she was playing with her toys when she heard a loud noise. She looked out the window and saw a big, scary dog. Lily was frightened and ran to her mom. 

"Mommy, I'm scared!" Lily cried. 

"It's okay, sweetie," her mom said, picking her up. "Let's go inside and I'll make you some cookies." 

Lily felt better and went to the kitchen with her mom. While her mom was cutting the cookies, Lily touched her ear and said, "Mommy, my ear hurts." 

Her mom looked at her ear and saw a little scratch. She put a band-aid on it and gave Lily a cookie. Lily smiled and forgot all about the scary dog.

Billy had a lemon. It was yellow and round. He wanted to stay with it so he held it tight. He put it in the fridge to keep it cool. He stayed with it for a long time. He bounced the lemon on the floor. It bounced very high. Then he squeezed it. The lemon was very tight. He squirted some of the juice onto his face. It felt cold and wet. Billy liked the feeling. The lemon made him smile. He tried to stay with it forever.

Lily and Ben were going to the park with their mom. They were very happy because it was a sunny day and they liked to play on the swings and slides. Mom told them to put on their hats and sunscreen to protect their skin from the sun.

"Mom, can I wear your sunglasses?" Lily asked. She liked how mom's sunglasses looked on her face. They were big and shiny and made everything look cool.

"Sure, Lily, you can wear them, but be careful not to lose them. They are very important to me. They remind me of your dad. He gave them to me as a gift before he went away," mom said. She smiled and kissed Lily on the cheek.

Lily nodded and put on the sunglasses. She felt very grown-up and special. She held mom's hand as they walked to the park. Ben ran ahead, excited to see the other kids and the toys.

At the park, Lily and Ben had a lot of fun. They swung on the swings, slid on the slides, and chased each other on the grass. Lily forgot about the sunglasses and left them on a bench when she went to get some water. She did not see a big dog that came and sniffed the bench. The dog liked the smell of the sunglasses and picked them up with his mouth. He ran away with them, wagging his tail.

"Hey, that's my mom's sunglasses!" Ben shouted. He saw the dog running away with the sunglasses. He was a good brother and a reliable friend. He ran after the dog, trying to get the sunglasses back.

"Ben, wait!" Lily cried. She realized she had lost the sunglasses and felt very bad. She was afraid mom would be sad and angry. She ran after Ben, hoping he could catch the dog.

Mom saw what happened and followed them. She was worried about her kids and her sunglasses. She hoped they would be safe and find the dog.

Will they get the sunglasses back? How will mom react? What will they learn from this adventure? You can continue the story or end it here.

Once there was a girl named Anna who loved to wear silly clothes. One day she put on a fun green skirt with yellow stripes. She twirled and danced around in the skirt and it looked so silly! 

Anna decided to go outside and show her skirt to her friends. When she got to the park she waved at her friends, "Look at my skirt!" she said.

All her friends started to laugh, but then one boy named Sam said, "Why are you wearing that silly skirt?"

Anna stood up tall and said, "I like my skirt and I want to show it off!"

Sam smiled and said, "I think your skirt is nice. You look very happy in it."

Anna smiled and twirled around again in her skirt, she knew she looked silly but she didn't care. She was proud of her skirt and happy to show it off.

Lily was very happy. Today was her birthday. She had a party with her friends. They played games, ate cake and opened presents. Lily got a big doll from her mom and dad. She loved her doll very much.

But then, something bad happened. Lily saw Sam, her best friend, playing with her doll. She got angry. She ran to Sam and shouted, "That's mine! Give it back!" She grabbed the doll and pulled hard. Sam pulled back. They both fell down. The doll broke. Its head came off.

Lily and Sam started to cry. Their moms and dads came to see what was wrong. They saw the broken doll and the sad children. They felt sorry for them. They tried to fix the doll, but it was too late. The doll was gone.

Lily's mom hugged her and said, "I'm sorry, honey. I know you loved your doll. But you shouldn't have fought with Sam. He is your friend. He wanted to play with your doll, not hurt it. You need to say sorry to him."

Lily looked at Sam. He was still crying. He looked at her with his big eyes. He said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I didn't mean to break your doll. I liked your doll. I wanted to share it with you. Can we still be friends?"

Lily felt a warm feeling in her heart. She remembered that Sam was her best friend. He always made her laugh. He always shared his toys with her. He was nice to her. She said, "I'm sorry, too, Sam. I was mean to you. I should have let you play with my doll. You are my friend. I still like you."

Lily and Sam hugged each other. They stopped crying. They smiled. Their moms and dads smiled, too. They were happy that Lily and Sam made up. They said, "That's good, kids. You are good friends. Friends say sorry when they make mistakes. Friends forgive each other. Friends have fun together."

Lily and Sam nodded. They agreed. They went back to the party. They played with the other toys. They ate more cake. They had fun. They forgot about the broken doll. They remembered their friendship.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Rose who liked to explore outside. Everyday, Rose's mom would warn her not to wander too far away. One day, Rose went further than her mom had said and she came across a big bush. 

Curious, Rose decided to wander inside. Once she got deep in the bush, it was very noisy with all of the animals chirping and buzzing in the air. Rose was so excited to explore more, but then she heard her mom's voice calling to her from far away. 

Startled, Rose ran out of the bush towards her mom's voice. When she reached her mom, Rose felt a bit scared because she knew her mom must be mad. But her mom just said "I warned you to not wander too far, but I'm glad you're safe". Rose was so relieved and learned a lesson that it is important to always listen to her mom.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He loved playing hockey with his friends. They would play every day after school in the park.

One day, Timmy's mom bought him a new hockey stick. It was very soft and he loved it. He couldn't wait to use it in their next game.

When Timmy arrived at the park, he saw that his friends were already there. They were all playing with their old sticks. Timmy was excited to show his new stick to his friends.

As they started playing, Timmy's new stick suddenly broke into two parts. He was sad that he couldn't play anymore. But his friends were kind and shared their sticks with him. From that day on, Timmy learned that it's not about having the best equipment, but about having fun with your friends.

One day, Mary was in the park playing with her friends. They were running and laughing and having a lot of fun. Suddenly, Mary saw something blinking across the park. It was at the end of a row of trees.

She walked over to it and saw it was a funny looking bird! It had a blue head, a yellow body and pink legs. Every time it blinked its eyes, it made the biggest, brightest light. It was amazing!

Mary reached out to touch it and it flew away. She watched it fly across the park, and it started blinking again at the end of the row of trees. She tried to follow, but it was too fast!

Mary had so much fun watching the funny blinking bird. She was sad it flew away, but maybe one day she'd see it again.

Jimmy was playing with his truck in the backyard. He was having a lot of fun, pushing it around and making engine noises. But then he started to feel tired and he yawned. His careless behavior had made him tired and he was ready for a nap. He carefully put his truck away and headed inside. He went to his room and lay on his bed and quickly fell asleep. 

Jimmy's truck stayed outside in the backyard, waiting for him to play with it again. The sun was going down, so the truck waited until the morning when Jimmy woke up. He yawned as he stepped out of his room and stretched. Excited to play with his truck, he quickly ran to the backyard. With a huge smile on his face, he ran out into the sunshine and began playing with his truck for the day.

Sara and Ben were twins who liked to play outside. They had a big yard with a swing, a slide and a sandbox. One day, they decided to make a cake with sand and water. They mixed and poured and shaped the sand in a big pan. Then they put it on the slide to bake in the sun.

"It will be a yummy cake," Sara said. "We can share it with Mom and Dad."

"Yes, and with Fluffy too," Ben said. Fluffy was their cat who liked to nap under the tree.

They gazed at their cake with pride. It looked so good and brown. They waited and waited for it to be ready. But the sun was very hot and made them thirsty and tired. They went to get some juice and cookies from the kitchen.

When they came back, they saw Fluffy licking their cake. He had climbed on the slide and dug his paws in the sand. He made a big mess and ruined their cake.

"Fluffy, no!" Sara and Ben shouted. They ran to the slide and tried to shoo him away. But Fluffy was faster and jumped off the slide. He ran away with a piece of sand cake in his mouth.

Sara and Ben were very sad and angry. They had worked so hard to make their cake. They wanted to be successful and make their parents happy. But Fluffy had spoiled their plan.

They looked at each other and hugged. They decided to try again another day. They cleaned up the slide and the pan and the sand. They hoped Fluffy would not come back and ruin their cake again. They learned that sometimes things go wrong, but they can always try again.

Once upon a time there was a small boy who loved to look up at the sky. He looked up at it every day and watched as the clouds moved by.

One day he saw something he had never seen before. Two clouds were quarreling with each other as they drifted through the sky! The boy was very surprised and he watched as the small clouds bumped and banged against each other.

All of a sudden, the little boy heard a loud noise from the sky. He looked up to see that the two clouds had made up and were now smiling at each other.

The small boy smiled and waved to the clouds. He was happy to see that the two clouds had made up after all. He couldn't wait to tell his friends about what he had seen!

Once upon a time there was a strong princess. She lived in a tall castle made of white stone. Each day, the princess would ride her horse to explore the land.

One day, the princess arrived at a dark cave. She heard a strange noise coming from inside. It sounded like someone was in trouble.

The princess bravely stepped inside the cave. She saw a dragon in the corner. "HELP!" yelled the dragon. The princess ran over to see what was wrong.

The dragon had a heavy chest attached to his back. The chest was so tight and the lock wouldn't open. The princess saw the dragon was in pain.

The princess tried to open the lock with her sword. After many tries, she couldn't do it. She knew she had to find a way to help the dragon.

The princess had an idea. She gently urged the dragon to take a deep breath. As the dragon did, the chest suddenly opened. 

The dragon thanked the princess with a warm smile. He explained that the chest was full of harsh jewels. He was glad to be free of the heavy burden.

The princess and the dragon became friends. They hugged goodbye and the brave princess returned to her castle.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily who loved to wear her purple hat. One day, she went to the park to play with her friends. She put her hat on the bench and started playing. 

Suddenly, a gust of wind blew and her hat disappeared! Lily started to cry and her friends asked what was wrong. "My hat is gone," she said sadly. 

"Don't worry, we'll help you find it," said her friend Jack. They searched high and low, but the hat was nowhere to be found. Just when they were about to give up, a little bird flew down and brought Lily her purple hat back. Lily was so happy and thanked the bird. From that day on, she never took her hat off again.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tim. Tim loved to race his toy cars on the floor. He had a red car, a blue car, and a green car. One day, Tim went to the beach with his family. He played in the sand and splashed in the tide. 

Tim saw some other kids racing on the beach. He wanted to join in, so he grabbed his red car and started to race. But the tide was coming in fast, and Tim didn't notice. Suddenly, a big wave came and took Tim and his car out to sea. 

Tim's family searched for him, but they couldn't find him. They were sad and cried a lot. They knew Tim was an honest boy who loved to race, but the tide was too strong. Tim was never seen again.

Jane was a young girl, with long brown hair and bright blue eyes. Today she was feeling a bit sad, so she put on her favourite yellow dress and went outside to see if it would make her feel better.

As she walked, she noticed a very wealthy man living in a big, white house, with a big fence and a swimming pool. Jane wondered what it must be like to be so rich and feel so lucky. She thought about it for a minute, then shrugged her shoulders; she knew she wasn't that wealthy.

Then she noticed a bright yellow flower growing in the garden. She smiled and ran over to it. She plucked the flower from the ground and held it up to smell it. The sweet smell made Jane feel happy again!

With her flower in hand, Jane ran home and put it in a jar by the window sill. From now on, the yellow flower would be her reminder of the joy she can feel no matter what life brings her way.

Once upon a time, there was a little child named Timmy. Timmy was playing in his backyard when he saw a big truck. The truck was there to load some boxes. Timmy was curious about the boxes and went closer to see what was inside.

Suddenly, a loud noise scared Timmy. He looked up and saw a big forklift. The forklift was moving the boxes into the truck. Timmy was frightened and ran back to his house.

From his window, Timmy watched the truck drive away. He felt happy that he wasn't near the big forklift anymore. Timmy learned that it's important to be careful around big machines.

Sara and Tom are brother and sister. They like to play in the garden. Sara is four and Tom is three. They have a big ball and a small car.

One day, they see a hole in the fence. They are curious. They want to know what is on the other side. They crawl through the hole. They see a big dog. The dog is brown and fluffy. It has a red collar.

"Hello, doggy!" Sara says. "Do you want to play with us?"

The dog wags its tail. It likes Sara and Tom. It runs to them and licks their faces. They giggle. They throw the ball and the dog fetches it. They push the car and the dog chases it. They have fun.

But then they hear their mom calling. "Sara! Tom! Where are you? It's time to come in and have a bath!"

They look at each other. They are dirty. They have mud on their clothes and their faces. The dog has mud on its fur and its collar.

"Uh-oh," Tom says. "We have to go, doggy. Bye-bye!"

They crawl back through the hole. They run to their mom. She sees them and gasps.

"What have you been doing?" she asks. "You are not clean at all! You need a bath right now!"

Sara and Tom nod. They are sorry. They hug their mom. They say goodbye to the dog. They hope they can play with it again. They go inside and have a bath. They wash the mud off. They become clean again. They are happy.

Jack and Jill were best friends. Jack wanted to show Jill an exciting surprise so he sent her a letter. In the letter it said that he was going on a rich jog. Jill was so excited when she heard this news, so she ran out of the house and hurried over to Jack. 

When she arrived, her eyes lit up with joy when she saw that Jack was wearing a brand new running outfit. He explained to her that he was going on a jog around a nearby park owned by a rich family. She was so happy that she decided to join him!

The two friends enjoyed their jog as they chatted and exchanged stories. When they finished, they were both exhausted, but they had a lot of fun and were very happy they were able to spend time together. They hugged each other goodbye and promised to go on a jog together soon.

Once upon a time, there was a big dragon. The dragon was very nice. He lived in a big forest. One day, he met a small girl. The girl was lost and scared.

The dragon wanted to help the girl. He said, "Trust me, I will take you home." The girl trusted the dragon. She climbed on his back, and they flew through the sky.

Soon, they found the girl's home. The girl was very grateful to the dragon. She gave him a big hug. From that day on, the dragon and the girl were the best of friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to read books. Her mommy had a big bookcase in her room. It was very deep and had many books in it.

One day, Lily wanted to read a book from the bookcase. But she was too short to reach it. So, she asked her mommy to pick her up. Her mommy picked her up and she was able to get the book she wanted.

Lily was very happy because she loved to read. She read the book all by herself and it made her feel very grown up. From that day on, she would ask her mommy to pick her up whenever she wanted to read a book from the deep bookcase.
