They run to their houses with the camera. They are lively and happy. They show their parents the pictures. Their parents are surprised and proud.

"Where did you find the camera?" Mom asks.

"In the park," Lily says. "Can we keep it?"

Mom and Dad look at each other. They do not know who owns the camera. They decide to call the park office and ask.

"Maybe someone lost it and is looking for it," Dad says. "We should try to find them and give it back."

Lily and Tom are sad. They like the camera. But they also want to be good and honest.

"Okay," they say. "But can we use it one more time?"

Mom and Dad agree. They let Lily and Tom use the camera again. They take more pictures of themselves and their parents. They have fun. They hope the camera will find its owner. And they hope they will make a new friend.

The new pilot felt excited. She was finally going to fly her first plane! She put on her pilot hat and buckle her seatbelt.

"Ready for take-off?" asked Grandpa. He was coming along with her today.

"Yes!" She smiled.

The plane began to move. Faster and faster it went until it left the ground. The pilot felt happy.

"Woah, look at that!" said Grandpa, pointing down. The pilot looked and saw big farms, houses and a river.

"Look! We can wave to the people," Grandpa said. The pilot waved to the people below and smiled.

The plane flew for a while until it was time to land. Grandpa and the pilot felt proud.

"That was awesome!" said Grandpa.

"Yes," said the happy pilot, "flying a plane is the best!"

Once there was a girl named Playful who was three years old. She was a curious and adventurous child and she loved exploring new places.

One day, Playful noticed a beautiful clock in her grandmotherâ€™s house. She had never seen one before and she was really excited to take a closer look. She looked at the clock carefully and saw the big round face, the two hands that were pointing at different numbers and the beautiful chimes that sounded when it was time for something to happen.

Playful was so excited that she wanted to try the clock. She held the clock in her hands but it felt uncomfortable and soon she put it back. Playful then said goodbye to her grandmother, but not before looking back at the clock one last time.

Ben and Mia are friends. They like to play at the zoo. They see many animals. They see lions, monkeys, and birds. But their favorite animal is the hippo. The hippo is big and gray. He lives in the water.

One day, it is very cold. The water is icy. Ben and Mia go to see the hippo. But they do not see him. They only see ice. Where is the hippo? They are sad.

"Maybe he is hiding under the ice," Ben says.

"Maybe he is sleeping," Mia says.

"Maybe he is cold and lonely," Ben says.

They want to help the hippo. They have a plan. They run to the gift shop. They buy a big scarf. It is red and warm. They run back to the hippo's pool. They see a hole in the ice. They see the hippo's nose. He is breathing.

"Hello, hippo!" Ben and Mia shout. "We have a gift for you!"

They throw the scarf over the ice. The hippo sees it. He is curious. He pushes his head out of the hole. He grabs the scarf with his mouth. He wraps it around his neck. He looks happy.

"Thank you, Ben and Mia!" the hippo says. "You are very kind. You made me warm and cozy."

Ben and Mia smile. They are happy too. They wave to the hippo. They go to play with other animals. They are good friends.

Once upon a time there was a generous fireman. He was always out and about, helping people in need. One day, the fireman was travelling around town when he spotted a little 3 year old boy. The boy was sad and alone. The generous fireman wanted to make the boy feel better, so he asked if he could sign. The 3 year old nodded and followed the fireman to an open field.

The fireman reached into his pocket and pulled out a piece of paper. He started to trace a big smiley face on the paper, and when he was done the boy laughed. He was so happy that the fireman had taken the time to make him smile.

The 3 year old boy thanked the generous fireman and pointed to the sky. The fireman lifted his head and saw a bright rainbow stretching across the sky. The fireman smiled back and waved goodbye as he made his way off into the sunset. The little 3 year old boy watched him go, and he smiled, knowing that he had been helped by a generous fireman.

The little girl gazed up at the palace. Its tall walls and spires seemed like something out of a dream. She could almost imagine herself as a princess in that magical place.

But when she tried to go inside she felt a bit uncomfortable. Walking around such grand and fancy rooms made her feel like she didn't belong.

So the little girl stayed outside. She ran around the gardens, played in the fountain, and hugged the trees. She was more comfortable being out of the palace.

At the end of the day she took one last look at the palace, taking it all in with one last gaze. Then she ran off, eager to come back to the palace when she was a bit older.

Molly and her mommy were walking very quickly. Molly was holding her mommy's hand and giggling. The sun was bright and the air was chilly.

"Where are we going, Mommy?" asked Molly.

"We're going to find your tutor," said Mommy, hurrying her along.

Molly was excited and asked, "What is a tutor?"

"A tutor is someone who helps you learn," said Mommy, squeezing her hand.

The two hurried down the icy sidewalk until they reached a large building. Molly gasped in surprise. "Mommy, what is this place?"

"This is where your tutor works," said Mommy, a smile playing at the corners of her mouth. "Let's go in and say hello!"

Molly and her mommy hurried into the building, smiling and laughing. Molly was so excited to meet her tutor. She was going to learn lots of new things today!

Once upon a time there was a white spoon. The spoon was very lonely, but then one day, an amazing thing happened. From the spoon, a flower began to bloom. The flower was so beautiful, with leaves of green and petals of pink. The spoon was so proud and couldn't believe it was able to make something so wonderful!

All the animals in the forest stopped to admire the flower: the birds sang, the rabbits hopped, the beavers tumbled. They were all so amazed!

Then, something even more special happened. All of a sudden, the flower started to sparkle with magical silver stars. "Look!" said the little spoon, "I made something so special!" 

The spoon smiled and hugged the flower, and the magical silver stars twinkled in the air. The spoon and the flower were so happy, and the spoon knew that it would never be lonely again. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. He loved to run and play outside. One day, he saw his mom worry about something. Timmy asked her what was wrong, and she said she was worried about the bills. Timmy didn't want his mom to worry, so he decided to help. 

He went outside and jogged around the neighborhood, looking for ways to earn money. He helped an old lady carry her groceries and she gave him a dollar. He picked up trash in the park and a man gave him two dollars. Timmy was happy that he could help his mom and make some money at the same time. 

When he got home, he gave his mom the money and she was very grateful. Timmy felt proud of himself for being helpful and not selfish. From that day on, he always looked for ways to help others and make a difference in his community.

Once upon a time, there was a boy. He was so small that he couldn't reach the ceiling. His name was Tom and he loved to have fun.

One day, Tom's mom gave him a big blue box. He was so excited. He could carry it all around the room. He asked what was in it and she said it was a surprise.

Tom was curious, so he opened the box. Inside it was a blue nose. He thought it looked so funny. He carried the nose around the house with him.

Tom had a lot of fun with his blue nose. Everywhere he went, he would carry his nose with him. He would show it to everyone and make them laugh. Tom loved his blue nose.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Tom and Lucy. Tom had a big, nice sweater on. He loved it very much. 

One day, Lucy asked Tom "Can I have your sweater?"

But Tom said "No, I like it too much!"

But Lucy said "Please, Tom! I'm so cold!"

Tom thought hard then he said "Okay, you can wear my sweater but tell me when you want to give it back!"

So Lucy put on Tom's sweater and said "Thank you Tom!"

Lucy was so happy and so warm in the nice sweater.

But after a while, Tom asked "Can I have my sweater back, please?"

And Lucy said "Yes, I surrender it to you!" 

Tom was happy and said "Thank you for being so nice, Lucy!" and he put on his sweater.

And they both lived happily ever after.

Once there was a little caterpillar who wanted to go for a walk. He crawled along a path and eventually he came across a big, juicy bubble. He wanted to get closer so he kept crawling and crawled and crawled until he was right next to it. The caterpillar wanted to pop it but he was too frightened. He looked around, but there was nobody to help him. The caterpillar was stuck! 

He thought for a moment, and then he decided to try wiggling his way into the bubble. He inched very slowly and carefully until he was inside it. Now he was safe, like he was in his own little world! He wriggled around until he was tired and he curled up and went to sleep. 

The next morning, the sun rose and the bubble popped. The caterpillar was so startled he jumped and scurried away, never to be seen again.

Lily and Ben are playing in the park. They see a big bottle on the grass. It is green and shiny. Lily wants to see what is inside. She runs to the bottle and picks it up.

"Look, Ben, look!" she says. "It has water and bubbles!"

Ben comes closer and looks at the bottle. He sees the water and bubbles too. He thinks they are pretty. He wants to touch them.

"Can I poke them?" he asks Lily.

Lily nods and gives him the bottle. Ben pokes the bottle with his finger. He feels the water and the bubbles. They are wet and cold. He giggles.

"Poke, poke, poke!" he says.

Lily giggles too. She pokes the bottle with her finger. She feels the water and the bubbles. They are wet and cold. She likes them.

"Poke, poke, poke!" she says.

They poke the bottle together. They have fun. They make the water and the bubbles move. They make sounds with their mouths. They are happy.

They are nice friends. They share the bottle. They play with the water and the bubbles. They poke, poke, poke.

Once upon a time there was a man who was sad. He wanted to escape from his sadness so he decided to pray. He closed his eyes, looked up to the sky and said "Please, show me a way to feel good again". Suddenly, he felt a fresh breeze on his face. He opened his eyes and saw a big sky full of beauty. He smiled and knew that everything would be alright. He took a deep breath and prayed with a light heart. His prayers were heard and he was able to escape from his sadness. He felt good again. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sue. Sue lived in a small house with her mom, dad, and her cat, Fluffy. One day, Sue was playing with Fluffy in her room. She saw a broken toy on the floor. "Oh no, Fluffy! My toy is broken," Sue said.

Sue's mom heard her and came into the room. She saw the broken toy and the light from the window shining on it. "Sue, let's cover the toy with a cloth and put it away," Mom said. "We can fix it later." Sue nodded and covered the broken toy with a soft cloth.

The next day, Sue's dad fixed the broken toy. Sue learned that it is important to take care of her things and ask for help when needed. She also learned that sometimes, things can be fixed if we are patient and work together.

Once upon a time there was a wild stove. It was so wild that it grew bigger every single day. One day, the stove grew so tall that it reached up to the sky. At this point, it was so tall that it could no longer fit inside the house. 

The stove was so wild, that it decided to move away to explore the world. So, it climbed over the hills and through the forest. Everywhere it went, the wild stove grew bigger and bigger.

Soon the stove became so big that it stopped growing. It was so wild that it just stayed outside the house, enjoying the world around it.

The wild stove lived happily outside for the rest of it life, growing bigger and bigger as time passed.

Once upon a time, there was a gentle horse named Brownie. Brownie loved to run and play in the fields. One day, Brownie was playing when he got a thorn in his hoof. The thorn hurt Brownie and he couldn't walk.

Brownie was sad and scared. He didn't want to be stuck in the field all alone. But then, a little girl came along. She saw Brownie and knew she had to help. The girl gently took the thorn out of Brownie's hoof and gave him a hug.

Brownie was so happy! He could walk again and play in the fields. Brownie and the little girl became friends and had lots of fun together. They played games and went on adventures. Brownie was grateful that the little girl helped him when he needed it.

Once there were two brothers, named Tim and Jamie. Tim was older, and Jamie liked to follow him around all the time. Whenever Tim asked him to do something, he always said yes!

One day, Tim told Jamie to join him for an adventure. Jamie was so excited. They were about to embark on their biggest journey yet.

At first it was fun, but then it got harder. The sun started to shine brighter, and the ground seemed to freeze. Finally they reached their destination: an operation. It was terrible. 

Jamie wanted to turn back, but Tim insisted they continue. He was determined to finish what they had started. 

So they went into the terrible operation and froze. Moments later, they heard a loud noise that sounded like all of their dreams coming true. Suddenly, Tim took out a key and opened the door â€” they had done it! 

The brothers had completed their mission, and now Jamie knew that his big brother was truly brave and forever dependable.

Sam and Mia were playing in the backyard. They found a can of spray and a lighter. They did not know what they were, but they looked fun.

"Let's spray this on the grass and make a flame!" Sam said.

"OK, but be careful!" Mia said.

Sam shook the can and pressed the button. A mist came out of the can. He moved the lighter near the mist and clicked it. A big flame burst out of the mist and made a loud noise.

"Wow, look at that!" Sam said.

But the flame was too big and too hot. It spread to the grass and the flowers. It reached the fence and the tree. It made more noise and more smoke.

"Help, help!" Mia screamed.

She ran to the house and called for Mom and Dad. Sam dropped the can and the lighter and followed her. He was scared and sorry.

Mom and Dad came out of the house and saw the fire. They were angry and worried. They called the firemen and tried to put out the fire with the hose.

The firemen came with a big truck and a loud siren. They wore helmets and coats. They used a big hose and a lot of water. They put out the fire and checked the damage.

They talked to Mom and Dad and Sam and Mia. They told them that the spray and the lighter were very dangerous and should not be played with. They told them that they were lucky that no one was hurt, but that they had to pay for the damage.

Mom and Dad were very sad and very mad. They hugged Sam and Mia and told them that they loved them, but that they had to learn a lesson. They took away their toys and their TV and their snacks. They made them do chores and say sorry.

Sam and Mia felt very bad and very ashamed. They wished they had never played with the spray and the lighter. They wished they had listened to Mom and Dad. They learned that fire was not a game, but a flame that could hurt and destroy.

One day, Mom and Dad went outside to look at their lawn. The grass was an ugly yellow color, so Dad was sad. He began to tear at the grass with his fingers. After he was done, the lawn looked much better. Mom and Dad were so happy! 

They began to plant some plants and mom put in some pretty yellow flowers. Dad put in some rocks to make it look nicer. The lawn was beginning to look beautiful.

The next day, something strange happened. Mom and Dad found the lawn covered in ugly brown weeds! Dad was so angry that he started to tear out the weeds. Soon enough, the weeds were gone, but the lawn was very messy. 

Mom and dad worked hard to clean up the lawn and make it look nice again. After lots of work, they finally managed to make the lawn look beautiful and green. They were so happy to see the beautiful lawn!

Once upon a time there was a boy named Sam. He didn't like to learn very much in school and he often frowned when it came to doing his schoolwork. Then one day his parents decided they would hire a tutor to help him. 

The tutor came over every day and taught Sam new words, numbers and letters. Sam started to feel happier and more normal when it came to school.

One day when the tutor came over, she brought something special. It was a book filled with puzzles and games. Sam smiled and the tutor taught him how to play the different games. He started loving numbers and letters more and more.

At the end of the week, Sam smiled when he got all of his schoolwork done correctly. He knew that the tutor helped him get better at school and he was so happy. It made him think of the future and how much he would learn if he kept getting help from the tutor.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys every day. One day, she found a playful puppy in her yard. Lily wanted to play with the puppy, but the puppy was too small and couldn't lift its paw.

Lily said, "I wish you could play with me, little puppy."

The puppy barked and said, "I want to play too, but I can't lift my paw."

Lily thought for a moment and said, "I have an idea! Let's play catch with this ball. You can use your nose to push it to me."

The puppy was excited and they played catch for hours. They became best friends and played together every day. Lily learned that even if someone can't do something, there is always a way to have fun and play together.

Every day, Dan ran as fast as he could. He ran past the trees, the flowers, and the armchair by the window. Dan wanted so badly to play in the armchair. He tried to reach it but he was just too small.

One day when Dan was running, he noticed something. The armchair was closer to him than before. He reached as far as he could and his fingers touched the armchair. He was so happy that he could finally play with it.

Dan played in the armchair every day at the same time. He wiggled and bounced in his regular way. One day, when he was playing in the armchair, the armchair tilted and wobbled. Dan was so scared that he slipped out and he fell to the ground. He hurt his arm and started to cry. 

Dan learned his lesson that day. The armchair wasn't meant for him to play in, no matter how much he wanted to. He had to stay away, no matter how close it seemed.

Once upon a time there was a blueberry. It was so blue and pretty. One day, the blueberry started to change. It got bigger and bigger. 

One sunny morning, a 3 year old child found the big blueberry. She was so excited that her eyes lit up. She picked it up and slowly put it in her pocket.

The child walked home very carefully. She was careful to not drop the blueberry on the ground. 

When she got home, she showed the blueberry to her mom. They put it in a bowl and the mom put some ice cream and whipped cream on top. 

The child was so happy. She ate the blueberry with a big smile on her face. The blueberry was the best ever!

Once there was a little girl named Judy. She tried on lots of pretty dresses in the store. One dress was pink and she loved it so much. But it was very expensive.

Suddenly, a selfish lady came and bought the dress before Judy could. Judy was very sad. She wanted the pink dress so badly!

The lady felt bad and wanted to make it right, so she gave Judy another dress. It was not pink but she liked it too. Judy was so happy!

She used a stick to twirl around and the dress made a beautiful swirl. Suddenly, Judy fell on the ground. She was not hurt, but her dress was dirty. Judy was sad, but she knew she could wash the dress and wear it again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to draw and color. One day, she drew a picture of a silly monster. She showed it to her mom and said, "Look at my creative monster!"

Dad said, "Wow, Lily! You're so creative! What's the result of your monster's silly joke?"

Once upon a time, there were two best friends named Lucy and Amy. They were both very poor and they struggled to find food every day. 

Amy and Lucy decided to go in search of something to eat. But as they walked around the village, they just couldn't find anything. They were so hungry and so tired. 

Then, they saw an exit at the end of the village. They decided to go through it to try and find food. Amy and Lucy struggled to make their way through the exit, which was very dark and scary. 

Eventually, they made it to the other side. To their surprise, they found lots of food and water. They had finally found something to eat! They filled their tummies and felt so relieved and happy. 

Amy and Lucy looked out at the village, feeling thankful and content. They were no longer poor or hungry, and they had found a way to survive.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Jane. She was very alert and liked to watch things on the big screen.

She was so happy with the game that she never wanted to stop. She played the game until it was time to go to bed.

The next day, Jane was still very alert and couldnâ€™t wait to play the game again. She put it on the screen and kept playing. And she kept playing it every day.

The End.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy who lived in a small village. One day, there was a big earthquake that shook the ground and made everything wobble. Timmy was scared and didn't know what to do. His dad told him that everything will be okay and that they just need to be careful.
