His dad told him that sometimes, the best thing we can do is just be there for our friends and accept them for who they are. Timmy didn't understand what his dad meant by "accept", but he knew that he wanted to help Billy. So, he went to Billy's house and sat with him. They talked about the earthquake and how scary it was. Timmy made Billy laugh by doing silly faces and making funny noises.

Timmy learned that being there for someone is important and that we should never judge others for their mistakes. His dad told him that it's foolish to think that we are better than others just because we have more things or because we didn't experience the same things they did. Timmy promised himself that he will always be there for his friends and accept them for who they are.

Once upon a time, there was a little mouse named Timmy. Timmy loved to eat cheese. He would always go to the pantry to find some cheese to eat. One day, Timmy found a big piece of old cheese. He was so happy and ate it all up.

But after a while, Timmy started to feel sick. He had eaten too much old cheese and it made him delay his work of collecting food for the winter. Sadly, Timmy did not finish collecting enough food in time and when winter came, he had nothing to eat. Timmy was very sad and hungry. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside with his toys. He had a big red ball that he loved to kick and throw. Timmy also had a toy car that he liked to drive around.

One day, Timmy saw a big storm coming. He heard thunder and saw lightning in the sky. Timmy was scared of the storm, but he knew he was safe inside his house.

Later that night, Timmy's mom read him a story about a good wizard who owned a magic wand. Timmy loved the story and wished he could own a magic wand too. Suddenly, there was a loud noise outside. Timmy looked out the window and saw that a big tree had fallen down in his yard. 

The next day, Timmy went outside to play and saw that his toy car was stuck under the fallen tree. He tried to move the tree, but it was too heavy. Just then, a man with a chainsaw came to help. The man was a good neighbor who owned a big truck. He cut the tree into pieces and moved it out of the way. Timmy was happy that his toy car was safe and he thanked the good neighbor for his help.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named John. He was three years old. One day, John wanted to play chess with his mom, but she said no. He got very sad. He went to his room and tried to find something to do.

John saw his favourite toy - a little rabbit - and a box of chess pieces. He heard his mom yell, so he decided to hide. He put the rabbit in the box and hid behind his bedroom door. 

John heard his mom coming in, so he stayed very quiet. She rummaged through the room for a few minutes. She gave a rude yell and said, â€œWhere's my chess pieces?â€

John jumped out from his hiding spot. He told his mom, â€œI'm sorry! I was playing hide and seek with my rabbit!â€ John's mom couldn't stay mad at him, so she smiled and hugged him tight. 

John played chess with his mom and they both had lots of fun!

Once upon a time, in a big forest, there was a little bunny named Ben. Ben loved to play with his friends, but sometimes he would get sad. One day, Ben's friend, a wise old owl, told him about a magic word that could make him happy. The magic word was "add."

Ben wanted to try the magic word right away. He went to his friend, a tiny ant, and said, "Let's add some fun to our day!" They played and laughed together, and Ben felt happy. The result of using the magic word was that Ben and his friends had a great time.

But Ben also learned that the magic word could be harsh. One day, he used the word "add" to put too much salt in his soup. The result was that the soup tasted bad. Ben learned that he needed to be careful with the magic word. From that day on, Ben only used the word "add" to make good things happen, and he and his friends lived happily ever after.

Tom and Lily were twins who liked to play with their toys. One day, their mother gave them a big jar of jam and some bread for a snack. She told them to share nicely and not to make a mess.

Tom and Lily took the jar and the bread to their room. They put some jam on their bread and ate it. It was sweet and sticky. They wanted more. But there was only a little jam left in the jar.

"I want the last jam!" Tom said. He grabbed the jar and tried to open it.

"No, I want it!" Lily said. She pulled the jar from Tom's hands and opened it.

They both reached for the jam with their spoons. They pushed and shoved each other. The jam spilled out of the jar and spread all over the bed, the floor, and their clothes.

"Look what you did!" Tom yelled.

"It's your fault!" Lily yelled back.

They heard their mother coming. They were scared. They knew they had been selfish and naughty. They tried to hide the jam and the mess, but it was too late.

Their mother opened the door and saw the sticky disaster. She was angry and sad.

"Tom and Lily, what have you done?" she asked. "Why did you not share the jam? Why did you make such a mess? You have wasted the jam and ruined your clothes. You have been very selfish and unkind to each other."

Tom and Lily felt ashamed. They knew their mother was right. They said sorry to their mother and to each other. They helped their mother clean up the mess. They learned their lesson. They promised to share and be nice to each other from then on.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Lucy. She was organized and always had her things ready. One day she wanted to go to the park. She opened her trunk and got ready to go. But then, her mummy said she had to delay. Lucy was sad but knew that it was best to listen. She put everything back in her trunk very organized. 

The next day, Lucy was excited to go to the park! She opened her trunk, got ready, and off she went. She had a lovely day and was really happy. She had remembered to be organized and everything went as planned. 

At the end of the day, Lucy beamed when she noticed she was able to go to the park without any delays.

Once upon a time there was a happy little girl called Sarah. She loved to play in the garden. One day, she found a diary in the grass. She opened it and read the words inside. They were easy to understand. 

Suddenly, Sarah heard a loud noise - a slap! She looked around, but she couldn't see who had done it. She was scared, so she quickly hid the diary in her pocket. 

Sarah ran back into the safety of her house. There, she opened the diary again and read the easy words inside. She smiled as she realised she knew what to do next. 

Sarah closed the diary and hid it away safely, so that no-one else could find it. From then on, she always kept it safe and sound. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a nice little boy named Tony. He loved to go outside and play. Today Tony was feeling extra hungry for dinner.

He went into the kitchen and saw something on the table. It was a special purple dinner! Tony was excited and he couldn't wait to taste it. He picked up a spoon and put some of the dinner onto it.

Tony brought the spoon up to his mouth and took a bite. It was so yummy! He loved his purple dinner. Tony kept eating and eating until he had a full tummy.

He was so happy that he had tasted the special purple dinner. Tony smiled and said, "This was the best dinner ever!" And he happily went back outside to play.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved candy, especially lollipops that were big and round. One day, Lily started to imagine that she had a whole bag of lollipops. She was so happy! 

Lily was also very intelligent, she knew how to count all her lollipops and share them with her friends. They all had a great time together, laughing and playing. 

As the sun started to set, Lily and her friends said goodbye and went home. Lily fell asleep with a smile on her face, imagining all the candy she would have tomorrow. The end.

Steve was playing and he heard his dad say "it's time to follow me and go on vacation". Steve was excited as he followed his dad to the car. Steve could see people in colorful clothes, delicious smells and happy faces.

Steve and his dad went on a plane for the first time. The air was fresh and the sky was blue. Steve loved looking out of the window at the clouds. His dad said it was a fair day for a vacation!

At the end of their journey, Steve and his dad arrived at their vacation spot. It was so beautiful with lush green trees and a crystal clear lake. The sun was shining and it was warm.

Steve enjoyed running and jumping around. He also liked making castles in the sand. His dad watched him and smiled with joy.

At the end of their vacation, Steve and his dad went to the airport to fly back home. Steve's dad said that it had been a fair vacation. Steve smiled and said he wanted to go back soon!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved animals. She wanted to see a dolphin very badly. So, one day, she made a request to her mom.

The little girl said, "Mom, can I see a dolphin?"

Her mom smiled and replied, "Yes, you can. There is a cold lake just down the road. Maybe you can find one there."

So, the girl grabbed her coat and hat and went to the lake. When she got there, she stood on the shore and called out to the dolphins in the distance. Suddenly, she saw a fin poking above the surface of the water.

The dolphin swam closer to the shore and the little girl was so excited. She watched as the dolphins swam around in the cold water, laughing and playing.

The little girl smiled and waved goodbye to the dolphins as she walked home. She was so happy that her request had been met!

Once upon a time, there was a small girl named Lily. She loved to play at the park with her friends. One day, Lily's mom told her they were going to a new park. This made Lily very excite because she loved exploring new places.

When they arrived at the park, Lily saw that it was very small. She felt a little disappointed because she thought it would be bigger. But then, she saw a big slide and a swing set. Lily couldn't wait to play on them.

As she was playing, Lily noticed a group of kids playing a game. They asked her if she wanted to join in. Lily felt nervous at first, but then she decided to give it a try. To her surprise, she was really good at the game and had a lot of fun.

At the end of the day, Lily realized that even though the park was small, she had a great time playing and making new friends. She couldn't wait to come back and play again.

Once upon a time there was a snail. The snail wanted to get to the mailbox. But it wasn't easy! The snail had to be careful and slow. So it started to crawl.

The snail crawled through the grass and over the rocks. The snail moved so slowly. But it kept on going. After a while, the snail made it to the mailbox.

The snail was so happy! It had made it to the mailbox, all by itself. It had been careful and slow, and it was so proud.

The snail went back home with a smile. It knew if it was careful and slow it could do anything.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She liked to play hide and seek with her friends. One day, Lily found a big bag of cocoa in the kitchen. Her mom said it was available for her to make hot chocolate. Lily was very happy and made a delicious drink. She decided to hide the cocoa so her little brother wouldn't drink it all. She found a good spot and felt proud of herself for keeping it safe.

Once upon a time, there was a bald man. He loved to take long walks in the forest. One day, he was walking through the trees when he saw something special at the end of the trail. A little girl with a big smile was standing there. He approached her and she gave him a big kiss on his bald head. 

The man smiled and thanked her. He thanked her for the kiss and for bringing a little joy to his walk in the forest. The man quickly said goodbye and started walking along the trail again. As he continued walking, he smiled, knowing he had been shown kindness from a stranger. 

The man was never seen in the forest again, but whenever people walk down that same trail, they are always reminded of the kindness of the little girl who kissed a bald man.

Jimmy was an eager boy. He loved to explore and wanted to see what was over the hill. So one day he decided to put on his shoes and go on an adventure. He ran up the hill, laughing and glee. When Jimmy reached the top he saw a beautiful sunset. The colors lit up the sky and Jimmy felt so happy. He watched the sun set until it was dark, then he put his shoes back on and ran back home. He knew that over the hill was a magical place and he couldn't wait to explore it again.

Lily and Ben were playing with their cars on the floor. They liked to make them go fast and make loud noises. Lily had a red car and Ben had a blue car.

"Look at my car, it has more speed than yours!" Ben said, zooming his car past Lily's.

"No, my car is faster, watch this!" Lily said, pushing her car harder.

They raced their cars back and forth, trying to beat each other. But then, Lily's car hit a chair leg and flipped over. It broke one of its wheels and stopped moving.

"Oh no, my car is broken!" Lily cried, picking it up and looking at it.

"I'm sorry, Lily, it was an accident," Ben said, feeling bad.

"Your car is still fine, you can keep playing. But I have to quit, my car is ruined," Lily said, feeling sad.

She put her car down and hugged her knees. She didn't want to play anymore.

Ben saw that Lily was sad and he had an idea. He went to his toy box and found another car. It was green and had four wheels. He brought it to Lily and gave it to her.

"Here, Lily, you can have this car. It's not red, but it's still fast and fun. I have another blue car, we can play together," he said, smiling.

Lily looked at the green car and then at Ben. She smiled too and took the car.

"Thank you, Ben, you are very nice. I like the green car, it's pretty. Can we still be friends?" she asked.

"Of course we can, Lily, you are my best friend. Come on, let's race again!" he said, holding his blue car.

They put their cars on the floor and started playing again. They made them go fast and make loud noises. They had fun and they were happy.

James was a cute three year old. He lived in a big house with lots of toys. He had a lot of fun playing with them.

One day, he wanted to choose something new. He looked around the house and saw a shiny ashtray on the table. He could not believe it, it was so pretty! So he decided to choose it and take it with him.

He was very excited and started to play with it right away. He pretended it was his own little car and drove it around the house. He was laughing and having a lot of fun.

He kept playing with the ashtray. He rolled it around the house, pretending it was a toy car. He eventually decided to put it in his room, so he could keep playing with it whenever he wanted.

James loved his new toy and it was the perfect choice for him!

Jack was a little boy who loved to run. He ran everywhere. He ran so fast that he got passed by many people. One day, Jack made a plan. He wanted to increase his speed so he could pass everyone else. 

He started practicing every day. He ran a little bit faster each time. Jack was so excited and he was getting better and better. Pretty soon, he was running faster and faster. 

One day, Jack looked around and he noticed that he was passing everyone else. He had increased his speed so much that he was now the fastest runner. He was so proud of himself and everyone else said he was amazing. 

Jack had been determined to increase his speed and he was happy that he had achieved his goal. From then on, he was the fastest runner around and he always enjoyed a good race.

Tom likes to go to the library with his mom. He likes to look at the books on the shelf. He likes to find books with pictures of animals, cars, and stars. He likes to sit on the floor and read with his mom.

One day, Tom sees a new book on the shelf. It has a picture of a big red dragon on the cover. Tom likes dragons. He wants to read the book. He takes the book from the shelf and shows it to his mom.

Mom looks at the book. She says, "This book is not for you, Tom. This book is for big kids. It has hard words and scary stories. You will not like it." She puts the book back on the shelf.

Tom is sad. He wants to read the book. He thinks the dragon looks nice, not scary. He thinks the book will be fun, not hard. He does not listen to his mom. He waits for his mom to look away. Then he takes the book from the shelf again. He runs to a corner and opens the book.

Tom starts to read the book. He does not know the words. He tries to guess what they mean. He looks at the pictures. He sees the dragon breathing fire and roaring. He sees the people running and screaming. He sees the houses burning and falling. He feels scared. He does not like the book. He wishes he listened to his mom.

Tom closes the book. He runs back to his mom. He says, "I'm sorry, mom. You were right. This book is not for me. This book is too scary. I want a mild book. A mild book with nice dragons, not mean dragons. Can we find a mild book, mom?"

Mom hugs Tom. She says, "It's okay, Tom. I'm glad you came back to me. I'm not mad at you. I love you. Yes, we can find a mild book. A mild book with nice dragons, or whatever you like. Let's go to the shelf and look together."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved to play the piano. She had a little piano at home and she practiced every day. But she didn't like to listen to her mommy and daddy when they told her to practice more. She thought she was already good enough.

One day, there was a big piano competition in town. The little girl wanted to join, but her parents knew she wasn't ready yet. They told her she needed to improve her skills before she could join. But the little girl didn't listen and joined the competition anyway.

During the competition, the little girl played the piano, but she made many mistakes. She didn't win and felt very sad. Her parents told her that it was okay to lose, but she should have listened to them and practiced more. The little girl learned that it's important to listen to your parents and improve your skills before trying new things.

Once upon a time there was a brave fireman who loved to help people. One day, he was out on a mission to fight a fire. Everyone was so impressed by his courage and bravery. 

As he went to fight the fire, he got very thirsty. He saw a fresh river nearby, so he went to have a drink. 

Just then, a little frog hopped up to him. The frog said, "Can I have a sip, too?". The fireman smiled and said, "Of course you can!" 

The fireman shared his drink with the little frog, and everyone who saw them was very impressed! They cheered and praised the fireman for his kindness and bravery. The fireman and the little frog both smiled - they had made a wonderful friendship!

Once there was an enormous swim. It was so big that it was bigger than a house. The sun was beaming down, making the water sparkle.

The little girl was be so excited to swim in the enormous swim. She put on her swimsuit and jumped into the water. She swam for a long time, until her arms and legs were tired.

The girl got out of the swim and dried off in the sun. She was so pleased with how big the swim was and how much fun she had. She was happy to be able to swim in such an enormous swim.

Lily loved to write in her diary every day. She had a pink diary with a lock and a key. She wrote about her friends, her toys, her dreams and her secrets. She did not want anyone to read her diary, because it was hers.

One day, Lily came home from school and saw her brother Tom in her room. He had her diary in his hand and was reading it out loud. He was laughing and making fun of her.

"Dear diary, today I ate a yummy cake at the party. It had chocolate and cream and sprinkles. I wish I could have another slice. I love cake so much. Cake is my best friend." Tom read in a silly voice.

Lily felt angry and sad. She ran to Tom and tried to grab her diary. "Stop it! Give it back! That's mine!" she shouted.

Tom was bigger and stronger than Lily. He held the diary high above his head. "No, this is too funny. Listen to this. Dear diary, today I saw Ben at the park. He has blue eyes and curly hair. He smiled at me and I felt shy. I think he likes me. I like him too. He is so cute. I want to kiss him." Tom read in a mocking voice.

Lily felt embarrassed and hurt. She started to cry. "You're mean! You're a bad brother! Leave me alone!" she sobbed.

Tom saw Lily crying and felt sorry. He realized he had been mean and rude. He regretted reading her diary and making fun of her. He lowered the diary and gave it back to Lily. "I'm sorry, Lily. I was just joking. I won't read your diary again. Please don't cry." he said.

Lily took her diary and hugged it. She wiped her tears and looked at Tom. She was still angry, but she also felt sorry for him. He looked sad and ashamed. She decided to forgive him. "It's okay, Tom. I forgive you. But don't do it again. And don't tell anyone about Ben. He's my secret." she said.

Tom nodded and smiled. He hugged Lily and said, "I won't, I promise. And you know what? Ben is lucky to have you. You're a good sister. And you have good taste in cake." he said.

Lily smiled and said, "Thank you, Tom. You're a good brother. Sometimes. And you have good taste in jokes. Sometimes." she said.

They laughed and went downstairs to have some yummy cake together. They forgot about the diary and the secrets. They were happy.

Once upon a time there was a girl. Her name was Jill. Jill had a cupboard she kept all her special things in. She wanted to keep it safe so she was very careful who she trusted.

One day her best friend, Ben, asked if he could put something in the cupboard. Jill wanted to trust him but she wasn't sure if she should. She thought long and hard, then finally she said yes.

Ben was so happy! He thanked Jill and said he wanted to show her something special in the cupboard. He opened it carefully, put something in it, shut the door and smiled.

"You're so tough, Jill," he said. "I knew I could trust you".

Jill felt so proud. She knew she had made the right decision. From that day on, the cupboard was even more special to her and it was filled with lots of special surprises!

Tom and Ben were friends who liked to play in the sand. They made castles and bridges and tunnels with their buckets and shovels. One day, they found a big shell in the sand. They opened it and saw a shrimp inside. The shrimp was pink and shiny and had many legs.

"Wow, look at this shrimp!" Tom said. "It is so pretty. I want to keep it."

"No, I want to keep it!" Ben said. "I found it first. It is mine."

Tom and Ben began to quarrel. They pulled the shell from each other and shouted. The shrimp was scared and tried to hide in the shell.

"Stop it, stop it!" a voice said. It was Lisa, their big sister. She came to see what was wrong. "Why are you fighting over a shrimp? It is not a toy. It is a living thing. It needs water and food and space. You cannot keep it in a bucket or a jar. It will die."

Tom and Ben felt ashamed. They looked at the shrimp and saw that it was unhappy. They realized that they were being selfish and mean.

"Sorry, Lisa," Tom said. "You are right. We should not keep the shrimp. We should let it go."

"Sorry, Lisa," Ben said. "You are right. We should not quarrel. We should share and be kind."

Lisa smiled and hugged them. She was proud of them. She helped them carry the shell to the water. They gently put the shrimp back in the sea. The shrimp was happy and swam away.

"Bye, shrimp!" Tom and Ben said. "Thank you for showing us your beauty. We hope you have a good life."

Tom and Ben learned a lesson that day. They learned that quarreling is bad and sharing is good. They learned that animals are not toys and they deserve respect. They learned that Lisa was clever and caring. They decided to be better friends and better people.

Once upon a time there was a kitchen. It was all empty with nothing in it.

Then one day something special arrived in the kitchen. It was a big box!

Mum and dad said it was time to unpack and something special was inside the box.

So mum and dad worked together to unpack and suddenly the kitchen was not empty anymore.

There was lots of nice things in it, like a fridge with yummy food inside and a big table to eat at.

But then they noticed something strange. In the corner of the room was a dead mouse!

Mum and dad laughed and said that was not part of the special things inside the box. They took the dead mouse away and left the kitchen lovely and clean. 

That night the family all ate together in the kitchen and felt very happy.

Tom and Lily are friends. They like to play in the garden. One day, they find a big bottle of soap. They want to make bubbles.

"Look, Tom, I have soap!" Lily says. She opens the bottle and pours some soap on her hand.

"Me too, me too!" Tom says. He grabs the bottle and pours some soap on his hand.

They blow on their hands and make bubbles. The bubbles are big and shiny. They laugh and clap.

"More, more!" Tom says. He pours more soap on his hand. He blows harder and harder.

"Stop, Tom, stop!" Lily says. She sees something bad. The soap is going in Tom's ears. "The soap will make you deaf!"

But Tom does not hear Lily. He blows more and more. The soap fills his ears. He can't hear anything.

"Tom, Tom, can you hear me?" Lily says. She shakes Tom's arm. She is scared.

But Tom does not answer. He does not hear Lily. He does not hear anything. He is deaf.

Lily cries. Tom cries. They are sad. The soap is bad. The end.

Tom and Lily liked to play in the big park. They saw many trees, flowers, birds and bugs. They had fun running, jumping and hiding. One day, they found a big oak tree. It had a hole in its trunk. Tom and Lily wanted to see what was inside.

They went closer to the hole. They saw a shiny bottle. It had a label that said "Drink me". Tom was curious. He wanted to try the bottle. Lily was scared. She said "No, Tom, don't do that. It might be bad for you. It might make you sick or crazy or shrink."

But Tom did not listen to Lily. He took the bottle and drank some. He felt funny. He looked at Lily. She looked very big. He looked at his hands. They were very small. He had shrunk. He was as small as a bug. He cried "Help, Lily, help!"

Lily heard Tom's tiny voice. She saw him on the ground. She was shocked. She did not know what to do. She looked at the bottle. It had another label that said "Eat me". It had a small cake inside. Lily thought maybe the cake could make Tom big again. She took the cake and gave it to Tom. He ate some. He felt funny again. He looked at Lily. She looked normal. He looked at his hands. They were normal too. He had grown back. He was happy. He hugged Lily and said "Thank you, Lily, thank you!"

Tom and Lily learned a lesson. They learned not to touch or drink or eat things that they did not know. They learned to listen to each other and be careful. They learned that curiosity can be good, but also dangerous. They decided to leave the bottle and the cake in the hole and never go near the oak tree again. They went back to their home and told their mom what had happened. She was glad that they were safe and smart. She gave them a hug and a kiss and said "I love you, Tom and Lily, I love you!"

Once upon a time there was a clumsy cow called Daisy. Daisy was always getting herself into all sorts of trouble. One day she found a box of powder at the end of a rainbow. She sniffed the powder and it made her sneeze.

Suddenly, Daisy's feet began to get bigger and bigger and bigger. Soon, Daisy was so big she could not even fit through the doorway.

Laughing, Daisy shouted to her friends, â€œLook, look at me now!"

But her friend, a tiny mouse, said, "Oh no, what have you done?"

Daisy was puzzled and replied, "I don't know, I only sniffed the powder!"

The mouse said, "Well I think you must have eaten some of the powder, it appears to have caused you to increase in size!"

Daisy quickly ran back to the end of the rainbow and put the box of powder away. She was very careful never to touch it again. 

And so, Daisy stayed the perfect size, living happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Amy. Amy lived in a small house with her mommy and daddy. She loved to play in the park near her house. In the park, there was a modest fountain. Amy liked to watch the water go up and down.

One sunny day, Amy went to the park with her mommy. They saw a small bird near the fountain. Amy wanted to peek at the bird. She walked slowly and quietly to the bird. The bird looked at Amy and said, "Hi, I am Timmy the bird. Do you want to play with me?"

Amy was so happy to have a new friend. She said, "Yes, Timmy! Let's play together." Amy and Timmy played near the fountain all day. They splashed in the water and had lots of fun. When it was time to go home, Amy said, "Bye, Timmy! See you tomorrow!"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to explore the jungle near her house. One day, she went on a walk and saw a cool monkey swinging from a tree. "Hi monkey!" said Lily. "What are you doing up there?"

"I'm just playing," said the monkey. "Do you want to come up and play with me?"

Lily was a little scared, but she really wanted to see what it was like to swing from a tree like a monkey. So she climbed up and started swinging too. It was so much fun! They swung back and forth, up and down, and laughed and laughed.

When it was time to go home, Lily said goodbye to the monkey and promised to come back and play again soon. She was so happy to have seen the cool monkey in the jungle.

Tom and Lily were best friends. They liked to play together and pretend they were kings and queens. One day, they saw a big toy palace in the shop window. It was incredible. It had many rooms, a garden, a bridge and a flag.

"Wow, look at that palace!" Tom said. "I want to buy it and live in it."

"Me too!" Lily said. "But it is very expensive. We don't have enough money."

They decided to save their pocket money and buy the palace together. They worked hard and did chores for their parents. They put their coins in a jar and counted them every day. They waited and waited until they had enough.

They ran to the shop with their jar of coins. They were very happy and excited. They asked the shopkeeper for the palace.

"Sorry, kids," the shopkeeper said. "The palace is sold. Someone else bought it this morning."

Tom and Lily were very sad and angry. They cried and shouted. They wanted the palace so much. They felt like their dream was broken.

"Who bought it?" Tom asked.

The shopkeeper pointed to a boy outside. He was holding the palace and smiling. It was Ben, the meanest boy in their school. He always teased and bullied them.

"Ha ha, look what I have!" Ben said. "The palace is mine. You can't have it. You are too poor and stupid."

Tom and Lily felt very hurt and mad. They hated Ben. They wished they could take the palace from him. They tried to grab it, but Ben pushed them away. He ran away with the palace, laughing.

Tom and Lily were left alone, with no palace and no money. They felt like they had lost everything. They hugged each other and cried. They wished they had never seen the palace. They wished they had never tried to buy it. They wished they had a different friend.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird. The bird liked to fly and sing in the trees. One day, the bird found a nest with some fragile eggs inside. The bird knew to be careful not to break the eggs because they were delicate. The bird watched over the eggs and counted the number of days until they hatched. Finally, the eggs cracked open and baby birds came out. The bird was happy to see the nature around her growing and changing.

Tom and Lily were two rabbits who liked to play in the farm. They saw a big barrel near the barn and wanted to hop inside. They thought it would be fun to roll and bounce in the barrel.

"Come on, Lily, let's hop in the barrel!" Tom said.

"OK, Tom, but be careful. The barrel looks old and shaky," Lily said.

They hopped in the barrel and started to roll and bounce. They laughed and squeaked as they felt the wind in their fur. They did not see the farmer coming with his dog.

The farmer saw the barrel moving and heard the noise. He thought there was something inside that he could sell or eat. He grabbed the barrel and put it on his truck. He did not know there were two rabbits inside.

"Hey, what are you doing? Let us out!" Tom shouted.

"Help, help, we are trapped!" Lily cried.

But the farmer and his dog did not hear them. They drove away with the barrel. Tom and Lily were scared and sad. They did not know where they were going or what would happen to them. They wished they had not been so clumsy and curious. They wished they had stayed in their burrow. They missed their home and their friends. They hoped someone would save them, but no one did. The end.

Once there was a tiny kitten named Tim. He was the best kitten in the whole world. He had soft fluffy fur and bright green eyes. 

One day, Tim felt something strange in the air. Suddenly, the ground started shaking. Tim had never felt anything like it before. He was so scared and felt very miserable.

Just then, Tim's mommy came running into the room. She picked him up, held him close and said "It's alright Timmy, it's just an earthquake. Don't worry, I love you."

Tim meowed a tiny meow and nuzzled against his mommy's chest. He felt so safe and happy, knowing his mommy was there.

As the earthquake stopped and everyone started to calm down, Tim thought to himself "I love my mommy, she always makes me feel so safe."

Mabel was very excited. She was going to the dentist's office for the first time. She couldn't believe that soon her tooth would look yummy.

At the dentist's office, Mabel was a little bit scared. But, the dentist was friendly and told Mabel not to worry. He said he was going to touch her tooth to take care of it.

Mabel listened very carefully to the dentist. He showed her how to brush her tooth so it would stay yummy. He gave her a little toothbrush and tasty toothpaste.

At the end of the visit, Mabel's tooth looked yummy and bright. She gave the dentist a big smile. She was happy to know that her tooth was healthy.

Tom and Lily were at the park with their mom. They saw a big slide and ran to it. Tom got there first and climbed up the ladder. Lily followed him, but Tom did not want to share.

"Go away, Lily!" Tom shouted. "This is my slide! You are too small and slow!"

Lily felt sad and angry. She wanted to slide too. She did not think Tom was being nice. She tried to climb up, but Tom kicked her with his foot. Lily fell down and hurt her knee. She started to cry.

Mom heard Lily's cry and came to see what happened. She saw Tom on the slide and Lily on the ground. She was not happy with Tom.

"Tom, why did you kick your sister?" Mom asked. "That was very selfish and mean of you. You should share the slide with her. It is not only yours."

Tom felt ashamed and sorry. He realized he had been wrong. He slid down and hugged Lily.

"I'm sorry, Lily," Tom said. "I was selfish. You can slide with me. Do you want to go again?"

Lily nodded and smiled. She forgave Tom. They climbed up the ladder together and slid down. They had fun and laughed. Mom watched them and smiled too. She was glad they made up.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy had a key to his toy box, and he loved playing with his toys. One day, Timmy's friend Billy came over to play. Billy wanted to play with Timmy's toys, but Timmy didn't want to share.

"I want to play with my toys alone," Timmy said.

"That's not fair," Billy said, looking sad. "We can play together and have fun."

Timmy disagreed with Billy, thinking that playing alone was better. But then he realized that sharing was not foolish, but actually a good thing to do. So, he gave Billy a toy to play with, and they had fun together. Timmy learned that sharing was important, and he felt happy that he could make his friend happy too.

Once there was a little girl called Steph. Steph was three years old and wanted to choose the perfect table for her room. She thought about it for a long time. She wanted something special.

One day, she went with her parents to a furniture shop. There were lots of tables to choose from. She looked at them all, but none of them seemed perfect. Just when she thought she wouldn't find one, she saw it. It was a beautiful wooden table with a big smile on it. She knew it was the one!

So, Steph chose the perfect table. She brought it home and it made her very happy. Every evening, she would sit at her table and draw or colour. And when she was finished, she'd put the things away neatly, just like her mum and dad had taught her.

The table was perfect. It was just what she needed.

Once upon a time, there was a very adventurous girl. One day, she was walking out of her house in search of something exciting. 

When she saw a box in the middle of the street, she ran over to it and started to open it. Inside, she found many delicious snacks! She was very excited and couldn't wait to start munching. 

Suddenly, she heard a voice from behind her. It was a boy. He said, "What are you doing with my box?"

The adventurous girl replied, "I'm just trying to eat the snacks inside! They look yummy!" 

The boy said, "Sure, go ahead! But make sure you chew slowly." 

So, the adventurous girl quietly continued to chew the snacks inside the box. She ate all kinds of delicious things such as candy and chips. When she was done, she thanked the boy and skipped away. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play outside. One day, she found a gray beetle crawling on the ground. She picked it up and showed it to her mom. "Look, Mommy! I found a beetle," she said.

Her mom smiled and said, "Beetles are very interesting. But remember, we should always be gentle with them." Lily nodded and put the beetle back on the ground.

Later that day, Lily and her mom were making soup for dinner. Lily helped her mom stir the pot. "Can I stir too?" she asked. Her mom said yes and gave her a spoon.

As they stirred the soup, Lily remembered what her mom said about being gentle. She said, "Mommy, we should be gentle with the soup too. Just like we were gentle with the beetle."

Her mom smiled and said, "That's right, Lily. We should always be gentle with everything we touch." And from that day on, Lily always remembered to be gentle with the things around her.

Sara liked to examine things. She liked to look at them, touch them, smell them, and sometimes taste them. She examined flowers, rocks, bugs, and toys. She was very curious and wanted to learn.

One day, she found a shiny thing in the grass. It was round and hard and had a hole in it. She wondered what it was. She picked it up and examined it. It felt cold and smooth. She put it to her ear and heard a voice.

"Hello, hello, hello," the voice said. It sounded funny and echoed. Sara giggled. She liked the voice. She wanted to talk to it.

"Hello, voice," she said. "Who are you? Where are you?"

"I am a coin, a coin, a coin," the voice said. "I am in your hand, your hand, your hand."

Sara was amazed. She had never heard a coin talk before. She wanted to show it to her mom. She ran to the house, holding the coin tightly.

"Mom, mom, mom," she shouted. "Look what I found. It is a coin and it can talk. Listen, listen, listen."

She put the coin to her mom's ear and waited for the voice. But there was no voice. There was only silence.

"Sweetie, this is just a coin," her mom said. "It can't talk. You must have imagined it."

Sara felt sad and confused. She was sure the coin had talked to her. She looked at the coin again and saw something she had not noticed before. There was a tiny hole in the other side of the coin. She realized that the voice had come from a small speaker inside the coin. Someone had tricked her. She felt angry and betrayed.

She threw the coin on the floor and stomped on it. She heard a crack and a hiss. The coin broke and smoke came out of it. She had ruined the coin and the voice.

She started to cry. She had lost her new friend and her mom did not believe her. She wished she had never examined the coin. She was not proud of herself. She was ashamed.

Once upon a time, there were two friends. One was big and one was small. The small friend wanted to go outside to play with his big friend. But the big friend said, "No, I can't go outside because the wind will prevent us from having fun."

The small friend thought for a moment and then said, "Let's go to the garden instead. I know a big plant that we can play with!"

So the big and small friends went to the garden. They saw the big plant and started playing with it. They laughed and played until their tummies growled, and then they went back to the house.

The big and small friends were happy. With the big plant in the garden, they were able to have fun even when the wind was blowing. They made sure the big plant was safe, so the wind couldn't prevent them from having fun!

Once upon a time, in a land full of trees, there was a little cherry tree. The cherry tree was very sad because it did not have any friends. All the other trees were big and strong, but the cherry tree was small and weak. The cherry tree was envious of the big trees.

One day, the cherry tree felt a tickle in its branches. It was a little spring wind. The wind told the cherry tree not to be sad. The wind said, "You are special because you have sweet cherries that everyone loves." The cherry tree started to feel a little better.

As time went on, the cherry tree grew more and more cherries. All the animals in the land came to eat the cherries and play under the cherry tree. The cherry tree was happy because it had many friends now. The cherry tree learned that being different can be a good thing. And they all lived happily ever after.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toys and books. But sometimes they fight over them. They want the same toy or book and they do not want to share.

One day, their mom says, "Anna and Ben, I have a surprise for you. We are going to visit your aunt Lucy. She works at a university. A university is a big place where people learn many things. You will see many new things there."

Anna and Ben are excited. They pack their bags and get in the car. They say goodbye to their dad and their dog. They drive for a long time. They see many cars and trees and houses on the way.

They arrive at the university. Aunt Lucy is waiting for them. She hugs them and says, "Hello, Anna and Ben. I'm so happy to see you. Come, I will show you around the university. It is a very lively place. Lively means there are many people and things happening."

Aunt Lucy takes them to a big building. She says, "This is where I work. I teach people about animals. Do you like animals?" Anna and Ben nod. They love animals. They follow Aunt Lucy inside. They see many pictures and models of animals on the walls and shelves. They see a big skeleton of a dinosaur. They are amazed.

Aunt Lucy says, "This is a dinosaur. It was a very big and strong animal. But it is not alive anymore. It lived a long time ago. Do you want to touch it?" Anna and Ben say yes. They reach out their hands and touch the dinosaur bones. They feel hard and cold.

Anna and Ben look at each other. They smile. They do not fight anymore. They are happy to learn new things. They say, "Thank you, Aunt Lucy. This is a very cool place. We like the university." Aunt Lucy smiles too. She says, "You're welcome, Anna and Ben. I'm glad you like it. There are many more things to see. Come, let's go."

Tom and Lily were brother and sister. They liked to play with their toys in their room. But sometimes they fought over the toys and made a lot of noise.

One day, their mom came to their room and said, "Tom and Lily, you have to share your toys and be nice to each other. If you fight, you will make me sad and angry. Do you remember what I told you about being kind?"

Tom and Lily nodded, but they did not really listen. They were ignorant. They thought they knew better than their mom. They wanted to have all the toys for themselves.

Later, their mom went out to buy some food. She said, "I will be back soon. Be good and don't fight. I love you." She kissed them and left.

Tom and Lily waited for a while. Then they started to play with their toys again. But soon they began to argue. Tom wanted to play with the truck, but Lily wanted to play with the doll. They pulled and pushed and shouted.

"Give me the truck! It's mine!" Tom said.

"No, it's mine! You had it yesterday!" Lily said.

They did not hear their mom's voice in their heads. They did not remember what she told them. They were ignorant.

Suddenly, they heard a loud noise outside. They looked out the window and saw a big fire. The fire was near their house. They saw smoke and flames and people running. They were scared.

They ran to the door, but it was locked. They could not get out. They cried and screamed for their mom. They wished they had listened to her. They wished they had been kind to each other. They were not ignorant anymore. They were sorry.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her dolls and sing songs. One day, Lily's mommy told her it was time to take a bath. Lily didn't want to take a bath because she didn't like the shampoo. It was too spicy for her.

Lily's mommy said, "Lily, you have to take a bath. You don't want to be stinky." Lily replied, "But mommy, I don't like the spicy shampoo." Her mommy said, "I know, but we don't have any other shampoo right now."

Lily took her bath and her mommy dried her off. Later that night, Lily's head started to hurt. She told her mommy, "Mommy, my head hurts." Her mommy said, "Let me raise you up and give you some medicine." But it was too late. Lily got sicker and sicker and had to go to the hospital. She learned that using the wrong shampoo can be very dangerous.

Ben and Lily were twins who liked to play with their toys. They had many toys, but they did not like to share them. They each had a big sack where they kept their toys. They did not let each other look inside their sacks.

One day, Ben saw Lily's sack on the floor. He was curious and wanted to see what toys she had. He opened her sack and took out a doll, a car, a ball and a book. He thought they were nice toys and he wanted to keep them. He put them in his sack and hid it under his bed.

Lily came back from the garden and saw her sack was open. She looked inside and saw that some of her toys were gone. She was angry and sad. She knew that Ben had taken them. She went to his room and saw his sack under his bed. She opened his sack and took out a train, a bear, a puzzle and a crayon. She thought they were nice toys and she wanted to keep them. She put them in her sack and ran to the living room.

Ben and Lily did not talk to each other for the rest of the day. They played with their new toys, but they did not feel happy. They felt guilty and lonely. They missed their old toys and their twin.

At night, they were very sleepy. They went to their beds and hugged their sacks. But they could not sleep well. They tossed and turned and had bad dreams. They wished they had not taken each other's toys.

The next morning, they woke up and felt sorry. They realized that they had been mean and selfish. They decided to give back the toys they had taken. They went to each other's room and exchanged their sacks. They said sorry and hugged each other. They felt happy and relieved. They learned that sharing is caring and that toys are more fun when you play with your twin.

Once upon a time, there was a green bird. She flew over the trees and down to the ground. The bird wanted to find a special person to help her.

She flew until she saw a building. She saw a sign that said "veterinarian". She had no idea what that meant, but she wanted to find out.

The bird passed through the door and there was a lady inside. The bird hop-hopped up to the lady, who smiled at her. The lady said she was the veterinarian and she could help her. The bird was happy, and the veterinarian took her to a special room.

The veterinarian took out a bright light and looked at the bird's feet. She said the bird was healthy and she passed the test. The bird thanked the veterinarian, and the veterinarian said she could go back and fly.

The bird flapped her wings, and it felt so good. She flew high into the sky, a happy green bird.

Once upon a time, there was a soft, red apple. It was floating down the river when a fish called out, "Follow me!" The apple obeyed and the fish lead it to a special place.

The fish said, "This is a good place to stay. The apple said, "I'm not sure. What if someone takes me?"

The fish answered, "Don't worry, I will stay and protect you." The apple felt much better and thanked the fish.

The apple and the fish stayed in the special place for a long time. They played hide and seek, and the apple made the fish laugh. They even sang songs together.

Finally, the apple said goodbye to the fish and went back down the river. But the apple never forgot the fish, and every time it saw a swimming fish, it smiled.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim was not feeling well, so his mom gave him a pill to help him feel better. Tim looked at the pill and thought it was too big for him. He did not want to take it.

Tim's friend, Sam, came to visit. Sam saw the pill and asked, "Why did you not take the pill, Tim?" Tim said, "It is too big, and I am scared." Sam was not selfish and wanted to help. "Let me pass it to you, and I will help you take it," Sam said.

With Sam's help, Tim took the pill. Soon, Tim felt much better. He was happy that Sam was not selfish and helped him. They played together all day and had lots of fun. Tim learned that it is good to have friends who help when you need it.

Once upon a time, there was a house with a nice, calm roof. Every day, a man called the supply man came to the house. He brought different things with him that the people living in the house needed. He brought food, toys and all sorts of other things. The family happily welcomed the supply man each time he came.

The supply man made sure everyone had enough food to eat and he made sure the house had supplies to stay warm and safe. He was happy to help and was always very friendly. After each delivery he said goodbye with a smile.

One day, the supply man needed help to fix the calm roof. He asked the family if they could help and everyone eagerly said yes. They worked together and fixed the roof so it was nice and strong.

The family was very happy that their roof was fixed and the supply man was very pleased too. The house was much safer and the family had a nice, calm roof once again. They thanked the supply man with a big smile for his help. He waved goodbye and the family watched him drive away.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Sally. Sally wanted to go outside and play in the sunshine, but the sky was dark. Suddenly, the sky was filled with lots of bright lightning! 

Sally was very scared and ran inside the house. She looked out the window and watched the lightning. There were lots of big flashes and loud noises. But then it stopped and the sun came out again.

Sally was so happy, she ran back outside. She wanted to show everyone how brave she was. She shouted, "I'm ready!" She wanted to do something special, so she asked her friends to come outside to play. She shouted, "Please come out! It's so nice outside now!"

Her friends came out and they started to play. They laughed and had lots of fun in the sunshine. Sally did feel brave now, she knew she could handle the lightning again.

One day, Grandpa got a very special surprise. His new motorcycle was ready to ride! He was so excited, he put on his leather jacket and hopped on.

As he started to zoom down the road, he saw something delicious on the side. It was a big, red apple! He quickly grabbed it and took a big bite.

Suddenly, the motorcycle started to shrink! Grandpa was zooming around on a mini motorcycle, and it was very fun. He smiled and laughed as he drove all around the neighborhood.

When it was time to go home, Grandpa's motorcycle returned to its normal size, and he drove away. It was the most delicious and exciting day!

Ash was a gifted boy. He was only 3 years old but he saw many things!
One day, he saw a rabbit hopping in the garden. He watched the rabbit as it hopped from bush to bush. The rabbit had a streak of grey ash down its back! Ash was so excited to see the rabbit.

Next, Ash saw a bird in the sky. He had never seen a bird so close. As it flew closer, Ash could see its beautiful blue feathers. He waved and shouted "Hello Bird!"

Finally, Ash saw a squirrel hiding in the trees. It was white and had a big fluffy tail! Ash was delighted to see the squirrel and wanted to get closer. But the squirrel ran away before he could reach it.

Ash had seen so many different animals that day. He was very happy and proud of his gifts!

Once upon a time there was a little girl who lived in a stable. Every morning she would wake up early and enjoy the sunrise. She would listen to the birds singing in the sky and smell the fresh scent of grass and hay. She was very happy in her stable.

One day, the little girl went outside and saw something even more amazing than the sunrise. There was a pony in the meadow nearby and it was enjoying a snack. The little girl was so happy she ran over to say hello to the pony.

"Hello pony!" she said. "My name is Lucy. Would you like to be friends?"

The pony looked up at her with a twinkle in its eye. "Yes, I would like that," said the pony.

The little girl was so excited to have a new friend. She quickly ran back to the stable and put on her riding gear. She was ready to go. She hopped on the pony's back and the two of them rode around the meadow, enjoying the day and the beauty of nature.

The little girl was so happy and the pony seemed just as content. As long as the little girl lived in the stable, she and the pony enjoyed each day together. The two of them were the best of friends.

The little girl was playing in the garden. She was looking around and noticing everything. She noticed a wet plant. She reached out her hand and touched the leaves. They were so soft and wet. She looked closer and saw that the plant had lots of little white flowers on it.

Suddenly, she heard a noise. She looked up and noticed a bird flying in the sky. She watched as it flew down and landed on the wet plant. She smiled as the bird started to eat the small white flowers.

The little girl was happy to be outside. She liked playing in the garden and noticing all the things around her. She liked looking at the wet plant and watching the birds. It made her very happy.

Once there was a little boy who wanted to go on adventures. His mommy bought him a scooter to help him get around. On the first day, he was a bit weak and struggled to manage the scooter. But, after some practice, he got better and better. He got so good that he scooted all around the park. Everywhere he went, he felt so adventurous. He explored all of the paths, trees and rocks.

When he got tired, he would rest for a bit. He knew that he had to manage his energy so he could keep having fun. And he did! He managed his energy perfectly so he could play all day. He even managed to show off to his friends and pretend he knew how to do all sorts of tricks.

He quickly became a pro at scootering around the park. He was so proud of himself and his mommy was very proud too. He smiled as he scootered around, knowing he had managed to get really good at it.

Timmy was so excited because his parents gave him the best present ever - a furry helicopter! He loved the softness of its fur and the sound of its whirring blades. He took it outside and spun it around and around, making it go higher and higher. Suddenly, he let go and the helicopter slipped away like a bird, soaring up into the sky. 

Timmy was sad now and he wished he had held onto the helicopter for just a little bit longer. He started to regret not playing with it longer and wished he could get it back again. But it was too late, the helicopter was way up in the sky and too far away to grab. 

Timmy wished he could fly a helicopter like that and never let it go. Now he was sad, but he was closer to fulfilling his wish. After all, if he kept practicing and learning, maybe one day he could fly a helicopter and never regret it again.

Once upon a time there were two friends:
Tom and Tim. Tom was a selfish boy who liked to stir things up. Tim was a kind boy who would help out in any way he could.

One day, Tom and Tim were playing in the garden when Tom decided that he wanted to make some whip cream. He gathered the bowls, spoons and milk and started to mix them together.

"Be careful," said Tim.
Tom looked up from his stirring, "Don't worry. I know what I'm doing," he replied.

After a few minutes of stirring, the cream was just right.

Tom looked up and said, "See? I told you I knew what I was doing!"

Tim smiled and said, "Yes, but sometimes you can be so selfish!"

Tom frowned and said, "But I just wanted to make something special."

Tim smiled and said, "I know, and it looks delicious!"

The two friends shared the whip cream, laughing and talking as they ate.

Once there was a strong farmer. He worked on his farm every day with his two dogs. One day the farmer noticed the fields were wide and needed some work. He and his dogs got to work and spent the day trimming and plowing. As the day went on, the farmer worked and worked until the field was ready. By the end of the day, the farmer was very tired, but he was proud of his work. The field looked big and strong, perfect for planting crops. The farmer smiled and thanked his dogs for all their help. Together they had done a great job and the farm was ready for the next season.

Once upon a time there was a little boy who went to the beach. He built a sandcastle and wanted to look for crabs. So he picked up a net to help him search. He saw a lot of lovely shells and a few crabs too.

He put all the shells in the net and put them in his pocket. He was happy doing this but he wanted to search for more crabs. So he used the net and splashed it in the ocean. All of a sudden, he felt a big pull on his net! He knew something nice was inside. 

He slowly pulled up his net and was so happy with what he saw. There were two lovely crabs inside, separated from each other! He couldnâ€™t have been any happier. He knew his day was complete and his sandcastle would have real crab friends!

Henry had a large figure. He wanted to mix it with something else to make it more interesting. He noticed a large load of mud. Henry thought it might look fun to mix the two together. So he threw his figure into the mud. But it was too big and it got stuck. Henry tried and tried, but he couldn't get it out. He was sad and he had to leave the figure there. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy had a red vest that he loved to wear. It made him feel happy and warm.

One day, Timmy's mom told him that he had to clean his room. But Timmy didn't want to clean his room. He wanted to play with his toys. So, he decided to ignore his mom and keep playing.

But ignoring his mom was a serious mistake. When his dad came home, he saw Timmy's messy room and got very upset. Timmy realized that he should have listened to his mom and cleaned his room. From that day on, Timmy always listened to his parents and never ignored them again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to eat toast with jam on it for breakfast every day. Her favorite jam was strawberry because it was very sweet and yummy.

One day, Lily got jam all over her hands and face while she was eating. Her mom told her she needed to wash her hands and face before she could go play. Lily went to the sink and washed her hands and face with soap and water.

Later that day, Lily went to the park to play with her friends. They all wanted to play on the popular slide, but it was very dirty. Lily remembered how important it was to wash things that were dirty, so she got a bucket of water and washed the slide until it was clean. Now all of her friends could play on it safely!

Tommy and Amy were walking to the park together. Amy was very excited to go, but Tommy seemed a bit nervous. 

"What's wrong Tommy?", asked Amy.

"I'm not sure I want to go to the park" said Tommy quietly. 

Amy was puzzled. She asked Tommy why he felt nervous. 

Tommy sheepishly replied "I heard the park has a bakery, and I don't like pastries".

Amy smiled and said "But don't you like cookies? They have those too!"

Tommy thought for a moment and decided he wanted to try some cookies. So the two friends decided to discuss the best way to get to the park. Soon enough they were on their way and Tommy was feeling much less nervous.

Once upon a time there was a boy named Paul. He was very kind and humble. He liked to help people and always had a smile on his face.

One day, he was walking down the street, when he saw an old woman in a doorway. He stopped and talked to her and listened to her stories. She was very happy to see him.

Paul wanted to help the woman, so he gave her a hug. She was so touched by Paul's kindness, that she gave him a present.

The present was a tiny box. When Paul opened the box, he saw a beautiful necklace with a face on it. He recognized the face right away. It was the face of the woman.

Paul was very happy and thanked the woman for the necklace. From then on, he wore it around his neck and was reminded of the old woman and her humble kindness.

Jim was very frightened when he arrived at the barber's shop. It was his first time getting a haircut! He didn't want his mum to leave him alone with the strange man.

"Don't worry," said the barber. He smiled and handed Jim a big lollipop. "I'll look after you and give you the best haircut ever."

Jim's frown disappeared and he couldn't help but be excited. The barber put a cape around him, and the chair felt like a magic carpet ride. Soon, Jim felt his hair being trimmed, and the barber even gave him some funny glasses to look through. When Jim looked in the mirror, he saw the best haircut ever! He was so happy, he forgot all about being scared.

Mum smiled when she saw Jim. She was so proud of him for sitting so still for such a long time.

"Well done, my boy!" she said, giving him a big hug. 

Jim smiled and couldn't wait to show his friends his new haircut.

Once there was a girl named Amy who was three years old. She was very strong, she could lift things that were heavier than she was! Every day Amy would study very hard.

"Daddy, what is it like to study?" she asked one day.

"It means to look hard at something and learn it, Amy," her dad said.

Amy was very happy and she wished she could study even harder. But there was just too much to learn and she felt overwhelmed.

"Daddy, can you help me?" Amy asked.

"Sure can," he said. "We can study together. Then our wishes will both be stronger!"

So, that's what the two of them did. They studied together, and before Amy knew it, she was learning new things faster and easier than ever before!

One day, Jimmy went to the garden to play. He was so happy that he lay on the grass and enjoyed the sunshine.

Suddenly, Jimmy found something on the grass. He ran closer and saw it was a hanger. Jimmy smiled and picked it up. It was hard and felt cool.

"What shall I do with it?" Jimmy said to himself. Just then, Jimmy had an idea - he would make a swing. He looked around and found a long, strong branch on a nearby tree. 

He hung the hanger onto the branch and tried it out. "Hurray! It's a swing", shouted Jimmy. He swung for a few minutes and then decided to lie down for a rest.

Jimmy leaned back into the swing and hugged the hanger. The swing was hard but comfy and Jimmy felt so happy. 

"Thank you hanger," he said, smiling. "You've made my day!"

Once there was a deaf girl who liked to have fun. On every holiday, she liked to fold just about everything she saw. She folded all of her blankets, her pillows, her stuffed animals and even her clothes! 

One day, she went on a vacation with her family. On the airplane, she was bored so she started to fold the napkins and tissues they gave her. When she saw the people around her, she even tried folding their newspapers and books. 

When they arrived at their destination, the little girl thought it was the perfect time to have some more fun. She found lots of things to fold, like her mom's towel, her dad's hat and even her brother's shoes! Then, she kept making fun folding shapes, like animals, birds and drums.

Finally, it was time to go back home. On the flight, the girl was not as bored as before. So, instead of folding, she just watched all the people around her. She was so amazed how everybody was talking, it almost felt like a special holiday for the deaf girl!

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny named Benny. Benny was very shy and always stayed close to the ground. One day, Benny met a friendly squirrel named Sammy. Sammy asked Benny if he wanted to play hide and seek.

Benny was nervous but agreed to play. Sammy counted to ten while Benny hid behind a tree. Sammy found Benny quickly and they played again. This time, Benny counted and Sammy hid.

When it was Sammy's turn to count again, Benny had an idea. He dug a hole in the ground and hid inside. Sammy looked and looked but couldn't find Benny. Finally, Benny popped out of the hole and surprised Sammy.

Sammy was impressed by Benny's clever hiding spot and they both laughed. Benny learned that sometimes it's good to be brave and try new things. The moral of the story is to not be shy and to count on yourself to have fun.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to read her dictionary very fast. One day, she went to the park to play with her friends. 

"Hey Lily, do you want to play with us?" her friends asked.

"No, I want to read my dictionary," Lily replied.

"But we're playing a fun game, you'll like it!" her friends said.

Lily didn't mind and kept reading her dictionary. Suddenly, she felt a strong wind and a big branch fell on her head. She got hurt and had to go to the hospital.

From that day on, Lily learned that it's important to play with friends and not just mind her dictionary all the time.

One day it was raining. The rain was cold and wet. A little girl named Grace was looking out of a window. She saw an old man outside. He was grumpy. He had an umbrella, but the rain was coming down so hard that it did not help much. 

Grace felt sorry for the old man, so she got a glass from the kitchen. She opened the window and offered it to the old man. He smiled. He thanked her and put the glass over his head. The glass kept him dry and he thanked Grace again.

Grace smiled and waved goodbye. She was happy that she could help the grumpy old man.

Once upon a time, there was a famous cat. All the other cats wanted to be like the famous cat! One day, the famous cat found some celery in her garden. She was so happy! She accepted the celery and showed all of her friends. Everyone was excited, and they all wanted some celery too. 

Every day, the famous cat accepted the celery and shared it with her friends. All of the cats could now enjoy being famous and eating delicious celery! They were very happy and enjoyed the celery every day.

The End.

Once upon a time, in a small village, there lived a little girl named Lily. She had a pretty bracelet that her mom gave her. She wore it every day. Lily loved to blink her eyes and watch the bracelet sparkle in the sun. One mild day, she went to the park to play.

At the park, Lily met a boy named Tim. Tim saw Lily's bracelet and wanted to have it. He said, "Lily, can I have your bracelet? It's so pretty." Lily thought for a moment and then said, "No, Tim. My mom gave it to me. It's special."

Tim was sad, but he understood. They played together all day and had lots of fun. When it was time to go home, Lily looked at her bracelet and thought of her new friend. She decided to give Tim another bracelet from her collection.

The next day, Lily gave Tim a different bracelet. He was so happy! They played together every day and became best friends. They learned that sharing and being kind made them both happy.

The moral of the story is that sharing brings happiness to everyone.

Lily and Ben were best friends. They liked to play in the open field near their homes. They ran, jumped, and rolled in the grass. They saw many animals and flowers.

One day, they found a big hill in the field. It was very high and steep. Lily wanted to climb it, but Ben was scared. He said, "It is too hard. We might fall. Let us go back."

Lily said, "No, Ben. We can do it. It will be fun. I will help you. Come on, be brave." She encouraged him to follow her. She held his hand and started to climb.

Ben was still scared, but he trusted Lily. He followed her up the hill. They climbed slowly and carefully. They stopped to rest and look around. They saw the field, the trees, the sky, and the sun. They felt happy and proud.

They reached the top of the hill. They shouted, "We did it! We did it!" They hugged and smiled. They saw a big rainbow in the sky. It was beautiful and bright. They said, "Wow! Look at that! It is a gift for us!"

They thanked the rainbow and the hill. They slid down the hill and ran back to the field. They played some more and then went home. They told their parents about their adventure. They said, "We climbed a big hill. We saw a rainbow. We had fun. We are brave." Their parents hugged them and said, "We are proud of you. You are brave. You are good friends."

Once upon a time there was an ugly rod. It was old and rusty. Every day it stood by itself at the bottom of a ditch. One day, a little 3 year old girl called Sarah walked by. She saw the rod and was interested in it. She bent down and picked it up. It felt funny and cold, like it had been in the ditch for a long time. 

Sarah was excited and wanted to take the ugly rod home with her. She thought it would be fun to draw and colour on it. Sarah stood back up and put the rod over her shoulder. She ran all the way home, passing through fields and over bridges, with the rod very securely held in her hands. 

Back at home, Sarah put the rod in her bedroom. Every time she saw it she felt so happy and excited because she knew she was the only person who had it. She was amazed at how ugly and yet special it was all at the same time. She could not believe she had found this amazing rod. 

The rod lay in Sarahâ€™s bedroom for a long time and she still stands by it every day. She knows that the ugly rod is part of her and she will never forget it.

He was so excited. Tom ran to the door to go outside. He saw the sun shining brightly in the sky.

John had a troubled day. After school, he decided to go to the park. He sat down and put his backpack on the rail. Suddenly, he heard a voice. He looked around and saw a girl. She waved and said "Hi!". John wasn't sure what to do but he waved back.

The girl said her name was Jill and she asked him if he wanted to play. John smiled and said yes. They played tag and hide and seek together. At one point, they both ended up on the rail together laughing.

John and Jill had so much fun together. By the time they said goodbye, they were both smiling and happy. They said they would meet again soon and waved goodbye.

John went home feeling much less troubled than when he left school. He had a new friend now and he was very excited to meet her again soon.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy who loved to play with his toys. He had a big collection of cars, trucks, and trains. One day, Timmy found a shiny rock in his backyard and he thought it was a treasure. He said, "This is mine!"

Timmy's mom saw him holding the rock and said, "Let's record this moment in our photo album!" Timmy smiled and held up the rock for the picture. But then, the sky turned gloomy and it started to rain. Timmy and his mom ran inside and looked at the picture they just took. They laughed and said, "Even though it's raining, we still had fun!"

Once upon a time there was a sunflower. It was a very fine sunflower. Its petals were bright and yellow and it was in a pretty garden. Everywhere the sunflower went, it made the garden look pretty.

One day, someone said they were going to let the sunflower go. The sunflower was scared, but it also felt excited. It didn't know what was going to happen.

The sunflower was taken away and it started to get cold. It had no place to go. It was so scared and tried to find some sunshine. But there was none! 

The sunflower was so sad and lonely. Eventually, it died because it didn't have enough sunshine. So the bad ending was that the sunflower was let go and it never came back.

Lily was in her classroom. She saw a large desk in the corner which was the teacher's. Although it was distant, she could see the colorful papers and objects on it. Lily was only three but she was learning a lot in school. She wanted to learn new things!

So one day, while her teacher was not around, Lily decided to walk to the desk. When she got there she looked carefully at all the things on the desk. She touched a pencil and pretended to write like her teacher did. She also looked at a book and pretended to be a scientist. Even though she couldn't read yet, she had fun pretending!

After a few minutes, Lily heard someone coming. It was her teacher. She quickly ran back to her seat. On her way she was very careful to make sure she didn't get caught.

The next day, Lily was very happy when the teacher asked her to come to the desk. She had learned that it was OK for her to explore and use her imagination. So, she went to the desk with a smile on her face, ready to learn something new.

Once upon a time, there was a big purple rocket. It stood tall and shiny in the sun. One day, a little boy named Tim saw the rocket and wanted to go inside. He knew that if he could enter the rocket, he would find something fun.

The next day, Tim went to the rocket with his friend, Sue. They were both very excited to see what was inside. They opened the door and entered the rocket. Inside, they found a big red button with a sign that said, "Do not push." Tim and Sue looked at each other and smiled.

They knew they shouldn't push the button, but they couldn't resist. Tim pushed the button and suddenly, the purple rocket started to shake. It went up, up, up into the sky! Tim and Sue were so happy to be flying in the rocket. They looked out the window and saw the stars and the moon. They knew that they had found the fun they were looking for.

Once upon a time, there was a big, strong bear. The bear wanted to try some oat, but his friend the fox wanted to resist. The bear was very brave, but the fox was clever and brilliant.

The fox said to the bear, "Let's not eat oat. It's not nice!" But the bear was determined. He said "I won't resist! I will try the oat!"

So the fox knew he could not stop the bear. With a tiny bit of fear, he replied "Okay, but you might be sorry!"

The bear ate the oat and it was delicious. But suddenly, he started to feel very sick. He could not move, he was in so much pain. The fox was sad, he knew he was right to resist.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat mint candies. One day, her mom gave her a whole bag of mints. Lily was so lucky!

Lily went to play with her friends. She shared some mints with them. Her friends loved the mints too. They asked Lily where she got them. Lily told them her mom gave them to her.

Later that day, Lily's friends went to the store to buy their own mints. But they didn't have any money. They asked Lily if she could share her mints again. Lily said no. She remembered her mom telling her that it's not nice to ask for things you can't have. So, Lily's friends went home without any mints. Lily felt sad for them, but she knew it was the right thing to do.

Once upon a time, there was a smart little girl named Lily. She loved to test things out and see how they worked. One day, she decided to test the bathroom sink by turning on the faucet and watching the water flow.

But something went wrong. The water didn't stop flowing and soon the bathroom was filled with water. Lily tried to turn off the faucet, but it was stuck. She didn't know what to do and the water kept rising.

Eventually, the water flooded the whole house and Lily's family had to move away. Lily was very sad that her testing had caused such a big problem. She learned that sometimes it's important to be careful when testing things out.

Once upon a time, there was a fox. He was lonely. He wanted a friend.

But he didn't know anyone. He didn't know how to get a friend.

Then one day, he saw a rabbit. He said hello. The rabbit said hello back.

The fox was happy! He had a friend. He wanted to learn more about the rabbit.

So the fox asked the rabbit to stay. The rabbit said yes.

The fox and the rabbit became best friends. They learned all kinds of things together. They played and had fun together.

The fox was no longer lonely. And he was very happy.

Once upon a time, there was a stubborn rabbit. He always ran away from people and animals. One day, he wanted to hide from the world. He hopped into a hole and stayed there.

He was so snug inside the hole. But the hole was too small for his big, fuzzy ears! He couldn't stay inside for very long.

The rabbit tried his best to find another spot to hide. He hopped and hopped, until he found the perfect place. He hopped inside a bush and moved some leaves to cover himself.

People and animals were still near, but he was hidden well. The rabbit was so happy with his hiding spot! He stayed there until the sun went down. Then he hopped away to find his dinner.

The stubborn rabbit always found the best spots to hide from the world. He was very clever!

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She was very nice.
One Wednesday morning she woke up, and saw the sun shining outside. She decided it was going to be a nice day. So the little girl opened the curtains, and looked out the window.

She saw her garden and she wanted to go play in it. So the little girl opened her bedroom door and stepped out. Then she opened the front door and went outside.

The little girl saw all the beautiful flowers in her garden. She wanted to pick one. So she opened the garden gate and ran over to them.

She plucked a beautiful red flower from the ground and thanked the garden for being so nice. The little girl went back inside, feeling happy and content.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to play in the kitchen with his toy pan. One day, Tim saw a tiny bug in the kitchen. The bug wanted to escape, but it was stuck in a corner.

Tim said to the bug, "Don't worry, little bug. I will help you escape!" He took his toy pan and gently scooped up the bug. Tim carried the bug to the open window and set it free.
