The bug was very grateful to Tim. It said, "Thank you, Tim, for helping me escape. I am so grateful!" Tim smiled and waved goodbye to the bug. From that day on, Tim and the bug became the best of friends.

Sara liked to play with her mom's makeup. She liked to put on lipstick, eyeshadow, and blush. She thought she looked pretty and grown-up. But her mom did not like it when Sara used her makeup. She said it was not for little girls. She said it could make Sara's skin bad or hurt her eyes.

One day, Sara saw her mom's makeup bag on the table. She wanted to play with it again. She knew her mom would be angry, but she could not resist. She took the bag and ran to her room. She locked the door and opened the bag. She saw many colors and shiny things. She smiled and started to put them on her face.

But she did not know how to use them well. She put too much lipstick and it smeared on her teeth. She put too much eyeshadow and it made her eyes look dark and scary. She put too much blush and it made her cheeks look red and hot. She looked in the mirror and did not like what she saw. She felt sad and scared. She wanted to take it off, but she did not know how.

She heard her mom knocking on the door. She said, "Sara, open the door. What are you doing in there?" Sara felt more scared. She did not want her mom to see her face. She did not want her mom to be mad at her. She said, "No, mom, go away. I don't want to talk to you."

Her mom felt troubled. She did not know what was wrong with Sara. She did not know why Sara was hiding from her. She said, "Sara, please open the door. I love you. I want to help you. I'm not angry. I'm worried." Sara heard her mom's voice and felt sorry. She did not want to make her mom worried. She did not want to be mean to her mom. She loved her mom too. She said, "OK, mom, I'll open the door. But don't laugh at me. I made a mistake."

She opened the door and showed her mom her face. Her mom did not laugh. She hugged Sara and said, "Oh, Sara, you don't need makeup to be pretty. You are beautiful just the way you are. Makeup is for grown-ups, and even they don't need it all the time. It's OK to make mistakes, but you have to be careful with things that are not for you. Come on, let's go to the bathroom and wash your face. I'll show you how to do it gently and safely."

Sara nodded and followed her mom. She felt better and learned a lesson. She decided not to play with her mom's makeup again. She decided to play with her own toys instead. She said, "Thank you, mom, for being nice to me. I'm sorry for being naughty. I love you, mom." Her mom said, "I love you too, Sara. You are my sweet girl." They smiled and hugged. They were happy.

Once upon a time, there was a girl called Amy. She liked to create things with her toys. One day, she had a great idea. She wanted to create an escape. With some sticks, stones and sweet honey, she made a wonderful escape. 

First, she found some sticks and started to build the escape. She used the sticks to make a wall. Then she put some stones around the wall to make sure no one could get over the wall. Finally, she put some sweet honey on top of the wall. The honey made the escape smell sweet. 

Then, Amy went into the escape and put a door in front of it. She locked the door so that no one could get in. Now Amy had her very own escape! She could hide away from her family and play without being bothered. 

Amy was very happy because she had made her own escape. She had used her imagination to create something that was just for her. And it was sweet too!

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Max. Max lived in a big city with many other dogs. Max always tried to be the best dog he could be.

One day, Max saw a new dog named Sam. Sam was very good at running and jumping. Max was jealous of Sam because he wanted to be the best dog. Max tried to run and jump like Sam, but he could not do it. Max was sad.

Max's mom saw him and said, "Max, you don't need to be like Sam. You are good at many things too." Max listened to his mom and tried to be happy with what he could do. Soon, Max and Sam became friends and played together. Max learned that it is better to be happy with who you are than to be jealous of others.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Jake. Jake was an adventurous boy, who loved to explore new places. He wanted to store new things and trade with others.

One day, Jake decided to go on a trading mission. He brought along some of his treasures and he was super excited! He hopped on his bike and pedaled off, with a sense of determination. 

When Jake reached the trade area, he saw lots of interesting things. He started trading and he was delighted when he got something special in return. He went home feeling very happy and proud.

Jake stored all of his new treasures in his closet, waiting to use them in his next big adventure!

Once, there was an elderly man who was walking down the street. He was looking for something, but he did not know what. Suddenly, the wind blew, and it lead the man to a little store. Inside the store, the man smelled something sweet and minty. He followed the smell, and it lead him to a display of mints. The man was so happy! He bought a bag of mints and thanked the store owner for helping him find what he was looking for. He smiled and walked away, munching on the delicious mints. The elderly man was so happy that the wind had lead him to the store. Whenever he wanted a mint, he knew what to do-- thanks to the wind that lead him to the store.

Once upon a time, there was a big castle. In the castle, there lived a loyal king. The loyal king had many friends. They all liked to play and have fun.

One day, the loyal king said to his friend, "Let's give food to everyone in the castle!" His friend was happy and said, "Yes, let's do it!" So, they went to the kitchen and took lots of food. They gave apples, bananas, and bread to everyone.

The people in the castle were very happy. They said, "Thank you, loyal king!" The loyal king and his friend smiled. They were happy to give and help others. From that day on, they always gave and shared with everyone in the castle.

One day, a boy named Jack want to eat pie for dinner. He asked his mom for some, but she said no. Jack was sad and asked why not. His mom told him that the pie he wanted was too hard to make.

Jack thought for a while and then had an idea. He asked his mom if she wanted help. She said yes and they both went off to the kitchen. Jack opened the cupboards and found what they needed to make the pie.

Then they got to work. Jack's mom showed him how to mix the ingredients and roll out the dough. Jack was having so much fun!

When the pie was in the oven, Jack said, "We did it! It will be easy to take out." His mom agreed and told Jack to shut the oven door. 

But when Jack shut the oven door, he heard a loud ping! His mom had forgotten to put the timer on. The pie was cooked, but it had gone a bit brown on top.

Jack's mom smiled at Jack and said, "See, it wasn't so hard to make the pie after all." Jack smiled and they both enjoyed the warm, delicious pie.

Once upon a time, there was a helpless pit. It was deep and dark, and no one ever came near it. One day, there was a soft noise and something started to happen. A tiny flower had begun to bloom, right in the darkest corner of the pit. It was the most beautiful thing the pit had ever seen. The flower shone and brought light and happiness to the helpless pit. Everyone was amazed and happy, but the flower didn't stay forever. Soon, the petals began to fall off and the flower disappeared. But the pit was still happy because the flower had made it bloom. 

The End.

One day, Joe was very troubled. He wanted to fix something but he didn't know what. He walked around, looking for something to do, when he saw an old, rusty motorcycle. He knew right away what he wanted to do - decorate it! He got some paint, glue and some sparkles and set to work. He painted the bike different colors and added some sparkles to make it even more special. When he was done, Joe was so proud of his work. Everyone in the town would stop and admire Joe's beautiful, decorated motorcycle. Joe was no longer troubled. He was so happy and excited to show off his work.

Once upon a time there was a little boy named Tom. Tom was very sick and one day his mom took him to the doctor. "Hello doctor," mom said. Tom heard the doctor say, "Hello Tom, I can help make you better."

The doctor looked in Tom's ears and said, "You need medicine!" Mom said it looked expensive but the doctor said it was worth it and would help Tom feel better. 

Mom bought the medicine and gave it to Tom. He took it like a big boy and soon he felt much better. Tom was so happy and ran around the house singing and laughing.

The End.

Once upon a time, there was a furry cat named Kitty. Kitty lived in a small house with a little girl named Sue. Sue loved Kitty very much and played with her every day.

One day, Sue made a sandwich for lunch. She put it on a plate and sat down to eat. Kitty came over and sniffed the sandwich. She liked the smell and wanted some too. Kitty looked at Sue and said, "Meow, meow!" Sue knew that Kitty was asking for some of her sandwich.

Sue said, "Kitty, you can't have my sandwich. It's not for cats." But Kitty did not give up. She meowed louder and louder, demanding some of the sandwich. Sue finally gave in and shared a small piece with Kitty. They both enjoyed their lunch together and were happy.

Lily and Ben were friends. They liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a big dog. The dog had a red collar and a long tail. The dog looked friendly.

"Hello, dog!" Lily said. "Do you want to play with us?"

The dog wagged its tail and barked. It came closer to Lily and Ben. Ben was scared of the dog. He hid behind a tree.

"Lily, be careful!" Ben said. "We don't know the dog. It might bite us."

Lily did not listen to Ben. She trusted the dog. She thought the dog was nice. She gave the dog a snack. She had a cookie in her pocket. The dog ate the cookie and licked Lily's hand.

"See, Ben? The dog is helpful. It likes us. It is our friend." Lily said.

Ben shook his head. He did not trust the dog. He thought the dog was greedy. He wanted to go home.

Lily and the dog played for a while. They ran and jumped and rolled on the grass. Ben watched them from the tree. He felt lonely and sad.

Then, something bad happened. The dog saw a squirrel. The dog wanted to catch the squirrel. The dog ran after the squirrel. The dog forgot about Lily. The dog pulled Lily with its collar. Lily fell down. She hurt her knee. She cried.

"Help! Help!" Lily shouted. "The dog is hurting me!"

Ben heard Lily. He ran to help her. He tried to pull the dog away. But the dog was too strong. The dog bit Ben's arm. Ben cried too.

A man came to the park. He saw Lily and Ben and the dog. He was angry. He was the dog's owner. He shouted at the dog. He took the dog away. He said sorry to Lily and Ben. He said they should not play with strange dogs. He said they should be careful.

Lily and Ben were hurt. They were scared. They were sorry. They learned a lesson. They learned to not trust strange dogs. They learned to listen to their friends. They learned to be careful.

Once upon a time there was a gifted hockey player. He was very good at playing the sport. Every day he practiced his skills in the park.

He would rest between drills and games. He would take a break and sip some water. After resting he was ready to practice again.

Sometimes his hockey marbles would go very fast. He was so proud when his mom cheered him on. He could feel that he was getting gifted at playing hockey.

At the end of the day he was tired. He needed to rest his body and mind. So he grabbed his hockey stick and went home. He needed some rest to be ready for the next day.

Once upon a time, there was a little rabbit named Remy. Remy loved to race with his friends. One day, Remy saw a big, dirty carrot. He wanted to take it home, but it was too big.

Remy asked his friend, Tim the turtle, for help. "Tim, can you help me take this big, dirty carrot home?" Remy asked. Tim said, "Yes, Remy! Let's race to see who can get it home first!" So, Remy and Tim started to race with the big, dirty carrot.

Remy was very fast, but Tim was slow. Remy got tired and stopped to rest. Tim kept going and won the race. Remy was sad, but Tim said, "We can share the big, dirty carrot, Remy!" They both smiled, and together, they cleaned the carrot and ate it.

Mommy was careful. She took Jack to the doctor and the doctor said he needed an x-ray. Jack was a bit scared but Mommy held him tight.

The doctor put a special machine over Jack and said, "We need to take a picture. This machine takes a special x-ray. It will be over soon."

Mommy smiled and hugged Jack. The doctor said, "We need to take a few x-rays and we will replace them. That means we will take one and put another in so we can see how Jack is doing."

After the x-rays were taken Jack was feeling a bit better. The doctor said that Jack was going to be all better very soon. Mommy and Jack hugged and they were so happy.

Once upon a time there was a mixer. The mixer liked to wave hi to everyone. It was an easy thing for it to do. The mixer waved to the birds in the sky and the ants on the ground. Everyone was happy to see the mixer wave.

One day the mixer had an idea. It wanted to mix some things together. It waved to the trees and asked if it could have some leaves. The trees said yes and waved back. The mixer then waved to the sun and asked if it could have some heat. The sun agreed and waved back.

The mixer waved to the clouds and asked if they would give it some water. The clouds did and the mixer had everything it needed. The mixer then waved its arms around and mixed all the things together.

The mixer had made something new and it was very happy. The end.

Tom and Mia are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they find a peanut on the ground. Tom picks it up and looks at it.

"What is this?" he asks Mia.

Mia knows what it is. She likes to eat peanuts. She explains to Tom.

"This is a peanut. It is a kind of food. You can eat it, but you have to peel it first. It has a rough skin that you have to take off. Inside, it has a soft and yummy part. Do you want to try?"

Tom is curious. He wants to try the peanut. He tries to peel it, but it is hard. He asks Mia for help.

"Can you help me peel it? It is too rough for me."

Mia helps Tom peel the peanut. She gives him half of it. They both eat it and smile.

"Mmm, this is good. Thank you for explaining, Mia. You are a good friend."

Tom and Mia are happy. They share the other half of the peanut. Then they go back to playing in the park. They have fun.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who lived in a big world. She spoke and smiled at everyone she saw.

But the other people in the world didn't talk to her. They only talked to each other. The little girl felt very spoiled.

One day, the little girl was walking along a path. Suddenly, she heard a small voice whisper, "Hello". It was coming from a small, furry creature.

The little girl was very surprised. She began to talk to the creature, who was a special fairy. The fairy said that the little girl had a very kind heart.

The little girl was so happy that someone had finally spoken to her. She thanked the fairy, who waved goodbye and flew away.

From then on, the little girl felt much less spoiled. Whenever she felt lonely, she remembered her special friend and smiled.

Once upon a time, there was a dry tree. An owl lived in the tree. The owl had a friend, a little mouse. The mouse lived in a hole near the tree. One day, the owl and the mouse wanted to play a game.

The owl said, "Let's measure our tails!" The mouse thought it was a fun game. They both took turns to measure their tails. The mouse's tail was long, but the owl's tail was short.

The owl said, "You win, little mouse!" The mouse was very happy. They both laughed and played more games. The owl and the mouse were best friends and always had fun together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved playing with her toys and going outside to play in the sun. One day, Lily's mom asked her to deliver a package to their neighbor. 

Lily was so excited to help her mom. She grabbed the package and ran outside. The package was wrapped in brown leather and she held it tightly in her little hands. 

As she walked to the neighbor's house, she saw some kids playing with a ball. They asked her to play with them, but she said she couldn't because she had to deliver the package. 

When she arrived at the neighbor's house, she knocked on the door. The neighbor opened the door and said, "Thank you for delivering this package, Lily. You are such a good helper." Lily felt proud and happy, not ashamed like she had felt earlier when she couldn't play with the other kids.

Once upon a time there was a worm who smiled a lot. The worm was very mysterious and his friends couldn't figure out why he was always so happy.

One day the worm decided to tell them his secret. He said, "Every morning I wake up early and I go outside. I crawl around in the dirt and see all the pretty flowers. It makes me smile."

The friends were very surprised by the worm's story. They asked, "Can we come and see the flowers with you?"

The worm smiled and said, "Yes! Come and see the flowers with me. Let's go tomorrow morning."

The next day, the worm and his friends went outside and saw the beautiful flowers. They laughed and played and the worm smiled all day long.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in her garden every day. Her mommy always told her to be careful and stay close to the house.

One day, Lily's ball bounced over the fence and into the neighbor's garden. She went to get it, but she saw a big dog there. She was scared, but the dog was very dependable and didn't bark at her. 

"Can I have my ball back, please?" asked Lily. The dog picked up the ball in his mouth and jumped over the fence to give it back to her. "Thank you!" said Lily. From then on, she wasn't scared of the dog anymore and they became friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He loved to play with his toys every day. One of his favorite toys was a soldier. The soldier was very brave and always protected Timmy's other toys.

One day, Timmy saw a poor man on the street. The man looked sad and hungry. Timmy wanted to help the poor man, so he gave him some food and toys to play with.

The soldier toy saw what Timmy did and felt proud of him. The soldier knew that Timmy was a kind and caring boy. From that day on, Timmy and the soldier played together every day and always helped others in need.

Once upon a time there was a clever boy. His name was Bill. Every day Bill would go to the park to play. His favorite game was catch.

One day Bill brought a golf ball. He wanted to try playing catch with it. So Bill threw the golf ball up in the air, and he tried to catch it. But the ball was tricky and Bill could not catch it.

He kept trying again and again, until finally he got it! Bill was excited, he had caught the golf ball! He was so clever.

From then on, Bill used the golf ball whenever he wanted to play catch. He caught it every time and had lots of fun.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, her mom asked her to help prepare dinner. Lily was happy to help. She washed the vegetables and set the table.

Then, her mom asked her to cut some tomatoes with a knife. Lily was scared of the sharp knife. "It's okay," said her mom. "I'll show you how to hold it safely." Lily watched carefully and tried it herself. She was proud of herself for being brave.

After dinner, Lily's mom told her, "You did a great job helping me. Remember, sometimes things might seem scary, but if you try, you can do it!" Lily smiled and felt happy that she helped her mom.

Once upon a time, there was a colorful bird. The bird liked to sing and play the flute. One day, the bird met a frog. The frog liked to cook. They became good friends.

"Let's have a fun day!" said the bird. "I will play the flute and you can cook for us." The frog was happy and said, "Yes, I will cook yummy food for us!"

The colorful bird played the flute. The frog cooked some tasty food. They ate and had a great time. They played and laughed all day. The bird and the frog were very happy to be friends.

Once upon a time, there was a famous comet in the sky. Every night, the comet shone brightly for all to see. Everyone could tell it was special.

Then one night, something bad happened. A big, bad storm came and the comet became stuck in the sky. It was so far up high that no one could reach it.

Suddenly, a superhero appeared. With her special power she reached up from the ground and rescued the comet. She brought it safely back to Earth and the people cheered. 

The comet was now safe. It could be seen in the sky every night, shining brightly. Everyone was very thankful the superhero had rescued the famous comet.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily was very hungry and she went to her mom and said, "Mommy, I want to eat something yummy." 

Mommy said, "How about a banana? They are very tasty and good for you." 

Lily said, "No, I don't want a banana. I want something else." 

Mommy said, "Okay, let's see what we have in the kitchen." 

Suddenly, Lily looked up at the ceiling and saw a spider hanging there. She was anxious and said, "Mommy, look at the spider on the ceiling! It's scary!" 

Mommy said, "Don't worry, Lily. I will take care of it. But remember, we should never be afraid of something just because it looks scary. We should always be brave and face our fears." 

Lily learned that it's important to be brave and not let fear control her. And mommy made her a delicious sandwich to eat, which made her very happy. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lizzy. She was only three years old and loved to whistle. 

One day, she found a case, and it was very special. She looked inside and saw a tiny whistle. She put it to her lips and blew, and it made a fast, high-pitched sound. 

Lizzy ran all around, whistling as fast as she could. She twirled and leapt, and the sound echoed all through the air. Everything seemed to be filled with music! 

Lizzy went back home, but she never forgot how much fun it was to whistle so fast. Every day, she would take out the case and blow the whistle. No matter how much time passed, it was still Lizzy's favorite thing to do!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who was ready to explore. One bright sunny day, she decided to wander off and explore the forest near her home.

As she walked along the path, she stepped on something hard and pointy - it was a root! The root warned her to be careful. It said, "Be careful little girl!"

She was surprised to hear the root talking, but she quickly nodded her head and continued on her way. Soon, she came to a big bush.

The bush had red berries and the girl wanted to pick them. But then the root warned her again, "The berries are not ready to eat!"

The little girl paused and thought about the root's warning. She realized that the root was trying to help her and looked for another place to pick berries.

She thanked the root for warning her and found a bush full of ripe, juicy berries. She had a lovely snack, thanked the root for its help, and went on her way.

Billy was excited. Today he was going to ride in the car with his dad. They were going camping. Billy watched out the window, admiring the trees and fields they passed. When they finally arrived, they parked the car and got out. Billy was excited to see their tent. It was big and orange and bright. His dad put it up and Billy helped. Then they went and collected some twigs and logs for the fire.

When it got dark, they lit the fire and sat around it. Billy was so happy and even made some shapes by tossing sticks into the flames. He watched the flames until it was time to go to sleep. He and his dad went into the tent and fell asleep.
 
Even though it was noisy outside the tent, Billy was so relaxed he could barely stay awake. He drifted off thinking of their next adventure and how much fun it would be. The next morning, Billy woke up feeling excited to ride and explore the woods.

Once upon a time there was a mole who lived in a gloomy forest. He liked to cover himself in dirt so he blended in with his surroundings.

One day, the mole was feeling a bit lonely, so he decided to explore the forest to find some other animals. He saw a scarlet bird perched on a branch and a funny little rabbit hopping around the bushes.

But then the mole noticed something even more exciting â€“ a sunny meadow full of wildflowers! He scampered across the meadow, stopping to smell the flowers and jumping around in the sun. He had never felt so happy!

Suddenly, he felt a heavy rain start to fall and he quickly ran back to the gloomy forest to take cover. He burrowed into the dirt and soon he was dry and warm again.

The mole stayed in his forest for a long time, but he would often remember that sunny meadow and all the wonderful flowers he had seen.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to watch TV. His favorite show was about a cool superhero who could fly. One day, Timmy's mom said it was time to turn off the TV and go outside to play. Timmy didn't want to leave his cool superhero show.

Timmy's mom tried to convince him, but he refused to leave the TV. He started to cry and throw a tantrum. His mom got upset and turned off the TV. Timmy was so mad that he ran outside and didn't come back for a while.

When he finally came back, he realized that playing outside was cool too. He apologized to his mom and promised to listen to her next time. From then on, Timmy made sure to balance his TV time with playing outside.

Lily and Ben are best friends. They like to play together every day. They have a loyal dog named Spot. Spot likes to run and jump and bark.

One day, Lily and Ben go to the park with Spot. They see a big stage with many people. They hear music and singing. They want to see what is happening.

They go closer to the stage. They see a man with a guitar and a woman with a microphone. They are singing a song. Lily and Ben like the song. They clap their hands and dance. Spot barks and wags his tail.

The man and the woman finish the song. They say thank you to the people. The people clap and cheer. Lily and Ben clap and cheer too. Spot barks and wags his tail more.

But then, something happens. The woman drops the microphone. It makes a loud noise. The people stop clapping and cheering. They are silent. Lily and Ben are silent too. Spot is silent too.

The woman picks up the microphone. She says sorry to the people. She says she will sing another song. The people are not angry. They are kind. They clap and cheer again. Lily and Ben clap and cheer again. Spot barks and wags his tail again.

Lily and Ben are happy. They like the music and the singing. They like the man and the woman. They like the people. They like the park. They like Spot. They are best friends. They hug each other and smile.

Anna and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to run, jump and slide. They had a lot of fun. But after a while, they felt tired and thirsty.

"Let's rest for a bit," Anna said. "I have some juice and crackers in my bag."

"OK," Ben said. "I'm hungry too."

They sat down on a bench and opened Anna's bag. Anna gave Ben a juice box and a cracker. She took one for herself too.

They sipped their juice and nibbled their crackers. They felt better.

But then, Ben made a funny face. He spit out his cracker and said, "Yuck! This is spicy!"

Anna looked at her cracker. It had red dots on it. She remembered that her mom had packed some spicy crackers for her dad. She had taken the wrong bag by mistake.

"I'm sorry, Ben," Anna said. "These are not for us. These are for my dad. He likes spicy things."

Ben drank some more juice and said, "It's OK, Anna. I don't like spicy things. But I like you. You are my friend."

Anna smiled and said, "You are my friend too, Ben. Next time, I will bring some sweet things for us."

They hugged and finished their juice. Then they got up and played some more. They had a lot of fun.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird. The bird was very happy and loved to sing all day long. One day, the bird was feeling very tired and decided to lay down on a branch to rest. While resting, the bird saw a big red berry on the ground. The bird was very hungry and wanted to eat the berry, but it smelled funny. The bird remembered that its mom had taught it about poison and knew not to eat it. The bird was grateful to its mom for teaching it about danger. The little bird continued to sing and fly happily in the sky.

Once upon a time, there was a little duck named Quack. Quack lived in a pond with his friends. One day, Quack's mommy asked him to cook dinner for their family. Quack was nervous because he had never cooked before, but he wanted to make his mommy proud.

Quack went to the pond to find some food for dinner. He found some yummy fish and some fresh vegetables. He put them in a pot and started to cook. Quack stirred the pot and waited for the food to be ready.

Finally, dinner was ready and Quack's family loved it! They were so proud of him for cooking such a delicious meal. Quack was happy and not nervous anymore. From that day on, Quack loved to cook and make yummy meals for his family and friends in the pond.

Lily was a nice girl who liked flowers. She had a flower bed in her garden, where she planted many seeds. She watered them every day and waited for them to grow. She wanted to see the pretty colors and smell the sweet smells.

One morning, she woke up early and ran to the window. She saw something new in her flower bed. It was a big, yellow flower, with a round face and long petals. It looked like a sun. Lily was very happy. She put on her shoes and ran outside.

"Hello, flower!" she said. "You are so pretty and bright. Do you have a name?"

The flower smiled and nodded. It said, "Yes, I do. I am a sunflower. I like to follow the sun and turn my face to it. It makes me warm and happy. Do you like the sun, too?"

Lily nodded, too. She said, "Yes, I do. The sun is nice and bright. It makes me warm and happy, too. Can I be your friend, sunflower?"

The sunflower smiled again. It said, "Of course, you can. You are a nice girl who likes flowers. You planted me and watered me and waited for me to grow. You are my friend, Lily."

Lily hugged the sunflower and said, "Thank you, sunflower. You are my friend, too. You are the best flower in my flower bed. I will come and see you every day."

The sunflower and Lily became good friends. They talked and played and watched the sun together. They made each other happy. They were the nicest pair in the garden.

Lily was a lazy cat. She liked to sleep all day on the warm rug. She did not like to play with the other cats or help her mom with the chores. She only wanted to nap and dream.

One day, Lily saw a bright ball of sunshine outside the window. It looked so pretty and shiny. She wanted to pick it and keep it for herself. She jumped off the rug and ran to the door. She asked her mom to let her out.

Her mom said, "Lily, you can go out, but be careful. The sunshine is not a toy. It is very hot and can hurt you. And don't forget to come back before dark."

Lily did not listen to her mom. She thought she knew better. She ran outside and chased the sunshine. She tried to catch it with her paws, but it always moved away. She followed it across the yard, over the fence, and into the woods.

She did not notice that the sky was getting darker and the air was getting colder. She did not hear the other animals making noises. She did not see the shadows creeping up on her. She only saw the sunshine, and she wanted it more than anything.

She finally reached a clearing where the sunshine was resting on a big rock. She jumped on the rock and tried to pick the sunshine. But it was not a ball. It was a fire. And it burned her fur and skin. She screamed and ran away. But it was too late. She was hurt and lost and scared.

She wished she had listened to her mom. She wished she had stayed on the rug. She wished she had been a good cat. She learned that being lazy and greedy was not good. She learned that the sunshine was not for picking. She learned that some things are better to look at than to touch.

One day, a little boy named Tim wanted to watch his favorite show on the television. Tim was very calm as he sat on the floor in front of the television. He waited for his show to start.

His mom walked into the room and said, "Tim, please stand up and turn on the television." Tim stood up and pushed the button on the television. The screen lit up, and his show began to play.

As Tim watched his show, a friendly dog named Spot came into the room. Spot sat down next to Tim and watched the television too. They both enjoyed the show and were very calm and happy.

Once upon a time there was a curious rabbit. He liked to explore and one day he came across a shiny buckle. He decided to have a closer look so he hopped closer. It was a very special buckle that fastened a belt around a tree. 

The rabbit knew the tree could use some help, so he wanted to lend a helping hand. He hopped over to the tree and tugged the belt tight. The buckle shined and clicked shut. 

The rabbit was so proud of what he had done. He hopped away feeling happy and satisfied. The tree was thankful for the rabbitâ€™s kindness and knew that it could always count on the rabbit to lend a helping hand.

Once upon a time, there was a big, heavy rock. It was too heavy for anyone to move. One day, a little bird flew by and saw the rock. The bird wanted to play with the rock, but it was too heavy to lift.

The bird felt sad and left the rock alone. But then, a little mouse came along. The mouse saw the rock and wanted to play with it too. The bird warned the mouse that the rock was too heavy to move, but the mouse didn't listen and tried to move it anyway.

The mouse couldn't move the rock, and the bird told the mouse that it should have listened and ignored the rock. From that day on, the little bird and the little mouse played together and ignored the big, heavy rock.

Once upon a time, there was a happy dog named Spot. Spot loved to run and play in the park with his friends. One day, Spot's friend Max got sick and couldn't play anymore. Spot was sad because he missed playing with Max.

Spot decided to visit Max and see if he was feeling better. When Spot arrived, Max was still feeling sick and could not stand up. Spot stayed with Max and kept him company until he felt better.

Finally, Max returned to the park and was healthy again. Spot was so happy to see his friend and they played together again. They both felt very happy and healthy.

Once upon a time, in a small village, there was a girl named Lucy. Lucy wanted to try her luck and paint a pastel. She had a box of colours, but her brother Timmy insisted on using the green pastel. Lucy was selfish and argued with him, thinking that she should be the one to use it. But she agreed with Timmy, not wanting Timmy to be disappointed.

A week went by and Lucy tried her luck. She mixed many colours together to create a beautiful mural, showing a bright sunshine and a lake with swans and pink flowers. She suddenly ran out of colours to use and realised that the only colour she had left was the green pastel. Lucy was surprised and thankful to her brother, who had insisted on using the green pastel instead. 

That day, Lucy learned a lesson. She realised that it was not always necessary to be selfish, instead, it was far more beneficial to put others' ideas first. Had she not listened to her brother, she would not have completed her vibrant mural. 

The moral of this story is to never be too selfish and always take the time to listen to the ideas of others. You never know when another's opinion could turn out to be just what you needed.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Bobo. Bobo was always ready to play and have fun. One day, he saw a big step in the park. He thought it would be fun to jump on it.

Bobo tried to settle near the step, but he was too excited. He ran around and around, not paying attention to where he was going. He didn't see the big hole near the step.

Bobo kept playing near the step, not knowing about the hole. He was so happy and ready to jump. But then, Bobo fell into the hole. He couldn't get out and he was very sad. The fun day at the park had a bad ending for poor Bobo.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and her favorite was a teddy bear. One day, Lily's mom gave her a shiny coin and told her it had a special value. Lily didn't understand what that meant, but she loved the way the coin sparkled in the light.

Later that day, Lily's dad came home and asked her to help him count some apples. Lily loved to count and she was very good at it. She counted the apples one by one and told her dad the number. Her dad was very proud of her and said she was very smart.

Before going to bed, Lily put her shiny coin in a safe place. Her mom had told her that it was important to keep it safe because it was valuable. Lily felt happy knowing that her coin was safe and that she had learned a new word - valuable. She fell asleep with her teddy bear, dreaming of counting more apples and finding more valuable things.

Once upon a time, in a big forest, there was a fearful tiger. The tiger was scared of everything. He was scared of the wind, the rain, and even the little bugs.

One day, the fearful tiger found a small, lost kitten. The kitten was all alone, and it was sad. The tiger wanted to help the kitten, so he decided to carry it on his back. Together, they walked through the forest, looking for the kitten's home.

As they walked, the fearful tiger started to feel brave. He was not scared of the wind or the rain anymore. The little kitten made the tiger feel strong. Finally, they found the kitten's home, and the tiger was very happy. From that day on, the tiger was not fearful anymore. He had a new friend, and they lived happily in the big forest.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy liked to play outside with his friends. One day, Timmy's friend Billy had an axe. Timmy thought the axe was cool and asked if he could hold it. Billy said yes and gave Timmy the axe. 

Timmy swung the axe around and accidentally dropped it. The axe was hot from the sun and Timmy burned his hand trying to catch it. He started to cry and Billy asked what was wrong. Timmy showed him his burnt hand and said "It's hot and hurts!" Billy told Timmy to go inside and put some cold water on it. 

Timmy went inside and put his hand under some cold water. It felt better and he stopped crying. He learned to be careful with hot things and not to play with axes. From that day on, Timmy and Billy played catch instead. The end.

Once upon a time there lived a little girl who only had her doll to keep her company. She went to her closet one day and found a secret surprise waiting for her. Inside the closet was a little tiny door with a key hole. She tried the key she had carried around with her all day and it fit perfectly! She opened the door and found an empty room. 

It was so quiet and lonely, that the little girl started to weep. Then, suddenly she heard a tiny voice from inside the room. It was the doll she had brought with her! The doll said to her, â€œDonâ€™t worry little one, I will keep you company. Together we will fill this empty room!â€ 

The little girl smiled, no longer feeling alone and cried no more. She knew that with her special companion, the closet would never be empty again. 

The end.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Lizzie. She was three years old.

One day, Lizzie wanted to surprise her mum. She went out into the garden and saw a rough old stick in the ground. She made a promise to herself that if she dug it up she would give it to her mum as a gift.

Armed with a spade, Lizzie started to dig. The stick was stuck in the ground and Lizzie had to dig hard to get it out. Eventually she managed to free the stick and she proudly held it up for all to see.

That day, Lizzie kept her promise. She gave the stick to her mum as a surprise gift. Lizzie's mum was very pleased with her daughter's thoughtfulness and thanked her with a big hug. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a grumpy man. He was always complaining about things, from the weather to the size of the universe. Nothing was ever good enough for him.

One day, he decided to take a long walk. He walked and walked until he came to a pond. When he looked in the pond, he saw a large fish with shiny scales. The fish was smiling!

At first, the grumpy man was confused. But then he saw the sign by the pond that said 'Compliment Fish'. If you complained, it would give you a compliment. The grumpy man gave it a try.

He complained to the fish about everything in the universe. He said it was too big, too small, and it wasn't what he wanted it to be.

The fish responded with a big smile. It gave the grumpy man a big compliment: "You have such a big heart and you have been so kind to others. Your generosity and compassion make the universe a brighter place." 

The grumpy man was so surprised and so touched. His bitter attitude melted away and he filled with warmth. He thanked the fish and smiled from ear to ear. 

The grumpy man had never felt so happy. He thanked the fish one last time and walked away feeling much better.

Once there was an old man. He saw an old brick and thought it would be fun to take it home to play with. So he went to steal it. 

He was hiding behind a tree when he heard someone coming. He saw it was a little girl. She looked at the old brick and said, "That'll be nice to have for building my house."

The old man said, "You can't take that. I'm going to steal it for myself."

The little girl replied, "Well, you can't do that. That's not nice."

The old man thought for a minute. Then he said, "How about I share it with you? We can both have it and play together."

The little girl smiled and said, "Yes, that sounds fun!"

So they both took the old brick home and had lots of fun building together.

Anna and Ben were playing in the yard with their dog, Spot. They liked to throw a ball and watch Spot run and catch it. But sometimes Spot ran too far and tried to go under the fence to the other side.

"Spot, no!" Anna shouted. "You have to stay here with us. The fence is there to keep you safe."

But Spot did not listen. He squeezed under the fence and ran away. Anna and Ben were very sad and scared. They did not know where Spot went or if he would come back.

They ran to their mom and told her what happened. Mom hugged them and said, "Don't worry, we will find Spot. He is a good dog, but he is also very curious. Maybe he saw something interesting on the other side of the fence. Let's go look for him."

They got in the car and drove around the neighborhood. They called Spot's name and looked for him. They asked some people if they had seen him, but no one had. They were about to give up when they saw a sign that said, "Lost dog. Looks like Spot. Please call this number."

They followed the sign to a house with a big yard. There they saw Spot, playing with another dog. He looked happy and wagged his tail when he saw them.

"Spot!" Anna and Ben cried. They ran to him and hugged him. Spot licked their faces and barked.

"Hello, are you looking for this dog?" a man asked. He was holding the sign and a phone.

"Yes, he is ours. He ran away from our yard. We are so sorry. He is usually very obedient, but he likes to explore," Mom said.

"That's okay. He is a very friendly dog. He came to our yard and made friends with our dog, Rex. They have been having fun together. But we knew he had a family, so we put up the sign. Here, you can have him back," the man said.

He handed Spot's leash to Mom. Mom thanked him and gave him her phone number, in case Spot ever escaped again.

"Come on, Spot. Let's go home. And no more running away, okay?" Mom said.

"Okay, Mom. I'm sorry. I love you," Spot said in his dog way.

Anna and Ben smiled. They were happy to have Spot back. They decided to replace the old fence with a new one, so Spot could not go under it anymore. They also gave him a new ball and a bone, so he would have more fun in their yard. Spot was happy too. He loved his family and his new friends. He learned his lesson and never ran away again.

Once upon a time there was a wise owl who loved to carry spaghetti. Every day, he gathered as much spaghetti as he could carry and flew away. As he flew, he would drop some of the spaghetti in different places. He wanted to share it with everyone!

One day, he noticed three little birds on the ground. They were huddling together and they were very cold. So the wise owl decided to drop all of his spaghetti down to the three little birds. They clapped their hands together with delight!

The three little birds thanked the wise owl and everyone had a happy spaghetti feast! From that day on, the wise owl carried spaghetti every day and spread lots of happiness. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toy blocks. One day, she wanted to make a very big stack. But, the blocks kept falling down. Lily was not happy.

Lily's big brother, Tom, saw her trying hard. He wanted to help her. Tom told Lily, "Let me support you." Together, they tried to make the stack. They put one block on top of another. The stack was getting taller and taller.

Finally, the stack was very big. Lily and Tom were successful. They were so happy that they could make the big stack. They hugged each other and played with the blocks all day long.

Tom and Jen like to play with their toy cars. They have a big stadium where they can race and crash their cars. They pretend they are drivers and fans and make loud noises.

One day, Tom's car breaks. The wheel falls off and the car stops. Tom is sad and angry. He throws his car on the floor and cries.

"Tom, don't cry," Jen says. "We can fix your car. I have glue and tape. Come, let's go to the table and fix it."

Tom and Jen go to the table and find the glue and tape. Jen puts some glue on the wheel and sticks it back to the car. Then she wraps some tape around it to make it stronger.

"There, your car is fixed," Jen says. "Let's go back to the stadium and race again."

Tom smiles and hugs Jen. He is happy and thankful. He picks up his car and runs to the stadium. He and Jen race and crash their cars again. They have fun and forget about the scary broken car. They are good friends.

Once there was a girl named Sarah. She was three years old and she liked to explore. One day, she asked her mom to explain what style meant. Her mom smiled and said, "Style is the special way you do things. It's like your own special way of doing things that's different from other people."

Sarah thought about that for a while and then asked, "What's normal?" Her mom answered, "Normal means what most people do or what's typical or common. For example, most people wear clothes, so wearing clothes is normal."

Sarah was very happy with her mom's explanation. She already had her own special style, but now she knew special didn't have to mean not normal. She decided she was happy to be both special and normal!

Tim and Jen are playing in the garden. They have a big bucket of water and some cups. They like to pour water on the flowers and on each other.

"Look, Jen, I can pour water very high!" Tim says. He lifts his cup and pours water in the air. The water falls on his head and makes him wet.

"Ha ha, Tim, you are silly!" Jen says. She pours water on Tim's shirt and makes him wetter.

They laugh and splash each other. They do not see a small mouse hiding under a leaf. The mouse is scared of the water. He does not like to be wet. He wants to run away, but he is trapped by the bucket.

The mouse sees a hole in the bucket. He thinks he can escape through the hole. He runs to the hole and squeezes inside. But the hole is not empty. It is full of smelly cheese. The cheese is old and rotten. It sticks to the mouse's fur and makes him smelly.

"Yuck, what is that smell?" Tim says. He smells the cheese in the bucket. He does not like the smell. He looks inside the bucket and sees the mouse.

"Jen, look, there is a mouse in the bucket!" Tim says. He points to the mouse.

"Wow, a mouse!" Jen says. She looks at the mouse. She sees the cheese on the mouse. She thinks the mouse is cute. She wants to touch the mouse.

"Can I hold the mouse, Tim?" Jen says. She reaches for the bucket.

"No, Jen, the mouse is smelly!" Tim says. He pulls the bucket away from Jen. He does not want Jen to touch the mouse.

The mouse is scared of Tim and Jen. He does not want to be held. He wants to be free. He bites the cheese and makes a hole. He jumps out of the bucket and runs away.

"Bye bye, mouse!" Jen says. She waves to the mouse.

"Bye bye, smelly mouse!" Tim says. He throws the cheese away.

They go back to playing with the water. They forget about the mouse. They have fun in the garden.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Lucy. She was only three years old and she loved to explore. One day, she decided to go on an adventure.

She walked through a big forest until she reached a meadow. In the meadow were lots of animals, including deer and rabbits. Lucy was a bit frightened, but the animals gave her a warm welcome.

She watched them for a while and noticed that they were eating something tasty. She wanted to know what it was. She was brave and cautiously stepped closer. As she moved towards them, the deer and rabbits become less frightened.

Suddenly, Lucy noticed carrots and apples scattered around the meadow. She excitedly ran over and stuffed her pockets with the yummy treats.

The animals were happy to include Lucy in their snack time! She happily hugged the animals goodbye before heading home to enjoy her treats.

Once upon a time, there was a wide carpet that could talk. It lived in a little girl's room. The little girl, named Lily, loved to play on the carpet. One day, Lily asked the carpet, "Why are you so wide?" The carpet replied, "I am wide so that you and your friends can play on me."

One day, Lily's friend, Tim, came over to play. They played with their toys on the wide carpet. Tim accidentally spilled juice on the carpet. Lily got upset and said, "Now my carpet is dirty!" The carpet replied, "It's okay, I can be cleaned."

Lily's mom helped clean the carpet. Lily and Tim said sorry to the carpet. The carpet replied, "It's okay, just remember to be careful next time." The moral value of the story is to always say sorry when you make a mistake and to learn from it.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Kim. She was very hungry. She was looking for something good to eat, but she was having a hard time finding it.

Just then, she saw something colorful coming down the street. She couldn't believe her eyes! It was a giant orange mask! It had two big eyes and a big smile on the front.

Kim knew she had to try it! She ran over to the mask and put it on her face. She felt so strange and silly with it on, but she also felt happy and excited.

Suddenly, the mask started to move and come alive! It started to speak to Kim and said, â€œCome with me and I will show you something special and yummy - something to cure your hunger!â€

Kim was so excited! She followed the mask down the street and around the corner. When they arrived, she saw the most delicious looking feast she had ever seen!

Kim was so hungry and went right to it, eating and enjoying all the food. When she was done, she thanked the mask for bringing her to such a wonderful feast.

The mask smiled, gave her a hug, and said, â€œYou're welcome! Come back anytime you're feeling hungry!â€ Kim thanked the mask again and waved goodbye as she skipped away, full and happy.

Once there was a horse. His name was James. He said "hello" to all his friends. He was a normal horse, but he liked to eat a lot of apples.

One day, James went to visit his friends. He said "Hello" to the other horses. They said "Hello" and "Nice to meet you".

The horses wanted to go for a walk. James said "Let's go together". So the horses started walking.

They went to the fields and said "What a nice day". The sun was out and the birds were singing. They ate some grass and then ran and played.

James was happy to have new friends. They all said goodbye and went home. James said "See you soon!"

Once there was a loyal dog named Rex. Rex was a very strong dog and he loved to push things around. He even liked to push a big steel ball around the yard. Whenever he had the chance, he'd push the steel ball across the grass, faster and faster.

One day Rex was pushing the steel ball around the yard when a cat came by. The cat saw Rex pushing the big steel ball and he thought it looked like fun. He wanted to push the ball too, so he ran up and pushed it with his paws.

Rex saw the cat pushing the ball, so he barked to show he didn't like it. The cat ran away, but Rex was still loyal to the steel ball. He chased after it and kept pushing it around the yard.

From then on, Rex was always loyal to the steel ball. He pushed it around the yard every time he had a chance, no matter what distractions he faced.

Once upon a time, there was a clumsy little boy called Pete. He lived in a big house with his family.

One day, Pete wanted to go to the bathroom. He was very excited to go on his own. He got lost on his way.

Suddenly, he saw a big man. The man smiled at Pete and said, "Where are you going?"

Pete said, "I'm trying to find the bathroom."

The man said, "Don't worry, I will deliver you there safely."

Pete thanked the man and followed him. Soon, they arrived at the bathroom. 

The man said, "Here you are. Be careful next time, ok?"

Pete nodded and said, "Thank you, Mister."

The man smiled and said, "You're welcome." Then, he walked away.

Pete was very happy that he found the bathroom. He learned a valuable lesson about not being too clumsy!

Once upon a time, there was a farmer who had a mule. The mule was very strong and dependable. The farmer used the mule to plow the fields and carry heavy things.

One day, the farmer had to go to the market but he had no one to take care of the mule. He asked his son if he can manage to take care of the mule. The son said yes, he can manage.

The son fed the mule and gave him water. He brushed the mule's fur and talked to him. The mule was happy and so was the farmer when he came back from the market. The farmer was proud of his son for being so dependable and taking care of the mule.

Once upon a time, there was a fish named Nemo. Nemo lived in a nice reef with his friends. One day, Nemo's friends wanted to play a game, but Nemo didn't want to play. He tried to resist, but they kept asking him to play. 

Nemo swam away from his friends and found a new part of the reef he had never explored before. He saw lots of nice things like colorful plants and shiny rocks. Nemo was so happy he resisted the urge to go back to his friends and instead kept exploring the reef. 

As Nemo swam, he saw a big fish coming towards him. The fish looked scary, but Nemo remembered to resist his fear and stay calm. The big fish swam past Nemo and didn't hurt him. Nemo felt proud of himself for being brave and exploring the reef on his own.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved playing with his toy jet. He would make it fly all around the room and make loud whooshing sounds.

One day, Timmy's mom asked him if he was hungry. Timmy said yes and his mom made him a yummy sandwich. But Timmy didn't eat it all, he wanted to play with his jet some more.

Later that day, Timmy's friend Billy came over to play. Billy wanted to play with the jet too, but Timmy didn't want to share. They got into a fight and Timmy's jet broke.

Timmy felt sad and realized that he should have shared his toy. His mom told him that it's important to be kind and share with others. Timmy learned his lesson and promised to share his toys from now on. He also learned that it's important to test our actions and make sure we're doing the right thing.

Once upon a time, there were two friends, Rian and Ella. They were on an adventure to explore the underground world. They were so excited! First, Rian showed Ella a secret cave. Ella was amazed by all the different rocks and crystals. Then, they came across a cave full of strange animals. Ella was scared, but Rian showed her that the animals were friendly. After that, Rian was feeling very brave and showed Ella a deep, dark hole. Ella was scared, but she followed Rian because she trusted him. Suddenly, something moved in the hole. It was a big, fat, careless groundhog! Ella screamed and the groundhog ran away. Rian and Ella laughed, then quickly ran out of the underground world.

The end.

John went to the market one day with his mom. He saw a beautiful blue kite that he really wanted. His mom told him he couldn't have it, but he wouldn't listen. He was too excited and ran to the kite to grab it. 

Suddenly, a tough foot stepped on the kite. John was scared and turned around. There was a big man with a mean look on his face. â€œMommy,â€ John said, scared.

The man said, â€œI run the market and I wonâ€™t provide for any children running around and taking things that donâ€™t belong to them.â€ John was still scared and backed away slowly.

His mom told the man she was sorry and would pay for the kite. But the man said it was too late and he wanted John to learn a lesson. He told John to never take things that don't belong to him again, and he made John leave the market.

John and his mom had a bad ending that day. He never got the kite and he was reminded to never take things that weren't his.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. Her name was Linda. She was very brave, but she was also a little scared. One day, Linda decided to go explore a special place called the Crystal Room. She walked into the room, and suddenly she started to tremble. Everywhere she looked she could see beautiful crystals. They sparkled like diamonds. Linda was so amazed by the pretty crystals that she laughed and started to dance around the room. 

But then, Linda started to feel afraid. She started to cry. Suddenly, the room began to shake! Linda was so scared that she ran out of the room. Outside, she was safe. But the room was still trembling.

Linda was very confused. She thought it was funny that a room could tremble like that. She spread the news to all of her friends. Everyone wanted to go see the Crystal Room and experience the funny trembling. They all had a great time exploring and admiring the crystals. Linda was so happy that she had made a new discovery.

Anna was a thoughtful girl who liked to learn new things. She was good at reading, writing, and counting. She wanted to do well on her exam at school. She studied hard every day and listened to her teacher.

The day of the exam came. Anna was nervous but excited. She hoped she would remember everything she learned. She sat at her desk and waited for the teacher to give her the exam paper. She looked around and saw her friends. Some of them looked happy, some of them looked scared.

The teacher handed out the exam papers. Anna opened hers and started to read the questions. She knew some of them, but some of them were hard. She tried to think of the answers, but she felt confused. She looked at the clock and saw that she had only a few minutes left. She felt panic in her chest.

She looked at her paper again and saw a question that she did not understand at all. She did not know what to write. She felt tears in her eyes. She wanted to ask the teacher for help, but she was afraid to raise her hand. She felt like she was going to fail the exam.

She could not take it anymore. She let out a loud scream that made everyone in the room jump. The teacher ran to her and asked her what was wrong. Anna sobbed and pointed at her paper. She said, "I don't know, I don't know, I don't know!"

The teacher looked at her paper and saw the question that made her scream. It was a trick question that had no right answer. It was meant to test the students' creativity and logic. The teacher smiled and said, "Don't worry, Anna. This question is not important. You can write anything you want. There is no wrong answer. You are a thoughtful girl, I'm sure you can come up with something interesting."

Anna looked at the teacher and felt a wave of relief. She wiped her tears and smiled. She realized that she had been too worried about the exam. She decided to write something funny and silly for the trick question. She finished her exam and handed it to the teacher. She felt proud of herself.

The teacher graded the exams and gave them back to the students. Anna got a high score. She was happy and surprised. She looked at the trick question and saw what she wrote. She laughed and showed it to her friends. They laughed too. The trick question was: "What is the meaning of life?" Anna wrote: "To have fun and eat ice cream." The teacher wrote: "Good answer!"

John was a 3 year old boy. He always wanted to do something special. One day, his mum came to him and said: "John, do you want to decorate our front window?"

John was very excited and said: "Yes, I'd love to!"

His mum said: "Ok, but first let's go shopping. We should find some ornaments for you to hang up."

So, John and his mum went shopping. They found some nice ornaments and some bad ones. John found one he really liked and said: "Mum, can I have this one?"

His mum did not allow him to take the bad one and said: "No, John. It looks bad. Let's find another one."

So, John and his mum kept looking until they found the perfect ornament. John hung the ornament up and he was very excited and happy to have decorated the front window.

Sara and Tom love to play with their kayak. It is brown and big and floats on the water. They like to paddle and splash and see the fish and the birds. One day, they find a small island with a lot of flowers and trees. They decide to explore it and have a picnic.

"Look, Sara, what a pretty necklace!" Tom says, picking up a string of shells and beads. He puts it around Sara's neck and smiles. "You are very pretty, Sara. Do you want to marry me?"

Sara giggles and nods. "Yes, Tom, I want to marry you. You are very nice and funny. But how can we marry?"

Tom thinks for a moment. He remembers that his mom and dad had a ring and a cake and a party when they married. He looks around and sees a big leaf and a berry. He takes the leaf and makes a hole in it. He puts the berry in the hole and makes a ring. He gives it to Sara and says, "Here, Sara, this is your ring. Now we are married."

Sara puts the ring on her finger and hugs Tom. "Thank you, Tom, this is a beautiful ring. Now we are married."

They share their sandwich and juice and have a cake of cookies. They dance and sing and laugh. They are very happy. They get back in their kayak and paddle home. They tell their mom and dad that they are married. Their mom and dad smile and hug them. They are proud of their children. They say, "You are very sweet, Sara and Tom. But you are still very young. You can play and pretend, but you are not really married. You have to grow up and learn a lot of things before you can marry. But we love you very much and we are happy that you are friends."

Sara and Tom understand. They are not sad. They know that they are still children and have a lot of fun to have. They keep their necklace and ring and kayak. They play and pretend and dream. They are still friends. And maybe, one day, when they are big, they will marry for real.

Once upon a time, there was a bee who loved honey. He flew around looking for flowers and collecting the sweet honey. Everywhere he went, people told him how amazing he was.

One day, he saw a giant tree with lots of honey. He was so excited! He flew all around it, gathering as much as he could. But then, a huge gust of wind came and blew him away. He tried to stand up, but the wind was too strong.

Luckily, a friendly bear came to help! He took the bee back to the tree and helped him to stand up. Together they filled the bee's jar with honey. The bee was so happy and thanked the bear many times.

The bee flew away with his jar of honey, feeling so lucky. He knew he could never forget the amazing bear who helped him.

Once upon a time, there was a dog named Spot. Spot was very attractive and everyone loved him. He had a red leash that his owner, Tim, would use to take him on walks. One day, Tim and Spot went to the park.

At the park, they saw a big puddle. Tim knew that Spot loved to play in water. He thought, "I bet Spot will get all soak soon." Tim let Spot off his leash to play. Spot ran straight to the puddle and jumped in. He splashed around and got all soak.

After playing in the puddle, Spot was very wet and dirty. Tim put the leash back on Spot and took him home. When they got home, Tim gave Spot a bath. Spot was clean and attractive again. Tim was happy he had foreshadowed Spot getting soak, and they both laughed about their fun day at the park.

Once upon a time, there was a nosy little fly. He liked to buzz around and see what everyone was doing. One day, he saw a girl trying to repair her toy car. The fly wanted to help, but he was too small.

The girl saw the fly and said, "Hello, nosy fly! Can you help me fix my toy car?" The fly nodded and tried his best to help. He held a tiny part of the car with his little legs while the girl put it back together.

After they finished, the girl thanked the nosy fly and gave him a big hug. They became friends and played together every day. The fly was happy that he could help and learned that even little creatures can make a big difference.

Johnny was so excited to go for a walk in the park. It was such a beautiful day; the sun was shining brightly, and the sky was a clear blue. As Johnny and his mom walked across the park, Johnny pointed to a tall tree with a bird's nest at the top. The bird in the nest made a delicate sound that caught Johnny's attention. Together, they looked up into the sky, watching the birds fly and flutter around, chirping and singing. Then, as they gazed in wonder, they heard a flute playing gentle melodies. Johnny and his mom turned around and saw a man, wearing a wide-brimmed hat and carrying a flute. Johnny was amazed at how much the flute looked like the delicate bird he had seen in the nest, so he asked his mom if he could go closer to listen. She said yes, and Johnny, captivated by the music of the flute, walked up to the man and listened to the beautiful sounds. The delicate flute music made Johnny feel like he was floating in the sky with all of the birds, and he smiled in delight.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and explore the woods behind her house. One day, she found a smooth rock that was perfect for skipping on the lake. 

As she was skipping the rock, she heard a whisper coming from the bushes. "Who's there?" she asked. A little squirrel poked his head out and said, "Hi, my name is Sammy. I like to play too!" 

Lily was so happy to have made a new friend. They played together for a long time until it started to get dark. "I have to go home now," Lily said. "But we can play again tomorrow!" 

Sammy nodded and whispered, "Okay, see you tomorrow!" Lily skipped home, holding her new smooth rock tightly in her hand, excited to come back and play with Sammy again.

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a man with a big shiny thing that made loud noises. He was playing jazz, he said.

"What is jazz?" Lily asked.

"It is a kind of music that makes you feel happy and free. You can play jazz with many different things, like this saxophone, or a piano, or a drum," the man said.

He showed them how he blew into the saxophone and moved his fingers to make different sounds. Lily and Ben clapped and danced to the music.

"Can we try?" Ben asked.

"Sure, but be careful. It is not easy to play jazz. You have to listen and improvise," the man said.

He gave them the saxophone and helped them hold it. Lily tried to blow into it, but only made a squeaky noise. Ben tried to press the buttons, but they were too hard. They both laughed.

"It is fun, but hard," Lily said.

"Yes, it is. But you can learn if you practice and love jazz," the man said.

He took back the saxophone and played a song for them. It was fast and smooth and had many colors. Lily and Ben wondered how he could do that. They liked jazz.

They thanked the man and said goodbye. They ran back to their mom, who was waiting for them on a bench. She had a big orange balloon for them.

"Look, mom, we learned about jazz today!" Lily said.

"Wow, that sounds exciting. What is jazz?" mom asked.

Lily and Ben tried to explain, but they could not find the right words. They decided to show her instead. They took the balloon and pretended it was a saxophone. They blew into it and pressed it and made funny noises. They smiled and danced and had fun. Mom smiled too.

They were playing jazz.

Once upon a time, there was a kind girl named Lily. She loved to bake cookies with her mom. One day, Lily's friend came over to play. They played with dolls and blocks, but then Lily's mom brought out some fresh cookies from the oven. Lily's friend admired the cookies, and Lily shared them with her friend. 

Later that day, Lily's mom needed some help carrying groceries into the house. Lily was a helpful girl, so she helped her mom carry the bags. Her mom admired how kind and helpful Lily was. After they finished, her mom rewarded her with a cookie. Lily was so happy and grateful for the cookie and for being a helpful girl.

Once upon a time, there was an enormous door. It was so big that it touched the sky. And it stayed this way for many days.

One day, it started to rain. The rain came down and soon the door was soaking wet. It was raining so hard and the door was so wet that it was making a puddle around it.

Soon, a little bird came by and saw the big puddle. She flew down and began to paddle in it. She hopped around and she was so happy!

After she was finished playing, the little bird flew away, leaving the enormous door still soaking wet. And it stayed this way until the sun came out and the rain was gone.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big tree with a crack in the trunk. They want to see what is inside the crack.

"Let's stand on this rock and look inside the crack," Anna says.

"OK, but be careful," Ben says.

They climb on the rock and peek into the crack. They see a nest with three baby birds. The baby birds are fluffy and yellow. They open their mouths and make noises.

"Wow, look at the baby birds! They are so cute!" Anna says.

"They are impressive! I wonder where their mom is," Ben says.

Suddenly, they hear a loud squawk. They look up and see a big bird flying towards them. It is the mom bird. She is angry and scared. She thinks Anna and Ben want to hurt her babies.

"Uh-oh, we have to go!" Ben says.

They jump off the rock and run away. The mom bird chases them for a while, then goes back to her nest. Anna and Ben are safe, but they are also sorry.

"We didn't mean to bother the baby birds. We just wanted to see them," Anna says.

"Me too. Maybe we can come back another day and watch them from far away," Ben says.

They hug each other and go home. They learned a lesson. They should not touch or disturb wild animals. They should respect and admire them.

Once upon a time, there was a lady who had a very special style. She was very happy with her style, but one day it stopped working. She got very sad because she didn't know how to fix it.

So she went to find a helper. The helper knew all about repair, and he came to help. He looked at the lady's style and told her what to do. He said she would need to get a special tool to make the repair.

The lady found the tool, and the helper showed her how to use it. He was so helpful and sweet. After a few minutes, the style was fixed and it looked perfect. The lady was so happy and thanked the helper for his help.

From then on, she enjoyed her style every day and appreciated her helper for his kindness. They became friends and had lots of sweet adventures together.

Once upon a time there was a silly little kitty called Minnie. She was always very curious and loved to explore.

One day, Minnie promised herself she would go and explore the unknown. In the distance, Minnie saw something she had never seen before. It was a mysterious eye, staring right at her.

"Who are you?" she asked.

"I am the mysterious eye. I can help you explore the unknown if you promise to stay safe and be careful," replied the mysterious eye.

The curious and brave Minnie promised to stay safe and take care of herself and soon she was exploring all sorts of unknown places.

Moral: We all must make sure to stay safe and take good care of ourselves even when exploring something unknown.
Once upon a time, there was a big log. The log was in the forest. It was very heavy and brown. The log liked to be in the sun and the rain. The log was happy.

Once upon a time, there was a very ordinary girl named Sally. She was always looking for something new and exciting to do. One day, she decided to go to the park and have a picnic. She packed up her lunch and headed off. 

When she reached the park, Sally was very disappointed. All of the other kids were playing on the swings, slides and the sand pit. But Sally had no one to play with. 

That's when Sally had an idea. She would plan her own game! She took an old ashtray and put it in the middle of the park. She imagined that it was a castle and declared that whoever could get to the ashtray first, would be the winner.

Sally spread the word about her game and the park began to fill with children eager to win. They all ran as fast as they could towards the ashtray. Sally was the first to reach it. She had planned it that way! She was the winner, and everyone else had to give her lots of hugs and claps for her victory. 

Sally had a lot of fun that day and she was very proud of her victory. She went home with a smile and told her parents all about her game. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. She was very anxious, because she was about to try a new food: cauliflower. 

Her mom said, "Lucy, try this cauliflower! It's yummy!" But Lucy was scared. 

"No way," she said. Then she started to cry. 

Her mom said, "It won't hurt you. Just try one little bite." 

So Lucy took a tiny bite. It was yummy! 

Suddenly, she wasn't anxious anymore. Lucy said, "Mommy, I like cauliflower!" 

Every day after that, Lucy ate more and more cauliflower. She couldn't get enough of it! 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a bunny named Benny who loved to hop all around. One sunny day, Benny saw a funny-looking cane lying on the ground. He picked it up and started to play with it, pretending he was a wizard.

Suddenly, a wise old turtle named Tommy appeared and said, "Benny, be careful with that cane. It may look funny, but it's actually very powerful. You could hurt yourself or others if you're not careful."

Benny didn't listen and continued to play with the cane. But as he was hopping around, he accidentally hit his friend, a squirrel named Sammy, with the cane. Sammy was hurt and had to go to the doctor.

Benny felt very sorry and realized that Tommy was right. He promised to always be careful with things that may seem funny or harmless but could actually be dangerous. From that day on, Benny hopped around with caution and never played with strange objects again.

One morning, the sun was shining brightly when suddenly, it started to rain. Soon, big drops of water were falling fast and it was raining harder and harder.

Jojo and his mom were sad because they couldn't go outside and play. But then, Jojo had an idea - he said, "Mom, let's make dough!" So the two of them went into the kitchen and mixed together flour and water to make some dough.

Once the dough was ready, Jojo and his mom had lots of fun making shapes and figures with it. They rolled it into little snakes and made round doughnuts and cut out canoes. After a while, the rain had stopped and outside the sun was shining again. Jojo and his mom were happy, for now they could go outside and play!

Once upon a time, there was a chubby cat named Bob. Bob had a friend, a little fly named Tim. They liked to play together in the big green park.

One sunny day, Bob said to Tim, "I wish I could own a big red ball to play with." Tim thought for a moment and said, "Let's go find one!"

Bob and Tim looked high and low, but they could not find a big red ball. Then, they saw a little girl with a big red ball. Tim asked her, "Can we play with your ball, please?" The little girl smiled and said, "Yes, you can!"

Bob and Tim played with the big red ball all day. They were so happy. In the end, they didn't need to own the ball, because they had fun playing together. And they made a new friend, too.

Once upon a time there was a quiet rock. It was dead like the night time, but it was peaceful. 

One day a little girl who was only three came and sat next to the rock. She touched the rock and it felt warm. She rocked the rock back and forth and it made a nice noise. 

Soon more kids came and found the rock. They rocked it together and it got louder and louder and it was so much fun. 

The kids all sang a special song and even though the rock was dead, it kept rocking with them. 

When the song was over and the sun had come out, the kids all said goodbye to the rock. But they all knew they would come back again, because the rock was so peaceful and quiet.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tom. He loved to eat delicious cookies. One day, Tom's mom baked a big plate of cookies and left them on the table to cool down.

Tom saw the cookies and wanted to eat them. But the cookie jar was open, and he knew he should wait for his mom to say it was okay. Tom thought about what to do. He remembered that it was good to be patient and listen to his mom.

Tom decided to wait for his mom. When she came back, she was so happy that he had waited. She told him he could have two cookies for being a good boy. Tom learned that waiting and being patient was the right thing to do, and the cookies tasted even more delicious because he had waited.

Once upon a time there was a fancy yacht. On the yacht were two friends. They were both very happy.

The two friends hugged each other. They were so excited to be on the fancy yacht. They looked around and smiled. They felt like they were in a special place.

They hugged again before they explored the yacht. They looked at every corner of the fancy boat. Then they laughed and hugged each other again. They were so happy to be together.

The two friends hugged one last time before they waved goodbye. It was the happiest day on the fancy yacht!
