Lily was so happy to make her mommy proud. From that day on, whenever something needed fixing, Lily was always ready to perform her toy tool kit magic.

Peter was a little rabbit. One day he was feeling hot so he decided to do some exercise. He hopped up the hill. As he hopped, he felt the warm sun on his back. It was so hot!

He hopped faster and when he reached the top he was panting. He took a deep breath and hopped around. He leaped and skipped in the open field. The sun was shining very bright and everything was hot. Peter hopped for a long time. He felt happy and strong.

When the sun started to go down, Peter stopped to rest. He lay down in the warm grass and laughed. He had had so much fun exercising. Peter hopped home happily. He was tired but he had enjoyed himself. He was ready for bed.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Amy who was very shy. She never wanted to talk and her face was always red. Every day, Amy sat alone in the park, dreaming of her future. 

One day, she saw a boy carrying a pistol. She was so scared that she started to cry. The boy said "Don't be scared, I won't hurt you. I promise!"

Amy looked up at the boy and he smiled. She slowly smiled back, feeling a little bit braver. The boy said, "Would you like to come play with me?" She nodded and he showed her how to use the pistol. 

Amy was so excited that she had made a new friend. She even said a few words, speaking for the first time! She and the boy played together every day and Amy got braver and braver.

The boy and Amy promised each other that they would always be friends. And they kept that promise - forever.

Tom is a fireman. He wears a red uniform and a big hat. He drives a powerful truck with a loud siren. He helps people when there is a fire.

One day, Tom gets a call. There is a fire at a school. He and his friends rush to the scene. They see smoke and flames. They hear children crying. Tom is brave. He grabs a hose and sprays water at the fire.

"Help, help!" a voice shouts. Tom looks around. He sees a little girl trapped in a window. She is scared and hot. Tom climbs a ladder and reaches the window. He breaks the glass and pulls the girl out. He wraps her in a blanket and carries her to safety.

"Thank you, thank you!" the girl says. She hugs Tom. "You are a hero!"

Tom smiles. He is happy he saved the girl. He gives her a bottle of water. "Here, drink this. It will make you feel better."

The girl drinks the water. She feels cooler and calmer. She looks at Tom's uniform. She thinks he is very cool. She says, "When I grow up, I want to be a fireman like you!"

Tom laughs. He says, "You can be anything you want to be. Just remember to be brave and kind."

The girl nods. She says, "I will. And I will always remember you, Tom the fireman!"

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little duck named Ducky. Ducky loved to play with her friends in the pond. One day, Ducky's friend, Bunny, came to her and said, "Let's have a race!" Ducky agreed and they started to race around the pond.

Ducky was winning the race when suddenly, she stepped on a soft spot in the ground and fell into the water. She tried to swim, but her feathers were too heavy and she started to soak in the water. Bunny tried to help her, but it was too late.

Ducky's friends were very sad and they all gathered around her. They said their goodbyes and watched as Ducky floated away. Bunny said, "I'm sorry we raced, Ducky. It was just for fun." Ducky's friends learned that sometimes, having fun can be dangerous and they should always be careful.

Once upon a time, there was a woman who was very crazy. She would always do silly things and make others laugh. One day, she went to the park and saw a little girl crying. The woman asked the girl what was wrong, and the girl said she lost her favorite toy.

The crazy woman told the girl not to worry and started to pick up all the leaves on the ground. The little girl was confused but watched as the woman picked up each leaf and put it in a pile. Finally, the woman found the toy under one of the leaves.

The little girl was so happy and grateful to the crazy woman. The woman told the girl that sometimes things may seem lost, but if you keep trying and don't give up, you can find what you're looking for. The little girl learned a valuable lesson that day and thanked the crazy woman for helping her.

Jack was a 3-year-old boy and he loved to bounce. He liked to bounce so much, he even bounced when he walked down the street. One day, he reached a park with a big rubber bounce house. He was so excited to jump inside. 

Jack hopped in and started to bounce. He said to himself, "This is so much fun! I'm going to bounce until I can't anymore!" He kept jumping around and laughed as he flew high into the air. 

Suddenly, he heard his mom calling him from outside. 

"Time to go home, Jack!" said mom.

Jack did not want to leave so he asked his mom.

"Mom, can we come back tomorrow?" 

His mom smiled and said, "Sure thing. Now let's go home and have some yummy dinner!" 

Jack happily ran outside and saw his mom with a dictionary and a big smile on her face. 

"What's that dictionary for?" asked Jack.

"I want to check up on something," said his mom with a twinkle in her eye.

Jack and his mom went home, and he enjoyed his yummy dinner. He was eagerly waiting for the next day so he could visit the bounce house again!

Once upon a time, there was a humble wardrobe. It lived in a small house with a girl named Lily. One day, it started to rain outside. The rain made the wardrobe feel sad.

Lily saw the rain and said, "Oh no, the rain is here. I don't like the rain." The wardrobe wanted to help Lily, so it opened its door wide. "Come in, Lily," it said. "I will keep you safe from the rain."

Lily went into the wardrobe and closed the door. But the rain kept falling, and the house started to fill with water. The wardrobe tried to keep Lily safe, but the water came in too fast. The wardrobe felt very bad. The rain did not stop, and Lily and the wardrobe could not get out.

Once upon a time, there was a great mommy. She had an idea to create something fun. She went to her house and got some paper and markers. Then she gathered her little ones around the table. She had them each draw a head on the paper. After everyone was done, she put the head shapes together in a fun way and created something special. It was a great mommy bear! Everyone cheered with joy when mommy showed them what she had created. They all hugged the great mommy bear and laughed. The mommy was so proud of her creation - she knew it would be a lifelong memory for her family. They gave the mommy bear lots of cuddles and love. And from then on, it was a fun reminder of the day when mommy created something special.

Janie had a shiny new bike. She was ready to go for a ride. But first, she put on her helmet. It was strong, like her. She loved the way it covered her head. She hopped on her bike and started pedaling fast. Soon, the wind was blowing in her hair. Janie felt so strong and brave as she rode around. Sometimes she weaved around trees and other times she rode over hills. Everywhere she went, her strong helmet was covering her head like a shield. Janie felt free and strong on her bike!

Once upon a time, there was a blue pigeon. It flew high in the sky and landed on a tree. A bad person came and tried to steal the blue pigeon. But the blue pigeon was smart and flew away quickly. The bad person was sad because they couldn't catch the blue pigeon.

Mum took the thick bag out of the cupboard. She put the bag on the kitchen table. With a smile, she opened the bag and took out a toy. It was a truck with shiny wheels. She showed it to Davey and his eyes lit up.

Mum then said, "We need to remove the bag now so we can play with the truck." She carefully folded the bag up and put it back in the cupboard. She removed the truck from the bag and put it on the table.

Davey was so excited to play with his new truck. He grabbed it and rolled around the kitchen. Rolling and giggling, he raced the truck around the table and chairs. The thick bag was now forgotten in the cupboard.

Once upon a time there was a teddy bear called Tom. Tom loved to bathe in the warm sunshine and drink sweet tea.

One sunny day, Tom had a special treat. His mummy took him for a tea party on the beach. Tom gathered some soft sand near the water's edge and made a cozy spot for himself, then he sat down with a cup of tea.

Tom sipped his tea, feeling the warm liquid slip down his throat. Then he lay back and let the sunshine bathe his body. He imagined he was a dolphin, gliding through the waves.

When the sun started to sink in the sky Tom knew it was time to go home. He said goodbye to his sandy spot and gathered up his tea cup. Waving to the beach he turned and ran back to mummy, feeling full of joy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Grace. Grace was obedient and always did what the grown-ups told her. Her parents were so proud of little Grace.

One day, Grace and her parents had to go to the lawyer. Grace didn't understand why, but she knew it was important, and she was still obedient.

At the lawyer, Grace's parents said that someone had broken the law. Grace didn't understand what the law was, but she could tell this was something serious.

The lawyer said that if everyone was obedient, they could try to fix the problem. Grace was so good, her parents gave her a hug, as if they were proud of her.

Grace didn't understand completely what was happening, but she knew something was about to change. Her parents were doing everything they could to make sure the law was followed. 

The lawyer and her parents worked hard to make sure that justice was served. In the end, the law was obeyed, and it was because of Grace's obedience. 

The moral of the story is that being obedient is good.

Once upon a time there was a perfect little mouse. The mouse lived in a big, tall tree. One day, the mouse wanted to find some food. So, the mouse ran and ran, looking for something to eat.

But then, the mouse saw a scary cat coming closer and closer! The mouse was scared and ran away. But the cat was very fast. The mouse was about to be caught!

But then, a kind knight came and saved the mouse! The knight scooped up the mouse up in his arms, and quickly took it away from the cat.

The mouse was so happy and thanked the knight for saving it. From then on, the mouse was very safe and happy to be alive. The knight had saved the perfect little mouse!

Sara was a gifted girl. She could sing, draw and read very well. She loved to learn new things and share them with her friends. One day, she went to the park with her mom and saw a big tree with red apples.

"Mom, can I have an apple?" Sara asked.

"Sure, honey. But you have to ask the farmer first. He owns the tree and the apples," Mom said.

They walked to the farmer, who was sitting on a bench. He had a kind smile and a straw hat.

"Hello, sir. My name is Sara and this is my mom. We like your apples. Can we have one, please?" Sara said.

"Hello, Sara and Mom. You are very polite. Of course you can have an apple. You can pick one yourself. But be careful, some of them are not ripe yet," the farmer said.

"Thank you, sir. How do I know which ones are ripe?" Sara asked.

"Well, you can look at the color. The ripe ones are bright red and shiny. The unripe ones are green or yellow and dull. You can also feel them. The ripe ones are firm and smooth. The unripe ones are hard and rough. You can also smell them. The ripe ones have a sweet and fresh smell. The unripe ones have a sour and bitter smell," the farmer explained.

Sara nodded and thanked the farmer again. She ran to the tree and looked for a ripe apple. She hoped to find the best one. She saw many apples, but some were too high, some were too small, some were too green, some were too yellow. She searched and searched until she saw one that was perfect. It was bright red and shiny, firm and smooth, sweet and fresh. She reached for it and plucked it from the branch.

She ran back to her mom and the farmer, holding the apple in her hand.

"Look, Mom. Look, sir. I found the best apple. It is ripe and beautiful. Can I eat it now?" Sara said.

"Wow, Sara. You are very gifted. You found the best apple indeed. Yes, you can eat it now. Enjoy it, honey," Mom said.

"You are welcome, Sara. You are very smart and curious. You learned how to pick a ripe apple. I hope you like it. It is a gift from nature," the farmer said.

Sara smiled and thanked them both. She bit into the apple and tasted its juicy and delicious flavor. She was happy and proud. She had a great day at the park. She learned something new and got a wonderful gift. She hoped to come back again and see the farmer and the apples. She hoped to share them with her friends. She hoped to sing, draw and read more. She was a gifted girl.

Jimmy was a curious three year old. He loved discovering new things. That day he had a special mission, he wanted to fit his cocoa in the deep cupboard. He thought and thought but it did not fit.

He asked his mom for help. "Mommy, my cocoa won't fit in the deep cupboard," he said. 

"Maybe it's too big, Jimmy," his mom suggested. 

Jimmy thought and then had an idea. He took the cocoa to the kitchen and cut the bar in half. Then he went back to the deep cupboard. He tried again and it fit! 

Jimmy was so happy that he jumped around with joy. He had found a way to fit the cocoa inside the deep cupboard. He couldn't wait to show his mom what he had done.

One day, a weird barrel was walking down the street. Suddenly, it paused in front of a house. The house was old and rundown. The barrel looked around in amazement. It had never seen anything like it before. 

The barrel shuffled closer and closer until it peered inside the window. What it saw amazed him even more. There were all kinds of strange things inside. There were toys, books and weird objects that he had never seen before. He wanted to explore the house. 

So he started walking again. He reached the door and tried to open it, but it was locked. He paused and wondered what to do now. Suddenly, he heard a noise coming from inside the house. He listened closely and realized that someone was speaking. He knew he had to get inside. 

He pushed his barrel up against the door. To his delight, the door creaked open. He shuffled inside and looked around. He was in a strange house, but he knew he had a chance to explore and have some fun. He couldn't believe his luck.

Once there was a little girl named Lilly. She was 3 years old and loved to explore the world and meet new friends.

One day, Lilly was walking in the park when she saw a scared puppy. The puppy was so fearful and was trembling all over. But when Lilly smiled at him, he wagged his tail.

Lilly knew that he wanted a friend to play with. So, she decided to recommend a game of tag. The puppy was delighted and they played together for hours. She saw him smile and it made her happy too.

"You were so brave today, little pup," said Lilly.
"I know," he replied. "But I couldn't have done it without your smile."

One day, two friends decided to plan an adventure. They looked around the room and saw a big, safe couch. They knew that the couch would be the perfect spot for their adventure.

The two friends jumped on the couch and pretended it was a boat. They sailed up and down the living room, pretending to be pirates. They even made noises, like â€œYarr!â€ and â€œAhoy there me mateys!â€

They sailed around the room for hours, until they finally became too tired. Then, they hopped off the couch and headed off to take a nap. 

The two friends had a lot of fun doing their couch adventure, and they even learned a few new words, like â€œYarr!â€ and â€œAhoy there me mateys!â€ They knew that the safe couch was the perfect place for their fun adventure!

One day, there was a wild seat in the park. It was big and made of wood. Mum sat down and she asked her little girl if she wanted to sit too. The little girl said yes and she sat on the seat.

Mum told the little girl she was going to spoil her. She took out some food from her bag and she gave it to the little girl. The little girl was so happy to eat the food. She was having so much fun.

After the little girl finished her food, the two of them decided to play a game. They had so much fun together in the park. The little girl was laughing and having a great time.

At the end of their visit, the little girl and her mum got up from the wild seat. They hugged each other and said goodbye to the seat. They thanked it for letting them play and be together. The seat was happy too.

Once upon a time there was a brave little girl named Daisy. Daisy loved to try new things, even when they seemed a bit scary.

One day, Daisy had a big task to repair. Even though it seemed hard, Daisy was determined to do her best.

She began working on the project, step-by-step. She was scared at first, but as she kept going, she realized that it wasn't as difficult as it seemed. With a smile on her face, Daisy fixed the broken item and was so proud when she saw it was all repaired.

From that day on, Daisy was not scared of trying new tasks or fixing broken items. She knew she could do it.

Tom and Mia were playing with a balloon in the park. They liked to toss it to each other and watch it float in the air. Sometimes, they would try to catch it with their palms, but it was slippery and bouncy.

"Look, Tom, I can hold it with one hand!" Mia said, as she squeezed the balloon with her fingers.

"Wow, you are great, Mia!" Tom said, as he clapped his hands. "Can I try?"

"Sure, here you go!" Mia said, as she released the balloon and threw it to Tom.

Tom reached out his palm and tried to grab the balloon, but he missed. The balloon flew away from him and towards a big tree.

"Oh no, the balloon!" Tom said, as he ran after it.

Mia followed him, but they were too late. The balloon got stuck on a branch and popped.

"Pop!" They heard a loud noise and saw the balloon burst into pieces.

They stopped and looked at each other. They felt sad and disappointed.

"I'm sorry, Tom, it was my fault," Mia said, as she hugged him.

"No, it's okay, Mia, it was an accident," Tom said, as he hugged her back.

They decided to go back to their mom and dad, who were sitting on a bench nearby. They told them what happened and asked for another balloon.

Mom and dad smiled and gave them a new balloon. They said they were proud of them for being kind and sharing.

Tom and Mia thanked them and went back to playing. They were happy again and forgot about the popped balloon. They had fun with their new balloon and each other.

Once there was a little girl who came across a hippo. The hippo looked friendly and the little girl wanted to give it a pet. Her mom warned her not to touch the hippo. The little girl had never seen a hippo before and she wanted to pet it so bad! 

The hippo was very big and strong and looked like it could hurt her. Her mom warned her again that it was not safe and to stay away from it. She listened to her mom and stood back to watch. 

The hippo was only available for a short time, so the little girl watched it for as long as she could. She noticed its little mouth, big feet and huge nose. She said goodbye to the hippo as it walked away. 

The little girl was sad to see it go and was glad her mom had warned her to stay away so she would be safe.

One day, a man was walking in the park. He liked to see the birds and the flowers. He was happy and calm.

But then, he saw a big dog. The dog was barking and running at him. The man was fearful. He did not like dogs. He thought the dog would bite him.

He ran away from the dog. He shouted, "Help! Help! Go away, dog!"

A woman heard him. She was the owner of the dog. She called the dog. She said, "Rex, come here! Stop! He is a nice man. He will not hurt you."

The dog listened to the woman. He stopped barking and running. He wagged his tail. He wanted to play with the man.

The woman came to the man. She said, "I am sorry. My dog is friendly. He just wants to say hello. He will not bite you. Do you want to pet him?"

The man was still fearful. He did not trust the dog. He said, "No, thank you. I have to go. Goodbye."

He walked away from the woman and the dog. He was glad he was safe. He did not want to see the dog again. He hoped the woman would keep the dog on a leash. He wished he had a cat. He liked cats. They were quiet and soft.

Once upon a time, in a small village, there was a race. A little boy named Tim wanted to win the race. He had an idea to practice every day. Tim was a persistent boy, and he never gave up.

Every day, Tim would run and run. He would run in the morning and in the evening. He would run when it was sunny and when it was rainy. His friends would sometimes ask him to play, but Tim wanted to win the race, so he kept running.

Finally, the day of the race came. Tim was ready. He put on his shoes and went to the starting line. The race began, and Tim ran as fast as he could. He was so fast that he won the race! Everyone cheered for Tim. He was so happy that his idea and his hard work had helped him win.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved trains and always played with his toy train tracks. One day, Timmy's friend Billy came over to play. 

"Let's play trains!" said Timmy excitedly. 

"Okay!" said Billy. 

They started to play and Timmy loaded the train with toy animals. Billy thought it was silly and laughed. 

"Look at all the silly animals on the track!" said Billy. 

Timmy smiled and they continued to play together, making all sorts of silly train noises. It was a fun day for both of them.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play with blocks and make towers. One day, they have a task. Their teacher says they have to make a big tower with all the blocks. They are happy and start to work.

But Tom is not happy. He is angry and bored. He does not want to make a tower. He wants to break the towers. He waits for Anna and Ben to look away. Then he runs and pushes their tower. It falls down and makes a loud noise.

"Tom, stop!" Anna says. "You are bad. You prevent us from doing our task. Go away!"

But Tom does not listen. He laughs and runs to another tower. He pushes it too. It falls down and makes another loud noise.

"Tom, stop!" Ben says. "You are mean. You prevent us from having fun. Go away!"

But Tom does not listen. He laughs and runs to the last tower. He pushes it hard. But he is not lucky. The tower is too big and heavy. It falls on him and makes him fall too. He cries and says "Ow!"

Anna and Ben run to him. They are not angry anymore. They are sorry. They help him get up and hug him.

"Tom, are you okay?" Anna says. "We are sorry you are hurt. Do you want to play with us?"

"Yes, please," Tom says. "I am sorry I was bad. I was jealous of your towers. Can we make one together?"

"Of course," Ben says. "We are friends. We can share and help each other. Come on, let's make the biggest tower ever!"

They smile and hug again. Then they go to the blocks and start to build. Their teacher is proud of them. She says they are good and smart. They are happy and have fun.

Once upon a time there was a little boy called Bob. His mommy and daddy told him it was time to go to Grandma's house. He was so excited as he knew Grandma always made a delicious cake for him when he visited.

Bob put on his shoes and off he went. As he arrived, Grandma was in the kitchen. There was such a delicious smell! She was busy mixing and stirring the cake batter. Bob couldn't wait to try it!

Grandma brought the cake out of the oven. It was round and golden. Bob watched as Grandma put the finishing touches on it with some cream and cherries. It looked so delicious!

Bob and Grandma then headed outside. Grandma said to Bob, "Let's dance round the garden!" Bob couldn't believe it! He loved to dance and this sounded like so much fun.

They danced round the garden, laughing and having the best of times. When they stopped, Grandma took Bob back inside and there it was - a round delicious cake waiting for him.

Jane and her mom were going to a restaurant. Jane was very excited. They arrived at the restaurant and it was so lovely. It had a nice garden and some birds were singing. Jane and her mom went inside.

When they stepped in, the restaurant seemed very clean. Everything was in its place. Jane said, "Mommy, this restaurant is so nice! Look, it's so clean."

Her mom smiled and said, "This place looks lovely, Jane. It's clean, so we can eat here without worry."

Jane was happy that the restaurant was clean. She smiled and said, "Let's eat here! Then we can have a lovely time."

Mom smiled and said, "Yes! Now let's have a lovely time with lots of delicious food." Jane couldn't wait to start eating in the clean and lovely restaurant.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to swim in the pool with her uncle. One day, Lily's uncle said, "Let's see who can dive the deepest!" Lily was excited and said, "Okay!"

They both took turns diving into the pool. Lily's uncle was very good at diving, but Lily was still learning. Her dives were a bit dull, but she tried her best. After a few tries, Lily's uncle said, "You're doing great, Lily! Keep practicing and you'll be a great diver one day!"

Lily smiled and said, "Thanks, uncle! I love swimming with you!" They continued to swim and dive in the pool until it was time to go home. Lily couldn't wait to practice her diving again and show her uncle how much she had improved.

Tom and Mia are playing with blocks. They like to make different shapes and colors with the blocks. Tom has a lot of black blocks. He likes to make a pattern with them. He puts one black block, then two black blocks, then three black blocks, and so on.

Mia sees Tom's pattern. She thinks it is pretty. She wants to make the same pattern. She takes some of Tom's black blocks. She puts them next to her blocks.

Tom sees Mia taking his blocks. He is angry. He says, "Mia, stop! Those are my blocks! You can't take them!"

Mia says, "But I like your pattern. I want to make it too. Please, can I have some of your blocks?"

Tom says, "No, you can't. You have your own blocks. You can make your own pattern. Give me back my blocks!"

Mia feels sad. She does not want to make Tom angry. She gives him back his blocks. She says, "I'm sorry, Tom. I didn't mean to make you mad. I just liked your pattern."

Tom feels sorry too. He sees that Mia is sad. He says, "It's okay, Mia. I'm sorry I yelled at you. You can have some of my blocks. We can make the pattern together."

Mia smiles. She says, "Thank you, Tom. You are a good friend. I like your pattern. And I like you."

Tom smiles too. He says, "You're welcome, Mia. You are a good friend too. I like your blocks. And I like you."

They hug. They share the blocks. They make the pattern together. They are happy.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Jack and Pete. They were both very crazy, but Jack was a bit crazier than Pete.

One day, Jack found a big hoop and he started to play with it. He spun it around and around and laughed with glee. Pete was amazed and he just stared at the hoop, fascinated.

Jack was so into the hoop he started running around with it, going crazy in circles! Pete laughed and ran after him, trying to keep up.

Jack eventually tired out, so he sat down and put the hoop on the ground. He and Pete both stared at the hoop for a few minutes, astonished at how much fun it had been. Then they went off to find more fun things to do.

Once upon a time, there was a little baby who wanted an automobile. One morning, the baby went to the garage and saw an ugly automobile.

The baby said, "I want the ugly automobile!"
The baby's dad said, "Okay, but only if you say thank you."

The baby said, "Thank you!" and hopped into the ugly automobile. Even though the automobile was old and rusty, the baby loved it. 

The baby and dad went for a drive around the city and the baby waved at all the people they passed. When they got back, the baby said, "Thank you Daddy, for the automobile!"

The dad smiled and said, "You're welcome, baby. That's very kind of you to say thank you."

The baby smiled and hugged his dad. The baby was so happy to have his very own ugly automobile.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He was very lucky because he had a big red balloon. Timmy loved to play with his balloon all day long.

One day, Timmy was playing outside when a gust of wind blew his balloon away. Timmy was sad because he couldn't reach his balloon anymore. Suddenly, he saw his mom coming out of the house with a big box. 

His mom opened the box and inside was a present wrapped in shiny paper. Timmy was so excited and happy that he forgot all about his balloon. He reached out to grab the present and tore off the wrapping paper. It was a toy car! Timmy was thrilled and played with his new toy all day long.

Tom and Mia are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big slide. Mia wants to try it. Tom is anxious. He thinks the slide is too high.

"Come on, Tom. It will be fun!" Mia says. She runs to the slide and climbs the steps. Tom follows her slowly. He looks down and feels scared.

"Mia, wait for me!" Tom says. He tries to catch up with her, but he is too slow. Mia reaches the top of the slide and sits down. She smiles and waves at Tom.

"Are you ready, Tom?" Mia asks. She pushes herself and slides down. She laughs and shouts. "Whee!"

Tom is at the top of the slide. He wants to go down, but he is afraid. He holds on to the rail and does not move.

"Tom, what are you doing?" Mia calls from the bottom. "Don't you want to slide?"

Tom looks at Mia. He sees that she is happy and safe. He wants to be with her. He cares for her. He takes a deep breath and lets go of the rail. He slides down. He feels the wind and the speed. He is surprised and excited. He reaches the bottom and smiles.

"Mia, I did it!" Tom says. He hugs Mia. "That was fun!"

Mia hugs Tom back. "I knew you could do it, Tom. You are brave!"

Tom and Mia are happy. They slide again and again. They have fun in the park.

Once upon a time, there was a small kangaroo named Joey. Joey loved to hop and play with his friends in the forest. One day, Joey saw a big, scary animal he had never seen before. It was a lion!

Joey ran back to his friends and told them about the lion. His friend, a wise old owl, questioned Joey about what he had seen. Joey described the lion's big teeth and sharp claws.

The owl knew just what to do. He gathered all the animals in the forest and they made a plan to scare off the lion. They worked together and scared the lion away. Joey was grateful to have such smart and brave friends. From that day on, Joey knew that he could always count on his friends to help him when he was scared.

Once upon a time, there was a big elephant. The elephant had a long trunk that he used to eat and drink. One day, the elephant woke up feeling very sleepy. He rubbed his eyes and yawned. Then, he saw the sun rise in the sky. 

The elephant decided to take a walk to wake himself up. He walked through the jungle and saw lots of animals. He saw a monkey swinging from a tree, a lion taking a nap, and a bird flying in the sky. 

After his walk, the elephant felt much better. He was not sleepy anymore. He used his trunk to drink some water from a nearby river. Then, he went back to his family and they all had a big feast together.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to ride his bike around the lake. One day, Timmy saw a foolish little duck swimming in the lake. The duck kept diving under the water and coming back up again. Timmy thought it looked like fun, so he decided to ride his bike into the lake!

But as soon as Timmy hit the water, he fell off his bike and started to sink. The foolish duck swam over and helped Timmy back to the shore. Timmy learned that it's not always a good idea to follow others and do foolish things. He realized that it's important to be safe and make smart choices. From that day on, Timmy rode his bike around the lake, but never again tried to ride it in the water.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy liked to carry things around with him wherever he went. One day, Timmy found a newspaper on the ground. It was big and had lots of words on it. Timmy thought it was cool and decided to carry it with him.

As Timmy walked around with the newspaper, he saw a big dog running towards him. The dog looked dangerous because it was barking loudly and had sharp teeth. Timmy was scared, but he remembered he had the newspaper with him. He held it up and the dog ran away because it was scared of the newspaper.

Timmy was happy that he had the newspaper with him because it helped him stay safe from the dangerous dog. He continued to carry it with him everywhere he went and showed it to all of his friends. They thought it was cool too! The end.

Lily liked to wander in the park. She saw many things: trees, flowers, birds, dogs. She liked to say hello to them. One day, she saw a big tunnel. It was dark and long. She wanted to see what was inside.

She walked into the tunnel. It was cold and quiet. She could not see much. She heard a noise. It was a train. It was coming fast. Lily was scared. She ran out of the tunnel. She looked for her mom.

Her mom was busy. She was talking on the phone. She did not see Lily. Lily cried. She wanted her mom. She did not like the tunnel. She did not like the train. She wanted to go home.

A man saw Lily. He was kind. He asked her what was wrong. He helped her find her mom. He told her not to wander in the tunnel. He said it was dangerous. He said the train could hurt her.

Lily hugged her mom. She was happy. She said sorry. She said she would not wander in the tunnel again. She said she would stay with her mom. Her mom hugged her back. She said she loved her. She said she was glad she was safe. They went home together.

Once there was a fat cup. It was happy being fat, but it wanted to be even happier. One day, it decided to grow. So, it grew and it grew until it was so big it couldn't grow any more. 

Just then, something amazing happened. A bunch of flowers started to bloom right out of the cup! All different colors of flowers came out of the cup. They were so pretty and they made the cup even happier. 

The cup was now the happiest it had ever been. Every day it would look at its beautiful flowers and feel so proud that they had grown from it. The flowers made the cupâ€”and everyone who saw themâ€”very happy indeed.

The sun showed its face in the morning sky and it shone brightly. The birds flew up to the sky and sang their happy song.

Then, a little girl named Lucy came out of her house and looked up. She saw the bright sun and the fluffy clouds. She was so happy that she jumped up with excitement!

Lucy: "Look at the beautiful clouds! I wish I could go up and touch them!"

Suddenly, there was a rumble in the sky. Something had blocked out the sun and the sky had become dark.

Lucy looked up and saw that a big selfish cloud had come between the sun and the sky.

Lucy: "No, not that selfish cloud! Get away!"

But the selfish cloud didn't move. It just stayed there and blocked out the sun.

Lucy was sad and she slowly walked back to her house. The sun slowly returned and the sky became sunny and bright once again.

Lucy was surprised that the selfish cloud had gone away. She was so happy that she smiled and shouted in joy.

Lucy: "Yay! Thank goodness the selfish cloud is gone!"

Once upon a time there was a silly bear called Tim. He liked to explore the world and find fun new things. One day he went for a walk and noticed a mysterious knob. He tried to turn the knob but nothing happened. He got very frustrated and started to chew it.

Suddenly, something magical happened! The knob opened and Tim was very surprised. Inside there were lots of delicious sweets. He grabbed as many as he could and started to chew them.

No sooner than he started, however, the knob started to close. Tim got scared and tried to run away. But, it was too late and the knob closed before Tim could escape, trapping him inside!

Tim was very frightened and started to cry. Then, just when he thought all hope was lost, he noticed the knob. He quickly realized that the only way to escape would be to chew the knob.

He grabbed the knob and started to chew. Sure enough, it opened and opened wide enough for Tim to escape. Tim was so relieved and ran off, never to touch a silly knob ever again.

Once upon a time, there was a bear named Benny. Benny loved to eat sweet honey from the beehive. One day, Benny saw a file on the ground. He picked it up and wondered what it was for. 

Benny decided to ask his friend, a rabbit named Rosie. "Rosie, what's a file for?" he asked. Rosie replied, "It's a tool to make things smooth." 

Benny thought about this and decided to use the file on the beehive to make it easier to get the honey. But when he tried, the beehive broke and the bees got angry. 

Rosie came to help and said, "Benny, you need to yield to the bees. They need their home to stay safe." Benny realized his mistake and apologized to the bees. From that day on, Benny and Rosie enjoyed sweet honey together, but Benny never used a file on anything without asking for help first.

Once there was a tall fence in a park. It was so tall that no one could get over it. There were lots of animals who lived on the other side of the fence. Every day they jumped up and down, trying to look over the fence.

One day a small mouse was jumping up and down, trying to get a peek. But he couldn't reach the top. He wanted to run on the other side and play with all the animals. 

Then the mouse had an idea. He ran up to the fence and called out: â€œCan someone please open the fence?â€

Suddenly a big hand appeared from the other side. It was a human hand! The human opened the fence, and all the animals were so happy and excited. They ran around and played together on the other side. 

When it was time to go home, the humans closed the fence. The mouse and all the other animals waved goodbye to the humans. 

The mouse was so pleased that he'd asked for help. From then on, he knew he could always rely on humans to help him.

Molly was at the beach. She was having so much fun! She saw a crab and wanted to take it home with her. Molly carefully picked up the crab and looked at it. It was a purple crab!

Molly put it in a bucket and walked home. She asked her dad if she could keep the crab. Her dad said yes, as long as she took good care of it.

Molly put an aquarium in her room for the crab. She made sure it was filled with clean water, food and rocks for the crab to hide. Molly named the crab Purple.

Molly loved her crab. She would play with it and watch it crawl around its home. After a few weeks, Molly's dad said it was time to release the crab back into the wild.

Molly took the crab to the beach. She carefully put the crab in the wet sand. Molly said goodbye to her crab and watched as he scampered away.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy liked to play outside with his friends. One day, Timmy's mom gave him a pumpkin to use for Halloween. Timmy was very excited because he had never had a pumpkin before.

Timmy and his friends decided to carve the pumpkin. They used a knife to cut out a face and make it look spooky. Timmy thought it looked fine, but his friends thought it was the scariest pumpkin they had ever seen.

After they finished carving the pumpkin, Timmy's mom helped him put a candle inside. When it got dark outside, they lit the candle and the pumpkin glowed. Timmy was so happy to see his pumpkin all lit up. He went to bed that night dreaming about all the fun he had with his friends and his fine pumpkin.

Once there was a brave soldier who was on a mission. He had to go past a scary jungle and deep down into a dark cave. As he walked closer and closer to the cave he heard a loud sound, it was so loud that it made him jump. He quickly realised that it was only a lion roaring and he felt a bit better. 

The soldier was now near the cave entrance, he looked around it was so amazing. He saw enchanting lights and heard the sound of a waterfall. He took a deep breath and stepped inside, it was even more amazing. 

He followed a twisty path and soon enough he came to a room full of shimmering treasures. He was about to grab some of the jewels when he heard the lion roar again. The soldier was brave, he stood his ground and roared back. The lion was so surprised that the soldier was not scared that it quickly ran off. 

The soldier was victorious and finished his mission. He even got to keep some of the sparkling jewels as a reward. He knew it was an amazing adventure and smiled with joy.

Once upon a time, there was a big cat named Tom. Tom had a favorite toy, a ball with ink inside. He loved to play with it all day. One day, Tom saw a deep hole in the ground. He thought it would be fun to drop his ink ball in the hole and see what happens.

As Tom leaned over the hole, the ink ball slipped from his paws and fell in. He tried to reach it, but the hole was too deep. Tom felt sad and didn't know what to do. Just then, a little mouse named Tim came by. Tim was small, but he was very smart.

Tim saw Tom's problem and had an idea. He found a long stick and helped Tom get the ink ball out of the deep hole. Tom was very happy and thanked Tim. They became good friends and played together every day. The moral of the story is that even small friends can be a big help.

Once upon a time there lived a little boy called Ben. Ben was three years old, and he loved exploring the world.

One day, Benâ€™s mum took him outside to the garden. She told him that there were lots of things to learn outside.

Ben couldnâ€™t wait to explore the garden! He looked at all of the strange things growing there, and saw a big, round green fruit that he had never seen before. Ben asked his mum, â€œWhat is this?â€

His mum said, â€œThat is called a lemon. Lemons are sour and they can be used to make food and drink taste nice. But you must not eat a lemon! Eating it would be like eating poison.â€

Ben was curious. He asked, â€œWhat is poison?â€ 

His mum explained, â€œPoison is something very bad, and it can make you sick. So never eat a lemon!â€

Ben was sad. But then his mum said, â€œBut, you can learn to make lemonade. Lemonade is juice made from lemons that's sweet, not sour. It's yummy and much better for you than poison.â€

Ben smiled. He was excited to learn how to make lemonade!

Once upon a time there were two friends, Tim and Tom. Tom wanted to build something special. He had some wire and he wanted to use it. Tim asked Tom what he was going to make and Tom said he was not sure yet.

Tim said he had an idea and asked if Tom could trust him. Tom said yes and so Tim slowly worked with the wire for a long time. He used the competitive wire to wrap it around a stick.

When he finished, Tom was amazed! It was the best swing in town! Tim said, "I knew you could trust me." They spent all day swinging on the swing and having a lot of fun. 

Tom and Tim stayed friends from that day on and always trusted each other. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a proud crane who lived by the lake. Every day, the crane would fly through the sky and enjoy the view. 
One day, the crane noticed a small boat that had been abandoned. The boat was starting to rot. The crane felt sad to see such a beautiful boat in such a terrible state. 
The crane turned to the sky and said, "I will have to fix this boat so no one else has to see it like this." 
So the crane flapped his wings and flew from tree to tree, gathering wood and strong leaves. He worked hard to rebuild the boat until it was as strong as it was before. 
The crane was proud of his work and stared proudly at the boat before taking off back to the lake. 
He said to himself, "No one else has to see this boat rotted and in ruins. It's all fixed now!"

Once, there was a boy. He was three years old. He liked to hang out with his friends.

One day, he went to the library to find a story. He looked around but he couldn't find one. He was very sad.

Then he saw a big book. It had pretty pictures and it looked very interesting. He looked inside and saw a story. It was a story about a magical bird.

He read the story and found it very useful. He loved the story and he wanted to hang it on the wall so he could see it every day.

The boy was so happy. He had found a useful story that he could hang on the wall. The end.

Once upon a time there was a guard. His job was to make sure the castle was safe and perfect. Every day he rocked back and forth in his chair at the castle gate, watching the people come and go.

One day, a little girl came to the castle. She wore a beautiful purple dress and had golden hair. She saw the guard and shouted, "Hi, guard!"

The guard smiled and said, "Hi! What brings you to the castle today?"

"I am here to find the perfect gift!" the little girl said.

The guard rocked back and forth in his chair and laughed. "I'm sure you will find something perfect!"

The little girl nodded and skipped away. Later that day she returned with a big box in her arms. When she opened it, the guard saw a beautiful toy castle inside.

"It's perfect!" the guard said.

The little girl smiled and said, "Now the castle is safe and you can rock in your chair, knowing you are guarding something special!" 

The guard was so happy he rocked back and forth in his chair with joy. He was proud to be the perfect guard at the perfect castle!

Once upon a time, there was a bear who was very jolly. He loved to run and play in the forest. One day, he was running and teasing when he came across an animal he had never seen before. It was a funny little creature. The bear thought it was so funny that he laughed and laughed. The funny creature laughed too. They both had so much fun they decided to be friends. From that day onwards they were the best of friends. They would play and tease each other every day and the bear always felt so jolly.

Once upon a time there was a little boy called Tom. Tom loved fruit. He knew all the different kinds of fruit and he always ate lots.

One day Tom went to the fruit store. He wanted some apples because they were his favourite. He looked at the apples but all of them were dull. It made him very sad. 

He asked the shopkeeper, "Do you have any nice apples?" But the shopkeeper said, "Sorry, I only have dull apples today." Tom knew he would have to look for nice apples somewhere else.

Tom kept walking and soon he found another fruit store. When he got there he saw lots of colourful, juicy apples. He was so happy! He asked the shopkeeper, "Can I have three apples please?"

The shopkeeper said, "Yes, of course!" Tom knew he had found the perfect apples. He thanked the shopkeeper, paid for the apples and went home. 

Tom was so excited to have the delicious apples. He and his family all enjoyed them and they were so pleased he had been able to find nice apples. He was a very happy little boy.

Lila and Tom were playing in the park. They liked to run and jump on the grass. The grass was green and soft. But some parts of the grass were brown and dry. Lila and Tom wondered why.

They saw a man with a big hose. He was spraying water on the grass. He wore a hat and a shirt with a flower on it. Lila and Tom were curious. They ran to the man and said hello.

"Hello, little ones. What are you doing here?" the man asked.

"We are playing on the grass. But why is some grass brown and dry?" Lila asked.

"Well, the grass needs water to grow and stay green. Sometimes, the sun is too hot and the rain is too little. Then the grass gets thirsty and sad. That's why I'm here. I'm trying to restore the grass. Do you know what restore means?" the man explained.

Lila and Tom shook their heads. They did not know what restore meant.

"Restore means to make something good again. Like when you fix a broken toy or heal a hurt knee. I'm giving water to the grass so it can be happy and green again. Do you want to help me?" the man offered.

Lila and Tom nodded. They liked to help. The man gave them each a small hose. They sprayed water on the grass with the man. They had fun and learned a new word. They helped to restore the grass.

One day, a normal boy was outside playing in his garden. He saw a witch in his garden and he was scared. He wanted the witch to go away. He closed his eyes and wished for her to be gone. When he opened his eyes, she was still standing there. He got angry. He ran towards the witch and kicked her with all his might. She went flying away and landed in a nearby field. The boy was so happy. He smiled and went back to playing. He had saved his garden from the witch! He was proud of himself.

One day, a dog named Spot wanted to teach his friend, a cat named Fluffy, how to sit on his heel. Spot was very good at sitting on his heel, but Fluffy was not. Fluffy was a little scared to try because she did not think she was fit enough to do it.

Spot said, "Don't worry, Fluffy! I will help you. Just watch me sit on my heel like this." Spot showed Fluffy how to sit on his heel, but Fluffy was still scared. She did not want to fall down.

Fluffy said, "I don't know, Spot. What if I fall?" Spot told Fluffy not to be scared. He said, "I will catch you if you fall. Just try your best, and you will see that you can do it too!"

So, Fluffy tried to sit on her heel, just like Spot. At first, she wobbled a little bit, but then she did it! Fluffy was so happy that she could sit on her heel. She thanked Spot for teaching her, and they both played together all day.

Once upon a time there was a child. This child was very playful and happy, but one day they started to feel lonely. The child wanted something to keep them company.

So, the child started to look around. Soon, they spotted a harmless seat. The child decided to make the seat their new friend by sitting on it.

At first, this seemed like a great idea. But after a while, the seat started to hurt the child. It was so uncomfortable, the child was in pain.

The child tried to move away, but it was too late. The seat had become dangerous and the child was in danger. Sadly, this was the end of the child's friendship with the harmless seat.

Once upon a time, there was a big, strong bear. He went for a walk in nature. He felt so happy and brilliant! He was looking forward to a nice, peaceful day in nature.

Suddenly, something strange appeared. It was a tall, dark creature that he had never seen before. He was scared, but he decided to talk to it. He said "Hi there, who are you?" 

The creature didn't answer. Instead, it started to growl. The bear was so scared. He quickly ran away. The creature followed him!

The bear was fast, but the creature was faster. It caught up with him and ate him in one bite! The bear had a bad ending and never made it back home.

The group was huge. It was filled with lots of people who were all friendly and happy.

But then one day something happened to make them resist. They didn't want to do something they were told to do, so they stood together, strong and proud.

The people in the group held hands tightly and thought of ways to avoid what they were asked to do. They talked and discussed until finally they agreed on the best way to resist.

Next they gathered together in one big circle and started to make noise. They shouted together in an act of unity to show their resistance.

The group was so huge that the people on the other side couldn't ignore them. They heard the people in the group and understood how proud they were.

The group had proven that resist is powerful thing when you stand together.

Mia liked to collect things. She had a box full of shiny stones, feathers, stickers and shells. She liked to look at them and make patterns with them. Sometimes she gave them to her friends as gifts.

One day, she saw a big calendar on the wall of her classroom. It had pictures of animals and numbers for each day. She thought it was very pretty and wanted to have it. She asked her teacher, Miss Lee, if she could take it home.

"Sorry, Mia, you can't take the calendar home. It belongs to the school and we need it to learn about the days and months. But you can look at it here as much as you like," Miss Lee said.

Mia felt sad. She really liked the calendar and wanted to collect it. She wondered if there was a way to get it.

The next day, she had an idea. She brought her box of shiny stones, feathers, stickers and shells to school. She went to Miss Lee and said, "Miss Lee, I have a gift for you. I want to trade with you. You can have my box of things and I can have the calendar. Please?"

Miss Lee smiled. She saw that Mia was very thoughtful and generous. She said, "Thank you, Mia, for your gift. It is very kind of you to offer me your box of things. But I can't trade with you. The calendar is not mine to give. It is for everyone to share. How about this? You can keep your box of things and I will give you a special sticker for each month. You can stick them on a paper and make your own calendar. Would you like that?"

Mia thought for a moment. She liked the idea of making her own calendar with stickers. She nodded and said, "Yes, I would like that. Thank you, Miss Lee. You are very nice."

Miss Lee gave Mia a hug and a sticker for January. She said, "You are very welcome, Mia. You are a very good collector and a very good friend."

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He loved to eat spaghetti with a fork. One day, Timmy's fork fell on the ground and got dirty. He was sad and worried because his mom would be angry.

Timmy's mom saw him looking sad and asked him what was wrong. Timmy told her about his dirty fork and how he was worried. His mom smiled and said it was okay, she could clean the fork. Timmy was happy and felt better.

The next day, Timmy went to school and saw his friends eating with fancy forks. He felt embarrassed because he only had a plain fork. But then he remembered what his mom said and felt better. He knew that his fork was special because it was his.

Ben was sad. He wanted to go to the park with Mom and Dad, but they said no. They said it was too cold and wet outside. Ben did not like cold and wet. He liked sun and fun.

Ben looked out the window. He saw a little bug on the glass. It was an inch. It had six legs and a long body. It was brown and black. Ben liked inch. He wanted to play with it.

Ben opened the window. He put his hand out. He said, "Hello, inch. Do you want to be my friend?" The inch did not say anything. It just walked on the glass. Ben tried to touch it, but it was too fast. It walked away from Ben's hand.

Ben was sad again. He said, "Please, inch. Don't go. Stay with me. We can have fun." The inch did not listen. It walked to the edge of the window. It found a small hole. It crawled through the hole. It was gone.

Ben cried. He said, "Bye, inch. I miss you. Come back soon." He closed the window. He went to his bed. He hugged his teddy bear. He hoped the inch would come back. He hoped the sun would come out. He hoped he could go to the park. He hoped he would be happy.

Once upon a time, there was a peaceful place. A little boy was walking through the peaceful place. He was looking for something. Suddenly he saw a lollipop! He got so excited. He walked over and began to poke the lollipop with his finger. He was curious to see what would happen. Suddenly, the lollipop started to spin around and around! He was so surprised. He wanted to play more with the lollipop, so he poked it again. Again, the lollipop started to spin. He had so much fun playing with the lollipop. Soon, his mom called him and he had to rush back home. But before he left, he gave the lollipop one last poke and then said goodbye. He went back home feeling happy.

Once there was a girl who was very creative. She had a lot of ideas for fun projects and she loved to invent new things. One day she had an idea to make a bulb that could be used to light up a room. She was excited and got to work on improving the bulb.

She searched for different materials and started to put the bulb together. She was so happy to see how it was coming out. She was using her creative skills to make it better and better!

Finally, it was finished. She switched it on and the room lit up with a bright light. She had improved the bulb and it was working great! She was so excited and proud of her work. She kept inventing new things and improving them with her creative skills.

John was a chubby boy. One day, he was playing in the garden with his toy tools. He was having so much fun. Suddenly, his brother ran up to him and slapped him on the arm. 

John was very surprised and scared and started to cry. His mom heard the crying and ran outside. She looked at John and saw that his brother had slapped him. She was very angry. She turned to John's brother and said "No slapping!". 

John's brother looked very sorry and said he was sorry. John's mom hugged him and said it was okay. John stopped crying and looked at his brother. He smiled and hugged him too. 

John and his brother went back to playing with the toy tools and had lots of fun together. They learned that it was not nice to slap someone.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Mia. She loved to draw with her pastel colors. One day, she saw something unusual outside her window. It was a big, round, and shiny thing. She wanted to find out what it was.

Mia put on her shoes and went outside. She walked and walked until she found the unusual shiny thing. It was stuck in a tree. Mia wanted to solve the problem and get the shiny thing down. She thought about how she could do it.

Mia had an idea! She took out her pastel colors and drew a big ladder. She climbed up the ladder and reached for the shiny thing. With a big smile, she pulled it out of the tree. Mia solved the problem and took her new shiny thing home to show her mom and dad. They were so proud of her.

Once upon a time there was a girl who loved to solve puzzles. On this special day, she had three puzzles that she wanted to complete.

The first puzzle was made of plastic and it was hard to solve. The girl tried to think of the right way to put it together and after a few tries, she finally did it!

The second puzzle was also plastic and it was very hard. The girl was determined to figure it out and so she kept on looking and thinking hard until she finally solved it.

The last puzzle was made of hard plastic and it looked like it would be tricky to solve. But the girl never gave up and after a few attempts, she managed to put it together.

Suddenly, a voice said, "You did it! You solved all three puzzles!" The girl looked around and saw a big doggy smile at her. She smiled back and said, "I did it all by myself!"

Mumma was carrying today. She had lots of different things in her arms. She was carrying a blanket, a book, and two teddies. It was a very foolish idea because the pile was much too big for her. She kept trying to manage it, but it was just too heavy.

Suddenly, her little boy came along and saw mumma struggling. He took the blanket from her and said, "Let me carry today, mumma". He was so pleased to be helpful and smiling from ear to ear. Together they carried the pile and it was much easier.

Mumma was grateful for the help and said, "You are so helpful! Thank you". They had a big hug, happy that they had succeeded together.

Once upon a time there was a strong gorilla. He was so strong, he could squeeze rocks! One day, he went to the doctor to get an x-ray. When he got it, he was so excited to look at it. He could see all of his bones! He squeezed the x-ray and it made a funny sound. It was so fun! Then he made a silly face and laughed. He thanked the doctor for the x-ray and hopped on his way. The end.

One day, a little girl called Sally was feeling helpless. She had lost her favourite toy, and she didn't know how to find it.

Luckily, her mum heard her plea. She gave Sally a warm hug and said, "I promise I will help you look for it." The mum then knelt down next to a chest and began to polish it.

The chest was old and dusty, but after a few minutes, it shone brightly and Sally could see that it had a big old lock on it. She looked closely and saw that the key was shaped like a star.

Sally called out, "I found it!" She quickly grabbed the key and used it to open the chest. Inside was her toy - the one she had lost!

Sally's mum smiled and said, "I'm so glad that I was able to help you find it. That is why I promised you I would help." Sally smiled too, and thanked her mum.

Once upon a time there was a pirate. He was very tall and always wore a big black hat. One day the pirate decided to go on a journey. He sailed away in his big boat until he reached a big island.

The pirate saw something that made him very excited - it was a big treasure chest! He couldn't wait to open it. He opened it and found lots of gold inside. He tried to carry it back to his boat, but it was heavy.

Then the pirate had an idea. He stretched his arms and legs in all directions to make himself bigger. Now he was big enough to carry the treasure! He smiled and was happy. 

On his way back, the pirate felt guilty. He thought he should share the treasure with everyone. So, he started taking some for himself and then giving some away.

Eventually, the pirate went back to his boat with a small pile of gold. He was happy that he had shared and his journey was over. He knew it was a good thing to be nice and share. The end!

Once upon a time, there was a bright alert blue bird who lives on top of a tall tree. One clear day, the sun was shining so brightly that the bird could no longer stay awake. So, the bird paused for a moment and decided to take a nap in the sun.

Suddenly, the bird was awoken with a loud noise. It was the sound of thunder! The blue bird spread its wings wide and flew to an empty branch just as the sky was getting grey. Cautiously, the bird looked around and saw a storm building up in the sky.

The bird then paused again, as if it was building up the courage to fly to safety. With one flutter of its wings, the bird set off, faster and faster, trying to catch up with the dark clouds. The storm was getting bigger and bigger and it was getting windier and windier. 

Finally, the bird managed to stay ahead of the storm and landed safely on a tree in a sunny spot on the other side. The blue bird was happy that it had made it in time, and it watched the storm fly away with its bright alert eyes.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who was very sad. She had lost her special gem. Her gem was bright and sparkly, and she had been playing with it all day.

The little girl was very lonely, so she started to cry. But then she felt a warm hand holding hers. It was her best friend. They hugged, and her friend tried to comfort her.

The next day, her friend took her to a dark cave. In the cave there was a glimmer of light - and right at the center of it was the same little gem that she had lost! She was overjoyed and hugged her friend.

The two friends celebrated the rest of the day together, playing with the little gem in the darkness of the cave. They were happy and cozy, and the little girl's sorrow turned into joy.

Tommy loved to play with his aeroplane. He made it fly in the air and zoom around the room. He pretended it was going to faraway places and having adventures. He did not like to share his aeroplane with anyone.

One day, his cousin Lily came to visit. She saw Tommy's aeroplane and wanted to play with it too. She asked Tommy, "Can I have a turn with your aeroplane, please?"

Tommy said, "No, it's mine. Go away." He hugged his aeroplane and turned his back to Lily.

Lily felt sad and angry. She thought Tommy was being spoiled and mean. She tried to grab the aeroplane from Tommy, but he resisted. He pulled it back and shouted, "Stop it! Leave me alone!"

They started to fight over the aeroplane. They tugged and pushed and yelled. They did not hear their mums calling them to come for lunch.

Their mums came into the room and saw them fighting. They were not happy. They took the aeroplane away from both of them and said, "That's enough. You two need to learn to share and be nice to each other. No more aeroplane for today. Now come and eat your lunch."

Tommy and Lily felt sorry and ashamed. They realized they had been silly and rude. They said sorry to each other and hugged. They decided to play something else after lunch. They hoped they could play with the aeroplane again tomorrow, but only if they could share and have fun together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who wandered through the forest. She peered around each tree looking for something special. As she kept walking, she noticed a post and stopped to take a look. It was open and she looked inside. There was a small bird! She gasped in wonder and stepped closer. The little bird flew into the air, chirping away. She smiled and watched it fly. She wondered if the bird would come back and she looked up in the sky hoping to see it again. Then she knew what she must do and she wandered the forest searching for an open post that the bird might have gone to. She never forgot the adventure that day and she will forever wander the forest in search of a post that's open. 

The End

The sun was shining in the clear, blue sky. Down in the wild meadow, a little girl named Sarah was picking flowers. She explored the tall grass with such joy and curiosity! 

Suddenly, a mosquito sprang out of the wild grass and flew right past Sarahâ€™s ear. â€œSnap!â€ Sarah exclaimed, as she tried to swat it away with her hand. But the mosquito flew off into the grass before she could touch it. 

â€œMosquitoes are so wild!â€ Sarah said to no one in particular. But even though she had tried to swat the mosquito away, she felt a longing to try and catch it. What fun that would be!

Sarah ran around the meadow, snapping her hands and trying to catch the wild mosquito. No matter how hard she tried, the mosquito stayed just out of reach. 

But Sarah was not about to give up! She moved around the meadow again, this time with an even bigger smile. She snapped her hands, and suddenly the mosquito flew right into her hands. â€œYes!â€ Sarah exclaimed. She had finally caught the wild mosquito!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and solve puzzles. One day, her mom gave her a new puzzle. It was on a tray and had many pieces. Lily was very excited to play with it.

Lily started to put the pieces together. She found a piece that looked like it fit, but it was fake. She tried another piece, and it fit just right. Lily knew that she had to look carefully to find the right pieces. She felt like a smart detective.

As Lily solved more and more of the puzzle, she could see a picture of a beautiful garden. She remembered that her mom had said there was a special surprise in the puzzle. Finally, Lily put the last piece in place. The surprise was a lovely butterfly! The fake piece helped her learn to look closely and solve the puzzle. Lily felt proud and happy.

Tom and Lily like to play with toys. They have many toys, but their favorite is the helicopter. The helicopter is long and red. It can fly in the air and make noise.

One day, Tom and Lily are playing with the helicopter in the garden. They take turns to fly it and catch it. They are having fun.

But then, Tom throws the helicopter too hard. It flies over the fence and lands on the road. Tom and Lily run to the fence and look. They see a big car coming. The car hits the helicopter and breaks it.

"Oh no!" Tom and Lily cry. "Our helicopter is broken!"

They are very sad. They want their helicopter back. They go to their mom and tell her what happened.

Mom hugs them and says, "I'm sorry, my loves. That was an accident. Sometimes things break. But don't worry, we can get a new helicopter. Or maybe we can fix this one. Let's go and see."

Mom takes them to the road and picks up the broken helicopter. She looks at it and says, "Hmm, it's not too bad. Maybe we can glue it together. Do you want to help me?"

Tom and Lily nod. They are happy. They go with mom to the house and get some glue. They help mom to put the helicopter back together. It takes a long time, but they do it.

The helicopter is not perfect, but it can still fly and make noise. Tom and Lily are proud. They thank mom and hug her. They go back to the garden and play with the helicopter again. They are careful not to throw it too hard. They are happy.

Once upon a time there were two best friends, Martin and Ellen. They were both 3 years old and were always playing together. 

One day, Martin and Ellen were playing together in the garden. But something happened that made them both very sad.

Martin had picked a flower from the flowerbed. Ellen said to him "That's not nice, you mustn't do that!" But Martin didn't listen.

Ellen's dad saw what had happened and he was very angry. He called out in a fierce voice "Martin, that was not ok! You need to be punished!"

Martin was very scared, he started to cry. He and Ellen's dad put their hands together and he said: "Martin, you must make a print of your hand with your finger, so that you will remember next time that it is not ok to pick flowers." 

Martin made a print in the soft soil as a punishment, and he promised he will never pick a flower again. 

Ellen and her dad hugged Martin and they all went inside to have a nice warm drink.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big bottle on a bench. The bottle has a skull and a word on it. The word is poison.

Anna and Ben are curious. They want to know what is in the bottle. They go to the bench and watch the bottle. They see a man come to the bench. He is not polite. He yells at Anna and Ben. He says the bottle is his and they should go away.

Anna and Ben are scared. They run away from the man and the bottle. They find their mom and dad. They tell them what they saw. Mom and dad are worried. They say poison is bad. It can make people sick or die. They say Anna and Ben should never touch or drink poison. They say they should always be polite and careful.

Anna and Ben are sorry. They say they will not be curious about poison again. They say they will be polite and careful. Mom and dad hug them. They say they are proud of them. They say they love them. They go home and have a snack.

Once upon a time there was a little boy called Sam who was three years old. One morning, Sam woke up and he was very hungry. He wanted a banana! Sam went searching for a banana, but he couldn't find one anywhere.

Then Sam heard a scary sound. It was coming from behind a big bush. Sam was scared, but he was also still very hungry. He was brave and walked up to the bush.

When Sam got closer, he saw a banana! But there was a big, scary spider sitting on the banana. Sam knew he had to get the banana or he would stay hungry.

At first he was scared of the spider, but he knew he had to get the banana. With one big leap, Sam grabbed the banana. The spider scurried away!

Sam was very happy - he had found a delicious banana to eat. He enjoyed every bite of it. Sam was glad that he was brave enough to go and get the banana.

Anna and Ben were playing in the backyard. They had a big box of toys and they liked to make up stories with them. Anna picked up a saw and pretended to cut a branch from a tree. Ben picked up a teddy bear and hugged it.

"Look, I'm a builder!" Anna said. "I can make anything with this saw!"

"That's cool!" Ben said. "Can you make me a house?"

"Sure, I can!" Anna said. "But first, I need some wood. Where can I find some wood?"

Ben looked around and saw a fence. He pointed to it and said, "There! There's some wood!"

Anna nodded and ran to the fence. She put the saw on the wood and started to move it back and forth. She made a loud noise and some dust.

"Wow, you're incredible!" Ben said. "You're really cutting the wood!"

Anna smiled and said, "Thank you! I'm almost done!"

But then, they heard a growl. They turned around and saw a big dog. The dog was angry. It did not like the noise and the dust. It barked and ran to Anna and Ben. It wanted to bite them.

"Help!" Anna and Ben shouted. They dropped the saw and the teddy bear and ran to the house. They slammed the door and locked it.

The dog reached the fence and saw the saw and the teddy bear. It sniffed them and decided to chew them. It tore them apart and made a mess.

Anna and Ben watched from the window and felt scared and sad. They lost their toys and their fun.

"Sorry, Anna," Ben said. "I should not have told you to cut the fence."

"It's okay, Ben," Anna said. "I should not have listened to you. We should have asked Mom and Dad first."

They hugged each other and said, "We're sorry, Mom and Dad."

They hoped Mom and Dad would not be mad at them. They hoped they would get new toys soon. They hoped the dog would go away. They learned a lesson. They would not play with the saw again.

Once upon a time there was a little octopus. Every day he would bounce around the ocean and have lots of fun. One day, he decided to bounce up higher and higher until he reached the surface of the water. He could now see the world outside the ocean!

The little octopus decided to bounce around the beach. He saw a ball and decided to bounce it back to a little boy. The little boy was so excited and ran away with the ball. The octopus was so proud of himself, he bounced all around the beach in celebration. 

Soon, the little octopus became tired. He hopped back into the water and took a nap. After he woke up, he decided to go explore the ocean deeper down and went off on a new adventure.

Once upon a time, there was a brave lion. He was the bravest lion in all the land. Everywhere he went, he would roar so loudly that everyone could hear him. 

One day, the lion decided to take a walk. He found a mop and decided to use it like a broom. He was so creative, he kept walking and using the mop over and over. 

Suddenly, he heard a loud noise. He stopped walking and looked around. He saw a big, angry tiger coming towards him. The tiger roared at the lion and was ready to fight. The lion bravely roared back, protecting his mop. 

The lion used his mop and fought the tiger. He was so brave and creative, he quickly managed to win the battle. The lion was happy and proudly roared in the air. 

From then on, the lion was known as the bravest and most creative lion in all the land.

Lily and Ben were best friends. They liked to play in the park and pretend they were superheroes. One day, they found a big black hat under a tree. It had a pointy top and a silver buckle.

"Wow, look at this hat!" Lily said. "It is so cool!"

"Can I try it on?" Ben asked.

"Sure, here you go," Lily said. She gave the hat to Ben and he put it on his head.

Suddenly, Ben felt a strange feeling. His eyes turned green and his nose grew long and crooked. He started to laugh in a wicked way.

"Ha ha ha! I am a witch now!" Ben said. "I can do magic and cast spells!"

Lily was scared. She did not like the new Ben. He did not look like her friend anymore. He looked mean and scary.

"Ben, take off the hat!" Lily said. "You are not a witch, you are my friend!"

"No, I like being a witch!" Ben said. "It is more fun than being a superhero! Watch this!" He waved his hand and a gust of wind blew Lily's hair.

"Stop it, Ben! That is not nice!" Lily said. She ran to Ben and tried to pull the hat off his head. But the hat was stuck. It did not want to come off.

"Help me, Lily!" Ben said. He did not like being a witch anymore. He wanted to be himself again.

Lily and Ben pulled and tugged at the hat. They worked together and finally the hat came off. Ben's eyes turned blue and his nose became normal. He smiled and hugged Lily.

"I am sorry, Lily," Ben said. "I was a bad witch. I did not mean to hurt you."

"It is okay, Ben," Lily said. "You are my friend. I forgive you."

They threw the hat away and ran to the swings. They decided to play superheroes again. They agreed that being a witch was not cool at all.

Once upon a time, there was a mighty river. Everyday, lots of traffic would come over the river. Boats, cars, planes. All sorts of things!

But one day, a strange thing happened. The boats, cars and planes began to vanish. One by one they all disappeared in a flash!

The people were so surprised. Where did they go? Where had they all gone?

Nobody could figure it out. Until one night, they saw a bright light over the river. It was so bright that it lit up the sky. As the people watched, they saw all the boats, cars and planes flying back over the river!

They were so relieved, and they were so happy. All their traffic had come back! The people celebrated and cheered, and the mighty river was flowing again.

Once upon a time, there lived a modest mouse. He lived in a small hole in a tree and was quite happy. One evening, he heard a loud crackle and saw a bright envelope appearing in the sky. The mouse was curious and questioned what it could be.

He walked towards it and when he arrived, he found that it was an envelope. He opened it, and inside there was a letter addressed to him. He was surprised and asked himself who could have sent it. He read the letter and it said, "I am a fairy, and I was sent here to give you a special gift. I have put it in this envelope".

The mouse was very excited and opened the envelope. inside was a small key. He looked at the key and then he heard a faint voice say, "There is something special at the top of the tree. Use this key to open the door and you will find something wonderful". 

The mouse was delighted and climbed the tree with the key in his hand. When he reached the top, he opened the door with the key and there was a chest full of gold coins. The mouse was so happy that he could barely contain his joy. He thanked the fairy for the gift and put the envelope back in his hole so that he could remember the special moment forever.

Tommy was having a nice day. He stepped outside and saw the event. It was a modest event with lots of smiling people. He tried to join them, but he stumbled and fell! He brushed himself off and joined the event. Everyone around was so happy and he had a wonderful time. He felt like he was part of something special. Finally, the event ended and Tommy fell asleep in his bed, dreaming of the modest event.

Once upon a time, there was a little bear who loved to play outside. One day, he went into the forest to play. It was a beautiful season, with the sun shining and the birds singing. The little bear was having so much fun, he didn't notice the dark clouds gathering in the sky.

Suddenly, the wind started to blow, and the little bear heard a loud noise. He looked up and saw a big storm coming. The little bear knew he needed to find shelter quickly. Just then, a polite rabbit came by and warned the little bear about the storm. The little bear followed the rabbit and they found a cozy cave to hide in.

As they waited for the storm to pass, the little bear realized that it was important to pay attention to the weather and to listen when someone warns you about danger. From that day on, the little bear always checked the weather before he went outside to play.
