Once upon a time, there was a jolly little boy named Andy. He loved to explore and have adventures.

One day, Andy was out in the garden playing, when he saw an exciting big red box with a silver buckle on the front. He ran up to it, and wondered what was inside.

Andy was ready to open the box, but then it started to shake. Soon, it disappeared right before his eyes!

He was so surprised, he shouted out, "Where did it go?"

All of a sudden, a friendly voice answered, "I took it away!"

Andy looked around, but he couldn't see anyone. "Who are you?" he asked.

Then, a small fairy with a sparkly wand appeared in front of him. "I am the magical fairy of surprise. I give you a surprise, if you use your buckle."

Andy was so excited, he quickly put on his buckle. The magical fairy waved her wand, and the big red box reappeared with a jolly surprise inside it.

Andy was delighted! He thanked the magical fairy of surprise, and ran off to explore what was in the box.

One day, Tom went for a walk. He was very happy. He found a stick in the park. He also found a piece of chalk on the ground. He was very excited.

Tom smiled and picked up the chalk. He looked around, but nobody was there. It was so quiet. Tom liked quiet.

Tom started to draw a picture on the ground with the chalk. He drew a big red heart and some circles and stars. Then he made some more shapes and lines. Tom drew until the chalk ran out.

When the picture was all done, Tom smiled and looked at it. He was very proud of his drawing. He wanted everyone to see it so he ran to get his mum.

When his mum saw the picture they both laughed. Together they walked back to the park and showed everyone the picture he had made. Everyone was so impressed with Tomâ€™s artwork.

Once there was a little girl who was three years old. She was always curious about the things around her. One day, she wanted to fix a broken toy. She asked her mom for help.

Her mom looked at the toy and she saw that it needed a nail. But the little girl did not know how to use it. Her mom saw that she was a little bit scared. So she encouraged her daughter to try to use the nail.

The little girl held the nail and tried to push it into the wood. She was happy when she saw that it went in. She held it firmly and put it in the right place.

The girl was so proud of what she had done and so was her mom. The toy she fixed was gray, just like the nail she used. From then on, she knew that if she put her mind to it, anything was possible.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Sarah. She loved to read and was very smart. Everyday she read from her books, and she got better and better.

Soon enough, Sarah was reading really well. She read every day and she read all kinds of stories. She read about princesses and monsters and pirates.

But Sarah didn't just read once in a while, she read every day. She made a regular time in the day to read and soon she had read so many books! Everyone was proud of the smart little girl.

One day Sarah's Mommy asked her what she was reading. Sarah said she was reading her favorite book. It was lots of fun! Sarah had become such a good reader.

Sarah is now 10 years old and she still reads every day. Her regular reading makes her smarter every day. And she loves it!

Mum and Dad took Tommy to the store. Tommy was very excited and he wanted to pick out something nice.

"Can I get a new toy please?" asked Tommy.

"No," said Mum. "Maybe next time. Today, we're here to get a purse for you."

Tommy couldn't believe it. "A purse?" he asked.

"Yes, a purse," said Dad. "We want you to have a purse of your own so that you can carry it with you wherever you go."

Tommy looked around. He saw lots of different purses in all sorts of colours. But none of them seemed quite right. Then, at the very back of the store, he saw a long, black purse. It was just perfect.

"I want that one," said Tommy, pointing to the purse.

Mum and Dad both smiled and agreed. They bought the purse and gave it to Tommy. He held it in his hands and smiled. He accepted it and hugged it close.

"Thanks, Mum and Dad!" said Tommy.

"You're welcome, Tommy," said Dad with a smile.

One day, a powerful steel machine came to life. It could speak, and everyone was very afraid. The machine said, "I want to be friends with everyone". Even though everyone was scared, they were also curious. So, they asked the machine what it wanted to show them.

The machine replied, â€œI want to make a place for everyone to be safe and happy.â€ Everyone was so excited! They started to work with the machine and soon enough, a beautiful city was built. Everyone was so proud of what the powerful machine helped them do.

The people and the machine were now friends and they decided to have a party! They danced and spoke with each other and thanked the machine for all its hard work. From then on, the city was safe and happy. The machine had made their dreams come true.

One day, a little girl named Lucy found a tray. The tray was big and red. Lucy was glad she found it. She knew she could use the tray for many fun things.

Lucy took the tray to her room. She saw her mom fold clothes. Lucy wanted to help. She put the clothes on the tray and carried them to her room. The clothes were nice and neat. Lucy's mom was happy and gave her a big hug.

Lucy and her mom then used the tray to eat lunch. They had yummy sandwiches and juice. They were both glad they found the tray. It made their day more fun. And they lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a jolly old man. His name was Tom. Tom loved to lend things to people. One day, a little girl named Jane asked Tom to lend her a pistol. 

"Please, lend me a pistol," she said.

Tom thought hard and long. He wanted to help her.

"Yes," he said, "I will lend you the pistol."

Tom gave Jane the pistol and she was so excited.

"Thank you, Tom!" said Jane, giving him a big hug.

Tom smiled. He was so happy to be able to lend something to Jane. From then on, he was known far and wide as the "Pistol Lending Man".

Tom and Jen are friends. They like to look at the stars at night. They have a big book with pictures of stars and planets. They want to see a comet. A comet is a star with a long tail. The book says a comet will come soon.

One night, Tom and Jen go outside with their book and a flashlight. They look at the sky. They see many stars, but no comet. They are sad. They want to see the comet.

"Where is the comet?" Tom asks.

"I don't know," Jen says. "Maybe it is late."

They wait and wait. They get cold and sleepy. They are not ready to go home. They want to see the comet.

Then, they see a bright light in the sky. It is the comet! It has a long tail. It is beautiful. Tom and Jen are happy. They jump and clap.

"Look, look, the comet!" Jen says.

"Wow, wow, the comet!" Tom says.

They look at the book. The book says the comet has a name. The name is Halley. Tom and Jen like the name.

"Hello, Halley!" Tom says.

"Hello, Halley!" Jen says.

They wave at the comet. The comet waves back. Tom and Jen smile. They are ready to go home. They have seen the comet. They are friends.

One day, there was a little boy. He was very creative! He wanted to count something, so he decided to count the tuna in the kitchen. He saw one, then two, then three! He was so happy, he kept counting. He kept going until he counted all twelve tuna. He was counting them so fast and he was so proud of himself. 

After he counted all the tuna he smiled and exclaimed, "I counted all the tuna! I am so creative!" He was so proud of himself. 

He was having so much fun counting, he decided he wanted to count something else as well. He looked around the kitchen and realized he could count the spoons! He started counting the spoons in the drawer and he was able to count all fifteen! He was so excited to have counted all fifteen spoons. 

The little boy was so pleased with himself. His counting was so creative and he had so much fun counting the tuna and the spoons. He couldn't believe he had done it all on his own.

Once upon a time, there was a funny looking bird. He had long and flexible wings, and he loved to soar in the sky. One day, the bird was flying around when he noticed a hole in the ground. He thought it looked interesting, so he flew down to investigate it.

Once he got closer to the hole, the bird was shocked to find that an animal was stuck inside of it. The bird offered to help the animal out, but it was so scared that he just stayed still. The bird knew that he had to find a way to help the animal.

He flew up and looked down. He noticed that the hole was very deep and that it had curved walls. He thought for a moment, and then he had an idea. He flew down and started to peck at the walls of the hole, slowly shaping the edges until it was curved enough for the animal to turn around. 

The bird was so proud of his work that he returned to the ground. The animal then saw the chance of escape and ran away from the hole. The bird was happy to have helped.

The moral of this story is that we should always be flexible when it comes to helping others. With a little thought and effort, we can often find a way to come to the aid of those in need.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play with toys. One day, they find a big box in the park. The box has a picture of a yacht on it.

"Wow, look at this!" Anna says. "It is a yacht. A big boat that can go on the water."

"Can we open it?" Ben asks. "Maybe we can play with it."

Anna nods. She and Ben open the box. Inside, they see a yacht. But it is not a regular yacht. It is a toy yacht. It is made of plastic and has wheels.

"Wow, this is cool!" Ben says. "But how can we play with it? It cannot go on the water."

Anna thinks. She has an idea. She points to the slide in the park.

"Let's take it to the slide!" she says. "We can pretend that the slide is the water. We can make the yacht go down the slide and say 'whee!'"

Ben likes the idea. He and Anna take the yacht to the slide. They put it on the top and push it down. The yacht slides down fast and makes a noise.

"Whee!" Anna and Ben say. "This is fun!"

They play with the yacht on the slide for a long time. They are happy. They have a new toy and a new game.

Tommy was playing with his truck. It was his favorite toy. He watched it excitedly as it raced around the floor. Suddenly he saw something. It was fierce. He was scared.

It was an angry dog. It was snarling and barking loudly. It was clearly very mad. Tommy was scared and backed away. But the dog was faster, it was coming closer and closer.

Tommy tried to run but the dog was too fast. It pounced on Tommy and bit him. Tommy screamed in pain. His truck lay forgotten on the floor as the dog ran away.

Tommy's skin was burning and throbbing. He had been bitten and it hurt a lot. Tommy's parents rushed to his side. They saw the teeth marks and they knew that the dog had pinched him. Tommy was crying. His parents were worried and sad. 

Sadly the dog was never found and Tommy was scarred for life. The fierce dog had caused Tommy a great deal of pain and sorrow.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Anna. She was three years old and loved to read. But one day, she wanted to read a story that she couldn't find in her book. 

She asked her parents where she could find the story, and they explained that Anna could use the network. Anna was unsure what the network was, so her parents showed her how to connect to to the network. Anna soon realized that the network was reliable, and could provide her with the stories she was looking for. 

Anna read all kinds of stories from the network. She found stories about princesses, dragons, and knights. She even found stories about astronauts and robots. 

Anna had so much fun every day reading stories from the network. She was so happy to have a reliable network that could provide stories she wanted to read. 

The End.

Once upon a time, there was a nosy little bird. He was always asking questions and poking his beak into things. One day, the bird saw something interesting â€“ a big veil laying on the ground. He flew down to get a closer look and noticed a big mark on it. 

The nosy bird was curious, so he decided to go and find out what the mark was. He started flying around, asking everyone he saw about the mark. Everyone he met said they didn't know what it was, so the little bird kept looking. 

Finally, he found the answer he had been searching for. The mark on the veil was the signature of the King, who had dropped the veil from his castle window. Everyone in the kingdom was so happy to have their King back, and the nosy bird felt proud for being able to mark the veil and help find the King.

Once there was a boy called Jake. Jake wanted fruit but the fruit was icy! He didnâ€™t know how to use it.

But then Jake had an idea. He put the ice covered fruit in a big bowl and he used a spoon to break it up. He stirred it around and around until it was all smooshy.
 
Then he found some melted ice in the bowl and realised that he could use this too! He added some milk and some sugar, and before long it was yummy. 

Jake was very happy with his creation. From then on, every morning he would make icy fruit juice!

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She was so excited because she was going to pick berries. It was going to be a fun day!

She walked far and wide until she finally came to a distant berry bush. It was filled with big, juicy berries. She reached down and began to pick them.
 
The little girl added berry after berry to her basket. When it was full she waved goodbye and skipped home. 

When she got home the little girl showed her mom all the berries she had picked. Her mom smiled and added them to the basket full of other berries. They would be enough for a big berry pie! 

The little girl and her mom made the pie together, and it tasted delicious! It was the best day ever.

Once upon a time there lived a kind old lady called Grandma. Grandma always loved to gather around her family and friends. On this particular day, Grandma decided she wanted to gather all her family around the kitchen sink.

When everyone had gathered Grandma said "Let's all be calm and look at the sink". Everyone looked into the sink and saw a fish swimming around! Grandma said "This fish must have come from a magical world!"

Grandma scooped up the fish and put it into her ocean-blue bucket. Everyone was so excited to see the fish, they all laughed and giggled with joy.

Grandma said goodbye to the fish asking it to be calm and stay in the bucket until it's home was ready to receive it. Grandma and her family gathered for one last hug and said goodbye to the fish as it slowly disappeared into the water.

The End.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny named Benny. Benny loved to play with his friends all day long. He would hop and jump around, and his friends would chase him. But when it was time for Benny to nap, he would always refuse. He thought napping was a waste of time.

One day, Benny's friends were all tired and needed to nap. But Benny didn't want to stop playing. He didn't realize that his friends needed rest to keep playing with him. So, they left him alone and went to nap.

Benny felt lonely and sad. He realized that he needed his friends, and he needed to nap too. He found a soft spot under a tree and took a nap. When he woke up, he felt refreshed and ready to play again.

Benny learned that napping was important, and he also learned that friends are like a network. They help us and we help them. From that day on, Benny always took naps and played with his friends, and they all had fun together.

Once upon a time there was a princess. She lived in a castle with a giant black bell. Every morning, at sunrise, the bell would ring very loudly. She would love to admire her beautiful jewelry in the glowing sunrise light while hearing the bell ring.

One morning, when the bell went to ring, it suddenly stopped. The princess was very worried! She went to investigate why the bell had stopped ringing.

She got to the bell tower and saw a big black bird on the bell, making it stay still. 

"What are you doing?", the princess asked the bird.

"I'm looking for my necklace. I lost my beautiful black jewelry here yesterday!", said the bird. 

The princess was so sorry to hear that and instantly offered her help. She searched and searched until finally she found his necklace. 

The bird was very happy and, out of thanks, he rang the bell before flying away.

The princess smiled, happy that the bird was safe and the bell was ringing again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play dress-up and wear her favorite pink dress. One day, her mom took her to the beach to sail on a big boat. Lily was so excited to wear her dress on the boat.

The boat sailed smoothly on the calm sea, and Lily felt happy and free. But suddenly, dark clouds appeared in the sky, and the wind started to blow hard. Lily's dress was flapping wildly, and she felt scared. 

The boat started to rock and sway, and Lily's dress didn't fit her anymore. It was too big and too heavy. Lily felt uncomfortable and wanted to take it off, but her mom told her to keep it on. 

The wind grew stronger, and the boat hit a big wave. Lily fell overboard and was swept away by the rough sea. Her dress weighed her down, and she couldn't swim. Sadly, Lily never returned home.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. He loved to listen to his mom as she read him stories every night. Tim liked to learn new words, and he was always excited to hear the fun language in the stories.

One day, Tim met a naughty cat named Max. Max liked to play tricks on Tim, like hiding his toys and making a mess in his room. Tim didn't like Max's naughty games, but he still wanted to be friends with the cat.

Tim decided to teach Max how to be nice. He would read stories to Max and show him the fun language he had learned. Max started to listen to Tim and soon, he stopped playing naughty tricks. Tim and Max became the best of friends, and they loved to listen to stories together.

Once upon a time, there was a girl who had a purple elevator in her very own house. Every morning, she would let the elevator take her upstairs to the top floor. She would look out the window and wave to her friends below.

One day, the girl let her friends come up in the elevator and they all had a special treat. The girl had packed a special bag with yummy snacks so they could all have a picnic in the living room.

After the picnic, the girl's friends said goodbye to each other and let the elevator take them back downstairs. The girl waved goodbye as the elevator descended. 

And they all lived happily ever after! The End.

John was a poor little boy. He wanted more than anything to go to the park. But every day, he wished and wished, and nothing ever happened.

One day, he went outside and started to walk. Suddenly, he saw a big open field full of trees and grass. He ran over, and saw the most beautiful park he had ever seen.

John had found the park he had been wishing for all his life! He could not believe it. He ran around and played for hours, and it was the greatest day of his life.

John goes to the park every day now, and it makes him so happy. Every time he goes, John remembers how he had wished so badly and never thought he would ever find it. But sometimes, wishes do come true.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy had a red cap that he loved to wear every day. It made him feel happy and powerful. 

One day, Timmy went to the park to play with his friends. He was having so much fun that he didn't notice when his cap fell off his head. Timmy didn't realize he had lost his cap until he got home. 

He looked everywhere for it, but it was nowhere to be found. Timmy missed his cap so much that he cried himself to sleep that night. 

The next day, Timmy went back to the park to look for his cap. But it was gone forever. Timmy was so sad and couldn't stop crying. He missed his cap and felt powerless without it. The end.

Tom and Lily were twins who liked to study different things. Tom liked to study animals and plants. Lily liked to study stars and fire. One day, they found a big book with pictures of different kinds of flames. They wanted to learn more about them.

They asked their mom if they could use a candle to see the flames. Their mom said yes, but only if they were careful and did not touch the fire. She gave them a candle, a lighter, and a glass jar. She told them to put the jar over the candle to see what would happen.

Tom and Lily went to the backyard and lit the candle. They saw the flame flicker and dance. They liked the colors and the warmth. They took turns putting the jar over the candle. They saw the flame get smaller and smaller. They wondered why.

"Maybe the flame needs air to breathe," Tom said.

"Maybe the jar is too big and the flame is scared," Lily said.

They tried different things to make the flame bigger again. They moved the jar closer and farther. They tilted the jar and shook it. They blew on the candle and made a wish. Nothing worked. The flame stayed small and weak.

Tom and Lily felt frustrated. They wanted to study the flame, but they could not make it happy. They did not know what to do.

They decided to ask their mom for help. They brought the candle and the jar to their mom. They told her what they did and what they saw. They asked her why the flame was sad.

Their mom smiled and hugged them. She explained that the flame needed oxygen to burn. Oxygen was a kind of air that was invisible but very important. She said that when they put the jar over the candle, they trapped the oxygen inside. The flame used up the oxygen and had none left. That was why the flame got smaller and smaller.

She showed them how to lift the jar slightly and let some fresh air in. She said that this way, the flame would have enough oxygen to burn brightly again. She said that they could try different sizes and shapes of jars and see how the flame changed.

Tom and Lily thanked their mom and went back to the backyard. They were happy to see the flame grow and shrink as they played with the jars. They learned a lot about flames and oxygen. They had fun studying fire.

James and his dad were outside looking at the sky. 

"Look, James! An aeroplane!" said Dad.
He pointed to the sky.

James looked up and saw the big aeroplane in the sky. It was very high and had thick white wings. He was excited!

"Ah, ah look at it go!" exclaimed James.

Dad smiled and said "Yes! That aeroplane is flying away in the wind. Wouldn't it be fun to fly on an aeroplane?"

James nodded and said "Yes, let's go on an aeroplane, Dad!"

Dad laughed and said "Maybe we will, one day. Would you like that?"

James smiled, and nodded his head. He knew that one day he and his dad would get on an aeroplane and fly away.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. It was her birthday today and she was very excited. She woke up early in the morning and ran to her parents' room.

"Mummy, daddy, it's my birthday today!" she said with a big smile on her face.

"I know, sweetie. We have a surprise for you," her mother replied.

Lily was curious and asked, "What is it?"

"We have a special gift for you. It's a beautiful dress that you can wear to your birthday party tonight," her father said.

Lily was so excited that she started to jump up and down. "Yay! I can't wait to hang up my new dress in my closet!" she exclaimed.

Her parents laughed and hugged her. They knew it was going to be a wonderful birthday for their little girl.

Once upon a time, there was a big theater. It had a big, red sign and lots of windows. It looked beautiful from afar, but up close it was ugly. 

Inside, there were lots of people. They were sitting in seats and looking at a big screen. They were watching cartoons and laughing. 

Suddenly, the lights in the theater turned off and the show ended. Everyone got up, waved goodbye and left. 

Soon, the theater was empty. It was quiet and still. The only thing left were the ugly seats and the big, red sign. 

The end.

The little girl wanted to buy something. She had a penny. She was very excited. She started to hurry to the store. 

When she arrived, she saw so many things. They were all so expensive. She felt sad. 

Then, she remembered her penny. She looked around the store. She found a picture. It was just one penny! She was so happy. 

She grabbed the penny and hurried home. She showed everyone the picture. She was proud of her purchase. 

From then on she saved her pennies. She was happy that she had found an expensive picture with just one penny.

Once upon a time, there were two friends: John and Mary. They were always playing together and having lots of fun. One day, John thought of a game to play. He said: "Let's play hide and seek behind the blanket!".

Mary smiled and said "Ok!" But, then she shook her head and said "No, I don't want to".

John asked: "Why not?".

Mary frowned and said: "I think it's a dull game. I don't want to play".

John disagreed. He said: "No, it's a great game. Let's try it. I'm sure it will be fun!".

Mary thought for a moment and then said: "I don't know. I'm feeling a bit calm now. I'd rather just sit with my blanket and read a book".

John smiled and said: "Ok! We can do that! Let's just sit together and read".

Mary smiled and said "Yes, that sounds wonderful to me".

So, John and Mary agreed to enjoy a calm afternoon together, reading and snuggling under Mary's blanket.

Lisa loved to bake with her mom. They made cakes and cookies and pies. Lisa liked to stir and pour and taste. She always wore her pink jacket when she baked. It was her baking jacket.

One day, Lisa saw a big jar of sprinkles on the shelf. They were shiny and colorful. Lisa wanted to use them on her cake. She asked her mom, but her mom said no. She said the sprinkles were not for baking. They were for something else.

Lisa was sad and curious. She wondered what the sprinkles were for. She waited until her mom was busy. Then she climbed on a chair and reached for the jar. She opened it and saw the sprinkles. They looked harmless. They looked like candy.

Lisa took a handful of sprinkles and put them in her mouth. She expected them to be sweet and crunchy. But they were not. They were spicy and hot. They burned her tongue and made her cough. Lisa dropped the jar and the sprinkles spilled everywhere. She cried and ran to her mom.

Her mom heard her cry and saw the mess. She was angry and worried. She hugged Lisa and gave her some water. She asked her what happened. Lisa told her the truth. She said she was sorry. She said she wanted to bake with the sprinkles.

Her mom explained that the sprinkles were not for baking. They were for decorating. They were for making firework pictures on the sidewalk. They were for fun, not for eating. She said Lisa should never touch them again. She said Lisa should always listen to her mom.

Lisa nodded and said she understood. She said she learned her lesson. She said she would never eat the sprinkles again. She said she still loved to bake with her mom. She said she hoped her mom still loved her.

Her mom smiled and kissed her. She said she still loved her very much. She said they could bake another cake together. She said they could use some other sprinkles. She said they could use some that were harmless. She said they could use some that were sweet and crunchy. She said they could use some that were pink. Like Lisa's jacket.

There were two friends, Ben and Molly. Ben was always telling Molly about the things he knew. One day he said, "I recommend getting a diamond. It's one of the best things ever." Molly thought it was a good idea, so she said she would get one.

The next week, Ben and Molly went to the store. Ben thought Molly should get a real diamond, but Molly said she didn't have enough money so she was going to get a fake one instead. Ben was disappointed and tried to convince her to get the real diamond, but she didn't want to listen. 

Eventually, Molly bought the fake diamond and they both left the store. Little did Molly know, the diamond was fake! Ben knew all along, but he didn't want to tell Molly because he wanted her to learn her lesson.

The next week when Molly looked at her diamond, it started to fall apart. She was upset and wished she had listened to Ben. Molly called Ben and said, "I should've taken your advice! I wish I had gotten the real diamond!" Ben just said, "I told you so!"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the sunshine. One day, she went to the park with her mommy and daddy. 

Lily saw some pretty flowers and wanted to gather them. She picked them carefully and put them in her basket. 

After playing for a while, Lily's mommy noticed that her cap was missing. They looked everywhere and finally found it under a dirty pile of leaves. Lily's mommy cleaned it up and put it back on her head. 

Lily was happy to have her cap back and continued to gather more flowers. She had a fun day at the park with her family. The end.

Once upon a time, in a green forest, there was a family of birds. They lived happily in a big tree. One day, a big storm came and the wind blew the birds' home away. The family was very sad.

The little bird, named Tim, wanted to help his family. He nodded his head and said, "I will find a new home for us!" Tim flew around the forest, looking for a new tree to live in. But every tree he found was too small or not safe for his family.

Finally, Tim found a big and strong tree. He nodded his head and knew it was the perfect home for his family. He flew back to his family and told them about the tree. The family was so happy and they all went to the new tree together.

In their new home, the family of birds was safe and happy again. The big storm had passed, and the green forest was peaceful once more. Tim was very proud that he had helped his family. They all lived happily ever after in their new tree home.

John was very excited. He was going to have a telephone call today! He had never made or received a call before. 

John was not sure what to do, so his mum showed him how to answer the telephone. She said to say 'hello' when it starts ringing and to talk calmly. 

John waited and waited until he heard the telephone ring. He ran over and picked up the receiver. He said 'hello' in his calmest voice but he was so excited inside. 

His uncle was at the other end of the phone. John was so happy to hear his voice. They talked for ages. 

John was delighted that he had made his first telephone call. He was very proud of himself for answering the call and talking calmly.

Lily liked to skip in the park. She skipped with her mom and dad. She skipped with her dog. She skipped with her friends. Skipping made her happy.

One day, she saw a new thing in the park. It was small and black and had six legs. It was an insect. Lily wanted to see it better. She stopped skipping and went closer.

The insect was restless. It moved fast on the grass. It did not like Lily. It made a loud buzz. It flew at Lily's face. Lily was scared. She ran away.

Lily's mom and dad saw what happened. They hugged Lily and told her it was okay. They said the insect was a bee. They said bees can sting, but they also make honey. They said bees are good for flowers and trees.

Lily felt better. She learned something new. She decided to skip again. But she did not go near the bees. She skipped with her mom and dad. She skipped with her dog. She skipped with her friends. Skipping made her happy.

Once upon a time, there was a nice little boy. His name was Joe. Joe wanted to explore a secret chamber. So he opened the door of the chamber and stepped inside. Inside, he saw something he had never seen before. Everything around him was frozen! Joe looked around and saw that the walls, floor and ceiling of the chamber were all frozen solid. He also saw a nice icy chair in the middle of the room! Joe touched the chair and it felt cold and he realized it was frozen too! Joe was so excited! He had found the perfect place to explore. He stayed in the chamber for a while and explored. After a while he got tired and went back outside. Joe was so happy that he had frozen his way into this chamber. The chamber had been so much fun that Joe vowed to go back soon!

Once upon a time there lived a painter. He was a very clumsy painter and often knocked things over when he was working. One day he was painting a window when he accidentally knocked over his paint bucket.

"Oh no!" he cried as he watched the paint spill all over the floor.

Just then his friend, a goat, came over to help him. "Let's leave the mess for now," the goat said. "Come on, I know a better place to paint."

The painter agreed, so he left the spilled paint and followed the goat. As they walked, the goat pointed out things for the painter to paint. Soon enough, they reached the more perfect spot for the painter to work. 

The painter smiled and thanked his friend. He unpacked his painting supplies and began to work. The clumsy painter was careful not to tip over his paint bucket this time. He continued to paint until the sun was setting and he was finished.

The painter smiled as he admired his work. He waved goodbye to his friend and headed home with a happy heart.

One day, Mum and Dad were in the kitchen. Dad was looking around and noticed the dishwasher. "This dishwasher is so expensive!" he said.

Mum replied, "Yes, but it's a very good one." 

Just then, their three year old daughter, called Bella, walked in. She had heard Dad and said, "What's 'expensive' mean?"

Mum smiled and said, "It's when something costs a lot of money."

Bella thought for a moment, and then noticed a shiny tea cup on the shelf. She pointed and said, "Mum, is that expensive?"

Mum laughed, "No, it's not expensive, sweetheart. But we should put it back in the cupboard, or it might break."

So Bella put the cup back in the cupboard. Then she looked at the dishwasher again, and said, "I don't like expensive things!"

Max was walking through the park. He was looking for something interesting. Suddenly, he heard a sound. It sounded like someone was crying. Max was curious, so he followed the sound to a bush. 

He saw a small spider sitting inside the bush. The spider was crying.
Max asked, ''What's wrong little one? Why are you so sad?''

The spider replied in a little voice, ''I got stuck in this bush and I'm too small to get out. I'm so ashamed.''

Max looked at the spider and said, ''Don't worry, I will help you.''

Max carefully reached into the bush and picked up the spider. He listened to it and said, ''There you go, now you can go wherever you want.''

The spider smiled and said, ''Thank you so much!'' Then it crawled off into the grass. 

Max watched the spider go and felt glad that he could make the little spider happy.

Gus was a nosy boy. His mom always warned him not to be so nosy but he just couldn't help it. Today he was exploring the grocery store. He had never been in one before. 

Gus started to wander around the aisles. He glanced down every aisle, poking his head into each one. Suddenly an old lady appeared and started scolding him. Gus was so scared he just shrugged and ran away. 

Gus kept on running until he wasn't sure where he was. He stopped to catch his breath but he had no idea how to get back home. He started to cry, feeling scared and alone. 

Gus got more and more lost. He had been wandering for hours when the sun started setting. Suddenly he started to feel very tired and was about to fall asleep when he heard noises coming toward him. 

Gus opened his eyes and saw a group of grown-ups coming his way. He knew he was in trouble. He wanted to run away again, but there was nowhere to go. The grown-ups grabbed him and he had to go with them, never to be heard from again.

Once upon a time, there was a princess named Lily. She had a delicate crown on her head and a pretty dress. One day, she saw a guard outside her castle. She asked him, "What are you doing here?"

The guard said, "I am here to protect you and your castle."

Lily was excited to hear that. She said, "Thank you for guarding me. I feel safe now."

The guard smiled and said, "It's my pleasure. It's important to keep you safe."

Lily felt happy and safe with the guard around. She continued to wear her delicate crown and play in her castle. The end.

Lily and Tom were twins who liked to play outside. One day, they saw a big bird with white and black feathers. It was a swan. The swan was swimming in a pond near their house.

"Let's follow the swan!" Lily said. "Maybe it will take us to a new place."

Tom nodded. He liked to explore. They ran after the swan, but they did not tell their mom where they were going.

The swan led them to a forest. The forest was cold and dark. Lily and Tom felt scared. They could not see the pond or their house anymore.

"Where are we?" Tom asked. "I want to go back."

"Me too," Lily said. "But I don't know the way."

They heard a loud noise. It was the swan. It was calling for them. They followed the noise and saw the swan again. It was waiting for them near a stream. The stream was clear and peaceful. The swan looked at them with kind eyes.

"Thank you, swan," Lily said. "Can you show us the way home?"

The swan nodded. It swam along the stream, and Lily and Tom walked beside it. Soon, they saw the pond and their house again. They were happy and relieved.

They ran to their mom and hugged her. They told her what happened. Their mom was angry and worried. She scolded them for leaving without telling her. She also thanked the swan for helping them.

"Next time, you must not follow strangers, even if they are animals," their mom said. "You could get lost or hurt. You must always stay with me or someone you know and trust."

Lily and Tom nodded. They learned their lesson. They said sorry to their mom and to the swan. They also said thank you to the swan again. The swan smiled and flew away. Lily and Tom waved goodbye. They never forgot the swan and the stream.

Once upon a time there was a kind, gentle king who ruled over a small kingdom. He was very beloved by his people and was known for always making wise decisions. 

One morning, the king was taking a walk in his garden, when he noticed a delicate cloth on the ground. It had beautiful gold embroidery and must have belonged to a very rich person.

The king picked up the cloth and wondered how it had gotten there. At that moment, one of his servants hurried over to him. 

The servant announced, "Your Majesty! You must lead us to find out who the cloth belongs to. It looks like a priceless heirloom and we should return it to the rightful owner."

The king agreed and set off with his servants on a journey to find the owner of the cloth. After a long search, the king and his servants found the true owner of the cloth - a poor family living in a nearby village.

The kind king took the cloth to the family and thanked them for their hard work and care. He also taught them a valuable lesson : always look after your possessions and take care of them as if they are as delicate as the cloth. 

The family thanked the king and his servants for their kindness. From that day on, the king and his people led by example and taught others the same valuable lesson.

One warm spring day, a little girl named Lucy was playing in the garden. As she ran around, she saw a big puddle. She splashed her feet in the puddle, feeling the cool water on her skin. She felt so spoiled to be able to play in the sun while the water tickled her feet.

Next, she ran to the pond. There, she saw some fish swimming around. She burst out giggling and made lots of big splashes. The fish were scared and quickly swam away.

Lucy enjoyed running around and playing in the sunshine all day. When it was time to go inside, she was sad - she had been having so much fun. But she knew there would be lots more warm, sunny spring days for her to enjoy soon.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside with his friends. One day, Timmy and his friends decided to play a game of tag. Timmy was very excited to play.

As they were playing, Timmy fell and hurt his knee. His friends helped him up and asked if he was okay. Timmy said his knee hurt but he wanted to keep playing. His friends said he should rest and let his knee get better.

Timmy didn't listen and kept playing. He thought he was fit enough to keep going. But as the game continued, Timmy's knee hurt more and more. He couldn't complete the game and had to go home early.

When Timmy got home, his knee was very swollen and he couldn't walk. His mom took him to the doctor and they found out that Timmy had hurt his knee badly. Timmy had to stay in bed for a long time and couldn't play with his friends. Timmy learned that it's important to listen to your body and rest when you're hurt.

Once upon a time, there was a powerful cat named Tom. Tom lived in a small house with a big bell. Every day, Tom liked to drink milk from a bowl. One day, Tom saw a mouse named Jerry near his house.

"Hello, Jerry!" said Tom. "Do you want to play with me and my big bell?" Jerry looked at the bell and said, "Yes, I want to play with you and your big bell, Tom!"

Tom and Jerry played with the big bell all day. They laughed and had fun. When they were tired, they drank milk together. They became good friends and played with the big bell every day.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. Her name was Jane and she was very excited. She loved playing outside and exploring in the yard.

One day, Jane was outside playing in the grass. Suddenly, she saw a big insect. She had never seen an insect like it before! She was so excited that she let out a big scream.

Jane's mom heard her daughter's loud scream and came to see what was wrong.

"What happened, sweetheart?" her mom asked.

Jane pointed towards the insect and said "Mommy, look! A bug! It's huge!"

Her mom smiled and said: "Yes, that's a grasshopper. He's much bigger than the other bugs you've seen before!"

Jane smiled and said "He's so cool! Can I catch him?"

Her mom nodded and Jane ran to catch the grasshopper. She was so excited that she was jumping up and down with joy!

The end.

Maddy was a three year old girl and she was very organized. She always brought her toys in a neat pile to her room. One day, Maddy saw the mailman coming to her house. She ran outside to get the mail from him, and he gave her a big stack. She was so excited, she couldn't help but to tear the envelopes open. When she was finished, all of the mail was gone!

Maddy's mom heard the noise and walked outside to see what she was doing. "Maddy, what have you done?" asked her mom.

Maddy held up the torn pieces of paper, her face full of guilt. "I tore open all of the mail," she said sadly.

Her mom smiled and said, "That was very organized of you. I'm glad you remembered to open the mail."

Maddy smiled and ran off to show her friends her handiwork.

Once upon a time there was a coat. The coat was very old, but it was still so beautiful. Every day, the old man would take the coat outside. Then, he would take a soft cloth and start to polish carefully. 

One day, his three-year-old granddaughter came to visit him. She asked him, â€œGrandpa, what are you doing?â€

He smiled and replied, â€œIâ€™m polishing this coat. It used to be very shiny. See? Now itâ€™s so beautiful again.â€

The little girl smiled and said, â€œCan I help?â€

â€œOf course you can!â€ the old man said. So the two of them started polishing the coat together. When they finished, it had become even shinier and more beautiful than ever before. The little girl was so proud!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to wear fancy dresses and play with her dolls. One day, she went to the park with her mom and saw a boy playing with a ball. She wanted to play too, so she went up to him and said, "Hi, can I play with you?"

The boy looked at her and said, "Sure, but first I have a question for you. What's your name?"

"My name is Lily," she said with a smile.

"That's a pretty name," the boy replied. "My name is Max. Do you want to play catch with me?"

Lily nodded and they started playing. It was so much fun that they didn't even notice how quiet it had become around them. When it was time to go home, Lily said goodbye to Max and thanked him for playing with her. She went home feeling happy and excited to have made a new friend.

Once upon a time, there was a loud man. He wanted to find treasure. So he went looking for it everywhere. He asked everyone, "Where is the treasure?"

One day, the man saw a little girl. He asked her, "Where is the treasure?" But the girl just shook her head and said nothing.

The man got very angry. He shouted, "Come with me! I want to show you where the treasure is!" The little girl was scared. She came with the man and he took her to a dark, scary cave.

The loud man said, "This is where the treasure is!" But, when the man opened the cave, there was nothing inside.

The little girl was so upset. She said, "There is no treasure here!" But the loud man just laughed and said, "Ha ha! You will never find treasure! You will never be rich!" and he walked away, leaving the little girl all alone in the dark.

Once upon a time, there was a mum and a dad. Both of them were very organized. During the day, the dad worked in a big building, while the mum stayed at home and cooked tasty food.

Every evening, when the dad came home, the mum hugged him and said: "I've found something to increase the fun!" The dad was curious.

The mum asked him: "Do you want to try this whip?".

The dad laughed and said: "Yes!" So they went outside to their garden, where they had lots of fun playing with the new whip.

The dad soon got better and better at using the whip. The mum was so proud of him. He would jump here and there, and make funny shapes with the whip in the air!

The mum and dad laughed a lot and said that the whip had really increased their fun! They enjoyed playing with it together every evening.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Anna. She was three years old and very brave. One day, Anna imagined a guard. He was standing tall, wearing a suit and a hat. He wore a big smile on his face.

Anna was very nervous. She didn't know what the guard wanted. But he was friendly. He told Anna that he was there to take care of her. He would always watch over her and protect her.

Anna was happy to have the guard there. She felt much safer. She knew that even when she was on her own, the guard would always be there to take care of her. 

Every day, Anna would imagine the guard watching over her and she was never scared again.

One day, a funny cat and a little dog went to play at the park. They liked to run and jump on the soft grass. The sun was shining and the sky was blue.

The funny cat saw a big net near the trees. "What is that?" said the cat to the dog. The dog said, "I don't know, but let's go see!" They ran to the net and looked at it. The cat said, "I think we can play with this!"

The cat and the dog played with the net all day. They jumped over it and ran around it. The sun started to go down and it was time to go home. The cat said, "That was so much fun!" The dog said, "Yes, we should play with the net again tomorrow!" And they went home, happy and tired from their fun day at the park.

Once upon a time there lived a brave little mouse who liked to explore. One day the mouse decided to explore a big forest. As he made his way through the forest, he heard a whistle. 

The mouse was scared but brave at the same time and so he followed the sound of the whistle. He soon found an elderly man with a big grey beard.

The mouse shouted 'Who are You?' but the man did not answer. The mouse asked again 'Why are you whistling?'

The old man smiled and said 'I'm just enjoying the nature.'

The mouse was so brave and curious, he dared to ask 'Can I join you?' 

The old man grinned and said 'I'd love that.'

So the brave little mouse joined the elderly man in the forest, and they enjoyed the nature together. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved going to the library with her mommy. One day, Lily saw an ugly monster in the library. She was scared and didn't know what to do.

Lily's mommy saw that she was scared and asked her what was wrong. Lily told her about the ugly monster. Her mommy answered, "Don't worry, sweetie. There are no monsters in the library. Let's go take a closer look."

Together, they walked over to where Lily had seen the monster. It turned out to be just a big, ugly statue. Lily laughed and said, "That's not a monster, it's just a statue!" Her mommy smiled and they continued to enjoy their time at the library.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in her backyard. It was big and green with smooth grass. Lily liked to run and jump around in it.

One day, Lily saw her neighbor's toy and she wanted to play with it. She asked her neighbor if she could play with it, but the neighbor said no. Lily was sad and went back to her backyard. 

But then, Lily remembered something her mom had told her. She remembered that it's not nice to take things that don't belong to you. Lily decided to be a good girl and not take her neighbor's toy. She gained something very important that day - the value of being honest and respectful.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her dolls and her favorite toy was a pink teddy bear. One day, she went to the park with her mom and lost her teddy bear.

Lily was very sad and cried a lot. Her mom tried to comfort her and said, "Don't worry, we will find your teddy bear. Let's look for it together." They searched the park but couldn't find the teddy bear anywhere.

Suddenly, Lily saw a pale man with a hat walking away from them. She pointed at him and said, "Mommy, that man has my teddy bear!" But it was too late, the man had already left with the teddy bear.

Lily's mom tried to prevent her from chasing after the man, but Lily was too upset and ran after him. Unfortunately, the man was too fast and Lily couldn't catch up. She returned to her mom crying even more.

From that day on, Lily learned to take better care of her things and never let them out of her sight. But she never forgot her favorite teddy bear and always wondered where it went.

Bob was a 3 year old boy who was very curious about the world around him. One day, his mom told him that he was going to have to take a test. Bob was embarrassed because he didn't know what a test was.

So, he asked his mom what a test was. She smiled and explained that it was like an activity but much harder. She said that if he tried his best, he would do great!

The next day, Bob woke up early and went to school. He was a little bit nervous but he was determined to do his best. During the test, he tried to answer every question correctly. 

When the results came out a few days later, Bob was relieved to see he had done well. He was even more relieved to see that none of his friends had done better than him. Bob hadn't been embarrassed about his score; he had done his best and he was proud of that.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Anna. She had a big, purple ball. She loved to play with it every day. One day, she saw a weak, small bird in her yard. The bird could not fly well.

Anna said to the bird, "Do not be sad, little bird. I will help you." She took the bird inside her house. She gave it food and water. The bird started to feel better.

The bird looked at Anna's purple ball and said, "I admire your ball, Anna. It is so big and pretty." Anna smiled and said, "Thank you, little bird. I am happy you like it." They played with the ball together. Soon, the bird felt strong and could fly again. The bird and Anna became the best of friends.

Mum was anxious. She had many things to do and the day was flying by. But she decided to take a moment and relax with her little daughter. So they sat together on the couch, snuggled up close.

Mum hugged her daughter and kissed her thumb. "Time for a nap, little one," she said.

The little girl rubbed her eyes and stretched. She opened her mouth wide and let out a big yawn. Mum smiled and hugged her again. She was so sweet and tired.

Soon, the little girl was sound asleep. Mum stayed close and stroked her daughter's head. All was peaceful and calm.

Mum was so grateful for the quiet moment. It was the best way to relax and feel less anxious. Even a few minutes could make a difference. It was amazing what a yawn could do.

One day, a little girl was walking outside, wearing her pink shoes. She saw a pretty butterfly, and decided to follow it. She carried her shoes and ran across the field. 

The butterfly was fast and she had to run to keep up with it. Finally, the butterfly flew into a small tree. The little girl smiled and said, "hello, butterfly!"

The butterfly looked at her and asked, "would you like me to carry your shoes?". The girl was surprised, but nodded and said yes. The butterfly said, "I will take them to a safe place". 

The little girl was glad. She thanked the butterfly and watched as it flew away, taking her shoes. A few minutes later, the butterfly returned with the shoes and said, "here they are, safe and sound!". 

The little girl smiled. She thanked the butterfly and hugged it, before putting on her shoes. She waved goodbye to the butterfly and skipped off, happy to have her shoes back.

Once upon a time, in a wild forest, there was a kind bunny named Bobo. Bobo had many friends in the forest. One day, Bobo found a bottle of lotion. He did not know what it was, but he took it with him.

Soon, Bobo met his friend, Toto the turtle. Toto had dry skin and felt sad. Bobo showed Toto the lotion and said, "Let's try this on your skin!" They put the lotion on Toto's skin, and it felt much better. Toto was very happy and said, "Thank you, Bobo!"

From that day on, Bobo and Toto shared the lotion with all their friends in the wild forest. Everyone felt better and thanked Bobo and Toto for their help. They all played and had fun together, and they lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toy cars. He had a red one, a blue one, and a green one. Timmy's favorite thing to do was to make his cars zoom around the room.

One day, Timmy's grandpa came to visit. Grandpa had a big, curly mustache that Timmy loved to touch. Grandpa also brought a bag of chips that were very spicy. Timmy didn't like spicy things, but Grandpa said they were very tasty.

Later that day, Timmy and Grandpa were playing with the toy cars. Timmy made the red car zoom around the room, but then it crashed into the green car. Grandpa said, "Oh no! Looks like we need a mechanic to fix those cars." Timmy didn't know what a mechanic was, but he soon found out when Grandpa took him to a car repair shop.

At the shop, Timmy saw a man with a big mustache just like Grandpa's. The man fixed the cars and Timmy was so happy. He thanked the man and went home with his cars, ready to zoom them around again.

Once upon a time, there was a group of fish living together in the sea. One day, one of the fish named Daisy started feeling very thoughtful. She couldn't stop thinking about something very special.

Daisy asked the other fish, "Have you ever seen something called ink?"

The other fish shrugged and said, "No, what is it? We have never seen it before."

Daisy replied, "It's a magical thing! If you gather it together, it becomes very colourful. I want to go find some ink and make something special."

So Daisy and all of her friends started to gather up ink. They looked far and wide until they had found enough ink.

When they were done, Daisy came up with a wonderful idea. With the help of her friends, they made something very special and colourful.

The friends were very happy with the creation and Daisy was very thoughtful. She was very happy to have made something special with her friends.

Once upon a time, there was a family who decided to go for a picnic in the park. The sun was shining and the birds were singing. Everyone was excited.

The dad brought all of the food, including spaghetti. He cooked the spaghetti over the fire in the park. The mother brought the plates, forks and spoons.

The family ate the spaghetti in the park and it was delicious! Everyone was grateful for the delicious food. After they finished eating, they played a game of tag and then lay down on the grass and looked at the clouds in the sky.

Before they left, they made sure they put all the rubbish in the bins and put out the fire. Then they all went home happy, feeling grateful for the wonderful picnic in the park.

Once upon a time, there was a big gray elephant named Elly. Elly was sad because she thought she was ugly. She had big ears and a long nose, and she felt different from the other animals.

One day, a little bird named Benny flew to Elly. Benny saw that Elly was sad and asked, "Why are you sad, Elly?" Elly told Benny that she felt ugly and did not like her big ears and long nose. Benny looked at Elly and said, "I think you are not ugly. You are special."

Benny promised to show Elly how her big ears and long nose made her special. They went to the river, and Benny asked Elly to use her long nose to spray water on the dry plants. Elly did and the plants grew happy and green. Then, Benny asked Elly to use her big ears to fan the hot animals. Elly did, and all the animals felt cool and happy.

Elly learned that being different was not ugly. She was special and had her own way to help others. Elly and Benny became best friends, and they lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, her mom said, "Lily, we're going to visit grandma at the beach!" Lily was excited because she loved the sea. 

When they arrived, they went for a walk on the beach. Lily saw a crab and said, "Mommy, what's that?" Her mom said, "That's a crab. It lives in the sea." Lily was confused because she thought crabs lived in the sand. 

Later that day, they went to visit grandma. Grandma had a surprise for Lily. She took her to a nearby aquarium where Lily saw all kinds of sea creatures. Lily was so happy and said, "Thank you, grandma! I love visiting you at the beach!"

There was a little girl who was playing in the park. She saw a yellow balloon floating in the sky. She was so excited that she started to wave her arms in the air. She wanted the balloon to come closer to her.

Suddenly, the wind blew the balloon right in front of her. She was so happy that she laughed and waved her hands more. She grabbed the balloon and hugged it tightly.

The little girl started to walk around with the balloon. Everywhere she went, people waved and smiled at her. She was having such a great time! She even made balloon animals and showed them to her friends.

Finally, it was time to the little girl to go home. She looked up at the sky and said goodbye to the yellow balloon. She waved and waved until she couldn't see it anymore. She was sad to see it go, but she was happy to have so much fun.

Mum and Dad were so busy. They were in the kitchen, making dinner and tidying the house. They worked hard, but they always had time to give each other a kiss.

Daddy stopped to give Mum a big kiss. He said, "I love you."

Mum smiled and said, "I love you too".

They looked around the house, and saw a big chair in the corner. Daddy glanced at Mum and said, "Why don't we sit in the chair and have a cuddle?".

Mum smiled and they both went over to the chair and sat down. Daddy put his arm around Mum and they kissed again. They stayed like that until they heard a noise in the kitchen.

Mum said, "We better go, it's getting late and we need to finish the dinner".

They gave each other one last kiss, then went back to the kitchen. After dinner, they both sat in the big chair and cuddled, until they fell asleep.

Tom and Jen were twins who liked to play outside. They had a big yard with a swing, a slide and a sandbox. Sometimes, they helped their dad with the grill, where he cooked meat and corn for dinner. They knew the grill was hot and they had to be careful.

One day, Tom and Jen were playing with their toy cars in the sandbox. They pretended they were racing on a track. Tom had a red car and Jen had a blue car. They made zooming and honking noises as they moved their cars around. Tom wanted to win the race, so he pushed his car faster and faster. Jen tried to catch up, but Tom was too quick.

Tom saw the grill nearby and had an idea. He thought he could make his car go even faster if he put it on the grill. He did not think about how hot the grill was or how it could hurt his car. He ran to the grill and threw his car on it. He shouted, "Look, Jen, my car is on fire! I win!"

Jen saw what Tom did and felt scared and sad. She knew the grill was dangerous and she loved her brother. She did not want him to get burned or lose his car. She ran to the grill and tried to grab Tom's car. But the car was too hot and it burned her hand. She screamed and dropped the car. She started to cry.

Tom heard Jen's scream and saw her hand. He realized he had done a bad thing. He felt sorry and ashamed. He ran to Jen and hugged her. He said, "I'm sorry, Jen, I'm sorry. I was silly and mean. Are you okay?"

Jen felt Tom's hug and heard his words. She knew he was sorry and he loved her. She felt compassionate and forgave him. She said, "It's okay, Tom, it's okay. I love you. But don't do that again, okay?"

Tom and Jen went inside and told their dad what happened. Their dad was angry and worried. He scolded Tom for being reckless and careless. He praised Jen for being brave and kind. He took them to the bathroom and put some cream and a bandage on Jen's hand. He said, "You two are lucky it was not worse. You have to be careful with the grill. It can burn you and your things. You have to respect it and listen to me. Do you understand?"

Tom and Jen nodded and said, "Yes, dad, we understand. We're sorry. We won't do it again."

Their dad hugged them and said, "I love you both. Now, let's go have some dinner. I have some meat and corn for you. And some ice cream for dessert."

Tom and Jen smiled and said, "Yay, ice cream!" They followed their dad to the kitchen and ate their dinner. They learned their lesson and never played with the grill again.

Once upon a time, there was a big bean. It was the biggest bean in the garden. All the other beans were small. The big bean was very proud.

One day, a little girl saw the big bean. She wanted to pick it. But the big bean did not want to be picked. It wanted to stay in the garden with its friends. So, the big bean told the little girl to go away.

But the little girl did not listen. She kept following the big bean. The big bean tried to run away, but the little girl was too fast. Finally, the big bean had an idea. It called all its friends to come and help. Together, they made a big wall around themselves. The little girl could not get through. She went away, and the big bean and its friends were safe.

Once upon a time, there was a little bear named Teddy. One day, Teddy woke up early and wanted to go outside to play. He went outside and saw a little bird with a broken wing. The bird said, "I can't fly, can you help me?"

Teddy said, "I will help you!" He went back inside and got a bandage for the bird's wing. He carefully put the bandage on the bird's wing and the bird said, "Thank you, Teddy! You are so kind."

Then, a nosy rabbit came hopping by and said, "What are you doing, Teddy?" Teddy replied, "I am helping my new friend, the bird. He can't fly because his wing is broken, so I put a bandage on it." The rabbit said, "Wow, you are a great friend! Can I help too?" Teddy said, "Of course!" And they all played together happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and her favorite toy was a teddy bear. One day, Lily's mom gave her a piece of cake to eat. Lily was so happy that she took a big bite from the cake. Suddenly, her teddy bear started to shrink! 

Lily was scared and didn't know what to do. She looked around and saw a knife on the table. She picked up the knife and tried to cut the cake, but the knife was too big for her little hands. So, Lily put the knife down and thought of another idea. 

Then, she remembered that her teddy bear was safe in her pocket. She quickly took the teddy bear out of her pocket and hugged it tightly. To her surprise, the teddy bear started to grow again! Lily was so happy that she hugged her teddy bear even tighter and ate the rest of her cake. From that day on, Lily made sure to always keep her teddy bear safe in her pocket.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Daisy. Daisy carried her little pet mole in her arms - it was so small and cute! Everyone thought the little mole was very attractive and admired it very much.

One day, Daisy was playing in the park when a boy named Andy saw the mole. "What's that?" he asked her. Daisy beamed and said, "It's my pet mole". 

Andy asked if he could pet the mole, Daisy said yes and Andy gently stroked the mole's head. The mole felt happy and curled up in Daisy's arms and made little squeaky noises.

Andy smiled at Daisy, "Your mole is very attractive," he said. Daisy smiled back and said, "Thank you, Andy". Then, Daisy and Andy played together in the park until it was time to go home. Daisy carefully carried her mole all the way home.

Once upon a time, there was a pilot named Timmy. Timmy was a dependable pilot who flew big planes in the sky. He loved his job very much.

Once upon a time there was a clever girl who lived in a big city. One day, the girl decided to go exploring. She saw tall buildings, bright lights and many people. The girl was so excited to explore this new place.

Suddenly, the girl heard a loud yell from a tall building. She was scared and started to cry. But then she remembered how clever she was and decided to go find the source of the noise. She walked around for a few minutes until she saw a big window with a figure in it.

The girl saw that the figure was actually a man who was yelling at someone outside of the building. He was sad and frustrated and seemed to be having a fight with someone.

The girl felt sorry for the man and wanted to help. She yelled out to him and asked what was wrong. The man was surprised to hear her voice, and then paused and seemed to calm down a little. He told her his story, and thanked her for listening.

At the end of the day, the girl felt proud of herself. She had used her clever mind to help a person in need, and she went back home with a big smile on her face.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Sarah. She was three years old and loved to explore. One day, she went outside to play.

Sarah saw a flower in the garden and wasn't sure what it was. She went to get her mom to ask what it was. Her mom showed Sarah an orange flower. It was so pretty.

Once there was a dog named Fluffy. It was a small and cuddly dog. 
Fluffy wanted to play with a ball, but it was too dirty. All the dirt made it have a rough texture.
Fluffy looked around and saw a cat named Tom borrowing a ball from a mouse. Fluffy asked Tom for the ball, but he said no. 
So Fluffy went to look for a cleaner ball. He found one and asked the little mouse if he could borrow it. The mouse said yes, and Fluffy was so excited. 
He jumped around and thanked the mouse. Fluffy then ran with the ball playing until he was tired. Slowly, he went back to give it back to the mouse. 
The mouse was happy to get it back and thanked Fluffy for taking good care of it. 
Fluffy was so proud to have play with a clean ball, and he never borrowed a dirty ball again.

Tom liked to play with pebbles. He had many pebbles of different colors and shapes. He liked to make patterns with them on the ground. He liked to pretend they were his friends.

One day, he found a very special pebble. It was shiny and smooth and had many colors. It looked like a rainbow. Tom was very happy. He named the pebble Ray and put it in his pocket.

He wanted to show Ray to his mom and dad. He ran to his house. But on the way, he tripped and fell. He scraped his knee and cried. He felt something fall out of his pocket. It was Ray.

He looked for Ray on the ground. But he could not see him. He saw many other pebbles, but not Ray. He felt very sad. He lost his special pebble.

He heard a voice. It said, "Don't cry, Tom. I'm here." He looked up. He saw a brilliant light in the sky. It was Ray. He had become a star.

"Ray, is that you?" Tom asked.

"Yes, Tom. It's me. I'm sorry I fell out of your pocket. But I'm still your friend. I'll always shine for you at night. You can make a wish on me."

Tom smiled. He wiped his tears. He said, "Thank you, Ray. You're the best pebble ever. I wish you're happy as a star."

"I am, Tom. I am. And I wish you're happy too. Good night, Tom."

"Good night, Ray." Tom said.

He went home and told his mom and dad about Ray. They hugged him and kissed his knee. They said he had a very big imagination. Tom said he had a very big heart. He looked out the window and saw Ray twinkling. He waved to him and went to sleep. He dreamed of pebbles and stars.

Once upon a time, there was a little black cat. The cat was very soft and liked to sleep in the sun. One day, the cat went outside to play. The cat saw a bird and tried to catch it, but the bird flew away. The cat was sad and went to find something else to do.

The cat saw some butter and decided to spread it on a piece of bread. The cat was having fun until it accidentally knocked over the butter. The butter spilled all over the floor and the cat slipped and fell. The cat hurt its leg and had to go to the vet. The vet said the cat's leg was broken and it would never be able to play again. The cat was very sad and missed playing outside.

Once upon a time there lived a little boy called Tim. Tim liked to explore and learn many new things.

One day, Tim wanted to go out and see the world. He put on his coat and went out into the garden.

The garden was full of mist. Tim was shy and scared of getting lost in the strange mist.

He looked around for someone to help him. Suddenly, he saw a little bird perching on a tree.

Tim asked the bird, "Little bird, can you help me?" 

The little bird replied, "I cannot help you, but I can teach you a lesson. If you want to explore, you must study first so that you know what you are doing."

Tim thanked the little bird and went back inside. From then on, Tim spent more time studying before he explored the world.

The moral of the story is that it is important to have knowledge before going out on a new adventure.

Once upon a time, there was a brave dog called Bob. He lived in a very nice house with his owner. One day, Bob's owner wanted to fix something in the house, so he got a screw to help. But when he tried to use it, it wouldn't go in. Bob saw this and decided to help. He found a different screw and let his owner use it. His owner was so happy and thanked him for being so brave. After he fixed the thing, Bob ran around the house, happy to have been so helpful. The end.

One day, a girl named Lily found a tray full of yummy cookies. She wanted to eat them all, but she knew she should share with her friend, Tom. So, she split the cookies into two piles. One pile for her and one pile for Tom.

"Tom, I have yummy cookies!" Lily said. "I split them for us to share."

But Tom was not happy. He wanted more cookies. "No, I want more!" he said. This made Lily sad. She thought she had split the cookies fairly.

Lily and Tom talked about the cookies. They decided to ask their mom to help them split the cookies again. Mom made sure both Lily and Tom got the same amount of yummy cookies. Now, they were both happy and could enjoy their yummy cookies together.

Once there was a chubby little girl. She was playing in her room, when all of a sudden she heard a loud "rip"! She looked around and saw that her favorite dress was torn in two. She began to tear up.

Her mom saw her crying and said, "It's okay honey, don't cry." She took the little girl by the hand and went to the store to buy her some new clothes.

They went through so many different stores, but the little girl couldn't find anything nice that she liked. Until, at the very last store, they found a perfect dress - it was exactly the color of a shimmering rainbow!

The girl was so excited and put it on right away. She looked in the mirror and laughed. She wanted to wear her new dress everywhere! She even convinced her mom to buy her a matching pair of shoes!

The little girl was so happy that she had tears of joy in her eyes. She gave her mom a big chubby hug and thanked her for helping her find the perfect dress. And from that day on, she never stopped smiling!

Once upon a time, there was a big elephant named Ellie. Ellie was very heavy and weighed a lot. She loved to eat peanuts and bananas, which made her even heavier. One day, Ellie saw a beautiful sunset and it made her very happy.

But the next day, it started to rain and Ellie became miserable. She didn't like getting wet and muddy. She decided to go for a walk to cheer herself up. As she walked, she saw a big scale and decided to weigh herself. She was surprised to see that she had lost some weight! This made her feel much better and she went back home feeling happy again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her pillow, which was soft and fluffy. One day, Lily's mom asked her to help store some toys in the closet. Lily was happy to help.

As they were putting the toys away, Lily saw an incredible toy that she wanted to play with. She asked her mom if she could take it out of the closet, but her mom said no. Lily was sad and started to cry.

Her mom explained to her that sometimes we can't have everything we want right away. We have to wait and be patient. She told Lily that it's important to be grateful for what we have and to take care of our things, like her pillow.

Lily understood and felt better. She hugged her pillow and said thank you to her mom. From that day on, Lily learned to be patient and grateful. She also took good care of her pillow and stored it safely every night.

John was so happy to be at the fair. He saw so many amazing things and wanted to explore. Suddenly, John sneezed. People at the fair looked his way and he blushed. When he looked up, he was surprised to see his teacher. His teacher was at a meeting but now she was walking towards him.

John thought he was in trouble. He tried to explain what he was doing but quickly realized he was in trouble. His teacher said, â€œThis isnâ€™t a fair for you to play. You should be in school.â€ Then she took him home.

Anna and Ben like to play with their toy cars. They have many cars of different colors and sizes. They race them on the floor and make noises like vroom and beep.

One day, they find a shiny coin on the floor. It is round and brown and has a picture of a man on it. Anna picks it up and shows it to Ben.

"Look, what is this?" she asks.

Ben looks at the coin and says, "I don't know. It is not a car. Maybe it is a button."

Anna shakes her head. "No, it is not a button. It is too hard and heavy. Maybe it is a medal."

Ben shakes his head. "No, it is not a medal. It is too small and flat. Maybe it is a cookie."

Anna laughs. "No, it is not a cookie. It is not sweet and yummy. Maybe it is a copper."

Ben is curious. He has never heard of a copper before. He asks, "What is a copper?"

Anna replies, "I don't know. I heard Mommy say it once. She said she needs more coppers to buy things. Maybe it is something you can trade for toys or candy."

Anna agrees. They put the coin in their pocket and run to find Mommy. They hope she will tell them more about coppers and what they can do with them.

Once there was a gentle girl named Rose. Rose loved climbing the stairs to get to the top of the house. Every time she was on the stair, Rose felt like she was the Queen of the house. She liked to make believe the stair was her own secret castle.

One day Rose's mom called her name. Rose was very excited and quickly ran to the stair. She waved goodbye to her mom and started to climb the stair. It was such a fun adventure. With each step she felt she was getting closer to becoming a queen.

At the top of the stair, Rose felt like she was really a queen. She stood on the landing looking down at her mom and suddenly she realised how big her mom was. Rose felt so amazed, she waved back to her mom with a big smile.
