Once upon a time there was a big volcano. It was very tight, but it was not all happy. One day, something bad happened to it. All of a sudden, it exploded and destroyed everything in the area. Everything was torn apart and it made a really big mess.

The people nearby were so scared, they all ran away. But they were all saved, because the volcano just destroyed things - there was no lava. It had all disappeared.

But then something amazing happened. All of the mess went away and everything was clean again. The area looked like new and the people were happy. They could go back to their homes and all was good.

The volcano was fixed and very tight again, but this time it was happy. Everyone was happy that the volcano was okay and so was the area. They all had a big party to celebrate the volcano being safe and tight!

Once there was a little boy who was feeling lucky. He decided to go on a special adventure one day. He put some special items in his pocket, and brought his favourite toy. 

He walked through the woods and heard the wind whisper. He was getting closer and closer to the secret place. He could feel his pocket starting to get heavy with the items he had collected. 

Finally, he made it to the special spot. He could feel the luckiness in the air. He quickly dug into his pocket and grew even luckier when he found the magic stone. 

The little boy smiled and whispered "thank you". He was so happy he had found this special lucky thing. Then he made sure to carefully store it away back in his pocket. He was off on the adventure of a lifetime.

Lily and Ben are twins. They like to play with animals. One day, they go to the zoo with Mom and Dad. They see many animals, like lions, monkeys, and elephants. They are very happy.

They come to a big cage with birds. The birds have many colors, like red, blue, and yellow. Lily and Ben want to see them closer. They rush to the cage and put their faces on the bars. They say hello to the birds.

But one bird is not happy. It is pale and sad. It does not sing or fly. It sits on a branch and looks at Lily and Ben. Lily and Ben see the bird and feel sorry for it. They ask Mom and Dad why the bird is pale and sad.

Mom and Dad say the bird is sick. It needs a doctor and medicine. They say the zoo people are trying to help the bird. They say Lily and Ben can pray for the bird to get better.

Lily and Ben nod. They say bye to the bird and tell it to be strong. They hope the bird will get better soon. They go to see other animals, but they do not forget the pale and sad bird. They pray for it in their hearts.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside in the park with his friends. One day, he went to the park to play with his friends, but he couldn't find his favorite toy car. He looked everywhere, but he couldn't find it. Timmy was very sad because he had lost his favorite toy car.

As he was looking for his toy car, he saw a wire on the ground. The wire was long and thin, and it looked like it had been there for a long time. Timmy picked up the wire and started to play with it. He twisted and turned the wire, and he made all kinds of shapes with it. Timmy was having so much fun playing with the wire that he forgot about his toy car.

After a while, Timmy's mom called him to go home. As he was leaving the park, he saw that the wire was dry. It had been lying on the ground for so long that it had become dry. Timmy thought it was funny that a wire could be dry. He decided to take the wire home with him and show it to his dad. When he got home, he showed the wire to his dad, and they both laughed at how silly it was that a wire could be dry.

Once upon a time two friends, Jack and Jill, were playing in the park. Suddenly, a big sign caught Jack's eye. It said "Do Not Fight". But Jack forgot the sign and started to fight with Jill. Jill was very worried because she thought Jack might get in trouble. But then Jill's mom ran over and stopped the fight. She gave them both a hug and reminded them to follow the sign. From then on, Jack and Jill were always careful to follow the sign and were never worried about fighting.

Once upon a time, there was a dog named Max. Max was a loyal dog who loved to walk with his owner, Tim. One day, Tim and Max went for a walk in the forest. It was very foggy and they could barely see because of the mist. Max was scared at first, but he stayed close to Tim and kept walking. Suddenly, they heard a noise in the bushes. Max barked loudly to scare away whatever was there. Tim was proud of Max for being so brave. They continued their walk and eventually the mist cleared up. Max was happy to have gone on a walk with his loyal owner.

Once there was a wealthy family with three kids. Two of them were in university, but the youngest one was only three. He wanted to go to university too!

One day, the three university students decided to take the youngest one with them on a fun day out. As they drove to the university, the little kid cheered with joy. 

When they arrived, the little kid wanted to explore everywhere. He ran around and screamed with excitement!

The university students showed him all the places and got him some ice cream. He was having so much fun!

At the end of the day, the family drove home and the little kid felt so happy. He dreamed of one day going to university too.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Max. Max liked to run and play in the park with his friends. One day, Max hurt his paw while playing. His owner took him to the veterinarian who helped Max feel better. Max was happy and wagged his tail.

Max liked to go on walks with his owner. One day, they walked by a construction site. It was very noisy! Max wondered why the big machines made so much noise. His owner explained that the machines were building a new building. Max thought it was interesting and wagged his tail. 

At night, Max slept in his cozy bed. He dreamed about playing with his friends and going on walks with his owner. Max was happy and felt loved. The end.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Lisa. She was sad, because she had broken her favorite toy. But her mommy was there to comfort her.

Mommy put Lisa on her big, soft mattress and hugged her. As her Mommy rocked her back and forth, Lisa felt a little better. 

Mommy sang a sweet song to Lisa and soon all her sadness had turned to dull happiness. Lisa snuggled into her mattress and closed her eyes. 

Soon Lisa was sleeping soundly and the sadness was forgotten. Lisa dreamt a happy dream and when she awoke, she knew that everything was going to be OK.

One day there was a wealthy lady who had a beautiful brush. She loved her brush very much and would take care of it like it was made of gold. 

One summer day, the wealthy lady was out for a walk and before she knew it, the day had gotten so hot that the brush started to melt. She was sad and tried to find the brush but it was nowhere to be seen. 

The wealthy lady was so worried about her beloved brush and wanted to get it back. She asked her neighbors if they saw where her brush had gone but none of them had seen what happened. 

She was determined to find her brush, so she started to search everywhere. Finally, after a long search, she found her brush covered in melted pieces! 

The wealthy lady was so relieved to see her brush safe and sound. She gave it a good clean, smiled and went on her way with her brush once again.

Once upon a time, there was a brown wolf. He was walking through the woods. He was feeling a bit thirsty, so he wanted to find a stream to get a drink. Suddenly, he heard an interesting sound.

The sound was coming from a little brown bear. The wolf said: "What are you doing?"

The bear looked up and said: "I am drying myself. I swam in the stream and now I am drying my fur."

The brown wolf smiled. He said: "I am thirsty. Can I have a drink?"

The bear said: "Yes, come and have a drink."

So the wolf went to the stream. He put his face in the cold water and drank. When he finished drinking, he thanked the little bear and said goodbye. The brown wolf went on his way and the brown bear returned to drying himself.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sue. Sue had a big bedroom with fancy things in it. She loved her room very much. One day, she saw a small flower in her room. The flower was trying to bloom.

Sue said to the flower, "Hello, little flower! Why are you trying to bloom in my bedroom?" The flower said, "I want to be a fancy flower in your room." Sue liked the idea, but she knew that flowers needed sun and water to grow.

Sue tried to help the flower. She gave it water and put it near the window. But the flower did not get enough sun. It tried very hard to bloom, but it could not. The flower became sad and said, "I am sorry, Sue. I cannot be a fancy flower in your room."

In the end, the flower did not bloom. It stayed small and sad. Sue felt bad for the flower. She wished she could help it more. But she knew that flowers needed sun and water to grow, and her bedroom was not the best place for a flower to live.

Tim and Mia were friends who liked to play on the sand. They had a big bucket and a small shovel. They wanted to make a castle near the sea.

But Tim and Mia had a quarrel. Tim said, "I want to use the shovel. It is mine." Mia said, "No, I want to use the shovel. You had it before." They pulled the shovel and shouted at each other.

The sea was watching them. The sea did not like their quarrel. The sea thought they were stupid. The sea said, "Stop it, you two. You are not nice. You are not sharing. You are making me angry."

Tim and Mia did not hear the sea. They kept on quarreling. The sea got angrier and angrier. The sea made a big wave and splashed them. The wave took their bucket and shovel and carried them away.

Tim and Mia were wet and sad. They lost their bucket and shovel. They looked at the sea. The sea looked at them. The sea said, "Now you see. You should be kind and share. You should not quarrel. You should be friends."

Tim and Mia felt sorry. They said, "We are sorry, sea. You are right. We were stupid. We will be kind and share. We will not quarrel. We will be friends."

The sea smiled and said, "That is good. I am glad. Here is your bucket and shovel. You can have them back. But be careful. Do not make me angry again."

Tim and Mia thanked the sea. They hugged each other and said, "We are sorry, friend. We will not fight again. We will play nicely."

They took their bucket and shovel and made a castle near the sea. They had fun and were happy. The sea was happy too. The sea watched them and said, "They are good friends. They are smart. They learned their lesson."

Once, there was a modest sack who was filled with colourful prints. The sack was very proud of himself, for he had all these wonderful prints. But when the time came for him to share, he was so scared. He thought if he shared the prints, he would not have enough for himself.

One morning, two young children came running to the sack. They wanted the prints to play with and make pictures. The sack was so scared and he didn't want to share. But then he thought of the pleasure that sharing his prints might bring - he could even make more prints to replace the ones he gave away.

The sack was stronger than his fear and he decided to share his prints with the two children. When the children began talking, drawing and playing with their new friend - the prints - the sack felt a warmth in his heart like he had never felt before.

The sack learned his lesson - he realised how important it was to share and love, not keep things only for yourself. Sharing something can make you feel good, and even make other people smile.

Once upon a time there was a brave girl named Susie. She wanted to do something very special and so she decided to go and ask the King for an invitation. The King was very impressed with Susie's brave spirit so he gave her an invitation to an amazing competition.

Susie was so happy to receive the invitation and she ran off to join the competition. She was a little bit scared but Susie was determined to be brave. As Susie started the competition, she realised that it was very difficult. The competition was full of challenges that she had to face.

The competitors all cheered when Susie had to face the most difficult and bitter challenge. The challenge was so hard but Susie was brave and she decided to dare it. She faced the challenge with courage and won the competition. Everyone was so proud of her and congratulated her for being so brave. 

That day, Susie learned that when you dare to do something difficult, it can be very rewarding.

Lily and Tom were friends who liked to paint. They had many colors and brushes and papers. They painted flowers and cars and animals and houses. They had fun and made pretty pictures.

One day, they saw a big iron in the room. It was shiny and had a long cord. They wondered what it was for. They wanted to try it. They thought it could make their pictures better.

"Let's paint the iron!" Lily said. "It will look nice with red and blue and yellow."

"OK!" Tom said. "But we have to be careful. It is high and heavy. We need a chair to reach it."

They got a chair and climbed on it. They took their paints and brushes and started to paint the iron. They did not know that the iron was hot. They did not see the light on the iron. They did not hear the hiss of the steam.

"Ow!" Lily cried. "The iron is hot! It burned my hand!"

"Ow!" Tom cried. "The iron is hot! It burned my brush!"

They dropped their paints and brushes and jumped off the chair. The iron fell down too. It landed on their papers and made a big fire. The fire spread to the curtains and the carpet and the sofa. The room was full of smoke and flames.

"Help!" Lily and Tom screamed. "Fire! Fire!"

They ran to the door and tried to open it. But it was locked. They banged on the door and shouted for help. But no one came. They were trapped in the room with the fire. They were scared and sorry. They wished they had not painted the iron. They wished they had listened to their mom and dad. They wished they had been good. But it was too late. The end.

Joey was walking in the park. It was a dry day, the sun was out and Joey felt happy. He saw a print on the ground. He bent down to look at it. It was a butterfly! Its wings were yellow and orange, and it looked very beautiful.

Joey wanted to take the print home to show his mommy. He tried to pick it up, but it would not yield. He put his hand in the dirt and tried to lift it up again, but it still wouldn't move.

Joey was very sad. He walked away, kicking his feet in the dust. Suddenly, he thought of an idea! He got a leaf and carefully placed it on top of the print. Then he pushed the leaf and the butterfly print flew up into the air!

Joey smiled and clapped his hands. He took the dry print and ran home to show his mommy!

Once upon a time, there was a big whale. He was very happy swimming in the ocean. One day, he met a little fish. The fish asked, "Do you have any food to supply me?" The whale replied, "I don't have any food, but I can take you to a place where you can find some."

The whale took the little fish to a beautiful orange reef. The fish was so happy to see all the food he could eat. The whale said goodbye and swam away. But as the little fish was eating, a big shark came and ate him up. The whale never saw the little fish again.

The end.

Mama and Dad took me outside to play. The sun was big and warm. We found a big pile of dirt. Dad said we were going to bury something. We dug a big hole in the dirt and put something old inside. Then Dad pushed the dirt back in the hole. He said we were burying it. 

Afterwards, we all stood up and looked at the dirt. The sun was shining on it. Mama said it was very special. I smiled and looked at the sun. It was so bright and made me happy. 

We all took a step back and then Dad said goodbye. He said that the old thing was sleep now and we wouldn't see it again. I wasn't sure what he meant, but I decided to just smile and nod. We all waved and said goodbye. 

I looked at the dirt one last time before walking away. The sun was so bright. I knew I would always remember this day and the old thing we buried.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside with her friends. One day, they decided to have a picnic. Lily's mom made a yummy meal for them to eat. They sat on a blanket and ate sandwiches and fruit.

After they finished eating, they played a game of catch. Lily threw the ball really far and her friend caught it. Suddenly, a fierce wind blew and they had to stop playing. They quickly packed up their picnic and ran inside. Lily was happy that they had a fun day outside.

Once upon a time, there was a fancy car. It was shiny and had big wheels. The car was going on a trip to a faraway place. It had a radio that played music. The driver loved to sing along.

As the car drove, it saw a big mountain in the distance. The driver knew they had to go over the mountain to arrive at their destination. The car started to climb up the mountain, but it was very steep. The driver had to be careful.

Finally, the car made it to the top of the mountain. The driver looked out and saw a beautiful view. They could see for miles and miles. The radio played a happy song, and the driver sang along. They knew they were getting closer to where they wanted to go.

Once there was a bear who liked to hang out in a zigzag forest. He loved the trees with their zigzag branches and the colorful birds that flew between them. Every day the bear went on a walk and hung upside down from the branches. 

One day, the bear noticed something different. A tidy little house had appeared. He wondered who who could be living inside it. So he waited and watched. 

As he watched, he saw a family of deer walking around the tidy little house. They were all wearing neat little outfits and looked very happy. The bear was so intrigued that he decided to hang around a little longer to see what happened. 

The bear watched as the family went inside the tidy little house. He could smell delicious food and heard a lot of laughter coming from inside. He was so happy for them, and realized he was the luckiest bear in the world to have found such a special place. 

The bear decided to hang around and visit the family every once in a while. He found that their zigzag forest was always filled with happiness, laughter and love.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to draw and color pictures with her crayons. One day, she wanted to print out a picture she drew on her mommy's computer. 

But then, Lily's mommy got very sick and had to go to the hospital. Lily was sad and scared because she loved her mommy very much. 

When they got to the hospital, Lily saw that the lights were very bright and the walls were white. But then, a nurse gave her a coloring book and some crayons to keep her busy while her mommy was getting better. 

Lily stayed at the hospital for a few days, but finally her mommy was all better and they got to go home. When they got home, Lily printed out her picture and showed it to her mommy. Her mommy was so proud of her and gave her a big hug.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her friends in the park. One day, Lily saw a little boy sitting alone on a bench. She asked him if he wanted to play with her and her friends. 

The little boy was happy and said yes. He took a step towards Lily and they all played together. They played on the swings, the slide, and even had a picnic. 

At the end of the day, Lily said to the little boy, "I'm glad we united and played together. It was so much fun!" The little boy smiled and said, "Me too, thank you for being my friend." And they all went home happy.

Once upon a time, there was a wide angel who lived in the sky. She was kind and always looked for ways to help others. One day, she saw a little girl who was crying. The angel flew down and asked her what was wrong. The little girl said that her toy was lost. So the angel decided to lend the girl one of her toys to play with. The girl was so happy and thanked the angel and soon they were playing together. The angel was glad she could lend a helping hand and the little girl had lots of fun with her new toy. They were both very happy. The end.

Once upon a time there was a dull world. Everything was the same day in and day out. No one ever laughed or smiled. The people were always sad.

One day, something exciting happened. A giant crack appeared in the sky and it started to split the world in two. All the people stopped to look up and marvel.

Suddenly everything started to change. The two halves of the world were so different. Everything in one half was so bright and colourful. The other half was still dull though. Everyone was very confused.

The people of the colourful world began to laugh and sing. They were so happy to see the dull world gone. Even the people in the dull half smiled as they watched their friends having fun.

The split world lived happily ever after. The colourful half was full of laughter and joy, and the dull half was happy just to watch.

Once upon a time, there was a big yellow dog named Sunny. Sunny loved to play outside in the sun. One day, he saw a newspaper on the ground. It was a windy day, so the newspaper was moving around.

Sunny wanted to play with the newspaper. He ran to it and put his paw on it. The newspaper did not move anymore. Sunny was happy. He picked up the newspaper in his mouth and started to shake it. The newspaper made a fun sound when he shook it.

Sunny played with the yellow newspaper all day long. He shook it, ran with it, and even hid it. When it was time to go home, Sunny took the newspaper with him. He wanted to show his family his new toy. They all played with the yellow newspaper together and had a great time.

Once upon a time, there was a little rabbit named Bun Bun. Bun Bun woke up one morning and saw the sun shining bright outside. He wanted to go play with his friends, but he was feeling very hungry. So, he went to get some carrots from the garden.

But when he got there, he saw that the carrots were very deep in the ground. He tried to pull them out, but he couldn't. "I am struggling," he said to himself.

Just then, his friend, Squirrel, came by. "What's wrong, Bun Bun?" Squirrel asked. "I can't get these carrots out of the ground," Bun Bun replied. "I will help you," Squirrel said. Together, they pulled and pulled until they finally got the carrots out. "Thank you, Squirrel," Bun Bun said. They both enjoyed a tasty snack and played together all day long.

Tom and his Mom went on an adventure. They went to a museum. Tom had never been to one before. 

When they arrived, he saw so many interesting things. Tom was amazed. He saw a big dinosaur and a big ship. It was so fun.

Tom and his Mom looked carefully around the museum. His Mom was very reliable and they explored everything carefully. Tom was so happy. 

When they were done, they knew they had a great day. He was so excited to come back!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sarah. She was three years old. She liked to sing, so every day she would go outside and sing a song.

One day, when Sarah was singing in her garden, a bow came to visit her. It had come down from the sky! It was a colourful bow, with bright purple and pink feathers.

Sarah was so excited, that she asked the bow if it wanted to join her in her singing. The bow happily agreed! 

The two of them sang and danced in Sarah's garden all day long. When it started to get dark, the bow said goodbye and flew off. 

Just then, Sarah noticed that the ground felt very icy! A cold wind had blow in and the garden looked so pretty, covered in a blanket of white. Sarah continued singing, as the icy wind night blew through her icy garden.

Once upon a time there was a very important chamber. It was full of magical things that made people very happy.

One day, a little girl came to the chamber and she wanted to explore. She opened the door and saw lots of lovely things that she wanted to touch.

Suddenly, a big dragon appeared and he said, "I don't want anyone entering my chamber!" The little girl was very scared, so she ran away.

The big dragon was very angry. He destroyed the chamber and it was gone forever.

The little girl was very sad. She cried and said, "Why would he do that? The chamber was so important." 

The dragon replied, "Sometimes even important things must be destroyed to make room for new and exciting things." 

The little girl understood what the dragon had said, and she started looking forward to discovering the new and exciting things that might come her way.

Once upon a time there was a small girl named Sophie. She wanted to find a mine to explore.

One day she went on a walk and saw a mine. She was very excited. 

Sophie entered the mine and looked around. She had a special stick in her hand. Suddenly, something sparkled in the dark. What could it be? 

Sophie struck her stick against it and the sparkles stopped. She looked closer and saw something was shining in the darkness. It was a diamond! 

Surprised, Sophie said out loud, "I found a diamond!"

Suddenly, she heard a voice. It came from a man who was hiding in the corner of the mine. He said, "Well, this diamond is mine." 

Sophie was not scared. She was thoughtful. She asked the man, "If I give the diamond to you, can I explore the mine?" 

The man thought for a moment and said, "Yes, but be careful."

Sophie thanked him and gave the diamond to the man. She explored the mine and had a great adventure. She went home with many stories to tell.

Once upon a time there was a small sunflower called Willow. Willow was so small every day she had to balance precariously on her thin stem. To make matters worse, the wind was always blowing and Willow had to work hard to stay standing.

But Willow was persistent. She held her head high, even when the wind increased in strength. Then one day something amazing happened. A group of children stopped at her field and the smallest gave her a lovely smile.

Willow couldn't believe it: she had made a friend at last.

But suddenly the wind blew even harder. Willow felt herself losing her balance. She desperately looked to her new friend for help but he had gone.

Willow felt helpless. The wind blew her over and she was never seen again. And the little sunflower never made any more friends.

Once upon a time, in a big, tall tree, there lived a little bird named Timmy. Timmy loved to fly and play with his friends. One day, Timmy saw that the leaves were changing colors. It was fall, and he wanted to celebrate with a big party.

Timmy told his friends about the party. They all got very excited. But there was one problem. Timmy's tree was so tall that some of his friends were scared to fly up there. Timmy didn't know what to do. He wanted everyone to have fun at his party.

Then, Timmy had an idea. He asked his friends to help him find a smaller tree for the party. They all looked and looked, and finally found the perfect tree. It was not too tall, and it was just right for everyone. So, they all helped to set up the party in the new tree. When the day came, all of Timmy's friends were able to join the celebration. They played games, ate yummy food, and had a lot of fun. Timmy was so happy that everyone could enjoy the fall party together.

Lily and Tom are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big bus near the park. The bus is yellow and has many windows.

"Let's go see the bus!" Tom says. He runs to the bus.

"Wait for me!" Lily says. She follows Tom.

They get to the bus. The bus is empty. The door is open.

"Can we go inside?" Lily asks.

"Sure, why not?" Tom says. He climbs up the stairs.

Lily climbs up too. They look around. They see many seats and a big wheel.

"Wow, this is fun!" Tom says. He sits on the driver's seat. He pretends to drive the bus.

"Beep beep!" He says. He honks the horn.

Lily laughs. She sits on a seat behind Tom. She pretends to be a passenger.

"Where are we going?" She asks.

"We are going to the zoo!" Tom says. He makes animal noises.

They play for a while. They feel happy and excited.

Then, they hear a voice.

"Hey, what are you doing here?" The voice says.

They look up. They see a man. The man is angry. He is the bus driver.

"Uh oh!" Tom says. He feels scared.

"Quick, hide!" Lily says. She feels scared too.

They jump off their seats. They look for a hidden place. They find a small space under a seat. They crawl under it.

They hope the man will not find them. They feel nervous and sorry. They wish they did not go inside the bus.

Tom and Lily were twins who liked to explore. One day, they found a swamp near their house. They saw frogs, snakes, and bugs in the water. They also heard strange noises and smelled bad things.

"Wow, this swamp is impressive!" Tom said. "It has so many animals and sounds!"

"Yes, it is impressive, but also scary!" Lily said. "I don't like the smell and the noises. Maybe there are monsters here!"

Tom laughed. "Don't be silly, Lily. There are no monsters in the swamp. They are only in stories. Come on, let's go closer and see what we can find!"

Tom and Lily walked towards the swamp, holding hands. They were curious and brave, but also careful. They did not want to fall in the water or get bitten by a snake.

As they got closer, they saw a big log sticking out of the water. It looked like a good place to sit and watch the swamp. Tom and Lily climbed on the log and sat down.

"Look, there is a frog!" Tom said, pointing to a green spot on a leaf.

"And there is a dragonfly!" Lily said, pointing to a blue flash in the air.

They watched the swamp for a while, enjoying the sights and sounds. They did not mention the smell or the noises anymore. They were having fun.

Suddenly, the log moved. It was not a log at all. It was a crocodile!

Tom and Lily screamed and jumped off the log. They ran back to their house as fast as they could. They did not stop until they were safe inside.

They told their mom what happened. She hugged them and said they were very lucky. She said they should never go to the swamp again. She said it was too dangerous and not a place for children.

Tom and Lily agreed. They did not want to see the crocodile again. They decided to explore somewhere else next time. Somewhere less impressive, but more friendly.

Once there was an attractive mommy who was making a steak for dinner. She cut it up into small pieces and put it on a plate.

The three year old saw the yummy steak and wanted to try it. He asked his mom if he could have some and she said yes. He was so excited that he took a bite and it was the best thing he ever tasted!

After dinner, he helped his mommy bury the steak bones in the garden. He dug very deep and pushed the bones way down so the chickens wouldn't get them.

His mommy laughed and praised him for his hard work. He felt so proud of himself and smiled as he watched his mommy fill the hole with dirt.

The next day, the three year old was able to pick some of the tasty vegetables growing in the garden!

Lily and Tom were playing with their blocks in the living room. They liked to build towers and bridges and castles. But sometimes they argued about who had more blocks or who had the better idea.

"Give me that block, Lily!" Tom said. "I need it for my bridge!"

"No, Tom, it's mine!" Lily said. "I found it first!"

They both pulled on the block and it broke in half. They were both very sad and angry.

"Look what you did, Lily!" Tom said. "You broke my block!"

"It's your fault, Tom!" Lily said. "You were too rough!"

They started to cry and shout at each other. Their mom heard them and came to the living room.

"What's going on here?" she asked. "Why are you making so much noise?"

"Tom broke my block!" Lily said.

"Lily broke my block!" Tom said.

Mom looked at the broken block and sighed. She picked up the two pieces and held them in her hands.

"Look, kids, this block is not very strong. It can't hold much weight. If you pull on it too hard, it will snap. Do you understand?" she said.

Lily and Tom nodded. They felt a little sorry for breaking the block.

"Can you fix it, Mom?" Lily asked.

"I'm afraid not, Lily. It's too broken. But you have many other blocks to play with. Why don't you share them and work together?" Mom said.

She gave them each a piece of the block as a reminder.

"OK, Mom. We'll try," Tom said.

They hugged Mom and said sorry. Then they went back to their blocks and started to build a new tower. They took turns and helped each other. They were happy again.

Mom smiled and went to the kitchen. She opened the fridge and took out a lemon. She wanted to make some lemonade for the kids. She cut the lemon and squeezed it into a pitcher. She added some water and sugar and stirred it well. She tasted it and made a face. It was too sour. She added some more sugar and tasted it again. It was better. She poured some lemonade into two cups and brought them to the living room.

"Here you go, kids. Some lemonade for you. It's very refreshing," she said.

Lily and Tom stopped playing and took the cups. They thanked Mom and drank the lemonade. They liked it. It was sweet and sour and cold.

"Yummy, Mom. Thank you!" Lily said.

"This is the best lemonade ever, Mom. You're the best!" Tom said.

They gave Mom a big kiss and a hug. They were very grateful and happy.

Mom smiled and hugged them back. She was very proud and happy. She shut the fridge and sat down with them. They drank their lemonade and played with their blocks. They had a lot of fun. They were a happy family.

Once upon a time there was a human called Lila. She lived in a big house and had many friends. 

Lila liked to take baths in the morning. She would use lots of warm water and bubbles to bathe. After, she would be all nice and clean!

One morning, Lila was taking her bath, when a rare fish appeared in her bathtub! He was an unusual color and had a beautiful tail.

The fish smiled at Lila, so she decided to keep him as a pet. She named the fish Spot and started giving him baths every day!

Spot the fish and Lila became the best of friends and enjoyed their daily baths together.

Sara and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to run, slide and swing. They also liked to look for things. Sometimes they found leaves, flowers or stones. Sometimes they found bugs, worms or snails.

"Look, Sara, I found a big snail!" Ben said, holding a brown shell in his hand. "It has a slimy body and a tiny head. Do you want to see?"

Sara nodded and came closer. She saw the snail slowly poke out its head and feelers. She thought it was cute and funny.

"Can we keep it?" she asked Ben. "We can make a home for it in a box. We can give it water and grass."

Ben was thoughtful. He liked the snail, but he also knew that snails liked to live outside. He remembered what his mom had told him.

"Snails need a lot of space and fresh air," he said. "They also need other snails to be happy. If we keep it in a box, it might get sick or sad."

Sara frowned. She did not want to make the snail sick or sad. She wanted to make it happy.

"Then what can we do?" she asked.

Ben had an idea. He looked around and saw a big tree. He saw some green leaves and some brown ones.

"Let's find a nice spot for the snail under the tree," he said. "We can make a bed of leaves for it. We can also find some friends for it. Maybe there are more snails under the leaves."

Sara smiled. She thought that was a good idea. She helped Ben find some more snails and some leaves. They made a cozy home for the snails under the tree. They watched them crawl and munch on the leaves.

"Bye, snails," they said. "Have a good day. We will come back and visit you."

They waved to the snails and ran back to the playground. They felt happy and proud. They had been thoughtful and kind to the snails. They had also learned something new. They had fun playing and finding things.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to blow bubbles with her bubble wand. One day, she tried to blow a really big bubble, but it was too heavy and kept popping. She felt sad and wanted to give up.

But then, her mommy came outside and encouraged her to keep trying. She showed Lily how to blow the bubble slowly and gently. Lily tried again and this time, the bubble floated high into the sky!

Lily was so happy and proud of herself. She thanked her mommy for encouraging her and giving her the confidence to keep trying. From that day on, Lily blew bubbles every day and became really good at it.

Once there was a big girl called Sue. She loved to skip. Every day she would go outside and play.

One day Sue was playing and saw a big, white door. She wondered what was on the other side and so she skipped up to it.

When she opened the door, Sue found a lovely garden. There were flowers and trees and she even saw a pretty bird. She skiped around the garden, smelling the flowers and playing chase with a butterfly.

Soon it was time for Sue to go home so she skiped back to the big door and went through the exit. She waved goodbye and smiled as she came out to the other side. Sue knew she would come back and visit the garden again soon.

John was a humble boy. He wanted to be successful so he made a plan. He decided the best way to succeed was to build something. So, he grabbed some bricks and started working. 

Every day, John spent hours putting one brick at a time on top of another. Soon, he had built a big tower. He was very proud of himself. 

John's success came on the day he had finished building the tower. He stepped back, looked at his tower and smiled. He had succeeded! 

John was happy. He had worked hard and achieved something with his own two hands. He was even more humble now, knowing success is something you create yourself.

Tom and Mia are friends. They like to play with blocks and dolls. One day, they are playing in the garden when Tom starts to sneeze.

"Achoo! Achoo! Achoo!" Tom sneezes loud.

"Are you sick, Tom?" Mia asks. She is worried.

"No, I am not sick. I am allergic to flowers. They make me sneeze." Tom says.

Mia looks at the flowers. They are pretty and colorful. She likes them.

"Can I pick some flowers for you, Tom? Maybe they will make you feel better." Mia says.

Tom shakes his head. He knows the truth. Flowers will make him sneeze more.

"No, thank you, Mia. Flowers are not good for me. They make my nose itch and my eyes water." Tom says.

Mia thinks for a moment. She wants to help Tom. She has an idea.

"I know what will make you feel better, Tom. A hug!" Mia says. She runs to Tom and gives him a big hug.

Tom smiles. He feels warm and happy. He stops sneezing.

"Thank you, Mia. You are a good friend. A hug is better than flowers." Tom says.

Mia smiles too. She is proud. She helped Tom.

"You are welcome, Tom. You are a good friend too. A hug is better than anything." Mia says.

They hug again. They are happy. They go back to playing with blocks and dolls.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Anna who was very happy. Every day, she would smile and play with her toys in her bedroom.

One day, Anna saw a tall cabinet with a shiny door in her bedroom. She couldn't reach it but she was very curious about what was inside of it. She tried to open it with her tiny hands but it wouldn't open.

Suddenly, Anna's mom entered the room and saw the cabinet. She smiled at Anna and said, "Let me help you!" She opened the door and inside there were lots of beautiful costumes and decorations. 

Anna's face lit up and she said, "Mommy, I'm ready to dress up!" Anna's mom smiled and they both began to dress up and play. 

When they were done, Anna smiled with joy - she was so happy and ready to show her family her new costume!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the park. One day, she saw a big green tent in the park. She ran to the tent and looked inside. There was nobody there.

Suddenly, she heard a voice behind her. "Hello, little girl!" said the voice. It was a friendly man. "Would you like to come inside the tent and play with me?" he asked.

Lily was a little scared, but the man looked kind. She nodded her head and went inside the tent. The man showed her some toys and they played together. Then, he gave her a hug and squeezed her tight. "Thank you for playing with me," he said.

Lily smiled and ran back to her mom. "Mommy, I played in a big green tent and a man squeezed me tight!" she said happily. Her mom was a little worried, but Lily explained everything and they both laughed.

Once upon a time there was a boat called Sunny. It sailed out on the ocean. One day it sailed to a new place and a new person got on board. 

The person said, "I am here to keep the ocean safe from danger." Everyone on board was happy because they thought the new person would take care of the ocean.

The new person was on the boat for a long time. He kept things away from the ocean and stopped bad things from happening.

One day he said, "I have to leave now." Everyone on board was sad. But no one could stop him from leaving.

The boat sailed back out on the ocean, but something was different. Now there was no one to keep the ocean safe anymore. The ocean was in trouble and there was no one left to help.

Once upon a time there was a corn field. It was full of tall stalks. Each one was loaded with juicy yellow corn. It was the sweetest corn ever!

One day, a careless wind blew across the field. It covered the corn with dust and dirt. The stalks were hidden and the corn was hidden too.

The farmer was very sad. He had no way to find his precious corn. He looked and looked, but it was gone.

Suddenly, a funny bird flew down. He had a big yellow corn cob in his beak! He dropped it in the farmer's hand. The farmer was so happy. 

The bird had covered the corn with its feathers to keep it safe. The farmer was so thankful! He thanked the bird and raced back to the corn field. The stalks looked happy to see him. He carefully planted the corn cob back in the earth. 

The farmer found all his corn! He was so happy! From then on he was extra careful to make sure the corn was safe.

Once there was a boy and he was very dependable. He had a big job to do. He had to number all the melons in his backyard. He was excited to start and he never gave up.

The boy counted slowly, starting with one. He worked slowly and carefully until he got to 20. He was sure all the melons were right. He took a big, deep breath and went back to the start.

He worked really hard and number all the melons, one by one. When he was done he was happy and excited. He had been dependable and he had done a great job. His mom was very proud of him.

Once, there was a big race. Many kids ran in the race. One boy, Tom, wanted to win. He wanted the victory. He saw another boy, Sam, who was very fast. Tom was jealous of Sam.

On the day of the race, Tom thought of a plan. He saw a big bag. He decided to fill it with sand. When Sam was not looking, Tom put the heavy bag on Sam's back. Sam did not know.

During the race, Sam was slow. He said, "Why am I so slow?" Tom ran fast and won the race. He was happy with his victory. But then, someone saw the heavy bag on Sam's back. They knew Tom cheated.

Everyone was mad at Tom. They gave the victory to Sam. Tom was sad and had no friends.

Once upon a time there was a nosy staff member. He worked in a store and asked a lot of questions. He was always asking people if they needed help and what they were looking for.

One day, a customer wanted to buy something and the nosy staff member asked lots of questions. The customer was getting frustrated. She wanted to be left alone.

The customer asked the nosy staff member to close the store, so she could buy something in peace. But the nosy staff member refused. He said it was against the store rules.

The customer was annoyed, so she walked away. But the nosy staff member followed her and kept asking her questions. In the end, the customer was so mad that she had to close the store herself! She was very happy when the store was finally closed and she could buy what she needed in peace.

Once upon a time, there was a harmless little frog who liked to sit on a lily pad. Every day, he would sit and look around, watching the clouds and the bees. One day, he noticed something different - the pond was getting bigger! A flood had come and filled the pond, but the little frog was not scared. He just kept sitting, as the water around him kept rising.

He watched as the other animals in the pond started swimming. The fish and ducks were having a great time, swimming and playing together. The little frog wanted to join them, but he didn't know how to swim. The water seemed too deep and he was too scared.

So, instead of swimming, he just sat there on his lily pad. He watched the fish, ducks, and other animals, and he felt happy. All the creatures were harmless and friendly, and he enjoyed the view. The little frog sat and watched the flood until all the water drained away.

Once upon a time, there was a big elephant named Ellie. Ellie had a very heavy neck because she loved to eat lots of yummy leaves. One day, Ellie was walking in the jungle when she saw a little monkey crying.

"What's wrong, little monkey?" asked Ellie.

"I lost my mommy," said the monkey, still crying.

"Don't worry, I will help you find her," said Ellie kindly.

So, Ellie and the little monkey walked together through the jungle, looking for the monkey's mommy. They searched and searched until they finally found her. The little monkey was so happy to be reunited with her mommy and she gave Ellie a big hug.

"Thank you for helping me, Ellie," said the little monkey with a smile.

"You're welcome," said Ellie, happy to have made a new friend. "Now, let's go eat some yummy leaves together!"

Anna was a very cheerful girl. She especially loved playing outside. One day, while Anna was playing in the garden, her mum came and called her inside.

Anna said, "Mum, why? I'm having so much fun!"

Mum smiled and said, "Anna, I need you to help me lift a blouse out of the cupboard. Will you come and help?"

Anna was very excited to help, so she followed her mum inside. Mum lifted the blouse from the cupboard and showed Anna.

"Now," said Mum, "Can you help me lift the blouse on my bed?"

Anna was eager to help, so she reached up and together with her mum, they lifted the blouse onto the bed.

When it was done, Anna said, "There!", feeling very proud of her work. 

Mum smiled and said, "Well done, Anna. You did a great job."

Anna was very cheerful as she gave her mum a big hug. She was so glad she had helped.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. He loved to play basketball. He had a red basketball that he played with every day. One day, Timmy's friend Billy came to play with him. Billy had a new basketball, it was blue. 

Timmy was not happy. He felt miserable because he wanted a blue basketball too. But then he remembered something his mom told him. She said that it's important to accept what you have and be happy with it. So Timmy decided to accept his red basketball and play with Billy and his blue basketball. 

They played together and had lots of fun. Timmy realized that it doesn't matter what color his basketball is, as long as he's playing with his friends. From that day on, Timmy was happy and no longer felt miserable.

Mummy was very troubled. She had a little pinch on her arm and it was hurting her. Daddy put some ointment on it and it made her feel better.

"What's that?" she asked him.

Daddy smiled and said, "That's a pinch."

Mummy asked, "Who pinched me?"

Daddy explained, "It was a bug. It hurts a lot, but it will be okay soon."

Mummy noticed that Daddy was very kind. She smiled and hugged him.

"Thank you Daddy," she said. "You're the best."

Daddy hugged her back and said, "You're welcome, sweetheart."

Mummy was very happy and the pinch was soon all gone. Daddy made everything better.

Sara and Ben were playing in the kitchen. They liked to pretend they were chefs and make yummy food. They had a big box of toys that looked like fruits and vegetables. Sara wanted to organize the toys by color. She said, "Let's put the red ones here, the green ones there, and the yellow ones over there."

Ben nodded and helped her. He picked up a toy that looked like celery. It was green and long and had leaves. He said, "Where does this go, Sara?"

Sara looked at the celery and said, "It goes with the green ones, silly. It's green, see?"

Ben said, "But it has some yellow too, look." He pointed at the leaves. "Maybe it goes with the yellow ones."

Sara shook her head and said, "No, it's mostly green. It goes with the green ones. Trust me, I know."

Ben shrugged and put the celery with the green toys. He said, "Okay, if you say so. But I think it's a little bit yellow too."

They finished organizing the toys by color. They were proud of their work. They decided to make a salad with the toys. They took a big bowl and put some lettuce, tomatoes, carrots, and celery in it. They mixed them with a spoon. They said, "Yum, yum, this looks good."

They pretended to eat the salad. They made crunching noises with their mouths. They said, "Mmm, this is delicious. We are good chefs."

They did not see that their mom was watching them from the door. She smiled and said, "You are very good chefs indeed. And very good at organizing too. I'm proud of you."

She came into the kitchen and gave them a hug. She said, "Do you want to try some real salad? I have some in the fridge."

Sara and Ben nodded and said, "Yes, please. We love salad."

Mom took out a bowl of salad from the fridge. She said, "Here you go. There's some celery in it too. Do you like celery?"

Sara and Ben looked at the real celery. It looked like the toy celery, but it was wet and crunchy. They said, "Yes, we like celery. It's green and a little bit yellow."

They took some salad and ate it. They liked the real celery too. They said, "Thank you, mom. This is yummy."

Mom said, "You're welcome, my sweeties. You know what? You have a hidden talent for cooking. Maybe you can help me make dinner tonight."

Sara and Ben smiled and said, "Yes, we can. We like to help you. We like to cook. We like to organize. We like to eat. We like everything."

They hugged mom and said, "We love you, mom."

Mom said, "I love you too, my little chefs."

One day, Billy was out for a walk. He saw a thin lip on the ground. He picked it up and was puzzled, so he asked his mom what it was. She smiled and told him it was a lip, used for singing. Billy was sad that no one wanted the lip, so he asked his mom if he could keep it. His mom said yes and asked if he wanted to learn how to use the lip.

Billy eagerly accepted his mom's offer and they started practicing. His mom showed him how to blow and make different sounds with the lip. Soon, he was making beautiful noises that he had never heard before. His mom was so proud of him!

Billy was very happy with his new lip and proudly showed it off to his friends. He accepted the compliments and noticed that even his friends were starting to get interested in playing the lip. Billy was feeling extra happy and satisfied with himself that day!

Once upon a time, there was a vehicle. He was independent, so he could go wherever he wanted.

One day, he saw a field with lots of animals. He wanted to join them, but they didn't trust him. The animals said, "You can't stay because you're a vehicle!"

The vehicle was very sad. He wanted to play games with the animals, but they didn't want him around.

The vehicle started to suffer, because he felt alone and rejected. He wanted to show them that he wasn't any different from the other animals.

Then the vehicle had an idea. He asked the other animals, "Can I racing around with you? I want to show you that I'm just like you!"

The animals agreed, so the vehicle raced around with them. Soon, the animals saw that the vehicle was just like them. They accepted him as one of their own.

The vehicle was so happy. They played games every day, and he no longer felt lonely or rejected. He was finally accepted by the other animals in the field.

Once upon a time there was a helpless little girl. She wanted to send very important mail, but she didn't know how. She wanted to make sure it reached its destination. 

The little girl looked around and saw a mailbox. She smiled and decided to take it. Taking it was tricky, so the girl asked her dad for help. He taught her how to carefully take the mailbox.
 
The little girl was so excited to use the mailbox. She put her mail inside and sent it away. She waved goodbye to her letter as it vanished into the mailbox. 

The little girl felt so proud of herself for successfully taking the mailbox and sending her mail. She knew that it would soon reach its destination. What a happy day for the helpless little girl!

Once upon a time there was a very quiet girl. Her name was Lisa. She liked playing with her dolls and playing make believe. She also liked playing with makeup. One day she decided to give her makeup to her best friend, Debby.

When Lisa gave Debby the makeup, she hugged her and said, "Thank you for this gift!"

Lisa was so happy to see the look of surprise and joy on Debby's face. Her friend valued her gift so much.

Then the two girls sat and talked together in the quiet room. The soft light from the sun shone through the window and surrounded them.

Suddenly Lisa and Debby both smiled. They both knew that their friendship was something special and something to be valued.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Jane. She was three years old, and she loved holidays. One day, she was very excited for a special holiday coming up. But, when the day arrived, she felt a bit pale.

"Why did the holiday have to delay?" she asked her mom.

"I'm sorry, sweetie," her mom said, "But it couldn't be helped. We'll just have to wait for the holiday to arrive. But the good news is, it will be here soon!"

Jane smiled at her mom, feeling a little better. After a few days, the holiday finally arrived. Jane was so happy that she could hardly contain her excitement. She spent the day with her family and friends, attending special holiday events and eating yummy food.

When the day was done, Jane felt amazing. She realized that even though the holiday had been delayed, it was all worth it in the end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved eating waffles for breakfast every day. One morning, her mommy made her waffles, but they were burnt. Lily was sad because she didn't like the taste of burnt waffles.

She said to her mommy, "Mommy, I don't like these waffles. They taste yucky."

Her mommy said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I didn't mean to burn them. Can you forgive me?"

Lily thought about it for a moment and then said, "Yes, mommy. I forgive you. Can we make new waffles together?" 

And so, they made new waffles together and they were delicious. Lily was happy again and forgave her mommy for burning the first batch of waffles.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She loved to study. One day, she found a large jar filled with green beans. She knew they were dangerous so she decided to study them very carefully.

She took out one bean and studied it close up. She also moved it around and looked at it from different angles. Next, she shook it. It made a very loud and strange noise. The girl was scared of the noise, but she continued on with studying the mysterious bean.

Finally, she knew what made the loud sound. It was filled with small pebbles. The girl was so excited to learn about this new discovery. She decided to use all the other beans to make a noisemaker.

The little girl was so happy and proud of herself for studying the dangerous beans and learning about them. She decided to use her noisemaker every day to play and have fun. The end!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He loved cars and had a red motor car that he played with every day. One day, he accidentally broke the motor car and it stopped working. Timmy was very sad because he loved his motor car so much. 

His mommy saw how sad Timmy was and decided to buy him a new motor car. She took him to the store and they picked out a shiny blue motor car. Timmy was so happy and he played with it all day long. 

But Timmy was a little bit spoiled and he wanted more and more cars. His mommy told him that he didn't need so many cars and he should be happy with the ones he had. She asked him to count the number of cars he had and he realized he had many more than he thought. From that day on, Timmy was grateful for his toys and never felt spoiled again.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to climb trees, but he was too short to reach the branches. One day, he found an axe in the shed and decided to use it to chop down a tree. 

"Timmy, what are you doing with that axe?" asked his mom. 

"I'm going to chop down a tree so I can climb it," Timmy replied politely. 

His mom explained that chopping down trees was dangerous and that he could hurt himself. She suggested that he ask his dad for help instead. 

Later that day, Timmy's dad helped him climb a tall tree in the backyard. Timmy was so happy that he thanked his dad politely. From that day on, Timmy never used the axe to chop down trees again.

Once upon a time, there was a tiny pepper plant. Its leaves were soft and green and it grew in a deep, wide pot. Every day, it was given lots of love, care and water by its very kind owner. Every night, its owner carefully checked how it was growing and was so pleased as its leaves began to get bigger and bigger.

One day, the owner went to check the pepper plant and found that one of its leaves had fallen off due to a strong gust of wind! The owner was sad and tried to fix it, but it was too late. However, the owner soon realised a valuable lesson - the pepper plant needed to be given extra care and protection from strong winds, or else it wouldn't grow very well.

So from then on, its owner put a barrier around the deep pot so the pepper plant could grow tall, strong and safe.

The moral of the story is that good care and protection are essential for anything to grow big and strong - just like the pepper plant!

Once upon a time there were two friends Sarah and Jack. They were playing in the park together. Jack found a worm on the ground and showed Sarah. Sarah was very excited and wanted to keep it. But Jack wanted to play with it. They both wanted different things, so they started to quarrel. 

The quarrel went on for a while, until someone had an idea. They decided to put the smooth worm on a table and make it into a race. Sarah and Jack both cheered each time the worm made a move. They cheered as the worm went round and round the table. 

In the end, the worm won the race and Sarah and Jack were so happy. They both gave the worm a hug, then put it safely back outside. The quarrel was over and Sarah and Jack were happy again.

Lily was sad. She did not want to go to her aunt's house. She wanted to stay home and play with her toys. She complained to her mom.

"Mom, I don't like aunt Jen. She is boring and mean. She always tells me what to do. She never lets me have fun. Can we please stay home?"

Mom shook her head. She smiled at Lily and hugged her.

"Sorry, honey, but we have to go. Aunt Jen is very helpful. She helps us when we need her. She is not boring or mean. She loves you very much. She has a surprise for you at her house. You will like it, I promise."

Lily was not convinced. She pouted and crossed her arms. She followed her mom to the car. She hoped the surprise was something good.

When they got to aunt Jen's house, Lily saw a big box in the living room. It had a bow on it. Aunt Jen smiled and waved at Lily.

"Hello, Lily! I'm so happy to see you! I have a special gift for you. Do you want to open it?"

Lily was curious. She forgot to complain. She ran to the box and tore the paper. Inside was a beautiful doll. It had long hair and a pretty dress. It looked like a princess. Lily gasped and smiled.

"Wow! Thank you, aunt Jen! She is so pretty! I love her!"

Aunt Jen hugged Lily and kissed her cheek.

"You're welcome, sweetie. I'm glad you like her. She is yours to keep. You can play with her as much as you want. I hope you have fun."

Lily was happy. She hugged her mom and aunt Jen. She thanked them for the gift. She played with her doll all day. She did not complain anymore. She learned that aunt Jen was not boring or mean. She was helpful and kind. She loved her very much.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She lived in a small village with her family. One day, her mother asked her to go to the store to buy some wheat for dinner. 

Lily went to the store and asked the lady for some wheat. The lady gave her a big bag of wheat and told her to be careful on her way back home. 

As she was walking home, Lily noticed that the sky was getting gloomy and dark. She started to feel scared and wished she was home already. Suddenly, she heard a voice behind her. 

"Hello there, little girl. Do you need some help?" It was a kind old man who offered to walk her home. Lily felt relieved and thanked the old man for his help. 

Finally, they arrived at her house and her mother was happy to see her. Lily told her mother about the kind old man who helped her on her way home from the store. Her mother was grateful and thanked the old man too. From that day on, Lily never forgot to say thank you to those who helped her.

Once upon a time, there was a little lamb. She was a humble lamb, who loved to do things at her own speed. Everywhere she went, people smiled at her because she was so gentle and kind.

But, the humble little lamb didn't feel like she belonged anywhere. She looked around, but she didn't know if she belonged to a farm or a forest. 

One day, the little lamb saw a rabbit. The rabbit had a cozy little burrow and a group of friends who accepted it. The humble little lamb was so excited - this is where she belonged!

The friends welcomed the gentle little lamb with open arms. They ran and played together, and even the rabbit went at the little lamb's slow speed. 

The little lamb was very happy. From then on, she knew she belonged with her new friends in the burrow. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She lived in a big house with her mommy and daddy. One day, her mommy told her they were going to clean the attic. Lily was very excited because she had never been up there before.

When they got to the attic, they found a big box. Inside the box, there was a letter. The letter said that Lily's family was very wealthy and they were going to receive a lot of money. Lily didn't understand what "wealthy" meant, but she knew it was something good because her mommy and daddy were very happy.

After they read the letter, they went back downstairs and had a big celebration. They danced and sang and Lily felt very happy. She didn't know what the letter said, but she knew it was something special.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She had a toy rabbit that she loved very much. One day, Lily's mom suggested that they go to a beautiful park. Lily was excited and said, "Yes, please!"

At the park, they saw lots of trees, flowers, and a big pond with ducks. Lily's mom suggested they have a picnic by the pond. They ate sandwiches and fruit, and Lily's mom suggested they play a game of catch.

After playing, they went to a lab where Lily's mom worked. It was a big room with lots of machines and tools. Lily thought it was very interesting, but also a bit scary. Her mom showed her some pretty crystals that were very beautiful. Lily was happy to have seen something new and exciting.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily went for a walk in the forest with her mom. They saw many trees and flowers. Suddenly, Lily saw a cute mushroom. She said, "Look, Mommy! I see a cute mushroom!" 

Her mom said, "Don't touch it, Lily. It might be dangerous." 

But Lily didn't listen. She picked up the mushroom and put it in her mouth. Soon, she started feeling sick. Her mom took her to the hospital, but it was too late. The mushroom was poisonous and Lily didn't make it. 

From that day on, her mom always warned her to be careful and never pick up anything she sees in the forest.

Once upon a time, there was a big bear who liked to work hard. Every day, he would go out into the forest and chop down trees, carry water and do many other jobs. But one day, after so much hard work, the bear noticed that his skin had become very dry, with patches of it peeling off. Despite doing all that work, the bear had not been drinking enough water! 

The bear was very scared and knew he needed to do something before it became too late. So he went to the river and started gulping down water from the river one by one. After drinking so much water, the bear's skin became soft, smooth and huge.

The bear was so happy and from then on, made sure to drink plenty of water everyday. Working hard is important, but it is also necessary to drink lots of water so your skin remains healthy.

Once upon a time, there was a wild bunny. The bunny was pale and had big feet. He liked to bounce all around the meadow. He would jump and hop and have lots of fun. He would go bouncing and playing from morning till night. He was so happy and carefree!

One day, he saw something shiny in the leaves. He went to take a closer look and saw a sparkly ring. The bunny picked it up in his big teeth and started to bounce away with it. 

Soon a tall woman appeared, and the bunny stopped to look at her. She told the bunny that the ring belonged to her grandchild. She said if the bunny gave it back, she would reward him with more bounces.

The bunny was happy and hopped around a few times before giving the ring back. The woman thanked the bunny and said that he could come back whenever he wanted and bounce around in the meadow.

The bunny was so happy and thanked the woman before hopping away. He enjoyed bouncing around the meadow from then on, and was always careful to keep an eye out for anything shiny!

Once upon a time, there was a green frog named Freddy. Freddy loved to hop around and catch flies for lunch. One day, he met a little girl named Lily.

"Hi, I'm Lily. What's your name?" the little girl asked Freddy.

"My name is Freddy. Nice to meet you," replied the green frog.

Lily wanted to catch Freddy and keep him as a pet, but Freddy didn't permit it. "I'm sorry, Lily. I don't want to be your pet. I like hopping around in the pond," said Freddy.

Lily understood and let Freddy go back to his pond. From that day on, they were friends and would visit each other often.

Once upon a time, there was a mama. She had a baby that she took care of. Every day, mama would feed the baby.

One day, mama met a stranger. The stranger was very boring and mama didn't want to talk to him. But the baby smiled at the stranger and he smiled back.

So mama decided to be nice and feed the stranger. She gave the stranger some food and water. The stranger was so happy and thanked mama. 

Mama fed the baby and the stranger. After they were all full, they said goodbye and mama took the baby home. 

The baby said goodbye to his new friend with a smile and mama's heart filled with love. She was happy that her baby was so kind to the stranger.

Once upon a time, there was a deep forest. In this forest lived an owl. The owl loved to tie things with its strong claws. Every day it would tie small pieces of string around trees and plants. 

One day, the owl saw a little girl walking through the forest. The owl wanted to play with her and flew down to the ground beside her. The owl showed the little girl how to tie the string around the trees and plants. 

The little girl was amazed! She tried to tie the string around one of the trees but she couldn't make it look as nice as the owl did. The owl showed her how to do it properly and gave tips to help her to make it look neat. 

The little girl was very happy and smiled when she finished tying the string around the tree. She thanked the owl for helping her and waved goodbye. The owl watched the little girl walk away with a big smile on its face. 

 from then on, the owl was always happy whenever the little girl visited the deep forest.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat yummy snacks like cookies and candy. One day, her mommy gave her a cookie that tasted very tasty. Lily ate it quickly and asked for another one.

But her mommy said, "No, Lily. You can only have one cookie a day. Too much sugar is not good for you."

Lily was sad and started to cry. Her daddy came into the room and asked her why she was crying. Lily told him that she wanted another cookie but her mommy said no. Her daddy nodded and said, "Your mommy is right, Lily. Too much sugar can make you sick. You should listen to her."

Lily stopped crying and realized that her daddy was right. She didn't want to get sick. She hugged her daddy and said thank you. From that day on, she only ate one cookie a day and was happy and healthy. The end.

Once upon a time, there were two friends named Melissa and Jack. They decided to travel together. Melissa brought a bubble wand, and made lots of big, good bubbles. Jack loved it! He jumped and laughed, trying to catch the bubbles in his hands.

They traveled around the garden, watching the bubbles drift away. Every time the bubble wand waved, more bubbles came out. Soon, the sky was full of colorful bubbles!

The two friends kept exploring, popping all the bubbles along the way. But then, something magical happened. All of a sudden, one of the bubbles started to grow bigger and bigger, until it was big enough for both Melissa and Jack to fit inside!

Once they were inside, they started to fly! Jack was so excited he couldn't stop laughing! They floated high in the sky. The sun was bright, and it felt so good!

They eventually made it back home, and Melissa and Jack were both so happy. The bubble had taken them on a wonderful adventure together. From now on, they would always remember their fun travels in the bubble!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. He loved to play with his toy plane. He wished he could be a pilot when he grew up. Tim was a bit spoiled, and he always wanted more toy planes.

One day, Tim saw a big plane in the sky. He wanted to fly just like that! So, he asked his mom for a new toy plane. His mom said, "If you are good, I will think about it." Tim was very excited and tried to be good.

The next day, Tim's mom had a surprise for him. She gave him a toy plane with a pilot inside! Tim was so happy. He played with his new toy all day. And from that day on, Tim knew that if he was good, he could get what he wanted.

Once upon a time there was a slow cage. Inside the cage was a little animal. The animal's name was George.

George was very sad because he wanted to get out of the cage. But the cage was too strong and George could not open it. He had tried many times, but it was too hard. 

Then one day, something very special happened. A friendly fairy flew into the room. She had a magical key that could open any kind of cage. 

The fairy opened up the cage and George was so happy! He could finally move around and experience the world outside. He waved goodbye to the fairy and happily ran away.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his blocks. He would build tall towers and knock them down with a big smile on his face. One day, Timmy's friend Billy came over to play. Billy brought some cool new blocks that Timmy had never seen before. They were different colors and shapes, and they made Timmy laugh when he saw them. 

Together, Timmy and Billy built the coolest tower ever. It was so tall that it almost touched the ceiling! They laughed and played with their blocks all afternoon. When it was time for Billy to go home, Timmy felt sad. But he knew that he could play with his blocks again tomorrow, and that made him happy. From that day on, Timmy and Billy were the best of friends, and they always had fun playing with their cool blocks.

Once upon a time, there was a bad man called Red. He had a stupid heart and did bad things. He wanted to deliver a bad thing to an old lady. 

The old lady was nice and she didn't want to take it. But Red was mean and he wouldn't listen. He said he must deliver it.

The old lady said, "I won't take it, it's bad". 

But Red said, "I have to deliver it. It's my job." 

Just then, a good fairy came by. She saw Red and the old lady. The fairy said, "I can deliver something for the old lady. It's a good thing, not a bad thing". 

The old lady was so happy and said, "Thank you fairy! That's so kind of you". 

Red was surprised and he was so angry. His stupid heart was full of anger. But the old lady was so happy and she had a nice thing to keep. 

The End.

Once upon a time, there was a big tiger. The tiger was nice and liked to play with his friends. One day, it started to rain. The tiger and his friends went to find a place to stay dry.

They found a big cave that was available for them to stay in. The tiger and his friends went inside the cave to stay dry. They played fun games while they waited for the rain to stop.

After a while, the rain stopped. The tiger and his friends went outside to play again. They were happy that they found a place to stay dry. They played all day long in the sun, and they had a great time.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys on the porch outside her house. One day, she accidentally knocked over a jar of marbles and they scattered all over the porch. Lily was embarrassed because her mom had just cleaned the porch that morning.

Lily tried to pick up the marbles but she couldn't find them all. She felt sad because she knew she had made a mess. Her mom saw what happened and came outside to help. Together, they picked up all the marbles and put them back in the jar.

Lily learned that accidents happen and it's okay to make mistakes. She also learned that it's important to clean up after yourself and take responsibility for your actions. From that day on, Lily was more careful when playing with her toys on the porch.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was very curious and loved to explore. One day, she went for a walk on a path in the woods. She saw a butterfly and followed it.

As she walked, she met a friendly squirrel. "Hello, little girl," said the squirrel. "Where are you going?"

"I'm following this butterfly," said Lily. "I wonder where it's going."

The squirrel warned her, "Be careful, little girl. This path can be dangerous. You never know what you might find."

Lily didn't listen to the squirrel and kept following the butterfly. Suddenly, she arrived at a dark cave. She was scared, but her curiosity got the best of her. She went inside and found a treasure chest. But as she reached for it, she heard a growling sound. It was a big, scary bear!

Lily quickly ran out of the cave, back onto the path. She was safe, but she learned a valuable lesson. From then on, she always listened to the advice of her animal friends.

One day, a little boy named Billy decided to go for an adventure in the forest. He was feeling brave and excited and couldn't wait to see what fun things he would find. He followed the trail, jumping over sticks and leaves as he went. Suddenly, the sky grew dark and gloomy. A big wind started to blow and it looked like a storm was coming. Billy started to panic and he ran down the trail as fast as he could to find his way out of the woods. He was so frightened, but he kept running until he reached the edge of the forest. He was out at last and safe! Billy had a great time exploring the woods, but he was glad he was always safe in the end.

Once there was a young girl named Sally. Sally was very competitive, and loved to play games with her friends.

One day, Sally was playing with a few of her friends in the park when she noticed a big tree. She noticed something shiny in the tree trunk, so she decided to climb it up and take a look.

When she got to the top, she saw a tiny jar with a small metal lid. She opened it and a white puff of smoke came out, and floated away.

Suddenly, Sally started to feel strange. She felt her body get smaller and smaller. She was shrinking!

"What's happening?" Sally asked.

A voice said, "You've had your wish granted! You're shrinking!"

Sally looked around and saw her friends were growing, while she was shrinking. They were now much bigger than her.

Sally was now the same size as a three year old! She was so excited, she couldn't wait to go home and show her friends.

When she arrived at home, she found that everything was much bigger than it used to be. She was now so small, it was easier to run around and play all the competitive games she loved.

It was like a dream come true!

Once upon a time there was a dark cane. It was special and it wanted to find a perfect match. It looked in the sky and down the street but could not seem to find one. So it decided to take a walk.

It went to the park and saw a lot of different things but still could not find its match. Then, it heard a happy voice! It was a three year old boy. He had a cane, too, and it shone brightly in the sunshine. The dark cane and the boyâ€™s cane looked very similar. 

The dark cane was so happy that it had finally found its match. The two canes spent the day walking and playing together. They laughed and had lots of fun.

At the end of the day, when the sun began to set, the boy said goodbye and gave his cane to the dark cane. Now, the dark cane was never lonely. It always had its perfect match by its side.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Emily. Emily had a regular job. Every day, she had to complete a task. Her parents would urge her to do it and Emily was happy to help. 

The task was something that Emily loved doing. Each morning she would wake up, have some breakfast and then head straight to the task. She always worked hard and would often be finished before lunchtime. 

Emily was so proud of her work. Whenever her parents came to check on her, they always had big smiles on their faces. They were so pleased that she completed her task on a regular basis. Emily was also proud and smiled back at them. 

After she had finished her task, Emily would always take a reward from her parents. It could be anything from a piece of candy to a book. She would always be excited to see what reward was waiting for her. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys all day long. He had a big toy box where he kept all his toys. Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside with her friends. One day, Lily and her friends decided to have a picnic. "I will prepare the sandwiches," said Lily. "And I will bring the juice," said her friend, Sarah.

Sara loved her pony, Max. She liked to brush his fur, feed him carrots, and ride him around the farm. Max was a good pony, and he always listened to Sara. He was her best friend.
