Once upon a time, there was a brown balloon. The balloon was so big and full of air that it floated up high in the sky. It looked like it wanted to go even higher!

Just then, a little bird saw the balloon. He was so tired from flying around the sky all day that he decided to rest on top of the balloon. He curled up, closed his eyes and went to sleep.

But then, the balloon started to move up higher and higher. The bird woke up and flew away as fast as he could. The balloon went higher and higher until it popped and lots of tiny pieces of brown flew down.

The little bird flew away with a smile on his face. He was very glad that he was able to rest on the balloon. And now the balloon was gone so the little bird continued his journey.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had strong arms from playing outside all day. One day, she found a pair of sunglasses on the ground. She put them on and felt very cool.

Lily decided to peek through the sunglasses and see what she could find. She walked and walked until she found a big, scary dog. The dog barked and Lily got scared. She tried to run away, but her strong arms couldn't carry her fast enough.

The dog chased Lily and she fell down. The sunglasses broke and the dog bit her. Lily cried and cried until her mommy came to help. From that day on, Lily knew to be careful and not peek at scary things.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who loved to play in the snow. She built an igloo out of big, white blocks of snow and said, "This will be my new home." 

The girl made a door and windows for her igloo and even filled the inside with cozy blankets and her favorite toys. But the igloo was missing something - snow!

The girl put on a big coat and hat, grabbed her shovel and went outside to gather more snow. She worked hard and soon the igloo increased in size. 

When the little girl went inside, it was dark and dirty. She knew she had to clean it up so she started scrubbing the walls and picking up the dirt. She sang a happy song as she worked. 

When she finished cleaning the igloo, it looked beautiful! She sat inside, admiring the walls, admiring her igloo, the home she had made with her own two hands.

Once upon a time, there was a big volcano. It was very hot and red. Many people lived near the volcano, but they were scared of it. They thought it might explode and hurt them.

One day, a kind man came to the village. He told the people that they should not be scared. He said that the volcano was not going to explode. He supported the people and made them feel better.

The man was right. The volcano did not explode. The sky was clear and blue. The people were happy and grateful to the man. They learned that it is important to support each other and not be scared of things that might not happen.

Once upon a time there was a wealthy family who lived in a big house. One night, there was a huge storm. It was so powerful it made the house shake! 

The family were scared, but the Dad was brave. He said â€œI need to close the windowsâ€. So he pushed them shut, and he pushed the door shut too. 

The storm blew and blew, but the house stayed safe and strong. The family were relieved and very happy. 

The storm passed at last and the sun shone again. The wealthy family thanked their Dad for pushing the windows and door shut, and for keeping them safe.

Once upon a time there was a tasty butterfly. It fluttered around a garden and everyone who saw it, valued it. Everyone wanted to play with it and they could, because the butterfly was very friendly. But, the butterfly had some plans. 

It flew away to get some tasty snacks. So, it searched the garden for something yummy to eat. Eventually, it found some delicious plants and ate them all up. 

The butterfly was happy with its meal and it was also very full. So, it flapped its wings and flew back to the garden. Everyone smiled when they saw it again. They all valued the butterfly and were overjoyed that it came back. The butterfly continued to flutter around the garden until the sun went down. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a busy little girl who liked to bake. She made cakes, cookies, and breads. One day, after she finished baking, she got an axe from her father. She wanted to find sticks in the forest to use for baking.

When she got to the forest, she saw many big trees. She wanted to chop a tree to get some sticks, so she tried to use the axe. It was too heavy for her to use, but she was determined.

She kept attempting to chop the tree until she finally managed to get a few sticks. She was very proud of the sticks she got and was thankful to her dad for the axe. She went home smiling, and the sticks were used to bake something special.

Ben and Lily were going to the park with Mom. They had a wagon full of toys and snacks. Ben wanted to pull the wagon, but Lily wanted to pull it too. They both grabbed the handle and pulled hard. The wagon did not move. It was stuck on a rock.

"Let go, Lily!" Ben said. "It's my turn!"

"No, it's mine!" Lily said. "You had it yesterday!"

They pulled and pulled, but the wagon did not budge. Mom came over and saw them. She was frustrated.

"Stop, Ben and Lily!" Mom said. "You are not being nice. You have to share the wagon. Why don't you unpack some toys and play with them instead?"

Ben and Lily let go of the handle. They looked at the wagon. It had a lot of toys inside. There were balls, dolls, books, and crayons. They decided to unpack some toys and play with them. They took out a ball and a doll and gave them to each other. They said sorry and hugged.

Mom smiled. She was happy. She helped them unpack some snacks and books. They sat on a blanket and ate and read. They had fun at the park. They forgot about the wagon. They learned to share.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play hide-and-seek with her friends. One day, she decided to peek behind the big tree in her yard. 

As she peeked, she saw a little bird sitting on a branch. The bird was very quiet, and Lily didn't want to scare it away. 

Lily watched the bird for a while, but then she heard her mom calling her. It was time to come inside for dinner. 

Lily was sad to leave the bird, but she knew she would come back to visit it again. She went inside and saw that her mom was busy cooking dinner. They sat down to eat together and talked about their day. Lily was happy to have such a nice family.

Once upon a time, there was a little frog named Freddy. Freddy lived in a pond with his friends. One day, they decided to go on an adventure to find an oasis. 

Freddy and his friends hopped and jumped through the forest. Suddenly, they saw an enormous oasis in front of them. They were so happy and excited to see it. 

But then, they heard a loud growl. It was a big, scary lion. The lion said, "This is my oasis. You can't come here." 

Freddy was brave and said, "Please, Mr. Lion. We just want to rest and drink some water. We will be quick and won't bother you." 

The lion thought for a moment and said, "Okay, but be quick. I'm watching you." Freddy and his friends were so relieved and grateful to the lion. They rested and drank some water, and then continued on their adventure.

Once upon a time, there was a family who loved firework displays. On the night of a big event, they decided to watch the firework show from their garden.

The little girl was especially excited for the beautiful firework display. She clapped her hands as her parents set off each one. They were all so lovely! 

The girl cheered and waved her hands as sparkles filled the night sky. She loved watching the different shapes and colours explode in the sky. It seemed like the firework show went on forever, and the little girl was so happy. 

At the end of the night, the little girl's parents gave her a big hug. They said they could not love her more than they loved watching the firework show. It was both wonderful and lovely.

John, a 3-year-old, was curious and independent. He wanted to explore the world by himself.

John was walking around in the garden when he noticed something. He saw a small hole in the ground. He had never seen it before, so he decided to take a closer look.

John then said to his mom, â€œWhatâ€™s this, Mommy?â€

His Mom replied, â€œI donâ€™t know John, why donâ€™t you search and find out?â€

John was so proud and happy that he found the coin all by himself, without help from Mommy. He was very independent and he was even more thrilled to continue his search!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a brown dog named Max. One day, Lily and Max went for a walk in the park. Lily wore her favorite brown boots.

As they walked, Max saw a squirrel and started to move towards it. "Max, come back!" Lily said. Max didn't listen and ran after the squirrel. Lily tried to catch him, but she fell down and hurt her knee. 

"Ouch! My knee hurts," Lily said. Max heard her and quickly came back. He licked her face and Lily felt better. "Thank you, Max. You're my best friend," Lily said as she hugged him. They continued their walk, with Lily holding Max's leash tightly so he wouldn't move too far away again.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to work in the garden with his dad. They would plant flowers and vegetables all day long. One day, Tim's dad told him, "If you work hard, you will get a reward."

Tim was excited and worked very hard. He watered the plants and pulled out the bad weeds. He was very tired, but he knew his reward would be worth it. He thought about what his reward might be. Maybe it would be a toy or a big ice cream cone.

One day, Tim's dad picked a big, red pepper from the garden. He said, "Tim, your reward is this spicy pepper!" Tim was confused but took a big bite of the spicy pepper. His mouth felt hot, and he ran to get a drink of water. After the spicy feeling went away, Tim laughed with his dad. They had a fun day in the garden, and Tim learned that rewards can be surprising.

Once upon a time, there was a calm little girl named Lucy. She loved to draw with her pastel crayons. One day, she decided to send a picture to her friend, Tim.

Lucy drew a big sun, a blue sky, and a green tree with her pastel crayons. She put the picture in an envelope and went to the mailbox. She put the envelope inside and closed the door.

Tim got the picture and was very happy. He looked at the calm sun and the pretty tree. He felt happy and calm too. Tim and Lucy both loved the pastel picture, and they became best friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Mia. She was three years old and very curious. One day, Mia was helping her mom in the kitchen. 

Mia asked her mom, "What are you doing?"

Her mom replied, "I'm cutting oranges so we can have some juice. Watch carefully!"

Mia watched as her mom cut the oranges into small pieces. Then Mia said, "The oranges look so juicy and sweet!"

Her mom smiled and said, "Yes, but don't forget that oranges are also a bit bitter."

Mia thought a moment, then said, "Can I help? Can I cut the oranges too?"

Her mom said, "Sure. Here, you can weigh the oranges to make sure each piece is the same size."

Mia was happy and carefully weighed each orange before cutting it. She was careful to make sure each piece was the same size. 

When Mia was done, her mom clapped and said, "Good job! The oranges are cut perfectly." 

Mia was thrilled and they both enjoyed a glass of fresh, sweet orange juice.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy who loved to play outside. One day, Timmy's mom told him it was time to come inside because it was getting dark outside. Timmy didn't want to go inside, but he knew he had to behave and listen to his mom.

Later that night, Timmy was getting ready for bed when he realized his favorite stuffed animal, Mr. Bear, was dirty. Timmy didn't want to sleep with a dirty Mr. Bear, so he asked his mom if she could wash him. But his mom said she didn't have time to wash Mr. Bear right then.

Timmy was upset and didn't want to sleep without Mr. Bear. He started to cry and his mom tried to calm him down. Finally, Timmy's mom had an idea. She gave Timmy a clean towel and told him he could wrap Mr. Bear up like a burrito and sleep with him that way. Timmy was happy with this solution and went to bed with a clean towel-wrapped Mr. Bear.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Jack who went out to the garden with his father. Jack's dad was a farmer and Jack wanted to help him.

"Look at all these tomatoes!" Jack's dad said. He pointed to a huge plant with lots of bright red tomatoes growing on it.

"Let's sell them," he said. The dad picked up the tomatoes, and Jack followed him happily.

On the way to the market they passed by a dark alley. "That's a strange place," thought Jack.

At the market, Jack watched his dad carefully sell the tomatoes. He was so proud of his dad.

When it was time to go back home, Jack gave his dad a huge hug. 
"Thank you for helping me sell the tomatoes," his dad said, with a big smile.

And from then on, Jack and his dad went to the market every week to sell their tomatoes.

Anna and Ben are playing in the garden. They see an aeroplane in the sky. It is big and white and makes a loud noise.

"Where is the aeroplane going?" Anna asks.

"I don't know. Maybe to another country," Ben says.

They watch the aeroplane until it is very small and far away.

"Let's pretend we are flying too," Anna says. She runs and spreads her arms like wings. Ben follows her.

They run and jump and laugh. They feel the wind on their faces and the sun on their backs.

They see a lemon tree near the fence. It has yellow fruits that look like balls.

"Can we pick some lemons?" Ben asks.

"OK, but be careful. They are sour," Anna says.

They pick two lemons and peel them. They take a bite and make a funny face.

"Yuck! They are very sour!" Ben says.

"They make my mouth hurt," Anna says.

They spit out the lemons and drink some water from the hose.

They look at each other and giggle.

"That was a bad idea," Anna says.

"Next time, let's pick apples. They are sweet," Ben says.

They agree and go back to playing. They forget about the sour lemons and the aeroplane. They are happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy liked to play with his toy cars and trucks all day long. One day, Timmy's mom gave him a new toy car. It was red and shiny, and Timmy loved it. 

Timmy's dad came home from work and saw Timmy playing with his new car. "That's a cool car, Timmy. Do you know what it can do?" asked Timmy's dad. "No, what can it do?" Timmy asked. "It can zoom really fast!" said Timmy's dad. 

Timmy was excited to try it out. He pushed the car and it zoomed across the floor. "Wow, it's so fast!" Timmy said. He played with it all day and discovered that it was very useful for racing his other cars. 

The next day, Timmy took his new car to the park to play with his friends. They were all amazed by how fast it could go. Timmy was proud to show off his new car and the useful things it could do.

Once upon a time, there was a flower. It was a fancy flower because it was special. Every day, it grew larger and larger. It liked to drink water and gave off a sweet smell.

One day, there was lots of waste near the flower. It had been left by some people. The flower didnâ€™t like it and tried to move the waste away, but it was too big.

The flower asked for help from the sun and the wind. Together, they moved the waste away. The flower grew bigger and bigger, and the sweet smell became stronger.

The flower was so fancy and proud of itself for sorting out the waste. It kept growing until it was the biggest it had ever been!

Once upon a time, there was a baby who wanted to pick something special. He went to a shop and saw an ancient case. He picked it up and looked inside. It was full of unbelievably shiny gems and jewels. He couldn't believe his eyes. He was so excited and he knew this case was perfect. He quickly picked it up and wrapped it up with a big red bow. He smiled and couldn't wait to show his mum and dad. He rushed home and when they saw the case they were so surprised. He was so proud and he knew this case was very special. He kept it on his shelf for all to see. Everyone was so amazed by the ancient case.

Bella was a stubborn little girl. She wanted to do everything herself.

One day she saw her dad getting the news. He was surprised. He said he had to go somewhere.

Bella wanted to go too. She put on her coat and followed him. But dad said it was too far and he was going alone.

That made Bella angry. She stamped her foot and said she would follow him, no matter what.

Dad told her to stay, but Bella wouldn't listen. She kept rising. Everywhere she went, she followed dad.

Finally, dad had to accept that she was coming too. He put his arm around her and they went together.

Once there was an ant named Tom who wanted to be successful. Every day he set off on new adventures, but no matter how hard he tried, he found it hard to succeed.

One day, Tom saw a stair leading up to a bright light. He decided to set off and follow it. He went on and on, slowly stepping up each stair until he reached the top.

At the top, he saw a big tree full of tasty treats. He was so happy! He decided to stay for a while and enjoy the treats.

But then he heard a voice. "What are you doing here?" it said.

Tom looked around, and saw a big lion standing in front of him. He was very scared.

"I'm sorry, I just wanted to be successful," he said.

The lion smiled. "That's a very noble goal. You can't become successful by just sitting around. But if you work hard and don't give up, you will be successful in the end." 

Tom thanked the lion and set off on a new journey, determined to succeed.

Sam and Lily were on a big boat with their mom and dad. They liked to look at the water and the birds and the other boats. One day, the boat stopped at a port. The port was a place where many boats came and went. There were also many people and things there.

"Can we go and see the port, mom?" Sam asked.

"Yes, but you have to stay close to us and be careful," mom said.

Sam and Lily followed their mom and dad off the boat. They saw many new and interesting things. They saw big cranes that lifted boxes and cars. They saw small boats that carried people and fish. They saw shops that sold food and toys. They saw flags and signs of different colors and shapes.

"Look, Lily, what is that?" Sam pointed at a shiny object on the ground.

Lily bent down and picked it up. It was a coin with a picture of a man and some words on it.

"Maybe it is money," Lily said.

"Let me see," Sam said. He took the coin from Lily and examined it. He looked at the picture and the words. He tried to read them, but they were too hard.

"I don't know what it says," Sam said.

"Maybe we can ask someone," Lily said.

They looked around and saw a man wearing a hat and a badge. He looked friendly and kind.

"Excuse me, sir, can you help us?" Lily asked.

The man smiled and came closer.

"Sure, what do you need?" he asked.

"We found this coin and we don't know what it is," Sam said. He showed the coin to the man.

The man looked at the coin and nodded.

"This is a great coin," he said. "It is from another country. It is very old and rare. You are very lucky to find it."

"Wow, really?" Sam and Lily said.

"Yes, really. You can keep it as a souvenir of your visit to the port. Or you can trade it for something else," the man said.

"What can we trade it for?" Sam asked.

"Well, there are many things you can choose from. You can buy some candy, or a toy, or a book, or a hat, or anything you like," the man said.

Sam and Lily looked at each other. They thought hard. They liked candy, and toys, and books, and hats. But they also liked the coin. It was shiny and special and great.

They decided to keep the coin. They thanked the man and put the coin in their pocket. They held hands and walked back to their mom and dad. They were happy and excited. They had a great day at the port.

Once upon a time, there was a small boy called Tim. He was only three years old and very curious. One day, while playing in the garden, he heard a strange sound. He looked around and saw a small cricket hopping near him.

Tim was excited and wanted to play with it, but the cricket warned him not to.

"No Tim, not today. It's too dark now," said the cricket.

He listened carefully and noticed a different rhythm coming from the cricket's wings. It was a beautiful sound and he wanted to hear more. He carefully leaned in to get nearer.

The cricket warned Tim again, but he didn't listen. Suddenly, he felt a light tap on his nose.

"Ouch!" Tim said.

The cricket looked at him gently and said, "Tim, was that fun? You must be careful or you will hurt yourself."

Tim had learned his lesson and thanked the cricket for warning him. He said goodbye and felt grateful for the wonderful rhythm of chirping wings he heard.

Jill awoke one morning with a mild feeling. She stepped outside and into the sunshine. In the corner of the garden she noticed something glistening in the sun. She kneeled down to take a closer look and was surprised to see a shell. She picked it up and ran inside to show her mom.

"Mom! Mom!" Jill yelled in excitement, "I found this in the garden!"

Her mom smiled and said, "That's a beautiful shell. Where did you find it?"

Jill replied, "I knelt down in the corner and I saw it in the sun."

Her mom was so proud of her for finding such a beautiful shell. She thanked Jill for the lovely surprise and gave her a big hug.

Jill was very happy and from that day forward she kneeled down in the garden to look for more shells. She never quite found another one like the first one, but the feeling of finding it was always mild and special.

Once there was a clever rabbit who wanted to keep a cross safe. He went around asking different animals if they could help him. He asked the cat, the dog, and the fox, but they all said no. The rabbit was disappointed, but he kept searching. Finally, the rabbit asked the owl. The owl said, "Yes! I will keep it safe." The rabbit was so happy. He hopped along, happy that his cross was in good hands. The owl kept the cross safe and the rabbit was happy. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a very stubborn dog named Max. Max was always barking and never listened to Lily. One day, Lily was playing with Max and accidentally hit her head on a rock. She started to cry and suffer from a headache. Max saw Lily was hurt and finally listened to her when she told him to go get her mom. Her mom came running and took Lily to the doctor. The doctor said that Lily had a bump on her head but she would be okay. From that day on, Max was no longer stubborn and always listened to Lily.

Billy was a very anxious 3 year old. He was scared of a lot of things and was always worried. One day, Billy and his mum went to the park. They were walking along a path with a hedge, and Billy saw something that scared him. He started crying, saying that the hedge was scaring him. 

Mum reassured him there was nothing to be scared of. She said that the hedge was just a nice big bush with lots of green leaves. She asked him to come closer and touch it. 

At first Billy was scared, but he eventually plucked up the courage to go and touch the hedge. When he did, he felt the soft leaves and laughed. He wasn't afraid of it anymore.

Mum was so proud of Billy for facing his fear, and he was proud of himself too. He had learnt that sometimes things don't always look as scary as they first seem.

Once upon a time, there was a lively little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside and run around with his friends. One day, Timmy's friend Billy came over to play. 

"Hi Timmy!" said Billy. "What do you want to do today?" 

"I want to play with my new missile toy!" said Timmy, showing Billy his new toy. 

"That looks cool!" said Billy. "Can I play with it too?" 

"Sure!" said Timmy. "Let's wrap it up in this blanket so we can pretend it's a secret weapon." 

So, Timmy and Billy wrapped up the missile toy and ran around the yard pretending to be secret agents on a mission. They had so much fun together that they didn't even notice when it started to rain. 

"Uh oh, we better go inside before we get wet!" said Timmy. 

"Good idea!" said Billy. "Let's go play inside." 

And so, Timmy and Billy spent the rest of the day playing inside, having just as much fun as they did outside. The end.

Sara and Ben were playing in the snow. They made a big snowman with a hat and a scarf. They gave him a carrot nose and two rocks for eyes. They were very happy.

But then a big dog came. He saw the snowman and ran to it. He barked and jumped. He wanted to play with the snowman. He bit the scarf and pulled it. He knocked off the hat and the nose. He made the snowman fall apart.

Sara and Ben were fearful. They ran to their house. They closed the door. They hugged each other. They cried.

"Mommy, mommy, a big dog ruined our snowman!" they said.

Mommy came and hugged them. She saw the dog outside. He was wagging his tail. He was not mean. He was just playful.

"Shh, shh, it's okay, my loves. The dog didn't know. He thought the snowman was a toy. He didn't want to hurt you. He just wanted to have fun," she said.

She opened the door and called the dog. He came and licked her hand. He was friendly. She gave him a treat. He wagged his tail more.

"See, he is a good dog. He is sorry for what he did. He wants to be your friend. Do you want to pet him?" she asked.

Sara and Ben looked at the dog. He looked at them. He was cute. They were not fearful anymore. They nodded. They went to the dog and petted him. He licked their faces. They laughed.

They were happy again.

Mommy smiled. She said, "Now, why don't you all come inside and have some hot chocolate? Then you can take a nap. You must be tired after playing in the snow."

Sara and Ben agreed. They followed Mommy inside. They drank hot chocolate. They took a nap. They dreamed of making another snowman. And of playing with the dog. They were happy.

One day, a little girl named Lily found a comb in her room. She liked the comb because it was easy to hold and made her hair look nice. Lily felt comfortable when she used the comb. She wanted to show her friend, Tom, her new comb.

Lily went to Tom's house and knocked on the door. Tom opened the door and stared at the comb in Lily's hand. "What is that?" Tom asked. "It's my new comb," Lily said. "I like it because it makes my hair look nice." Tom wanted to try the comb too, so Lily let him.

Tom used the comb, but he didn't know how to use it right. He pulled too hard and some of his hair came out. Tom started to cry. "I don't like the comb. It hurts!" he said. Lily felt bad and took the comb back. She didn't want her friend to be sad. From that day, Lily never shared her comb with anyone again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat rice for dinner every day. One day, her mom made a lovely bowl of rice with some vegetables. Lily sat down to eat, but she didn't feel like eating the vegetables.

"I don't want to eat the vegetables," Lily said.

"But they're good for you," her mom urged.

Lily didn't want to listen, but her mom kept urging her to eat the vegetables. Finally, Lily took a bite and realized they were actually delicious.

"Yum, these are really good!" Lily said with a smile.

From that day on, Lily always ate her vegetables with her lovely bowl of rice.

Once upon a time, in a mysterious land, there lived a small girl. She was always carrying a basket full of cherries. Everywhere she went she was wearing her little basket and it was always full of cherries. 

One day, the girl was walking along the edge of a large lake. She noticed something strange and mysterious in the water. It was glowing a bright pink color like a cherry. She wanted to find out what it was. 

So she put her basket of cherries down and ventured out into the lake. She was scared but also very brave. After a little while of swimming, she managed to reach the mysterious object. It was a big glowing cherry! 

The girl was so excited. She held the cherry in her hands and carried it back to shore. She put the special cherry in her basket with the other cherries and walked home. 

The girl never forgot the mysterious cherry. She kept it in her basket and it glowed every time she opened it. She was never without her basket of cherries and her mysterious glowing cherry!

Once upon a time, there was a fair ambulance. It was big and very strong. It went up and down the streets and weighed a lot.

One day, the ambulance stopped at a house. Inside was a little girl who was very sick. The ambulance weighed the girl and took her to the hospital.

At the hospital the doctor weighed the girl. He gave her medicine and then the girl felt better.

The ambulance weighed the girl again and then took her home. Through the window, the girl waved goodbye to the ambulance as it drove away. And from then on, the fair ambulance drove down the street, weighing heavy with its load of love.

Once upon a time, there was a powerful wizard named Roy. He liked to perform magic tricks. One day, Roy had an amazing idea. He decided to turn a pear into a magical creature. 

Roy grabbed a pear from his garden and started to perform special magical powers. Suddenly, the pear changed into a colorful creature with wings and a sparkly tail. The creature couldn't talk, but Roy could feel it was very happy.
 
Roy asked the magical creature, "What can I call you?"
The creature didn't say anything, just flew high up into the sky! 

Roy watched the magical creature fly with amazement. He called the creature "Pear" in remembrance of the simple pear he used to perform his magic. 

From that day forward, Roy and Pear were best friends. Roy would perform magic tricks and Pear would help him with his special powers. They had lots of fun together. 

The End.

Billy looked up at the sky and smiled. The sun was shining so brightly in the sky. He had never seen anything so pretty and he wanted to be part of it. So, Billy grabbed his diary and wrote down all the things he saw in the sky. All the beautiful birds and shapes, the bright blue color of the sky. He quickly filled up his pages in the diary.

But then he noticed something else. He saw some dark clouds in the sky. They made the sky look kind of scary and he wanted to go inside. So, he closed his diary and ran back inside his house.

But after a while, the dark clouds had gone and the sun was shining again! Billy smiled and was happy to go out and play. He picked up his diary and looked at it, the sun was shining on the pages like a bright light. He smiled and knew that everything was ok again. He couldnâ€™t wait to write some more of his special memories in his diary.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named John and he loved to play outside. One day, he and his brother saw a high box in their garden. 

John's brother said: "John, let's part this box open and see what's inside!"

John was so excited to open the box, so he quickly agreed. Together, they tried to part the box open but it was so high, they couldn't reach it. 

John's brother then said: "Let's get a chair and put it near the box. Then, we will be able to part it open!"

John smiled. They both grabbed a chair, put it near the box, and part the box open. To their surprise, inside the box was a big toy train set! John and his brother laughed and played with the train set for hours. 

John and his brother had so much fun that day!

Once upon a time, a little girl named Gilly had a ranch. The ranch was big and green, and Gilly loved it very much. 

One day, Gilly's mom gave her a special present; it was a pink ranch! Gilly was excited and proud of her new ranch, and she couldn't stop playing with it. 

At the ranch, Gilly and her mom cared for all kinds of animals, like horses, cows and sheep. Gilly even tried to give them treats, and made sure they were happy and healthy.

One day, Gilly found a wild and wounded deer at the ranch. Gilly and her mom did their best to help it, and after some time, it was healthy again and ready to go back to the wild. 

Gilly was sad to see the deer go, but she knew that the deer belonged outside. She gave the deer one last hug, before sending it away with a smile. Gilly was happy that she could help the deer, and that her pink ranch could give it a safe haven.

Once upon a time there was a little boy named Jack. Every day, he would go outside and play with his friends in the sun. One day, Jack decided to play in the mud. He jumped in and thought it was so fun! His friends laughed because Jack was covered from head to toe in thick mud.

Jack squished and giggled in the mud. He ran around and then he slipped and fell! This made his friends laugh even more. Jack laughed too; he thought it was funny too!

When he was done playing in the mud, Jack went to take a bath. He scrubbed with soap until all the mud was gone and then he was clean. Jack ran outside again and his friends laughed and Jack laughed with them. It was such a fun day!

Lily and Max are friends. They like to play with toys. They have many toys in their room. But they also like to see who has more toys. They are competitive.

One day, they decide to count their toys. Lily says, "I have more toys than you. See, I have one, two, three, four, five, six toys. You have only five toys. I win!"

Max says, "No, you don't win. You forgot to count this toy. It is mine. See, it has my name on it. Max. Now I have six toys too. We are the same."

Lily says, "No, we are not the same. That toy is not yours. It is mine. See, it has my name on it too. Lily. You wrote your name on it with a marker. That is not fair. You cheated!"

Max says, "No, I did not cheat. You gave me this toy as a gift. See, it has a bow on it. You said it was for me. You can't take it back. That is not nice!"

Lily and Max start to argue. They pull the toy from each other. They are angry and sad. They forget to have fun.

Mom hears them and comes to their room. She says, "What is going on here? Why are you fighting over a toy? You have so many toys to share and enjoy. You should be happy and kind to each other. You are friends, remember?"

Lily and Max look at Mom. They look at the toy. They look at each other. They feel sorry. They say, "We are sorry, Mom. We are sorry, friend. We don't want to fight. We want to play. Can we play together?"

Mom says, "Of course you can play together. That is what friends do. But first, you have to say sorry to the toy too. You hurt its feelings. It is a nice toy. It wants to be loved by both of you."

Lily and Max say, "We are sorry, toy. We love you. You are a nice toy. You can be with both of us. We can take turns. We can play with you and with our other toys. We can have fun."

Mom says, "That's good. I'm proud of you. Now, give each other a hug and a smile. And then, let's go to the kitchen. I have a surprise for you. I made some cookies for you. They are yummy. Do you want some?"

Lily and Max say, "Yes, please! We love cookies. Thank you, Mom. You are the best. Come on, friend. Let's go. We are hungry."

Lily and Max hug and smile. They hold the toy and their hands. They follow Mom to the kitchen. They are happy and friendly. They are not competitive anymore.

One day, a boy named Tom found a big hat in his dad's closet. It was a pirate hat, with a skull and bones on it. Tom liked the hat and put it on his head. He said, "I am a pirate now. I will sail the sea and find treasure."

Tom took his dad's coat and belt and made a pirate costume. He also took a wooden sword and a paper map. He went to the backyard and pretended it was his ship. He said, "Ahoy, mateys! Let's go to the island and dig for gold."

But Tom was a naughty pirate. He did not share his map or his sword with his sister, Lily. He said, "This is my treasure and my ship. You can't play with me. Go away, Lily." Lily was sad and angry. She said, "You are a mean pirate, Tom. You are not nice to me. I will tell mom."

Lily ran to the house and told mom what Tom did. Mom was not happy. She said, "Tom, you are in trouble. You can't take dad's things without asking. You can't be rude to your sister. You can't be a pirate. You have to be a good boy."

Mom went to the backyard and took away Tom's hat, coat, belt, sword and map. She said, "You have to say sorry to Lily and dad. You have to give back their things. You have to end your pirate game. You have to play nicely with Lily."

Tom was sad and sorry. He said, "I am sorry, mom. I am sorry, Lily. I am sorry, dad. I was a naughty pirate. I will be a good boy. I will share and be kind. I will end my pirate game. Can we play something else?"

Lily smiled and hugged Tom. She said, "It's okay, Tom. I forgive you. You can be a pirate sometimes, but you have to be a nice pirate. You have to ask and share and be polite. Can we play princess and dragon?"

Tom nodded and smiled. He said, "Okay, Lily. I will be a nice pirate. You can be a princess and I will be a dragon. We will have fun and be happy. We will play together."

Mom smiled and kissed them. She said, "That's good, Tom and Lily. I love you both. You are my sweet children. You can play princess and dragon, but be careful and don't break anything. Have fun."

Tom and Lily said, "We love you too, mom. Thank you. We will be careful and don't break anything. We will have fun."

They put on their new costumes and played princess and dragon. They had fun and were happy. They ended their pirate game and started a new one. They were nice to each other and to mom and dad. They were good children. The end.

Lily was a thin daughter who liked to dance. She danced in her room, in the garden, and in the park. She wanted to dance on a big stage, like the dancers she saw on TV.

One day, her mom said, "Lily, I have a surprise for you. We are going to see a dance show. Do you want to come?"

Lily was very happy. She put on her best dress and shoes, and hugged her mom. "Thank you, mom. You are the best!"

They went to the theater, and found their seats. Lily saw the big stage, the bright lights, and the colorful curtains. She was very excited.

The show started, and Lily watched the dancers with wide eyes. They were so graceful, so strong, so beautiful. She clapped and cheered for them.

But then, she saw something that made her sad. One of the dancers was very thin, like her. She looked tired and pale. She stumbled and fell, and the other dancers had to help her up. The audience gasped and whispered.

Lily felt sorry for the thin dancer. She wondered why she was so thin, and why she danced when she was not well. She turned to her mom, and asked, "Mom, why is that dancer so thin? Does she not eat? Does she not rest? Does she not have a mom who supports her?"

Her mom looked at the thin dancer, and sighed. She hugged Lily, and said, "I don't know, Lily. Maybe she has a problem, or maybe she wants to be thin for the dance. But you are right, she needs support. She needs someone who loves her, and cares for her, and tells her she is beautiful just the way she is. Like I do for you, Lily. You are my daughter, and I support you. No matter what you do, or how you look, I will always love you and be proud of you."

Lily smiled, and hugged her mom back. She said, "I love you too, mom. And I want to be a dancer, but not a thin dancer. I want to be a healthy dancer, and a happy dancer. And I want you to be there, to support me, and to watch me dance."

Her mom kissed her, and said, "You will be, Lily. You will be."

Once upon a time there was a girl named Lily who wanted to save the day. She had a modest shield that she thought she could use to solve the problem.

Lily went outside and found a dragon that was making a huge mess. The dragon was tearing apart buildings and creating a lot of destruction! Lily knew she had to figure out a way to solve the problem.

She held up her shield and the dragon stepped back. She used her modest shield to protect herself and all of the people who were in danger. She was so brave!

Lily used the shield to push the dragon out of the town. Everyone cheered as the dragon flew away. Lily was so happy that she was able to solve the problem and save the day. Everyone thanked her for her bravery.

Once there was a furry kangaroo. She hopped around in the sunny meadow all day. But she didn't hop alone, she was with her friends.

One day, the furry kangaroo wanted to try something new. She thought it would be fun to turn around in the meadow. So she turned, round and round she twirled. She hopped in circles around the meadow with all her friends. They even sang a song about turning.

The furry kangaroo was so proud of her turning. She showed her friends how to do it. They liked it so much and soon they were all turning around the meadow together.

The meadow was filled with laughter and singing. The furry kangaroo was so happy. She was proud that her turning had made her friends smile. They all had a wonderful time turning around the meadow.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She had a pet. It was a noisy dog. Every day the little girl wanted to make her noisy pet happy. So she worked very hard. 

She took her pet for long walks and fed her delicious food. She played with her pet in the garden. Best of all she taught her pet lots of tricks. 

When it was time for bed the pet always snuggled up beside the little girl and together they would fall asleep. 

The little girl and her pet were very happy together because they worked so hard to make each other happy. They shared lots of fun times together and were always noisy!

Once upon a time, there was a polite little turtle. Every day, the turtle would travel a different path and try to find something fun to do.

One day, the turtle stumbled upon a large shell. The shell was beautiful and looked like it might have something special inside. Thinking it was a fun find, the turtle reached into the shell and discovered something remarkable!

The shell yielded a shiny coin! The turtle was so excited and couldn't believe his luck. The turtle took the coin with him, but before he left, he thanked the shell for its gracious gift.

The small turtle was overjoyed and promised himself to never forget the polite shell. He was so proud of his gift that he went home to show his family. The turtle now cherishes the coin forever!

Once upon a time, there was a happy little girl who loved going on adventures. Yesterday, she decided to go visit a new place. She walked and walked until she found an open field. There were lots of different plants and animals there. She ran and explored the open field and was so excited. She saw butterflies and animals she had never seen before. She also found some sweet flowers that she picked and smelled. The little girl had such a fun time that she didn't want to leave. She said she wanted to visit the open field again soon.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there lived a mild cat named Kitty. Kitty loved to play with her ball and eat her food. One day, while playing outside, she saw a big dog. The dog barked and Kitty started to tremble. She was very scared.

Kitty had an idea. She ran back to her house and hid under the bed. The big dog couldn't find her there. Kitty felt safe and stopped trembling. She was happy that her idea worked.

Later, Kitty's friend, a small bird, came to visit. The bird told Kitty that the big dog was gone. Kitty came out from under the bed and started to play again. She played with her ball and her friend, the bird. They had a great time and Kitty forgot all about the big dog.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the park. One day, she saw a squirrel running up a tree. 

"Hi squirrel! What are you doing?" asked Lily.

"I'm getting some nuts for the winter," replied the squirrel.

Lily thought the squirrel was very ancient because she had never seen a squirrel before. 

"Wow, you're an ancient squirrel!" exclaimed Lily.

The squirrel giggled and said, "No, I'm not ancient, just a little older than you." 

Lily smiled and said, "Okay, have fun getting your nuts!" and ran off to play with her friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she went to the park to play. She saw a daisy and picked it up. She loved its yellow color and its soft petals. 

Suddenly, a boy came and took the daisy from her hand. "Hey, that's mine!" Lily said. But the boy ignored her and ran away. Lily felt troubled and sad. 

She went to her mom and told her what happened. "Don't worry, Lily," her mom said. "Sometimes people can be mean, but you can always find more daisies in the park. Let's go find some together." 

Lily smiled and felt happy again. She learned that even when someone ignores her or takes something away, there is always a way to feel better.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in the park with her friends. One day, Lily and her friends were playing when they saw a big, deep hole in the ground. They looked inside and saw something shiny. It was copper!

Lily's friends wanted to take the copper, but Lily knew that it was not right to steal. She told her friends that they should leave it alone. But her friends did not listen and took the copper anyway.

Lily felt sad because she knew that stealing was wrong. She went home and told her mom about what happened. Her mom was proud of her for doing the right thing and not stealing. From that day on, Lily made sure to always do what was right, even if her friends wanted to do something wrong.

Once there was a little human called Kate. She wanted to win something amazing. Every day she practised hard.

One day, Kate felt ready. She put on her special outfit and took a deep breath. She was ready to win something amazing!

Kate went to the big room where the competition was taking place. She was the only human. Everyone cheered for her.

Kate put in lots of effort and ran as fast as she could. In the end, she won! Everyone was so happy for her. She had won something amazing! 

Kate was so excited. She went home and celebrated with her family. It was a magical day!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a black cat named Midnight. One day, while playing outside, Lily saw a butterfly. "Look, Mommy! I see a butterfly!" she exclaimed. 

Her mommy said, "Yes, Lily, it's beautiful. If you catch it, I'll give you a reward." 

Lily ran after the butterfly, but it was too fast. She was sad that she couldn't catch it. Midnight saw her sad face and meowed, "Don't worry, Lily. I'll help you catch the butterfly." 

Together, Lily and Midnight caught the butterfly and brought it to her mommy. "Good job, Lily and Midnight! You caught the butterfly, so here's your reward," said her mommy, giving her a piece of candy. Lily was happy and hugged Midnight.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in the park with her friends. One day, she found a shiny jewel on the ground. She wondered where it came from.

Lily decided to show her mommy the jewel. "Look, mommy! I found a pretty jewel!" she said. Her mommy looked at it and said, "That's a very special jewel, Lily. We should keep it safe."

Lily's mommy put the jewel in a special box and locked it. Lily was sad that she couldn't see the jewel anymore. But her mommy said, "Don't worry, Lily. We will open the box again someday and you can see the jewel again." 

Years went by and Lily grew up. One day, her mommy gave her the special box. Lily opened it and saw the jewel. She remembered the day she found it and wondered how it had gotten there. She decided to keep the jewel safe, just like her mommy had done before.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Sarah. She was three years old and very curious.

One day Sarah went to her favorite store with her mom. When they got there, Sarah saw lots of new things. She wanted to try them all, but her mom said no. Sarah started to get upset and refused to leave.

The store staff noticed Sarah and wanted to help. They found a warm, soft blanket and offered it to Sarah. She instantly stopped crying and hugged the blanket. 

The store staff asked Sarah if she wanted to try any of the new toys. She shook her head and said "no". The staff smiled and said, "It's okay if you refuse. We understand." Sarah gave them a big smile and she and her mom left the store. 

Sarah was very happy. She had a warm, soft blanket and she knew the store staff really cared.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and swing on her swing set. One day, Lily's mom asked her to help with the laundry. Lily saw all the clothes piled up and felt helpless. But then, her mom showed her how to sort the clothes by color. Lily felt happy to help and soon the clothes were all sorted. After finishing, Lily went outside to swing and felt proud of herself for being a helpful girl.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Jake. Jake had an exciting idea one day. He asked his mom, "Can I go to the beach, please?" His mom smiled and said, "Yes, of course you can go." 

So Jake packed his bag and took the bus to the beach. While he was on the bus he got curious. He wanted to know what sort of things he would find on the beach. He wondered and wondered.

When Jake finally arrived, he was so excited. He saw pretty sand and lots of cheap things he could buy. He was running around and looking at everything when he heard a voice. A man had a table that was full of things for sale. He said, "Welcome to the beach, young man. What can I do for you?"

Jake smiled and said, "I'd like to buy some of those cheap things you have there." The man laughed and said, "You must have a good eye for a bargain! Go ahead, take a look around."

Jake had a great time looking at all the different items. He felt like he had made a great discovery and was happy with his purchase. When he got home, he knew he had made the right choice. He wondered what else he would find the next time he went to the beach.

Once upon a time, there was a hot jellyfish. The jellyfish wanted to be successful, so it swam and swam. But the ocean was so deep and so wide that it was hard to find the way.

But the jellyfish kept on swimming. Finally, it saw a bright light at the end of the tunnel. The jellyfish swam towards the light, and at last it succeeded.

The jellyfish was so happy. It was the happy, hot jellyfish and had succeeded in finding its way.

The jellyfish danced and splashed in the ocean far and wide. It was so happy that it succeeded and found its way.

The end.

Milly and her brother were playing in the garden. They loved to run around and explore. Suddenly, a magical fairy appeared. She was very small and sparkly. Milly and her brother were in awe. The fairy waved her wand and made Milly's brother disappear. He popped up in a faraway place. 

Milly was so worried. She didn't know how to find him. She asked the fairy if she could help. The fairy spread sparkles in the air and pointed in the direction of her brother. Milly followed the sparkles and eventually, she found her brother. He was so proud of himself for being brave enough to go on an adventure.

Milly and her brother hugged and celebrated. The fairy made sure they were safe and waved goodbye. Milly and her brother were so happy to be back together. Milly was so proud of her brother!

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play his guitar. He would strum it every day and make great music. One day, Timmy's little sister came into his room and tried to pinch his guitar strings. Timmy got mad and told her to stop. But then he showed her how to play a song and they made great music together. From that day on, Timmy and his sister played guitar together every day and had lots of fun. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird. The bird was very happy and loved to fly around. One day, the bird saw a big bird zooming in the sky. The little bird was amazed and wished to be as fast as the big bird.

The little bird decided to practice flying faster every day. After many days of practice, the little bird became very fast and could zoom through the sky just like the big bird. The little bird was very proud of itself and thought it was better than all the other birds.

One day, the little bird saw a storm coming and decided to fly through it to show off its speed. But the storm was too strong, and the little bird couldn't handle it. The little bird got lost and couldn't find its way back home. The little bird was very scared and sad. It realized that being humble was more important than being fast. The little bird wished it had never left its home.

Lily and Ben like to play in the park. They run and jump and slide and swing. They have a lot of fun. Sometimes they play pretend games. Today they pretend to be animals.

"I am a lion," says Ben. He roars and crawls on the grass. "Hear me roar!"

"I am a bird," says Lily. She flaps her arms and hops on the bench. "Hear me tweet!"

They make funny noises and faces. They make each other laugh.

But then they see a man on a bike. He wears a black robe and a white wig. He looks like a judge. He stops near them and looks at them.

"What are you doing, children?" he asks. He sounds angry.

"We are playing," says Lily.

"We are animals," says Ben.

The judge shakes his head. He does not like their game. He thinks they are silly and loud.

"You are not animals," he says. "You are children. You should act like children. You should be quiet and polite and respectful. You should not run and jump and make noise. You should sit and read and learn."

Lily and Ben do not like the judge. They think he is mean and boring. They do not want to sit and read and learn. They want to run and jump and make noise. They want to play.

They look at each other. They have an idea. They smile.

They run away from the judge. They run to the other side of the park. They run to the pond. They see some ducks. They pretend to be ducks.

"Quack, quack, quack!" they say. They splash and swim and nibble on bread. They have fun.

The judge tries to follow them. He rides his bike. But he is slow and clumsy. He falls off his bike. He gets wet and dirty. He loses his wig. He looks funny.

Lily and Ben see him. They laugh. They do not care what he says. They are happy. They are animals. They are children. They are free.

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play with their toys. They had many toys, but their favorite ones were the cars and the trains. They liked to make roads and tracks with their blocks and pretend they were driving or riding.

One day, their mom said she had to go to the factory. She worked at the factory and made clothes. She said she would be back soon and asked them to be good. She gave them a kiss and left.

Lily and Ben decided to play with their cars and trains. They made a big road and a big track in the living room. They had fun driving and riding, but soon they started to argue.

"I want to join your road with my track," Ben said. "It will be more fun."

"No, you can't," Lily said. "Your track is too big and it will mess up my road. You have to play on your own."

"But I want to play with you," Ben said. "You are being bossy."

"I am not bossy," Lily said. "You are being silly. Go away."

They both got angry and stopped talking to each other. They played on their own, but they felt sad and lonely.

After a while, their mom came back. She saw them sitting on opposite sides of the living room, with their toys scattered around.

"What's going on here?" she asked. "Why are you not playing together?"

Lily and Ben told her what happened. They both said the other one was being bossy and silly.

Mom sighed and said, "You know, you are very lucky to have each other. You are twins and you should share and join your toys. It doesn't matter if your road and your track are different. You can make them work together and have more fun. Why don't you try?"

Lily and Ben looked at each other and felt sorry. They said sorry to each other and hugged. They agreed to join their road and their track and play together. They moved their blocks and made a bridge and a tunnel. They drove and rode their cars and trains across the bridge and through the tunnel. They laughed and had fun.

Mom smiled and said, "That's better. I'm glad you are playing together. You are good twins and I love you both." She joined them and played with them too. They all had a happy time.

Once upon a time, there was a leopard named Smith. Smith liked to complain about his life all the time. Every morning, he would complain about how he didn't have money or friends. 

One day, Smith saw a fast cheetah running in the savannah. Smith was astonished at how fast the cheetah was. He started to complain to a nearby monkey. 

"This cheetah is so fast,â€ Smith said. â€œIt's not fair!â€

The monkey replied, "No one said life is fair, Smith. Maybe you should try running - it can help you feel better."

Smith thought about this and decided to give it a try. He started running every morning. With practice, he soon became faster and faster.

One day he ran so fast, he beat the cheetah. He was so proud and happy! Smith no longer complained about his life, because he was having so much fun.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved going to the park with her mom and dad. One day, they saw a big truck with a picture of a waffle on it. Lily was very curious and asked her parents what it was. They told her it was a waffle truck that sold yummy waffles.

Lily was feeling adventurous and wanted to try a waffle. So, they went to the truck and bought one. It was warm and crispy, and it tasted delicious! Lily was so happy she tried something new.

After eating their waffles, they went to play in the park. Lily loved going down the slide and swinging on the swings. She had so much fun with her mom and dad. They promised to come back to the park and try more new things together.

Once upon a time there was a printer. He was very old and cranky. He needed oil to keep going and keep printing! He looked everywhere for oil. He couldn't find any! He asked some healthy animals if they knew where he could find some. A friendly frog said he knew a way. He took the printer to a pool of healthy oil. The printer was so excited, he printed away as fast as he could. He was so happy to have oil again and he thanked the friendly frog for his help. They all danced and sang until the sun went down. The printer went home, feeling very content and happy.

Once upon a time there was a boy called Ben. He was three years old and he loved watching films.

One day, Ben asked his daddy to take him to the cinema. His daddy said yes and they set off in the car.

As they were driving Ben was so excited. The road was smooth, and the car drove really fast. He waved out of the car window, and saw lots of different animals.

Finally, Ben and his daddy arrived at the cinema. Ben was amazed - there were so many people and all the colours were so bright. He couldn't wait to watch the film!

Ben's daddy got the tickets and they went inside. They found their seats and soon the film started. Ben was mesmerized - he watched from start to finish and didn't move a muscle.

When the film finished, Ben was so happy he had been able to watch his favourite movie. He gave his daddy a big hug, and thanked him for the wonderful day.

Once upon a time, there were two friends, Lucy and Jack. They liked to talk to each other all the time. One day, Lucy had a surprise for Jack. She gave him a card.

Jack was so happy! He hugged Lucy and said thank you. On the card there was a special message from Lucy. It said, "Let's talk every day!"

The friends talked a lot every day after that. They talked about regular things like sports, school, and spending time with their families. They also talked about their dreams and what they wanted to do when they grew up.

At the end of the day, Jack and Lucy were very happy! They knew that they would always be friends and talk to each other every day. Just like the card said.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to go on adventures with her stuffed animal, Teddy. One day, Lily and Teddy decided to go on a trip to the beach. 

They packed their bags and went to the hotel. The lady at the front desk said, "We have a room available for you." Lily was happy and said, "Yay! We get to stay here!" 

After they settled in, Lily and Teddy went to the beach. They built sandcastles and played in the water. Suddenly, it started to rain. Lily said, "Oh no! What's happening?" 

Teddy said, "Don't worry, Lily. We can go back to the hotel and play games." So, they went back to the hotel and played games until the rain stopped. Lily and Teddy had a fun adventure at the beach and at the hotel.

One day, Tommy was walking around his house feeling a little worried. His mom had left the room and she said she would be back soon, but Tommy wasn't sure what that meant. He kept walking, looking around and feeling a little bit silly. Finally, he saw his mom was in the kitchen, making his favorite snack: ice cream. Tommy felt happy and all his worries vanished. He laughed at how silly he was to walk around and worry so much. Mom had been right, it was nothing to worry about!

Ben was a cat who liked to play with his tail. He would chase it, bite it, and swing it around. He thought his tail was the best toy ever. But one day, he saw something new in the garden. It was a big, fluffy, white dog.

The dog ran up to Ben and said, "Hello, cat. Do you want to play with me?"

Ben was scared of the dog. He did not like his loud bark and his big teeth. He hid behind a bush and said, "No, thank you. I have my tail to play with."

The dog was sad. He wanted to make a new friend. He said, "But your tail is not fun. It is just a part of you. You cannot join it or throw it or fetch it. Come and play with me. I have a ball and a stick and a bone. They are much more fun than your tail."

Ben was curious. He peeked out from the bush and saw the dog's toys. They looked interesting and colorful. He wondered what they felt like and how they moved. He said, "Maybe I can try your toys for a little while. But I still like my tail the best."

The dog was happy. He said, "Sure, cat. Come and join me. We can share my toys and have fun together. Maybe you will like them as much as I do."

Ben came out from the bush and followed the dog to his toys. He was a little nervous, but also excited. He tried the ball and the stick and the bone. He found out that they were fun to join and throw and fetch. He also found out that the dog was not so bad. He was friendly and playful and gentle. He said, "Thank you, dog. You have nice toys and you are a good friend. I still like my tail, but I also like you and your toys."

The dog was glad. He said, "You are welcome, cat. You are a good friend too. I still like my toys, but I also like you and your tail. We can play with both of them."

Ben and the dog became friends. They played with their toys and their tails. They had fun and learned new things. They were not troubled anymore. They were happy.

Tom and Lily are playing with their toys in the living room. They have many figures of animals, cars, and people. They like to make stories with them and pretend they are in different places.

"Look, this is a lion and this is a zebra. The lion is hungry and wants to eat the zebra. What will the zebra do?" Tom asks Lily, holding the figures in his hands.

Lily thinks for a moment. She does not want the zebra to be eaten. She looks around and sees a distant window. She has an idea.

"Maybe the zebra can run to the window and jump out. Then the lion cannot catch him. He can find a new home with other zebras," she says, moving the zebra figure towards the window.

Tom nods. He likes Lily's idea. He moves the lion figure after the zebra, but he makes it slower and tired.

"The lion is too slow and too tired. He cannot run to the window. He gives up and looks for another food. The zebra is safe and happy," he says, making the lion figure lie down and the zebra figure jump out of the window.

Tom and Lily smile. They have solved the problem of the lion and the zebra. They hug each other and look for another story to play.

Once upon a time there was a man with a big, bushy mustache. He was very friendly and always smiled a lot.

One day a little girl asked him why he had such a big mustache. The man smiled and replied, "It helps me stay healthy."

The little girl wasn't sure what the man meant, so she asked again. The man explained, "Eating lots of vegetables and keeping active helps me stay fit and healthy."

The little girl smiled and said, "That's so cool! I wish I had a mustache too."

The man replied with a hearty laugh, "No, a mustache isn't necessary for staying healthy. Eating your vegetables and playing outside are all you need." 

The little girl smiled and nodded in agreement. She was very relieved because she wasn't sure if having a mustache was a requirement for having a healthy body.

Once upon a time, there was a distant peach tree. Every day, the tree said "hello" to the sun and the sky. One day, a bird landed on the peach tree and said "hello". The peach tree was so happy it gave the bird a big peach. The bird said thank you and flew away. 

The peach tree was now sad. It said goodbye to the sun and the sky and wished they could be together longer. The sun smiled and said "I will come back soon".

Before long, the sun was back. And this time, it was joined by an ant. The ant said "hello" to the peach tree and the peach tree said "hello" back. The ant asked the peach tree for a peach, and the peach tree gave one. 

The ant thanked the peach tree and took away the peach. The peach tree said goodbye, but it knew the sun and the ant would always come back. It was happy to know that it had friends that were distant, but still very close.

Little Billy was sitting on the grass in the park. He was looking at all the other kids playing and having fun. He wanted to join, but he didn't know how. Suddenly, he noticed one tall kid walking away from all the other kids. Billy ran over, wanting to ask him about how to join. The tall kid stopped and looked around. He saw Billy, and he shrugged.

Billy had an idea. He asked the tall kid if he could help him learn how to do something special like the other kids were doing. The tall kid smiled and said yes. He showed Billy how to do the buckle. He taught Billy to be careful and take his time while doing it.

When Billy was finished, the tall kid cheered and hugged him. All the other kids in the park saw and ran over to join in the hug. From then on, Billy was part of the group and learned lots of new things. Every time he saw the tall kid, they would both shrug as if they were saying "Look what we can do!"

One morning, the sun peeked through the window and shone in Little John's bedroom. John woke up with a big yawn and he was so excited for the day.

John's mom said, "Let's go outside, honey!" 

"I want to go look for deer!" said John.

John and his mom went outside and saw a filthy deer right beside the tree. John smiled and exclaimed, "Look, mommy. A deer!"

John and his mom watched the deer as it pranced around. After awhile, the deer ran off and disappeared into the woods. 

John hugged his mom and said, "That was fun, mommy. Can we come see the deer again someday?" 

John's mom smiled and said, "Sure we can, honey. Let's get back inside now and wash up for breakfast."

John and his mom went back inside and washed their hands. Then, they had a delicious hot breakfast and started a new day together.

Once upon a time, there was a little lamb. Its name was Jilly and it loved playing in the mud. Every day, Jilly would jump and skip around and make the most perfect mud pies. 

One day, Jilly was in the middle of making the perfect mud pie when suddenly, it saw its Mum coming. Its Mum said, "Jilly! What are you doing? You need to remove that mud!" Jilly said, "But, Mum! I'm having such fun. My mud pies are perfect!"

Mum replied, "I'm sorry, Jilly, but you must remove that mud. You're getting too muddy and I won't have it." Jilly looked sadly at her mud pie and slowly began to remove all the mud and put it back in the ground. 

But all was not lost! Jilly soon found a much better way to have fun. She and her Mum laughed and ran through the meadows, enjoying the warm sunshine and fresh air. It was just the perfect way to have fun!

Jack and his mom went shopping together. They were looking for a special treat. Suddenly, Jack saw a big jar of candy. He yelled out and asked his mom if he could buy it. His mom mentioned to him that he could have one of the treats in the jar, but if he took any extra treats she would be very disappointed. Jack was a bit confused but promised to obey his mom.

Jack was ecstatic when he finally got his treat. He thanked his mom and put the sweet candy in his pocket. He couldn't wait to get home and savor it. As he walked along, Jack was very excited and kept mentioning to his mom how he couldn't wait to enjoy his special treat. His mom was happy that Jack was so thrilled by the treat and smiled as she watched him run ahead.

Once upon a time there was a family who were travelling to a new place. The mother had two kids, a 3 year old who loved to read and an older brother who was always playing. 

One morning, the family loaded their luggage into the car and got ready to go. As the car drove away, the 3 year old picked up a book and started to read. His brother, who wasn't interested in books, complained that the ride was boring.

When the family arrived at the new place, the 3 year old was the only one who was prepared. The other people around him were busy trying to get their luggage out of their car. The 3 year old was already finished reading his book and he had been carrying his luggage all along. 

The family watched in amazement, the 3 year old had been prepared because of his love of reading. His brother, on the other hand, was struggling with an ugly, heavy suitcase.

The moral of this story is that being prepared pays off. Through reading, the 3 year old was able to foresee the journey and be ready for it. It is important to always be prepared and reading can help us do just that!

Once upon a time, there was a little baby named Tim. Tim had a pretty crib in his room. It was the perfect size for him. He loved to sleep and play in his crib. One day, Tim's mommy came into his room.

"Tim, I have a surprise for you," said Mommy. Tim looked up and saw a big box. He was very excited to receive a surprise.

Mommy opened the box and took out a soft, fluffy bear. "This is for you, Tim," she said. Tim smiled and hugged the bear. He loved his new friend.

Tim and the bear played all day. They had so much fun together. At night, Tim took the bear to his perfect crib. They slept side by side, happy and cozy.

From that day on, Tim and the bear were always together. They played, laughed, and slept in the perfect crib. Tim and the bear were the best of friends, and Tim knew he was very loved.

Once upon a time, there was an incredible lion. He was so big and brave! Every day he used to roam around the jungle looking for adventure. One day he came upon a lake and saw something incredible. There in the lake was a family of hippos! He watched them for a while and thought that it was the best thing he had ever seen.

The lion courageously walked closer to the lake. The hippos saw him and started to make noises. But, instead of being scared, the lion showed them how brave he was by roaring back! The hippos were so amazed that they wanted to be friends.

The lion and the hippos started to play together. They raced around the lake and splashed in the water. They were having so much fun!

At the end of the day, the lion said goodbye to his new friends and went on his way. He felt so happy inside because he had made some incredible, new friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved playing with her toy sheep. One day, Lily's friend Emma came to play with her. They played together for a while, but then Emma wanted to go home. 

Lily said, "Wait! Let's fold our sheep and put them away first." 

Emma said, "I can't. I'm deaf and can't hear you." 

Lily felt sad for Emma and wanted to help her. She thought for a moment and said, "I have an idea! Let's use our hands to show each other what we mean." 

So Lily showed Emma how to fold the sheep and put them away. Emma smiled and said, "Thank you, Lily. You're a good friend." 

From that day on, Lily and Emma used their hands to communicate and became even closer friends. The moral of the story is that even if someone is different from us, we can still find ways to understand and help each other.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tom. Tom wanted to go on an adventure, so he jumped onto his bike and pedalled away. On the way, he saw a big door with a lock on it. He stopped and said, â€œI want to see whatâ€™s on the other side of that door.â€

Tom got off his bike and went to the door. He tried to turn the lock, but it wouldnâ€™t open. Then he saw a key, lying on the ground next to the door. Tom picked it up and tried to turn it in the lock, but it was broken.

Tom looked around and noticed a rock nearby. He grabbed the rock and started to rub it against the broken lock. Suddenly, the lock clicked and the door opened. Tom felt so excited and he couldnâ€™t wait to find out what was behind the door.

Tom stepped inside and it was full of toys and games. He shouted with joy, â€œThis is the best adventure ever!â€

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to drink milk from her pink cup every day. One day, her mom forgot to buy milk from the store. Lily started to cry because she loved milk so much. Her mom felt humble and said sorry to Lily.

Lily suffered without milk for a few days until her mom went to the store and bought more. When Lily saw the milk, she was so happy and drank it all up. She hugged her mom and said thank you. From that day on, her mom never forgot to buy milk again.

Once upon a time there was a happy boy. Every day he liked to play outside in his comfortable house. One day, the boy decided he wanted to win something! He asked his mom what he could win and she said he should go outside and play games with his friends. So, the boy went outside and played all sorts of games with his friends. He ran races, played tag and more. After a while, he started to win every game! His friends were so happy for him. In the end, the boy won so many games that he felt like a champion. He had lots of fun and felt very comfortable in his own skin. The boy had won and he was proud!

Ben is a big dog who lives with his family. He loves to play, eat and sleep. He is a spoiled dog, because his family gives him many things. They provide him with food, water, toys and a soft bed. Ben is happy and grateful.

One day, Ben's family goes out for a long time. They tell him to be a good dog and stay at home. They leave him a big bone to chew on. Ben is excited and runs to the bone. He bites it and makes loud noises. He thinks it is the best bone ever.

But then, he hears a knock on the door. He stops chewing and goes to see who it is. He sees a small dog outside. The small dog is dirty and thin. He looks sad and hungry. He says to Ben, "Hello, can I have some of your bone? I have not eaten for a long time."

Ben feels sorry for the small dog, but he also likes his bone very much. He does not want to share it. He says to the small dog, "No, this is my bone. Go away and find your own bone." He growls and shows his teeth.

The small dog is scared and sad. He says to Ben, "Please, just a little bit. I am very hungry and cold. You have so much and I have nothing." He begs and whines.

Ben thinks for a moment. He remembers how his family provides him with many things. He remembers how they love him and care for him. He realizes that he is a spoiled dog, and that the small dog needs his help. He feels ashamed and sorry. He says to the small dog, "I am sorry, I was mean to you. You can have some of my bone. Come in and warm up. Maybe we can be friends."

The small dog is happy and grateful. He says to Ben, "Thank you, you are very kind and generous. You are a good dog." He comes in and shares the bone with Ben. They chew and talk and play. They become friends.

Ben learns a lesson. He learns that sharing is better than being selfish. He learns that being spoiled is not good. He learns that being kind and helpful is good. He is happy and grateful.

Once upon a time, there was a birdcage. It was very tall and had a scary face on it. Every day, the birdcage would open and a bird would come out to flutter high in the sky.

One day, the birdcage closed. It wouldn't open. The bird was very scared and kept jumping up and down. With a loud noise, the birdcage opened again and the bird flew away. It was happy to be free.

But then the birdcage closed again. And this time it stayed closed. The bird was so scared and kept banging the birdcage with its beak. But the birdcage was too strong and the bird was too weak. The bird stayed inside for days and days, until finally the birdcage opened again.

The bird flew across the sky, never wanting to get close to a birdcage again. It was so happy to be free and to soar high in the sky.

Tom and Mia are playing in the park. They like to pretend they are superheroes. Tom has a stick. He says it is his weapon. Mia has a scarf. She says it is her cape.

"Look, I can fly!" Mia says. She runs and jumps with her scarf. Tom follows her. He swings his stick. He says he is fighting bad guys.

"Be careful, Tom!" Mia says. "Don't hit anyone with your weapon. You have to behave."

"I know, I know," Tom says. "But I have to save the world!"

They see a big dog. The dog is barking. It has a collar and a leash. But no one is holding the leash. The dog is loose.

"Uh-oh," Mia says. "That dog is scary. Maybe it is a bad guy."

"Or maybe it is a friend," Tom says. "Let's go and see."

They walk towards the dog. The dog sees them. It stops barking. It wags its tail. It looks happy.

"Hi, doggy," Mia says. She holds out her hand. The dog sniffs it. Then it licks it.

"See, it is a friend," Tom says. He puts down his stick. He pets the dog.

The dog likes them. It follows them. They play together.

A man comes. He is looking for the dog. He sees the leash on the ground. He sees the kids and the dog.

"Hey, there you are!" he says. He picks up the leash. He thanks the kids. He says they are very nice.

"You have a good dog," Mia says.

"He is a good dog, but he sometimes runs away," the man says. "He likes to explore. But he can be dangerous. He could get hurt or hurt someone else. He has to behave."

He puts the leash on the dog. He says goodbye to the kids. He walks away with the dog.

The kids wave to the dog. They are sad. They liked the dog.

"Maybe we can see him again," Tom says.

"Maybe," Mia says. "But we have to be careful. He is not our dog. He has an owner. And he has to behave."

They go back to their game. They pick up their weapon and their cape. They are superheroes again. They have fun. They behave.

Once there was a little girl called Spike. She loved exploring the world and she was always so happy. She looked around everywhere to see all of the special things.
