One day, Timmy and his daddy went to the park to play. They brought a special game that Timmy's daddy had made. It was a surprise for Timmy. Daddy told Timmy that they were going to play a game where they had to open a special box. Timmy was very excited to play.

Daddy and Timmy started playing the game. Daddy was very competitive and tried his best to open the box before Timmy. But Timmy was very clever and opened the box first! Inside the box was a special prize for Timmy. Daddy was very happy for Timmy and they both laughed and played together for the rest of the day. Timmy learned that sometimes it's not about winning, but about having fun with your daddy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. She was only three years old but she was very brave. One day, Lucy went for a walk in the woods. 

As she was walking, something hot brushed against her arm and Lucy jumped! It was a giant herb! The herb was so big, it scared her.

Lucy was about to run away but then she heard a sweet voice. The herb said, â€œDonâ€™t be scared. I wonâ€™t hurt you.â€

Lucy felt a bit better. She asked the herb, â€œWhat do you do?â€ The herb replied, â€œI make the woods smell nice!â€ Lucy smiled and thanked the herb. They said goodbye, and Lucy continued her walk.

The end!

Once upon a time, a little girl named Lily went on a picnic with her mommy and daddy. They ate sandwiches, fruit, and cookies. Suddenly, Lily spilled her juice on her dress. She felt ashamed and started to cry.

Her mommy said, "Don't cry, Lily. We can go to the store and buy you a new dress." 

Lily stopped crying and smiled. After they finished their picnic, they went to the store and found a pretty new dress. Lily was so happy and thanked her mommy and daddy. 

"I love picnics," Lily said. "Me too," said her mommy. "It's always fun to spend time with our family."

Once upon a time, there was a pretty kitty who lived with its mommy in a nice home. The kitty was always so careful, but one day it noticed something strange. A thief had snuck into their home while they were sleeping. The kitty grazed the furry creature and soon realized it was not its mommy.

The thief was scared, so it quickly ran away. The kitty jumped up and chased after it. The thief could not get away fast enough, but it was still able to make it far away. Mommy came out of the house and saw the kitty gone. She called for her, but the kitty was too far away and couldn't hear.

Mommy searched the entire neighborhood, but she couldn't recognize the thief or the kitty. She started to get scared and soon worried that the thief had taken away her pretty kitty. After much searching, she sadly went home without the kitty. The kitty never returned home and was never seen again.

Alice was a three year old girl who liked to explore the world. One day she asked her mom if she could go out and explore. Her mom said she could, but only if she took Mommy's friend Lucia with her.

Alice and Lucia went for a walk in the park. While they walked, Alice saw a lot of interesting things. Suddenly, Lucia stopped and listened. "What is it?" asked Alice. Lucia grinned and said, "It's jazz!" Lucia offered to teach Alice to dance to the jazz.

Alice soon was twirling and skipping with Lucia. She felt confused by the moves but still had fun. They danced faster and faster until Lucia said they should take a break. Alice was exhausted, but said she wanted to keep going. Lucia smiled and offered Alice a snack and a drink. After they ate and drank, Alice went back to dancing with Lucia.

Alice had so much fun dancing with Lucia. She was no longer confused by the moves, but instead pirouetted and jumped with ease. Alice was sad when it was time to go home, but she promised herself to keep dancing.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big tent. It has many colors and pictures. They hear music and voices. They want to go inside.

"Come on, Lily, let's see what's in there!" Ben says. He holds Lily's hand and runs to the tent.

"Wait, Ben, maybe we need a ticket," Lily says. She is a little scared. She sees a man at the door. He wears a funny hat and a red coat. He smiles at them.

"Hello, little ones, do you want to see the show?" he asks. He has a ticket in his hand.

"What show?" Ben asks. He is curious.

"The show of wonders, of course! You will see wild animals, brave acrobats, and magic tricks. It's the best show in town!" the man says. He gives them the ticket.

"Wow, that sounds fun!" Ben says. He pulls Lily to the door.

"Thank you, mister," Lily says. She is polite.

"You're welcome, enjoy the show!" the man says. He opens the door for them.

Lily and Ben enter the tent. They see a big ring with lights and seats. They find a place to sit. They are excited. They can't wait to see the show of wonders. They clap their hands and cheer. They have a great time.

The sun was shining, and the birds were singing in the trees.
Nina loved exploring the world around her. Today she decided to explore the kitchen.

When she arrived, her father was in the kitchen preparing an impressive pastry. He used flour, sugar and butter to create the treat. Nina wanted to help, but everything seemed so big for her tiny hands.

Her father smiled and said, "You can't use the oven now, but you can use your imagination. That is no less valuable." 

Nina began thinking of all the things she could imagine. Her mind was bustling with ideas. Pretty soon, she created an even more impressive pastry with her thoughts.

This experience taught Nina that even though she may not be able to do things now, it doesn't mean she can't use her imagination. It can help her create something truly amazing!

Once there was a little boy named Jimmy. He was very obedient and always listened to his parents. One day, Jimmyâ€™s parents gave him a special medal. It was shiny and made of gold. Jimmy was so excited about his medal that he couldnâ€™t sit stillâ€”he wanted to show it to everyone. 

Jimmy's mom noticed how excited he was and suggested that he show off his medal to his grandparents and cousins. So, Jimmy hopped into his parentsâ€™ car and they drove to his grandparents' house. 

When Jimmy arrived, he proudly showed off his medal to everyone. Grandma and Grandpa were so happy to see their obedient grandson and gave him a hug. His cousins were very impressed and wanted to try the medal on. Jimmy happily showed them how to put it on and they all dressed up like they had won the medal, too. 

At the end of the visit, Jimmy gave his cousins a hug and they said goodbye. Jimmy was so excited to show off his medal, but he was tired, too. So, his parents helped him into his seat and Jimmy happily fell asleep on the way home.

Ben and Sam are brothers. They share a room and a bed. Ben is older and has hair. Sam is younger and bald. Sam likes to play with Ben's hair and pull it. Ben does not like that. He tells Sam to stop, but Sam does not listen.

One night, Ben has an idea. He covers his head with a hat. He hopes Sam will not see his hair and leave him alone. He goes to sleep. Sam sees the hat and wonders what is under it. He is curious. He tries to take off the hat, but Ben holds it tight. Sam pulls harder and harder. Ben wakes up and yells.

"Sam, stop it! You are hurting me! Why do you always bother me?"

Sam says, "I want to see your hair. I like your hair. I wish I had hair like you."

Ben feels sorry for Sam. He realizes Sam is not mean, just lonely. He takes off his hat and shows Sam his hair. He says, "You can touch my hair, but gently. Do not pull it. It is not nice to hurt others. And you do not need hair to be happy. You are my brother and I love you. You are special the way you are."

Sam smiles and hugs Ben. He says, "Thank you, Ben. I love you too. You are a good brother. I am sorry for pulling your hair. I will be nice to you."

They cuddle and fall asleep. They are happy. They learn to respect and care for each other.

Lily loves to play with her red guitar. She likes to sing and strum the strings. She pretends she is a rock star on a big stage. She has a lot of fun with her guitar.

One day, she hears a knock on the door. She wonders who it is. She puts down her guitar and runs to the door. She peeks through the hole. She sees her friend Ben. He has a big smile on his face.

"Hi, Lily!" Ben says. "Can I come in and play with you?"

"Sure, Ben!" Lily says. "Come in, come in!"

Lily shows Ben her red guitar. She asks him if he wants to try it. Ben nods. He picks up the guitar and holds it. He tries to strum the strings, but he makes a loud noise.

"Oops!" Ben says. "I don't know how to play the guitar. Can you teach me, Lily?"

"Of course, Ben!" Lily says. "It's easy and fun. Just follow me."

Lily and Ben sit on the floor. Lily shows Ben how to hold the guitar and how to move his fingers. She sings a simple song and Ben joins her. They laugh and clap. They have a lot of fun with the red guitar.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to go on walks with her mom and dad. One day, they decided to go on a hike in the mountains. They packed snacks and water and started their journey. 

As they were walking, Lily noticed a man jogging towards them. He seemed very happy and full of energy. "Hello!" he said. "What a beautiful landscape we have here!" 

Lily's dad smiled and replied, "Yes, it's amazing. We love coming here." 

Suddenly, they heard a loud noise. It sounded like a tree falling. They looked up and saw a big rock rolling down the mountain. They quickly realized it was heading their way. They all started to run, but Lily's mom tripped and fell. 

The man who was jogging quickly ran towards them and helped Lily's mom get up. They all made it to safety, but they were very scared. "Thank you so much for helping us," said Lily's dad. "You saved us from being dead." 

The man smiled and said, "No problem. I'm just glad everyone is okay." From that day on, Lily and her family always remembered to be careful when they went on hikes in the mountains.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Max and Sally. They were very happy together, but wanted to do some things by themselves. So they decided it was time to be independent.

Max and Sally soon found a special trap. It had a big red button and they knew they could use it to separate. So they pushed the button and it made a loud *click!* noise.

Max and Sally were now on their own. They could explore by themselves, make different choices and learn new things. But no matter what, they were still friends and would always stay close in their hearts.

They could still have fun together when they wanted, but also be independent and explore the world on their own. Max and Sally were so happy that the trap could help them be independent. And they lived happily ever after!

Timmy was walking through the park on a dull day. He saw a bird up in a tree and he smiled.

"Hello bird!" he said. But the bird was asleep, and Timmy's voice disturbed it.

The bird opened its eyes and squawked. "Who are you?" it said. 

"I'm Timmy!" he said. "What are you doing up in the tree?"

"I'm resting," said the bird. "The days have been long and tiring, so I'm taking a nap." 

Timmy smiled. "I understand," he said. "I guess we both need some rest on a dull day." He waved goodbye, and ran off to play.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily was holding her calendar and she accidentally dropped it on the floor. Her mommy heard the sound and asked, "What happened, Lily?" 

"I dropped my calendar," Lily said. 

Her mommy picked up the calendar and saw that it was cold outside. "It's a cold day today, Lily. We should wear our warm coats when we go outside," her mommy said. 

Lily nodded and put on her coat. They went outside and had a fun day playing in the snow. When they came back inside, they had some hot cocoa to warm up. Lily looked at her calendar and smiled. It was a great day! The end.

Carl and his mom were walking through the park. His mom said, "We need to get to the jeep soon - we have to go home!" 

Carl said, "Ok, Mommy! I'll help you find it."

Carl and his mom looked around the park. After a while, Carl stopped and said, "Look - there it is! I see the jeep!"

Once they got to the jeep, Carl's mom opened the door and sat down. She said, "Now let's make sure we don't forget anything."

Carl looked around and said, "We have everything! Should I close the door?"

His Mom said, "Yes, but make sure it's closed tight." 

Carl grabbed the door and shut it. He said, "I think it's closed tight." 

His Mom smiled and said, "Good job! You always remind me to be careful. Now let's go home!"

Little Max was sitting in the garden, looking wistfully at the birds gliding gracefully in the sky. His dad was teaching him how to rock from side to side.

"Now Max, sit up nice and straight and use your feet to push off the ground." said his dad.

Max tried to rock as best as he could, stopping and pushing off the ground in a steady rhythm.

"Dad, can I have a race with the birds in the sky?" said Max.

His dad smiled and said, "Perhaps one day you'll join them, but right now we should practice your rocking."

Max was jealous of the birds' freedom, but he kept rocking, determined to make his dad proud. 

And then one day, he could rock higher and faster than ever before. He was surprised by his own ability and looked proudly up at the sky.

"Max, now you are ready for a race with the birds!" said his dad.

Max cheered with joy and raced to the window, the birds seemingly in slow motion as he flew out of the window, soaring through the sky and rocking with the wind. 
 
His dad watched with pride, knowing Max had used his practice to find his wings and become the fastest of all.

Once upon a time, a little boy named Timmy went outside to play. He saw a big puddle and jumped in it. His shoes got wet and he felt happy. Then, his mom called him inside for lunch.

At lunchtime, Timmy's mom gave him a sandwich and a glass of milk. He took a bite and realized the sandwich was disgusting. He said, "Mommy, this sandwich tastes yucky." She replied, "Sorry, Timmy. I accidentally used old bread. Let me make you a new one."

While his mom made a new sandwich, Timmy decided to draw a letter to his grandma. He wrote "G" for grandma and drew a picture of a flower. He put the letter in an envelope and asked his mom for a stamp. She said, "Sure, let's go to the post office." On the way, they saw a big fountain. Timmy said, "Mommy, can we soak our feet in the water?" She said, "Of course, let's do it!" They took off their shoes and socks and put their feet in the water. Timmy felt happy again.

Once there was a naughty little boy who liked to play. He was very curious and he liked to explore. One day he was playing by the TV and he had a great idea. He wanted to store things in it! He brought his toys to the TV and put them inside. He was so proud of himself that he ran around, shouting about it. But then he realized something - he couldn't get them back out! He was stuck! His mama was so mad when she saw. She said, "That was naughty of you. You can't store things inside the TV!" The little boy was very embarrassed, but he knew his mama was right. He apologized and promised to never do it again.

Once upon a time there lived a very troubled princess. She was always very sad and had no friends to cheer her up and lighten her mood. 

One day, while walking around the palace grounds she stumbled upon an old tree. The tree was huge, it was green and was the oldest tree in the garden. 

The princess decided to touch the tree and when she did, a voice came from inside! "Warning! There is a secret hidden inside this tree. Only special people should know about it"

The princess was so amazed that the tree talked to her. She asked the tree to tell her the secret and the tree refused. It said it was too special for her and that she must find the secret herself. 

The tree warned her not to tell anyone about this secret, as it could cause a lot of trouble. Staring out from the top of the tree, the princess smiled and a secret adventure had begun.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they find a big box. They want to make something with it.

"Let's make a boat!" Lily says. "We can row on the pond."

"Good idea!" Ben says. "But how do we make a boat?"

They think hard. They find some sticks and leaves. They tape them to the box. They make a sail and a flag. They make two oars from cardboard.

"Wow, our boat is ready!" Lily says. "Let's go to the pond."

They carry the boat to the pond. They put it on the water. They get in. They row with the oars. They pretend they are pirates.

"Ahoy, matey!" Ben says. "This is fun!"

"Look, a duck!" Lily says. "Hello, duck!"

The duck quacks. It swims near the boat. It pecks at the leaves. It likes them.

"Hey, duck, that's our sail!" Ben says. "Stop it!"

The duck does not stop. It pecks more leaves. The sail falls off. The boat starts to sink.

"Oh no, our boat!" Lily says. "We have to get out!"

They jump out of the boat. They swim to the shore. They are wet and sad.

The duck quacks. It swims away with the leaves.

"Bad duck!" Ben says. "It ruined our boat!"

Lily looks at Ben. She sees he is shivering. She takes off her scarf. She wraps it around him.

"Here, Ben, this will keep you warm," she says. "Don't be sad. We can make another boat."

Ben smiles. He hugs Lily. He feels grateful.

"Thank you, Lily," he says. "You are a good friend."

They walk back to the park. They hold hands. They are still friends.

Anna and Ben are playing in the kitchen. They like to pretend they are cooks. They have a big pan and some spoons and cups. They fill the pan with water and put it on the table.

"Let's make soup!" Anna says. "I will add some salt and pepper."

She takes a spoon and pretends to sprinkle some salt and pepper in the water. She stirs the water with the spoon.

"Can I help?" Ben asks. He wants to stir the water too.

"Yes, you can help. Pass me that cup, please." Anna says. She points to a cup on the shelf.

Ben reaches for the cup, but he is too short. He tries to stand on his toes, but he loses his balance. He falls and knocks over the pan. The water spills all over the table and the floor.

"Oh no!" Anna cries. "Look what you did! You made a big mess!"

She is angry with Ben. She thinks he is clumsy and silly.

"I'm sorry, Anna. I didn't mean to." Ben says. He feels sad and sorry. He didn't want to make Anna angry.

He picks up the pan and tries to wipe the water with a cloth.

"Let me help you, Ben." Anna says. She sees that Ben is sad and sorry. She is not angry anymore. She thinks he is nice and kind.

She takes another cloth and helps him wipe the water.

"Thank you, Anna. You are a good friend." Ben says. He smiles at Anna.

"You're welcome, Ben. You are a good friend too." Anna says. She smiles back at Ben.

They hug and make up. They decide to play something else. They are happy again.

Lily and Tom were friends who liked to play together. They had many toys, but their favorite was a big red truck. They took turns to drive the truck around the yard, making loud noises and having fun.

One day, a new boy named Ben came to play with them. He saw the truck and wanted to try it. He asked Lily and Tom if he could have a turn. Lily said yes, but Tom said no. He was jealous of Ben and did not want to share the truck. He grabbed the truck and drove away, leaving Lily and Ben behind.

Lily and Ben felt sad and angry. They decided to do something else. They went to the kitchen and asked Lily's mom if they could help her cook. Lily's mom said yes and gave them some dough and cookie cutters. They rolled the dough and cut out shapes of stars, hearts, and flowers. They put them on a tray and baked them in the oven. They smelled so good and looked so pretty.

Tom saw them from the window and felt curious. He parked the truck and came inside. He saw the cookies and wanted to try them. He asked Lily and Ben if he could have one. Lily and Ben looked at each other and smiled. They said yes and gave him a cookie. They told him they made them together and that they were very yummy.

Tom tasted the cookie and liked it. He said sorry to Lily and Ben for being mean and not sharing the truck. He said he wanted to be their friend and play with them. Lily and Ben forgave him and hugged him. They said they wanted to be his friend too and play with him. They shared the cookies and the truck and had a great time.

The moral of the story is: Sharing is caring. It is better to be kind and generous than to be selfish and greedy. You can have more fun and make more friends when you share.

Lily liked to mail stories to her grandma. She wrote stories with crayons and stickers. She put them in envelopes and gave them to mom. Mom put stamps on them and took them to the big box.

One day, Lily was very tired. She had played a lot with her toys and her dog. She did not want to write a story. She wanted to sleep. But she did not want to make grandma sad.

She had an idea. She took a picture book from her shelf. She opened it and looked at the pictures. She made up a story with the pictures. She told the story to mom. Mom wrote the story on a paper. Lily put the paper and the book in a big envelope. She gave it to mom.

Mom smiled and said, "What a nice story, Lily! Grandma will love it!" She put a stamp on the big envelope and took it to the big box.

Lily was happy. She hugged mom and said, "I love you, mom. I love grandma, too." She went to bed and dreamed of grandma reading her story.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily's mommy gave her a gift. It was a doll with a pretty dress. Lily was so happy and hugged her mommy. "Thank you, mommy! This is the best gift ever!" she said.

Later that day, Lily's friend, Tommy, came over to play. Lily wanted to show Tommy her new doll. "Tommy, look at my new doll! My mommy gave it to me as a gift," she said. Tommy looked at the doll and said, "Wow, Lily! That's a very thoughtful gift from your mommy. Let's play with your doll together!" 

Lily and Tommy played with the doll and had so much fun. They pretended the doll was a princess and they were her knights. They watched the doll dance and sing. Lily was happy that she had such a good friend like Tommy. And she was grateful for her mommy's thoughtful gift.

Once upon a time, there was a clever girl. Her name was Paige. She liked to spin and she was very good at it.

One day, Paige went to a special place to spin. She spun faster and faster. A bright, fun light shone all around her and amazing music filled the air! 

When she stopped spinning, Paige was filled with special power. She felt so strong and special.

Paige knew that the spinning had given her this special power. She thanked the special place for showing her and decided to go back soon to spin again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl with black hair. Her name was Lily. Lily had a big dog named Max. Max was her best friend. Lily loved Max very much and always played with him. 

One day, Lily went to the park with Max. She saw a girl she didn't know. The girl had black hair like Lily. Lily felt scared because she didn't know the girl. But Max ran to the girl and licked her face. The girl laughed and Lily saw that Max liked the girl. 

Lily knew she could trust Max because he was always nice to everyone. So Lily went to the girl and they played together. They had so much fun! Lily was happy she met a new friend. From that day on, Lily and the girl with black hair played together every day at the park.

Tom and Sue like to play with their toys. They have many toys, but their favorite is the missile. The missile is big and red and makes a loud noise when they push a button. They pretend the missile can fly to the moon and back.

One day, Tom and Sue want to play with the missile, but they cannot find it. They look in their room, in the living room, in the kitchen, but the missile is not there. They are sad and angry. They think someone took their missile.

They go to their mom and tell her what happened. Mom listens and hugs them. She says she knows where the missile is. She says she put it in the garage, because it is too big and too noisy for the house. She says the missile is expensive and they have to be careful with it.

Tom and Sue are happy and run to the garage. They see the missile on a shelf. They take it down and hug it. They say sorry to mom and thank her. They promise to play with the missile outside and not inside. Mom smiles and says she loves them. They love her too. They go outside and play with the missile. They have fun.

Billy was scared. He had to move and he didn't want to. He had to leave his house and go to a strange place. He stood by the drain with his grandmother.

Grandma: "Billy, come. It's time to move."
Billy: "No! I don't want to move!" 
Grandma: "It's okay, sweetheart. We'll be okay. I'm here with you."

With his grandma's soothing words, Billy felt a bit more brave. He finally stepped away from the drain and followed his grandma to the car. Billy was still scared, but he was happy to have his grandma with him. They drove away in the car and Billy waved goodbye to his old house. 

Soon enough, they arrived at their new home. Billy looked around, surprised at how different it was. He took a deep breath and he felt a little less scared. He couldn't believe he'd moved far away from his old house. With his grandma by his side, they walked inside and started a new adventure.

One day, there was an octopus who was swimming in the wide open sea. He was looking for food and friends. Suddenly, he saw another octopus waving his tentacles at him. 

The other octopus asked, "Do you want to be friends?"

The first octopus smiled and said, "Yes, I would like that very much."

The two octopuses swam together for a long time, talking about everything that was happening in the sea. They even made up silly games to play. 

The octopuses cared for each other. Each time one of them got hurt, the other one was there to help and hug. 

The two octopuses remained the best of friends until the very end. Whenever they saw each other, they always smiled and waved at each other with their wide tentacles.

Once upon a time, there was a cute little rabbit. He had big ears and a big, fluffy tail. His name was Bounce.

Every day Bounce would hop through the forest, looking for something special. He was searching for something called "butter". Heâ€™d heard that it was really yummy.

One day, as Bounce hopped along looking for the butter, he came across a charming little stream. The water was crystal clear and sparkled in the sunshine. Bounce just had to take a closer look.

Bounce hopped closer and closer to the stream but then, something went wrong. He slipped on a rock and went flying into the water. The water was cold and deep, so Bounce started to panic. He wasnâ€™t sure heâ€™d be able to get out.

Just then, he spotted a beam of bright light. It was the butter! He had finally found it. Using all his strength, Bounce bounced out of the water and grabbed the butter. It was the most delicious thing he had ever tasted.

Bounce happily hopped away, with the delicious butter in his paws. He had solved his own problem and was feeling very pleased with himself.

Sara and Ben are twins. They like to play in the garden. They have a big tree with a swing. They take turns to swing high and low. They laugh and shout.

One day, their mom says, "I have to send a letter to grandma. She is far away. She misses you. Do you want to help me?"

Sara and Ben say, "Yes, mom. We love grandma. Can we draw pictures for her?"

Mom says, "Of course. You can use these crayons and paper. I will write some words for her. Then we will put everything in an envelope and go to the mailbox."

Sara and Ben sit on the floor and draw. Sara draws a flower. Ben draws a car. They use many colors. They are happy.

Mom writes, "Dear grandma, we hope you are well. We miss you too. Sara and Ben made these pictures for you. They are very proud. We love you. Mom."

She puts the letter and the pictures in an envelope. She seals it and writes grandma's address. She says, "Come on, kids. Let's go to the mailbox. It is not far. We can walk."

Sara and Ben hold mom's hands. They walk to the mailbox. It is a big red box with a slot. Mom lifts Sara and Ben one by one. They put the envelope in the slot. They hear a thud.

Mom says, "There. We have sent the letter to grandma. She will be very happy when she gets it. She will write back to us soon."

Sara and Ben smile. They hug mom. They say, "Thank you, mom. We love you."

They walk back to the garden. It is a sunny day. The birds are singing. The wind is blowing. The garden is peaceful. Sara and Ben feel good. They go to the swing. They swing high and low. They laugh and shout. But sometimes, they are quiet. They listen to the silence. They think of grandma. They hope she is peaceful too.

Janie was really excited. Her mum had given her a special task. She was going to the store with her mum to buy an ice cream cone for herself. Janie was so excited she couldn't sleep the night before!

When Janie and her mum arrived at the store, Janie chose the biggest, fluffiest cone she could find. She was so excited she could hardly contain herself.

Janie's mother saw the excited look on Janie's face and said, "It looks like you really want this cone, Janie. You must have been very pleased that I allowed you to pick out this cone".

Janie smiled wide, nodded her head and said, "Thank you, mum! I'm sure this cone will be very useful!" 

Janie and her mum went home, where Janie enjoyed the most delicious cone she had ever tasted! From then on Janie was extra careful with her things, since she knew how useful it was to have them.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who was very eager to play the violin. She looked at her mum and asked, "Mum, can I grab my violin?" Her mum smiled and said, "Of course, sweetheart!"

The little girl ran over to the violin case and grabbed the instrument. With a big smile on her face, she hugged it close.

The mum watched as her daughter played and felt happy that her child was so eager. With every note she played, the little girl's face lit up with joy. 

At the end of the song, the mum smiled and said, "That was beautiful, sweetheart!" The little girl smiled back and gave her mum a big hug.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys all day long. One day, Lily's mom gave her a big teddy bear to play with. Lily was so happy and proud of her new toy.

Lily loved to rub the teddy bear's soft fur. It made her feel so cozy and warm. She played with the teddy bear all day long, giving it big hugs and kisses. 

When it was time for bed, Lily held onto her teddy bear tightly. She felt so proud to have such a special toy. As she drifted off to sleep, she dreamed of all the fun adventures she and her teddy bear would have together.

Once upon a time, there was a hidden measure. It was so small that nobody could see it. But it was in an old box and it was very important.

Every day, it stayed in the box, but it started to rot. The little measure was getting old and smelly. It smelled so bad that it made everyone turn away.

One day, a curious little boy opened the box. He saw the measure, but it was all rotten. He wanted to keep it, but it was too bad.

So the little boy decided to put the rotten measure in the garden, so it could start to grow again. He planted it and watered it every day.

After a few months, the measure was back to normal! It was hidden again but it looked new and beautiful. The little boy was so happy and he kept it safe in the box so it would never rot again.

Ducky was a little duck who had a very special secret. One day she went to the park with her mom. When she arrived, she saw a big square. It was so big that she had to jump to see the top of it!

Ducky started to poke the square with her tiny feet. Suddenly, a voice said, "Why are you poking my square?"

Ducky was worried. She didn't know where the voice had come from. But then she looked up and saw a tall bird standing on top of the square.

The bird said, "This square is my home. Please don't poke it."

Ducky said sorry and told the bird about her special secret. When the bird heard the secret, it smiled and said, "That's a wonderful secret. I won't tell anyone!"

Ducky was so happy that she hugged the bird. Then her mom called her to leave the park. Before leaving, Ducky waved goodbye to her new friend and the tall bird waved back.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved going to the festival with his mom and dad. They always got to eat delicious food and play fun games. 

One day, Timmy and his family were walking to the festival when Timmy saw a big tree. He wanted to climb it, but his mom said, "Be careful, Timmy. You might fall." 

At the festival, Timmy saw a big candy apple. It looked so delicious that he asked his dad if he could have one. His dad said, "Sure, Timmy. But be careful not to drop it." 

Later, Timmy was playing a game and he won a prize. He was so excited that he ran to show his mom. But he tripped and fell. His mom helped him up and said, "It's okay, Timmy. You're okay." 

Timmy learned that it's important to be careful and listen to his parents. And even if he falls, they will always be there to help him up.

Tik and Tuk were two small frogs. They were walking down a path when they spotted an old temple in the distance. The temple had been there for ages.

"Wow, look at it," said Tik to Tuk.

"Yes, it looks very alert," said Tuk.

What could it be? They thought.

So, they hopped closer to the temple and peeked in. Inside, they saw something very strange. It was a huge rock floating in the air!

The rock was swaying gently from side to side and making a gentle rocking sound.

Tik and Tuk were so surprised, but the rock looked so peaceful and beautiful.

They decided to stay and watch for a while, so they hopped up onto the stone and began to rock right along with it. 

They felt so happy and relaxed, like they were part of the temple.

They stayed there, rocking back and forth in harmony, until the sun started to set. 

Then, they hopped back home with a happy smile. Because they knew that they had discovered something amazing - the power of the alert temple.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toys and their dog, Spot. Spot is a big, furry dog who likes to lick their faces and run with them in the yard.

One day, Anna and Ben are playing with their purple ball. They throw it to each other and to Spot. Spot runs fast and catches the ball in his mouth. He brings it back to them and wags his tail. Anna and Ben laugh and clap their hands.

But soon, they start to feel tired. They yawn and rub their eyes. Mommy comes and says, "It's time for a nap, my sweeties. Come on, let's go to your room." Anna and Ben nod and follow Mommy. They hug Spot and say, "Bye, Spot. See you later."

Mommy takes them to their room, where they have two beds with soft blankets and pillows. She tucks them in and kisses their cheeks. She says, "Sleep well, my loves. I'll be here when you wake up." She turns on a small lamp that makes a warm glow. She leaves the door ajar.

Anna and Ben close their eyes and snuggle with their teddy bears. They feel cozy and safe. They hear Spot's snores from the living room. They smile and drift into a nap. They dream of purple ball and Spot and Mommy. They are happy.

Anna and Ben are friends. They love to play outside in the grass. The grass is green and soft. They run and jump and laugh in the grass.

One day, they see a big dog in the grass. The dog is brown and furry. He has a collar with a name. His name is Max. Max is friendly. He wags his tail and licks their faces.

"Hi, Max!" Anna says. "Do you want to play with us?"

"Yes, please!" Max barks. "I love to play in the grass too!"

Anna and Ben throw a ball for Max. Max runs and catches the ball. He brings it back to them. They take turns to throw the ball. They have fun together.

Max is a healthy dog. He eats good food and drinks clean water. He gets a lot of exercise and love. He is happy in the grass with Anna and Ben. They are happy too. They are friends.

Once upon a time, there was a delicate little princess. She had long blonde hair and she often wore pretty dresses. She was a very happy princess, almost all of the time.

One day, she went outside to play and it began to rain. She was so surprised and her mouth made a big 'O'. She felt a shock in her chest and the shock made her frown.

The princess was sad because all of her plans had been ruined by the weather. But then she saw a rainbow in the sky and she cheered up again. The colours were so beautiful that it made her smile. 

The princess smiled and her frown went away and she knew that even though rain could ruin plans, it could also bring beautiful surprises.

Lily and Ben like to cook with Mom. They have a big book with many pages of recipes. Mom lets them choose what to cook today.

Lily picks a page with a picture of a cake. She says, "I want to cook a cake, Mom. It looks yummy."

Ben picks a page with a picture of a pizza. He says, "I want to cook a pizza, Mom. It looks cheesy."

Mom smiles and says, "We can cook both, but we need to go to the store first. We need some eggs, flour, sugar, cheese, and tomatoes. Can you help me make a list?"

Lily and Ben nod and get a paper and a crayon. They write down the words Mom says. They are good at writing. Mom says they are reliable helpers.

They go to the store and buy the things they need. Then they go back home and start to cook. Lily and Ben help Mom measure, mix, pour, and spread. They have fun and make a mess. Mom puts the cake and the pizza in the oven. They wait and smell the good food.

Soon, the cake and the pizza are ready. They look like the pictures in the book. Lily and Ben are proud of their cooking. They say, "We did it, Mom. We cooked a cake and a pizza."

Mom hugs them and says, "You did a great job, Lily and Ben. You are wonderful cooks. Let's eat and enjoy our food."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and her cat, Mittens. One day, Lily's mom asked her to clean up her room with a mop. Lily didn't want to clean up because she wanted to keep playing. 

But then, Lily's mom told her that if she didn't clean up, she couldn't play with Mittens. This made Lily very sad because she loved Mittens so much. She decided to clean up her room with the mop, but she was still jealous of all the other kids who were playing outside. 

As she was cleaning, she started to think about how much fun she could be having outside. Suddenly, she had an idea. She decided to change her attitude and be happy about cleaning her room. After she finished cleaning, she went outside and played with the other kids. She realized that sometimes, it's good to change your attitude and be happy with what you have.

Once upon a time, there was a cat called Naughty. Naughty was always up to mischief! One day, Naughty saw a juicy steak on the kitchen table. He moved closer to it, trying to get a better look. Before he knew it, he had pounced on the steak. 

Naughty was about to take a bite when he heard a loud yell! It was his mom! She was very angry and said, "Naughty, get away from that steak!" Naughty was scared and quickly moved away.

Naughty hung his head in shame, wishing he hadn't been so naughty. He knew he had been very bad and he would have to be extra careful in the future. He quietly crept away, vowing to never touch the steak again.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Emma who loved to paint. Every day she would wear her favourite dress, pick up her brush and go outside to paint.

One day, Emma was feeling lucky, so she decided to go to her favourite spot by the lake and paint. She chose some bright colours and began to paint a pretty picture.

Suddenly, Emma heard a voice. "Can I have a go?" it said. 

"Sure!" Emma said. "What should I paint?"

"Oh, just something magical!" the friendly voice replied. 

Emma smiled and began to paint a beautiful rainbow. When she was finished the voice said, "Wow, that's amazing! You're really talented".

Emma felt proud and was so glad she had decided to wear her favourite dress and go outside to paint that day. She had been ever so lucky!

Molly was excited. Today was a special day. She was going to pack her bag. It was a fancy bag with lots of pockets. 

Molly found a note inside that said a word. Molly thought it was a special word. She was excited and wanted to show everyone.

Molly began to pack her bag. She put in a blanket, her bear, and her book. 

Then she emptied out a box and packed the special word inside. She was careful with it because it was so fancy. 

Finally, Molly was ready to go. She stood up and looked at her fancy bag. She couldn't wait to show everyone the special word she had packed.

One day there was a rare fan in the middle of the room. It was a beautiful fan, with large and colorful feathers on the edge. Little Billy wanted to touch it and play with it.

Billy's mom said, "Billy, don't touch that fan. It is too rare, we must welcome it."

Billy said, "Mom, why did you welcome the fan?"

His mom replied, "The fan is so special, so rare, it deserves a special welcome. Don't worry, you'll get to play with it when I say it is okay."

Billy did not understand, but he promised to follow mom's instructions.

The next day, Billy's mom said it was okay for him to welcome the fan. He took it in his hands, carefully, and waved it in the air. Suddenly, the fan began to spin and the feathers glowed brightly in the light. Billy squealed with joy as the fan filled the room with a magical, gentle breeze.

Billy now knew why his mom said it was important to welcome the fan. Because of the beautiful experience it created!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily was very impatient. She wanted to help her mom cook dinner. Her mom said, "Okay, Lily, you can help me cut the vegetables."

Lily was so happy. She took a bowl and put the vegetables in it. Then, she started to cut them with her safe little knife. She cut a carrot, a potato, and a tomato. She put them all in the bowl.

Her mom looked at the bowl and said, "Good job, Lily! Now we can cook the vegetables for dinner." Lily smiled and felt proud. She learned that even though she was impatient, she could still help her mom and do a good job.

Once, there was a girl called Sally. She was three years old. One day she was out for a walk with her mom.

Sally was wearing her new purple socks, which she was very proud of. But then something embarrassing happened! Sally's socks suddenly fell off. Her mom smiled, but Sally was embarrassed.

Sally carefully put her socks back on and made sure they were really secure. She did not want her socks to fall off again.

Then she and her mom continued to walk. This time, Sally was very careful. Every few steps, she looked down to make sure her socks were still on.

The end.

John and his mom were having dinner. The dinner was hot and the room was warm. John wanted to hang up his coat. He went over to the coat rack and hung it up. He was happy to have a place to put it. 

John was getting bored during dinner. The conversation was dull and he was not interested. He wanted something to do. So he looked around the room. He saw that there were a few pictures on the walls. 

John thought it would be fun to hang them up. He asked his mom if he could hang them up. She said yes and handed him some string. He grabbed the pictures and used the string to hang them up. 

He was very proud of his work. The walls were no longer dull. He was happy to have something to do during dinner. He smiled when his mom praised his work. Dinner was a lot more fun with his pictures on the walls.

Once upon a time, there was an orange cat. She was always very happy and loved to play.

One day the cat was walking past the house of two brothers. The older brother had just finished a joke and the younger brother was laughing.

The orange cat stopped and sat down. She listened to the joke and smiled. Then the older brother noticed her and said "Hi! Do you want to hear another joke?"

The orange cat said "Yes please." So the older brother told another joke and the orange cat laughed and laughed.

The brothers realized that even animals could understand and enjoy jokes. They decided that it was important to make people smile and laugh.

The brothers went away feeling happy and the orange cat went on her way with a smile on her face.

Moral: Making people laugh is important. It helps us to make friends and boosts our mood.

Once upon a time there was a mighty dragon. He lived high up in the sky above a green valley. From time to time, the dragon would fly through the air, breathing out flame from his mouth.

One day, the dragon was passing over a large hill when he saw something that made him stop. Sitting on the hill was a small, round hat. It was the most beautiful hat the dragon had ever seen, and it fit him perfectly. 

The dragon decided to take the hat for himself. So he picked it up and flew to his home. 

Once he arrived back, the dragon showed his hat to all his friends. 

"Look how nicely it fits!" said the dragon. "It's the most beautiful hat I have ever seen!"

But one of his friends replied: "No way! Let me try it on. Maybe it will fit me better than it fits you!" 

The dragon smiled and said: "Go ahead, my mighty friend, I'm sure it will fit you perfectly too." 

And so, it did. The hat fit the mighty dragon's friend as well as it fit the dragon. They both smiled, and the dragon proudly wore his beautiful hat every single day
after that.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tweety. Tweety was very happy because she had just learned how to fly. She decided to fly to her friend's house to play. On her way, she saw a man jogging in the park. She thought it looked like fun, so she decided to try it too. 

But Tweety was very fragile, and she fell down and hurt her wing. She was very sad and didn't know what to do. She saw a big building with a red cross on it and flew inside. It was a hospital! 

Inside the hospital, Tweety met a kind nurse who took care of her. The nurse gave her some medicine and put a bandage on her wing. After a few days, Tweety's wing was all better and she could fly again. She was very happy and grateful to the nurse for helping her.

Once upon a time, there was a twin brother and sister. They both loved to swim in the big river. One day, the twin brother thought of an idea. He decided that he wanted to swim to the other side of the river. So, he jumped in the water and swam across the river.

As he swam, the water tasted bitter. But he kept going. The twin brother was determined to reach the other side of the river.

After a few minutes, he finally made it to the other side of the river. He was so proud of himself for making it across!

He swam back to the edge of the river and waved at his twin sister on the other side. She was so happy to see him that she started to jump up and down. Then the twins played in the river together until it was time to go home.

Once upon a time there was a mommy and a baby. Mommy had a mixer. One day, baby saw the mixer and wanted to try it. Mommy said, "No, this is not for babies. It could be dangerous." But baby was silly and did not listen. He grabbed the mixer and turned it on. 

Suddenly, it started to make a lot of noise and the kitchen became a mess. Mommy was so angry. She said, "I told you this would happen! Now, you must be punished!" Baby started to cry. 

Mommy gave baby a time out and told him never to touch the mixer again. She said, "You were very stupid to do this. Mixers are not for babies." Baby promised that he would never do it again, and he was very sorry. 
 Yeah, mommy was right. Baby should have listened.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play hide and seek with his friends. One day, Timmy decided to hide under his mattress. He thought it would be a great hiding spot.

But then, Timmy's mom came into his room and saw that the mattress was all messed up. She got grumpy and asked Timmy what happened. Timmy felt bad and told her that he was playing hide and seek.

His mom explained to him that it's not okay to hide in places that could hurt him, like under the mattress. Timmy felt sad and apologized. From then on, he only hid in safe places and never made his mom grumpy again.

One day, a little boy named Tim found a big, modern motorcycle. It was shiny and new. He wanted to ride it, but he was too small. So, he asked his mom for help.

"Mom, can I ride this motorcycle?" Tim asked. His mom said, "No, Tim. You are too little. But we can bake a cake instead!"

Tim liked the idea of baking a cake. They went to the kitchen and got flour, sugar, and eggs. They mixed everything together and put it in the oven. The cake smelled yummy.

When the cake was ready, Tim and his mom ate it together. They laughed and had a great time. Tim forgot about the motorcycle and was happy with his mom and the cake they baked together.

Once upon a time there was a boy with two buckets. One bucket was full of sand and the other was empty. He wanted to play a game with his friends and began to share the sand. He was happy and released it from the bucket into the air.

His friend was jealous because his bucket was empty. The boy said, "Don't be jealous! You can have some of my sand too!" He gave his friend a big scoop of sand, and their faces lit up with excitement.

The two boys enjoyed releasing the sand into the air and watching it sprinkle on them. They laughed and smiled as they took turns scooping and releasing the sand. The friends were joyous as they enjoyed their simple playtime. 

"We better keep some sand to play with another day!" the boy said. So they put the rest of the sand back in the bucket and waved goodbye.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to run and jump and slide. They saw a big pond with ducks and frogs. Lily wanted to go closer and feed them.

"Wait, Lily!" Ben said. "Mommy warned us not to go near the pond. It is deep and wet and cold. You could fall in and get hurt."

Lily did not listen to Ben. She was ignorant. She thought she knew better. She ran to the pond and threw some bread to the ducks. The ducks came closer and quacked. Lily smiled and reached out her hand.

Suddenly, a big splash made Lily scream. A frog had jumped out of the water and landed on her hand. Lily was scared and dropped the bread. She tried to run away, but her foot slipped on the mud. She fell into the pond with a splash.

Ben ran to help Lily. He grabbed her hand and pulled her out of the pond. Lily was wet and cold and dirty. She was crying and shivering. Ben hugged her and said, "It's okay, Lily. I'm here. Don't cry."

Mommy heard the noise and came to see what happened. She saw Lily and Ben by the pond. She was angry and worried. She scolded Lily for being ignorant and not listening to her warning. She praised Ben for being brave and helping his sister. She took them home and gave them a warm bath and a hot drink.

Lily learned her lesson. She said sorry to Mommy and Ben. She promised to be more careful and listen to warnings. She realized that the pond was not a good place to play in spring. She decided to play with the ducks and frogs from a safe distance.

Once upon a time, there was a little mole. He was very shy and liked to hide. He called out to his friends, but none answered. Suddenly a voice called back, "Hey, little mole!" The mole was so surprised. He jumped out of his hole and saw a bright bird. The bird hopped closer and said, "Hi, I'm Pete. Would you like to be my friend?" The little mole was very shy, but he said, "Yes"! Pete and the mole became best friends. They played together all day and ate delicious food that Pete brought. The little mole was so happy to have a friend.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there lived a miserable cat named Tom. Tom was sad because he had no friends to play with. Yesterday, he tried to make friends with the little birds, but they flew away.

One day, Tom saw a little dog named Max. Max was running around and having fun. Tom wanted to play with Max, but he was scared. He decided to try and stop being scared.

Tom walked up to Max and said, "Stop, Max! Can we be friends?" Max looked at Tom and smiled. "Of course, Tom! Let's play together!" From that day on, Tom and Max played together every day, and Tom was not miserable anymore.

Once upon a time, in a small village, there was a fearful little mouse. The mouse was scared of everything. One day, he went out to find some food. He saw a big, round, yellow cheese. The cheese was on a high shelf. The mouse wanted to eat the cheese, but he was too scared to climb up.

A kind, wise owl saw the mouse and wanted to help him. The owl said, "Don't be fearful, little mouse. I will help you get the cheese. Just trust me and put your fear away." The mouse was still scared, but he wanted the cheese very much. So, he listened to the owl and tried to be brave.

The owl flew up and gently took the cheese off the shelf. Then, he put the cheese on the ground for the mouse. The mouse was so happy and thanked the owl. From that day on, the mouse was not fearful anymore. He learned that with the help of friends, he could be brave and put his fears away. The moral of the story is: when we trust and help each other, we can overcome our fears.

Once upon a time, there was a wealthy plant. It was the most beautiful one anyone had ever seen. Every day the plant would dance in the sun and the wind. All the animals in the forest were so happy to see it. 

But one day, something strange happened. A giant cloud flew over the plant, and it started to get dark. An old owl flew out of the cloud and warned the animals. "The wealthy plant is in danger!" he said. 

The animals were so scared, but they did not give up. They formed a plan and worked together every day. They cleared the ground around the plant and put all the leaves around it. 

The next day, the sun shined brightly and the cloud was gone. The plant was safe! All the animals rejoiced and celebrated the wonderful plant. The animals shared a special bond and kept careful watch over the wealthy plant for the rest of time.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a big dog named Max. Max was very frightened of everything. One day, Max was playing in the park when he saw a cat. The cat was sitting on a wall.

Max wanted to be friends with the cat, so he called out, "Hello, cat! Do you want to play?" The cat looked at Max and said, "No, I don't want to play with you. You are a big dog and you might hurt me."

Max was sad, but he knew the law said that big dogs should be careful with small animals. So, he walked away from the cat. But as he walked away, he tripped and fell. Max was hurt and cried out loud.

Nobody came to help Max because they were all too frightened of the big dog. Max was all alone, and he felt very sad. The bad ending made Max wish he was not so big and scary, so he could have friends to play with.

"Vroom, vroom, my truck is very fast and strong," Tom said. "It can go anywhere and do anything."

"My doll is very pretty and kind," Lily said. "She likes to help people and animals."

"What is that on your doll's dress?" he asked Lily. He used the word "question" to ask something.

"That is a pin," Lily said. "It is a small thing that can hold things together. Mommy gave it to me. She said it was very special."

"Can I see it?" Tom asked. He reached out his hand to take the pin.

Tom felt sad and angry. He wanted to see the pin and play with it. He did not understand why Lily did not want to share.

"That is not fair," he said. "You always have to share. Sharing is good."

"No, I don't have to share," she said. "The pin is mine and I love it."

"Tom wants to take my pin and he does not understand that it is special to me," Lily said.

Mommy sighed. She knew that Tom and Lily were both wrong. They needed to learn how to respect each other and their things.

"Tom, you should not try to take Lily's pin without her permission. It is her toy and she can decide what to do with it. You should ask her nicely and respect her answer. Maybe she will let you see it or play with it another time," Mommy said.

"Lily, you should not be selfish and rude. It is nice to share your toys with your brother sometimes. He is curious and interested in your pin. You should explain to him why it is special to you and let him look at it or touch it gently. Maybe he will appreciate it and like it too," Mommy said.

Tom and Lily nodded. They understood what Mommy said. They felt sorry for hurting each other's feelings.

"I'm sorry, Lily," Tom said. "I should not have tried to take your pin. Can you tell me why it is special to you?"

"I'm sorry, Tom," Lily said. "I should not have been mean to you. I can show you my pin. It is special to me because Mommy gave it to me. It was her pin when she was a little girl. She said it was a gift from Grandma. It has a flower on it and it sparkles in the light."

Tom looked at the pin and smiled. He saw the flower and the sparkle. He thought it was pretty and special too.

"Wow, that is a nice pin," he said. "Thank you for showing it to me. I understand why you love it."

Lily smiled back. She felt happy that Tom liked her pin. She felt generous and kind.

"You're welcome," she said. "Do you want to play with it for a little while? You can put it on your truck if you want. But be careful not to lose it or hurt yourself."

Tom was surprised and happy. He did not expect Lily to share her pin with him. He felt grateful and careful.

"Really? Thank you, Lily. That is very nice of you. I will be careful with your pin. I will not lose it or hurt myself. I will give it back to you soon," he said.

Tom and Lily hugged each other. They said sorry and thank you. They felt like friends again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the mud. One day, she found a big brown puddle of mud. Lily jumped in it and got all dirty. 

When she came back inside, her mommy said, "Lily, you are covered in mud! Let's give you a bath." Lily's mommy filled the tub with warm water and bubbles. She helped Lily take off her muddy clothes and put her in the tub. 

Lily's mommy washed her hair and scrubbed her body clean. After the bath, Lily felt so fresh and clean. Her mommy gave her some yummy food to feed her hungry tummy. Lily was happy and ready for a good night's sleep. The end.

Once upon a time, there lived a jolly family in a house by the sea. Every morning, they would wake up with the ring of a clock. Mom and dad would get up to cook a delicious breakfast while their little boy would play in the garden.

The family always ate together, with mom cooking yummy omelettes and dad making bacon and eggs. Everyone was always singing and smiling while they ate and it made everyone feel nice and warm inside.

After breakfast, the family would all go for a walk and collect shells by the sea. They would laugh when dad would make silly jokes and laugh even more when little brother was tickled and laughed louder than them all!

At the end of the day, when the clock said it was time for bed, the family would gather around the table and eat the special dinner mom had cooked. All of them were so full from the food and so happy from the day that they went to bed feeling happy and sleepy. 

At night, the clock was the last thing they heard before the sandman came to take them away to sweet dreams.

Once there was a little boy. He was very happy and polite. He liked to explore his garden. One day he noticed a big hook in one of the bushes. He went to take a closer look, and then he screamed! He had found a giant, bustling bug. It scared him so much that he ran away!

But then the bug said, "Hey, don't run! I'm a friendly bug! I just wanted to say hi!" The boy was a bit scared, but after hearing the bug's polite words, he stopped and came a bit closer.

The boy started to talk to the bug and he soon became fast friends. They talked and explored the garden together. The bug helped the boy look for more things to discover. What an interesting day!

Once upon a time there was a famous man. He was very nice and made lots of people happy. One day he made a promise to everyone. He said "I will do something wonderful and amazing." Everyone was very excited and couldn't wait.

The man began to wonder what he should do. He thought about it for a long time. He decided to turn the sky into a rainbow. Everyday for one hour the sky filled with color. All the children were so happy. They ran and laughed as they saw the rainbow in the sky.

The man kept his promise. He filled the sky with color and joy. Everyone said, "Thank you for making us happy". The man smiled and said, "My pleasure". He was very famous now. Everyone knew his name and admired what he had done.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys and ride his bike on the road. One day, Timmy's bike broke and he couldn't ride it anymore. He was very sad.

But then, Timmy's dad said he could replace the broken part on the bike and it would be as good as new. Timmy was so happy! His dad fixed the bike and Timmy was able to ride it on the great road again.

Timmy learned that sometimes things break, but they can be fixed and made great again. He was grateful for his dad's help and promised to take good care of his bike from then on. The end.

Tom and Anna are friends. They like to play with toys. One day, they find a big box in the yard. The box has a lock on it.

"Wow, what is in the box?" Tom asks.

"I don't know, but I want to see," Anna says.

They try to open the lock, but it is too hard. They pull and push, but nothing happens.

"Maybe we need a key," Tom says.

"Where can we find a key?" Anna asks.

They look around the yard, but they do not see a key. They see a man walking by. He has a big bag.

"Excuse me, sir, do you have a key for this lock?" Tom asks.

The man stops and looks at them. He has a serious face.

"No, I don't have a key. That is my box. You should not touch it. It is not for you," he says.

He takes the box and puts it in his bag. He walks away.

Tom and Anna are sad. They wanted to see what was in the box. They wonder what the man was hiding. They go back to their toys. They hope to find another box someday.

Once upon a time there was a boy who was very hungry. He looked in his cupboard and saw a cauliflower. He loved cauliflower and he was very happy.

The boy called his mom so she could help him prepare it. Mom came over and boiled the cauliflower. It smelled really nice.

They added cheese and made a yummy dish. The boy was so excited. He gobbled up the cauliflower and it was so tasty.

The boy was no longer hungry, so he went outside to play in the sun with his friends. He called out to them "Come play with me!" 

Everyone had so much fun playing together. The boy and his friends went home with big smiles on their faces. The boy was very happy to have eaten a delicious cauliflower dish.

Once upon a time, there was a shy little girl named Lily. She had big brown eyes and a small nose. She loved going to school, but she was always afraid to talk to new friends. One day, she went to school and saw that her teacher had scattered a lot of toys in the classroom. 

Lily's classmate, Tom, saw her standing alone and asked, "Do you want to play with me?" Lily felt happy and replied, "Yes, please." They played with the toys and had so much fun together. After a while, Tom said, "You are a good pupil, Lily. You should talk more often. You are my new friend." 

Lily smiled and felt proud. From that day on, she wasn't shy anymore and she talked to her classmates. She learned that making friends is easy and fun. She loved going to school even more and played with Tom every day. They scattered toys around the classroom and had the best time together.

Sara and Tom are playing in the park. They see a big tree with many leaves. They want to climb the tree and see what is up there.

"Can we climb the tree, please?" Sara asks her mom.

"Be careful, okay? The tree is very big and high. And don't touch any nests or birds. They might get scared or angry," her mom says.

Sara and Tom nod and run to the tree. They find a low branch and pull themselves up. They climb higher and higher, looking for nests and birds.

"Look, Tom! I see a nest!" Sara says, pointing to a small hole in the trunk. "Do you think there are eggs or babies inside?"

"I don't know. Let's go closer and see," Tom says.

They climb to the hole and peek inside. They see a small bird sitting on some eggs. The bird looks at them with big eyes and makes a loud noise.

"Shoo! Shoo! Go away!" the bird says.

Sara and Tom are surprised and scared. They shrug and say sorry to the bird.

"Sorry, bird. We didn't mean to bother you. We just wanted to see your nest. It's very nice," Sara says.

"Yeah, sorry, bird. We'll leave you alone now. Bye-bye," Tom says.

They climb down the tree and go back to their mom. They tell her what they saw and heard.

"That's very interesting, Sara and Tom. You were very brave and polite to the bird. But remember, nests and birds are not toys. They are living things that need their space and privacy. Next time, you can look at them from a distance, okay?" their mom says.

"Okay, mom. We understand. Nests and birds are not toys. They are living things," Sara and Tom say.

They hug their mom and go play some more in the park. They have fun and learn something new.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tweety. Tweety loved to fly high in the sky and sing songs. One day, Tweety saw a big zigzag in the sky. Tweety didn't know what it was, so he asked his friends. They guessed it was a storm coming.

Tweety decided to fly away from the zigzag, but he got lost. He flew and flew, but he couldn't find his way back home. He was scared and sad. But then, he remembered something his mom had told him: "If you ever get lost, just follow the sun and you will find your way back home."

So, Tweety followed the sun and it led him back home. He was so happy to be back in his perfect little nest. Tweety learned that sometimes it's okay to guess, but it's always better to ask and learn. And if you ever get lost, just remember to follow the sun.

Once, there was a noisy dog. He liked to bark and run around a lot.

One day, he was running near the stove when he decided to take a bite. He bit the stove and it made a loud, awful noise. Everyone inside was scared. 

The dog saw that he had made a mistake and ran away. He was scared that he would get in trouble.

He found a safe place to hide. He waited for a long time, until he was sure that everyone had gone away. Then, he slowly came back out to the stove.

The stove was safe now, but it was important for him to remember to never, ever bite the stove again.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Mia. She was feeling very restless. So, one day Mia decided to go to the park.

At the park, Mia saw lots of wonderful things. She saw the trees and the flowers. She saw the birds singing in the sky.

Mia had the best time picking flowers and chasing butterflies. She was so happy that she put some flowers in her pocket.

When she was ready, Mia went to the playground. There, she saw a swing and decided to have some more fun. She was so excited that she jumped onto the swing and started to swing higher and higher.

After a while, Mia got tired and it was time to go home. She reluctantly left the park but was happy that she had had such a great time.

Mia went home with a pocket full of flowers and a heart full of joy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She was three years old and liked to explore.

One day, she went to the beach. She saw a shrimp lifting something from the water. The little girl started to laugh. She thought it was funny how the shrimp kept lifting the thing.

But then the little girl noticed that the thing in the water was disgusting. She put her hand over her nose and scrunched up her face. It was a smelly fish!

The little girl laughed and laughed. She thought it was hilarious how the shrimp was trying to lift the smelly fish from the water. She was so glad she didn't get too close to it.

Once upon a time, there was a furry tour. All of the tour's friends were so excited to go! Everyone was excited for the tour, which was so magical because it glowed. All the people and animals on the tour felt so happy, and when the tour glowed, it was the most special feeling of all.

One night in particular, the tour glowed brighter than it ever had before. Everyone was amazed by the bright light and they all jumped with excitement. They felt like they were in a dream! As the furry tour glowed brighter and brighter, they felt like they were on a magical journey.

At the end of the tour, everyone who had been on the furry tour agreed it was the best night ever. They had felt like they were part of something special and magical. All of the friends shared wonderful memories about the tour and enjoyed the peaceful glow for the rest of the night.

Timmy was sad. His baseball had rolled away to an area he couldn't reach. Suddenly a dependable friend walked up and said, "I can help you." He grabbed the ball and smiled. Timmy was so happy he forgot to say thank you. He just smiled and hugged his new dependable friend.

The two of them ran around the park throwing and catching the baseball. Timmy was having so much fun that he forgot how sad he was. His new friend was dependable, and very good at playing baseball.

After a while, Timmy's mom had to go, and his new friend had to leave too. They said goodbye and his new friend frowned. That made Timmy sad all over again. He said goodbye and waved until his friend was gone. He went home feeling lonely. 

Seeing his new friend frown made Timmy realize that he had not properly thanked him for getting the baseball. It was important for Timmy to stay grateful, so the next day Timmy sent his friend a card saying "Thank you for being dependable and helping me get my baseball". His friend smiled and they became friends for a long time.

Once upon a time, there was a silly monkey. He was very foolish and always got into trouble.

One day, he decided he wanted to find a banana. He thought it would be fun. He looked all around, but couldn't find one. He was getting frustrated, so he started to guess. He guessed he should look up in the tree.

Sure enough, when he looked up he found the biggest banana he had ever seen. He grinned from ear to ear, and it was so funny! He grabbed the banana and raced back to his home. He was so happy he had figured it out.

The monkey quickly ate the banana and felt much better. From then on, he was careful not to be so foolish!

Once upon a time there was a lonely duck. The duck quacked each day but nobody answered. One day when the duck was quacking, a surprise came from the sky! Water was leaking from the clouds! The duck was so happy that it splashed and quacked. 

The duck was no longer lonely. The rain made a big, wet puddle and all kinds of animals came to play. It was fun to splash and laugh together in the rain. 

The surprise rain stopped after a while, but the lonely duck was happy again. It now had friends to quack with each day! They even made a secret promise that they would always be friends. 

The end.

One day, there was a modern horn. It was a loud horn! It made noise every day. The noise was so loud, everyone could hear it. 

One day, a small boy named Tom woke up from his sleep. He heard the noise of the horn and it surprised him. He wondered where the noise was coming from. 

Tom decided to search for the horn to figure out where the noise was coming from. He searched high and low, near and far. After a long search, Tom eventually found the modern horn! He had finally found the source of the noise. 

Tom realized the horn had been there all along. From then, he wouldn't be surprised by the noise of the horn anymore!

Once upon a time there was a nice lady who wanted to earn some money. She decided to sell her special textures. They were very soft and bright.

The lady put some of the textures in a basket and took them to the market. Everyone admired the textures when they saw them. They were so soft and shiney.

The lady sold all of her textures. She was very pleased and said thank you to everyone who bought them. She was very polite.

At the end of the day the lady had earned a lot of money. She was very proud and happy. She went home and bought herself a special treat.

The end.

Bob was a little boat. One day, he decided to sail away. He waved goodbye to his mom and dad and they blew him kisses as he sailed away. 

Bob sailed and sailed until he saw an island. it was very messy. Bob sailed to the shore, but he couldn't get to the land because it was too muddy.

But then, Bob saw someone! It was a lawyer. 

"Hello!" Bob yelled to the lawyer.

"Hello there, little boat!" the lawyer said. "I can help you get to the land. I'm a lawyer and I know the law of the sea. Follow me!"

The lawyer waved to Bob and Bob followed him. With the lawyer's help, Bob made it to the messy land. 

Bob was so happy! He had made it to the island without getting stuck in the mud. 

The lawyer smiled and said, "You did it! Good job, little boat!" Then he waved goodbye and sailed away. 

Bob was very proud of himself. He had sailed to a new adventure on his own.

Once upon a time there was a kind girl named Amelia who was always very polite. One day Amelia had an excellent idea. She decided to send a surprise in the mail!

Amelia took a piece of paper and wrote a note. It said, "I have a surprise for you!" She put the note in an envelope and mailed it to her best friend.

Her friend was so excited! She waited all day for the mail to come and was very pleased to receive the envelope. When she opened it, she saw the surprise. It was a special bracelet!

Amelia's friend was delighted with the gift. She thanked Amelia for sending such a kind, thoughtful surprise. Everyone was very happy that Amelia had been so polite and sent such a lovely surprise through the mail.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toy kayak in the bathtub. One day, Timmy's mom forgot to supply him with more bubble bath. Timmy was frustrated because he loved to make big bubbles with his kayak. 

Timmy decided to ask his mom for more bubble bath. But when he went to the bathroom, he saw that his mom had already gone to bed. Timmy was sad because he really wanted to play with his kayak. 

Suddenly, Timmy had an idea. He remembered that he had some shampoo left in his bathroom. He thought that maybe the shampoo could supply him with enough bubbles to play with his kayak. Timmy tried it out and it worked! He was so happy that he could play with his kayak again.

Once upon a time, there was a happy boy named Timmy. He loved playing with his computer. It was his favorite toy. One day, Timmy's computer stopped working. He felt sad and wanted to complain to his mom. 

"Mama, my computer is broken. I can't play with it anymore," Timmy said. 

His mom saw how sad he was and tried to cheer him up. She told him they could take the computer to the store to get it fixed. Timmy felt a little better and smiled. 

After a few days, they got the computer back and it was working again. Timmy was so happy and cheerful. He thanked his mom and played with his computer all day long. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sophie. She liked to have fun and explore the world around her. One day, Sophie decided to explore her mommy's kitchen. 

As Sophie looked around, she saw an interesting looking machine on the counter. It was so exciting and she wanted to find out what it was. She asked her mommy, "What is this?"

Mommy smiled and said, "That's a coffee machine! It makes coffee for adults. Do you want to try it?"

Sophie nodded eagerly and gave it a squeeze. But it wasn't very comfortable and it made her feel a bit uncomfortable.

Her mommy laughed and said, "Oh Sophie, I think it's best if adults use the coffee machine."

Sophie smiled and went back to exploring the kitchen. She was glad her mommy was there to help her and make her feel better.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to drink tea with her grandma. One day, her grandma made her a cup of spicy tea. Lily took a sip and her mouth felt hot. She didn't like it. 

The next morning, Lily woke up early to watch the sun rise. She sat outside with her cup of tea. As she sipped her tea, she noticed the sky turning pink and orange. The sun was rising! Lily felt happy and warm inside. She realized that even though she didn't like spicy tea, she loved watching the sunrise with her cup of tea. 

From then on, Lily and her grandma would wake up early to watch the sunrise together. They would drink their tea, but Lily always made sure to ask for a non-spicy one. They loved spending time together and watching the world wake up.

Once upon a time, there was a busy cat. She wanted to find something to do, so she went out for a walk. 

The cat saw a bush in the park. She wanted to explore, so she walked right up to it. 

The bush was very tall. She jumped and jumped, trying to make it to the top. It was hard, but after a few tries she was able to make it! 

Once she reached the top, she looked around and saw lots of things she could do. The cat was so excited! 

She started to play, climbing and jumping from branch to branch. Soon she was getting really tired, so she decided to go home. 

Just as she was about to leave, she noticed a small bird's nest in the bush. She knew she had to complete the job. 

So, the cat carefully moved the branches aside and carefully reached for the nest. When she had taken it down, she felt so proud - she had completed the job!

Once upon a time, there was a strange hat. It was a mysterious blue hat and it was always on the move!

One day, the hat was playing hide and seek. It hid in a cupboard but nobody could find it. Everyone searched far and wide, but they could not find the mysterious hat.

But then, a little boy came along. He had big eyes and he was three years old. He opened the cupboard and he saw the hat. When he saw the blue hat, he smiled and reached out his hand.

The mysterious hat flew out of the cupboard and into the little boy's lap. He hugged the hat and he put it on his head.

The little boy and the mysterious blue hat were best friends from then on.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Anna who liked to pretend. One sunny day, she went outside and saw a beautiful landscape. She wanted to go explore it and made her way to a nearby field.

When she got there, she ran around and pretended she was a fairy. She flew around, making sure she was being obedient. Suddenly, she heard a funny noise and saw a cow in the field.

Anna went closer to the cow and asked, "What are you doing?"

The cow replied, "I'm eating the grass in this field. Do you want to play with me?"

Anna was very excited and said, "Yes!"

They played together for a few hours, pretending they were explore the beautiful landscape. Eventually, Anna had to go home, so she waved goodbye to the cow and went back inside.

The End
