One day, a little gray squirrel was playing in the park. He liked to jump from tree to tree and find nuts to eat. He had a lot of fun with his friends, but he also liked to ask questions.

"Where do the nuts come from?" the squirrel asked his friend, the bird. The bird did not know the answer, so the squirrel asked the cat. The cat did not know the answer either. The squirrel wanted to find the answer, so he kept asking all his friends.

One day, the squirrel saw a big tree with lots of nuts. He asked the tree, "Where do the nuts come from?" The tree said, "I make the nuts for you and your friends to eat." The squirrel was so happy to find the answer. He told all his friends and they had a big party with lots of nuts to eat.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to read books, but she didn't have a bookcase to keep them in. One day, her mom bought her a bookcase, and Lily was very happy.

But then, Lily's little brother, Timmy, started knocking over her books and making a mess. Lily didn't like that, and she was very sad. She asked her mom to help her solve the problem.

Her mom suggested they make a deal with Timmy. He could play with Lily's toys if he promised to stop knocking over her books. Timmy agreed, and Lily was happy again. She finished organizing her books on the bookcase, and Timmy played with her toys. Everyone was happy in the end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and explore the world around her. One day, she went on a walk with her parent and they came across a big hill. 

Lily said, "I want to climb the hill, but it looks too steep. What should I do?" 

Her parent said, "I recommend that we take it slow and steady. We can hold hands and help each other up." 

Lily thought that was a smart idea and they started to climb the hill together. As they reached the top, Lily felt proud of herself for making it all the way up with her smart parent by her side.

Once upon a time, there was a young tree. It was tall and strong. Each day, it swayed in the wind and rustled its deep green leaves. 

One day, it noticed a velvet caterpillar slowly moving up one of its branches. The caterpillar was small and yellow. The tree asked the caterpillar, "What are you moving up my branch for?" The caterpillar replied, "I'm looking for a cozy place to rest and have a snack." 

The tree welcomed its new guest, and the caterpillar thanked it. Then the caterpillar moved into a corner of the branch and began to eat one of the leaves. Meanwhile, the tree watched and admired the young caterpillar. 

The caterpillar stayed with the tree until it was ready to move on, and then thanked the tree for its hospitality. The tree was happy to have looked after the young caterpillar, and sent it on its way with a gentle rustle of its leaves.

One day Sally and Sadie had a very nice day. They decided to fly their kite. The sky started to get dark, and then they heard a noise. 

Sadie said, "What is that noise?"

Sally said, "I don't know. Maybe its a tornado!"

The noise got louder and then the ground started shaking. They looked around and they saw a tornado rising towards the sky. They ran inside to hide.

After the tornado left, everything outside was dark and messy. Sally and Sadie looked out the window and saw everything was destroyed. But they were both happy that they were safe. 

The next day, the sun was up and everything was nice again. Sally and Sadie went outside and flew their kite again. They had lots of fun that day.

Once upon a time there was a cat called Andy. He was very envious of the other animals. Whenever they ate, he wanted to eat the same. Whenever they drank, he wanted to drink the same too.

One day, Andy saw a symbol on the wall. It was a beautiful bright triangle and it was winking at him. He was intrigued and wanted to know what it was. 

So Andy walked right up to the symbol and he started to lick it. He was so thirsty and he knew that the symbol could help him. As he licked it, he began to drink. He had never tasted anything so sweet before! 

Andy drank and drank, until he was full and refreshed. He was so happy and he thanked the symbol. From that day onward, Andy was always looking for symbols to drink from. He was so very happy he had found it!

Ben and Mia are friends. They like to play with toys and books. One day, Ben brings a new toy to Mia's house. It is a microscope. Ben says, "Look, Mia, this is a microscope. It can make small things big. Do you want to try?"

Mia nods and smiles. She likes to see new things. Ben puts a slide with a flower on the microscope. He turns a knob and the flower becomes bigger. Mia looks through the eye-piece and says, "Wow, Ben, the flower is so pretty. It has many colors and shapes. Can I see more?"

Ben nods and smiles. He puts another slide with a bug on the microscope. He turns another knob and the bug becomes bigger. Mia looks through the eye-piece and says, "Eek, Ben, the bug is so ugly. It has many legs and eyes. It is scary. I don't like it."

Ben laughs and says, "Don't be scared, Mia, it is just a toy bug. It can't hurt you. It is interesting to see how different things are. Do you want to see something else?"

Mia nods and says, "Yes, Ben, but something nice, not scary." Ben puts another slide with a candy on the microscope. He turns the knob and the candy becomes bigger. Mia looks through the eye-piece and says, "Mmm, Ben, the candy is so sweet. It has many crystals and colors. It looks yummy. Can I have some?"

Ben laughs and says, "Sorry, Mia, you can't eat the candy. It is too small. But I have a real candy for you. Here, take one. It is sweet and yummy. We can share."

Mia takes the candy and says, "Thank you, Ben, you are a good friend. I like your microscope. It is a fun toy. We can see many things with it. But I like candy more."

Ben and Mia eat the candy and laugh. They are happy. They like to play with the microscope and with each other. They are good friends.

Once upon a time, there was a boy that lived in a cold, dark place. He was alone and had no friends. He was always cold and he was sad.

One day, he found a lump of coal. He knew that coal was used to keep people warm. He carefully picked it up and held it tight.

Suddenly, something hard hit the boy on his back. He dropped the coal and started to cry. He turned around and saw a mean giant. The giant had slapped him with a big hand.

The boy was scared. He quickly grabbed the coal and ran. He ran hard and fast until he was out of the cold, dark place. He was never cold or sad ever again.

Once there was a little boy. He was very curious and liked to explore the world. He loved going to the park and watching things. One day he decided to try something new - he went to the train station! He was so excited to see the big, long train and its many bells.

As he was standing there, he could hear a soft whistling sound in the air. He looked around to see what it was and noticed an old man nearby, whistling a happy tune. The man was wearing overalls and a big hat. The little boy was so surprised!

He watched the old man for a while and was amazed at how serious he was when the train started. He was watching it very carefully and clapping his hands in time with the whistling. The little boy smiled, it was such a fun sight! 

When the train finally came to a stop, the old man smiled and waved goodbye. The little boy waved back and thought he might try to whistle too one day!

Lily and Max are twins. They like to play on the porch. The porch has a swing, a table, and some toys. Lily and Max have fun on the porch.

One day, Mom says, "Lily and Max, it is time to go inside. The porch is messy. You need to tidy up your toys."

Lily and Max do not want to go inside. They want to play more. They think of a plan.

They say to Mom, "Mom, can we show you something? We made a surprise for you on the porch."

Mom is curious. She says, "OK, show me your surprise."

Lily and Max take Mom to the porch. They point to the swing. They say, "Look, Mom, we made a nest for you. We used some leaves, some sticks, and some feathers. You can sit on the swing and pretend you are a bird."

Mom smiles. She says, "That is very sweet of you, Lily and Max. Thank you for the nest. But you still need to tidy up your toys. The porch is not a forest. The toys do not belong on the floor."

Lily and Max sigh. They say, "OK, Mom, we will tidy up our toys. But can we sit on the swing with you for a little bit?"

Mom says, "Sure, you can sit on the swing with me for a little bit. But then you have to tidy up your toys. Deal?"

Lily and Max say, "Deal!" They sit on the swing with Mom. They cuddle and giggle. They pretend they are birds. They are happy on the porch.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Alice and Betty. Alice loved to play in the snow. She made snowballs and snowmen, but she loved ice best of all.

Betty was jealous of how much fun Alice was having. She said to Alice, "Let's stay and play in the snow all day." Alice smiled and said yes.

The two friends played together in the snow until it was too cold. But before they went home, Alice wanted to play with the ice. She took a big chunk of ice and started to throw it around.

Betty couldn't help but feel jealous. "Let me stay and play with you," she begged. But Alice just kept playing with the ice.

Finally, Betty couldn't take it any longer. "Please, Alice," she said. "Can I stay with you and play with the ice, too?"

Alice smiled and said yes. The two friends had a wonderful time playing with the ice together and soon the sun was setting. Betty had so much fun that she forgot all about her jealous feelings. 

The two friends said goodbye and went home for the night. What a happy day!

One day, three wise little birds were out and about searching for something to eat. They flew high and they flew low, but they couldn't find anything. Suddenly, they spotted something interesting in the nearby park - jelly! The birds knew that jelly was yummy and they all wanted some. They swooped down to the ground and surrounded the jelly.

The birds all had an idea. One of them suggested that they wrap the jelly tightly with their wings so that they could take it back to their nest. All three of them agreed and they started to wrap the jelly together. They worked together, wrapping the jelly until it was completely covered.

Once the jelly was safely wrapped, the birds flew away with their yummy treat. Only one problem - it started to slip! But, these three wise birds were prepared and held it securely until they arrived back at the nest.

Once there, the birds unwrapped the jelly and shared it with their friends. Everyone was very happy and enjoyed the treat. The three birds were very proud of their hard work and wise planning, and all enjoyed the delicious jelly.

Once there was a boy named Tom. He was a very honest boy who always wanted to find where he belonged. One day, Tom went outside and it was raining really hard. Tom was scared because he saw that water was everywhere, flooding his street! 

Tom was so scared and didn't know what to do. He wanted to find somewhere safe to belong. Luckily, Tom's mom heard his cries and ran outside to help. She told Tom to hold her hand and she took him to a nearby shelter.

The shelter was warm and dry. Tom felt like he belonged there. He soon made lots of friends who played with him all day. They were all honest and kind, just like Tom. They had lots of fun playing until the rain stopped, and then it was time to go home.

Tom felt so happy. He realized that even though he had been scared of the flood, his mom had been there to help him and he had found a place where he belonged.

Once upon a time, there was a happy little girl. She loved playing outside in the fresh air.

One day while playing, she saw a mud puddle. She was so excited. She started jumping into the mud. Splat! Splat!

Suddenly, something thin and white slithered out of the mud. The little girl was surprised. 

She jumped out of the mud and said, â€œWhat is that?â€

The thin white thing looked up at her and said, â€œIâ€™m a little snake. I was taking a nap in the mud.â€

The little girl and the snake played together all day. They had so much fun! When it was time to go home, the little girl said goodbye and gave the snake a big hug. 

The snake said, â€œI had a great surprise today. It was fun!â€ 

The little girl smiled and said, â€œMe too! See you next time.â€ And she ran home all full of excitement.

Anna and Ben were playing in the park with their dolls. They liked to pretend they were doctors and nurses, and they had a small bag with bandages and stickers. They carried their dolls to a bench and put them on a blanket.

"Your doll is very sick," Anna said to Ben. "She needs a serious operation."

Ben nodded. He was worried about his doll. He hoped Anna could make her better. He watched as Anna took out a bandage and wrapped it around the doll's head.

"Good job, doctor," Ben said. "But what about her leg? It looks broken."

Anna frowned. She did not have any more bandages. She looked around and saw a sign on a fence. It said "Do not enter. Construction site. Danger."

Anna had an idea. She said to Ben, "I know where we can find more bandages. Come with me."

She grabbed her doll and ran to the fence. She did not see the big word "no" on the sign. She did not know what it meant. She thought it was part of the fence. She lifted the fence and crawled under it. Ben followed her.

They saw a big pile of wood and metal. They looked like bandages to them. They carried some of them to their dolls. They did not hear the loud noise of a truck coming closer.

The truck driver saw the fence was open. He was angry. He said, "Hey, you kids! What are you doing here? This is a law. You cannot be here. It is very dangerous. Get out now!"

Anna and Ben were scared. They dropped the wood and metal and ran back to the fence. They did not want to get in trouble. They did not want to get hurt. They carried their dolls and their bag and ran to their mom.

Their mom was waiting for them on a bench. She saw their faces and their dolls. She said, "What happened? Why are your dolls so dirty? And what are those things on their heads and legs?"

Anna and Ben told her what they did. They said they were sorry. They did not know it was a law. They did not know it was dangerous. They just wanted to help their dolls.

Their mom hugged them. She said, "I'm glad you are safe. But you have to be careful. You have to listen to the signs. They are there for a reason. They tell you what you can and cannot do. They are serious. Do you understand?"

Anna and Ben nodded. They said they understood. They said they would not do it again. They said they loved their mom. Their mom smiled. She said she loved them too. She said they could go home and clean their dolls. She said they could play doctor and nurse again. But only with bandages and stickers.

One day, a boy and a girl were playing in the park. They saw a big bush with red berries. The boy said, "Let's split the berries and eat them. They look yummy." The girl said, "No, we don't know if they are good or bad. Maybe they are sour or bitter or make us sick. We should ask mom or dad first."

But the boy did not listen. He was foolish and greedy. He ran to the bush and picked some berries. He split them with his teeth and put them in his mouth. He made a face and spat them out. They were very sour and bitter and made his tongue hurt. He cried and said, "Ow, ow, ow! These berries are bad! They hurt my mouth!"

The girl ran to him and said, "I told you not to eat them. You were foolish and did not listen. Now you have to drink some water and wash your mouth. Come, I will help you." She took his hand and led him to a fountain. She gave him some water and said, "Next time, listen to me and be careful. Don't eat things you don't know."

The boy said, "I'm sorry, I was foolish and greedy. Thank you for helping me. You are a good friend. Next time, I will listen to you and be careful. Don't eat things I don't know." He hugged her and said, "You are welcome. You are a good friend too. Let's go and play something else." They smiled and ran to the swings. They had fun and forgot about the bad berries. They learned a lesson and never ate things they didn't know again.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She went to camp with her friends. They played outside and had fun. When it was time to go inside, Lily's mom said, "Make sure you clean up your room." 

Lily and her friends picked up their toys and put them away. They were happy to help. After they cleaned, they sat down to talk. They told each other stories about their day. They laughed and had a good time. 

At night, Lily went to bed feeling tired but happy. She was happy because she had fun with her friends and helped clean up. She was excited to go back to camp the next day and talk with her friends again. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play dress up with her dolls. One day, she went to the park and saw a boy who looked sad. She asked him, "Why are you sad?" The boy said, "I lost my toy." Lily felt kind and wanted to help the boy. She said, "Let's look for your toy together!" 

They searched and searched but couldn't find the toy. Lily saw that the boy was still sad. She thought of a way to make him smile. She said, "Let's play dress up! We can be pirates and find treasure!" The boy smiled and said, "Okay!" They both dressed up and pretended to be pirates. They found a treasure chest filled with candy and toys. The boy was happy again and gave Lily a big smile. They became friends and played together every day.

Mama and Papa prayed every morning. They prayed for good things and a normal day.

One morning, Mama opened a big book and took out a piece of leather. She said, â€œPapa, look what I found! We can make a toy for the children to play with.â€

Papa looked at it and said, â€œThatâ€™s a good idea. Letâ€™s make something special.â€ He smiled at Mama, then they started to pray.

Mama and Papa made a special leather toy. It looked like a bear. They named it Roary.

The children were so happy. They laughed and hugged Roary.

The next morning, Mama and Papa prayed again. â€œThank you for giving us a normal, happy day,â€ they said.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to sing and dance all day long. One day, she went to the park and met a boy named Jack. Jack said, "Hello, do you want to play with me?"

Lily said, "Yes, I want to play. What do you want to play?"

Jack said, "Let's play hide and seek."

Lily said, "Great idea! I love to play hide and seek."

They played for a while and then Lily said, "Do you want to sing a song with me?"

Jack said, "Sure, what song do you want to sing?"

Lily said, "Let's sing the song about zero. It goes like this: Zero, zero, nothing there. Zero, zero, everywhere!"

They sang the song together and had a great time. From that day on, Lily and Jack became best friends and played together every day.

Once there was a girl, who was three years old. She was very brave and wanted to explore the world. One day she decided to go into the forest near her house. She ran around, exploring the trees and flowers, until she came across an old dead tree. She decided to stay by it. She noticed a tie on it's trunk. She wondered what it was doing there. She slowly reached out to touch it, but suddenly the wind blew and it shook. That scared her so she ran all the way back home, but she still thought about the tie all the time. She imagined many stories about why the tie was there, but one thing she knew for sure, it wanted her to stay away from it.

Once upon a time there was a hunter. He wanted to catch a bear today so he got up early in the morning and prepared his modern tools and equipment. He was all ready, he just had to hurry. 

The hunter began walking through the woods. He had been walking for over an hour, when suddenly he heard a noise. He stopped, listened and heard it again. It was the sound of a big bear!

The hunter picked up his pace and started hurrying. Faster and Faster. 

The hunter soon saw the bear and quickly yelled, "Stop! I'm a hunter and I have to catch you!" 

The bear looked at the hunter and shouted back, " I won't be caught easily. Hurry and you might still get me!" 

The hunter ran faster and faster, trying to outrun the bear, but it was no use. The bear was too fast. 
In the end, the hunter had to slow to a walk and go back home. He knew he had to come up with a better plan before he could catch the bear.

Tom and Mia were hungry. They wanted to eat something sweet and juicy. They saw a big bowl of fruit on the table. There were apples, bananas, oranges and grapes.

"Can we have some fruit, Mom?" Tom asked.

"Of course, my loves. You can have one each. But wash your hands first," Mom said.

Tom and Mia ran to the sink and washed their hands. Then they came back to the table and picked their fruit. Tom chose an apple and Mia chose a banana.

They peeled and bit their fruit. They made happy sounds.

"Mmm, this apple is so good. It tastes like sunshine," Tom said.

"Yum, this banana is so soft. It tastes like cream," Mia said.

They ate their fruit until there was nothing left. They felt full and happy.

"Thank you, Mom, for the fruit. It was delicious," Tom and Mia said.

"You're welcome, my loves. I'm glad you liked it. Fruit is good for you. It makes you strong and healthy," Mom said.

She hugged them and kissed them. They hugged and kissed her back. They loved each other very much.

Once there was a mommy and a daddy. The mommy was very busy. She was running around everywhere. One day she had many errands to do. 

The mommy left her house early in the morning. She went to the grocery store, the post office and the bank. She even stopped at the pet store. She was having a very busy day!

On her last stop, the mommy tried to catch the bus. But she wasn't fast enough. The bus left without her. She had to find another way to get home. 

The mommy decided to take a taxi. But the taxi driver made a wrong turn. Suddenly, the mommy was in the hospital! It was very busy there. 

The mommy was afraid. But the doctor and nurses helped her. They made her feel happier. They told her everything was okay.

After a while, the mommy was able to catch a ride home. She felt relieved. She was just glad to be back home safe!

Mila and her dog Spot liked to play in the park. They ran and jumped and chased each other. Spot was a cheerful dog. He wagged his tail and licked Mila's face.

One day, Mila and Spot saw a flea on Spot's fur. The flea was tiny and black. It jumped from one spot to another. Mila tried to catch it, but it was too fast.

"Stop, flea!" Mila said. "You are not nice. You make Spot itch."

The flea did not listen. It laughed and said, "You can't catch me. I am the best jumper in the park. I can fill your dog with bites."

Mila was angry. She did not like the flea. She had an idea. She picked up a jar and ran after the flea. She waited for the flea to jump, and then she put the jar over it.

"Ha! I got you, flea!" Mila said. "Now you can't bite Spot anymore."

The flea was sad. It did not like the jar. It was dark and small. It could not jump or laugh.

"Please, let me go," the flea said. "I am sorry. I will not bite Spot again."

Mila thought for a moment. She felt sorry for the flea. She did not want to be mean. She lifted the jar and let the flea go.

"Thank you, Mila," the flea said. "You are kind. I will find another place to live."

Mila smiled and hugged Spot. Spot licked her face. He was happy. He did not itch anymore.

They went home, feeling cheerful. They had a good day in the park.

Once upon a time there was a harmless lady. She went on an adventure everyday and today she was walking through the forest. Suddenly she heard a noise that sounded like it was coming from the bushes. 

The lady peered inside the bush and saw a cute little bunny. Every time the bunny saw the lady he would run away. But the lady was patient so she just smiled and waited. After a while the bunny got closer and closer until the lady could touch him. 

The bunny then began to repeat the same thing over and over again. The lady thought it was so cute so she started to repeat the same thing back. Together they said â€œHop hop hop down the road!â€ 

They played together for a while until the lady had to go home. As she said goodbye the harmless lady waved to the bunny before starting her journey back.

Once upon a time there were two brothers who loved playing together. One day they were playing in their garden. Suddenly one brother saw a prune and decided to eat it. But his brother said the prune was his and snatched it away. The other brother was so angry that he pushed his brother to the ground.

Mama was very angry and told the boy that he had to be punished for his bad behaviour. She asked him to say sorry to his brother. The boy was very sorry and gave his brother a hug. 

Mama was happy that he had said sorry, but she knew he had still done wrong so she told him he must sit in the naughty chair for five minutes. The boy was very sad but he saw that Mama was trying to help him and he said okay. 

After five minutes the boy got out of the naughty chair and Mama hugged him and told him that she loved him. They all had a happy day and remembered what a bad thing it was to push his brother.

Ralph was playing in the garden one day when it started to thunder. His mum came out and told him it was time to go inside the house. Ralph wanted to stay outside but she told him no. 

Ralph was feeling very spoiled and didn't want to listen to his mum so he ignored her and stayed in the garden. It was raining heavily and the thunder was getting louder and louder. Ralph didn't want to go inside, he wanted to keep playing. 

Suddenly, his mum shouted: "Ralph, get in the house now!" Ralph was so scared of the thunder he got up and quickly ran inside the house. 

His mum said: "Ralph, when mommy tells you something you must listen, otherwise you can get into dangerous situations!" 

Ralph felt a bit spoiled and said: "But I wanted to keep playing!" His mum replied: "It's important to listen so we can keep you safe."

Ralph learned that day that it's important to listen to his mum, even if he felt spoiled.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and explore the world around her. One day, she found a shiny rock and put it in her pocket to keep as a memory.

As she was playing, she saw a big dog running towards her. The dog looked friendly, but Lily's mom warned her to be careful around dogs she didn't know. Lily remembered her mom's warning and stayed still until the dog ran away.

Later that day, Lily wanted to show her shiny rock to her friend, Timmy. She reached into her pocket, but the rock was gone! She realized that she must have been careless and lost it while playing. She was sad, but her mom reminded her that memories are in our hearts, not just in things we keep.

Once upon a time, there lived a strong little girl. She was only three years old, but she was very brave, and she loved to explore.

One day, she found something very strange. It was a big, shiny shoe! She didn't understand what it was, and she was very curious, so she picked it up and put it on her foot. It fit perfectly!

The little girl was very happy and she ran around her house, wearing the shiny shoe. It felt strong on her foot, and she liked it a lot. She ran outside to show her friends and they were very surprised to see the strong shoe on her foot.

The little girl and her friends laughed and played outside, wearing their strong shoes. They all felt brave and happy, now that they knew what the strange shoes were. 

From then on, the little girl and her friends loved wearing their strong shoes! They felt happy and understood that exploring new things can be exciting.

Tom and Anna are friends. They like to play together in Anna's room. Anna has a big carpet with many colors and shapes. Tom thinks the carpet is attractive. He likes to look at it and touch it.

One day, Anna has an idea. She says to Tom, "Let's spread the carpet on the floor and pretend it is a magic carpet. We can fly to different places and have fun." Tom likes the idea. He says, "Yes, let's do that. Where do you want to go first?"

Anna thinks for a moment. She says, "I want to go to the zoo. I want to see the animals and hear them make noises." Tom nods. He says, "Me too. I like the zoo. I like the monkeys and the lions and the elephants." They both sit on the carpet and hold hands. They close their eyes and imagine they are flying to the zoo.

They pretend they see the animals and talk to them. They make animal noises and laugh. They have a lot of fun. They forget about everything else. They feel happy and free on the magic carpet. They are the best friends in the world.

Once there was a happy little boy who loved to whistle. He would whistle while he walked and while he played. One day he decided to go on a walk and as he walked, he kept on whistling. 

He saw a beautiful flower and smiled. He put his face very close to the flower and smiled even bigger. He smelled the sweet perfume of the flower and began to whistle a special tune. 

The birds heard the tunes he whistled and were so happy, they all joined in with their own whistles. Even the bees buzzed in harmony. 

But soon, the boy started feeling a bit bored. He thought he would try something else, so he started skipping and jumping instead. He pretended he was a frog and hopped all the way home. 

Before he knew it, he was home. He was happy and singing a different tune. He didn't mind being bored for a minute because it made his little adventure even more fun!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved sitting by the fireplace in her cozy house. One day, she noticed that the fireplace looked dirty and old. 

Lily asked her mom, "Can we clean the fireplace, please?" 

Her mom said, "Yes, we can restore it to make it look new and shiny again." 

Lily was very clever and helped her mom clean the fireplace. They scrubbed and wiped until it sparkled like new. 

Lily said, "Look how pretty it is now! Let's light a fire and enjoy it." 

Her mom smiled and said, "You're right, Lily. It's much better now." And they sat by the fireplace, feeling warm and happy.

Mummy and Daddy were very happy. They had a new car and were going for a drive. They opened the door and got into the car. Suddenly, Mummy said: "Oh no! I forgot the brush!" Daddy said, "It's ok. We can get it later."

But Mummy was not happy. She said: "No, I need the brush right now!" So they got out of the car and went back into the house to get the brush.

When they got back to the car, they saw that someone had taken it! Daddy was angry and tried to find the car thief, but he was gone.

Mummy and Daddy were very sad. They had lost the car they were so happy to get, and they didn't know what to do.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sarah. She was very brave, but sometimes she was a bit anxious. One day, Sarah decided to go to the theater. She had never been to a theater before, so she was extra anxious.

When Sarah arrived, she noticed that the theater was a bit cold. She began to shiver a bit. Suddenly, a kind theater worker saw Sarah. She gave Sarah a cozy blanket so she would not be cold. Even with the blanket, Sarah was still a bit afraid. But soon enough, Sarah's fear faded away and she was able to enjoy the show!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily went to the park with her mommy. While they were walking, Lily saw a band playing music. She loved the music and asked her mommy if they could stay and listen. Her mommy said yes and they sat down on the grass.

Lily watched the people dancing and clapping their hands. She wanted to dance too but was too shy. Suddenly, a little boy came up to her and said, "Do you want to dance with me?" Lily smiled and said yes. The boy took her hand and they danced together.

Lily felt so happy and said to the boy, "Thank you for holding my hand. You're a perfect dance partner!" The boy smiled and said, "You're welcome. I like dancing with you too." From that day on, Lily and the boy became good friends and always danced together whenever they saw the band playing at the park.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Jack. Jack loved playing with his toys and going on adventures. One day, Jack's mom asked him to go to the store to buy some milk. Jack was excited to go on this adventure all by himself.

As Jack walked to the store, he saw a man in a black mask running away from a store with a bag in his hand. Jack knew something was not right. When Jack arrived at the store, he saw that the man had stolen a toy from the store. The store owner asked Jack if he saw the man's number plate. Jack remembered the number and told the store owner.

When Jack returned home, he saw the man in the black mask walking down the street. Jack felt guilty for not telling his mom about the man earlier. Jack quickly ran to his mom and told her everything. His mom was proud of Jack for being brave and for helping the store owner. From that day on, Jack always made sure to zip his lips and tell his mom if he saw anything suspicious.

Alice was excited. She was going on a trip with her family! She couldn't wait to go exploring.

They all got into the car and drove off. Along the way, Alice watched out the window as the scenery changed.

When they arrived, Alice looked around. Everything was so different and new.

Alice and her family got out of the car and went to check-in at the airport. Alice saw lots of people with their luggage. She helped her family carry their suitcases over to the desk.

Soon, it was time to board the plane. Alice was nervous. She hung on to her dad's hand tight. But once the plane was in the air, she felt excited again. She enjoyed looking down at the clouds and watching the world below.

When the plane landed, Alice was relieved. She was so happy to surrender her troubles and start her adventure.

Once upon a time there was a man named Jack. Every day, Jack went for a jog. One day, Jack was jogging and he smelled something spicy. It smelled really good! He followed the smell and came to a yummy shop. He went inside and saw there were lots of different spicy treats. Jack recognized one of the treats. It was his favorite, a yummy spicy cookie! He asked for it and the shopkeeper gave it to him. Jack thanked the shopkeeper and went on his way. Jack enjoyed his yummy spicy treat as he jogged back home. He was very happy he had been able to recognize the delicious treat!

The night was dark. Jack looked out his window and saw the stars shining. He wanted to stand on the stars! 

He opened the window and started to climb out. He stood on the windowsill, but then he started to wobble.

The wind was blowing and Jack began to fall. He screamed and flapped his hands, but he was still falling.

He landed in a big pile of leaves! It was dark but Jack could see the stars twinkling from the ground. Jack smiled. He was happy to be able to stand on the leaves and look at the stars.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to stand on her tiptoes and look out the window. One day, her mommy said she could go outside and play. Lily was so excited! She ran outside and saw her friends. They asked if she could play with them, and her mommy said it was okay. She was permitted to play with her friends. They played and laughed and had so much fun together. When it was time to go back inside, Lily was sad because she didn't want the fun to end. But she knew she could play with her friends again tomorrow. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little lamb named Lily. Lily had a white coat made of soft wool. She loved to play with her friends in the green fields. One day, Lily's friend, a sheep named Sally, became jealous of Lily's wool. Sally wanted to have wool as soft and white as Lily's.

Lily didn't understand why Sally was jealous. She tried to explain to Sally that all sheep have wool, but Sally didn't listen. One day, Lily decided to reveal a secret to Sally. She told Sally that her wool was special because she ate lots of healthy grass and drank lots of water. Sally realized that she needed to take better care of herself to have soft and white wool like Lily's.

From that day on, Sally and Lily played together happily in the green fields. Sally was no longer jealous of Lily's wool and they both enjoyed running and jumping together. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Mia. Mia was three years old and she loved to be independent. One day Mia was feeling curious and she wanted to explore. She saw a mirror on the wall and walked up to it. 

Mia put her hand on the cold mirror and started to rub it. As she rubbed, she saw fog appear on the glass and wondered what would happen. She kept rubbing until the fog cleared and suddenly Mia could see her face in the mirror. 

She looked into the mirror and smiled. Mia liked what she could see and the more she rubbed, the more she could see her reflection. She rubbed the mirror with her soft hands, then waved her hand at her reflection and giggled. Mia had lots of fun rubbing the mirror. 

When Mia's mom came home, she saw Mia with a big smile on her face looking into the mirror and enjoying her new discovery. She was proud that her daughter was so independent and could find joy in simple things like a mirror. 

Mia and her mom said goodbye to the mirror and went off to explore something else. Mia was happy to be so independent and she knew that it was all thanks to the special mirror.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. He had a soft toy that he liked a lot. The toy was a cute dog. Tim would play with the dog every day. He named the dog Spot.

One day, Tim went to camp with his mom and dad. He took Spot with him. They played games, sang songs, and had fun. Tim was very happy at camp. He loved to run and jump with Spot.

But, one day, Tim lost Spot. He looked and looked, but could not find him. Tim was very sad. He cried and cried. His mom and dad tried to help him find Spot, but they could not. Tim went home from camp without Spot. He missed his soft toy dog very much.

Once upon a time, there was a group of little bunnies. One of the bunnies was different from the rest, for he was much tougher than the rest! He was brave, strong and daring.

Every day, the bunnies would hop around in the meadow, playing and having fun. All the other bunnies were scared to try any daring jumps, but the tough bunny could hop higher than the rest.

The other bunnies began to get jealous of how tough the bunny was and they started pushing him around. The tough bunny tried to stay brave and hop around but the group kept bullying him.

One day, the tough bunny decided enough was enough and he loudly declared, "I may be different, but I will still be brave and keep hopping!"

The other bunnies realised their mistake, apologising for their meanness and accepting the tough bunny for who he was.

From then on, each bunny was accepted for who they were and the group hopped happily together!

The moral of this story is that it is important to accept everyone for who they are, no matter how different. Everyone should be accepted and celebrated for their unique qualities!

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. He had a large glove that he loved to wear when he played outside. One day, Timmy accidentally tore a hole in his glove while playing with his friends. 

Timmy's friend Billy saw the hole and said, "Oh no! Your glove is broken. Can you repair it?" 

Timmy replied, "I don't know how to repair it. I'll just have to ask my mom." 

When Timmy got home, he showed his mom the hole in his glove. She said she would try to repair it, but it might not look as good as new. 

The next day, Timmy went back outside to play with his friends. But when he tried to catch a ball, the hole in his glove got bigger and the ball went flying away. Timmy was sad and his friends didn't want to play with him anymore because he couldn't catch the ball. 

Timmy learned that it's important to take care of your things and to ask for help when you need it.

Lila and Ben are friends. They like to play with toys. They have a big box of toys. They can find many things in the box.

One day, they want to play with paper and crayons. They look in the box. They see a file. The file has many papers inside. Some papers are white. Some papers are blue. Some papers are yellow.

"Look, Ben, I found a file!" Lila says. "We can use the papers to draw!"

"Good, Lila, let's draw!" Ben says. "I want a blue paper. You can have a yellow paper."

They take the papers and the crayons. They sit on the floor. They start to draw. Lila draws a sun. Ben draws a fish. They are happy.

They draw for a long time. They use many crayons. They make many pictures. The file is empty. The floor is full of papers.

"Wow, Lila, we made a lot of pictures!" Ben says. "They are very nice!"

"Yes, Ben, they are very nice!" Lila says. "But we have no more papers. The file is empty. The game is over."

They look at each other. They are sad. They want to play more.

Then, they hear a voice. It is Mom. She comes in the room. She sees the papers on the floor. She smiles.

"Hello, Lila and Ben!" Mom says. "What are you doing?"

"We are drawing, Mom!" Lila and Ben say. "But we have no more papers. The file is empty. The game is over."

Mom picks up the file. She opens it. She shows them something. It is a surprise.

"Look, Lila and Ben!" Mom says. "The file is not empty. There is something else inside. It is a book. A book with many stories. Do you want to read it?"

Lila and Ben are happy. They love books. They love stories. They nod.

"Yes, Mom, we want to read it!" Lila and Ben say.

Mom sits on the couch. She puts the book on her lap. She invites Lila and Ben to join her. They cuddle with Mom. They feel warm.

Mom opens the book. She reads the first story. It is about a rabbit and a turtle. Lila and Ben listen. They laugh. They ask questions. They imagine.

The game is not over. The game is different. The game is fun.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was very sleepy and wanted to take a nap, but she couldn't fall asleep. She imagined a world where she could sleep soundly.

Suddenly, she heard a whistle coming from outside. She got up and looked out the window. It was her friend, Billy. He had a big smile on his face and said, "Hi Lily, do you want to come play with me?"

Lily rubbed her eyes and yawned. "I'm too sleepy to play right now," she said. "But can you whistle me a lullaby so I can fall asleep?"

Billy nodded and started whistling a soft tune. Lily closed her eyes and listened to the beautiful sound. Soon, she was fast asleep and dreaming about all the fun adventures she would have with Billy when she woke up.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her shiny mirror. She looked at herself in the mirror every day and smiled. One day, Lily was eager to show her mirror to her friends. She ran outside to find them. 

When she found her friends, she showed them her shiny mirror. They were amazed by how it could reflect the sun and shine so bright. They all wanted to play with the mirror too. So, they took turns holding it and looking at themselves. 

Lily was happy to share her shiny mirror with her friends. They all had fun playing with it and seeing themselves in it. When it was time to go home, Lily hugged her mirror tightly and said goodbye to her friends. She couldn't wait to show it to them again tomorrow.

When they arrived, the boy was amazed. Everywhere he looked, there were bright colourful packages and big bins full of food! The mom asked him what he wanted to get. The boy smiled and said "I want one of those nice boxes full of apples!"

Once upon a time there were two best friends, Bob and Joe. They were always so happy and had a lot of fun together. One day the two friends decided to have a race in the park. Bob was very determined to win and Joe wanted to do his best too.

Bob and Joe starting running and soon Bob was ahead. He was getting closer and closer to the finish line and Joe was becoming more and more frustrated. But soon Bob crossed the finish line and won the race. He was so proud and excited to have won the trophy!

Joe sadly looked down at the ground, feeling a bit sad he hadn't won. Bob noticed this and asked his friend, â€œWhy are you so sad Joe?â€ 

Joe replied, â€œIâ€™m just a bit frustrated that I didn't win.â€ Bob smiled and said, â€œItâ€™s ok! At least you tried your best. Here, you can have the trophy!â€ Joe was so happy and smiled his biggest smile.

Sara and Ben are having lunch with Mom. They have sandwiches and juice. Mom gives them each a napkin to wipe their mouths.

"Thank you, Mom," Sara says. She puts the napkin on her lap.

"Thank you, Mom," Ben says. He tries to put the napkin on his head.

"Ben, that's not where the napkin goes," Mom says. "The napkin is for your mouth, not your head."

"But I want to wear it like a hat," Ben says. He likes hats. He has many hats at home.

"Sorry, Ben, but the napkin is too small to be a hat. It doesn't fit your head. It will fall off," Mom says.

Ben looks at the napkin. It is white and square. It is not like his hats. His hats are colorful and round. He tries to make the napkin round, but it tears.

"Oh no, Ben, you ripped the napkin," Mom says. "Now you don't have a napkin or a hat."

Ben feels sad. He likes the napkin. He likes hats. He wants both.

"Mom, can I have another napkin, please?" Ben asks.

"OK, Ben, but only if you promise to use it for your mouth, not your head," Mom says. She gives him another napkin.

"I promise, Mom," Ben says. He wipes his mouth with the napkin. He smiles.

"Good boy, Ben," Mom says. She smiles too.

Sara and Ben finish their lunch. They have a good time with Mom. They have napkins and sandwiches and juice. They don't need hats.

Once upon a time there was a curious little girl. She loved to explore and build things. One day she went on a walk and found something unusual. It was a big horn! She thought it was so cool.

She decided to take the horn home with her. There she built a special horn house for it, with a door and windows. She played with the horn every day, making more and more noise until she had made all sorts of unusual sounds.

Every day the little girl built something new with the horn. She was so happy and felt so proud of her creations. It was a lot of fun!

Soon enough, the little girl had built a special home for her horn and they were best friends. Every day they played together and created new and unusual sounds. It was a happy time!

Once upon a time, there was a kind rabbit. The rabbit liked to move around and play with his friends. One day, the rabbit saw a big rainbow in the sky. He was so happy to see all the pretty colors. 

The rabbit wanted to get closer to the rainbow, so he started to move towards it. As he got closer, he saw that the rainbow was very far away. The rabbit was sad because he couldn't reach it. 

But then, the rabbit remembered how kind his friends were. He asked them for help, and they all worked together to make a rainbow for the rabbit to play with. The rabbit was so happy and grateful for his kind friends. From that day on, he knew that he didn't need to reach the big rainbow in the sky because he had his own special rainbow made just for him.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was very happy because today was her first day of class. She put on her new dress and said to her mom, "I am ready for class!"

Her mom replied, "You look very pretty, Lily. I hope you have a good day."

When Lily arrived at class, she saw a girl who had a lot of toys. She said, "Wow, you have a lot of toys. You must be wealthy!"

The girl smiled and said, "Yes, I am very lucky. Would you like to play with me?"

Lily shook her head and said, "Yes, please!" They played together and had a lot of fun. At the end of the day, Lily said, "I had a great day in class. I made a new friend!"

Once upon a time, there was a rabbit named Skip. Skip loved to hop. He hopped everywhere he went. One day, Skip hopped over to his friend, Turtle.

"Hi, Turtle!" he said.

"Hi, Skip!" said Turtle.

The two friends smiled at each other. Then Turtle said,

"Let's have a hopping race!"

Skip was so excited. He said,

"Yes! Let's hop!"

They both took off with fierce speed. Skip hopped with all his might and soon he was ahead of Turtle. But as he got close to the finish line, he noticed a big hand right in his way.

He stopped and looked up. It was a fierce-looking monster! He was so scared that he forgot to hop and lost the race.

Turtle ran up to him and said,

"That's okay, Skip. It's better to be safe than sorry."

Skip nodded and smiled. He was glad that he stopped when he did. From then on, Skip never forgot to be careful when he hopped.

Once upon a time, a small girl named Robin was walking through the forest. Suddenly, she saw something sparkly in the bushes. She jumped over, to see what it was. Suddenly, she revealed a pretty ornament. It was made of shiny gold and silver. Robin thought it was so neat, she decided to take it home with her.

When Robin arrived home, she carefully placed the ornament she found on the kitchen table. Her mom and dad were very surprised to see it. They asked where she had found it, but Robin couldn't remember exactly. The mysterious ornament was from an unknown place.

Robin's mom and dad decided to hang the ornament on their Christmas tree. Every night, when Robin looked at the tree, the shiny ornament sparkled and sparkled. She was very happy that she had found the ornament and it was now part of her family.

Once upon a time, there was a bridge. It was a noisy bridge. All the cars drove over it, honking and beeping.

One day, a big family crossed the bridge on their way to the park. They wanted to have fun!

When they got to the park, the family found a happy place to play. There were swings, slides and other fun things.

After the family finished their picnic lunch, the kids started to play a game. They ran around, chasing each other and laughing.

At the end of their fun day, the parents called the kids together. They kissed each and every one of them. They said goodbye and crossed the noisy bridge again.

Tom and Lily were playing in the park. They saw a big box under a tree. It was brown and had a lock on it.

"What is in the box?" Lily asked.

"I don't know. Maybe it is a mystery," Tom said.

They wanted to open the box and see what was inside. They tried to pull the lock, but it was too hard. They looked for a key, but they could not find one.

"Maybe we can ask someone for help," Lily said.

"No, I want to open it by myself," Tom said. He refused to ask anyone for help. He was stubborn and curious.

He saw a big rock near the box. He had an idea. He picked up the rock and threw it at the lock. He hoped it would break the lock and open the box.

But the rock bounced back and hit Tom in the head. He fell down and cried. He was hurt and bleeding.

Lily was scared and ran to get help. She saw a man with a uniform and a badge. He was a police officer.

"Help, help, my friend is hurt!" Lily shouted.

The police officer followed Lily to the box. He saw Tom on the ground and the rock and the lock.

"What happened here?" he asked.

Lily told him what they did. The police officer was angry and shocked.

"This is not a mystery box. This is evidence from a crime scene. You should not touch it. It is dangerous and illegal. You are in big trouble," he said.

He called an ambulance for Tom and a backup for the box. He took Lily to his car and waited for her parents.

Tom and Lily learned a hard lesson. They should not be nosy and disobey the rules. They should not play with mysterious things. They should ask for help when they need it. They should be careful and safe.

Once upon a time, there was a little boat that loved to sail on the big blue sea. The boat was made of wood and had a white sail that would catch the wind and take it wherever it wanted to go. One day, the boat sailed to a faraway island where it saw a tall pine tree. The tree was so tall that it touched the sky! The boat was amazed by the tree's beauty and decided to stay there for a while.

But as the day turned into night, the sky turned pale and the wind started to blow very hard. The boat tried to sail away, but the wind was too strong and it couldn't move. Suddenly, a big wave came and hit the boat, making it crash into the pine tree. The boat was broken and it couldn't sail anymore. The little boat was very sad because it couldn't sail on the big blue sea anymore.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys, especially her dolls and teddy bear. One day, Lily went to the park with her mommy and daddy. There, she saw a big castle made of sand. She was so happy and wanted to play in it.

Lily was sad that she couldn't play in the castle, but she was happy to play with her dolls and teddy bear. She hugged them tightly and felt comforted. She knew that even though she couldn't play in the castle, she still had her favorite toys to hold and play with.

Steve smiled, pulling a small box out of his pocket. "This is for you. Please take it home with you."

Emily opened the box to find a beautiful necklace inside. The necklace had a lively butterfly charm.

"Thank you, Steve," she said, excitedly.

Emily put the necklace on and went home with a happy heart. She couldn't wait to tell her parents what the strange man had done. But little did she know, this stranger would soon come back into her life in

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sue. She had a big, clear jar. One day, Sue found a strange drink. It was called poison. Sue did not know what poison was.

Sue's mom saw her with the poison. She told Sue that poison was bad. Sue should not have it. Sue's mom took the poison away. She put it on a high shelf.

Sue was sad, but she still had her clear jar. She filled it with pretty rocks and flowers. Sue was happy again. She learned that some things are not good to have.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with paper and make things like airplanes and hats. One day, she was playing with her paper airplane when her brother, Max, came into the room.

"We're just playing with paper airplanes," Lily said. 

"That's okay, just try to keep it a little quieter," their mom said. 

Lily and Max continued to play quietly and zoom their paper airplanes through the air. They had so much fun together!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a brother named Tom. Tom was a new brother. Lily was very happy to have a new brother. She wanted to visit him every day.

One day, Lily went to visit Tom. Tom was in his room. Lily opened the door to Tom's room. She saw Tom in his bed. He was very small. Lily wanted to play with her new brother.

Lily tried to play with Tom, but he was too small. She tried to give him a toy, but he didn't want it. Lily was sad. She wanted to have fun with her brother, but he was too new.

Lily went to her mom and asked, "When can I play with Tom?" Her mom said, "Tom is very new, so you have to wait." Lily didn't like waiting. She was very sad.

The next day, Lily tried to visit Tom again. But this time, Tom was not in his room. Lily asked her mom, "Where is Tom?" Her mom said, "Tom is gone. He was too new and too small." Lily was very sad. She didn't get to play with her new brother.

Once upon a time, there was a happy little girl. Her name was Lola and she was three years old.

Lola lived close to the beach, so most days she would go and play by the sea. Today was no different and the weather was warm and sunny.

Lola found a bucket and filled it up with sand. Then she started to walk toward the edge of the ocean, with the bucket full of sand.

"Careful, Lola!" her dad said behind her. "You don't want to spill it!" 

But it was too late. The bucket was already wet and all her sand was soaking into the sea.

Lola was disappointed, but then an event happened. A huge wave came and soaked her from head to toe!

Lola's dad laughed and the two of them played in the waves for a long time, until Lola was all soggy and it was time to go home.

Once, there was a group of children who went for a walk in the woods. Along their walk, the kids noticed something shiny and smooth on the ground. It turned out to be a beautiful ornament! One of the kids picked it up and said, "I'm going to keep this ornament." The other kids quickly mentioned that it might be someone else's, and they should put it back. The child who had picked it up agreed and placed the ornament back on the ground. As the children continued on their walk, they heard someone laugh. Looking up, they saw an old lady waving at them, who said, "Thank you for finding my ornament and returning it to me. I'm so glad you had the kind hearts to do the right thing!". 

The moral is that doing the right thing is always the best thing. Even if it doesn't seem like it has a reward, it always pays off in the end. The children had some foreshadowing from their friends to do the right thing and that paid off when the old woman expressed her gratitude. The children were happy to have done a good thing, and the old lady was happily reunited with her smooth and shiny ornament.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who loved to pick different things from the garden. She spent her day eagerly picking flowers and leaves. One day she stumbled upon something different from the usual things she picked. This was a pattern!

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play the drums. He would bang on them all day long. One day, Timmy's friend came over to play. Timmy was so excited to show his friend his drums. 

But, Timmy was careless. He pushed his friend too hard and his friend fell down. Timmy felt very bad. He realized that he needed to be more careful when he played with his friends.
