The bull showed him around the ranch and introduced him to all of the colorful animals living there. Henry had so much fun, he decided to come back to the ranch often to play with the bull and explore.

Once upon a time, there was a big lion in the jungle. He liked to roar very loudly so that all the animals could hear him. One day, a little girl came to the jungle. She had a pretty bracelet on her wrist. The lion saw the bracelet and thought it was very nice. He asked the little girl if he could wear it. She said yes and put the bracelet on the lion's paw. The lion was very happy and felt mild and calm wearing the bracelet. From that day on, the lion would wear the bracelet every time he wanted to feel mild and calm.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He loved to play outside and get dirty. One day, he came inside with his clothes all muddy and his face covered in dirt.

His mom saw him and said, "Timmy, you're filthy! You need to take a bath." Timmy didn't want to take a bath, but he knew he had to listen to his mom.

After his bath, Timmy went to talk to his dad. "Daddy, thank you for my new toy," Timmy said. His dad smiled and said, "You're welcome, Timmy. Now be careful with that razor on it."

Timmy didn't know what a razor was, but he knew he had to be careful. He played with his new toy and stayed clean for the rest of the day.

Tom and Sue were friends who liked to play in the big house. The big house had many rooms and doors and stairs. One day, they found a new door that was locked. They wanted to see what was inside.

"Maybe there is a treasure or a toy or a cake," Tom said.

"Or maybe there is a monster or a trap or a ghost," Sue said.

They looked for a key, but they could not find one. Then they saw a hole in the wall. It was big enough for them to crawl through.

"Let's go in and see," Tom said.

"I don't know, it looks dark and scary," Sue said.

But Tom was curious and brave, so he went in first. Sue followed him, because she did not want to be alone. They crawled through the hole and came out in a big chamber. It was dark and cold and dusty. There were many things in the chamber, but they were old and broken and dirty.

"This is not fun, this is boring," Tom said.

"Let's go back," Sue said.

But when they turned around, they saw that the hole was gone. It was covered by a big stone that fell from the ceiling. They were trapped in the chamber. They were helpless.

"Help! Help!" they shouted, but no one heard them.

They cried and hugged each other. They wished they had not gone in the chamber. They wished they had listened to Sue. They were sorry for being naughty and curious.

Then they heard a sound. It was a voice. It was coming from a small window in the wall.

"Hello, hello, are you there?" the voice said.

It was their friend Ben. He had seen them go in the hole and followed them. He had seen the stone fall and blocked the hole. He had looked for another way to get to them. He had found the window.

"Ben, Ben, we are here, we are here!" Tom and Sue said.

"Don't worry, I will help you," Ben said.

He ran to get a rope and a flashlight. He came back and threw the rope through the window. He told Tom and Sue to tie it around their waists. He pulled them out one by one. He gave them the flashlight and hugged them.

"Are you okay? Are you hurt?" he asked.

"We are okay, we are okay, thanks to you," Tom and Sue said.

They were happy and grateful. They thanked Ben for saving them. They said they were sorry for being foolish and reckless. They said they learned their lesson. They said they would never go in the chamber again. They said they would always listen to their friend.

Ben smiled and said, "You are welcome. I am glad you are safe. You are my friends. Friends help each other. Friends solve problems together. Friends are good."

The end.

Once upon a time, Lily was a pretty flower. She lived in a garden with her friends. One day, Lily saw a fierce cat running towards the garden. She was scared and ran to her friends.

Lily said, "Help! A fierce cat is coming!" Her friends said, "Don't worry, we will protect you." They all ran towards the cat, but the cat was too fierce. It caught Lily and took her away.

Lily's friends were very sad. They missed her very much. They hoped that Lily would come back one day, but she never did.

Once there was a small bird called Copper. Copper was thick and strong and could fly very fast. One day, Copper was flying very high and not paying attention and flew into a tree.

Copper couldn't fly away and was very scared. Suddenly she heard a voice, it was an old bird who lived in the tree. He asked, "Why are you afraid little bird?" 

"I flew too close and now I can't move," Copper said, tears filling her eyes. The old bird said, "It looks like you were going too fast, maybe you should pause more often". 

Copper thanked the old bird and understood his lesson. She paused to fly beside the tree, testing her wings before going higher. She was grateful for the wise words the old bird had given her. 

The moral of the story is that itâ€™s important to take time to think before making decisions. Taking a pause can help us see things more clearly and can even save us from danger.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He was a bright and happy three-year-old. He was always exploring and learning new things. 

One day, Timmy wanted to go on an adventure. He wanted to cross the nearby river to explore the other side. But he was scared and hesitated.

â€œMommy,â€ Timmy said, â€œI donâ€™t trust myself to cross the river.â€ 

â€œOh, Timmy,â€ his mommy said, â€œYou donâ€™t need to be afraid. Just trust your own wisdom. Your bright mind will guide you.â€ 

Hearing his mommyâ€™s encouraging words, Timmyâ€™s fear melted away. He stepped onto the bridge and crossed the river to explore the other side. He found many new friends and exciting places! 

Timmy learned that day that he can trust himself and his own wisdom. He was a bright and courageous boy!

Once upon a time there was a kitty. She was playful and always running around. One day she wanted to explore the world, and she tried to escape from the house. She opened a door which was not very big and she got out.

Once she was outside, she started to look around. She was happy to see lots of new things. But then she saw a big and scary dog. She was so scared that she wanted to escape again.

But then an angel appeared. She was wearing a blue dress and she looked gentle. The angel said to the kitty, â€œDo not be scared. I will help you.â€ The angel took the kitty's paw, and rubbed it with a soft cloth. Then the angel dried it with a towel.

The kitty was happy because she felt safe and secure, so she said goodbye to the angel and ran off to explore the world.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to watch films with her family. One day, they went to the cinema to watch a movie. But the film was too noisy and Lily didn't like it. She started to weep quietly. 

Her mommy noticed and asked, "Why are you crying, my dear?" 

Lily replied, "The film is too noisy and it hurts my ears." 

Mommy hugged her and said, "It's okay, we can leave if you want. We can watch another movie next time." 

Lily stopped weeping and smiled. She learned that it's okay to speak up when something bothers you. It's important to take care of yourself and your feelings.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and run around in the grass. One day, she was playing with her ball when it bounced away from her and went down a hill. Lily tried to get it, but it was too quick for her.

She started to cry because she was sad that she lost her ball. But then, her big brother came to support her. He went down the hill and got the ball for her. Lily was so happy and gave her brother a big hug.

Later that day, Lily and her brother went to the park. They saw a terrible storm coming, and Lily was scared. But her brother told her not to worry because he would support her and keep her safe. They sat under a tree and watched the rain come down. Lily felt so happy and safe with her brother by her side.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to draw pictures. One day, he drew a big, green tree. He was very proud of his drawing. Tim wanted to hang his picture on the refrigerator. His mom said, "Yes, you can hang it, but first, we need to clean the refrigerator."

Tim and his mom started to clean the refrigerator. They wiped it and made it look nice. While they were cleaning, Tim's little sister, Lily, came into the room. She saw Tim's drawing and wanted to hang her own picture too. She took Tim's picture off the refrigerator and tried to hang her picture.

Tim was very angry. He yelled at Lily, "That's my spot! Give it back!" Lily started to cry. Their mom came and said, "Tim, you need to share. There is room for both pictures on the refrigerator." But Tim didn't want to share. He grabbed his picture and ripped it in half.

Now, no one could hang their pictures on the refrigerator. Tim felt bad and realized that he should have shared with his sister. The moral of the story is to always share with others, because being selfish can lead to a bad ending.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a pet rabbit named Bun Bun. Bun Bun was very healthy and loved to eat carrots. One day, Lily noticed that Bun Bun was not eating his carrots and was weeping. Lily knew something was wrong with Bun Bun.

Lily's mom took Bun Bun to the vet. The vet looked at Bun Bun and said he needed a tube to help him feel better. The tube would help Bun Bun eat his food. After the tube was put in, Bun Bun started to feel better and stopped weeping. Lily was so happy to see Bun Bun feeling healthy again.

From that day on, Lily made sure to always give Bun Bun healthy food so he would never have to weep again. And Bun Bun was grateful to have such a caring owner like Lily.

Once upon a time, there was a furry friend. He was round, like a ball, and he liked to roll around. He rolled around in the grass, and over pebbles. He even rolled up and down hills!

One day, the furry friend rolled right up to a hungry baby bear. The bear said, "I'm so hungry!" The furry friend said, "Let's be friends!"

The baby bear said, "But I don't have any food!" The furry friend said, "Don't worry! We can find some together!" They rolled and rolled and finally found a big bowl of honey.

The baby bear was so happy! He said, "Thank you, my furry friend!" They shared the honey, and had lots of fun.

The furry friend and the baby bear are still friends today. They like to go on adventures and roll around together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was very excited because she was going to take her new puppy, Max, for a walk. Lily loved Max very much and wanted to give him a good name. 

As they walked, Max sniffed everything he saw and wagged his tail. Lily thought about what to name him. Suddenly, Max barked at a squirrel and Lily knew the perfect name for him. She decided to call him Squirrel because he loved chasing them. 

Lily and Squirrel continued their walk and had lots of fun together. When they got home, Lily's mom asked her what she did. Lily said, "I took Squirrel for a walk and I named him Squirrel because he chased one!" Everyone was happy and Lily felt proud of herself for taking care of her new friend.

Once upon a time there was a jolly girl called Lucy. She had a bright smile and always saw the fun in things. 
One day, Lucy saw something amazing in the sky - it was twinkling and moving across the sky like a shooting star. She wanted to find out what it was, so she ran outside to investigate.

As she looked up, she saw that it was a magical hot air balloon. It was filled with a family of four - a mom, a dad and two children who were about her age called Clara and Charlie. Charlie waved at Lucy, and Lucy waved back. 

The family in the hot air balloon introduced themselves as the Smiths. They said that they had been on a long journey and were just stopping to look around. Lucy was delighted to meet them and invited them to stay with her and have some fun. 

The Smiths accepted Lucy's invitation, so the five of them jumped and laughed in the sky together. They showed Lucy how to steer the hot air balloon and she felt like a magical balloon pilot with the wind in her hair. 

The magical balloon journey through the jolly sky was an adventure Lucy will never forget!

Once upon a time there was a little girl who loved to play. She wanted to join all the big kids in their favorite game. The game was to shoot arrows at a target and try to hit it.

The little girl wanted to join in, but she didn't have an arrow. Everyone else was very competitive and she was scared they would not let her play.

The little girl was sad until she saw a stick in the grass and picked it up. She brought it to the target and set it up.

The little girl took a deep breath and then reached into the grass to pick up three stones. She closed her eyes and threw the stones one by one.

The stones flew through the air and struck the stick. The little girl was so surprised when she opened her eyes, her arrow had hit the target!

The big kids cheered and the little girl was so happy she could take part in the game. From then on, the little girl learned to shoot arrows and was the most competitive of all.

Jack and James were best friends. One day, they were walking down the street, when they saw a barber. The barber was shaving a man's beard. Jack and James wanted to have a turn. 

But the barber said no. He said the scissors were only for grownups.

Jack and James were mad. So they started to fight. They pushed and punched each other, until they were wet with sweat. 

Suddenly, the barber stepped in between them. He said fighting was not a good thing to do. He said that grownups should help children, not fight. 

The barber was right. So Jack and James hugged each other and were friends again. They thanked the barber for helping them. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a strong boy named Tim. Tim liked to collect things. He had many toys, rocks, and sticks in his room. One day, Tim was playing outside with his friends. They were running, jumping, and laughing.

Tim saw a pretty rock on the ground. He wanted to collect it. But when he bent down to pick it up, Tim fell and hurt his knee. It was bleeding. Tim started to cry. His friends ran to get help.

Tim's mom came outside with a bandage. She put the bandage on his knee. Tim felt better right away. His mom told him that he was very strong. Tim smiled and went back to play with his friends. They all had a fun day together.

Tom and Mia like to play with wood. They have many wood blocks and sticks. They can make houses, cars, animals and more. They have fun together.

One day, Tom wants to make a big tower with all the wood. He says to Mia, "Let's make a tower. It will be tall and strong. We can use all the wood we have."

But Mia does not want to make a tower. She wants to make a boat. She says to Tom, "No, let's make a boat. It will be fast and pretty. We can use some wood and some paper."

Tom and Mia start to argue. They both want to use the wood for their own idea. They pull and push the wood. They say, "Mine, mine, mine!"

Then, they hear a loud noise. They look up and see a big bird. The bird has a clear beak and clear wings. It is shiny and beautiful. The bird flies down and picks up some wood with its beak. It flies away with the wood.

Tom and Mia are surprised. They stop arguing. They watch the bird fly away with their wood. They say, "Wow, wow, wow!"

They look at each other and smile. They say, "Let's share the wood. We can make a tower and a boat. We can play together."

They hug and start to change the wood. They make a tower and a boat. They have fun together. They hope to see the clear bird again.

Once upon a time there was a pretty house. Inside the house was a special room that was in the attic. It was a place for special things. One day, when the family was napping, something magical appeared.

The family had never seen anything so special and so strange. It was a sparkly, floating creature. It looked like a fairy and glowed in the dark. It had wings that made it look like it was swimming through the air.

The family was amazed. They wanted to see the creature up close. So they all ran up to the attic. But when they arrived, the fairy was gone.

The family thought they were dreaming. But then something appeared at the window. It was the fairy!

The beautiful creature flew in to the room and hugged the family. They were so happy that they wanted to keep the fairy forever.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the hot sun. One day, her mommy told her that a big hurricane was coming soon.

Lily was scared and asked her mommy, "What is a hurricane?"

Her mommy explained, "A hurricane is a big storm with lots of wind and rain. We need to stay inside and be safe."

Lily was sad that she couldn't play outside anymore. But she knew it was important to be safe. When the hurricane came, she watched from the window as the wind and rain got stronger and stronger. Finally, the storm passed and the sun came out again. Lily was happy to be able to go outside again and release her energy by running and playing.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved playing in the snow with her friends. One day, Lily and her friends built a big snowman. They used sticks for arms and rocks for eyes. The snowman was so big, they could all hug it at the same time.

As they were playing, a boy named Jack came by. He was wearing an orange hat and scarf. "That's a nice snowman," he said. "Can I play with you guys?"

Lily and her friends looked at each other and sighed. They didn't want to play with Jack because he always took their toys and didn't share. But then Lily remembered something her mom had told her. "We should always be kind to others," she said. "Let's let Jack play with us."

So they all played together and had lots of fun. Jack even shared his snacks with them. Lily learned that it's important to be kind to everyone, even if they're not always nice to you. And they all lived happily ever after, playing in the snow and making new friends.

Once upon a time, there was an adorable little girl. She was so curious about the world that everyday she would open the door to explore a new place. She found many wonderful things on her journey as she opened each door.

One day she opened a door and saw a huge garden full of colorful flowers. It was the most beautiful thing she had ever seen. She opened more doors and found a huge lake. It was sparkling in the sunshine. She opened another door and found a magical forest. She even saw a baby squirrel nestled among the trees.

The little girl opened the last door and was amazed to see a whole new world! It was a magical kingdom with beautiful castles, a bustling market and delicious smelling food stalls. She couldn't wait to explore this wonderful new place.

The girl explored this new world until it was late, and she had to go home. But she was happy and content, for she had opened a world of beautiful thing that day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play with her hoop. She would twirl it around and around, trying to keep it up in the air as long as she could. One day, she accidentally stepped on her hoop and broke it. 

Lily's mom saw what happened and said, "Oh no, Lily! Your hoop is delicate and cannot be fixed." 

Lily felt sad and regretted not being more careful with her hoop. She said, "I'm sorry, Mommy. I didn't mean to break it." 

Her mom hugged her and said, "It's okay, Lily. We can always get you a new hoop. But next time, let's make sure to play with it in a safe place." 

Lily smiled and felt happy knowing that her mom still loved her, even though she broke her hoop. From then on, she made sure to play with her toys carefully and in a safe place.

Ben and Lily were best friends. They liked to play together every day. They had many toys, but their favorite was a big box of blocks. They could build anything they wanted with the blocks.

One day, they decided to have a contest. They wanted to see who could build the tallest tower with the blocks. They each took some blocks and started to stack them. They were very careful not to make their towers fall.

"Look at my tower, Lily!" Ben said. "It is very high and strong."

"Mine is higher and stronger, Ben!" Lily said. "I used more blocks and different colors."

They kept building and building, until they ran out of blocks. They looked at their towers and tried to measure them with their eyes.

"Who won, Ben?" Lily asked.

"I don't know, Lily," Ben said. "They look the same to me."

They thought for a moment. Then they smiled at each other.

"Maybe we both won, Lily," Ben said. "We had fun and we used all the blocks. That is a success."

"Yes, Ben, you are right," Lily said. "We are both winners. And we are both playful."

They hugged each other and laughed. Then they knocked down their towers and started to build something new. They were happy and proud of their work. They always chose to be kind and creative.

Once upon a time, there was a lazy cat named Whiskers. Whiskers liked to sleep all day and never wanted to play. One day, Whiskers saw a trail of ants on the ground. 

"Can I follow the trail?" Whiskers asked the ants.

"Yes, you can follow the trail," said the ants.

Whiskers followed the trail and found a big picnic. The ants had lots of food and were having fun. 

"Can I join the picnic?" Whiskers asked.

"Yes, you can join the picnic," said the ants.

Whiskers had so much fun at the picnic that he decided to stop being lazy and play more often.

Once upon a time there was a seal. He lived in the sea with his friends, but he often felt all alone. One day, a dolphin swam up and offered to be his friend. The seal was very glad!

They played together for hours every day. The dolphin showed the seal all the places in the sea and taught him how to catch fish. The seal couldn't believe how lucky he was to have such a wonderful friend!

When time came for the dolphin to leave, he gave the seal a very special gift. He offered a necklace which sparkled with the sunlight. The seal was so glad! He hugged the dolphin and said goodbye.

The seal wore the necklace everywhere he went and showed it to all his friends. He would tell them the story of how his special friend had offered him such a special gift. The seal was very glad to have such a wonderful friend!

Tom and Sue were playing in the yard. They liked to run and jump and laugh. They had a lot of toys, like balls and dolls and cars. They had a modern house, with big windows and bright colors.

"Look, Tom, look!" Sue said, pointing at the sky. "What is that?"

Tom looked up and saw a big, dark cloud. It was spinning and roaring. It was a tornado. He felt scared.

"Come on, Sue, we have to go inside!" Tom said, grabbing her hand. "The tornado is coming!"

But Sue did not want to go inside. She wanted to see the tornado. She thought it was pretty and fun.

"No, Tom, no!" Sue said, pulling her hand away. "I want to stay here! I want to play with the tornado!"

Tom tried to make Sue listen, but she was stubborn. She ran towards the tornado, laughing and clapping. Tom cried and shouted, but she did not hear him.

The tornado came closer and closer. It was very big and very loud. It picked up Sue and her toys and threw them in the air. Tom watched in horror as Sue disappeared in the storm. He ran inside and hid under the bed. He wished he could save Sue, but he could not. He was alone and sad. The tornado was bad.

Anna and Ben were playing in the garden. They liked to dig and plant seeds. They had a big box of seeds with many colors and shapes. Anna wanted to plant radishes. She liked radishes. They were red and round and crunchy.

"Look, Ben, I have radish seeds. Let's plant them here," Anna said. She made a hole in the dirt with her finger and put a seed in it. She covered it with dirt and patted it gently.

Ben nodded. He liked radishes too. But he also liked to scatter seeds. He thought it was fun to see them fly in the air. He grabbed a handful of seeds from the box and threw them in the air. They landed everywhere. Some on the dirt, some on the grass, some on the flowers.

"Ben, what are you doing?" Anna asked. She was angry. She did not like to scatter seeds. She liked to plant them neatly. "You are wasting the seeds. And you are making a mess."

Ben shrugged. He did not think he was wasting the seeds. He thought he was making the garden more beautiful. He smiled and threw another handful of seeds. "I am making a surprise. Maybe we will have many different plants. Maybe we will have a rainbow garden."

Anna frowned. She did not want a rainbow garden. She wanted a radish garden. She picked up a radish from the basket and bit it. It was bitter. She made a face and spit it out. She did not like bitter radishes. She liked sweet radishes. She looked at Ben and had an idea. She handed him the radish. "Here, Ben, try this. It is very good."

Ben took the radish and bit it. He also made a face and spit it out. He did not like bitter radishes either. He liked sweet radishes. He looked at Anna and saw her grin. He realized she had tricked him. He felt silly and mad. He threw the radish at her. She dodged it and threw another one at him. They started a radish fight. They laughed and ran and threw radishes at each other. They forgot about the seeds and the garden. They had fun.

John had a lovely sister. He loved to play with her and they were the best of friends.

One day, John's sister got sick and had to stay in bed. John wanted to help her feel better, so he held her hand and whispered words of love. He sang her his favorite songs and told her special stories.

After a few days, John's family knew that his love was helping his sister heal. They could see that his pepper words and songs were making her smile and she was soon feeling much better.

John was so happy that he could heal his sister with just love. He had shown her just how much he cared and he was glad that his love had helped bring her health back.

Once upon a time there was a little boy who loved to explore. He wanted to see all the wonders of the world. 

So one day he walked and walked until he came to the edge of a huge forest. He was excited to explore the forest. 

He ventured in. Soon enough, he came across an extraordinary sight. A giant tree that had a swing that went way up high, so high he could touch the sky. He was so excited he just had to give it a try. So he climbed up the tree and squeezed himself onto the swing seat. 

He started swinging and swaying and before long he was feeling so merry and carefree. Suddenly, he felt a massive hand squeeze him tight. He looked around and saw an old and miserable giant. The giant spoke in a grumbling voice, "You don't belong in my forest, get away!" 

The little boy was scared and quickly jumped down from the swing. He was so sad, he had to leave the wonderful adventure he had been having. He quietly went home, feeling more than a little miserable.

Lily and Ben were going to the park with Mom. They liked the park because it had swings and slides and a big pond with ducks. On the way, they saw a big sign with bright colors and letters. Mom said it was a billboard and it told people about things they could buy or do.

"What does it say, Mom?" Lily asked.

"It says that there is a new toy store in town and they have a lot of fun toys for kids like you," Mom said.

"Can we go, Mom? Please, please, please?" Ben begged.

"Maybe another day, sweetie. We don't have much money right now and we need to save for other things," Mom said.

Lily and Ben felt sad. They wanted to see the new toy store and play with the toys. They wondered what kind of toys they had and if they would ever get to have them.

They reached the park and tried to have fun, but they couldn't stop thinking about the billboard. They wished they had more money or that someone would give them a toy as a gift.

As they were leaving the park, they saw a man with a big smile and a red hat. He was holding a bunch of balloons and a sign that said "Grand Opening! Free Toys for the First 100 Kids!"

"Look, Mom, look!" Lily shouted.

"Wow, what a lucky day!" Mom said. "Let's go and see what they have!"

They ran to the man and he gave them each a balloon and a ticket. He said they could go inside the new toy store and receive one toy of their choice.

Lily and Ben were so happy. They thanked the man and went inside. They saw shelves and shelves of toys of all kinds: dolls, cars, puzzles, books, games, and more. They had a hard time deciding what to pick.

Lily chose a doll with a pink dress and a bow. She named her Daisy and hugged her tight. Ben chose a car with a remote control. He said it was the coolest car ever and he couldn't wait to race it.

They went back to Mom and showed her their toys. Mom was happy for them and said they deserved a treat. She said they could go to the ice cream shop and get a cone.

Lily and Ben smiled and said they loved Mom. They said they loved their toys too and they were the best gifts ever. They forgot about the billboard and the money. They were just happy and grateful. They had a wonderful day.

One day, a little boy named Tim went to the park with his mom. Tim was very creative and loved to play with his toys. At the park, he saw a big tree and wondered what was behind it. He asked his mom, "Can I go see what's behind the tree?"

His mom said, "Sure, but only for a minute!" Tim ran to the tree and found a little girl named Sue. Sue was sad because she lost her toy. Tim wanted to help Sue feel better.

Tim thought for a moment, and then had an idea. He said, "Let's make a new toy from sticks and leaves!" They worked together to make a creative toy. Sue was happy again, and they became friends. They played together until it was time to go home.

Once upon a time, there was a popular otter. This otter had many friends. Everyone liked the otter because he was so nice.

One day, the otter was swimming in the water. He saw a big fish. The otter called to the fish, "Hello, fish! Do you want to be my friend?" The fish said, "Yes, I want to be your friend!"

The otter and the fish played all day. They swam and had fun. All the other animals saw them and called, "We want to play too!" So, the otter, the fish, and all the other animals played together. They were all happy and had a great day.

Once upon a time, there was a prince and a princess who lived in a castle on the east side of a big forest. Every morning, the prince and princess would ride their horses in the forest. But one day, something naughty happened.

While exploring the forest, the prince and princess noticed that a big stone was blocking their path.

"This stone is so big, how can we pass?" asked the princess. 

The prince smiled and said, "Let's see if our horses can pass it!"

The prince and princess gave it a try and the horses passed the big stone! 

The prince and princess were so proud of themselves and their horses, and they rode off happily into the east.

Lily liked to play with her mom's jewelry. She liked the shiny rings and necklaces and bracelets. She liked to pretend she was a princess or a fairy. But she knew she had to be careful. Mom said jewelry was not for children. Mom said jewelry was very special and expensive.

One day, Lily saw a pretty ring on mom's dresser. It was red and sparkly. Lily wanted to try it on. She looked around. Mom was not in the room. Lily took the ring and put it on her finger. It was too big for her. It slipped off and rolled under the bed. Lily tried to reach it, but she could not. She was scared. She did not want to lose mom's ring. She did not want to make mom angry.

Lily started to cry. She did not know what to do. She heard mom coming. She hid under the bed. Mom came in and saw the ring was gone. She looked everywhere. She could not find it. She was worried. She thought someone had taken it. She called dad. She told him the ring was missing. She asked him to come home.

Dad came home. He helped mom look for the ring. They moved the furniture. They checked the drawers. They could not find it. They were sad. They thought the ring was gone forever. They did not know Lily had it.

Lily felt bad. She knew she had done something wrong. She knew she had been foolish. She wanted to say sorry. She wanted to give the ring back. She crawled out from under the bed. She held the ring in her hand. She said, "Mom, dad, I have something to tell you."

Mom and dad saw Lily. They saw the ring. They were surprised. They asked Lily what happened. Lily told them the truth. She said she had taken the ring. She said she had lost it under the bed. She said she was sorry. She said she would never do it again.

Mom and dad hugged Lily. They were not angry. They were happy. They were happy they had found the ring. They were happy Lily had told them the truth. They said, "Lily, we love you. We are glad you are honest. We are glad you are safe. Thank you for giving us the ring back. But please, do not play with our jewelry again. It is not for children. It is for grown-ups."

Lily nodded. She said, "I understand. I am sorry. I love you too. Thank you for forgiving me." She gave them the ring. She gave them a kiss. She learned her lesson. She never played with their jewelry again. She played with her own toys. She was a good girl.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Jack and Jill. They both loved to play in the park and eat tasty treats.

One day when Jack and Jill were walking in the park, they saw some yummy treats in a nearby tree. Jack asked Jill, "Let's steal the treats!" Jill was very excited and agreed.

They climbed the tree and grabbed the treats. When they looked closely, they saw that the treats had a symbol on them. Jack and Jill were very surprised by the symbol.

Jack asked Jill, "What do you think the symbol means?" Jill didn't know, but she was excited to find out.

When Jack and Jill got home, they asked their parents about the symbol. They found out that the symbol meant that the treats were yummy, and that it was ok to eat them.

Jack and Jill were happy that they could eat the yummy treats. They agreed to never steal again.

Tom and Lily were playing in the park. Tom had a guitar and Lily had a ball. Tom liked to make music with his guitar. He sang songs and strummed the strings. Lily liked to roll and bounce her ball. She threw it high and caught it low.

"Can I try your guitar?" Lily asked Tom.

"OK, but be careful. It is my favorite toy," Tom said. He gave his guitar to Lily and took her ball.

Lily held the guitar and tried to play it. But she did not know how to make it sound nice. She hit the strings hard and made a loud noise.

"Stop! You are hurting my guitar!" Tom shouted. He ran to Lily and tried to take his guitar back.

But Lily did not want to give it up. She held it tight and pushed Tom away.

"Let go! It is mine!" Tom said.

"No, it is mine!" Lily said.

They pulled and pushed and fought over the guitar. They did not see the old man who was sitting on a bench nearby. He was eating a lemon and making a sour face. He did not like the noise and the fighting. He got up and walked to Tom and Lily.

"Hey, you two. Stop that right now. You are being very rude and noisy. Why don't you share your toys and play nicely?" he said.

He took the guitar from Lily and the ball from Tom. He gave the guitar to Tom and the ball to Lily. He also gave them each a slice of lemon.

"Here, try this. It is sour, but it is good for you. It will teach you a lesson. Maybe next time you will be more polite and friendly," he said.

Tom and Lily took the lemon and bit into it. They made a sour face and spit it out. They did not like the lemon at all. They looked at each other and felt sorry. They realized they had been mean and silly.

"I'm sorry, Tom. I should not have pushed you. Can I play with your guitar again?" Lily said.

"I'm sorry, Lily. I should not have shouted at you. Can I play with your ball again?" Tom said.

They hugged and said sorry. They gave back their toys and played together. They took turns with the guitar and the ball. They sang songs and rolled and bounced. They had fun and were happy. The old man smiled and nodded. He sat back on the bench and ate his lemon. He liked the lemon and the peace.

Once upon a time there was a little boy. His name was Tim.

One day, Tim was playing in a field. He saw a big sausage. It looked yummy!

He picked it up, but then a voice shouted, "Stop!" 

Tim turned around and saw a rough man. He held out his hand and said, "Pay me for that sausage!" 

Tim felt scared. He had no money. He was about to cry, but then another voice spoke up.

It was an old woman. She reached into her pocket and pulled out some coins. She said, "Here, take this and I will pay for Tim's sausage."

The rough man looked surprised. He said, "Okay," and took the coins. Then he left.

The old woman smiled at Tim. She said, "You're very lucky. Don't ever forget how much kindness can mean."

Tim smiled back. He thanked the old woman and enjoyed his sausage with a happy feeling in his heart.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Lola. Lola was very smart and she loved to pretend. 

One day, Lola went to school and saw a big blackboard. She wanted to pretend that the blackboard was a powerful castle. 

Lola then used her hands to draw on the blackboard. She made colorful pictures of a princess and a knight. She pretended the knight was saving the princess from the evil wizard. 

Lola was so happy with her pretend play that she spent the whole day playing. She was so good at pretending that her teacher and friends were amazed.

At the end of the day, Lola had to leave the school but she promised herself to come back to pretend again.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tom. Tom loved to go swimming in the lake with his friends. One day, Tom and his friends went to the lake to play. They splashed around in the water and had so much fun.

After swimming, Tom and his friends went to Tom's house to draw pictures. Tom drew a picture of his dog, Max. His friends drew pictures of their families. Tom's mom came in and looked at the pictures. She said, "Wow, these are great pictures! But remember, it's important to be honest when you draw. You don't want to make things up."

Tom's friend said, "I drew a picture of a dragon! It's not real, but it's still fun to draw." Tom's mom said, "That's okay, as long as you're honest about it being imaginary." Tom and his friends smiled and continued drawing pictures. They had a great day together.

Once upon a time there was a small bunny who could hop very high. He loved to hop around the meadow and look for the sweetest flowers to pick. One day, the bunny decided to go to the marketplace to find treats to bring home.

When the bunny got to the marketplace, he noticed some yummy treats that he had never seen before. He tried to go closer but there was a giant and he did not look happy. The giant shouted out that the treats were not to be shared and the price was very high.

The bunny was very sad and thought he would never be able to get any of the treats. He asked the giant if he could please help, but the giant was too tall and he just walked away. The bunny begged and pleaded but the giant didn't listen.

The bunny was left alone and all alone, he hopped away sadly. He now knew that he would never get his hands on any of the sweet treats he saw. Poor bunny!

Once upon a time, there was a grumpy doll. He was always frowning and no one liked him. 
One day, a little girl had a wonderful idea. She decided to design a dress for the grumpy doll. She got some fabric, scissors, and buttons. 
The little girl worked really hard and when she was done, she showed her doll the beautiful dress she had designed. 
The doll was so happy! He smiled and thanked her for the dress. From that day forward, the grumpy doll was always happy and everyone loved him. 
The little girl was so proud of what she had designed. She took the grumpy doll with her everywhere she went. 
They were the best of friends.

Tom and Lily are friends. They like to play with blocks and dolls. But today, they have a quarrel. Tom wants to build a big tower with all the blocks. Lily wants to make a house for her dolls with some blocks. They do not share the blocks. They pull and push the blocks. They yell and cry.

Mom hears the noise. She comes to see what is wrong. She sees the blocks and the dolls on the floor. She sees Tom and Lily with angry faces. She is not happy. She says, "You are not playing nice. You are not being good friends. You have to share the blocks and the dolls. Or you have to play with something else."

Tom and Lily do not listen to Mom. They still want the blocks and the dolls. They do not say sorry. They do not hug. They do not smile. They keep on quarreling. Mom is very sad. She says, "That's enough. You have to stop. You have to go to your rooms. You have to think about what you did. You have to stay there until dinner."

Tom and Lily go to their rooms. They slam the doors. They are still angry. They do not have the blocks and the dolls. They do not have their friend. They do not have fun. They have an incredible bad day. They wish they had played nice. They wish they had been good friends. They wish they had shared the blocks and the dolls. But it is too late. They have to wait until tomorrow. Maybe then, they can say sorry, hug, smile, and play again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in her yard with her toys. One day, she found a box in the yard. She tried to open it, but it was stubborn and wouldn't budge. 

Lily's mom came outside and asked, "What are you doing, sweetie?" 

"I found a box, but it won't open," replied Lily. 

Her mom tried to open the box too, but it was still stubborn. "Maybe we need a key," suggested her mom. 

Lily and her mom searched around the yard and found a key that fit perfectly. They opened the box and inside was a surprise - a new toy for Lily to play with! She was so happy and grateful to her mom for helping her open the box.

Once upon a time, there was a compassionate dog named Buddy. Buddy liked to help his friends. One day, Buddy and his friend, a little bird named Tweet, went on an adventure to find a treasure.

They walked and walked until they found a big tree. Buddy and Tweet looked up and saw the treasure box in the tree. Buddy climbed the tree and got the treasure box. They were so excited!

It was getting late, so Buddy and Tweet decided to sleep under the tree. They were tired from their big adventure. As they slept, they dreamed about the fun they had finding the treasure. And they knew they would always remember this special day.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Lucky. He loved to play and run on the ground. One day, Lucky saw a big red ball. He wanted to play with it so much. He ran very fast to get the ball.

Lucky was so happy with the big red ball. He ran and jumped with it. But then, he saw a big cat. The cat was not nice. It wanted to take Lucky's ball away. Lucky did not want that to happen. So, he yelled at the cat very loud.

The big cat did not like the yell. It became very mad. It jumped on Lucky and took the ball away. Lucky was very sad. He tried to get the ball back, but he could not. The big cat ran away with the ball, and Lucky was left alone on the ground.

Tim and Sam are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big lake. They want to swim in the lake. They run to the lake.

But the lake is not safe. There are signs that say "No Swimming". There are rocks and weeds in the water. There are also ducks and fish that can bite. Tim and Sam do not see the signs. They do not hear the people who shout "Stop!" They are deaf. They cannot hear anything.

They jump in the lake. They splash and laugh. They do not know they are in danger. They do not see the big wave that comes. The wave is from a boat. The boat is fast and loud. The boat does not see Tim and Sam. The boat is too close.

The people on the shore are scared. They wave and scream. They want to help Tim and Sam. They want to unite them with their families. They call 911. They hope it is not too late. They pray for Tim and Sam.

Once upon a time, there was a squash. He was very happy in the sunshine, but something was wrong. He could hear a harsh noise coming from outside. It was loud and it scared him.

The squash peeked outside his little home. He saw a machine spraying water. It was loud and scared the squash even more. He felt very sad and he wanted to hide.

But then, something wonderful happened. A nice lady came and sprayed the squash with soft, gentle water. She sprayed the machine too. The harsh noise stopped and the squash felt happy again.

The lady hugged the squash and gave him a warm smile. She promised to always make sure the squash was happy. The squash smiled back, happy to have a new friend.

Once there was a little bird. He was a very happy bird, and every day he liked to sing. He also liked to play. He would fly high into the sky and dance around. Sometimes he would soar very fast, but other times he would fly slow.

The bird liked to sing for his friends. All the animals liked to listen to him sing. The birds and the squirrels and the little bunnies came to watch him.

Every time he sang, he felt happy inside. He knew that he was making all his friends happy too.

So he kept singing, and playing, and flying slow. He sang a very happy song and everyone wanted to join in. Everyone sang together, and it was the most beautiful sound ever. 

When the song was over, the whole forest smiled. The little bird was very proud of himself. He knew that he had made his friends very happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to take showers, especially when the water was warm. One day, while Lily was taking a shower, her favorite toy, a rubber duck, disappeared! She looked everywhere but couldn't find it.

Lily was sad and didn't know what to do. She asked her mom for help, but even her mom couldn't find the rubber duck. Lily felt like she lost her best friend. She cried and cried until her mom had an idea.

Her mom suggested they take a bath together and look for the rubber duck. So, they filled the bathtub with warm water and bubbles and got in. As they were playing, Lily saw something yellow peeking out from behind the shampoo bottle. It was the rubber duck! It didn't disappear after all, it was just hiding. Lily was so happy to have found her toy again and hugged it tightly. From that day on, she made sure to always keep her rubber duck safe in the shower.

Once there was a little girl called Tilly. She had a box of toys she liked to play with. One day she wanted to play with her toys, but her mom said no.

"Tilly, we have to delay the fun for now," Mom said.
"But why?" Tilly asked, feeling weak.
"We have to go to the store first," said her mom.

Tilly was upset, but she came along with her mom to the store. She wanted to go home and get back to playing with her box of toys.

At the store, Tilly saw a lot of interesting things. She was so happy to be out and about, she forgot about her box of toys at home. 

When they got home, Tilly ran to the box of toys and laughed as she played with them. 

Mom smiled, relieved that Tilly was happy and had forgotten about the delay.

Once upon a time there was an ordinary boy. He was very excited one day because he found a pair of sunglasses. He thought they looked cool so he put them on his face and zipped outside.

The sun was very bright and the sunglasses made him feel like he was a king. He felt so happy he just wanted to zip around. He zipped up the street, around the corner, and hopped over a fence. 

Then he saw something amazing! He saw a bird with the most beautiful wings zip around in the sky. He was so excited he tried to zip very high in the air like the bird. He tried but he didn't quite make it. 

So he just kept zipping around the garden wearing his special sunglasses. He thought it was so much fun that he didn't want to take them off. He kept them on until evening and snuggled into bed with a huge smile on his face. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy had a rug in his room that he loved to play on. It was soft and cozy. One day, Timmy's friend came over to play. They decided to play a game, but it wasn't easy. They had to think really hard. Suddenly, they started to fight over who was winning. Timmy's mom heard the noise and came to see what was happening. She told them to stop fighting and play nicely. Then, she showed them an easy way to play the game without fighting. Timmy and his friend were happy and continued to play on the rug together. The end.

Tommy was in his bedroom. It was dark outside and he was feeling a bit scared. He lay in bed and listened to all the creaks and cracks in the house. Suddenly, he heard a loud thump and jumped up in his bed. He looked around and saw a big post of wood that had fallen down. He was scared, but then he remembered that it's daddy who had put it there. Daddy had said it was to help keep bad things away from their house.

Tommy lay back down and thought about the post. He was glad it was there so he could feel safe and not scared. He thought about how big and strong it was. Then, just as he was slowing nodding off to sleep, he heard a sound coming from outside. It was a very scary sound and he quickly lay very still in his bed.

But after a few minutes, the sound had gone. There was silence for a while and then Tommy heard the sound of daddy's footsteps outside the window. He felt better, the post was doing it's job! With that thought in mind, he snuggled in his blankets and fell asleep.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved playing with her toys and taking bubble baths with her shampoo. One day, Lily's mom asked her to sort her toys into two piles: one for the broken toys and one for the good toys. Lily was frightened to do it because she didn't want to throw any of her toys away.

But her mom explained that it's important to sort things out so we can see what we need to fix or get rid of. Lily started sorting her toys and realized that some of them were really broken and she couldn't play with them anymore. She felt sad, but she knew it was the right thing to do.

From that day on, Lily learned that sorting things out can be helpful and make things better. She started sorting her clothes and books too, and even helped her mom sort the groceries. And every time she took a bubble bath with her shampoo, she remembered the lesson she learned about sorting things out.

Lily liked to play in the garden. She liked to look at the flowers and the bugs. One day, she saw a cricket on a leaf. It was green and shiny. Lily wanted to touch it.

She was careful. She did not want to hurt the cricket. She put out her hand very slowly. The cricket did not move. Lily touched its back. It felt smooth and hard.

But then, the cricket jumped. It jumped very high and far. Lily was scared. She did not know where the cricket went. She looked around. She could not see it. She started to cry.

Mama heard Lily cry. She came to the garden. She saw Lily was sad. She asked her what was wrong.

Lily told Mama about the cricket. She said she was sorry. She said she did not mean to make it go away. She said she was worried. She worried the cricket was lost or hurt.

Mama hugged Lily. She told her it was okay. She told her the cricket was not lost or hurt. She told her the cricket was just scared. She told her the cricket could jump very well. She told her the cricket would find a new leaf to sit on.

Lily felt better. She stopped crying. She smiled at Mama. She said thank you. She said she loved Mama. Mama said she loved Lily too. They went inside to have a snack. Lily hoped the cricket was happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play with her red coat. She would wear it every day, even when it was hot outside. One day, Lily went to the park to play with her friends. She ran around and played tag, but then she got too hot and took off her coat. She left it on a bench while she played.

A foolish boy saw the coat and thought it was his. He put it on and ran away. When Lily noticed her coat was gone, she asked her friends if they had seen it. One of her friends said, "I saw a boy with a red coat. He zipped it up and ran away." Lily knew it was her coat and she was sad.

Lily went home without her coat and told her mom what happened. Her mom said, "Don't worry, we will get you a new coat." But Lily was still sad because she loved her old coat with the hook on the front. From that day on, Lily made sure to always keep her coat close to her so nobody could take it again.

Once upon a time, in a green forest, there lived an old lion. The old lion was very sad and helpless because he was too old to hunt for food. He was very hungry and tired.

One day, a small mouse came by and saw the old lion. The mouse said, "Old lion, why are you so sad?" The lion replied, "I am old and helpless. I cannot hunt for food anymore." The mouse felt sorry for the old lion and said, "I will bring you food every day. Please do not eat me."

The old lion was very thankful and promised not to eat the mouse. As days went by, the mouse brought food to the old lion every day. The old lion was happy and healthy again. One day, the old lion accidentally stepped on the mouse's tail. The mouse cried in pain, but he knew the old lion did not mean to hurt him.

The mouse said, "I forgive you, old lion. I know you did not mean to hurt me." The old lion was very sorry and thanked the mouse for forgiving him. From that day on, the old lion and the mouse became best friends. They learned that forgiveness and helping each other made them both happy and strong.

The moral of the story is to always be kind and forgive others, even when they make mistakes.

Once there was a family, who had a 3 year old little girl named Lucy. She was curious and wanted to learn new things all the time. So her Mom and Dad decided to get her a tutor.

The tutor was a nice, gray-haired lady named Mrs. Smith. She came to their house and taught Lucy a lot of things. These lessons included numbers, letters and shapes. She also taught her how to count and how to spell.

Mrs. Smith was wonderful! She brought colorful books and crayons, and they would do puzzles together. Lucy learned bowling and how to bake a cake. She was growing smarter and smarter!

At the end of each lesson, Lucy gave Mrs. Smith a big hug and thanked her. She really appreciated all the help. Lucy and Mrs. Smith had a lot of fun together!

Once upon a time, there was a playful bunny named Benny. He loved to hop and play all day long. One day, Benny met a little girl named Lily. They became friends and played together in the park.

As they played, they saw a big, scary dog. Benny was scared and wanted to run away, but Lily told him to pause and be brave. They stood still and the dog walked away.

Later, Benny and Lily had a race. Benny wanted to win so badly, but he was getting tired. Just when he thought he couldn't go on, he saw the victory line. He pushed himself harder and won the race.

Benny and Lily were so happy and hugged each other. They knew they could conquer anything if they were brave and determined. From that day on, they played together every day and had many more victories together.

Once upon a time there was a modest Missle. He remembered being with his family, but he had been gone for a very long time. Everywhere he went, he was reminded of his family, and it made him feel sad. One day, he decided to find his family again. He flew far away to the place where he had last seen them. When he arrived, he found them all waiting for him. Everyone was so happy to see each other. They hugged and cried together. 

The modest missile was so glad he remembered to come back home and be with his family. They all lived happily ever after!

Sara and Tom are friends. They like to play together. Today, they go to the pool with their moms. They are very happy.

They arrive at the pool. They see many people. Some people are big, some people are small. Some people are loud, some people are quiet. Sara and Tom say hello to the people. They are polite.

They put on their swimsuits. They jump into the water. They swim and splash. They have fun. They see a ball. They want to play with the ball.

"Can we have the ball, please?" Sara asks a boy who has the ball.

"Sure, you can have the ball. Here you go." The boy says. He gives them the ball. He is polite.

"Thank you, you are very nice." Tom says.

"You're welcome. Have fun." The boy says.

Sara and Tom play with the ball. They throw it and catch it. They laugh and smile. They are happy. They share the ball with other kids. They are polite.

They have a good day at the pool. They make new friends. They learn to swim. They are polite. They are happy.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Meggy. She was only three years old and she loved playing with the equipment from her daddyâ€™s garage.

One day, when her dad was away, Meggy decided to go into the garage. She had to stand on a box to see over the top of the work bench. When she looked inside, she saw all the expensive equipment!

Meggy thought it would be so much fun to play with it for a while. She touched the tools and felt them with her tiny hands. Then she started to pick them up and make noises like she was fixing something.

Just then, her father walked in. Meggy was so embarrassed! He was really upset and shouted at her, telling her never to go into the garage again.

Since then, Meggy has never been allowed back in to the garage. She still looks with hope, but all she can do is stand outside and wish.

Once upon a time, there was a princess. She had a beautiful foot, but she didn't like it. She thought it was disgusting. One day, a prince came to the castle and saw the princess. He thought she was very pretty. "Will you marry me?" he asked. 

The princess was surprised. "Why do you want to marry me?" she asked. 

"Because you are beautiful," the prince said. "And I like your foot." 

The princess was happy. She said yes, and they got married. They had a big party and everyone danced. The princess forgot about her foot and had fun with the prince.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Josh and Beth. Josh found a flute and he was extremely happy. He asked Beth to join him and they started to play the flute together.

Josh asked Beth 'What number shall we play?' Together they counted 1,2,3 and started to play the flute. They had so much fun!

Suddenly, Josh's mom came into the room and saw the flute. She said 'Uh-oh, this flute looks familiar. Have you taken it from the living room?'

Josh and Beth became very quiet. Josh looked down and felt guilty. He knew he had taken the flute from the living room. He admitted it and said 'Sorry mommy'. 

Josh's mom gave him a hug and said 'It's ok. It's important to always tell the truth. I forgive you. Now please put the flute back.'

Josh and Beth put the flute back in the living room and felt better. They promised each other to always be honest and never take things without asking. 

The End

Once upon a time, there was a deer named Bambi. Bambi lived in a forest with lots of trees. One day, it started to rain and Bambi got wet. Bambi wanted to stay dry and keep comfortable. So, Bambi went to a cozy cave and stayed there until the rain stopped. When the rain stopped, Bambi went back to the forest and played with other deer. They were happy and had fun together. Bambi always remembered to keep comfortable and stay dry when it rained.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the park. One day, she found a new stick on the ground. It was long and brown. She picked it up and smiled.

Lily started to play with her new stick. She twirled it around and pretended it was a magic wand. She even tried to balance it on her nose like a circus clown. She was having so much fun that she didn't notice the time passing by.

As the sun started to set, Lily realized it was time to go home. She hugged her stick and smiled. She couldn't wait to play with it again tomorrow.

Once upon a time, there were two friends, Jenny and Matt. They lived in the same neighborhood.

One day they found out that there was a tube in the attic that they could not solve. Matt had no idea how to do it, so he called his friend Jenny to help. Jenny was very smart, so she knew how to solve it.

First, Jenny asked Matt what he knew about the tube. Matt said he didn't know anything and he felt very ignorant. Jenny told him to not worry and that she could help him.

When Matt told Jenny what he knew about the tube, Jenny knew exactly how to solve it. She told Matt that the tube was very easy to solve and that all he had to do was open it up and use his imagination.

So, Matt and Jenny grabbed the tube and opened it up. They found so many beautiful things inside that Matt had never noticed before. He was so happy and he thanked Jenny for solving the tube for him. Jenny was glad that she was able to help her friend and they both had a fun afternoon full of solving and playing!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in the park every day. One day, Lily saw a big statue of a horse in the middle of the park. She thought it was so pretty and wanted to touch it.

Lily went to the statue and reached out to touch it. Suddenly, she heard a loud voice say, "Don't touch me!" Lily was scared and ran away.

The next day, Lily went back to the park and saw the statue again. This time, she said, "I'm sorry for trying to touch you yesterday. I didn't know you could talk." The statue replied, "It's okay. I hope we can be friends now."

From that day on, Lily and the statue became friends and had lots of fun adventures together in the park.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys, but his favorite was his toy car. One day, Timmy's mom asked him to help her wrap a present for his grandma. Timmy was excited to help and got out the wrapping paper and tape.

As they were wrapping the present, Timmy noticed his mom's equipment bag on the floor. "What's in there?" he asked. "Just some tools for work," his mom replied. Timmy thought it looked cool and asked if he could play with it. His mom said no, because it was too dangerous for him.

After they finished wrapping the present, Timmy's mom noticed that some of the tape was missing. She asked Timmy if he took it, and he said yes. He felt guilty for taking it without asking. His mom forgave him and they finished wrapping the present together. Timmy was happy to help and learned that it's important to ask before taking things.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Lily. Lily was only three years old and loved to explore the world. She didn't know what could be in the woods and often played around it.

One day, as she was walking, she heard something strange coming from a jar by her feet. When she opened it, a big, scary monster was inside. The monster was so terrible that she screamed.

The monster said, "Don't be scared, Lily. We just want to play with you."

Lily was so frightened she couldn't speak. She ran away from the jar and left the monster inside.

When she got home, she told her parents about the scary monster in the jar. They were so relieved that she was safe and warned her about how dangerous it is to play in the woods.

After that, Lily learned a valuable lesson about being careful and only going to places that she feels safe in. Although some things can be scary, if you stay brave, everything will be okay.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a favorite chair that she loved to sit in. One day, she noticed that her chair was broken. It made her sad because she couldn't sit in it anymore.

Lily tried to fix the chair by herself, but she couldn't. She asked her mom to help her, but her mom was too busy. So Lily tried to sit in the chair anyway, but it broke even more. 

Lily started to cry because she loved that chair so much. She tried to rub the broken parts together to make it better, but it didn't work. Sadly, Lily had to throw away her favorite chair and she was very upset. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a crazy bird. He loved to fly around the sky and the garden. One day, he saw a cake in the garden and wanted to try it. He flew down to get a closer look. But when he got close, a big dog came from out of nowhere and tried to eat it! The bird looked for help but there was no one around. Suddenly, he had an idea. He started to fly around the dog and kept flying faster and faster. The dog got dizzy and fell down. The bird then grabbed the cake and flew off into the sky. He enjoyed the delicious cake and had no more trouble from the crazy dog. The End.

Once upon a time, there was a pink bunny named Rosie. Rosie was glad because she had lots of friends to play with. One day, Rosie and her friends went to a field to play. The sun was very bright and Rosie had to blink her eyes a lot. Suddenly, Rosie saw a big pink flower in the field. She was so happy to see it that she started to hop towards it. When she got closer, she saw that the flower was as big as her! Rosie was so glad to have found such a beautiful flower. She blinked her eyes again and again, looking at the pink petals. Rosie's friends came over and saw the flower too. They were all amazed and glad to see it. From that day on, Rosie and her friends visited the pink flower often, and they were always glad to see it.

Once there was a little girl named Chloe. Chloe was three years old and she had a modern toy. She wanted to play with it, but her friend disagreed. Chloe did not understand why her friend did not want to play.

So, they went outside and tried something else. Chloe thought of a game. Chloe and her friend both knelt down on their knees. Chloe suggested they play a game and her friend did not disagree.

Chloe's friend was happy. They played for hours. They laughed, jumped and made up new games. After a while, Chloe and her friend disagreed again as to what to do. Chloe wanted to play with her modern toy, and her friend wanted to keep playing outside. They both laughed and had a great time.

Max was a lonely little boy. He wanted to go outside and play but he was scared. He sat on his room, feeling sad.

His mom came to him and said "I want to spoil you, Max! I've got something special for you!" Max was so excited.

His mom went away and came back with a big, shining box. Inside the box was a big bar of soap. Max was so happy! He had never seen soap like this before. 

Max's mom took him outside and let him play in the garden. He was so happy and he decided to use the soap to make bubbles. He watched the bubbles and laughed.

Max knew that he was never lonely with his mom and the special soap. From then on, Max always felt happy and spoilt!

One day, Jenny and her mommy were playing a game. Jenny was having lots of fun. Suddenly, Jenny's mommy said, "Let's quit." Jenny was sad. She wanted to keep playing.

Mommy took out her phone. "I'm going to make a call," she said. 

Jenny asked, "What are you doing?"

Mommy replied, "I am looking for someone who can help us."

Mommy talked to someone on the phone. Then she said, "Okay, we won't quit. I found someone who can help us." 

Jenny was happy. She asked, "Who is it?"

Mommy smiled and replied, "It is someone who is very independent. She can help us have even more fun with the game." 

Jenny was so excited. She couldn't wait to meet this new person!

Sara and Ben like to play with their toys. They have many toys in a big sack. They dump the sack on the floor and make a mess. They pretend to be pirates and princesses and animals. They have fun.

But Mom does not like the mess. She tells Sara and Ben to clean up their toys and put them back in the sack. She says she will read them a story if they do. Sara and Ben say yes, but they do not do it. They keep playing and making more mess.

Mom comes back and sees the mess. She is angry. She says no story for Sara and Ben. She says they have to go to bed without a story. Sara and Ben are sad. They say sorry, but Mom does not listen. She takes the sack and the toys and puts them away. She says they can have them back tomorrow if they are good.

Sara and Ben go to bed without a story. They cry. They wish they had listened to Mom. They wish they had a story. They think Mom is silly. But they are sillier.

One day, Mama and Mama's friend, Michelle, decided to go for a walk together. Mama was introducing Michelle to all of their neighbours. 

First, they came to the mailbox. Then, they stopped at Sally's front porch. Finally, they walked up to a big, tall house. 

â€œAh, this is my house,â€ said Mama. Inside, she opened the large, wooden cabinet and showed Michelle a present. 

Michelle was very excited, but she was also impatient. â€œCan I see it? Can I see it?â€

Mama smiled. â€œSure you can!â€ she said, and handed Michelle a big, colourful box. 

Michelle opened the box and jumped up and down. She was so happy - she was like a little jumping bean. 

Mama laughed. â€œI'm so glad you like it,â€ she said. 

Michelle agreed. â€œMe too! It's the best present ever!â€ 

Mama and Michelle hugged, and continued on their walk together.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Sam and Emma. Sam loved animals and Emma loved to help.

One day, the two friends went to the forest. After walking a while, they found a small animal. Its fur was dry and it was shivering.

Sam said to Emma, "Let's help the animal."

Emma agreed, so they decided to find food and make a warm bed for it.

They gathered some leaves and sticks to provide a dry bed. Then they found some berries to provide food.

The animal was happy and thanked them with a squeak. From them on, they came often to the forest to provide fur and food. The little animal was well taken care of. 

The end.

Yesterday, Jack decided to go to the park. It was a noisy place, with lots of people and birds chirping very loudly. But Jack didn't mind. He liked to watch the birds flutter around and see the other children run and play.

He decided to swing on the swing first. It was a lot of fun, but it made a lot of noise. Jack laughed and waved his arms in the air as he swung back and forth.

Then, he decided to try the slide. He climbed to the top and slid down, shouting with joy. He was so happy he went down the slide again - and again!

Finally, Jack decided it was time to go home. He had had a very busy and noisy day at the park. But he had lots of fun and was glad he had decided to go yesterday!

Once upon a time there was a small jeep that lived in the forest. He was a very happy jeep, always rolling around and making friends with all the animals in the forest. One day, he noticed that a bee was in trouble. The bee was stuck in some thick mud and couldn't get out.

The jeep thought to himself, "I must help the bee!". He bravely rolled up right next to the bee and used all his strength to hold onto the poor bee. This gave the bee the strength to crawl out of the mud and fly away. The jeep was so proud to have helped his friend and felt really good inside.

That's when the jeep learned an important lesson. He knew that if he used his strength to help others, it would make him feel even better. From then on, the jeep was always helping the other animals in the forest, and they all appreciated his kind heart.

Once there was a little girl who found a special gift. It was a box with a yellow ribbon tied around it. She was so excited to see what was inside and carefully opened it. Inside she found a tough toy truck. She screamed and jumped up and down with happiness.

She took the truck outside to play with it and had a wonderful time. That night she put her truck away carefully. The next morning something strange happened. When she went to get the truck she found the box had been torn open.

The girl was sad and cross. Someone had been in her room and taken her truck. She ran to tell her mom and dad. The little girl felt so disappointed and sad.

But then her mom and dad took her outside in front of their house. There, standing in the driveway, was a shiny new truck. It was an even bigger and tougher truck than the one she had before.

The girl clapped her hands and hugged her mom and dad. She was so excited to get such a beautiful gift. She thanked her parents and quickly ran to her new truck. She knew that no one could ever take this truck away from her.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny named Benny. Benny loved to play in the garden with his friends. One day, Benny found a carrot that was very dirty. He wanted to clean it so he could eat it, but he didn't have any water.

Benny went to his friend, a little bird named Billy, and asked him for some water. But Billy was not feeling peaceful that day and said no. Benny was sad and didn't know what to do. Suddenly, he saw a big puddle of water that had sprung up from the ground after a rainstorm.

Benny hopped over to the puddle and washed the carrot until it was clean. He was so happy that he could finally eat it. But then, Billy came over and saw what Benny had done. He felt bad for not helping and apologized to Benny. From that day on, they were friends again and played together in the garden in peace.

Once upon a time, there was an adventurous ant named Andy. Andy loved to explore and go on big trips. One sunny day, Andy decided to climb a tall tree to see what he could find.

As Andy climbed higher and higher, he met a friendly bird named Betty. Betty asked, "What are you doing, little ant?" Andy replied, "I want to reach the top of this tree and see the world!" Betty smiled and said, "That sounds fun! I will help you reach the top."

With Betty's help, Andy reached the top of the tree. They looked around and saw many beautiful things. They saw a pretty flower, a big hill, and a blue pond. Andy was so happy he had made a new friend and reached the top of the tree. Together, they had a great adventure, and Andy learned that with a little help, he could reach anything.

Once upon a time, there lived a young person who loved adventure. But, this person was not alone; they had an ancient drawer filled with ancient secrets.

The young person went to the drawer and opened it. Inside were maps, books and an old compass.

The young person looked at the compass and wondered where it could lead them. Suddenly, a friendly voice spoke. 

"Encourage your curiosity!" it said.

The young person smiled and started to explore the maps in the drawer. As they followed each map further, they imagined places they could go and adventures they could have. Suddenly, the compass glowed in the night, leading them to one of the maps.

The young person followed the map and it led them to an ancient temple with many treasures. With encouragement, the young person was able to find the magical treasure! 

Ever since that day, the young person was able to explore their curiosity with the help of the ancient drawer.

Once there was a little girl called Jenny. She was a very cheerful girl. Every day she liked to play with her phone. One day, when she had her phone in her hands, she dared to do something silly. She dared to hide it in a drawer, so her mom and dad couldn't find it.

But Jenny was too smart for her own good. Because she had hidden her phone, when her mom called for her, there was no way for Jenny to answer. She knew she had made a mistake.

So Jenny was very sad. No matter how hard she looked, she couldn't find her phone. It was gone forever. Jenny was no longer cheerful. She had made a bad decision. She should have never dared to hide her phone.

Ben and Lily were best friends. They liked to play with their toys, draw pictures and sing songs. One day, they had a big fight. Ben wanted to play with Lily's new doll, but Lily said no. She said it was her doll and Ben could not touch it. Ben got angry and grabbed the doll from Lily. Lily got angry and pushed Ben. They both started to cry and shout.

"Give me back my doll!" Lily said.

"No, it is mine now!" Ben said.

They did not want to share or say sorry. They turned away from each other and sat in different corners of the room. They felt sad and lonely.

Their mom came in and saw them. She asked them what was wrong. They told her what happened. She said they both did something bad. She said they should forgive each other and be friends again. She said they could both play with the doll if they took turns. She said they would be happy if they did that.

Ben and Lily looked at each other. They remembered how much fun they had together. They did not want to be mad anymore. They said sorry to each other and hugged. They said they forgave each other and they were still best friends. They agreed to share the doll and play nicely. They smiled and laughed.

Their mom was proud of them. She said they did a good thing. She said they showed their will to be kind and fair. She said she loved them very much. She gave them a big hug and a kiss. They felt happy and loved. They thanked their mom and went back to play. They had a great time with their toys, pictures and songs. They were happy.

Sam and Ben are friends. They like to play in the pool. The pool is big and blue. They splash and swim and have fun.

One day, they see a sack near the pool. The sack is brown and heavy. They wonder what is inside.

"Let's open it!" Sam says.

"OK!" Ben says.

They pull the sack to the pool. They open it. They see many balls. The balls are red and yellow and green and purple. They are shiny and round.

"Wow! Balls!" Sam says.

"Let's play with them!" Ben says.

They take the balls out of the sack. They throw them in the pool. They make big splashes. They laugh and cheer.

But then, they see a man. The man is angry. He runs to the pool. He shouts at them.

"Hey! Those are my balls! Give them back!" the man says.

Sam and Ben are scared. They are weak. They cannot fight the man. They say sorry.

"Sorry, mister. We did not know. We just wanted to play," Sam says.

"Sorry, mister. We will give them back. Please don't be mad," Ben says.

The man is still angry. He takes the sack. He takes the balls. He leaves.

Once there was a little boy. He was three years old and loved playing games. One day, his mum told him to do a puzzle. He was excited and went to his bedroom to get it.

When he returned with the puzzle, his little brother was crying. The little boy said, "What's wrong?". His brother said, "Big brother slapped me!" The little boy was very angry. He said, "That's disgusting! You never hit someone, it's wrong!"

The little boy wanted to show his brother what was right and what was wrong. Together, they finished the puzzle and when they were done, the little boy said, "That was fun! Let's do it again. But let's remember never to slap others."

The little brother smiled and said, "Ok!" The two little boys hugged and promised never to hit each other again. Moral of the story; always be kind and never hit anyone.
