But before they left, Lily remembered to lock the door so that no one could come inside while they were playing. They ran outside and had a lot of fun together.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim was a good boy, but sometimes he would scream. He would scream when he was sad, and he would scream when he was mad. One day, Tim found a smooth rock. He liked the rock very much, so he took it to his secret chamber in his room.

In the chamber, Tim would play with his toys and the smooth rock. But one day, his friend, Lily, came to play with him. When Tim showed her the smooth rock, Lily wanted to play with it too. Tim did not want to share the rock, so he screamed at Lily. Lily was sad and left Tim's house.

Tim felt bad for making Lily sad. He thought about what he did and decided to share the smooth rock with her. The next day, Tim went to Lily's house and gave her the rock. They played together and had lots of fun. Tim learned that sharing is good and it makes others happy.

Lily and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toys. They have many toys: cars, dolls, blocks, books, and more. But sometimes their toys are messy. Mom says they have to sort their toys before they can watch TV.

Lily and Ben start to sort their toys. Lily puts the dolls in a pink basket. Ben puts the cars in a blue box. They work together to sort the blocks by color and shape. They put the books on the shelf.

"Look, Mom, we sorted our toys!" Lily says. She is proud of her work.

"Good job, Lily and Ben!" Mom says. She smiles and gives them a hug. "You are very helpful and smart. I love you both."

Lily and Ben hug Mom back. They feel happy and warm. They think Mom is the best.

"Can we watch TV now?" Ben asks.

"Sure, you can watch TV for a little while. But first, let me show you something." Mom says. She takes them to the window and points outside.

"Wow, look at that!" Lily says. She sees a big rainbow in the sky. It has many colors: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, and purple.

"It's so pretty!" Ben says. He likes the rainbow.

"It's adorable!" Mom says. She hugs Lily and Ben again. "Just like you two."

Once upon a time there was a bossy little girl. Every day she would boss her mom and dad around.

Her parents were tired of it and they decided to punish her. They told her she had to go to the hospital.

The little girl was scared and didn't want to go. But her parents said she had to.

When she got to the hospital, she was surprised. All the doctors and nurses were nice to her. They smiled and gave her toys and candy.

Finally, her parents came to get her. They were sorry they had punished her. But they said it was important to be nice and listen.

The little girl learned her lesson. She hadn't been nice before, but now she was very polite. And she never bossed her parents around again.

Once there was a nice little girl who wanted to buy an ice cream with her pocket money. She went to the store, but then realised she only had a few cents.

Suddenly, the little girl saw a mint growing by the store entrance. She carefully picked it and showed it the shopkeeper.

The shopkeeper smiled and said, "If you pay with the mint, I will give you an ice cream for free!"

The little girl was so happy, and thanked the shopkeeper. She paid with the mint, and got the yummy ice cream she wanted.

The little girl was very happy and enjoyed her nice treat. She was glad that she was able to pay with the mint and get her ice cream.

Lucy was excited. She was waiting in front of a big locked door. Her dad was with her. He was unlocking the door with a really big key.

When he opened the door, Lucy saw that behind it was an oak tree. It was so big! She looked up and saw lots of leaves and branches.

Her dad put his hand on her shoulder and pointed to something on the tree. He showed her a little bird's nest filled with feathers.

Lucy was so excited. She ran around the oak tree, picking up feathers and pretending she was a bird. She held the feathers close to her heart and thanked her dad for unlocking the big door and showing her the amazing oak tree.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily who loved to play with water. One day, she decided to pour water on her bed. She thought it would be fun to jump on the wet sheet. But her mom saw what she did and got angry. She scolded Lily and told her not to pour water on her bed again.

Lily felt sad and went to her room. She saw her long hair in the mirror and decided to cut it to make herself feel better. She took a pair of scissors and started cutting her hair. But she accidentally cut too much and her hair became very short. She started crying and her mom came to see what happened.

Her mom tried to fix her hair but it was too short. Lily had to go to school with short hair and all her friends laughed at her. She felt embarrassed and wished she had not poured water on her bed.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Jill. She was very tired, so every day she would take a nap. One day, she decided to take a test while she was napping. As she was sleeping, she heard a loud noise and suddenly her test was split into two pieces! Jill was so shocked that she quickly woke up. She was very surprised to see that the pieces of her test were spread all over. 

Jill quickly grabbed the pieces and put them back together. But no matter how hard she tried, the paper wouldn't stay together. She was getting tired from trying so hard and she knew she had to find a better way. 

She thought for a second and then had an idea! She got some glue from the kitchen and then carefully put the pieces of her test back together. After a few minutes, the test was together again! 

Jill was so relieved that she decided to take another nap. As she slept, she dreamed of all the tests she would split in the future!

Tim and Sam were brothers. They liked to watch television after school. They watched cartoons and games and animals. But their mom said they had to complete their homework first. She gave them books and pencils and paper.

Tim did his homework quickly. He wrote his name and drew some shapes and numbers. He showed his mom his paper. She smiled and said, "Good job, Tim. You are very smart. You can watch television now." Tim was proud. He ran to the living room and turned on the television.

Sam did not do his homework. He did not like to write or draw. He wanted to watch television. He hid his books and pencils and paper under his bed. He sneaked to the living room and joined Tim. He pretended he did his homework too.

But their mom knew. She checked under Sam's bed and found his books and pencils and paper. She was angry. She went to the living room and turned off the television. She said, "Sam, you did not do your homework. You lied to me. You cannot watch television. You have to go to your room and do your homework now." Sam was sad. He cried and said, "I'm sorry, mom. I don't like homework. I like television." But mom did not listen. She took him to his room and closed the door.

Tim felt sorry for Sam. He wanted to share his television with him. But he also wanted to watch his favorite show. He did not know what to do. He looked at the television. He looked at Sam's door. He felt bad. He wished they both did their homework. He wished they both could watch television. He wished they both were proud.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy who loved quizzes. He would make a quiz everyday and ask his friends to play. 

One day, the boy received an invitation to take a special quiz. He was excited because he had never seen a quiz like this before. 

He followed the invitation and it took him to a sour garden. He was surprised to see many sweet and sour fruits growing in the garden. He opened the door and walked in. 

Suddenly, he heard a voice say, "Welcome!" He saw a thick, green monster at the center of the garden. It was the quiz monster. The boy was a bit scared but he was also very excited. 

The monster asked him many simple questions and the boy answered them one by one. Finally, the monster said that he had passed the quiz. The boy thanked the monster and ran home, full of joy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She was only three years old and very spoiled. Everywhere she went, people told her she was the best.

One day, the little girl was walking with her mother and saw a big bowl of ice cream. Eager to have it, she asked for some, but her mother said no. She scowled and let out a big yawn.

The next day, the little girl and her mother were walking by the same bowl of ice cream. The little girl's mother said, "We can have some ice cream now, if you still want it." The little girl smiled and said yes.

When they arrived at the bowl of ice cream, a big crowd had gathered. They were all yawning and complaining that the ice cream was cold. The little girl still wanted the ice cream and asked her mother why everyone was yawning.

Her mother explained that too much of a good thing can be bad. If people economize what they have, they can stay happy. The lesson here is that too much of a good thing can be spoiled, and it's okay to take things in moderation.

Once there was a little boy called Jack who was always very excited. One day he went outside to play and gathered some big stones. His mom noticed and said, "Jack, what are you doing with all those stones?".

Jack smiled and said, "I'm going to remove my stomach!" 

His mom looked so surprised! She said, "You can't remove your stomach. It's not possible and you can get hurt if you try." 

Jack listened carefully and thought for a while. Finally he said, "I know Mommy. I was just pretending. I knew it wouldn't be possible." 

His mom said, "That's my clever boy. You should always use your brain before doing something. It's better to think twice before acting." 

Jack smiled and agreed. He was excited to learn this new lesson and knew that if he used his brain before doing something, he could stay safe.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to have tea parties with her toys. One day, she invited her teddy bear to join her for tea. But when she poured the tea, she accidentally spilled it on her teddy bear. 

"Oh no!" cried Lily. "I'm worried that I ruined my teddy bear."

"Don't worry," said her teddy bear. "I don't value tea as much as I value spending time with you. Let's just enjoy our tea party together."

Lily was relieved and happy to hear this. They continued to have their tea party and enjoyed each other's company. From that day on, Lily knew that spending time with loved ones was more important than things like tea.

Lila was a compassionate girl who liked to help animals. One day, she found a bird with a broken wing in her garden. She gently picked up the bird and brought it inside. She asked her mom to prepare a box with some soft cloth and water for the bird.

"Mom, can we keep the bird until it gets better?" Lila asked.

"Well, we can try, but we have to be very careful. The bird might be scared or hurt. We have to let it rest and not touch it too much," Mom said.

Lila nodded and put the bird in the box. She noticed that one of its feathers was loose. She carefully took the feather and put it in her pocket. She thought it was very pretty and soft.

The next day, Lila checked on the bird. It looked a little better. It moved its wing a little and made a small sound. Lila smiled and whispered, "Hello, bird. I'm Lila. I'm your friend. I hope you feel better soon."

The bird looked at Lila with its bright eyes. It seemed to understand. It made another sound and tilted its head. Lila felt happy. She took out the feather from her pocket and showed it to the bird.

"Look, this is your feather. It fell off yesterday. It's very pretty. Can I keep it? It reminds me of you," Lila said.

The bird nodded and flapped its wing. It seemed to say yes. Lila thanked the bird and put the feather in her hair. She thought they looked like friends. She hoped the bird would get better soon and fly again. She was a compassionate girl who liked to help animals.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Molly. She was very worried, because she had lost her favorite toy. One night, while she was crying in bed, she heard a gentle hooting sound. Molly opened her window and a friendly owl flew in. 

Molly was surprised, but the owl only wanted to help. It flew around the room, searching until it found Molly's toy. It bowed its wings and dropped the toy in Molly's lap. 

Molly was amazed and asked the owl, â€œWhat are you?â€

The owl hooted again and said, â€œI'm an owl! I saw that you were worried so I wanted to come and restore your toy. Now, please have a good night's sleep.â€

Molly thanked the owl and fell asleep with a smile on her face. From that day on, Molly was sure that owls were magical creatures who could make any worries go away.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and run around in the park. One day, she fell and got a cut on her knee. It hurt a lot and she started to cry.

Her mommy saw her crying and asked, "What happened, Lily? Did you hurt yourself?"

Lily showed her mommy the cut on her knee and said, "It's sharp and it hurts."

Mommy took Lily to the doctor. The doctor was very nice and put a bandage on her knee. Lily felt better and asked her mommy, "Is the doctor cheap?"

Mommy smiled and said, "No, the doctor is not cheap, but he helps us feel better when we're hurt."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in the park with her friends. One day, while playing hide and seek, she saw an unusual butterfly. It was so pretty and colorful!

Lily ran to her friends and said, "Look! Look! An unusual butterfly!" Her friends ran over to see it too. They all wanted to catch it, but it was too high up in the sky. "I wish we could reach it," said Lily.

Suddenly, an old man with a kind spirit walked by. "What are you looking at?" he asked. Lily pointed to the butterfly and said, "We want to catch it, but it's too high up." The old man smiled and said, "I have an idea. Let's all hold hands and reach for it together." 

So, they all held hands and reached up towards the butterfly. And to their surprise, the butterfly flew down and landed on their hands. They all smiled and laughed. Lily said, "Thank you, old man. Your spirit is very kind." The old man smiled and said, "You're welcome, children. It's always nice to help others." And they all walked away, happy and content.

One morning, a little boy woke up and looked out the window. It was incredibly interesting. The sunrise was a beautiful mix of blue and yellow.

He was so excited he couldn't wait for the day to start. He quickly got out of bed and put on his shoes.

The little boy was ready for the day, so he went outside. Suddenly, his friend came running up, shouting "Hi!"

The two boys smiled at each other and then started to separate. They wanted to explore different things in the garden.

The little boy was curious, so he wandered around, looking at the flowers and listening to the birds singing.

The sun was shining higher in the sky now and the little boy noticed a butterfly. He watched as it gracefully fluttered away, a reminder of the beauty of the sunrise. 

He spent the morning happily exploring and when he got tired he returned to the house with a smile on his face. He had had an interesting morning.

Once there was a boy. His name was Tommy. Tommy was three years old and he was very restless. He wanted to do different things, but he couldn't. He was obeying the law.

Every day Tommy would hope for something special to happen. He wanted to go on a boat, but he knew that was not possible. He wanted to fly in an airplane but his mom said that was too dangerous. He imagined running down the beach and jumping into the ocean, but his mom said he didn't know how to swim.

Tommy felt restless and wanted more. But he was happy knowing that his mom and dad loved him and obeyed the law. Tommy was a good boy and always hoped for something fun to do. He never got angry and kept hoping for something special.

Once upon a time there was a boy who was very naughty. He loved to play outside in his car. One day he was pushing his car around in the backyard and he wasn't being careful. He went too far and he lost his car! The boy was so sad and he started to cry. 

The boy's mom heard him and came outside to help. She spotted the car over by the fence and ran to get it. She hugged the boy and gave him back his car. The boy was so happy that he had found his car again. 

His mom said that he must always be careful when playing with his car so he doesn't lose it again. The boy said he would and he never lost his car ever again!

Jim and Joe were best friends. Every day, they played together under the warm sunshine.

One morning, when the sun started to rise, Jim and Joe went for a walk. As they walked, Jim looked up and saw the beautiful sunrise. He could feel the warmth of the sun on his face. It was delicious.

Just then, Jim noticed a delivery truck driving by. A smile appeared on his face. He knew that the truck was delivering something special - it was Jim and Joe's favorite food!

They quickly ran back home, and sure enough - the delivery truck was there. Jim and Joe were so excited they could hardly wait! The driver gave them their food, and they thanked him.

Jim and Joe enjoyed their delicious lunch together in the bright sunshine. They were so happy to be together, and they celebrated the beautiful sunrise in their own special way.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. He was a troubled boy who liked to dare his friends to do things. One day, he dared his friend, Sam, to climb a big tree in the park.

Tim and Sam went to the park to see the tree. It was very tall! Tim looked at the tree and said, "I dare you to climb to the top!" Sam was scared, but he did not want Tim to think he was not brave. So, he started to climb the tree.

As Sam climbed higher and higher, Tim watched from below. Suddenly, Sam slipped and fell to the ground. He was hurt and crying. Tim felt very bad for daring Sam to climb the tree. They called for help, and soon, Sam was taken to the hospital.

At the hospital, the doctor helped Sam feel better. Tim promised never to dare his friends to do dangerous things again. From that day on, Tim and Sam played safe games and had lots of fun together. And they lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Susie who wanted to help her mommy with the laundry. But her mommy said no and insisted Susie play in her room instead. So Susie grabbed her favorite toy iron and plopped down in her room. She started to iron her dolls' clothes like her mommy ironed their clothes.

Susie started to feel very nervous as the iron started to get very hot. She decided to go ask her mom for help. She timidly asked her mom, "Mom, the iron is too hot and it scares me." Her mom smiled and came over to help.

"Don't worry Susie," her mom said. "I will help you." But Susie insisted on doing it herself. So her mom showed her how to turn the knob on the iron to make it cooler. Susie was so happy! She gave her mom a big hug and said thank you. Mama smiled and they went back to their chores.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play with her pink blocks. She would stack them up high and then knock them down, giggling with joy. One day, Lily's little brother came over and wanted to play with her blocks too. 

Lily said, "No, these are my blocks. You can't play with them." 

Her brother got sad and said, "Please, Lily. I just want to play with them for a little bit." 

Lily thought about it but then said, "No, I don't want to share." 

Later that night, Lily felt bad about not sharing her blocks with her brother. She regretted not being kind to him. The next day, she went to her brother and said, "I'm sorry for not sharing my blocks with you. Do you want to play with them now?" 

Her brother smiled and said, "Yes, thank you, Lily." They played together and had lots of fun stacking the blocks up high and knocking them down. From then on, Lily always shared her blocks with her brother and they played together happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to bake with her mommy. One day, they decided to make cupcakes. They got out the flour, sugar, and eggs. They used a mixer to mix everything together. 

Lily loved the smell of the cupcakes baking in the oven. When they were done, they took them out and let them cool. Then, they put gray frosting on top. Lily was excited to taste the cupcakes. She took a big bite and smiled. They were delicious!

Once upon a time, there was a girl who was only three years old. She had a favorite bowl that she always used to eat her food with. One day she decided to take the bowl with her when she went out to explore the world.

Unfortunately, she forgot to take the bowl back with her when she went home. She was so sad because she felt like a part of her was missing.

The next day, she decided to look for the bowl. She eventually found it near some weird trees near her home. She was so happy to find her bowl.

From then on, the girl remembered to never forget something special to her ever again. She knew that it always felt weird if she did not have her bowl.

This story tells us that it is always important to remember to pick up something special to us. Even if it might seem small, it can mean so much.

Once upon a time, a man was walking along a path. He had a big glass jar in his hand. Suddenly, he stumbled and the jar fell out of his hand and broke. Shards of glass scattered across the path.

The man felt sad. He wanted to pick up the glass, but it was so small he couldn't see it. Suddenly, he heard a noise. He looked up and saw a little bird hovering over the path. The bird was deaf but it could still feel the man's sadness.

The bird flew around the path collecting all the pieces of glass. It dropped them in the man's hand. The man was so happy and thanked the bird. Then, he gathered all the glass and put it in a small box.

The man was no longer sad and the bird flew away. They both lived happily ever after.

Lila and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a sign that says "Do not pick the berries". The sign has a picture of a red berry with a cross over it.

Lila says, "Look, Ben, berries! They are red and pretty. I want to eat them."

Ben says, "No, Lila, we cannot eat them. The sign says no. They might be bad for us. Let us play on the swings instead."

Lila says, "But I am hungry. And the berries look yummy. Just one, please?"

Ben says, "No, Lila, no. Come on, let us go."

Lila does not listen to Ben. She runs to the bush and picks a berry. She puts it in her mouth. She smiles. She thinks it is sweet.

But then, she feels sick. Her tummy hurts. Her mouth burns. She spits out the berry. She cries.

Ben hears her cry. He runs to her. He sees the berry on the ground. He says, "Oh, no, Lila, you ate the berry. The sign was right. The berry is bad. We need to get help."

He takes her hand and runs to the park keeper. He tells him what happened. The park keeper calls an ambulance. He says, "Do not worry, kids. The berry is not very dangerous. It just makes you feel sick for a little while. You will be fine soon."

Lila and Ben go to the hospital. They get some medicine. They feel better. They say sorry to the park keeper. They say sorry to each other. They learn to obey the sign. They never eat the berries again. They still play in the park. But they play on the swings instead.

Once, there was a farmer who had to make a long journey. To make sure he was ready for the adventure, he packed his bag. He put in food, clothes and more. He even packed a shovel - it was deep and heavy!

The farmer began his journey and walked a very long way. He crossed rivers, walked through a deep forest and climbed a mountain. Finally, he arrived at his destination.

The farmer was so happy he had packed all the things he needed. Without them, he wouldn't have been able to complete his journey! He looked deep into the horizon and grinned. His adventure had officially begun.

Lily and Ben were playing in the garden. They saw a big hole in the ground. It was a well. Lily wanted to look inside the well. She imagined there were many things in the well. Maybe there were fish, or frogs, or coins, or jewels.

"Come on, Ben, let's see what's in the well!" Lily said.

"No, Lily, that's a bad idea. The well is deep and dark. You might fall in and get hurt. Or you might get stuck and no one can hear you. That would be terrible!" Ben said.

But Lily did not listen to Ben. She ran to the well and leaned over the edge. She tried to see what was in the well. She did not see anything. She only saw her own face in the water. She was curious and leaned more and more.

Suddenly, she lost her balance and slipped. She screamed as she fell into the well. She splashed into the cold water. She was scared and wet and cold. She cried for help.

Ben heard Lily's scream and ran to the well. He saw Lily in the water. He was worried and sorry. He ran to the house and called their mom. Mom came with a rope and a bucket. She lowered the bucket into the well and told Lily to grab it. Lily grabbed the bucket and mom pulled her up. Lily was safe but she was still scared and wet and cold.

Mom hugged Lily and wrapped her in a towel. She scolded her for being foolish and disobedient. She told her to never go near the well again. She told her to listen to Ben and be careful. She told her to use her imagination for good things, not bad things.

Lily was ashamed and sorry. She apologized to mom and Ben. She learned her lesson. She realized that the well was not a fun place to play. She realized that Ben was a good brother who cared for her. She realized that imagination was a good thing, but only if she used it wisely. She promised to be more careful and obedient. She thanked mom and Ben for saving her. She hugged them and said she loved them.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was very excited to take a test at school. The test was about colors and shapes. Lily's mom helped her study every night before bed.

On the day of the test, Lily felt impatient. She wanted the test to start right away! Finally, it was time for the test. Lily did her best and answered all the questions correctly. When the test was over, Lily said "thank you" to her teacher.

Lily was happy because she did well on the test. She knew that her mom would be proud of her too. From that day on, Lily loved taking tests because she knew she could do a good job.

Once upon a time there was a boy. He wanted to go on a big adventure, but he didn't know where to go. So he asked his mom. She said why don't you take the road?

So the boy grabbed a bag, packed his lunch and off he went! He walked and walked until he found a new road. His eyes sparkled with excitement, this was it! He'd go here! 

The boy walked and walked and soon he noticed the road was getting richer and richer. He could see flowers, trees and all sorts of plants along the way.

He soon came across a big mountain. The mountain was so big he couldn't cross it! But he had an idea! He decided to add a bridge to the road. He found some nearby sticks, gathered some stones and he built a big bridge over the mountain.

He was so proud of himself! Not only did he find a new road to explore, but he also added a bridge to help him get across it! Now, the boy can travel everywhere and see all the wonderful places the road had to offer!

Tom and Sam are brothers. They like to play with cars and trucks. One day, they find a big battery in the garage. It is shiny and black.

"Look, a battery!" Tom says. "We can use it for our cars."

"No, it is mine!" Sam says. "I saw it first."

They start to fight over the battery. They pull and push and yell. The battery is heavy and hard.

"Ow!" Tom cries. He drops the battery. He looks at his hand. It is red and wet. He sees a sharp metal thing sticking out of the battery. It cut his hand.

"Ha ha, you are hurt!" Sam says. He picks up the battery. He smiles. He thinks he won.

But then, he feels a shock. The battery is hot and zappy. It hurts his hand and arm. He drops the battery. He screams.

Mom hears the noise. She runs to the garage. She sees the boys and the battery. She is scared and angry.

"What are you doing?" she asks. "That battery is dangerous. It is not a toy. It can make fire and burn you. And it is thin and old. It can break and leak bad stuff."

She takes the boys to the bathroom. She washes their hands. She puts bandages on their cuts and burns. She tells them they are naughty and foolish. She says they can't play with cars and trucks for a week. She says they have to stay in their room.

Tom and Sam are sad and sorry. They hug each other. They wish they did not fight over the battery. They wish they listened to Mom. They wish they had a good day.

Mellie was a 3 year old girl who loved to joke around with her mom. Her mom always said Mellie was a "silly goose" when she did it. One day, Mellie was having a lot of fun and she began to joke around. She started saying silly words and waving her hands around.

Mellie's mom smiled and said, "You are such a silly girl Mellie! Do you want to hear a spell?" Mellie was so excited and said yes. 

Mellie's mom started to say the spell, which sounded very strange to her. But as her mom spoke, the spell began to fill the room with a bright pink light. Mellie felt strange and a bit scared, but she kept watching. 

Suddenly, a big pink monster appeared in the room and started leaping around! Mellie covered her eyes and started to cry. Her mom was so shocked that she forgot what the spell was supposed to do. The monster kept leaping around and the pink light began to get brighter and brighter.

Mellie's mom tried to make the monster go away, but it wouldn't. Eventually, the monster leapt towards Mellie and frightened her even more. The monster kept getting closer and closer and Mellie and her mom had to flee their house. They never returned and no one knows what happened to them.

Anna and Ben were best friends. They liked to play in the park every day. They had a lot of fun on the swings, the slide and the seesaw. They always listened to their mums and dads and were very good.

One day, they saw a big hole in the ground. It was a well. They had never seen a well before. They were curious and wanted to look inside. But there was a sign that said: "Danger! Do not go near the well!"

"Let's go and see what's in the well!" said Ben. He was naughty and did not care about the sign.

"No, Ben, we can't!" said Anna. She was scared and did not want to break the rule. "The sign says it's dangerous. We might fall in and get hurt. We should trust the sign and stay away."

But Ben did not listen to Anna. He ran to the well and peered over the edge. He saw some water and some stones. He thought it was boring. He wanted to see more. He leaned over further and further.

"Ben, stop! You're going to fall!" shouted Anna. She ran after him and tried to pull him back. But it was too late. Ben lost his balance and slipped into the well. He screamed and splashed.

Anna was very scared. She did not know what to do. She looked around and saw a man walking by. He had a big hat and a long beard. He looked kind and friendly.

"Help! Help! My friend is in the well!" she cried. She waved her arms and pointed to the well.

The man heard her and came over. He saw Ben in the well and quickly got a rope. He threw one end of the rope to Ben and told him to hold on. He pulled Ben out of the well and hugged him.

"Are you okay, son?" he asked. He checked Ben for any cuts or bruises.

"I'm okay, thank you," said Ben. He was wet and cold and ashamed. He realized he had been very naughty and foolish.

He looked at Anna and said: "I'm sorry, Anna. You were right. I should have trusted the sign and listened to you. You are a good friend."

Anna smiled and said: "It's okay, Ben. I'm glad you're safe. You are still my best friend."

The man smiled too and said: "You are very brave, Anna. You did the right thing to ask for help. You are a good girl."

He took them to their mums and dads and told them what happened. Their mums and dads were very worried and angry. They scolded Ben for being naughty and praised Anna for being good. They thanked the man for saving Ben and gave him a big hug.

Anna and Ben learned a lesson that day. They learned to trust the signs and the rules. They learned to be careful and not to be naughty. They learned to be good friends and to help each other. They never went near the well again.

Lily and Ben are young. They like to play outside. They have a big toy helicopter. They take turns to fly it in the air.

"Look, Lily, I can make it go high!" Ben says. He pushes a button and the helicopter zooms up.

"Wow, Ben, that's cool!" Lily says. She claps her hands. She wants to try too.

"Can I have a turn, Ben?" she asks.

"OK, Lily, but be careful. Don't crash it," Ben says. He gives her the controller.

Lily holds the controller. She makes the helicopter go left and right. She smiles. She likes to fly it.

But then she sees a big bird. The bird flies near the helicopter. The bird wants to catch it.

"Oh no, a bird!" Lily says. She is scared. She does not know what to do.

"Quick, Lily, bring it down!" Ben says. He runs to help her.

But it is too late. The bird grabs the helicopter with its claws. It flies away with it.

"Hey, that's our helicopter!" Ben shouts. He is angry. He wants his toy back.

Lily and Ben are sad. They lose their helicopter. They go inside. They tell their mom what happened.

Mom hugs them. She is sorry. She says, "Don't worry, kids. It's just a toy. Maybe the bird will drop it somewhere. Maybe we can find it later. Or maybe we can get a new one."

She gives them a cookie. She says, "But you know what? You did a good thing today. You shared your toy. You took turns. You were nice to each other. That's more important than a helicopter."

Lily and Ben nod. They feel a little better. They say, "Thank you, mom."

Mom says, "You're welcome, kids. Now, do you want to play something else?"

Lily and Ben think. They say, "Yes, mom. Can we play dress up?"

Mom says, "Sure, kids. What do you want to wear?"

Lily and Ben smile. They say, "We want to wear helmets. We want to be helicopter pilots."

Once upon a time there was a magical jam jar. Every day it filled with a different flavour of sweet jam. One day when the jar was full, the bottom of the jar started to get very hot. The heat melted the bottom of the jar into a big sticky pool.

The jam spread everywhere. It was a big mess! The jam was so sticky that it made the floor rough.

The sticky mess was too big to clean up. So a clever child had an idea. She grabbed a spoon and started scooping the jam back into the jar. Soon, the jar was full of jam again!

The child wanted to make sure the jar didn't melt again. So she put it in the fridge, where it stayed safe and cool. From then on, the jar of delicious jam was always safe from melting away!

Once upon a time, a little girl lived in a big house. One day it was her birthday and her mummy and daddy had a surprise for her! They brought out a big box - inside was a beautiful red cushion! The little girl was so excited she jumped up and down. 

She quickly ran to get her toys, ready to act out stories on the cushion. She opened her dolly's house, got all the dolls out and then put them around the cushion. She made up lots of stories that her dolls could 'act' out on the cushion. 

Every day the little girl would find different toys and act out stories on the cushion. She acted out stories with fire engines and dragons, with little animals and even with her teddies! She had so much fun and the red cushion was the centre of her imagination. 

The little girl would take the red cushion with her everywhere she went - it was such a beautiful and comfy cushion! Even when she was all grown up and moved away, she would take the cushion with her and act out stories. She was never too old for a red cushion with special magical powers!

Lily and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toys in their room. But sometimes they get bored and do naughty things. One day, they find a big roll of toilet paper in the bathroom. They think it is fun to throw it around the room and make a big mess.

"Look, Lily, I can throw it very far!" Ben says, as he tosses the toilet paper over the bed.

"Wow, Ben, you are so strong! I can throw it high!" Lily says, as she throws the toilet paper up to the ceiling.

They laugh and giggle as they see the toilet paper fly and land everywhere. They do not hear their mom coming up the stairs.

"Ben! Lily! What are you doing?" Mom says, as she opens the door and sees the messy room. She is very angry and surprised.

"Uh-oh, Mom is here!" Ben says, as he drops the toilet paper and tries to hide behind the pillow.

"We are sorry, Mom, we were just playing!" Lily says, as she runs to hug Mom and give her a kiss.

Mom sighs and shakes her head. She loves her twins, but they are very naughty sometimes. She tells them to help her clean up the mess and put the toilet paper back in the bathroom. She also tells them not to throw things in the room, because they can break something or hurt someone. She says they can play with their toys or read a book instead.

Lily and Ben nod and say they are sorry. They help Mom clean up the mess and put the toilet paper back in the toilet. They promise not to throw things in the room again. They hug Mom and say they love her. Mom smiles and says she loves them too. She gives them a snack and a story, and they have a nice time together.

One day, a little boy was playing in his backyard when he saw a chamber he didn't recognise. He wandered closer and looked inside. Suddenly, he noticed something was inside, and he panicked! He ran back inside and told his mother.

His mother looked inside, and saw a baby bird. She said the baby was fine and was probably just scared. She carefully brought it out of the chamber and released it into the garden. The little boy watched it fly away feeling relieved that all was well.

However, his relief was short-lived. Looking closer at the chamber, the little boy realised it was a beehive and it was home to a swarm of bees! As soon as he saw them, he panicked and ran away, leaving his mother to deal with the bees.

But with her calm and careful personality, she managed to get rid of the bees without incident and they were all safe. The little boy was relieved, and certainly learnt a lesson about not getting too close to things you don't understand!

One day, a little boy named Tim went to the park. He saw a big slide and a tall tree. Tim wanted to play on the slide, but it was too dry. So, he asked his friend, Sam, for help.

"Sam, can you help me make the slide less dry?" Tim asked. Sam thought for a moment and said, "Yes, I have an idea!"

Sam went to the tree and started to shake it. Many leaves fell from the tree. Tim helped Sam pick up the leaves and put them on the slide. The leaves made the slide not dry anymore.

Now, Tim and Sam could play on the slide. They took turns sliding down and laughed a lot. They were very happy that they could play together on the slide.

Once upon a time, there was a charming little girl called Emma. She liked nothing more than exploring the world with her trusty microscope.

One day, Emma found a very special stone, but it was broken. She wanted to make it special again, so she took it to a wizard who could restore it.

He told Emma: "Don't worry, it can be restored! But it's going to take some magical powers."

Emma smiled, trusting the wizard. After some magical sparkles, beautiful music, and a puff of smoke, the wizard handed the stone back to Emma. She was so happy to see it looking beautiful and whole again!

The wizard winked and said: "Now, Emma, do you see what restoring things can do? When something is broken, remember to use your powers to make it as good as new!"

Once upon a time, there was a poor little girl named Lily. She loved to play with cards and collect them. One day, she met a boy named Max who also liked cards. They became friends and played together every day.

One day, they found a special card that they both wanted. They started to quarrel about who would get it. Lily said, "I saw it first!" but Max said, "I want it more!" They argued and argued until they both got upset and went home.

The next day, Lily brought a surprise for Max. She gave him a shiny new card that she found. Max was happy and said, "Thank you, Lily! You are my best friend!" From then on, they shared their cards and never quarreled again.

Anna and Ben are friends. They go to the same class at school. They like to play and learn together. One day, their teacher tells them they will have a special guest. He is a farmer who will show them some animals.

Anna and Ben are very excited. They love animals. They hope to see a cow, a pig, a sheep, or a horse. They wait for the farmer to come. When he arrives, he has a big truck. He opens the back of the truck and takes out a crate. Inside the crate, there is a small, fluffy, white animal.

"Hello, children," the farmer says. "This is a rabbit. His name is Snowy. He is very soft and gentle. He likes to eat carrots and lettuce. Who wants to pet him?"

All the children raise their hands. They want to touch the rabbit. The farmer smiles and takes out Snowy from the crate. He holds him in his arms and walks around the class. He lets each child stroke Snowy's fur. Snowy is very calm and mild. He does not bite or scratch. He only wiggles his nose and ears.

Anna and Ben are the last ones to pet Snowy. They are very happy. They think Snowy is the cutest animal they have ever seen. They wish they could have a rabbit like him at home.

"Thank you, farmer," Anna says. "Snowy is very nice. Can we give him something to eat?"

"Sure, Anna," the farmer says. "I have some carrots and lettuce in the truck. Do you want to help me get them?"

"Yes, please," Anna says. She looks at Ben and offers him her hand. "Do you want to come with me, Ben?"

Ben nods and takes her hand. They follow the farmer to the truck. They help him carry the carrots and lettuce to the class. They share them with the other children. They feed Snowy and watch him munch and crunch. They laugh and clap. They have a lot of fun. They thank the farmer again for bringing Snowy. They hope to see him again soon.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy had a toy car that he loved to play with all the time. One day, Timmy went to the park to play with his car. He drove it around and around, but then he got tired and wanted to go home.

Timmy started to walk home, but then he realized he had left his toy car at the park. He was sad because he loved his car so much. Timmy's mom saw that he was sad and asked him what was wrong. Timmy told her that he had left his car at the park. His mom said, "Don't worry, we can go back and return to the park to get your car."

So, they went back to the park and found Timmy's toy car. Timmy was happy and thanked his mom for being so useful. They walked home together quietly, with Timmy holding his car tightly in his hand.

Tom and Lily were twins who liked to play outside. They had a big garden with many flowers and trees. They also had a swing, a slide and a sandbox. They loved to swing high, slide fast and make castles in the sand.

One day, they decided to have a picnic in the garden. They asked their mom to make them some sandwiches and juice. Mom said yes and gave them a basket with their food and drinks. She told them to share nicely and have fun.

Tom and Lily took the basket and went to the garden. They found a nice spot under a big tree. They spread a blanket on the grass and opened the basket. They saw four sandwiches and two bottles of juice. They were very hungry and thirsty.

Tom said, "I want this sandwich. It has cheese and ham. It is my favorite." He took the sandwich and bit into it.

Lily said, "I want this sandwich too. It has cheese and ham. It is my favorite." She reached for the sandwich, but Tom pulled it away.

"No, this is mine. You can have the other one. It has peanut butter and jelly. It is your favorite." Tom said.

Lily frowned. She did not like peanut butter and jelly. She wanted cheese and ham. She said, "No, I don't want the other one. I want this one. You are being mean. Give me some of your sandwich."

Tom shook his head. He did not want to share his sandwich. He said, "No, I won't. You can have the juice. I don't like juice. I like water."

Lily did not like juice either. She liked water. She said, "No, I don't want the juice. I want the water. You are being selfish. Give me some of your water."

Tom said, "No, I won't. You can have the sunshine. I don't like sunshine. I like shade."

Lily did not like sunshine either. She liked shade. She said, "No, I don't want the sunshine. I want the shade. You are being silly. Give me some of your shade."

Tom and Lily started to argue. They raised their voices and made faces. They did not notice that their mom was watching them from the window. She saw them fighting and felt sad. She decided to teach them a lesson.

She went to the garden and walked towards them. She said, "What are you doing? Why are you fighting? Don't you know how to share?"

Tom and Lily stopped arguing and looked at their mom. They felt ashamed. They said, "Sorry, mom. We were being bad. We wanted the same things and did not want to share."

Mom said, "That is not nice. Sharing is caring. You are twins. You should love each other and help each other. Do you want to make me happy or sad?"

Tom and Lily said, "We want to make you happy, mom. We love you and we love each other. We are sorry. We will share."

Mom smiled. She said, "That is good. I am glad you are sorry. I have an idea. Why don't you split your sandwiches and your drinks and your shade and your sunshine? That way, you can both have some of everything and enjoy your picnic."

Tom and Lily thought that was a good idea. They said, "Yes, mom. That is a good idea. We will split our things and have fun."

Mom said, "Good. I am proud of you. Now, let me help you. Here, I will cut your sandwiches in half. You can have one half of each. And here, I will pour your juice and your water in two cups. You can have one cup of each. And here, I will move your blanket a little bit. You can have some shade and some sunshine. There, now you have a nice picnic. Bon appetit!"

Tom and Lily thanked their mom and hugged her. They said, "Thank you, mom. You are the best. We love you."

Mom said, "You are welcome, my darlings. I love you too. Now, enjoy your picnic and play nicely. I will be inside if you need me."

Tom and Lily nodded and smiled. They ate their sandwiches and drank their drinks. They felt happy and full. They shared their shade and their sunshine. They felt warm and cool. They played with their toys and with each other. They felt fun and friendly. They had a wonderful picnic. They learned that sharing was not difficult. It was easy and fun. They learned that sharing was caring. It made them and their mom happy. They learned that sharing was good. It made their garden a better place.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Lucy. She was only 3 years old. 

One day, Lucy was very tired. She was so tired she could not go to the park to play with her friends. 

Instead, she decided to stay home and help her mom with the dishes. She watched carefully as her mom put all of the dishes in the dishwasher. "This looks like fun," she thought! 

So Lucy tried it too. She put her plate and cup in the dishwasher and closed the door. She looked very proud and happy that she had helped out. 

Her mom smiled and said, "Good job Lucy! Now how about we take a break? You look very tired." 

Lucy smiled and said, "Yes Mommy, I think I'd like that!"

Once there was a little girl named Kate. She was only three years old and loved to explore. One day, she suggested to her mom that they go to the park. Her mom said yes, so they went.

At the park, Kate found a lot of fun things to do. She found a slide she could go down and a swingset she could play on. She also found a screw on the ground. She didn't know what it was, so she asked her mom.

Her mom said it was a screw and that it could be dangerous. She suggested that Kate not touch it. Kate said OK, but she thought it looked kind of scary. She wanted to play with it but she listened to her mom and left it alone.

When it was time to go home, Kate was sad to say goodbye to the park. She had a lot of fun and learned something new about screws. Her mom said it was time to leave, but Kate knew she would come back soon.

Once upon a time, there was a little triangle. It was very fragile and didn't have any friends.

The triangle went to the park one day and saw two other shapes, a circle and a square. The triangle wanted to join them, but the two shapes didnâ€™t pay attention. The triangle called out â€œHello!â€

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She had a very special bow. It was a soft pink bow with sparkles. Every day the little girl would show her bow to all her friends.

One day, the little girl decided she wanted to show even more people her bow. So she went to the park. As she walked around the park, the little girl held her bow out for everyone to see.
