Mama showed Thomas the little birds singing in the trees. He smiled and clapped his hands in delight. She also showed him the beautiful colours of the sunrise that spread all across the sky.

Thomas was so happy to have seen the sunrise. He thanked Mama for showing him and she hugged him tightly. The sun was now up in the sky and Thomas knew a new day was here.

Once upon a time, in a small village, there lived a weak old man named Tom. Tom had a big iron, which he used to press his clothes. One day, he needed help with his iron because it was too heavy for him.

Tom went to his friend, Sam, and said, "Sam, please help me with my iron. I am too weak to use it." Sam agreed and said, "Sure, Tom. I will help you." So, Sam went to Tom's house and helped him press his clothes with the iron.

After they were done, Tom thanked Sam and said, "Thank you, Sam. You are a good friend." Sam smiled and said, "You're welcome, Tom. I am always here to help you." And from that day on, they became the best of friends and always helped each other when they needed it.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to go to her grandma's house because she always had cookies and milk for her. But one day, Lily's little brother spilled milk on the table and made a big mess. 

Grandma got upset and started to quarrel with Lily's brother. Lily felt sad and didn't know what to do. She remembered her mom telling her to always be helpful, so she went to the kitchen to get a napkin to clean up the mess. 

As she was cleaning, Lily noticed a smelly odor coming from the trash can. She knew that her grandma had forgotten to take out the trash. So, she took the trash out and put a new bag in the can. 

When Grandma saw what Lily had done, she smiled and gave her a big hug. Lily felt happy that she could help and make things better. From that day on, Lily always remembered to be helpful and to keep things clean and tidy.

It was a cold day. The trees were all icy. Kids were outside playing, running and laughing.

In one corner of the playground, a little girl named Emma was drawing in the sand. She was putting patterns and shapes together to design different things.

Suddenly, she saw her friend, Mia, walking towards her. "Hi Mia!" Emma said.

Mia was carrying a big envelope. She said, "I got a surprise for you!"

Emma was so excited that she started jumping. She said, "Let's open it and see what's inside!"

Mia opened the envelope and out came a big icy lolly. Emma was so happy.

She said, "Thanks Mia! I love my surprise!"

Once upon a time there was a girl called Pauline. Pauline wanted to fly one day, but she knew that was impossible because she was too heavy. She was embarrassed about her weight and tried to stop eating so much food.

One day, Pauline's mommy decided to help her. She suggested that Pauline go for a walk every day, to help her become lighter. Pauline was happy with this plan and started walking every day.

Soon, she started to feel lighter and happier. She soon found that she had prevented herself from getting any heavier. Pauline was so pleased with herself!

Every day she went for a walk, and she soon found that she had become the lightest she had ever been. She was so proud of herself that she could fly now! She was no longer embarrassed about her weight and did her best to stay healthy and fit.

The end.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Lucy. She was walking on the beach one day when she found a beautiful shell. She picked it up and was admiring it when suddenly a big wave came and washed the shell away.

Lucy was very sad and was about to cry, but then she heard a noise behind her. It was something big and it was coming closer! Lucy was scared.

She turned around and saw a dangerous-looking animal. She had never seen anything like it before. It had a big, sharp claw and it was snapping at her. Lucy was so scared that she ran away as fast as she could.

Luckily, she managed to get away from the dangerous animal. But from that day on, Lucy was careful when she went near the shell on the beach. She didn't want to get scared again!

Once upon a time, there was a famous airport. All the people around it knew how famous it was. Everyday, many people would miss the airport, because it was so special.

One day, something bad happened. All the people were running away and leaving the airport. It was a sad moment, because everyone missed the airport so much.

When they were gone, there were only a few people left. The airport had no more visitors. It felt so lonely. Then, people started to forget the airport. Everyone stopped talking about it and the famous airport was forgotten. 

The airport was all alone and it missed the people who used to visit it. It was a bad ending for the airport and all the people who used to miss it.

Once upon a time there was a boy. He was troubled. He did not feel happy. He did not know why.

One day he heard a story. This story was about a kind princess. She was kind to everyone. Everyone in the land was happy when she was around.

The boy was interested in the story. He decided to find the princess. He walked and walked until he found her palace.

The princess saw the boy and she smiled. She could tell he was troubled so she asked him what was wrong. The boy told her his story and she listened carefully.

The princess was very kind. She hugged the boy and told him everything would be alright. She showed him around the palace and had fun.

The boy smiled and felt happy. He was no longer troubled. He thanked the princess and went home, happy and content.

Sara was very sad. She had a toy cat that she loved very much. She played with it every day and hugged it at night. But one day, her brother Tom took her toy cat and pulled it very hard. He wanted to see how far it could stretch. He did not care that he was hurting Sara's toy cat.

"Stop it! Stop it!" Sara cried. "You are being terrible! Give me back my toy cat!"

But Tom did not listen. He laughed and pulled harder. He did not see that the toy cat was tearing apart. He did not hear the toy cat make a sad sound. He did not feel Sara's tears on his arm.

Suddenly, the toy cat broke. The stuffing came out and the head fell off. Tom dropped the toy cat and looked at it. He was shocked. He did not mean to break it. He just wanted to have some fun.

Sara ran to the toy cat and picked it up. She sobbed and tried to put it back together. But it was too late. The toy cat was ruined. Sara looked at Tom with anger and sadness.

"You are very bad!" she shouted. "You broke my toy cat! You are not my brother anymore!"

She ran away with the toy cat and locked herself in her room. Tom felt very sorry. He did not know how to fix his mistake. He wished he had not been so terrible. He wished he had not stretched Sara's toy cat. He wished he could make Sara happy again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Rosie. She loved playing outside and was always so excited to wear her red boots! 
One day, Rosie was playing in the park and when it was time to go home, she couldn't find her boots anywhere. She started to cry, asking everyone if anyone had seen them. Then, a kind old man said he had seen her boots somewhere in the park.

Rosie and the man went to look for the boots. After a few minutes of searching, the man found the boots under a tree - and they were still red!

Rosie was so happy and thanked the old man. She put on the boots and ran home, making sure never to forget them again. 
She still wears her red boots every day, for playing in the park and for other adventures.

Avery was so excited. She had been playing with her puzzle when Mom said it was time for a nap. Avery was very tired, but she did not want to miss out on her wild puzzle.

So Avery thought of a plan. She put the puzzle pieces carefully under her pillow and then crawled into bed. Mom tucked her in and Avery closed her eyes.

She pretended to be asleep, but behind her closed eyes, she was thinking about her wild puzzle. Avery felt the pieces under her pillow and imagined all the wonderful shapes and colors.

Soon, Avery felt her eyes getting heavy and she slowly drifted off to sleep. In her dream, Avery worked on her wild puzzle and solved it in no time. She dreamed of wild animals, shapes and colors.

When she woke up, Avery smiled. She grabbed the puzzle pieces from under her pillow and began to work on it again. It was almost complete and Avery felt wonderful. She continued to work on her wild puzzle until it was finished.

Once upon a time, there was a big bird. The bird was very loud and liked to sing all day long. One morning, the sun started to rise and the bird woke up. It looked out of its nest and saw the sun in the sky. The bird started to sing even louder because it was happy. The end.

One day, Dan and his mom went to the store. As they walked around, Dan spotted a bookcase. He quickly started to run!

His mom smiled, and said, "Come join me here. It's okay."

Dan ran over and asked, "What is it?"

His mom said, "It's a bookcase. You can put your books on it." 

Dan thought for a moment, then said, "I want to join!"

His mom gave a slow nod, and said, "Well, okay. Here, take my hand and we'll walk to it together." 

Eventually, they reached the bookcase. Dan looked up and said, "It's really big!"

His mom chuckled and said, "Yes it is. But we'll go slow. We'll figure out how to get it home, okay?" 

Dan smiled and said, "Yes, okay!" So Dan and his mom went slow and carefully carried the bookcase home, already looking forward to all the fun reading they would do together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Alice. She was three years old and loved to explore. Today, Alice wanted to go for a walk in the park. 

Alice grabbed her coat and she went outside with her puppy, Fluffy. In the park, Alice saw a big, green tree and decided to climb it. 

Alice: "Wow! It looks so easy."

Alice easily climbed up to the top of the tree and found a secret hiding spot. Inside the secret spot was a pack of yummy gum!

Alice: "Oh wow! I can have a yummy gum!"

Alice chewed some gum, but she started to get sleepy. She curled up in the tree and fell asleep. When she woke up, the sun was setting and night had come. 

Alice's puppy, Fluffy, was still waiting for her at the bottom of the tree. They both went home and Alice had a great adventure. She thanked the tree for its easy climb and went to bed. 

Alice was so happy and content with her day that night she had the sweetest sleep.

Tom and Lily were twins who liked to play in their room. They had many toys, but their favorite thing was to jump on their big mattress. They pretended it was a trampoline, a boat, or a castle.

One day, their mom told them she had a surprise for them. She said she had mailed a letter to Santa, and he would send them a gift soon. Tom and Lily were very excited. They wondered what Santa would bring them.

The next week, a big box arrived at their door. Their mom said it was from Santa, and they could open it together. Tom and Lily ran to the box and tore off the paper. Inside, they saw another mattress. It was smaller and thinner than their old one.

"What is this?" Tom asked. "This is not a gift. This is stupid."

Lily agreed. She felt sad and angry. "Why did Santa send us this? We already have a mattress. We don't need another one."

Their mom smiled and hugged them. She said, "Santa didn't send you this mattress. He sent you something else. This mattress is for your new baby brother, who will come soon. He will sleep in your room with you, and he will need a place to rest. This is his gift from Santa."

Tom and Lily looked at each other. They felt confused and curious. They had never seen a baby before. They wondered what he would look like, and how he would play with them.

"Can we still jump on our mattress?" Tom asked.

"Of course you can," their mom said. "But you have to be careful and gentle with your baby brother. He is very small and fragile. You have to share your toys and your space with him. He will be your best friend."

Tom and Lily nodded. They decided to give the new mattress a chance. They moved it next to their old one, and made a cozy nest for their baby brother. They hoped he would like it. They also hoped he would like to jump with them, when he was bigger. They thanked Santa for his gift, and waited for their baby brother to come.

Once upon a time there was a daddy. He was a big, strong daddy who had a messy house. He wanted to clean it up, but it was much too big a job. 

So the daddy decided to gather his little one. He said, "You help me clean up this mess, and we'll have a nice time together!". His little one was so excited to help.

So together, the daddy and his little one began to gather the mess. They put toys in the toy box, crayons in the color box, and books in the book shelf. With lots of hard work and laughter, the little one's daddy finished cleaning up the house. 

The daddy and the little one were both very happy. The little one was proud that he had helped his daddy clean and tidy the house. The daddy was proud too, popping bubble wrap with his little one afterwards - it was a job well done!

Once there was a little boy who had a favourite truck that he liked to play with. Every day he would take it with him to the park to show his friends. One day when he went to the park he met a new boy who asked to play with his truck. The little boy was hesitant but he decided to be honest and accept the new boy.

At first, the little boy worried that the new boy might not be kind and careful with his truck. But the new boy said he would be gentle, so the little boy accepted the offer and let him borrow the truck.

The new boy played very nicely with it, and when the time came to go home, he gave back the truck even better than it was before.

The little boy learned an important lesson when the new boy was honest with him. He learned that it is okay to accept help from others, even when it can be scary that things might not work out. Being honest and true will bring great rewards in the end.

Once there was a boy who had a very gifted sister. He wanted to mention her to everyone he met. He knew she was special and he wanted everyone to know it too.

Everyday he brought her up in conversation. Whenever he saw his friends he talked about her. He told them about her cool hobbies, her intelligence and her kind heart.

His sister was thrilled when she found out how much he admired her. She was touched he was so eager to mention her to other people.

The two were closer than ever, and the boy continued to mention his sister to everyone he met. He was so proud and couldn't wait to show her off to the world!

Once upon a time, in a small village, there was a broken toy. The toy was very sad. It could not play with the other toys. One day, the toy had an idea. It wanted to gather all the toys and fix them.

The broken toy told all the other toys about its plan. They all agreed to help. They worked together to gather all the broken toys in the village. They wanted to fix them before the sunset.

But as the sun began to set, the toys realized they could not fix all the broken toys in time. The sunset came, and the broken toys were still broken. The toys felt sad that they could not help their friends. The broken toy's plan did not work, and they all went to sleep with heavy hearts.

Lily was a little bird who loved to fly. She liked to soar high in the sky and feel the wind on her wings. She also liked to sing sweet songs to her friends and family.

One day, Lily smelled something yummy. She followed her nose and saw a big pie on a window sill. It was round and brown and had steam coming out of it. Lily thought it was a gift for her. She flew closer and closer to the pie.

But the pie was not for Lily. It was for Mrs. Jones, who had baked it for her husband. She saw Lily trying to take a bite of her pie and shouted, "Shoo, shoo, go away, you naughty bird!" She waved her arms and scared Lily.

Lily was so frightened that she flew away very fast. But she was not careful and hit a branch on a tree. She fell to the ground and hurt her wing. She cried and cried, because her wing was delicate and now it was broken.

Luckily, Lily's friends and family heard her cry and came to help her. They carried her to a safe place and wrapped her wing with a soft cloth. They gave her some seeds and berries to make her feel better. They told her that she should not try to eat pies that belong to people, because they are hot and dangerous. They also told her that she was a good bird and they loved her very much.

Lily learned her lesson and said sorry to Mrs. Jones. She also thanked her friends and family for taking care of her. She hoped that her wing would heal soon, so she could fly and sing again. She also hoped that Mrs. Jones would make another pie, and maybe share a little piece with her.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. She loved to sing and dance. Her dream was to sing at the opera. Lucy was very patient, always waiting for her chance to shine.

One day, Lucy's mom said, "Today we will go to the opera!" Lucy was so excited. When they got there, Lucy saw a big stage. She wanted to sing on that stage. She asked her mom, "Can I sing on the stage, please?" Her mom said, "Not today, Lucy. But if you keep practicing, maybe one day you can."

At the opera, they saw a play about a fire. The fire was big and red, and it burned very bright. Lucy watched the play and thought about how she would sing on that stage one day.

Lucy went home and practiced her singing every day. She was patient and never gave up. And one day, her dream came true. She sang at the opera, and everyone clapped for her. Lucy was so happy, and she knew that being patient had helped her reach her dream.

Sara and Ben are playing in the yard. They see a big hole in the fence. Sara wants to go and look. Ben warns her.

"No, Sara, do not go. Mom said it is bad. There are mean dogs on the other side. They can bite you."

But Sara does not listen. She is curious. She crawls through the hole. Ben follows her. He is scared.

They see a big dog house. There is a sign that says "Beware of Rex". Rex is a big, black dog. He is sleeping on a rag. He looks angry.

Sara and Ben are quiet. They do not want to wake up Rex. They try to go back to the hole. But Rex hears them. He opens his eyes. He growls. He jumps up. He runs after them.

Sara and Ben scream. They run fast. They reach the hole. They crawl through. Rex cannot fit. He barks. He bites the fence.

Sara and Ben are safe. They hug each other. They are sorry. They say to each other.

"We should have listened to Ben. He was right. Rex is mean. We will not go there again."

Mom hears them. She comes out. She sees the hole. She sees Rex. She is angry. She scolds them.

"You are naughty. You did not obey me. You could have been hurt. You are lucky Rex did not catch you. You will not play in the yard for a week. You will stay inside."

Sara and Ben are sad. They cry. They say to Mom.

"We are sorry, Mom. We learned our lesson. We will not do it again."

Mom hugs them. She is still angry. But she loves them. She says to them.

"I love you, Sara and Ben. But you have to be careful. You have to listen to me. And to each other. You have to be good."

Sara and Ben nod. They say to Mom.

"We love you, Mom. We will be good. We will listen to you. And to each other."

Mom smiles. She is cheerful. She says to them.

"Good. Now, let's go inside. And have some cookies."

Once upon a time, there was a panda. He was a very friendly panda and his name was Pete. One day, Pete's mommy said to him, "Pete, you are going to meet someone special today." Pete was very excited.

When he got to the special place, he saw a girl. Her name was Lydia. She was a very nice girl. Lydia and Pete said hello and introduced themselves to each other.

Pete thought Lydia was really nice and he really liked her. He asked her to come and play with him. Lydia said yes!

The two of them had a really nice time together. They played tag and hide and go seek. Lydia even showed Pete a special tight hug. Pete thought the hug was really nice. 

The two of them became the best of friends after their introduction. Every day, they would go to the park and play together until it was time for Pete to go home. It was a tight friendship that lasted for many years.

One day, his mom saw him looking sad. She asked what was wrong, and Johnny explained that his friend Jimmy had a baseball but he didn't. His mom smiled, and told him to stay right there. She then went and returned with a big surprise â€“ a baseball of his own!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Jenny. She was three years old and loved playing in the park.

One day, Jenny was at the park when it started to rain. She got very wet.

Jenny's mother saw her and ran over to her. She said, "Let's go home and examine the makeup you are wearing."

Jenny happily said, "Okay!" and followed her mum home.

When they got home, Jenny's mother said, "Let's examine your makeup and see if it's still on properly."

Jenny examined it carefully, and found that it was still on, even though she had been out in the rain.

Jenny's mother smiled and said, "Well done. Now, go and find something else to play with."

Jenny smiled and thanked her mother. And she had a wonderful time playing with her toys at home.

Once upon a time, there was a wealthy family who owned a purple house. They all lived happily together in this pretty house, until one day a problem happened.

Suddenly, the house started to shake and roll! Everyone inside the house became scared and started to panic. They started running and screaming as the house shook harder and harder.

Finally, it stopped shaking and the family could get out of the house. When they did, they saw that their purple house had moved across the street! They were so scared that all they could do was laugh.

They found out that an old rich man had moved their house from one side of the street to the other side. All the family laughed so much, knowing that everything was now back to being happy and safe. The end.

One day, a happy cat named Tom found a radio. He lay down next to it and listened to fun songs. He liked the music and started to dance. Tom was so happy that he wanted to show his friend, Sam the dog.

Tom went to Sam's house and said, "Sam, come see what I found! It plays fun songs!" Sam came with Tom to see the radio. They both lay down and listened to the music. They were very happy and danced together.

But then, the radio stopped playing music. Tom and Sam were sad. They tried to make it work, but they could not. They lay down next to the radio, not happy anymore. The fun songs were gone, and they missed them.

Once upon a time, there was a happy girl named Lily. She loved to dance and twirl around in her pretty dress. One day, she went to visit her friend who lived in a big house with lots of toys. Her friend's dad was a wealthy man who had a big knife collection. 

Lily and her friend were playing with dolls when they heard music coming from the living room. They went to see and found the dad dancing with his wife. They looked so happy and free. Lily wanted to dance too, so she started to move her body to the beat. 

Suddenly, the dad stopped and showed them his knife collection. Lily was amazed by how shiny and sharp they were. But she knew that knives were not toys and should only be used by grown-ups. So, she went back to dancing with her friend, feeling grateful for the simple joys in life.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play hide and seek with her friends. One day, she found a big sheet in her house. It was clear and shiny. Lily decided to use the sheet to play hide and seek with her friends.

She hid under the sheet and waited for her friends to find her. They looked everywhere but they couldn't find her. Lily giggled as she heard her friends calling her name. She was happy that the clear sheet helped her hide so well.

Finally, Lily's friends found her under the sheet. They all laughed and played together. Lily was happy that she found the sheet and had so much fun playing with her friends.

Sara and Tom were playing with their toys in the living room. They liked to pretend they were superheroes and villains. Sara was the good superhero and Tom was the bad villain. They ran around the room, making noises and having fun.

But then, they heard a loud noise from the kitchen. It sounded like a big crash. They stopped playing and looked at each other. They were frightened. What was that noise? They wondered.

They decided to go and see what happened. They held hands and walked slowly to the kitchen. They saw their mom and dad standing by the counter. There was a broken plate on the floor and some food spilled. Their mom and dad looked angry and sad.

"What happened?" Sara asked.

"We had a fight," their mom said. "We were arguing about something and we dropped the plate. We're sorry we scared you."

Sara and Tom felt sorry for their mom and dad. They didn't like to see them fight. They wanted them to be happy and love each other.

They hugged their mom and dad and said, "We love you. Please don't fight. Please unite."

Their mom and dad smiled and hugged them back. They said, "We love you too. You're right. We shouldn't fight. We should unite. We're sorry we made a mess. Let's clean it up together."

They all worked together to clean up the kitchen. Then they went back to the living room. They turned on the screen and watched a funny movie. They laughed and cuddled on the couch. They were happy and united.

"What is this place?" said Lucy, "This place is so special."

Suddenly, she heard a little voice call out, "Lucy, I have a surprise for you." 
Lucy was scared but the voice sounded kind, so she followed it and it led her to a big old tree.

The voice said, "Lucy, look inside the tree." Lucy opened the little door to the tree, and inside she found a sparkly fairy.

"Lucy, I just want to show you a little bit of wonder. Why don't you come with me and we can explore the woods together."

Lucy hesitated. She looked up at the sky and saw dark clouds gathering. She remembered the trembling feeling she had felt when she first arrived. She was worried something bad would happen.

But the fairy remained cheerful and said, "Don't worry, I'm here to protect you. So please, come explore with me and together we will find some peace."

Once upon a time, there was a sailor. He liked to travel on his boat. One day, he woke up feeling grumpy. He didn't know why he felt that way. He went to his boat and started to sail. 

As he sailed, he saw many things like fish and birds. He felt a little better. Then, he saw a big whale. The whale was so big that the sailor felt small. The sailor forgot about feeling grumpy and felt happy to see the whale. 

After a while, the sailor went back home. He felt tired but happy he had traveled and saw many things. He went to bed and had good dreams about his adventure on his boat. The end.

Sara was a smart girl who liked to read books and learn new things. She had many books in her room, but she wanted more. She asked her mom and dad to buy her more books, but they said no. They said she had enough books and she should share them with her brother and sister.

Sara was not happy. She did not want to share her books. She thought her brother and sister were not smart enough to read them. She sighed and went to her room. She locked the door and started to read a book about the weather. She liked to learn about the sun, the rain, the wind and the snow.

But soon she heard a knock on the door. It was her brother. He said he wanted to read the book about the weather with her. He said he liked to learn about the sun, the rain, the wind and the snow too. Sara said no. She said the book was hers and he could not read it. She told him to go away.

Her brother was sad. He sighed and went to his room. He did not have many books, but he had a toy car. He liked to play with his toy car and make it go fast. He thought maybe Sara would like to play with his toy car too. He went to her door again and knocked. He said he wanted to share his toy car with her. He said they could play together and have fun.

Sara said no. She said she did not like toy cars. She said they were boring and silly. She told him to go away again.

Her brother was very sad. He sighed and went to his room. He did not want to play with his toy car alone. He wished Sara would be nice to him and share her books.

But Sara did not care. She kept reading her book about the weather. She thought she was very smart and did not need anyone else.

But then something happened. The weather changed. It started to rain very hard. The rain made a loud noise on the roof and the windows. Sara was scared. She did not like the rain. She wanted it to stop. She wanted to see the sun again.

She ran to her mom and dad. She said she was afraid of the rain. She asked them to make it stop. They said they could not make it stop. They said the rain was part of the weather and they had to wait for it to pass. They said they could read a book or play a game to pass the time.

Sara said she did not want to read a book or play a game. She said she wanted to see the sun. She said she hated the rain. She said she hated the weather.

Her mom and dad looked at her. They said she was not being smart. They said she was being selfish and rude. They said she should be grateful for the books she had and the weather she had. They said she should be kind to her brother and sister and share with them. They said they loved her, but they were disappointed in her.

Sara felt bad. She realized she had been wrong. She realized she had hurt her brother and sister. She realized she had been ungrateful and foolish. She sighed and said she was sorry. She said she wanted to be smart and nice. She said she wanted to share her books and play with her brother and sister. She said she loved them and the weather.

Her mom and dad smiled. They said they were proud of her. They said they forgave her. They said they loved her too. They hugged her and said they would read a book and play a game with her and her brother and sister.

Sara was happy. She ran to her room and opened the door. She saw her brother and sister waiting for her. They had brought their books and toys. They said they wanted to share with her and learn with her and have fun with her. They said they loved her and the weather.

Sara smiled. She said she loved them and the weather too. She said she was sorry for being mean. She said she wanted to be smart and nice. She said she wanted to share her books and play with their toys. She said they were the best brother and sister ever.

They hugged and laughed. They read the book about the weather and played with the toy car. They learned about the sun, the rain, the wind and the snow. They had fun and were happy.

The rain stopped. The sun came out. The weather was beautiful. Sara was smart and nice. She learned a lesson. She learned to share and be kind. She learned to love her family and the weather. She learned to be happy.

Once upon a time, there was a girl. Her name was Daisy and she was very intelligent.

She lived on a farm with her family. Every morning, Daisy's mom would cook food for everyone. Daisy wanted to help her mom cook, so her mom taught her how to make pancakes.

When the pancakes were ready, Daisy was so proud! Everyone in the family were so happy with Daisy's pancakes.

From then on, Daisy helped her mom cook all the time. She was so happy to help her mom make delicious food for everyone. The family was very proud of Daisy.

Once upon a time there was a girl. Her name was Jane. Jane was a very special girl. She had special power.

One day, Jane went outside and saw a weird bird. She wanted to play with the bird, but it flew away. Jane was sad.

Then, a kind man came by and asked if Jane needed help. Jane told him about the bird. The kind man said, "I have a thing that can help you!" He gave Jane a pair of binoculars. They let her see far away.

The kind man said, "I need to go now, but you can keep the binoculars. You can lend them to your friends later when you are done." Jane was very happy and thanked the kind man.

From then on, Jane was able to use her power to see far away and help her friends. She always remembered to lend the binoculars when she was done playing with them.

There was once a silly dog who liked to eat things. One day, he had an idea. He thought it would be fun to bite into an apple. So, the dog got an apple and bit into it. But it turned out the apple was too hard. The dog's teeth couldn't bite through the apple. He tried and tried but he couldn't get through it. Finally, he gave up and decided not to bite the apple anymore. He had a silly idea but it didn't work out!

Anna liked music very much. She liked to sing and dance and clap her hands. She also liked to listen to her big sister play the violin. The violin made pretty sounds that made Anna happy.

One day, Anna saw a violin in a shop window. It was small and shiny and had a bow. Anna wanted the violin very much. She asked her mom, "Can I have the violin, please?"

Mom looked at the violin and said, "That violin is very expensive, Anna. We don't have enough money to buy it. Maybe when you are older, you can have a violin."

Anna felt sad. She wanted the violin now. She said, "But I want to play the violin like big sister. I want to make pretty music."

Mom hugged Anna and said, "I know, sweetie. But playing the violin is not easy. You have to practice a lot and learn many things. Big sister has been playing for a long time. Why don't you ask her to teach you some songs?"

Anna thought about it. She liked big sister and she liked to learn. Maybe she could play the violin with her someday. She said, "Okay, mom. I will ask big sister to teach me. But can I still look at the violin in the window?"

Mom smiled and said, "Of course, you can. But remember, the violin is only a thing. The music is in your heart."

Anna nodded and smiled. She held mom's hand and walked to the window. She looked at the violin and imagined playing it. She heard the pretty sounds in her head. She felt happy. The violin was distant, but the music was close.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside in the park. One day, he found a treasure in the sand. It was a shiny gold coin. Timmy was so happy and wanted to show his mom. 

But suddenly, the coin disappeared from Timmy's hand. He looked around, but it was nowhere to be found. Timmy was sad and confused. He asked his friends if they had seen it, but they hadn't. 

Timmy's mom came to pick him up, and he told her about the treasure. She was alert and asked him to show her where he had found it. But when they got there, the treasure was gone. 

Timmy was disappointed and his mom was worried. They went home and Timmy couldn't stop thinking about the treasure that had disappeared. He learned that sometimes, things don't stay with us forever.

George was very excited. He was going to the park with his mom. He grabbed a key and skipped to the door. He wanted to open it on his own. He tried the key in the door, but it wouldn't turn. He tugged and tugged, but nothing happened. Suddenly, the key snapped! George was ashamed. He started to tear.

Mommy came over and said "It's ok, George. We can use my key instead." She put the broken key in her pocket. She hugged George and wiped away his tears.

George was still ashamed, but he felt better. Mommy opened the door with her key, and the two of them went to the park. They had a wonderful time playing games and eating ice cream. Before the day was over, George had forgotten all about the broken key.

Ben and Sam were brothers. They liked to play with their trucks in the yard. They had big trucks and small trucks, red trucks and blue trucks, trucks that made noise and trucks that were quiet.

One day, they saw a new truck in the street. It was a shiny black truck with a big bow on it. "Wow, look at that truck!" Ben said. "It must be a gift for someone. Maybe it is for us!" Sam said. They ran to the truck and touched the bow. It was soft and smooth.

"Hello, boys," a voice said behind them. They turned and saw a man with a smile. He was wearing a hat and a coat. "Do you like my truck?" he asked. "Yes, sir, it is very nice," Ben said. "Can we play with it?" Sam asked. The man nodded. "Sure, you can. Why don't you hop in and see how it feels?" he said.

Ben and Sam were happy. They climbed into the truck and sat on the seats. They pretended to drive and honk the horn. The man closed the door and locked it. He went to the front and started the engine. He drove away with the boys inside.

Ben and Sam were scared. They tried to open the door and the window, but they could not. They shouted and cried, but no one heard them. The man did not stop. He took them far away from their home and their mom and dad. He was a bad man. He wanted to sell the boys to someone else.

Ben and Sam were sleepy. They had no food and no water. They hugged each other and hoped someone would find them. But no one did. They never saw their trucks or their yard or their family again. They were very sad. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play pretend with her toys. One day, she decided to pretend that she was a princess. She put on a sparkly dress and a tiara on her head. 

Lily's little brother, Max, came to play with her. He wanted to play too. Lily said, "You can be the prince in my kingdom." Max was happy and said, "Okay, I will be the prince." 

They played under the big oak tree in their backyard. Lily used her creative imagination to make up a story about the princess and the prince. Max listened carefully and played along. They had so much fun pretending to be in a magical kingdom. 

As the sun started to set, their mom called out to them. "Time to come inside for dinner!" Lily and Max didn't want to stop playing, but they knew they had to go in. They promised to play pretend again tomorrow.

Once there was a big race involving all of the animals. They were running on a track that zig zagged through a great big forest. As the race began, the animals ran as fast as they could.

One of the animals was a stubborn little rabbit. He wanted to win the race so he ran faster than everybody else. But one of the animals saw him cutting across the track. He was trying to ignore the rules.

But the wise old owl knew what the rabbit was doing. He wouldn't let the rabbit ignore the rules and he made sure to bring the rabbit back to the track.

The rabbit kept running and running but the owl stayed close behind. The rabbit was so stubborn and wanted to win but in the end he didn't. He came in second place, just behind the owl. The other animals congratulated the owl and ignored the stubborn rabbit.

Once there was a little girl named Jill. She had a special blanket. It was fit and snug around her tiny body.

Whenever Jill was scared she would grab her blanket and hug it tight. She felt safe and calm when she had it.

One day she was in her bed, playing with her blanket. She saw a monster, in her room! It tried to fright her. Jill screamed and grabbed her blanket. Quickly, she ran and hid in the corner.

Then, she took a deep breath. She remembered what her mummy saidâ€¦ She was brave and strong!

Jill stood up and marched right over to the monster. It was so scared it started to shake! Jill said â€œI sack you, go away!" The monster ran right out of the room.

Jill smiled and hugged her blanket. She felt fit and brave and she knew she could take on any monster with her blanket by her side.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in her garden. One day, she saw a beautiful rose. She was curious about it and wanted to touch it. But her mother warned her, "Don't touch the rose, Lily. It has thorns that can hurt you."

Lily felt sad and asked her mother, "Why can't I touch the rose? It looks so pretty." Her mother replied, "You can look at it and enjoy its beauty, but you don't need to touch it."

The next day, Lily went to the garden and saw a butterfly stuck in a spider web. She wanted to help the butterfly, but she was scared. She remembered what her mother had said and realized that sometimes we don't need to touch things to appreciate them. She carefully took a stick and gently freed the butterfly.

From that day on, Lily learned that sometimes we need to be patient and careful. We don't always need to touch things to enjoy them. And most importantly, we need to help others when they need it.

Once upon a time there was a spoiled little boy named Noah. Noah loved playing all day long. One day he saw something very strange, a fan in his garden. He ran to his dad and said, "Dad! Dad! What's this?" His dad replied, "That's a fan, Noah." Noah was so excited, he grabbed it and started playing with it. He moved the fan around and around and something amazing happened. 

Suddenly, the fan revealed something special, a large box full of presents! Noah was so surprised and happy. Then, his dad said, "Oh, Noah it looks like someone left you a present. You must have been very good this year." Noah knew he had been spoiled this year and smiled. The fan had revealed a whole box of presents!

Ben and Lily liked to play with their toys in their room. They had many toys, but their favorite ones were the blocks. They could make many things with the blocks, like houses, cars, and animals. They had a big shelf where they kept their blocks and other toys.

One day, they decided to make a big tower with their blocks. They wanted to make the tallest tower ever. They took all the blocks from the shelf and started to attach them together. They made the tower higher and higher, until it reached the ceiling.

"Wow, look at our tower!" Ben said. "It is so big and original!"

"Yes, it is amazing!" Lily said. "Let's show it to Mom and Dad!"

They ran out of the room to find their parents. They wanted to make them proud of their tower. They did not see that their tower was not very stable. Some of the blocks were loose and wobbly.

When they were gone, the tower started to shake. It leaned to one side, then to the other. It could not stand anymore. It fell down with a loud crash. It hit the shelf and made it fall too. The shelf and the tower broke into many pieces. The blocks and the other toys scattered all over the floor.

When Ben and Lily came back with their parents, they saw the mess. They were shocked and sad. Their tower was gone. Their shelf was broken. Their toys were ruined.

"Oh no, what happened?" Mom asked.

"Our tower fell down!" Ben cried.

"And it broke our shelf and our toys!" Lily sobbed.

Mom and Dad were angry and disappointed. They scolded Ben and Lily for being careless and wasteful. They told them to clean up the mess and to go to bed without dinner. They took away their blocks and said they could not play with them for a long time.

Ben and Lily felt very sorry and ashamed. They wished they had not made such a big tower. They wished they had been more careful and respectful. They learned a hard lesson that day. They never forgot it.

Once upon a time, there was a popular dinosaur. He liked to play and explore in the forest, and every day he would gather stones. All the other dinosaurs noticed and started to gather stones too.

One day, the popular dinosaur went deep inside the forest. When he came back, he held something in his mouth. All the other dinosaurs wondered what it was.

"What have you got?" One of the dinosaurs asked. 

"It's a surprise," the popular dinosaur replied with a mischievous sparkle in his eye. He gathered the other dinosaurs round him and showed them what was in his mouth. 

It was a big red shiny stone. Everyone was amazed. It was so sparkly, shiny and bright.

Suddenly, the popular dinosaur shouted, â€œLetâ€™s make a sparkle mountain! We can gather all the stones in the forest and pile them up in a neat stack.â€

The other dinosaurs agreed and they set to work. Before long, they had built a huge sparkle mountain with all the stones they had gathered. All the dinosaurs celebrated and they all agreed that the popular dinosaur was the best!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy had a friend named Billy. They played together every day and had lots of fun. But one day, Billy was being rude to Timmy. He wouldn't share his toys and kept pushing Timmy away.

Timmy felt sad and didn't know what to do. He wanted to play with Billy but he didn't like how he was acting. So, Timmy decided to settle the problem by talking to Billy. He told him how he felt and asked him why he was being mean.

Billy realized he was wrong and said sorry to Timmy. They hugged and became friends again. From that day on, Billy was never rude to Timmy again and they played together happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a beautiful horse called Daisy. Daisy lived in a stable and loved eating hay. She was very fragile, and not very strong, but she was extremely kind to everyone she met.

One day, Daisy was feeling very lonely, and wished she had someone to share the hay with. Then, she heard a rustling noise coming from the back of the stable. She walked towards it, and saw a little foal lying in the hay. 

Daisy was so surprised and happy to meet the foal. She quickly ran up, and nuzzled the new friend. The foal was also very happy to meet Daisy, and it recognized her right away. They instantly became best friends, and shared their hay everyday. 

They laughed and ran and played together. Daisy made sure to take extra care of the foal, because she knew it was very fragile.

The two friends never parted and were inseparable. They loved their hay and each other, and they both recognized that they had something special.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play in their room. Sometimes they make a big mess with their toys and clothes. Mommy is not happy when she sees the mess.

One day, Mommy says, "It is time for a bath, Anna and Ben. You are very dirty and messy. Come with me to the bathroom." Anna and Ben do not want to stop playing. They say, "No, Mommy, we want to play more."

Mommy is not happy. She says, "You have to take a bath, Anna and Ben. It is good for you. You will feel clean and warm. I have a surprise for you after the bath." Anna and Ben are curious. They wonder what the surprise is. They follow Mommy to the bathroom.

Mommy fills the tub with water and bubbles. She helps Anna and Ben take off their clothes and get in the tub. They splash and play with their rubber ducks and boats. They wash their hair and body with soap. They have fun in the bath.

Mommy says, "It is time to get out, Anna and Ben. You are very clean and shiny. Here is your surprise." She gives them each a soft and fluffy bathrobe. Anna's bathrobe is pink and Ben's bathrobe is blue. They put on their bathrobes and hug Mommy. They say, "Thank you, Mommy, for the bath and the bathrobes. We love you."

Mommy says, "I love you too, Anna and Ben. You are very sweet and good. Now let's go to your room and clean up the mess. Then we can read a story and go to bed." Anna and Ben agree. They hold Mommy's hand and go to their room. They put away their toys and clothes. They make their bed and tidy their room. Mommy is happy. She reads them a story and kisses them good night. Anna and Ben fall asleep in their cozy bathrobes. They dream of more surprises.

Once upon a time, there lived two sisters - Mona and Toni. Mona was three years old and Toni was seven. Mona and Toni loved to play. Mona especially liked to play with dolls.

One day, Mona was playing dolls with Toni when suddenly, Mona's doll broke. Mona was very sad, it seemed like her doll was broken beyond repair.

Toni said to Mona, "Don't worry, Mona. Let's get you a new doll".

Mona replied, "No, Toni. I don't want a new doll. I want to fix my doll".

Toni said, "I don't know if you can fix it, Mona. The body is very distant".

Mona smiled and said, "Don't worry, I can fix it".

So, Mona got to work and in no time, she had fixed her doll. Mona was so happy, she gave Toni a big hug.

Mona's doll was back to its old self and everything was good again. Mona and Toni enjoyed many more games together.

Lily and Tom were playing in the park. They saw a big tree with red apples. Lily wanted to eat an apple. She tried to reach for one, but she was too small.

"Tom, help me get an apple!" she said.

Tom was taller than Lily. He climbed on a rock and stretched his arm. He grabbed an apple and gave it to Lily.

"Thank you, Tom!" Lily said. She bit the apple. It was sweet and juicy.

But then they heard a loud voice. It was the farmer who owned the tree. He was angry.

"Hey, you kids! Stop stealing my apples!" he shouted. He ran towards them with a stick.

Lily and Tom were scared. They dropped the apples and ran away. They did not want to get hit by the stick.

They ran back to their mom, who was sitting on a bench. She hugged them and asked what happened.

"We saw a big tree with red apples, mom. We wanted to eat one, but the farmer was angry. He chased us with a stick, mom. He was mean!" Lily said.

Mom looked at the tree and the farmer. She understood. She said, "I'm sorry, kids. You should not take things that are not yours. The farmer worked hard to grow the apples. He was angry because you took them without asking. Next time, you should ask first, or find another tree with no one around."

Lily and Tom nodded. They felt sorry for the farmer. They learned a lesson. They wondered if the farmer would forgive them. They hoped he would. They decided to say sorry to him next time they saw him. They also decided to share their toys with each other. They hugged mom and said, "We love you, mom." Mom smiled and said, "I love you too, kids."

Once there was a strong cow. Every day the cow would decide what treat she wanted to have. She usually decided to have fresh grass, but one day she decided to have some bad food instead. 

The cow ate the bad food and soon she got sick. The cow became weak and couldn't stand. 

The farmer tried to help the cow, but it was too late. The cow got worse and worse until she passed away. 

The farmer was very sad and gave the cow a big hug. He was very upset that the cow decided to eat the bad food and it had a bad ending.

Once upon a time there was a dancer. She was a happy girl and loved to dance. One day she wanted to go for a swim. So she went outside and put on her swimming suit. She jumped into the pool and started to soak. The water felt cold, but it felt nice too. After a while, she looked up and saw a distant dancer performing in the sky. She thought it was the most beautiful sight she had ever seen. She was so happy that she started swimming around, just to get closer to the distant dancer. 

Although she swam and swam, the dancer never got any closer. But that didnâ€™t stop the happy girl from trying. Every day sheâ€™d go out and swim and try to get closer. She soaked up the sun and just enjoyed watching the distant dancer dance. She realized that no matter how close she thought she was getting, the distant dancer would always stay far away. 

She had lots of fun that summer trying to get closer to the distant dancer. Eventually, the summer ended and it was time for her to go home. But when she closed her eyes, the distant dancer was still in the sky dancing for her.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Lily went on an adventurous walk in the park with her mommy. They saw many trees and flowers, and even some birds flying in the sky.

Lily was thirsty and asked her mommy for some water. Her mommy poured some water from a bottle into a cup for her. Lily drank the water and felt much better.

As they continued their walk, the sky started to get dark. Lily told her mommy that she was scared of the dark. Her mommy hugged her and said, "Don't worry, I'm here with you. We'll get through it together."

Lily felt much better and they continued their walk until they reached home. Lily was happy and told her daddy all about their adventurous walk in the park.

Once upon a time, there was a little brown mouse looking for something. He was searching high and low but he couldn't find it. He became sad and confused. Suddenly, he noticed a big nut in the distance. He knew this nut was just what he was looking for!

The little mouse tried to get to it, but it wasn't easy. The nut was high up and there were no stairs to climb. He began to struggle but he wasn't giving up. He tried again and again.

Finally, after a long search and lots of struggling, the little mouse reached the nut. He was so happy. He ate the nut and enjoyed it. Now, every day the little mouse searches and struggles to find something else yummy.

Tim and Sam were brothers who liked to play outside. One day, they found a filthy cat under their porch. The cat was hurt and scared. It had a big cut on its leg and dirt on its fur.

"Look, Sam, a cat!" Tim said. "Can we help it?"

Sam nodded. He ran inside and got some water, a towel and a bandage. Tim stayed with the cat and talked to it softly.

"Don't be afraid, cat. We are nice. We want to heal you. You can be our friend."

The cat meowed and let Tim touch it. Sam came back and helped Tim clean the cat's wound and wrap it with the bandage. The cat purred and licked their hands.

"Good cat. You are brave. What is your name?" Sam asked.

The cat looked at them with big eyes and meowed again.

"Let's call him Lucky. He is lucky we found him." Tim said.

Sam agreed. They carried Lucky inside and gave him some milk and food. They made a cozy bed for him in a box. Lucky snuggled with them and fell asleep.

Tim and Sam smiled. They were happy they healed Lucky. They hoped he would stay with them forever.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat rice with her family every day. One day, Lily's little brother got a toy that she really wanted. She felt jealous and sad.

But then, Lily's brother did something amazing! He danced and sang a silly song. Everyone in the family applauded him and cheered. Lily felt happy for her brother and forgot all about her jealousy.

After dinner, Lily's mom gave her a big hug and told her how proud she was of her for being happy for her brother. Lily felt warm and loved inside. From that day on, Lily learned that it's better to be happy for others than to feel jealous.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Lily wanted a puppy. She asked her mommy every day, "Can I have a puppy, please?" But her mommy always said no.

One day, Lily went to the park and saw a lovely puppy playing with its owner. The puppy was so cute and friendly. Lily wished she could have a puppy just like that one.

A few days later, Lily's mommy surprised her with a puppy of her own! Lily was so happy and couldn't believe it. She gained a new friend and companion. She named her puppy Daisy and they played together every day. Lily was so grateful for her lovely puppy and knew she would always take care of her.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play on his tablet screen all day long. But his mom said it was time to surrender the tablet and go outside to play. Timmy didn't want to surrender his screen, he wanted to keep playing his game.

Timmy's mom took the tablet away and told him to go outside and play. Timmy got crazy mad and started to cry. He didn't want to play outside, he wanted his tablet screen back. But his mom said no and told him to find something else to do.

Timmy went outside and saw his friends playing with a ball. He joined in and they had so much fun. Timmy realized that surrendering his screen wasn't so bad after all. He had a great time playing with his friends and forgot all about his tablet screen.

Once there was a yellow bird named Steve. He lived in a big tree but he was alone. He wanted to make friends but he didn't know how. 

One day Steve got an idea. He would build a house in the tree and maybe someone would come and join him. He worked so hard and he gathered sticks, leaves and feathers. With a lot of hard work, Steve was able to build his house. 

The next day, a little frog came near Steve's house. He was looking for a place to escape from the rain. Steve was so happy. He welcomed the frog into his house and they became friends. 

They both worked together to make the house bigger and better. They decorated it with yellow flowers, painted it yellow and made it the most beautiful house. 

Steve and the frog spent many happy days together in their house in the tree until one day a bird showed up. She had been searching for a place to escape from the storm. Steve and the frog made her feel welcome and she became their new friend. 

Steve, the frog and the bird lived happily ever after in their yellow house in the big tree.

One day, Tom and his Mom went to borrow a movie. Tom was excited to pick a special one. He asked his Mom if they could borrow an action movie, one that was exciting and would make him laugh. His Mom said, "Let's check the shelves and see what we can find, then you can decide."

Tom and his Mom looked at all the movies. There were funny ones, exciting ones, and some that were scary too. Tom looked extra carefully for just the right one. Finally, he found one that looked fine.

He pointed it out to his Mom and asked, "Can we borrow this one?" She nodded and said, "Yes, we can borrow this one!"

Tom was so excited to finally have the movie he wanted. He knew it was going to be an adventure and he couldn't wait to watch it. He hugged his Mom and thanked her.

When they got home, Tom was so happy to put the movie in and get ready to watch. It was going to be a fun night!

John was excited about Tuesday. It was a special day for him. Every Tuesday, he got to study with Ms. Lisa. He liked her very much because she always was so kind and nice.

John put on his special t-shirt and packed his pencil and paper into his bag before he left the house. He waved goodbye to his mom and ran all the way to Ms. Lisaâ€™s house.

When he arrived, Ms. Lisa showed him the room filled with books. John was amazed. He had never seen so many books before! Ms. Lisa then showed him an atlas and said, â€œToday we are going to study geography.â€

John was thrilled. He giggled and said, â€œImpressive! Letâ€™s get started!â€

Ms. Lisa smiled and began to tell him all about the world. They spent the whole afternoon looking at maps, learning about continents, and exploring. John enjoyed it so much that he asked to stay longer.

At the end of the day, John waved goodbye to Ms. Lisa. He thanked her for teaching him about the world and for making Tuesday such an impressive day.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Jone and Peter. They played in the sunshine, in the park and grew very happy together. But one day a loud sound filled the air and they didn't understand what it was. 

"What's that noise?" Asked, Jone. 
Peter replied, "It's a war. Sad things happen in wars." 

Jone and Peter became very sad and scared. They both knew that wars made people unhappy and so they started to grow a garden together. 

They planted all kinds of beautiful flowers, trees and vegetables. As the garden grew bigger, so too did their smiles. 

By working on the garden and caring for the plants, Jone and Peter found a new way to be happy. They had grown a garden of joy!

Once upon a time, there was a dolphin named Dolly. Dolly was very gifted and could jump very high out of the water. One day, a boy named Timmy went to the beach to play. He saw Dolly swimming and wanted to say hello. Timmy kicked his feet and ran to the water to meet Dolly. Dolly splashed water all over Timmy and they became friends. From that day on, Timmy would visit Dolly every day and watch her jump high out of the water. He thought Dolly was the most gifted dolphin in the whole wide world.

Sara and Ben were playing in the living room. They liked to pretend they were grown-ups. Sara found an empty ashtray on the table. She thought it was a hat. She put it on her head and said, "Look at me, Ben! I'm a princess!"

Ben laughed. He saw a book on the shelf. He thought it was a treasure map. He took it and said, "Look at me, Sara! I'm a pirate!" He opened the book and pointed at a picture. "This is where the gold is!"

Sara and Ben decided to go on an adventure. They walked around the room, looking for clues. They bumped into a lamp and made it fall. They heard a loud noise and saw a flash. They smelled something bad. They saw smoke coming from the lamp.

"Uh-oh," Sara said. "We broke the lamp!"

"Run!" Ben said. "It's a fire!"

They ran to the door and tried to open it. It was locked. They started to cry. They were scared.

"Help!" Sara shouted. "Help!"

"Help!" Ben echoed. "Help!"

Mom and Dad heard their cries. They ran to the living room. They saw the smoke and the broken lamp. They saw Sara and Ben by the door. They unlocked the door and opened it. They hugged Sara and Ben and took them outside.

"Are you okay?" Mom asked. "What happened?"

"We were playing," Sara said. "We didn't mean to break the lamp."

"We were sorry," Ben said. "We were afraid."

Mom and Dad looked at the empty ashtray on Sara's head and the book in Ben's hand. They smiled. They were glad Sara and Ben were safe.

"It's okay," Dad said. "We know you were playing. But you have to be careful. Lamps are not toys. They can be dangerous."

"And ashtrays are not hats," Mom said. "They are for grown-ups who smoke. Smoking is bad for you. You should never touch an ashtray."

Sara and Ben nodded. They took off the ashtray and the book. They said they were sorry again. They said they would not play with lamps and ashtrays anymore.

Mom and Dad kissed them and said they loved them. They said they would clean up the mess and fix the lamp. They said they would read them a story later.

Sara and Ben smiled. They loved Mom and Dad. They were happy. They learned a lesson. They went to play with their toys. They did not raise any more trouble.

Once there was a mom and a dad. Every night they asked their three-year-old, Jack, if he was hungry. Every night Jack said yes, so Mom and Dad cooked steak for him.

Mom said, "Here is your steak, Jack, it smells fair!"

Jack looked at the meat. He had never seen so much meat before. He said, "I don't want it, it's too much!"

Mom and Dad laughed and Dad said, "Come on, Jack. it's just the right amount. Answer the question, do you want it?"

Jack smiled and said, "Yes, I want it!" So, Mom and Dad gave him the steak.

Jack ate all the steak and said, "Delicious!"

Tom and Sam are friends. They like to play with cars. They have many cars of different colors and sizes. They make sounds like vroom and beep when they move the cars.

One day, they find a big car in the garage. It is red and shiny. It has four wheels and a steering wheel. Tom and Sam want to try it. They climb inside the car and pretend to drive.

"Let's go to the park!" Tom says.

"OK!" Sam says.

They turn the key and the car starts. It makes a loud noise. Tom and Sam are happy. They push the pedals and the car moves. They turn the steering wheel and the car goes left and right.

But they do not know how to stop. The car goes faster and faster. They see a tree in front of them. They are scared.

"Stop! Stop!" Tom shouts.

"I don't know how!" Sam cries.

They look for a button or a lever that can stop the car. They see a word on the dashboard. It says reverse. They do not know what it means, but they think it might help.

"Push it! Push it!" Tom says.

Sam pushes it. The car makes a beep sound and changes direction. It goes backwards. It goes away from the tree. Tom and Sam are relieved.

But they do not see the fence behind them. The car hits the fence and breaks it. The car stops. Tom and Sam are shocked. They hear a voice.

"Hey! What are you doing with my car?" It is the owner of the car. He is angry. He comes out of the house and sees the damage.

Tom and Sam are sorry. They get out of the car and say sorry to the owner. They say they were playing and did not know how to stop.

The owner is still angry, but he sees that they are just kids. He tells them that the car is dangerous and they should not touch it. He tells them to go home and tell their parents what they did.

Tom and Sam nod and run away. They are sad and scared. They say they will never play with cars again. They say they will play with something else. Something that has rhythm and is not dangerous. Like drums.

Lily and Ben were playing in the garden. They saw many flowers of different colors. Lily liked the pink ones best. Ben liked the yellow ones best. They picked some flowers and gave them to each other.

"Thank you, Lily. Your flower is very pretty," Ben said.

"Thank you, Ben. Your flower is very bright," Lily said.

They smelled their flowers and smiled. They saw a big flower that was not open yet. It was green and round.

"What is that?" Lily asked.

"I don't know. Maybe it is a ball," Ben said.

They touched the green flower. It was soft and fuzzy. They tickled it with their fingers. The green flower moved a little.

"Wow, it is alive!" Lily said.

"Maybe it is a bug," Ben said.

They were scared and curious. They moved closer to the green flower. They heard a small sound. It was like a sneeze.

"Ah-choo!"

The green flower opened. It was a sunflower. It had many yellow petals and a brown center. It looked at Lily and Ben with a happy face.

"Hello, little ones. I am Sunny. I was sleeping. Your tickles woke me up. They felt like a massage. Thank you for making me bloom," the sunflower said.

Lily and Ben were very surprised. They had never heard a flower talk before. They did not know what to say. They looked at each other with confused eyes.

"Hello, Sunny. We are Lily and Ben. We are sorry for waking you up. We did not know you were a flower. We thought you were a ball or a bug," Lily said.

"That's okay. I don't mind. You are very nice and friendly. Do you want to be my friends?" Sunny said.

"Yes, we do. You are very nice and friendly too. And very beautiful," Ben said.

They smiled and hugged the sunflower. They became friends. They played and talked in the garden. They learned many things from Sunny. They had a lot of fun.

Once upon a time, there was a brave little boy. He wanted to be the best, but he had a lot to learn. He practiced hard each day but he wasn't succeeding.

One day, he heard about a special whip. This whip could help him learn and succeed! So the little boy ran to get the special whip. When he got there, the whip was filthy and covered in grime.

The little boy was brave, so he cleaned the whip. He scrubbed and scrubbed, until the whip was nice and shiny. He was so excited and couldn't wait to try it out.

He practiced and practiced with his new whip. And soon he was succeeding more and more. The brave little boy had finally found his special whip!

Once there was a brave little girl called Sarah. One day, Sarah was feeling very adventurous and decided to take a walk in the woods near her house. As she walked, she kept an eye out for the creek she had heard so much about. With each step, the creek seemed closer and closer! 

Finally, Sarah got to the edge of the creek. She paused and looked down. The water looked so clear and the sun shone brightly in a fair way on the surrounding rocks. Sarah was tempted to jump in, but something made her hesitate. She thought it was too dangerous and she was scared to dare it. 

Still, Sarah just couldn't resist the urge to feel the water. She slowly made her way down the side of the creek, until she was standing right at the edge. She slowly reached out her hand to touch the water. It felt even colder than she expected. 

Sarah looked in amazement - the creek was so much more beautiful than she expected! She finally mustered up the courage to jump in. She was delighted to find out that the water was still quite shallow. She realized that it was nothing to be afraid of, and she delighted in the feeling of the fair waters on her skin. 

From that day forward, Sarah was always up for a dare. She had overcome her fear of the creek, and she came to know it like the back of her hand.

Lily and Ben were playing in the garden. They had a big blanket and some toys. They wanted to have a picnic under the sun.

"Let's spread the blanket here, Ben," Lily said. She put the blanket on the grass and smoothed it with her hands.

"OK, Lily," Ben said. He opened the toy chest and took out some plates, cups and food. He put them on the blanket. "Look, we have sandwiches, juice and cookies. Yum!"

They sat on the blanket and ate their picnic. They talked and laughed and shared their food. They felt happy and warm in their chests.

"This is a lovely day, Lily," Ben said. He smiled at his sister.

"Yes, it is, Ben," Lily said. She hugged him. "You are a lovely brother."

They finished their picnic and packed their toys. They folded the blanket and put it in the chest. They held hands and went back to the house. They had a lovely time in the garden.

One day, a little girl named Lucy went to the store with her mom. They wanted to buy sugar for a cake. On the way, they saw a big, scary dog. Lucy was scared, but her mom said, "Don't worry, it's just a dog."

When they got to the store, Lucy's mom told her, "Stay here and rest while I get the sugar." Lucy sat on a bench and waited. A little boy came up to her and said, "Hi! My name is Tom. What's your name?" Lucy said, "I'm Lucy. We are getting sugar for a cake."

Tom and Lucy played together while they waited for Lucy's mom. They talked about the scary dog and how they both didn't like scary things. When Lucy's mom came back, she had the sugar and some candy for Tom and Lucy. They all went home to make the cake and had a fun day together.

Once upon a time there was a boy. His name was Ben. Ben was 3 years old and he loved buying things. Every day he would go to the store with his mom. Today they were going to buy some new toys.

They went to the store and Ben looked around. Then he saw some colorful toys that he wanted to buy. But something wasn't right. There was a thief in the store! He was sneaky and wearing a filthy coat.

Ben yelled, "Mommy, the thief has toys!" His mom looked around and saw the thief. She called for help and the thief ran away.

Mommy hugged Ben and said, "You did the right thing by telling me about the thief. Thank you for keeping us safe."

"You're welcome," said Ben. He was so happy that he and his mom were safe. From then on, he was even more careful when they went to the store.

Once upon a time there was a smart girl named Sam. She was very intelligent and loved to play, dance and run. One day she decided to ignore her friends and go to the park on her own.

At the park, Sam saw many other kids playing and laughing. She wanted to join in the fun too, but they ignored her. Feeling lonely, Sam watched the other kids playing, and felt more and more sad until finally she went home.

That night, Sam made a plan. She decided that tomorrow she would be brave, so that when she went back to the park her friends would no longer ignore her.

The next day, Sam went back to the park and said hello to everyone. They were surprised and welcomed her with open arms. From then on, no one ignored Sam again. They all had fun playing together and soon became best friends. 

Sam was proud of herself for being brave and making friends. She proved that being intelligent and positive can help turn a bad day into a fun one.

John was walking around outside when he saw something very impressive! It was a tall cactus with bright green spikes. He had never seen something like it before. 

John started running towards it, excited to get a closer look. He touched it with his hands to feel its sharp spikes. But then, he heard a voice.

"Where do you think you're going?" it said.

John turned around and saw a small cactus near the tall one. The small one had a face and it was talking to him. 

John said, "I'm just going to look at the tall cactus. Its so impressive!"

The small cactus said, "You can look all day, but if you want to see the really impressive one, you have to go inside." 

John took a step back, looking around. It was very dark inside the cactus. But then he remembered what the small cactus said. So he took a deep breath and went inside. 

John was amazed. Inside the tall cactus was a magical waterfall, glowing with bright colours. He had never seen anything so impressive!

Once upon a time there was a nosy bird. It wanted to look at all the things in the world. One day it decided to stay near a nest full of baby birds.

The nosy bird watched the baby birds very carefully. It tried to listen to their conversations. It was very excited when they started to play.

But soon the mother bird noticed the nosy bird. She told it to go away. The nosy bird didn't want to leave so it stayed where it was.

The mother bird was a bit annoyed so she told the nosy bird a story. It was a story about the dangers of being nosy.

After the story was finished the nosy bird flew away. It learned an important lesson that day. It was important to stay away from things that don't belong to you and to not be too nosy!

Once upon a time there was a girl named Tess. She loved to swim in the sea and one day, while she swam, she met a dolphin. Tess was so happy that she talked to the dolphin. She said: "Hi dolphin! Will you be my best friend?" The dolphin smiled and said: "Yes, I will be your best friend." 

Tess and the dolphin played together every day but one day Tess had a lot to do so she forgot to go to the beach and meet her dolphin friend.

When Tess remembered, she was very sad and she said to herself: "I hope my dolphin still remembers me and is still my friend." 

So Tess went back to the beach and there was the dolphin, smiling. The dolphin said: "Hello Tess! I knew you would come back and be my friend again. You are so honest." Tess was very happy and the two of them kept playing together.

The end.

One day, a little girl saw something very exciting at the beach. It was a big, red dolphin waving its tail! She smiled and waved back at the friendly dolphin. The dolphin swam closer and closer and it seemed like it wanted to play.

The little girl was so happy. She ran close to the shore and waved at the dolphin some more. She could even feel the splash as the dolphin jumped through the waves.

The little girl wanted to get closer. She wanted to touch the friendly dolphin, so she tried to wade into the ocean. But the water was too deep and she only managed to get wet.

The little girl watched as the dolphin swam away. She waved goodbye, feeling a little sad that they couldn't play together. But in her heart she knew that she'd get to play with the dolphin again soon.

Once upon a time, there was a swan named Lily. She was very pretty and had feathers as white as snow. One day, Lily went to the pond to swim but she saw that it was very dirty. She didn't like it at all. 

Lily decided to organize a group of ducks to help her clean the pond. They worked hard, but suddenly a mean alligator appeared. He wanted to eat Lily and her friends. 

But Lily was very brave and used her strong wings to scare the alligator away. She saved all her friends and they continued to clean the pond until it was sparkling clean. As a reward, they all shared a juicy orange that they found near the pond. From that day on, Lily and her friends knew that they could always count on each other to solve any problem.

Mandy and her friends were playing in the park near a beautiful fountain. "Wow!" Mandy said. "It looks so peaceful." She admired the fountain and the children watched as the water bubbled. Suddenly, Mandy had an idea. "Let's stir the water!" she exclaimed.

The children laughed and walked up to the fountain. They grabbed sticks and began to stir the water. The water swirled and splashed as they moved the sticks around. 

Mandy noticed that the churning water was getting stronger and stronger. "Let's get out of here," she said. "Something isn't right." Her friends followed her lead and they ran away from the fountain. Just then, the fountain burst through the top and water came flying out. 

Mandy and her friends watched in awe at the display. "That was close," she said. "I'm glad I had a feeling that something was wrong." 

The children eventually went back to the fountain, this time to admire its force and beauty. They had stirred the fountain in the most peaceful way.

On Tuesday, Tom had to dress in his best clothes. He did not like his best clothes. They were too tight and too scratchy. He wanted to wear his blue shirt and his green pants. But his mom said no. She said they had to go to a big place with many people. She said it was important.

Tom did not want to go to the big place. He wanted to stay home and play with his toys. He liked his toys. They were fun and colorful. They made him happy. But his mom said no. She said they had to go to the big place. She said it was for his dad.

Tom did not understand. He asked his mom where his dad was. He missed his dad. He had not seen him for many days. He wanted to hug him and hear his voice. But his mom said nothing. She just hugged him and cried.

They went to the big place. It was a church. There were many people. They were all dressed in black. They looked sad and quiet. Tom did not know them. He felt lonely and scared. He held his mom's hand.

They walked to the front of the church. There was a big box. It was covered with flowers. Tom saw a picture of his dad on the box. He remembered his dad. He loved his dad. He wanted to see his dad. He ran to the box. He tried to open it. He shouted, "Dad, dad, where are you?"

But the box did not open. The people gasped. The mom screamed. The priest stopped. Tom cried. He did not know. He did not know that his dad was gone. He did not know that it was his dad's funeral. He did not know that he would never see his dad again.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park. They saw a big brown dog with a ball in his mouth. Lily liked dogs and wanted to pet him. Ben was afraid of dogs and stayed away.

"Come on, Ben, he is nice!" Lily urged. She ran to the dog and reached out her hand. The dog growled and showed his teeth. Lily got scared and ran back to Ben.

"See, I told you dogs are bad!" Ben said. He hugged Lily and tried to make her feel better.

A man came and called the dog. He saw Lily and Ben and said, "I'm sorry, kids, he doesn't like strangers. He is very old and grumpy. You should always ask before you touch a dog. They might bite you if they feel threatened."

Lily and Ben nodded and said, "We're sorry, sir. We won't do it again."

The man smiled and said, "That's good. Dogs can be good friends, but you have to respect them and their space. Here, you can have his ball. He doesn't play with it anymore."

He gave them the ball and walked away with the dog. Lily and Ben thanked him and played with the ball. They learned to be careful and polite with animals.

One day, Sarah and her mommy went to a big, wide field. The field was bright and green and the sun made the grass look like golden coins.

Mommy patted the seat next to her so Sarah squished in. The two of them watched some black birds fly near the edge of the field.

Mommy and Sarah started to discuss the birds. Their wings were so thin and long! They talked about the colors on their feathers, and how they seemed to almost float away.
