Sarah pointed and said, â€œLook, mommy! The birds even have brown eyes!â€

Mommy nodded, â€œYes, Sarah. They do. What wonderful creatures.â€

The two of them smiled and watched in awe until the birds flew over the horizon. They hugged each other before beginning their walk home.

Lily was a little girl who liked to play dress-up. She had many clothes and hats and shoes in her big sack. She liked to pretend she was a princess or a fairy or a doctor. One day, she found a veil in her sack. It was white and shiny and had flowers on it. Lily put it on her head and felt very pretty.

She wanted to show her veil to her friends. She ran outside with her sack and her veil. She saw Anna and Ben playing with a ball. She called them and said, "Look at my veil! Isn't it lovely?" Anna and Ben looked at her and smiled. They said, "Yes, it is very lovely. Can we try it on?" Lily said, "No, it is mine. You can't have it." She hugged her sack and her veil and ran away.

She saw Tom and Mia playing with a doll. She called them and said, "Look at my veil! Isn't it wonderful?" Tom and Mia looked at her and nodded. They said, "Yes, it is very wonderful. Can we see it?" Lily said, "No, it is mine. You can't touch it." She hugged her sack and her veil and ran away.

She saw Sam and Zoe playing with a puzzle. She called them and said, "Look at my veil! Isn't it amazing?" Sam and Zoe looked at her and frowned. They said, "Yes, it is very amazing. But why are you so mean? You don't want to share with anyone. You are not a good friend." Lily said, "No, you are not good friends. You want to take my veil. It is mine. You can't have it." She hugged her sack and her veil and ran away.

She ran and ran until she reached a big tree. She sat under the tree and looked at her veil. She felt very lonely and sad. She wished she had someone to play with. She wished she had someone to tell her how pretty she was. She wished she had someone to hug her and make her happy. She realized she had been very selfish and rude. She had hurt her friends' feelings. She had been fearful of losing her veil, but she had lost something more important: her friends.

She decided to go back and say sorry to her friends. She hoped they would forgive her and play with her again. She put her veil back in her sack and ran back to where she had seen them. She saw them playing together and having fun. She felt very sorry and ashamed. She went to them and said, "I am sorry, friends. I was very mean and silly. I don't want to keep my veil to myself. I want to share it with you. You can try it on and see how lovely you are. You can play with it and have fun. You are more precious to me than my veil. Will you be my friends again?" Her friends looked at her and smiled. They said, "We are happy you are sorry, Lily. We forgive you and we love you. You are a good friend. We are glad you want to share your veil with us. It is very kind of you. You are very lovely, too. Come and play with us." They hugged her and took turns wearing the veil. They played and laughed and had a good time. Lily felt very happy and grateful. She learned that sharing is caring and that friends are more valuable than things.

The little girl was feeling very independent. She had a flashlight in one hand and she was ready to explore. She stepped outside and began to look around. There was a big tree in the front yard and she wanted to see what was up in the branches. She clapped her hands together and the lights on the tree came on. She squealed with delight and pointed the flashlight at each of the tiny lights. It was so exciting! She clapped her hands again and the lights turned off. She smiled and ran back inside. She loved being independent!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He loved to play outside with his friends. One day, Timmy and his friends were playing hide and seek. Timmy hid in a big sack that was lying on the ground. His friends couldn't find him, so they started to yell his name. Timmy felt safe inside the sack, but he wanted to surprise his friends. So, he jumped out of the sack and scared them. They all laughed and continued playing their game. Timmy was happy that he could have fun with his friends and be safe at the same time.

Once there was a very gloomy label. The label was all by itself, with no friends to play with. So, it decided to try and find some new friends. 

The label went on a journey to look for them. First, it partied up a mountain, but all the animals and plants were too busy to stop and chat. Then, it ventured down into a big wide valley, but all the animals and plants were too busy to notice it. 

Disheartened, the label kept going. After a while it found a river which looked more inviting. The label partied downstream and discovered a wonderful meadow filled with friendly animals and plants. The label was so happy and waved to all its new friends. 

The gloomy label soon made many new friends, and never felt alone again.

Once upon a time there was a young girl named Lucy. She was 3 years old and loved to play all the time. One day she went to school for the first time. She was so excited! 

She went to her classroom and met all her friends. They had fun playing together and exploring their classroom. 

But then Lucy slipped on the floor, which made all of her friends laugh. Lucy was so embarrassed. She was very rude and said mean words to them. 

The teacher saw this and said, "We must be nice and polite to our friends. Lucy, it's not nice to say mean words." 

Lucy felt bad for saying mean words to her friends, so she said she was sorry and gave them big hugs. From then on, Lucy remembered to be nice and polite in the classroom.

Tom and Sue are friends. They like to play on the farm. They see many animals on the farm. They see cows, pigs, sheep, and horses.

One day, they see a big gray horse in the barn. The horse is eating hay. Tom and Sue want to pet the horse. They go near the horse and say hello.

"Hello, horse. You are big and gray. Can we pet you?" Tom asks.

The horse looks at Tom and Sue. He nods his head. He likes Tom and Sue. He lets them pet his nose and mane. He makes a soft sound. He is happy.

Tom and Sue are happy too. They smile at the horse. They say thank you. They give the horse some more hay. They hug the horse. They are friends with the horse. They have fun on the farm.

Once upon a time, there was a strong winter. It was so cold that it made the wind rush around. One day, a brave little girl named Amy decided to go out into the cold. She wore a big warm coat and rushed around in the snow. She played tag with her friends, built igloos and threw snowballs. Everyone was so happy and the winter was so strong she did not get cold.

But then it started to snow and the snowflakes got bigger and bigger. Knowing it was too dangerous to stay out in the cold, Amy rushed back home. Even though she was safe and warm indoors, she still liked to look out of the window and watch the flakes fall. All of a sudden, she saw a bright yellow leaf fluttering in the snow - a sure sign of the end of winter.

Amy was so excited. She loved winter but she knew that a new season was coming soon and she wanted to explore it too. She waved goodbye to the snow, knowing that the strong winter was over.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to take naps every day, but her brother Jack liked to prevent her from sleeping. He would make fake noises and jump on her bed. This made Lily very upset.

One day, Lily decided to talk to Jack about how his actions made her feel. She told him that she really needed her nap time and that he was preventing her from getting the rest she needed. Jack felt bad and promised to stop.

From that day on, Jack stopped making fake noises and jumping on Lily's bed during nap time. Lily was so happy and grateful that she gave Jack a big hug. They both realized that talking things out and understanding each other's feelings was the best way to solve their conflict.

The farmer woke up early. He looked up at the light. It was still very dark outside. Then he went to the barn. In the barn, he could see the animals. He looked at the cows, chickens, pigs and sheep. They were all looking at him. He smiled.

The farmer walked around the barn. He talked to the animals and patted them. He understood how to look after them. He gave them food and made sure they were okay.

Then, he went outside to the fields. He looked up at the light in the sky. It was getting brighter and brighter. He started to work. He dug the ground and planted some seeds. Little by little, he understood how to make the plants grow.

When the sun was high in the sky, the farmer looked around. He was proud of all his work. The light shone around the farmer and the animals. He was happy.

Once upon a time, there was a bee who liked to dream. He dreamed of flying and exploring the world, but the other bees said he was too slow. He sat on a leaf and sighed. Suddenly, he heard a buzzing sound. It was a hive full of other bees! He wanted to join them, but he was afraid. He tried again and again, but he was still too slow.

One day, he decided it was time to make his dream come true. He flew around the hive, a bit slower than the other bees, but he still kept up with them. He felt like he was part of the hive! He flew with his new friends and enjoyed the warm summer air. He felt so happy and free!

He thanked the hive for helping him make his dream come true. It was the best day ever! Now, he'll never forget the hive and his slow but steady wings!

Mommy and baby brother went to the store. Inside, they saw lots and lots of toys. Mommy asked, "What do you want baby brother?" Baby brother said with a big smile, "Please birthday!" Mommy answered, "Well, that's a great choice!" 

They looked around the store and found a great birthday present. Mommy asked, "How about this!" She held up a box with a bright and organized birthday toy inside it. Baby brother smiled and said, "Yes! Please!" 

Mommy and baby brother headed home to plan a birthday party. They invited all of baby brother's friends and it was so much fun. There were games, cake and presents - it was the most organized birthday ever!

Once upon a time there were two best friends, Tom and Tim. Tom and Tim were playing in the park.

Tim said to Tom, "Let's play hide and seek!"
Tom was so excited and they started to look for a good hiding spot.

Tom found a secret spot behind the big tree. It was very attractive, with lots of colorful flowers. Tim counted to three and Tom hid behind the tree.

Tom waited and waited, but Tim couldn't find him. Tom started to giggle. Finally, Tim found Tom and said, "You found a secret place! It's so attractive!"

Tom beamed with pride and said, "I did! Let's see who can find the best secret spot next time!"

Tom and Tim laughed and continued to play.

Once there was a little girl. Her name was Amy. One day, she wanted to go on an adventure. So she asked her mom if she could go and explore. Mom said, "Yes, but be careful and stay close by."

Amy was so excited. She looked around and found a big long field. "This is perfect," she thought. She walked into the field and started to explore. She saw butterflies, flowers and bee's buzzing around. 

Suddenly, she heard a voice. "Help! Help! Can you help me find my way home?"

Amy looked around and saw a small rabbit in the corner. "Don't worry, little rabbit," she said. "I'll help you find your way home!"

She followed the rabbit through the long field until they reached a small wood.

The rabbit said, "Thank you for helping me find my way home. I'll never forget you!"

Amy smiled and waved goodbye. Then, she continued with her adventure until it was time to go home. 

What a wonderful day she had!

Once there was a mommy and a daddy. Mommy and Daddy had a little girl. Her name was Lily.

One day, Lily saw a snake. She was scared! Then, Lily's Daddy saw the snake too. He said, "Don't worry, Lily. I will get rid of the snake."

Lily and Daddy talked and discussed what to do. Daddy said that the snake needed to go away. Lily agreed. 

Then, Daddy got a shovel. He was really loud. The snake heard the noise and ran away. Lily and Daddy smiled. 

The mommy came outside and asked, "What's going on?". Lily and Daddy discussed what had happened and then the mommy smiled, too. They were all happy that the snake was gone. 

Lily said, "Let's celebrate. Let's have ice cream!" Mommy and Daddy smiled and agreed. They all had a wonderful time. 

The End.

Once upon a time, there lived a long microphone. It lived in a house with lots of people. One day, all the people wanted to remove the microphone from the house. So they thought of a plan and all came together to pick the microphone up, even the little ones.

The microphone was so long and heavy, that many of the people had to help. After much effort, they finally managed to get it outside. Everyone was very proud and clapped their hands.

But then a funny thing happened. The microphone started singing. Everyone laughed and started dancing around the microphone. The party was so good that no one wanted to remove the microphone anymore.

So the microphone stayed in the house, and even though it was sometimes loud, everyone was happy with it around. They all agreed that the long microphone was cool. The End.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and explore the world around her. One day, she found a shiny violin in her attic. She was curious about it and wanted to play it.

Lily tried to play the violin, but it didn't sound right. She asked her mom to help her, but her mom didn't know how to play it either. Lily was sad because she couldn't make music with the violin.

One day, Lily's grandpa came to visit. He saw the violin and knew how to play it. He showed Lily how to hold the violin and play it. Lily was so happy! She played the violin every day and got better and better. She was careful not to spoil the violin and always put it back in its case when she was done playing.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big truck. The truck has a lot of gold. The gold is shiny and bright.

"Wow, look at the gold!" Anna says. "It is so pretty!"

"Can we touch it?" Ben asks. "Maybe it is soft and warm."

They run to the truck. They want to touch the gold. But a man is in the truck. He is sleepy. He does not see Anna and Ben.

"Hello, mister!" Anna says. "Can we see your gold?"

The man wakes up. He is angry. He yells at Anna and Ben.

"Go away, you little rats!" he says. "This is my gold! You cannot have it!"

He honks his horn. He scares Anna and Ben. They run away. They are sad and scared.

"Sorry, mister!" Ben says. "We just wanted to meet your gold!"

They go back to the park. They find a shiny rock. They pretend it is gold. They are happy again. They play with the rock. They forget about the truck and the man.

Once upon a time, there was a good little girl named Emily. She liked playing in the park with her friends and looking at the flowers and trees.

One day, Emily's mommy said they were going to the museum. Emily didn't know what a museum was, but she was excited!

When they got there, Emily saw so many things. She saw old books, and stuffed animals, and lots of paintings. They were all so interesting!

After looking around for a while, Emily and her mommy had lunch. Emily's mommy cooked a yummy sandwich for both of them. Emily ate it up! It was so good.

When they were done, they looked around some more. Emily had a great time at the museum, and she wanted to thank her mommy. So, she gave her a big hug and said, "Mommy, I had a really good time today!"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to read books. Every day, she would sit in her cozy chair and read her favorite stories. 

One day, Lily's parents took her on a trip to a luxury hotel. The hotel was very fancy and had a big pool. Lily was so excited to swim and play in the lively water. 

After swimming, Lily went back to her room and read a book about a princess. She felt like a princess herself in the luxurious hotel. She was so happy and couldn't wait to read more books and have more fun.

Once upon a time, there was a big party. It was a marriage party. Everyone was happy and having a good time. At the party, there was a man who was folding paper. He was making pretty things for the kids. The kids were very excited to see what he would make next.

The man said, "I will make something very special soon." The kids could not wait to see what it was. They knew it would be good because the man was very good at folding paper. They watched him fold and fold, waiting for the surprise.

At last, the man finished folding the paper. He showed the kids a beautiful paper heart. The kids clapped and cheered. The man gave the heart to the bride and groom. Everyone knew that the heart was a sign of good luck for their marriage. The kids were very happy to see the bride and groom smile. The man's surprise made the marriage party even better.

Sara and Tom are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a cute dog. The dog is brown and fluffy. It has a red collar.

"Can we pet the dog?" Sara asks Tom.

"Maybe. Let's ask the owner first," Tom says.

They walk to the owner. The owner is a nice lady. She smiles at them.

"Hello, kids. Do you like my dog?" she asks.

"Yes, we do. He is very cute. What is his name?" Sara says.

"His name is Spot. He is a friendly dog. You can pet him if you want," the lady says.

Sara and Tom are happy. They pet Spot. Spot wags his tail. He licks their faces.

"Spot likes you. He is always looking for new friends," the lady says.

"Can we play with him?" Tom asks.

"Sure. But be careful. He has a lot of heat. He can run very fast. He likes to chase balls and sticks," the lady says.

She gives them a ball and a stick. Sara and Tom throw them for Spot. Spot runs after them. He brings them back. They have fun.

But then, something happens. Spot sees a squirrel. He barks. He runs after the squirrel. He forgets about the ball and the stick. He forgets about Sara and Tom.

"Spot, come back!" the lady shouts.

But Spot does not listen. He follows the squirrel. He runs out of the park. He runs into the street.

Sara and Tom are scared. They see a big car. The car is coming fast. The car does not see Spot.

"Spot, watch out!" Sara and Tom scream.

Will Spot be okay? Will he come back to the park? Will Sara and Tom see him again?

Anna likes cereal. She eats it every morning with milk. She likes to make noises with her spoon and mouth. She thinks it is fun.

But Mom does not like noisy cereal. She says, "Anna, please eat quietly. You are too loud. You will wake up your baby brother."

Anna does not want to wake up her baby brother. She loves him. She wants him to sleep well. She says, "Sorry, Mom. I will eat quietly."

She tries to eat quietly. But she still makes some noises. She likes the crunchy sound of the cereal. She likes the slurpy sound of the milk.

Mom hears the noises. She says, "Anna, you are still too loud. If you cannot eat quietly, you have to clean your bowl and spoon. You have to put them in the sink."

Anna does not want to clean her bowl and spoon. She wants to eat her cereal. She says, "But Mom, I am hungry. I want to finish my cereal."

Mom says, "You can finish your cereal, but you have to eat quietly. Or you have to clean your bowl and spoon. You choose."

Anna thinks. She does not like to clean. She likes to eat. She says, "OK, Mom. I choose to eat quietly."

She eats her cereal very quietly. She does not make any noises. She finishes her cereal. She is happy.

Mom is happy too. She says, "Good job, Anna. You ate quietly. You did not wake up your baby brother. You can put your bowl and spoon in the sink now."

Anna puts her bowl and spoon in the sink. She says, "Thank you, Mom. I love you."

Mom says, "I love you too, Anna. You are a good girl."

Lily liked to go to the grocery with her mom. She saw many things there: fruits, vegetables, bread, milk, eggs, and more. She liked to help her mom put things in the cart. Sometimes, she got a sticker or a cookie from the nice people who worked there.

One day, Lily saw something new at the grocery. It was a small plant in a pot. It had green leaves and tiny purple flowers. Lily thought it was pretty. She asked her mom what it was.

Mom said, "It's a lavender plant. It smells good and it can grow bigger and bigger. Do you want to take it home and put it in our garden?"

Lily nodded. She liked the idea of having a lavender plant in their garden. She imagined how it would grow and make their garden more lively and colorful. She hoped it would attract bees and butterflies.

Mom smiled and put the lavender plant in the cart. She said, "Good choice, Lily. You have a green thumb. That means you are good at taking care of plants. Maybe you can help me water it and prune it when we get home."

Lily was happy. She hugged the lavender plant and said, "Thank you, Mom. I love you and I love our garden."

George the bear was very lonely. He watched the gray clouds roll by, feeling sad. But then he saw a brightly colored box, sitting in the grass. He opened it, and inside was a video. He was excited, so he put the video into the special machine and looked at the screen. 

Suddenly, the video started playing a song. George was filled with joy, and he started to dance. He spun around in circles, hopping up and down and singing. 

But then something bad happened. George didn't know that videos rot over time, and this video was really old. The colors started to fade and then the video suddenly stopped. George felt really sad, but then he remembered that he could go outside and dance in the rain and look for more adventures. 

And everyone lived happily ever after. The End.

Once upon a time there was a little bunny living in the woods. The bunny wanted to explore but was faced with a big problem. In front of the bunny was a big hill. The hill was icy and made of slippery stones.

So the bunny tried to go up the hill. But the bunny wasnâ€™t very strong and slipped and slid going downhill again and again.

The bunny was getting a bit sad but did not give up. He took a deep breath and tried again. The bunny wiggled his feet and bounced himself up, bit by bit.

At last, the bunny reached the top! He was so happy to have made it and looked around at the beauty of the woods.

The bunny was glad that he had not given up and he had managed to struggle up the icy hill.

Once upon a time, there was a hunter. The hunter liked to play games. He had a dog, and the dog was his best friend. They played together every day. The hunter wanted to find the perfect game to play with his dog.

One day, the hunter found a game called "Who Can Run Fast?" The hunter and the dog played the game. They ran and ran, and the dog was very fast. The hunter was happy because the dog was good at the game. They played the game many times, and the dog always won. The hunter thought the game was perfect for his dog.

The hunter and the dog played the game every day. They had lots of fun, and the dog always won. The hunter was very proud of his dog. They were the best of friends, and they lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a dirty dog named Max. Max liked to dig in the mud and play with his friends. One day, Max found a big, shiny thing in the dirt. It was an axe. Max did not know what it was, but he thought it was fun to play with.

Max showed the axe to his friend, a little bird named Tim. Tim looked at the axe and said, "Be careful, Max! The axe is very sharp!" But Max did not understand what "sharp" meant. He just wanted to play with his new toy.

Max and Tim decided to play a game with the axe. They would take turns trying to hit a small ball with the axe. Max swung the axe and hit the ball very far. Tim tried to hit the ball too, but the axe was too heavy for him. They laughed and played until it was time for dinner. At the end of the day, Max and Tim learned that the sharp axe was a fun toy, but they should always be careful when playing with it.

Once upon a time, there was an octopus. It was big, and soft, and smooth. Its eight long tentacles moved in the water.

One day, the octopus saw a group of fish and decided to join them. The fish were discussing what to do later in the day, and the octopus wanted to join the conversation.

"Hello, fish!" said the octopus.

The fish were surprised. "Who said that?" they asked.

The octopus waved its tentacles. "It's me!"

The fish were even more surprised. They had never seen an octopus before!

They started discussing what they could do with the octopus. Finally, they decided they wanted to show the octopus how to swim.

So they swam with the octopus, and showed it how to move its tentacles in a smooth, graceful way. The octopus had a great time, and the fish were so proud!

Once upon a time, there was a girl who loved playing at the beach. Every day, she would make a new sandcastle and get sand all over her clothes. 

One day, her mother said to her, "Next time you go to the beach, promise me you won't get so messy, okay?" The girl was sad, but she nodded and said, "I promise." 

The next day at the beach, the girl found it really hard to only play a little bit in the sand and not get messy at all. But she remembered her mum's words, so she tried her best to stay clean. 

When her mum saw her later, she was glad that the girl had kept her promise and stayed clean. The mum said to the girl, "I'm glad that you remembered your promise. It's important to keep your promises. Doing so shows respect and is the right thing to do."

The girl smiled and hugged her mum, understanding the importance of promises and her mum's love. From then on, she always kept her promises, no matter how hard it was. 

Moral of the story: Keeping your promises shows respect and is the right thing to do.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She loved to wear pretty clothes and always wanted to look good. One day, Lily saw her friend Emma wearing a beautiful dress that she wished she had. She asked Emma where she got it from, but Emma didn't want to speak and just walked away.

Lily felt sad because she really wanted that dress. She decided to ask her mom to buy her a similar one, but her mom said they couldn't afford it. Lily was upset and didn't know what to do. She thought about it all day and decided to make her own dress. She went to the store and bought some fabric and started to fashion her own dress.

It wasn't perfect, but Lily was proud of herself. She wore it to school the next day and everyone complimented her on how good she looked. Even Emma spoke to her and said she liked her dress. Lily was happy that she didn't give up and found a solution to her problem. From that day on, Lily knew that she could make anything she wanted if she put her mind to it.

Anna and Ben are playing with their toys in the living room. Anna has a doll and Ben has a car. They are having fun making noises and moving their toys around.

"Look, my doll can dance!" Anna says, spinning her doll on the floor.

"My car can go fast!" Ben says, zooming his car across the carpet.

They play for a while, until they see a big box on the table. It is a present from their grandma. They run to the box and try to open it.

"What is inside?" Anna asks, pulling at the ribbon.

"Maybe it is a cake!" Ben says, poking at the paper.

They rip off the paper and open the box. Inside, they find a colorful top. It has stripes and stars and a long string. They take it out and look at it.

"A top!" Anna says, smiling.

"How do we play with it?" Ben asks, holding the string.

They see a note from their grandma. It says:

"Dear Anna and Ben,

I hope you like this top. It is a special toy that can spin and make music. To play with it, you have to wind the string around the top, then pull it hard and let it go. It will spin on the floor and make a nice sound. It is a healthy toy, because it makes you move and laugh. Have fun with it!

Love, Grandma"

Anna and Ben read the note and follow the instructions. They wind the string around the top, then pull it hard and let it go. The top spins on the floor and makes a nice sound. It looks like a rainbow.

"Wow, it is so pretty!" Anna says, clapping her hands.

"It is so cool!" Ben says, jumping up and down.

They take turns spinning the top and watching it. They laugh and cheer. They are happy with their present. They thank their grandma and hug each other. They play with the top until it is time for dinner.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved to explore. One day, she ventured into the forest and saw a palm tree. She was so scared but curious at the same time, she couldn't resist taking a closer look. She reached out her small hand and touched its trunk. Suddenly, an angry voice shouted at her. It was the palm tree!

The little girl was so startled that she yelped in surprise. She asked the palm tree why he was so rude. The palm tree replied that he was scared when she touched him and tried to protect himself. The little girl understood and promised never to do it again. She thanked the palm tree and went back home, never to be so brave again.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there lived a mom, a dad, and their daughter, Sue. Sue was a happy girl who loved to play with her toys. One day, mom and dad told Sue that they would welcome a new baby soon. Sue was very excited and couldn't wait to have a little brother or sister.

One day, a new girl moved next door. Her name was Lily. Sue wanted to play with Lily, but Lily was rude. She didn't want to share her toys with Sue. Sue was sad and told her mom and dad about it. They told her to be patient and kind, and maybe Lily would change her ways.

A few weeks later, mom and dad welcomed a baby boy into the family. Sue was so happy to be a big sister. She loved her little brother very much. One day, Lily saw Sue playing with her baby brother and wanted to join them. Sue remembered what her mom and dad said and let Lily play with them. Soon, Lily learned to be kind and share her toys. Sue and Lily became best friends, and they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a rhinoceros who had a very big urge. She wanted to explore and go somewhere new, but her home was warm and green. 

One day, it started to snow. The rhinoceros was so excited. With each snowflake, her urge grew stronger and stronger. 

The rhinoceros ventured out and the snow felt icy on her skin. She roamed and roamed, but she could not find what she was looking for. 

The sun came up and the snow was gone, but the urge was still there. The rhinoceros looked around, trying to find a new adventure. 

And then, in the distance, she saw it. An icy mountain, full of possibilities. With one last push, she urged herself forward and up the mountain. 

The rhinoceros climbed higher and higher. At the top, she found exactly what she was looking for â€“ adventure, excitement, and a new home.

One day, a huge owl lived in a big tree. The owl was very wise and could talk. All the animals liked the owl because he was nice and helped them.

A little bird went to the owl and said, "I can't find my way home. Can you help me?" The owl was happy to help. He looked around and saw the bird's nest. He ordered the bird to follow him.

The bird and the owl flew through the sky. They went over the trees and the grass. Soon, they found the bird's nest. The bird was happy and thanked the owl. The owl smiled and flew back to his big tree.

Once there was a girl. She was outside in the garden. She saw something small and she wanted to open it. She got closer and saw an insect. She was a bit scared at first, but then she saw that it was normal. 

She decided to open her hands and hold the insect close. It didn't move at first, but then it started crawling on her hand. She smiled and watched carefully.

It was fun watching the insect go from one place to another. She followed it with her eyes. Then, suddenly, it flew away! She was surprised, but she saw that it was normal. 

She waved it goodbye and went back inside with a smile.

Lily and Ben are playing with blocks. They like to make different patterns with the blocks. They use red, blue, yellow and green blocks.

"Look, I made a pattern with red and blue blocks!" Lily says. She shows Ben her pattern. It is red, blue, red, blue, red, blue.

Then they hear a noise. It is their mom. She is calling them for lunch.

"Come on, kids. It is time for lunch. Please wash your hands and come to the table." Mom says. She is in the kitchen.

They go to the kitchen. They see their mom. She has made sandwiches and fruit for them. They are hungry.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Rita. She was gentle and sweet and was always nice to everyone. One day Rita was walking in the park and noticed something shiny. She decided to take a closer look. As she got closer, she realized that someone had stolen someone else's toy.

Rita was very sad because she knew the toy belonged to someone else. But then she looked at the toy, she noticed that part of it was broken. She put her small muscle into work and managed to fix it.

Rita picked up the toy and decided to find who it belonged to. She went all around the park, showing the toy to anyone who looked like they were searching for it. Finally, she found a young boy who was looking for the toy.

Rita quietly gave the toy to the boy, who looked at her in surprise. He thanked her and said, "You taught me a very important lesson: to respect peopleâ€™s belongings and to treat others with kindness."

Rita smiled, feeling proud of herself. She had done something good and made a difference. Later that day, Rita thought to herself, "When you are gentle and kind, you can do magical things!"

Once upon a time, there was a big red car. The car loved to speed down the street. One sunny day, the car saw a little girl named Mia. Mia was sad because she lost her toy horse. The car wanted to help Mia find her toy.

The car said, "Mia, let's go find your toy horse! We will be safe and I will not speed too much." Mia smiled and got into the car. They went to the park and the store, but the toy horse was not there. Then, they went to the stable where horses lived.

At the stable, Mia saw her toy horse. It was safe with the real horses. Mia was happy and thanked the car. They went back home, and the car made sure to speed just a little bit, so Mia could have fun. From that day on, Mia and the car were best friends.

Sara liked to read books. She had many books on her bookshelf. She liked to look at the pictures and the words. Sometimes, her mom or dad would read to her.

One day, Sara saw a new book on her bookshelf. It was not a regular book. It was big and shiny and had a red ribbon. Sara was curious. She took the book and opened it.

Inside, she saw many photos of her family. There was her mom and dad, her grandma and grandpa, her aunt and uncle, and her cousins. There was also a photo of Sara when she was a baby. She smiled.

She ran to her mom and showed her the book. "Mom, look! What is this book?"

Her mom hugged her and said, "This is a special book, Sara. It is a photo book. It has pictures of our family. It is a gift from your grandma and grandpa. They made it for you."

"Why did they make it for me?" Sara asked.

"Because they love you very much, Sara. And because they want to remind you of them. They live far away, so we don't see them often. But they are always in our hearts. And this book helps us remember them."

Sara nodded. She felt happy and warm. She said, "I love them too, mom. And I love this book. Can we read it together?"

"Of course, Sara. Let's read it together. And maybe we can call them later and say thank you."

Sara and her mom sat on the couch and looked at the photo book. They talked about the family and the memories. Sara felt closer to her grandma and grandpa. She was glad they gave her such a wonderful gift.

Lily and Ben were friends who liked to play jokes on each other. One day, Lily had a plan to make Ben laugh. She found a big box and hid inside it. She waited for Ben to come home from school and put the box near his door.

When Ben saw the box, he was curious. He opened it and Lily jumped out. "Boo!" she shouted. Ben was so surprised that he fell backwards. He looked at Lily and started to giggle. "That was a good joke, Lily!" he said.

Lily was happy that Ben liked her joke. She helped him get up and they went inside to have a snack. They shared some cookies and milk and talked about their day. Lily told Ben about the funny things she saw at the park. Ben told Lily about the new song he learned at school.

But then, Lily's brother Max came in. He saw the box and the cookies and he was angry. He wanted to play with the box and eat the cookies. He grabbed the box and threw it away. He took the cookies and ran to his room. "Stop, Max!" Lily and Ben shouted. "You spoiled our fun!"

Max did not care. He locked his door and ate the cookies. He felt sick and his face turned pale. He wished he had not been so mean to Lily and Ben. He realized that jokes are better than spoils. He decided to say sorry to them and share his toys. He hoped they would forgive him and play with him again.

Lily and Tom were on a big boat with their mom and dad. They liked to look at the water and the fish and the birds. One day, they saw a small island with trees and sand. Mom and dad said they could go and play there for a while.

Lily and Tom were happy and ran to the shore. They saw a lot of shells and rocks and sticks. They wanted to make a castle with them. They started to grab the shells and rocks and sticks and pile them up. They worked hard and had fun.

But then, they heard a loud noise. It was the boat. Mom and dad were calling them. They said it was time to go back. Lily and Tom did not want to leave their castle. They said they wanted to stay on the island.

Mom and dad said no. They said the island was not safe. They said there were big waves and strong winds and wild animals. They said they had to hurry or they would be stuck. Lily and Tom were scared. They did not like big waves and strong winds and wild animals. They were weak and small.

They grabbed their hands and ran to the boat. Mom and dad helped them get on. They waved goodbye to their castle and the island. They were sad, but they were also glad. They knew they were safe and loved on the boat. They hugged mom and dad and said thank you. They hoped to see another island someday.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Spot. Spot loved to chew on things. His favorite thing to chew was a long piece of string. Spot would always play with his original string, the one he found when he was a baby dog.

One day, Spot met a cat named Mittens. Mittens was playing with a ball of yarn. Spot said, "Hi Mittens! Can I chew your yarn?" Mittens said, "No, Spot! This is my yarn. But you can play with your string!"

So, Spot and Mittens played together. Spot chewed on his original string, and Mittens played with her yarn. They had lots of fun together. And from that day on, they became the best of friends, always playing and sharing their toys.

One day, a car needed help. It was stuck and couldn't move. So, its owner called out for a mechanic. The mechanic came in a big truck with lots of tools. He was very friendly and gentle.

The mechanic used a big tool to fix the car. He made sure it was safe and could drive. Then, he asked if anyone could lend him a hand. So, the owner and the child living nearby helped him.

The mechacnic thanked them for their help. He fixed the car carefully. Finally, the car was ready to go and it was very safe. The mechanic said goodbye to the owner and the child. Then, he drove away in his truck.

The car was now working well. The owner and the child were very happy to help and lend a hand. They felt good that the car was safe now and wouldn't get stuck again.

Once there was a girl named Molly. She was very happy every day. One day, Molly found a big, comfortable blanket. She laid it on the floor and started to fold it. First, she folded it in half and then in half again. Next, she folded both ends and finished with a big, square blanket. Molly was so excited with her blanket that she decided to use it to have a nap. She laid down on it and slept until the end of the day. She was so comfortable and felt so happy that she took the blanket with her wherever she went.

Once upon a time, there was a little duck named Ducky. Ducky lived in a pond with his family and friends. One day, Ducky saw a bright and shiny object in the water. It was a raft! Ducky had never seen a raft before, so he climbed on it and started to play.

But suddenly, the raft started to move! Ducky tried to get off, but he couldn't. He was scared and didn't know what to do. Luckily, Ducky's mother saw him and quickly came to his rescue. She helped him escape from the raft and brought him back to safety.

From that day on, Ducky learned an important lesson. He realized that sometimes things that look fun can be dangerous. He promised to always be careful and listen to his mother's advice. And whenever he saw a bright and shiny object, he would remember to think twice before playing with it.

Once there was a very important angel. He lived in the clouds and was in charge of loading things. Every night he went to a special place and loaded special magical things from the sky. The angel carried them back to the clouds and stored them there.

One night, something strange happened. The angel saw a moonbeam streaming from the sky and it glowed with a bright light. He knew that something important must be inside so he grabbed it and loaded it into the sky.

The next morning something amazing happened. The sky was filled with beautiful sparkly lights. Everywhere the angel looked he could see them twinkling and shining. They were so beautiful that everyone stopped and looked.

The angel knew then that what he had loaded was even more important than he had thought. He had loaded the stars! The angel smiled knowing he had done a very important task.

Joe was a very stubborn three year old. He loved to play outside, but his mom told him he needed to pay for new shoes. He really didn't want to pay for something he didn't need.

That's when Joe had a great idea. He ran over to the garden and found a big mint plant. He picked two leaves and smiled.

That's when Joe's mom saw him. "Joe, what are you doing?"

Joe smiled and said, "I'm going to pay for my shoes with these leaves, momma."

His mom smiled and said, "Okay, but you're still going to need some money too."

Joe smiled and nodded. He kept picking mint leaves and soon he had enough to pay for his new shoes.

When Joe went to get his shoes, the store clerk was amazed. Joe had paid the exact amount needed. Joe was very proud of himself.

Joe's mom was surprised, but even more proud of her stubborn son. She couldn't believe he had paid for his shoes with mint leaves. From then on, Joe knew he could always find a creative way to pay for anything.

Once upon a time there was a mysterious bean. It was in a special cup and nobody knew what it was.

One day, a little boy called Tom happened to find it. He was very curious and he wanted to know what it was.

He decided to pay someone to find out what it was. He found a wise old man and offered him some money to tell him what it was.

The wise old man agreed and he looked at the mysterious bean carefully. He said that the bean was magical and if Tom looked after it, it would bring him luck.

Tom thanked the wise old man and he couldn't believe his luck! He took the bean home and cared for it every day. He always felt very happy when he looked at the mysterious bean.

Ben and Lily were playing with their toys in the living room. Ben had a red car and Lily had a yellow doll. They liked their toys, but they also wanted to try each other's.

"Can I play with your car, Ben?" Lily asked.

"OK, but only if I can play with your doll, Lily," Ben said.

They agreed to trade their toys for a while. They were happy and obedient children who shared nicely.

But then, Lily spilled some juice on the car. The car was wet and sticky. Ben was sad and angry.

"Look what you did, Lily! You made my car dirty and wet! Give it back to me!" Ben shouted.

"I'm sorry, Ben. I didn't mean to. Here, take your car. But it's still a good car. It can go fast and make noises," Lily said.

Ben took his car and tried to dry it with a towel. He rubbed and rubbed, but the car was still wet. He was not happy.

"Lily, you ruined my car! It doesn't work anymore. It doesn't go fast or make noises. It's a bad car now. I don't want it. I want your doll!" Ben said.

"But Ben, you can't have my doll. It's mine. And you already played with it. It's not fair. You have to keep your car. It's your trade," Lily said.

They started to argue and cry. They were not happy or obedient children anymore. They were selfish and mean.

Their mom heard them and came to the living room. She saw the wet car and the yellow doll. She saw the juice and the towel. She saw the angry faces and the tears.

"What's going on here, Ben and Lily? Why are you fighting over your toys?" Mom asked.

They told her what happened. They blamed each other. They wanted to change their trade.

Mom shook her head. She was not pleased.

"Ben and Lily, you made a bad choice. You traded your toys, but you didn't take care of them. You spilled juice on the car and you didn't dry it properly. You made it wet and dirty. You broke your promise and you wanted to take back your trade. That's not how you play or share. That's not how you treat your toys or your friends. You need to say sorry and fix your mistake," Mom said.

She made them apologize to each other and to their toys. She helped them clean and dry the car. She showed them how to make it work again. She told them to be more careful and respectful next time.

Ben and Lily felt sorry and ashamed. They hugged each other and their toys. They thanked Mom for her help. They learned their lesson.

They decided to trade their toys again, but only for a little while. They played nicely and gently. They were happy and obedient children again.

Once there was an ant. He was small and brave. He was looking for food.

He started to chew it. He was very hungry. He chewed and chewed. Suddenly, he heard a loud noise. He was scared and he ran away quickly. 

But, he was so happy he found the amazing apple. With a full tummy, he marched back to his home. 

The end!

The little girl was playing in the garden when she saw a butterfly. She was so excited and chased after it. She followed it everywhere, but it was just too fast. She wanted to reach out and grab it, but it was always out of sight. 

Suddenly, a big scary dog appeared. He barked and growled loudly. He was very bossy and refused to let the little girl near the butterfly. She felt scared and stepped back. 

Fortunately, the girl's mom was nearby and came to her rescue. She gave the dog a stern look and told him to go away. He refused again, but the mom did not give up and kept scolding him. Finally, he decided to go and the little girl was able to go back to chasing the butterfly.

Once there was a little boy called Joe. He was three years old and loved to play. He had a cosy room that he loved and he always made sure his toys were in neat piles.

So Joe opened his bedroom door and stepped out into the hallway. He left the house and made his way out into the garden. Joe followed the sunshine and soon he was out of the garden and at the stream. He crossed the stream and continued his way. 

Joe had the most wonderful adventure and saw so many new things. After a few hours he realised he was far from home, but he was not scared since he had his fierce belt with him. 

Joe eventually made his way back home and went to bed exhausted but happy. He smiled as he snuggled his belt close and fell asleep knowing he was brave and he could go on any adventure he desired.

Once upon a time, there was a girl. She was very brave and loved adventures. One day she decided to explore the forest.

As she was walking through the trees, the ground suddenly shook. The girl was in shock! But without hesitating, she stood strong and kept walking.

Soon she came across a friendly fox. He took the girl to his home in the forest. She found it very easy to make friends with all the animals there.

The girl had the best adventure ever! She learned that sometimes you have to stand up to a shock if you want to find something special!

Sam and Lily were playing in the park. They liked to run and jump and slide. They saw a big helicopter in the sky. It was making a loud noise.

"Look, look!" Sam said. "A helicopter!"

"What is it doing?" Lily asked.

"I don't know. Maybe it is going to help someone. Helicopters are strong. They can fly very high and fast."

Sam and Lily watched the helicopter. It flew over the trees and the houses. It was shiny and red. It had a big fan on top and a small fan on the back.

The helicopter came closer to the park. It landed on a big field. Sam and Lily ran to see it. They were curious and excited.

"Wow, it is so big!" Sam said.

"Can we touch it?" Lily asked.

A man came out of the helicopter. He was wearing a helmet and a suit. He smiled at Sam and Lily.

"Hello, kids. Do you like my helicopter?" he asked.

"Yes, yes!" Sam and Lily said.

"This is a rescue helicopter. I help people who are hurt or in trouble. Sometimes I take them to the hospital. Sometimes I bring them water or food. Do you want to see inside?"

"Yes, please!" Sam and Lily said.

The man opened the door of the helicopter. He showed them the seats and the buttons and the screens. He let them wear his helmet and his headphones. He told them how to blink the lights and how to talk to the other helicopters.

They went back to playing in the park. They pretended to be helicopters. They made the noise and blinked the lights. They felt strong and happy.

Once upon a time, there was a yummy apple tree. It had many red apples. A little boy named Tim loved to eat the apples. He would visit the tree every day.

The moral of the story is: always be kind and help others. When you do good things, good things will happen to you.

Once there was a frog. Its name was Top. Top was very small but it wanted to explore the world. So one day Top made up its mind and decided to take a journey.

Once upon a time there was a clever fox. He had a furry tail that was orange and fluffy. Every day he worked very hard.

Tom and Lily are brother and sister. They like to watch films on the big screen. Sometimes, they go with their mom and dad to the cinema. Sometimes, they watch films at home on the TV.

Once there was a family who had a garden. In the garden they grew lots of lovely veggies. One of the veggies was a big, bright orange squash.

Once there was a mule that was very delicate. She lived in a grassy field and everyday she would fill her belly with the sweet grasses around her. She was so happy in her field.

The frog jumped up right next to the boy, and before the boy knew what was happening, the frog had bit him on the hand! The boy gasped and ran away, holding his hand which now hurt. He looked back and saw the frog hopping away, looking proud of itself. 

The boy never forgot the lesson he learned that day - even the youngest creatures can bite!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her dolls and dress them up in pretty clothes. One day, she found a sparkly dress that made her feel famous. She put it on and twirled around in front of the mirror.

But then, Lily's mom called her for dinner. She didn't want to take off her beautiful dress, so she wore it to the table. As she ate, some spaghetti sauce spilled on her dress and she couldn't get it out. Lily was very sad because her dress was ruined.

The moral of the story is that sometimes we need to be careful with things that are special to us. We should take care of them so they can last a long time.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lucy. Lucy was very independent. Everywhere she went, she picked things up, like leaves, rocks and flowers. 

One day, Lucy went on a walk and picked a special lamp. It was shiny and bright, with a silvery handle. Lucy carried the lamp back home, feeling very proud. 

That night, Lucy put the lamp in her bedroom. When she turned it on, lots of wonderful things happened. Lights danced all over the walls, and Lucy could see all the colours of the rainbow. She giggled and clapped her hands. 

Lucy loved her special lamp. Every night she would pick it up and turn it on, reminding herself that she was independent.

Cindy woke up. She looked around, and saw that the sun was already shining. She quickly put on her mitten and felt so excited to go outside.

Her mom said, "Where are you going, Cindy?".

"Outside!", Cindy replied.

Cindy ran outside and saw a big tree with lots of tasty apples. She picked one of the apples, took a big bite and it was so delicious! 

Cindy enjoyed the morning in the garden and ate lots of tasty apples. She gathered some apples in her mitten and brought them home. 

When Cindy arrived home, she showed her mom the apples she had collected in her mitten. Her mom was so proud and said, "Good job, Cindy! Let's make an apple pie with these apples". 

Cindy smiled and said, "Yummy!"

Once upon a time, there was a wise owl who lived in a tree. Every Tuesday, the owl would fly to the river to catch fish for dinner. But one day, it started to rain and the owl got wet. So, the owl flew back to its tree to dry itself off. 

The owl flapped its wings and shook its feathers to get dry. After a while, the sun came out and the owl felt warm again. It decided to wait until next Tuesday to catch fish. From then on, the owl always checked the weather before going out to catch fish.

One day, Sam and Lily were playing in the park with their ball. They liked to kick the ball to each other and run after it. They were having fun and laughing.

But then, a big dog came out of nowhere and ran towards them. It barked loudly and showed its teeth. Sam and Lily were fearful. They did not know what to do. They dropped the ball and ran away.

The dog chased them and grabbed the ball in its mouth. It ran away with the ball. Sam and Lily were sad. They had lost their ball. They did not know where the dog went.

They ran to their mom, who was sitting on a bench. They told her what happened. She hugged them and said, "I'm sorry, my loves. That was a bad dog. It should not have taken your ball. But I'm glad you are safe. You did the right thing to run away. Sometimes, we have to lose something to protect ourselves."

She pointed to an ambulance that was parked nearby. She said, "See that big car with the red cross and the lights? That is an ambulance. It helps people who are hurt or sick. Sometimes, the dog can bite people and make them bleed or feel pain. Then, they need the ambulance to take them to the hospital. You were lucky that the dog did not bite you. You were brave and smart."

Sam and Lily nodded. They understood. They felt better. They learned that losing a ball was not as bad as losing their health. They thanked their mom and gave her a kiss. They decided to play something else in the park. They hoped that the dog would not come back. They hoped that the people in the ambulance would be okay. They hoped that they would find another ball someday.

It was a gloomy day outside, but Sarah wanted to play. She ran to the garden with her bucket, ready to have some fun.

Sarah filled her bucket with water from the pond, then she grabbed a pebble. She looked up at the sky and threw the pebble in the water. It made a huge splash!

"That was fun!" Sarah said with a smile. She filled her bucket up again, this time with more pebbles. She skipped around the pond and threw the pebbles in the water, one after the other. Each time, they made a big splash!

Sarah was getting hungry, so she ran back inside. She spread some delicious raspberry jam on her toast and enjoyed a yummy snack.

"What a nice day," Sarah said with a full tummy. Now she was ready to go back outside and make even more splashes!

Once upon a time, there was an old man who was very hungry. He saw a campfire and decided to warm himself up. He stepped closer to the campfire and soon he was warm and toasty.

Suddenly, a gust of strong wind blew and the flames grew bigger. The old man backed away, but it was too late. His clothes had already caught on fire. He screamed for help but it was too late. He kept burning until he was all gone.

Everyone in the town had seen it and learnt a lesson from it. They learnt that they should be careful with things like fire. They knew that it was dangerous and never to be played with.

The old man's sight could still be seen by everyone as a reminder of what happened. He reminded them to be careful and never too trusting with their sight.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to draw and make shapes with her crayons. One day, she decided to draw a triangle. She used her green crayon to make the lines straight and even.

Lily's mom was cooking dinner in the kitchen. Lily asked, "Mommy, can I show you my triangle?" Her mom said, "Yes, Lily. I allow you to show me your triangle after I finish cooking."

Lily was very impatient. She wanted to show her mom right away. But she knew she had to wait until her mom was finished. So, she sat at the table and drew more shapes with her crayons until her mom was ready to see her triangle.

Jack was very bored. His mom had asked him to come to her bedroom. She had something to offer him. Jack thought it was probably something fun.

But when Jack got there, he saw that his mom was giving a lecture! She was talking about something Jack didn't understand. It was very dull.

Jack didn't want to listen to the lecture. He wanted to go play. So he snuck out of the room and ran outside. He could hear his mom calling after him, but he kept running until he was out of sight.

Jack found his friends and they played together for the rest of the day. And Jack never paid attention to any lectures ever again.

Once upon a time, there was a little bear named Teddy. Teddy had soft fur that he loved to snuggle with. One day, Teddy saw his friend, a little rabbit named Benny, who had a shiny new toy. Teddy felt jealous and asked, "Where did you get that toy, Benny?"

Benny replied, "I designed it myself! Do you want to design a toy too?"

Teddy was excited and said, "Yes, please! Can we design a toy together?"

Benny happily agreed and the two friends spent the day drawing and coloring their toy designs. When they were finished, they showed their designs to each other and Teddy felt proud of his creation. From then on, Teddy was no longer jealous of Benny's toy because he had designed his own special toy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She had a long, thin crack in her bedroom wall. One day, she decided to stay and watch the crack. She wanted to see what would happen.

She stayed by the crack for hours. But nothing ever happened. No matter how long she stayed, the crack never changed.

But then a funny thing happened. One day, she felt a gentle breeze coming from the crack. It blew through the room and made her giggle. She stayed there until the breeze went away.

After that, the little girl knew she could stay by the crack for a long time and always enjoy the gentle breeze. The crack brought her much happiness.

Once upon a time, there lived a lively young reindeer in the North pole. He was always so excited about the snow and he loved playing out in the cold! One day, he decided to go off into the snow and explore. 

So off he went, exploring the snow and having fun. But suddenly he noticed something he hadn't seen before - a big, deep hole in the snow. He went over to have a look and noticed it was full of ice.

Just then, his mother noticed what was happening and called out to him. She warned him to stay away from the hole and said, "Don't go too close! The ice is too cold for a reindeer like you!"

The young reindeer listened carefully and promised to stay away from the deep and chilly hole. He thanked his mother for her warning and promised to be more careful from then on. 

The lively reindeer was much more cautious and kept a safe distance from the deep, icy hole. He kept a smile on his face and continued exploring the snow. 

The end.

Once upon a time there was a kind boy called Bill. He was always looking for things to do in the backyard. One day he found a box in the corner of the garden, it was an old wooden box, but Bill couldn't open it. He tried his hardest, but he couldn't budge the lid.

His mom came to help him. She smiled kindly down and explained that the box was locked with a special key, which they couldn't find. She said the only way to open the box was to find the key. Bill was very excited. He asked his mom if he could go on a key hunt in the backyard.

His mom said yes and gave him a hug. She said to be careful and reminded him to take his teddy with him. Bill found lots of things in the backyard but no key. Then, he saw something shiny in the tall grass. He bent down and there it was, the key! He carefully put it in the keyhole of the box and it opened!

Inside was a beautiful bird, with colourful feathers. Bill was so excited that he hugged the bird. His mom explained that the bird was hurt and must have been locked in the box for a long time. They decided to release the bird back into the wild so it could fly free again. 

Bill and his mom opened the back door and looked up at the bird. They waved goodbye as it flew high up into the sky

One day, Timmy was feeling good. He saw a wagon and wanted to take a ride. He felt so excited that he ran to it. He hopped in and was ready to go!

But then, Timmy saw that the wagon was too big for him. He was sad because he couldn't take a ride.

But then he saw a nice lady. She said that she would help him. She put him in the wagon and then pushed him around the park. Timmy felt so happy!

He felt so good riding around in the wagon. He was so glad he found a friend to help him. He waved goodbye to the nice lady and thanked her.

Timmy walked home with a big smile on his face. He knew he would never forget the fun wagon ride he had that day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily's mom gave her a ball of yarn to play with. Lily loved the yarn and started to play with it. She wrapped it around her toys and made a big mess.

Suddenly, Lily's cat, Mittens, came into the room and scared her. She managed to grab the yarn and ran out of the room. But the yarn was tangled and Lily couldn't untangle it. She was sad and didn't know what to do.

Then, Lily's mom came to help her. She managed to untangle the yarn and Lily was happy again. They both worked together to clean up the mess and put the yarn away safely. From that day on, Lily learned to be careful with the yarn and not to get scared of her cat.

Sam and Tom are friends. They like to play with cars and trucks. One day, they see a big factory near their park. The factory makes toys. Sam and Tom want to see the toys.

They go to the factory gate. A man is there. He is angry. He says, "Go away! This is not a place for kids. You cannot come in."

Sam and Tom are sad. They say, "But we want to see the toys. Please let us in."

The man says, "No! The toys are for rich people. You are not rich. You have no money. Go away or I will call the police."

Sam and Tom are scared. They run away from the factory. They go back to the park. They play with their own cars and trucks. They say, "We do not need the factory toys. We have fun with our toys. We are happy."

One day, a small girl named Joanna was sitting outside. She was looking at a big field of corn and she was so amazed. The corn was so tall and it was very peaceful. Joanna couldn't take her eyes away, she just wanted to stare at the corn forever. 

Joanna got up and started walking through the field. She couldn't believe how tall all the corn was! She felt like she was walking in a forest. Suddenly, she heard a sound. It was a bird singing in a nearby tree. It was the most peaceful sound Joanna had ever heard. She stopped and just stared at the bird. 

The bird was so pretty, with its colorful feathers and its long beak. Joanna felt so relaxed and she was filled with joy. She just wanted to stay and stare at the bird forever. 

But after a while, Joanna knew it was time to go home. She said goodbye to the bird, waved at the field of corn and walked away, feeling so peaceful.

Once upon a time, there was a big, brown bear. He was very boring and didn't like to play. One day, a little girl came to visit the bear. She tried to make him smile by telling him funny jokes and silly stories. But the bear just looked at her with a sad face.

The little girl didn't give up. She brought her favorite toy, a colorful ball, and asked the bear to play with her. At first, the bear didn't want to, but then he saw how happy the little girl was. He started to play with her and even smiled a little bit.

From that day on, the bear wasn't boring anymore. He would play with the little girl every time she visited him. And every time they played, the bear would smile a big, happy smile.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys, but he always had trouble finding them because they were all over the place. One day, Timmy's mom came into his room and said, "Timmy, let's organize your toys so you can find them easily." 

Timmy was excited to organize his toys because he wanted to be smart like his mom. They started by putting all the cars in one pile, all the blocks in another pile, and all the stuffed animals in a third pile. Timmy's mom showed him how to put the toys in their right places, so he could find them when he wanted to play. 

After they finished organizing, Timmy felt proud of himself. He said to his mom, "Look, Mommy! I'm smart like you now!" His mom smiled and said, "Yes, you are, Timmy. And now you can play with your toys without any trouble finding them." Timmy was happy and played with his toys all day long, knowing exactly where to find them.

Once there was a little girl who lived in a house. She was only three years old, but she was very passionate about her home. Every day she would go outside and run around with her friends. She would laugh and play, and be so filled with joy.

But one day, the little girl noticed something strange. She saw that the other houses around hers were run down and not hopping with the same energy they used to have. She was curious and concerned, but she tried to stay hopeful.

That night she talked to her mom and asked her what was happening with the houses. Her mom explained that many people had been struggling and had to move away. The little girl's heart filled with compassion and she was determined to figure out a way to help.

The next day she gathered her friends together to brainstorm ideas about how to give back to the community. They talked and shared, and finally settled on a plan. They would collect canned goods from their local food bank and then bring them over to the empty houses. They felt filled with hope, knowing that even the little things they do can make a big difference.

The little girl and her friends had started something that was wonderful and compassionate. And they taught all their friends and family that itâ€™s never too late to hope.

Ben was restless. He did not want to nap. He wanted to play with his cars and trucks. But Mom said he had to nap. She put him in his bed and gave him a kiss. She said she would make tuna for lunch. Ben liked tuna.

But Ben did not sleep. He tossed and turned. He kicked his blanket. He looked at his cars and trucks on the shelf. He wanted them. He got out of his bed and tiptoed to the shelf. He reached for his red truck. But it was too high. He stretched and stretched. He lost his balance and fell.

He hit his head on the floor. It hurt. He screamed. He screamed loud. Mom heard him. She ran to his room. She saw him on the floor. She saw the blood on his head. She was scared. She picked him up and hugged him. She said it was okay. She said she would take him to the doctor.

Ben cried. He did not want to go to the doctor. He wanted his red truck. He wanted his tuna. He wanted his mom. He was restless. He screamed.

Ben and Lily were very hot and thirsty. They had been walking in the sand for a long time. They wanted to find water and shade. They saw a big hill in front of them. Ben said, "Maybe there is something good behind the hill. Let's go and see."

They climbed the hill and looked down. They saw a green place with trees and a pond. They ran down the hill and into the green place. They felt happy and cool. They drank some water and ate some fruits. They said, "This is an oasis. It is a new and nice place for us."

But they did not know that someone else lived in the oasis. It was a big and mean lion. He saw Ben and Lily and wanted to eat them. He hid behind a tree and waited for them to come closer. He acted like he was not there.

Ben and Lily saw a big and soft bed of grass. They wanted to rest and sleep. They walked towards the bed of grass. They did not see the lion. The lion got ready to jump on them.

But then they heard a loud roar. It was another lion. He was bigger and stronger than the first lion. He lived on the other side of the oasis. He did not like the first lion. He wanted to chase him away. He ran towards the first lion and attacked him.

Ben and Lily heard the roar and saw the lions. They were scared and ran away. They climbed the hill and looked back. They saw the lions fighting and biting. They said, "The oasis is not a safe place for us. Let's go and find another place." They left the oasis and walked in the sand again. They hoped to find a better place.

The windy day was quiet and still. Little Timmy decided to take a walk. As he walked he found something smelly. It was a box! Curious, he opened it to explore. Suddenly a giant dragon flew out of the box! Timmy was so scared, he stood there and couldn't move.

"RRAAAAAAAAWR!" The dragon bellowed.

"I am here to strike!"

Timmy was so scared, he didn't know what to do. Suddenly he heard a wise old voice. It said,

"Do not be afraid, Timmy. Strike the dragon with your courage."

So Timmy gathered up all his courage and shouted,

"No! You will not strike me!"

The dragon was so surprised. He flew away, never to be seen again.

The windy day was quiet again and Timmy felt proud of his bravery.

Once upon a time, there was a young girl called Molly. Molly was very brave, so one day she decided she wanted to explore a cave. 

Molly found the cave and she yawned as she looked inside. She was very excited because she knew it was a rare cave. Molly had never seen a cave like this before, and she was eager to find out what was inside. 

Molly shrugged, took a deep breath and entered the cave. She was surprised to find that it was very dark, but she kept exploring and soon she saw something. It was a small sparkling rock. Molly's eyes widened with excitement. She had never seen a rock so rare before. 

Molly was so tired from exploring the cave, so she yawned and decided to take the rare rock home with her. Molly was so happy she had found such a special stone. She thanked the cave for the adventure, and she smiled on her way back home.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved playing with her dolls and running around in the park. One day, Lily went to the park to play with her friends. She was having so much fun that she didn't notice her favorite doll was missing.

Lily looked everywhere for her doll, but she couldn't find it. She started to cry and a kind lady asked her what happened. Lily told the lady about her missing doll.

The lady called the police and they came to help. They searched the whole park and found Lily's doll, but it was broken. Lily was very sad and cried even more. The police tried to cheer her up, but it didn't work.

Lily went home with her broken doll and her parents tried to fix it, but it was too broken. Lily was sad for a long time and never went to the park again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved sunflowers and would always pick them to give to her mom. One day, she saw a modern vase and thought it would look nice with her sunflowers. She begged her mom to buy it for her.

When they got home, Lily put her sunflowers in the modern vase. But she didn't realize that the vase was too heavy for the table. Later that day, the vase fell and broke into tiny pieces. Lily was sad that her vase was gone, but her mom told her that it was a lesson to be careful with things.

The next day, Lily was playing outside when she saw a butterfly. She wanted to catch it, but it flew away. Then, she saw a sunflower and wanted to pick it, but it was frozen. Lily remembered her lesson and knew that she couldn't force things to happen. She decided to leave the sunflower where it was and went back inside to play.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside and explore the world around him. One day, Timmy found a can of gas in his backyard. He thought it looked interesting and decided to play with it.

Suddenly, the gas disappeared and Timmy was confused. He looked around but couldn't see it anywhere. Then, he smelled something disgusting and realized the gas had turned into a bad smell.

Timmy learned that gas can be dangerous and should never be played with. He promised to always ask an adult before touching anything that he doesn't understand.

Once upon a time, there was a big van. The van was very pretty and graceful. It had many colors on it. People liked to look at the van when it went by.

One day, the van wanted to go very fast. It wanted to speed down the road. So, the van went faster and faster. It zoomed by trees and houses. The people who saw the van were very surprised.

But, the van did not see a big rock in the road. The van hit the rock and went boom! The pretty van was not so pretty anymore. The people were sad to see the van all broken. And that is the end of the story.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved playing outside with his friends. One day, Timmy and his friends went to the park to play. They saw a big, tough dog in the park. Timmy's friend said, "That dog looks scary."

Timmy said, "Don't worry. I know what to do. Watch this!" Timmy picked up a stick and threw it far away. The dog ran after the stick and Timmy and his friends were safe.

Later that day, Timmy and his friends saw a big, round spring in the park. Timmy said, "Let's turn the spring and see what happens!" They turned the spring and water came out. Timmy's friends were so happy and they all laughed and played in the water. Timmy was proud that he knew what to do with the dog and the spring.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the park with her friends. One day, Lily found a shiny coin on the ground. She picked it up and showed it to her friend, Timmy.

"Look what I got, Timmy! It's a coin!" said Lily.

"Wow, that's so cool! You're so strong for finding it," replied Timmy.

Lily felt proud of herself for being strong and finding the coin. She decided to save it in her piggy bank at home. From that day on, Lily always looked for coins when she played outside with her friends. She wanted to get more coins and become even stronger.

Once upon a time, a big elephant was walking in the jungle. The elephant was very hungry and was looking for something yummy to eat. Suddenly, he saw a banana tree and went to eat some bananas. 

After the elephant ate the bananas, he felt happy and full. Then, he saw a little boy and said, "Thank you for letting me eat your bananas." The little boy smiled and said, "You're welcome, Mr. Elephant."

The elephant continued to walk through the jungle, feeling happy and satisfied. He saw some other animals and said hello to them. The animals were happy to see the friendly elephant and they played together. The end.

Mama was sad. She said Benny must go to bed. Benny didn't want to sleep. He wanted to play on the lawn outside. So he asked mama with his sad eyes if he could just stay outside for a few minutes, but mama said no.

Mama hugged Benny and he could tell she was sad. He patted her arm and said it was ok. Benny knew he had to sleep, so he said goodbye to the lawn and went inside his bedroom.

Benny snuggled under his covers and thought about the lawn until he was so sleepy, he closed his eyes and soon he was dreaming. In his dreams he played in the lawn, running and laughing until he woke up in the morning. 

Mama was there in the morning, giving Benny a big hug. She said sleep was important and he had to go to bed early the next night too. But Benny smiled and said the lawn was very fun and he was glad he got to dream about it. Mama smiled too and said they could go back to the lawn soon.

Once upon a time, there was a generous blueberry bush. Every day, it would give out blueberries to the people in the town. They were always so happy when the blueberries came! One day, however, something strange happened. All of the blueberries disappeared! Where did they go? Everyone searched for them but no one could find out. Suddenly, it started to rain, and that's when the mystery was solved. It turned out that the generous blueberry bush had hidden all of its blueberries inside the raindrops to keep them safe! And they all lived happily ever after. The End.

Once upon a time, there was a man with a big, bushy mustache. He loved his mustache very much and would stroke it all day long. One day, he went outside and it was very cold. The wind was blowing and there was icy snow on the ground. 

The man decided to go inside and make some hot cocoa to warm up. He got out a big pot and added some milk and cocoa powder. He stirred it all together and it started to smell really good. 

As he was pouring the hot cocoa into his mug, he accidentally spilled some on his mustache. It was now covered in brown, chocolaty goodness! He couldn't help but laugh as he licked the hot cocoa off his mustache. From that day on, he always added a little extra cocoa powder to his hot cocoa to make it extra chocolatey. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she went to a restaurant with her mommy and daddy. When they got there, Lily spilled some juice on her dress. Her mommy gave her a napkin to wipe it off.

After they ate, Lily felt very tired. She asked her mommy if they could go home so she could take a nap. Her mommy said yes and they left the restaurant.

When they got home, Lily's mommy sent her to her room to take a nap. Lily slept for a long time and when she woke up, her face was pale because she was still very tired. But then she remembered that she had a fun day with her mommy and daddy and that made her happy again. The end.

Once there was a smart little boy. He loved to learn new things. So his mom got him a bookcase. He was so excited! He put all of his books in the bookcase and he could easily find them whenever he wanted. 

One day the little boy was very hungry so he went to the kitchen. There was something new on the table to eat. He looked closer and saw that it was a delicious apple. He ate it up and smiled!
