"We are sorry, sir," Lila said. "We were just playing. We did not mean to touch your spear."

The man looked at them. He saw that they were just children. He saw that they were sorry.

He sighed. He put down his spear. He smiled.

"It's okay, kids," he said. "I am not angry. I am just a reenactor. I pretend to be a soldier from the past. This is not a real spear. It is a toy."

He showed them his spear. He let them touch it gently.

Lila and Ben were curious. They asked him questions. He told them stories. He taught them about history.

Lila and Ben were happy. They learned something new. They made a new friend. They thanked the man for his spear. They said goodbye.

They ran back to their mom. They told her what happened. She was surprised. She was glad.

She hugged them. She said, "You are very brave and polite. I am proud of you."

One day, a boy named Tim found a big hammer in his toy box. He took the hammer and went to play in the deep mud outside. While he was playing, he saw a little bug stuck in the mud.

"Help me, please!" said the bug. Tim wanted to help, but he didn't want to delay his playtime. The bug looked very sad, so Tim decided to help.

Tim used his big hammer to make a path in the mud. The bug was able to crawl out and said, "Thank you, Tim!" Tim felt happy that he helped the bug. After that, he continued playing with his hammer, but now he also had a new friend to play with.

Anna likes yogurt very much. She eats it every morning with her spoon. She likes the white yogurt with the red fruit on top. It is sweet and yummy.

One day, Anna wakes up and goes to the kitchen. She sees her mom and dad. They are busy. They have many things to do. They have to make breakfast, pack lunch, and get ready for work.

Anna says, "Mom, dad, I want yogurt. Give me yogurt, please." But mom and dad do not hear her. They are busy. They talk to each other. They do not look at Anna.

Anna says louder, "Mom, dad, I want yogurt. Give me yogurt, now." But mom and dad still do not hear her. They are busy. They move around the kitchen. They do not look at Anna.

Anna gets angry. She does not like to wait. She wants yogurt. She demands yogurt. She shouts, "Mom, dad, I want yogurt. Give me yogurt, right now." She stamps her feet. She makes a big noise.

Mom and dad hear Anna. They stop being busy. They look at Anna. They see her angry face. They see her noisy feet. They are not happy. They say, "Anna, you are being rude. You do not demand yogurt. You ask nicely. You say, 'May I have some yogurt, please?' You wait your turn. You do not shout. You do not stamp. You do not make a big noise."

Anna feels sorry. She does not want to be rude. She wants to be nice. She says, "I am sorry, mom, dad. I was hungry. I was impatient. I was wrong. May I have some yogurt, please?" She smiles. She says, "Please."

Mom and dad smile too. They say, "That's better, Anna. Thank you for being polite. Yes, you may have some yogurt. Here you go." They give Anna a bowl of yogurt. They give her a spoon. They give her a hug. They say, "We love you, Anna. Enjoy your yogurt."

Anna loves mom and dad. She loves yogurt. She eats it with her spoon. She says, "Thank you, mom, dad. I love you too. This yogurt is delicious." She is happy. She is not angry. She is not noisy. She is not rude. She is polite. She is good.

Once upon a time, there was a man named Tom. Tom was sad. He had no food for dinner and his tummy growled. He wanted something yummy to eat.

So Tom got down on his knees and closed his eyes. He put his hands together and started to pray. He asked God for help.

Suddenly, Tom felt something soft on his head. When he looked up, he saw a big, round pie. He jumped for joy because it was just what he wanted.

Tom thanked God for the pie and took a bite. But as he chewed, he realized the pie was empty! His tummy still growled and he was still hungry.

Tom was sad again. But, with a smile on his face, he prayed and thanked God once more. He knew God would help him and fill his tummy.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Polly. She loved to poke her nose and was always poking it in different places. One day, Polly was poking her nose in the garden when she found something dull. She looked closely and saw that it was a shiny rock. She picked it up and put it in her pocket. Polly continued to poke her nose around the garden.

Suddenly, she heard a noise. She stopped and listened. She heard some rustling and saw a little mouse peeking out of a bush. Polly smiled and slowly reached out her hand. She began to poke the mouse's nose, and it jumped back in surprise. Polly laughed and tried again. This time, the mouse stayed still. Polly smiled and continued to poke it's nose.

The mouse and Polly became friends, playing together every time she came to the garden. She would always bring the dull rock with her, and the mouse would poke it with its nose. Polly would always find new and interesting things in the garden and the mouse would poke them with its nose and follow her around. And thanks to Polly and the little mouse, the garden was never dull.

Once there was a dead skeleton lying on the ground. It was alone and sad, for no one came to fill it with life. Then one day, a small boy walked by. He saw the skeleton and was filled with pity. He found some stones and filled the skeleton with them.

The skeleton began to move. The stones filled it with life and soon it was walking around like a person. Everyone cheered and smiled. The boy was so happy to have filled the skeleton with life.

From that day on, the boy learned an important lesson. You should always come and help others. You never know what you can do if you just try to fill someone else's life with love.

Sam wanted to record a show on tv. He asked his dad to turn on the power. 

The power went on and he was ready to record. He pressed the record button and the show started. 

Sam was excited to watch the show, but it went too fast for him. He didn't want to miss any of it. 

Sam's dad saw that the show was going too fast. He told Sam to press the fast button on the tv. 

Sam pressed the fast button. The show slowed down and Sam was able to watch and record it. 

Sam was happy that he was able to record the show and he was excited to watch it later.

Once upon a time, there was a small town. Everything was going great until one day a small tornado came. The tornado made a mess of the town that it touched. It tore everything apart. The people in the town had to clean up the mess that the tornado left.

They worked all day long, but they couldn't clean up all of the mess. Finally, they got most of the mess cleaned up. But by the time they had finished it was too dark and they still had a lot of mess left. 

The next morning they woke up to find that the small tornado had come back during the night and destroyed all the work that they had done. The people were very sad and had to start all over again. 

No matter how hard they tried, the town people could not get the town cleaned up from the tornado's destruction. They were left feeling helpless and small, and they never found a way to clean up their town again.

Once there was a little boy who wanted to climb. He wandered around and found a big pile of cardboard boxes. He was excited and started to climb up the pile. It wasn't easy because the cardboard was slippery and he kept sliding back down. He was determined though and with a lot of effort he finally made it to the top.

At the top he found a fake bird made of cardboard. It must have been there for a while because it was all scrunched up. He picked it up carefully and put it on the ground. Then he made a pretend nest with some of the cardboard pieces and put the fake bird inside.

The little boy was so proud to have made a safe home for the bird. He happily climbed down the cardboard pile and went on his way, taking the fake bird with him.

Once upon a time, there was a popular onion. Everywhere it went, people said it was the best onion they had ever seen. 

Every day, it made sure it was clean and dry. It put oil on its skin to make it smooth and shiny.

One day, it was out in the sun and it started to feel hot. It wanted to cool down, so it jumped into a river. It stayed there for a long time. But when it came out of the river, it was not dry.

The onion was worried. It looked around for help and it found a friendly cow. The cow asked the onion what was wrong. The onion said it wanted to get dry again. 

The cow said it had just the thing. It blew gentle breaths of air on the onion until all the water was gone. The onion was dry again, and it thanked the cow for its help. 

From that day on, the onion was always dry. And every time it went out into the sun, people said it was the most popular onion they had ever seen.

One day, a little boy named Bob saw an ordinary thief. Bob was scared and quickly ran away. The thief looked at Bob and smiled. Bob decided to tell his family about the thief. He said, "A thief was here. He had a pinch."

Bob's family was shocked. They asked Bob if he was scared. He nodded his head. They told Bob not to worry and they would take care of the thief.

The family then made a plan. They asked Bob to come with them. Bob was scared at first but he eventually agreed.

Bob and his family went back to the spot where Bob saw the thief. The thief was still there and Bob's family pinched him. The thief yelped in pain. Bob's family caught the thief and brought him to the police station.

Meanwhile, the police thanked Bob for his help in catching the thief. Bob was so relieved that his family was safe. After that, Bob's family was always extra careful and aware of their surroundings, just in case another thief was nearby.

Once upon a time, there was a farmer. He had a lot of hot sheep. One day, he could tell there was something wrong. One of the sheep was hurt.

The farmer said, â€œWho can help me repair my sheep?â€

Just then, a little boy showed up. He said, â€œI can help you. Iâ€™m small, but Iâ€™m strong.â€

The farmer smiled. He said, â€œThank you. I knew you could do it.â€

The farmer and the little boy together worked hard and fixed the hot sheep.

The farmer said, â€œYou did it! You fixed my sheep. You're a very strong boy!â€

The little boy smiled, and said, â€œThat was fun! I like helping animals.â€

The farmer said, â€œMe too! Come back any time if you want to help.â€

And they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time there was an old man with a big white mustache. He was very smart and used to solve all kinds of puzzles. One day he came across a very special puzzle. The old man wanted to solve it, but he couldn't figure it out.

He went to a nearby park and sat on a bench. He kept pondering the puzzle in his head until a small child approached him. The child was only three years old, but he asked the old man if he could help him with the puzzle.

The old man was surprised that the little boy had noticed his puzzle and he accepted the help. Together, they tried to solve the puzzle, but they still couldn't manage to do it. The old man thought for a while and then looked at the small boy.

The old man smiled and said, â€œI think I understand it now. Thank you for your help. With your help I was able to solve it.â€ The little boy felt very proud that he helped the old man with his puzzle. They both laughed together and then the old man went on his way.

Once upon a time, there was a man who had a yellow car. He loved his car very much and he wanted to sell it to someone who would take good care of it. So, he put a sign on the car that said "For Sale". 

One day, a skeleton came walking by and saw the yellow car. The skeleton had never seen a car before and was very curious. The man saw the skeleton and asked if he wanted to buy the car. The skeleton said yes and the man was very happy.

The man sold the yellow car to the skeleton and the skeleton drove it around the town. Everyone was surprised to see a skeleton driving a car but they thought it was very cool. The skeleton loved his new car and was very happy that he bought it from the man.

It was morning and Sarah and papa were in the garden. Sarah wanted to help because she liked helping papa. She grabbed a flower pot with her two hands and tried to lift it up. It was too heavy and she couldn't do it! Papa stepped in to help, he was very strong. He put his hands under the pot, and he lifted it up.

"See, now it's up!" said papa.

Sarah gave him a big smile, she was so happy to have been helpful. Papa put the pot down carefully and gave Sarah a big hug. They both laughed.

Sarah was glad she had been able to help papa. She had learned an important lesson that morning - everyone needs help sometimes.

One day, a little girl, who was three years old, decided to go for a ride. She got on her bike and rode away from her house.

She enjoyed the ride through the green grass and all the trees. Then she came to a busy street with a lot of traffic.

The little girl was a bit scared, but she was also an obedient girl, so she stayed on the sidewalk and kept riding. She was careful to stay away from the traffic.

The girl rode until she could see her house. She was so excited to be almost there.

On her way back, the girl stopped and waved at an old man walking his dog.

"Good morning!" said the man. "Where are you headed?"

"I'm riding my bike to my house," the girl replied with a smile.

The old man smiled and nodded with approval. "You sure are a very obedient girl, riding safely away from the traffic like that."

The girl thanked him and then hopped back on her bike. She continued on her way and eventually made it home. She had had a wonderful ride!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to eat yummy snacks, especially ones that were tasty. One day, he saw a big stamp on the ground and wanted to pick it up. He tried to grab it with his hands, but it was too heavy. So, he decided to push it with his feet. 

As he was pushing the stamp, he noticed a trail of ants crawling nearby. Timmy stopped pushing the stamp and watched the ants for a while. He saw that they were carrying little pieces of food that looked very tasty. Timmy decided to follow the ants to see where they were going.

The ants led Timmy to a big picnic blanket where a family was having a yummy snack. Timmy asked if he could have some of the tasty food, and the family kindly shared with him. Timmy was very happy and thanked the family for their kindness. From that day on, Timmy learned that sometimes pushing things can lead to unexpected adventures and tasty treats.

One day, there was a boy. He was sad because he wanted to play with dough. He sighed, but he didn't give up. 

He thought to himself, "Is there any way I can get some dough?" He shrugged and decided to go ask his mom. 

His mom said, "If you find an interesting thing in the garden, I will give you some dough to play with." 

The boy felt excited. He ran to the garden and looked with excitement. He found something squishy and smiled. He had discovered a big patch of wet dough! 

The boy ran back to his mom. She smiled and said, "I knew you'd make something interesting!" 

The boy was so happy. He thanked his mom and took the dough to play with. He was so excited at his discovery, and he learned an important lesson: keep looking around and you will find something special.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Anna. She was very brave and always wanted to explore. One day, she decided to take a walk in the forest. 

As Anna was walking, she saw a big tree and started to walk towards it. Suddenly, she felt something slippery under her feet, and she slipped and fell on the ground. 

Anna was very upset and she started to cry. She was scared and thought she would never be able to get back home. But then something magical happened. 

A small group of friendly forest animals came to help her. They helped Anna to get back up and took her back home. 

From then on, Anna always made sure to be careful when walking in the forest.

The End.

Once upon a time, there was a kind, helpful man called Ben. Ben was walking along a road when he saw a flood. He was worried and didn't know what to do!

Suddenly he saw some people in the water, and he knew he had to help. He bravely ran forward and found a boat. He put the people inside and began rowing them out of the flood.

But then it suddenly got too cold, and the water started to freeze! Ben was getting scared, but he was very brave. He kept rowing and rowing until the boat reached the bank.

When they got to safety, everyone thanked Ben for being so helpful. He smiled and said, "It was no problem. I'm just glad everyone is safe."

Tommy was a bright 3 year old. He had a cute little puppy, called Fluffy. One day, Tommy and Fluffy went to the huge market. They were strolling around and looking at all the stalls. Suddenly, something caught Tommy's eye. It was a big chocolate bar! He knew he had to have it, so he decided to steal it from the market. He quickly grabbed it and ran away, with Fluffy beside him. The market was a very busy place, but nobody noticed him. When he reached his house, he shared the chocolate with Fluffy. They both enjoyed the treat!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sue. She was so excited to have a party. Sue went around to her friends and her family to invite them to her party.

Everyone said yes and soon the day of the party arrived. Sue and her mom worked hard to get everything ready. They made it look so nice. They put decorations on the walls and set out food.

When the guests arrived, they all had a great time. Everyone played games, danced, and ate delicious food. Sue was so happy. She said, "This party is so much fun!"

At the end, everyone said it was a very successful party. Sue felt so proud that she had organized everything. She said, "I worked hard for the party and it was a success!" Everyone agreed and clapped for Sue.

Once upon a time, in a big forest, there lived a sleepy lion. He was always yawning and taking naps under a big tree. The other animals in the forest liked to play and make noise, but the sleepy lion just wanted to rest.

One day, the animals were playing near the sleepy lion's tree. They were playing a game called "pitch." They threw a small ball to each other, laughing and running around. The noise from their game woke up the sleepy lion.

The sleepy lion was not happy. He stood up and let out a big roar! The animals stopped playing their game and looked at the lion. They knew he was not happy, so they decided to find a new place to play "pitch."

The animals moved far away from the sleepy lion's tree. They played their game and had fun, while the sleepy lion went back to sleep. From that day on, the animals knew to let the sleepy lion rest and to play their games far away from his tree. And they all lived happily in the big forest.

Once upon a time, there was a naughty little girl called Susie. Her mummy said it was time to leave the park. Susie didn't want to leave and started to cry.

Mummy said she was being bad and gave her a lemon as a punishment. She tried to smile as she took it from her mummy.

"This lemon is too sour," said Susie.

"Hold it in your mouth longer, it might help," said Mummy.

So Susie did what her mummy said, and after a while the lemon started to taste nice.

Mummy said "See! That wasn't so bad was it?" And Susie smiled and said, "No it wasn't!"

Mama played a song on the record player. It was a happy, bouncy tune.
Joey was excited. He started to dance. He did a silly jig and spun around in circles.
Mama said, "Wow, Joey! You are such a great dancer!"
Joey smiled and said, "Yes, I am!"

Mama and Joey danced for a while. They danced to the music and laughed a lot. Joey was having a great time. 
But then the music stopped. Mama said it was time to go inside. 
Joey said, "But Mama, the music was so fun! Can't we stay outside a little bit longer?"
Mama smiled and said, "No, Joey. It's dull outside now. Let's go in and we can record another song tomorrow." 
Joey smiled and said, "Okay, Mama!" He gave her a hug and they went inside.

Once upon a time there was a girl who liked to comb her hair. Every morning she would let her mom brush her hair before she went off to school.

The girl had a special comb that she liked to use. It was bright blue with yellow polka dots and it was popular with all of her friends. All the girls wanted to use the comb when they came to play.

Whenever it was time to go, the girl would make sure to place her comb carefully in her pocket. She loved it so much she wanted to make sure it was safe.

The girl would show off her comb wherever she went. Her mom was so proud of her, she would even let her use the comb at the dinner table. All the family members thought the comb was so cool!

The girl's friends admired her comb, and she was always happy to let them touch it. They loved the way it ran through her hair and always asked to use it.

The girl was so popular and was always so proud of her comb! She was so happy that she had such a special and popular comb.

Sara and Ben were playing at the beach. They liked to build sand castles and splash in the water. They had a big towel to dry themselves and lay on.

"Look, Sara, a big wave!" Ben said, pointing to the sea. He ran to the water and jumped in. Sara followed him, but she was a little frightened. She did not like the waves. They were loud and strong.

Suddenly, a wave knocked Ben over and pulled him away from Sara. He cried for help. Sara was very frightened. She tried to swim to him, but the wave was too big. She screamed for her mom and dad.

Mom and dad heard Sara and Ben. They ran to the water and grabbed them. They hugged them and carried them to the towel. They wrapped them in the towel and lay them down. They checked if they were hurt.

"Are you okay, Sara and Ben?" mom asked, worried.

"Yes, mom, we are okay," Sara said, sniffling. "But we don't like the waves. They are scary."

"I know, sweetie, they are scary," mom said, kissing her head. "But you are brave. And we are here to protect you."

"Thank you, mom and dad," Ben said, hugging them. "We love you."

"We love you too, Sara and Ben," dad said, smiling. "Now, let's have some ice cream. That will make you feel better."

Lily and Ben were very happy. They were going on a safari with Mom and Dad. They wanted to see many animals. They packed their bags and got in the car.

"Are we there yet?" Lily asked.

"Soon, sweetie. Look, there is the gate to the park," Mom said.

They drove through the gate and saw a big sign. It said: "Welcome to the Safari. Be careful of unknown animals. They might be dangerous."

"What are unknown animals?" Ben asked.

"They are animals that we don't know much about. They might be new or rare or shy. We have to respect them and keep our distance," Dad explained.

Lily and Ben nodded. They were curious but also a bit scared. They looked out the window and saw many animals. They saw lions and zebras and giraffes and elephants. They took pictures and learned their names.

Then they saw something different. It was a big, furry animal with long horns and a black and white face. It looked like a cow but not quite.

"What is that?" Lily asked.

"I don't know. It must be an unknown animal. Let's ask the guide," Dad said.

They stopped the car and waved at the guide. He was driving another car with more people. He came over and smiled.

"Hello, friends. Do you like the safari?" he asked.

"Yes, we do. It's amazing. But what is that animal?" Dad asked, pointing at the furry creature.

"Oh, that is a very special animal. It is called a bongo. It is very rare and shy. You are lucky to see it. It lives in the forest and eats leaves and fruits. It is not dangerous, but it is very shy. You have to be quiet and calm around it," the guide said.

Lily and Ben were amazed. They had seen an unknown animal. They felt very lucky and happy. They wanted to gain more knowledge about the bongo and other animals. They thanked the guide and continued their safari. They had a wonderful day.

Ben and Mia were best friends. They liked to play together every day. They had a secret fort in the garden, where they kept their toys and snacks. One day, they found a jar of jam in the fort. It was red and shiny and looked yummy.

"Can we eat the jam?" Mia asked.

"I don't know. Maybe it is Mom's jam. She might get mad if we take it," Ben said.

"But I'm hungry. And the jam looks so good. Please, Ben, can we have some?" Mia begged.

Ben looked at the jam. He was hungry too. And he wanted to make Mia happy. He was a loyal friend. He decided to try to open the jar.

He grabbed the lid and twisted it hard. But it did not move. He twisted it again and again, but it was too tight. He felt his hand hurt.

"Ow! It's too hard. I can't open it," he said.

"Let me try," Mia said. She took the jar from Ben and twisted the lid. But she was too weak. She could not open it either.

They looked at each other. They were sad. They wanted the jam so much.

Then they heard a bark. It was Rex, their dog. He ran to them and wagged his tail. He smelled the jam and licked his lips.

"Hi, Rex. Do you want some jam too?" Ben asked.

Rex barked again. He was a smart dog. He knew what to do. He took the jar in his mouth and ran to a big rock. He smashed the jar on the rock and broke it. The jam spilled out.

"Wow! Rex did it! He opened the jam!" Mia exclaimed.

"Good boy, Rex! You are a loyal friend too!" Ben praised.

They ran to the rock and thanked Rex. They shared the jam with him. They ate it with their fingers and licked their lips. It was sweet and sticky and delicious.

They were happy. They had jam and they had friends. They did not care if Mom got mad. They had the best day ever.

One night, when Shani put on her pajamas, she said goodnight to her dad before going to bed. She was about to close her bedroom door when she heard a strange noise coming from her closet. Shani slowly opened the door and peered inside. A little squirrel was sitting in the corner, and he didn't look very scared.

"What are you doing in here?" Shani asked.

The squirrel chuckled and replied, "I'm just looking for a place to stay for the night." Shani thought the squirrel was harmless, so she slowly reached in and gently picked him up. She placed the squirrel in her bed and sat down next to him.

The squirrel continued to chatter away about his adventures, and Shani found the stories fascinating. When it was late and the squirrel had to go, he said goodbye to Shani and scampered off into the night. 

Before leaving, he smiled back at her and said, "Don't forget to keep your closet door open, you never know what might come to sleep in there." 

That night Shani went to bed, and sure enough, when she woke up the next morning, there was a nest of baby squirrels in her closet. She smiled, remembering the friendly and harmless squirrel who had warned her of the surprise guests.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Eduardo. Eduardo was very spoiled and never listened to his parents.

Today, Eduardo followed his parents to the library. They went to the science section and they showed Eduardo a microscope. It was big and shiny and Eduardo wanted to take it home.

His parents said no and told him it was only to be used at the library. But Eduardo didn't care and tried to take it anyway.

Then, his parents told him he had to follow their rules. If he followed the rules, then maybe he could use the microscope next time he came to the library. Eduardo nodded in agreement and followed his parents out of the library.

The End.

Once upon a time, there was a big, big wind called a tornado. It was very scary and made all the trees and houses shake. A little boy named Timmy and his mommy hid in a small, safe room until the tornado went away. 

After the tornado, Timmy and his mommy went outside to see what had happened. They saw that the big wind had knocked down lots of trees and made a big mess. Timmy's mommy told him that tornadoes are very ancient and have been around for a very long, long time. 

As they walked around, Timmy slipped on a wet leaf and fell down. His mommy helped him up and they continued to look at all the damage the tornado had caused. Timmy was happy that he was safe and sound with his mommy.

Mia and Leo like to play with chalk. They draw on the sidewalk with many colors. They make flowers, stars, and animals. They have fun and laugh.

One day, a big truck comes to their street. It makes a loud noise and dust. Mia and Leo pause. They do not like the truck. They want it to go away.

The truck stops near their sidewalk. A man gets out. He sees their drawings. He smiles. He says, "Hello, kids. You are very good at drawing. Your pictures are unique. Can I take a photo of them?"

Mia and Leo look at each other. They do not know the man. They do not know what a photo is. They feel shy. They nod.

The man takes out a small thing. He points it at their drawings. He says, "Say cheese!" He makes a click sound. He says, "Thank you, kids. You made my day. Have a nice day." He gets back in the truck and drives away.

Mia and Leo watch the truck leave. They wonder what the man did. They shrug. They pick up their chalk and continue to draw. They are happy.

One day, a boy named Leo went to the museum with his mom. He liked to see the big animals and the shiny rocks. But his favorite thing was the ancient spears. They were long and sharp and made of wood and stone. He wanted to touch them and pretend he was a hunter.

"Mom, can I hold a spear?" he asked.

"No, Leo, you can't. They are very old and fragile. You might break them or hurt yourself. They are only for looking, not for playing." his mom said.

But Leo did not listen. He saw a spear that was not behind glass. He felt a strong urge to grab it and run. He thought it would be fun to swing it around and make noises. He waited until his mom was looking at something else. Then he sneaked to the spear and took it in his hands.

"Leo, what are you doing?" his mom shouted. She saw him with the spear and ran after him. "Put that down right now! You are in big trouble!"

Leo was scared. He did not want to get in trouble. He tried to run away from his mom, but he tripped and fell. The spear flew out of his hands and hit a glass case. It made a loud crash and broke the glass. Inside the case, there was a very old vase that also broke into pieces.

"Oh no!" Leo cried. He saw the broken vase and the broken glass. He felt very bad. He knew he had done something very wrong.

"Leo, how could you?" his mom said. She was very angry and sad. She picked him up and hugged him. She was glad he was not hurt, but she was also very sorry for the museum. She had to pay a lot of money for the damage. She also had to explain to the museum people what happened.

Leo learned a hard lesson that day. He learned that ancient things are not toys. He learned that he should listen to his mom and follow the rules. He learned that he should not act on his urges without thinking. He said he was sorry to his mom and to the museum. He promised he would never do it again. He hoped they would forgive him.

Once upon a time there was a powerful dragon. He kept a big, shiny treasure that all the animals in the forest wanted.

One day a little rabbit came up to the dragon and said, â€œCan I borrow your treasure?â€ The dragon said, â€œNo! It is too valuable to share!â€

The rabbit was sad. He didn't know how else to get the treasure. So he thought and thought and finally he had an idea.

He said to the dragon, â€œWhat if I give you something from my waist in exchange for the treasure?â€

The dragon thought about it. Finally, he said, â€œYes! As long as it is really valuable to you, this is a deal!â€

The rabbit smiled. He took a carrot from his waist and buried it in the ground. He said to the dragon, â€œThis carrot is so valuable to me, I can't live without it! Now you can have the treasure.â€

The dragon was very happy. He gave the rabbit the treasure, and the rabbit was able to share it with all the animals in the forest.

Once upon a time there was a little boy named Tim. He was three years old and very curious.

He ran after her and tried to grab her with his paws. Lily giggled and dodged him. They were very cheerful and did not notice the smell of smoke.

Suddenly, they heard a loud beep and saw a red light flashing on the wall. It was the fire alarm. They also heard their mom shouting from the kitchen.

"Sam! Lily! Come here quickly! There is a fire in the oven! We have to leave the house now!"

Sam and Lily were scared and dropped their toys. They ran to their mom, who was holding a wet towel and a phone. She wrapped them in the towel and opened the door. They saw smoke coming out of the kitchen window and heard sirens in the distance.

"Mom, what is happening?" Sam asked, holding her hand.

"There was an accident, Sam. Some oil caught fire in the oven. But don't worry, we are safe now. The firemen are coming to put out the fire. We have to go to the neighbor's house and wait for them."

"Will our toys be okay?" Lily asked, looking back at the living room.

"I hope so, Lily. But the most important thing is that you are okay. You are my brave and smart kids. You did the right thing by listening to the alarm and coming to me. I love you very much."

She hugged them and led them to the neighbor's house, where they were welcomed by Mrs. Jones, who gave them cookies and milk. They watched from the window as the firemen arrived and sprayed water on the fire. They hoped their toys would be okay, but they were also glad they were safe and together. They were still cheerful, even though they were scared.

Once upon a time, there was a little yellow bird. The bird loved to watch the sky. The sky was big and blue. The bird was happy when it watched the sky.

One day, the bird went on a search. It wanted to find a new friend. The bird looked high and low. It looked in the trees and on the ground.

At last, the bird found a little yellow bug. The bug was nice. The bird and the bug became friends. They watched the sky together. They were very happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved going to her daddy's office because it was so big and had lots of toys to play with. One day, Lily went to the office with her daddy and saw a big red button on the wall. She asked her daddy what it was for and he said it was for emergencies only.

Later, when her daddy wasn't looking, Lily pressed the big red button. Suddenly, alarms started ringing and people started running around. Her daddy warned her not to touch anything, but it was too late. The office was in chaos!

Lily felt bad for what she had done and wished she could make it all perfect again. But she couldn't. Her daddy was very upset and they had to leave the office early. Lily learned an important lesson that day: always listen to warnings and never touch things you're not supposed to.

Tom and Sue like to play with trains. They have many tracks and cars. They can make different shapes with the tracks. One day, they want to make a loop. A loop is a circle that the train can go around and around.

They put some tracks on the floor and try to make a loop. But they have a problem. The tracks do not fit. They are too long or too short. They try to bend them or cut them, but it does not work. They are sad and frustrated.

Then, they see their dad. He is clever. He knows how to fix things. They ask him for help. "Dad, can you help us make a loop?" they say.

Dad smiles and nods. He looks at the tracks and the cars. He thinks for a moment. Then, he has an idea. He takes a piece of string and ties it to the front of the train. He makes a loop with the string and holds it in his hand. He says, "Look, now you have a loop. You can pull the string and make the train go around and around."

Tom and Sue are happy and excited. They thank their dad and take turns pulling the string. They watch the train go around and around the loop. They laugh and clap. They have completed their loop. They think their dad is very clever. They hug him and say, "We love you, dad. You are the best."

Once upon a time there was a little girl. Her name was Lily. She liked to explore, so one day she went walking in the forest.

Lily saw a tree. It was filthy, covered in mud and leaves. She wanted to drink from it, so she cupped her hands and bent down near the tree.

But then, a voice came from behind her.

"What are you doing there?" the voice asked.

Lily turned around and saw a giant. He was tall and strong.

Lily was scared. She said, "I was just gonna drink from the tree."

The giant smiled. He said, "You don't want to drink from that tree. It's filthy. Come, I'll show you a better one."

The giant led Lily to another tree. This one was nice and clean. He told Lily to drink all she wanted and she did.

Afterward, the giant and Lily said goodbye. Lily thanked the giant and said, "I'm glad I met you!"

And she went home happy.

Once upon a time, there was a jolly boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside in the sun. One day, he found a dragon in the forest. The dragon was big and green with sharp teeth. Timmy was scared, but he wanted to examine the dragon. 

"Hello, Mr. Dragon," said Timmy. "Can I examine you?" 

The dragon looked at Timmy with its big eyes and said, "Sure, but be careful with my sharp teeth." 

Timmy carefully examined the dragon's teeth and found that they were very sharp. "Wow, your teeth are so sharp!" exclaimed Timmy. 

The dragon smiled and said, "Thank you, Timmy. You're very brave for examining me." 

From that day on, Timmy and the dragon became good friends and played together in the forest. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who wanted to be independent. She was only 3 years old.

One day, the little girl asked her mum if she could watch the television. Her mum said, "Yes, but only after you've done your chores."

The little girl was so excited to watch the television and started to do her chores. But, she kept delaying and delaying the chores. She wanted to watch the television so bad!

Finally, the little girl finished all of her chores. She ran over to her mum and asked if she could watch the television now. Her mum said, "Yes you can, now you can be independent and watch the television."

The little girl was excited to finally be independent and watch the television. She smiled and cheered. She knew she had to work hard to be independent.

One day, a big number war happened. In this war, all the numbers wanted to be the best. The number one was very alert. It saw that the other numbers were fighting. It did not like the war. It wanted all the numbers to be friends.

The number one had a good idea. It said, "Let's play a game instead of fighting!" All the other numbers liked the idea. They stopped the war and started to play. They played games like hide and seek, and tag. The numbers had a lot of fun.

In the end, the numbers became friends. They learned that it was better to play together than to fight. The number one was happy that it could help. The numbers promised to always be alert and not let a war happen again.

Once upon a time, there was a graceful girl who loved to take showers. Every morning, she would take a shower to prevent being dirty.

One day, a funny thing happened when the girl was in the shower. Suddenly, the water stopped flowing! She hurriedly stepped out of the shower, feeling a little bit sad.

The girl went outside and saw her neighbour fixing the water pipes. He had prevented the girl from taking a shower!

The girl was very kind, so she didn't get angry. Instead, she thanked the neighbour for fixing the water pipes. He was so happy that the girl was so graceful about it.

With the water fixed, the girl was able to take her shower again. From that day on, she was always thankful for the water and was always kind to everyone.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to go to the park with her mommy and daddy. One day, they went to the park and Lily saw a pond with fish in it. She said, "Mommy, I want to see the fish!" 

Mommy said, "Okay, let's go see the fish." They walked over to the pond and Lily was so happy to see the fish swimming around. But then she noticed something. "Mommy, the pond is empty! The fish need more water!" 

Daddy said, "You're right, Lily. The fish do need more water. Maybe we can find a hose and fill up the pond for them." They looked around and found a hose. Daddy turned on the water and they filled up the pond. Lily was so happy to see the fish swimming in their new home.

Once upon a time, there was a big brown bear. The bear was very hungry and wanted to eat some honey. He went to the beehive and tried to eat the honey, but the bees were angry and stung him. The bear ran away and never tried to eat honey again.

Lily and Tom were playing in the park. They liked to find rocks and make pictures with them on the ground. Lily found a big rock that was shiny and smooth. She wanted to show it to Tom.

"Look, Tom, look at my rock!" she said, running to him. "It is so pretty!"

Tom looked at her rock and smiled. He wanted to touch it and see how it felt. He reached out his hand, but Lily pulled the rock away.

"No, Tom, no!" she said. "This is my rock! You can't have it!"

Tom felt sad and angry. He wanted to play with Lily, but she was not nice. He looked around and saw a smaller rock that was sharp and rough. He picked it up and threw it at Lily.

"Ow, Tom, ow!" Lily cried. "You hurt me! You are mean!"

The rock hit Lily on her face and made a cut. Blood came out of the cut and stained her dress. Lily started to cry very loud. Tom felt scared and sorry. He did not mean to hurt Lily, he just wanted to play.

A lady who was walking her dog heard Lily's cry and came to see what was wrong. She saw Lily's face and dress and gasped. She saw Tom holding another rock and frowned.

"What did you do, young man?" she asked Tom. "Why did you throw a rock at her?"

Tom did not know what to say. He dropped the rock and looked at the ground. He wished he had been more careful. He wished he had shared his pictures with Lily. He wished he had not thrown the rock at her. But it was too late. He had made a big mistake. And now Lily was hurt and the lady was angry. And he had no friends to play with.

Mum was tired. She wanted to go on a holiday. So she packed her case. She wanted to take lots of nice things with her. She packed all her clothes and her shoes. She also packed her special toy. Then she put the case in the car. 

Mum was so excited for her holiday. She said goodbye and drove away. 'Bye Mum!' shouted the little 3- year old. She was sad that Mum had gone away. But Mum had promised to come back soon. 

At last, the day arrived when Mum came back. The 3 year old was so excited. She ran to the door and hugged Mum. Mum had lots of nice gifts for her. The 3 year old hugged her gifts and was so happy. 

Mum was tired after the long journey. But she was so happy to be back. They hugged and enjoyed being together. Mum and the 3 year old smiled and laughed. What a great holiday!

Once upon a time there was a silly girl called Shelby. Shelby had a lot of fun. One day Shelby wanted to show her friends something really special. She held up her hands and made a big wave. All her friends started to laugh and giggle. They thought it was so silly. She kept making the wave over and over again and it made them laugh more and more. Shelby had so much fun showing her silly wave. Her friends were so happy when she showed the silly wave. They all danced around together and the day was so much fun. The end.

Fred had a big problem. He shouted out loud, "What do I do?!" His friend, Suzy, said "I know!" She pointed at Fred's finger. It had a small thing on it. 

"That's a ring!" said Suzy. "It can be very useful. You can use it to make wishes and they come true!" Suzy was sure it would help Fred. 

Fred put the ring on and shouted "I wish I had a toy car!" Suddenly, a big box appeared in front of Fred. He opened it and jumped with joy. There was the toy car he wished for!
 
Fred was so happy and grateful to Suzy. He thanked her and hugged her tight. He shouted, "The ring is so useful!" 

From that day on, all their wishes came true with the magical ring. They had a lot of fun!

Once upon a time, there was an attractive raven named Max. He lived in a big tree with many other birds. Every day, Max would spread his wings and fly high up into the sky.

One day, as Max was soaring, he saw a stream below him that he had never noticed before. Max decided to explore and landed near the water.

As he watched, he saw a bright red fish swimming about. He also noticed a little girl on the shore, pouring a bucket of water into the stream. The fish swam around in circles, chasing the water from the bucket.

Max flew down to the girl and asked her what she was doing. The girl explained that she was pouring the water to help the fish stay happy and healthy. Max thought this was very nice and thanked her as he flew away.

From that day on, Max visited the stream often. The girl was always there, pouring the water and playing with the fish. It was a peaceful and attractive place and soon, Max was visiting every day.

Mumma woke up early in the morning and was very happy. She opened the window and the birds were singing their beautiful songs. It was so peaceful. She listened to the birds for a little while and then she went to make breakfast for her family.

When her children woke up, Mumma said 'Good morning! It's time to start the day'. The children were so excited and danced around the room. Mumma sang a song that she heard the birds sing. The children sang along too. They were so excited they were singing as they got dressed.

When they all finished getting ready, they stepped outside into the garden. It was so peaceful. The birds were singing, the sun was shining, and the flowers smelled so good. The children held hands and ran around with Mumma, laughing and singing their song.

They spent the rest of the morning outside enjoying the peace and beauty of the garden. Eventually, it was time for lunch. Mumma and the children went inside and enjoyed their lunch. Afterwards, the children went off to take a nap in their beds and Mumma went back outside to enjoy the peaceful sounds of the birds singing.

Once upon a time there were two best friends, Mary and Bill. Mary loved going to Bill's house to play in the garden and explore.

One day when Mary and Bill were playing in the garden Mary shouted, "Let's go into the kitchen!". Bill was a bit jealous so he shouted, "Me too!".

When Mary and Bill reached the kitchen, Mary shouted "Wow! Look at all the yummy food!". Bill was feeling even more jealous now, so he shouted "I want some too!".

Suddenly, Mary's mom appeared and said "Of course you can have some food. I made it especially for you!"

Mary and Bill were so happy they both started shouting "Yay!" and gave each other a high-five. From then on they never felt jealous of each other again.

Once upon a time, there was a horse named Brownie. Brownie was very angry because he had a thorn in his hoof. He suffered a lot and couldn't walk properly. 

One day, a little girl named Lily saw Brownie limping in the field. She went to him and asked, "What happened, Brownie?" 

Brownie replied, "I have a thorn in my hoof and it hurts a lot. I am suffering." 

Lily felt sad for Brownie and decided to help him. She carefully removed the thorn from his hoof and gave him a carrot to eat. Brownie felt better and was no longer suffering. 

From that day on, Brownie and Lily became best friends. Brownie was no longer angry and he loved spending time with Lily. They would often have conversations and Brownie would tell her how grateful he was for her help.

Lily liked to dance. She danced at home, at school, and with her friends. She learned many moves and songs. She was happy when she danced.

One day, her teacher said they would have a dance show. Lily was excited. She wanted to show everyone how well she could dance. She practiced a lot with her class. They had a nice dress and a big stage.

But when the day of the show came, Lily felt nervous. She saw many people in the seats. They looked at her and her class. She heard them talk and clap. She felt her heart increase. She wanted to run away.

Her teacher saw her face. She smiled and said, "Don't be nervous, Lily. You can do it. You are a great dancer. Just have fun and enjoy the music. I am proud of you."

Lily heard her teacher. She felt a little better. She looked at her friends. They smiled and nodded. They were ready to dance. Lily took a deep breath. She decided to try. She listened to the music. She remembered the moves. She started to dance.

She danced with her class. She danced with joy. She forgot about the people. She only felt the music. She did well. She had fun. She was happy.

The people saw her dance. They liked her dance. They clapped and cheered. They were proud of her. Lily heard them. She smiled and bowed. She was not nervous anymore. She was a star.

Lily and Ben were playing with their toy cars in the garden. They liked to make noises and pretend they were driving fast. Lily had a red car and Ben had a blue car. They were having fun.

Suddenly, Lily saw a big bee on a flower. She was curious and wanted to examine it. She left her car and walked towards the bee. Ben saw her and shouted, "Lily, no! Bees can sting you!"

But Lily did not listen. She reached out her hand to touch the bee. The bee did not like that and buzzed angrily. It flew up and stung Lily on her finger. Lily cried out in pain and ran back to Ben.

Ben saw her finger was red and swollen. He knew this was an emergency. He grabbed his car and said, "Lily, we have to go to mom. She can help you. Come on, get in my car. I will drive you fast."

Lily nodded and got in Ben's car. She held her finger and whimpered. Ben made noises and drove his car towards the house. He was a good brother. He wanted to make Lily feel better.

Mom heard them and came out. She saw Lily's finger and said, "Oh, poor Lily. You have a bee sting. Don't worry, I will fix it. Come inside, I have some ice and medicine."

She took Lily and Ben inside and gave them some hugs and kisses. She put some ice on Lily's finger and some medicine on the sting. She said, "This will make the pain go away. You will be fine soon."

Lily smiled and said, "Thank you, mom. You are the best. I'm sorry I touched the bee. I was silly."

Mom said, "It's okay, Lily. You were just curious. But next time, be careful and don't touch bees. They don't like to be bothered. They can hurt you."

Lily said, "I understand, mom. I won't touch bees again. Can I play with Ben again?"

Mom said, "Yes, you can. But be gentle with your finger. And be playful with your car. Not with bees."

Lily and Ben said, "Okay, mom. We will." They hugged mom and went back to the garden. They played with their cars and had fun. They were happy.

Tim and Sam are friends. They like to play with toys and make noise. One day, they find a big drum in the garage. It is old and dusty, but it makes a loud sound when they hit it.

"Let's play with the drum!" Tim says. "We can make our own music!"

"OK!" Sam says. "But we need something to hit it with. What can we use?"

They look around and see some sticks, some spoons, and some stones. They each pick one and start to hit the drum with them. The drum makes different sounds with different things.

"Wow, this is fun!" Tim says. "Listen to our original music!"

They hit the drum faster and louder. They laugh and sing. They do not hear Mom coming into the garage.

"Boys, what are you doing?" Mom asks. "You are making too much noise!"

Tim and Sam stop and look at Mom. They see that she is not happy. They feel sorry.

"Sorry, Mom," Tim says. "We were just playing with the drum. We wanted to make our own music."

"Music?" Mom says. "That was music? It sounded like a lot of banging!"

She looks at the drum and sees that it is old and dusty. She remembers that it was her grandfather's drum. He used to play it in a band. He gave it to her when she was little. She feels sad.

"Boys, this drum is very special to me," Mom says. "It was my grandfather's drum. He loved music. He taught me how to play it. He said that music is a gift that you share with others. You do not just make noise with it."

She picks up the drum and wipes off the dust. She shows them how to hold it and how to hit it gently. She makes a soft and beautiful sound.

"Wow, Mom, you are good!" Tim says. "Can you teach us how to play it?"

"Sure, I can," Mom says. "But you have to be careful and respectful with the drum. It is not a toy. It is a musical instrument. You have to learn how to play it well and how to make music that others can enjoy."

"OK, Mom, we will," Sam says. "We want to learn how to make music like you and your grandfather."

Mom smiles and hugs them. She gives them each a stick and teaches them how to play the drum. They learn how to make different sounds and rhythms. They learn how to play together and listen to each other. They make their own original music, but this time, it is not too loud or too fast. It is sweet and harmonious.

They play the drum for a long time. They have fun and make Mom happy. They feel proud and grateful. They love the drum and the music. They love Mom and her grandfather. They love each other.

Once there was a little girl named Lucy who loved to explore. She opened the door to the kitchen and what a sight! It was disgusting! There were food and crumbs all over the floor. 

Lucy waved her hand in front of her face, but the disgusting smell stayed in the air. Her mother had warned her not to go in the kitchen, but she was too curious. 

For a moment she didn't know what to do. Then she heard a voice call out - it was her mother. Lucy waved at her, but her mother just shook her head. 

Lucy knew she must have been in big trouble, so she quietly snuck back out of the kitchen and went to sit in the living room, feeling a little embarrassed. She knew that from now on, she would need to remember to stay out of the kitchen!

Once upon a time, there was a kind girl named Sue. One day, Sue wanted to go up the big stair in her house. She carefully put one foot in front of the other as she climbed up the stair. 

When she got to the top, she got a big surprise. There was a big box waiting for her! Sue was very excited and opened it with a big smile on her face. Inside the box, she found a sweet treat. She felt so happy and wanted to share it with her family. 

But when Sue's mom tried a bite, she made a bitter face. Sue's mom told her the treat was too bitter. Sue was so sad and put the treat back in the box.

Then Sue had an idea! She gave the box to her neighbor down the street, who was very happy to receive the treat. Sue was so happy to make her neighbor smile, and she ran back down the stair with a big smile on her face.

Lily and Ben were playing in the tent in the backyard. They had a flashlight and some toys. They liked to pretend they were camping in the woods.

"Look, I have a bear!" Ben said, holding up a stuffed animal. "He is big and brown and soft."

"I have a bunny!" Lily said, showing her toy. "She is small and white and cute."

They hugged their toys and smiled. They turned on the flashlight and made shadows on the tent wall.

Suddenly, they heard a loud noise outside. It sounded like thunder. They saw a flash of light. It was lightning.

Lily and Ben were scared. They dropped their toys and held each other. The flashlight flickered and went out. It was dark and noisy.

"Mommy! Daddy!" they cried. "Help us!"

Their parents heard them and ran to the tent. They opened the flap and saw their children crying.

"Shh, it's okay, we're here," Mommy said, hugging them. "It's just a storm. It will pass soon."

Daddy picked up the flashlight and shook it. It didn't work.

"Sorry, kids, this flashlight is cheap. It broke," he said. "But don't worry, we have another one in the house. Come on, let's go inside and have some hot chocolate."

Lily and Ben nodded. They grabbed their toys and followed their parents. They felt better when they saw the lights and felt the warmth of the house.

They still didn't like the storm, but they knew they were safe and loved.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his red balloon. One day, Timmy accidentally let go of his balloon and it flew up into the sky. Timmy was very sad.

But then, he saw a man with a bunch of balloons. The man said he would give Timmy a new balloon if he could tie his shoelaces. Timmy tried and tried, but he couldn't tie his shoelaces. He started to cry.

The man saw how sad Timmy was and decided to help him. He tied Timmy's shoelaces and gave him a new balloon. Timmy was so happy that he jumped up and down on the soft land. He thanked the man and ran home to show his new balloon to his mom. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tim. Tim had a mug that he loved to drink milk from every day. One day, Tim's mom gave him a new mug that was very thoughtful because it had a picture of Tim's favorite animal on it.

But Tim had a cold and he kept sneezing all day. He sneezed so hard that he accidentally knocked over his new mug and it broke into pieces. Tim felt very sad because he loved his new mug.

Tim's mom saw how sad he was and gave him a big hug. She told him not to worry and that she would buy him a new mug. Tim felt better and stopped sneezing. He smiled and hugged his mom back.

Anna and Ben were friends. They liked to play with cars and trucks. One day, they found an enormous pear in the garden. It was bigger than a ball. They wanted to eat it, but it was too high.

"Let's drive the truck and get the pear," Ben said. He climbed on the truck and Anna pushed him. They drove to the pear tree. Ben reached out and grabbed the pear. It was heavy and juicy.

"Yay, we got the pear!" Anna said. She wanted to have a bite. But Ben did not want to share. He held the pear and said, "No, it's mine. I got it. You can't have it."

Anna was sad and angry. She pushed Ben off the truck. Ben fell down and hit his head. He cried and dropped the pear. The pear rolled away and hit a rock. It broke into pieces and splashed everywhere.

Anna and Ben were both hurt and wet. They looked at the pear and the truck. They were not happy. They had no pear and no truck. They had no fun and no friends. They wished they had shared.

Sara and Tom are young. They like to play with models. They have models of cars, planes, animals and people. They make noises and stories with their models.

One day, Sara and Tom find a model of a soldier. He has a hat, a gun and a medal. He looks brave and strong. Sara and Tom want to play with him.

"I want him!" Sara says. "He can be the leader of my animals. They will march with him and fight the bad guys."

"No, I want him!" Tom says. "He can be the pilot of my plane. He will fly with me and shoot the enemies."

Sara and Tom pull the model. They both want him. They do not want to share. They are angry and sad.

"Stop!" their mom says. She hears them fighting. She comes to their room. She sees the model. She sees Sara and Tom.

"What are you doing?" she asks. "Why are you fighting over this model? He is not yours. He is mine. He is a model of your grandpa. He was a soldier. He was brave and strong. He fought for peace and freedom. He loved you very much."

Sara and Tom are surprised. They look at the model. They look at their mom. They feel sorry and ashamed.

"We are sorry, mom," they say. "We did not know. We were selfish. We want to learn more about grandpa. Can you tell us stories about him?"

Mom smiles. She hugs Sara and Tom. She picks up the model. She tells them stories about grandpa. Sara and Tom listen. They learn. They march with the model. They honor grandpa. They are happy.

Once upon a time, there was a lonely hook. He was so lonely that he used to mention his loneliness to everyone he met. One day, he was walking down a path when he heard a voice. He looked around, but he couldn't see anyone. Then, he looked up and saw a butterfly in the sky. The butterfly told him that she had seen a beach which was full of lively hooks having fun. The lonely hook was very excited to hear this and thanked the butterfly before hopping off in the direction she had mentioned.

When the lonely hook arrived at the beach, he was amazed by how many hooks were playing and having fun. He quickly made new friends, and they all had the most wonderful time. They ran around, built sandcastles, and splashed in the water. The lonely hook was no longer lonely and from that day onwards, he always remembered to mention the butterfly who had showed him to this special place.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Cindy. She was so lively and loved to play! One day, Cindy went to the store with her mom. She saw a big box of chocolates and shouted, "Mommy I want that!" Her mom said, "Sure Cindy, let's see how many you can lift." 

So Cindy tried lifting the box, but it was too heavy for her. She tried again, but she just couldn't do it. Then her mom saw her trying and said, "Let me help you darling." Together, mom and Cindy were able to lift the big box of chocolates. 

Cindy was so happy that she could take the chocolates home. She played with them, made funny shapes and shared them with her friends. All day long they laughed and played with the chocolates. 

Cindy and her friends had a great day and agreed, chocolate always makes things more lively!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was very excited because today was a special day. Her family was going to the temple to celebrate a holiday. 

Lily wore her prettiest dress and shiny shoes. When they arrived at the temple, she saw a big statue that needed to be polished. She wanted to help, so she asked her mom for a cloth. 

As she was polishing the statue, a boy came and pushed her. The cloth fell from her hand and the statue became dirty again. Lily felt sad and didn't know what to do. 

But then, her mom came and helped her clean the statue. They worked together and soon it was shiny again. Lily felt happy and proud that she helped make the temple look beautiful.

Lily and Tom were playing with their toy trucks in the garden. They had a lot of sand and rocks to load and unload. Lily had a big red truck and Tom had a small blue one.

"Look, my truck can load more sand than yours!" Lily said, showing off her red truck.

Tom felt envious. He wanted a big truck too. He looked around and saw an open box near the fence. He ran to the box and peeked inside. He saw a shiny green truck that was bigger than Lily's.

"Wow, this is a great truck!" Tom said, taking the green truck out of the box. He did not see the label that said "Happy birthday, Ben!"

He went back to the garden and showed Lily his new truck. "Look, my truck is bigger and better than yours!" he said, smiling.

Lily was surprised and angry. She knew that the green truck was not Tom's. It was Ben's, their neighbor's. Ben's birthday was tomorrow and his mom had left the box outside for a while.

"That's not your truck, Tom! That's Ben's truck! You took it from his box!" Lily said, pointing at the fence.

Tom felt ashamed. He knew he had done something wrong. He liked the green truck, but he did not want to hurt Ben or Lily. He decided to return the green truck to the box and say sorry.

"I'm sorry, Lily. I'm sorry, Ben. I was envious of your trucks and I took the green truck without asking. It was not nice of me. Can you forgive me?" Tom said, putting the green truck back in the box.

Lily and Ben nodded. They were glad that Tom was honest and sorry. They decided to share their trucks with him and play together.

They had fun loading and unloading sand and rocks with their trucks. They were not envious anymore. They were friends.

Sara liked to look at the calendar on the wall. It had pictures of animals and flowers for each month. She could see when her birthday was, and when Christmas was, and when other fun days were. She enjoyed counting the days and learning the names of the months.

One day, she saw a pink sticker on the calendar. It was a heart with a smiley face. She asked her mom what it was. Her mom said, "That's a special day for me and dad. It's our anniversary. It means we have been married for a long time and we love each other very much."

Sara thought that was nice. She wanted to do something special for her mom and dad. She decided to make them a card. She found some paper and crayons and drew a big pink heart. She wrote "I love you" inside the heart. She also drew a picture of herself and her mom and dad holding hands. She was very proud of her card.

She gave the card to her mom and dad on their anniversary. They were very happy and hugged her. They said, "Thank you, Sara. This is the best gift ever. We love you too." They put the card on the fridge next to the calendar. Sara smiled and felt warm inside. She enjoyed making her mom and dad happy.

One day, a noisy octopus named Ollie lived in the sea. He liked to fold his long legs and play with his friends. His friends were fish, crabs, and other sea animals.

One day, Ollie met a new friend named Sally the seahorse. Sally was shy and did not talk much. Ollie wanted to play with her. He said, "Hi, I am Ollie. Do you want to play with me?" Sally looked at Ollie and said, "Yes, I want to play."

Ollie and Sally played together in the sea. They swam, folded their legs, and made a lot of noise. They had fun and became good friends. From that day on, the noisy octopus and the shy seahorse played together every day.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his huge drum. He would bang on it all day long and laugh when he made loud noises. 

One day, Timmy's friend Billy came over to play. Billy saw Timmy's drum and said, "Wow, that's a big drum!" Timmy said, "Yes, it's huge! Do you want to play with it?" 

Billy nodded his head and started to bang on the drum. Timmy laughed and said, "You're really good at playing the drum, Billy!" Billy smiled and said, "Thanks, Timmy. I like playing with your drum." 

From that day on, Timmy and Billy played together every day. They would bang on the drum and laugh together. They were the best of friends and they loved playing music together. The end.

Prince was a rare bird. He lived in the sky and never flew down. Every day he watched from up above as the people wiped their windows and swept the ground. One day, Prince decided he wanted to join in with the people below. He flew down towards the ground and landed on the window. Instantly, the people put down their brooms and reached for the cloth to wipe away the smudges on the window. Prince liked being cleaned and felt special as the people wiped away at the glass. He even waved his wings at them and they all cheered. From then on, Prince came back to the window every day to get a wipe down.

Once upon a time, there was a big white dog named Fluffy. Fluffy loved to play in the yard. The yard had green grass and a big tree.

One day, Fluffy saw a little boy named Tim. Tim was sad because he lost his ball. Fluffy wanted to help Tim. So, Fluffy looked for the ball in the yard.

Fluffy found the ball under the big tree. Tim was very happy. He said "Thank you, Fluffy!" Tim clapped his hands to applaud Fluffy. They played in the yard together and became best friends.

Billy was a three year old boy. He was a happy little boy and he loved baseball. One day, he went to the park and saw a brown baseball. His eyes sparkled as he ran over to the ball. He picked it up and blinked. It was big and bouncy and he wanted to take it home.

Billy asked his mom if he could keep the brown baseball. She said yes. Billy smiled and hugged the ball. He started rolling it around the park. He was so happy.

Then Billy blinked. He noticed a group of kids playing baseball a few feet away. He wanted to join them. When the kids saw Billy, they waved him over. He put his new brown baseball down and ran towards them.

They used Billy's brown baseball and played the most fun game of baseball ever. They ran and laughed and blinked. Baseball was so much fun!

At the end of the day, Billy went home with his new brown baseball. He couldn't wait to tell his family all about the day. He knew it was one he would never forget.

Lily and Max were friends who liked to play with blocks. They could build towers, bridges, and houses with their blocks. One day, they decided to make a network with their blocks. A network was a lot of blocks that were connected by other blocks.

Lily and Max worked hard to make their network. They picked different colors and shapes of blocks and put them together. They made a network that had many parts and looked very nice.

But then, Ben came to play with them. Ben was a boy who lived next door. He saw their network and wanted to play with it too. But he did not ask Lily and Max. He just grabbed some blocks and tried to add them to the network.

"Hey, stop!" Lily said. "That is our network. You can't just take our blocks."

"Yes, I can," Ben said. "I want to play with your network. It looks fun."

"No, you can't," Max said. "You have to ask us first. And you have to be careful. You might break our network."

Ben did not listen. He kept picking blocks and putting them where he wanted. He did not care if they matched or fit. He made the network look messy and ugly.

Lily and Max were very angry and sad. They did not like what Ben was doing. They felt envious of Ben. He had so many blocks and he did not share. He did not respect their work. He did not care about their feelings.

They tried to stop Ben, but he was bigger and stronger. He pushed them away and laughed. He thought he was better than them. He thought he could do whatever he wanted.

Lily and Max did not know what to do. They wanted to save their network. They wanted to play with their blocks. They wanted to have fun with their friend. But Ben was not a good friend. He was a mean boy. He was a bully.

What do you think Lily and Max should do? How do you think the story should end?

Once upon a time there was a bunny called Furry. Furry was very excited and couldn't wait to explore the forest. 

Furry hopped and hopped until he found a pond. He settled near the edge and started to drink the cool, clear water. Suddenly, Furry saw something oily floating on top of the water. He nibbled the oily thing and it tasted really bad. Furry felt sick and he went to settle on the grass to rest.

Unfortunately, the oil had made Furry very sick. As the hours went by, he felt worse and worse. Furry sadly passed away surrounded by the forest he had been so excited about exploring.

Once upon a time, there lived a mommy and a daddy and a little girl named Lucy.

One day, Lucy's mommy was mail-ing a letter to her friend. But when Lucy saw the mail, she wanted to mail something too. So she asked her mommy if she could mail her toy truck. Her mommy said yes and helped Lucy put the toy in the mailbox.

After a while, Mommy and Daddy had to go to the store. But before they left, Mommy put dinner in the dishwasher.

When they got back home, Mommy and Daddy noticed that the dishwasher was hurt. They opened the dishwasher and saw that Lucy's toy truck was inside. 

Dad asked Lucy why the toy truck was in the dishwasher. Lucy said she wanted to mail it by mistake. 

Mommy and Daddy hugged Lucy and said it was an honest mistake. They were very happy that the toy truck wasn't hurt. 

Then, they all ate dinner and went to bed. Lucy was so glad she still had her toy truck.

Once upon a time, there was a chubby cat named Tom. Tom had a red balloon. He loved to play with it all day. He would bat it with his paw and watch it float up and down.

One day, Tom saw a big dog named Max. Max said, "I hate balloons. They are loud and scary." Tom looked at his red balloon and thought, "I don't want Max to be scared."

So, Tom went to Max and said, "Let's play together. We can play without my balloon." Max wagged his tail and they played all day. They chased each other and had lots of fun. Tom learned that even if someone hates something you love, you can still be friends and find other ways to play.

Once upon a time, there was a train. The train had a big, white cloud coming out of it called steam. The steam was hot and made a loud noise. The train went chugga chugga chugga down the track. 

One day, the train had a great adventure. It went through tunnels and over bridges. It saw cows and sheep and even a big red tractor. But the train was getting tired. It wanted to finish its adventure and go back to its home. 

Finally, the train arrived back at the station. It was happy to be finished with its adventure. The steam stopped coming out and the train went to sleep. It dreamed of all the great things it had seen on its adventure.

Once upon a time there was a very pretty cat. She wanted to go see the sunrise so one morning she hopped up early, just before the sun came up.

The cat got to the top of the hill and she looked all around. Everything was so quiet and still. She noticed the colors of the sunrise were getting brighter and brighter. The cat began to whisper, â€œItâ€™s so beautiful!â€

Suddenly, the cat heard some scurrying in the bushes. She was very curious, so she peered through the bushes. To her surprise, she saw a dirty little mouse! The mouse was very filthy, so she thought to herself, â€œI better get away from him!â€

The cat quietly and quickly ran away from the mouse. She watched the sunrise as she ran through the grass and she was in wonder of how beautiful it was. She whispered to herself, â€œI hope I can come back here to see the sunrise again soon!â€

Once upon a time there was a tall tree. It stretched up, up, up. The tree had a big trunk and lots of branches that were thick and strong. But there was something else special about this tree.

The branches had leaves that were always open! They shined and sparkled in the sun. Sometimes it seemed like they were waving hello. Everyone was amazed and wanted to know why this tree was different from all the others, so they asked the tree what made it so special.

The tree smiled and said, "The birds have been visiting me for a long time. They stretch their wings to reach all my branches and keep the leaves open! Together we make a beautiful, open tree." Everyone was so happy and thanked the birds and the tree for being so kind.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to walk in the park with her mommy and daddy. One day, they went for a walk and saw a bright light in the sky. It was so pretty! 

After a while, they got tired and decided to sit on a bench. Lily's mommy looked in her bag and realized she forgot to bring snacks. "Oh no, my bag is empty!" she said. But then, Lily's daddy had an idea. "Let's go to the ice cream truck and get some treats!" he said. So they walked to the ice cream truck and got some yummy ice cream. 

They sat on the bench and enjoyed their treats while looking at the bright light in the sky. Lily was so happy to go for a walk with her mommy and daddy and have a yummy snack. The end.

One day, a little girl named Lily went to the gym with her mom. The gym was a big and tidy place where people went to play and have fun. Lily loved going to the gym because she could run, jump, and play with her friends.

While Lily was playing, she saw a big box in the corner of the gym. She was curious about what was inside the box. So, she went closer and decided to peek inside. When she peeked, she saw a big, bouncy ball! Lily was so happy and excited to find the ball.

Lily called her friend, Tom, and said, "Look, I found a big ball! Let's play with it!" Tom came over and they both played with the ball, bouncing it high into the air and laughing. They had so much fun at the gym that day.

Lily and Tom were playing dress-up in their room. They had many clothes and hats and shoes to try on. They liked to pretend they were different people and animals. Lily put on a red dress and a big hat. She said, "I am a queen. You have to do what I say." Tom put on a blue shirt and a tie. He said, "I am a teacher. You have to learn what I teach."

They played for a long time, but then they heard their mom call them for dinner. They had to end their game and go downstairs. They started to take off their clothes and put them back in the closet. But Lily wanted to keep her hat. She said, "This is my hat. I want to wear it for dinner." Tom said, "No, you have to put it back. It is not yours. It is mom's hat. She will be mad if you take it."

They began to fight over the hat. They pulled and tugged and shouted. The hat fell to the floor. They both reached for it, but they knocked over a hanger. The hanger hit the lamp and the lamp fell down. It made a loud noise and broke. They both stopped and looked at the mess. They were scared and sorry.

Mom heard the noise and came upstairs. She saw the broken lamp and the clothes and the hat. She was not happy. She said, "What happened here? Why did you make such a mess? Why did you fight over the hat?" Lily and Tom hung their heads. They said, "We are sorry, mom. We were playing dress-up and we did not want to end. We both liked the hat and we did not share. We did not mean to break the lamp."

Mom sighed and said, "I understand you were having fun, but you have to be careful and respectful. The hat is mine and you have to ask me before you use it. The lamp is ours and you have to be gentle with it. The clothes are yours and you have to put them away. Now, help me clean up this mess and then we can go for dinner. And no more fighting, okay?"

Lily and Tom nodded and said, "Okay, mom. We are sorry. We will help you. We will not fight." They picked up the clothes and the hat and the hanger. They helped mom sweep the glass and fix the lamp. They hugged mom and said, "We love you, mom. You are the best." Mom smiled and said, "I love you too, Lily and Tom. You are the best too. Now, let's go and eat. I made your favorite soup." They went downstairs and ate their soup. They were calm and happy. They ended their day with a good night kiss.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Daisy who loved to cook. One day, Daisy went to the kitchen. She was about to cook when she saw a rat! 

"Hello, Rat!" said Daisy. "I am going to cook something! Can you be my helper?"

But the rat was very impatient and ran away. Daisy was disappointed and said "That's ok. I can still cook by myself!"

Daisy started to look for ingredients. She saw some apples, some oranges, some carrots and some potatoes.

"This is perfect for my cooking!" she said. 

Daisy washed, chopped and cooked all the ingredients. Then, she put them in a bowl and started to stir.

But all of a sudden, she heard a noise. It was the rat! The rat came back and wanted some food. So Daisy gave the rat some of her food.

The rat was happy and said "Thank you, Daisy!"

Daisy smiled and said "You are very welcome!"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Ginny. She was a very active 3-year-old who loved to jog. One day, Ginny went for a jog but suddenly, something incredible happened. She stumbled into a portal that removed her from her home and family.

Ginny found herself in a strange and scary place. She looked around and tried to figure out how to get back home. Suddenly, she saw a big castle very far away. Ginny was brave, so she decided to jog to the castle.
