Tiny was no longer scared, she was excited about her discovery. She wanted to play more, but she was tired and it was time to go home. She waved goodbye to all her new friends in the park and ran to catch up with her mommy.

Once upon a time, there was a big race in the forest. All the animals were excited to run and see who was the fastest. The rabbit, the fox, and the bear were all there, ready to go. 

But then, the rabbit saw that his friend the turtle was sad. The turtle said he couldn't race because he was too slow. The rabbit knew that the turtle was kind and generous, so he decided to help him. 

The rabbit said, "I will carry you on my back, and we will race together. It doesn't matter who wins, because we will have fun and be happy together." The turtle was so happy and grateful that he cried tears of joy. 

In the end, the rabbit and the turtle crossed the finish line together. They didn't win the race, but they won something more important: the value of friendship and kindness.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her dolls and teddy bears. One day, Lily's mom bought her a new toy horse. Lily was very happy and wanted to play with it right away.

Lily's mom urged her to be careful with her new toy. But Lily was too excited and played with it carelessly. She accidentally dropped the toy and it broke. Lily felt sad and didn't know what to do.

Her mom saw that Lily was upset and asked her what happened. Lily displayed the broken toy and told her mom what happened. Her mom hugged her and said, "It's okay, accidents happen. Let's see if we can fix it together." And they spent the rest of the day fixing the toy horse together.

Once there was a little baby. She was very happy and loved to play in the water. Every day, she would go to the beach and splash around in the warm ocean water. The little baby would make big splashes and the water would fly in all directions. All the other children would watch with big smiles as she enjoyed herself. 

One day when the little baby went to the beach, she decided to go swimming. She swam around happily, splashing and playing and laughing. When she was done, she swam back to shore. As she got out of the water, she made one big splash that made all the other children laugh. 

The little baby laughed too and smiled. She had had so much fun and couldn't wait to go back and play in the water again the next day.

Once upon a time, in a big sky, there was a chubby bird named Jet. Jet liked to fly high and play with his friends. He was a happy bird and always had fun.

One day, Jet saw a big tree with a lot of yummy fruits. He told his friends, "I recommend this tree for our lunch!" Jet and his friends went to the tree and ate the fruits. They were very happy.

But Jet didn't know that there was a cat hiding near the tree. The cat saw Jet and his friends and wanted to catch them. When Jet saw the cat, he was scared. But he was brave and told his friends to fly away. Jet and his friends flew fast and high, and the cat could not catch them. They were safe and happy again.

Once upon a time there was a naughty boy called Marcus. He was always doing mean things. His mother was very unhappy and always gave him warnings.

One day Marcus took an egg from the cupboard and threw it on the floor. His mother was very, very angry. She told Marcus he must not do bad things, and that he would be punished if he did. Marcus was very sad. 

A few days later, Marcus did something even worse. He hit his brother and made him cry. His mother was angry and told Marcus he had to be punished for his bad behaviour. 

The next day, Marcus was in his bedroom feeling very miserable. Just then, his mother came in and said it was time for his punishment. She made him stand in the corner for 15 minutes. Marcus was very embarrassed and felt ashamed. 

From that day forward, Marcus was much more careful about how he behaved. His mother had shown him that it was important to be good and follow the rules.

Once upon a time, there were two friends. They were hungry, but they did not have any food. They wanted to get some food, but it was tough. They tried to get some food, but it kept getting prevented. 

They kept trying and trying, but it was no use. Suddenly, the friends got an idea. They quickly ran to the garden. They found some tough food and started eating it. 

The food was a bit hard to eat, but it was tasty and made them feel good. The friends were happy and went on their way. They will always remember how tough food prevented them from being hungry. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim was part of a club with his friends. They all liked to play together and have fun.

One day, they found a cheap toy in the park. It was a small, broken car. They wanted to fix it and play with it. Tim's friend Sam said, "We can trust each other to help fix the toy."

They worked together to fix the car. Tim found a wheel, and Sam found some glue. They put the wheel on the car and it was as good as new. They took turns playing with the car, and they were all very happy.

The club of friends learned that by trusting each other, they could do anything. They played with the cheap toy car every day, and it brought them lots of joy. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time there was a goat named Sam. Sam was a funny goat with a big, round head and long ears. He lived on a farm with his friends.

Every day, Sam would play near the river. One day, when Sam was at the river, he saw a big wave. It was so big and smooth! Sam loved it and wanted to see it again.

Sam thought and thought and came up with an idea. He decided to try to balance on his two hooves and see the wave again. He hopped up and down, up and down and slowly built up his balance.

Finally, after a few tries, the wave appeared from around the corner and Sam saw it! He was so excited!

"Hooray! I found it!", he said with a loud, happy voice. 

His friends heard him and came running to join Sam and his big, smooth wave. 

They all had the best time jumping, playing and balancing together next to the wave!

Mommy had two special presents to give to her three year old daughter.

The first was a dependable teddy bear. It was warm and fluffy and perfect for cuddling. The little girl hugged her bear tight and smiled.

The second present was a bit more unusual. It was an oyster! She had never seen one before and the little one was curious. Mommy told her to hold it and feel the smooth surface. Then Mommy showed her how to fold the shell open. Inside was a beautiful pearl! The little girl had never seen anything so pretty before. She was delighted.

From that time on, the teddy bear and the oyster were her two most dependable friends. She held them every day, sure they would always be there to comfort her.

Once upon a time, there lived a boy named Tom. Tom liked mint a lot. He always thought it was the best taste ever! One day, Tom was feeling very sorry. He had done something wrong, and he wanted to say sorry. He went to the shop and bought a big packet of mints.

Tom gave the mints to his friends and said he was sorry. His friends seemed happy, and they smiled at him. Even though he had done something wrong, they still wanted to be friends with him.

Tom felt much better. He knew that even if he did something wrong, he could still say sorry with mints. His friends were happy, and he was happy too.

Once there was a small rock. It was very modest. The rock grew tired of rolling around. So it decided to stop. But it could not stop itself, it needed help. So it called out for help. 

A little girl heard the rock's cry. She was playing outside in her yard. She rushed over to the rock and asked what it needed. 

The rock told the little girl it wanted to stay in one place. So the little girl moved it to a nice spot in her garden. 

The rock was happy and stayed in the spot forever. It never needed to roll around again. The little girl was very proud of her modest rock. It was great to have something stop in one place.

Sara and Ben love to play in the garden. They like to dig, water, and plant seeds. They also like to look for bugs and birds. Sometimes they pretend to be animals or fairies.

One day, they find a big, shiny stone in the garden. It is round and smooth and has many colors. Sara picks it up and says, "Look, Ben, what a pretty stone! Maybe it is magic!"

Ben takes the stone and says, "Maybe it can make us become anything we want! Let's try it!"

They close their eyes and wish very hard. Sara wishes to become a butterfly, and Ben wishes to become a lion. They open their eyes and look at each other.

But nothing has changed. They are still Sara and Ben, holding the stone. They feel sad and confused.

"Maybe the stone is broken," Sara says.

"Or maybe we need to say a magic word," Ben says.

They try different words, like "abracadabra", "please", and "banana". But nothing works.

They are about to give up, when they hear a voice.

"Hello, children. What are you doing with my stone?"

They turn around and see a lady with a big hat and a basket. She is smiling and has a mild voice.

She is the gardener. She tells them that the stone is not magic, but a special kind of rock that she found in the mountains. She says that she likes to keep it in the garden, because it makes her happy.

She also tells them that they don't need a stone to become anything they want. They can use their imagination and their creativity. She says that she likes to pretend to be a bird or a flower sometimes.

She invites them to join her in the garden, and shows them how to make crowns and necklaces with leaves and flowers. She also teaches them the names of the plants and the animals.

Sara and Ben forget about the stone. They have fun with the gardener, and learn many new things. They decide that the garden is a magical place, after all.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who lived in the town. Her name was Jane. Jane was very persistent. 

Every morning, Jane's mom would remind her to get dressed, brush her teeth and then eat breakfast. Jane always listened to her mom. 

Sometimes, Jane and her mom would go to the park, or visit a friend in the town. No matter what they did, Jane's mom would always remind her to be kind and polite. 

Jane was so happy in the town and she loved it very much. Everywhere she went, people would tell Jane that she was so persistent. 

Jane's mom was very proud of her daughter and she always thanked her for being so persistent. Jane was so happy and she felt loved.

Once upon a time, there was a little green frog that lived in the garden. Every day, it would hop and sneak to find treats like flies and worms.

One day, the frog found a pepper! It was pink, round and looked so yummy. The frog carefully took it in its tiny little hands and started to eat it.

Suddenly, it felt a burning sensation and started to jump around. It wanted to escape the pepper!

The frog jumped and hopped back to the garden and shouted, "Help me! Help me!"

Luckily, a little bird was nearby and heard the frog's cries. It pecked the pepper out of the frog's hands and said, "There, you don't have to eat it anymore!"

The frog was happy and thanked the little bird. From that day on, the frog learned to be more careful when it comes to food!

Lily likes to get stamps from her teacher. Stamps are small pictures that stick on paper. Lily has many stamps of animals, flowers and stars. She puts them in her book and shows them to her mom.

One day, Lily sees a new stamp on the teacher's desk. It is a stamp of a bunny. The bunny is white and soft. Lily loves bunnies. She wants to get the stamp of the bunny.

She asks the teacher, "Can I have the bunny stamp, please?"

The teacher smiles and says, "Yes, you can, Lily. But first, you have to do your work. You have to write your name and draw a circle."

Lily nods and does her work. She writes her name and draws a circle. She shows her work to the teacher.

The teacher says, "Good job, Lily! You did your work very well. Here is your bunny stamp."

The teacher gives Lily the stamp of the bunny. Lily is very happy. She says, "Thank you, teacher!"

She puts the stamp of the bunny in her book. She touches the stamp. It is soft. She thinks the bunny is cute. She hugs her book and smiles.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Jane. Jane loved to go on adventures and explore. One day she decided to explore the store. She was looking for something special.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Lucy. She was very small and had lots of curly hair.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play with colors. They have many colors in a box. They can make pictures with colors on paper.

One day, Lily and Ben want to make a picture for their mom. They find a big paper and some colors. They sit on the floor and start to draw.

Mom opens the door and sees them. She smiles and hugs them.

"Wow, what a beautiful picture!" she says. "You are so good with colors. I love it. Thank you, Lily and Ben."

Lily and Ben are proud and happy. They give their picture to mom. They are ready to play with colors again.

John and his mom went to the store. When they got there, John observed a lot of interesting things. One thing he noticed was a red dessert. It was in a shiny glass bowl and looked very tasty. He wanted to try it.

John asked his mom if he could have some. His mom smiled and said yes. She filled a small bowl with the red dessert and let John take it home.

When they got back, John eagerly ate the dessert. He loved it and asked for more! His mom agreed, so she prepared some for lunch the next day.

Lily was a little girl who liked to climb. She climbed on chairs, on tables, on trees, and on walls. She was not afraid of heights. She wanted to see everything from above.

One day, she climbed on a big shelf in her room. She saw many books and toys on the shelf. She wanted to play with them. She reached for a teddy bear, but she lost her balance. She fell down from the shelf and hit her head on the floor. She cried very loud.

Her mom and dad heard her cry and ran to her room. They saw her on the floor with blood on her head. They were very scared. They picked her up and took her to the car. They drove to the hospital very fast.

At the hospital, the doctor looked at her head. He said she needed an operation. He said it was not a big operation, but it would help her head heal. He gave her a mask to breathe. He said it would make her sleep.

Lily was very tired. She felt her eyes close. She dreamed of climbing on clouds and stars. She dreamed of her teddy bear. She dreamed of her mom and dad.

When she woke up, she saw her mom and dad next to her bed. They smiled and hugged her. They said she was very brave. They said the operation was over and she was fine. They gave her a new teddy bear. She liked it very much.

Lily was happy. She still liked to climb, but she was more careful. She did not climb on shelves anymore. She climbed on playgrounds and hills. She climbed with her mom and dad and her teddy bear. She climbed and had fun.

Once there was a boy called Jack. He was eager to learn everything he could, and turned his attention to designing. He grabbed a piece of paper, so he could design wonderful pictures.

Suddenly a large, enormous sheet came tumbling down from the sky. It had colourful pictures all over it and Jack was amazed.

He asked his grandfather "What is this?"

His grandfather replied "It is a magic sheet, son. Let us make something together"

Unfortunately things went wrong as the day came to an end. The sheet flew away and they couldn't find it again. They both felt sad. Grandfather said "It is gone forever. Let us find something else to do." Jack could only cry.

One day, a shy spider named Sam lived in a big tree. Sam liked to stir his web all day. He was happy to be alone and play in his tree.

One sunny day, a big bird came to the tree. The bird saw Sam and wanted to be friends. Sam was scared but the bird was nice. They played and stirred the web together.

But then, a big wind came. The wind blew the web away. Sam and the bird were sad. They could not play together anymore. The bird flew away and Sam was alone again.

Once upon a time there lived a little girl called Lily. She was three years old and loved to dance when she heard her favourite music. One day, she was dancing around her bedroom when she noticed a little bottle on her floor. She was so confused. She had never seen it before.

Suddenly, the bottle began to move. Lily was so surprised she stopped dancing and watched carefully. Out of the bottle popped a little man. He was wearing a sparkly suit and had a funny looking hat on his head.

The little man said to Lily, "Would you like to dance with me?"

Lily smiled and said, "Yes please!" So the little man and Lily began to dance. They twirled around the room and laughed and laughed.

When they finally stopped, the little man said, "Thank you for dancing with me. Goodbye and good luck." He then jumped back into the bottle and vanished.

Lily smiled and continued to dance around the room. She knew she would always remember her special dancing friend in the little bottle.

Once upon a time, there was a jolly little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and get dirty. One day, her mom said, "Lily, it's time to wash up for dinner." Lily replied, "Okay, Mommy!" 

After Lily washed her hands, she saw a newspaper on the table. She asked her mom, "What's that?" Her mom said, "It's a newspaper. It tells us what's happening in the world." 

Lily thought for a moment and then asked, "Can I read it?" Her mom smiled and said, "Sure, but you might not understand everything." Lily looked at the newspaper and saw lots of words and pictures. She didn't understand most of it, but she felt very grown-up reading it. 

Later that night, Lily told her dad about the newspaper. He said, "Wow, you're becoming quite the reader!" Lily smiled and felt very proud of herself. She went to bed that night feeling happy and excited to learn more.

Grace was a very curious 3 year old girl. One day, she suggested to her mom that they should go to the garden. Her mom agreed and they set out on their merry way. 

When they arrived at the garden, Grace was amazed. She ran around carelessly, exploring with her eyes every corner of the garden. She was so excited to see the flowers, the funny bugs and all the different colors around her. 

Her mom cautioned her to be careful as she moved around, but Grace was too eager to pay attention. She kept being careless and her mom had to keep reminding her to be careful while still letting her explore her surroundings. 

At the end of their garden Oventure, Grace was tired, but very happy. She had learned so much and was filled with wonderful stories to tell her family at dinner that night.

Once upon a time, there were two best friends who loved to play together. One day, they decided to go for a zoom. They played and laughed as they ran down the street. They had so much fun! 

But when it was time to go home, one of the friends forgot to look both ways before crossing the street. His friend yelled stop, but it was too late. Luckily, a safe driver was nearby and was able to help them cross the road safely. 

After that, the two friends made a promise to each other: They would always look both ways before crossing the street to stay safe. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sue. Sue had a favorite hanger in her room. The hanger was red and shiny. She loved to hang her pretty dresses on it. One night, it was very dark outside. Sue was scared.

She called out to her mommy, "Mommy, I am scared of the dark!" Her mommy came into the room and hugged Sue. "Do not be scared, Sue. I promise to keep you safe," said her mommy.

Sue felt better with her mommy's promise. They turned on a small light to make the room less dark. Sue and her mommy picked out a pretty dress from the red hanger. They put the dress on Sue, and she felt happy. Sue was not scared anymore.

One day, a little girl named Anna went to visit her grandma, who lived in a big house with a lovely garden. Anna loved to play with the flowers, the birds and the cat in the garden. She also liked to talk to her grandma, who was very old but very kind.

"Grandma, can I lead the cat to the pond?" Anna asked. "I want to show her the fish and the frogs."

"Of course, my dear," grandma said. "But be careful not to let her fall in the water. She might not like it."

Anna nodded and took the cat by the collar. She walked slowly and gently, so the cat would not be scared. The cat was soft and warm, and purred in Anna's arms. Anna felt happy and proud to lead the cat.

When they reached the pond, Anna sat down on a bench and put the cat on her lap. She pointed to the water and said, "Look, cat, there are fish and frogs. They are swimming and jumping. Do you see them?"

The cat looked at the water with curiosity. She saw the fish and the frogs, and also her own reflection. She tilted her head and meowed. Anna laughed and stroked the cat's fur.

"You are a good cat," Anna said. "And you are a good friend. I like to lead you to the pond. Do you like it too?"

The cat licked Anna's cheek and snuggled closer to her. Anna smiled and hugged the cat. She felt happy and loved. She and the cat stayed by the pond for a long time, watching the fish and the frogs, and listening to grandma's stories.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys all day long. One day, Timmy's mom told him it was time to go to the park. Timmy was very excited!

At the park, Timmy saw a bright red ball. He wanted to play with it, but another boy was already playing with it. Timmy asked the boy if he could play with the ball too, but the boy said no.

Timmy's mom saw what happened and said, "Timmy, it's not nice to be selfish. You should share your toys with others. Remember, it's important to be kind and make others happy too."

Timmy understood what his mom said and went to the boy with the ball. He asked the boy if he wanted to play with Timmy's toy car. The boy said yes, and they played together happily. Timmy learned that sharing is important and it made him feel good to make someone else happy.

Jill and Ben like to play in the garden. They have a big bucket and a small scale. They fill the bucket with soil and put it on the scale. They want to see how much the soil weighs.

"Look, Ben, the scale says ten!" Jill says. "That is a lot of soil!"

"Let me try!" Ben says. He takes some soil out of the bucket and puts it in his hands. He puts his hands on the scale. "Now the scale says eight. I have two soil in my hands!"

Jill and Ben laugh. They think it is fun to weigh the soil. They take turns putting soil in and out of the bucket and the scale.

But then Mom comes out of the house. She sees the mess they have made. She is not happy.

"Jill and Ben, what are you doing?" Mom says. "You have spoiled the garden! The soil belongs in the flower beds, not on the scale. And look at your clothes, they are dirty!"

Jill and Ben feel sorry. They did not mean to spoil the garden. They only wanted to play.

"Sorry, Mom," they say. "We will clean up the soil and the scale. And we will change our clothes."

Mom smiles. She knows they are good kids. She helps them clean up the garden. She tells them they can play with the soil again, but only in a sandbox. She also tells them they can weigh other things, like toys or books or fruits. She says weighing is a good way to learn about numbers and sizes.

Jill and Ben nod. They like to learn new things. They hug Mom and say thank you. They are happy to play in the garden.

Mom was very excited. She had a surprise for the family! She shouted, â€œLook everyone! I bought a new tire!â€ 

The kids ran over, eyes wide with excitement. Mom asked, â€œDo you want to go for a ride?â€

The two kids shouted, â€œYes!â€ and ran outside to the tire. Mom followed them and helped them get into the tire. 

The tire spun and spun, making the kids giggle. Mom said, â€œBe careful, donâ€™t get too excited!â€ But the kids were too busy having fun to listen. 

After a few spins, the kids were tired. They thanked Mom for the fun ride and ran inside for a snack. Mom smiled, happy to see her kids so excited.

John had a lot of money, but it wasnâ€™t reliable. He wished he had someone to help him.

One day, John went to a store and saw a nice lady. He asked her if she wanted to help him keep his money safe. The lady smiled and said yes.

John told the lady about his money, and the lady gave him a new name. She said the new name was Captain Save-A-Lot.

John thanked the lady and gave her some of his money. He was glad to have someone reliable to keep his money safe. He knew Captain Save-A-Lot would help him keep his money safe. 

From then on, whenever John had money he would always call on Captain Save-A-Lot. John was happy and his money was safe and reliable.

Once there was a mommy and daddy. They wanted to go to the store. But when they got there, it was so crazy! Everything was upside down and running around. So mommy and daddy said, "Let's go home". But then they saw something they wanted. It was a special toy car! So they got it and went back home. They thought the store was so crazy! But they were happy they got the toy car they wanted.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She was three years old and loved to play. One day, she asked her mom for some gum.

Her mom said, "No, you can't have gum!"

The little girl started to complain and said, "Please mom, I want some gum!"

But her mom said, "No, it's too stupid. Go play with your toys."

So the little girl went off to play. After a while, she started to complain again about not having any gum.

Her mom said, "Stop complaining. You can have some gum in a few minutes."

The little girl was happy and waited patiently. Finally, her mom gave her a big piece of gum. The little girl was so happy and began to chew it right away. She was glad she stopped complaining and got her gum!

Once there was a lucky boy. He was very happy and always smiled. One day his mom told him she had a special surprise for him. He was so excited! 

The boy waited eagerly for the surprise. He jumped up and down and asked his mom, "What is it?". Finally, the surprise arrived: it was a big box full of toys. The boy was so excited and very thankful. He couldn't stop smiling. 

The boy opened the box and received so many toys. He played with them all day long. He was so lucky to have received such a special surprise from his mom. He was a very happy boy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved going to the beach. One day, she went into the water and saw a jellyfish. It was hard and didn't look very friendly. Lily was scared and ran out of the water. 

But then, she saw a little boy crying because he lost his toy boat in the water. Lily knew she needed to help him. She remembered her daddy telling her that jellyfish can help people when they get stung. So, she went back into the water and caught the jellyfish with a bucket. 

She brought the jellyfish to the little boy and put it on his arm where he got stung. The jellyfish's sting made the little boy feel better. He stopped crying and thanked Lily. She felt happy that she could help someone and make a new friend. From that day on, Lily wasn't scared of jellyfish anymore.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily's mom asked her to help set the table for dinner. Lily happily agreed and went to get the plates and forks from the cabinet. 

As she was setting the table, Lily noticed that the cabinet was a pretty blue color. "Mommy, the cabinet is blue!" she exclaimed. 

Her mom smiled and said, "Yes, it is. It's one of my favorite colors." 

After they finished setting the table, Lily's dad came home from work. "Wow, the table looks great!" he said. 

Lily beamed with pride and said, "I helped set it!" 

Her parents were so proud of her and they all enjoyed a delicious dinner together. The end.

Once upon a time, in a beautiful land, there was a big rhinoceros. He was very strong and liked to help his friends. He had many friends who loved him because he was always nice and kind.

One day, the rhinoceros and his friends were playing near a big tree. They saw a small bird trying to fly, but it could not. The bird needed support to learn how to fly. The rhinoceros had an idea. He told his friends to wait and see what he would do.

The rhinoceros went to the tree and pushed it gently. The tree moved a little, and the bird could now jump from branch to branch. The bird was happy and thanked the rhinoceros for his help. The rhinoceros smiled and said, "I am always here to support my friends."

The small bird practiced flying every day. Soon, it could fly very high and fast. The bird was so happy that it sang a beautiful song for the rhinoceros and his friends. They all danced and played together, knowing that they could always count on each other for support.

Once upon a time, there were two best friends, Linda and Kate. They were excited to go to a warm summer picnic at the park.

Linda and Kate ran around in the park, playing tag and eating yummy snacks. Then they heard music playing. It was so nice that they wanted to dance.

"Let's dance!" said Linda.

Kate agreed. "Yeah, let's dance!"

So they both stood up and started twirling and swaying to the music. They were so happy that they started to laugh.

Suddenly, a voice called out from behind them.

"Hey you two, stop for a moment and listen!"

Linda and Kate stopped dancing and looked around to see who was talking. It was an old man with a guitar.

He smiled at them and said, "The music sounds much better when you listen with your ears and your hearts."

Linda and Kate nodded and listened to the old man play. Then they started to dance again, this time with more feeling and love.

The music was beautiful, and Linda and Kate were having the best time. The sun was warm and they danced until they could hardly keep their eyes open. What a wonderful day!

Once there was a small girl named Daisy. Daisy was very smart, but she also loved to play. One day, she went outside to the park with her teddy bear.

When she got to the park, Daisy ran to the swings. She loved swinging! She wanted to go higher and higher. She was going so fast that her teddy bear was scared and shouted: "Woah, slow down, Daisy!" Daisy laughed and kept swinging.

Soon, Daisy got tired and wanted to rest. She looked around and noticed a nice shelter next to the swings. It was big and had a roof and a bench. She sat down and hugged her teddy bear. They both felt better and happy in the shelter.

They stayed in the shelter until night. Daisy was so smart and brave! She had a great day swinging and being safe in the shelter.

One day, Tommy and his mum were walking in the park. Tommy was pointing at a squirrel and smiling. His mum was so happy to see him happy.

Suddenly, Tommy started to cry. His mum was worried. She asked him why he was crying.

Tommy took a deep breath and told her that he was scared of the big bird that was flying over them. 

His mum took Tommy in her arms and said,"It's ok, Tommy. It won't do anything to you. We just need to be careful". 

Then, his mum took out a small bag of oats from her pocket and held it in the air. She said, "Look, Tommy. The bird wants a snack!"

The big bird flew towards them and ate the oats from mums hand. Then, it flew away.

Tommy smiled and hugged his mum tight with a big smile. His mum said, "See, I told you you don't have to cry. Being careful is the key." 

The end.

Tommy likes to play with his toy fly. He makes it zoom and spin in the air. He pretends it is a real fly that can go anywhere. He likes to make it land on his nose and tickle him.

One day, Tommy's big sister Lily takes his toy fly. She says it is hers now and she will not give it back. She runs away with it and Tommy chases her. He is angry and sad. He wants his toy fly back.

Lily goes to her room and locks the door. She plays with the toy fly on her bed. She makes it go very fast and very high. She laughs and thinks she is clever. But then, she makes a mistake. She throws the toy fly too hard and it hits the wall. It breaks into pieces and falls on the floor. Lily is shocked and scared. She knows Tommy will be mad.

She hears Tommy knock on the door. He says, "Lily, give me back my toy fly. It is mine. You are mean." Lily does not know what to do. She feels sorry for Tommy and for the toy fly. She opens the door and says, "Tommy, I am sorry. I broke your toy fly. It was an accident. Please don't be mad at me."

Tommy sees the broken toy fly on the floor. He feels very sad. He says, "Lily, why did you do that? You ruined my toy fly. It was my favorite. How can you fix it?" Lily says, "I don't know, Tommy. Maybe we can glue it back together. Maybe we can find a new one. Maybe we can make a new one. Please forgive me, Tommy. I love you."

Tommy looks at Lily. He sees that she is sorry. He remembers that she is his sister and he loves her too. He says, "It's okay, Lily. I forgive you. I love you too. But I still miss my toy fly. Can we try to heal it?" Lily says, "Yes, Tommy. Let's try to heal it. Maybe it will fly again. Maybe it will make us happy again." They hug and smile. They pick up the pieces of the toy fly and go to find some glue. They hope they can heal it and make it fly again.

Once upon a time there was a nice man who wanted to build something special. He started to look for things he could use. He found wood, some nails and some paint. He put them together and he built a very original house. He liked his house very much and he was very happy with his work. 

After some time, he decided to make something else. This time, he wanted to build something he could eat. He gathered some tasty ingredients and he was ready to make a delicious salad. He put carrots, tomatoes, cucumbers and lettuce together and he made a very original salad. 

The man was so proud of his work that he invited some of his friends to come and try his salad. Everyone was surprised at the excellent taste of the salad and they said that the man was a very good builder. He was so pleased that he ate the salad with a big smile on his face. 

The end.

One day two young children were marching down the street. One was the older brother and the other was the younger sister. They were walking down the street in a row, when the younger sister said to her brother, "I'm tired, can we have a break?"

The older brother replied, "No, we can't. We need to keep marching. Once we reach the finish line, we can rest."

The younger sister started to cry, but the older brother kept marching. After a while, they reached the finish line and were so proud of themselves.

The older brother said to the younger sister, "You see, with hard work and determination, we can reach our goals."

The sister smiled, happy to have her brother by her side.

The moral of the story is that you can do anything you set your mind to, as long as you work hard and never give up.

Once upon a time, there was a fisherman named Tom. He liked to plan his day by the sea. One day, Tom was confused. He could not find his net to catch fish. He looked and looked, but it was gone.

Tom asked his friend, Sam. "Did you see my net?" Sam shook his head. "No, I didn't see it." Tom was sad. He could not catch fish without his net. But Sam had an idea. "Let's look together," he said.

Tom and Sam looked all around. They looked near the sea and in the sand. At last, they found the net under a big rock. Tom was so happy! Now he could catch fish again. Tom and Sam went to the sea and caught many fish together. They were the best of friends.

Once there was a little boy named Sam. He was only three years old and he was always curious and adventurous. One day, he was playing at the beach when he saw something unusual in the sand. He bent down and carefully plucked it out of the sand. It was an incredible oyster!

Sam was so excited. He had never seen an oyster before. He looked at it with amazement and wanted to see what was inside. So he slowly turned it over and opened it. Inside was a beautiful pearl!

Sam's eyes widened in surprise. He couldn't believe his luck. He ran home to show his mum the incredible pearl he had found in the oyster. When she saw the pearl, she gasped in amazement.

Mum: "Wow, Sam, that's incredible! You found this in the sand?"

Sam beamed with pride.

Sam: "Yes! I turned the oyster over and there it was!" 

Mum smiled and gave Sam a big hug. She was so proud of her little explorer. 

They both knew that this would be an amazing keepsake from this special day.

Once upon a time, there was a monkey who liked to run around. He would run and jump and play all day long. One day, he was running too fast and he fell down. He hurt his leg and couldn't run anymore. 

The monkey was sad and couldn't play with his friends. But then, a kind friend came to visit him. The friend was careful and helped the monkey feel better. She brought some food and stayed with him until he felt better. 

The monkey learned an important lesson that day. He learned that it's important to be careful when running and playing. And he also learned that having kind friends is very important. From that day on, he was more careful when he ran and played, and he always remembered to be kind to his friends.

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play outside. They loved nature and all the animals and plants they could see. Sometimes they would make up games and challenges for each other. They would dare each other to do things that were fun or scary.

One day, they saw a big tree with a hole in it. They wondered what was inside. Lily dared Ben to put his hand in the hole and see what he could feel. Ben was not afraid. He said he would do it if Lily did it too. They agreed and walked towards the tree.

But they did not know that someone else was living in the hole. It was a grumpy old owl who did not like visitors. He was sleeping when he heard the twins coming. He opened his eyes and saw two small hands reaching into his home. He was very angry and decided to teach them a lesson.

He waited until Ben's hand was close enough and then he bit it hard. Ben screamed and pulled his hand out. He saw blood and a big mark on his finger. He cried and ran to his sister. Lily was shocked and scared. She hugged Ben and said she was sorry. She did not dare to put her hand in the hole.

The owl watched them from the hole. He was satisfied and went back to sleep. He hoped they would never come back. He liked his peace and quiet. He did not like nature's games.

One morning, a girl named Grace wanted to go fast. She put her shoes on and grabbed her bike. Then she ran out of her house, ready to go! 

Grace rode her bike fast around the block. The wind blew in her hair as she smiled and laughed. She wanted to keep going faster and faster. 

Soon, she reached the end of the block and stopped. She panted and smiled. She wanted more. 

Grace rode her bike back home. She waved to her neighbors as she went by. Home at last, Grace was happy. She had gone fast and it was a great morning.

Once upon a time there was a big, empty house. A family of four used to live there but now only one person remained.

Her name was Linda. She was a happy and kind woman who kept her promise to never leave her home. Every day she sat in her chair and waited for something to happen.

One morning she heard a mysterious noise coming from outside. She looked out her window and couldn't believe her eyes. A magical creature had been standing there!

Linda asked the magical creature what it was doing there and it told her that a surprise was waiting for her. At that moment the magical creature vanished as quickly as it came.

Linda was amazed and happy. She ran out of the house to see what the magical creature had promised. To her surprise, the empty house was suddenly filled with beautiful things. Linda realized that the magical creature had kept its promise.

Once upon a time, there was a bird. The bird loved to fly high in the sky and feel the wind on its wings. One day, the bird saw a TV in a window. It was playing a show about other birds flying and soaring in the sky. The bird felt proud of its own flying skills and wanted to soar even higher. 

The bird flew up and up, flapping its wings with all its might. It felt the wind pushing against it, but it kept going. Finally, the bird reached the clouds and soared even higher. From up there, it could see the whole town and all the other birds flying below. The bird felt very proud of itself for reaching such great heights. 

As the sun began to set, the bird knew it was time to come back down. It flew back to its nest, feeling happy and content. From that day on, the bird soared higher and higher every time it flew. It never forgot the feeling of pride it had when it first saw the TV show about soaring birds.

Lily and Max are twins. They like to play in the big building where they live. One day, they want to go to the roof and see the sky. They run to the elevator and push the button.

"Wait for me!" Lily says. She slips on the floor and falls down. Her knee hurts and she cries.

Max runs back to her and helps her up. He hugs her and says, "I'm sorry, Lily. Are you okay?"

Lily nods and wipes her tears. She says, "I'm okay, Max. Thank you. Can we still go to the roof?"

Max smiles and says, "Yes, we can. Come on, the elevator is here."

They get in the elevator and push the button for the roof. The elevator goes up and up and up. They see the numbers change on the wall. They count together, "One, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten!"

The elevator stops and the door opens. They see the roof and the sky. They run outside and feel the sun and the wind. They see the birds and the clouds. They laugh and play.

They find a big jar of candy on a table. They open it and see many colors and shapes. They smell the sweet candy and their mouths water. They take some candy and eat it. They share and say, "Mmm, this is good!"

They hear a voice say, "Hello, kids. Do you like the candy?"

They turn around and see a man with a hat and a smile. He says, "I'm the janitor. I work here and I clean the roof. I brought the candy for you. I saw you playing here sometimes and I thought you would like a treat."

Lily and Max say, "Thank you, mister. You are very nice. We like the candy and the roof."

The man says, "You're welcome, kids. You can come here anytime you want. But be careful and don't slip on the floor. And don't eat too much candy or you'll get a tummy ache."

Lily and Max say, "Okay, mister. We will be careful and we won't eat too much. Bye!"

They wave to the man and go back to the elevator. They push the button for their floor. They go down and down and down. They see the numbers change on the wall. They count backwards, "Ten, nine, eight, seven, six, five, four, three, two, one!"

The elevator stops and the door opens. They see their mom waiting for them. She says, "There you are, kids. Where have you been?"

Lily and Max say, "We went to the roof and we saw the sky and we ate some candy. A nice man gave it to us. He works here and he cleans the roof."

Their mom says, "Wow, that sounds like fun. But you should tell me before you go to the roof. It can be dangerous. And you should brush your teeth after eating candy. It can make your teeth bad."

Lily and Max say, "Okay, mom. We're sorry. We will tell you next time. And we will brush our teeth. We love you, mom."

Their mom says, "I love you too, kids. Come on, let's go home."

They hug their mom and go to their apartment. They brush their teeth and wash their faces. They tell their mom about their adventure on the roof. They show her the candy they have left. They say, "This is the best day ever!"

The end.

Once upon a time, there were two boys. They were in a team and were always happy to help each other. Jimmy was always so polite. Whenever someone said hello to him, he would always smile.

One day Jimmy and his team were playing in the park. Some other kids were playing too. The kids were having a lot of fun.

Jimmy's friend Tom saw the other kids playing and wanted to join in. He walked up to them and asked if he could play. The other kids said yes and Jimmy smiled at Tom.

The other kids invited Tom to join their team. Jimmy was so happy that his friend had a new team to play with. He smiled at Tom, who politely thanked the other kids.

From then on, Jimmy and Tom always smiled at each other whenever one of them would join a new team. They knew that, no matter what, they would always have each other.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who loved to pray. One day, she went outside and saw a mysterious plant growing in her garden. She said, "This must be a special plant! What should I do?" 

The little girl thought and then said, "I should pray to find out what this plant needs."

So, the little girl folded her hands and began to pray. Suddenly, she heard a voice from the mysterious plant.

The plant said, "I need some sunshine and water, and I will grow tall and strong." 

The little girl smiled and said, "Thank you for telling me what you need. I will give you plenty of sunshine and water, so you can keep growing." 

The little girl took care of the mysterious plant and it soon became tall and strong. She was very proud and happy. The end.

Sara likes pink. She has a pink dress, a pink hat, and a pink bike. She also likes mint. She has a mint plant in her garden, and she likes to smell it and taste it.

One day, Sara sees a big pink box in her living room. She runs to it and opens it. Inside, she finds a lot of mint candy. She is very happy. She takes one and puts it in her mouth. It is sweet and cool.

"Wow, this is the best candy ever!" she says.

She takes another one, and another one, and another one. She does not stop. She does not blink. She does not hear her mom calling her for lunch.

Soon, the box is empty. Sara feels sick. Her tummy hurts. Her mouth burns. She wants to spit out the candy, but she can't. She starts to cry.

Her mom comes and sees her. She is very angry and worried.

"Sara, what have you done? You ate all the candy? Do you know how bad that is for you? You could get very sick! You are in big trouble, young lady!" she says.

She picks up Sara and takes her to the bathroom. She makes her drink water and brush her teeth. She says she will call the doctor.

Sara is very sorry. She wishes she did not eat all the candy. She wishes she listened to her mom. She wishes she did not like pink and mint so much.

Once upon a time there were two friends, a fox and a rabbit. The fox loved to play and the rabbit loved to take naps. 
One day the fox decided to build a home and asked the rabbit for help. The rabbit was tired and wanted to sleep instead. The fox insisted that the rabbit help, but the rabbit refused. 
The fox, with a careless attitude, started gathering leaves to build the home alone. But after a few minutes, the fox had made a mess and the home was falling down. 
The rabbit then insisted that the fox needed help and together they started over. This time the fox had to listen and work with care. The new home was beautiful and they were proud of their work. 
The moral of the story is that two heads are better than one. We should always listen to others and never do important things without help.

Sara and Ben liked to play in the park. They liked to dig in the sand and look for shiny things. One day, they found a big gem in the sand. It was red and sparkly.

"Wow, look at this!" Sara said. "It is so pretty!"

"Let me see!" Ben said. He grabbed the gem from Sara's hand. "It is mine!"

"No, it is mine!" Sara said. She pulled the gem back. They started to fight over the gem.

An elderly lady was walking by. She saw the children fighting. She wanted to help them. She walked over to them and said, "Hello, children. Why are you fighting?"

They stopped fighting and looked at her. She had a kind face and a long dress. She smiled at them.

"We found this gem in the sand," Sara said. "But he wants to take it from me!"

"No, she wants to take it from me!" Ben said.

The lady nodded. She said, "I see. Well, maybe I can help you. Do you know what this gem is?"

They shook their heads. They did not know.

The lady said, "This gem is very special. It is a magic gem. It can grant you one wish. But you have to share it. If you both make a wish, it will come true. But if you fight over it, it will disappear. Do you understand?"

They nodded. They did not want the gem to disappear. They wanted to make a wish.

The lady said, "Good. Now, close your eyes and hold the gem together. Think of something you really want. Then say it out loud. Ready?"

They closed their eyes and held the gem together. They thought of something they really wanted.

Sara said, "I wish I had a big dollhouse!"

Ben said, "I wish I had a fast car!"

They opened their eyes and looked around. But nothing happened. The gem did not grant their wishes. It did not even sparkle anymore. It was just a dull stone.

They looked at the lady. She was not smiling anymore. She was laughing. She had a wicked face and a black cloak. She said, "Ha ha ha! You fools! You fell for my trick! This gem is not magic. It is just a fake. I made it to lure greedy children like you. And now, I will take it back. And I will take you too. You will be my slaves in my dark castle. Come with me!"

She grabbed their hands and dragged them away. They screamed and cried. But no one heard them. No one helped them. They never saw the park or their families again. They were trapped with the evil lady forever. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play sports. He played soccer, basketball, and baseball. He was very good at all of them.

One day, Timmy's mom took him to the store to buy some new sports equipment. Timmy saw a crazy looking ball that he really wanted. He begged his mom to buy it for him, but she said they couldn't afford it.

Timmy was sad, but he remembered that he had some money saved up from doing chores. He asked his mom if he could pay for the ball himself. She agreed, and Timmy was so happy to have his new crazy ball. He played with it every day and it made him very happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim had a small pocket in his red shirt. One day, Tim put a spicy pepper in his pocket. He wanted to play a fun game with his friends.

At the park, Tim met his friends, Sam and Lily. They played on the swings and slides. Tim forgot about the spicy pepper in his pocket. He blinked as he thought of his game.

Later, Tim, Sam, and Lily were very hungry. They sat down to eat their lunch. Tim blinked and remembered the spicy pepper in his pocket. He took it out and put it in his sandwich. When he took a big bite, his mouth felt hot! Tim laughed and shared the spicy pepper with Sam and Lily. They all laughed and had a fun, spicy lunch.

One day, three year old Daisy was playing in her backyard. Suddenly, she noticed a bright blue bird perched at the top of the stairs. It chirped loudly and she smiled. 

Suddenly, the bird flew into the air and twirled around. With one graceful movement, the bird dove into the bushes. 

Daisy hopped up and ran to the top of the stairs. She peered into the bush but the bird was gone! She was a bit sad but then she heard a noise coming from the other side of the bushes.

She crept over to the other side and saw the blue bird resting in a bright pink flower. She couldn't believe how colourful it was! Clapping her hands loudly, Daisy asked the bird, "Hello, where did you go?". 

The bird chirped and flew away. Daisy watched it dive into the sky and smiled. She ran back to the stairs and waved goodbye to her new friend.

Lila and Tom were playing in the park. They saw a big statue of a man with a harp. The harp had many strings and looked shiny.

"Who is that?" Lila asked.

"That is a musician," Tom said. "He makes music with the harp. He lived a long time ago. He is ancient."

Lila and Tom wanted to touch the harp, but it was too high. They tried to climb the statue, but it was too heavy. They could not move it.

"Let's weigh the statue," Lila said. "Maybe we can find out how heavy it is."

They found a big scale near the statue. It had numbers and a needle. They pushed the statue onto the scale, but nothing happened. The needle did not move.

"The scale is broken," Tom said. "The statue is too heavy for the scale. It is heavier than a car or a bus or a house."

Lila and Tom were amazed. They wondered how the musician could play the harp if it was so heavy. They decided to make their own music with sticks and stones. They tapped and clacked and sang. They had fun. They forgot about the statue and the harp. They were happy.

Lily liked to play in her big wardrobe. She had many dresses and hats and shoes that she could try on. She felt like a princess or a fairy or a pirate. Sometimes she pretended that the wardrobe was a magic door to another world.

One day, her brother Tom came into her room. He saw Lily playing in the wardrobe and he wanted to join her. He opened the door and climbed in. He saw a coat and a scarf and a hat that he liked. He put them on and said, "Look, Lily, I'm a snowman!"

Lily was not happy. She did not like Tom taking her things. She said, "No, Tom, you are not a snowman. You are a foolish boy. You have to ask before you use my things. And you have to be careful. The wardrobe is old and it might break."

Tom did not listen to Lily. He thought she was silly and bossy. He said, "I don't care. I like the wardrobe. It is fun. And I'm not foolish. You are foolish. You are a baby."

He started to jump and dance in the wardrobe. He made a lot of noise. He knocked over some boxes and some hangers. He did not see that the wardrobe was shaking and cracking.

Lily tried to warn Tom. She said, "Tom, stop! You are making the wardrobe fall apart. You will hurt yourself and make a mess. Please, come out now!"

But Tom did not hear Lily. He was too busy having fun. He did not notice that the wardrobe was about to collapse. He did not see the door falling off and the shelves breaking and the clothes flying out.

Suddenly, there was a loud crash. The wardrobe fell down and Tom fell with it. He was buried under a pile of wood and cloth. He felt a pain in his head and his arm. He started to cry.

Lily ran to Tom. She was scared and sorry. She said, "Tom, are you okay? I'm sorry I was mean to you. I was just trying to warn you. The wardrobe was old and it was not safe."

Tom looked at Lily. He was hurt and ashamed. He said, "I'm sorry too, Lily. I was foolish and rude. I should have listened to you. You were right. The wardrobe was not fun. It was dangerous."

Lily hugged Tom. She said, "It's okay, Tom. I forgive you. Let's go and tell Mom and Dad. They will help us. And maybe they will buy us a new wardrobe. A stronger and safer one."

Tom nodded. He said, "Yes, let's go. And maybe they will buy us some ice cream too. To make us feel better."

Lily smiled. She said, "Yes, maybe they will. That would be nice."

They held hands and walked out of the room. They left behind the broken wardrobe and the scattered clothes. They learned a lesson. They learned to be careful and to listen to each other. They learned to be kind and to share. They learned to be smart and not foolish.

One day, a fast cat and a slow dog were playing in the park. The fast cat liked to lift things up and down. The slow dog liked to watch the fast cat lift things.

But then, they saw a big jail with a little bird inside. The bird was sad and wanted to go out. The fast cat and the slow dog wanted to help the little bird.

The fast cat used its strong legs to lift the jail door up. The slow dog pushed the door with all his might. Together, they opened the jail and the little bird was free. They all played happily in the park.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Jo. Jo was three years old and she loved playing in the park.

One day Jo was playing on the swings with her toy elephant. As she was swinging back and forth, she saw a little hole in the ground.

"What is that?" Jo asked herself.

She got off the swings and went to take a closer look. The hole was underground. Jo thought this was very strange.

Just then, a friendly rabbit popped out of the hole. He was wearing a tiny hat and a waistcoat, too!

"Where did you come from?" Jo asked the rabbit.

"I live underground," the rabbit replied. "I'm very confused. Can you help me?"

Jo thought for a moment. Then she smiled and said,

"Yes! I can help you. I'll put you back in your hole and you can stay underground."

So Jo picked up the rabbit, who thanked her, and carefully placed him back in the ground where he belonged.

The rabbit was very happy to be home. Jo was happy to help, too. And they both lived happily ever after. The End.

Once upon a time, there was a girl. She was very brave and wanted to explore the world. One day, she was walking in a forest when she came to a big, high sign. It said "Danger - do not go ahead!". But the brave girl decided to examine the sign and keep walking.

Soon she realised she had made a mistake, because the deeper she went into the forest, the higher the trees became. She started to feel very scared.

At last, the girl found an even bigger, higher sign. It said "Danger - do not go any further!" But this time the brave girl decided to obey the sign, and she stopped walking. 

But unfortunately, it was too late. Just then, the highest tree in the forest came tumbling down! The brave girl was crushed beneath it, and the forest was full of sadness. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a soft and fluffy deer named Bambi. Bambi loved to eat green leaves and play with his friends in the forest. One day, Bambi's friend Thumper came to visit him.

Thumper said, "Bambi, did you feel the ground tremble? I think something big is coming!"

Bambi was scared and asked, "What should we do?"

Thumper replied, "Let's hide behind those bushes over there." 

So, Bambi and Thumper hid behind the bushes and watched as a big and loud monster truck drove by. Bambi's heart was still trembling with fear, but he felt safe with his friend Thumper by his side.

One day, a little girl named Lucy went to visit her grandpa. Her grandpa was bald and had a big smile. He lived in a small house near the big aeroplane place. Lucy loved to watch the aeroplanes fly up in the sky. 

When Lucy got to her grandpa's house, she said, "Grandpa, can we go see the aeroplanes today?" Grandpa smiled and said, "Yes, Lucy. We can go see the aeroplanes, but first, we must find my big hat." Lucy helped Grandpa look for his hat, but they could not find it anywhere. 

Later, they went to the big aeroplane place without the hat. They saw a big, shiny aeroplane take off into the sky. Just then, the sun came out from behind the clouds. Lucy looked at her grandpa and saw him squinting his eyes. She remembered the hat and said, "Grandpa, you need your hat to protect your bald head from the sun." Grandpa laughed and said, "You're right, Lucy. Next time, we'll remember to find my hat before we visit the aeroplanes."

Tom and Mia are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big dog. The dog is black and has sharp teeth. The dog barks at them. Tom and Mia are scared. They think the dog is dangerous.

"Run, Mia, run!" Tom says. He holds Mia's hand and they run away from the dog. The dog chases them. Tom and Mia see a fence. They climb over the fence and hide behind a tree.

The dog cannot climb the fence. It stops and growls. Then it goes away. Tom and Mia are safe. They hug each other.

"Thank you, Tom," Mia says. "You are brave. You saved me from the dog."

Tom smiles. He feels happy. He says, "You are welcome, Mia. You are my friend. I will always help you."

They look at each other. They see some scratches on their skin. The fence hurt them when they climbed over it. They say, "Ouch!"

They go to the park bench. They find some band-aids in Tom's backpack. They put the band-aids on their skin. They feel better.

They decide to go home. They hold hands and walk together. They are careful. They do not want to see the dog again. They are glad they have each other. They are good friends.

Once there was a pink mouse. The mouse wanted to find a place to fit in. Everywhere the mouse looked was very different. The mouse was sad and wanted to escape. 

One day, the mouse saw some other little animals. They were also pink like the mouse and playing together. The mouse felt happy and the animals welcomed it. 

When the mouse tried to fit in, it was different. But the other animals liked the way the mouse was different. So the mouse stayed with them and began to play with the other animals.

The mouse had found a place where it could fit it and did not need to escape. The mouse was happy and the other animals were happy too. They all lived happily together as friends.

Once upon a time there was a little boat. It liked to pass the harbor. Every day it sailed by, looking out for its friends.

One day it noticed something unusual. Another boat was in the harbor. It was a bigger boat and it was very restless. The little boat was worried.

Suddenly the little boat had an idea! It went closer to the harbor and waved hello to the bigger boat. The bigger boat looked surprised and waved back. The two boats started to have a chat.

The bigger boat was going on a long journey and it was feeling lonely. The little boat was happy to help and offered to pass by the harbor every day to keep the bigger boat company. The bigger boat accepted the offer and was very happy.

The two boats became good friends and looked forward to seeing each other every day while they both passed the harbor. They were very content with the arrangement.

Jenny was pushing her toy truck outside. She loved pushing it and listening to the rumbling engine noise it made. Suddenly, she saw a really big structure. It was a tall, ready fort made by her daddy! Jenny was so excited that she ran up to it. She began pushing it with all her might. Push, push, push! The structure began to move ever so slightly. It was so fun. Jenny kept pushing until it looked the way she wanted it. When it was all done, Jenny was ready to play inside her fort! She thought about how she pushed it until it was just perfect for her.

Once upon a time, there was a baby. The baby slept in a crib. One day, the baby woke up and started to cry. The baby's mom came in and picked up the baby. The baby was feeling lazy and didn't want to play. Mom tried to make the baby happy with some toys, but the baby just wanted to sleep. Finally, the baby fell asleep and mom put the baby back in the crib. The baby slept for a long time and woke up feeling better.

Ben and Lily liked to help Mom in the kitchen. They wanted to be good cooks like her. Mom let them stir the soup, cut the bread, and set the table. She said they were her little helpers.

When the soup was ready, Mom told Ben and Lily to serve it to Dad and Sam, their big brother. Ben took a big pot and a ladle. Lily took four bowls and four spoons. They walked carefully to the dining room, where Dad and Sam were waiting.

"Here is your soup, Dad and Sam," Ben said. "We helped Mom make it. It is very yummy."

"Thank you, Ben and Lily," Dad said. "You are very kind. The soup smells good."

Lily put a bowl and a spoon in front of Dad and Sam. Ben poured some soup into each bowl. He tried not to spill any. He was very proud.

They all sat down and ate the soup. They said it was delicious. Mom came with the bread and butter. She smiled and said they did a great job.

After they finished, Mom asked Ben and Lily to help her with the dishes. They said yes. They took the bowls and spoons to the kitchen. Mom showed them how to put them in the dishwasher. She said the dishwasher was a machine that washed the dishes for them. She said it was very handy.

Ben and Lily liked the dishwasher. They thought it was fun to push the buttons and hear the water. They wanted to see how it worked. Mom said they could watch, but they had to be careful.

They watched the dishwasher for a while. They saw the water spray and the soap bubbles. They heard the noise and the steam. They asked Mom many questions. She answered them and explained.

When the dishwasher was done, Mom opened it. She took out the dishes and dried them. She asked Ben and Lily to help her put them away. They said yes. They followed her and put the dishes in the right places.

They finished the dishes. Mom hugged them and said they were very helpful. She said she was proud of them. She said they could have a treat.

Ben and Lily were happy. They liked to help Mom in the kitchen. They liked to serve soup and use the dishwasher. They said they wanted to do it again. Mom said that was fine. She said they were good cooks. She gave them a cookie and a glass of milk. They said thank you and ate their treat. They said it was yummy. They smiled and hugged Mom. They loved her.

There was a scared dog called Jack. He was lost and couldn't find his way home. He started to cry and everyone in the town heard him. 

A young boy named Tom heard him and ran to help him. When Tom found Jack, he was scared and didn't want to move. Tom talked to him softly and sang him a poem. Jack liked the poem and it made him feel better.

Tom said he wanted to take Jack home. Jack was still scared and didn't want to go. Then, Tom asked Jack if he wanted to go with him, just for a little while. Jack agreed and Tom held his paw.

Tom and Jack started walking to Tom's home. Suddenly, Jack saw a big pond in front of them. He remembered the stories his parents had told him before about the big pond. He was very scared and started to pull away from Tom. 

Tom held on tight and jumped into the pond. He saved Jack from falling in. Jack was so happy and thanked Tom for keeping him safe. 

Tom and Jack walked away, holding paws, and they lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a penguin named Pete. Pete loved to travel to new places. One day, he decided to go to the North Pole. It was very icy there, but Pete had a warm coat. 

As he was walking, he found a handle on the ground. It was a shiny handle that sparkled in the sun. Pete picked it up and carried it with him on his journey. 

After a while, Pete met some other penguins who were lost. They didn't know how to get back home. Pete used the handle to dig a path through the snow and they all followed him. They were very happy to have found their way home. 

From that day on, Pete always carried the handle with him on his travels. It helped him and others when they needed it. Pete was a happy penguin who loved to explore new places and help his friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One night, she had a bad dream called a nightmare. She woke up feeling scared and uncomfortable. 

Lily went to her mom's room and said, "Mommy, I had a bad dream. It was scary." 

Her mom hugged her and said, "It's okay, Lily. What happened in your dream?" 

Lily said, "I was in a dark forest and I heard a loud noise. It was a bell ringing." 

Her mom said, "That's just a bell ringing in your dream. It's not real. You don't have to be scared." 

Lily felt better and went back to sleep. From that night on, she knew that even if she had a nightmare, she could always talk to her mom about it.

Billy was playing in the garden. He was making a big sandbox with a toy shovel. Suddenly, he saw a big, scary dinosaur! It was very big and had a lot of sharp teeth. Thankfully, the dinosaur was lazy and it didn't chase Billy. But it began to try and eat some of his toys! Billy tried to fight back, but the dinosaur was too strong. He crossed his arms and said, "No! I won't let you eat my toys!" He started to resist the dinosaur. He shouted and stomped his feet, but the dinosaur wasn't scared. Suddenly, his mom came outside and started to yell at the dinosaur. She scared it away and it ran away. Billy was so happy that he had someone to help him resist the dinosaur.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Joe. He was walking through a forest when he came across a rare wet bird. Joe wanted to keep the wet bird as a pet and so he reached out to grab it. But before he could, the bird flew away. Joe was sad, but he knew he needed to keep walking to get home. 

Suddenly, Joe heard an unexpected sound. He looked around and saw the wet bird had returned. He was so excited and wanted to take the wet bird home with him. 

"No", said a voice from behind the trees. Joe looked around and saw an old man standing there. The old man said, "That bird belongs in this forest. He is a very rare bird and must stay here." Joe was sad and argued with the old man. He pleaded with him to let him keep the bird, but the old man refused. Joe sadly had to return back home without the wet bird.

Once there was a little girl who had a doll on her porch. The girl loved her doll and hugged it every day. One day, the little girl wanted to sort her dolls so she put them on the porch. She put all the red dolls in one pile and all the blue dolls in another.

The fierce wind came and blew the dolls away. The little girl ran around trying to sort the dolls and put them in piles but the wind kept blowing them away. She started to cry, because she could not sort the dolls.

Suddenly, a fairy appeared. She waved her wand and said a magical spell. She waved her wand again and the wind stopped blowing. The little girl was so happy and started to sort her dolls again. She finished sorting the dolls and put them back on the porch. She was so glad the fairy had helped her sort her dolls.

Once there was a little boy who really wanted to play. He had all the toys he wanted, but he was getting bored. He decided to take a walk. 

As he walked, he came across a big, brick wall with a door. He was curious, so he opened it. Inside he found a cozy room with a comfy chair and some books. He sat in the chair and started to read.

He became so comfortable that he forgot about his walk. But then he noticed something strange. There was no exit! He tried to open the door he had come in, but it wouldn't budge. 

He started to worry. He didn't know how to get out. He shouted, "Help! I'm stuck!"

Moments later, his mom heard him and ran to his side. She said, "Don't worry, I'm here now. I'll help you find an exit." She opened the door and together they walked out. 

The little boy was relieved and hugged his mom. He said, "Thanks for helping me. I'm so glad to have you!"

Once upon a time, there was a little boy. He was looking for something to pick. He saw a jet in the deep sky. The little boy wanted to pick the jet. He felt so happy.

He jumped up and grabbed the jet. He started to fly around in the sky. The little boy was so excited. He made big deep circles in the sky.

Suddenly, the little boy heard a loud noise. He looked down and saw a big truck. The truck was so big and strong. The truck had to pick up the jet.

The little boy was sad that he had to let go of the jet. He waved goodbye as the truck drove away with the jet in the back. The little boy watched until he couldn't see the jet anymore.

The little boy was sad, but he knew the jet would be happy with the truck. He smiled and went back home. He had a wonderful time and would never forget it!

Once upon a time, there was a little fox named Fred. Fred was very important to his family because he was the best at hide and seek. One day, Fred was playing hide and seek with his siblings. He found a really good hiding spot behind a big tree. 

As Fred was hiding, he heard a little girl walking nearby. She was carrying a basket of apples. Fred thought the apples looked tasty, so he jumped out of his hiding spot and ran towards the girl. 

The girl saw Fred and got scared. She dropped her basket and ran away. Fred felt bad for scaring the girl, so he decided to return the basket to her. He found her crying in a nearby field. 

Fred approached the girl and said, "I'm sorry I scared you. Here's your basket back." The girl was surprised that Fred could talk. She smiled and said, "Thank you, little fox. You're very important too." From that day on, Fred and the little girl became good friends and played hide and seek together.

Jim was sad. He wanted to play with his friends but they had all gone. Jim thought of a plan - he would make a promise. He would put the promise in a box and save it for his friends when they returned. 

He all made the promise. He put it in the box and locked it. He hoped his friends would remember it when they came back. 

But soon after that bad things started happening. The box got bigger and bigger, and soon it was bigger than Jim. He couldn't open it because it had grown so big. 

One day the box began to shake and rumble. Jim knew it was too late, he had made the wrong promise. It was a sad ending.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Alice. She was three years old and very happy. 

One day Alice went to the garden with her mom. When they got there, Alice saw a butterfly fluttering across the grass. She started running after it, her arms outstretched. 

Mom shouted, "Alice, stop!" But it was no use. Alice couldn't catch the butterfly and she got more and more troubled. 

Finally, mom said, "Let's take a break. Let's sit in the garden and have a snack. "

Alice and her mom ate some snacks in the garden. When they were done, Alice was no longer troubled. She and her mom hugged and they enjoyed the garden together.

Once upon a time, in a wild garden, there lived a little ant named Andy. Andy was a hard worker and loved to serve his ant friends. Every day, he would help them find yummy food.

One sunny day, Andy met a big bee named Betty. "Hi, I am Andy," said the ant. "I like to serve my friends. Can I help you find some food?" Betty the bee smiled and said, "Yes, please! I am hungry."

Andy and Betty looked around the wild garden. They found tasty flowers for Betty and sweet crumbs for Andy. They became good friends and loved to play together. From that day on, Andy and Betty always helped each other and served their friends in the wild garden. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once there was a little girl named Tess. Tess was three years old and loved playing with her friends. One day they decided to play hockey outside. Tess was excited to play and grabbed her stick. 

As they started playing, Tess noticed that her friends were ignoring her. She didn't understand why and felt very sad. She tried to talk to them, but they just continued to ignore her. Tess felt a bit teary. 

Fortunately, Tess's mum saw what was happening. She came out of the house, gave Tess a big hug and said, "Don't worry Tess, let's play a mild game of hockey together". 

Tess smiled, and felt better. She and her mum played together in the mild sunshine and soon Tess's friends were playing with them too. Tess had a wonderful time, and from then on her friends were much nicer.

John was a little boy who loved to go fast. One day, he and his mom went for a drive. John saw a cable stretched across the road. He asked what it was, and Mom said it was a "speed bump". 

Mom said they would have to slow down to go over the speed bump. Then she asked John if he wanted to go faster. John smiled, so Mom went faster.

But then John noticed the cable was weak. He shouted, "Mom, slow down!" Mom noticed the cable too, and quickly put on the brakes. The car stopped just in time, right before it reached the cable. 

John was relieved that Mom had slowed down in time. She winked at him and said, "See, it pays to pay attention." Then they continued on their drive, slowly this time.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a big car. The car was very sleepy. It was so sleepy that it could not go fast. The car wanted to wake up and go fast like the other cars.

One day, a little boy named Tim came to the car. Tim wanted to help the sleepy car. He knew that cars need fuel to go fast. Tim asked his mom for some fuel. Mom gave Tim a can of fuel.

Tim took the can of fuel to the sleepy car. He touched the car and poured the fuel in. The car woke up and was very happy. Now, the car could go fast like the other cars. The car thanked Tim for his help, and they became the best of friends.

Tom and Lily are playing in the park. They like to slide, swing and run. They are having fun. But then, Tom sees a big dog. The dog is brown and has a long tail. Tom likes dogs. He runs to the dog and says, "Hello, dog. Can I pet you?"

The dog is friendly. He wags his tail and licks Tom's face. Tom laughs and pets the dog's ear. The ear is dry and soft. Tom says, "Your ear is dry, dog. Do you need water?"

Lily sees Tom and the dog. She is scared of dogs. She thinks they are loud and mean. She calls Tom and says, "Tom, come back. The dog might bite you."

Tom says, "No, Lily. The dog is nice. He likes me. Look, he lets me touch his ear."

Lily says, "But Tom, we have to return. Mom said we have to be home soon. It is getting dark."

Tom says, "Okay, Lily. I will return. But can I say goodbye to the dog first?"

Lily says, "Yes, Tom. But hurry up."

Tom hugs the dog and says, "Bye, dog. You are a good dog. I hope I see you again."

The dog barks and wags his tail. He is happy. He likes Tom too.

Tom and Lily run back to their mom. She is waiting for them at the gate. She says, "There you are. Did you have fun?"

Tom and Lily nod and smile. They tell their mom about the dog. She says, "That sounds nice. But next time, be careful. Not all dogs are friendly. And always ask the owner before you pet a dog."

Tom and Lily say, "Okay, mom. We will."

They go home and have dinner. They are tired and happy. They dream of the dog and his dry ear.

Ben likes to play with his blocks. He can make many things with them. He can make a house, a car, a tower, or a train. He likes to add more blocks to make his things bigger and better.

One day, he finds a frog in his yard. The frog is green and wet and fast. It hops and jumps and croaks. Ben thinks the frog is fun. He wants to play with it. He tries to catch the frog, but the frog is too fast for him.

Ben has an idea. He runs to his room and gets his blocks. He makes a big wall with them. He leaves a small hole in the wall. He puts some water and some bugs near the hole. He hopes the frog will come and see.

He goes back to the yard and looks for the frog. He sees it near a flower. He sneaks up behind it and grabs it. He is happy. He runs to his wall and puts the frog inside. He thinks the frog will like his new home.

But the frog does not like it. It does not want to stay in the wall. It wants to be free. It sees the hole and jumps through it. It hops and jumps and croaks away. Ben is sad. He looks at his wall and sees the frog is gone. He wishes he could play with the frog again. He learns that some things are better to watch than to catch.

Once there was a gentle little girl. She loved to explore and find new things. One day, she found a temple. She thought the temple was so beautiful, so she went inside.

But as soon as she stepped inside, she noticed something strange. Everyone was so quiet and still. The little girl quickly realized that no one liked the temple. They all hated it.
