Lily nodded and kept walking with her mom. She looked at the sky and the trees and the flowers. She saw many things, but no rainbow. She felt a little sad, but she did not give up. She said to herself, "I will see a rainbow today. I will, I will, I will."

Suddenly, she felt a drop of water on her nose. Then another, and another. It started to rain. Lily and her mom ran to a big tree to stay dry. Lily looked at the sky and saw that the sun was still shining. She thought, "Maybe this is my chance. Maybe there is a rainbow now."

She looked around and saw something bright and colorful in the air. It was a rainbow! It was big and beautiful and had all the colors she liked. She was so happy and excited. She pointed at the rainbow and said, "Mom, look! A rainbow! A rainbow! I see a rainbow!"

Her mom looked and saw the rainbow too. She hugged Lily and said, "You did it, Lily. You found a rainbow. You are a lucky girl. And you have a big dream."

Lily smiled and said, "Yes, mom. I have a big dream. And I love rainbows. They are not terrible. They are wonderful."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to hear stories from her grandma. One day, her grandma told her an incredible story about a little bird who refused to fly. The little bird was scared to fly because he thought he would fall.

Lily listened carefully to the story and thought it was amazing. But then she asked her grandma, "Why did the little bird refuse to fly?" Her grandma explained that sometimes we are scared to try new things, but if we don't try, we will never know what we are capable of.

Lily thought about this and decided to be brave like the little bird in the story. She refused to be scared and tried new things. She learned that sometimes it's scary at first, but the more she tried, the easier it became. And that's how Lily learned to be brave and never refuse to try new things. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play with her toys. She had a special teddy bear that she adored and took everywhere with her. One day, Lily's mom told her they were going to a meeting with some other moms and their children. Lily was excited to play with other kids, but she didn't want to leave her teddy bear behind.

Before they left, Lily's mom asked her to weigh her teddy bear on a scale. Lily didn't understand why, but she did it anyway. At the meeting, Lily had a lot of fun playing with the other kids. They played games and sang songs. But then, Lily's mom asked her to weigh her teddy bear again. This time, Lily understood why. Her teddy bear had lost weight! 

Lily's mom explained that they had a surprise for her. They had taken her teddy bear to the teddy bear hospital to get him fixed. Lily was so happy and hugged her teddy bear tightly. From that day on, Lily made sure to weigh her teddy bear regularly to make sure he stayed healthy and happy.

Once upon a time, there were two best friends, Jane and Sara. One day, they decided to come to the beach. Jane was excited to go, but Sara was feeling a bit sad.

When they arrived at the beach, they saw an ice-cream stand.

"Let's get an ice-cream!" Jane exclaimed.

"No, I don't feel like it," Sara said sadly.

"Come on, it'll make you feel better," Jane encouraged.

Sara reluctantly agreed, and they bought a strawberry ice-cream. But when she took a bite, her face made a funny expression.

"What's wrong Sara?" Jane asked.

"It's bitter," Sara replied. 

Jane hugged her. "Don't worry, I'll get you another one," she said.

So Jane got Sara her favorite chocolate ice-cream, and Sara was all smiles again. 

The two friends enjoyed their ice-creams at the beach until the sun went down. They waved goodbye as they came back home.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who had a big wish. She wanted to explore the ocean. She jumped up and down, and asked her mom if they could go. Her mom said yes, so they got onto a boat and sailed away.

It was a very big ocean - bigger than the little girl had ever seen. She started to explore, and found lots of hidden treasures in the waves. She even found a starfish! Suddenly, a big fish started to tease her. It splashed around in the water and laughed.

The little girl tried to get away from the big fish, so she dived deeper into the water. But the big fish followed her - it was having too much fun! Eventually, the little girl got so tired that she swam back to the boat and fell asleep. In the morning, she was already dreaming of her next adventure in the big, hidden ocean.

One day in the river, an otter named Jack was swimming. As he looked around, he noticed a wide beach. Wanting to explore further, Jack began to swim towards it.

As he got closer to the beach, something strange happened. He felt an urge to explore it. Jack swam closer and closer and soon found himself on the beach. He was amazed to see how wide it was.

As he looked around, another otter appeared. "Hi Jack, why are you here?" the otter asked. 

Jack replied, "I felt an urge to explore this wide beach. What about you?" 

The otter said, "I felt the same urge. We should explore this beach together!"

Jack and the other otter had a great time exploring the beach and finding new things. They were both very happy that they had followed their urge.

Once upon a time there was a red vehicle. It was a bright, shiny car. It went fast and made funny noises.

The car belonged to a kind old man. Every day he drove the car around town bringing smiles to the children. He would wave and say hello. The children loved the car and its old driver.

One day the old man had a very special mission. He drove in the red car for a long time and eventually stopped at a big field. The old man got out of the car and shouted, â€œI demand that you come out!â€

The children were confused as to what was happening. Suddenly, out of the tall grass emerged a great, white elephant! The children were amazed. The old man had used the red car to find the elephant. He smiled and said, â€œYou are safe now.â€ 

The old man had used the red car to bring the elephant back to its home and save it from danger. The children thanked him for being so kind and brave. They waved goodbye as the old man and the elephant drove away in the red car.

Sam was a little boy. One day, he went for a walk in the park. Suddenly, he saw something he had never seen before. It was a big, unknown machine. He wanted to find out more about it, so he walked closer.

When he arrived, he met a friendly pilot. The pilot told him she flew the machine. She was very happy to show Sam around the inside of the machine.

Sam enjoyed his time with the pilot. She showed him all the buttons and switches. She talked to him about all the things the machine could do. Sam was very excited and asked lots of questions.

When it was time to leave, the pilot smiled and said goodbye. Sam thanked her and told her that he had enjoyed meeting her. As he walked away, he looked back at the unknown machine and waved goodbye.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy called Sam. He was three years old, and he loved to explore. 

One day, Sam went for a walk in the woods. He came to a lovely tunnel and he wanted to go inside. He searched and searched, but couldn't find an entrance. 

Just then, a friendly rabbit hopped up to him. 

"Hello!" said the rabbit. "Can I help you?" 

Sam was very excited. "Yes please!" he said. "I want to go in this tunnel." 

The rabbit smiled. "I know a way in!" it said cheerfully. "Follow me!" 

The rabbit led Sam through the woods, until soon, the two of them were standing in front of a small door in the side of the tunnel. 

Sam was delighted. He opened the door, and thanked the rabbit.

The rabbit waved goodbye, and Sam stepped inside the tunnel. He was amazed by what he found - there were all sorts of things to explore! So Sam spent the rest of the day searching around, and having a lovely time.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy who loved to play with his toy gun. He would pretend to shoot at birds and animals in the park.

One day, Timmy saw a big black bird with shiny feathers. "Wow, a raven!" he said. He aimed his gun and pretended to shoot, but the raven didn't fly away. It was a fake raven, just a statue.

Suddenly, a real raven appeared and sat on a tree branch. "Hello, little boy," said the raven. "Why do you shoot at fake birds?"

"I don't know," said Timmy. "It's just fun."

"That's not very nice," said the raven. "You shouldn't shoot at anything, even if it's fake. One day, you might hurt someone."

Timmy felt bad and put his toy gun away. But when he got home, he found his dad's real gun and started playing with it. He didn't know it was loaded. He accidentally shot himself and died. The raven watched from the tree, sad that Timmy didn't listen to his advice.

Sam and Jane were best friends, who always had fun together. One day, they decided to have a picnic in the park. As they unpacked their food, they could not agree on what to use on their sandwiches.

"Let's use butter," said Jane.

"No," said Sam, "I want to use oil."

Jane thought that oil was too messy and argued, "No, butter is better!"

Sam disagreed. He thought oil was fair because it tasted delicious and was healthy too. In the end, they reached a compromise and used both butter and oil on their sandwiches.

So the two best friends had a very yummy picnic with their fair sandwich spread. They laughed and smiled, happy to disagree and still remain good friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little bug. It was tiny, with big eyes. It scurried around, jumping from leaf to leaf. Suddenly, it noticed something. It was a small girl, staring at it from far away. She was only three years old, with big eyes and a curious look.

The bug and the little girl stared at each other for a while. The bug was so small, and the girl so big. It wondered what she was thinking. Then the girl smiled and pointed her finger at the bug. It felt safe and happy.

The little girl slowly reached out her hand. She wanted to touch the bug. The bug stayed still, and the girl touched it gently. She was so gentle. Then she suddenly stood up and walked away. The little bug watched her go until she disappeared behind the trees. It was sad to see her go, but it also knew they would meet again someday.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Jenna. Jenna was a very enthusiastic person and wanted to have lots of fun.

One day, Jenna was out for a walk in the park when suddenly she heard police sirens. "What could that be?" thought Jenna. She rushed to find out what was happening.

When Jenna got there, she saw lots of police officers running around. She was so excited and went over to talk to one of them.

"Officer, what's going on?" she said.

"There's been a robbery, miss," replied the officer.

Jenna was very excited. She thanked the officer and rushed off to tell her friends and family. She ran around telling everyone what had happened and her enthusiasm was infectious. Soon, everyone was talking about it! 

The police were able to catch the robber and Jenna was happy that justice had been served. 

That was the exciting story of Jenna and the police!

Lily liked to create things with her toys. She had many blocks, dolls, cars and animals. She made houses, roads, farms and stories with them. She had a lot of fun playing by herself.

One day, she heard a loud noise outside. She looked out the window and saw a big truck. The truck was carrying a lot of boxes. The truck driver was trying to park, but he hit a tree. The boxes fell off the truck and blocked the road. The truck driver was sad and angry.

Lily wanted to help. She grabbed her hero doll, who wore a cape and a mask. She ran outside with her doll. She said to the truck driver, "Don't worry, my hero will help you!" She put her doll on the ground and pretended that he was flying. She moved him around the boxes and made him lift them with his super strength. She made sounds like "Whoosh!" and "Zap!" and "Hooray!"

The truck driver saw Lily and her doll. He smiled and laughed. He said, "Thank you, little girl. You and your hero are very useful. You cleared the road for me. You are very kind and brave." He gave Lily a hug and a box. He said, "This is a gift for you. It has something special inside. I hope you like it." He got back in his truck and drove away.

Lily was happy. She ran back to her house with her doll and her box. She opened the box and saw a beautiful book. It had pictures and words about different heroes and their adventures. She said to her doll, "Look, we have a new book. We can create more stories with it. You are the best hero ever!" She hugged her doll and started to read. She felt proud and excited.

Once there was a big, hairy teddy bear named Ben. He was cozy and cuddly and his fur was made from velvet. His best friend was a little girl named Lulu. 

The two friends liked to play together. One day, Lulu decided she wanted to show Ben how to do a bow. She tried to show him the way to make the bow, but it took a few tries before he finally got it!

Lulu said, â€œA-ha! Youâ€™re a good learner! Goodness, Ben, you look so cute when you bow!â€ Ben was so pleased that he bowed even lower than before. He was so proud of himself, and Lulu too!

The two friends were so happy, they hugged and laughed. Lulu smiled so big that you could see all her teeth! From then on, Ben and Lulu practiced the bow every day. They even bowed to each other at the end of each day, as a way of saying goodbye.

Once upon a time there were two pets, a kitten and a puppy. They lived together and enjoyed playing and cuddling. Every night, the kitten would give the puppy a massage to make her feel happy and relaxed. One day, the puppy refused the massage. The kitten was very sad and asked why. The puppy explained that she had been feeling "rude" lately. No matter how hard the kitten pleaded, the puppy would not change her mind. 

At the end of the night, the puppy changed her mind and let the kitten massage her. The puppy felt better afterwards and the kitten was happy too. 

This story shows that sometimes it's important to think twice before refusing a kindness. Being friendly and kind to others can make everyone happier!

Mummy and Daddy were picking flowers in the garden. Mummy picked a red daisy, Daddy picked a purple thistle and the little girl picked a beautiful lily. The lily was her favorite because it was so fluffy and white and the aroma was heavenly. 

Daddy said, "Let's bring this lily inside and put it on the windowsill." 

Mummy said, "How about we make it a surprise?" 

So the family all went inside and the little girl put the lily on the windowsill. 

When she stepped back to admire her work, she noticed a bright yellow butterfly that had landed on the lily. The little girl smiled. 

Mummy said, "Oh my, that lily looks so warm and cozy with the butterfly on top."

The little girl nodded, delighted with her surprise. And, from that day on, the warm lily became a happy reminder of the special family day.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys and run around outside. One day, Timmy was playing with his toy truck when he heard his mom calling him for dinner. 

Timmy ran inside and sat down at the table with his family. His mom had made spaghetti, Timmy's favorite. As Timmy was eating, he accidentally spilled some sauce on his shirt. 

Timmy's older sister, Sarah, started to laugh and said, "Ha ha, Timmy, you look silly with sauce on your shirt!" Timmy felt embarrassed and didn't want to eat anymore. 

His mom saw that Timmy was upset and said, "It's okay, Timmy. It's just a mild stain. We can wash it out." Timmy felt better and finished his dinner. 

After dinner, Timmy's mom sat him down and said, "Timmy, it's not nice to laugh at someone when they make a mistake. We should always be kind to others." Timmy nodded his head and promised to be kind to others from now on.

Lily and Sam were playing with their dolls. They had a tea party with cups and plates and cookies. Lily poured some tea for Sam and said, "Here you go, Sam. Drink your tea. It is yummy."

Sam took a sip and made a face. He said, "No, Lily. I don't like this tea. It is cold and bitter. I want juice."

Lily was angry. She said, "Sam, you are rude. This is my tea set. You have to drink the tea. It is not cold. It is warm. And it is not bitter. It is sweet. You are a bad guest."

Sam was angry too. He said, "Lily, you are bossy. This is our game. I can drink what I want. You are a bad host."

They started to argue and shout. They pushed each other and knocked over the tea set. The cups and plates and cookies fell on the floor. They made a big mess.

Mom heard the noise and came to see what was wrong. She saw Lily and Sam and the tea set. She was not happy. She said, "Lily and Sam, what are you doing? Why are you fighting? Why did you break the tea set?"

Lily and Sam stopped fighting. They felt sorry. They said, "Mom, we are sorry. We were playing tea party. But we didn't like the tea. And we quit the game. And we made a mess."

Mom said, "Lily and Sam, I understand. But you have to be nice to each other. You have to share and take turns. You have to respect each other's choices. And you have to clean up your mess. Do you understand?"

Lily and Sam nodded. They said, "Yes, Mom. We understand. We are sorry. We will be nice. We will share and take turns. We will respect each other's choices. And we will clean up our mess."

Mom smiled. She said, "That's good. I'm glad you learned your lesson. Now, how about some real juice and cookies for a snack?"

Lily and Sam smiled too. They said, "Yes, Mom. Thank you, Mom. We love you, Mom."

They hugged Mom and helped her clean up the tea set. Then they had some juice and cookies and played nicely together. They forgot about the cold and bitter tea. They were happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little worm named Wiggly. Wiggly was a very happy worm. He lived in a big garden with lots of delicious food to eat. Every day, Wiggly would wiggle around the garden, looking for yummy things to munch on.

One day, Wiggly met a new friend, a tiny bug named Buggy. "Hello, I am Wiggly," said the little worm. "Hi, I am Buggy," said the tiny bug. Wiggly and Buggy decided to play together in the garden. They had so much fun playing hide and seek, and laughing all day.

As the sun started to set, Wiggly and Buggy got very tired. They decided to settle down and rest under a big, green leaf. As they lay there, Wiggly said, "Buggy, today was so much fun! I am so happy we are friends." Buggy smiled and said, "Me too, Wiggly! Let's play again tomorrow." And so, the little worm and the tiny bug closed their eyes and went to sleep, dreaming of more fun days together in the big, beautiful garden.

Once upon a time, there was a little bear named Teddy. Teddy loved to play in the forest with his friends, the rabbits and the squirrels. One day, they went on an adventure and found an incredible tree with lots of yummy berries. But then, they saw a big, scary wolf. The wolf wanted to eat them all up! 

Teddy had an idea. He climbed up the incredible tree and grabbed a big stick. He hit the wolf on the head with the stick, and the wolf ran away. Teddy and his friends were safe! 

But then, they heard a loud noise. It was the sound of a big truck coming to cut down the incredible tree. Teddy and his friends knew they had to do something to save their home. They all worked together to stop the truck and protect the tree. 

In the end, the tree was saved and Teddy and his friends were very happy. They knew that they could always count on each other to solve any problem that came their way.

Once upon a time, there was a light bunny who lived in a green forest. The bunny liked to hop and play all day. But one day, the green forest started to lose its color.

The light bunny wanted to restore the green color to the forest. So, the bunny asked his friends, the birds and the squirrels, to help him. They all tried to find a way to make the forest green again.

But no matter what they did, they could not restore the green to the forest. The light bunny and his friends were very sad. The forest stayed not green, and they could not play in it anymore.

Alice was walking through the park when she saw a red ashtray lying on the ground. She wondered why it was there, so she asked her mom. Her mom said that she didn't know. Alice decided to carry it home with her. When she got home, she asked her older sister why it was there. Her sister just shook her head and said she didn't know. So Alice thought it must be a special ashtray. She placed it on her windowsill and kept it there for a long time.

One day, Alice's mom asked her what the red ashtray was for. Alice was so proud that she had a secret. She told her mom that it was a special ashtray that was used for making wishes. Her mom smiled and said, "That's a wonderful idea Alice". Alice was so happy that her mom liked her special ashtray. From then on, when she was feeling down, she would sit in front of the red ashtray and make a wish.

One day, Toby had a big event. He was so excited! He put on his special outfit and waved goodbye to Mommy. At the event, Toby saw many people. Everyone was working and having a good time.

Toby noticed a smelly food cart and his mouth started to water. He asked one of the workers what kind of food they had. "We have hot dogs and hamburgers," said the worker. Toby wanted to try a hot dog.

He ordered the hot dog and waited. When his order was ready, Toby took a big bite. But something was not right. "It tastes yucky," he said.

The worker laughed. "That's because the hot dog is smelly," he said. Toby was so embarrassed! He thanked the worker and quickly went home. Mommy laughed when she heard the story. From then on, Toby was more careful when choosing his food!

Once upon a time there was a girl named Sarah. She was curious and liked to play with the toys around her. One day, Sarah got a new model truck. She was so excited that she ran to show it to her friend, Ben. The truck had bouncy wheels so when Sarah ran it around, it would bounce up and down! 

When Ben saw the truck, he said, "Wow! That's impressive!" 

Sarah was very proud of her new toy. She drove it around the room, making it bounce up and down. Then, she and Ben decided to play tag. Sarah jumped and bounced around, with the truck in her hand. 

Ben laughed and asked, "Where did you get that truck? It's so much fun!"

Sarah said, "My dad got it for me! He said it was very impressive!"

The two friends smiled and kept playing with the truck, bouncing and laughing the whole time!

Once upon a time there was a very playful cube. Every day it would bounce and roll around the room. Sometimes it would even float in the air!

The cube was so full of energy that it never wanted to rest. Until one day it found a cozy corner and decided to take a nap.

It was so peaceful in the corner that soon the cube was fast asleep. It slept and slept for a whole day!

When it woke up, the cube was happy and full of energy once again. So it bounced around the room, playful and joyful.

But then it remembered how peaceful it was when it was resting and from then on it made sure to take regular naps, so it could play even more energetically.

Billy was having a bad morning. Nothing seemed to be going his way. He even saw his best friend on the playground, but she didn't want to lend him her ball.

Billy was so sad and lonely. He wished he had something to do. That is when he saw a pony near the sandbox. He asked the pony if he could lend him a ride. The pony said yes and Billy was so excited.

He got on the pony and had so much fun! He rode around the playground and the pony even let him ride it up and down the slide. Billy was so happy that the pony had lent him the ride.

Billy thanked the pony and said goodbye. He had such a fun morning and was so glad he had asked to lend the pony. Billy smiled and waved as he walked home.

Once upon a time, there was a big blueberry. It was in a pond and wanted to swim. But it couldn't swim without help.

Lucky for the blueberry, there was a very helpful fish living in the pond. He saw the blueberry and wanted to help it. The fish used its fins to push the blueberry through the water.

The fish and the blueberry swam around the pond together. They had lots of fun. After a while, the blueberry grew a bit too tired to keep swimming. The fish said goodbye and swam away.

The blueberry found a sunny rock to rest on. It felt warm and peaceful and the blueberry was happy. The end.

Once upon a time there were two friends. One was called Bob and the other was called Bill. 

Bob asked Bill if he could go to the park with him. Bill said no and Bob was very sad. He sat on the steps of the house and began to cry.

Then Bill came over to him and said, "Why are you so sad, Bob?"

Bob said, "You said I can't go to the park with you and it makes me feel envious."

Bill said, "Maybe I can help. I can give you my pass to the park. That way you can go without me."

Bob was so happy and hugged his friend. He said, "Thank you, Bill! That was very kind of you."

They both headed off to the park. Bob was so excited to go and couldn't wait to have fun.

Once upon a time, there was a monkey. The monkey loved to eat bananas. One day, the monkey found a brilliant banana. It was the most beautiful banana the monkey had ever seen. 

The monkey said, "Wow, this banana is brilliant! I am going to eat it now." 

Just as the monkey was about to take a bite, a little boy walked by. The boy said, "Hello, Mr. Monkey. That banana looks delicious." 

The monkey replied, "Yes, it is very yummy. Would you like to share it with me?" 

The boy said, "Yes, please." And so, the monkey and the boy enjoyed the brilliant banana together.

Once there was a mother and her three year old daughter, Molly. 
Molly really wanted to sleep in her own bed but her mom said it was still too soon. 
Molly remembered that when she was even littler, she used to sleep in a crib.

Molly said, "Mommy, can I sleep in my crib please? It's so little, I think I can fit!" 
But mom said no, it was too little and she was too old. 
Molly was so sad and asked, "Why can't I sleep in my crib? It's so cozy and fun!"

Mom said, "It's too small, Molly. You're getting so big that you need a big bed now. Come on, I'll have a fun time picking out a big bed with you!" 

Molly smiled. She wasn't sure why her crib couldn't be her bed anymore, but it was funny to think of sleeping in a big bed!

Once upon a time there was a rabbit. She was a very happy rabbit. She hopped around and enjoyed the sunshine every day. She had lots of friends in the forest, they all played together.

One day the rabbit was feeling extra brave. She decided to explore a new part of the forest. She hopped off towards an open field.

As she got to the middle of the field, she saw a big log with an open doorway. The rabbit went to take a look inside. She rubbed the walls as she walked in. Then she heard a voice.

"Hello there! I am the turner. Stop rubbing the walls, they do not like it", the turner said.

The rabbit was so scared she flew away. But the turner was not done with her. He followed the rabbit and he kept turning and turning until the rabbit's body was so twisted that she couldn't move anymore. 

The rabbit was very sad. She had to stay in that spot forever.

The end.

Little Tommy was playing with his toys in his bedroom one day, when he heard a knock on the door. He opened the door to find a famous person standing there, holding a large desk. 

"Hello Tommy," said the famous person. "I've come here to give you a desk. I thought you might like to have it in your room."

Tommy was so excited! He thanked the famous person for the desk and then asked them why they were giving him such a special gift. 

The famous person replied, "I want to encourage you to keep learning and to realize your dreams." 

Little Tommy smiled and hugged the famous person. He was so grateful for the desk and he realized that the famous person was giving him more than just a special giftâ€”they were also giving him an encouraging message. With a smile, he ran off to his bedroom to set up his new desk.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Spot. Spot loved to play with his stuff, like his ball and his bone. One day, Spot went to the park to play with his friend, a cat named Mittens.

Spot said, "Mittens, let's play with my stuff!" Mittens agreed, and they played together. Spot bit his bone, and Mittens played with the ball. They were very happy.

But then, Spot bit Mittens by mistake. Mittens was upset and said, "Ouch, Spot! That hurt!" Spot felt sad and said, "I'm sorry, Mittens. I didn't mean to bite you."

Mittens forgave Spot, and they continued to play with Spot's stuff. They learned to be more careful and had lots of fun. In the end, Spot and Mittens were happy friends again.

Mummy and Daddy were discussing the day. "We're ready for our trip to the zoo," said Daddy.

Mummy said, "Yes, but I have an itch on my nose that won't stop."

Suddenly, their daughter, named Joy, appeared. She said, "What are you talking about?"

Daddy smiled, "We are discussing our plans for the zoo today. It's going to be so much fun!"

Joy beamed, "Yay! I'm ready! Let's go!"

So they all headed out the door, ready to explore the zoo. On the way, Mummy scratched her nose and soon the itch was gone!

"Let's go and find the monkeys!" said Joy as they arrived. 

"Yes, let's do just that!" said Daddy.

Anna liked to play with her dolls. She had many dolls, but her favorite was Lily. Lily had long hair, a pink dress, and a shiny necklace. Anna would brush Lily's hair, dress her up, and talk to her.

One day, Anna found a big mirror in the attic. She thought it would be fun to play with Lily in front of the mirror. She carried Lily and the mirror to her room. She put the mirror on the floor and knelt down with Lily. She smiled at the mirror and said, "Hello, mirror! This is Lily. She is my best friend. Do you want to be our friend too?"

The mirror did not answer. Anna thought the mirror was shy. She said, "Don't be shy, mirror. We are nice. Look, Lily has a necklace. Do you like it?" She held Lily closer to the mirror. She saw the necklace sparkle in the mirror.

But then, something bad happened. The mirror broke. Anna heard a loud noise and felt a sharp pain. She saw blood on her hand and on Lily's dress. She saw pieces of glass on the floor. She saw Lily's necklace broken. She saw Lily's face cracked. She screamed.

Her mom heard her scream and ran to her room. She saw Anna and Lily and the mirror. She was scared and sad. She hugged Anna and said, "Oh, Anna, what have you done? Are you okay? Let me see your hand. It's bleeding. We need to go to the doctor."

Anna cried and said, "Mom, I'm sorry. I didn't mean to break the mirror. I just wanted to play with Lily and the mirror. But the mirror broke and hurt me and Lily. Lily is dead, mom. Look at her face. She is dead."

Her mom said, "No, Anna, Lily is not dead. She is a doll. Dolls don't die. They can be fixed. We can get her a new face and a new necklace. She will be okay. But you are not a doll. You are my daughter. You are alive. And I love you."

Once there was a little girl who liked to run. Every day she enjoyed going outside and running around in the soil. She liked the feeling of the sun and the wind on her face while she ran.

One day the little girl was feeling very sleepy, even though it was morning. She didn't want to run anymore, so she decided to sit in her garden.

Suddenly, a rabbit hopped up to her.

"Why aren't you running today?" asked the rabbit.

The little girl replied, "I'm feeling sleepy today".

The rabbit said, "Why don't you take a little nap and then you can go running again. I'll wait for you if you like".

Suddenly, a little puppy popped his head out of the bush and said, â€œHello! My name is Spot. Would you like to take me for a walk?â€ Karen was so excited. She said, â€œYes, please!â€ 

Karen took Spot around the park and they had so much fun. Karen was so polite and gentle with Spot, and he was so happy with her and followed her everywhere. 

Karen and Spot became best friends and now go for a walk in the park every day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she was playing in the park when she saw a thief run past her. The thief had stolen a cake from a lady's basket. Lily wanted to help, so she ran after the thief.

When she caught up to the thief, she said, "Give back the cake, please. It's not nice to take things that don't belong to you." The thief was surprised by Lily's creative solution and gave back the cake.

Later that day, Lily went home and told her mom about what happened. Her mom was proud of her for being brave and kind. She said, "Lily, it's important to always do the right thing, even when it's hard. And remember, we should never take things that don't belong to us. We should always ask first or cook our own treats." 

From that day on, Lily always remembered her mom's words and became known as a creative problem solver who always did the right thing.

Once upon a time, there was a rabbit who wanted to borrow a light. She asked a frog to help her, but the frog said no.

The rabbit felt sad, so she asked a bird. The bird said yes and gave her a very unusual light. It was round and glowed blue.

The rabbit was happy and thanked the bird. She hopped away with the light and the frog was jealous. He wanted to borrow the light too!

The rabbit used the light to find her way through the dark woods. It lit up her path and she was safe.

The end!

Once upon a time, there was a young boy. His name was Timmy and he was very naughty. One day, his parents scolded him for not being good. 

Timmy felt very sad. He ran away from his house and went to the park. He wanted to hide so he climbed up a chimney. He saw a long and unusual looking tree in the park. It was pink with yellow spots.

When he touched the tree, it started to move. It opened its eyes and started to talk. It said that it was a magical tree, and it could forgive Timmy for being naughty. 

Timmy was very happy. He apologised to the tree and thanked it for forgiving him. Then he hugged the tree and ran back home. His parents were very happy to see him and were glad that he was forgiven. They hugged him tightly and told him they loved him. 

Timmy and his parents lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Lily. She was playing in her garden when she saw a man walking high up in the sky. She was very surprised and ran to her mommy to tell her what she saw. 

"Mommy, look," Lily said. "A man is in the sky."

Mommy chuckled and said, "That's impossible, sweetheart. There's no man in the sky." 

But Lily insisted, so the two of them went outside to take a look. Sure enough, a man was walking among the clouds up in the sky.

As soon as the man saw Lily and her mommy, he smiled and waved. He waved his hands up and down and suddenly, a million little stars started to scatter across the night sky!

Lily was so excited and clapped her hands. She and her mommy watched in awe as the stars lit up the sky one by one. 

"Oh, this is so beautiful," Mommy said. "Let's thank the man for giving us such a lovely show." 

Lily thanked the man and thanked the stars too and after that they went inside to get some rest. 

The next day, the man was gone and all that was left were beautiful starry night sky and a happy little girl. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a man who liked to write. He would always sit quietly at his desk and scribble words on paper. One day, a little girl came to visit the man. She asked him, "What are you writing, Mister?"

"I'm writing a story," replied the man. "Would you like to help me?"

The little girl nodded her head and the man gave her a pencil and some paper. They both wrote together, quietly and happily. When they finished, the man read the story aloud and the little girl clapped her hands with joy.

From that day on, the man and the little girl wrote many stories together. They always sat quietly and enjoyed each other's company. The end.

One day, a little girl named Joy saw a green caterpillar. It had black spots on its back. She looked at the caterpillar and decided to count them. She had a lot of fun counting the spots. She counted eight. That made her happy. 

After she finished counting, she wanted to give the caterpillar a little surprise. She picked some green grass and put it on the caterpillar's back. The caterpillar was really happy with its new snack. 

The caterpillar thanked Joy and crawled away. Joy was happy that she made the caterpillar's day better. From then on, she decided to count things she found in nature and give them surprises whenever she could.

Josh and Simone were walking in the park. It was a sunny day and the flowers were blooming. Josh pointed to a stadium and said, "Look, Simmi! There's a big stadium over there. Can you see it?" Simone smiled and said, "Yes, I can see it. Do you want to go explore it?" Josh nodded and they walked towards it.

They arrived at the stadium and admired the giant structure. Josh was amazed and said, "Wow, the stadium is so tall!" Simone looked around and said, "Let's explore it. I dare you to go first!" Josh hesitated and said, "I'm a little scared. What if there are monsters inside?" Simone put her hand on his shoulder and said, "Don't worry. It'll be alright. I'll be right beside you." Josh smiled and was ready to face his fear.

With Simone's gentle reassurance, Josh stepped into the stadium. He was surprised to see that it was empty and filled with bright sunshine. They explored the stadium and laughed at the funny shapes in the shadows. It was an adventure that Josh would never forget. 

At the end of the exploring, Simone said, "It's time for us to go home. Are you ready?" Josh was sad to leave, but he was also happy that he had been brave enough to face his fear. He smiled and said, "Yes, I'm ready. Thank you for

Once there was an elephant named Elle. Elle was alert and liked to explore the forest. Every day, Elle would walk through the forest looking for food.

One day as Elle was walking through the forest, she found something unusual. It was a big, orange fruit on the ground. Elle had never seen something like this before! She decided to try it and it tasted delicious.

Elle wanted to bring the fruit back to the other elephants so that they could enjoy it too. She tried to pick up the fruit, but it was too heavy for her. She needed help.

Just then, Elle spotted two other elephants in the distance. She waved at them and they came running over. Elle explained that she wanted to share the fruit with everyone and asked them if they could help her.

The elephants understood and each grabbed one end of the fruit. Together, they made their way back to the herd and shared the delicious orange fruit. 

Everyone was so excited to try it and thanked Elle for being so alert!

Once upon a time, there was a king who wore a large crown on his head. He loved to play with his toys and would often pause to take a break. One day, he lost his crown while playing and couldn't find it anywhere. He paused and looked all around his castle but still couldn't find it. 

The king asked his friends to help him look for his crown. They searched high and low but still couldn't find it. The king started to feel sad because he loved his large crown so much. Just when he thought he would never find it, his dog came running up with the crown in his mouth. The king was so happy that he paused to give his dog a big hug. From then on, he made sure to always keep his crown safe while he played.

Once there was a little girl. She was three years old and wanted to succeed. But she wasn't sure how. 
Suddenly, she had an idea! She decided to go and get a rope. She went to the store and found the nicest, fancy rope. 
Back at home, she tied one end of the rope to a tree in the backyard. Then she grabbed onto the rope and began to swing. 
Back and forth she went, higher and higher, and soon she felt like she was soaring! She closed her eyes and imagined she was achieving her dreams. 
At last she opened her eyes and knew she had truly succeeded. She smiled and hugged the fancy rope, knowing it had been the perfect way to reach her goal.

Once upon a time there was a shark who lived in the sea. He liked to eat a lot, especially fish. Every day he would take a slow swim through the deep blue sea and find the biggest fish he could.

One day, while he was swimming, he heard a loud yell! He quickly spun around and saw a little boy standing on the shore.

"What are you doing?" asked the shark.

The little boy replied, "I'm looking for food - can you help me?"

The shark said, "Sure! Hop on my back, and I'll take you through the sea so you can find food."

The little boy hopped on and they started swimming. The shark moved slowly, looking for the biggest fish he could find. Soon enough, the little boy found a fish to eat, and the shark was happy she could help.

The boy thanked the shark and said goodbye, then he hopped off and returned to shore. The shark waved goodbye, and then kept swimming, looking for more food.

Once upon a time, there were two friends. One day, they were walking together and saw something very big. It was a giant! The giant was huge and both of the friends felt scared.

They decided to run and hide. But the giant saw them and started to chase them. So the two friends tried to run away but the giant was too fast. They were getting very frustrated.

Just then, a friendly bird flew down and had an idea. It said to them, "Jump in this barrel and roll away! The giant won't be able to see you!" So the two friends ran and jumped in it. They held on tight and rolled away. The giant couldn't find them.

At the end, the two friends were safe and they never saw the giant again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved ice cream and always asked her mom for it. One day, her mom took her to the park and they saw a man with a big ice cream truck. Lily's eyes grew big and she asked her mom for a cone. 

"Can I have ice cream, please?" she asked her mom gently. 

Her mom smiled and said, "Yes, you can have some ice cream, but you have to eat it slowly and not make a mess." 

Lily nodded her head and took a lick of her ice cream. It was so yummy that she started to stretch her arms out with excitement. "This ice cream is so good!" she said to her mom. 

Her mom laughed and said, "I'm glad you like it, Lily. Just remember to be gentle with it." 

Lily smiled and enjoyed her ice cream, feeling very happy.

Once upon a time, there was a dead shell. It was very quiet and still.

A little boy came along and saw the dead shell. He became very excited. He picked up the shell and put it in his bucket.

The boy decided to take the shell to his house. He went to his backyard and found some rocks. He put the dead shell and the rocks in the bucket.

He took the bucket to the front of his house and loaded the rocks and the dead shell into a wagon. He pulled the wagon as fast as he could back to his house.

When he got home, the boy unloaded the rocks and the dead shell from the wagon. He placed them in the yard and started to build. He made a castle with the rocks and the dead shell.

The little boy was so happy. He had made a castle all on his own with a dead shell!

Jack and his dad were walking down the road. Jack's dad promised to take him to the park. As they walked, Jack saw something broken on the ground - it was his favourite toy car! 
He was very sad and asked his dad to fix it. His dad promised he would try his best. 
They kept walking and soon they arrived at the park. Jack was so excited and he started running in circles. When he stopped, he realised that dad was gone. He looked around and couldn't find him. 
Jack was really scared. Then he saw his dad walking back from the road. His dad's face was sad. He told Jack that he had tried to fix the car, but he couldn't. He had promised to try his best, but he couldn't keep his promise. 
Jack was so disappointed he started crying. He knew that his dad had tried, but still the car was broken.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside and explore the earth. One day, Timmy found a worm on the ground. He thought it was disgusting, but he didn't want to hurt it. So, he gently picked up the worm and put it in the grass. 

As Timmy continued to explore, he saw a butterfly flying in the sky. He tried to catch it, but it flew away. Timmy decided to pause and take a break. He sat down on the grass and looked up at the clouds. 

Suddenly, he felt something tickling his hand. It was the worm from earlier! Timmy smiled and let the worm crawl on his hand. He realized that even though the worm was disgusting to him, it was still a living creature on this earth. Timmy promised to always be kind to all creatures, big and small.

Once upon a time there was a ship that sailed on the sea. All of the people on board were having a wonderful time until they saw something terrible. A giant wave was coming towards them! Everyone was so scared, so they held on tight.

Suddenly, the wave came and it was so big that it made the ship go up and down. The people were terrified and clung to each other. But then something amazing happened. A big blue whale jumped out of the wave and started pushing the ship away from the wave. Everyone cheered with excitement and hugged each other.

The whale kept pushing until the wave was gone. The ship was safe. The whale then swam away. Everyone thanked the whale and knew that it had saved their lives.

The people all hugged each other, some even squeezed each other really tight. Everyone was so happy that they were safe and that the whale had saved them all.

Davey and his mommy were talking in the backyard of their house. Davey asked, "Mommy, can I have a pet?" Mommy replied, "No, Davey. Not now. Our backyard is too messy." When he heard this, Davey was sad and he hoped he could have a pet someday.

A few weeks later, Davey and his mommy were walking in the park. They saw a lost puppy, so they took him home. Davey was so happy and he took care of the puppy every day. Davey was so excited to have a pet!

Sadly, the backyard was still very messy and Davey's mommy was not very happy with the mess. She said to Davey, "I told you we can't have a pet with this mess in the backyard. We have to clean the backyard first. Until then, the puppy has to go away." Davey was very sad and he had to say goodbye to his pet and watch him go away.

This story has a moral: When you want something, make sure you are prepared for it and it won't be taken away from you in the end. If Davey had cleaned up his backyard, he would have been able to keep his pet.

Once upon a time there was a bear named Bob who lived in the woods. One day, Bob felt very sleepy and he didn't feel like doing anything. Unfortunately, he had to find some food, so he started to walk around to look for something to eat.

Suddenly, Bob heard a loud noise. He was a bit scared so he slowly peeked around the corner. What he saw made him very surprised! It was two foxes, arguing and fighting over something. Bob felt bad for them, so he decided to try and help.

He stepped into the clearing and said, "Hey! Why are you fighting?"

The foxes looked at Bob and stopped. The bigger fox said, "This is my food, but the other fox said that it was his too."

Bob thought for a minute, then he said, "I have an idea. Why don't you both step back and I'll increase the amount of food so that there's enough for both of you?"

The foxes looked at each other and then agreed with Bob's plan. As Bob had promised, he added more food so that both of the foxes could have equal amounts. The foxes thanked him and promised him to not fight again.

Bob was glad that he could help. He felt really happy as he continued his journey to find food.

Once, there was a little boy named Tim. He loved to play outside in the sun. One day, he saw a big cooler in his yard. He did not know what was inside, but he wanted to find out.

Tim thought he could open the cooler by being foolish. He started to jump and dance around it. But nothing happened. He felt sad and sat down to think. Then, he saw a key on the ground. He picked it up and thought, "Maybe this key will open the cooler."

Tim put the key in the cooler and turned it. The cooler opened! Inside, there were many fun toys and games. Tim was so happy. He learned that being foolish did not help, but thinking and looking for the key did. Now, Tim could play with his new toys and have more fun in the sun.

John was just a little boy and he loved to explore. He had heard about a distant island, so he decided to find it. He studied maps and asked grown-ups until he found out where it was.

John packed his things and set off on a boat. After a few days of sailing, he arrived on the island. It was beautiful and full of amazing things to do. John was very excited.

He spent days exploring the island. He found interesting plants and animals, and even made new friends. He was very happy.

The island was also independent. It didn't have a ruler and the people lived in harmony. Everyone looked after each other and cared for their environment. It was a place where John could grow and learn new things.

So, John decided to live on the island. He made a house there and grew a garden. His new friends helped him to learn more about the island and eventually he felt like he belonged.

John had found his own special island and he was happy.

Once upon a time there was a girl who liked to play outside. One day she was playing when a storm came. The storm was so loud that the girl was scared. But then the girl saw something. It was a fake key. She smiled and realized that she had something that could lock away the storm. 

Quickly, the girl grabbed the key and ran outside. She waved the key with all her might and the storm seemed to calm down. She kept waving it and finally, the storm went away. 

The girl had done it! She had locked away the storm. Everyone celebrated and the girl was very proud of herself. From then on she kept the fake key with her, just in case the storm came back.

Once upon a time, there was a curious fish. It liked to explore the deep, blue sea. One sunny day, the fish was splashing around when it saw a big, yellow star. The fish said, "Hi, Star! Can I play with you?"
 The star said, "Sure! Let's have a splashy time together!"

So, the fish and the star played together. They swam very fast and they jumped high, making big splashes in the water. They played hide and seek and laughed and laughed! The fish said, "We will stay together forever!" The star said, "Yes, all the time!"

When it was time to go, the fish said goodbye and waved as it swam away. The star twinkled and waved goodbye until the fish was out of sight. 
The fish kept thinking about the star, wondering what fun things they could do together next time.

Once upon a time, there was a beautiful sheep. Her name was Molly. 

She was special because she liked to pay in a different style. She liked to do things her own way. 

One day, Molly was buying treats at the store. She noticed that everyone else was paying with coins, so she decided to pay with a flower instead. 

The shopkeeper wasn't sure at first, but after he saw Molly's happy smile, he accepted her payment. 

From then on, Molly was always able to get treats at the store. Everyone respected her different style of paying. 

The End.

Once upon a time there lived a sweet little girl called Elle. She was three years old and loved to play. One day Elle saw in the sky a bright, shiny laser. She wanted to touch it so she clapped her hands loudly.

The laser heard her so it came nearer and nearer. Elle was so excited and clapped harder and harder until the laser was within reach. But the laser kept going around and around, just a little out of Elle's reach.

Elle kept trying to catch the laser, clapping and shouting in excitement. She was very persistent and didn't give up until the laser finally let her catch it. Elle was delighted and proudly carried the laser home. Afterwards, Elle spent the rest of the day playing with her new laser toy.

Lily was sad. It was a gloomy day. The sky was gray and the rain was falling. She could not go outside and play with her friends. She wanted to do something fun.

She saw her mom write a note on the kitchen table. She asked her mom, "What are you doing?"

"I am writing a note for dad. He is at work. I want to tell him I love him and I miss him," her mom said.

Lily thought that was nice. She wanted to write a note too. She asked her mom, "Can I write a note?"

"Sure, you can write a note. Who do you want to write to?" her mom said.

Lily thought for a moment. She said, "I want to write to my teddy bear. He is in my room. He is lonely. I want to tell him I love him and I miss him too."

Her mom smiled. She gave Lily a piece of paper and a crayon. Lily went to her room. She wrote a note for her teddy bear. She drew a heart and a smiley face. She wrote, "I love you, teddy. You are my best friend. From, Lily."

She put the note on her bed. She hugged her teddy bear. She felt happy. She said, "There, now you are not lonely. We can have fun together."

She and her teddy bear played with her toys. They read a book. They sang a song. They had a tea party. They forgot about the gloomy day. They had a lot of fun.

Once upon a time, there was a young boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside and explore. One day, he saw a big building with a sign that said "library". 

Timmy went inside and saw lots of books. He found one about a little worm that liked to eat apples. As he read, he noticed the pages were starting to rot. 

He went up to the librarian and said, "Excuse me, this book is rotting. Can you please fix it?" The librarian smiled and said, "Of course, Timmy. Thank you for letting me know." 

Timmy was happy that he helped the book and the librarian. He knew that taking care of things was important, even if they were just books in a big building.

Jim was a little boy who loved visiting the garage. It was big and noisy and filled with exciting things. From the outside it looked a little dirty and disgusting, but Jim thought it was amazing.

One day, Jim went to the garage to get some help from the friendly mechanic.

"Good morning, little man," said the mechanic. "What can I do for you?"

Jim squealed with excitement. "My bicycle needs to be repaired!" he said.

The mechanic smiled. "Don't worry, I'll help you," he said.

The mechanic spent the morning inspecting, cleaning and repairing Jim's bike until it was as good as new again. 

Jim was so happy. He thanked the mechanic and ran home to show his mom the new bike. 

From that day on, Jim couldn't stay away from the garage. He was always helping out, finding broken toys and bikes that needed repairing. 

Jim loved visiting the garage, even though it was still a bit dirty and disgusting. He knew that the friendly mechanic was always there to help him.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside and explore the world around him. One day, he was walking in the park when he stumbled over a big rock. 

"Ouch! That hurt," Timmy said as he rubbed his knee. 

Suddenly, he saw something shiny on the ground. It was a steel toy car! Timmy picked it up and started playing with it. He made the car go vroom vroom all around the park. 

As he played, he noticed a funny looking bird watching him. "Hello, little bird. Do you want to play too?" Timmy asked. 

The bird just chirped and flew away. Timmy continued to play with his new toy car and had lots of fun. From that day on, he always kept his eyes open for more cool things to find in the park.

Once there was a boy and his pillow. The boy was very rude and he did not allow his pillow to do anything. The pillow was very unhappy because it could not play or speak. 

One day the pillow had had enough of being treated badly and it decided to run away. It hopped off the bed and scurried away, leaving the boy behind. 

The boy felt sad and realised he had treated the pillow badly. He called out for the pillow and begged it to come back. 

The pillow thought about it for a moment and decided to give the boy another chance. It hopped back onto the bed and allowed the boy to give it a big hug. 

From then on the boy was always kind to his pillow and never disallowed it from doing anything. He was very sorry for how he had acted before and was very thankful to have his best friend back.

Once upon a time there was a bunny who loved to hop. Every day the bunny would jump around and explore the area. One day it came across a large field of dandelions. It was so lovely! The bunny hopped over to smell the sweet scent and it was even better than it expected. 

The bunny hopped around the field and enjoyed it. After a while it noticed a small girl sitting and watching it. The bunny hopped over to the girl and they started talking. The bunny learned that the girl had many opinions on life. The girl said that she loved the bunny's hopping and that she wished she could do the same.

The bunny and the girl became friends and talked to each other every day. They shared their opinions on the world and the bunny shared its wonderful hopping. Every day, they enjoyed the lovely view of the dandelions and the bunny showed the girl how to hop around just like it did. They were so full of love!

One day, a little otter wanted to try something new. "I wonder what I can do today," the otter thought. Then, he spotted a big hill in the distance. "I want to try springing up that hill!" he said.

So the otter started springing. He hopped and bounced up the hill. At first it seemed impossible, but the otter kept trying. After a few tries, he made it to the top!

The otter was so proud of himself. He said "I hope I can do this again. It was so much fun!"

The otter continued springing up and down the hill every day. He became so successful that all the other animals watched in admiration. 

"Well done," they said. "You did a fantastic job."

The little otter smiled with pride. He knew he had done something special.

Steven was walking through the woods and he saw something gray on the ground. He went closer to take a look and saw a cute little fox with its head covered in a gray blanket. Steven said to the fox, "Hello!"

The fox looked up at Steven with wide eyes. It said, "Help me! I'm stuck!"

Steven knelt down so he could help the fox. He carefully moved the top away and saw that the fox had caught his tail in a prickly bush. Steven untangled the fox's tail and the fox thanked him.

The fox stood up and said, "Thank you for helping me. I am so glad that you covered me!"

Steven smiled and said, "You're welcome! It's nice to help friends." He waved goodbye as the fox ran back into the woods and disappeared in a flash of gray.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who wanted to reach the top of a mountain. The mountain was so tall and she was so small that her friends thought it was impossible for her to get to the top. But she was determined and so she started walking up the mountain every day.

Soon the little girl was walking up the mountain regularly and she was getting closer and closer to the top. Every day she pushed herself just a bit further and soon she was so high that she couldn't even see her friends any more. But she kept going, step by step, until one day she finally reached the very top of the mountain.

The little girl was so happy to reach the top and all her friends below cheered for her victory. She was so proud of herself for achieving something that had seemed impossible. And the little girl went down the mountain with her head held high, knowing she could do anything she put her mind to.

Once upon a time there was a strong man. He was happy because he had a shiny season he wanted to show everyone. He was so proud of it that he smiled all the time.

One day, he went outside to show off his shiny season. He twirled around and when the wind blew, his shiny season would twirl around too. Everyone was impressed and happy.

But then, the wind was too strong. All of a sudden, it blew too hard and his shiny season flew away. He ran and tried to grab it, but it was too far away. The wind carried his shiny season away and he never saw it again. He was so sad and no one cheered him. 

The strong man was very sad and he never smiled again. He never found his shining season again and he never was happy.

One day, Mama was cooking in the kitchen. She was making something delicious! The smell was so good.

Mama went and sat on the couch. She was so cozy! But then, she heard a terrible sound.

She got up to investigate. She did not feel so cozy anymore! Mama looked all around the kitchen and found the problem. The pot was boiling and had boiled over!

Mama knew what to do. She turned off the cooktop and wiped up the mess. The kitchen was clean again! Mama sat on the couch, but this time she felt so relieved.

One day, three year old Molly was marching around her house. She marched up and down the stairs and zigzagged her way through the hallway. After a few minutes, Molly was breathing heavily and ready to rest.

Molly's mom saw that she was tired and asked, "Molly are you okay?"

Molly smiled and said, "I was marching around the house and it was so fun!"

Molly's mom smiled and said, "It sounds like you were having a good time. Where did you march to?"

Molly replied, "I marched up and down the stairs and zigzagged around the hallway!"

Molly's mom laughed and said, "Wow, that sounds like a lot of fun. Are you ready for a rest now?"

Molly nodded her head, tired from all the marching. She smiled and said, "Yes, I'm ready for a rest." 

So, Molly and her mom both headed to the living room to rest together after a fun day of marching around the house!

Kelly was very creative. She loved to draw and paint, make funny faces and design funny costumes. One day she went for a walk in her neighborhood. When she got to the corner, she saw her neighbor outside. Kelly was excited to see her! She waved and ran up to say hello.

Kelly's neighbor smiled and asked what she was doing. Kelly said that she wanted to spend the afternoon doing creative things. Her neighbor said that was a wonderful idea and asked if she could join. Kelly said yes!

They decided to do some painting together. Kelly hopped up into her neighbor's yard and gathered some of the colorful leaves from the ground. She painted the leaves different colors and made a picture of the trees in her neighbor's yard.

Kelly and her neighbor spent the afternoon creating beautiful artwork with the leaves they found. When they were done, they smiled and hugged each other goodbye. Kelly was very proud of the artwork she made with her neighbor, and she couldn't wait to show her parents!

Jack was a very serious three year old. Every day he had to stand in front of his school. He was determined to make everyone proud. 

Jack wanted to do the best he could at school, so he would always arrive early. He couldn't wait to learn new and exciting things! On the first day, he was so excited that he forgot to stand very straight and the teacher noticed. 

The teacher said to him, "Jack, stand up straight, please. School is a serious place and it's not good to slouch. We are here to learn and do our best." 

Jack was aware that he had made a mistake and he was very embarrassed. He used his biggest muscles to try and stand as straight as possible. All he wanted now was to do his best and make his teacher proud. 

He stood tall each day when he arrived at school and soon he was proud that he could stand without slouching. Jack was happy to know that he could make himself and his teacher proud.

Once there was a boy who had a loyal friend. Everyday they would spend time together playing round in the park. Every morning they would spin around in circles and giggle until their cheeks turned red. They would spin until the sun went down and stars filled the night sky. The boy and his friend would spend time together until their dad's came to pick them up.

The boy and his friend always had fun together. One day, the boy decided to give his friend something special. He had saved his pocket money for months and bought his friend a round brush to brush his hair.
