The toy had lots of little nails in it, and the little girl wanted to remember where each nail went. She used her intelligent mind to remember where to place each nail and at the end of the day she finished her toy. She was so proud of her work! When her mom came home, the little girl showed her the finished toy, and her mom clapped with joy. The little girl was very proud of her accomplishment, and promised to always remember how intelligent she was.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside in the fresh air. One day, Timmy went to the park with his mommy. They walked on the grass and saw a lot of trees. Timmy loved the trees because they were tall and green. 

After a while, Timmy felt tired and wanted to go home. His mommy said they needed to close their eyes and take a nap. So, they found a cozy spot on the grass and closed their eyes. But then, Timmy smelled something smelly! He opened his eyes and saw a skunk nearby. His mommy told him to stay still and quiet, so they wouldn't scare the skunk. 

Finally, the skunk went away, and Timmy and his mommy got up to leave. They walked back to their car and drove home. Timmy was happy to be back on his own land, where he could play and not worry about smelly skunks.

Ben was very worried. He was in the park with his parents. He saw something that made him scared. It was a long spike sticking out of the ground. He shouted to his parents, "What is that?" His dad said, "It's okay, it's just a spike." His mom explained, "It's there to stop people from driving their cars in the park." Ben was relieved, but he still was a bit worried. He made sure to stay away from the spike while they explored the park.

Once upon a time, there was a big house full of bright colors. Mommy and Daddy hung pictures of rainbows and puppies on the walls.

Mommy said, "Let's make the house stay clean!"

Dad smiled and said "Yes! Let's do it!" 

They put away the toys, vacuumed the carpets, and washed the windows. Then, Mommy and Daddy hung up a new white curtain. 

Mommy said, "Now our house looks nice and clean!"

Dad smiled and said, "Yes it does! Now let's find pretty pictures to hang!"

Mommy and Daddy hung pictures of sunny landscapes, crystal waterfalls and bunch of colorful butterflies. 

Mommy said, "We did it! Our house is so bright and clean!"

Once upon a time, there was a big ranch in the countryside. The ranch was very ordinary, with cows and horses and chickens. One day, a family came to visit the ranch. The ranch owner said, "Welcome to my ranch!" 

The family was very happy to be there. They saw the cows eating grass and the horses running around. They even got to collect eggs from the chickens. It was a fun day at the ranch. 

As they were leaving, the ranch owner said, "You are always welcome to come back and visit my ranch." The family smiled and said, "Thank you for a great day at your ranch!" They drove away, happy and grateful for the ordinary but wonderful experience.

Once upon a time, there was a big brown bear. The bear loved to eat honey from the beehive. One day, the bear met a little girl. The girl had a label on her shirt that said her name was Lily. 

"Hello, Lily," said the bear. "What are you doing?"

"I'm looking for my toy," said Lily. "I lost it in the woods."

The bear thought for a moment. "I'll help you find it," he said, nodding his head.

Lily was very grateful. "Thank you, bear," she said. "You're very thoughtful."

Together, they searched the woods until they found the toy. Lily hugged the bear and they became good friends. From then on, the bear would often visit Lily and they would play together.

Lily was a little girl who liked to play with her dolls. She had many dolls, but her favorite was Anna, who had a pink dress and a charming smile. Lily always took Anna with her when she went out.

One day, Lily and her mom went to visit her grandma, who lived in a big house. Lily was happy to see her grandma, who gave her a hug and a cookie. But she was also curious about the other rooms in the house. She asked her mom if she could explore.

"OK, but be careful and don't go too far," her mom said. "And don't open any doors that are locked."

Lily nodded and ran off with Anna. She saw many doors, some open and some closed. She peeked into some of the open ones and saw a bedroom, a bathroom, a kitchen, and a library. She wondered what was behind the closed ones.

She came to a door that had a sign that said "Do Not Enter". Lily felt a tingle of excitement. She wanted to know what was inside. She tried the knob, but it was locked. She looked around and saw a key on a hook. She reached for it and put it in the lock. She turned it and heard a click. She opened the door and stepped in.

She gasped. The room was dark and dusty. There were many old things, like books, toys, clothes, and pictures. But there was also something else. Something big and furry and scary. It was a bear!

The bear saw Lily and roared. It stood up on its hind legs and showed its teeth and claws. Lily was terrified. She dropped Anna and ran back to the door. But the door was shut and locked. She had left the key inside. She banged on the door and screamed for help.

"Mom! Grandma! Help me! There's a bear in here!"

Her mom and grandma heard her and came running. They saw the sign and the key and realized what had happened. They quickly opened the door and pulled Lily out. The bear growled and tried to follow, but they slammed the door and locked it again.

Lily hugged her mom and grandma and sobbed. She was sorry for being naughty and opening the door. She was also sad for losing Anna. Her mom and grandma comforted her and told her it was OK. They also explained that the bear was not real, but a stuffed animal that belonged to her grandpa, who used to collect them. He had put them in a special room to keep them safe.

Lily felt a little better, but she still missed Anna. She asked her mom and grandma if they could get her back. They said they would try, but they had to wait until the bear calmed down. They took Lily to the living room and gave her some milk and cookies. They also gave her another doll to play with, but Lily knew it was not the same as Anna.

She hoped that Anna was OK and that the bear was not mean to her. She wished she could meet her again and tell her she was sorry and that she loved her. She hoped that Anna still had her charming smile.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. She had a big box. She wanted to unlock it, but she did not know how. Lucy was sad.

One day, Lucy met a boy named Tim. Tim had an idea. He said, "I can help you unlock the box." Lucy was happy. She felt lucky to have a new friend.

Together, they found the key to unlock the box. Inside the box, they found many toys. They played all day and had lots of fun. Lucy and Tim became best friends. And they were lucky to have each other.

Lily liked to play dress-up with her dolls. She had many dolls, but her favorite was Anna. Anna had long hair and a pink dress. Lily liked to comb Anna's hair and put clips and ribbons on it. She wanted to make Anna look pretty and have style.

One day, Lily found a pair of sunglasses in her mom's closet. They were big and shiny and had stars on them. Lily thought they would look good on Anna. She put them on Anna's face and smiled. "You look so cool, Anna!" she said. "Do you like your sunglasses?"

Anna did not answer. She was a doll, and dolls could not talk. But Lily pretended that Anna could talk. She moved Anna's head up and down and made a voice for her. "Yes, Lily, I like my sunglasses. They make me feel like a star. Thank you for being my friend."

Lily hugged Anna and said, "You're welcome, Anna. You're my best friend. I love you." She kissed Anna's cheek and looked into her eyes. She noticed something strange. Anna's eyes seemed to blink. Lily was surprised. She had never seen a doll blink before. She wondered if it was a magic doll.

She asked Anna, "Did you blink, Anna? Can you see me?" She moved Anna's sunglasses up and down and watched her eyes. Anna blinked again. Lily gasped. She felt scared and excited at the same time. She ran to her mom and showed her Anna. "Mom, mom, look! Anna can blink! She's alive!"

Her mom looked at Anna and smiled. She was not scared or excited. She was gentle and calm. She said, "Lily, Anna is not alive. She's a special doll. She has batteries inside her. When you put the sunglasses on her, they activated a sensor that made her eyes blink. It's a fun feature, but it's not magic. Do you understand?"

Lily nodded. She understood. She felt a little silly, but also happy. She still loved Anna, even if she was not alive. She said, "I understand, mom. Anna is a special doll. She has style and she can blink. She's still my best friend. Can I keep the sunglasses for her?"

Her mom laughed and said, "Of course, Lily. You can keep the sunglasses for her. They suit her very well. You have a good eye for style, my dear. Now, why don't you go and play with Anna some more? I'm sure she likes your company."

Lily smiled and said, "Okay, mom. Thank you. I love you." She hugged her mom and ran back to her room. She put the sunglasses back on Anna and said, "Come on, Anna. Let's have some fun. You're the coolest doll ever. And you can blink!"

Once upon a time, there was an elephant. He was very creative and wanted to try something different. He decided to increase his age to become bigger. One day, he used his magic to become older. As he got older and older, he was happy to see that he was increasing in size. Eventually, he was the biggest elephant around. Everyone was so impressed with his creative plan. The end.

Sara and Ben are twins. They like to play in the kitchen with Mom. Mom is making soup for lunch. She tells Sara and Ben to be careful. The soup is very hot and spicy.

"Spicy means it will make your mouth burn," Mom warns. "Do not touch the pot or the spoon. And do not taste the soup until it is cool."

Sara and Ben nod. They promise to listen to Mom. They play with their toys on the floor. But Ben is curious. He wants to know how spicy the soup is. He sees Mom go to the phone. He thinks she is not looking.

Ben sneaks to the stove. He reaches for the spoon. He dips it in the soup. He brings it to his mouth. He takes a sip.

"Ow! Ow! Ow!" Ben cries. He drops the spoon. He runs to the sink. He turns on the water. He drinks from the faucet. His mouth is on fire.

Mom hears Ben. She runs to the kitchen. She sees the spoon on the floor. She sees the soup on the stove. She sees Ben at the sink.

"Ben, what did you do?" Mom asks. She is angry and worried.

"I'm sorry, Mom," Ben says. He is still drinking water. "I wanted to try the soup. But it was too spicy. It hurt my mouth."

Mom hugs Ben. She is glad he is not hurt. But she is also disappointed. "Ben, you broke your promise," she says. "You did not listen to me. You were not careful. You could have burned yourself."

"I know, Mom," Ben says. He feels bad. He looks at Sara. Sara is shaking her head. She is not happy with Ben.

"Ben, you have to be more obedient," Mom says. "Spicy things are not for little kids. They are for grown-ups. Next time, you have to wait until I say it is okay."

"Okay, Mom," Ben says. He is sorry. He wants to make Mom happy. He wants to make Sara happy. He wants to make a new promise. "I will not do it again. I will be a good boy. I will listen to you. I will be careful."

Mom smiles. She kisses Ben. She is proud of him. She is proud of Sara. She loves them both. She says, "That's a good promise, Ben. I believe you. Now, let's clean up this mess. And then we can have some soup. But not too spicy. Just right for you and Sara."

Once upon a time, there was a big whale who lived in the ocean. The whale was very happy and loved to swim around all day. One day, the whale got hurt when it bumped into a rock. It hurt a lot and the whale didn't know what to do.

Luckily, the whale saw a boat nearby and decided to go and ask for help. The people on the boat were very kind and took the whale to a store where they had medicine for animals. The medicine helped the whale feel better and soon it was swimming around again, happy as can be. From that day on, the whale was more careful when swimming near rocks.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside in the park. One day, he saw a pigeon flying in the sky. The pigeon looked so free and happy, and Timmy wanted to be just like the pigeon.

Suddenly, Timmy heard a loud noise. It was a group of big, mean bullies. They wanted to take Timmy's toy truck away. Timmy was scared and didn't know what to do. But then, he remembered the pigeon he saw earlier. The pigeon surrendered to the sky and flew away. Timmy decided to surrender his toy truck to the bullies and run away.

As Timmy was running away, he saw a kind old lady sitting on a bench. She noticed that Timmy looked sad and asked him what was wrong. Timmy told her about the bullies and how he surrendered his toy truck. The old lady smiled and said, "You did the right thing, Timmy. It's always better to be kind and surrender something small than to fight and get hurt."

From that day on, Timmy learned to be like the pigeon and surrender when things got tough. And he also made a new friend in the kind old lady at the park. Plus, he got a new toy truck from his mom, so he didn't even miss the one he surrendered. And it was a good thing too, because it was a hot summer day and Timmy wanted to play with his new truck in the cool shade.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to explore the desert. He saw a cactus with prickly needles. Timmy touched the cactus and it hurt! He learned that cactuses are very prickly and not to touch them. 

One day, Timmy found a spicy pepper on the ground. He picked it up and took a bite. It was so spicy that he had to drink lots of water. Suddenly, the pepper vanished from his hand! Timmy was very surprised and looked around to see where it went. 

Timmy continued to explore the desert, but he was always careful around the cactuses and spicy peppers. He never saw the spicy pepper again, but he knew that it could vanish at any moment.

Once there was a gentle princess who wanted a change. She knew she needed a needle to do it, but she didn't know where to get one. One day, she found a magical needle in her garden. She was so excited! She picked up the needle and held it gently. She still wasn't sure what to do with it, so she showed it to her parents.

Her parents thought it was a great idea! They brought out some colorful threads and showed her how to use the needle. The princess started to stitch the colors together. She wasn't so gentle at first and poked her finger, but she kept trying.

Finally, the princess finished, and put the needle down. She had made a beautiful picture! She was so proud of herself and knew she had changed her world with just a needle! Everyone was thankful to have such a creative, gentle princess.

Lily and Max were adventurous kids. They liked to play in the park and explore new things. One day, they saw a big slide that looked very fun. They ran to the slide and waited for their turn.

"Me first, me first!" Lily shouted. She climbed up the ladder and slid down fast. She laughed and felt happy.

"My turn, my turn!" Max said. He followed Lily and slid down too. He smiled and felt proud.

They played on the slide for a while, until they saw another kid coming. He was bigger and meaner than them. He pushed them away and said, "This is my slide. Go away, you losers!"

Lily and Max felt angry and sad. They did not like the mean kid. They wanted to play on the slide. They did not want to go away.

"Hey, that's not nice!" Lily said. "We were here first. You have to share!"

"No, I don't!" the mean kid said. "This is my slide. I win, you suffer!"

He slid down again and again, and did not let Lily and Max have a turn. He laughed and taunted them.

Lily and Max did not know what to do. They looked at each other and had an idea. They waited for the mean kid to slide down again, and then they ran up the ladder together. They slid down fast, one behind the other, and bumped into the mean kid. They knocked him off the slide and made him fall on the ground.

"Ow, ow, ow!" the mean kid cried. He felt hurt and scared.

Lily and Max felt brave and happy. They had stood up to the mean kid. They had made him suffer.

"Ha, ha, ha!" they said. "We win, you lose!"

They slid down again and again, and enjoyed the slide. They did not let the mean kid have a turn. They laughed and cheered.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Jack. Jack loved to have coffee with his mom. One day, Jack asked his mom if he could have some coffee. 

His mom looked down at him and smiled. She said, "Yes Jack, I think you could have some coffee today."

Jack was very happy and immediately ran to the kitchen. He grabbed a mug and carefully poured some of mom's coffee into it. 

He took a sip and said, "Mmmm, this coffee is yummy!"

Mom smiled and replied, "I'm glad you like it, Jack."

Jack took another sip of the coffee and said, "Thanks, mom. I'm so grateful you gave me some coffee!"

Mom reached out and ruffled Jack's hair. She said, "You're welcome, Jack. Anything for my special boy!" 

Jack smiled, and then went back to enjoying his coffee.

Once upon a time there was a little red worm. She lived in a garden with lots of other worms. One day, the little red worm had a big request. She asked all the other worms if any of them could help her.

All the other worms shook their heads and said no. The little red worm was very sad. 

Suddenly, an idea popped into her head! She thought that maybe a bird could help her get what she wanted. So the little red worm looked around and saw a beautiful red bird near the apple tree. 

She went up to the bird and asked him if he would help her. The bird said yes and flew away. After a few minutes the bird was back. He had brought the little red worm a tasty apple! 

The little red worm was so happy and thanked the bird. She took the apple and enjoyed it with all the other worms.

Once upon a time, there was a happy fish named Nemo. Nemo swam in the bright blue sea every day with his friends. One day, they found a big reef with lots of colorful coral. Nemo wanted to explore the reef, but it was too deep for him to swim down. So, he asked his friend Dory to help him.

Dory was happy to help and she swam down to the reef. Nemo watched as Dory kneel down and looked closely at the coral. She found a hidden treasure and brought it back to Nemo. They were both very excited and swam back to their friends to show them the treasure.

From that day on, Nemo and Dory visited the reef often, and they always found new and exciting things to discover. They never forgot the bright colors of the coral and the fun they had exploring together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sarah. She had a furry teddy-bear that she loved very much. One day, Sarah was playing in her garden and she saw a rock under the tree. She wanted to take it away, so she tried to pick it up. But it was too heavy to carry!

She started to weep, feeling so sad and frustrated. Suddenly, her teddy-bear came up to her and said, "I'll carry the rock for you, Sarah!" Sarah was happy and smiled again. She put the rock on Teddy's back and they danced away together.

But as They reached the house, Sarah realised there wouldn't be enough space for the rock. She started to wept again. Her teddy-bear had an idea. "I can hide the rock here in the garden, and bring it to you whenever you need it."

And so it was. Every time Sarah needed the rock, Teddy went and got it for her. Whenever Sarah was sad or crying, Teddy made her feel better with the rock. Sarah was so grateful to have such a loyal and furry friend by her side.

Once upon a time, there lived a little boy named Jack. He wanted to find a fun story to read.

So one day, Jack went over to his grandma's house. When he got there, he asked, "Grandma, do you have any stories?"

Grandma said, "Yes, I have a very special story. Would you like to hear it?"

Jack said, "Yes, please!"

Grandma started the story. It was about a little rabbit who wanted to find adventure. So, the rabbit decided to leave his home to look for it.

Jack smiled and said, "That's a nice story, Grandma!" He thanked her, and then waved goodbye.

Jack was happy. He found a great story to take home with him. With a skip in his step, he left Grandma's house and went on his way.

Once upon a time there were two teams. They were very different. One team was small, the other big.

The small team wanted to cross a big lake. But they couldn't do it themselves.

So they asked the big team: "Can you help us push the boat across the lake?"

The big team thought for a moment. Then the captain shouted: "Yes, of course! Let's do it together!"

So the two teams worked together. They pushed and pushed the boat. They splashed in the water. It was so much fun.

Finally after a long time, they made it across the lake. "Yay!" everyone cheered.

The two teams high-fived each other. They had done it. They had worked together and made it!

Bob was a 3 year old boy who loved bananas. Every morning he would wake up and eat a big banana for breakfast.

One day, he decided to go to the store to buy more. When he arrived, he saw a big, yellow banana that made him very excited. He asked his mom to buy him the banana, and she said yes.

He was so happy he wanted to take a bite of the banana right away. But when he did, he noticed the banana was bad. It was brown, slimy, and smelled funny. Bob was very sad.

His mom comforted him and said not to worry. The store was kind and offered him a new, fresh banana. Bob was excited again and took a big bite. It was delicious!

Once upon a time there was a robot. The robot was very sad because it had been searching for a long time and could not find anything.

One day, the robot remembered that it still hadn't searched the harsh forest. So, it traveled to the forest and started to search.

Suddenly, the robot heard a noise. Following the sound, it discovered a little puppy. The puppy was sad and shaking. The robot was not sure how to help, but it decided to take the puppy with it.

The robot brought the puppy back to its home and soon, it was cheerful and happy. The robot felt proud and realized it hadn't wasted its time searching in the harsh forest.

Once upon a time, there was an old tree. One day, a mysterious whistle was heard coming from it. 

Two children playing nearby stopped in their tracks. 

"What was that?" the first child said. 

The second child shook their head. "I don't know, let's investigate!" 

They both crept up to the tree, and peered around. A surprise awaited them - inside a small hole in the trunk was a wonderful gift. 

It was a whistle, shining in the sunlight. 

The two children gasped. 
"It's beautiful," the first child said. 

The second child carefully reached in and grabbed the mysterious find. 

She held it in her hands and with a deep breath, blew it. 
The sound that emerged revealed a secret - a flock of colourful birds flew out of the tree! 

The children jumped and clapped, watching as the birds flew away. 

The mysterious whistle will always be a reminder of the amazing mystery they revealed.

Sammy was very excited. He was going to go see his grandmother and he couldn't wait. When he arrived, he saw a shiny bunch of ash on the ground. It sparkled in the sun and Sammy couldn't resist. He picked up the ash and ran off.

Sammy's grandmother was in the garden, but when she saw Sammy running with the ash, she got angry. She shouted, "No Sammy, you must not steal!" Sammy was scared so he put the ash down where he found it.

He tried to run away, but his grandmother had seen him. She gave him a big hug and said, "It's okay Sammy, I forgive you. But next time don't steal things you find on the ground." Sammy was relieved. He smiled and promised not to do it again. 

After that, Sammy and his grandmother had a lot of fun playing together in the garden. He was so excited to be with her and never forgot the lesson he learned that day.

Once upon a time there was a little boy. He loved to play.

One day he was playing in the park with his friends. His hands were getting dry from all the playing.

He said â€œMy hands are so dry. What can I do?â€

One of his friends said â€œLetâ€™s get some water from the fountain and wet your hands.â€

The little boy said â€œYes, thatâ€™s a good idea.â€

When he was done, his hands felt so much better. He said â€œThank you for helping me. Now I can play some more.â€

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She loved to wear pretty clothes every day. One day, her mom brought home a lovely cloth with flowers on it. Lily was so excited because she wanted to decorate her room with it. 

She asked her mom if they could hang the cloth on the wall. Her mom said yes and they used tape to put it up. Lily was so happy to see the lovely flowers on her wall. She even put some stickers on the cloth to make it look more beautiful. 

Now, every time Lily went to bed, she looked at the lovely cloth on her wall and felt so happy. She loved how it made her room look so pretty. And that's how Lily decorated her room with a lovely cloth.

Once upon a time there was a brilliant battery. The battery was very special and could mix things. One day, the battery wanted to mix some glue and water to make something special. 

So the battery mixed the glue and water together in a bowl. As they mixed, they started to make a wonderful bubble mixture. The battery was very excited! The bubble mixture was very strong and the bubbles were bigger and brighter than ever.

The battery was so proud of its bubble mixture, that it shared it with all its friends. Everyone loved the bubble mixture, and the battery was so proud to be the one that mixed it. The battery was very proud of its brilliant bubble mixture. 

The battery was so happy that it mixed the glue and the water and made something so special. From then on, the battery was known as the brilliant battery!

Once upon a time, two friends, Tom and Jill, decided to go for a walk. They decided to cross a meadow, but when they arrived, they were stopped by a fence. Tom said, "I can't reach the top. What should we do?"

Jill said: "Let's use my wool. It is long and thin, and it will help us climb over the fence."

The friends tried to climb the fence using the wool. It took some time, but after a few attempts, they both managed to get over the fence.

When they were on the other side, they looked back and saw the fence they had climbed. Jill said to Tom, "What a clear fence! We should have seen it earlier".

Moral: It is important to take time and look closely at any obstacle before trying to solve it.

Once upon a time, there was a fast car named Speedy. Speedy loved to go fast. One day, he had to take luggage to the other side of town.

On the way, Speedy saw his friend, Slow Snail. Slow Snail said, "Watch out, Speedy! There is a big hole in the road ahead." Speedy felt guilty for always going so fast and not paying attention. He thanked Slow Snail for the warning.

Speedy slowed down and carefully went around the hole. He safely took the luggage to the other side of town. From that day on, Speedy learned to slow down and pay attention to the road.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy who loved playing football. One day, Timmy and his friends went to play football at the park. It was very cold outside and the ground was icy. Timmy's friend, Johnny, said "I'm cold and my hands tremble". Timmy said "Me too, but let's keep playing football!" 

They played for a while, but then Timmy kicked the ball too hard and it went over the fence. They couldn't get it back. Timmy said "Oh no, what are we going to do now?" Johnny said "Let's ask the man who lives in that house to help us get the ball back". They went to the man's house and asked him. The man said "Sure, I'll help you get your ball back". He went to his backyard and got the ball for them. Timmy said "Thank you so much, sir. You're very kind". The man smiled and said "You're welcome. Now go play some more football!"

Once upon a time, there was a brave girl who loved to play games. One day, she saw a marble on the ground. It was very hard and shiny. The brave girl wanted to save it, so she put it in her pocket. 

Then, the brave girl went to play in a tree. But suddenly, she heard a loud crack. The tree was falling down! The brave girl tried to jump away, but she couldn't.

The brave girl held her pocket tight. She wanted to save the marble. But it was too late. The tree fell on her and she couldn't move.

The brave girl said goodbye to the hard marble. She couldn't save it. In the end, she was very sad.

Once upon a time, there was a stubborn little girl. She lived in a small village. Every day she was in a hurry to do her chores. She raced around, trying to get them all done. One day, she was hurrying so much that she almost ran into a wall! Luckily, she stopped in time to avoid a crash. From then on, she ran around a little less quickly. After that, she always remembered to take the time to enjoy her village and the people around her.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play together in the park. One morning, they see a poor dog. The dog is dirty and hungry. It has no home.

"Look, Lily, a dog!" Ben says. "Can we help it?"

Lily nods. She loves animals. She has a cat at home. She goes to the dog and pets it. The dog wags its tail. It likes Lily.

"Hello, dog," Lily says. "What is your name?"

The dog barks. It has no name. It has no owner.

"Can we take it home?" Ben asks. He wants to give the dog a name and a bed.

Lily shakes her head. She knows her mom will not let them. Her mom is allergic to dogs. She sneezes a lot when she sees one.

"No, Ben, we can't," Lily says. "But we can support it. We can give it some food and water. And we can play with it."

Ben smiles. He thinks that is a good idea. He runs to the store and buys some dog food and a bowl. He comes back and fills the bowl with water. He puts the food next to it.

"Here you go, dog," Ben says. "Eat and drink. You must be very thirsty and hungry."

The dog eats and drinks. It is very happy. It licks Ben's hand. It likes Ben.

"Thank you, Ben and Lily," the dog says. "You are very kind. You are my friends."

Ben and Lily hug the dog. They are happy too. They have a new friend. They play with the dog until the sun sets. Then they say goodbye and go home.

They promise to come back the next morning. And the next. And the next. They support the poor dog until it finds a home. And they always remember it.

One day, Mom and Dad took Sarah to a big field. Sarah loved visiting the field because she could always see something new. Today, she wanted to see what was there.

Suddenly, Sarah saw something that made her very happy. She saw a deer! The deer was so big and had a big, beautiful antler. Sarah thought it was so beautiful and ran to tell Mom and Dad all about it. 

Mom and Dad were very proud of Sarah. They said they were happy she paid attention to the important things around her. 

But then Sarah noticed something else. There were some mean people in the field hunting the deer. Sarah was so sad. She didn't like the hunters and she hated that they were trying to hurt the deer. 

Mom and Dad told Sarah that sometimes bad things happen, but it was important to remember why they came to the field in the first place - to appreciate and enjoy the natural beauty around them.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She liked to go to the gym with her mommy. One day, they were at the gym and Lily was getting impatient. She wanted to go home and play with her toys.

Her mommy said, "Lily, we can't go yet. I need to finish my workout."

Lily replied, "Mommy, can I cut the paper with my scissors while we wait?"

Her mommy smiled and said, "Sure, Lily. That's a great idea. Let's go get some paper." 

Lily happily cut the paper into little pieces while her mommy finished her workout. They both had fun at the gym that day.

The pale desk was in the corner of the room. It looked big and was very tall.

The man came up to the desk and opened it. Inside the desk was a big piece of cloth. It was a pale colour too.

The man took the cloth out of the desk and started to fold it. He folded it up very neatly and slowly. Then, he put the cloth back inside the desk.

The man stood back and looked at the desk. He smiled as he saw that everything was neat and tidy. Then he turned and left the room.

Once there was an engine. It was shiny and strong. It always worked hard and was persistent.

One day a boy named Benny came to admire the engine. He was three years old and he was amazed by how it worked. He watched as the engine moved and made loud noises. He seemed to be in a trance watching it move.

Benny touched the engine and said, "Wow! This engine is really strong! I want to be like it when I grow up."

The engine continued to work, but it seemed to be happier knowing that Benny admired it. Benny looked up at the engine and smiled. He was full of admiration.

From that day on, Benny was persistent and worked hard to be like the engine. He kept working hard and eventually he became just as strong and persistent as the engine.

Mummy was busy hanging the washing on the line. She was talking to baby. "Look up at the sun!" said Mummy. "Can you see it?" Baby smiled and stuck its lip out. "The sun is big and round," said Mummy.

Then they heard a noise. It was Grandma! She was hanging a set of wind chimes. "Listen to the chimes," Grandma said. "They make a nice sound, don't they?" Baby smiled and nodded its head.

Mummy and Grandma hung more clothes on the line together. "Mummy and Grandma are so busy," said Baby. Mummy and Grandma smiled. They were happy doing something together.

When they were finished, Grandma said "Let's have some ice cream!" Baby was so excited it jumped up and down! They went inside to enjoy a yummy treat!

Once upon a time there was a small boy who was very scared. Every day he would try to find things that would make him feel better. One day he saw a beautiful poem written on the wall. He read it over and over until he knew it by heart. 

The poem made him feel brave and strong. Every time he felt fearful, he would take out the poem and say it to himself. He was so proud that he knew all the words.

He wanted to show his friends the poem, so he tried to write it down. He pushed the pen and slowly wrote down every word. He was so excited when he finished and he showed everyone the poem. 

His friends and family loved it so much that they memorized it too. Whenever someone was feeling fearful the boy would recite the poem and help everyone feel happy and brave. 

The End.

Once upon a time there was a bowl that was filled with delicious fruit. There were apples and oranges, pears and grapes. All of it was so juicy and ripe that it made the bowl's mouth water.

One day, two children named Jack and Jill decided to take a break from their play and enjoy the delicious bowl of fruit. Jack was the first to reach for an apple, but Jill wanted a pear. She stuck out her hand and bowed politely for the pear, when suddenly a voice called out from behind them.

It was their mom. "No one gets to eat that fruit until you both bow politely and say 'please'"

Jack and Jill both looked at each other in surprise, but they knew they had to listen to their mom. So they both bowed and said please in unison, and their mom replied "Thank you!".

Then they both enjoyed their delicious bowl of fruit.

One day, a little ship named Ship was sleeping on the water. The sun began to wake up, and the sky turned pink and orange. Ship started to wake too. Slowly, Ship opened its eyes and saw its friend, Bird, flying above.

"Good morning, Ship!" said Bird. "Do you want to play today?"

Ship smiled and said, "Yes, I want to play! But I am fragile, so we must be gentle."

Bird nodded and they started to play together. Ship would make small waves, and Bird would fly low and touch the water. They laughed and played all day, being careful not to hurt the fragile ship.

As the sun started to go to sleep, Ship and Bird said goodbye. They promised to play again another day. Ship closed its eyes and went to sleep, dreaming of the fun day it had with its friend.

Once upon a time, there was a little fish named Nemo. Nemo loved to swim in the deep blue sea with his friends. One day, Nemo and his friends were playing a game of tag when suddenly, Nemo saw a shiny pearl at the bottom of the sea. 

Excitedly, Nemo swam down to get the pearl, but as he got deeper and deeper, the silence around him grew stronger. Suddenly, Nemo heard a big voice say, "Who goes there?" It was a big, scary octopus! 

Nemo was scared, but he knew he had to be brave. He said, "It's just me, Nemo. I saw a pearl and wanted to dive down to get it." The octopus laughed and said, "Well, you're a brave little fish. Take the pearl and go play with your friends." Nemo quickly grabbed the pearl and swam away as fast as he could. He was happy to be back with his friends and told them all about his adventure.

Once upon a time, there was a little mouse named Timmy. Timmy wanted to go on an adventure, so he went outside to explore. He saw a big hole in the ground and thought it looked fun to go inside. But it was too difficult for him to climb down.

Suddenly, Timmy heard a loud noise. It was a group of animals who were applauding. They saw Timmy trying to climb down the hole and wanted to help him. The animals worked together to make a ladder for Timmy to climb down safely.

Timmy was so happy and grateful for the animals' help that he started to applaud too. He felt brave and excited to have new friends to go on adventures with. From that day on, Timmy and the animals went on many exciting adventures together, always helping each other and applauding their successes.

Lily was very hungry. She wanted to have some juice and a sandwich. But Mommy said she had to wait. Mommy was busy doing a puzzle. She said it was almost complete.

Lily tried to be patient. She played with her dolls and her blocks. She looked at her books and her stickers. But she still felt hungry. She looked at Mommy's puzzle. It had many pieces. It looked hard.

Lily had an idea. She wanted to help Mommy. She crawled to the table and reached for a puzzle piece. She tried to fit it in the picture. But it did not match. She tried another piece. And another. And another.

Mommy saw what Lily was doing. She smiled and thanked her. She said Lily was a good helper. She said they could finish the puzzle together. Then they could have some juice and a sandwich.

Lily was happy. She hugged Mommy and gave her a kiss. She said she loved Mommy and puzzles. She said she was not hungry anymore. She just wanted to complete the puzzle with Mommy.

Once upon a time there was an ancient tree. Every day it would grow bigger and bigger. One day, the tree took an special trip. It was so excited!

It flew high in to the sky and looked out over the world below. The tree felt so small compared to everything else around it. Suddenly, the tree grew and grew until it was the tallest tree in the whole world! 

The tree looked down and it could see the whole world. It could see all the beautiful places below it. Everywhere the tree looked it could see wonderful things.

The tree was so happy that it took a trip every day. It saw so many wonderful things every day and grew taller and taller. And so, the tree stayed the tallest tree in the world for many years.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys, but he was always afraid of the skeleton toy his dad gave him.

One day, Timmy's sister Sarah came to play with him. She saw the skeleton toy and said, "That's a little scary, Timmy. Can we move it to the other room?"

Timmy agreed, but he was still scared. As they moved the skeleton toy, it fell and broke into little pieces. Timmy was upset, but Sarah said, "Don't worry, we can fix it."

Together, they glued the skeleton back together and Timmy realized it wasn't so scary after all. "Thank you, Sarah. You're the best sister ever!" Timmy said with a smile.

Lily was very excited. It was Wednesday, and she had a special plan. She wanted to play pirates with her big brother Max. She had a paper hat, a wooden sword, and a red scarf. She hid behind the sofa and waited for Max to come home from school.

Max opened the door and saw Lily's hat on the floor. He smiled and picked it up. He knew Lily liked to play pirates. He put the hat on his head and said, "Ahoy, matey! Where is the captain of this ship?"

Lily jumped out from behind the sofa and waved her sword. She shouted, "I am the captain, and you are my prisoner! Surrender, or I will make you walk the plank!"

Max pretended to be scared and said, "Oh no, please spare me, captain! I will do anything you say!"

Lily grinned and said, "Then you have to give me your cookie and play with me until dinner!"

Max agreed and gave Lily his cookie. They played pirates for a long time, and had a lot of fun. Lily was happy that her plan worked. She loved her big brother very much.

Once upon a time there were two humans. One was very alert, and the other was sleepy. The alert human said, "Let's go for a walk." But the sleepy human just stayed in the same spot. 

The alert human said, "Come on! Let's walk into the forest." But the sleepy one just shrugged and said, "No." 

"Oh, come on!" said the alert human. "It'll be fun!" 

Finally, the sleepy human agreed and they started walking into the forest. But when they got there, they got separated. The alert human kept walking and calling out the sleepy one's name, but he couldn't find him. He was all alone. 

Finally, he heard someone call out his name. He looked up and there was the sleepy human! He had found him! 

The alert human breathed a sigh of relief and said, "Let's go home together!" 

And so that's what they did. They always stayed together from then on!

One day, a hunter woke up in a peaceful forest. He felt happy and excited for the day ahead. He put on his warm coat and grabbed his bow and arrows.

As he was walking through the trees, he heard a noise. He stopped to listen carefully. He heard the sound of birds chirping and the rustle of small animals in the bushes.

The hunter kept walking until he spotted something in the distance. It was a small deer! He was very careful and quiet, so the deer didn't notice him.

The hunter slowly drew his bow and then pulled back the string. He let his arrow fly and it hit the deer in the side. The deer let out a loud cry and ran away. The hunter had found his lunch!

That night, the hunter cooked the deer over the fire and ate it with a smile. He felt very satisfied and happy. Then, he curled up and fell asleep, dreaming of peaceful, hunting days.

The sun peeked over the horizon and the day began. Emily happily gazed out her window at the new day. She saw the trees and birds and felt so full of joy. Emily could not wait to start her day. 

She put on her clothes and headed to the kitchen. There she saw a big table filled with all sorts of healthy food. Emily was ready to eat! She scooped a big spoonful of oatmeal and squished it in her mouth. The taste was so delicious!

Emily smiled and started to walk outside. She gazed up with wonder at the bright blue sky and all the birds flying around. Everything was so peaceful and beautiful. Emily took a deep breath and smiled. 

She spent the day running around in the park, exploring and playing with her friends. Before Emily knew it, the sun was setting, and it was time to go. 

Emily gave one last gaze of the beautiful day, full of sunshine and fresh air, and headed home happy and content.

Once upon a time there was a friendly baby. He loved exploring and playing his favorite games. One day, while he was out and about, he saw something very special. It was a beautiful poem, written on a big piece of paper. He was so delighted, he showed it to his mom right away.

His mom smiled and read him the poem. It was about kindness, and the beauty of the world. The baby smiled along, and soon started to memorize it.

Every day, he would recite the poem to his mom and the family. He was so proud of what he had learned. His mom loved it too, and she praised him for his effort.

At school, the friendly baby learnt even more poems and he proudly shared them with his classmates. Everyone was delighted to hear him share his poems, and soon he was known as the poem boy. 

He kept on learning and showing new poems so everyone could enjoy them. He was very proud of how friendly he was, and everyone smiled when they heard him speak. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little mouse who wanted to escape. He was stuck in a filthy drum. He could not get out! He could see a hole in the middle of the drum, but he was too small to fit through it.

Suddenly, the little mouse heard a loud thump! He was so scared! He was brave and looked to see what it was. He saw a friendly cat outside the drum. The cat was meowing and reaching into the drum with her paw.

The mouse slowly moved closer to the cat's paw and grabbed it. The cat held on tight and gently lifted the mouse out of the drum. The mouse was so happy to be free.

The cat and the mouse said goodbye and went on their way. The mouse was so excited to escape the filthy drum. From then on, he was always careful and tried not to get stuck in a drum again.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Mandy who loved to hang stuff from her bedroom ceiling. Her mom thought it was incredible. She had hung wind chimes, ribbons and paper stars. Many days she would just sit in her room and admire the stuff that hung from the ceiling.

One day, Mandy decided she wanted to hang something new. She ran outside to see what she could find. She saw a butterfly in the garden. She quickly grabbed it and ran back inside. She gently hung the butterfly from a string and watched it fly around the room. It was incredible!

Mandy was so happy that she decided to hang a little gift for her mom. She ran to the kitchen and grabbed an apple and a banana. She hung them from the ceiling too. Her mom was so surprised! When she came into the room, she smiled. She was so happy with Mandy's incredible hanging stuff.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy called Tony. His mum mentioned to him that he should always try to do his best. Tony wanted to be successful, so he decided to try to climb in a big hole.

Tony's mum saw him and said "No, Tony. You must not climb in that hole, it's dangerous!" But Tony did not listen. He was determined to reach the bottom of the hole.

Tony climbed and climbed until he couldn't see the sky anymore. But then he slipped. Tony fell down deeper and deeper until he reached the very bottom of the hole.

Tony was stuck and his mum could not hear him anymore, no matter how much he shouted. He was stuck in the hole for days and days. Eventually, Tony was never seen again.

Tony's mum was very sad and she never mentioned success again.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Jack. One day, Jack was helping his mom do the chores and he was given a special job. His mom said, "Jack, I need you to find the hidden leak in the kitchen and clean it up". 

Jack was excited to help his mom. He went to the kitchen and searched high and low, but he couldn't find the leak anywhere. He went to his mom and said, "Mommy, I can't find the leak". His mom smiled and said, "Look behind the curtains, Jack. That's usually where it's hiding". 

Jack looked behind the curtains and sure enough, he found the leak. He quickly got a rag and cleaned up the mess. His mom thanked him for doing such a good job, and gave him a hug. Jack was very happy to have helped his mom.

Mom said â€œLetâ€™s weigh you.â€ So she took Jack to their bathroom and put him on a big scale.

Anna and Ben were playing in the snow. They made a big snowman with a hat and a scarf. They wanted to give him a face, but they did not have any stones or carrots.

"Look, there is some ice on the pond!" Ben said. "Maybe we can use it for the eyes and the nose."

They ran to the pond and broke some ice with a stick. They took two small pieces for the eyes and one big piece for the nose. They ran back to the snowman and tried to attach the ice to his face.

But the ice was slippery and cold. It did not stick to the snow. It fell to the ground and broke into smaller pieces.

"Oh no!" Anna said. "Our snowman has no face!"

She started to cry. Ben felt sad for his sister. He was compassionate. He hugged her and said, "Don't cry, Anna. We can find something else for the face. Maybe some leaves or berries."

He looked around and saw a bush with some red berries. He picked some and brought them to Anna.

"Here, these can be the eyes and the nose. They are bright and pretty. And they will not melt."

He helped Anna attach the berries to the snowman's face. They smiled and admired their work.

"Look, our snowman has a face now!" Anna said. "He looks happy and friendly."

They gave their snowman a hug and a kiss. They named him Berry. They played with him until it was time to go home. They said goodbye and promised to come back tomorrow.

Once upon a time there was a boy called John. He loved to play outside in his garden with his big fluffy teddy bear. One day, he took his bear with him to the meadow and the two of them had a lovely time. 

John decided to wrap his bear up tight in a big blanket and take him for a nap in the sunshine. As he was wrapping the blanket up, he noticed that his bear became very itchy. So he stopped wrapping and tried to tickle the bear to make it feel better. 

The bear spoke up and said â€œThat doesnâ€™t help! Can you wrap me up really tight, please? That way I won't be so itchy.â€

John was surprised that his bear could talk! He wrapped him up tight in the blanket and gave the bear a big hug. The bear soon began to doze off in the sunshine and John felt very happy that his bear was feeling a lot better.

They both had a nice snooze in the meadow until it was time to go home.

Once upon a time, there was a little bee named Buzz. Buzz lived in a hive with his friends. One day, Buzz wanted to explore the world outside of the hive. His friend, Buzzy, warned him to be careful because there were fierce animals outside. 

Buzz stepped outside and saw a big flower. He flew towards it to collect some nectar. Suddenly, he saw a big, fierce bird flying towards him. Buzz quickly flew back to the hive and told Buzzy what happened. 

Buzzy said, "I told you it's dangerous outside, Buzz. You need to be careful." Buzz realized that Buzzy was right and promised to be more careful in the future. From that day on, Buzz stayed inside the hive and never ventured outside again.

Once upon a time, there was a monster who was not very clever. He was always getting into trouble and causing chaos. He would bump into things and break them, and he would cry when things didn't go his way. 

One day, he decided to try to improve himself. He thought, "If I am more careful with things, maybe I won't break them." So he started to practice being more careful. He practiced walking in a straight line, and he worked on being gentle with all the things around him. 

When the monster had practiced for a long time, he became very clever. He could now walk in a straight line without bumping into anything, and he could handle things without breaking them. Everybody around him was so proud of him for improving! 

The monster was so happy that he had worked hard to become more clever. He thought, "Being careful and clever is a great way to get along in the world." 

And that's how the monster improved himself and became super clever!

Tom and Mia are playing in the park. They see a big dog with a hunter. The hunter has a long stick that makes loud noises. Tom and Mia are scared of the dog and the stick.

"Let's hide behind the tree," Tom says to Mia. They run to the tree and watch the dog and the hunter.

The dog sees a bird in the sky. It barks and runs after the bird. The hunter tries to stop the dog. He pulls on a rope that is around the dog's neck. But the dog is too strong. It pulls the hunter with it.

"Ow! Stop! Bad dog!" the hunter yells. He falls on the ground and drops his stick. The stick makes a loud noise. The bird flies away. The dog is happy. It wags its tail.

The hunter is upset. He is dirty and hurt. He picks up his stick and looks for his dog. He sees Tom and Mia behind the tree. He is angry.

"Hey, you kids! What are you doing here? This is not a place to play!" he shouts.

Tom and Mia are scared. They hold hands and run away. They go back to their mom and dad. They tell them what they saw. Their mom and dad hug them and say they are brave. They give them ice cream and take them home. Tom and Mia are happy. They do not like the dog and the hunter.

Once upon a time, there was a worm who lived in the ground. His name was Eric. He was very small and loved to play in the dirt. One day, Eric went to visit his friend. His friend's name was John. 

Eric and John said hi and were having so much fun when they noticed something smelly. It was a pile of dirt which was full of worms! Eric was so excited and asked John to play with him in the pile. 

John refused. He said, "No way! I don't want to get my hands dirty and smelly from those worms!" Eric was very sad. He wished he could have fun with his friend in the pile of worms. 

But then John had a great idea. He said, "Let's play with the worms in a different way! We can make them into a tower. That way we can still have a lot of fun, but our hands won't get dirty or smelly at all!" 

Eric was so happy and both of them began to make the tower with the worms. They laughed and enjoyed the game together. So they learned that they could still have fun without getting smelly.

Once upon a time, there was an adorable little boy called Joey. His favorite thing to do was to go to the store and buy a yummy pie. All the people who worked at the store loved him because he was so charming. 

One day, Joey and his mom went to the store, and Joey asked her to buy him a pie. His mom said, "Of course I will buy you a pie, Joey. You are cute and adorable!".

Joey was very excited, and couldn't wait to get the pie. The shop assistant gave him the pie and asked, "Do you have to pay now or later?". Joey said, "I have to pay later. I don't have any money with me. I'm only three years old!". 

The shop assistant thought Joey was so cute and said, "Don't worry, you can pay next time you come." Joey thanked the shop assistant and then ran off with the pie. He was so excited to eat his delicious treat!

One day, an elderly man was walking down the street looking at the billboard. Suddenly, he heard a snap. He turned around and saw a little 3-year-old boy standing behind him. The boy had snapped a picture of the billboard with his camera. The old man laughed and asked the boy why he wanted a picture of the billboard. The boy said it was because the billboard was so pretty. The old man smiled and nodded, agreeing that the billboard was beautiful indeed.

The two of them stood there and admired the billboard for a while, until the old man told the boy that it was time to go home. The boy said goodbye to the old man and then ran off, skipping away down the street with a smile on his face. He was happy to have taken a picture of the pretty billboard.

One day, a cute little girl named Lily went to her garden. She had a small bag of beans. She wanted to grow big bean plants. Lily dug a hole in the ground and put a bean in it. She covered the bean with dirt and gave it some water. "Grow big and strong, little bean," she said.

The next day, Lily saw a small bird in her garden. The bird looked at the place where Lily put the bean. "Are you looking for my bean?" Lily asked the bird. The bird nodded its head. Lily thought the bird was hungry, so she gave it some seeds to eat. "You can visit my bean, but don't eat it, okay?" The bird nodded again and flew away.

Days went by, and Lily took care of her bean every day. The bird came back to visit, too. One day, the bean started to grow into a big, strong plant. Lily was so happy! The bird came back and saw the big bean plant. It nodded its head and flew away. Lily knew that the bird was happy for her and her big bean plant.

One day, Joe and his mom went to the store. Joe could hardly contain his excitement. "Why are we here, Mom?" he asked.

His mom smiled and said, "We need some oats, so let's unpack them." Joe didn't know what oats were. But he quickly found out as mom took out a big bag of oat cereal. It was so rich and creamy; he knew it was going to be delicious.

Joe cheered and clapped. He couldn't wait to have it for breakfast. Mom laughed at Joe's enthusiasm and said, "I'm glad you like it, Joe. We can start eating it in the morning." 

Joe smiled and hugged his mom. He was so happy that they had found such a rich and tasty oat cereal to enjoy.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She was hungry, so she decided to go fishing. She grabbed her net and ran to the lake. 

When she got there, she carefully put her net in the water. She waited and waited, but nothing came out. She was so sad that she started to cry. 

Just then, a big fish came swimming by. The little girl was so excited, she quickly put her net over the fish. She caught it and laughed with joy!

The little girl happily trotted home with her fish. That night she feasted on her catch. She was so happy and full she couldn't help but laugh!

Once upon a time, in a small village, there was a little girl named Lily. She liked to point at things she saw. One day, Lily saw a distant hill. She wanted to go there and see what was on the other side. So, she asked her mom if she could go.

Her mom said, "Yes, but be careful when you cross the road." Lily was excited and started her journey. She walked and walked until she reached the road. She remembered what her mom said and looked both ways before crossing the road. She crossed safely and continued her walk to the distant hill.

When Lily reached the hill, she saw a beautiful valley. She was happy that she listened to her mom and crossed the road safely. She went back home and told her mom about her adventure. The moral of the story is to always listen to your parents because they want to keep you safe.

Once upon a time, there was a jolly mom and her daughter. They lived in a small house near a big farm. The mom loved to feed the animals on the farm every day.

One day, the daughter wanted to help her mom feed the animals. They both went to the farm with big smiles. They fed the cows, the pigs, and the chickens. The animals were happy to see them.

But then, a big storm came. The wind blew, the rain fell, and the mom and daughter got very wet. They tried to run back to their small house, but they couldn't see where they were going. The mom and daughter got lost and couldn't find their way home. They were very sad and scared.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Daisy. She was only three years old. Daisy was on her own in the house, and she was feeling curious. She wanted to explore!

Daisy tiptoed down the hallway and she saw a big curtain stretching across the room. It was so long that she didn't know what was on the other side.

Daisy took a deep breath and said, â€œhello? Is anyone there?â€

A harsh voice answered, â€œyes, what do you want?â€

The next day, Daisy's mother took her back to the room with the curtain and opened it up so that Daisy could see what was on the other side. 

It was a beautiful playroom filled with toys and games! Daisy was so happy that she ran in and started playing. 

Through the curtain, Daisy had found a wonderful world full of fun and laughter.

One day, the mommy decided to take her three-year-old daughter to the park. When they arrived, the little girl was so excited. She couldn't wait to explore the grass, climb the trees, and run around. 

Mommy reminded her daughter not to go too far. Then she gave her a treat. It was a little cardboard box filled with sugary sweets. The daughter loved it! She was so happy! 

After that, they went for a walk around the lake. It was so charming. Mommy showed her daughter some ducks and birds. She reminded her daughter not to make too much noise when she saw them. 

Finally, it was time to go home. Mommy gave her daughter one last treat. It was her favourite ice cream. As a special treat, mommy added a little extra topping. The daughter grinned from ear to ear. It was the perfect end to a lovely day.

Mama was very mad because the house was very messy. She said "we have to clean up now!" So they got to work.

Mama and her children grabbed their cloths and buckets. They started to scrub and wipe to make everything clean. They even had to clean under the bed, which was very dusty.

Mama was very happy when everything was clean. She gave her kids a big hug and said "Great job! That was so helpful."

After that, Mama gave them a tip. She said it was for being so nice and helping her clean. The children were so excited!

But then someone knocked on the door. It was neighbour Sam, but he was being very rude. He said he wanted to come in, but Mama said no.

Mama said Sam needed to say "please" and "thank you" first. He looked embarrassed and apologized. Mama said he could come in next time he was more polite.

Once upon a time, there were two friends called Roger and Robbie. They were both three years old and were very good friends. They were always playing in the park together.

One day, the friends wanted to do something special. They decided to unite and make something pink. They found some rub in the park and they mixed it with water to make pink paint.

They had so much fun painting their masterpiece in the park with lots of pink paint. Everyone who walked past stopped and admired their creativity. 

Once their masterpiece was finished, Robbie and Roger hugged each other and said: "We made something special together, we united!"

From that day onward, the two friends played together in the park every day.

Once upon a time there was a little bunny named Daisy. Daisy was so excited because she had a new present - a carrot! Daisy was very gifted, and liked to show off her gifts to her friends. She shook the carrot in her hands and hopped over to ask them if they wanted to play a game with it.

"Look! I have this carrot! Let's play with it!" Daisy exclaimed.

Her friends looked at Daisy and the carrot and started laughing. They all agreed that it looked like a lot of fun so they started playing. They took turns shaking the carrot, trying to make it hop across the ground. Every time Daisy shook it, it hopped a bit farther.

After a while, Daisy and her friends got tired of playing with the carrot. But Daisy was still proudly carrying it as she hopped away to go home. She was happy to have a new present and even happier that her friends had enjoyed playing with it.

Once upon a time there was a lady who was very, very sad. She felt miserable every day. She kept seeing the same gray clouds, and nothing made her happy.

One day she decided to go outside and take a walk in the woods. She felt the warm sunshine and heard the birds singing. She looked around her and saw a beautiful, green field, with a big rake lying in the grass.

The sunshine was so warm and bright, and the lady felt a beam of sunshine all around her. She felt as if the sunshine was shining in her heart, lifting away all her sadness and worries.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved treats, especially chocolate ones. One day, Lily went to the park with her mommy and daddy. While playing on the swings, she saw a dog. The dog was big and Lily felt fearful. 

She told her mommy and daddy about the dog and they mentioned that he was friendly. They asked if Lily wanted to pet him and she said no. But then the dog came closer and Lily saw that he was wagging his tail. She slowly reached out her hand and petted the dog.

Once upon a time there was a wide river that cut through the forest. On one side of the river, a family of rabbits lived peacefully. They had plenty of food to eat and were very happy. 

One day, the rabbits were out gathering food when they heard a terrible noise coming from the river. They looked over and saw a large bear struggling in the water. The bear had become stuck in the river, and was in danger of drowning. The rabbits quickly ran to help.

The rabbits tried to pull the bear out, but they were too small. They needed a plan! 

Just then, one of the rabbits had an idea. "Let's get a big pill and put it in the river," said the rabbit, "We can place the pill in between the bear and the river's edge. That way, it will prevent the bear from drifting away with the current!" 

The other rabbits liked the idea, so they quickly found a pill and put it in the river. Sure enough, it worked! The pill was wide and strong enough to keep the bear in place, until someone larger could come and rescue it.

The rabbits were glad that they could help, and they were also proud of their quick thinking. This story reminds us that with a bit of creativity and cooperation, even the smallest of us can make a big difference.

Lily did not go away. She said: "No, you are wrong. The mall will be bad for the nature. It will make noise and trash and smoke. The trees are not useless. They are beautiful and important. I will not let you cut them. I will save them!"

Lily climbed on the truck and took the saw. She threw it away and ran to the trees. She hugged them and said: "Don't worry, trees. I am here. I will protect you. You are my friends."

The truck driver was angry and scared. He called the police and said: "Help! There is a crazy girl on my truck. She took my saw and ran to the park. She is trying to stop me from cutting the trees. Come and get her!"

The police came and saw Lily and the truck driver. They asked them what happened. Lily told them her story. The truck driver told them his story. The police listened and thought. They said: "Lily, you are brave and kind. You care about nature and you want to save it. But you cannot take things that are not yours and you cannot climb on trucks. That is dangerous and wrong. You have to be careful and respectful. Truck driver, you are greedy and rude. You don't care about nature and you want to destroy it. But you cannot cut trees that are not yours and you cannot laugh at children. That is harmful and mean. You have to be responsible and respectful."

The police took the saw and the sign from the truck driver. They said: "We will not let you cut the trees. The trees are part of the park and the park is for everyone. The park is a place where nature and people can live together and be happy. You have to find another place for your mall. And you have to say sorry to Lily and the trees."

The truck driver was ashamed and sorry. He said: "I am sorry, Lily. I am sorry, trees. I was wrong and selfish. I will not cut you. I will find another place for my mall. And I will plant more trees there."

Lily was happy and proud. She said: "Thank you, police. Thank you, truck driver. I am glad you changed your mind. I hope you will be nice to nature from now on. And I hope you will visit the park and see how beautiful it is."

The police and the truck driver left. Lily stayed with the trees. She sang to them and played with them. The birds and the flowers and the other animals came and joined her. They thanked her and praised her. They said: "You are a hero, Lily. You saved the trees and the park. You are a friend of nature. You are famous!"

Once upon a time there was a little boy called Johnny. Johnny was only three years old but he already knew a lot of things. One day, Johnny asked his mom if he could do a quiz. 

"Yes, of course!" said Mom. 

Johnny happily ran to the kitchen table and waited for his quiz. 

Mom pulled out a big book and showed Johnny a picture of a river. "What will happen when spring comes?" she asked. 

Johnny thought for a moment. He had never seen a river in the spring before. He answered, "The river will get bigger!" 

Mom smiled and replied, "That's right! That's very humble of you." 

Johnny was so proud of himself for getting the answer right. He couldn't wait to share his newfound knowledge with his friends!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved to eat avocados. One day, her mom brought home a big, green avocado from the store. The little girl was so excited to eat it!

But when she took a bite, she realized it was very spicy. She didn't like it at all. So she asked her mom to unpack the avocado and take out the spicy part.

But her mom didn't know how to do that. So the little girl kept eating the spicy avocado, even though she didn't like it.

Later that night, the little girl got a tummy ache. She felt very sick and had to go to the hospital. The doctors said she ate too much spicy avocado and it made her very sick.

From then on, the little girl learned to be careful when eating new foods. She never wanted to feel sick like that again.

One day, a bird saw a rhinoceros in the mud. The bird was hungry and wanted to eat some bugs on the rhinoceros. The bird flew down and landed on the rhinoceros's back. The rhinoceros did not like the bird. He felt a tickle and shook his big body.

The bird was scared and flew up again. He did not want to fall off. He wanted to soar in the sky and be free. He looked for another place to find food. He saw a lake with some fish. He flew to the lake and dived into the water. He caught a fish and ate it. He was happy and full.

The rhinoceros was still in the mud. He was filthy and hot. He wanted to cool off and be clean. He saw the lake and walked to it. He splashed into the water and washed off the mud. He felt better and refreshed.

The bird and the rhinoceros did not see each other again. They lived in different places and liked different things. But they both enjoyed the lake and the sky. They both had what they needed. They were both happy.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Molly. She was three years old and very smart.

One day Molly was in the garden with her mom. She saw a smelly fork in the dirt. Molly asked her mom what she could do with the fork. Her mom said, "You can solve the problem of what to do with the smelly fork."

Molly thought long and hard. She came up with a solution. She picked up the fork, put it in the trash can, and washed her hands afterwards.

Molly had solved the problem of the smelly fork! Her mom was so proud of her.

Molly learned a valuable lesson that day. Whenever she had a problem, it was important to think it through and find a solution. This way, she could solve any problem, no matter how smelly!

One day, Maggie was feeling very adventurous. She put on her belt and snuck upstairs. When she peeked around the corner, she saw Mommy and Daddy talking in the living room.

Maggie's ears started to burn with curiosity. She wanted to hear what they were saying. She took a few tiny steps towards them, but stopped when Daddy said "No, that's not a good idea". Maggie's stomach flipped, she was afraid she was in trouble.

Maggie tried to back away as quietly as possible, but Mommy noticed her. Maggie froze as Mommy walked over and knelt in front of her.

"What did your Daddy say, Maggie?" Mommy asked.

Maggie looked at her feet and mumbled, "That it wasn't a good idea".

Mommy smiled and said, "That's right. You have to be careful when you're being adventurous, especially when you're sneaking around and trying to peek in on Mommy and Daddy's conversations."

Maggie hugged Mommy and said, "I'll be careful next time." 

Mommy nodded and said, "It's always good to be adventuresome. Just remember to be safe." Maggie nodded and went off on her next grand adventure.

Once there was a duck who loved solving mysteries. Everywhere she went, she tried to figure out answers to questions. But one day, she came up against a puzzling problem that she couldn't seem to solve.

The duck went to ask her friend, the clever owl, for help. "This problem seems impossible to solve," she said, honestly. "Can you help me with it?"

The wise owl sighed. "That's easy," he said. "The key is to be honest with yourself and your friends. Honesty is the best way to solve any problem. And that's the secret to solving this one, too.

The duck understood and thanked the owl for his wisdom. After that, she was able to solve her problem with the power of honesty. From then on, she made sure to use her new knowledge whenever a problem arose.

The moral of this story is to be honest with yourself and others, as it is the best way to solve problems.

Anna and Ben like to play with their toys. They have a lot of toys, but their favorite is the record player. They can put a record on it and hear music and stories. Sometimes they sing along or dance.

One day, Anna and Ben found a new record in their room. It was a gift from their grandma. They were very happy and wanted to listen to it. They put the record on the player and turned it on. It was a story about a princess and a dragon.

Anna and Ben listened to the story and pretended to be the princess and the dragon. Anna wore a dress and a crown. Ben wore a mask and a cape. They acted out the story and had fun.

But then, Ben got too excited and jumped on the record player. He wanted to roar like the dragon. He did not see the needle that played the record. He stepped on it and it broke. He also hurt his foot. He cried out loud.

"Ow, ow, ow! It hurts, it hurts!" Ben said.

Anna heard him and ran to him. She saw the broken needle and the record. She was sad and angry.

"Ben, what did you do? You broke the record and the player! Grandma gave us that! And you hurt yourself!" Anna said.

"I'm sorry, Anna. I did not mean to. I was just playing. It was an accident." Ben said.

Anna felt sorry for Ben. She saw his foot was bleeding. She got a band-aid and put it on his foot. She hugged him and said:

"It's okay, Ben. I forgive you. But you have to be more careful. The record player is not a toy. It is for listening, not for jumping. And you have to take care of your foot. It will get better soon." Anna said.

"Thank you, Anna. You are a good sister. I love you." Ben said.

"I love you too, Ben. You are a good brother. But next time, let's play with something else." Anna said.

They smiled and hugged. They put away the record player and the broken record. They decided to play with their blocks instead. They were happy again.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a creative little girl named Lily. She loved to draw, paint, and make things with her hands. One day, she found a raven with a hurt wing. The raven could not fly. Lily wanted to help the raven return to his family.

Lily said to the raven, "Don't worry, I will help you!" She used her creative skills to make a soft bed and a little house for the raven. Every day, she fed him and took care of his hurt wing. Soon, the raven started to feel better.

One day, the raven's wing was all better, and he could fly again. The raven said, "Thank you, Lily, for helping me return to my family!" Lily was happy to see the raven fly away. She knew that helping others was a good thing to do. The moral of the story is to always be kind and help others in need.

Once upon a time, there was a kind girl named Jill. Jill had a pet dog who she loved very much. One day, Jill took her dog for a walk and they went to the park.

At the park, Jill saw some swings. She wanted to have some fun so she ran to the swings and started to hang on them. She laughed and laughed as she hung in the air.

As she was hanging on the swing, Jill's pet dog saw some butter on the ground. He ran over and started to lick it. Jill laughed and said, "That's ok, my dog. Butter is kind". Then she helped her dog pick up the butter and they both went home.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who lived in a big city. One day, Lily's parents took her to a country fair. There were lots of animals and games to play. Lily loved it!

Later that day, Lily and her parents sat down to read the book together. Lily was so happy that she got a new book. She said to her parents, "Thank you for taking me to the fair and recommending this book. I love learning about the animals in the country!"

Once upon a time, there was a little town. The people in the town needed help. They couldn't do everything they wanted to do.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who wanted to go on an adventure. She decided to visit a hotel.

The little girl was so scared that she wanted to leave. She quickly ran around to all of the doors and windows, closing them tightly.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a girl. She was three years old and had lots of fun. One day, the girl went to the kitchen. She saw something amazing - an original toy! She quit playing with her toys to play with the new one. She spent all day having fun in the kitchen, playing with the original toy.

For the rest of the week, the girl returned to the kitchen to play with her favorite original toy. With her new toy, she made happy memories that she would treasure forever.

Once upon a time, there was a cute dolphin in the sea. The dolphin loved to swim and play with its friends. One day, the dolphin saw a big number of fish swimming nearby. From that day on, the dolphin always looked for big numbers of fish to play with.

One day, a cat and a dog were playing in the park. They found a tasty pill on the ground. The cat wanted to eat it, but the dog wanted it too. They did not know what to do.

They sat down to discuss who should get the pill. The cat said, "I saw it first, so I should eat it." The dog said, "But I am bigger and need it more." They both wanted the pill very much.

Then, a big bird came down from the sky. The bird took the tasty pill away. The cat and the dog were sad. They learned that they should share things and not fight.

Mira was three years old. She was playing in the garden when she heard a loud noise. She looked up and saw her mom coming outside.

Mira's mom said, "What has happened here?"

Mira's mom smiled. She said, "It's okay. Just be careful next time!"

Mira was happy that she still had her mom's love, even when she made a mistake.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She loved to drink cocoa. One day, she accidentally dropped her cocoa mug and it broke into pieces. She felt sad and started to cry. Her mom heard her and came running to see what happened. Lily told her that her cocoa mug was broken. Her mom hugged her and said, "Don't cry, Lily. We can buy a new mug." Lily stopped crying and smiled. Then, she shouted, "Thank you, Mommy!"

Once upon a time, there was a little small sailboat that lived by a small river. The sailboat always felt so lost and unsure of what was to come.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Jane and Fred. They lived far away from each other so they only wrote letters. One day Fred wrote to Jane with a special pen. The pen had ink inside of it that changed colour. Jane was so excited!
