Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside. One day, he saw a cricket hopping around in the grass. Timmy thought the cricket was very cute.

Timmy's mom came outside and asked him what he was doing. "I'm watching the cricket, Mommy!" Timmy said. "Do you mind if I keep watching him?"

"No, I don't mind," said Timmy's mom. "But be careful not to step on him."

Suddenly, Timmy noticed that the cricket wasn't moving anymore. "Mommy, the cricket is deaf!" Timmy said sadly. "He can't hear me talking to him."

"It's okay, Timmy," said his mom. "Maybe you can find another cricket to be friends with." And so, Timmy went on a search for another cricket to play with.

Once upon a time, there was a poor little girl called Sarah. Sarah was a very unhappy girl, who would often complain about her life.

One day, Sarah went to visit a wise old man, who lived in a far away place. She told him all the things she was complaining about, but the wise man just smiled.

He said to Sarah, â€œThere is something very special about you, Sarah. You may be poor, but your smile is more valuable than any riches in the world.â€

Sarah was surprised. She asked, â€œWhat do you mean?â€

The wise man replied, â€œWhen you smile, you can make the world seem like a brighter place. Always remember that when you feel like complaining.â€ 

Sarah smiled, thanked the wise man for his words, and then said goodbye. From that day onward, she tried to remember the wise manâ€™s advice: keep smiling, and the world will usually feel a little brighter.

One day there was a bald man who worked in a factory. Every morning he would wake up and go to work. One day something strange and wonderful happened - it started to spring!

The man felt so happy he decided to take the day off, so he jumped out of bed, put on his coat and quickly ran outside! The ground was wet and muddy. He laughed as he splashed around and enjoyed the warm air. The sun was shining, the birds were singing and the flowers were blooming all around him.

He noticed a butterfly fluttering around and stopped to watch it. Suddenly the butterfly flew onto his head and rested there. He was amazed and knew that this was a special moment! He kept walking and enjoyed the fresh air and beauty of the world around him.

Soon enough he had to go back to the factory but he knew that he would always remember the special day when he felt the beauty and joy of spring.

Once upon a time, there was a big whale. The whale was very proud. He liked to swim in the deep blue sea. He had a friend, a small fish. They played together every day.

One day, the whale saw a big ship. The ship was making a lot of noise. The whale did not like the noise. The small fish was scared too. They wanted the ship to go away.

The whale had an idea. He would complete a big jump over the ship. He swam very fast and jumped high in the sky. The people on the ship saw the big whale and stopped making noise.

The ship went away. The whale and the small fish were happy. They could play in the deep blue sea again. The whale was very proud of his big jump.

Once upon a time, there was a new pit. In the pit, there were many colors. A boy named Tim wanted to paint with the colors.

Tim took a brush and started to paint. He painted the sun, the sky, and the trees. He was very happy with his painting.

When Tim was done, he showed his painting to his mom. She loved it too. They put the painting on the wall. Tim and his mom smiled at the beautiful painting.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny named Benny. Benny was very lonely because he didn't have any friends to play with. One day, Benny found an old frame in the woods. He thought it was pretty and decided to take it home.

When Benny got home, he showed the frame to his mom. She thought it was nice too, and they decided to test it out by putting a picture inside. They found a picture of Benny's family and put it in the frame.

Benny was so happy with his new frame and picture. He didn't feel as lonely anymore because he had his family with him all the time. From then on, Benny always looked for things to put in his frame and he knew that he would never be lonely again.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Dave. He was playing with his classmates in the playground. Suddenly, he noticed two girls, Lucy and Daisy, were being unkind to each other. Dave was very sad.

Dave ran up and said, "What's wrong?" Lucy said, "Daisy is being disgusting! We don't want to play together anymore!" Daisy looked very sad. Dave said, "We should separate if someone is being unkind, but we should not be mean and hurt each other's feelings."

The girls both thought about this and agreed. They went off to separate parts of the playground, and stayed there for a while.

When it was time for them to go back to the classroom, Lucy and Daisy had learned their lesson about being kind to each other. They hugged and apologized to each other, and went back to enjoy their day together.

Moral of the story: No matter how angry we are, it is never ok to be mean or hurtful to others. We should always choose to separate if things become too uncomfortable, and to learn to be kind instead.

Once upon a time there was a pink spear. It was so shiny that it shone like a sparkly star!

One day a little girl was playing with it. She loved her pink spear very much and wanted to show it to the world.

So, the girl decided to send her pink spear on a special journey. She sent it far away, over the hills and far away.

The wind blew and the sun shined as the pink spear soared through the sky. All the animals cheered as it flew, wishing it a very safe journey.

Finally, the spear arrived at its destination. It had opened a very special door for a very special journey.

The little girl smiled, knowing that her pink spear had been safely sent on its way.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved going to the post office with her mom. One day, they went to the post office to buy stamps. Lily saw a pretty picture and asked her mom if they could buy it. Her mom said, "Yes, we can buy it. It's an original painting." 

Lily was very happy and said, "I want to put it on my wall!" Her mom smiled and said, "We can put it on your wall when we get home." 

As they left the post office, Lily asked her mom, "Can we come back here again?" Her mom replied, "Of course we can. We can come back anytime we want." 

Lily was excited and said, "I love going to the post office with you, Mommy." Her mom hugged her and said, "I love going with you too, Lily."

Once upon a time, there was a brave little girl named Mia. She lived in a small house with her mommy and daddy. In their house, they had a warm fireplace where they liked to sit and talk.

One day, Mia and her mommy were sitting by the fireplace. Mia was playing with her toys and her mommy was knitting. They heard a loud noise outside. Mia looked at her mommy and said, "What was that?" Her mommy said, "I don't know, let's go see."

Mia and her mommy went outside and saw that a big tree had fallen down. It was very close to their house. Mia's mommy told her, "You were so brave to come outside with me. Now, let's go back inside and close the door to stay warm by the fireplace." They went back inside and sat by the fireplace, feeling safe and warm.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. He had a great big bucket. He liked to play with it outside in the sun. One day, he went to the park with his mom.

At the park, Tim met a new friend named Sue. Sue saw Tim's bucket and said, "Wow! That's a great big bucket!" Tim replied, "Thank you! I like to display my toys in it." Sue asked, "Can I play with you and your bucket?" Tim said, "Yes, let's play together!"

They played and had fun with the bucket. They filled it with sand, water, and even leaves. Tim and Sue showed their moms the display of all the things they put in the bucket. The moms were happy to see them playing together. Tim and Sue became best friends and played with the great big bucket every time they went to the park.

Once upon a time, there was a van that left the house. It rolled down the street and around the corner. Inside the van, the man was very fearful. He was scared about where the van was going.

The van rolled faster and faster until it stopped at a big river. The man looked around and saw a long bridge. He was even more fearful because he was scared to cross it.

But then the man saw a boat sailing down the river and so he decided to jump inside and roll away in it. The boat went over the bridge, slowly and safe, and soon it came to a sandy shore.

The man stepped out of the boat and waved goodbye to the boatman. He was no longer fearful, he was happy because he had reached the other side!

One day, Sally was running in the park with her hoop. Suddenly, she saw a cute little squirrel with a long tail. Sally was so excited that she wanted to play with it.

She ran closer and the squirrel stopped. Sally smiled and said, "Hi Squirrel! Can I play with you?" 

The squirrel just looked at her and didn't answer. Then another squirrel came closer, hopped around the first one and then ran away. Sally smiled again and said, "Please, can I play with you?" 

The first squirrel looked at Sally and then hopped to the hoop. Sally was so happy that she clapped her hands and started to play with the squirrel. They played tag with the hoop, hopping around in circles and having lots of fun. 

In the end, they both stopped. Sally thanked the squirrel and ran off home. She had lots of fun playing with her new friend in the park.

Once upon a time, a child named Jane was playing with her marbles. She was so excited to print the beautiful colors on the ground. But something disgusting happened. The marbles started falling into a puddle nearby and their colors began to fade away. Jane thought she would never get them back. 

Suddenly, an old man appeared and he had a magical device in his hand. He explained to Jane that he can make all the colors of the marbles come back to life. Jane was so excited and asked the old man to print the colors of all her marbles. 

The old man waved his magical device over the puddle and the colors slowly started to come back. Jane was jumping and screaming with joy. The colors of the marbles were even brighter and more beautiful than before. 

From then on, Jane was always careful not to put her marbles in any disgusting puddles. She was very happy that the old man could make all the colors come back to life.

Once upon a time, there was a tire. It was old and wobbled down the street. It was busy, spinning around and around. A little girl named Jenny stepped outside to see what was happening. She was so surprised! 

The old tire had come to life and started to dance and twirl across the street. Its movement was graceful, like a dancer. Jenny giggled and clapped her hands with excitement.

The tire suddenly stopped. It jumped up and down, then rolled away. It was gone. 

Jenny ran back inside to tell her mom what she had seen. Her mom smiled and said, "It sounds like you just saw a magical tire!" She thanked the tire for surprising Jenny. 

Jenny was so excited! She would never forget the special surprise the tire had given her.

Once upon a time, there was a little fish. The fish liked to swim in the big blue sea. One day, the fish saw something new. It was a spark in the water. The fish wanted to see the spark up close.

Every day, the fish and the baby jellyfish would swim and play in the sea. They had lots of fun. The fish would swim fast, and the baby jellyfish would follow. The fish and the baby jellyfish were very happy. And they were the best of friends.

Once there was a bird that lived in a nest. The nest was a very special one, it was made out of sticks and twigs. One day the bird noticed that his nest was not in the best shape. It was cracked and broken, so the bird decided to repair it.

The bird worked hard to fix his nest. He carefully gathered the extra twigs, sticks, and feathers and placed them one by one in the cracks. After a while he had repaired the whole nest. He was so proud of his work!

The bird was now very cheerful. He spent all day sitting in his nest, looking at the beautiful view of the sky. He was so happy and content that he sang a song to celebrate his nest and his accomplishment of repairing it. 

From then on, the bird always felt satisfied and safe in his nest, and was always happy and cheerful.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was very eager to see her grandma, who lived far away. One day, Lily's mom said they were going to visit grandma soon. Lily was so happy and started to jump up and down with joy. 

When they arrived at grandma's house, Lily couldn't wait to see her. She ran to the door and knocked. Grandma opened the door and gave Lily a big hug. Lily was so happy to see her grandma, she couldn't stop smiling. 

Later, when it was time to go home, Lily said goodbye to her grandma and promised to visit again soon. Grandma replied, "I can't wait to see you again, Lily." Lily looked back and waved goodbye with a big smile on her face.

John had a twin brother, Adam. They loved to play together every day and they always shared their toys. John was a generous twin and always let Adam have the first turn. One day, they went to the park and Adam had an idea. He said, "Let's play a game! We'll find something to stare at and then see who can stare the longest." John agreed and they each looked around the park until they found something to stare at.

Adam spotted a bird and chose the bird as their target. They both started to stare. Adam thought he was winning, but John was determined to be the winner. He kept on his focusing. He didn't blink once. Finally, after what felt like hours, Adam looked away and gave up. John had won the game! Adam was surprised and clapped for his brother in admiration. He said, "You won because you were generous with me. Thank you for sharing this game with me, John." John and Adam hugged and headed off home after a fun day.

One day, two kids were playing at the park. They wanted to do something special and unusual.

The first kid said, "Let's attach a rocket to a playground swing!"

The second kid replied, "That sounds fun! Let's try it!"

So the two kids ran to the playground to get a rocket and a swing. They attached the rocket to the swing and the swing started to move very fast.

The kids shouted in excitement as they flew over the park. It was an unusual experience and they were so happy.

When it was time to go home, the kids said goodbye to each other with huge smiles on their faces. They had so much fun on their unusual adventure.

Once upon a time, there were two best friends, George and Tim. George and Tim loved to go on adventures together. One day, George and Tim decided to cross a bridge to seek a new adventure.

As George and Tim began to cross the bridge, George felt very uncomfortable. He could feel fear bubbling up inside of him. But, Tim was brave and kept going! 

Halfway across the bridge, Tim stopped and turned to George. "Why are you not coming, George?" he asked. 

George replied, "I'm scared! I don't like this bridge." 

Tim put his arm around George and said, "It's ok, my friend. I will be here for you." George then knew that he could be brave and keep going.

Soon, they had made it to the other side of the bridge! But, George was very relieved when they arrived. They both hugged each other and laughed with joy, while George still had a few tears in his eyes. 

"Let's never cross this uncomfortable bridge again," said George. 

Tim smiled and said, "Agreed!"

Once upon a time there lived a girl named Jane. Jane loved ice cream and dreamed of having it every day.

One day, she saw a sign that said, "Cheap ice cream here!" Jane was so happy that she ran to the store. She got her mom to buy her a cone of ice cream, which she ate quickly.

That night, she dreamed of going back to the store and having another cone of ice cream.

The next day, Jane returned to the store and asked her mom to buy her another cone of ice cream. Her mom smiled and happily obliged.

Jane happily licked her creamy cone and said, "Thanks for getting me my ice cream, mommy!" 

Her mom replied, "You're welcome, Jane! It's so nice to see you enjoy it so much!"

Lily and Tom are friends. They like to play in the park. They see a big slide. It is wide and shiny. Lily wants to go first.

"Can I go first, Tom?" Lily asks.

"OK, Lily. You can go first. But be careful. The slide is fast," Tom says.

Lily nods and climbs up the ladder. She sits on the slide and holds on tight. She feels the wind in her hair. She goes down very fast. She is happy.

"Wow, that was fun!" Lily says when she reaches the bottom. She jumps off the slide and runs to Tom. She shakes his hand. "Your turn, Tom!"

Tom smiles and climbs up the ladder. He sits on the slide and lets go. He goes down very fast, too. He is happy.

"Wow, that was fun!" Tom says when he reaches the bottom. He jumps off the slide and runs to Lily. He shakes her hand. "That was easy!"

Lily and Tom laugh. They hug each other. They are good friends. They like to play in the park. They like the wide slide. It is fun and easy.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. He loved to throw his toy ball. One day, Tim went to a theater with his mom and dad. He was very excited. At the theater, he saw a big girl named Sally. Sally had a toy ball too. Tim felt jealous of Sally's ball because it was bigger and brighter.

Tim said to Sally, "Can I throw your ball?" Sally said, "No, it's mine." Tim was sad. He wanted to throw the big ball. But then, he had an idea. He told Sally, "If you let me throw your ball, you can throw my ball too."

Sally liked the idea. So, they both threw each other's balls and had lots of fun. They became good friends. Tim learned that sharing can make everyone happy.

Once there was a naughty boy called Tim. He loved to cook, but he was always a bit careless when he did it. One day, as he was cooking, he spilt some lotion into the food. Suddenly, the food tasted strange and Tim felt very silly. He quickly cleaned up the mess and made some more food that turned out delicious. From then on, he was extra careful to not let lotion get into his food.

Once upon a time, there was a big purple bear. The bear loved to have picnics in the park. One sunny day, he decided to invite his friends to a picnic. He was very excited.

The purple bear wanted to write a note to his friends. He found a pen and some paper. He wrote, "Come to my picnic! Love, Purple Bear." He gave the notes to his friends, the red bird, the blue dog, and the yellow cat.

On the day of the picnic, the purple bear and his friends met at the park. They had yummy food like apples, cookies, and juice. They played games and had a lot of fun. The purple bear was so happy that he wrote a thank you note to his friends. They all had a great time at the picnic.

Tommy was playing in the park when he saw something. It was a bug! Tommy had never seen a bug before and he was so excited. He wanted to touch the bug, but the bug was shaking. He could tell it was scared. 

"It's ok little bug," said Tommy in a gentle voice. "I won't hurt you." He reached out his finger, but the bug shook more than before. 

Suddenly, a harsh voice said, "Leave the bug alone, Tommy." It was Tommy's mom. "That bug is shaking because it is scared. You can look at it, but don't touch it." 

Tommy understood and watched the bug shuffling away. He waved goodbye and said, "Bye bye little bug."

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He loved to run and play outside. One day, he saw a fancy hat in the park. He picked it up and put it on his head. He felt very special wearing it.

As he jogged around the park, he saw a group of kids playing a game. They asked him to join, and he happily agreed. Timmy was very good at the game and soon he was leading the group. Everyone was having fun and laughing.

Suddenly, Timmy saw a man walking towards them. He looked very angry. Timmy remembered his mom telling him not to talk to strangers. He quickly led the group away from the man and back to their parents. They all thanked Timmy for keeping them safe. From that day on, Timmy always remembered to be careful and never talk to strangers.

Bob was playing near the pool when he said, "I'm going to dive in!" His dad said, "All right, but be careful and don't go too deep!" Bob smiled and said, "I will!" He took a deep breath and dove into the water. 

Bob swam down to the very bottom, where he saw a strange chamber. He peered inside, and it was full of sparkly rocks! Bob swam as fast as he could and gathered up as many as he could fit into his hands. 

Then he heard his dad's voice. "Bob, come back up! It's time to get out of the pool!" Bob quickly put the rocks in his pocket and dove up to the surface. He smiled at his dad, and then ran off to play with his friends.

Once upon a time there was a young bear. His name was Bob and he loved to play in the forest. He was always running around chasing bees and butterflies, and the other animals admired him for his energy and spirit.

One day, Bob decided to take a nap under a big tree. He curled up in a comfortable spot, and he dozed off.

While he was sleeping, he had a wonderful dream. He saw himself swimming in a clear lake with his friends, and playing tag around the trees. Suddenly, the dream ended. Bob woke up and realized he had been dreaming for a long time.

He yawned a tiny bear yawn, stood up and stretched, and he smiled to himself. Bob had had a great nap, and he set off to explore the forest once again.

Once upon a time there was a generous man who lived in a big house. Every morning he went out to the garden and admired all the flowers. He loved to sit in the garden and enjoy the warm sunshine.

One day, the man saw something in the garden that he didn't recognise. It was a tiny wrap with a bow on the top. He knew that there must be something special inside. He carefully opened the wrap and found a big chocolate cake!
 
The man was so happy. He admired the cake for a long time and then he went inside his house to find a plate for the cake.

He called his neighbour, a little girl named Eva. He said to her, "Eva, I have a very special treat for you. Would you like a piece of this delicious cake?"

Eva was so happy, she had never seen such a generous man before. She said, "Yes, please! I would love to have some cake."

The man cut the cake and gave a big piece to Eva. She ate it and thanked him for being so generous.

Once upon a time, there was a big forest. In the forest, there was a wild lion. The lion was very hungry and wanted to eat something tasty. So, he went to a nearby farm where he saw a cow. The lion thought the cow looked delicious, so he tried to catch it. But the farmer saw the lion and quickly came to serve the lion some beef. The lion was happy and ate the beef instead of the cow. From that day on, the lion visited the farmer every time he was hungry, and the farmer always served him beef.

Once upon a time there was a girl who wanted to explore. She wanted to go on an adventure, to discover the world.

So she decided to take a walk in the playground. She saw a bee buzzing around the flowers. She watched the bee for a while and soon discovered that the bee was very busy pollinating the flowers.

The girl was so amazed by what she saw, she decided to tell her friends. Everyone had their own opinion on the bee's work, but no one was sure why it was so busy.

The girl decided to find out more. She followed the bee around the playground and soon discovered that the bee was collecting pollen to take back to its hive. 

The girl went home with a happy heart and a new understanding of the bees busy life.

Once upon a time there was a baby who had two legs. They were colorful like a rainbow. One day, the baby was playing in the garden and running around when he fell. He was sad because his leg had hurt when he fell.

He started to cry until his mommy came over to help him. She picked him up and hugged him tight. He felt better and stopped crying.

Mommy then took him inside and put a bandage on his leg. She told him to be careful and said, "Be sure to look where you are walking next time!" This made the baby smile.

His mommy also made him a new colorful toy to play with. The toy cheered him up, and he was no longer sad. He thanked his mommy and they hugged again.

The baby now always looks where he's going when he's playing in the garden. He's learned that it's important to be careful so he doesn't fall again.

Once upon a time there was a little boy called Joe. Joe was 3 years old.
Every night, he loved to snuggle up on the sofa and read stories with his lamp. His lamp was the most special thing to him, as it lit up all his unknown adventures.

One day, Joe went to his room with his lamp. He was excited for what he would discover. Suddenly, he heard a noise coming from outside his window. It was two birds, teasing each other! Joe wondered what they were saying, he wished he could understand them.

The birds teased each other for a while, until Joe heard one of the birds say "the lamp is for Joe!"

Joe suddenly realised that the two birds were trying to help him. He thanked them for the advice and looked around his room for the lamp. Right there, by his bed, he found the unknown lamp that he had been searching for. 

He smiled and turned on the lamp. It lit up Joe's room and gave him a sense of comfort. Joe had found his own little world, thanks to the help of the two birds.

The End.

Mama and papa were busy in the kitchen. Mama had a bowl in her hands, and she was stirring something with a spoon. Papa had a bowl, too. He was adding something to it.

"What are you preparing?" asked Mama. 

"I am making a mild whip," said Papa.

Mama smiled. She added some more of the ingredients to her bowl. 

"Let's see who can make a better whip!" said Papa. 

Mama finished preparing the ingredients in her bowl, while Papa stirred his ingredients until they were all combined. 

When they were both done, Mama put the bowl in the oven, and Papa whipped up the contents of his bowl. 

The whip was light and fluffy. Papa tasted it and smiled. 

"This is so mild," said Papa. 

Mama smiled, too. They had both prepared a delicious and mild whip!

Once upon a time, there was a famous snack. It was a yummy cookie. Everyone loved it. The cookie was sweet and tasty. It was the best snack in the town.

One day, a little boy named Tim wanted to taste the famous snack. He asked his mom for the cookie. His mom said, "Yes, you can have the cookie." Tim was very happy.

Tim took a big bite of the cookie. It tasted so good! He shared the cookie with his friends. They all loved the famous snack. They played and ate the cookie together. It was a fun day.

One day there was a hairy monster. He was so hairy that he had trouble seeing through all of his hair. He wanted to organize his hair, so he looked around for something he could use. Suddenly he saw a scarf on the table. He picked it up, and the scarf was so soft and colorful.

The monster wrapped the scarf around his head. It was so comfortable and he could finally see through the hair! He was so happy! He liked his new look so much that he wore the scarf everywhere. He even took it in the rain and it still looked great!

The monster was so pleased with his new scarf. He could organize all of his hairy hair, and it was beautiful! The monster was very proud of his scarf and he was glad that he had found it. He would never forget the day he organized his hair with the scarf.

Sam and Jen were best friends. They liked to play in the park with their toys. Sam had a red car that could zoom very fast. Jen had a pink bike that she could jog on. They had fun racing each other and making noises.

One day, they saw a big dog in the park. It was black and furry and had sharp teeth. It barked loud and ran after them. Sam and Jen were scared. They tried to get away, but the dog was faster. It caught up with Sam and bit his car. The car broke into pieces and stopped zooming. Sam cried and dropped his car. Jen stopped her bike and ran to him.

"Are you okay, Sam?" Jen asked. She hugged him and looked at his car. It was dead. It could not zoom anymore.

"I'm sorry, Jen. I should have listened to you. You told me not to zoom too close to the dog. But I wanted to win the race. I was silly and mean." Sam said. He felt bad and sorry.

"It's okay, Sam. I forgive you. You are my friend. But you have to be careful and kind. The dog was angry and scared. He did not like us zooming and jogging near him. He wanted to be left alone. We have to respect other animals and people." Jen said. She was wise and nice.

Sam and Jen learned a lesson. They said sorry to the dog and gave him a bone. The dog wagged his tail and licked their faces. He was happy and friendly. They played with him and their toys. They zoomed and jogged together, but not too fast or loud. They had fun and were safe.

One day there was a little girl. She liked to go for walks. She liked to look at all the things around her. She was very alert and noticed a interesting building across the street. It was big and made of glass. The little girl decided to go over and take a closer look.

She saw a big sign that said "office". There were lots of people walking in and out. The little girl could see they were all busy with their work. She watched them until it was time to go home.

When the little girl was walking home it had started to get very hot. The sun was shining very bright and it was melting the snow on the ground. The little girl could feel her shoes getting very warm. 

When the little girl got home she was happy and excited to tell everybody about her day. She was alert in noticing the office across the street and delighted that the sun melted the snow!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her puzzle toys. One day, she was playing with her puzzle when a piece vanished.

Lily asked her mom, "Where did the puzzle piece go?"

"I'm not sure, Lily," her mom said. "Let's look for it together."

They looked all over the room, but they couldn't find the missing piece. Lily was sad because she couldn't finish her puzzle. But then, her mom had an idea.

"I have a reliable friend who can help us," her mom said.

They called the friend and she came over to help. She searched the room and finally found the missing puzzle piece under the couch. Lily was so happy that her puzzle was complete again. She thanked her mom and her mom's reliable friend for helping her find the missing piece.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there lived a little girl named Lily and her mom. One day, Lily got sick. She felt hot and her throat hurt. Her mom was worried.

Mom gave Lily some medicine to make her feel better. Lily didn't like the taste, but she took it anyway. After a while, she started to feel good again.

Lily said, "Thank you, Mom, for the medicine." Mom smiled and hugged Lily. They were both happy that Lily felt better. From that day on, they always said "thank you" when someone helped them.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Sarah. She was very curious and always asking questions. One day Sarah asked her mommy, "What is a stage?"

Her mommy smiled and said, "A stage is a place where people act out pretend stories."

Sarah smiled and asked, "What do you mean by pretend?"

Her mommy explained, "Pretend means fake. It means that people are pretending to be someone they are not." Sarah thought this was very exciting and asked if she could act out a pretend story too. Her mommy said yes and the two of them worked together to make up a pretend story to act out. 

Sarah loved it! She used her hands and her feet and her voice to pretend to be a princess. She felt so proud of herself for creating a make-believe world to explore.

That night before she went to bed, Sarah asked her mommy if they could do pretend stories again tomorrow. Her mommy smiled and said, "Of course, my sweet. Pretend stories are loads of fun!"

Molly was a busy bee. She was always alert and ready for an adventure. But today Molly had a very special mission. She needed to find a needle. 

She had heard that the needle was large and shiny. So Molly began to look for it near the pond. Sure enough, she found it!

Molly was so happy. But she knew she couldn't just leave the needle there. It needed to be replaced by something else. So she looked around and found a big rock. 

Molly carefully put the rock in the spot where she had found the needle. There! It was done. Now no one would trip over the needle. 

Molly smiled to herself and happily went on her way. She felt proud knowing she had done something to help others.

One day, a boy and his mom lay together on a beach. They watched as big white sails floated on the light blue ocean. They watched the sails all day and had lots of fun. 
The boy said, "Mom, can I go sailing?" Mom said, "Yes, you can go sailing." 
So, the boy went out. He walked down to a boat and saw a light sail. It was so light that he could lift it up by himself! He put the sail in the boat and jumped in too.

The boy pushed the boat out and got into it. He grabbed the sail, and it floated him away. He watched the light sky above, the sail flapping in the wind. Then, he sailed around the ocean all day long. 

When the day was over, the boy and his sail were back on the beach, where he had first begun. Mom was waiting, and she hugged him tight. She said, "I am glad you had a fun day of sailing." The boy smiled and said, "Yes, it was light and fun!"

Once upon a time, two best friends had a plan. They wanted to have a fun time together, so they decided to go to the movie.

But it was a rough day at the movie. One friend wanted to watch a scary movie, while the other wanted to watch a funny one. They fought over their different ideas and ended up leaving the movie early and mad at each other.

The two sad friends thought and thought. They finally realised that they should have each respected the other's opinion. They should have listened and planned together before deciding which movie to watch.

The two friends hugged each other and learned a very important lesson. When you plan with your friends, it is more fun when everyone is included in the decision.

Once upon a time, there was a boy who loved to play games. Every time he won a game, he was given a trophy to show off to his friends. One day, the boy was playing a game and he was determined to win a trophy. Even when it was difficult, he tried not to resist. He kept playing and in the end, he won a shiny trophy! The boy was so happy. 

The next day, the boy wanted to try another game. But this one was a little too hard for him. He wanted to win another trophy, but he found this game too tough! After trying for a while, he wanted to give up. But he remembered the mild feeling of winning the trophy, and he resisted his urge to quit. After more practice, he finally won his second shiny trophy! 

The boy was so proud of himself. He had resisted the urge to give up, and now he had two trophies to show his friends. He proudly displayed his trophies in his room, so he could always remember how he had resisted and won!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy. His name was Tom. Tom was 3 years old and liked to play in the garden.
One day, Tom wanted to eat a pizza. He asked his mum to make one and she did! But when he touched it, it was all sticky.
Tom's mum told him he had to wash his hands before eating the pizza. Tom liked washing his hands, so he ran to the bathroom and grabbed the pink soap. He put some of the soap on his hands and washed them in the tap. 
After he had washed them, Tom rushed back outside. He was so excited to eat the pizza! But when he opened the box, he noticed something scary inside. It was a big spider! 
Tom was a bit scared, but he remembered that his mum had told him not to be afraid of spiders. So he bravely said: "It's OK little spider. You can stay if you want".
The spider crawled away, and Tom got to eat his pizza. He was so happy!

John and his mom went to the store. John saw a lot of things he wanted, but his mom said they could only get one. He wanted ice cream, but his mom said it wasn't lunchtime yet. He thought for a long minute and then he mentioned ice. His mom smiled and said that sounded like a good idea! 

John was so excited. He got a bowl of colorful ice cubes. He liked them because they were so cold. He also liked the warm syrup that he could pour over the ice. His mom got him a spoon and he started eating away. He was so happy to have something different for lunch. 

Later that day, John told his friends about his lunch of ice cubes and syrup. He told them how cold and tasty the ice cubes were and how warm and sweet the syrup was. All of his friends wanted to have ice cubes and syrup for lunch too!

Mama and Sparkle were on a tour. Sparkle was very excited. She clapped her hands and said "Yay! I'm so happy". Mama took Sparkle's hand and invited her to look around. Everywhere they looked, they saw people walking, laughing and chatting.

They finally stopped at a pond. Mama said "Look, Sparkle! It's so pretty". Sparkle squealed with delight. There were ducks swimming in the pond and some of them were eating bread. Sparkle couldn't wait to feed them. 

Mama asked Sparkle if she wanted to give the ducks some bread, and Sparkle nodded eagerly. Mama took out a handful of bread and spread it on the water. The ducks happily gathered them up. 

But as time went on, the water started to get dry. Sparkle was sad. Just then, a little girl came and brought a bucket of water to refill the pond. Sparkle was so happy that the pond was filled again with water. Mama and Sparkle waved at the little girl as she walked away.

Tom and Lily were playing in the garden. They liked to dig holes and find worms and bugs. They also liked to pick flowers and make bouquets for their mom.

One day, they found a big pink flower that smelled very nice. They wanted to take it home and put it in a vase. But when they tried to pull it out, they saw that the stem was brown and soft. It was rotting.

"Yuck!" Tom said. "This flower is bad. It is rotting. We can't take it home."

Lily was upset. She liked the pink flower. She wanted to keep it. She started to cry.

"Don't cry, Lily," Tom said. "We can find another flower. A good flower. A flower that is not rotting."

He looked around and saw a yellow flower that was bright and happy. He picked it and gave it to Lily.

"Here, Lily. This is for you. A yellow flower. It is not rotting. It is good. Do you like it?"

Lily stopped crying. She smiled and took the yellow flower. She smelled it and hugged Tom.

"Thank you, Tom. I like the yellow flower. It is good. You are a good brother."

They ran back to their mom and showed her their flowers. She smiled and hugged them.

"You are good children," she said. "I love your flowers. And I love you."

Tom likes to swing on the big swing in the park. He swings high and low, and feels happy. He likes to see the sky and the trees and the birds.

One day, he sees a fireman in the park. The fireman is dirty, because he has been fighting a fire. He has a big hose and a big truck. Tom thinks the fireman is cool. He wants to talk to him and see his hose and truck.

But the fireman is busy. He has to water the flowers in the park, because they are dry and sad. He does not have time to play with Tom. He tells Tom to stay away from the hose and the truck, because they are not toys.

Tom feels sad and angry. He wants to play with the fireman. He thinks the fireman is mean. He decides to swing higher and higher, and then jump off the swing. He thinks he can fly like a bird.

But he is wrong. He cannot fly like a bird. He falls to the ground and hurts his knee. He cries and cries. He wishes he had listened to the fireman.

The fireman hears Tom crying. He runs to him and helps him. He puts a bandage on his knee and gives him a hug. He tells him he is sorry he was busy, and that he can play with him later. He shows him his hose and his truck, and lets him sit inside. He tells him he is brave and smart, and that he can be a fireman when he grows up.

Tom feels happy again. He says thank you to the fireman, and tells him he is cool. He learns a new word: fireman. He swings on the swing again, but not too high. He smiles and sings a song.

Once upon a time, there was a big lake. In the lake, there was a fish named Sam. Sam was a foolish fish. He liked to play and swim all day.

One day, Sam saw a boy. The boy was writing on paper. Sam thought it was fun. He wanted to write too. But he was a fish, and fish can't write.

Sam asked his friend, the duck, to help him. The duck took a stick and wrote in the mud. Sam was happy. He learned that even a foolish fish can have fun with friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little pan. The pan was very dry. It lived in a small house with a kind girl named Lily. Lily liked to keep her pan clean and dry.

One day, it rained outside. The pan was scared it would get wet. Lily saw the pan and said, "Don't worry, pan. I will keep you dry." She put the pan in a safe place, away from the rain. The pan was happy and thanked Lily.

After the rain stopped, the sun came out. Lily took the pan outside to play. They played all day and had lots of fun. The pan stayed dry, and Lily kept it safe. They were best friends, and they lived happily ever after.

Jimmy was hungry and he wanted to go out for dinner. He asked his mommy if they could go to a restaurant. She said yes and they went out. 

When they arrived at the restaurant, Jimmy was amazed. He saw a big building with gray walls and a few doors. He wanted to go inside, but his mommy said they needed to kneel first. 

Jimmy kneeled and prayed with his mommy. After they finished, they went in.

The restaurant was full of delicious foods. Jimmy was so excited! He saw burgers, fries and ice cream. He ordered a burger and fries. He also ordered some ice cream to go. 

After they ate, they said goodbye to the restaurant and went home. Jimmy had a fun day out with his mommy and he was very full.

Once there was a bunny who lived in a mine. He was a very happy bunny who loved to eat carrots. One day, he was hopping around the mine when he saw something that he had never seen before. It was a big monster! The bunny was scared and wanted to run away.

He asked the monster what it was doing there. The monster said it was looking for gold. The bunny warned the monster to be careful, because the mine was very dark and scary. The monster said it wasn't scared and hopped in.

The bunny shook his head, thinking the monster was being stupid. A few minutes later, he heard a loud bang from inside the mine. The bunny ran over to see what had happened. The monster had fallen down a hole, and was stuck!

The bunny warned the monster that this would happen if it wasn't careful. In the end, the bunny had to help the monster out of the hole. After that, the bunny decided it was best to stay away from the mine.

Once upon a time there was a kind, compassionate man who went to the market each day. He wanted to fill his bag with lots of food to share with others in need.

When he arrived, he saw a boy. The boy was very small and sad. The compassionate man stopped and asked him what was wrong. The boy explained that he was very hungry and had no food to eat.

The kind man smiled and filled his bag with fruits and vegetables from the market. He then handed it to the boy and the boy's eyes lit up with joy.

The compassionate man said, "Eat this food and stay healthy." Then he waved goodbye as he continued on his way.

The boy was so thankful. He was full of happiness from the kind man's gift. And the market was filled with the joy of giving!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved going to the museum with her mommy and daddy. They would see lots of cool things like big dinosaurs and shiny rocks.

One day, Lily saw a pretty vase in the museum. She wanted to touch it, but her mommy said no. Lily was nervous because she really wanted to touch it. 

A man came up to them and said, "Would you like to see a special part of the museum?" Lily's mommy said yes, but Lily was still nervous. 

The man took them to a room with lots of expensive things. Lily saw the pretty vase again and she couldn't resist. She touched it and it broke into a million pieces. The man got angry and Lily and her family had to pay lots of money to fix it. Lily felt sad and her mommy said, "We should have listened and never touched things in the museum."

Once upon a time there was a powerful jellyfish called Louie. He swam in the sea and he loved to listen to the waves. 

One day, Louie heard something different. It was a voice, calling out to him. "Louie, I need help," it said.

Louie was scared at first but then he decided to listen. He swam as close as he could and he saw a little girl. 

"My kite is stuck in the tree. Will you help me get it back?" asked the girl. 

Louie was powerful and brave, so he said yes. He swam as fast as he could to help the little girl. He used all his power to move the kite down from the tree. 

The little girl was so happy that she gave Louie a big hug. Louie was so grateful and thanked her kindly. They said goodbye and Louie swam away, happy that he had helped.

Once upon a time there were two peanuts who were very different. One peanut was small and round. The other was big and long. One day, the small peanut said to the big peanut, â€œLet's go on an adventure!â€ 

The peanuts went far away and found a big, empty bowl. The small peanut said, â€œLet's fill it up with something special!â€ 

The big peanut got very excited and said, â€œI know! Let's fill it with lots and lots of peanuts!â€

So the two peanuts filled the bowl with all different kinds of peanuts. Some were big, some small. Some were round, some were long. 

When the bowl was full, the two peanuts proudly looked at their work. Then, the small peanut said, â€œThis looks yummy. Let's eat them all up!â€ 

And so they did! The two peanuts had a great time eating the different kinds of peanuts until their bowl was empty. 

The end.

Once upon a time, in a land far away, there lived a little boy who loved to play. His name was Phil and every day, he made his home more bright and gay.

One evening, Phil was out looking for fun; he followed a rabbit past the setting sun. As night approached, Phil began to despair, he wondered how he would get home from there.

Suddenly, Phil heard a loud noise. He looked around and saw a fire! He was scared, but he wanted to enjoy the rare sight, and stayed there all night. 

Phil watched the flames and repeated to himself, "I'm so brave, I'm not scared of this." Then he heard a voice calling, "Phil! Come back here and we'll make you a nice meal!" 

Phil ran back and saw his mom, holding a plate full of food. He smiled and said, "Thanks mom! I knew you'd come find me!" His mom gave him a hug and said, "No matter what happens, I'll always repeat that I will come find you!"

One day, a little boy named Tim was playing outside. He saw a big, disgusting bug. Tim was scared, but he wanted to look at the bug. The bug did not move. It remained still.

Tim asked the bug, "Why are you not moving?" The bug said, "I am trying to have a dream. I want to dream about flying high in the sky." Tim thought that was a good dream to have.

Tim said, "I will help you." He picked up the bug and put it on a leaf. The bug closed its eyes and started to dream. Tim was happy that he could help the bug have a dream.

Once there was a girl named Sally who loved to dance. She was always moving around her house, singing and dancing. One night when Sally was dancing, her mom came in and put her to bed.

Before Sally went to sleep, she thought about dancing and imagined a peaceful place where she could dance forever. She closed her eyes and imagined a beautiful place full of trees and flowers. In the middle of the forest was a big, open grassy area where Sally could do her favorite dance.

Sally knew that if she slept well, she would be able to go to her peaceful place and dance the next day. So she went to sleep feeling peaceful and happy. 

In the morning, Sally got to dance in her secret place. She moved around, twirling and jumping, smiling and laughing. As she danced, a warm breeze made her dance even more and she felt a peaceful feeling inside her heart. 

Sally danced until she was tired and then she hugged herself and said: "I love to dance in my peaceful place, it makes me feel so happy."

Molly was a happy girl. Every morning, she stepped out of her house and into the warm sun. On this day, the sky was grey. Molly looked up, and saw rain. It started to sprinkle, so Molly quickly stepped back inside. She watched from the window as the rain came down heavier and harder.

Molly felt sad. She wanted to go outside and play, but the rain kept coming. Her mom came over, and said, "Don't be sad, Molly. The rain will go away soon." She put her arms around Molly, and said, "The rain will stop, I promise. Let's be honest and have a tea party instead."

Molly smiled. She liked the idea of a tea party. She quickly stepped into the kitchen and started to get ready. She set the table and put on her favorite dress.

Molly and her mom drank tea and ate cookies. They talked and laughed together. The rain kept pouring down outside. But instead of being sad, Molly and her mom enjoyed their honest tea party together. Eventually, the rain stopped and Molly stepped outside to play with her friends.

Once upon a time, there was a brave little girl named Nora. She liked to play in the park with her friends, and she wanted to be the best at everything she did.

One day, Nora was playing a game where her group was trying to climb a purple tree. Everyone had fun, but Nora wanted to be the first one to reach the top. She tried very hard to reach above the rest, but she kept slipping and sliding down.

"I can't do it," said Nora, starting to weep. 

Her friends all gathered around her and said, "It's okay if you can't do it; success isn't always about winning."

Nora smiled at all of them and tried one last time, and this time she reached the top! Everyone cheered for her and she felt very proud of herself.

Nora learned that day that it's okay not to be the best at everything, and that success isn't about winning. Sometimes, it's just about trying your best.

Once there was a girl named Lucy. She was only three years old, but she loved to design things. She always used her imagination and built beautiful things.

One day, Lucy saw a squash. She wanted to design something with it. She took her favourite pieces of coloured paper and scissors and started cutting shapes out of the paper. She was very persistent, and she wouldn't give up until she had a finished design.

When she was done, she showed her design to her mummy. She said, "Mummy, look at my design! I made it with the squash!"

Mummy was very proud of Lucy and said, "That is a wonderful design! You are so clever and persistent."

Lucy smiled and said, "Yay! I love making designs!"

Once upon a time there was a mighty world. In this world lived many kind animals. One of the animals, a cheezy, was always behaving well. He helped his friends and was always very polite.

One day, the cheezy had the chance to explore the world. He hopped on a big, green bus and went on a long journey. Everywhere he went, he showed how mighty he was by behaving well and always saying 'hello' to the other animals that he met.

The cheezy eventually returned home with lots of stories to tell. All the other animals were amazed by his tales. They all learnt from the cheezy's travels and promised themselves that they too would behave mighty and explore the world for themselves one day. 

The cheezy had shown them that being kind and behaving well could take you on wild and wonderful adventures.

Once upon a time there was a small boy living deep in a forest. One day he happened upon a small pond and decided to take a look. The boy saw something he didn't recognize and he was curious. He walked closer and peered in. He saw a fish, swimming around happily in the water. 

The boy squinted and spoke to the fish. "What are you?" he asked. The fish replied, "I'm a fish, silly! Can't you tell?"

The boy shook his head. "What do you need to live?" he asked.

The fish answered, "I need oxygen and tasty food."

The boy thought for a moment and then he grinned. He recognized that the fish was a living creature, just like him. He waved at the fish and said goodbye before running off to explore some more.

Once upon a time, there was a bird. Each afternoon, the bird tried to build its home. The bird wanted to make a cozy nest in a tree. 

The first day, the bird collected sticks from the ground. But it was hard work, and the bird soon got frustrated. 

The next afternoon, the bird tried again. This time, the bird found some leaves to make the nest even cozier. 

But then the rain came, and the breeze blew the nest apart. The bird was very sad and frustrated. 

The bird looked up at the sky and said, "Who will help me build my nest?" 

The bird tried again and again, but it couldn't make the nest stay together. No matter what the bird tried, the nest wouldn't stay put. The bird was so frustrated that it eventually gave up. 

The bird never got to live in its cozy nest. And it was a very sad ending.

Once upon a time, there was a big cop named Bob. Bob was very strong and he helped people in the town. One day, Bob saw a magic trick. A rabbit disappeared! Bob was amazed. He looked around but he couldn't find the rabbit. 

Bob asked the magician how he did the trick. The magician said he couldn't tell Bob because it was a secret. Bob was sad because he wanted to know how the rabbit disappeared. 

The next day, Bob went to the magic shop and bought a magic kit. He practiced and practiced until he could make things disappear too! Bob was so happy that he could do magic tricks. He showed everyone in the town and they were amazed, just like Bob was when he saw the rabbit disappear.

Once there was a pink elephant. She wanted to know how much she weighed, so she went to the scale to find out. She was so excited to learn she weighed a lot! But when she stepped off the scale, an alarm went off. It was so loud that the pink elephant screamed and ran away. She was so scared that she never went back to the scale again. 

The end.

Once upon a time there was a black infant. He rested in his crib all day and watched the world outside his window. Every day he saw old birds flying in the sky and young children playing in the grass. Every night he heard the night creatures stirring in the darkness.

One day the infant decided he wanted to explore outside his window. He pushed his way out of the crib and flopped into the grass below. He was amazed by the world around him. Everything seemed so big and he was so small.

He rested near a tree and looked up in the sky. He saw a blackbird flying above him and then he noticed a yellow butterfly fluttering near his face. He reached out to touch it, but it flew away.

The infant watched until the sun began to set. When it was too dark to see he tucked himself back into his crib and closed his eyes. He felt tired and content after his exploration. The night was peaceful and he soon fell asleep, happy to rest after a full day of adventure.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He loved to play outside in the garden. One day, while he was digging in the dirt, he saw a mole. The mole was small and brown, with tiny paws and a long nose.

Timmy wanted to catch the mole, but he didn't want to scare it. So he whispered to the mole, "Don't be afraid, little mole. I won't hurt you." The mole looked up at Timmy with its shiny black eyes and then scurried away.

Timmy was sad that he couldn't catch the mole, but he knew that it was better to let it be. Later that day, Timmy saw something blue in the garden. It was a beautiful butterfly! Timmy smiled and thought to himself, "Maybe the mole whispered to the butterfly to come visit me."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to swim in the pool. One day, she saw a frog in the pool. The frog was very ugly, but Lily was not scared. She dared herself to catch the frog.

Lily slowly swam towards the frog. The frog hopped away, but Lily was quick. She caught the frog in her hands and showed it to her mommy. Her mommy said the frog was not ugly, but cute.

Lily was happy that she caught the frog. She put the frog back in the pool and swam around with it. From that day on, Lily was not scared of any ugly frogs in the pool.

Once upon a time, there was a powerful elephant called Emma. Emma had a very big trunk and she was admired by the other animals in the forest.

One day, Emma was walking through the forest and she found a skull lying on the ground. She was curious and wanted to pick it up.

Suddenly, a voice said "Please leave the skull alone." It was a small mouse who was living in the forest.

The elephant smiled kindly and said "OK. I will leave the skull". She left it there and continued her walk through the forest.

The other animals in the forest were amazed by Emma's actions. She had shown them that it was always important to please others and to show respect.

The moral of the story is: Always be kind and consider the feelings of others before taking any action.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She lived in a house with her mommy and daddy. One day, Lily's mommy asked her to help with dinner. She said, "Lily, can you please put the pot on the stove?" Lily did as she was told and put the pot on the stove.

While the pot was heating up, Lily's daddy came into the kitchen. He looked at Lily and said, "Wow, Lily, you're looking very thin. Are you eating enough?" Lily thought for a moment and then said, "Yes, Daddy. I'm not lying. I eat all my veggies!"

Lily's mommy smiled and said, "That's good to hear, Lily. Now let's finish making dinner!" And they all worked together to make a delicious meal.

Once, there was a little girl called Sophie. Sophie was three years old and she loved playing board games. Every day, she asked her parents to play. But instead, the parents would always tell her: "No, now is not the time to play. We are busy." 

Sophie was very frustrated. 

One day, Sophie went to the store with her parents. She saw a board game that she really wanted. When her parents told her that she couldn't have it, Sophie began to cry. 

Instead, her parents bought her a simple board game that they said they could play together. They became the most dependable team.

Every day, Sophie and her parents played the board game. Soon, Sophie became a dependable player and won every game. 

In the end, Sophie learned that when she was dependable, it was easier to get what she wanted. She was happy that this time, her parents had listened to her and given her something she treasured!

Once upon a time, there was a big lion who lived in a jungle. He liked to roar very loudly, scaring all the other animals. One day, he saw a little mouse who was carrying a pencil. The lion asked the mouse why he was carrying a pencil, but the mouse didn't answer.

The next day, the lion was walking in the jungle when he saw smoke coming from a tree. He got closer and saw that the mouse had started a fire with the pencil. The fire was so hot that the tree started to burn. The lion realized that the mouse had used the pencil to start the fire.

From that day on, the lion and the mouse became friends. The lion promised to never roar at the mouse again, and the mouse promised to only use the pencil for drawing and not starting fires. They lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little duck named Ducky. Ducky loved to swim in the pond with his friends. One day, it started to rain a lot and the pond started to get bigger and bigger. The water was coming so fast that it looked like a big river. Ducky got scared and started to swim faster and faster to get away from the flood.

Ducky's friends were also swimming fast to get away from the flood. They all swam to a big tree and climbed up to stay safe. Ducky was very ashamed because he was the last one to get up the tree. But his friends were happy that he made it.

After the rain stopped, the flood went away and the pond was back to normal. Ducky and his friends were happy to be back in the pond, but they knew they had to be careful when it rained so they wouldn't have to speed away from a flood again.

Once upon a time there was a brave sailor called Tom. He looked and looked but he couldn't find the right ornament to put on his ship. Then he noticed a sparkly one floating in the sea.

He went over to take a closer look, but it was very dangerous. The sea was getting higher and higher and was going to soak him!

Fortunately, Tom was smart and he had an idea. He found a very long stick and used it to get the sparkly ornament. He put it carefully on his ship and it lit up the sky. Everyone was amazed and cheered for Tom.

Tom was so proud of himself! He had saved the day and got the perfect ornament. He and his ship sailed happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a curious little girl named Mia. She loved to wear her favorite skirt and play outside. One day, she saw a big box in her yard. She wanted to know what was inside.

Mia tried to open the box, but it was shut very tight. She pushed and pulled, but the box would not open. Mia felt sad and wondered what to do next. She really wanted to see what was inside the box.

Then, Mia had an idea. She asked her big brother, Tom, to help her. Tom was strong and knew how to open the box. With a big push, the box opened! Inside, they found a new toy to play with. Mia was so happy, and they played together all day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was very curious and loved to explore. One day, she found a birdcage in her backyard. Inside the birdcage was a pretty bird with colorful feathers. The bird was sad and didn't smile.

Lily wanted to make the bird happy, so she brought it some seeds to eat and water to drink. She talked to the bird and sang it a song. Slowly, the bird began to smile and chirp happily.

Lily was so happy that she had made the bird happy. She decided to keep the birdcage in her room so she could take care of the bird every day. From that day on, the bird smiled and sang every day, and Lily was the happiest girl in the world.

Beth had a cheap toy. It was a circle. She held it up and turned it around. She leaned closer to it and watched the colors fall in different places. "Wow!", she said in amazement.

Suddenly, Beth heard a loud noise. She stepped back and leaned against a wall. There, she saw a giant bird flapping its wings. The wings were like circles that made a loud noise as they moved up and down. Beth was scared and started to cry.

But then, the bird leaned its head down to Beth and said, "Do not be scared, little one. I am only here to help you." Beth looked at the bird and smiled. She reached out her hand and touched the bird's beak.

The bird smiled and said, "Now, tell me what you have in your hand?" Beth looked down and said, "It's my cheap toy. It's a circle." The bird nodded his head and said, "Yes, that's right. It will be your best friend forever."

Beth smiled and hugged the bird. She was so happy. She held the cheap circle toy in her hand and the bird gave her lots of love. From that day on, Beth and thebird were the best of friends.

Once upon a time there was a little boy, who was three years old. He was walking in the dark. He was scared and he wondered what he would find.

He heard all sorts of strange noises in the dark. He felt frightened by all he could not see. He heard a loud crunching noise and wondered what it could be.

He kept walking until he saw a big, bright light. He felt happy and ventured closer. He was amazed to find a big, bright star! His fear had vanished and he was no longer frightened. 

The little boy smiled and looked up at the stars. There were so many beautiful lights in the sky. He had never seen anything quite like it before. He thought he would wonder and explore this nighttime view forever.

John and his mom were walking down the sidewalk to the park. John was excited to play but his mom had something special in store.

"When we get to the park, you will see something wonderful," she said.

John had no idea what it could be, and he asked his mom, "What is it?"

But she just smiled and replied, "You'll see!"

When they finally arrived, the park was filled with big, colorful balloons. John was delighted! Suddenly, a loud alarm went off and the balloons rose into the air.

John's mom said, "That's the perfect time for us to make a wish. Make your wish, then let go of the balloon and watch it fly away."

John thought long and hard about his wish. He wished for something perfect and then let go, watching his balloon drift away in the sky. 

John smiled and turned to his mom, "Did you make a wish?" he asked.

She winked and replied, "I already got my wish." 

John looked around, still wondering what his mom had wished for. Then, he saw it: his mom's wish was him, the perfect little boy.

Jessie had a thin guitar. It made him happy to play it. Every day, he would strum the strings and pluck little tunes. One day, however, something strange happened. He felt a tickle in his nose. He paused his playing and then he sneezed! His guitar made a funny noise when he sneezed. He smiled and continued playing, with the guitar sounding slightly different after the sneeze. Jessie kept playing and eventually the strange sound went away. Jessie kept his guitar thin and kept playing delicious melodies every day.

Once there was an ant who wanted to be powerful. He asked all of the animals in the forest how he could be powerful. A fox told him that he could act. The ant asked the fox what he meant by act. The fox said, "Acting is when you pretend to be something else but you don't really change."

The ant was excited. He decided to try it out. He pretended to be a lion. He widened his eyes, put his hands on his hips, and roared like a lion. All of the animals were scared. The ant was proud that he made them all scared.

"I am powerful!" the ant exclaimed. He continued to act like a lion and strutted around the forest. All of the animals kept their distance. The ant was very proud of himself and laughed and smiled.

He had learned that by acting, he could be powerful. He was so happy that he decided to act like a lion every day. Whenever he got scared, he acted like a lion and all the animals in the forest were scared too.

Once upon a time, there was a gray block. It sat on a table all by itself, without any other blocks around. The gray block wanted to find a friend, but it just sat there alone.

One day, it decided to try something. It rolled off the table and onto the floor. At first, it was scared, but then it started to have fun. It rolled around in circles, trying to find someone to be friends with.

Soon, the gray block heard a voice. It was a blue block, calling out to the gray one. The blue block asked if the gray one wanted to play together. The gray block was so excited!

The two blocks played together all afternoon. They raced around the room, built towers with their blocks, and even hugged each other at the end. The gray block was so happy to have found a friend. It had tried, and it worked!

One sunny day, a little girl went for a walk. She saw a big barn in the middle of the field. She was so excited and cheerful that she ran to it. She stopped in front of the barn and grabbed the door handle. Suddenly, she slipped and fell. But she wasn't sad. She laughed and got back up. She opened the barn door and ran inside. It was full of hay and old wheelbarrows. The light in the barn was shining brightly. She felt so cheerful being in the barn. She explored every corner of it and pretended it was her own house. She was so happy. Then, after a while, she ran out of the barn and went back home with a big smile on her face.

Once upon a time, there was a baby named Timmy. Timmy was a happy baby who loved to play with his toys. One day, Timmy's big brother was playing with a ball and accidentally struck Timmy's toy tower. The tower fell down and Timmy got upset.

Timmy's mom saw that he was upset and picked him up. She kissed his forehead and told him it was okay. She helped Timmy build a new tower and they played together until it was time for Timmy's nap. Timmy went to sleep with a smile on his face, happy to have a loving family who cared about him.

Once upon a time, in a small school, there was a green room. In this green room, there was a class of little kids. They liked to play, laugh, and learn new things. Their teacher, Miss Lily, was very kind and loved to teach them.

One day, Miss Lily asked the class a question. She said, "What color is the grass outside?" The kids thought for a moment and then shouted, "Green!" Miss Lily smiled and said, "Good job, everyone!"

The next day, the class went outside to play. They saw the green grass and remembered Miss Lily's question. They were happy that they knew the answer. They played all day on the green grass, and when they went back inside, they told Miss Lily how much fun they had.

Once there was a garden. Every day the guard would come to the garden and spray the flowers. Every flower was so proud, standing tall and happy in the sunshine. The guard was proud of his work, he enjoyed making the garden look pretty.

One day a butterfly flew over the garden. It was a big and colourful butterfly, flying gracefully around the flowers. It was so beautiful that the guard just watched in awe. He was very proud that he had made such a lovely garden.

The guard continued to spray the garden every day, taking extra time to make the flowers look even more beautiful. Soon more and more animals came to the garden. Rabbits, birds and butterflies all fluttered around, taking in the beauty of the garden. The guard smiled, he was so proud of his work.

Once upon a time, there was a long pumpkin. The pumpkin was so long that it reached the sky. One day, a little girl walked by and saw the long pumpkin. She said, "Wow, that pumpkin is so long!"

Suddenly, a naughty boy came and disturbed the pumpkin. The little girl said, "Hey, why did you do that? You shouldn't disturb things that don't belong to you."

The naughty boy said sorry and walked away. The little girl felt happy that the pumpkin was safe. She learned that it's important to respect other people's things and not disturb them. The end.

Once there were two friends, Jack and Jill.
They were playing a game together.
Jack said to Jill, "Let's spin around! It'll be fun!"
Jill was a bit embarrassed because her friends were watching, but she decided to spin around with Jack. 
They both spun very fast in circles.
Suddenly, Jack stopped spinning and he held up a skull he had found! Jill was surprised. 
Jack said, "Look what I found!"
Jill smiled and said, "That's cool!" 
They put the skull down, and the two friends spun around together for a few more times until they were both dizzy and laughed the whole time.

Teddy and his friend, Lucy, were playing in the park. The sky was wide and blue and Teddy couldn't help but smile. 

Suddenly, Lucy stopped playing.

"Teddy, I'm so excited," Lucy said. "My dad said I can study to be a scientist when I'm older!"

Teddy smiled and replied, "That sounds like a lot of fun! What will you study?"

Lucy paused for a moment and then answered, "My dad said I'll be studying oat plants."

Teddy was puzzled, "Oat plants?"

Lucy smiled wider and said, "Yes, oat plants. They grow in fields and make lots of food for animals and people. I'll learn more when I'm older!" 

Teddy was excited for his friend, and couldn't wait to see what Lucy would discover when she studied oat plants.

Tim and Sam like to play with their toy trucks and cars. They have a big mixer that can turn and make noise. They also have a small loader that can lift and dump sand.

One day, they go to the park with their mom and dad. They find a big pile of sand near the swings. They are very happy and run to the sand with their toys.

Tim takes the mixer and Sam takes the loader. They pretend to build a road with the sand. Tim turns the mixer and makes noise. Sam lifts the sand with the loader and dumps it into the mixer. They work together and have fun.

But then, a big boy comes to the sand. He has no toys. He looks at Tim and Sam and their toys. He wants to play with them. He tries to take the mixer from Tim. Tim says no and holds the mixer. The big boy pushes Tim and makes him fall. Tim cries and drops the mixer.

Sam sees what happens. He feels sad for Tim and angry at the big boy. He wants to help Tim. He thinks of a plan. He drives the loader to the big boy. He lifts some sand with the loader and dumps it on the big boy's head. The big boy is surprised and drops the mixer. He feels the sand in his hair and eyes. He cries and runs away.

Tim stops crying and sees Sam. He sees the mixer on the ground. He picks it up and hugs Sam. He says thank you to Sam. He says Sam is kind and brave. Sam smiles and says he is happy to help Tim. He says Tim is his best friend. They hug and play with their toys again. They are very happy.

One day, a little boy was playing in the garden. He saw a jet! The jet was very big and it was shining. It had two fat wings.
The little boy was very scared. He did not know what to do.
Suddenly, a magical lady appeared and said to the little boy, "Don't be scared. I can help you! I will make sure the jet will not fly away."
The little boy was so relieved. He thanked the magical lady and said, "Thank you for helping me!"
The magical lady said, "You're welcome." Then, she waved her hands and the jet transformed into a big, fat, purple balloon! 
The little boy smiled as the balloon flew away. He was very happy he had been helped.

Once there was a man and a woman who wanted to marry each other. But they wanted to find the perfect way to do it. They looked all around for the perfect fit!

One day, the couple went to the beach. There was a pretty little pond nearby, and the water was calm. The couple loved it and decided that this was the perfect way to marry.

So the couple hopped into a little boat and sailed around in the water. It was the perfect fit for the marriage! When the boat stopped, the couple got out and sang a special song. Then, they said their special words and even kissed each other.

The couple was now married and they were so happy! They hugged each other and smiled. That was the perfect way to marry!

Lily and Ben like to play with soap. They make bubbles and foam and pretend they are in a spa. One day, they have a big idea. They want to perform a show for their mom and dad with soap.

They take all the soap they can find and go to the bathroom. They fill the tub with water and soap and make a lot of bubbles. They put on their swimsuits and get ready to perform. They have a microphone made of a hairbrush and a stage made of a towel.

"Welcome to our soap show!" Lily says into the hairbrush. "We are going to sing and dance and make you laugh!"

Ben nods and starts to sing a silly song. He splashes the water and makes funny faces. Lily joins him and they dance around the tub. They are having a lot of fun.

But they are also making a big mess. The bubbles and water spill over the tub and onto the floor. The soap gets on the walls and the mirror. The bathroom looks like a snowstorm.

Mom and dad hear the noise and come to see what is going on. They see Lily and Ben in the tub, covered in soap and bubbles. They see the bathroom, wet and messy.

"What are you doing?" mom asks, surprised.

"We are performing a soap show!" Lily and Ben say, proud.

Mom and dad look at each other and smile. They are not angry. They are happy to see their children having fun and being creative. They clap and cheer for their soap show.

"Bravo! Bravo! You are very talented!" dad says.

"Thank you! Thank you!" Lily and Ben say, bowing.

They get out of the tub and dry themselves. Mom and dad help them clean the bathroom. They put away the soap and the hairbrush and the towel. They hug and kiss their children and tell them they love them.

Lily and Ben are happy. They love to perform. They love to play with soap. They love their mom and dad. They have a good day.

John was a curious three year old. He loved looking and exploring the world around him. One day, he decided to go on an observation mission. He went outside and saw a wide open space filled with blue sky. He looked up and observed the fluffy white clouds that were moving around in the sky. He then looked down and spied a massive blue lake. He was filled with awe and delight.

John continued to observe and explore his surroundings. He saw an incredible array of plants and animals that moved around and made lots of different noise. He saw a bright blue butterfly and watched it land on a flower. He also saw a big black bird swimming in the lake.

John had a wonderful day of observation. He learned a lot and was filled with joy by the beauty of the world around him. He decided that he would go out and explore more often.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there was a charming little spider. The spider liked to play with his friends, the ants. One day, the spider said to the ants, "Let's unite and make a big, fun game!"

The ants were happy and agreed to play. They all worked together to make a big web. The spider taught the ants how to make the web strong. The ants were excited to see the web grow bigger and bigger.

One sunny day, a big wind came and tried to blow the web away. The spider and the ants held on tight to the web. They worked together and saved their web from the wind. The spider and the ants were very happy that they united and made a strong web. They knew that together, they could do anything.

One day, the little girl wanted to go on a big adventure. She saw a long road ahead of her that stretched for miles and miles. There was no traffic on the empty road. The little girl decided to race down the long, empty road. 

She held her breath and wished for a good race. She closed her eyes and counted to three. She opened them and heard a loud rumble nearby. It was the sound of traffic. 

The little girl was so excited. She laughed with joy and started to race the traffic down the long road. 

The wind whirled around her as she raced the cars. The little girl felt alive and happy. Suddenly, she heard a loud honk! It was a car. The little girl laughed and waved goodbye to the traffic as she reached the end of the road. 

The little girl had a great adventure racing down the long road. She knew she would never forget the fun she had that day.

Once, there was a little girl named Sophie. She was three years old and loved to explore. 
One day, Sophie wanted to climb something. She spotted an old computer and decided to try it out. 
She gently grabbed its edges and started to climb. She climbed higher and higher until she was nearly at the top. 
Sophie looked out of the window and smiled. She saw a deep blue sky so far away. 
Then, Sophie heard her mom's voice. "Sophie! What are you doing up there?!"
Sophie looked down and said "I'm climbing!"
