Her mom smiled. "That sounds like fun! Climb down now and come get a snack!"

So Sophie carefully climbed back down the old computer and followed her mom to the kitchen.

Once there was a little girl named Lila who was very tired. She had been so busy playing that she hadn't taken the time to rest. Lila wanted to keep playing but her body was telling her that she needed to stop and take a break.

One day, Lila's mommy noticed how tired she was. She hugged Lila and said, "Lila, you need time to rest and heal." Lila didn't understand what her mommy meant.

That night, Lila went to bed early and fell asleep. When she woke up the next day, she felt so much better. She realized that taking time to rest made her feel better.

Now, whenever Lila feels tired she takes time to rest and heal. And soon, she is full of energy again.

Jim was a quiet boy. Every week he would go outside and record the birds singing. It was his favorite thing to do. 

One day, his mom asked him why he always went out to record the birds. He replied that it made him feel happy and grateful. 

His mom smiled, and she said: "That's wonderful, Jim. Why don't you keep track of how often you hear the birds each week? That way you can be more grateful for the singing of each one."

Jim thought for a moment and then he quickly said: "Yes! I will record them every week. That would be fun!"

So, every week for the rest of the summer, Jim went out and kept a record of the birds he heard. He was so grateful for their singing, and he loved counting each one.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Tara. She loved spending time outside playing with animals. One day, she decided to go to the forest and make a pretend picnic for her and her friends. Tara bought lots of delicious food for the picnic and even prepared her favourite spoiled fruit salad. 

Just as she was setting up the picnic blanket and getting ready to call her friends, something strange happened. All the food seemed to vanish into thin air! Tara was so confused, she couldn't understand what had happened! She searched everywhere, but the food was nowhere to be seen. 

Tara was sad, but she decided to look on the bright side. After all, she was surrounded by animals and it was a beautiful day. She started laughing and playing with the animals, and soon forgot about the vanishing food. Suddenly, much to her surprise, the food reappeared! The animals had been hiding the food so they could join the picnic too! 

The result was a fun day out with lots of laughs and great memories. Tara was so happy that her spoiled fruit salad hadn't gone to waste. All of them had a wonderful time and the animals were happy too. They all sang and danced until the sun went down. What a magical day!

One day, Little Timmy was walking in the park and he saw something unusual! It was a reindeer! Timmy had never seen a reindeer in the park before and he was very happy. He ran over and greeted the reindeer.

The reindeer smiled and said, "Hello Timmy, my name is Chris. Do you want to be friends?" Timmy was very glad and accepted the offer.

They became good friends and often went to the park together. Chris the reindeer taught Timmy about nature and animals and they played lots of fun games.

Timmy was so glad to have a new friend and he loved spending time with Chris the reindeer. They had lots of fun together and Timmy could not have been happier.

Once upon a time, there were two people. The first person was called Ann, and the second person was called Joe. Joe had a yellow balloon. 

Ann asked Joe to let her play with the yellow balloon. Joe said that he didn't want to, so he kept the balloon all to himself. 

Ann was very sad. She didn't want to play anymore.

Then, something special happened. Joe let Ann play with the yellow balloon. They both had a great time playing together and laughing. 

At the end of their playtime, Joe said to Ann, "Letting others play together is more fun than playing by yourself." 

From that day on, Ann and Joe were very happy and they both learned the valuable lesson that it is more fun to share and let others play.

Tom and Mia like to play catch in the park. They have a red ball that they throw to each other. Sometimes they run and jump to catch the ball. Sometimes they miss and the ball rolls away.

One day, they see a new path in the park. It is made of stones and dirt. They wonder where it goes. They decide to follow it with their ball. They take turns to throw and catch the ball as they walk on the path.

The path leads them to a big pond. They see ducks and fish in the water. They also see a bridge that goes over the pond. They want to cross the bridge and see what is on the other side. They throw the ball one more time and run to the bridge.

But the ball does not land in Mia's hands. It bounces off the bridge and falls into the pond. They hear a splash and see the red ball sink into the water. They are sad and scared. They do not know how to get their ball back. They look at each other and start to cry.

Then they hear a quack and see a duck swim to the ball. The duck picks up the ball with its beak and brings it to the edge of the pond. The duck drops the ball on the grass and wags its tail. Tom and Mia are happy and surprised. They thank the duck and hug each other. They pick up their ball and run back to the path. They decide to play catch in the park and not near the pond. They are glad that the duck helped them. They think the duck is their new friend.

One day, a blue bird was flying in the sky. The blue bird had big ears. The blue bird liked to listen to the sounds around it. It could hear the wind, the leaves, and the other animals.

The blue bird had a friend, a little girl. The little girl liked to play with the blue bird. She would bring the blue bird food and they would eat together. The blue bird would listen to the little girl sing.

One day, the little girl had a sad face. The blue bird wanted to help. The blue bird used its big ears to listen for something to make the little girl happy. It heard a song from another bird.

The blue bird went to find the bird with the song. It asked the bird to come and sing for the little girl. The bird said yes, and they flew back to the little girl.

When the little girl heard the song, she smiled. The blue bird was happy to see her friend happy again. They all sang and played together, and the blue bird's big ears listened to the happy sounds.

Once there was a little girl who loved to race. Everywhere she went, she would run faster and faster. One day, she saw something pink and shiny. It was a symbol and it made the little girl so excited. She had to touch it and race around the symbol. 

The little girl ran faster and faster, until she was out of breath. She kept running around the symbol and then suddenly she tripped and fell. She cried out in pain and the symbol turned into dust. 

The little girl was so sad. She had wanted to keep the symbol forever, but now it was gone. She had been too eager and she learnt her lesson never to race too fast.

Once there was a little boy named Timmy. He was really smart! His Mommy and Daddy bought him a pair of mittens. The mittens were red and warm. They were just the right size, they fit Timmy perfectly.

Everyday, Timmy put on his mittens and went outside to play. He'd play in the garden and build castles in the sand. He'd run around with his friends, their faces all rosy and warm. Timmy loved having mittens that fit him so well.

When it started to snow, Timmy and his friends all went outside to play. Timmy's mittens kept his hands nice and warm. He scooped up chunks of snow and made snow angels. Then he built a snowman. Timmy was so happy, his mittens definitely kept him warm.

Timmy was so thankful for his mittens. They fit him so nicely and kept him warm. He was smart for having mittens to stay outside and play. Timmy's Mommy and Daddy were very proud of him.

Once upon a time, there was a poor man who walked with a cane. He needed the cane to help him walk because his leg hurt. One day, his friend came to him and asked to borrow the cane. The poor man was kind and said yes, he could lend the cane to his friend. 

The friend used the cane for a little while and then brought it back to the poor man. The poor man was happy to have his cane back because he needed it to walk. 

Even though the poor man didn't have much, he was still happy to help his friend. He knew that sometimes people need help and it's important to be kind and lend a hand or a cane when you can.

Jack was a boy who really loved cartoons. Every day he would watch his favourite cartoon and it would make him happy. One day, Jack was feeling a bit sad. He was missing his mom who was away on a trip. His dad tried to cheer him up by reminding him about his favourite cartoon. 

He showed him pictures of his favourite characters and talked about how much fun it would be to watch tomorrow. Jack couldn't help but smile. Dad reminded him that whenever he was feeling sad he could always watch a cartoon. 

The next day, Jack and his dad watched the cartoon together and laughed at the funny bits. Before they knew it, they had both forgotten that Jack had been feeling sad. Jack had been reminded of his favourite cartoon and it put him back in a happy mood again.

Once upon a time, there was a nosy kid named Tim. He liked to look at everything and ask many questions. One day, Tim saw a big box in his room. He wanted to know what was inside.

Tim asked his mom, "What is in the box?" His mom said, "That is a surprise, but you cannot open it until I say so." Tim was sad, but he waited for his mom to leave the room.

When his mom left the room, Tim tried to open the box. But, his little dog, Spot, started to bark loudly. Tim's mom came back and saw him trying to open the box. She said, "Tim, you must wait for the right time to open the box." Tim felt bad for not listening to his mom.

From that day on, Tim learned to be patient and not to be too nosy. He waited for his mom to tell him when it was time to open the box. When the day came, Tim found a new toy inside the box. He was happy and thanked his mom for the surprise.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to run, jump and slide on the grass and the swings. They were happy and laughed a lot.

But then they saw a big hill. It was very high and had many rocks and trees. Lily and Ben wondered what was on the other side of the hill. Maybe there was a lake, or a castle, or a dragon.

"Let's go and see!" said Ben. He was brave and curious. He started to climb the hill.

"Wait for me!" said Lily. She was also brave and curious, but she was more careful. She looked for a safe path to follow Ben.

They climbed and climbed, until they reached the top of the hill. They were tired and thirsty, but they were also excited. They looked at the other side of the hill.

They saw a beautiful sight. There was a field of flowers, with many colors and smells. There was a stream, with clear water and fish. There was a rainbow, with bright and shiny colors. And there was sunshine, with warm and gentle light.

"Wow!" said Ben. "This is amazing!"

"Yes!" said Lily. "This is wonderful!"

They smiled and hugged each other. They were happy and proud. They had found a new place to play and explore. They thanked the sunshine for showing them the way.

One day, Joe went out for a walk. He put on his watch and decided to go explore the woods. As he stepped into the forest, he found a big and slimy mud puddle. Joe opened his mouth wide and said: "Oh no! How do I get across this puddle?"

Just then, a small but honest bird flew down from the sky. It looked at Joe with its beady eyes and said: "What's wrong, Joe? Need help?" Joe nodded, so the bird said: "I can help you with my wings! I will wipe the mud away, so you can cross the puddle safely."

Joe beamed and said: "Thank you, kind bird! I knew I could count on you." He watched as the bird used its wings to wipe away the mud, and soon the puddle was gone. Joe said goodbye to the bird and walked across the puddle. He smiled as he thought to himself: "Honest friends are the best friends!".

Lily and Ben like to play in the yard. They have a big truck and a small ladder. They load the truck with rocks, sticks and leaves. They pretend they are workers.

One day, they see a big house across the street. It has a scary roof. It is dark and pointy. They wonder what is inside. They want to see.

They take their truck and ladder and go to the house. They put the ladder on the wall. They climb up. They look at the roof. They see a hole. They want to go in.

They load the truck with more rocks, sticks and leaves. They make a pile under the hole. They climb on the pile. They reach the hole. They peek inside.

They see a big spider. It has many legs and eyes. It is hairy and shiny. It makes a loud noise. It jumps at them.

They scream. They fall off the pile. They run away. They leave their truck and ladder. They go back to their yard. They hug each other. They are scared.

They never go to the big house again. They play with their truck and ladder in the yard. They are happy.

Once upon a time there were two children, Peter and Mary. Peter and Mary were very excited and decided to go to the museum. In the great museum, they saw a huge fierce dinosaur and began to spin around it. Suddenly, the dinosaur started to spin too.

The children were frightened and ran to tell the museum keeper. The museum keeper was very angry with Peter and Mary. He told them it was not allowed to spin around the dinosaur. 

The museum keeper said that spinning around fierce things can be dangerous and we should show respect for them. He also said that the dinosaur needed to be left alone so it could stay fierce and powerful. 

The children were sorry and promised to never spin around the dinosaur again.

Moral of the story: We should show respect for things that are strong, fierce, and powerful.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Jack. Jack loved reading books. One day, he was exploring in a dark forest, when he stumbled upon a strange looking book. Jack was very excited and opened the book.

Inside the book, he found a funny story. He enjoyed it very much and decided he wanted to keep it. Jack took the book home, and he enjoyed reading it again and again.

One day, Jack decided to take the book to school to show his friends. But when he arrived at school he noticed something strange. He found out that his friends had the same book.

Jack felt a little sad, he realised that all his friends had been enjoying the same book. He should have been more careful and shared his book with his friends, so that everyone could enjoy reading it.

Moral: Always share and be kind, so that everyone can enjoy the things you love.

Once upon a time, there lived two friends on a planet far away. The first friend was called Tom, and the second was called Sam.

One day, Tom asked Sam, "Let's go on an adventure! We can choose whichever planet we want!"

Sam replied, "Great idea! Let's go to the original planet!"

So, with excitement, the two friends put on their backpacks and set off on their journey. 

They quickly arrived at the original planet and discovered many new, interesting things. They explored the moon, the stars, and the galaxies. Everywhere they looked, they saw something amazing. 

"I'm glad we chose this planet," said Tom.

"Me too!" said Sam. "Let's come back here again and explore some more!" 

And so, the two friends smiled, hugged, and enjoyed the beautiful view before them. They had found the perfect place to explore and were truly happy.

Once there was a girl named Jill. Jill was three years old and she was very busy. She liked to keep things neat and tidy. Every morning she got out her folder and she started to polish it. She loved the way that when she polished it the folder looked so shiny.

When she was finished polishing her folder, she put it back on her shelf. She was so proud of it that she wanted everyone in the house to see it. But it was so quiet in the house, that no one noticed.

Jill didn't mind that no one noticed, she was proud of her folder. She knew that it would be very shiny and neat each day because she polished it every morning. She was happy to have her very own shiny little folder.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to play outside in the wind. She liked to run and feel the wind in her hair. One day, Lily's mommy bought her a new dress. It was pink and had flowers on it. Lily was very happy and she twirled around in her new dress.

Later that day, Lily went to the park to play. She saw a boy playing with a ball and she wanted to play too. So, she went up to the boy and asked if she could play with him. The boy said yes and they played together for a long time. The wind blew and made their hair fly all over the place. Lily was having so much fun in her new dress, playing with her new friend and feeling the wind on her face.

Once upon a time, there was a clumsy bird named Bobo. Bobo lived in a small nest on a big tree. He had many friends, but he was not good at flying.

One day, Bobo wanted to go play with his friends. But his mom did not permit him to fly. She was scared Bobo would fall and get hurt. Bobo was sad and felt left out.

Bobo's friends saw him sad and had an idea. They all came to Bobo's nest and played with him there. Bobo was so happy. His mom saw how careful they were and permitted Bobo to play with his friends in the nest.

Once upon a time, there were two sisters named Jane and Annie. Jane was bossy and liked to boss Annie around all the time. Annie, however, usually didn't like it when Jane was bossy, but she usually complied with what Jane said.

One day when they were outside, Jane started to record the birds and their songs with her smartphone. Annie, though, wanted to jump around in the field. Jane got mad and told Annie that she should take care of the recording instead. Annie was unhappy, but she did as Jane said. 

Suddenly as Annie was walking, she had a fall. She scraped her knee and started to cry. Jane rushed over and hugged Annie and was very sorry she had been so bossy. She decided to put away the phone and the two girls started to play in the field. 

The moral of this story is to not be bossy to your friends and family. It is important to think of others first and to make sure everyone is having fun.

Tim likes trains. He has many trains at home. He plays with them every day. He makes them go fast and slow. He makes them stop and go. He makes them say choo-choo.

One day, Tim goes to the park with his mom. He sees a big train on the tracks. He wants to ride the train. He asks his mom, "Can we ride the train, please?"

His mom says, "Yes, we can. But we have to wait. The train is not available now. It is busy. It will come back soon. Then we can ride it."

Tim waits with his mom. He is excited. He watches the train go by. He counts the cars. He waves to the people. He hears the whistle.

After a while, the train comes back. It stops at the station. The conductor says, "All aboard! The train is available now. Come and ride with us!"

Tim and his mom bring their tickets. They get on the train. They find a seat. They look out the window. They see the trees, the flowers, the animals, and the other trains. They enjoy the ride. Tim is happy. He loves trains.

Once upon a time, there was an adventurous flower named Petal. She loved exploring the world and meeting new friends. One day she decided to sail away in search of a new harbor.

Petal found a small harbor and saw a beautiful, blooming flower garden. She made many new friends and enjoyed playing with them. The days were so fun and Petal couldn't help but smile.

One day, the wind started to pick up and Petal felt the urge to go. She bid her friends farewell and sailed away. Petal's final destination was a wonderful, magical harbor.

When Petal arrived, she saw the most amazing sight. Hundreds of flowers were blooming in the harbor. Bright, beautiful colors filled the air and, for a moment, Petal felt like she was dreaming.

The harbor was an amazing place. Everywhere she looked, flowers were blooming and Petal felt happy and adventurous all over again. She stayed in the harbor with her new friends and enjoyed the beautiful blooms.

Once upon a time, there lived a mommy and her little girl. They were very busy all the time. One day, the mommy asked the little girl to go fix the cupboard. 

The little girl was excited about helping her mommy. She said â€œYes, mommy! I will fix the cupboard!â€ She grabbed her tools and marched off to the cupboard.

The little girl tried and tried to fix the cupboard but no matter what she did, it still wouldnâ€™t work. She got more and more frustrated with it. In her anger, she kicked the cupboard and it broke.

The little girl started to cry and the mommy was angry. She said to the little girl, â€œYou shouldnâ€™t let your anger get the best of you and break things. We have to be patient and stay calm, even when weâ€™re busy.â€

The little girl felt bad. She realized she should have been more patient and not let her anger get the best of her. She learned her lesson and the cupboard was never fixed.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys on his rug. One day, Timmy spilled his juice on the rug and it became wet. He asked his mommy to help him dry it.

While they were waiting for the rug to dry, Timmy's little sister came in and wanted to play with his toys. Timmy said, "No, these are my toys!" His sister got angry and they began to fight over the toys.

Mommy came back in and saw them fighting. She said, "Stop fighting! You can both play with the toys on the rug." Timmy and his sister stopped fighting and played together on the dry rug. They had so much fun playing together that they forgot all about the fight. The end.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Molly. She was three years old and loved to play with dolls.

One day, Molly was playing dress-up with her dolls. She put her dolls in all sorts of different fashions. As she was playing, she felt tired and wanted to take a nap.

Molly went to her bedroom and climbed into her bed. She closed her eyes, took a deep breath and felt very calm. Molly imagined a special place where she could go, full of bright colors and new fashions.

She opened her eyes and found herself in a magical place. She could see a rainbow of colors and all kinds of pretty dresses, shoes and hats. Molly was so excited! She twirled around and around and looked at all the new clothes.

Then, she saw something special - a big golden wheel! Molly walked up slowly and put her hand on it. She gave the wheel a turn and the wheel began to spin. Suddenly, all the fashions changed into new, beautiful clothes! Molly was very happy and felt so calm.

The End.

Bee and Ant were friends. They liked to play and help each other. One day, they saw a big hole in Bee's hive. The hole was bad. It let the rain and the wind come in. It also let the honey drip out. The honey made a sticky mess on the ground.

"Oh no!" said Bee. "My hive is broken. How can I fix it?"

"Don't worry," said Ant. "I can help you. I know how to fix things. We need some mud and some leaves. Come with me."

Bee and Ant went to find some mud and some leaves. They worked hard to fill the hole with mud. Then they covered the mud with leaves. They made the hive strong and cozy again.

"Thank you, Ant," said Bee. "You are a good friend. You fixed my hive. Do you want some honey?"

"Yes, please," said Ant. "I love honey. It is sweet and yummy."

Bee and Ant went inside the hive. They shared some honey and some stories. They were happy and warm.

But then they heard a loud noise. It was a bear. The bear smelled the honey. He wanted to eat it. He saw the hive and the sticky mess on the ground. He thought it was disgusting.

"Yuck!" said the bear. "This honey is dirty and gross. I don't want it. I will find another hive."

The bear left the hive alone. He went away. Bee and Ant did not see him. They did not know he was there. They kept eating and talking. They did not care about the disgusting mess. They only cared about their friendship.

Once upon a time, there was a silly goat named Jim. He lived near a meadow and liked playing there in the sunshine.

One hot summer day, Jim forgot to take a rest and kept playing in the meadow as the sun set. Suddenly, he heard a loud roar and a big bear appeared!

Jim was very scared and tried to run away, but the bear was too fast. Jim shouted to the bear, "Please don't hurt me!" 

But the bear didn't listen and chased Jim into the woods. Even though Jim was very scared, he remembered something the farmer had told him about bears. 

Jim yelled out, "Stop! I know a secret way to get food that won't leave you so hungry!"

But the bear kept chasing Jim and eventually, the bear caught up and ate poor Jim. 

This story reminds us that no matter how silly we are, it is important to remember to be careful and listen to what grown-ups tell us.

Once upon a time there was a big, impressive castle. It was like a dream come true for many children who wanted to explore it. 

One day, a little three year old boy came to the castle with his family. He was so excited to get inside but he couldn't manage to open the giant doors. He tried again and again but still couldn't get the door open.

The little boy looked around and he saw his family and they were all smiling. His dad soon said, "I'm sure if you work hard and focus, you can get it open." 

The little boy tried harder and he finally opened the doors of the castle. Everyone was so impressed and praised him for his hard work and determination.

This story teaches us that everything is possible if we try hard and never give up. With enough effort, we can open every door in front of us.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her hoop in the park. One day, while she was playing, she saw a boy with a big, disgusting bug on his shirt. Lily didn't like bugs, but she felt sorry for the boy. She went up to him and said, "Don't worry, I'll kiss the bug goodbye!" And she did! The boy was so happy that he gave Lily a big hug. From that day on, they became good friends and played with their hoops together every day. The end.

Lila loved to play the violin. She had a small violin that her mom gave her for her birthday. She liked to make music with it and sing along. She practiced every day and learned new songs.

One day, Lila wanted to show her friend Ben how she could play the violin. She invited him to her house and took him to her room. She picked up her violin and said, "Look, Ben, I can play the violin. It is easy and fun. Do you want to try?"

Ben nodded and reached for the violin. He did not know how to hold it or how to use the bow. He pulled the bow too hard and too fast. He made a loud and ugly noise. Lila frowned and said, "No, Ben, you have to be gentle and slow. Like this." She took the violin back and showed him how to play.

But Ben did not listen. He grabbed the violin again and tried to play. He was rough and careless. He broke one of the strings. He did not stop. He broke another string. He did not stop. He broke the third string. He did not stop. He broke the last string. He did not stop. He broke the bow. He did not stop. He broke the violin. He split it in half.

Lila gasped and cried. She was very sad and angry. She loved her violin and now it was ruined. She said, "Ben, you are very bad. You broke my violin. You split it in half. You are not my friend anymore. Go away!"

Ben was scared and sorry. He did not mean to break the violin. He did not know how to play. He said, "Lila, I am sorry. I did not want to break your violin. I wanted to play with you. Please forgive me. Please be my friend."

But Lila did not listen. She was too upset. She threw the broken violin and bow at Ben. She told him to leave and never come back. She ran to her mom and hugged her. She told her what happened. Her mom was sorry and hugged her back. She said, "Lila, I know you are sad. But you can get a new violin. And maybe Ben can learn to play better. And maybe you can be friends again. But you have to be kind and patient. And you have to share and teach. Playing the violin is easy and fun. But being a good friend is hard and important."

Once upon a time there was a powerful tour. It was a tour like no other. On this tour the most amazing things were revealed.

First, they revealed a gigantic mountain that was so high it reached the clouds. Everyone was amazed by its powerful height.

Next, they revealed a deep ocean filled with bright fish. Everybody oohed and ahhed over the beautiful creatures.

Finally, they revealed a secret cave filled with sparkling jewels. Everyone was amazed at how beautiful they were.

Everybody had a wonderful time on the powerful tour. Everything they saw was so nice and the secrets they discovered were really cool. The tour revealed the best parts of the world to them and they will never forget it.

Once upon a time, there was an old tree in the middle of the forest. "What is this old thing?" asked a curious 3 year old girl, as she reached out to touch it. 

Suddenly, the old tree began to move. The little girl was so frightened that she backed away. But the tree was very kind and called to her, "Come closer! I won't hurt you." The little girl hesitantly stepped closer to the tree. 

The tree then revealed a hidden door that no one in the forest had ever seen before. The tree said, "If you open this door, you will find something special. It may take courage, but if you try, who knows what wonders you will find." 

The little girl was unsure at first, but then she bravely opened the door. Inside, she found an entire world filled with amazing things to explore. She spent the entire day exploring and playing. 

This teaches us that no matter how uncomfortable something may seem at first, if we just have courage and believe in ourselves, we can find wonderful and hidden treasures.

Once there was a hungry bear. He was feeling grumpy. He went walking in the woods to find something to eat. Suddenly he saw a powerful tree. He could see lots of different fruit on its branches. He felt very excited. He climbed the tree to pick some of the yummy fruit. The bear enjoyed the delicious fruit and felt happy and full. The power of the fruit made him feel strong and healthy. He thanked the tree for giving him such yummy fruit and happily went on his way.

Lila and Ben were playing in the attic. They found a big box with many old things inside. They saw a lamp, a hat, a doll, and a bottle. The bottle had a label on it. The label said "Do not open".

"What is this?" Lila asked.

"I don't know. Maybe it has something cool inside. Let's open it!" Ben said.

"No, Ben. The label says no. It could be bad. We should listen to the label." Lila said.

But Ben did not listen. He was curious. He opened the bottle. A green smoke came out. It smelled disgusting. It made Lila and Ben cough and sneeze.

"Ben, why did you do that? That was a bad idea. Now we are sick." Lila said.

"I'm sorry, Lila. I wanted to see what was inside. Maybe it was a magic bottle. Maybe it could make us glow or fly or something." Ben said.

But it was not a magic bottle. It was a poison bottle. The green smoke was very bad for Lila and Ben. It made them feel worse and worse. They tried to call for help, but no one heard them. They lay down on the floor, feeling very sick and sad. The lamp in the attic was the only thing that glowed. It glowed dimly, like a dying star. The end.

Jimmy was walking along the beach. He saw something strange in the sand. He asked, "What is that?"

His dad smiled and said, "I think it's a jellyfish. Do you want to take a closer look?" 

Jimmy was excited. Dad picked it up carefully and showed it to him. It was a very slow jellyfish, with long tentacles. 

Dad said, "Why don't you guess what color it is?"

Jimmy thought for a moment and said, "I think it's pink!"

Dad smiled and replied, "You're right! It is pink."

Jimmy was very proud that he had guessed the right color. They watched the jellyfish for a while before putting it back into the sea.

At the breakfast table Henry yawned. His mom and dad were surprised. 
"Henry, why did you yawn?" they asked. 
"I saw something that made me sleepy," Henry replied with a yawn.

His mom and dad looked around to see what it was. Then in the kitchen they saw a big soft pillow in a bowl. 
"Ah, it was the pillow in the bowl," said his mom. 

His dad then said, "Henry, you shouldn't use a pillow in a bowl as a toy. A bowl has a special use. It's for putting food in so you can eat it." 

Henry smiled and said, "I won't do that again. I know it's important to use things in the right way." 

His mom and dad were glad Henry had learned a valuable lesson. From then on, Henry used the bowl only to put food in it. 

The moral of the story is that it's important to know how to use things properly.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a black cat named Mittens. One day, Lily was playing with Mittens and she dropped her toy. Mittens went to get it for her, but he got into trouble. He accidentally knocked over a vase and it broke into many pieces. Lily's mom was not happy, but Lily told her it was her fault because she dropped her toy. Lily's mom forgave her and they all played together with Mittens.

Once upon a time, there was a young boy who wanted to go on an adventure. He wanted to explore a big, scary maze. But he couldn't find his way out. He felt so helpless.

Suddenly, he heard a voice calling his name. He turned around and saw a friendly, shining light. It was an angel! The angel said it would bring the boy out of the maze, and that it would guide him to safety.

The angel flew up above and shone a light on the path ahead. The boy followed the light and eventually made it out of the maze. He was so happy! He thanked the angel for bringing him out of the maze and back home again.

The angel smiled and said, â€œIt was my pleasure!â€ Then, it flew off into the sky and the boy went back inside his house. He was so relieved he had made it out of the maze. From that day on he never ventured into a maze again!

John was walking through the park. He saw something very interesting. He moved closer, and saw that the grass was being pulled! He saw a lady pulling the grass and throwing it away. He was very curious. He asked her what she was doing, and she said she was getting rid of the weeds. 

John thought it was even more interesting. He wanted to help too. He looked for weeds, and then he started to pull them out with the lady. He was so happy to help, and the lady was very thankful. 

They worked together until all of the weeds were gone. When they were done, the grass looked nice and beautiful. John and the lady smiled, and they said goodbye. 

John was so happy to see the park looking nice and knew that he had done a good job. He gave himself a big hug and went home, feeling very proud.

Once upon a time, in a small house, lived a little girl named Lucy and her lazy cat, Tom. They liked to play together all day long. One day, Lucy's mom made some hot cocoa for them to drink. Lucy was very happy and said, "Thank you, Mom!"

But Tom was a little worried. He had never tried cocoa before. He looked at the cup and said, "Lucy, what is this?" Lucy smiled and said, "It's cocoa, Tom! It's good and warm. Don't worry, you will like it."

So, Tom took a small sip of the cocoa. He liked it a lot! Tom and Lucy drank their cocoa and played together. They had a fun day, and Tom was not worried anymore.

Mia likes to match things. She has a box of cards with pictures of animals and things. She likes to find two cards that are the same and put them together. She thinks it is fun and easy.

One day, Mia sees a birdcage in the living room. It is big and shiny and has a door. Inside the birdcage, there is a bird. The bird is pale and has a long tail. It makes a loud noise. Mia thinks the bird is pretty and wants to play with it.

She goes to her box of cards and looks for a card that matches the bird. She finds one that has a pale bird with a long tail. She is happy and runs to the birdcage. She shows the card to the bird and says, "Look, bird, I have a card that matches you. Do you want to be my friend?"

The bird looks at the card and at Mia. It does not like the card. It thinks the card is not a real bird. It does not want to be Mia's friend. It makes a louder noise and flaps its wings. It tries to bite the card and Mia's fingers.

Mia is scared and sad. She drops the card and runs away. She cries and says, "The bird does not like me. The bird does not want to match. The bird is mean."

Mia's mom hears Mia crying and comes to see what is wrong. She sees the birdcage and the card on the floor. She hugs Mia and says, "I'm sorry, Mia. The bird is not a toy. The bird is a pet. The bird does not understand cards. The bird needs a different kind of friend. Maybe you can find another card that matches something else. Or maybe you can draw a picture of the bird and give it to the bird. Maybe then the bird will like you."

Mia stops crying and thinks. She says, "Okay, mom. I will try. I still like the bird. I want the bird to like me too." She goes to her box of cards and looks for another match. She hopes the bird will be nice.

Once upon a time, there was a farmer. The farmer had a farm with many animals. He had cows, pigs, and chickens. The farmer liked to keep his farm clean and organize.

One day, a rare bird came to the farm. The bird was very big and very loud. The bird started to make a mess. It knocked over the farmer's things and scared the animals. The farmer did not like the mess and the noise.

The farmer tried to make the bird go away. He clapped his hands and shouted, "Go away, bird!" But the bird did not listen. The farmer was sad and did not know what to do.

Then, the farmer had an idea. He gave the bird some food. The bird ate the food and became happy. The bird stopped making a mess and making noise. The farmer and the bird became friends.

From that day on, the rare bird helped the farmer organize the farm. The farmer was happy, and the farm was clean and peaceful again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Amy. She loved to store her toys in a special space in her room. One day, she became anxious because she could not find her favorite toy, a small blue car.

Amy looked everywhere in her room, but the blue car was not there. She felt sad and asked her mom for help. "Mom, I can't find my blue car. Can you help me?" Her mom said, "Of course, Amy. Let's look together."

They searched the whole house, and finally, they found the blue car under the couch. Amy was so happy and said, "Thank you, Mom!" From that day on, Amy always made sure to store her toys in the special space in her room, so she would never feel anxious about losing them again.

Once upon a time there was a fat young cat named Blink. He lived in a cosy warm home at the end of the street.
Each day, Blink the cat would go down to the park to play with his friends and explore the meadow. One day, while running and playing, he noticed a group of children at the other end of the park. His curiosity kicked in and he decided to go and explore.

He started walking slowly towards the group, but just as he was about to reach them, one of the children saw him and shouted, â€œLook thereâ€™s a cat!â€ 
The other children became excited and ran towards blink. They were so fascinated by him and wanted to play with him.

But Blink wasnâ€™t sure what to do, so he just blinked. He blinked one eye, then the other. The children giggled as Blink continued to blink and soon, everyone was blinking together! 

They all had lots of fun that day. Blink had made new friends and was glad that he decided to explore the park that day.

Tom and Lily were playing in the park. They liked to pretend they were lions and roar at each other. They also liked to make marks on the ground with sticks and stones. They said they were making a map of their lion kingdom.

One day, they saw a big dog in the park. It was unknown to them. It had black fur and a long tail. It looked at them with curious eyes. Tom and Lily were not afraid. They thought the dog was a friend.

"Hello, dog!" Tom said. "Do you want to play with us? We are lions. We can roar and make marks."

The dog wagged its tail and barked. It seemed to like the idea. It ran towards them and sniffed their faces. Tom and Lily laughed and petted the dog.

"Let's show you our map," Lily said. "We made it with sticks and stones. It has our den, our lake, and our mountain."

They led the dog to their map. They pointed at the marks and explained what they meant. The dog nodded and licked their hands.

"Can you roar like a lion?" Tom asked. "We can teach you. It's easy. You just open your mouth and say 'roar'."

Tom and Lily demonstrated their roars. They sounded loud and fierce. The dog watched and listened. It opened its mouth and tried to roar. But instead of a roar, it made a squeak. It sounded funny and cute.

Tom and Lily giggled. The dog looked embarrassed. It tried again and again, but it could not roar. It only squeaked.

"It's okay, dog," Lily said. "You don't have to roar. You can bark. Barking is good too. We like barking."

Tom agreed. "Yeah, barking is good. You can be our barking lion. We can still play together. We are friends."

The dog smiled and barked. It was happy. It liked Tom and Lily. It liked being their barking lion. They played and had fun. They roared and barked and made marks. They were a happy lion family.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Daisy. She loved to explore and always dreamed of travelling the world.

One day, she decided to visit the airport with her mom. As soon as they arrived, Daisy's eyes lit up. She loved watching the airplanes take off and imagining the different places they could go.

Mom observed Daisy carefully and said: "Daisy, why don't we go on a trip?" Daisy was so excited and nodded her head. She couldn't believe her dream was coming true.

So they packed their bags and headed to the airport. They had to be flexible, but it was all worth it. 

Although Daisy was a bit scared of flying, she ignored her fears and they hopped on a plane. Before they knew it, they were in a new country. Daisy was thrilled to explore and see all the new things. 

The best part of all was that Daisy could now say she had been to the airport.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. The girl had a stick. She liked to use the stick to draw in the sand.

One day, she went to the beach. She found a lot of seashells and sea rocks. The girl wanted to keep the shells for herself.

Suddenly, she heard something in the water. It was a fish in trouble! He was stuck in a net that was too tight. The girl was scared, but she knew she had to help. So, she grabbed the stick and started to help the fish. The girl first struggled to cut through the net. But slowly, the net started to tear. Then, the little girl reached in and pulled out the fish. She had saved him!

The fish thanked the girl and swam away back into the sea. The girl was happy. She had used her little stick to save him.

Anna liked to speak to her toys. She had a bear, a doll, and a frog. She gave them names and voices. She pretended they were her friends.

One day, she was playing with them in the kitchen. She saw a big pot on the stove. It smelled good. She asked her mom, "What is that?"

Mom said, "That is soup. It is for dinner. Do you want to try some?"

Anna nodded. She loved soup. Mom gave her a small bowl and a spoon. Anna took a sip. It was hot and tasty. She said, "Mmm, this is good soup. Do you want some, bear?"

She held the spoon to the bear's mouth. The bear did not open his mouth. Anna was confused. She said, "Bear, why don't you want soup? Soup is good. Don't you like soup?"

She tried the doll and the frog. They did not open their mouths either. Anna was more confused. She said, "Doll, frog, why don't you want soup? Soup is good. Don't you like soup?"

She looked at her mom. Mom smiled. She said, "Anna, your toys can't eat soup. They are not real. They can't speak or open their mouths. Only you can do that."

Anna thought for a moment. She said, "But they speak to me. They are my friends. They have names and voices."

Mom said, "That's because you have a big imagination. You make them speak in your mind. That's fun. But they can't really speak or eat. Only people and animals can do that."

Anna understood. She said, "Oh, I see. So they don't need soup. But I do. Can I have more soup, please?"

Mom said, "Of course, you can. You are a good girl. And you have good friends. Even if they are only toys."

Once upon a time, in a busy little town, there lived a girl named Lily. She loved to wake up early to see the sunrise. The sky would turn pretty colors like pink and orange. Lily liked to watch the sun come up with her dog, Max.

One day, while watching the sunrise, Lily heard a snap. She looked around and saw a little bird. The bird had a broken wing. Lily wanted to help the bird, so she picked it up gently and took it to her mom.

Lily's mom knew how to fix the bird's wing. She used a soft cloth and some tape. Soon, the bird was all better. The bird was so happy, it sang a beautiful song for Lily and Max. From that day on, they all watched the sunrise together, and the town became even busier and happier.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside in his backyard. One day, he found a colorful ball. He was so happy to have found it.

Timmy's mom called him inside for lunch. She made him a sandwich and gave him a glass of milk. "Mommy, can I bury my ball in the backyard?" Timmy asked.

His mom said, "Why do you want to bury your ball?"

Timmy replied, "I want to bury it so I can find it later and play with it again."

His mom smiled and said, "Okay, but make sure you remember where you bury it." So, Timmy went outside and buried his colorful ball in the backyard. He couldn't wait to dig it up and play with it again.

Once upon a time, there was a tiny mouse who lived deep in the woods. Every day, he gathered tasty treats to eat, like nuts and berries.

One night, the mouse heard a loud noise outside his burrow. He looked outside and saw flashes of lightning in the sky! He was scared and tried to go back inside, but the lightning scared him too much.

The mouse's best friend was a bear who lived nearby. He saw how scared the mouse was and said, â€œItâ€™s okay, little mouse. Thatâ€™s just the sky doing somersaults. The lightning is weak and it canâ€™t get you.â€

The mouse felt much better after the bear talked to him. He gathered up his courage and looked up at the sky. Sure enough, the lightning was weak and very far away.

The mouse smiled at the bear and said, â€œThanks for being my friend.â€ Then they both went back to their burrows.

Once upon a time, there was a girl called Mummy. Mummy was very nosy. One day, Mummy was feeling a bit sad.

Mummy's best friend, Sally, saw that Mummy was feeling down. So Sally said, "I can give you a massage. It will make you feel better". Mummy said, "Yes please."

Sally gave Mummy a lovely massage. Mummy felt all better and she smiled. She said, "That was so nice. I love it!"

Sally said, "Anything for you, Mummy. I love you!" Mummy was so happy. She hugged Sally and said, "I love you too". They hugged each other for a very long time. 

The end.

Once upon a time there was a rich goat who lived in a big, fancy house on the side of a hill. He had lots of toys and always ate the best food. Everyone came from far and wide to admire the goat's rich life and all the things he had.

One day, the rich goat decided to go for a walk around the hill. As he walked he came across a group of children who were walking in the opposite direction. When the children saw the goat, they all cheered and ran up to him. They began to admire the goat and his fancy house, and asked him questions about it. The goat proudly told them all of the details.

The children enjoyed their conversation with the rich goat, and they soon all decided to visit his house. When they arrived, they ran around, exploring the house and all of the amazing things that the goat owned. The children had a wonderful time, and they all admired the goat even more.

Being the generous goat that he was, the rich goat decided to reward them with a treat. He asked the children to pick their favourite food and he made sure they all had plenty to eat. The children thanked the goat and thanked him again as they returned home.

Since then, the rich goatâ€™s house has become a popular destination for children. They all know that the generous goat will always be happy to see them, and all the amazing things he has to show them, and

Gus loved to drive his reliable vehicle. Every day, he would hop in, start it up and drive off! But today, Gus was disappointed. When he went to turn on the vehicle, it wouldn't start. He resisted turning away and tried again and again, but it just wouldn't go. He had to find someone else to help him. 

So Gus walked off to find help. He walked past a house and saw a mechanic. Waving his hands, he called out, "Please help me!" The mechanic smiled and said he'd help. 

They both went back to the vehicle and the man opened the hood. Right away he saw the problem, but he knew Gus could fix it. The mechanic showed Gus what to do and said, "If you resist giving up, I promise your vehicle will be reliable again." 

Gus followed the mechanic's instructions, and quickly he heard the engine roar to life! He jumped for joy and thanked the mechanic. He promised to stay reliable and never give up again.

Once upon a time there was a boy named Pete. Pete was very clever, but he did not like to do schoolwork. He wanted to play all the time!

One day, Pete decided to read a new novel. He opened it and discovered something strange inside. There was an old key!

He wondered what the key could open. Pete thought really hard and finally he had an idea. Maybe the key could open a door! He grabbed the key and ran outside.

At the end of the garden, Pete found an old door. He put the key in the lock and twisted it round and round. Suddenly, the door swung open. Pete was amazed!

Inside Pete found a big, big surprise. It was a room full of toys! He smiled from ear to ear. He had used his intelligent thinking to open the door! That was the best day ever!

Once there was a fast cat. He wanted to go on a great adventure. He ran to a tree and started to climb it. When he got to the top it was very high. He was scared but excited at the same time. Suddenly, he saw a needle fly past him, fast! He quickly ducked as the needle shot past. He heard a little giggle and he looked down. There was a little girl standing there, she was holding a long stick with a needle attached. "That was a lot of fun!" the girl said. The cat was confused, why did the girl shoot the needle? The girl wanted to play with the cat and said, "I need to shoot needles so you can come and play with me!" The cat was happy and he jumped down and played with the girl all day. They ran around and chased each other, and the cat even taught the girl how to climb trees. It was a great adventure for both of them, and the cat was glad he didn't need a needle to have fun.

Once upon a time there was a cupboard. It was full of goodies that would spoil if not eaten soon. Every day, a graceful girl named Rose opened up the cupboard to get a treat. Rose was so gentle and careful with the cupboard, she always made sure everything stayed safe and stayed happy. One day, Rose's mom opened up the cupboard and saw how tidy it was. "My Rose has spoiled this cupboard. She took such wonderful care of it!" said her mom proudly. Rose smiled and blushed and felt so proud of her work. Every day she opened up the cupboard to get a treat and every night she carefully closed it before going to bed. The cupboard was always graceful and happy, thanks to her special care.

Once upon a time, there was a brown trunk. The trunk was old and dusty.

One day, the trunk had an idea. He decided he would go for a swim!

So he hopped into the water and started swimming. But he was in the water for too long and he got very wet.

He tried to dry himself by the sun, but he still stayed wet. So he decided he needed help.

He asked a bird to help him dry. The bird flew up in the sky and got some warm air. Then he used his wings to blow the warm air onto the trunk.

Finally, the trunk was dry! And he was so happy. Now he could do whatever he wanted!

Once upon a time, there was a clever little bear. He was always looking for a way to make new friends. One day, he had a great idea!

He took some powder and put it into the river. He collected some of the powder in a cup and put it in the middle of the path. He waited and soon he saw a little rabbit coming down the path.

The little bear remembered what he had been taught by his mother: to be kind to all animals. So he offered the rabbit some of the powder from his cup! The rabbit was so happy, it hopped around and around.

The rabbit was so happy to have made a new friend. It wanted to thank the bear for being so kind. As a token of its appreciation, it took some of the powder from the bear's cup and blew it around the bear's face. The bear waved and giggled as the powder flew around him.

From that day on, the little bear and the rabbit have been the best of friends. The bear is always so clever when it comes to making new friends. He never forgets the power of kindness.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play in her garden. One day, she found a worm crawling on the ground. She thought it was very interesting, and she picked it up gently. The worm was wiggly and slimy, but Lily thought it was cute.

As she was playing in the garden, she noticed a big, shiny apple hanging from a tree. It looked very important to her, and she wanted to pick it. But as she reached out to grab it, she accidentally tore a leaf off the tree. She felt bad and put the leaf back where it belonged.

Later that day, Lily went back to the apple tree and saw that the worm had made a little home in the torn leaf. She was happy to see that the worm had found a safe place to live, and she realized that even though the leaf was torn, it was still important to the worm. From then on, Lily made sure to be careful with the plants in her garden, knowing that even the smallest things can be important to someone else.

Anna likes to dance. She dances in her room, in the garden, and in the park. She wears a pink dress and a flower crown. She spins and jumps and twirls.

One day, she sees a big poster. It has a picture of a dancer. The dancer wears a shiny dress and a tiara. She has a big smile. The poster says: "Come and see the ballet show!"

Anna wants to see the ballet show. She asks her mom: "Mom, can we go to the ballet show? Please, please, please!"

Her mom nods. She says: "Yes, we can go to the ballet show. But you have to be quiet and sit still. The ballet show is not like your dancing. It is very serious and graceful."

Anna nods. She says: "OK, mom. I will be quiet and sit still. I want to see the serious and graceful dancer."

They go to the ballet show. They sit in a big hall with many people. The lights go down. The music starts. The dancer comes on the stage. She is very beautiful. She moves like a swan. She lifts her legs and arms. She leaps and spins. She makes no sound.

Anna watches the dancer. She is amazed. She thinks: "Wow, she is so good. She is not like me. She is not silly. She is very serious and graceful."

But then, something funny happens. The dancer slips on the floor. She falls down. She makes a loud noise. She looks very surprised. The people in the hall gasp. Some of them laugh.

Anna laughs too. She thinks: "Oops, she is silly. She is like me. She makes mistakes. She is not so serious and graceful."

She claps her hands. She says: "Bravo, bravo, dancer! You are very good. And you are very funny. I like you."

Her mom smiles. She says: "Yes, she is very good. And she is very funny. You are right, Anna. You like her."

The dancer gets up. She smiles too. She bows to the people. She says: "Thank you, thank you, everyone. And thank you, little girl. You are very kind. And you are very smart. You know that dancing is not only serious and graceful. It is also silly and fun."

She winks at Anna. She says: "Maybe you can be a dancer too. You have a pink dress and a flower crown. You have a big smile. And you have a big heart."

Anna nods. She says: "Yes, maybe I can be a dancer too. I have a pink dress and a flower crown. I have a big smile. And I have a big heart."

She hugs her mom. She says: "Thank you, mom, for taking me to the ballet show. It was the best show ever. I love you."

Her mom hugs her back. She says: "You're welcome, Anna, for taking you to the ballet show. It was the best show ever. I love you too."

Once upon a time, there was a kind girl named Daisy. Daisy liked to explore. One day, Daisy went to a special room. Inside, there was a big switch. She wanted to reach it, but it was too high. Daisy was not angry. She stayed calm. She thought of a way to reach the switch.

Daisy looked around. She saw a pile of boxes. Daisy stacked the boxes one on top of the other. She did it one by one. Soon, Daisy was tall enough to reach the switch. She stretched out and flipped the switch.

Suddenly, the room lit up! Daisy was so happy. She was proud of herself for staying calm. With her good problem-solving skills, she was able to reach the switch and light up the room. Daisy smiled and skipped away.

Once upon a time there was a boy called Ben. Ben was very smart. He enjoyed playing chess, a game where you move small pieces on a board. 

One day, Ben was playing chess with his friend. He was feeling excited, but an accident happened. His friend's piece moved fast and it struck Ben's checker! 

Ben got very angry and started to cry. His friend was very sorry, but Ben did not feel better. His friend wanted to give him a small and soft bunny toy, as a gift. But Ben would not accept it. 

Ben felt so sad, that he never wanted to play chess again. That was the end of their game and it had a bad ending.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a yellow toy chest in her room. Every day, she would open the chest and play with her toys.

One sunny day, Lily decided to set up a tea party for her dolls. She took out her tea set from the yellow chest and set it up on a small table. She invited all her dolls to the tea party.

Lily and her dolls had a great time at the tea party. They laughed and played all day. When the sun went down, Lily put all her toys back into the yellow chest and said goodnight to her dolls. She was so happy and couldn't wait for the next day to play again.

Once upon a time there was a mighty toy. The toy was a big teddy bear and it was liked by everyone who saw it.

One day, a little boy named John saw the toy and he wanted to wear it. So he put it on and it was so big and heavy that he couldn't move.

John was stuck and a stranger came by. He asked John what had happened and John told him the story.

The stranger chuckled and said, "That's too bad. I don't think you can ever take it off!"

John was scared and asked the stranger what he should do, but the stranger just walked away, leaving John to figure it out by himself.

And so John had to wear the mighty toy forever! The end.

One day, a boy went for a walk. He saw a cheap toy snake on the ground. The toy snake was not real, but it looked like a real snake. The boy picked up the toy snake and took it home with him.

At home, the boy played with the toy snake. He made the snake strike at his toys. The toys fell down when the snake hit them. The boy laughed and had fun with his new toy snake.

Later, the boy showed his mom the toy snake. She was happy that he found a cheap toy to play with. They played together, making the snake strike at other toys. The boy and his mom had a fun day with the toy snake.

Once upon a time there was a girl called Jean. She was three years old.
One day while she was playing in the garden Jean found a basket. It was filled with special things - one of them was a special toy. Jean was so happy!

But Jean's brother was very jealous. He wanted Jean's toy all for himself. So his took the toy and ran away!

Jean was so sad. She wanted her toy back, but she didn't know where her brother had gone. Suddenly she had an idea. She decided to bury the basket near the tree in the garden and hope that her brother would find it.

Jean dug a deep, deep hole and put the basket in it. Then she covered it up with lots and lots of dirt and stones. Then she went inside to wait.

But Jean's brother was very, very stupid! He never even looked for the basket. So Jean's special toy stayed buried forever!

Once upon a time, there was a helpful girl named Lily. She loved to read books and spend time with her friends. One day, she found a new book at school. The book was about a kind bear who helped everyone in the forest.

Lily read the book to her friends. They all liked the story. They wanted to be like the kind bear in the book. So, they decided to help others too. They helped their teacher clean the classroom. They also helped their friends when they fell down or needed a friend to play with.

As they spent more time being helpful, Lily and her friends felt happy. They learned that being kind and helpful to others made them happy too. The moral of the story is to be kind and helpful, just like the kind bear in the book.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a beautiful cup that she loved to drink juice from. One day, she was playing with her cup and accidentally dropped it. The cup broke into many pieces and Lily was very sad.

Her mom tried to fix the cup, but it couldn't be fixed. Lily remained sad for a while, but then her mom gave her a new cup that was just as beautiful. Lily was so happy and drank her juice from the new cup every day. She loved her new cup and it remained her favorite for a long time.

Once upon a time, there was an ice cube who was very upset. He was sitting outside a big store.

The store was filled with lots of exciting things to buy. The ice cube wanted to go inside, but he was scared. What if he melted?

He was so upset that he started to cry. Then a big, friendly dog came up to him.

The dog said, "It's ok little cube. I am here to help." She gently picked up the ice cube in his mouth and went inside the store.

The ice cube was amazed. He saw so many interesting things and felt so safe with the friendly dog. When he left the store, he was no longer upset. He was happy!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy. He had a very special pine tree in the backyard of his house. The little boy loved to look at the pine tree, and to play around it.

One cold, miserable day, however, the little boy noticed that the pine tree was not looking very happy. Its needles were drooping and its branches were starting to look weak.

The little boy was very worried about the pine tree, so he decided to take care of it. He fetched some water, some soil and some mulch, and gave them to the pine tree. He also made sure to put some of his own love into it!

After a few days, the pine tree began to look very happy again. The little boy was very proud that he was able to take care of the pine tree, and now it was his own.

Mommy told Frannie to go to bed, but she didn't want to quit playing with her toy. She kept playing and playing with it, until it grew very dead. She started to cry, because she wanted her toy to be alive again. 

Mommy held her and said, "It's ok Frannie, we can find you a new toy." She dried Frannie's tears and looked around the room until she found a new toy, a beautiful car. 

Frannie was so happy, she hugged Mommy and said, "Thank you Mommy!" She was so excited to play with the new car, that she forgot all about the old toy. She quickly quit crying and enjoyed playing with her new car.

Once there was a baby who loved books. Every day, she went to the library and she saw a big bookshelf, filled with colorful books. She smiled at all of the books.

One day the baby was glad to be there, because a kind man was there. He welcomed the baby and said, "Hello, little one, do you like books?"

The baby looked up and nodded her head. She smiled and said, "I love books!"

The kind man said, "Well then, let's go look at the bookshelf. I think you'll find something you like!"

The baby smiled and the two of them went over to the bookshelf. The baby was so excited to see so many books to choose from. She chose one and the kind man said, "It looks like you found a good book!"

The baby nodded and thanked the kind man. The man said, "You're welcome. I'm glad you like the book." The baby hugged the book and said, "Thank you for introducing me to books." 

The kind man smiled and said, "My pleasure. It's always a pleasure to welcome new readers. Keep reading and let the books take you on many wonderful adventures!" 

And that's what the baby did. She read every chance she got and soon the books took her on many magical adventures.

Once there was a little girl named Emily. She was very curious and liked to laugh and joke with her friends. Today she wanted to show them how graceful she could be. So she jumped very high and each jump was an inch higher than the one before. 

Soon, she was laughing and joking with them as she jumped higher and higher. Emily was so graceful, her friends were amazed at how high she could jump. She jumped all the way until the sun set and she had to go inside. 

As she said goodnight to her friends, she joked "See you tomorrow". Everyone laughed, and Emily went to bed with a smile on her face.

Once upon a time, there was a troubled cell. It had been trapped inside its small space for a very long time and was feeling sad.

Then, one day, something amazing happened. The cell heard a sound. It was the sound of spring!

The cell was so excited. Through the small opening, the cell could feel the sunshine and the cool, fresh air.

The cell started to move. It was becoming bigger and bigger. The cell was springing from its small space onto the new, wonderful world.

The cell was very happy. It had finally been freed from its troubled space and could now explore this exciting new place.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Sarah. She loved to tie pretty bows. She had long beautiful hair and she liked to tie it up with ribbons.

One day, her mum and dad gave her a special gift. It was a neat box with a pretty bow tied on the top. Sarah was very excited and wanted to know what was inside.

Her mum said, "Let's tie the ribbon first, then you can take a look!"

So Sarah tied a neat bow on the box. When she was done, her mum said, "Now you can open the gifts."

Sarah opened the box and it was full of fun toys. She was so happy and thanked her parents for being so successful in finding her the perfect gift.

Once upon a time, there lived a little girl called Lucy. She loved playing with her toys and being creative.
One morning, she decided to try and make something special. She gathered up some of her toys and looked around for something else to use.
Just then, she spotted an old statue in a corner of her room. She picked it up and dusted it off.
"This statue needs a wash!" said Lucy.
So she fetched a bucket of soapy water and began to clean the statue. As she scrubbed and wiped the statue, the mysterious old stone came alive in her hands.
Soon, it was all clean and shiny. Lucy was very pleased with her work.
"You look beautiful," she said as she gave it a final polish.
And with that, she had created something truly special and unique.
