Once upon a time, there was a hot day. A mummy and her little boy were playing outside on the grass. They each had a piece of string and the mummy showed the boy how to make a knot. The mummy showed the boy how to spread out the knot and move it around. The boy was having fun and laughed as he moved the knot around. Suddenly, a gust of wind caught the knot and it was lifted up and spreadout around the garden. The little boy laughed as he watched the knot move around the garden. The mummy smiled and the little boy kept chasing the knot around and around until the sun went down.

Once upon a time, there was a boy called Jack. Jack was three years old and he loved to make new friends.

On this particular day, Jack wanted to introduce himself to his new neighbor. He was very excited so he grabbed a yummy candle and knocked on the neighbor's door.

A lady called Mrs. Smith opened the door. Jack smiled and said, â€œHello. I'm Jack. Would you like to be my friend?â€

Mrs. Smith smiled and said: â€œYes, I'd love to! Here, why don't we light this yummy candle together and make a wish for our new friendship?â€ 

Jack and Mrs. Smith lit the candle, made a wish and enjoyed the yummy smell of the candle. From that day on, Jack and Mrs. Smith were the best of friends!

Once upon a time, there was a mommy who loved her little girl very much. She wanted to always keep her safe. The mommy worked hard every day to make sure her little girl was happy and protected. 

The little girl had a big, organized room filled with toys. On her dresser was a photo of her and her mommy. Whenever the little girl looked at the photo, she smiled.

The mommy knew that a smile was a sign of feeling safe and happy. She wanted to make sure her little girl was always happy and safe, even when she wasn't in the same room.

The mommy put special locks on the door and windows. But the best way she protected her little girl was with hugs and kisses. 

The little girl knew her mommy was always taking care of her and she felt safe, no matter where she was. 

The little girl smiled, knowing that her mommy would always protect her and keep her safe.

Once upon a time, there was a big, hairy dog named Max. Max was very kind and loved to play with his friends. One day, Max saw a small bird that was sad.

Max wanted to comfort the bird, so he went to the bird and asked, "Why are you sad?" The bird said, "I cannot fly high like the other birds, and they laugh at me." Max felt bad for the bird and wanted to help.

Max had an idea. He called his friend, the wise old judge, who was a turtle. The judge told the other birds to be nice to the small bird. They all learned to be kind and play together. The small bird was happy, and Max felt good for helping his new friend.

Once there was a little boy named George. He was always so happy and eager to explore. Everywhere he went, he followed his urge. 

One day, George decided to visit his neighbor, who had a farm. His neighbor had all sorts of animals like chickens, ducks and cows. When George saw them, he was so excited and he wanted to feed them!

So, George went out to the barn and grabbed a handful of sweet, juicy apples. He couldn't wait to see the animals' happy faces when he offered them the food! 

George approached the chickens first, who were so excited to get a snack from George. He couldn't stop smiling as he watched them eat, and he even shared a little of his apples with the cows. 

When George was done feeding the animals, his neighbor thanked him. George was filled with joy and he thanked his neighbor in return. He was so happy that he had been able to witness everything and help out. He couldn't wait to come back to the farm again soon.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to watch the birds in her backyard. One day, her daddy asked her if she wanted to help him grill some burgers. Lily was excited to help.

As they were grilling, Lily noticed her daddy had a thoughtful expression on his face. "What are you thinking about, Daddy?" she asked.

"I'm just thinking about how lucky we are to have each other and this yummy food to eat," her daddy replied.

Lily smiled and watched the burgers sizzle on the grill. She couldn't wait to try one. When they were done, she took a big bite and exclaimed, "This is the best burger ever!" Her daddy smiled and gave her a big hug. They enjoyed their meal together, watching the birds fly by.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy who loved puzzles. He always felt happy when his mum or dad gave him a new puzzle, and he would work on it for hours. 

One day, he had a new puzzle, and he decided to settle down and open it. As he opened the box, the little boy felt even more excited. But right when he started to put the puzzle together, he heard a loud noise outside. 

His mum and dad explained to the little boy that a storm was coming. So the little boy had to pack away his puzzle and go to his room for safety. He was very sad that he couldn't finish the puzzle that day. 

The next day, the storm was gone and the sun was out. The little boy was now allowed to finish the puzzle and he settled down with a big smile on his face. He was so excited to finish the puzzle! When he was done, the puzzle was beautiful. The little boy was so proud of himself and he couldn't wait to show his mummy and daddy.

Once upon a time there lived a family of three. The mom always wanted to make everyone happy, especially her little girl. One day the mom started to think of something fun to do as a family. She thought of visiting a park and looked around to find the perfect one.

The mom and daughter soon found one that had a big, green field and lots of trees. As they started to explore the park there was a sign that said 'no running' on it. The mom told her daughter that the sign meant they had to obey the law, so they had to walk slowly instead of running.

As they kept exploring they came across a big pond with ducks and swans swimming in it. The little girl giggled when the swans started quacking. After they finished exploring the park, they started to walk back home. It was a wonderful day and the little girl wished every day could be that fun.

Once upon a time there was a girl who wanted to add some mail to her mailbox. She wanted to do it quickly so she decided to run to the mailbox. But as soon as she started to run, her friend saw her. The friend wanted to be fast too and add their mail. The two girls started to race to the mailbox. 

The girl thought she could get there first, so she added her mail quickly. But her friend was faster and added her mail first. The girl was very disappointed and she began to cry. 

The moral of the story is to think before you act. If the girl had taken the time to think before running, she may have been able to add her mail faster and gotten the result she wanted.

Once there was a little girl who had a toy car made of steel. She liked to take it everywhere she went so she could play with it.

One day, the little girl went to the park with her toy car. While she was playing, she let go of her toy and it flew away into the sky. She really missed it and was very sad. 

The little girl felt hurt that she couldn't find her toy car. She sat down on the grass and started to cry. 

Then, a kind old man came and asked what was wrong. The little girl told him about her toy car. The old man said he would help her find it and they both started searching. 

After a while, the old man found the toy car in a nearby bush. He gave it to the little girl and she was so happy. She thanked him and gave him a big hug. 

The little girl never forgot that day and she always treasured her toy car made of steel.

One day Little Bear went to the river. He liked to watch the steam rising up from the water.

He looked around and saw a boat. Little Bear decided he wanted to add it to the river. It was a little boat, so Little Bear used his paws to push it in.

The boat bobbed up and down in the river. Little Bear watched as the water lapped at the boat. The sun was setting and Little Bear watched the steam lifting up from the river.

He was happy to add the little boat to the river. He watched as it floated away, enjoying the steam and looking forward to seeing it again.

Once upon a time, in a small village, there was a kind girl named Lily. Lily was very compassionate. She loved to help others and share her toys with her friends. She had a big box of toys that she would let her friends play with.

One day, Lily's friends came to her house to play. They saw a shiny nail on the floor. They picked it up and started to play with it. They did not know that the nail could spoil their toys. They played and played, and soon, the nail had made holes in many of Lily's toys.

When Lily saw the holes in her toys, she was sad. But she did not get angry with her friends. Instead, she told them that playing with the nail had spoiled her toys. Her friends felt sorry and promised to be more careful next time. They learned that they should not play with things that can hurt or spoil their toys. And Lily, being compassionate, forgave her friends and continued to share her toys, making sure they only played with safe things.

Once upon a time there was a gray castle. Every morning and night the people around the castle would applause for the king and queen. One day, a little girl wanted to see the castle. Her parents said she could go. 

The little girl was so excited that she ran all the way to the castle's gates. The gatekeeper said she couldn't go in without the key. She had to find the special key to enter the castle. 

The little girl looked high and low but couldn't find the key. Then something magical happened. She saw a little gray mouse scurrying up the castle wall. It had something shiny in its paws. It was the key! 

The little mouse dropped the key and the girl quickly grabbed it. She clapped her hands in glee and thanked the mouse. Now she could open the castle and applaud the king and queen!

Once upon a time there was an ordinary family. They had two children, who were always happy to play together.

But one day, the siblings began to quarrel. They were shouting, making a lot of noise, and not listening to each other. Mummy and Daddy were not happy and so they decided to send the children outside, away from the house. 

So they sent them to the garden to play. They asked them to make the soil nice and soft by patting it down.

The children worked together, happily and quietly. After some time, they had made the soil look beautiful. While they were playing, they stopped quarreling and started to enjoy themselves. 

Mummy and Daddy were so pleased, that they rewarded the children with a delicious ice cream. The children smiled and the family was happy again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She had two toes on each foot. One day, she decided to go outside and play. She laid down on the grass, and looked up at the sky. It was bright and sunny, and she felt happy.

She started to doze off as she laid there, when suddenly she heard a loud noise. She quickly got up, and saw that her toe was stuck in a bush. She tried to pull it out, but it was too difficult. She started to cry and was afraid she wouldn't be able to get it out.

Suddenly, her mom ran up to her and started helping her pull at the toe. With a lot of hard work, the little girl finally got her toe out! She was so happy that she had her toe back, and she thanked her mom for saving her. The little girl learned that day that when things get difficult, it's always better to ask for help.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to explore the world around her. One day, she went on a big adventure with her family to see a big mountain with fire inside called a volcano. Lily was so excited to see the volcano and learn all about it. 

When they arrived, they saw the volcano was big and tall. It had lots of rocks and dirt around it. Lily's dad told her to be careful because the volcano could erupt and be dangerous. But Lily was ready to learn all about the volcano and how it worked. 

Lily and her family watched the volcano for a while and saw some smoke and fire coming out of it. Lily asked her dad lots of questions about how the volcano worked and why it was so big. She learned that volcanos can be very powerful and can change the land around them. Lily was happy to have seen the big volcano and was ready for more adventures. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. He had a favorite blanket. It was soft and warm. Tim took it everywhere he went. He loved his blanket very much.

One day, Tim's mom said, "Tim, you need to quit taking your blanket everywhere. You are a big boy now, and big boys don't need blankets all the time." Tim was sad, but he wanted to be a big boy. So, he left his blanket at home when he went to play outside.

While playing, Tim met a girl named Sue. Sue was healthy and strong. She saw Tim looking sad and asked, "Why are you sad, Tim?" Tim told her about his blanket and how he had to quit taking it everywhere. Sue said, "It's okay, Tim. We can still have fun without your blanket."

Tim and Sue played together all day. They ran, jumped, and laughed. Tim forgot about his blanket for a while. When it was time to go home, Tim said, "Thank you, Sue. I had fun even without my blanket." Sue smiled and said, "You're welcome, Tim. See you tomorrow!"

From that day on, Tim and Sue played together every day. Tim learned that he could be a big boy and have fun without his blanket. And sometimes, when he was at home, he still snuggled with his soft, warm blanket.

Once upon a time there was a heavy raft. It belonged to a family who all wanted to go on a fun, riverside journey. 

The father lifted the heavy raft and put it in the river. Then he, his wife and the two children, clambered inside. They were all so excited for the fun ahead. 

The family started their journey, but suddenly it started raining heavily. The rain was so strong, it made the raft sway from side to side. The father told them all to get off, so they jumped into the water with their life jackets on. 

But after a while they all had to surrender. The heavy raft was starting to drift away and they could not get back on it. The waves were too high and the family were too exhausted. 

So they waved goodbye as the heavy raft slowly drifted off, and they all hoped to see it again soon. Then they decided to walk home together, clingin to their life jackets. 

And they all lived happily ever after. The end.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Jane, who loved playing in her garden. She always sang happy little songs and liked to play with her marbles. One day, she noticed something unusual in the garden - a shiny marble all by itself. She excitedly picked it up and called it her magic marble.

Suddenly, the marble started to whisper something. Jane was so surprised she almost dropped it! She listened carefully, and the marble whispered "Magic garden". Jane couldn't believe it! 

So, she decided to explore her garden. When she looked around, she saw that it wasn't the same place she loved anymore. Everything was empty and grey! 

But then Jane remembered the whisper of her magic marble and ran to a special corner she had never noticed before. As soon as she arrived, everything became colourful and happy again!

The little girl was so pleased and grateful that she took the marble and hugged it tightly. As she looked closely, she saw some tiny words written on it: "Create your own magic". 

Jane smiled to herself and thanked her marble for bringing the magic back to her garden. From that day on, Jane shared her secret with her marbles - and the garden was filled with lots of joy and laughter!

Once there was a very anxious little boy. He was playing with his toys one day when he heard something. He started to yell. He was so scared!

Suddenly, a big tuna fish appeared! The tuna was big and it scared the little boy even more. He started to cry and yelled even louder. He was so afraid of the tuna fish!

But then, his mommy came to the rescue! She picked him up and hugged him tight. She showed him that the tuna fish was friendly and not something scary to be scared of. The little boy was relieved and hugged his mommy back.

From then on he wasn't so anxious. The tuna fish had become his new best friend!

Once upon a time, there was a mighty workman. He was strong, and worked very hard all day long. But one day he found a task that was too much for him.

The workman stopped to rest on the side of the work. He was very tired! Then he saw a little ant.

The workman asked the ant, "Do you have any ideas on how to finish my work? It's too much for me to do on my own!"

The ant replied, "It may take time and hard work, but if you try hard to yield, you can do it. "

The workman smiled and thanked the ant. He knew he had a lot of work to do, but he said that even he could do mighty things with a lot of hard work and effort.

The workman continued his work, and with each task he completed, he felt stronger. He kept going until he had finished the task! He smiled with pride, realizing that there was nothing too hard or too big for him.

The moral of the story is that with a lot of hard work and effort, even the mighty can yield when faced with a challenge.

Once there was a mommy and a baby. They were walking in the park to have some fun. Then they saw a ugly whip lying on the ground. The baby wanted to play with the whip, but the mommy said no. The baby cried and started to make a fuss. The mommy really wanted to please the baby, so she said they could park the whip somewhere safe. They parked the whip under a tree, so nobody could take it away. The baby was happy again, and the mommy and the baby continued enjoying the park together.

Once upon a time, there was a little hedgehog named Spike. Spike had spiky hair all over his body. He loved to play with his friends in the forest. One day, Spike got lost in the forest and he was upset. He didn't know how to find his way back home. 

He saw a friendly bird and asked for help. The bird listened carefully and told Spike to follow the sun. Spike followed the bird's advice and soon he found his way back home. He was so happy and grateful to the bird for answering his question. From that day on, Spike made sure to always pay attention to where he was going so he wouldn't get lost again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved to explore. One evening she went on an extra special adventure. She was excited and wanted to discover what she could find.

The little girl found a path that seemed dark and mysterious. A light caught her eye at the end of the path. She felt so brave and walked closer. As she got closer and closer, the light shone brighter and brighter! She realised the light was high up in the sky.

The little girl parted the clouds and saw a beautiful full moon. She was so excited that she wanted to tell everyone what she had found. The little girl wanted to explore more, so she promised to come back and part the clouds again. 

One night, the little girl parted the clouds and saw the most beautiful sight. There were thousands of stars shining brightly. She felt so lucky and knew one day, she would be able to explore the stars. It was like a forever adventure!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to ride her scooter outside in the park. One day, Lily's mom said, "It's a mild day, Lily. You can go outside and play with your scooter." 

Lily was so happy and ran outside with her scooter. She rode her scooter around the park and saw her friend, Timmy. Timmy said, "Can I ride your scooter, Lily?" Lily said, "Sure, but be careful and don't turn too fast."

Timmy started to ride the scooter and turned too fast. He fell off and hurt his arm. Lily felt sad and said, "I'm sorry, Timmy. I should have been more careful." Timmy went to the hospital and had to wear a cast on his arm for a long time. Lily learned that it's important to be careful and not turn too fast on her scooter.

Once upon a time, there lived a little girl. She had a fan which she liked to take everywhere.

One day, the little girl went outside to play. She wanted to show her fan to her friends. But when she opened the fan, out flew hundreds of butterflies! They flew up and away, scattering in every direction. The little girl watched in amazement as they flew off, vanishing into the distant sky.

The little girl was sad to see her butterflies go, but happy to know that they were free. She waved goodbye to them as they flew away, and she took her fan with her wherever she went, so more butterflies could come out and scatter whenever she opened it.

Sam and Ben are brothers. They like to play in the garden. One day, they see a big hole in the fence. They want to see what is on the other side.

"Let's go, Sam!" Ben says. "Maybe there are animals or toys there."

"No, Ben. Mom said we should not go out of the garden. It is not safe." Sam says. "There might be a trap or a terrible thing there."

But Ben does not listen. He runs to the hole and crawls through. Sam follows him. He does not want Ben to be alone.

They find themselves in a field. There are flowers and trees and birds. Ben is happy. He runs around and picks some flowers. Sam is scared. He looks around and sees a big net on the ground. He thinks it is a trap.

"Ben, come back!" Sam shouts. "There is a trap here. We have to go back to the garden."

But Ben does not hear him. He sees a butterfly and chases it. He runs into the net and gets tangled. He cries and tries to get out. Sam runs to him and helps him. He pulls and tugs and succeeds. He frees Ben from the trap.

"Thank you, Sam. You are a good brother." Ben says. "I am sorry I did not listen to you. Let's go back to the garden. I do not like this place."

They crawl back through the hole and run to their mom. She hugs them and asks them where they have been. They tell her the truth. She is angry and sad. She tells them they should never go out of the garden again. They might get hurt or lost. They say they are sorry and promise to obey her. They learn their lesson. They are happy to be safe in the garden.

Lily and Tom are playing in the kitchen. They want to cook a cake for mom. Lily is bossy. She tells Tom what to do.

"Tom, get the eggs. Tom, get the flour. Tom, get the milk. Tom, get the sugar. Tom, get the bowl. Tom, get the spoon. Tom, get the pan. Tom, hurry up!" Lily says.

Tom is tired of Lily's orders. He does not have fun. He wants to do something else.

"Lily, I don't want to cook. I want to play with my cars. You are too bossy. You do everything yourself." Tom says.

Lily is angry. She wants to cook with Tom. She thinks cooking is fun. She does not want to play with cars. She thinks cars are boring.

"Tom, you are silly. Cooking is fun. Cars are boring. You have to help me. We are a team. Mom will be happy if we cook a cake for her." Lily says.

Tom and Lily start to argue. They raise their voices. They make a mess. They spill the eggs, the flour, the milk, and the sugar. They drop the bowl, the spoon, and the pan. They do not notice mom coming home.

Mom sees the kitchen. She sees Lily and Tom. She is not happy. She is angry.

"Lily and Tom, what are you doing? Why are you making such a noise? Why are you making such a mess? You are not cooking. You are fighting. You are not a team. You are naughty." Mom says.

Lily and Tom feel sorry. They stop arguing. They apologize to mom. They help mom clean the kitchen. They hug mom. They say they love her.

Mom forgives Lily and Tom. She hugs them back. She says she loves them too. She says they can cook a cake together another day. She says they have to be nice to each other. She says they have to share and take turns. She says they have to have fun.

The little girl was so excited; she was going to buy a waffle. She walked into the shop, the bells jingling as she opened the door.

The girl said to the shopkeeper, "Waffle please!"
The shopkeeper smiled and said, "What kind of waffle would you like? We have chocolate, lemon and strawberry."

The girl thought carefully, then said, "Strawberry waffle please!"

The shopkeeper nodded and said, "That's a delicious choice. Here you go - it's a delicate and tasty strawberry waffle!"

The girl was so happy. She thanked the shopkeeper and skipped outside, waffle in hand, ready to enjoy it in the sunshine.

Once there was a gifted little girl named Gina. She was only three years old, but she was very special. Everywhere she went, people stopped to admire her.

One day, Gina and her family went to the woods. When they got there, it was very quiet. They all listened carefully, and soon they heard something that made them all smile. Gina heard it first and she shouted to her family "Come!" 

The family all followed Gina and they were soon in a beautiful meadow. Right in the middle of the meadow was a family of deer, a doe and her two fawns. Gina was awestruck. She looked at the deer so quietly and gently that the deer did not move.

Gina was so special and gifted that she had a special way with animals. She was able to communicate with the deer, and soon they were all playing together. The family spent the rest of the day in the meadow, enjoying Gina's special gift.

Once upon a time, there was a navy. It was filled with fish, dolphins and seals. The navy was creative. It had different colors, shapes and sizes. Everyone loved the navy.

One day, a seal in the navy told a lie. He said, â€œI saw a whale swim past us!â€ Everyone in the navy was excited, but when they looked for the whale, it wasnâ€™t there. The seal had lied.

Everyone in the navy was so sad. They talked about how important it is to be honest. They realized that lying never leads to anything good.

The seal was ashamed of himself. He apologized for lying, and promised to never do it again. From then on, he was honest and creative. Everyone in the navy was happy, and they learned an important lesson.

Once upon a time, there was a happy dog named Spot. Spot loved to play at the park. One day, Spot met a pretty dog named Daisy. They played and had fun together. Spot knew he wanted to marry Daisy one day.

The next day, Spot and Daisy went to the park again. They played with a big red ball. Spot was very alert. He knew he had to be careful and watch out for Daisy. He wanted to keep her safe.

One day, while they were playing in the park, Spot found a shiny ring. He knew this was the perfect time to ask Daisy to marry him. Spot gave the ring to Daisy, and she said yes! They were so happy and continued to play at the park every day.

One day, a boy named Tim was walking with his mom and dad. They were in a big park and it was very hot. Suddenly, Tim noticed that the trees were creating a lot of shade. He said to his mom and dad, "Look! The shade is wide!" His mom and dad smiled. They were happy to see how wide the shade was.

They walked a bit further and the shade was getting bigger. Tim shouted, "Yay! The shade is increasing!" Mom and dad laughed. The sun was still very hot and the shade was a relief. 

They kept walking and they looked up. The shade was above them and it made them feel cool. Tim said, "Look! The shade is still increasing!" Mom and dad smiled and they agreed.

Suddenly, they reached a part of the park with no shade. The sun was very hot and they were all hot. Tim said, "Let's walk back so I can see the shade increase again!" Mom and dad smiled and they all walked back to see the shade getting bigger. 

By the end of their walk, the shade was very wide. They were all feeling cool and refreshed. Tim said, "It's great to see the shade increase!" and mom and dad agreed.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. Her name was Lucy, and she was three years old.

One day, Lucy saw something purple in the sky. She wondered what it was and went to take a closer look. When she got closer, she saw it was a ghost!

The Ghost was scared and asked Lucy not to cut it. Lucy, who didn't know what "cut" meant, agreed to not cut it.

The Ghost, feeling relieved, thanked Lucy with a sparkly gift. After, he flew away.

Later, Lucy asked her mom about the word "cut", and her mom explained that it means to hurt or destroy something. Lucy was happy she never cut the Ghost, as it would have been unkind to hurt something.

The moral of this story is that it's important to always be kind and to always think before you act.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Dolly. Dolly lived in a small empty building with her family. One day, she wanted to go outside to explore. Her mom said, "It is too hot outside, so let's sit in the empty building".

Dolly asked, "What can we do in the empty building?" Mom said, "We can play make-believe!"

So they sat down together in the empty building. Dolly pretended to be a princess and her mom was a queen. They pretended to go on lots of adventures, like looking for the lost treasure of the forest. 

As they played, they heard a noise outside. A small bunny hopped into the building and sat next to them. It was the cutest bunny that Dolly had ever seen! They all smiled at each other and continued to play make-believe until the sun went down.

Once upon a time there was a little boy called Peter. Peter was playing in his garden with his toy iron. He found it very amusing to pinch the iron. All of a sudden, he heard a loud noise. It scared him, so he ran to his mother for help.

"Mama, what was that noise?" Peter asked.

"Don't worry, Peter," said his mother kindly. "It was just Mr. Smith ironing his clothes. He needed to press them so they look nice and smooth."

Peter thought this was very kind of Mr. Smith. So Peter decided to pinch his toy iron in order to help him out. It wasn't as powerful as a real iron, but he hoped it would still help make Mr. Smith's clothes look nice.

The next day, Peter ran to Mr. Smith's house to show him the iron.

"Wow, thank you, Peter!" said Mr. Smith, with a smile. "You're a very kind boy!"

Peter was very proud of himself. From then on, he always liked to help out any way he could. He learned that helping others can make them feel happy. All thanks to his toy iron.

Once there was a little boy named Jack. He loved playing outside on a sunny day. Jack was very loyal to his kite and often took it with him when he went outside. He would plan his days accordingly so that he could be sure to spend some time flying his kite.

One day Jack made a plan to fly his kite for a really long time. He carefully checked that the string was secure and that his kite was ready to go. Then he ran outside to find the perfect spot for flying.

Jack was thrilled as the kite went higher and higher. He enjoyed the freedom of flying and the breeze in his hair. He felt so proud of his loyal kite and the plan he had made. Jack spent the whole morning running around and playing with his kite. He couldn't have asked for a better day.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy liked to play outside in the sun. One day, Timmy's mommy gave him a juice box. Timmy was so excited to drink it, but he couldn't open it. Tom and Jane hugged and went back to playing their game. From then on, they always remembered to be gentle with each other.

Once upon a time, there was an original robot. He wanted to stand up for himself, so he decided to fight. He was brave and strong, but the other robots were bigger and mean. Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She was three years old. She liked to dream about things she wanted to do and places she wanted to go. She also liked to see her neighbor.

Once upon a time, there were two sweet friends called Tom and Jill. Tom and Jill were the best of friends and loved to do everything together. One day, Tom and Jill were in the woods looking for a special treat.

There was once a rich family who owned a big, red automobile. The whole family piled into the car and went to the park. They laughed and talked as they drove. 

When they arrived at the park, they saw a huge puddle. The big automobile couldn't fit through it so Dad said, "Hey kids, let's split up!"

The kids were very excited and ran off in different directions. Dad and mom smiled at each other and went for a walk.

When Dad and Mom returned from their walk, they were very surprised to see their children playing in the mud. They laughed and said, "Good job splitting up!" 

And that's how the rich family split up and had fun at the park.

One day, John was playing outside in the rain. He splashed in puddles and kicked up mud. He was having lots of fun, and was almost completely soaked.

He went inside to tell his mom. "Mom, I'm ready to go play again," he said.

"Not so fast, John," said Mom. She pointed to John's muscles. "You have to dry off first before you go back out there, otherwise you'll catch a cold."

When he stepped outside again, the sun was out and the sky was blue. John was so excited that he ran full speed and laughed with joy. He was happy he'd listened to his mom, and he'd stopped to get ready for the adventure ahead.

Once upon a time, there were two brothers, Jack and John. One day, Jack was feeling very excited, and he decided to take out his jar of marbles. 

â€œWould you like to play with me?â€ asked Jack, looking up to his big brother John.

From that day onwards, John and Jack always put things back where they belonged. This taught them the lesson to be tidy and organised all the time.

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play with their toys. They had many toys, but they always wanted more. They asked their mom and dad for new toys every day. Mom and dad said no, because they had enough toys and they should be happy with what they had. But Lily and Ben did not listen. They cried and whined and threw tantrums. They said they were not happy and they wanted more toys.

One day, mom and dad had to go to work and they left Lily and Ben with their grandma. Grandma was very kind and gentle. She made them pancakes for breakfast and read them stories. She also gave them a big box of toys that she had saved from when mom and dad were little. Lily and Ben were very excited. They opened the box and saw many toys that they had never seen before. There were cars and dolls and puzzles and books and blocks and animals. Lily and Ben grabbed the toys and ran to their room. They did not say thank you to grandma. They did not share the toys with each other. They fought and snatched and broke the toys. They made a big mess in their room.

Grandma heard the noise and came to their room. She saw the toys scattered and torn and ruined. She saw Lily and Ben crying and yelling. She was very sad and angry. She said, "Lily and Ben, you have spoiled the toys that I gave you. You have spoiled the fun that you could have had. You have spoiled the day that we could have spent together. You have been very selfish and ungrateful. You do not deserve these toys. You need to learn to be happy with what you have and to share and care for others. Now you have to clean up this mess and put the toys back in the box. And you have to say sorry to me and to each other. And you have to sit in the corner and think about what you have done. No more toys for you today."

Lily and Ben felt very ashamed and sorry. They did what grandma said. They cleaned up the mess and put the toys back in the box. They said sorry to grandma and to each other. They sat in the corner and thought about what they had done. They realized that they had been very bad and that they had hurt grandma and themselves. They wished they had been more kind and thankful and happy. They wished they had played nicely with the toys and with each other. They wished they had spent more time with grandma and listened to her stories.

The rest of the day was very quiet and boring. There was no more noise and fun and laughter. There was only silence and sadness and regret. Lily and Ben learned a hard lesson that day. They learned that being greedy and spoiled can make you lose what you have and what you love. They learned that being happy and grateful and sharing can make you gain more than you expect. They learned that being good and respectful and loving can make you and others happy. They learned that sometimes, less is more.

Once upon a time, there was a small church. Inside the church, there was a little girl. She liked to dream big dreams. Every day, she would sit in the church and imagine wonderful things. She dreamt of being a princess in a far away castle, and of being able to fly like a bird.

Every day, when she stepped out of the church, she would see an old lady. The old lady was always smiling at the little girl. She always said hello and asked the little girl what she had dreamt of while in the church.

One day, the old lady asked the little girl if she could come with her. The little girl agreed, and followed the old lady down a small path that led away from the church. As they walked, the old woman talked to the little girl about how she too had dreamt big dreams when she was a child.

At the end of the path, the little girl and the old lady entered a magical forest. This was the place that the old lady had dreamt about when she was a child. Together, the two of them explored the forest and talked about the things they had dreamt of.

The little girl was so excited to have been able to share this special adventure with the old lady. She thanked her and promised to keep dreaming big dreams inside the little church.

Once upon a time, in an ordinary little town, there lived a boy named Tim. Tim was very hungry. His stomach made loud noises. He wanted to eat something yummy.

Tim saw a big apple tree. He asked his friend, Sam, "Can you please help me get an apple?" Sam agreed and helped Tim climb the tree. They both picked apples and ate them. But the apples were not ordinary apples.

Soon, Tim and Sam felt sick. Their stomachs hurt a lot. They cried out, "Oh no! What did we eat?" They did not know that the apples were bad apples.

In the end, Tim and Sam were still sick. They learned a lesson to not eat apples from that tree again. Their ordinary day turned into a very bad day.

Once there was a mountain and upon it a billboard. Each day the sun shined brightly and the trees sang. But one day, the sun became very harsh, and the billboard got bigger and bigger.

The animals were scared and ran away from it. They gathered around to figure out what to do. 

The peacock spoke first. "Let us ask the mountain," said the peacock.

The animals shouted to the mountain. They asked, "Why does the billboard increase? It's too harsh for us."

The mountain replied, "I cannot stop it. It is beyond my control." 

The animals then looked around at each other, but no one had any idea how to make the billboard reduce. So the animals kept running away from the bright and harsh billboard. 

All the animals lived in fear, until one day the sun went away and the billboard reduced back to its original size. The animals rejoiced and ran home, happy to be back in the peaceful mountain.

Once upon a time, there was a little tree. It was very young, but it liked to grow. So every day, it would try to get bigger.

One day, though, something bad happened. A mean, ignorant person chopped the little tree into a bunch of pieces. The little tree was so sad and angry!

But then something wonderful happened. The pieces of the little tree started to grow! Even though it was chopped into pieces, it was still able to grow.

Eventually, the pieces grew into a big and beautiful tree. The tree was even bigger than it used to be!

At the end, the little tree taught everyone an important lesson: you should never give up, no matter how ignorant someone is.

Once upon a time, there were two best friends named Tom and Jane. Tom and Jane were both three years old and liked playing together.

One day, Tom wanted to go on an adventure. Jane was worried but Tom told her he would be all right. So off they went.

As they explored, Tom noticed something shiny and sparkling in the grass. Tom reached for it and realized it was a sparkling stone. He held it in his hand and showed it to Jane.

â€œLook! I found a sparkling stone!â€ Tom said, smiling.

Once there was a brave man. He had an axe and he was always very alert. One day, he felt a little worried. So he grabbed his axe and ran into the dark woods. He was very brave, but he was also very scared. He felt the trees around him, swaying in the wind. He felt his heart racing. He was so alert and focused, looking for any signs of danger. Suddenly, he heard a noise! He couldn't believe his ears. He gripped his axe tightly and felt ready to take on anything. He was brave and alert. He had made it through the dark woods and now he felt proud.

Mary was a young girl who often felt very sad. She wanted to make her sadness go away, so she went out in search of wisdom. Everywhere she looked, Mary saw people with wisdom, but they all refused to share it with her.

After a long day of looking, Mary finally found a wise old woman. The woman was happy to share her wisdom with Mary and she held her hands. With her hands in the woman's, Mary suddenly felt better.

The woman spoke to Mary, telling her that everyone needs wisdom to be strong and happy. She said that it was ok to feel sad, but that Mary must always hold tightly onto the wisdom she found.

Mary thanked the woman for her kind words and promised to always treasure her wisdom. With her new knowledge, Mary was able to face each day with a smile.

Mama was very excited. She had a special box in her hands that she was about to unpack. "Let's see what's inside," she said to her daughter. The daughter was very curious and could not help but wonder what was inside the box. 

Mama carefully took out the first item, it was a gray teddy bear. They both hugged the bear and laughed. Then mama unpack the next item, it was a strawberry! It was so big and juicy that they both couldn't wait to eat it. 

The daughter asked if she could eat the strawberry right away, but Mama said that she wanted to take it to the park and share it with everyone. The daughter was so happy, she knew that everyone was going to love the strawberry. 

Mama packed up the box and they went to the park. Everyone was so excited to see the big, juicy, red strawberry. They all shared it with each other - it was the best strawberry ever!

Once there was a little girl named Mia. She was feeling very anxious because she saw something strange in her backyard - a tunnel!
 Mia wanted to fix it and make it better.

She walked up to the tunnel and said "Let's fix it together!"

After she filled the tunnel up all the way, Mia stepped back and looked at her work. The tunnel was fixed! She was so proud of herself and smiled with joy.

Once upon a time, there was a little gray cat. The cat loved to play outside. One day, the cat went to the park to play.

At the park, the cat saw a big tree. The tree had a nice view. The cat wanted to climb the tree and see the view. So, the cat started to climb the tree.

Once there was a brave little girl named Sarah. She loved to explore the beach near her house.

One day, Sarah went down to the beach. She wanted to examine the sand. But when Sarah tried to touch the sand, she noticed that it felt very hot! Sarah was shocked.

"Why is the sand so hot?" Sarah asked herself. She looked pretty puzzled by this.

Just then, Sarah noticed a turtle. It was a stubborn turtle and it wouldn't move.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She was very adventurous. One day she went to the park and saw a big slide. She wanted to go down the slide so she tried it.

Mandy and Sam were walking in the park. Mandy said to Sam, "Let's find something interesting" Sam said, "Let's look over there" They saw a silver car. They went up to the car and Mandy said, "Let's show it!" Sam said, "Yes!" They showed the car to their parents.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy. His name was Tim. He was three years old. 

One day, Tim was playing in the garden when he discovered a delicate flower. He admired its beauty and took a closer look at it. 

Suddenly, Tim heard a voice. It was a fairy! "Well done, Tim!", said the fairy, "You found the magical flower."

The fairy replied, "It needs some oil to help it become strong and powerful. If you put some oil on the delicate flower, it will give you a special power."

Tim was delighted! He put a drop of oil onto the delicate flower, and then applauded. 

Suddenly, the magical flower glowed brightly and the special power was revealed. From then on, Tim always kept the flower nearby. Whenever he wanted to use the magic, he would applaud, and the delicate flower would help him. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a dog named Max. Max had a pretty collar that he liked to wear. The collar was his favorite thing in the world. Max's friend, a cat named Luna, did not have a collar. Luna was sad and wanted a collar too.

Once upon a time, there was a gentle prune. The prune was so nice and shiny, everyone wanted to examine it. One day, a 3 year old child came up to it and started to examine it. Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play and have fun. One night, Lily's mommy told her it was time for bed. Lily didn't want to go to her bedroom because it was cold in there.

Lily went back to her bedroom but she was still cold. She couldn't sleep, so she got up and went to the living room again. This time, mommy was really upset. She told Lily to go back to bed and stay there.

Lily went back to her bedroom but she was still cold and couldn't sleep. She started to cry. Suddenly, she heard a loud noise outside. She was scared and didn't know what to do. She wanted her mommy, but she was too scared to leave her bedroom. Unfortunately, the bad ending is that Lily was too scared to get help and ended up getting hurt.

One day, Little Joe was playing in his garden. He saw a big, tall fence. Little Joe was so excited. He said to his mom, "Mom, I can spray the fence and make it all colorful!"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Anna. She was three years old, and she loved exploring.

Jack was happy to be at the beach. He had been looking forward to it all day. He saw lots of people jumping in the water and surfing on their boards. Everyone was having a lot of fun.

Once upon a time there were two best friends, Sally and Matt. They were always together, doing all sorts of fun things. 

One day, Sally and Matt were walking around in the woods when they saw a fierce bear. Sally was scared and wanted to turn back, but Matt said that they should trust the bear and keep going.

So they decided to take a chance and keep walking. They came up to a big clearing where the bear was eating some food.

Sally said, "I'm scared. What if the bear is mean?"

The bear smiled at them and even offered them some of his food. They happily shared it with the bear and even became friends with him.

Once upon a time, there lived a little girl called Lucy who was three years old. Lucy loved to rock in her chair. She'd rock back and forth, from side to side, singing to herself.

One day, she was in her chair and she noticed something strange. There was a man standing in front of her TV! She didn't know who he was.

Lucy was a bit scared, so she decided to stay in her chair. She asked, "Who are you?"

The man replied in a gruff voice, "I'm here to fix the TV. Don't worry, I'm an expert."

Lucy didn't think he looked very expert. In fact, he seemed quite ignorant! But since he said he was here to help, she smiled and said, "Okay, I guess you can stay and work on the TV."

The man nodded and set right to work. Lucy kept rocking in her chair, watching him, but eventually he fixed the TV. Afterward, he said goodbye and left.

Lucy was glad the TV was fixed, and she was glad the ignorant man was gone. From now on, her rocking chair was all hers!

Once upon a time, there was a frog called Fred. He was different from the other frogs because he liked to wear lots of crazy clothes!

One day, Fred decided to go for a walk. He could not believe what he saw: all the other frogs were wearing the same clothes!

Fred was very confused. He asked what everyone was doing.

"We're all wearing the same clothes to fit in!" everyone replied.

But Fred shook his head. He said that it was more important to be yourself rather than fit in with everyone else.

So, Fred taught all the other frogs a valuable lesson: it is alright to be different and to wear whatever you like. After all, only you know what you feel comfortable in!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Lucy. She liked to park her bicycle under the big tree in the park. Every day, she went to the park to ride her bicycle.

One day, she was riding her bicycle and saw the moon in the sky. It was so bright and looked so graceful. She stopped and just stared at it for a few minutes.

Suddenly, she heard a noise. It was a flock of birds flying above her head. They were so graceful and looked so beautiful! Lucy smiled and watched them until they flew away.

After that, she put her bicycle back in the park and went home.

Once upon a time, there was a bright whale. He was gliding through the sea, enjoying the sun that sparkled down on the water. All of a sudden, a little girl jumped into the sea beside him. She said, "Hello, whale! I want to examine you!"

The whale was so surprised that he stopped swimming. He looked at the little girl and said, "Why do you want to examine me?"

The little girl smiled and said, "Because you look so shiny and I want to get a closer look."

The whale thought for a moment and then said, "Ok, I suppose that would be okay. But you have to be gentle."

The little girl nodded and began to examine the whale. She looked at his fins and his tail, and then brushed her hand softly across his shiny skin. When she was finished, the whale said, "Thank you for examining me, it was very nice to meet you!"

The little girl smiled, waved goodbye, and swam away. The whale watched as she disappeared into the distance, then he turned and went back to enjoying the sunny day.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who loved to travel. She loved exploring new places and seeing different things.

One day, she went to the beach and played in the warm, hot sand. Then she decided to go on an adventure. She traveled to a forest and saw many amazing things like a bubbling stream, a big and tall tree and even a huge mirror.

Then she traveled back home, happy to have gone on such a fun adventure. Everywhere she went, she remembered the big mirror she saw in the forest.

"Wow, you are doing a great job, Lily and Ben. You are very good helpers. The meal looks lovely. Let's set the table and call dad." Mom says.

They put plates and forks and napkins on the table. They also put the pasta and cheese and the salad on the table. They call dad, who is working in his office. He comes and hugs them and says he is hungry.

"Look, dad. We made dinner for you. We made pasta and cheese and salad. Do you like it?" Ben says.

"I love it, Ben. And I love you and Lily. And I love mom. You are a wonderful family. Thank you for this lovely meal." Dad says.

They all sit down and eat. They talk and laugh and enjoy the food. They are happy and close. They say thank you to mom and to each other. They clear the table and wash the dishes. Then they have fruit and cake for dessert. They read a story and go to bed. They dream of more fun things to do tomorrow.

Once upon a time there were two beetle friends, Daisy and George. Daisy was so excited to go outside and explore the sunshine. But George was feeling a bit nervous.

"Why are you so nervous George?" asked Daisy. 

"I'm worried I'll spoil the fun," replied George.

So Daisy and George decided to stay close together and took tiny steps on their way out. All of a sudden Daisy spotted a colourful flower petal. She pointed it out to George and they both knew it was special. 

Suddenly a little bee came and touched the flower with its antennae. Daisy and George were so excited they both jumped into the air. But George was feeling very nervous.

"Let's jump again, I know it will be fun!" said Daisy. 

George said, "I'm still a bit nervous, but I'll try it anyway." So Daisy and George jumped together, feeling very brave, and it was so much fun!

Tina was very scared when it was dark outside. But her mommy knew just the thing to help. She got out a dependable flashlight and gave it to Tina. You can use it to feel brave, her mommy said while she smiled and gave Tina a hug.

Tina wiped away her tears and with the flashlight in her hands, she was ready to explore. For a long time she searched for new things to find. Then, when a gentle whisper brushed past her, Tina stopped in her tracks! She shone the flashlight around and saw a beautiful butterfly.

Tina smiled and whispered a happy hello to her new friend. She would always have the flashlight to depend on when it was time for a nighttime adventure.

One day, a curious little girl and her family went on a ride. They got into their truck and drove off. 

The little girl was excited to be on the ride. She loved trucks and was curious to see where they were headed. But soon her curiosity turned to worry. 

The truck started to make funny noises and the ride got bumpy. The little girl was scared and started to cry. 

Fortunately, the truck made it through the rough patch and the ride continued. Everyone was relieved and the little girl was excited to find out where their ride would take them.

One day Mama and her daughter went on an adventure. Mama had a special key and she used it to lock the door. They walked down the street and saw a weird looking house. Mama took out a piece of paper and said, â€œI need to read this page.â€

â€œWhat does it say?â€ asked the little girl.

â€œIt says, letâ€™s go find the magic,â€ said Mama.

So they went inside the weird house. As they explored, they saw a room with a magic box. Mama opened the box and found a key inside.

â€œThis key can lock and unlock the magic,â€ said Mama. She put the key into the box and it made a sparkly noise.

â€œLetâ€™s go explore some more,â€ said Mama.

So they went around the house and found more secrets. By the time they were done, the sun was setting.
