Lily and Tom were friends who liked to play music. Lily had a drum that she loved to bang with her hands. Tom had a flute that he blew with his mouth. They made a lot of noise, but they had fun.

One day, they went to the park to play music for the birds and the squirrels. They found a nice spot under a big tree and started to play. The birds and the squirrels came to listen and dance. Lily and Tom were happy.

But then, a big dog came running to the park. He saw Lily's drum and thought it was a toy. He ran to Lily and grabbed her drum with his teeth. He ran away with the drum, wagging his tail.

Lily was very sad. She cried and cried. Tom was angry. He shouted at the dog.

"Hey, you bad dog! Give back Lily's drum! That is not your toy! That is her music!"

The dog did not listen. He kept running with the drum. He thought it was fun to make Lily and Tom chase him.

Lily and Tom ran after the dog, but they could not catch him. He was too fast and too strong. He was a mighty dog.

They ran and ran, until they came to a house. The house had a fence and a gate. The dog ran inside the gate and closed it with his paw. He thought he was safe.

But the house was not his house. It was the house of a farmer. The farmer had a lot of animals: cows, pigs, chickens, and a cat. The animals did not like the dog. They did not like his noise and his smell.

The dog saw the animals and wanted to play with them. He dropped the drum and ran to the animals. He barked and jumped and chased them.

The animals were scared and angry. They did not want to play with the dog. They wanted him to go away.

The cow mooed and kicked the dog with her hoof. The pig oinked and bit the dog with his snout. The chicken clucked and pecked the dog with her beak. The cat meowed and scratched the dog with her claws.

The dog was hurt and scared. He wished he had not taken the drum. He wished he had not run to the house. He wished he had listened to Tom.

He ran to the gate and opened it with his paw. He ran out of the house and back to the park. He saw Lily and Tom waiting for him. He saw the drum on the ground.

He felt sorry for what he had done. He went to Lily and Tom and wagged his tail. He licked their faces and gave them the drum.

Lily and Tom were surprised and happy. They forgave the dog and hugged him. They thanked him for giving back the drum.

The dog learned his lesson. He learned that he should not take things that are not his. He learned that he should be nice to other animals. He learned that music is better than toys.

He asked Lily and Tom if he could play music with them. They said yes and smiled. They gave him a flute and taught him how to blow it. They played music together for the birds and the squirrels. They became friends.

The moral of the story is: Do not be greedy and selfish. Be kind and respectful. Share and enjoy music.

Lily and Ben were playing in the garden. They liked to dig in the dirt and look for bugs. Lily found a big worm and showed it to Ben. Ben said, "Ew, that is disgusting! Put it back!" Lily said, "No, it is my friend. I will keep it in a jar." She ran inside the house to find a jar.

Ben followed her, but he stopped at the door. He saw something on the roof. It was big and black and furry. It had a long tail and sharp teeth. It was a rat. Ben was scared. He said, "Lily, come back! There is a rat on the roof!" But Lily did not hear him. She was in the kitchen, looking for a jar.

The rat saw Ben and jumped down from the roof. It landed on Ben's head and bit his ear. Ben screamed and ran away. Lily heard him and came out of the kitchen. She saw the rat on the ground and Ben crying. She said, "What happened? What is that?" Ben said, "It is a rat! It was on the roof and it bit me!" Lily said, "Oh no, that is disgusting! We need to tell mom!"

They ran to the house and found mom. Mom saw Ben's ear and said, "What happened to you? You are bleeding!" Ben said, "A rat bit me! It was on the roof!" Mom said, "A rat? On the roof? That is not good. We need to call the pest control." She took Ben to the bathroom and cleaned his ear. She put a band-aid on it and gave him a hug. She said, "You are brave, Ben. I am sorry that happened to you."

Lily felt bad for Ben. She said, "I am sorry too, Ben. I was not listening to you. I was busy with my worm." She showed him the jar with the worm inside. Ben said, "That is okay, Lily. I am glad you have a friend. But can you please keep it away from me? I do not like worms. They are disgusting." Lily said, "Okay, Ben. I will keep it in my room. But can I show it to dad when he comes home?" Ben said, "Sure, Lily. But do not let the rat see it. It might want to eat it." They laughed and hugged. They were happy to have each other.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside and run around. One day, Timmy's mom said, "Timmy, it's time to do some exercise." Timmy didn't want to do exercise, but he knew he had to listen to his mom.

As Timmy was doing his exercise, he saw a bird fall from the sky. Timmy said, "Mommy, look! The bird fell down." His mom said, "Oh no, the bird might be dead." Timmy felt sad for the bird.

Timmy's mom picked up the bird and they took it to the vet. The vet said the bird was just tired and needed some rest. Timmy was happy to hear that the bird wasn't dead. From that day on, Timmy made sure to always do his exercise so he wouldn't fall down like the bird did.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Lily was walking in the park with her mommy. It was a rainy day and there were many puddles on the ground. Lily loved to jump in them and splash water everywhere. Suddenly, she saw a shiny penny in one of the puddles. 

"Mommy, look! I found a penny!" Lily said, pointing at the puddle. 

Her mommy smiled and said, "You're so lucky! Let's pick it up." 

As they bent down to pick up the penny, a frog appeared out of nowhere and hopped into the puddle. 

"Ribbit, ribbit!" the frog said. 

Lily giggled and said, "Hi froggy! You're in my puddle!" 

The frog hopped away and Lily and her mommy continued their walk, feeling happy and lucky to have found a penny and met a friendly frog.

Max loved to swim. He would put on his floaties and go to the pool at his house. He loved the way the cool, clean water would feel on his skin. One day, his mommy came to the pool with a magazine. 

"Mommy, what's that?" Max said, pointing at the magazine. 

"It's a magazine," his mommy said. "It has stories and pictures in it!"

Max smiled. He grabbed the magazine and jumped in the pool. He swam around, looking at the pictures in the magazine as he swam. He laughed as he flipped through the pages, feeling the cool, clean water on his skin.

Finally, he swam back to his mommy and handed her the magazine. He had had so much fun swimming and reading the magazine. 

"Thank you for the magazine, Mommy!" Max said with a big smile.

His mommy smiled back. "You're welcome, sweetheart!"

Lila and Ben loved to play with their dad's old record player. They liked to put on different records and dance and sing along. Sometimes they pretended to be rock stars or pirates or princesses. One day, they found a record that had a picture of a big wave and a surf board on it. They wondered what it sounded like.

"Let's play this one!" Ben said, holding the record.

"Okay, but we have to be careful. Dad said we can only play with his records if we are obedient and don't scratch them," Lila said.

They put the record on the player and turned it on. They heard a loud sound of water crashing and a voice saying "Surf's up, dudes!" They laughed and started to jump and dance around the room, pretending to surf on the carpet.

"Look at me, I'm a surf champion!" Ben shouted, waving his arms.

"Me too, me too!" Lila said, spinning around.

They were having so much fun that they didn't hear their dad coming home from work. He opened the door and saw them making a mess of his record collection. He was not happy.

"Hey, what are you two doing?" he asked, frowning.

"Sorry, Dad, we were just playing with your records," Lila said, looking guilty.

"We found this cool one with surf music," Ben said, holding up the record.

Dad looked at the record and smiled. He remembered that it was his favorite record when he was a kid. He used to dream of surfing on big waves like the ones on the cover.

"I see. Well, I'm glad you like it, but you have to be more careful with my records. They are very old and fragile. And you have to ask me before you use them, okay?" he said.

"Okay, Dad, we're sorry," Lila and Ben said.

Dad hugged them and said, "It's okay, I forgive you. How about we listen to this record together and I'll tell you some stories about surfing?"

"Yay, that sounds fun!" Lila and Ben said.

They cleaned up the records and put them back in their sleeves. Then they sat on the couch with Dad and listened to the surf music. Dad told them about the time he went surfing with his friends and how he fell off his board and got a big bruise. He also taught them some surf slang and showed them some surf moves. Lila and Ben learned a lot and had a great time with their dad. They decided that surfing was cool and that they wanted to try it someday. They also decided that they would be more obedient and respectful of their dad's records. They loved their dad and his records.

Once upon a time there was a man who wanted to sell something. He had a big switch. He wanted to make other people happy with the switch, so he went around selling it.

He went to a market and saw many people. He was scared to go up to them, but he was so proud of the switch. He kept thinking, "I have to sell my switch". 

So he went up to the people and said, "I'm selling my switch". He showed them the switch, and they liked it very much. They bought it and went away with a smile.

The man was so happy and proud. He had sold his switch, and he was feeling very good!

Mommy was very happy. She opened the thin folder and smiled. Little Jimmy saw her smiling and nodded. He was very excited because he knew something special was inside the folder.

Mommy pulled out two tickets and showed them to Jimmy. His eyes lit up and he nodded again, this time much more excitedly. Mommy told Jimmy that the tickets were for a fun park.

Jimmy was so happy he jumped up and down. He clapped his hands and asked if he could go today. Mommy smiled and said yes, it was time for a fun day out! She hugged Jimmy and they both nodded. 

They grabbed their bags and ran out the door. Jimmy waved goodbye to the folder as they left, never forgetting the surprise tickets that he found inside.

One day, a girl named Lily went to the park with her mom. She had her chalk with her to draw on the sidewalk. Lily found a comfortable spot and started to draw a big sun.

A boy named Tim came and said, "I want to use the chalk too!" Lily didn't want to share, so they both started to cry. Their moms came and told them, "You need to learn to share and relax."

Lily and Tim listened and decided to share the chalk. They drew a big, beautiful rainbow together. They both felt happy and learned that sharing can be fun.

Once upon a time there were two children, James and Liza. They were very excited because they decided to explore a mill that they saw.

"Let's go inside." said James. 
"Yes, that looks interesting." said Liza.

So they opened the door and went inside. Everything was strange and new. They heard strange noises and saw lots of machines. 

Suddenly, James heard a loud noise. "What was that?" he asked.
Liza looked around and said, "I don't know, but let's leave now!"

So they quickly ran out of the mill. But when they closed the door behind them, they saw a giant ditch and they couldn't get back. They were stuck and couldn't get out. Their adventure had to end like this.

Once upon a time there was an enormous robot. He was making a special part for his robot friend. He worked hard almost all day and night. He was very careful putting the tiny part together. Eventually he finished. The robot was so happy with the new part! He was very excited to put it in his robot friend.

The enormous robot picked up the part and carried it carefully through the forest. Suddenly, it saw a huge lake. He thought it was so pretty! He even saw a few fish swimming around. He wanted to stay and watch the fish, but he had to keep going.

He reached his robot friend's house and installed the new part. When he fixed the part, the robot friend felt all better. He thanked the enormous robot and they both said goodbye. The enormous robot went back home with a smile on his face, glad he had helped his friend.

Once there was a little girl named Caroline. She was just 3 years old and loved to play. One day, her mommy took her to the park.

Caroline was so excited! She ran around and jumped on the swings and laughed. Then she saw something interesting. Caroline pointed at it and asked her mommy, "What's that?"

"It's a band," said Mommy. "Do you want to listen?"

Caroline nodded her head. The music coming from the band was modern and Caroline liked it. She danced and clapped her hands. After feeling happy and being silly, Caroline and Mommy went home.

Tom and Lily were playing with their cars on the floor. They liked to make them go fast and crash into each other. Tom had a red car and Lily had a blue car. They pretended they were racing on a big road.

"Look, my car is faster than yours!" Tom said, pushing his car hard.

"No, mine is faster!" Lily said, pushing her car harder.

They pushed and pushed their cars until they reached the wall. Then they turned them around and pushed them again. They did not see the plug on the floor. It was connected to the lamp on the table.

Tom pushed his car so hard that it hit the plug. The plug came out of the wall and made a loud noise. Tom and Lily were scared. They looked at the plug and saw sparks coming out of it.

"Uh-oh, what is that?" Tom asked.

"I don't know, it looks bad," Lily said.

They wanted to run away, but they were curious. They went closer to the plug and touched it. They felt a big shock. It hurt a lot. They screamed and fell down.

Their mom heard them and ran to the room. She saw them on the floor and the plug on fire. She was very angry and sad. She called for help and tried to wake them up. But it was too late. They did not wake up. They were gone.

Once upon a time, in a friendly little town, there was a port by the sea. In this port, many boats came and went every day. The people in the town loved to watch the boats and pretend to be sailors.

One sunny day, a boy named Tim and his friend, Lily, went to the port. They saw a big boat with a friendly captain. The captain waved at them and said, "Ahoy, little sailors! Would you like to pretend to be sailors with me today?"

Tim and Lily were very excited. They said, "Yes, please!" They put on their pretend sailor hats and climbed onto the big boat. The friendly captain showed them how to steer the boat and how to tie knots.

They spent the whole day pretending to be sailors with the friendly captain. They sailed the boat around the port, waving at the people on the shore. As the sun began to set, they went back to the dock.

Tim and Lily said goodbye to the friendly captain and thanked him for the fun day. They went home and told their families all about their adventure at the port. From that day on, they always loved to pretend to be sailors in the friendly little town by the sea.

One day, a mom was in the kitchen making a delicious melon salad. Her two children, Mary and Jake, were very excited to try it.

Just as the mom was about to serve the salad, Jake saw an ugly bug on it. He ran to his mom and yelled, "Mommy, there's an ugly bug on the melon!" 

The mom said, "Oh no! Don't worry, honey. Let me use a wet wipe to take it away." She wiped away the bug carefully.

Once the bug was gone, the mom said, "Wiping away the ugly bug was the right thing to do. We have to keep our food clean and healthy."

Mary and Jake nodded and they all ate the delicious melon salad together.

Once upon a time, there was a huge pig. She had a nice home in a meadow filled with pretty, pink flowers. Every morning, the pig would head off to the nearby forest to have breakfast.

One morning, the pig was yelping as she left her home. Another animal, a small rabbit, who lived in the nearby burrow, heard the pig and came out to see why she was yelping.

The rabbit asked, "Why are you yelping like that?"

The pig replied, "Today is the day I have to go to the doctor. I'm scared because I'll have to have an x-ray!"

The rabbit gave the pig a little hug and said, "Don't be scared. If you go to the doctor and do what he asks, everything will be ok."

The pig felt a little better after hearing the rabbit's words, and together they skipped off to the doctor. At the doctor's office, the pig was scared, but she yielded and did what the doctor asked. Afterwards, the doctor exclaimed, "The x-ray looks great! You can go home now."

The pig and the rabbit hugged each other and walked back to the meadow together. The pig realized that by yielding and doing what the doctor asked, she was rewarded with good news.

The moral of the story is: yielding can sometimes yield good results.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved to draw. She had many colors and her favorite was pink. She also had an eraser.

One day, the little girl wanted to color outside. She was so excited that she ran off to find the perfect spot.

She found a big tree and she seated herself down. Her eraser was in her hand and she was getting ready to draw.

Suddenly, she felt something beneath her! It was her eraser! She had been so careful not to lose it. She laughed at herself and put it back in her pocket. 

Now she could go back to drawing. She was so careful to keep her eraser safe while she enjoyed creating her masterpiece in the sunshine.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved getting packages in the mail. One day, her mommy told her that a package was coming in the mail for her. Lily was so excited!

The next day, the mailman came and brought a big package for Lily. She opened it up and saw that it was empty! She was so sad and didn't understand why there was nothing inside.

But then, her mommy told her to clap her hands three times. Lily did as she was told and suddenly a surprise popped out of the package! It was a big, fluffy teddy bear that Lily loved to hug and play with. She was so happy and knew that her mommy had set up a special surprise just for her.

Tim and Joe were the best of friends, they did everything together. They played together and even shared a special trophy. But one day, something strange happened. Joe became very selfish. He wanted to keep the trophy all to himself and not share it with Tim.

Tim felt sad and upset, he wanted to share the trophy with his best friend like always. So he had an idea, he decided to reverse things. He put the trophy back, where it had been before.

This made Joe very happy, but he was still selfish. He wanted to keep the trophy all to himself and not share.

Tim was very sad, but he decided that if Joe was not willing to share the trophy then it was best to leave it be. So with a heavy heart, Tim walked away and left the trophy alone.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He was playing in his backyard when he found a magic wand. He picked it up and said, "Wow, this is magic!"

Suddenly, a fairy appeared and said, "I am the fairy of the magic wand. You can make anything happen by pulling the wand."

Timmy was so excited and he pulled the wand. The fairy then turned his ordinary toy car into a real car. Timmy was amazed and said, "This is so cool! Thank you, fairy!" The fairy smiled and said, "You're welcome, Timmy. Just remember, with great power comes great responsibility." And with that, the fairy disappeared. Timmy played with his new car and promised to use the magic wand wisely.

Jack was running up the stairs. He smiled and laughed as he ran up each step. When he reached the top of the stairs and saw the pale door, he stopped and said to himself, "I'm almost finished!"

Suddenly, he heard a voice from inside the room. "Not so fast, Jack!" It was his mother. She opened the pale door and stepped out. 

"You must finish the stairs properly," she said. "No more running! See, take the stairs like this." She then started walking down the stairs step by step. 

Jack watched her and then nodded. He started taking the stairs slowly as his mother had shown him. When he finally finished the stairs, he looked up to her with a smile. 

"Very good, Jack," she said. "Now you can play in your room!" She ruffled his hair and gave him a hug before leading him up the stairs.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy had a bin in his room where he kept all his toys. One night, Timmy's mom told him to clean up his toys and put them in the bin before he went to sleep. Timmy was tired and didn't want to clean up, so he just threw all his toys in the bin and went to bed.

As he was falling asleep, Timmy heard a strange noise coming from the bin. It sounded mysterious and scary. "Mommy, what's that noise?" Timmy asked. "It's just your toys settling in the bin," his mom replied. But Timmy wasn't convinced.

The next morning, Timmy woke up to find that all his toys had disappeared from the bin. "Where did my toys go?" he asked his mom. "Maybe they're hiding," she said. But Timmy knew something was wrong. That night, as he was getting ready for bed, he heard the mysterious noise again. This time, he knew he had to investigate. He carefully opened the bin and found his toys, all sleeping peacefully inside. From that night on, Timmy made sure to put his toys in the bin properly so they could all sleep soundly.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play outside. One day, they see a big swamp near their house. They want to go and look.

"Can we go to the swamp?" Anna asks Ben.

"Yes, let's go!" Ben says. "Maybe we can find frogs and bugs."

They run to the swamp. They see green water and brown mud. They see plants and trees. They hear birds and frogs. They smell something funny.

"It is lovely here!" Anna says. "I like the swamp."

"Me too!" Ben says. "Look, I found a frog!"

He picks up a frog and shows it to Anna. The frog is slimy and wet. It croaks and jumps. Anna laughs and claps.

"Can I hold it?" Anna asks.

"Sure!" Ben says. He gives the frog to Anna. She holds it gently. The frog is ticklish and wiggly. Anna smiles and pets it.

"You are a nice frog," Anna says. "Do you like the swamp?"

The frog croaks again and nods. Anna and Ben giggle. They are happy. They like the swamp and the frog. They are friends.

One day, Tim was in his room playing with his toys when he saw something move. He looked again and saw a little mouse running across the floor. He shouted for his Mommy because he was scared.

Mommy came running in and saw the mouse too. She quickly grabbed her broom and chased it out the door. Tim felt embarrassed so he didn't say anything.

Mommy knew something was wrong and asked him what it was. Tim hung his head and said he felt guilty that he had shouted out. 

Mommy smiled and told him, "It's okay sweetheart, you can shout when you're scared. That's why I have walls in this house - to keep us safe."

Tim smiled and kissed his Mommy on the cheek. He was glad he still felt safe, even when he shouted.

Once upon a time, there was a raven. He was a big, black bird and he loved to pick the juiciest berries. One day he found the most delicious berry ever! He picked it carefully, as it was very fragile.

But as he flew away with his prize, a mischievous little boy saw him. He quickly reached out and tried to pick the berry away from the raven. But the raven was too fast. He flew higher and higher, out of the little boys reach.

The little boy was sad, but he was still determined. He didn't give up. He kept watching the sky for the raven, until he finally spotted him flying in the distance. He ran as fast as his little legs could go, trying to catch up. But the raven was too quick. In the end, the raven enjoyed his juicy berry all by himself.

John and his mum were in the backyard playing a game. John was always so excited to be outside and his mum would raise her voice in delight as he played with his toys. But then, something funny happened. John wanted to keep playing, but when he raised his hand, his mum shook her head and told him it was time to go back inside. John was sad; he felt something had changed and he wasn't sure why. He asked his mum but all she could do was give him a hug and explain that he could play in the backyard tomorrow. John understood, but he wasn't happy. He missed the fun he had been having before. He knew things had to change, but he wished they could stay the same.

Lily and Max are twins. They like to play in the park with their mom and dad. One day, they see a big truck with a shiny silver box on it. They run to the truck and ask the driver what is inside.

"Hello, little ones," the driver says. "This is a special box. It has music in it. Do you want to hear?"

"Yes, yes!" Lily and Max say. They love music. The driver opens the box and turns on a switch. The box makes a loud noise. It sounds like drums and horns and bells.

Lily and Max clap their hands and dance. They think the noise is fun. But their mom and dad do not like it. They cover their ears and frown.

"Please, turn it off!" their mom says. "That is not music. That is noise. It hurts our ears."

The driver smiles and turns off the switch. The noise stops. The park is quiet again.

"Sorry, ma'am," the driver says. "This is not normal music. This is a new kind of music. Some people like it, some people don't. I like it. It makes me happy."

Lily and Max look at their mom and dad. They do not understand why they do not like the noise. They think it is fun.

"Can we hear it again?" they ask.

Their mom and dad shake their heads. They take Lily and Max by the hand and walk away from the truck.

"Maybe when you are older, you will like it," their dad says. "But for now, let's go and play with the swings. They make a nice sound, too."

Once upon a time there was a bunny who had a deep hole in his fur. The bunny wanted to get it fixed so he went to the animal doctor. The doctor used a needle and thread to stitch up the bunny's fur. The doctor explained to the bunny that the stitches would help prevent any more holes from forming. The doctor was careful and made sure the stitches were very neat. The bunny was happy and thanked the doctor for preventing any more holes from appearing. The end.

Jimmy was playing in his back yard when he noticed a bush. He thought it looked fun and he wanted to build something. So he started collecting small twigs and rocks from around the yard. He stacked the rocks and twigs on top of the bush and the nosy neighbors started to watch what he was doing. Jimmy kept working until he had built a small fort around the bush. He threw some leaves on top and it looked like a secret hideaway. Then he crawled inside and he was very pleased with his work. He had built a cozy spot all by himself!

One day, a little boy named Tim and his dog, Spot, went for a walk. They saw a big tree and wanted to play under it. They ran to the tree and started to play. But Tim saw that Spot had a terrible limp. Tim asked, "Spot, why are you limping? Does your foot hurt?"

Spot looked at Tim and said, "Yes, my foot hurts. I stepped on a sharp rock." Tim felt sad for Spot and wanted to help him feel better. Tim had an idea. He suggested, "Let's go home and put a bandage on your foot. Then you will feel better."

They went home and Tim put a bandage on Spot's foot. Spot stopped limping and wagged his tail. They both went back to the tree and played all day. Tim and Spot were happy and had a great time playing under the big tree.

Once upon a time, there was a young girl named Joe. Joe loved playing in the forest. One day, Joe was playing in the forest when she heard a loud noise.

"Help me," said the noise.

Joe looked around, but she couldn't find where it was coming from. Suddenly, she saw a little bird. The bird's nest had fallen off a tree made of wood. 

"Oh no," said Joe. "I will help you."

Tom and Anna are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they find a big ball. It is red and shiny. They want to roll the ball.

Once upon a time, a big, fluffy cloud was in the sky. She was feeling very lonely, but she didn't know why. Soon, an even bigger, brighter cloud appeared in the sky, and she felt so happy! Together, they moved around the sky, looking for something exciting to do. 

Suddenly, something big and shiny appeared in the sky! It was a beautiful rainbow! The two clouds chased it around the sky, thinking it must be delicious! Finally, they reached the end of the rainbow. All they found were two pots of yummy raindrops. The clouds were so happy! They played together in the sky, eating raindrops and having lots of fun. 

The sky seemed so big and bright, glimmering with all their fun! The clouds were so happy, they decided that they would stay in the sky forever.

Lila and Tom were friends who liked to play outside. One day, they saw a big hill with smoke coming out of it. They wanted to see what it was, so they ran towards it.

Mama told Matty not to wander away, but Matty started walking. He was curious and wanted to explore.

Sammy was so excited, it was a beautiful day outside and he was wearing his new rainbow shirt. He'd never seen anything so attractive.

Once upon a time, there was a humble mouse named Peanut. Peanut lived in an airport. Every day Peanut would wake up and begin to chew on the delicious food in the airport. Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Lila. She was only three years old and very curious about the world. One day, she found an interesting note lying on the ground. She quickly grabbed it and started to guess what it said.

Lila showed the note to her mum and asked her what it was. Her mum said that it was a special note that only she could understand. Lila was a bit disappointed, but she wanted to guess what the note said so she asked her mum to help her.

The note taught Lila how to be kind, patient, and understanding. It also taught her how to appreciate the important things in life. That's why she kept it as a special reminder in her pocket at all times. It made her feel comfortable and happy!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lola. She was 3 years old and liked to play in her backyard.

Lola had a special toy. It was a blue car and it was her favorite. She parked it under the big tree in the backyard.

One day, as Lola was playing with her car, she heard a happy whistle coming from the tree. She looked up and saw a bright, light bird! Lola stared at the bird in amazement.

The bird was whistling a tune to Lola and she smiled. She hopped around in happiness and sang along. 

Lola and the bird whirled and twirled around the tree, making each other laugh. Then, Lola went to get a toy for the bird, so they could play together. 

The bird and Lola laughed and played together before the bird flew away. From that day on, Lola remembered her little friend and the happy whistling they shared.

Once upon a time there was a proud season. It came with a lot of warmth and sunny days! Everybody was happy and danced and twisted in joy.

Once upon a time, a young frog was sitting in a seat by the lake shore. The fog was slowly rolling in and blanketing the lake. He felt very lonely and ignored by the other creatures and he was ignorant of what lay ahead.

The thick fog began to cling to the frog and he shivered, but couldn't seem to move. He felt so small and helpless, and the lonely feeling only grew.

Suddenly, a large and friendly dragonfly flew nearby. He called out to the frog, saying, "Do not feel so small! Everything will soon become clearer."

The frog felt a spark of hope, but he remained in his seat, still feeling helpless. All at once, the fog began to part and the lake came into view, full of frogs just like him.

The dragonfly directed the young frog's attention to his companions and said, "You are not alone and things will get better. Do not be ignorant of your possibilities. Open your eyes and look around. You have the chance to make a great life for yourself."

The frog hopped up from his seat and joined his fellow frogs in the lake. He learned that the darkness of the fog only made the light of the sun shine brighter. The moral of the story is to never forget that no matter how lost or helpless you feel, you are never alone.

Once upon a time there was a big mighty elephant. He loved playing with his friends and eating lots of yummy food. One day his parents came to visit. They were so happy to see the mighty elephant. Once upon a time there was a rabbit. She was a very happy rabbit because she always had a big smile on her face.

Suddenly, a little girl appeared. She was wearing a big crown and was holding a big, fat candle. The little girl smiled when she saw the rabbit. She set down the cake and asked the rabbit to help her light the candle.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy liked to play with his toys and run outside. One day, Timmy's grandma came to visit him. She brought a bottle of juice for Timmy to drink.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Jane. She was walking to school one day, carrying her umbrella. Suddenly, it began to rain. Jane looked up and saw a boy. He was standing there, with an umbrella too.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Jane. She was 3 years old and loved to wear her mom's apron. Once there was a girl called Jane. She was keen and eager for an adventure. One day she packed some gears for a journey. As she was about to go, her mom caught her and said: "Where are you going, Jane?" She hastily answered: "I'm going adventuring!"

Her mom smiled and told her: "You have to have all the important gears for this. Here, take these" and handed Jane a backpack. She put on the backpack and said goodbye to her mom. Jane began walking on her adventure.

She soon came across a river. The river was wide and strong and the current was strong. Jane looked around and saw a rope hanging across the river. She was determined to get across, so she grabbed the rope and took a deep breath. She held the rope tightly and jumped across.

On the other side, she found something beautiful - a waterfall! She was so eager to explore it, so she walked to the edge of the falls and looked down. She held on tight to her gear, and carefully climbed down.

At the bottom, she saw a sparkly lake and a lot of plants. Jane's adventurous spirit lit up and she spent the whole day exploring the lake and discovering more new and exciting things. Before sunset, Jane climbed all the way back up and went home, eager to share the stories of her journey!

John and Mommy were in the kitchen. John wanted a piece of cake. Mommy looked at the cake. It was pale. Mommy said, "Let's weigh the cake first."

John watched as Mommy put the cake on the table. Then, she put a big thing on top of the cake. It was a scale. John watched as his mommy lifted the scale. The scale moved and a number appeared. Mommy said, "I think the cake is the right size."

Once there was a group of friends. They were all very excited to go to the theater. They each dressed up in silly outfits.

Once upon a time there was a rolling ball. It was red and shiny and it loved to roll around.

Once upon a time, in an ordinary town, there lived a girl named Jane. She liked to sell pretty things at her small shop. One day, a boy named Tom came to her shop. He wanted to buy a gift for his mom.

Once upon a time, there was a bird named Sammy. Sammy loved to swim in the pond near his home. One day, he met a duck named Danny. Danny was very friendly and asked Sammy if he wanted to swim with him. Sammy was excited and quickly agreed.

Daniel was excited to go on a walk. His mom and dad included him in the outing and he liked going outside. As they were walking, Daniel saw a beetle! It was a big beetle and it had lots of colors. Daniel was amazed. He wanted to get closer to the beetle, but his mom said he shouldn't.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Pete. Pete was three years old and he was very curious.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she put on her cap and went outside to play. She ran and jumped and laughed in the sun.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved to play outside in the snow. Every day she would bundle up in her warmest coat and head into the backyard. She loved to make snowballs, and then throw them at anything that moved - trees, bushes and even her dog!

One day, while playing in the snow, she decided to make her very own snow fort. She packed and patted the snow until it was nice and solid. But when she tried to cut it into an even shape with her shovel, she couldn't do it. She pushed and prodded, but the snow was too stubborn. 

The little girl sighed and sat in the snow, frustrated. Suddenly, her dog ran up to her, carrying a sharp piece of wood in his mouth. She took the wood and examined it. 

"This just might work," she said, and with a big smile she started sharping the edges of the snow fort until it was perfect. Suddenly she heard a loud cheer from behind her. It was her dad standing there, watching her work. "Good job! You're so stubborn," he said. 

The little girl smiled, happy to have conquered the snow, and she hugged her dad, who gave her an extra big hug. She knew that being stubborn could sometimes get you what you wanted - and that was a lesson she would never forget.

Once upon a time, a little deer named Timmy was walking in the forest. Suddenly, he saw a disgusting and slimy puddle. He didn't want to touch it and so he stepped aside. But then he heard a strange sound coming from the puddle.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Bella. Bella was very imaginative and loved playing pretend. One day, Bella found a little pole and decided to play with it.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside in the park. He would run around and pick up sticks and rocks. One day, Timmy saw a big pile of grass. He decided to throw the grass up in the air and watch it fall down.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with cardboard boxes. He would build forts and castles out of them. One day, Timmy's mom gave him a big cardboard box to play with. Timmy was very happy and started building his castle.

Instead, Timmy went to his dad and asked for a tool to help him. His dad gave him a screwdriver, and Timmy used it to remove the wheels from his sister's toy car. His sister was upset, but Timmy said sorry and promised to fix it. He cleaned the filthy wheels, put them back on the car, and gave it back to his sister. She was happy, and Timmy felt good for doing the right thing.

Once upon a time, there was a thin ball that liked to bounce. The ball had a friend named Speed. Speed was a fast car. They liked to play together in the park.

One day, Speed and the thin ball decided to have a race. Speed went fast, and the thin ball bounced high. They raced to the big tree in the park. The thin ball bounced higher and higher, while Speed went faster and faster.

In the end, Speed won the race. The thin ball was happy for his friend. They both had a fun day. After the race, they went home to rest. They knew they would play together again soon.

Once upon a time, there was a blue jellyfish in the sea. He was a very happy jellyfish and always swam around and smiled at all the other creatures.

One day he noticed a big yellow fish swimming towards him. "Hello," said the yellow fish. "What are you up to?"

The jellyfish smiled and said, "I'm just swimming and playing around."

The yellow fish smiled and said, "That sounds like fun! I'd like to join you."

The jellyfish said, "Sure - let's go!"

So they swam away together, playing and having lots of fun.

But then, all of a sudden, the sea started to shake. "Oh no!" said the jellyfish. "We need to get out of here. Quick, shut your eyes and hold your breath!"

The yellow fish did as he was told, and soon the shaking stopped. When it was over, the jellyfish opened his eyes. He was relieved to see that the yellow fish was still there.

The yellow fish said, "That was scary! But we're okay now, right?"

The jellyfish smiled and said, "Yes, we're okay. Now let's go back to swimming and playing."

And so they did - splashing around, playing and having lots of fun. The blue jellyfish was so happy to have a new friend to play

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. Her name was Amy and she was three years old. She loved to go to the playground.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Sue. Sue really wanted to improve her house, so she decided to paint her toilet! She got the paint from the store and she made it a lovely bright blue. 

Sue was very proud of her new toilet and she invited all her friends over to admire it. Even Sue's mom and dad were impressed by the paint job!

Sue's mom was so happy that she decided to make everyone a very tasty treat as a reward. She made a big cake with lots of sprinkles, and everyone ate it up with joy.

Sue was so proud of her improved house, and her sister was so happy too. They decided that they would help the rest of the family improve their homes too. Sue and her sister had made their home much better and brighter!

Little Marvin was walking through the park on a sunny week. He saw a bald man crying. Marvin had never seen anyone crying before and he was very curious. So he asked the bald man why he was crying.

The bald man said to Marvin, "I'm crying because I'm sad. I don't have enough money to buy my train ticket home."

Marvin was so sad to hear this. He wanted to help the bald man and he knew the perfect thing to do. He ran home and grabbed his piggybank and brought it back to the man. He opened it up and showed the man all the coins inside.

The bald man was so happy to see how much money Marvin had. With this money, he was able to buy his train ticket home.

As the man took the tickets and his piggy bank back, he said something to Marvin that he would never forget. He said, "Thank you for helping me in my time of need. Even though you are only three years old, you have the biggest heart of all."

From that day forward, Marvin went to the park every week, ready to lend a helping hand.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lisa. She had a job to do. Her mom told her to take a message to her grandma. The message was, "I love you." Lisa had to be patient and remember the message.

On her way, Lisa met a talking bird. The bird said, "Hello! What's your message?" Lisa told the bird, "My message is, 'I love you.'" The bird liked the message and wanted to help. The bird said, "I will repeat the message with you so you don't forget." Lisa and the bird walked together, saying the message over and over.

When they got to grandma's house, Lisa and the bird said the message together, "I love you." Grandma was so happy. She hugged Lisa and the bird. The moral of the story is to be patient, and when you work together, you can make others happy.

Doug was walking in the park when he saw an ostrich. He thought it would be funny to tease the ostrich, so he prepared an apple. His friend Jim was with him and warned him not to be too selfish.

Doug thought a snack would be enough to make the ostrich happy, so he picked up the apple and slowly approached the ostrich. 

"Hey there," Doug said to the ostrich.

The ostrich didn't move and seemed to be scared of Doug. 

Jim said, "I told you not to be too selfish! Now the ostrich is scared of you. You can't tease it like that!"

Doug stared at the ostrich and felt bad for teasing it. 

Suddenly, the ostrich took the apple from Doug's hands and ran away!

Doug laughed and laughed. He knew the ostrich was okay after all!

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Maxi who loved pretend. Everyday she would play pretend with her favorite toys, like her little measure. Maxi was always so persistent when it came to pretend!

One day, Maxi was playing a game of pretending she was a pirate. She had her measure tucked in her belt and was pretending to explore the high seas. She sailed around, searching for treasure and adventure.

Maxi sailed for a long time, but eventually she became tired and decided to rest for a bit. She put her measure down on the ground, but as she closed her eyes to relax, she felt something strange. Suddenly, the measure started to move and slide away from Maxi!

Maxi opened her eyes in surprise and noticed that her measure was slowly sliding backwards. Suddenly Maxi had an idea! She raced forward and held onto the measure with all her might. Maxi was persistent, and she refused to let go until the measure stopped sliding. And after a few seconds, it finally did.

The measure never moved again and Maxi was so proud that she was able to use her persistence to stop it. Maxi continued on her pretend adventure, always happy to have her measurement with her.

Once upon a time there was a little boy. His name was Toby and he was 3 years old. 
Toby loved sailing. He would go sailing often with his mom and dad.

Toby was very excited. His mom and dad said that this was going to be a very special sail.

As they sailed, Toby suddenly saw something ahead. It was an ordinary looking sailboat. But it was different than any sailing boat Toby had seen before.

Toby's mom and dad said, "That's our sailboat. It's a surprise for you!" They had spoiled Toby with a sailboat of his very own!

Toby was so happy. He couldn't believe it! His own sailboat! Toby knew that he would have lots of fun sailing it around the lake. 

The End

Jim was the bravest astronaut! He was the first one to record a moonwalk. He put on his spacesuit, adjusted his helmet and took a giant step out of the spaceship. As he floated in the air, he could see the Earth, twinkling in the night sky. 

Jim took in a deep breath. He had oxygen in his suit, so he wasn't worried. He extended his arm and waved. It was a fierce moment! He shouted "Hello, Earth!" 

Back on the spaceship, his crew were cheering and recording the moment. They were so proud of their brave friend! Jim smiled and waved to them one more time before floating back to the spaceship. 

Jim exclaimed "That was awesome! I can't believe I recorded a moonwalk!" 

His crew nodded in agreement and looked at their brave friend with admiration. Jim had done it! He had recorded a brave moonwalk and made history.

Ralph was clumsy and he loved to rush around. He remembered when his dad told him that he should never rush, but he didn't listen.

One day, Ralph rushed to his bedroom and pulled out a toy box. He opened it and saw a bell inside. Ralph quickly picked up the bell and rang it.

His mom's voice came from downstairs, "Ralph, it's time for dinner. Don't rush too much!"

Ralph quickly put the bell back in the toy box, closed it and ran downstairs. He quickly sat at the dinner table and smiled. He was ashamed that he was rushing again.

His dad saw him and said, "Ralph, remember - it's OK to rush sometimes, but it's important to take your time too."

Ralph nodded and said, "I'll try to remember, dad."

Since then, Ralph has learned to be less clumsy and to take time to enjoy the things he does.

Once upon a time there was a girl who wanted to go on an adventure. She put her favourite toy bear in her bag and set off.

Then she saw a big mountain and wanted to climb it. She was trying very hard but it was difficult. She felt a bit scared, so she yelled out "Help!"

Suddenly her mummy was there, and the girl was embarrassed that she had made so much noise! Her mummy said it was alright and gave her a hand up the mountain.

The girl made it to the top and when she looked in her bag, she saw her favourite toy bear was gone. She yelled out "No!" and was very sad. But then, she looked down the mountain and saw her mum. She had her bear!

The girl was so happy and waved at her mummy. Together, they went home and the girl never forgot the adventure she had gone on.

Rob was walking down the street when he heard some crying. He looked around and saw a little girl on the ground next to a rail. She was sobbing.

Rob went up to her and asked, "What's wrong?"

The little girl sniffled and said, "I fell off the rail."

Rob reached out and said, "It's ok. Are you hurt?"

The little girl shook her head no, but still cried. Rob knew he had to do something to make her feel better. He said, "Do you like games?"

The little girl wiped her tears away and said, "Yes!"

Rob said, "Let's play a game. It's very important that you stay in the middle of the rail."

The little girl nodded and said, "Ok!" She gave Rob a big hug and thanked him.

Rob smiled and said, "You're welcome."

The little girl gave him one last hug before she started walking back to the rail. This time she was careful not to fall and she made it to the other side.

Rob watched the little girl scamper away and couldn't help but smile. He was glad he could help.

Once upon a time there was a big, colorful heart. The heart was so colorful that everyone wanted to take it home and chew on it.

The heart was clever and knew that if it was chewed too much it would become small and broken. So it decided to roll away and find a safe place.

The heart bumped, skipped and rolled its way across the meadow until it reached the house of an old, wise bear. The bear asked the heart why it was travelling alone.

The heart told the bear that it was looking for a safe place to stay because it was afraid of being chewed too much.

The wise bear smiled and told the heart that it was very important to be careful about what it chose to chew on. He said that too much chewing can lead to bad things.

The old bear also said that chewing on the right things can open your eyes and lead to beautiful things.

The heart thanked the old bear for his advice and continued its journey. Ever since then, it has been more careful of what it chooses to chew on!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a parent who loved her very much. One day, they went to the park together. Lily saw a big, black dog and she was scared. Her parent held her hand and told her not to worry. They walked past the dog and went to play on the swings. Lily felt happy and safe with her parent holding her. The end.

Once upon a time there was a boy who looked for an adventure. He ran down to the beach, hoping to find something fun.

He looked around the shore and saw a large octopus in the sand. The boy wanted to catch it. He waited and waited, but the octopus kept running away from him.

Finally, the octopus got stuck in the sand. The boy ran so fast and caught the octopus. It felt slippery and slimy. 

The octopus tried to get out of the boy's hands, but he was strong and held tightly. Suddenly, the octopus made a bad sound. It made the boy jump and he dropped the octopus. 

The octopus swam away, leaving the boy by himself. He was happy that he got to catch the octopus, even though it was bad.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and look at the pretty flowers. One day, she saw a charming butterfly fluttering around the garden. She wanted to catch it and keep it as her pet.

Lily chased after the butterfly, but it flew away. She tried again and again, but the butterfly always got away. She felt sad and frustrated. She wanted that butterfly so badly.

Then, she had an idea. She went inside and got a jar with a lid. She went back outside and waited patiently for the butterfly to come back. When it did, she quickly put the jar over it and caught it. She was so happy! She had finally caught the charming butterfly she wanted.

But then, she realized that the butterfly was not happy in the jar. It wanted to fly free in the garden. Lily felt bad for taking it away from its home. So, she opened the jar and let the butterfly go. She learned that sometimes, what we want may not be what is best for others.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved the color pink and had a favorite cable that she always played with. One day, Lily's mom told her that they were going to visit her grandma's house.

Lily was very excited and asked, "Can I bring my pink cable with me?" Her mom said, "Yes, you can bring it, but you have to nap first before we leave."

Lily didn't want to nap, but she knew she had to if she wanted to go to her grandma's house. She closed her eyes and fell asleep with her pink cable in her hand.

When Lily woke up, she saw that her pink cable was missing! She looked for it everywhere but couldn't find it. She was so sad and started to cry.

Then, her grandma came into the room and asked, "What's wrong, Lily?" Lily told her about her missing pink cable. Her grandma smiled and said, "I have a surprise for you!" She went to her closet and pulled out a brand new pink cable for Lily. Lily was so happy and hugged her grandma tight. From that day on, Lily never forgot to take her nap before going on a trip.

Molly was a dependable girl and she loved carrying around her purse. Everywhere she went, she would fill it with collected treasures and it became a precious part of her life.

She was so happy that she had something dependable like her purse. She knew that no matter what, it was there for her and it would help her carry her most precious things.

Once there was a little girl named Mary. Mary was very strong and very brave. 
One day, Mary wanted to explore the woods. She put on her shoes, grabbed her bucket and set off! 
As she walked, she saw a big chain lying on the ground. It was thick and strong. She didn't know what it was for.

Mary and the lion became best friends. They explored the woods together and had lots of fun. Mary was never alone again.

Once upon a time, there was a large dog. He loved to explore and run around. One day, he saw something new and was very excited. He barked and took off running. 

The dog had found a trail. He followed it deep into the forest. As he walked, the trail got bigger and bigger. Soon, the dog came to a pond. There were so many frogs jumping around. 

The dog barked, "What are you guys doing?"

One of the frogs hopped right up to the dog and said, "We are having a lot of fun. Will you join us?" 

The dog smiled and said, "Yes! I will follow and play with you." 

So, the large dog followed the frogs and they all played together the rest of the day. The dog never forgot this special day and always loved to follow the trail whenever he had the chance.

The dark curtain twisted in the wind. Winnie watched from her bedroom window as the fabric billowed and moved like a ghost. It was a strange sight, and she felt a chill run down her spine. She was sure something interesting was going to happen.

The next morning, Winnie crept down the stairs. All was quiet, but she knew something was about to happen. Sure enough, as she slowly peered around the corner, she saw the dark curtain moving by itself! She watched it swaying and swirling in the wind, almost like something was inside.

Winnie ran upstairs and grabbed her mom. "Come see, mama!" she said. Her mom followed her to the door and they both watched in amazement as the dark curtain swayed and twisted in the wind. They both knew something was inside.

Her mom slowly pulled back the dark curtain and there, sitting on the porch, was an old man with a twinkle in his eye. He welcomed Winnie and her mom with a smile and introduced himself as a traveling salesman. It turns out he'd been using the dark curtain to hide himself as he looked for a place to stay the night! Winnie was amazed and her mom was thankful that nothing scary was hiding in the dark curtain after all.

John was a little boy who liked to be very polite. He was at the park one day when he saw a little girl playing. She had dirt allover her shirt, so he decided to be extra polite.

John walked up to the girl and asked nicely, "Can I help you?". The little girl smiled and nodded her head. John then bent down and pulled a handkerchief out of his pocket. He used it to carefully wipe off the dirt from the girlâ€™s shirt.

The little girl was very thankful for the help. She said, "Thank you very much!" John smiled and said, "You are very welcome". John was so happy that he had been polite and he knew the little girl was too. The two friends were very happy.

Once upon a time, there was a hunter. He was very enthusiastic about going on adventures. One day, he grabbed his bow and arrows and set off into the woods. He kept his eyes open and his ears alert, hoping to find something exciting.

He wasn't sure what he was looking for, but he felt like it was around there somewhere. He kept walking until he came to a clearing. He saw a rabbit hopping around, nibbling on a flower. The hunter was thrilled â€“ he knew that this was exactly what he was looking for!

He carefully grabbed his bow and took aim. He let his arrow go and, just like that, the rabbit was his. He was so enthusiastic, he couldn't help but do a little dance of joy. The hunter was very happy with his catch. He went home with a great big smile on his face.

Jimmy had an old desk in his room. Every day he was very grateful for it because it held all kinds of special items. He used it to record all his adventures. He had paper, pencils, markers and a special recorder. 

Jimmy liked to draw pictures and write stories on the paper. He also liked to make recordings of himself talking. He spoke about all kinds of happy things like playing outside and eating his favourite food. 

Today, Jimmy was excited because he had a new thing to record. He was going to record a song from his grandmother. She had taught it to him over the phone. He set up the recorder, sat down at the desk, and began singing the song. 

The recording went great. Jimmy listened to it over and over. He smiled, happy with the sound of his voice. He was very grateful for his desktop and all it could do.

Once upon a time, there was an ordinary penguin. He was walking around looking for something to do when he came across a printer. He had never seen anything like it before. The penguin was very curious. He stepped up to the printer and pressed a button.

Much to his surprise, the printer started to make noise. Out came a piece of paper with pictures on it. The penguin was amazed. He was so excited that he ran around showing all his friends. 

The penguin then spread the word that if you press the button on the printer something new will get printed. All his friends wanted to try it out and from then on the penguin was known as the printing penguin!

Tim and his mom were walking through the field. Tim was six years old and he loved the outdoors. He ran and jumped around, looking at all the brilliant colors in the field. Suddenly, he noticed a beautiful lily. He ran over to it and said to his mom, "Look, Mom! It's so beautiful!"

His mom smiled and said, "You've gained a new friend, Tim. That's a lily." Tim gave the flower a big hug and it was as if he had gained a true friend. 

Mom bent down and said, "Lilies are a symbol of hope and growth. They remind us that even when it feels dark, there is still light." Tim looked at the brilliant colors of the flower and smiled. 

Then, Tim ran back to his mom and hugged her tight. She said, "It's amazing what you can gain in life when you take pause to look around you." 

Tim and his mom smiled together, and continued to explore the beautiful field.

Rufus was walking through the park when he suddenly saw something in the bushes. He was scared and started to scream.

A voice said: "Rufus, it's just me, Will. Don't be scared." 

Rufus recognised Will's voice and calmed down. He asked Will: "What are you doing here?"

Will smiled and said: "I'm looking for the normal thing".

Rufus was confused so he said: "What is it? Let's find it!" 

Will laughed and said: "Let's look together."

So they went off through the park searching for the normal thing, whatever it may be.

One day, a little boy named Tim lost a tooth. He was very happy because the tooth fairy would come at night. Tim put the tooth under his pillow and went to sleep.

In the dark, a tiny fairy named Lily came to save the tooth. She looked under the pillow and found it. But it was so dark that she could not see well. Lily bumped into a toy and made a loud noise.

Tim woke up and saw Lily. He said, "Who are you?" Lily said, "I am the tooth fairy. I came to save your tooth." Tim smiled and went back to sleep. In the morning, he found a shiny coin under his pillow.

One day, a little boy named Jack went out to the woods to explore. He was so excited; he hadn't ever been to the woods before!

He was walking and looking around when he noticed something strange. He saw a big barrel and he thought it was weird. He walked up to it and touched it. Suddenly, he heard a big sigh!

Jack wondered what made the sigh. He was so curious. As he got closer and looked inside the barrel he saw a creature.
Jack was so surprised! He never seen something like it before. It was weird.

The creature asked Jack if he wanted to play. Jack was a little scared but was excited too. He said yes and they both giggled and had lots of fun playing together.

Jack promised he will come back soon and they said their goodbyes. Jack promised he would never forget his new friend in the weird barrel.

Once there was an enormous tree. Its leaves were green and soft. A big, white cloud floated by and it looked like a puffy pillow. An ant crawled up the tree. 

The ant wanted to touch the leaves of the tree. He stretched out one of his legs and reached out to touch the first leaf. It was so cool and soft on his little legs. He moved up to the next leaf and touched it too. He felt like a tiny explorer. 

The ant moved higher and higher up the tree. He touched more and more leaves as he went. The leaves were so enormous that he had to keep climbing. Finally he reached the very top and saw the horizon. 

The ant smiled and waved goodbye to the enormous leaves of the tree. He was so grateful for his adventure and for being able to touch the leaves. He scurried back down the tree. 

The ant looked up at the enormous tree from below and smiled. He was happy to have touched the leaves and to have seen the horizon.

Once upon a time there was an octopus named Sam. Sam liked to organize things - he liked to organize them in specific ways to make sure that everything was in its place. 

One day, Sam decided to organize two big rocks together to make a rock tower. Sam worked hard, and he was almost done.

"Sam, be careful!" called out Sam's mother. "You can be clumsy sometimes!"

Sam was careful, and he was able to finish the tower. But then the ground began shaking, and the tower started wobbling and then falling.

Sam was scared, but then he noticed something strange. Another octopus had just come out of the rocks! It was organizing and stacking the rocks back up!

Sam smiled as he was able to get his rock tower back because of the clumsy octopus!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she went on a walk with her mommy and daddy. They walked and walked until they saw a big building called a lab. Lily's mommy and daddy told her that a lab is a place where scientists do experiments. 

Lily was curious and wanted to see what was inside the lab. She asked her mommy and daddy if they could go inside. They said no, but Lily didn't give up. She looked around and found a small hole in the fence. She went through the hole and found herself inside the lab. 

Lily looked around and saw lots of beakers and test tubes. She saw a scientist doing an experiment and asked him what he was doing. The scientist explained it to her and Lily thought it was fine. She was happy to have found a new place to explore.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to go fishing with her dad. They would go to the lake every weekend and catch lots of fish. One day, while they were fishing, Lily saw a fish that was stuck in some weeds. She wanted to save the fish, but her dad said they couldn't because it was too dangerous.

Lily felt sad for the fish and said, "I don't want the fish to suffer. Can't we help it?"

Her dad replied, "I know you want to help, but it's not safe. We have to think about our safety too."

Lily understood, but she still felt sad for the fish. She didn't want to be selfish and only think about herself. So, she decided to pray for the fish and hope that it would be okay. From that day on, Lily always made sure to be kind to the fish they caught and to never be selfish with her love and care for them.

Leo was a little leopard who lived in the jungle with his mama and papa. He liked to play with his friends, but sometimes he felt gloomy. He did not like the rain, the dark, or the loud noises.

One day, he was playing hide and seek with his friends, when he heard a big thunder. He got scared and ran to find his mama. He saw her under a big tree, with her tail around her. He ran to her and rubbed his head on her fur.

"Mama, I don't like the thunder. It makes me feel gloomy," he said.

Mama leopard hugged him and licked his ears. "I know, my little Leo. But the thunder is not bad. It is just the sky talking to us. It tells us that it is going to rain, and that the rain will make the plants and the animals happy and healthy."

"But the rain is wet and cold. And it makes the jungle dark. I don't like the rain either," Leo said.

Mama leopard smiled and said, "But the rain is also fun and beautiful. It makes the flowers smell nice, and the rainbows shine. And it makes the mud soft and squishy. You can slide and splash and make mud pies. And when the rain stops, you can see the sun and the stars again. And you can play with your friends some more."

Leo thought about what his mama said. He looked at the raindrops falling from the leaves, and the colors in the sky. He felt a little less gloomy. He said, "Maybe the rain is not so bad. Maybe I can try to have fun with it. Can we make mud pies, mama?"

Mama leopard nodded and said, "Of course, my little Leo. Let's go and make some mud pies. And then we can rub them on each other and laugh."

Leo and his mama ran to the mud and started to make mud pies. They rubbed them on each other and laughed. They felt happy and warm. They did not mind the thunder or the rain anymore. They had fun with the rain.

Once there was a bear. The bear liked to play dress up. So it put on its special costume. It liked the way the costume made it feel.

'My costume looks great!' the bear said.

Then something funny happened. The bear stretched and the costume became too small.

'Oh no!' the bear said. 'Maybe I have to get a new costume'. 

The bear was worried as it looked through the store. All of the costumes were so expensive.

A rabbit by the bear said, 'You can stretch your old costume. It might fit again'.

The bear smiled. It stretched the costume and it was just the right size.

'I can wear my costume again!' the bear said.

The bear was so happy the costume fit after all. It hopped around with joy, wearing its special costume.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny named Flopsy. Flopsy loved to hop and play in the meadow. One day, Flopsy felt a tickle in her nose and she sneezed really loud. "Achoo!" she said.

But then, something strange happened. Every time Flopsy sneezed, she made a funny rhythm with her feet. "Thump, thump, thump!" went her feet. Flopsy didn't know what was happening, but she liked the sound.

However, her friends didn't like it at all. They got angry and told her to stop making noise. Flopsy didn't want to make her friends angry, so she tried to stop sneezing. But no matter how hard she tried, she couldn't stop the rhythm from coming out.

Once there was a family who wanted to go on a walk. They had been stuck inside all day and they wanted to get out and explore. So Mommy, Daddy and their little boy, Jack, all put on their shoes and went outside.

At first, Jack was excited. He loved being outside and looking at the trees and flowers. But then the family reached a busy street with lots of traffic and Jack started to feel bored. He asked Mommy and Daddy "What can we do?"

Mommy and Daddy thought for a moment and then had an idea. They told Jack to look at the power lines above the street. "Let's see what we can see up there," they said.

Jack saw that the power lines were full of birds. He watched them flutter around and swing from the lines. He thought it was really cool.

Jack said "Let's hang from the power lines too!" Mommy and Daddy looked at each other and smiled. They said "No! That would be too dangerous and we don't want to get hurt!"

So instead Daddy showed Jack how to use his binoculars to get a closer look at the birds. Then they watched for a long time. Jack soon forgot about being bored and enjoyed the beautiful view instead.

Once upon a time, there was a naughty girl called Jenny. She had an old cardboard box in her room and she was always sneaky when she opened it.

One day, her mom asked her what was in the box. Jenny said it was a secret.

"Jenny," her mom said. "You can't keep secrets like this. What is in the box?"

Jenny opened the box, and she showed her mom. Inside it was some special powder. It shone brightly in the light.

Jenny smiled. "It's for melting snow, Mommy. I'm going to be so naughty! I'm going to sprinkle it around the garden and make the snow sparkle!"

Her mom smiled. "That's a very naughty idea," she said. "Be careful with it, okay?"

So Jenny went outside into the garden and sprinkled the sparkly powder around. It made the snow glitter even more. Jenny giggled and jumped around in the snow. She had lots of fun with her special powder.

Once there was a baby bunny named Bounce. Bounce was so small and fluffy. One day Bounce wanted to explore the garden, so he hopped off on an adventure. 

When Bounce was exploring, he didn't realize there was a big bulldog in the garden! The bulldog was so scary and started chasing Bounce. Bounce hopped and hopped but he couldn't get away. 

Just then, Bounce tripped and fell over and started crying. The bulldog's owner heard the cries and came to help. He gave Bounce a big bandage and said, "It's okay Bunny, you can bounce like before." 

Bounce hopped as high as he could and thanked the kind man. From then on, every time Bounce hopped, he would remember the act of kindness and the bandage.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Liza. She was very hungry and wanted some food. She had no food so she decided to cook something. She looked around her house, but all she found was mail. She tried to cook the mail, but it wouldn't get hot. Liza was still very hungry. 

She had an idea and thought of going to the store. Liza walked to the store and asked the storekeeper for something to eat. The storekeeper told her that she had to buy something to cook. Liza explained that she had nothing to buy and only had mail. The storekeeper was very kind and told Liza that he would give her something if she made a paper airplane out of the mail.

Liza started to make the paper airplane and soon it was ready. She put it on the table and the storekeeper handed her a delicious chocolate cake. Liza was happy and thanked the storekeeper for the cake. 

The moral of the story is that you can get things in creative ways. Liza was very hungry, but she was able to get the cake by using her creative mindset and making a paper airplane. We can learn from Liza that with determination, creativity and hard work, we can accomplish many great things!

Once upon a time, there was an adorable woman who loved to climb. Every day, she would climb up a hill to see the world from above.

Sara and Ben are friends. They like to play outside. But today it is very cold. They see snow on the ground and in the air.

"Let's make a snowman!" Sara says. "It will be fun!"

"OK!" Ben says. "But we need a plan. How do we make a snowman?"

Sara thinks. She is smart. She says, "We need three big balls of snow. One for the head, one for the body, and one for the bottom. We also need a hat, a scarf, a carrot, and some rocks."

"Good plan!" Ben says. "Let's go!"

They work hard. They roll the snow into balls. They stack them up. They find a hat, a scarf, a carrot, and some rocks. They put them on the snowman.

"Look!" Sara says. "We made a snowman! He is big and nice!"

"Yes!" Ben says. "He is great! But he looks cold. Let's give him a hug!"

They hug the snowman. They feel happy. They are good friends. They have a good plan.

Tom and Ann are friends. They like to play on the farm. They see a big cow. The cow is black and white. The cow has a bell on its neck.

"Let's catch the cow!" Tom says. He runs after the cow. Ann follows him.

The cow sees Tom and Ann. The cow does not like them. The cow runs away. The cow makes a loud moo. The cow goes to the open gate. The gate leads to the road.

"Stop, cow, stop!" Ann shouts. She tries to close the gate. But the gate is too heavy for her. The cow pushes the gate with its nose. The gate swings open. The cow runs to the road.

"Oh no, cow, no!" Tom cries. He sees a car on the road. The car is fast. The car does not see the cow. Tom is scared. He hopes the cow is safe.

What will happen to the cow? Will Tom and Ann catch the cow? Will the car stop in time? How will the story end?

Once there was a small boy named Tim. He wanted to go outside and play but he was hurt. His knee was badly scraped and it was very sore.

Tim had to stay home instead. His mommy took him to the doctor's office. She asked the doctor for help.

But the doctor did help Tim. He showed Tim how to use bandages whenever he got hurt while playing outside. 

Little Tim thanked the doctor and went outside. He was careful not to get hurt again.

Once there was a duck that lived in a pond. It was a very powerful duck and it was always very proud of that. 

One day, something changed. The duck's pond began to dry up. All the other animals had to leave, but the duck remained. It decided to stay, no matter what happened. 

One day, a strange animal visited the duck. It was a rabbit. The rabbit said to the duck, 'Why do you remain here? There is no water left!'. But the duck, being very powerful and proud, just smiled and said, 'I am the only one here. I will remain no matter what happens'. 

The rabbit shook its head and accepted the duck's decision. Even though the duck's pond was dry, it remained very powerful. In the end, the duck's power allowed it to stay in the pond until it was filled again with water.

Once upon a time there was a little boy called Joey. He was shy, so he didn't like to be around many people. One day, Joey went to the park with his mom and dad. He saw a big tree in the park and decided to kneel down and take a closer look. Joey put his hands on his knees and looked up at the tree. 

Mom and Dad said, "Why don't you give the tree a hug?"

Joey was shy, so he shook his head and said, "No."

But Mom and Dad knew he wanted to give the tree a hug. So, they kneeled down next to Joey and said, "It's OK to be shy. Let's give the tree a hug together!"

Joey smiled and reached out his little arms to hug the tree. He felt happy and brave. Joey, Mom, and Dad all hugged the tree together. Then they got up and skipped off to play in the park.

Once upon a time, there was a clever little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and explore the world around her. One day, she went to the park with her mom and saw a police officer.

"Mommy, who is that?" she asked.

Once upon a time, there was a big wheel. It was stuck between two trees and no one knew how to move it.
