Once there was a young girl who was very compassionate. One day, she went shopping with her mother and found the most beautiful towel. It was bright yellow and soft like a cloud.

The girl begged her mother to buy it for her. Seeing the child's excitement and understanding the value of a special toy, her mother decided to spoil her. She bought the towel and the girl was delighted. 

The girl loved her towel! She stretched it out and hugged it. She used it for playing and for drying herself off after a bath. From then on, it was her most prized possession.

Whenever she needed an extra special comfort, the girl would cuddle up with her bright yellow towel and feel the compassionate love from her mother.

One day, a white owl lived in a big tree. The white owl loved to fly at night and look for food. The white owl had a friend, a small brown mouse. They liked to play together in the forest.

One day, the white owl saw a big, red apple on the ground. The white owl wanted to share the apple with the small brown mouse. But the apple was not good. It was old and it had started to rot. The white owl did not know that the apple was bad.

The white owl and the small brown mouse ate the bad apple. Soon, they both felt sick. They were very sad because they could not play together in the forest anymore. The white owl and the small brown mouse learned that they should not eat food that is old and rotten.

Once upon a time, there was a friendly swan who lived in a big pond in the woods. Everyday she liked to swim around, singing and talking to the other animals who lived there.

One day the swan saw something strange up in the sky. It was a big, loud machine that was coming closer and closer. As it got near, the swan suddenly saw why it was making so much noise--it was delaying. She was so scared she started to swim away.

But then something amazing happened! One of the friendly people in the machine waved at the swan and smiled. She was so shocked, but happy too. She waved back and kept swimming.

Finally, the machine flew away, leaving the friendly swan all alone in the pond. But that was okay, because she knew her special moment with the kind people in the machine would stay with her forever.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Jane. Jane seemed so tired all the time. She always felt like it was too hard to do anything. She wished she could have some food that could help her get more energy.

One day, Jane saw a special kind of food and decided to eat some. She ate it quickly, but it didn't seem to make her feel any better. She was still feeling very tired.

"Maybe I should eat some more," she thought. So she did.

But after she ate the second helping of food, she still didn't seem to have any more energy. She felt even more tired than before.

"What is wrong with me?" she asked.

Suddenly, Jane started to feel very weak and dizzy. She quickly passed out on the floor.

And that's how Jane's story ended with a bad ending.

Lily and Tom were playing hide and seek in the dark. Lily was the seeker and Tom was the hider. Lily had a flashlight to help her find Tom. She looked under the bed, behind the curtains, and in the closet. She could not see Tom anywhere.

"Tom, where are you?" Lily called out. "I give up, you can come out now."

But Tom did not answer. He was hiding in the basement, behind some boxes. He was deaf, so he could not hear Lily. He thought she was still looking for him. He smiled and waited for her to find him.

Lily was worried. She wondered why Tom did not come out. She decided to look for him in the basement. She took her flashlight and went down the stairs. She saw some boxes and moved them aside. She saw Tom kneeling behind them. He looked surprised and happy.

"Lily, you found me!" Tom said. He hugged Lily and gave her a high five.

"Tom, I was calling you for a long time. Why didn't you answer?" Lily asked.

"Sorry, Lily. I did not hear you. I am deaf, remember?" Tom said.

"Oh, yes. I forgot. You are deaf. But you are also very good at hiding. You are the best hider ever!" Lily said.

"Thank you, Lily. You are the best seeker ever. And the best friend ever!" Tom said.

They both laughed and went back upstairs. They decided to play another game. They had a lot of fun together.

Tom and Lily were playing with their cardboard castle. They had made it with their dad, who was very good at cutting and sticking. They liked to pretend they were a king and a queen, and they had a lot of fun.

But one day, their dog Spot ran into the castle and knocked it over. He was very excited and wanted to play, but he did not know he was breaking their castle. Tom and Lily were very sad. They cried and shouted at Spot. "Bad dog! Go away! You ruined our castle!"

Spot felt sorry and wagged his tail. He did not mean to make them unhappy. He licked their faces and tried to cheer them up. But Tom and Lily were still angry. They did not want to play with him.

Their dad heard the noise and came to see what was wrong. He saw the broken castle and the sad children. He hugged them and said, "Don't worry, my loves. We can repair the castle. It will be as good as new. Do you want to help me?"

Tom and Lily nodded. They wiped their tears and smiled. They liked to help their dad. He gave them some more cardboard, some tape, and some scissors. They worked together to fix the castle. They made it even bigger and better than before. They added some windows, some flags, and some flowers.

When they were done, they were very proud of their castle. They thanked their dad and gave him a big hug. They invited Spot to join them. They said, "We are sorry, Spot. We know you did not mean to hurt our castle. You are our friend. Do you want to play with us?"

Spot barked happily. He was glad they were not mad at him. He ran into the castle and wagged his tail. He pretended he was a guard dog, and he protected the king and the queen. Tom and Lily laughed and played with him. They were a jolly family. They had a lot of fun.

Mia and Ben are twins. They like to play outside with their dog, Spot. Spot is a big, black dog with a white spot on his chest. He is very friendly and enthusiastic. He likes to run and jump and chase balls.

One day, Mia and Ben decide to go for a walk with Spot. They put on their coats and hats and shoes. They ask their mom if they can go. Mom says yes, but they have to stay on the street and not go too far. Mia and Ben agree. They take a leash and a ball and go outside.

They walk along the street, looking at the houses and the cars and the trees. They see some other kids playing in a park. They wave and say hello. They throw the ball for Spot and he runs after it. He brings it back and wags his tail. He is having fun.

But then, something bad happens. Spot sees a squirrel on the other side of the street. He forgets about the leash and the ball and the twins. He runs across the street, chasing the squirrel. He does not look for cars or bikes or people. He is too excited.

Mia and Ben are scared. They call out to Spot. "Spot, come back! Spot, stop! Spot, no!" They try to follow him, but they remember what mom said. They have to stay on the street. They do not want to get hurt or lost. They do not know what to do.

They see a lady walking by. She has a kind face and a blue dress. They ask her for help. "Excuse me, lady, can you help us? Our dog ran away. He is a big, black dog with a white spot. He chased a squirrel. We have to find him. He is our best friend."

The lady smiles and nods. She says, "Don't worry, kids, I will help you. I like dogs, too. I have a dog at home. His name is Rex. He is a small, brown dog with a curly tail. He likes to play with balls, too. Let's search for your dog together. Maybe he is still nearby. Maybe he is in the park or behind a house or under a car. We will look everywhere. We will call his name. We will find him. He will be happy to see you."

Mia and Ben feel better. They thank the lady and hold her hand. They start to search for Spot. They hope he is safe and not scared. They hope he will hear them and come back. They love him very much. They are his family.

Once upon a time, there was a mommy who wanted to teach her little girl something new. She picked her up and took her outside. Mommy showed her a big open space and pointed to the sky. She said, "Look at that, my darling. That's called a bird."

The little girl was excited. She smiled and watched the bird fly away. Mommy then put her down and held her hands. She said, "Now I'm going to teach you something else. Can you put your hands around my waist?"

The little girl tried and she could fit both of her hands around her mommy's waist. Mommy said, "That's good. Now I'm going to teach you something else. Can you keep your arms open wide like this?"

The little girl tried and she was able to keep her arms open wide. Mommy said, "Good job, my darling. Now, whenever you open your arms wide like this, always remember I am here to help you."

The little girl smiled and hugged her mommy with both of her arms. She couldn't wait to learn more lessons with her mommy. The end!

Once upon a time there was a little boy named Joe. He was three years old and loved going to the beach. One day Joe asked his mom to take him to the beach. His mom agreed and they got in the car and drove off.

When they arrived at the beach, Joe ran out of the car and directed his attention to the sand. His mom smiled and began to explain what sand was. She said it was made from tiny pieces of rocks that were too small to pick up. She also said that the sand felt soft and nice between the toes. Joe thought that sounded fun and asked if he could try it.

His mom said yes and Joe started to play in the sand. He made sand castles, a tunnel, and lots of tiny mountains. He was so happy at the beach and didn't want to leave. Suddenly, his mom told him it was time to go home. Joe was disappointed but his mom promised him something sweet when they got home. 

Joe jumped up and started to follow his mom to the car. When they got home, Joe's mom showed him some cupcakes. Joe's eyes lit up - they all looked so delicious. Joe's mom picked out the biggest cupcake and handed it to him. Joe thanked her, and the cupcake tasted sweet and even sweeter because his mom had promised it!

Once there was a little girl named Sarah. She was three years old. One day, Sarah was in the kitchen. She saw some candy that was in a jar. 

"I want to eat the candy," she thought. 

But Sarah knew she wasn't allowed to have any candy without asking her parents first. She knew she had to use the words 'Please' and 'Thank you'. So Sarah asked her mom if she could have some candy.

"No, Sarah," her mom said. "It's too much candy. You can have something else."

Sarah was not happy. She really wanted the candy. But she was ashamed to ask her mom again. So Sarah used her sneaky plan. She reached into the jar and grabbed a handful of candy.

Then Sarah heard a loud voice. It was her mom.

"Sarah! Put the candy back! We don't take things without asking!"

Sarah felt embarrassed. She put the candy back in the jar, and she knew she had been wrong. She never used candy without asking again.

John was feeling gloomy as he walked through the park. He noticed a tall tree and decided to shoot at it with his slingshot. 

John's friend Madelyn saw him and said, "Why are you shooting at the tree?" 

John replied, "It's fun!" 

But Madelyn wasn't so sure. She said, "But why would you want to shoot a nice tree like that?" 

John shrugged and said, "I just like shooting stuff!" 

Madelyn shook her head and said, "It's not nice to shoot people or trees." 

John frowned, but he agreed and said, "Okay, I won't shoot the tree anymore." The two friends walked away from the tree, and John started to feel better as he saw the bright blue sky above him.

Once upon a time, there was a boy. His name was Bob. Bob was a happy person and always liked to explore. 
One day, he saw a weird door. He walked up to it and tried to open it, but it was locked! Bob had seen this strange door before, but he never could open it. 
He thought up a plan. He knew that if he could find the right key, he could open the door. He asked his friends if they knew the name of the key. They all said no. 
Bob kept searching and then one day, he found it! He took the key and put it in the lock. He twisted it and the door opened! He was so excited. Bob had found the key to open the strange door. 
He looked inside and it was full of surprises! Bob had an amazing day exploring the weird door.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and draw pictures. One day, she went to the park with her mom and saw a man with an enormous diamond ring. She asked her mom what it was and her mom told her it was a diamond.

Lily wanted a diamond too, so she asked the man where he got it. He told her he planned to give it to his wife as a gift. Lily thought that was a great idea and decided to plan a surprise for her mom too.

Later that day, Lily asked her mom what her favorite color was and her mom said it was blue. So, Lily planned to draw her a picture with lots of blue in it. When her mom saw the picture, she was so happy and hugged Lily tight.

But then, Lily's little brother came and accidentally tore the picture. Lily was upset and cried. Her mom saw what happened and told Lily that accidents happen and that they could plan to make a new picture together. And so, they did.

Sandy was a thin bear and he was very sad. He had been alone for months and he wanted to stay with his family. He suffered a lot without them.

One day, a kind man saw him walking around and offered him a ride. He was so happy and nodded yes. The man drove him back home! When Sandy saw all his family and friends, he couldn't believe it.

They were so happy to see him and hugged him tight. Sandy was so happy and never wanted to stay apart from his family ever again. He could finally forget about the pain he had suffered all alone.

One day, a boy named Tim went to the park. He wore his favorite pants. They were red and had big pockets. Tim liked to play on the swings and slide. He also liked to play with his toy car.

While playing, Tim met a girl named Sue. Sue had a big bag of spicy chips. She asked Tim, "Do you want some chips?" Tim said, "Yes, I like spicy chips!" They shared the chips and talked about their favorite games.

Suddenly, a big bee came near them. Tim was scared. He did not like bees. The bee landed on Tim's pants. Tim used his hand to slap the bee away. The bee flew away and did not come back. Tim and Sue were happy. They continued to play and eat their spicy chips.

One day, Sam was very hungry. He had been playing all afternoon and needed something to eat. He looked in the kitchen but all he could see was a big prune. He didn't like prunes, so he started to worry. 

Sam's mom saw him standing there, so she went to the cupboard and took out some fresh fruit. There were oranges, apples, and bananas! Sam was so excited he started jumping up and down.

He eagerly grabbed a banana and started eating. As he ate, he forgot all about the prune. He felt so much better now that he wasn't hungry anymore. He was so happy he even started singing a song!

So, Sam learned that day that it's important not to worry, because usually things turn out alright in the end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Ann. She went with her mom and dad to a special place. This place was very unique. When they arrived, Ann saw many different animals like cats, dogs and rabbits. Ann was so excited! Her parents told her they were at the veterinarian's office.

There, Ann watched as the veterinarian unpacked all kinds of special items to help take care of the animals. Ann even got to pet a few of the furry friends.

The vet showed her the tools they used to measure weight and temperature, tubes they used to give medicine, and more. Ann was amazed to learn how vets care for animals.

After a while, it was time to go. Ann was sad to leave, but her parents promised that someday she could come back. She hugged all the animals goodbye, and she knew she had a very unique experience.

Once upon a time, there was a nosy rabbit named Benny. Benny loved to hop around and see what everyone was doing. One day, Benny saw a carrot in the garden and he wanted to eat it. But the carrot was too big for him to carry.

Benny asked his friend, a wise old owl, "How can I get the carrot?" The owl replied, "You need help from your friends. Together, you can unite and pull the carrot out of the ground."

Benny went to his friends, a group of squirrels, and asked for their help. They all agreed to help Benny get the carrot. They united their strength and pulled the carrot out of the ground.

Benny was so happy that he got the carrot with the help of his friends. He shared the carrot with all of them and they all enjoyed it together. From that day on, Benny learned that sometimes it's better to work together and unite to achieve a goal.

Once there was a little girl named Sarah. Sarah was so shy that she would never speak up. Nobody knew what she was like or what she was thinking.

One day Cynthia, Sarah's best friend, came over. Cynthia asked Sarah if they could bake something together. Sarah was scared, but she said yes. 

They gathered all the ingredients, and carefully measured them. They placed everything into the bowl, and stirred until it was nice and creamy. Then they put it all into the oven.

The smell was amazing! Cynthia and Sarah waited until the timer buzzed to a big zero. Out came the delicious cake. It was golden brown, and smelled so good.

Cynthia and Sarah smiled at each other. They were so happy. That day, Sarah had become braver and less shy. They shared the cake and enjoyed it together.

Once upon a time, there was a bright model. It was a very pretty model. It was made of paper and had lots of colours on it. 

The model was empty, so the child wanted to fill it. They grabbed some crayons and began to colour! Every stroke of the crayon made the model brighter and brighter. 

Soon enough, all the colours were used up. Finally, the model was filled with bright, colourful shapes. The child admired it, looking at how pretty it had become. They were so happy! 

The end.

Once upon a time, there were two best friends who loved to play together - Alex and his pet dog, Spot. One day, Alex brought a metal toy car to play with. He put it down and started playing, but Spot got too excited and SNAP - the metal car broke. Alex got worried and started to panic. 

"Spot, why did you break my toy?" Alex asked with a sad voice. 

Spot whimpered and curled up with his tail between his legs. He knew he had done something wrong.

Alex was still worried, but he knew he had to forgive Spot. He gave his furry friend a big hug and said, "It's ok, I still love you Spot".

Spot was so happy that he started jumping up and down, and the two best friends went back to playing and having fun together.

Teddy and his Mom were walking through town. Suddenly, Teddy saw something sparkly and he wanted to pick it up. His Mom said, "No, Teddy. That could be very dangerous." 

They kept walking, but Teddy kept asking and wanting to pick it up. Eventually, his Mom agreed and Teddy picked up the sparkly object - it was a small bottle of medicine. His Mom said that this medicine was very rare, so they decided to take it to the doctor. 

At the doctor's office, the doctor studied the medicine and said it was safe for Teddy. He discussed with Teddy's Mom if it was ok for Teddy to take the medicine, and they all agreed it was a good idea. 

Teddy took the medicine and felt much better afterwards - the doctor said it was a good thing they found this rare medicine!

Once there was a boy who loved to compete with his friends. He was very competitive, and he always wanted to win in all the games they played. 

One day, he thought of a new game. He wanted to see if he could change the measure of something. He grabbed a ruler and measured his arm. Then he asked his friends to try and measure something bigger or smaller than him. 

At first, no one could succeed in changing the measure. But then his friend Jerry tried and measured his foot. It was bigger than the boy's arm! Everyone cheered for Jerry and the boy was impressed. 

From then on, the boy was always excited to play games with his friends. He was even more competitive, trying to change the measures of different things and see who could win!

Frank was confused. He had a guitar but did not know what to do with it. He looked around for help. Suddenly, his mom came in. She smiled at him and said, "I'll show you what to do." She took the guitar and showed him how to separate the strings. Frank was excited. He watched his mom carefully as she pulled each string. He tried to do the same. After several tries he was able to separate the strings. Frank was so happy he started to play the guitar. His mom watched him while he played the guitar. Soon, they were singing and playing together. Frank had so much fun!

One day, Bob and his Mummy went to the park. When they got there, they saw something strange in the sky. Bob asked his Mummy what it was, so she explained that it was called fog.

The fog was very thin and looked like a white cloud. It was also very soft and mysterious. Bob was curious and wanted to touch the fog. So they both walked closer and Bob reached out his hand. As Bob touched it, the fog felt cold and made his hand wet.

Bob was very surprised. He had never felt anything like this before. It was like a secret, hidden in the sky. He and his Mummy watched the fog for a while, until it slowly disappeared. 

Bob and his Mummy were both very happy to have seen the fog and Bob was so excited to learn something new. He kept asking questions about it for the rest of the day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sally. She loved to dance. Every day she would twirl and jump around with joy.

One day, Sally heard music coming from a nearby station. She skipped over and saw a big pile of soft pillows. She plopped down and started to dance. She jumped, twirled and laughed with delight. 

Soon all the other children joined Sally. They twirled and spun together in a circle. Everyone was having so much fun! Even the birds and the bees were dancing to the music.

When their dance was finished, Sally's mother called her home. Sally said goodbye to the other children and skipped away. As she walked, she could still feel the rhythm of the music in her heart.

Once upon a time there were two siblings, Sam and Lucy. Sam was very curious and he loved to ask questions. One day he asked his mom, "What is meat?". His mom replied, "Meat is food that comes from animals. We shouldn't eat too much of it." Sam disagreed, he thought that eating lots of meat was cool.

The next day his mom said, "Tomorrow we'll be going to the park and we won't be eating meat". Sam became frustrated and asked, "But why?". His mom replied, "There are no animals in the park, so there's no meat. We'll bring some food from home". Sam shook his head and said "It's not fair".

His mom then said, "No, it is fair. We can't always do what we want to do. We must respect all living things, no matter how small. So we won't be eating meat tomorrow in the park."

Sam thought about it for a moment and then he replied, "Okay mommy, I understand now".

The Moral of the story is that it is important to respect all living things, big and small. We may not always get what we want, but we should always be respectful of everyone and everything around us.

Tommy wandered the beach, searching for shells and other treasures. As the sun moved across the sky, he eventually found something unusual near the shoreline. It was a hook! He picked it up and tried to figure out what it was for. But he found nothing else, just the one lonely hook.

He was a bit frustrated, but then he spotted something in the sand. He quickly ran over and saw it was a rope, connected to the hook. He started pulling the rope with excitement. After a few moments, he found a small bucket at the end of the rope!

Tommy was elated. He looked up to the sky and smiled. Then he ran to his mom, who was sitting under a nearby umbrella. â€œMom, look what I found!â€ he said. â€œIt's a hook and a bucket!â€

His mother chuckled. â€œThat's wonderful, Tommy!â€ she said. â€œYou can use the hook for fishing, and the bucket for collecting shells.â€

Tommy was so excited that he ran off to find his dad and tell him all about his discovery.

One day a little girl named Lucy was playing with her toys when she heard a funny noise outside. She opened the door and saw a big truck with a mechanic working on it. The mechanic was friendly and greeted Lucy with a wave.

"Hi there!" said the mechanic. "What are you up to?"

Lucy smiled and replied, "I'm playing with my toys!"

The mechanic nodded and paused to think. "Hey, do you want to help me out?"

Lucy's eyes lit up and she eagerly said, "Yes!"

The mechanic handed Lucy a wrench and asked her to help him tighten a few screws. Lucy was so excited and worked hard on the task. After a few moments, the mechanic smiled and said, "Thank you for your help, that was really friendly of you."

Giggling, Lucy waved goodbye and ran inside to tell her mom about her special adventure with the friendly mechanic.

Once upon a time, there were two friends named Sarah and Tony, who loved to go for walks in their town. One day, they wanted to explore a part of town they hadn't seen before. They had to choose which way to go. There was a beautiful creek with a bridge that crossed over it or a dark, mysterious forest. 

Tony chose the creek and they headed towards the bridge. It was a beautiful walk and they found a lot of new things to explore. But when they reached the bridge, they stopped. It looked old and dangerous, and they weren't sure if it was safe to cross. 

Sarah stopped and thought for a moment. She said to Tony, "Let's not cross it, Tony. It looks too dangerous. Let's find another way."

Tony realized Sarah was right, and they chose the safe option. They found a nicer, safer bridge to cross, and they safely made it to the other side of the creek and found some wonderful things to explore.

The moral of the story is that it is important to choose the safe option, even if it is not the most exciting. Taking chances can be dangerous and it is better to make wise choices.

Tom and Sam are friends. They like to play with tools. They have a hammer, a saw, a screwdriver and some nails. They want to make a house for their toys.

They find a big box and some wood. They put the box on the floor and cut the wood with the saw. They make holes in the wood with the hammer and the nails. They talk to each other while they work.

"Look, Sam, I made a door for the house!" Tom says.

"Good job, Tom! I made a window for the house!" Sam says.

They are happy with their house. They put their toys inside and pretend they live there. They have fun.

But soon they get tired. They work hard and it is hot. They sweat and yawn. They need a break.

"Tom, I am tired. Can we stop now?" Sam asks.

"Me too, Sam. Let's have some water and a snack." Tom agrees.

They put down their tools and go to the kitchen. They drink some water and eat some cookies. They feel better.

They go back to their house and play some more. They are proud of their work. They smile and hug. They are good friends.

Once upon a time there was a sunflower named Lucy. She loved to dance. Every day, she would play happy music and twirl around the garden.

One day, Lucy was dancing when she bumped into a bee. The bee was so gentle, he gave her head a squeeze. Lucy was so grateful. She thanked the bee with a twirl and soon they were dancing together. 

They twirled and bounced all around the garden. When they stopped to take a break, Lucy asked the bee why he was so happy. The bee replied, "My honey is the sweetest in the world, and when I make my honey, I get to dance!" Lucy smiled and gave the bee a big squeeze. 

From that day on, Lucy and the bee were the best of friends, always dancing, buzzing and having lots of fun in the garden.

Once upon a time, a big whale lived in the sea. The whale was slow and liked to swim all day. One day, the whale saw a small fish swimming by. The fish was so fast and made the whale feel sad because it couldn't swim as fast. 

The whale asked the fish, "How do you swim so fast?" The fish replied, "I balance my body and move my tail quickly." The whale tried to balance its body and move its tail quickly, but it was too big and slow. 

The whale felt sad and thought it could never be as fast as the fish. But then, the whale had an idea! It asked the fish, "Can you teach me how to balance?" The fish agreed and taught the whale how to balance its body. 

After lots of practice, the whale was able to balance and swim faster than ever before! The whale was happy and thanked the fish for teaching it how to balance. From that day on, the whale and the fish became good friends and swam together in the sea.

Tim and Tom are brothers. They like to play with their toys. They have cars, trains, blocks and dolls. But they do not like to share. They always fight over the toys.

One day, Tim sees Tom playing with his favorite car. He gets angry. He runs to Tom and grabs the car. He says, "This is my car! Give it to me!"

Tom does not want to give the car. He holds it tight. He says, "No, this is my car! I found it first!"

They pull and tug on the car. They yell and scream. They do not hear their mom coming.

Mom sees them fighting. She is not happy. She says, "Stop it, boys! You are being bad! You will destroy the car if you keep pulling it!"

But they do not listen. They keep pulling the car. The car breaks in half. They both cry.

Mom takes the car away. She says, "You have to share your toys. If you do not share, you will have no toys. You will go to your rooms for a minute and think about what you did."

Tim and Tom go to their rooms. They are sad. They wish they had not fought over the car.

They see their hairy dog, Spot, on their beds. Spot is happy to see them. He wags his tail. He licks their faces. He makes them smile.

They hug Spot. They say, "We are sorry, Spot. We love you. You are our best friend."

They learn to share their toys. They play nicely with Spot. They do not destroy their toys anymore. They are good brothers.

Once upon a time, a little boy named Tim went to visit his grandma. She lived in a small house near the woods. Tim liked to play with his toys and eat cookies at grandma's house.

One day, Tim saw a weak bird outside. He was worried about the bird. He asked his grandma, "What can we do to help the bird?" Grandma said, "We can give it some food and water."

They put food and water near the bird. The bird ate and drank. Soon, it felt better and could fly again. Tim was happy to help the bird. He and his grandma went back inside and enjoyed their cookies.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Maddie. She loved to mix things together in her playroom. One day, Maddie mixed together lots of different colors and made something new. It was a pretty color she had never seen before!

Maddie wanted to move the new color around, so she started to make some motion with it. She moved the new color quickly and slowly, round and round. It made her very happy to do this.

When Maddie was done, she noticed something. By mixing the colors together, and then making motion with the mixed color, Maddie had made something special. It was an easy way to mix colors and make something new! Maddie couldn't believe it. She was so proud of herself for making something cool and easy.

Once upon a time, there was a girl. She was playing with her toys and having lots of fun.

Suddenly, she heard a loud noise and became very fearful. She searched for the source of the noise but could not find it. She kept trying until she found a well.

She slowly approached the well, and as she was about to finish exploring, she heard the noise again and it seemed to be coming from the well. She was scared and did not know what to do.

But, before she could turn back, the ground beneath her feet began to shake, and she heard a loud rumble. She tried to escape, but it was too late. The ground opened up and the well had swallowed her up!

The girl was never seen again, as fear had taken over her life. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She was brave and fun. One day, she was playing outside with her friends when something scary happened.

She saw a big, dark card floating through the sky. It was so big and so scary! She was so scared she ran to her house and hid under her bed.

Her mom found her and asked what had happened. The little girl told her mom about the card. Mom said â€œThatâ€™s okay, sweetie. You donâ€™t have to be scared. Itâ€™s just a cardâ€¦â€

The little girl felt better after hearing her momâ€™s words. She looked out the window and there it was - the card had flown away. The little girl was so happy and she ran outside to play with her friends again.

The End!

Once there was a wide and open field. In the field, there were two children playing. They were running and laughing, having lots of fun. 
Suddenly, one of the children felt sick. He stopped playing and said to the other, "Let's go home." 
They went back to the house, and the sick child's mommy gave him medicine. The medicine tasted a bit funny but it made him feel better. 
Soon, he felt all better and wanted to go back out to the wide open field to play. His friend said, "Let's go!" 
They happily ran back to the field and continued playing until it was time for dinner.

One day, Tom had a very special tool. It was big and yellow, and Tom was so proud of it. Every time he used it, it would glow brilliantly. Everyone was amazed how intelligent Tom was with his tool. Tom was always eager to use his tool and show it off.

One day, Tom decided to use his tool. But as he was playing, something went wrong. The toolâ€™s glow quickly changed to a deep, menacing red. Everyone ran away in fear, including Tom. He was so scared that he quickly ran away too and never came back. 

But something even worse happened. Whenever the tool would glow red, a rain of bad things would come afterwards. People were terrified of the tool, and bitterly blamed Tom for it.

Tom never returned and his beloved tool was left behind. People avoided the tool, scared of its deep red glow. Unfortunately, Tom and his tool were never seen again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily was very happy because she loved going on adventures with her family. One day, she went on a camping trip with her mom and dad. 

At night, they went for a walk in the forest. Lily was holding a flashlight and looking at all the trees. Suddenly, she stumbled on a rock and fell down. She started to cry. 

Her mom and dad came running over to her. "Are you okay, Lily?" her mom asked. "I fell down," Lily said while wiping her tears. "It's okay," her dad said, "let's get up and keep walking." 

Lily held her dad's hand and they continued their adventure. She was happy again and excited to see what else they would find in the forest.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was very restless and couldn't sit still. Her mommy gave her a gift, a soft and cuddly teddy bear. Lily hugged the teddy bear tightly and felt happy.

Lily's mommy asked, "Do you like your gift, Lily?"

Lily nodded her head and said, "Yes, mommy. Teddy is my friend."

Lily then asked her mommy, "Can we go outside and play?"

Her mommy replied, "Sure, but first we need to rest for a little while."

Lily hugged her teddy bear again and said, "Okay, mommy. I'll rest with Teddy."

Mandy and her mom were walking through a big park. Mandy saw lots of boats in the lake and she was excited to ride one. She asked her mom if they could go for a boat ride.

Her mom said, "Maybe later, Mandy. It looks a bit cold out there."

Mandy shivered and wrapped her blanket around her. Her mom smiled and said, "It looks like you need to get inside to stay warm."

Mandy and her mom headed towards the house. When they got there, her mom said, "Let's make something to eat. We can use the dishwasher to help us cook."

Mandy liked the idea and they began cooking. But when they opened the dishwasher, they saw a mouse inside! Mandy's mom looked very serious and said, "We can't turn it on now. We will have to find another way to cook the food."

Mandy started to look around the kitchen. She finally found an old pot and said, "We can use this pot to cook the food."

Her mom smiled and said, "That's a great idea, Mandy!"

So Mandy and her mom were able to cook their dinner without the dishwasher. Mandy was glad that even though there was a problem, she could help to solve it.

The dark was all around. Jack was confused. He didn't know what to do. He looked around, but all he could see was the dark. Then, he had an idea. He started to fold his hands together. He folded and folded, and soon the darkness wasn't dark anymore. Instead, the darkness was filled with soft light and happy colours! Jack was no longer confused. He was filled with joy and happiness!

Once there was a beautiful poppy who loved to dance. Every day she would twirl and hop around the meadow nearby. It made her so glad to move her feet and be wild and free.

One evening a little girl spotted the dancing flower and was amazed. She asked the poppy, "Can I dance too?".
The poppy grinned and replied, "Yes! Of course, my dear. Just move your feet and let the music in your heart show you the way".

The little girl joined in and the two of them danced together, around and around in circles. It was so much fun! They laughed and spun until the sky was filled with stars.

When they were done, the little girl was so very glad. She hugged the poppy one last time before heading home. They both knew that they would be dancing together again soon.

Once upon a time, in a big forest, there lived a little squirrel named Tim. Tim loved to travel from tree to tree with his friends. They played games and had fun all day long.

One day, Tim saw a very tall tree. He wanted to go to the top of the tree. His friends told him it was dangerous, but Tim was brave and wanted to try. He started to climb up, up, up the tree.

When Tim got to the top, he looked around and saw the whole forest. It was so beautiful! His friends cheered for him from below. Tim was happy he made it, but he knew it was dangerous. He climbed back down and promised to be careful. From then on, Tim and his friends continued to travel and play, but they always stayed safe.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Amy. One day she went to the park with her mom. 

She ran over to the swings and hopped right on. She was so excited! She started to move back and forth, back and forth. 

Suddenly, she heard a weird sound. She stopped and looked around. A big bird had landed on the swing next to her. The bird disturbed Amy! 

But then the bird flew away, and Amy was happy again. She hopped back on her swing and smiled as she went back and forth, back and forth.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his uncle. His uncle was very funny and always made Timmy laugh. One day, Timmy and his uncle went outside to play. Timmy saw a pretty butterfly and tried to grab it, but it flew away. His uncle told him not to worry and that there were many more butterflies to see. Suddenly, the sky became very dark, and Timmy was scared. But his uncle turned on a light and everything became bright again. Timmy was happy and hugged his uncle. They continued to play and have fun together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, her mom asked her to help make pancakes for breakfast. Lily was excited to help, but she found it hard to mix the batter. Her arms were little and the batter was thick.

But Lily didn't give up. She kept mixing and mixing until the batter was smooth. She poured the batter onto the pan and waited patiently for it to cook. When it was finished, she proudly showed her mom the delicious pancakes she made all by herself.

The moral of the story is that even if something is hard, you can finish it if you keep trying. And sometimes, the end result is even better because you worked hard for it.

Once upon a time, there was a boat in the middle of the sea. It was a very colorful boat. It had bright blue and green stripes, and lots of stars and circles. 

The boat floated and bobbed up and down in the water. A young girl was sitting next to the boat, and she was observing the boat very carefully. 

She smiled and looked at the bright colors. Then she stretched out her small hand and touched the boat. She laughed happily and laughed at how the boat felt. 

The little girl observed the boat again. She saw that the boat was still floating in the water, and the colors were still very colorful. She was very happy to see the boat and smiled.

Once upon a time, there was a big house with a long hall. The hall was so large that you could run and play in it all day long. One day, a little girl came to the big house to visit her grandma. She was excited to see her grandma and explore the big house.

As they walked down the hall, the little girl noticed a door that was closed. She asked her grandma what was behind the door, but her grandma said it was a surprise and they would have to wait to find out. The little girl couldn't wait to see what was behind the door.

Later that day, after they had lunch, her grandma took her to the door and opened it. Inside, there was a big room with a TV. Her grandma said they could watch their favorite show together. The little girl was so happy and they sat down to watch. It was the best surprise ever!

Once upon a time, there was a little squirrel named Sammy. Sammy loved to collect nuts. He would run around the forest, gathering nuts and storing them in his treehouse. One day, while Sammy was collecting nuts, he met a bossy squirrel named Benny. Benny wanted all the nuts for himself and told Sammy to stop collecting them.

Sammy didn't know what to do. He had never met a bossy squirrel before. Benny kept telling him to stop, but Sammy knew he needed the nuts to survive the winter. Finally, Sammy stood up to Benny and told him that he couldn't stop collecting nuts just because Benny said so.

Benny was surprised by Sammy's bravery and realized that being bossy wasn't the best way to make friends. From that day on, Benny and Sammy collected nuts together and shared them equally. The moral of the story is to stand up for yourself and not let others boss you around.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a toy train with a big engine that she loved to play with. One day, Lily's mommy told her it was time to take a bath. Lily didn't want to stop playing, but she knew she had to listen to her mommy. 

As she was taking a bath, Lily felt lucky to have so many fun toys to play with, including her train with the big engine. She made sure to wash all of her toys too so they could be clean and happy just like her. 

After her bath, Lily's mommy helped her dry off and get dressed. Lily was excited to play with her toys again, especially her lucky train with the big engine. She knew that taking a bath was important to stay clean and healthy so she could have more fun playing with her toys.

Once upon a time, there was an ordinary sunflower. The sunflower loved to hide and play hide and seek all day! Every day, it would hide in a different place - behind the tree, in the grass, behind a rock.

One day, the sunflower decided to hide in the clouds. It imagined the clouds were like pillows, full of softness and fluff. It was so cozy, it stayed there all day, giggling inside its little cloud beds!

As the sun began to set, the sunflower noticed a beautiful, golden sunset. It basked in the warm, golden light and decided it never wanted to leave these wonderful clouds.

The sunflower continued to hide in the clouds every day. Slowly, the sky became more and more orange and red until the sunflower was surrounded by a rainbow of colors! It was the most beautiful thing it had ever seen - and it wanted to stay here forever. 

So that's exactly what the sunflower did - and it continues to hide in the clouds, snuggled and cozied up with its rainbow friends, forever and ever and ever!

Missy was a very fit three year old. She loved to play in the park and do all sorts of fun things with her parents. One day, when they were out in the park, they came across an egg.

Missy was so excited to see it - she had never seen an egg before. When she asked her parents what it was, they explained that it was an egg.

Missy wanted to pick it up and see it. But, when she went to reach for it, her parents asked her to surrender the egg.

Missy was confused. She did not understand why she should surrender it. She asked her parents why they wanted her to surrender it and they explained that they wanted to protect it.

Missy thought about this for a moment, and then she finally agreed. She had to surrender the egg back to its home in the park. She did this, and then she and her parents went home happy. Even though Missy had to surrender the egg, she felt good that she had done the correct thing and been fit.

Jill was on a special trip. She couldn't wait to explore and find new things. Jill saw something that was very exciting and unusual! 

It was something called yoga. She had never seen anything like it before. She wanted to learn more about it. 

Jill decided to try it and so she joined a warm room with lots of people. They all smiled and made her feel welcome. Everyone was doing the same poses and breathing in a focused way. 

Jill felt scares at first but with the help of her friends, she started to feel more relaxed. It was a warm experience and she felt the energy of the group. 

Jill came away from the experience with a smile on her face. She had found something special and new. She would always remember this day and the amazing thing she had found.

Once upon a time, there was a farmer named Suzy. She had a big brown gate. Every day, Suzy went outside and opened the gate. She would go to the market and sell her vegetables.

One day, Suzy opened her gate, but the sun was so warm and bright! She was too tired to go to the market. Instead, Suzy decided to take a nap under the big brown gate.

Suddenly, there was a knock on the gate. Suzy awoke to find a market buyer.

"Hi Suzy, I'm here to buy your vegetables," said the buyer.

"Oh, that's wonderful," said Suzy. She joyfully sold her vegetables to the buyer and thanked him for coming by.

"No problem," said the buyer, as he waved goodbye.

Since then, Suzy always opened her big brown gate to the market, but sometimes she would take a nap under it.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play outside. One day, they see a big rainbow in the sky. It has many colors: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, and purple.

"Wow, look at the rainbow!" Lily says. "It is so pretty!"

"Yes, it is!" Ben says. "Do you think we can touch it?"

Lily and Ben run to the rainbow. They want to hold it in their hands. But the rainbow is too far away. They cannot reach it.

"Maybe we need a ladder," Lily says.

"Or a rocket," Ben says.

They look around. They do not see a ladder or a rocket. They only see a tree, a swing, and a ball.

"Maybe we can make a rainbow," Lily says. "We can use the ball and the swing."

"How?" Ben asks.

Lily has an idea. She takes the ball and throws it in the air. The sun shines on the ball. The ball makes a little rainbow on the ground.

"Look, Ben, a rainbow!" Lily says.

Ben sees the rainbow. He is glad. He runs to the rainbow. He tries to hold it in his hands. But the rainbow is too small. It disappears.

"Oops, it is gone," Ben says.

Lily throws the ball again. The ball makes another rainbow. Ben tries to hold it again. But the rainbow is gone again.

They do this many times. They have fun. They laugh and giggle.

They do not need a ladder or a rocket. They have a ball and a swing. They have each other. They are happy.

Lily was sick. She had a bad cough and a sore throat. Mommy gave her some medicine, but Lily did not like it. It was bitter and yucky. She made a face and spit it out.

Mommy was upset. She said, "Lily, you need to take your medicine. It will make you feel better." She tried to give Lily the medicine again, but Lily turned her head and said, "No, no, no!"

Lily ran away from Mommy. She wanted to play with her toys. She did not want to take the medicine. She ran to her room, but she did not see the ball on the floor. She stepped on the ball and stumbled. She fell down and hurt her knee. She cried out loud.

Mommy heard Lily cry. She ran to her room and saw Lily on the floor. She picked her up and hugged her. She said, "Oh, Lily, are you okay? You have a boo-boo on your knee. Let me get a band-aid for you."

Lily stopped crying. She looked at Mommy and said, "I'm sorry, Mommy. I was naughty. I did not take my medicine. Can I have it now?" Mommy smiled and said, "Yes, Lily, you can have your medicine now. I'm glad you changed your mind. It will make you feel better." She gave Lily the medicine and a glass of water. Lily drank it and made a face, but she did not spit it out.

Mommy kissed Lily and said, "Good girl, Lily. I love you. Now, let's go to bed. You need to rest and get well." Lily nodded and said, "I love you too, Mommy. Thank you for the medicine and the band-aid." Mommy tucked Lily in and turned off the light. Lily closed her eyes and fell asleep. She dreamed of happy things.

Once upon a time, there was an ugly anchor who was very lonely. He wanted to explore the world, but had no one to go with him. One day, he decided to pack his things and go on an adventure.

The anchor said to the fish, "Will you come with me on my adventure?" 

The fish said, "Yes! I will be your friend!"

So, the anchor and the fish packed their things and set off on their adventure. They toured the world together, having fun and becoming good friends. 

They had so much fun exploring and making memories together! 

The end!

One day, a little girl explored her neighbourhood. She found a modern tree that caught her eye. She wondered how to solve the mystery of the tree. She looked at it closely and saw a nest in its branches. A little bird flew out of the nest and the little girl smiled.

The bird flew around the tree and the little girl followed it. The bird's wings were strong and it landed on one of the tree's branches. The little girl was delighted and wanted to continue exploring. She wanted to say hello to the bird, but it flew away. 

The little girl was sad but she had an idea. She asked her dad for help and he gave her a ladder. She carried the ladder to the modern tree and tried to reach the bird's nest. She was so close. She climbed just a bit higher and there it was - the bird's nest! She was so happy that she had solved the mystery. 

The little girl thanked her dad for helping her and went to bed with a smile on her face. The modern tree was her new best friend.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Jack. He wanted a taxi all to himself! So one day, Jack decided to design his own taxi. He felt so proud of what he had created. He could go wherever he wantedâ€”whenever he wanted!

His younger brother, Tom, was very jealous. Tom wanted a taxi too, but he just couldn't find the time to build one. Every day, he watched Jack get into his own taxi and roll right off into the city.

One day, Joe had a difficult day at school. He was bored and frustrated. He didn't like to use the chalk on the whiteboard. He hated the way that it felt when it scratched the board.

The teacher took out a big box of colourful chalk. Joe was excited! She showed him how to draw a picture. Joe quickly created an amazing picture with the chalk. He loved the way it moved and felt. 

Joe now looked forward to coming to school. He no longer hated the chalk. He used it to make beautiful pictures and stories with his teacher.

Once upon a time, there was a grumpy bear named Bob. Bob lived in a small house in the woods. He loved to eat popcorn all day long.

One day, Bob heard a knock on his door. He opened it and saw a little girl. The girl said, "Hi, I'm Lily. Can I have some popcorn, please?" Bob was grumpy, but he liked to share. So, he gave Lily some popcorn.

After they ate the popcorn, Lily said, "Thank you, Bob." Then, she went back to her house. Bob was not grumpy anymore. He was happy he made a new friend. Before going to bed, Bob remembered to lock his door. And from that day on, Bob and Lily were the best of friends.

Once upon a time, in a big tree, there was a little squirrel. The little squirrel loved to find nuts. One day, he found a big, rough nut on the ground. He was very happy and said, "Wow! This is the biggest nut I have ever seen!"

The little squirrel tried to open the rough nut, but it was too hard. He said, "I need help to open this nut." So, he asked his friend, the bird, for help. The bird tried to open the nut with its beak, but it was still too hard. They both said, "We need more help."

They went to their friend, the strong bear. The bear tried to open the rough nut with his big paws. With a loud crack, the nut opened! Inside, there were many small, tasty nuts. The little squirrel, the bird, and the bear shared the nuts and said, "Thank you for helping us open the rough nut!"

From that day on, the friends always helped each other when they found something hard to do. They learned that working together made things easier and more fun. And they all lived happily in the big tree.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Sarah. She liked playing on the playground with her friends.

One day when she was playing, Sarah saw a big track. "Wow!" she said, pointing at it. She asked her friend, "What is this?"

Her friend replied, "It's a track. A lot of people work hard on it!"

Sarah was excited - she wanted to try it. She asked her friend, "Can I try?"

Her friend said, "Sure! Just be careful."

Sarah stepped onto the track. She worked very hard, running around the track and jumping over the bumpy parts. After a while, she was tired, but she still wanted to keep playing. She said to her friend, "I love this track. I think I'm gonna keep playing!"

Her friend smiled and said, "That's great. You work so hard on the track!"

Sarah was so proud of herself - she felt like she had accomplished something. And she knew that if she kept working hard, she'd get even better at it. From then on, Sarah spent a lot of time playing on the track, and she got better and better.

One day, a nosy cat named Zip saw a lime on the ground. Zip was curious about the lime. He sniffed it and pawed at it. The lime rolled away from Zip, and he chased after it.

As Zip played with the lime, a little girl saw him. She laughed and clapped her hands. "Look, Mommy! The cat is playing with the lime!" she said. Her mommy smiled and watched Zip.

Zip liked the little girl and her mommy. He picked up the lime in his mouth and brought it to them. The little girl giggled and petted Zip. From that day on, Zip, the little girl, and her mommy became good friends, and they played with the lime every day.

Once upon a time, there was a little crab named Tim. Tim lived by the ocean and loved to play in the sand. One day, Tim saw a big wave coming towards him. He tried to move away, but his little legs weren't fast enough. The wave swept Tim away into the ocean.

Tim didn't know how to swim, so he struggled to stay afloat. He tried to call for help, but no one came. The tide was too strong, and Tim couldn't keep up. He felt scared and alone.

Just when Tim thought he couldn't hold on any longer, a kind dolphin saw him struggling. The dolphin was compassionate and wanted to help Tim. She swam over and carried Tim safely to the shore.

Tim was grateful to the dolphin and thanked her for being so kind. From that day on, Tim never forgot to be careful around the ocean and always remembered the compassionate dolphin who saved his life.

John wanted to play in the park. He saw the funny pitch with two baseball bats propped up against the fence. As he walked towards them, he heard a voice. 

"Do you want to play a game?" John turned and saw a smiling girl.

John nodded his head. "Yes!"

The girl grabbed one of the bats and handed it to John. "Let's play," she said.

John was so excited. He felt the ball in his hands and knew it was going to be a lot of fun. They spent the afternoon playing ball and running in the pitch. When they tired, they stopped and the girl said, 

"That was a lot of fun. Do you want to do it again tomorrow?"

John smiled. "Yes! I want to play again tomorrow."

The girl picked up the bats and smiled. "It'll be fun. See you in the pitch!" 

John waved goodbye, already looking forward to the next day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She wanted to go on a trip with her family, so she packed her luggage. Her mom said, "Lily, don't forget to pack your favorite dress." 

Lily replied, "I already did, Mommy! Can we go now?"

They went to the airport to catch their flight, but there was a problem. The flight was delayed. Lily got bored and said, "Mommy, can we bake cookies while we wait?"

Her mom said, "That's a great idea, Lily! Let's go buy some cookie dough."

They bought the cookie dough and baked cookies together. They became so popular that other people in the airport wanted to try them too. But they didn't have enough cookies to share with everyone. Lily felt sad that they couldn't share with everyone, but her mom said, "Don't worry, Lily. We can always bake more cookies next time."

Once upon a time, there were two best friends who loved to play. Their names were Toni and Jack. 
One day, when Toni and Jack were playing in the park, Toni saw something shiny near a tall tree. She ran over to it, but Jack followed her and said, "What is it?" 
Toni looked down and saw a bag of sugar. She smiled and said, "Let's take it home."
Jack was very shy and he shook his head no. He said, "We can't steal it. That's not nice."
Toni picked up the sugar and said, "Come on. Nobody will know!" 
But Jack still said no, and even though Toni was sad, she knew Jack was right. So they left the bag of sugar behind and went back to playing.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She was very happy with her life, and she liked to wear pink clothes.

One day, the little girl was playing with her friends. She saw a big, pink flower in the garden. She wanted to pick it, so she went over to take it. 

Suddenly, a big voice came from behind her. "Hey! That's my flower. Don't pick it!" the voice said. 

It was the big cat. The girl was sad and her face began to scrunch up. Hot tears filled her eyes, and started flowing down her face. She began to cry. 

The big cat's face changed, and he said, "Hey now, don't cry. You can pick that flower. It's okay."

The little girl smiled through her tears and wiped her face. She thanked the big cat and carefully picked the flower. 

The little girl and the big cat became friends, and from then on she always asked permission before picking any flowers. The end.

Once upon a time there was a boy named Frank. Frank loved to play with his sock. He thought it was so fun to throw the sock in the air and catch it. One day, Frank jumped into his garden and decided to play forever. He threw the sock up as high as he could and ran to catch it. He ran so fast that, poof! The sock disappeared.

Frank was very confused. He started thinking about where the sock had gone. He looked up in the sky and shouted, â€œsock, where are you?!â€ 

Just then, Frank heard a voice from up above. â€œI'm up here!â€ it said. Frank looked up and saw the sock floating in the air.

Tina watched the colorful birds flying in the sky. She smiled and reached out her arms for a hug. She stood on her tiptoes and tried to reach the birds, but they were too high up. A gust of wind blew in and the birds flew around. Tina laughed as she watched the birds playing. Then they flew away and Tina was sad. She hugged her stuffed toy and twirled around, watching her colorful skirt swing around her. All of a sudden the birds flew back and landed right in front of her. She jumped in surprise and then gasped in delight. The birds gave Tina a big colorful hug and then flew away. Tina smiled and watched them until they were just a speck in the sky.

James loved to play. He always had lots of fun. Today, he was playing in the garden with his friends when suddenly the sky became dark and grey. Lightning flashed in the sky and thunder roared. 

James became frightened and started to cry. His friends huddled together, holding hands. "It's ok," one of them said as he pointed at the ink-black clouds.

Just then, the rain started. Big drops of rain fell from the sky, but James still wanted to play and have fun. He shouted out, "Let's run and play in the rain!"

His friends sighed in relief. They ran and played in the rain, laughing and splashing. James smiled. Even if he was a bit frightened, the rain was still fun.

Mark was a shy 3-year-old boy. He sat alone in the corner of the room, watching all the other children laugh and play with their parents. He wished he could be like them, but he was too scared to join in.

Then one day, he saw a plate full of delicious cakes on the table in the middle of the room. He had never seen cakes before, so he was even shyer than before. He wanted to try one, but he was too scared.

His mummy saw him looking at the cakes and said, "Go on Mark, why don't you try one?" But Mark was still too scared. He didn't think he would fit in if he ate one.

So Mark's mummy said, "It's okay Mark, you can have one if you want." But Mark still didn't move. He looked so sad and shy that his mummy just gave him a kiss and said, "Maybe next time." 

Unfortunately, that next time never came. Mark never tasted the cakes and he never managed to fit in. He stayed in the corner all his life, watching the others and wishing he could be brave enough to join in.

Bob was a mouse. He saw an orange pebble on the ground and wanted to keep it. So he picked it up, put it in his pocket, and ran away with it. When he got home he wanted to keep it forever, so he printed a picture of it. But when he went to print the picture, the ink was too dark, and instead of a lovely orange pebble, it printed a square that was black. Bob was sad and his orange pebble was gone forever.

Once upon a time there was a spider who wanted to join the club. The spider had heard of the club and was very excited to take part.

The spider asked the other members of the club how he could join. 
"You have to be an honest spider to join this club," said one pigeon. 

So the spider started crawling all around, trying to be as honest as possible. He even stopped to help a caterpillar that was stuck in a tree. The other club members were impressed. 

"Well done, Spider," said the pigeon. "You can join the club!" 
The spider was so happy that he did a dance on the ground. He thanked the pigeon and said, "I'm so glad I was honest!"

The other members of the club welcomed the spider into the club and they all enjoyed lots of fun and games. The spider was so happy to be part of the club.

Once upon a time, there lived a very pretty little girl. Every day, she would take her scooter around the city and explore new places.

One day, she came across an injured bird. She quickly brought some food and water to the bird, hoping it would help to heal it. Then, she placed the bird into a cozy basket and waited until dark.

Suddenly, the bird flew out of the basket. The little girl was so happy to see it fly away. She sat under a tree and watched the bird in the night sky.

The next day, the little girl came back to the spot. She was relieved to find that the bird had healed and was flying around again. She wanted to do something special for the bird, so she brought a new pair of shoes for it. They were so pretty and sparkly!

Once upon a time there was a shortcut. A jogger decided to use it every day. One day, a big hurricane came. The wind was so strong, it was angry! Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. She was three years old and loved exploring her neighborhood. 

One day, she decided to go on an adventure and explore the forest. She grabbed her special folder and put some snacks inside before she left. Then, she went on her way. 

When she got to the forest, she saw a tall tree with a huge nest on top. Inside the nest, she saw a very rich bird with beautiful feathers. The bird looked at Lucy and asked, "What are you doing here?"

The two new friends explored the forest together. Soon, the bird showed Lucy something very special. It was a secret tree filled with delicious fruit. They ate and had fun until it was time to go back home. 

Lucy was so happy that she made a new friend and that they decided to explore the forest together! She put all her treasures and snacks back in her special folder and went home with a smile on her face.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play outside. One day, she found a baby owl that had fallen out of its nest. The owl was very small and didn't have any feathers yet. Lily felt sad for the owl and wanted to help it.

Lily knew that the owl needed to be warm and dry, so she picked it up and took it home. She attached a cozy blanket to a box and put the owl inside. She gave the owl some water and waited for its mommy to come back.

After a while, the mommy owl came back and was very happy to see her baby safe and warm. Lily felt happy too, knowing that she had helped the little owl. The moral of the story is that it's important to help others when they need it.

One day, Jack was playing in the park. He was running around and having a great time. While Jack played, he saw something sparkly out of the corner of his eye. It was a toy tractor with a bright red shovel. Jack couldn't resist, so he slipped it into his pocket and kept playing. 

After he finished playing, Jack rushed home to show his parents his new toy. He showed them proudly and they applauded him. But then his father saw the toy and he said, "Jack, where did you get this?" 

Jack was very scared. He knew he should not have taken the toy. He started to cry and snivel. His father asked him again, "Did you take this from somewhere?"

So his father said, "Okay Jack, we have to give it back to the park. Tomorrow morning you have to take it back and put it in the regular spot so it won't get lost again. Then you can come back to your crib and take a nap. 

Jack understood and nodded. So the next day, Jack and his father returned to the park. Jack placed the tractor in its original spot, and after that he was allowed to go back to his crib for a regular nap. 

The end

Once upon a time there were two friends, Jim and Lilly. Jim was poor and Lilly was very rich. They were both walking through the woods one day when they spotted a large pear tree.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tom. Tom was 3 years old and he loved to play at the park.

John and Tara were playing in the park. John looked towards the horizon and saw an ancient house in the distance. He said to Tara, "Let's go explore the old house!"

Tara agreed, so they ventured off to the house. When they got there, John saw a desk in the corner. He said, "Let's search inside the desk!"

John was sad but he knew Tara was right. They returned the treasure to the desk and quietly left the old house. Even though they couldn't keep the treasure, they had an amazing adventure that they would never forget.

Once there was a bear named Larry. One day Larry wanted to go on an adventure, so he decided to jog. He was feeling very grateful because it was such a beautiful day! Larry jogged and jogged until he spotted something in the sky. It was a jet! He had never seen a jet before and he was very excited.

Larry waved to the jet as it flew over. The pilot of the jet could see him and smiled. The pilot waved back to Larry and flew away. Larry felt so grateful that he got to see the jet. 

He kept jogging and visited all kinds of places. Everywhere he went, he had the most amazing adventures. Whenever he thought about the jet, he felt so grateful. He thanked the pilot for making his day so special.

Once upon a time, there was a little frog called Hop. Hop was very adventurous and liked to explore. One day, Hop decided to explore a new space. It was dark, and Hop felt a bit fearful. But that didn't stop him!

He hopped along, looking around. Suddenly, he saw a stream of something coming towards him. It was pouring down from the sky! Hop jumped away in shock! He was so scared he hopped right back home.

When he got home, he told his friends about the mysterious pouring thing that he had seen. They said it sounded like rain. His friends laughed and told him rain was nothing to be fearful of.

So the next day, Hop ventured out again. He wanted to find the rain and see what it was like. Sure enough, he found it pouring from the sky! He hopped into the space, and felt the cool wet drops on his back. It felt so nice!

Hop jumped around happily in the rain. He wasn't fearful anymore; he was having the best time ever!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lisa. She liked to go on long walks with her mom, who whistled while they walked.

One day, Lisa and her mom were walking along a path, when Lisa saw something that she had never seen before - a tall, metal pole in the ground. She curiously ran up to it, to take a closer look.

Her mom, who was still whistling, asked Lisa what she was looking at. Lisa excitedly told her mom that it was an unknown pole!

Her mom asked her why she thought that it was unknown. Lisa replied that she didn't know what it was for, but it sure looked cool. 

The mom smiled and told Lisa that the pole was to hang a swing from, so that kids could have fun. Lisa was so excited that she ran back to the house to ask her dad to put a swing from the pole so she could play.

Once upon a time, there lived a little girl who was very adventurous. She often dreamed of traveling to far away places. One day, she ventured deep into the forest; her heart full of excitement. 

As she wandered through the trees, she stumbled upon a deep and dark chest. She had no idea what was inside! She peered into the chest, and was surprised to recognize something glimmering in the shadows. She opened the chest, and found a beautiful map!

The girl's eyes lit up with wonder. With this magical map, she could navigate to any place she wanted. She quickly tucked the map into her pocket and hurried off on many exciting adventures. 

Happy and fulfilled with each journey, the little girl thanked the mysterious chest for aiding her on her way. She will recognize the magical chest whenever she passes by.

Once upon a time there was a bunny called Fred. He liked to hop around his garden and play games. One day, Fred was hopping and he hopped so high that he reached the roof of his house! He was very surprised! 

Fred found a very unusual surprise on the roof. It was a butterfly! Fred tried to catch the butterfly but it kept flying away from him. When Fred tried to follow it, the butterfly flew even higher! Fred was so excited to find such an unusual creature on his roof. 

Then, Fred noticed a jar. It had a very special lid with a hole in it. He realized that he could catch the butterfly by putting the jar over it and then closing the lid.

After a few tries, Fred managed to catch the butterfly! Fred took his butterfly to his garden and watched it flutter around. From that day on, Fred went up onto the roof whenever he wanted to find something unusual.

Tom had a long face. He was sad because he could not fit in his old hat. His hat was too small for his big head. He liked his hat very much. It was blue and had a star on it.

One day, he saw a new hat in the shop. It was red and had a rocket on it. He wanted to try it on. He asked his mom if he could.

"Sure, Tom. But remember, you have to pay for it if you like it," his mom said.

Tom nodded and ran to the hat. He put it on his head. It was too big. It covered his eyes and ears. He could not see or hear anything. He felt silly.

"Tom, where are you?" his mom called.

Tom tried to answer, but his voice was muffled by the hat. He stumbled around the shop, bumping into things. He knocked over a shelf of books. He tripped over a toy car. He fell on a pile of clothes.

"Tom, are you okay?" his mom asked, finding him under the hat.

Tom took off the hat and looked at his mom. He had a long face again. He did not like the new hat. It did not fit him at all.

"I'm sorry, mom. I don't want this hat. I want my old hat," he said.

His mom smiled and hugged him. She had a surprise for him. She took out his old hat from her bag. She had fixed it for him. She had added some fabric and a button to make it bigger.

"Look, Tom. I made your hat fit you. Do you like it?" she asked.

Tom's face lit up. He loved his hat. It was still blue and had a star on it. But now it also had a button that made a beep sound when he pressed it.

"Wow, mom. Thank you. This is the best hat ever. It fits me perfectly," he said.

He put on his hat and pressed the button. It beeped and made him laugh. He hugged his mom again. He was happy. He had a short face.

Once upon a time, there was a girl called Katie. She was three years old and loved to play. On this particular day, her mum was busy and so Katie decided to go out by herself. 

She excitedly ran out of her house and down the street. Eventually, she came across a park with lots of trees. Katie decided to explore. Suddenly, she found an old boot behind a tree. She looked inside and saw that it was locked!

Katie shouted out: "Mum! Mum! Look what I've found!" But there was no answer. 

She asked herself: "How do I open this boot?" She scratched her head, trying to think of a way. Then she had an idea. She ran back to her house to get the key. 

When Katie returned, she placed the key in the lock and tried to turn it. It worked! The boot opened and inside were all sorts of normal things, like a teddy bear, a toy car and a bouncy ball. 

Katie squealed with delight. She had such a fun time playing with all the things she'd found!

Tim and Sam were brothers who liked to play with toy guns. They had many toy guns of different colors and shapes. They liked to shoot at each other and make loud noises. They thought it was fun and exciting.

One day, they decided to play in the garden. The garden was full of flowers and plants that their mom and dad had grown. They were very pretty and smelled nice. Tim and Sam did not care about the flowers and plants. They only wanted to shoot at each other and make loud noises.

They ran around the garden, shooting and shouting. They did not see where they were going. They stepped on the flowers and plants. They broke the stems and petals. They made a big mess. The garden was not pretty anymore. It was sad and ugly.

Mom and dad heard the loud noises and came to see what was happening. They saw the garden and were very angry and sad. They scolded Tim and Sam for being careless and rude. They told them to stop playing with toy guns and to help clean up the garden. They also told them to apologize to the flowers and plants.

Tim and Sam felt sorry and ashamed. They realized they had done something bad. They said sorry to mom and dad, and to the flowers and plants. They helped clean up the garden and tried to fix the damage. They learned to be more careful and respectful of nature. They also learned that playing with toy guns was not as fun as playing with other things. They decided to play with balls and blocks instead. They had more fun and made less noise.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was very nervous because she was going to start school soon. Her mom told her that everything would be okay and that she would make lots of friends.

Lily remembered what her mom said and told Jack that everything would be okay. They became friends and played together while their moms finished their meal. When Lily went to school, she saw Jack again and they were happy to see each other. They were no longer nervous because they had each other.

The little girl stopped crying and smiled. Then the soldier gave the little girl some of the straw he gathered and said," Here, you can use this straw for your bed.â€ 

The little girl was so happy and she hugged the soldier. Together, they both fell asleep in the cozy old barn.

Once upon a time, there was a crazy stick. It had lots of energy and it loved to run and jump. Every day, it would wake up ready for adventure. 

One day, it decided to take a nap in a tree. As it was sleeping, a group of birds flew by and dropped a seed near it. Suddenly, the seed began to grow into a big tree.

The crazy stick was so surprised that it leapt from its sleepy spot. It circled the tree and saw that a bird had made a nest in the branches. The stick laughed and stretched its arms wide.

It decided to make its own nest nearby. It used some of the twigs and leaves it found on the ground and made a comfortable place to lay down. Then, it curled up in the nest for a much needed nap.

When the stick finally woke up, it felt so refreshed. It thanked the bird for helping it find the perfect place for a nap. The stick hopped down from its nest and went off in search of more adventures!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tom. He loved to taste sweet desserts. One day, Tom saw a fine, big cake on the table. It looked so yummy that he wanted to eat it all by himself.

Tom's mom said, "Tom, you can have a small piece of the cake, but you must share the rest with your friends. Sharing is good and makes everyone happy." Tom thought about it and decided to share the cake with his friends.

Tom and his friends ate the cake together. They all said, "Yum! This dessert is so good!" Tom felt happy because he shared the cake with his friends. He learned that sharing is a fine thing to do, and it made everyone feel good.

Then, Snowy saw something shiny at the top of the stair. He ran up the steps, curious and excited. Lily and Ben followed him, but they were not as fast. They had to hold the railing and watch their feet. They wondered what Snowy had found.

When they reached the top, they saw Snowy sitting on a big box with a bow. It was a present for their birthday, which was tomorrow. Snowy had ripped the paper a little and was playing with the ribbon. Lily and Ben gasped and smiled. They wanted to see what was inside.

"Snowy, you naughty cat!" their mom said, coming out of her room. "You spoiled the surprise! This is for Lily and Ben, not for you!" She picked up Snowy and gave him a kiss. "But you are very thoughtful, too. You wanted to share your gift with them, didn't you?"

Lily and Ben hugged their mom and thanked her for the present. They said they were sorry for following Snowy, but they were curious, too. They were thoughtful, too.

Once upon a time there was a little boy who had a plate full of healthy food. He poked it with his finger and he was excited to eat it all. But then, he heard something. Once upon a time, in a big park, there was a yellow flag. The flag lived near a big tree. The tree had many friends, like birds and bugs. Every day, the yellow flag would wave hello to all the friends.
