Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She had a big imagination, and she loved looking up at the sky. One day, when she was looking up she saw something very weird. It was like nothing she had ever seen before.

Once upon a time, there was a red ball. The red ball lived in a big park. One day, a little boy named Tim found the red ball. He played with the red ball all day.

One day, a little girl named Lily went outside to play. The weather was sunny and warm. She saw her friend, Tim, sitting on the grass. He looked sad and sorry.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Daisy. She lived near a wild forest, which was her favorite place. One day, Daisy decided to jog in the forest. She grabbed her red umbrella and set off.

The tiger spent the next few minutes looking for the bird, but he couldn't find him anywhere. He was getting frustrated, until all of a sudden the bird hopped out from behind the tree and said "Boo!" Once upon a time there was a happy little child. The child's name was Abigail and she was three years old. Every day Abigail would go out to play in the park.

Eventually he had to fly down and go back to his life. His adventure was exciting but he knew that the sky was too high for something as small as a pigeon. But the small pigeon never forgot the amazing things he imagined when he flew up so high.

Once upon a time there was a cat called Pat. Pat lived in a big home with his mom and dad. He liked playing with his toys and exploring the house. 

One day, Pat wanted to go outside to play. His mom said he had to stay at home and ignore the things outside. Pat felt sad, but he obeyed his mom. 

So, Pat stayed at home and played with his toys. But he kept looking out the window and wanting to go outside. His mom noticed and bought him a new toy to keep him busy. It was a big truck, and it was very cheap. 

Pat loved his new toy truck! He played with it all day. Soon he forgot all about going outside and was happy staying at home. He and his mom smiled at each other. Pat had learnt his lesson and now always ignores the things outside and is happy playing with his toys at home.

Lily liked balloons. She liked to blow them up and tie them. She liked to make them fly and bounce. She liked to play with them with her friends.

But Max did not like balloons. He was scared of them. He thought they were loud and mean. He did not like to see them or touch them. He hated when Lily played with them.

One day, Lily brought a big red balloon to school. She was very happy. She showed it to her friends and they smiled. But Max saw the balloon and he was very worried. He wanted the balloon to go away.

He had an idea. He found a sharp stick and he hid it in his hand. He walked up to Lily and her friends. He pretended to be nice. He said hello and asked to see the balloon.

Lily was surprised. She did not know Max wanted to play. She was kind and she gave him the balloon. She hoped he would like it.

But Max did not like it. He held the balloon and he poked it with the stick. The balloon popped with a loud bang. Lily and her friends screamed and jumped. Max laughed and ran away.

Lily was very sad. She liked her balloon and she wanted to play with it. She did not understand why Max did that. She felt angry and hurt. She cried and hugged her friends.

Max was not happy. He thought he would feel better after he popped the balloon. But he did not. He felt guilty and mean. He saw Lily crying and he felt sorry. He wished he did not poke the balloon. He wished he was nice.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She lived in a big, brown house. Every morning she would get dressed and go outside. She would explore and look for special things.

One day she went to the park. There were lots of trees and the grass was green. She saw something interesting on the ground. She bent down and saw it was a brown prize. She was so excited! She had found it all by herself.

The prize was a big, shining star. She looked at it and felt so happy. She quickly put it into her pocket, and ran back home.

When she got home she showed her mum the prize. Her mum said 'Well done! You found a special prize. You can keep it forever.'

The little girl was so proud of her prize. She kept it safe in her room. She would look at it every day to remember how she found it. She loved her special brown prize.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tweetie. Tweetie was very graceful when she flew in the sky. She loved to sing and play with her bird friends.

One day, Tweetie's bird friend, Chirpy, came to her and said, "Hey Tweetie, let's go play a quiz game!" Tweetie was excited and said, "Yes, let's go!" 

Chirpy had a tricky quiz for Tweetie. She asked, "What is the thing that you use to poke things?" Tweetie thought for a moment and said, "Is it a stick?" Chirpy said, "No, it's something smaller." Tweetie thought again and said, "Is it a finger?" Chirpy said, "Yes, that's right!" 

Later that day, Tweetie was flying in the sky when she saw a big, juicy worm on the ground. She remembered the quiz and used her beak to poke the worm. She was so happy that she got the quiz right and found a yummy snack!

Once upon a time there were two friends, a smart bear and a clever rabbit. They decided to celebrate and have a fun time together. The bear said he had an idea. He grabbed some wooden rails and placed them on the ground. Then he asked the rabbit to grab onto the rails.

The bear then told the rabbit to slide all the way down the rail. The rabbit was hesitant at first, but the bear convinced him to give it a try.

The rabbit was a bit scared but he was an intelligent creature and he knew that the bear only wanted to give him a good time. So he followed his friend's lead and hopped onto the rails.

The bear smiled as he watched the rabbits slide down the rails. He cheered and the two of them celebrated together. They were so happy that they decided to do it once more and soon they were laughing and having a great time together.

Together the two of them celebrated and had a wonderful day.

Once upon a time, there was a cop. He was a very brave cop, but he had one problem - he was deaf.

But the cop wasn't too worried about that. He imagined he could leap tall buildings and catch robbers all by himself.

Every day, he set out wearing his police uniform. He looked around with his sharp eyes and listened carefully with his big ears. He searched for bad people who were breaking the rules.

When he found someone doing something wrong, he would stop them and tell them off. Then he would take them to the police station where they would get into trouble.

The brave cop was never afraid. He knew he could do it all, even though he was deaf.

Once upon a time, there was a wild smelly bear who liked to explore. He would travel for many days, sometimes even weeks, before he returned to his cozy cave in the forest. 

Every time he returned home, he was always excited to find something new. He often found strange places and things that made him happy. One day, he decided to travel farther than usual, away from his home, to discover something special.

As he roamed, the wild smelly bear found a delicious berry bush and decided to stay and eat some of the yummy fruit. After eating all of the berries, the bear was so full that he decided to take a nap in a sunny clearing.

When the bear woke up, it was dark outside and he realized it was time to return home. He ran and ran, until he eventually arrived back at his nice, cozy cave. The bear was so happy to be home, he smiled and curled up to take another nap. 

The end!

Once upon a time there was an ancient poppy. The poppy lived in a warm meadow and was very beautiful. One day, a small 3 year old girl and her mum walked into the meadow. The little girl saw the ancient poppy and went over to it. She bent down, and asked her mum what it was. "That is an ancient poppy," her mum said. 

The little girl wanted to pick it, but her mum said no. Then the ancient poppy began to speak. It said, "Please don't pick me little girl. I'm too old and fragile. I need to stay here in this meadow." The little girl was surprised, she didn't know a poppy could talk. 

The little girl and her mum listened to what the poppy said. So they decided to leave it where it was and keep walking. As they were walking away, they heard the ancient poppy say, "Thank you for understanding, little girl." The girl smiled, and waved goodbye to the ancient poppy.

Mama came into the kitchen with a tray of fresh berries. "Taste these," she said to her daughter, who was three.

The little girl's eyes sparkled. "They look so kind," she said.

Mama smiled. She put the tray in front of her daughter and picked up a berry. "Mmmm," Mama said. "It is yummy."

The little girl picked a berry and popped it in her mouth. She rolled it around and smiled. "It's sweet!" she said.

Mama smiled again. "Yes, that's because they're ripe."

The little girl looked up at Mama. "Can I have more? Please?"

Mama laughed. "Of course you can!" she said. She filled the little girl's plate with the sweet, juicy berries.

The little girl smiled and gobbled up the berries. They tasted so good!

Mama sat back and watched her little girl, happy that she had enjoyed her snack.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Mandy. She loved playing with her flag. Every morning, Mandy would run outside and play with her flag until she felt tired.

But no matter how loudly Mandy called, her flag could not be found. And so, Mandy went back home feeling very sad, never to find her flag.

Once upon a time, there was a family that loved to go to the park. One day the family piled into the car and drove to the park. 

When they arrived, the child was so excited. She ran around the park to explore. She started playing on the swing and the slide.

Suddenly, she noticed a broken tuna can lying on the ground. She asked her mom why the tuna was broken. Her mother said, "It must have been left here by someone playing here earlier." 

The child was worried. She didn't want to leave the park because she was scared it would still be there when she came back. She asked her mom, "Mom, can't we put the broken tuna in the trash?" 

Her mother said, "Yes we can, sweetheart. It's the right thing to do. Let's do it right away!" 

The family tidied up the park, and put the broken tuna in the trash. After that, the family had fun playing together in the park.

Once there was a little boy who liked to play. But one day he was naughty and did something bad. He decided to break a mirror. He looked at the dirty mirror and stomped his foot on it. It broke into lots of pieces. 

The little boy was very scared. He wished he hadn't broken the mirror. Suddenly a scary monster appeared in front of the boy. The monster made a big noise and scared the boy.
 
The monster said, "Now you must pay for breaking the mirror!" The boy was very sad and started to cry. He understood his mistake, but he was too scared to say sorry. 

The monster said, "You can either give me your toy or never play again!" The little boy was very scared, so he gave the monster his toy. 

The monster ran away and never came back. The little boy was very sad. He had to learn his lesson - never break a mirror!

Once there was a cute little puppy. His name was Jack. He was so adorable. Every day he would go out and play in the sunshine.

One day Jack was playing outside when he suddenly saw a hanger in the grass. He thought it looked like a great toy. So he jumped and tried to grab it. Suddenly he slipped and started to fall.

Jack tumbled and tumbled until he reached the bottom of the hill. He lay still for a moment. Then he lifted his head and shook the dirt off.

But Jack soon realized that he had lost his hanger. He looked around, but he couldn't find it anywhere. Jack began to feel sad. 

But then Jack remembered how his mom had always told him that if he ever lost something, she would help him find it. So Jack smiled and ran back up the hill.

Sure enough, Jack found his hanger! It was lying right where he had fallen. He was so happy that he could almost jump out of his fur!

He took the hanger back home and told his mom all about his adventure. She said he was so brave and hugged him tightly. 

Jack and his mom played with the hanger all afternoon. They laughed, spun it around and made funny shapes with it. It was an amazing day.

Lila was a smart girl who liked to help her mom in the kitchen. One day, her mom was making soup for lunch. She asked Lila to get a big pot from the cupboard.

Lila looked at the pots and picked one that was shiny and round. She tried to fit it on the stove, but it was too big. It covered two burners and stuck out over the edge. Lila said, "Oops, this pot is too big for the soup."

She put the big pot back and looked for another one. She saw a small pot that was blue and square. She tried to fit it on the stove, but it was too small. It only filled one burner and left a lot of space. Lila said, "Oh no, this pot is too small for the soup."

She put the small pot back and looked for another one. She found a medium pot that was red and oval. She tried to fit it on the stove, and it was just right. It filled one burner and had enough room for the soup. Lila said, "Yay, this pot is perfect for the soup."

She gave the pot to her mom, who smiled and said, "Thank you, Lila. You are a smart girl who knows how to fit pots on the stove. Now let's make some yummy soup together." Lila was happy and proud. She helped her mom chop some carrots and celery and add them to the pot. They stirred the soup and waited for it to boil. Then they enjoyed a delicious lunch of soup and bread. Lila said, "I love soup and I love helping you, mom." Her mom said, "I love you too, Lila. You are a great helper and a wonderful daughter." They hugged and smiled.

Once upon a time there was a mommy and her baby. Mommy wanted to keep the baby safe, so she taught the baby to not touch anything yellow. 

Mommy said, "Baby, please don't touch the yellow because it might be dangerous. It's better to be safe and prevent any harm."

But one day, the baby saw a yellow butterfly fluttering around. The butterfly was so pretty, and it looked harmless.

The baby asked, "Mommy, can I touch the butterfly?"

Mommy said, "Yes, you can, baby. That butterfly is harmless and won't hurt you. But remember, don't touch the yellow things that don't look harmless."

The baby nodded and smiled. From then on, the baby knew to be careful when it came to yellow.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to dance. She would move her body to the rhythm of the music and twirl around the room. One day, Lily's mom signed her up for a dance class.

At the class, Lily met a boy named Max. Max was having a difficult time learning the dance moves. "I can't do it," Max said sadly. "It's too hard."

Lily smiled and said, "Don't worry, Max. I'll help you. We can practice together." So, Lily and Max practiced the dance together and soon they were both doing it perfectly. They even got to use scissors to cut out paper shapes for their costumes. At the recital, Lily and Max danced beautifully to the rhythm of the music and everyone clapped and cheered.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She had curly hair and loved to explore. Every morning she would go out into her garden and find something new.

One day, while the girl was playing, she saw a big, juicy apple on the ground. She picked it up and wanted to eat it right away. But it was too big! So she ran into the kitchen and asked her mom, "Please can I have a piece of the apple?" Her mom smiled and cut the apple into pieces. The girl took a bite and it was so tasty!

The girl ate her apple and thought of other tasty treats she could make. She asked her mom, "Please, can I make some cookies?" Her mom said yes and the girl got to work. She gathered ingredients and mixed them together. Soon, delicious chocolate chip cookies were in the oven.

The girl smiled as she pulled the cookies out of the oven. They smelled so yummy and tasted even better. She shared them with her mom, who said they were the best cookies she had ever tried.

The little girl was so happy and proud of herself! From that day on she loved to explore her garden and make tasty treats.

Once there was a sister who loved to design things. She loved to draw pictures and build models with her toy blocks. One day, she decided to design the most delicious snack for her little brother. She gathered some of the most tasty ingredients and put them together.

When she finished, she proudly presented her tasty creation to her brother. He couldn't get enough of it! He was so delighted, he ran around the house happily showing it to everyone.

The sister was so pleased with how her snack turned out. No matter how much her brother ate, it seemed she could always design more delicious snacks. 

The end.

John was a three-year-old boy who was always looking for fun and adventure. One day, he was playing in the garden and found a nice apron. He ran over to it, and picked it up excitedly.

"Wow, this apron looks fun," he said to himself. 
He tried it on and spun around.

John then decided he wanted to keep it, but he didn't know how. Suddenly, he heard his father's voice from inside the house.

"John, is that you?" his father called out.

John nervously ran inside. He thought his father would be cross that he had taken the apron without asking.

"I found this apron in the garden," he said, feeling a bit scared.

But his father only smiled. "That's okay, you can keep it! It's available for you," he said.

John was so happy. He had found the perfect apron and his father had said he could keep it! He ran back outside, apron and all, ready to explore and have more adventures.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy was very hungry and wanted to eat something yummy. He asked his mom, "Can we bake some cookies, please?" His mom said, "Yes, we can bake some cookies."

While they were baking the cookies, Timmy's mom showed him a shield. She said, "This is a shield. It can protect you from harm." Timmy thought the shield was cool and wanted to play with it.

Finally, the cookies were done baking and they smelled delicious. Timmy and his mom took the cookies out of the oven and let them cool down. They ate the cookies and they were very tasty. Timmy was happy and full, and he felt safe knowing about the shield.

Once upon a time, there was a little figure. He was very small and he had no name. One day he decided to take a walk. As he was walking, he lay down on the ground.

Suddenly, a little boy came around the corner. He saw the figure lying on the ground and said, "Hello there! Who are you?" 

The figure said, "I don't have a name, but I'm looking for one. What's your name?" 

The little boy smiled. "My name is Max," he said. 

Max lay down next to the little figure and said, "We can be friends! Why don't I call you Little Figure?" 

The little figure was so excited! He jumped up and said, "I like that! From now on my name is Little Figure!" 

And so Little Figure and Max became best friends. They would always lay down together and tell stories. Little Figure was very happy to finally have a name.

Once upon a time, there was a friendly bear who lived in a beautiful landscape. He loved walking around and exploring the world. One day, when he was walking around, something strange happened. Suddenly, the bear vanished! He was gone!

The little bear was really scared, but he thought he would be okay. He looked around and eventually he saw a friendly bunny. He decided to ask the bunny where he was.

"Where am I?" he asked.

The bunny replied, "You are in the magical land of Dreamland! That's why you vanished."

The bear was so excited! He thanked the bunny and started exploring Dreamland. Everywhere he looked the landscape was so beautiful. He had so much fun and made so many new friends!

After many days of exploration, the little bear decided it was time to go home. He was sad to leave but he was happy he got to explore Dreamland. The friendly bunny gave him a big hug and waved goodbye as he vanished back home.

Once upon a time, there were two friends. One was named Jack and the other was named Jill. They liked to play sports together.

One day, Jack and Jill were playing tag outside. Jill was running away from Jack with a big smile on her face.

Jack yelled, "I'll never catch you!"

Jill just laughed and kept running around and around. But then she got tired and stopped to take a break.

Jack whispered to Jill, "It's ok. You can slow down. Play honestly."

Jill smiled, feeling relieved. She knew her friend was always looking out for her. They hugged and started to play tag again.

They had so much fun that they never stopped playing. And they became the best of friends.

Once upon a time, there were two best friends who lived in a small town. Their names were Jack and Sarah.

One day, Sarah asked Jack to explain why the town was so special. Jack thought carefully and then said, "The town is so powerful because it has the best people in it". 

Sarah looked around and nodded her head. She said, "Yes, the people of our town are so kind and helpful".

Jack smiled and said, "That's true. We're lucky to live here". 

Sarah smiled back and agreed. She said, "I'm so glad we're best friends". 

And they both agreed that they were more powerful together!

John was playing in the park with his friends. He saw a delicious looking cupcake in a nearby mug. He pointed at it and said, "I want that!". His friend Chloe said, "No, you can't eat that. It's not yours." 

John stood and looked angry. He folded his arms and said he wanted it. Chloe just shook her head. John started feeling frustrated and he kicked the ground.

John's mom saw the children from a distance and joined them. She asked what was happening and they told her. She looked at the delicious cupcake and smiled. 

Then she said, "I can give you something just as delicious, John. Then everyone will be happy." She bought John an ice cream cone and everyone enjoyed it.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sarah who was three years old. She was very curious and loved to explore new places.

One day, Sarah was playing in her kitchen when she came across a big, fancy dishwasher. She started pushing buttons and playing with all the gadgets.

Suddenly, the dishwasher started up and made a lot of noise. Sarah felt embarrassed and tried to hide.

Her mom heard the noise and came running into the kitchen. She said: "What are you doing Sarah?" Sarah looked up and said: "I was just playing with the dishwasher, Mama!"

Mama laughed and said: "Oh, Sarah! Be careful next time, the dishwasher can be dangerous!" 

Sarah nodded and said: "Okay Mama, I'll be careful!" With that, Sarah went back to her room to find something new to explore.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Sue. She was very tired and wanted to go to bed. So she went to her room and shut the door. Inside her room there was a bed that was brown. Sue hopped into bed and snuggled up close. She was so warm and cozy in her brown bed that she soon fell asleep!

John and his family were on vacation. They wanted to explore the sea, so they requested a dependable yacht. They were so excited! The yacht was big and brightly coloured. It was ready to sail on the waves.

John's dad was a captain, so he knew how to sail the yacht. He took everyone on a journey around the island. John and his siblings all had turns steering the yacht. Everyone was having fun!

At the end of the day, John's dad asked if everyone knew how to sail the yacht. Everyone nodded yes. They said good-bye to the dependable yacht and made plans for their next adventure.

Once there was a pup who was feeling very sick. His mom said he needed to see a veterinarian. So they set off on their way.

The veterinarian was so kind. He spoke to the pup in an gentle voice. He readied a big syringe filled with medicine. It looked harsh but the pup knew it was going to help him get better.

He had to take the medicine every day. Every morning and night the pup would take it. Slowly the pup started to feel better. After a few weeks the pup was completely better!

The pup was very happy and thanked the veterinarian for making him all better. The veterinarian said it was his pleasure.

Once there was a little girl named Sasha who loved to play in the garden of her house. Every day, Sasha would spot a lot of patterns on the ground; circles, diamonds and squares. There were stones of all colors: red, blue and green. One day, as she was exploring, she noticed a soft pattern with a stem in the middle that looked like a flower. She quickly decided to pick it.

Once upon a time, there was a little rabbit named Remy. Remy lived in a hole underground. He loved to play with his friends and eat carrots. One day, Remy saw a big, red ball. He thought it was a giant carrot. Remy was very foolish and wanted to eat it.

Remy tried to bite the ball, but it was very hard. He felt sad and didn't know what to do. He remembered his mom told him to pray when he needed help. So, Remy closed his eyes and prayed for help.

Suddenly, Remy's friend, a wise old owl, came to help him. The owl told Remy that the ball was not a carrot, but a toy. Remy felt happy and thanked the owl. From that day on, Remy and his friends played with the red ball and had lots of fun. And Remy never tried to eat a ball again.

Once upon a time, there was a lazy fox. He was so lazy, he didn't want to hunt for his own food. So one day, he decided to try and find a trap he could open and eat whatever was inside.

He searched and searched until he found one. He was so excited and he quickly opened it. Inside, he found some yummy food!

He was about to take a bite, when he heard a voice say, "I wouldn't do that if I were you!"

The fox looked up and saw a rabbit peering out of the trap. The fox said, "Oh, why not?"

The rabbit said, "Well, this is my trap, so you'd better leave my food alone."

The fox frowned and said, "But I'm so hungry and I'm so lazy, I don't want to go and get my own food!"

The rabbit laughed and said, "That's okay, I know how it feels. Let me help you. I'll teach you how to make your own traps, that way you'll never have to be hungry again!"

The fox was so thankful, he thanked the rabbit and promised he would never steal food again. They both stayed friends and the fox was forever grateful to the rabbit for helping him.

One day, there was a little boy who loved playing outside. He wanted to play in the sun all day long, but his mommy was worried. She wanted to keep him safe, so she warned him about the hot sun. 

The boy always obeyed his mommy so he listened to her warning. Instead of playing in the sun, he played in the shade. The little boy was sad that he couldn't play in the sun, but he liked playing in the shade too.

One day, his mommy found a big, noisy fan. She turned it on and it made a lot of wind. Then, she warned her son again to stand away from the fan. The little boy was scared of the fan, but he did as he was told.

The boy's mommy was very worried, so she turned off the fan and hugged the boy. She told him that she only wanted to keep him safe. The little boy smiled, happy that his mommy cared so much about him. He was happy to be safe and warm in his mommy's hug.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved cookies more than anything in the world. One day, Timmy's mom baked a big batch of cookies and gave him one to eat. Timmy was so happy and took a big bite of the cookie. 

After eating his cookie, Timmy started to feel tired. He went to his room and lay down on his bed. But he couldn't sleep because he still had some energy left. So, he decided to kick his ball around the room. 

Timmy kicked the ball so hard that it hit the wall and bounced back to him. He kicked it again and again until he was too tired to play anymore. Then he snuggled up with his favorite teddy bear and fell asleep, dreaming of cookies and kicking his ball. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a small girl. Her name was Daisy. Daisy liked to wander. One day, Daisy decided to wander away from her house. She wanted to see what was beyond her garden. She began to wander down a nearby path until she saw a tiny house. It was so small, she thought it was a hut! Curious, Daisy went up to investigate.

When she got close, she realized it was the home of a little mouse. Daisy tiptoed around to the front of the mouse's home. Suddenly, a friendly little mouse came out. He greeted Daisy with a cheery hello! Daisy was so excited, she asked the mouse his name. He said his name was Tico.

Tico invited Daisy to explore around his house. Daisy was mesmerized by how small and cozy Tico's house was. Daisy and Tico became fast friends. They went on all kinds of adventures every day.

Whenever Daisy felt like wandering, she went to pay Tico a visit. The two friends would explore and chat until the sun went down. Daisy and Tico were the best of friends, and their happiness knew no bounds.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and sing songs. One day, Lily's mom asked her to help sign a letter. Lily didn't know how to sign, but her mom showed her how to write her name.

Later that day, Lily went to her friend's house to play. Her friend had a big curtain in her room. Lily thought it was so pretty. She asked her friend if she could play behind the curtain. Her friend said yes, and Lily had so much fun hiding and playing peek-a-boo.

But when Lily went home, she smelled something funny. It was her shoes! They were so smelly from playing outside. Lily's mom told her to take them off and put them outside to air out. Lily didn't like the smell, but she knew it was important to keep her shoes clean.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. He loved to step and jump all day. One day, he saw a big ashtray in the living room. He wanted to play with it, but his mom said, "No, Tim! That is not a toy."

Tim felt frustrated. He really wanted to play with the ashtray. So, when his mom went to the kitchen, he took the ashtray and started to play. But, oh no! The ashtray fell on the floor and broke into pieces.

His mom heard the noise and came back. She was not happy. "Tim, I told you not to play with the ashtray," she said. Tim felt sad and said, "I'm sorry, Mom." His mom hugged him and said, "It's okay, but you need to listen next time." Tim learned his lesson and never played with things that were not toys again.

Once upon a time there was a generous day that made everyone happy. Everyone loved to play in the sun, run around and smile. One day, all the fun seemed to vanish. No one could find it anywhere. All the kids were sad.

The generous day was confused and wanted to find the fun again. So, it thought and thought of what could have happened. Then, the day had an idea. It decided to make a rainbow.

The day mixed all the colors together in the sky and it worked! Soon the happy fun was back, and everyone was excited. The generous day smiled and even made an extra gift of sunshine. Everyone was happy and the fun stayed with them all day long.

Once upon a time, there was a happy little girl who loved to swim. She wanted to splish and splash in the water all the time. She'd put on her red bathing suit, grab her swim float and jump right in.

One day, the little girl went to the beach. She saw lots of other kids swimming and playing in the water. But one man caught her eye. He had a big mustache and a very lively personality.
 
The little girl looked back at the man, who smiled and waved. She quickly waved back. Then, she went into the water, ready to swim. 

She swam around for a little bit, until the man in the mustache came up to her and said, "Would you like to swim with me?" The little girl, excited to have a new swimming buddy, eagerly said yes.

Tom and Ann were humble kids who lived with their mom and dad in a small house. They liked to play with their toys and read books, but they also liked to help their parents with chores. One day, their mom asked them to number the ashtrays in the living room, because she wanted to clean them.

"What is number?" Tom asked.

"Number is when you say one, two, three, and so on," Ann explained. "You can use a crayon to write the number on the ashtray, like this." She showed him how to write a one on the first ashtray.

"Oh, I see," Tom said. "Can I do the next one?"

"Sure, you can do the second one," Ann said. "But be careful, the ashtrays are dirty and breakable."

Tom and Ann started to number the ashtrays, but they did not notice that their dad had left his cigarette on the sofa. The cigarette was still burning, and it slowly made a hole in the cushion. Smoke started to come out of the sofa, but Tom and Ann were too busy with the ashtrays to smell it.

"Look, I did the third one," Tom said proudly.

"Tom, Ann, what is that smell?" she asked. "Is something burning?"

They turned around and saw the smoke coming from the sofa. They gasped and ran to the sofa, but it was too late. The sofa was on fire, and the fire was spreading to the curtains.

"Mom, help!" they cried. "The sofa is on fire!"

Their mom grabbed a blanket and tried to put out the fire, but it was too big. She called the firemen, and they came with a big truck and a loud siren. They sprayed water on the fire, and they put it out. They also checked if Tom and Ann were okay.

"Are you hurt?" one of the firemen asked.

"No, we are not hurt," Tom and Ann said.

"But how did this happen?" the fireman asked.

Tom and Ann looked at each other, and then at the ashtrays. They saw the cigarette that their dad had left on the sofa. They felt very sorry and scared.

"We were numbering the ashtrays for mom," Tom said.

"And we did not see the cigarette," Ann said.

The fireman nodded and said, "I see. Well, you should never play with ashtrays or cigarettes, because they are very dangerous. They can start a fire, and a fire can hurt you and your house. Do you understand?"

"Yes, we understand," Tom and Ann said.

They hugged their mom and said, "We are sorry, mom. We did not mean to start a fire."

Their mom hugged them back and said, "I know, my loves. I'm glad you are safe. But you have to be more careful next time, okay?"

"Okay, mom," Tom and Ann said.

They learned a lesson that day, and they never played with ashtrays or cigarettes again. They also thanked the firemen for saving their house, and they gave them some cookies. The firemen smiled and said, "You are welcome, kids. You are very humble and brave."

Mummy was so proud of her and said, "You are so dependable. You make me very happy."

The daughter smiled and replied, "Thanks Mummy!" Then she kept playing with the puzzle. 

Mummy wanted to make sure her daughter had fun, so she said, "Do you need some help?"

The daughter shook her head and replied, "No, I can do it. I'm a dependable puzzle master!"

Mummy laughed and gave her daughter a hug. "You make me so proud. I love you."

The daughter smiled and replied, "I love you too, Mummy."

Once upon a time, there was a smart cat named Tom. Tom lived in a small house with his best friend, a little girl named Sue. One day, Sue had a big idea. She wanted to celebrate the night with Tom.

Sue said to Tom, "Let's have a fun night party!" Tom meowed happily, and they started to plan. They put up pretty lights and set out yummy food. They invited all their friends, like the dog, the bird, and the rabbit.

As the night began, everyone came to the party. They played fun games, ate good food, and danced to happy songs. Sue and Tom were so happy to celebrate the night with their friends. And when the night was over, they knew they had the best party ever.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who enjoyed creating things. One day, the little girl saw a file on the floor. She was curious and wanted to explore it. She picked up the file and opened it. Inside, she found a blank piece of paper. 

The little girl got excited and decided to get creative. She grabbed some crayons and set to work. She drew a picture of a big sun, a beautiful tree and some friendly animals. Eventually, she created a magical scene.

The little girl felt very calm. She knew that she had made something special. She put the crayons back and took the file with her. 

The little girl admired her creation and smiled. From that day on, every time she looked at her file, she felt calm. The little girl had created a magical masterpiece!

Once upon a time there were two friends, Mary and Tom. Every day they would meet up to talk and play. Today, Mary came over with an apple. She asked Tom if he wanted to have a bite. Tom was so happy! 

They both sat down and discussed the apple. Mary suggested they eat it slowly, so it would last longer. Tom agreed and he was careful not to bite too big a piece. Together they shared the apple and savored every bite. 

When they had finished, they discussed how delicious it was. Both Mary and Tom agreed they had never tasted something as yummy! They were so happy to have shared this special moment together. 

The two friends shared a big hug and both went home with happy hearts, until the next time they could meet.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play with numbers. They have cards with numbers on them. One day, they want to play a new game.

"Let's prepare a cake with numbers," Lily says.

"How do we do that?" Ben asks.

"We need a big paper, some crayons, and scissors. We can draw a cake and cut out numbers to put on it," Lily explains.

They find the things they need and start to work. They draw a big cake with orange frosting and sprinkles. They cut out numbers from one to ten. They have fun putting the numbers on the cake.

"Look, our cake is ready!" Lily says.

"It looks yummy!" Ben says.

They count the numbers on the cake. They have one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, and ten.

"Wait, we forgot something," Lily says.

"What did we forget?" Ben asks.

"We forgot zero. Zero is a number too," Lily says.

"Where can we put zero?" Ben asks.

"Let's put it on top of the cake. It can be a candle," Lily says.

They cut out a zero and stick it on the cake. They pretend to blow it out.

"Happy number cake day!" they say to each other.

They laugh and hug. They love their cake with numbers.

Ben was very excited. Today was his uncle's birthday party. He got dressed up in his best outfit and went to the park. The sun was shining bright and the trees were green and tall.

When he arrived, he saw his uncle holding a big, red balloon. He was very happy and gave him a big hug. 

"Help me stand it up!" his uncle said pointing to a big, white cake.

Ben carefully stood up the cake and then his uncle lit the candles. He was very careful with the fire. 

He gave Uncle a big hug and asked, "Can I have some cake?"

"Of course you can, but make sure that it isn't too hot or you might burn your tongue!" Uncle said. 

Ben waited a few minutes until the cake was not so hot and then carefully cut a piece for himself. It was delicious! He gave Uncle another big hug and they both enjoyed the delicious cake.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to draw pictures and sing songs. One day, she wanted to write a note to her mommy. She took out her crayons and paper, and started to draw a picture of a flower.

Her mommy came into the room and asked, "What are you doing, Lily?" Lily said, "I'm making a note for you!" Her mommy smiled and said, "That's so sweet, Lily. Can you read it to me?"

Lily looked at the note and said, "I put slow love in this picture for you, mommy." Her mommy hugged her and said, "Thank you, Lily. I love it so much." From that day on, Lily knew that putting slow love into everything she did was the best way to show her love for others.

Once upon a time, there was a tall lion. He lived in a big jungle with other animals. One day, the lion wanted to show off his strength.

He jumped as high as he could and then he landed on a tree. He thought he was very brave, but the tree broke!

The lion was not happy. He wanted to find something else to break and show how brave he was. But, he looked around and all he could find were other animals.

He couldn't break them, so the lion just sat down and smelled the flowers instead. The other animals were happy that the lion didn't break anything else.

Sam and Lily were friends who liked to play together. They had many toys and games, but their favorite thing was to make things with paper, glue, and scissors. They were very creative and made animals, flowers, and cars.

One day, a big storm came to their town. It was a hurricane, and it was very loud and scary. Sam and Lily's parents told them to stay inside and be safe. They were scared, but they also wanted to have fun.

They decided to unite their paper, glue, and scissors and make something new. They thought hard and came up with an idea. They made a big paper kite that looked like a dragon. They used many colors and shapes, and they gave it eyes, teeth, and wings.

They waited for the storm to pass, and then they went outside with their kite. The wind was still strong, but not scary. They ran and flew their kite in the sky. It looked like a real dragon, and they felt brave and happy.

They saw other kids who also wanted to play with kites. They invited them to join them, and they shared their paper, glue, and scissors. They made more kites of different shapes and sizes. They had a lot of fun and made new friends.

They learned that even when things are bad, they can be creative and unite with others. They also learned that kites are fun, and dragons are cool.

The bird was very tiny and weak. It sat on the ground, wishing it could soar in the sky like its friends. One day, it saw an umbrella lying on the ground. The bird saw this as the perfect opportunity to fulfill its dream, so it flew up to the umbrella and clung onto it.

The bird was so pleased and excited, as it started to soar in the sky with the umbrella. It flew higher and higher until it reached the clouds. The bird was so happy and it laughed and sang, as it travelled through the sky.

The bird looked down, and saw its friends looking up smiling at it. After some time, the bird decided that it was time to go back down, so it let go of the umbrella and glided back down to the ground. The bird was very tired but proud, that it was finally able to soar in the sky like its friends.

Once upon a time there was a girl who loved to swim. She wanted to go swim in the sea but it was too far away, so she decided to swim in the lake near her home. She was so excited!

When she reached the lake, the girl was amazed by the sparkly, still water. She put on her special swimsuit and jumped into the lake. She swam around for a long time, feeling the powerful strength of the water.

The girl decided to try something new and she began to stir the water with her hands and feet. She was amazed by what happened: the water formed into beautiful patterns! She continued stirring and it made her feel so excited and happy.

Once she was done, the girl felt very proud of herself. She had discovered a new way to enjoy the water and she felt so powerful.

The girl smiled and silently thanked the lake for such a wonderful experience. She then jumped back in and enjoyed her swim.

Once upon a time, in a faraway land, there lived two friends: Bill and Ben. They were always happy together and had lots of fun. 

One day, however, they had a quarrel. Bill did not want to play with Ben anymore and thought he was too annoying. This made Ben very sad and he started to cry.

High above the two friends, in the sky, a delicate cloud appeared. It was very white and fluffy and the sunbeams shone straight through. From up inside the cloud, it started to rain ever so gently. 

The gentle rainfall washed away all their quarrel and sadness. They smiled at each other and realised they could still be friends, no matter what. 

Then, they set off and had lots of fun together, just like they used to.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She loved to ride her pink bike in the park. One day, she saw a boy sitting on a bench with a book open on his lap. 

"Hi, what are you doing?" Lily asked.

"I'm reading a page from my book," the boy replied.

"Can I ride my bike around you?" Lily asked.

"Sure, go ahead!" the boy said.

Lily rode her bike around the boy and the page he was reading. She felt happy and free as she rode in circles around the bench. The boy smiled and watched her ride until she was ready to go home. From that day on, Lily would often ride her bike in the park and say hello to the boy reading his book.

Ben liked to play with his aeroplane. He made it fly in the air and zoom around the room. He was proud of his aeroplane. It was red and shiny and had a big wing.

One day, Ben invited his friend Tom to play with him. Tom came to Ben's house and saw the aeroplane. He wanted to play with it too. He asked Ben if he could hold it.

Ben said no. He did not want to share his aeroplane. He said it was his and only his. He did not care if Tom was his friend. He was mean and selfish.

Tom was sad and angry. He did not like Ben anymore. He decided to teach him a lesson. He waited until Ben was not looking and grabbed the aeroplane. He ran to the window and threw it out.

The aeroplane flew in the air and then crashed on the ground. It broke into pieces. Ben saw what Tom did and cried. He ran to the window and shouted at Tom. He said he hated him and never wanted to see him again.

Tom did not care. He was glad he broke the aeroplane. He said Ben deserved it for being a bad friend. He left Ben's house and never came back.

Ben was left alone with his broken aeroplane. He was sad and sorry. He wished he had shared his aeroplane with Tom. He wished he had been a good friend. He learned a hard lesson. He lost his aeroplane and his friend. He was not proud anymore. He was lonely and sad.

Once upon a time, there was a big and strong bear. He was very clever, but he was also very rude. Every day he would try to be nice to the other animals he met, but they usually didn't like him.

One day, the bear saw an elephant carrying a heavy load on her back. The bear wanted to help her so he started pushing from behind. The elephant was so happy!

The bear kept pushing the elephant for many miles. The weight of the load was getting bigger and bigger and the bear started to get tired. Suddenly, a lion appeared and threatened to eat the bear.

But the elephant was very smart. She quickly thought of a plan to prevent the lion from attacking. She growled loudly at the lion until it ran away.

The bear was so grateful! He thanked the elephant for saving him. From that day on, the bear was much more careful and tried to be less rude.

Sara loves her bird, Lila. Lila is yellow and sings very nice. Sara puts Lila in a birdcage every night, so she can sleep safe. The birdcage is high on a shelf, so the cat can not get it.

One day, Sara wants to play with Lila. She asks her mom to get the birdcage down. Her mom says, "Be careful, Sara. Don't let Lila fly away." Sara nods and takes the birdcage to the garden. She opens the door and puts her hand inside. Lila hops on her finger and chirps.

Sara smiles and talks to Lila. She says, "You are a good bird, Lila. I love you." She lets Lila sit on her shoulder and walk around. Lila likes the sun and the flowers. She flaps her wings and sings.

But then, Sara sees a big black bird in the sky. The bird is hungry and wants to eat Lila. The bird dives down and tries to grab Lila. Sara screams and runs. She tries to prevent the bird from getting Lila. She covers Lila with her hand and hugs her tight.

The bird misses and flies away. Sara is scared and sad. She says, "I'm sorry, Lila. I almost lost you." She kisses Lila and puts her back in the birdcage. She says, "You are safe now, Lila. I will never let you go." She takes the birdcage inside and puts it high on the shelf. She says, "Good night, Lila. I love you." Lila says, "I love you too, Sara." And they both sleep well.

Once upon a time there was a soldier who was in a big hurry. He had to do something very important, but he did not know what it was. He ran and ran until he came to a big, tall hill. At the top of the hill he saw a crazy lion. The soldier was scared so he ran away! He had to hurry to get away from the lion, so he ran faster than he had ever run before. Finally, he made it to safety and that made him feel very happy. The End.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She loved to rock. Everywhere she went she was rocking back and forth. She rocked on the swing and she rocked in her chair and she rocked all around the house.

One day, her mom and dad noticed how much she liked to rock. They decided to give her a very special reward. It was a brand new rocking chair, just for her. 

The girl was so excited when she saw the chair. She hopped right in and started rocking back and forth. She was so proud of her rocking chair.

Every day, she would rock until she got too tired. Then she'd sit back and smile. She was so happy to have her rocking chair that she never wanted to leave it.

The little girl rocked and rocked, until one day she became the best rocker ever. Her mom and dad were proud of her, and gave her a big hug and a special reward. It was a super-special toy truck, just for her. It was the best toy ever!

The little girl was so happy. She thanked her parents for the amazing rocking chair and for the special toy truck. From then on, she rocked her chair and played with her toy truck every day. She was the proudest rocker around.

Once upon a time, there were two brothers. They were the best of friends, but they were also very different.

One day they had a quarrel. They disagreed and wanted different things. One brother wanted something different than the other.

They kept arguing and got very angry. Finally the older brother had an idea. He suggested they have a round. They would each get a turn to make their case and explain why they thought their way was better.

The younger brother was excited by this. He loved having the chance to make his point. He told his brother all of his original ideas.

The brothers talked and talked, and when they were done, they agreed on a plan. This plan was not completely what either of them desired, but they were both happy with it. 

They hugged and made up, and were happy to be friends once again.

Once upon a time, there was a clever bunny. The bunny wanted to have a party with his friends. He invited all his animal friends to come to his party. The bunny made a cake and lots of treats for his friends.

At the party, the bunny and his friends played games and ate lots of yummy food. But then, something bad happened. A big storm came and separated the bunny and his friends. They all got scared and ran away.

The bunny was sad that his party didn't end well. But he knew that he would see his friends again soon.

Once upon a time, there was a man who wanted to build a restaurant. He wanted it to be very modern and fancy. He worked hard every day to make his dream come true. He used bricks, cement, and wood to build the walls and the roof of the restaurant. 

When the restaurant was finally finished, the man felt very proud. He invited all his friends and family to come and see his new restaurant. They were all very impressed with how modern and beautiful it looked. They sat down at the tables and ordered some yummy food. 

The man was very happy to see everyone enjoying themselves in his restaurant. He knew that he had worked hard to build it, but it was worth it because now he could share it with others. From that day on, the man's restaurant became very popular and people from all over the town came to eat there. The end.

Once upon a time, there were two friends, Jack and Jill. They were walking through the forest together when they saw something in the distance. It was an acorn! 

Jack said to Jill, â€œLook! An acorn! Letâ€™s go and get it!â€ 

The two friends ran towards the acorn, but then Jack stopped and said, â€œWait. That acorn is too far. We canâ€™t reach it.â€ 

Jill smiled and said, â€œDonâ€™t worry. I have an idea! We can ask the trees to help us.â€ 

So Jack and Jill closely watched the acorn tree. At first, nothing happened. But then, very slowly, the tree started to move closer and closer. 

Jack and Jill clapped and shouted for joy! The tree had showed them the acorn!

Once upon a time there was a boy called Jack. He loved to have fun. One day, he was feeling excited and wanted to explore. He put on his shoes and ran outside. He saw a big tube, and he wanted to go inside. So, he climbed in and started to zoom. 

The tube was long and dark, and the walls were rough. But Jack still wanted to go deeper. He zipped and zapped around the tube until he felt like he was going to burst with fun. 

Suddenly, a bright light came from one of the ends of the tube. He scooted and scurried, and soon he came out of the tube at the other end. It was a beautiful day with a big blue sky and birds singing. Jack was glad he had gone inside the tube, even though it was a bit rough. He smiled and ran around, feeling happy and free.

Once upon a time there were two children, Jack and Jill. They wanted to go to the camp so they asked their parents. But their parents said they were too young, so Jack and Jill decided to go on their own! 

Jack and Jill looked around the camp, they saw so many things they hadn't seen before - trees, flowers and animals. But they had to be careful. 

Jill picked up a rock and said, â€œI'm going to throw this rock!â€ 

Jack put his hand on her shoulder and said, â€œNo, no! You have to be careful!â€ 

Jill listened to Jack and put the rock down. After that they explored the camp and had a lot of fun!

Ben and Lily were twins who liked to celebrate their birthday. They always asked their mom and dad for waffles with syrup and whipped cream for breakfast. They loved waffles because they were sweet and fluffy and made them happy.

On their fifth birthday, they woke up early and ran to the kitchen. They saw a big pile of waffles on the table, with a candle on each one. They also saw many presents wrapped in colorful paper and ribbons. They were so excited that they hugged their mom and dad and said, "Thank you, thank you, thank you!"

Mom and dad smiled and said, "You're welcome, sweeties. We love you very much. Happy birthday!"

Ben and Lily blew out the candles and made a wish. They wished to be wealthy when they grew up, so they could buy more waffles and presents for themselves and their friends. They did not know what wealthy meant, but they heard it on TV and thought it sounded good.

They ate their waffles and opened their presents. They got new toys, books, clothes, and games. They played with them all day and had a lot of fun. They also shared some of their waffles with their dog, Spot, who wagged his tail and licked their faces.

They had a great birthday and felt very lucky. They did not know that they were already wealthy, because they had a loving family, a cozy home, and each other.

Once upon a time there was a happy boy. His name was Mike. One day Mike went to the park. He was so excited that he wanted to clap his hands. So he clapped and smiled.

While Mike was clapping, he noticed something shiny in the distance. It was a lamppost! It was so tall and had a wide base. Mike wanted to touch the lamp, but he was too small to reach it.

Mike wanted to get closer to the lamp, so he ran around it. When he did, the lamp lit up the sky! The bright light made Mike want to clap his hands again. He clapped until his hands were big and red.

Mike was very happy. He ran to show his mom the beautiful lamp. When she saw it, she smiled and clapped for Mike. Mike was so proud. He was happy to have found such a wide and wonderful lamp.

Once upon a time there was a boy named Ben. He was three years old and liked to explore his garden. One day, Ben found a rose. It was a beautiful green rose. He was so excited he gave the rose a big hug.

Ben's mum saw him and asked, "What are you hugging?"

Ben smiled and said, "It's a rose. A green rose. And I like it!"

Mum smiled too. "That's lovely, Ben. Would you like to put it in a vase so we can always remember how wonderful it is?"

Ben beamed and said, "Yes, please!"

So Mum put the rose in a vase and Ben kept it on the windowsill to see every day. He remembered how lovely it was to give it a big hug and smiled whenever he saw it.

The mommy was getting ready to go outside. She put on her dress and shoes.

"Mama," said the three year old, "I want to dress too so I can come outside with you!" 

"That's a great idea!" said Mama. "Let's go to your room and find something for you to wear."

The three year old picked out a bright yellow dress that she liked. She quickly got dressed and put on some shoes. 

"Do you want to go for a jog with me?" Mama asked. 

The three year old thought about it for a moment and then smiled. "Yes! Let's go for a jog!"

Mama was impressed by her intelligent decision. She took the girl's hand in hers and they began running together. 

They jogged around the block, laughing and talking the entire way. After a while, the 3 year old got tired and they stopped to walk. 

"That was a lot of fun!" she said, and Mama agreed. 

The three year old was very happy with her intelligent choice to go for a jog with Mama. She knew she would never forget this special morning.

Amy was feeling very ashamed. She had a big band she needed to mail to her friend. But Amy did not know how to mail it. She asked her mother for help, but her mother was too busy.

So Amy asked her big brother Tim. He said yes and picked up the band. He grabbed some tape and started to mail it. 

Amy watched him carefully and when Tim was done, she thanked him. Tim said she was a big girl and was now able to mail things on her own. 

Amy was very happy. She was not ashamed anymore and was proud of herself.

Once upon a time, there was a brave soldier who was very competitive. He wanted to be the best of all the soldiers and show everyone that he had value. He trained hard and practiced every day to make himself stronger and faster.

Soon he was able to do more push-ups and run faster than anyone else. Everyone respected him and valued his skills. He was very proud of himself.

The other soldiers wanted to be like him, but no one could match his strength and speed. Everyone wanted to be like the brave soldier, but no one could ever beat him. He was competitive and his value was unmatched.

The end.

Little Jimmy was so excited. He had a new crystal to admire. He had never seen anything so beautiful before. He had been waiting all day to see it. Finally, his dad opened the box and Jimmy's face lit up.

He held the crystal up to the light and watched as the light shone through it. Little Jimmy grinned from ear to ear. The bright colors and sparkles delighted him.

Jimmy's dad explained that the crystal was very special and deserved to be treated with care. Jimmy was proud that his dad thought so much of him that he trusted him with this special crystal.

Jimmy ran around the room with the crystal in his arms, admiring it from all angles. As the hours passed, Jimmy's eyes started to get heavy, and he had to put it down and go to bed. 

Before he went to sleep, Jimmy held the crystal one last time and gave it a big kiss. With the crystal in his arms, Jimmy closed his eyes and fell asleep with a big content smile on his face.

Once upon a time there was a bird named Max. He loved being able to soar through the sky. One day however, Max felt helpless when his wing was injured. He couldn't fly anymore and he was stuck on the ground. 

Max's friends noticed this, so they came over to help. "Don't worry, Max," they said. They set up a nest for him and brought him things to eat.

Max was so happy he began to settle in. He was grateful for his friends' help. He felt safer in his nest and didn't feel so helpless anymore.

One day Max had an idea. He asked his friends, "What if I set up a will? That way, if something happens to me, you can take care of my nest."

Max's friends thought this was a great idea. So Max wrote a will that his friends would follow after he was gone. He was so relieved to have this plan in place. 

Max's friends made sure to take care of him and the nest. With their help, Max was able to settle in to his new home peacefully.

Once upon a time, in a big, big world, there was a little blue bird. The bird was very cold and was looking for something that she could belong to. One day, she flew very high and spotted a warm, yellow house with a flexible roof. 

The bird flew down and tapped the roof. She called out â€˜Are you cold too? I am looking for a place to belong!â€™ Slowly, the roof of the house moved and opened up. Out popped a friendly little mouse. The mouse smiled and said â€˜Yes, I am cold too. Why donâ€™t you come inside and we can both be warm?â€™ 

The bird was very happy. She flew down and came inside. It was warm and cozy in the house. The bird and the mouse cuddled up close and kept each other warm. They had a new friend and a place to belong. The flexible roof closed up and they were safe. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time there was a gifted boy. His name was Jack and he was three years old. He had a very special problem to solve.

One day, Jack said "I'm in trouble, what can I do?". His mom knew just what to do. She said to him, "I know! Let's mail something to Daddy".

Jack was very excited and went to get his favorite toy. He took it to the post office and asked the postman to mail it to his dad.

The postman was very kind. He said, "I'm sure your dad will love it". So Jack thanked him and smiled.

When Daddy received his package, he was delighted! He called Jack to thank him. Jack was so happy that he had been able to help his dad, even from far away. 

It was all thanks to the postman and Jack's quick thinking that the trouble was solved.

Once upon a time, Tom played alone. His heart felt so sad and he was very lonely. Every day he would sit in the same spot and watch the birds in the sky, until one day something different happened.

A beautiful girl suddenly appeared. She asked Tom, "Do you want to make music with me?" Tom was so surprised and nodded yes. The girl then handed him a stick, and started tapping the ground in a special rhythm.

Tom jumped in and followed the rhythm she made. He began tapping his own stick in the same way. As their rhythm danced through the air, something magical began to happen. The birds in the sky started swaying to their beat.

The girl smiled and let out a little laugh. She said, "That was so nice, thank you." Suddenly, a sour smell filled the air and a big cloud arrived! The girl quickly said goodbye and vanished.

Tom realized that the sour smell was a warning that something bad was coming. Whatever it was, the girl had not been permitted to stay, so she had to leave. But Tom felt happy, he now knew that the power to make beautiful music was inside of him and he was no longer alone.

Once upon a time, there was a hunter who went on a journey to find an impressive treasure. He packed his things and left home early in order to start his adventure.

On his way, the hunter noticed a shiny object in a meadow. He went closer and found out it was a big coin. He was very happy and said to himself, "Wow, this is impressive!" He polished the coin and put it in his pocket.

The hunter kept walking and eventually reached an old tree with a door. He knocked on the door and a gnome opened it. 

"Who are you?" the hunter asked. 

"I am a keeper of the impressive treasure," the gnome answered. "I will give it to you if you can solve my riddle."

The hunter was excited and thought, "This can be my lucky day". He tried to solve the riddle but it was too hard. After trying over and over again, the hunter finally got the answer right. 

The gnome was very impressed and gave the hunter the treasure. The hunter thanked the gnome and polished the treasure carefully before he left. He was so happy to have found such a wonderful treasure.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tom. Tom loved to play outside. One day, he found a big stick in the park. He picked it up and started to play with it. He was very happy.

Tom saw a small bird who was not healthy. The bird could not fly. Tom felt sad for the bird. He wanted to help the bird get better. Tom thought of using the stick to help the bird.

Tom put the stick near the bird. The bird used the stick to rest. Tom gave the bird some water and food. Soon, the bird got healthy and could fly again. The bird was very happy and so was Tom.

The moral of the story is to always help others when they need it.

John and his dad went for a walk in the woods. As they walked, Dad mentioned that a factory had opened up in the woods. John was excited about the factory and wanted to explore it. 

Dad warned him that it would be dangerous to explore the factory. But John said he was brave and wanted to go anyway.

Eventually, Dad reluctantly agreed to take John to the factory. As they walked, Dad reminded John to stay close, as it was a dangerous place. 

As they made their way to the factory, they were surprised to find it full of smoke. Dad noticed how dangerous the smoke was and quickly grabbed John to take him away. Then they heard a loud explosion. 

The factory had blown up, and the explosion left a large crater in the woods. Dad and John were safe, but the factory was destroyed.

Once there was a little car. It was a bright red car. It liked to zoom around the village. One day, the car went into the forest. Suddenly, it found a puddle. It was a puddle of oil, and it was very dirty.

The car said to the oil, "Oh no! What happened to you? You are so dirty!"

The oil said, "I am just so sad. I want to be clean so I can zoom around like you, but I can't. Can you help me?"

The car smiled and said, "Of course I can help you! I'll take you to the car wash and then you will be clean and happy. Ready to go?"

The oil said, "Yes! Let's go!"

So off they zoomed to the car wash. When the car and the oil got there, the car wash was filled with soapy bubbles and loud noises. But soon enough, the car wash was done and the oil was clean.

The oil was so happy! "Thank you so much!" the oil said. "Now I can finally zoom around like you!"

And so the car and the oil zoomed off, together, into the sunset.

Ralph was a cute little monkey. He was three and always running around. One day, his mum said, "Ralph, I need you to go to the store and buy me a big piece of cardboard."

Surprised, Ralph looked at his mum. "Why, mum?" he asked.

His mum smiled. "You'll see," she replied.

Ralph went to the store and got the cardboard. When he came back, his mum told him to take it out to the backyard. There, she helped him to make a fort out of the cardboard.

When he was done, Ralph asked, "What are we gonna do with it?"

His mum smiled and said, "Why don't you reverse into it and hide? I'll be able to find you, but it'll be fun to try!"

Giggling, Ralph did what his mum said and, soon enough, he was playing a game of hide and seek. He felt like he was inside a secret cave and was so happy.

Once there was a little girl. She loved to play outside with her scooter. Every day she would pick it up and ride around the yard. She liked to pretend she was a big racer.

But one day, something happened. When the little girl was riding her scooter, she heard a scary noise! She was scared, but she kept going. Then she saw something even more scary - a big monster!

The little girl was so scared she dropped her scooter and ran away as fast as she could. She ran all the way home and she never picked up the scooter again. She was too scared to go back.

But the really amazing thing happened later that day. The monster was gone. In its place was a kind old lady! She gave the little girl a big hug and said, "Don't be scared. You can pick up your scooter anytime you want."

The little girl smiled and thanked the old lady. From then on, she was no longer scared to ride her scooter. She picked it up and went riding every day!

Once there was a girl named Sue who loved to help others. She was always very compassionate and understanding. One day Sue was walking by a store and she noticed a label lying on the ground. She bent down and picked it up, but her foot slipped on the wet ground and she fell! Sue was left lying there with the wet label in her hand.

The store owner saw what happened and came out to help. He was very compassionate and called an ambulance for Sue. The ambulance came and took her to the hospital where she felt better soon.

The store owner told Sue that the label she slipped on must have come off his shop window. He thanked her for picking it up and gave her a new label to put back in its place. Sue thanked the store owner and happily went on her way.

The sun was gloomy and it made the day seem so still.

Bob wanted to go outside and play, so he pushed open the door and ran out.

Everything seemed so big and exciting. He saw huge trees and colourful flowers. But then he noticed that the playground wasn't open yet.

Bob was sad and he didn't want to go back inside. But his mom told him he had to wait.

Bob sighed and crossed his arms. He knew he had to wait before he could play.

So he waited and waited, watching the sun until it was time to go in. 

But just before he went inside, he saw the playground open. He smiled and pushed open the gate and ran inside, ready to have fun.

Once upon a time there was a panda who was very rich. She had lots of money and a nice big home to live in. But she was feeling sad. She was lonely and sad because she was living all by herself.

One day, while she was sad and alone, a kind bear came to her home. He wanted to help the panda, and said that he would protect her and keep her safe. He spent all of his time playing with her and helping her feel better.

They became good friends and the bear kept coming back every day. He always made sure the panda was happy and safe. Every night, he slept near the panda and kept her safe from all the scary things.

They eventually became very close and the panda was no longer lonely or sad. She never had to worry about anything because she knew her bear friend was always there to protect her.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Sam. Sam was a good boy, but sometimes he didn't always behave. He would whine and throw things and make mom and dad mad. Sam learned how to behave with his bow and arrow, and now it's one of his favorite things to do! Every time he plays with it, he always remembers to be careful and act responsibly. 

That's the story of how Sam learned to behave with his new bow and arrow!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Bree. She had bright eyes, brown hair and loved to explore.

One day, she decided to go on an adventure to the forest. When she arrived, she saw a mysterious cave. She walked in and saw something amazing.

Inside, she saw a big pile of gray powder. She felt the powder with her fingers and it was very soft. She wanted to show it to someone so she ran home to tell her mom.

Tom and Mia like to play with their toys in the sun. The sun is warm and bright. It makes their toys shine. Tom has a file. He likes to file his cars and trucks. Mia has a doll. She likes to brush her doll's hair.

The sun does not shine on them anymore. It hides behind a cloud. The file breaks. The doll's hair falls off. Tom and Mia cry. They have no fun. They have a bad day.

Once upon a time, there was a modest sack. It was small and plain, and belonged to a 3-year-old child called Tim.

Tim liked the sack very much, so he decided to carry it around wherever he went. Every morning he would reach for it, and repeat the same words; "My lovely sack".

It began to get a bit old, so he decided to give it a makeover. He used special colours and decorated it with ribbons, so it became very bright and sparkly.

Once he was done, Tim held the bright sack and repeated the same phrase, "My lovely, special sack".

From then on, Tim would carry his unique sack around with him, wherever he went. He was so proud of it, and he would repeat the same words over and over again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had an ugly doll that she loved very much. One day, Lily wanted to take her doll for a walk, but she couldn't find her shoes. Her mommy came to help her and tied her shoes for her. 

As they were walking, they saw a big building with lots of books inside. Lily's mommy told her that it was a library and they could borrow a novel to read at home. Lily was very excited and picked a book with a princess on the cover. 

When they got home, Lily sat down to read her novel while her mommy made dinner. She hugged her ugly doll tightly and felt very happy. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a doggy who lived in a house with his family. The doggy was very happy and loved to play with his family. One day, he was given a thick bone. The doggy was very excited. He wanted to show the bone to his family, so he picked it up with his mouth and bit it. But he bit it too hard. His teeth went right through it. Now he had no bone!

The doggy was very sad. He went outside to see if he could find another bone. He ran around and around until he found another bone. It was not as thick as before, but the doggy was excited. He grabbed the bone and put it in his mouth. He bit it, and it broke too. Now he had no bone again.

The doggy was very frustrated and this time, he was angry too. He looked all around for a bone, but every bone he found was too thin and he had to leave it behind. Eventually, he got tired and went back home. When he arrived, he was sad because he had no bone to show his family. He would have to go without a bone. 

The bad ending of the doggy's story teaches us that sometimes even if we try, we don't always get what we want. It can be sad, but remember: it's okay to not always get what you want!

On Tuesday, Jack and his mom went outside to play. Jack loved playing with mom. Suddenly, Jack saw a harsh man with a deep voice. He was shouting at the birds. Jack was scared.

Jack's mom smiled and said, "Let's go say hi to the man!". Jack wasn't sure. He said, "No mom, he looks mean." 

But mom just kept walking. When they got closer, Jack saw the man had a mean face. He shouted, "Go away!" 

Jack was scared. He grabbed onto his mom's hand and cried. Mom was angry and picked Jack up. She took him home and said, "You're not allowed to go outside anymore!"

Jack was sad. He had wanted so much to play with his mom. But now he couldn't because of the harsh man. He knew now that he must always be careful when exploring the world.

Tom and Lily were playing in the park. They liked to find twigs and make things with them. Tom made a sword and Lily made a crown. They were having fun.

Then they saw a big twig on the ground. It was long and thick and had many branches. It was unique. They both wanted it.

"Look, a big twig!" Tom said. "I want it for my sword!"

"No, I want it for my crown!" Lily said. "It is pretty!"

They ran to the twig and grabbed it. They pulled and pulled. They did not want to share.

"Let go!" Tom said.

"No, you let go!" Lily said.

They were angry and sad. They did not play anymore.

Then they heard a voice. It was their friend Ben. He was walking his dog.

"Hi, Tom and Lily!" Ben said. "What are you doing?"

"We are fighting!" Tom said.

"We want this twig!" Lily said.

Ben looked at the twig. He had an idea.

"Why don't you share the twig?" Ben said. "You can both use it for your things. It has enough branches for a sword and a crown. And you can play together."

Tom and Lily thought about it. They liked Ben's idea. They let go of the twig.

"Okay, let's share the twig!" Tom said.

"Yes, let's share the twig!" Lily said.

They smiled and hugged. They thanked Ben. They used the twig for their sword and their crown. They played together. They were happy.

Ben and Mia were playing with their new water guns in the backyard. They had a lot of fun spraying each other and running around. But then Ben noticed that his water gun had a leak. Water was dripping from a small hole near the trigger.

"Hey, Mia, look! My water gun is broken!" Ben said, showing her the leak.

"That's too bad, Ben. Do you want to use mine?" Mia asked, holding out her water gun.

"No, I don't want yours. I want mine!" Ben said, refusing to take Mia's water gun. He was very impatient and wanted to fix his water gun right away.

"OK, then. I'll go play by myself." Mia said, shrugging. She ran to the other side of the backyard and started spraying the flowers and the grass.

Ben tried to cover the leak with his finger, but it didn't work. He tried to tape the hole, but it didn't stick. He tried to glue the hole, but it didn't dry. He was getting very frustrated and angry. He threw his water gun on the ground and stomped on it.

"Stupid water gun! I hate you!" Ben yelled.

But then he heard a loud hiss and a splash. He looked down and saw that his water gun had exploded. Water was everywhere, and so was glue and tape and plastic. Ben was soaked and sticky and dirty. He started to cry.

"Mia, Mia, help me!" Ben called, hoping that Mia would come and comfort him.

But Mia didn't come. She was too busy playing with her water gun, which worked perfectly. She didn't hear Ben's cries, and she didn't care. She was happy and didn't want to share.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Ben. Ben lived in a small, open nest on top of a post. Every day, Ben would fly around and play with his friends in the park.

One day, Ben saw a big, dark cloud in the sky. It started to rain. All of Ben's friends flew away to find shelter. But Ben decided to remain in his open nest on the post.

The rain poured down, but Ben stayed in his nest. As the rain stopped, the sun came out. Ben's friends returned to the post to play. They saw that Ben was safe and dry. Ben was happy he remained in his nest.

Once there was a fisherman who wanted to go fishing. He got into his boat and sailed away on the open water.

The fisherman was very busy. He put his net in the water and then pulled it back up slowly. There were lots of fish in his net! He smiled and was very happy.
