When the fisherman got home, he opened his net and saw a lot of different fish. He was so excited! He did a happy dance and celebrated his great catch.

The fisherman was so pleased. Fishing was his favorite thing to do, and now he had the best catch ever!

Tim and Sam are brothers. They live in a big house with Mom and Dad. They like to play with cars and balls and books. One day, they are playing in their room when they hear a loud noise. The floor starts to shake and the walls start to crack. They are scared.

"Mom! Dad! What is happening?" Tim shouts.

"It's an earthquake, boys! Come here, quick!" Mom calls from the living room. She is holding a flashlight and a backpack. Dad is holding the door open.

Tim and Sam run to Mom and Dad. They hug them tight. They feel the house move and hear things fall and break. They hope their toys are okay.

"Let's go outside, it's safer there," Dad says. He leads them to the car. They see other people running and screaming. They see smoke and fire and dust. They see some houses that are broken and some that are gone. They are sad.

"Look, there's our school," Sam says. He points to a big building. It has a big hole in the wall and some windows are gone. He sees some kids and teachers outside. They look scared and hurt. He sees some that are not moving. He thinks they are dead. He feels sorry for them.

"Are they going to be okay?" he asks Mom.

"I don't know, honey. I hope so. But some of them might not. Earthquakes are very bad. They can hurt a lot of people and things," Mom says. She wipes a tear from her eye.

"Can we help them?" Tim asks.

"Maybe later, when the earthquake is over. Right now, we have to go somewhere safe. We have to watch out for each other. We have to be brave and strong," Dad says. He starts the car and drives away. He looks for a place where they can stay until the earthquake is over. He hopes it will be soon. He hopes they will be okay. He hopes their house and their toys will be okay. He hopes their friends and their school will be okay. He hopes the earthquake will stop. He hopes.

Deeva was a very happy 3 year old girl who loved to go on adventures. Today she decided to go for a walk in the park. As she was skipping and singing, she stumbled on a pretty label that someone had dropped. She was very glad to see it!

Once upon a time there was a brave boy named Max. He was always obedient and never spoiled. One day, Max went outside to play in the sun. He saw a great big puddle, with water that shined like a diamond.

Max ran to the puddle with a smile on his face. He wanted to jump in, but his mom yelled at him to stop.

Once upon a time, there was a girl who was very attractive. Her name was Sally. One day, she stumbled while walking in the park. She was very surprised and stopped to take a look at what she stumbled on. It was a big, juicy juicy apple. She smiled and picked it up.

One day, a little girl named Mia went to the gym with her mom. The gym was big and had many things to play with. Mia saw a fancy dress hanging on the wall. She wanted to try it on and play.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a toy car that she loved to play with. One day, Lily's toy car was broken. She looked at it and said, "Oh no! My car is broken. I want it to be fixed."

Once upon a time, there was a nice white rabbit. He had a kind heart and liked to play in the garden. One day, he went for a walk and found an apple tree. He looked up and noticed a big, red apple high in the tree.

He jumped and tried to grab the apple but he couldn't reach it. He was feeling sad when the tree began to speak.

"Hello! Can I help you?" said the tree.

The rabbit said, "Yes, can you help me get the red apple?"

The tree said, "Yes, I can help you. Close your eyes and make a wish."

The rabbit closed its eyes and wished. Suddenly, a big, kind fairy appeared. She was wearing a white dress and had big, beautiful wings.

The fairy said, "Hello, little bunny. I am here to help you. I will get you the red apple."

She waved her wand and the red apple appeared in the rabbit's paws. The rabbit thanked the fairy and hopped away with the red apple.

Peter was a 3-year-old boy. He loved exploring the woods near his house. One day, he went for a walk with his Mommy. As they walked, Peter could hear a mysterious voice. He asked his Mommy what it was.

Ben and Lily were playing in the park with their ball. They liked to kick the ball to each other and run after it. Sometimes the ball went too far and they had to chase it.

One time, the ball rolled into the street. Ben ran after it without looking. He did not see the big car coming fast. Lily saw the car and shouted, "Ben, stop! Car!"

But Ben did not hear her. He reached the ball and picked it up. The car was very close. It honked loudly. Ben was scared. He dropped the ball and tried to run back. But he was too late. The car hit him and he fell down.

Lily screamed. She ran to Ben and saw blood on his head. He was not moving. She cried and hugged him. She wanted him to wake up.

The car stopped and the driver got out. He was sorry and scared too. He called for help on his phone. He said, "Please, come quickly. I hit a boy. He needs a hospital."

Soon, a big truck with a red cross and a loud siren came. It was an ambulance. Two people in white clothes got out. They had a stretcher and a bag. They put Ben on the stretcher and put a bandage on his head. They put him in the truck and told Lily to come with them. They said, "Don't worry. We will take him to the hospital. He will be okay."

Lily got in the truck and held Ben's hand. She hoped he would open his eyes and talk to her. She was sad and scared.

The ambulance drove fast to the hospital. It was a big building with many windows and doors. It was not empty. There were many people inside. Some were sick and some were helping.

The people in white clothes took Ben to a room. They put him on a bed and hooked him to some machines. They said they had to do some tests and fix his head. They told Lily to wait outside. They said, "We will rescue him. He is brave and strong."

Lily waited outside. She prayed for Ben. She wanted him to be well and play with her again. She missed him.

After a long time, one of the people in white clothes came out. He smiled and said, "Lily, I have good news. Ben is awake. He is doing better. He wants to see you."

Lily was happy. She ran to the room and saw Ben on the bed. He had a big bandage on his head, but he was smiling. He said, "Lily, I'm sorry. I was silly. I should have listened to you. Thank you for being my friend."

Lily hugged him and said, "Ben, I'm sorry too. I was scared. I'm glad you are okay. You are my best friend."

They smiled and held hands. They were happy. They had rescued each other.

John and his mommy were going to the park. As soon as they opened the park gate, John started jumping up and down in excitement! He looked around and everything was orange. There were orange trees, orange leaves, and even orange birds in the sky.

John noticed his mommy was smiling and asked, "Mommy, why are you so excited?"

Mommy smiled and said, "Because this is the most amazing world! Everywhere you look, you can see something new and exciting. Let's explore and find out what's out there!"

John was so excited he ran off in one direction and his mommy in the other. Everywhere he looked John noticed something orange and exciting. He spotted an orange butterfly, orange flowers, and even a big orange balloon!

John and his mommy spent the whole day exploring the orange world, and were very happy when they got back home.

Katie loved to watch her owner's dog, Toby. Every day, Katie would sit and watch as Toby ran around and played in the garden. She would sometimes join in too, and Toby loved this.

Katie smiled and watched as Toby happily ran around with his new bone. She was very proud of Toby and thankful that she could enjoy watching him.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Lola. She was very happy, but she was also worried. She had a bad skin rash, and it made her feel sad.

Once upon a time, there were two bears. They were friends, but one day they started to fight. They growled and clawed at each other. It was very loud and scary. 

After a while, they stopped fighting and felt sad. They didn't want to be mad at each other anymore. So, they decided to go on a trail together. They walked and walked, and saw many trees and flowers. 

The bears found some berries, but they were sour. They made funny faces and laughed. They realized that it was better to be friends than to fight. From that day on, they went on many adventures together and never fought again. The end.

Once there was a group of friends who were playing in the park. They were very happy and enjoyed exploring the park together.

Once they were done, Jimmy and his friend played with the bubbles and splashed each other. They had a great time and laughed so much!

Jimmy loved inviting friends over for baths. He wouldn't trade it for anything else!

He went to the park to rest his knee and saw a little girl playing with her toys. "Hello there!" the man said. "What are you playing with?"

"I'm playing with my dolls," the little girl replied.

"That's great," said the man. "Do you want to see me perform a magic trick?"

"Yes, please!" the little girl exclaimed.

As she kept walking, she heard a noise up ahead. She went to investigate and saw a big bird. It was eating a pepper it had found in the garden. She asked it if she could have one too, but the bird said no. He had to save the rest for his friends.

The little girl kept walking until she saw a pond. It looked so dull and grey, she wanted to make it more fun. Suddenly, the bird flew by and said she could get the peppers to put in the pond. She thanked him and ran to get the peppers.

When she returned with the peppers, she threw them into the pond. The water sparkled and the fish seemed to like it too! Her mother had seen everything and smiled. She said the little girl was allowed to do these kind of things!

The little girl smiled and continued on her walk. She was so glad she was allowed to make the pond more fun.

Billy loved to decorate. He always gardened by his porch and created unique designs to put around it. 

One day, his mom wanted to decorate the porch too. She bought a big box of decorations, but they didn't look as good as what Billy had made. 

Billy was upset. He didn't want mommy to change his special decorations. He started to cry and threw the new decorations off the porch.

This made mommy very angry. She yelled at Billy and told him that he was being very naughty.

Billy was very sad now, as he didn't mean to make mommy angry. He decided to try and fix it. He took the decorations and put them back up, but this time he made a unique design with them. 

Mommy smiled when she saw the decorations. She was very proud of Billy and hugged him tight. From then on they would always work together to decorate the porch and make it even more beautiful.

Tommy was walking in the park and he observed a bird chirping up in a tree. He smiled and ran over to take a closer look. 

"Hello," said the little bird. "My name is Bella. What's yours?"

Tommy smiled and said, "My name is Tommy. I love birds!"

Bella smiled back. "I love people too! I can teach you some of my bird songs if you like."

Tommy laughed and said, "Yes please!"

So Bella sang her best songs while Tommy observed her closely. Then a little girl walked over. She was poor and had only a few birds perched on a stick.

"Where did you get these birds?" asked Tommy.

"I found them outside my house," said the little girl. "I found some eggs too, but there's not enough love coming from my home. So I wanted to make sure these birds found a good home. Would you like them?"

Tommy smiled and said, "I would love to give them a home. What do you think, Bella?"

Bella smiled and said, "I think that's a very kind thing for you to do. I'm sure these little birds will be happy with you."

So Tommy took the little birds home and he spent all day watching them, singing his songs and giving them lots of love.

Once upon a time, there was a poor man. He had no money to buy soup. So every night he would shrug, hungry and sad. He just couldn't seem to catch a break.

One day he heard there was a market far away where he could buy soup for cheap. He was so excited that he set off on a long journey.

He walked for many miles, but when he finally arrived at the market, he found out the soup was too expensive for him. He was so disappointed that he shrugged sadly and had to turn back home.

He never got any soup and he still had no money. He felt so helpless and poor that he had to shrug at the horrible ending.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the sunshine. One day, she went to the creek with her mommy. They saw a big, hairy spider crawling on a rock. They splashed and played in the creek until it was time to go home. Lily was happy because she got to spend time with her mommy and didn't have to think about the hairy spider anymore. The end.

Once there was a loyal cat who always wanted to go on adventures. The cat wished it could carry the most wonderful things around and explore the world.

The child smiled and said, "Alright, let's do it!"

So, the cat and the child packed up their things and headed off to the park. They carried books, toys, drinks, and snacks. Along the way, the cat showed the child all kinds of things and asked them to listen carefully and look closely.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy who liked to explore. He found a big stone and was very happy. He liked looking at the stone and touching it. He was so grateful to have found it.

The little boy was tired from playing, so he decided to relax next to the stone. He lay down and closed his eyes. The sun was shining brightly, and he felt very cozy beside the stone.

He relaxed and enjoyed the moment. Before long, he was in a deep sleep. When he woke up, the sun was setting. The little boy was so grateful that he was able to rest beside the stone.

He got up and looked at the stone once more. He said goodbye, thanked it and waved goodbye. He smiled and ran home, feeling fortunate and happy.

Sam and Dan were best friends. Every day they took the subway to go to the park to play together. But one day Dan ignored Sam. He acted like he didn't even know him. Sam was frustrated. Sam was sad and angry. He found a bench and sat there for a long time feeling alone. When it was time for Sam to go home, he got on the subway and looked for Dan. He wanted to forgive him, but Dan was nowhere to be seen.

Sam was frustrated when he couldn't find Dan, but he was determined to find him the next day. He promised himself that he wouldn't give up until they were friends again. 

The next day, Sam waited at the park for Dan. And sure enough, Dan showed up. When Dan saw Sam, he was happy to apologize for ignoring him. Sam was relieved and they both laughed and talked about their adventures.

The two friends weren't going to let anything come between them again. And now they make sure to meet at the park every day.

Once upon a time, there was a happy little girl. She loved to play in the park all day. One day, she was playing in the park and she dropped her favourite toy. She looked around, but she could not find it. She was so sad, because she had lost her toy.

Once upon a time, there was a family with two children. The brother and sister were both very cheerful. One day, the two were playing in the living room when the brother decided to remove the vase from the table.

The sister stopped him and said, "No! We should leave the vase alone. It's mommy's special vase."

But the brother insisted and removed the vase from the table. Unexpectedly, the vase shattered and broke into pieces.

The mother was very kind and understanding. She said, "It's okay. I'm just happy that you two are safe. That vase can be replaced, but you two can never be."

One day, Anna saw a red balloon. It was tied to a tree and Anna wanted to buy it. She only had a few coins but she decided to sell her language to get the balloon.

Anna was so happy; she thought she had special powers. She took the red balloon, thanked the tree and ran home. She had fun playing with the balloon, even though it didn't last long. 

Anna was sad when it eventually popped, but at least she had sold her language. The money she got from selling her language was enough to buy a bigger and better balloon the next time around.

Once upon a time there was a little bunny named Ben. Ben loved to hop around and explore the world. One day Ben decided to go on an adventure and he hopped off into the sunny meadow.

He hopped around and suddenly felt the ground move beneath his feet. Ben looked down and he was standing on a trampoline! He jumped up and down so that he could feel the springs bouncing him back up. He laughed and laughed as he jumped and jumped. 

Ben was so busy jumping that he didn't realise he was getting tired! Suddenly, he hopped back through the hedge, feeling safe, and made his way back home to his bunny hole, ready for a nap.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Frank. Frank was only three years old and wanted to explore the world. One day, he came upon a big swamp. The swamp was strange and gray. Frank was scared to venture in, but he was very curious. He asked his mom, "Mommy, can I go into the swamp?"

His mom smiled and said, "Let's go home now!"

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside with his friends. One day, they decided to go on an adventure to see a volcano. Timmy thought it sounded interesting.

As they walked, Timmy's friend asked him, "Do you like to jump and spring like a frog?" Timmy said, "Yes, I do! It's so much fun!" They laughed and continued on their journey.

Timmy was happy to have gone on this adventure with his friends. He learned that jumping and springing like a frog can make a long walk more fun, and that volcanoes can be very interesting to see.

Lila and Max were twins who liked to play outside. But today, it was raining hard and they had to stay inside. They felt bored and grumpy.

"Mom, can we go out?" Lila asked.

"No, sweetie, it's too wet and cold. You might get sick. Why don't you relax and read a book or draw a picture?" Mom said.

Lila and Max did not want to read or draw. They wanted to run and jump and splash in the puddles. They looked out the window and saw the rain falling and falling.

"Rain, rain, go away, come again another day!" they sang.

But the rain did not go away. It kept falling and falling.

Lila and Max sighed and lay down on the couch. They closed their eyes and tried to relax. But they still felt bored and grumpy.

Then, they heard a knock on the door. They opened their eyes and saw their friend Sam standing outside. He was holding a big umbrella and a bag.

"Hi, Lila and Max! Do you want to play with me?" Sam asked.

"What do you have in your bag, Sam?" Lila asked.

Sam smiled and opened his bag. He took out some books, some crayons, some stickers, and some cookies.

They laughed and talked and shared. They forgot about the rain and their boredom. They felt happy and relaxed.

Mom watched them from the kitchen and smiled. She was glad that Sam came to visit. He was a thoughtful friend and he made this rainy day more fun.

When it was time to go inside, Mommy asked, "Did you have fun swinging with the bottle, Jimmy?"

Once upon a time, there was a young boy named Timmy. He loved to go on adventures in the woods with his dog, Max. One day, they went on a walk and found a trail.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved chocolate more than anything in the world. One day, her mommy gave her a big, powerful chocolate bar. Lily was so happy that she ate it all up in one go!

Luckily, Lily's mommy heard her crying and came to help. She unlocked the door and hugged Lily. From that day on, Lily learned to be careful when she locked doors. And she never ate too much chocolate again! The end.

Once there was a loyal dog named Rosy. Every day Rosy would run around her backyard, enjoying the sunshine and the fresh air. She loved to explore and soon she had seen all of her backyard.

The ocean was so big, but Rosy was brave and loyal. She jumped and ran through the waves, feeling the spray in her face and the sun on her back. Lily and Ben were playing with marbles in the park. They had many marbles of different colors and sizes. They liked to roll them on the grass and see how far they went.

"Look, Lily, I have a big blue marble. It is very shiny and smooth," Ben said, holding his marble in his hand.

"I have a small red marble. It is very pretty and bright," Lily said, showing her marble to Ben.

They rolled their marbles together and laughed. They had fun.

But then, the sky became dark and cloudy. It started to rain. Lily and Ben ran to the bench under the tree. They did not want to get wet.

"Oh no, our marbles!" Lily cried. "They are still on the grass. We have to get them back."

"But it is raining. We will get wet too," Ben said. "And it is dark. We may not see them well."

Lily thought hard. She wanted to solve the problem. She had an idea.

"I know. We can use our jackets as bags. We can put them over our heads and run to the grass. We can pick up our marbles and put them in our jackets. Then we can run back to the bench. We will not get wet and we will not lose our marbles," she said.

"That is a good idea, Lily. You are very smart. Let's do it," Ben said.

They did what Lily said. They used their jackets as bags and ran to the grass. They picked up their marbles and put them in their jackets. Then they ran back to the bench. They did not get wet and they did not lose their marbles.

They were happy. They hugged each other and smiled.

"We did it, Lily. We solved the problem. We have our marbles back," Ben said.

"Yes, we did, Ben. We are a good team. We have fun with our marbles," Lily said.

They waited for the rain to stop. They played with their marbles on the bench. They had fun.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a brother named Max who was very slow. Max liked to walk slowly and take his time. One day, Lily and Max went to the park. Lily wanted to play on the swings, but Max wanted to walk around and look at the flowers. Lily wondered why Max was so slow, but she didn't say anything.

Once upon a time there was a kind man named Bob. Bob worked hard every day to help other people. 
One day, Bob was feeling very tired. He had been working for a long time and he needed a break. He lay down on a park bench and closed his eyes. 
He was just about to start dozing off when a little bird flew over to him. The bird had a long, rubbery neck and it blinked its eyes a few times. Bob smiled and said hello to the little bird. 
The bird chirped and bob felt a little bit better. He reached out his hand and the little bird hopped on. They stayed there for a while, Bob stroking the bird's feathers.

Bob had a kind heart, and the little bird knew it. With one more blink, the little bird thanked Bob and flew away.

After class, Miss Lily said, "Timmy, remember that being nervous is okay. But, you can always learn to be brave. I am proud of you." Timmy smiled and felt proud too. From that day on, Timmy was never too nervous to read in front of the class again.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Ben. He loved to listen to music. Whenever he heard a song, he would move and dance around.

"Can I play with your doll?" Tom asked Lily.

Lily gave Tom her doll and took his truck. She drove it around the grass and made honking sounds. Tom looked at the doll and smiled. He liked her hair. He pulled it hard.

"Ow!" the doll said. She had a voice box inside her. "That hurts!"

"I'm sorry, Lily. I didn't mean to," Tom said. He looked sorry too.

Lily hugged her doll and tried to fix her hair. She did not want to play with Tom anymore. She wanted to go home and keep her doll safe.

"Let's go, Mommy," Lily said. She walked to her mommy, who was sitting on a bench.

"Thank you, Lily. I won't do it again. I'm sorry," Tom said.

Lily and Tom hugged and said sorry. They decided to play with their own toys. They were still friends. Mommy and Tom's mommy smiled and said they were proud of them. Lily's doll was rare, but so was her friendship.

"Look, I made red and orange!" Sara said.

"I made yellow and green!" Ben said.

They moved their brushes to the middle of the paper. But then they saw a problem. They both wanted to paint blue and purple.

"No, I want to paint blue and purple!" Sara said.

"No, I want to paint blue and purple!" Ben said.

They both pushed their brushes to the same spot. The paints mixed and made a brown mess.

"Oh no, we ruined the rainbow!" Sara said.

"We can't complete it now!" Ben said.

They felt sad and angry. They put down their brushes and crossed their arms.

Just then, their mom came in. She saw the paper and the paints. She smiled and said, "What a beautiful rainbow! You two are so lucky to have each other. You can share and make anything together."

Sara and Ben looked at their mom. They looked at the paper. They saw that the brown mess was not so bad. It looked like a pot of gold at the end of the rainbow.

They smiled and said, "Thank you, mom. You are right. We are lucky to have each other. We can share and make anything together."

They hugged their mom and each other. They picked up their brushes and completed the rainbow. They were happy.

Once upon a time, there was a very fast onion named Gary. He was so fast, that he could even race the wind. He liked to brag about his speed to all of his friends. 

One day, Gary decided to challenge the wind to a race. He wanted to prove that he was even faster than the wind. So, he zoomed off without a thought! 

When Gary approached the wind his friends were worried. They shouted out to Gary to quit the race and come back, but Gary didn't listen. He wanted to prove that he was the fastest. 

The wind started to pick up and Gary was struggling to keep up. Soon enough, he was too tired to keep up with the wind and Gary had to quit the race. 

Poor Gary! All this excitement had been for nothing. 

Despite his failure, Gary's friends assured him that he was still the fastest onion that they ever knew.

Jimmy was sad it was over but he was also happy that he got to see the funny lightning. He was so glad he got to watch it with his mom.

Once upon a time, there was a bird. He had a big, soft wing. Every morning, he stretched out his wing and bowed. He bowed to the sun and said, "Good morning!".

One day, a new bird came to the park. The new bird had the same soft wing, so the old bird flew to him and bowed. The new bird bowed back and said, "Hello!".

The two birds became friends. Every morning, they flew together and bowed to the sun. They talked and sang in the sun, too. They were the happiest birds in the park!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a rag that she loved very much. One day, she was playing with her rag and it got stuck under the couch. She tried to reach it, but she couldn't. 

Lily's mommy came to help her. She asked Lily to pull the rag while she lifted the couch. Lily pulled and pulled, and finally the rag came out. She was so glad to have her rag back!

From that day on, Lily made sure to keep her rag in a safe place so it wouldn't get stuck again. And whenever she played with it, she made sure to pull it gently so it wouldn't get lost.

It was a beautiful day and Maria was playing with her friends. They were having so much fun playing together. Suddenly, Maria saw an ugly cut in her arm. She cried and asked "What happened?" Her friends said that it was dark outside and they should go inside. 

Maria was scared and she wanted to go home. Her friends said that if she stayed the cut will just disappear. Maria agreed but she was still afraid.

After a while, Maria's friends had to leave. Maria put a bandage on her cut and tried hard to ignore it. Soon it became dark and the cut started to hurt a lot. Maria wanted to go home, but her friends were gone and she didn't know what to do. All of a sudden, the cut started to disappear. Maria was relieved and decided to try to find her way home.

When Maria made it home, she quickly ran to the bathroom. But instead of the cut being gone, it had become bigger and uglier. Maria shouted for help but no one came. Her cut just kept getting bigger and bigger until it had completely taken over her arm. In the end, Maria disappeared forever and nobody ever saw her again.

Once upon a time there was a queen who loved to go for walks in the woods. One day she went for a walk and discovered a new path. With a big twist she turned onto the path and kept walking. She kept moving along until she came to a big surprise: a brand new castle! It was so shiny and pretty that the queen was very excited. 

The queen was so happy with her new discovery that she decided to move into the castle. She invited all her friends to come celebrate with her. Everyone had so much fun but the queen still wasn't done. She had a big twist up her sleeve: from then on she would be the queen of the new castle! 

All her friends were so happy that they decided to stay with the queen at the new castle forever. They all had so much fun together, playing new games, baking cakes and exploring the woods. And every time the queen thought about the twist that led her to the new castle, she was so grateful and thrilled with joy.

Once upon a time, there was a team of four friends. They were Tom, Tim, Kim, and Jim. They liked to play together every day. They would run, jump, and laugh in the park. They enjoyed being together and having fun.

One sunny day, they decided to have a picnic. They all brought yummy food to share. Tom brought apples, Tim brought sandwiches, Kim brought cookies, and Jim brought juice. They sat on a big blanket under a tree and enjoyed their yummy treats.

After they ate, they played games like tag and hide-and-seek. They laughed and had a great time. When the sun began to set, they said goodbye and went home. They knew they would enjoy more fun days together as a team.

Once upon a time, there was a sweet girl called Anna. She was so adorable!

One day, Anna went looking for a special place. She wanted to find a camp. She looked high and low, all around her home. But she couldn't find a camp.

So Anna asked her Mom and Dad for help. And they took her to a beautiful camp and Anna was so excited! She saw lots of new things, and even some furry animals.

At the camp, Anna also found some new friends to play with. She had so much fun with her new friends!

And finally, at the end of the day, Anna went back home. She had a wonderful time at the camp. Anna was so happy!

Once upon a time, there was a girl called Sally. She was three years old and was very confused.

One day, Sally was sitting in her bedroom and looked up at the ceiling. It was very high, and she couldn't understand why. Sally asked her mom why the ceiling was so high.

Her mom smiled and said, "That's just the way it is, dear. The ceiling is just part of the design of your room."

Sally was still confused, but was happy that she was able to sit in her room and look at the ceiling. She would sit in her room often and just stare at the high ceiling wondering why it was so far away. 

Sally would sometimes wave at the ceiling and say hello to it, but she always wondered why it seemed so far away.

Once there was a little boy named Ben. Ben liked shiny things, so when he saw a copper penny on the ground he ran over to get it. He liked the way the penny glinted in the sun.

But when Ben picked the penny up, he noticed a little ant underneath. The ant was trying hard to carry a small piece of food back to its nest. Ben knew the penny was too heavy for the ant, so he decided to help.

He knew the ant would not give up, so Ben insisted that he take the penny inside his house. He placed the penny in a special place in his room and promised to help the ant get its food back. He was determined and very persistent.

After several tries Ben was able to get the food to the ant's nest. The ant was very happy and thanked Ben for his kindness. Ben smiled and thanked the ant back. He was glad the ant was safe, and now he could keep the shiny copper penny that he found.

One hot day, Anna dreamt of having an ice cream. She wanted this so badly that she could feel it in her tummy. Her Mommy said that if Anna used her own money, then she could buy an ice cream. Anna was so excited! But the problem was, Anna had no money. She thought about what she could do and then she had an idea. She wanted to do some work so she could earn some money. 

Anna helped her Mommy clean the house; she swept, dusted and wiped things. After a few hours, she had enough money to buy an ice cream. She was so happy. When she saw the ice cream parlor, she felt a rush of wonder. There were so many flavors to choose from! 

But then, a gust of hot wind blew and the ice cream started to melt. Anna felt like she was struggling. She worked so hard and now her ice cream was melting away. She tried to take small bites but it was too hot. 

In the end, Anna decided to share the ice cream with her Mommy. They both enjoyed it a lot and Anna knew that she had learned an important lesson. She knew that struggle sometimes leads to wonderful things.

Lily liked to read books. She had many books in her room. Some books had pictures and some books had only words. Lily liked both kinds of books. But her favorite book was a novel. A novel was a big book with many words and a long story. Lily's novel was about a girl who went on an adventure with a dragon.

Every night, Lily read a part of her novel before she went to sleep. She wanted to know what would happen next. She liked the girl and the dragon. They were brave and smart and kind. They had many friends and enemies. They had to find a magic stone to save the world.

One night, Lily was reading the last part of her novel. She was very excited. The girl and the dragon had reached the place where the magic stone was hidden. But they also saw a big and bad dragon who wanted to take the stone for himself. The two dragons fought in the sky. The girl tried to help her dragon. Lily held her breath. She hoped the girl and the dragon would win.

Then, something amazing happened. The girl found a way to make the bad dragon fall. She used a rope and a stick and a rock. She was very clever. The bad dragon crashed to the ground. The girl and the dragon got the magic stone. They had saved the world. Lily was so happy. She clapped her hands. She cheered. She hugged her novel. She had read the best story ever.

Lily was also very tired. She had read a lot. She put her novel on her nightstand. She turned off the light. She snuggled in her bed. She closed her eyes. She dreamed of the girl and the dragon. She smiled. She was fit. She was ready for a new day. And a new book.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy who loved the summer. He loved to go outside and play in the warm sun. He often made cheerful toys with the sand, and he practiced singing and dancing for his friends.

One day, the little boy was playing in the park and he heard clapping. He looked to see where the sounds were coming from, and he saw a group of people sitting in a circle. They were smiling and clapping their hands. 

The little boy asked, "What are you doing?"

The people said, "We are applauding. That means we are showing our appreciation for something!"

The little boy smiled and joined in, clapping and cheering with the others. He was so happy that he clapped and laughed, enjoying the summer. 

The little boy had a great time clapping and laughing with the others, and he couldn't wait to tell his friends back home how much fun he had.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Mark. Mark was always looking for food to eat. One day, Mark heard about some hidden food. He wanted to find it so he started to look everywhere.

Mark sniffed the ground, but he still couldn't find anything. He looked inside the fridge, but no luck. Then, he dug in his garden and he was so happy when he found the hidden food. He quickly ate it all up!

Mark looked around his garden and smiled. He was so glad that he was able to find the hidden food. From then on, he always kept an eye out for more secret snacks.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who was very angry. Her name was Jessica and she had an orange lollipop that she wanted to eat. She held it in her hand but when she tried to bite it, a funny thing happened. The lollipop was really sharp and it hurt her teeth. 

Jessica started to cry because she was very sad. Her mommy heard the crying and came over to see what was wrong. Mommy asked Jessica to show her the lollipop. When Mommy saw the lollipop, she knew why it had felt sharp.

The lollipop was made of candy and it had been decorated with tiny rocks that were quite sharp. Mommy quickly threw away the lollipop and gave Jessica a new and special treat. She gave Jessica a big and soft lollipop that was so yummy!

Jessica was so happy. She said thank you to Mommy and gave her a big hug. From that day on, Jessica was very careful when she picked her lollipops.

The family were out painting in the park in the winter. It was cold, but they were having fun. Dad had a pot of bright green paint. He asked little Toby, who was three, to help him paint. 

Toby replied, "Yes please!" Dad dipped a brush into the paint and handed it to Toby. Toby carefully painted a big circle on the ground. He said, "Look, Daddy. I'm making a big round smooth circle!"

"That's great, Toby!" said Dad. Toby smiled and continued painting. As he painted, he laughed and sang, "I'm painting in the winter, I'm making it bright," he sang. 

When the painting was finished, Toby and Dad stood back and smiled. They looked at the bright, smooth circle in the winter park and they were both very proud.

One day, a boy named Tom found a bottle. It was an incredible bottle. It was big, shiny, and colorful. Tom was very happy. He wanted to show it to his best friend, Sue.

Tom ran to Sue's house. He said, "Sue, look at my incredible bottle!" Sue looked at the bottle. She liked it too. Sue said, "Tom, where did you find it?" Tom mentioned that he found it near the big tree in the park.

Tom and Sue went to the park with the bottle. They wanted to play with it. They took turns holding the bottle and showing it to their friends. But then, a big dog came. The dog wanted the bottle too. The dog took the bottle in its mouth and ran away.

Tom and Sue were very sad. They tried to get the bottle back, but the dog was too fast. They lost their incredible bottle. They went home with tears in their eyes. The bottle was gone, and they couldn't play with it anymore.

Once upon a time, there was a large port. It looked so grand and majestic. All the boats docked there were huge and beautiful.

One day, a little three year old girl came to the port. She saw a large boat and said, "That's my boat!"

Her mom smiled and said, "Yes, sweetheart, but it doesn't belong to us. We don't own it."

The little girl thought for a moment and then said, "If we can't own a boat like this, then everyone should be able to use it. We should share it." 

Her mom smiled and said, "That's a wonderful idea, sweetheart. That's the right thing to do."

The moral of the story is that we should all share our resources and help others. We don't have to own everything to be generous and have fun.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with dough and make all sorts of shapes. One day, she made a big ball and rolled it high up in the air.

Her little brother, Max, saw it and said, "Wow, Lily! That's so high!"

Lily replied, "Yes, it is! Let's march around it and see how big it is." So they marched around the ball of dough, singing and laughing.

Suddenly, the ball of dough fell and splattered all over the ground. Max said, "Oh no! What happened?"

Lily explained, "I rolled it too high and it couldn't stay up anymore. That's okay though, we can make another one!" And they happily went back to playing with dough.

Once upon a time there was a boy called Jack. He was three years old and loved carrots. He wanted to always have a carrot to eat.

One day Jack was walking in the park and he saw a rabbit hopping about. The rabbit looked hungry, so Jack thought he might give him a carrot. He handed the carrot to the rabbit who eagerly ate it up.

Jack thought that the rabbit was so nice. He thought it was compassionate of him to share his carrot. To show his appreciation he started to talk to the rabbit. He told it about his day and about his love for carrots. 

The rabbit and Jack talked for some time and then the rabbit hopped away. Jack felt happy and proud that he had been compassionate and shared his carrot. He knew that it had made him and the rabbit both feel better.

Tom and Sue liked to play by the harbor. They liked to see the big boats and the small fish. They liked to hear the water and the wind. But they did not like the gray clouds. The gray clouds meant rain and thunder.

One day, they saw a new boat in the harbor. It was red and shiny. It had a big flag and a loud horn. Tom and Sue wanted to see it closer. They ran to the dock and looked for a way to get on the boat.

They saw a rope hanging from the boat. The rope was long and thick. Tom had an idea. He said to Sue, "Let's pull the rope and make the boat come to us." Sue nodded. She liked Tom's idea. They grabbed the rope and started to pull.

But the rope was not for pulling. The rope was for tying. The rope was tied to a big anchor under the water. The anchor was heavy and strong. It did not move when Tom and Sue pulled. But the boat did.

The boat started to move towards the dock. It moved fast and loud. It moved too fast and too loud. Tom and Sue did not see the boat coming. They only heard the horn. It was a warning horn. It was a scary horn.

Tom and Sue dropped the rope and ran away. They ran as fast as they could. They ran to their mom and dad. They were safe. But the boat was not. The boat crashed into the dock. It made a big noise and a big splash. It broke the dock and the boat.

Tom and Sue were sorry. They did not mean to break the dock and the boat. They did not know the rope was for tying. They only wanted to see the boat closer. They learned a lesson. They learned to be careful by the harbor. They learned to not pull ropes that are not for pulling.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and have fun with her friends. One day, Lily and her friends decided to build a tent in the backyard. They used blankets and pillows to make the tent cozy.

Lily noticed that the sky was getting dark and gray. She said to her friends, "I think it's going to rain soon. We should go inside." Her friends agreed and they all went inside the house.

Later that night, Lily's mom asked her how her day was. Lily replied, "It was great! I got to play outside with my friends and we built a tent. But then it got gray outside and we had to go inside." Her mom smiled and said, "That sounds like so much fun, Lily. I'm glad you had a good day."

Anna and Ben were twins who loved to play outside. They had a big garden with many flowers and trees. They also had a small patch where they grew some vegetables, like carrots and lettuce. Their favorite vegetable was the pumpkin, because it was big and round and orange. They liked to make faces on the pumpkins and pretend they were their friends.

One day, their mother told them that they could pick one pumpkin each for Halloween. They were very happy and ran to the garden. They looked at all the pumpkins and tried to find the best ones. Anna saw a huge pumpkin that was almost as big as her. She thought it would make a great lantern. She ran to it and tried to lift it, but it was too heavy. She asked Ben to help her.

Ben was looking at a smaller pumpkin that had a funny shape. He thought it would make a funny face. He liked it very much. He heard Anna calling him and turned around. He saw the huge pumpkin and said, "Wow, that's a big pumpkin! Do you want it?"

"Yes, please help me take it to the house. It's too heavy for me," Anna said.

Ben hesitated. He wanted to keep the smaller pumpkin, but he also wanted to help his sister. He remembered that their mother always told them to share and be kind to each other. He decided to help Anna. He said, "OK, let's take it together. But can I have the smaller pumpkin? I like it too."

Anna smiled. She said, "Sure, you can have it. Thank you for helping me. You are a good brother."

They lifted the big pumpkin together and carried it to the house. Their mother was waiting for them. She praised them for their choice and said, "You have picked two beautiful pumpkins. I'm proud of you for working together and sharing. Now let's clean them and carve them."

They followed their mother to the kitchen. They washed the pumpkins and cut off the tops. They scooped out the seeds and the pulp. They were surprised when they saw what was inside the big pumpkin. It was rotten and spoiled. It smelled bad and had worms and bugs in it. They felt sick and dropped the pumpkin. It splashed on the floor and made a mess.

They looked at the smaller pumpkin. It was fresh and sweet. It had no worms or bugs in it. It smelled good and looked happy. They felt happy too. They said, "We like this pumpkin better. It's not spoiled. It's perfect."

Their mother nodded. She said, "Sometimes, the biggest things are not the best things. Sometimes, the smallest things are the most precious things. You have learned a valuable lesson today. Don't judge a book by its cover. Don't be greedy or selfish. Be grateful and generous. That's what makes you happy."

Anna and Ben hugged their mother. They said, "We're sorry for the mess. We're glad for the lesson. We love you, Mom."

They cleaned up the mess and carved the smaller pumpkin. They made a funny face on it and put a candle inside. They placed it on the porch and admired it. It glowed in the dark and smiled at them. It reminded them of their love and their joy. They were happy.

Once there was a little boy named Mark. Mark had a favourite board. He loved it dearly and kept it close to him at all times. One day, Mark took his board and went to the park. 

As Mark walked, he heard a fierce growl. It was loud and scary, but Mark was brave. He looked around and realised the growl was coming from a huge dog. Its eyes were wide and its fur was standing up. The dog was growling at Mark's board. 

Mark was scared, but he didn't want to lose his board. He decided to face the dog. He stepped closer to it and said, "Please don't hurt my board!" 

But the dog just kept growling. Finally, it stopped and looked at Mark. It stepped closer and gently licked Mark's hand. Mark was so relieved, he hugged the dog and thanked it for being so kind and giving his board back!

Tom and Lily were playing with their toys in the living room. They liked to make noises and pretend they were animals. Tom was a lion and Lily was a bird.

"Roar!" Tom said. "I am a fierce lion and I will catch you, bird!"

"Tweet, tweet!" Lily said. "You can't catch me, lion! I am too fast and I can fly!"

They ran around the sofa and the table, laughing and having fun. But then they heard a loud noise from upstairs. It sounded like a big bang.

"What was that?" Tom asked, stopping his roar.

"I don't know," Lily said, stopping her tweet. "Maybe it was a monster!"

They looked at each other with wide eyes. They were scared of monsters. They decided to go upstairs and see what it was. They held hands and walked slowly to the stairs.

"Maybe we should number the stairs," Lily said. "That will make us brave."

"OK," Tom said. "You start."

Lily nodded. She put her foot on the first stair and said, "One."

Tom followed her and said, "Two."

They kept going, saying the numbers out loud, until they reached the top of the stairs. They saw a door that was open. The noise came from there.

"Ten," Lily said. "That's the last stair. Are you ready, Tom?"

"Yes," Tom said. "Let's go, Lily."

They walked to the door and peeked inside. They saw their big brother, Sam, playing with his drums. He was making a lot of noise with his sticks.

"Hi, Tom and Lily," Sam said. "Do you like my music?"

Tom and Lily looked at each other and smiled. They were not scared anymore. They realized it was not a monster, just their brother.

"Hi, Sam," they said. "We like your music. It's very loud."

"Can we play with you?" Lily asked.

"Sure," Sam said. "You can be my singers. Come on, let's make a song!"

Tom and Lily ran into the room and joined Sam. They sang and drummed and had fun. They forgot about the lion and the bird. They were happy.

One day, Tom felt very sore. He asked his mommy for help. She smiled and set up a massage for him.

Mommy made Tom lay down on the table. Then she got all the materials she needed for the massage. She rubbed his back softly and Tom felt much better.

Tom asked for more. Mommy said she would make a massage session available every week. Tom was very excited.

Tom felt relaxed after the massage. He thanked his mommy for taking care of him and for setting up the massage. Tom knew he would feel better now.

Once upon a time, there was a panda. Every day he liked to go to the icy river and splash around. He always had so much fun. One day, though, he noticed something strange. Instead of his splashing just making the water splash around, he was actually making a huge iceberg float away!

The panda was so excited. He wanted to go and explore the big icy island he had just made. He hopped and splashed over to it, and noticed a little bird on the edge of the iceberg.

"Hi!" said the little bird. "Where did this ice come from?"

The panda smiled. "I made it with my splashes. Would you like to take a ride on it as it drifts away?"

The little bird flew over and landed on the iceberg. "Yes!" he said, "this is so much fun!"

They sailed away together, chatting and laughing, until the sun set and the iceberg melted away. They had such a great adventure.

Arya and her dad were very excited. They had all of the equipment they needed to make a tower. They had lots of blocks, colourful plastic tubes and several modest sized boxes. Arya and her dad carefully arranged the equipment and started to make the tower.

First they put all of the blocks on the floor and stacked them together. Then Arya's dad took two of the plastic tubes and put them on top of the blocks. They were very steady and strong.

Next Arya's dad lifted some of the boxes and placed them in-between the plastic tubes. He made sure they were balanced and secure.

Arya helped too. She added the last of the blocks to the top of the tower. They were on board with how tall the tower was and clapped in joy!

They stood back and admired their creation. The tower was very tall and it felt great to have made it!

Once, there was a little girl named Alice. She wanted to build a tower that was as tall as the sky. But it was hard work, and after a while it became boring.

Alice asked her dad to help her complete the tower, but her dad said he was too busy. So Alice worked alone. She tried and tried, but it seemed like she was never going to finish it.

Alice was frustrated and upset, so she went for a walk. She saw a little boy also trying to build a tower, only his was much larger. He was working really hard and having lots of fun.

Alice talked to the boy and he showed her how he was completing the tower. He said he was taking his time, enjoying himself, and that was why he was succeeding.

Alice realized her mistake was not taking the time to enjoy the tower building process. She had been so focused on finishing that she forgot to have fun.

The moral of the story is that it's important to enjoy the journey, not just focus on the end result.

Once upon a time there was a factory. It was very cold inside. One day two friends, Simon and Peter, went to visit the factory. Simon wanted to put his hand in some of the machines to see how they worked. Peter said it was too cold, and that they should leave. 

Simon didn't want to go. He wanted to put his hand in the machine and feel how it worked. "I want to put my hand in the machine," he said.

Peter was worried. He said it wasn't safe. "It's too cold and too dangerous," he said.

Simon frowned. He didn't want to leave. He wanted to put his hand in the machine. But he knew Peter was right, so he reluctantly agreed. 

So the two friends left the factory. Even though Simon was disappointed that he couldn't put his hand in the machine, he was grateful to Peter for looking out for him.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to run and play outside. One day, she saw a big bird in the sky. It flew very fast and Lily was amazed. She watched it until it was out of sight. 

Later that day, Lily and her friends were playing a game. They had to count how many times they could jump rope without stopping. Lily was very good at it and jumped a big number of times. Her friends were impressed and clapped for her. 

At night, Lily went to bed feeling happy and proud. She dreamed about the bird and jumping rope. She knew that she could do anything if she tried her best.

Once upon a time there was a small boy named Peter. Peter was 3 years old and loved Tuesdays. Each Tuesday he would go out and play with his friends.

One Tuesday, Peter decided to give his friends a surprise. He made a big bow and hid it behind his back. He waited until his friends were all gathered, then he jumped out and shouted, "Surprise!"

He held up the big bow and his friends were so surprised they couldn't speak! Peter was very proud and happy.

But then something embarrassing happened. Peter tripped and fell over. His big bow flew across the room! His friends laughed and Peter was embarrassed.

Peter's friend Tim stepped forward and said, "That was brave of you Peter, don't be embarrassed".

Peter smiled and said, "Thanks. I'm still excited to show you my bow."

And from then on, Peter wasn't embarrassed to show his special surprise, and the group had many fun Tuesdays playing together.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Daisy. Every day she would ask her parents to teach her new things.

One day, Daisy saw a model car on the table and asked her mum to teach her about it. Daisy's mum said she would, but first Daisy had to do her chores. Daisy was sad, but she agreed and finished her chores.

Once the chores were done, Daisy's mum taught her all about the model car. She showed her how to put it together and all the amazing features it had. Daisy was very happy and she was proud of the model car she had made.

The next day, Daisy and her mum went to the park. Daisy wanted to show everyone her model car, but when she got to the park she saw another girl playing with an even bigger and more amazing model car than hers. Daisy became very sad, she wished she could have that car too.

But then Daisy's mum came up with an idea. She said "Maybe I can teach you how to make a bigger and more amazing model car". Daisy was very excited and thanked her mum for the offer! Daisy's mum taught her all she needed to know and Daisy became the proud owner of a bigger and better model car.

Jim was on a tour. He thought it would be a fun and interesting way to spend the day. Everywhere he looked he could see things that were dirty and needed to be cleaned. He thought it was not very thoughtful of some people to leave things in a mess.

So Jim decided to do something about it. He took out a cloth from his pocket and started to clean. He wiped away the dirt and made everything look much better.

He went from place to place cleaning even the smallest things. Everywhere he went, people thanked him for cleaning. Jim felt very proud of himself and he had a great time on his tour.

Anna and Ben are playing with their toys in the living room. Anna has a doll and Ben has a car. They are having fun, but Anna wants to play with the car too.

"Ben, can I have the car?" Anna asks.

"No, it's mine. You have the doll," Ben says.

"But I like the car. It's fast and shiny. Please, Ben, let me have it," Anna says.

"No, Anna, go away. You always want what I have," Ben says.

Anna gets angry. She does not like to share. She demands the car from Ben. She pulls the car with her hands. Ben pulls back. They tug and tug. The car breaks in half. They both cry.

Mom hears the noise. She comes to the living room. She sees the broken car and the crying children. She is not happy.

"What happened here?" Mom asks.

"Anna wanted my car. She broke it. It's not fair," Ben says.

"I just wanted to play. Ben was mean. He did not share," Anna says.

Mom sighs. She picks up the broken car and the doll. She puts them on the shelf. She kneels down and hugs Anna and Ben.

"Listen, children. You have to learn to share and be kind. You have many toys. You can take turns and play together. Breaking things is not nice. It makes everyone sad. Do you understand?" Mom says.

Anna and Ben nod. They are sorry. They wipe their tears. They hug Mom.

"Can we have another toy?" Anna asks.

"Only if you promise to share and be nice," Mom says.

Anna and Ben promise. They are eager to play again. Mom gives them a ball and a book. They thank Mom. They play with the ball and the book. They share and they are nice. They are happy.

Once upon a time there was a bunny named Jack. He loved to race in his garden early in the morning. Jack had lots of friends who lived nearby so they would all come to race in the garden together after breakfast.

One day, Jack had an idea. He wanted to have a special race. He ran home to ask his mom if he could use some of the hay that was stored in the shed.

"Mom, can I please use some of the hay in the shed? I want to have a special race!" he said. 

"Well," Mom replied, "that hay is a bit expensive, but I guess you can use some if it's for a good cause."

So Jack got to work. He carefully moved the hay and formed a race track. His friends were very excited, and soon the race began. Everyone ran as fast as they could, and Jack was the first one to cross the finish line.

Everyone cheered for Jack and his special race. From then on, Jack and his friends would race on the special track every day.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny named Benny. Benny was furry and loved to hop around in the grass. One day, Benny saw a big, shiny gun on the ground. Benny didn't know what it was, so he asked his friend, a little bird named Billy.

"Billy, what's that?" Benny asked, pointing at the gun.

"That's a gun, Benny. It's very dangerous. You should stay away from it," Billy warned.

Benny wanted to learn more about the gun, so he hopped closer to it. Suddenly, the gun went off and Benny was hurt. Billy quickly flew to get help, but it was too late. Benny had learned a tough lesson about guns and their danger.

Mommy and Johnny walked over to the truck. Johnny was very excited. Mommy opened the back of the truck and began to carefully load something into it.
