Once upon a time there were two best friends, Bob and Nancy. Every day they would go together to the forest nearby to play. One day, Bob wanted to cut down a tree with an axe. Nancy looked scared and said, "Let's not chop down a tree. That's wrong." But Bob just rolled his eyes and grasped the axe.

Nancy looked more and more miserable as she watched Bob chopping down the tree. Finally, she shouted, "Stop!" With a sigh, Bob put down the axe and they sat together on the ground. 

To cheer Nancy up, Bob suggested, "Let's go skipping around the pond." Nancy smiled and skipped around the pond with Bob. The sun shone on their faces. 

Nancy forgot about the axe and she laughed as she skipped around the pond with Bob. Soon, the pond looked like a swirling of colours and Nancy was no longer miserable. They were back to being the best of friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy had a brilliant idea to build a sandcastle at the beach. He asked his mom to come with him to the beach. 

When they arrived, Timmy started building his sandcastle. He was having a lot of fun until a big wave came and destroyed his sandcastle. Timmy was sad and started to cry. 

His mom came over and gave him a big hug. "Don't worry, Timmy," she said. "Let's rub our hands together and build an even bigger and better sandcastle!" Timmy smiled and they started to build again. In the end, their sandcastle was even more brilliant than before.

Anna and Ben love to play with their toy trains. They have many trains of different colors and shapes. They like to make tracks on the floor and pretend they are driving the trains.

One day, they find a new train in a box. It is a huge train, bigger than any of their other trains. It is black and shiny, with a red funnel and a yellow whistle. It has a button on the side that says "Press me".

Anna and Ben are curious. They press the button and the train makes a loud noise. Puff, puff, puff! Steam comes out of the funnel and the whistle blows. The train starts to move on its own, along the track. Anna and Ben are amazed and excited. They follow the train as it goes around the room.

But then, the train goes too fast. It bumps into a chair and falls off the track. It lands on the floor with a crash. Anna and Ben are scared. They run to the train and try to pick it up. But it is too heavy for them. They look at the train and see a label on the bottom. It says "This train belongs to Grandpa. Do not touch".

Anna and Ben feel sorry. They did not know the train was Grandpa's. They think Grandpa will be angry with them for breaking his train. They start to cry.

But then, they hear a voice. It is Grandpa. He comes into the room and sees the train and the children. He is not angry. He smiles and hugs them. He says "Don't worry, my dears. The train is not broken. It is just a little old and needs some fixing. I'm glad you like it. It was my favorite toy when I was a little boy. Do you want to play with it with me?"

Anna and Ben nod and smile. They are happy. They love Grandpa and his train. They help him put the train back on the track and press the button again. The train makes a loud noise and steam comes out of the funnel. The whistle blows and the train moves along the track. Anna and Ben laugh and clap. They play with the train and Grandpa for a long time. They think the train is the best toy ever.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim was different from other kids. He liked the silence a lot. Tim had a friend named Sam. Sam liked to talk and play loud games.

One day, Tim and Sam were playing in the park. Sam was making a lot of noise, and Tim felt sad. He wanted some silence. So, Tim said to Sam, "Can we play a quiet game? I like the silence."

Sam thought for a moment and then said, "Okay, let's send a message to the birds." They sat down and wrote a message on a piece of paper. They tied the message to a stick and put it in the ground. Then, they sat in the silence and waited for the birds to read their message.

As they sat in the quiet park, Tim and Sam felt happy. They learned that being different is okay, and it's good to try new things. From that day on, they played both loud and quiet games together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl and her mommy. One night they made a special treat â€“ a candle! The girl was so excited and laughed loud.

Mommy lit the candle and the room filled with a sweet smell. The girl clapped her hands and smiled. But then, the girl's little brother came in and spoiled the special night. He was loud and noisy, and the candle went out!

The girl was sad, but her mommy said it was ok. She gave the girl a hug and said, â€œWeâ€™ll light the candle again soon!â€ So, the girl felt better and smiled. 

The next night, the family lit the candle again and the girl laughed loud. They had a special night, and it was made even better with the smell of the candle!

Once there was a little girl called Lucy. One day Lucy wanted to go for an adventure, so she took her luggage and hopped on a bus.

When she arrived at the destination, she was excited to explore. As she wandered around, Lucy tried to guess what she would find.

Just then, she heard a voice speaking. She looked around and saw a friendly man.

Lucy asked the man, "What is this place?"

The man smiled and said, "This is a successful market. People come here to sell and buy things."

Lucy was amazed. She said goodbye to the man and continued exploring the market. She guessed that she would have a successful adventure. And she was right!

Once there was a race. All the animals wanted to win it. They wanted to be the fastest.

One animal was an adorable cat. She wanted to win. But she knew she was not very fast. So she practiced and practiced.

Every day, the cat worked hard. Gradually, she started to run a little faster. And every day she was improving.

Finally, it was time for the race. All the animals were ready. With one big cheer, they began.

The cat tried her best. She kept running as fast as she could. And she won! Everyone was so proud of her.

Anna and Ben were going on vacation with their mom and dad. They were very happy. They packed their bags and got in the car. They drove for a long time to the big airport.

At the airport, they had to wait in a line. Anna and Ben were bored. They saw a big window with many planes outside. They wanted to see the planes. They told their mom and dad they were going to the window. Their mom and dad said okay, but don't go too far.

Anna and Ben ran to the window. They saw many planes. Some were big, some were small. Some were white, some were blue. Some were taking off, some were landing. They pointed and shouted. They had fun.

But they did not see their mom and dad. Their mom and dad did not see them. Their mom and dad were busy with their bags and tickets. They moved to another line. They thought Anna and Ben were behind them.

Anna and Ben turned around. They did not see their mom and dad. They saw many people. Some were tall, some were short. Some were old, some were young. Some were smiling, some were frowning. They did not know anyone. They were scared.

They looked for their mom and dad. They walked around. They called their names. But they did not find them. They felt lost. They felt sad.

Their mom and dad looked for them. They walked around. They called their names. But they did not find them. They felt worried. They felt angry.

They asked a nice lady for help. The nice lady wore a badge. She worked at the airport. She said she would help them find their children. She used a loud speaker. She said, "Anna and Ben, please come to the information desk. Your mom and dad are looking for you."

Anna and Ben heard the loud speaker. They heard their names. They heard their mom and dad were looking for them. They felt happy. They ran to the information desk. They saw their mom and dad. They hugged them. They said they were sorry. They said they wanted to see the planes.

Their mom and dad hugged them. They said they were sorry. They said they were glad they found them. They said they loved them. They said they were going on vacation.

They thanked the nice lady. They took their bags and tickets. They went to their plane. They boarded the plane. They sat in their seats. They buckled their belts. They looked out the window. They saw the planes. They saw the airport. They saw the nice lady wave goodbye.

The plane started to move. The plane went faster and faster. The plane lifted off the ground. The plane flew in the sky. The airport disappeared. The vacation began.

One day, a duck decided to go for a swim in the pond. Suddenly, it saw something strange. It was a little seed that was beginning to grow! The duck was so excited, watching it grow bigger and bigger.

As the seed kept growing, the duck noticed it was taking up space in the pond. Its feathers became all ruffled and it became very upset. It didn't know what to do.

So, the duck decided to hop onto the seed and have a closer look. It was a big, green tree! The duck quacked in amazement as it realised there was now less water in the pond. It had to find a new pond to swim in.

The duck hopped off the seed, said goodbye to its old pond and flew far away. It eventually found a new home by a bigger pond and happily hopped into the refreshing water for a swim. The duck was no longer upset and was excited to grow old in its new home.

Once there was a little bird called Billy. He loved to fly high in the sky, and laughed when the wind blew through his feathers.

One day, while Billy was flying, he saw something in the sky. It was a wreck, hanging high above. He was curious so he flew toward it, wanting to get a closer look.

Just as he flew closer, he felt a gust of wind. He was swept away and found himself hanging on the wreck, unable to fly away. He felt scared and helpless.

Suddenly, an old wisebird flew up to the wreck and asked Billy what he was doing. Billy explained how he was curious and flew too close to the wreck. The wisebird said that curiosity often leads to danger, and it is important to be careful.

Billy thanked the wisebird and flew back home. He learned an important lesson that day and always remembered to be careful of what he was curious about.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Anna. She was three years old and wanted to play outside in her garden. She ran to open the door, but it would not open. Anna tried and tried, but the door wouldn't budge. She became frustrated and cried out, "Why won't the door open?!" 

Just then, her father came to help. He held her hand and said, "Let's unite and open the door together". So, Anna held her father's hand and with a big tug, the door opened. 

Anna and her father opened the door, stepped outside and discovered the most beautiful garden. Anna was amazed by all the wonderful colours and wonderful smells.

From then on, Anna and her father helped each other out whenever they could. Anna realised that when they united and worked together, they could achieve much more than they ever could alone.

The moral of the story is: together we are stronger.

Once upon a time, there was a brown dog named Buddy. Buddy loved to play outside with his friends. One day, Buddy and his friends went to the park to play. They saw a grill and wanted to make some food.

Buddy's friend, a little girl named Sarah, put some food on the grill. When the food was ready, she used a big fork to twist it. The food smelled yummy, and it made Buddy's tummy rumble. He couldn't wait to eat!

After they ate the tasty food from the grill, Buddy and his friends played all day. They were very happy. When the sun went down, they went home, tired but smiling. Buddy couldn't wait for another fun day at the park with his friends.

Once upon a time, there was a small stream in the woods. It wound from way up high on the mountains, to way down below in a valley.

Suddenly, it started to rain very heavily. The drops of water chattered on the leaves and rocks of the forest. "Come on stream," said a single bird, "you can do it!"

The stream was determined. It pushed past the rocks and under fallen trees. Little by little, the stream grew faster and wider.

Soon the stream burst into a bright, bubbling spring. It poured down the mountainside, filling up the valley below with its sparkly water. 

"Look at the spring," cheered the bird. "It's so heavy and strong!"

The stream had done it. It had come from way up high, to way down in a valley. 
 
The stream smiled as it continued to pour its way through the woods.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to bake cookies with her mom. One day, Lily's mom said, "Lily, let's bake some cookies today!" Lily was so happy and said, "Yay! I love baking cookies with you!"

They went to the kitchen and started to bake. They mixed flour, sugar, butter, and eggs together. Then, they put the cookies in the oven to bake. While they were waiting, Lily noticed that their carpet was dirty. She said, "Mom, our carpet is dirty. It makes me sad." 

Lily's mom replied, "Don't be sad, Lily. We can clean the carpet after we finish baking our cookies." Lily smiled and said, "Okay, Mom. Let's finish baking first!" After a while, the cookies were ready and they sat down to eat them. Lily was so happy and said, "These cookies are yummy! Baking with you always makes me happy."

The sun was shining on the beautiful lake. A family was out for a picnic. They laughed and played together and it was a perfect day.

The little boy was so excited. He wanted to explore the lake. So he asked his dad if he could get in and go for a swim. His dad said yes, so he splashed into the water.

The water was so cool and the little boy was having so much fun. He paddled and floated around, exploring the lake.

After some time, the little boy became very tired, so he decided to get out of the lake. All of a sudden, he was surprised to find his dad had brought a boat and he knew just what his dad had planned. They set off in the boat, moving slowly and peacefully across the lake, soaking in its beautiful surroundings.

The family sailed around the lake until the sun began to set and the stars came out. It was a perfect way to end their adventure.

Once upon a time, there was a large potato. He was the biggest one of all. He smiled and wiggled away and the other potatoes laughed. Suddenly, the sun came out and the large potato sparkled! Everyone in the field was awed, and they started to clap their hands and applaud him.

The large potato felt so happy that he started to run around. He was so excited, so he started to jump and spin around. All of his friends watched and laughed and clapped their hands!

Afterwards, they all thanked the large potato for making them smile and they decided to bake him in the oven. When he was done, they all cheered and applauded again. The large potato was so pleased. He looked up at the sky and thanked the sun for making him so sparkly and special.

Once upon a time there was a lily. The lily was so pretty and gentle. She was playing in the garden when it started to rain. The rain made the ground rough and the lily became very sad.

The rain kept coming down and the lily got heavier and heavier. She was so sad because of the rain, she couldn't move anymore. She just stayed their, stuck in the ground.

Suddenly, a kind fairy appeared. She had a magical wand and waved it around the lily, making the ground softer. The lily was so happy! Now, she could fly away in the wind. 

The lily flew away in the wind until she was almost weightless and completely at peace. That's how it is with lilies, no matter how rough the weather, they can always find a way to fly free.

Once upon a time, there was a sleepy cat named Love. Love liked to roll around in the grass. One sunny day, Love went outside to roll and play.

Love saw a big ball and wanted to play with it. Love rolled the ball down a hill. The ball rolled faster and faster. Love ran after the ball, feeling less sleepy now.

At the bottom of the hill, Love met a dog. The dog said, "I want to play too!" Love and the dog played with the ball. But then, the ball rolled into a big, dark hole. Love and the dog could not get the ball back. They both felt sad and went home.

Once upon a time there was a pink ball. It was very bouncy and it loved to play.
One day, the ball went to explore outside. Everywhere it bounced, it sent up puffs of dust. The sun shone pink in the sky and happy little birds sang. The ball was so excited it bounced all across the green grass, higher and higher!

When the sun went down, the ball was still happy, but very tired too. It bounced one last time and, whoosh, it disappeared! Under the light of the stars, the ball left a little cloud of pink dust behind.

Suddenly, the ball jumped back into view! It had been bouncing and playing all around the world! It was so happy to be back home and to feel the soft grass again. It started to bounce, sending up dust with every jump, always reminding us that playtime is fun!

Once upon a time there was a little boy. He was feeling very uncomfortable. He had a big secret and no one knew it.

One day, he decided to go for a walk. He saw two big birds zip through the sky. He wished he could do that.

He decided to zip through the park, but oh no! He ran into a tree and hit his head. He was so embarrassed and felt very uncomfortable.

The little boy ran home and cried. His secret was still safe, but he was very sad and uncomfortable. He would never dare to zip through the park again.

The little girl wanted something sweet. She was very obedient, so she asked politely. She went to her mom and said, "Mommy, may I please have candy?" Her mom smiled and said yes.

The little girl was so excited. She could hardly contain her joy. She thanked her mom very much and ran to find the candy.

She looked in all the drawers and found the candy she was looking for. She grabbed the candy and ran back to her mom.

The little girl happily said, "Thank you for the candy, mommy!" She was so happy that her mom agreed to her request. She went and sat down in the couch and sat there eating her candy. She was a very obedient little girl and had done exactly what she was supposed to do.

Once there was a white cube. It was a very special cube because it could do amazing things. When the cube was placed on the ground, it would jump and spin around. Everyone wanted to try it out, but it was very slippery, so it was hard to hold on. But then one day, a boy was brave enough to wipe his hands on it before trying. Sure enough, the cube stayed in his hands. The boy was so happy, he spun around with the cube for hours. He even showed his friends how to wipe the cube before trying. Now everyone can play the white cube game.

Lily and Anna are sisters. Lily is big and Anna is little. They like to play together in the park. They swing on the swings, slide on the slide, and run on the grass.

One day, they see a big dog in the park. The dog is brown and fluffy. It has a long tail and a wet nose. The dog runs to Lily and Anna and licks their faces. Lily and Anna laugh and pet the dog.

"Hello, doggy!" Lily says. "What is your name?"

The dog barks and wags its tail. It likes Lily and Anna.

"His name is Max," a voice says. Lily and Anna look up and see a boy. The boy is holding a leash. He is the dog's owner.

"Hi, I'm Lily and this is Anna," Lily says. "We like your dog. He is very friendly."

"Hi, I'm Ben," the boy says. "Max likes you too. Do you want to play with him?"

"Yes, please!" Anna says. She smiles and hugs the dog.

Lily, Anna, Ben, and Max play together in the park. They have a lot of fun. They are happy and smile a lot. They make new friends.

Once upon a time there was a wide barrel. It was a special barrel and it had a very special job. Every day a big truck would come by and have a long hose. The long hose would connect the truck to the wide barrel.

The truck would have lots of water. The water would pour from the truck and into the wide barrel. When the barrel was full of water, the truck would take it away.

The wide barrel held lots of water. Every day the truck came back to have more water. The truck filled the barrel and then it took it away.

The wide barrel could not do this alone. It needed the truck to help it. Every day the truck and the wide barrel worked together to make sure eating and drinking were special.

Once upon a time, there lived a family in a small house. They bought a brand new iron to help them with their daily chores. The iron was their favorite because it was shiny, smooth and original. 

Every morning, the family would use the iron to press the clothes. But one day, the iron's handle broke so it stopped working. The family was so sad and couldn't delay fixing it. They took it to the store and asked for help. 

The storekeeper examined the iron carefully and said he could fix it. He worked on it for a few minutes and soon, the iron was back to its original form. 

The family was so happy and decided to treat the storekeeper with a special cake. From that day onwards, the iron worked like a charm and the family was able to press their clothes on time!

Lila was sad. Her doll had a rip on her lip. She loved her doll very much. She wanted to make her doll happy again.

She went to her mom and showed her the rip. "Mom, can you help me? My doll has a boo-boo on her lip. It hurts her."

Mom looked at the doll and smiled. "Don't worry, Lila. I can help you. I have a needle and some thread. I can restore your doll's lip. Do you know what restore means?"

Lila shook her head. "No, mom. What does it mean?"

Mom explained. "Restore means to make something good again. Like when you clean your room or when you fix a broken toy. It means you make it useful again. Do you know what useful means?"

Lila nodded. "Yes, mom. Useful means you can do something with it. Like my doll. She is useful because I can play with her and hug her and talk to her."

Mom smiled again. "That's right, Lila. You are a smart girl. Now, let me restore your doll's lip. It will only take a few minutes. Then you can play with her again."

Mom took the needle and the thread and sewed the rip on the doll's lip. She was very careful and gentle. She made the lip look good again. She gave the doll back to Lila.

Lila was happy. She hugged her doll and kissed her lip. She thanked her mom. "Mom, you are the best. You restored my doll's lip. She is happy again. And so am I."

Mom hugged Lila and her doll. "You are welcome, Lila. I'm glad you are happy. You and your doll are very useful to me. You make me happy too."

Mum was very angry. She was making lots of noise.

"You are being so foolish!" she said.

Young Ben had been playing with an old cube. He was trying to load it onto the truck.

"I just wanted to help!" Ben said. His eyes were filling up with tears.

Mum saw how upset Ben was. She sighed and gave him a hug.

"It's okay," she said. "Let's try it together."

Mum and Ben took the cube and carefully loaded it onto the truck.

"That's much better," Mum said. "Now don't be so foolish in the future."

Ben smiled and nodded. He knew he was very lucky to have such a kind mother.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to write poems. He would write them in his notebook every day.

One day, Timmy's little sister, Sally, took his notebook and scribbled all over it. Timmy was very upset. He wanted to yell at Sally, but his mom said that wasn't nice. She said he could be mad, but he couldn't be mean.

Timmy thought about it and decided to write a poem about how he felt. He wrote about how Sally wasn't allowed to touch his things without asking. He wrote about how his notebook was special to him and how Sally made him feel sad. When he read his deep and meaningful poem to his mom, she hugged him and said she was proud of him for using his words instead of being mean.

Once upon a time, there was a nice boy named Timmy. Timmy loved playing with his toys, especially his toy car. One day, Timmy's friend Billy came over to play. Billy wanted to play with Timmy's toy car, but Timmy didn't want to share.

Billy said, "Timmy, can you please lend me your toy car? I promise to take good care of it."

Timmy thought about it and finally agreed. Billy was very happy and played with the toy car for a long time. But then, Billy accidentally broke the toy car. Timmy was upset, but Billy apologized and promised to fix it.

The next day, Billy took the toy car to the x-ray machine at the hospital to see if he could fix it. The x-ray showed that the toy car was broken and needed some glue. Billy fixed the toy car and returned it to Timmy. Timmy was happy again and thanked Billy for being honest and fixing his toy car.

Alvin was excited as he was unpacking his suitcase. Inside, he found a big surprise - a toy boat! The boat was blue and had a funny flag on the top. Alvin couldn't wait to play with it. He grabbed it and ran to the nearest river.

He lined the boat up carefully and said goodbye as he watched the boat sail away. It went very far, until he couldn't see it anymore. 

Soon, it was getting dark and Alvin was a little worried. He started to dream about his boat getting lost or stuck. Suddenly, he saw a light in the distance. He ran closer and noticed it was his boat!

Alvin was so happy he had found it. He rushed over and picked it up. But when he got closer, he noticed the back of it was wet. He looked around and saw it had been pushed onto some big rocks. He reached out and ran his finger along the side. He felt a deep cut.

Alvin was sad. He knew it was time to go home. He carefully packed the boat into his suitcase and walked back. Even though his boat was hurt, he knew he had a great adventure.

Once upon a time, there was a mighty fox. He loved to jump all day, with not a care in the world. One day, he found a pen lying in the grass. He picked it up and examined this strange object. After a few moments, he realised he could use it to jump even higher. He wrote a spell on a piece of paper and threw the pen in the air. Suddenly, the mighty fox started to jump up, higher and higher. He sailed over the treetops and even flew further than the clouds. Finally, after a long adventure, the fox landed back at the same spot. His spells had been fulfilled and he was content!

Once upon a time there was a fat penny. She looked so shiny and beautiful that she made a young boy smile. The boy picked up the penny and decided to take it home with him.

When he arrived home, the boy's mother said, "You can't keep the penny, it doesn't belong to us. You have to return it."

The boy wasn't too happy about that but he had no choice. He slowly walked back to the place where he had found the penny and put it back on the ground. 

Suddenly, a fat rat jumped out of nowhere and snatched the penny away. The boy was so surprised that he forgot to chase after the rat.

The boy never saw his penny again. He was very sad.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Olive. She was only three years old and always wanted to learn more. 
One day, Olive's mommy told her that if she wanted to learn, she had to work hard. Olive was so excited and began practicing her ABC's and counting numbers right away! 
"Mommy, what else can I learn?" asked Olive. 
Her mommy replied "One day, Olive, you'll learn how to read and write if you keep working hard". 
Olive smiled and kept practicing her ABC's and counting. She knew she had to be very determined. 
Once Olive felt confident in her ABC's and counting, she asked her mommy again "Can I learn something else now?" 
Her mommy smiled and said "Yes Olive, you can learn how to ride a bike". 
Olive was so excited she started practicig that very day. At the end of the week, she had learned how to ride a bike! Olive felt so proud of herself for learning how to do something so hard. 

The moral of the story: with hard work, anything is possible!

Once upon a time, there was a persistent sock. It loved to slide down the slide! The sock was so happy when it was at the top of the slide, ready to have fun.

It always slid down slowly and carefully, making sure it was safe. The other socks laughed and cheered when the persistent sock was sliding down. They loved watching it go down.

When the sock got to the bottom, it would stand up, brush itself off, and then slide back up. The sock did this over and over again, repeatedly sliding down and back up the slide.

The other socks knew that the persistent sock needed a rest, so they all decided to join it. The persistent sock was so excited to have its friends slide with it! 

That day, every sock slid up and down the slide, laughing, cheering, and having a great time. And the persistent sock smiled, so glad that its friends were having just as much fun as it did.

One day, Sol was happy and excited because his parents had taken him to the park. He ran around the play area, looking at all the things he could do. He saw a big slide and almost giggled when he saw it. 
His parents encouraged him to go up and try it out. Sol climbed up the stairs, slowly and carefully until he reached the top of the slide. Then he took one big step and slid down the slide. He felt a rush of air on his face and his stomach rose up in the air. 
He loved it so much he said he wanted to do it again. His parents said he could but that he must be careful and not be too careless. So Sol paid attention to what he was doing and went up the slide again. He went down carefully and slowly, enjoying every second of it. He smiled when he reached the bottom and ran back up the stairs to go down the slide again. 
He went up and down the slide until he was too tired to keep playing. Then he went home, happy and content.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play outside. She would run and jump and laugh in the sunshine every day. But on Sundays, she knew it was time to take a bath. Her mommy always made sure she was clean and smelled nice for church.

One Sunday, Lily's mommy told her they were going to visit her grandparents. Lily was excited to see them, but she was also worried. Her mommy's car was old and sometimes it didn't work very well. Lily wondered if they would make it to her grandparents' house on time.

After her bath, Lily put on her favorite dress and waited for her mommy to finish getting ready. When they got in the car, Lily noticed her mommy was driving very carefully. She was being reliable, just like Lily's daddy always was. And sure enough, they arrived at her grandparents' house right on time.

Lily had a wonderful day with her grandparents, and on the way home, she fell asleep in the car, dreaming of all the fun she would have playing outside again tomorrow.

Sally was 3-years-old and loved to make things. One day she was having fun in her room when she got a wonderful idea. She decided to make an object out of paper and glue.

She was feeling so proud of herself that she wanted to mail it to her grandparents. She put it in an envelope, addressed it to Grandma and Grandpa, and put it in the mailbox. She was very excited to show them her creation.

The week after she mailed it, Sally was excited for her grandparents to write back to her. But when the letter came, it was smelly. Grandma had opened the envelope and found the object inside was dripping wet and growing mold. 

Sally was so upset that she started to cry. Despite her best intentions, the object was ruined and it couldn't be mailed. Grandma had to tell Sally to try again the next time.

Once upon a time there was a lion who lived in the jungle. He had a big, deep roar. All the animals in the jungle were scared of him. 

One day, he saw a lamp in a tree. He was very alert and he wanted to get it. He climbed the tree and tried to grab it, but he couldn't quite reach it. 

He tried to roar, but it didn't work. The animals in the jungle laughed at him. The lion was very angry and tried again and again, but still couldn't get the lamp. 

Suddenly, a little mouse came along and said, "I can help you". The lion was very thankful. He asked the mouse to climb the tree and get the lamp for him. 

The mouse climbed the tree and grabbed the lamp. The lion thanked the mouse and gave him a big hug. The animals in the jungle were very impressed. 

From then on, the lion and the mouse were best friends, and the animals in the jungle welcomed them both.

One sunny summer day, a little boy named Tim went to the park with his mom. They saw a man with a big box. The man said, "I need to deliver this box to my friend. Can you help me, Tim?"

Tim said, "Yes, I can help!" So, Tim and his mom helped the man carry the big box. They walked and walked until they found the man's friend. The friend was very happy to see the box.

Inside the box was a spicy snack. The friend said, "Thank you for helping deliver my spicy snack. Let's all share it!" They all sat in the park and enjoyed the spicy snack together. Tim was proud that he could help, and he had a fun summer day.

Once there was a bald man and he liked to play sports. Every day he would go outside and count how many times he could throw the ball up in the air before he caught it.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl and a little boy, who both wanted to have an adventure. So, one day, they decided to crawl to the park.

Lila and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. They see a big tree with a long trunk. They want to hug the trunk.

Lila runs to the tree first. She wraps her arms around the trunk. She says, "This is my tree. I hug it."

Ben is sad. He wants to hug the tree too. He says, "No, this is our tree. We can hug it together."

Lila and Ben start to argue. They pull and push each other. They are not friends anymore.

A bird is watching them from a branch. The bird is smart. It knows how to make them stop. It flies down and lands on the trunk. It says, "Tweet, tweet, tweet. This is my tree. You can't hug it."

Lila and Ben are surprised. They look at the bird. They see that the bird is small and cute. They think that the bird is funny. They forget to argue. They laugh.

The bird says, "Tweet, tweet, tweet. You can hug the tree if you hug each other first."

Lila and Ben smile. They hug each other. They say, "We are sorry. We are friends again."

They hug the trunk together. The bird joins them. They are happy.

John was very proud of his new book. He hugged it close and showed it to his mum. He hugged the book like it was his best friend. His mum smiled, she could tell he valued it.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. Her name was Lucy and she was three years old. Everyone who knew her loved her very much.

Once upon a time, two friends named Jack and Jill were very eager to play together. They had a long stand still they needed to cross in order to unite. As they were walking, they were showing off their favourite toys.

John was a loyal boy. He loved helping people, even if it was as simple as carrying groceries or opening jars. He tried his best to do what his parents asked and was rewarded with a pastry.

"What's wrong?" his mom asked. "Why don't you want to finish your letter?"

His mom smiled and said, "It's okay. You can take your time, and as long as you try your hardest, you're still being loyal. Trust me - good things come to those who are loyal."

John looked up at his mom and smiled. He restarted the letter with a new confidence and soon, he had finished it.

Once upon a time, there was a gifted little girl named Grace. Grace was curious about the world and always wanted to learn new things. She was so smart that her parents decided to hire a tutor to help her with school.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Sarah. One day, Sarah started to walk to the beach. She wanted to explore the ocean.

When she arrived at the beach and saw the ocean, Sarah was amazed. She had never seen so much water! The waves were gentle and there was sand everywhere.

Sarah was so excited, she took off her shoes and socks and began running towards the ocean.

Then a voice called out, "Sarah, stop! You know you can't go into the water, it's too deep!"

Mum put her arm around Sarah and said, "I know, but not today. We'll come back another time, okay?"

Sarah nodded and they both walked away, the ocean glimmering in the sunlight.

Once upon a time, there were two best friends. They were out in a field, having a fun time. One of them looked at the bush and said, "Look! I bet I can kick the bush!" So he ran up to the bush and gave it a big kick. It was funny because the bush shook and bounced a bit.

The two friends laughed and kept playing. Pretty soon, both of them were running around and kicking other things like trees and rocks. Everything was so much fun!

The friends kept playing until it was time for them to go home. But before they said goodbye, they ran up to the bush one more time and gave it a final kick. The bush wobbled and swayed, making them laugh so much!

And with that, they had the best time ever. The bush was a lot of fun and they were sure to come play with it again real soon.

Lily was a girl who liked to help others. She was good at solving problems. One day, she saw a boy crying in the park. He had lost his ball in a big bush.

"Can I help you?" Lily asked.

"I can't find my ball. It's my favorite. It's red and shiny," the boy said.

Lily looked at the bush. It was very thick and prickly. She could not see the ball. But she had an idea.

"Wait here. I'll be back soon," she said. She ran to her house and got a stick. She came back to the park and gave the stick to the boy.

"Use this to poke the bush. Maybe you can find your ball," she said.

The boy took the stick and thanked Lily. He poked the bush carefully. He heard a rustle. He saw something red and shiny. He reached in and pulled out his ball.

"Yay! I found it! Thank you, Lily. You are very smart and kind," he said.

Lily smiled. She was happy to help. She made a new friend.

The moral of the story is: Helping others can solve problems and make friends.

Once there was a dishwasher who was very mysterious. He lived in a tall house with no one around. Every day he would finish cleaning all the dirty dishes.

One day, the mysterious dishwasher decided to go for a walk in the woods. As he was walking he took a wrong turn and ended up in a spooky cave full of bats! He was so scared but he kept trying to find a way out.

After a while, the dishwasher saw a strange light in the middle of the cave. He came closer and saw it was a big pile of dishes! He was very relieved and started washing the dishes one-by-one.

But just as he finished, a loud noise came from outside! It was a big, angry bear and it wanted the mysterious dishwasher to leave. The dishwasher was too scared to move and the bear chased him out of the cave.

Once upon a time, there was a furry loop. Every day, the loop liked to wander. He would wander through the grass and around the trees.
It was a sunny day and the loop was feeling happy, so he kept wandering until he came to a big hill. He was so excited to explore what was on the other side!

The loop slowly climbed the hill, enjoying the feeling of the grass tickling his furry body. He kept going until he reached the top and looked around. There was a field full of flowers!

The loop couldn't resist. He started to wander through the field, careful not to step on any of the flowers. The colors and scents of the flowers made the loop feel so peaceful, and soon he had made a big loop around the field. 

The sun was setting now and the loop knew it was time to go back home. He said goodbye to the flowers and wandered back through the grass and trees until he was safely home in his furry loop again.

Sweety was a 3 year old girl who lived on a farm. Sometimes her mommy would give her a razor and show her how to use it. Sweety was always amazed and wondered what it was used for.

Sweety thought about this and wondered why the cat was so scared of the razor. She soon decided that she would keep the razor far away from the cat and make sure to keep the garden tidy.

Once upon a time there was a little boy named Max. He was three years old and he had big dreams. Every day he would look up in the sky and daydream about what he wanted to be when he grew up.

One morning, Jack woke up feeling jolly. He couldn't remember why, but he was so happy that he wanted to go find something to do right away. Then, he remembered that he wanted to write a story. He ran to his bedroom and grabbed a hammer out of his toy box.

Just then, his mom came in. "Jack, what are you doing?" she asked.

Timmy was walking through the park when he saw something shiny in the grass. He bent down and saw it was a mine. He was so excited he immediately started to poke it.

Suddenly, a voice said, "Stop poking it!" Timmy quickly stood up and saw a small person. The person was dressed in a modest outfit and had a small hat on their head.

Once upon a time, there lived a purple cow. One day, the cow wanted to escape! It jumped the fence of the farm and ran away.

The farmer thanked the veterinarian, then took the cow back to the farm. The cow never tried to escape again!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She had a big worry that made her very hurt. One day, she met a kind man. He asked why she was so worried and hurt. The little girl told him her worry. He hugged her and said he could help her. She smiled, and they went on a walk together.

Once upon a time there was a boy named Jack. He loved to ride his bike and he was always so excited when he got to go to the station to ride. One day, Jack was at the station and he saw a beautiful orange bike. He knew he had to have it! Jack decided to take the bike home and he was so happy. 

The next day, Jack went back to the station to take a ride. But when he got there, the orange bike was gone! Jack was so sad and started to cry.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy who loved to play with his large red wagon. Every day he would take it outside and use it to explore his neighborhood.

One special day, the little boy took his wagon to a big open meadow by the river. He lay down in the tall grass, put his hands behind his head and looked at the big, blue sky.

Suddenly, he heard a deep voice. "Why are you lying here?" it said.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Sandy who was always looking for adventure. One day, Sandy decided to go explore a quiet valley nearby. She walked and walked until she reached the valley. When she got there, Sandy was in for a big surprise.

The moral of this story is that it's important to keep things normal. Sometimes, when things look broken, it's best just to leave them be.

Once upon a time there was a wise old man who kept a skull on his desk. He spent all his days polishing it with a cloth.

Once upon a time, there was a cat named Tom. Tom was an interesting cat. He liked to stretch every day. One day, Tom met a dog named Max. Max was a big dog who knew many things. They became friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to climb mountains with her parents. One day, they found a very ugly mountain. It was covered in brown rocks and had no trees or flowers. Lily's parents wanted to climb it, but Lily refused. She said it was too ugly and scary.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He loved to ride his bike in the park. One day, he saw his friend Billy and they decided to ride together. They rode and rode until they saw a big tree. Timmy wanted to look up at the tree, but he couldn't see the top.

Once upon a time, there was a cute bunny. The bunny loved to play in the grass. One day, the bunny saw a big cloud in the sky. The cloud was white and fluffy, just like the bunny.

Once upon a time, there was a small box. It was fragile, so everyone was very careful not to break it. The box belonged to a little girl who loved it very much.

Once upon a time, there was a princess who had a special crystal. The princess was very sad. The crystal was very sad too. The princess wanted to fight with something bad. One day, a big bad dragon came along. He wanted the crystal, so he roared and growled.

Once upon a time, there was a penny. The penny was all alone but it was very noisy. Every day it called out "Hi, hi, hi!"

Once upon a time, there was a red goose. The red goose lived in a small pond. The pond was very dirty. The red goose did not like the dirty pond. The red goose wanted a clean pond to play in.

Once upon a time, there lived a tiny mouse. His home was behind a large wooden crate. One day, a big cat came along and saw the crate. He moved the crate and the mouse quickly ran away.

The mouse was so excited to show off his new bottle. He played many games with it. But then, his bottle got broken. The mouse was sad and started to cry.

Sara and Tom were playing in the kitchen. They liked to pretend they were chefs and make different dishes with the food they found. Sara saw a bunch of celery on the counter and had an idea.

"Tom, do you dare to eat this celery?" she asked, holding up a green stalk.

Tom looked at the celery and made a face. He did not like celery. It was bitter and crunchy and made his mouth dry. He shook his head.

"No, I don't dare. Celery is yucky. I only like carrots and apples and cheese," he said.

Sara smiled. She liked to tease Tom and make him do things he did not want to do. She thought it was fun.

"Come on, Tom. Don't be a baby. It's just celery. It's good for you. It makes you strong and healthy. If you eat it, I will give you a cookie," she said.

Tom looked at the cookie jar on the shelf. He loved cookies. They were sweet and soft and made him happy. He thought for a moment. Maybe he could eat the celery and get a cookie. Maybe it was not so bad.

"Okay, Sara. I will eat the celery. But only one bite. And you have to give me a cookie," he said.

Sara nodded. She gave Tom the celery and watched him take a small bite. Tom chewed the celery and made a grumpy face. He did not like it at all. He spit it out in the trash can and ran to the sink to drink some water.

"Yuck, yuck, yuck! Celery is the worst. I hate it. I never want to eat it again," he said.

Sara laughed. She thought Tom was funny. She took a cookie from the jar and gave it to Tom.

"Here, Tom. Here is your cookie. You are a brave boy. You ate the celery. I am proud of you," she said.

Tom took the cookie and smiled. He was glad he ate the celery. He got a cookie and made Sara happy. He ate the cookie and felt better.

"Thank you, Sara. You are a nice sister. You gave me a cookie. I am sorry I was grumpy. Can we play some more?" he said.

Sara hugged Tom and nodded.

"Of course, Tom. We can play some more. We are chefs. We can make anything we want. But no more celery. Okay?" she said.

Tom agreed. He did not want to eat celery ever again. He and Sara played in the kitchen and had a lot of fun. They were happy.
