One summer, two children went to the park. One was called Jack and the other was called Emily. While playing, they noticed a big pile of leaves.

Emily said, "Let's bury ourselves in the leaves!"

Jack thought it was a great idea and they both quickly began to bury themselves.

Suddenly, they heard a horrible smell. It was so disgusting that they decided to stop burying.

Jack and Emily got out of the leaves and saw a dead bird, which had been buried there a while ago.

They both looked at each other with sad eyes and realised that something once alive was now gone. 

They decided it was better to admire the beauty of nature by looking but not touching.

The moral of the story is that we should never touch or take anything from nature unless we understand what it does for us and the consequences of taking from it.

Once there was a mom and dad who had a little girl. She was 3 years old and loved playtime. One day, she asked if she could keep something she found on the ground. It was a red stone and it was very beautiful.

Her mom said, "No, that isn't yours. You can't keep it." But the little girl wanted the stone and started to cry.

But soon she got bored and wanted a new toy. She started yelling and throwing things. Her mom and dad said, "That's enough. You can't act like this. You need to quit!"

Once there was a little boy who loved playing in the park. Every day he would look around for new things to explore. One day, he heard a strange voice coming from a tall tree nearby. He looked up and saw a bird singing from a branch. He listened carefully to the bird's melodic song. The little boy stood there for a long time, listening to the voice of the bird.

The little boy couldn't help but smile. He thought the voice was so beautiful. Finally, he waved goodbye to the bird and said, "Thank you for bringing me so much joy!"

The bird replied, "Anytime, my young friend. Just remember: always take time to appreciate the beauty of nature. Don't take it for granted." 

The little boy nodded in understanding and said, "I won't forget." Then he ran off to the playground, happy and full of joy.

The moral of the story is that we should always take time to appreciate the beauty of nature. From listening to the song of a bird to admiring the skyline, looking at the natural world can bring us so much joy. When we appreciate the world around us, everything will seem a little more beautiful.

Once there was a little girl called Anna. She was only three years old and she loved to help her mom in the kitchen. One day, when Anna was in the kitchen with her mom, she saw a long cane in the corner of the room.

When the mixture was ready, Anna and her mom put some of it on a plate. It looked so yummy! Anna and her mom sat down together at the dinner table and enjoyed the delicious dinner they had cooked with the long cane.

Once upon a time there lived a little girl called Jane. Jane had a best friend who she played with every day. One day, her friend dared her to do something brave. Jane was a bit scared, but she knew she could do it.

 Jane was so happy she had taken the dare and was so proud of her brave little friend. They hugged and ran off to find their next adventure.

"Yum, yum!" Ben says. "But no key."

"Maybe the key is in another tree," Mia says. "Let's look over there."

They run to another tree and look for a key. They see a squirrel with a shiny thing in its mouth. It is a key!

"Hey, squirrel!" Ben shouts. "Give us the key!"

The squirrel looks at them and runs away. It climbs up the tree and hides in a hole.

Ben and Mia are sad. They cannot open the box. They walk back to the box and sit next to it.

"Maybe we can find another key tomorrow," Ben says.

"Or maybe the squirrel will change its mind and give us the key," Mia says.

They hug each other and smile. They are loyal to each other. They do not need a box to have fun. They have each other.

As they got closer, Timmy's mom warned him to stay away from the volcano. She said it was dangerous and could erupt at any time. Timmy listened to his mom and kept his distance.

Later that day, Timmy and his mom had a picnic. Timmy opened his lunch box and found a sandwich with disgusting green mold on it. He didn't want to eat it, so he threw it away. Timmy learned that sometimes things that look cool can be dangerous, and sometimes things that look disgusting can be harmful too.

Once upon a time there were two little mice, Bill and Dave. Bill was very curious. He liked to explore and find new things.

One day, Bill found a big folder in the corner of the room. He picked it up and shook it. It made a weird noise. He opened it and saw many strange things inside.

Bill asked Dave if he wanted to explore the folder too. Dave thought it was a crazy idea and said no. But Bill was so excited that he couldn't wait!

He took out a few things from the folder and started to replace them with other things he found around the room. He put rocks and pieces of yarn in the folder. He put coins and feathers in too.

When Dave saw what Bill was doing, he gasped. "That's crazy!" he said. "You can't keep doing that!"

Bill looked up and smiled. "Why not?" he said. "It's fun!"

Dave shook his head, but he couldn't help but smile too.

Mommy had a suggestion for her two little daughters. She wanted one of them to wear the pink dress. Her oldest daughter, Sarah, wanted to wear it, but her little sister, Ann, wanted to wear it too. 

Mommy asked "Which one of you wants to wear the pink dress?" Sarah excitedly said that she wanted to wear it, while Ann sadly said that she wanted to wear it too. 

"Do you have an idea?" Mommy asked. Sarah suggested that they both wear the dress at the same time. "That sounds like fun!" Mommy said. 

The sisters put on the dress together and ran around the house, spinning and laughing! They looked so happy in their pink dress. Mommy was glad that Sarah had suggested the idea.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Lucy. She was only three years old and full of energy. One day, Lucy's mom and dad took her to the zoo. Lucy was so excited!

First, they bought a ticket and stepped inside. Lucy looked around in wonder. Everything was so exciting and new. Everything was so big!

Next, they stepped into the penguin exhibit. There were so many penguins waddling around. Lucy was so excited and laughed with glee.

Then they stepped into the monkey exhibit. The monkeys were so playful and the air was mild. They jumped and chattered and showed off for Lucy. She laughed so hard and clapped and cheered for them.

At the end of the day, Lucy's mom and dad gave her a ticket. It was for an ice cream and Lucy was so happy. She stepped up to the counter and chose her ice-cream. 

It was a wonderful day and when Lucy stepped out of the zoo she was already asking to come back the next day!

Once there was a little dog called Max. Max was a friendly pup but was always getting into trouble. One day, Max ran out of the house and down the street. There he saw a dangerous mug. Max wanted to have a closer look and started to twist around the mug.

Suddenly, his friend Amy arrived. She shouted, "Max, what are you doing?! That mug could be very dangerous!"

Max stopped and looked at Amy. He said, "I just wanted to twist the mug around a bit. It looks like so much fun!"

Amy shook her head and said, "No! That mug is very dangerous. Let's go back home and play something safe."

Max agreed and followed Amy back home. He learned an important lesson - it's best to stay away from dangerous things!

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Lily who loved to explore. One day, she went to the forest to find a special surprise.

Soon, she spotted a diamond in a bush. She picked it up and it felt heavy in her hands. She wanted to know how much it weighed so she decided to find a weighing machine.

Lily walked to her house and asked her mom. Her mom showed her a weighing machine. Lily placed the diamond on the machine, hoping it wouldn't be too heavy.

The result was terrible - the diamond weighed a lot! Lily was surprised and amazed that a small diamond could be so heavy.

The diamond was so beautiful and special that Lily decided to keep it and take it wherever she went. From that day on, she and her diamond shared many adventurous days together.

Once there was a girl named Jill. She was 3 years old and she loved lollipops. Every day Jill and her mum would go out for a walk. They would always pick a special lollipop for Jill to enjoy. 

One day, Jill and her mum went to the park and picked a strawberry lollipop. Jill loved it! She and her mum walked around the park with it and enjoyed the sunshine. It was very healthy. 

After the walk, Jill hugged her mum and ran to their garden. She looked for a place to hide her lollipop - under a tree, between the rocks and in the flower bed. But nothing felt just right. 

Suddenly, Jill remembered the perfect place. She ran to the sandbox and buried her lollipop in the sand. She returned to her mum with a happy smile. 

Jill never forgot where she buried her lollipop. And every now and then she still goes to the sandbox and remembers that special day with her mum.

Once there was a caterpillar living in a tree. The caterpillar loved to explore and each day it crawled to a new part of the tree. One day, the caterpillar found a bright, sunny spot near a branch and decided to stay there for a while.

But soon the caterpillar started to feel uncomfortable because it was so hot, so it decided to hide in the shade. It crawled to a dark spot and started to feel better. But when the caterpillar looked around, it noticed how dry the bark was here.

The caterpillar felt sad because it knew that the tree was thirsty and needed water. So, it decided to teach its friends how to help water the tree.

The caterpillar taught its friends to be patient and wait for rain to come. When it did come, the rain would fill up the tree and make it strong and healthy. After learning the lesson, the caterpillar and its friends danced in the raindrops and felt happier than ever.

In the end, the caterpillar and its friends learned the important lesson that together they could help dry things.

Once upon a time, there was a nice lady. She had an orange in her hand. She wanted to carry it to the park.

The lady was very safe. She walked slowly so that she would not fall down. She crossed the street carefully.

When she reached the park, she saw lots of children playing. She put down the orange and said, "Who wants to have some yummy orange?"

All the children came running to the orange. They laughed and giggled as they ate the orange. The lady smiled and was happy.

The lady was happy that she had carried the orange to the park. All of the children were happy too.

Sara and Ben wanted to decorate their room. They liked to be creative and make things. They had paper, scissors, glue, and crayons. They also had a measure. It was a long tape with numbers on it.

They decided to make a paper chain. They used the measure to cut the paper into strips. They made the strips different colors. Then they glued the ends of the strips together to make circles. They put one circle inside another circle and glued them again. They did this until they had a long chain.

They hung the chain on the wall. They also made some stars and flowers with the paper and crayons. They glued them on the chain and on the wall. They were very happy with their decoration. They showed it to their mom and dad. Mom and dad said they were very creative and proud of them. Sara and Ben smiled and hugged them. They liked to decorate their room.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play in the water. One day, he went to the river with his mom. Timmy saw some ducks swimming in the river. He wanted to play with them. So, he jumped into the water and started to splash around. 

His mom said, "Be careful, Timmy. Don't splash too much." 

But Timmy didn't listen. He splashed and splashed until he got tired. Then, his mom took him out of the water and they went home. 

For dinner, Timmy's mom made some rice. Timmy loved rice. He ate it all up and felt very calm and happy. He said to his mom, "Thank you for the rice. It was yummy." And his mom smiled and said, "You're welcome, Timmy. I'm glad you liked it."

Peter was so excited! He had been playing with his friends all day and now they were taking a walk near the woods. When they arrived, they saw a big stream with many stones on one side.

Peter asked his friends if they wanted to go and explore. His friends said no, so Peter went by himself. As he stepped onto the stones, he slid on one and landed in the stream!

At first he was scared, but then he saw something cute swimming around in the water. It was a small frog!

Peter wanted to pick it up but the frog refused. He tried again, but the frog refused. He decided to accept what the frog refused and let it stay in the stream.

So then he just played in the stream and watched the small frog hopping around.

The moral of the story is that sometimes it is important to accept other peoples' wishes and respect their refusal.

Once upon a time, there was a big and strong bear. He was walking through the forest and he found something shiny on the ground. He stopped and stared at it. It was a big mineral! The bear was excited. He wanted to pick it up and show it to the other animals in the forest.

He reached out and grabbed it with his paw. But, it was too heavy for him. He could not lift it.

He just stood there, staring at it. He thought and thought about how he could get the mineral out of the ground. Suddenly, an idea came to him. He lay down on the ground and he blew and blew really hard. Suddenly, the mineral popped out of the ground! The bear was so excited.

He looked around and saw a big bird in the sky. He waved up at the bird and yelled "Come down and help me!" The big bird landed next to the bear and, together, they managed to pick up the big mineral and carry it away. 

The bear shouted and laughed all the way home. Everyone in the forest was so happy to get the big mineral.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved playing outside in the sunshine. One day, she found a delicate flower in her garden. She picked it up and showed it to her friend, Timmy.

Timmy said, "I want to destroy the flower!"

Lily said, "No, that's not nice. The flower is beautiful and we should take care of it."

Timmy didn't listen and tried to destroy the flower. But Lily stopped him and told him that it's not good to destroy things that are delicate and beautiful. She taught him that we should always take care of nature and not harm it. From that day on, Timmy learned to appreciate the beauty of nature and the importance of taking care of it.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. Her name was Lila. She was playing in her garden one day when a stranger came for a visit. Lila was very scared and started to cry. 

The stranger saw her and said, "What's wrong?"

Lila said, "I'm scared! Who are you?"

The stranger replied, "I'm just a kind stranger. I want to help you." 

Lila wiped her tears away and said, "Will you carry me away from here?"

The stranger smiled and said, "Yes, I'll carry you away from this miserable place!" He picked up Lila in his arms and slowly carried her away into the distance. 

The end.

Louis had a plan. He wanted to visit all the places that he knew. He had a regular, everyday packed lunch. Inside, he had jam sandwiches, a special treat. 

So, Louis set off. He visited his house, and then he went to the park to play. He saw the swings, and he went on all of them. He even made a sand castle with his friends. 

Louis visited the beach next. He looked for all the shells he could find, and he put them into a big pile. When he was done it almost looked like a castle. 

Then, Louis visited his favourite place, the grocery store. He ate some free samples and picked up some jam for his sandwiches. He was smiling all the way home. 

At the end of the day, Louis realised that he had a great day. He was so happy he had decided to visit all of his favourite places.

Once upon a time, there was a little cat who was very troubled. She wanted something to eat, so she went exploring around her house. As she looked around, she suddenly felt the ground trembling beneath her feet. After a while, the trembling stopped, and the cat spotted a sandwich on the floor.

The cat was very excited. She quickly ran towards the sandwich and started to eat it. It was so delicious! Her tummy felt full and the cat was very content.

But then something strange happened. The cat started to feel a strange trembling again. At first it was slow, but soon it was very fast. The cat felt scared, so she quickly ran out of the house.

The cat waited outside until the trembling stopped. Then she sighed with relief. From now on, she would always be careful when looking for food.

Once upon a time, there was a harbor. It was very big and impressive. In this harbor, there lived a special family of ducks. These ducks loved to share. Every day, the ducks would share their food and their fun with all the other animals. 

One day, a fisherman sailed his boat out to the harbor. As he sailed, he noticed the ducks happily sharing all the things around them. He was very impressed. He had never seen ducks like that before. He knew then he had found a very special place.

The fisherman shared his story with a special friend. Soon, lots of people came to the harbor to meet the ducks and learn their secret. Everyone was very impressed. 

The harbor and the ducks had plenty of love, food and fun to share. Everyone who visited the harbor was happy, and everyone left feeling full of joy. 
The harbor was forever known as the Sharing Harbor - the place to be for love, food and fun!

One hot day, Joe was outside playing in the sun. Suddenly, he heard something in the distance. Joe slowly crept to look, and he saw a cool monkey! Joe was very excited and ran over to the monkey. He said, "Hello, Monkey! My name is Joe. What are you doing?" 

The monkey replied, "I'm washing in the river. It's a great way to stay cool in this heat!" Joe was curious and asked, "Can I wash too?" The monkey smiled and said, "Of course! Come join me!" 

So Joe and the monkey washed in the river together. Joe was laughing and having such a great time that time flew by. Joe looked up and realized he had to go home, but he said goodbye and thanked the monkey for the cool adventure.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved eating soup, especially chicken noodle soup. One day, Lily's mom made her a big bowl of soup for lunch. But when Lily took a bite, she started to shiver because the soup was too hot. 

Lily's mom blew on the soup to cool it down, and then Lily took another bite. This time, the soup was just right and it tasted delicious. Lily ate the whole bowl and felt very happy. 

Later that day, Lily and her mom went to the park to play. They saw a squirrel running around and doing crazy things. The squirrel was jumping from tree to tree and even doing flips in the air. Lily thought it was so funny and she laughed and laughed. 

After a fun day at the park, Lily went to bed feeling warm and cozy. She thought about the yummy soup and the silly squirrel and felt very happy.

Once upon a time, there was a big, tall tower. Inside the tower, there lived a kind girl named Lily. She liked to play with her toys and have fun with her friends.

One sunny day, Lily saw her friend, Tim, playing with an interesting toy. She wanted to play with it too. She asked Tim, "Can you lend me your toy, please?" Tim said, "Yes, you can play with my toy."

Lily and Tim played with the interesting toy near the tower. They had so much fun together. After playing, they said goodbye and went back to their homes. Lily was happy that Tim lent her the toy, and they became best friends.

Tom and Lily were playing pirates on the beach. They had a big boat made of sand and sticks. They had a flag with a skull and a hat with a feather. They also had an anchor made of a rock and a rope.

"Ahoy, matey!" Tom said to Lily. "We are the best pirates in the world! We can find treasure and fight sharks!"

"Arrr!" Lily said. "But we need to be careful. There are other pirates who want to steal our boat and our treasure. Look, there is one over there!" She pointed to a boy who was walking with a bucket and a shovel.

Tom and Lily grabbed their sticks and ran to the boy. They pretended to be very angry and scary.

"Stop, you scurvy dog!" Tom shouted. "This is our boat and our treasure! Go away or we will make you walk the plank!"

The boy looked surprised and scared. He dropped his bucket and shovel and ran away.

"Ha ha ha!" Tom and Lily laughed. "We scared him away! We are so strong and brave!"

They went back to their boat and lifted their anchor. They pretended to sail away to find more treasure.

But then they heard a loud voice.

"Tom! Lily! Time to go home!" It was their mom. She was standing on the shore.

Tom and Lily looked at each other. They did not want to go home. They wanted to play more.

"Can we play a little more, mom?" Tom asked.

"Please, mom?" Lily added.

Their mom shook her head. "No, you can't. It's getting cold and dark. You need to come home and have dinner and a bath. Come on, hurry up!"

Tom and Lily sighed. They knew they had to obey their mom. They dropped their anchor and their sticks. They took off their flag and their hat. They said goodbye to their boat.

"Bye bye, boat!" Tom said.

"Bye bye, treasure!" Lily said.

They ran to their mom and hugged her. She smiled and kissed them.

"Did you have fun, my little pirates?" She asked.

"Yes, mom, we did!" Tom and Lily said.

They told her about their adventure and how they scared away the other pirate.

Their mom listened and nodded. She was proud of them.

"You are very strong and brave, my little pirates!" She said. "But now you need to be very quiet and still. Do you know why?"

Tom and Lily shook their head.

"Because it's time to freeze!" Their mom said.

She tickled them and they laughed. They pretended to freeze like statues.

They played freeze until they reached their car. Then they got in and drove home.

They had a warm dinner and a hot bath. They put on their pajamas and brushed their teeth. They went to bed and cuddled with their mom.

She read them a story about pirates and treasure. She kissed them goodnight and turned off the light.

Tom and Lily closed their eyes and dreamed of their boat and their adventure.

They were happy. They were the best pirates in the world.

Once upon a time there was a sad home. Everyone living there felt alone. The sky was grey and the sun was hiding. No one had energy for anything.

One day, a curious bird flew by the sad home. It peeked inside the windows and saw something strange. It was a tiny girl, dancing and singing! She was happy and full of fun. The bird watched her smile, wondering why nobody in the sad home was happy like her. 

So the curious bird flew down and landed near the tiny girl. It asked her if she would like to come fly away with it and explore the world outside. The tiny girl said yes!

They both flew over the sad home, leaving it behind. Everywhere they went the girl smiled and laughed. She was no longer sad. The curious bird had changed her world forever.

Once there was a kid who wanted to dive. He ran to the pool, but it was closed. He was so sad. He sat and watched the water, wishing he could swim.

Then he noticed a bad man. The man was walking towards the pool. The kid was scared and ran away. He hid behind a tree and watched.

The bad man opened the pool and jumped in. Then he started swimming and diving. The kid was so excited to see the bad man dive. He wanted to do it too.

The bad man swam away, and the kid ran to the pool. He jumped in and started to dive. He dived up and down, over and under the water. He was having so much fun! Finally, the kid smiled and said, â€œI can dive!â€

Emily was a little 3 year old girl. One day, she went outside to play. She looked up at the sky and it was a bright summer day. The sun was shining and it was very hot.

But then, Emily saw a fan. It was blowing the cool breeze around her. She loved to play in the cold air. She reached up and grabbed the fan. She smiled as she felt the air blowing on her face.

Emily looked around and saw that the other kids were enjoying themselves too. They were playing sports and having fun in the sun. But Emily was content just playing with the fan. It was just what she needed to stay cool in the hot summer weather.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she decided to create a special dessert for her mom. She picked some cherries from the tree and mixed them with sugar and milk. Her mom was happy and said, "This is delicious, Lily! You are a great chef!"

But then, something serious happened. Lily's little brother, Jack, came running into the kitchen and accidentally knocked over the dessert. Lily was very upset and cried, "Oh no! My dessert is ruined!"

Her mom tried to comfort her and said, "It's okay, Lily. We can clean it up and make another one tomorrow." But Lily was still sad and didn't want to make another dessert. She went to bed feeling very disappointed that her hard work had been destroyed.

Once there was a lonely bird in the sky. He flew around aimlessly, looking for a friend. He had been flying for hours and still hadn't found someone.

Then one day, he saw a pencil on the ground below him. He flew down and landed beside the pencil. He was very excited!

The bird said to the pencil, "Hello! Are you a friend?"

The pencil just lay there. So, the bird asked again. "Do you want to play with me?"

The pencil just stayed there on the ground. The lonely bird felt very sad. He wanted someone to talk and play with. 

So, the bird decided to do something. He picked up the pencil with his feet and shoot it very high into the sky. He watched as it flew higher and higher until it became a tiny speck in the sky.

The bird smiled, knowing that the pencil was happy and no longer lonely. He flew away contentedly, back to his own life.

Lily and Ben were playing with marbles on the floor. They had many marbles of different colors and sizes. They liked to roll them and make them hit each other.

"Look, I have a big red marble. It is mighty. It can knock down all your marbles," Ben said. He rolled his red marble and hit Lily's blue marble. Lily's blue marble rolled away.

"That is not nice, Ben. You should share your marbles and play fair," Lily said. She was sad and angry.

"I don't want to share. I want to win. My red marble is the best," Ben said. He rolled his red marble again and hit Lily's green marble. Lily's green marble rolled away.

Lily had only one marble left. It was a small yellow marble. She did not think it was mighty. She thought it was weak. She wanted to cry.

But then she had an idea. She picked up her yellow marble and poked Ben's red marble with it. Ben's red marble did not roll. It cracked.

"Hey, what did you do? You broke my red marble. That is not fair," Ben said. He was shocked and sad.

"I poked it. You said it was mighty, but it was not. It was fragile. You should not be mean and boastful. You should be kind and humble," Lily said. She felt sorry for Ben, but also proud of her yellow marble.

Ben looked at his broken red marble and then at Lily's yellow marble. He realized that he was wrong. He said sorry to Lily and asked her to be his friend. Lily smiled and said yes. They hugged and shared their marbles. They learned that size and color do not matter. What matters is how you treat others.

Once upon a time there were two friends, a bear and a monkey. One day, the bear was feeling a little worried. He wanted a banana but he didn't know where to find one. So, the monkey suggested they go to the nearby park and find a banana tree.

The bear and the monkey were very careful as they made their way to the park. Once they got there, the bear was so excited! He spotted a banana tree! The bear quickly picked some bananas and put them into his pocket.

The monkey and the bear chatted as they made their way home. The bear was so happy he had some bananas and he no longer had to worry. They had a great day and the bear was very thankful to his friend for helping him find the banana tree.

Once upon a time, there was a bald man named Bob. Bob went to check his mailbox and found a big envelope inside. He opened it and saw a letter from the bank. The letter said he owed them a lot of money.

Bob started to panic and didn't know what to do. He went to his friend, Timmy, and showed him the letter. Timmy said, "Don't worry, we can help you. Let's call the bank and ask for help."

Bob felt better and they called the bank. The bank explained everything to them and they made a plan to pay the money back slowly. Bob was happy and thanked Timmy for his help.

Once there was a family who lived by the harbor. They liked to watch the ships come and go every day. But something was missing. One of the family members was deaf. They could not hear the ships as they sailed past. They would watch the ships and miss their sound.

One sunny day something special happened. The family decided to go to the harbor. The deaf family member felt the gentle breeze and the sun on their face. They smiled and felt the water on their feet.

When they got back home they felt so happy! They enjoyed the trip to the harbor and could hear the sound of the ships too. But something still felt missing. They missed the noise of the ships when they weren't there. 

So the family went back to the harbor. Every day they would return and watch the ships come and go. The deaf family member felt the same gentle breeze and the sun on their face. They smiled and felt the same water on their feet. The family was so happy because now everyone could hear the ships, even the deaf family member.

Once there was a boy named Paul who was only three years old. One day, Paul was playing in the backyard when he spotted a big mound of icy snow. 

"Can I play with it?" Paul asked his dad.

"Sure," said his dad. Paul was so excited. He rolled around the icy snow, laughing and feeling so free.

But then, suddenly, there was a loud crash. His dad hadn't seen the old wall that Paul was playing near and he crashed into it with the tractor. The wall was left with a big crack in it.

"Oh no," gasped Paul's dad. He went over to the wall and tried to restore it. But no matter what he did, the crack still remained.

Paul felt so bad and he wanted to help. He slowly walked over to the wall and carefully placed the icy snow all around it.

His dad beamed at him and smiled. With the snow in place, the wall was restored. The score was 1 for Paul and 0 for the wall.

Paul and his dad hugged and Paul smiled with pride. He had saved the day.

Once upon a time, there was a dependable dog named Spot. Spot loved to play with his friends in the park. They would run, jump, and have lots of fun.

One day, Spot found a big bag of rice. He thought it would be fun to bury the rice and play a game with his friends. So, he dug a big hole and put the rice in it. Then, he covered it with dirt.

Spot called his friends to play a game of finding the rice. They all looked and looked, but they could not find it. Finally, Spot showed them where the rice was. They all laughed and had a great time. Spot was a very dependable friend.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Jack and Jill. They were very close and liked to do everything together. Every day, they would play in the park down the street and chat with all their friends.

One day, they were playing and having a lot of fun when Jack decided he wanted to try something new. He ran over to an old tire, pushed it over on its side, and started teasing Jill with it. She laughed and rolled the tire back and forth, teasing Jack with it.

The tire was unique because it was very old and had lots of patches and words written on it. Jack and Jill kept playing together with the tire until they got tired out and had to go home. They had a lot of fun with the tire and thought of lots of different ways to use it.

They kept playing and having fun together for a long time, and always remembered the unique tire.

One day, a little boy named Tim went for a walk with his mom. They went to a big park. In the park, they saw a man giving away pretty rocks. The man was very generous.

Tim asked the man, "What are these rocks?" The man replied, "These are special rocks called minerals. They come from the ground and are very pretty."

Tim's mom said, "Thank you for the pretty rocks." The man smiled and replied, "You're welcome. I hope you like them." Tim and his mom went home with their new minerals and had a fun day at the park.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Jill. She was so full of life and energy that she never sat still! 

One day, Jill's mother gave her some colorful dough and asked her to play with it. "Please don't go too fast," her mom cautioned. 

Jill agreed, but as soon as Mom left the room, she started rolling the dough across the floor. She made a game of seeing who could make their dough move the fastest! 

When Mom came back in the room, she saw Jill with dough all over her dress and scattered on the floor. â€œWhat happened?â€ Mom asked. Jill, feeling embarrassed, told her mother the truth. 

Mom smiled and said something important, â€œJill, it's ok to want to speed up sometimes, but know that it's best to go slow. That way you can take the time to do a good job and make sure everything is the way you want it.â€ 

Jill understood and learned her lesson: impatience may not yield the best results. She now always remembers to go slow and the results are much more colorful!

Once upon a time, there was a kind and friendly dog named Max. Max loved to play fetch with his ball in the backyard. One day, Max's owner asked him to help with the dishes. Max didn't know what to do, so his owner showed him the dishwasher. Max was amazed by the dishwasher and watched as his owner put the dishes inside.

Suddenly, Max saw a knife on the counter and tried to play with it. His owner quickly stopped him and said, "No, Max! Knives are sharp and can cut you." Max was sad that he couldn't play with the knife, but he was happy to help with the dishes. He watched as the dishwasher cleaned the dishes and made them shiny and clean. From that day on, Max loved to help his owner with the dishwasher and never played with knives again.

Once there was a boy who wanted to make the world a better place. He decided to start with his house. He thought of one way he could do this.

He walked to the table and looked around. He wanted to help his family and decided that covering the table would be helpful. He found a big, colorful blanket and he carefully spread it out on the table.

The blanket made the table look cozy and he was very proud of himself. He thought it was the best way to help his family.

The family was very happy with the boy and thanked him for being so helpful. They hugged him and all enjoyed their dinner together with the cozy table.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to play dress up with her dolls. She would put on fancy dresses and pretend to go to parties.

One day, Lily's mommy brought home a magazine with lots of pretty pictures. Lily loved looking at the pictures and pointing out all the colors.

Later that day, Lily's mommy told her they were going to a special party. Lily was so excited and couldn't wait to dress up in her prettiest dress. But when they got to the party, everyone was wearing normal clothes. Lily was surprised but still had fun playing games and eating cake.

From then on, Lily learned that sometimes it's okay to dress up and be fancy, but it's also important to be normal and have fun just being yourself.

Molly was a regular girl who loved to play all day. Her favorite toy was True, a stuffed puppy that she always kept close. Whenever True wasn't around, Molly would miss him.

One day, Molly decided to take True outside to play. She ran and jumped, playing tag with True, up and down the street.

Soon, it was time to go home, so Molly hugged True and began to walk back. As they walked, Molly realized something! She had left True at the park. Molly was so sad, she missed him already.

Molly ran back to the park as fast as she could. When she arrived, Molly saw True, right where she had left him. She scooped him up in her arms, and thanked the stars she was able to find him.

Molly was so glad True was safe and with her. She never wanted to miss him ever again.

Harry the hare loved to hide. He would find a spot to hide and count to ten before he would pop up, thinking he was being sneaky. One day, he was outside, looking to hide, when he saw something colorful and shiny on the ground. It was a piece of gum! He immediately wanted it, but it looked so fake. He knew it wasn't real, so he decided to hide it in case someone else wanted it. But, suddenly, he had an even better idea. He picked up the gum and hid in the closest bush, then he started counting. Just a few seconds later, a rabbit hopped by and stopped right in front of the bush. Harry giggled and shouted, "Boo!" The rabbit was so scared that it hopped away, leaving the gum behind. Harry had found the perfect hiding spot! He kept the gum, and he had learned a new way to have fun and maybe even get a sweet treat.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to sing and dance all day long. One day, her mommy came to her and said, "Lily, I will teach you how to bake a cake today!" Lily was so excited! 

Her mommy told her to get a bowl and put some flour and sugar in it. Then, she told her to crack some eggs and mix everything together. Lily was a little confused, but her mommy told her to keep trying and not to give up. 

After some time, the cake was ready! It looked so brilliant and smelled so yummy! Lily was so proud of herself and she told her mommy, "Thank you for teaching me how to bake a cake!" Her mommy smiled and told her, "You did a great job, Lily. I'm so proud of you!"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to dance and listen to music. One day, she heard some jazz music coming from a distant place. She wanted to move her body to the beat of the music, so she asked her mommy if they could go there.

"Mommy, can we go there? I want to move my body to the jazz music," Lily said.

"Sure, let's go there!" said Mommy.

So, they went to the distant place where the jazz music was playing. When they arrived, Lily saw people dancing and moving to the beat of the music. She joined them and danced happily. She loved the jazz music and the way it made her feel. 

After a while, they went back home. Lily was tired but happy. She told her mommy, "I love jazz music. It makes me want to move and dance all day long!"

Mum and Dad were so happy, because they had a new baby! Everyone knew the baby's name was Sam.

Mum sent Sam off to the park. He was so excited! He felt the wind in his hair, which made him giggle.

But something was strange. Everything was so quiet. Sam looked around, but all he saw was silence. He called out to his Mum, but all he heard was deafening silence. 

"Mum? Where are you?" he asked.

Suddenly, a voice filled the air. It was Mum's voice. 

"I'm here, Sam," she said. "You won't see me, but I'm here. I'm sending you lots of love."

Sam smiled. He knew he was surrounded by Mum's love, even when things were silent.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She went to a breakfast place with her mom. Lily's mom asked, "What do you want to eat, Lily?" Lily said, "I want sausage and eggs." 

The waiter came and said, "Good morning! What can I serve you?" Lily's mom said, "We want two plates of sausage and eggs, please." 

When the food came, Lily was so excited to eat the sausage. She picked it up with her hands and it was messy. Lily's mom said, "Use your fork and knife, Lily. Don't be messy." 

Lily ate her sausage and eggs with her fork and knife. She said, "Yummy! I like sausage." Her mom said, "I'm glad you like it, Lily." They finished their breakfast and went home. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She had a yellow measuring tape. She went around measuring things in the house. She had lots of fun measuring the sofa, the windows, and her dad's shoes.

Then, one day she saw a pastry. It was a big, yellow pastry. She decided to measure it. She took out her measuring tape and measured the pastry all the way around. It was two inches thick and six inches long.

The little girl smiled. She loved measuring things. She measured the pastry one more time just to be sure. When she was done, she put the measuring tape back in its box and went off to play.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She liked to help her mom in the kitchen. Her mom would give her an apron to wear so she wouldn't get her clothes dirty. One day, Lily was helping her mom make cookies. She was so excited to mix the dough and put it in the oven. 

Suddenly, Lily slipped on a piece of flour on the floor. She fell down, but she wasn't hurt. Her mom helped her up and asked if she was okay. Lily said yes and continued to help her mom. 

After the cookies were done baking, Lily's mom gave her a cool cookie to eat. Lily was happy and felt proud that she could help her mom make something yummy. From that day on, Lily always made sure to be careful and watch out for anything slippery on the floor.

Tom liked to visit his uncle Ben. Uncle Ben had a big house with many toys and books. Uncle Ben was kind and funny. He always played with Tom and told him stories.

One night, Tom slept over at uncle Ben's house. He had his own room with a soft bed and a night light. The night light was a star that glowed in the dark. Tom liked the star. It made him feel safe and happy.

But Tom could not sleep. He heard a strange noise outside his window. He was scared. He got out of bed and looked out. He saw a big, bright ball in the sky. It glowed more than the star. It moved fast and made a loud sound.

Tom ran to uncle Ben's room. He knocked on the door and cried. Uncle Ben opened the door and hugged Tom. He asked him what was wrong. Tom told him about the ball in the sky. Uncle Ben smiled and took Tom to the window.

He pointed at the ball and said, "That is not a ball, Tom. That is a plane. A plane is a big machine that can fly. People use planes to travel far away. The plane glows because it has lights. The lights help the pilot see at night. The plane makes a loud sound because it has engines. The engines help the plane go fast."

Tom looked at the plane and listened to uncle Ben. He felt better. He understood what the plane was. He was not scared anymore. He thanked uncle Ben and gave him a kiss. Uncle Ben took Tom back to his room and tucked him in. He turned on the star and said, "Good night, Tom. I love you. Sleep well."

Tom smiled and said, "Good night, uncle Ben. I love you too. Thank you for the star and the plane." He closed his eyes and fell asleep. He dreamed of flying with uncle Ben in a plane that glowed.

Jake was a three year old boy who loved robots. One day he was walking in the dark when he heard a voice. A robot was speaking. 

The robot said, "Hello there! Who are you?"

Jake was so surprised that he couldn't speak at first. But then he said, "Hi! I'm Jake." 

The robot asked him, "Jake, would you like to come and play with me?"

Jake was very excited and said, "Yes, I would love that!" He followed the robot until they arrived at a bright garden. There were many fun things to do and the two of them played games together until it was time for Jake to go home. 

Jake thanked the robot and said goodbye. He waved as he walked away, feeling very happy that he had made a new friend.

Once upon a time there was a cow named Spot. Spot lived in a big, old barn with lots of other animals. One day, Spot felt very lonely. She wished she had a friend to talk to. 

That's when she saw a small blue bird perched on the barn door. Spot felt hopeful and said "Hello, birdie." The blue bird said "Hello, Spot. Where have you been?". Spot told the bird all about her time in the barn.

The thoughtful bird listened to all of Spot's stories, and Spot felt so much better for having a friend to listen.

From that day, Spot and the blue bird were best friends. Whenever Spot felt lonely, she would talk to her friend and feel hopeful again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play at the park with her friends. One day, Lily and her friend Timmy were playing on the swings when they saw a funny looking pole. 

Lily asked Timmy, "What is that silly pole doing here?" Timmy replied, "I don't know, maybe it's for the birds to sit on." Lily thought that was a foolish idea, but she didn't say anything. 

As they continued to play, Lily's mom called out to her, "Lily, it's time to go home now." Lily said goodbye to Timmy and ran over to her mom. "Mommy, did you see the funny pole at the park?" she asked. 

Her mom smiled and said, "Yes, I saw it. It's called a flagpole and it's used to hold up a flag." Lily was amazed and asked, "Can we come back to the park tomorrow and see the flag on the pole?" Her mom nodded and they walked home together, happy and excited for their next trip to the park.

Sara and Tom are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big truck with a cage on it. Inside the cage, there are some animals. Sara and Tom run to the truck to look at the animals.

"Wow, look at that lion!" Tom says. "He is so big and strong. I admire him."

"Yes, he is amazing," Sara says. "But he looks sad. Why is he in a cage?"

The truck driver hears them and comes to talk to them. He is wearing a uniform and a hat. He smiles at Sara and Tom.

"Hello, kids. Do you like the animals?" he asks.

"Yes, we do," Sara and Tom say.

"These animals are from the zoo. I am taking them to a new home. They will have more space and friends there. They are not happy in the zoo. The zoo is like a jail for them," the truck driver explains.

"Oh, I see. That is good," Sara says.

"Can we see the other animals?" Tom asks.

"Sure, come with me. I will show you," the truck driver says.

He leads them to the other side of the truck. There, they see a giraffe, a zebra, a monkey, and a parrot. Sara and Tom are amazed by the different colors and shapes of the animals.

"Look at that parrot!" Sara says. "He is so pretty. He has red and blue and green feathers. Can he talk?"

"Yes, he can. His name is Coco. He likes to say hello and sing songs. Do you want to hear him?" the truck driver asks.

"Yes, please!" Sara and Tom say.

The truck driver opens the cage and takes out Coco. He puts him on his shoulder and says, "Hello, Coco. Say hello to the kids."

"Hello, hello, hello!" Coco says. He flaps his wings and makes a funny noise.

Sara and Tom laugh. They think Coco is very smart and funny. They want to play with him more.

"Can we hold him?" Sara asks.

"Sure, but be gentle. He is very friendly, but he can bite if he is scared," the truck driver says.

He gives Coco to Sara. Sara holds him carefully and strokes his feathers. Coco likes Sara. He says, "Pretty, pretty, pretty!"

Sara smiles. She feels happy. She says, "Thank you, Coco. You are pretty, too."

Tom waits for his turn. He wants to hold Coco, too. He admires Coco's colors and voice. He hopes Coco will like him, too.

The end.

Once upon a time, there lived a girl named Lucy. She was very brave and she liked to explore new things. One day, she saw a strange robot in her garden. It was different from the other robots she had seen before.

Lucy went closer to the robot and began to touch it. She felt something strange and pulled her hand back. The robot started moving and it frightened her. 

"Don't be scared," the robot said. "I am here to help you. I can make your garden safe and help you with your chores."

Lucy felt relieved. She knew she could count on the robot to help her. She asked the robot if it could start working and it agreed.

Lucy soon realised her mistake and she started to regret not being more careful. She knew she should have been more careful around robots. Lucy promised to always be safe when she was near robots.

The end.

Lily and Sam were best friends. They liked to play with dolls and cars and blocks. One day, they went to the park with their moms. There were many other kids there. Some of them were nice, but some of them were mean.

A group of mean kids came to Lily and Sam. They took their dolls and cars and blocks. They laughed and ran away. Lily and Sam were very upset. They cried and hugged each other. Their moms came and saw what happened. They were angry and sad.

The moms went to the group of mean kids. They told them to give back the toys. They told them to say sorry. They told them to be kind. The mean kids were scared. They did not want to get in trouble. They gave back the toys. They said sorry. They looked down.

Lily and Sam got their toys back. They were happy. They thanked their moms. They decided to play somewhere else. They found a nice spot under a tree. They played with their dolls and cars and blocks. They smiled and laughed. They shook hands and said, "We are best friends."

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Joey. He lived in a big house with his mom and dad. 
One day, Joey wanted a nice new toy. But a new toy was very expensive! His mom and dad said no.

That made Joey very sad and he started to cry. Then his mom had an idea. She said they could play a game. If Joey won the game, he would get a nice reward - he could have the toy he wanted!

So they all played a game. Joey worked very hard, but he couldn't win the game. His mom and dad said no toy.

Joey didn't give up. He kept fighting for the toy. He wanted it so badly! And in the end he won the game. 

His mom and dad were very proud of him. They gave him the reward he fought for - the new toy! Joey was so happy. He had his expensive new toy!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in her backyard, but one day she saw a rat! She didn't like rats because they were dirty and scary. 

Lily went to her mom and said, "Mommy, I saw a rat in the backyard! It's not clean!" Her mom said, "Don't worry, Lily. I'll clean it up." 

After her mom cleaned up the backyard, Lily went outside to play. But she saw another rat! She went back to her mom and complained, "Mommy, there's another rat! I don't like rats!" 

Her mom said, "I understand, Lily. But remember, rats are also living creatures. We have to be kind to them too." From that day on, Lily tried to be kind to all animals, even rats.

Once upon a time, a mom and her two little ones were playing together. The two little ones were silly and laughing a lot.

The mom had a secret to reveal just for the two little ones. She took out a bandana. It was a special tie with lots of bright colors.

The two little ones were so excited. They wanted to know more about the surprise.

The mom told them a story about following a rainbow to the pot of gold. She told them that the tie was the special key.

The little ones looked confused, so mom was able to reveal to them that the tie was used to open the pot of gold. The two little ones were filled with excitement and delight.

The mom then tied the bandana around the two little ones. As the tie was fastened tight, the two little ones were filled with joy and excitement.

The end.

Once upon a time there lived a kind and generous lady. One day she felt sick, but she was not worried. She had some special medicine that she could spray.

The lady found the medicine and sprayed it onto her cheek. Soon enough it made her feel much better. She was so happy!

"Whoever invented this medicine was very clever," the lady said.

Just then an angel appeared in a blaze of light. "Thank you for your kind words!" said the angel. "I invented the medicine. I knew it would help you get better."

The lady was so grateful for the angel's generous gift. She thanked the angel and asked if there was anything she could do to repay the favour.

"Oh no," said the angel, who then flew away. "You have already repaid me by feeling better."

The lady smiled, knowing that she had been helped by a very generous guardian angel.

Once upon a time, there lived a bad ostrich. All the other animals in the jungle admired it because it was so beautiful. Every day, the ostrich would go for a stroll in the jungle and it was very happy.

One day, an elephant wanted to admire the ostrich too. So it started following the ostrich while it walked around the jungle. The ostrich did not know why, so it started running away. The elephant kept trying to catch up with the ostrich, but it was too slow.

Just then, the ostrich saw a small bird. It flew so fast and it was so pretty. The ostrich was so amazed that it stopped running. The elephant was happy too and it stopped following the ostrich. 

The ostrich and the small bird admired each other for a little while before flying away in different directions. The ostrich felt so much better now that it was away from the bad elephant. It knew that it was back to its old self again.

Once upon a time there was a mean, old lady. She did not like to be kind or compassionate to anyone. She only cared about one thing - measuring. She measured everything, from the trees to the sky, from the raindrops to the clouds. 

One day, she saw a little girl, who was trying to fold a piece of paper. The old lady wanted to measure the paper, even though it was too small for her to bother with. The little girl was frightened, and she said no. But the old lady wouldn't listen, and she tried to take the paper anyway.

The little girl, in desperation, picked up her most precious possession - a tiny paper doll - and ran away. The old lady chased after her and finally caught her, but the little girl thanked her for the wrong thing. Instead of thanking the old lady for trying to measure the paper, she thanked her for being so compassionate.

The old lady was furious, and decided to punish the little girl by taking away her paper doll. The little girl cried and pleaded, but the old lady wouldn't listen. The old lady took away the paper doll and never gave it back. The little girl never saw her most precious possession again.

Once there was an ugly pupil. He was very sad because he never felt like he belonged at school. One day, he was sitting alone playing with his blocks when the teacher saw him. 

The teacher walked over and said: "Why are you so sad?"

The pupil looked up and said: "I don't fit in here. Nobody likes me".

The teacher smiled and said: "You belong here just like everyone else. I can provide you with a special friend who can be your buddy. That way you're never alone!"

The pupil was so happy. He now had a new friend to play with at school. 

The moral of the story is: everybody needs someone to provide a little companionship - otherwise it can be a very lonely experience!

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Mia. She had a boo-boo on her hand and it was very sore. 

Mia asked her mom for a bandage for her sore hand. Her mom said, "No, you don't need one, sweetie. It will heal on its own". 

But Mia kept insisting for a bandage. "Mommy, please? Please can I have a bandage?" she asked her mother. 

Finally, her mom gave in. She found a different bandage, much different than the regular ones. It had sparkles and pictures on it. 

Mia was so excited and happy. She put the bandage on her sore hand and showed it off to everyone! 

The end.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Susie. She had a very special toy, a soft bear with a shiny red bow. Every day, Susie would spin around and around holding the bear in her arms, feeling the wind in her hair and giggling with delight. As she spun, she always remembered the happy memories of playing with her bear.

One day, Susie decided to take her beloved bear to the park. As she ran around with her toy in her arms, Susie felt so excited she couldn't sit still. She held up her bear and began to spin faster and faster, becoming dizzy and laughing with joy. 

The memories she had of playing with her bear were now stronger and brighter than ever before. Susie knew that these would always be her happy memories no matter what. The feeling of spinning with the bear in her hands would stay with her forever!

Once upon a time there was a tall mommy. She loved to tell stories. Every night she would tell a special story to her 3 year old daughter. 
"Tonight I will tell you a very special story," the mommy said. 
The 3 year old's eyes lit up with excitement. 
So the mommy began to tell her daughter a story about a magical land filled with beautiful creatures. 
As the mommy told the story, her daughter's imagination ran wild. She imagined the creatures with bright colors, big wings and giant horns. 
The mommy's story was filled with so many exciting details that the 3 year old was soon lost in the magic of it all. 
When the mommy was done telling her story, the daughter thanked her for the wonderful experience. 
She felt so lucky to have such a tall mommy who could tell such stories.

Johnathan was a 3 year old boy who liked to go outside and play. One day he went to the park with his mom and dad. As he was running around and playing, he tripped and fell down in front of a lot of people. Everyone started laughing at him and he felt embarrassed.

Johnathan's mom and dad saw what had happened and were quick to help him up. They gave him a hug and told him that it was ok and that everyone slips up sometimes.

Johnathan felt better knowing his mom and dad were there for him. He realized that life can be a little embarrassing at times, but itâ€™s useful to know you can rely on your family for love and support.

Johnathan decided to never forget the lesson he learned that day at the park: life can be scary, but family is always there to help you.

Molly and her mom were spending the day together. Molly wanted to pick out an interesting sweater from the store. Her mom suggested getting a colorful one that had rainbow stripes. Molly was excited and couldn't wait to try it on. She quickly grabbed the sweater, and put it on her.

When she looked in the mirror, she smiled as she admired how colorful the sweater was. Then, Molly asked her mom to suggest a place to go wearing her new sweater. Mom thought for a moment, before suggesting the park. Molly thought this was an interesting idea, so she agreed to go. 

At the park, Molly had so much fun wearing her new sweater. She ran around, jumped, and played tag. Everybody thought her sweater was so special. Molly was so excited to wear her new sweater all day.

One summer, there was a girl who loved to move. Everywhere she went, she seemed to be on the go. She loved to jump, run, and swim any chance she had.

But one day, she was feeling bossy. She wanted to make all the boys and girls move with her. She told them what to do and when to do it.

The other children didn't like it. They tried to tell her to stop, but the girl wouldn't listen. She kept bossing them around.

Finally, one of the children had an idea. He said, "Let's all play a game! We can pretend to be animals, and we'll all move together!"

And that's how the bossy girl learned how to have fun with all the other children during the summer. They even made up their own animal-movement game, and now it's a favorite activity during the summer.

Once upon a time, there was a gray bird that was very, very fast! Every morning it would lift off the ground and soar through the blue sky. People in the park would watch the bird with amazement!

One day, the gray bird saw some kids playing with a kite. They were running, trying to make the kite go up in the sky. So the gray bird flew over and tried to help. It flew around and around, lifting higher and higher!

The kids were so excited! They cheered as the kite flew higher and higher with the help of the gray bird. When the kite finally landed back on the ground, the bird happily flew away to its nest. 

The kids could never forget the fast, gray bird that helped them lift the kite in the sky. They hoped it would come back soon!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the sunshine. One day, she saw an ugly butterfly flying around her garden. It had brown wings and spots on its body. 

Lily didn't like the butterfly because it looked strange. She tried to catch it with her hands, but it flew away. So, she decided to kick a ball instead. She kicked it high in the sky and it flew like a bird. 

Suddenly, the butterfly landed on the ball and Lily saw it up close. She realized that even though it was different, it was still beautiful in its own way. From then on, Lily never thought of the butterfly as ugly again. She learned to appreciate all the different things in the world.

Jimmy's mom was in the kitchen cooking dinner. It was nice and clean like it usually was. "What are you doing in there?" Jimmy asked. 

His mom smiled and answered, "I am making your favorite food for tonight!"

Jimmy felt very excited about that and went to the kitchen to show his mom something. Once he got there, he noticed something was not right. The kitchen was filthy! There were food scraps on the floor, grease on the walls and spills on the counter. 

"Mommy, what happened?" Jimmy asked. "I was cleaning up mess the neighbors made," his mom answered. 

Jimmy was sad because he didn't get to show his mom his surprise. Then, he ran out to the neighbors house and knocked on the door. He asked the neighbors to please clean up the mess they made. But the neighbors just laughed and shut the door.

Jimmy was so sad he started to cry. His mom felt bad and tried to clean up as much as she could, but it was too late. The kitchen was a mess and Jimmy's surprise was ruined.

Once there was a girl named Lily. She was so excited because today she was going to collect some pines. She put on her fancy dress and hat, and went outside.

When she got to the pines, she was so excited! She wanted to collect as many as she could. Carefully, she picked one up, and shook it to make sure there were no bugs hiding inside. Then she put it in her special basket.

She kept going, and soon she had a full basket of pines. Lily was so happy with her collection that she decided to bring them home.

At home, Lily was so proud of her lovely collection. Her mom and dad smiled, and told her she did a great job. She smiled, and then showed off her fancy dress to her parents.

Lily had a wonderful day collecting pines with her fancy dress on!

Once there was a little girl named Amy. Amy was very stubborn and wanted to do things her own way. 

One day, Amy's Mom asked her to measure out some special spice for the cake. But Amy refused. 

"No. I want to do it my way," she said.

Amy's Mom smiled. "That is a very stubborn word," she said.

But Amy was not going to give up. She took the measuring spoon and measured out the spice carefully. She used just the right amount, and she was very proud of herself.

"See, Mom," said Amy. "I measured it perfectly."

Amy's Mom smiled. "I knew you could do it," she said. "You were very stubborn, but it paid off." 

Amy was happy. She had used the right word and it had worked out for her. She was so proud of herself.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved to ride her bike. Every day, she would jump on her bike and ride around the neighborhood, always taking the same path.

One day, something extraordinary happened. As she took her route, an angel appeared in front of her! She was so excited to see it. The angel spoke to the little girl, saying "You must spread love and kindness in the world. Are you willing to do that?"

The girl nodded her head, understanding the task ahead of her. The angel smiled and said, "Ignorance is not the answer - open your eyes to all creatures on earth". With that, the angel flew away, leaving the little girl to ponder this message.

From that day forward, the little girl dedicated her life to being kind and helping those around her - because of her, the world became a better place!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a brown dog named Max. One day, Lily and Max went for a walk in the park. Max saw a squirrel and chased after it. Lily tried to call Max back, but he didn't listen.

Suddenly, Max got his paw stuck in a knot. He yelped in pain. Lily ran over to help Max and saw the knot was too tight. She tried to untie it, but she couldn't. A kind old man saw what happened and came over to help. He untied the knot and Max was free.

Lily thanked the old man and learned that it's always good to talk to someone when you need help. The old man said, "When you're in a knot, don't be afraid to talk and ask for help." From then on, Lily always talked to someone when she needed help, just like the old man said.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Mimi. Mimi was three years old and she liked to explore. One day Mimi decided to take a walk in the woods. 

As Mimi was walking, she heard a strange sound. She stopped and listened. The sound was getting louder. Then the sound stopped and Mimi saw a big, messy nest in the tree.

Mimi looked up and she saw a bird. She said hello. The bird flew down and took a small stick in her beak. It dropped the stick on the ground then flew back to its nest. 

Mimi picked up the stick and took it back to her home. Mimi was excited to show her mom the stick she had taken from the woods. 

Mimi's mom said, â€œThatâ€™s a nice stick Mimi! Where did you take it from?â€

Mimi said, â€œI took it from the woods. There was a bird making a lot of noise in a messy nest in a tree!

One day, Mary was sitting on the grass in the park, eating a sandwich. She chewed it slowly, looking around. Suddenly, something sparkly caught her eye - it was a silver necklace glistening in the sun. Mary noticed it was near a bush, so she crawled over to take a closer look. 

When she got close, Mary could see that the necklace was suspended from a thin branch. She reached out to take it in her tiny hand and felt it's cool metal. 

Just then, a voice called out from behind her. It was an old woman. 
 
"Do you like it?" she said.

Mary was a bit anxious but nodded and smiled.

"It's yours," the woman said warmly. "I saw you admiring it and thought you might like to have it."

Mary thanked the woman politely, before heading home with the new silver necklace in her pocket. From that day onward, every time Mary chewed her lunch in the park, she would also play with her silver necklace, and think back to the day when she had first seen it.

Once there was a little girl and her name was Lisa. She had a modest home full of love and her daddy was always there to make her smile. Every day he would take her for a walk and sing her a song. She loved it! 

One day, Lisa asked her daddy to repeat the song for her. He said yes and sang it over and over again until he got tired. Lisa giggled and thanked her daddy for singing it so many times. She felt so special when he showed her all of his love. 

Every day since then, Lisa asked her daddy to repeat the song and he always said yes. He loved her so much and she loved him too. Together they were the happiest they could be.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a room with a door and a special thing called a knob. The knob was round and shiny and it helped her open and close the door. 

One day, Lily's mommy came to her room and saw that the door was not closed. She said, "Lily, please close the door so the cold air won't come in." Lily got up and turned the knob until the door was closed perfectly. 

Lily was happy because she did a good job closing the door. She loved her knob and knew how to use it to keep her room warm and cozy. From that day on, Lily always made sure to close the door with the perfect knob.

Once there was a hungry bunny. He was hopping through the woods in search of something to eat. Suddenly, he stopped. He sniffed the air with his nose. What was that delicious smell?

The bunny hopped through some bushes and discovered a patch of juicy carrots! He munched on a few of the carrots and felt very happy. He hopped around the carrots and found more surprises.

The bunny discovered a juicy apple and he hopped around it, excitedly. He was so happy and so hungry, he ate the apple in a few bites. Yum!

After that, he hopped a little further. He sniffed the air with his nose and discovered a big, juicy strawberry! He hopped over to it and with one bite, he slurped it all up.

It was a great day for the hungry bunny. He had discovered lots of tasty treats and was very full. He hopped away, feeling happy and content.

Once there was a pupil who was very creative. He liked to use his imagination to come up with different ideas. One day, he had a great idea. He decided he was going to try and win a special competition - a race! 

He practised and practised with all his might, so that he could become faster. On the day of the competition, he was ready to win! He made sure that he had his running shoes and a bottle of water. 

The race started, and the pupil sprinted forward. He ran as fast as he could, and finally, he crossed the finish line first. He had won the race! Everyone cheered and congratulated the pupil on his victory. 

He was so proud of himself. He knew that all his hard work, practice and creativity had paid off. He had won the race and achieved something special, and it made him very happy.

Steve was very happy. He had a new model. It was the biggest and the most important one. He was so excited to load it up with pieces. He carefully put the pieces together. Then he tried to turn it on. But it didn't work. He was so sad. He tried to fix it, but he couldn't. It was broken forever. Steve was so sad that his important model didn't work.

Once upon a time, there was a gifted puppy named Spot. Spot was not like other puppies. He could bounce very high. Spot loved to bounce all day.

One day, Spot saw a big, red ball. He wanted to bounce on it. Spot ran and jumped on the ball. He bounced higher than ever before! Spot was so happy.

Spot's friends saw him bounce. They wanted to bounce too. Spot taught his friends how to bounce high. Now, all the puppies could bounce and play together. They had so much fun.

One sunny day, Andrew was walking through the woods when he heard a strange sound. He stopped and looked around. What was it? He followed the sound and found a well in the middle of the clearing. The sound was coming from inside the well. He looked over the edge and saw a fluffy grey bird perched on a log inside the well. The bird was whistling a happy song.

Andrew was amazed. He said "Hello! Can you whistle for me?" The grey bird stopped and looked up at him. Then it began to whistle again, this time a little louder. Andrew's eyes sparkled. He said "Wow! That's amazing!"

The bird hopped forward and said "Look at the thick walls of the well. I can make my whistles louder in here. Clap your hands and I will whistle louder!"

Andrew was overjoyed. He clapped his hands, and the bird whistled louder and louder. Andrew smiled and said "Thank you for the beautiful song!" The bird smiled back, and flew away with a final happy whistle.

Once upon a time there was a net. The net stood in the park. One day, a little girl saw the net and went over to it. She thought it was funny.

The girl picked up the net and ran around with it, splashing through puddles. She enjoyed playing with it.

The next day, the girl went back to the park with the net. She saw a group of kids playing together. She showed them the net and everyone wanted to play.

The kids took turns throwing a ball over the net. It was so much fun. Some of them ran around and tried to catch the ball in the net. Everyone had a great time.

At the end of the day, the girl put the net back where it stood before. But she knew she would be back soon to play with it again.

Once upon a time there was a small bunny called Alice. Alice liked to do things all by herself. She was very independent. One day Alice went to visit her friend. When she arrived there was a big fridge in the middle of the room. Alice had a great idea. She opened the fridge and found a big surprise. She saw yummy ice cream. She wanted to eat it all by herself, so she grabbed a bowl and the ice cream. She closed the fridge and enjoyed her ice cream. She remembered to always be independent. 

The next day Alice and her friend were playing outside. Alice saw a fridge in the garden. She was so excited and rushed over. She opened it and saw something sparkly. It was a magic wand! Instinctively, Alice remembered what to do with the wand - make a wish. She closed the fridge and made her wish. She wished to always remember to be independent. In that moment, she felt so special. 

Alice will never forget the magical moment when she found the magic wand in the fridge, and she will always remember to be independent.

Once upon a time, there was a little cat named Kitty. Kitty loved to spend time with her best friend, a dog named Max. They liked to play and run in the park together.

One day, Kitty and Max went to the station. It was a big place with lots of people and loud noises. Kitty was frightened. She held Max's paw to feel safe.

Max saw that Kitty was frightened, so he took her to a quiet spot near the station. They sat down and played together until Kitty was not frightened anymore. They were happy to spend time together and be best friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to collect pretty stones and shiny seashells. One day, she went to the beach with her mom and found a big, beautiful seashell. She was so happy and said, "Look mom, I won this seashell!" 

Suddenly, a boy named Jack came over and said, "I want your seashell, give it to me!" Lily said, "No, I found it and I want to keep it." Jack got angry and said, "I'm smarter than you, so I deserve it more!" 

Lily thought for a moment and said, "Being intelligent doesn't mean you can take things that aren't yours. It's not fair. I collected this seashell and it's mine." Jack realized that Lily was right and apologized. They became friends and collected more seashells together.

Tommy was playing with his toy car outside in the sunshine. He kept zooming it around and around and it was so much fun.

But after a while Tommy got tired. He looked around and saw a nice big tree nearby. He decided to rest beside it.

Tommy lay down under the tree and it felt really nice. He felt like he could stay there forever. Then he heard a noise.

It was a quiz! There were lots of questions being asked. Tommy opened one eye and saw an open book with lots of pictures. He was curious.

Tommy decided to give the quiz a try. He read the questions and tried his best to answer them. He felt so proud when he finished it.

Tommy felt happy and rested. He closed his eyes and enjoyed the peace and quiet of the tree. He knew that playing with his toy car could wait until tomorrow.

Mum and Dad brought home a big hoop for Maria. She was so excited! She sat down on the floor and watched as Mum and Dad placed the hoop around her.

"Wow, it so big!" said Maria.

"Yes, it is big and fun," said Mum.

Mum showed Maria how to count as she jumped through the hoop. She was a bit clumsy, but she was very happy.

"One, two, three!" Maria said, counting each time she jumped through the hoop.

Mum and Dad watched and smiled. They were so proud of Maria. She had so much fun that it was hard to take her away from the hoop.

The next day, Maria asked Mum and Dad to bring out the hoop again. They quickly set it up and Maria began counting and jumping all over again.

"One, two, three!" she said, smiling all the while.

Once upon a time there was a cute little kitten. Every day, the kitten would sit by the window and watch the birds. One day, the kitten saw something special. It was a big, shiny screen! The kitten wanted to add the screen to its life.

So the kitten asked its mom if it could have the screen. Mom said yes, and the screen came to live in the house. The kitten was so happy!

Every day, the kitten would sit in front of the screen and watch the birds. It was so much better than the window! The kitten added songs, stories, and lovely pictures to the screen. 

The kitten was so excited to share its new screen with its friends. The friends had so much fun with the kitten, now that there was a big, shiny screen to use.

And that's how the cute little kitten added a screen to its life.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny named Skip. He loved to skip all day long. One day, while he was skipping near a cliff, he saw a dirty bird.

"Hello, dirty bird!" Skip said. "Why are you so dirty?"

The dirty bird looked sad. "I fell in the mud," he said. "Now I can't fly."

Skip wanted to help his new friend. He thought of a plan. "I know!" he said. "I will find some water and we will clean you up."

Skip skipped away to find water. He found a small pond and brought some water back in a big leaf. Together, they cleaned the dirty bird.

"Thank you, Skip!" said the bird, now clean and happy. "Now I can fly again." The bird flew high in the sky, and Skip went back to skipping near the cliff, happy to have helped a friend.

Once upon a time, there was a wide market for everyone to go. Little Jack and his mommy were there to look around. Suddenly, Jack saw a toy he wanted. But someone else had already taken it. They started to fight over the toy, until Jack's mommy had to separate them.

"Jack, it's not nice to fight over toys," said Jack's mommy. "It's better to try and share with others."

Jack looked down at his feet. He felt sorry for fighting with someone.

"I'm sorry," said Jack to the other person. "We can share the toy."

The other person smiled and said, "Thanks Jack, that's very nice of you."

So, they shared the toy and they both were happy. From then on, Jack and his mommy shared everything they bought at the market.

Once upon a time Sam and Sally wanted to play a game. So they asked mommy if they could. Mommy said, "Yes, you may." Sam and Sally were so happy they shouted, "Yay!"

They ran outside and set up the game. Sam found a ball and Sally found a bat. They were ready to play.

While they were playing, Mommy came outside with something yummy. It was ice cream! Mommy said, "I brought this for you as a treat. But only if you permit it." Sam and Sally said, "Yes, we permit it!" They had a great time playing and eating the yummy ice cream together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a soft teddy bear that she loved very much. One day, Lily was playing with her bear when she heard a loud noise outside. She went to look and saw that her friend, Tommy, was in trouble. 

Lily ran outside and asked Tommy what was wrong. Tommy said that he lost his favorite toy and couldn't find it anywhere. Lily thought for a moment and then remembered that she had seen the toy earlier. She ran back inside her house and found the toy. 

Lily ran back outside and gave the toy to Tommy. He was so happy that he started to clap his hands. "Thank you, Lily!" he said. "You are the best friend ever!" Lily smiled and hugged her teddy bear. She was happy that she could help her friend.
