Once upon a time, there was a little bird. The bird liked to fly in the sky and feel the wind on its feathers. One day, the bird saw a big storm coming. It was scared and didn't know what to do. But then, it saw its friend, a big eagle, who came to support it. The eagle said, "Don't worry little bird, I will help you." The eagle flew with the little bird and kept it safe from the storm. The little bird felt grateful and alert, looking out for any other storms that might come. From that day on, the little bird knew it had a friend who would always be there to support it.

Once upon a time, there was a girl called Sue. She had a number in her hand. She loved to turn it around and around. Sue was very patient. She waited and waited until the number turned. Suddenly the number flew up like a bird and away. Sue was so excited! She chased it around the garden and under the tree. Then, with one final turn, the number came flying back and landed in Sue's hand again. She was so happy! From then on, Sue always took her number with her wherever she went.

Karen was very excited. She was four years old and she was going to learn how to do math. She went to school and saw all the other children who were lively and ready to learn. Karen joined them, but she was a bit nervous, too.

The teacher told the students it was time to learn how to make math. She gave them some problems to solve. Everyone was working hard, but Karen wasn't sure what to do.

Karen's hand slowly went up. The teacher walked over and asked her, "What's wrong?" She replied, "I don't understand how to make math." 

The teacher smiled and explained it slowly and carefully. She said, "The best way to make math is to use your fingers! Count and add little blocks of numbers together to solve the problem." 

Karen was relieved. With the help of the teacher, she began to understand and make math. She was happier and more lively than ever before. She worked hard until she could solve the problem. Karen was proud that she could make math!

Once upon a time, in a small town, there lived an elderly lady named Nana. Nana loved to dive into the big pool in her backyard. One day, as she was diving, she heard a little bird cry.

"Help me, please!" said the little bird. "I hurt my wing and need a stitch."

Nana felt sad for the little bird. She took the bird into her house and gently put a stitch on its wing. The little bird was so happy, it started to sing a beautiful song.

Days went by, and the little bird's wing got better. It was time for the bird to fly away. Nana and the bird went to the backyard, and Nana helped the bird dive into the air.

"Thank you, Nana!" the little bird said as it flew away. Nana waved goodbye, feeling happy that she could help her new friend. From that day on, every time Nana would dive into her pool, she would remember the little bird and smile.

Once upon a time, there was a bald man named Tom. Tom loved to eat candy, but he didn't like the taste of it when it was dirty. One day, he went to a candy store to buy some candy, but he noticed that the candy looked dirty. He asked the store owner to polish the candy, but the owner said no.

Tom got very upset and started to cry. He really wanted the candy, but he didn't want to eat it if it was dirty. Suddenly, a kind little girl walked into the store and saw Tom crying. She asked him what was wrong, and he told her about the dirty candy.

The little girl went up to the store owner and asked him to polish the candy for Tom. The store owner listened to the little girl and polished the candy. Tom was very happy and thanked the little girl for helping him. From that day on, Tom always went to the candy store with the little girl because she had a good taste in candy.

Tom and Lily like to play with their toy guns. They pretend to be cowboys and shoot at each other. They make loud noises and run around the yard. They have a lot of fun.

One day, a new boy moves in next door. His name is Ben. He sees Tom and Lily playing and wants to join them. He knocks on the fence and says, "Hi, I'm Ben. Can I play with you?"

Tom and Lily look at him and smile. They say, "Sure, you can play with us. We are friendly. What do you like to play?"

Ben says, "I like to play with toy guns too. I have one in my house. Can I go get it?"

Tom and Lily say, "Yes, you can go get it. We will wait for you here."

Ben runs to his house and comes back with his toy gun. He shows it to Tom and Lily. They say, "Wow, that's a cool toy gun. It looks real."

Ben says, "It is real. My dad gave it to me. He is a soldier. He said I can shoot with it."

Tom and Lily are shocked. They say, "No, no, no. You can't shoot with a real gun. That's very dangerous. You can hurt yourself or someone else. You can only shoot with toy guns. They are safe and fun."

Ben doesn't understand. He says, "But my dad said I can shoot with it. He said it's fun. He said I'm a big boy."

Tom and Lily say, "No, you're not a big boy. You're a little boy. And little boys don't shoot with real guns. They shoot with toy guns. Real guns are for grown-ups. And they are not fun. They are scary and bad."

Ben feels sad and angry. He says, "You're mean. You don't want to play with me. You don't like me. I don't like you either. I'm going to shoot you."

He points his real gun at Tom and Lily. They scream and run away. They hide behind a tree and call for help. They hope Ben doesn't shoot them. They are very scared. They wish Ben was friendly and played with toy guns. They wish he was their friend.

Once upon a time, a boy named Timmy wanted to watch TV. He asked his mom, "Can I watch TV now?" His mom said, "Yes, but only for a little bit."

Timmy turned on the TV and watched his favorite show. But then, the TV started to delay and the picture got all fuzzy. Timmy was sad and said, "Mom, the TV is broken."

His mom came to check and said, "Oh no, the TV needs to be fixed. We'll have to call someone to help us." Timmy asked, "Will it take long?" His mom said, "I hope not, but it might be a little sour waiting for it to be fixed."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and dress up in pretty clothes. One day, Lily's mom asked her to help clean up her closet. Lily was excited to see what was inside.

As they started to clean, Lily found a box of toys that she had forgotten about. She looked through them and found a teddy bear that she really liked. She told her mom that it was interesting and she wanted to keep it.

Her mom said that the teddy bear was very old and might be valuable. Lily didn't understand what that meant, but she knew she wanted to keep it anyway. She put it on her bed and hugged it tight. From that day on, the teddy bear became her favorite toy.

Once upon a time, there was a young boy and a young girl who were walking through the forest. The young boy saw a leaf laying on the ground and he said, "Let's admire the leaf together". The girl said, "We can't admire a leaf that is already on the ground. We need to look for a strong and beautiful leaf up in the tree." 

The young boy thought for a moment and then nodded his head in agreement. So the boy and girl found a tall tree with a lush green leaf at the top. The boy looked up and said, "Let's admire this one." The girl smiled and said, "Yes, this is the perfect one to admire". 

The boy and girl admired the leaf up in the tree while looking all around them. They admired the sun rays streaming through the branches and the sounds of the birds in the air. The boy and girl felt happier and more peaceful just from looking and admiring all the beauty in nature. 

Moral: It is important to appreciate what nature has to offer and to admire the beauty in life.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to eat yummy food. One day, her mom gave her a tasty cookie. Lily was so happy and said, "Thank you, Mommy! This cookie is so yummy." 

After eating the cookie, Lily went outside to play in the garden. She saw a maze and wanted to go inside. "Mommy, can I go in the maze?" she asked. "Yes, but be careful and don't get lost," her mom replied. 

Lily went inside the maze and had fun finding her way out. Suddenly, she saw a big boy coming towards her. He said, "Excuse me, can you yield and let me pass?" Lily didn't know what yield meant, so the boy explained it to her. She moved aside and let him pass. 

Finally, Lily found her way out of the maze and ran back to her mom. "Mommy, I found my way out of the maze! And I learned a new word - yield!" she said happily. Her mom smiled and gave her a hug.

Once upon a time, there was a gray panda named Pandy. Pandy liked to eat bamboo and play in the forest. One day, Pandy met a little girl named Lily. Lily wanted to play with Pandy, but Pandy didn't want to play with her.

"I don't want to play with you," said Pandy.

"Why not?" asked Lily.

"Because I want to quit playing now," said Pandy.

Lily felt sad, but she didn't give up. She asked Pandy again and again until Pandy finally agreed to play with her. They played together all afternoon and had so much fun. From that day on, Pandy and Lily were the best of friends.

Once upon a time, there was a big clock in a small room. The clock was mysterious. It had a face and two hands. Every day, the clock went "tick-tock, tick-tock." 

One day, a little girl named Lucy came into the room. She looked at the clock and said, "Hello, clock! Why are you so mysterious?" The clock did not answer. It just went "tick-tock, tick-tock." Lucy felt a tickle in her nose. She tried to hold it in, but she could not. "Achoo!" she sneezed.

The sneeze was so big, it made the clock's hands move. The clock said, "Thank you, Lucy! Your sneeze helped me. I was stuck, but now I can move again." Lucy smiled and said, "You're welcome, clock!" From that day on, the mysterious clock and Lucy were the best of friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved to tell jokes. She thought herself to be the funniest person around and would make all of her friends laugh with her stories.

One day, the little girl decided to go for a walk in a forest on a very icy day. She was wearing her warmest clothes, so she didn't feel the cold at all. She soon came upon a group of animals, and wanted to show off her funny jokes.

Without thinking, the little girl began to tell her jokes, but the animals were not amused. They thought that the joke ruins the cold atmosphere of the icy forest and ran away, leaving the little girl very sad.

The little girl had spoilt her joke and the animals left. She suddenly realized that her jokes had not been very kind. From that day on, she decided to be extra careful every time she told jokes, and make sure she didn't spoil them!

Once upon a time there was a fit man. He was really nice and he wanted to rescue his best friend.

His best friend was having a bad day and he was stuck in a tall tree. So the fit man said, "Don't worry! I will rescue you!" And he began to climb the tree.

The fit man got to the top of the tree, but he couldn't rescue his best friend from up there. The friend was too scared to come down.

Then the fit man had a great idea. He remembered that the friend's favourite food was beef. So the fit man went down, got some beef and brought it back to the tree.

The friend saw the beef, and it made him feel better. He climbed down and the fit man gave him the beef. He was so happy to be rescued!

Max was a very stubborn 3 year old. He didn't like to share his things or talk to people. One day, he was at the park and he saw a shoe. It was a nice shoe, so he didn't want to share it with anyone. He decided to take it home with him. 

When he got home, he put the shoe in his room, but his mom found it. She asked him where he got it, but he didn't want to talk about it. He just locked himself in his room and kept the shoe for himself. 

His mom was very stubborn, too. She asked him over and over again to tell her where he got the shoe, but Max remained tight-lipped. Finally, his mom had to take the shoe away. Max was very sad, but he knew better than to talk about it.

Once upon a time, there was a kind man who owned a lemon stand. He would serve lemonade to all the people who passed by. He was very wise and knew how to make the best lemonade in the whole town.

One day, a greedy man came and asked for all the lemons. The kind man said no because he needed them to serve lemonade to the people. The greedy man got angry and decided to take all the lemons by force.

The kind man was sad because he couldn't serve lemonade anymore. Without any lemons, he had to close his stand. The people in the town missed his lemonade and the kind man was very sad. The greedy man didn't care and enjoyed all the lemons by himself. The end.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She loved to make things. She especially liked to make things with her needle and thread. She was very good at using the needle to stitch things together. 

One day, the girl wanted to make something special. She got some colorful fabric and sat down to sew. She tried her best to make something nice. She worked for a long time.

When she was done, she had made a beautiful quilt! Everyone was so happy with it. All the colors looked lively and the stitches were neat and strong.

The little girl was very proud. She said to everyone, "Look what I made! Isn't it great?" 

Everyone cheered. They said, "Wow! You are very good at improving things with your needle and thread!" 

The little girl smiled. Then she said, "I'm going to make a new quilt soon. And it's going to get even better!"

Tom and Mia are playing in the garden. They see a big white sack near the fence. They wonder what is inside.

"Let's open it!" Tom says.

"OK, but be careful. Maybe there is something sharp or scary inside," Mia says.

They run to the sack and pull the string. The sack opens and many colorful balls fall out. Tom and Mia are happy. They start to throw the balls at each other and laugh.

But one ball is not like the others. It is small and hard and has a needle on it. Tom picks it up and feels a pain in his hand.

"Ow! Ow! Ow!" Tom cries. "This ball hurts me!"

Mia sees the blood on Tom's hand. She is scared. She drops the balls and runs to Tom.

"Let me see, let me see. You have a needle in your hand. We have to take it out," Mia says.

She tries to pull the needle out, but it is stuck. Tom screams louder.

"Help! Help! We need Mommy!" Mia shouts.

Mommy hears them and comes to the garden. She sees the white sack, the balls, and the needle. She understands what happened.

"Oh, no! You found the sack of old ornaments. These are not toys. These are for the Christmas tree. Some of them have needles to hang them. You have to be very careful with them," Mommy says.

She takes Tom to the house and washes his hand. She takes the needle out and puts a bandage on it. She hugs Tom and kisses him.

"You are very brave, Tom. I'm sorry you got hurt. The needle is out now. You will be OK," Mommy says.

Tom feels better. He smiles and hugs Mommy back.

"Thank you, Mommy. I love you," Tom says.

Mia comes to the house too. She is sorry for Tom. She brings him a ball that is soft and fluffy. She gives it to him.

"I'm sorry, Tom. I didn't know the ball had a needle. I hope you like this ball. It is nice and safe," Mia says.

Tom likes the ball. He thanks Mia and hugs her.

"I like this ball, Mia. You are a good sister. I love you," Tom says.

They play with the ball together. They are happy again. They forget about the white sack and the needle. They only remember the colorful balls and the love.

Little Jack was so proud of his igloo. It was the biggest one in the neighbourhood and he had worked so hard on it with his dad.

Little Jack's dad called to him from the porch. "Let's go for a walk!" he said.

Jack eagerly jumped up and ran over. "Where will we go?" he asked.

Dad smiled. "Let's go and visit the Arctic Igloos," he replied.

Little Jack was so excited. He ran ahead of his dad as they made their way to the igloo village. As they got closer and closer, they could see all the igloos in their bright colours. 

Little Jack gasped in amazement. Dad pointed to the biggest one in the village. "I bet that's the most important one," he said.

Little Jack smiled. His dad was right. He ran ahead and urged his dad to follow. As they got closer, Jack could see his dad's proud smile.

Once there was a little girl who wanted to do something special. She had a box of pretty ornaments that she wanted to take somewhere. She was so glad that she could carry them in her bag.

So the little girl went outside and found the most special place. She went up to the top of a hill and put her ornaments all around. She made a beautiful garden with the ornaments.

The little girl was so very glad when she looked around at her special place. The sun shone in the sky and the ornaments glittered in the light. She was glad she could carry the ornaments to the place.

The little girl came back to the same place every day. It was her favorite place in the world, and she was always glad when she could carry the ornaments back with her.

The little girl had a wonderful time playing with her ornaments and making her special place even more beautiful. Her garden was so very nice that it was like something out of a storybook! She was very glad for all of the fun she had with her ornaments.

Once upon a time, there was a lively three year old called Jack. He was playing with his toy car outside in the sun when he spotted something in the distance. It was a jar of jam, sitting all on its own. Jack couldn't resist it and ran over to grab the jar.

Suddenly, a gruff voice called out behind him. It was Jack's father, and he did not look happy.

"What is that you've got there, Jack?!" he said. 

"It's jam, Dad!" Jack explained.

Jack's dad shook his head and said, "No son, that jam belongs to someone else. You must part with it".

Jack began to cry and pleaded to keep the jam, but his father was adamant that he had to give it back. He eventually gave in, and put the jar of jam back in its original spot. 

Jack trudged away sadly, feeling disappointed and empty. He knew he had done the wrong thing, but he couldn't help wishing he still had that jar of jam.

One day, two friends went on a trip. They were so excited! But the trip did not go as planned. It was really hot out, and their car broke down. The two friends started to feel hungry, so they stopped at a diner for lunch.

When their food came, it was disgusting! It was cold and not tasty. Their faces made a funny expression as they looked at the food.

The two friends decided to take another trip. But this time they bought food in advance. The food they picked was delicious and they had a lot of fun! They didn't have any problems and happily finished their trip.

Once upon a time there was a girl who had a problem. She wanted to buy something but she had no money. She had an idea. She decided to sell her knotted blanket. She took her blanket and went to the market. 

The girl was a bit scared. All the people were busy and bustling around and everyone was talking in a distant language. She went up to a stall and offered the blanket for sale. The shop keeper looked at the blanket and smiled warmly. He said he would give her money for it and the girl was very pleased. 

Having sold her blanket, the girl was now able to buy the things she wanted. She felt happy and relieved that she had solved her problem and had money to buy what she needed. She was so proud of herself!

Molly was playing in the park. She saw a butterfly flutter by and began to applaud. The butterfly was so amazed, it flew up in the sky and circled back around before coming to rest on a nearby tree. 

Molly clapped her hands and smiled. She wanted to try and catch the butterfly, so she took out an old saw and started sawing through the branch of the tree. The saw was wet from the rain, but Molly kept sawing until the branch broke and the butterfly flew away, still fluttering and shimmering in the sunlight. 

Molly smiled and applauded the butterfly. She knew it was gone, but she just wanted to express her admiration for the beautiful creature. Molly waved as it flew away and then ran off to find something else to do.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy had a belt that he wore every day. It was a brown belt with a shiny buckle. Timmy thought it was the coolest belt ever.

One day, Timmy went to school and his teacher talked about a boring book. Timmy didn't like boring things, so he didn't want to read it. But then his friend mentioned that the book had a cool adventure in it. Timmy was interested in adventures, so he decided to give the book a try.

As he read the book, Timmy sat back and adjusted his belt. He was happy he gave the book a chance because he found a new adventure to enjoy. From that day on, Timmy always listened when his friends mentioned something new.

Once upon a time, there were two friends called Joe and Molly. Joe and Molly loved to play together. One day, Joe said to Molly, "Let's go get pizza!" Molly clapped her hands and was very happy. 

So, Joe and Molly went to the pizza shop. When they arrived, Molly chose a big piece of pizza and Joe chose a small one. But when Molly tried it, she said, "This pizza is bad!" Joe laughed and said, "Maybe you just don't like pizza!" 

Molly thought and then said, "Maybe I do like pizza, but this one is bad!" Joe shrugged and ate his pizza anyway. Molly was sad, but Joe said, "Let's go somewhere else. I bet they'll have better pizza!"

Once upon a time, there was a mouse. The mouse was small and its fur was very soft and blue. 

The mouse ran across the floor of the house, looking for something to do. Then it saw a little boy. He was 3 years old, with blond hair and a big, happy smile.

Once there was a chubby boy who loved school. Every day he would go to his classroom with a big smile on his face. His teacher always believed in him and was very kind.

One day, a little girl named Sue went for a walk. She saw a delicate butterfly on a big rock. Sue wanted to touch the butterfly, but she was scared to hurt it. She thought, "I need to be gentle with the butterfly because it is delicate."

Sue saw a note on the ground near the butterfly. She picked it up and read, "Be kind to all creatures." Sue thought about the note and decided to be kind to the butterfly. She said, "Hello, butterfly! I will be kind to you."

Sue walked away and saw a boy named Tim. Tim was sad because he lost his toy. Sue remembered the note and decided to help Tim. They looked for the toy together and found it under a tree. Tim was happy and said, "Thank you, Sue! You are kind."

The moral of the story is to always be kind to others, whether they are people or creatures.

Once upon a time, there was a little seed. The seed lived in a big garden with many other seeds. One day, it started to rain. The rain helped the seed grow into a brilliant, strong plant.

The hurricane went away, and the sun came out. The plants were happy and they kept growing. The brilliant plant said, "We did it, friends! We stayed strong and now we can grow even more." And they all lived happily in the garden.

Once upon a time there was a tower that was so tall and strong. But it was very dangerous, so no one ever went near it.

Once upon a time, in a big green park, there was a spoiled little girl named Lucy. She loved to dance and feel the rhythm of the music. One sunny day, Lucy went to the park to play.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and explore the woods behind her house. One day, she went on a walk with her mommy and they found a trail that led deep into the forest.

Once upon a time, there was a small tiger. She was walking through the woods, when she saw something unknown. She was curious and wanted to know what it was. She slowly crept closer and closer, until she could see what it was. It was a tiny animal that she had never seen before! Once upon a time there was a little girl called Grace. Grace liked to touch things and explore the world with her hands and fingers.

Peter was very nervous. He had never been in an aeroplane before and was not sure what to expect.

Once upon a time, there was a big blue bird. It lived in a tree with lots of leaves. One day, the bird saw a lime on the ground. It was very sour! Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to play with his toys and run around outside. One day, Tim went to the park with his mom. He played on the swings and went down the slide.

One day, a little girl named Sue found a broken apron in her house. She wanted to fix it. So, she went to her mom and said, "Mom, can we fix this apron?"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who liked to cook. Every evening, she enjoyed spending time in the kitchen, cooking all kinds of items. She mixed ingredients in a bowl and stirred things in a pot.

Once upon a time, there was a playful bee. He loved to fly around the meadow and play. One day he decided to visit a nearby flower.

"Mommy, I love winter!", Sally exclaimed. She was so excited to feel the snow on her face and see the snowflakes twirling in the sky.

Once upon a time, there was a town. Everyone in the town was happy â€“ until something bad happened. The town became bitter.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who was scared. She was so scared she wanted to stay in her bed forever. But then one day, a zigzag came to her window. It was so funny! Once upon a time, there was a butterfly. It was different to all the other butterflies, because it was big and bright and bold. It liked to fly so high in the sky and shine its bright colours in the sunshine.

Once there was a puppy called Bob. Bob loved to crawl around and explore. One day, while he was crawling around, he saw a long, shiny rod on the floor. One sunny day, a little girl named Elsie wanted to go for a walk. She asked her mom for permission, and her mom said, "Yes, you may go, but be polite and stay away from the hedge."

Lily and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toys and books. But sometimes they fight. Lily wants to play with the doll and Ben wants to play with the car. They yell and pull and cry.

Once there was a dance. It was a special dance because it was for a deaf child.

Once there was an uncle. He was very wise. He loved to fold things. He would fold paper into shapes and fold clothes neatly in the drawer.

Once upon a time, there was an ancient igloo. Inside the igloo, there was a special pot. Every day, the pot would pour out a magic liquid. Sam is a big boy who likes to learn new things. He has a book with many pictures of animals and plants. He likes to look at the book and ask his mom what they are.

One day, he sees a picture of a cell. It is very small and has many parts. He points to the picture and asks his mom, "What is this?"

His mom smiles and says, "That is a cell, Sam. A cell is a tiny thing that makes up everything alive. You have many cells in your body, and so do I, and so do the animals and plants."

Sam is curious and wants to know more. He asks his mom, "How can I see a cell? It is too small for my eyes."

His mom says, "You need a special tool called a microscope. A microscope can make small things look bigger. I have one in my office. Do you want to see it?"

Sam nods and says, "Yes, please!"

His mom takes him to her office and shows him the microscope. She puts a slide with a drop of water under the microscope and lets Sam look through the eyepiece. He sees many cells moving and changing. He is amazed and says, "Wow! They are so cool!"

His mom says, "Yes, they are. They are also very important. They help us grow and stay healthy. They also help us make delicious food."

Sam asks, "How do they make delicious food?"

His mom says, "Well, some cells can turn sunlight and water into sugar. That is how plants make their food. And some cells can turn sugar and oxygen into energy. That is how we and animals make our food. And some cells can make different flavors and smells. That is how we enjoy our food."

Sam says, "I like sugar and energy and flavors and smells. Cells are awesome!"

His mom says, "Yes, they are. And you are awesome, too, Sam. You are a smart boy who likes to learn. I am proud of you."

She hugs him and says, "I love you, Sam."

He hugs her back and says, "I love you, too, mom. Thank you for teaching me about cells."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She wanted to go outside and play, but she couldn't find her shoes. She looked under the bed, in the closet, and even in the toy box, but she couldn't find them anywhere.

Once upon a time there was a young girl named Elin. She was very curious, so one day she asked her mum a big question, "What is trade?"

Her mum was surprised by the question, but she smiled and said, "If someone has something that someone else wants, they can trade it for something else". Elin thought for a moment, then said, "Then why do people not just give things away for free?". Her mum smiled again, and said, "It's not always so simple. People need to get something back in return".

Elin was happy with the answer and she began to think. She then asked, "What is it like if a person doesn't trade fairly, mum?". Her mum paused, then said sadly, "Well, then they would be ashamed." Elin's face fell, and she said, "But why?". "Well, it's not nice to use people", replied her mum softly.

Elin thought hard, and then she said, "OK. I understand now. People should always be nice and trade fairly." Her mum was so proud of her that she hugged Elin tightly and said, "That's right! It's important to remember that".

The two of them hugged for a long time and were very happy together. Elin had learned a valuable lesson that day, and she would never forget it.

Tom and Mia like to play in the park. They have a ball and a frisbee. They throw them to each other and catch them. They have fun.

He sees Tom and Mia in the puddle. He says, "What are you doing? You are making a mess. You are not allowed to play in the puddle. You have to go home and get dry."

The police man says, "It is okay. I know you did not mean to be bad. But you have to be careful. The puddle is dirty and can make you sick. And you can get hurt if you slip and fall. Next time, play somewhere else."

Tom and Mia nod. They say, "Thank you, police man. We will do that." They pick up their ball and frisbee. They run to their mom and dad. They tell them what happened. They go home and get dry. They learn their lesson.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a dependable friend named Bear who always stayed by her side. One day, Lily and Bear went to the store to buy some candy. Lily put her wallet in her pocket and they walked to the store.

The neighbor called an ambulance, but it was too late. Timmy's grandma had passed away. Timmy was heartbroken and didn't understand what had happened. He missed his grandma and all the fun times they had together. From that day on, Timmy learned that sometimes people get sick and don't get better, and it's okay to feel sad and miss them.

Ben and Lily were going to the zoo with their mom. They were very happy and excited. They wanted to see the lions, the monkeys, and the elephants. Mom said they had a surprise for them at the zoo, but she would not tell them what it was. She said they had to guess.

"Is it a new animal?" Ben asked.

"Is it a big toy?" Lily asked.

Mom smiled and said, "You will see when we get there. It is something very special."

Ben and Lily were anxious to find out. They tried to guess all the way to the zoo. They looked out the window and saw cars, trees, and houses. They did not see anything that looked like a surprise.

When they got to the zoo, Mom bought the tickets and gave them a map. She said, "Follow me. I will show you the surprise. It is at the end of this path."

Ben and Lily followed Mom. They saw many animals on the way. They saw the lions, the monkeys, and the elephants. They were happy, but they still wanted to see the surprise.

They reached the end of the path. There was a big gate with a sign that said, "Penguin View". Mom opened the gate and said, "Here we are. This is the surprise. We can go inside and see the penguins."

Ben and Lily gasped. They loved penguins. They had seen them on TV, but they had never seen them in real life. They ran inside the gate and saw a big pool with many penguins. The penguins were swimming, diving, and sliding on the ice. They were black and white and very cute.

Ben and Lily were amazed. They clapped and laughed. They thanked Mom for the surprise. They said, "This is the best view ever. We love the penguins. They are so fun and cool."

Mom hugged them and said, "I'm glad you like it. I knew you would. I guessed right."

Once upon a time, there were two best friends - a lion and a monkey. They were good friends and always went on adventures together. 

One day, they decided to go to the jungle. The sky was blue, but the lion was worried. He said, "The sky is so blue. I think it might rain!" 

The monkey laughed. He said, "Don't worry, my friend. Let's have some fun in the jungle instead!"

But as soon as they arrived in the jungle, it started to rain. The lion was worried that they would get wet. He shouted, "Let's go back home before we get too wet!"

But the monkey was excited. She said, "Let's play in the rain! The jungle always looks the most beautiful when it rains."

And so the two friends happily played in the rain. The lion soon wasn't so worried anymore, and he and the monkey laughed together all the way home.

Once upon a time there was a silly little mouse who lived in an old armchair. One day, the mouse was getting very bored. He wanted to do something exciting.

Then an idea came to him! He scurried to the corner of the armchair and started to print. He printed pictures of all his friends and family with his tiny little feet. He made all kinds of silly shapes and colors.

As he was printing away, he heard a noise. The noise was coming from the armchair's leg! It sounded like it was saying, "Look what I can do too!"

The mouse was so excited. He quickly finished printing and ran over to the armchair's leg. When he got there, the mouse saw a little spider printing too! The spider was making shapes and colors just like him.

The mouse and spider became very good friends. They printed together every day! And they both learned that being silly is lots of fun.

John went to the store and saw a nice hat that he liked. He asked his mom if he could buy it and she said, "No, we don't want a hat today".

John got very angry and he screamed, "But I want a hat!" His mom said, "No, John. We already have enough hats at home." John got even angrier and he was so mad he wanted to burn the hat.

But then he heard someone say, "That's a stupid idea, John." It was his mom. She said, "If you burn the hat, it will be ruined! We don't want to do that". John realized it wasn't a good idea, so he stopped. 

His mom gave him a hug and said, "Let's go home, for we don't need a new hat today". John smiled and said, "Ok, mommy". So, they went home without the hat.

Once upon a time there was a great dancer. She wanted to be the best dancer ever. But she was only little and she didn't know how to do it. Every night she would close her eyes and dream. She dreamed of dancing perfectly and making everyone smile. Then one night a great thing happened. As she was dreaming, a fairy came and gave her special shoes. The shoes had sparkles on them and they made the dancer fly. When she would look down the town was so small, but when she looked up the stars seemed so big. The dancer flew around and danced high in the sky. Everywhere she went people cheered and clapped. They loved her great dancing! When she woke up the dancer realized it was all a dream. But she knew that if she tried her very best she could make her dreams come true. So everyday she worked hard and the great dancer became even better!

Once there was a big bear with soft fur. His name was Ted. Every day he liked to sit in the garden and watch the birds chirping in the trees. One day he heard something very noisy. He looked up and saw a little boy. The boy was walking and holding a big red balloon. Ted watched as the little boy reached out and grabbed the balloon's string. He pulled it and the balloon started to move through the sky. Ted wanted to say hello, but he was too shy.

Then, the little boy saw Ted. He smiled and ran over. He grabbed both of Ted's paws and gave him a big hug. Ted felt so loved. He smiled back at the little boy and waved goodbye.

From then on, whenever the little boy came to play in the garden, Ted was waiting. He always gave him a big hug. Ted loved to listen to the little boy's loud laughs and watch him pull his balloon all around. It was his favorite game.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was very excited because her parents told her they were going to the store to buy candy. When they got to the store, Lily's mom gave her a penny to buy a piece of candy. 

Lily was so impatient, she didn't want to wait in line. She kept tugging on her mom's shirt and asking when it was their turn. Finally, it was their turn, and Lily ran to the candy aisle. 

She saw so many different kinds of candy, she didn't know which one to pick. She started to unpack all the candy, looking for the perfect one. But then, another little girl came and wanted to buy candy too. 

Lily got upset because she thought the other girl was going to take the candy she wanted. But her mom reminded her to share and be kind. Lily ended up picking her favorite candy and sharing some with the other little girl. They both left the store happy with their treats. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a young girl named Lily. She had a playful puppy named Max. They loved to play together in the park every day. One day, Lily and Max went for a walk and they saw a little bird with a hurt wing. 

Lily said, "Oh no, the bird is hurt. We need to help it." Max barked and wagged his tail. He wanted to help too. Lily gently picked up the bird and rubbed its wing. The bird felt better and could fly again. 

The bird chirped happily and Lily said, "We helped the bird. That was very kind of us." Max barked again and licked Lily's face. He was very happy too. From that day on, Lily and Max helped all the animals they saw in the park. They were very kind and playful friends.

Once there was a little girl named Lizzie. She was three years old and loved to rock in her closet.

One day as she was rocking, she heard a loud noise coming from behind the closet door. She opened it to see what had made the noise, and out came a crazy monkey!

The monkey hopped around the room, laughing and joking. Lizzie didn't know what to do.

Then the monkey spoke.

"Let's rock together!" he said.

So the little girl and the crazy monkey rocked together in the closet. They laughed, sang and jumped around until it was time for Lizzie to go to bed.

The monkey waved goodbye and hopped off into the night. Lizzie smiled and wondered what crazy adventures they would have together tomorrow.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and make things with her hands. One day, she decided to make a robot out of some old boxes and paper. She was very creative and used her imagination to make the robot look cool.

But when her little brother saw the robot, he started to complain. He said it didn't look like a real robot and that it was too big. Lily felt sad and didn't know what to do. She went to her mom and told her what happened. Her mom said, "Don't worry, Lily. You did a great job and your robot is very creative."

Later that day, Lily's mom was ironing some clothes and Lily asked if she could help. Her mom said yes and showed her how to use the iron. Lily was very careful and did a good job. She felt proud of herself and forgot about what her brother said earlier. From then on, Lily knew that it was important to be creative and not to let anyone else's complaints bring her down.

Once upon a time, there was a poor little girl named Lily. She lived in a small house with her mom and dad. They didn't have much money, but they always had corn to eat. 

One day, Lily's mom told her they were going to prepare a special dinner. Lily was excited and asked what they were going to eat. Her mom said it was a surprise. 

Lily helped her mom prepare the corn by shucking it and washing it. She could smell the delicious aroma coming from the kitchen. 

Finally, dinner was ready. Lily's mom brought out a big pot of corn chowder. It was the most delicious thing Lily had ever tasted. She was so happy that they could make such a tasty meal with just a few simple ingredients. From that day on, Lily never felt poor again because she knew that with a little preparation, they could make something amazing.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who lived on a farm. Her name was Daisy and she was three years old. One day, Daisy went outside and saw a funny sheep. It was making strange noises and Daisy started to laugh.

"What are you joking about?" she asked the sheep. But the sheep just kept making the same noise.

"I think he likes to joke!" said Daisy's dad. 

Daisy nodded and looked around the farm. Everything was so green and beautiful. "This is amazing!" she said.

Then Daisy saw a chicken and it had the most beautiful skin she had ever seen. Daisy wanted to touch it, but her dad said no. "It doesn't like strangers to touch its skin," he said. 

But Daisy smiled and said, "That's ok, I still think it's amazing!" 

Daisy went to bed that night thinking about all the amazing things she had seen on the farm. She had seen a funny sheep joke and a chicken with beautiful skin.

Once upon a time, there was a little boat named Bob. Bob lived in a harbor. The harbor was big and dark at night.

One day, Bob met a big boat named Betty. Betty said, "Hi Bob! Want to play with me?" Bob said, "Yes, let's play soak!" So, they splashed water on each other and had fun.

As the sun went down, the harbor became dark. Bob and Betty went home. They said, "Good night!" to each other. They were happy and tired from playing soak all day.

Once there was a boy named John. He wanted to go get an ice cream cone. He went to the store with his mom and saw all the different flavors. He looked around until he saw something special and it made him smile. It was a blue ice cream cone! He was so excited and quickly asked his mom to order it for him. His mom said yes and ordered the blue cone for him. John was so happy, the blue cone looked so delicious and he couldn't wait to eat it. He went outside and ate the ice cream cone so quickly he finished it in no time. It was so tasty and he smiled with joy. He said "Mom can I have another blue cone please?" His mom smiled and said yes.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Abi. Every day Abi would go to the beach and build sandcastles. One day, Abi went to the beach with her parents to build a sandcastle. But just as they were finishing the sandcastle, it started to rain. 

Abi's parents were worried that Abi would get wet and they quickly said goodbye to the beach. When they arrived home, Abi was presented with a towering stack of towels. Abi was so happy! She received the tower of towels with immense joy.

Her mother said, "these towels will keep you warm and dry Abi. However, you must use them modestly, one per day". Abi nodded and thanked her mother for the towels.

The next day Abi took one of the towels to the beach with her. She dried herself off with the towel and kept warm in the modest towel. 

Abi had a wonderful day at the beach. She was so happy she had received the tower of towels.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. They have a meeting every day after lunch. They share their toys and snacks.

One day, a big boy comes to the park. He sees Lily and Ben. He wants to play with their toys. He does not ask. He just takes them. He teases Lily and Ben. He says they are silly and small.

Lily and Ben are sad and angry. They want their toys back. They think of a plan. They are clever. They pretend to cry. They say they want to go home.

The big boy laughs. He thinks he won. He puts the toys down. He walks away. He does not see Lily and Ben. They stop crying. They run to their toys. They pick them up. They smile.

They have their toys back. They are happy. They say bye to the big boy. They say he is not nice. They go to their meeting. They play and share. They are friends.

Billy was playing in the park. He saw a big, bald man throwing a ball. Billy wanted to try too. He ran over and asked the bald man if he could throw the ball too. The man said yes, so Billy picked up the ball and used all his muscles to throw it far away. He was so proud of himself! The bald man smiled when he saw how far Billy threw the ball. Billy was so happy he could throw the ball almost as far as the bald man. Billy and the bald man kept throwing the ball together until Billy got tired. It was a fun day!

Once upon a time, there was a girl called Katie. She was 3 years old and she loved to explore. One day, she was walking through the woods, poking at things with a stick.

Suddenly, she spotted a jug. It was red and shiny, and it was sitting in the middle of the forest. Katie was so excited that she started poking it with her stick.

The jug moved, and Katie felt uncomfortable. She wanted to run away, but she was too curious. She poked a little harder, and then the jug opened!

Inside the jug was a little mouse. The mouse was so scared that it started to shake, so Katie picked it up and patted it until it felt calmer.

So, Katie and the mouse became friends and they had a great time together, exploring the woods. Because of Katie's poke, they were able to have a wonderful adventure together.

Sara and Tom were happy. They moved to a new house with Mom and Dad. They had many boxes with their things. They wanted to unpack and play.

Mom and Dad said, "First, we need to unpack the big things. Like the beds, the sofa, the table and the chairs. Then, you can help us unpack the small things. Like your toys, your books, your clothes and your pictures."

Sara and Tom nodded. They waited for Mom and Dad to unpack the big things. They looked out the window. They saw a person walking a dog. The person was regular. The dog was not. The dog was very big and very fluffy. It looked like a bear.

Sara and Tom ran to the door. They wanted to see the dog. They opened the door and shouted, "Hello, person! Hello, dog!"

The person and the dog stopped. They looked at Sara and Tom. The person smiled. The dog wagged its tail.

"Hello, kids!" the person said. "We are your new neighbors. My name is Anna. And this is Bruno. He is a friendly dog. Do you want to pet him?"

Sara and Tom nodded. They ran to Anna and Bruno. They petted the dog. He licked their faces. They laughed.

Mom and Dad came to the door. They saw Sara and Tom with Anna and Bruno. They smiled.

"Hello, Anna. Hello, Bruno. We are Sara and Tom's parents. We just moved here. We are happy to meet you."

"Hello, parents. We are happy to meet you too. Welcome to the neighborhood. Do you need any help to unpack?"

Mom and Dad thanked Anna. They said they were almost done. They invited Anna and Bruno to come in. They said they had cookies and juice.

Sara and Tom were happy. They made new friends. They forgot about the boxes. They wanted to play with Bruno. They thought he was the best dog ever.

Once upon a time, there was a lovely little girl called Sarah. She was only three years old and she loved to play. Everywhere she went she would take her crayons. 

One afternoon, the sun was shining and Sarah decided to go for a walk in the park. She was colouring the leaves with her crayons when she heard a voice.

"Hi Sarah, what are you doing?"

Sarah looked up to see a friendly old lady. "I'm drawing!" Sarah said excitedly.

The old lady smiled. "It looks lovely. I bet your mum and dad love it too!"

Sarah nodded. "I love them and they love me!"

The old lady smiled again. "Of course they do! That is what love is all about." 

Sarah felt happy and she said goodbye to the old lady. She put her crayons in her pocket and went home with a big smile on her face.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy who wanted to learn lots of new words. So he asked his mom if he could borrow a dictionary from the library. His mom said yes, so the little boy was very excited.

The next day, the little boy and his mom went to the library. There were lots and lots of books. The librarian found some big black dictionaries for the little boy.

The librarian smiled and said, "These black dictionaries have lots of words that you can learn. I'm going to lend them to you for two weeks."

The little boy quickly thanked the librarian, and he grabbed the two big black dictionaries. He raced home and began reading the books right away.

He had so much fun learning new words in the big black dictionaries. He kept them for two weeks and then returned them to the library. He thanked the librarian again, and said he was really happy to borrow the dictionaries.

One day, Mary and her little brother John were walking around in the park. Suddenly, they saw something enormous! In the middle of the park was a beautiful white display. There was an amazing display of white flowers everywhere! 

Mary and John were so excited that they ran closer. John noticed a big white butterfly and tried to get it, but it flew away. 

"John, you need to respect nature," said Mary. "You can look at all these wonderful things, but you also have to take care of them."

John thought about it for a moment and nodded. "You're right," he said. 

From then on, whenever Mary and John visited the park, they respected the white display of flowers and took care of them. 

The moral of the story is that we should appreciate and take care of the things we have in nature.

There was a quiet jungle in the middle of the town. In this jungle there was a little toy store where a boy named Jack often played with his toys.

One day, Jack was playing by the store when he saw something special. It was a big, green toy. He wanted it very much.

He went into the store to ask the toy seller how much it was.

"How much do you want for the big, green toy?" Jack asked.

"That will be five coins," the toy seller replied.

Jack paid the toy seller and then ran outside to play with the special toy. He was so happy to have it in his hands. 

The toy seller smiled. He was happy that he was able to sell the special toy.

Once upon a time there was a boy who was playing outside in a park. His name was Todd and he had lots of fun. He was running and jumping but then he stumbled and bumped his knee. He cried very loud.

A kind lady came over and said, "Oh, what a mess! Let's see if your shoe can help. Do you have a buckle?"

Todd nodded and wiped away his tears. He went to his shoe and showed the woman the buckle. 

The woman knelt next to Todd and said, "Look, let's try to buckle the shoe tight to help your leg not hurt. See how this buckle can be pushed onto the shoe?"

Todd watched and nodded. He tried to buckle his shoe and soon it was really tight and felt better. He smiled and thanked the lady. 

The lady smiled and said, "Oh, your shoe looks much better now that it's not so messy. Have fun playing!"

And Todd was back to playing outside, happy and no longer in pain.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy who wanted very much to ride in an aeroplane. He looked up at the sky and could see the planes flying above, and he hoped and hoped that one day he would be able to ride in one. 

One day, his wish came true! His parents took him to a special place called an airport. He saw lots of aeroplanes getting ready to fly up high. He was so excited! 

The little boy said goodbye to his parents and they gave him a big hug. Then he climbed into a big aeroplane and it flew up up into the sky. The view was beautiful and he saw lots of little houses, trees and rivers far below.

The little boy was so happy that he laughed and clapped his hands. He got a little snack too - some sour lemon candy! He loved it and ate it quickly. 

The aeroplane flew for a long time before it finally flew back down to the airport. The little boy kept hoping and hoping that he would be able to ride in an aeroplane again one day.

John was standing outside with his mom. He imagined what it would be like to have a peach in his hand. It would be so juicy and sweet. He could almost taste it.

His mom looked down at him and said, "Do you want to go to the store and get a peach, John?"

John's eyes lit up. He nodded in excitement and followed his mom to the store.

John and his mom got to the store, and he could not believe his eyes. The peaches were all so big and juicy. He carefully chose a pale peach that looked like a dream.

John ran up to his mom and showed her the peach. He waited with anticipation as she paid for it. They walked out of the store and waited for the other side of the street to be clear so they could cross.

When it was clear, John's mom held his hand, and they crossed the street. She opened the peach and shared it with John. It was sweet and juicy, just as he imagined it.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Jenna. Jenna was just three years old. She loved exploring the outdoors and playing with animals. 

One day, Jenna went to the woods to spend time with her friends. Suddenly, she heard a loud roar coming from the trees. Jenna was so scared that she started to cry. 

"Don't worry, Jenna," one of her friends said. "It's just a powerful monster."

Jenna wanted to run away, but her friends said they wanted to stay and see what it was. Jenna was still scared, but she followed her friends. 

When they reached the monster, they saw it was very big and powerful. Jenna was so scared that she started trembling. Her friends noticed and told her that they would protect her. 

Jenna was relieved to know her friends would help her. The monster was of course a bit scared, as well. Slowly, she and her friends started to spend time with the monster and soon, the monster had become their best friend.

Once upon a time, there was a huge garden with lots of different plants and flowers. Every day, at noon the sun would shine down and something special would happen. All the flowers in the garden would begin to bloom! Big red roses would turn upwards, tiny daisies would stretch out and enormous sunflowers would show their bright faces.

The garden was very beautiful and everybody who visited it couldn't help but smile. Days were filled with the bees buzzing over the petals and the birds singing in the trees. Even at night the garden was twinkling with fireflies lighting up the dark sky.

As time passed, the garden continued to get more and more beautiful. It seemed like every time the sun shone down its beauty would increase. Soon enough, everyone in the town began to marvel at the garden and its enormous blooms. It had become a special part of the town and everyone was happy.

Once upon a time, there was a young child named Leo. Leo loved playing with all his toys, his stuffed animals and his car. One sunny day, Leo wanted to go outside and play in the park.

When Leo arrived to the park, he was so excited to run and play on the monkey bars. But when he got there, something strange had happened. All of the fellow children were standing still, they weren't moving at all! Leo was so surprised and asked what was happening.

The other children told him that they were playing a game called "freeze". He had to stop when someone yelled out "freeze". It was a lot of fun, so Leo joined in with them.

But as the game went on, Leo started to feel a little upset because he was playing for so long and felt like he was missing out on something. One of the other children explained to Leo that he could stop playing at any time, and then do his job. 

The other children called out to Leo and reminded him that he had work to do too. Leo was happy that his friends were looking out for him and he finished the game and went off to do his job.

The moral of the story is that it is important to take breaks between playing and doing your job. Doing something you are required to do can prevent us from feeling upset in the long run.

Once upon a time, there was a boy called Jim. Jim was only three years old and he was worried because he wanted to iron his mum's dress.

He asked his mum where the iron was. His mum reached high up and got it down from the top shelf. It was big and the handle was long.

Jim looked at the iron and he was worried because it was so big. His mum smiled and told him not to worry. She helped him plug in the iron, switch it on and showed him how it worked.

Jim was so happy that he could help iron his mum's dress. He smiled as he ironed and even though the iron was big, he wasn't worried anymore.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily was playing with her toys when her mom asked her to help clean the house. Lily didn't want to clean, but her mom said, "If you help me clean, we can play afterwards." 

Lily agreed and started to mop the floor. While she was mopping, she saw some dust and sneezed. "Bless you," said her mom. "Thank you," said Lily. 

After they finished cleaning, Lily's mom said, "We did a good job. Now, what do you want to play?" Lily thought for a moment and said, "Let's play with my dolls." Her mom smiled and said, "That sounds like a fun idea. Your dolls are available in your room." 

Lily ran to her room and started to play with her dolls. She was happy that she helped her mom and now she could play with her favorite toys. The end.

Once upon a time there was a giant. He was tall, strong, and always smiled. Everywhere he went people thanked him for his kindness.

One day, he went to the beach. He found a small smooth stone and picked it up. It was round and felt nice in his hand. 

He looked around for a place to put it. Then he saw a little boy and said, "Would you like this stone?"

The boy's face lit up and smiled. He said, "Yes, thank you giant!"

The giant smiled and said, "You're welcome! Enjoy your smooth stone." He waved goodbye to the boy and walked away. 

The little boy thanked the giant again and hugged his new smooth stone.

Once there was a little boy named Jack. He was sad because he had been complaining all day. He wanted to go out and play, but it was raining outside. 
Jack's mother wanted to cheer him up, so she told him a story. 
She said, "Once upon a time, there was a beautiful princess. She was always happy, until one day she fell and hurt her arm."
Jack stopped complaining and listened.
His mother continued, "The princess was really sad, because she couldn't do the things she loved to do. But then one day, she met a friendly dragon who helped her. He showed her that it was ok to be sad, but also it was important to be brave and try new things. "
Jack smiled. He was happy to hear the story and started to feel better. He decided to brave the rain and go out and play. 
He waved goodbye to his mother and said, "Thank you for the story, it made me feel better when I was sad and complaining." His mother smiled and waved back.

Sara and Ben are twins. They like to go to the museum with Mom and Dad. The museum has many things to see and learn. Sara likes the animals and Ben likes the cars.

One day, they go to the museum and see a big sign. The sign says "Hide and Seek". Sara and Ben love to play hide and seek. They ask Mom and Dad if they can play. Mom and Dad say yes, but they have to stay in the same room and not run or touch anything.

Sara and Ben start to play. Sara counts to ten and Ben runs to hide. He sees a big car with a shiny hood. He thinks it is a good hiding spot. He crawls under the car and waits for Sara to find him.

Sara looks around the room. She sees many cars, but not Ben. She thinks he is very good at hiding. She walks to the other side of the room and sees a helpful lady. The lady wears a badge that says "Museum Guide". Sara asks the lady, "Have you seen my brother? He is hiding from me."

The lady smiles and says, "I think I have. He is under the car with the shiny hood. Do you want me to show you?"

Sara nods and says, "Yes, please. Thank you for being helpful."

The lady takes Sara to the car and points under the hood. Sara sees Ben's feet sticking out. She says, "I found you, Ben! You are a good hider, but the lady helped me."

Ben crawls out from under the car and says, "You are a good finder, Sara. And the lady is very nice. Can we say thank you to her?"

Sara and Ben say thank you to the lady and give her a hug. The lady says, "You are very welcome. You are both very polite and smart. I hope you enjoy the museum."

Sara and Ben smile and say, "We do. We love the museum. And we love playing hide and seek."
