The car smiled and said, â€œYes! I can read you.â€

The words smiled and said, â€œGreat! Letâ€™s go for a ride!â€

So the car and the words went for a ride. They had a lot of fun! The car read the words and the words told stories. They both had a wonderful time!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Amy. She had a lot of toys. One of her favorites was a colorful toy boat. She liked to take it out and play with it in her bathtub.

One day, Amy was playing with the boat in the bathtub, when suddenly it started to rain! The little boat started to soak up the water and sink. Amy cried out in fear.

But then, something amazing happened. Her mommy came and took the boat out. She carefully dried it off and put it back in the tub.

Now, instead of sinking, the colorful boat floated all around the tub! Amy was so happy and she splashed and played with it for hours! 

Every time it started to rain, Amy's mommy would come to the rescue and make sure her special boat stayed safe and colorful. 

The end!

Lily liked to help her mom in the house. She liked to wipe the table and the chairs with a cloth. She liked to wipe the dust from the books and the toys. She liked to wipe the windows and make them shiny.

One day, Lily wanted to help her mom with the fireplace. She saw some ashes and some wood on the floor. She thought they were dirty. She took her cloth and tried to wipe them. But the cloth got black and the ashes flew in the air. Lily coughed and sneezed.

Mom heard Lily and came to see what was wrong. She saw Lily with a black cloth and a dirty face. She saw the ashes and the wood on the floor. She saw the fireplace was cold and empty. She was not angry, but she was worried.

Mom hugged Lily and said, "Lily, you are a good helper, but you should not wipe the fireplace. The fireplace is not for wiping. The fireplace is for making fire. Fire is hot and bright and cozy. But fire can also be dangerous and hurt you. You should never touch the fireplace without me or dad."

Mom took Lily to the bathroom and washed her face and hands. She threw away the black cloth and got a new one. She cleaned the floor and the fireplace. She put some new wood in the fireplace and lit a match. She made a fire that was hot and bright and cozy. She and Lily sat on the couch and watched the fire. Lily felt warm and happy. She said, "Mom, I love you and I love the fireplace. But I will not wipe it again." Mom smiled and said, "I love you too, Lily. And I love that you want to help. But next time, let's wipe something else."

Billy was playing in his garden when he heard someone crying. He was curious, so he went to investigate. He found a little girl, who was sitting in front of an oven.

Billy asked her why she was crying. The girl looked up at him, and said "My mommy is gone, and I am so very spoiled. I am all alone now."

Billy was very sad when he heard what the girl said, but he was determined to help her. He searched all around for her mommy, but he could not find her anywhere.

Finally, Billy had to tell the girl the bad news - her mommy was not coming back. The girl cried and cried, but Billy held her tight and told her everything was going to be alright.

The moral of the story is that even in times of sadness, it can still be important to help others in need.

Once upon a time, there was a mom and dad and their three-year-old daughter. The daughter loved to imagine. One day, the daughter imagined there was a fierce storm outside. The weather was wild and windy. Lightning filled the sky!

The daughter was scared, so the mom and dad hugged her and helped her feel safe. They told her that if she ever felt scared, she could just imagine herself in a sunny playground, with butterflies and sweet-smelling flowers.

This made the daughter feel much better. She imagined a bright and sunny world, with no fierce weather. She also imagined playing with her family, and having lots of fun. The daughter felt very happy - just thinking of the sunshine made her forget all about the fierce storm outside!

Lily and Max liked to play in the swamp behind their house. They liked to make mud pies and look for frogs and bugs. But one day, they saw a big truck near the swamp. The truck had a loud noise and a long hose. The hose was sucking up all the water from the swamp.

"Hey, stop that!" Lily shouted at the truck. "You are taking our swamp away!"

The truck driver did not hear her. He was busy with his hose. He wanted to make the swamp empty and dry. He said the swamp was dirty and smelly and bad for the town.

Max ran to the truck and tried to pull the hose. He was angry and scared. He did not want to lose his swamp. He loved the swamp and all the animals in it.

"Let go, kid!" the truck driver said. He pushed Max away. "This is my job. I have to make the swamp empty and dry. It is good for the town."

Lily and Max did not think so. They thought the swamp was good for the town too. They thought the swamp was beautiful and fun and full of life. They did not want to see it empty and dry.

They ran back to their house and told their mom what was happening. Their mom was surprised and worried. She did not know about the truck and the hose. She did not know why someone wanted to make the swamp empty and dry.

She called the town hall and asked some questions. She found out that the truck and the hose belonged to a company that wanted to build a new mall on the swamp land. She did not like that idea. She liked the swamp and all the animals in it too.

She told Lily and Max to get their coats and boots. She said they were going to the swamp to stop the truck and the hose. She said they were going to make the swamp wet and full again. She said they were going to save the swamp and all the animals in it.

Lily and Max smiled and cheered. They were happy and proud. They followed their mom to the swamp. They were ready to make a difference.

Once upon a time, there were two best friends. One day, the friends wanted to do something fun. So, they decided to form a band!

The friends told each other what instruments they wanted to play. One of them wanted to play the drums and the other wanted to play the guitar. They could hardly wait to get started.

After getting their instruments, the friends practiced day and night. They made lots of noise, but it was a happy noise! Soon they were ready to play their first show.

The friends told everyone about the show, and soon the place was packed! Everyone was so excited to hear their music. When the band started playing, everyone was charmed by their music.

After the show, everyone wanted to hear more from the band. The two friends were so pleased that everyone liked their music. They also knew that their band was just the beginning of a wonderful adventure!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and eat yummy snacks. One day, Lily saw her mommy putting on makeup and she wanted to try it too. 

Lily's mommy warned her that makeup was only for grown-ups and it wasn't safe for little children. But Lily didn't listen and she pulled her mommy's makeup off the table. She put on the lipstick and eyeshadow, thinking she looked pretty.

But when Lily's mommy saw her, she was very upset. She explained that pulling things without permission was wrong and that makeup wasn't for little kids. Lily felt bad and apologized. From then on, she learned to always ask before taking things and to wait until she was older to play with makeup.

Once there lived two friends in the woods, Mary and John. Mary was very patient and John liked to explore.

One day, Mary spotted a deer in the woods. She pointed to it and excitedly said to John, "Look! A deer!"

John looked and said, "Let's go closer!" Mary nodded in agreement. 

Cautiously, the two friends approached the deer. Suddenly, the deer stopped, raising its head and it's front legs and looked towards Mary and John. Mary could see it was about to sign.

John exclaimed, "That looks like a sign!"

"Yes," Mary replied, "the deer wants us to stay and talk." 

John and Mary leaned close to the deer, both of them full of curiosity. The deer stayed still and watched the two friends with its big brown eyes.

The deer was patient and taught the two friends how to survive in the woods. Mary and John were so thankful and waved goodbye to the deer as they left. 

At that moment, the deer knew it had done its job.

Jim heard a loud noise outside. He saw a large truck in front of his house and he was curious. He went over to investigate. Jim noticed two strong men were pulling a big couch out of the back of the truck. He realized it was a sofa and thought it was just what his family needed.

The men put the large couch inside the living room. Everyone was so happy. Jim's mom began to hug the couch while his dad smiled. His mom said it was the best gift ever and that she loved it.

Jim knew that the love his family shared was even bigger than the large couch he had been given. He saw how it was already making his home even more special. He was happy and pulled his family together for a group hug to thank them for such a wonderful gift.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved playing with his toys. One day, he found a medal on the ground. It was shiny and had a star on it. He showed it to his mom and asked, "What is this?"

"It's a medal, Timmy. It's like a prize for doing something good," his mom replied.

Timmy was so happy to have found a medal. He wore it around his neck and showed it to all his friends. But one day, he accidentally stepped on it and it became flexible. "Oh no, I destroyed my medal," Timmy said with a sad face.

"Don't worry, Timmy. It's okay. You can still keep it and remember the good times you had with it," his mom said, trying to cheer him up.

Timmy smiled and realized that even though his medal was no longer shiny and perfect, it still held a special place in his heart.

Once upon a time, there was a girl. She had lots of stuff. Her stuff was new and pretty.
Every day, the girl would go outside and play for hours. One day, when she was done playing, she came back inside... and all her stuff was gone. She looked around, but she couldn't see it anywhere.
Suddenly she realized - someone had taken her stuff! Her stuff had disappeared.
The girl felt very sad. She was upset that someone had taken her pretty new stuff.
But then, something really magical happened! The girl looked around and she realized that her stuff had come back! She was so happy - all her stuff was there, just as it was before.
The girl was so glad to have her stuff back - she promised to take better care of it from now on. And she was never sad again!

Once upon a time, there was a big fire in the forest. The animals were scared and ran away. But the brave firefighters came to prevent the fire from spreading. They used big hoses to spray water on the flames. 

One firefighter saw a little bird's nest in a tree. He climbed up high to get it down safely. The little bird was happy and chirped loudly. 

After a while, the fire was put out and the animals came back to their homes. The little bird saw a match on the ground and was curious. But the firefighter told the bird that matches are dangerous and should only be used by grown-ups. The little bird learned an important lesson and was grateful for the firefighter's help.

Once upon a time there was a big bird. He wanted to design something special, but he didn't know what to do. He asked some of his friends and they all had different ideas. One thought he should make a nest, one thought he should make a rainbow and another thought he should make some new law.

The big bird thought about it and decided to design something that could make everyone happy. He decided to make a friendly law that everyone wanted to follow. He worked day and night to design the law and finally he brought the law to the people of the forest.

The people loved the friendly law and both the animals and birds in the forest were happy. They were no longer fighting and instead were being kind to each other. The big bird was pleased with what he had done and he was also very proud of himself.

The moral of the story is that designing something with a friendly purpose will always be better. It makes everyone happy and that's what really matters.

Once there was a kid named Lucy. She really wanted to go in a tent, so she asked Mom if she could go. Her Mom said yes, and she was so excited!

All of Lucy's friends were talking about a popular tent that was in the park. Everyone wanted to go and see it. so Lucy said goodbye to Mom and went to the park. 

When she got there, Lucy saw the big, popular tent. She wanted to go inside, so she ran up, opened the door and held it opened with both her hands. 

But when she looked inside, she saw that it wasn't just a tent, but a huge indoor playground! There were slides, swings and all sorts of fun things. Lucy couldn't believe it - she was so excited that she ran inside and started playing. 

Since then, the popular tent has been Lucy's favorite place to be. Whenever she asks Mom to go, they never say no!

Ben and Mia like to play in the park. They skip and run and laugh. They see a big hill with a lot of flowers. They want to go up the hill and pick some flowers.

But on the way, they see a hole in the ground. It is a trap. Someone put a trap there to catch animals. Ben and Mia are scared. They do not want to fall in the trap.

They see a man near the trap. He is bald and mean. He has a net and a cage. He wants to catch animals and sell them. He sees Ben and Mia and says, "Hey, you kids, get away from my trap. It is not for you. It is for rabbits and squirrels and birds."

Ben and Mia do not like the man. They do not like his trap. They want to help the animals. They have an idea. They say, "OK, we will go away. But can we give you a flower? It is very pretty and smells good."

The man thinks they are silly. He says, "A flower? What do I need a flower for? But OK, give me one. Maybe it will make me lucky."

Ben and Mia pick a flower from the hill. But they do not give it to the man. They throw it in the trap. The trap snaps shut. The man is angry. He says, "Hey, you tricked me. You are bad kids. Let me out of here."

Ben and Mia laugh. They say, "No, we are good kids. We saved the animals. You are a bad man. You should not hurt animals. Stay in the trap until someone finds you."

They skip and run away. They are happy. They did a good thing. They go to the hill and pick more flowers. They give them to their mom and dad. They tell them the story. Their mom and dad are proud of them. They hug them and kiss them. They say, "You are brave and smart and kind. We love you very much."

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Megan. She was three years old and liked to explore the world around her. 
One day, Megan went for a walk in the forest. She saw a hairy stage and stopped to look at it. She wondered what she should do. 
"Maybe I could play on the stage," she said to herself. 
But then, Megan remembered what her mother had said: "Mind the stage, Megan, and be careful!" 
Megan did not want to be naughty, so she decided to just look at the hairy stage and keep her distance. 
She smiled and said, "That's a good idea. I will mind the stage and be careful. That's the right thing to do." 
So Megan looked at the hairy stage, quietly admiring its beauty. Then she continued on her walk.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved to observe. Every day she would look at the birds in the trees and the people walking by her house. One day, she decided to go to the store. The store was full of sweet treats and the girl could not wait to get one. She looked around and saw an ice cream that she wanted. She reached up to grab it, but it was too high for her to reach. The girl felt sad. But then she noticed a sweet box of cookies. She smiled and reached out to grab them. As she enjoyed her treats, she continued to observe her surroundings. It was such a beautiful day.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny named Benny. Benny was very scared of the dark and he always felt fearful when he had to go to bed at night. One night, Benny's mommy came into his room to tuck him in and she noticed that he was very scared. She asked him what was wrong and Benny told her that he was afraid of the dark.

Mommy bunny comforted Benny and told him that she would always be there to protect him. She also told him a story about a bunny who got trapped in a hole but was able to escape by using his strong legs. Benny listened to the story and felt much better. He hugged his mommy and went to sleep feeling safe and happy.

Once upon a time there was a graceful girl. She loved to draw pictures. Every day she would finish the most beautiful drawings.

One day the girl was very tired. She wanted to finish her picture, but she was too tired. She laid down and closed her eyes.

As she slept, she dreamt about the picture. When she woke up, the picture had finished itself, and it was even more beautiful than she had imagined! The girl clapped her hands with delight.

So from then on, whenever the girl was too tired to finish a picture, she would take a nap. And when she woke up, it would be finished - graceful and beautiful. And she was very happy.

Once upon a time there were two best friends, Sam and Joe. Sam was very small and always laughed a lot. Joe was a bit bigger and was very obedient. 

One day, Sam and Joe were playing in their backyard when they heard a loud noise. It was coming from their neighbour's garden. They decided to peek in and found a tiny puppy stuck in the mud.

Sam said, "let's help him to escape!"
Joe said, "yes, let's do it!"

They quickly filled a bucket of water and helped the puppy to drink. The puppy felt much better and was able to run around again!

Sam and Joe were very happy. They waved goodbye to the puppy and went inside to have a drink.

The end.

Once there was a mommy and her little boy. Mommy was always very busy working around the house. One day, she was in the kitchen using her mixer. The little boy asked mommy what she was doing, but she just shrugged. He asked why and mommy said she was making a treat. Mommy was so busy that the little boy couldn't help her, so he decided to just watch her while she worked. After a while, mommy finished and said the treat was ready. The little boy was so excited and couldn't wait to try it!

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Daisy. Daisy was very happy but she was also very curious. She wanted to know everything! One day, she asked her mum if she could have a shower. Her mum said yes, Daisy was so excited.

When Daisy was in the shower, she noticed how graceful the warm water felt. She wiped the droplets off the shower wall with her finger and watched them twinkle like rainbows. She reached around with her hands, looking for things to explore. Suddenly, she felt something tickle her toe. 

Daisy looked down to find a small dragon! Daisy smiled and asked the dragon what his name was. The dragon replied, â€œMy name is Sparks! I live in the shower and can make wonderful things happen. Would you like me to show you?â€ 

Daisy nodded her head and almost immediately, the shower filled with water shaped like horses and castles! She smiled and laughed as the water danced around her.

When Daisy got out of the shower, she was so happy. She thanked Sparks and made sure to remember the wonderful magic he showed her.

Once upon a time, there was a big, pretty boat called a yacht. It was very attractive. The yacht had many colors, like red, blue, and yellow. It looked nice on the water.

One day, a nice man went on the yacht. He wanted to provide food for his friends. He had apples, bananas, and cookies. They were very yummy. His friends were happy to eat the food on the pretty yacht.

They all had a fun day on the attractive yacht. They played games, ate food, and laughed a lot. The sun was shining, and the water was calm. It was a great day for everyone on the pretty yacht.

Once there was a girl named Daisy. Daisy wanted to have some new clothes, so she went to the store. She saw a beautiful cloth with bright colors and shapes on it. She wanted to own it. 

"Can I buy this cloth?" Daisy asked the shopkeeper.

"Yes, of course," the shopkeeper smiled.

So Daisy gave the shopkeeper some money and then the shopkeeper gave Daisy the cloth. Daisy was very happy. She took the cloth and went home. 

When she arrived home, Daisy wanted to make clothes out of the cloth. But it was hard and Daisy didn't know how. 

Daisy asked her mom for help. Her mom showed Daisy how to use needles, thread and scissors to sew the cloth and make new clothes. Daisy was excited and together they made a dress. 

When they finished the dress, Daisy tried it on. It fit her perfectly and it looked even better than the cloth in the store. Daisy was so happy with her new dress and she owned it!

Annie lived in a great big house with her family. Every day, Annie's mommy would give her a special stack of cards. Annie received them with a huge smile on her face. 
 
One day, Annie's mommy said, "Annie, I've been working on something special for you. Take a look outside the window." 
 
Annie went to the window and saw a great big pile of toys! She was so happy that she jumped up and down and said, "I receive it! Thank you mommy!" 
 
Annie's mommy said, "You are welcome. I hope you can play with your new toys and have lots of fun." 
 
Annie ran outside and started playing with the stack of toys. She was so happy that she shouted, "This is the greatest stack of toys ever!"

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim had a toy saw that he loved to play with. He liked to pretend that he was a builder and built many things with his saw. One day, Tim saw a big tree in his yard. He wanted to build something with the tree, so he went to get his saw.

Tim started to cut the tree with his saw. He tried very hard, but the tree seemed too big for him. He got upset because he could not cut it. Tim's mom saw him and told him to stop. She said the tree was too big for him to cut with his toy saw. Tim did not listen to his mom and kept trying to cut the tree.

Then, as Tim was cutting the tree, it fell down. The tree fell on Tim's playhouse and broke it. Tim was very upset. He cried because his playhouse was broken. His mom told him that he should have listened to her. Now, Tim did not have a playhouse to play in anymore. The ending was bad for Tim because he did not listen to his mom.

Molly was playing in her backyard when she heard a fierce noise. She looked up and saw a missile shooting through the sky. Molly jumped into a puddle and started to splash.

"What are you doing?" said her mom.

"I'm splashing!" yelled Molly. "The missile was fierce so I wanted to be safe!"

Mom laughed and said, "That's a good idea, but I think the missile is gone now."

Molly peeked out of the puddle and looked around. The sky was clear, so she stopped splashing and came out of the puddle.

"I'm glad the missile is gone," she said.

"Me too," said Mom. She gave Molly a big hug and said, "Let's go back inside now."

Molly and Mom went inside, and Molly stopped worrying about the fierce missile.

Once upon a time, there was a mechanic named Tom. Tom liked to prepare cars. He made them go fast and smooth. Tom was very good at his job.

One day, it was very bitter outside. It was cold and windy. Tom went to work and saw a car that needed help. The car was sad because it could not go fast. Tom wanted to help the car.

Tom worked hard to prepare the car. He fixed the parts and made it better. The car was happy and could go fast again. Tom was happy too. He went home, feeling warm inside even though it was still bitter outside.

Once upon a time, there was a dancer named Sandy. She was a beautiful dancer and she loved to perform for her family and friends.

One day, Sandy got hurt and she was very upset. She had hurt her ankle and was worried she would never dance again.

Sandy's mother saw how distressed she was, so she decided to help. She put a bandage on Sandy's ankle and sang her a special healing song. She said, "Everyone gets hurt sometimes, but that doesn't mean you can't still dance. With a little time and patience, you will heal and be dancing again!" 

And that's exactly what happened. Sandy's ankle healed and she could dance again. She remembered the lesson her mom had taught her; that sometimes when life is tough, the best thing to do is to be patient and give it time. Eventually, you will heal and be better than before!

Once upon a time there was a heavy truck. The truck belonged to a man called Ben. One day, the truck stopped working, so Ben took it to a mechanic.

When Ben arrived at the mechanic's shop, the mechanic told him that the truck had frozen. He said it needed fixing before Ben could drive it away.

Ben asked the mechanic, "Can you fix it?"

The mechanic looked at the truck and said, "Yes, I will fix it. But it will take me some time."

So Ben left the truck at the mechanic's shop and came back a few days later.

When he arrived, the mechanic said, "It is fixed! You can drive your truck away now."

Ben was so happy. He drove the truck home, and it never froze again.

Lily and Ben were playing with their toys in the living room. Lily had a doll and Ben had a car. They were having fun, but they also wanted to share.

"Can I play with your car for a minute, Ben?" Lily asked.

"OK, but only for a minute. Then you give it back to me," Ben said.

Lily took the car and made it zoom around the floor. She liked the car. It was fast and shiny. Ben watched her and waited.

"Can I play with your doll for a minute, Lily?" Ben asked.

"OK, but only for a minute. Then you give it back to me," Lily said.

Ben took the doll and hugged it. He liked the doll. It was soft and pretty. Lily watched him and waited.

They played with each other's toys for a minute. Then they looked at each other and smiled.

"You know what, Ben? You can keep the car. I have another one at home," Lily said.

"Really? Thank you, Lily. You are very generous," Ben said.

"You know what, Lily? You can keep the doll. I have another one at home," Ben said.

"Really? Thank you, Ben. You are very generous, too," Lily said.

They hugged and laughed. They were happy. They did not need to trade back. They had made a new friend.

Once upon a time, there was a sailor. He loved to sail on the big sea. The sailor had a little boat. He would go far, far away. The sun was hot, and the sky was blue.

One day, the sailor felt dizzy. He did not know why. He sat down in his boat. The boat began to tremble. The sailor was scared. He held on tight to the boat.

The boat stopped trembling. The sailor felt better. He was not dizzy anymore. The sailor smiled. He was happy to sail again. The sailor and his boat went home.

Once upon a time, there was a big, red bus. The bus loved to travel. It would go up and down the road, taking people where they wanted to go. The bus was always happy to help.

One day, the bus saw some toy soldiers having a war. They were fighting and pushing each other. The bus felt guilty because it did not want to see anyone get hurt. The bus wanted to help, but it did not know how.

Then, the bus had an idea. It would take the toy soldiers away from the war and show them how fun it was to travel. The bus opened its doors and the toy soldiers climbed in. They went on a long ride, and the toy soldiers saw many new things. They were so happy, they forgot all about the war. The bus felt proud and knew it had done a good thing.

Once upon a time, there was a jet. It was huge, shiny and very expensive. Every day, the jet would zoom around the sky. It would soar high up in the air above the other planes. The jet would fly around the world.

One day, the jet flew very close to three little children. The kids were amazed and they wanted to fly too. So they asked if they could join the jet on its next journey. The jet said yes!

The three little kids climbed into the jet and soon they were soaring up high in the sky. They flew above the clouds, higher and higher. The kids felt very happy and free. 

When the jet was tired, it slowly glided back down to the ground. After saying goodbye to the jet, the three kids ran off to tell their friends about their big adventure. 

The end!

Once there was a young girl named Lena. She was only three years old and often asked her mom to take her to the sea. Lena loved to look for shells in the waves and on the shore.

One day, at the beach, Lena asked her mom if she could pick up a shrimp. Her mom said it was okay, but warned Lena that the shrimp was likely dead. Lena was excited as she found a big shrimp in the water and carefully brought it to shore.

Suddenly, the shrimp started to move! Lena gasped in surprise and asked her mom "Is the shrimp alive??". Her mom smiled and said that it was just playing - some aquatic animals pretend to be dead to avoid getting eaten by predators. Lena was so excited that her shrimp was alive and put it carefully back into the water. 

From then on she always asked her mom if the shrimp she found was really dead or just pretending. Her parents always had to remind her that if a shrimp was actually dead she should put it back in the water as quickly as possible.

Once there was a little girl who loved to dance. Every day she would spin and twirl and move her feet. She was so happy.

One day her mommy took her to the park. The little girl saw a big, loud dancer on the stage. She was so excited that she wanted to try it too!

The little girl ran up to the stage, and without any warning, she started to twirl and move her feet. Everyone laughed and smiled.

"Can I join you?" the little girl asked the dancer. 

The dancer smiled and said, "Sure thing! Come on up and show us your moves!" 

The little girl and the dancer danced together. The little girl started to throw her arms around, and the dancer threw her head back and laughed. Everyone was so happy and it was so loud. The little girl couldn't believe how much fun she was having. 

At the end, the little girl gave the dancer a big hug and thanked her. The little girl said goodbye with a smile and went to go explore the park. She couldn't wait to come back and dance with the loud dancer again!

Once upon a time, there was a big river. In the river, there lived a large crocodile. The crocodile liked to lie in the sun on the riverbank. 

One day, a little mouse came to the river to get a drink. The mouse saw the crocodile and was scared. The crocodile said, "Don't be afraid, little mouse. I won't hurt you." 

The mouse drank some water and went on its way. The crocodile watched the mouse go and thought to itself, "I could eat that little mouse if I wanted to." 

The next day, the crocodile saw the mouse again. This time, the crocodile was hungry. It remembered what it had thought before and decided to try to catch the mouse. But the mouse was too quick and ran away. The crocodile learned that it was not good to lie about being friendly.

One day, Tom went to a party. There was a big cake on the table. It was a dry cake, but it looked yummy. Tom was happy to see the cake.

At the party, Tom saw a little bug. The bug wanted to eat the cake too. Tom did not want the bug to eat the cake. He tried to pinch the bug, but it was too fast.

Tom asked his friends for help. They all tried to pinch the bug together. The bug was too fast for them too. Then, they had a good idea. They gave the bug a small piece of the dry cake. The bug was happy, and it did not bother them anymore.

Once upon a time there was a happy little girl. She liked to zoom around and have lots of fun. One day she went outside and saw a lady. The lady was walking down the street. She was wearing a colourful dress and had a big smile on her face.

The little girl wanted to say hello to the lady, so she zoomed over to her. The lady was so glad to see the girl and asked her what she was doing. The little girl said she was having fun and wanted to play. 

The lady said that the girl should go and play in the park, and then they could zoom together! The little girl was glad, so she ran to the park to play. After a while, the lady joined her, and they had lots of fun together. They ran and skipped and zoomed all around the park.

When it was time to go home, the little girl said goodbye to the lady. She thanked the lady for joining her and for making her day so wonderful. The little girl was glad that she met the lady and thought of her often after that. And they both zooming around and having lots of fun.

Once upon a time, there was a helpful dog named Spot. Spot loved to lend a paw to his friends. One sunny day, Spot went for a walk in the park.

In the park, Spot saw a girl named Lucy. Lucy was sad. "Why are you sad?" asked Spot. Lucy said, "I lost my ball in the tree." Spot wanted to help Lucy.

Spot lent a paw and jumped high to get the ball. He gave the ball to Lucy. Lucy was happy. "Thank you, Spot!" she said. From that day on, Lucy and Spot were best friends. And they played happily in the park every day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sunny. Sunny was very obedient and always did what her mommy and daddy said. One day, her mommy and daddy told her they were going on a special trip. Sunny was very excited and hoped it would be a lot of fun.

When they arrived, they saw a big gun. Sunny was scared at first, but her mommy told her it was okay. She said the gun was only for protection. Sunny believed her and wasn't scared anymore.

On the way home, Sunny told her mommy and daddy that she was thankful for the gun. She said it made her feel safe. Her mommy and daddy smiled and gave her a big hug.

They were proud that Sunny was so obedient, and that she could believe in them. From then on, Sunny felt very safe whenever they went on trips. It was a happy ending!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Daisy. Daisy was very curious and excited to explore the world around her.

One day, Daisy decided to set a little fire in her backyard. She was very careful, so she was able to build the fire in a modest size. The fire was warm and inviting.

Daisy and her friends played near the fire, telling stories and laughing. Soon, it was time to say goodbye to their fire. Daisy and her friends grabbed some buckets of water and filled them up, and then slowly poured them on the fire to put it out. Daisy made sure the fire was out before they left, and then she said goodbye to the fire. 

Daisy and her friends had lots of fun playing near the fire and were sad to see it go. But Daisy knew that it was important to keep the fire modest and to always put fires out properly.

Once there was a little boy named Bob. He was an energetic three year old and he loved playing outside. One day, Bob went outside to play in the wind. But when he got there, he felt something terrible was happening. He saw there was trash everywhere! 

Bob started to feel very sad and he said to himself, "I want to clean this up." He put on his gloves and started to pick up the trash. 

Then, a big gust of wind came through and all the trash went flying back into the air! Bob started to get frustrated and he yelled, "Why does this keep happening?!" 

Just then, Bob's mom came outside and saw what was happening. She smiled and said, "Come on Bob, let's both clean up together and next time use some rocks to hold the trash in place." 

Bob was excited for the challenge and together he and his mom began to clean up the area. Slowly but surely, Bob's playground went back to being the happy place it had been before.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved candy very much. One day, she went to the store with her mom and saw a big jar of candy. She asked her mom if she could have some, but her mom said no because she had already had too much candy that day.

Lily was sad, but then she saw a little boy who looked sad too. She asked him what was wrong, and he said he had lost his favorite toy. Lily cared about the little boy and wanted to help him, so she looked for his toy with him. They searched high and low, and finally, they found it under a bush.

The little boy was so happy and thanked Lily for being so gentle and kind. Lily felt happy too, knowing that she had helped someone else. She realized that caring about others was even better than having candy.

Tom and Lily were at the beach with their mom and dad. They liked to play in the sand and splash in the water. They saw some fish and crabs and shells. They were having fun.

"Look, Tom, a shark!" Lily said, pointing to a big gray shape in the water. She was scared.

"Don't worry, Lily, it's not a real shark. It's a toy shark. See, it has a smile and a fin. It's playful, not mean." Tom said, picking up the toy shark and showing it to Lily. He was brave.

"Are you sure, Tom? It looks like it can chew us." Lily said, still not sure.

"Trust me, Lily, it's just a toy. Here, you can hold it and see for yourself. It's soft and squeaky. It won't chew us, it will chew the sand." Tom said, giving the toy shark to Lily. He was kind.

Lily took the toy shark and felt it. It was soft and squeaky. She squeezed it and it made a funny noise. She laughed. She was not scared anymore.

"Thank you, Tom, you're right. It's a playful toy shark. Can we play with it together?" Lily said, smiling at Tom.

"Sure, Lily, we can play with it together. Let's make it swim and jump and chew the sand. It will be fun." Tom said, smiling back at Lily.

They played with the toy shark in the sand and water. They made it swim and jump and chew the sand. They had fun. They were happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Ema who wanted to fly to an island. She ran to her mom and asked if she could fly to the island. 

"Ema, I don't think you can fly to an island," her mom said.

Ema blinked in frustration. She knew that if she could just get to the island, her dreams would come true. 

She decided to try anyways. She ran to the beach, stared out at the ocean, and wished with all her might. 

Suddenly, a magical seagull appeared and flew around her. She was so happy that she jumped and laughed with joy! 

The seagull flew off in the direction of the island. Ema followed the seagull until they both landed on the island. She was so excited! 

She realized that she could make her dreams come true on the island, and she was filled with joy. She ran around laughing, and she knew that anything was possible!

Sara and Ben love to get mail from their grandma. She lives far away, but she always sends them letters and cards with stickers and stamps. Sara and Ben like to look at the stamps and see the pictures of animals, flowers, and places.

One day, they got a big envelope from grandma. Inside, there was a letter, a card, and a small box. Sara and Ben opened the box and saw four cookies. They were shaped like stars and had sprinkles on them. They smelled yummy.

"Wow, grandma made us cookies!" Sara said.

"Let's eat them!" Ben said.

They each took a cookie and bit into it. It was soft and sweet and crunchy. They smiled and said, "Mmm, yummy!"

They read the letter and the card. Grandma wrote that she missed them and loved them. She also wrote that she made the cookies for them and hoped they liked them. She said she used a special stamp to send them the box. She asked them to look at the stamp and tell her what they saw.

Sara and Ben looked at the stamp. It was a big, round, blue stamp. It had a picture of the earth and the words, "Happy Earth Day". They did not know what Earth Day was, but they liked the stamp.

"Grandma is so nice," Sara said.

"Yes, she is," Ben said.

They decided to write a thank you letter to grandma. They got some paper and crayons and drew pictures of themselves, the cookies, and the stamp. They wrote, "Thank you, grandma. We love you. The cookies are yummy. The stamp is pretty. Happy Earth Day."

They put the letter in an envelope and asked their mom to help them mail it. They hoped grandma would get it soon and be happy. They also hoped she would send them more cookies and stamps. They loved getting mail from grandma.

Once there was a little bunny named Benny. Benny was very shy and didn't like to talk to other animals. One day, he saw a big knot in a tree that worried him. He didn't know what to do about it.

Benny went to his friend, a little bird named Bobby. "Bobby, I saw a big knot in a tree and it worries me," Benny said. "Can you help me?"

Bobby flew up to the tree and pecked at the knot until it came loose. "Don't worry, Benny. I got it!" Bobby said. Benny was so happy that he hopped up and down.

From that day on, Benny wasn't as shy anymore. He knew that he could always ask his friends for help. And whenever he saw a knot, he knew that Bobby would be there to help him.

Once upon a time there was an ancient spot in the forest. A little girl named Molly took a trip to the spot to see what it was like. As she looked around, she saw that it was very old and seemed to be magical.

"What is this place?" said Molly to a nearby bird.

The bird chirped and then said, "This is an ancient spot. It has been here for many, many years."

Molly was interested in the spot so she decided to stand right in the center of it. Suddenly, she felt a tingle pass through her body.

"What was that?" said Molly, feeling a bit scared.

The bird said, "That was the magic of this spot. It will give you strength."

Molly was surprised, but also excited. She thanked the bird and then stood in the spot for a few moments more, feeling the strength it gave her. Then she waved goodbye and left the ancient spot.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Mark. He was full of energy and liked to play silly games everyday. One day, he found a piece of rope on the ground. He decided to make a waist for his teddy bear.

"Hey, Teddy, do you want a waist?" asked Mark.

His teddy couldn't answer, so Mark said, "Yes, you can have one, silly Teddy".

Mark started tying the rope around Teddy's middle and the teddy started to look like he had a waist. Mark then got some markers to decorate the waist, and when he was done his teddy was very proud of his new waist.

Marks laughed and said, "You look silly, Teddy, but it's the best waist ever!"

From then on, Mark and his teddy played all sorts of silly games together with their colourful waists.

Tom and Sam are friends. They like to play with cars and blocks. But today, they have a problem. They have to go to a big party with their moms and dads. They have to wear suits.

Tom does not like suits. He thinks they are itchy and tight. He wants to wear his red shirt and blue jeans. He says to Sam, "Suits are bad. I don't want to wear a suit. Do you?"

Sam likes suits. He thinks they are cool and smart. He wants to look like his dad. He says to Tom, "Suits are good. I want to wear a suit. You should too."

Tom and Sam start to argue. They say mean things to each other. They do not want to play anymore. They make each other sad and angry.

Their moms see them fighting. They are not happy. They say to Tom and Sam, "Stop fighting. You are friends. You have to go to the party together. You have to be nice to each other. You have to unite."

Tom and Sam do not know what unite means. They ask their moms. Their moms say, "Unite means to join and help each other. To be a team. To share and care. To have fun and be happy."

Tom and Sam think about it. They do not want to fight. They do not want to be sad and angry. They want to be friends. They want to have fun and be happy. They say sorry to each other. They hug and smile.

They decide to wear suits. But they also decide to wear something else. Something that makes them happy. Tom wears his red shirt under his suit. Sam wears his blue jeans under his suit. They look funny and cool. They laugh and run to the party.

They are nervous. They do not know many people at the party. But they have each other. They are united. They are friends. They are happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little rabbit named Benny. Benny had a very soft and fluffy tail that he loved to show off to his friends. One day, Benny's friend Sally came to visit him. Sally had a new toy, a red ball, that she wanted to play with Benny.

Benny was very excited to play with Sally and her new toy, but he was afraid his tail might get tangled in the cord of the ball. He asked Sally, "Will your toy make my tail hurt?"

Sally replied, "No, Benny. The cord is very soft and won't hurt you. Let's play!"

Benny and Sally played with the ball for a while, but then something bad happened. Benny's tail got tangled in the cord of the ball and he couldn't move. Sally tried to help him, but she couldn't untangle the cord. Benny started to cry and said, "I'm stuck! I'm stuck!"

Sally remembered what Benny had said earlier about the cord and weighed her options. She quickly ran to get some scissors and carefully cut the cord to set Benny free. From that day on, Benny and Sally made sure to play with toys that didn't have cords, so they wouldn't get tangled again.

Lily and Ben were waiting for their mom to come home. They were hungry and bored. They looked out the window and saw a big truck. The truck stopped in front of their house. The driver got out and opened the back. He took out a big box and carried it to the door.

"Who is that?" Lily asked.

"I don't know," Ben said. "Maybe he has a present for us."

They ran to the door and opened it. The driver smiled and said, "Hello, kids. I have a delivery for your mom. She ordered some pastries from the bakery. Do you know what pastries are?"

Lily and Ben nodded. They loved pastries. They were sweet and yummy and soft. They sometimes had them for breakfast or as a treat.

"Can we have some?" Lily asked.

The driver laughed and said, "Sure, why not? Your mom said you were good kids. Here, take one each. But don't eat them all. Save some for your mom, okay?"

He gave them each a pastry wrapped in paper. Lily chose a croissant with chocolate. Ben chose a muffin with blueberries. They thanked the driver and closed the door.

They sat on the couch and unwrapped their pastries. They took a big bite and smiled. They were delicious.

"Mom will be happy," Ben said.

"Yes, she will," Lily said. "But we should hide the box. It's a surprise."

They agreed and put the box under the table. They finished their pastries and licked their fingers. They heard a car in the driveway. It was their mom.

"Mom is here!" they shouted. They ran to the door and hugged her.

"Hi, kids. I missed you. How was your day?" mom asked.

"It was good," Lily said.

"It was great," Ben said.

They smiled and winked at each other. They had a secret. They couldn't wait to see mom's face when she saw the pastries. They knew she would love them too.

Once upon a time, a girl named Penny was walking through a park. She saw a colorful universe above her, with twinkling stars and white clouds. Penny was excited and said to the sky, "I want to drop something up there!" Then, a voice said, "You can't, it's too high!" Penny was sad and started to walk away. 

Then, a little boy's voice called out, "Hey, Penny! I can make it up there. I can drop a balloon for you!" Penny was so happy that she said Yes!

The little boy tied a string to a big, colorful balloon. He held the string and counted to three. On three, he let go of the string, and the balloon floated up, higher and higher, until it was out of sight. 

Penny said, "Thank you! I can't believe the balloon actually made it to the colorful universe!" 

The little boy replied, "Me too! Maybe next time we can bring something even more special." With that, Penny smiled and they both continued on their way.

Once upon a time there were two friends, a black cat named Tom and a white dog named Max. 

One day, Tom and Max decided to go on an adventure. They went into a deep and dark forest. They were both very brave, but a little scared too. 

Suddenly, Tom heard a loud noise. He stopped and was quiet. He took a deep breath and called out "Who's there?". To his surprise a big, impressive owl appeared. 

The owl said, "I am here to warn you. There is something dangerous in these woods and you must leave now". 
Tom and Max were very scared but the owl's voice was calm and polite. 

Tom was brave and thanked the owl for the warning. Then he and Max went home. They were both glad to leave the scary woods. 

From that day on, Tom and Max always remembered the owlâ€™s warning and never returned to the dark forest.

Alice was playing alone in the garden. She had a pale plastic toy car and a pale plastic boat. Suddenly her brother arrived with a friend and ignored her.
 
Alice asked: "Can I play too?"
 
But her brother and his friend ignored her. So Alice got angry and ran away to the other side of the garden. She saw an old pale plastic barrel and decided to play with it.

Alice put the car and the boat in the barrel and pretended it was a swimming pool. She played happily for a while. Then her brother and his friend came over and asked if they could play with her.

Alice smiled, took out her plastic car and boat, and said: "Yes, of course!"

Once upon a time there lived a young girl named Sandy. She lived in a big house with her family.

Every day, Sandy's mom set the alarm before leaving for work. But one day, Sandy accidentally moved the clock's hands and the alarm went off much earlier than it usually did!

Sandy ran to her mom's room and shouted, "Help! The alarm is ringing loudly!"

Her mom laughed and said, "It's alright, Sandy. We'll just turn it off."

So they both moved to the kitchen and turned off the alarm. Now they had to hurry so they would not be late.

They moved quickly throughout the house, and soon they were out the door. They had a great day and came back home in time to set the alarm again.

Once upon a time, there was a little duck named Ducky. Ducky loved to play in the water. One day, Ducky saw a big rock in the water. Ducky wanted to go on the rock, but was scared to fall in the water.

Ducky tried to balance on the rock, but kept falling in the water. Ducky was sad and wanted to go home. Suddenly, a light shone on the rock. Ducky saw that it was a firefly! The firefly said, "Don't worry, Ducky. I can help you balance on the rock."

The firefly flew around Ducky and gave Ducky the power to balance on the rock. Ducky was so happy and thanked the firefly. From that day on, Ducky could balance on any rock in the water thanks to the firefly's light.

Once upon a time there was a brown rabbit. The rabbit loved to explore. One day the rabbit was hopping through the grass, looking for something silly and fun.

Suddenly, the rabbit discovered a small hole in the ground. The hole was near a little tree and the rabbit thought it might be fun to explore the hole. When the rabbit peered inside, she saw a sparkly surprise. 

It was a tiny inchworm! The brown inchworm was shiny and pretty. The rabbit was so happy to find it that she hopped away to show her friends.

The rabbit quickly told her friends about the inchworm. They were all so excited to see it. Together, they watched the inchworm squiggle and wiggle around. The rabbit discovered that the inchworm liked to eat grass and leaves. 

The friends all enjoyed watching the inchworm for the rest of the day. The rabbit was so proud that she had found such a sparkly surprise!

Once upon a time, there were two best friends: Sarah and Michael. They loved to go on adventures together. One day they decided to go exploring in a wood.

As they walked through the wood, they came across a rare photo that someone had left behind. They were so excited and asked each other what it could be.

Sarah picked up the photo and saw that it was of a very special place. They asked each other what they should do with the photo. Michael said they should keep it safe, so they decided to put it in Sarah's pocket.

They set off to explore more of the wood, but kept an eye out for other rare things they might find. Sarah had the rare photo tucked safely away. They had a fantastic day and went home with lots of stories to tell.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there lived two friends, Tom and Tim. They always played together. One day, they decided to race. The one who would win the race would get a big clap from everyone.

The race started, and both friends ran as fast as they could. Tom was ahead, and Tim felt bad. He wanted to win, too. So, Tim thought of a plan. He picked up a rock and threw it at Tom's leg. Tom fell down and felt hurt.

Tim won the race, but no one clapped for him. They saw what he did to Tom and felt ashamed of Tim. Tim realized that cheating was wrong. He said sorry to Tom and promised never to cheat again. From that day on, they played fair and had even more fun. The moral of the story is: "winning is not important, but playing fair is."

Once there was a mule. He was very hungry. He wanted to find something to eat. He looked and looked, but he couldn't find anything to eat. He was so sad.

He started walking, and walking, and walking. He didn't know where he was going. He got tired, and he lost his way. 

He kept walking and he kept looking for something to eat. He was so hungry. 

Finally he found a farm. He went into the farm looking for some food. The farmer was happy to see him, and he gave the mule some hay to eat. The mule was so happy, and he ate all the hay. 

The mule was no longer hungry, and the farmer was happy to have a new friend. They never lost each other again.

Once upon a time, in a small forest, there was a fairy named Lily. Lily was a good fairy, but she had a terrible problem. She did not know how to win at games with her friends. Every time she played, she would lose and feel very sad.

One day, Lily was playing a game with her friend, Tom the squirrel. They were running a race to see who was faster. Lily tried her best, but Tom was very fast. He won the race, and Lily felt terrible. She wanted to win, too.

Lily asked her friend, Sam the wise owl, for help. Sam told her to practice and not give up. So, Lily practiced every day. She ran and ran until she got faster. One day, she raced with Tom again. This time, Lily won! She was so happy that she could finally win.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy was very smart and loved to perform magic tricks for his friends. One day, he went to his friend's birthday party and decided to perform a special trick. 

Timmy asked his friend to pick a card from his deck and keep it a secret. Then, he shuffled the deck and asked his friend to put the card back in. Timmy started to perform his magic trick, but suddenly, there was silence in the room. 

Timmy looked up and saw that his little sister had knocked over a vase and broken it. Timmy's friend was upset that the magic trick was interrupted, but Timmy knew that family was more important than performing. He helped his sister clean up the mess and apologized to his friend. 

In the end, Timmy's friend forgave him and they continued to have a great time at the party. Timmy learned that sometimes things don't go as planned, but it's important to be kind and help others when they need it.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Jack who liked to bounce. He would bounce on his bed and on the grass in the summer. Sometimes he would even bounce to the moon!

One day, when the sun was warm and shining, Jack wanted to bounce outside. He asked his Mom if he could go outside and bounce. She said yes, but he had to wait for her.

Jack waited outside the door and bounced up and down. His Mom opened the door and said, â€œLetâ€™s go in the garden and you can bounce there!â€ 

Jack was so happy! He ran to the garden and bounced on the grass. The sun was so warm and Jack just kept bouncing. His Mom watched and smiled. 

Jack was having so much fun that he didn't want to stop. He asked Mom if he could bounce forever. She laughed and said, â€œNo, but maybe next time.â€ 

Jack smiled and asked if he could bounce for one more minute. His Mom agreed, so Jack kept bouncing until he was all tuckered out!

Garry was very curious. He wanted to fly in a helicopter. One day, his dad brought him to a park and they saw a colorful helicopter there. Garry ran up to it. He wanted to touch it. His dad said, "Wait, we need to polish it first." They took out a cloth and they polished the helicopter. When they were done, his dad took him into the helicopter. Garry was very happy. They flew high above the ground. The view was beautiful. Garry waved to all the people below. Later, they landed the helicopter back at the park. Garry couldn't wait to come back and fly in the helicopter again!

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Jenny. One day Jenny was walking in the park when she saw something sparkly on the ground. When she looked closer she saw it was a bracelet. It was a pretty bracelet and it was very flexible. Jenny was so excited that she had found it and ran home to show her mummy.

Mummy said that the bracelet was very special, and Jenny should give it away to someone special. So Jenny thought about all the special people in her life and decided to give the bracelet to her best friend.

The next day Jenny was so excited and put the bracelet into a special bag for her friend. Her friend was so happy and excited when Jenny gave her the bracelet. They both said it was so special, and they each wore it proudly, day and night.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and eat yummy snacks. One day, her mom gave her a spicy chip to eat. Lily's mouth felt hot and she drank some water to make it better.

Later, Lily went outside to play with her staff. She tried to balance the staff on her head, but it kept falling down. She tried again and again, but it still wouldn't balance. Finally, she asked her mom for help.

Her mom showed her how to balance the staff by holding it in the middle. Lily tried it and it worked! She was so happy and proud of herself. From then on, she played with her staff every day and practiced balancing it.

Once upon a time there was a bright vehicle. It was red and shiny and it made a funny noise.

The vehicle had something special inside. It was a magical driver. He had a big white hat, and he made the vehicle go. He was very strong and could lead the vehicle anywhere very quickly.

One day, the magical driver lead the bright vehicle down the street. He led it around turns and over bumps. Everyone smiled as the bright vehicle drove by. The magical driver waved to them and the vehicle honked its horn.

Finally, the magical driver lead the bright vehicle back home. He parked the vehicle in the drive and said goodbye. The magical driver went on to lead many more bright vehicles on many more adventures!

There was an adorable little girl named Lucy. She had long blonde hair and loved to splash in the pool. It was a hot day, so Lucy went out to the backyard to play in her pool. She went inside the house to get her cooler full of snacks and water bottles.

When she arrived back in the backyard, Lucy smiled as she saw the water glistening in the sun. She put on her swimsuit and jumped in the pool. She felt so cool and splashy! She held her cooler tight and floated around the pool. 

Lucy's mom looked out the window and saw her daughter having so much fun. She opened the door and yelled out to Lucy, "Are you having a nice time?" 

Lucy smiled and shouted back, "Yes! It's the best day ever!" She splashed some more and her mom just watched, admiring her daughter's happiness.

Once upon a time, there was a small mouse living in a nice, warm cave. He was always very curious, and he questioned a lot of things. One evening he decided to go out of his cave, so he could explore the world.

On his adventure, he came across a big bird who was flying high in the sky. The bird asked him, "Where are you going, Mouse?"

The mouse replied, "I am going exploring, I have an urge to explore the world!"

The bird said, "Things can be dangerous out there. Be careful, no matter how small you are, your courage can take you far."

The mouse nodded and said, "Of course, I will always be careful."

The bird smiled and said, "Good, be brave and never be afraid of asking questions."

The mouse smiled and said, "Thank you for the advice."

From then on, the mouse kept what the bird said in mind, and with his newfound courage and willingness to ask questions, he was able to explore the world without any harm.

The moral of the story is that even something small and timid can be very brave and strong if it questions and asks for advice.

Nina and her brother had gear. It was special gear because it was very shiny and they both loved it. The gear was dangerous because there was a sharp edge on it and they had to be careful.

They decided to go and explore with their gear. They ran to the park and saw all the trees and grass. It was fun, but they had to stay safe. Every time they went near the gear they had to be careful, because it was dangerous.

Nina and her brother had lots of fun in the park. They played with the gear and ran around. They laughed and enjoyed the day.

Eventually, it was time to head home. They packed up their gear, but were careful not to get cut. They were brave and did it, and soon they were home.

Nina and her brother had enjoyed their day playing with their gear. They had discovered something new, and it was dangerous. But, despite the danger, they had had lots of fun!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Jacob. Jacob liked to go to the park and play. One day, he went to the park to look for his friends.

As he walked, he saw an orange bird perched on a branch of a tree. Jacob was amazed and he whispered, "What is that beautiful bird?".

The orange bird fluttered its wings and chirped. Jacob noticed that the bird seemed sad, so he said, "Would you like some help?".

The orange bird started to pray to God. Jacob joined in, and together they prayed for happiness. As they finished praying, the orange bird flew away.

Once upon a time, there was a loud penguin. He lived near the top of a big hill. Every morning, he would rise early and look out over the hill. He looked for fish swimming near the shore.

One day, he was looking out when he saw a large boat. Penguins cannot swim that far, but he wanted to try. He hoped the boat would take him to where the fish were.

So he rose up to the top of the hill and yelled as loud as he could. The people on the boat heard him and came to get him. They took him to the shore where he was able to find all the fish he wanted!

He was so happy and he thanked the people on the boat. The people were all so kind and they took him back to the forest where he lived.

The penguin rose every morning and went back to the shore, so he could find all his fish. He was never too loud, but he always had a big smile on his face!

Mum and Dad had a surprise for the kids - a trip to the park! Everyone was excited, except for little Julie who wanted to stay at home and draw. "Come on, don't be such a grouch," said Mum. She carried Julie's paper and crayons, and everyone headed to the park.

Once they arrived, everyone ran off to play. But Julie was feeling a bit bossy and wanted to stay near her parents and draw. She sat on the grass and pulled out her crayons and paper. Her parents watched as she made a lovely picture of the park.

When she finished, Mum carried the paper over to show the others what Julie had drawn. They oohed and ahhed, and then it was time for everyone to go back home. Julie carried her paper and her crayons, feeling proud that she made such a nice picture. She smiled at Mum and Dad and went off to play with her brothers and sisters.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Chip. He lived in a tree way up high in the sky. Every day, he liked to sing and dances in the sunshine.

One day, Chip heard a mysterious sound coming from the tree next to him. At first, he was scared, but then he realized it was a horn! The horn was making a happy tune, and it made Chip feel better.

So, Chip decided to join in the music. He opened his beak and started to sing along with the horn. Soon, all the birds in the sky were singing together, making a beautiful song. 

The sun was setting, and Chip flew down to the ground. He said good bye to the horn and flew away. Chip was happy to have made some new friends and to have found something mysterious and fun.

Once there was a boy and he was sad. He wanted to cry. He went to the ocean so he could cry and nobody would hear.

The ocean was so big and white and blue. He felt better when he looked at it. He put his toes in the wave and it was wet and cold.

The boy wanted to find something useful. He looked around and saw a piece of wood and some seaweed. He smiled and put them on dry land.

Then the boy began to cry. He cried and the ocean took away his tears. When he finished crying, he felt better.

He took his useful things and went home feeling happy. He looked back at the ocean and smiled. The ocean had made him feel better.
