"Mom!" he shouted. "I think it's time to come inside!"

His mom came to the door and said, "Yes, I think it is. Come in and we can make some cookies together."

Jack smiled and ran inside to help his mom make cookies.

Once there was a boy named Jack. He was three years old and very curious. He loved to explore and find new stuff. One day, he decided he wanted to fight with his brother. He was feeling very rough and full of energy. He ran around the house trying to find something to fight with. He saw a pile of stuffed toys in the corner of his room. He grabbed the toys and ran over to his brother who was sitting on the couch. 

Jack shouted, â€œLetâ€™s Fight!â€ His brother just laughed and shook his head. Jack threw one of the soft stuffed animals at his brother who ducked out of the way. Jack was feeling very brave and kept throwing the stuff around the room. His brother started to get angry and tried to grab the stuff from him.

The two of them were wrestling and fighting over the toys. They both got rough and Jack was being brave. They ended up in a big pile of stuffed animals, laughing and happy. Jack was proud that he had fought and won.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who loved to admire the world around her. Everywhere she went, she would take a look, and admire the beauty.

One day, the little girl was admiring a field of daisies. She use to come out to the field every day to admire the bright and beautiful colors. As she was looking at them one day, a big old dog appeared and began barking at her.

The little girl was scared and looked around for help. As luck would have it, a dependable lady appeared. Seeing the little girl's fear, she walked up to the dog and scared him off. She then turned to the little girl and said, "You should never go anywhere by yourself. You need a dependable person to always look after you."

The little girl thanked the dependable lady, but her words went in one ear and out the other. In the future, the little girl kept going out alone and, sadly, bad things would happen to her.

The moral of this story is that you should never go outdoors alone. We should recognize and appreciate the value of relying on dependable people.

Once there was a reindeer named Silly. He lived in the North Pole with the other reindeers. Every night, he would play with his friends and have fun. He was the happiest reindeer in the North Pole.

One day, Silly was playing in the snow and he heard a noise. He was scared, so he ran away. Then he saw something moving in the snow. He was very scared. 

Silly's friends asked him why he was so scared. He told them he had seen something moving in the snow. His friends told him it was probably just a silly little snowman, and not to worry. 

But Silly was still scared. He kept imagining all the things that could be hiding in the snow. Suddenly, he heard the noise again, and he ran away. 

His friends tried to follow him, but he didn't want to be found. He was too scared. Eventually his friends caught up to him, and they all hid in a very tall tree for the night. 

The next morning, Silly found out that the noise he'd heard was actually a baby polar bear. He was very embarrassed he'd been so scared. From then on, Silly was known as the 'silly reindeer'. 

The End.

Once upon a time, there was a small girl called Lucy. She was three years old and liked to explore her garden. One day, she noticed something funny in the dirt. It was an egg! 

Lucy was excited, she had never seen an egg before. She carefully picked it up and held it in her hands, wondering what might be inside. 

Suddenly, the egg started to crack. Lucy watched as the egg opened. Out came a baby bird, which was really small and fluffy. The bird jumped out and started to fly away. 

Lucy wanted to know more, so she called out to it. She said "Where are you going?". The birds rough voice replied, "Follow me". Lucy started to follow the bird, repeating "Follow me" all the way.

The bird flew back to the nest and Lucy got to see all of her baby brothers and sisters. Lucy was amazed, and she watched them for a long time. 

The end.

Sara and Ben like to go to the zoo with Mom and Dad. They see many animals, but their favorite is the otter. The otter is brown and furry, and it swims and plays in the water.

One day, Sara and Ben see the otter holding a rock in its paws. The otter hits the rock on a shell and cracks it open. Then it eats the yummy food inside the shell.

Sara and Ben are curious. They want to touch the rock and the shell. They ask Mom and Dad if they can. Mom and Dad say yes, but they have to be careful. The rock and the shell are rough and can hurt their fingers.

Sara and Ben go to the fence and reach out their hands. The otter sees them and swims over. It gives them the rock and the shell. Sara and Ben say thank you and feel them. The rock is hard and smooth. The shell is sharp and bumpy.

Sara and Ben are happy. They give the rock and the shell back to the otter. The otter nods and swims away. Sara and Ben wave goodbye and smile. They learned something new today. They like the otter very much.

Once upon a time, there was a young girl who wanted to be successful. Every night, when she went to sleep, she dreamed of her success. She believed that if she worked hard, she could make her dreams come true.

Every morning, she got up and did her best. She ran faster, learned harder and read more. She never gave up.

One day, she achieved a great success. Everyone was so proud of her. She felt happy and excited. Thanks to her hard work, her dreams had come true!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and explore the world around her. One day, while playing in the park, Lily saw a butterfly. She followed it around, but it flew away.

Lily felt sad because she wanted to catch the butterfly. But her mom told her to ignore it and find something else to do. So, Lily went to the swings and had fun.

Later, Lily and her mom went to the store to buy food. They saw many fruits and vegetables available. Lily picked out a big red apple and her mom put it in their cart.

When they got home, Lily's body was tired from playing and shopping. She ate her apple and went to bed. She dreamed of catching the butterfly and having fun in the park again.

One day little Tom had an exam. He was very scared. He was afraid he would not do well. Then he had an idea! He decided he would try something original. 

Tom took out a sack. He filled it with all kinds of things. He put rocks, feathers, sticks and shells in the sack. 

The day of the exam came. Tom opened his sack and small things flew everywhere. Everyone in the room was surprised. 

In the end, Tom passed his exam! His original idea worked. He was so happy! Everyone was impressed with his creativity. 

From then on, Tom was not scared of exams anymore. He was ready to try something original every time.

Lily and Ben like to play pretend. They have a big box that they use as a car. They take turns to be the driver and the passenger. They make noises like a car and go to different places.

One day, they pretend to go to the zoo. They see lions and monkeys and elephants. They have fun and laugh a lot. But then, Ben hits a bump and the box tips over. Lily falls out and lands on the floor. She cries and holds her side. It hurts a lot.

Ben is sorry and runs to help Lily. He says he is sorry and gives her a hug. He gets a band-aid from his mom and puts it on Lily's side. He says it will make it better. Lily stops crying and smiles. She says thank you and gives Ben a kiss.

They decide to play something else. They pretend to be doctors and nurses. They take care of each other and their stuffed animals. They are happy and forget about the bump. They are good friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and her puppy, Max. One day, Lily's mommy gave her a message to give to her daddy. But Lily accidentally dropped the message and it broke into many pieces.

"Oh no! Daddy needs the message. What should we do?" cried Lily.

"Don't worry, we can hurry and put the pieces back together," said Max.

So, Lily and Max worked together to fix the broken message. They put all the pieces back together and delivered it to Lily's daddy just in time. Daddy was very happy and gave Lily and Max a big hug. From that day on, Lily learned to be more careful with important messages.

Once upon a time there was a mighty cow. She was so strong, she could even move mountains! One day she found herself stuck in a muddy pit. As hard as she tried, she could not get herself out, and she was starting to get very tired.

Just then, a 3 year old child passed by. He looked in the pit and saw the mighty cow. He smiled at her kindly and said, "Don't worry, mighty cow! I will help you."

The child took out a cloth and he started to rub the cow all over. He rubbed and he rubbed. And soon enough, the cow was no longer muddy. She looked so happy!

The child said to her, "Climb on my back and hold on tight!" The cow did as she was told, and with his help, she managed to climb up and out of the pit.

The mighty cow was so thankful! She didn't know how she would have ever gotten out of the pit without the child's help. She was so happy, she gave the child a big cow kiss on the cheek! The child smiled and they both went on their way, happy ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to talk to everyone he met. He would talk to his mom, his dad, and even his toys. One day, Timmy's mom took him to church. At church, Timmy saw a man who had an orange shirt on. Timmy wanted to talk to the man, but he was too shy.

After church, Timmy's mom asked him why he didn't talk to the man with the orange shirt. Timmy said he was too scared. His mom told him that it's important to be brave and talk to new people. Timmy realized that he missed out on making a new friend.

The moral of the story is that it's okay to be shy, but it's important to be brave and talk to new people. You never know, you might make a new friend just like Timmy could have made a new friend with the man in the orange shirt.

Anna and Ben are in school. They like to learn new things. The teacher writes on the blackboard. She writes words and numbers. She asks the children to choose one word and one number and say them out loud.

Anna raises her hand. She chooses the word "cat" and the number "three". She says, "Cat, three". The teacher smiles and says, "Good, Anna. You are smart".

Ben raises his hand. He chooses the word "ignorant" and the number "zero". He says, "Ignorant, zero". The teacher frowns and says, "No, Ben. That is not a nice word. That is a rude word. You are not ignorant. You are learning".

Ben does not understand. He thinks ignorant is a good word. He thinks it means he knows everything. He says, "But I am ignorant. I know everything. You are ignorant. You know nothing".

The teacher is angry. She says, "Ben, that is very wrong. You are being disrespectful. You do not know everything. You have to listen and learn. I know many things. I am here to help you. You have to say sorry".

Ben is confused. He does not want to say sorry. He thinks he is right. He says, "No, I am not sorry. You are sorry. You are ignorant".

The teacher is sad. She says, "Ben, you are making me sad. You are making your friends sad. You are making yourself sad. You have to choose to be kind and humble. You have to choose to respect and learn. You have to choose to say sorry".

Ben looks around. He sees Anna and the other children. They are looking at him. They are not smiling. They are not playing. They are not talking. They are quiet. They are sad.

Ben feels something in his chest. He feels something in his eyes. He feels something in his mouth. He feels sorry. He says, "I am sorry. I was wrong. I was rude. I was ignorant. I want to be kind and humble. I want to respect and learn. I want to be your friend".

The teacher smiles. She says, "Thank you, Ben. That is very brave of you. That is very wise of you. That is very good of you. You are not ignorant. You are learning. You are my friend".

Anna smiles. She says, "Me too, Ben. You are my friend. You are smart. You are nice. You are not ignorant. You are learning".

Ben smiles. He feels something in his chest. He feels something in his eyes. He feels something in his mouth. He feels happy. He says, "Thank you, Anna. Thank you, teacher. Thank you, friends. I am happy. I am not ignorant. I am learning".

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Lucy. She was 3 years old and loved exploring. One day, she was playing in her bedroom when she noticed something special. Right beside her bed was a tall cupboard.

"Whatâ€™s in the cupboard?" she asked her mother.

"Oh, you canâ€™t open the cupboard," her mother said. "Itâ€™s off limits."

But Lucy was determined to find out what was inside. So while her mother wasnâ€™t looking, she reached up and pulled the cupboard open. Inside, there were all sorts of fun things - dolls, toys and games!

Lucy was so excited, she started reaching for them. But then, her mother noticed what she was doing.

"Lucy, you canâ€™t play with those things," her mother said sternly. "I had set down the rules, and you must follow them."

Lucy knew she had been naughty, so she put everything back and shut the door quietly. She knew that she must follow the rules to avoid getting into trouble.

Once upon a time, there was a beautiful fridge. It lived in a small house with a boy and his mom. The fridge was always full of yummy food. The boy loved to eat from the fridge.

One day, the boy wanted to eat a big cake from the fridge. His mom said, "No, you cannot eat the whole cake. You must share with your friends." The boy was sad, but he listened to his mom.

The next day, the boy brought the cake to his friends. They all shared the cake and had a great time. The boy was happy to share the cake. He learned that sharing is caring, and it is more fun to share with friends.

Mandy was a little girl who wanted to buy something from the vendors. She had some money, but it was hard to decide. One day, she and her parents went to the vendors. She saw a perfect toy for her and asked her mom if she could buy it. 

Mandy's mom said yes and gave her money to the vendor. Mandy was so happy she wanted to load it into the car right away. She was so excited she couldn't wait to play with it. 

When they got home, Mandy had the perfect toy. She was so happy and thanked her mom and dad. She ran into her room and started playing with it right away. And she kept it loaded beside her bed as she slept that night. 

Mandy was very happy with her perfect toy. She was reminded of how thankful she was to her parents, who made her perfect dream come true.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved adventure. Every day she would go to the porch and explore. Today was different though. As she stepped out, the porch was shrouded in a mysterious fog. Despite the fog, she wasn't scared. Suddenly, a sound came from the fog. It was a deep, sad noise. The little girl frowned and peered into the fog. She saw a little rabbit, who was crying. 

The little girl was filled with concern for the famous and knelt down to comfort it. She asked him, â€œWhat is wrong?â€ The rabbit, who was too scared to speak, simply shook his head. 

The little girl was determined to help the frightened rabbit. She reached out and stroked its head. The rabbit took a deep breath, looked up and smiled. The little girl's kind act had comforted the rabbit and made it feel better. 

The little girl learned an important lesson that day - that by being kind, we can make people feel happy and special. She knew that if she had not been kind, the rabbit would have still been sad and scared.

Once upon a time there was a girl and a boy. The girl was very kind, and she loved to give the boy lots of kisses.

The boy was old enough to talk, but he was still very cute. He liked it when the girl kissed his face, and so he asked for more.

The girl was so happy that the boy wanted her to kiss his face, but one day the boy said something mean and stupid.

The girl felt very sad, and she didn't know what to do. Then she thought it would be nice to give the boy one more kiss on his face, to show he was sorry.

So the girl leaned in close and gave the boy a big kiss on his face. The boy was so happy, he smiled and hugged her. 

The girl was glad she kissed him and everything was good again.

Once upon a time there was an old factory. Inside the factory were two friends who lived together. Every day, they worked together and played together.

One day, the two friends found out that the old factory was closing. They were very sad and didn't know what to do.

So, they decided to separate to find their own ways. The first friend said goodbye and headed off in one direction. The second friend said goodbye and went in a different direction. 

The two friends never saw each other again, but each one was able to find a good new place to live and be happy. The old factory was all alone, but it was happy too. 

The end.

Once upon a time there was a rich man who had a spear. He kept the spear very safe in a treasure chest. But one day the man was very, very poor and he had to sell his spear. He thought and thought about what to do, but he only had one choice. So, he took the spear and sold it for a lot of money. Now he was very, very rich again! He was so happy to have his money back. The man never forgot to be thankful for the money from selling his spear. He was careful never to be poor again.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Emily and Sarah. They liked to have fun. One day Emily thought of a great idea. She said, "Let's have a party!"

Sarah smiled and said, "That sounds like fun, let's do it!"

So Emily and Sarah put together a lively party. They got decorations and yummy treats. They invited all their friends and soon the house was full of laughter and smiles.

Everyone had a great time. They played, sang, and laughed. Everyone said the party was the best ever!

At the end of the night, Emily and Sarah were so happy they had decided to have a party. They felt they had become closer friends and had lots of wonderful memories.

Mum said it was Sunday and Sally wanted to get up. She felt weak but mum said she needed to have some breakfast. Sally loved Sundays. She got special cereal that was colourful and had sprinkles on top. She happily ate her breakfast while mum made her a special drink. 

Then Mum said it was time to get dressed. She got a pretty dress with lots of bows. She felt like a princess. 

Then they went out to the park. It was so much fun, Sally got an ice cream and went on the swings. She was getting tired so she said goodbye to the park and they went home. 

Mum said that it was bed time. Sally was too weak to play anymore, so she said goodnight to Mum and went to bed.

Once there was a brave little dog named Raider. Every day, Raider would go on an adventure. He would explore the woods and find new places. One day, he came across a big, dark cave. It was frightening, but he was brave, so he decided to go in.

As he entered the cave, he heard a loud sound that disturbed him. He paused and listened. He heard a deep growl. Raider was scared but he knew he had to move forward if he wanted to find the secret of the cave.

He bravely stepped further and further into the cave. The growling grew louder and louder. Then, suddenly, he found a giant bear. The bear seemed angry and he was ready to attack. Raider was now very scared!

But Raider stayed brave. He howled back at the bear and it stepped away. Raider had won! He had been successful in his adventure today. Raider felt proud of being brave and left the cave, happy.

Once upon a time, there was a big, strong lion who lived in the jungle. He was very proud of his strength and liked to roar loudly to show off. One day, a little monkey came to him and said, "Mr. Lion, can you please stop roaring so loudly? It hurts my ears and makes me scared." The lion got angry and started to complain, "Why should I stop? I am the king of the jungle and I can do whatever I want!" 

But the little monkey was not afraid and said, "Please, Mr. Lion, think about others and be kind." The lion thought about it and realized that he was being selfish. He decided to listen to the monkey and be more gentle. 

Later that day, the lion saw a hunter with a gun in the jungle. The hunter was looking for animals to shoot. The lion remembered what the little monkey had said and decided to protect his friends. He roared loudly to warn them and chased the hunter away. The animals were very grateful and thanked the lion for being brave and kind. From that day on, the lion learned to use his strength for good and not to complain when others asked him to be gentle.

The puppy was so excited as he ran into the park. He rushed around, sniffing the grass and trees. Then, he saw something shiny and stopped. It was a shiny, new ball! He barked with excitement.

"Let's play with it, little puppy!" said a kind girl with a big smile. She was wearing a pink dress and had tidy, long hair. 

The puppy wagged his tail. He rushed up to the girl and she giggled, as he licked her skin. She threw the ball across the park and the puppy rushed after it. 

He was so happy! He ran after the ball and brought it back to the girl every time she threw it. They played until the sun began to set. 

The girl gave the puppy a big hug, before she said goodbye. "You are a very tidy pup!" she said. The puppy gave her one last lick before she left. 

The puppy was so happy that he rushed around the park before heading home. He fell asleep with a big smile on his face.

Once upon a time, there was a bunny called Bob. Bob loved to hop. One day, Bob saw a long, dark shadow. The shadow belonged to a big bird.
Bob started to hop away. The bird called out, "Where are you going?"
Bob was so scared that he couldn't answer. 
The bird said, "Don't be afraid, I just want to be your friend."
Bob was so grateful and said, "Thank you! I really don't want to be alone." 
The bird said, "Let's play together! What would you like to do?"
Bob replied "Let's hop together!"
So, Bob and the bird hopped away and had a great time together. Bob was so grateful to have a new friend! The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved watching cartoons on TV all day long. One day, her mom asked her to help with the groceries. Lily was not happy about it, but she still went to the store with her mom.

At the store, Lily saw a big red car. She asked her mom, "Can we drive that car, please?" Her mom replied, "No, Lily. We can't drive that car. It's not ours."

Lily felt sad, but then she remembered that she should be proud of herself for helping her mom. She said to her mom, "Mom, I'm proud of myself for helping you. Can we watch a cartoon when we get home?"

Her mom smiled and said, "Of course we can, Lily. You deserve it." And they drove home in their own car, feeling happy and proud of each other. The moral of the story is that helping others can make you feel proud of yourself.

Once upon a time there was a humble man. He was a very nice man and he loved history. He loved learning about the past and all the stories that had been told. 

Every day he went to the library and read books and looked at maps. He wanted to learn more and more about the world.

One day, he went on an adventure! He took a train to a far away land and it was very dry and hot. He looked around and saw the history of the land through the old buildings and monuments. He was so proud of himself for going on this adventure and learning about the history.

When it was time to come home, the man was tired and a bit thirsty, so he stopped by a store to get something to drink. He bought a cold glass of lemonade and drank it as he walked home.

As he arrived home, he knew he had learnt something special on his adventure. He was happy because he had taken the humble step of learning the history of the world.

Once upon a time, there was a small pepper. It was growing in a garden near a big tree. The pepper was happy, but it wasn't sure why. One day, it decided to ask the tree why it was happy.

It asked, "Why am I so happy?". The big tree was quiet for a moment and then it said, "You are happy because you are alive".

The small pepper was surprised. It started thinking about the words the tree had said. It thought about how amazing it was to be alive and when it looked around, it realised that the garden was full of other small peppers.

The pepper was so happy that it thanked the tree and went off to show its friends. Now, every time the pepper looks out into the garden, it remembers what the tree said and it smiles.

Once upon a time, there were two friends who were always fighting. They would scream and yell and push each other over. When both friends were upset, nothing would make them happy.

One day, one of the friends had an idea. Instead of fighting, why not give each other a massage?

The friends thought this was a great idea and started doing it regularly. They would trade massages and talk to each other instead of fight.

The friends quickly learned that massage was far better than fight and they started to become the best of friends.

The moral of the story is that good things come when you find a way to work together and be kind. Sometimes it takes courage to do something different, but it's worth it in the end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Mary. Mary liked to rub her favourite toy, an original bear. Every night she would cuddle the bear close to her.

One day, Mary noticed something strange about her bear. He seemed to be getting bigger. Every time she rubbed him, he got bigger and bigger, until he was almost too big to hold!

Mary was so excited. She asked her mum to help her put the bear in her bed. When she woke up the next morning, the bear was gone!

Mary burst into tears. She couldn't find her bear anywhere.

But then, she heard a faint sound. It sounded like a voice! She followed the voice and it led her to a small box. Inside the box was her original bear!

Mary was so happy. She hugged the bear close and he was the same size as before. Mary never stopped rubbing her original bear, and they stayed happy together forever after.

Lily and Ben were playing with a big ball in the park. They liked to roll the ball to each other and catch it. Sometimes they rolled the ball very fast and sometimes very slow.

One day, they saw a new boy sitting on a side of the park. He had a small ball and he looked sad. Lily and Ben wanted to be his friend, so they rolled their big ball to him and said hello.

"Hi, I'm Lily and this is Ben. What's your name?" Lily asked.

"I'm Sam. I'm new here. I don't have any friends," Sam said.

"You can play with us. We have a big ball and it's fun to roll it," Ben said.

Sam smiled and joined them. They rolled the ball to each other and had a lot of fun. Sam showed them how to bounce his small ball and they learned a new game.

They played until it was time to go home. They said goodbye and promised to play again tomorrow.

Lily and Ben were happy. They had made a new friend and shared their big ball. Sam was happy too. He had found friends and learned a new game.

The moral of the story is: It is good to be kind and share with others. You can make new friends and have more fun.

Once upon a time there was an ugly frog named Bob. Bob lived in a pond in a forest filled with trees. One day, Bob saw a bee flying in a zigzag way. Bob was scared and he started to panic.

"Oh no!" shouted Bob. "What should I do?". 

But the bee didn't answer! It kept flying in the zigzag way.

Bob was so scared that he jumped out of the pond. He ran and ran until he couldn't run any more. He looked back and the bee was still following him in the zigzag way.

Bob knew what he had to do. He jumped up on a rock and started to yell at the bee. 
"Go away!" he shouted. "Go away!"

The bee was so surprised that it flew away. Bob was so happy that he started to jump and hop around the pond. He was free from the scary bee and he was so glad.

Yesterday, Pete and his mom went to the park. The sun was so bright, and Pete felt so happy. 

Pete's mom asked, "What do you feel, Pete?"

Pete replied, "I feel so free! I feel so strong! I feel like I can run forever!" 

His mom smiled and said, "That's wonderful. Let's take a walk together, okay?"

Pete said, "Yes! Let's go together!"

So they walked to the lake and watched the birds as they flew up in the bright sky. They laughed as they watched the ducks swim around the lake, and Pete felt so happy. 

Yesterday was such a nice day.

Jill and Sam were happy to move to a new house. They had many boxes to unpack. Jill liked to unpack her toys and books. Sam liked to unpack his cars and trains.

One day, they saw a big hole in the garden. "What is that?" Jill asked. "Maybe it is a mole," Sam said. "A mole is a small animal that digs in the ground. It has a long nose and soft fur."

They wanted to see the mole. They waited near the hole. They were very quiet. They hoped the mole would come out.

Soon, they saw something move in the hole. It was not a mole. It was an orange cat. The cat had a bell on its neck. It looked at them and meowed.

"Hello, cat!" Jill and Sam said. "Are you the one who made the hole?" The cat nodded and rubbed its head on their legs. It was friendly. Jill and Sam liked the cat. They decided to name it Mole. They took it inside and gave it some milk. They unpacked a box and made a bed for it. Mole was happy to have a new home. Jill and Sam were happy to have a new friend.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who loved to raise her pillow. Every day she would grab it with both hands and throw it up in the air. It felt so fun and freeing!

One day, the little girl saw a box of pillows that were available in the store. She was so excited and pointed to them, asking her mom to buy one of the pillows. Her mom said yes and they brought the pillow home.

The little girl couldn't wait to raise her new pillow! She ran up to her bedroom and grabbed it with both hands. Then, taking a deep breath, she threw it up in the air. She watched in delight as the pillow came back down and landed perfectly on her bed.

The little girl raised her pillow many times over the years, but the first time will always be her favorite.

One morning, Mum and Bobby were in the living room. Bobby looked around at the carpet and saw something strange.

"Mum, what is that unusual thing over there?" Bobby asked.

Mum couldn't believe her eyes. There, on the carpet was a strange creature.

"That's a very unusual creature Bobby. We should probably add it to our collection of strange creatures!" said Mum.

But the creature didn't agree and soon the living room was filled with loud noises.

"No!" the creature said and Bobby was scared.

Mum and Bobby didn't know what to do. Then Mum had an idea.

"Maybe we can add something special to the carpet to make the creature feel more comfortable," she suggested.

Together, Mum and Bobby added some soft cushions to the carpet. The creature looked much happier and thanked them before jumping onto the cushions and settling down. Bobby smiled. 

From that day forward, the carpet was never the same!

Once there was a boy. He felt lucky because he had a guitar. His guitar was special, so he waved to it whenever he saw it.

The boy loved to make music with his guitar. He added strings, and he strummed the strings. He sang happy songs into the night.

One day, a friend gave the boy a surprise. The surprise was a new guitar, even more special than the first. So of course, the boy waved to it. He was so lucky to have two guitars, and he was so excited.

The boy plucked the strings of both guitars. He made beautiful music with them. Whenever he saw his guitars, he waved at them with a smile. He was so happy.

Once upon a time, there was a man who liked to work in his garden. He had a big shovel and a small rake to help him. He liked to plant flowers and watch them grow. One day, he found a shiny medal in the dirt. It was so pretty! He showed it to his friends and they said he deserved it for all his hard work.
