One day, Jack's mum made him a special present - a big tasty cake! It was iced with colourful sprinkles and Jack couldn't wait to eat it. He was so excited that he almost forgot to tie a knot in the ribbon on the box. 

But Jack remembered just in time and he made the strongest knot he could. Then he smiled as he put the cake on the table and untied the ribbon.

Everyone enjoyed the tasty cake, especially Jack. In the end, it was so delicious that nobody even remembered why Jack had tried to tie the toilet shut!

Once upon a time, there was a big, smelly cat. The cat liked to play with a ball. One day, the cat saw a little boy with a ball. The boy's name was Tim.

Tim said, "Hi, cat! Do you want to play?" The cat nodded and they started to play. Tim would throw the ball and the cat would strike it with his paw. They played for a long time and had lots of fun.

After playing, the cat found a bag with a zip. The cat opened the zip and found a nice, soft bed inside. The cat was very happy and said, "Thank you, Tim!" Tim smiled and said, "You're welcome, cat! Now you can sleep in your new bed." The cat went to sleep in the bed, and they were both very happy.

Once upon a time there was a small pond in a big field. Every morning a bird would come to the pond to supply water.

One morning, the bird saw a frog sitting by the pond.

Frog: "Hello bird, can you supply me some water?

Bird: "Yes, hop in and I'll supply you the water you need."

So, the frog hopped into the pond and the bird sprinkled some water on the frog with her beak. The frog felt much better after being supplied with the water.

Then, the frog said, "Thank you bird! You have supplied me with a nice drink."

The bird smiled, spread her wings and flew away. From that day onwards, the bird would come to the small pond every morning to supply the frog with water.

Tim and Jen were twins who liked to play outside. One day, they saw a big road with many cars and trucks. They wanted to cross the road and see what was on the other side.

"Let's go, Tim," Jen said. "I dare you to cross the road with me."

"No, Jen, that's bad," Tim said. "Mom said we should not go near the road. It's not safe. The cars and trucks are fast and loud. They can hurt us."

Jen did not listen to Tim. She was brave and curious. She ran to the road and waited for a gap. She saw a chubby cat on the other side and wanted to pet it.

"Come on, Tim, don't be scared," Jen said. "Look, there's a cat. It's so cute and chubby. I want to play with it."

Tim was scared and angry. He did not want to cross the road, but he did not want to lose Jen. He followed her to the road and tried to stop her.

"Jen, stop, please," Tim said. "The road is dangerous. The cat can wait. Let's go back to our yard. Mom will be mad if she sees us here."

But Jen did not stop. She saw a gap and ran to the other side. She reached the cat and smiled. She bent down to touch it.

"Hi, cat," Jen said. "You're so soft and chubby. Do you want to be my friend?"

But the cat did not want to be Jen's friend. The cat was scared and angry. It hissed and scratched Jen's face. Jen cried out in pain and shock.

"Ow, ow, ow," Jen said. "Bad cat, bad cat. Go away."

Tim saw Jen get hurt and ran to help her. He crossed the road and hugged her. He saw blood on her face and felt sorry for her.

"Jen, are you okay?" Tim said. "I'm sorry, Jen. The cat was mean. Let's go home. Mom will make you feel better."

Jen nodded and sobbed. She held Tim's hand and walked back to the road. They looked both ways and crossed the road. They ran to their yard and called for Mom.

Mom heard them and came out. She saw Jen's face and gasped. She took them inside and cleaned Jen's wound. She put a band-aid on it and kissed it.

"Jen, what happened?" Mom said. "How did you get this scratch?"

Jen looked at Tim and felt ashamed. She knew she did something wrong. She told Mom the truth.

"I'm sorry, Mom," Jen said. "I dared Tim to cross the road with me. I wanted to see the cat. But the cat was bad and hurt me. I'm sorry, Mom. I won't do it again."

Mom hugged Jen and Tim and said, "I'm glad you're okay, Jen. But you should never dare Tim or anyone to cross the road. The road is not a place to play. It's very dangerous. You could have been hit by a car or a truck. You could have been badly hurt or worse. You have to listen to me and Tim. We love you and we want you to be safe. Do you understand?"

Jen and Tim nodded and said, "Yes, Mom. We understand. We love you too. We're sorry, Mom."

Mom smiled and said, "It's okay, Jen and Tim. I forgive you. But don't ever do that again. Promise me."

Jen and Tim promised and hugged Mom. They learned their lesson and never dared to cross the road again. They played in their yard and made friends with a nice dog instead.

Once upon a time there was a jolly little boy who loved playing in the mud. He wore his favorite blue socks all the time, even when it was time for bed. His mom was always telling him to put his socks away, but he just wanted to keep playing and always delayed.

One day he came home from playing and forgot to change his socks. His mom saw that he was still wearing his muddy blue socks and said, "You must put these away now!"

So the little boy reluctantly took off his socks, dried them off and put them away in his sock drawer. As he put them away he thought about the fun he had playing in the mud and smiled.

From that day on, he made sure to always put his socks away in a timely manner. And each time he remembered how his jolly day of playing almost delayed it.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the rain and jump in puddles. One day, she got very muddy and her mom said, "Lily, you need to take a shower."

Lily didn't want to take a shower because she liked being muddy. But her mom said, "You can't go to bed all dirty. You need to get clean." So Lily took a shower and it was so much fun! She splashed and played with the water.

After her shower, Lily's mom gave her a big towel to dry off with. Lily wrapped herself up in the towel and said, "I love showers! They make me feel ancient!" Her mom laughed and said, "You mean refreshed, Lily. Showers make you feel refreshed." And Lily smiled and said, "Yes, refreshed!"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who had a plan. She wanted to share her plan with her friends. She invited them over for a fair game day. 

When they all arrived, the little girl said, "Let's play a game and see who can get to zero first!" Everyone loved the idea and they all got set up with the scoring board.

The little girl and her friends took turns rolling the dice and sometimes they would be ahead, but sometimes they would be behind. But in the end, the little girl's plan worked and she won the game with a fair score of zero.

Her friends cheered for her and said, "That was such a fair game!" 

The little girl smiled and said, "It was fun, wasn't it!" 

And they all agreed.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys, but he always wanted more. One day, his mom took him to the store to buy a new toy. Timmy saw a toy he liked, but it was very cheap and had a rough texture. His mom asked him if he really wanted it, and Timmy said yes.

When they got home, Timmy played with the toy for a little while, but he didn't like it very much. He realized that just because something is cheap, it doesn't mean it's good. He also noticed that the texture of the toy was not very nice to touch. Timmy learned that it's important to value things that are good quality, even if they cost more.

From that day on, Timmy was more careful about the toys he asked for. He wanted toys that were good quality and felt nice to touch. He knew that sometimes it's better to spend a little more money to get something that will last longer and make him happier. Timmy was happy he learned this lesson and he always remembered it.

Once upon a time,there was a girl named Rachel. She enjoyed playing with the birds in the park and she loved to look at the stars in the sky.

One day, Rachel was feeling thoughtful and didn't feel like playing in the park. She decided to go for a walk. As she walked around the block, she heard an alarm ringing. Rachel thought it was very loud and it kept repeating every few minutes. She wanted to make it stop, so she tried to figure out where it was coming from. 

She kept walking and eventually she came across a house with an open window. Rachel realised the alarm was coming from inside that house! She was about to run away when she saw an old man struggling to get out of his chair. Rachel was very thoughtful and decided to help him.

She went inside the house and helped the old man turn off the alarm. He was so happy and thanked Rachel with a hug. From then on, Rachel would visit the old man often and help him with daily tasks. The old man and Rachel became very good friends!

Once upon a time there was a fierce book. It increased in size every day. One day, a tiny little girl found it. She was only three years old but was very brave. She opened the book and saw big, colourful pictures. She quickly fell in love with the book! She shared the book with her friends and every day they would look at it and see new pictures. They laughed and played. The book kept increasing in size so there were always new, exciting pictures to see! The friends had so much fun and the book was so fierce that they wanted to keep it forever!

The family was outside playing in the garden. The mother was pushing the father on the swing. The children were running and laughing.

Suddenly, the baby of the family started crying. The father ran to him and picked him up.

The little brother was jealous of all the attention the baby was getting. He started to cry too.

The mother tried to calm the little boy but he was too embarrassed to stop. He knew he was jealous and he didn't want his family to know.

The father asked, "What's wrong, my little one?"
The little brother said softly, "I was jealous of the baby getting so much attention." 

The mother smiled and said, "It's okay to be jealous on occasion. What can we do to make you feel better?" 

The father looked at the little boy and said, "Let's play a game of hide and seek." 

The little boy smiled and nodded. He soon forgot all about his embarrassment and enjoyed playing the game with his family.

One sunny day, Mommy and little Pete went to the park for a picnic. Pete brought his toy truck with him. As soon as he arrived, he started playing with it on the track.

But then, a jealous bully showed up. He wanted to play with the truck too. He grabbed the truck from Pete and tried to keep it for himself. 

"No!" shouted Pete, and he tried to get his truck back. But the jealous bully was too strong and bit Pete's hand.

Mommy saw what happened and she quickly took the truck away from the bully. Then, she scolded the bully to keep him away from Pete.

"Don't ever hurt my son again, or else I'll call the police," Mommy warned.

The bully ran away, never to be seen again. And Pete was able to play on the track with his truck with no fear.

Once there was a little girl who wanted to be smart. Her mom told her that if she wanted to be smart, she should always pay attention and ask questions. So every day, the little girl would sit on her seat, take out her pillow, and listen to her mom.

One day, the little girl asked her mom: "Mom, how can I be smart?" Her mom smiled and said, "By being curious and paying attention to what's around you."

The little girl was so excited. She hopped off her seat, grabbed her pillow, and ran out to find something smart. She explored the playground and found a caterpillar crawling up a tree. She watched the caterpillar and asked it questions. She was so focused that she didn't even notice the storm clouds rolling in.

Suddenly, it started raining. The little girl was getting soaked, but she still kept her eyes on the caterpillar. The caterpillar finally reached its destination and the little girl smiled. She ran back home, grabbed her pillow, and jumped onto her seat.

The little girl was so proud of herself. She had been curious and paid attention and she learned a lot. Her mom was proud of her too â€“ she had learned an important lesson. Being smart means paying attention to your surroundings.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved going on trips with his family. They always had lots of luggage to bring with them. One day, they went on a trip to the beach. Timmy was so excited to play in the sand and water. 

But when they arrived at the beach, they saw that it was very crowded. Timmy's family couldn't find a spot to put their towels down. They kept walking and walking, but every spot was taken. Finally, they found a small spot near the water. 

Timmy's dad started to unpack the luggage. But then, a man came over and said that they were on his spot. Timmy's dad tried to explain, but the man was not honest. He said that he had been there for hours. Timmy's dad didn't want to argue, so he just packed up the luggage and they left the beach. 

Timmy was sad that they couldn't play at the beach. He asked his dad why they had to leave. His dad just said, "Sometimes people kneel on the truth, and we have to go somewhere else." Timmy didn't understand, but he knew that he didn't like that man.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Ruby. She liked watching cartoons on the TV. One day when Ruby got home from school, her room was very messy. She was very sad and wanted to tidy it up. So, Ruby's mum sent her to the supermarket to get some cleaning supplies.

At the supermarket, Ruby saw lots of colourful cartoons on the shelves. Some were of animals and some were of princesses. She wanted to get them all! But her mummy told her to only pick one. So, she picked her favourite one and was very happy.

When she got back home, she saw that her room was still a bit messy. Then, she realised that her Mum had sent her to the supermarket so that she could help tidy it up, rather than buying cartoons. So, Ruby decided to clean her room first and then play with her cartoon. 

Finally, she tidied her room and it was neat and tidy again. She was so proud of herself! Now, Ruby was ready to watch her favourite cartoon and enjoy some fun!

Once upon a time, there was a big wardrobe in a little girl's room. The little girl's name was Lily. The wardrobe was very big and had many clothes inside. One day, Lily was very hungry. She wanted to find something to eat.

Lily thought, "Maybe there is some food in the wardrobe." She went to the wardrobe and tried to push it. At first, it was hard to push, but then it moved. Behind the wardrobe, she saw a small door. Lily was curious and opened the door.

Inside the door, Lily found a tiny room with a small table. On the table, there was a plate of yummy cookies. A little mouse was sitting next to the cookies. The mouse said, "Hi, Lily! I am also very hungry. Can we share the cookies?" Lily smiled and said, "Yes, we can share!" So, Lily and the mouse ate the cookies together and they were not hungry anymore.

Nina was a little girl. Every day she went to learn new things. One day she decided to go to the beach and she was so excited. As she arrived she took off her shoes and felt the wet sand on her feet. It was amazing!

The ocean was big and blue and Nina wanted to explore it. She watched some other children playing and she wanted to learn from them. She saw how they were gently splashing in the water and how they were gathering shells. Nina was so excited that she started to do the same.

After a while, Nina learned how to splash, just like the other children. She smiled and soon enough she was swimming in the water. She even saw some fish and it was amazing. Nina loved the beach and everything she had learned. She had a great day and went home with a smile on her face.

Lily and Ben were playing in the dark. They had a flashlight and a tent. They liked to pretend they were explorers in a jungle. They saw many animals and plants with the flashlight.

But then they heard a loud noise. It was a big bear. The bear was hungry and angry. It wanted to eat Lily and Ben. Lily and Ben were scared. They did not want to be eaten.

They decided to fight the bear. They used the flashlight to make the bear blind. They shone the light in the bear's eyes. The bear roared and covered its eyes. Lily and Ben ran fast to the tent. They zipped it up and hid inside.

The bear tried to find them. It sniffed and scratched the tent. But it could not see them. It was still blind from the flashlight. Lily and Ben held each other and hoped the bear would go away.

After a while, the bear gave up. It was too tired and sore. It walked away to find another food. Lily and Ben heard the bear leave. They were happy and relieved. They had fought the bear and won. They hugged the flashlight and thanked it for saving them. They were brave explorers.

Lily liked to teach her dolls how to read. She had many books with big letters and pictures. She sat on the couch with her dolls and opened a book. She pointed to a word and said, "This is cat. Cat says meow. Can you say cat?"

One of her dolls nodded and said, "Cat. Meow." Lily smiled and gave her a hug. "Good job, Daisy. You are a smart doll."

Another doll raised her hand and said, "Lily, can I read too?" Lily looked at her and said, "Of course, Rosie. You are a pretty doll. You have a pink dress and a bow. Do you like pink?"

Rosie nodded and said, "Yes, I like pink. It is a nice color. Can you show me a pink word?" Lily turned the page and found a word that was pink. She said, "This is pig. Pig says oink. Can you say pig?"

Rosie said, "Pig. Oink." Lily clapped and said, "Very good, Rosie. You are a fast learner."

Lily was happy to teach her dolls. She thought they were attractive and fun. She loved to read with them on the couch. She said, "You are my best friends. I will teach you more words tomorrow." The dolls smiled and said, "Thank you, Lily. We love you too." They hugged and kissed and fell asleep on the couch.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily had a very expensive toy that she loved to play with. One day, Lily took her toy to school to show her friends. When she got to school, her friend Sarah saw the toy and asked if she could play with it.

Lily said no and kept the toy close to her head. Sarah got upset and said, "Why won't you share your toy with me?" Lily didn't know what to say, but she felt bad. Later that day, Lily's teacher talked to her about sharing and being kind to others.

The next day, Lily brought her toy to school again. This time, when Sarah asked to play with it, Lily remembered what her teacher said and decided to share. They both played with the toy and had fun together. Lily felt happy and learned that it's important to be kind and share with others.

Once upon a time, there was a dependable bus. It drove around all the time, giving rides to people. One day, the bus stopped outside a house and made a loud noise. This scared a little 3 year old who was inside the house. She was so scared that she didn't want to go out. 

The bus driver felt bad, so he decided to make it up to the girl. He decorated the inside of the bus with balloons and colourful paper, and drove around the neighbourhood to all different places. The girl loved it, and it wasn't long before she was a regular passenger. 

The dependable bus and the girl had lots of fun together. She even started to like the loud noise that it made when it stopped outside her house. Everyone in the neighbourhood loved the bus too, and it became a dependable friend to the 3 year old.

Mummy and Daddy were sitting in the garden. They were very happy. Daddy looked up from his book and said, "Shall we permit Sam to go and get an egg from the farm?" Mummy said, "I think that sounds like a lovely idea."

So Daddy and Mummy took Sam to the farm. When they arrived, there were lots of chickens and eggs. Sam was so excited that she ran over and pointed at her favorite chicken. Daddy asked the farmer if she could have an egg from that chicken and the farmer said yes.

Sam was so happy that she ran back with the egg, careful not to drop it. When they got home, Mummy cracked the egg into a bowl. She cooked it and made Sam an egg sandwich. Sam said, "Thank you Mummy, this is the happiest day ever!"

Once upon a time, there was a prince and a princess. The prince loved the princess very much and wanted to marry her. All of the people in the kingdom were very excited for them.

The day of their wedding arrived, and the princess was feeling very nervous. Suddenly, there were loud noises in the sky. It was a missile! Everyone was scared and started to run.

The prince grabbed the princess and said: "Don't be nervous, we are going to marry because I love you." They looked into each other's eyes and both felt so brave. The prince asked: "Do you want to marry me today?" 

The princess smiled and said: "Yes, I want to marry you." 

They hugged each other and celebrated as the missile flew away. Everyone rejoiced and the prince and princess lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time there was a bean. The bean was sad and did not move. He really wanted to move but he just stayed in one spot. Then one day, an angry bird came near the bean. The bird was very mad. He made a lot of noise. The bird's noise scared the bean and he quickly moved away. He moved away to a new spot. The bean was very happy now. He felt so excited to move and explore the new area! Every day the bean moved around finding new and exciting things. He never stopped moving and was always exploring! The bean finally found a happy home.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Marley. She was so happy and she always loved to explore. Late one afternoon, Marley went to the park to play with her pet dog, Bear. 

Suddenly, Marley stumbled over a large rock. Bear ran to Marley and licked her face. Marley said, "Oh Bear, thank you so much!"

Bear looked up at Marley with a big, happy smile. He had an idea - he wanted to take Marley to get a small salad for dinner. Marley jumped up and said "Yes please!".
 
So Marley and Bear went to the store, and Bear grabbed a soft lettuce and some tasty tomatoes from the vegetable aisle. Marley said "Yay, bear, this is perfect - let's take it home and make a salad for dinner".

Marley and Bear went home and made a lovely salad for dinner. The salad was so tasty and soft and Marley said "Thank you, Bear," as she hugged her furry friend. 

"You're a very special friend," Marley said to Bear, as they finished their dinner. "And I'm so lucky to have you!"

Once upon a time there was a big, hot spider. He lived in a dark cave, but he was very brave.

One day, the spider had an idea. He wanted to try brewing a special drink. He mixed many special ingredients, including poison.

The drink was very hot, so the spider had to be careful. He put on his special gloves and drank a little bit. He felt very strange afterwards, but he was glad he was brave enough to try his special drink.

The spider was so happy with his drink that he decided to share it. He cooked up more of his special potion, and gave it out to all the other spiders. They all loved it so much that they made it their favorite drink!

Once upon a time, a little girl named Amy loved to play by the stream. She brought her dolls to the river and made a tidy picture. As she was very young, she was still learning many words.

One day, when she visited the stream, a frog jumped out. Amy was so excited. She said, "Hi Frog! I love you!"

The frog croaked back, "I love you too!"

Later, Amy cooked a special lunch for the frog and invited him over. They shared the lunch and had a great time. Every day, when Amy visited the stream, the frog would come play with her.

Amy and the frog would splash in the stream and build sand castles around it. Amy loved the frog so much and they shared a special friendship.

The river was always clean and tidy when Amy visited and she made sure it was kept that way. 

Amy and the frog lived very happily by the stream.

Once upon a time there was a little girl, she was three years old. She loved to make up stories and explore her world.

One day the girl went outside to find something fun to do. She noticed a curious creature hopping around and it made her smile.

The little girl asked what it was, and the creature replied, "I'm a kangaroo!" She was so curious, she wanted to learn more.

The kangaroo said, "I can guess. Do you want to play a game?" The girl said, "Yes!" and the kangaroo hopped away.

The kangaroo came back with a big bag of surprises. Each surprise was a creative way of guessing the answer. The girl had fun making her guesses, and soon the kangaroo had her own fun playing with the little girl. 

At the end she got all the answers right. "You're very creative!" said the kangaroo as it hopped away.

The little girl smiled and waved goodbye. She had such a great time playing and will remember this day for many more years to come.

One day, a boy named Tim and his dog, Spot, went for a walk in the big park. They saw a wide tree with many branches. Tim said, "Let's go climb that tree, Spot!" Spot wagged his tail and barked, "Yes, let's go!"

As they climbed the tree, they heard an alarm sound. "What's that?" asked Tim. "I don't know," barked Spot. They looked around and saw a little bird stuck in a hole. The bird was making the alarm sound because it needed help.

Tim and Spot went to the little bird. Tim said, "Don't worry, bird. We will help you!" They worked together to get the bird out of the hole. The bird was happy and thanked them. Tim and Spot felt good for helping a friend. They continued their fun day at the park, playing together under the wide tree.

One day, Bob was playing at the beach with his toy truck. He watched the waves crash on the shore and saw people surfing on the waves. He wanted to join them, but he knew he was too small.

Bob's mom told him not to get too close to the water, but his curiosity got the better of him. He crept closer and closer to the shore. Suddenly, he slipped and fell in!

The water was very cold and he started to cry. But then Bob saw all the surfers playing in the waves and he smiled. He paddled and paddled until he caught a wave. He was so brave and obedient that the surfers even clapped and cheered for him!

Bob had so much fun surfing that day, and his mom was proud that he had been so brave but also obedient. From then on, Bob was excited to go to the beach and try surfing again.

Once upon a time, there was an elderly man who used to take a walk every day. One day, he felt an itch on his nose and was about to scratch it when suddenly he spotted a young boy and girl nearby playing tag!

The elderly man was quite excited to see the children playing and laughing together, so he decided not to scratch his nose. He watched them as they ran around and he smiled.

After a few minutes, the children's mother noticed the elderly man watching the children and asked him why he was there. The elderly man replied, "I'm just here to see how lovely you and your children are behaving."

The mother was pleased and thanked him for not scratching his nose while the children were playing. She realized what a kind gesture this was from the elderly man, and she thanked him again before he left.

The story has a moral value - it is important to always behave in a kind and courteous way, even when you have an itch.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys all day long. One day, he was playing with his toy zebras when his mom called him for lunch. 

Timmy's mom made him a sandwich with spicy mustard on it. Timmy took a bite and said, "Mom, this sandwich is too spicy for me!" 

His mom replied, "Oh no, I didn't mean to make it so spicy. Let me make you a new one." 

As she was making a new sandwich, Timmy accidentally dropped one of his toy zebras on the floor. He picked it up and said, "Oops, I dropped my zebra. Can you fix it, Mom?" 

His mom smiled and said, "Of course, I can fix it. But first, let's eat our sandwiches and then we can play with your toys together." 

Timmy was happy and excited to spend time with his mom. They ate their sandwiches and played with Timmy's toy zebras all afternoon. It was a fun day for Timmy and his mom. The end.

Rudy was a little boy. He wanted an igloo very badly. His parents told him that igloos were very expensive. He tried to manage his money, but it was hard. 

One day, he got an idea. He wanted to make his own igloo! He got a bucket of snow and began building. He stacked the snow and made it tall. He added a roof, a doorway and even two windows.

When he was done, Rudy had made his very own igloo! It wasn't as fancy as an expensive igloo, but he was proud of it. He invited his friends over to play inside. Together they laughed and sang and had a wonderful time.

Rudy had managed to make his own igloo and it was a great success!

Tom and Sam are friends. They like to play with cars and balls. One day, they find a big map on the wall. The map shows the world. The world has many places and colors.

Tom points to a place on the map. He says, "This is my home. It is red and blue." Sam points to another place on the map. He says, "This is my home. It is green and yellow." They look at each other. They do not agree.

Tom and Sam start to argue. They say, "My home is better. Your home is bad." They push and pull the map. They tear the map. The map falls to the floor. They are sad and angry.

Mom comes in. She sees the mess. She is not happy. She says, "What did you do? Why did you fight?" Tom and Sam do not answer. They look down. They are sorry.

Mom says, "You should not fight over the map. The map is not your home. Your home is here, with me and your family. The map is just a picture of the world. The world is big and beautiful. It has many homes and people. You can learn about them and be friends with them. You can ask them questions and share your stories. That is easy and fun."

Tom and Sam listen to Mom. They nod. They say, "You are right, Mom. We are sorry. We will not fight over the map. We will learn about the world and be friends with everyone." Mom smiles. She hugs them. She says, "That is good. I love you both. Now, let's clean up the map and put it back on the wall." Tom and Sam help Mom. They are happy. They are friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside, but one day it started to rain. Lily's mom told her to come inside, but she didn't want to. She slipped on the wet grass and got her dress dirty. 

Lily's mom gave her a rag to clean herself up. Lily didn't like the rag because it wasn't comfortable like her dress. She said, "Mommy, this rag is scratchy. Can I use my dress instead?" 

Her mom said, "No, Lily. Your dress is wet and we need to wash it. The rag will make you clean and comfortable again." So, Lily used the rag and felt much better. She learned that sometimes we have to do things we don't like to be comfortable again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sarah. She loved to play outside in the sun with her friends. One day, they went to the park to play. They ran around and had so much fun. 

After a while, Sarah's friend said, "I'm thirsty. Can we get some water?" Sarah replied, "Yes, let's go get some water." They went to the water fountain and drank some water. Sarah noticed that the water was not clean. She said, "This water is dirty. We need to find clean water." 

They looked around and saw a pond. Sarah said, "Let's go see if the water in the pond is clean." They went to the pond and saw that the water was clean. Sarah said, "This water is clean. We can drink it." They drank some water and it was so refreshing. They played by the pond and had so much fun. 

As the sun began to set, Sarah's friend said, "It's getting late. We need to go home." Sarah replied, "Okay, let's go home now." They went home, but Sarah remained happy because she had such a fun day with her friend.

Once upon a time there lived a little girl called Polly. One day she was walking with Grandma when she saw a strange tunnel. It was dark and very long. Grandma said it was crazy and that they shouldn't go inside. But Polly wanted to see what was inside, so she shrank down really small and stepped inside the tunnel.

"Don't worry, Grandma," she said. "I'll be right back!"

But when she took one step inside, she couldn't see the end of the tunnel. "This is so weird," she thought. She kept walking but it felt like forever.
 
After what seemed like hours, Polly finally saw light at the end of the tunnel. When she got there, she just couldn't believe what she saw. Grandma had made the tunnel shrink to fit around Polly, making it look like a hallway!

Polly was so excited. She flew out, hugged Grandma and said, "That was so crazy! Can we do it again?"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily felt very sick and her mommy took her to the doctor. The doctor checked her and said, "Don't worry, Lily. You will be fine soon."

Lily asked, "When will I be fine, doctor?"

The doctor replied, "You will be fine when the medicine arrives."

After a little while, the medicine arrived and Lily took it. She felt much better and said, "Thank you, doctor. I feel fine now."

The doctor smiled and said, "You're welcome, Lily. I'm glad you feel better now."

Once there was a boy named Tim. Tim liked to organize his toys. One day, he found a flashlight under his bed. He was very happy and played with it all day.

At night, Tim heard a loud noise outside. He felt scared but wanted to be brave. Tim took his flashlight and went to the door. He saw a big shadow and felt a little embarrassed because he thought it was a monster.

But it was just a big tree branch. Tim went back to bed, but he forgot to close the door. When he woke up, he saw that his toys were all gone. He was very sad and learned to always close the door at night.

One day, a boy named Tim went to play a game with his friends. They wanted to play a game where they had to grab a ball and make a score. It was a clear, sunny day, so they were all very happy to play outside.

Tim was very good at the game. He could run fast and grab the ball easily. His friends cheered when he made a score. They all laughed and clapped for Tim. They played the game for a long time and had lots of fun.

When it was time to go home, Tim and his friends were tired but happy. They all said bye and went back to their houses. Tim couldn't wait to play the game again on another clear day with his friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Shannon. She was three years old and was always curious about the world. She was visiting her uncle and aunt's house.

One day, Shannon asked her aunt if she could go to the station. Her aunt said yes, so Shannon put on her colorful coat and cap, and went out.

When Shannon reached the station, she was very excited to see lots of colorful trains. She wanted to get on one of them and explore.

Suddenly, an announcement came over the loudspeaker: "All passengers, please put your bag on the train before boarding."

Shannon smiled, and put her bag on the train. She was delighted to be going on her first train journey.

"Where is the train taking me?" Shannon asked her aunt.

"It's your surprise, Shannon." said her aunt. "Let's find out when we arrive".

Shannon smiled, and went on an adventure.

Once upon a time, there was a silly old man who liked to scatter his things everywhere. He always made a big mess in his house, but he never bothered to clean it up. One day, he bought a mop to help him clean.

He tried his hardest, but he couldn't use the mop to do the job. The mop just seemed to make a bigger mess. Every time he tried to use it, it made a huge mess and he had to start over again.

Finally, he learned how to use the mop. He was so happy that he could use it to clean up his house. He scatted it around the house and soon there were no more messes. He felt silly for not learning how to properly use the mop sooner. 

The end.

Tommy was watching his bird ï¬‚y in the meadow. He saw the bird pick up the red rubber ball and take it up in the air. Tommy was so glad! 

He ran to the meadow and shouted "Come back with my rubber ball!" He was so excited and hoping the bird would hear him. 

The bird dropped the ball and Tommy shouted "yes!". He ran to the ball and picked it up. Then he heard a voice.

"You are so lucky, Tommy," said a nice old lady. "You said the magic words and the bird listened to you." 

Tommy was confused at ï¬rst but then he saw the old lady's smile and he knew that he was glad he asked for the rubber ball. He thanked the old lady and ran back home with his red rubber ball.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys every evening. One day, her mom brought home a new toy for her. It was a shiny red car.

Lily was very happy and she said, "Mommy, can we play with my new car tonight?"

Her mom replied, "Of course, Lily! We can play together."

That evening, Lily and her mom played with the new car until it was time for bed. Lily was so happy that she fell asleep with a big smile on her face. From that day on, Lily played with her new toy car every evening with her mom.

Once upon a time, there was a clumsy bear. He had a very special memory to share. So he set off to send it far and wide.

But sending is harder than it looks, even for a clumsy bear. He tried and tried all day long, but no matter how hard he tried, he couldn't get the memory to go away.

Then, one night, he had an idea. He decided to send the memory on the wind. So that's what he did.

The memory flew on the wind, far and wide, spreading the special memory to everyone it touched. 

And the clumsy bear was so happy that he was finally able to send his special memory, so that everyone could enjoy it.

Once upon a time there was a girl called Emma who wanted to go on a special journey. She made lots of plans and told her mummy and daddy all about it.

On the day of the journey they all got in the car and set off. Emma was very excited and kept pointing out all the things she could see along the way.

After a while they arrived at a beautiful lake. Emma quietly looked around taking it all in. Then, with a big beaming smile on her face, she said 'I am so proud of this journey I have made today'.

Mummy and Daddy were really happy to hear this and they both gave Emma lots of cuddles. She knew that she had just had the best day ever.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to run and play with her friends. One day, they decided to have a race. Lily was very competitive and wanted to win.

During the race, Lily's friend Sarah fell down and started to cry. Lily stopped to help her up and give her a napkin to wipe away her tears. Even though she lost the race, Lily felt happy that she helped her friend.

Later that day, Lily's little brother started to complain about being bored. Lily suggested they play a game together. They had so much fun playing that Lily forgot all about the race and winning. She realized that being kind and making others happy was more important than being competitive.

One day, Little Joe was walking in the park. He saw something he hadn't seen before: a bright red boot! He was very excited, so he walked up to it and wanted to take a closer look. He observed it and thought it looked easy. Just then, he heard a voice behind him.

"That's my boot," said the voice. Little Joe turned around and saw a big smile on the face of an old man.

"Is it easy to use?" asked Little Joe.

"Of course it is," said the old man. "It's been used for a very long time, but it's still very comfortable. Go ahead and try it on, Little Joe."

So Little Joe did. He observed that the boot could be easily put on and off, and it fit perfectly. Little Joe was very happy with his new find. From that day forward, he always kept it in his bedroom and wore it on special occasions.

Once upon a time, there was a big world. It was so big that nobody could see the end of it. One day, the sun came up and it was very brilliant. The trees and flowers were happy and danced in the wind. 

But then, a mean dragon came and started to breathe fire. The world became dark and scary. The people were afraid and didn't know what to do. They tried to fight the dragon but it was too strong. 

Just when they thought it was the end, a brave knight came and defeated the dragon. The world became bright again and everyone was happy. They thanked the knight for saving them and the world. The end.

One day, a family moved into a new house. They were very excited! When they got inside, they saw a big box. Daddy said, "Let's unpack this and see what's inside!" Inside the box was a new bookshelf. Everyone was so happy. Mommy said, "Now we can put all our books in it!" They quickly started to unpack the bookshelf. First, Daddy took out the screws and helped Mommy put the bookshelf together. After the bookshelf was ready, they all put the books on it. There were so many new books. Everyone smiled and said they were very happy with their new bookshelf! What a great day it was!

Mandy was three years old and loved playing with her toys. She was also very proud of her new piano. She had asked her family for a piano on her birthday and they had surprised her with one. 

One day her mummy suggested to her that she should play a song on her new piano. Mandy knew the way to play "Twinkle, Twinkle Little Star" and was so proud when she played it perfectly. Her mummy was so pleased with her and they shared a hug.

Then Mandy's mummy suggested that she should take lessons and learn how to play properly. Mandy was a bit scared as it sounded hard but she nodded and said yes to mummy. Now, Mandy practices hard every day to learn how to play the piano properly, and her mummy smiles proudly whenever she hears her daughter playing.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Emily. She was three-years-old and loved to play in the garden with her pets. One day, while Emily was playing with her doggy and kitty, she noticed a strange triangle in the dirt. It was big and green and sparkly. Emily was scared and didn't know what to do.

Suddenly, a voice came from the triangle. "Can you trust me, Emily?" it said. Emily looked around, but she couldn't see anyone.

"Who are you?" asked Emily.

"I am magical triangle, Emily. I want to be your friend," said the triangle.

Emily wasn't sure if she could trust the triangle. But, then the triangle said something that made her feel brave. "I can show you lots of fun games to play," said the triangle.

Emily smiled and said, "Yes! I will trust you."

The triangle was very happy. He played lots of fun games with Emily, like tag and hide and seek. Emily laughed and had lots of fun. 

The day ended too soon and Emily felt a bit ashamed that she was so afraid of the magical triangle at first. She hugged the triangle goodbye, then went home. 

Emily still plays with the triangle every day and they are the best of friends. Emily has learned to trust and have lots of fun.

One day, a little girl named Sophie went for a walk with her mom. As they were walking, Sophie noticed something bright and black in the sky. She asked her mom what it was and her mom told her it was a bird. Sophie and her mom watched the bird fly around in circles.

As they kept walking, they noticed more of the black and bright birds in the sky. Sophie was fascinated by how they were flying and asked her mom what kind of birds they were. Her mom told her they were crows.

As the day went on, Sophie continued to notice the birds in the sky. They were getting louder and louder. Eventually she and her mom looked up and saw hundreds of crows flying above them! Sophie was amazed by how many there were, and laughed as she watched them all fly around in the sky above her.

Once there was a little girl. She was three years old and loved cats. Every morning, she went to the park to see her favorite cat.

The cat had long fur. It was so soft that the girl always wanted to pet it. But the cat would never let her get too close. 

The little girl was sad. She wanted the cat to understand that she was just a little girl who loved cats. 

One day, she decided to bring the cat a treat. She brought some kibble and put it down in front of the cat.

The cat sniffed it and eventually ate it. She felt so happy - she finally understood that the little girl meant no harm.

From that day forward, the girl and the cat were friends. Every morning, the long furred cat would come to the park to see the little girl. They would play and the girl would pet it, and they both were happy.

Once upon a time, there was a girl called Lily. She was so happy and she loved to explore. One day, she found a big, old lamp in the attic.

She was so excited, she couldn't believe her luck. She ran downstairs and grabbed her friend, Tom. Tom said he wanted to help her try and find out what was inside! Lily was delighted!

Tom and Lily put their heads together and explored the lamp. They opened it with an old key and found some bitter-tasting pills.

Lily was surprised, but excited too! She liked the taste, even though it was a bit sour. Tom followed her lead and even asked for more.

They shared the pills and had a great time. Tom and Lily stayed up all night, telling stories and laughing by their special lamp. They both wanted to have many more days like this!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to eat pizza and always made a big mess. His mom would give him a napkin to clean up his face.

One day, Timmy was playing with his toys when he heard a loud noise. He looked outside and saw a big, sharp truck. He ran to his mom and said, "Mommy, there's a big truck outside! It's very sharp!"

His mom looked out the window and saw the truck too. She became very alert and quickly told Timmy to stay inside. Timmy was scared but he listened to his mom. They waited until the truck drove away and then Timmy went back to playing with his toys.

One day, Mary went to the zoo with her family. Mary saw many animals. She saw lions, tigers, monkeys, and elephants. Mary was most excited to see the elephants. They were so big and had long trunks. Mary watched them as they lay in the sun.

Mary's mom said that elephants were very useful animals. They can carry things with their trunks and help farmers do their work. Mary thought it was very impressive that elephants could be useful to people. Mary wanted to learn more about elephants.

Mary and her family kept watching the elephants. They saw them lumbering around the zoo and playing in the mud. Mary smiled as she watched them lay in the sun. She thought that elephants were amazing and she loved them very much.

Bob was excited to go to the park, but when he got there he saw something surprising - his friends were all sliding down the slide! Bob had never seen any of them play on the slide before. He wanted to join them, so he took a running start and tried to slide down. But suddenly, he felt something sharp. Bob looked up and saw a large, shiny knife had been stuck in the slide. He was very scared, and he quickly backed away.

Bob's friends saw what had happened and told him there was nothing to worry about - their parents had put the knife there to keep any wild animals away. Bob was relieved, but still confused. He asked why it was there, and one of his friends explained that some animals could be dangerous and they had to be careful.

Even though Bob was still uneasy, he decided to try sliding down the slide again. But this time he was extra careful - and it was worth it. Bob slid all the way to the bottom and felt proud. Suddenly, his friends yelled out "Slide down again!" Bob was surprised, but he couldn't resist - they had something special planned.

When Bob reached the bottom, he found a big bowl of hot and spicy popcorn. Bob had never tasted anything like it before, and it made him happy! He thanked his friends for being so thoughtful, and for taking the time to make something special for him. From then on, Bob knew that there

The little girl was proud. She wore a beautiful dress, and wanted to show it off. She went to the park and sat on the grass. 

She smiled as she looked around the park. The trees were green and the flowers were blooming. She could hear the birds singing. The air was fresh and the sun was shining. 

Suddenly, the little girl saw something. It was a beautiful butterfly, sitting in the middle of a bright red flower. It made the little girl very happy. 

Then spring came, and the little girl was so proud. She saw all the new buds on the trees, and heard the chirping of the birds. She felt like she was part of the beautiful scenery. She smiled and sat in the park, watching the world around her in awe.

Once upon a time, there was a triangle. It was made of wood and the sides were painted red and blue. But one of its angles was broken.

The little triangle was so sad and made a big frown. He didn't have anyone to play with. So he decided to have a nap and dream about having friends.

Then, just as he was about to fall asleep, he heard a great noise outside. It was a big truck with a funny waving flag on its hood. Out of it came three happy triangles!

The little triangle was so excited! He ran over to them and the triangles all waved and welcomed him. They liked his red and blue paint and didn't even mind his broken angle. Now they could play together!

The little triangle was so happy he forgot he was tired and had wanted to nap. Instead he ran with his new friends and they played all day long. 

The little triangle was so glad he had made new friends, and they didn't even mind his broken angle!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy. His name was Billy. He was three years old.

One day, Billy went to the store with his mom. He saw a big bag of meat. His mom said "Do you recognize this, Billy?" He said yes, and he knew it was meat.

But later, it made Billy uncomfortable. He didn't like the way it looked. So Billy's mom decided to buy something else. She picked some fruit instead.

Billy was happy. He was glad he didn't have to eat the meat. He smiled and waved goodbye to the meat as he left the store.

Mum was busy teaching Emily the art of baking cakes. Emily was very excited, as baking cakes was her favourite activity. As Mum prepared all the ingredients, Emily paid close attention, wanting to learn all that she could.

"Mum, can I visit the bakery one day?" Emily asked with a broad smile on her face as she stirred the mixture.

Mum stopped what she was doing and looked Emily in the eyes. She replied, "Yes, you may visit the bakery, but for now let us continue teaching you how to make cakes at home."

Emily was very excited and continued mixing the ingredients, but after a while she began to feel a little uncomfortable. She stopped mixing and said, "Mum, I feel a bit uncomfortable can we take a break?"

Mum smiled and gave Emily a hug. "Yes, it's time for us to take a break. Let's go and get some fresh air."

Emily and Mum put on their coats, grabbed a book, and went out to visit the park. At the park they both enjoyed the fresh air, read the book and played some games, until they both forgot all about the feeling of being uncomfortable.

Once there was a girl and she was playing in her garden. She held a pink balloon in her hands. As she hugged the balloon tightly, she could feel its icy coldness on her skin. 

Suddenly the wind started to blow. The girl could feel the balloon slipping away from her grasp. She held it tighter and raced in the wind's direction. 

The girl looked up and saw the pink balloon dancing in the sky. With all her might, she tried to reach the balloon. But it was so high. 

The girl saw a tree and quickly climbed up. With her outstretched arm, she grabbed the pink balloon. She then hugged it and slid back down to the ground. 

The girl held the icy cold pink balloon with both hands. She felt so delighted and laughed out loud in happiness. From that day on, the girl always held her pink balloon whenever she went outside to play.

Once upon a time there was a clumsy little rabbit. He was always hopping around and trying to get everywhere. Everyone loved him, but they were very concerned he might get into some trouble.

One day, he decided that he was going to try and climb up the wall and into the window. He couldn't reach, though, so he asked his dad if he could climb up.

Dad said no. He told little rabbit that he was too clumsy and it wasn't safe for him to try.

But then Dad had an idea. He got a big screen and asked the little rabbit to help him put it up in the window. Little rabbit was so excited! Dad said it was okay for him to look at everything through the screen, and he happily agreed.

Little rabbit hopped around happily, and the Dad smiled. He knew that the screen would permit little rabbit to enjoy the view without getting into any trouble.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Lucy. She was three years old, and she loved to play outside.

One day, her mother said to her, "Lucy, let's go to the post office." Lucy was very excited because she loved going to the post office and looking at all the different letters.

At the post office, Lucy said excitedly, "Mom, can I buy a postcard?" "Yes, Lucy," said her mother, "but remember not to spoil it." 

"I won't spoil it, mom," said Lucy. She bought some postcards and wrote a letter to her friend. 

But when she put it in the post box her mummy saw, Lucy had drawn on the postcard.

Mummy said sadly, "Oh, Lucy, you have spoiled the postcard and it can't be sent now." She could see that Lucy was hurt, so she gave her a hug. "Let's go home and write a new letter," mummy said. 

So Lucy wrote another letter to her friend and it was sent the very next day. 

And they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time there was a small whale who lived in the ocean. She pretended to be the biggest whale in the ocean, and so she told lies. One day she went to a charming little island and when she arrived, all the other whales were on the beach. She was shocked to see that everyone there was much bigger than her. Even though she felt embarrassed, she tried to act like she was the biggest whale so she continued to lie.

Everyone on the island laughed at her and the whale was so sad. Just when she was going to leave, an old whale came up to her and said: "Lying does not make you bigger, it makes you smaller. Be honest and do the right thing, that's how you make yourself big."

The young whale thanked the old whale and realised that it was better to do the right thing than to keep lying. From then on, she was honest and told the truth. She became the biggest and most charming whale in the ocean. 

Moral of the story: It's best to be honest and do the right thing, even when it doesn't seem like the easy choice.

Once there was a Penny. Penny was so restless. Every day she wanted to improve.

One morning she decided to go on a big adventure. She walked past the garden and the fields. Finally, she reached a pond. The water was so sparkly and clear.

Penny wanted to go in, but she was a bit scared. Then she saw a frog. The frog said, "Come in and play with me! You can float on my lily pad and improve your swimming".

Penny was so excited! She jumped into the pond with the frog. They played and swam together. Penny was getting better and better.

Finally, it was time for Penny to go home. She said goodbye to her frog friend and hopped off. She felt so proud of how much she had improved.

Once upon a time, in a regular house, there lived a little girl named Lucy. Lucy loved to play with her toys, eat ice cream, and gain new friends. One sunny day, Lucy went outside to play in her yard.

As she played, she saw a new boy next door. The boy looked sad and lonely. Lucy wanted to make him feel better, so she walked up to him with a big smile on her face. She said, "Hi! I'm Lucy. Do you want to play with me?"

The boy's face lit up, and he smiled back at Lucy. His name was Tom. They played all day long, having so much fun together. They played with balls, dolls, and even made a fort. Lucy and Tom became best friends.

From that day on, Lucy and Tom played together every day. They shared many smiles and laughs. And Lucy was so happy that she could gain a new friend just by sharing her smile.

There was a boy named Sam. He was three years old. Sam had a big coat. It was red and blue. Sam liked to show his coat to everyone. He would take it off the coat hanger and display it proudly.

When Sam went outside, he always wore his coat. It was normal for him to wear it outside. It would keep him warm. But when Sam was at home, he liked to show off his coat. He would spin around and display his coat for his family. 

Sam loved his coat. It was very special to him. Everywhere he went, he made sure to display his coat. He was very proud of it.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys and watch cartoons. One day, he found a tube in his backyard. The tube was long and colorful. Timmy picked it up and looked through it. He saw the world in a different way.

The next day, Timmy's mom noticed that he was acting strange. He was quiet and troubled. She asked him what was wrong, but he wouldn't say. That night, Timmy went to bed early. He had a strange dream about the tube. In the dream, the tube showed him something scary.

The next morning, Timmy woke up feeling better. He went outside to play and saw the tube again. This time, he knew what to do. He used the tube to look at the world in a different way, but he was careful. He didn't want to see anything scary again. From that day on, Timmy knew that the tube was special and he would always use it wisely.

Once upon a time, there was a rich man who owned lots of money. He had an envelope filled with lots of coins and notes. 

One day the man wanted to hide his envelope so no one would find his money. He looked around and saw a basket filled with fruit. 

The man smiled and said, "I'm sure no one will think to look in there!" He quickly put the envelope in the basket and hid it beneath the fruit. 

The man felt relieved that his envelope and money was safe. That night he went to bed feeling happy and secure. 

The next morning, the man went to the basket to look for his envelope but it was gone. Another friend had taken it and run away with it. 

The man was very angry, but he knew it was his fault for not hiding it better. He had been too careless. 

But the man learned his lesson and the next time he hid his envelope in a secret place - and this time it stayed safe and sound!

Once upon a time there was an enormous clay pot. It was so large, it took two people to carry it! One day, a friendly dog named Ben lay down peacefully on top of the pot. But something strange happened. The pot started to wobble and shake! Ben was worried, but soon enough the pot started to move around the room, with Ben still on top!

The pot wound its way around the living room, with Ben still on top! He didn't know where it was going, or why it was moving, but he had a feeling something magical was going to happen.

Soon enough, the pot came to a large open window at the end of the room. Ben could see the bright morning sun out the window, and a large open garden outside. Then Ben realized what the pot was doing- it was taking him outside! Sure enough, the enormous clay pot came to a stop in the middle of the garden.

Ben jumped off the pot and took a deep sigh of relief. He had never seen such an enormous clay pot before, but he was glad it had taken him to such a wonderful place. Ben stayed in the garden for the rest of the day, exploring and making new friends. 

The moral of the story is that you never know what life will bring until you lay down and go with the flow!

There was a smart lion. He had a piano in his house. Every day he would sit and play the piano, while roaring out loud. Other animals in the jungle heard him play and thought he was great, so they started roaring with him. 

One day, a hunter heard the roaring, and he came closer to investigate. He saw the lion playing his piano and decided to take him away. The lion was too scared to roar anymore. 

The moral of this story is that it is important to be careful and not get too loud. Even though the lion was smart and had a great talent, it was not smart enough to be quiet and he ended up in danger.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Annabelle. She wanted to keep all of her best memories and experiences in one place, so she decided to start a journal. Every day she added something special that made her smile, like a funny phrase her dad said or a picture of her and her friends. Annabelle also added anything that made her sad or angry so she could remember and learn from it.

One day, Annabelle asked her mommy if she could help her sick neighbour. Although her mom said she could, her daddy said no. Annabelle knew that it was the right thing to do, so she refused to listen to her daddy and went anyways. After helping her neighbour, Annabelle felt happy and proud.

She wrote about the experience in her journal for others to see. As she wrote, she realized she had acted with compassion, even when she was told "no". This made Annabelle smile and she felt really good about her decision.

Annabelle continued to help anyone who needed it and write about her experiences in her journal. She also kept learning and growing more compassionate.

Once upon a time there was a quiet house. So quiet that the people inside couldn't talk. A 3-year-old boy named Sam wanted to break the silence.

He asked his mother, "Why so quiet?" His mother replied, "Let's listen. Do you hear it?" Sam concentrated hard and then said, "I don't hear nothing." His mother smiled and said, "That's the sound of silence."

Sam thought about that for a moment and then asked, "What can I do to make noise?" His mother gently said, "I recommend you be slow and gentle. Let's play a game and be extra quiet."

So they played a game, but it was really quiet. Sam liked the quiet, even though it still felt strange. After a while, he said, "That was nice, but can we make some noise now?" His mother said, "Yes, but remember to be gentle. We don't want to make too much noise."

Sam and his mother made noise, but they kept it slow and gentle. In the end, they had lots of fun and Sam decided he liked silence as well as noise.

Once upon a time, there was a cold day. A girl named Amy went outside to play. She saw a big box. The box had pretty pastel colors on it. Amy knew she should not open the box, but she could not resist.

Amy opened the box and found a warm hat inside. She put the hat on her head. It was so warm and cozy. She felt happy. The cold did not bother her anymore. Amy played outside all day with her new hat.

Later, Amy's mom came outside. She saw the pastel box and smiled. She knew Amy would find the warm hat inside. She was glad Amy could not resist the box. Now, Amy could play outside and stay warm on the cold day.

Once upon a time, there was a kind bus driver named Tom. He drove his bus every day and always smiled at the children who rode with him. One day, the bus broke down and Tom didn't know what to do. 

A little girl named Lily asked Tom what was wrong. Tom said, "My bus is broken and I don't have another one to replace it." 

Lily had an idea. She said, "I have a toy bus at home that you can borrow until your real bus is fixed." 

Tom was so grateful and borrowed Lily's toy bus. He drove it carefully and the children still had fun riding with him. 

The moral of the story is that being kind and helpful can make a big difference, even if it's just lending a toy bus.

Once upon a time there was a cute bird. He had two wings and he liked to fly around. One day he decided to go find a new home. But where should he go? He looked around and saw many choices. He saw trees, hills and rivers. After much thought, he chose the prettiest place he could find. It was a charming little lake with a big willow tree by the shore.

The bird flew down to the lake and landed on the willow tree. He decided this was the perfect spot. He liked the peacefulness of the lake and the sunny weather. The bird spread out his wings and said, "This is my home now."

He was so happy with his choice. The bird spent the days flying around the lake. He had so much fun swimming and eating the tasty bugs. Every night he would rest in the willow tree. The bird felt so cozy and content like he had found his forever home.

Once upon a time, there was an amazing cabin. Inside, it was warm and cozy with a fireplace and lots of stuffed animals. One day, the cabin's owner decided to invite two of his friends for a visit. 

They came on a sunny day, and the three of them played all sorts of fun games. They ran around outside and chased each other. They laughed and had an amazing time.

Inside, they watched movies and ate snacks. By the end of the day, they were all very tired, but they had so much fun that they wanted to stay even longer! 

The friends had such a good time that they wanted to invite their other friends to come visit the amazing cabin. They all said they couldn't wait to come back and have another amazing day of fun and laughter.

Once there was a boy named Joe. Joe wanted a haircut, so one day he decided to start. He went to the barber's shop and sat down in the chair.
