The mom looked for a long string and some markers. Carefully, she tied the string to two trees, one on the left and one on the right. She stretched the string up to the sky. Then, she took a marker and started to mark the string every centimetre.

When the mom was done, she looked at her work with a big smile on her face. She knew that if she could measure the sky, then any other thing big or small would not be a problem. She knew that if she was patient, hard work could measure anything.

Lila and Tom were best friends. They liked to play in the park with their toys. One day, they saw some big kids coming. The big kids looked mean and angry. They wanted to take Lila and Tom's toys.

"Give us your toys, or we will hurt you!" one of the big kids shouted.

Lila and Tom were scared. They did not want to lose their toys. They did not want to get hurt. They hugged each other and held their toys tight.

"No, these are our toys! Go away!" Tom said.

The big kids laughed. They moved closer to Lila and Tom. They reached out their hands to grab the toys.

"Stop! Leave them alone!" a voice said.

Lila and Tom looked up. They saw Sam, their older brother. Sam was strong and brave. He came to the park to protect them. He stood in front of Lila and Tom and faced the big kids.

"These are my sister and brother. You cannot take their toys. You cannot hurt them. Go away, or I will make you go away!" Sam said.

The big kids did not laugh anymore. They saw that Sam was stronger than them. They did not want to fight him. They did not want to start a war. They turned around and ran away.

Lila and Tom were happy. They thanked Sam for saving them. They gave him a hug and a kiss.

"You are the best brother ever!" Lila said.

"You are our hero!" Tom said.

Sam smiled. He hugged them back. He was glad he could protect them.

"Let's go home and have some cookies," Sam said.

Lila and Tom nodded. They picked up their toys and followed Sam. They felt safe and loved. They were a happy family.

Once there was a boy named Charlie. Charlie wanted to go on an adventure. He needed a passport for the adventure, so he went to the store. At the store, the storekeeper asked for a fee. Charlie didn't have the fee. The storekeeper got very angry. He started to fight with Charlie. Charlie tried to run away, but the storekeeper was too fast. Suddenly, an icy wind blew. It was enough to scare the storekeeper. Charlie used that chance to run away. He quickly grabbed the passport from the storekeeper and ran away. But his adventure was only just beginning.

Once upon a time, in a little house, there lived a girl named Lily. Lily had a big, original mirror that she loved. She would look into the mirror and make funny faces every day.

One day, Lily's friend, Tom, came over to play. Tom saw the original mirror and said, "Wow, that's a big mirror! Can I borrow it for a day?" Lily thought about it and said, "Okay, you can borrow it, but be careful!"

Tom took the mirror to his house and put it in his room. He looked into the mirror and made funny faces, just like Lily. Tom had so much fun with the mirror.

The next day, Tom brought the mirror back to Lily's house. "Thank you for letting me borrow your mirror," Tom said. "I had so much fun!" Lily smiled and said, "You're welcome! I'm glad you liked it."

From that day on, Lily and Tom would take turns borrowing the original mirror and making funny faces together. They became the best of friends and had lots of fun with the big mirror.

Once there was a little girl called Bella. Bella had a best friend called Harry. Every day they would play together and have lots of fun.

One day, Bella and Harry were playing hide and seek. Bella ran and found a good place to hide. But when Harry came to look for her, he couldn't find her. Bella waited and waited, but Harry never came.

Finally, Bella realised that Harry had forgotten their game. She was sad, so she went back to Harry's house.

When they met, Bella said: "Harry, did you forget our game?"

Harry said: "Oh, I'm sorry Bella, I did forget. I'm so sorry".

Bella smiled and said: "That's okay, Harry. It's fair to forget sometimes".

Bella and Harry hugged and went to play together again. They had a wonderful day and never forgot to play together again.

Once upon a time, there was a nosy vegetable farmer. He loved to grow big, juicy vegetables in his garden. Every morning, he would wake up early and go outside to check his vegetables.

One morning, he heard a voice coming from his vegetable patch. He was curious and went over to see who it was.

"Hello!" he said, "Who are you?" 

"I'm a three-year-old. I wanted to make something special with your vegetables!"

The farmer was amazed. He smiled and said, "That's wonderful! You can take whatever you like. Let me know if you need any help."

The little boy thanked the farmer and went to work collecting vegetables. He found tomatoes, cucumbers, carrots, and peppers and began to make something special with them. 

After a while, the farmer was so curious that he had to go check on the boy. As he walked up, the farmer saw the little boy smiling and proudly holding a big plate of vegetable salad.

He smiled and said, "You did a wonderful job! I'm so proud of you."

The little boy beamed with pride. The nosy vegetable farmer had made his day!

One day, a very special day arrivedâ€”it was Mommy's birthday! The family was so excited and planned a delicious treat for her. They all worked together to bake a yummy cake.

Everyone was so proud of their work in the kitchen, but then something disgusting happened. Little Johnny dropped the cake on the ground. Everyone was so sad that the surprise was ruined.

But Mommy was so happy that her family had put their effort into something special for her. Finally, they went back to the kitchen and baked a new cake.

The new cake turned out to be even better than the first one. It tasted so sweet and was just perfect for Mommy's special day. Everyone was so glad that the nasty surprise didn't ruin the birthday!

Once there was a little girl named Emma who loved to play. One day, Emma went to the living room and saw a black cushion on the floor.

â€œWhatâ€™s that?â€ she asked.

Her mum replied, â€œItâ€™s a cushion, a special seat for you to rest on.â€

Emma was so excited that she immediately sat down and played on it. She jumped back and forth, and flopped around like she was an acrobat!

"Woohoo!" Emma shouted in glee.

When she got tired, Emma lay down on the cushion and looked up at the sun streaming through the window. "This is the best ever!" she said.

Emma played on her cushion many days afterwards and always had loads of fun.

Once upon a time there was a naughty mouse who liked to steal things. One day, he saw something sparkly in the grass. It was a blue button rolling around in the wind. He liked the way it looked so he decided to steal it. But then, a harsh voice yelled out, "Hey, give back my button!" 

The mouse froze, not knowing what to do. He slowly turned around and saw a big cat standing there. He said, "I didn't mean to steal it. I wanted to keep it for myself, but I will give it back if you want."
 
The cat replied, "I want it back. You must never steal from others, or you will get in trouble." 

The mouse nodded and handed back the button. He promised himself that he would never steal again, and he kept his promise. The cat thanked him for being honest and the mouse scurried away, never looking back.

Imagine a band of happy, healthy friends. There were five of them. Bob the bear, Daisy the dog, Peter the pig, Mila the mouse and Sammy the spider. 

They started on a great adventure. First, they went to the park to play. They ran around, played tag and ate ice cream. Next, they visited the forest to climb trees. They laughed as they raced higher and higher up the branches!. 

Finally, it was time for them to say goodbye. They said, "Farewell!" and hugged each other. Then they went off in different directions. 

The five friends will always remember the fun times they had together, and will look forward to meeting up again soon!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to cook with her mommy in the kitchen. One day, they decided to make cookies. Lily helped mix the dough and put it in the oven to bake. While they waited, they watched a funny cartoon on TV. 

When the cookies were done, they took them out of the oven and let them cool. Lily took a bite and made a sour face. They had put too much lemon in the batter! But they didn't give up. They added more sugar and tried again. This time, the cookies were sweet and delicious. Lily was happy and proud of what they had made together.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named John. He had a brown sweater he loved very much and wore every day. John believed if he had the sweater, everything would be okay. One day, something happened and the brown sweater was gone. No one knew where it was!

John was very sad and was sure he would never find his sweater. He asked everyone he saw if they knew where it was, but no one had seen it. He searched his house, the park and the playground, but no luck. He was so sad that he cried.

But then something amazing happened! A neighbor had seen the brown sweater and asked if it belonged to John. He ran over and when he saw it, he knew it was his! He was so happy and believed all was right with the world again. He put on the sweater and hugged it tight, never wanting to let it go.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Emily. She wanted to go for a walk, so she put on her shoes and set off outside. 

On her way, she passed by a big hill. "I want to roll down the hill," said Emily. 

Her mom said, "That sounds like fun, but be careful not to get hurt!" Emily nodded and began rolling down the hill. Before she knew it, she had rolled right to the bottom of the hill. 

To her surprise, she saw a big zero at the bottom. She bent down to take a closer look. "What is this zero?" Emily asked. 

"It's a zero, honey," her mom said. "When you roll a zero, it means you've earned zero points." 

"But it doesn't hurt," said Emily. 

Her mom smiled and said, "No, Emily, rolling a zero can't hurt you." 

Emily grinned and started rolling around the zero, having lots of fun. She smiled, and ran back to the top of the hill. 

And ever since then, Emily has loved rolling around the zero!

Peter was very hungry. He looked around and saw a big building. He wanted to go inside and see what was inside. So he ran to the building. He opened the door and walked inside.

He saw a lot of books and shelves with books on them. He was so excited! He wanted to read the books. So he picked up one of the books and started to read.

He was very happy. He read a lot of stories. He was so happy he could read. Then he started to get very hungry again. He stopped reading and left the building.

He ran home and found his mom. She made him a delicious lunch. He ate it all very quickly. He was so full and he was no longer hungry.

He was very happy that he was able to read the books and then get something to eat. He knew he'd be back at the building to read more stories soon.

Once there were two little bunnies. All they wanted was some cheese. One bunny was gentle and the other bunny was more rambunctious. 

They decided one day that they would go and find some cheese. They hopped off, down the path and into the forest. After searching and searching, eventually they found a big piece of cheese! 

The gentle bunny was excited and wanted to savor the cheese, but the rambunctious bunny wanted it all now! Eventually, the bunnies decided to take turns. They each had a big bite, savoring each morsel, until eventually their treat was gone. 

The little bunnies were so happy with their adventure that they decided to go find cheese more often. The gentle bunny taught the rambunctious bunny how to be more careful and gentle with their treats. Each time they found cheese, they would share and enjoy it together.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tommy. Tommy was three years old and he loved playing with his toys.
One day, Tommy was playing with his toys when he came across a strange looking grape. It was smooth and purple and Tommy had never seen one like it before. He was about to pick it up, when he heard a voice. 
"Please pause," it said. "That's my grape!". 
Tommy looked up and saw a smiling old lady. 
"This is my special grape," she said. "It tastes delicious and I want to share with you". 
Tommy smiled and paused. He reached out and took the grape from the lady's hand. As Tommy took a bite, he felt its sweetness and smoothness. He loved it!
 
The old lady smiled and watched Tommy happily eat the grape. "Thank you," she said. 

Tommy smiled and then waved goodbye to the old lady as he skipped away to play with his toys. From then on, Tommy always paused and enjoyed a special grape when the old lady was around.

Mum and Dad took Alex to the beach. Alex was very excited and skipped around the sand. All of a sudden, he spotted something amazing. It was a big rock that sparkled in the sun. He was so excited that he wanted to lift it.

Mum said, "That's an amazing rock. Can you lift it?". Alex tried with all his might and eventually he managed to lift the rock. He laughed with joy and ran around the beach with it. 

Dad said, "That's an amazing rock, Alex. Can you carry it to me?". Alex tried to carry the rock but it was too heavy. He struggled and worked hard but eventually he managed to lift it again. 

Mum said, "Well done, Alex. You are so strong. You did an amazing job lifting that rock". Alex was so proud of himself and felt so strong. He held up the rock and said to Mum and Dad, "I did it!".

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She lived in a house with her mom and dad. One day, Lily's mom asked her to help clean the house. Lily was happy to help. She took a mop and started cleaning the floor. 

While she was cleaning, her dad came and saw her. "You are doing a great job, Lily! I support you," he said. Lily felt happy and kept cleaning. 

After some time, Lily's mom came back and saw the clean floor. "Wow, Lily! The floor looks so beautiful now. You did a great job," she said. Lily smiled and felt proud of herself. 

From that day on, Lily always helped her mom and dad in cleaning the house. She knew that it made them happy and she felt happy too.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Joe. He loved to play outside. One day, Joe saw a big blue top. He was so excited, he ran over to it. Joe picked up the top, put it on the ground, and started to spin it. He laughed as it spun round and round. 

The top stopped spinning, but Joe wanted it to keep going. He stepped away and yelled, "I want the top to spin!" 

Suddenly a voice came out of the sky. It said, "If Joe wants the top to keep spinning, he needs to take the spin test." 

Joe wasn't sure what a spin test was, but he was brave. He looked up and said, "Okay, I'll take the test!"

The voice said, "Good! To finish the spin test, you must spin the top until it stops by itself. Go ahead and try."

So Joe stepped forward, blew on the top to make it spin, and watched as it spun round and round. Finally, it stopped spinning on its own. Joe had passed the spin test! 

The voice said, "Congratulations Joe! Now the top will spin forever."

Joe was so happy, he jumped for joy! Now he could enjoy spinning his big blue top as long as he wanted.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play pretend with her toys. One day, she decided to wrap her teddy bear in a blanket and pretend he was a baby. She rocked him back and forth and sang him a lullaby.

Suddenly, Lily heard an enormous noise outside. She looked out the window and saw a big truck driving by. It was so big, it looked like a giant! Lily pretended the truck was a monster and she had to hide from it.

After the truck passed, Lily unwrapped her teddy bear and gave him a big hug. She was happy to have a friend to play pretend with.

Jimmy was excited to go to the beach. He had never seen a beach before but his mom told him it was going to be a lot of fun.
Jimmyâ€™s mom packed a bag with some snacks and beverages and Jimmyâ€™s dad brought a big umbrella. They also packed some folding chairs and a large beach blanket.
When they got to the beach, Jimmy was amazed. He could see the water and it was so wide. The sand was soft and Jimmy liked running his toes through it.
Jimmy wanted to go in the water but he wasn't sure if the water was too deep. His dad recommended he take one inch steps and then he could count how long it took to get to the water.
Jimmy followed his dadâ€™s recommendation and was able to get to the water. It was the perfect day and Jimmy had lots of fun.

Once there was an angel who wanted to relax. She found a nice quiet spot, but it was very hard to find silence. Everywhere was so noisy! She tried very hard to relax and finally she closed her eyes and started to drift off. 

But just then, she heard a voice. 

"Are you an angel?", it said.

Startled, the angel opened her eyes and saw a little boy. He was only 3 years old, but he was smiling brightly. 

The angel was curious, so she asked, "What made you think I was an angel?"

"Because," the little boy said, "angels come to make people relax. That's what my mommy tells me. When I am feeling noisy and upset, she tells me to think of an angel." 

The angel smiled. "That's a good idea," she said. "When you need help to relax, just think of an angel. That will help."

The little boy nodded and said, "Thank you! Bye!." The angel waved and watched as the little boy scampered away, then she closed her eyes and relaxed.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Flora. Flora was always so busy and she never seemed to have enough time. One day she was so busy that she forgot to wash her toys. She felt a little bit guilty, but could not find the time to do the chores.

So that evening, when Mum came home she asked if Flora had washed her toys. "No," said Flora, feeling very guilty. Mum said, "That's OK. But you need to clean your toys as soon as you can. Look at all this dust!"

The next day, Flora made sure to find some time to wash her toys. She felt very happy once she had washed all the dirt away. Mum was very pleased when Flora showed her the clean toys. And Flora was no longer guilty!

Once upon a time, there was a little penguin named Pip. Pip loved to waddle around and play with his penguin friends. One day, Pip decided to create a big snow fort. He worked and worked until the fort was as tall as he was! 

But then, a big polar bear came along and wanted to play too. Pip was anxious because he knew polar bears could be dangerous. The polar bear started to knock down the snow fort and Pip tried to stop him. 

But it was too late. The polar bear knocked down the fort and Pip was stuck underneath. Pip's friends tried to help him, but it was too late. Pip had been hurt and couldn't move. The friends were sad and didn't know what to do. And that's how the story of Pip the penguin ended.

Once upon a time there was a wealthy farmer who lived on a farm. He loved growing crops and taking care of his animals.

One day he woke up and decided he didn't want to be a farmer anymore. So he quit the farm. He sold all the animals, the crops and the farm and made a lot of money.

He went to a new land and lived in a really nice house. He bought lots of toys and sweets and was very happy.

But one day he was walking in the park and he saw a little farm. He remembered how much he loved taking care of the animals and plants on his own farm and he decided to quit his fancy life and go back to the farm.

So the wealthy farmer went back to his farm and he was very happy once again. He took care of his animals and crops, he made new friends and he was never so happy.

Tommy was very nervous when he went to the library with his mum. He had never been to a library before and had never seen so many books! His mum was nice and told him it was ok to be a bit scared. She said they could take some books home to read.

At the library they quickly found lots of books they liked. Tommy picked out one that was full of pictures and his mum chose one with lots of words. They both took them to the front desk to pay.

At home, Tommy was so excited about his new book. He and his mum read it together and he loved looking at all the pictures. From then on, Tommy and his mum went to the library every week. They always took home two books and spent lots of time reading them.

Tommy felt much less nervous at the library, and his mum was so proud of him!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a bed with a big, bouncy mattress. Every night, she would jump on the mattress and make a lot of noise. Her mommy would tell her to stop, but she never listened.

One day, Lily's mommy went to the store and left the house unlocked. A bad man came in and saw Lily's mommy's purse. He wanted to take it, but he heard Lily jumping on the mattress and making a lot of noise. He got scared and ran away.

When Lily's mommy came back, she saw that her purse was still there. She was happy, but then she saw that Lily's bedroom was a mess. The mattress was on the floor and the window was open. She looked outside and saw that Lily was gone. She searched everywhere, but she couldn't find her. Lily had jumped out the window and hurt herself. She had to go to the hospital and couldn't jump on her mattress anymore.

Once upon a time, a boy named Timmy went to the hospital. He was feeling sick and needed to see the doctor. Timmy was scared, but the nurses were very nice to him. They gave him stickers and a teddy bear to hug. 

When Timmy saw the doctor, he felt even more scared. But the doctor was also very nice. She checked Timmy's temperature and gave him some medicine. Timmy started to feel better. 

After a little while, Timmy's mom came to pick him up from the hospital. She gave him a big hug and told him how proud she was of him for being so brave. Timmy felt happy and relieved. He knew that even when he was scared, he could always find help and nice people to hug at the hospital.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her pillow every night before bed. Her pillow was soft and fluffy, and she loved to hug it tight.

One day, Lily's mom became very harsh with her. She scolded Lily for not cleaning up her toys. Lily felt very sad and cried herself to sleep that night.

The next day, Lily's pillow became very hard and uncomfortable. She couldn't sleep well and felt very tired the next day. She realized that her sadness and tears had made her pillow change.

Lily learned that being sad and crying can make things become worse. She promised herself to always try to be happy, even when things are hard.

Once upon a time, there was a funny little mouse called Sam. Sam had the most creative ideas, but no one paid much attention to them.

One day, Sam decided to do something about it. He grabbed a big box and started to squeeze it with all his might. His tiny little paws managed to create the most amazing sound.

A nearby pigeon heard the sound and was so surprised that it asked, "What was that sound?"

Sam grinned and replied, "It's my creative idea! I'm using the box to make music!"

The pigeon was so impressed that soon all the animals started to join in. Soon, the forest was full of funny little animals squeezing boxes, creating the most wonderful music. 

Everyone had a wonderful time and Sam finally felt appreciated for his creative talent.

Once upon a time there was a girl. She had a long, red scarf. The girl wanted to cut the scarf in two.

She went outside and the wind was blowing. She held the scarf high in the air and the wind caught it. The wind blew the scarf all over the sky.

The girl was sad, because now she could not cut the scarf in two. But then, the wind blew the scarf back down to the girl. But it was a long, long scarf, so it was now twice as long as before.

The girl was so happy, and she quickly cut the scarf in two. She kept one piece of the scarf, and gave the other piece to her best friend.

The girl and her friend were very happy, and they both wore the red scarves with a smile.

Tom likes to polish his dad's razor. He thinks it is a shiny toy that makes his dad's face smooth. He waits for his dad to go to work, then he sneaks into the bathroom and takes the razor from the drawer. He rubs it with a cloth until it sparkles.

One day, Tom sees a unique thing on the wall. It is a big mirror that shows him and the razor. He wonders what will happen if he touches the razor to his face. He thinks it will make him look like his dad. He lifts the razor and moves it closer to his cheek.

But the razor is not a toy. It is sharp and hurts Tom. He feels a sting and sees red on his face and on the mirror. He drops the razor and starts to cry. He runs to his mom and shows her his boo-boo. She is scared and angry. She hugs him and puts a band-aid on his cut. She tells him to never touch the razor again. She says it is dangerous and not for kids.

Tom is sorry and sad. He does not want to polish the razor anymore. He says he is sorry to his mom and his dad. He learns his lesson and plays with his safe toys instead. He likes his cars and his blocks and his teddy bear. He does not need the razor to look like his dad. He loves his dad and his dad loves him, even with a band-aid on his face.

Charlie the monkey was feeling very scared. He had seen a big, scary animal and he didn't know what to do. He wanted to hide, so he crept into a corner full of furniture. He noticed a nice, comfortable chair to sit on and he snuggled in. 

Suddenly, he heard a gentle voice. It was a mouse who had been watching him. He spoke softly, "Don't be scared, little one. I'm your friend."

Charlie was very relieved. He liked the mouse, and he realized that he could trust him. He felt much better.

The mouse smiled at Charlie and said, "The furniture here is very good. It will keep you safe. There is nothing to be scared of now."

Charlie looked around and realized the mouse was right. He thanked his little friend and smiled. From that day on, Charlie knew that he could always trust his furry friends.

Once upon a time, there was a lazy cat named Tom. Tom liked to sleep all day and didn't like to play with his friends. One day, Tom's friend Jerry came to visit him. Jerry was a little mouse who liked to play and have fun. 

"Hey Tom, do you want to play with me?" asked Jerry.

"No, I'm too lazy to play," replied Tom.

Jerry didn't give up and tried to convince Tom to play with him. "Come on Tom, let's crawl under the sofa and play hide and seek," said Jerry.

Tom thought for a moment and finally agreed to play. They crawled under the sofa and started to play. Suddenly, they heard a loud noise. It was an arrow that had hit the wall behind them. They were scared and quickly crawled out from under the sofa. 

"Let's go play somewhere else, it's not safe here," said Jerry.

Tom agreed and they went to play outside. They had a lot of fun and Tom realized that playing with friends was much better than sleeping all day. From that day on, Tom was never lazy again and always played with his friends.

Once there was a young girl called Louisa. She had bright eyes and big ears. Every morning, she ran to the lake to bathe.

One day, she was being careless and jumped into the lake without looking. Suddenly, her foot got caught and she couldn't move. She was scared and started to cry.

A frog nearby heard her crying and said, "Don't worry, young one. I can help you." The frog took out a key and set her free.

Louisa thanked the frog. She promised to be more careful and said goodbye. She went home, changed into her night clothes, and ran to the lake to bathe again. 

This time she was extra careful and enjoyed the peaceful feeling of being in the water of the lake. She smiled.

Lily and Ben are playing in the garden. They have a big box of toys. They like to dig holes and bury their toys. Then they pretend to be pirates and look for treasure.

"Look, I found a shiny ring!" Lily says, holding up a plastic ring. "It is so pretty!"

"Wow, can I see?" Ben asks, running over to her. He takes the ring and puts it on his finger. "It is too big for me. You can have it."

"Thank you, Ben. You are a good friend." Lily says, smiling. She gives him a hug.

They hear a loud noise. It is their dog, Rex. He is barking and jumping. He sees their toys in the holes. He thinks they are bones. He starts to dig them out.

"Hey, stop it, Rex!" Ben shouts. "Those are our toys, not your bones!"

"Bad dog, bad dog!" Lily says, waving her arms. "Leave our toys alone!"

But Rex does not listen. He digs faster and faster. He throws dirt and toys everywhere. He makes a big mess.

Lily and Ben are sad. They worked hard to bury their toys. Now they are all dirty and broken. They do not have any treasure left.

They look at Rex. He is happy. He has a big smile on his face. He has a toy car in his mouth. He thinks he found a bone.

"Rex, you are a silly dog!" Lily says, shaking her head. "That is not a bone. That is a car. Cars need oxygen to go. Bones do not need oxygen."

"Oxygen?" Ben asks, tilting his head. "What is oxygen?"

"Oxygen is what we breathe." Lily says, pointing to her nose. "We need oxygen to live. Cars need oxygen to go. Plants need oxygen to grow. Everything needs oxygen."

"Wow, oxygen is important!" Ben says, nodding. "Can we see oxygen?"

"No, we cannot see oxygen. Oxygen is invisible." Lily says, shaking her head. "But we can feel oxygen. Oxygen is in the air. Air is what we feel when we blow."

Lily and Ben blow. They feel the air on their faces. They laugh.

"Blowing is fun!" Ben says, blowing again.

"Yes, blowing is fun!" Lily agrees, blowing too.

They blow and blow. They make bubbles with their spit. They blow at Rex. Rex barks and chases the bubbles. He drops the toy car.

Lily and Ben see the toy car. They run to get it. They wipe the dirt off. They push the car. The car goes.

"Look, the car is going!" Lily says, clapping her hands. "The car has oxygen!"

"Yes, the car has oxygen!" Ben says, cheering. "The car is happy!"

Lily and Ben are happy too. They have a toy car. They have oxygen. They have each other. They have fun. They forget about the mess. They forget about the toys. They forget about the bones.

They play with the car. They play with Rex. They play in the garden. They are happy.

Anna and Ben were adventurous twins who liked to explore the woods behind their house. One day, they found a big pile of ash near a burnt tree. They wondered what had made the fire and what was inside the ash.

"Maybe it was a dragon," Ben said. "Maybe there are dragon eggs in the ash."

"Let's look," Anna said. She took a stick and poked the ash. She saw something shiny and round. "Look, Ben, I found one!"

She lifted the stick with the shiny thing on it. It was a metal ball with a button on it. Anna was curious and pressed the button.

Suddenly, the ball made a loud noise and a bright flash. Anna and Ben dropped the stick and covered their eyes. When they opened them again, the ball was gone. It had vanished.

"Wow, what was that?" Ben asked.

"I don't know," Anna said. "Maybe it was a magic ball. Maybe it took us to another place."

They looked around and saw that the woods were different. The trees were taller and greener, and there were strange flowers and animals. They heard a roar in the distance.

"Maybe it was a dragon," Ben said again.

"Maybe we should go back," Anna said.

But they didn't know how to go back. They had no stick, no ball, no ash. They had only each other and their adventurous spirit. They decided to explore the new woods and find a way home. Maybe they would meet a dragon, or maybe something else. They held hands and walked on.

Once there was a foolish rabbit who was always on the lookout for surprises. One day, he was hopping around in the grass when he spotted something shiny. He hopped closer and found that a big surprise was waiting for him- a big piece of meat! He couldn't believe it.

The rabbit had never seen meat so big before and he was so excited. He grabbed the meat and quickly started to munch it all up. He was so happy and couldn't believe his luck. 

But then the rabbit heard a loud noise. He looked up and saw a farmer coming towards him. The farmer was not happy about the rabbit eating his meat and he started to shout. The rabbit was so scared he quickly hopped away and never came back. 

The rabbit had been very foolish to trust such a surprise, but it taught him a valuable lesson- never trust anything that looks too good to be true!

Once upon a time, a mummy, daddy and their little girl went to a park. The little girl was excited. She ran around, played with the other children and had lots of fun. Suddenly, she noticed something weird. It was a weapon that someone had left behind in the sandpit.

The little girl got curious. She picked it up, as she hadn't seen anything like it before. It felt cold and heavy in her hands. She looked around to see if anyone noticed her, but no-one was paying attention.

Suddenly, she realized what it was. She was holding a weapon. It made her feel scared and she quickly put it back where she found it. After that, the little girl went back to playing with her friends. She had learnt an important lesson that day. We must all be careful and never touch weird things!

Once upon a time, there was a naughty little boy who loved to ride his tricycle. He loved the way the tricycle felt under his skin as the wind blew through his hair. 

One day he was riding his tricycle in the park when he saw a beautiful blue and yellow bike. He stopped and admired the bike and wanted it for himself. 

Suddenly, the little boy heard someone coming and he quickly hopped on his tricycle and rode away as fast as he could. He giggled to himself when no one saw him and rode as far away from the bike as he could.

When he got home, he was a bit tired but still very happy! He had a new adventure to think about and he was full of smiles. He couldn't wait to ride his tricycle again.

Sara and Tom are friends. They like to play in the park. They have a ball and a kite. They run and laugh and have fun.

One day, a big dog comes to the park. The dog is not nice. He barks and chases Sara and Tom. He wants their ball and their kite. Sara and Tom are scared. They run away from the dog. They look for a safe place.

They see a fence. The fence is tall and strong. It has a gate. Sara and Tom run to the gate. They open it and go inside. They close the gate. The dog cannot get in. He is angry. He jumps and scratches at the fence. He makes a loud noise.

Sara and Tom are inside the fence. They see a house. The house is small and cozy. It has a window and a door. They see a lady. The lady is kind. She smiles and waves at Sara and Tom. She comes to the gate. She opens it and talks to the dog. She tells the dog to go away. The dog listens. He stops barking and chasing. He walks away.

Sara and Tom are happy. They thank the lady. The lady invites them to her house. She gives them cookies and milk. She tells them stories and sings them songs. She is a grandma. She likes Sara and Tom. Sara and Tom like her too.

They are glad they found the fence. They are glad they met the grandma. They are glad they are safe and warm. They do not weep anymore. They smile and hug the grandma. They are friends.

One day, a little boy named Tim found a long stick. He called it a "spear". Tim liked to play with his spear in the yard. The spear was not strong. It was delicate. Tim had to be careful with it.

One day, Tim saw a big bug. He wanted to catch it with his spear. But the bug was fast. Tim started to panic. He ran after the bug, but he could not catch it.

Tim's mom saw him panic. She told Tim not to worry. Tim's mom helped him catch the bug. They put the bug in a jar. Tim was happy. He learned that it is okay to ask for help when he feels panic.

One day, a little girl named Lucy went to the park. She saw her friend, Tim, who was sad. Tim said, "I lost my diamond." Lucy wanted to help, so she said, "Let's look for it together."

They looked high and low. The sun was harsh, but they did not stop. They looked under the slide and behind the swings. Then, Lucy had an idea. She said, "Tim, let's perform a dance to make the diamond come back."

So, Lucy and Tim danced and danced. They jumped and twirled. Suddenly, they saw something shiny near the sandbox. They ran over and found the diamond! Tim was so happy, and he said, "Thank you, Lucy, for helping me find my diamond."

From that day on, Lucy and Tim were the best of friends. They always helped each other, no matter what. And sometimes, they would perform their special dance, just for fun.

Once upon a time there was a brave cow. She was called Daisy and she lived on a hot farm. Every day she would slip around the fields, enjoying the sun and the warm heat.

One day, Daisy decided to be extra brave. She wanted to go outside the farm and explore. As she started to slip away from the farm, Daisy saw some tall trees and lovely green grass. She kept slipping until she found a big pond.

Daisy was amazed. She had never seen a pond before. She saw ducks swimming around and the sun twinkling on the water. She wanted to go and explore, but she was scared. Was it safe?

To be brave, Daisy stepped forward and started to slip carefully around the pond. She was so happy and soon she forgot to be scared. She looked around, enjoying her new world. She was so glad to be brave and explore. 

Then, before she knew it, Daisy had slipped right back to the farm. She went back to the cows, feeling proud and happy with herself. She had been brave, and she found a great secret. She had seen a pond!

Once upon a time there was a boy called Jim. He was three years old and he liked to count things. One day, he found a tool in his garden. It was a healthy tool. Jim was very excited about his discovery and he began to explore it.

He took it to his friend's house and began to count the different parts of the tool. First, he counted the screws, then he counted the pieces of metal, and finally he counted the handle. Jim was so happy that he had found the tool and that he could count all the things he saw.

He went home feeling very proud of himself. He showed his family the tool and he explained how he had used it to count things. Everyone was impressed by Jim's counting skills and healthy tool. From that day on, Jim had a lot of fun counting all the things he could find.

Mum had something special for John. She was getting ready to make him a surprise. She went to the kitchen, picking up a tray.

She prepared the tray carefully. On it she put two pieces of toast and some jam. Then she cut a banana, added some slices of cheese, and some orange juice.

John was so excited when he saw the tray full of delicious surprises. He was so happy that he gave Mum a big hug.

But then, something went wrong. John accidentally knocked over the tray and all the yummy food went everywhere. He felt so miserable.

But Mum was very kind. She hugged John to make him feel better and told him she'd make another tray full of surprises. John smiled, feeling much better again.

Once upon a time, there were two friends - Franny and Tom. Tom had a special knob that he liked to show off. One day, Franny asked Tom why he liked the knob so much. "This knob is very fancy," said Tom. "It's from the King's palace." Franny gasped. She wanted one too! 

Tom smiled. He wanted to share the knob with his friend. He made a plan to visit the King's palace so he could get Franny a knob of her own. The two friends went to the palace and asked the King for a fancy knob for Franny. 

The King said, "I'm happy to share my knob with your friend. I hope you both enjoy it." The friends thanked the King and went back home with the new knob. From then on, they shared the knob whenever they could. It was their favourite thing to do!

Bob and his sister Sally were walking along the beach.

Bob saw something in the sand and shouted "Look!"

Sally ran over and saw a bright green palm tree. Its leaves were swaying in the breeze.

"This tree must have been here for a long time," said Sally. "It looks very reliable!"

Bob agreed and they both started climbing the tree. They laughed and shouted as they went higher and higher until they reached the top.

They stayed up there for a while, enjoying the view.

"This is the best adventure ever," said Bob.

Sally smiled and shouted, "Let's do it again tomorrow!"

Once there was an egg that was not happy. He argued about everything and was very disagreeable. Everyone shook their heads and said he was crazy.

One day the egg decided to take a walk around the farm. It was sunny and he felt brave. As he looked around, he saw a little goat playing in a field and he smiled. He went over to introduce himself but the goat didn't want to talk. He just frowned and disagreed with everything the egg said.

The egg became angry and yelled at the little goat, who just looked away. Then, the egg grabbed the goat and tried to shake him. The goat was frightened and began to run away. Suddenly, the egg jumped and was knocked over by a tree branch.

The poor egg lay there, motionless. Everyone ran to help him but it was too late. The crazy egg had died. The goat, feeling a little guilty but also a little relieved, ran away never to be seen again.

Lily liked to look at the sky. She saw many clouds. Some were big and white, some were small and gray. She wondered what they felt like. She wanted to touch them.

One day, she had a good idea. She asked her dad to help her. He had a big balloon. He filled it with air and tied a string to it. He gave it to Lily. She smiled and said thank you.

Lily held the string and ran outside. She looked for a cloud that was low and close. She saw one that was fluffy and soft. She ran towards it with the balloon. She hoped to succeed.

She reached the cloud and lifted the balloon. She tried to touch the cloud with the balloon. But the cloud was not solid. It was made of tiny drops of water. The balloon went through the cloud and came out wet.

Lily was surprised and a little sad. She did not touch the cloud. She did not succeed. But she learned something new. She learned that clouds were not like balloons. They were different and beautiful.

She looked at the sky again. She saw many clouds. She smiled and said wow. She still liked to look at the sky.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and explore the world around her. One day, she saw a beautiful purple flower by the river. She picked it up and smelled it, it smelled so sweet.

As she walked along the river, she saw a big rock. She climbed on top of it and looked down at the river. It was so big and flowed so fast. She wondered where it went and what was at the end of it.

Suddenly, she saw a man walking towards her. He looked very wise and kind. Lily asked him where the river went and what was at the end of it. The man smiled and explained that the river went all the way to the ocean, where it met the big blue sea. Lily was amazed and thanked the man for explaining it to her. She knew she would always remember this day by the river and the wise man who taught her about it.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Sarah. Sarah was three years old and she was very brave.

One day, Sarah went for a walk in the forest with her grandparents. As they were walking, Sarah noticed a cobweb in a tree. She asked her grandparents what it was. They explained it was a cobweb, spun by a spider.

Sarah wanted to look at the cobweb, so she bravely ordered her grandparents to lift her up high so she could get a closer look. The cobweb was so delicate and sparkly Sarah was mesmerised.

Suddenly, a harsh voice shouted at Sarah from behind. It was a scary old man. He was angry about Sarah looking at his cobweb and he ordered her to go away.

Sarah was scared, but she was brave. She held her grandparents' hands tight and together they walked away from the cobweb.

Once upon a time there was a face that was very sad. His name was Charlie and he had no ticket. He wanted to go to the fun park, but he had no ticket.

He looked around, but he could not find one. Then, he saw a ticket lying on the ground. It looked very old, but it was a ticket. He was very happy!

He picked it up, but it was very tight. He tried to pull it, but it wouldn't come off. He wanted it, so he gave it a bite. The ticket came off and he was very happy.

He ran to the fun park and showed his ticket to the man. He was so shocked, he couldn't believe it! Charlie went inside and had fun. He couldn't stop smiling for the whole day!

Once upon a time, a nosy king lived in a castle. He was nosy, because he liked to look out of the window to see what was happening all around. 

One day when he looked out, the king saw that the door to the castle was open! He was worried that something might get in, so he hurried over to close it. 

He reached the door and he closed it. Now the castle was safe and nothing could get in. 

The king then returned to his window to keep an eye on things, but this time he made sure that the door stayed closed.

Once upon a time there was a mummy, daddy and their little girl called Sarah. One day they were taking a walk in the wild woods when they spotted a strange frame lying on the ground.

Mummy said, "That's so strange - what could it be?"

Daddy pointed and said, "There's something inside."

Sarah ran over and looked inside. "It's a wild squirrel!" She cried.

Mummy laughed and said, "Let's take it home and keep it as a pet."

So, Daddy picked up the frame and the happy family went home with their new pet!

Sara and Ben are twins. They like to play in the backyard. They have a swing, a slide and a sandbox. Sometimes they share, sometimes they fight.

One day, they see a big box in the backyard. It is open. They run to the box and look inside. There are many toys and books and clothes. They are happy and excited.

"Wow, look at all these things!" Sara says. "Can we play with them?"

"I don't know," Ben says. "Maybe they are for someone else."

They hear Mom calling from the house. "Sara, Ben, come here please. I have something to tell you."

They leave the box and go to Mom. Mom smiles and hugs them.

"Guess what, my loves?" Mom says. "You are going to have a baby brother or sister soon. These are some things for the baby. Do you want to help me sort them out?"

Sara and Ben are surprised and curious. They have many questions.

"Is the baby in your tummy?" Sara asks.

"Yes, it is," Mom says.

"When will the baby come out?" Ben asks.

"In a few months," Mom says.

"Can we play with the baby?" Sara asks.

"Of course, you can," Mom says. "But you have to be gentle and careful. The baby will be very small and fragile."

Sara and Ben nod. They want to be good big siblings. They go back to the backyard with Mom and help her manage the things for the baby. They are happy and proud. They can't wait to meet the baby.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside, especially near the river. One day, Lily's mom asked her a question. "What did you have for lunch?" her mom asked. Lily thought for a moment and then answered, "I had a peanut butter sandwich." 

Later that day, Lily was playing by the river when she accidentally dropped her favorite toy in the water. She felt so ashamed that she had been careless. But then, her dad came to the rescue and fished the toy out of the river for her. Lily was so happy and grateful that she hugged her dad tightly. 

From that day on, Lily made sure to be extra careful near the river. And whenever her parents asked her a question, she always made sure to answer truthfully.

Once upon a time, there was a young girl named Sally. She was only three years old, but already knew how to do so many things. One day, her mom asked her if she wanted to watch a film. Sally said, "Yes!" So they put on a film in their living room and Sally listened to all the sounds coming from the TV.

The film was about a normal family who lived in a cute little house. Sally watched as the family went on fun adventures and she smiled in delight. Sally was especially thrilled when they went to the zoo and saw so many animals! She loved listening to the chirps and roars of the creatures.

After the film was done, Sally said, "Can we watch it again?" Her mom said, "Yes, but later. We must do something else now." So Sally put her feet on the floor and dashed off to play. She knew it would only be a short while before she got to listen to the film again.

Once upon a time, there was a busy pick. Every day it would wander around the garden, looking for things to pick. It was never ever still, it was always so busy.

One day, the pick was walking around, when it saw a big rock in the way. The pick tried pushing the rock, but it was so heavy. So the pick just decided to stay with the rock and chat.

The pick soon realised the rock had a lot of wisdom to share. The rock said to the pick "Don't worry about being busy all the time, take some time to stay and appreciate the world the way it is".

The pick listened carefully and realised the rock was right. So from that day on, the pick made sure to take some time out each day to stay and appreciate the world around it.

The moral of this story is that it's ok to take some time to stop and appreciate the world around us. Even the busiest pick can find some time to stay and enjoy the moment.

Jack was walking outside one day. He saw a puddle on the sidewalk and ran over to it. Suddenly, he heard someone calling his name. He turned around to see his mom.

"Jack, don't jump in that puddle!" She said.

Jack looked up at her and said, "Why not?"

His mom said, "It's very cold and you might get separated from me."

Jack understood. He shivered a little and stepped away from the puddle. He thought the puddle was a bit scary too.

Jack and his mom continued walking. Jack waved goodbye to the puddle. He promised himself to only jump in puddles when mom was watching.

Ben and Mia were playing in the woods. They liked to pretend they were hunters, looking for animals. They had sticks for spears and leaves for hats. They were very quiet and careful.

Suddenly, they saw a big deer. It was brown and had horns. It was eating grass in a distant clearing. Ben and Mia blinked. They had never seen a deer before. They wanted to get closer and touch it.

"Let's go, Mia," Ben whispered. "We can be friends with the deer."

"No, Ben," Mia whispered back. "The deer might be scared of us. We should stay here and watch."

But Ben did not listen. He dropped his stick and ran towards the deer. He shouted, "Hello, deer! I am Ben! Do you want to play?"

The deer heard Ben and looked up. It saw him coming and got frightened. It turned and ran away, fast and far. Ben stopped and felt sad. He had scared the deer away.

Mia ran after Ben and hugged him. She said, "It's okay, Ben. The deer was not angry. It was just shy. Maybe we can see it again another day. Come on, let's go back and find our sticks. We can still be hunters."

Ben nodded and smiled. He said, "Okay, Mia. You are right. We can still be hunters. And maybe we can find other animals to play with. Come on, let's go."

They held hands and walked back to the woods. They were still friends and still hunters. They had fun and learned something new.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys all day long. He had a lot of cars, trucks, and trains that he would play with. One day, it started to rain really hard and the water started to rise. Soon, it was a big flood outside and the water was very thick. 

Timmy looked out the window and saw that the flood was getting closer to his house. He was scared, but his mom told him not to worry. She said they would be safe inside. So, Timmy and his mom played games and read books while they waited for the flood to go away. After a while, the rain stopped and the flood went down. Timmy was happy that he and his mom were safe and that he could go back to playing with his toys.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was very happy because she loved to play outside. One day, Lily went for a walk in the park and saw a beautiful butterfly. She wanted to catch it and name it, but she didn't know how. 

Suddenly, she saw a boy running and playing with his kite. Lily was so excited that she started to run too, but she didn't see a big hole in the ground. She fell down and hurt herself. 

Lily's mom came to help her and took her to the hospital. Lily learned that it's important to be careful when playing outside. She also learned that she should never give up on her dreams, but she should always be safe. Even though Lily was hurt, she was still happy because she learned an important lesson.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She had a friend named Max who was very good at drawing. Lily loved to watch Max draw and would always ask him to draw her pictures. Max was gifted and could draw anything Lily wanted.

One day, Lily and Max went to the park to play. Lily saw a shiny toy in the sandbox and wanted to play with it. Max told her to be careful because the toy looked old and broken. Lily didn't listen and started playing with the toy. Suddenly, the toy broke and Lily hurt her hand.

Lily started crying and Max tried to help her. He told her to be quiet so they wouldn't get in trouble. But Lily didn't trust Max anymore and blamed him for her injury. She went home and told her mom what happened. Her mom scolded her for not listening to Max and not being careful.

From that day on, Lily didn't want to play with Max anymore. She learned that it's important to trust your friends and listen to their advice.

Once there was a clever little mouse who lived in a big old house. She was sneaky and quick and her owner never knew she was around, but the mouse knew she was clever. 

Every day, the mouse collected all the crumbs she could find for her breakfast. One morning the mouse visited the kitchen and heard the owner's voice from upstairs. She hurried to hide, but just as she was crawling out of sight, she bumped into a box that made a loud noise. 

The owner shouted from upstairs, "Who's there?" But the mouse was too scared to answer. She quickly ran out of the room and hid in a safe spot.

The next morning, the mouse was more careful when she scurried to the kitchen. She gathered her crumbs and then went very quietly out of the room. 

The mouse learned a valuable lesson that day: even when she was clever, she still needed to be careful.

Once there was a little boy named Johnny. He was three years old and he loved to explore. One day Johnny decided to go for a walk. As he was walking he heard a loud noise. It was coming from a house up ahead. Johnny was curious, so he decided to see what was going on.

When he got close to the house he heard people speaking. The voices were loud and angry. Johnny did not understand what they were saying, but he could tell that the people were fighting. Johnny thought this was very disgusting. 

Suddenly Johnny heard another voice inside the house. It was a gentle voice that said, â€œStop arguing and let us speak about peace.â€ Johnny was curious to find out who was speaking. He tiptoed closer to the house and saw that it was an old man. 

The man said, â€œLet's all stop shouting and talk about peace.â€ Johnny was amazed at how such a small voice could bring so much peace. He smiled and quietly went back on his way, happy that he had seen something so peaceful.

Once upon a time, there was a gentle cat named Fluffy. Fluffy loved to step around the house and play with his toys. His favorite toy was a little ball that he would chase and jump on.

One day, Fluffy was playing near the table where his owner, Mommy, had her coffee. The coffee was in a big cup, and it smelled good. Fluffy wanted to see the coffee, so he stepped closer to the table.

As Fluffy stepped closer, he accidentally bumped the table. The coffee started to shake and wobble. Fluffy was scared, but he knew he had to be gentle. He carefully stepped back and watched as the coffee stopped shaking. Fluffy was happy that he didn't spill the coffee, and he went back to playing with his ball.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and go on adventures. One day, she went to visit her grandma who lived in an ancient house.

"Hi grandma!" said Lily, holding a present in her hand.

"Hello dear, what do you have there?" asked her grandma.

"It's a present for you!" replied Lily with a smile.

Her grandma opened the present and was surprised to find a beautiful necklace inside. "Thank you so much Lily, it's lovely!" she said.

Lily then noticed a jar on the shelf and asked her grandma, "What's in that jar?"

"It's a jar of candy, would you like some?" her grandma asked.

Lily nodded and her grandma twisted off the lid of the jar. They both enjoyed some candy together and had a wonderful day.

Once upon a time, there was a cat who was very shy. He loved playing with the other animals, but he was always too scared to do it. He wished he could be more brave.

One day a kind fairy came to him and said he had a special gift for the cat. He said "I believe in you, so here is a magical tail!" The cat was so surprised and happy.

The fairy told him he could use his tail to do whatever he wanted. So the cat began to practice and practice. He tried all sorts of things with his tail. And soon he felt much more brave and started to play with all the other animals.

The cat was so proud of his magical tail and he felt so happy. He now believes in himself and knows he can do anything!

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Maya. She liked to pick flowers, but one day she made a mistake. She was picking a flower from the neighbor's garden when she got caught.

The neighbor was so angry and put Maya in jail. Maya was very scared and she had no idea what to do. She started to cry and told the jailer she was sorry for her mistake.

Then, the jailer had an idea. She was not too fond of the neighbor either and thought it was very stupid of him to put Maya in jail. So the jailer let Maya go and told her never to pick the neighbor's flowers again.

Maya thanked the jailer and vowed never to make that mistake again. From then on, she only picked flowers from her own garden.

Once upon a time, there were two friends. They lived far from each other, but they never stopped dreaming of playing together.

One day, the first friend said, "I want to show you something special". So the friends started painting the universe. One painted stars and planets, the other created boats and birds.

Suddenly, the second friend shouted, "Wow, let's make something else!" The first friend replied, "Let's make a big lucky rainbow!"

So the pair mixed their paints and inventions to make a bright, lucky rainbow. As they finished, they both knew they had created something special.

The friends shared a hug and promised to create something even bigger next time. They knew that if they worked together, they could paint the most wonderful universe.

One day, a boy named Tom got a new scooter. He was very happy. He rode the scooter all day long. It was so much fun! But after a while, Tom started to feel uncomfortable. He was tired and needed to rest.

Tom saw his friend, Sue, and said, "Sue, my legs feel funny. I need to rest." Sue looked at Tom and said, "Okay, let's sit down and rest for a bit." So, they sat down under a big tree and rested. Tom felt better after resting.

After a while, Tom wanted to ride his scooter again. But when he went to get his scooter, it was gone! Tom and Sue looked everywhere, but they could not find the scooter. Tom was very sad. He had lost his new scooter, and he could not ride it anymore.

Once there was a lazy dolphin who lived in the sea. One day, the dolphin saw a boat. She swam over to the boat to take a closer look.

The dolphin asked the people in the boat, "What are you doing here?"

The people replied, "We are here to provide food for you and all the other dolphins in the sea."

The dolphin was so happy and thanked the people in the boat. From that day on, the people in the boat provided food for the dolphins every day.

The dolphin and all the other dolphins were so happy and content. They were never hungry or lazy anymore.

Once there were two friends, Tom and Sam. Tom had a triangle and he was very happy. But then something bad happened.
Tom suffered a lot. He was so sad that he dropped his triangle. He started to cry and Sam felt terrible.

Sam wanted to make Tom feel better so he gave him a hug. Tom felt a little bit better. He remembered the triangle and remembered that it was bad. So he asked Sam what to do.

Sam knew the answer: He picked up the triangle and took it to the playground. There they found lots of toys and children who were playing happily. Tom and Sam went up to them. They asked the children if they wanted the triangle.

The children were so excited and quickly took the triangle. Then Sam turned to Tom and said, "Don't worry, Tom. You don't have to suffer anymore because of the bad triangle". Tom smiled and they all went to enjoy the playground.

John had a new game. He wanted to play it every day. But his mom wanted him to do serious things. She said playing the game was a waste of time. Every day, John was sad. He wanted to play the game, but his mom was always making him do serious things. Every night, John wished he had played the game. He would regret not playing it.

One day, John's mom was busy. She said he could play the game for one hour. John was so excited! He played and played and had so much fun. When the hour was up, John was sad again. He wished he had more time to play. He regretted not playing longer.

John kept on wishing he had played the game more. He realized that he should have listened to his mom and done serious things, too. From then on, he played the game but only after he was done with serious tasks. He never regretted again.

It was a warm summer day. Jake and his Mom were playing together in the garden. Jake saw a navy dragonfly zip past him and said to his Mom, "Did you see the fly zip past us? Can I go and catch it?" His Mom said Yes and Jake ran after it.

He chased the fly with his net, trying hard to catch it. The fly was zipping around Jake, but he was determined to catch it. After a few minutes, he managed to catch the dragonfly and lift it up to show his Mom. He was very excited.

His Mom said, "That is a beautiful navy dragonfly, well done, Jake!"

Jake smiled and said, "I'm going to keep it warm in this jar!" He put the fly into the jar carefully and showed it to his Mom. She was very proud of him. 

The End.

Once upon a time there was a humble shrimp who lived in the sea. He was very small and liked to swim around in the water.

One day, the shrimp wanted to explore the beach. He swam up onto the sand and started to explore. Suddenly, a huge wave came and crashed onto the shore. The shrimp was scared and ran away!

He hurried back into the sea but the wave had been too big and he was very wet. The shrimp didn't know what to do! Then he saw a lady with a towel. The lady smiled and said, â€œHere, let me help you.â€ She took the towel and wiped the shrimp dry.

The shrimp thanked the lady for being so kind. He was very happy that she had helped him. From then on, he was always very careful when exploring near the beach, but he never forgot how kind the lady had been.

Once upon a time, there was a big train. The train was very wide and had lots of carriages. The train would go "choo choo" as it went down the tracks. One day, the train was going up a big hill and it started to get very hot. The train started to make steam come out of its chimney. The steam was white and fluffy like a cloud. Suddenly, the train driver had to sneeze! He sneezed so hard that the steam went everywhere! The train driver said "excuse me" and everyone on the train laughed. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a witch. She lived in a small house. The witch had a big hat and a long nose. She was a stubborn witch. She liked to work all day.

One day, the stubborn witch went to the woods. She wanted to work on a spell. She met a big dog. The dog wanted to play with her. The witch said, "No, I have to work." The dog was sad.

The stubborn witch worked all day. She finished her spell. The dog came back. The witch saw the dog was sad. She decided to play with the dog. They played and had fun. The stubborn witch learned it was good to take breaks and play too.

They counted to three and opened their eyes. With a cool brain, they thought of a solution and stopped fighting. Now they were friends again, and could play together in the park.

One day, a restless vase appeared in the room. It was a big, pink vase with lots of flower decorations. All of the other things in the room were bored, but the vase looked excited. It tapped its foot and moved around to get a better look at its surroundings.

Suddenly, a magical light filled the room and out of the vase stepped a tiny fairy. She was wearing a bright yellow dress and sparkly green wings. She smiled at the startled things in the room, waved her wand and magical music appeared. 

The other things began to dance around the fairy and the vase. The music was so cheerful that the room filled with laughter. Even the restless vase seemed to be happy and it swayed from side to side.

Suddenly the music stopped and the fairy waved her wand and disappeared into the vase. The other things smiled as the vase disappeared from the room. They never saw the fairy or the vase again, but they still remembered the joyful moment when the fairy first appeared.

Billy's father warned him about fake fireworks and reminded him to ask for permission before playing with them, but Billy didn't pay attention and just nodded in agreement.

Once at the park, Billy enjoyed the beautiful colors in the sky and soon noticed kids playing with fake fireworks. He asked his parents if he could have some. His parents agreed since they thought the fake fireworks were harmless.

Unfortunately, one of the fake fireworks had a real firework inside. When the firework was lit, it created a big explosion which caused Billy to get injured.

The moral of the story is that even if something is fake, it's important to only handle it with caution and always get permission before using it. Ignoring this rule could lead to a bad ending.

But then, she saw a key. She picked up the key and looked carefully where it came from. She saw a big door with a lock. She wondered what was behind it.

She put the key in the lock and turned it. She opened the door and saw a lot of toys! She was so happy! 

Suddenly, a monster popped out of the toys! It scared the little girl! She started to run away and cried: "That was terrible!" 

But then, the monster said with a kind voice: "Do not be scared!" The monster gave her a big smile and showed her a lot of surprise. The little girl was very happy. She hugged the monster and said "Thank you!" 

The monster waved goodbye and the little girl went home with a big smile.

One day, an old sailor was walking along the beach. He looked around and saw a small child sitting in the sand, making a sandcastle.

The sailor smiled and asked the child, "What is your name?"

The child looked up at the sailor and said, "My name is Lizzy."

The sailor asked, "Lizzy, would you like to go on a boat ride with me?"

Lizzy smiled and thanked the sailor. She hopped up, grabbed the sailor's hand, and ran with him to the harbor.

When they arrived, the sailor pulled out a tiny boat with a sail. The old sailor said, "Climb in, Lizzy, and I'll take you on a great adventure."

Lizzy thanked him again, snuggled into the boat, and they sailed along the coast. As they sailed, they laughed and smiled and watched the waves splash against the hull. 

When the sun started to set, the sailor steered the small boat back to the harbor. Lizzy said goodbye to the sailor, thanking him for the wonderful adventure. 

The old sailor waved goodbye as Lizzy ran off, already daydreaming about the next adventure the two could have together.

Imagine a dolphin swimming through the ocean, looking for new and exciting places to explore. The sun is shining and the water is comfortable. Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside with her friends. They would run and jump and laugh all day long. One day, Lily's friend Sarah was being bossy and telling everyone what to do. Lily didn't like it when Sarah was bossy.

Lily knew what to do. She stopped playing and helped Sarah up. She walked her to her mom's house and told her what happened. Sarah's mom took her to the doctor and she got better soon. Lily felt happy that she could help her friend.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She was three years old, and she loved to go on big adventures. One day, she decided to go search for a witch.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl and a little boy. They were only three years old. They were best friends. One day, the little girl had an idea. She wanted to make a white chain. She and the little boy began to count the white pieces they found. With each piece, the chain began to grow longer.

When the chain was almost done, something bad happened. The little girl and the little boy were playing and accidentally broke the white chain. They were so sad. They cried until the sun went down. 

The little girl and the little boy tried their best to fix the chain, but they couldn't. In the end, they never finished the white chain.

Sara and Tom were twins who liked to play and learn. They also liked to eat dessert after dinner, like cake or ice cream. But sometimes they ate too much dessert and felt sick.

One day, their mom made a big chocolate cake for dessert. Sara and Tom were very happy and wanted to eat a lot of cake. But their mom said, "You can only have one slice each. If you eat too much, you will get a tummy ache."

Sara and Tom nodded and said, "OK, mom." They ate their dinner and waited for dessert. When their mom brought the cake, Sara and Tom gazed at it with big eyes. It looked so yummy and sweet.

Their mom cut two slices of cake and gave one to Sara and one to Tom. She said, "Enjoy your dessert, but don't ask for more. Remember what I said."

Sara and Tom said, "Thank you, mom." They ate their cake slowly and savored every bite. It was the best cake they ever had. They felt happy and full.

But then they saw that there was still a lot of cake left on the plate. Sara and Tom looked at each other and felt tempted. They wanted to have another slice of cake. They thought, "Maybe mom won't notice. Maybe we won't get sick. Maybe we can eat more cake."

They looked at their mom, who was busy washing the dishes. They thought, "Now is our chance. Let's grab another slice of cake."

But then they remembered what their mom said. They remembered how she made the cake for them with love and care. They remembered how she wanted them to be healthy and happy. They remembered how they promised to listen to her.

They looked at each other again and shook their heads. They said, "No, we won't eat more cake. We will obey our mom. We will be good twins."

They put their plates in the sink and hugged their mom. They said, "We love you, mom. We are sorry for thinking of eating more cake. We are happy with what we have."

Their mom smiled and hugged them back. She said, "I love you, too, Sara and Tom. I am proud of you for being honest and respectful. You are good twins."

Sara and Tom felt warm and cozy in their mom's arms. They learned that dessert is good, but too much dessert is bad. They learned that listening to their mom is good, but disobeying their mom is bad. They learned that being good twins is good, but being greedy twins is bad.

They learned a valuable lesson that day. They learned to be thankful and content. They learned to gaze at dessert, but not to grab it.

Tom and Sam were friends who liked to play with cars. One day, they saw a new boy in the park. He had a big red car that looked very new and shiny. Tom and Sam wanted to play with him and his car.

"Hi, I am Tom and this is Sam. What is your name?" Tom asked the new boy.

"I am Ben. This is my car. It is very rich and fast. Do you want to see?" Ben said. He smiled and showed them his car.

Tom and Sam nodded. They followed Ben to a hill. Ben put his car on the hill and pushed it down. The car zoomed down the hill and made a loud noise. Tom and Sam clapped and cheered.

"Wow, that is a cool car. Can we try?" Sam asked.

Ben shook his head. "No, this is my car. You can't touch it. It is too rich for you. You have old and dirty cars. Go away." He said. He was rude and mean.

Tom and Sam felt sad and angry. They did not like Ben. They turned around and walked away. They did not want to play with him anymore.

As they walked away, they heard a loud crash. They looked back and saw Ben's car. It had hit a rock and broken into pieces. There was a big crack in the car. Ben cried and screamed. He had lost his rich car.

Tom and Sam felt sorry for Ben. They knew how it felt to lose something. They decided to be kind and help him. They went back to Ben and introduced themselves again.

"Hi, we are Tom and Sam. We are sorry about your car. Do you want to play with us and our cars? We have many cars and we can share." Tom said.

Ben looked at them. He felt ashamed and sorry. He had been rude and mean to them. He realized that his car was not important. He wanted to have friends.

"Thank you, Tom and Sam. I am sorry for being rude and mean to you. You are very kind and nice. I would like to play with you and your cars. Can we be friends?" Ben said.

Tom and Sam smiled and nodded. They gave Ben some of their cars and they played together. They had fun and laughed. They became friends.

The moral of the story is: It is better to be kind and share than to be rude and greedy. Friends are more important than things.

Sam was a curious boy who liked to examine everything he saw. One day, he found a big onion in the kitchen. He wondered what it was and how it smelled. He picked up the onion and peeled off the brown skin. He saw many white layers inside.

He wanted to know more, so he brought the onion to his nose and sniffed it. It smelled very strong and made his eyes water. He sneezed and rubbed his eyes. He felt a burning pain in his eyes and nose. He dropped the onion and cried.

His mom heard him and ran to the kitchen. She saw him holding his face and the onion on the floor. She knew what happened and felt sorry for him. She hugged him and took him to the sink. She washed his eyes and nose with water. She told him the onion was a food that made people cry. She said he should not examine it with his nose. She gave him a cookie and a kiss.

Sam learned his lesson and never examined an onion again. He still liked to be curious, but he was more careful. He asked his mom before he touched anything new. He did not want to cry or hurt himself again. He was a smart boy.

John was walking with his daddy along a beach. He could hear the waves crashing against the shore. Suddenly, he spotted a dolphin. He was so excited that he started running towards it.

Daddy shouted, "John, wait!" He ran after John, but it was too late; John was already exploring the beach.

The dolphin was swimming close to the shore, so Daddy said to John, "Let's wipe the water off the dolphin."

John happily agreed and took a towel from Daddy. He slowly and gently wiped the dolphin, while Daddy stayed close by.

The dolphin seemed so calm and appreciative, and it made Daddy smile to see how gentle and loving his son was towards it.

John smiled at Daddy and said, "The dolphin is so happy!"

Then they went on to explore the shore. It was a wonderful day!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who wanted to drive a car. She asked her parents if she could, but they said 'no'. The little girl wanted a license, so she kept asking her parents for one. 

Finally, her parents said she could get a license, if she drove with them first. The little girl was happy and put on a seatbelt. 

They got in the car and drove to the license center. While driving, her parents said it was important to obey traffic rules. The little girl listened and nodded her head. 

The family finally arrived and the little girl handed her paperwork to the clerk. The clerk said 'you're too little for a license'. The little girl felt bad. 

Her parents said she could practice driving with them and take the test when she was ready. The little girl smiled and said 'yes, please'. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved playing with his toy cars and trucks. One day, Timmy's mom brought home a big machine. It was very heavy and made lots of noise.

Timmy asked his mom, "What is that big machine for?" His mom replied, "It's to protect our house from bad storms."

Timmy was happy to know that the machine would protect his house. He asked his mom if he could help. His mom said, "Yes, you can help by bringing me some tools."

Timmy felt important as he helped his mom fix the machine. He was proud to know that he was helping protect their house. From that day on, Timmy made sure to always help his mom protect their home.

Once upon a time, Grandma and Grandpa took their grandchild, Jack, to a museum. Jack was only three years old and very excited. He had never been to a museum before.

As they walked around, Grandpa showed him all the exciting things in the museum. Jack learnt a lot of new things. Suddenly he saw a large glass jar filled with candy. He asked his Grandpa if he could have some of the candy.

Jack soon learnt to be polite so that he could get the candy the next time. Grandpa and Grandma were very proud of him.

Once upon a time there was a wood house in the middle of the woods. It was very old and broken. One day a blue bird came and perched on the roof. He started to zip around the roof and make a big noise. All the animals in the forest were frightened by the sound!

Suddenly, a big loud noise, like thunder, filled the sky and the bird flew away. The animals looked up and saw a giant eagle soaring through the sky. Everyone was amazed. The eagle had a big package in his talons. He flew over the broken wood house and dropped his package through the roof! All the animals gasped. 

The package was full of shiny tools and new wood. The eagle had brought the house a present! He hovered in the sky and watched as the animals fixed the broken wood house. They used the tools to patch up the holes in the walls and they used the wood to build a new, safe roof- and that's how the wood house was saved!

Jimbo was wandering through the woods. He saw something bright. It was a ball of yarn. Jimbo reached his hands out and touched it. He liked the way it felt. It was soft and fluffy. He picked it up and held it close to his chest.

Once upon a time there was a thin woman. She loved to go outside and pretend. One day she asked a nearby 3-year-old, "Do you want to come and pretend with me?"

And so they did, often returning to the garden to twirl and spin in circles, pretending to be beautiful princesses.
