"You can play after you eat your dinner. It's almost ready. Come to the kitchen and wash your hands," Mom said.

Lily and Ben did not want to stop playing, but they were also hungry. They followed Mom to the kitchen. Mom had made spaghetti and sauce for dinner. It smelled good.

"Here, hold your plates and sit down," Mom said. She gave them each a plate and a fork.

"Can I have some sauce, please?" Lily asked.

"Me too, me too!" Ben said.

Mom poured some sauce over their spaghetti. She also gave them some bread and butter.

"Be careful, the sauce is hot. Don't burn your tongues," Mom said.

Lily and Ben ate their dinner. They liked the sauce. It was tasty and sweet. They also liked the bread and butter. They ate until they were full.

"Thank you, Mom, for the dinner," Lily and Ben said.

"You're welcome, kids. I'm glad you liked it. Now, do you want some dessert?" Mom asked.

Lily and Ben nodded. They wanted some dessert. Mom gave them each a bowl of ice cream. It was cold and creamy. They ate their ice cream and licked their spoons.

"That was yummy, Mom," Lily and Ben said.

"You're welcome, kids. Now, it's time to brush your teeth and go to bed. You must be sleepy after playing and eating so much," Mom said.

Lily and Ben were sleepy. They yawned and rubbed their eyes. They followed Mom to the bathroom and brushed their teeth. Then they went to their bedroom and put on their pajamas.

Mom tucked them in their beds and kissed them goodnight.

"Goodnight, Mom. We love you," Lily and Ben said.

"Goodnight, kids. I love you too. Sweet dreams," Mom said.

She turned off the light and closed the door. Lily and Ben cuddled with their teddy bears and fell asleep. They dreamed of toy cars and sauce and ice cream.

The little girl was excited. She had her very own recorder and she couldn't wait to record something. She looked around her house and she noticed the celery in the kitchen. She grabbed it and took it over to her recorder. She held the celery close to the recorder and said it smelled sweet. Then she started recording, she said "The celery smells sweet".

The little girl was so proud of her recording and so excited. She played it back and it sounded great. She recorded it again and again, and each time it sounded sweeter and sweeter. The girl had so much fun playing the recording back and listening to how sweet the celery sounded.

The little girl was so happy with her recording and playing it back gave her so much joy. From that day on she always recorded the smells that she liked best. She liked to find new sweet things to record and share with her friends.

One day, Ben was in the kitchen with his mom. He wanted to help with dinner but his mom kept telling him he was too little. Ben was feeling frustrated.

He let out a big sigh and said to his mom, "Please let me help!"

His mom smiled and said, "Okay, Ben. You can set the table."

Ben was so happy! He grabbed the tray and started putting plates on it. He was so excited to be helping that he wouldn't take no for an answer when his mom tried to help. Ben was being very stubborn.

After dinner, Ben's mom gave him a big hug and said, "Thank you for helping, Ben. You did a great job!"

Ben smiled and let out a happy sigh. He was glad he could help and proud of himself for being so stubborn.

Once upon a time, there lived a poor little girl. She had no mum or dad, but she had a wish. She wished she could hold something of her own.

One day, as she was walking down the street, she spotted a shiny stone in the road. She picked it up and held it tightly. This was her mine!

She kept that stone with her always. She kept it in the pocket of her dress, tucked away safe and sound.

The little girl would hold her stone and think of her wish. One day maybe she would not be so poor.

The end.

Once there was a dull avocado lying on the ground. All of a sudden it snapped! A little girl had stepped on it. She was very surprised and confused. She had never seen anything like it before. She picked up the avocado and went to ask her mum what had happened.

Mum said the avocado was old and it had cracked when the little girl stepped on it. She then explained to her daughter that avocados can be eaten. The little girl was so happy, she couldn't wait to try one.

Mum picked up the avocado, gave it a wash and cut it into slices. The little girl tried a piece and she loved it. She ate the whole avocado and it became her favourite food.

From that day onwards, the little girls mum would get avocados from the store and the little girl would be so excited. Every time she would snap a piece off her avocado and eat it.

Once upon a time there was a boy named Tommy. Tommy was three years old and he loved to whistle. One day after his dinner, Tommy grabbed his dirty plate and whistled a happy tune. He went out into the garden and sat under the apple tree.

As Tommy whistled, the birds began to sing along. He watched them fly from branch to branch and it made him whistle even louder. All he wanted was to keep on singing and whistling with the birds, so he just kept going.

When it started to get dark, Tommy's mom called him to come inside. As he walked back in, he blew one last big whistle at the birds. They all flew away, leaving only the sound of Tommy's whistling in the air.

Lily and Max liked to play in their room. They had many toys and books to have fun with. One day, they decided to make a big castle with their blocks and pillows. They used the bookcase as a wall and put a flag on top.

"Look, our castle is so big and strong!" Max said. "We are the king and queen of this land!"

Lily nodded and smiled. She was very creative and liked to imagine things. She took a book and pretended it was a magic wand. She waved it at Max and said, "Abracadabra, you are now a frog!"

Max laughed and made a ribbit sound. He hopped around the castle and tried to catch a fly. Lily giggled and chased him with her wand.

They were having so much fun that they did not hear their mom calling them for lunch. She came to their room and saw the mess they had made. She was not happy.

"Stop, stop, stop!" she said. "What are you doing? You have to clean up this mess and come to eat. You can't leave your toys and books everywhere!"

Lily and Max stopped playing and looked at their mom. They felt sorry for making her angry. They loved their mom and did not want to upset her.

"Sorry, mom," they said together. "We were just playing. We made a castle with the bookcase and the blocks and the pillows."

Mom sighed and smiled. She knew they were just using their imagination and having fun. She was proud of their creative minds. But she also wanted them to be tidy and respectful.

"I know, I know," she said. "You are very creative and smart. But you also have to learn to put things back where they belong. And you have to listen when I call you. OK?"

Lily and Max nodded and hugged their mom. They said they would help her clean up and then go to eat. They also said they loved her very much.

Mom hugged them back and said she loved them too. She was glad they were such good kids. She helped them put the blocks and the pillows and the books back in their places. Then they all went to the kitchen to have a yummy lunch.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny named Hop. Hop was very humble and kind. One day, Hop found a note on the ground. The note said, "You are special". Hop felt happy and grateful. 

Hop wanted to share the note with all of his friends. So, Hop hopped to his friend's house. His friend was surprised and happy to see Hop. Hop gave the note to his friend and said, "You are special too". 

Hop and his friend hopped together to their other friends' houses. They shared the note with all of their friends. Everyone felt happy and loved. From that day on, Hop and his friends knew that they were all special and important.

Anna and Ben are playing in the park. They see a big light in the sky. It is the sun. The sun is bright and warm.

"Look, Anna, the sun is smiling at us!" Ben says.

Anna smiles back. She likes the sun. She claps her hands and says, "Hello, sun! Thank you for making us happy!"

The sun hears Anna and Ben. It is happy too. It sends them a rainbow. The rainbow has many colors. It is pretty and shiny.

"Wow, Anna, look at the rainbow! It is like a big candy!" Ben says.

Anna nods. She likes candy. She claps her hands again and says, "Hello, rainbow! Thank you for making us pretty!"

The rainbow hears Anna and Ben. It is happy too. It sends them a shower of raindrops. The raindrops are cool and wet.

"Hey, Anna, feel the raindrops! They are like a big shower!" Ben says.

Anna giggles. She likes showers. She claps her hands one more time and says, "Hello, raindrops! Thank you for making us clean!"

The sun, the rainbow, and the raindrops are all happy. They love Anna and Ben. They give them a big hug.

Anna and Ben hug them back. They are happy too. They love the sun, the rainbow, and the raindrops. They say, "Thank you, thank you, thank you!"

Then they run to their mom. She has a picnic basket. She has sandwiches, cookies, and juice. They are yummy.

Anna and Ben eat and drink. They share with their mom. They tell her about the sun, the rainbow, and the raindrops. She listens and smiles.

They all have a good day. They all clap their hands. They all say, "Yay!"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. She was three years old.
One day, Lucy saw a gray bird. It was hopping around in the grass. She thought the bird was so pretty.

Lucy said to the bird, "Hi! What's your name? Would you like to join me for a meal?"

The bird hopped closer to Lucy and said, "Chirp! Chirp! My name is Tweet. Yes, I would love to join you for a meal!"

So Lucy and Tweet had a meal together. They ate yummy food and drank sweet juice. They chatted and laughed and they had so much fun.

When it was time to go, Tweet said goodbye. She said, "Chirp! Chirp! It was nice to join you for a meal, Lucy!"

Lucy smiled and waved goodbye to Tweet. She was so happy to have a new friend.

John was an independent three year old. He loved to do things all by himself, like putting his shoes on or picking out his clothes.

One day, John's mom told him he had to do some exercise. He didn't want to though. He wanted to own his own time, so he asked his mom "But why, Mommy?"

Mom said, "Doing exercise is important for your body so you can be healthy and strong. And it's fun too! Let's try it!"

John thought about it for a minute, but then he decided it was a good idea. He said, "OK, I'll try it."

So John and his mom did some exercise together, and it was really fun. They laughed and ran and did lots of jumping. When they were done, John felt really proud of himself. He felt he owned his own time, and that he could do whatever he wanted.

One day, a little cat named Kitty was very hungry. She went outside to look for some food. She saw a big, red ball. Kitty thought, "I can play with the ball and find food later."

Kitty used her paw to push the ball. It rolled and rolled. The ball hit a bush, and out came a little mouse with a long tail. The mouse saw Kitty and said, "Why did you push the ball into my home?"

Kitty said, "I'm sorry, Mouse. I was hungry and wanted to play. Can we be friends?" The mouse nodded, and they played with the ball together. After playing, they found some food and shared it. Kitty and Mouse were happy and full.

Once there was a little girl named Emma. She was three years old and loved to explore. She wanted to find something fun and exciting to do.

One day, she got an idea. She grabbed a map and started to look at it. She saw a big, blue ocean which looked like it was just waiting to be explored. She decided to dive into the ocean and find out what was there.

Emma started packing her things. She grabbed her swimsuit and a few other things. With a few final checks she was ready. She took a deep breath and jumped into the sea.

Emma was so excited to explore the ocean. She started swimming around looking for something, but it was too deep for her. She quickly became worried and started to swim back to the shore.

Finally, she made it back to the beach. She was so relieved to be back safe and sound. Emma knew she had to be more careful next time she decided to explore. She took her map and put it away carefully, knowing she would use it many times in the future.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. He loved to taste new foods. One day, Tim went to a big fair with his mom. There were many fun things to see and do at the fair. Tim saw a big, light balloon in the sky. He wanted to get one for himself.

Tim and his mom walked around the fair. They saw a food stand with many treats. "Mom, can I taste that?" Tim asked, pointing at a tasty-looking snack. "Of course," said his mom, and she bought the snack for him. Tim took a bite and smiled. It was the best thing he had ever tasted.

As they walked to the exit, Tim saw a man selling light balloons. "Mom, can I have a light balloon too?" he asked. "Yes, you can," his mom replied. Tim picked a bright red balloon and held it tightly. They left the fair, and Tim couldn't wait to come back next year.

Ben likes to write. He has a big book and a blue pen. He writes his name, his mom's name, and his dog's name. He writes some letters and some numbers. He writes some shapes and some colors. He is very proud of his book.

One day, he shows his book to his friend Sam. Sam likes to write too. He has a small book and a red pen. He writes his name, his dad's name, and his cat's name. He writes some words and some pictures. He is very proud of his book.

"Look at my book!" Ben says to Sam. "I write a lot of things!"

"Look at my book!" Sam says to Ben. "I write a lot of things too!"

They look at each other's books. They like what they see. They smile and hug.

"Can you whistle?" Ben asks Sam.

"No, I can't," Sam says. "It is too hard. Can you whistle?"

"Yes, I can," Ben says. "I will show you."

He puts his lips together and blows. He makes a loud sound. It sounds like a bird.

"Wow, you can whistle!" Sam says. "That is cool!"

"Thank you," Ben says. "Do you want to learn?"

"Yes, please," Sam says.

Ben teaches Sam how to whistle. He tells him to make his lips small and round. He tells him to blow softly and slowly. He tells him to try different sounds.

Sam tries to whistle. He blows and blows. He makes some noises. Some are high, some are low. Some are long, some are short. He is having fun.

"I did it!" Sam says. "I can whistle!"

"Good job!" Ben says. "You are a good whistler!"

They whistle together. They make a song. They are happy. They are friends.

In the park, there was a young boy named Tommy. Tommy was restless and he kept running around the big trees. His father said, "Tommy, we are going to the hospital." Tommy was scared and he asked, "Why are we going to the hospital?". His father replied, "We are going to visit your grandpa. He has been feeling very unwell." 

When they arrived at the hospital, Tommy was still restless. He kept running around the chairs and scanning the room. His father said, "Let's go and see grandpa now." Tommy was still scared but he wanted to see grandpa. 

When they got to the room, Tommy said, "Hi grandpa!" Grandpa replied, "Hello Tommy, it's great to see you!" Tommy asked, "Are you feeling better?". Grandpa said, "I'm getting better every day. But I'm still a bit tired. Would you like to sit and rest with me?" 

Tommy was happy. He sat down on the bed and asked his grandpa about what he did in the hospital. Grandpa told Tommy about how he was getting better, and how he took lots of walks around the hospital. Tommy then asked, "Can I come too?". Grandpa smiled and said, "That sounds like a wonderful idea." 

Tommy and his grandpa took a walk around the hospital together. Tommy was finally feeling restful,

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved spaghetti with sauce. One day, Timmy was eating his spaghetti and accidentally tore his shirt. He was sad because he loved that shirt. 

But then, Timmy's mom came to the rescue with a new shirt. Timmy was lucky to have such a kind mom. He put on his new shirt and continued eating his spaghetti with sauce. 

After dinner, Timmy helped his mom clean up the kitchen. He accidentally knocked over the sauce and it spilled on the floor. But Timmy wasn't worried because he knew his mom would help clean it up. They worked together and soon the kitchen was clean again. Timmy went to bed feeling happy and lucky to have such a great mom.

Once upon a time, there was a big family who lived in a house. They loved to eat dinner together every night. One day, the mom made a special dinner with an expensive fork. 

The little girl asked, "Mommy, why is that fork so fancy?" 

The mom replied, "It's a special fork for special dinners. It's very expensive."

After dinner, the little girl wanted to help clean up. She asked her brother, "Can you pass me the fork?"

Her brother passed the fork to her and said, "Be careful, it's very expensive."

The little girl smiled and said, "I will be careful."

Once upon a time, there were two friends, Jack and Jane. They were playing together in the park with their wagon. Jack wanted to pull the wagon and was so excited to play. Jane was happy too, but she said "Wait a minute! Let's delay, we should get a sparkly toy first!"

So, they went to the popular store. When they arrived, the store was full of different kinds of toys. It was so hard for them to choose just one - all the toys looked exciting! But finally, Jack chose a fire truck with red and blue colors. Jane was so excited and said "Can I play with it too?" Jack said "Yes!"

After they bought the toy, they went back to the park with the wagon. They had so much fun playing together. They even got to give their wagon a ride too.

The end!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to wander around her garden and look at all the pretty flowers. One day, she found a big squash hiding behind a bush. 

Lily picked up the squash and showed it to her mom. "Look, Mommy! I found a big squash!" she said with a smile. 

Her mom was proud of Lily's successful discovery. "Wow, Lily! That's a really big squash. Maybe we can make some delicious soup with it," her mom said. 

Lily was happy to have found something new and exciting in her garden. She continued to wander around, looking for more treasures to discover.

Lily liked to collect things. She had a box full of shiny stones, feathers, buttons and shells. She liked to look at them and sort them by color and shape. She was very tidy and kept her box under her bed.

One day, she heard a noise under her bed. She lifted the blanket and saw a rat. The rat was holding one of her shiny stones in its mouth. Lily was scared and angry. She shouted at the rat.

"Hey, rat! That is my stone! Give it back to me!"

The rat looked at Lily and squeaked. It did not want to give up the stone. It liked shiny things too. It had a nest under the bed, full of things it had collected from the house. It had bits of paper, string, cheese and coins.

"Please, rat, let me have my stone. It is very special to me. I found it in the park with my dad. You can have something else from my box. How about this feather? It is soft and pretty."

Lily held out the feather to the rat. The rat sniffed the feather and dropped the stone. It took the feather and ran back to its nest. Lily picked up the stone and put it back in her box. She was happy to have her stone back, but she felt sorry for the rat. It was lonely and wanted to collect things too.

She decided to share some of her things with the rat. She took out some buttons and shells and put them near the rat's nest. She hoped the rat would like them and be her friend. She smiled and said to the rat.

"Here, rat, these are for you. You can collect them and make your nest more shiny. Maybe we can play together sometime. I like to collect things too."

Sara liked to look at the owl in the big tree. The owl had big eyes and soft feathers. Sara thought the owl was attractive. She wanted to be friends with the owl.

One day, Sara brought some nuts and seeds to the tree. She hoped the owl would like them. She called to the owl, "Hello, owl! Do you want to play with me? I have some food for you!"

The owl looked at Sara and blinked. He did not want to play with Sara. He wanted to sleep. He was tired from hunting at night. He said to Sara, "Hoo, hoo, go away! I do not want to play. I do not want your food. Leave me alone!"

Sara felt sad and angry. She did not like the owl's words. She said to the owl, "You are mean and rude! You do not know how to be nice. I quit! I do not want to be your friend anymore!"

She threw the nuts and seeds on the ground and ran away. She did not look at the owl again. The owl did not care. He closed his eyes and went back to sleep. He did not need Sara's friendship. He was happy by himself.

Once upon a time, there was an old lady who loved to drink coffee every morning. She had a special mug that she always used for her coffee. One day, she accidentally dropped her mug and it broke into many pieces. She was very sad and didn't know what to do.

But then, a kind neighbor came over and let her borrow a new mug to use for her coffee. The old lady was so happy and grateful. She thanked the neighbor and promised to take good care of the new mug.

The next day, the old lady woke up early and went to make her coffee. She carefully poured the hot coffee into the new mug and took a sip. It tasted delicious! She realized that the new mug was even better than her old one. From then on, she used the new mug every day and was always thankful for her kind neighbor who let her borrow it.

One day, Jenny wanted to go on an adventure. She put on her bright dress, grabbed her teddy bear, and set off. First, Jenny wanted to visit the park. As soon as she arrived, she laughed and smiled. She ran, jumped, and spun around in the grass. 

On the way home, Jenny saw a small shop. She stopped and looked inside. Jenny saw something shiny! She peeped in and saw a little puppy. It was so cute, it had one bright, sleepy eye which was slowly closing. It was starting to wink at her! 

Jenny wanted the puppy, so she asked if she could have it. Mommy said it was too late to take it home today, so she promised to come back the next day to pick it up. Jenny waved goodbye and left, so excited for tomorrow.

Once upon a time, there were two little girls. One of them had a special toy car. The other girl wanted to play with it and asked to borrow it. The girl with the car said yes, but asked that the other girl take care of it. 

The other girl took the car and went to the market. She went too fast and bumped into some boxes, which made the toy car break. The girl felt bad and knew she had done something wrong.

The girl with the car was angry and the other girl told her that she was sorry. She said she would buy her a new one and she said she would learn her lesson and not start something she couldn't finish.

The girl with the car was happy with the offer and the two girls hugged each other. From then on, the girls always thought about how their actions could affect other people. They learned that starting something bad could end in a bad way.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside with his friends. One day, Timmy's mom noticed he was feeling sick. She took his temperature with a thermometer and saw that he had a fever. 

Timmy's mom told him he needed to rest and stay inside until he felt better. Timmy was sad because he couldn't play with his friends, but he knew he needed to get better. 

The next day, Timmy woke up feeling better. His fever had gone down and he felt tough enough to play outside again. He ran outside to meet his friends and saw the sun rise in the sky. Timmy was happy to be outside again and playing with his friends.

Once upon a time there was a mouse. The mouse liked to scamper and play in the grass. But one day, the mouse was being very lazy. Instead of scampering and playing in the grass, the mouse just laid there in the sun.

Suddenly, a mean cat came out of nowhere. The cat had seen the mouse sleeping and wanted to trap it. The cat laid a big trap for the mouse. The mouse was scared and tried to run away. But the trap was too close and the mouse could not escape.

The mouse had to think of a way to escape the trap. Suddenly, it had an idea. The mouse thought to act lazy like it was before. When the cat came closer, the mouse laid down and pretended to be asleep. The cat was sure that the mouse was lazy and left without trapping it.

From then on, the mouse knew to behave better. Never again did it lay in the sun so lazily.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved music and always wanted to play the flute. One day, her mommy bought her a flute and she was so happy. 

Lily tried to play it, but it didn't sound good. She asked her mommy why it didn't sound like the music she heard. Her mommy said, "You have to examine the flute and see if everything is okay."

Lily looked at the flute and found out that one of the holes was covered. She fixed it and tried to play again. This time, it sounded beautiful! She was so successful in playing the flute. 

The moral of the story is that if you want to do something, you have to examine everything to make sure it's right. If you do that, you can be successful in anything you want to do.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved dinosaurs. He had a toy dinosaur that he carried with him everywhere he went. One day, Timmy went to the park to play. While he was there, he saw a foolish dinosaur walking around. It was really big and scary-looking. Timmy decided to follow the dinosaur to see where it was going. 

Timmy followed the dinosaur through the park and into the woods. The dinosaur was very fast and Timmy had to run to keep up. Eventually, they came to a big cave. The foolish dinosaur went inside and Timmy followed. 

Inside the cave, Timmy saw that the foolish dinosaur was actually very friendly. It just wanted to play with Timmy and show him around. They had a lot of fun together, playing games and exploring the cave. When it was time to go home, Timmy said goodbye to the dinosaur and promised to come back and visit again soon.

Once there was a little boy, who felt very miserable. He had been feeling sad all day and his friends wanted to cheer him up. So they asked him to go play outside with them. He didn't feel like it, so he stayed inside. But suddenly he heard his friends calling for him. They were outside making jokes and having fun. The little boy smiled and decided to join them outside. He could hear them laughing and having a good time. 

When he got outside he saw them all dancing together. He watched and smiled as they moved around in circles. His friends noticed him and started to dance around him too, laughing and joking. The little boy couldn't help but start to laugh too. His friends were joking around and making him smile. 

Soon the little boy was really laughing. He felt much better and was no longer miserable. He enjoyed dancing and joking with his friends and was soon feeling much happier. He hadn't realized how much funnier things could be when you're with your friends!

One day, a little girl had a great idea. She wanted to dive into an ashtray. She had seen some grown ups do it, so she thought she'd try it too!

The little girl found an ashtray and stood on it. She was ready to dive! But first, she took a deep breath and closed her eyes. She felt ready. She wanted to do something different.

The little girl jumped in the air and made a big dive. She went straight into the ashtray! It wasn't normal, but she was so proud of herself.

When she came back up, the little girl was really happy. She couldn't believe she had done it. It felt like she had done something special. She put the ashtray back down and went off to play.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny named Snowy. Snowy was very white and fluffy. One day, Snowy went to the forest to play with his friends. They played hide-and-seek, but Snowy couldn't find his friends. It was getting dark and Snowy was scared. Suddenly, he felt a pinch on his tail. It was his friend, the squirrel! They went home together and Snowy felt happy again. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a special brush that she loved to use to brush her hair every day. One day, she accidentally dropped the brush on the floor and it broke into tiny pieces. Lily was sad because she understood that the brush was fragile and couldn't be fixed.

Her mommy saw how sad Lily was and decided to take her to the store to get a new brush. Lily was so happy when she saw all the pretty brushes at the store. She picked out a new one that was pink and sparkly. She made sure to be extra careful with her new brush because she understood that it was fragile too.

From that day on, Lily brushed her hair every day with her new brush and she was very happy. She understood that even though things can break, there is always a way to fix them or find something new to replace them.

Once upon a time, there was a tiny bear called Timmy. He was so small and he loved to play all day long. One day he decided to go on an adventure. He decided to take some soap with him so he could clean his hands when he got dirty.

Timmy was so brave and he thought he could do anything he wanted. So he climbed to the highest tree in the woods he could find. He was so proud of himself when he reached the top!

When he got to the top, he shouted as loud as he could "Nobody can beat me!" Suddenly he heard clapping and saw a group of animals smiling at him. They had been watching him and were applauding his bravery. Timmy was so happy and he thanked them for their kindness.

However, his happy feeling didn't last for long. He was very sleepy and his eyes started to close. He almost fell from the tree because he was so tired. Luckily, the animals shouted to him and woke him up. He thanked them again.

After that, Timmy promised himself he would never climb the tree again when he was so sleepy. He learnt that it was important to be careful in life and to never put yourself in danger.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy called Billy. He was only three years old and loved to play in the garden. Every day, his mom told him to wash his hands after playing outside.

One day, Billy found something very exciting in the garden. It looked like a little comet, like the ones he'd seen in books about space. It was a bit spoiled from being in the garden, but Billy thought it was the most wonderful thing he'd ever seen.

Billy didn't want to wash his hands, he wanted to keep playing with the comet. His mom said, "Billy, you need to wash your hands. That comet is very dirty."

But Billy wasn't listening and he kept playing with it. His mom got angry and shouted, "Billy, come here right now and wash your hands!"

Billy was scared but he knew that he had to do what his mom said. So he reluctantly washed his hands, dried them off and put the spoiled comet back in the garden. He looked at it sadly as he left, wishing that he could keep playing with it.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was very clumsy and often tripped and fell. One day, she wanted to borrow her friend's toy car. She asked her friend nicely, and her friend said yes.

Lily was so happy to have the toy car, she put it in her mouth to show her friend. But then, she accidentally swallowed the car! She tried to cough it up, but it was stuck in her throat.

Her parents took her to the hospital, but it was too late. The toy car had gotten stuck in her throat and she couldn't breathe. Lily passed away, and her friend was very sad.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a harmless cow named Beef. He lived in a sunny meadow and he loved eating grass and flowers.
One day, Beef saw something that excited him. It was a bunch of horses running in the meadow. They ran so fast, they seemed like they were flying!
Beef couldn't help himself and he began to run with them. He felt so alive and he wished the moment would never end. 
But then, the horses stopped and looked at Beef.
"What are you doing here? You don't belong here," one horse said.
Beef was scared. He thought the horses would be mad at him.

The mommy was right. The little girl remembered the earlier foreshadowing, and it saved her life.

Once upon a time, there was an ordinary little girl called Anna. Anna had an aunt who was very kind and generous.

One day, Auntie said to Anna, "Would you like to borrow my bike? I can lend it to you."

Anna's eyes lit up and she smiled. "Can I really, Auntie?"

"Of course, my darling. You can ride it in the garden if you like," said her aunt. 

So Anna hopped on the bike, and she pedalled around in the sunshine. When she had finished, Anna thanked Auntie for lending her the bike.

Auntie smiled, "You're welcome, my Anna."

Once upon a time, there was a young boy named Tim who loved to play outside. One day, he found a bottle with a strange liquid inside. He thought it was juice, but it was poison! Tim was smart and knew not to drink things he didn't know, so he went to his mom for help.

Tim's mom knew that the poison was dangerous, so she told Tim to reverse, or go back, and put the bottle where he found it. Tim listened to his mom and took the bottle back to where he found it, so no one would get hurt.

The moral of the story is that if you find something you don't know or understand, it's important to ask a grown-up for help. They can keep you safe and teach you what to do.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and run around outside. One day, she went to the park with her mom.

At the park, Lily saw a boy playing with a ball. She wanted to play too, so she asked him, "Can I play with you?"

The boy said, "Sure! I notice you have a pretty dress on."

Lily smiled and said, "Thank you! What's your name?"

"My name is Jack," the boy replied. "What's your favorite word?"

Lily thought for a moment and said, "My favorite word is fair. I like it when things are fair for everyone."

Jack nodded and said, "That's a good word. Let's play fair and take turns with the ball." 

Lily and Jack played together for a while, and they had lots of fun. When it was time to go home, Lily said goodbye to Jack and thanked him for playing with her. She went home happy, thinking about her new friend and the word fair.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a pretty pink purse that she loved to carry around everywhere she went. One day, while she was walking in the park, a scary man approached her and asked if he could see her purse. 

Lily was scared, but she didn't want to be rude, so she handed him her purse. The man opened it up and looked inside. "Ha ha ha," he laughed. "This is just a joke! There's nothing in here but some old toys and a snack."

Lily was relieved that the man wasn't going to take her purse, but she was still upset that he scared her. She went home and told her mommy what happened. Her mommy hugged her and said, "Don't worry, Lily. You did the right thing by giving him your purse, but you should never talk to strangers."

From that day on, Lily always made sure to stay close to her mommy and never talked to strangers. And whenever she felt scared, she would remember that her mommy was always there to protect her.

Once upon a time, there was a big orange sun in the sky. It made everything feel good and bright. 

Josey loved watching the sun. But one day, something was strange. The sun was hanging low in the sky, but it was not going down.

Josey asked his mom what was happening. "It's a special day," she said. "There's a promise in the sky that we can always count on." 

Josey was excited. "What promise?" he asked.

His mom smiled. "The promise of a new day," she said. "Every morning, the sun holds its promise until night."

Josey smiled. He knew that no matter what, the promise of the orange sun will always be there.

Once upon a time there was a poor witch. One day she was walking through the woods when she heard a loud sound. She looked up and saw an arrow shooting through the sky. She caught the arrow and saw that it was from a little boy with a bow and arrow.

The witch said: "Hello, little boy! Why are you shooting arrows?"

The boy said: "I'm trying to hit apples off the tree so I can eat them."

The witch said: "That's a very brave thing to do. Do you need any help?"

The boy said: "Yes, please! I could use some help."

So the witch used her magic to make a ladder appear so the little boy could climb up to get his apples. The little boy was so happy, he gave the witch a big hug and thanked her for being so helpful. 

The witch smiled and said: "You're welcome, little one. Always remember to help those who are poor like me." 

The boy thanked the witch again and the witch flew away on her broomstick. The little boy was very happy and he thanked the witch for all her help.

Once upon a time there was a mighty pumpkin. It was so big that even a grown-up wouldn't be able to pick it up. Every day a small boy named George would come and look at the huge pumpkin. One morning George had a clever idea. He ran off and got some of his toys. He asked his dad for some help and together they lifted the big and mighty pumpkin onto the wagon.

George was so happy, he took the wagon and drove it off. He found some friends on the way and stopped to show them the pumpkin. They all laughed and waved as he drove on. 

When he got home, George wanted to get the big and mighty pumpkin off the wagon. He needed help so he asked his mum and dad to lift it off the wagon into the garden. Together they lifted the pumpkin and George planted it in the ground. 

Now, every day George would come and check on his mighty pumpkin and one day it would be perfect to pick.

Once upon a time, there were two young friends discussing an exciting adventure. One of them was excited about the idea of a fancy picnic.

"Let's have a picnic!" she said.

Her friend smiled and nodded in agreement. They then discussed what they would bring to the picnic, like sandwiches and cake.

The two friends began planning the picnic and soon they had everything they needed and were ready to go. They grabbed their blankets and drinks, and ran out of the house.

The sun was shining brightly when they arrived at the perfect spot for their picnic. The grass was soft and inviting and everything looked just perfect.

They spread out their blankets and unpacked their delicious snacks. The two friends laughed and talked as they enjoyed their fancy picnic and enjoyed the summer day.

Once upon a time, there was a big jungle. Many animals lived there. One day, a little birdie saw a lion. The lion was hurt and could not move. The birdie felt sad and wanted to help the lion. So, the birdie went to other animals and asked for their help. A monkey, an elephant, and a giraffe came to help. Together, they moved the lion to a safe place. The lion was happy and thanked the animals. From that day on, the lion and the birdie became friends.

Once upon a time there was a young girl who loved to listen.
Every day she would sit by the window and listen - to the birds, the wind, the rain. But one day, she heard something different.

It was a loud noise and it grew louder and louder. The girl looked up and saw a missile in the sky. She had never seen anything like it before!

Suddenly, the missile split into many pieces and started to fall. The girl watched as the missiles fell closer and closer. She wanted to run and hide, but she was too scared.

Then she heard something else - a voice coming from the sky. It was calm and strong. It said, "Don't worry, everything will be alright".

The young girl felt a lot better after she heard the voice. She watched as the missiles slowly landed on the ground and she knew that the voice had been right. Everything was alright.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Molly. One day, she took some paint and some paper to draw a jet. Her mother said, â€œMolly, why donâ€™t you paint something strong instead?â€ Molly thought for a moment and then asked, â€œWhat is strong, mommy?â€

Her mother smiled and said, â€œA heart is strong. You can paint it with all the love in your heart for those you love.â€

Molly thought about that for a minute and then started to paint a big and colourful heart. She wasnâ€™t finished yet so she started again the next day. She worked on it for days and finally, it was complete. It was a very strong heart.

Mollyâ€™s mother was so proud of her. She said, â€œMolly, that heart is so strong and so full of love. Keeping love in our hearts will always make us strong.â€

Molly smiled at her mother and said, â€œI know. Love is the strongest of all feelings.â€ 

Moral of the story: Love is the strongest force of all and can make us strong.

Once there was a girl who was very clumsy. One day she slipped and fell right in front of a cabin. The cabin was a little bit scary, but the girl was curious. She took a deep breath and decided to go inside.

When she opened the door, it creaked. She paused, feeling a bit scared but she kept going. As she walked through the cabin, she kept being clumsy. She bumped into things and knocked some things over.

Suddenly, the girl heard a voice coming from the corner of the cabin. It seemed to say "I'm hiding here, can you help me find a way out?". The girl got really excited. She replied "Yes! I'll help you".

The girl had to think carefully about the best way for the creature to escape. It was a challenge because the cabin was full of furniture and boxes. After a few minutes of thinking, the girl found a plan.

She said "Let's try to climb on the pile of boxes. That should be easy for you to get over the top and then you can slide out the window!". Sure enough, the creature was able to get out of the cabin with the girl's help.

The girl was so happy that she helped the creature. She waved goodbye as it ran off and the girl smiled to herself.

Once upon a time, a mommy bird had a little infant bird. The mommy bird built a nest high in a tree to keep her infant bird warm. One day, the mommy bird went out to find some food for her baby. 

While the mommy bird was away, a big storm came. The little infant bird started to worry because he was all alone in the nest. Suddenly, a big gust of wind blew the nest out of the tree and onto the ground.

The mommy bird came back and saw the nest on the ground. She was worried about her baby, but when she looked inside the nest, she saw that her little infant bird was safe and sound. The mommy bird was so happy that her baby was okay, and she cuddled him to keep him warm.

Dave liked to poke. He pocked things like cushions and balls. One day he poked the curtain in his living room. He liked how it felt, so he started poking it more and more.

Then something unusual happened. A tiny creature peeked out from behind the curtain. It was a curious looking animal, with bright green eyes. Dave was so surprised that he nearly fell over!

The creature spoke to Dave, and asked what he was doing. Dave explained that he was just poking the curtain. The creature was amused by his story, and the two of them became fast friends.

They talked and laughed together all day long, and the animal even showed Dave a secret hiding place behind the curtain. Dave and the creature poked the curtain together many more times, and Dave never forgot the unusual creature who lived behind it.

Lily loved to skip with her doll. She named her doll Anna and gave her a pink dress and a yellow hat. Lily and Anna skipped in the park, in the garden, and in the house. They were very happy.

One day, Lily's mom said, "Lily, we are going to visit Grandma. Do you want to come?" Lily nodded and smiled. She liked Grandma. Grandma always gave her hugs and kisses and yummy cookies. Lily ran to get Anna. She wanted to show her to Grandma.

Lily and her mom got in the car and drove to Grandma's house. Lily held Anna on her lap and sang to her. When they arrived, Grandma was waiting at the door. She hugged Lily and her mom and said, "Hello, my dears. Come in, come in. I have something for you."

Lily and her mom followed Grandma into the kitchen. There was a big plate of cookies on the table. They smelled so good. Lily's mouth watered. Grandma said, "These are for you, Lily. I made them with chocolate and nuts. Your favorite. Do you want one?"

Lily said, "Yes, please, Grandma. Thank you. They look yummy." She took a cookie and bit into it. It was soft and sweet and crunchy. She said, "Mmm, this is the best cookie ever. Can I have another one?" Grandma smiled and said, "Of course, you can. But first, let me see your doll. She is very pretty. What is her name?"

Lily said, "Her name is Anna. She is my best friend. We like to skip together. Do you want to skip with us, Grandma?" Grandma laughed and said, "Why not? I haven't skipped in a long time. Let's go to the backyard and have some fun." She took Lily's hand and Anna's hand and they went outside. They skipped and laughed and played until it was time to go home. Lily hugged Grandma and said, "I love you, Grandma. You are the best. Can we come again soon?" Grandma said, "I love you too, Lily. You are the best. And yes, you can come again soon. Anytime you want." Lily smiled and said, "Yay!" She got in the car with her mom and Anna and waved goodbye to Grandma. She was very happy.

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play outside. They had a toy helicopter that they took turns to fly. One day, they saw a big helicopter in the sky. It was loud and shiny and made them curious.

"Let's walk to the park and see the helicopter," Lily said.

"OK, but we have to be careful and not go too far," Ben said. He was thoughtful and did not want to get lost.

They walked to the park, holding hands and looking up. The helicopter was landing on a field. They saw some people in uniforms get out. They wanted to get closer and see what they were doing.

"Come on, let's go," Lily said. She was brave and did not like to wait.

"No, Lily, we have to stay here. Mommy said not to talk to strangers," Ben said. He was scared and did not like to break the rules.

But Lily did not listen. She let go of Ben's hand and ran to the field. Ben tried to stop her, but he was too slow. He shouted her name, but she did not hear him.

The people in uniforms saw Lily running to them. They were not friendly. They were bad. They had guns and masks and bags. They were robbing the helicopter. They grabbed Lily and put her in a bag. They threw the bag in the helicopter and flew away.

Ben was shocked and sad. He cried and cried. He wished he had stopped Lily. He wished he had been more brave. He wished he had been more thoughtful. He wished he had his sister back. But it was too late. The helicopter was gone. And so was Lily.

Once upon a time, there was a rich man named Tom. Tom had a big house and many toys. One day, Tom saw a little bird in a small jail. The bird was sad and wanted to fly.

Tom said, "Little bird, I will help you." Tom went to the jail and used his hands to lift the door. The bird was free and happy. The bird said, "Thank you, Tom!"

From that day, Tom and the little bird were best friends. They played together every day. Tom learned that helping others made him happier than his big house and many toys.

Once upon a time, there lived a little boy called Jimmy. Jimmy was so excited for the day; he was about to visit the zoo for the very first time. He wanted to meet all the animals.

Jimmyâ€™s mom said, â€œBe careful, Jimmy! Donâ€™t wander too far away, okay?â€ Jimmy nodded and said, â€œYes, mommy!â€

As Jimmy started exploring, he suddenly heard a loud roar. Jimmy was scared; he thought it might be a scary animal. He decided to go a bit closer to have a look.

He saw a big and scary tiger in a big cage with thin strips. Carefully, he reached out his hand and realised the strips were made of metal. He wondered why the tiger was in the cage.

His mom had taught him that animals needed to be free; they should roam around in the wild. Then, Jimmy realised if he set the tiger free the tiger would hurt him so he decided not to.

He said to himself, â€œI hope all the animals find a nice and safe home.â€

Moral of the story: Everyone has the right to hope for a better world. We should all try our best to make it a reality.

Tom was a gifted boy who liked to drive his toy car. He drove it very fast and made loud noises. He did not care if he bumped into other toys or people. He thought he was the best driver in the world.

One day, he drove his toy car outside and saw a big house with a red roof. He wanted to drive on the roof and see how high he could go. He found a ladder and climbed up with his toy car. He drove on the roof and felt very happy.

But then, he drove too fast and lost control. His toy car flew off the roof and landed on the ground. It broke into pieces. Tom was scared and sad. He wanted his toy car back. He cried and cried.

A kind lady who lived in the house heard him and came out. She saw what happened and felt sorry for him. She gave him a hug and a cookie. She also gave him a new toy car that was shiny and blue. She said, "This is a gift for you, but you have to be careful and respectful when you drive. Driving is fun, but it can also be dangerous. You have to think of others and not just yourself. Do you understand?"

Tom nodded and said, "Yes, I understand. Thank you for the gift. I'm sorry for driving on your roof. I won't do it again. I will be a good driver from now on." He smiled and hugged the lady. He learned his lesson and was grateful for the gift.

Lily was a little girl who liked to play with dolls. She had many dolls, but her favorite was Queen Rose. Queen Rose had a pink dress, a shiny crown and long hair. Lily loved to comb her hair and make her talk.

One day, Lily went to the park with her mom and Queen Rose. She saw some other kids playing with balls and bikes. They looked like they were having fun. Lily wanted to join them and make new friends.

She asked her mom, "Can I play with them, please?"

Her mom said, "Sure, honey, but be careful and don't lose Queen Rose. She is very special to you."

Lily nodded and ran to the other kids. She said, "Hi, I'm Lily. Can I play with you?"

The other kids looked at her and laughed. They said, "No, you can't. You are too little and you have a silly doll. We don't like dolls. We like balls and bikes. Go away!"

Lily felt sad and hurt. She said, "But I want to play with you. Please, let me join. Queen Rose is not silly. She is a queen. She is very popular and nice."

The other kids laughed louder. They said, "A queen? Ha ha ha! That's a stupid name for a doll. She is not popular. She is ugly and boring. Watch this!"

One of the kids grabbed Queen Rose from Lily's hands and threw her in the air. Queen Rose flew high and then fell on the ground. Her dress ripped, her crown broke and her hair tangled. Lily screamed and ran to get her. She picked her up and hugged her. She cried, "Queen Rose, I'm sorry. I'm so sorry. You are my best friend. I love you."

The other kids kept laughing and pointing at her. They said, "Look at her. She is crying over a doll. What a baby. Go home, baby. You don't belong here."

Lily felt very bad. She wished she never tried to join them. She wished she stayed with her mom and played with Queen Rose. She ran back to her mom and showed her what happened. Her mom was angry and sad. She said, "Oh, Lily, I'm sorry. Those kids were very mean and rude. They should not have done that. Queen Rose is a beautiful doll and you are a wonderful girl. Come on, let's go home and fix her. We don't need them. We have each other."

Lily nodded and snuggled with her mom and Queen Rose. She said, "Thank you, mom. I love you. And I love Queen Rose. She is still my favorite."

The end.

Once upon a time, there were two best friends called Tom and Daisy. Tom and Daisy were always excited to play together and today they had a big race. Tom was a rabbit and Daisy was a frog.

The friends darted across the big meadow as fast as they could, hopping, jumping and zooming. Tom really wanted to win, while Daisy was just having fun.

At the finish line, they were both puffing and out of breath. It was a tie! The friends hugged and jumped for joy.

Suddenly, Daisy noticed something strange in the bushes. She ran over and it was a big, beautiful pizza!

Tom and Daisy couldn't believe their luck. They tore off pieces and shared it with each other. It tasted so delicious!

The happy friends laughed and hugged each other. They had won the race and enjoyed the beautiful pizza. They would always remember this special day.

There was a boy named Tim. He had a modern toy car. One day, Tim went to the store with his mom. He saw a candy he wanted. But Tim did not have a penny to buy it.

Tim started to complain. He wanted the candy so much. His mom said, "No candy today, Tim." Tim was sad. He went back home with his mom.

At home, Tim played with his modern toy car. He smiled and forgot about the candy. Tim's mom was happy. She knew Tim didn't need the candy to be happy.

One day, a little girl named Abigail was out on a stroll. She looked up at the sky and saw a big, white cloud. Suddenly, she saw something else - a beautiful flower blooming! It was the most beautiful flower Abigail had ever seen - red and yellow petals amongst bright green leaves. Abigail couldn't help but smile at the sight of it.

She wanted to take it home so she could always remember how beautiful it was. Carefully, she reached for the flower, but just as she was about to grab it, she heard a voice.

"That's my flower!" the voice said.

Abigail looked around. It was coming from the little mailbox next to her.

"Don't you want to see it bloom?" Abigail asked.

"Yes please!" the mailbox replied.

So Abigail watered the flower every day, and watched it bloom bigger and bigger. Every time it bloomed, Abigail smiled, and so did the mailbox.

Once there was a little girl. She was very impatient to cook. Her mummy had a folder full of recipes. The little girl wanted to try them all. 

So she took the folder to the kitchen. She got out the pots and pans. She stirred and mixed and tasted. 

The little girl was so excited. She was cooking her very own meal. Her mummy came to check and saw that the little girl had done a very good job. 

The little girl was so proud. She gave the folder back to her mummy, hugged her tight and cried, 'I did it!'

Once upon a time, there was a special girl named June. June was very gifted, and she liked to dance everywhere she went. One day, June was walking in the park and heard the sound of a pipe. She stopped dancing and listened closely. The music of the pipe made her start dancing again.

June began to spin and jump, twirl and leap. With each movement, she felt more and more happy. The music made her feel like she was flying. June let the pipe's music take her away and she danced until the sun began to set. 

When the light in the sky changed colors, June stopped and took a deep breath. She had enjoyed her time dancing and thanked the pipe for the lovely music. Then she waved goodbye and skipped away with a smile on her face.

Once upon a time there was a rocket ship. It was big and shiny. One day a little boy named Timmy wanted to open the rocket. He said, "I want to open the rocket and see inside." 

His dad said, "You can open the rocket, but it might be smelly in there."

So Timmy took a deep breath and opened the rocket. He went inside and it did smell bad. But, he was brave and looked around. There were rocket buttons, dials and levers. It was so exciting. 

Then Timmy shouted, "Let's go! Come on Dad, let's go fly the rocket." 

Dad said, "OK, let's go." So they went on a wonderful rocket ride and had a lot of fun. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a boy who was very impatient. He had the most special toy, a box of beautiful stones. But it made the boy sad, because they all looked the same.

One day, the room got dark and he was so scared. He held the box of stones tight and shook them up, so they would scatter all over the floor. 

The boy was now excited because the stones weren't all the same! Some were round, some were sparkly, and some were smooth. He jumped around and laughed, enjoying his special stones.

The boy gathered all the stones up in his toy box and hugged them tight. He knew that the darkness would not make him scared again. The shining, shimmering stones made sure his room stayed nice and bright.

Once upon a time, there was a girl called Molly. She loved going outside to play. One day, Molly asked her dad if he could borrow a baseball. Her dad said yes, so Molly took it outside to play.

Molly played with the baseball all day in the garden. She threw it in the air and caught it again. She ran around the garden with it too. Molly liked the baseball so much!

Then, Molly had an amazing idea. She wanted to play baseball with her friends. So she asked her dad if she could take the baseball to her friend's house and borrow some more baseballs. He said yes, and Molly raced to her friend's house with her amazing baseball.

When Molly got there, all her friends had baseballs too. They played together in the garden all afternoon. Everyone had so much fun, and they played together until it was time to go home.

Molly took the baseball back to her house and thanked her dad for borrowing it to her. Then they went inside, happy and tired from a day of playing baseball.

Sam and Lily are twins. They like to play with their toys in their room. But sometimes they fight over the same toy. One day, they both want to play with the cool train that makes noise and moves.

"Give me the train!" Sam says.

"No, it's mine!" Lily says.

They pull and tug on the train. The train breaks in two. Sam and Lily start to cry.

Mom hears the noise and comes to their room. She sees the broken train and the sad twins. She is not happy.

"Sam and Lily, what did you do?" Mom says. "You broke the train. That was not nice. You need to share and be kind to each other."

Mom makes them stand in the corner and listen to her lecture. She tells them why they should not fight and how they can say sorry and fix the train.

Sam and Lily feel bad. They say sorry to Mom and to each other. They hug and make up. They use glue and tape to fix the train. They take turns to play with it. They smile and laugh.

Mom sees them and smiles too. She is proud of them. She says, "Good job, Sam and Lily. You learned your lesson. Sharing is caring. Fighting is not fun. I love you both."

The end.

The little girl was very excited. Today she was going to try and succeed. She was trying to get a special medal. She had watched people get the medal before and she was determined to get one too.

The little girl ran and jumped and tried to do her best. Finally, she finished and was delighted to be told she had succeeded. She was handed a lovely medal.

The little girl was so proud and excited. She hugged it close and ran home to show everyone. Her family was so proud of her and they all hugged and said how lovely she was.

The little girl kept her medal safe and put it on special display in her room. She would look at it and remember this day with love and pride.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tweetie. Tweetie lived in a cage made of metal bars. One day, a big bird named Red saw Tweetie and wanted to be friends. Red asked politely if Tweetie wanted to join him and fly around the park. Tweetie was scared at first, but then he felt brave and said yes.

Red helped Tweetie out of his cage and they flew together in the bright blue sky. Tweetie felt free and happy. Red was very polite and showed Tweetie all the pretty flowers and trees in the park. Tweetie was so happy to have a new friend and to be free from his cage. From that day on, Tweetie and Red were the best of friends and flew together every day.

Once there was a boy who wanted to taste something sweet. He grabbed a spoon and went outside to find something sugary. But what he found instead was a peaceful pond. He decided to take a big spoonful of the water and see if it tasted sweet.

Unfortunately, it didn't taste sweet. In fact, it tasted very salty! He was sad and upset. He wanted something sweet, not something salty! He thought and thought and then decided to take a brave step. He would try and make the water taste sweet.

So he grabbed his spoon and started to butter the pond with it. He added sweet things like sugar, honey and chocolate. He stirred the mixture with his spoon until it was all mixed up. Then he took a spoonful, brought it to his mouth and tasted it.

To his surprise, the water was sweet! He was so happy! Now he could enjoy the peaceful pond and taste something sweet.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to bake cookies with her mom in the kitchen. One day, when they were baking cookies, Lily's mom noticed something strange with the oven. She said, "Lily, look at the oven. It doesn't look normal. Something might be wrong with it."

Lily looked at the oven and saw that it was making a strange noise. She said, "Mommy, what's wrong with the oven? Why is it making that noise?" Her mom replied, "I don't know, Lily. We should call the repairman to come and look at it."

So, they called the repairman and he came to look at the oven. He said, "Don't worry, everything is normal now. I fixed the problem." Lily was happy that the oven was fixed and they could continue baking cookies together. They baked lots of cookies and had a fun day in the kitchen. The end.

Once upon a time there was a blue tomato. It loved to slip around. Every morning it would slip out of its home and go exploring. 

It would slip over the hills and around the trees. It would go so fast that the birds and the bees couldn't keep up. 

The blue tomato soon made friends with a big yellow sun. The sun would follow the tomato as it slipped around and around. 

Every day the blue tomato would slip back home in the evening, exhausted but happy. It was content to spend its days slipping around and making new friends. 

And they all lived happily ever after. The end.

Tom and Sue like to play outside. They have many toys, but they like to share. Tom has a red truck and Sue has a blue bike. They lend their toys to each other and have fun.

One day, they see a stream near their house. The stream has clear water and small fish. Tom and Sue want to play with the stream. They bring their toys and a bucket.

Tom says, "I want to fill the bucket with water and fish. Can I use your bike to carry the bucket?"

Sue says, "Yes, you can use my bike. But be careful. Don't spill the water or hurt the fish."

Tom says, "Thank you, Sue. You are very nice. I will be careful."

Tom fills the bucket with water and fish. He puts the bucket on the bike and rides back to Sue. Sue is waiting for him. She has organized their toys on the grass. She has made a road for the truck and a bridge for the bike.

Sue says, "Look, Tom. I have made a play area for us. We can use the water and fish to make a pond. We can drive the truck and the bike around the pond."

Tom says, "Wow, Sue. You are very smart. You have organized our toys very well. This looks like fun."

Tom and Sue play with their toys, the water and the fish. They are happy and friendly. They lend their toys to each other and have fun.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play the violin and would practice every day. One day, she was playing in front of her friends when she made a mistake. She felt ashamed and wanted to stop playing.

But then, her mom told her something important. She said, "It's okay to make mistakes. You can always reverse them and try again." Lily didn't understand at first, but her mom explained that she could go back and fix her mistake by practicing more.

Lily listened to her mom and kept practicing. She got better and better at playing the violin. And whenever she made a mistake, she would just reverse it and try again. She learned that it's okay to make mistakes and that she shouldn't feel ashamed. The moral of the story is to always keep trying and never give up.

John was walking down the street, thinking about what he needed to buy. Then he saw it: a vendor selling fresh fruits and vegetables. He thought that this was a great place to buy food, so he slowly walked over. But when he got closer, he realized something was wrong. The vendor's stand was filthy, and John hesitated to buy anything. He thought that maybe he should look for something else, but then again he thought about how hungry he was. So he decided to take the risk and went to the vendor and bought an apple. 

When he took a bite, he found that it was delicious! He quickly realized that the vendor was selling great food, despite the place being so dirty. John thought it was funny how, with a little patience and trust, he found the yummiest apple and it was worth the extra effort.

Once upon a time, there was a big bird. The bird had many feathers that were colorful. One day, the bird wanted to spread its wings and fly. So, it flew high into the sky and looked down at the world below. 

The bird saw a little girl who was lost. She was looking for the exit, but she couldn't find it. The bird wanted to help her, so it flew down and landed next to her. The little girl was deaf, so she couldn't hear the bird. But the bird used its wings to show her the way to the exit. 

The little girl was so happy that she hugged the bird. The bird was happy too, because it had helped someone. From that day on, the bird always looked for ways to help others. And whenever it wanted to fly, it remembered the little girl and how it had helped her find the exit.

Once upon a time, there was a girl. Her name was Sue. She had to take an exam. She felt really weird about it.

But Sue was smart and brave. She worked very hard to complete the exam. It took a long time, but she kept at it.

Finally, on the day of the exam, she was ready. She was very proud of what she had done.

The exam was very long and difficult. But Sue kept thinking of her goal and she used her big brain to answer every question.

When the exam was over, Sue felt really happy. She had done it! She had completed the exam.

Sue felt very proud of herself. Even though taking the exam was weird, she had done a great job!

Paul was playing with his football in the garden one day. He saw a pigeon in the tree and was very excited. He wanted to catch the pigeon, but it flew away. Paul was very impatient. He sighed loudly and kicked the football.

Suddenly, the football got stuck between two fence posts. Paul tried to get it out but he couldn't. He started to scream and cry. His mom heard him and came running out. 

"Paul what is wrong?" she asked.

"It's stuck, I want it back," Paul said.

"Don't worry - I can help you. Let's try together," said his mom. 

With a few pushes and pulls, they managed to get the football out. Paul was overjoyed and hugged his mom tightly. 

"We did it!" Paul shouted. The pigeon however, was long gone â€“ it had escaped!

Once upon a time, there was an ancient pine tree. Every day a little girl named Etta would come and sit next to it. 

One day, Etta decided she wanted to make something special. She carefully tore up some big leaves into small pieces and then folded them into shapes. She made a bird and a ball and many other shapes. 

Etta twirled and hopped around the tree, admiring her creations. The tree watched her, amazed. Finally, Etta took some more pieces of leaves and carefully folded them into a crown. She hopped around the ancient pine tree, proudly wearing her leafy crown. 

The ancient pine tree was beaming with joy. Etta and the tree were now inseparable friends, and whenever Etta folded her leaves, the two were always together, happy and cheerful.

Once upon a time, there was a boy who wanted a pie. He asked his mom if he could go get a pie. His mom said yes and opened the door for him.

He went outside and skipped down the street. He saw a big, loud truck selling pies! He was so excited that he ran to the truck.

He asked the man at the truck for a pie. The man gave him a big, delicious pie. He gave the man some money and said "Thank You!" 

The boy held the pie tight and quickly ran back home. He opened the door and showed his mom the pie. His mom said it looked yummy! 

The boy and his mom ate the pie together. It was the best pie they ever tasted!

Lily and Ben were playing with their toys in the garden. They had a lot of fun with their cars, dolls, and blocks. But they had only one crown, and they both wanted to be the prince.

"I want to be the prince!" Lily said, grabbing the crown from Ben's head.

"No, I want to be the prince!" Ben said, pulling the crown back.

They started to fight over the crown, and they made a lot of noise. Their mom heard them and came to see what was wrong.

"Why are you fighting, Lily and Ben?" she asked. "You have so many toys to play with. Why don't you share the crown and take turns being the prince?"

Lily and Ben looked at each other. They did not like to share. They wanted to have the crown all the time.

"But mom, sharing is disgusting!" Lily said.

"Yeah, sharing is disgusting!" Ben agreed.

Their mom shook her head and smiled. She had an idea.

"Okay, if you don't want to share the crown, then you can't be the prince. You can be something else. How about a frog? Frogs don't need crowns. They just hop and croak and eat flies. Do you want to be frogs?"

Lily and Ben made a face. They did not want to be frogs. Frogs were slimy and gross. They did not want to hop and croak and eat flies.

"Yuck, frogs are disgusting!" Lily said.

"Yeah, frogs are disgusting!" Ben said.

They looked at the crown again. It was shiny and pretty. They liked to wear it and pretend to be the prince.

"Maybe sharing is not so disgusting," Lily said.

"Yeah, maybe sharing is not so disgusting," Ben said.

They decided to share the crown and take turns being the prince. They said sorry to each other and hugged. Their mom was happy to see them get along.

"Good job, Lily and Ben," she said. "Sharing is not disgusting. Sharing is nice. Sharing is what princes do."

Once there was a little girl who was very sad. She had lost her favourite doll and she felt so upset. She lay down in her bed, closed her eyes and began to weep. Her tears made her feel so quiet inside, and soon she was curled up in a little ball. Then, just as she was starting to feel a bit better, she heard a noise outside her window. She peeked out and saw her mum, dad and brother holding her favourite doll. They had gone out to find her and had brought it back as a surprise. She smiled and was no longer upset. She ran outside to thank them and hugged them all. They were so happy that the little girl was smiling again.

One day, Dad and Maggie went to an airport. Maggie was so excited. Dad said they were going on an adventure. Dad prepared their suitcases and made sure they had everything they needed.

Maggie asked, "Where are we going Daddy?" 

Dad said, "We are flying to Grandma's house. She is very excited to see you." 

Maggie smiled with excitement.

They got to the airport and through security with Joy. They took the train and arrived at the gate. Maggie couldn't contain her excitement.

The flight on the plane was long, but Maggie was happy. When they arrived at Grandma's house, she was so grateful. Grandma hugged Maggie and welcomed them inside. 

It was the best day ever.

Lily was a big girl who liked to play with her dolls. She had many dolls, but her favorite was Anna, a nurse doll who wore a white dress and a red hat. Lily liked to pretend that Anna was taking care of sick people and animals.

One day, Lily's brother Tom came into her room and saw Anna on the bed. He wanted to play with her, but Lily said no. She said Anna was her doll and he had to ask first. Tom was angry and grabbed Anna from the bed. He ran away with her, laughing.

Lily chased after him, shouting and crying. She wanted her doll back. She followed him to the kitchen, where he climbed on a chair and put Anna on the microwave. He pressed some buttons and said, "Now Anna will shrink and you can't play with her anymore!"

Lily was scared and sad. She didn't want Anna to shrink. She tried to reach the microwave, but she was too short. She called for her mom, who was in the living room. Mom heard her and came to the kitchen. She saw what Tom had done and was very angry.

She took Anna out of the microwave and checked if she was okay. She was not hurt, but she was very hot. Mom put her in a bowl of cold water to cool her down. She told Tom to say sorry to Lily and to go to his room. She said he was very naughty and mean.

Tom said sorry, but he didn't mean it. He went to his room, still feeling angry. Lily hugged Anna and thanked her mom. She said she was sorry for yelling and crying. She said she loved Anna and she was her best friend. Mom smiled and said she was proud of Lily. She said she was a humble and kind girl who cared for her dolls. She said she could play with Anna in her room, but she had to be careful with the microwave. Lily nodded and said she understood. She took Anna to her room and played with her. She was happy and grateful.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Daisy. She had two feet, but one of them was broken. Daisy was very sad.

One day, Daisy's mum put a new foot in the shopping trolley. When she saw it, Daisy was so excited! The new foot was bright and sparkly.

When they got home, Daisy's mum helped her to replace the broken foot with the new one. Daisy was so happy with her new foot that she was soon running and jumping around the house.

Daisy was so excited to finally be able to play with all her friends again. With her new foot, she could do anything she wanted.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a cute little girl called Anna. She loved going on safaris. One day, she asked her friend if she would go on a safari with her. Her friend said she would, but only if Anna could lend her some money. Anna was very happy and asked her Mum if she could lend her some money. Her Mum said yes, and gave Anna enough money to lend to her friend.

So, the two friends went on a safari together. It was a very exciting adventure! They saw lots of amazing animals and things. They had a great time.

When the safari was over, Anna lent her friend the money she had borrowed. Her friend was very happy and thanked Anna for the loan.

The two friends had a wonderful time on safari and Anna was happy she was able to lend her friend the money to make their adventure even more fun.

One day Little Tommy went for a walk in the park and he saw a fuzzy, furry animal. He said to himself, â€œI wonder what kind of animal this is?â€ 

He went up to the animal and realized that it was a rabbit. He was so excited! He said, â€œHello, Rabbit. What are you doing here?â€ 

The rabbit looked at Little Tommy and said, â€œIâ€™m looking for my lost label. Itâ€™s really important to me and I need to find it.â€ Little Tommy said, â€œIâ€™ll help you look for it!â€ 

They searched high and low in the park, but they couldnâ€™t find the rabbitâ€™s label. Little Tommy offered to carry the rabbit home so they could look there. The rabbit said, â€œThank you! Thatâ€™s very kind of you.â€
