The rabbit was so happy and said, â€œThank you so much! I was so worried that it was gone forever.â€ Little Tommy was glad he could help.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Andy. He liked to explore outside and so he went for a walk in the woods one day. He got to a cliff and could not believe how high and wet it was. He wanted to go over it to explore what was on the other side.

Suddenly he heard someone calling him from below. He looked down and saw his mom.

"Andy, don't come any closer!" she said. "The cliff is too wet and it's not safe to cross."

Andy wanted to ignore his mother's warning, but then he remembered how much he loved her. He listened to her and stopped walking.

"Thank you for listening to me," his mom said with a smile. "Now why don't you push the rock to try and get to the other side."

Andy was excited to try and he pushed the big, wet rock. After a few pushes, he made it over the cliff and waved goodbye to his mom before he continued exploring the other side.

Once upon a time, there was a bird called Joe. Joe was a very obedient bird, who always listened to his mom.

One day, Joe asked his mom, "Can I fly really high today?" His mom said, "Yes, go ahead."

So Joe flew high and higher. He was so happy, and he kept flying. Soon, he was so far away!

When Joe stopped flying, he looked around and he noticed he didn't recognise anything. He wasn't sure where he was.

Then, out of the corner of his eye, he saw another bird. "What's your name?" Joe asked.

The other bird said, "My name is Blue. Where are you from?"

Joe told Blue that he had flown far away. Blue said, "Let me show you the way back."

So Blue and Joe flew together until they reached Joe's home. Joe thanked Blue and said goodbye.

As Joe flew home, he was so happy he had such a good friend. He looked forward to their next adventure together.

Sara loved ice cream. She liked to lick it and feel it melt in her mouth. She liked all the colors and flavors of ice cream. But she did not like to share it.

One day, Sara went to the park with her mom and her brother Tom. Mom bought them each a cone of ice cream. Sara chose chocolate, Tom chose vanilla. Sara was happy with her ice cream, but she saw that Tom's ice cream was bigger than hers. She wanted his ice cream too.

She waited until Tom was busy playing with a ball. Then she ran to him and grabbed his cone. She took a big bite of his ice cream and ran away. Tom saw her and cried. He ran after her and tried to get his cone back. But Sara was faster and ran to the swings.

Mom heard Tom crying and saw what Sara did. She was angry and sad. She went to Sara and took her cone away. She gave it back to Tom and said sorry to him. She told Sara that she was very naughty and made Tom sad. She said that Sara had to say sorry to Tom and share her ice cream with him.

Sara felt bad. She felt guilty. She knew she did a bad thing. She did not want to hurt Tom. She loved Tom. She went to Tom and said sorry. She gave him half of her ice cream. Tom smiled and hugged her. He said he loved her too. He gave her half of his ice cream. They licked their ice cream and felt it melt in their mouths. They were happy again.

Mom smiled and hugged them both. She said she was proud of them for being kind and forgiving. She said they had good hearts and good lungs. She said they needed their lungs to breathe and laugh and sing. She said they should always take care of their lungs and their hearts. She said she loved them very much. They said they loved her too. They finished their ice cream and played together. They had a good day.

Once upon a time there was a boy who was three years old. He was very wise for his age. One day he decided to go to a museum. He had heard a lot about them and wanted to see for himself.

He stumbled his way around the museum. He looked at all the strange items with curiosity and delight. There were so many things to see, he couldn't keep still! He made his way around to all the different exhibits and learnt a lot.

He found a special corner in the museum, full of wise objects. He didn't know what all of them were but he could read the signs to find out. He learnt about old cultures, extinct animals, and historical artifacts.

He stumbled out of the museum at the end of the day, content and happy with all his discoveries. He had learnt a lot and was very wise!

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big slide. Lily wants to go on the slide, but Ben is scared.

"Come on, Ben, it is fun!" Lily says. She has an urge to slide down fast. She is not afraid.

"No, Lily, it is too high!" Ben says. He shakes his head. He is obedient to his mom, who told him to be careful.

Lily runs to the slide and climbs up the ladder. She sits on the top and smiles. She waves to Ben.

"Look, Ben, I am going to slide!" she says. She pushes herself and slides down. She laughs as she feels the wind in her hair.

Ben watches Lily slide. He sees her laugh. He thinks she looks happy. He feels a little urge to try the slide too. He walks to the ladder and holds on to the rails. He climbs up slowly. He reaches the top and sees Lily waiting for him.

"Hi, Ben, you did it!" Lily says. She is proud of her friend. She holds his hand.

"Hi, Lily, I did it!" Ben says. He is proud of himself. He looks at the slide. He is still scared, but he wants to have fun.

"Are you ready, Ben?" Lily asks.

"Yes, Lily, I am ready!" Ben says.

They slide down together. They laugh as they feel the wind in their hair. They are happy. They are brave. They are friends.

Once upon a time, there was a girl who was very brave. She wanted to show everyone how strong and beautiful she was. So, she found a delicate mirror and decided to look at her reflection. She saw that she was so pretty! But as she looked closer, she saw something strange. Suddenly, she saw a monster in the mirror! It scared her so much that she started to cry. She could not believe it. The monster seemed so real! She ran away and was never brave enough to look in the mirror again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to read books. One day, Lily went to the library to find a book to read. She looked and looked, but she couldn't find one she liked. 

Suddenly, she saw a boy with a book. She asked him, "Can I see that book?" The boy said, "Sure, but it's a disgusting book." 

Lily looked at the book and said, "I don't care if it's disgusting. I want to read it." The boy said, "Okay, but you better hurry. The library is closing soon." 

Lily took the book and started to read it. She thought it was really gross, but she kept reading. Then, she found something really interesting in the book. She was glad she read it, even though it was disgusting. She returned the book and left the library, feeling happy that she found a good book to read.

Once upon a time, there was a jolly girl named Jane. One day, Jane was in her room and felt hungry. She saw an apple on her bed. She was so happy! She sat down on her bed and ate her apple up. 

Afterwards, Jane felt happy and jolly. She said to herself, "That was so yummy!" 

Then, she went downstairs to find her mom. She said with a smile on her face, "Mommy, I ate my apple. It was so good!" 

Her mom smiled and said, "Great job, Jane! Apples are so healthy and tasty. I'm proud of you!"

Jane was so happy. She said, "I'm going to sit outside and play now." 

And so Jane went out to sit and play in the sun, feeling jolly and content with her full tummy.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy had a loyal dog named Max. Max loved to watch Timmy play with his toys. One day, Timmy's mom gave him a lime to try. Timmy didn't like the taste of the lime, but Max ate it all up! From that day on, Timmy and Max would always share their snacks and watch movies together. They were the best of friends. The end.

Tim and Mia are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big fan on the grass. The fan is spinning and making wind.

"Wow, look at the fan!" Tim says. "It is so big and fast!"

"Can we touch it?" Mia asks.

They run to the fan. But a man is sitting next to the fan. He is reading a book.

"Hello, kids," the man says. "Do you like my fan?"

"Yes, we do!" Tim and Mia say. "It is cool and fun!"

The man smiles. He is humble. He does not think he is better than others.

"Thank you," he says. "I made this fan myself. It is a hobby. I like to make things that work."

"Can you show us how it works?" Tim asks.

"Sure," the man says. "But be careful. Do not touch the blades. They are sharp."

He shows them a switch and a battery. He explains how the fan spins and makes wind.

Tim and Mia are amazed. They learn something new. They thank the man and say goodbye.

They go back to play. They are happy. They have a new friend. And they have seen a big fan.

Lily and Tom were jolly friends who liked to play in the park. They had a ball, a kite and a bike. They ran, flew and rode all morning. They had so much fun that they forget to drink water.

"Tom, I am thirsty. Are you thirsty too?" Lily asked.

"Yes, Lily. I am thirsty too. Let's go to the fountain and drink some water," Tom said.

They left their toys and went to the fountain. But when they got there, they saw a big dog drinking from the fountain. The dog was big and hairy and had sharp teeth. Lily and Tom were scared of the dog.

"Tom, what do we do? I want to drink water, but the dog is there," Lily said.

"Me too, Lily. But the dog is scary. Maybe we can wait until he goes away," Tom said.

They hid behind a bench and waited for the dog to leave. But the dog did not leave. He drank and drank and drank. He drank all the water from the fountain. Lily and Tom were sad and thirsty.

"Tom, the dog drank all the water. Now we have no water to drink," Lily said.

"I know, Lily. That is not fair. The dog is mean. He should share the water with us," Tom said.

They decided to go back to their toys and find another way to get water. But when they got back to their toys, they saw another surprise. A girl and a boy were playing with their ball, their kite and their bike. The girl and the boy were happy and jolly. Lily and Tom were angry and sad.

"Hey, those are our toys. Give them back to us," Lily said.

"No, they are not. We found them here. They are ours now," the girl said.

"That is not true. We left them here for a moment. We went to drink water, but a dog drank all the water. We are thirsty and we want our toys back," Tom said.

The girl and the boy did not listen. They laughed and played with the toys. Lily and Tom did not know what to do. They forget to drink water and they lost their toys. They wished they had not forget to drink water. They wished they had not left their toys. They wished they had a jolly day.

Once upon a time, there was a nice school for children. Every morning the children would go to school and wait for teacher in their classroom. One day, their teacher arrived with a big surprise. She brought a big blackboard to class! 

The teacher said, "Children! Look what I got for you! It's a blackboard!" The children were excited and yelled, "Wow, a blackboard! What shall we do with it?"

The teacher smiled and said, "Let's write stories on it." She gave each of the children a piece of chalk and asked them to be quiet. Once it was quiet, she said, "Ok, let's start!" 

The children all eagerly wrote their stories on the blackboard. The teacher was very pleased with the children and said, "Nice job! You have all done a very nice job!"

Tom and Lily are playing in the park. They see a big flag on a pole. The flag is red and white and blue. It moves in the wind.

"Look, Lily, a flag!" Tom says. "I want to touch it."

Tom runs to the pole. He tries to reach the flag, but it is too high. He leans on the pole and jumps, but he cannot touch it.

"Tom, be careful!" Lily says. "You might fall."

Lily runs to Tom. She holds his hand. She helps him to lean on the pole.

"Maybe we can touch it together," she says.

They lean on the pole and jump together. They touch the flag with their fingers. They feel happy.

Suddenly, they hear a loud noise. It is a siren. A fire truck is coming to the park. It is red and shiny. It has a big ladder and a hose. It is very noisy.

"Wow, a fire truck!" Tom says. "Let's go see it."

They let go of the pole and the flag. They run to the fire truck. They see the firefighters. They wear helmets and coats. They are brave.

"Hello, kids," one firefighter says. "Do you like the fire truck?"

"Yes, we do!" Tom and Lily say. "It is very noisy and cool."

The firefighter smiles. He gives them stickers. They have flags and fire trucks on them.

"Thank you, firefighter," Tom and Lily say. "You are very nice."

They stick the stickers on their shirts. They wave to the firefighter and the fire truck. They go back to the pole and the flag. They lean on the pole and jump again. They have fun in the park.

Once upon a time, on a bright sunny day, there lived a young girl, named Lucy. She loved to play all day long with her friends. One day, Lucy awoke to the sound of loud thunder, which made her nervous. She went outside to see what was happening and noticed that the bright sunny day had changed. The sky was now blue and there were strong winds, making trees sway and leaves fly.

Lucy was confused and scared. She asked her mom, "What's happening?" Her mom replied, "It's a hurricane, dear. A big, powerful storm that can change the weather and make it very dangerous."

Suddenly, Lucy heard the loud thundering noise again, but this time it was much closer. She ran to her mom and said, "Mom, I'm scared!" Her mom said, "It's okay, Lucy. Stay inside and we'll be safe."

Lucy and her mom stayed safe in their home until the hurricane was gone. After the storm was over, the sky was back to its bright sunny state and Lucy felt better.

She smiled and said, "Mom, I'm glad the hurricane changed and we're safe." Her mom nodded in agreement and said, "Me too, dear. Me too."

Once upon a time, three children went on an adventure. They wanted to prepare something special. They went to the store and looked around.

They saw a tire. It was big and round. They decided to buy it. Next they picked up some healthy food. They chose fruits, vegetables and a special treat.

The children went home and prepared their tire. First they covered it with a big blanket. Then they put the food inside. Finally, they gathered some friends and jumped. They rolled and laughed. They had a lot of fun. 

After all their playing, the children went inside for dinner. They enjoyed their healthy meal. Then they all slept with big smiles on their faces. 

The end!

One day, two children went to the beach to swim. One child was older and the other was only three years old.

They went to a special place to swim with a boat. The boat was regular, which means it was neither big nor small.

The three year old was very excited to get in the boat. He put on a life-jacket, just like the other child. They paddled the boat out until they reached the deep water.

The older child wanted to dive in and explore the bottom, but the three-year old only wanted to swim around the boat. He kicked his feet and moved his arms to make himself swim. He was so proud of himself for swimming!

When they were finished swimming, the two children paddled back to the shore. The three-year old had so much fun and can't wait to go swimming again.

Little Jack was walking down the street. He saw a big, modern building and he thought it was so cool. He wished he lived there. But then he saw a group of people. Jack didn't like them; he hated the way they looked. He was scared, so he ran away. 

When Jack got to the end of the street, he felt much better. He looked around and he saw a big park. There were trees and swings, and it was so much nicer than the modern building. Jack knew it was a safe place, so he decided to stay and play. 

Jack spent the whole afternoon playing games in the park. He forgot all about the people he had seen and the thing he hated. All was well.

Mummy was going to the grocery store with Jack and Jill. "Jack, do you want to come with me?" Mummy asked. "Yes!" Jack replied.

Mummy and Jack went inside the store and Jack saw lots of food and snacks. Mummy said: "Let's get some fruit". They picked some apples and oranges and put them in a bag. 

As they were going to pay, Mummy saw a large grocery basket. She said: "This looks handy! Shall we get it?" Jack wanted it and so they bought it. 

On the way home, they stopped at the park and Mummy offered Jack the apples and oranges. Jack was very happy and munched on the fruit while they walked. 

When they got home, Jack was so pleased with the grocery basket that he said: "Thank you Mummy" and he gave her a big kiss.

Tim and his mom were in the store. Tim saw a great pair of pants. He asked his mom if he could get them. His mom said, "Yes, those look great on you." 

Tim was so excited. He put them on and hopped up and down saying, "Look, Mommy, look how I stand in them!" His mom smiled and said, "Yes, you look very handsome in those pants. Great job!" 

Tim was so proud of himself. He asked one more time if he could keep the pants. His mom said, "Yes, let's get them. You look super sharp in them!" 

Tim was so happy. He said, "I love my new pants!" 

His mom said, "I'm glad you love them. They look great on you!" 

Tim was the happiest he had ever been. Now he had a great pair of pants to show off to his friends.

Once upon a time, there were two friends, Molly and Jack. Molly was very happy and Jack was very patient. One day, they were playing in the garden. Molly wanted to run around and play catch but Jack wanted to hang a picture in the garden. 

Molly was very naughty and kept running around and wouldn't help Jack. Jack was very patient and tried to show Molly how to be helpful. He helped Molly to hang the picture in a big frame on the wall.

When the frame was finally hung, Molly realised that Jack had been very patient with her, even though she had not been behaving. She thanked him and they hugged. From then on, Molly made sure to be patient and kind, just like Jack.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to chew his food very loud. One day, Tim went to visit his uncle. His uncle was very kind and made yummy food for Tim.

While they were eating, Tim chewed his food very loud. His uncle asked him to chew softly, but Tim did not listen. He thought it was fun to be loud. His uncle felt sad that Tim did not listen to him.

Later, Tim saw his uncle was not happy. He thought about what he did wrong. Tim knew he should be a good boy and listen to his uncle. The next day, Tim chewed his food softly, and his uncle was happy. Tim learned that listening to others is very important.

Once upon a time there was a lamp. It was magical and so bright! It was hard to control, and often made things happen that no one expected. 

One day, the lamp started to act in a very difficult way. It wouldn't stop shining and it lit up the whole room! Everyone was so surprised. 

But then, something amazing happened. The lamp suddenly became a beautiful fairy! She waved her wand and made everything go back to normal. 

The people cheered and thanked the fairy for making it easy again. From then on, the lamp was everyone's friend. The end.

The little boy was so excited. He was going to the airport with his family. He could not wait to go on his first airplane.

He watched as his mom and dad loaded their bags into the car. His face was filled with excitement as his dad opened the car door for him. 

As the car drove closer to the airport, his excitement grew. He could see planes taking off and landing from outside the car window. Suddenly, he heard a roar. He looked up and saw a huge plane taking off into the sky! 

The little boy screamed with excitement. His mom laughed and said, "Don't worry, soon it will be our turn to take off in one of these planes." The little boy was very restless as they pulled up to the airport. He was ready to get out and explore. 

His dad opened the car door, and the little boy jumped out. He ran around the airport, marveling at all the big planes. Then, he heard a loud announcement that their plane was ready for boarding.

The little boy screamed with delight. His mom smiled, and said, "Let's go!" They all grabbed their bags and ran to their plane, excited for the adventure to come.

Once upon a time there was an incredible bear. He loved taking a bath. Every day he'd fill up the bathtub with warm water and splash about in it. He even brought in a special spoon to use as a toy.

One day, he decided to let someone else join him. So he invited a little duck to come bathe with him. The duck was very excited! She paddled around the bathtub with the bear and the spoon.

They had so much fun playing together! Even when the bear got out to dry off the little duck stayed in the bathtub splashing around. In the end, they both had a wonderful bath time.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat snacks, especially crackers and cheese. One day, her mom told her she couldn't have a snack because it was almost dinner time. Lily was sad, but she surrendered and waited for dinner.

Later that evening, Lily's dad came home from work. He had a harsh day at work and was feeling grumpy. Lily tried to cheer him up by giving him a hug and a kiss. Her dad's face softened and he smiled. He realized he had surrendered to his bad mood and needed to be more positive.

After dinner, Lily's parents surprised her with a special snack - ice cream! Lily was so happy and grateful. She surrendered to the joy of the moment and enjoyed every bite. From that day on, Lily learned that surrendering to the good things in life can bring happiness.

Jamie was upset. He wanted to swim but his parents said no. Jamie was frustrated. He asked them again and again but they still said no. 

He sat on the side of the pool and stirred the water with his foot. The ripples broke the surface of the water into many tiny rings that moved away from him. 

He watched them go and it made him smile. He loved to watch the ripples and thought that if he stirred hard enough, he could create enough ripples and he could swim. 

He stirred for a long time until he was tired. Finally, his parents said yes! He jumped in the pool with a big splash and swam with happy arms and legs. He was so pleased that he swam and stirred the water all afternoon.

Daughter and Dad were walking in the park. The sky was blue and the sun was warm. Daddy stopped and pointed at a big elephant. 

"What's that?" asked Daughter.

"That's an elephant. We must mind him," said Daddy.

Daughter stared at the elephant. He had long, smooth ears and a long trunk. He was so big but so gentle.

"But, Daddy, why should we mind him?" asked Daughter.

"Because," said Daddy, "he's very important to the park. He helps keep it clean and safe." 

Daughter nodded and smiled. She knew that it was time to be careful and mind the elephant.

Once there was a persistent hippo. He asked lots of questions and always wanted to know the answers. One day he asked his friend, 'Why is the sun so bright?' His friend didn't know how to answer. So, the hippo decided to find the answer for himself.

The hippo was very persistent. He searched in the sky and in the trees but could not find the answer. He asked the birds and the bees but no one seemed to know the answer. He decided to keep looking until he found it.

The hippo looked for days, weeks and months but still he couldn't find the answer. Until one day he stumbled upon a wise old owl. He asked the owl, 'Why is the sun so bright?' The owl hooted and said, 'Because it is full of light!'

The hippo was so happy to get an answer. He learned that no matter how long it takes, it is important to be persistent because the answer will eventually be found.

Once upon a time there was a little boy. He loved to wander. Every day he would leave his home and wander around the neighbourhood.

One day, he stumbled upon a vendor. The vendor was a reliable one, who sold delicious fruits and vegetables every day. The boy was very excited and asked his mother, "Can I buy something from the vendor?"

The mother replied, "Yes, you can. It's important to be reliable and keep your promises. If you promise to buy something from the vendor, you must do so, even if you change your mind later."

The little boy understood the meaning of reliable and promised the vendor to buy from him. From that day onwards, the boy was always reliable, kept his words and never let anyone down.

Once upon a time there was a little boy named Joe who loved exploring new places and new things. He was always very curious and asked lots of questions. 
One day Joe's mommy took him to the tall building to ride in the elevator. Joe was excited and asked all sorts of questions. 
As they both got into the elevator, Joe asked his mommy: "Mommy, what is an elevator?"
His mommy smiled and said: "It is a safe way to take us up to the higher floors". 
Joe was so amazed he wanted to ride the elevator again. 
His mommy taught him a valuable lesson. She said: "Joe, always be honest and understand people. If you are honest and try to understand others, they will do the same to you. 
Joe nodded and said: "I understand, mommy!" From that day onwards, Joe was more honest and understanding in his daily life. 
The moral of the story is that understanding and being honest can bring most positive outcomes and help us get along with others.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Sam and Sue. Sam wanted to play a game. He said, "Let's race to the castle!" 

Sue was very excited. She said, "Yes! Let's go!" 

So they started to run. They were racing very fast. Sam was ahead of Sue, but Sue was still trying hard to catch him. 

Suddenly, they reached the castle. They were both so happy. They had a lot of fun playing together. 

The End.

John was walking in the park. He looked down and saw a strip on the ground. He thought it was so fine! He picked it up and decided to take it home with him. 

On the way, he saw his friend Mary. Mary asked, "What do you have there?" 

John said, "I found this strip and Iâ€™m taking it home." Mary smiled and said, "That looks so fine! Can I have it?"

Mary thanked him and happily took the strip. She said "Thank you! I'll take good care of it. Bye!"

John smiled and waved goodbye. He was glad that he was able to make his friend happy. He kept walking and looking forward to getting home.

Once upon a time there was a family who had a yellow yacht. One day they decided to go out on the yacht and have fun. They took the yacht out on the water and played games, laughed, and ate yummy snacks. 

When they finished their fun, they drove the yacht back to the dock. But when they got there, they noticed something was wrong. They spotted a big hole in the side of the yacht, and they knew they had been spoiled!
 
They were sad and upset, because they loved their yellow yacht. But then they decided to be brave and find a way to fix it. They got some tools, new pieces of wood, and paint. Then they all worked together to fix the yacht. 

In the end, the family had made the yacht as good as new - and back to its usual yellow colour! They were so happy that they all danced on the dock. And from then on, they always made sure to take extra care of their yellow yacht.

Ben was sick. He had a bad cough and a hot head. He stayed in bed all day and night. He did not want to play or eat or talk. He only wanted to sleep and feel better.

His mom and dad were sad. They gave him water and medicine and hugs. They read him stories and sang him songs. They hoped he would get well soon.

One morning, Ben woke up and saw the sunrise. It was bright and orange and pink. It made his room glow. He felt a little better. He smiled and said, "Mom, dad, look! The sunrise is pretty!"

His mom and dad came to his bed. They saw the sunrise too. They were happy. They hugged him and said, "Yes, it is very pretty. And so are you. You are getting stronger, Ben. We are proud of you."

Ben felt their love. He felt the warmth of the sunrise. He felt a little stronger too. He hoped he would get well soon and play and eat and talk again. He hoped he would see more sunrises with his mom and dad. He closed his eyes and thanked the sunrise for making him feel better.

John and his mom were walking in the park. He had a little bag with him filled with smooth round marbles. He smiled when he saw the other children playing with their marbles, rolling them across the ground. Suddenly his mom became angry. She told John to release his marbles into the grass.

"Why, mom?" John asked.

"Because it's not nice to take all the fun away from the other children," his mom replied. She looked sternly at John and repeated her request.

John sighed and reluctantly opened his bag letting the marbles roll away one by one. He watched sadly as other children ran after them and squealed with delight.

John knew his mom was right, but he was still angry. He kicked a rock as they walked away. His mom picked it up and put it in her pocket.

"Let's find a special marble for you instead," she said.

John smiled and quickly forgot about his anger. He ran ahead, looking for the perfect marble.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside with his friends. One day, Timmy and his friends decided to play a game of catch. Timmy tried his best to catch the ball, but it kept slipping out of his hands. 

Suddenly, the ball flew over Timmy's head and landed in a nearby net. Timmy ran over to the net and tried to get the ball out, but it was stuck. He pulled and pulled, but the ball wouldn't budge. 

Timmy's friends came over to help him. They all tried to get the ball out of the net, but it was no use. Timmy's arm started to hurt from pulling so hard. Just when they thought they would never get the ball back, Timmy's big brother came to the rescue. He easily got the ball out of the net and gave it back to Timmy. Timmy was so happy and grateful to his brother for helping him.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim had a special toy called a microscope. He loved to sit and look through it to see things up close.

One sunny day, Tim went outside to play. He brought his microscope and sat under a big tree. The ground was dry because it had not rained for many days.

Tim looked at the dry leaves and the tiny bugs through his microscope. He was so happy to see the small world up close. And that is how Tim spent his day, sitting under the tree with his microscope, exploring the tiny world around him.

Sara and Tom were twins. They liked to help Mom and Dad with the Christmas tree. They put lights and stars and balls on the tree. They were very happy.

But there was one ornament that Sara and Tom both wanted. It was a shiny snowman with a red hat and a carrot nose. Sara saw it first and took it from the box. She wanted to put it on the tree.

"Give me the snowman!" Tom said. He tried to grab it from Sara. Sara held it tight. She did not want to share.

"No, it's mine!" Sara said. She and Tom started to struggle. They pulled and pushed and shouted.

Mom and Dad heard the noise. They came to the living room. They saw Sara and Tom fighting over the snowman. They were very sad.

"Stop, stop!" Mom said. "Why are you fighting? You are twins. You should love each other and share."

"But I want the snowman!" Sara and Tom both said.

Mom took the snowman from them. She looked at it. She saw a small tag on it. She read it.

"This snowman is very special," Mom said. "It was a gift from Grandma and Grandpa. They made it for both of you. They wanted you to enjoy it together. They love you very much."

Sara and Tom felt sorry. They looked at each other. They said sorry too.

"Can we have the snowman back?" Sara asked.

"Yes, you can," Mom said. "But you have to promise to share it and take turns. And you have to hug and say I love you."

Sara and Tom nodded. They hugged and said I love you. Mom gave them the snowman. They smiled and thanked her. They put the snowman on the tree. They held hands and looked at it. It was very shiny and pretty. They were very happy.

One day, a little girl went outside to play. As she looked around, she saw a fast squirrel. She was so excited to see the squirrel! She wanted to play with it. She tried to get close to it but it was very fast and wouldn't let her catch it. 

The squirrel hopped up a tree and the little girl jumped up and down excitedly. She watched it run along the branch and jump from tree to tree. She ran around the yard, trying to keep up with the squirrel, but it was too fast. 

She watched the squirrel until it disappeared into the bushes. She had so much fun playing try to catch the squirrel. She knew that it was a game that she could never really win, but it was still a lot of fun.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toy cars and trucks. One day, Timmy found a shiny piece of iron on the ground. He picked it up and showed it to his mom.

"Look, Mommy! I found a pretty rock!" Timmy said.

"That's not a rock, Timmy. That's a piece of iron. It's very valuable," Mommy said.

Timmy didn't understand what "valuable" meant, but he liked how the iron looked. He kept it in his pocket and went back to playing.

Later that day, Timmy's friend Johnny came over to play. Johnny saw the piece of iron in Timmy's pocket and said, "Wow, that's cool! Can I have it?"

Timmy thought for a moment and said, "Okay, you can have it."

Johnny took the iron and went home. Timmy didn't think much of it, but his mom told him that he shouldn't give away things that are valuable.

A few days later, Johnny's mom came over to Timmy's house. She was very angry.

"Johnny got sick because he played with that piece of iron you gave him. It was rusty and not safe to play with," she said.

Timmy felt bad. He didn't know that the iron was dangerous. He learned that even things that look mild can be harmful.

Once upon a time, there was a beautiful evening with a purple sky. All the animals outside were busy singing and playing in the sun.

However, the purple evening came to an end. As night started to fall, the animals said goodbye and went home. But then something unexpected happened!

In came a purple dragon! Everyone was scared, but the dragon was friendly. He said he was looking for some friends to include him in their games.

The animals all paused to think. Then the little squirrel said, "Let's include him!" 

Everyone agreed and they all had a wonderful evening of playing together. The dragon even taught them a new game, and they had so much fun!

When the night ended, the dragon flew away. But the animals always looked forward to having the purple dragon return to their evening fun.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to skip and play outside. One day, her mommy told her that she had to go to her job. Lily wasn't happy because she wanted to play more.

But then, her mommy said that Lily could come with her to the job. Lily was eager to go! When they arrived, Lily saw that her mommy's job was very busy. There were lots of people working on computers and talking on phones.

Lily was happy to be there with her mommy, but she still wanted to skip and play outside. So, her mommy took a break and they went outside to skip together. They had so much fun! After that, Lily was happy to stay at the job with her mommy.

One day, Thomas was playing in his backyard. He saw something strange -a little vine that was growing in the garden. He wanted to take a closer look. 

He ran over to the vine and tried to unpack it. Thomas pulled and pulled, but it wouldn't come out. 

His mom saw what he was doing and said, "Thomas, that vine will not come out. Youâ€™re going to have to leave it be."

Thomas said, "But Mom, I just want to see whatâ€™s inside this little vine!"

His mom said, "I understand, but the vine needs to stay where it is right now. Could you help me with something else instead?" 

Thomas was disappointed, but he agreed. He found something else to do, and he let the little vine stay. 

The end.

Mum and Dad took their little girl to the park. She was excited to explore all around. The first thing she saw was a tall tree. She was curious and wanted to know more.

Mum smiled and said, "Listen closely. Can you hear the birds in the tree? They are singing their songs." Little girl listened, and smiled. She heard the birds and it made her happy.

The little girl saw a big sandbox. She ran to it and saw all the shapes inside. She was so excited and full of joyful thoughts. She asked Mum, "What are the shapes for?"

Mum smiled and said, "The shapes can be used to make houses and castles. Use your imagination and be thoughtful as you build." 

The little girl listened carefully to Mum's words. She was now filled with thoughts of hope and creativity. She began to dig and play in the sandbox, and create her own shapes.

One day, there was a mum and a daughter in the park. The daughter was three, and her name was Lila. She loved playing outside.

'Let's look for shells in the sand,' said mum.

Lila was excited to find shells and she began to search on the ground. She removed some stones to find the shells.

'Lila, don't take the stones away. Let them stay and help the shells grow,' said mum.

Lila did not know why the stones had to stay, so her mum tried to teach her the reason. 

'If the stones are removed, the shells will not be able to get the food they need to survive. Without the food, they'll feel very sad and bitter', mum explained.

Lila found it hard to understand, but she nodded her head so her mum would be happy. They put the stones back in their places and searched for some shells. Soon, they found some shells they could take home and show their family. Both Lila and mum felt excited!

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy liked to play sport with his friends. They would run and kick a ball together. Timmy was very good at sport because he practiced every day.

One day, Timmy found a little bird that had hurt its wing. He knew he had to help the bird. Timmy gently picked up the bird and held it in his hands. The bird was obedient and didn't try to fly away.

Timmy took the bird to his mom and dad, who helped him take care of it. They gave the bird some food and a cozy place to rest. Timmy felt happy that he could help the little bird. From that day on, Timmy always made sure to be kind to animals and hold them gently.

Once upon a time, there was a boy who liked to go to the park. He liked to run and play in the park. His mommy brought a net so he could play with it. He liked to try and catch bugs in the net. 

When he went to the park, the sun was shining and it felt warm. So he took off his shoes and ran around in the grass. He saw a butterfly fluttering around and tried to catch it in the net. His mommy told him that butterflies are too quick for the net, but he kept trying anyway. 

After a while, the sun started to set. The boy put on his shoes and said goodbye to the park. He was sorry that he couldn't catch the butterfly, but his mommy said they would come back and try again.

Once there was a little bunny. It was a very happy bunny and it loved to hop around. One day, the bunny was exploring in the meadow when it noticed something was different. It stopped hopping and suddenly felt afraid. Its nose trembled and it was very alert.

Then, the bunny heard a loud noise. It looked around, wondering where the noise was coming from. That's when it saw a big, scary bear, standing in the middle of the meadow.

The little bunny froze in place and trembled with fear.

The bear said in a friendly voice, "Don't be scared, little bunny. I just want to be your friend. Can we be friends?"

The bunny was still a little scared, but it got brave and slowly nodded its head yes.

The bear smiled and said, "That's great! Let's go explore the meadow together."

The bunny was so happy that it had made a new friend. Together, they ran and hopped around the meadow, having lots of fun. From then on, the bunny and the bear were the best of friends!

Once upon a time there was a shy girl. She liked playing with dolls and getting cozy with her family. One day, she got something special - a pitcher filled with warm milk. Her mommy said she could pour it however she wanted.

The little girl decided to give some to her dolls. She thought it was fun to pour it in the little cups she had. When it was all gone she was proud of herself. She felt she had done something valuable.

The next day, the little girl was even shyer than before. But she still had some courage. She wanted to pour her mommy a cup of mil. The little girl was nervous, but she did it. Her mommy was proud and gave her a big kiss.

The little girl felt so proud. She learned something valuable - that she could do things, even if she was a little shy.

Once upon a time there was a guard. He was a very strong and brave guard and he looked after a lot of different places. One of his favourite jobs was to look after a very nosy village.

Every day he would recommend things to keep the village safe and happy. He would always remind the villagers to be polite and kind to each other.

One day, the guard was walking around the village when he heard a loud noise. He ran to the source of the sound and spotted a naughty cat. The cat was being nosy and had knocked over some things in the village.

The guard quickly sorted out the mess and then caught the cat. He brought the cat back to the village elder.

The guard recommended that the cat should go and live in a different village, far away from the nosy villagers. The elder noted his wise suggestion, and thanked the guard for his help. 

The guard bowed his head and smiled. He continued to look after the village and kept on recommending sensible things to keep it safe and happy.

One day, Tom and Sue were playing with paper. They wanted to cut the paper, but they only had one pair of scissors. Tom said, "Let's share the scissors, Sue!"

Sue said, "Okay, Tom! I will cut first." Sue cut the paper. It was tough to cut, but she did it. Then, she gave the scissors to Tom. Tom cut the paper too. It was tough for him as well, but he was happy to do it.

After they both cut the paper, they made a big mess. Tom and Sue looked at each other and laughed. They had fun sharing the scissors and cutting the tough paper. Then, they cleaned up the mess together.

Once upon a time there was a big, enormous bell. Every day it would ring and the sound was so loud that all the village people could hear it.

One day, a little girl named Clara was walking by the bell when she heard it ringing. She was so fascinated, she climbed up to the very top. She reached up and touched the bell and, to her surprise, it felt really soft and warm.

Clara realized that the bell was covered with a cloth. She touched it and found it was really, really soft. She began to wonder what the cloth was made of.

The Village Chief noticed Clara on top of the enormous bell and hurried over to help her down. He smiled and explained that the cloth was made with special wool from a faraway mountain. He said the cloth made the bell sound even better.

The village people were very happy to know that their bell was so unique. From then on, the bell would ring every day, louder and clearer than ever before.

Once upon a time there were two friends who were playing together. One was called Billy and the other was called Sarah.

Billy had a toy gun and he wanted to shoot. He asked Sarah, â€œLetâ€™s shoot something!â€ But Sarah was scared and said, â€œNo! We shouldnâ€™t!â€

Billy said, â€œLetâ€™s shoot the white stove!â€ Sarah was scared, but she said, â€œOK, letâ€™s try.â€

They pointed the toy gun at the white stove and then Billy said, â€œReady, aim, shoot!â€ He pulled the trigger and a loud bang came from the gun.

Billy and Sarah looked at the stove. It was still white and nothing had happened.

Sarah smiled and said, â€œSee, nothing happened! We shouldnâ€™t shoot things!â€

Billy agreed and they went off to play something else.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to paint. She would paint all day long with her colorful paints. One day, Lily wanted to paint a picture for her mommy's birthday. She was so excited to show her mommy her beautiful painting. 

But then, Lily realized that she didn't have any red paint left. She searched and searched, but she couldn't find any red paint. Lily started to cry because she wanted to make her mommy's painting perfect. 

Suddenly, Lily's big sister came into the room. She saw that Lily was sad and asked her what was wrong. Lily explained that she couldn't paint her mommy's picture because she didn't have any red paint. Her sister smiled and said, "Don't worry, Lily. I have some red paint that you can use." Lily was so happy and proud of her big sister for helping her. She painted the most beautiful picture yet and gave it to her mommy on her birthday.

Once there was a little girl called Lucy. She was very curious and brave.

One day, Lucy and her mommy were walking in the park. Suddenly, Lucy saw a guard. He was wearing a blue hat and smiling. Lucy wanted to talk to him. 

She leaned closer and called out, "Hello!" The guard smiled and said, "Hi there! Can I help you?" 

Lucy was very cheerful. She said, "I like your hat. Can I touch it?" The guard nodded and said, "Of course!" Lucy gently leaned towards his hat and touched it softly. 

The guard smiled and said, "Thank you for being so friendly!" Lucy smiled back and waved goodbye.

One day, a boy named Tim found a marble. It was not an easy marble to see. It was tiny and hid under a big rock. Tim picked up the marble and put it in his pocket.

Tim went to his friend, Sue. "Look at my marble," said Tim. Sue did not care. She ignored Tim and kept playing with her toy. Tim felt sad that Sue did not look at his marble.

Later, Tim saw a girl named Amy. He showed her the marble. Amy liked it. "Wow, what a nice marble!" she said. Tim felt happy. They played with the marble together and became good friends.

Josh and his mom went to the store. They got tons of cool things. But still, Josh wanted just one more thing. His mom said no. Josh was very angry. He shouted and he made his mom so scared that she froze.

Then Josh had a silly idea. Josh wanted to go in the elevator without his mom! He thought he was old enough. But Josh was wrong. He pressed the button and the elevator doors opened, but Josh could not get out. He was stuck!

Josh learned a valuable lesson that day. He learned that it's never a good idea to do things without your mom's permission. Next time, Josh will follow his mom's advice.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tom. Tom liked to play with cars, but one day he couldn't get one of his cars to work. He was very sad.

Tom's mummy told him to take the car to see the mechanic. This made Tom feel excited. He grabbed the car and ran off to the mechanic.

The mechanic looked at the car and said it needed to be repaired. This made Tom happy, because he wanted his car to work again. But then the mechanic showed him something. The mechanic said the car was fake!

Tom was sad, but then the mechanic said he could fix the car and make it real. Tom was happy, because the mechanic was going to repair the car.

Soon the car was repaired and it worked better than ever. Tom was thrilled and drove the car around everywhere. He was so happy that the mechanic could repair his car.

The end.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She was three years old and excited about studying.

One day she was playing with a bubble. She watched it closely and studied how it floated in the air, wide and round. "This bubble is so pretty," she said.

Suddenly, the bubble floated away. The girl ran after it to try and catch it. It was so wide and she couldn't catch up. Suddenly the wind picked up and the bubble flew away.

The little girl was sad and started to cry. But then, she saw a rainbow in the sky. She smiled and studied it closely. She thought she could reach the rainbow if she flew on the back of a bird.

The end.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Jill. She had a favourite snack that she ate every day: toast with jam.

One morning, Jill woke up feeling a bit nervous. She was about to go to a new school. She took a deep breath and made some toast with jam.

When she spread the jam on her toast, she noticed something strange. It was not just strawberry jam, but something different. It was purple and it smelled yummy. It was blueberry jam!

Jill gasped and said, "This is such a tasty surprise!". 

Then she took a bite and smiled. The blueberry jam tasted delicious. She finished her toast and went to school feeling much better.

From that day onward, Jill began bringing blueberry jam to school every day.

Bobby was out in the garden, gazing at the trees. The leaves danced in the warm breeze and the sun was shining brilliantly. He felt so small amongst the giant trees.

He looked up and saw a bird perched in the branches, singing joyfully. Bobby felt a strong desire to join the bird, but he was too helpless to even try. He sighed sadly. 

Suddenly, his dad appeared beside him and gave him a hug. He said, "Don't feel helpless, Bobby. I promise I'll take you up there one day."
 
Bobby looked up at his dad with shining eyes. "Really?" he asked, still hopeful. His dad smiled and said with a gentle nod, "Yes, I promise." 

Bobby smiled and hugged his dad tightly. He'd never felt so happy and excited. In that moment, he knew that his dad's promise was one that he could always rely on.

Once there was a little girl. Her name was Anna.

She had green eyes and blonde hair. Every day she liked to play in the snow and go sledding. 

One very cold day, Anna went sledding. As she went sledding, she saw something shiny in the snow. She went over to see what it was. 

She picked it up and then saw that it was money. She was so excited! 

Anna ran to a nearby store to buy some hot chocolate. When she got there, the shopkeeper said, "That will be five dollars please."

Anna looked down at her money and saw that she only had four dollars. She said to the shopkeeper, "I'm sorry, I only have four dollars. Can I still have the hot chocolate?"

The shopkeeper smiled and said, "Sure you can! I think it's nice of you to offer me some of your icy cold money." Anna thanked him and then went on her way, with a big cup of nice warm hot chocolate!

Once there was a wise old man who had a lot of gas. He wanted to enjoy it, so he decided to take a drive one day. He drove to a wonderful park and enjoyed the nice view. He got out of his car and started to smell the beautiful flowers. He felt the sun on his face and he smiled.

The man walked around the park, enjoying the sights and smells. He heard the birds chirping and he saw the trees blowing in the wind. He spotted a squirrel and watched it scurry around.

The man went to a nearby lake and watched the fishes swimming around. He wondered if they enjoyed the water as much as he enjoyed it.

The wise old man finished his day feeling happy and content. He was thankful to have so much gas for his car. It allowed him to travel and enjoy the world around him.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to eat ice cream. One day, Timmy's mom gave him a teaspoon to eat his ice cream with. Timmy was very slow at eating his ice cream, but he enjoyed it very much.

After Timmy finished his ice cream, he went to play with his toys. But then, he accidentally knocked over a vase and it broke. Timmy was scared because he knew he did something wrong. He thought about lying and telling his mom that the vase broke on its own. But Timmy knew that lying was not good, so he told the truth and said he broke the vase.

Timmy's mom was proud of him for telling the truth, and she hugged him. She said it was okay and that accidents happen. From that day on, Timmy learned that it's always best to tell the truth and not to lie.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a lonely boy named Mark. He had a little case that he took with him everywhere. Inside the case, he had his favorite toys and snacks.

One day, Mark went to the park to play. Another boy saw Mark's case and wanted it. The boy tried to take the case away from Mark. Mark didn't want to give it away, so they both started to fight over the case.

A wise old man saw the fight and came to help. He told the boys to share the case and play together. Mark and the other boy listened to the old man. They started to play and share the case. Soon, they became good friends. The moral of the story is that sharing can bring people together and make friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved playing with her kitten, Mittens. Mittens was very small and cute. Lily always made sure that Mittens was safe and happy.

Susie was playing at the beach. She picked up a shell and held it in her hand. She could feel how smooth and hard it was and it looked so pretty. She thought it would be a great toy to play with.

Once upon a time, there was a young boy who wanted to explore the world around him. One day, he came across an old hut and wanted to explore inside. But when he tried to push the door open, it was locked. He looked around, but couldn't find the key anywhere.

Tom and Mia were twins who liked to play outside. One day, they saw a big building with many windows and colors. They wondered what was inside the building and how it was made.

"Let's go and see!" Tom said. He ran towards the building, but Mia stopped him.

"Wait, Tom! We don't know if we can go there. Maybe it's not safe. Maybe it's someone's home. Maybe they don't want us to see." Mia said. She was careful and smart.

Tom did not listen to Mia. He was curious and brave. He said, "Don't be scared, Mia. It's just a building. It looks brilliant. Maybe there are toys and games and candy inside. Come on, follow me!" He pulled Mia's hand and dragged her to the building.

They reached the door of the building and opened it. They saw a big hall with many people and machines and wires. They heard loud noises and saw bright lights. They were amazed and scared. They did not know what to do.

Suddenly, a man saw them and shouted, "Hey, you two! What are you doing here? This is a power plant. It's very dangerous. You could get hurt or cause a problem. Get out of here, now!"

Tom and Mia nodded. They said, "We understand, mom. We're sorry. We won't do it again. We learned our lesson."

They hugged their mom and each other. They learned that wonder is good, but not without wisdom. They learned that building is brilliant, but not without safety. They learned to be careful and smart, as well as curious and brave.
