The children said â€œYes mummyâ€ and very carefully, they picked it up. The vase felt soft to the touch and the children looked at each other and smiled.

The children continued to play in the garden and after a while, mummy called them for dinner. The children remembered the vase and quickly put it back where they had found it.

Once inside, mummy noticed the children had been careful and praised them for being so sensible. The children smiled, happy that they had remembered to put the vase back where it belonged.

Once upon a time there was a green field. There were a lot of animals living in it. One day a little rabbit noticed something strange in the middle of the field. It was a big, soft player. The rabbit hopped closer and saw that the player was filled with tiny white balls. 

The rabbit said: "Oh wow, what do you think is inside it?". 

Just then, a squirrel pranced around the corner. He had seen what was inside the player and he said: "I bet you can't guess, but it's something really fun". 

The rabbit's eyes lit up and he said: "Can we open it?". 

The squirrel giggled and said: "Yes! Go grab it and open it". 

The rabbit grabbed the soft player and opened it. Inside was a pile of delicious bright yellow fruit. The rabbit jumped up and cheered. He had never seen such a treat before! The rabbit and the squirrel shared the fruit and had a wonderful day playing in the green field.

Once upon a time, there was a small boy named Ted. He was three years old and he was very curious. One day, he asked his mom to keep a special promise. His mom said, "Sure! I'll keep this promise." Ted was so glad. He smiled and hugged his mom.

The promise was to take him to the park the next day. Ted knew that his mom never broke her promises, so he was very excited. The next day they went to the park and Ted was filled with joy. He played with his friends and he ran around. He made some new friends too!

At the end of the day, Ted's mom asked him if he had a good day. He said yes and gave her a big hug. He was so glad to have a mom who kept her promises. He knew that he could always count on her. Ted and his mom kept their special promise together and it filled their hearts with joy.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Hannah. She was three years old and she loved competitions. She was very competitive and wanted to always win.

Every day at noon, Hannah's mum took her to the park to play. On this special day Hannah wanted to succeed. She asked her mum if she could try to swing the highest on the swings. Her mum agreed and smiled.

So Hannah began to swing. She went higher and higher, almost as high as the trees! When the bell smelt 12 o'clock, she knew she had to try one more time. She pushed as hard as she could and eventually flew up into the sky!

Hannah had done it; she had succeeded! Her mum was so proud of her and they both celebrated with a big hug. From then on Hannah knew that with enough hard work and determination, she could achieve anything she set her mind to.

Once there was a blue bird named Bob. Bob seemed to like exercise. Every day, Bob would go out and fly around the tree in the backyard. All of the other birds watched Bob and thought it was very nice.

One day, Bob wanted to try to do something even more fun. He heard that some of the other animals did a special kind of exercise. So he hopped over to the garden to watch them. 

Bob saw a frog hopping up and down and a caterpillar spinning in circles. It all seemed very nice and Bob wanted to join them. So he began to flap his wings and fly as high as he could. 

The other animals watched Bob with a big smile. They thought it was wonderful that Bob wanted to exercise with them. He was having so much fun and everyone was happy. 

Bob was very proud of himself. From that day on, he always wanted to do that special exercise with his friends. It seemed like they were having the best time!

Once upon a time there was a sweet little girl named Daisy. She lived in a big house with her mom and dad. One day, Daisy heard a knock on the door. Her mom and dad said, â€œItâ€™s a stranger. Donâ€™t open the door!â€ Daisy was brave and opened the door anyways. Standing there was a serious man. He asked, â€œWhere is your mommy?â€ Daisy was scared, so she didnâ€™t answer. The man asked again and Daisy explained that her mommy was in the kitchen. The man thanked her and quickly walked away.

That night, Daisy asked her mom why the stranger was so serious. Her mom said, â€œHe probably had an important question and hoped for an answer.â€ Daisy thought about it for a second, then said, â€œThatâ€™s good. If a stranger needs an answer, I can help them find it.â€

One day, a young boy named Bob and his mom went to the beach. The sky was gloomy and a fog rolled in. Bob and his mom decided to build something special in the sand.

They got to work, and Bob was very excited - he loved building things with his mom. As they were building, strange things started to happen. The fog got thicker and darker. Bob was scared. 

But his mom was calm and said, "Don't worry Bob, I'll keep you safe." Finally, their building was finished and an amazing surprise was revealed. 

The fog had cleared, and a beautiful rainbow was revealed in the sky, with a pot of gold at the end. Everyone was so happy and the gloomy day was forgotten. 

Bob couldn't believe it - he thought the fog and gloominess had ruined the day, but instead it brought something even more magical. He loved spending time building with his mom, but he was even more grateful that it had brought him to this magical place.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny named Benny. Benny was very lively and loved to hop around all day long. One day, Benny was playing in the woods when he heard a loud noise. He turned around and saw a big, scary fox! The fox wanted to eat Benny for dinner.

Benny was very scared and knew he had to escape. He ran as fast as he could, hopping over rocks and through bushes. The fox chased him, but Benny was too quick. Finally, Benny found a small hole in a tree and squeezed inside, safe from the fox.

Benny was very happy to have escaped from the fox, but he was also very tired. He fell asleep inside the tree, dreaming of all the fun adventures he would have the next day. From that day on, Benny was always careful when playing in the woods, making sure to look out for any dangers lurking around.

Once upon a time there were two friends named Anna and Sam. They wanted to climb the tall mountain, but Anna was afraid. Sam tried to be nice to Anna and said the mountain was attractive. But Anna continued to complain.

Anna said the mountain was too big and she couldn't climb it. But Sam said they could do anything if they tried, so they started walking. The mountain seemed so tall and Anna complained the whole way up.

Eventually they reached the top. Anna looked around and it was nice and clear. They made it! 

But when they went to go back down, Anna started to complain again. She said the way down was too scary. Suddenly, they heard a loud rumble and the mountain started to shake. Big rocks started to fall and Anna screamed. 

They were both trapped on the mountain and Anna had to complain until the end. Unfortunately, neither of them survived the rockslide.

Once upon a time, a little boy wanted to make a cake for his mom's birthday. He went to the grocery with his dad and picked out the ingredients list given by his mom. 

In the kitchen, the little boy started mixing all the ingredients together to make the cake batter. He was so excited! 

But he made a mistake. He forgot to put in the sugar! It was too late, he thought. He felt really sad and his dad came over to comfort him. 

His dad said, "It's okay. We can still fix this! Let's go to the grocery and get some sugar. We'll be back soon!" 

So the two of them ran to the nearest grocery to buy some sugar. The little boy was so happy that he could finish the cake for his mom's birthday. 

At the grocery, the little boy found the sugar he needed and the dad bought it for him. They quickly ran back home and mixed the sugar into the cake batter. 

The little boy cheered with joy. He had made the perfect cake just in time! He kept the cake high and proudly took it to his mom.

Once there was a little girl who really wanted to go on the slides at the park. She asked her mom and dad if she could go but they said no. The little girl was very sad. 

She decided to have a plan to try and go on the slide even though her parents said no. She had an idea. She ate three bowls of oatmeal and went to the park. 

When she got to the park she ran to the slide. She felt very fit and strong. She ran up the stairs and looked down the slide. It was big but she thought she was big enough too. 

The little girl was very excited but then she heard her parents calling. She felt her stomach drop. She covered her ears and made her decision. She decided to go down the slide because she thought she was fit enough and she wanted to do it. 

So she went down the slide! She screamed the whole way and when she got to the bottom she was very proud of herself. The little girl knew that she made the right decision.

One day in summer, a little girl was walking down the road. She felt scared because it was very quiet and she couldn't see anyone else around. Suddenly, she heard a noise, and she looked up to see a big animal. The girl was really scared and she didn't know how to run away from it.

But then the girl noticed something. The animal looked kind of sad and it didn't look like it would hurt her. In fact, it was just a big kitty cat! The girl reached out and started petting the kitty cat, and it started purring. Suddenly, the girl wasn't scared anymore - she was happy.

From that day on, the girl and the kitty cat were best friends. Every summer, they would hang out in the same spot and the girl would always remember how the kitty cat wasn't scary - it was just looking for a friend.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play in the yard. They have a ball, a bike, and a doll.

One day, they see a bird in the yard. The bird is red and blue. It is pretty. Lily and Ben want to see the bird.

They go near the bird. They say, "Hello, bird. Do you want to play with us?" The bird looks at them. It says, "Tweet, tweet, tweet."

Lily and Ben laugh. They say, "You are funny, bird. What is your name?" The bird says, "Tweet, tweet, tweet."

Lily and Ben think. They say, "We will call you Tweet. You are our new friend, Tweet." The bird says, "Tweet, tweet, tweet."

They play with the bird. They throw the ball, ride the bike, and hug the doll. The bird flies and sings. They have fun in the yard. They are happy.

There was a big frog. He liked to hop all day. He hopped from side to side. He hopped up and down. He even hopped behind the big hill.

One day, the frog was hopping around the hill when he noticed something. He hopped closer and saw a small exit. It was broken. He hopped closer and hopped inside.

Inside the exit, the frog saw something special. There was a big jar with candy inside. The frog's eyes sparkled and he hopped over to it.

Just then, he heard a voice. 
"What are you doing in here?" it said.

The frog looked around and saw a small girl.

He said, "I wanted to see what was inside this exit. Is this your candy jar?"

The girl smiled and said, "Yes, it's my jar. Would you like to have some candy?"

The frog smiled and hopped over to the jar. He ate some of the sweet candy and thanked the girl.

Then, he hopped away and continued his hopping around the hill.

John was a busy little three-year-old. He loved to explore and asked lots of questions. One day, he asked his mom all about the ceiling. She told him that the ceiling was like an open lid on their home. She said that it owned the room, keeping them safe and sheltered.

John was so intrigued by the ceiling that he decided to give it a try himself. He slowly reached up and touched the open ceiling with his little hand. It felt strange and smooth! He giggled and laughed.

John's mom saw how excited he was about the ceiling and asked if he wanted to explore some more. He shouted out yes! So, she picked him up so he could see the ceiling from above.

John was in awe. He pointed out the lights and decorations on the ceiling. He also noticed how the ceiling was really big and how it owned the whole house!

After their exploration, John felt so happy. He had learned a lot about the ceiling and now he owned the knowledge.

Once upon a time there was a blue truck. The truck was so excited because it was going to be parked in a very special place.

The truck arrived at a park. It was a beautiful park and the truck had never seen anything like it. But something seemed strange. What was it?

The truck looked around and it soon found out what it was â€“ there was a tunnel at the other side of the park. It was a modest tunnel, not grand like the truck was used to seeing.

The truck was curious and it wanted to see what was in the tunnel. It gathered up some courage and it drove right up to the entrance.

Suddenly, the truck heard a voice. It was the voice of a little girl.

â€œCome in,â€ said the girl. â€œI know whatâ€™s inside and I want to show you!â€

So the truck followed the little girl into the tunnel. And when it stepped inside, it was amazed. It was filled with sparkling lights and colourful decorations. The truck felt like it had discovered a really special place.

The truck was so excited that it gave a gentle beep so that everyone could know how happy it was. The little girl smiled as the truck beeped, and the truck knew it had made a new friend.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play and share. One day, they find a big box of clay. They want to create something fun with the clay.

"I know!" Anna says. "Let's make lollipops with the clay. We can pretend to eat them and give them to our dolls."

"Good idea!" Ben says. "I like lollipops. They are sweet and colorful. I want to make a red one and a blue one."

They start to roll and shape the clay into lollipops. They stick them on sticks and decorate them with beads and glitter. They are very proud of their creations.

"Look at my lollipops!" Anna says. "They are so pretty. Do you want to try one?"

"Sure!" Ben says. He takes a bite of Anna's blue lollipop. But it is not sweet. It is hard and bitter. He spits it out and makes a face. "Yuck! This is not a lollipop. This is clay. It tastes bad and it hurts my teeth."

"I'm sorry, Ben!" Anna says. "I forgot that clay is not food. It is only for playing. Are you okay?"

Ben nods. He is not happy, but he is not angry. He knows that Anna did not mean to hurt him. He is still her friend.

"It's okay, Anna." He says. "Let's not eat the clay lollipops. Let's give them to our dolls. Maybe they will like them."

"Okay." Anna says. She smiles and hugs Ben. "You are a good friend, Ben. Thank you for playing with me."

They give the clay lollipops to their dolls and play with them. They have fun and forget about the bad taste. They are happy.

Once upon a time there was a very fragile bird. She lived in a lovely tree in the woods. Every day she went out and searched for tasty bugs.

But one day a big scary cat leapt out of the bushes and tried to grab her. She flew away as fast as she could and wasn't caught, but she dropped some of the bugs she was carrying. 

The fallen bugs became waste that was spread around the forest. The poor fragile bird was very sad that the yummy bugs were now waste.

So she worked hard to pick up all of the waste and put it back in the tree. Now every day the bird can eat all of the tasty bugs she can find, without having to worry about the big scary cat!

Once upon a time there was a girl named Anna. Anna was excited because it was her birthday. Her mummy had given her a beautiful wardrobe for her bedroom. She filled it with all sorts of colourful clothes.

Every morning she enjoyed dressing up in her new clothes. She had a pair of trousers with flowers, a dress with stars, and a pretty shirt with spots. She looked in the mirror and smiled.

Anna loved her wardrobe and always enjoyed playing dress up. When her friends came over she showed them her wardrobe and they all laughed and yelled with excitement. 

One day, Anna and her friends decided to have a dress up party. They put on the most creative outfits and twirled around in circles. At the end of the party, they all drifted off into the sunset, feeling happy and content.

Anna and Ben were going on a trip with their grandma. They were very happy to see new places and have fun. But they hated to pack their luggage. They had to put their clothes, toys, books and snacks in big bags. It was hard to close them and carry them.

"Anna, Ben, hurry up! We have to go to the airport soon!" Grandma called from downstairs. She was elderly and had a cane. She could not help them with their luggage.

"Grandma, we are almost done!" Anna shouted back. She tried to zip her bag, but it was too full. She looked at Ben. He was sitting on his bag, hoping to make it smaller.

"Ben, you can't take all your cars and trucks. You have to leave some at home. There is no space in your bag!" Anna said.

"But I love them! I want to play with them on the trip!" Ben said. He did not want to give up his toys.

"Ben, please. We have to go. Grandma is waiting. And you can play with other things on the trip. Maybe you can see real cars and trucks!" Anna said. She took some of his toys and put them in a box.

"No, no, no! Give them back! They are mine!" Ben cried. He grabbed the box and pulled it. Anna pulled it too. They started to fight.

"Anna! Ben! Stop it! What are you doing?" Grandma came upstairs. She saw them fighting over the box. She was angry and sad.

"Grandma, Ben is being selfish! He wants to take all his toys and there is no room in his bag!" Anna said.

"Grandma, Anna is being mean! She wants to take away my toys and I love them!" Ben said.

"Anna, Ben, listen to me. You are both being silly. You can't take everything you want on the trip. You have to share and be nice. And you have to respect your luggage. It is not a toy. It is for your things. If you break it or lose it, you will have trouble. Do you understand?" Grandma said.

Anna and Ben looked at each other. They felt sorry for fighting. They nodded.

"Yes, Grandma. We understand. We are sorry." They said.

"Good. Now, let's pack your luggage properly. And then, let's go and have a wonderful trip!" Grandma said. She smiled and hugged them. Anna and Ben smiled too. They hugged her back. They did not hate their luggage anymore. They loved their grandma.

Once there was a little girl called Polly. She wanted to play with all the other children but she felt very embarrassed. She was the only one who couldn't stand up.

But then something very exciting happened. Grandpa bought some special equipment for her. It was a special chair that helped her stand up.

Polly felt so proud and happy. She cried with delight when she was finally able to stand and join in the fun with all the other children.

Everyone clapped as Polly stood and played together with her friends. They all learned the importance of helping each other and never giving up no matter what.

Polly and the other children had so much fun together. She was so proud of the special equipment that made it all possible.

Once upon a time there was a little goat who liked to be independent. The goat liked to take adventures on their own and not rely on anyone for help. The goat loved exploring and meeting new friends. 

One day, the goat gathered enough courage to go on a great adventure. The goat went far from its home and into a new and exciting place. The goat found all sorts of new things, from bright colored flowers to delicious looking fruit. 

The goat kept exploring and gathering until it had a big pile of items. The goat felt big and happy with all of their new things as they gathered for their journey back home. 

Finally, the little goat made it home. All of its friends were so excited to see the goat, and to hear all of their adventures. All of the goats were so proud of their brave and independent friend. 

The little goat was happy to be home safe and sound and to show off all of its gathered treasures.

Once upon a time, there was a big bird. The bird had big wings and could fly very high. One day, the bird flew to a place where it was winter. The snow was very cold and the bird felt chilly. The bird decided to fly back to where it was warm.

Once upon a time, there was an adorable little puppy who lived with its family in a cozy home. He always loved to explore the house and play with everyone. One day, the puppy noticed something really interesting near the kitchen: an oven. 

The puppy bounded over to the oven and started jumping around excitedly. He was fascinated by the sight of the oven and was determined to get inside it.

The puppy's mom noticed her little pup and smiled. "Oh my, what are you up to little one?" she asked.

The puppy responded with a bark and kept jumping around the oven. 

The mom laughed and said, "Oh, it looks like you really want to see what's inside the oven! Well, don't worry, I'll have it open soon enough." 

The mom opened the oven and the puppy was so excited to see what was in there! He jumped around, sniffing and exploring. As the puppy scampered around, the mom could not help but smile at his adorable antics. 

The puppy explored the oven, making sure to use only his nose of course! He was so happy to have seen the inside of the oven and soon went back to playing with his family. 

The End.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved pumpkins. He liked to pick them from the garden and play with them. One day, Timmy had a big pumpkin he wanted to carve. But it was messy work and he didn't want to do it alone.

His friend, Sally, came over to help him. They took turns scooping out the pumpkin guts and making silly faces. When they finished, they had a pumpkin that looked like a funny monster. Timmy was so happy, he shouted, "I win!" Sally laughed and said, "No, we both win because we had fun together."

Once upon a time, there was a brave little bunny named Benny. Benny loved to play outside in the sunshine, but he was afraid of the dark night. One night, Benny's mom asked him to go to bed early. Benny didn't want to go to bed early because he wanted to play more. He complained to his mom, but she said it was time for bed.

Benny went to bed, but he was scared of the dark. He heard a noise outside and got even more scared. He started to cry and complain to his mom. His mom came to his room and told him that everything was okay, and that she was there to protect him. Benny felt better and went back to sleep.

The next day, Benny was proud of himself for being brave. He realized that he didn't have to be scared of the dark because his mom was always there to protect him. Benny learned that even though he didn't like going to bed early, it was important to get enough sleep so that he could be strong and brave like his mom.

One winter day, Jack and his mom were going to celebrate his third birthday. He was so excited he put on his mittens and went outside to play in the snow. 
Jack found a friend there and they started playing together. His mom was watching from afar, feeling happy and generous. Suddenly, the friend stumbled and the mitten slipped off Jack's hand. 
Jack said to his mom: "Mommy, my mitten is gone!" She quickly replied: "It's okay. Let's find it!" He looked everywhere but couldn't find it anywhere. 
His mom then said: "I'm sorry, Jack. We'll have to say goodbye to your mitten. Let's be generous and give a sincere wish for whoever finds it." 
Jack was sad, but they both celebrated his birthday, even though he had no mitten. Jack learned the importance of being generous and wishing the best to the ones you hold dear.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved to explore. She was very curious and excited to find out what she would discover.

One day, she found a box with a colorful mask inside. She was amazed by its shiny colors and wanted to take it home. She held the mask close to her chest and the box too.

The girl was about to lift the box when she heard a noise coming from the corner of the room. She looked over and saw a smiling cat wearing the same mask she had found. The girl was so excited and wanted to give it try.

The girl immediately put on the mask and skipped over to the cat. The cat seemed happy to see her wearing the same colorful mask.

The girl lifted the box and brought it back home. She showed her mom and dad the mask, and they were both happy to see it.

The little girl and the cat wore the colorful masks in many adventures to come. The masks were always a reminder to the little girl of how much fun it is to explore and make new discoveries.

Once there was an elderly man. He was sitting in a chair in the park, enjoying the sun.

Suddenly, a child ran up from out of nowhere. She threw her arms up into the air and yelled, "I'm gonna throw this chair!" She grabbed the chair from the elderly man and pulled it back, ready to throw it!

"No! Stop!" the elderly man yelled, quickly standing up.

But the child didn't listen. She threw the chair as far as she could and it went sailing across the park.

The elderly man laughed and said, "That was a pretty good throw."

The child was proud and smiled. She ran back to the elderly man and hugged him. "Thank you," she said.

The elderly man nodded and said, "You are very welcome."

Jeff was a 3 year old who loved playing hide and seek. One day he was playing and he noticed something unknown behind the couch. Jeff was very curious, so he decided to explore. 

When he peeked behind the couch he noticed that his room was full of water. He had no idea why his room was wet and he was very scared. Jeff quickly realized that he was in trouble.

He started thinking of ways he could dry the room. Then Jeff remembered that his parents had a big fan which he could use. So he grabbed the fan and started blowing the water out of the room.

After a few minutes, Jeff was able to dry the room and make it safe. He was happy he could help and he felt like a big hero. He settled onto the couch and took a nap. He had never seen such big trouble and he was proud of himself for figuring out a solution.

Tom and Anna were playing in the park. They liked to run and slide on the grass. They had a lot of fun. But then they saw a big puddle. It was shiny and wet.

"Let's jump in it!" Tom said. He ran towards the puddle.

"No, Tom, don't!" Anna said. She was scared. She had a bad memory of slipping in a puddle and hurting her knee. She did not want Tom to get hurt too.

But Tom did not listen. He jumped in the puddle with a splash. He laughed and splashed some more. He did not see the rock in the puddle. He stepped on it and slipped. He fell down and hit his head. He cried out loud.

Anna ran to him. She was sorry and worried. She hugged him and said, "I'm sorry, Tom. Are you okay?"

Tom was not okay. He had a big bump on his head. It hurt a lot. He was angry and sad. He said, "Why did you let me jump in the puddle? You are a bad friend!"

Anna was hurt by his words. She said, "I tried to stop you, Tom. I was afraid you would slip. I have a memory of slipping in a puddle and it was not fun. I wanted you to be safe and happy."

Tom looked at her. He saw her tears and her band-aid on her knee. He remembered how she had slipped in a puddle and how he had helped her. He felt sorry and ashamed. He said, "I'm sorry, Anna. You are a good friend. I was not careful. I should have listened to you."

Anna smiled and said, "It's okay, Tom. I forgive you. Let's go to the nurse and get some ice for your bump. Then we can play something else."

They held hands and walked to the nurse. They were still friends. They felt peaceful and glad. They learned to be more careful and to listen to each other. They had a good memory of playing in the park.

Lily liked to go to class with her friends. She learned new things and played fun games. She had a teacher who was nice and reliable. He always helped her when she was stuck or sad.

One day, Lily woke up and felt sick. She had a fever and a sore throat. She could not go to class. She was sad and cried. She wanted to see her friends and her teacher. She asked her mom if she could call them.

Her mom said no. She said Lily had to rest and drink water. She said Lily could call them when she felt better. Lily was angry and threw her pillow. She did not want to rest. She wanted to go to class.

She did not listen to her mom. She sneaked out of her room and found her phone. She called her teacher. She hoped he would make her feel better. She said hello and told him she was sick.

But the teacher did not say hello back. He did not sound nice and reliable. He sounded angry and mean. He said Lily was naughty and rude. He said she should not call him. He said he did not want to talk to her. He said he had a new favorite student. He said he did not like Lily anymore. He hung up the phone.

Lily was shocked and hurt. She could not believe what he said. She felt worse than before. She dropped the phone and ran back to her room. She cried and cried. She wished she had listened to her mom. She wished she could forget what he said. She wished she could remember the good times with her teacher. But she could not. She had a bad day. She had a bad ending.

Once upon a time, there was a chubby rabbit named Bun. Bun loved to eat grapes. One day, Bun went to the grape field to eat some grapes. But then, a big bird came and wanted to eat Bun. "I will protect you, Bun!" said a kind mouse. The mouse jumped on the bird and the bird flew away. "Thank you!" said Bun, feeling safe. 

But then, a big and mean fox came. "I want to eat you, Bun!" said the fox. "I will protect you, Bun!" said the mouse bravely. But the fox was too strong and he ate both Bun and the mouse. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a hunter. He was walking through the woods, when suddenly he heard a splash. He looked around, but he couldn't see anyone. So he kept walking until he saw a lake. The lake was empty. It looked so still and peaceful. 

The hunter walked closer and closer to the lake. Then he heard another splash! He was sure something was in the lake. So the hunter crept closer and closer until he could see it. 

It was a frog! The frog was swimming around in the lake, splashing and playing. The hunter was surprised to see a frog so far away from home. He decided to take it with him and keep it as a pet. 

The hunter scooped up the little frog and brought it home. From that day onwards, the hunter and the frog were the best of friends. They would go for walks in the woods and splash in the lake. 

The End.

Once upon a time, there was a fierce dog named Max. Max lived with his family in a small house. They loved him very much. One day, Max saw his family pack things in big bags. They were going on a trip!

Max wanted to help. He went to the kitchen and saw his mom put things in the dishwasher. "Can I help?" asked Max. His mom said, "Yes, you can put the cups in the dishwasher." Max was happy to help his family.

When they finished, they all went on the trip. Max and his family had a great time. They played and laughed together. Max was happy that he helped his family pack and with the dishwasher. They all loved their trip and Max was a very good dog.

Once upon a time, there were two friends, Jack and Susie. Jack had a big, warm, cozy sweater, which he wore every day. Susie was so envious of Jack's sweater, so one day, she asked him:

Susie: "Jack, can I have your sweater?"

Jack: "No, I like my sweater very much. Why don't you make your own?"

Susie thought of a great idea. She found wool and needles and started to make her own sweater. She tried and tried, and with Jack's help she improved it little by little. 

At last, Susie had herself a very nice sweater, which Jack thought looked even better than his. Susie was so happy and Jack was so proud of her!

The End

Once upon a time, there was a mighty stream. It was the biggest and the strongest stream around. Everyone who lived near it loved it and played in it every day. One day, a little boy named Andy wanted to join in the fun.

He had never been in a stream before, so he was a bit scared. He asked his mom, "Please can I go in the stream?" His mom said yes, and gave him a big smile.

Andy was so excited! He put on his water shoes and went down to the stream. He was amazed by the power of the mighty stream. He felt small, but was so happy to be there.

Andy splashed and played for hours. He laughed with joy and thanked his mom for helping him have such a fun day.

At the end of the day, Andy decided the stream was his new favorite place. He said to the stream, "Thank you for being so mighty! Please let me come back soon." 

The stream seemed to whisper back, "You're welcome! Come back soon." And Andy did.

Once there was a little boy. He was three years old, and his name was Tom. Tom had a favourite toy - a brown teddy bear. One day, Tom had a special treat. His mummy bought him a small purple ball. Tom was so excited!

Tom took the purple ball outside to play. He rolled the ball around and chased it, giggling with delight. But then, he accidentally dropped the ball in a mud puddle. Tom's face fell.

Mummy came out to check on Tom. Tears were streaming down his face.
"Oh, dear," said Mummy. "It looks like your purple ball is starting to rot. I'm sorry, sweetheart."
Tom didn't understand. He just knew that his ball was broken. 

Mummy looked around for something else for Tom to play with. And then, she spotted Tom's brown teddy bear. 
"Look, Tom," she said. "There's your bear. He's still in good condition. You can play with him today."
Tom smiled, and hugged the teddy bear close. He was happy again. 

The End.

Once there was a little boy called Jack. His mommy asked him what he wanted for lunch and he said, "melon!"

Jack's mommy took him to the market and they saw a wide melon. It was so big and round. Jack was so excited that he reached out to grab it.

"No, no Jack," his mommy said. "We need to ask if we can have it first."

At the market Jack saw a man who sold the melon. He asked the man, "Can I have the melon please?"

The man looked at Jack and smiled. He said, "Yes, sure. I will allow you to have the melon."

So Jack and his mommy took the wide melon home and shared it for lunch. It tasted so sweet and Jack was so happy he had been allowed to have it.

Once upon a time there was a girl. She was very happy and always smiled. But one day she began to miss her lip.

Her lip was very soft and brought her lots of joy. Her smile was now sad and lonely without it.

So the girl tried very hard to find her lip. She looked up and down, but it was nowhere to be found. She asked everyone she knew, but no one had seen it. 

It was so difficult for the girl to not have her lip. She cried and searched and searched, but she never found it.

The girl never did find her lip, but she learned an important lesson. With a smile, she realised even without her lip she was still as happy as before.

Once upon a time, there was a tall giraffe named Gerry. Gerry loved to listen to music and would always smile when he heard a good song. One day, Gerry was walking in the jungle when he saw a small monkey crying.

"What's wrong?" Gerry asked.

"I lost my banana," the monkey replied sadly.

"Don't worry, I'll help you find it," Gerry said with a smile.

Gerry and the monkey searched high and low, but they couldn't find the banana. Just when they were about to give up, they heard some music playing in the distance. They followed the sound and found a group of animals having a party. And there, on the table, was the monkey's banana!

The moral of the story is that if you help others, good things will happen to you too. And always remember to smile and enjoy the music!

Once upon a time, there was a little bird. Every day, the bird went to deliver a pretty pastel to all its friends. But one day, it was not a normal day. The bird had to deliver a special present! It was exciting! The bird flew to all of its friends and finally, each one had their special present. After that, it was back to normal and the bird gave out pretty pastel to all its friends. The bird was happy, and so were all the other animals. They all had something special to remember this day!

Once upon a time there was a bear. It was a safe bear, which meant that it was not a scary bear. Every morning, the bear's favorite thing to do was to go out into the forest and taste the sweet honey. 

So the bear would meander through the tall trees and look for the sweetest honey. But the bear had a problem. Other animals in the forest wanted to steal his honey! 

One day, the bear found a hidden spot deep in the forest. When he reached the spot, there was already a pot of honey waiting for him. It was the sweetest honey he had ever tasted. 

The bear stayed in the secret spot and enjoyed his new found honey every day. He was so happy and because he was safe, he didn't have to worry about anyone taking his sweet honey away.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and her friends. One day, she went to the park and met a boy named Jack. Jack had a weird hat on his head.

Lily said, "Hi Jack, that's a weird hat. Where did you get it?"

Jack said, "My mom got it for me. Do you want to play with me?"

Lily said, "Sure! What do you want to play?"

Jack said, "Let's play with our toy cars. I have a red one and a blue one."

Lily said, "I have a yellow one and a green one. How do we play?"

Jack said, "We can race them on this path. I'll manage the red one and the blue one, and you can manage the yellow one and the green one."

Lily said, "Okay, let's race!" And they had lots of fun playing together. After they finished playing, they exchanged phone numbers and became friends in their network of friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to travel with her family to different countries. But one day, her mommy realized that Lily's passport was missing. 

Mommy said, "Oh no! We can't go on our trip without your passport. It's very important to have it."

Lily said, "What can we do?"

Daddy recommended that they go to the passport office to get a new one. So, they went to the passport office and got a new passport for Lily. 

Now, they could go on their trip and have lots of fun adventures together!

Once upon a time, there was a poor shark swimming in the ocean. He was very sad because he did not have any friends to play with. Then one day, he saw a fish swimming towards him. "Hello!" said the fish. "What's wrong?"

The shark replied, "I have no one to share the ocean with."

The fish smiled and said, "I can be your friend. Let's share the ocean together."

The shark was so happy! He and the fish swam around the ocean, playing together and having lots of fun. They became the best of friends, and they shared everything.

And they lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time there was a pirate who went on a big adventure. He took his boat out to sea and set off in search of treasure. 

As the day passed, he sailed from one island to the next, but there was nothing to be found. The pirate soon grew tired and weary. 

Suddenly, a voice called out from the deep depths of the ocean: "Take me with you and I will show you the way to find treasure!" 

The pirate was surprised but he felt it was worth a try. He asked the voice: "What's your name?" 

The voice replied: "I'm a mermaid! And my name is Mimi!" 

The pirate was hesitant but decided to take Mimi with him. She guided him to a hidden cove and when his boat came to a stop there was the biggest pile of treasure he has ever seen! 

The pirate was so happy he shouted out in excitement. Mimi was happy too and said: "Well done! You did a fine job. And now, the treasure is yours." 
The pirate was thrilled and thanked Mimi for helping him find the treasure. He waved goodbye and sailed away with his boat full of riches.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Max. Max loved to play baseball with his friends. One day, Max's friend asked him if he wanted to play baseball with him. Max said, "Yes, I want to play baseball with you!" Max's friend said, "Okay, but do you have a reliable bat?" Max didn't know what reliable meant, so he asked his friend. His friend said, "A reliable bat means it won't break easily." Max shrugged and said, "I don't know, let's go ask my dad." Max's dad gave him a reliable bat to use and Max was very happy. They played baseball all day and had a lot of fun. The end.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Priscilla. She was three years old and loved to play outside. One day, while playing in her garden, she found an odd looking squash in a bush. She was curious and wanted to take a closer look, so she picked it up.

But before she knew it, something strange started happening. The squash began to sparkle and suddenly it started to grow bigger. Priscilla was scared so she started to cry.

The squash then said with a raspy voice, â€œStop crying and dress me up!â€

Priscilla was too scared to do anything so she stayed in place. But the squash started to grow bigger and brighter, so she ran inside the house and locked the door.

The squash kept growing until it was the same size as Priscilla. It started knocking on the door, asking to be dressed up. Priscilla was too scared to answer, so the squash eventually went away, never to be seen again.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a puppy who lived with a family. The puppy was happy, but one day there was a loud noise outside. The puppy was scared, so it ran and hid. The family looked outside and saw police. Suddenly, they all got very worried.

The police were looking for something. The family prayed that they would not find it. The puppy prayed too, even though it didn't know why.

The police found what they were looking for and left. Everyone was relieved and hugged their puppy. They all thanked God for keeping them safe.

The family learned that when we are scared, if we pray and have faith, everything will be okay. They all promised to pray whenever they were scared. The End.

Tim and Sam are friends. They like to play in the park. There is a big slide in the park. Tim and Sam want to go on the slide.

But there is a problem. There is a big rock on the slide. The rock is thick and heavy. It blocks the way. Tim and Sam cannot go on the slide.

"Who put the rock on the slide?" Tim asks. "That is not nice."

"Maybe we can move the rock," Sam says. "Let us try."

Tim and Sam push the rock. They push hard. But the rock does not move. It is too thick and heavy. Tim and Sam are sad. They cannot go on the slide.

Then they see a girl. The girl is Lily. Lily is nice. She likes to help. She sees Tim and Sam. She sees the rock on the slide.

"Hello, Tim and Sam," Lily says. "Do you need help?"

"Yes, please," Tim and Sam say. "There is a big rock on the slide. We cannot move it. We cannot go on the slide."

Lily has an idea. She has a rope. The rope is long and strong. She ties the rope to the rock. She pulls the rope. She pulls hard. The rock moves. It slides off the slide. The slide is clear.

"Yay, Lily!" Tim and Sam say. "You are smart and kind. You helped us. Thank you."

"You are welcome," Lily says. "Now we can all go on the slide. Let us have fun."

Tim, Sam and Lily go on the slide. They slide down. They laugh. They are happy. They are friends.

The moral of the story is: Helping others is good. It makes everyone happy. Friends work together. Friends have fun.

Once, there was a little girl who loved to go to the playground. She would smile and laugh as she swung on the swing. One day, she happily went to the playground again.

However, when she got there, she saw that part of the playground was being repaired. Her smile turned downward and she began to complain. "That's not fair!" she said, pointing to the side that was being fixed.

The playground attendant came over to explain that the side was broken and he was fixing it. But the little girl was not happy. She kept complaining and the attendant gave her an idea.

He said that if she could build something on the other side that was just as hard to break, maybe he could leave the broken side alone. The girl was excited by the challenge and immediately got to work.

She gathered wood, she hammered nails and soon, she had built a sturdy fence. When the attendant saw it, he was astonished. He praised her for her hard work, and declared that the side didn't need to be repaired after all.

The little girl was thrilled! She smiled and laughed as she played on both sides of the fence. From then on, she was known as the girl who never stopped trying.

Once upon a time there was a little dog. His name was Spot. Spot wanted to go for a run, but he couldn't find a track anywhere. He looked around and shrugged. He didn't know what else to do.

Suddenly, he saw a track in the distance and he was excited! He ran as fast as he could and when he arrived, he noticed it was a really hard track. He tried to run on it but it was so slippery and bumpy. Spot felt so frustrated.

He really wanted to go for a run, but he couldn't do it on this track. He stood there and shrugged. He was so disappointed.

Suddenly, he had an idea. He found some leaves and put them on the track. It made it much softer and more comfortable. Spot jumped for joy! He was so happy he was able to make the track less hard.

He ran and ran and had so much fun! When he got tired, he ran back to his house with a big smile on his face. From then on, he always made sure to make the track softer before his runs.

Once upon a time, there was a bald man who liked to dive. He lived near a big bridge. Every day, he would go to the bridge and look at the water. He wanted to dive into the water from the bridge, but he was scared.

One day, the bald man saw a little bird dive into the water from the bridge. The bird looked happy and had so much fun. The bald man thought, "If the little bird can do it, I can do it too!" So, he decided to dive from the bridge the next day.

The next day, the bald man went to the bridge. He was very excited and a little scared. He looked at the water and thought of the little bird. He took a deep breath and jumped. But the bald man didn't know how to dive well, and he got hurt. He should have learned to dive safely before trying to jump from the bridge.

Once upon a time there was a red truck. The truck was very old but it had a silver shell. One day the truck went for a drive.

As the truck drove along, it passed a field of cows. The cows were all grazing in the red grass. Suddenly the truck noticed something special in the field.

The truck stopped and its driver shouted: "What's that? Load it up, quick!" 

The driver was talking about a big silver box. It was very heavy, so the driver and the truck had to work together to load it. Finally, the box was load and the truck drove off with it.

Nobody knows what was inside that silver box, but they do know that it was very special!

Once upon a time there was a princess who lived in a castle. The princess had long, delicate hair and wore a sparkling crown. One day the princess found a small pin on the ground. She picked it up and looked at it closely.

The princess shrugged. She wasn't sure what the pin was for, but it looked so delicate and special. She wanted to find out what the pin was for and what she could do with it.

So, the princess set off on a journey. She asked everyone she met if they knew what the pin was for. Nobody knew.

Finally, the princes reached the edge of a large field and saw a small girl playing with a kite. She had a pin in her hand. The princess asked the girl what she was doing and the girl said she was using the pin to make a hole in the kite so she could fly it.

The princess smiled and thanked the girl. She was glad she had found out the purpose of the pin. She hugged the girl and walked home, content that she had discovered the pin's secret.

Jim was a three year old boy with a big backyard. He liked to spend hours playing in the yard. Every morning, Jim would jump out of bed, eager to get to the yard.

Today he decided to do something special. He stood at the entrance of the yard and looked around. It seemed very interesting. He saw some colorful flowers, tall grass and some big trees. He couldn't wait to explore it all.

He ran around and saw so many things. He especially loved the pond and the swings. Jim stood in the middle of the yard admiring it all. It was the most interesting place he had ever seen.

Jim spent many days exploring his backyard. He loved the adventures he discovered and the stories he made up. He often stood in the yard and admired its beauty. Jim's backyard was his favorite place.

Once upon a time, there was a rod that was very big and strong. It was an enormous rod and it had a special name. Everyone called it "Super Rod". Super Rod was so strong that it could lift anything. All the children wanted to try Super Rod and see what it could do. 

One day, a little 3 year old boy named Robbie heard about Super Rod and wanted to try it. He asked his mom if could lift it, and she said yes. 

So, Robbie and his mom went to go find Super Rod. When they arrived, they saw that it was even bigger and more powerful in real life. Robbie was very excited and he asked his mom if he could try it. She said yes and began to help him. 

Robbie was able to move Super Rod! He was so proud of himself. He felt happy and strong. The other children were amazed that he could lift such an enormous rod. From then on, everyone knew the 3 year old boy as Super Robbie.

Once upon a time there was a famous tower. It was big and tall and everyone wanted to see it. But nobody could enter the tower, and nobody knew what was inside.

One day, while everyone was walking around admiring the tower, a small bug appeared. The bug revealed a secret door right at the bottom of the tower. Everyone was amazed!

So the people all filed inside to see what was there. When they opened the door, they saw a huge surprise. Inside the tower were lots of delicious treats. Everyone was so happy. There were also lots of fun games and toys to play with.

The people had such a great time at the tower that it became even more famous. Everyone started talking about the amazing tower and all the fun things inside. They all spread the secret and the famous tower was loved by people for a long time.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her soft teddy bear and go on adventures. One day, Lily and her mommy went to the lake to row a boat. They had so much fun rowing and looking at the fish in the water.

After they finished rowing, Lily wanted to go on another adventure. She saw a big tree and wanted to climb it. But her mommy said it was too dangerous and they should go home. Lily was sad but listened to her mommy.

On the way home, they saw a big dog. Lily wanted to pet the dog but her mommy said it was not safe. The dog was not friendly and might bite her. Lily listened to her mommy and did not use her hand to pet the dog.

When they got home, Lily was happy to see her daddy. But he was not feeling well. He had a fever and was very sick. Lily's mommy called the doctor but it was too late. Daddy passed away and Lily was very sad. She hugged her soft teddy bear and cried.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play on her couch all day long. One day, her mom told her that she could not play on the couch anymore because it was getting dull. Lily was very sad and started to cry.

Her mom saw how sad she was and asked her, "Why are you crying, Lily?" Lily replied, "I want to play on the couch, but you don't permit me to." Her mom smiled and said, "I didn't say you can't play on the couch, Lily. I just said it's getting dull. Let's make it fun again!"

Lily was very happy and helped her mom decorate the couch with colorful pillows and blankets. Now, the couch was not dull anymore and Lily could play on it all day long. She hugged her mom and said, "Thank you for permitting me to play on the couch again!"

Once there was a little girl who was very fearful. One night she heard a loud noise coming from her bedroom. It sounded like something was inside her room. She didn't want to look, but she was very curious. So she slowly opened her bedroom door and peeked in.

Inside she saw a big, scary computer. It was making strange noises and flashing all sorts of colors. The little girl was so scared, she quickly shut the door and ran into her mom's room.

Her mom hugged her tightly and asked her what was wrong. The little girl told her mom about the scary computer, and her mom said it must just be a dream.

So, the little girl and her mom snuggled together and went back to sleep. The next morning, when the little girl opened her bedroom door, the computer was gone. She smiled, relieved that it was all just a dream.

Once there was a boy. He liked to throw things. Especially rice. He loved to toss it in the air and watch it fall back down. One day he decided to throw the rice into a pond. But the pond was sour! It ruined the rice. The boy was very upset. He had destroyed all of the rice. There was nothing he could do and he never threw rice into a pond again.

Once upon a time, there were two friends. One was a car and one was a plane. The car was so excited to go on an adventure with the plane.

The plane was all ready to zoom off, its wings wide and ready for flight. The car tooted its horn and its tires were ready to roll. They both went off to explore the world.

The car and the plane zoomed through the countryside. They passed by a river, where the plane dipped its wings close to the water. The car followed closely behind.

At last, they arrived at a tall hill. The plane flew up high and then tip-toed down the other side. The car followed and it was so much fun! They laughed and played all the way home.

They arrived back safe and sound with lots of fun stories to share. They'd had a great adventure, and were both ready for the next one!

Once upon a time, a girl named Sarah wanted to go on an adventure. She asked her mom if she could go. Mom said yes, but told Sarah to make a promise not to get lost.

Sarah promised and then set off on a journey. It was a bit scary but she was brave. As she went, she saw a magic wand. She picked it up, and suddenly, things changed. 

The forest lit up and Sarah could see a talking bird perched on a tree branch. Sarah was so excited and a little bit scared.

The bird said, "I can show you some really cool magic, if you promise to return the wand when you're done."

So Sarah promised and the bird waved its wand and suddenly, Sarah was spinning in circles in mid-air, up and up and up! When she got her breath back, she thanked the bird who nodded and said, "You kept your promise so I kept mine - that was some cool magic!"

Sarah hugged the bird and then put the magic wand back where she found it. She went home happy and excited about her magical adventure.

Once upon a time, there was a cat and a dog. The cat liked to joke a lot. The dog liked to read the newspaper. One day, the cat found an interesting newspaper. The cat wanted to joke with the dog about the newspaper.

The cat said, "Look, dog! This newspaper says cats can fly!" The dog looked at the cat and said, "You are joking, cat. Cats cannot fly." The cat laughed and said, "You are right, dog. I was joking."

The dog smiled and said, "It is good to joke, but we must tell the truth too." The cat and the dog learned that it is fun to joke, but it is important to be honest. They both read the interesting newspaper and had a fun day together.

Lily liked to design things. She had many crayons and papers and stickers. She liked to make pictures of flowers and animals and houses. She also liked to help her mom in the kitchen. She wanted to design something for her mom.

She found a white apron in the drawer. She thought it was too plain. She wanted to make it more pretty. She took some crayons and stickers and started to draw and stick on the apron. She made a big heart and wrote "I love mom" inside. She also made some stars and rainbows and butterflies.

She was very proud of her design. She wanted to show it to her mom. She put on the apron and ran to the living room. She saw her mom sitting on the couch, reading a book. She said, "Mom, look what I made for you!"

Her mom looked up and smiled. She saw the colorful apron on Lily. She said, "Wow, Lily, that's a beautiful apron! Did you design it yourself?"

Lily nodded and hugged her mom. She said, "Yes, mom, I did. I wanted to make you happy. Do you like it?"

Her mom hugged her back and kissed her cheek. She said, "I love it, Lily. And I love you more. You are very creative and sweet. Thank you for this wonderful gift."

Lily felt very happy. She said, "You're welcome, mom. I'm glad you like it. Can we wear it together when we cook?"

Her mom said, "Of course, we can. Let's go to the kitchen and make some cookies. You can help me with the dough and the shapes."

Lily and her mom went to the kitchen, wearing the apron. They had fun making and baking cookies. They shared them with dad and brother when they came home. They all said the apron was very pretty and the cookies were very yummy. Lily felt very proud and loved. She thought her mom was the best mom in the world. She thought her design was the best design in the world.

Once upon a time, there was a wealthy man who had lots of money and a great life. Every day, he would eat lots of delicious food to keep him strong and healthy.

One day, the wealthy man needed to make a special phone call, so he went to get his cell. He took it out of his pocket and he started dialing the number. Then, he put it to his ear and waited to hear the voice he had been longing to hear.

But something strange happened. As he was talking, the cell started getting bigger and bigger. In amazement, the wealthy man watched as the cell became a big pie. Then, he knew just what to do.

He quickly grabbed a spoon and started eating the pie. It was delicious. From that day on, the wealthy man always kept an extra pie on hand just in case he ever needed to make a special call.

Once upon a time, there was a bug who was very reliable. He was small and fast, so he was always on-the-go. One day, he was out and about, looking for food, when he heard a voice call out.

"Bug! Please stay!" said the voice.

Bug stopped and looked around, but he couldn't see who was calling him.

Then he heard the voice again.

"Bug! Please remain here!"

Bug was puzzled, but he decided to obey the voice and remained. Suddenly he saw a little girl in front of him.

"Hi, Bug!" she said. "I'm Lucy, and I'm three years old. I'm looking for a friend and I think you're perfect for the job."

Bug smiled and said, "I will stay and be your friend, Lucy. I promise to be reliable."

And so, Bug and Lucy became best friends, and remained together for a very long time.

Once upon a time there was a wealthy tiger who lived in the forest. Every day he would dance around the trees - leaping and twirling. All the other animals in the forest began to take notice of the tiger when they heard his joyful music.

Soon, a group of other animals from the forest - deer, squirrels and birds - started to join the tiger in his dancing. They twirled and jumped around the trees. As their music got louder and louder, everyone in the forest began to dance together. 

The tiger noticed the animals all around him, and smiled. He was glad that he and his friends had found something that made them so happy. From then on, every day the wealthy tiger and the other animals would dance their way through the trees in the forest.

Once there was a little boy named Joe. He was 3 years old and he loved to play outside.

One day, Joe and his mom went to the park. While they were playing, they saw some grey clouds in the sky. Joe's mom said it looked like it was going to rain.

Joe didn't want the weather to ruin their fun. Suddenly, he had an idea. He held out his hands and started to lift. He lifted and lifted until the grey clouds were gone.

Everyone was amazed. Joe had made the rain go away. He beamed with pride.

But then one mean person was so rude. He said, "You can't do that!" Joe was sad but he knew he had done a good job. He smiled and went back to playing with his mom.

One week, a little boy named Max went for a walk. He discovered an empty box on the ground. He was very excited to see what was inside.

Max opened the box and found a puppy! The little puppy was wagging its tail and looked very excited to be found. Max was so happy, he couldn't believe it!

"Is this puppy really for me?" Max asked.

His mom nodded. "Yes Max, it's all yours! I'm going to encourage you to take good care of it!"

Max was so happy. He picked up the puppy and gave it a big hug. He held the puppy close and smiled at his mom.

Max spent the whole week taking care of his new puppy. He fed him, walked him, and played with him. The puppy was very happy. Max's mom was so proud of how Max was taking care of the puppy. She would encourage him every day to keep it up. 

Max and his puppy became the best of friends. He was so excited to have found his furry buddy and he looked forward to many more fun weeks ahead.

Once upon a time, there was a family who loved to bake. They made sweet cookies and cakes every day. One day, the family decided to mix all their favorite ingredients together to make a super sweet cake. They laughed and had fun mixing everything up.

But something went wrong. The cake was too sweet and made the family feel sick. They went to bed feeling unwell. The next morning, they all woke up feeling even worse. They had to go to the hospital where the doctors tried to help them, but it was too late. The family had mixed too many sweet things and it made them very sick. They learned a lesson that day to not mix too many sweet things together. The end.

Once there was a little boy named John. He was very cheerful. One day he had a great idea! He wanted to buy a notebook. So he grabbed his money and skipped to the store. 

When he arrived, there were so many notebooks to choose from. He wanted one that was just the right size and perfect for writing. He grabbed a cheerful notebook with bright colors. 

John was so excited! He quickly paid for it and rushed home. He grabbed some markers and paper and began filling up the notebook with all of his ideas. 

He continued to fill the notebook with lots of drawings and stories. It was so much fun! John was very cheerful as he shared his notebook with his friends and family.

Billy was having a great day playing in the park with his friends. He had a new toy gun and he was running around shooting pretend bad guys. Then he saw something silver sparkling in the grass. He went over and picked it up - it was a silver coin!

Billy was very excited, but his friends had started to leave. He decided to take the coin home and show it to his dad.

When Billy got home, he ran straight to his dad and showed him the coin. His dad smiled and said, "Wow, what a great find! You can keep it for yourself."

Billy was so happy he ran outside to tell his friends. But when he got back to the park, he realised his silver coin had gone. He looked around but he couldn't see it anywhere.

Billy went back home and told his dad what had happened. His dad was so angry! He said, "That was your lucky coin! You must find it, or else!"

Billy found some friends and they started searching the park. After a few hours, they finally found the silver coin! Billy was so relieved, and he quickly ran home to show his dad.

When Billy's dad saw the silver coin, he was so happy. He said, "Well done Billy! You are very brave."
 Billy was so proud and he couldn't stop smiling. He put the silver coin in a safe place and never lost it again

One day, John and his mom were out in the woods. John was looking to find some lumber for his toy boat. They had been scourging for hours, but hadn't found anything yet. 

"Are you sure there's lumber around here, Mom?" asked John.

"Of course," she said happily. "Just keep looking, I'm sure we'll find it."

John kept searching, but soon stumbled upon an ancient chest. He excitedly opened it, demonstrating his dependable strength. Inside, he found the lumber he was looking for.

John quickly improved his toy boat, since his strength was now dependable. With newfound confidence, John raced off with his boat in the river. He sailed faster than ever, enjoying the adventure he had found. 

John sure was glad he found that lumber!

At the end of the day, they drove back home and Lucy said goodbye to her uncle. She ran inside and showed her parents her toy tool and explained how she had helped cut the grass.

One day, a mysterious man came to a small town. He walked down the street and everyone noticed him.

The mayor of the town was very curious and asked him why he was there. The mysterious man said he wanted to build something. 

The mayor asked what it was that the man wanted to build. The man said he wanted to build a score. 

The mayor was amazed. He asked what it was for. The man said it was a surprise and it was for everyone in the town.

The townspeople worked together to help the mysterious man build his score. 

When it was finished, everyone was so excited. They could not believe it. 

The mysterious man said that it was now time to play the score. 

The town was filled with happiness and excitement. Everyone worked together to play the score, and when they finished, they all cheered! 

The mysterious man smiled and said, "Today you have made a mysterious score and it will be here forever and ever." 

The townspeople cheered even louder and celebrated the mysterious score they had built together.

One day, there was a wise Grandpa who wanted to teach his grandchildren something useful. He gathered the little ones around and put a tray of apples in front of them. 

Grandpa said, "Now it is time for you to learn about sharing. Who would like to go first?"

The little ones looked at each other. Then one brave boy stepped forward. Grandpa smiled and said, "Go ahead and take two apples." The boy eagerly grabbed two apples from the tray.

Then Grandpa explained that it was not fair for only one child to get two apples, since the other children did not. He said, "Now it's your turn." He looked at the other children and asked them to take one apple each. 

At first, the children were hesitant but Grandpa explained that it would be wise to share the apples. After a few moments, they all decided to share. 

Soon enough, all the children had an apple of their own and they were all happy. Everyone learned an important lesson that day â€“ sharing is caring.

Once upon a time, there was a modest pear tree. In the tree were two pears. One was big and one was small.

The small pear wanted to be picked but was shy. It said to the big pear, "I want to go with you when you get picked." The big pear agreed and waited for someone to come.

Soon a nice man came and plucked both pears off the tree. As soon as they were in his hand, both pears yielded to the man and he was very happy.

The man took the pears home and ate them. They were yummy and sweet. The man said to himself, "This modest little pear tree really did yield some tasty fruit!"

Once upon a time there was a silly monkey. He was very foolish and always getting into trouble. 

One day the monkey was very hungry, so he decided to search for some food. He searched high and low, but all he could find were some grapes. So the monkey ate the grapes and his tummy felt better. 

But suddenly the monkey began to feel very dizzy. He wobbled around and soon became very confused. He forgot all about looking for food, and just lay there until he felt better.

The end.

Once upon a time there was a little boy. He was three years old and his name was Tom. Tom was a very happy little boy. One day he found an orange pill on the ground. He picked it up and looked at it.

Tom had no idea what it was. He started to cry because he didn't know what the pill was. Suddenly, his mom appeared. She knew what the pill was and told Tom it was a vitamin pill. She said it would make him feel better if he took it.

Tom stopped crying and he was happy again. His mom gave him a cup of water and he took the orange pill. He told his mom it tasted funny, but he felt much better. 

Tom was happy that his mom knew what the pill was, otherwise he would have cried forever!

Once upon a time there were two kids, a little boy and a little girl. The two were best friends, and loved playing together.

The little boy had a tube. Whenever he played with it, the little girl would join him. She thought the tube was so much fun!

One day, while they were playing, they heard a loud noise. It scared the little girl, so she grabbed the tube and ran away.

The little boy was sad. All he wanted was his tube back.

He ran to the little girl's house and knocked on the door.

"Little girl," he yelled. "I need my tube back!"

The little girl opened the door. She was keeping the tube for herself, but when she saw how sad the boy was, she felt guilty. 

"Here," she said softly. "You can have your tube back."

The little boy was so happy! He hugged the little girl and together they kept on playing.

One day, two friends decided to go on an adventure.
They grabbed their big map, and took off.
They started walking and soon, the sun was high in the sky.
It was very hot, so they took a break.
They looked at the map and decided to keep going.
Before long, they had gone through the woods and found a big lake.
They both took off their shoes and went swimming.
Then they took some food and ate it by the lake.
It was a great day, and it ended with them looking at the starry sky.

John was walking in a new place. He had never seen it before. He could hear birds singing in the trees. It was a nice place.

John saw a tough mountain in the distance. He wondered what was up there. Even though the mountain was tough, John wanted to try to climb it.

Suddenly, John heard a voice. It said, â€œHey! What are you doing?â€

John turned around and saw a man. He said, â€œHi. Iâ€™m trying to climb the tough mountain.â€

The man smiled and said, â€œThatâ€™s brave of you. But be careful. That mountain is really tough!â€

John thanked the man for the warning, then he started his climb. He kept going until he reached the top. From the top, the view of the place was amazing.

John was glad he listened to the man. The tough mountain was well worth the challenge!

Tom and Mia are friends. They like to play with toys and draw pictures. One day, they find a big feather on the grass. It is white and smooth and soft.

"Wow, look at this feather!" Tom says. "It is so pretty!"

"Can I touch it?" Mia asks. "It looks so nice!"

Tom gives the feather to Mia. She rubs it on her cheek and smiles. "It feels so good!"

They take the feather to their playroom. They want to make something with it. They look for paper, glue, scissors and crayons.

"I know!" Tom says. "Let's make a bird!"

"OK!" Mia says. "That sounds fun!"

They cut out a bird shape from the paper. They glue the feather on the tail. They draw eyes, a beak and wings with the crayons. They are very careful and happy.

They complete their bird. They hold it up and admire it. It is colorful and cute.

"We did it!" Tom says. "We made a bird with the feather!"

"We are so clever!" Mia says. "Let's show it to Mom and Dad!"

They run to their parents and show them their bird. Mom and Dad are proud and surprised.

"What a beautiful bird!" Mom says. "You are very creative!"

"Where did you find the feather?" Dad asks. "It is so smooth!"

Tom and Mia tell them about the feather on the grass. They say they want to find more feathers and make more things.

Mom and Dad hug them and praise them. They say they can go to the park and look for more feathers.

Tom and Mia are happy. They love their bird and their feather. They can't wait to play and create more.

Once there was a chubby little bunny. He heard about a cool pass in a far away town. He hopped and hopped until he reached the pass. He was so excited to be there. 

When he arrived at the pass, the bunny noticed something in the distance. The sun was beginning to rise above the horizon. He hopped another step forward and the sun shone brighter and brighter. He had never seen a sunrise before and it was beautiful! 

The bunny stayed at the pass until the sun had risen completely. He felt so happy and content that he hopped and bounced joyfully back home. As he hopped, he looked forward to the sunset he would see that day.

Once there was a very grumpy girl named Alley. She didn't like to wear clothes of any kind and she was always very unhappy.

One day, Alley's mom caught sight of her walking out of the house with no clothes on. She asked Alley why she wasn't wearing any clothes.

Alley said, "Mom, I just don't like wearing clothes. I feel better without them."

Her mom knew this wasn't the best way for Alley to live, so she had an idea. She said, "Alley, why don't you try wearing some fashionable clothes? I think you would like it!"

At first, Alley didn't want to wear clothes, but after a while, she changed her mind. She started wearing fashionable clothes whenever she went out and soon she felt much better about being in public.

Soon all of her friends were asking for her fashion advice and recommending her to others.

Once again, Alley was very grumpy. But now she was grumpy in the best way possible - she felt confident and comfortable with her fashion. She had found something that made her happy!

Tom and Lily were going to the park with their mom. They liked the park because it had swings, slides and a big sandbox. They walked on the sidewalk and held mom's hand. They saw many cars and buses on the road. That was traffic.

"Look, mom, a fire truck!" Tom said. He pointed at the red truck with a loud siren. It zoomed past them and made a lot of noise.

"Wow, that's cool!" Lily said. She liked the fire truck too. She wondered where it was going.

"Maybe there is a fire somewhere and the fire truck is going to help," mom said. "We should be grateful that there are brave people who can put out fires and save others."

They crossed the street when the light turned green. They had to wait for a long time because there was a lot of traffic. They heard another siren behind them. It was an ambulance. It also zoomed past them and made a lot of noise.

"Mom, what is an ambulance?" Lily asked.

"An ambulance is a car that helps people who are hurt or sick," mom said. "It takes them to the hospital where doctors and nurses can make them feel better."

"Are the people in the ambulance screaming?" Tom asked. He was scared of the siren.

"Maybe they are, or maybe they are quiet," mom said. "But we don't have to be afraid of the ambulance. It is there to help them, not to hurt them."

They reached the park and saw the swings, slides and sandbox. They ran to play and forgot about the traffic and the sirens. They were happy and grateful to be at the park with their mom.

One ordinary day, John woke up. He felt so happy and hoped that it was going to be a big day. He brushed his teeth and ate breakfast, then he was ready for the day.

John and his mom went outside to play. They walked and laughed and sang until it got quiet. John realized that he liked this silence and he wanted it to stay forever.

John and his mom kept walking. Soon, they came across a large park. He remembered that this was the place he had always hoped to visit. His eyes sparkled and he ran ahead.

John and his mom raced each other around the park. Along the way, they saw lots of lovely things. John smiled and was filled with happiness. For the rest of the day, he continued to hope that this moment would never end. 

The sun began to set and John knew it was time to go home. He said goodbye to the park and back to the ordinary day he had before. He took one last look, smiling to himself. He secretly hoped he would come back one day.

Once there was a cactus. It was in the desert and had sharp spikes, but it was safe. It stood tall and was very strong. Every day the wind would blow, but the cactus was able to balance. It was so strong it never fell down!

One day, a little bird flew by and saw the cactus. It was so amazed by its ability to balance. The bird wanted to learn how to balance like the cactus. So it sat down near the cactus and watched it very carefully.

The wind kept blowing and the cactus stayed still. Every time the wind blew, the cactus would move its body and balance again. It was a strange sight!

The bird watched the cactus and practiced balancing until it was able to do it too. From then on, the bird kept practicing and eventually got so good, it reminds us of the cactus.

Once upon a time there were two bunnies named Pinky and Fluffy. Every day they hopped around the garden looking for something delicious to eat. 

One day, when Hopa and Fluffy were hopping, they saw a big jug near the bushes. 

Pinky asked Fluffy, "What is that?"

They hopped over and saw that the jug was filled with lots of soft, yummy carrots. 

Pinky said, "Oooooh, yummy! Let's hop over and get something to eat!" 

So they hopped over, grabbed a carrot each, and enjoyed the delicious snack.
