Lily and Ben felt sorry and sad. They said, "We're sorry, Mom. We just wanted to have fun and taste the sauce. We didn't mean to make a mess." They helped Mom clean up the sauce and the cars. They put on clean clothes and ate their pasta. They learned their lesson. They promised to be more careful and respectful when they play with their cars.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She loved to explore and discover new things. One day, when she was walking, she saw a colorful rainbow in the sky. She started jumping and clapping with joy. She exclaimed, â€œWow! A rainbow!â€

The little girl wanted to get closer to the rainbow. She started running but the rainbow slowly disappeared. Suddenly, it started to rain. The little girl was disappointed but she did not give up.

She kept running, and then she saw a giant pot. She stopped and said, â€œMaybe I can drink the rainbow if I catch all of the raindrops!â€ The little girl grabbed the pot and started to catch raindrops. After a while, she was finally able to drink the rainbow! The raindrops made the rainbow liquid sweet and yum!

The little girl was so happy that she was able to drink the rainbow. She shouted with joy, â€œI did it! I did it!â€

John and his mom went to the cafe. John saw a big menu on the wall, and the words on it were very clear.

John said, "Mom, I want this!" He pointed to the blueberry pancake.

Mom smiled and said, "Okay, let's mark it." She marked the menu with a pencil.

Then, they asked the waiter to bring them the marked menu. 

The waiter said, "Yes, I will be back soon with the marked menu for you."

Mom smiled again. "Thank you, we will wait." 

John waited with excitement for the pancakes to come. He was happy because he knew his marked menu was coming soon!

Once, there lived a boy named Alex. He was three years old and he loved to watch cartoons on TV. He felt very glad when he got to watch them.

One day, Alex and his mom decided to go to the park. As they got there, he saw many children playing and having fun. He was excited and asked his mom if he could join them. 

His mom said, "Yes, you can join them and use your imagination to play." Alex listened and ran over to the children. 

He started playing with everyone else. They were all pretending they were in a cartoon. Alex was so happy to be joining in the game. He used his imagination to pretend he was a character. They all had a great time.

When it was time to go home, Alex was very glad. He hugged his mom and thanked her for taking him to the park. He enjoyed playing with the other children. Alex had lots of fun and made new friends.

One day, an ant wanted to make some nice art. But he didn't know how! So he asked his friendly friends for help.

"How can I make nice art?" he asked.

The rabbit smiled and said, "You can print it!".

The ant was so excited! He thanked his friend and said goodbye.

He went to the store and bought some printing paper. He put it on the ground, and with a special machine, he printed the prettiest picture he had ever seen! All his friends came over to see it, and they were amazed. 

"That looks so nice!" shouted the mouse.

The ant beamed with pride. He had made something beautiful, all by himself. He thanked his friendly friends for the help. They all smiled and said, "You did a great job!" 

Together, they enjoyed the beautiful art the ant had printed.

Once upon a time there was a small girl named Grace. She was three years old and full of energy. One day Grace decided to go outside to search for something cool. She looked all around her, but all she could see was brown rocks, blue sky, and green grass. But then, Grace noticed something strange - a tiny green bug on a tree. Grace had never seen a green bug before, so she was very excited and began to search for more bugs like it.

After searching and searching, Grace finally found something else - a whole family of green bugs! She was so happy and excited that she almost forgot to tell her mom. This made her mom a bit unhappy, as she had been trying to tell Grace to stay away from bugs.

But what Grace didn't know was that these green bugs were very dangerous. She had been ignorant of the fact that these bugs could be harmful. Thankfully, her mom arrived just in time. She quickly shooed away the bugs, and explained to Grace why these bugs were dangerous. Grace listened carefully and promised never to search for bugs again without her mom's permission.

One day there was a little girl. She was fancying she would take a bath. So, she got all ready and asked her mummy for a bath. Her mummy was very happy and laughed in a funny way. She went into the bathroom and saw lots of shiny and colourful bottles. 

The little girl looked at all the bottles carefully and chose one that smelled nice. She poured the bubble bath into the water and then rolled up her sleeves. She was very excited! 

The little girl lay in the bath and splashed around; it was lots of fun. She felt so relaxed in the warm and bubbly water. When she was done, she put on her pyjamas, feeling very refreshed. 

From that day onward, she liked to take a bubble bath every evening, and it helped her get ready for a good night's sleep.

Once upon a time, there were two friends, James and Emily. They were going to take a trip together, but they began to quarrel before they could go.

"My passport is better than yours," said James.
"No, mine is better!" argued Emily.

Their quarrel got bigger and bigger, until Emily had enough. She ran away, leaving James alone. James was so sad that he started to cry. He was so upset that he decided to take the trip alone.

The trip turned out to be terribly bad. Everything was wrong. Nothing went as planned. He went home feeling worse than ever.

When he returned home, he walked into the living room and saw Emily and James sitting together, laughing. They had made up and were no longer quarrelling! James felt a wave of happiness come over him. 

From then on, they agreed to never quarrel again!

Once there was a farmer who had three sheep. He liked to take them for a walk in the morning and play with them in the meadow. One day when he was out walking with the sheep, he noticed one of them was looking very dirty. He looked around and he saw a muddy pond nearby. He had an idea and suggested that the sheep jump in the pond and get clean. The sheep thought this would be a fun game and so they jumped into the muddy pond. After the sheep were dirty, the farmer got them all out of the pond and they were as clean as can be! The farmer and the sheep were very happy. The sheep continued to play and the farmer looked on, content that his sheep were clean.

Spring rolled around and with it came new surprises. The rich colours of nature began to glimmer in the sunshine and animals stepped out of their homes to look around.

Billy was out with his parents one day when he noticed a butterfly struggling to fly up into a tree. He watched as it tried to reach a branch, but the wind was too strong. His dad asked if he wanted to help the butterfly and, of course, Billy said yes.

He reached up and carefully grabbed the branch and let the butterfly crawl onto it. Billy let go and the butterfly fluttered away. He felt rich with joy and smiled as he watched it go.

That night, Billy and his parents went to bed. As he lay in bed, Billy could feel the comfort of his parents' love. He felt warm and happy, like the feeling he got when he helped the butterfly. In that moment, he knew he had to surrender to the love of his family.

Once upon a time there was a girl called Sally. She was three years old and loved to pretend. One day Sally was feeling very sad. She wanted to do something to make her happy. 

Sally went outside and saw a beautiful row boat. She decided to pretend. Sally pretended that she was sailing away on an adventure. She smiled and felt much better. 

Sally got into the boat and pretended to be the captain. She started rowing, pretending she was in the middle of the ocean. She used her arms to make the boat go faster and faster. 

Soon Sally was back home, but she still felt a little sad. Her mom noticed and gave her a big hug. Now Sally felt better and the adventure could continue another day.

Mummy was in the living room. She was putting on her pretty clothes for an important meeting. Suddenly, she noticed something naughty.

"Bizzy," Mummy said sternly, "why are you bowing in my clothes?"

Bizzy was a three-year-old girl. She had been playing in Mummyâ€™s closet. She pointed to a bow that had fallen on the floor.

"That bow was pretty," Bizzy said pleadingly.

Mummy sighed. She picked up the bow and put it back in the closet.

"You must be careful with my clothes," Mummy said. "And no more bowing, okay?"

Bizzy nodded solemnly. She knew she had been naughty. 

From then on, she was extra careful around Mummyâ€™s clothes. But every now and then, she would take out the bow and give it a big, twirly bow.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play outside. One day, she went to the park with her mom and saw her friend Timmy playing on the monkey bars. Lily wanted to play too, but she was scared.

"I don't think I can do it," Lily said.

"Don't worry, I'll support you," Timmy said.

Lily felt better and tried to climb up, but she couldn't. She started to cry.

"It's okay, Lily. Your brain just needs to figure out how to do it. We can try again later when you feel more fit," her mom said.

Lily felt better and went to play on the swings. She knew that with practice and support, she would be able to climb the monkey bars someday.

The man was very intelligent and loved horses. Every day, he would go to the pasture to check on them. One day, he took a special horse out for a walk.

The horse was very nervous, but the man was patient. He offered words of encouragement and the horse began to yield to the man's commands.

The man smiled as the horse trotted along, making progress. He was proud of his horse and the progress it was making.

However, the man soon ran into trouble. A pack of wolves emerged from the woods and started chasing after the horse and man. The man cried out in fear, but the horse stood its ground and turned back.

The man shouted in joy, thankful that the horse had been so intelligent. But it was not enough -- the wolves managed to catch the horse and attack it. 

The man screamed in terror, his joy quickly turning to despair. He had lost his beloved horse and it was all his fault. He had trusted too much in the horse's intelligence and underestimated the danger.

Once upon a time, there was a red car named Max. Max loved to drive fast and do loops around the track. One day, Max met a lion named Leo. Leo liked to roar very loudly. 

"Hi Leo," said Max. "Why do you like to roar so much?"

"I roar to show everyone that I am big and strong," replied Leo.

Max thought for a moment and then said, "I like to do loops to show everyone that I am fast and brave."

Leo smiled and said, "We are both very good at something. Let's be friends and show everyone what we can do together!"

Max and Leo became best friends and would often do loops and roar together. They were very happy and everyone could see that they were the best of friends.

Once upon a time there was a little man called Bob. Bob went for a walk in the park. He was feeling silly and decided to play hide and seek. He closed his eyes and counted to ten. He couldn't find anyone!

Suddenly, Bob heard a strange noise. He opened his eyes and there, sitting in a tree, was a little creature with furry ears. The creature had bright eyes and a cute tail.

Bob wasn't scared. He asked the creature: "What are you?"
The creature replied: "I'm a fox! I like to bite things!"

Bob thought it was silly to bite things, so he said: "No, that's not nice!"
The fox disagreed and it smiled. "Why don't you try it? It's fun!"

So, Bob opened his mouth and he tried to bite the fox's fluffy tail. But it was too fast! All he felt was a tickle in his tongue.

The fox laughed and said: "That was silly! Now it's my turn! Come closer."

Bob took a deep breath and stepped closer. The fox opened its mouth wide and bit his lung. Bob screamed and ran away.

That night, Bob had a dream about silly little foxes that bit each other's tails. He had learnt his lesson - he would never try to bite anything ever again!

Once upon a time there was a rabbit and a fox who were very good friends. They liked to go for walks in the woods and play together. 
One day, the fox found a long stick in the woods and split it in two. He gave one half to the rabbit and kept the other half for himself. 
The rabbit was very delighted and held his stick tight. But the fox became very sad and became upset. He wanted the stick to stay one single piece, so they could hold it together.

The rabbit was very confused and asked the fox why he was so upset. The fox told the rabbit that even though his stick was split into two, they could still stay together and hold each one of the pieces, understanding that friendship was more valuable than a mere stick. 

The rabbit and the fox realized that things that are shared together can create stronger connections and bring more happiness than keeping them to oneself. 

The moral of the story is that friendship is more important than material things. Always remember to appreciate what you have and share it with others!

Jill was so excited to see her grandpa. He looked so charming in his favourite sweater. He was drinking a big glass of juice and gave Jill a big smile.

"Hello my beautiful girl, it's so nice to see you!", he said. Jill ran towards her grandpa and hugged him tightly. Grandpa looked at her and said, "I have something special for you, my dear".

He asked Jill to close her eyes and gave her something. "Ok, you can open them now!" He said with a smile. Jill opened her eyes and was so incredibly excited to see that it was a new toy.

Grandpa then encouraged her to play with the toy and said, "I'm so proud of you.You can do anything you want in life if you put your mind to it."

Jill was playing with the toy in the garden, when suddenly, a big gust of wind threw the toy right over the fence. Jill ran to get it, but it was too late. The toy had gone. Jill was so upset and started crying. Grandpa tried to encourage her, but it was too late. The charming moment had been ruined.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She liked to play outside in the park with her friends. One day, Lily fell down and got a big boo-boo on her knee. Her mommy gave her a band-aid to put on it, but it didn't help.

Lily's grandma came to visit and saw her boo-boo. She said, "Let me help you with that." She took out a needle and thread and started to stitch up the boo-boo. Lily was scared at first, but her grandma made her feel calm and cool.

After a little while, the stitching was done and Lily's boo-boo was all better. She was so happy and gave her grandma a big hug. From that day on, Lily knew that if she ever got hurt again, her grandma would be there to help her pass through the pain.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play outside with their bikes. One day, they see a new road near their house. It is green and shiny. They want to ride on it.

"Can we go, Mom?" Anna asks. Mom looks at the road. She sees some signs and cones. She shakes her head.

"No, sweeties. That road is not ready. It is still wet. It is for cars, not bikes. You can get hurt if you go there," Mom says.

Anna and Ben are sad. They want to have fun. They look at each other. They have an idea. They nod and smile.

They go to their backyard. They find some paint and brushes. They paint their own road on the grass. They make it green and shiny. They draw some signs and cones. They ride their bikes on their road. They have fun.

Mom sees them from the window. She smiles. She is proud of them. They are creative and safe. She goes outside and joins them. She rides a bike on their road. They laugh and hug. They love their green road.

Once upon a time, there was a modest farm. On this farm, there were many animals. One of the animals was a chicken. The chicken was very happy on the farm.

One day, the farmer had to load hay onto his truck. The chicken wanted to help. The chicken tried to pick up the hay with its beak, but it was too heavy. The chicken felt sad.

Then, the farmer saw the chicken trying to help. He smiled and said, "Thank you, chicken." The chicken felt happy again. From that day on, the chicken and the farmer were best friends.

Cory was a curious three-year-old. He wanted to explore the world around him and find out what he could see.

One day Cory was playing in the garden and he noticed there was an ugly bug on the ground. He wanted to take a closer view and see what it was, so he asked his mum:

"Mum, can I supply a view?"

Mum smiled and said, "Yes, of course you can, my darling. Just go ahead and take a look."

So Cory carefully bent down and looked closely at the bug. It had lots of legs and antennae! He watched it scuttle along the ground before flying away.

He ran back to his mum, excited and amazed what he had seen.

"Mum, did you see the ugly bug?" he asked.

Mum smiled and said, "Yes, I did. It was quite an interesting view!"

One day, a little boy named Tim went with his mom to the grocery store. They needed to buy food for dinner. Tim saw a broken toy on the floor. He wanted to pick it up, but his mom said, "No, Tim. That toy is broken. Let's go find some good food."

Tim and his mom walked around the grocery store. They found apples, carrots, and bread. Tim saw a big dog outside the store. He wanted to pet the dog, but his mom said, "Tim, we must remain inside the store. The dog might be lost."

Tim was sad, but he listened to his mom. They finished shopping and went home. Tim's mom made a yummy dinner. They ate together and talked about their day. Tim was happy he could help his mom at the grocery store.

Once upon a time, there was a wide field with lots of green grass. In the field, there was a sheep who loved to eat the grass. Every day, the sheep would lean down to eat the grass.

One day, a big storm came and the wind blew very hard. The sheep was scared and didn't know what to do. But then, the sheep remembered that there was a big rock in the field. The rock was very wide and could protect the sheep from the wind.

So, the sheep ran to the rock and leaned against it. The rock was so wide that it protected the sheep from the wind. The sheep was very happy and felt safe.

From that day on, the sheep knew that whenever there was a big storm, it could always go to the rock and lean against it for protection. And so, the sheep lived happily ever after in the wide field.

Once upon a time there was a seal. He was a very special kind of seal, because he was purple. Every day he would go around and record the noises of the sea. He thought it was lots of fun to be able to listen to the tunes of the ocean.

One day the seal went to a nearby beach and he looked for something special. Suddenly, he spied a shiny purple shell. He knew it was special, so he grabbed it. He carefully took it back to his home.

He wanted to find a way to keep the shell safe. Then he remembered he had an old recording machine. He used it to record the noise of the sea and he used it to record the sound of his shell. Now he always was able to listen to the sound of the shell whenever he wanted.

The seal was so happy. He knew his shell was safe and he was able to enjoy the sound of the sea any time he wanted. He had recorded the sound of his purple shell forever.

Lily and Sam were playing in the park. They liked to slide, swing and run. Lily had a new watch that her mom gave her. It was pink and shiny and had a flower on it. She was very happy with her watch.

"Look at my watch, Sam!" Lily said, showing him her wrist. "It tells me the time and it makes a beep sound."

"Wow, that's a nice watch, Lily!" Sam said, admiring it. "Can I try it on?"

"Okay, but be careful with it," Lily said, taking off her watch and giving it to Sam. "It's very special to me."

Sam put on the watch and smiled. He liked how it felt on his arm. He pressed a button and heard the beep sound. He pressed another button and saw some numbers change. He pressed another button and saw a light flash.

"Look, Lily, it has a light too!" Sam said, waving his arm in the air.

Lily was about to answer, when she saw a big dog running towards them. The dog was barking and wagging its tail. It looked friendly, but it was also very fast and big.

"Sam, watch out!" Lily shouted, pulling Sam away from the dog. "The dog might take your watch!"

Sam was scared and held on to Lily. The dog jumped on them and licked their faces. It was trying to play, but it was also very strong and heavy. It knocked them down and scratched their clothes.

"Hey, stop that!" Lily said, pushing the dog away. "Bad dog! Leave us alone!"

The dog did not listen. It saw the watch on Sam's arm and tried to bite it. It thought it was a toy. Sam screamed and tried to protect his arm.

"Help! Help!" Sam cried. "The dog wants my watch!"

Lily was very brave and thoughtful. She knew she had to prevent the dog from hurting Sam and taking his watch. She grabbed a stick and waved it at the dog. She made a loud noise and said, "Go away! Go away!"

The dog was surprised and scared. It backed away from Lily and Sam. It did not like the stick or the noise. It ran away to find another game.

Lily and Sam got up and hugged each other. They were safe and happy. Lily checked Sam's arm and saw that it was not hurt. She checked her watch and saw that it was not broken. She was very relieved and proud.

"Are you okay, Sam?" Lily asked, putting her watch back on.

"I'm okay, Lily," Sam said, smiling. "Thank you for saving me and your watch. You are very brave and thoughtful."

Lily and Sam walked back to their moms, who were waiting for them. They told them what happened and showed them the watch. Their moms were very glad and proud. They gave them hugs and kisses and said, "You are very good friends. You take care of each other and share your things. We love you very much."

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim had two arms, one on the left and one on the right. One day, Tim went out to play in the dark night.

In the dark, Tim could not see well. He did not know where his toys were. So, he used his arms to feel around and find them. Tim found his ball, his doll, and his toy car.

Then, Tim heard a noise. He did not know what it was. He was a little scared. But, he used his arms to feel around and found his dog, Max. Tim was happy to know it was just Max. They played together in the dark and had a lot of fun.

Sam and Lily were playing in the park. They saw a big tree with a hole in it. They wanted to see what was inside.

"Can we go look, please?" Sam asked Lily.

"OK, but be careful. Maybe there is a bug or a snake in there," Lily said.

They walked to the tree and peeked into the hole. It was dark and quiet. They heard a soft voice.

"Hello, little ones. Do you want to play with me?" the voice said.

Sam and Lily were curious. They could not see who was talking.

"Who are you?" Sam asked.

"I am a spirit. I live in this tree. I am lonely and bored. Come inside and I will show you some fun things," the voice said.

Sam and Lily thought it sounded nice. They wanted to have fun.

"OK, we will come in. But we have to go back soon. Our mom is waiting for us," Lily said.

They crawled into the hole and followed the voice. They did not know that the voice was lying. It was not a friendly spirit. It was a hungry spirit. It wanted to eat them.

The spirit led them to a dark and cold place. It had sharp teeth and claws. It smiled and said, "Thank you for coming, little ones. You are my dinner today."

Sam and Lily were scared. They tried to run away, but it was too late. The spirit grabbed them and bit them. They screamed and cried, but no one heard them.

The spirit ate them and felt happy. It had not eaten for a long time. It said, "That was delicious. I hope more children come to play with me."

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Jane. She was only 3 years old and liked to jog every day. One day, Jane decided to jog to the park. She was so excited to explore!

When Jane arrived at the park, she saw something large and round. It was a pear tree! Jane saw lots of pears hanging, so she ran to them and started picking them. 

Suddenly, Jane heard a voice. It was an old man sitting on a bench. "Do not pick those pears, they are not yours," he said in a serious tone.

Jane was scared, and she started to jog away. But then she noticed something on the ground and stopped. It was a pear that had fallen from the tree.

"It's ok if I pick this one, right?" Jane asked the old man. 

The old man smiled and said, "Yes, you can pick this one, it's ok".

So Jane picked the fallen pear and jogged home, happy to have something to eat. She made sure to obey the old man's serious instructions.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She was three years old and her name was Lily.

On this day, Lily's mommy needed help. So she asked the nurse to come deliver the baby.

Lily was very excited and waited for the nurse. When the nurse arrived, she was very kind. But Lily was a bit fearful of someone new.

The nurse said, "Hello Lily, I'm here to help your mommy and deliver your new baby brother or sister".

Lily smiled and said, "Yay! An extra special gift!"

The nurse said, "Yes! It will be a special day, but you will have to be a very brave girl. Can you do that for your baby brother or sister?"

Lily bravely said, "Yes, I can be brave!" Then Lily gave the nurse a big hug.

The nurse smiled and said, "Thank you. I'm so proud of you. Now, let's go help your mommy."

At the end of the day, Lily's family welcomed the new baby. Lily was so glad she was able to be brave and help the nurse deliver the special gift.

Once upon a time there was a little worm. He was going for a walk when he met a tough man. The man asked the worm, "Do you want to go on an adventure?" The worm nodded.

The man smiled and took the worm with him. They walked to a big park and the man said, "Let's have some fun!" They ran and played on the slides. The worm was very happy.
 
The two friends kept playing until it was time for the worm to go home. He gave the tough man a big hug and then nodded goodbye. The man said, "Goodbye my friend. I'm glad we had fun today." The worm waved and went home.

Once upon a time there was a jolly old woman. She was always cheerful and liked to whistle. Every day she would take a walk and watch the world go by. One day, as she was walking and whistling, a 3 year old boy caught her eye. She watched him playing with a toy car on the sidewalk.

The old woman smiled and went over. She asked him, "What are you playing?"
The boy replied, "I'm making my car go fast!"

The old woman laughed and said, "That sounds like fun. Let's play a game. I'll see if I can whistle louder than your car,"
The boy nodded eagerly and said, "OK!"

The old woman breathed in deep and then began to whistle as loud as she could. She smiled as she watched the little boy and his car. The higher she whistled the faster the car seemed to go. The boy laughed and cheered as she went faster and faster. 

Finally, the boy exclaimed, "You won!"
The old woman clapped her hands and said, "Yes! That was a good game. Would you like to play again?" 
The little boy beamed and said, "Yes please!" So, the two of them played again, this time the woman laughing as the little car went faster and faster.

Once there were two friends who used to play together every day. They pretended to be superheroes and they had lots of fun. One day they started to fight. They each took a newspaper and started using it to hit the other one. The newspapers weren't strong enough though and they broke. All of a sudden they both remembered an old original newspaper that was in their friend's house. So they both ran over to their friend's house and found the old newspaper. They fought really hard but in the end they hugged each other and laughed. They put the old original newspaper away and went on to have more fun.

Kiki was a very happy little girl. She played in her garden for hours every day. She loved to feel the sun on her skin and the wind blowing through her hair.

Kiki's mum called, "It's time for your bath, Kiki!" Kiki shouted, "Yay!" She ran inside and hopped into her bathtub. The water was warm and felt tight around her.

Kiki had two special bath toys - a round rubber duck and a square sponge. She liked to squeeze the duck with her hands and rub the sponge in circles all over her body.

Kiki's mum came into the bathroom. She smiled and said, "I see you are having a lot of fun! Now, make sure you wash all the places that your sponge touched, ok?"

Kiki nodded and said, "Okay." She watched as her mum poured some soap onto her sponge in the shape of a square. Kiki floated the soap-covered sponge around the bathtub, and soon the whole tub was filled with sudsy bubbles!

Kiki sang and splashed in the water until it was time to get out. When she was all dried off, Kiki hugged her mum and said, "Thank you for helping me bathe!"

Once upon a time, a little boy named Tim found a big brown raft. He wanted to ride it on the river near his house. He asked his mom, "Can I ride the raft on the river, please?"

His mom said, "No, Tim. The river is too fast. It is not safe for you to ride the raft alone."

Tim was sad, but he thought of a plan. He asked his big sister, Jane, to ride the raft with him. Jane said, "Okay, let's ride the raft together, but we have to be careful."

They went to the river and started to ride the raft. Suddenly, they saw a big rock in the water. Jane said, "Tim, help me! We need to move the raft away from the rock!"

Tim and Jane worked together to push the raft away from the rock. They were safe and happy. They rode the raft all the way back home and told their mom about their adventure. From that day on, Tim and Jane always played together and helped each other.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was very curious and loved to explore the world around her. One day, she went to the park with her friends. They played on the swings and slides, but then they saw a big ball.

Lily's friend wanted to keep the ball for herself, but Lily said, "Let's share it!" They played with the ball together and had so much fun. In the end, they both felt like they had won a victory because they had such a good time together.

Lily went home happy, knowing that sharing is always the best way to make friends and have fun.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She liked to draw pictures and make things with paper. One day, she wanted to make a special folder to keep all her drawings in one place. 

Lily asked her mommy for some paper and scissors. She carefully cut the paper and folded it to make a folder. She was so proud of herself for making something all by herself. 

Later that day, Lily felt restless and wanted to draw more pictures. She remembered her special folder and went to get it. She put all her drawings inside and felt happy knowing they were safe and organized in her new folder. From that day on, Lily made sure to keep her special folder close by so she could add more drawings to it whenever she wanted.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and run around. Her mommy told her that exercise is important to stay healthy. So, Lily would run and jump and play every day. 

One day, Lily's room was very messy. Her toys were all over the place. Her mommy said, "Lily, we need to clean up your room. Let's remove all the toys and put them in their right places." 

Lily helped her mommy and they organized all her toys in their proper spots. After they finished, they sat down on the floor and did some stretching exercises. Lily loved spending time with her mommy and keeping her room neat and tidy.

Once there was a mighty promise. It came from a glowing star up in the night sky. Everyone had high hopes for the promise. All the little kids wanted it to be true.

One night, a little girl looked up at the sky and made a wish. She wished that the promise would come true and make her world a better place. Suddenly, the whole sky glowed brighter than ever!

Then a wonderful thing happened. All the people in the world heard a magical voice coming from the glowing star in the sky. The voice said that the promise would come true and everyone felt very happy.

Lucy wanted to add texture to her picture. She saw her cat, Fluffy, and had an idea. She asked Fluffy to walk on her picture with his dirty paws. But Fluffy was stubborn and did not want to help. Lucy was sad.

Then, Lucy's mom came and saw her sad face. She helped Lucy find a sponge to make the texture on her picture. Lucy was happy again. She finished her picture and showed it to Fluffy. Even though Fluffy was stubborn, he looked at the picture and purred.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Mara. She was very adventurous and always looking for something fun and exciting to do.

One day, she went to play in the park. She saw a desk in the corner of the park and decided to sit down. But when she tried, the desk was stuck! She tried and tried to move it, but it just wouldn't budge.

Mara was so sad, she started to weep. She grabbed a stick from the ground and used it to hit the desk. She did this until it finally moved. She was so relieved, she stopped weeping.

She went home very happy and excited. Later, Mara went back to the park to show her friends her accomplishment.

Once upon a time there was an aeroplane. It was very colorful and it liked to fly up in the sky. One day, two friends saw the aeroplane and wanted to take it for a ride. So, they asked their mom if they could get in and go for a ride.

Mom smiled and said, â€œYes, if you promise to be careful.â€

The two friends were very excited and gave each other a big high-five. They jumped inside the plane and the engine started as they flew up into the sky.

The sky was so blue and the clouds looked like cotton candy. The two friends flew around and around, giggling and pointing at all the things they saw. They looked down at all the colorful houses and buildings. They flew so high the birds looked like tiny dots.

The two friends had so much fun, they stayed up in the sky all day until they gave the aeroplane back to mom. They hugged her and thanked her for giving them such a wonderful ride.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Emily. She was three years old and loved playing with toys. One day, Emily received a brand new model airplane. She was so excited!

Whenever it's safe, Emily took her model plane outside and flew it. One day, while she was flying it, the wind blew the plane away! Emily started to cry, but her dad said, â€œDon't worry, we'll get it back.â€

They went to the park and started looking for the model plane. Finally, they found it. But when Emily tried to fly it again, the plane just wouldn't go up. Emily's dad said, â€œIt looks like the wind was too strong and it made the model plane break. That was stupid.â€ 

Emily didn't understand why the wind had made the plane break. But her dad explained, â€œSometimes, the wind is too strong for things to stand up against it. That's why it was stupid for us to fly the plane in such a strong wind.â€ 

Emily still didn't understand, but she smiled and said, â€œOkay, I'll be more careful next time.â€

One day, Mommy and Daddy took Sara the 3-year-old to the park. Mommy and Daddy were happy, but Sara was scared. She saw a cop. The cop looked dangerous. Mommy and Daddy talked to the cop. After that, they all walked away together.

Sara didn't know why they talked to the cop. She was too scared to ask. Daddy held her hand tight and told her everything was OK.

When they got home, Daddy told her that the cop was there to keep everyone safe. He said the cop was like a big friend who made sure no-one was in danger.

Sara felt better and knew the cop was there to help keep her safe. She was no longer scared.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Sam. One day, Sam wanted to go on an adventure, so he asked his mom if he could go. His mom said, "Not yet, but soon enough."

Months passed and Sam waited patiently, until one day his mom said, "It's time, Sam! Get in the car and let's go!"
Sam was so excited! 
His mom drove them out of the city and through the countryside. Everywhere Sam looked, he saw tall trees, small animals, and beautiful flowers. After a few hours, they reached their destinationâ€”a small town in the country.

The days passed and Sam explored the countryside. He found a river, a bridge, and more colorful trees. He was having so much fun!

But it was time to go home. Sam was very sad and asked his mom if he could stay a bit longer. His mom smiled and said, "We can come back another time, Sam. It takes a lot of persistence to see a place you love twice!" Sam smiled, and they drove back home.

Once upon a time there was a unique queen. She lived in a big castle and had lots of nice things. 
One day, the queen wanted to go for a walk. As she walked through the forest, she came to a big tree. Suddenly, someone grabbed her from behind the tree. 
It was a bad man who had a mean face! He carried the queen away and she was never seen again. 
The story of the queen and the bad man ended sadly and the queen was never seen again.

Lily and Max were best friends. They liked to play in the park with their toys. One day, they saw a big pool of water near the slide. It looked shiny and fun.

"Let's go splash in the pool!" Max said, running towards it.

"Wait, Max!" Lily said, following him. "Mommy said pools can be dangerous. We need to be careful."

Max did not listen. He jumped into the pool and splashed around. He laughed and shouted. Lily watched him from the edge. She was scared.

"Max, come back!" Lily said. "The pool is too deep. You can't swim. You might sink."

Max did not hear her. He was having too much fun. He tried to swim to the other side of the pool. But he was not strong enough. He started to sink. He felt water in his mouth and nose. He could not breathe. He was scared.

"Help! Help!" Max cried. "Lily, help me!"

Lily heard him. She ran to the pool and grabbed his hand. She pulled him out of the water. He coughed and gasped. He was wet and cold. He was sorry.

"Thank you, Lily," Max said. "You saved me. You were right. The pool was dangerous. I should have listened to you."

Lily hugged him. She was glad he was safe. She was a good friend.

"Next time, listen to me when I warn you," Lily said. "I don't want you to get hurt. I want you to be safe."

Max nodded. He learned his lesson. He said sorry to Lily and to Mommy. He never played in the pool again. He played with Lily on the slide. They had fun. They were safe.

Once upon a time, there was a pretty planet called Earth. All kinds of animals lived there, from big elephants to tiny ants. One day, a rabbit was hopping around when it noticed something strange. What was it? The sun was disappearing! 

The rabbit hopped to the nearest pond and yelled, "Hey frog! Do you know what's happening?" 

The frog said, "Maybe the sun is trying to take a nap. Can you see any clouds?" 

The rabbit said, "No, just the sun is gone. It seems like it has disappeared." 

The frog said, "I think it will come back soon. But if it doesn't, let's make a plan to keep the planet pretty." 

And they did! They planted trees and flowers and helped the animals. When the sun came back, the pretty planet was more beautiful than ever!

Tom and Lily were playing with their toys in the living room. Tom had a big truck and Lily had a doll. They were happy and shared their toys.

But then, Sam came in. Sam was their older brother and he was mean. He saw Tom's truck and he wanted it. He said, "Give me your truck, Tom. It is mine now."

Tom said, "No, Sam. It is my truck. You have your own toys. Go away."

Sam did not listen. He grabbed Tom's truck and ran away. Tom was sad and angry. He cried, "Sam, give me back my truck. You are a thief. You steal my truck."

Lily wanted to help Tom. She had an idea. She said, "Don't cry, Tom. I have glue. We can glue Sam's shoes to the floor. Then he can't run away with your truck."

Tom liked Lily's idea. He said, "Yes, Lily. Let's do that. Where is the glue?"

Lily said, "It is in the kitchen. Come with me."

They went to the kitchen and found the glue. They sneaked to Sam's room and saw him playing with Tom's truck. He did not notice them. They put glue on his shoes and ran away.

Soon, Sam wanted to go to the bathroom. He tried to stand up, but he could not. His shoes were stuck to the floor. He said, "Hey, what is this? Why can't I move? Help!"

Tom and Lily heard him and laughed. They said, "Ha ha, Sam. We glued your shoes to the floor. Now you can't steal our toys. Give us back Tom's truck."

Sam was scared and sorry. He said, "Please, Tom and Lily. Forgive me. I was wrong. I will give you back your truck. Just help me get out of this glue."

Tom and Lily felt sorry for Sam. They said, "OK, Sam. We will help you. But you have to promise not to steal our toys again."

Sam said, "I promise. I promise. Please, help me."

Tom and Lily got a scissors and cut Sam's shoes. They were very tight and hard to cut. But they managed to free Sam. Sam gave Tom his truck and said, "I am sorry, Tom. Here is your truck. It is very nice. Can we play together?"

Tom said, "Yes, Sam. We can play together. But you have to share and be nice."

Sam said, "I will. I will. Thank you, Tom and Lily. You are good siblings."

They hugged and went to the living room. They played with their toys and had fun. They were happy and shared their toys.

Once upon a time, there was a big, big dog named Max. Max had a patch of brown fur on his back. One day, Max was playing in the park with his friend, a little girl named Lily. 

Lily said, "Max, can you reveal what's under your patch of fur?"

Max replied, "I don't know, Lily. I've never looked."

So, Lily lifted up the patch of fur and revealed a large, white spot on Max's back. Max was surprised and happy to see it. 

"Wow, Lily! That's a big spot!" said Max.

Lily smiled and said, "It's beautiful, Max. You're a special dog." 

From that day on, Max was proud to show off his large, white spot to everyone he met.

Once upon a time there was a jolly little caterpillar. He liked to explore and was full of energy! One day, he was walking around his garden and spotted a pear on the ground. He couldn't believe his eyes! He was so excited, he wanted to show it to everyone. 

He quickly ran back to his house and knocked on the door. From inside, a friendly voice asked him to come in. He went inside and saw a ginger cat. The cat asked, "What is it, caterpillar?"

The caterpillar replied, "Look what I found! A pear!" He held up the pear and the cat's eyes widened.

The cat responded, "I love pears! Let's have a picnic and share it." The caterpillar was so happy he jumped up and down.

They spread a blanket and talked about the caterpillar's adventure while they ate the pear. When they were finished, the caterpillar said, "That was jolly!" And when it was time to go home, the caterpillar left feeling very content and happy.

Anna and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to slide on the big slide. It was fun and fast. They took turns to go down the slide.

One time, Anna saw a small pebble on the slide. It was white and shiny. She wanted to pick it up and keep it. She thought it was a pretty stone.

"Look, Ben, I found a pebble!" she said, holding it in her hand.

"Let me see!" Ben said, reaching for the pebble.

"No, it's mine!" Anna said, pulling her hand away.

They started to fight over the pebble. They pushed and pulled and shouted.

"Stop it, you two!" a voice said. It was their mom. She had seen them fighting from the bench.

She came over and took the pebble from Anna's hand.

"This is not a toy. It's a pebble. You can't slide with it. It can hurt you or someone else. You have to share and be nice to each other. Do you understand?" she said.

Anna and Ben nodded. They felt sorry for fighting.

"Can we still slide, mom?" Ben asked.

"Yes, you can. But first, you have to say sorry to each other and give each other a hug," mom said.

Anna and Ben said sorry and hugged. They smiled and ran to the slide. They slid down together and laughed. They forgot about the pebble. They had more fun sliding with each other.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who wanted to visit a new place. She asked her mom if she could go outside and have an adventure. 

Her mom said yes, and the little girl was so excited. She put on her coat and went outside. She saw a lady walking down the street and decided to go up to her and say hello. 

The little girl said 'Hello!' to the lady, who smiled back. The lady asked if the little girl wanted to go on a walk with her. The little girl happily said yes and they started walking down the street. 

The lady was very spoiled. She liked to buy clothes and eat treats. The little girl was amazed and followed the lady as she went shopping. The lady also gave the little girl chocolates and candy, and the little girl was so happy. 

When it was time to go home, the little girl thanked the lady for her visit and gave her a big hug. The little girl skipped down the street, dreaming of the fun she had on her visit with the spoiled lady.

John and Tyler were brother and sister. John was three and Tyler was four. One day Tyler said to his brother;

"John, let's go exploring together!"
Tyler was so excited, but John was not sure.

John said, "No, I'm scared". Tyler frowned and said, "What's wrong?".
John shook his head and said, "I'm afraid I won't hear something".

Tyler looked at John, confused. John was deaf, so he would not hear if something was coming.

Tyler smiled and said, "It's ok, don't worry. I'll be your eyes and ears, and we'll stay close. I'll make sure you're safe."

John smiled and felt a little better. He said, "OK, let's go!" 

They went off on their adventure, and John had hope in his heart. He knew that his brother was looking after him, and he knew that he was safe.

Once upon a time, there was a little rabbit named Benny. Benny loved to play outside with his friends, but one day he found a big hole in the ground. It was so deep that he couldn't see the bottom. 

Benny knew he shouldn't go near the hole because it was very harsh and dangerous. But he wanted to know how deep it was, so he decided to count how many hops it would take to get to the bottom. 

Benny hopped and hopped, counting each hop until he reached the bottom. When he got there, he found a treasure chest filled with carrots! Benny was so happy and he knew he had found a great number of carrots. 

From that day on, Benny knew that even though something might seem harsh or dangerous, it could lead to a great reward if he was brave enough to explore it.

The sun was bright in the sky and everyone was having fun. But something was about to change. There was a dark cloud in the sky that was growing bigger and bigger. The wind blew and it was getting closer. 

Everyone knew what was about to happen. The lazy clouds were about to let it out. It started to rain - big, fat drops of water were coming down from the sky. 

Big people were running to their houses, but Sue was standing there. She loved the rain, so she opened her eyes wide and opened her mouth to catch some drops. She knew the rain would last for a while, so she decided to take a nap. 

When she woke up, she saw that her surroundings were so peaceful and clean. Everything was green and the sun was back in the sky. Her eyes sparkled with joy and she knew that the lazy clouds had done their job.

Once there was a little boy called Sam who was very excited about his first visit to the golf course. His Grandad had brought him to see all the amazing things he could do there.

Sam was shocked when he saw the size of the golf course. It seemed to stretch on forever, with all kinds of paths he had never seen before. But Grandad warned him that he must not go off exploring on his own.

So they stayed together, walking up and down the green paths and looking at all the different trees and plants. They watched some people playing golf and Grandad told Sam how it works.

When it was time to go home, Grandad warned Sam not to forget what they had learnt today so they can come back again soon. Sam nodded and smiled because he was very excited to come back soon and learn more about golf.

Once upon a time there was a girl called Sarah. She wanted to go on a boat, so she asked her mom if she could. Her mom said yes, so they went to the harbor. 

When they got to the harbor, Sarah saw a boat that she liked. She wanted to get on it, but her mom said no, she had to wait until the boat was ready. Sarah was sad, but she thought it would be ok. 

The boat left the harbor, and Sarah was happy. She thought about where the boat would go and what she would see. 

Suddenly, the boat came to a stop. Sarah looked around and saw that the boat was stuck. Everyone said sorry. Sarah was sad, but she tried to think of a way to get the boat unstuck. She thought and thought about it, and then she had an idea. 

She shouted out, "I know what to do! We can use the anchor!" Everyone on the boat was so excited and quickly got the anchor ready. They dropped the anchor, and it worked! The boat was unstuck, and Sarah was happy.

Everyone said, "Thank you, Sarah!", and they all sang as the boat went on its way. They were so happy and grateful to Sarah for saving the day.

Once upon a time, there was a magical kingdom. All the people in the kingdom loved decorating for parties. They had lots of fun choosing decorations for their parties.

One day, the queen had a special request. She asked the people to decorate her palace for a royal party. Everyone was excited to help.

The people worked together to put up bunting and balloons. They even made a funny sword decoration to hang on the wall. Everyone thought it was great and the queen was very happy.

When the party arrived, the decorations looked beautiful. Everyone laughed and had fun. The funny sword decoration made everyone smile. 

At the end of the night, the queen said a big thank you to everyone. She said the decorations were beautiful and the party was perfect.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny named Henry. He lived in a gloomy forest, surrounded by tall trees with long twigs. One day, Henry decided to explore the forest.

He saw an old, gnarled tree and wanted to climb it, but he couldn't reach the first branch. He cried out of frustration.

Suddenly, a friendly bear popped out from behind a bush. "What's wrong?" asked the bear.

Henry explained that he couldn't reach the first branch of the tree and asked the bear for help. The bear smiled and said, "I can help you." He bent a twig and later revealed a strong, large ladder.

Henry was so happy and thanked the bear many times. He was able to climb the tree and explore the rest of the forest.
 
The moral of this story is that even small animals can count on kind and helpful friends when needed.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved her teddy bear named Teddy. One day, Lily went to the park with Teddy. She was playing with him when she accidentally dropped him in the pond. Teddy was wet and dirty. Lily was so sad and helpless. She didn't know what to do.

Suddenly, a kind old man came by and saw that Lily was upset. He asked her what happened. Lily told him about Teddy and how he was now dirty and wet. The old man said, "Don't worry, I can help you. We can replace Teddy with a new one." Lily was happy and thanked the old man.

But the old man took Lily to a store and bought her a new teddy bear. Lily was happy to have a new teddy bear, but she felt bad for her old teddy bear that was still in the pond. She learned that it's important to take care of the things we love and not replace them so easily.

Molly was walking outside with her mom. The sky was bright and sunny. Then suddenly, Molly heard a loud sound. She said to her mom, "What was that?" Her mom replied, "Oh, that was just thunder." Molly knew that sound. She said, "I like thunder!" Then, she looked up at the sky and saw the clouds moving. 

Molly was proud of herself for knowing what thunder was. She smiled and then asked her mom, "Can I look for thunder again? Please?" Her mom was proud too and said, "Of course! You can look for thunder whenever you want."

Molly kept looking up at the sky. Every time she heard thunder, she was so happy and proud. She was proud that she knew what thunder was. She felt like she could do anything and had the biggest smile on her face.

The sky was bright and the sun was shining. Up in the sky, a mysterious bird was flying around in circles. Suddenly, the bird flew straight ahead and disappeared into a maze. 

On the ground, two little children were looking up at the sky. They were puzzled as to where the bird was going. 

"Let's go find the bird," said one child. 

The other child was a bit apprehensive. "It seems very mysterious in there," he said.

The first child replied, "Come on, let's try! I'm sure we can find the bird in the maze." 

So they both ran into the maze. They ran and twisted around the turns and soon they came to a clearing. There, in the middle of the clearing, was the mysterious bird, perched atop a tall tree. 

They stood in awe at the sight. The bird flew up in the air and the two children ran around the maze, laughing and shouting with joy. 

The bird had taken them on a mysterious journey and now it was time for them to go home.

The sun was shining in the sky, and a little girl was outside with her dad. She was wearing a skirt with a pretty waist. She had been playing with her toys, but now she wanted something more creative.

So she asked her dad, "What can I do?" Her dad smiled and said, "I have an idea!" He showed her a stick and said, "Let's make a drawing on the ground!"

The little girl was excited, so she grabbed the stick and started drawing circles, stars and other shapes in the dirt. Soon her dad was joining in too. They laughed and made more and more drawings.

When the sun started to set, the little girl's dad said, "It's time to end our drawing game." They looked over their drawings one last time, then kissed them goodbye.

The little girl felt so creative and happy. She waved goodbye to her dad and skipped off, thinking about her wonderful day.

John was excited. He was going to the park with his Mom. He got ready and ran outside. When they arrived at the park, John saw something in the sky. It was a picture! It was a big triangle with lines and dots. It seemed to appear out of nowhere. John asked his Mom what it was.

She smiled. She said, "It is an honest picture. Honest people put it in the sky for us to see. It's a special way to say hello to everyone in the world". John thought it was amazing. He wanted to stay and look at the picture, but soon it disappeared.

John and his Mom went back home and talked about the picture. John said he wanted to show it to his friends. Now when he looks into the sky, he knows the picture will appear again.

Once upon a time, there were two friends, Jack and Jill. They were playing together in the park. All of a sudden, Jack started to panic when he saw a big stack of books falling out of Jill's bag! The books started falling everywhere, and Jill couldn't pick them up fast enough. 

Jack was worried, so he tried to help. He started running around and gathering the books into a big pile. Soon, the stack of books was back together again.

Jill was very happy and thankful for Jack's help. Jack felt glad that he had been reliable and helped his friend. They hugged each other, and then went back to playing in the park. The end.

Molly and her mum were walking in the park. The sun shone and the flowers were very pretty.

â€œMolly, can you catch that key over there?â€ asked her Mum.

Molly looked where her Mum was pointing, and she saw the key. She ran across the park and jumped up high. She reached out her hand and caught the key.

â€œGood job, Molly!â€ said her Mum, and she smiled. 

Molly was very happy. She showed her Mum the key. â€œCan I keep it?â€ asked Molly.

Her Mum shook her head. â€œNo, we should put it back where it belongs. We must do the right thing.â€

So Molly and her mum walked back to the door where the key was supposed to go. Molly put the key in the lock, and it fit perfectly. 

â€œYou did a very good job catching that key, Molly,â€ said her Mum, giving her a hug.

Once upon a time there was a mommy and a tiny baby. The baby was so adorable! Mommy loved cuddling with her every day.

One evening there was an emergency. Mommy had to run out and help!

So the baby was left all alone. She started to get scared, but then she saw something outside her window. It was a friendly puppy!

The puppy started playing with the baby, and soon they were having lots of fun. They played together until the sun went down. 

Finally, mommy came back. She was so happy to see the puppy and the baby playing together. 

The puppy stayed for dinner and then it was time for him to go home. He said goodbye and waved, then ended the happy playtime.

Once upon a time there were two bears called Dave and Lucy. They lived in a forest and liked to play games. One day, they decided to play a game with blueberries. They had to see who could pick up the most.

Dave found a huge heavy blueberry. He tried to pick it up, but it was too heavy! Lucy laughed and said, â€œI think I can win this time!â€

So Lucy picked up the heavy blueberry, and Dave picked up the other blueberries. In the end, Lucy was the winner. She had picked up the most blueberries! Dave was very proud of Lucy and told her that he was happy she won.

Then, they ate all the blueberries together and went for a walk in the forest. They had lots of fun and made lots of new friends. The end.

Once upon a time, a ship sailed on the sea. It sailed over the waves, near and far. Suddenly, the ship saw an island and sailed to the shore.

The ship was glad to see the island. There were trees and flowers and birds singing. The ship captain wanted to explore the island, so the ship stopped.

The captain and the crew got off the ship and started to explore. They saw fun things and heard interesting sounds.

But soon the captain remembered something. He said to the crew, "We must tell the people back home about our adventure!" So the captain and the crew went back to the ship and sailed away.

The captain was glad to have such an adventure. He knew the people back home would like to hear about it. So he told them all about his journey on the ship and his amazing adventure on the island.

Once upon a time there was a nice pig. He lived in a small house near the fields. The pig was very happy with his life and loved playing in the sun.

One day, the pig had a bad surprise. He was stuck in a fence! He was scared and tried to get out, but it was very hard. He struggled and stuck for a long time, but he couldn't get out.

Finally, his friend the fox came to help him. With a lot of pushing and pulling, they managed to get him out. The pig was very happy.

The pig and the fox hugged and said goodbye, then the pig went home. He was tired but glad he was free, and he promised to never forget about the fox's help. The pig was very happy and never struggled like that again.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who loved to speed around. Every day she would put on her special shoes and run as fast as she could around the garden. One day, the little girl was running, when she got to the end of the garden and noticed something very exciting, a hedge!

The hedge was tall and fancy, with bright red and yellow leaves all along it. The little girl had never seen something so fancy before and she was so excited that she jumped up and down and shouted " Woo-hoo! "

The little girl ran up to the hedge and began to run around it as fast as she could. She loved the sound of the leaves rustling against each other as she sped around the hedge. She laughed and giggled as she exercised her speed, and she continued running around the hedge until she was out of breath. 

Finally, the little girl stopped and looked around. She had created a magical path around the hedge, and she turned around and plopped down on the grass to admire her work.

Once upon a time, there was a pretty little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her dolls and toys, but she didn't like to share them with her friends. One day, Lily's mom gave her a beautiful bracelet to wear on her hand. Lily loved it so much that she didn't want to take it off, not even when she went to bed.

That night, Lily had a dream about a fairy who told her that if she didn't start sharing her toys, she would lose her pretty bracelet forever. The fairy also said that if she prayed and asked for forgiveness, she would be able to keep her bracelet and make new friends.

When Lily woke up, she remembered her dream and started to think about what the fairy had said. She realized that sharing was important and decided to invite her friends over to play with her toys. They had so much fun together, and Lily felt happy because she knew she had done the right thing. She also prayed before going to bed, thanking the fairy for her advice.

From that day on, Lily always shared her toys with her friends, and her bracelet stayed on her hand, reminding her of the lesson she had learned. She knew that praying and being kind to others was the best way to keep her pretty things and make new friends.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Julia. She was three years old and very enthusiastic. Every day she would get up early and look out of her window. She could see the park in the distance and it made her very happy.

One morning, Julia put on her favourite dress and went to the park. When she got there, she saw some children playing games that looked like lots of fun. Julia became very excited and asked her mom if she could join them.

Julia's mom said, "Yes, of course you can. But first, I want you to remove your shoes."

Julia followed her mom's instructions and removed her shoes. Then she ran to join the other children playing. She was so enthusiastic that she had a lot of fun. 

At the end of the day, Julia went home happy and content, with lots of wonderful memories.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys all day long. One day, Timmy's friend came over to play with him. His friend had a cool toy that Timmy wanted to play with. Timmy asked his friend if he could lend him the toy for a little while. His friend said yes and Timmy was very happy.

The toy had a smooth texture and was very fun to play with. Timmy loved how it felt in his hands. He played with it for a while and then gave it back to his friend. Timmy's friend was happy that Timmy liked the toy so much.

Timmy's mom came in and saw the toy. She thought it looked very modern and cool. She asked Timmy's friend where he got it from. Timmy's friend said his mom bought it for him at the store. Timmy's mom said she might go to the store and get one for Timmy too. Timmy was very excited and thanked his friend for lending him the toy.

Once upon a time, there was a happy family. One day, as they were sitting in their cozy home, they heard a loud noise. They had a leak! Water was pouring out and everyone panicked.

The father quickly grabbed a big towel and started soaking up the water while the mother called a plumber. It was no easy job, but after a while the water stopped leaking. Everyone was so glad!

The mother and father hugged each other in relief. The plumber fixed the leak and the happy family was safe once more. From that moment on, they always made sure to check for any leaks in their home.

Once upon a time, there was an island far away in the sea. On this island, three friends lived. They were regular friends, they had fun together, played and laughed. But sometimes, they would quarrel too. 

One day, they had a big quarrel. They shouted and yelled, but none of them wanted to give in. They quarrelled for hours, until it was dark and the sky was full of stars.

The next day, when the tide came, Bubbles stayed with Fin. They swam together and played in the water. Fin did not shiver or hide. He was happy and not worried anymore. From that day on, Fin and Bubbles were best friends and they played in the tide every day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the garden. One day, she found a caterpillar on a leaf. It was brown and fuzzy.

Once upon a time, there was a mighty creature. It was very powerful and loved to go on adventures.

Once upon a time, there was a big house. There was a big tree in the front yard, and a swing in the backyard. Every day, a family moved around the house and the yard. They were happy.

But one day, something strange started to happen. Smoke moved around the house. It was grey and it made everything strange. But the family didn't know where it was coming from. 

So the family moved around looking for the source of the smoke. Then, they found it! It was a big fire! The family was scared, so they moved away quickly. 

The family was relieved the fire was so far away. They called the fireman to put out the fire. Soon, the fire was gone and the family moved back near the house.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She liked to play outside in her yard with her toys. One day, she heard a sound that made her stop playing. It was a beautiful song that sounded like it was coming from up high in the sky.

Lily looked up and saw an angel with big white wings singing the song. She was amazed and watched as the angel flew away. Lily felt happy and knew that the angel's song was special. She wanted to hear it again, so she waited outside every day hoping to hear it once more.

Days went by and Lily didn't hear the angel's song again, but she didn't give up hope. She knew that the angel's voice was high and sweet, and that it would come back to her one day. And it did! One sunny day, Lily heard the angel's song again and she smiled with joy. From that day on, Lily knew that angels were real and that they could sing beautiful songs for everyone to hear.

Mum and Dad squabbled about the puzzle. Dad said it was too hard for the three year old and Mum said it was perfect because it was going to help the child learn. They were both very cross with each other.

The child sat on the floor, watching them bicker. The child was too scared to get involved in the quarrel.

"Let the child decide," said Mum sternly.

Dad looked thoughtful. He rubbed his chin then he asked the child, "Do you want to try the puzzle?"

The child smiled and nodded. With a huge grin, the child reached out and grabbed the puzzle.

The Mum and Dad watched with joy as the child worked on the puzzle. Soon the child was finished! It was perfect.

Mum and Dad hugged the child. They had forgotten all about the quarrel, and were happy that their little one had been brave enough to try the puzzle. With smiles all round, the family finished the day together.

Once upon a time, there was a very rich man. The man always wanted new things. So, he went everyday to the store and he always ordered something.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Janie. She was very independent and loved to play around the house.

Everyday, Jack and Jill would play tag and Jack would repeatly tag Jill. Jack and Jill were having lots of fun together and also became best friends. They played tag every day until they grew old.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Mike. He was a curious little boy and loved to explore. One day Mike decided to go on an adventure.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Marcy. She lived in a big city and was very interested in fashion. She loved to admire all the beautiful clothes that were in the store windows.

The three friends Jack, Cindy and Tom were playing together one day at the park. They were very happy! They played tag and laughed and ran around.

Suddenly, Jack and Cindy started to quarrel. They argued very loudly and Tom was very sad. He wanted to make them smile again.

Once upon a time, there lived a family of four. They had a lovely olive tree in their garden. Now and then, they would part the olives from the tree, and enjoy them together.

Once upon a time, there was a little birdie named Blue. Blue loved to fly high in the sky and land on trees. One day, Blue wanted to send a letter to his friend who lived far away. So, Blue went to the post office to mail the letter. 

On the way back, Blue saw a big and comfortable nest on a tree. Blue thought it would be nice to rest there for a while. But the nest belonged to another birdie who didn't want Blue to stay. Blue felt sad and flew away to find another place to rest.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the big green grassy field near her house. One day, she saw a red ball bouncing towards her. Once upon a time, there was a restless little girl who wanted to go on an adventure. So, her mummy said she could take a towel with her and go for a walk in the park.

Once upon a time, there was a special boy called Peter. He wanted to help the world become a better place. Every day, Peter came up with ideas to help his neighbourhood.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Matt. Matt had a special message to share with the world. She wanted to tell everyone how important it was to be kind to each other.

But Matt was being very selfish. She kept the message all to herself, even though she knew it would help others.

One day, Matt was playing in the park. As she walked past a group of children, one of them reached out and touched her very gently.

Matt stopped and looked around. She realized that everyone in the park - the children, the birds, and the flowers - was connected. Everyone was part of the same family.

Matt finally understood her message: we are all connected and we must take care of each other. She shared her message with all the children in the park. They were so excited that they all smiled and cheered. 

From then on, Matt shared her message with everyone she met - sharing kindness and joy with the world.

It was a sunny day and two friends, Jake and Lucy, were playing in the park. They saw something in the water. It was a big otter! Jake wanted to get closer and pushed the otter with his foot. Suddenly, the otter jumped up and it scared Lucy. The otter was so sleepy and it did not want to move. Jake and Lucy watched it and they thought it was so fun. 

Soon, the otter started to move again and it swam away. Jake and Lucy waved goodbye and then they started running back to the park on the other side of the lake. They chased each other until they were both very tired. Then, they sat down together and laughed about the sleepy otter. 

Jake and Lucy had a wonderful day!

Once upon a time there was a little bird who lived in a big tree. Every day she would dream up new things to do and then she would follow them. One day the little bird had a very thoughtful idea; she wanted to make a folder!

So, she started to look for things to make the folder out of. She saw some leaves and thought they would be perfect. She picked a few of the best leaves and started to glue them together.

It wasn't easy, but eventually the little bird had made her folder! She was so proud of it that she wanted to show it to everyone. And so she flew around the tree, showing off her new folder to all the other birds.

Everyone was very impressed and thought the little bird was very thoughtful. From then on she kept her folder close to her and she was always ready to show it off to her new friends.

Lila and Ben were best friends. They liked to play with their toys and share them with each other. One day, they found an enormous box in the garage. It was bigger than their bed. They wondered what was inside.

"Let's open it!" Ben said.

"OK, but we have to share whatever we find," Lila said.

They pulled and pushed the box until they made a hole. They peeked inside and saw many colorful things. They saw books, clothes, games, and pictures. They also saw a big flag with stars and stripes.

"What is this?" Lila asked.

"It's a flag. It's from a nation. A nation is a big place with many people and houses and cars," Ben said. He remembered what his dad had told him.

"Wow, it's pretty. Can we play with it?" Lila asked.

"Sure, but we have to be careful. It's very old and special. It belonged to my grandpa. He was a soldier. He fought for the nation. He was brave and strong," Ben said. He felt proud of his grandpa.

They took the flag out of the box and spread it on the floor. They pretended to be soldiers and heroes. They saluted and marched and sang. They had a lot of fun. They also looked at the other things in the box and learned about the nation and the world.

They played until it was time for dinner. They folded the flag and put it back in the box. They also put back the other things. They thanked their grandpa for sharing his stories and memories with them. They hugged each other and smiled.

They were happy. They had shared a wonderful adventure.

Once upon a time, there was a nosy girl named Joy. Whenever the neighbour did the laundry, Joy wanted to watch. One day, she got a bit too close and stepped on the wet clothes.

The neighbour, Mrs. Johnson, didn't get mad. She knew that Joy was curious and trusted her to be careful. Mrs. Johnson even asked Joy to help put the clean clothes away.

Joy was so happy to help! She trusted Mrs. Johnson to show her how to do the laundry right. It wasn't easy--loading the machine and getting the clothes dry--but Mrs. Johnson never scolded Joy if she made a mistake. She just corrected her and praised her when she did something right.

That day, Joy learned to trust herself and trust that people can be kind. And she also learned that being nosy isn't always a bad thing--as long as you trust the people around you.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to wear her big, warm coat when it was cold outside. One day, Lily's mom told her to put on her coat and follow her. Lily asked, "Where are we going?" Her mom said, "I will lead the way."

They walked outside and it was very cold. Lily's face turned pale because of the cold wind. She said to her mom, "I'm cold." Her mom replied, "Don't worry, your coat will keep you warm." They walked and walked until they reached a big park with lots of trees. Lily's mom said, "Let's go play!" Lily was so happy and ran to the playground.

Lily's mom watched her play and smiled. She said, "I'm glad we came outside today." Lily replied, "Me too, Mommy. Thank you for leading me here." They played and had fun until it was time to go home. Lily hugged her mom and said, "I love you." Her mom hugged her back and said, "I love you too."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to cook with her mommy in the kitchen. One day, they decided to make cookies. Lily put all the ingredients in a big bowl and mixed them together. Then, she put the cookie dough on a tray and put it in the oven to cook.

After a few minutes, Lily smelled something burning. She opened the oven and saw that the cookies were burnt. She was sad and started to cry. Her mommy hugged her gently and said, "It's okay, we can make more cookies another day."

Lily wiped her tears and decided to put the burnt cookies in a bag to throw them away. But as she was walking to the trash can, she tripped and fell. The bag of burnt cookies spilled all over the floor. Lily was sad again, but her mommy hugged her gently and said, "It's okay, accidents happen."

Even though the cookies were burnt and spilled, Lily learned that it's okay to make mistakes and that her mommy will always be there to hug her gently.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved eating candy. Every Wednesday, he would go to the store to buy some candy. But one Wednesday, the store had no candy left. Timmy was sad and cried.

Once there was a little boy who wanted to play outside. He saw an ugly pine tree in the forest and decided to climb it. He grabbed a branch and started to climb up, but he soon realized it was too high. He started to get scared but then he thought to himself, I can do it! I just have to hope.

So, the brave little boy kept climbing and eventually he made it to the top. From the very top of the pine tree, he could see all the way past the forest to the little town. He was so excited to see the town, he waved and shouted, "Hello!"

The little boy smiled, thinking how wonderful it was to see the town from the top of the ugly pine tree. He thanked the pine tree for helping him reach his goal, and started to climb back down. 

From that day on, the little boy would hope for great things and knew that no matter how high or how hard he had to climb, he could do it.

Once there was a little girl called Sarah. She was a brave three-year-old. One day Sarah went outside and saw a big box. She was curious and wanted to explore it. She walked closer and opened the lid. Inside was a funny looking toy. Sarah was glad. She reached in to pick it up but something scared her. It was a spooky noise! 

At first Sarah was scared but then she remembered she was brave. She took a deep breath and looked inside the box again. She saw the funny toy was shaking and making the spooky noises. Sarah was so happy that she had not been scared away.

She was really glad she had not been scared by the funny toy.

Sam was trying to learn how to write. He was sitting at the kitchen table with a pen and a piece of paper. He asked his daddy, "Can you help me write?"

He pointed and asked, "Daddy what is this?"

Sam took a sip. "Yummy! Daddy, you are the best!"

Once upon a time, in a small place, there was a red ball. The red ball had many friends who liked to play with it. They would roll it, bounce it, and throw it in the air. The red ball was very happy because it felt valued by its friends.

It was a bright and sunny day, and the little birds were chirping in the trees. Everywhere, animals were waking up and getting ready to start their day.

When everyone was exhausted from the Nut Shuffle, they all agreed it was one of the best celebrations ever! They had fun playing, eating, and dancing together in the harmless way of nature. All of the animals smiled in awe of the beauty of nature and its celebration of life.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Lucy. She was three years old and loved to explore her house. One day, she found an old flute tucked away in a cupboard.
