Buzzy was so curious that he decided to fly over to the strange hive. He buzzed around it a few times, and then decided to peek inside. It was full of different kinds of goodies that he'd never seen before!

He smiled and flew back to his own hive with some of the treats. Ever since then, Buzzy has been skipping around the garden with a bit more excitement. He never knows when he'll find a new and exciting hive!

Once upon a time there was a penguin. He was ugly and he didn't have any friends. One day he saw a pretty bird flying in the sky and he wanted to be friends with it.

So the penguin yelled "Hey! I want to be your friend!"
The bird said back "No, I don't want to be friends with an ugly penguin like you!"
The penguin was sad. He didn't know what to do.

Suddenly, he had an idea. He remembered he had something special in his pocket. He took it out and showed it to the bird. It was a shiny balloon. The bird loved how sparkly it was!

The bird asked the penguin "What can I do with it?" 
The penguin said "Attach it to the branch up there and it will stay in the sky forever!" So the bird attached the balloon to the branch and flew away.

The penguin was happy that the bird was now his friend. He wasn't so ugly anymore. From that day on, the penguin was never alone. He had a very special friend.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Pip. Pip loved to listen to the sounds of the forest. One day, Pip found a delicate egg on the ground. 

Pip was worried that the egg might break, so she asked her friend, a wise old owl, what to do. "You must be very careful," said the owl. "Eggs are fragile and delicate. You must keep it safe and warm." 

Pip was happy to have the owl's advice. She listened carefully and then flew away with the egg in her beak. She found a cozy nest and carefully placed the egg inside. 

Days went by and Pip listened closely to the egg. She heard a faint tapping sound. Suddenly, the egg cracked open and a tiny chick emerged. Pip was overjoyed and chirped happily to her new friend. "Hello little one," she said. "I'm so glad you hatched safely!"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lola. One day, Lola was walking in the park and she felt sad. She saw a boy playing in the sunshine and wanted to join in.

The boy asked "Why are you so sad?"

Lola said "I'm sad because I have a lot to solve and I don't know how to do it".

The boy said "Don't worry! You can do hard things. Close your eyes and think fast. With sunshine, even hard things can be solved".

Lola felt hopeful. She took a deep breath, closed her eyes and thought hard. When she opened her eyes, she had the answer!

Lola smiled and said "Thank you, Sunshine Boy! With your help, I solved it!"

The moral of the story is that with sunshine, even hard things can be solved. With hard work and determination, we can solve any problem.

Lily and Ben like to play with dough. They have many colors of dough. They can make shapes and animals with dough. They have fun with dough.

One day, they find a new dough in the kitchen. It is brown and soft. Lily and Ben want to play with it. They touch the dough. It is sticky and smelly. They do not like it.

"Yuck! What is this dough?" Lily asks.

"It is not dough. It is bread. Mommy is making bread," Ben says.

They hear Mommy coming. They hide the dough behind their backs. They smile at Mommy.

"Hello, my little bakers. What are you doing?" Mommy asks.

"We are playing with dough," Lily and Ben say.

Mommy sees the dough behind their backs. She smells the dough. She laughs.

"That is not dough. That is bread dough. It is for baking, not for playing. It is smelly because it has yeast. Yeast makes the bread rise and fluffy," Mommy explains.

Lily and Ben look at the dough. They do not understand.

"Can we play with it?" Lily asks.

"No, you cannot. It is not good for playing. It is good for eating. But you can help me make the bread. Do you want to?" Mommy asks.

Lily and Ben nod. They like to help Mommy. They wash their hands. They follow Mommy to the oven. They see a big pan with more dough. Mommy puts the dough in the oven. She sets the timer.

"Now we wait. The bread will bake and smell good. Then we can eat it with butter and jam. How does that sound?" Mommy asks.

Lily and Ben clap. They are happy. They wait for the bread. They smell the bread. They do not touch the bread. They know it is hot. They wait for Mommy to cut the bread. They eat the bread. They like the bread. They do not like the dough. They like to play with dough. But they like to eat bread.

Once upon a time, there was a pink bear. One morning the bear woke up and went for a walk outside. As the bear strolled, it observed the wonderful things around it. The bear noticed the shining sun, the puffy clouds, and the tall trees.

Suddenly, the bear came across a little girl. She was very sad and had tears in her eyes. The bear approached her with compassion and asked her why she was crying.

The girl told the bear she couldn't find her mommy. The bear showed the girl its warm hug, and told her not to worry; her mommy was sure to come back.

The bear observed the girl take comfort in its embrace. Finally, the girl stood up and continued her search. With that, the bear said goodbye and went its own way. It had been a wonderful day!

It was a very hot day and Marty the Bear was feeling lazy and tired. He wanted to find something fun to do, but he couldn't think of anything. Suddenly he remembered something. "I know!" said Marty, as he remembered a special challenge from his friends. They had told him about a large oak tree in the forest under which a mystery was hidden. Marty knew that if he solved the mystery, he would have loads of fun.

Excited, he got up and ran off to the woods. As he arrived, he saw the large oak tree up ahead of him and he was filled with anticipation. He searched the tree's trunk and branches, but he couldn't find the mystery. Just then, he spotted a small hole behind the tree. He carefully peered inside and saw a shiny object. "What's this?" he said. Marty had solved the mystery.

He reached inside and pulled out a shining golden treasure chest. Inside were lots of bright and colourful toys and treats. Marty was so happy, he decided to stay in the shade of the large oak tree to play with his new treasures. His solved the mystery and it was a day of fun and adventure.

One day, a small kitten was playing in the garden. His tail was long and fluffy and he had big, round eyes. He was very curious and explored everything. As he was walking past a tree, he heard a whistle. He stopped and looked all around to try and find out where the noise was coming from. After a few moments of searching, he saw a little bird perched on the edge of a branch. The bird was chirping happily and its tail was swinging back and forth as it sang.

The kitten watched in awe and enjoyed listening to the bird's cheerful tune. He wanted to join in the song, but wasn't sure how. The bird kept chirping, so the kitten meowed gently in reply. The bird stopped singing and kept its eye on the kitten. The kitten meowed again, this time being more persistent with its meowing. Finally, the bird started to whistle again, this time slower, like it was teaching the kitten a song.

The tiny kitten was in awe. He followed the bird's tune and tried to get it just right. He was so focused and eager to learn the song, determined to make it perfect. After some time, the kitten managed to whistle almost exactly like the bird. He was so proud of himself and could hardly believe it! The bird smiled and chirped one last time to show its approval before flying away. As it disappeared, the happy kitten meowed in reply.

Once upon a time, there was a little cat. The cat had a dirty paw. It was nervous because it did not like dirty paws. The cat wanted to play with its friends, but it was scared that they would see its dirty paw.

The cat saw a soft cloth. It thought, "I can use this to wipe my paw!" The cat was happy to find a way to clean its paw. It wiped and wiped until the paw was clean.

Now, the cat was not nervous anymore. It ran to play with its friends. They played all day, and the cat was very happy. The cat knew that if its paw got dirty again, it could just wipe it clean.

Once upon a time there was an independent pumpkin. It was very special. Every day it suggested going on an adventure. One day the pumpkin decided to take its own advice. It rolled away from its patch and started exploring. 

The pumpkin met a rabbit, two birds, and a frog. They all suggested things to do. The pumpkin enjoyed learning about the world and finding new experiences. The rabbit suggested they hunt for mushrooms, the two birds suggested picking berries in the forest, and the frog suggested catching tadpoles in a nearby stream. 

The pumpkin was so excited. It tried all their suggestions and had an amazing day. At the end of the day, the pumpkin said goodbye to its new friends, thanked them for all the suggestions, and went on its way back to the pumpkin patch.

The independent pumpkin had learned many new things and felt full of excitement. It had a wonderful day thanks to its friends' help.

There was a very thick fire. It was very hot and it made a lot of smoke. Two little children, Sammy and Jack, were very scared. They wanted to touch it. 

Their mom said, "No, you must not touch the fire, it's too hot". But Sammy and Jack were very curious and tried to touch it anyway. 

Their mom said, "It's not a good idea to touch the fire, it's too hot. It could hurt you". 

But Sammy and Jack didn't listen, they reached out and touched it! Immediately they felt the heat, and they quickly pulled their hands away. 

Their mom said, "See, I told you not to touch the fire, it can burn you!" 

After that, Sammy and Jack stayed far away from the thick fire. They knew it was too dangerous to touch it!

Mummy took Jack to the park. He looked around and saw lots of things to play with. Jack's eyes lit up when he saw a swing! It was big and green. He sprinted towards it, his chubby legs pumping up and down. Mum laughed and hurried after him.

Jack laughed as he went higher and higher on the swing. He let go with his hands and he flew through the air. Jack shouted with glee.

When he got off the swing, Jack spotted a stone. It was pink and shiny. He picked it up to look at it, but it was too heavy. So Jack rolled it along the ground. He laughed as it went faster and faster, then it finally stopped. 

Mummy asked Jack if he wanted to go back to the swing and Jack nodded his head. He hopped back onto the swing, excited to fly again. He kicked his legs out and the swing started to move. Round and round and round he went, feeling just like a bird. 

Mummy watched Jack have so much fun, then it was time to go home. Jack hugged his stone close to his chest and ran off, back to the swing one last time.

One day, Mama and Baby were walking in the garden. Mama pointed to a large cauliflower, and said to Baby, "Look Baby, isn't it beautiful?" Baby looked excitedly and said, "Yes, Mama, it is beautiful." Mama wanted to encourage Baby to try something new. She said, "Come, try it." Baby looked hesitant and shook her head. 

Mama smiled at Baby and said, "It's okay, Baby. Let's try it together. It'll be fun!" Baby thought for a moment, and then smiled. She said, "Okay, Mama."

Mama had cut up some of the cauliflower, and Baby carefully tasted it. She was surprised! It was tasty and crunchy! She smiled at Mama and said, "I like it!" Mama was relieved and happy, and said, "See, Baby, it's good, right? Now let's put it into the pot and make a peaceful dinner." Baby smiled, and said, "Yes! Let's do it!" 

Mama and Baby cooked together, and were proud of their peaceful dinner. Mama said to Baby, "See, Baby, I encouraged you to try something new, and you tried it! That's great!" Baby smiled and said, "Yes, Mama. It was yummy!"

Once there was a little girl. She was very small and was only 3 years old. One day, she had a bright idea. She saw a big television and wanted to push it. She thought, "Maybe if I push this, something cool will happen!"

But the television wouldn't move. The little girl was so frustrated, she started to cry. Then, she heard a voice. It said, "What are you doing? That's a very stupid idea."

The little girl looked up and saw her mom. Her mom said, "You can't push the television - it's too big and too heavy. Don't be so stupid!"

The little girl pouted and walked away. It was a silly idea, she thought. Maybe she would find something she could push next time.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat ice cream with a spoon. One day, she went to the ice cream store with her mom. They looked at all the flavors and Lily picked her favorite, chocolate!

But when they got home, Lily was troubled. She couldn't find her spoon! She looked all around the kitchen and even asked her mom to help. Finally, her mom said, "Lily, did you check inside the ice cream container?" 

Lily opened the container and there it was! Her spoon was inside, waiting for her to use it. Lily was so happy and thanked her mom for helping her find it. She learned that sometimes things can include surprises, even her spoon!

Once upon a time there was an ancient crack in the ground. One day, a little girl noticed the crack and decided to take a closer look.

"What is this?" asked the little girl.

"It is an ancient crack," answered her father. "It has been here for many years and it's very special."

The little girl touched the crack with her fingers. It felt rough and cool.

"Can I take a nap here?" she asked.

"Of course," said her father.

So the little girl laid down in the crack with a smile on her face. She fell asleep and had the best nap ever. When she woke up, the little girl was so happy. Since then, she often goes back to the ancient crack to take a nap in the sunshine.

Once upon a time, there was a lively raven. He flew high in the sky and his feathers were so dark that he looked like a storm cloud. The raven liked to soar in the sky, but one day he appeared on the ground. He landed gently on soft grass and looked around. He saw a field with bright yellow flowers, so he hopped through them and sung a happy song. The flowers swayed with the wind and the sun shone on his wings.

The raven then hopped to a big tree and flapped his wings. He wanted to rest a while, so he perched on a branch. He took a deep breath and closed his eyes. All of a sudden, he heard a noise and his eyes snapped open. He was so surprised to see a little bunny hopping below him! The bunny had a big smile and a twinkle in his eyes. The raven chirped in happiness and flapped his wings as he flew away.

He soared in the sky and looked down at the ground. The bunny was gone now, but it was nice to see a creature so alive and full of joy. The raven smiled and continued to fly through the sky, happy and lively!

John was a small boy with black hair. He lived with his parents in a little house. One day, his parents gave him a special toy. It was green and had a funny face. John was so excited he didn't know what to do.

John started to rub the toy with his hands. Suddenly, the toy started to shake and change colour. It was now black! John was so surprised and he just kept on rubbing the toy.

The toy made a funny sound. John kept rubbing until the toy remained still. Then, John played with his black toy all day long. He enjoyed the day very much.

Sammy was playing in the park when he saw something strange. In the corner of the park was a tiny world, like an ant could fit there. Sammy was mesmerised, so he moved closer to look.

But as he got closer, he heard loud noises coming from the world. It was a battle! Animals and humans were fighting with each other and food were everywhere. Sammy was scared and he wanted to get away.

He was about to turn and run when he noticed a small bird on the ground. The bird was hurt, it's feathers were scruffy and its stomach was empty. So Sammy picked up the bird and fed it.

Soon the bird began to get fit. It moved around more and its feathers were becoming pretty. But still there was a battle in the tiny world. Sammy wanted to help the bird go back home, but he didn't know how to end the battle.

But then he had an idea. If he could get some food to the animals and the humans, maybe he could feed them and stop the fight. So he put some food in the centre of the world and gradually the battle began to die out.

The world was now fit, peaceful and full of food. Sammy had saved the day and the little bird was safe. He felt proud for making a difference and for helping his small feathered friend.

Once upon a time, there was an animal. He was a large, brown bear. But he was broken. One day, he was walking and carrying a big stick, but he was too heavy. The stick dropped to the ground and made a loud noise. The animal was sad and he started to cry.

But then out of the corner of his eye, he saw a bright, yellow butterfly. He watched as it fluttered around and lit up the sky. Seeing the butterfly made him feel better and he stopped crying. He bent down and picked up the stick. Then, he went on his way.

As the animal went on his way, he saw a broken bird in a tree. He reached up and carefully dropped the stick. Then, he used the stick to help the bird and carefully carried her away until she felt safe.

The animal was happy that he was able to help the bird, but he felt a little sad about his broken stick. He put the stick back where he had found it and smiled as he saw the bright, yellow butterfly flying around again. 

The animal was still broken, but he was content knowing that he had made the world a brighter, and safer, place for one small animal.

Once there was a tidy player. He liked to do tricks like kicking a round ball from one place to another. He was always very careful with his stepping too. Every day he would practice his tricks and stepping in the field outside his house.

One day, after practicing for hours, the player stepped wrong. He stumbled and could not recover. He fell right on a big rock, and all of his tricks were forgotten. He started to cry.

Meanwhile, a small animal in the field nearby watched this happen, and saw the player start to cry. The animal knew that the player was in trouble, so it came closer to his side. The animal hopped next to the player and stepped on the ground in a very special way. After watching the animal, the player understood what he had to do. He tried the same steps and suddenly, all his tricks came back! He was so relieved.

It was the little animal's special way of helping the player. And from that day onwards, the player always made sure his steps were very tidy and safe.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Tom and Pete. Tom liked to walk and Pete liked to jump. They both had a jolly time together.

One day, Tom and Pete decided to go for a walk. Tom brought a long, soft rope with him. They walked and walked until they saw a big hill.

Pete had a great idea. He said, "Let's use the rope to slide down the hill." 

Tom was so excited! He tied one end of the rope to a tree and the other end to his waist. Then Pete pushed him and he slid down the hill on the rope! It was so much fun!

When they finished sliding down the hill, they both had big smiles on their faces. Tom and Pete had a jolly time together and they walked home happily.

Once upon a time, there were two sisters. One of them was very quiet and the other sister was very active. One day, the active sister wanted to escape. She couldn't find a way out of the house, so she started to try unusual things. She tried climbing the walls, but she couldn't reach the top. She tried jumping out of the window, but she wasn't tall enough.

Finally, she thought of an unusual plan. She took a long blanket and tied it to the roof. Then, she climbed up the blanket and used it to escape out of the window. She was so happy and shouted with joy. The other sister smiled and cheered her on.

The active sister had escaped and she was free! That night, both sisters shared a very special moment. They laughed, hugged and enjoyed the freedom that came with her escape. What an unusual adventure!

Once upon a time there were two bears who were very different. One bear was fat and one was slim.

The fat bear always wanted to do big things, but he always failed. The slim bear was content with doing small things and he always succeeded.

One day, the slim bear wanted to get some cauliflower for dinner. He worked very hard for it and after a few days he got it. The fat bear thought it was too hard and he gave up.

The slim bear taught the fat bear an important lesson. He said: "It is better to try and succeed with small things than to try and fail with big things".

The fat bear took this lesson to heart and from then on he stopped trying to do big things. He kept at the small things he could do and he finally started to succeed.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the park. One day, she saw a merry-go-round and asked her friend, "Can we spin on it?"

Her friend said, "Yes, let's spin around and around!" They both got on the merry-go-round and started to spin. Lily felt so dizzy, but she didn't want to stop spinning.

Suddenly, they saw a big fire in the distance. They quickly got off the merry-go-round and ran to tell the grown-ups. The firemen came and put out the fire. Lily felt proud that she helped to save the day.

Once upon a time, there was a mummy who had to decide what to make for dinner. She put on her apron and went to the kitchen. 

In the kitchen, she saw a funny looking hat. She thought it was foolish to wear such a hat and decided to leave it in the kitchen. 

But then the little boy came in and wanted to wear the hat. He begged and begged for the mummy to let him wear it. 

The mummy thought for a moment, and then decided that it was ok for the little boy to wear the funny hat. 

They both laughed and laughed until mummy got back to deciding what to make for dinner.

Once upon a time there was a chubby little lab. He was so happy and playful that he liked to stay in his lab all day. It was so much fun for him to stay there, he would look around and explore. He found lots of exciting things to explore and play with.

One day he found a big box filled with soft, furry toys. He stayed in the box for hours, playing and cuddling the toys. He knew this was the place for him to stay and explore. He liked the feeling of being safe and happy.

The lab enjoyed staying in his lab every day. He would run around and explore. He would look for something new and always have lots of fun. He even ate chubby treats in his lab so he could stay happy and healthy.

The lab had so much fun playing and staying in his lab every day. He loved the feeling of being safe, happy and having fun. He knew he would never want to leave his lab. He would always stay if he could.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to play outside. One day, she went on a walk with her mommy and daddy. Suddenly, Lily felt an itch on her arm. She scratched and scratched but the itch wouldn't go away.

Lily's mommy asked her, "What's wrong, sweetie?" Lily answered, "My arm itches!" Her mommy said, "Let's put some cream on it when we get home."

Lily was excited to get home and put cream on her itchy arm. When they finally arrived home, her mommy put cream on her arm and the itch went away. Lily was so happy and excited that she gave her mommy a big hug and said, "Thank you for answering my itch!"

One day, a jolly cat named Tom was playing with his toy. He loved his toy so much. But one day, his toy broke. Tom was very sad.

Tom had an idea. He would find a new toy to replace his old one. So, he went to look for a new toy. He looked and looked, but he could not find a toy he liked.

At last, Tom found a toy he liked. It was a big, soft ball. He played with it all day. But when it was time to sleep, Tom could not sleep. The big, soft ball made a loud noise when he moved it. It would wake him up.

Tom knew he had to find a new toy that would not wake him up. So, the next day, he looked again. He found a small, quiet toy. It was just right for him.

Now, Tom was a jolly cat again. He had a new toy that did not wake him up. He played with it all day and slept well at night.

One day, Tim went to play in the yard. He saw a mysterious box. It was big and blue. Tim was very curious.

He asked his mom, "What is in the box?" She said, "It's a surprise, but I will remind you later."

Tim played with his toys and forgot about the box. His mom came out and said, "Do you want to open the box now?" Tim was excited and said, "Yes, please!"

They opened the box together. Inside was a big, red ball. Tim was so happy. He played with the ball all day in the yard.

Ben and Lily are at the park with Mom. They see a big fountain with water that goes up and down. They want to play near the fountain, but Mom says no. She says the water is cold and they might get wet.

Ben and Lily are sad. They want to have fun with the water. They see some ducks swimming in the fountain. They think the ducks are happy. They ask Mom if they can feed the ducks. Mom says yes, but they have to be careful.

Ben and Lily take some bread from Mom and go to the fountain. They throw some bread to the ducks. The ducks come closer and eat the bread. Ben and Lily are happy. They laugh and clap.

But one duck is angry. He does not like to share the bread. He wants all the bread for himself. He quacks loudly and chases the other ducks away. He sees Ben and Lily and thinks they have more bread. He swims fast to them and tries to bite them.

Ben and Lily are scared. They scream and run away from the fountain. Mom hears them and comes to help. She sees the angry duck and shoos him away. She hugs Ben and Lily and says they are safe.

Ben and Lily are glad. They say sorry to Mom for going too close to the fountain. Mom says it is okay, but they have to be more careful next time. She says they can go to the playground and play on the slide. Ben and Lily smile and say yes. They leave the fountain and the angry duck behind. They have fun on the slide.

Once upon a time, there was a bossy girl who liked to play with her iron. Every day she pretended she was a superhero and fought with the bad guys. 

But one day, something made her sad. No one could make her stop from weeping. Even her iron and her superhero cape could not cheer her up. 

Her mum came to give her a hug, and wiped her tears away. She said the kindest things, that made the girl feel special. 

The little girl was still sad, so mum asked her why she was crying. The little girl said that she was sad because her best friend couldn't play with her, but it made her feel happy when mum hugged her. 

The next day, the little girl was smiling and playing with her iron again. But she would never forget the day she wept, and the hug her mum gave her too.

Once upon a time, there was a jeep. It was perfect. The jeep loved to travel, so it urged its little driver to take it on an adventure.

The driver was a 3 year old child and they were very excited. "Let's go!" they shouted and the jeep roared with delight.

They drove through the countryside, passing fields and animals. All the while, the jeep urged its passengers to keep going until they reached the beach.

Once they were there, the jeep stopped and looked around. The little driver couldn't help but admire how perfect it looked. Suddenly, something strange happened - the jeep rolled into the sea!

The child thought they were done for but the jeep drove them all the way to a nearby island. It was perfect. The child laughed and thanked their jeep for a wonderful excursion.

Tommy was walking through the park all alone. He was feeling very lonely, but he was determined to find something to do to keep himself busy. He heard a loud whistle in the distance, so he followed the sound.

When Tommy arrived at the end of the park, He saw a young man playing a flute. He was surrounded by a strip of brightly coloured flags and Tommy was fascinated. He stood and watched the man perform.
 
After a few minutes, the man noticed Tommy and gave him a warm smile. 
â€œHey little one! Would you like to join me in my performance?â€

Tommy was very excited. He ran over and grabbed a flute from the man. He started to play and the two of them began to create a beautiful melody. All the loneliness that had been weighing down on Tommy suddenly disappeared.

Everyone that was walking through the park stopped to listen and enjoy the music. After a while, when the sun had gone down, the man and Tommy stopped playing and said their goodbyes. 

Tommy continued his walk home, but this time, he was no longer lonely. He whistled happily as he remembered the special moment they had shared.

Once upon a time, there was a careless peach tree. The sun shone, the birds sang and the little peach tree grew.

One day, a little girl called Emily was walking in the woods. She was so excited when she spotted a peach on the careless tree. She stretched up and grabbed it.

"This peach looks so delicious!" Emily said.

But when she went to take a bite, she tasted something sour.

"Why does this peach taste bad?" Emily asked.

The tree sighed. "I've become carelessly over-ripe," he explained.

Emily smiled. She knew what had to be done.

"If I give you lots of love and water," she said, "you'll become strong and healthy again."

And sure enough, with Emily's help, the careless peach tree became a beautiful, healthy tree, with lots of juicy peaches.

Tim and Mia were playing in the park with their ball. They liked to kick the ball to each other and run after it. Sometimes they saw cars on the road and they tried to guess their colors and shapes.

"Look, Mia, a red car!" Tim shouted, pointing to a shiny car that zoomed past them.

"I see it, Tim, it's very fast!" Mia said, clapping her hands.

They watched the car disappear around the corner and then they saw another car coming. But this car was very different from the red car. It was enormous, with big wheels and a loud horn. It was a truck, but Tim and Mia did not know that word.

"Wow, what is that?" Tim asked, his eyes wide.

"I don't know, but it's huge!" Mia said, holding Tim's hand.

The truck stopped near the park and the driver got out. He was a tall man with a hat and a beard. He smiled at Tim and Mia and waved to them.

"Hello, kids, do you like my truck?" he asked.

"Yes, we do, it's amazing!" Tim said.

"Can we see it closer?" Mia asked.

"Sure, come on, I'll show you around. But first, can you do something for me?" the driver said.

"What is it?" Tim and Mia asked.

"Can you whistle?" the driver asked.

Tim and Mia nodded. They had learned how to whistle from their dad. They put their lips together and blew. They made a soft sound, like a bird.

"Very good, very good!" the driver said, clapping his hands. "Now, can you whistle louder, like this?" He put his fingers in his mouth and blew. He made a loud sound, like a whistle.

Tim and Mia tried to copy him, but they could not. They only made funny noises and spit.

The driver laughed. "Don't worry, it takes practice. But you know what? You can use my horn instead. It's much louder and easier. Do you want to try?"

"Yes, please!" Tim and Mia said.

The driver took them to his truck and showed them a big button on the dashboard. He told them to press it and see what happened.

Tim and Mia pressed the button and the truck made a loud honk. They jumped and giggled. They pressed it again and again, making the truck honk louder and louder.

They had so much fun with the truck and the driver. They forgot about their ball and the other cars. They only wanted to whistle and honk. They were very happy.

One day, a little girl named Lily went to the park. She loved to skip and play. The sun was shining and the birds were singing. Lily saw her friend, Tim. Tim was looking for a book to read.

"Hi Tim!" said Lily. "What are you doing?"

"I want to read a book, but I don't have any," said Tim. "Do you know where I can find one?"

Lily thought for a moment. "Yes! My mom has a big bookcase at home. There are many books available. Let's go and see!"

Lily and Tim skipped all the way to Lily's house. They found the big bookcase in the living room. Tim picked a book with lots of pictures. They sat down and read the book together. They were very happy.

Tom and Sam were friends who liked to play soccer. They had a blue ball that they kicked in the park. One day, they saw a big stadium where many people were watching a soccer game. They wanted to go inside and see the game too.

They ran to the gate, but a man stopped them. He said they needed tickets to enter the stadium. Tom and Sam did not have tickets. They felt sad and angry. They saw a hole in the fence near the gate. They thought they could sneak in through the hole.

They set their blue ball on the ground and crawled through the hole. They were inside the stadium. They felt happy and excited. They ran to the seats and watched the game. They cheered for their favorite team.

But soon, another man saw them. He was a security guard. He asked them where their tickets were. Tom and Sam did not have tickets. They felt scared and guilty. The security guard took them to the gate and told them to leave. He also took their blue ball and said they could not have it back.

Tom and Sam walked out of the stadium. They felt sad and sorry. They had lost their blue ball and their chance to see the game. They had done something wrong and they knew it. They wished they had not sneaked in through the hole.

They learned a lesson that day. They learned that they should not try to get something for free that belongs to someone else. Lily and her friends helped to sort the sandwiches and clean up the spilled drinks. They had fun playing and eating their picnic, even though there was a little accident. From that day on, they were more careful with the cooler and made sure to say sorry if they made a mistake.

One day, Ben and Lily were playing in the park with their ball. They liked to kick the ball to each other and run after it. They were having fun and laughing.

Suddenly, they felt the ground shake and heard a loud noise. It was an earthquake! They were scared and did not know what to do. They saw people running and screaming. They saw cracks in the road and buildings falling.

"Ben, what is happening?" Lily asked.

"I don't know, Lily. It is an earthquake. It is bad. We have to be safe," Ben said.

They looked around and saw a big tree. They ran to the tree and knelt under it. They held each other and prayed. They hoped the earthquake would stop soon.

After a while, the shaking stopped and the noise became quiet. They saw the sky was red with dust and smoke. They saw people helping each other and looking for their families. They saw firefighters and police and ambulances.

"Ben, Lily, are you okay?" They heard a familiar voice. It was their mom. She had been looking for them. She was happy and relieved to see them. She hugged them and kissed them.

"Mom, we are okay. We were under the tree. We were scared, but we prayed and stayed together," Ben said.

"Mom, we are sorry. We lost our ball. It rolled away when the earthquake started," Lily said.

"That's okay, my sweeties. I'm so glad you are safe. The ball is not important. You are important. You are brave and smart. You did the right thing. You knelt under the tree and prayed and stayed together. That's what matters. I love you so much," Mom said.

They all walked home together, thankful for each other and for being alive.

The moral of the story is: In times of trouble, we should kneel and pray and stay together. We should not worry about things that are not important. We should be thankful for what we have and for being alive.

"Ready, set, go!" Tom shouted and started to run. Sam followed him, but he was not as fast. He saw that Tom was ahead of him and felt angry. He wanted to win, so he had a bad idea. He threw his cheese at Tom, hoping to make him drop his.

But Tom saw the cheese flying towards him and moved his head. The cheese missed him and landed on the grass. Tom kept running and reached the finish line. He turned around and saw Sam still running with an empty spoon.

"Ha ha, I won!" Tom said. "You are a bad loser, Sam. You cheated and threw your cheese at me. That is not fair."

Sam felt ashamed and sorry. He knew he had done wrong. He ran to Tom and said, "I'm sorry, Tom. You are right. I was a bad loser and I cheated. I should not have thrown my cheese at you. That was not nice. Can you forgive me?"

Tom looked at Sam and saw that he was sincere. He smiled and said, "It's okay, Sam. I forgive you. You are my brother and I love you. Next time, let's play fair and have fun. And maybe we can share the cheese instead of racing with it."

Sam nodded and hugged Tom. They both learned a lesson that day. They learned that cheating is wrong and that being competitive is not as important as being kind and loving. They also learned that cheese is yummy and better to eat than to throw.

"Sam, Sam, wake up!" Lily cried. She shook him and hugged him, but he did not answer.

A man and a woman heard Lily's scream and came to help. They saw Sam and called for help. They tried to comfort Lily, but she was too sad and scared.

Once upon a time, there were two friends, Jack and Jill. They were always very competitive and were determined to be the best at everything. Today, they were both determined to see who could poke the most holes in a paper.

Once upon a time there was a bunny who wished to be the fastest bunny in the world. Everyday he would practice running around the meadow, increasing his speed every time. And they all lived happily ever after, spoiling the lucky turkey with treats every day.

One day, a little dog named Spot was playing in the park. He saw a big ball and wanted to play with it. Spot tried to push the ball, but it was very heavy. He felt the weight of the ball as he tried to move it.

Spot's friend, Kitty, saw him and said, "What are you doing, Spot? Why are you rushing?" Spot replied, "I want to play with this big ball, but it is too heavy." Kitty was alert and had a great idea. "I can help you, Spot!" she said.

Together, Spot and Kitty pushed the big ball. They played and had lots of fun. Spot was happy that his friend helped him. They learned that playing together was more fun than playing alone.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Sarah. She was very happy and loved to play in the park with her friends. 

One day, Sarah stepped into the park and something wonderful happened - fireflies began to dance in the sky! Sarah was so excited and wanted to have fun with them. She looked up and said "Hello fireflies, send me a message!"

The fireflies flew down and gave Sarah a joyous surprise - they sent sparks of pretty colours across the sky! Sarah gasped in amazement as the twinkling lights danced above her.

Soon night came and Sarah was feeling very hungry. She looked around for something tasty to eat and saw a cake covered with sprinkles. She grabbed it and took a big bite. It was so yummy! Sarah had a delicious cake and the fireflies still filled the sky with beautiful colours. 

Sarah had a great evening and went home happy, dreaming of the fireflies and tasty cake.

Once upon a time, there was a sleepy cat named Tom. Tom lived in a little house with his best friend, a girl named Lucy. They loved to play together all day long.

One sunny day, Lucy was thirsty. She wanted some juice to drink. Tom decided to help her. He went to the kitchen and gathered all the fruits he could find. There were apples, oranges, and grapes.

Tom and Lucy made juice from the fruits they gathered. They mixed the apples, oranges, and grapes together. It tasted so good! After they drank the juice, they felt happy and not thirsty anymore. Tom was still a sleepy cat, so he curled up in his bed and took a nap. Lucy gave him a hug and said, "Thank you, Tom, for helping me today."

Once upon a time there was a little girl who loved to play. She went to the park every day, with her friends and her mom.

One day, her mom brought a special golf club. She was so excited! She held it in her hands and it felt so comfortable. She swung it around and it made her feel happy.

But then something strange happened. The golf club suddenly disappeared! The little girl looked everywhere and called out, but it was gone. The little girl was so sad.

Then, a few days later, her mom took her back to the park. And then out of nowhere, the golf club came back! It had just mysteriously vanished but now it was back.

The little girl was so happy! She hugged the golf club tight and said, "Welcome back!"

From then on, the little girl always played with her special golf club. She felt comfortable and free with it, safe from it ever vanishing again.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Daisy. She loved to play in her garden and explore under the bushes. She enjoyed spotting the bugs and bright flowers.

One day, she spotted something totally different. It was a magical fairy! She was so pretty, with a soft pink dress and sparkling wings. Daisy was so excited and couldn't believe her eyes.

â€œOh hello!â€ said the fairy, with a smile on her face. â€œMy name is Twinkle and I'm here to make your wishes come true.â€

Daisy was so thrilled. She quickly realized that she had the power to make wishes come true. She wished for a puppy and said, â€œI wish for a puppy!â€

Twinkle nodded and said, â€œYour wish will come true. Just be patient and you'll see!â€

And so, Daisy waited. Sure enough, a few days later, a cute little puppy appeared in the garden! Daisy realized that if she believed in magic, anything was possible.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside with her friends. One day, they decided to build a sandcastle at the beach. 

Lily used her little shovel to make a big pile of sand. Her friends helped her pat it down to make it strong. They built tall towers and a big wall around their castle. 

As they were playing, a fat dove flew down and landed on top of their castle. It looked at them with its shiny black eyes. Lily and her friends giggled and watched the dove as it sat there for a while. 

When it was time to go home, Lily and her friends were sad to leave their sandcastle behind. But they knew they could come back and build another one soon. And maybe the fat dove would visit them again. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a big lion. He was big and strong and he liked to roar very loudly. One day, he was walking through the forest, when he discovered something round and blue. It was a big blueberry! The lion was so excited, he started to roar. He was so excited to find the blueberry he forgot to be careful. As he bit into it, the juice went everywhere! All over the lion's face and his mane. He was so happy that he kept on roaring and roaring. All the animals in the forest were a bit scared of the roaring, but they all knew that the lion was just happy to have found the big blueberry. The lion kept on roaring and walking around the forest until the blueberry was all gone!

Once upon a time, there was a little rabbit named Benny. Benny loved to hop around and play with his friends in the forest. One day, Benny's friend, a chipmunk named Charlie, saw a beautiful velvet ribbon on the ground. Charlie was enthusiastic and said, "Wow, this is so pretty!" 

Benny replied, "I worry that someone might be looking for it. We should try to find the owner." 

Charlie didn't want to listen and kept the ribbon for himself. The next day, they saw a sad deer looking for her lost velvet ribbon. Benny remembered what he said and told Charlie that they should return the ribbon to the deer. 

Charlie realized his mistake and apologized to the deer. The deer was happy and thanked Benny and Charlie. Benny felt proud that he did the right thing and helped someone in need. The moral of the story is that it's always better to do the right thing, even if it's hard.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Janie. She wanted to pick some flowers for her mom. She looked around for the prettiest ones, but then she saw something very unusual. There was a big muscle moving around in the bushes! Janie was a bit scared, but then the muscle stopped and said "hello".

Janie was brave and said "hello" back. The muscle said "I'm sorry but I am looking for my mom. Have you seen her?" Janie had not seen it's mom, so she said "no".

Then the muscle said "can you help me look for her? I am getting worried." Janie felt a little sorry for the muscle so she said "yes".

Then they both started looking around the bushes. Janie picked some flowers while they were searching. Eventually they found the muscle's mom and they were both very happy. 

Janie gave the flowers to the muscle and its mom as a thank you for helping her find them. The muscle and its mom thanked Janie and then they all said goodbye.

Once upon a time, there were two friends. Their names were Pam and Sam. Pam was always calm and helpful. Sam was always trying to do something new and exciting. One day, Pam decided to play a game with Sam. She wanted to see if he could stay calm while they played.

The game they chose was a counting game. Sam had to count to ten and get one point for each number he could say correctly. The winner would be the one with the highest score at the end.

Sam arrived feeling excited and ready to play. Pam was very calm and confident. As they played, the score kept getting higher and higher. In the end, Pam was the winner.

Sam was discouraged and sad. He wanted to win too. Then Pam said something that made Sam feel better. She said, "It's ok if you don't win. It's more important to be calm, even when you don't get what you want."

The moral of the story is that it's important to stay calm and be helpful even when things don't turn out the way we want them to. With this attitude it's almost certain that good things will arrive in the end.

Once there was a little boy called Jack. He was three years old and loved to be outside in the garden. One day he saw a hose and asked his mum what it was for. 

Mum said, "It's a hose, Jack. It can pull water from the tap to help water the plants." 

Jack brightened up and said, "I want to try it!" 

Mum smiled, "Okay, here you go. Just make sure there is water available first."

Jack went over to the tap and pulled the hose until the water started flowing. He was so excited to see how it was working, his little face glowed with joy. 

He laughed as he moved the hose around the garden, carefully watering each plant. He was happy to help and enjoyed every moment he spent with the hose.

Once upon a time there was a kind girl who loved to swim. She would swim every day in the big lake near her house. One day, while she was swimming, she saw something strange in the water. She got closer and saw it was a file! The girl was so excited and decided to pick it up. She then opened the file and saw it was full of kind notes from her friends! She was so happy and swam away with the file. From that day on she was sure to always carry the file with her whenever she swam. She liked to think of it as her special friend that came with her to the big lake.

Sara was a big sister. She had a baby brother named Tom. Sara loved Tom very much, but sometimes she was jealous. She wanted to play with Mom and Dad, but they were busy with Tom.

One day, Sara saw Tom sleeping in his crib. She had an idea. She took her doctor kit and went to examine Tom. She put a stethoscope on his chest, a thermometer in his mouth, and a band-aid on his arm. She said, "I am a doctor. I will make you better, Tom."

But Tom did not like Sara's game. He woke up and started to cry. He spit out the thermometer and pulled off the band-aid. He was scared and hurt. He wanted Mom and Dad.

Mom and Dad heard Tom's cry and ran to his room. They saw Sara and her doctor kit. They were angry and worried. They said, "Sara, what did you do to Tom? You should not play with him like that. You could hurt him or make him sick. He is a baby. He needs love and care, not games and toys."

Sara felt sorry and ashamed. She said, "I am sorry, Mom and Dad. I wanted to play with you, but you were busy with Tom. I wanted to examine him, like you do. I wanted to be intelligent, like you are."

Mom and Dad hugged Sara and said, "Sara, we love you very much. You are a big sister and a smart girl. You can play with us and with Tom, but you have to be gentle and kind. You can examine him, but only with your eyes and your words. You can ask him questions, like how he feels, what he likes, and what he learns. You can help him grow and learn, too. That is how you show your intelligence and your love."

Sara smiled and said, "Thank you, Mom and Dad. I understand. I will be a good sister and a good doctor. I will love Tom and play with him nicely."

She went to Tom's crib and said, "Hi, Tom. I am sorry I scared you. I love you. Do you want to play with me?"

Tom stopped crying and looked at Sara. He smiled and reached for her hand. He said, "Yes, Sara. I love you, too. You are my sister. You are intelligent."

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sarah. She was three years old and very happy.

One evening, Sarah went to visit her Granny. Granny was her favorite person; she always had special treats for Sarah.

But when Sarah arrived, Granny was not happy. Granny was angry. Sarah wondered why Granny was so mad.

"Why are you angry, Granny?" asked Sarah.

"I'm angry because you didn't behave," said Granny. "You have to be a good girl to come over and see me!"

Sarah thought about it. She knew Granny was right, so she promised to behave better next time.

Granny smiled. She gave Sarah a hug and said, "Good girl! Go play now and have fun."

Sarah did just that. She smiled and played throughout the evening, learning all about how to behave.

Once upon a time, there was a duck who liked to repeat things. He liked to say "hello!" over and over again. He said it so often, his friends nickname him "Hello Duck."

One day, he was walking near a lake when he saw something shiny in the water. He reached out to grab it and he almost fell in the lake! But his friends saw him and ran over to help. They found out that the shiny thing was a hard shell!

Hello Duck was so excited. He excitedly said "shell!" and then he said it again. And then again. He said it so much, his friends started laughing. He repeated it one more time, and then he ran home with his shell.

From then on, he kept the shell with him. Whenever he was feeling lonely or sad, he would hold the shell and say "shell," and it made him feel better. He kept repeating things that made him happy, like "friends" and "duck," too!

Once upon a time there was a poor boy. His name was Jim. He was very sad because he had no pedal for his bike. One day, Jim saw a pedal growing in his garden. He was so excited he ran to get it. 

Jim pushed the pedal into the bike and it fit perfectly! He was so excited he began to pedal around the garden. 

Just then, he noticed his neighbour, Bob, looking down from his window with a jealous look on his face. 

Jim stopped pedaling and went to Bob's window. He said, "You can have it, Bob! We can share it." 

Bob's face filled with happiness and he said, "Thank you so much, Jim!"

Jim was really proud of himself. Sharing was better than keeping it all to himself. 

The moral of this story is that sharing is better than being poor.

Once upon a time, there was a little rabbit named Bun. Bun loved to hop around and play with his friends. One day, Bun felt very tired and needed to rest. He found a cozy spot under a big tree and closed his eyes. 

As he rested, he thought about how much he loved his family and friends. He felt a warm feeling in his heart and knew that love was a wonderful thing. 

After a while, Bun woke up feeling refreshed and ready to play again. He was persistent in his desire to have fun and didn't give up until he found his friends. They played together all day, and Bun was happy knowing that he could always rest when he needed to.

Once upon a time, there was a big structure in the park. It was a little gloomy, but all the kids loved to play there. One day, a group of friends went to the park to have fun together.

Tom, the bravest of the friends, decided to dive into the ball pit near the structure. He jumped in with a big smile on his face. His friends clapped and cheered as he played in the colorful balls.

The sun started to shine, making the gloomy structure look bright and happy. The friends spent the whole day playing, laughing, and diving into the ball pit. They had a great time and couldn't wait to come back to the park again.

One day, Jack was walking in the woods. He felt wild and bold. He heard a noise. "What was that?" he said out loud. He listened more closely. He heard a gentle voice.

Jack looked around, but he couldn't see anyone. Then, he saw a little bird sitting on the branch of a tree. The bird said: "My name is Daisy. What's yours?"

Jack smiled. "My name is Jack," he said. Daisy flew down to him. She said: "Today is a wild day! Let's explore! "

Jack and Daisy talked and played. They found a cozy clearing in the forest. Jack and Daisy listened to the sounds of the forest - the singing birds, the rustling trees and the bubbling stream. 

Jack's time in the woods flew by. Later he bid Daisy farewell and promised to come back again.

Billy was feeling fearful. He was standing in the park, watching a big jug by his feet. He didn't know why it was there, but it made him scared.

Suddenly, an old man appeared. He had a friendly smile, and he spoke gently. He asked Billy why he was feeling so scared. 

Billy told the old man about the jug. The old man listened carefully and then explained why he needn't be scared. He said the jug was being used for a game. It was filled with water and players had to try and move it without spilling any. Billy smiled and slowly his fear began to disappear.

Billy thanked the old man for showing him the game. He watched as the players took turns, delighted. He couldn't believe he was no longer fearful.

Once there was a little girl called Abigail who loved to play with her toys. She had a toy horse and a toy elephant, a toy doll and toy blocks. But most of all, Abigail loved her toy bear.

One day, the toy bear looked very tired and sad. Abigail knew that something was wrong. So she gave the bear a big hug and asked what was wrong.

The toy bear said, "I'm so ugly! I wish I didn't look this way!"

Abigail smiled, and said, "Don't worry, I will pray and ask God to make you beautiful."

And so Abigail closed her eyes and prayed. She asked God to make the toy bear beautiful and happy.

And when Abigail opened her eyes, the toy bear was looking happier and more beautiful than ever before!

Abigail was so happy and thanked God for answering her prayers. From that day onward, Abigail and her toy bear were always happy and had lots of fun together.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy lived in a house with his mommy and daddy. One day, Timmy and his family went on a trip to the west. They saw lots of big mountains and beautiful sunsets. But one day, the sky turned gloomy and it started to rain. Timmy's mommy and daddy got worried because they didn't know where to go. But then, they saw a sign that said "Shelter". They followed the sign and found a little house where they could stay until the rain stopped. Timmy was happy because he got to play inside with his toys. After a while, the rain stopped and the sun came out again. Timmy and his family continued their trip to the west, but they never forgot the little house that saved them from the rain.

Once upon a time, there were two friends named Max and Wendy. Max was a shy boy and Wendy was a brave girl. 
They liked to play chess together every day. 

One day, Wendy looked up from the game and saw Max blink. She smiled and said, 'Let's play again tomorrow.' Max smiled and nodded.

The next day, Wendy came to Max's house and knocked on the door. Max opened the door and smiled. He invited her in and Wendy saw a chessboard on the table. 

Wendy starting setting up the pieces and Max watched. He smiled shyly and blinked a few times. 

When Wendy was done, she said, 'Let's play!' 
Max and Wendy played chess together every day. They had lots of fun and became the best of friends.

Once upon a time, there was a wild and amazing creature. It shined so brightly that its light filled everything around it. It really was very shiny!

The wild creature flew through the night sky, looking for its friends. As soon as it saw them, it shined even brighter! Its friends were so happy to see it!

The wild creature waved at them and said "Hi!", then it flew around in circles and made a show of its shining! Everyone was so amazed at how the wild creature shone in the night sky.

Then, everyone flew together and went on a journey. They explored wild places in the sky and saw amazing things. Everywhere they went, the wild creature shined and lit up the night!

They all had a wonderful time thanks to the wild creature's amazing shine!

Once upon a time, there was a tired little bear named Ben. He lived in a big forest with many trees. One of his favorite trees was a tall pine tree. Ben loved to play near the pine tree every day.

One day, Ben found a hat under the pine tree. He thought, "I want to wear this hat!" So, Ben put the hat on his head. He felt very happy and proud.

Ben's friend, a small bird named Lily, saw him wear the hat. She said, "Ben, you look nice in the hat!" Ben smiled and said, "Thank you, Lily!" They played and laughed near the pine tree all day long.

Once upon a time there was a clever bunny. His name was Jack. He had a special weapon which he used to protect his friends.

One silly day, Jack was out walking in the forest with his friends. Suddenly, they heard a loud noise! What was it? 

"Let me take a look," said Jack bravely. So he bravely grabbed his weapon and ran off to the source of the noise. 

He found a giant monster! It was big and very scary. The monster shouted, "I will get you!" 

But Jack bravely held up his weapon and shouted back, "No, you won't! I will protect my friends!" 

The monster saw that Jack was brave. He knew that he had met his match! So the monster turned and ran away.

Jack had saved the day! His silly weapon had protected his friends from the giant monster. From then on, Jack was a hero.

Once upon a time, there was a naughty little boy. He loved to play tricks. One day, he went to pick a pear from the tree. But before he could pluck it off the tree, he had an idea.

He asked the pear, "Where are you going?". The pear didn't answer him. So, the naughty boy began to shake the tree. The pear was so scared that it rolled onto the ground and broke into pieces.

The naughty boy sighed. He knew he had done something wrong. He knew he should never have asked the pear that question. Now he would have no treat to eat. 

The end.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She was very sad. One day she decided to go for a walk. 

As the little girl walked, she noticed a door in front of her. She wanted to see what was inside so she put her hand on the handle and opened it. Inside, she saw a big open room. 

At the far end of the room there was a huge head made of stone. The little girl was curious so she walked closer to take a look. Then her head started to move! 

The little girl was very scared, but the head spoke. It said it was sorry for being so sad. It said that it had been alone for a long time and just wanted a friend. 

The little girl smiled and said she would be happy to be the head's friend. From that day onwards, the little girl and the head were the best of friends!

Josh and his dad were in the garden. Josh's dad was getting ready to do some work. Josh saw a pipe lying on the ground and he asked "What's this?" His dad said "It's a pipe, Josh. Let's see if it matches the others."

Josh found another pipe and he was so excited. He said "This one matches the other one, Dad!" His dad smiled and said "That's great! Let's put them together." Josh and his dad put the pipes together and they worked.

Josh was very proud that he helped his dad. His dad said "Well done, Josh! You did a really good job." Josh smiled and said "Thanks, Dad!" Then, they both hugged each other and Josh was even more proud. He was so happy that he helped his dad.

Once upon a time, there was a small bird who loved to sing. One day, the bird fell down from the tree and felt a lot of pain in its wing. The bird tried to fly, but it couldn't. It felt sad and scared.

The bird saw a kind cat who came to question it. The bird told the cat about its pain and how it couldn't fly. The cat felt sorry for the bird and wanted to help. The cat took the bird to a wise owl who knew how to heal small birds.

The owl examined the bird's wing and gave it some medicine. After a few days, the bird's wing felt better and it could fly again. The bird was happy and grateful to the cat and the owl. From that day on, the bird sang even more beautifully than before.

Once upon a time, there was a hot day. The sun was shining brightly in the sky and it was hard work to be outside.

A little girl was out playing and all of a sudden she got very thirsty. But she was too far away from her house and all she had was her little coat pocket.

The little girl ran up to a store and asked if they could help. The store keeper smiled and said of course. He gave her a cold, hard bottle of water and the little girl was so happy. She thanked the store keeper and then headed home, feeling refreshed and happy again.

The little girl learned that day that if you work hard, you can store enough energy and strength to get through even the hottest of days.

Once upon a time, there was a magical lady named Suzy. Everyone who knew her liked her because she was very kind and loving. 

One day, Suzy decided to give a massage to an ignorant person in need. She knew that a massage would help them heal.

So Suzy took the person's hand and said, "I'm here to heal you with a massage." The person smiled and said, "Thank you for your kind words."

Suzy then proceeded to massage the person. With each stroke the person felt the tension leaving their body. After the massage was finished, the person thanked Suzy very much.

The next day everyone noticed a big difference in the person. They said, "Wow, you look great. What changed? " The person replied, " Suzy gave me a massage and it made me heal."

Everyone thanked Suzy for her great work. Suzy was happy to see the transformation and she was thankful that she helped heal the ignorant person in need.

Sam and Jane were playing in the park. It was a warm day and they were having fun. Suddenly, Sam saw something shining in the grass. "What is it?" he asked.

Jane said, "Let's find out." She bent down and opened her hand. Inside her hand was a shiny gold ring.

"Wow," said Sam. He reached out his finger to take it. It felt warm against his skin.

Suddenly, a woman ran up to them. "That's my ring!" she shouted. "Give it back to me at once!"

Sam and Jane were so scared, they dropped the ring and ran away. 

The woman picked up the ring and smiled cruelly. "It's too late," she said. "You'll never get it back now."

Once upon a time, there was a helpless cow. The cow was feeling very sad. She had no one to talk to, and no one to play with.

One day, thecow heard a beautiful song. She turned towards the song to see a little girl singing. The cow was so happy to see the girl singing - she had never seen anyone sing before.

The little girl sang and played with the cow, and soon the cow was no longer feeling sad or helpless. The cow ran around and jumped in the field and played with the girl.

When the sun went down, the girl waved goodbye to the cow and continued on her way. The cow was so happy that she started singing too, and she sang all through the night.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to walk on the path in the forest. He always felt happy when he was on the path. One day, Timmy was walking on the path when he saw a big rock. He wanted to pick up the rock, but it was too heavy. 

Suddenly, a bird flew down and landed on the rock. The bird said to Timmy, "Be careful! That rock can strike you and hurt you." Timmy listened to the bird and didn't touch the rock. He thanked the bird for warning him and continued walking on the path. 

As Timmy walked, he saw a butterfly. The butterfly was flying around the flowers. Timmy said to the butterfly, "Hello! I like your pretty wings." The butterfly replied, "Thank you! I like your happy face." Timmy smiled and continued walking on the path, feeling happy and safe.

Once there was a little girl. She was three years old. She had a lucky snack to eat. It was a cookie.

The little girl wanted to hang the snack up high in the tree. She climbed up the ladder and hung the snack on a branch. She then carefully climbed back down the ladder.

When the little girl looked up at the snack, she was very happy. She was very lucky to have such a yummy treat! She thanked the tree for watching over it.

The little girl enjoyed her snack. She had a lot of fun! She was so lucky to find such a tasty treat. She couldn't stay long, but it was a great snack!

Once upon a time there was a kid named Danny. He was playing all alone, but he was not scared. 

Suddenly, he saw a big bug. Danny felt fearful and he backed away slowly. 

"What do you want?" he asked the bug.

The bug answered, "I want to take a trip on your lip." Danny was surprised, but he agreed. He kissed the bug and closed his eyes.

The bug flew away and Danny finished his journey. Suddenly, he heard a noiseâ€”it was the bug coming back. 

The bug said, "Thank you for the ride. Now I have to go back to my home. Goodbye." 

Danny waved goodbye, and he suddenly realized why the bug wanted to ride on his lip. The bug needed to get back to its family. Danny felt happy and relieved.

The sun was hot on the beach, and the ocean sparkled. Little Jimmy was excited to play in the water. He grabbed his bucket and started walking towards the water.

As Jimmy walked, he thought about all the wonderful creatures living in the ocean. He wanted to be careful and not bother the creatures.

When Jimmy reached the ocean, he washed his hands and feet. He was so thoughtful! He made sure not to disturb the ocean creatures. Then he filled up his bucket with sea water and collected some shells.

Jimmy was so happy to explore the ocean! He was so thankful for the chance to experience the beauty and life of the ocean. He washed his hands and feet, and then walked back to the sand. What an amazing day!

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to visit the market with their mom. The market has many things to see and smell and touch. There are fruits and flowers and toys and clothes. Anna and Ben always want to buy something, but mom says they have to save money.

One day, they see a wealthy lady at the market. She has a big hat and a shiny dress and a lot of bags. She buys everything she likes. She does not care about the price. She sees Anna and Ben and smiles.

"Hello, little ones," she says. "Do you like the market?"

"Yes, we do," Anna and Ben say.

"What do you want to buy?" the lady asks.

Anna points to a doll with a pink dress. Ben points to a car with four wheels.

"They are very nice," the lady says. "But they are too expensive for you, right?"

Anna and Ben nod. They feel sad.

The lady laughs. "Don't be sad. I will buy them for you. You can have anything you want. I have a lot of money."

She gives the doll to Anna and the car to Ben. They are very happy. They thank the lady.

Mom sees what happens. She is angry. She takes the doll and the car from Anna and Ben. She gives them back to the lady.

"Thank you, but no thank you," mom says. "We don't need your money. We don't want your gifts. We are happy with what we have."

The lady is surprised. She does not understand. She shrugs and walks away.

Mom hugs Anna and Ben. She tells them that money is not everything. She tells them that they have to work hard and be grateful for what they have. She tells them that they are wealthy in their own way.

Anna and Ben understand. They love their mom. They do not need the doll and the car. They have each other. They are happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She liked to play outside in the sunshine. One day, she saw some pretty berries growing on a bush. She thought they looked yummy, so she picked one and ate it. 

But then, she started feeling sick. Her tummy hurt and she felt dizzy. She remembered her mommy telling her that some berries can be dangerous to eat. She knew she needed help, so she called out for her mommy.

Her mommy heard her call and came running. She saw that Lily had eaten a dangerous berry and knew she needed to go to the doctor. They went to the hospital and the doctor helped Lily feel better. From then on, Lily knew to always ask her mommy before eating any berries.

Once upon a time, there was a truck. It was a pretty truck. It had blue paint and shiny wheels. 

One day, two kids decided to play a game with the truck. They took turns guessing who would drive the truck first. 

The first kid guessed it was her turn, but the second kid guessed it was his turn. The hands on the clock showed it was the first kid's turn. They laughed and smiled, because they both guessed correctly. 

The kids rushed to the truck. The first kid sat in the driver seat and the second kid climbed into the passenger side. Then, they took a special drive around the block. 

When their drive was over, they hugged each other. They had such a fun time together in the pretty truck.

One day, Tom and Lily were playing in the garden. They saw a big box with a lock on it. They were curious and wanted to see what was inside.

"Let's open the lock!" Tom said.

"But we don't have a key," Lily said.

"Maybe we can break it," Tom said. He picked up a stick and hit the lock hard. But the lock did not open.

"Stop it, Tom! You are being naughty!" Lily said. "That box belongs to Dad. He said we should not touch it."

Tom did not listen. He hit the lock harder and harder. He made a lot of noise. He did not see Dad coming from the house.

"Tom! Lily! What are you doing?" Dad shouted. He was angry. He took the stick from Tom and put it away. He lifted the box and carried it inside.

"Sorry, Dad," Tom and Lily said. They felt bad.

Dad came back and sat down with them. He looked at the box and sighed.

"Do you know what is in this box?" he asked.

Tom and Lily shook their heads.

"This box has a very special gift for you. It is a globe. A globe is a ball that shows the earth. The earth is where we live. It has many places and people and animals. I wanted to show you the globe and teach you about the earth. But you broke the lock and ruined the surprise."

Tom and Lily gasped. They did not know that. They felt worse.

"We are sorry, Dad," they said again. "We did not mean to be naughty. We were just curious."

Dad smiled and hugged them.

"It's okay, my loves. I know you were curious. Curiosity is good. But you also need to be careful and respectful. Sometimes, things are locked for a reason. You need to ask before you touch. Do you understand?"

Tom and Lily nodded.

"Yes, Dad. We understand. We will ask next time."

Dad kissed them and said.

"Good. Now, let's go inside and see if we can fix the lock. And then, I will show you the globe and the earth. And we will have fun learning together."

Tom and Lily smiled and followed Dad. They were happy. They learned a lesson. And they still got a gift.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside in the sun. One day, Timmy went for a walk in the woods. He saw a monster! The monster was big and scary, but it didn't hurt Timmy. It just wanted to be friends. Timmy and the monster played together and had fun.

As the sun started to set, the monster started to glow. Timmy thought it was really cool. The monster's skin was dry and bumpy, but Timmy didn't mind. He still thought the monster was his new best friend. Timmy and the monster said goodbye and promised to play again soon. Timmy went home happy, knowing he had made a new friend.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys and make colorful drawings with his crayons. One day, Timmy's dad needed to go to the gas station to fuel up their car. 

Timmy asked, "Can I come with you, Dad?"

His dad replied, "I'm sorry, Timmy. You are too little to come with me to the gas station. It's not safe for you."

Timmy was sad, but he understood that his dad didn't permit him to go. 

Later that day, Timmy was playing with his toy car when he remembered something important. "Dad, can I ask you a question?"

"Sure, Timmy," his dad replied.

"Why do we need fuel for our car?"

"Well, fuel is like food for our car. It helps our car move and go places," his dad explained.

Timmy thought about it for a while and realized that just like how his dad didn't permit him to go to the gas station because it wasn't safe, fuel was also important for their car to be safe and work properly. The moral of the story is that sometimes we may not understand why we can't do certain things, but it's important to trust that our parents are making the right decisions to keep us safe.

John saw a big tree and he wanted to pick its fruits. He ran to the tree and climbed it very quickly. When he got to the top, he was very surprised to see a lot of red apples. He started to pick them one by one and put them in his bag.

Suddenly, he felt very thirsty. He looked around and saw a river nearby. He quickly climbed down from the tree and ran towards the river. When he arrived, he saw that the water was very hot.

John said to himself, "Wow, this water is very hot. What should I do?"

He decided to find a different place and he looked around. He finally saw a big pond and he ran towards it. When he arrived, the water was very cold. He was so happy and he started to drink with his hands. He was very satisfied.

Danny had a big dream. He dreamed that he was flying in the sky, with the bright blue sun shining in the background and the wind blowing through his hair. Danny was so happy!

But then, all of a sudden, he noticed a big, red ashtray in the clouds. He was confused and didn't know why it was there. He flew closer until it filled up the sky in front of him.

The ashtray was red, the same colour as his favourite toy fire truck. He leaned in to take a better look and noticed that the ashtray was full of gold coins.

Danny was so excited! As he looked around, he saw more red ashtrays filled with gold coins. He decided to reach out and grab one. With a smile on his face, he picked up the ashtray.

As soon as Danny held it, he woke up. He was back in his bedroom and the sun was shining through his window. Danny was disappointed, but he knew it had been a great dream and that he'd never forget it!

Once upon a time, there was a boy who was very curious. He wanted to explore the world and find out what was out there.

One day, he was walking in the forest and he saw something up ahead. He stopped to take a closer look and he saw it was a big chimney. It was rising high above the trees and he was very curious about what was inside.

He started walking closer to the chimney. As he reached the entrance, he heard a voice from inside.

"Who's there?" it said.

The little boy was scared, but he answered "It's me!"

A man with a big white beard then stepped out of the chimney. He said, "What are you doing here, little one?"

The boy said, "I was just curious about what was inside your chimney."

The man smiled and said, "Welcome! Come inside and explore."

The little boy was so happy, he went inside and enjoyed himself. He stopped often to explore and ask questions. Ultimately, he had a wonderful time and learned lots of things.

Once upon a time, there was a funny island. On this island, there lived a boy named Tim and his pet cat, Max. They liked to play together in the sand and the sun. One day, they found a big pot near the water.

Tim and Max decided to stir the pot. They put in sand, water, and leaves. They stirred and stirred, laughing and having fun. They didn't know what they were making, but it was a fun game to play.

As they stirred, the pot started to shake. It shook more and more, and then it tipped over. The sand, water, and leaves spilled out and covered Tim and Max. They were stuck and couldn't get out. They were sad and scared, and they wished they hadn't played with the pot.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her tools in her backyard. One day, while she was playing, she found a shiny hammer. It was so pretty and looked very rich.

Lily was so happy and showed the hammer to her friend, Timmy. "Look, Timmy! I found a pretty tool!" she said.

Timmy looked at the hammer and said, "Wow, that's so cool! Can I play with it too?"

Lily thought about it for a moment, but then she started to weep. "I don't want to share my pretty tool," she said sadly.

Timmy hugged her and said, "It's okay, Lily. You can keep your pretty tool. I'll find my own tool to play with."

Lily stopped weeping and smiled. She realized that it was better to share her toys with her friends. From that day on, Lily and Timmy played together with all their tools, and they were very happy.

Once there was a little girl. She was only three years old. Every morning, she would pray. She would say, "Please help me be a good person."

One sunny day, she went to the store. In the store she saw a beautiful flower. She asked her mom if she could buy it. But her mom said, "No, it's too expensive."

Then, the little girl said, "I'll pray harder. Maybe then I can get it." So, the girl prayed very hard.

Soon, she saw a cheap flower. It was almost as pretty as the one before. She asked her mom if she could buy it. Her mom said yes, and the girl was very happy. 

The little girl took the flower home. She put it in a special place near her bed. Every morning, she would look at the flower and think, "I prayed and I got my flower. Thank you!"

One day, Benny was walking in the park with his mommy. The trees were tall and Benny saw something he had never seen before. It was a big cobweb in between two big trees. Benny was amazed!

He asked his mommy, "What's that?"

His mommy smiled, "That's a cobweb."

Benny was intrigued, so his mommy started to teach him about cobwebs. She said, "Cobwebs are made by tiny spiders. They use their webs to catch their food."

Benny was so excited and he wanted to learn more. "Can I make one too?" he asked.

His mommy laughed and said, "We can try! It won't be easy, but with practice you can learn how to make one."

Benny and his mommy spent the afternoon making cobwebs from some yarn and a few sticks. By the end of the day, Benny had learned how to make a cobweb! He was very proud and he couldn't wait to show his dad when he got home.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Amy. She was three years old and loved to play. One day, she was playing with her toys when she saw something. It was small and moved fast.
