Mom said: "It is over there. See the bag that is fit for a boy?"

Marky looked around and found his bag. He was so excited. He now had a bag just like mom.

Mom said: "Let's go!"

Marky grabbed his bag and ran off with a big smile on his face. He was so excited for their visit to grandma's house.

Once upon a time, there was a wild sugar. It was so sweet that even the birds wanted to eat it. But the sugar would not budge. All it did all day was sleep.

One day a little boy came along. He had three years, and was very brave. He wanted to wake up the sugar.

So he shook it and shouted. But nothing happened. The sugar was still sleeping. So the boy took some water and sprinkled it on the sugar.

Suddenly, the wild sugar woke up! It was so happy and jumped around. Then it ran away and disappeared. The little boy was so excited but all he could do was watch as the wild sugar scampered away. 
The next day, the little boy went back to the spot he had seen the wild sugar, and found a sweet treat waiting for him! The wild sugar had left a surprise for him - a little sugary treat.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Lucy. She had lots of toys in her room, including a special magnet. One day, the magnet accidently split into two pieces.

The pieces were too small for Lucy to hold. She was very sad, and started to cry. She was so upset that she started to hurt herself.

Suddenly, something magical happened. The two pieces of the magnet magically bounced off the floor, and put themselves back together. 

When the magnet was whole again, Lucy was so happy that she gave it a big cuddle. She would always be careful with it from then on!

Once upon a time there was a cool, blue cooler. It was a very old cooler and it was absolutely charming. Every morning it would sit in the same spot, near the garden. One day, the cooler decided to move. It rolled out of its spot, was careful to not run into anything and started to move down the road.

It was a sunny day and the cooler was happy. It passed a few trees, then came to a field with lots of flowers. It was such a beautiful place! The cooler kept going and eventually came to a river. It wanted to get close to the water and have a drink, so it rolled closer. 

Then something amazing happened! A family of ducks came swimming towards the cooler! They were so cute and friendly - the cooler felt so happy! The ducks swam around the cooler like they were saying hello. The cooler waved its lid in greeting. They all moved around with the river's current, enjoying the moment. 

After a while, the cooler and the ducks said goodbye. The cooler started to roll away and soon came back to its old spot. It was time to rest and the cooler was content. It lay in the sun, happy and charming.

Sara and Ben went to the zoo with their mom. They saw many animals, like lions, monkeys, and elephants. They liked to watch them and learn their names.

When they came to the bird house, they saw a big cage with many colorful birds. Some were big and loud, some were small and quiet. Sara pointed to a bird with a long tail and asked, "Mom, what is that bird?"

Mom looked at the sign and said, "That is a peacock. It can spread its tail like a fan and show its beautiful feathers."

Ben was curious and wanted to see the peacock's tail. He walked closer to the cage and said, "Hey, peacock, show me your tail!"

But the peacock did not listen. It turned its head and ignored Ben. Ben tried again, louder and louder, but the peacock still did not care.

Sara saw that Ben was angry and said, "Ben, stop yelling. You are scaring the bird. The bird is delicate and needs to be calm and happy."

Ben did not understand. He said, "But I want to see its tail. It is so pretty. Why does it not show me?"

Mom explained, "The peacock only shows its tail when it wants to. It is not a toy that you can turn on and off. You have to be patient and respectful. Maybe if you are quiet and gentle, it will show you later."

Ben thought about it and said, "Okay, Mom. I will be quiet and gentle. But can you guess when it will show its tail?"

Mom smiled and said, "I cannot guess, Ben. It is a surprise. Maybe if we come back later, we will see it. Or maybe we will see something else that is amazing. The zoo has many wonders to discover."

Sara and Ben nodded and followed Mom to the next cage. They hoped to see the peacock's tail, but they also wanted to see more animals and have fun. They loved the zoo and all its creatures.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Mint who was very troubled. Everywhere she went, she carried buckets and bags to collect things.

One day, Mint was walking in the park. She saw a beautiful feather and put it in her bucket. She noticed a pretty stone on the ground and added it to her collection. She even found a tiny shell and added it too!

Mint kept searching the park and came across a big apple tree. Its branches were full of apples. Mint reached up and picked one and put it in her bag. She ate the apple and felt so happy!

Mint kept looking around and finally found the most special item of all - a shiny silver coin! She put it in her collection and went home with a happy heart.

Mint now had a wonderful collection that she could look at and enjoy, and she was no longer troubled.

Once upon a time, there was a helpless little bunny who worked at a club. 
Everyday, the bunny had to move around the club cleaning up and helping the customers. It was hard work, but the bunny liked making people happy. 
One day, he noticed a strange thing in the corner of the club. He cautiously moved closer to take a look. It was a special box with a big colorful button on the side.
The bunny was so curious, he just had to press it. As soon as he did, he heard a loud noise and felt something moving beneath his feet.
The bunny hopped away, feeling helpless and a little scared. But then suddenly, the box opened up and he saw a lot of sweets inside.
The bunny was so excited! He had discovered a secret surprise that only he knew about. From then on, he would come back everyday to press the button and enjoy the secret treats.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Mary. She had long, dark hair, and she was very tidy. 
One day, Mary was playing in the backyard when she accidentally stepped too close to a bonfire. In an instant, she was burning! 
Soon afterwards, Mary was taken to the hospital. The doctors worked very hard to make her better. They put cream on her burns and gave her water to drink. 
Finally, Mary felt much better and she could go home. She made sure to stay far away from the bonfire so she wouldn't get burned again.

Once there was a little girl named Poppy. She loved to explore the outdoors and look for different things. One day, Poppy saw a bee buzzing around a wild poppy flower. It was the prettiest flower she had ever seen! Poppy smiled and decided to pluck it for herself. Just as she was about to touch it, the bee suddenly snapped at her! She quickly stepped back and watched as the bee flew away.

Poppy decided to pick the poppy flower anyway. She gently touched it and it felt so soft and smelled sweet. Poppy was so excited to take it home - she had never seen such a beautiful flower before. She carefully put it in her pocket and started skipping back home. Along the way, she stopped to smell the flower and think about all the wonderful things she could do with it.

When Poppy arrived home, she excitedly pulled the poppy out of her pocket. She held it up in front of her face and took a big sniff. It smelled so sweet! She smiled and then quickly went to show her mom what she had found. Her mom was so proud of Poppy and gave her a big hug.

That night, Poppy placed the poppy in a special spot on her nightstand where she could look at it every day. It always made her feel so happy, so she named it her "happy poppy".

One day, two friends, Bob and Steve, were walking through a gloomy forest. They saw a frog sitting on a rock. Bob wondered what the frog was doing all alone. Steve suggested that they play with it. 

So Bob carefully scooped up the frog, and put it in a shallow pond nearby. The frog was not happy! It was hopping all over the pond, looking to get out. But, there was no way out.

Then Bob had an idea! He took off one of his shoes and filled it with the water from the pond. He put the frog in the shoe and set it down on the grass. The frog was so happy that it started to sing! 

Steve and Bob looked at each other, smiled, and watched the frog soak in the sun. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a small man called Bob. Every morning he woke up with the sunrise and got ready for his day. One morning, Bob was feeling sad and empty. He didn't want to go out, so he stayed at home.

Suddenly, his best friend came to visit. His friend said: "Hey Bob! Come and split with me! Let's go explore the world!" Bob was hesitant at first, but eventually he agreed.

So the two of them went outside together. They explored the sunny fields, played games and enjoyed themselves. Bob was having so much fun, he began to smile and feel happy again.

At the end of the day, they said goodbye to each other. Bob thanked his friend for showing him the beauty in being alive. After his best friend left, Bob was very thankful for the special day they shared.

This moment taught Bob a valuable lesson: when you feel empty and alone, the best thing to do is to find a friend and share your experiences. With friendship, the sunrise will always be brighter.

Once upon a time, there was a big, hot, incredible world. Imagine a world full of big, colourful mountains and lots of friendly animals and birds. Everyone was very happy, and it was a place full of fun and adventure.

One day, a little girl went exploring in the hot world and she found something incredible. As she looked around, she saw a large blue lake, filled with beautiful creatures swimming around. She took a big breath and jumped in.

The water was so warm and the little girl was so happy. She swam for hours, surrounded by incredible colours and wonderful sights. After a while, she got so tired, she decided to float on her back and let the sunshine dry her off.

It was one of the most amazing experiences of her life, and she never forgot it. She had imagined a hot, incredible world, and she discovered it.

Mrs. Smith was walking down the road with her three year old daughter, Shannon. As the wind blew around them, Shannon grew chilly and started to shiver. Mrs. Smith grabbed her scarf from her coat pocket and wrapped it around her daughter tightly. 

Shannon smiled, happy to have the warmth, and the two kept on walking. After a few moments, they arrived at their destination. It was a big field with lots of toys in organized sections. Shannon squealed with joy and ran forward, eager to start playing. Mrs. Smith followed closely behind her with a big smile!

Anna and Ben were playing in the park with their toy vehicles. Anna had a red car and Ben had a blue truck. They made vroom-vroom noises as they drove them on the grass and the sand.

"Look, Anna, I can make my truck jump over this hill!" Ben said, as he pushed his truck hard and made it fly in the air.

"Wow, Ben, that's cool!" Anna said, and clapped her hands. "Can I try?"

"Sure, Anna, here you go." Ben said, and gave her his truck. Anna tried to make it jump, but it landed on a smelly pile of dog poop.

"Yuck, Anna, your truck is smelly now!" Ben said, and wrinkled his nose. "You need to wash it!"

"I'm sorry, Ben, I didn't see the poop!" Anna said, and felt sad. "How can I wash it?"

"Let's go to the fountain, Anna, there's water there." Ben said, and took her hand. "Come on, it's okay, we can make it clean again."

They ran to the fountain, where they saw other children playing with water. They dipped their truck in the water and rubbed it with their hands. The poop came off and the truck was shiny again.

"Look, Ben, your truck is not smelly anymore!" Anna said, and smiled.

"Yay, Anna, you did it!" Ben said, and hugged her. "You're a good friend!"

They clapped their hands and laughed. Then they went back to play with their vehicles, happy and clean.

One day, a little girl was walking in the park when she noticed an elderly lady. The lady was staring at a big sunflower. The little girl smiled and stared at the sunflower too. She liked how bright and yellow it was. Suddenly, the elderly lady turned to the little girl and smiled. She leaned down and gently picked the sunflower from the ground. She gave it to the little girl and said, â€œThis is for youâ€. The little girl was so happy, she hugged the sunflower and giggled. Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play with toys and listen to music. They have a big radio in their room. The radio can play many songs and stories.

One day, it is almost Christmas. Anna and Ben want to give a present to their mom and dad. They think hard. What can they give them? They look around their room. They see the radio. They have an idea.

"Let's give them the radio!" Anna says. "They like music too."

"But how can we give them the radio?" Ben asks. "It is too big and heavy."

"We can wrap it!" Anna says. "We can use paper and tape and ribbon. It will look nice."

They find some paper and tape and ribbon in the closet. They work hard. They wrap the radio with the paper. They stick the tape on the edges. They tie the ribbon in a bow. They are happy. They have a big present for their mom and dad.

They carry the present to the living room. They put it under the tree. They wait for their mom and dad to come home. They are excited.

They turn on the radio. They listen to music and stories together. They are happy. It is a good Christmas.

Once upon a time there was a nosy little girl called Jane. Jane was always on the go, never staying in one place for too long. One day, she decided to go exploring.

But when it got dark, the children had to go home - but not before bringing a few friends with them. They had made friends with some of the animals in the attractive valley, and wanted to take them home with them. So the children filled their pockets with cute little friends, and off they went.

They had a wonderful day, and were so happy to bring some of the valley's animals home with them.

Lily and Tom are playing hide and seek in the park. Lily is the seeker and Tom is the hider. Lily counts to ten and then says, "Ready or not, here I come!"

Lily looks for Tom behind the trees, under the bench, and near the slide. She cannot find him. She thinks he is very good at hiding. She walks around the park and says, "Tom, where are you?"

Tom is hiding in a big box near the trash can. He thinks he is very clever. He hears Lily's voice and smiles. He wants to see her face when she finds him. He decides to peek out of the box for a minute.

But when he peeks out, he sees a big dog running towards him. The dog is black and furry and has a loud bark. Tom is scared. He does not like dogs. He thinks the dog wants to bite him. He screams, "Help! Help!"

Lily hears Tom's scream and runs to him. She sees the dog and the box. She picks up a stick and waves it at the dog. She says, "Go away! Go away! Leave Tom alone!"

The dog sees the stick and the girl. He thinks they are not fun. He runs away to find another game. Lily drops the stick and opens the box. She sees Tom inside. He is sweaty and hot. He hugs Lily and says, "Thank you! Thank you! You saved me!"

Lily hugs Tom and says, "You're welcome! You're welcome! Are you okay?"

Tom nods and says, "I'm okay. But I don't like dogs. And I don't like hiding in boxes. They are hot and scary."

Lily says, "Me too. I don't like dogs. And I don't like looking for boxes. They are hard and boring."

Tom says, "Do you want to play something else?"

Lily says, "Yes, please. How about tag?"

Tom says, "Okay. Tag sounds fun. You're it!"

Lily says, "No, you're it!"

They laugh and run around the park. They forget about the dog and the box. They have fun playing tag.

Anna and Ben were playing in their room. They had many toys and books and pictures. They liked to decorate their room with their things. They put stickers on the wall, and hung drawings on the door, and made a fort with blankets and pillows.

Suddenly, they heard a loud noise outside. It was thunder. They looked out the window and saw dark clouds and rain. They felt scared and ran to their mom.

"Mom, mom, there is thunder and it is dark!" they cried.

Mom hugged them and said, "Don't worry, my loves. Thunder is just the sound of the clouds talking to each other. And dark is just the color of the sky when it is sleepy. It will be bright and sunny again soon."

She took them to the kitchen and gave them some cookies and milk. She said, "Why don't we decorate some cookies with sprinkles and frosting? That will be fun and yummy."

Anna and Ben smiled and nodded. They forgot about the thunder and the dark. They decorated their cookies with different colors and shapes. They ate some and shared some with mom. They felt happy and safe. They thanked mom for the cookies and the hug. They said, "We love you, mom. You are the best."

Once upon a time, there was a leaf. The leaf wanted to rise up high in the sky, like a kite. It tried to flap its edges, but the wind was too slow. 

So the leaf found an idea. It decided to find something sour. It saw a lemon and asked it for a little bit of help. The lemon was sour and strong enough that it could help the leaf rise up high. The leaf felt the sour lemon push it up and up until it was higher than the clouds!

The leaf was so happy that it was flying. It spread its edges to go even higher. It flew over the trees, houses, and even the ocean! 

Finally, after a long journey, the leaf had to come down. But it had made its dream come true, and it had risen higher than it ever thought possible!

Once upon a time, there were two friends. They were both happy and liked to play together. One day they wanted to do something special so they invited their friends to join them. Soon, a big group of happy friends had gathered.

The friends liked to hug and they all gave each other big hugs. The group was so happy. But then they noticed someone far away looking lonely. They wanted to make the person feel better so they decided to give him a big hug too. 

They all ran towards him and hugged him. He was very surprised and began to smile. He felt so happy to be part of the group.

From that day on, the group was even closer and happier. They would always remember to reach out to the people who felt distant and offer them a big hug.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Sarah. She loved to explore the world around her. One day Sarah decided to go for a walk.

As Sarah was walking she saw a man in the distance. He was not moving at all. The man seemed to be frozen. Sarah knew that this was not normal so she decided to take a closer look.

When Sarah got closer to the man she noticed the look on his face was dull. He was not moving like the other people that she had seen walking around. She knew that something was wrong and felt very scared.

Sarah wished that the man could move again, so she started to clap her hands together. To her surprise the man started to move again. The man said thank you and gave Sarah a big hug.

Sarah was so happy that she was able to help the man. From then on whenever Sarah was scared she would clap her hands together, just in case!

Once upon a time, there was a powerful train named Big Red. He loved to go fast on the rails. One day, he saw a little bird named Bluey.

"Hi, Bluey!" said Big Red. "Do you want to race with me?"

Bluey said, "Yes, let's race to the big tree!"

Big Red and Bluey started the race. They went very fast. Big Red was on the rail, and Bluey was in the sky. They both wanted to succeed and win the race.

As they got close to the big tree, Bluey was ahead. But then, Big Red used his powerful engine to go even faster. In the end, Big Red won the race.

"Good job, Big Red!" said Bluey. "You are very powerful and fast!" They both laughed and played together, happy to be friends.

Lily and Ben were playing with their toys in the living room. Lily had a big doll and Ben had a small car. Lily liked her doll very much, but she wished she had a car too. She asked Ben if she could play with his car for a while.

"No, this is my car. You have your doll. Go away!" Ben said. He was not very friendly.

Lily felt sad and angry. She wanted to have a car too. She thought of a plan. She saw a bottle on the table. It had a label that said "shrink". She did not know what that word meant, but she thought it might make things smaller. She took the bottle and sprayed some of it on Ben's car.

Ben saw what Lily did and shouted. "Hey, what are you doing? Stop it! You are making my car shrink!"

Lily laughed. She thought it was funny to see Ben's car get smaller and smaller. She picked up the tiny car and put it in her pocket. She said, "Now I have a car too. And you have nothing. Ha ha!"

Ben was very upset. He cried and ran to his mom. He told her what Lily did. Mom was not happy. She scolded Lily and made her give back the car. She said, "Lily, that was not nice. You should not take things that are not yours. And you should not use things that you do not understand. You could have hurt Ben or yourself. You need to say sorry to Ben and share your toys."

Lily felt sorry. She realized she was wrong. She gave back the car to Ben and said, "I'm sorry, Ben. I was mean. I should not have sprayed your car. Can we be friends again?"

Ben was still sad, but he forgave Lily. He said, "It's okay, Lily. I'm sorry too. I should have been more friendly. Can we play together?"

Lily and Ben hugged and smiled. They decided to play together and share their toys. They learned a lesson. They wished they would never fight again.

Once upon a time there was a fire. It was very messy. All around it were things that were beginning to rot. 

Suddenly, a little girl arrived next to the fire. She was wearing a big yellow hat on her head. She saw how messy the fire was and felt sad. 

The little girl decided to help. She got some water from the nearby river and started to put it on the fire. As the water hit the fire, it started to shrink, until it disappeared. 

The little girl was happy to see that the fire was not messy anymore. She smiled and cheered. Then, she continued walking, happy and proud of what she had done. 

The end.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Jack and Jill. They liked to explore the woods. One day, Jack said, "Let's go and find mushrooms!" Jill thought this was a good idea.

They started to look for mushrooms. Jack saw a big mushroom and he said, "I'm going to pick that mushroom!" But Jill said, "No, that's a stupid mushroom. Let's go and find another one!"

So they kept on walking and they saw some small mushrooms near a bush. Jack and Jill separated, so they could each look for mushrooms in different places.

Jack found a group of mushrooms and he said to Jill, "Look, I've found these beautiful mushrooms!" Jill took a look and said, "These mushrooms look much better than the first one - let's take them home!"

And they picked up all of the mushrooms and took them home - and that's the end of the story!

One day, a girl named Sally wanted to print a picture. She liked to draw and color. She drew a big salad with many colors. There were red tomatoes, green lettuce, and yellow peppers. She was happy with her picture.

Sally showed her mom the pretty salad picture. Her mom was grateful and gave her a hug. Sally felt warm and loved. She wanted to make more pictures for her mom.

Sally and her mom went to the store. They bought real salad things like the picture. They made a big salad together. They ate it for dinner. Sally felt happy and proud.

Once upon a time, there was a gloomy doll. One day, it started to ring. It made a loud noise, like a bell. 

The doll had a secret. Whenever it rang, a magic door would open. Through the door, the doll could go on exciting adventures. 

The first time the doll rang, it went to a farm. It saw cows and horses, and even a rooster. The rooster crowed loudly, but the doll wasn't scared.

The most fun adventure happened when the doll rang again. It flew up, up, up into the sky. High above the clouds, it saw the world below. Everything looked so small!

The last time the doll rang, it found itself back on the shelf. It was happy to have gone on so many exciting journeys.

From that day on, the doll's eyes sparkled with joy every time it rang.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sue. Sue loved to play in the park. Her favorite thing to do was to slide down the big slide. One hot day, she went to the park to play with her friends.

While playing, Sue and her friends found a small trap near the slide. They were curious about the trap. Sue thought it was for catching bugs. Her friend Tom thought it was for catching birds. They decided to watch the trap and see what would happen.

As they played and watched the trap, they saw a little bug walk into it. The bug was caught! Sue and Tom were excited. They let the bug go and continued to play. They had so much fun on the hot day, sliding down the slide and watching the trap catch bugs.

Jen and Tom were playing with their dolls in the living room. They liked to make up stories and act them out. Jen had a big doll with long hair and a pink dress. Tom had a small doll with a hat and a blue shirt.

"Let's go upstairs and set up a tea party for our dolls," Jen said. "We can use Mommy's cups and plates."

"Okay," Tom said. "But we have to be quiet. Mommy is napping upstairs. She is not feeling well. She is pale and has a sore throat."

They tiptoed upstairs with their dolls and went to Mommy's room. They saw Mommy sleeping on the bed. She looked pale and tired. They did not want to wake her up.

They went to the closet and found some cups and plates. They set them up on a small table in the corner. They pretended to pour tea and serve cookies to their dolls. They whispered and giggled.

"Would you like some more tea, Miss Doll?" Jen asked.

"Yes, please, Mr. Doll," Tom answered.

They had fun playing with their dolls. They did not notice that Mommy had opened her eyes and was watching them. She smiled and felt happy. She was glad that Jen and Tom were such good children. She loved them very much.

Tom and Jen are friends. They like to play and help each other. They are a good team. One day, they see a big box in the park. They want to see what is inside.

"Maybe there are toys or candy in the box," Tom says.

"Let's open it and find out," Jen says.

They go to the box and try to lift the lid. But the lid is too heavy and stuck. They push and pull, but nothing happens.

"Maybe we can solve this problem," Tom says. "We can look for something to help us open the lid."

"Good idea," Jen says. "You look over there, and I look over here."

They split up and search for something to help them. Tom finds a stick and Jen finds a rock. They run back to the box with their tools.

"Look, I have a stick," Tom says.

"And I have a rock," Jen says.

They use the stick and the rock to pry the lid open. They hear a click and a hiss. They are happy. They think they solved the problem.

But they are wrong. The box is not a toy box. It is a trap. Inside the box, there is a snake. A big, angry snake. It jumps out of the box and bites Tom and Jen. They scream and cry. They are hurt and scared. They are not safe.

The end.

Josh was an adventurous little boy. He loved going on adventures and exploring. One day, Josh decided to visit the reef. He asked his mom if he could go and she happily included him on the trip. 

On the way to the reef, Josh asked lots of questions about what he would see. His mom told him about all the incredible sea creatures that lived there. 

When they arrived at the reef, Josh was amazed. He had never seen so many beautiful and colourful fish.

He snorkelled in the clear water and even spotted a small shark. "Come look!" Josh cried. His mom swam over as quickly as she could.

"Wow," his mom said. "That was adventurous, wasn't it?"

Josh shook his head and said, "Let's come back tomorrow, please!"

Joey was very kind. He always said hello to everyone he saw. But one day, when he was walking in his garden, Joey saw a cactus. He said hello but it didn't answer. Joey thought it was being rude and ignoring him. He asked it again but it still didn't answer. Joey got mad and decided to ignore the cactus instead. He wouldn't even look at it.

A few days later, Joey was walking again in his garden and he saw the cactus. He wanted to ignore it but his kind heart wouldn't let him. He smiled at it and said, "Hello! I'm sorry for not saying hello to you earlier."

The cactus didn't answer, but Joey felt better for not ignoring it.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Rose. Rose loved sunsets and dreamed of exploring the world.

One day when she was playing in the park, Rose imagined that she was on a far away adventure. She pictured a row of ancient boats that she could take to explore. She was so excited!

"I'm going to be a great explorer!" she said to her friends. 

All of a sudden, a huge storm came and the sky turned dark. Wind and rain poured down. Rose and her friends were so scared! Rose tried to make a getaway but the storm only seemed to get worse. 

Soon, the ancient row of boats she imagined floated away and disappeared. She knew she could never reach them now.

Rose was heartbroken as she walked home alone in the rain. She learned that sometimes, even if you dream and imagine, things don't always turn out the way you expected.

Lily and Ben were very happy to move to a new house. They had many boxes with their toys and clothes. They wanted to unpack them and play in their new rooms.

"Can we unpack now, Mom?" Lily asked.

"Not yet, sweetie. We have to wait for Dad to come home. He has the keys to the rooms," Mom said.

Lily and Ben were sad. They wanted to unpack now. They looked around the living room. They saw a big couch. It was red and blue and yellow. It had many shapes on it. It was a unique couch.

"Wow, look at this couch!" Ben said. "It looks like a puzzle. Let's play on it!"

Lily and Ben climbed on the couch. They jumped and bounced and slid. They had fun. They did not see the sign on the couch. It said: "Do not sit on the couch. It is very old and fragile. It will break."

The couch made a loud noise. It cracked and snapped and collapsed. Lily and Ben fell to the floor. They were hurt and scared. They cried.

Mom heard the noise. She ran to the living room. She saw the broken couch and the crying children. She was angry and worried.

"What have you done?" Mom yelled. "This couch was very special. It belonged to Grandma. She gave it to us as a gift. It was very expensive and rare. You have ruined it!"

Lily and Ben felt very bad. They said they were sorry. They did not mean to break the couch. They just wanted to play.

Mom did not listen. She said they were naughty and careless. She said they had to go to their rooms and stay there. She said they could not unpack or play until Dad came home. She said he would be very mad too.

Lily and Ben went to their rooms. They were sad and lonely. They wished they had not played on the couch. They wished they had waited to unpack. They wished they had a different new house. They wished they had a different mom.

Sam was a 3 year old boy and he loved playing outdoors. One nice day he went outside and saw something exciting. His dad was showing him two purple tires. Sam was so excited - he had never seen anything like it before! 

His dad explained that these were special tires made for a bike. Sam was so happy he was about to get a new bike with these tires. He couldn't wait to take it for a ride. 

The next day, Sam was ready to go for a ride with his new bike. He put on his helmet and his dad helped him get on. As he started to pedal his bike, he felt so happy as the purple tires carried him along. 

Sam had so much fun zooming around the neighborhood with his new bike. He felt so much freedom and joy with the purple tires. He was one happy 3 year old!

Once upon a time, there was a garden. It was full of brightly coloured flowers and tall green trees.

Every day, the garden looked different. Today, a little girl was in the garden and she was busy. She was picking up leaves and twigs and putting them in a pile.

The girl worked very fast. She wanted to finish the garden quickly. Soon, all of the leaves and twigs were gone and the little girl was done. She thanked the garden for all its help and smiled.

The garden looked so much better now. The girl was very proud of what she had done. She promised to always look after the garden from now on.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside in the park with his friends. One day, they heard a strange sound coming from the woods. It was a loud noise that made them all feel scared.

Timmy decided to be brave and lead his friends to investigate the sound. As they got closer, they saw a dangerous animal! It was a big bear that had gotten lost in the park. Timmy knew they had to be careful, so he told his friends to stay back while he called for help.

The park rangers came and safely captured the bear. Timmy felt proud that he was able to lead his friends to safety and help the park rangers. From that day on, Timmy and his friends knew that they should always be careful when they hear a dangerous sound.

John was a jolly boy. Every day he would pick flowers and play with his toys. One day, his mom wanted to give him a special treat.

"John, would you like a cake?" she asked.

John was so excited. "Yes, please!" he said.

His mom drove to the store and picked out a beautiful cake. When they arrived home, she put the cake on the kitchen table.

John's eyes lit up. He could feel how special the occasion was. He knew he would be able to enjoy the cake today.

John's mom grabbed a knife, cut a piece and gave it to John. He took a bite and it was the most delicious cake he ever tasted! He was so happy and jolly that day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Anna. She was only three and loved to play outside. One day, Anna decided to take a walk in the dark woods. She loved the trees and the animals that lived there.

As Anna walked deeper into the woods she got very scared. It was dark and very quiet. Suddenly, she heard a faint sound coming from the trees. She tiptoed closer to investigate and there, in the centre of the dark forest, sat a little bear. 

The bear was eating jam and Anna was amazed. She wanted some too, so she asked the bear if she could have some. The bear said no and Anna began to cry. She begged the bear but he said no again. 

Just then Anna heard a voice from above that said: "Believe, Anna. If you believe hard enough, anything is possible". Anna looked up and saw a bright star in the night sky. Taking the words to heart, Anna put her hands together and closed her eyes. She believed with all her might and when she opened her eyes, there was a jar of jam in front of her!

Anna was surprised and overjoyed. She thanked the star for her kind words and happily enjoyed her jam. Anna was so happy she decided to share her jar with the little bear and from then on, they were the best of friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Clara. She had long blonde hair and a great big smile.

One day, Clara was outside playing in her garden when she found a handle. She picked it up and wondered what it might belong to. 

Suddenly, a voice called out to her. 

"Clara, where did you find that handle?" Clara looked up and saw a tall man with a frown on his face. 

"I found it in the garden," Clara said. 

"That's terrible!" the man said. "That handle belongs to my axe. I must have dropped it!" 

The man thanked Clara for finding his handle and took it back to his house. Clara was happy she had been able to help someone, and glad that the handle belonged to someone.

Once upon a time, there was a bird named Blue. Blue loved to fly high in the sky and look for food. One day, Blue saw a perfect land with lots of seeds and fruits. Blue decided to take a rest and eat some food.

While Blue was eating, a big storm came and blew Blue away. Blue tried to fly back to the perfect land but the wind was too strong. Blue flew and flew but couldn't find the perfect land again. Blue was lost and hungry.

Days passed and Blue became weaker and weaker. Blue couldn't fly anymore and fell to the ground. Blue never found the perfect land again and sadly passed away. The end.

Once there was a little girl who didn't like the things she did. She felt ashamed of them. 

One day, she went into a special chamber. It was dark and quiet in there. She didn't like the chamber at all. She felt scared and angry.

The little girl started to hate the chamber because it made her feel ashamed. She wanted to get out, but she felt trapped and alone. 

Finally, the chamber opened and the little girl ran out. She was happy to get away from it. 

The little girl never went back to the chamber again. She was relieved to be away from it, and she never wanted to go back.

Ben and Sam were brothers who liked to play in the sand. They had a big bucket and a small shovel. They made hills and holes and castles. They pretended they were kings of the desert.

One day, they saw something shiny in the distance. They ran towards it, hoping it was a treasure. But it was not a treasure. It was an oasis, a place with water and trees and grass. Ben and Sam were very happy. They drank some water and ate some dates. They felt cool and fresh.

But then they saw a fat camel lying under a palm tree. The camel looked sleepy and bored. Ben had an idea. He said to Sam, "Let's kick the camel and see what it does. Maybe it will run or spit or make a funny noise."

Sam thought it was a bad idea. He said, "No, Ben, don't kick the camel. It is not nice. The camel did not do anything to us. Maybe it will get angry and hurt us."

But Ben did not listen. He ran towards the camel and kicked it hard on its side. The camel woke up with a loud roar. It was very angry. It jumped up and chased Ben and Sam. It bit Ben on his arm and Sam on his leg. It made them cry and bleed.

Ben and Sam ran away from the oasis, back to the sand. They wished they had never kicked the camel. They wished they had been nice and gentle. They learned a hard lesson. They were not kings of the desert. They were just naughty boys who got punished.

Once upon a time there was a little boy called James. He was just three years old.

One day James wanted to try something new. He quit his favourite game and started playing something different. His mom was happy with his decision.

Next day, James' mom asked him for his opinion about the new game. James thought it was good. He liked it very much as he could learn lots of new things from it.

James' mom was very pleased with his opinion. She said to him, "Good job James! Taking a risk and trying new things can be really fun."

James felt happy. From that day, he quit his old game and started playing the new one.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to skip and play in the park. One day, as she was skipping, she looked up at the sky and saw a bright comet. It was so beautiful and shiny. She wished upon the comet for something special.

The next day, a wealthy man came to the park and saw Lily skipping. He was impressed by how happy she looked. He asked her what she wished for when she saw the comet. Lily told him she wished for a big ice cream cone. The wealthy man smiled and said he would buy her the biggest ice cream cone she had ever seen.

Lily was so happy and grateful. She enjoyed her ice cream cone and skipped all the way home. From that day on, she knew that sometimes wishes really do come true.

Ben is a boy who likes to play with cars. He has many cars of different colors and sizes. He likes to make them zoom and crash on the floor. He is very bossy and does not like to share his cars with anyone.

One day, his mom brings home a new baby sister. Ben is curious and wants to see her. He goes to her room and sees her sleeping in a crib. He also sees a basket full of toys next to her. He looks inside and sees some cars. He thinks they are his cars and he wants to take them.

He reaches for the basket, but his mom stops him. She says, "No, Ben, those are not your cars. Those are your sister's cars. She got them as a gift. You have your own cars in your room. You need to share and be nice to your sister."

Ben does not like what his mom says. He says, "But I want those cars! They are better than mine! She does not need them! She is too small to play with them!"

His mom says, "Ben, that is not how you talk to your mom or your sister. You need to be kind and respectful. You can play with your sister's cars if you ask her nicely and include her in your game. Maybe she will let you play with her other toys too. But you cannot take them without asking. That is rude and selfish."

Ben thinks for a moment. He does not want to be rude and selfish. He also wants to play with the new cars. He decides to try what his mom says. He goes to the crib and looks at his sister. She is awake and smiling. He says, "Hi, sister. I am Ben. You are cute. Can I play with your cars? I will include you in my game. We can make them zoom and crash together. It will be fun."

His sister giggles and reaches for a car. She gives it to Ben. Ben says, "Thank you, sister. Here, you can have this one. It is red. It is my favorite. But I will share it with you. Because you are my sister and I love you."

His mom smiles and hugs them both. She says, "That's very nice, Ben. I am proud of you. You are a good brother. And you are not bossy anymore. You are a good friend."

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tom and a little girl named Sue. They were brother and sister. They had a bedroom that they shared. In the bedroom, they had a big toy box with many toys.

One day, Tom and Sue found a fake snake in the toy box. It was green and long. They both wanted to play with it. Tom said, "Let's share the snake." Sue agreed, and they played with the snake together.

They took turns pretending to be scared of the snake. They laughed and had a lot of fun. After they played, they put the fake snake back in the toy box. Tom and Sue were happy because they shared and had fun in their bedroom.

Once upon a time, there was a brave knight who lived in a castle. He had a shield and a clean sword. One day, a dragon came to terrorize the kingdom. The knight bravely faced the dragon.

"Stay back!" shouted the brave knight.
The dragon roared in response and angrily puffed fire into the sky.

The knight brandished his clean sword and waved it at the dragon. The dragon got really mad. It opened its mouth wide and roared again. 

The knight was determined to beat the dragon. He stepped closer to the dragon and shouted, "Go back to your cave! I command you!"

The dragon glared at the knight, but could not stand up to his bravery. It obediently flew away into the sky, never to threaten the kingdom again. The knight saved the day!

Once there was a puppy named Mike. One day he saw a match on the ground and he wanted to catch it. But a rabbit was also trying to catch it. Mike wanted to get the match, but he was a bit too small.

The rabbit was bigger and he could reach it first. He was ready to catch it, but Mike shouted: "Stop! That's not fair!"

The rabbit answered: "Why? I just want it more than you."

Mike said: "That's not fair! You're being selfish!"

The rabbit didn't want to be said that he was selfish. So he stopped and said: "OK, you can have it. It's not worth arguing over."

Mike was very happy and he quickly caught the match. He thanked the rabbit and they both went their own way.

Once upon a time there was a wise doll. She mixed with all kinds of people. One day, she met a funny man. He had a wheelbarrow full of sweets. He said: "Let's mix together some of those treats!"

The wise doll started to mix all the different sweets. She mixed chocolates and lollipops and gummy bears. After a while, the wheelbarrow was full of yummy treats!

The funny man was happy. He gave the wise doll a big hug and said: "Let's give these treats to all the kids in the park!"

So the wise doll and funny man went to the park. The kids were so happy when they saw the treats! They ran around and had a lot of fun.

The wise doll was happy too. She had made all the kids smile. She knew she had made the right mix!

Once there was a little girl and she wanted an expensive balloon. She asked her mum, but her mum said no because it was too expensive. The little girl was sad.

The little girl asked her grandma, but her grandma said no too. The little girl's eyes started to fill with tears. Then, her grandpa said he would buy the balloon. The little girl smiled and nodded.

The little girl and her grandpa went to the shop and he bought the balloon. But, when they arrived home the balloon had gone! It had floated away. The little girl was so sad and she cried. Her grandpa said he was sorry. He gave her a hug.

The little girl nodded and she knew that her grandpa had tried his best. The balloon had been too expensive and it was gone.

Once upon a time, there was a lady who wanted a muffin. She knew where to go to get a muffin-- the bakery! So she got up and started walking.

The lady was very patient. She took her time and walked slowly. When she arrived at the bakery, she saw a shelf full of muffins. She carried the muffin to the counter and the baker said, "One muffin for you, please!"

The lady thanked the baker and carried her muffin outside. She sat down on a bench and enjoyed her muffin. She was so happy that she had been patient and walked all the way to the bakery!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who had a large yearning for adventure. She asked her father if he would take her on an exciting journey. He agreed but said she needed to prepare for a long journey.

So, she spent the next couple of days collecting supplies. On the day of their departure, she was ready and excited. 

They set off bright and early. As they were walking, they came across an inviting meadow. There she found a strange and magical rock. She decided to rub the rock with her hands. Suddenly, an old man appeared out of nowhere.

Once upon a time, there was a grumpy bear named Rudy. Rudy loved sports, but he was always so grumpy!

Once upon a time, there was a grumpy cricket who lived in a big, green field. He was always angry and never wanted to play with the other animals. One day, a little girl named Lily came to the field to play. She saw the cricket and said, "Hello, little cricket. Why are you so grumpy?"

The cricket was surprised and happy. Lily gently picked him up and released him into the air. The cricket flew away, feeling free and happy. From that day on, the cricket was no longer grumpy and would sing beautiful songs wherever he went. Lily was happy to have helped the little cricket and they became good friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside with her toys. One day, a big wind came and made a tornado. The tornado was very scary and made all the toys disappear. Lily was sad because her favorite toy, a teddy bear, was gone.

But then, she saw a naughty squirrel running away with her teddy bear! Lily chased after the squirrel and finally caught it. She took her teddy bear back and was happy again. The tornado disappeared and the sun came out. Lily played with her toys and had a great day. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily and her mom went to the store to buy some groceries. While they were shopping, Lily saw a toy that she wanted to buy. She asked her mom if she could get it, but her mom said no because they didn't have enough money.

Lily insisted that she wanted the toy, but her mom explained that they needed to buy food first. Lily was sad, but she understood. As they were walking down the aisle, Lily saw a glass jar and wanted to hold it. Her mom let her handle the jar carefully, and Lily was glad that she got to help.

On the way home, Lily and her mom talked about the things they bought and what they were going to make for dinner. Lily was excited to help her mom cook. When they got home, Lily insisted on helping with everything, and her mom was glad to have such a helpful daughter. They had a delicious dinner and played with some toys before going to bed.

Once upon a time there was a rat. His name was Peter and he was very brave. One day, Peter started to explore the world outside his house. He came across a bottle full of a strange liquid. Peter sniffed it and it smelled bad. He thought it was poison.

Though he was scared, Peter decided to drink a drop. Suddenly, the poison tasted sweet! Peter was so surprised that he dropped the bottle and it broke. From the poison spilled out a rare gem.

Peter was so excited that he started jumping up and down. A nearby rabbit watched him curiously.

The rabbit asked, "What happened? Why are you so happy?"

Peter smiled and said, "I found something very special. It's a rare gem that I found in the bottle of poison I drank!"

Once upon a time there was a boy who felt sleepy. He wanted to go to wake and explore the unknown. So he jumped out of bed and started running. He ran and ran, until he got to a strange and unknown place. He saw some animals walking about and an unfamiliar tree. He was scared.

The boy heard a voice, it said "Do not feel scared, come closer and learn more about the unknown". The boy was curious, so he listened to the voice and stepped closer. The voice continued, "Welcome to the unknown, I am the friendly wake. I will help you explore and discover new things in this world".

The boy felt excited and no longer scared. He thanked the wake and looked around. He saw so many new and different things, each one even stranger than the last. He could feel the newness of it all and he felt different too. 

The boy smiled and said to the wake, "I'm ready to explore and learn more". The wake agreed, and off they went!

One day, a tall girl was walking outside. She saw a banana lying on the ground and said, â€œOh! I believe this is a special banana.â€ So the girl decided to pick it up and take it home.

When she got home, she asked her mom what she should do with the banana. Her mom said, â€œMaybe you should save it for a special occasion.â€

The girl was confused. â€œWhat special occasion?â€ she asked her mom. Her mom just smiled and said, â€œYouâ€™ll see. Just put the banana in the fridge and wait.â€

So the girl put the banana away and waited. A few weeks later, the girl finally found out what the special occasion was: it was her 3rd birthday. Her mom was planning to make a special banana cake to celebrate.
