Once upon a time, there was a smart boy named Timmy. He was very good at solving puzzles and riddles. One day, his teacher asked him to decorate the blackboard with colorful chalks. Timmy was very happy to do it because he loved drawing.

He drew a big sun with a happy face and a blue sky with fluffy clouds. He also drew a green tree with red apples and a yellow bird sitting on its branch. When he finished, his teacher was amazed at how intelligent Timmy was.

From that day on, Timmy became the class decorator. He decorated the blackboard every week with new drawings and colors. All his classmates loved his beautiful and creative decorations. Timmy was very proud of himself and he knew he had a special talent.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Mia. Mia was quite a shy girl and she rarely said yes to anyone who invited her to do something. But one day, a friend of hers called Tom asked her to come to his house for a party. Mia got very excited and said yes to this invitation.

When she arrived, she immediately felt welcomed and comfortable.Tom had decorated the house beautifully and everyone was very friendly. Mia felt happy that she had accepted the invitation.

Mia and her friends had fun playing together and dancing. They ate delicious food and laughed a lot. Mia even made some new friends that day.

At the end of the day, Mia thanked Tom for inviting her. She was glad she had accepted the invitation and it made her feel even more comfortable.

Mia and Tom looked forward to more fun days together, and Mia became more open to accepting invitations.

Jen and Tom were friends. They liked to play in the park. They liked to swing and slide and run. They knew summer was fun.

One day, Jen had a new dress. It was pink and pretty. She showed it to Tom. "Do you like my dress?" she asked.

Tom nodded. He liked Jen's dress. But he liked his shorts more. They were blue and loose. He could move and jump in them. He did not like tight clothes.

"Let's go to the slide!" Tom said. He ran to the slide. Jen followed him. She wanted to slide too.

But when Jen got to the top of the slide, she saw a problem. Her dress was too long and tight. It got stuck on the slide. Jen could not move. She was scared.

"Help me, Tom!" she cried. "My dress is stuck!"

Tom heard Jen. He ran back to the slide. He saw Jen's dress. He pulled it hard. It did not come off. He pulled harder. It ripped.

Jen was free. She slid down the slide. She was happy. But she was also sad. Her dress was ruined.

"I'm sorry, Jen," Tom said. "I did not mean to rip your dress."

"It's okay, Tom," Jen said. "You helped me. You are a good friend."

They hugged. They knew they were still friends. They knew summer was not over. They knew they could play again. But they also knew they had to be careful with their clothes.

Lily likes to eat carrots. They are orange and crunchy and good for her eyes. She always asks for carrots when Mommy makes dinner. But today, she is not hungry. She plays with her toys and forgets about her plate.

"Come on, Lily, finish your carrot," Mommy says. "It's getting cold and you need to eat something."

Lily shakes her head. She does not want to finish her carrot. She wants to play more. She sees a white bunny outside the window. The bunny is hopping and nibbling on the grass. Lily thinks the bunny is cute and funny.

"Look, Mommy, a bunny!" Lily says. She points to the window.

Mommy looks too. She smiles and has an idea. She picks up the carrot and breaks it in half. She gives one half to Lily and keeps the other.

"Let's pretend we are bunnies too," Mommy says. "We can hop and nibble on our carrots. Maybe the bunny will come and play with us."

Lily likes this game. She takes the carrot and hops around the room. She nibbles on the carrot and makes bunny noises. Mommy does the same. They have fun and laugh. The bunny outside sees them and comes closer. It wiggles its nose and ears. It wants to join the game.

Lily and Mommy finish their carrots. They are happy and full. They wave to the bunny and say goodbye. They clean up their plates and toys. They hug and kiss. They go to bed and dream of bunnies.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Sarah. She was three years old and very energetic. Every morning she would jump out of bed and run around the house, jumping and laughing. 

One day Sarah decided that she wanted to try balancing. She looked around and found a tall stick which she decided she could use to balance on. She set the stick on the ground and hopped on top of it.

Sarah's dad watched her with a big smile and clapped his hands. He called out "Hey Sarah! You are doing a great job balancing. It looks like you are going to be an expert in no time." 

Sarah felt very proud as she kept balancing and speeding up. She laughed out loud every time she felt herself going faster.

"Yay!" She shouted out "I'm doing it!"

Her dad encouraged her to keep trying and with each passing day Sarah became more and more enthusiastic about balancing. 

Finally, one day she was able to balance perfectly. She jumped up and down in celebration and her dad praised her for her hard work.

Sarah was so proud of herself and she smiled with joy. She could not believe that she had managed to master balancing at such a young age.

The sun was setting and Sam was getting ready for bed. As Sam looked out of the window, he saw a huge question mark in the sky. He stared at it for a moment.

Mum came into the room and asked, "What are you looking at?". Sam pointed to the huge question mark in the sky. Mum smiled, "I think it's time for some bedtime stories."

Sam was excited for his bedtime story but he couldn't stop staring at the question mark. Mum began telling him a story about a brave knight who had to answer an important question, but she stopped and said, "The answer is up there." She pointed foreshadowingly at the huge question mark in the sky.

The knight in the story tried to find the answer to the question, and finally one night, he made it to the top of a tall mountain and the huge question mark came into view. When the knight got to the question mark, he realised the answer to his question was within himself.

Sam gasped with wonder and surprise. He couldn't believe it. Mum smiled at him and said, "Sometimes, the answers to our questions can be found within us." 

Sam lay back in bed feeling amazed and grateful as he watched the huge question mark in the sky slowly disappear.

Lily and Max were playing in the park. They liked the slide a lot. They took turns to go down the slide. Lily went first, then Max, then Lily, then Max.

But then a big boy came. He said he wanted the slide. He pushed Lily and Max away. He said they were too small and he was big. He said the slide was his.

Lily and Max were sad and scared. They did not know what to do. They looked at their mom. Their mom was on a bench. She was reading a book. She did not see the big boy.

Lily wanted to tell their mom. She said to Max, "Let's go to mom. She will help us." But Max was obedient. He said, "No, mom said we have to play nice and share. We have to wait for our turn."

Lily did not like that. She said, "But he is not nice. He is mean. He does not share. He took our slide." Max shrugged. He said, "I don't know. Maybe he will go soon. Maybe he will get bored."

Lily and Max waited and waited. But the big boy did not go. He did not get bored. He kept going down the slide. He laughed and shouted. He did not care about Lily and Max.

Lily and Max were very sad. They missed the slide. They wished the big boy would leave. They wished their mom would see. They wished they could have fun.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there was a little boy named Tim. He had a big, soft mattress in his room. Tim loved to jump on his mattress and play all day. It would excite him so much.

One day, a new friend named Sam came to play with Tim. Sam was very polite and always said "please" and "thank you." They played with toys and had a lot of fun. Then, Tim showed Sam his big, soft mattress.

Tim and Sam started to jump on the mattress, and they both felt excited. But then, Tim's mom came into the room. She told them it was not safe to jump on the mattress. Tim and Sam stopped jumping and listened to her.

From that day on, Tim and Sam learned to be polite and listen to their parents. They also learned that it is important to be safe while playing. And that was the moral value they learned: always be safe and listen to your parents.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and go on adventures. One day, her mom said, "Lily, let's go visit grandma!" Lily was excited to see her grandma and said, "Yay! I want to ride in the car!"

As they drove to grandma's house, they saw a big wheel at the fair. Lily said, "Mom, can we go on the wheel?" Her mom said, "Sure, we can visit the fair after we see grandma."

When they arrived at grandma's house, Lily saw a scary spider on the wall. She said, "Mom, the spider is scary!" Her mom said, "Don't worry, I'll take care of it." After they said hi to grandma, they went to the fair and rode the big wheel. Lily had so much fun and couldn't wait to visit grandma again.

Mama was so excited. She had finished making a special sheet. It was incredible! Mama held it up so they could both look at it.

"Wow!", the three year old exclaimed.

Mama smiled and said, "Would you please help me put it on the bed?"

The child put her hands on her hips. "No!" she shouted. She didn't want to help.

Mama frowned. "Please darling," she asked, "it will only take a minute and then we'll do something fun together."

The child thought for a moment, then nodded. She helped Mama put the incredible sheet on the bed. When it was finished, the child turned to Mama and said, "Can we play now?"

Mama smiled with relief. "Yes!" she said. "Let's go!"

They ran outside and played in the sunshine. It was an incredible day.

One day, a clumsy dog named Max went for a walk. Max liked to stare at things. He stared at the sun, the trees, and the birds. Max was very happy.

Max saw a man with a big bottle. The man said, "This is wine." Max did not know what wine was. The man was not careful and he dropped the bottle. The wine spilled everywhere.

Max looked at the wine and said, "Oh no! I will help you clean it." The man and Max cleaned the wine together. They became good friends and had a fun day.

Once upon a time there was a jolly little girl. She loved to play in the garden and explore. She was always curious and full of adventure.

One day the girl was playing in the garden when she heard a whistle. She had never heard a sound like that before and wanted to find out what it was.

The girl followed the sound until she reached a fence. She tried to see what was on the other side, but it was too tall for her. So, she decided she would find a way to jump over it.

The girl tried jumping over the fence but it was too hard. She looked around and saw a box she could stand on. She pushed it to the fence so she could stand on it and reach the top.

Finally, the girl was able to reach the top and get a look at the other side. There she saw a little puppy playing with a stick.

The girl was so excited, she jumped off the box and ran over to the puppy. The puppy was so happy to see the girl. She picked up the stick and the puppy ran around.

The little girl was so happy that she has finished a task. She laughed and whistled to the puppy as they played together. They both had a jolly time.

Once upon a time, there lived a hairy mole. He liked to hide in his hole in the ground. One day, he decided to go for a walk around the garden. While he was out walking, he noticed a big, beautiful flower. He wanted to hide in it, so he wriggled his way inside. The flower had a sweet smell and was very soft. He closed his eyes and fell asleep.

When he woke up, he heard some noises. He peeked out of the flower and saw two little children playing. He stayed very still and hid. The kids were so excited to find the hairy mole. They called out to each other and ran around, trying to catch the mole. But the mole was too fast. He quickly jumped out of the flower, ran away and hid in his hole.

The children searched all over the garden, but they could not find him. The mole was still safe in his hole.

The End!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to travel and explore new places. One day, she went for a walk in a big field. She saw lots of flowers and butterflies. She felt happy.

Suddenly, she saw a grumpy old man. He looked angry and didn't want to talk to her. Lily tried to be friendly, but the grumpy man just grunted and walked away.

Lily felt sad and decided to go home. On the way, she tripped and fell. She hurt her knee and started to cry. No one was there to help her. She felt alone and scared. The bad ending was that Lily had to crawl all the way home with a hurt knee.

Once there was a person. They were walking down the street when another person called them. The first person was happy and wanted to say hi, but the other person said no. They refused to talk.

The first person was very sad. They didn't know why the other person was so harsh. They wanted to know, but the other person refused to explain.

The first person was left standing, feeling lonely and confused. They didn't understand why the other person had been so mean and refused to let them talk.

But then the first person remembered something. They weren't alone. They had friends who had always been there for them. They thought about all the good times they had had with their friends and decided to forget about the nasty other person.

So the first person smiled and went back to their friends. They knew that with the help of their friends, nothing harsh could bring them down.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sue. Sue was always curious and loved to explore. One day she found an unknown door with a shiny handle. Sue wanted to touch the handle. She grabbed it and tried to turn it, but it wouldn't move.

Sue got a little frustrated and said, "It won't move. What should I do?" Suddenly, a voice came from the other side of the door. It said, "Hey, little girl. To open the door you must shut it first."

Sue was surprised! She didn't know why, but she figured it was worth a try. So she tried to shut the door, but it wouldn't move. Again, the voice said, "Hey, little girl. To shut the door, you must turn the handle first!"

Sue turned the handle and to her surprise the door shut! She was so excited and said, "It worked! Now what's behind the door?" 

Sue opened the door and to her delight she saw a whole new world she had never seen before. She exclaimed, "Wow! This is amazing!" and she went exploring, discovering all the unknown places and things that awaited her.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Jane. Jane was brave and strong, and she loved to march. One day she decided to march through the woods. As she marched, the sights were very nice and she smiled at the pretty trees and flowers. 

But then, something scary happened. Suddenly, the woods became dark, and Jane heard loud cries coming from deep within the trees. She felt a bit scared but steeled herself and kept marching. 

As Jane marched, she started seeing more and more mysterious sights. There were strange shapes in the trees, and big shadows all around. Jane became more and more scared, but she kept marching, determined to find her way out of the woods.

Finally, Jane emerged from the woods, back into the sunshine. She was relieved to be out of the scary forest. She smiled and waved goodbye, proud of herself for marching through the woods and out the other side!

It was a cloudy day and the sky was dark. Suddenly, it started to rain. People had to take cover from the rain and ran for shelter. But one thief was too shy to do the same. He stood still, getting soaked in the wet rain. He was not brave enough to do anything else. He kept still and shivered. His clothes were wet but he kept still and waited until the rain had stopped. After a while, the rain stopped and the thief could move again. He was still wet, but he managed to escape without being seen.

Mummy was making dinner in the kitchen. She was using a ruler to measure the ingredients.

Mummy said to me, "Can you help me measure, sweetheart?"

I asked her, "How?"

"I need you to find something quick," said Mummy.

I looked around and found some spoons and forks. I asked, "Can I use these?"

Mummy smiled and said, "Yes, but make sure you measure each spoonful carefully. We want them to be all different sizes."

So, I started measuring the ingredients. I spooned some and measured it with the ruler. I made sure each measurement was a little different.

"That looks great," said Mummy, when I finished.

"What a great helper you are," she said with a smile.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy who loved to explore. One day, he decided to go for a swim in a big blue pond. When he got there, he saw a big, dirty shark! He was scared and decided to quickly swim away.

Suddenly, the shark followed him! He started to swim faster, but the shark kept coming closer and closer. He was so scared that he decided to dive deeper in to the water.

But it was too late. The dirty shark bit his leg and dragged him to the bottom of the pond. He squirmed and tried to get away, but the shark was too strong. In the end, the little boy lost his battle with the dirty shark, and he was never seen again.

Once there was a boy named Bob. He was three years old and he loved to play chess. Bob was amazingly good at the game and he loved the thrill of winning.

One day, Bob and his dad decided to have a chess match. Bob was so excited and he did his best. He thought he had won but his dad said that he had lost. Bob was so disappointed and he just shrugged.

The next week, his dad decided to show him an amazing trick. He put the chess pieces back on the board and Bob couldn't believe his eyes. Somehow, his dad had managed to win the match. Bob grinned with excitement and he was amazed. 

Bob learned a valuable lesson and he remembered to be a good sport even when he lost. Every time his dad beat him, he just shrugged and accepted it.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved to ride her bike. She had a big sister who was very bossy and always wanted to ride her bike too. One day, the little girl's sister asked to borrow her bike. The little girl didn't want to lend her bike because she was afraid her sister would break it.

But her sister kept asking and asking until the little girl finally gave in and let her borrow the bike. The sister rode the bike too fast and didn't pay attention to where she was going. Suddenly, she hit a big rock and the wheel of the bike broke. The little girl was very sad because she knew she wouldn't be able to ride her bike anymore. She wished she had never lent it to her bossy sister.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy was very sleepy and wanted to take a nap. He went to his room and lay down on his bed. Suddenly, he heard a loud noise outside his window.

He got up to see what it was and saw a bird trying to fly but its wing was caught in a wire. Timmy felt bad for the bird and wanted to help. He went outside and gently tried to free the bird's wing from the wire.

The bird was very happy and said, "Thank you for helping me! You are so kind." Timmy felt happy too and said, "I like to help animals." The bird then asked, "Can you kick the wire away so no other animals get hurt?" Timmy kicked the wire and it flew far away. The bird flew off into the sky and Timmy went back to his room. He was tired from all the excitement and fell asleep right away.

Once upon a time, there was an ancient castle. Inside the castle, there was a big room where a player was playing a game. Suddenly, someone knocked on the door. The player stopped playing and opened the door. It was the king's messenger. 

"Please sign this paper," said the messenger. 

"What is it for?" asked the player. 

"It's for the king's birthday party. You are invited to play music," said the messenger. 

The player signed the paper and happily went to the party. The king loved the music and everyone had a great time. The player felt proud and happy to have been a part of the celebration.

Once upon a time, there was a big elephant named Ellie. Ellie had a large bag on her back that she carried everywhere she went. One day, Ellie met a little rabbit named Benny.

Benny asked Ellie, "What's in your bag?"

Ellie replied, "It's a surprise! Do you want to see?"

Benny nodded his head excitedly and Ellie opened her bag. Inside the bag was a big, juicy watermelon. Benny's mouth watered and he asked, "Can I have some?"

Ellie hesitated and said, "I want to share, but I must resist eating it all myself. Maybe we can share it together."

Benny was grateful and they both enjoyed the sweet watermelon. From that day on, Ellie and Benny were the best of friends and shared everything in Ellie's big bag.

Sammy was a little boy who loved to explore the world around him. One night, he found a flashlight in his bedroom and he thought it was so cool that he turned it on and off again. Suddenly, he heard his mom's voice coming from downstairs.

"Sammy, it's time for bed. Please turn off the flashlight," she said. Sammy did as he was asked and the room was very quiet. 

After Sammy was tucked into bed, he heard bells ringing outside the house. He imagined what it would be like if he went out to explore the night. 

His mom heard the bells too and called up to him, "Sammy, stay inside, it's not safe out there. It's too dark and no one is around to help you. It's better to be safe and stay inside. "

Sammy realized that it was better to be safe and follow his mom's advice. He was glad he had been quiet and stayed inside so he wouldn't get into any trouble.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toy cars and trucks. One day, Timmy's mom asked him to help her carry a big box. Timmy was excited to help his mom and he tried to lift the box, but it was too heavy for him.

Timmy's mom saw that he was struggling and she said "Don't worry, Timmy. I will support the box while you help me carry it." Together, they lifted the box and carried it to the car.

On the way to the car, they saw a man who was deaf. Timmy's mom explained to him that the man couldn't hear them because he was deaf. Timmy didn't understand at first, but he knew that they needed to be extra careful around the man.

They safely put the box in the car and Timmy felt proud that he could help his mom. From that day on, Timmy always tried to support his mom whenever she needed help carrying things.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside and explore the world around him. One day, he saw a new boy in the park who he had never met before. Timmy felt nervous to talk to the new boy, but he wanted to be friends with him.

Timmy walked over to the new boy and said, "Hi, my name is Timmy. What's your name?" The new boy replied, "My name is Jack. Nice to meet you." Timmy felt happy that he had introduced himself to Jack.

As they played together, Timmy noticed that Jack had a hole in his boot. Timmy said, "Hey, your boot has a hole in it. Do you want to borrow my boots?" Jack was grateful and thanked Timmy.

The moral of the story is that it's important to introduce yourself to new people and help others when you can.

Jim was a very spoiled little boy. He had everything he wanted and would often throw tantrums when he didn't get his way. His mom thought it was time to teach him a lesson and take him to space.

She asked Jim, "Do you want to go to a special planet? It's a place where you can hang in space with no gravity!" Jim was excited and said, "Yes, please! Let's go!"

Mom and Jim got into a rocket and flew to the planet. When they arrived, Jim was amazed. Everything was floating, so he floated too.

He said, "Mom, this is the best planet ever! Can I hang on the planet forever?"

Mom laughed and said, "It's a fun place to visit, but don't forget your responsibilities here on Earth." Jim understood and smiled.

They spent the day playing games in the zero gravity and when it was time to go home, Jim said, "I'm so lucky to have been spoiled, thank you for the best day ever!" and they flew back to Earth.

Once there was a clever rabbit called Judy. One day Judy saw a big tree. She wanted to cut it down, so she could make a house. But she couldn't find a saw, so she looked around for something else to use.

Suddenly, she saw a little frog called Fred. Judy had an idea. She asked Fred if he could help her to cut down the tree. She smiled and said, â€œCan you make me a saw?â€

Fred thought for a moment. Then he said, â€œYes I can!â€. He clapped his hands and the biggest saw appeared. Judy was very happy and clapped her hands too.

They cut down the tree and Judy was able to make a nice house. Judy was very thankful for Fred's help and thanked him for being so clever.

The moral of this story is that if you are clever and think outside the box, you can achieve your goals.

Once upon a time, there was a happy little girl named Lily. She loved to listen to her mommy read her stories before bed. One night, her mommy was feeling sad and started to frown while reading. This made Lily feel worried and she asked her mommy what was wrong. Her mommy explained that she had a bad day at work, but promised to try and be quiet while reading the rest of the story. Lily felt better knowing her mommy was okay and snuggled up to listen to the rest of the story. They both fell asleep feeling happy and loved. The end.

Once upon a time there was a bright moon in the sky. On one special night, a little girl stepped outside. She looked up and saw the moon. It was so soft and pretty. She wanted to kiss it.

So, the little girl raised her arms and blew a big kiss up to the moon. She was sure that the moon felt it. She thought she even saw the moon smile! 

Then something special happened. A sparkly star shot down from the moon and landed in the little girl's hand. It was the softest thing she had ever felt. She thanked the moon with another kiss and went back inside. 

From that day forward the little girl kept the star close and was sure to blow the moon kisses every night. Whenever she was feeling sad or happy, she would look up and feel that the moon was looking down at her with a big smile.

Once there was a little girl named Kate. She loved walking around her house, especially the living room. There was a big, soft rug in the middle of the room which always made the living room feel peaceful.

One day, while she was playing, Kate asked her mother, "Can I go play on the rug?"

Her mother said, "No, Kate. I'm sorry, but you are not allowed to play on the rug."

Kate whined and begged her mother, "Please, Mama. Can I just play there for a little bit?"

But her mother refused. "No, you cannot play on the rug. It's too dangerous. You can play on the floor instead."

Kate gave her mother a disappointed look and went to play on the floor next to the peaceful rug.

Sam and Mia liked to joke with each other. They were friends who lived near the big river. One day, they found a raft made of wood and rope. It was flexible and could float on the water.

"Let's go on the raft and have fun!" Sam said.

"OK, but be careful. The river is fast and deep," Mia said.

They climbed on the raft and pushed it into the water. They used sticks to paddle and steer. They saw fish and birds and trees. They laughed and joked and sang.

"Look, there is a bridge!" Sam said. "Let's go under it and see what's on the other side."

"OK, but be careful. The bridge is low and dark," Mia said.

They paddled towards the bridge. As they got closer, they heard a loud roar. It was a waterfall. The water was falling down from the bridge and making a lot of noise and bubbles.

"Help! We have to turn back!" Mia said.

"I have a joke for you!" Sam said.

"This is no time for jokes!" Mia said.

"What do you call a raft that goes over a waterfall?" Sam said.

"What?" Mia said.

"A splash!" Sam said.

They both screamed as the raft went over the edge. They got wet and cold and scared. But they also felt a thrill. They held on to the raft and each other. They landed in a calm pool of water. They were safe.

"That was not funny!" Mia said.

"Sorry, I was trying to make you laugh," Sam said.

They looked at each other and smiled. They were still friends. They joked with each other. They had fun. They paddled back to the shore and went home. They told their parents about their adventure. They said they would never go on the raft again. But they knew they would.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was very hungry and wanted to eat her meal. Her mommy made her a sandwich with peanut butter and jelly. Lily took a bite and said, "Yummy!" 

Suddenly, she heard a noise outside. She asked her mommy, "What's that sound?" Her mommy said, "Let's listen." They heard birds chirping and a dog barking. 

After finishing her meal, Lily wanted to play outside. But when she went out, she felt the icy wind blowing. She said, "Brrr, it's cold!" Her mommy said, "Let's go back inside where it's warm." 

Lily cuddled up with her mommy and said, "I'm happy we listened to the sounds outside and had a yummy meal together." Her mommy smiled and said, "Me too, sweetie."

Mia loved holidays. She always felt so excited when she heard her parents talking about the different holidays that were coming. One particular holiday she was always looking forward to was the purple holiday.

On this holiday the whole family would dress up in purple clothes and Mia was so excited to pick out her new purple dress for the special day. Once everyone had gathered, the whole family would go for a walk around the neighborhood.

On the purple holiday, Mia always felt a special kind of feeling. As they walked around she could feel her body starting to tremble. She never knew why, but as long as her mom and dad were with her, it was ok.

Mia looked forward to the purple holiday every year and the special feeling she got while they walked around. It always made her tremble, but she knew that as long as her parents were with her, everything was going to be ok.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Every day, he went outside to play games with all of his friends. 

Tim was always excited to play and always wanted to win, so he tried his best every time. One day, he was playing on the jungle gym, and all his friends were jealous of how good he was. 

A lawyer walked by and said to them, "Why don't you all give Tim a challenge and make him prove that he is the best?"

All of the children agreed, so they made a contest. Whoever could stay on the jungle gym the longest would be crowned the winner. Tim was very happy and took on the challenge. 

He made it to the end, but his friends said he cheated. The lawyer stepped in and said, "you must all prove that he was guilty of cheating before you can declare him the winner".

The friends started arguing, but the lawyer said there was no need. He had seen Tim play the entire time and said he was the clear winner. 

Everyone was happy and celebrated Tim's victory. From that day on, he was nicknamed the 'King of the Jungle Gym' and everyone know not to mess with him.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a toy car that she loved to play with. One day, she met a boy named Max. Max saw Lily's toy car and said, "I want to buy your car." Lily replied, "Okay, I will sell it to you."

Max was so happy to have the car, he started to play with it right away. He pushed the car and watched it go with great speed. Lily said, "Wow, your car is really fast!" Max smiled and said, "Yes, it's my favorite toy now."

After a while, the sun started to go down and it started to get cold outside. Lily said, "It's getting too cold to play outside. Let's go inside and warm up." Max agreed and they went inside to drink some hot chocolate. They talked about their favorite toys and had a great time together. From that day on, Lily and Max became good friends.

Once upon a time there was a little boy called Tom. Tom was only three years old. One day, Tom decided he wanted to go out for a walk. When Tom arrived outside, it was very windy. The trees were swaying in the wind and the water of the lake was making big, ugly waves. 

Tom was fascinated by the waves. He wanted to touch them. He asked his mom if he could go closer to the lake. She said yes, but to be careful. 

Tom carefully walked closer to the water. He could see the waves slapping over a large sack on the shore. Tom was excited and he ran closer to the sack. He reached his tiny hands out, and tried to open the sack. Suddenly, the sack started to move! 

Tom jumped back in surprise. He called out to mom, "Mom! The sack is moving!" and mom ran closer. 

Mom opened the sack and a dog popped out! Tom laughed with excitement and pet the dog. Then, he realized it was his neighborâ€™s dog. The dog jumped around, happy to be freed from the ugly sack! 

Tom gave the dog a big hug, and then took it back home to his neighbor. 

The End.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She was very excited because she was going to a special party. To get ready for the party, she put on her favorite pants. 

The pants were red and she loved them. Then, the little girl wanted to look extra special for the party. So her mommy showed her how to fold the pants. 

The little girl was so excited that she could make her pants look even better. She folded the pants in all sorts of ways. Then, she put them back on and looked in the mirror. 

She was so happy that she had learned how to fold her pants. She thought it looked so nice that she decided to wear her folded pants to the party. Everyone at the party thought she was amazing and they clapped and cheered.

The little girl was so excited that she skipped around and danced all night. She was so proud of her folded pants and never forgot the magical moment.

Once there was a sad little seed. It was so lonely and wanted to grow, but no one wanted to help it. Then one day, a kindly farmer saw the seed. He filled a pot with soil and placed the seed inside. Then he gave it food and water, and it started to grow bigger and bigger. 

The seed blossomed and soon it was covered in big, beautiful petals. It was so happy to have a family of its own. Every day, the farmer would come and visit. He would fill the pot with new soil and water the flower. 

The flower grew bigger and stronger, and the farmer was so proud. He always was there to check it was happy and healthy. The flower was so glad to have someone to take care of it. Soon its sadness was gone, and it was glowing with joy.

Once upon a time there was a naughty little girl. She loved to play and she loved to talk. But one day she had to go to a long lecture with her mom. It was very boring.

The little girl said to her mom, "Mom, why do we have to listen to this long lecture?" Her mom replied, "It's important, honey. We need to know this information."

But the little girl did not want to listen anymore. She thought the lecture was very boring. So she decided to act naughty. She started to talk loudly and to make funny faces.

Finally, her mom spoke up. She asked her daughter, "Why are you being so naughty?" The little girl was surprised. "Why can't I talk and be happy?" she asked. Her mom just smiled and said, "Because the lecture is important, sweetie."

So the little girl and her mom finished the lecture. And the naughty little girl learned an important lesson: Be kind and patient when listening to a lecture.

Once upon a time, there was a charming boy. He was three years old and he loved to collect things! Every day, he would play with his favourite toy and after, he would look for special things to collect.

One day, the boy decided to go for a walk. He saw a pie shop which looked very inviting. He went inside and saw lots of lovely pies in the window. He was so excited!

The boy asked the man in the shop if he could collect one of the pies. The man smiled and said yes. He chose a delicious looking strawberry pie and put it in his basket. He thanked the man and ran off home.

When he got home, he shared the pie with his family. It was the most delicious pie they had ever tasted! They thanked the boy for collecting the charming pie. From then on, the boy collected the most delicious pies and shared them with his family!

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a humble teacher. She had a big blackboard in her class. Every day, she would carry the blackboard to the big tree in the park. She taught kids under the tree.

One sunny day, a little boy named Tim came to the park. He saw the teacher and her blackboard. He was curious and asked, "What are you doing with the blackboard?"

The humble teacher smiled and said, "I teach kids here. Would you like to learn with us?" Tim was happy and said, "Yes, please!" So, he sat down with the other kids under the tree.

Every day, Tim and the other kids learned new things from the humble teacher. They loved to carry the blackboard, and they loved to learn. They all became good friends and had lots of fun together. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was an old man. He was elderly and his bones ached in pain. The old man was sad. He needed money to buy food.

So the old man decided to sell something. He went to the town square with a basket of apples. There were many people in the town square, but nobody wanted to buy the old man's apples.

Then a little boy arrived. He was only three years old and he was very excited about the apples. He asked his mum if he could buy some. His mum said yes and reached for her purse.

The old man was so happy that the little boy wanted to buy his apples. He smiled at the boy and gave him two extra apples for free. The little boy thanked the old man and ran off to show his mum his new snacks.

The old man was relieved. He had enough money now to buy food and his pain was gone. He was happy that he had been able to sell something and make a little boy smile.

Nina was lying in the grass when she heard a noise. She looked up, and saw a little red bug. She looked closer and saw it had six legs. As it crawled on the grass, she reached out to touch it. 

"Hi Bug," she said.

The bug stopped and looked at her with its buggy eyes. Nina smiled.

Then something funny happened. The bug flexed its little red muscle and jumped into the air. 

"Wow!" said Nina. 

The bug landed and scurried away. Nina watched it until it was out of sight. 

She sat and thought about the little red bug and its funny muscle. She reached out to touch the grass and smiled, remembering how the bug had jumped so high.

There was a girl named Alicia. She loved to write. Every day she would find a quiet spot and write. One day Alicia was walking in the park when she saw something great. There were many blueberries. Alicia smiled and ran over. She started picking some of the blueberries and put them in her pocket to take home.

When she got home, Alicia put the blueberries in a bowl and got some paper and a pencil. She started to write. She wrote about the great blueberries she had found and how much fun it was picking them. It took her a while to write, but the final results were worth it.

Alicia smiled while she looked at her writing. She was proud of the great story she had written. She finished eating her blueberries and knew that she would cherish her writing forever.

Sara and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toys. Sara likes to play with dolls and Ben likes to play with cars. One day, they find a big ball of yarn in their grandma's closet.

"Look, Sara, yarn!" Ben says. "We can make things with it!"

"Yes, Ben, yarn!" Sara says. "But what can we make?"

They think hard. Sara has an idea. She takes some yarn and wraps it around a doll. She makes a dress for the doll.

"See, Ben, I made a dress!" Sara says. "Do you like it?"

Ben nods. He has an idea too. He takes some yarn and ties it to a car. He makes a trailer for the car.

"See, Sara, I made a trailer!" Ben says. "Do you like it?"

Sara nods. They are happy with their creations. They show them to their grandma.

"Wow, Sara and Ben, you are very creative!" Grandma says. "You made good things with the yarn!"

"Thank you, Grandma!" Sara and Ben say. "We value the yarn. It is fun to play with!"

Grandma smiles. She hugs them and gives them a cookie. She is proud of them. She values them. They are good children.

Once there was a boy who was very lonely. Every day he wanted to have a friend, but he did not have one. 
One day the boy went to his favourite place - the beach. He saw all the people playing together and smiled. But, he was still alone.

Then he saw something very surprising under the sand. He bent down, and saw a baby crab! He gasped because he was so excited.

The baby crab was very small and needed a friend. The boy was so happy to find him, and picked him up.

The two of them were now friends and they played together on the beach. The boy was no longer lonely and he was very happy.

Once upon a time, there was a friendly girl. She wanted to go surfing. But she didn't have any surf, so she was sad.

Then, her mom saw her sad face and told her they could go shopping. They went to the store and found the perfect surf, and the best part was that it was cheap!

The girl was so excited, she dropped to her knees. She thanked her mom with hugs and kisses, and off they went to the beach.

The girl had so much fun surfing that day, and she even rode the biggest wave ever! She was so happy and thanked her mom again for the cheap and perfect surf. They lived happily ever after.

Once there was a bunny who was very restless. He wanted to visit new places! Every day, he hopped and hopped until he found a special place.

The bunny saw a big bush that was full of beautiful berries. He hopped up to the bush and began to eat the berries. They were very sweet and juicy! 

He ate and ate until the bush was empty. As he hopped away, he felt so full and content. He thought that visiting the bush with the berries was very nice. 

So every day he would come back to visit the bush and pick the berries. In his restless way, he explored and he ate and he had so much fun!

Once there was a little boy named Joe. He wanted a crown to wear on his head. Everyday, he looked in the sky and pointed to the silver crown in the clouds.

One day, Joe decided to reach out to get his dream crown. He climbed up a tall tree and leaned his arm out toward the sky. But it was too high, and he could not reach it. Joe was sad and cold as he came down.

Then he had an idea! He used a ladder to stand on, and was finally able to lean far enough to reach his prize. He proudly put the crown on his head and smiled.

Joe realised that he can be successful if he puts in some hard work. So from then on, he worked hard and never gave up. Joe knew that if he keeps trying, he will one day get his crown.

Lisa and her dad were at the store. Dad wanted to buy a birthday present for Lisa. He looked around and saw a really pretty doll. "Let's weigh it," he said to Lisa. 

He placed the doll on the store's scales. They both saw the number 10 appear. Dad sighed. "That's too expensive!" 

But then Lisa had an idea. "Let's go to the opera!" she said. They went to the opera and bought two tickets. The tickets were not expensive at all. 

When Dad and Lisa came back, he put the tickets on the scales. The number 3 appeared this time. "Perfect," said Dad with a smile. They bought the tickets and the doll. 

"Happy Birthday, Lisa!" Dad said, giving her the doll and the tickets. Lisa was so happy. Dad had found the perfect present!

Once upon a time there was a white tray. It was big and fuzzy but very soft. It sat on the kitchen counter waiting.

Suddenly, something appeared. It was a tiny mouse. It was small and cute and it hopped onto the tray. It didn't take long before the mouse found a big piece of cheese.

The mouse happily gobbled up the cheese and started to look around the tray. The tray was filled with different foods. There were treats, fruits and vegetables. The mouse hopped around the tray and tried everything.

When the mouse finished, it didn't seem to want to leave. So he sat on the tray and enjoyed the view. He stayed all day until he finally went away.

The white tray was left all alone, until something else appeared. A big orange cat hopped onto the tray, and started to eat the food. But that's another story for another day.

One day, Mommy took Sammy to the store. Sammy saw all the colorful zip-up clothes and wanted one. He asked Mommy, "Can I have one?" Mommy said, "We need to decide."

A few minutes later, they found the perfect colorful zip-up sweater. Sammy was very happy and said, "I love this one!" 

Mommy smiled and said, "I'm glad you like it. Do you want to decide to buy it?" Sammy nodded his head and said, "Yes!" 

So, Mommy and Sammy went to the checkout and bought the colorful zip-up sweater. Sammy felt very excited and couldn't wait to wear it. He knew he had made a good decision!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Emma. She loved helping people and was very compassionate. She was looking for something to do each day that could make someone happy, so she started to be very careful with what she valued.

One day, Emma went on a walk and saw a glass on the ground. She knew she had to help, so she carefully picked it up and put it back in its place. She felt happy that someone else wouldn't have to worry about it being broken.

From then on, Emma always valued glass and things around her, and she was delighted to help others too. She always took care to be careful and compassionate to make sure that everything was kept safe. This made her and others feel very happy.

The End.

Once upon a time, there lived a little boy. He had an enormous room in his house, but he wasn't sure what he should do with it. He thought and thought until he had an idea! He decided to make his own scale in his enormous room! 

Every day, the little boy would weigh toys in the room. His mom would help him measure the toy's weights. He'd place a toy on one side and then place weights on the other side until it weighed the same. He was having lots of fun weighing all his toys. 

Once he was finished, he decided to take his scale outside to show all his friends. He wanted to see who had the lightest toy and who had the heaviest toy! Everyone had so much fun weighing their toys with the little boy's homemade scale. 

The little boy learned that day that the weighing can be fun. That he didn't need complicated math to weigh objects. All he needed was a little imagination, some weights, and an enormous room to do it in!

Timmy had a big problem. He wanted to go on the swings, but he wasn't tall enough. He tried to stand up and reach the swing, but it was no use. Timmy's mom saw him and said, "What's the matter, Timmy?"

Timmy said, "I can't get on the swing, yet."

"Well," said his mom, "let's try something else. What if I give you a boost?"

Timmy nodded and his mom boosted him up. He was so excited to be on the swing, something he had never done before!

But then something strange happened. Timmy started to swing higher and higher, until he was up in the air!

Timmy's mom gasped, "Timmy! I had no idea you could fly! I don't know how to get you down!"

Timmy just laughed and smiled. He tried to figure out how to come down, but it was an unknown thing to him. Suddenly, he felt a blast of wind and he was back on the ground.

This time, Timmy was tall enough to reach the swing all by himself! His mom laughed and said, "I think you'll be able to get on the swings from now on!" 

Timmy smiled and said, "That was fun! I want to try it again!"

Molly was a 3 year old girl who loved to fly. One sunny day she was in the garden with her dad and she spotted a jet flying in the sky.

Molly: "Daddy, can I fly in a jet?"

Dad: "Of course, Molly. But first you have to be calm and listen to me."

Molly took a deep breath and tried her very best to be calm. The dad had something important to tell her.

Dad: "Molly, when you fly in a jet, you must always follow the pilot's commands. If a pilot demands you to do something, you must do it right away, OK?"

Molly nodded her head. She was very excited to finally fly in a jet!

Soon, Molly and her dad were inside the jet and the pilot was taking them on an amazing journey. Everyone was calm and the flight was smooth. Molly smiled, she was enjoying the view from the sky. This was the best trip ever!

Mum and Sam were walking in the park together on a nice, calm day. As they strolled, Sam noticed a university in the distance.

"Mummy, what is that?" he asked.

"That is a university. People go there to learn," explained Mum.

Sam was intrigued. "Can I go?"

"No, sweetheart. Not yet. You have to be older," said Mum.

Sam was disappointed and started to cry.

"Let's bury your sadness. We can dig a hole and bury it like a seed," said Mum.

So Mum and Sam found a spot in the park and started to dig. When they had finished, Sam felt much calmer and was very proud of the job he had done.

They covered the hole with soil and marked it with a stone so that someone could find it again one day. 

Mum smiled, "Now your sadness is buried."

Mia and Ben liked to play in the garden. They had a well that was very old and deep. Sometimes they imagined that there were magic things in the well, like fairies or dragons or stars.

One day, they decided to drop a stone in the well and listen for the splash. Mia went first. She picked a small stone and threw it in the well. She put her ear to the edge and waited. She was patient. She heard a splash after a long time.

"Wow, that was far!" she said.

Ben wanted to try too. He picked a big stone and threw it in the well. He put his ear to the edge and waited. He was not patient. He did not hear a splash.

"Where is the splash?" he asked.

"Maybe your stone was too big," Mia said. "Maybe it got stuck."

Ben was not happy. He wanted to hear a splash. He imagined that his stone had landed on a dragon's head and made it angry.

"Maybe the dragon will come out and roar at us," he said.

Mia was scared. She did not like dragons. She imagined that the dragon had fire in its mouth and wings on its back.

"Maybe we should run away," she said.

They ran away from the well and hid behind a tree. They waited for the dragon to come out. They were very quiet. They did not hear a roar. They did not see a fire. They did not see a wing.

"Maybe there is no dragon," Ben said.

"Maybe it was just a stone," Mia said.

They looked at each other and laughed. They were silly. They went back to the well and played some more. They imagined other things in the well, like fairies or stars. They had fun.

Once upon a time there was a match. It was a very special match. Everyone wanted to watch the match. The match was scary but everyone wanted to support it.

So the match started and everyone was very excited. They held up signs and cheered for the match. But then something happened. The match started to get scary! Everyone was scared.

But then something amazing happened. All of the people in the crowd started to support the match. They cheered and clapped. They showed everyone their match was not scary.

At the end of the match, everyone was happy. They had all supported the match and it was a success! Everyone was proud and happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Cindy who lived in a big house. On a special day, she decided to explore the house and went upstairs. When she got there, she was surprised to see a party with all her friends! She was so excited, she didn't know what to do.

Everyone was laughing and playing and she couldn't stop smiling. Then she noticed her mom and dad walking in with big birthday presents. Cindy was so confused! She had no idea there was going to be a surprise party for her.

All the guests sang the happy birthday and ate some cake. Cindy was so happy, she laughed and danced with all her friends. The surprise party for Cindy was the best day ever!

There was a fearful mouse who lived in the kitchen. One day, the mouse saw a spoon in the cupboard. It was shiny and looked yummy. So, the mouse decided to crawl over to the spoon to sneak a snack.

Suddenly, the mouse heard a loud noise in the kitchen. It was so scary! The mouse was so fearful that it forgot about the spoon and hid under the counter. 

Next, the mouse decided to peek out from its hiding spot. When it did, the mouse saw the spoon still there and the noise was gone. So, the mouse bravely crawled out from the counter and scurried to the spoon. It ate the remains of the snack and felt happy. 

The mouse learned a valuable lesson - never be too fearful!

The day was sunny. Tom and his mom went to the market. He saw a peach and asked his mom, "Can I get it, please?" She said, "Yes, it looks yummy!"

Tom grabbed the peach and wanted to eat it right away. He put the peach in his pocket and ran outside to the backyard. He pulled out the peach and took one big bite. It was so juicy and yummy! As he was about to take another bite, he heard a snap. He looked up and saw a bird had taken the rest of the peach from his hand!

Tom was so shocked that he forgot about the snap he heard. But he remembered later. He had learned a lesson to never leave a yummy peach unattended!

The little girl was so excited as she entered the room. She looked around and saw the printer. It was shiny and slick and looked brilliant! She took a piece of paper and placed it in the printer. Then she pressed the big red button. The printer started printing! The little girl was so happy, her mouth opened wide in amazement.

She watched eagerly as the paper slowly came out. There were shapes and colours. They were all so brilliant! She started to laugh and clap. She had never seen anything so wonderful. She took the paper out of the printer and looked at it closely. It was a picture of a big yellow duck!

The little girl was so proud of her picture. She ran to show her mom. Her mom was just as impressed as the little girl. Together they both looked at the picture and smiled. The little girl was so proud of herself. She had printed something all by herself!

Once upon a time there was a little blue kangaroo. She was the happiest kangaroo in the world and she wore a pink bow in her hair.

"Hello, Spot!" said the owner.

"Woof woof!" barked Spot.

The owner saw how dirty Spot's fur was and said, "Come on, Spot! Let's go home and give you a bath."

Spot followed his owner home. When they got there, the owner gave Spot a warm bath and dried him off. Spot was very happy to be clean again.

"Thank you, owner!" said Spot.

"You're welcome, Spot," said the owner. "Now you're a clean and happy dog!"

Once upon a time, there was a generous vendor who had lots of interesting things for sale. Every day, he would wrap up his parcels with lots of care and attention, making sure that each one was securely packaged.

One day, a little three-year-old girl came to the vendor's stall, drawn in by its bright colours and interesting shapes. She had been saving up all her pocket money for this exciting adventure.

The vendor smiled kindly at her.

"Welcome," said the vendor. "What can I help you with today?"

The little girl looked around, wide-eyed with excitement. She pointed to a box full of shiny objects.

"Can I have that?" she asked.

The vendor smiled again.

"Of course. I have something special for you. Let me wrap it up for you."

The vendor carefully wrapped up the parcel, making sure it was extra secure. He then handed it to the little girl with a big smile.

"Thank you," said the little girl. "You're so generous!"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. She was only three years old and loved exploring her house. One day, she was looking for something interesting to find. She looked under the bed, in her closets and in the drawers.

Finally, Lucy went to the kitchen and opened up a big drawer. Inside she found an old apron. She was so excited and put it on right away.

â€œMama! Mama! Look what I found!â€ Lucy shouted.

Mama came in and said, â€œOh my! Thatâ€™s my very old apron! Where did you find it?â€
