The nervous friend smiled, feeling proud and happy. Both of them were glad they filled up their pencil case!

Tom and Mia are friends. They like to play with paint. They have many colors of paint. They can make red, blue, yellow, green, purple, and orange. They can paint pictures of animals, flowers, cars, and houses.

One day, they find a new color of paint. It is brown. They are curious. They do not know what to paint with brown. They discuss with each other.

"Maybe we can paint a tree," Tom says. "Trees are brown."

"But trees have green leaves too," Mia says. "We need green paint for the leaves."

"Maybe we can paint a bear," Mia says. "Bears are brown."

"But bears have black eyes and nose too," Tom says. "We need black paint for the eyes and nose."

They think hard. They look around. They see a big box. The box is brown. They have an idea.

"Maybe we can paint the box," they say together. "The box is brown. We can paint it with brown paint. We can make it look like a house. We can paint a door, a window, and a roof. We can play inside the box."

They are happy. They get the brown paint. They paint the box. They make a house. They play inside the house. They have fun with paint.

Tom and Lily were playing in the park with their ball. They liked to kick the ball to each other and run after it. Sometimes they missed the ball and it rolled away. They had to be careful not to go near the road, because there were many cars and buses that went very fast.

One day, they saw a big red car with a loud siren and a flashing light. It was an ambulance. It was going to help someone who was hurt. Tom and Lily stopped playing and watched the ambulance speed by. They wondered who was in the ambulance and what happened to them.

"Wow, that was fast!" Tom said.

"Yes, it was. The ambulance has to go fast to get to the hospital," Lily said.

"Why does it have a siren and a light?" Tom asked.

"So the other cars can see it and let it pass. The ambulance is more important than the other cars," Lily explained.

Tom nodded. He thought the ambulance was cool. He wished he could ride in one someday.

The next day, Tom and Lily were playing in the park again. They kicked the ball to each other and ran after it. But this time, Tom was not careful. He did not see the road. He chased the ball too far and ran into the street. A car was coming. It was going very fast. It could not stop in time.

Lily saw what happened. She screamed. She ran to Tom. He was lying on the ground. He was not moving. He was bleeding. Lily was scared. She cried. She did not know what to do.

She heard a siren and saw a light. It was an ambulance. It was coming to the park. It was coming to help Tom. Lily hoped it was not too late. She hoped Tom would be okay.

The ambulance stopped near Tom. Two people got out. They were wearing white clothes. They had a bag and a stretcher. They ran to Tom. They checked his pulse and his breathing. They put a bandage on his wound. They lifted him onto the stretcher. They put him in the ambulance.

One of them came to Lily. He knelt down and smiled. He said, "Don't worry, little girl. We're going to take your friend to the hospital. He's going to be fine. He's very brave. You're very brave too. Do you want to come with us?"

Lily nodded. She wanted to be with Tom. She wanted to see him get better. She got in the ambulance. The other person got in too. He closed the door. He turned on the siren and the light. The ambulance started to move. It went very fast. It went faster than the other cars. It went faster than the day before. It went faster than Lily had ever seen. It went faster than Tom had ever dreamed.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Clarabelle. She was only 3 years old. One day her parents took her to a colorful stadium. Clarabelle was so excited to explore the wide space and see what activities she could do. 

As Clarabelle was walking around the stadium she saw a group of kids playing a game. She got closer to see what they were doing and one of the kids noticed her and invited her to join them. The other kids all said hello and began to explain the game to her.

"It's called 'Guess Who' and the goal is to guess which character someone is thinking about," the girl said. Clarabelle was eager to join in. She thought for a bit, wondering who she should choose. 

Suddenly, it came to her. Clarabelle smiled and said, "I'm going to choose you, my new friend!" All the kids smiled in surprise. 

From that day on, Clarabelle learned the valuable lesson that it is always nice to share and be kind.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She had a snack in her hand that she wanted to eat. But when she tried to open it, she struggled. She pulled and pushed, but it wouldnâ€™t open. She started to feel hurt, so she started to cry.

Jane saw an exciting thing. It was a purple newspaper! She had never seen one before and wondered what was in it. Jane wanted to look, so she grabbed the newspaper and opened it. Inside, she saw funny pictures and lots of words. It all looked very interesting.

Once upon a time there lived a little girl named Daisy. Daisy was three years old and loved wearing her new red coat! Everywhere she went she put her coat on and it kept her warm.

One day she was wearing her coat and decided to visit her grandmother's house. As Daisy approached the door of the house she could smell something delicious cooking. It smelled so good that it made her tummy rumble!

Daisy knocked on the door and before her grandmother opened it she called out.

"Who is it?"

"It's me, Daisy!" Daisy answered.

Her grandmother opened the door and Daisy could see that she was wearing an apron over her coat. "Oh, hello Daisy!" her grandmother said with a big smile. "I'm so glad you're here, come inside and have a taste of the delicious food I'm making!"

Daisy stepped inside and couldn't help but smile as she enjoyed the delicious smells! She couldn't wait to try her grandmother's cooking!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play and have fun, but sometimes she would forget to be kind to others. One day, Lily went to an island with her family. She felt lucky to be there and wanted to explore everything.

As she walked around the island, she saw a group of animals playing together. She wanted to join in, but they didn't let her because she had been mean to them before. Lily felt sad and realized that she had not been a good friend.

Feeling sorry, Lily went back to the animals and apologized. They forgave her and let her play with them. They had so much fun together that they started to clap and cheer. Lily learned that being kind is important, and that friends are always there for each other.

Once there was a small bear named Brownie. He lived in a lake full of ice and snow. He loved it there, but he also wanted to explore the world. 

One day, Brownie decided to try something new. He grabbed his ice cubes and started to melt them. When the ice melted, he became very excited. 

He said, "Oh, I can make a poem out of the melted ice!" He quickly formed some words in his mind and wrote them on the ice.

"This is my poem," he said to himself. He was so proud of his work, but it melted quickly. 

Brownie was sad, but then he got an idea. He said, "I can make a new poem every day!" From then on, Brownie wrote a different poem every day. He was very happy with his small creation.

Mum and Dad had a big plan. They wanted to explore new places so they packed their bags and went to the airport. Dad grabbed their passports and checked them in. The tickets were ready and they boarded their flight.

The journey was long and the air was bitter. Mum and Dad sat next to each other and closed their eyes. After a few hours they landed at their new destination.

They wanted to experience the new place and get to know the culture so they got a map and planned their tour. Everywhere they looked they found exciting things.

They spent the next few days getting around the city, tasting new foods and taking pictures to remember their special trip. Eventually it was time to go and their passports were ready.

Mum and Dad thanked the city and flew back home. They were happy they had planned their adventure and shared great memories together.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy liked to play outside with his friends. They would run and jump and play games. Timmy's mommy told him that it was important to exercise and move his body to be healthy.

One day, Timmy's friend Billy got a new toy. Timmy was jealous because he wanted a toy like that too. But then he remembered what his mommy said about being happy for others instead of feeling jealous. Timmy knew it was important to be kind and share with his friends.

So, Timmy and his friends played together and had fun. They did some exercises too, like jumping jacks and stretching. Timmy felt happy and healthy, and he knew that being a good friend was more important than having a new toy.

The little girl was very excited. She was going to hug her new pet.

The pet was a fish and it was purple. It had a big orange fin and was very competitive.

The little girl had an oxygen tank. She placed it in her tank so that her fish always had enough oxygen.

The little girl carefully picked the fish up and gave it a big hug. She was so happy to have a friend.

The fish looked very happy too. It swam around in its tank and made friends with its new owner.

The girl and her fish became fast friends. They hugged every day and never stopped enjoying each other's company. It was the perfect competitive friendship!

Once there was an elderly man walking down the hall. He walked very slowly, one step at a time. As he walked, he noticed something strange. Out of the corner of his eye he saw something appear. He stopped and looked closely. It was a magical creature!

The creature was very small and had wings. He was surprised to see it and wondered what it wanted. The creature flew around the hall, fluttering and flapping its wings. The man watched it curiously. After a few minutes, the creature flew away.

The man continued walking down the hall and soon forgot about the strange creature. But he felt like something special had just happened. Maybe it was because the creature had appeared. Maybe it was a sign of something special in the future.

Once upon a time, there was a playful puppy. His name was Max. Every day, he chased around the garden and barked at the birds. One day, he found a bone in the grass. He was so excited!

Max picked up the bone with his teeth and started to carry it around. Suddenly, he heard a loud noise in the bushes! He was scared and started to run. But the bone was too heavy, and he couldn't run fast.

The noise came closer. It was a cat! Max was scared, but the cat was very playful. It started to run around Max, swatting playfully at the bone. Then, it gave the bone a big strike with its paw!

Once upon a time there were two friends, Mary and Bob. Mary and Bob loved playing together and were always supporting each other. 

One day, Mary asked Bob if he wanted to go for a drive in Mary's car. Bob agreed and so Mary applie for a license and was given one.

From that moment on, Bob and Mary stuck together, supporting each other and never letting the other give up, no matter the risks. For if a friendship is dead, so are hearts.

Once there was a family of birds. They were looking for a new home and flew over a big field. Then, they spotted a chimney! The birds flew closer and saw that the chimney was empty.

Once upon a time, there lived a little girl named Lilly. Lilly was very scared one day because she saw a big dark cloud in the sky.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and her favorite toy was a teddy bear named Brownie. One day, Lily went to her room to play with Brownie but she couldn't find him. She looked everywhere but he was nowhere to be found.

Once upon a time, Amy and her mommy went to the mall. Amy was very excited because she had some new shoes. When they got to the mall, Amy and her mommy saw many other mommies and kids.

Once upon a time, there was a little rock. The rock was very good and always had a big smile on its face. It lived in a pretty garden with many flowers and trees.

Once there was a little girl named Sunny. She was only three years old and loved exploring nature.

Anna likes to do yoga with her mom. Yoga is when you make shapes with your body and breathe slowly. Anna thinks yoga is fun and good for her. She likes to copy her mom and stretch her arms and legs.

Jane learned that it was important not to touch things without asking first. She would never forget her mistake and she never wanted to feel that uncomfortable again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to jog in the wild forest near her house. One day, she met a rabbit who was sad. "Why are you sad?" asked Lily. "I want to study, but I don't know how," replied the rabbit. 

Lily had an idea. "I can teach you how to study! It's easy," she said. So, every day after their jog, Lily would teach the rabbit how to study. They would read books and practice writing. 

Soon, the rabbit was very smart and happy. "Thank you, Lily! You taught me how to study and now I'm smart," said the rabbit. Lily smiled and replied, "You're welcome! Remember, studying is important and can make you happy." 

From that day on, Lily and the rabbit would jog and study together in the wild forest, always learning and growing smarter. The moral of the story is that studying is important and can bring happiness.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sarah. She was an independent, brave three year-old.

One day, Sarah woke up, ready to watch her favorite film. She walked over to the TV, but it was not working. She looked around the room and saw that the cable was not plugged in. Sarah was very frustrated and could not figure out how to plug it in.

Just then, Sarah heard a voice. It was her Dad. "What's wrong my brave girl?" he asked her. Sarah told him that she wanted to watch her favorite film, but she couldn't plug in the cable.

"Do you want me to help you?" Dad asked. He bent down to Sarah's level and explained how to plug in the cable.

Together, the two of them got the cable plugged in, and Sarah's favorite film was on. She was so happy to be independent and be able to do it all herself with Dad's help. She happily watched her film and Dad smiled, proud of his brave little girl.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Lily. She was so excited because today was a special day - it was her birthday. Lily was so happy that she began to bow to show her appreciation for the special day.

At the same time, her grandfather was looking out of the window, watching the festivities and smiling. He had a very special memory of his own birthday - it was a memory that made him smile, but also made him feel a little weird. 

As Lily skipped around outside, her grandfather came to the window and called her over. She came up to the window, and he put his hand lovingly on her head.

Grandfather: "Lily, do you know how special today is?"

Lily: "Yes, it is my birthday!"

Grandfather: "That's right! Today, you have a special memory that will last forever. Don't ever forget it." 

Lily smiled and gave her grandfather a big hug before going back outside to enjoy the rest of her birthday party. From that day on, she would always remember what her grandfather said. She cherished the memory of her birthday, and the weird feeling she felt when her grandfather told her about it.

Once there was a dry pie. Princess Jane wanted to take a picture of it. She asked her friend, Tommy. Tommy said, "Sure!" The two of them went to Tommy's house.

When they got there, Tommy pulled out a big, black machine. Princess Jane said, "What is that?" Tommy laughed and said, "It's a printer. It takes a picture and prints it out." 

Princess Jane was very excited. She smiled and said, "Let's print the pie!" Tommy put the picture in the printer and pressed a few buttons. After a few moments, the printer spat out a picture of the dry pie. Princess Jane clapped her hands and said, "Yay! That looks great!" 

They both held up the picture and smiled. Then, they enjoyed eating the dry pie. It was delicious!

Once upon a time, there was an envious little pig called Tibbs. Tibbs looked hungrily at a pot of delicious soup that his friend, Spot, was happily eating. He leaned over and asked Spot: "What's that?"

Spot smiled and said: "It's amazing soup! I just made it myself."

Tibbs was even more envious now - he wished he could have some of that soup too. He leaned closer and said: "Can I have some?"

Spot frowned and said: "No - this is all mine. Find your own soup."

Tibbs was very sad now. He wished he could have some of Spot's soup, but he knew it was no use. He sadly walked away, still feeling envious of Spot and his delicious soup.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Jack. Jack was a happy and active child who loved to play around wherever he went.

Today, Jack was feeling very tired so he decided to take a nap. He found a big tree and he decided to take a stand underneath it. He snuggled up to the trunk and closed his eyes.

As Jack was sleeping, he felt something touch his arm. He opened his eyes and saw a butterfly looking at him. "Hello," said Jack, rubbing the sleep from his eyes.

The butterfly said nothing and continued to touch Jack's arm. It felt so soft that Jack smiled and nodded his head in agreement. 

The butterfly flew away and Jack slowly got up and stretched his legs. He felt much better and much less tired. 

Jack smiled and said thank you to the butterfly before he went off to play.

Once upon a time, there was a chubby bunny. She was so chubby she couldn't wear regular socks. So she found some chubby socks and put them on.

"I wonder where I can find more chubby socks?" the bunny asked her friend.

Her friend smiled. "Let's examine all of these socks," he said, pointing to a pile of socks.

The bunnies sifted through the pile of socks and found a few more chubby socks.

"Yes!" the bunny said, hopping up and down. "Now I have enough chubby socks!"

The bunny grabbed all of her chubby socks and hopped away, happy and content. The end!

Lisa and Billy were playing in the backyard one day. Billy was sad and he started to complain.

Lisa said, "What's wrong, Billy?".

Billy said, "I want a pet, but my dad says we can't have one".

Lisa said, "That's too bad". She then had an incredible idea. She said, "We can find a bird in a cage".

Billy said, "Where can we find one?".

Lisa said, "Let's go to the park. I bet some people are selling birds there".

So the two of them went to the park, and sure enough there were people selling bird cages. Billy was so excited and he picked out the biggest one. It had an incredible songbird inside.

Billy was happy and he no longer had to complain. He had a pet of his very own.

Once upon a time there was a blue lawyer who printed documents all day. He was very good at his job and his bosses were very proud of him.

One day, the blue lawyer thought he should print something he had never printed before. He decided to print a special wish of his own. He wrote a wish and put it in the printer but nothing happened. He was very frustrated and thought it was impossible to make his wish come true. 

He went back to his desk and moaned and groaned. His bosses heard him and asked him what was wrong. He told them what he did, so they said it was impossible to make his wish come true on his own. He needed help from his friends and family.

The blue lawyer was so grateful and said he would never print a wish without them. He later realised that teamwork was the key to making his dreams come true.

The moral of the story is that the power of teamwork can help us achieve our goals in life. No one can make their wishes come true on their own.

Once upon a time there was an ant. He wanted to find something to keep. He looked around and saw a shiny rock. He was very excited and took it back home. The ant worked hard to keep it safe. He put it in a box and kept it near him all the time. 

One day, the ant was taking a walk, when he heard a noise. He looked around and saw a dog. The dog was ready to chase the ant. The ant was so scared and thought quickly. He knew he could not take the rock with him, so he hid it in the ground and kept running. 

Luckily, the ant managed to escape. He was so relieved and happy. He ran back home and found his rock still in the ground. He was ready to keep it again. From that day on, the ant kept the rock close by, so he would never lose it again.

Once upon a time, there was a girl called Lila. She had a very special toy car, but it was not a good fit for the tracks in her room.

She wanted to make it fit, so she thought and thought about how to do it. Then she had a bright idea.

Lila took her toy car and leaned it against the wall. She put her hands on the car and pushed her weight against it.

With the car leaning against the wall, the tracks fit! With a big smile on her face, Lila drove her toy car along the tracks, around and around her room.

Lila was very happy, she had used her will to make her toy car fit!

Once upon a time there was a little girl, she was three years old. She had an orange rake and she would play with it everyday. One day, when she was playing, she made a mess in the garden. Her mum saw it and she got very mad. 

Mum said to her, â€œYou made a big mess, you need to pay with a punishment.â€ 

The little girl looked scared and said, â€œIâ€™m sorry, please donâ€™t punish me.â€ 

Mum said, â€œDonâ€™t worry, if you tidy up the garden with your orange rake, I wonâ€™t punish you.â€ 

So the little girl went to work with her orange rake and tidied up the garden. When she finished, she was very proud of her work. 

Mum smiled and said, â€œWell done! This garden looks beautiful. You donâ€™t have to be punished.â€ 

The little girl was so happy and she hugged her mum. From that day on, she was always careful not to make a mess.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play with flags. They have many flags of different colors and shapes. They like to wave them and pretend they are in a parade.

One day, they go to the park with their flags. They see a big hill. They want to climb the hill and put their flags on top. They think it will be fun.

They start to climb the hill. It is hard. They get tired. They stop to rest. They look at their flags. They have to choose one flag to put on the hill. They cannot carry all of them.

Anna says, "I want to choose the red flag. It is bright and pretty. It will look good on the hill."

Ben says, "I want to choose the blue flag. It is thin and light. It will wave in the wind."

They do not agree. They start to argue. They say, "My flag is better. Your flag is worse."

They get angry. They do not want to share. They do not want to play together.

They sit on the hill. They hold their flags. They are sad. They miss their friend.

They look at each other. They see their friend is sad too. They feel sorry. They say, "I am sorry. Your flag is good too. Can we share?"

They smile. They hug. They are friends again.

They choose to put both flags on the hill. They tie them together. They make a new flag. It is red and blue. It is bright and thin. It waves in the wind.

They are happy. They play with their new flag. They have fun. They say, "We like our flag. It is the best flag. It is our flag."

Once upon a time, there was a happy girl named Dolly. Dolly liked to jump around and play all day. 

One day, Dolly was so excited about playing that she jumped up onto the kitchen counter. She was very interested in the thing her mommy was drinking from the cup - it smelled funny, like coffee. 

Dolly decided that she wanted to try it too, so she took a sip. But the coffee was too yucky for her, it was so bitter that she could not drink it.

Dolly made a funny face and jumped back down off the counter, never wanting to try coffee again. She decided she would rather stick to playing and jumping, instead. 

The end.

Once upon a time there was a mommy, who loved to cook. 
Mommy wanted to cook something special for lunch. 
She looked out the window and saw snow. 
It was so quiet and pretty outside.

Mommy had an idea. She said to her 3-year-old child, "Let's make snow soup for lunch!"
The child smiled and said, "Yes, let's cook snow soup!"

So mommy and her child went outside to gather the snow. 
They filled a big pot full of snow and brought it back inside. 
Mommy added some vegetables, spices and a bit of water to make the soup.

Then they put the pot on the stove. Soon, the house was filled with the yummy smell of snow soup cooking. 
Mommy and her child enjoyed a delicious, quiet lunch together. 
They even had seconds!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved cars and trucks and anything with wheels. One day, Timmy's dad took him to a big car show. Timmy saw lots of cool cars, but one caught his eye. It was a bright red race car with a big engine.

Timmy's dad said, "That car was designed by a very helpful man." Timmy didn't know what "designed" meant, but he knew it sounded important. He asked his dad to explain. His dad said, "To design something means to make it special and unique. The man who made that car worked hard to make it fast and cool."

Timmy was impressed. He watched the race car zoom around the track and cheered it on. Later that day, Timmy and his dad went home. Timmy couldn't stop thinking about the race car. He wanted to design his own car someday, just like the helpful man who made the red race car.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny named Benny. Benny loved to play in the forest and eat carrots. One day, Benny saw a hunter with a gun. The hunter looked confused and did not know where to go. 

Benny was scared and ran to his friends, the squirrels. The squirrels told Benny that hunters like to shoot animals and that he should be careful. They also told him that hunters sometimes set traps to catch animals. 

Benny listened to his friends and was very careful. One day, he saw a carrot inside a trap. Benny wanted the carrot so badly, but he remembered what his friends had told him about traps. He knew that if he went inside the trap, he might get hurt. So, he decided to shut his eyes and walk away. 

Benny learned that it is important to listen to your friends and be careful. He also learned that sometimes you have to give up something you really want to stay safe. From that day on, Benny was always careful in the forest and never went near any traps.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Jack. Jack loved to play with dough and make funny shapes like snakes and cakes. One day, Jack's mom made a rich cake with lots of chocolate and cream. Jack was so happy and ate a big piece of cake.

Suddenly, Jack felt sick and needed to escape to the bathroom. He tried to run, but he slipped on the dough he had left on the floor. Jack's mom heard the noise and came to see what happened.

"Are you okay, Jack?" she asked.

"No, I feel sick," Jack said.

Jack's mom called the doctor, but it was too late. Jack had eaten too much cake and got sick. Jack learned a lesson to not eat too much rich cake and to always clean up his dough.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Jake. Jake was three years old and he loved to explore.

One day, he went for a walk in the woods and he decided to take a peek inside an old cabin. As he walked in, he noticed a big mirror in the corner and he was curious. He went over to take a closer look and then he saw a huge, dark figure behind him. 

Jake got scared and started to panic. He tried to run away, but the dark figure followed him. He was so scared that he ran as fast as he could.

Suddenly, he came across a small pond. He stopped and turned around. But the dark figure was nowhere to be seen. Then he saw something in the water. It was his reflection in the mirror.

Jake was relieved. The dark figure was gone and he was safe. He put his hand up against the mirror and realised that the figure was actually him. The reflection in the mirror had been so scary because he had been too deaf to hear the reflection's voice!

Once there was a man and his daughter. The man loved his daughter very much and wanted her to have the best in life. One day, he decided to take his daughter on an adventure. He wanted to find something special and very rich.

The two of them headed out, walking through the woods. After a long day of walking, the man suddenly realized that he had no idea where they were! He was lost.

The man and his daughter sat down to rest and talked. "Daddy, where are we going?" his daughter asked.

The man thought for a moment and then said, "We are going to find something very special and very rich. We are going to find something that will make you very happy."

The two of them continued walking and soon they found something amazing. It was a huge box filled with gold. They had found something very special and very rich. 

The man and his daughter were very excited. They knew this was the best gift for her. They hugged each other, very happy that they had found something so special. From that day on, the man and his daughter never had to worry about money again. They were very rich!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat salad, especially the one with tomatoes and lettuce. One day, Lily went to the park with her mom and dad. She was so happy to play on the swings and slide. But then, she realized that she lost her favorite toy, a little yellow duck. 

Lily looked everywhere, but she couldn't find it. She felt sad and started to cry. Her parents hugged her and told her that it was okay. They were grateful that they had each other and the fun they had at the park. 

After a while, Lily stopped crying and decided to look for her duck again. She searched under the slide and behind the swings. And finally, she found it! Lily was so happy and hugged her little yellow duck tightly. She was grateful to have found it and couldn't wait to go home and eat some salad.

Once upon a time, there was a foolish boy who wanted to fly a helicopter. He set about building one. He collected some pieces and tried to piece them together. But he couldn't make it work. 

He kept trying and eventually the foolish boy thought he'd made it work. So he set off to fly the helicopter. But it still wasn't working! He flew too high up into the sky. 

The foolish boy was stuck and he couldn't get down. After a while, he ran out of energy and tumbled to the ground. He wasn't hurt, but he was stuck there. Nobody could help him get back up. 

The foolish boy learned his lesson and he never tried to fly a helicopter again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a big sister named Emma. Emma was very mean to Lily, and she would always call her ugly. One Tuesday, Lily was skipping down the road when Emma came up to her and said, "You're so ugly, no one will ever want to be your friend!" 

Lily started to cry and ran away. She went to her mom and told her what happened. Her mom hugged her and said, "You're not ugly, you're beautiful just the way you are." Lily felt better and decided to talk to Emma about how her words hurt her feelings. 

The next day, Lily went up to Emma and said, "You hurt my feelings when you called me ugly. I don't like it when you talk to me like that." Emma felt bad and said sorry to Lily. From then on, Emma stopped calling Lily ugly and they became good friends.

Once upon a time there was a boy who was very foolish. One day he was walking down a street when he saw a big, shiny car. He thought it looked so exciting that he kept looking at it. The driver of the car noticed and said, "Hey silly! What are you doing? Go away!"

The boy felt very embarrassed - he had made a foolish mistake, but he didn't want to do it again. So he thanked the driver and walked away.

The boy soon learned a valuable lesson - repeating foolish behaviour will only lead to more trouble. From then on, he was careful to not do anything too silly. And he always remembered to think carefully before he acted.

Once upon a time there was a dependable little turtle called Toby. One morning, Toby was walking around his pond, looking for something to do.

Suddenly, he spotted a big oat floating in the water. Toby became very excited and decided to dive in and get it.

He swam all the way to the oat and grabbed it with his little flippers. Once he had it, he brought it back to the shore.

Toby could not believe his luck. He had never seen such a big oat before. He decided to take it home.

When Toby got back, he proudly showed the oat to his mum. Toby's mum smiled and said, â€œToby, you are so dependable. I am proud of you!â€

Toby beamed with happiness and decided to keep the oat for lunchtime.

Once upon a time, there were two little boys. One was named Peter, and the other was called Fred. Peter was a bit bossy and always tried to tell Fred what to do. 

Today, Peter arrived with something exciting - a lecture! He showed Fred the lecture and said, "Look what I brought!" 

The lecture was about animals and both boys were very excited to learn all about them. They followed the lecture together, with Peter in charge. He talked a lot and acted very bossy. 

When the lecture was over, Peter said, "That was fun! I brought us this exciting lecture and now we have learned so much about animals." 

The boys thanked Peter for bringing the lecture and went out to play. They talked a lot about animals and enjoyed the day.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Amy. She loved to pretend like she was in different places. One day she decided to pretend she was a train.

Amy ran around the living room pretending to be a train. She looked around for something that would help her to pretend like she was a train. Suddenly she saw a very long cable on the floor.

Amy picked up the cable because it was heavy. She used it as if it was a train track. She pretended like she was chugging along the track, and making lots of noise. She sang songs about being a train and made train noises. 

Amy had so much fun pretending to be a train. She used the cable to make her pretend train track and she stayed on it for a long time. This way she could pretend to be a train as much as she wanted.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to run and play outside. One day, she went to the park with her mom. They saw a big track there. Lily was so excited to run on it.

"Mom, can I run on the track?" asked Lily.

"Sure, Lily. But first, we need to rest a little bit," said her mom.

Lily was getting impatient. She wanted to run right away. But she listened to her mom and rested for a few minutes. Then she ran on the track as fast as she could. It was so much fun!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to draw and color with her crayons. One day, her mommy gave her a big box with a bow on top. Lily was so happy because she knew it was a present just for her.

She used her scissors to cut the ribbon and opened the box. Inside, there were lots of new crayons and markers. Lily was so excited that she started to stretch her arms out wide. She felt gifted to have such a wonderful present from her mommy.

From that day on, Lily used her new crayons to draw lots of pictures. She loved to stretch her imagination and make colorful art for her mommy and daddy to see. And every time she looked at her new crayons, she felt happy and gifted all over again. The end.

Mia and her mommy were planning something special, but Mia didn't know what it was. She asked her mommy and she said, "Wait and see!"

They drove to the veterinarian's office and Mia was excited. She had never been to a veterinarian before and she wondered what would happen.

When they arrived, Mia saw a big brown dog. He was panting and seemed very happy. Mia knew the dog must be spoiled! Her mommy said the dog's name was Buster and he needed help from the vet.

At the vet's office Mia found out why she was there. The vet and her mommy were planning treatment for Buster. Mia thought it was so nice her mommy was helping Buster get better. 

Mia saw the vet give Buster medicine and check his heart. They also took a picture of Buster and checked his teeth. Buster was feeling much better!

Mia learned a lot that day. No matter how spoiled her furry friend was, he still needed to see the veterinarian to stay healthy. And, Mia discovered, being kind to animals was an important part of life!

Little Tommy loved to paint. He had a big blue box filled with paint in the corner of the room. Today he was going to paint a picture of some honey he had seen in the park.

He grabbed a brush and some yellow paint and started to paint. He used the brush to make shapes that would look like honey. But then his mom walked in and started to laugh. 

"What is so funny, Mom?" Tommy asked.

"Is that honey you're painting?" Mom said.

Tommy nodded.

"Honey isn't yellow! It's golden and amber!" Mom explained.

Tommy frowned and put some orange paint on the painting.

"That looks much better!" Mom said. "Now, what does honey smell like?"

Tommy thought for a moment. "Smelly!" he finally said.

Mom laughed again. "No, it doesn't smell bad. It smells sweet and delicious!"

Tommy smiled and added a few more brush strokes to make the honey look even sweeter. It was finished. Now he had a painting of some smelly honey.

Lila liked to play with her dolls. She had a pink dress for her doll, and a pink crown. She pretended her doll was a princess, and she was a prince. She lifted her doll and said, "You are my princess. I will take you to the castle."

But Tom, her brother, did not like her game. He wanted to play with his cars. He saw Lila's doll and said, "That is not a princess. That is a silly doll. Give it to me." He grabbed the doll from Lila and threw it on the floor.

Lila was very sad and angry. She cried and said, "No, Tom! That is my doll. You are mean. Give it back to me." She ran to the floor and picked up her doll. She hugged it and checked if it was hurt.

Tom laughed and said, "You are a baby. You cry for a doll. Dolls are for girls. I have cars. Cars are for boys. They are fast and cool." He zoomed his car on the table and made loud noises.

Lila did not care what Tom said. She loved her doll and her pink dress and her pink crown. She said, "You are wrong, Tom. Dolls are not for girls only. And cars are not for boys only. I can play with both. And I can be a prince if I want to. You are not the boss of me." She lifted her doll again and said, "Come on, princess. Let's go to the castle. We don't need Tom." She walked away with her doll and left Tom alone.

Bella was a little girl who liked to play with fire. She thought fire was pretty and warm and fun. She did not listen to her mama and papa, who told her fire was dangerous and could hurt her. They said she should never touch fire or play with matches or candles. They said she should be careful around the fireplace, where they burned coal to keep the house cozy.

One day, when her mama and papa were busy in the kitchen, Bella saw a shiny matchbox on the table. She was curious and foolish. She took the matchbox and ran to the fireplace. She saw some black coal that was not burning. She wanted to make it burn like the other coal. She opened the matchbox and took out a match. She scratched it on the box and it made a spark. She was happy and excited. She brought the match close to the coal and waited for it to catch fire.

But the coal did not catch fire. It was wet and cold. Instead, it made a loud hiss and a puff of smoke. The smoke went into Bella's eyes and made them sting. She dropped the match and cried out. She blinked and blinked, but her eyes still hurt. She rubbed them with her hands, but that made them worse. She was scared and sorry.

Her mama and papa heard her cry and came running. They saw the matchbox and the smoke and the coal and the match. They knew what Bella had done. They were angry and worried. They took Bella to the sink and washed her eyes with water. They hugged her and scolded her. They told her she was very foolish and naughty. They told her she could have burned herself or the house. They told her she should never play with fire again.

Bella felt ashamed and sad. She said she was sorry and she would not do it again. She said she learned her lesson. She said she did not like fire anymore. She said she liked water and ice and snow. She said she would be good and careful. Her mama and papa forgave her and kissed her. They said they loved her and they were glad she was okay. They said they hoped she would remember her mistake and be wise. They said they would get her some eye drops and a bandage. They said they would read her a story and tuck her in bed. They said they would watch over her and keep her safe.

Once upon a time, there was a very sleepy little owl called Owen. He lived in a tree right next to a big, beautiful rainbow. Every day, Owen would try to collect the rainbow in his arms. 

One day, while he was out collecting the colours one by one a big, friendly butterfly flew by and said â€œWhat are you doing?â€ 

Owen looked up and said â€œIâ€™m trying to collect the rainbow so I can put it in my tree and it will stay safe.â€ 

The butterfly said â€œYou canâ€™t collect a rainbow, itâ€™s just light thatâ€™s made of colours. Thatâ€™s why it changes all the time.â€ 

Owen frowned and said â€œOh. Then what can I do?â€ 

The butterfly smiled and said â€œWell, why donâ€™t you enjoy the rainbow and learn something new every day? That way, it will always stay with you.â€ 

Owen thought that was a very good idea so he thanked the butterfly and flew off, feeling much less sleepy. He was so happy that he could always be close to his rainbow.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Anna. She had a favorite aunt who came over to see her every day. One day when Anna's aunt came over, Anna had a bad feeling about it. She asked her mom why and her mom said that her aunt was not feeling very well. 

Anna was scared, but she decided to go and see her aunt. When Anna came near, her aunt turned away from her. Anna's mom told her to try and talk to her aunt.

Anna: "Aunt, why are you feeling bad?"

Aunt: "I am sad because I cannot do the things that I used to."

Anna was sad, too. She didn't understand why her aunt couldn't do things. She thought maybe if she gave her aunt a hug, it would make her feel better. Anna hugged her aunt tightly and said, "I love you, aunt!"

Aunt's sadness turned into a smile. She hugged Anna back and said, "I love you too!" From that day on, Anna's aunt felt better and the two of them enjoyed spending time together.

Lily likes to collect numbers. She has a book with many numbers in it. She likes to look at them and say them out loud. She knows one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten.

One day, she goes to the park with her mom. She sees a big puddle. She runs to it and jumps in. She feels the water splash on her legs. She laughs and says, "Wet! Wet! Wet!"

She sees something shiny in the puddle. She bends down and picks it up. It is a coin. It has a number on it. She says, "Look, mom! A number! It is five!"

Her mom smiles and says, "Good job, Lily! You found a number in the puddle. Do you want to keep it?"

Lily nods and says, "Yes, please! I want to collect it. It is my wet number. Can I find more?"

Her mom says, "Sure, you can look for more. But be careful not to get too wet. And don't forget to share with your friends if they want to play too."

Lily says, "Okay, mom. I will share. I like numbers. And I like wet." She runs to the puddle again and looks for more numbers. She is happy.

Once upon a time there was a little boy. He was 3 years old, and his name was Joe.

Joe was feeling gloomy one day, so his mommy took him outside to play. He thought it would be fun to try and find worms in the dirt.

He began to dig, and soon he found one! But then, another worm popped out, and then another, and another! He was so excited to see so many worms.

Joe decided to take one home, so he put it in a jar and covered it with leaves. He took it inside and put it on his shelf.

Joe thought and thought about how he should take care of the worm. He decided the best thing would be to feed the worm carrots, and give it water every day.

He felt very happy taking care of his worm and was no longer gloomy.

Tom and Ben are brothers. They like to play hockey in the park. They have colorful sticks and a black puck. They take turns to hit the puck and score goals.

One day, they go to the park with their mom. She sits on a bench and reads a book. She tells them to have fun and be careful. Tom and Ben run to the hockey field and start to play.

"Look at me, Ben!" Tom says. "I can hit the puck very hard and fast!"

He swings his stick and hits the puck. But he misses the goal. The puck flies over the fence and hits a car. The car makes a loud noise and the alarm goes off.

"Oh no!" Ben says. "You broke the car, Tom! What will we do?"

Tom is scared. He drops his stick and runs to his mom. He hopes she did not see what happened.

"Mom, mom!" he says. "Can we go home now? I'm tired and hungry."

His mom looks at him and then at the car. She sees the puck and the dent. She is angry and sad.

"Tom, what did you do?" she says. "You hit the car with the puck! That's very bad! You have to say sorry and pay for the damage!"

Tom feels bad. He wishes he did not play hockey. He wishes he listened to his mom and relaxed on the bench. He knows he is in big trouble. He starts to cry. He does not like this ending.

Once upon a time there was a wise old man who lived in a small factory. He had been stirring things in the factory for many years, always working hard. 
One day, he wanted a little helping hand. He knew exactly the right person for the job - a three year old! So the wise old man called for the child and asked for their help. 
The three year old was so happy. They ran over to the factory and began to stir things up. They stirred the big pots, moved things around and tidied up the shelves. 
The wise old man was very pleased with their work. He praised the three year old for their help and gave them a big hug. The three year old thanked the wise old man and left the factory with a smile on their face. 
And so the wise old man and the three year old lived happily ever after, stirring things up in the small factory.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to play outside in the mud and dirt. Her mommy always reminded her to take a bath and wash her hair with shampoo. But Lily didn't like to take a bath, she thought it was boring.

One day, Lily went outside to play and got very dirty. She didn't notice that a zipper on her jacket was broken. She kept playing and rolling around in the dirt. When it was time to go inside, she tried to zip up her jacket but it wouldn't close. She didn't want to tell her mommy because she was afraid she would get in trouble for breaking the zipper.

The next day, Lily's mommy noticed that her jacket was dirty and the zipper was broken. She asked Lily what happened and Lily told her the truth. Her mommy was proud of her for being honest and promised to get her a new jacket. From that day on, Lily learned that it's always better to tell the truth and take a bath when you're dirty.

Once upon a time there were two best friends- Jack and Jill. 
Jack and Jill went to explore underground. But it was too dark and they couldn't see. Jack told Jill "We need help!". Suddenly, a bright light appeared and made everything clear. 
It was their friend, the sun! Jack and Jill were so happy that the sun came to help. The sun shone brighter and brighter and lit up the underground. Jack and Jill could see all around and they started to explore. They found lots of cool and hidden things underground. 
Finally, when they had seen enough, the sun helped Jack and Jill find their way out and they went home happy. 
The end.

Sam and Mia liked to play with their toys in the living room. They had many toys, like cars, dolls, blocks and books. But they did not like to put their toys away when they were done. They left them on the floor, on the couch, on the table and everywhere.

One day, their mom came home from work and saw the mess. She was not happy. She said to Sam and Mia, "You need to return your toys to their places. The living room is not organized. It is hard to walk and find things. And it is not safe. You can trip and fall and hurt yourself or break something. Please, help me clean up."

Sam and Mia did not want to clean up. They wanted to keep playing. They said to their mom, "But mom, we are having fun. We will clean up later. Can we play for a little longer?"

Their mom said, "No, you cannot play for a little longer. You have played enough. It is time to return your toys to their places. You can play again tomorrow, but only if you keep the living room organized. Now, come on, let's do it together. It will be faster and easier."

Sam and Mia sighed. They knew their mom was right. They did not want to trip and fall and hurt themselves or break something. They did not want to make their mom unhappy. They decided to help their mom clean up. They returned their toys to their places. They put the cars in the box, the dolls in the basket, the blocks in the bag and the books on the shelf. They made the living room organized.

Their mom smiled. She said to Sam and Mia, "Thank you, Sam and Mia. You did a good job. The living room looks much better. I am proud of you. Now, how about we have some cookies and milk as a reward?"

Sam and Mia smiled too. They said to their mom, "Yes, please. We love cookies and milk. And we love you, mom."

They hugged their mom and went to the kitchen. They enjoyed their cookies and milk. They were happy. They learned to return their toys to their places and keep the living room organized.

Once a there was a girl named Mia. She was very envious of her brother, Pete. He had a toy pin that she wanted. But her mum wouldn't let her have it. Mia started to yell and tell her mum that it was not fair. 

Her mum explained to Mia that she was too young to have the pin. This made Mia angrier and she began to yell even louder. 

Suddenly, her mum gave in and let Mia play with the pin. Mia was so happy that she jumped up and down, and shouted with joy.

From that day onwards, Mia knew that her mum was always there to take good care of her. Whenever she was feeling envious, she just had to yell, and her mum would always understand.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Molly. She was only three years old but already very brave. One day, Molly decided to explore the forest near her house. As she walked, she heard a deep growl. Molly was scared as she looked up and saw a big monster.

The monster said, "Hi Molly. I'm Richie the Rich Monster. I'm stuck in this tree and I need your help to get out. Can you lift me? Please?"

Molly had the courage to help Richie the Rich Monster. She lifted him out of the tree. Richie thanked Molly for helping him.

"You showed me how to be brave. You are a very kind and special girl," Richie said.

Molly smiled as she watched Richie slowly make his way out of the forest. He waved farewell and said, "Goodbye, Molly!"

Once there was a puppy called True. He was a very lively pup with lots of energy. Every day he would run around the yard and bark with joy. But one day, True started to frown. His family was so sad. They had never seen him this way before. 

True's family decided to take him for a walk. As soon as they got outside, his eyes lit up. True started to bark with excitement. He laughed and ran around, just as lively as before. 

True's family was so happy to see him happy again. They knew that true was truly a lively pup. As they walked, they saw True smiling and they knew they'd made the right decision. True had reminded them that being happy should be kept true.

Once upon a time there was a big bird. He wanted to celebrate his day. He asked his friends for help. They agreed to help him.

The big bird said, â€œLetâ€™s fly to the law and celebrate together.â€ The birdâ€™s friends said yes.

So, the big bird and his friends started to fly. They flew higher and higher, and the bird was very happy.

The big bird had nowhere to go. He was lost forever. His friends had to go home without him. They tried to help him but it was too late.

The bird had to stay in the strange place until the end. He could never celebrate his day.

Sam liked to do projects. He liked to attach pieces of cardboard together to make something new. He often used a glue gun and pieces of bright felt, string, and buttons. 

Today Sam wanted to try something different. He gathered together his materials, some pieces of modest-looking cardboard. He could attach them together with his glue gun to make something new. 

Sam began to attach pieces of cardboard together, securing them with the glue gun. After a while, he looked at his creation and smiled. He had made a beautiful box with different colorful pieces of cardboard. 

Sam was very proud of his box. Now he wanted to fill it with somethingâ€”but what? He thought and thought until he decided to put inside his small toys. He attached a piece of string to the top of the box so he could carry it around. 

Sam took his box with him everywhere! He liked to take things out and put them back inside. He had made a very special and beautiful box from modest-looking cardboard.

Once there was a girl named Jane. Jane was invited to a party. She was very excited to go to the party, it sounded like it was going to be very fun and full of games. 

When Jane arrived to the party, it was so crazy! There were kids running around, the music was loud and there was a bouncy castle.

Suddenly, Jane's mom told her it was time to leave the party. Jane was very upset. She had just arrived and did not want to go home yet. 

"Mom, I don't want to leave yet," said Jane. But her mother said it was time to go and Jane had to leave the party.

Jane was very sad as she left the party and went home. She was so disappointed that she had to leave the crazy party.

Once upon a time, there was a modest farmer who had a big field full of fruits and veggies. Every day, he went out to the field to take care of his crops and harvest what was ready. 

One morning, he went out to his field to find that some of his radishes were ready to be gathered. "Ah, they are so ready," he said as he loaded them into his bag.

Just as he was about to leave, his young neighbour Evan ran up to him.

"What do you have there, sir?" Evan asked.

The farmer smiled. "I have some radishes that I am loading into my bag."

Evan's eyes grew wide. "Can I have one?"

The farmer shook his head. "These radishes are for my family but I have some others growing in the field. Why don't you pick one for yourself?"

Evan's face lit up. "Thank you, sir!"

The farmer smiled and patted the boy on the head. He watched with a modest pride as Evan ran off to pick his own radish.

Once there was a big girl who had a large hat. She liked to wear her hat because it made her feel special. One day, the girl wanted to show off her hat to the world.
So she put on her hat and went for a walk. As she kept walking, she noticed other kids were looking at her hat. They commented how large and special it was. 
The girl was so proud of her hat. She even started to run with her hat on. But, as she was running, she suddenly tripped over and her large hat flew off her head. 
She quickly stood up, but the hat was gone. She looked all around and screamed, but it was too far away for her to find it. The girl was so sad and did not have her special hat anymore.

There was a man and a little girl. The man asked the girl, "What do you want to do today?"

The girl thought for a moment and said, "I want to be successful."

The man smiled and said, "That is a great goal. How do you plan to succeed?"

The girl smiled back. She was confident. She said, "I'm going to be delicate and kind to everyone I meet today."

The man was proud of her. He said, "I'm sure you will succeed today."

The little girl smiled and ran off. She was excited to start her day. Throughout the day, she was delicate and kind. Everyone noticed and they said kind things to her.

In the end, the girl had succeeded. She accomplished her goal! She was very happy and celebrated with the people around her.

Once upon a time there was an attractive pot. It belonged to a kind family. Everyday the family put food in the pot, and it made them so happy. But one day the pot disappeared! Everyone searched and searched but the pot couldn't be found. 

They were so worried. Then one day, a nice person found the pot and decided to return it to the family. When the family saw the pot again, they were so happy! They thanked the kind person with a big hug and some rewards.

The pot stayed with the family forever after that. They kept it safe and cherished it. They knew it was important to return things that didn't belong to you.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Jack. He was very adventurous and always looking for new fun. One day, Jack was walking in the park with his parents when he saw a funny looking man. Jack's parents laughed as the man told a joke. Jack thought this was really fun and wanted to try it too. He made up a joke and told it to his parents. They laughed and hugged him. That made Jack smile. From then on, Jack told jokes all the time and made his family laugh and smile. He even started to tell jokes to friends he made at school. Everyone always said that Jack was a great joker and laughed at his jokes. From then on, Jack kept finding new funny jokes to tell and kept his family and friends amused with his adventures and funny jokes. No one could resist Jack's point and the world became a funnier place because of him!

"Look, Mom! I can slide!" said the three-year-old excitedly. She already knew how to slide down the big slide at the park. 

Mom smiled. "Yes, you are so flexible!" 

The little girl then happily raced to the top of the slide and sat down. She eagerly started moving down, faster and faster, until she reached the bottom. 

Mom praised her. "You did so well! Do you want a banana?" 

The little girl nodded her head. She unwrapped the banana and took a bite. It was delicious! 

The girl smiled and said, "Let's slide again!"

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He loved to draw pictures and show them to his family. One day, Timmy drew a picture of a bunny and wanted to print it out. His mom helped him put the paper in the printer and press the button.

Later that day, Timmy's family went to a picnic. They brought a basket full of yummy snacks. Timmy was so excited to show his bunny picture to his cousins. But when he reached into the basket, he accidentally spilled all the snacks on the ground. He felt embarrassed and didn't want to show his picture anymore.

But then, Timmy remembered that he printed out a copy of his bunny picture. He took it out of his pocket and showed it to his cousins. They loved it and even helped him pick up the snacks. Timmy felt happy and proud of his picture. From that day on, he always kept a printed copy of his drawings in his pocket, just in case.

One day, Dad went to the garden to observe all of the flowers. He thought one particular flower was very beautiful. His three year old daughter followed Dad, running around, and wanted to pick the flower too. 

"Please don't pick the flower," Dad said. He didn't want her to ruin the flower. 

She smiled and said, "But why Dad? It looks so pretty."

"I know, but if you pick it, it won't look so pretty anymore," said Dad.

Suddenly, a crazy wind blew and picked the flower all by itself. The three year old looked in amazement, and said, "Look Dad! It's a magical flower."

Dad smiled and said, "Yes, amazing isn't it? That's why I wanted you not to pick the flower." 

The little girl learned her lesson that day and knew never to pick the flowers in the garden.

Once upon a time, there was a rich space. It was filled with stars that sparkled and planets that shone bright. Every day, the creatures, big and small, were happy and free.

But one day, a dark cloud descended on the space. It was a large and heavy cloud, so the creatures all suffered. They tried their best to chase the dark cloud away, but nothing worked. 

"What can we do now?" shouted the small creatures. 

Suddenly an answer came from a wise old star. "Fly up high," he said. "Fly up high and watch the dark cloud float away." 

So the creatures all flew up high, past the dark cloud and away. As they soared through the sky, their suffering melted away. And soon enough, the sky was bright and clear once again. 

The creatures were happy, and the rich space was peaceful. They turned to the wise old star and thanked him for guiding them, and from that day on, they never stopped flying up high.

Once upon a time, there was a graceful bird named Bluey. Bluey loved to fly high in the sky and play with his friends. One day, while Bluey was playing, he saw his friend Bunny crying.

"What's wrong, Bunny?" Bluey asked. Bunny said, "I can't finish my race. My leg hurts." Bluey knew this was an emergency. He wanted to help Bunny finish the race and feel happy again.

Bluey had an idea. He asked his friend Elephant to help. Elephant was big and strong. Elephant carried Bunny on his back and walked to the finish line. Bunny was so happy and thanked Bluey and Elephant.

The other animals cheered for Bunny, Bluey, and Elephant. They learned that helping friends in an emergency is a good thing to do. And they all played together, happy and safe.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily went to the park to play. She saw a little puppy and went to play with him. Suddenly, the puppy started to shrink! Lily was shocked! 

"Wow, you're so small now!" Lily said. 

The puppy barked fiercely and ran away. Lily was sad because she wanted to play with him more. She asked her mommy why the puppy shrunk and her mommy said it was because he was a magical puppy. 

Lily smiled and went home, excited to tell her friends about the magical puppy she met at the park.

Once there was a cool girl named Lily. Lily was very excited because she was going to school for the first time! She quickly put on her pretty dress and shiny shoes and ran outside to the bus stop.

When the bus arrived, several kids were already waiting by the side of the road. Lily could feel her heart pounding as she got on the bus. She rubbed her hands together nervously and looked around.

Lily quickly realized that some of the kids on the bus were not very nice. They were teasing her, and a few even tried to take her new backpack away. Lily kept rubbing her hands together and stayed strong. 

Finally, the bus arrived at school and all the kids scrambled off. Lily was relieved, but she knew she would have to face the bullies tomorrow. She decided to ask her teacher for help and to stay cool. Lily was determined to have a great first day at school!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the park. One day, she saw a bird flying in the sky. She wanted to grab it, but she couldn't reach it. 

Suddenly, she saw a piece of bread on the ground. She picked it up and threw it in the air. The bird came down to grab the bread. But then, a big cat appeared and grabbed the bird. 

Lily felt helpless and sad. She said to the cat, "Please let the bird go." But the cat didn't listen and ran away with the bird in its mouth. Lily cried and went back home. She learned that sometimes, we can't always help others, but we can always try.

One day, a little boy named Tim went to the park with his mom. They saw a stubborn lizard on a rock. The lizard did not want to move. Tim looked at the lizard and said, "Hi, lizard! Why are you so stubborn?"

The lizard looked at Tim and said, "I need to choose a new home. But I can't find one I like." Tim thought for a moment and then said, "I can help you choose a home, lizard!"

Tim and the lizard looked around the park. They saw a big tree, a small bush, and a tall rock. The lizard looked at all the homes and said, "I choose the big tree!"

Tim and his mom helped the lizard move to the big tree. The lizard was happy in his new home. Tim said, "Bye, lizard! Have fun in your new home!" The lizard waved goodbye and said, "Thank you, Tim!"

Once upon a time, there were two best friends named Sam and Sarah. Sam and Sarah were very adventurous. Every night they would grab the flashlight, and go on a great wander.

One night the two friends were having so much fun, they got lost. It was dark and they could not find their way home.

Sam said to Sarah, "Where are we?"

Sarah thought for a moment and said, â€œWe are lost. I donâ€™t know.â€

But then Sam smiled. He said, â€œLetâ€™s wander a bit more. Maybe weâ€™ll find our way home.â€

Sarah clapped her hands and said, â€œYay! Letâ€™s go!â€

So the two friends kept wandering until they eventually found their way back home. They were so happy to be home safe and sound. They were more adventuresome than ever.

The end!

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved going to the park and playing with his friends. One day, Timmy went to the park and played for a long time. When he was ready to go home, he realized he lost his favorite toy car. Timmy looked everywhere, but he couldn't find it.

Timmy's mom took him to the shop to buy a new toy car. They went to a big green shop with lots of toys. Timmy was so happy to see all the toys. He looked around and found a toy car that looked just like his lost one. Timmy's mom bought him the new toy car and he was so happy. 

From that day on, Timmy made sure to take better care of his toys so he wouldn't lose them again.

Once upon a time there was a girl called Mia who liked to sing. One day Mia wanted to try something new, so she decided to go surfing. She was very excited and asked her mum for help.

So Mia and her mum went to the beach. Mia had never tried surfing before, but she was very patient and tried her best. Her mum showed her how to catch the small waves and Mia followed what she said.

Mia tried to stay on the surf board but she kept falling off. She laughed and soon she was laughing every time she fell off. After a few tries, Mia finally got the hang of it and she was standing on the board.

Mia was so happy that she started to sing. She sang a song of joy and gratitude for the wonderful feeling of riding the waves. Mia was smiling from ear to ear and enjoyed her first time surfing.

Sandy and her team were so excited. Today they were having a picnic in the park. They got to the park and spread out a blanket on the grass. Sandy looked around and smiled.

As the team opened their backpacks, there was laughter all around. They took out their yummy sandwiches and juice boxes. "Let's play catch!" yelled Sandy. Everyone cheered and got out the colorful ball.

Suddenly, the ball flew up in the air and Sandy raced to catch it. Unfortunately, it fell too fast, and it landed on a fragile flower. Sandy was sad, but her team cheered her up. "Don't worry Sandy," they said. "Let's just laugh and have a great time!" And Sandy and her team laughed and laughed and enjoyed the rest of their time in the park.

Anna liked to play with her dolls. She had many dolls, but her favorite was Lily. Lily had a pink dress and long hair. Anna took good care of Lily and always made her comfortable.

One day, Anna went to the park with her mom and Lily. She saw a girl who had no dolls. The girl looked sad. Anna wanted to make her happy. She asked her mom if she could lend Lily to the girl. Her mom said yes, but told her to be careful.

Anna went to the girl and said, "Hi, I am Anna. This is Lily. She is my doll. Do you want to play with her?" The girl smiled and said, "Yes, thank you. I am Mia." Anna and Mia played with Lily on the swings and the slide. They had fun.

But then, a boy came and grabbed Lily. He said, "This is my doll now. She is made of steel. She is strong and cool." He ran away with Lily. Anna and Mia were shocked and scared. They cried and called for help.

Anna's mom heard them and came quickly. She saw the boy with Lily and ran after him. She caught him and took Lily back. She said, "This is not your doll. This is Anna's doll. She lent it to Mia. You cannot take what is not yours. That is wrong and mean." She gave Lily back to Anna and Mia. She hugged them and said, "I am sorry this happened. You are very brave and kind. You did a good thing by sharing your doll. I am proud of you." Anna and Mia felt better and thanked her.

Anna and Mia hugged Lily and said goodbye. They promised to play again soon. Anna was happy to have her doll back, but she was also happy to have a new friend. She learned that lending can be nice, but stealing can be bad. She also learned that steel is not always better than pink. She thought that Lily was the best doll in the world. She was comfortable and loved.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Annabelle. She was a very organized girl and she loved playing with drums. Every day she would bring her drum to the park and put on a show.

One day, a mean boy came to the park and saw Annabelle. He was very angry because he wanted to play with the drums too. He yelled at Annabelle and tried to take the drum away from her.

But Annabelle was too organized and she held on tight. The mean boy got madder and madder and eventually, he became so angry that he picked up the drum and threw it away. Annabelle was very sad and she ran home crying.

The mean boy had ruined Annabelle's special day. He had brought a bad ending to Annabelle's fun.

Once upon a time, there was a rabbit named Benny. Benny lived in a big field with lots of other rabbits. One day, Benny saw a butterfly and said, "Wow, look at that pretty butterfly!"

His friend, Sammy, asked, "What are you looking at, Benny?"

Benny said, "I'm observing the butterfly. It's so pretty!"

Sammy said, "I love how you notice all the pretty things, Benny. You're so compassionate."

Benny felt happy and said, "Thanks, Sammy. I love watching the butterflies and smelling the herbs in the field. It makes me happy."

Lily was excited to go to the zoo with her mom and dad. She wanted to see the lions, the monkeys, and the elephants. She also wanted to take pictures with her new camera. She got the camera for her birthday and she loved it.

Before they left, Lily had to organize her backpack. She put her camera, her water bottle, her hat, and her snacks inside. She zipped it up and put it on her back. She was ready to go.

"Are you sure you have everything, Lily?" her mom asked.

"Yes, mom, I have everything," Lily said.

"OK, then, let's go to the zoo!" her dad said.

They got in the car and drove to the zoo. Lily looked out the window and saw many things. She saw cars, trees, houses, and people. She wondered what she would see at the zoo.

When they arrived, they bought their tickets and entered the zoo. Lily was amazed by all the animals. She saw giraffes, zebras, penguins, and bears. She took out her camera and started to take pictures. She wanted to remember everything.

She saw a sign that said "Lion Exhibit". She ran towards it, followed by her mom and dad. She wanted to see the lions up close. She hoped they would roar.

She reached the lion exhibit and saw a big cage with two lions inside. They were lying on the ground, sleeping. Lily was disappointed. She wanted to see them move and play.

She decided to take a picture anyway. She held her camera in front of her face and pressed the button. But nothing happened. She pressed it again. Still nothing.

She looked at her camera and saw a red light. She turned it over and saw a message. It said "Battery Low".

Lily felt sad. Her camera was out of power. She couldn't take any more pictures.

She showed her camera to her mom and dad. They looked at it and sighed.

"Oh, Lily, I'm sorry. We forgot to charge your camera before we left," her mom said.

"It's OK, mom. It's not your fault," Lily said.

"Maybe we can find a place to charge it at the zoo," her dad said.

"Or maybe we can buy some new batteries," her mom said.

They tried to cheer Lily up. They told her they could still see the other animals and have fun. They told her they could take pictures with their phones and share them with her later.

Lily nodded. She tried to smile. She still wanted to see the zoo. But she wished her camera was working. She wished she could take pictures of the lions. She wished they would roar.

Once upon a time, there was a youth named Timmy. Timmy was a fat boy who loved to eat candy and play with his toys. One day, Timmy's mom asked him to clean up his toys.

Timmy replied, "I don't want to clean up my toys. I want to eat candy."

His mom said, "If you clean up your toys, you can have some candy later."

Timmy thought for a moment and said, "Okay, I will clean up my toys. But first, let me count how many toys I have."

Timmy counted his toys and realized he had too many. He decided to give some away to his friends. His mom was proud of him for being kind and sharing with others. In the end, Timmy got his candy and was happy he cleaned up his toys.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird who wanted to try something new. He wanted to fly up to the sun and feel the warmth on his wings. However, his mother was very worried. She tried to prevent the little bird from flying so high by telling him again and again how dangerous it was.

"It is too dangerous up there," the mother said. "Why take such a risk?"

But the little bird wanted to try something new and refused to listen to his mother's warnings. He flapped his wings and flew higher and higher, until he was almost at the sun. 

Suddenly, the little bird felt a sharp pain throughout his body. He had not heeded his mother's advice and his wings had gotten too close to the sun. He tried to fly back down, but his wings had been burned and he could not fly.

The mother was very sad and she picked up the little bird in her beak. She flew him back home and said softly to him "Listen to your mother's advice. It is for your own good."

The moral for the story is simple: always listen to your parents. They are only trying to prevent anything bad from happening to you.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. Her name was Amanda. She was very sad. Her belly was empty, and she was very thirsty.

But then one day, Amanda found a banana. She was so happy. She felt grateful for the banana.

But then she started to suffer again. The banana was hard and green. She tried to bite into it, but her little teeth couldn't bite through it. She started to cry.

But then she saw an old man. He was very kind. He helped Amanda break open the banana and mush it up so that she could eat it.

Amanda was very grateful. She ate the banana, and it tasted so sweet. She was so happy she no longer had to suffer from hunger.

Lila and Ben are friends who like to swim in the sea. They have a big boat that they can ride on the water. One day, they see a map that shows a treasure under the sea. The map says they have to go west, where the sun goes down.

"Let's go find the treasure!" Lila says. "Maybe we can find gold and jewels and shells!"

"OK, but we have to be careful. The sea can be deep and dark and scary," Ben says. "We need to take our masks and fins and tubes."

They put on their gear and start the boat. They follow the map and go west. They see many fish and plants and rocks in the water. They look for the spot where the map says the treasure is.

They find a big empty chest that looks old and rusty. They think the treasure is inside. They dive into the water and swim to the chest. They open it and look inside.

But there is nothing in the chest. It is empty. No gold, no jewels, no shells. Only sand and seaweed.

"Aw, there is no treasure!" Lila says. "The map was wrong. This is not fun."

"Maybe the treasure is somewhere else. Maybe someone took it. Maybe it was a joke," Ben says. "But we still had fun. We saw many things in the water. And we have each other."

They hug and smile. They swim back to the boat and go home. They are still friends who like to swim in the sea.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sally who loved to ride her bike. But one day, her bike would not move. She looked down, and noticed that the pedal had come off!

Sally told her mom about it, and she said, "we need to find a new pedal that belongs to your bike so it will fit." So they set off to the bike store.

When they got there, Sally's mom found the perfect pedal. She asked the shopkeeper, "Does this pedal belong to Sally's bike?"

The shopkeeper looked at the bike and said, "Yes, it will fit perfectly!"

Sally was so happy, and thanked her mom and the shopkeeper.

When they got home, Sally's mom put the new pedal on the bike. Sally hopped on her bike and rode off, feeling like she belonged.

Once upon a time there was a tiny girl named Jane. She was three years old and loved to play outside. Every day, when the sun shone bright in the sky, Jane and her mommy went for a walk in the park.

One day, Jane and her mommy went to the park and when they got there, it began to rain. Jane started to cry because she did not want to get wet. Fortunately, Jane's mommy was very smart and had brought an umbrella. She opened the umbrella and put it over Jane so she wouldn't get wet.

Jane smiled when the umbrella kept her warm and dry. Her mommy smiled too and said, "See, we don't have to cry when it rains. Our umbrella will keep us warm and dry!" Jane laughed and said, "I love my umbrella!"

Once upon a time there was a big boat. The boat was floating on the sea. Suddenly, it started to move towards a big reef. The reef was underwater and made of coral. It was so big and beautiful!

The boat sailed close to the reef. Suddenly a giant fish came out of the reef. It splashed around the boat and everyone on the boat was so excited! Then the fish swam away and the boat kept floating towards the reef.

When the boat was very close, everyone on the boat got ready to jump in the water. They all had their swimming suits on. One by one, they entered the reef. Everyone had so much fun swimming around the coral and exploring the reef.

The sun started to set and it was time to go back to the boat. Everyone said goodbye to the reef and promised to one day come back. Then they all got back on the boat and sailed away.

Once upon a time there was an elderly lady. She went for a walk in the park and saw a very happy face. She recognized the face as someone she had seen before. It was her old friend Tom! She was so excited to see him after so many years and ran to give him a big hug. Tom was so surprised to see the elderly lady and had a huge smile on his face. He was glad to recognize her and soon both were laughing and chatting about old times. They talked for a while and then Tom and the elderly lady said their goodbyes and went their separate ways. It was so nice to see an old familiar face!

Ben and Lily are playing with their toys. They have many toys of different shapes and colors. Ben likes to sort his toys by shape. He puts all the circles in one pile, all the squares in another pile, and so on. Lily likes to sort her toys by color.
