Anna and Ben were twins who liked to play together. They had many toys, but their favorite was a big star that lit up and made sounds. They would pretend it was a spaceship or a fairy or a monster. They always shared the star and had fun.

One day, their mom said they had to go to the park with their aunt. She said they could bring one toy each. Anna and Ben both wanted to bring the star, but there was only one. They started to fight over it and pull it from each other.

"Stop it, you two!" their mom said. "You have to separate and choose another toy. The star is too big and heavy for the park. You can play with it when you come back."

Anna and Ben did not want to separate or leave the star. They cried and said it was not fair. Their mom said they had to listen or they would not go to the park at all. She put the star on a shelf and told them to hurry up.

Anna and Ben were very sad and angry. They did not talk to each other or their aunt on the way to the park. They did not play with their other toys or the swings or the slide. They just sat on a bench and looked at the sky.

They saw many birds and clouds and planes, but they did not care. They wished they had their star. Then they saw something shiny and bright. It was a real star, sparkling in the daylight. They had never seen a star in the day before.

They pointed at it and said, "Look, a star!"

They looked at each other and smiled. They realized they missed each other and their star. They hugged and said they were sorry for fighting. They decided to share the star and play together again.

They told their aunt they wanted to go back home and see their star. She said they could, but they had to be kind and say thank you to their mom. They agreed and ran to the car.

They got home and ran to their room. They saw their star on the shelf, still lit up and making sounds. They were so happy they jumped and clapped. They took the star and played with it, pretending it was the star they saw in the sky. They thanked their mom and said they loved her and each other. They learned that sometimes they had to separate, but they always had their star.

Once upon a time, there was a fat gray rabbit. He was very messy. Every day, the rabbit would hop around and leave bits of rubbish behind him. One day, he decided to try something new. He wanted to be clean.

So the rabbit got to work. He started picking up the bits of rubbish and tidying them away. He worked very hard to make sure everything was all nice and clean. When he was done, the rabbit felt very pleased.

He hopped around his new clean space and admired how tidy everything was. He was so happy that he shouted out loud, â€œEverything is so clean!â€

The rabbit was proud of himself. He smiled and hopped away, feeling happy and satisfied.

The Cat entered the Room. It's Brain was thinking what to do. The Room had a spicy smell. The Cat sniffed and gave a big meow. Suddenly the Cat saw a Mouse. It ran very fast, but the Cat was faster. The Cat chased the Mouse around the Room. It was so much fun! The Cat and Mouse ran around until the Mouse ran out of the Room. The Cat stayed in the Room and sniffed the spicy smell. It liked it very much.

Little Fred had been waiting all day for his mom to unlock the door. As soon as she opened the door she saw a wild surprise. A fox was inside their house! Little Fred's mom was so afraid that she screamed. Little Fred stepped in front of his mom and tried to get the fox to calm down. He slowly reached out and offered the fox a bowl of his favorite sauce. The fox was really hungry and it started to relax. Little Fred slowly unlocked the cage and the fox ran out the door. Little Fred's mom thanked him for being so brave. Little Fred was very proud he could help unlock the mystery of the wild fox.

Once there was a little baby fish. He liked to swim around in the big ocean and make lots of friends. One day he woke up feeling a bit tired. He realized that he was running out of oxygen and needed some help.

So he looked around for his friends. He saw a big fish with a golden tail. He asked the big fish for some help. The big fish said that he could give him some oxygen from the ocean. It smelled really rich and the little fish felt a bit better.
 
From then on the baby fish always hung out with the big fish. The big fish gave the little fish lots of oxygen and the little fish kept feeling very happy and energized. They swam around the ocean together and always felt better with the rich oxygen!

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Ella. Ella's daddy had a very special box, and it was locked with a nail. Ella was curious to see what was inside, so she asked her daddy to open it.

Daddy said no. He said that what was inside was hidden, so Ella had to be very patient. Ella was disappointed, but waited for her daddy to tell her what was in the box.

One day, when Ella was at her daddy's office, she saw him using the special box. Daddy printed out lots of pictures, and Ella got curious.

She asked daddy if she could look and he said yes. When Ella opened the box, she saw lots of beautiful pictures of her and her family. She was so happy and thanked her daddy for being so patient.

The next day, Ella and her daddy went to the beach and they took out the special box and printed pictures of their special day together. Ella was so happy to share her hidden pictures.

Sam was a wealthy three-year-old who loved to slides. Every day he would go to the playground with his best friend Tyler. They would climb the ladder to the top of the slide and race to the bottom.

One day, Sam and Tyler were sliding on the slide when Tyler shouted, "Move faster, Sam!" Sam laughed and tried to move as quickly as he could.

Tyler looked at him and said, "We will never be the first ones to get to the bottom if you don't move faster." Sam smiled, took a deep breath and shouted "I'm ready!"

They raced down the slide and, to their surprise, Sam was the first to reach the bottom. Tyler was so happy for Sam that he gave him a high five.

Sam and Tyler continued to race down the slide together, enjoying their time in the playground. Sam was proud of himself for being the first one to the bottom and Tyler was proud of his friend for being so wealthy.

Once upon a time there was a grumpy old bear. He lived in a big forest and was very unhappy. The other animals in the forest didn't like his grumpy ways and stayed away from him.

One morning the sun shone brightly in the sky. The bear had never seen such wonderful sunshine before and it made him feel a bit better.

The bear saw a bright yellow butterfly land in front of him. The butterfly introduced itself as Sunshine. The bear and Sunshine talked for a while.

The bear found himself smiling more and more as he talked to Sunshine. She was so cheerful and friendly that the bear couldn't help but like her. 

The two became the best of friends and the grumpy bear stopped being so grumpy. The animals of the forest accepted the bear and all were happy.

The sunshine kept the bear happy and he loved it.

Lily and Ben are playing with their toy guns in the garden. They like to pretend they are cowboys and robbers. Lily is the cowboy and Ben is the robber. They run and hide behind the trees and the bushes.

"Bang, bang, I shoot you, robber!" Lily shouts.

"No, you miss, cowboy!" Ben shouts back.

They laugh and chase each other. They have fun.

Mum and Dad are watching them from the window. They smile and shake their heads. They love their children. They are a happy family.

"Time for lunch, kids!" Mum calls.

Lily and Ben drop their toy guns and run to the house. They are hungry.

"Thank you, Mum, for the yummy food!" Lily says.

"Thank you, Dad, for the cool toys!" Ben says.

Mum and Dad hug them and kiss them. They are kind and proud.

"Thank you, Lily and Ben, for being good and sweet!" Mum says.

"Thank you, Mum and Dad, for being the best family!" Ben says.

They eat and talk and laugh. They are a happy family.

Once upon a time there were two best friends. Mark and Tim were always so lively! Every day they would go and play together in the park.

One day, they found a shiny rock lying in the grass. They decided to take it home and polish it. They worked hard, rubbing the rock with their cloths until it was so smooth and shiny.

Once it was good and polished, they put it on the shelf in Mark's bedroom. It was their very own special rock. Every time Mark and Tim were together, they would look at their shiny rock and be so proud of their work.

From then on, Mark and Tim were the liveliest and best friends in the park. Everywhere they went, people smiled. They were sure to brighten up anybody's day!

Once upon a time, there was a big red truck. It was very loud and made lots of noise. One day, the truck was driving down the road and saw a little girl playing with her toys. The truck was very nosy and wanted to see what the girl was doing.

Suddenly, the truck remembered that it had to deliver some boxes to the store. So, it drove away from the little girl and went to the store. When it got there, the truck unloaded the boxes and the store owner was very happy.

After that, the truck went back on the road and saw the little girl again. This time, the truck didn't stop to be nosy. It just drove by and waved to the girl. The little girl was very happy to see the truck and waved back. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat lemons because they were sour and tasty. One day, Lily's mom bought a bag of lemons from the store. Lily was very excited to eat them, but her mom said they needed to test if they were good first.

Lily asked, "What does 'test' mean, Mommy?"

"It means we need to check if the lemons are good to eat," her mom replied.

Lily and her mom squeezed the lemons to see if they were juicy and smelled good. They found out that some were good and some were bad. They threw away the bad ones and kept the good ones to eat.

Lily was happy because she got to eat the good lemons. She said to her mom, "These lemons are so good! Thank you, Mommy!"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Sarah. She loved to paint, and enjoyed looking for pebbles and painting them with bright colours. 

One day, Sarah found a broken pebble. She thought it was a shame that this pebble was broken, so she wanted to make it look nice. She grabbed her paints and started to paint the pebble. 

When she finished, the pebble was a beautiful rainbow of colours! It looked so much better than when she had found it. Sarah was so proud of her work and she decided to show it to her mum.

"Look Mum," said Sarah. "I painted this broken pebble, now it's a rainbow like the one in the sky!"

Sarah's mother smiled at her daughter and said, "That's wonderful Sarah. You put some lovely colours on that pebble. Well done!" 

Sarah was very happy and she now had a beautiful rainbow pebble to show all her friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sally. She loved to eat jelly. One day, her mommy made a big jar of yummy jelly. Sally was very happy. She wanted to share the jelly with her friends at school. Her mommy said, "That's a fair idea!"

The next day, Sally woke up late. She was in a hurry to go to school. She forgot to take the jelly with her. When she got to school, her friends were sad. They were looking forward to the jelly. Sally felt bad. She knew she had to make it right.

After school, Sally went home and told her mommy what happened. Her mommy helped her make more jelly. The next day, Sally remembered to take the jelly to school. Her friends were so happy. They all enjoyed the jelly together. Sally learned that it's important not to forget things, especially when it comes to sharing with friends.

Once upon a time there lived two best friends, Alex and Ella. They enjoyed playing together at Alex's house, under the big tree in the garden. 

This day they decided to play a special game. Alex told Ella that they were going to decorate the tree. Ella asked: "What's decorate?" 

Alex smiled and said: "We are going to make it look pretty. We will include lots of ornaments." 

Ella giggled and asked: "What's an ornament?" 

Alex said: "You will see. Let's go look for the decorations!" 

So the two friends went off in search of ornaments. They found colorful ribbons, pieces of cloth, and glittering stones. They included them all on the tree, until it was beautiful!

When the friends were finished Ella said: "It looks so calm and pretty!" Alex smiled and said: "Yes, it does!"

And from that day on this tree was the calmest and happiest place in the garden.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny named Floppy. Floppy loved to play outside in the dirt with his friends. One day, Floppy's mom told him to come inside and take a bath because he was very dirty. Floppy didn't want to take a bath because he was having too much fun playing with his friends.

Later that night, Floppy went to bed feeling worried. He started to think about all the dirt on him and how he didn't take a bath. He was afraid his mom would be mad at him. Floppy couldn't sleep because he was too worried.

The next day, Floppy woke up feeling very sick. His mom took him to the doctor and they found out that he had gotten very sick from all the dirt on him. Floppy felt very sad because he didn't listen to his mom and take a bath. From that day on, Floppy always made sure to take a bath and stay clean.

Once upon a time there was a little boy named Jack. He was a very curious boy who always wanted to explore the world outside.
One day, much to his delight, his mother decided to let him go out. Jack was so excited! He went outside and saw a white pastry on the ground. He wanted so badly to try the pastry but his mother warned him not to. She said, "No Jack! You must prevent eating that pastry!"

Jack was very curious, so even though his mother warned him he still wanted to try the pastry. He asked his mother again, and she said, "No Jack! We don't know where it comes from and it is not safe to eat it." 

Jack was disappointed, but he understood why his mother wouldn't let him try the pastry. He looked at the white pastry longingly before he went back inside with his mother.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside in his backyard. One day, Timmy saw a soldier walking down the street. The soldier had a big hat and a big gun.

Timmy asked the soldier, "What are you doing here?" The soldier said, "I'm here to protect our country." Timmy thought that was very cool.

Later that day, Timmy found a disgusting bug in his backyard. It scared him! He ran to his mom and said, "Mommy, there's a disgusting bug in the backyard!" His mom came to look and said, "Don't worry, I'll take care of it."

Timmy felt better knowing his mom would protect him from the scary bug. Just like the soldier was protecting their country.

Once there was a wide river that ran through a mysterious forest. A 3 year old girl named Laura wanted to explore the forest, but her Momma shook her head, warning her that the river was too wide and dangerous to cross. But Laura wanted to explore all the same and sneakily began to make plans. 

One sunny day Laura snuck out early in the morning and climbed down a tall tree to get to the water's edge. She smiled when she saw it sparkle in the sunlight and wanted to jump in and explore. But before she could do that, she saw a big black animal. Its eyes were already fixed on her and it did not look pleased.

"What do you want?" Laura asked, her tiny voice shaky with fear.

The creature said, "I have been waiting here for ages and no one has heeded my warning. If you try to cross me, you will get wet. I can't let you do that."

Laura smiled and asked, "What do I need to do?" 

"Wash me" the creature said mysteriously.

Laura didn't understand what that meant, but she knew she had to try something. She found some stones by the shore and started to wash the creature until it was gleaming in the sunlight. 

When she was finished, the creature smiled. "Now you can cross this river, but be careful." 

Laura thanked

Once there was a little mouse called Peanut. He loved to spin around and around until he felt so dizzy. He would spin on the furniture, with his friends and even on the ground!

One day, Peanut decided to spin on the filing cabinet in his house. He spun it so fast that he knocked all the filing papers off and scattered them everywhere.

When he saw what he had done, Peanut was so sad. He felt guilty for making such a mess. He quickly gathered all of the files and put them back in the cabinet.

Peanut learned an important lesson that day - it's so much better to have fun without being reckless! Always be careful when spinning because being dizzy isn't worth the mess you might make!

One day, a little boy named Tim went with his mom to the park. They saw a smooth slide that Tim wanted to try. Tim felt so excite to go down the slide. He ran to the slide and climbed up the steps.

"Ready, set, go!" Tim shouted as he slid down the smooth slide. He laughed and clapped his hands. "Mom, can I go again?" he asked.

"Yes, you can go again," Mom said with a smile. Tim went down the slide many times. He was so happy to play at the park. After a while, Mom said it was time to go home. Tim was tired but he didn't want to leave yet.

"Please, Mom, can I slide one more time?" Tim asked. Mom nodded and Tim went down the slide one last time. As they walked home, Tim couldn't wait to come back to the park and play on the smooth slide again.

Billy went out of his house to the beach. He was very excited. He put on his swimming suit and he couldn't wait to get into the water.

Billy saw a mighty mailbox that the birds had built. He ran over to it, and looked inside. There was a note inside! Billy opened it up and read it.

"Would you like to go swimming?" the note said. Billy smiled. He knew exactly what to do.

He ran back to the beach, took a deep breath, and hopped into the water. He started swimming as fast as he could, moving his arms back and forth. He felt so free in the water!

Suddenly, he heard a voice. It was the birds in the mighty mailbox! They were cheering him on.

"You're doing great, Billy!" they said.

Billy kept swimming, feeling happy and strong. He enjoyed his mighty swim in the ocean.

Ben and Lily were playing with their toy cars on the floor. They made loud noises and zoomed their cars around. They had a lot of fun.

Mom was in the kitchen, making a cake. She needed to be quiet and careful, because the cake was difficult to make. She did not want to disturb the cake or it would be a wreck.

But Ben and Lily were too noisy. They did not hear Mom when she asked them to be quiet. They did not see Mom when she came to the door. They only saw their toy cars.

Mom tripped over a toy car and dropped the cake. The cake fell on the floor and broke into pieces. It was a wreck. Mom was sad and angry.

"Ben! Lily! Look what you did!" Mom shouted. "You disturbed the cake and made it a wreck! This cake was difficult to make and now it is ruined!"

Ben and Lily stopped playing and looked at Mom. They saw the cake on the floor and felt sorry. They did not mean to make Mom sad and angry.

"We are sorry, Mom," Ben and Lily said. "We did not know you were making a cake. We did not want to disturb you or the cake. We were just playing."

Mom sighed and hugged Ben and Lily. She was still sad and angry, but she loved them.

"I know you were just playing, but you need to be more careful and quiet," Mom said. "The cake was for Dad's birthday. Now we have no cake."

Ben and Lily thought for a moment. They had an idea.

"Mom, we can help you make a new cake," Ben said.

"Yes, Mom, we can help you and be quiet and careful," Lily said.

Mom smiled and nodded. She was glad that Ben and Lily wanted to help.

"Okay, let's make a new cake together," Mom said. "But first, we need to clean up this mess."

Ben and Lily agreed and helped Mom clean up the wreck. Then they went to the kitchen and made a new cake. They were quiet and careful and did not disturb the cake. The cake was not difficult to make with their help. It was beautiful and delicious. Dad was happy and surprised when he saw the cake. He thanked Mom and hugged Ben and Lily. They all had a happy birthday party.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a kind boy named Tim. Tim loved to help people. One day, Tim's mom told him about a game. She said, "If you do something good and repeat it every day, you will get a reward."

Tim was very excited about the reward. He thought hard about what good thing he could do. The next day, Tim saw an old lady with a heavy bag. He helped her carry the bag to her house. The old lady was very happy and said, "Thank you, Tim!"

Tim remembered the game and decided to repeat helping the old lady every day. He carried her heavy bag to her house each day. On the last day of the week, the old lady gave Tim a big reward. It was a huge bag of candy! Tim was very happy and learned that being kind and repeating good things brings rewards.

Once upon a time, there was a little person who played in the park every day. One day, while running around, the person lost something very important. He looked around, but he couldn't find it.

The person saw another person walking by and asked, "Did you see where I lost it?" 

The other person answered, "No, but I can help you look. What did you lose?"

The little person said, "I lost my ball. It's a big, green one."

The two people searched together, but they couldn't find it. Finally the other person said, "I have an idea. Why don't we go a bit slower, and take turns calling for it?"

The little person agreed and the two people started walking around and calling for the lost ball. After a few minutes, the little person heard a faint call from one direction. He listened carefully and heard his ball!

The person followed the sound and finally saw where it had rolled. He picked it up and smiled. He was so happy to have found it. He thanked the other person for helping him look and promised to always walk a bit slower to keep an eye out for things he might lose.

There was a tall girl. She loved doing chores. One day, she found a dishwasher. It was very shiny. She was very excited. She opened it to see what was inside. It was full of dishes! She was so happy. She put on some gloves and started washing the dishes. She went up and down, scrubbing them clean. After she was done, she put the dishes away. She felt so proud of her work. She enjoyed the feeling of accomplishment. The girl had a great time spending time with the dishwasher. It was a special day.

One day, mommy and daddy took Tom to the park. Tom was very happy. He saw some birds flying in the sky and some squirrels running around. Then he saw something shiny on the ground. It was a copper penny! Tom shouted with delight and ran to pick it up.

Mommy smiled at him and said, "Let's organize your penny with the others!"

Tom ran back over to where his parents were sitting. They had a jar there with other pennies in it. Tom carefully put his penny in the jar and Daddy said, "Let's add another penny to it every day and by the end of the year, we'll have a nice collection. We can be happy together!"

Tom smiled and hugged his parents. He was so lucky to have such a great family. He couldn't wait to organize more pennies with them!

Once upon a time, there was a brave boy named Fred. Fred was on a big adventure in his small, red car. Suddenly, he heard a loud yell for help. Fred rushed to find where the noise was coming from. 

When he arrived, Fred saw a package that was stuck in a big, red tree. The package was making the noise! The package had dropped from a plane high in the sky and it was trapped in the branches of the tree but couldn't get back down.

Fred was determined to rescue the package. He climbed up the trunk of the tree and carefully reached out for the package. After struggling for a few minutes, he finally grabbed it and brought it safely down.

When the package was on the ground again, Fred opened it up. Inside the package, he found a bag of bitter candy. So even though the rescue was difficult, Fred was glad he was able to help. He knew the package was needed and was happy he could rescue it.

Sam and Mia were playing in the park. They saw a big dog with brown fur and a long tail. The dog ran to them and barked.

"Hello, doggy!" Sam said. He wanted to pet the dog.

"No, Sam, don't!" Mia said. She was scared of the dog. She thought the dog might bite them.

The dog came closer and sniffed Sam's head. Sam laughed and touched the dog's nose. The dog licked Sam's face and wagged his tail.

"See, Mia, he is nice!" Sam said. He hugged the dog.

Mia was still scared. She hid behind a tree and watched. The dog saw Mia and ran to her. He jumped on her and chewed her hair.

"Help, Sam, help!" Mia cried. She felt the dog's teeth on her head.

Sam ran to Mia and pulled the dog away. He said to the dog, "No, bad doggy! Don't chew Mia's head! That hurts!"

The dog looked at Sam and Mia. He tilted his head and whined. He did not mean to hurt Mia. He wanted to play with them.

Sam and Mia saw the dog's sad eyes. They felt sorry for the dog. They patted the dog and said, "It's okay, doggy. We are not mad at you. But you have to be gentle. Don't chew our heads. Chew this instead."

They gave the dog a stick. The dog took the stick and wagged his tail. He chewed the stick and ran around. Sam and Mia laughed and played with the dog. They were not scared anymore. They made a new friend.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the sunshine with her friends. One day, they decided to have a picnic in the park. 

Lily's mommy made her a sandwich and gave her a drink in a fancy cup. "Wow, this cup is so pretty!" said Lily. "Yes, it's expensive, so be careful with it," replied her mommy. 

As they were eating, Lily's friend Billy accidentally knocked over the cup and it fell onto a spike on the ground. "Oh no, my cup!" cried Lily. "Don't worry, we can get you a new one," said her mommy. 

After the picnic, they went to the store and found a new cup that was just as pretty. Lily was so happy and took a big drink from it. "Mmm, this drink is yummy!" she exclaimed.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She wanted to play but her mom said it was time for exercise. So the little girl hung a light rope from the ceiling. She loved to swing and twirl around! She laughed and smiled as she felt the rope move with her. 

When she was finished, she hung the rope back on the ceiling. Then her mom said it was time for some more exercise. So the little girl started jumping around! She loved how it made her feel light and happy. She laughed and jumped until she felt tired.

When she was done, she hung the rope back up on the ceiling. She was ready for a nap, so she said goodnight to her rope and went off to sleep. She had a wonderful time exercising and hanging from her light rope. The End.

Once upon a time, there was a flower that wanted to go on an adventure. It peeked out of its home, a garden, and saw a beautiful world that it wanted to explore. With careful steps, it slowly began to display its travels.

A little ant watched the flower carefully, and a butterfly flew past and waved. Then the flower found a big pond full of fish. The colors were so bright and the fish swam so fast!

Suddenly, the flower saw a rainbow in the sky. It felt so excited and the colors were so beautiful! The flower decided to roam around some more, so it kept on displaying.

Soon, the flower found another garden. It was full of colorful flowers and looked so inviting. The flower loved the view, and wanted to stop and take a rest.

So it carefully tucked itself amongst the other flowers and admired its beauty. After a while, it thought about how it could display its appreciation. With one big smile, the flower put out its petals and showed the garden its biggest thank you.

Once upon a time, there was an iron. It was very powerful. It could burn anything.

One day, a little girl, who was only three years old, saw the iron. She tried to pick it up, but it was too heavy.

The girl asked her mommy, "What is this big, heavy thing?"

Her mommy said, "It's an iron. People use it to burn clothes."

The little girl's eyes got wide. She thought it was magical!

"But don't touch it," her mommy warned. "It's too powerful for you."

The little girl knew her mommy was right. But she still liked to watch the iron burn clothes. She thought it was very cool.

Once upon a time, there was a brave boy. He liked to do brave things, like skipping rocks and climbing trees. One day, his mom said that she wanted to buy something special for him. The boy was so excited! He begged her to tell him what it was, but she just smiled and said he would have to wait and see.

So the brave boy waited. He thought and thought about what his mom could be buying for him. He just couldn't figure it out.

Finally, his mom took him to the store. She opened her purse and said, "Now I will buy it! Are you ready?" The boy was so excited! She pulled a new bike out of the store and handed it to him. What a surprise!

The brave boy was so pleased and thankful for his mom. He quickly got on the bike and took a ride around the block. Everyone clapped and cheered for the brave boy and his new bike. He had been so brave and patient while waiting to find out what his mom was going to buy.

Grandpa was sitting in his big chair, eating popcorn and watching TV. He was a little deaf, so he had to turn the volume up high.

Suddenly, Grandpa stopped talking, and started to nod. Grandma was in the kitchen and saw Grandpa nodding. She came over and said, "What are you nodding about, Grandpa?" 

Grandpa carefully took a piece of popcorn and smiled. He said, "Oh, I was just thinking about how happy I am for you and Grandma. You two are so sweet together." Grandma smiled, and nodded back. 

Grandpa put down the popcorn and said, "Let's go for a walk in the park if you want. We can eat some popcorn and talk about old times." Grandma smiled and nodded again. 

Off they went, into the park, sharing a bag of popcorn and chatting away. They listened to the birds chirping, laughed, and enjoyed the warm sun. Grandma and Grandpa were so happy - and not a bit deaf anymore.

Harry was very hungry. He wanted to eat a potato for dinner. But he was nervous about cooking it. He had never cooked a potato before. 

His mom saw him looking nervous and said, "Don't worry Harry. Cooking a potato isn't hard. Let me show you how." 

Harry was very excited. He watched as his mom put the potato in the pot and filled it up with water. She then put the pot on the stove and turned it on. 

After a few minutes, his mom checked the potato. "It's ready!", she said. But Harry wanted to wait a little bit. He wanted the potato to be extra cooked. 

His mom smiled and said, "Ok, no problem. We can delay a bit longer to cook the potato." 

Harry was so happy. Before he knew it, dinner was ready. It was the best potato he ever tasted.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat food, especially pizza and ice cream. One day, Lily's mom took her to a famous restaurant where they had the best pizza in town. Lily was so happy and she ate a lot of pizza.

After they finished eating, Lily's mom asked her, "Do you want to pray before we leave?" Lily nodded her head and closed her eyes. She prayed to thank God for the yummy food and for her family.

As they walked out of the restaurant, Lily said to her mom, "That was the best pizza ever! Can we come back here again?" Her mom smiled and said, "Of course, we can come back anytime you want." Lily was so happy and couldn't wait to eat more delicious food at the famous restaurant.

Once upon a time, there was a small boy named Toby. Toby was very curious, and he wanted to explore the world around him. One day, he was playing in the park with his friends when he noticed a strange thing in the corner. It was a cooler! Toby touched the cooler, and it felt very cool and smooth.

Suddenly, Toby saw something even more exciting. It was a small black bug! Toby got closer, and he touched it very carefully. The bug felt like a tiny pet, and Toby was so happy! He wanted to take the bug home.

Toby asked his mom if he could take the bug home with him, and she said yes! Toby carefully put the bug in the small cooler and took it home with him. When he got home, he was so excited to have a new pet. Toby and the bug played together for a long time and Toby was the happiest he had ever been.

Once upon a time there was a gentle cage. Inside the cage was a small sack. The sack was filled with all kinds of things. The little sack danced around the gentle cage every day. Every evening the little sack would open itself up and out of it would come a hundred bright stars. The stars shone so brightly that it lit up the night sky. The gentle cage and the little sack made the most beautiful display of stars twinkling in the night sky. Everyone was in awe of the night sky and the beauty it created. The little sack would then put away the stars until the next night. The little sack and the gentle cage always shared a special bond and created a beautiful starry night for everyone to enjoy.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Jane who had a pet. It was a furry dog called Rusty. Every morning, Jane would wake up early and play with Rusty in the backyard.

She would whisper to him and tell him lots of stories. Rusty always seemed to understand and listen eagerly. Jane would then make sure he was ready for their daily walk around the block before they had breakfast.

Sometimes, Jane would get so excited shouting and playing with Rusty, that he would bark out loud. But when it was time for her to go inside for dinner, she would just whisper to him softly because she knew he always liked that. He would lay his head on his paws and listen intently to her until she finished. It was the perfect way to end the day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Emma. She was three years old and liked to spend her time playing and exploring.

One day Emma went for a walk with her mum. When they arrived at the park, Emma saw something sparkly on the ground. It was a mineral! Emma was so excited and clapped her hands. She asked her mum if she could pick it up and keep it. Her mum said yes, and they got back home.

When they arrived, Emma put the mineral on a shelf in her bedroom. She wanted it to be tidy, so she tidied up all around it.

Then Emma sat down and looked at her mineral. She was so proud of it, and clapped her hands again. She kept it in her room for many years, and always made sure it stayed tidy.

One day, a little girl named Jane was out exploring near the lake. As Jane peeked around, she saw a boat floating on the lake. She thought it looked like fun and wanted to explore the boat. 

As she got closer, she noticed it was a fancy boat. She asked her mom if they could get it, and her mom said, â€œNo, itâ€™s probably too spoiled.â€ 

Jane was disappointed, but started to come up with a plan. She said, â€œMom, maybe we can peek inside and see if it would be okay.â€ 

Her mom thought about it for a moment and then said, â€œOkay, letâ€™s take a look.â€ 

So, Jane and her mom went on board the boat and to their surprise, everything was in good condition. The boat was not too spoiled after all. 

Jane was overjoyed, she hugged her mom and thanked her for giving her the chance to peek. 

Jane and her mom spent the rest of the day exploring the lake in the boat, and Jane was so glad she asked to take a peek.

Lily and Ben like to play in the garden. They see many flowers and bugs. They see a big tree with a hole. They hear a loud buzz.

"What is that?" Lily asks.

"Maybe it is a hive," Ben says. "Hive is where bees live. Bees make honey."

Lily and Ben want to see the hive. They go near the tree. They see a round thing with many bees. It is yellow and brown.

"Wow, look at the hive!" Lily says. "It is so big!"

"Can we get some honey?" Ben asks. "I like honey. It is sweet."

Lily and Ben try to get closer to the hive. They do not see the thin branch on the ground. They step on it. It makes a snap.

The bees hear the snap. They get angry. They fly out of the hive. They chase Lily and Ben.

"Ouch, ouch, ouch!" Lily and Ben cry. "The bees sting us!"

They run away from the hive. They run to the house. They find their mom.

"Mom, mom, help us!" Lily and Ben say. "The bees sting us!"

Mom sees the red spots on their skin. She hugs them. She puts some cream on their spots.

"Shh, shh, it is okay," Mom says. "The bees are gone. You are safe."

Lily and Ben feel better. They learn a lesson.

"Next time, we will not go near the hive," Lily says.

"Yes, we will leave the bees alone," Ben says.

They smile at Mom. They say sorry. They hug Mom. They love Mom.

Once upon a time, there was a strong boy named Tom. Tom loved to lift things. He would lift his toys, his books, and even his little sister. One day, Tom found a big boot in the yard. It was very, very big. He wanted to show his friend, Sam.

Tom called Sam and said, "Come see what I found! It's a big boot!" Sam came running to see the boot. They both looked at it and thought it was very funny. They tried to lift the boot together, but it was too heavy.

Tom and Sam asked their friend, Lily, to help them lift the boot. With all their strength, they lifted the boot high in the air. They were very proud of themselves. They played with the boot all day and had lots of fun. The three friends were always strong together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to learn new things, so her mommy took her to a school where they teach little kids like her. The school was very cheap, so mommy was happy.

Lily learned many things at school, like how to count and how to say her ABCs. But one day, she forgot to shut the door of her classroom when she went outside to play. When they came back inside, they saw that a bird had flown in and was flying around the room!

The teacher quickly shut the door and told the kids to be quiet. She then taught them how to catch a bird safely and they all worked together to catch it. After that day, Lily always remembered to shut the door tightly when she left the classroom.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Buddy. Buddy lived in a calm house with his family. Every day, Buddy would play outside with his friends.

One day, Buddy and his friends wanted to scare each other for fun. They took turns hiding and jumping out to say, "Boo!" Buddy was very good at hiding, so he scared his friends the most.

Buddy's friend, a small cat named Whiskers, said, "I want to try to scare you, Buddy!" So, Buddy closed his eyes and let Whiskers hide. When Buddy opened his eyes, he looked around for Whiskers. But Whiskers was very good at hiding too, and Buddy could not find him.

"Boo!" Whiskers jumped out from behind a tree, and Buddy got a big scare. They both laughed and played together until it was time to go home.

From that day on, Buddy and Whiskers had a new game to play together. They loved to scare each other and have fun with their friends. And even though they got scared sometimes, they knew it was all in good fun, and they felt safe and happy in their calm homes.

Tommy was so excited. He had never had a pet before. His mom told him that today they were going to get a new kitten. On the way to the pet store, Tommy kept looking out the window. He saw lots of big trees and other houses.

When they arrived, Tommy couldn't believe how many kittens were in the store. He saw white ones, black ones and even striped ones. Finally, he chose a cute orange and white kitten. 

The shopkeeper said to Tommy, "Now, remember to give her lots of love. She's very big for a kitten."

As Tommy played with his new kitten, he asked his mom what should he call her. She said, "Why don't you name her Tippy?" 

Tommy liked that and said, "I love my little Tippy!" He hugged his kitten and then went in search of a box to keep Tippy in. Soon he found an old shoe box and said, "Tippy can stay in here with me." He closed the top of the box gently so Tippy wouldn't get scared.

Then Tommy smiled and said, "We are going to have lots of fun together!"

Once upon a time there was a fly. The fly wanted to measure how far it could fly. So it started to flap its wings and flew up high in the sky. It flew and flew until it could not see the ground. It was grateful that it had wings to help it measure how far it could fly.

Then the fly started to fly down again. When it was close to the ground again, the fly was so happy that it had measured its own journey!

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She loved to ride her bike in the park. One day, she saw a lady with a pretty perfume bottle. Lily asked if she could smell it. The lady said yes and opened the bottle. The perfume smelled like flowers and made Lily happy.

Later, Lily tried to ride her bike, but it wouldn't go. She felt frustrated and didn't know what to do. Then, she remembered her dad told her to check the tires. She saw that they were flat and needed air. Lily asked her dad to help her and he did. After that, she rode her bike happily again.

Sandy was a curious and adventurous three-year-old. Every morning, Sandy and her mom would walk to the store for breakfast.

At the store, Sandy saw a box of cereal with a picture of an exciting roller coaster. "Mommy, what's that?" she asked, pointing at the box.

Her mother smiled. "That's a cereal," she said. "It's called 'Adventurous Flakes'. Do you want to try it?"

Sandy nodded eagerly. Her mother put the cereal in their basket and they headed for home.

Once home, Sandy grabbed a bowl, poured in the cereal, and added some milk. She tasted it and her face lit up. "It's delicious!" she exclaimed.

Her mother smiled again. "Yes, I recommend Adventurous Flakes. It's a nice way to start the day." 

Sandy finished the cereal and hopped down from the chair. "Mommy, can we get Adventurous Flakes every day?" she asked.

Her mother laughed. "Sure," she replied. "It sounds like it's your new favorite!"

Once upon a time there was a witch. She was very bossy and wanted everyone to do exactly as she said. One day in the woods, the witch said, "Let's pass through this path!" Everyone did as the bossy witch said and began to pass through the path.

As they went, the witch saw a little rabbit. She waved her wand and said, "Hop ahead of us!" But the rabbit wouldn't move. The witch was not happy. She kept waving her wand and said, "Come on, Hop! Hop now!" The rabbit still wouldn't move.

The witch got really angry. She waved her wand again, jumped in the air and said, "Hop very fast now!" Finally, the rabbit hopped very fast and everyone passed through the path.

The witch smiled and everyone was happy. They all thanked the bossy witch for her help and went on their way.

Once upon a time, there was a bright and curious cat. His name was Max.
One day Max was out exploring when he stumbled upon an interesting building. He went inside and found a computer! Max knew nothing about computers, but he was determined to learn.

Max started to press some of the buttons on the computer. A voice suddenly said: "Hi Max! Follow me and I will show you how to use the computer". The voice was coming from the computer!

Intrigued, Max followed the computer's instructions. The computer taught him how to type, how to use the mouse, and how to search the internet. Max was so excited he could learn about computers!

As Max continued to follow the computer's instructions and explore the world of computers, he grew brighter and brighter. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to cook pancakes with her mom. One day, Lily wanted to make a big pancake for her dad's birthday. But, when she tried to flip the pancake, it broke into pieces.

Lily started to cry and her mom came to see what happened. "What's wrong, Lily?" her mom asked.

"I can't make a big pancake for dad's birthday," Lily said, wiping her tears.

"Don't worry, Lily. We can join the pieces back together and make a tight pancake," her mom said with a smile.

So, they worked together to join the broken pieces of the pancake and make it tight. Lily was so happy that she could still make a pancake for her dad's birthday. And her dad loved the pancake so much that he ate it all in one bite!

Ruben was walking in the park on that fine morning. He was whistling a happy tune. Suddenly, he heard a noise. "What's that?" he asked himself.

Suddenly, the sky turned dark and the wind started to blow. Then, a hurricane came! All the birds flew away and the leaves whirled around. Ruben was scared!

But then, he heard a whistle. He turned his head and saw an old man. The man was wearing a yellow hat and a long, grey cloak. He was smiling at Ruben and he was also whistling.

Ruben felt calmer and he whistled back at the old man. Then, the hurricane stopped and the sky became clear and blue. Ruben was happy and the old man smiled. "The hurricane is gone now," said the old man, "Everything is fine."

Once there was a little boy who loved to explore. One day, he was walking through the woods when he spotted something interesting. It was a skeleton! He was so excited. He had never seen one before, so he decided to investigate.

He went closer and noticed that the skeleton was holding something. It was a bottle! He thought it must contain something special, so he picked it up.

The boy took the bottle, but suddenly, a scary voice said:

"That's mine!"

The boy was frightened and said, "I'm sorry! I just wanted to take a look!"

The voice said, "No, it's not for looking. It's for drinking."

The boy looked around and realised that the voice belonged to an old man who was standing next to a nearby tree.

The old man told the boy that he used to be an adventurer and the bottle contained a magical drink that gave him the strength and courage to explore. Now, he wanted to give it to the little boy so he could have the same courage.

The boy was so excited. He thanked the old man and drank the magical drink. It was so yummy. Now, he felt even more brave and ready to explore the woods.

Once upon a time there was a poor queen. She didn't have many nice things and lived a lonely life. One day while walking in the forest, she met a small child. The child looked sad, so the queen stopped to ask why. The child said she was looking for her family, but she did not know how to find them. The queen was kind, and offered the child help. 

Over the next few days, the queen helped the child search the area. Finally, the child found her parents. She was very happy, but the queen was still sad. The child said thank you to the queen and embraced her with a hug. Being hugged made the queen smile and she knew she was doing the right thing. 

The family then thanked the queen for her help and invited her to stay with them. The queen accepted, and she soon started to recognize the family as her own. She never felt so happy before. From that day on, the queen was part of the family and felt like she belonged. The poor queen now had family, and she was very pleased.

Once upon a time there was a young pig. She wanted to measure how tall she was. She started to measure so she could find out. She used a stick and placed it on the ground. Then she stood up beside it. She measured again, and she was very tall! The pig was happy and she knew that she was growing every day. She shared her news with all the other young pigs and showed them how she measured herself. They all wanted to measure too! They measured each other and found out that all the young pigs were growing taller. They were so excited and ran around celebrating their growth. The young pig was happy to have all her friends around her, and they were all very proud of their measurements.

Once upon a time, there was a beautiful princess. This princess had an amazing chest. Inside the chest was something special. For hours and hours every day, the princess would raise the lid and look inside.

Once, when the princess opened the chest, she saw a perfect diamond. It was her most treasured item. She kept this precious diamond in the chest and made sure to take good care of it.

The princess wanted to make sure the diamond stayed perfect so by day she used sunshine to help it sparkle and by night she used moonlight to help it shine.

Every day, the princess would admire the diamond and she was proud of her perfect chest. She knew nothing could ever beat it.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his rubber ball. He would bounce it up and down and all around. One day, Timmy's big sister came into his room and said, "Timmy, can I play with your ball?"

Timmy said, "Sure, you can play with it, but be careful. I don't want you to destroy it."

His sister bounced the ball and accidentally threw it too hard. It bounced off the wall and landed in a weird spot behind the dresser. Timmy's sister tried to reach it, but her arm was too short.

Timmy said, "Don't worry, I'll get it." He crawled behind the dresser and found the ball. It was a little squished, but it was still okay. Timmy and his sister continued to play with the ball until it was time for dinner.

Once upon a time there was a nosy pot. It could do lots of work all day but it was so nosy that it made the other items mad. The pot was always asking questions and always wanted to know what everyone else was up too.

One day while the pot was working in the kitchen, it noticed a large bowl on the counter. The pot asked the bowl why it wasn't doing any work and the bowl replied, "What makes you think I'm not? I'm holding these lovely apples and keeping them safe till its time for them to be eaten."

The pot paused and thought for a moment and then replied, "Oh! I'm sorry for asking. You are doing important work too."

The pot learned its lesson that day and from then on it kept its nosy nature in check.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Wendy who was three years old. She was very curious.

One day, Wendy found a mask. She was confused because she did not know what it was used for. She asked her mom, "Mom, what is this?" To which her mom replied, "Oh, it's a mask for playing dress up."

Wendy was so excited! She put on the mask and started to imagine she was someone else. She said to her mom, "Mom, can I play dress up?"

Her mom smiled and said, "Yes, but first you must have a nap."

Wendy was confused. She had never had a nap before. But she followed her mom's instructions, and soon fell asleep. After taking a long nap, Wendy was full of energy. She was ready to play dress up with her mask!

So, Wendy put on her mask, and began to imagine herself as a superhero. Her mom watched proudly, and soon enough, Wendy was full of smiles.

From that day on, Wendy nap with her mask on, and played dress up regularly. She was never confused about what the mask was used for ever again.

Once upon a time, there was a happy little bird named Tweet. Tweet loved to whistle and sing all day long. One night, Tweet had a nightmare and woke up feeling scared. But then Tweet remembered a cheerful song that always made him feel better. So Tweet started to whistle the song and soon felt happy again.

The next day, Tweet met a new bird friend named Chirp. Chirp was very cheerful and loved to sing too. Tweet and Chirp became best friends and would whistle and sing together all day long. They even made up a special song that they would whistle when they were feeling scared or sad.

From that day on, Tweet never had a nightmare again. Whenever he felt scared, he would just whistle his special song and feel cheerful once more. And with Chirp by his side, he knew he would never be alone.

One day, a human was walking down a street. She was ready to try something new. Suddenly, she felt an urge to do something different.

She stopped walking and asked a 3 year old nearby, "What should I do?"

The 3 year old smiled and said, "Let's go to the park!"

The human smiled and said, "That sounds like a great idea!" 

So, they walked over to the park. When they arrived, the 3 year old urged the human to try the swings. She then got onto one and spent the rest of the day having fun! 

The human had a wonderful time. Thanks to the 3 year old, she was able to experience something new and have a great time.

Once there was a little girl called Anna. Anna wanted to help her mom, so she said she wanted to carry herbs. Her mum said that she had to be very careful. 

Anna went outside and found some herbs in the garden. She picked them carefully and put them in a basket. She was very happy because she had helped. 

The next day, Anna went back to the garden. This time she was even more careful because her mom had asked her to be careful. She chose the freshest herbs and carried them back to the house in her basket. 

When she got home, her mom was very proud of her for being so careful. She used the herbs to make a delicious soup for the family to enjoy. 

Anna was so happy that she had helped her mum make a yummy meal. She had learned that being careful can be very helpful.

Cody was a little boy who lived in a small house with his mom. He loved exploring his neighborhood with his best friend, Simon. One day, Simon told him something very interesting. He said there was an old neighbor who was very wise and kind.

Cody was excited and wanted to meet the old neighbor. So they quickly went to the old neighbor's house to say hello. The neighbor greeted them with a big nod. He had a big smile on his face and seemed very welcoming.

The neighbor then asked them why they were there. Cody told him that Simon said he was a wise neighbor and they wanted to learn from his wisdom. The old neighbor was pleased and asked Cody and Simon to come back the next day. He said he had a special story to share with them.

The boys nodded with excitement and said goodbye to the old neighbor. The next day, after arriving at the old neighbor's house, the old neighbor began to tell a story about a wise wizard. He said the wizard learned about the importance of friendship and kindness from a young boy, similar to Cody, who was always kind to his neighbors.

Cody and Simon, amazed by this story, nodded in agreement. In the end, the old neighbor told the boys that being kind and wise was always the best choices. This moment was a lesson for Cody, who realized that being kind and having wise friends was the key to a happy life.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the green grass and look up at the blue sky. One day, she saw a beautiful butterfly with wings as red as a rose. She admired the butterfly and followed it as it flew from flower to flower.

Lily wanted to catch the butterfly and keep it as her own, but she knew that would not be kind. So, she decided to just watch it and enjoy its beauty. As she sat there, she felt hungry and remembered the buttered toast her mom had made for her. She ran inside and took a big bite of the warm, buttery bread.

As she ate, she thought about the butterfly and how lucky it was to have such pretty wings. Lily realized that even though she couldn't keep the butterfly, she could still admire it and be happy for its beauty. She went back outside with her buttered toast and watched the butterfly until it flew away.

Sara and Ben like to play in the park. They like to swing, slide and run. One day, they see a big hill with a hole. They want to see what is inside.

"Let's go in the hole!" Ben says.

"No, we should not go in the hole. Mommy and Daddy warn us to stay away from holes. They can be dangerous." Sara says.

But Ben does not listen. He runs to the hole and jumps in. Sara follows him. She does not want him to be alone.

They go down the hole and see a dark tunnel. They walk in the tunnel and see many bones. They are scared.

"Ben, these are skeleton bones. They are from people and animals that died. We should go back. This is not a good place to play." Sara says.

But Ben does not listen. He sees a big skeleton with a shiny thing in its hand. He wants to have the shiny thing.

"Look, Sara, a treasure! I want to take it." Ben says.

He runs to the skeleton and grabs the shiny thing. But the shiny thing is not a treasure. It is a trap. It makes a loud noise and the tunnel starts to shake. Rocks fall from the ceiling and block the way out.

"Ben, you are silly! You make the tunnel angry. Now we are stuck. We have no way out. We have no food, no water, no light. We are in an empty hole." Sara says.

She cries and hugs Ben. Ben cries and hugs Sara. They are sorry for not listening to Mommy and Daddy. They hope someone will find them and help them. They are very scared.

One day, a huge bird was sitting in a tree. The bird was alone and it looked very sad. 

A little boy saw the bird and wanted to say hello. He walked up to the tree and pointed at the bird. The bird then spread out its huge wings and looked right at the boy. The boy exclaimed in amazement. 

The bird flew down and landed right next to the boy. The boy was fascinated by the bird's tail which was enormous. He reached out and touched it very softly. The bird seemed to like it and started purring. 
 
The boy and the bird became friends. They played around for the rest of the day and the boy promised to come back tomorrow. 
The boy waved goodbye and the bird spread its huge wings and flew away.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside in the garden. One day, Timmy found a worm on the ground. The worm was wiggly and slimy, but Timmy thought it was cool.

Timmy's mom came outside and saw the worm in Timmy's hand. "Oh, that's a rare worm," she said. "It's not often we see worms like that around here."

Timmy was excited to show his mom the worm. "Mommy, look at this worm!" he said. "It's so wiggly!"

His mom smiled. "Can you whistle for me, Timmy?" she asked.

Timmy puckered his lips and tried to whistle. "I can't do it, Mommy," he said.

"That's okay, Timmy," his mom said. "Maybe one day you'll be able to whistle like a bird."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved to pretend. Every day, she would close her eyes and imagine all kinds of wonderful things. One day, she pretended to be a snake, winding through the grass and slithering away. 

The little girl's mom saw her, and decided to join in the fun. She grabbed a fragile stick from the ground and draped it across her back.

"Look Mommy!" the little girl said. "I'm pretending to be a snake now!"

Mommy laughed and said, "That's great! Are you going to be a scary snake or a friendly one?"

The little girl thought for a moment before responding. "I'm going to be the friendliest snake ever. That way I won't frighten anyone!" 

Mommy was proud of her little girl and gave her a hug.

"That's very wise," she said. "You can still have fun pretending to be a snake, but remember to be gentle and kind."

The little girl smiled and nodded her head, then went back to pretending to be a snake.

One day, a raven saw something very exciting. It was a modern dance! The raven wanted to join in, so it started to jump up and down. This caught the attention of some other birds who also wanted to dance! So they all began dancing together.

The birds moved around gracefully and joyfully, twirling in time to the music. Soon, more and more animals came to join in the modern dance. Each animal had their own unique way of moving.

The dance kept going on for hours. When it was done, the raven smiled. It had been a wonderful and exciting day. All of the animals knew that they had experienced something special together!

Once upon a time there lived a little girl who was very happy. She loved to laugh and play with her friends. One day, the little girl went to visit her grandmother. Her grandmother said she wanted to give her a big kiss. But the little girl refused and said she didn't want to.

The grandmother was very sad, so she gave the little girl a lecture about why she should always accept a kiss from her loved ones. The grandmother explained to the little girl how important it is to show love and affection so that we do not feel alone or unknown. 

The little girl understood her grandmother's lesson, so she hugged her, then she kissed her. 

The moral of this story is that we should always show love and affection for the ones we love so that we donâ€™t feel unknown or alone.

Lily and Ben are playing with their toys in the living room. Lily has a file that she found in her dad's office. She likes to pretend that it is a book with many stories. Ben has a fake phone that he got for his birthday. He likes to pretend that he is talking to his friends.

"Look, Ben, I have a file with many stories. Do you want to hear one?" Lily asks.

"OK, Lily, but first I have to make a call. Hello, hello, is this Sam?" Ben says into his fake phone.

Lily waits for Ben to finish his call. She opens the file and looks at the papers. She sees many words and numbers that she does not understand. She makes up her own stories based on the pictures and colors.

"Ben, are you done? I have a story for you. It is about a cat and a mouse. The cat is red and the mouse is blue. They are friends, but they like to play tricks on each other." Lily says.

"OK, Lily, I am done. Sam says hello. What is your story?" Ben says.

Lily tells Ben her story. She shows him the pictures in the file. She says that the cat and the mouse live in a big house with many rooms. She says that one day, the cat put a fake mouse in the mouse's bed. She says that the mouse was scared, but then he saw that it was a fake mouse. He laughed and said that the cat was funny. He decided to put a fake cheese in the cat's bowl. He said that the cat would be surprised, but then he would laugh too.

Ben listens to Lily's story. He likes the pictures and the colors. He says that the cat and the mouse are good friends. He says that he likes to play tricks on his friends too, but only for fun. He says that he and Lily are good friends too.

Lily and Ben smile at each other. They hug and say that they love each other. They put the file and the fake phone back where they found them. They go to play with their other toys. They are happy.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Sally. Sally liked to go to the garden and play.

One day, Sally saw a rake in the garden. She thought it was very interesting. She wanted to play with it. So she picked up the rake and made a game out of it.

Suddenly, it started to rain. Sally used the rake to lock the garden gate. She didn't want to get wet!

When the rain stopped, Sally put the rake back where she found it. She said goodbye to the garden, and ran off to play inside.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was very excited because today was her birthday party. Her mom had decorated the house with lots of balloons and streamers. Lily's friends came over and they all played games and ate cake.

After the party, Lily's mom asked her to help clean up. Lily wanted to help, so she took a big spoon and measured the leftover cake into containers. She was very proud of herself for helping her mom.

Later that night, Lily went to bed with a smile on her face. She thought about how charming her party was and how much fun she had with her friends. She fell asleep dreaming of the next party she would have.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He had a task to clean his room, but he didn't want to do it. He wanted to play with his toys instead. 

One day, something bad happened. Timmy's mom tripped on one of his toys and hurt her foot. She was very angry and sad. Timmy felt bad too. 

He realized that he should have listened to his mom and cleaned his room. He learned that it's important to do your tasks and be responsible. 

From then on, Timmy made sure to keep his room clean and modern, and he always did his tasks right away. He didn't want anything bad to happen again.

Once upon a time there was a little puppy named Sam. He was very friendly and loved by everyone. Every day, Sam went to the park to visit his friends. He was always so happy when he did. 

But one day when Sam went to the park, his friends had all gone home. Sam was so sad. His friends had promised to play with him but they didn't keep their promise. 

Sam was so disappointed but he eventually decided to never trust easily. He tried to remain friendly with everyone but he always made sure to check whether they meant it when they promised something. 

This made sure that Sam never got his heart broken when his friends had gone away for good. The moral of the story is to always remain friendly, but make sure to keep your promises too!

Once upon a time there was a strong fish in the big pond. Every day it loved to splash around in the cool water. One day, the fish came across a new texture in the pond. It felt so soft and squishy.

Excited, the fish asked "What is this?!"

A frog replied, "It's a lilly pad! You can rest here whenever you splash in the pond."

The fish was intrigued. It felt the soft, squishy texture again and hopped onto the lily pad. It enjoyed the strong feeling beneath its scales.

The fish and the frog hung out in the lily pad, splashing and playing in the pond. They had a lot of fun and became good friends.

The end.

Once upon a time, an old man went for a walk. He had a bag of money with him. 
The old man looked around and he saw a little boy. He said, "Let's play a game!" 
The man asked the boy to follow him. The little boy liked the game and was excited to go along. 
The old man and the little boy went through the streets, following the old man's path. 
Eventually they came to a very old building. The old man stopped and opened the door with his key. Inside, the old man showed the little boy the money. 
The oldman said, "Now you can keep this money and you can use it to buy something nice." 
The little boy was so happy! He thanked the old man and ran home, happy to have found some money.

Once upon a time, in a land far away, there lived a jolly fairy. She was always so happy and excited to visit tiny tots each day. On one bright, sunny day the fairy was travelling to pay a visit to little Amy.

As the fairy got closer to Amy's house, she started to feel very tired. She was so tired she had to take a break and she let out a big yawn. Little Amy, who was playing outside, heard the fairy yawning.

"Why are you so tired, fairy?" Amy asked curiously.

The fairy smiled and said, "I am so tired because I have a very special surprise for you tonight. You'll just have to wait and see!"

Later that night, Amy was already in bed when she heard a knock on her window. When she opened the curtains, there was the jolly fairy holding a present in her hands. It was the surprise she had been hinting at earlier in the day! 

Amy happily opened the present to find a sparkly wand. It was just as jolly as the fairy, shining brightly in the night sky. Little Amy had never felt so excited.

Amy thanked the fairy and waved goodbye. The fairy smiled and said, "Goodnight! I can't wait to see what you do with your new wand!" With that, the fairy flew away, excited to see what adventures it would bring to little Amy.

Once there was a boy named Tom. Tom was three years old. Tom was a very tough boy and he loved exploring his garden. One day while he was playing he suddenly saw something. It was a poppy!

Tom was shocked. He had never seen such a beautiful flower before. He knew he had to meet it. With great excitement, he crawled closer and closer to the poppy.

When he reached the poppy, he smiled and spoke softly. "Hello poppy," he said, "may I meet you?"

The poppy replied in a gentle voice, "Yes, Tom, you may meet me if you'd like."

Tom was surprised and delighted and he looked up at the poppy and thanked it. They spent the day together, talking and getting to know each other better. Tom learned that the poppy was really tough and could survive through anything.

Tom was very happy and he promised the poppy that he would come again soon to meet it and spend more time with his new friend.

Frankie was having a tidy afternoon in his room. He had put all his toys and books away and was very pleased with himself. Suddenly, his mother came in with a worried look on her face.

"Frankie," she explained, "there is some trouble outside, I need you to stay inside."

Frankie couldn't understand what was wrong, but he nodded and promised to stay in his room. He couldn't help but feel a little scared about the trouble his mother was talking about.

However, a few minutes later, there was a loud knock at the door. When Frankie's mother opened it, two friendly, tidy policemen were standing outside.

"Mrs. Johnson," they explained, "we got a call that you were in some troubleâ€¦ May we come in?" 

Frankie's mother thanked the policemen and quickly explained that everything was fine. She thanked them for their help and the two friendly, tidy policemen set off again.

Frankie was relieved that the trouble was gone. He smiled to himself, happy that his room was so tidy, and thankful that the trouble outside had been sorted out.

It was a modest evening. The sky was a calm and peaceful blue with a few friendly clouds.

The sun, who was ready to take a nap, started to dry up the dew on the grass. He made sure the ground was warm and cozy.

The birds were flying around, singing their evening songs. They were happy they had enough food before the sun dried up.

The animals started to nibble on their dinner too. A rabbit was chomping on some carrots, a squirrel was munching on some nuts and a fox was licking a bowl of creamy milk.

The sun soon said goodnight and left for a rest. The evening felt peaceful, just like the sky.

Once there was a puppy, who was so scared of everything. He was always so scared of new sights and sounds.

One day, while he was exploring the backyard, he saw something he'd never seen before. It scared him so he ran away. As he was running away, he felt something bite him in the leg.

He was so scared he ran back inside the house. He didn't want to go back outside again.

The next day, he went out to explore the yard again, but this time he was more careful. He kept an eye out for scary sights and he looked around for anything that might bite him.

He was much braver than before and eventually he didn't mind exploring the backyard anymore. He soon remembered that not all sights are scary and that sometimes things that bite can be friendly too.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside with his friends. One day, they decided to play a game with a flag. They would take turns holding the flag and running around the yard.

Timmy was very excited when it was his turn to hold the flag. He ran as fast as he could, but then he tripped and fell. The flag flew out of his hand and snapped in the wind.

Timmy's friends were worried, but Timmy was calm. He knew it was just an accident and that they could fix the flag. They all worked together to tape the flag back together, and soon they were back to playing their game. Timmy was happy that his friends were there to help him when he needed it.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys, but she was always careful not to break them. One day, she found a door with a big knob on it. She turned the knob and went inside.

Inside the room, she saw a big machine that was broken. The machine was used to make toys for children. Lily wanted to help, so she asked the machine what was wrong. The machine said that it needed a new part to work again.

Lily went on an adventure to find the missing part. She looked everywhere, and finally found it in a nearby store. She brought it back to the machine and fixed it carefully. The machine started to work again, and Lily was happy that she could help make toys for children. From that day on, Lily visited the machine every day to help it work and make toys for children.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily's mom bought a new rug for their living room. It was red and soft. Lily loved it.

But then, Lily's little brother came running in with muddy feet. He jumped on the rug and made it dirty. Lily's mom was angry and said, "We need to change this rug now!"

Lily helped her mom take the rug outside to shake off the dirt. While they were doing that, Lily saw a big, fierce dog walking down the street. She said to her mom, "Look at that fierce dog! I'm glad he's not in our house." 

After they cleaned the rug, Lily's mom put it back in the living room. It looked as good as new. Lily was happy to have her soft, red rug again.

Once upon a time, there was a jolly girl named Lily. Lily lived on a small island with her family. She loved to play with her friends and sing songs.

But, one day, a big storm came to the island. The wind blew and the rain fell. Lily and Tom were scared. They tried to find a safe place to hide. But the storm was too strong. The island was not safe anymore. Lily and Tom could not marry, and they were very sad.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Sue. She loved to play outside and look for animals in the garden. One day, she went to the lake with her family. As soon as she saw the lake she was so excited that she wanted to go for a swim. But, her mom said she couldn't because she was too little.

Sue felt very helpless. She watched as all the other children splashed in the water. She was so jealous! She wanted to go and have fun with them. But she couldn't because she was too little.

Suddenly, Sue saw a fish swimming in the lake. She was so amazed that she watched it for a long time. She wished that she could swim in the lake with the fish.

But, the little girl was still too little. She was helpless and could only stand, look and wish.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He had a toy car that he loved to play with. One day, he left his car outside and went inside to eat lunch. When he came back outside, his car was gone!

Timmy looked all around but couldn't find his car. He asked his mom for help, but she didn't know where it was either. Timmy was sad and didn't know what to do.

The next day, Timmy went outside to play and saw his toy car sitting on the front porch. He was so happy! He knew that his mom must have found it and put it there for him. Timmy gave his mom a big hug and said, "Thank you for being so useful!" From that day on, Timmy made sure to always stand his toys up and put them away so they wouldn't get lost again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She liked to draw and write in her journal. Her journal was a special book where she wrote about all the fun things she did every day.

Lily's mom was proud of her for writing in her journal. She said, "Lily, you are such a good writer! Keep writing about all the fun things you do." And Lily smiled, happy to have such a nice mom.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play in the park with his friends. One day, Timmy's ball rolled into the pond. Timmy couldn't swim and was scared. His friends didn't know what to do, so they went to get Timmy's mom.

Timmy's mom heard their urge for help and quickly ran to the pond. She saw Timmy struggling in the water and knew she had to rescue him. She jumped in and pulled Timmy out of the pond. Timmy's mom was happy that she could help, and Timmy was grateful to be safe.

After the incident, Timmy's mom explained to him the danger of water and why he shouldn't play near it. Timmy was ignorant of the danger before, but now he understood and promised to be more careful. From that day on, Timmy and his friends played in the park, but always stayed away from the pond.

One day, brave Toby was walking outside. He saw the sun shining brightly and he felt so hot. He thought to himself that he should find some shade to cool off in. But Toby wasn't a quitter - he was brave! So he kept walking until he saw a tree with a big branch overhanging the path. He looked up to the sun and back at the branch and thought to himself, "I can do this!". So he decided to climb the tree and he kept on going higher and higher until he reached the branch. As soon as he lay down on the branch, the sun shone even brighter! Toby was so happy - the shade kept him cool and he felt brave for conquering the tree. With a smile on his face, Toby stayed up in the tree until the sun went down.

Once there was a boy who was grumpy because his friends were playing a game without him! He went to his toy box full of things that he could play with, but he couldn't find the one he wanted. Suddenly, he saw a match box with a bright green design with yellow stars. He opened the box and inside he saw little wooden matches. 

He was so excited that he got to play with them. He began pointing to single matches and quickly found a curious game. He used the matches to make a tiny bridge over the kitchen table and started putting the matches in a line. He made it longer and longer until it became a very long bridge.

The boy was so proud of himself and laughed with glee. Suddenly he remembered that he was grumpy before and now he was laughing and playing. He realized that the simple match box was the exact thing he was looking for. He kept playing until his friends came back with the toy that he wanted - and he suddenly had a brilliant idea!

He pointed to the match box, smiled, and showed his friends the bridge he had made. All of them were amazed and instantly started to create their own bridges. The boy was no longer grumpy; he was happy knowing that the simple match box made everyone smile too.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Lucy. She was a very brave girl. One day, she saw something green on the ground. It was a belt! Lucy wanted to save it, so she picked it up. She took it home with her.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Emma and Anna. The two were best pals and always had a lot of fun together. Jenny was a 3 year old girl who lived with her family in a big house. She loved to wear her favourite dress; it was bright blue with white spots on it. Every morning, before she went to nursery, her mum helped her get dressed in her special dress.

One day, when Jenny was getting dressed, she asked if she could wear her favourite dress in the playground. Jenny's mum gently explained to her that it was a very busy playground and that her dress might get dirty while they were running and playing.

Mum smiled and said, "Of course, you should always value your things. But the playground is a busy place and sometimes it's best to wear something else so that your dress stays clean."
