Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat pasta, especially with tomato sauce. One day, her mom asked her to help her with the groceries. Lily was happy to help and carried a big sack of groceries all by herself.

As they were walking home, they saw a man who dropped his groceries on the ground. Lily's mom asked her to help the man pick up his things. Lily felt proud that she could help someone else.

After they finished helping the man, they went home and cooked the pasta. Lily's mom told her how proud she was of her for helping others. Lily learned that it's important to be kind and helpful to others, even if it means carrying a heavy sack of groceries.

Sophia was a grumpy 3 year old. She had a box filled with crayons.

Once upon a time, there was a loyal dog named Max. Max belonged to a family of three. Mom, dad and the 3 year old daughter, Lily. Ever day Lily would go outside to play with Max, and Max was the happiest dog in the world.

One day, Lily and Max had a plan. Lily wanted to make a special sauce for her family. "Let's get some ingredients from the store," she said to Max. So they put on their shoes and headed to the store.

When they got there, Lily picked up all the ingredients for the sauce and then the two headed home. 

When they got back, Lily got to work making her sauce. Max watched as Lily mixed and stirred all the ingredients together. After a few minutes, a delicious smell filled the kitchen.

"We did it!" said Lily, holding up the completed sauce proudly. "It's perfect. Thank you Max for helping me with my plan."

Max just smiled and wagged his tail. He was always loyal to Lily, no matter what!

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy who loved to play with his toy cars. One day, Timmy was playing with his red car and accidentally drove it into a wall. The car got a big scratch and the wheels stopped turning. 

Timmy's dad saw what happened and said, "Let's try to reverse the car and see if it works." They turned the car around and pushed it backwards. The wheels started turning again and the scratch disappeared! Timmy was so happy that his car was fixed.

Later that day, Timmy went to the park with his mom. They saw a group of people playing with sticks and hitting a little ball. Timmy asked his mom what they were doing and she said, "They are playing golf with a club." Timmy thought the club looked dull and didn't understand why anyone would want to play with it. 

As they were walking away, Timmy heard one of the golfers say, "I need to reverse my swing and hit the ball in the opposite direction." Timmy didn't know what that meant, but he knew it was important for the golfer to do.

Tommy was a 3 year old boy who loved to catch things. One day he was in the garden and he saw a pink radio lying on the ground. He was so excited and ran to pick it up.

Carly and her mom were outside, playing with Carly's new soccer ball. She kicked it around and smiled as she watched it fly. "Look, mommy!" Carly said, pointing to the ball.

Her mom applauded and praised her. "That was so cool! You have amazing kicking skills, Carly!"

Carly laughed and said, "Thanks, mommy! I guess I'm a natural!" She ran over and hugged her mom, who hugged her back. Even though it was only a game, she knew she had accomplished something special.

Ted and his friend Sam were walking on the beach.

"Listen!" said Sam.

Ted stopped and listened. He could hear the sound of the waves coming in.

"It's the tide," said Sam.

"What's the tide?" asked Ted.

"It's great! The tide is like a big wave that comes in and out," said Sam.

Ted smiled and watched the tide rolling in. He enjoyed the great sound of the wave.

Suddenly, they heard a loud boom. They looked up. The sky was sparkling with various colors.

"What's that?" asked Ted.

"It's fireworks," said Sam. "It looks great, doesn't it?"

Ted nodded, smiling. He had never seen anything so beautiful.

He listened to the boom of the fireworks until they slowly faded away and the tide rolled back out to the ocean.

One day, Bob saw a lock. He had never seen one before and he was curious. He reached forward to feel the edges and it made a click sound. Bob was a bit fearful, but he still wanted to open it. He looked around, but he didn't see anyone. He slowly and carefully twisted the lock and the lid opened with a loud creak! 

Inside he saw something sparkly, but he couldn't tell what it was. He felt around in the box, and he finally discovered some colorful stones. He excitedly brought them out and looked at them in the sunlight. 

He looked back at the lock and thought it was so cool. He didn't know how it worked, but he felt like he conquered something big. He put the box back and slowly closed the lid with a click. He smiled and moved away, feeling triumphant.

Once upon a time, there was an iron. It was shiny and impressive. Every day, the iron went around the town. It was a special iron because it had a very important job.

One day, Sam found some clay. He was so excited! He picked it up and ran over to the park.

Once upon a time, there was an incredible automobile. It had shiny wheels and a loud engine. Everyone who saw it said it was so cool.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat spaghetti, it was her favorite food. One day, Lily's mom made spaghetti for dinner. Lily was so impatient, she couldn't wait to eat it. She kept asking, "Is it ready yet?"

After dinner, Lily was so full she could barely move. She took a step towards her bedroom and fell asleep as soon as her head hit the pillow. From that day on, Lily asked for spaghetti every night and was always impatient for it to be ready.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Julia. She was always excited to play outside with her friends. One day when she went out to play, she saw a large pond. Julia was fascinated by the water and asked her friend, "What is that?" Her friend said, "It's a pond! You can dive into it!" Julia was so excited she just had to try. She asked her friend if they could do it together and soon they were running and diving into the pond!

The water felt nice and cool, and Julia laughed and played with her friend all afternoon. When the sun began to set, Julia got out of the water feeling quite tired. As she looked out at the pond, she saw a beautiful rainbow and smiled.

Julia was happy to have made a new friend that day. From then on, when the sun was setting, she would dive into the pond to see the rainbow. Every time, she felt more and more tired, but she still had fun every time.

Molly was jogging around the park one day in her orange t-shirt. She saw a mug on the ground so she stopped to pick it up.

Millie nodded and said, "Yes, please. Can I have it?" 

Molly nodded and said, "Yes, of course you can have it." 

Millie happily took the mug and thanked Molly. She ran off with the orange mug and continued with her jog around the park.

Once upon a time, there was a family who wanted to do something fun. They all decided to go to the hockey rink. When they arrived, it was very exciting. Everyone was wearing different things. There were some people wearing red shirts, blue pants and green shoes.

When everyone was ready, the game began. The two teams raced across the ice with their hockey sticks. They were playing all different kinds of tricks with the puck. It was a lot of fun to watch.

At the end of the game, the family was very happy. They had all enjoyed their fun time together. Everyone was excited to come back again and have another game of hockey. They all said goodbye and went home.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. Her name was Magu. Magu was three years old.

One day, Magu was walking down the street. The street was very long and bumpy. Magu wanted to rock to make the ride more fun.

Magu saw an old man on the street. She said, "Hi Mister! Can you help me rock?" 

The old man laughed. "You sure can," he said. 

The old man was very flexible. He showed Magu how to rock on the street! First, the old man showed Magu how to stand. Then, he showed her how to bend her knees and swing her arms. Magu rocked with the old man until they reached the end of the street. 

"Thank you Mister!" said Magu as she waved goodbye. She was so excited to rock on the street!

Once upon a time, there was a big, lazy octopus. It lived in a big box, filled with fun things to play with. Everyday, the octopus would reach in and pull out a surprise. One day, the octopus heard a noise coming from outside the box. It saw some people carrying it away from its home.

The octopus was afraid, but it soon realized that the people were actually helping it. The people unpacked the box and set the octopus free. The octopus felt excited! It was so happy to finally explore all the new places around it.

The octopus happily spent the day exploring and playing. As it watched the sunset, the octopus felt so content and relaxed. It went to its special spot and watched as the stars twinkled in the night sky.

The lazy octopus was so thankful to the people who unpacked it and gave it a chance to explore the world. The octopus gave them a big, sticky hug and said thank you.

Once there was a boy who loved to wander. He loved to find new places and explore them. One day, he went on an adventure. The boy brought his black wallet with him. While he was wandering, he found a new spot in the woods. He explored the area and found some interesting things. He kept collecting items in his wallet. Eventually, the day ended and he went home. He was so excited to show his parents all the things he found. The boy learned a lot on his wander and he wanted to go back and explore more.

Once upon a time, there were two friends: Bill and Jake. They were fun, happy and always playing together. One day they started a big, serious war. They began to run around outside, throw rocks and sticks at each other and make lots of noise.

The war went on for days and the two friends tried to be the toughest and prove who was the best. With every day that passed, the war became more and more serious.

Finally one day, Grandma heard all the noise and came outside to see what was happening. She asked the two friends why they were fighting and told them it was wrong to have a war and be so mean.

The two friends listened to Grandma and agreed to stop the war and be kind to each other. They hugged each other, said sorry and became friends again. From that day forward, they always knew to not fight and be nice to one another.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She was so excited when her family told her they were getting a new house. She ran around and said, "This is the best day ever!"

The family moved in and the little girl was amazed by everything in the house. She couldn't believe how big it was and she loved all the new things.

But when she looked up at the ceiling, she was even more amazed. There was a big round window and the sky was so blue. She wanted to stay and look at it forever.

So her parents said that she could stay there and look out the window while they finished unpacking and getting settled. She was so happy, she couldn't believe that she was in her new house.

The little girl stayed there, looking at the sky, until it was time to go to bed.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She was very worried because she had lost her radio. She looked all around the house, but the radio was nowhere to be found.

She started to cry. Then, her mom came in and saw her crying. Her mom hugged her tight and said, "What's wrong?".

The little girl told her mom that she had lost her radio. Her mom smiled and said, "Let's go look for it together".

They looked everywhere, but they couldn't find it. Then, the mom had an idea. She asked the little girl to help her lift the couch and she said, "There it is! Your radio was under the couch!"

The little girl was so relieved and she gave her mom a big hug. She was so happy to have found her radio. Together, they sat on the couch and listened to music from the radio.

Lily was sick. She had a bad cough and a sore throat. She did not want to play or eat. She only wanted to sleep. Her mom was worried. She gave Lily a pill to make her feel better. But Lily did not like the pill. It was big and bitter. She spit it out.

"Please, Lily, you have to take the pill," her mom said. "It will help you get well soon."

"No, no, no!" Lily cried. "I don't want the pill. It's yucky!"

Her mom tried to be patient. She hugged Lily and said, "I know, sweetie, but it's good for you. How about this? If you take the pill, I will let you watch your favorite show. The one with the lovely princess and the funny dragon. You love that show, don't you?"

Lily thought for a moment. She did love that show. It always made her laugh and smile. She wanted to see the princess and the dragon. Maybe the pill was not so bad after all. She nodded and said, "Okay, mom, I will take the pill. But only if you let me watch the show."

Her mom smiled and said, "Deal." She gave Lily a glass of water and the pill. Lily swallowed the pill quickly and made a face. Then she ran to the couch and turned on the TV. Her mom joined her and cuddled with her. They watched the show together and laughed and smiled. Lily felt a little better. She was glad she took the pill. And she was glad her mom let her watch the show. She loved her mom very much.

Lily liked to do yoga with her mom. Yoga was when they made shapes with their bodies and breathed slowly. Lily liked to stretch and twist and balance. She felt calm and happy.

One day, Lily and her mom went to a fancy place to do yoga. It was a big room with soft mats and colorful pillows. There were many other people there, too. Lily saw a lady with a shiny dress and a man with a funny hat. They looked nice.

Lily and her mom found a spot on the mat and waited for the teacher. The teacher was a friendly woman with long hair and a bright smile. She said hello to everyone and told them to follow her.

The teacher showed them how to do different yoga shapes. Lily tried to copy her, but some of them were hard. She felt her legs and arms get tired. She wanted to rest.

She looked at her mom and saw that she was still doing the shapes. Her mom looked happy and relaxed. Lily wanted to be like her mom.

She decided to keep trying, but not too hard. She remembered what the teacher said: "Yield to your body. Listen to what it needs. Don't force it. Be gentle and kind."

Lily nodded and smiled. She yielded to her body. She did the shapes that felt good and skipped the ones that didn't. She breathed slowly and felt calm and happy.

She looked at her mom again and saw that she was looking at her, too. Her mom smiled and said, "You're doing great, Lily. I'm proud of you."

Lily felt warm and fuzzy. She hugged her mom and said, "I love you, mom. And I love yoga."

Once upon a time, a little girl named Sally was searching for something. "What could it be?" she asked herself out loud.

Sally looked high and low throughout her home but she couldn't find it. Suddenly, she saw her favorite armchair in the corner. She ran over and decided to search there.

Sally searched everywhere on the armchair. She was about to give up, when she finally felt something yummy! She felt a smile on her face and opened her hands, and there it was. A tasty, sweet treat!

"Yay!" she yelled with excitement. Sally quickly ate the treat and thanked her armchair for the surprise.

Once there was a little boy called Mike. He was three years old and he liked music. He listened to songs and liked to imagine playing a guitar.

Mike got a guitar as a birthday present, and he was so excited. He held it in his hands and it looked so shiny and new. He thought about strumming it and making music.

Mike tried to strum the guitar. But it didn't make any sound. He held it to his ear and listened - and it was empty. He was so sad. He thought and thought about what he could do. 

But then he had a great idea. He ran to the kitchen and got an empty plastic bowl. He turned it upside-down and used it like a drum. He strummed the guitar and he could now make music and have lots of fun. 

Mike was so happy and he thought this was the best birthday ever!

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Fiona. Fiona was 3 years old and she liked to run. One day, Fiona went outside with her mom to play. Suddenly Fiona started to run too fast and she tripped over a rock. She hurt her foot really bad and started crying.

Her mom took her quickly to the hospital. She was so scared she curled up in her mom's lap. Once at the hospital, the doctors put Fiona in a big red chair and checked her foot. After lots of tests, the doctors said Fiona had to stay in the hospital for a few days.

Fiona didn't like this plan but mom said that it was ok. She explained that the hospital would make Fiona's foot all better. Fiona was so brave and stayed in the red chair to get bandages. After many days of rest, Fiona was all better and she could run again. She was so happy.

The end.

Tom and Anna were twins who liked to play in the kitchen. They had a big pan that they used to make pretend soup. They put water and toys and leaves in the pan and stirred it with a spoon. They said it was the best soup ever.

One day, they saw a new pan on the shelf. It was shiny and red and had a lid. Tom and Anna wanted to play with it. They both reached for it at the same time. They pulled and tugged and shouted. "It's mine!" "No, it's mine!" They did not want to share.

Mom heard the noise and came to the kitchen. She saw the twins fighting over the new pan. She was not happy. She took the pan away from them and put it back on the shelf. She said, "This is not a toy. This is a special pan for making cakes. You can't play with it. You have to share your old pan."

Tom and Anna felt sad and sorry. They did not want to make Mom angry. They looked at each other and said, "We're sorry, Mom. We love you." They hugged Mom and gave her a kiss. Mom smiled and said, "I love you too. You are my charming twins. How about we make a cake together with the new pan?"

Tom and Anna nodded and clapped. They were happy again. They helped Mom to get the ingredients and the bowl and the mixer. They poured and mixed and poured again. They gazed at the batter and licked the spoon. They said, "This is the best cake ever."

Once upon a time, there was a big empty room. Everyone thought it was too dusty and lonely. So one day a mummy, a daddy and their little baby decided to transform the room. They took out the dust and filled the room with lots of cushions and blankets. They put up wide walls and painted them many colours. Then, the mummy and daddy put lots of toys in the room. The little baby smiled with joy.

The baby loved his new room. Every day he tried something new. He climbed on the pillows, rolled on the blankets and played with the toys. He felt excited and happy.

One day, the mummy and daddy heard the baby talking. They stopped to listen. He said: "I love this room. I love it so much! Can I share it with my friends?" 

The mummy and daddy smiled. They understood the baby's wish. They slowly nodded. They decided to open the room to all the children in the neighbourhood. Together, the mummy and daddy turned the room into a playground for everyone.

The baby's friends became so happy. Everyone loved the big, wide playground. The baby's simple wish had become the source of love and joy for the neighbourhood. 

This story teaches us to share our love and happiness with people around us. That's how a big, empty room became a wide and wonderful playground.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who had a great idea. She wanted to see the stars in the sky from her bedroom. So one morning she took a big step and climbed up the stairs. When she finally reached the top of the stairs, she slowly opened the door and stepped out onto the balcony.

The night sky was dark and the stars were shining brightly. She took a deep breath and looked up at the stars. She felt so happy and excited as each star shone brighter than the last. The little girl felt so great that she wanted to stay there forever.

Then, something magical happened. A shooting star appeared and it was so beautiful! It was like the star was shining just for her. She clapped her hands in happiness, and then the star disappeared into the sky.

The little girl felt so special, like she was the only one who saw the star shine. She smiled, hugged herself and went back to bed. Every night now she stares up at the stars, hoping that one day another shooting star will come back and shine just for her.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved playing with her toys, especially her toy helicopter. One day, she accidentally dropped her helicopter and it broke. She was sad and didn't know what to do.

Her mom came in and saw that Lily was upset. She asked her what happened and Lily told her about her broken helicopter. Her mom said, "Don't worry, I can teach you how to fix it."

Lily was excited and watched as her mom showed her how to put the helicopter back together. They worked on it together and soon it was fixed. Lily was so happy and thanked her mom for teaching her how to fix her helicopter. From that day on, she took extra care when playing with her toys.

Once upon a time, there was a chicken named Kim. Kim was a very special chicken because she would always ask lots of questions.

One day Kim asked her farmer friend, â€œWhat is the most difficult thing youâ€™ve ever done?â€

The farmer replied, â€œThe most difficult thing Iâ€™ve ever done was to get a chicken to lay an egg.â€

Puzzled, Kim asked how she was supposed to do it. The farmer said she had to be very brave.

Kim was brave and tried her hardest, but she just could not lay an egg. She was feeling so sad, when suddenly an egg came out!

Kim was so proud of herself that she screamed of excitement. This taught Kim a valuable lesson to never give up because with hard work and bravery you can accomplish anything, no matter how difficult.

Tommy saw a peanut. He was so excited! He wanted to try it and see what it tasted like. But it was bitter. He didn't like the way the peanut tasted. He made a sour face and stuck his tongue out. Tommy decided to leave the peanut alone and keep looking around. He kept on exploring and soon he forgot all about the peanut.

John was walking down the street when he heard a terrible ringing. He followed the sound to a bookcase. John saw that there was something still inside it. To his surprise, it was an orange frog! When John asked the frog why it was making such a loud noise, the frog said he was thirsty.

John fetched a glass of water and gave the frog a drink. The frog thanked him and asked if he would like to be friends. John said yes and the frog hopped away.

John was kind of sad to see the frog go and wished he could play with him more. Then, he had an idea. He went back to the bookcase and looked up recipes for frog stew. 

John was just heating up the pot when the frog returned with some of his friends. "Terrible!" shouted the frog, "What are you doing?" 

John quickly explained that he just wanted them to be friends and have something to eat together. The frog smiled and said, "Okay, let's eat!" 

And so every Sunday, John and his frog friends ate a delicious meal together.

It was a sunny day. Little Bob was in the garden playing with his toy pistol. He was very eager to try out his new gun. It had a bright yellow cap, and could make a funny noise when it sprayed. 

He wanted to see if the little gun could shoot something. So he found a long piece of string and he held it tightly between his hands. Then he aimed the gun at the string, and he sprayed it with the gun.

Zzzzoom! The gun sprayed the string and Bob was so excited. He sprayed the string again and again and he couldn't stop smiling. He watched as the string went spinning and twisting in the air. 

Bob laughed and ran around in circles as the string spun around him. He had so much fun! After a while, he realised it was getting late and it was time to go in. He put his gun away and ran inside, already excited to come back and play the next day.

Once there was a popular little boy. He was always running around, playing games and he was always happy. One day, he decided to go for a walk in the park. He ran to a big green bench and decided to sit down for a rest. He looked around the park and saw lots of things to explore.

He looked left and he saw a playground, he looked right and he saw some ducks. After a few minutes, he wanted to return home. So he got up from the bench and started walking. Suddenly, he heard some grown-up voices. Two strange men were coming from behind the bench. They saw the little boy and started to run after him.

The little boy was scared and started to run. He ran faster and faster away from the bench as the two men chased him. But the men were too fast and soon they caught up with him. They took the little boy away with them and he never returned home after that day.

Once there was a beautiful girl called Amy. One day Amy wanted to know how hot it was outside, so her mum found a thermometer. Amy loved the thermometer, it had a long, shiny, silver handle that she loved to twist and turn. She enjoyed feeling its smooth surface and the coolness of the silver.

One day, Amy went outside and she could see a beautiful bird singing in the sky. Curiosity got the better of her and she wanted to get closer to the bird, so she walked and twisted her way up the hill. When she finally got to the top, she saw the bird and it was even more beautiful than before. She took out the thermometer and held it up. It said the weather was hot and sunny!

Amy smiled, she was so pleased she could see the beautiful bird, and the thermometer told her how hot it was. Amy loved the thermometer and she continued to twist and turn it in her hand as she made her way back down the hill.

Billy was a little three year old boy who loved playing with cars.
One day he saw a noisy car while he was playing outside.
He shouted, "Wow, look at that car. It's so noisy!"
Billy's mom came outside and asked him what was so noisy.
Billy pointed at the car and said, "That car is so noisy!"
Billy's mom smiled and said, "Yes, it sure is noisy. Let's go for a ride in it. Come on, let's go make some noise!"
Billy happily climbed into the car and made a lot of noise with his mom that afternoon.

Once there was a rabbit who was hopping through the meadow. He stopped when he saw a bean. He wanted to eat it, but then he heard a voice. It was an old owl who was perched on the branch of a nearby tree.

"Don't eat that bean, little rabbit," the owl warned.

But the rabbit was hungry and very tempted. So he picked up the bean and was about to eat it, when the owl spoke again.

"Lucky for you, rabbit," the owl said. "That bean is magical. If you eat it, you'll stay a rabbit forever and never grow. Is that what you really want?"

The rabbit shook his head. He didn't want to stay a little rabbit forever. The owl was right. He was very lucky the owl had warned him. So the rabbit hopped away without eating the bean.

The moral of the story is: it is always important to listen to warnings and take advice from wise people. They just might save you from making a big mistake.

The day was warm and the sun was shining. The sky was big and blue.

John and his mommy went outside. John was three years old and he LOVED to explore. 

"Look," said John, pointing to a hose that was laying on the ground. "What's that?"

"It's a hose," said his mommy. "We can use it to water the plants in the garden."

John grabbed the hose and ran around the garden. He noticed how cool the water felt as it sprayed him.

John's mommy laughed. "Let's sit down and cool off," she said. 

John and his mommy sat down in the shade. The cool air felt good on their skin. They watched the water from the hose sparkle in the sun.

John gave a big smile. He was happy to spend the day outside with his mommy.

Once upon a time there was a girl called Lisa. She was walking in the field with her family. Suddenly, she felt an itch on her arm. She moved her arm trying to scratch the itch away. Everywhere she moved, the itch followed her!

Lisa was starting to get really frustrated. She went to ask her mum for help.

Lisa said:"Mummy, I have an itch and it won't go away."

Her mum replied:"Oh dear, let me take a look."

Lisa showed her mum the itch and her mum quickly realised they had to go to the doctor. Lisa was embarrassed but knew she had to go anyway.

The doctor was able to help and soon Lisa was relieved from the itch. She was so happy that she could move around freely and not worry about the itch!

Molly was tired of being so lazy. She decided to go outside and help her mom fix the garden. Mom had said that the soil needed to be repaired. 

Molly grabbed her shovel and started to dig. As she dug, she found some stones in the soil. She picked them up and put them in a pile. 

Molly worked hard for hours. She was so excited to show her mom what she had done. Molly noticed that her mom was smiling. 

Mom said, "You have done a great job. The soil is looking much better." Molly was so proud of herself. 

Now the garden was ready for planting. Molly was happy that she had repaired the soil and helped her mom.

Once there was a girl. She was very sad and she was weeping. Her best friend was a tall pole. Every day she would come and weep beside it.

One day her friend the pole asked her, "Why do you keep on weeping?"

The girl answered sadly, "My beloved book is lost and I cannot find it."

The tall pole said, "Don't cry, I will help you find it." 

The girl and her friend the tall pole searched everywhere but they couldn't find the book. Finally, they looked in the girl's house and they found it!

The girl was very happy, she hugged the pole and said, "Thank you, my friend!" 
The tall pole smiled and said, "You're welcome!"

Once upon a time there was a man. He wanted to buy a wife, so he looked for a very long time. Finally, he found the perfect wife. She was a brown lady and he liked her very much.

The man gave the brown lady a big smile and asked if she wanted to be his wife. The brown lady said, "Yes". She was very happy.

They got married and the man was so happy to have the brown lady as his wife. After they married they went shopping. The man bought his wife a new dress and some new shoes. They were so happy together.

They shared many wonderful moments together. They were very happy and they still are today.

Ben and his mom were walking in a park on a gray day. Ben loved being outside but he hated this season.

"Why do you hate this season so much, Ben?" his mom asked.

"It's always dark and cold," Ben complained.

His mom smiled. "Wait and see," she said. "You won't always feel that way."

A few weeks later, the weather was much warmer and the days were brighter. Ben noticed something special in the park. Everywhere looked full of life.

"Look, Mom!" said Ben gleefully. He pointed to the trees, now budding with leaves of different shades of green. He smiled at the sight of the sun shining on the grass.

Ben laughed and said, "I don't hate this season anymore! This season is so full of life!"

His mom smiled, happy that he had come to see the beauty of the season.

Once upon a time there was a little boy named Jack. His mommy said he had to be extra clean and tidy today. So Jack did what Mommy said and he cleaned his room.

Soon he was all done, and he was feeling really excited. He went to the door and opened it, and there was the mailman! He had a big bag full of mail.

Jack ran up to the mailman and said, "What did you bring me today?"

The mailman smiled and said, "Let's take a look!" He opened his bag and pulled out something for Jack. It was a shoe, soft and warm. Jack was so happy he laughed and said, "Ohh, this is for me?"

The mailman nodded and smiled. But suddenly, he felt something bite his hand! Jack had a puppy, and he was biting the mailman!

The mailman laughed and said, "Well, that's ok. He's a clean pup, so it's alright."

Jack and the mailman laughed, and then the mailman said goodbye and went on his way. Jack waved goodbye and then closed the door. He was so happy to get his new shoe, but even happier to still have his clean puppy!

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Sarah. Sarah loved to shoot her bow and arrow around the garden. One day, Sarah wanted more arrows so she decided to make some. She found some yarn and some sticks, and soon she had made her arrows. 

Sarah thought the yarn looked so pretty she wanted to keep it for something special. She put the yarn in a small basket and then leftover sticks in the corner. 

The next day, Sarah decided to take her arrows out to the garden to play. When she started shooting, she found the arrows weren't very good. They felt a bit heavy and slow, and some of them even had a bitter taste. 

Sarah was confused and a bit disappointed. That's when she remembered the basket of yarn she had put away. It must have been damp when she put it in the basket, and it had made the yarn bitter. 

Sarah went back inside and put the basket of yarn out in the sun to dry. She then went back outside and made some new yarn arrows - light and fast, just the way she wanted them. The arrows were perfect and she was one happy little girl.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his little drum. He would bang on it all day long! 

One day, Timmy's mom suggested that they go to the park. Timmy was so excited! He brought his little drum with him to the park. 

At the park, Timmy saw some other kids playing. They were playing with a big drum. Timmy's mom suggested that he go over and play with them. Timmy was shy at first, but he started to play with the other kids and their big drum. 

Timmy had so much fun playing with his little drum and the big drum with his new friends. He couldn't wait to come back to the park and play again!

Once there was a wise zebra. He lived in a big forest and every day he would stir up the dirt with his hooves. One day in the forest, he saw a little girl. He watched her for about a minute and she started to walk toward him.

The girl said, â€œHello, Mr. Zebra. What are you doing in the forest?â€

The zebra replied, â€œIâ€™m stirring the dirt with my hooves. I like to mix it up.â€

The girl smiled and said, â€œThatâ€™s really cool. Can I help?â€

The zebra nodded and said, â€œSure you can. Here, take one of my hooves and help me stir.â€

So the wise zebra and the little girl took turns stirring the dirt with the zebraâ€™s hooves. They mixed it up real good and the zebra said, â€œThank you for helping me. It was a lot of fun.â€

The girl smiled and said, â€œYouâ€™re welcome, Mr. Zebra. I had fun too.â€ And with that, they both went their separate ways.

Once upon a time, there was an old man. He was walking through a dark alley late at night. Suddenly he heard a noise! He looked around and saw an old toilet. He started to tremble with fear. He thought something bad was going to happen.

He started to run away, but it was too late. A big, scary monster appeared and he chased after the old man. He ran and ran as fast as he could, but the monster was faster. He screamed for help, but no one came.

The old man could not escape and the monster grabbed him. He was so scared that he closed his eyes and waited for the monster to do something awful. He trembled with fear, waiting and waiting. Unfortunately, the monster ate him and the old man was never seen again.

Once upon a time, there were two old twins. They were named Jack and Jill.
One day Jack was playing with a bucket in the garden. He decided to pour some water into it. He filled it so full that some of the water spilled out and made a puddle in the grass.

Jill saw the puddle and asked her brother what he was doing. He replied, â€œIâ€™m pouring water, donâ€™t you want to join?â€ She nodded eagerly and joined in the fun. The twins filled the bucket again and again and soon the puddle was much bigger.

The twins had so much fun that they forgot about the time. As the sun went down, the twins looked at their big puddle and decided to turn it into a pond. They carefully poured the water around the edges of the puddle and soon it filled up and became a beautiful pond.

The twins stood back and admired their work. The old twins smiled and laughed, knowing that their pond would stay there forever, even when they were grown up.

Once upon a time there was a humble bear living in a forest. One day, the bear decided to go exploring. After walking through the forest, the bear finally came across a strawberry patch. Astonished, the bear shouted "Wow!"

The bear was so excited that he couldn't help but pick some strawberries. Suddenly, something unexpected happened. From behind a tree came a voice saying: "Surprise!"

Startled, the bear turned around and was delighted to see an old friend. The bear couldn't believe its eyes and said: "It's great to see you! What are you doing here?"

His friend replied: "I saw some strawberries and I thought I'd surprise you!" The bear smiled and thanked his friend for the surprise. Together, they decided to pick some strawberries and go back home.

"Oh no!" cried Jack. He had just come out of the store, and realized he had forgotten something very important. He had to deliver it in time, but he could not remember what it was.

He tried to remember, but everything he thought of was wrong. Then he shouted, "MUSTACHE!"

Jack remembered he was supposed to deliver a strong mustache to his dad! He raced back inside the store and grabbed the item, then ran out quickly.

He managed to get back to his dad's house just in time. Jack quickly delivered the mustache and his dad thanked him.

"Thank goodness you remembered! You make a great delivery boy! I'm so happy you remembered," he said with a smile.

Jack felt proud and strong for delivering the mustache on time. He knew he had to be quick and remember what he was supposed to do. From now on, he was going to always remember in the future!

Once upon a time, there were two friends, Angie and Sarah. They were best friends, and they did everything together. 

One day, they decided to go for a walk in the woods. As they walked, they came to a hill with a large tree on the top.

"Let's climb up the hill," said Sarah.

Angie and Sarah scrambled up the hill, and when they reached the top, they noticed a patch of soft, brown earth.

"Let's bury our wish!" said Angie.

"Yes!" Sarah agreed.

So they each drew an ordinary wish on a piece of paper and then they put the two pieces of paper in the patch of brown earth and buried them. 

"Do you think our wish will come true?" Angie asked.

Sarah smiled and nodded. "I hope so," she said.

And they both went on their way, with a smile and hope in their hearts.

John and Mary were very adventurous. Every day they tried new things and explored their world. 

One day, they decided to shoot some corn. John took out his toy gun and Mary held the corn in her other hand. She smiled and said, "Let's shoot it!" 

So they both started shooting the corn. But suddenly, something went wrong. The gun shot too far and it hit a nearby tree. John and Mary were very sad and they decided to stop playing. 

John sadly said, "We shouldn't have been so adventurous."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved going to the circus with her mommy and daddy. Her favorite part of the circus was when the clown came out to play. She thought he was so funny and silly.

One day, Lily went to the circus, but it was very cold outside. She was shivering and her nose was red. She asked her mommy if they could go home, but her mommy said they couldn't leave until the circus was over.

During the circus, the clown did a magic trick where he made a toy disappear. After the show, Lily went up to the clown and asked him where the toy went. The clown said he buried it in the ground. Lily thought that was funny and asked if she could help him bury something too.

The clown smiled and gave Lily a balloon. He said, "Let's bury this balloon together!" Lily was so excited and they buried the balloon in the ground. From that day on, Lily never forgot about the silly clown who buried a balloon with her at the circus.

Timmy and Pepper went to the circus owner and asked if Pepper could perform. The owner said yes and gave Pepper a special costume. Pepper performed tricks like rolling over and jumping through hoops. Once there was a brilliant little boy called Bob. One day, Bob decided to play a joke on his mom. 

He snuck into the kitchen and took out a big melon from the fridge. He placed it on the living room rug and when his mother came in, Bob jumped out and shouted, "SURPRISE!"

But his mom wasn't very happy about the joke. She scolded Bob for taking the melon from the fridge.

Bob was very sad. He went to his room and cried. 

The next day, his mom realized that she had been too harsh and came to apologize. But Bob still felt very bad and he said he'd never play a joke on her again.

Once there was a little girl called Sara. She was very excited about the day ahead as she had seen mum and dad working in the kitchen. Sara went into the kitchen to see what was happening. 

Mum and dad were putting food onto a brown plate. Sara loved the plate as it was the same colour as her favourite teddy. The plate was filled with delicious food and Sara's tummy began to rumble. 

Mum and dad finished their work and sat down for dinner. Sara thanked them for their hard work before tucking in. She enjoyed the food on her plate and ate it all up. 

When dinner was finished, mum and dad thanked Sara for enjoying the food. Sara smiled and thanked them again before heading off to play with the teddy that was the same colour as the plate.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved candy and he always wanted more. One day, Timmy's mom gave him a big bag of candy. Timmy was so happy that he ate all the candy in one day.

The next day, Timmy's friend Billy came over to play. Billy saw that Timmy had no candy left and asked if he could borrow some. Timmy said yes and gave Billy some candy. Billy was happy and went home.

Later that day, Timmy's mom asked him if he wanted to play a game. Timmy said yes and they played a game with a powerful flashlight. Timmy loved the game and had so much fun. When the game was over, Timmy's mom said, "Timmy, you know what? You were so good at the game, I think you deserve some more candy!" Timmy was surprised and happy. He realized that sharing his candy with his friend had made him feel good and now he was getting rewarded for it. From that day on, Timmy learned that sharing is powerful and can bring happiness to everyone.

Once upon a time, there were two friends called Sam and Ben. Sam was always a bit more daring and one day he suggested to Ben, "Let's go and visit the fools on the other side of the town". Ben was a bit scared, but agreed. 

They set out early in the morning, walking across the town to get to the fools. After a long journey, they finally got there. 

The fools were looking very strange and silly, making loud noises and waving their arms around. Sam and Ben started to laugh. One of the fools got angry, and said to the boys sternly, "You better leave now!" 

So Sam and Ben said goodbye to the foolish fools and ran away, back to their homes. 

They never returned to visit the foolish fools again.

John and his mom were at the park. John wanted to play sports, so he ran across the grass. He saw a big, deep lake.

Mom: John, don't go too close!

John stopped, but he was so excited to play sports. He wanted to look for a sport he could do. Then he saw a sport he liked.

John: Mom, look!

Mom: What is that?

John: It looks like a sport I can do there.

Once upon a time, there was a small red car. The car liked to drive around the town. One day, the car met a big blue truck. The truck had a basket full of fruit.

"Hello, car!" said the truck. "Do you want some fruit from my basket?"

The car looked at the basket and saw a sour lemon. The car did not like sour things. The car said, "No, thank you. I do not like sour fruit."

The truck smiled and said, "That's okay. Have a nice day!" The car and the truck drove away, happy to have met a new friend.

One day, a gray cat named Tom went for a jog. He liked to run and play outside. While he was jogging, he found a shiny marble. It was very pretty and he wanted to keep it.

Tom saw a little girl named Sue who was sad. She had lost her marble and could not find it. Tom wanted to help her, but he also wanted to keep the marble for himself.

Tom thought about it and decided to give the marble to Sue. He knew it would make her happy. When he gave her the marble, Sue smiled and thanked Tom. They became good friends and played together every day.

Once upon a time, there was a normal prince who lived in a big, beautiful castle. The prince loved playing with his toys and having fun with his friends. One day, he decided to go on an adventure and explore the kingdom. 

He packed his bag and loaded it onto his horse before setting off on his journey. As he rode through the forest, he saw a little cottage. Inside was a sweet old woman. 

The prince asked the old woman if he could help her with anything. She told him that she needed logs to make her fire. The prince was eager to help and loaded the logs onto the back of his horse. He thanked the old woman before riding off. 

The prince really enjoyed his adventure, and when he returned home, he was excited to tell his family all about it.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play together at the park. One day, they see a lady doing yoga on the grass. She is bending and stretching her body in different ways.

"Wow, look at her!" Lily says. "She can do so many things with her body. I want to try too!"

"Me too!" Ben says. "Let's go and ask her if she can teach us."

They run to the lady and say hello. The lady smiles and says her name is Mia. She says she is happy to show them some yoga moves.

"Yoga is good for your body and your mind," Mia says. "It makes you strong and calm. But you have to be careful and listen to your body. Don't do anything that hurts or feels bad."

Lily and Ben nod and promise to be careful. Mia shows them how to do some easy poses, like the cat, the dog, the tree, and the butterfly. Lily and Ben have fun trying to copy her. They feel their muscles and their breath.

But then, Ben tries to do a pose that is too hard for him. He tries to stand on one leg and lift the other leg behind him. He loses his balance and falls down. He bumps his head on a rock and starts to cry.

Lily and Mia run to him and see if he is okay. Ben has a small cut on his forehead and it is bleeding a little. He feels scared and helpless.

"It's okay, Ben," Lily says. "It's just a small boo-boo. We will get you some help. Don't cry."

Mia says she has a first-aid kit in her bag. She takes out a band-aid and a wet wipe. She cleans Ben's cut and puts the band-aid on it. She gives him a hug and says he is brave.

"Thank you, Mia," Ben says. "You are very nice. I'm sorry I tried to do something too hard. I won't do it again."

"That's okay, Ben," Mia says. "You were just curious and adventurous. That's good. But sometimes you have to know your limits and respect your body. Yoga is not a competition. It's a practice. You can always learn and improve at your own pace."

Lily and Ben say they understand. They thank Mia again and say goodbye. They go back to their parents and tell them what happened. Their parents are glad they are okay and proud of them for trying something new. They say they can do yoga again another day, but only with Mia or another teacher. Lily and Ben agree and promise to be careful. They hug each other and smile. They are still friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Jenny. She was very tired and wanted to take a nap. She found a big, squishy bin in her room and settled inside it. Jenny thought it was the cosiest place ever. She put some of her favourite stuffed animals in the bin too. She felt so happy and settled down for a nice long sleep.

When she woke up, Jenny was feeling much better. She helped her mom clean up all the toys and put them away in the bin. She had so much fun tidying up with her mom.

When it was all done, Jenny felt really happy and relieved. She said goodbye to her mom and went back to her bin to settle down into it. She snuggled up with her stuffed animals and went back to sleep.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Sarah. She was three years old. One day she wanted to do something fun, so she decided to climb. She went to the backyard and saw a big hole. Sarah thought it would be a great adventure, so she climbed in the hole. 

Once inside, Sarah realized there was a big tree with a lot of apples. She was so excited! She started picking the apples from the tree and eating them. They were so delicious and sweet. Suddenly, Sarah heard someone calling for her. It was her mom. But Sarah didn't want to leave the hole, so she hid. 

When her mom finally found her, she saw that Sarah was covered in dirt and her clothes were spoiled. She was very upset. But even after she scolded Sarah, she couldn't help but to enjoy the deliciousApple that she had eaten. Sarah's mom hugged her and they laughed together.

Once upon a time, there was a clever girl called Elisa. She loved to explore and find out how things worked. One day, Elisa was playing near her house when she heard a noise. It was coming from deep in the woods. Elisa was curious and wanted to find out what it was. She walked carefully through the forest until she found a pond. The pond was so clear that Elisa could see all the way to the bottom. But there was something else there. Sitting half in the water, half on the bank, was a broken toy. Elisa was filled with wonder. How had it gotten there? Elisa thought and thought. Then suddenly she knew the answer! She picked up the broken toy, ran back to her house and used clever hands to fix the toy. When it was all back together, Elisa had made a new friend. They were so happy they danced until it was dark. That night Elisa looked up at the stars and thanked them for her new friend.

Once upon a time, a girl went to the store with her mom. She was excited to go, because she saw some other kids with goodies when she went with her mom before.

At the store, her mom asked her what she wanted. She saw an attractive cauliflower and wanted it. So her mom ordered it and put it in the shopping cart.

The girl was so happy that she got something she wanted. She asked her mom if she could keep it with her, but her mom said no. Instead, she told her that she could get something else at the store.

The girl was disappointed, but she followed her mom around the store. Soon, they passed by a toy that the girl wanted. But her mom said they didn't have enough money.

The girl was really sad. She wanted the toy, but she had to leave the store with only the cauliflower. This was not the happy ending she wanted.

Tom and Lily were on a trip with their mom and dad. They stayed in a big hotel with many rooms and a pool. Tom and Lily liked the pool, but they also liked to play in their room. They had many toys and books and crayons.

One day, Tom and Lily were bored. They wanted to have more fun. They decided to make a big mess in their room. They threw their toys and books and crayons everywhere. They drew on the walls and the bed and the floor. They ripped the sheets and the pillows and the curtains. They laughed and shouted and had a lot of fun.

But their mom and dad did not have fun. They heard the noise and came to see what was wrong. They opened the door and saw the big mess. They were very angry and sad. They said to Tom and Lily:

"What did you do? You destroyed the room! This is very bad! You have to clean up and say sorry! The hotel will be very mad at us! We have to pay a lot of money!"

Tom and Lily were scared. They did not know they did something bad. They thought they were just playing. They started to cry. They said to their mom and dad:

"We are sorry! We did not mean to destroy the room! We were bored! We wanted to have fun!"

Their mom and dad hugged them and said:

"We know you did not mean to destroy the room, but you have to be careful and respectful. You cannot make a big mess like this. You have to ask us before you play with something. You have to follow the rules of the hotel. You have to say sorry to the hotel people and help us clean up. Do you understand?"

Tom and Lily nodded and said:

"We understand. We are sorry. We will help you clean up. We will say sorry to the hotel people."

They helped their mom and dad clean up the room. They put their toys and books and crayons back in their bags. They wiped the walls and the bed and the floor. They fixed the sheets and the pillows and the curtains. They said sorry to the hotel people. The hotel people were still mad, but they accepted their apology. They said:

"Next time, be more careful and respectful. Do not destroy the room. Do not make a big mess. Follow the rules of the hotel. Have fun, but not too much fun."

Tom and Lily learned their lesson. They said:

"OK. We will be more careful and respectful. We will not destroy the room. We will not make a big mess. We will follow the rules of the hotel. We will have fun, but not too much fun."

They went back to their room and played quietly. They read their books and drew their pictures and played with their toys. They did not throw anything or rip anything or draw on anything. They were good and happy.

The next day, they went to the pool and had more fun. They saw a fat man in a swimsuit. He jumped in the water and made a big splash. Tom and Lily laughed and said:

"Look at the fat man! He is funny! He makes a big splash!"

The fat man heard them and smiled. He said:

"Hello, kids! I am the fat man! I like to make a big splash! Do you want to join me?"

Tom and Lily said:

"Yes, please! We want to join you!"

They jumped in the water and made a big splash with the fat man. They had a lot of fun. They did not destroy anything. They did not make a big mess. They followed the rules of the pool. They were good and happy. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a curious little girl called Alice. Alice loved exploring new places. One day she decided to go for a walk outside. 

Alice soon came across a lake. She could see a fisherman in his boat, working hard to catch some fish. Alice was so curious, she wanted to join the fisherman and learn how to catch fish too. 

Alice asked the fisherman if she could come with him and the fisherman kindly said no. Alice was disappointed, but she didn't give up. She asked the fisherman again. 

The fisherman looked at Alice and with a smile he said: "You are too small to help me catch the fish. Look at this big boat I am in, it is far too dangerous for you." 

Alice still wanted to try, so the fisherman explained to her that she could watch him from the shore. Alice was so excited. She said goodbye to the fisherman and found a spot by the lake. She watched the fisherman patiently and learned a lot. 

Alice was a very curious girl and she now knew how to be a fisherman too.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys and run around outside. One day, Timmy was playing with his toy car when he saw a big, fierce dog.

On Lily's birthday, Max was so excited to give her the present. Lily opened the present and was so happy to see the toy. She gave Max a big hug and thanked him for being such a loyal friend. From that day on, Max and Lily played with the toy together in her room every day.

After a while she began to realize what she was waiting for. It was for her family, who had gone for the day and hadn't come back yet. Sara smiled and felt excited, then sat and waited some more.
 
When her family finally came home, they were greeted by a very happy Sara. Suddenly, the waiting had been worth it! She felt excited and energized now. Although it had felt dull waiting, now she was very glad she had. 

The end!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to run and play all day. One day, Timmy heard about a race where the winner gets a prize. Timmy wanted to win the prize, so he started to practice every day.

On the day of the race, Timmy was very excited. He saw many other kids there, but he wasn't scared. He knew he practiced hard and was ready to run. The race started and Timmy ran as fast as he could. He could see the prize in the distant, and it made him run even faster.

Finally, Timmy crossed the finish line first and won the prize! He was so happy and proud of himself. He learned that if he starts practicing early, he can achieve anything he wants.

Once upon a time, there was a girl called Amy. She had an uncle who was very nice. One day, her uncle asked her to play a game with him. He said it was called Surrender.

Amy felt scared but she wanted to make her uncle happy, so she said yes. They started to play and Amy tried hard to win. But she soon got very frustrated because she kept losing.

Suddenly, her uncle stopped the game. He had lost too. Then he said, 'I surrender!' and Amy was so happy. But she was a bit worried because she could see that her uncle looked very hurt.

Amy didn't want her uncle to feel bad, so she reached over and gave him a big hug. Her uncle smiled and hugged her back. Then they went back to playing but this time, they both had more fun.

At the end of the day, they were both very happy. They had learned that it's OK to surrender sometimes; all you need is a big hug when you do.

Molly's mom smiled and explained that the license was like a pass that proved the truck belonged to the man driving it. Molly nodded, but still wondered.

Once there was a little girl who believed in magic. Everyday she would go on an adventure to find special things. One day, as she was exploring, she came across a piano.

The little girl was amazed. She had never seen a piano before. She touched the keys and was surprised at how they moved. She believed that if she closed her eyes and made a wish the piano would play magic music.

The little girl closed her eyes and made her wish. As if her wish was granted, the music began to play. The little girl opened her eyes and danced. This piano was full of magic and adventure!

The little girl believed in the magic of the piano and visited it whenever she could. She was always greeted with a beautiful sound, as it brought her on a journey of music and magic.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Macy. Macy wanted to go outside, but it was raining very hard. She asked Mommy and Daddy if she could go outside. But Mommy and Daddy said, "No, it's too wet and dangerous for you to go out." 

Macy then looked out her window and saw a boat. She was so curious and had an idea. She asked Mommy and Daddy if she could take the boat on an adventure. Mommy and Daddy said, "Well, we need to find an anchor to keep the boat in one place."

Macy was very sorry, but she knew what she had to do. She went and asked her neighbours if they had an anchor she could use. Some of the neighbours said no, but then one of them said he had an old anchor that she could use.

Mummy was very cross and told Max he must be more careful. He knew he had been naughty and he said sorry. Mummy said it was OK and gave him another present to play with.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who was upset. She ran away from home and sat on a bench in the park, feeling very sad.

Suddenly, she heard a voice behind her.
"Why are you so upset?" asked the voice.

The little girl turned around to see an old lady, smiling at her.
"I want to go home, but I'm too scared," said the little girl.

The old lady nodded.
"Let me help you. Come with me and I will heal your sadness," she said.

The little girl followed the old lady to her house. The old lady gave her a plate of food and a hug.

The little girl ate the food and felt better. She thanked the old lady for healing her sadness.

Once upon a time there was an ordinary bunny. One day he went out for a walk. He came across a colourful button lying on the ground. It was so pretty that he wanted to wear it.

"Why don't you just wear it?" the squirrel said.

But the bunny said he was afraid that it would not fit.

"Don't worry, it will fit. Just take it and try it on," said the squirrel.

So, the bunny took the button, and amazingly it fit perfectly.

He was so happy he started to jump around.

The moral of this story is that sometimes we need to be brave and try things to find out if they work. We shouldn't be afraid to try!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Jane. She loved to play outside and explore. One day, she went on an adventure in the park and she found a glove. It was a bright blue colour, and it made her very happy. She picked it up, and showed it to her mom.

When it was time for bed, her mom had to remind her to take off the glove. Jane reluctantly said goodbye to her glove, and off to bed she went. She was excited to explore the park again and find more treasures.

Once there was a little boy, who every day would gather his toys. He was very reliable, and had lots and lots of fun!
