Tom took the letter and ran to his room. He opened it and read it. It said:

"Dear Lily, I miss you very much. I hope you are happy and have fun. I made you a picture of us playing in the park. I hope you like it. Love, Anna."

Tom did not like the picture. He thought it was ugly and silly. He took a pair of scissors and cut the picture into tiny pieces. Then he threw them in the trash. He laughed and felt very clever.

Lily came home from school and looked for her mail. She did not see it on the table. She asked her mom, "Mom, where is my mail? Did Anna write to me?"

Mom said, "Yes, she did. I saw it on the table this morning. Maybe Tom took it to his room. Go and ask him."

Lily ran to Tom's room and knocked on the door. She said, "Tom, do you have my mail? Please give it to me. I want to read Anna's letter."

Tom opened the door and smiled. He said, "Sure, I have your mail. Here it is." He handed her a handful of paper pieces. He said, "This is Anna's letter. And this is her picture. Do you like it?"

Lily looked at the paper pieces and felt very sad. She recognized Anna's handwriting and her drawing. She realized that Tom had ruined her mail. She said, "Tom, why did you do this? This was very mean. Anna is my friend. I love her. You are a bad brother."

Tom shrugged and said, "I don't care. I was bored. And I don't like Anna. She is stupid. And so are you."

Lily started to weep. She ran to her mom and hugged her. She showed her the paper pieces and told her what Tom had done. Mom was very angry and scolded Tom. She said, "Tom, you are in big trouble. You have to apologize to Lily and write a letter to Anna. And you have to stay in your room for the rest of the day. No TV, no games, no snacks. You should be ashamed of yourself."

Tom did not apologize. He did not write a letter. He did not stay in his room. He sneaked out of the window and went to play with his friends. He did not care about Lily or Anna. He did not care about anything.

Lily did not stop weeping. She missed Anna very much. She wished she could see her again. She wished she could have her mail back. She wished she had a better brother. She was very unhappy.

Once upon a time, there were two friends named Joe and Mike. They were very brave and liked to fight. One day, they had an incredible idea. They decided to put a basket on their heads and have a fight! Joe and Mike circled each other. They ran around and whacked each other with the basket on their heads. They laughed and ran faster and faster, until Joe tipped Mike over! They both fell down, laughing and smiling. It was an incredible fight!

Once upon a time, there was a farmer who planted some seeds in the soil, hoping for a good crop. But the sun was too hot and the soil was too dry, so the farmer's crop was not very good.

The farmer was sad and didn't know what to do, so he made a fake seed. He hoped that it would help his crop to grow, but it didn't work. In the end all the seeds he planted turned out to be fake and the crop was ruined.

The farmer was very sad and knew that he had made a mistake by planting fake seeds. He wished he had planted real ones in the soil, but it was too late now. 

The farmer had to accept that there were no crops and he hoped he would never make the same mistake again.

Once upon a time, there were two friends. One friend was called Sally and the other was called Jack. One day, Sally had a fun idea. She said to Jack, "Let's play with marbles!"

So they went to the store and picked out some marbles. They had some real ones and some fake ones. Sally wanted the real ones and Jack wanted the fake ones. So they each got to own two marbles.

After they chose, they raced back home. They decided to play a game of marbles. Sally went first, using her real marble. It rolled really fast and knocked all of Jack's fake marbles out of the circle.

Sally laughed and Jack smiled. They both enjoyed the game and had lots of fun. Jack was so happy that he gave one of his real marbles to Sally as a gift. 

Sally was really happy. Now she owned three real marbles and Jack still owned his two fake ones. The friends ran off together to play more of their marble game. 
 
The end.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toy cart and fill it with her favorite toys. One day, she went to the park with her cart and found a lost puppy. She was so happy to have a new friend and decided to take the puppy home with her.

When she got home, her mom was surprised to see the puppy. Lily explained that she found it at the park and wanted to keep it. Her mom was grateful that Lily had a big heart and decided to keep the puppy.

As the puppy grew, Lily had to change her cart to a bigger one so she could take the puppy for walks. She was very happy to have a new friend and a new cart to play with. From that day on, Lily and her puppy went on many adventures together in their cart.

Once upon a time there were two little cats. They liked taking care of their home and keeping it clean. One day, they welcomed a tiny mouse into their house.

The two cats became friends with the mouse, they even shared their food with him. The mouse was very happy and had lots of fun.

But one day when the mouse was playing in the garden, he found some waste. He didn't know that it was bad for him, so he began eating it.

Soon the cats noticed that the mouse was looking hurt, so they quickly called a doctor. 

The mouse was so relieved when the doctor came, he was welcomed warmly. The doctor helped the mouse stay healthy and the cats took care to remind him not to eat waste again. 

The mouse was very grateful, they all became even closer friends after that day. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there lived a girl named Amy. She loved the snow, and she wished for more of it every day. One cold winter morning, Amy looked outside her window and saw that the sky was grey. She was so sad that she began to demand more snow! 

Suddenly, creative ideas started to fill her head. She started to think of ways to make more snow. Amy put on her boots, opened the door and ran outside. She made snowballs and created a big snowman. The snowman was so happy and it made Amy smile. 

The snowman asked Amy a question: "Are you happy now?". She happily answered yes and thanked the snowman. From that day on, Amy was always happy. Whenever she wanted more snow, she just needed to be creative!

Once there was a little boy. He was three years old. His name was Jack.

One day, Jack was very curious about a big red trunk he found. He wondered where it had come from and what was inside. He wanted to solve the mystery.

Jack went up to the trunk and tried to open it. But it was very heavy and he couldn't open it, no matter how hard he tried.

Just then, his mommy came into the room. She saw the trunk and said,

"Oh, Jack. This looks like a fun puzzle. Let's see if we can solve it together".

Jack and his mommy worked together to try and open the trunk. Finally, they reached in and took out a big red ball.

Jack was so excited! He cheered and cheered, showing the ball to his mommy.

He had solved the mystery of the red trunk!

John was a young boy about three years old. He was very spoiled, and often disagreed with his parents. One day, he disagreed with his dad and refused to do what he was asked. His dad got very angry and yelled at him.

"John," he said, "you should stop being so disobedient and do as I say!"

John kept disagreeing. His dad got even more angry and said, "If you don't listen, I'm going to spank you!"

John got scared, but he still disagreed. So his dad spanked him. John was sad and started to cry. His dad was mad and decided he would not talk to John for a long time.

John did not learn his lesson and kept disagreeing. From that day forward, he and his dad were never very close. John kept being spoiled and kept disagreeing, which made it much harder for them to get along.

Once there was a curious little girl named Sally. She loved to explore the world around her. 
One day, Sally found some ingredients in the kitchen and decided to make a muffin. She added flour, sugar, milk, and an egg. She mixed it all together and put it in the oven. She watched as the muffin began to rise.

After it was done baking, Sally eagerly took it out of the oven. It was a big, fluffy muffin. She put a little bit of butter on top and eagerly took a bite. The muffin was delicious!

Sally was delighted with her muffin and quickly ate the whole thing up. She was so proud of herself for making the muffin all by herself. She was now even more curious about the world around her!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Pat. She was three years old and loved to play with her friends.

One day, Pat and her friends were playing in the park. Pat had an apple, but it was broken. Her friends started to complain because they all wanted to eat it. 

Pat didn't know what to do, so she went to her mom for help.

"Mom, my friends are complaining because my apple is broken," Pat said. 

"That's OK. It's not nice to complain, but why don't you share the apple with your friends," her mom said.

So Pat took the broken apple and shared it with her friends. Everyone was happy and they all enjoyed the apple. 

The end.

Once upon a time there was a lucky little boy. His name was Tim. He had a special mirror. It was so shiny and sparkly. One day, Tim was playing with it. He took it outside to get a better look. Suddenly, he slipped and the mirror fell to the ground. It broke into a million pieces.

Tim was very sad. He wanted to make the mirror look like new. But he didn't know what to do. He asked his mom for help. She told him to take out the tool box and find the sharp knife.

Tim took out the knife and began cutting the mirror into small pieces. He worked very hard and in the end, the mirror looked just like it was before. Tim was very happy and he soon hugged the mirror.

"Thank you," he said. "I'm so lucky to have this mirror back."

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy liked to play outside and explore the world around him. One day, Timmy went on a walk with his mommy and they saw a big mill. Timmy thought the mill was very interesting and wanted to take a closer look.

As they got closer to the mill, Timmy started to feel uncomfortable. It was very loud and the wind was blowing hard. But Timmy still wanted to take a look inside. His mommy held his hand and they walked around the mill. Timmy saw big gears turning and lots of wheat being ground up.

After they left the mill, Timmy was happy he got to see something new, even though it was a little uncomfortable. He told his mommy he wanted to take another walk and see what else they could find. And off they went, hand in hand, exploring the world together.

Once upon a time, there was an ugly shark. He lived deep in the ocean. Every day, he swam around looking for something to eat. 

One day, he saw something floating on the water. He swam closer, expecting to find food. Instead, it was a little toy boat. 

The shark was surprised! He stayed in the water, watching the boat carefully. All of a sudden, a little boy jumped in the water! The shark was scared and tried to swim away quickly.

The little boy wanted to play in the ocean, so he grabbed onto the boat and started to paddle. He didn't see the shark, who was still watching him. 

The shark was curious. He wanted to see what the boy was doing, so he remained nearby and watched. After a while, the shark got bored and swam away.

The little boy was safe and he played in the ocean for the rest of the day. He never knew the ugly shark was there.

Once upon a time there was a lovely goose. Every day she'd go out of her pond and walk around the meadow. One day she saw a big tree. The goose split open the tree with her beak. Inside the tree she found a yummy surprise. It was a pile of gooseberries. The goose ate all of them and was so full and happy.

The sun was setting and it was time to go. The goose flew back to her pond and landed gracefully. She was so lovely and happy with the berries she found. She smiled and said goodbye to the tree. It was a lovely day.

Tom and Lily were playing in the snow. They wanted to make an igloo, like the ones they saw in a book. They rolled big balls of snow and stacked them up. They left a hole for the door. They were very proud of their igloo.

"Let's go inside and pretend we are polar bears!" Lily said.

"OK, but be careful. The snow might break if we are too loud," Tom said.

They crawled inside the igloo and made growling noises. They pretended to catch fish and eat them. They had a lot of fun.

But then they heard a fierce bark outside. It was Rex, the big dog from next door. He saw the igloo and thought it was a toy. He ran towards it and jumped on it.

"Rex, no!" Tom and Lily shouted.

But it was too late. The igloo broke and fell apart. Snow flew everywhere. Rex wagged his tail and licked Tom and Lily's faces. He thought he was playing with them.

Tom and Lily were sad and angry. They worked hard to make the igloo and Rex ruined it. They pushed him away and ran to their house. They told their mom what happened.

"I'm sorry, sweeties. Rex didn't know any better. He was just curious. Maybe you can make another igloo tomorrow," their mom said.

She gave them hot chocolate and cookies. She hugged them and kissed them. She said she loved them.

Tom and Lily felt a little better. They still liked Rex, but they wished he would leave their igloo alone. They decided to make a sign that said "No dogs allowed" and put it on their next igloo. They hoped Rex would understand.

Once upon a time, in a small house, a boy named Tim had a big alarm clock. It was red and loud. Every morning, the alarm clock would ring and wake Tim up for school. Tim was a very patient boy. He would wait for the alarm to stop before he got out of bed.

One morning, the alarm clock did not ring. Tim was still in bed when his mom came into his room. "Tim, why are you still in bed?" she asked. Tim said, "My alarm did not ring. I am waiting for it to strike."

Tim's mom said, "Oh no, the alarm is broken. We need to fix it." So, Tim and his mom took the alarm clock to a man who could fix things. The man looked at the alarm clock and said, "I can fix this for you." Tim and his mom were very happy.

The man fixed the alarm clock, and Tim took it home. The next morning, the alarm clock rang loud and clear. Tim woke up and got ready for school. He was glad that his alarm clock was working again, and he was proud of himself for being patient and waiting for it to be fixed.

Lily loved books. She liked to look at the pictures and hear the stories. She had many books in her room, but her favorite was the book about animals. She liked to see the lion, the monkey, the elephant, and the giraffe.

One day, Lily wanted to read her book about animals. She went to her room and looked for it. But she could not find it. She looked under her bed, in her closet, and on her shelf. She was sad and angry. Where was her book?

She heard a noise from the living room. She ran to see what it was. She saw her little brother, Ben, sitting on the floor. He had her book about animals in his hands. He was tearing the pages and throwing them in the air. He was laughing.

"Ben, stop!" Lily shouted. "That is my book! You are bad! Give it to me!"

She ran to Ben and tried to take the book from him. But Ben held it tight. He did not want to give it to Lily. He liked to tear the book. He thought it was fun.

They pulled and pushed. They yelled and cried. The book ripped in half. They both fell down. They both looked at the book. It was broken. They both felt sorry.

"I'm sorry, Lily," Ben said. "I didn't know it was your book. I just wanted to play."

"I'm sorry, too, Ben," Lily said. "I shouldn't have shouted at you. I was mad. I love this book."

They hugged each other. They picked up the pieces of the book. They went to their mom and told her what happened. Mom was not happy, but she was not mad. She said they could fix the book with some tape. She said they should share their books and be nice to each other. She said she loved them both.

Lily and Ben said they loved mom, too. They helped her fix the book. They looked at the pictures and heard the stories. They learned about the animals. They smiled and laughed. They were happy.

Tim and Jen wanted to visit the zoo. They liked to see the animals and hear their sounds. They asked Mom and Dad to take them. Mom and Dad said yes, but they had to save some money first. The zoo had a price to enter. It was not cheap.

They worked hard to save money. They helped Mom and Dad with chores. They sold some toys they did not play with. They put their money in a jar. They counted it every day. They were happy when they had enough.

They went to the zoo on a sunny day. They saw lions, monkeys, elephants, and more. They had fun and learned a lot. They came to the last cage. It had a sign that said "The Ugly Duckling". They were curious. They looked inside.

They saw a big, white bird. It had a long neck and a big beak. It had feathers all over. It was not a duckling. It was a swan. It was beautiful. They heard a voice behind them.

"Hello, kids. Do you like the swan?" It was the zookeeper. He smiled.

"Yes, we do. It is very pretty. Why do you call it the ugly duckling?" Tim asked.

"Well, that's a long story. You see, when it was a baby, it looked very different. It was gray and small and had no feathers. It lived with some ducks, but they did not like it. They said it was ugly and made fun of it. It was very sad. It ran away and found a pond. There, it met some other swans. They were kind and friendly. They told it that it was a swan, not a duck. It grew up and became beautiful. It was happy. It came to the zoo to share its story with others. It wants to teach people to be nice and not judge by looks." The zookeeper explained.

"That's a good story. We like it. Thank you for telling us." Jen said.

"You're welcome. I'm glad you enjoyed it. The swan likes visitors. It likes you too. See, it is waving its wing at you." The zookeeper said.

They looked at the swan. It was waving its wing at them. They waved back. They felt happy. They learned a lesson. They thanked the zookeeper and the swan. They left the zoo. They had a great day.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Walter and Katie, who were very adventurous.
They decided to go on a race one day. Walter said, "Letâ€™s race to the bell."
Katie replied, "Yay! I love races!"

They started running, faster and faster. Walter was a bit ahead of Katie, but she was trying her best to catch up. 
The bell started to ring, making a loud sound. Walter was getting closer, but Katie was not far behind.

When they both arrived at the same time, Walter said, "We did it! We both got here at the same time." Katie was happy and said, "Yay! We both won."
 
They jumped around in excitement as the bell kept ringing. Walter and Katie had been very adventurous, and now they both could say they had won a race!

Once upon a time, there was a princess called Daisy. Daisy wanted to design something special, so she set out on a quest. She traveled for a long time and faced many dangerous challenges. 

One day, she came across a magic door. Intrigued, she opened it to find a garden full of amazing things. Daisy was so excited that she ran inside and started designing. After a while, she found an old pocket watch.

"What a special watch!" Daisy said.

Suddenly, an old fairy appeared. "That watch is very old and very special," she said. "It will give you a lot of extra time - but be careful, it is also very dangerous".

Daisy thanked the old fairy and put the pocket watch safely in her pocket. She went back to designing something beautiful with the extra time that the magic watch gave her. In the end, Daisy was so pleased with her creation - a magical castle filled with joy and happiness.

Mom and Dad took Katie to the park. It was a sunny day and Katie was so excited.

They all went to the playground and Katie saw a big, tall slide. It looked fun but it was too tough for her to do it by herself.

So Mom said, â€œLetâ€™s try to solve it.â€ Dad found a small copper pipe and put it in the slide to help Katie.

They all cheered when Katie made it to the bottom of the slide.

â€œYay!â€ said Katie, â€œNow I can do it!â€

Mom and Dad both smiled at her. â€œYou did a great job solving it, Katie!â€

Anna and Ben liked to play with their toy cars. They had many cars of different colors and sizes. They made roads and bridges with blocks and books. They pretended to drive their cars to different places.

One day, they decided to make a big landscape with their cars. They used a green cloth for grass, a blue cloth for water, and some rocks and sticks for mountains and trees. They made a town with houses and shops, and a farm with animals and crops. They were very proud of their landscape.

"Look at our landscape!" Anna said to Ben. "It is so big and pretty!"

"Yes, it is!" Ben said. "Let's drive our cars around and have fun!"

They took their cars and started to drive. They made noises and stories as they played. They drove to the town, the farm, and the water. They had a lot of fun.

But then, they saw a big shadow over their landscape. It was their baby brother, Sam. Sam was curious about their cars and landscape. He crawled over and reached for them.

"Sam, no!" Anna shouted. "Those are our cars and landscape! Don't touch them!"

But Sam did not listen. He grabbed a car and put it in his mouth. He made a sour face and spat it out. He grabbed another car and threw it away. He pulled the cloths and knocked over the rocks and sticks. He ruined their landscape.

Anna and Ben were very sad and angry. They ran to Sam and tried to stop him. They yelled and cried. They wanted their landscape back.

"Sam, bad!" Ben said. "You broke our landscape! You are mean!"

Sam looked at them and smiled. He did not understand. He thought they were playing with him. He reached for another car.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sarah. She was always looking for something special. Every day she asked her parents, "Do you have something special for me? Can I have a jewel?" 

Her parents told her, "Wait until you are a bit older, then we will look for something special for you."

One day, Sarah's parents told her they had something special for her. Sarah was so excited! She went into the next room and saw a small box on the table. It had her name on it. Sarah opened the box and inside was a little jewel. It sparkled and glittered like a rainbow. Sarah smiled and said, "Thank you!" 

It was the most special thing Sarah ever had, and she never forgot the little jewel her parents gave her.

Once upon a time there was a boy named Joe. He was three years old and liked to play all day long. One day he was feeling really sad and wanted to be happy again.

Joe went to see a special doctor, who had a very tight smile and kind eyes. The doctor told Joe that to get better he had to follow some special fashion. He said Joe needed to laugh more and be around people who made him feel good.

Joe thought about this for a few days and then decided to try it. Every day afterschool he would play with his friends, laugh a lot, and tell jokes. Before he knew it he was feeling much better, and soon he felt happy again.

His friends, family, and doctor watched happily as Joe started to heal. They were all so glad that some special fashion and lots of laughter helped Joe feel better!

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Jack. He liked to play outside in his yard. One day, Jack's mom said he could buy something with his allowance. Jack started to look around and noticed a really cool toy in the store window. It didn't cost much money, so it was cheap. But then he saw something even better in the next store window. It was a colourful veggie garden for his yard! He wanted to buy it, but he knew his mom wanted him to save his money. 

Jack thought hard and decided to buy the veggie garden. He wanted to start growing his own tomatoes and carrots in his yard. He went home to show his mom and she was so proud of him for saving enough money. She helped him plant his new veggie garden and now it's growing lots of yummy veggies!

Once there was a girl called Lucy. She was three and she loved to play with her friends. One day, she was in a very big office. In front of her was a man in a big chair. He was the boss and he was looking at her very seriously.

She felt embarrassed and didn't know what to do. Then she remembered the thing that her mom had taught her. She put her hands together and bowed. She bowed very low, to show the boss that she was sorry.

The man smiled and said: "That's very nice of you Lucy." He was very pleased.

Lucy was happy that she had remembered how to show respect. From then on, she always bowed when she was in an office.

One day, a little boy named Tim was playing outside. He heard a loud noise that made him feel fearful. It was an ambulance going down the street. Tim watched it go by and wondered what was happening.

The next day, Tim went to play with his friend, Sam. They were playing near the street when they saw the ambulance again. This time, they heard the loud noise before they saw the ambulance. Tim and Sam were scared, but they knew the ambulance was there to help someone.

Later, Tim's mom told him that the ambulance was taking a sick person to the hospital. She said that the loud noise was to let people know it was coming. Tim and Sam felt better knowing that the ambulance was there to help people. They were no longer fearful when they heard the noise, and they knew that the ambulance was doing something good.

Once upon a time, there was a huge mouse. One day, he wanted to buy some new sunglasses. He had heard there was a really cool pair at the store. 

So, he went to the mailbox and mailed a letter asking the store to send him the sunglasses. After he mailed the letter, the mouse couldn't wait to get his glasses!

A few days later, the mail came and he quickly opened it. Inside there was a really big box and when he opened it, he saw the most cool and huge sunglasses ever! 

He was so excited, he put them on right away and shouted, "I'm the most stylish mouse in the world!"

Once upon a time, there was a little squirrel who wanted to borrow a nut from the big tree. She asked the old tree if she could borrow a nut from its branches, but the tree said no. The squirrel was embarrassed and walked away with her head down.

Suddenly, a bright blue bird flew down from the tree and said, "I have a nut I can give you." The squirrel was so happy, and thanked the bird. But then the bird said, "But I have a condition. You must first use your tail to pick up three feathers that have fallen out of my nest!" The squirrel said yes and scurried around to find the feathers. The bird was very pleased and gave her the nut.

The little squirrel was so excited, she thanked the bird again and hurried away to eat her nut. After she was done, she brought the bird's feathers back and thanked the bird again. The bird was delighted and said that she could borrow a nut from the tree whenever she wanted.

And from then on, whenever the little squirrel wanted a nut, she asked the tree, and the tree was kind enough to lend her one. The squirrel was so thankful and never forgot to return the loaned nut.

Sara and Mom went to the grocery store. Sara liked to look at all the things on the shelves. She had many questions. She asked Mom, "What is this?" and "Why do we need that?" Mom answered her questions and smiled.

But then Sara saw something that made her fearful. It was a big dog in the parking lot. The dog was barking and running around. Sara was afraid of dogs. She hid behind Mom and said, "Mom, I don't like the dog. Can we go home?"

Mom saw the dog too. She said, "Don't worry, Sara. The dog is not going to hurt us. He is just looking for his owner. He is probably lost and scared. Let's go inside the store and wait for a while. Maybe someone will come and get the dog."

Sara nodded. She held Mom's hand and walked inside the store. She felt safer with Mom. She hoped the dog would find his owner soon. She still had more questions to ask Mom.

There was a new bin in the playground at the park. It was big and blue and shiny. Eva loved it so much that she ran over to it and hugged it tightly. 

"This is my new bin," she said happily. 

Next, Eva started to climb on top of the bin. At first she was very careful, but then she started to get a bit too excited. Suddenly, she started to lose her balance and fall off the bin. 

Eva was scared, but she was not hurt. Her mum came over and said, 
"Well done Eva, you were so brave! Now let's go and get a drink because you worked up a sweat!" 

Eva smiled and was relieved. She said goodbye to her new bin and they both walked away.

Tom is a boy who likes to play with his toys. He has a car, a ball, a doll and a book. He loves his toys very much and takes good care of them. He puts them in a box when he is done playing.

One day, Tom hears a loud noise outside. He looks out the window and sees a big truck. The truck is moving fast and making a lot of smoke. Tom is scared and runs to his mom. His mom tells him to stay inside and not to worry.

But Tom is worried about his toys. He sees that the truck is coming closer to his house. He thinks that the truck might hit his house and break his toys. He does not want that to happen. He wants to save his toys.

Tom is a brave and intelligent boy. He waits until the truck is far enough and then runs to his box. He grabs his car, his ball, his doll and his book. He holds them tight and runs back to his mom. He is very fast and careful.

He makes it to his mom and hugs her. He shows her his toys and says, "I saved them, mom. I saved my toys." His mom smiles and kisses him. She says, "You are a very good boy, Tom. You are very smart and kind. I am proud of you." Tom is happy and proud too. He loves his mom and his toys. He is safe and happy.

Once upon a time, there was a baby bunny called Sam. Sam was always jumping and hopping around, never staying in one place for more than a few seconds. One day, Sam was hopping around so quickly that he hopped right off the floor and got stuck in a tree. He was feeling very sad and scared, because it was so high up.

Sam suddenly heard a voice coming from below him. It was his friend, Fred. Fred had seen what had happened and was asking Sam to come down. But Sam was too scared to move. So Fred got an idea. He went and found a really long stick, and he held it up for Sam to grab.

Sam was so relieved and happy, he quickly grabbed the stick and started climbing down. But then something awful happened. Halfway down the stick, Sam missed the floor and he fell right in a pile of garbage. It was disgusting!

But luckily, Fred was there. He ran over and grabbed Sam quickly and hugged him. Then he wiped off all the disgusting yucky stuff from Sam's fur. Sam was so happy to be back on the floor again, snuggling in Fred's arms.

Once upon a time, in a small village, there lived a boy named Tom. Tom loved to listen to stories. Every night, his mom would tell him a new story before he went to sleep. Tom was a good boy, but sometimes he was a bit ignorant.

One day, Tom's friend, Sam, came to play with him. They played with toys and had a lot of fun. Then, Sam started to tell Tom a story. But Tom didn't want to listen to Sam's story. He said, "I don't want to hear your story, Sam. I only like my mom's stories." Tom chose to ignore Sam's story.

Sam felt sad and went home. Later, Tom's mom found out what happened. She sat down with Tom and said, "Tom, you should always listen to your friends' stories too. It's not nice to ignore them. We can learn something from everyone's story." Tom realized his mistake and felt sorry.

The next day, Tom went to Sam's house and said, "I'm sorry, Sam. I was ignorant. Please tell me your story." Sam smiled and shared his story with Tom. They both listened to each other's stories and learned new things.

From that day on, Tom never ignored anyone's story. He knew that every story had something to teach him. The moral of the story is: always listen to others and don't be ignorant, because we can learn something from everyone.

Tom had a huge toy car that he loved to play with. It was red and shiny and made loud noises. He liked to drive it around the yard and pretend he was a racer. But he had a problem. His toy car was too big to fit in the garage. The garage was where he kept his other toys, like his bike and his ball and his teddy bear.

One day, Tom had an idea. He saw his dad's car parked in the driveway. His dad's car was also red and shiny and made loud noises. Maybe his dad's car could fit in the garage, and then he could put his toy car in the driveway. Tom thought that was a good plan. He ran to his dad's car and opened the door. He climbed inside and tried to find the keys. He did not know how to drive a real car, but he thought it was easy. He just had to turn the wheel and push the pedals.

Once upon a time, there was a gifted girl named Anne. Every day she liked to play in the bathtub. But one day, the bathtub was in a big mess with toys all over the place. Anne tried cleaning up the bathtub, but she couldn't complete it all on her own.

Anne was so happy that she and her brother had been able to complete their task. They hugged each other before taking a nice bath together in the sparkling clean bathtub.

Lily and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toys in their bedroom. But they do not like to clean up. Their bedroom is very messy. There are dolls, cars, books, and blocks everywhere.

One day, Mom comes to their bedroom. She is not happy. She says, "Lily and Ben, look at this mess! You need to clean up your toys right now. Or you will not get any dessert after dinner."

Lily and Ben do not want to miss dessert. They love cake and ice cream. But they do not want to clean up either. They look at each other. They have an idea.

They decide to hide their toys under the bed, in the closet, and behind the curtains. They think Mom will not see them. They say, "OK, Mom, we will clean up our toys. We will be very fast."

Mom goes to the kitchen. Lily and Ben start to hide their toys. They think they are very clever. But they are not.

Mom comes back to their bedroom. She sees the bed, the closet, and the curtains. She knows what they did. She says, "Lily and Ben, this is not cleaning up. This is hiding. You are not fooling me. You need to put your toys in their boxes and shelves. Or you will not get any dessert after dinner."

Lily and Ben are sad. They know they made a bad choice. They say, "Sorry, Mom. We will not hide our toys again. We will clean up our bedroom for real."

Mom smiles. She says, "That's good. I will help you. And if you finish before dinner, you will get a surprise."

Lily and Ben wonder what the surprise is. They hope it is something fun. They start to clean up their bedroom. They learn their lesson. They decide to be more tidy next time.

Once upon a time, there was a wide path in the woods. It had a big zigzag in the middle. Many animals liked to play on the path.

One day, a rabbit and a squirrel were playing near the zigzag. They wanted to have a race to see who was faster. So, they decided to split up and race to the end of the wide path.

The rabbit hopped fast and the squirrel ran fast too. They went around the zigzag and kept going. The animals in the woods watched and cheered for them. At the end of the race, the rabbit and the squirrel were both very fast, and they finished at the same time.

Everyone was happy and had fun. The rabbit and the squirrel became best friends. They played on the wide path with the big zigzag every day.

Once upon a time there was a robot who lived in a big machine. He was very happy because every day he would stretch his arms and legs.

One day the robot was feeling a little bit tired, so he decided to have an adventure outside his machine. He stretched his legs and walked through the new world.

The robot found lots of things he had never seen before, like a river and a big tree. He stretched his arms and smiled.

Then, the robot became very tired. He stretched his legs back to his machine and lay down to sleep.

The robot had a lovely dream and the next day he was no longer tired. He stretched his arms and legs, and went out to explore again.

Once there was a girl. She met a dog. The dog was funny.

The girl asked the dog, "Hello, who are you?"
The dog smiled and said, "I'm a dog."
The girl laughed. She said, "You are funny!"

The girl answered, "My name is Molly."

Tommy and Lily were playing in the park. They saw a big pond with many ducks and fish. They wanted to feed them some bread. They asked their mom for some bread. Mom gave them each a slice and said, "Be careful, don't go too close to the water."

Tommy and Lily walked to the pond. They saw a cute otter swimming in the water. The otter saw them and came closer. It looked hungry and friendly. Tommy and Lily smiled and threw some bread to the otter. The otter caught the bread and ate it. It made a happy sound.

"Hello, otter!" Tommy said. "Do you like bread?"

"Yes, I do!" the otter said. "It is very tasty. Thank you for sharing."

"You're welcome, otter!" Lily said. "Do you want to play with us?"

"Sure, I do!" the otter said. "But I can't leave the water. How can we play?"

Tommy and Lily thought for a moment. Then they had an idea. They said, "We can march around the pond. You can swim along with us. We can sing a song. Do you know how to march and sing?"

"Yes, I do!" the otter said. "I learned from the ducks. They march and sing all the time. Let's do it!"

Tommy and Lily nodded. They held hands and started to march around the pond. The otter followed them in the water. They sang a song. It went like this:

"We are marching, marching, marching
We are marching with the otter
We are happy, happy, happy
We are happy to be friends"

The otter sang along with them. It went like this:

"I am swimming, swimming, swimming
I am swimming with the children
I am grateful, grateful, grateful
I am grateful for the bread"

They marched and sang and laughed. They had a lot of fun. Mom watched them and smiled. She was glad they made a new friend. She took a picture of them and said, "What a lovely day!"

Lily and Max were best friends. They liked to play in the park near the pond. There were many ducks and swans in the pond. Lily and Max loved to feed them bread and watch them swim.

One day, they saw a new swan in the pond. It was white and big and had a long neck. Lily thought it was the most charming swan she had ever seen. She wanted to give it all her bread. Max thought it was a mean swan. He saw it snap at the other ducks and swans. He wanted to scare it away.

Lily and Max began to quarrel. Lily said, "This swan is so charming. I want to be its friend. It needs more bread than the others." Max said, "No, this swan is so rude. It hurts the other birds. It does not need any bread. It needs to go away." They pulled and pushed each other. They dropped their bread on the ground.

The swan saw the bread and swam towards them. It opened its beak and hissed. It bit Lily's hand and Max's leg. They cried out in pain and ran away. The swan ate all the bread and flapped its wings.

Lily and Max learned their lesson. They should not quarrel over the swan. They should share their bread with all the birds. They hugged and said sorry to each other. They went home and put some ice on their wounds. They hoped the swan would be nicer next time.

Once upon a time there was a driver who was collecting books for the library. He was very careful about the books and made sure each one was put away safe and sound.

One day he was collecting books from a small house. He drove his truck over and parked outside. Just as he was about to start unloading the books he noticed a little girl and her dog. The girl was very upset and crying.

The driver bent down and asked her what was wrong. She explained that she had lost her book that she was supposed to return to the library the same day. She was so sad.

The driver gave her a big smile and said "That's okay, I'll help you find it!". He searched around the house until he finally found it tucked away behind the couch.

The little girl was very happy and gave the driver a big hug. She went back to the library and returned the book, thanks to the driver. From that day forward, the driver always kept an eye out for books that were in need of collecting!

Lily and Sam like to play at the park. They like to swing on the swings, slide on the slide, and run on the grass. One day, they hear some music from the other side of the park. They run to see what it is.

They see a band playing some songs. The band has a guitar, a drum, a flute, and a singer. The music is loud and happy. Lily and Sam clap their hands and dance along.

Once upon a time there was a great man who had a guitar. He loved to play it and people would gather around to listen. One bright day, an old friend of the man stopped by.

Once there was a fish who lived in the ocean. He wanted to succeed, so he decided to try and swim as fast as he could. He swam and swam until he was very tired, but he had not gone very far. 

He heard a voice from above. He looked up and saw a bird flying in the sky. The bird asked him, "Why are you swimming so fast?" The fish replied, "I am trying to succeed." The bird said, "You could try fishing and catching a tuna. That would help you succeed too!" 

The fish thought this was a great idea and he began to fish. He was careful and patient. After a long time, he felt a tug on his line. He pulled and pulled, and soon he had a big tuna! 

He was very proud of himself for succeeding. He was happy and full from the tuna he had caught. He knew he had accomplished something great. The bird flew away, but the fish stayed in the ocean, proud of himself and happy to have succeeded.

Once upon a time, there was a boy who had a magic razor. Every morning he would wake up, take the razor and pretend to shave. He loved how the razor glowed brightly in his hand.

One day, Ben and Lily went to the park with their mom. They liked to play on the swings, the slide and the seesaw. They also liked to look for bugs and flowers in the grass.

But today, there was a big boy in the park who was very rude. He pushed Ben off the swing and took his turn. He slid down the slide and kicked Lily's feet. He jumped on the seesaw and made it go up and down very fast. He did not share or say sorry.

Ben and Lily were very sad and angry. They told their mom what the big boy did. Their mom said, "That is not nice. He should not do that. Let's go and talk to him."

They walked to the big boy, who was now throwing rocks at the birds. Their mom said, "Hello, what is your name?" The big boy did not answer. He threw a rock at their mom. It hit her on the leg and hurt her.

Their mom said, "Ouch! That is very rude and mean. You should not throw rocks at people or animals. That can hurt them. You need to stop and say sorry."

The big boy did not stop or say sorry. He threw another rock at their mom. It missed her, but it hit a bee. The bee was very angry. It flew to the big boy and stung him on the nose.

Ben and Lily and their mom watched the big boy and his mom. They felt sorry for the big boy, but they also thought he learned a lesson. They hoped he would be nicer next time. They went back to play and have fun. They said, "Thank you, bee, for helping us." The bee buzzed and flew away.

Once upon a time, there was a brave knight. He had a shiny sword he liked to use. Every day he'd use it to practice his sword fighting. One day he had to use his sword in a real fight. Once upon a time, there was a little bird with fragile wings. The bird loved to fly high up in the sky, but one day it fell down and broke its wing. The bird was very sad and could not fly anymore.

Tim's mom saw this and taught Tim to share. Tim learned that sharing was good and made others happy. He shared his snacks with Sue, and they both enjoyed them together. From that day on, Tim was not selfish anymore and always shared his snacks with his friends and family.

Anna loves to play with her mom's jewelry. She likes to put on the shiny rings, the pretty necklaces and the sparkly earrings. She feels like a princess when she wears them.

One day, Anna finds a long necklace in her mom's drawer. It has many colors and beads. Anna thinks it is very beautiful. She wants to try it on. She puts it around her neck and looks in the mirror. She smiles and twirls.

"Anna, what are you doing?" her mom asks. She comes into the room and sees Anna with her necklace. She is not happy. She takes the necklace from Anna and puts it back in the drawer.

"Mom, why are you angry?" Anna asks. She does not understand.

"Anna, this necklace is very special. It was a gift from your grandma. She gave it to me before she went to heaven. It is not a toy. You cannot play with it. You could break it or lose it. Do you understand?" her mom tells her.

Anna feels sad. She did not know the necklace was so important. She loves her grandma and misses her. She does not want to make her mom sad too.

Her mom hugs her and kisses her. She is not angry anymore. She is glad that Anna is sorry and loves her.

Anna nods and smiles. She is happy again. She and her mom go to her room and play with her dolls. They have fun and forget about the necklace.

Tom and his mom went to the mailbox together. Tom held Spike in one hand and the letter in the other. He opened the mailbox and put the letter inside. Tom was so happy that he was able to mail the letter. He thanked his mom and gave Spike a big hug.

Once upon a time there was a little dog who loved to explore the big world. One day, he decided to go for a walk in the backyard of his owner. It was a warm day so the grass and the trees were swaying in the breeze. The little dog was excited and he started running and playing around.

Suddenly, he noticed that everything around him had gone still and quiet. He looked around, confused, and noticed that everything was frozen solid! Everything had been frozen by a special power and the little dog couldn't move.

He started to feel really dizzy and confused. He tried to move, but nothing happened. Then he saw his owner coming outside. His owner had a look of surprise in his eyes as he saw the little dog frozen in place.

He slowly waved his hand towards the little dog and, in a flash, the dog was free again! Everything came back to life and the little dog could move again.

The little dog was so happy and relieved! He thanked his owner for saving him and promised to be careful in the future. From then on, the little dog was much more careful when he walked around his owner's backyard. The end.

Once upon a time, in a big park, there was a playful little girl named Lily. She loved to play on the swing. She would go up and down, laughing and having fun.

One day, Lily saw a small cat stuck in a tree. The cat was scared and couldn't get down. Lily wanted to help the cat, so she tried to think of a way to solve the problem.

Lily had an idea! She climbed onto the swing and swung as high as she could. When she was close to the tree, she reached out and grabbed the cat. Then, she brought the cat down to the ground. The cat was happy and safe, all thanks to Lily and her playful swing.

Sam and Mia were playing in the garden. They liked to dig holes and find worms and bugs. They saw a big pumpkin that was lying on the ground. It was orange and round, but it had some brown spots on it.

"Look, a pumpkin!" Sam said. "Can we take it home?"

Mia shook her head. "No, Sam. That pumpkin is bad. It is rotting. See the brown spots? They are yucky. The pumpkin is sick."

Sam frowned. He wanted to take the pumpkin home. He thought it was pretty. He touched the pumpkin with his hand. It was soft and wet. He pulled his hand back. It was sticky and smelly.

"Yuck!" Sam said. "You are right, Mia. The pumpkin is bad. It is rotting. Let's leave it here."

They ran away from the pumpkin. They saw a man who was walking by. He was bald. He had no hair on his head. He was carrying a big bag.

"Hello, children," the man said. "What are you doing?"

"We are playing," Mia said. "We found a pumpkin, but it was bad. It was rotting."

The man nodded. "I see. That pumpkin is bad. It is rotting. It was left here by the farmer. He had too many pumpkins. He could not sell them all. He threw them away."

"That is sad," Sam said. "Why did he have too many pumpkins?"

The man sighed. "Because of the flood. There was a lot of rain. The river was too full. It spilled over the land. It made the fields wet. The pumpkins grew too fast. They were too big. They were not good. They started to rot."

"That is sad," Mia said. "We don't like the flood. We don't like the rot. We like good pumpkins."

The man smiled. "I like good pumpkins too. That is why I have this bag. It has good pumpkins in it. They are small and sweet. They are not rotting. They are good for eating. Would you like one?"

Sam and Mia nodded. They liked good pumpkins. They liked the man. He was bald, but he was nice. He gave them each a good pumpkin. They thanked him and ran home. They showed their mom the good pumpkins. She was happy. She said they could make pumpkin pie. They liked pumpkin pie. They liked good pumpkins. They did not like the flood. They did not like the rot.

Once upon a time there were two friends, John and Steve. They were very close and always had lots of fun together. 

One day they were walking through the forest when they heard something strange. It was the sound of a whisper. They stopped to listen and it sounded like a elderly person talking. 

John and Steve moved closer. As they got near they saw a cute old lady, talking softly to herself. She was talking about wisdom. 

John and Steve said hello, but the old lady kept talking softly. She said to them, "If you use wisdom, you will always have fun together." 

John and Steve thanked her before they carried on with their journey. They thought deeply about what she said and from that day forward they would always try and use wisdom when making decisions. 

The moral of the story is that wisdom can help bring people closer.

Once upon a time, there was a monster. He was very big and very scary. One day, he got confused and didn't know where he was. He tried to walk forward, but he kept bumping into things. 

Suddenly, he saw a little boy. The boy was very brave and not scared of the monster. The boy said, "Hello, Mr. Monster. Are you lost?" The monster nodded his head and said, "Yes, I am confused." 

The boy had an idea. He told the monster to turn around and walk the other way. The monster did what the boy said and started to walk in reverse. Soon, he found his way back home. From that day on, the monster and the boy were friends.

Tom and Lily were playing cops and robbers in the garden. Tom had a toy pistol and Lily had a hat and a badge. They ran around the trees and the flowers, pretending to chase each other.

"Stop, robber, or I will shoot!" Tom shouted, pointing his pistol at Lily.

"No, you can't catch me, I'm too fast!" Lily said, running away.

Tom followed her, but he did not see the big rock on the ground. He tripped and fell, and his pistol flew out of his hand. It landed in a pile of dog poop.

"Yuck!" Tom said, looking at his smelly pistol. "That's gross!"

Lily saw what happened and laughed. She ran back to Tom and helped him get up.

"Are you okay, cop?" she asked.

"I'm okay, but my pistol is not," Tom said, making a sad face.

Lily smiled and gave him a hug.

"That's okay, we can share mine," she said, handing him her hat and badge. "Now we can be partners and catch the bad guys together."

Tom smiled and put on the hat and badge. He thanked Lily and gave her a high five.

They picked up the smelly pistol and threw it in the trash. Then they went back to playing cops and robbers, having fun in the garden.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tom. Tom was very brave and always wanted to go to the beach. One sunny day, his parents decided to take him.

The beach was beautiful. Tom ran and played on the sand. Suddenly, he saw a shark swimming far away in the ocean. Tom was scared and he felt helpless.

Ben was a little boy who liked to play pretend. He had a uniform that looked like a fireman. He wore it when he played with his toy truck and hose. He believed he was a real fireman who could put out fires and save people.

One day, he saw a big fire in the kitchen. His mom was cooking and left the stove on. Smoke and flames came out of the pot. Ben ran to his room and put on his uniform. He grabbed his toy hose and truck. He believed he could put out the fire.

He ran to the kitchen and sprayed his toy hose at the fire. But the water did not come out. It was only a toy. The fire did not stop. It got bigger and hotter. Ben's mom saw him and yelled. She was scared and angry. She grabbed Ben and ran out of the house. She called the real firemen.

The real firemen came with their big truck and hose. They put out the fire and checked the house. They said it was not safe to go back inside. Ben's mom hugged him and cried. She was glad he was not hurt. But she was also very mad. She said he was naughty and should not play with fire. She said he should not believe he was a fireman. He should listen to her and stay away from the stove.

Ben felt sorry and sad. He did not mean to start the fire. He wanted to help. He liked to believe he was a fireman. He liked his uniform. But he did not like to make his mom cry. He said he was sorry and he loved her. He said he would not play with fire again. He said he would only play pretend in his room. He hoped his mom would forgive him and his uniform would not burn.

The sun was warm, and the air was peaceful. Hannah stood by the edge of the pool and dipped her toes in. She watched the cascading water and felt the coolness on her skin and she began to shiver with delight. 

Suddenly, a friendly voice called out to her, "Hello Hannah! Why don't you come in and play?", it asked. Hannah smiled as she recognised the voice of her big brother, Jack. She splashed into the calm waters and started to swim around, feeling free and content.

"Jack, I can go really deep!" she shouted, amazed at her newfound courage.

Jack smiled back at her, and held her hand, guiding her deeper and deeper. Soon enough, the pool began to feel much colder and Hannah started to shiver.

"It's too cold, Jack," she said, her little teeth chattering as she spoke.

But just as she was about to turn around and swim back up, Jack pulled her close and whispered into her ear, "Don't worry Hannah, the pool is peaceful. I'll stay with you, it's going to be ok".

Hannah felt safe and with her big brother by her side, her shivering ceased. She swam back up, eyes filled with courage and joy. 

The sun shined down and peace filled the air. Hannah had conquered her fear and she was ready for more.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat candy and cookies, but her mom said she could only have one treat a day. One night, Lily had a nightmare about a big scary monster. She woke up and felt scared. 

But then, her mom came in and gave her a big hug. Lily squeezed her mom back and felt better. Her mom also had a surprise for her - a delicious chocolate chip cookie! Lily was so happy and took a big bite. It was the best cookie she had ever tasted. 

From that night on, Lily knew that even if she had a nightmare, her mom would always be there to give her a hug and a delicious treat to make her feel better.

Once there was a girl who had a gun. One day, she was walking through the woods. The ground was rough and she got lost. She started to cry.

Then, suddenly, she saw an old man. He was nice and friendly. He said he would help her find her way back home. She was so happy!

The old man took out a special stick. It was a magic stick that he had found in the woods. He used it to rescue her. Together they walked on the rough ground, back to her home.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Millie. She was three years old and very excited about riding her bike for the first time. Millie had settled in the seat of her brand new bike and was pushing the pedals with her feet. Soon enough she was rocking along on her bike, her little feet pushing the pedals around and around.

Millie was rocking along until she hit a small stone and fell off the bike. She was not hurt but her bike was a bit broken. Happily Millie fixed the bike and was soon rocking away again. She eventually finished her first bike ride, feeling successful and happy.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy had a helpful sister named Lily who always helped him with his toys. One day, Timmy and Lily went to their bedroom to play. Timmy had a new toy truck that he was excited to play with.

Timmy felt happy that Lily was being helpful. They worked together to fix the truck and played together happily ever after.

Once there was a little girl who liked to spin. She twirled around and around and it made her very happy. One day she decided to take her pet hamster to the veterinarian. When they got inside, the veterinarian was very angry. The little girl was scared and tried not to spin, but it was too hard. The veterinarian saw her spinning and told her she had to stop. The veterinarian said she had to be still so he could take a look at the hamster. The little girl wasn't sure why the veterinarian was so angry, but she liked her hamster and wanted to do what was best. So, she took a deep breath and stopped spinning. The veterinarian looked at the hamster and said he was healthy. The little girl was relieved and gave the hamster a hug.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside, especially when it rained. One day, she saw a big puddle in the street. She jumped in it and got her shoes all wet. 

Her big brother, Max, came outside and saw her. "Lily, you shouldn't jump in puddles. You'll get sick," he said. 

Lily didn't want to stop playing, so Max decided to teach her a game. They took turns jumping over the puddle, trying to see who could jump the farthest. It was a very competitive game, but they had a lot of fun. 

After a while, Lily was tired and ready to go inside. Max helped her take off her wet shoes and socks. "Thanks for teaching me a new game, Max," she said with a smile. Max was happy to spend time with his little sister and teach her something new.

Once upon a time there was an oak tree in a forest. Every day the oak tree had to watch the animals in the forest quarrel. It was always sad to watch them fight.

One day, a fake fox came and joined the quarrel. He had no tail and yelled very loudly. The animals in the forest were so scared of the fox but he just kept on yelling.

The oak tree did not like the fake fox very much. He wanted the animals to be happy and friendly again. The oak tree shouted to the fox, "Go away and leave the animals alone!"

The animals were so happy and the oak was relieved. From that day forward the animals in the forest didn't quarrel with each other anymore. They were all happy and stayed friends.

John was playing at the beach with his mom. He noticed all the water around him, the wet sand and the foamy waves. Suddenly, he remembered he had forgotten his sand bucket. He laughed at how foolish he had been.

The waves were getting bigger and bigger. John and his mom decided to take a rest under a big tree, watching the ocean. It was getting windy and the waves crashed against the shore.

John noticed something sparkly in the water. He jumped up and ran towards it, shouting excitedly. His mom followed close behind. When they got to the water, they saw a big fish swimming around playfully.

John and his mom watched the fish for a while, smiling happily. The fish happily splashed around and seemed to be enjoying the attention. Eventually, John and his mom said goodbye to the fish and walked back up the beach. They both felt grateful for the special moment they had shared with the sea creature.

Once upon a time, in a big green forest, there lived a gentle bunny named Bobo. Bobo had a little spot on his ear that made him special. He loved to play with his friends and join them in their games.

One sunny day, Bobo saw his friends playing near the river. They were trying to cross the river by jumping on the big stones. Bobo wanted to join them, but he was scared of the water. His friends told him, "Don't worry, Bobo. We will help you cross the river."

Bobo was scared, but he knew his friends were there to help him. He took a big breath and started to jump from one stone to another. With each jump, his friends cheered him on. Finally, Bobo made it to the other side of the river. He was so happy that he joined his friends in their fun game.

Bobo learned that with the help of his friends, he could do things that he was scared of. The gentle bunny with the little spot on his ear became braver because of his friends' love and support. And the moral of the story is, when we help each other, we can do anything we want.

One day, a kid was playing with his pet in the backyard when his eyes caught a glimmer from the tree. He saw that there was a shiny gem stuck in the trunk. The kid said to his pet, "Look there's a glittery gem in that tree." His pet didn't believe him, but the kid was sure.

The kid took the shiny gem out and tried to put it in his pocket, but the gem was too big. He tried and tried, but it wouldn't fit. The gem was too tight. The kid's pet watched him in confusion. 

The kid didn't want to leave the gem behind, so he came up with a plan. He looked around and found a stick. He stuck the stick in the crack of the trunk, and then he started to tear. 

The kid worked hard until suddenly, the sound of cracking loudly filled the air. The kid had managed to tear the trunk in two. The gem fit perfectly in his pocket, and the kid felt happy that he could bring it home. He felt relieved as he held the gem tight in his pocket.

Hank and his sister Claire were playing in their backyard. Claire was pushing the swing, while Hank decided to make himself a lemonade. He grabbed a pitcher and opened the fridge.

"What are you doing?" asked Claire, peeking over the door. "Making lemonade," said Hank, smiling.

He squeezed some lemons into the pitcher and stirred it with a spoon. Then he took out a jug of water and poured it into the pitcher. When he was done, he took two glasses and filled them with the lemonade.

"Wow, that looks yummy," said Claire.

Hank smiled. He then took out an eraser and two tall chairs from inside. He put the chairs in front of the swing and the eraser in the middle.

"Let's play checkers!" he said, excited.

Claire smiled, and the two of them started their game. Everyone had a great time and enjoyed the lemonade Hank made.

Once there was a girl called Sarah. She was very curious and wanted to learn everything she could. So every day, Sarah would study and learn new things.

One day, Sarah found an old ornament and she wanted to put it on her shelf. But it was too tight, so Sarah could not put it up. She wanted to find a way to make it fit, so she studied how to do it.

Finally, Sarah managed to make the ornament fit on her shelf. She felt so proud and happy! From this, Sarah learnt an important lesson: if you study and never give up, you can succeed in anything.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved to collect things. She would save every shiny rock, leaf, and flower she found in her backyard. 

One day, she noticed a strange leak coming from her garden. Her parents told her it was water from the rain but she was convinced it was something special. She gathered up a bucket and started to collect the mysterious liquid. 

As she collected more and more, other kids in the neighbourhood saw what she was doing. They were envious of her and asked her what she was doing. The little girl smiled and said â€œIâ€™m collecting something special.â€ 

The other kids were curious and wanted to join her, so the little girl let them help. Soon enough, the whole neighbourhood was collecting the mysterious liquid. Everyone was so excited and happy!

Once upon a time, there lived a little boy named Sam. Sam was a very happy boy because he liked to explore outside. One day, Sam went to the forest to look for something special. He searched and searched, until he finally found something - a yummy root! He was so excited and he couldn't wait to try the root. 

But when Sam ate the root, his tummy hurt so much that he started to cry. He was so sad. Suddenly, he heard something coming from nearby. It was a gentle voice saying, "Don't cry, Sam". 

Sam looked up, and he saw an old man sitting on a tree stump. He asked the old man what he could do to help his tummy. The old man said that he should eat a banana and that it would make him feel better. 

So Sam ate the banana, and he felt much happier. From then on, whenever he felt sad he would find a yummy root in the forest - and that would always make him feel better.

Once upon a time there was a pumpkin plant. Every day it grew and grew until one day it was very big. 
Then, one day, a tiny seedling appeared and it grew into a small pumpkin. 
As the days went by, the pumpkin continued to grow bigger and bigger. It was so important to the farmer. 
Soon, it was the biggest, most beautiful pumpkin that the farmer had ever seen!
He was so excited and couldn't wait to pick it and make a delicious pumpkin pie. 
The pumpkin was so special and the farmer learned just how important it was to keep growing and taking care of the plants. 
The end.

Anna and Ben were twins who liked to help their mom in the kitchen. One day, mom asked them to peel some onions for the soup. Anna and Ben each took an onion and a knife and started to peel.

Anna peeled her onion very fast and threw the skin in the trash. She wanted to finish first and show mom how good she was. Ben peeled his onion very slowly and carefully. He wanted to make sure he did not cut himself or waste any onion. He put the skin in a bowl to use for compost later.

When they were done, Anna said to Ben, "Look, I peeled my onion faster than you. You are so slow and lazy. Mom will like my onion more than yours."

Ben felt sad and hurt by Anna's words. He said to Anna, "It is not nice to say that. Peeling onions is not a race. Mom will like both our onions because we helped her. And I did not throw away the skin. I saved it for the garden. That is good for the earth."

Mom heard their conversation and came to the kitchen. She smiled at Ben and said, "You are right, Ben. I admire how you peeled your onion with care and respect. You are a jolly and helpful boy. And I admire how you saved the skin for the compost. You are a smart and green boy."

She looked at Anna and said, "And I admire how you peeled your onion with speed and skill. You are a fast and clever girl. But I do not admire how you spoke to your brother. You were rude and mean. You should apologize to him and learn to be kind and humble."

Anna realized she was wrong and felt sorry. She said to Ben, "I am sorry, Ben. You are a good brother and I love you. Can you forgive me?"

Ben hugged Anna and said, "Of course I forgive you, Anna. You are a good sister and I love you too. Let's be friends and help mom together."

Mom hugged them both and said, "I am proud of you, Anna and Ben. You are both wonderful children and I love you very much. Now let's make some delicious soup with our onions."

The moral of the story is: Be kind and humble to others, and respect the earth.

Once there was a faucet in a back yard. It sparkled in the sunshine, but it was old and kind of rusty. Every spring, when the flowers started to wake up after a long winter, the faucet would wake too!

One spring, something funny happened. The faucet started to gurgle and spit and water started to come out! Everyone was surprised because the faucet had been still for so long. 

A little boy named Tommy was the first one to run over to the faucet. He was so excited to find water gushing out. He was a bit foolish though, because he didn't check to make sure it was okay first. Water splashed everywhere, and it even made mud puddles.

His mom came over to take a look. She scolded Tommy for not being careful around the faucet. She grabbed his hand and said, â€œNext time, be a bit more thoughtful, okay?â€

After that, Tommy was extra careful around the faucet. Every time it would spring to life in the spring, Tommy would stand by and make sure it was running safely. He never made the same mistake again.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy was feeling very sick, so his mommy took his temperature with a thermometer. She put the thermometer in Timmy's mouth and waited for it to beep. 

After a few minutes, the thermometer beeped and mommy saw that Timmy had a fever. She gave him some medicine to help him feel better. Timmy was so happy that his mommy knew how to use the thermometer to check his temperature. 

Timmy's mommy was very humble and always helped him when he was sick. Timmy loved his mommy very much and was grateful for all the things she did to take care of him.

Once upon a time, there were two friends, Robin and Daisy. They loved playing together. One day, they decided to go the park. At the park, Robin found a long line of ants. She pointed and said "Look Daisy, adorable ants." Daisy smiled and said, "Let's follow them." Robin and Daisy followed the line of ants until they reached the other side of the park. Once upon a time, there was a mommy and a little girl. The mommy had a whip and the little girl liked to play with it.

The mommy said, "No, you can't do it! The whip will hurt you!"

The little girl was determined and asked her mommy, "Why not?"

The little girl smiled and said, "I'm proud of me, too!"

Lily and Ben were drawing pictures with crayons on a big paper. They liked to make animals and flowers and houses. Lily was making a cat with a pink bow. Ben was making a car with four wheels.

"Look at my cat, Ben. Do you like it?" Lily asked.

"Yes, Lily. It is very pretty. Look at my car, Lily. Do you like it?" Ben asked.

"Yes, Ben. It is very fast. Can I draw a driver in your car?" Lily asked.

"OK, Lily. But hurry. Mom will come soon and we have to clean up." Ben said.

Lily took a black crayon and started to draw a face in the car. But she made a mistake. She drew a big nose that looked like a banana. She did not like it. She wanted to erase it.

"Ben, do you have an eraser?" Lily asked.

"No, Lily. I don't have an eraser. Maybe we can find one in the drawer." Ben said.

They went to the drawer and opened it. They saw many things inside. They saw pencils and scissors and glue and stickers. But they did not see an eraser.

They did not want Mom to see the banana nose. They wanted Mom to see the nice cat and the fast car. They wanted Mom to be happy. They hurried to find the eraser.

Once upon a time there was a boy named Tim.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the park with her friends. One day, they found a big slide and they all took turns sliding down it. Lily loved the feeling of the wind in her hair as she slid down the slide.

As they were playing, they saw an ugly dog walking towards them. The dog looked sad and scared. Lily and her friends decided to show the dog some love and kindness. They brought the dog some food and water and played with him. The dog soon became happy and wagged his tail.

From that day on, the dog would come to the park to play with Lily and her friends. They would slide down the slide together and have so much fun. Lily realized that even though the dog was ugly, he was still a good friend and she loved him just the same.

Once upon a time, there lived a little girl called Daisy. Daisy was very lucky and had lots of friends. But there was one thing that scared her--the big and scary wolf!

Every day, Daisy would go outside to play. But sometimes, when she least expected it, the wolf would appear from the dark woods! Daisy was very scared, but her friends were always there to help her.

One day, Daisy and her friends spotted the wolf again. But, instead of being scared like before, Daisy decided to be brave. She ran up to the wolf and petted it! The wolf was so surprised that he just sat there, politely!

The next morning, Daisy woke up to find that the wolf was gone. She wasn't sure if she would ever see her wolf friend again. But Daisy still felt very lucky. She knew the wolf was looking out for her, even when she couldn't see him.

Once upon a time there was a chubby little girl called Amy. She was only three years old and already full of curiosity. She especially enjoyed exploring the big old house she lived in.

So, very carefully, Amy backed away and left the vase in peace. She knew that it looked very special and fragile. As she left the room with a smile, she looked back at the vase and whispered: "Goodbye!".

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside in the sun. One day, Timmy found a bow and arrow. He wanted to try it out. 

Timmy pulled back the arrow and let it go. The arrow flew through the air and split a tree in two. Timmy was amazed!

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She loved to wear her green skirt because it made her feel happy. One day, Lily's mommy wanted to teach her how to bake cookies. Once upon a time, there was a little car named Cari. Cari was sad because she had no fuel. She wanted to go fast and play with her friends, but she couldn't. Cari hoped that she could find some fuel soon.

Cari got the fuel and went to play with her friends. They all had fun, and Cari shared the fuel with them. They were all very happy. In the end, Cari learned that sharing with friends is a good thing to do.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved cake very much. One day, her mom baked a cake for her birthday. It was a big, yummy cake with lots of frosting. Lily was so happy when she saw it.

Her friend, Timmy, came over to celebrate with her. They sat down at the table to eat some cake. Timmy said, "I can't hear the music. Are you deaf, Lily?" Lily replied, "No, I can hear just fine. Maybe you need to poke your ears."

Timmy poked his ears and suddenly, he could hear the music. They both laughed and enjoyed eating the cake together. It was a happy birthday for Lily.

Once there was an old man who had a pole. Every day, he would load it onto his truck and drive away. The truck was old and slow, but he was happy to ride around in it.

The little girl was fascinated by the pole and asked if she could have it. The old man smiled and said yes. He unloaded it from the back of the truck and gave it to her.

The little girl was so excited to have the old pole that she hugged the old man and said â€œThank you!â€

The old man drove away, happy that he could make someone's day.

One day, a little boy was feeling sad. He was sitting down in front of the television and watching cartoons. He heard someone knocking on the door. He opened the door and he was so surprised. It was his best friend!

After they finished clapping, the little boy was no longer sad. His best friend was the best medicine for his sadness. He waved goodbye to his best friend and went back to watching cartoons on the television.

Once there was a dependable cow who lived on a farm. She had the most beautiful horn which she was proud of. Every morning, the cow would go out for a walk and finish in the same spot by the river.

The next morning, the cow and the farmer raced around the farm. The cow had a strong start, but the farmer was right behind her. Just when the cow thought she was going to finish first, the farmer suddenly sprinted ahead and crossed the finish line first.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside with his friends. One day, Timmy's friend Johnny found a trophy in the park.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. She wanted to go to the park, but her mom said she needed to stay home. Lucy was sad and struggled to find something fun to do.

Once there was a girl named Elle. She was very brave and was always up for a challenge! One day she saw something in the bathroom that needed to be fixed. She thought to herself "I am so brave, I can do this!"

Once upon a time, there were two best friends, Carrie and Sam. They were very dependable and always stuck together. One day, Carrie said to Sam, â€œLet's climb the stairs!â€ so they grabbed hands and ran up the stairs.

Once upon a time, there was a famous bee called Buzzy. Buzzy liked to explore and discover new things. One day, Buzzy decided to fly around his meadow and see what he could find.
