Tom and Jen are friends. They like to play with toys. One day, they find a big toy car in the garage. It has wires and batteries. Tom wants to attach the wires to the batteries. He thinks it will make the car go faster.

"Look, Jen, I can make the car faster!" Tom says. He takes a wire and touches a battery.

"Ow!" Tom cries. He feels a shock in his hand. He drops the wire and the battery. He is sad and scared. He does not like the shock.

"Tom, are you okay?" Jen asks. She is worried about Tom. She runs to him and hugs him.

"I'm okay, Jen. But the shock hurt. It was not fun." Tom says. He hugs Jen back.

"I'm sorry, Tom. Maybe we should not play with the wires and batteries. They are not toys. They are dangerous." Jen says.

"You are right, Jen. They are not toys. They are for grown-ups. We should play with our own toys. They are safe and fun." Tom says.

Tom and Jen leave the big toy car in the garage. They go to their room and play with their own toys. They are happy and careful.

The moral of the story is: Do not play with things that are not toys. They can be dangerous and hurt you. Play with your own toys. They are safe and fun.

Simon and Molly were very excited to play together. They got their toys out and were ready to start. But then their mum noticed something was wrong.

Their cable had split. Now the two toys were different. Simon's was on one side and Molly's was on the other. They both wanted to play together, but how?

Mum had an idea. She took some sticky tape and stuck the cable back together. Now Simon and Molly were connected again.

They cheered and thanked their mum. Now they could play together! They were very happy to be back together again.

Once upon a time, there was a young girl who loved silver. Every night, she went to bed with a silver key in her pocket.

One night, the girl went to the old silver door and put the key in the lock. She turned the key and the door opened. Inside, she found lots of sparkling silver. She was so excited.

The next day, the girl went back to the door but it was now locked. She tried the key but it didn't fit in the lock. She was sad, but she knew she would find a way to open it again.

So every day she came back with something different trying to unlock the door. She tried a fork, a spoon and then a sock! But nothing worked.

Until one day, she tried the silver key again and it fit perfectly. She was so happy. She opened the door and ran inside, the silver was shining bright. She grabbed it all and ran home to show her family.

From that day on, the young girl was the happiest she had ever been with her special silver lock and key.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a clock in her room that tick-tocked all day long. One day, Lily's mommy came into her room and said, "Lily, it's time for bed. Let's spread your blanket tight over you."

Lily climbed into bed and her mommy spread the blanket tight over her. "Mommy, can you tell me a story?" asked Lily.

"Of course," said her mommy. "Once upon a time, there was a little bunny who wanted to spread some jelly on his toast. But he couldn't find the jelly jar anywhere."

Lily giggled and said, "Silly bunny! Where did the jelly jar go?"

"He finally found it hiding behind the clock," said her mommy.

Lily yawned and snuggled under her blanket. "Goodnight, mommy," she said.

"Goodnight, Lily," her mommy whispered, turning off the light.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim had a brown toy that he loved very much. One day, he lost his toy and was very sad.

Tim looked everywhere for his toy. He asked his friend, Sam, "Did you see my brown toy?" Sam said, "No, but let's look for it together." They looked all around, but they could not find the toy.

Then, Tim called his mom for help. She said, "Let's look in your room." They went to his room and found the toy under his bed. Tim was very happy and said, "Thank you, Mom and Sam!" The moral of the story is that when you need help, it's good to ask others, and working together makes things easier.

Once upon a time, there was a dependable fisherman. He lived near the river and every day he would go there to buy his fish. He was always happy when it was time to buy his fish because he knew he could always trust the fisherman. He never had to worry about the quality of the fish he was buying.

One day, the fisherman had a surprise for him. He asked the dependable fisherman if he wanted to go fishing with him. The dependable fisherman was so excited! He said yes and went with the other fisherman to the river. He spent all day catching fish and had so much fun.

When they were done fishing, the dependable fisherman had a lot of fish to buy. He thanked the other fisherman for taking him fishing, bought the fish and went home. He was so happy that he was able to buy lots of fish from a dependable fisherman. 

From then on, the dependable fisherman was his favorite place to buy fish and he went there whenever he wanted fish.

John and his Mom were running an errand one afternoon. As they walked, John saw a basketball. He ran up to it and peeked inside.
"Look Mom, an empty basketball!"
John's Mom smiled. "That's great, honey. Do you want to keep it?"
John was so excited. He ran back with the basketball and hugged it tight. 
John and his Mom kept walking, but now John had something special to hold on to. He peered inside the basketball every time they stopped.

At the store, John chose a few things to put inside the basketball. After each item, he peered inside to make sure everything fit. 
Back at home, John brought the basketball to his bedroom and peeked inside one more time. He was so proud of his work. The empty basketball was filled with treasures!

Little Josh was so excited. He was going to bury something special in the ground. He told his mom, "I'm gonna bury my toy truck in the ground." 

His mom smiled. "That's a great idea Josh, why don't you go pick a special spot?"

So Josh ran outside barefoot into the backyard. He found a little patch of grass and started digging a hole with a stick and his hands. He dug and dug until the hole was just deep enough for his little toy truck. He carefully put it into the hole, and then filled it back up with the dirt.

Then Josh said goodbye to his toy truck and smiled. "Bye truck! I'll come back and visit you soon." He then patted the dirt down and ran back inside. 

Josh knew he had buried something very special today and he could not be happier. he was sure he would never forget this special moment.

Lily and Max were at the beach with their mom and dad. They liked to play in the sand and look for shells and rocks. Sometimes they saw crabs and fish in the water. They had a lot of fun.

One day, they found a big, shiny shell in the sand. It was an oyster. Lily and Max wanted to open it and see what was inside. Maybe there was a pearl, they thought.

"Can we open it, mom?" Lily asked.

"Be careful, kids. Oysters can be sharp and hurt your fingers. And maybe the oyster is alive and does not want to be opened. You have to behave and respect the animals," mom said.

"But we want to see, mom. Please, please, please," Max begged.

Mom sighed and said, "Okay, but only if you are very gentle and use this knife. And you have to share whatever you find, okay?"

Lily and Max nodded and took the knife. They carefully pried the oyster open and looked inside. They gasped. There was a pearl, but not a white one. It was a pink one. And it was very cute.

"Wow, it's so pretty," Lily said.

"It's amazing," Max said.

They showed the pearl to their mom and dad, who were also surprised and happy. They said it was a rare and special find. They said Lily and Max could keep it as a souvenir of their beach day.

Lily and Max smiled and hugged each other. They decided to share the pearl and take turns wearing it as a necklace. They thanked the oyster for giving them such a beautiful gift. They said they were sorry for opening it and hoped it was not too angry. They put the oyster back in the water and said goodbye.

They had a wonderful day at the beach. They learned to behave and respect the animals. And they found a cute pink pearl. They were very lucky.

Once upon a time, there were two friends, Peter and Jake. They liked to travel a lot.

One day, they decided to take a trip on a hot air balloon. They got ready and went on the hot air balloon. They were so excited.

When they were flying, they saw a big curtain and wondered what it was. They flew closer and closer, but then, their balloon started flying away.

Jake cried, "Oh no! We're going the wrong way! What can we do?".

Peter, who was always so brave, said, "Don't worry, my friend. I have an idea".

Peter took a piece of string from his pocket, and with it and some clever thinking, he was able to catch the curtain. With it, Peter and Jake were able to travel closer and closer to the weird curtain.

When they were close enough, they saw that it was actually a giant waterfall. It was so beautiful, but they had been so careless and almost missed it.

Peter and Jake smiled at each other. Then, they laughed and waved goodbye to the waterfall before continuing their journey.

Sara and Tom were playing with paper and crayons. They wanted to make shapes and animals. Sara had scissors, but Tom did not. Tom asked Sara, "Can you lend me your scissors, please?"

Sara said, "No, they are mine. You can use your hands to tear the paper."

Tom was sad. He wanted to cut the paper, not tear it. He said, "Please, Sara, I will give them back to you. I just want to make a star."

Sara said, "No, no, no. Go away, Tom. You are annoying me."

Tom was angry. He did not like Sara. He wanted to make her sorry. He waited until Sara was not looking. Then he grabbed her scissors and ran away.

Sara saw Tom with her scissors. She was very mad. She shouted, "Tom, give me back my scissors, now!"

Tom did not listen. He laughed and ran faster. He did not see where he was going. He tripped over a toy and fell down. The scissors cut his hand. He cried out loud. He dropped the scissors and held his hand. It was bleeding.

Sara ran to Tom. She saw his hand. She was scared. She said, "Tom, are you okay? I'm sorry, I did not mean to make you angry. Here, take my crayons. They are nice and soft."

Tom did not want her crayons. He wanted his hand to stop hurting. He said, "Go away, Sara. You are mean. You did not lend me your scissors. Now I am hurt. I don't want to play with you anymore."

Sara felt bad. She wanted to help Tom. She wanted to be his friend. But Tom did not want her. He pushed her away. He cried louder and louder. Sara cried too. She wished she had lent him her scissors. She wished they had played nicely. But it was too late. They had both ruined their fun.

Once upon a time, in a big green forest, there lived a friendly squirrel named Sam. Sam loved to play with his friends and find nuts to eat. One day, while looking for nuts, Sam met a little bird named Bella.

"Hi, I'm Bella," said the bird. "Do you want to play with me?"

"Yes! I like to play," Sam replied. They played together all day long, running and jumping in the forest. They also found many nuts to eat.

As the sun began to set, Sam and Bella started to feel tired. "I think it's time to sleep," said Sam. Bella agreed, and they found a cozy spot under a big tree. Sam curled up in his nest, and Bella tucked her head under her wing. They both closed their eyes and went to sleep, dreaming of the fun they had that day.

Once upon a time there was a graceful bird. It always flew high above the town and would feed the clouds with its secret. The bird was so graceful that everyone in town wanted to see it but no one could ever get close enough.

One day a little boy found the bird. He was only three years old but he wanted to show the bird how much he cared. He started to give it bits of bread that his parents had given him. The bird ate them and seemed to like them.

The little boy kept feeding the bird every day until one day the beautiful bird flew away. It left behind its secret which was a shining feather. The little boy kept it safe like a treasure and knew that the bird would always be with him.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Daisy and Joe. Daisy was a shy girl and Joe was a happy boy. 

They were best friends and they liked to play together. But one day they had a quarrel. They both wanted to play a game but they could not agree - Daisy wanted to play hide and seek and Joe wanted to play tag. 

After a while they stopped quarreling and decided to do something else. They started to dance around the room. Joe jumped up and down and Daisy twirled around. They laughed as they danced and it was great fun. 

When they were tired of dancing Daisy said to Joe, "Let's play hide and seek now!" Joe was excited to agree and soon they were playing their favorite game together. 

They had so much fun playing hide and seek and making up new games that they both forgot about their quarrel. It was a happy day for Daisy and Joe.

Once upon a time there was a little bear. He wanted to climb up on the roof to spot the stars in the night sky.

He climbed up onto the roof and was amazed at what he saw! But the roof was slippery and soon the little bear started to slip. He was so scared that he folded his arms around to hold onto the roof.

The bear's father saw what had happened and ran outside. He helped the bear back down from the roof. The bear looked at his father's face and said: "I'm sorry Daddy".

His father smiled and said: "It's alright, my dear. Let's go inside and have some hot chocolate." So the little bear and his father hugged each other and went inside to have some hot chocolate.

The little bear was so excited to have spotted the stars that he folded the memory away in his heart.

Molly and Jack played together in the garden. Jack was wearing a lovely mask, with colourful feathers and a sparkly star. Molly thought it was very cool.

They decided to have a tea party. Molly brought her dolls, and Jack brought his mask. They had lots of fun, pouring pretend tea and eating pretend cake.

The sun began to set, so Jack and Molly hugged each other goodbye. Jack said he had better go home and take his lovely mask off.

Molly waved goodbye and then she watched as Jack disappeared from sight. She knew that even though they weren't together, their love would stay forever.

Once upon a time, there was a big gorilla. He lived in a jungle with his friends. One day, he wanted to decorate his treehouse. He asked his friends to help him. They all said yes! They picked out fine leaves and colorful flowers to decorate the treehouse. It looked so pretty! The gorilla was happy and thanked his friends. They all had fun together. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a tiny boy. He was very tidy and he had a special cup for his milk.

Every day the boy would drink his milk and he was always so happy. But one day, something different happened.

The boy went to his cup, but it was empty. He said to himself, "Where is my milk?"

He searched all around the house, but he couldn't find it. Then he asked his mum, "Where is my milk?"

His mum replied, "The cat has gained it."

The boy was so upset. He had no milk and he was very sad. 

The boy never saw his milk again, and he never felt so unhappy. No more milk for him again.

One day there was a little girl who was out playing in the park. She had a magical box of chalk and she didn't know what it could do. She saw a fluffy white bunny hopping around in the park and wished she could draw the bunny with her box of chalk.

The little girl asked the bunny, "Do you know what I can do with this box of chalk?"

The bunny replied, "Why don't you let me show you?"

The little girl happily agreed and the bunny hopped around in circles and shape in the park. The bunny's movements with the chalk created a beautiful yellow and pink drawing of flowers. 

The little girl was so amazed and thanked the bunny for helping. She was feeling lucky because of her magical box of chalk.

The little girl smiled as she watched the bunny hopping away, going about its own adventures. 

The little girl thanked the bunny again for being so helpful and said goodbye to her furry friend. She was looking forward to going back to the park again soon.

Once upon a time, there was a stubborn sheep. He didn't like the other sheep and he always wanted to be alone. One day, the other sheep let him go off on his own. He had a big roll of wool with him.

The sheep was very happy and he started to run. He sprinted through the fields and the hills. He jumped in and out of bushes.

When he came to a big stream, the sheep wanted to cross it but it was too wide and deep. Then, he had an idea! He got out his roll of wool and started to wrap it around his feet. He was very clever. 

He floated across the stream with the wool. Soon, the sheep was on the other side! He was so pleased with himself and the other sheep were very impressed.

From then on, the stubborn sheep was allowed to go off on his own when he wanted to. The wool had allowed him to cross the big stream.

Once upon a time there was a boy. He was three years old and very obedient. He loved to play in the park near his house.

Every day, he would run to the park. He loved to watch the birds and see the flowers. His mom and dad were very happy because he was a good boy.

In the park, he would play games with his friends. They would jump and run, and have fun together.

When it was time to go home, the boy would always run back home. He always obeyed his parents and stayed safe.

His mom and dad were very proud of their obedient and playful son. He always had lots of fun playing in the park!

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toy cars and trucks all day long. One day, his mom asked him to clean up his toys and go to bed, but Timmy didn't want to stop playing. He decided to ignore his mom and keep playing.

The next day, Timmy's mom took away his toy cars and trucks and told him he couldn't play with them until he cleaned up his room. Timmy felt uncomfortable without his toys, but he knew he had to clean up his room to get them back.

As Timmy was cleaning up his room, he found an old board under his bed. He didn't know what to do with it, so he asked his mom. She said they could use the board to make a new shelf for his toys. Timmy was so excited to have a new shelf for his toys, he quickly finished cleaning his room.

From that day on, Timmy learned to listen to his mom and not ignore her. He also learned that sometimes uncomfortable things can lead to something good, like his new toy shelf.

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play in their room. They had many toys, but their favorite was a big clock that made funny sounds. The clock had a red button that made it say the time, and a blue button that made it play music.

One day, Lily and Ben were playing with the clock when their mom called them for lunch. "Come on, kids, it's time to eat!" she said. Lily and Ben did not want to stop playing, so they ignored their mom. They pressed the red button and the clock said, "It's twelve o'clock. Time to eat!"

Lily and Ben laughed and pressed the blue button. The clock played a song that said, "Follow me, follow me, let's have some fun!" Lily and Ben liked the song, so they decided to follow the clock. They picked it up and ran out of their room. They did not see their mom, who was waiting for them in the kitchen.

They followed the clock down the stairs, through the hall, and out the door. They ran across the street, into the park, and up the hill. They did not see the cars, the people, or the signs. They only heard the clock, who said, "Follow me, follow me, let's have some fun!"

But the clock was not a good friend. It did not care about Lily and Ben. It only wanted to make them run and get tired. It did not tell them to be careful, to look both ways, or to stay close to home. It did not care if they got lost, hurt, or scared.

Soon, Lily and Ben realized that they had gone too far. They did not know where they were, or how to get back. They looked around and saw no one they knew. They felt hungry, thirsty, and cold. They wished they had listened to their mom, and not to the clock.

They hugged each other and cried. They did not know what to do. They pressed the red button, hoping the clock would help them. But the clock only said, "It's one o'clock. Time to eat!" They pressed the blue button, hoping the clock would play a nice song. But the clock only played a loud noise that hurt their ears.

They threw the clock on the ground and broke it. They did not like the clock anymore. They wanted their mom. They wanted to go home.

Luckily, a kind lady saw them and asked them what was wrong. They told her their names and where they lived. She called their mom and told her where they were. She gave them some water and a cookie and waited with them until their mom came.

Their mom was very worried and angry. She hugged them and scolded them. She told them they had been very naughty and foolish. She told them they should never follow a clock, or any other thing, that told them to do bad things. She told them they should always listen to her, and to their own hearts, that told them to do good things.

Lily and Ben felt very sorry and ashamed. They apologized to their mom and thanked the kind lady. They learned their lesson. They never played with the clock again. They never followed anything that did not care about them. They always listened to their mom, and to their own hearts, that cared about them.

One day, a little girl named Amy was playing in her room. She felt a bit nervous because it was her first day at a new school. As she looked around, she saw a big letter on her bed. She picked it up and read it. It was from her new friend, Tom.

Tom wrote, "Hi Amy! I can't wait to play with you at school. We will have lots of fun!" Amy smiled and felt less nervous. She wanted to write a letter back to Tom, but she felt a yawn coming. She was very tired from playing all day.

Amy went to her mom and said, "Mom, I want to write a letter to Tom, but I am so tired." Her mom said, "It's okay, Amy. You can write the letter tomorrow before school." Amy felt happy and went to bed. She knew she would have a great day at school with her new friend, Tom.

Once upon a time, there was a careless boy named Jack. One day, he decided to go for a swim in the sea. Jack went in deeper and deeper until he couldn't touch the ground anymore.

Suddenly, he saw a shark! Jack got so scared that he started to shiver. He didn't know what to do! He tried to swim away, but the shark was getting closer.

Then, Jack remembered his father had told him: "If you ever get scared, always look the shark in the eyes and say 'I'm not afraid!'". 

Jack looked the shark in the eyes and said "I'm not afraid!" He said it as loud and as firm as he could. To Jack's surprise, the shark swam away! 

The water became peaceful again. Jack was relieved and happy! He swam back to shore and never went to the deep ocean again.

Once there was a little girl. She was chubby and had beautiful blond hair and big brown eyes.

One day the little girl was walking in the park when she found an old newspaper. It was crumpled up and looked like it had been outside for a long time.

The little girl wanted to take the newspaper home with her. She carefully folded it up and tucked it under her arm.

On the way home she stopped at the store. She bought herself a new newspaper. She wanted to compare the old one to the new one.

When she arrived home, she spread out the old newspaper and the new one on the table. She carefully examined them side by side.

At last she closed the old newspaper and put it away. She kept the new one to read.

She was so happy with her discovery. It was like she found a treasure!

Little Andy was playing in the garden one sunny day when he heard a loud trumpet. He trotted over to see what it was. He arrived in the field, and noticed a bright yellow duck playing a trumpet. The duck quacked, "Hi Andy! Would you like to play with me? I'm practising to be a trumpet player!" Andy giggled and replied, "Yes, I would!"

The duck smiled, and held out her trumpet for Andy. She said, "Go on, have a try. Just push your lips together and blow." Andy put his lips together and blew gently. To his surprise, out came a loud sound! The duck laughed, "Good job! Keep blowing like that and you'll get better. Let's have a game. Ready, set, go!"

The duck started to quack and Andy had to use his trumpet to keep up with the quacks. Whenever the duck quacked, Andy had to yield a note from his trumpet. They carried on playing like this for a while and Andy became more and more alert. He was getting better at playing the trumpet. After a while, they both got tired and the duck said it was time to go. Andy thanked her for teaching him how to play the trumpet and promised to come back again. He waved goodbye and ran off, feeling very happy.

Once upon a time there was a cute little horse. Her name was Daisy and she loved to take long walks in the sunshine. One day as Daisy was walking along, she stumbled on a bumpy rock. She felt a bit scared but was determined to keep going.

Soon, Daisy found herself in a beautiful meadow. Everything around her looked so soft and inviting. She began to nibble on some of the sweet grass when she noticed a butterfly fluttering by her. She tried to chase it, but the butterfly flew too quickly!

So Daisy decided to take a rest and sit in the grass. Suddenly she heard a gentle neigh in the distance. She looked up and saw a lovely little foal trotting towards her. She had never seen a foal before and she was so excited!

Daisy slowly made her way closer to the foal and soon they were nose to nose. Daisy felt so happy to have made a new friend and the two of them started to play together. They tumbled around the meadow and had a wonderful time. 

By the end of the day, Daisy had made a new best friend and was feeling very content. She couldn't wait for the next time they could meet up and play together again.

Lily and Ben loved to play with their toy boat. It was red and white and had a big engine. They liked to sail it in the bathtub and make noises like "vroom" and "splash".

One day, they decided to take their boat to the pond in the park. They asked their mom if they could go, and she said yes, but they had to be careful and not lose their boat. They put their boat in a bag and walked to the park with their mom.

At the pond, they saw many ducks and geese. They were adorable and quacked and honked. Lily and Ben wanted to feed them some bread, but their mom said no, because it was bad for them. They agreed and took out their boat instead.

They put their boat in the water and turned on the engine. It sailed fast and made waves. They laughed and cheered and followed their boat along the shore. They saw other kids with their toys and said hello.

But then, something bad happened. Their boat sailed too far and got stuck in some reeds. They could not reach it or see it. They felt sad and scared. They called their mom and told her what happened.

Their mom hugged them and said it was okay. She said they could try to get their boat back, but they had to be patient and smart. She said she had an idea. She took out her phone and called someone.

Soon, a man came with a big net. He was their mom's friend and he worked at the pond. He said he could help them. He used his net to fish out their boat from the reeds. He gave it back to them and smiled.

Lily and Ben were so happy. They thanked the man and hugged their mom. They said they were sorry for losing their boat and they would be more careful next time. Their mom said she was proud of them and they could still play with their boat, but they had to stay close to her.

They agreed and sailed their boat again. They had fun and learned a lesson. They loved their boat and their mom and their mom's friend. They were a happy family.

Once upon a time there was a tall tree. It was so tall that it reached up into the sky. One day, a little boy touched the tree. Suddenly, the tree began to glow with a bright light. The boy was curious and excited. 

The boy said, â€œWhat happened?â€

The tree answered, â€œI lit up because you touched me.â€ 

The boy was very surprised. He asked the tree, â€œCan you do more?â€ 

The tree nodded, and from its branches, a rainbow of colors shone down. The boy was filled with joy. He touched the tree again, and the tree lit up with even more light. 

The little boy smiled big and said, â€œThis is the most beautiful thing Iâ€™ve ever seen.â€ 

The tree smiled back and said, â€œThank you for touching me.â€

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Cindy. She was very special because she could grow things with her magical spell. Wherever she went she would cast her spell and flowers would grow out of the ground. Even bees and butterflies followed her around! Everyone was so impressed by her magic.

Every day, Cindy would explore and find new places to grow things. She would use her impressive spell and make trees bloom and fruits sprout out of the ground. Birds would then come to eat the fruits that Cindy created. It was very cool! 

One day, Cindy wanted to make something really special. She closed her eyes, held her hands to her chest, and said her magical spell. When she opened her eyes, she couldn't believe what she saw! A big, beautiful castle had appeared out of nowhere. It was so impressive! 

From that day on, Cindy's magical spell was known all over the world. People admired her special talent and she was able to create even more amazing things!

Ben and Lily were twins who lived in a big city. They liked to see many interesting things in the city, like tall buildings, colorful cars, and noisy trains. One day, they went to the park with their mom and dad. They saw a big pond with ducks and fish.

Ben and Lily wanted to feed the ducks and fish. They asked their mom and dad to give them some bread. Their mom and dad gave them some bread and told them to be careful and not go too close to the water. Ben and Lily nodded and ran to the pond.

Ben and Lily threw some bread to the ducks and fish. The ducks and fish came to eat the bread. Ben and Lily were happy and laughed. They wanted to see the ducks and fish better. They went closer and closer to the water.

But they did not listen to their mom and dad. They went too close to the water. They slipped and fell into the pond. The water was cold and deep. Ben and Lily were scared and cried. They could not swim. They called for their mom and dad.

Their mom and dad heard them and ran to the pond. They jumped into the water and tried to save Ben and Lily. But the water was too cold and too deep. They could not reach Ben and Lily. Ben and Lily sank to the bottom of the pond. They did not come up again.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a big bear. The bear was very sad because he had a broken toy. He wanted to play with it, but he couldn't because it was broken. 

One day, a kind girl saw the bear and his broken toy. She wanted to help the bear, so she asked him if he wanted her to repair his toy. The bear was so happy and said yes. 

The girl took the toy and went home. She used some glue to repair it. It was a mild day, so she left the toy outside to dry. When it was ready, she brought it back to the bear. The bear was overjoyed and gave the girl a big hug to say thank you. From that day on, the bear and the girl were good friends.

Lily liked to wonder about many things. She wondered why the sky was blue, why the grass was green, and why the birds could fly. She also wondered what it would be like to ride a bicycle. She had seen other children ride bicycles on the street, and they looked so happy and fast.

One day, Lily's dad came home with a big surprise. He had a red bicycle for Lily. It was shiny and new, and it had a bell and a basket. Lily was so excited. She hugged her dad and thanked him. She wanted to try the bicycle right away.

Dad helped Lily put on a helmet and showed her how to pedal and steer. Lily was a little scared at first, but she was also brave and curious. She felt the wind in her hair and the sun on her face. She rang the bell and waved to her mom. She felt like she was flying.

Lily loved her red bicycle. She rode it every day, and she learned to go faster and turn better. She wondered what other places she could go with her bicycle. She wondered what other adventures she could have. She wondered what other surprises her dad had for her. She was a happy and wonder-full girl.

Once there was a nosy girl who wanted to explore the world. One day, she wanted to see what was at the top of a twisty tall tree. She looked up and saw that the branches were so high and thick, so she tied her skirt around the trunk.

"I'm a twisty climber!" the girl said. She started to climb up slowly but as soon as she got near the very top, she started to go faster. Suddenly, she could see the whole world from up high!

But then she heard voices calling from below. Her nosy neighbours were looking up from the ground, wanting to see what she was doing. The girl was embarrassed and quickly climbed back down.

"What were you doing up there?" an old lady asked.

"I was twisting around the tree and exploring the world," the girl answered.

The old lady smiled and said, "You sure are adventurous! Don't forget to take your skirt with you."

The nosy girl smiled and skipped away with her skirt in her hand, ready to explore the world again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sally.
She had a fancy bedroom with a soft, cozy bed.
One day, Sally was in her bedroom playing.
Suddenly she heard her mom calling her name.

Sally: "Mom, what is it?"
Mom: "Sally, remember, you must never lie. Lying is not nice."
Sally: "Yes, Mom, I won't lie."

Sally was sad because she really wanted to lie and pretend that her bedroom was even more fancy than it really was.
But Sally remembered what her Mom had said and decided not to lie. 
Instead, she hugged her Mom to show how much she loved her. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to mix different colors of paint together. He would mix blue and yellow to make green, and red and blue to make purple. One day, Timmy's mom asked him to help her hang up some clothes on the hanger. Timmy was happy to help, and he hung up all the clothes neatly.

As Timmy and his mom were hanging up the clothes, their nosy neighbor, Mrs. Johnson, came over. "What are you two doing?" she asked. "We're hanging up clothes," Timmy replied. "Oh, I see," said Mrs. Johnson, looking around. "What a nice mix of colors you have on those hangers!"

Timmy smiled proudly, knowing that he had helped his mom and made a nice mix of colors on the hangers. Mrs. Johnson smiled too, and went back to her own house. Timmy and his mom finished hanging up the clothes, and Timmy went back to his paint mixing, happy to have helped his mom and shown off his skills to their nosy neighbor.

Once upon a time, there were two friends, Ben and Betty. They both loved to laugh and were always very happy. 

One day, Ben and Betty were playing together in the park. Ben had a special sock and it was very popular amongst all the children in the park. The special sock had stars and stripes on it and it was Ben's favorite. 

As they were playing, they started to laugh and laugh until they couldn't stop. Everyone in the park noticed them and started to laugh too. Even the birds in the trees were laughing!

The laughter was so much fun that Ben and Betty kept on laughing until the sun set and it was time to go home. 

As Ben accidentally left his special sock behind in the park, Betty had one last giggle before she ran off to find it. When she returned with the sock, Ben and Betty burst into loud laughter again, happy that Ben had his favorite sock back. 

They laughed until the sun set and it was time to go home. Ben and Betty were very happy, and they both had a great time together in the park.

Once upon a time, there was a jolly frog named Freddy. Freddy loved to play his flute by the pond every day. One day, a little duck named Daisy waddled up to him and said, "Wow, you play so well! Can I try?"

Freddy handed her his flute and watched as Daisy blew into it. She made a loud, squeaky noise that made Freddy laugh. "That was great!" he said, applauding her effort.

From then on, Freddy and Daisy played music together every day. They had so much fun that all the other animals in the forest would come to listen and applaud their music. Freddy and Daisy were very happy, and they knew they would be friends forever.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved playing with his toy cars and trucks. One day, Timmy's dad brought home a new toy truck with a motor. Timmy was so excited to play with it, but he didn't understand how to make it go.

"Dad, how do I make it go?" Timmy asked.

"You have to press this button," Dad said, showing Timmy the button on the truck.

Timmy tried pressing the button, but the truck wouldn't move. He tried and tried, but he couldn't make it go. He was so sad and thought he wasn't successful.

"Don't worry, Timmy," Dad said. "You just need to keep trying. You'll understand how to make it work eventually."

So, Timmy kept trying and trying, and finally, he was successful! He made the truck go all by himself. Timmy learned that sometimes things are hard at first, but if you keep trying, you can understand and be successful.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to draw on paper with his crayons. One day, Timmy wanted to make a special picture for his mommy's birthday. He drew a brilliant rainbow with lots of colors.

But then, Timmy's little sister came and wanted to play with his picture. Timmy didn't want his picture to get ruined, so he decided to separate it from his sister. He put his picture up high on the fridge where his sister couldn't reach it.

Timmy's mommy loved the picture so much that she put it in a frame and hung it on the wall. Timmy was so happy that his picture was safe and his mommy loved it. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy who loved to play with his toy jeep. He would drive it around the house and make vroom vroom sounds. One day, Timmy's sister came into the room and asked, "Can I play with your jeep, Timmy?" Timmy replied, "Sure, but be careful not to throw it too hard."

His sister played with the jeep for a little while, but then she accidentally threw it too hard and it hit the wall. Timmy got upset and said, "You broke my jeep!" His sister felt bad and said, "I'm sorry, Timmy. Let's try to fix it together."

They worked together to fix the jeep, and when they were done, Timmy said, "It's all better now. Let's play together and have a peaceful time." They played with the jeep together, and Timmy's sister made sure not to throw it too hard again. They had a lot of fun and felt happy. The end.

Once there was a bear who lived in a deep valley. He was very lonely and wanted a friend. One day, he found a rabbit in the valley and asked the rabbit to be his friend. But the rabbit refused. The bear was so sad. He tried asking other animals, but they all refused too. The bear was lonely and walked through the valley by himself. Suddenly, he heard a noise. The bear looked all around and discovered a new animal in the valley. It was a tiny mouse. The bear asked the mouse to be his friend. The mouse happily agreed. The bear and the mouse became very good friends and played together every day in the deep valley.

Tom and Sam are friends. They like to play with cars and blocks. One day, Tom has a new car. It is red and shiny. Sam wants to play with it too.

"Can I have your car?" Sam asks Tom.

"No, it is mine. You can play with your own car," Tom says.

"But your car is nicer. Please, let me have it for a little bit," Sam begs.

"No, you will spoil it. Go away," Tom says. He pushes Sam.

Sam is angry and sad. He runs to his mom. He tells her what Tom did. His mom gives him a hug. She writes a message on a paper. She tells Sam to give it to Tom.

Sam goes back to Tom. He gives him the paper. Tom reads the message. It says: "Sharing is caring. Be a good friend. Don't spoil the fun."

Tom feels sorry. He looks at Sam. He says: "I'm sorry, Sam. You can play with my car. I was not nice to you."

Sam smiles. He says: "Thank you, Tom. You are a good friend. Can we play together?"

Tom nods. He says: "Yes, we can. Sharing is easy and fun."

They play with the cars and blocks. They are happy. They are friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy liked to play with his toys, especially his toy cars. One day, Timmy's friend Billy came over to play. Billy had a toy weapon that he wanted to show Timmy. Timmy got nervous when he saw the weapon because he didn't like scary things.

Billy noticed that Timmy was nervous, so he put the weapon away and they decided to play with Timmy's toy cars instead. They pretended that the cars were racing and they even tried to number the cars in order from 1 to 10. Timmy was happy that they were playing with his cars and not the scary weapon.

After they finished playing, Timmy's mom gave them some cookies and milk. They sat at the table and talked about their favorite toys. Timmy told Billy that he liked his toy cars the best and Billy said that he liked his toy weapon, but he promised not to bring it over again if it made Timmy nervous. From that day on, they had fun playing together without any scary weapons. The end.

There was once a thin monkey who lived in the jungle. He loved to joke with his friends. Every morning he made a joke as soon as he woke up. All of the other animals laughed and enjoyed his jokes. One day he met another monkey who was new to the jungle. He wanted to make her laugh too. So he made a joke and waited to see what she would do. She looked at him with a big smile, then she laughed and laughed. The thin monkey felt so happy that he could make her smile. Everyone in the jungle was very happy to have the new monkey. They all laughed and joked and had a lot of fun together.

Once upon a time there was a big party. All the guests were so polite.

The party was served lots of tasty treats and drinks. Everyone said how delicious everything was.

When the guests were done eating, they all stayed to talk and laugh. They said how nice it was to be together and to enjoy the party.

At the end of the night, the party was over. Everyone said goodbye to the host and thanked him for the nice party. They were very polite and kind.

The host thanked each guest for coming and said he had enjoyed their stay. Everyone left with a smile on their face and happy memories of the party.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy was very sleepy because he stayed up late playing with his toys. He wanted to take a nap, but he couldn't sleep because he was too excited. 

Timmy's dad came into the room and asked him what was wrong. Timmy told his dad that he was too excited because he won a big victory at his game. His dad was very proud of him and gave him a big hug. 

Then, Timmy's dad said he had a surprise for him. He printed out a picture of Timmy with his victory and hung it up on the wall. Timmy was so happy and felt proud of himself. He finally felt sleepy and took a nap while looking at his victory picture. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a furry dog named Spot. Spot loved to jog in the park. One sunny day, Spot met a little girl named Lucy. Lucy had a big smile on her face.

"Hi," said Lucy. "I like your furry coat."

"Thank you," barked Spot. "I like to jog. Do you want to jog with me?"

Lucy thought for a moment and then said, "Yes, I believe I do!"

So, Spot and Lucy jogged together in the park. They jogged up and down the hills, and around the big trees. They had so much fun that they became best friends.

From that day on, Spot and Lucy would always jog together in the park. They believed that they were the best jogging buddies ever. And they lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a beautiful gem that lived in the forest. Every day the gem shined brightly for all to see. One day, a naughty boy saw the gem and wanted to touch it. He ran to the gem as fast as he could and tried to pick it up. But the gem didn't want to be touched, so it called for help.

Suddenly, a kind fairy arrived and stopped the boy from picking up the gem. The fairy asked the boy why he wanted the gem and the boy said it was because it was so shiny and pretty. The fairy smiled and said the gem was special and should stay in the forest. The boy agreed and the fairy thanked him.

The fairy then helped the gem finish its task. She patted the gem, so it wouldn't be spoiled, and told it to stay in the forest. The gem thanked the fairy and said it would never leave. The fairy waved goodbye and flew away.

The gem stayed in the forest and was happy. Every day, when the sun shone, the gem shined too, so everyone remembered the kindness of the fairy.

Once upon a time, there was an unknown ornament. It was sparkly and colorful, and it was kept in a special box. One day, the ornament decided to explore outside.

It hopped out of the box and started to look around. Before long, it noticed a little girl. She was wearing a bright yellow dress and playing with a shiny ball.

The girl noticed the ornament and smiled. She reached out and said, "Can I keep you?" The ornament was so delighted! She said yes, and the girl carefully removed the ornament out of the box.

The girl took the ornament and put it on the window sill. She said, "Now you can watch the birds and trees!" The ornament was so happy to be out of the box, and it noticed its reflection in the window.

It was now the harmless ornament's very special home. And that is the end of the story.

Once upon a time there was a hot cactus. The cactus lived in the dessert and it was very happy. Then one day, the cactus started to get hot and hot. It got so hot that it just disappeared! The cactus was gone and it was never seen again. Where did the cactus go? Nobody knows. Nobody will ever know what happened to the hot cactus.

George and his Mommy were walking down the street. Suddenly, George stopped in front of a tall ice cream store. He looked up at his Mommy and asked, "Can I choose?" She smiled and said, "Yes, you can choose one."

George looked around excitedly. He saw many choices! He saw ice cream that was chocolate, strawberry and vanilla. He even saw ice cream with sprinkles! He thought and thought until he finally chose. He chose tall ice cream with rainbow sprinkles.

George and his Mommy walked up to the counter. He was so excited, he practically bounced! The nice lady at the counter handed George his tall ice cream. He put it up to his face and smiled.

George was so happy! He was so glad he was able to choose his own special ice cream. He licked it and smiled. Mommy and George enjoyed their special treat together.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Kim. She was three years old and she had beautiful, long hair. Every morning, her mom would sit her in front of the mirror while her dad split her hair into two parts. 

One morning, Kim's mom said, "What a deep split you have today, Kim. I can hardly tell it apart! Let's put a bow in each side of your hair so everyone can see."

Kim was so excited that she jumped up and ran out of the room. Moments later, she came back with two bows in her hands. She said, "Mommy, look at how beautiful my hair looks!" 

Her mom smiled and said, "You look very lovely today, honey. Now go play!" 

Kim looked into the mirror and smiled. She was very proud of the deep split in her hair and her new bowsâ€”she had never looked so beautiful before! 

Her mom gave her a big hug and said, "You look perfect, just the way you are!"

Once there was a little dog named Jack. He was so little and helpless, he could only crawl around. One day, Jack decided to explore the world around him. He started to climb up the stairs, but suddenly he saw something strange in the corner - a big pile of spaghetti! He just couldn't resist trying it.

Jack started crawling closer and he could smell the delicious spaghetti. He was about to eat it when suddenly he heard a voice: "No, Jack! You can't eat this spaghetti!" It was Jack's mommy. She had found him trying to eat spaghetti and she knew he was too little to do it on his own.

Jack was so embarrassed and he crawled away, feeling so helpless. His mommy smiled and said, "Don't worry, Jack. I'll make you your own plate of spaghetti for dinner later. You can have it then!" Jack was so happy and he crawled away to find something else to do. 

He never forgot that day, and he still loves spaghetti to this day.

The little girl was playing in the sun. She observed her surroundings with wide eyes and saw the clay in the dirt. She smiled with delight and began forming it into different shapes. 

Her father soon joined her. He watched her playing and said, "It looks like you are having fun with the clay."

The little girl was happy someone was observing her. She looked up at her father and said, "Yes! I'm making a cat. What should I do next?"

"Why don't you decorate it and make it spoiled?" her father suggested.

The little girl nodded eagerly and began adding details to her clay creation using the tiny rocks around her. When she finished, her cat was indeed spoiled.

The little girl smiled up at her father with pride and he smiled back. She had observed her environment and created something amazing with the clay.

Once upon a time, there was a competitive infant named Susie. Everywhere she went, Susie wanted to be the best. She would race the other babies around in their strollers and laugh whenever she won. 

One day, a voice came out of nowhere. It asked Susie, "Do you want to play a game?". Susie hesitated, "What kind of game?" she asked. 

The voice answered, "It's an answering game. I'll ask a question, and you have to answer." Susie smiled and said, "Yes, I want to play!"

So the voice started asking questions, and Susie answered them all without a problem. She was having so much fun. Then the voice said, "This is the last question. When the answer is right, you will be the winner."

Susie was so excited and started to answer with all her might. Suddenly, the voice proclaimed, "You are the winner! Congratulations, Susie!"

Susie was so happy and proud of herself. She had proven that she was the most competitive infant around!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. She wanted to play outside, but the weather wouldn't let her. It was too cloudy and cold. Lucy tried to resist, but the weather was too strong.

So instead, she decided to do some activities inside her house. But these activities were too boring. Lucy wanted something real fun. She tried to resist the urge to be bored, but nothing could make the day exciting.

Suddenly, an idea came to her. She ran to her room and found her old art supplies. She brought them to the living room and made a colorful picture. The picture was full of bright colors like blue, yellow, and pink.

Now Lucy was happy. She was no longer bored and she was proud that she resisted the urge to stay inside and be dull. Instead, she found a way to make her day more fun.

Jimmy was a little boy. He really liked to jog. Every day he would go to the park with his dad and jog along the path. 

Jimmy's dad liked to play the guitar. Every day when Jimmy and his dad went to the park, his dad brought his guitar and would play it while Jimmy jogged. 

At the park there was a fat cat. Jimmy really liked the cat and liked to talk to it when he was taking a break from jogging. One day the cat even chased Jimmy when he jogged past it!

The cat made Jimmy laugh. Jimmy and his dad would go to the park every day and Jimmy would jog while his dad played the guitar. It was always so much fun.

Lila was a little girl who liked to explore the woods near her home. She had a big stick that she used as a staff to help her walk and feel brave. One day, she saw a shiny red bird in a tree and wanted to get closer. She walked fast and did not look at the ground.

She did not see the big rock that was in her way. She stumbled and fell down. She hurt her knee and it bled. She cried and dropped her staff. The red bird flew away. Lila felt sad and scared.

Then she heard a soft sound. It was a brown dog that came out of the bushes. The dog licked her face and wagged its tail. It was a friendly dog. It picked up her staff in its mouth and gave it back to her. It helped her stand up and walked with her. Lila smiled and hugged the dog. The dog was compassionate. It was her new friend. They went back to her home together. Lila's mom cleaned her knee and gave her a band-aid. She was proud of Lila for being brave and kind. Lila was happy. She named the dog Rusty. They played in the woods every day.

Mommy was busy organizing the kitchen. She took out some cheese from the fridge. It was a big block of cheese, yellow and fine. She cut the cheese into small pieces. Mommy and Little Johnny took some of the cheese pieces. They also took some crackers and put them on the table. Mommy and Johnny had a nice snack. It was so yummy and fine! Mommy was happy that Little Johnny ate some of the cheese. He said it was the best cheese ever! They both laughed and enjoyed their snack. Then, Mommy put the rest of the cheese back in the fridge and continued to organize the kitchen.

Once upon a time there was a boy called Jack. He found a very delicate maze. It was a colourful maze with lots of twists and turns. Jack loved to play with his maze. He was always so excited to see what was at the next bend.

One day, Jack decided to stretch the maze out. He held the ends of the maze and started to pull. He wanted to see if he could make the maze longer. He pulled and pulled, until the entire maze was stretched out.

Jack loved the new way he could play with his maze! It was so much more fun to run inside the long maze. He felt like he was on an adventure. He kept trying to solve the maze, but it was so tricky. In the end he had lots of fun but never really made it to the end of the maze.

Jack was always careful not to break the delicate maze. Whenever he was done playing, he made sure to put the maze back together. That way he could play with it another day.

Mommy was in the kitchen. She wanted to cook a special dinner. She had a dependable recipe and the ingredients were lined up on the counter. One of the ingredients was pink. Mommy mixed it all together and put it in the oven.

Mommy and the little one watched and waited. Soon, a delicious smell filled the kitchen. Mommy took out the dish and placed it on the table. It was a beautiful pink casserole.

The little one tasted it. It was so yummy! Mommy smiled and said, "See, I told you I could cook something special." Even though she was dependable, the little one could see Mommy was surprised how delicious it was. 

From that day on, the little one knew that Mommy was dependable and could cook something yummy anytime.

Tommy was walking through the forest. He looked around, taking in all the beauty of the nature around him. Suddenly, he heard a loud noise from nearby. He was unsure of what it was.

He followed the sound and came to a small creek. He looked closer, and he saw a brown frog shaking on a rock in the water. Tommy was very excited, and he smiled.

The frog hopped up to the edge of the creek. He stared at Tommy with his big bulgy eyes, and Tommy could tell the frog was scared. Tommy was very honest and said, "Don't worry frog. I'm not going to hurt you."

The frog seemed to understand, and he stopped shaking. Tommy put his hand out and the frog hopped onto it. He was so excited! He wanted to take the frog home and make him a pet. 

Tommy thanked the frog for trusting him, and he carefully put him back into the creek. The frog hopped off away from the creek and onto the grass. Tommy waved goodbye to his new friend, and he was so happy to have met him.

Once there was a little girl. She was very stubborn. She was at a pitch watching her friends play. She wanted to join in but no one wanted her to. They all shut her out.

The little girl stamped her foot and said to the boys, "Let me play!" But the boys refused and shut her out again. She became even more stubborn and refused to leave.

Suddenly, one of the boys had an idea. He said, "I know, why don't we all play together?" All the boys agreed and shut the pitch door open for the little girl.

The little girl ran in with a big smile, and the friends all began to play together. From then on, nobody would ever shut her out again!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside, but there were many mosquitoes that would bite her. One day, Lily's mom told her to put on bug spray to keep the mosquitoes away. But Lily didn't want to wait and decided to go outside without it.

As she played, the mosquitoes came and bit her. She got very itchy and had to go inside. Lily's mom told her that if she had just delayed going outside and put on the bug spray, she would have been successful in avoiding the mosquito bites.

From that day on, Lily always put on bug spray before going outside. She learned that sometimes it's better to delay and prepare for success, rather than rushing into things and facing consequences.

Once upon a time there was a mild cabin in the woods. It was old and weatherworn, with a long front porch with two rocking chairs.

Inside the cabin was a mother and her two children, a boy and a girl. One day, the boy and girl wanted to explore the woods, so the mother told them to cover up in their coats and scarves to stay warm.

The two children ran excitedly into the woods, exploring anything they saw. They ran and played, covering themselves with leaves and twigs. They looked at different bugs and ate some wild berries. It was a mild day and the woods seemed to go on forever.

Suddenly, the mother called out for her children and they ran back to the cabin. Before she could scold them for running off, she saw their faces covered in dirt and leaves. She laughed and hugged them both, happy to have them safe and sound.

The mother and her two children stayed in the woods for many weeks. They explored and played, and when it was time to go home, they all felt a little sad. The mother reminded her children that they could come back and cover themselves in the leaves anytime they wanted to. They smiled and hugged her, happy to know they could come back to their mild cabin any time.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved playing with her toys, especially her dolls. One day, Lily's mom took her to the park to play. Lily was so happy to be outside and play on the swings.

Suddenly, a gust of wind came and scattered all of Lily's toys everywhere. Lily started crying because she didn't want to lose her toys. Her mom told her not to worry and they started picking up the toys together.

Lily's mom noticed that one of the dolls had a loose arm. She told Lily that they needed to tie the arm back on so the doll could be fixed. Lily was happy to see her doll fixed and hugged it tightly. "Thank you, Mommy!" she said.

After they finished picking up the toys, Lily's mom took her to a store to buy a new toy. Lily saw a cheap toy that she really liked and asked her mom if she could have it. Her mom said yes and Lily was so happy to have a new toy to play with.

One day, Jack the rabbit went out to pick cheese. He had been searching all morning, and eventually he found what he was looking for in a small cave. He hopped inside, and grabbed the cheese. However, he soon realized that it was very hard! Jack tried to take a bite, but he just couldn't manage it. He needed help!

Luckily, he found a large elephant nearby. He asked if the elephant could help him. After some thought, the elephant agreed. The elephant took the hard cheese and put it in the ground. She stomped her feet on it and broke it into small pieces. Jack was happy, and he thanked the elephant for help.

The two friends then shared the cheese. They had a great time, and before long Jack was off on his way again. He had learned an important lesson â€“ it pays to ask for help!

Once upon a time there was a popular girl named Emily who lived in the deep forest. She wanted to explore the forest, so she decided to take a walk. As she was walking, she saw a guard standing near the entrance of the forest.

Emily was afraid of the guard and stopped walking. The guard smiled and said â€œItâ€™s ok, you can explore the forest. I am here to make sure you stay safe.â€

Emily smiled and said â€œThank you, I will be careful. I hope I can find many fun things in the forest.â€

The guard nodded and said â€œI hope so too, have a nice day.â€

Emily smiled again and thanked the guard before walking into the forest. She saw many different kinds of animals and plants, but nothing that seemed interesting. She kept walking and walking, but there was still nothing.

Soon, Emily reached the end of the forest and she saw a big lake. At the lake, she heard a loud rumbling and she knew that something interesting was waiting for her. Emily hoped that it would be something she could keep with her, and she was right. When she looked inside the lake, she saw a big and shiny diamond.

Emily was so happy and excited to find the diamond, she quickly showed it to the guard. He smiled and said â€œCongratulations, Emily. You are now a popular girl!

Once upon a time, there was a boy called Tim. He was a very curious boy; he enjoyed finding out more about the things around him.

One day, Tim saw an old wagon. He thought that it looked very useful. So, he squeezed the wagon and rolled it around with him.

Tim kept playing with his wagon, but he soon found that it kept getting stuck. He tried pushing it harder, but it just wouldn't move. Tim decided to find someone who could help him fix the wagon.

He soon found a friendly mechanic who told him that the wagon's old wheels were too worn out to be useful. He said that Tim had to buy some new wheels to make the wagon useful.

Tim was very sad. He had been playing with his wagon for so long and didn't want to say goodbye to it. The mechanic said to Tim, "Things can be really useful if they are in the right condition. That's why it's important to take care of them and look after them."

Tim nodded and smiled. He thanked the mechanic for his advice. He also bought new wheels for his wagon and was soon able to play with it again.

Tim had learnt a valuable lesson that day - things will only be useful if we take care of them.

Lily and Tom were friends. They liked to play with cars and dolls. One day, they went to the park with their moms. There was a big slide in the park. Lily and Tom wanted to go on the slide.

They ran to the slide, but there was a long line of kids. Lily and Tom had to wait. They were sad. They wanted to go fast. They looked at the other kids. Some were big, some were small, some were nice, some were mean.

One kid was very mean. He was in front of Lily and Tom. He had a red shirt and a black hat. He pushed and kicked the other kids. He did not say sorry. He did not wait his turn. He went on the slide many times. Lily and Tom were angry. They wanted to tell him to stop.

"Hey, you are not nice!" Lily said to the mean kid. "You have to wait like us. You have to share the slide."

The mean kid laughed. He did not listen to Lily. He pushed her away. He said, "No, I do not have to. I am the best. You are poor and silly. Go away!"

Tom saw what the mean kid did. He did not like it. He wanted to help Lily. He ran to the mean kid. He said, "You are wrong. You are mean and rude. You have to change. You have to be kind."

The mean kid did not like what Tom said. He was very angry. He grabbed Tom's arm. He twisted it hard. He said, "No, you have to change. You have to be quiet. You have to go away!"

Tom cried. He felt a lot of pain. He dropped his car. He could not move his arm. Lily saw what the mean kid did. She was very scared. She ran to Tom. She hugged him. She said, "I am sorry, Tom. You are brave. You are my friend."

The mean kid did not care. He picked up Tom's car. He said, "This is mine now. You do not need it. You are poor and weak. Go away!"

He ran to the slide. He went on it again. He laughed. He did not see the big hole in the slide. He fell through it. He hit the ground. He broke his leg. He cried. He felt a lot of pain. He dropped Tom's car. He could not move his leg.

Lily and Tom saw what the mean kid did. They did not feel sorry for him. They felt happy. They said, "You are bad. You have to learn. You have to be sorry."
