The little girl felt sad. She had really wanted to go on an adventure and was now filled with regret. She showed her mom the colorful medal that she had found. It was a medal of courage. 

The mom said she was proud of her daughter for never giving up. She said sometimes we can't always do everything that we want, but it's important to show courage no matter what.

The little girl felt better after that and kept the medal close by. She would remember this lesson and never regret making the right decision.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys and explore outside. One day, Timmy went for a walk and found an unusual rock. It was very pretty and shiny, so Timmy decided to keep it.

As Timmy was walking home, he saw a little bird that had fallen out of its nest. Timmy wanted to help the bird, so he picked it up and brought it home with him. Timmy's mom told him that they needed to let the bird stay in a box with some food and water until it was strong enough to fly again.

Timmy went to bed that night, feeling happy that he had helped the little bird. But the next morning, when Timmy woke up, he found that the bird had passed away. Timmy was very sad and cried because he wanted the bird to stay with him forever. Timmy's mom hugged him and told him that sometimes things don't go the way we want them to, but we can still be proud of ourselves for trying to help. Timmy kept the unusual rock as a reminder of the little bird he tried to save.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toy cars and trucks all day long. One day, Timmy's favorite toy truck got stuck in a tree. He tried to get it down, but it was too high up.

Timmy saw his big brother, Jake, walking by and asked him for help. Jake was very powerful and lifted Timmy up to get the truck. But as Timmy was reaching for the truck, he accidentally knocked over a candle and started a flame. The flame grew bigger and bigger, and soon the whole tree was on fire.

Jake quickly tied a rope around Timmy and pulled him to safety. Together, they called the fire department and the firefighters came to put out the fire. Timmy was very grateful to his big brother for saving him and his truck. From that day on, Timmy learned to be more careful around flames and always ask for help when he needed it.

Once upon a time, there was a barber who was very careless. He was always in a rush and he never paid attention to what he was doing. One day, he was giving a haircut to a little boy. He was passing the scissors over the boy's hair, but he wasn't really looking and the scissors slipped, giving the boy a bad cut on the side of his head. 

The boy started to cry and the barber felt very sorry for what he had done. He told the boy that he was sorry and he gave him an extra big piece of candy to make him feel better. Then, he called his mom and explained what had happened. She was so upset that she ran to the barber's shop and she made him promise to be more careful from now on.

The barber learned his lesson and from that day on, he was very careful whenever he was giving someone a haircut. He made sure to pay attention and take his time. He was never careless again!

The sky was as blue as a summer day, when everything seemed easy and happy. Suddenly, a rainbow appeared against the bright sky and two small children ran outside to see it.

"Let's touch it! Let's try to reach it!" one of the kids exclaimed.

"No, we can't do that, it wouldn't be nice," the other replied.

Their father spoke softly. "You will not touch the rainbow. It doesn't belong to us. We must leave it alone and let it be."

The kids felt guilty and both of them knew that their father was right. Then, the rainbow changed and the children ran into the house, sad and disappointed.

As the night went on, it started to rain and the rainbow slowly faded away. The kids felt relieved and happy, knowing that it didn't have to be left alone anymore. They had changed the rainbow and that made them smile.

One day, a cat named Tom found a mitten on the ground. Tom was very proud of his new mitten. He wore it on his tail and walked around the yard.

Tom saw his friend, a dog named Max. Max saw the mitten on Tom's tail and laughed. Tom didn't care, he was still proud of his mitten. They played together in the yard.

Suddenly, Tom had to sneeze. When he sneezed, the mitten flew off his tail. Max and Tom looked for the mitten and found it under a tree. They both laughed and played with the mitten together.

Once upon a time there was a young girl named Anna. She kept a special journal full of her most precious thoughts and feelings. One day, she wanted to bury it in the ground outside her house. 

She dug a big hole and carefully placed the journal into it. Then she filled the hole back up until the journal was buried deep in the ground. 

Anna smiled. She knew that the journal was safe, and that no one would ever know that it was there. She was happy to have a special place all to herself. 

Anna wanted to come back to the spot every year and remember the day she buried her journal. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and pick flowers. One day, her mom asked her to help with the laundry. Lily didn't want to help because she wanted to play. Her mom said, "If you help me, we can go play after."

Lily helped her mom with the laundry and they hung it on the line to dry. As they were playing outside, Lily saw her friend's new toy and became envious. She asked her mom for a toy too, but her mom said they couldn't afford it right now.

The next day, Lily woke up early and saw the sun rise. She remembered how her mom said they couldn't afford a toy and felt sad. She decided to take some money from her mom's purse to buy the toy. When her mom found out, she was very upset and told Lily that stealing is wrong.

Lily learned her lesson and felt bad for what she did. She apologized to her mom and promised to never do it again. The moral of the story is that it's important to be honest and not take things that don't belong to you.

Once upon a time there was a kind little girl. She loved to play in the puddle on her way home from school. One day, the little girl gathered her courage and stepped into the puddle. Suddenly, a big wind blew in and the puddle began to flow away. 

The girl shouted for help but no one came. Suddenly, she was swept away by the fast flowing water. She tried to reach the big tree in her backyard, but failed. 

The kind girl then yelled out 'Somebody please help me!' 

The neighbours heard her cry, but they were too scared to do anything. The wind was getting stronger and stronger. Eventually, the little girl was taken far away by the puddle. 

The neighbours were very sad, but there was nothing they could do. The kind little girl was never seen again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Jazz. She loved to walk everywhere she went. One day, Jazz decided to take a walk in the woods. As she walked, she saw something dangerous. She was scared and wanted to go home but was too scared to move. Suddenly she heard some music. It was coming from a clearing in the woods. As she listened, she realized it was jazz music! She followed the music and found a group of animals playing instruments and dancing to jazz music. She was so surprised that she forgot she was scared of the dangerous thing in the woods. When the music stopped, Jazz thanked the animals and said goodbye. She walked safely home, feeling happy that she had found such a fun adventure.

Once upon a time there was a clever bird. The bird wanted to test its wings. So, it decided to have a parade! It flapped its wings, singing and dancing as it flew. Everywhere it flew, people could see it. They said, "That bird is so clever!"

The bird continued its parade as it swam and hopped across the pond. It rested from time to time, but never gave up. It kept testing itself, going higher and higher in the air.

Finally, after a long time, the bird arrived back home. It was proud of how far it had flown, and how brave it had been. The bird had passed its test! From then on, whenever it wanted, it could fly high in the sky.

One day, Tom and his family got a new puppy. Tom was so excited to take his new puppy for a walk. He went to get his new small leash to take the puppy outside. Tomâ€™s Mom said, â€œWait! You canâ€™t take the puppy out without asking me.â€ Tom asked, â€œPlease Mom, can I take the puppy outside?â€ But his Mom replied, â€œNo, I donâ€™t permit it.â€ 

Tom was so sad. He wanted to take his puppy out so badly! He thought of a plan. He grabbed the small leash and tried to take his puppy outside when his Mom was not looking. But his Mom noticed him and said, â€œTom! You are not allowed to take the puppy outside without my permission.â€ 

Tom kept trying to convince his Mom, but she stayed firm and said, â€œNo, Tom. I will not permit it.â€ Tom had no choice but to leave the puppy inside. He sadly walked away, leaving the small leash and the puppy inside.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She liked to play in her grandma's old house. One day, she saw a big cobweb in the corner of the room. She got scared and ran to her grandma.

"Grandma, there's a scary cobweb in the room," Lily said.

"Don't be scared, my dear. We can separate the cobweb from the room," her grandma replied.

So, they took a broom and gently separated the cobweb from the corner. Lily was happy and thanked her grandma for helping her. From that day on, Lily was no longer scared of cobwebs because she knew how to separate them safely.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to sing pretty songs and write notes to her friends. One day, she found a butterfly with pretty wings trapped in a jar. Lily felt sad for the butterfly and wanted to help it. She decided to release the butterfly from the jar. 

Lily opened the jar and let the butterfly fly away. The butterfly was so happy to be free and flew around Lily's head. Lily smiled and wrote a note to her mom about the butterfly. She told her mom how pretty the butterfly was and how happy she was to release it. 

From that day on, Lily felt happy every time she saw a butterfly. She knew that it was important to release them so they could fly free. And every time she wrote a note, she remembered the pretty butterfly and how happy it made her feel.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Penny. Penny loved shake shake shakes! Every morning she would get up and make herself a delicious shake by blending a few fruits and some milk. 

One day, Penny felt daring and decided to shake things up. She left her house and went walking down the street, shaking her arms and legs as she skipped along. 

When she got to the park, Penny noticed something rough and sparkly on the ground. She bent down and scooped it up. In her hands was a shiny penny!

Penny was so excited, she decided to put her penny to the ultimate test. She held the penny between her forefinger and thumb, and tried to shake it. She shook the penny hard and it stayed put!

Penny couldn't believe it! She had done the impossible. She had shaken a penny that didn't shake! As Penny beamed with pride, a voice behind her shouted, "Way to go, Penny!" 

Penny turned around to see her friend, Jake. Jake said, "From now on, they should call you Penny the Penny Shaker!" 

"I like that name," said Penny, laughing. "Now let's go make some shakes!"

Once upon a time, there was a charming little girl named Lucy. She had beautiful blonde hair and a big, happy smile. Her favorite thing was to play outside and explore nature.

One day, Lucy was walking through the woods when she came across a big cookie. She was so excited that she shouted, "Oh wow! A cookie!" She started to run towards the cookie, but then she remembered she was supposed to quit eating sweets.

Lucy sighed and said out loud, "I know mom said to quit eating sweets, but this cookie looks soooooo yummy!" She was trying so hard to decide what to do. Then a charming little squirrel came out of the trees and scolded, "Quit eating that cookie and go play outside, silly Lucy!"

Lucy smiled and said, "Thank you, squirrel. I think I'll quit eating the cookie and play outside instead." She waved goodbye to the squirrel and ran off to explore and find adventure.

Once upon a time, there was a man. He liked to zoom around in his car. It made him very happy.

One day, the man stopped by a store. He saw a bowl of tasty fruit. It looked so inviting.

"Ooh, that looks yummy!" said the man. "I'm going to buy it!"

He paid for the tasty fruit and quickly zoomed off. The man was excited to eat it.

While driving, he noticed a little boy. The boy was sad and walking all alone. 

The man pulled over. He offered some of his tasty fruit to the little boy.

The little boy smiled. "Thank you, mister!" he said.

The man smiled and zoomed away in his car. He was happy to have made a new friend.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Amy. She liked to explore the world around her.

One day, Amy was walking through a forest. Suddenly, she heard a loud ringing sound! She followed the sound and came to a big metal box with buttons. She was curious and pushed a button.

The metal box started to shake. A man with a grey hat came out. He said, "Hello Amy, I'll be happy to help you!"

Amy asked, "What's that box?" "It's an oxygen tank," the man replied. He showed her how it worked and how people use it to breathe clean air.

Then the man saw that the oxygen tank was very dirty. He smiled and said, "I think it needs cleaning. Would you like to help me?" Amy nodded and was very excited.

So Amy and the man worked hard to clean the oxygen tank. Finally, when it was all shiny and clean, they both gave a big smile and said together, "We did it!"

Once there was a girl named Lucy. She wanted to play outside a lot. But her parents would never permit it. Lucy was so sad about this. 

One day, Lucy's dad took her to the store. While they were there, Lucy saw something she liked right away. It was a plant with green leaves. Dad said it was an herb. Lucy was excited to take it home.

When they got back, Lucy was so happy to have her new herb. She took care of it and named it Herbomino. Lucy went to check on Herbomino every day.

But one day, when Lucy went to go check on it, something was wrong. Herbomino had a white funny-looking thing on it. It was disgusting!

Lucy's dad said she must have given it too much water. He told her it was very important to listen to the rules he had given about taking care of the herb. From then on, Lucy was always careful to give Herbomino just the right amount of water.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He loved to play games with his friends. One day, they decided to play a game of tag. Timmy ran as fast as he could, but his friend caught him and tagged him. Timmy wanted to play again, so he said, "Can we repeat the game?"

His friends agreed, so they played again. This time, Timmy was "it" and he had to tag his friends. He chased them around the playground, but they were too fast for him. Timmy started to feel tired and his shoelaces were tight, so he stopped to tie them. His friends waited patiently for him to finish and then they continued playing. They had so much fun that they repeated the game over and over again until it was time to go home.

Once upon a time, there was a dependable pool. It was a very special pool because it was always clean and always felt good. It was perfect for people to jump in and swim around. Every day, lots of children would splash and play together. 

One day, something happened that was very unusual. Someone came and locked the pool. The children were so confused. Why was the pool locked? What was going to happen?

The kids did not understand, but they kept looking for the answer. They asked the grown-ups why the pool was locked, but no-one had an answer.

In the end, the kids decided they should go find out themselves. They all gathered together and went to the pool to find the answer. When they got there, they saw a gate that was closed and locked. 

Suddenly, they realized the answer. The pool was locked so no-one would get hurt and so the pool would stay dependable for everybody. The kids smiled and agreed that this was a good reason for the pool to be locked. 

They all left the pool knowing that their dependable pool was safe once again.

Once upon a time, there was a little squirrel called Max. He was sad because he had lost his acorn. He looked everywhere and couldn't find it. 

Max asked his mom, "Mom, did you see my acorn?" His mom said, "No, I haven't, sweetie. Are you upset?"

Max said, "Yes, I am upset. I wanted to keep it for a long time." 

His mom said, "I care about you and it's okay to be upset. Let's go find another acorn together."

Max was happy and he smiled. He and his mom went out together to look for a new acorn. Finally, they found one and Max was so happy. He hugged his mom and they went home together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She was feeling very nervous and didn't know what to do. Eventually, she decided to go outside. She stepped out onto the porch and saw a big, fluffy cushion. 

The little girl was so excited, she started to wave her arms in the air. She twirled around and around, feeling giddy and happy. 

But then she spotted something moving in the bushes. It was a big, yellow cat. The cat looked at the little girl and she got very nervous again. She stopped waving, but the cat kept looking at her.

The little girl slowly tiptoed back inside the house, but the cat followed her. She ran to the big cushion and hid underneath it. The cat started to meow and the little girl pushed the cushion up against her face.

The cat sniffed around the cushion for a few seconds, before finally running away. The little girl let out a big sigh of relief. She had survived her adventure!

Once upon a time there was a girl who was very miserable. She loved to play alone and search for pebbles. Every day she would wander the meadows and look for the prettiest pebbles.

One day, while she was outside playing, an old man stopped by. He said to her: "What are you doing child? You should spend your days more wisely." 

The girl thought for a moment and then replied: "I love to find the prettiest pebbles, it makes me happy!"

But the old man shook his head slowly and said: "No, you should spend your time on something more worthy. What you are doing is a waste."

The girl felt very sad and continued to look for pebbles. But she was now miserable and unhappy.

The moral of the story is that you should use your time wisely. Don't do things that make you feel miserable. Find ways to make yourself happy by doing things you truly love.

Mum took Sally to the shop. There was a big bookcase. "That's silly!" laughed Sally. Mum smiled too. She took Sally's hand and they walked over to the bookcase. It was so big Sally could hardly see to the top. She couldn't take it home as it was so big. Mum took some books off the shelf and gave them to Sally. She was very excited. "Can I keep them?" she asked. Mum said, "Yes, but we have to take them home so you can read them". Sally put the books in her pocket and gave Mum a big hug. She was so happy. Mum and Sally went home with the books to read. Sally loved her new books and took care of them. She looked at the funny bookcase every time she went to the shop.

A little bear woke up one morning to a lovely day. He went outside to play and he heard some loud music coming from a nearby park. He was excited and went to investigate.

When he got to the park he saw a party. There were lots of people wearing party clothes, children running around and everyone was laughing and having fun. He heard music and the sound of people singing and clapping.

He crept closer and he heard a kind voice. He saw an old rabbit holding a balloon and singing. The rabbit saw the little bear and asked if he wanted to come join the party.

The bear was so excited! He jumped and danced around in circles and sang. Everyone was laughing and having a great time. The little bear felt so loved and it was the most lovely party he had ever been to!

Sam was walking in the park. He saw an old box on the ground. He went up to it and opened it. Inside, he found four pieces of tape. He was very excited, and wanted to take them home with him.

But as he picked up each piece, he realized that something was wrong. Every piece was broken. So Sam couldn't use them. He was a little bit sad, but he kept walking and looking for something else.

Finally, he found something in the grass. It was a big piece of tape. He smiled and picked it up. It was bright and shiny, and it wasn't broken. He put it in his pocket and ran home.

When he got back to his house, he showed his mom the tape. She was happy to see that Sam had found something special. She used the tape to decorate his room, and they both smiled.

One day, a family was getting ready for the festival. They were all wearing their best clothes and were very excited.

Daddy said to the little three-year-old girl, "Let's go to the festival!" The little girl was so happy, she kept repeating, "Festival! Festival!"

When they arrived at the festival, there were so many people! The little girl was overwhelmed and felt helpless. She didn't know what to do.

Daddy hugged her and said, "It's okay. We can stay together and explore. We can find our way around." He held her hand and together they walked around the festival, looking at all the sights and sounds.

The little girl felt a little bit better. She looked up at Daddy and said, "Festival, festival!" Daddy smiled and repeated after her, "Festival, festival!"

Lily was a girl who liked to play with her toys. She had many dolls and cars and blocks. She did not like to share them with anyone. She always said, "Mine, mine, mine!"

One day, she saw a spider on the wall. She was not afraid of spiders. She thought they were fun to watch. She wanted to play with the spider. She said, "Come here, spider. You can be my toy."

The spider did not want to be a toy. He wanted to be free. He said, "No, no, no. I am not a toy. I am a spider. I have a web and a family. Please let me go."

But Lily did not listen. She grabbed the spider and put him in a jar. She closed the lid and shook the jar. She said, "Now you are my toy. You will do what I say."

The spider was very sad and scared. He did not like to be in the jar. He did not like to be shaken. He did not like to be alone. He said, "Please, please, please. Let me go. This is not nice. This is not fun. This is not fair."

Lily did not care. She smiled and said, "You are mine, mine, mine!"

Then, she heard a knock on the door. It was her friend Sam. He came to play with her. He said, "Hi, Lily. Can I join you? What are you playing with?"

Lily showed him the jar with the spider. She said, "This is my toy. It is a spider. He does what I say. He is mine, mine, mine!"

Sam did not like what he saw. He felt sorry for the spider. He said, "That is not a toy. That is a spider. He is alive. He has feelings. He needs air and space and friends. You should let him go. That is the right thing to do."

Lily did not like what he said. She got angry and said, "No, no, no. He is my toy. He is mine, mine, mine. You cannot tell me what to do. You cannot join me. Go away, go away, go away!"

Sam was hurt and sad. He did not want to play with Lily anymore. He said, "Okay, okay, okay. I will go away. But you are not a good friend. You are not kind. You are not fun. You are bitter, bitter, bitter."

He left and closed the door. Lily was left alone with her jar. She looked at the spider. He looked at her. They did not smile. They did not talk. They did not play. They were both unhappy.

Lily realized that she had made a mistake. She had lost a friend. She had hurt a spider. She had been selfish and mean. She felt sorry and ashamed. She said, "I am sorry, sorry, sorry. You are not a toy. You are a spider. You deserve to be free. I will let you go. I hope you forgive me."

She opened the lid and let the spider go. He crawled out of the jar and onto the wall. He said, "Thank you, thank you, thank you. You have done the right thing. I forgive you. I hope you learn to share and care. I hope you find a friend. Goodbye, goodbye, goodbye."

He spun a web and left. Lily watched him go. She felt a little better. She learned a lesson. She decided to change. She said, "Goodbye, spider. I will miss you. I will share and care. I will find a friend. I will be kind and fun. I will not be bitter, bitter, bitter."

The end.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She was three years old and so excited to play. She had a special toy that she loved, it was made of velvet. 

One day she went to play with her toy and it started to burn! It was so weird. She ran to find her mom and said, "Mommy! The velvet toy is burning!"

Her mom came running and said, "Don't worry sweetheart, it's ok".

The mum grabbed the toy and threw it away. They both watched it burn and the mum said, "Well, that was weird!" 

The little girl nodded. She was sad because her special toy was gone but she was glad her mum was there to help. She hugged her and said, "Thanks mommy." 

The mom smiled and said, "You're welcome sweetheart."

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He loved to play with his toy cars and trucks all day long. One day, Timmy's mom took him to the park to play with his toys. Timmy was having so much fun playing with his trucks in the sand.

Suddenly, a big, rough dog came running over to Timmy and his toys. Timmy got scared and started to cry. The dog's owner came over and said, "I'm sorry, my dog didn't mean to scare you. He just wanted to play too."

Timmy's mom said, "It's okay, but next time please mention that your dog is coming over so we can be prepared." The dog's owner nodded and walked away with his dog.

Timmy was happy again and started to play with his trucks. But then, he noticed that one of his favorite trucks was missing. He looked around but couldn't find it. Timmy's mom said, "Maybe it's a symbol that it's time to go home." Timmy was sad but agreed. As they were leaving the park, Timmy saw the dog and his owner again. The dog was playing with Timmy's missing truck. Timmy's mom tried to get the truck back, but the dog wouldn't give it up. Timmy went home without his favorite truck and was very upset.

One day there was some snow on the ground. It was very cold and the ground was white. 

Jack was a little boy who liked to play in the snow. He was very excited and decided to go outside and play. 

Jack made a snowman and put a hat on it. He was very happy to see his snowman complete. 

Then Jack noticed that he was all alone in the snow. He felt a bit lonely because all of his friends were inside. 

Jack wondered what he could do to not be lonely anymore. He made a big snow angel and then he smiled. He was no longer lonely because he had found a new friend in the snow.

"Come on!" said Daddy to the little girl. She went over to the bow on the ground and picked it up.

"Wow, what a nice bow!" She looked at it and smiled.

She and Daddy went to the house and while they walked, Daddy explained what to do.

The little girl was confused. She didn't know why they needed a bow. Daddy showed her how to place the bow on the door of the house.

When they had finished, the little girl asked Daddy, "Why did we bow at the house?"

Daddy laughed and said, "It is a sign of respect. When you bow, you are showing that you are welcome at the house."

The little girl smiled, understanding better now. She bowed again, feeling happy and excited to be welcomed at the house.

Lila and Ben were playing with their toys in the living room. Lila had a doll with a delicate dress and Ben had a tool box with a hammer and a screwdriver. They were having fun, but they also wanted to see what their mom was doing in the kitchen.

"Mom, can we help you?" Lila asked, holding her doll.

"Sure, you can help me by setting the table," mom said, smiling. "But be careful with your toys, don't leave them on the floor."

Lila and Ben nodded and put their toys on the couch. They went to the kitchen and helped mom with the plates and the forks. They were proud of themselves for being good helpers.

When they finished, they ran back to the living room to play with their toys again. But they were surprised by what they saw. Their toys were gone!

"Where are our toys?" Lila cried, looking around.

"Did they disappear?" Ben wondered, feeling scared.

They heard a giggle from behind the curtains. They pulled them aside and saw their little brother, Max, hiding with their toys. He had taken them while they were in the kitchen.

"Max, give us back our toys!" Lila shouted, grabbing her doll.

"Max, that's not nice!" Ben scolded, taking his tool box.

Max pouted and said, "But I wanted to play too!"

Mom came to the living room and saw what happened. She hugged Max and said, "I know you wanted to play, but you can't take your siblings' toys without asking. That's not fair. You have to share and respect their things."

Max nodded and said, "I'm sorry, Lila and Ben. Can we play together?"

Lila and Ben smiled and said, "Of course, Max. We can play together. But don't make our toys disappear again!"

They all hugged and played happily with their toys. Mom watched them and smiled too. She was glad they learned to get along.

One day, Sammy was walking in the park. He heard a high-pitched sound coming from behind a bush. He carefully peeked around the bush and saw a pin. It was whistling! Sammy smiled and was happy to have found a whistling pin. 

He took the pin very carefully in hand and played with it. Sammy even tried to whistle along, but he couldnâ€™t make the same sound. Still, he was excited and wanted to show the pin to his friends. 

On the way home, Sammy stumbled and the pin flew out of his hands. He was worried and looked all around, but he couldnâ€™t find it! Sammy was so upset that he started to cry. 

Suddenly, he heard the same high-pitched sound coming from behind him. He turned around and saw the pin lying on the ground, whistling with a smile. Sammy was so happy, he laughed and picked up the pin and hugged it tight. He would never lose it again. 

From that day on, Sammy and the pin were the best of friends. They had lots of fun playing together in the park. Whenever Sammy was worried, the pin liked to whistle a sweet tune to cheer him up.

Once upon a time, there was a girl who liked to observe. She liked to look around and see things. One day, the girl saw a rake outside in the garden. She wanted to play with the rake, so she went outside.

First, the girl tried to pick up the rake. But, it was too big and too heavy for her. She was embarrassed that she couldn't lift the rake. But then she had an idea.

The girl sat down and began to push the rake around in the garden. She observed as the rake pushed the leaves from one side of the garden to the other. Soon, the garden was all neat and tidy.

The girl felt happy and proud of herself. She had done something special with the rake. And, nobody would need to know she couldn't lift it up!

Once there was a girl named Sue. Sue was three years old. One day, Sue wanted a pair of sunglasses. She looked for them everywhere. She looked in the store but could not find the perfect pair.

Suddenly, she saw something rare. It was a special pair of sunglasses! She was very happy and quickly asked her father to buy them for her.

Her father bought the sunglasses and Sue put them on. She examined them carefully. She liked them very much! But then something bad happened. The sunglasses were accidentally replaced.

Sue felt very sad. She looked everywhere but could not find them. Eventually, Sue's father bought her another pair of sunglasses, but they were not as special as the first ones. She wore them anyway and had a lot of fun with them.

Once, there was a little girl named Lisa. She was only three years old. One day, it started raining very hard outside of her window. Lisa looked out the window and saw her trees and the street shivering in the wind. 

Lisa's mom came into her bedroom and said, "Lisa, we need to take a shower so that you don't get cold." Lisa's eyes lit up and she shouted, "Yay! A shower!" She was excited to play in the water. 

Her mom took her into the bathroom and helped her undress. Lisa stepped into the shower and the warm water made her shiver with delight. She started splashing around, playing with the water and the foam. 

After the shower, Lisa dried herself and put on some warm clothes. She ran to her bedroom and said to her mom, "Let's go outside and play!" Her mom smiled and told her, "We can go outside after I finish cooking dinner. It will be slow, so you must be patient."

Mummy was very busy packing. She had lots of things to do.

Mummy said to little Molly, "I'm going to do some exercise. Will you be a good girl and watch TV while I'm gone?"

Molly smiled and said, "Yes Mummy!"

Mummy smiled back and said, "You must be patient while I'm gone. I won't be long."

Molly nodded and said, "I can be very patient, Mummy. I'll be here when you get back." 

Mummy gave Molly a kiss and said, "I know you will. I'll be back soon." 

Molly waved goodbye as Mummy left. Molly waited patiently while Mummy did her exercise. When Mummy finished, she came back and gave Molly a big hug and said, "That's enough exercise for today." 

Molly said, "Let's go home, Mummy!" 

Mummy smiled and said, "Yes, let's go!" They packed their things and went home.

Once upon a time there was a humble bird. Everyday the bird would wake up in the morning and soar across the sky. The bird's feathers were so soft and beautiful, a true delight to see. 

One day, the bird found a file on the ground. Intrigued, the bird picked up the file and opened it. The file was filled with wonderful things and the bird couldn't believe its eyes. 

"Wow," said the bird, "this looks so cool!" 

The bird knew it wanted to tell its friends about the file, so it decided to soar around and tell everyone. In no time, all the birds heard the news and came to take a look. 

"Wow!" they all said, "This file is amazing!" 

The humble bird smiled at all of its friends and together they knew they could explore the wonderful world of the file together.

Sara and Tom like to play in the pond. They see many frogs there. They want to catch a frog and keep it as a pet. They find a big, green frog that looks jolly. It hops and croaks on a lily pad.

"Look, Tom, a jolly frog!" Sara says. "Let's catch it!"

"OK, Sara, let's work together!" Tom says. They take a net and a bucket and go to the pond. They sneak up to the frog and try to scoop it up with the net.

But the frog is not jolly. It is angry. It does not want to be caught. It sees the net and the bucket and jumps away. It lands on Sara's head and makes a loud croak. Sara screams and falls into the pond. She gets wet and muddy.

"Help, Tom, help!" Sara cries. "The frog is on me!"

Tom tries to help Sara, but he slips and falls into the pond too. He gets wet and muddy. The frog hops off Sara's head and goes back to the lily pad. It laughs at Sara and Tom.

"Ha ha ha, silly kids!" the frog says. "You can't catch me! I am a jolly frog, but only when I am free!"

Sara and Tom are sad and mad. They do not like the frog anymore. They get out of the pond and go home. They are wet and muddy and cold. Their mom is not happy. She scolds them and makes them take a bath. They do not have a pet frog. They have a bad day.

Once there was a girl named Jane. She used to love collecting fancy stamps. One day she saw a really fancy stamp in the store. It was so nice that she wanted it right away. She quickly bought the stamp without thinking. 

But when she got home, she started to regret buying the stamp. She remembered that she had almost no money left and the stamp was really expensive. She was sad that she had bought something so fancy without saving up for it. 

But then her grandmother hugged her and told her that she was proud of her for being so brave. Jane was happy again and realized that she didn't regret the stamp. She was excited to show it to her friends and continue her collection.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to play outside. One day, he saw an enormous tree with a tunnel under it. He was very curious about what was inside the tunnel. He told his mom about the tree and the tunnel, but she said it might be a little scary for him.

The next day, Tim went back to the tree. He wanted to be brave and see what was inside the tunnel. Tim took a deep breath and walked into the tunnel. It was very dark, but he kept going. As he walked, he could hear strange noises coming from the tunnel. Tim started to feel a little scared.

Suddenly, Tim stumbled on something in the dark. He fell down and started to cry. Just then, he saw a little light at the end of the tunnel. Tim got up and walked toward the light. When he came out of the tunnel, he saw a beautiful butterfly. The butterfly made Tim smile and forget about his fear. He knew that sometimes, even when things seem scary, there can be something beautiful waiting on the other side.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Red. Red was walking in the forest when she saw a wolf. The wolf looked miserable. Red asked the wolf, "What's wrong?" The wolf said, "I'm lost. Can you tell me how to get home?" Red said, "Sure! My grandma's house is nearby. I can tell you how to get there." The wolf was very happy and thanked Red. They walked together and Red told the wolf the way to her grandma's house. The wolf found his way home and Red felt proud of herself for helping someone in need.

Once there was a cute mouse that lived in a small house. His name was Tom and he liked to have lots of adventures. One day Tom went outside and saw a man stealing something. Tom was very brave and he followed the man to see what he was stealing. When he got closer he realised the man was stealing lots of delicious treats from the bakery! 

So Tom snuck up to the man and he stole all the treats back. He ran away as fast as he could and took them back to his little house. 

Soon Tom had a huge pile of treats and he was so happy that he got to keep them. He knew he had to hide them so the sneaky man couldn't find them. So Tom made a secret hiding place in his house and he kept the treats there. 

Tom never saw the man again but he still kept his treats hidden, just in case. He was so happy to have saved them and he had such a delicious snack each day.

Once upon a time there was a little boy. He loved walking in the park with his mom. As they walked, they saw ducks swimming in the pond. The boy wanted to play with them. He whistled loudly to try to get their attention. He waved his arms and jumped up and down. 

The ducks heard the boy whistling. They swam towards him. He was so excited! He loved watching them swim. Suddenly, he saw an acorn on the ground. It was a big, wide acorn. He picked it up and whistled. The ducks got closer and closer. 

The boy threw the acorn in the pond. The ducks followed the acorn and quickly ate it up. The boy was so happy! He loved watching the ducks in the park. He and his mom walked away, whistling as they went.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who was very happy. She loved to play with her friends every day and she was always smiling.

One day she saw something interesting and picked it up - it was a small needle! She wanted to show it off and put it in her pocket.

The next day, she wanted to show her new treasure to her friends and so she printed a picture of it to put on an invitation. But when she put the needle in the printer it made a big mess!

The little girl was very sad - she was not happy anymore. She knew that she was not supposed to put the needle in the printer and she was never able to clean up the mess. The end.

Once there was a little three year old girl named Anna. She used to feel very glad to be able to wear a comfortable suit every morning. Today was no different. Anna woke up in the morning, got dressed and went outside. 

But outside in the garden was a surprise! There was a big opposing wall blocking her way. Anna was not very glad any more. 

Anna's mom came outside and said, "Don't worry Anna, you can climb up and over this wall".

So Anna started to climb and eventually she made it to the top. But she started to cry when she got there.

Anna's mom said in a comforting voice, "There there Anna, don't cry. Everything will be okay".

Anna felt relieved and glad again. She wiped her tears away and looked back at the wall. She felt proud of herself for making it over the wall. She knew that her mom was right, everything would be okay.

Larry and Lisa were best friends. They liked to play together with their stuffed animals and pal around in the park.

One day, Larry asked Lisa, â€œWill you marry me?â€ She said yes!

They decided to have a tea party to celebrate. Larry made the tea and it was so tasty. They toasted with their teacups and laughed.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved playing outside with his friends. One day, Timmy's mom asked him to go to the store to buy some milk. Timmy was excited to go on an adventure.

As Timmy walked to the store, he saw a little bird on the ground. The bird looked hurt and Timmy felt anxious. He wanted to help the bird, but he didn't know what to do. Timmy decided to find someone who could help the bird.

Timmy saw a man walking by and asked him to help the bird. The man knew just what to do and took the bird to a vet. Timmy felt happy that he was able to help the bird. He learned that it's important to look out for others and help them when they need it.

Suddenly Timmy felt an uncomfortable pull. He looked down and, to his surprise, he saw a thin string coming from the floor! He followed it with his eyes and saw that it ended under the sofa. So, Timmy decided to go on a search and pulled the string to get a better look. He pulled some more and suddenly a box appeared from underneath the sofa. Curious, Timmy opened it and found lots of toys inside. He pulled out a toy train and couldn't stop smiling. He decided to keep playing with the train until dinner time.

Once upon a time, there was a young boy named Timmy. He was very ignorant and didn't know much about the world. One day, he went to play with his friend Johnny. 

"Hey Johnny, do you want to play catch?" asked Timmy.

"Sure, but let's be careful not to split the ball," replied Johnny.

Timmy didn't know what "split" meant, so he asked Johnny. Johnny explained that it meant to break something into two pieces. 

"Oh, I understand now," said Timmy. 

They played catch for a while, but then Timmy accidentally threw the ball too hard and it split into two pieces. 

"Oh no, I'm sorry Johnny. I didn't mean to split the ball," said Timmy.

"That's okay, Timmy. We can still play with the pieces," replied Johnny with a smile. 

And so, they continued to play with the broken ball, and Timmy learned a new word that day.

Once upon a time, there was a blue tank. Inside the tank lived a little fish. It was so very small. One day, the fish wanted to escape the tank. So the fish called for help.

The fish said "Someone please help me! I want to escape this tank!"

Just then, a little girl heard the fish's plea for help. She ran over to the tank and looked inside.

The little girl said, "I can help you!"

The fish was so excited. Together, the little girl and the fish worked on a plan. The little girl grabbed a net and scooped the fish out of the tank. The fish was free!

The fish said, "Thank you so much! I was so happy to escape the tank."

The little girl smiled and said, "You're welcome. I'm so glad I could help you."

The little fish swam away, happy to be free. The little girl smiled and went on her way.

Ben liked to hold his toy guitar and pretend he was a musician. He would sing and strum along to his favorite songs on the radio. He felt happy and proud when his mom and dad clapped and cheered for him.

One day, he saw a real musician on the street. He had a big guitar and a hat with money in it. He played and sang so well that many people stopped to listen and give him money. Ben wanted to be like him. He ran to the musician and said, "Hi, I like your guitar. Can I hold it?"

The musician was gentle and kind. He smiled and said, "Sure, little one. But be careful, it's very precious to me." He lifted his guitar and handed it to Ben. Ben felt the weight and the smoothness of the guitar. He was so excited that he forgot to be careful. He swung the guitar around and hit a lamp post.

CRACK! The guitar broke in half. The strings snapped and the wood splintered. The musician gasped and cried out, "No! What have you done? That was my only guitar!" He snatched the broken pieces from Ben and hugged them to his chest. He looked at Ben with anger and sadness in his eyes.

Ben felt scared and sorry. He didn't mean to break the guitar. He wanted to say sorry, but he couldn't find the words. He ran back to his mom and dad, who saw what happened and were shocked. They apologized to the musician and gave him some money, but it was not enough to fix the guitar. The musician shook his head and walked away, sobbing. Ben watched him go and felt very bad. He wished he never touched the guitar. He wished he could make the musician happy again. But he couldn't. He had ruined his dream.

Once upon a time, there was a fat cat. His name was Twist. Twist loved to play with paper. He would spend hours batting and swiping at the pages. 

One day, Twist was playing with his favourite page. Suddenly, he twisted it up into a ball. He pounced on it but it was too hard to bite. So he tried to flatten it out. But every time he pushed on it, it twisted up again.

Twist was getting a bit frustrated. He meowed softly to the page.

"Why won't you stay flat?" He purred.

The page didn't answer, but Twist heard a voice next to him.

"Maybe you need to be gentler," said the voice.

Twist looked up and saw a mouse standing nearby. It had pink fur and a twitching nose. The mouse grinned.

"Why don't you try rubbing the page instead of pushing? It might stay flat then," said the mouse.

Twist gave it a try. Sure enough, the page stayed flat! Twist patted it and smiled.

"Thank you for your help," said Twist.

The mouse smiled. "Any time, friend," it said.

From then on, Twist and the mouse would play with paper together, rubbing the pages so they stayed flat.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved playing outside in the park. One day, she was running around when she saw a big rock on the ground. It was not smooth, and she almost tripped over it. 

Lily said, "This rock is not good. I will remove it." Then, she tried to lift it with her small hands, but it was too heavy. 

Just then, a friendly dog came over and barked, "Woof woof! Can I help you?" 

Lily smiled and said, "Yes please! Can you help me remove this rock from the ground?" 

The dog wagged his tail and with a strong pull, the rock was removed. Lily was happy and said, "Thank you, you are my hero!"

John was feeling very alert one day. He had a lot of fun painting his bedroom. He loved the feeling of the brush on the wall and the way the paint smelled as he was rolling it on.

When he was finished, he stepped back to admire his work. He was really proud of the memory he saved that day. It was a painting that he would remember forever. 

The next day, John shared his painting with everyone. They all liked it too. They thought it was so colourful and bright.

John was happy that he could share his memory with others. He was so proud of his painting. He was even more alert now to get busy and paint some more.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was very smart and loved to read books. One day, she looked out the window and saw her friend, Timmy, coming over to play.

"Hi Timmy!" Lily said excitedly.

"Hi Lily! What are you doing?" Timmy asked.

"I'm reading a book about a princess and her castle," Lily replied.

"That sounds fun. Can I read it too?" Timmy asked.

"Of course!" Lily said happily. "Let's sit by the window and read together."

So, they sat by the window and read the book about the princess and her castle. They had so much fun reading together that they didn't even notice the time flying by. When it was time for Timmy to go home, he said, "Thanks for letting me read with you, Lily. That was really fun."

Lily smiled and said, "Anytime, Timmy. Reading is always more fun with a friend."

Lily and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to dig in the sand and look for shiny things. Sometimes they found coins, buttons, or shells. They put them in their pockets and showed them to their mom.

One day, they found something very special. It was a big, hard, sparkly thing. It had many colors and shapes. It looked like a rainbow.

"Wow, what is this?" Lily asked.

"I don't know, but it's pretty," Ben said. "Maybe it's a mineral. Mom said minerals are things that come from the ground and have different colors."

"Can I hold it?" Lily asked.

"Okay, but be careful. Don't squeeze it too hard. It might break," Ben said.

He gave the mineral to Lily. She held it in her hands and looked at it closely. She saw red, blue, green, yellow, and purple. She felt happy and curious.

She wanted to see what was inside. She squeezed the mineral a little bit. Nothing happened. She squeezed it harder. She heard a crack.

"Oh no!" Lily said.

She opened her hands and saw that the mineral had broken into two pieces. She saw a shiny, silver thing inside. It looked like a star.

"What did you do?" Ben asked.

"I'm sorry, I didn't mean to," Lily said. "But look, there's something inside. What is it?"

They both looked at the star. It was very bright and beautiful. They had never seen anything like it before.

"Maybe it's a treasure," Ben said. "Maybe it's famous. Maybe we can show it to everyone and they will be amazed."

Lily smiled. She felt sorry for breaking the mineral, but she also felt excited. She gave one piece to Ben and kept the other.

"Let's go and find mom," she said. "She will know what it is. Maybe it's a magic star. Maybe it will make our wishes come true."

Once upon a time, there was a country. It was dark, so it was hard to see. One day, a man came to the country. He needed a special thing. He asked the people if they could borrow something. 

The people said yes, and the man was happy. He found the special thing he needed. Now he could make something new.

The man went back to the country and thanked the people. He had borrowed something special to make something new. Everyone was happy that the man had been able to make something new.

The end.

Once upon a time there was a brave girl named Kate. She wanted to be a lawyer when she was older. But the people said that she was too young to do that. 

So one day, Kate decided she would dare them to let her do it. She put on her yellow dress and went to the courtroom. 

The judge told her that she was too young and had to go home. But Kate said, "Please, I want to be a lawyer". The judge was so amazed, he said yes and even gave her a law book to read. 

Kate was so happy that she wanted to do a dance. She made the court laugh while she danced around the room. 

At the end of the day, Kate got to be a lawyer and changed the law for all young children. She taught them that they could do anything if they only dared to try.

Once there was a little girl. She wanted to go and see a house. The house was very big and smooth.

The little girl was scared of the house. She felt like she could not accept it. She looked up at the sky and noticed something. It was a big fluffy cloud with a beautiful rainbow. Rainbow taught her that she should accept anything that is special, even if it is a house.

The little girl smiled and decided to accept the house. She walked up to the front door and knocked.

The door opened and the little girl saw a new world. She climbed the stairs and found a nice room. She had never seen a house so smooth before.

The little girl was so happy. She felt like she was home. She accepted the house and never wanted to leave.

Once there was a little girl and her mom. The girl was three years old and very excited. She asked her mom if they could go on an adventure, so they put on their coats and went outside. 

The little girl got to pick where they went, so she decided to go to the park. They played on the swings and the slide, and the girl had so much fun. The girl laughed and smiled and hugged her mom. 

Suddenly, the girl started to feel upset. She wanted to stay and play, but her mom said it was time to go home. The girl stood in the park and cried, and the mom hugged her tight. The hug made the girl feel better, and they went home together. 

The little girl and her mom had a wonderful adventure, and the girl did not feel upset anymore.

Once upon a time there was a green frog who loved to explore. One day he jumped into a puddle and found a magical stone. He went closer to have a better look and could hear a voice. "Help me!" it said. 

The frog looked around and noticed a witch under the water. She was stuck in between the stones and could not get out. "Please help me!" she said. The frog didn't know what to do. He thought and he thought and then he decided to melt the stone. 

He took a deep breath and blew on the stone. It started to melt and soon the witch was free. She thanked the frog and said "To reward your kindness, I will teach you a special spell". 

The frog was so excited and he jumped up and down on the puddle. "What's the spell?" he said. The witch smiled. She said the spell slowly three times and the frog repeated after her. He waved his hand and poof! A basket of plump, juicy flies appeared in front of him. 

The frog was so happy and thanked the witch again. Then he took his basket of flies and ran away into the pond. He never forgot the magic spell and it was the best thing the witch ever taught him!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and go on adventures with her friends. One day, Lily's mommy gave her a quiz to see how much she knew about colors. Lily was so excited to show her mommy what she knew!

But when Lily's mommy asked her what color the sky was, Lily got embarrassed because she didn't know the answer. She felt like she was in a crazy situation and didn't know what to do. 

Lily's mommy saw that she was feeling embarrassed and gave her a big hug. She told Lily that it was okay not to know everything and that she was proud of her for trying her best. From that day on, Lily knew that it was okay to make mistakes and that she could always ask for help when she needed it.

One day, a little girl named Sarah was walking through the park. She saw a huge engine. It was loud and made a lot of noise. Slowly, she walked closer and closer. She noticed that the engine was very angry.

Sarah was scared. She wanted to run away but didnâ€™t want the engine to be mad at her. So she stopped and sat down near the engine.

The engine was still angry and loud but Sarah didnâ€™t move. She just sat and looked at the engine. After a few minutes, the engine stopped. It wasnâ€™t angry anymore.

Sarah smiled and got up. She waved goodbye to the engine before walking away and went back to play in the park.

Once upon a time, there was a red fish named Fin. Fin loved to swim in the big blue sea. One day, while swimming, Fin found a journal. The journal had many pictures and words. Fin wanted to show it to his best friend, Bubbles.

Fin swam fast to find Bubbles. When he found her, he said, "Bubbles, look at this journal I found!" Bubbles looked at the journal and smiled. She said, "Wow, Fin! That's a pretty journal. Let's look at it together."

Fin and Bubbles swam to a quiet spot and looked at the journal. They saw pictures of other fish and animals. They laughed and talked about the pictures. They had a fun time with the journal. After that, they swam back home, happy to have found a new treasure.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. One day, Timmy wanted to go on a journey to find a treasure. He asked his mom if he could go, but she said no because it was too dangerous. Timmy was sad and didn't understand why he couldn't go.

Later that day, Timmy's dad came home and Timmy asked him if he could go on the journey. His dad said yes, but only if he promised to be quiet and listen to his dad's instructions. Timmy was so happy and promised to be quiet.

As they walked on their journey, Timmy noticed that the trees were getting taller and the birds were getting louder. He asked his dad why everything was increasing. His dad explained that they were getting closer to the treasure, and that's why everything was getting bigger and louder.

Suddenly, they heard a loud noise and Timmy got scared. His dad told him to be quiet and stay close to him. They found the treasure and Timmy was so happy. He thanked his dad for taking him on the journey and promised to always listen to his dad's instructions.

Once upon a time, a little rabbit named Remy loved to speed. He would run very fast in the big green field. One day, Remy found a red radish. He was so happy because he loved to eat radishes.

Remy started to eat the radish very fast. He ate and ate until he felt dizzy. He sat down and held his tummy. Remy thought, "Maybe I should not eat so fast."

Remy learned his lesson. He knew that eating too fast can make him dizzy. From that day, Remy ate his radishes slowly and enjoyed them more. And he still loved to speed in the big green field.

One day, Joe and his mom were walking in the park. Joe saw a bird perched on a branch and he exclaimed, "Mommy, look! Look at the bird!"

His mom said, "Yes, Joe. It is so beautiful."

Then Joe asked, "Mommy, can I build something with wheat?"

His mom smiled and said, "Sure, why not? You can build something very original with wheat."

So Joe started to build his very own wheat house. He put the wheat kernels together and added a roof. He was so proud of his creation. When he was finished, his mom said, "Joe, it looks amazing! Your original wheat house is the most beautiful one I have ever seen!"

Joe laughed and said, "Thanks mom! I made it all by myself!"

Once upon a time there was a planet that was very far away. On this planet, there lived a little boy. He was very persistent. Every day, he would get in his big red car and go for a drive. 

He would drive through the forests and past the lakes. He also drove around the mountains and into the plains. Everywhere he went, he enjoyed the sights. 

The little boy kept his car in good shape. He oiled it and cared for it. His car was strong, and it allowed him to keep driving around the planet. 

One day, the little boy drove his car to the top of the highest mountain. At the top, he could see all of the planet. He smiled and waved at all of the people. 

The little boy drove his car every day, and he became an explorer. He was still very persistent, and with the help of his car, he continued to explore and discover places on the planet.

Once there was a grumpy school teacher called Mrs. Johnson. She was always so cross and never wanted to laugh or play.

On the wall of Mrs. Johnson's classroom was a big blackboard with chalk stuck to it. Every day the children in the classroom would come in and learn something new.

One day, Mrs. Johnson was feeling very grumpy and cross as usual. She was shouting and scolding the children and they all started to get very scared.

Suddenly, an angel flew into the classroom! The angel had a bright light around her and she said to Mrs. Johnson:

"It's time to heal your heart. Start by being kind to the children in your classroom."

Mrs. Johnson started to feel a warmth in her heart. She smiled at the children, hugged them and played games with them. Everyone was so happy.

At the end of the day, Mrs. Johnson felt much better and everyone thanked the angel for helping her to heal. The angel smiled and flew off into the bright blue sky.

Once upon a time, there lived two best friends. They were called Lily and George. Lily wanted to go for a picnic and George was very excited. Together they packed their lunch, grabbed a picnic blanket and went to the park.

They found a beautiful spot and spread the blanket. They had a lot of sandwiches and drinks, which looked very yummy. 

Then George said, "Let's play a game. Let's find a hole in the ground." 

Lily looked around and then screamed, "I found it. It's a drain!"

It was very impressive and George said, "Let's put the sandwiches and drinks inside." 

So, they did it and then, they both thought they had to put something in for Lily. Then George put a little flower inside it and said, "We will miss this drain when we go home."

The two friends hugged each other and said goodbye to the drain. They knew that this would be a special memory. 

The End.

One day Sammy and Mommy went to the park together. Sammy saw a tall man, so he asked Mommy who he was. Mommy smiled, and introduced Sammy to his new friend, the Ice Cream Man. 

The Ice Cream Man had a big truck with a colorful cone painted on its side. He had boxes full of different flavors of ice cream and some frozen treats too. Sammy was so excited to try something!

The Ice Cream Man gave Sammy an ice cream cone. It was his favorite kind - strawberry! Sammy enjoyed the sweet, cold treat as he went for a walk around the park with Mommy. But then something went wrong. 

Mommy suddenly looked very upset. She said it was time to go home without waiting for more treats from the Ice Cream Man. Sammy was sad, but he knew it was time to go home. 

At the end of the day, Sammy still had the best ice cream cone ever, and a new friend too.

One day, a friendly cat named Kitty heard a scream. She wanted to find out the mystery of the scream. Kitty walked and walked until she saw a little bird.

The little bird said, "Help! I can't fly. I screamed because I'm scared." Kitty wanted to help the little bird. She told the bird, "Don't worry, I'll help you."

Kitty and the bird tried and tried to make the bird fly. They became good friends. Soon, the little bird could fly again. They were both very happy and played together every day. The mystery of the scream was solved, and they had fun together.

Jack was a very attractive three year old boy who lived in a big house. Every day, he would wake up early in the morning, and get dressed in his clothes. His favourite clothes to wear were his bright red t-shirt and jeans.

One morning, Jack woke up extra early and decided to go outside to find something fun to do. He saw some pretty flowers in his garden and wanted to pick them. But as he went to pick them he heard a tiny voice behind him say:

"That's my garden! You can't pick my flowers!" Jack was surprised and quickly turned around. There he saw a tiny fairy, wearing a sparkly pink dress. The fairy smiled at him and said:

"You are an attractive little boy! Why don't you take a look around my garden instead? There's lots of fun things to do!"

Jack and the fairy quickly became the best of friends. Every day, Jack would help the fairy tend to her garden, and she would show him lots of magical things. Jack would always wear his favourite clothes so that the fairy could recognize him wherever they went. They were the best of friends and would often wake up early together to go explore the magical garden.

Tim likes to write with his crayons. He writes his name, his mom's name, and his dog's name on his paper. He writes big and small letters, and different colors. He is very proud of his writing.

One day, he goes to the park with his mom and his dog. He sees a big tree with many leaves. He wants to write on the tree. He takes his crayon and starts to write his name on the bark.

"Tim, stop!" his mom says. "You should not write on the tree. The tree is alive. It needs oxygen to breathe. Oxygen is the air we breathe. The leaves make oxygen for us and the animals. If you write on the tree, you hurt the tree and the oxygen."

Tim is surprised. He did not know that the tree is alive and needs oxygen. He feels sorry for the tree. He says, "I'm sorry, tree. I did not mean to hurt you. I like you and your leaves. You are very nice and green. You give us oxygen and shade. Thank you, tree."

The tree does not talk, but Tim thinks it is happy. He puts his crayon back in his pocket. He hugs the tree and says, "I will not write on you again. I will be polite and respectful. I will write on my paper or on the sidewalk with chalk. I will write nice things and share them with you and my mom and my dog."

His mom smiles and says, "That's very good, Tim. I'm proud of you. You are a good writer and a good friend to the tree. You learned something new today. You learned about oxygen and trees and being polite. You are a smart and kind boy."

Tim smiles too. He feels happy and proud. He likes to write and to learn. He likes his mom and his dog and the tree. He likes the park and the oxygen and the crayons. He likes his life. He thinks, "I will write more stories and share them with everyone. I will write about oxygen and trees and being polite. I will write about everything I see and feel and wonder. Writing is fun and good."

Once upon a time there was a little puppy. She was a very persistent pup, but she wasn't sure what to do. Then one day, she saw a spot on the ground. It looked like a little pile of dirt and stones.

The pup started to mix them together with her nose. Once done, the pup started to play and was so happy.

But then the pup started to hear her mommy's voice in the distance saying, "Let's go, puppy."

The pup was sad and started to cry, but her mommy said, "You were so persistent with that spot. Look what you made!"

The pup looked and saw a beautiful little flower garden! She was so happy that she had mixed the dirt and stones together.

From that day on, the little puppy mixed up dirt and stones every day to make something beautiful.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Rosa. Rosa loved to imagine. Especially, she loved to imagine incredible places.

One day, Rosa's dad gave her a very special map. On the map were images of many amazing places. Rosa looked at it carefully, entranced by all the colorful pictures.

At the center of the map was a graceful island. It was the most beautiful island Rosa had ever seen. She had to find out more about it.

Using her imagination, Rosa climbed onto the map and set off to explore the island. She went on a grand adventure, discovering extraordinary things about the island. Finally, she hopped off of the map and went back home.

Rosa loved exploring with the map and would often imagine new adventures. Her graceful island was always in her thoughts.

Once upon a time there was a little boy named Jack. He was three years old and he loved to play outside.

One day Jack was at the playground when he came upon a large rock. He thought to himself, "what a great rock, I can sit on it for a rest!"

So Jack sat on the rock and looked around. It was very peaceful, and he felt at ease. But then he heard a voice. It was coming from the rock.

"I'm so tired of being here," said the rock. "I want to be replaced with something new."

Jack was taken back by this. He smiled and said, "Don't worry little rock, I'm sure something bigger and better will come along soon enough."

As the days went by, nothing did come along. Jack kept coming back to the rock, each day promising the rock that he would be replaced.

One day finally a new park showed up, with swings, slides and much more. The rock was gone and something a lot better had taken its place.

Jack was relieved and happy that he had listened to the rock and kept his word. It taught him an important lesson, that it is important to keep our promises, even if they seem small.

James loved to do special things. He was a very gifted boy, even though he was only 3 years old.

One day, his mother took him outside. James looked up at the sky. The weather was nice and sunny. He loved the sun!

James thought about all the special things he could do. He decided to make a flower garden in his backyard. He asked his mom for some help and she agreed.

They went to the store to buy some flowers and soil. Then they went home to get to work. After a few hours, James' flower garden was complete.

James was so proud of what he had done. He enjoyed looking at his garden each day and enjoying the nice weather. He was happy and was happy to show everyone what he had done.

The sun shone high in the sky, and the birds were singing in the trees. Tom and Sophie were walking along the beach, looking for shells. "Look!" said Sophie, pointing out to the ocean. "What is that?"

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Lucy. She was three years old, and very excited about life.

One day, she was playing in the garden with her friends. Suddenly, they heard a noise coming from the kitchen.

When they entered, they saw the oven making a crazy noise. Lucy asked her friends, "What is making that noise? It's so loud!"

One of her friends said, "I think something is trying to come out of the oven!"

Lucy quickly grabbed a towel and opened the oven door. Out of the oven, a little bird flew out.

Lucy was so excited, and she said, "Let's bring the bird with us!" So Lucy and her friends walked around the garden, playing with the small bird.

The bird went everywhere with them, and Lucy and her friends were very happy. They named the bird Bring, and kept it with them all the time.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his ball and bounce it all around. One day, Timmy's mommy took him to a fancy museum. Timmy was so excited to see all the pretty things in the museum. 

As they walked around, Timmy saw a big ball that looked like his. He ran over and tried to bounce it, but it was too heavy. Timmy's mommy told him that it was a special ball that people used to play a game a long time ago. 

Timmy was so happy to see the ball, even though he couldn't bounce it. He had a great time at the fancy museum and couldn't wait to come back and see more cool things.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Jane. She liked washing her hands very much.

One day, Jane wanted to make a cake for her mom. She took some flour and milk, and put them together in a bowl. Then, she stirred the mixture with a spoon.

Finally, the mixture was ready to cook. She put the mixture in the oven and waited.

When the cake was done baking, Jane took it out. It looked so delicious! Jane was so excited. But when she looked closer, she saw that the cake was dull. It was not as bright and colorful as she wanted, so she decided to wash the cake.

Jane got a wet cloth and slowly wiped the cake. As she washed it, the cake started to shine. It was now nice and bright.

Jane was so happy that she gave the cake to her mom with a big hug. Her mom was delighted to see the beautiful cake her daughter had made.

Once upon a time, there was a kind girl named Lily. She liked to help her mom with the dishwasher. One day, the dishwasher stopped working and her mom was sad. Lily wanted to solve the problem, so she looked inside the dishwasher. She saw that a spoon was stuck in the dishwasher. She pulled it out and put it in its proper place. The dishwasher started working again! Her mom was happy and thanked Lily for being so kind and helpful.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Steve and Beth. They were playing in the garden when Beth said to Steve â€œLetâ€™s make a surprise!â€

Steve asked â€œWhat kind of surprise?â€
