The kangaroo hopped, skipped and jumped around with his friends all day. They tried to do fun tricks, like jumping over sticks and pretending to fly like birds in the sky. It was a wonderful time!

At the end of the day, the kangaroo said goodbye to his friends. He was so happy and lucky that they came to visit him, and play in the fields. He knew he would always have lots of fun when they were around!

Pip was walking along the street when he heard a whistle. It sounded so happy that he wanted to join in. He stopped and looked around, but he couldn't see where it was coming from. Then he looked down and saw a brick by his feet smiling up at him. Pip smiled back and picked it up. The brick was so cheap that Pip thought he might be able to make some music with it. He put the brick to his lips and tried to whistle. But instead of music, Pip made a strange sound. He laughed and tried again, but it still didn't sound quite right. He kept practicing until he could make a nice whistle. That evening, Pip showed off his new skill to all his friends. They watched as he twirled and spun, whistling along in a happy tune. Everyone agreed that Pip made some of the best music around.

Once upon a time, there was a chubby little girl. She was always looking for something to do. One day, she found a strawberry in her garden. She was very excited and asked her mum, "Mum, can I polish the strawberry?"

Mum smiled and said, "Yes, my darling. Use a cloth to do it." 

The little girl took a cloth and started to carefully polish the strawberry. She really enjoyed watching it shine. 

When she was done, the strawberry looked so special. She brought it to show her mum. 

Her mum said, "That looks amazing! You did such a great job polishing it." 

The little girl beamed with pride and smiled. She was so happy and proud of her shiny strawberry.

Once upon a time, there was a bunny named Lucky. Lucky loved to eat carrots all day long. One day, Lucky was in the garden looking for some carrots to eat. Suddenly, Lucky heard a whisper. It was his friend, the mouse. The mouse said, "I saw some yummy carrots over there." Lucky followed the mouse and found a big carrot. He was so happy and ate it all up. From that day on, Lucky and the mouse were good friends and whispered to each other all the time.

One day, a little girl named Mia wanted to create something cool. She thought and thought, and finally, she had an idea. She would make a beautiful castle out of cereal! Mia was very excited to start her project.

Mia asked her big brother, Tom, to help her. "Tom, can you help me create a cool cereal castle?" she asked. Tom looked at her and said, "No, Mia. I don't want to play with cereal. I want to play with my toys." Mia was sad but decided to make the castle by herself.

Mia worked very hard to make her cool cereal castle. She used all her favorite cereals to create it. But then, Tom saw how much fun Mia was having and wanted to join her. "Mia, can I help you now?" he asked. Mia thought for a moment and said, "Yes, Tom. We can create a cool cereal castle together!" They worked together, and in the end, they made the coolest cereal castle ever.

Once upon a time, there was a farmer. He was not a happy farmer. Some people said he was ugly. He did not care. He only wanted his farm to be nice.

One day, it was very hot. The sun was so bright. The farmer's plants were not happy. They needed water. The farmer was sad. He did not want his plants to be dry.

The farmer thought hard. He had an idea! He would ask his friends for help. They all came with buckets of water. They watered the dry plants. The plants started to dance! The farmer was happy. He thanked his friends. The ugly farmer's farm was nice again.

Once upon a time there was an ordinary couch. It was not special or anything, just a regular couch. On that couch lived two best friends, Fred and Joe. They were two little boys who loved to perform.

Every day they would come together to the couch and use their imaginations to create a show. They would do all types of silly dances and sing songs. They would pretend to be pirates and try to find buried treasure!

After their performances, they would jump off the couch and go outside to play. They would play tag, chase each other around the backyard, and even make up games of their own.

In the end, Fred and Joe had a lot of fun playing together. They would always come back to the ordinary couch to rest and plan their next great performance!

Lily liked to draw on paper with her crayons. She had many colors and made many pictures. She drew her family, her dog, her toys and her dreams. She was happy when she drew.

One day, she found a big paper on the table. It was white and clean. She thought it was for her to draw on. She took her crayons and started to draw. She drew a big sun, a big flower, a big bird and a big smile. She was very proud of her drawing.

But then, she heard a loud voice. It was her mom. She was angry. She said, "Lily, what did you do? This paper was not for you to draw on. This paper was important. It was for my work. You ruined it. You have to say sorry."

Lily felt sad and scared. She did not know the paper was for mom's work. She did not want to make mom angry. She wanted to make mom happy. She said, "Sorry, mom. I did not know. I just wanted to draw. I like to draw. I like you."

Mom looked at Lily. She saw her sad and scared face. She saw her big sun, her big flower, her big bird and her big smile. She felt sorry too. She said, "It's okay, Lily. I know you did not know. I know you like to draw. I like you too. But next time, you have to ask me before you use any paper. Some paper is not for drawing. Some paper is for other things. Do you understand?"

Lily nodded. She said, "Yes, mom. I understand. I will ask you next time. I love you, mom."

Mom hugged Lily. She said, "I love you too, Lily. Come on, let's find another paper for you to draw on. And let's be quiet. Dad is sleeping. He worked hard last night."

Lily smiled. She said, "Okay, mom. Let's be quiet. And let's draw together."

They went to Lily's room. They found another paper. They drew together. They were happy. They did not regret anything.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the sun. One day, she went to the park with her mom. They saw a train track and Lily thought it was incredible. 

Lily said to her mom, "Can we take a ride on the train?" Her mom said, "No, we can't. It's not safe." Lily was sad but she understood. 

Suddenly, they heard a loud noise. It was a train coming towards them. They didn't see it because it was hidden behind a tree. The train hit them and they both got hurt. 

Lily cried and said, "I wish we didn't take the path near the track." Her mom hugged her and said, "I wish so too." From that day on, they never went near train tracks again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Mandy. She would always be a very naughty girl, getting into all sorts of trouble.

One day, Mandy was playing with her dolls on the big, soft couch. She was having so much fun that she forgot to pick up her toys. Her mom saw what she was doing and warned her not to do it again. Instead of listening to her, Mandy just gave her mom a naughty nod.

When her mom left the room, Mandy started to giggle. She thought it was funny to nod naughtily. Her mom, on the other hand, was not happy. She knew Mandy should have started picking up her toys.

The next day, Mandy's mom told her that if she didn't pick up her toys, she would not be allowed to play with them anymore. This time Mandy nodded obediently and quickly began to put her toys away.

Mandy had learned her lesson. From now on, she knew she should always listen to her mom.

Tom and Sam are brothers. They like to play with their toys in their room. Tom is very organized. He puts his toys in boxes and labels them. He has a box for cars, a box for animals, a box for blocks and a box for ties. He likes to wear ties when he pretends to be a teacher or a doctor. Sam is not very organized. He throws his toys everywhere and mixes them up. He does not like to wear ties. He thinks they are boring and itchy.

One day, Tom and Sam are playing in their room. Tom is teaching his animals with a tie around his neck. Sam is building a tower with blocks and cars. Sam sees Tom's tie and thinks it is funny. He wants to play with it. He grabs the tie from Tom's neck and runs away. Tom is angry. He says, "That is my tie! Give it back! It belongs to me!" Sam says, "No, it is mine now! I want to play with it!" He wraps the tie around his tower and makes it look like a flag.

Tom and Sam start to fight. They pull and tug on the tie. They yell and cry. They knock over their toys and make a big mess. Their mom hears the noise and comes to their room. She sees the chaos and is not happy. She says, "What is going on here? Why are you fighting over a tie? You have so many toys to share and enjoy. You need to learn to respect each other's things and feelings. You are brothers and you should love each other." She takes the tie from them and puts it back in Tom's box. She makes them clean up their room and hug each other. She says, "Now, say you are sorry and play nicely." Tom and Sam say they are sorry and play nicely. They learn to take turns and ask before they borrow. They have fun with their toys and their ties. They are happy and so is their mom.

Once upon a time there was a big cat named Fluffy. She was loved and taken care of by her owners. One day Fluffy was very sick, so her owners took her to see the veterinarian.

When they arrived at the veterinarian's office they asked the receptionist to seat them. The receptionist found a place for Fluffy and her owners to sit down.

The veterinarian came into the office and asked what was wrong with Fluffy. Her owners explained that she was feeling very sick. After looking at Fluffy, the veterinarian said he could help her.

He then gave Fluffy some medicine which proved to be very useful. Fluffy felt much better after taking the medicine and she thanked the veterinarian for helping her.

The veterinarian smiled and said, "You are welcome, Fluffy. It's always nice to be able to help animals feel better." Fluffy and her owners thanked the veterinarian again for his expertise and bid him goodbye.

Lily and Max were best friends. They liked to play in the park with their toys. One day, they saw a big slide. Lily wanted to try it, but Max was scared.

"Come on, Max, it will be fun!" Lily said. She climbed up the ladder and sat on the slide. "Look, I will show you how to do it!"

She slid down fast and landed on her feet. She smiled and clapped her hands. "See, it was easy! You can do it too!"

Max looked at the slide. It was very high and steep. He felt his heart beat fast. He shook his head. "No, Lily, I can't. It is too scary. I will fall and hurt my foot."

Lily ran to him and gave him a hug. "You won't fall, Max. I will catch you. You are brave and strong. I will encourage you. You just have to try."

She took his hand and led him to the ladder. She helped him climb up. She sat behind him on the slide. She wrapped her arms around him. "Ready, Max? On the count of three, we will go. One, two, three!"

They slid down together. Max felt the wind in his hair and the thrill in his stomach. He screamed with joy. Lily laughed with him. They landed on their feet. They hugged each other.

"Wow, Lily, that was amazing! Thank you for encouraging me. You are a charming friend. Can we do it again?" Max said.

"Of course, Max. Anytime. You are a charming friend too. Let's go!" Lily said.

They ran to the slide again. They had a lot of fun. They learned that trying new things can be scary, but also exciting. They learned that encouraging each other can make them happier and braver. They learned that being charming means being kind and helpful. They were best friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and always wore her favorite jacket with a zipper. One day, she went to the park with her mom and saw a group of kids playing with a big ball.

Lily wanted to join in, but the ball was too high for her to reach. So, she asked her mom to help her raise her up. Her mom lifted her high into the air and Lily was able to touch the ball.

As she was playing, Lily noticed that her zipper was crazy and kept going up and down. She didn't want to stop playing, so she asked her mom to help her fix it. Her mom zipped it up and Lily was happy again.

After playing for a while, Lily and her mom went home. Lily was tired but happy that she got to play with the other kids. She hugged her mom and said, "Today was a fun day!"

Once upon a time, there was a boy called Jack. He liked to use his eraser to draw pictures.

One day, he decided to use two different erasers together. They were so different - one was big and the other was small. Jack tried to draw a flower with them.

He started by pressing the erasers to the paper but he couldn't keep them together. He kept trying, but the erasers kept separating from each other.

Then, Jack came up with a new idea. He put the erasers side by side and drew around them. He was so happy - his flower was finished! 

Jack had used the different erasers to make something special.

Once upon a time there was a pencil who was very selfish. He didn't like to share with the other pencils. He kept all his nice colours for himself and wouldn't even let the other pencils use them.

But one day, something strange happened. Suddenly, the selfish pencil started to glow. It glowed so brightly that all the pencils wanted to be near it. Even the selfish pencil wanted to get closer, so he shared some of his colours with the other pencils.

The pencils were so happy and the colour of the selfish pencil began to spread amongst them. It was a beautiful sight - all the pencils glowing in different shades of the rainbow. The selfish pencil felt so bright and happy that he decided to share all his colours with the other pencils.

He was no longer selfish; now he was a happy pencil!

Ben liked to write in his journal. He wrote about his toys, his friends, his family, and his dreams. He kept his journal under his bed, where no one could find it. He felt happy when he wrote in his journal.

One day, Ben came home from school and ran to his room. He wanted to write about the new book he read in class. He lifted his bed and reached for his journal. But it was not there. He looked around his room, but he could not see it. He felt sad and angry. Who took his journal?

He heard a giggle from the hall. He ran out and saw his sister, Lily, holding his journal. She was leaning on the wall and flipping through the pages. She had a big smile on her face.

"Hey, give that back!" Ben shouted. "That's mine!"

"No, it's not. It's funny!" Lily said. "Look, you wrote that you want to be a superhero. How silly!"

Ben felt embarrassed and mad. He tried to grab his journal, but Lily was taller and faster. She ran away, laughing. Ben chased her, but he could not catch her. He felt troubled. How could he get his journal back? How could he make Lily stop? He wished he had a superhero power.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a soft blanket that she loved very much. One day, she spilled some juice on it and it became dirty. She asked her mom to clean it for her, but her mom was busy and told her to wait.

Lily decided to clean it herself and got a jug of water. She poured the water on the blanket and rubbed it with a cloth. But the blanket didn't become clean, it became wet and heavy. She panicked and tried to dry it with a hairdryer, but it didn't work.

The blanket was ruined and Lily was sad. She wished she had waited for her mom to clean it. From that day on, she learned to ask for help when she needed it.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Sue. She was a regular girl who liked to go outside and play. 
One day, Sue went outside to play with her friends, who had brought their water shooter. They quickly filled them up and started running around shooting each other! Some of the shooters made zigzag patterns that flew through the air. 

Sue was having so much fun zigzagging around the yard and shooting her friends. But then suddenly, she heard an angry voice.

Sue turned to see her mom, who was not happy with all the shooting going on. She shouted "Sue, stop shooting right now!" 

Sue quickly put her water shooter down and said "Sorry Mom". She knew she had to be more careful if she wanted to keep playing with her friends. From that day forward, Sue made sure to play with her water shooter in a regular way.

Once upon a time there was a bunny named Eager. He was very keen and would always go on lots of adventures. Every morning he would hop out of bed eager to start his day.

Today Eager was feeling extra excited. He hopped out of bed and grabbed a pillow and a blanket. He was going on an adventure. He hopped out of the house and quickly ran off.

Eager soon arrived at a big park. There were lots of new things to explore. He hopped around the park, checking out all the different things.

But after a while, Eager started to feel a bit tired. So he looked around and found a soft, comfy pillow. He nestled right into it and fell straight to sleep. 

Eager had had a fun day full of adventures and was happy and ready for bed. He snuggled into his pillow and soon he was fast asleep.

One day, a little girl named Amy was walking in a huge forest. She was so excited because it was her first time to explore the woods. As she walked, she suddenly heard an unfamiliar noise. She stopped and listened carefully. Suddenly, Amy recognized the sound! It was the sound of a gas tank! 

Amy followed the sound and soon saw a huge gas truck parked right next to a tree. She was curious so she decided to take a closer look. When she did, she started to feel sick and dizzy. Amy realized that the truck had been leaking gas. 

Just then, the truck driver came out of the forest, and Amy tried to tell him that his truck was leaking gas. But he got angry and didn't recognize what she was saying. He started yelling and told her to go away. 

Afraid, Amy ran away, feeling sad that the truck driver had not recognized the danger. She vowed never to forget her experience in the huge forest. 
Unfortunately, the truck driver allowed the gas to leak for many weeks, and eventually the forest was destroyed. Sad indeed.

Sara loves animals. She wants to be a veterinarian when she grows up. A veterinarian is a person who helps animals when they are sick or hurt. Sara likes to play with her stuffed animals and pretend they are her patients.

One day, Sara finds a small bird in her backyard. The bird has a broken wing and cannot fly. Sara feels sorry for the bird and wants to help it. She carefully picks up the bird and brings it inside her house. She puts the bird in a shoebox with some soft towels and some water.

Sara tells her mom about the bird. Her mom is proud of Sara for being kind and brave. She says, "You are a good veterinarian, Sara. But we need to take the bird to a real veterinarian. They have special tools and medicine to fix the bird's wing."

Sara nods and agrees. She says, "Can I come with you, mom? I want to see how they help the bird."

"Of course, Sara. But you have to be calm and quiet when we are there. The bird is scared and needs to rest. And we have to clean our hands before and after we touch the bird. We don't want to make it sick or dirty."

Sara and her mom go to the veterinarian's office. They meet a nice lady who wears a white coat and a name tag. She says, "Hello, I'm Dr. Lee. I'm a veterinarian. What do you have in the box?"

Sara shows her the bird and tells her what happened. Dr. Lee smiles and says, "You are a very good veterinarian, Sara. You did the right thing to bring the bird here. Let me take a look at it and see what I can do."

Sara watches as Dr. Lee gently examines the bird. She uses a small scissors to cut the feathers around the wing. She uses a small stick and some tape to make a splint for the wing. She uses a small syringe to give the bird some medicine. She says, "The bird has a fracture in its wing. It will take some time to heal, but it should be able to fly again. I will keep the bird here for a few days and then release it back to the wild. Do you want to name the bird, Sara?"

Sara thinks for a moment and says, "I want to name it Sunny. Because it has yellow feathers and it makes me happy."

Dr. Lee says, "That's a lovely name, Sara. Sunny is lucky to have you as a friend. You are a very good veterinarian, Sara. Thank you for caring for Sunny."

Sara smiles and says, "Thank you, Dr. Lee. You are a very good veterinarian, too. Can I come back and visit Sunny before you let him go?"

Dr. Lee says, "Of course, Sara. You are always welcome here. Just remember to be calm and clean when you see Sunny. He needs your love and support."

Sara hugs her mom and says, "I love you, mom. And I love Sunny. And I love being a veterinarian."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to peek at her mom when she was cooking in the kitchen. One day, Lily's mom told her they were going on a trip to visit her grandma who lived far away. Lily was so excited!

When they got to the airport, Lily's mom gave her a passport. It was a special paper that would let them go on the airplane. Lily thought it was so cool! She looked at the passport and saw her picture on it. The pages were smooth and shiny.

As they waited for their flight, Lily peeked over the seats and saw a boy playing with his toy car. She wanted to play too, so she asked him if she could play with him. They had so much fun together!

Finally, it was time to get on the airplane. Lily showed her passport to the nice lady at the gate and they got on the plane. Lily looked out the window and saw the clouds. She couldn't wait to see her grandma!

Once upon a time, there was a young boy. He lived in a big house with his family. The boy was very regular and liked to play a lot.

One afternoon, he heard a knock at the door. He ran to answer it and was so excited to see who it was. He opened the door and invited the person in with a big welcome.

It was his best friend Henry. The boy and Henry said hello and hugged each other. They were so happy to see each other again.

The two boys decided to have a regular game of catch. They played for a long time and laughed until their sides hurt.

When it was time for Henry to go home, the boy gave him a big hug and welcomed him back anytime. The boy and his family waved goodbye as Henry walked home.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to jump on her bed, but her mattress was old and lumpy. Her mommy said they couldn't afford a new one, so Lily hoped one day they could.

One day, Lily's mommy entered her into a jumping competition. Lily was nervous because she had never jumped in front of people before. The competition was very competitive, and Lily's opponents were very good. But Lily didn't give up. She jumped and jumped until she couldn't jump anymore.

Lily didn't win the competition, but she learned that even though things might be hard, it's important to keep trying and never give up hope. And, one day, her mommy surprised her with a brand new mattress to jump on.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. He loved to play games with his friends. One day, Timmy's friend brought a new game to play. Timmy didn't know how to play, so his friend explained the rules to him. 

The game was called "Duck, Duck, Goose". Timmy thought it was fun and wanted to play again. But his friend said the game wasn't available to play anymore because it was time to go home. Timmy was sad, but his friend promised to bring the game back next time they played together. 

Timmy went home and told his mom about the fun game he played with his friend. He asked his mom if the game was available to buy at the store. His mom said yes and they went to the store to buy it. Timmy was so happy to have the game and he couldn't wait to play it again with his friends.

Sara and Ben are twins. They like to play outside. One day, they go for a walk with Mom and Dad. They see a big mill. The mill has a big wheel that turns and turns.

"Look, Sara, look!" Ben says. "The mill is making flour. The wheel is using water to make it turn."

Sara nods. She sees the water in the river. The water is calm and shiny. She sees some ducks in the water. They quack and swim.

"Can we feed the ducks, Mom?" Sara asks.

Mom smiles. She takes out some bread from her bag. She breaks it into small pieces. She gives some to Sara and some to Ben.

"Sure, you can feed the ducks. But be careful. Don't go too close to the water or the wheel. They can be dangerous," Mom says.

Sara and Ben say okay. They throw the bread to the ducks. The ducks are happy. They eat the bread and say thank you. Sara and Ben are happy too. They like the mill and the ducks. They have fun.

One day, a young boy named Mike went out for a walk with his mother. As they were walking along, Mike noticed two friendly deer in the nearby field. He was so excited that he immediately waved and said hello. 

Mike's mother smiled and said "Hi, dear deer!" The deer seemed to be very friendly and they both ran over to Mike, so he could pat them. Mike was overjoyed as he enjoyed petting the deer. 

Mike enjoyed the time he spent with the deer so much that he asked his mother if they could come back tomorrow. His mother said they could, so they returned every day to visit the friendly deer. The deer always greeted Mike in the same way, and Mike enjoyed it so much. 

Every day, Mike and his mother would go to visit the deer and they always enjoyed it. It was like they were old friends, and it made Mike so happy to be able to see them. Mike and his mother would be friends with the deer forever.

Once upon a time there was a young lion. One day it was walking through the forest and it heard a noise. It looked around to see what was making the noise but it couldn't see anything. It moved closer to investigate. 

Finally it saw a little bird, who was pecking at the ground for food. The lion felt hungry and knew it was time to feed. It slowly crept closer to the bird but just as it was about to grab it, the bird flew away! 

The lion felt very annoyed. It had been so close to catching its dinner. It sat down to think of what else it could do to get food. Suddenly the lion remembered it was young and didn't have to hunt! All it had to do was wait and its mother would come feed it.

The lion smiled and waited patiently. Sure enough, after a while it's mother came and gave it a big dinner. The lion ate happily, grateful that it didn't have to hunt for its food.

Once upon a time, there was an old man and an old woman who lived in an ancient house. One day, the old man opened a jar he had found in a corner of their home. Suddenly, the jars lid blinked. The old man and woman were very scared, so the old woman said, "What should we do?!" The old man said, "It must be some kind of magic. We should put it back quickly!"

But before they could do anything, an ancient spirit appeared in the room. The old man and woman were so frightened that they could not move. The spirit spoke to them in a deep voice, "You found my jar. Now you must pay the price!"

The old man and woman had no choice but to obey the ancient spirit. The spirit commanded them to give all of their possessions to him. They reluctantly gave away everything but their clothes.

When the ancient spirit left, the old man and woman were left with nothing. They were so sad and unhappy. They had to work many hours every day just to survive. Whenever they looked at the jar, they would blink and remember their bad luck.

Once upon a time, there was a unique man. He lived in a small, red house. The man had a big frown on his face all the time. He was sad because he did not have any friends.

One day, the man went for a walk. He saw a cat stuck in a tree. The cat was scared. The man wanted to help the cat. He climbed the tree and saved the cat. The cat was happy and the man's frown turned into a smile.

From that day on, the man and the cat were best friends. They played together, ate together, and slept together. The man was not sad anymore. He was happy because he had a friend. And the cat was happy too, because it had a unique friend who saved its life.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Susie. One day, she was feeling very sad and miserable. She had no one to play with and it seemed like nothing was going to make her feel better.

But then, she heard a very happy sound. It was coming from outside her house. What could it be? She wanted to know. She went outside to see.

Outside, Susie saw a clown. The clown was juggling and twirling and hopping around. Susie smiled. She suddenly felt happier.

The clown saw Susie and came over to her. He said, "Hello Susie. Do you want to play?" Susie smiled again. She nodded her head.

The two of them played together for a long time. They chased each other and laughed. By the end of the afternoon, Susie didn't feel so miserable anymore.

She smiled at the clown and said, "Thank you for making me so happy."

The clown said, "Anytime, Susie. I hope we can play together again soon."

Susie nodded and said, "I hope so too!"

Once upon a time, there was a lively girl. She liked nothing more than to go outside and kick around. Every day, she would go out in the sunshine and kick a ball. She felt so happy as she kicked the ball far away.

One day, she decided that she wanted to kick even higher. She started jumping, and jumping, and jumping, trying to use her feet to kick the ball even higher. Finally, the ball flew a little too high, and landed on the roof of her house.

The little girl was upset that she couldn't get her ball. No matter how hard she tried, she still couldn't reach it. She thought and thought about what to do, and came up with a plan.

She went to her mom and said, "I have an idea. Could you give me a will? Then I can reach the ball on the roof! Please?"

Her mom smiled and said, "Yes, of course you can have a will. I'm sure it will help you get your ball down."

The little girl was so happy! She thanked her mom and ran to the roof. With the will, she was able to reach the ball, and they were both happy. From then on, the little girl was able to kick her ball as high as she wanted. Every day, she was full of lively kicks, making her so happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Mary. Mary was very persistent and almost nothing could stop her. 

One day, Mary was sitting in her classroom in front of the blackboard. She was very determined to learn all the letters of the alphabet. Suddenly, Mary started to sneeze. Her teacher ran over to her, but Mary assured her she was okay. 

The teacher said to Mary, "I must insist that you leave the classroom for a few minutes and take a break, because you shouldn't be sneezing in here." But Mary shook her head and said, "No, I want to stay and learn all the letters of the alphabet." 

The teacher saw how persistent Mary was and felt proud of her. However, she still told Mary that she had to take a break, or else she might get a cold. Mary reluctantly agreed and left the classroom to take a break. 

After a few minutes, Mary returned again to the classroom. This time, she was feeling much better, and she was ready to learn the alphabet. As she persistently worked on the blackboard, the teacher smiled, happy that Mary was feel better and eager to learn.

Once upon a time there was a blue boy. The boy loved to explore and learn new things. One day he wanted to explore something special. He wanted to explore history! So he entered a big, old building.

Inside, he found many books and objects. Everything was so exciting! He touched some old things and read some stories about the past. He even saw a picture of a blue building from long ago.

He stayed in the building for a long, long time learning all he could about history. He felt like the building was his very own special place, like a secret treasure.

The blue boy was so happy that day. He felt like he was part of history! He was filled with excitement and joy at all he had learned. From that day on, he was a history expert!

John was a very curious little boy. Everywhere he went, he liked to observe the things around him. One particular day, John noticed two children playing in the park. One of the children was wearing an attractive hat. 

John went up to the children and asked, "What's that on your head?"

The child with the hat smiled and said, "It's my hat."

John wanted to see it, so the child let him try it on. It was warm and the rim felt nice on John's forehead. 

"Can I keep it?" John asked excitedly.

The child shook her head and said, "No, I'm sorry. But I hope you will remember this hat and always observe the things around you."

John smiled and thanked the child, and as he went home he thought about the hat and the words of the older child. 

John learned that day to always pay attention to his surroundings, and each day he tried to observe something new. Soon enough, he found his own hat-- it was attractive and he loved it!

Timmy was walking in the park when he remembered something his teacher had said to him. She said that keeping a diary helps people to show how they feel. He smiled and ran back home to get paper and some pens.

When Timmy got home he told his mom that he wanted to write a diary. His mom quickly said no. Timmy complained and asked why not? She said that writing a diary can take a long time and she wanted him to do something faster. 

Timmy argued that if he started writing a diary it would help him to understand why he felt some things. His mom thought for a minute and then said, â€œokayâ€.

Timmy was so excited! He grabbed a pen and paper and started writing in his new diary. He filled the pages with all of his thoughts and feelings.

Every day after he went to school, Timmy would sit and write in his diary. He still complained about his tasks, but now he had a safe place to do it. He found comfort in knowing he had a place to express himself.

One day, Joe had an idea. He wanted to play outside. He put on his shoes and ran out the door. He noticed the sky was a dull grey. He looked around, but it was too dull for him to have fun.

He noticed some leaves blowing across the ground. Then he had an idea. He picked up some of the leaves and made a pile. He noticed a stick and decided to use it to poke the leaves. It was so much fun!

Joe had a great idea to make his dull day more exciting. He kept playing with the leaves and picking up sticks. Suddenly he heard a voice. It was his mom, coming to tell him it was time to go inside.

Joe had a big smile on his face. He was glad he was able to notice such a great idea even on a dull day!

One day, two friends went for a walk. They felt gloomy, so they decided to try to make themselves feel better. They each picked up a stick, looked around and found a pin. They leaned down and put the pin on their sticks. Then they spun the sticks around and around until they looked like colourful twirlers. They laughed with joy and continued on their walk. 

Suddenly, they stumbled upon a field of beautiful flowers. They decided to pick some and put them into a basket. The flowers made them so happy that they ran around the field, making it their special playground. 

When they were done, they decided to take the blooms to their friends. On the way, they saw a man sitting on a bench, looking sad and gloomy. They went over to him and gave him the flowers. His face lit up and he said, "It's good to do a kind deed even when you don't feel well". 

The two friends smiled and hugged each other. They had leaned a important lesson that day. Even in gloom, we can still be kind to others.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a little girl named Lucy. She loved the color pink. One day, she saw a pink package on the table. She wanted to open it but knew she should ask her mom first.

Lucy went to her mom and asked, "Mom, can I open the pink package on the table?" Her mom said, "Yes, but first observe what is around it. Is there a name on it?" Lucy looked and saw her sister's name, Lily, on the package.

Lucy did not open the package because it was for her sister. When Lily came home, she was very happy to see her pink package. Lily said, "Thank you, Lucy, for not opening my package." Lucy felt good that she did the right thing. She learned that it is important to observe and respect other people's things.

Once upon a time, there was a mom and her daughter. The daughter was very special and loved to explore. One day, the daughter wanted to find something new and exciting. She saw something very interesting in the distance. She wanted to go and find out what it was, so she ran off to explore.

Mom watched her daughter get further away until she disappeared. She worried because she didn't know where her daughter had gone. Mom started searching in the streets, but she couldn't find her daughter anywhere.

Suddenly, Mom remembered something her daughter told herâ€”she heard something interesting down by the river. So Mom raced to the river. Sure enough, her daughter was there, playing in the water. Mom was so relieved and ran to hug her.

The daughter explained what she foundâ€”it was a fish with bright shining scales. She thought it was so interesting and wondered where it had gone. But when Mom arrived, the fish had already disappeared.

Once upon a time, there was a bunny named Floppy. Floppy was very happy, as it was spring time. He happened to run into a group of other bunnies who told him they were going on an operation. Floppy was excited and joined them.

The operation was to pick all the flowers in the garden. All the bunnies went hopping to the garden and began to pick the flowers. Everything seemed great, but then Floppy noticed a nasty, bitter smell. It was coming from a strange bush.

The bunnies were so disgusted by the smell, they all ran away as fast as they could. Floppy looked back and saw that strange bush had started to move. It was a grumpy old bear coming out of his hibernation!

The bear was mad that the bunnies had disturbed him. He growled and grumbled, but luckily no one was hurt. After that, they all decided to stay away from the nasty smelling bush and Floppy went happily back home to enjoy the rest of the lovely spring day.

One day Mommy and Billy went to the store. Everything was so noisy! Daddy said they were going to buy something special - a print!

Billy was excited. When they got to the store, Daddy told Billy to help fill it. Billy grabbed the big empty print and filled it with lots of colors. He was so excited to finish filling it.

When the print was full, Daddy showed it to Billy. He said it was the perfect thing to hang up in the house. Mommy and Daddy smiled because it looked great!

They all went home together, and Daddy hung the print up on the wall. Now it was all colorful and made the house look nice. Billy was so proud that he helped fill the print!

One morning, Mark woke up and was feeling very happy. He went to the kitchen and saw his mom next to the freezer, looking very busy.

"Mom? What are you doing?" Mark asked.

"I'm doing a very delicate job," she replied with a smile. "I'm going to grab some ice cream from the freezer and you can have it for breakfast."

Mark ran to the freezer and grabbed the ice cream. He was so excited as he put it onto the plate. His mom smiled as she watched him enjoy and soon enough, the ice cream was all gone. 

Mark was so happy that he asked for more.

"No sweetheart," she replied. "You have to wait until dinner to get some more. But it's okay, the freezer will keep our ice cream nice and cold until then!"

Once there was an orange suit. It was a special suit, made of a special material. The suit had a special mark on the side. Jane liked it very much.

She asked her mother, "What is the mark on the orange suit?"

Her mother replied, "It's a special mark. It is a sign of good luck!"

Jane was excited. She couldn't wait to wear the suit. Every morning she put it on and went out to play.

She would go to the park and fly a kite. Or, she would go to the beach and look for seashells. Everywhere she went, people would ask her about the mark on the orange suit.

"What is the mark on your special suit?" they'd ask.

Jane proudly answered, "It's a sign of good luck!"

Lily and Ben like to play with rocks and sand. They make a big hill with rocks and sand. They say it is a volcano. They find a red bottle and put it on top of the hill. They say it is lava.

They want to make the volcano go boom. They look for something to make it go boom. They see a box with a picture of a rocket. They say it is a supply for the volcano. They open the box and take out a rocket. They put the rocket in the red bottle.

They run away from the volcano and hide behind a tree. They wait for the volcano to go boom. They hear a loud noise and see smoke and fire. The volcano goes boom. The rocket flies out of the bottle and hits a bird. The bird falls to the ground.

Lily and Ben are scared and sad. They run to the bird and see it is hurt. They say sorry to the bird and try to help it. They find some water and a cloth and clean the bird's wound. They find some seeds and a worm and feed the bird. They stroke the bird and talk to it.

The bird feels better and thanks Lily and Ben. It says it is not angry with them. It says they are kind and brave. It says it will be their friend. It flaps its wings and flies away. Lily and Ben wave goodbye to the bird. They say they will not play with the volcano anymore. They say they will play with the bird instead. They hug each other and smile.

One day, a girl named Lily went for a walk in the woods. She saw a big, scary tree. It had long branches that seemed to stretch out like arms. Lily felt a little scared, but she wanted to see what was behind the tree.

As she walked closer, she found a pretty veil hanging on one of the branches. "I wonder who left this here," Lily said out loud. Just then, she heard a voice from behind the tree. "That's mine," said the voice. Lily was very surprised to see a funny-looking creature with big eyes and a long nose.

The creature asked Lily to give the veil back. Lily didn't want to, but she was scared of the creature. So, she gave it back. The creature put the veil on and said, "Thank you. Now, you can't see me anymore." And just like that, the creature disappeared.

Lily was sad that she couldn't see the creature anymore. She walked back home, thinking about her new friend. But when she got home, she found that her house was gone. The scary tree's branches had stretched out and taken her house away.

From that day on, Lily never went back to the woods. She knew that the scary tree and the creature with the veil were not her friends. She learned to be careful with things that she found in the woods, and she never forgot the day her house was taken away.

Once upon a time, there was a magical pony named Jasmine who lived in a charming little meadow. She was always very gentle and friendly. One day, she heard a plea for help.

Jasmine trotted over to see what was happening. The tiny fairy who lived nearby had lost the special measure she used to make the magic potions! The fairy had tried to look for it, but it was nowhere to be seen.

â€œPlease, can you help me find it?â€ asked the fairy.

Jasmine nodded yes, and began looking around until she spotted the measure. She triumphantly showed it to the fairy.

The fairy thanked Jasmine. â€œYour help has saved me!â€

Jasmine smiled and nodded her head. She felt very proud as she trotted back to the meadow, knowing that she had done a wonderful thing.

Maddy was a playful three-year-old girl. She loved to roll around in the park and play with her friends. One day, she was in the park when she saw something twinkling in the grass. She bent down to pick it up and saw that it was a red laser.

Maddy turned it on and watched the red light roll across the grass. She giggled with delight, until she heard a voice. 

"Hey, that's mine," said the voice.

Maddy turned and saw a tall man with a friendly voice. She smiled and asked, "Is it yours?"

The man smiled. "Yes, I must have dropped it when I was running around. It looks like it fits in your hand perfectly."

Maddy nodded, and handed it back to the man. He thanked her and ran away with a smile. Maddy watched him go, then rolled around in the grass, chasing the red light of the laser as it disappeared in the distance.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to dance and wear her green dress. One day, she saw a big dragon in the forest. The dragon was scary and Lily was afraid. But then, the dragon said he wanted to surrender. That means he didn't want to fight anymore. Lily was happy and did a little dance. She even taught the dragon how to be a dancer too! From that day on, Lily and the green dragon were friends and danced together in the forest.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toy rocket. One day, Timmy's rocket fell and broke into pieces. Timmy was very sad.

Timmy's mom saw him crying and asked, "What's wrong, Timmy?" 

"My rocket broke. It's not flexible anymore," Timmy said.

His mom said, "Don't worry, we can fix it." She took some tape and helped Timmy put the rocket back together. "Now it's all fixed. Lean it against the wall so it doesn't fall again."

Timmy was happy and said, "Thank you, Mommy. You're the best!" He played with his rocket all day long, and it never broke again.

Once upon a time, there was a big, strong tree. He was very intelligent and could remember lots of things that had happened in the past.

One day, a three year old boy called Timmy went up to the tree. He said to the tree: "Hello." The tree replied: "Hello Timmy. What can I do for you?" Timmy asked: "Can you tell me a story?" The tree thought for a moment and then said: "Yes, I remember an old story."

The tree began to tell Timmy an exciting story about a knight who fought many battles and went on many adventures. Timmy listened very carefully and was amazed by the story. When the tree finished the story, Timmy said: "That was wonderful. Thank you very much!"

The tree smiled and said: "It was my pleasure, Timmy. Remember, being intelligent can help you in life." Timmy smiled and said: "I will remember that." With that, Timmy waved goodbye to the tree and went home.

Once there was a little boy who was 3 years old called James. He wanted to have a new toy but they looked too expensive. 

One day, while he was out in the yard, a strong wind started to blow. He got scared and hid under a tree. Suddenly, in the wind he saw something flying towards him. It was a kite! It was small, colorful and very cheap. 

James was so excited that he screamed: "I need that kite!" He ran and grabbed it. 

James was so happy that he immediately wanted to go and fly the kite. He ran to his mother and said: "Mummy, I need to go and fly my new kite!"

His mother smiled and said: "Okay, let's go!" They opened the kite together, and off it flew in the wind. 

James was very pleased, and he had lots of fun flying his new kite. He learned that sometimes you don't need to buy the most expensive things!

Once upon a time there was a fierce lion. He lived in the wilderness and was always on the lookout for danger. One day, he was taking a stroll around the edge of his forest when he noticed a beautiful, colourful ornament on the ground. He decided to pick it up and have it as his own.

But as he was admiring it, he heard a loud voice. It was an elephant, who shouted, "Stop! Those are my things!"

He quickly dropped the ornament and stepped back. "I'm sorry," he said. "I just wanted to have something pretty to keep."

The elephant looked at him with gentle eyes and said, "It's alright, I understand. But I must prevent you from taking my things. Would you like to exchange a gift?"

The lion was surprised, but very happy with the offer. He agreed, thanked the elephant and searched in the forest for something nice to give in return. He found a special rock and brought it back to the elephant as a gift.

The elephant smiled, thanked the lion and said, "I'm glad you prevented this from turning into an unpleasant situation. Let us always remember to share what is beautiful and bright."

With that, they parted ways and went on their own separate adventures.

Once upon a time there were two twins. They were very close friends who loved each other very much.

One day, one of the twins got sick. He was sad and very unwell. The other twin felt very sad too and wanted to help his sick brother. 

So the twins decided to go to the doctor. The doctor checked on the sick twin very carefully and said to the other twin, "Don't worry, his sickness will clear soon". 

The doctor gave the sick twin some medicine and told him to rest. Then, the doctor said some special healing words. 

After a few days, the sick twin began to feel better and better. He was soon healthy and happy again! The other twin was very happy too. 

Finally, the sick twin was healed and the twins were happy and healthy together again.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Daisy. Daisy liked to explore and discover new things. One day she found a creek. It was so amazing! The water sparkled like diamonds in the sunshine. 

Daisy wanted to explore the creek, so she started wading through the shallow water. Suddenly, she saw a fish swimming by. Daisy wanted to follow the fish but it seemed to ignore her. Daisy was so frustrated that the fish wouldn't play with her so she decided to explore the edges of the creek instead. 

Daisy discovered all sorts of amazing things - rocks, flowers and slimy, slippery stones! She had so much fun exploring and discovering new things. 

By the end of the day, Daisy said goodbye to the creek, happy with all the new things she had found.

The skeleton was not feeling well. He was in a lot of pain and no one knew how to help him. One day, a little three-year-old girl named Zoe noticed the skeleton and asked, â€œWhatâ€™s wrong?â€

The skeleton replied, â€œIâ€™m not feeling normal and I need to be healed.â€ Zoe felt sorry for the skeleton and asked if she could help.

The skeleton said, â€œYes, if you give me lots of cuddles and hugs, it will make me feel better.â€

So, Zoe hugged and cuddled the skeleton. She even sang him some happy songs. The next morning the skeleton felt much better. He was back to normal again.

Zoe was so delighted to see the skeleton feeling better. She smiled and said, â€œIâ€™m so glad I could help.â€

Once upon a time, there was a brave little girl named Gigi. She was very independent and liked to do things by herself. One day, Gigi decided to play a guessing game with her neighbour. She asked him what a poison was. Her neighbour said it was something bad that we should not drink or eat.

Gigi thought about it for a little bit and then she started to guess. She said, "Is a poison something that you can find in a garden?" Her neighbour thought about this for a moment and then he said, "No, Gigi. That's not a poison, that's just some dirt!".

Gigi smiled and thanked her neighbour for playing the guessing game with her. She was proud of herself for being independent and trying to figure out the answer all by herself. She went home feeling very proud!

Once upon a time there was a daddy and his son. They both loved to decorate.

One day they decided to go to the creek to find decorations. The daddy showed his son how to look for lovely stones and shells.

They found some sparkly stones and some white shells. They put them in a bag and carried it back home.

When they arrived home the daddy used a clever plan. He made a beautiful necklace by threading the stones and shells onto a cord.

The son was so happy to have a special decoration. He gave his daddy a big hug and said thank you. Then they both wore the necklace and smiled at each other.

Once upon a time, there was a brave little boy. He liked to go on adventures. One day, he decided to follow the creek.

At first, it was fun. He saw some ducks in the water and he laughed at the way they would swim around. 

But soon, the little boy reached a dangerous part. He wanted to go back, but he was too scared. All of a sudden, the water started to rise and the creek was getting more and more dangerous. He didn't know what to do.

The little boy was so brave. Finally, he decided to get out and run back home. He managed to get out in time and he was safe.

The little boy learned an important lesson that day. He knew that even though it was fun to follow the creek, it could also be dangerous.

Jill liked to play with her dolls. She had many dolls, but her favorite was Lily. Lily had a unique dress with flowers and a big bow. Jill always took Lily with her when she went out.

One day, Jill and her mom went to the park. Jill wanted to cross the street and see the ducks in the pond. But her mom said, "No, Jill. You have to wait for the green light. The cars are fast and loud. They can hurt you and Lily."

Jill was sad. She loved the ducks. She looked at Lily and said, "Don't worry, Lily. We will see the ducks soon. Mom will permit us to cross when it is safe."

But then, Jill saw something shiny on the ground. It was a coin. Jill liked coins. She thought, "Maybe I can buy a candy with this coin. Lily would like that." She forgot about the cars and the green light. She let go of her mom's hand and ran to get the coin.

But she did not see the big truck that was coming. The truck honked and screeched. Jill was scared. She dropped Lily and the coin. She tried to go back to her mom, but it was too late. The truck hit her and Lily.

Jill's mom screamed and ran to her. She hugged her and cried. She called for help. Jill was hurt. She felt pain and blood. She looked for Lily, but she could not see her. She said, "Mom, where is Lily? I want Lily."

Her mom said, "I'm sorry, Jill. Lily is gone. The truck broke her. She can't play with you anymore."

Jill was very sad. She wished she had listened to her mom. She wished she had not run for the coin. She wished she had Lily. She said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I love you. You are my unique doll."

Once upon a time, in a big jungle, there lived a little monkey named Momo. Momo loved to play all day long with his friends. They would swing from tree to tree, laughing and having fun. But Momo's mom always told him to be careful, so he wouldn't fall and get hurt.

One sunny day, Momo and his friends were playing near the river. Momo's friend, Toto the tiger, mentioned a new tree they could try to climb. It was very tall, and they were excited to see who could go the highest. They all took turns climbing, being careful not to slip.

Momo was the last to climb the tree. He remembered what his mom said about being careful, so he made sure to hold on tight. Momo climbed higher and higher, until he reached the top. From there, he could see the whole jungle! Momo was so happy and proud of himself for being careful and listening to his mom. And from that day on, Momo always played carefully with his friends in the jungle.

Once there was a little girl named Rosie. She was very curious. She wanted to find out more about the world. One day, Rosie went to the park with her mom. She saw a butterfly and smiled. The butterfly was pink and pretty!

Suddenly, Rosie heard a voice. It said, "Trust your wisdom, Rosie." Rosie had no idea who was talking to her. But she decided to trust her wisdom. She followed the voice and went to a secret garden.

Inside the garden, Rosie found a bush of pink butterflies. She was so surprised and happy! She reached out to touch them but the butterflies flew away. Then the voice said again, "Trust your wisdom, Rosie."

Rosie remembered the words and trusted her wisdom. She played in the garden with joy, running and skipping around. She was filled with so much trust and wisdom. She left the secret garden feeling like she could take on the world.

Once upon a time there was a smart little girl called Milly who loved to find solutions to problems. One day she saw a big leak coming from the roof. Water was dripping on the floor. Milly wanted to help, so she got her bucket and brought it under the leak in the roof. The bucket began to fill up with the water that was dropping.

Milly thought and thought until she had an idea. She went and found a piece of plastic and put it over the leak. Now the drop stopped. Milly was very proud of her smart idea and the grown-ups praised her.

"Well done, Milly! Thanks for finding a solution to the leak," said Mummy with a smile.

"You've been very clever," said Daddy, giving Milly a hug.

Milly was so happy to be able to help. She had used her smarts to solve the problem and everyone was impressed. And from that day on she never stopped trying to find solutions to problems.

Tommy was looking for something to play with. He liked to build things and he was very busy. He went over to the furniture and saw an empty glass there. He decided to make it into something special. He took some straws and some cupcake wrappers and made an airplane. He put the airplane on the counter and admired it with a big smile on his face. 

Suddenly he heard a voice. "What are you doing?" asked the voice. Tommy turned around and saw another little boy who looked very curious. Tommy said, "I'm building an airplane!" The little boy seemed very interested and asked if he could help too. 

Tommy happily said, "Sure!" and the two of them started to work together. They put together the airplane even faster and soon it was finished. 

Tommy smiled and said, "Let's have a toast to celebrate our hard work." He then picked up the glass from the furniture and offered it to the other little boy. They both took turns to drink from it and then clicked the glass together. The little boys cheered and laughed. 

Tommy was very happy. He had made something special with his new friend and was now feeling very content. He put the glass back on the furniture, said goodbye to his friend and went off to play.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Jack who wanted to celebrate something very important. He grabbed his hammer and some nails and started building something special. 

His mom came to see what he was building. She asked, "What are you making, Jack?" 

Jack said, "I'm making something really important and I'm going to celebrate when it's ready!" 

He pounded the last nail in and said with a smile, "It's done! Let's go celebrate!" 

Everyone had a great time celebrating and Jack was very proud of his important work. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she went to the zoo with her mom and dad. They saw many animals, but Lily was most excited to see a leopard. 

Lily asked her dad, "Why is the leopard so important?" Her dad replied, "Leopards are important because they help keep the balance in nature." 

Suddenly, Lily saw a boy throwing rocks at the leopard's cage. She told her mom and dad what she saw. They went to talk to the boy and asked him why he was throwing rocks. The boy said he was bored and had nothing to do. 

Lily's dad told the boy, "It's not nice to throw rocks at animals. They are living creatures just like us. You should study about them and learn why they are important." The boy apologized and promised to never throw rocks again. 

The moral of the story is to always be kind to animals and to study and learn about them.

Once upon a time, there was a little crab named Sammy. Sammy lived in a shell by the beach. One day, Sammy met a little girl named Lily.

Lily said, "Hi Sammy! What are you doing?"

Sammy replied, "I am trying to find food for dinner. I need to be successful in catching some yummy snacks."

Lily asked, "What kind of snacks do you like?"

Sammy said, "I like to eat small fish and clams. They include lots of protein and vitamins that keep me healthy." 

Lily smiled and said, "That's cool, Sammy. I hope you have a good dinner tonight!"

Once upon a time, there was an old lady. She had a big book with lots of words called a dictionary. Every day, she would read it to learn new words. 

One day, a little girl came to visit the old lady. The girl saw the dictionary and asked what it was. The old lady said, "It's a big book with lots of words to help me learn." 

The little girl was curious and asked if she could read it too. The old lady smiled and said, "Of course, you can read it too. It's never too early or too late to learn new words." 

And so, the little girl and the old lady sat together and read the dictionary, learning new words and having fun. From that day on, the little girl loved to read and learn new things.

Jack was a 3 year old boy who loved ice-cream. Every week his mommy would take him to the store to buy him his favorite treat. But today, he saw something different - a fancy ice-cream with lots of sprinkles and chocolate syrup on top. He wanted to try it but he didn't know if it was his kind of ice-cream.

Jack asked his mommy: "Does this ice-cream belong to me?" 

His mommy smiled and said "Yes, this ice-cream belongs to you. You can try it if you like."

Jack was so excited he jumped up and down. He couldn't wait to have a taste of the fancy ice-cream. He grabbed the cone and happily licked the creamy goodness. 

It was delicious! Jack knew this fancy ice-cream definitely belonged to him.

Once, there were two best friends called Jane and Bob. One day, they decided to gather some cream to make something creative. 

Jane said to Bob, "I know what we can make, let's use the cream and make a cake!"

Bob was excited and said eagerly, "That's a great idea!"

So, they gathered the cream and went to Jane's house to bake. Jane and Bob put their ideas together and created the most delicious and creative cake ever. When it was finished, they showed it off to their friends and everyone said it was the best cake ever! 

The end.

Once upon a time there was a small bird who was very lazy. He often slept in his nest all day and never flew around. One day the bird shivered because it was cold outside. He wanted to find a cozy place to rest and keep himself warm, so he looked and looked until he found the perfect spot. It was a big tree that had lots of leaves to keep him from getting cold. The bird settled in and snuggled up in the leaves and was so comfortable! He fell asleep and didn't shiver again. He found his perfect spot and made it his new home. He was so happy and was sure he'd be warm and cozy all winter long!

Once there was a little girl named Sarah. She wanted to wear her mama's shoes. She put on one shoe, but it did not fit. "It's too small," said Sarah. She felt ashamed.

Mama told her not to worry. "Sarah, let's try the other shoe," Mama said. Together, Sarah and Mama tried on the other shoe, but it didn't fit either. Mama gave her a hug. "It's okay, Sarah. Some things don't fit," said Mama.

Sarah was sad. She wanted the shoes to fit, but it was too late. She had already tried both shoes.

Suddenly, Mama had an idea. She had a great big bucket of water. "Sarah, try the shoe in the water," said Mama. Sarah dipped one of the shoes into the water and it fit perfectly! She was so happy!

"See, Sarah," said Mama with a smile, "Sometimes things fit in water." Sarah smiled with joy and hugged Mama. She was no longer ashamed.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Jane. She was three years old and very smart. But she also loved music. Every day, she would listen to music and dance around.

One day, Jane had a great idea. She decided to pack her music so she could take it with her wherever she went. She got out her little suitcase and started packing.

First, she put a CD in the suitcase. Then she found a record player. She was very excited. But when she tried to pack the record player it was too big.

Jane got angry and frustrated. She stamped her feet and said some really stupid words. But then she had another idea. She would take the CD and make new music.

So Jane took some pieces of paper and tape, and made a new CD. She was happy! Now she could listen to music and dance wherever she went.

Ben was very sleepy. He wanted to stay in bed and cuddle his teddy bear. But his mom said he had to get up and get ready for school. She said he could have some toast and juice for breakfast.

Ben got out of bed and put on his clothes. He was still sleepy and did not look where he was going. He stumbled on his toy car and fell down. He hurt his knee and started to cry. His mom heard him and came to help him.

She picked him up and gave him a hug. She said she was sorry he fell and kissed his knee. She said he was a brave boy and he would be okay. She took him to the kitchen and put a band-aid on his knee.

She gave him some toast and juice and said he could watch some cartoons while she made coffee. Ben liked cartoons and smiled. He ate his toast and drank his juice. He felt better.

But then he saw his mom's coffee on the table. He was curious and wanted to try it. He reached for the cup and pulled it. But the cup was too heavy and hot. It spilled on the table and on Ben's shirt. Ben felt wet and burned. He screamed and dropped the cup. His mom heard him and came to see what happened.

She saw the mess and Ben's shirt. She was angry and scared. She said he should not touch her coffee. She said it was dangerous and bad for him. She said he was naughty and careless. She took him to the bathroom and took off his shirt. She put some cold water on his chest and said he was lucky he did not get hurt more.

Ben felt sad and sorry. He did not mean to spill the coffee. He did not know it was hot and heavy. He wanted to make his mom happy, not angry. He said he was sorry and he loved her. He asked her to forgive him.

His mom felt sorry too. She knew he did not do it on purpose. She knew he was curious and sleepy. She loved him too. She said she forgave him and she was sorry she yelled at him. She said he should be more careful and listen to her. She said she would get him a new shirt and clean the table.

She hugged him and said they would be okay. She said they would go to school and have a good day. She said she would make him some hot chocolate when they came back. Ben smiled and hugged her back. He said he would be good and he would wait for the hot chocolate. He said he did not like coffee anyway.

Young Jenny and her adorable bear were walking in the park. Suddenly the bear sneezed. Jenny smiled and hugged him tightly. Then she noticed something was wrong. The bear started to get smaller and smaller! Soon he was so small that he disappeared! 

Jenny was very sad and couldn't understand what had happened. Her bear had gone forever! Jenny cried and hugged the air and said goodbye to her lost bear. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He loved to play with his toy cars and trucks. One day, he went outside to play and saw a big rock. The rock was very heavy and Timmy couldn't lift it. 

He tried to push the rock, but it wouldn't turn. Timmy decided to leave the rock alone and went to play with his toys. After a while, he came back to the rock and tried again. This time, he pushed with all his might and the rock started to turn! 

Timmy was so happy that he ran to tell his mom. She was proud of him for not giving up and trying again. Timmy remained determined to move the rock and eventually he did. From that day on, Timmy knew that if he kept trying, he could do anything he set his mind to.

Once upon a time there was a little boy who wanted a new diary. He asked his mom but she said no. He was sad.

One day he was walking by the lake and he saw a boat with a big box inside. He waved his hand, and the boat came closer. Inside the box was a brand new diary!

The boy was so happy. He hugged the diary and thanked the boat. Then he waved goodbye and ran all the way home.

He kept the diary beside his bed and he wrote new stories in it every night before he went to sleep. He never went to bed without writing something in his new diary.

Once upon a time, in a small village, there was a pink house. In the pink house, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to carry water from the well to her house every day.

One day, while Lily was carrying water, she met a cat. The cat said, "Can you help me? I am very thirsty." Lily said, "Yes, I can give you some water." She gave the cat some water from her bucket. The cat was very happy.

But when Lily got home, she found out that she did not have enough water for her family. Her mom was very sad and said, "Lily, you should not give away our water. Now we don't have enough to drink." Lily felt bad and learned that she should always think about her family first.

Once upon a time there was a stubborn little tank.

He lived on the beach and he always made jokes about how slow he moved. All the other tanks were much faster, but he loved to tease them.

One day, the little tank met a girl. She laughed at his jokes and said she was very friendly. He was so happy! He decided to ask her to be his friend and come with him for a drive.

But the girl said no. She said she wanted a faster tank. She was so stubborn. The little tank felt very sad. 

He tried to joke again, but the girl just rolled her eyes and left him alone on the beach. He was very heartbroken.

The little tank never saw the girl again and his jokes stopped being funny. He was very lonely. 

The moral of the story is that stubbornness can have a bad ending.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a very thin cat named Mittens. One day, Lily was playing with her toys when she heard a noise coming from her closet. She was scared and didn't know what to do. 

But then, her big brother came to help her. He opened the closet and found out that it was just Mittens playing with some toys. Lily was so happy that her brother helped her and that Mittens was okay. From that day on, Lily wasn't scared of her closet anymore.

Mama was so modern. She had the latest gadgets and dressed in the newest clothes. Every day, she brought home something new.

One day, Mama brought home a pretend house. It was so fun. Mama showed me how to pretend to cook in the house's kitchen, how to pretend to sleep in the bedrooms and how to pretend to drive the pretend car.

I loved to pretend with Mama. We would pretend that we were having a tea party, going on an adventure in a space ship and having a birthday picnic. There were so many things to pretend.

Every day, Mama and I would pretend something new and magical. I wouldn't ever want our pretend days to end. Pretending with Mama was my favorite thing.

Once upon a time, there were two friends - Tom and Sarah. Tom and Sarah liked to play together every day. 

One day, they decided to go on an adventure. They wandered around a nearby park and found an old cloth on the ground. They bent down to get a closer look.
