The dreammaker smiled, and began telling Amy all the things she must do to make her dream come true. They made a plan and then the dreammaker said, "Now all you have to do is stay determined and keep working hard! I'm sure your dreams will come true eventually."

So Amy kept working hard and, sure enough, her dreams began coming true one by one. She was so proud of herself for working so hard!

Anna and Ben are playing a game. They have a big box and many small toys. They take turns to hide a toy in the box and the other one has to find it. They count how many toys they can find. The one who finds more toys will win.

It is Anna's turn to hide a toy. She picks a red car and puts it in the box. She covers it with some paper and says, "Ready!"

Ben looks in the box. He sees many things: a ball, a doll, a book, a hat. He moves them around and tries to find the car. He says, "Where is it? Where is it?"

Anna smiles and says, "It is hidden. You have to look harder."

Ben keeps looking. He finds a spoon, a sock, a crayon, a cup. He says, "This box is too full. There are too many things."

Anna says, "You have to find the car. If you don't, I will win."

Ben does not give up. He looks under the paper and sees something shiny. He says, "Aha! I found it! I found the car!"

Anna claps and says, "Good job, Ben. You are very smart. You found the hidden car."

Ben says, "Thank you, Anna. You are very kind. You hid the car well."

They hug and say, "We both win. We had fun." They put the toys back in the box and go to play another game.

Once upon a time there were two best friends, Lulu and Tim. They lived on a sunny island with their families. 

One day, Lulu got a bright idea. She went to her mom and said, "Can I borrow your palm? I want to play a game." Her mom said yes, so Lulu took the palm and went to find Tim.

When Lulu met Tim, she showed him the palm and said, "Let's play!" But Tim just shook his head. He said, "No way! That's too stupid!" Lulu was mad. She demanded that Tim play the game with her.

Tim did not want to play. But Lulu kept demanding. Finally, Tim sighed and said, "Okay, fine! I'll play with you." The two friends laughed and laughed as they chased each other around the island, asking each other questions and playing games with the palm. 

They had so much fun that they decided to it again the next day!

Tom and Sam were friends. They liked to play with toys. One day, Tom saw a motorcycle in the street. It was big and shiny. Tom wanted to ride it.

"Look, Sam, a motorcycle!" Tom said. "Let's go and see it."

"No, Tom, we can't," Sam said. "It is not ours. It belongs to someone else. We should not touch it."

But Tom did not listen. He ran to the motorcycle and climbed on it. He pushed the buttons and turned the handles. He made loud noises.

"Vroom, vroom, I am a motorcycle rider!" Tom said.

Sam was scared. He knew Tom was doing something wrong. He tried to stop him.

"Tom, come down, please," Sam said. "You are making a mess. You are getting dirty. You are making the motorcycle dirty. The owner will be angry. He will come back soon. He will see you. He will yell at you. He will tell your mom. You will be in trouble."

But Tom did not listen. He kept playing with the motorcycle. He did not care. He thought he was having fun.

Then, the owner came back. He saw Tom on his motorcycle. He was very angry. He shouted at Tom.

"Hey, you, get off my motorcycle!" he said. "What are you doing? You are ruining my motorcycle. You are scratching it. You are denting it. You are making it dirty. You are a bad boy. You have no respect. You have no manners. You have no brains."

He grabbed Tom and pulled him off the motorcycle. He slapped him hard. He called his mom. He told her what Tom did. He asked for money. He asked for sorry.

Tom was hurt. He was scared. He was ashamed. He cried. He wished he had listened to Sam. He wished he had not touched the motorcycle. He wished he had not left his toys.

Sam felt sorry for Tom. He went to him and hugged him. He tried to comfort him.

"I am sorry, Tom," Sam said. "You made a mistake. You did not think. You did not obey. You did not care. You hurt yourself. You hurt the owner. You hurt the motorcycle. You hurt your mom. You hurt me. You should not do that again. You should learn your lesson. You should be good. You should be smart. You should be kind. You should be happy."

The moral of the story is: Do not touch what is not yours. Listen to your friends. Respect other people's things. Be careful with your actions. Be sorry for your mistakes. Be good and happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to read books with lots of pictures. One day, she found a book with a pretty cover and decided to read it.

As she turned each page, she saw beautiful illustrations and learned new words. She felt proud of herself for reading all by herself. 

After she finished the book, she went to her mom and said, "Mommy, I did it! I read a whole book and I'm so proud!" Her mom hugged her and said, "I'm so proud of you too, Lily. You did a great job." 

From that day on, Lily read more and more books and continued to feel proud of herself for each one she finished.

Once upon a time there was a little boy called Michael. Every morning, his Mom would give him a big hug and ask him how he was feeling. 

"I'm feeling lovely, Mom!" he said one day.

His Mom smiled and said "That's wonderful! Could you please get the thermometer? I want to check how you feeling".

Michael ran to the bathroom, where he found a shiny thermometer. He brought it back to his Mom and said excitedly "Here it is!"

His Mom took the thermometer, put it under his tongue and smiled. After doing this, she hugged Michael and said "Thank you. You are a lovely boy". 

Michael smiled and hugged his Mom back. He was so happy that his Mom loved him so much. Together they hugged and laughed and shared their lovely feeling.

Once upon a time, there were five friends who were playing in the garden. They decided to have a contest to see who could find the most interesting thing. 

Bob found a weird herb and showed it to his friends. They all thought it was so cool and couldn't believe what he had found. 

Then Joe said, "Let's have a number contest. I bet I can find the most things." So they started counting things around the garden. Joe saw five birds, four trees, and seven flowers. 

Then Lucy said, "I think I can find more. Let me try." She found nine bugs and twelve leaves. Joe and Lucy had the most things, so they were the winners! 

The five friends had used their numbers to have a fun contest and were all very happy.

One day, a powerful ant named Tim found an umbrella. He knew this umbrella was special. Tim had a plan. He wanted to show his friends how strong he was. So, he decided to carry the umbrella to the top of a big hill.

Tim started to walk up the hill. It was hard work, but he did not give up. He knew his friends would be very happy to see him at the top. As he walked, he saw a little bug named Sam. Sam was sad because he could not pinch. Tim wanted to help Sam.

Tim said, "Sam, you can use my umbrella to learn how to pinch." Sam was very happy. He tried to pinch the umbrella and after some time, he could do it. Sam thanked Tim for helping him.

Tim continued to walk up the hill. When he reached the top, his friends were waiting. They were so proud of Tim. They clapped and cheered. Tim was happy he could help Sam and show his friends how powerful he was.

From that day on, Tim and Sam were best friends. They played together and helped each other. The umbrella was always with them, reminding them of the day they became friends.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She was walking outside and she saw a post. It was big and shiny. She rushed over to it and tried to touch it. Just then she heard a loud noise and she felt scared. She was so scared that her legs wouldn't move. Suddenly an old man rushed over and grabbed her arm. He held her tight and said, "Don't worry, it's just a post office." The little girl was not so scared any more. The old man smiled at her and said, "Come on, let's go home." So the little girl and the old man rushed home together. The end.

Once upon a time, a lively boy was playing in a field. Suddenly he spotted a secret garden! In the garden, there were colorful flowers and some spaghetti. The boy was so excited that he sprang into the garden. He picked the spaghetti and started playing with it. He twirled it around his head and made funny shapes with it. The boy had so much fun and laughed so much! After a while, the spaghetti got too slimy, so the boy tossed it away and ran back home, ready for another fun day tomorrow!

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Max. Max was very brave. He liked to help people. One day, Max went to the store. He wanted to work there.

At the store, Max met a big cat named Tom. Tom was not brave like Max. Tom was scared of everything. Max wanted to help Tom be brave too. They became friends and worked together at the store.

One day, a loud noise came from outside the store. Tom was scared, but Max knew he had to be brave. Max went outside to see what the noise was. It was just a big truck. Max showed Tom that there was nothing to be scared of. Tom learned to be brave like Max, and they both worked happily at the store together.

Bob was very happy. He loved to swing. Every day he would go to the park and swing on the swing set. On the swings he could reach up to the sky and almost touch the stars.

One day he went to the park to swing. As the swing went back and forth, Bob looked up at the stars. Suddenly, he noticed something special. He could feel a power that was greater than himself. It was the power of the universe. 

Bob felt like he fit in this universe. He felt like he belonged, like he had a place in it. That made him happy. He felt so connected to the universe, like nothing could stop him. The feeling stayed with him every time he swung. 

Bob knew that swinging made him feel special. He loved swinging because it made him feel connected to the bigger universe that surrounded him.

One day, a boy and his dog went to the park. The boy was happy, but the dog was sad. The boy did not know why the dog was sad. They played with a ball and ran around, but the dog was still sad.

A girl came to the park and saw the boy and his dog. She said, "Why is your dog sad?" The boy said, "I don't know." The girl said, "Maybe he wants to hear your voice more." The boy talked to the dog, but the dog was still sad.

The sky got dark and it started to rain. The boy and the girl went home, but the dog stayed in the park. The dog was still sad. The boy and the girl looked out the window and saw the dog in the rain. They knew they could not help the dog anymore.

Once upon a time there was a wealthy mouse. He lived in a cozy little house, and all day long he dreamed of the good things his wealth could buy. 

One day, the mouse felt the warmth of the sunshine on his face, and he began to melt with happiness. He was so excited that he put on his best party hat and danced around the room. 

Suddenly, he noticed something sparkly out of the corner of his eye. He crept up and saw that it was a pot filled with delicious cheese! The mouse scrambled to grab a piece and devoured it with a great big smile. 

From that day on, the mouse's dreams continued to come true. Every morning he was greeted with the warmth of the sun, and every evening he smiled at the memory of the cheese. He was a very happy mouse, indeed!

Once upon a time, there was a little peanut. He felt so fair, since he was the most special peanut in the whole world. 

He wanted to take time to explore, so he shut his eyes and thought of something magical. He imagined soaring through the sky, singing with the birds, and playing with the clouds.

Suddenly, he heard a funny noise. He opened his eyes and saw a chick that was chirping nearby. He smiled and his peanut-y heart beamed. The chick had shut his wings and was pecking around the ground looking for food.

The little peanut jumped at the chance to give the chick a helping hand. He rolled over to the chick and offered him a peanut. The chick happily chirped and ate the offering. The little peanut was so happy that he had made the chick fair.

One day, a bird wanted to fly high in the sky. The bird was very serious about flying. He flapped his wings and flew up, up, up!

As the bird flew, he saw a point far away. He wanted to go to the point. He thought, "I can fly there!" So, he flew and flew until he got close to the point.

When he got to the point, he saw a little bug. The bug said, "Hello, bird! Did you fly here?" The bird said, "Yes, I did! I flew very high to get here." The bug and the bird became friends, and they played together at the point.

Tim and Sam were brothers who loved to play with trains. They had many toy trains of different colors and sizes, and they liked to make them go on the tracks. Sometimes they pretended to be the drivers and made loud noises with their mouths.

One day, they saw a big train at the station. It was a real train, not a toy. It had a black engine that made steam come out of its chimney. The steam looked like white clouds in the air. Tim and Sam wanted to see the train up close, so they ran towards it.

"Wait, boys!" their mom called. "Don't go near the train, it's dangerous!"

But Tim and Sam did not listen. They were too excited to see the train. They crossed the yellow line that marked the safe distance, and climbed on the platform. They looked at the train with wonder and curiosity.

"Wow, look at this!" Tim said, pointing at a red lever. "I wonder what this does?"

"Let's find out!" Sam said, and pulled the lever.

Suddenly, the train started to move. It made a loud whistle and a loud rumble. Tim and Sam were scared. They tried to jump off the platform, but it was too late. The train was going too fast, and they could not escape.

The train hit them with a loud crash. Tim and Sam were hurt very badly. They cried and screamed, but no one could help them. Their mom ran to them, but she was too late. She hugged them and cried, but they did not answer. They were gone.

The moral of the story is: always listen to your mom, and do not play with things you do not know. They can be very dangerous and hurt you.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a big sister named Sophie. One day, Sophie brought home a pretty velvet dress. It was soft and smooth like a teddy bear. Lily loved it so much that she asked Sophie, "What is velvet?" Sophie explained, "Velvet is a special kind of cloth that feels thick and soft like a cuddly toy." 

Lily was so happy to learn something new. She ran her fingers over the velvet dress and felt how thick and cozy it was. She loved the way it looked too, with its shiny black color. Lily asked Sophie if she could wear the dress, but Sophie said it was too big for her. 

Lily was sad, but Sophie had an idea. She found a small piece of velvet and gave it to Lily. "You can keep this velvet," she said. Lily was thrilled to have a piece of the soft, thick cloth all for herself. She held it close to her face and felt its warmth. From that day on, Lily loved velvet and always wanted to touch and feel it whenever she could.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Jane. One night, Jane looked up and saw a star twinkling in the night sky. She wanted to get closer to the star, so she opened the door to her house and stepped outside.

Jane looked up at the star and wondered if she could reach it. She loved the star so much and it made her feel happy. She was determined to get to the star, so she started to walk through the night, towards it.

Jane kept walking until she saw a door in a big hill. She opened the door and went inside. Inside, she found a room full of stars and she was so excited! She wanted to take one of the stars and keep it with her forever.

Then, Jane had a serious thought. She realized that it wouldn't be right to take a star away from the room. So, she just smiled and decided to look at the stars one last time before leaving.

When she looked out of the window, Jane could see the twinkling star she saw before. She waved goodbye, realizing she could enjoy looking up at the star from her home. Jane was happy and smiled all the way home.

Lila and Tom were playing in the park. They saw a big, hairy dog. The dog had a sack in his mouth. He was running and barking.

"Look, a dog!" Lila said. "He has a sack. What is in the sack?"

"I don't know," Tom said. "Maybe toys. Or bones. Or candy."

Lila and Tom wanted to see the sack. They ran after the dog. The dog saw them and stopped. He wagged his tail and dropped the sack.

"Hi, dog," Lila said. "Can we see your sack?"

The dog nodded. He licked Lila's hand. He liked Lila.

"Can I pet you?" Tom asked. He was afraid of the dog. The dog was big and hairy.

The dog nodded. He licked Tom's hand. He liked Tom.

Lila and Tom petted the dog. They felt his soft fur. They opened the sack. They saw toys and bones and candy.

"Wow, dog," Lila said. "You have a lot of things. Can we play with you?"

The dog nodded. He barked happily. He shared his things with Lila and Tom.

Lila and Tom played with the dog. They threw the toys and the bones. They ate the candy. They had fun.

The dog was nice. He was not mean. He was not scary. He was a good friend.

Lila and Tom trusted the dog. They gave him hugs and kisses. They thanked him for his things.

"Bye, dog," Lila said. "We like you. We hope to see you again."

"Bye, dog," Tom said. "You are cool. You are fun. You are hairy."

The dog wagged his tail. He picked up his sack. He ran and barked.

Lila and Tom waved. They smiled. They had a good day.

Once upon a time there was a girl called Daisy. She was very stubborn and liked to act very silly. One day when Daisy was playing in the garden she found a pocket in the grass. She was very excited and decided to act out what she thought it could be. She pretended it was a home for a family of animals.

So she shouted to her mom: "Mom, look what I've found in the garden. It's a pocket!" Her mom came and looked at Daisy's pocket. She smiled and said "That's very clever Daisy, what are you going to do with it?".

Daisy looked up and said: "I'm going to act like it's a house for animals!". She went to find stones for the animals to sit on and some leaves for them to sleep on. Her mom watched her as she acted out her little play. Daisy was so stubborn that she was determined to make her pretend house perfect.

At the end of the day Daisy's pocket house was done and the animals were happy with their new home. Daisy was very proud of herself and went to bed with a smile on her face.

Tom and Anna are twins. They like to play in their room. They have many toys and books. But sometimes they get bored.

One day, they decide to explore the big drawer under their bed. They pull it open and see many things. They see old clothes, papers, crayons, and a bottle.

"What is this?" Tom asks, holding the bottle.

"I don't know. Maybe it is juice," Anna says.

"Can we drink it?" Tom says.

Anna shrugs. She is curious too. She opens the bottle and smells it. It smells funny. Not like juice.

"Let me try," Tom says. He takes the bottle and drinks a little. He makes a face. It tastes bad. Very bad.

"Yuck! This is not juice. This is icky," he says, spitting it out.

Anna laughs. She thinks it is funny. She drinks some too. She also makes a face.

"Yuck! You are right. This is icky. This is difficult to drink," she says, spitting it out.

They hear a voice. It is Mom. She is coming to their room.

"Tom, Anna, what are you doing?" she says.

They hide the bottle under the clothes. They act innocent.

"Nothing, Mom. We are just playing," they say.

Mom looks at them. She sees their wet mouths and their red faces. She sees the drawer open. She knows they are lying.

"Did you drink something from the drawer?" she asks.

They shake their heads. They are scared.

Mom finds the bottle. She reads the label. It says "vinegar".

"Tom, Anna, this is vinegar. This is not for drinking. This is for cooking. This can make you sick. Why did you drink it?" she asks.

They look down. They feel sorry.

"We were bored. We wanted to try something new. We thought it was juice," they say.

Mom sighs. She is not angry. She is worried.

"Tom, Anna, I know you are curious. But you have to be careful. Some things are not for drinking. Some things are dangerous. You have to ask me before you drink anything you don't know. Do you understand?" she says.

They nod. They understand.

"We are sorry, Mom. We won't do it again. We love you," they say.

Mom hugs them. She loves them too.

"Come on, let's go to the kitchen. I have some real juice for you. And some cookies. How does that sound?" she says.

They smile. They like juice and cookies. They follow Mom to the kitchen. They leave the drawer closed. They have learned their lesson.

Once upon a time, there was a clever duck. He had lots of adventures and wanted to try something new. So, one day, he decided to ride a bike. He wobbled around on the bike for a bit, but soon he got the hang of it. 

He swerved and looped around until he was a master at riding. Soon he was having so much fun that he invited all of his friends to join him. They all hopped on their own tiny bikes, and they took turns riding around together. 

The duck zoomed past them, shouting with joy. He was the clever one and they were happy they he was having so much fun. They laughed and played all day, until the sun started to set. Then they all said their goodbyes and the duck continued his adventure with a smile on his face.

Jill was looking for something very special - soup! She wanted the soup to be easy to make, but she couldn't find it anywhere. Everywhere she searched, she couldn't find what she was looking for. She visited lots of shops and even asked her friends if they had the easy soup she wanted. But they all said no.

Jill was getting very frustrated. She wanted the soup so badly, but couldn't find it. She decided to keep searching. She visited even more places, hoping to find what she wanted. Everywhere she looked seemed to be a dead end.

Finally, on the very last place she searched, she found it! She had searched high and low, and eventually she found the easy soup! She was so happy she had finally found it. She couldn't wait to make it for her friends. There was no better feeling than when she found the soup she had been looking for.

One day, a frog was hopping around a pond. It was a pretty frog, with bright green skin and a yellow belly. Suddenly, the frog heard a sound coming from the forest. The frog thought, "What is that noise?"

The frog hopped towards the forest. As he got closer, the frog started to worry. But he was curious and wanted to see what it was.

When he reached the edge of the forest, the frog saw a big, scary bear. The frog jumped in surprise and tried to run away. But the bear was too fast and caught the frog in its claws.

The bear growled and said, "I'm gonna eat you for dinner!"

The frog was so scared he couldn't move. After a few seconds, it was all over. The pretty frog was never seen again.

The story of the brave little frog, who ventured into the unknown despite his worries, ended with a bad ending. But it only goes to show that no matter how curious you are, sometimes things don't turn out the way you expect.

One day, there was a fireman who was very reliable. He always did his job to the best of his ability. The fireman climbed into his truck and drove off to the fire station.

He worked hard, day and night. He always made sure that every fire he fought was put out quickly and safely. He was reliable and strong. 

One day, he was climbing up a very tall ladder to a house when he heard a loud crash. Without thinking, he climbed faster and faster until he reached the window. Inside, he could see a small child, who was in trouble.

The fireman was able to rescue the child from the burning house and quickly put out the fire. Everybody was so grateful for the reliable fireman who had saved the day.

Tom and Mia are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big box near the pond. The box has a stamp and a label. It says "Mail to Grandma".

"Who is Grandma?" Tom asks.

"I don't know. Maybe she lives far away," Mia says.

They look inside the box. They see a soft toy. It is a duck. The duck has a yellow beak and a blue bow.

"Wow, what a nice duck!" Tom says.

"Can we play with it?" Mia asks.

They take the duck out of the box. They hug it and squeeze it. The duck makes a quack sound.

"Quack, quack, I'm a duck!" Tom says.

"Quack, quack, me too!" Mia says.

They run around the park with the duck. They pretend to swim and fly. They have fun.

But then, they hear a voice.

"Hey, where is my duck?" The voice is angry. It is a man. He is wearing a uniform. He is a mailman.

He sees Tom and Mia with the duck. He walks towards them.

"Give me back my duck! It is not yours! It is for Grandma!" He says.

Tom and Mia are scared. They don't want to give back the duck. They like the duck.

They look for a place to hide. They see a big bush. They run to the bush. They hide behind it. They hold the duck tight.

"Shh, duck, don't quack!" Tom says.

"Shh, duck, be quiet!" Mia says.

They hope the mailman will not find them. They hope he will go away. They hope they can keep the duck. They hope Grandma will not mind.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Tyler and Molly. They had a great time playing together every day. One day Tyler had an idea: they should play a game and speed around the park!

Molly thought this was a great idea, so off they went. Tyler ran as fast as he could, but Molly was faster and soon she was in the lead. Tyler shouted 'Hey Molly, show me your moves!' So Molly showed her special style of running and he copied her moves. Tyler was so fast!

But then he saw something strange. It was an unfamiliar person, running in an odd, fake way. He didn't look like he was running to win the game like Tyler and Molly were. Suddenly Tyler realized the person was sneaking around the park, trying to take something that didn't belong to him.

Tyler shouted 'STOP!' and the person stopped. The police arrived soon and arrested the fake runner. Tyler and Molly had saved the day!

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Spot. Spot loved to play ball on the pitch. He had a fine ball that was red and blue. One day, Spot saw a big tree near the pitch. He thought it was a great place to hide his ball when he was not playing.

The next day, Spot went to the pitch to play with his ball. He looked for his ball under the big tree, but it was gone! Spot was very sad. He looked all around the pitch, but he could not find his ball. Then, he heard a sound coming from the tree. It was a little bird.

The little bird had seen where Spot's ball had gone. The bird told Spot that a big wind had come and blew the ball far away. Spot thanked the little bird and went to find his ball. He walked a long way and finally found his ball near a big rock.

Spot was so happy to have his ball back. He ran back to the pitch and started playing again. The little bird watched Spot play and started to clap its wings. All the other animals saw the bird and started to applaud too. Spot knew that he had made a new friend and would always remember to keep his ball safe.

Sara and Ben love to swim in the sea. They have goggles and fins to see the fish and the reef. The reef is a big rock with many colors and shapes. Some fish are big and some are small. Some are red and some are blue. Sara and Ben like to play a game. They hide behind the reef and peek at each other. They try to surprise each other and make funny faces.

One day, they see a new fish. It is very big and has a long nose. It is gray and has spots. Sara and Ben are curious. They want to see it closer. They swim behind the reef and peek at the fish. The fish sees them and swims to them. It is not angry. It is friendly. It makes a noise like a whistle.

"Hello, fish," Sara says. "What is your name?"

The fish whistles again. It seems to say something.

"Can you talk?" Ben asks.

The fish nods. It points to its nose with its fin. It whistles again.

"Your nose is your name?" Sara guesses.

The fish nods again. It smiles.

Sara and Ben are amazed. They have never met a fish that can talk. They want to be friends with the fish. They swim with the fish and play with it. The fish shows them the reef and the other fish. It is very smart and strong. It can swim fast and jump high. Sara and Ben have a lot of fun.

They call the fish Nosey. Nosey likes his name. He likes Sara and Ben. They are his new friends. They promise to come back and visit him. They say goodbye and swim back to the shore. They are happy. They have seen a wonderful fish and learned a new word. They can't wait to tell their mom and dad.

It was a bright and sunny morning and the birds were singing. The ground was hard and dry. Then, something amazing happened. The ground started to spring! Out from the ground came a lot of junk. It was brown and smelly.

The junk was scattered everywhere. Some of it was brown and some was green. There were boxes and bottles of all shapes and sizes. A few of the brown bottles were covered in dirt.

The next day, a lady came and looked at the junk. She sorted through the mess, and carefully picked up some of the brown bottles. She said she could recycle the bottles and turn them into something new. 

Soon, more people came to take the junk away. Some of it was used to make new things and some was taken to the recycling center. 

The next day when the sun rose, the ground was tidy and clean. All of the junk had gone and the ground was ready to spring once again.

Once, there was a little girl called Emily. She was three years old. Every night, Emily's mum would close her door and say good night. Emily didn't like it. Every time, she wanted mum to stay in her room with her.

One night, Emily cried until her mum promised to stay with her. So, mum closed the bedroom door and sat on her bed. They both looked out of the window at the night sky.

Suddenly, the darkness was filled with a deep, sad silence. Emily was confused and a bit scared. She asked her mum, "What's wrong? Why is silences so sad?"

Mum explained that sometimes, even adults need a bit of a hug when it's quiet. Mum hugged Emily and spoke softly, "The silence will pass soon, and there will be happy noises again. It's OK."

Emily felt better and smiled. She closed her eyes and soon fell asleep in her mum's warm arms.

Once upon a time there was a kind giant named Bob. Bob was so kind and gentle that he stopped in the forest to help three little birds. 

The birds were hungry and asked Bob for some food. Bob smiled and reached into his pocket. He pulled out a handful of oats, which the birds quickly began to eat. 

Suddenly, the birds started to shrink! Bob was absolutely shocked and asked, "What happened to you?" 

One of the birds replied, "When we ate your oats, we drank the clear water from the stream and that is what made us shrink!"

Bob was amazed and thanked the birds for warning him. He promised to never again feed them oats and to always be sure there was clear water so that they wouldn't shrink again. 

The three little birds were so happy to be back to their original size. And from that day forward, Bob and the birds were the best of friends.

Once upon a time, there was a clever mouse who lived in the countryside. One day, the mouse was out exploring when it saw a pile of corn. The mouse was so excited and quickly began to eat it. Suddenly, something underneath the pile of corn revealed itself. It was a tiny door!

The mouse cautiously approached the door and carefully knocked on it. A small voice called out from behind the door, "Who is it?"

The mouse was so surprised. He answered, "It's a mouse. I'm looking for a place to live." 

The little voice said, "Come inside! I'm a squirrel, and I'm looking for a friend too!"

The mouse joyfully opened the door, and there was the squirrel, wearing a big smile on its face. 

The mouse and the squirrel became great friends. They played all day and bought lots of corn to share. The clever mouse was excited they were now best friends.

Once upon a time, there was an adventurous little fox. He was the bravest in all the land.

One day, he stumbled across a sparkling crystal that had been sitting in an old rotten log. He touched it gently. It was so beautiful! 

He admired it for a moment and then decided to take it home. He tucked it safely under his arm and raced back to his den. 

When he got there, he carefully placed the crystal in the centre of his den. He was so excited to have his very own crystal. 

Just then a wise old owl flew down from its perch in the tree and said, â€œThat is a special crystal, but it needs your help. If you keep it safe, it will take you on many adventures.â€

The fox was curious. He asked, â€œHow do I keep it safe?â€ 

The owl said, â€œBe sure to never let it rot. Always keep it away from the damp and darkness, then you will be able to go on the most incredible journeys.â€ The fox nodded and thanked the wise owl.

He set off on his first adventure that very day, with his crystal in tow. He discovered so many wonderful things and made lots of friends along the way. 

The fox had the most amazing time with his crystal and was so grateful for his new and adventurous life.

Once, there was a little boy who had a very special bed. Every night he would wake up, get into his bed and close his eyes.

One night he dreamed of swimming in the ocean. He saw all kinds of fish and even a shark. The shark was big and very friendly. He was thoughtful and watched over the little boy.

When the little boy woke, he was surprised by how much fun he had had. He thought the shark was so cool.

He asked his mom if he could go swimming in the ocean to try and find the shark. His mom smiled and said yes.

So the little boy packed his things and went to the beach. He looked and looked, but couldn't find the shark. He was sad and decided to take a nap.

Suddenly, he was woken up by sharp whiskers against his cheek. The little boy opened his eyes and there was the friendly shark!

The little boy laughed and hugged the shark. They had fun playing together in the sea. The shark was so thoughtful.

After many hours of play, the little boy said goodbye to the shark and promised to come and visit him again soon.

Tom and Jen are playing in the yard. They have a big shovel and a bucket. They want to dig a hole and bury something.

"What can we bury?" Tom asks Jen.

"Let's bury this can," Jen says. She shows Tom a can with a picture of a car on it. "It has oil inside. Oil is good for cars."

"OK," Tom says. He takes the can and puts it in the bucket. He follows Jen to a spot under the tree. They start to dig.

They dig and dig until they make a deep hole. Tom is about to put the can in the hole when he hears a loud noise. He looks up and sees a big truck coming down the road. The truck is red and has a sign that says "Danger".

"Look, Jen, a danger truck!" Tom says.

Jen looks up too. She sees the truck and gasps. She knows what the sign means. The truck is carrying something dangerous. Something that can explode.

"Tom, we have to stop!" Jen says. "We can't bury the can. The can has oil too. Oil and danger don't mix. They can make a big boom!"

Tom drops the can and runs to Jen. They grab the shovel and the bucket and run away from the hole. They hide behind the fence and watch the truck pass by.

They are scared, but they are also glad. They learned something new today. They learned that oil is good for cars, but not for burying. They learned that some things are dangerous and should be left alone. They learned to be careful and listen to each other.

They hug and smile. They are safe and happy. They decide to play something else. Something less risky. Something like tag or hide and seek.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Jane. She was only three years old and loved to explore the outdoors.

One day she went for a walk. She went down a long path until she noticed a delicate cone. It was light and sparkly and Jane was so curious! She wanted to take a closer look, so she leaned forward and reached out her hands. She was very careful and gentle so she wouldn't break the delicate cone.

As her fingers touched the sparkly cone, it began to glow and shine. Jane smiled as the cone sparkled in the sun. Suddenly, it lifted up off the ground and flew away! Jane giggled in delight as it flew higher and higher, until it was gone.

Jane was so excited. She leaned back and looked around. She was standing in a new, exciting place!

Once upon a time there was a girl named June. June was very competitive and loved to pick things. Every day she and her friends would go out and pick flowers and rocks. 

One day, June's friends all decided to do something special. They picked a tree and asked June to climb it. June wanted to show that she was the most competitive and said, â€œYes, I will climb the tree!â€

June's friends cheered and watched as she climbed higher and higher. But the branches became harder and harder to hold onto. June was scared and asked her friends, â€œPlease, can you help me?â€

But June's friends just laughed and said, â€œNo, you wanted to show us how competitive you are. You should be able to do it all by yourself.â€

June was stuck and didn't know what to do. Just then, a friendly voice said, â€œLet me help you, June. I know it can be hard to ask for help, but it's important to know when to do it.â€ June smiled, thanked the voice and let it help her down.

From that day on, June never forgot the lesson she learned: asking for help isn't a sign of weakness; it's a sign of strength.

Once there was a famous flute. It was special because it could make beautiful music. Everyone loved to listen to the flute's music.

One day, the flute got so excited playing the music, it began to split. The flute was very sad.

It asked the birds in the sky, "Why am I splitting?".

The birds replied, "Because you were playing so hard, you became too excited."

The flute was sad, but it knew what to do. It told the birds, "I'll be careful next time!".

The birds were happy. They said, "We can help you not split by playing the flute slowly and quietly."

So the flute learned to play slowly and quietly. Everyone was happy to hear the beautiful music the flute made. 
The famous flute split no more!

Once upon a time, there was an open letter that was sent to a little boy. The letter said that he had suffered something bad. The boy was sad and he cried. He called his mom to help him. His mom read the letter and explained that everyone suffers sometimes, just like the little boy did. She said that the little boy could be strong and find new ways to be happy even if he suffered. The little boy was still sad, but he was starting to feel better. Mom put her arms around him to give him a big hug and said, "Being open will help you heal." The little boy nodded and gave his mom a big hug back. He was feeling much better now. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a group of animals. They were very weak and looked very sad. The animals did not know what to do. Then, they saw a baby bird. It was struggling to fly. The animals decided to help the bird. They gathered around the small bird and offered their support.

The bird tried and tried, but it still could not get off the ground. Finally, one of the animals had an idea. He encouraged the others to join their wings and help the bird to fly. So thatâ€™s what they did.

The bird was very grateful. As the little bird soared into the sky, the group of animals saw how powerful teamwork could be. They learned that together, they were stronger than alone. Working together was the key to overcoming even the toughest challenges. The moral of the story is that if you work together, you can accomplish anything!

Lily and Tom are friends. They like to play together. One day, Lily has an idea. She says to Tom, "Let's visit the farm. We can see the animals and the tractor."

Tom likes the idea. He says, "Yes, let's go. Maybe we can feed the chickens and the cows."

They ask their moms if they can go. Their moms say yes, but they have to be careful and stay together. They give them some bread and carrots to share with the animals.

Lily and Tom walk to the farm. They see the chickens, the cows, the pigs, and the sheep. They give them some bread and carrots. The animals are happy and make noises. Lily and Tom laugh and pet them.

Then they see the tractor. It is big and red. But it is broken. One of the wheels is flat and the engine is quiet. Lily and Tom are curious. They want to see the tractor closer. They climb on it and pretend to drive.

But the farmer sees them. He is angry. He says, "Hey, what are you doing? Get off my tractor. It is broken and dangerous. You could get hurt."

Lily and Tom are scared. They say, "Sorry, sorry. We didn't know. We just wanted to see it."

The farmer says, "Well, now you have seen it. But you should not touch things that are not yours. And you should not go near the tractor. It is not a toy. It is a tool. I need it to work on the farm. But now it is broken and I have to fix it."

Lily and Tom say, "We are sorry. We won't do it again. We will go now."

The farmer says, "OK, go. But be careful and listen to your moms. And next time, ask before you visit the farm."

Lily and Tom say, "OK, we will. Bye, farmer. Bye, animals."

They run back to their moms. They tell them what happened. Their moms are not happy. They say, "You should not have climbed on the tractor. It was wrong and rude. And you could have been hurt. You have to be more careful and respectful."

Lily and Tom say, "We are sorry. We learned our lesson. We won't do it again."

Their moms say, "We hope so. We love you, but you have to be good."

Lily and Tom say, "We love you too. And we will be good."

They hug their moms and go home. They are still friends. But they don't visit the farm anymore.

Once upon a time, there was a mummy and daddy. Mummy and daddy wanted to build a very special house. They worked really hard and were very successful. Mummy painted the walls with pretty colours. Daddy put in special lights and carpets. 

Once the house was built, mummy and daddy celebrated by making lots of toast. Mummy and daddy could now live in a nice and cosy house. 

They looked around and smiled. They were so happy with their new house and what a successful job they had done. 

The end.

Once upon a time there was a big, red yawn. It opened wide and stretched out like a big bear getting ready for a nap. All the animals around the red yawn were curious. What was this big, red object?

The red yawn opened even wider and out popped a small little cat. The cat let out a big purr and started to play with the animals around the red yawn. The animals all had so much fun and eventually grew tired.

The cat looked tired and started to yawn. The animals said, "Goodbye cat, we had lots of fun today." The cat said, "Goodbye" and with one last big, red yawn, and hopped back inside the red yawn and went to sleep. 

The animals were pleased to have met the cat, and the red yawn became a special place for all the animals to gather and play. 
The End.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved playing with his toy trucks. One day, he was playing with his favorite red truck when he heard a loud noise outside. He looked out the window and saw a big, blue truck.

"Wow, that's a nice truck," Timmy said to himself.

He went outside to get a closer look and saw that the driver of the blue truck was stuck in the mud. Timmy asked the driver if he needed help.

"Yes, please," the driver said.

Timmy ran back inside to get his red truck. He drove it over to the blue truck and hooked it up with a rope. Together, they pulled the blue truck out of the mud.

"Thank you so much, Timmy," the driver said. "You're a very nice boy."

From that day on, Timmy and the driver became good friends. Timmy loved helping people in need and using his toy trucks to do it.

Once upon a time there was a naughty bear who lived in a forest. Every evening, he would go to a meadow and pray. One evening, he saw a beautiful rainbow while he was praying. He thought it was so pretty and wanted to touch it.

He said, "Please God, can I touch the rainbow?" But God didn't answer him.

Just then, a rabbit hopped past. The bear asked the rabbit, "Can I please touch the rainbow?"

The rabbit laughed and said, "No, naughty bear. You can't touch the rainbow. That's for God only."

The bear was sad, but he understood. He bowed his head and said, "Okay, I won't touch the rainbow. I'll just keep on praying." 

So, every evening the naughty bear kept on praying, and he was so happy.

Once upon a time, there was a happy cow named Betsy. Betsy was different from the other cows because she had spots all over her body. One day, Betsy met a little girl named Lily. 

"Hello, Betsy! You spin around like a ballerina!" said Lily. 

"Yes, I love to spin," replied Betsy. "But sometimes, the other cows make fun of me because I look different." 

"Don't worry, Betsy," said Lily. "Being different is what makes you special. I think your spots are beautiful." 

Betsy felt happy and grateful for Lily's kind words. From that day on, Betsy didn't feel ashamed of her spots anymore. She continued to spin and dance, feeling proud of who she was.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. On a hot summer day, she decided to go for a walk. As she was walking, Lucy saw a big, shiny door. She walked up to the door and struggled to open it, but it wouldn't budge. 

"Help!" Lucy shouted. 

A kind man nearby came over and offered to help. He placed his shoulder against the door and pushed. 

"Maybe it's just too hot," the man said. 

The man tried pushing again. This time, the door opened with a loud creak. 

Lucy thanked the man for his help and continued on her way. The sun was hot, but the day was perfect. Lucy kept walking until she reached the end of the road, content and happy.

Once upon a time, there was a forest where all the animals lived. The forest was their home and they loved it very much.

One day, the forest started to get very dry. The animals were very thirsty, so they all looked outside the forest for help.

A kind man came to the forest. He had a water can and he provided the animals with water. Even though the water was a bit bitter, the animals were very happy.

The kind man came back to the forest every day. He provided food and water for the animals. The animals were very thankful for his help. 

The animals were very happy in the forest and never became thirsty or hungry again. The kind man had provided them with all the things they needed. They were so grateful to him!

Once upon a time, there was a dolphin named Dolly. Dolly was very happy and loved to play with her friends. One day, Dolly's friends wanted to celebrate her birthday. They made a cake and sang happy birthday to Dolly.

But Dolly was feeling grumpy. She didn't want to celebrate her birthday because she was getting older. "I don't want to be old," Dolly said to her friends. "I don't want to celebrate."

Dolly's friends were sad that she didn't want to celebrate. They tried to cheer her up, but she wouldn't listen. Later that day, Dolly got sick and had to go to the hospital. Her friends were worried and went to visit her. But it was too late, Dolly had passed away. Her friends were very sad and wished they had celebrated her birthday when they had the chance.

Once upon a time, there was a dad and a baby. The dad and baby were very happy together. But then one day, the dad had to go away and the baby was sad. 

The baby wanted to find a way to be with the dad again. So he went looking for a way to unite with him.

He looked everywhere, but he couldn't find a way. Soon, he was so sad that he started to cry.

But then one day, while exploring, he came across a very special door. This door was the escape that he was looking for - an escape to unite with his dad.

He opened the special door, and there in front of him was dad! He was so happy that he ran straight into his arms. His dad was so glad to be with him, he picked him up and gave him lots of spoilt cuddles and kisses.

The dad and baby were reunited, and nobody ever made them apart ever again. They were reunited forever and ever.

Once, there was a young boy who was very rude. He never said nice things to anyone, and he thought he was better than everyone else.

One day, the boy's parents gave him a present. It was a book. But the boy didn't want it. He threw it away and said it was silly.

The boy's parents felt very sad. So they sent him away on a trip. He was going to visit his uncle, who lived in another city.

When he reached his uncle's house, he was surprised to find a library. He had never seen so many books before. He wanted to read the books, but he had to be nice to his uncle first.

But no matter how much he tried, the boy remained very rude. His uncle was so angry that he told the boy to leave his house. The boy had to return home without reading even one book.

The bad end of this story is a lesson for us all; no matter how much you want something, if you don't have good manners, you won't get it.

Once upon a time, there was a gentle rabbit, hopping around the garden. He wanted to gather some of his friends. He looked around for them, but couldn't find any. Until, he noticed something he had never seen before. It was a big, bright calendar on the wall! 

The rabbit was excited and slowly hopped closer, wondering what it could be. He touched it and suddenly, there were all kinds of animals, gathered in a circle. They were all smiling and waving!

The rabbit was overjoyed! He had so much fun with his new friends. Whenever he wanted to get together, he just had to look at the calendar.

The days passed, and the rabbit and his friends spent lots of time together, having fun and gathering around the warm sun. 

The days turned into years, and the rabbit was still gathering with his friends, thanks to the big, bright calendar!

Once there was a furry rabbit. He was very happy, but he was also very hungry. He was hopping through the forest, looking for something to eat. Suddenly, he saw a carrot! He quickly hopped to the carrot, picked it up and began to eat it. It was so yummy!

Suddenly, a big bear came walking by. The bear saw the little rabbit eating the carrot. The bear smiled and then he leaned down to the rabbit. He gently kissed the rabbit on the head!

The rabbit was so surprised! He had never been kissed before. The bear laughed and said, â€œThat was to show you that I care.â€ The rabbit smiled and thanked the bear. Together they hopped off into the forest.

Once upon a time, two friends walked through a park together. One of them was wearing a white top.

"Look!" said the friend wearing the white top, pointing to a big tree. "That tree looks so pretty!"

The other friend smiled. "Let's pass it," she said.

The two friends continued their walk, until they came to a pond. It was full of fishes.

The friends looked at the fishes and said, "These fishes are so colorful."

The friend wearing the white top noticed something else. "Hey! There's an orange fish."

The other friend smiled. "Let's pass it," she said.

The two friends kept walking until they came to a spicy food truck.

"This food looks amazing!" said the friend with the white top.
"Let's get something!" said the other friend.

They ordered some delicious spicy food and ate it with gusto. It was so tasty!

The two friends laughed and enjoyed their meal. The spicy food was a nice treat for their walk in the park.

Once upon a time, there was a modern band. The band made really cool music. All of the people in the town enjoyed listening to the band's music.

One day, while everyone was listening to the band at a concert, a giant bellowing noise filled the air. Everyone looked up and noticed a huge animal in the sky, and it was getting closer and closer!

Suddenly, the band stopped playing, and all of the people started to worry and scream. Then, one brave band member stepped forward and said that he had a plan. He said that he was going to try to rescue the animal!

He asked everyone to clap as loud as they could, so he could find the animal in the sky and bring it down safely. Everyone clapped, and the band member flew up in the air and grabbed the animal. The animal was so happy.

The band member brought the animal down to the ground, and everyone cheered. The band started to play again, and everyone celebrated. The band member was a hero and the modern band was very proud.

Once upon a time, in a small village, there was a reliable dog named Spot. Spot was always there to help his friends. One day, rain fell very hard. It rained so much that the village had a flood. The water was everywhere, and the animals were scared.

Spot went to his friend, Cat. Cat was on a tree, and she was very scared too. Spot said, "Don't worry, Cat. I will help you." Cat looked at Spot and said, "Thank you, Spot. I don't like this water. It's cold and tastes bad."

Spot swam through the water and got a big stick. He gave it to Cat, and Cat held on tight. Spot pulled Cat through the water to a safe place. All the animals were happy that Spot was there to help them. The rain stopped, and the village was safe again.

Lily was a patient girl. She liked to wait for her mom to come home from work. She would sit on the couch and look at her books. She would wonder what her mom was doing. Was she talking to people? Was she making things? Was she having fun?

One day, Lily heard a loud noise. It was the alarm. It was beeping and flashing. Lily was scared. She did not know what to do. She ran to the door and looked outside. She saw smoke and fire. She saw people running and shouting. She saw a big red truck with a siren.

Lily wanted her mom. She cried and called her name. She hoped her mom was safe. She hoped her mom would come soon.

"Mommy, mommy, where are you?" she sobbed.

Then, she heard a voice. It was her mom. She was on the phone. She sounded worried but calm.

"Lily, honey, are you okay? I'm sorry, I can't come home right now. There's a fire at my office. But don't worry, I'm fine. The firefighters are here. They are helping us. I love you so much. Can you do something for me?"

Lily sniffed and nodded. She was happy to hear her mom.

"What can I do, mommy?"

"Can you go to Mrs. Lee's house? She's our neighbor. She's very nice. She will take care of you until I come back. Can you do that, honey?"

Lily nodded again. She liked Mrs. Lee. She had a cat and a garden. She always gave Lily cookies and juice.

"Okay, mommy. I will go to Mrs. Lee's house. I love you too. Please be careful."

"Thank you, Lily. You're such a brave girl. I'm so proud of you. I'll see you soon. Bye, honey."

Lily hung up the phone. She grabbed her backpack and her teddy bear. She ran to Mrs. Lee's house. She knocked on the door. Mrs. Lee opened it and smiled.

"Hello, Lily. Come in, come in. I heard about the fire. I'm so sorry. Your mom called me and told me to look after you. Don't worry, she's okay. She'll be here soon. Do you want some cookies and juice?"

Lily nodded and smiled. She felt a little better. She went inside and sat on the couch. She hugged her teddy bear and looked at Mrs. Lee's cat. She wondered when her mom would come home. She hoped the fire would stop. She was patient. She waited.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to collect shiny rocks and pretty flowers. One day, she went for a walk in the park with her mom. She saw a lot of flowers and rocks on the ground and picked them up to add to her collection.

Suddenly, it started to rain. Lily and her mom ran to a nearby shelter. They waited for the rain to stop. When it stopped, they went home. Lily's mom said, "You need a shower, Lily. You're all wet." 

Lily took a shower and her mom helped her dry off. Then, Lily showed her mom all the rocks and flowers she collected. Her mom said, "Wow, Lily! You have a fair collection now!" Lily was happy and smiled.

Tom and his mom moved to a new house. They had many boxes to unpack. Tom was not happy. He missed his old house and his friends. He did not want to unpack his toys.

"Tom, can you help me unpack this box?" his mom asked. "It has your books and your puzzles."

Tom shook his head. "No, I don't want to. I want to go back to the old house."

His mom gave him a hug. "I know you are sad, but we have to unpack. This is our new home now. Maybe you will find something fun in the box."

Tom sighed. He opened the box. He saw his books and his puzzles. He also saw something else. It was a stuffed owl. It had big eyes and soft feathers. Tom liked owls. He picked up the owl and hugged it.

"Who gave you this owl?" his mom asked.

"It was from Grandma. She said it was a wise owl. She said it would help me with my worry."

Tom's mom smiled. "That was very nice of Grandma. She is very wise too. Do you feel less worried now?"

Tom nodded. He felt a little better. He decided to unpack his toys. He put the owl on his bed. He thought maybe the new house was not so bad. He hoped he would make new friends soon. He thanked Grandma for the wise owl. He thought maybe the owl would help him with his dreams.

Once upon a time, there was an ordinary mixer. The mixer was so big that it was taller than everyone in the room. The mixer had a lot of buttons and knobs, but no one knew how to use it.

One day, a little girl came into the room. She had big hair and bright eyes. She looked at the mixer curiously. She saw a red button and decided to press it. 

As soon as she pressed the button, the mixer started to whirr and hum. It mixed together a lot of ingredients until it made a yummy cake. The girl was so happy! She wanted to eat some of the cake.

But when she tried to get a piece, she found that the mixer was stuck. The girl knew what to do. She grabbed a big knife and carefully cut around the edges of the mixer, until it separated from the cake. 

The girl was very proud of herself. She enjoyed eating the cake, and the mixer was happy to be back in one piece. From then on, the girl used the mixer whenever she wanted to make a delicious cake.

One day, a smart cat named Tom found a ticket on the ground. He blinked his eyes to make sure it was real. Tom picked up the ticket with his paw.

Tom took the ticket to his friend, a dog named Max. Max looked at the ticket and blinked too. They were both very excited. They knew the ticket was for a fun ride at the park.

Tom and Max went to the park together. They gave the ticket to the man at the ride. The ride went up and down, making them laugh. After the ride, they went home, happy they found the ticket.

Ben and Mia were twins who liked to play with their toys. They had many toys, because their mom and dad were rich. They had dolls, cars, books, puzzles, and a big bell that made a loud sound.

One day, they decided to play a game with the bell. They took turns to hide the bell somewhere in the house, and the other one had to find it. They put the bell under the bed, behind the sofa, in the closet, and in the bathtub. They had a lot of fun.

But then, Ben had an idea. He wanted to trick Mia and make her look for the bell for a long time. He put the bell in the oven, and closed the door. He thought Mia would never find it there.

He ran back to the living room, where Mia was waiting. He said, "I hid the bell very well. You will never find it. Go and look for it."

Mia smiled and said, "OK, I will. But I am good at finding things. I will find the bell soon."

She started to look for the bell in the usual places, but she could not find it. She looked under the bed, behind the sofa, in the closet, and in the bathtub. She could not hear the bell anywhere.

She was about to give up, when she smelled something strange. She followed her nose to the kitchen, where she saw smoke coming out of the oven. She opened the oven door, and saw the bell. It was very hot and black. It did not make any sound.

She was very angry. She took the bell out of the oven with a mitt, and ran to the living room. She saw Ben laughing on the couch. She said, "Ben, you are very bad. You put the bell in the oven. You burned the bell. You ruined the game. I don't want to play with you anymore."

Ben stopped laughing. He saw the bell in Mia's hand. He felt sorry. He said, "Mia, I am sorry. I was trying to be funny. I did not mean to burn the bell. I did not know the oven was on. Please forgive me. I want to play with you."

Mia looked at Ben. She saw that he was sorry. She said, "Ben, I forgive you. But you have to be careful. You could have hurt yourself or the house. And you have to share your toys. The bell is ours, not yours."

Ben nodded. He said, "You are right, Mia. I have to be careful and share. The bell is ours. Can we still play with it?"

Mia said, "Yes, we can. But we have to wait until it cools down. And we have to find a new place to hide it. A place that is safe and fun."

They hugged each other, and went to look for a new place to hide the bell. They were twins who liked to play with their toys. And they loved each other.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She loved singing and always used her toy microphone to sing her favorite songs. One day, she felt bored and decided to go outside to play.

While playing, she found a real microphone on the ground. She felt happy and started singing loudly into the microphone. But then, a man came and took the microphone away from her. Lily felt sad and cried.

The moral of the story is that sometimes we should not take things that do not belong to us. It is important to ask permission before taking something.

Once upon a time, there were two good friends- a pot and a doggy. The pot's name was Cooper and the doggy was loyal and kind. Everyday Cooper and the doggy would go on an adventure and have lots of fun.

One day, Cooper and the doggy went to a big field. The field was green and sunshine was coming down. Cooper was so happy and said to the doggy, "Let's pick some flowers!" The doggy looked up at Cooper and agreed.

They picked many flowers and put them into Cooper's pot. They were so proud of the flowers. When they were finished, Cooper wanted to say thanks to the doggy, so he gave the doggy a big hug and said, "You are so loyal and kind. I'm very lucky to be your friend. I want to give you this pot of flowers, so you can remember our special times together."

The doggy was so happy and thanked Cooper. They hugged one more time and both knew they would always be good friends.

One day, a little boy named Tim and his dog, Spot, went for a walk. They saw a big tree and wanted to play near it. Tim was happy, but Spot was scared. Spot saw something behind the tree and did not want to go closer.

Tim said to Spot, "Don't be scared, I am here with you." They walked closer to the tree and saw a small bird. The bird had a hurt wing and could not fly. Tim and Spot wanted to help the bird.

They found a soft place for the bird to settle. Tim gave the bird some food, and Spot stayed with the bird on the left side to keep it safe. The bird was not scared anymore because Tim and Spot were there to help.

Ben came out from the curtain and laughed.

"You're right, Lily. The curtain is too small for both of us. Maybe we can find a bigger curtain to play with. Or we can play something else," Ben said.

Lily and Ben hugged and decided to play with their blocks. They had fun building towers and knocking them down. They forgot about the purple curtain. They were happy.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. Her name was Holly. Holly wanted to play in the park one day. When she got there, she saw a big pit. It looked very inviting so Holly decided to climb in. 

Holly was having a lot of fun in the pit. She was digging in the sand and walking around. But after a while, Holly started to throw sand at the people who were in the park. That was not a very good way to behave. 

A nice lady saw what Holly was doing and walked over. She sat next to Holly and said: â€œHolly, throwing sand is not very nice. Would you like something else to do in the pit?â€ Holly nodded. 

So the nice lady brought out some tasty apples. Holly was so happy! She shared the apples with the other children in the pit and they all enjoyed them. Holly had a lot of fun in the pit and behaved nicely!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who lived at the beach. Every day, she would take a bucket and shovel and build a sandcastle. She loved to watch the giant waves crashing against it. One day, she decided to build an extra big sandcastle!

As she was making it, a shark swam towards her. The girl screamed and ran away from the shark. But then, it swam up to her and said, "Don't be scared! I just want to help you build your sandcastle!"

The girl was still afraid, but the shark said, "I'm a friendly shark! I won't hurt you, I promise!" So the girl reached into her pocket and pulled out a little open bag of sand. She sprinkled it over the sandcastle and the shark used his tail to spread it around. Together, they built a beautiful sandcastle.

The girl and her new friend said goodbye and, as the waves gently washed away the sandcastle at the end of the day, the girl was happy knowing that she and the friendly shark had built something wonderful together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved playing with her toys and exploring the world around her. One day, she was playing with her dolls when her mom called her for lunch. 

Lily ran to the kitchen, but on the way, she accidentally bumped into the table and hurt her finger. "Ouch!" she cried. 

Her mom asked, "What happened, Lily?" 

"I hurt my finger," she replied. 

Her mom checked her finger and said, "It's okay, Lily. Let's put a band-aid on it." 

After lunch, Lily went back to playing with her dolls. But she wanted to play with her friend, Emma. She asked her mom, "Can I call Emma to come over and play?" 

Her mom said, "Sorry, Lily. Emma is not available today. She is busy with her family." 

Lily was sad, but she kept playing with her dolls. Suddenly, she heard a loud noise. It was her little brother, Max, who was playing with his toys too. Lily got angry and shouted, "Stop it, Max!" 

Max didn't listen and kept making noise. Lily got even angrier and threw her doll at him. Unfortunately, she missed and hit a vase on the shelf. It fell and broke into many pieces. 

Lily's mom came running, and when she saw what had happened, she was very upset. "Lily, you should never throw things when you are angry. You could have hurt Max or yourself," she scolded. 

Lily felt very sorry, and her mom hugged her, but she knew she had done something wrong. From that day on, she promised to always control her anger and be careful with her actions.

Once upon a time, there were two friends called Mary and Claire. Mary was very thoughtful while Claire was always curious. One day, they decided to go to the park. 

At the park, there was a big tree with branches that hung low and curved into a smile.

"Let's sit in the tree," said Claire. 

They both eagerly climbed and sat on a branch. Then, Claire noticed a shiny metal hook stuck to the trunk of the tree. 

"What do you think this hook is for?" asked Claire.

"I'm not sure," said Mary, very thoughtful.

Then, Mary had an idea. She took a string from her pocket, wrapped it around the hook and hung her bag.

"That's so cool!" said Claire.

Mary smiled. "Now our things are safe," she said. 

Claire and Mary laughed and played in the tree all day, thankful for the kind hook.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and eat snacks. One day, her mom gave her a large tray of cookies to share with her friends. Lily was very excited and wanted to show her friends the big tray of cookies.

When her friends arrived, Lily wanted to impress them by throwing the tray up in the air. But she didn't catch it and the tray fell on the ground, breaking into many pieces. The cookies were ruined and her friends were sad.

Lily learned that it's not good to throw things because they can break and people can get hurt. She also learned that it's important to share and be careful with things that are given to us. From that day on, Lily promised to be more careful and never throw things again.

Lily was very happy. Today was her birthday and she had a party. She invited her friends from the park to come and play. She had balloons, cake, and toys.

She saw Ben at the door. Ben was her best friend. He had a big box in his hands. He smiled and said, "Happy birthday, Lily! I have a present for you."

Lily was curious. She opened the box and saw a doll. The doll had long hair, a pink dress, and shoes. Lily loved the doll. She hugged Ben and said, "Thank you, Ben! She is so pretty. What is her name?"

Ben thought for a moment. He said, "Her name is Daisy. Do you like her?"

Lily nodded. She said, "I like her very much. Do you want to play with her?"

Ben nodded. He said, "Yes, I do. Can I offer her some cake?"

Lily giggled. She said, "Yes, you can. But be careful. She is clumsy. She might drop the cake."

Ben and Lily went to the table. They gave Daisy some cake. But Daisy was clumsy. She dropped the cake on the floor. Ben and Lily laughed. They said, "It's okay, Daisy. We still love you." They cleaned the mess and played with Daisy. They had a lot of fun at the party.

Ben and Mia like to play with their toys. They have cars, dolls, blocks and balls. They share their toys and have fun. But sometimes they lose their toys. They look under the bed, in the closet, in the drawers, but they cannot find them.

One day, they lose their favorite ball. It is red and bouncy and shiny. They look everywhere, but they cannot see it. They are sad and cry. Mom hears them and comes to help. She asks them where they last played with the ball.

They remember they played with it in the yard. They run outside and look for the ball. They see it on the roof of the shed. It must have bounced very high and landed there. They cannot reach it. They are sad and cry again.

Mom has an idea. She gets a ladder and puts it next to the shed. She tells Ben and Mia to be careful and hold her hand. She climbs the ladder and gets the ball. She gives it to Ben and Mia. They are happy and hug her.

They thank Mom and go back to play with the ball. They are careful not to throw it too high. They do not want to lose it again. They play until it is dark and quiet. They go inside and put their toys away. They say good night to Mom and go to sleep. They dream of their red and bouncy and shiny ball.

Once upon a time there was a young girl named Daisy. Daisy wanted a pet bird so she asked her mom if she could get one. 

"No Daisy," said her mom, "itâ€™s too much work to take care of a bird." 

Daisy was disappointed and sat down on the couch. Suddenly, she saw an advertisement on TV and it said that a nice birdcage was available in the store. Daisy asked her mom again if she could get a bird and this time her mom said "Yes!"

Daisy was so happy that she ran to the store and found the perfect birdcage. She asked the shopkeeper how much the birdcage was and he said it was only $10. 

Daisy accepted his offer and thanked him for the birdcage. She also thanked her mom for being so understanding and then went home. She excitedly put the birdcage in her room and it was the perfect place for her new pet bird. 

From that day on, Daisy and her pet bird were best friends.

Once upon a time, there was a patient little girl. She was very quiet and never made a peep. Everyday she would watch the world pass by her window.

One day, she saw something beautiful. There were colorful flowers and butterflies peeking out of the bushes. The girl was so excited!

She opened the window to get a better look. When she did, an even more beautiful sight appeared. It was a rainbow!

The little girl was so amazed but stayed patient as she watched the colors sparkle. She couldn't believe how beautiful it was. 

After a while, the rainbow faded away and the little girl went back to her window. She patiently waited for the rainbow to peek out again, and sure enough, the next day it did. 

The little girl was so happy and continued to patiently wait for the rainbow to peek out again each day. She knew that she just had to be patient to enjoy the most beautiful sight in the world.

Once upon a time, there was a cool, little robot. The robot had lots of exciting features. One day, the robot wanted to go exploring. So, it moved towards the exit and went outside. But, it was too hot outside, so the robot had to find a way to stay cool.

It suddenly had an idea. It saw a big tree with lots of leaves. So, the robot decided to replace its metal parts with lots of leaves. It worked! The leaves kept the robot cool. The robot was so excited, it danced around.

Now, every day the robot leaves the house with its new leaves and has lots of fun. It can stay cool for hours and hours. Best of all, the robot never gets too hot.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved flowers and always picked them in the garden. One day, she saw a modern toy in a store and demanded her mom to buy it for her. But her mom said no and told her that she already had many toys to play with. 

Lily was sad and decided to go to the garden to pick some flowers. As she was walking, she saw a butterfly and followed it. The butterfly led her to a beautiful lily flower. Lily was amazed by its beauty and picked it to take home. 

When she got home, she showed her mom the lily flower and her mom was happy to see Lily happy. Lily realized that she didn't need a modern toy to be happy, and that the simple things in life, like a beautiful flower, can bring joy too.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play games with her friends, but sometimes she felt lonely when they were not around. One day, she found a new game in her toy box. It was a soft ball that she could squeeze. She was so excited to play with it.

Lily played with the ball all day long, squeezing it and throwing it into the air. But when it was time for bed, she couldn't find the ball. She looked everywhere, but it was nowhere to be found. She felt very sad and lonely again.

The next day, Lily's mom found the ball under the couch. But when Lily squeezed it, it popped and broke. She was so sad that her favorite game was gone forever. She learned that sometimes things we love can be taken away from us, and it can make us feel very lonely.

John was an anxious little boy. Every day he liked to fly outside and explore. One day, he had an exciting idea. He wanted to fly higher than he ever had before! He got his wings and off he flew, into the sky. 

The clouds flew by and John flew faster, with each beat from his wings. He was so close to reaching his goal. Suddenly, he noticed some birds flying much higher and even faster. He wanted to keep up with them!

John was anxious. He hadn't flown this high before, and he didn't know if he could make it. But then he decided to give it a try. He took a deep breath and flew harder than ever. He was so close to the birds now!

Suddenly, John felt like he was floating. He had done it! He had flown higher than before and now he was gliding on the wind. John felt so proud of himself. He had turned his idea into a reality!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, Lily went to the beach with her mom and dad. She saw a tall wave and wanted to surf on it. Her dad said, "You're too little to surf, Lily. Maybe when you're older." 

Lily was sad but she saw a big box on the beach. She asked her mom if she could open it. Her mom said yes and Lily opened the box. Inside, she found a surfboard that was just her size. She was so excited! 

She ran to her dad and said, "Look, Daddy! I found a surfboard! Can I try to surf now?" Her dad smiled and said, "Sure, Lily! Let's go catch some waves!" Lily was so happy and she surfed on the tall wave like a pro. From that day on, Lily loved to surf and she always looked for treasure boxes on the beach.

Tom and Lily are friends. They like to play in the park. They have a ball and a kite. They have fun.

One day, they see a big hole in the grass. They are curious. They go to the hole and look inside. They see something shiny. They want to know what it is.

They try to reach the shiny thing, but the hole is too deep. They need a tool. They look around and see a stick. They use the stick to poke the shiny thing. It makes a noise. It is a bell!

They pull the bell out of the hole. It is very pretty. It has a ribbon and a tag. The tag has a name and a phone number. It is a lost pet's bell!

Tom and Lily are honest. They want to help the pet find its owner. They use Lily's phone to call the number. A lady answers. She is very happy. She says the bell belongs to her cat, Fluffy. She lost Fluffy two days ago. She thanks Tom and Lily for finding the bell.

Tom and Lily are proud. They solve the mystery of the shiny thing. They help the lady and Fluffy. They are good friends. They go back to playing in the park. They have fun.

Once upon a time, in a very far away land, there lived a very wealthy man. He had a very big house and lots of toys to play with.

One day, the man went outside of his house to see if there was anyone around that he could share his wealth with. He started to look far, and then he caught a glimpse of something glowing.

He came closer and then he found a small creature. It was no bigger than his hand, and it looked like a little star. He watched the creature for a minute and wondered what it was.

The little star creature suddenly shot across the sky and disappeared. The wealthy man was sad because he wanted to keep the creature for himself, so he wished for it to come back.

And amazingly, the star creature came back, glowing even brighter and bigger than before. The man reached out, and the creature stayed in his hands. From that day forward, the wealthy man and the star were the best of friends and he was very happy with his new friend.

Once there was a naughty girl named Lucy. She had long, brown hair that she liked to pull. One day, she was looking in the mirror, and she couldn't help but pull her hair. Her mom saw her and said "No, Lucy, that's not nice. Let's fix your hair." Lucy's mom combed out her hair and put it into a pretty ponytail. Then, she gave Lucy a big hug and said, "Now you look better!" Lucy was happy that her hair was fixed. From then on, she tried not to be so naughty with her hair!

Once there lived an old farmer. He had a kind heart and was very friendly. He used to help his neighbors whenever they needed it.

One day, his neighbor was in trouble and had lost all of his buckets. The kind old farmer offered to lend him a barrel for two days. 

His neighbor thanked him and took the barrel home. After two days, the neighbor unfortunately did not return the barrel. 

The old farmer waited and waited for the barrel to be returned, but it never was. He was sad that his neighbor did not keep his promise. 

The old farmer never saw the barrel again. He was very unhappy but had to accept the situation.
