Once upon a time, there was a monkey. He was very popular and had many friends. One day, he found a banana tree and started eating all the bananas. His friends asked him to share, but the monkey just yelled at them and said no.

His friends were sad and went away. The monkey soon realized that he was alone and had no one to play with. He felt lonely and sad. He realized that it was not good to be selfish and not share with his friends.

The monkey decided to apologize to his friends and share the bananas. His friends forgave him and they all played together. The monkey learned that sharing is important and it is better to have friends than to be alone.

There were two friends in the park. Their names were Jimmy and Jane. They care about each other very much.

They were playing together when Jimmy saw some work to do. He asked Jane to help him, and she said yes. 

They worked for a long time but the work was fun. When they were done, they looked around and felt very comfortable.

After they finished the work, they took a break. They played catch and hide-and-seek until it was time to go home. 

Jimmy and Jane said goodbye and hugged each other tightly. Both knew that they would always care for each other.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys on the floor. One day, her little brother came in and started to play with her toys too. Lily got mad and said, "No, these are mine!" Her brother got sad and started to cry.

Lily felt weird and knew she did something wrong. She said sorry and gave her brother a toy to play with. They started to play together and had fun. But then, they saw a spider on the floor. Lily's brother got scared and tried to shoot it with a toy gun. But Lily said, "No, don't hurt it. Let's put it outside."

They worked together and put the spider outside. They both felt happy and proud of themselves for helping the spider. Lily learned that sharing is important and that it's always better to be kind to others, even bugs.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was very tired after playing all day with her friends. She wanted to go home and take a nap. 

As she was walking, she saw a big box on the ground. She went to see what was inside and she saw a cute puppy! The puppy was lost and needed a home. 

Lily was so happy to receive the puppy as a gift. She took the puppy home and gave him a warm bed to sleep in. She played with him and gave him lots of love. 

From that day on, Lily was never tired again because she had a new friend to play with. She was happy to have a new addition to her home.

Tom and Lily liked to play with their toys in the garden. They had a big box of toys, but their favorite was the rocket. The rocket was red and shiny, and it made a loud noise when they pushed a button. Tom and Lily pretended they were astronauts, and they flew the rocket to the moon and the stars.

One day, they saw a new boy in the house next door. His name was Max, and he had a lot of toys too. He had a bike, a ball, a train, and a rocket. But his rocket was bigger and better than Tom and Lily's rocket. It was blue and silver, and it had lights and sounds and wings. Max saw Tom and Lily playing with their rocket, and he laughed.

"Your rocket is fake!" he shouted. "It's small and old and boring. My rocket is real! It's big and new and fun. You can't play with my rocket, because you are silly and you have a fake rocket."

Tom and Lily felt sad and angry. They liked their rocket, and they didn't like Max. They wanted to show him that their rocket was not fake, and that they were not silly. They had an idea.

The next day, they waited until Max was playing with his bike in the garden. Then they sneaked into his house, and found his rocket in his room. They took his rocket, and ran back to their garden. They put his rocket next to their rocket, and pushed the button.

But nothing happened. Max's rocket did not make any noise, or any lights, or any wings. It was just a plastic toy, with a sticker that said "rocket". Tom and Lily realized that Max's rocket was fake, and that he had lied to them. They felt happy and smart. They had a real rocket, and he had a fake rocket.

They heard Max shouting from his garden. He had seen them take his rocket, and he was very angry. He ran to their garden, and tried to grab his rocket. But Tom and Lily pushed him away.

"Your rocket is fake!" they shouted. "It's big and old and boring. Our rocket is real! It's small and new and fun. You can't play with our rocket, because you are silly and you have a fake rocket."

Max felt sad and angry. He liked his rocket, and he didn't like Tom and Lily. He wanted to show them that his rocket was not fake, and that he was not silly. But he had no idea how.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a toy horse that she loved to play with. One day, while she was playing with her toy horse, it fell down and broke.

Lily was very sad and started to cry. Her mom came to her and asked what happened. Lily told her that her toy horse broke and she didn't know how to fix it.

Her mom hugged her and said, "Don't worry, I will support you. Let's fix your toy horse together." They worked together to fix the toy horse and it was as good as new.

Lily was so happy and said, "Mom, you are so graceful at fixing things!" Her mom smiled and said, "Thank you, Lily. I am happy to help you."

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved cars and always wanted to ride in an automobile. One day, Timmy's parents promised him that they would take him for a ride in an automobile. Timmy was very excited and couldn't wait to go for the ride.

The next day, Timmy's parents organized everything and they all got into the automobile. Timmy was so happy to be in the car and he looked out of the window at all the trees and houses. They drove around for a while and then stopped at a park. Timmy had so much fun playing in the park and he was very happy that his parents kept their promise.

Once upon a time, there was a friendly house. It had four walls, a roof and four windows. One day, something odd happened. The walls started to move! 

The four walls moved in all different directions. Up, down, left and right. All the furniture in the house started to mix it up too, jumbling one way and then the other. 

At first, everyone was quite scared. They didn't know what was happening. Then, a voice called out from inside one of the walls, "Don't worry! I will put everything back in order".

It was a magical house elf that lived behind the walls. He had the power to make things move and he was using it to tidy up the house. 

He sang a little song as he moved the furniture around, putting it all in different spots to make the house look nice. 

Once he was done, everyone was so happy. The house was in order and everything looked so different. They thanked the house elf, who waved goodbye as he went off to work his magic in another house.

One day, a boy named Tim found a big drum in his room. He was very happy. He wanted to play the drum all day. Tim hit the drum fast and slow. The drum made a loud sound.

Tim's sister, Sue, was not happy. She said, "Tim, please stop! The drum is too loud!" Tim sighed and stopped playing. He felt sad because he wanted to play the drum, but he did not want to make Sue upset.

Then, Tim had an idea. He asked Sue to play with him. They took turns playing the drum, hitting it slow and soft. They both had fun and were happy. The conflict was over, and they played the drum together.

Once there was a boy who was three and loved to roll in the grass. One day while he was rolling, something shiny caught his eye. He stopped and said "What's that?"

His mom smiled and said "It's a treasure, maybe it's useful."

So the boy picked it up and saw it was a shiny coin. He rolled it around in his hands and grinned. Then he asked, "What can I do with it?"

Mama said "You can do whatever you want, it's your treasure and it can be very useful!"

The little boy thought for a moment and then said, "I'll save it for when I'm bigger!"

He put his coin in a safe place and went off to play and roll in the grass.

Once upon a time, a little girl went for a walk with her grandpa. Her grandpa was very old but patient. As they strolled along, the little girl looked up in awe at the beautiful yellow and pink flowers growing in the garden. Grandpa smiled and said, "Remain patient, little one! One day those flowers will bloom."

The little girl pondered the thought, but she didn't quite understand it. "Grandpa, what do you mean by 'remain patient'?"

Grandpa smiled. "It means, little one, that things won't always happen right away. We should wait and remain patient until the right time comes."

The little girl nodded, feeling a bit wiser. She took Grandpa's hand and said, "Thank you Grandpa, I will remember to remain patient. I love you!" 

Grandpa gave her a big hug and said, "I love you too, my little one."

The moral of this story is that patience is key. Even when things may seem to take a long time, it's important to remain patient and wait for the right time to make things happen.

Once there was a mommy and a little girl. The little girl was three years old. The mommy asked her what she wanted to do.

"I want to bake something," said the little girl.

So the mommy got out all the ingredients to bake a cake. They mixed flour and sugar and eggs together in a bowl. 

"Let's add in some chocolate!" said the little girl. 

The mommy smiled. "That's a great idea!"

They put the cake in the oven and waited for it to bake. While they were waiting, the little girl asked her mommy if they could also plant something.

"What kind of plant would you like to plant?" asked the mommy.

"A rose bush!" said the little girl, with an incredible grin.

So the little girl and her mommy went outside and planted a rose bush in the garden. When the rose bush was planted, they went back inside to get their incredible cake. They ate the cake together, and it was delicious.

Once upon a time, there was a young girl named Lily. She had a cat named Mittens who was very quiet when she slept. One day, Lily went to the park and saw a young boy playing on the swings. She thought he looked nice, so she went over to him and said hello. The boy smiled and they played together.

As the sun began to set, Lily and the boy sat on a bench and watched the stars come out. The boy leaned over and gave Lily a kiss on the cheek. Lily blushed and smiled. Mittens purred quietly on Lily's lap.

From that day on, Lily and the boy played together every day. They would swing on the swings, climb on the jungle gym, and have picnics in the park. Mittens would always come along and curl up quietly next to them. And sometimes, when the boy thought no one was looking, he would give Lily a little kiss on the cheek.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. Lucy was only three years old, but she was very brave.

One morning, Lucy decided to go on an adventure. Even though she was only three, Lucy wanted to explore the world! She walked and walked until she came to a beautiful beach.

Lucy was so amazed by the beach that she wanted to reach out and touch it. She reached out her palm and, to her surprise, the water moved towards it, gently touching her skin. She felt so grateful for this wonderful moment and smiled.

The next day, Lucy returned to the beach and once again, the water reached out to her. She was so happy, she laughed and laughed!

Timmy did not like broccoli. He thought it was green and yucky. He did not want to eat it for dinner. He wanted to eat pizza or macaroni.

"Timmy, you have to eat your broccoli. It is good for you. It makes you strong and healthy," Mommy said.

"No, I don't. I hate broccoli. It is bad for me. It makes me sick and sad," Timmy said. He pushed his plate away.

Mommy was not happy. She frowned and said, "Timmy, don't be rude. You have to try it. You might like it. It is tasty and crunchy."

"No, I won't. I don't like it. It is nasty and mushy," Timmy said. He crossed his arms and pouted.

Mommy sighed and said, "Timmy, if you eat your broccoli, I will give you a treat. You can have a cookie or a popsicle."

Timmy thought for a moment. He liked cookies and popsicles. They were sweet and yummy. He looked at his plate. He saw a small piece of broccoli. He decided to eat it. He picked it up and put it in his mouth. He chewed and swallowed. He made a face and said, "Blech!"

Mommy smiled and said, "Good job, Timmy. You ate your broccoli. How was it?"

Timmy shrugged and said, "It was okay. Can I have my treat now?"

Mommy nodded and said, "Yes, you can. What do you want? A cookie or a popsicle?"

Timmy thought again. He wanted both. He said, "Can I have both?"

Mommy shook her head and said, "No, you can't. You can have one or the other. You have to choose."

Timmy did not like to choose. He wanted both. He said, "But I want both. You did not mention that I have to choose. That is not fair."

Mommy said, "Timmy, you have to choose. You can't have both. That is too much sugar. You have to share. You can have one and give the other to Daddy. He likes cookies and popsicles too."

Timmy looked at Daddy. Daddy was sitting next to him. He was wearing a tight shirt. He had a big belly. He smiled and said, "Hi, Timmy. I like cookies and popsicles too. Do you want to share with me?"

Timmy did not want to share. He wanted both. He said, "No, I don't. You have a big belly. You don't need cookies and popsicles. You need broccoli."

Daddy laughed and said, "Timmy, you are funny. You are right. I have a big belly. I need broccoli. But I also like cookies and popsicles. They are fun and delicious. Can we share?"

Timmy thought some more. He liked Daddy. He was nice and funny. He decided to share. He said, "Okay, we can share. I will have a cookie and you can have a popsicle. But you have to eat your broccoli too."

Daddy said, "Deal. I will eat my broccoli too. Thank you, Timmy. You are a good boy. You are smart and kind."

Mommy said, "Yes, you are. I am proud of you, Timmy. You ate your broccoli and you shared. You are a good boy. You are brave and generous."

Timmy felt happy. He ate his cookie and gave his popsicle to Daddy. He said, "You are welcome, Daddy. You are a good Daddy. You are strong and funny."

They all hugged and smiled. They ate their dinner and their treats. They had a good night. They loved each other. The end.

Once there was a turkey who wanted to be independent. She liked taking her walks and going on her own adventures. One day she was sitting in her favorite spot when she saw a small child nearby.

The child said, "Hello, turkey. What are you doing?"

The turkey said, "I'm just sitting here, enjoying the day."

The child smiled and said, "May I sit with you?"

The turkey smiled, too. "Yes, I'd like that," she said.

So the child sat down beside the turkey, and they talked and watched the world go by. The turkey shared her stories of being independent, and the child listened with joy.

When night time came, the child said goodbye and thanked the turkey for letting him sit with her. The turkey waved goodbye and went on her way, feeling independent and happy.

Ben likes to print pictures with his crayons. He prints cars, animals, and stars. He prints on paper, on cardboard, and sometimes on the wall. His mom does not like when he prints on the wall. She says it is messy and hard to clean.

One day, Ben finds a big red crayon in his dad's office. He thinks it is a special crayon. He wants to print with it. He sees a white sheet on his dad's desk. He thinks it is a good place to print. He does not know it is an emergency sheet. His dad needs it for his work.

Ben prints a big dragon on the emergency sheet. He prints fire, scales, and teeth. He is very happy with his picture. He thinks it is lively and cool. He does not hear his dad coming.

His dad sees the emergency sheet with the dragon. He is very angry and scared. He yells at Ben. He says he ruined his work. He says he has to call someone right away. He says it is a big problem.

Ben is very sad and sorry. He does not understand why his dad is so mad. He does not know what an emergency is. He just wanted to print a dragon. He starts to cry. He wishes he did not print on the emergency sheet. He wishes he printed on paper instead.

Once upon a time there was a family with two kids, a brother and a sister. The brother was very jealous because his sister always wanted to be the only one who could play upstairs. So one day the brother went upstairs to join his sister in the playroom.

The sister was very scared and said to her brother, "You can't come up here! It's only for me!"

The brother frowned and said, "Why can't I come up here? We are both kids and we can have fun together!"

The sister thought for a moment and then smiled. She said to her brother, "OK, you can come up here. We can play together. We don't have to be jealous of each other."

The brother smiled too and they went upstairs to play together.

The moral of this story is that we should not be jealous and should always try to be kind to our siblings.

Sam and his mom went to a hotel for a holiday. They had a big room with a bed, a sofa, a TV and a window. Sam liked the window because he could see the cars and the people on the street.

One morning, Sam's mom said, "Let's go to the breakfast room and have some food. Are you hungry, Sam?"

"Yes, mom, I am hungry. Can I have some cereal and milk?" Sam asked.

"Sure, you can. Come on, let's go." Mom said. She took Sam's hand and they walked to the elevator. The elevator went down and made a ding sound.

They reached the breakfast room and saw many tables and chairs. There were also many plates and bowls with different kinds of food. Sam saw some cereal and milk and pointed to them.

"Mom, can I have some of that?" He said.

"Of course, you can. Here, let me help you." Mom said. She took a bowl and a spoon and filled the bowl with cereal and milk. She gave it to Sam and said, "Be careful, it might be hot. You have to stir it with your spoon first."

Sam took the spoon and stirred the cereal and milk. He saw the milk turn brown and the cereal become soft. He tasted it and smiled.

"Mmm, this is good. Thank you, mom." He said.

"You're welcome, Sam. I'm glad you like it." Mom said. She also took a bowl and some food for herself. They ate and talked and enjoyed their breakfast.

Sam thought that this was not an ordinary day. This was a special day. He was happy to be with his mom in the hotel. He wondered what they would do next. He hoped they would have more fun.

Once upon a time, there was a selfish king. He lived in a magnificent castle with lots of his servants.

Every morning he would get up and dress himself in his finest clothes. He loved to show everyone how rich and important he was.

The king was very mean to his servants. He made them do all the work and never said 'thank you'.

One day, a fairy appeared to the king. She said that he was being too selfish and had to change his ways.

The king listened to the fairy and started being kind to his servants. He shared his food with them and thanked them for all their hard work.

The king was very happy when he saw how much better his kingdom was because of his kindness. From then on, he was always sure to dress in his finest clothes, but also act with kindness and generosity.

Once upon a time, a lonely ghost lived in a big house. The ghost was sad because no one wanted to be his friend. He wanted to play with the kids who lived near his house, but they were all scared of him. The lonely ghost felt very sad.

One day, the lonely ghost had an idea. He decided to spread love and happiness to the kids. He thought that maybe they would not be scared of him if he did nice things for them. So, the ghost started to help the kids. He found lost toys and brought them back. He made pretty flowers grow in their gardens.

Soon, the kids noticed the nice things the ghost was doing. They were not scared anymore. They wanted to find the ghost and say thank you. When they found the lonely ghost, they all became friends. They played games and had fun together. The ghost was not lonely anymore, and they all lived happily ever after.

Tom and Sue were friends. They liked to play with toys and books. One day, they found a big jar of coins in Tom's house. They wanted to buy more toys and books with the coins.

They took the jar and went to the shop. They saw many things they liked. They gave the coins to the shop man and took the things. They did not count the coins. They did not ask for change. They were happy.

But when they came back to Tom's house, they saw Tom's dad. He was angry. He said, "Where is my jar of coins? I was saving them for a long time. They were very important to me. You took them without asking. You spend them all on foolish things. You are very naughty. You have to give them back."

Tom and Sue were scared. They said, "We are sorry. We did not know. We thought they were for us. We do not have the coins. We have the things. We can give you the things."

But Tom's dad said, "The things are not worth the coins. The coins were more than the things. You made a big mistake. You have to work hard to earn the coins back. You have to return the things to the shop. You have to say sorry to the shop man. You have to learn to be careful and honest. You have to be good friends."

Tom and Sue were sad. They had to do what Tom's dad said. They had to work hard and say sorry. They had to give back the things they liked. They had to lose the coins they found. They had a bad ending. They wished they had not been foolish.

Mommy was getting ready for dinner. She carefully put her clothes on and combed her hair. She said, "Come little one, let's go decorate the upstairs for dinner." Little Jenny was very excited. She hopped off the floor and ran upstairs.

When Jenny got to the top of the stairs she saw many heavy boxes of decorations. She grabbed one and tried to carry it down the stairs. It was very heavy! She tried her best, but she couldn't make it. She started to cry.

Mommy came up. She asked, "What happened, Jenny?" Jenny said, "This box is too heavy! I can't carry it!" Mommy said, "Oh, I see. That was a bad idea. Let me help you."

They both tried to carry the box down the stairs. This time it was too much for them and the box slipped. It tumbled down the stairs and broke into many pieces. Jenny was scared and Mommy was sad. They couldn't decorate the upstairs now.

Once upon a time, there was a farmer named Jack. Jack had a big sack. He put all his crops in the sack and took it to the market. He hoped to sell his crops and be successful.

On the way to the market, Jack saw a river. He was thirsty and wanted some water. He filled his cup with water from the river and drank it. The water was cold and refreshing.

At the market, Jack opened his sack and showed his crops to the people. They liked his crops and bought them all. Jack was very happy because he was successful. He packed his empty sack and went back home.

John was very excited to visit the zoo with his family. He had been looking forward to this all week and he couldn't wait to see all the animals. As he explored the zoo, he was especially drawn to the alligators. 

John was very curious and he didn't understand why the alligators were hanging from a tree. He asked his mom why and she tried to explain that the alligators were really just hanging from a branch, but John was too young to understand. 

Despite his mom's warnings, John just had to get close to one of the alligators. He was so ignorant and he thought the alligator was a toy. He reached up and grabbed the alligator by its tail and the alligator turned around and snapped at him, just as his mom had warned. 

John backed away in a fright and ran to his mom. His mom was so proud of him for being brave enough to explore the zoo and learn more about the fascinating alligators, even if he had been a bit ignorant and gone too close.

Lily and Tom were playing in the snow. They made a big snowman with a hat and a scarf. They gave him a carrot nose and two coal eyes. They named him Frosty.

"Hello, Frosty!" Lily said. "You are our friend. We will play with you every day."

"Yes, we will," Tom said. "But we have to be careful. The sun is very bright. It can make you melt."

Frosty smiled. He liked Lily and Tom. They were very kind. But he was also scared. He did not want to melt. He wanted to stay with them.

One day, the sun was very hot. Lily and Tom went inside to have lunch. Frosty felt very warm. He saw a big puddle under his feet. He was melting!

"Oh no!" Frosty said. "I have to escape. I have to find a cold place."

He looked around. He saw a sled near the fence. He had an idea. He jumped on the sled and pushed it with his feet. The sled started to move. It went down the hill. It went very fast. It made a zoom sound.

"Zoom, zoom, zoom!" Frosty said. "This is fun. But where am I going?"

He saw a big lake at the bottom of the hill. The lake was icy. It was frozen. Frosty was happy. He thought he would be safe there.

But he was wrong. The ice was thin. It could not hold his weight. When he reached the lake, the ice cracked. Frosty fell into the water. He felt very cold. He felt very wet. He felt very sad.

"Help, help, help!" Frosty said. "I made a mistake. I want to go back. I want to see Lily and Tom."

But no one heard him. No one saw him. He sank into the water. He disappeared.

Lily and Tom came back from lunch. They looked for Frosty. They saw the sled near the lake. They saw the hole in the ice. They knew what happened.

"Oh no!" Lily said. "Frosty is gone. He escaped. He melted."

"That's so sad," Tom said. "We loved him. He was our friend."

They hugged each other. They cried. They learned a lesson. They learned that sometimes it is better to stay where you are. They learned that sometimes escaping is not the answer. They learned that sometimes you lose what you love.

Anna and Ben liked to play with their toys in the yard. They had many cars, dolls, balls and blocks. Sometimes they shared their toys with their neighbor, Lily, who was very polite and nice. Lily always said please and thank you, and helped them clean up after playing.

One day, Anna and Ben were having a tea party with their dolls. They set up a table and chairs, and poured pretend tea in cups. They invited Lily to join them, and she brought her own doll. They had a lot of fun, pretending to chat and sip tea.

But then, they heard a loud noise. It was Max, the big dog from across the street. Max liked to chase cats, birds and squirrels. He also liked to knock over trash cans, dig holes and bark at people. He was not very polite or nice.

Max saw the tea party, and thought it looked like fun. He ran towards the table, wagging his tail and barking. He jumped on the table, and scattered the cups, plates and dolls. He grabbed one of the dolls in his mouth, and ran away.

Anna, Ben and Lily were very scared and sad. They cried and shouted at Max, but he did not listen. He ran back to his yard, and buried the doll in a hole. He thought he was very clever and funny.

Anna, Ben and Lily went to tell their moms what happened. Their moms were very sorry and angry. They went to talk to Max's owner, and asked him to control his dog. They also asked him to give back the doll, and to pay for the broken cups and plates.

Max's owner was not very polite or nice, either. He said it was not his fault, and that the kids should not leave their toys in the yard. He said he did not know where the doll was, and that he would not pay for anything.

The moms did not like his answer. They said they would call the police, and report his dog. They also said they would not let their kids play with him or his dog anymore.

Anna, Ben and Lily learned a lesson that day. They learned that some people and animals are not very polite or nice, and that they should be careful with their toys. They also learned that they had good moms, who loved them and protected them. They hugged their moms, and thanked them. They also hugged each other, and said they were sorry for losing the doll. They decided to make a new tea party, with new cups and plates, and a new doll. They invited Lily to join them, and they had a lot of fun. They also made sure to keep an eye on Max, and to stay away from him.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play hockey with his friends at the park. One day, Timmy and his friends found an ancient hockey stick in the bushes. They were so excited to use it!

Timmy's friend, Billy, said, "Let's examine the stick! It looks really old."

Timmy and his friends examined the stick closely. They saw that it had some scratches and was a bit rusty. But they were still excited to use it for their game.

During the game, Timmy scored the winning goal with the ancient hockey stick. His friends cheered and clapped for him. Timmy was so happy that he found the stick and that it helped him win the game.

From that day on, Timmy and his friends always used the ancient hockey stick for their games. They knew it was special and brought them good luck.

Once upon a time there were two best friends, Dan and Lou. Every day, Dan and Lou would play together in the park. Each day Dan would bring a toy rocket along with him.

One day, when they were playing in the park, Lou looked at the rocket and said: "I wish I had a rocket". Dan, who was very kind, said: "Don't worry, you can have mine!" He gave Lou his rocket and said: "You can keep it!"

One week later, both Dan and Lou went back to park to play another time. When they got there, Dan remembered his rocket and asked: "Where is my rocket?" Lou answered: "I have it", but he refused to give it back. He said: "I'm not giving it back".

Dan felt very sad and disappointed, but he had to accept that his rocket was gone. From that day, Dan remembered to always be kind, but to never be too trusting to his friends.

Once upon a time, there was a ladybug called Bob. Bob was always looking for useful things to do.

One day, Bob was walking around when he heard an odd sound. It was coming from a nearby then. He crept closer to investigate and saw a tiny caterpillar getting into trouble inside the then. "Help!" yelled the caterpillar.

Bob jumped into action. He carefully climbed into the then and then pinched the side of the then with his legs. It split open and the caterpillar crawled out to safety.

Once upon a time there was a little duck called Tom. Tom wanted to have an adventure and explore the world outside his pond. One day, Tom made an organized plan - he wanted to build a sail and go for a travel. He gathered all the materials he needed and soon he had the most beautiful sail ever made.

Tom was so excited that he couldn't wait to leave. He sailed far away and didn't look back.

As he sailed, he saw many interesting creatures and exciting locations. He felt so safe and protected travelling by sea. 

After a few days, a terrible storm hit the ocean and Tom's sail was no longer safe. He tried to protect it with all his might but it was no match for the storm. 

The sail broke to pieces and Tom was thrown into the sea. He tried to swim back to the shore but he was too exhausted and eventually sunk under the water and was never seen again.

One day, Oliver went to the backyard with his mom. He saw a big hole in the ground. His mom said, "We need to bury this here". He didn't know what it meant.

Oliver watched as his mom put the big thing into the hole. Then she started to fill it with dirt. He asked, "What is it, mommy?"

She said, "It's an old chimney. We have to take it out so we can build a new one." She looked frustrated.

The next day, when Oliver went back to the backyard, the big hole was gone. He said, "Mommy, I can't find the chimney!"

His mom smiled and said, "We buried it!"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to count. She could count up to ten all by herself. One day, Lily went to the park with her mom. They saw a tall tree and Lily said, "I want to stand under the tree." Her mom said, "Okay, but be careful not to climb it."

Lily stood under the tree and counted the leaves. Suddenly, she saw a bird fall from the sky and land on the ground. She ran to her mom and said, "Mommy, the bird is dead!" Her mom said, "Let's go see if we can help it." They went to the bird and saw that it was not moving. 

Lily's mom explained to her that sometimes animals get hurt and can't be helped. Lily said, "I will count the leaves on the tree for the bird." She counted all the leaves and said, "I hope the bird can be happy in heaven." Her mom smiled and said, "That was very kind of you, Lily."

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy liked to go for walks in the forest with his mommy. One day, they found a trail that they had never seen before. It looked scary, but Timmy wanted to explore it.

As they walked down the trail, they saw a big, scary monster. Timmy tried to kick the monster, but it didn't work. The monster chased them all the way back to their house. Timmy and his mommy were very scared.

From that day on, they never went back to that scary trail again. They stayed safe at home and played with their toys. Timmy learned that sometimes it's better to stay away from scary things.

Once there was a little girl and her name was Sue. Sue had a special shoulder blanket that she always kept clean. It was her very favorite thing in the world. 

One day, Sue rode her bike to the park. She had her shoulder blanket with her. When she went down the slides, the blanket got caught and it started to tear! Sue felt so sad and upset.

She sadly watched the tears in the blanket grow bigger and bigger. In the end, the blanket was too tattered to fix. But sue still hugged it tight to her shoulder and remembered all the happy times she had with her blanket before it was torn 

Sue decided to mend the blanket the best she could and hang it up in her room. That way she could always remember how special it was and that it kept her shoulder safe and clean.

Anna and Ben like to play with blocks. They build towers and bridges and houses with the blocks. They have many colors of blocks: red, blue, yellow, green and more.

One day, they find a new block in their toy box. It is white and shiny and has a button on it. Anna and Ben are curious. They wonder what the button does.

"Let me push it!" Anna says. She grabs the block and presses the button.

"Snap!" The block makes a loud noise and splits into two pieces. A small object falls out of the block. It is round and silver and has a hole in it.

"What is this?" Ben asks. He picks up the object and looks at it.

"I don't know," Anna says. "Maybe it is a coin. Maybe we can buy something with it."

"Or maybe it is a ring. Maybe we can wear it," Ben says. He tries to put the object on his finger, but it is too small.

"Ow!" Ben says. He pulls the object off his finger. It hurts. The object is very strong and hard.

"Let me see," Anna says. She takes the object from Ben and tries to bend it. She uses all her strength, but the object does not bend.

"Wow!" Anna says. "This object is stronger than us. How did it come out of the block?"

"I don't know," Ben says. "Maybe the block is magic. Maybe it has more objects inside."

They look at the two pieces of the block. They see more buttons on them.

"Should we push them?" Anna asks.

"I don't know," Ben says. "Maybe we should. Maybe we shouldn't."

They look at each other. They are scared and excited. They wonder what will happen if they push the buttons.

Once upon a time, there was a little fish named Nemo. Nemo loved to swim in the big blue ocean. One day, he met a friendly turtle named Timmy.

"Hi Nemo!" said Timmy. "Do you want to go for a jog with me?"

Nemo didn't know what a jog was, but he wanted to be friends with Timmy. "Sure!" he said.

Timmy and Nemo swam together through the ocean. Nemo noticed that Timmy was very calm and relaxed. "Why are you so calm?" asked Nemo.

"I like to take things slow," said Timmy. "It helps me enjoy life."

Nemo thought about this and realized that he was always in a hurry. He decided to try being more calm like Timmy. From that day on, Nemo and Timmy were the best of friends and they swam together every day.

Once upon a time, there were two powerful animals who lived in the safari. One was a lion and the other was a zebra. The lion asked the zebra if he wanted to marry him. The zebra was surprised and replied "But we do not look the same!"

The lion thought for a moment, then smiled. He said, "That's okay! We can still be married if we love each other." The zebra smiled too, and said yes.

On the day of the wedding, all the animals in the safari raced to the lion's house. All the animals were happy and cheered. After the ceremony, the animals danced and had a great time.

The next day, the lion and the zebra began their life together. They had lots of adventures together, and their love was very powerful. Everyone in the safari was very happy for them.

Once upon a time, there was a generous man. His name was Joe and he loved to give people prizes. One day, he was thinking about what to do for the children in town. He decided to enter them in a contest. Everyone was so excited when they heard about it. 

The contest was easy. All they had to do was draw a picture with their best colors. Joe knew the children would love it.

On the day of the contest, the children gathered around Joe. He gave out prizes to each and every one of them. Some got toys, others got sweets. Everyone was so happy to receive a prize from Joe. 

The winners of the contest went away feeling extra special. Joe was so generous to them and they were very grateful. From then on, Joe would enter the children in a contest often and they would always have lots of fun.

Once upon a time, there was a big lion. He had a golden mane and strong paws. He lived in a jungle with his friends, the monkeys and the birds. One day, the lion saw a shiny silver ball in the grass. He picked it up and played with it. The ball was so pretty and fair. The lion was happy.

Suddenly, the lion heard a loud roar. It was coming from the other side of the jungle. The lion got scared and ran to his friends. They all huddled together and waited for the roar to stop. After a while, the lion realized that it was just his friend, the tiger, who was practicing his roar. The lion laughed and they all played together with the silver ball. They had a fair and fun day in the jungle. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved the color purple. One day, she fell down and hurt her knee. Her mommy said, "We need to go see the doctor so he can help make it feel better."

Lily was scared to go see the doctor, but her mommy held her hand and said, "Don't worry, the doctor will be nice and help you feel better." When they got to the doctor's office, there were lots of toys to play with in the waiting room. Lily loved playing with the blocks and dolls.

When it was finally their turn to see the doctor, he was wearing a white coat and had a stethoscope around his neck. He asked Lily what happened and she told him about her hurt knee. The doctor checked her knee and said, "It's just a little scrape, but we need to clean it and put a purple bandage on it to make it feel better."

Lily was so happy to have a purple bandage on her knee. She said, "Thank you, doctor!" and her mommy said, "We're so lucky to have such a nice doctor to help us." The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a favorite cup that she always drank from. One day, Lily's mom put the cup in the cupboard and the little girl couldn't reach it.

Lily said to her mom, "Mommy, can you get my cup out of the cupboard? I want to drink from it."

Her mom smiled and got the cup from the cupboard. Lily was happy and drank from her favorite cup. From that day on, Lily knew that she could always trust her mommy.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny named Benny. Benny loved to play outside during the day, but he was always scared of the dark night. One evening, Benny was playing with his friends when he saw a big, nosy bird perched on a tree branch. The bird was staring at him and making him feel uneasy.

Benny decided to go back home before it got too dark. As he hopped along, he saw a shadowy figure standing in the distance. He couldn't see who or what it was, but he knew it wasn't friendly. Benny started to feel scared and wished he had stayed with his friends.

Suddenly, the big, nosy bird swooped down and started to attack Benny. Benny tried to run, but he stumbled and fell. Just as the bird was about to grab him, a bright light shone from behind the shadowy figure. It was Benny's mom, who had been looking for him. The light scared the bird away, and Benny was safe. From that day on, Benny learned to never be afraid of the night because he knew his mom would always stand by his side.

Once upon a time there was a cheerful skeleton. He lived in a big house and every day he would pretend. He had many fun things to pretend. 

One day he pretended he was a chef and cooked an imaginary meal. It was so good he pretended to eat it! Another time he pretended to be a pirate and sailed the big ocean. He had a fishing rod and a big hat. 

He also pretended to take care of animals. He gave them food, cleaned up after them and cuddled them. He felt very happy when he pretended to take care of them.

The cheerful skeleton was very busy as he had lots of things to pretend every day. But, he was very happy and always had a lot of fun. And he always ended his days feeling very content.

Once upon a time there was a mirror. The mirror was shiny and round. It was very pretty.

One day, a little boy came along. He was very polite. He said please and thank you. He liked the mirror and wanted to cover it.

The little boy carefully covered the mirror with a big blanket. It looked like a house. He was so happy.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Anna. She was so amazing and every day she would play in her garden. One day she saw something shiny in the water from her garden sink. She thought it would really nice to take it home with her. 

Anna put the shiny thing in her pocket and rushed inside to show her mom. But when she arrived she regreted her decision. She had just taken the sink plug! 

Her mom said, "You must learn that you can't always think of yourself. You have to think of others too!" Anna said sorry and put the plug back in the sink.

The next day, Anna looked in the sink and to her amazement, it was filled with beautiful flowers! The sink was no longer a sink but a garden and it was so amazing! 

From that day forward, Anna always thought of others before herself. She never regretted a single decision again.

Once upon a time, there was a wise cat named Tom. Tom loved to sing songs. One day, he found a microphone in the park. He was very happy and carried it home.

Tom decided to sing with his new microphone. He sang loud and clear. All the other animals in the park came to listen. They danced and clapped as Tom sang.

After a while, Tom got tired. He shut his eyes and rested. The other animals went home too. They all knew that Tom was a wise cat who could sing beautiful songs with his special microphone.

Ben and Lily were playing in the park with their mom. They liked to slide, swing and run. They saw a big van with many colors and pictures. The van had a sign that said "Ice Cream".

"Mom, can we have ice cream?" Ben asked.

"Sure, let's go see what they have," mom said.

They walked to the van and saw a man with a hat and a smile. He opened a window and said "Hello, what can I get you?"

"I want chocolate," Ben said.

"I want strawberry," Lily said.

"Okay, here you go," the man said. He gave them two cones with ice cream.

"Thank you," Ben and Lily said.

They paid the man and walked away. They licked their ice cream and smiled. It was sweet and cold.

But then, a big wind came and blew their hats away. It was very cold. Ben and Lily shivered.

"Mom, we are cold," they said.

"Let's go back to the car," mom said. "We can warm up there."

They ran to the car and entered. Mom turned on the heater and gave them blankets. They cuddled and ate their ice cream.

They were happy and warm.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Katrina. She was playing with her toys when she saw something unusual.
