Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a charming dress that she loved to wear. One day, Lily's mom asked her to help mix the batter for a cake. Lily was so excited to help, she mixed and mixed until the batter was perfect. 

After they put the cake in the fridge to cool, Lily went outside to play. While she was playing, her little brother came into the kitchen and tried to take a bite of the cake. But he accidentally knocked the cake onto the floor and it was ruined. 

When Lily came back inside, she saw the mess and started to cry. Her mom tried to comfort her, but Lily was so upset that she didn't want to listen. She ran to her room and didn't come out for a long time. 

The bad ending was that Lily didn't get to eat the cake she helped make, and she was sad for the rest of the day. But her mom promised they would make another cake together soon, and Lily felt a little bit better.

Molly and her dad were walking down the street. As they went, a funny billboard caught Mollyâ€™s eye. It showed a silly picture and said â€œLift with Care.â€ Molly asked her dad what it meant.

Dad smiled and said the billboard wanted people to be careful when they lift things. He asked Molly if she wanted to do some lifting with him. She jumped and said yes!

Dad and Molly went to the park. Dad grabbed a big stick and asked Molly to help him lift it. With a little help from Dad, she picked it up. Molly was so proud she was lifting things!

Dad gave her a big hug. They picked up leaves and twigs and then put them in the big trash can. Dad said Molly was a good helper.

Molly and Dad went home, tired but happy. Molly was so proud she lifted something all by herself!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy called Jack. Every night, Jack would watch the sun go down in the horizon, and he loved to see the pretty colours in the sky.

One night, Jack wanted to see the sunset from a different place, so he flagged down a taxi. The taxi driver was a kind old man and he agreed to take Jack to a special spot.

When they arrived, the skyline was so beautiful. But the taxi was too close to the edge of the river and the water looked so deep. The taxi driver asked Jack to get out of the car, but Jack refused to yield. 

The driver kept asking, but Jack was stubborn and he wouldn't move. Finally, the driver said, "Jack, you must always listen to the adults that are trying to help you, because they are always right." 

These wise words finally made Jack yield and he got out of the taxi. He realised how dangerous the situation could have been and thanked the taxi driver.

Moral of the story: Always listen to adults when they are trying to help.

Once upon a time, there was a small girl named Grace. Grace had just turned 3 and was very excited to learn new things.

Her mummy and daddy took her to the doctor. The doctor asked Grace to do an exam, so she could learn if she was healthy. Grace was brave, so she agreed to do the exam.

During the exam, Grace had to be gentle and delicate. She was careful not to hurt herself.

When the exam was finished, the doctor asked Grace what she would like as a reward. Grace thought for a moment and then made a request: she asked for a fluffy toy cat. The doctor smiled and gave her the toy she requested.

Grace was very proud that she listened and was gentle during the exam. She was happy to take home her new toy as a reward for a job well done!

One day, a little girl went out to explore the woods. She was wearing her favourite red shoes, with a small heel. Suddenly she felt the ground begin to tremble beneath her feet. She looked up and saw a huge animal around the corner. She gasped and backed away. 

The little girl looked closely at the animal. It was a bear! She said out loud in surprise, "Oh no!"

The bear saw the little girl and let out a big, deep roar. The little girl trembled with fear. She was so scared that she couldn't even move from her spot. 

Just then, the bear started walking away. He didn't seem like he wanted to hurt her. The little girl let out a huge sigh, relieved that the bear had gone away. 

After the bear had left, the little girl made a promise to herself that she would explore the woods again - but this time, with an adult.

Tim and Lily are playing in the park. They see a furry deer in the grass. The deer has big ears and a brown nose. Tim and Lily want to get closer to the deer.

"Look, Lily, a deer!" Tim says. "Let's go and say hello."

"OK, Tim, but be quiet. We don't want to scare the deer," Lily says.

They walk slowly and softly to the deer. The deer looks at them with big eyes. Tim and Lily smile and wave.

"Hello, deer. You are so furry and pretty. Can we pet you?" Tim asks.

The deer nods and lowers its head. Tim and Lily touch the deer's fur gently. It feels soft and warm. The deer makes a soft sound.

"I think the deer likes us, Lily. It is very friendly," Tim says.

"Yes, Tim, it is. The deer is our new friend," Lily says.

They hug the deer and the deer hugs them back. They are very happy. They play with the deer until it is time to go home. They say goodbye to the deer and thank it for being nice. The deer waves back and runs away. Tim and Lily hope to see the deer again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a shiny box that she loved to play with. One day, she took her box to the park and showed it to her friend, Tommy.

Tommy was glad to see the box and asked Lily if he could play with it. But Lily said no because she didn't want anyone else to touch her special box. This made Tommy sad, and he walked away.

Later that day, Lily went home and put her box on her dresser. She went to bed and fell asleep. In the middle of the night, she woke up to a loud noise. She saw that her box was gone! She was so sad and didn't know what to do.

The next day, Lily went back to the park and saw Tommy playing with her box. She was so glad to see it again! Tommy had found the box on the ground and had taken it home to keep it safe. Lily thanked Tommy and they played together happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a peaceful farm. On this farm, there was a big red barn. Inside the barn, many animals lived. They were all very happy.

One sunny day, a little duck walked to the barn. The duck wanted to meet new friends. The duck saw a cow, a pig, and a chicken. The duck said "hello" to all of them.

The cow, the pig, and the chicken were happy to meet the duck. They played games and had fun. The duck was happy too. Now, they were all friends in the big red barn. And they lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in her backyard. One day, she found a new toy. It was a long stick that she could use to measure things. 

Lily's mom saw her playing with the stick and said, "That's a nice rod, Lily. You can use it to measure how tall the flowers are." 

Lily was excited to try it out. She went over to the flowers and held the rod up to them. "Wow!" she exclaimed. "These flowers are taller than I thought!" 

Later that day, Lily's dad came home from work. He saw Lily measuring things with her new rod and said, "That's a great tool, Lily. You can use it to measure how much you've grown." 

Lily was curious. She held the rod up to herself and saw that she had grown a little bit since the last time she measured. She was so happy and proud of herself. From that day on, Lily used her new rod to measure everything she could find.

Once upon a time, there was a thin tower. It was very tall and stood all alone in the middle of a big field. Then, one day, a little girl came and started to shake the tower. She shook and shook until, suddenly, the tower came tumbling down. The little girl was so happy. She laughed and ran around and around the fallen tower. She had so much fun with it that she stayed and played until it was dark. Then she said goodbye to the tower and went back home.

Once upon a time there was a mom and her daughter. The daughter was very young, only three years old. She loved to play outside in the sun.

One day she asked her mom if she could stay out a little longer. Her mom said she could, as long as she was careful. So the little girl ran to the nearby park and started to have fun.

However, as she went to play with a toy, she saw something beautiful. It was a whip! She had never seen such a beautiful thing before. She wanted to take a closer look and started to walk carefully towards it.

But suddenly, her mom called her back. The little girl was so sad and gave the whip one last sigh before going back home. She knew she could not take it with her. 

So she ran back home and to her mom's side, saying goodbye to the beautiful whip.

One day, there was a special kind of girl. She was very curious about the world. Every day she asked lots of questions and explored the day with a sense of wonder.

One night, when she was tucked into bed, the girl heard a loud noise. She began to cry because she was scared. But then she remembered her mum and dad were there. She told them how scared she was and they gave her a hug. They told her she was safe and then they all hugged.

The girl felt better and she said sorry for being scared. Her parents smiled and said it was okay. They said they understood and they were happy she knew to talk to them. The girl hugged them again, thankful they had forgiven her. 

The girl was so happy that she hugged them every day from then on. And she promised to be more curious with her wonders and questions, instead of being scared.

Once upon a time there was a young fox. He had two big ears and a bushy tail. He loved to run and play in the sun. The sun made his fur shine and sparkle.

One day, he heard music coming from a nearby meadow. He ran to it and saw that there was a picnic happening. Everyone was happy and singing to the music.

The young fox was drawn to the music, and started to dance in the sunshine. He jumped and twirled around, sending his fur flying. Everyone clapped and laughed, enjoying the show.

The young fox was so happy that he twirled and danced even faster. The sun made his fur shine like a million stars. He was much happier than he'd ever been.

When the music stopped, everyone said good bye to the young fox. He waved goodbye, smiling as he watched them go. Then he turned and ran off into the bright sunshine, still feeling its warm energetic rays, his fur still shining brightly.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she went to a big stadium with her mommy and daddy to watch a soccer game. Lily was very nervous because she had never been to a stadium before.

As they were watching the game, Lily noticed a man sitting in front of them who was being very loud and rude. He was shouting and throwing things on the field. Lily's mommy and daddy told her that it's not nice to behave like that and that it's important to be respectful of others.

After a while, the man was removed from the stadium by security because of his bad behavior. Lily asked her mommy and daddy why the man had to leave. They explained to her that it's important to be kind and respectful to others, and that if we don't behave nicely, we might have to leave too.

Lily learned an important lesson that day. She realized that it's important to be kind to others and to always behave nicely. She knew that if she did that, she would always be welcome in the stadium and in other places too.

One day, Little Tommy wanted to go for a walk. He asked his mom for permission, and she said yes. So, he put on his shoes and walked out the door.

He took a path that he hadn't taken before and before long, he found a small clearing in the woods. On one of the trees in the clearing was a shiny knife. It looked very attractive to Tommy.

He walked over and picked it up carefully. Then, he heard his mom calling his name. "Tommy!" she said. "Come back!"

Tommy began to walk back the way he had come. When he got home, he showed his mom the knife. She sighed and said, "Oh, Tommy, be careful with sharp things like that."

Tommy nodded and put the knife away. From then on, every morning he went for a walk in the woods, but he never took the same path twice.

Minta was playing in her backyard when she heard a loud snap. She stopped and listened, but all she heard was birds chirping. She looked around but didn't see anything out of the ordinary. She continued to play and then she heard the loud snap again. 

Suddenly, there was a low grumble and a huge wake came from behind her. She turned around and saw a big, monster like dog. Minta ran and hid behind a bush near the fence. The careless dog was drooling and coming closer. 

"Who's there?â€ Minta asked in a shaky voice. She was too scared to move.

The dog did not answer and came closer. Minta was so scared that she started to cry. 

â€œIt's ok, little one,â€ said a gentle voice coming from the house. Minta saw her neighbor walking with a leash. â€œCome here, boy.â€ 

Minta watched in relief as the dog was gently led away. She thanked her neighbor before running back inside. From that day on, Minta was much more careful when playing in the backyard.

Once upon a time there was a fox who felt very miserable. It wanted to find a place to belong, but it had nowhere to go.

The fox asked around, hoping someone could help him. First, he asked a rabbit, but the rabbit said, "Sorry, I can't help you."

So the little fox kept looking. Eventually, he found a wise bird and asked, "Will you help me find a place to belong?"

The bird looked at the fox and said, "Yes, of course. I know a place. Follow me."

The fox and the bird flew for a long time. Finally, they reached the fox's new home. The fox was so excited to find a place he belonged. He thanked the bird and ran into the woods.

The fox was so happy to finally have a place to belong. He was never miserable again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Lucy. She was very thoughtful and never forgot to say her thank-yous.

One day she was walking down the street and she stopped to say thank-you to the birds tweeting in the trees. She said, "Thank-you birds, you make the street so nice". 

Just then, a kind old lady stopped to talk to Lucy. She said, "Good morning Lucy. It's very thoughtful of you to be thanking the birds". 

Lucy smiled and said, "Yes, I like to thank everyone for being nice to me". 

The kind old lady gave her a hug and said, "You are a very special girl". Lucy thanked the kind old lady for her hug and waved goodbye as she walked off down the street. 

And from that day onwards, whenever Lucy went for a walk, she always remembered to thank the birds for making the street so nice.

Once upon a time, there was a young girl named Emily. She liked to dance and jump around, especially when she was feeling happy. One day, Emily stumbled across a gray memory. She wasn't quite sure what it was, but it made her curious. 

"What's that?" Emily said as she pointed to the gray memory. 

Her mom came over and said, "These are memories, darling. They are special moments that we can keep forever." Emily nodded, understanding.

That evening, Emily decided to make the gray memory her own. She danced around it, swirling in circles and stomping her feet. She was so happy to have her very own memory. Emily joyfully spun around and around until the night sky began to come alive with stars. 

As the stars shined, Emily felt as if the gray memory had come to life. She knew then that she would always remember that special moment and she would always be able to choose to dance and be happy.

One day, Maggie the whale was feeling very grumpy. She rolled around in the water, sighing and grumbling, wondering why she couldn't be happy. 

The water around her suddenly grew very calm. From the depths of the sea, a little voice called out, "What's wrong?" 

Maggie looked down to see a tiny fish gazing up at her. She gave a deep sigh and said, "I'm grumpy. I just don't feel happy." 

The fish swam a little closer and said, "Let's go roll around together. That always makes me feel better!" 

Maggie smiled and the two of them started to roll around in the water. After a few minutes of playing, Maggie really did start to feel more cheerful. She thanked the fish and said goodbye before swimming away, no longer grumpy.

Lila and Ben were making a cake with Mom. They had to stir the flour, the eggs, the sugar and the butter in a big bowl. Lila liked to stir fast and make bubbles. Ben liked to stir slow and make swirls. Mom said they were both good helpers.

When they were done stirring, Mom poured the batter into a pan and put it in the oven. She told Lila and Ben to wait for the cake to bake. They could smell the cake and it made them hungry. They decided to play with their toys in the living room.

Lila found her doll and Ben found his truck. They pretended to have a tea party with the doll and the truck. They used cups and plates from their toy kitchen. They poured water and pretended it was tea. They said "cheers" and clinked their cups.

But then they heard a funny noise. It was a chirping sound, like a bird. They looked around and saw a cricket on the floor. It was green and shiny and had long legs. It jumped and chirped and made them laugh.

"Look, a cricket!" Lila said. "Let's catch it!"

"OK!" Ben said. "But be gentle!"

They put down their cups and plates and chased the cricket. They tried to catch it with their hands, but it was too fast. They tried to catch it with a net, but it was too smart. They tried to catch it with a jar, but it was too sneaky.

The cricket led them all over the living room, under the couch, behind the curtains, on the bookshelf. Lila and Ben had fun, but they also got tired. They ran and jumped and crawled and giggled, but they also yawned and rubbed their eyes.

Finally, the cricket stopped on the windowsill. It looked at them and chirped one last time. Then it flew away through the open window. Lila and Ben waved goodbye to the cricket. They were happy they had met it, but they were also sleepy.

They went back to their tea party and sat on the floor. They picked up their cups and plates and pretended to eat the cake. They said "yum" and "delicious" and "thank you". But they also closed their eyes and nodded their heads.

Mom came into the living room and saw them. She smiled and said "The cake is ready! Who wants a slice?"

But Lila and Ben did not answer. They were asleep on the floor, with their doll and their truck, their cups and their plates, and their dreams of the cricket. Mom covered them with a blanket and kissed them. She said "Sweet dreams, my little helpers. You can have the cake tomorrow."

One day, Bob decided to go outside and examine the lake. He was only three years old, but he was very wise. 

When Bob arrived at the lake, he saw a big fish swimming in the water. He excitedly said, â€œHello fish! What are you doing?â€ 

The wise fish replied, â€œI am swimming around the lake, looking for food and exploring. Would you like to join me?â€ 

Bob smiled and said, â€œYes, I would love to join you!â€ 

So, Bob and the wise fish swam around the lake together, examining the beauty of the lake and all the things living in it. They had a lot of fun exploring and Bob learned a lot about the lake. 

When it was time to go, Bob thanked the fish for his wise advice and said goodbye.

Once there was a girl, her name was Lola. She was three years old and loved to explore.

One day, Lola's mum said, "Lola, can you please go upstairs and get some plates?" 
"Okay, mummy," Lola said as she started to speed up the stairs. 

Soon enough, she spotted something hidden in her bedroom. It was a box! She opened it up and found some cool toys inside. She was so excited.

Lola shouted out, "Mummy, mummy, look what I found!"

Her mum came into the room, "Wow, what a surprise! It was hidden, but you found it! Well done Lola!" 

Lola smiled and thanked her mum. She spent the rest of the day playing with her new toys.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Sam and Joe. Sam was always busy working. Joe liked to tease him.

"Hey Sam!" Joe said. "You work too much!"

But Sam didn't listen. He just kept working. Joe kept teasing him until Sam had enough.

"Okay," said Sam. "Let's have a race!" He jumped up and starting running. Joe was surprised and started running after him.

They ran and ran until they reached the finish line. Joe had won the race, but he was happy that Sam was having fun.

Now they both were busy playing games together and never stopped having fun!

Henry was a brave little boy. He was only three, but he wasn't scared of many things. One day his mommy wanted him to go with her to the store. He was a bit frightened when he saw the store. It was a big, tall building.

Mommy said they were going to buy some powder. Henry asked what powder it was. Mommy said it was special powder that could help him when he was feeling sick.

Henry leaned into his mommy's side. He was still a bit frightened. They entered the store and Mommy went to get the powder. He waited for her next to the cash register and leaned against the wall. The cashier was nice and smiled at him.

Mommy came back carrying a big bag of powder. Henry felt his fears melting away. Mommy put her arm around him and hugged him tight. She said it was time to go home. 

Henry leaned against his mommy's side as they walked out of the store. He was still a bit scared but he was also feeling brave and safe. He couldn't wait to get back to his cozy bed.

Once upon a time, there was a dog called Jessie. Jessie was very happy and she liked to play. One day, there was some mail for Jessie. When she saw it, she was so excited. She opened it and found a yummy treat inside. She barked in delight and ran outside. 

At the same time, Josh was walking in the park. He saw Jessie and said, "Hi Jessie! What do you have in your mail?" Jessie smiled and said, "Look, I got a yummy treat!" Josh said, "A yummy treat? Wow, that's great!" 

Jessie was so happy she had something yummy to eat. She ate it right away and said, "This treat is so yummy, thank you mail!" 

From that day forward, Jessie loved getting mail, even if it was just an ordinary letter. She knew there was a surprise inside waiting for her.

Once upon a time, there was a brave little girl. One night, her town had a big fire. Everyone was in danger! She was very tough, so she ran to the hospital to save the people that were sick.

The girl went inside and helped the nurses move the beds and carry the people to safety. It was a tough job, but she worked hard. The girl brought everyone to the courtyard outside.

When the fire was over, everyone thanked the brave little girl. She had done a great job and had saved the hospital. The girl felt so proud of herself. She had done something amazing! 

The town was safe and the brave little girl had saved the day.

Lily and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toys in their room. But today, they have to go to the doctor. Mom says they need a check-up.

"Come on, Lily and Ben, we have to go now. Get your coats and shoes," Mom says.

Lily and Ben do not want to go. They want to stay and play. They feel sleepy. They had a big lunch.

"Can we go later, Mom?" Lily asks.

"No, we have to go now. The doctor is waiting for us. Hurry up, please," Mom says.

Lily and Ben feel an urge to cry. They do not like the doctor. He has a big needle. It hurts.

They put on their coats and shoes slowly. They drag their feet. They hope Mom will change her mind.

But Mom does not change her mind. She takes their hands and leads them to the car. She buckles them in their seats.

"Mom, we are scared," Ben says.

"I know, sweetie. But the doctor is nice. He will only give you a little poke. It will be over soon. And then we can go home and have a treat," Mom says.

Lily and Ben try to be brave. They hold each other's hands. They look out the window. They see cars and trees and birds.

They get to the doctor's office. Mom parks the car. She opens the door.

"Come on, Lily and Ben, we have to rush. We are late," Mom says.

Lily and Ben get out of the car. They follow Mom to the door. They hope the doctor will be nice. They hope the poke will not hurt. They hope the treat will be yummy.

Lily loves animals. She wants to be a veterinarian when she grows up. A veterinarian is a person who helps animals when they are sick or hurt. Lily has many stuffed animals that she pretends are her patients. She likes to sort them by size, color, and type.

One day, Lily's mom takes her to a real veterinarian clinic. Lily is very excited. She sees many cute animals there. She sees dogs, cats, rabbits, birds, and even a turtle. She wants to pet them all, but her mom tells her to ask first.

"Hello, I'm Dr. Lee," a friendly woman says. "Are you here to see me?"

"No, we are here to see your animals," Lily says. "Can I pet them?"

Dr. Lee smiles. "Sure, you can pet some of them, but not all. Some of them are scared or in pain, and they need to rest. You have to be gentle and quiet, okay?"

"Okay," Lily says. She follows Dr. Lee to a room where there are cages with different animals. Dr. Lee shows her how to touch them softly and talk to them softly. Lily likes the animals. She thinks they are all cute.

"Can I sort them?" Lily asks.

"Sort them? What do you mean?" Dr. Lee asks.

"Like this," Lily says. She points to her stuffed animals in her backpack. "I sort them by size, color, and type. It's fun."

Dr. Lee laughs. "That is fun, but you can't sort these animals. They have to stay in their cages, because they are not toys. They are real animals, and they need special care. Do you understand?"

Lily nods. She understands. She still likes to sort her stuffed animals, but she also likes to learn about real animals. She thinks Dr. Lee is a good veterinarian. She hopes to be one too someday.

Lily and Sam were playing in the park. They saw a big orange microphone on a stage. They wanted to sing and have fun.

"Can we use the microphone?" Lily asked Sam.

"Sure, let's go!" Sam said.

They ran to the stage and picked up the microphone. They sang their favorite songs and made funny noises. They laughed and clapped.

But then, a man came to the stage. He looked angry. He was the owner of the microphone.

"Hey, what are you doing with my microphone?" he shouted. "This is not a toy, this is for my show!"

He grabbed the microphone from Lily and Sam. He saw that the wire was cut. He was very mad.

"Who cut the wire? Did you do this?" he asked.

Lily and Sam were scared. They did not know that the wire was cut. They did not see the scissors on the ground.

"No, we did not cut the wire. We just wanted to sing," Lily said.

"Then who did?" the man asked.

They looked around and saw a naughty boy hiding behind a tree. He was holding the scissors. He had cut the wire to make trouble.

"It was him! He cut the wire!" Sam said.

The man saw the boy and ran after him. He wanted to catch him and teach him a lesson.

Lily and Sam felt sorry for the man. They learned that they should not touch things that are not theirs. They also learned that they should not lie or blame others. They decided to help the man fix the wire and apologize.

They said, "We are sorry, sir. We did not mean to hurt your microphone. We will help you fix it. And we will not touch it again."

The man was surprised. He saw that Lily and Sam were honest and kind. He forgave them and thanked them. He also let them sing one more song with his microphone. He said, "You are good kids. You have learned your lesson. You can sing one more song, but then you have to go. And remember, always ask before you use something that is not yours."

Lily and Sam nodded and smiled. They sang a happy song and said goodbye to the man. They went back to their parents and told them what happened. Their parents were proud of them. They hugged them and said, "You did the right thing. You are good kids. We love you."

Once upon a time there was a happy bird. She flew high in the sky and was glad to be free. Every day she would urge the other birds to explore new places. She loved to fly around and experience new things.

One day, the bird urged her friends to visit the nearby lake. She had heard many wonderful things about it and wanted to see it for herself. As they flew to the lake, the bird was delighted to see all the wildlife. Fish were swimming and ducks were wading in the clear water. 

The bird was so happy that she let out a loud chirp. Her friends all chirped along, glad they had traveled to the lake. She urged them to stay there and enjoy the beauty of the lake. They stayed for hours, enjoying the peaceful atmosphere and all the wildlife.

Near the end of the day, the bird said goodbye to her friends and flew off into the sky. She knew that the memories of the lake would stay with her forever.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Anna. One day, Anna asked her mum for a pepper. Her mum smiled and said, Yes, Anna!

So, Anna and her mum went to the market. There, they saw many different kinds of peppers. Anna was happy to see them all!

Suddenly, Anna saw a playful puppy in the market. She wanted to pet the puppy, so she asked her mum. Her mum said, Yes, Anna!

Anna was so excited to play with the puppy. She ran to it and petted it very carefully. The puppy was so sweet and playful! Anna was so happy.

The puppy and Anna played together all day. They played chase and fetch with a ball. Anna and the puppy had lots of fun.

At the end of the day, Anna gave the puppy a big hug before saying goodbye. Anna and her mum then went home with the peppers. Anna was very happy.

Once upon a time, there was a big, wild lion who lived in the jungle. He had a big, brown collar around his neck. One day, the lion went for a walk and saw a small, scared mouse. The mouse said to the lion, "Please don't eat me, Mr. Lion." 

The lion laughed and said, "I won't eat you, little mouse. You're too small to fill me up." The mouse was relieved and said, "Thank you, Mr. Lion. You're very kind." 

Later that day, the lion was taking a nap when he heard a loud noise. He woke up and saw that his collar was stuck in a tree branch. The lion tried to pull it out, but he couldn't. Just then, the mouse walked by and saw the lion in trouble. The mouse said, "Don't worry, Mr. Lion. I'll help you." 

The mouse climbed up the tree and gnawed through the collar, freeing the lion. The lion was grateful and said, "Thank you, little mouse. You saved me." From that day on, the lion and the mouse became friends and helped each other whenever they could.

Ben and Sam are brothers. They like to play hockey in the yard. They have sticks and a ball. They hit the ball with the sticks and try to score goals.

One day, their mom calls them from the house. "Boys, come inside for lunch!" she says. Ben and Sam do not want to stop playing. They are having fun.

"Can we play a little more, mom?" Ben asks. He is the older brother. He is thoughtful. He knows mom is busy and works hard.

Mom answers, "No, boys, you need to eat. It is cold outside. You can play again after lunch."

Sam is the younger brother. He is not thoughtful. He is stubborn. He does not like mom's answer. He says, "No, mom, we want to play now. Hockey is fun. Lunch is not."

Mom is not happy with Sam's answer. She says, "Sam, that is rude. You need to listen to mom. Come inside now or you will be in trouble."

Ben tries to help Sam. He says, "Sam, come on. Mom is right. We can play later. Let's go eat. Maybe we can have cookies for dessert."

Sam thinks for a moment. He likes cookies. He decides to listen to Ben. He says, "Okay, Ben. Let's go eat. But we will play more hockey after lunch, right?"

Ben nods. He says, "Yes, Sam. We will play more hockey after lunch. But we need to be nice to mom. She loves us and takes care of us."

Sam agrees. He says, "Yes, Ben. We need to be nice to mom. She loves us and takes care of us."

They put their sticks and ball away. They run to the house. They hug mom and say, "We are sorry, mom. We love you. Thank you for lunch."

Mom smiles. She says, "I love you too, boys. You are good brothers. Now, let's eat. And yes, you can have cookies for dessert."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the big green yard. One day, while she was running around, she stumbled and fell down. But she got up and kept playing.

Later, her mommy brought her a delicious peach for a snack. It was so juicy and sweet! Lily took a big bite and it tasted brilliant.

As the sun started to set, Lily went inside to get ready for bed. She felt tired from playing all day. But she was happy because she had a fun day outside and a yummy peach to eat.

Once upon a time, there was a kind and polite princess who lived far away in a grand castle. One day she had to choose a new necklace to wear and was very excited at the prospect. The princess wondered to herself, â€œWhich one should I choose?â€

Just then, her magical fairy godmother appeared in a flash of light. The kind fairy noticed the dilemma the princess was in and said, â€œWhy not choose the one with the pretty sparkles?â€ 

The princess smiled and said thoughtfully, â€œThat is a very polite suggestion. I think I will choose the one with the sparkles!â€ Upon hearing her decision, the fairy godmother nodded her approval and the princess put on the shiny and sparkly neck. She then looked in the mirror and smiled. She was very happy with her choice and the kind fairy godmother was pleased too. 

The End.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy who loved to play with his boat. He would take it to the pond and watch it float. One day, he saw a duck and he wanted to call it over. He tried and tried, but the duck was too far away.

The little boy was persistent and kept calling for the duck to come. Suddenly, a big wave came and knocked his boat over. The little boy was sad and cried. He tried to get his boat back, but it was too far away.

The little boy went home with a heavy heart, without his boat. He learned that sometimes, even if we call and try really hard, things don't always go as we want them to.

Once there was a friendly bunny that loved to bounce. The bunny loved to hop from the garden to the theater. Every day the bunny would bounce around the theater and make friends. Every morning, the bunny would meet his new friends at the theater and bounce around with them. After a while, they would all play together in the theater. They loved to have so much fun together that they would bounce all day! The bunny loved being at the theater with his friends and wouldn't miss a day of bouncing and playing together.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toys in the morning. But sometimes they quarrel over the same toy. They want to have it for themselves.

One morning, they saw a pretty doll in a pink dress. It was on the shelf in their room. They both wanted the doll. They ran to the shelf and grabbed the doll. They pulled and tugged and shouted.

"Mine!" Anna said.

"No, mine!" Ben said.

They quarreled so loud that their mom heard them. She came to their room and saw them fighting over the doll. She was not happy.

"Stop it, Anna and Ben!" she said. "You are twins. You should share and be nice to each other. The doll is for both of you. You can take turns playing with it."

Anna and Ben looked at their mom. They felt sorry. They let go of the doll and hugged each other.

"Sorry, mom," Anna said.

"Sorry, mom," Ben said.

They smiled and said sorry to each other too. They decided to play with the doll together. They gave the doll a name and a story. They had fun and did not quarrel anymore. Their mom was proud of them. She gave them a kiss and a hug. She said they were good twins. They were happy.

Once upon a time, there was a friendly dog named Max. Max loved to play and run around in the park. One day, Max was very tired and wanted to rest on his mattress. 

As Max was sleeping, he heard someone shout, "Hey, Max! Wake up!" It was his friend, the cat named Mia. "What's the matter?" asked Max. "I lost my toy mouse and I can't find it," replied Mia. 

Max got up from his mattress and helped Mia look for her toy mouse. They searched high and low until they finally found it under a tree. "Thank you, Max! You're such a good friend," said Mia. Max wagged his tail happily and went back to his mattress for a nap.

Once upon a time, there was a big gorilla named Bobo. Bobo was very strong and loved to eat bananas. One day, Bobo saw a little girl named Lily crying. Bobo asked, "Why are you crying, Lily?" Lily said, "I lost my toy."

Bobo was very thoughtful and wanted to help Lily find her toy. He said, "Don't worry, Lily. I will manage to find your toy." Bobo looked everywhere for Lily's toy. He looked under the bed, in the closet, and even in the toy box. Finally, Bobo found the toy and gave it back to Lily.

Lily was very happy and said, "Thank you, Bobo. You are my hero!" Bobo smiled and said, "No problem, Lily. I am always here to help." From that day on, Lily and Bobo were the best of friends and had many fun adventures together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. She was three years old and loved to explore. One day, she decided to explore the big forest next to her house. 

As she walked into the woods, it got quiet. There was no noise anywhere. It made her feel curious, so she kept going deeper into the woods. 

Suddenly, she heard a noise coming from a nearby tree. It was a funny noise, like the noise that birds make. She looked up and saw a bright, pink bird perched on a branch. 

The bird then spread its wings and started to fly around her. It made a lot of noise as it flew, making Lucy laugh. 

The bird stayed around for a while before it flapped its wings and flew away. Lucy watched until it was out of sight, then it got quiet again. 

As Lucy walked home, she smiled and thought of the noise the bird spread while it was with her.

One day, Bobby was playing in his room when his mama called him. She was standing in the living room, holding his new bright red shirt. She said, "Bobby, it's time to dress up."

But Bobby didn't want to put on his shirt. He wanted to play some more. He shouted, "No! I don't want to dress!"

Mama frowned. She said, "You must dress. Mama's very enthusiastic about this outfit."

Bobby was still mad. He didn't want to dress. He said, "No! I want to play more!"

Just then, his papa came out of the kitchen, carrying a big cake from the refrigerator. His papa said, "Come on, Bobby. Don't make mama angry. Put your shirt on and mama will give you a slice of cake." 

Bobby smiled. He quickly said, "Okay, papa!" He took the shirt and dressed himself quickly. He was happy to be wearing his new shirt and he was even more excited about the yummy cake.

Once there was a boy called Bob. He was very creative and he loved to draw on paper. One day he had a fantastic idea - he wanted to print pictures of his own onto a special shield.

Bob went to explore the treasure trove at the store and he found a unique shield that he thought would be perfect for his project. He took it to the till, paid for it and said goodbye to the kind shopkeeper.

Back at home, Bob carefully placed the shield on the table. He chose his favorite picture, carefully printed it and then held it up proudly. He had made something special and unique. 

Bob couldn't wait to show his friends his invention. He quickly called his friends and said, "Come and see my shield! I have printed a picture on it and it looks great! Can you believe it?" 

Bob's friends couldn't believe their eyes. They were so impressed with his work and they all agreed - Bob had made something very special.

Once upon a time, there was a mighty bear. Every day the bear liked to play a game. He would decide what he wanted to win, and he would shout it in a loud, deep voice. Every time the bear shouted, he won!

But one day, the bear met a little redbird. The bird sang a beautiful song and the bear wanted to win it. He shouted as loud as he could, but he just couldn't win it.

So the bear tried to think of a way he could win the bird's song. He thought and thought, until he had an idea. He said, "I will sing my own song, but louder and mightier than your song!"

The bird was amazed and frightened. But the bear sang his mighty song, louder and louder! Finally, the bear won the bird's song. The bird flew away, but the bear knew he had won the most beautiful song of all.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. She was only three years old. She loved playing outside in the sunshine and running around with her furry cat.

One day, she noticed a big hairy stack of hay in the corner of her garden. She got really excited and rushed over to it. She ran her fingers through the soft hay and shouted with joy.

Then, she decided to make a hideout in the stack. She carefully moved the hay to create little nooks and crannies, and a cozy hiding place. She was so excited when she was done and couldn't wait to go hide inside her hay stack.

Just then, her cat came over and meowed. Lucy called out, "Hi kitty! I made a stack house. Do you want to come inside and play?" The cat darted inside, and Lucy quickly followed. She was so excited to explore her new secret hideaway. 

The two of them curled up together in the cozy hay and stayed there for hours, filled with excitement.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved playing with his toys and eating ice cream on hot days. One Tuesday, Timmy's mom told him they were going to the park. Timmy was so excited!

As they were walking to the park, Timmy saw a big puddle of water on the sidewalk. He wanted to jump in it, but his mom prevented him from doing so. She said it was dangerous and he could get hurt.

When they arrived at the park, Timmy ran to the swings and started swinging higher and higher. Suddenly, he lost his grip and fell off the swing. He hurt his arm badly and had to go to the hospital.

Timmy learned a valuable lesson that day. He realized that sometimes his mom says "no" to prevent him from getting hurt. He also learned to be more careful on the swings. From that day on, Timmy always listened to his mom and was more cautious when playing.

Jim was a little boy who loved to study. He had many books and paper for writing. His favorite was a bright red track. He loved to play with it and follow the path with his eyes. He could imagine he was going on an adventure.

One day, Jim wanted to study his track very closely. He set up a big table and covered it with a white cloth. Carefully, he place the red track on the cloth and started to study. He looked at the colors, the curves, and the shapes.

It took him a long time to study the track, but Jim noticed something strange. The track had a switch near the end! He was surprised and curious. He pressed the switch and suddenly, the track began to move!

Jim was delighted. He watched, mesmerized, as the track moved in a circle. He couldn't believe it! He had studied his track very closely and had made a wonderful discovery. The end of his red track was magical and had a special surprise!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Sophie. Sophie liked to run. Every day she would go for a big run in her village.

One day, she went for a run and came upon a big building. It was a library. Sophie had never seen a library before and she was so glad. She ran right in.

Inside the library, Sophie found lots of interesting things. She found books and games and puzzles. She was so happy!

"Oh!" Sophie said. "What a fun place!"

Suddenly, an old man in the library smiled at her and said "Would you like to borrow some books today, Sophie?â€

Sophie was so grateful. She took three books home. She was so happy and couldn't wait to read them. 

The next day she went for a run, but this time, instead of going to the library, she went to the park and played with her friends. She was so glad she had found the library and was grateful she had something new to do.

John and his dad were walking in the park. John saw a swing and asked his dad to push him.

John said, "Please dad, offer me a push!"
John's dad laughed and said, "Of course I will offer you a push!"

John's dad brought John to the swing and started to push him. John laughed and said, "Faster, faster!"

John's dad pushed harder and higher until John felt his head getting dizzy. With a wide open mouth, he shouted, "Woohoo!"

After a few rounds, John said with a tired voice, "Time to stop!" His dad replied, "Time to take a break!" They smiled and walked to a nearby bench for a rest.

Mark was a very kind boy. He liked to make prints in the sand and draw pictures of his family. One day, he went to the beach and he spied something hidden in the sand. He dug it out and found a big box. Mark opened the top and saw inside lots of brightly coloured mark-making things. He was so very excited! He took them out and marked the sand. He made prints of his family and all kinds of shapes and designs. Mark was so happy to show his family what he had made. He said, â€œLook at all the kind prints Iâ€™ve made!â€ Everyone was so impressed, even the birds and the bees. Mark and his family had a fun day in the sand, making lots of colourful prints to mark their special day.

Lily was a shy girl who liked to play with puzzles. She had many puzzles with animals, cars, and flowers. She could solve them very fast and make nice pictures.

One day, she got a new puzzle from her grandma. It was a big puzzle with a zoom. A zoom was a thing that could fly in the sky and make loud noises. Lily had never seen a zoom before. She was curious and excited.

She opened the box and took out the pieces. She tried to find the corners and the edges. She looked at the picture on the box. It was a zoom with red and blue stripes. It had wings and a tail and a nose.

Lily started to solve the puzzle. She found the pieces that matched the colors and the shapes. She worked hard and had fun. She did not notice that her brother Max came into the room.

Max was not shy. He liked to play with balls and cars and trucks. He saw Lily's puzzle and wanted to play too. He grabbed some pieces and tried to fit them in. He did not look at the picture. He did not care about the zoom.

Lily was angry. She said, "No, Max, that is not right. You are messing up my puzzle. Go away and play with your own toys."

Max did not listen. He said, "I want to play with the zoom. It is cool. Let me help you."

He pushed some pieces and broke the puzzle. Lily cried. She said, "You are mean, Max. You ruined my puzzle. I don't want to play with you."

Max felt sorry. He said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I did not mean to hurt you. I just wanted to play with you. Can we fix the puzzle together?"

Lily stopped crying. She said, "OK, Max, but you have to be careful and follow the picture. The zoom is not easy to solve. It has many pieces and details."

Max nodded. He said, "OK, Lily, I will be careful and follow the picture. The zoom is hard to solve. But it is also fun and pretty."

They hugged and smiled. They worked together and solved the puzzle. They made the zoom fly in the sky and make loud noises. They were happy and proud. They showed their puzzle to their grandma and said, "Look, grandma, we solved the zoom. It is a gift from you. Thank you, grandma."

Grandma smiled and said, "You are welcome, my dears. You did a great job. I'm glad you solved the zoom. And I'm glad you played together. You are a good team."

Once upon a time, there was a happy bear called Toby. He lived in the forest with his family. Toby had lots of fun playing with them each day.

One day, Toby and his family heard a loud alarm. It was so loud, he knew it meant something was wrong. He wanted to stay together with his family, but the alarm made them separate.

Toby felt very sad that he had to leave his family. He didn't want to be away from them. So Toby started to look for his family. He tried to remember which direction they had gone in. 

He searched for a long time, but he still couldn't find them. Then, he heard the alarm again. This time it sounded different. Toby followed the sound and finally found his family.

They were all so happy to be together again! Toby was glad he hadn't given up and kept looking for them. They all hugged each other and never wanted to be separated again.

Mum and Dad were packing for a trip.

Mum said to Dad, "Let's get the egg in the suitcase."

Dad agreed and took an egg out of the fridge. The egg was big and round.

Mum said, "It's so big. I have a sweet idea. We could share the egg on the plane!"

Dad smiled and put the egg in the suitcase.

Mum said, "Let's pack the presents too!"

They packed the presents quickly and soon they were ready.

Mum said, "Let's eat the egg now. It's so sweet!"

Dad agreed, and they ate the egg together.

Mum and Dad smiled, excited for their trip.

John was playing in the park. He was running around and laughing. He saw a lawn and went over to investigate. It was green, and he wanted to play on it. He didn't know that it belonged to someone else.

John asked his friend, "I want to play on that lawn. Can I?"

His friend replied, "No, John. You can't play on that lawn. It belongs to someone else."

John said, "Stupid lawn! Why can't I play on it?"

His friend said, "Well, you don't know who it belongs to, so it wouldn't be right to play on it."

So John decided not to play on the lawn. He was still curious, but he knew he had to respect the lawn.

Once there was a beautiful flower who lived in a garden. One morning, the sun woke up the flower and it started to bloom. The flower spread its petals wide and looked marvellous.

Suddenly, the flower heard a noise. It was a bee buzzing around! The bee flew to the flower with a glass in its mouth. The glass was icy cold and it shimmered and sparkled in the sunshine.

The bee put the glass close to the flower and a drop of water came out. The drop was also icy cold and it landed inside the flower's petals. Suddenly, the flower felt so happy. It said, "Thank you bee for the cold and refreshing glass of water!" 

The flower was so thrilled it started to twirl and spin around and around in the sunshine. The flower felt so alive and knew it would stay this way every morning as long as it could get a glass of cold and icy water.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She went to the train station with her mommy and daddy. The train station was big and had lots of people. Lily saw a nice lady with a big smile. The nice lady helped Lily find her train. 

Lily got on the train and said goodbye to her mommy and daddy. She felt a little scared, but she knew she would see them soon. Suddenly, she heard a baby cry. Lily felt sad for the baby. She wished she could make the baby feel better. 

When Lily arrived at her destination, she saw her grandma waiting for her. She ran to her grandma and gave her a big hug. Lily felt happy to see her grandma again. She told her all about the nice lady and the crying baby at the train station. Grandma listened and smiled. It was a nice day for Lily.

Lily liked to watch yoga on TV. She saw people bend and stretch and breathe. She wanted to try yoga too. She asked her mom if she could join her.

"Sure, Lily, you can do yoga with me. But first, we need to eat breakfast. What do you want?" Mom said.

"I want toast and jam and juice," Lily said.

Mom made toast and jam and juice for Lily. She gave her a plate and a cup. Lily took a big bite of her toast. She made a face. "Yuck! This jam is sour!" she said.

Mom tasted the jam. She frowned. "Oh, no, you're right. This jam is bad. I'm sorry, Lily. Let me get you some honey instead," she said.

She went to the kitchen and looked for honey. She did not see it on the shelf. She opened the cupboard. She saw a big mess. The honey jar was broken. There was honey everywhere. And there was a bear. A big, brown bear. It was licking the honey. It looked at Mom. It growled.

Mom screamed. Lily heard her scream. She ran to the kitchen. She saw the bear. She was scared. She grabbed her mom's hand. They ran out of the house. They called for help.

The bear finished the honey. It was full. It was sleepy. It saw the TV. It saw yoga. It liked yoga. It went to the living room. It lay down on the mat. It did yoga. It bent and stretched and breathed. It was happy. It snored.

Lily and Ben were playing with their toys in the living room. Lily liked to be organized. She had a box for her dolls, a box for her cars, and a box for her blocks. Ben liked to be messy. He threw his toys everywhere and made a lot of noise.

"Ben, stop it!" Lily said. "You are making a mess. Put your toys in the boxes."

"No, I don't want to," Ben said. "I want to play with all of them. Look, I made a crane with my blocks. It can lift your dolls and cars."

Lily looked at Ben's crane. It was big and tall and had a hook. She realized that it was a cool toy. She wanted to play with it too.

"Can I try your crane, Ben?" she asked.

"Sure, Lily," Ben said. "You can play with my crane if I can play with your dolls and cars."

Lily and Ben smiled at each other. They decided to share their toys and play together. They realized that it was more fun to be friends than to fight. They had a good time with the crane, the dolls, and the cars. They were happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She liked to play with her dolls and teddy bears. One day, Lily's mommy asked her to help her with something. She needed Lily to kneel down and put a label on a box. 

Lily didn't know what a label was, but her mommy showed her a sticker with words on it. "This is a label," her mommy said. "Can you put it on the box for me?" 

Lily nodded and kneeled down to put the label on the box. She made sure it was clear and straight. Her mommy was very proud of her for helping out. From that day on, Lily knew what a label was and how to put it on things.

Once upon a time, there was an elephant and a mouse. They were good friends, but the mouse was always much cleverer.

One day, the mouse used some oxygen to make a great balloon. When the elephant saw it, she asked if she could have one too. The mouse was surprised, but he agreed.

The elephant's balloon was much bigger, and soon she couldn't even see the ground. She went higher and higher and when she looked down she started to panic. She shouted to the mouse: "Help me!"

The mouse thought quickly and told the elephant to let go of the balloon. The elephant was scared, but she did as she was told. The balloon came back down, and the elephant was relieved. But later, she began to regret not trying to think of a cleverer plan.

The end.

Once upon a time there was a special girl named Daisy who loved to skip in the grass. Every day she went outside in her original sneakers and she would skip and stumble through the grass.

Every day she would find something new. She might find a ladybug, a butterfly or a leaf that she could bring back to show her mom and dad. One day on her adventure she stumbled upon something shiny in the grass.

It was a big, round, golden rock! She was so excited and she just had to pick it up and take a closer look. She turned it around and around in her hands and made it sparkle in the sunlight. 

She wanted to take it home, so she put it in her pocket and went back inside to show her parents. She was so proud of finding this special treasure that she decided to keep it forever. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in her garden where she had a big cactus. One day, Lily's friend came to her garden to play. Her friend accidentally touched the cactus and got hurt. Lily's friend started crying and Lily felt sorry for her.

Lily's mother came to see what happened and saw that her friend was hurt. She asked Lily what happened and Lily told her that her friend touched the cactus and got hurt. Lily's mother wrapped a bandage around her friend's finger and told her that she will be okay.

Lily's friend stopped crying and thanked Lily's mother for helping her. Lily felt happy that her friend was okay and they continued to play in the garden. From that day on, Lily made sure to tell her friends to be careful around the cactus.

Once upon a time there were two best friends, Karen and Daisy. Karen and Daisy were always playing outside together.

One day, Karen found a hive in the trees. It was an amazing hive full of bees!

Karen and Daisy cheered in delight. They had worked together to make something beautiful!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the sunshine. One day, she went on a walk with her mommy. They walked through the park and saw many pretty flowers. 

Suddenly, Lily saw a dangerous snake on the path. Her mommy told her to stay back and not get too close. The snake slithered away and they continued on their walk. 

As they walked, Lily saw a butterfly and started to follow it. She led her mommy to a beautiful garden with lots of flowers. They sat in the sunshine and enjoyed the pretty view. It was a happy day for Lily and her mommy. The end.

Once upon a time there was a little boy named Ben. He lived in a far away place but he loved where he lived. He had one special thing in this distant place, the steel wall. Ben had a little red wagon that he loved to ride and pull things in.

One day Ben noticed something strange about the steel wall. It seemed to be demanding something from him. He couldn't figure out what it was so he just looked at it in confusion.

Suddenly, the steel wall let out a loud noise. Ben jumped in surprise and he knew the wall wanted something from him. So he pulled out his little red wagon and filled it up with rocks. He slowly pushed the wagon to the steel wall.

The steel wall was happy and slowly faded away, leaving behind a big red door. Ben opened the door and walked through. On the other side he saw a bright and beautiful new world. He was so excited and he knew the steel wall had been telling him to explore and find something new, something distant.

Sara and Tom were playing in the garden. They liked to dig in the dirt and look for bugs. Sara found a big worm and showed it to Tom.

"Look, Tom, a worm!" Sara said.

Tom looked at the worm and smiled. He wanted to touch it.

"Can I hold it?" Tom asked.

Sara nodded and gave him the worm. Tom felt the worm wriggle in his hand. He liked how it tickled his fingers.

"Let's make a home for it," Tom said.

He urged Sara to follow him to a corner of the garden. There was a strip of grass and some stones. Tom put the worm on the grass and covered it with some stones.

"There, now it has a house," Tom said.

Sara nodded and smiled. She thought the worm was happy in its new home. She and Tom sat on the grass and watched the worm peek out from under the stones. They felt peaceful and quiet. They liked to play in the garden.

Joey and his mom were playing outside in the hot sun. Joey was playing with his toy razor and was having so much fun! But then he got sleepy, and after a while he started to yawn. His mom noticed, and said to him, â€œJoey, are you tired?â€

Joey nodded his head. His mom said, â€œIt looks like itâ€™s time for a nap!â€ She took the toy razor from him, and then put her arm around him.

They both started walking inside. Joey was so sleepy, and he kept yawning. His mom tucked him into bed and said, â€œTake a good rest, Joey. Sweet dreams.â€ And with that, Joey drifted off to sleep.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She was only three years old. One day, she saw an aeroplane in the sky. She was very scared, but she wanted to touch it, so she closed her eyes and wished hard. Suddenly, she felt something soft and fluffy! She opened her eyes and saw that she was touching the aeroplane. She smiled and waved, and the aeroplane waved back. The little girl was so happy that she could touch the aeroplane, and she wasn't scared anymore!

Once upon a time, there was a little bee. The bee was very anxious because it had lost its way back to the hive. It flew and flew, but it couldn't find its home. 

Then, a kind girl saw the bee and wanted to help. She gently picked up the bee and brought it back to the hive. The bee was so happy to be home and thanked the girl. 

But, the other bees were not happy. They were angry at the little bee for getting lost and causing them worry. They decided to punish the little bee and didn't let it back into the hive. 

The little bee was sad and didn't know what to do. It wished it could restore its relationship with the other bees. The moral of the story is to always be kind and forgiving, even when someone makes a mistake.

Once upon a time, a jolly girl was playing in the garden, when she spotted something sparkly on the floor. She bent down to take a closer look and she saw it was a beautiful bracelet! She was delighted and wanted to try it on. However, as she reached out to pick it up, something else caught her eye. She peered around and saw a caterpillar crawling towards her. She giggled and reached out her hand for a poke. As soon as she touched the small, furry insect, she felt the pretty bracelet on her wrist. She looked at it in amazement, it was so special. The jolly girl felt so happy, she could wear the beautiful bracelet everywhere! She ran off to show her family and friends her sparkling new bracelet.

One day, there was a boy. He was walking outside and it was very gloomy. He looked around and noticed something different. There was a tall tree in the distance and it was inviting the boy to come nearer. 

The boy got closer and closer to the tree until he was standing right beneath its branches. Suddenly, the tree started talking to him. It suggested that the boy climb up the trunk and into its branches.

The boy was surprised but he trusted the tree and decided to try it. He carefully climbed until he was standing on one of the highest branches. From up there, he could see far into the distance. It was a wonderful view! 

He thanked the tree for suggesting it and said goodbye. Then he carefully climbed down and went home with a big smile on his face.

It was a nice day in the park. Anna and Kenny were playing outdoors. Anna had a big red balloon in her hand and Kenny was blowing bubbles. Suddenly, Anna started to sing a happy tune. Kenny stopped and said: "Oh, Anna! That sounds so nice! Can you sing it again?" Anna smiled and started to sing once more. The two children then held up the balloon and started to sing together. Other children heard them and soon the park was full of singing. Kenny and Anna laughed and hugged each other. It was a nice day after all.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys, especially his big red ball. One day, Timmy was playing with his ball when a mighty wind blew it away. Timmy was sad and cried out, "My ball is gone!"

His mom said, "Don't worry Timmy, we'll find your ball." They went outside to look for it, but it was nowhere to be seen. Timmy was so sad that he couldn't even eat his dinner.

The next day, Timmy's dad found the ball in the neighbor's yard. But when they went to get it, they saw that it had been chewed up by the neighbor's dog. Timmy was heartbroken and cried again. His mom hugged him and said, "It's just an object, Timmy. We can get you a new one." But Timmy knew that it wouldn't be the same.

One morning, a little girl named Gracie woke up. She heard a loud alarm. She was scared and ran to her father.

"Daddy," she said, "I heard a loud noise!"

"It was just the alarm clock," he said, reassuring her. "But don't worry. You are safe."

Just then, Gracie started to sneeze. Her father put a tissue in her hand and said, "You must have caught a cold."

Gracie was worried that she would be sick for a long time, but her dad said, "Don't worry. As long as you rest and take your medicine, you'll be safe and healthy soon!" Hearing this, Gracie felt much better. 

Thanks Daddy," she said and gave him a big hug. 

The end.

Gus was a 3 year old boy. He loved to hear jokes and he had a lot of them. He loved to tell them to everyone and everywhere he went.

One day, Gus went to a store and found a new shirt. It was a funny shirt with a joke on it. He thought it would look perfect on him. He tried it on and it fit him perfectly.

Gus was very happy with his new shirt. He laughed and smiled at the joke on the shirt. Then he realised something. The joke had changed! Gus was surprised and laughed even more. The shirt was always changing jokes!

Gus was so excited and he kept trying new shirts until he found one with a joke that made him laugh the most. It was the perfect fit and the perfect joke. He couldn't wait to show it to everyone.

The sun shone on the ground, scattering bits of light around it. Two little birds were chirping happily and playing together in the garden.

Suddenly, the birds stopped in their tracks. A small little girl, wearing a pale dress had appeared in front of her. She had a small waist and a long braid.

"What are you doing here?" asked one of the birds, in a stern voice.

The little girl looked startled. "I was just playing in the garden," she squeaked, and then her eyes began to fill with tears.

The bird softened its tone. "Oh, please don't cry. We didn't mean to scare you. We just wanted to know why you were here."

The little girl wiped her eyes and smiled. "I just wanted to play. Can I stay here?"

The birds looked at each other, then back at the little girl.

"Sure! We'd love to play with you," said the other bird. The little girl smiled brightly and the birds scattered around her as they continued their game.

Once upon a time there were two brothers, Bob and Joe. Bob was older than Joe and liked to help him with his work.

One day Bob asked Joe to help him with a tricky job. He said: "Joe, can you complete this for me?" Joe tried very hard, but he couldn't do it.

Bob felt guilty. He had asked Joe to do something he couldn't do. He gave Joe a big hug and said: "It's ok, don't worry. I'll help you finish it."

The brothers worked together and managed to complete the job! Bob smiled. Joe was so happy. He said: "Thank you, brother!"

They laughed and hugged each other. They knew that together, they could do anything.

Sara and Ben like to play with cards. They have many cards with animals on them. They try to find two cards that are the same. They call this game "match".

One day, they go to the park with Mom. They see a big sign with a map. The map shows many paths in the park. Sara and Ben want to explore the paths. They ask Mom if they can play "match" with the map.

Mom says yes, but they have to stay close to her. She gives them each a card with a picture of a path. She tells them to look at the map and find the path that matches their card. Then they can walk on that path with her.

Sara and Ben are excited. They look at their cards and the map. Sara has a card with a path that goes around a pond. She finds the path on the map. She points to it and says, "Look, Mom, I found my match!"

Ben has a card with a path that goes through a forest. He looks at the map, but he cannot find the path. He sees many paths, but none of them look like his card. He feels confused. He says, "Mom, I can't find my match. Where is it?"

Mom looks at Ben's card and the map. She smiles and says, "Ben, your card is special. It shows a hidden path that is not on the map. You have to look for a sign with a squirrel on it. That is the entrance to the forest path. Do you want to try to find it?"

Ben nods and says, "Yes, Mom, I want to find the hidden path. That sounds fun!" He looks around and sees a sign with a squirrel on it. He runs to it and says, "I found it, Mom, I found it!"

Mom, Sara and Ben follow the sign and enter the forest path. They see many trees and animals. They enjoy their walk and their game of "match".

Once upon a time there was a big old tree. It was so big that it touched the clouds. Every day lots of birds and animals came to the tree and they all supported each other.

One day a little mouse called Sally decided to climb the tree. She kept going higher and higher and soon she was so high that she could see the whole world. Then she heard a loud noise and quickly climbed down.

When Sally got back to the ground she saw a bright yellow bulldozer. An old man with big glasses was driving the bulldozer and wanted to cut the tree down.

Sally shook her head and shouted, "No! This tree supports us all. You can't cut it down!"

The old man looked surprised and smiled at Sally, "You are right my little friend. I'm so sorry."

Sally smiled and the old man turned his bulldozer away. The animals, birds and everyone else cheered for Sally and thanked her for protecting their big old tree.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys all day long. He never wanted to share his toys with his friends. One day, Timmy's mom explained to him that sharing is caring. She told him that it's important to trade toys with his friends so everyone can have fun.

Timmy didn't listen to his mom and continued to play with his toys all by himself. One day, Timmy's favorite toy broke and he couldn't play with it anymore. He was very sad and didn't know what to do. Timmy's mom explained to him that if he had shared his toys with his friends, he could have traded with them and still have lots of toys to play with.

Timmy realized that he had been spoiled and selfish. He decided to share his toys with his friends from then on. Timmy learned that sharing is important and makes everyone happy.

Lily has a pet cat. She loves her cat very much. Her cat is soft and white and has blue eyes. She likes to play with her cat and cuddle with her cat.

One day, Lily finds a hat in her closet. The hat is big and red and has a flower on it. Lily thinks the hat is pretty. She wants to wear the hat. She puts the hat on her head and looks in the mirror. She smiles and says, "I look nice in this hat!"

Then she sees her cat on the bed. She has an idea. She wants to share the hat with her cat. She takes the hat off her head and puts it on her cat's head. She says, "Now you look nice in this hat, too!"

But her cat does not like the hat. Her cat thinks the hat is ugly and heavy and itchy. Her cat shakes her head and tries to get the hat off. She meows and scratches and runs away. She does not want to wear the hat.

Lily is sad. She does not understand why her cat does not like the hat. She thinks the hat is pretty and fun. She chases her cat and says, "Please, please, wear the hat with me! It is a nice hat!"

But her cat does not listen. Her cat hides under the sofa and does not come out. She does not want to wear the hat. She wants to be a cat.

Lily is sad. She does not have anyone to wear the hat with. She puts the hat back in her closet and sits on the bed. She wishes her cat would come out and play with her.

Then she hears a knock on the door. It is her friend Ben. He has a pet dog. His dog is brown and furry and has a wagging tail. He likes to play with his dog and run with his dog.

Ben says, "Hi, Lily! Do you want to play with me and my dog? We can go to the park and have fun!"

Lily says, "Yes, Ben! I want to play with you and your dog! That sounds like fun!"

She gets up and grabs her coat and shoes. She does not take the hat. She does not need the hat. She has a friend and a pet to play with. She is happy.

She opens the door and sees Ben and his dog. They smile and bark and say, "Hi, Lily!"

Lily says, "Hi, Ben! Hi, dog!"

She pets the dog and the dog licks her face. She laughs and says, "You are a nice dog!"

Then she looks at her cat under the sofa. She says, "Bye, cat! I love you! Maybe later you will wear the hat with me!"

But her cat does not answer. Her cat does not care. Her cat is a cat.

Once upon a time there was a bus. It was very big and impressive. It drove around town with lots of people inside.

One day, the bus had a long journey and the driver was very tired. He stopped and took a rest. The passengers sat quietly and watched.

After a while, the driver felt all better. He started the bus again and drove everyone home. Everyone was very happy.

The bus drove around town, shining in the sun. Everyone was impressed by how big and strong the bus was.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in the park with her friends. One day, while they were playing, Lily saw a symbol on the ground. She didn't know what it meant, but it looked pretty.

Suddenly, a boy came up to them and started being rude. He said mean things to Lily and her friends. Lily didn't like it and she started to scream. Her friends didn't know what to do, but Lily stood up to the boy and told him to stop being rude.

The boy was surprised and didn't know what to say. He apologized and they all became friends. From that day on, Lily and her friends played together in the park and whenever someone was being rude, they stood up for each other. And whenever they saw the symbol on the ground, they remembered the day they became friends.

Once there was a girl named Beth and she was three years old. She had a wooden watch that she loved to play with. One day Beth was looking around her room and she saw something that she thought would match her watch. It was a bright, yellow, sour lemon! She smiled and picked it up. Beth wanted to show her friends what she found, so she ran outside to find them.

When Beth got outside she saw her friends playing catch. Beth showed them the sour lemon and the watch. Everyone thought the sour lemon and watch was a perfect match! They were all so excited and began playing a new game with the sour lemon and the watch.

They would throw the sour lemon back and forth and call out, â€œWatch!â€ as they threw it. Someone else would try to catch the lemon before it hit the ground and call out, â€œLemon!â€. It was so much fun, they couldnâ€™t stop playing! 

The friends played until the sun went down, they all said goodbye and went home. Beth held onto her watch, the perfect match to the sour lemon, and her friends smiles.

Sara loves yogurt. She eats it every morning with her mom and dad. She likes to mix it with fruit and granola. Sometimes she shares it with her cat, Fluffy.

One day, Sara went to the store with her mom. She saw a big shelf of yogurt. There were many colors and flavors. Sara wanted to try them all. She asked her mom, "Can we buy all the yogurt, please?"

Her mom smiled and said, "No, Sara, we can't buy all the yogurt. That's too much. We can buy two or three. Which ones do you want?"

Sara looked at the shelf. She saw a pink yogurt with strawberries. She saw a blue yogurt with blueberries. She saw a yellow yogurt with bananas. She saw a green yogurt with kiwis. She saw a purple yogurt with blackberries. She saw a white yogurt with vanilla. She saw a brown yogurt with chocolate. She saw a red yogurt with cherries. She saw a orange yogurt with peaches. She saw a lot of yogurt.

She said, "I want all of them. They look yummy."

Her mom said, "You can't have all of them, Sara. You have to choose. How about we ask that lady for help?"

Sara looked at the lady. She was elderly. She had gray hair and glasses. She wore a name tag that said, "Hello, I'm Betty. I work here."

Her mom said, "Excuse me, Betty. Can you help us? My daughter likes yogurt, but she can't decide which one to buy."

Betty smiled and said, "Sure, I can help you. Yogurt is good for you. It has calcium and protein. It makes your bones and muscles strong. It also has good bacteria that help your tummy. Do you know what bacteria are, Sara?"

Sara shook her head. She said, "No, what are they?"

Betty said, "They are very tiny things that live inside you. Some of them are bad and make you sick. Some of them are good and make you healthy. Yogurt has good bacteria that fight the bad bacteria. They are like little soldiers in your body. Do you like soldiers, Sara?"

Sara nodded. She said, "Yes, I like soldiers. They are brave and strong. They protect us."

Betty said, "That's right. Yogurt protects you, too. It also tastes good. Do you have a favorite flavor, Sara?"

Sara thought for a moment. She said, "I like strawberries. And blueberries. And bananas. And kiwis. And blackberries. And vanilla. And chocolate. And cherries. And peaches."

Betty laughed and said, "You like all the flavors, Sara. That's wonderful. But you can't buy all the yogurt. How about we play a game? I'll give you a clue, and you guess the flavor. If you guess right, you can buy that yogurt. If you guess wrong, you have to try another one. Are you ready, Sara?"

Sara nodded. She said, "Yes, I'm ready. Let's play."

Betty said, "Okay, here's the first clue. This yogurt is the color of the sky on a sunny day. What flavor is it?"

Sara said, "Blueberry!"

Betty said, "That's right. You can buy the blueberry yogurt. Here's the next clue. This yogurt is the color of a flower that smells sweet. What flavor is it?"

Sara said, "Strawberry!"

Betty said, "That's right. You can buy the strawberry yogurt. Here's the last clue. This yogurt is the color of a fruit that has a fuzzy skin and a big seed. What flavor is it?"

Sara said, "Peach!"

Betty said, "That's right. You can buy the peach yogurt. You did a great job, Sara. You guessed all the flavors. You can buy three yogurts today. Which ones do you want?"

Sara looked at the shelf. She saw the blueberry yogurt, the strawberry yogurt, and the peach yogurt. She said, "I want these ones. They are my favorites."

Her mom said, "Okay, Sara. You can have these ones. Thank you, Betty, for your help. You are very kind and patient."

Betty said, "You're welcome. It was my pleasure. I hope you enjoy your yogurt, Sara. Come back soon."

Sara said, "Thank you, Betty. You are very nice and smart. I like you. I like yogurt. I will come back soon. Bye."

Sara and her mom waved goodbye to Betty. They went to the cashier and paid for the yogurt. They went back to their car and drove home

One day, it started to rain. The sky was a deep, dark, black. Everything outside was wet and the landscape was filled with a thick fog. 
The rain kept falling. Rivers appeared and the grass was so soggy that everything was damp and slippery. 
The rain stopped after a while and the sun came up. The sky turned bright blue and the wet landscape reflected the beauty of the light. The clouds had cleared and the grass was back to its usual green. 
The cool wetness of the rain was gone and the landscape was a beautiful sight to see.

One day, Mandy was playing in her room. She saw a big, wide frame on the floor. Mandy was so excited, she wanted to rock it!

Mandy pushed the frame back and forth and it rocked really gently. She had so much fun! She smiled and clapped her hands.

Soon, it was time for a nap. Mandy was so sleepy she had to lay down on the frame to rest. She rocked herself while she fell asleep and had the best nap ever.

When Mandy woke up, she was still rocking on the wide frame. She smiled, then got up and ran off to play again!

Once there was a beautiful bird. It had wide wings and a feather that was bright orange. The bird loved to perch on a nearby tree. One day, the bird noticed a wide field. It wanted to explore.

The bird flew across the field. It observed the colourful flowers and the lush green grass. It was so happy to be free! Suddenly, it spotted something shining in the grass.
