The bird flew closer and saw it was a feather! It was different than the bird's own feather, but still so beautiful and shiny. Excited, the bird picked it up and flew off. 

The bird took the feather to its nest and kept it safe. Whenever the bird observed the feather, it felt so happy and excited. 

The end.

Once upon a time there was a rich elephant who wanted a ball. He looked high and low, in the sky and on the ground. Everywhere he looked, he just couldn't find the right ball.

So the elephant decided to search a little bit further. He walked through the forest and then he saw it! In the river was a big, round, colourful ball. He was so excited, he wanted the ball straight away.

The elephant ran to the river and took a deep breath. He dived right in and grabbed the ball. He lifted the heavy ball to the surface, and it was his.

He was so happy, he jumped and shouted. With the ball in his trunk, he skipped out of the forest and went back home with a smile.

Once there was a machine. It was very big and it could do lots of things. Every day the machine was patient and it worked hard to do its job.

Over time, the machine started to work better and better. It could do more things and went faster. Pretty soon the machine was doing its job very well.

This made the people who worked with the machine very happy. They wanted the machine to increase even more, so they worked hard and took care of it.

With lots of patience and hard work, the machine kept increasing and improving. Now it works amazingly fast and can do lots of things. Everyone is so happy with the machine and they are proud of all the hard work they put into it.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He loved to play with his toy helicopter. One day, Timmy's mom took him to a big store. In the store, there was a big display of toys. Timmy saw a fearful little girl crying because she couldn't find her toy. 

Timmy felt sad for the little girl, so he decided to help her. He flew his toy helicopter up high and looked around for the lost toy. Finally, he saw it on a high shelf. Timmy carefully landed his helicopter and climbed up to get the toy. He gave it to the little girl, who was very happy and hugged Timmy. 

From that day on, Timmy and the little girl were friends. They played with their toys together and had lots of fun. Timmy was happy that he could help someone in need.

There was a happy bunny named Benny who lived in a big field with his family and friends. One day, Benny found a shiny razor lying on the ground. He picked it up and showed it to his friends, but they told him it was dangerous and he should not play with it.

Benny didn't listen and kept playing with the razor. One day, he accidentally cut himself and it hurt a lot. His friends were sad and worried about him. They knew they had to help him.

They went to a distant store and found a special cream that could heal Benny's wound. They brought it back to him and carefully applied it. Benny felt better and was grateful to his friends for revealing the solution to his problem. From then on, he promised to be more careful and not play with dangerous things.

Jimmy and Alice were best friends. They liked to race each other every day.

One day, they saw a group of people on the other side of the park.

Alice said, "Let's go clap for them."
 Jimmy shook his head. He was too sleepy.

Alice said, "Come on. I don't want to go alone. Please?

Jimmy sighed. He reluctantly followed Alice across the park.

When they reached the group of people, Alice started to clap. But Jimmy just stood there, feeling too tired to move.

Alice, who was getting angry, poked Jimmy in the side. She said, "Clap! Clap!" 

Jimmy, who was getting scared, pushed Alice away.

The group of people stopped what they were doing and watched. They looked angry.

Alice started to cry. She said, "Jimmy, why did you do that?!"

Jimmy, who felt sad and scared, couldn't find any words. 

The group of people started to move towards Jimmy and Alice. Jimmy and Alice ran away as fast as they could. They were very scared and they never raced each other again.

Once upon a time, there was a big ship on the sea. The ship was very open, and the sun shone in. The ship was so big that many people could fit inside. 

One day, a little fish wanted to swim with the big ship. The fish swam and swam, but it was hard to keep up with the big ship. The fish tried and tried, but it was too tired. 

Suddenly, the ship went too fast and the fish got hit by the ship. The fish couldn't swim anymore and it was very sad. The ship kept going, not knowing what had happened. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the sunshine and pick flowers. One day, Lily saw a sign that said "Believe in yourself". She didn't know what that meant, but it sounded nice.

Later that day, Lily was playing with her toy ball when it got stuck in a tree. She tried to pull it out, but it was too tight. She started to cry because she thought she would never get her ball back.

But then she remembered the sign she saw earlier. She took a deep breath and believed in herself. She climbed up the tree and got her ball back. She felt so proud of herself and happy that she didn't give up. From that day on, Lily always remembered to believe in herself.

Once upon a time, there were two best friends. Both were very happy.

One day, one of them was feeling a bit scared. She was about to do something that she was unsure of.

"Will it be okay?" she asked her best friend. 

Her friend looked at her and smiled. "It will be alright," she said. "You can trust me."

The scared one took a deep breath. She knew she could trust her best friend.

Soon, they were back outside and it was very cold. But the scared one felt happy, because her friend had given her courage.

The two ran around in the cold, laughing and playing. Together, they had adventure after adventure, never once forgetting to trust one another. 

In the end, they ended back where they had begun, completely happy and filled with trust in one another.

Once upon a time there were two animals: a fox and a rabbit. They wanted to have a friend they could do things with, especially when they were bored. One day they heard a noise coming from behind a bush. They were a bit scared but they went to take a look.

They saw an owl perched on a branch. The fox and the rabbit said hello to him. The owl said hello back, and then introduced himself. His name was Dorian. The fox and the rabbit were happy to meet such a new friend.

The owl told them that he was writing a novel and asked if they would like to help him. The fox and the rabbit said yes and were excited to work with Dorian. They worked together for many days and soon the novel was ready. 

This story teaches us to be open to meeting new people and to not be afraid of trying new things. Making new friends can make all the difference, and collaborating with them can make our lives more exciting and enjoyable.

One day, a persistent little girl was playing with her favourite toy. Suddenly, she heard the doorbell. She ran to the door to see who it was. When she opened the door, she saw a delivery man with a special package. He smiled at the little girl and said, "This package is for you!" She thanked him and took the package inside.

The little girl was amazed. She opened the package and inside she found a beautiful new toy! She was so happy that she jumped up and down and gave the delivery man a big hug.

The delivery man showed the little girl how to turn on the toy. But, it didn't work. He tried again, but it still wouldn't work. The delivery man was persistent, though and he showed the little girl how to press the buttons in a different order. Finally, the toy worked!

The little girl gave the delivery man a big thank you and hugged him again. She couldn't believe her new toy worked! She said goodbye to the delivery man and ran off to play with her new toy.

The delivery man watched the little girl with a smile on his face. He was glad that he was able to deliver such a special package!

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Pete. He was walking through the farm when he saw a bull. Pete had never seen a bull before. He found it really interesting.

Suddenly, the bull started to yell. Pete was a bit scared and started to run away. But he couldn't help but to turn back and look. He saw the bull was still yelling.

Pete stepped closer and said, "Why are you yelling?"

The bull responded, "I'm a bit mad. You shouldn't have come so close!"

Pete apologized, said his goodbyes, and ran away. He never forgot his interesting experience with the bull who was yelling.

Lila and Ben were playing with their blocks in the living room. They liked to build towers and bridges and castles. They had a lot of fun with their blocks.

Suddenly, the floor started to shake. The blocks fell down and the pictures on the wall moved. Lila and Ben were scared. They did not know what was happening. They heard a loud noise outside. It was an earthquake!

Lila and Ben ran to their mom, who was in the kitchen. She hugged them and told them not to worry. She said the earthquake would stop soon and they would be safe. She said they should go under the table and hold hands.

Lila and Ben did what their mom said. They went under the table and held hands. They felt the table twist and turn, but they did not let go. They were loyal to each other. They knew they would be brave together.

After a while, the earthquake stopped. The floor was still and the noise was gone. Lila and Ben came out from under the table. Their mom checked on them and said they were okay. She said they were very good and smart. She said she was proud of them.

Lila and Ben smiled. They were happy they had their mom and each other. They hugged their mom and thanked her. They said they loved her. They said they loved their blocks too, even if they had to build them again.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toy laser. The laser was red and shiny and it would glow in the dark. Timmy thought it was very interesting.

One day, Timmy took his laser to the park to play with it. He was having so much fun until a big dog came and took his laser away. Timmy was very sad and didn't know what to do.

Suddenly, he saw something interesting. The laser was glowing in the dog's mouth! Timmy ran towards the dog and grabbed his laser back. He was so happy to have his laser back and he ran home to tell his mom all about his adventure.

Once upon a time there was a charming little girl and her father. Every day they liked to play together. One day the little girl had a paper in her hand. She ran to her dad, teasing him. Her dad smiled and said 'let's find something fun to do with the paper'. The little girl agreed.

They thought and thought. Finally, the dad had a fun idea. He taught the little girl how to make different shapes with the paper. She laughed and smiled as she twisted and folded the paper together.

Next, the dad showed her how to make a pretty paper flower. She was so happy that she ran around the house with it in her hand. As she ran she yelled 'Look at my charming flower, daddy!'. Her dad was so proud.

The dad and the little girl had a wonderful time playing together and learning about paper. And from that day on, they made sure to have lots of paper, so they could have fun and make things together.

Once upon a time, there was a tiny girl. She was very brave and loved to play outside. One day, she found a shiny shield.

"That looks pretty," the little girl said.

Suddenly, a silly monster jumped out from behind a bush. The monster grabbed the shield and ran away!

The brave little girl chased after him. When she finally caught him, she tried to pry the shield away.

The monster laughed a silly laugh. "I won't let you have it!"

But the brave little girl didn't give up. She told the monster, "Let me save the shield!"

The monster was touched by the brave girl's words. He smiled and gave her the shield.

The little girl was so happy. She hugged her shiny shield and skipped home. She was so glad to have saved it.

Once upon a time, there was a mole who wanted to have lots of friends. He searched everywhere, but no one seemed to value him. One day, he found a big and sleepy tree in a meadow. The mole watched the tree, and soon he saw ants crawling around the bark.

The mole was so excited! He decided to talk to the ants, and they quickly became friends. Every day, the mole would wake up early and chat with the ants. They played tag, tickled each other, and told stories.

The more the ants and the mole played together, the more the ants valued him. The ant colony even chose the mole to be their leader. As the days passed, the moled enjoyed his new life. He was sure that he was part of something special, and no longer felt sleepy or alone.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play soccer with his friends. They would kick the ball back and forth, trying to score a goal. 

One day, it was very cold outside and the ground was icy. Timmy's friend kicked the ball too hard and it went far away. Timmy knew he had to get the ball back, so he pulled on his warmest coat and went to find it. 

He looked and looked until he finally found the ball stuck in a pile of snow. Timmy pulled and pulled until he finally got the ball out. He was so happy that he ran all the way back to his friends to continue playing soccer. They all cheered when Timmy scored a goal with the ball he had worked so hard to get back. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to draw circles with her dull crayons. Every day, she would draw a circle and show it to her mom. 

One day, Lily saw a big circle in the sky. She looked up and saw a bright, shiny object. She wanted to touch it, so she ran outside. But the object was too high and too far away. 

Suddenly, a loud noise came from the object. It started to come closer and closer. Lily was scared and ran back inside. But the object crashed into her house and everything went black. 

Lily woke up in a hospital bed. Her house was destroyed and her family was gone. She was sad and alone. She wished she never saw the bright, shiny object in the sky.

John was very lazy and he did not like to pick things up. One day he was playing at the park when he saw a bird that was stuck in the fence. John was scared, so he ran to get help. When he got back he saw that a kind man had come and released the bird from the fence. He watched as the bird flew away. John was very happy that the bird was set free. He learned that being kind and helping others was really important. From then on, John was never so lazy. He was always picking up after himself, and helping others in need.

Once there was a mummy, who had wanted to get a special license. The mummy worked very hard to get it, but it wasn't easy. When she finally got the license, she was so happy. However, it was very fragile and she had to be careful.

One day, mummy took the fragile license for a drive. As she drove, she didn't pay attention and she accidentally broke the law. The police saw her and gave her a punishment.

Mummy was very sad and she knew she had done something wrong. She promised never to make the same mistake again. From then on, mummy was very careful and always made sure to obey the law.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tweety. Tweety was always restless and wanted to explore the world. One day, Tweety saw a wire hanging from a tree and decided to learn how to balance on it. 

Tweety flapped its wings and hopped onto the wire. At first, it was hard to balance and Tweety fell off. But Tweety didn't give up and kept trying. After a while, Tweety learned how to balance on the wire without falling off. 

Tweety was so happy and proud of itself for learning something new. It flew around and told all its bird friends about its new skill. From that day on, Tweety would often be found balancing on the wire, showing off its new talent.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside in the garden. One day, he saw a beetle crawling on the ground. Timmy thought the beetle was disgusting, but he wanted to play with it anyway.

Timmy decided to kick the beetle. He kicked it really hard and the beetle went flying into the bushes. Timmy laughed and thought it was funny. But what he didn't know was that the beetle had friends.

Later that day, when Timmy was playing in the garden again, he saw a swarm of beetles coming towards him. They were angry and they wanted revenge. Timmy tried to run away, but the beetles caught him and bit him all over. Timmy learned his lesson and never kicked a beetle again.

The sun was shining in the sky. It was a beautiful day. 

Abby and her mum went to the shop. Abby saw so many things! She especially liked the blue things. She saw blue teddies and blue hats. 

Abby and her mum parted the shelves. They found so many things that Abby liked! She found a blue doll and a blue book. 

Abby was so happy with her new things. She gave her mum a big hug! Then they went home and Abby played with her new blue toys. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Zigzag. Zigzag loved to run and play in the park. One day, Zigzag saw a big twisty slide. He wanted to try it, so he ran up to the slide.

Zigzag twisted and turned as he went down the slide. He went so fast that he fell off at the end. He felt embarrassed because all his friends saw him fall. But his friends did not laugh at him. They ran to help Zigzag get up.

Zigzag's friends told him not to be embarrassed. They all tried the twisty slide, too. They all twisted and turned, just like Zigzag. They had so much fun playing together. And Zigzag learned that it's okay to make mistakes, as long as you have good friends by your side.

Once upon a time there was a fine musician. He was called Robbie and he used to play his instrument every day. One day, he went to the park to play.

As he started playing his instrument, two young childrenâ€”Anna and Jackâ€”came to him. They sat around Robbie and watched him attentively. Anna then asked Robbie: "What kind of music are you playing?"

Robbie smiled at them and said: "I'm playing very nice music!" He then continued to play.

The two children clapped with joy. They started to dance around Robbie to the rhythm of the music.

Robbie was very happy to see them so joyous. He stopped playing and said: "That was so much fun! I'm always happy when children want to play music with me!"

Anna and Jack were delighted. They waved goodbye to Robbie, and ran off to play.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a silly little boy named Timmy. Timmy liked to play with his toys and watch the sunrise every morning. One day, Timmy's mommy asked him to remove his toys from the living room. Timmy didn't want to remove his toys, so he threw a tantrum.

The next morning, Timmy woke up early to watch the sunrise. But when he looked outside, he saw that the sky was covered in dark clouds. Timmy was sad because he couldn't see the beautiful sunrise. He decided to play with his toys instead.

As Timmy was playing, he accidentally knocked over a vase. The vase broke into a million pieces and Timmy got hurt. Timmy's mommy came running and saw what had happened. She was very upset with Timmy for not removing his toys and for breaking the vase. Timmy felt very bad and cried.

From that day on, Timmy learned to listen to his mommy and to always remove his toys when asked. And even though the sunrise was still hidden behind the clouds, Timmy knew that he could still have fun playing with his toys as long as he was careful.

Once upon a time there was a big blackboard in a classroom. It was so big that it almost reached the ceiling! The teacher had been writing on the blackboard all morning when something amazing happened. The blackboard started to talk! The teacher was very surprised and told the students to mind the blackboard.

The students were very excited and listened carefully. The blackboard said, "I am here to teach you something very special. I will tell you all a story that will help you to understand things better". The students were all eager to learn what the blackboard had to say.

The blackboard started to tell a story about a small bird that had a very big heart. The bird wanted to help all the other birds in the forest and make them happy. The blackboard said, "Remember the bird and the big heart. Always put your own big heart first and help others".

At the end of the story, the teacher smiled and thanked the blackboard for the lesson. The students all said that they had learned something very important and thanked the blackboard too. The blackboard waved goodbye and disappeared.

From that day on, the students always remembered to mind their own big hearts and to help others. It was a lesson that they would never forget!

Once upon a time, there was a pale race. Two runners were racing to the finish line. They were both running very fast! As the runners came closer to the finish line, the pale race was able to recognize them. It was their best friends! They both crossed the finish line together. The pale race cheered loudly as they reached the finish line. Everyone was so happy they could finish the race. They hugged each other to celebrate their victory. The pale race was so excited that they won the race together. It was a great day for everyone!

Once there was a mom and a dad and a little boy who was three years old. His mom said to him, "It's time to go on vacation!"

The little boy was so excited! He asked his mom, "Where are we going on vacation?"

Mom said, "We're going to a place with thick green trees and a big pond."

Later that day, the mom and dad and the little boy went on vacation. The dad said, "Let's play by the pond and be careful to not get too close."

The mom cheered, "Yes! Let's make sure we protect each other"

The little boy led the way. He laughed when he saw the big, thick trees. He ran around and felt so happy!

Maybe next time, they can go on vacation again!

Once upon a time, there was an old man who lived in a small house by the sea. He loved to fish and had a hook that he used every day. One day, he went out to fish and caught a big fish. When he tried to take the hook out, it got stuck in the fish's mouth. 

The old man tried and tried to get the hook out, but it wouldn't budge. Just then, a little boy came by and saw the old man struggling. "What's wrong?" asked the boy. The old man explained the problem and the boy said, "I know how to help! Shut your eyes and count to three." 

The old man did as the boy said and when he opened his eyes, the hook was out of the fish's mouth. "Wow, thank you so much!" said the old man. "You're welcome," said the boy. "I'm glad I could help." And with that, the boy ran off to play, leaving the old man with a big smile on his face.

Once upon a time there was an infant who could think and design things all on its own. One day it made a plan to fly away from its family. So it designed a kite with two strings and one big wheel.

The infant gathered materials to build its kite. But when it was done, it realized it couldn't fly the kite on its own. Suddenly, it heard the sound of the big wheel spinning and spinning faster and faster. Then off it flew, high up into the sky.

The infant sailed through the sky, feeling independent. It waved goodbye to its family and smiled as it went higher and higher. But as the sun went down, it became tired and decided to go back home.

The infant flew back down and landed safely near the home. It was happy to be back home and felt proud of the way it had designed the kite and been independent for a short time. From then on, it never stopped dreaming of what it could create and do.

Once there was a girl named Sarah. She was three years old and loved going to the movies. Every week her parents would supply her with tickets to the movie theater.

One night Sarah and her parents went to see an amazing movie about a big blue whale. They watched the whale sing and dance for the whole audience. It was so much fun!

After the movie, Sarah was so excited she couldn't even speak. She just kept smiling and jumping up and down. Her parents were happy too because they could see how much she enjoyed the movie.

Sarah would never forget that amazing movie. From then on she always begged her parents to supply her with tickets to the movie theater. And they were happy to oblige!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and explore the world around her. One day, she found a big knot in a tree. It was so big, she couldn't untie it no matter how hard she tried. 

Lily's friend, a little bird named Tweetie, flew over to see what she was doing. "What's wrong, Lily?" Tweetie asked. "I can't untie this knot," Lily replied. "I don't believe I can do it." 

Tweetie hopped onto the knot and began to peck at it with his beak. After a few minutes, the knot came loose! Lily was so happy and dizzy with excitement that she hugged Tweetie tightly. "Thank you, Tweetie! You're the best friend ever," she said. From then on, Lily knew that with a little help from her friends, she could do anything she believed in.

Once upon a time there was a farmer who owned a bull. The bull was very special, but the farmer was a bit jealous. So, one day, the farmer decided to take the bull to wander around the farm.

The bull was very happy. He wandered around and ate some juicy grass. He was so content that he even stopped to have a nap in the sun. But then, he heard a noise. It was loud and made him jump.

It was the farmer. He was mad and was shouting. The farmer was jealous that the bull was so enjoying himself. He yelled at the bull to come back. The bull ran back to the farmer and the farmer put him on his farm.

But, the bull knew he was meant to wander and would often find ways to wander around the farm during the day. He was always happy when he did this and so the farmer was always jealous.

The end.

Jill liked to knit. She had a big ball of wool and two sticks. She made a scarf for her dad. It was red and blue and long. She was proud of her scarf.

But one day, Jill left her scarf outside. It rained and rained. The scarf got wet and dirty. It was filthy. Jill was sad. She did not want to give her dad a filthy scarf.

She asked her mom for help. Her mom said they could wash the scarf. They put the scarf in a bucket of warm water and soap. They rubbed and scrubbed the scarf. They rinsed and wrung the scarf. They hung the scarf on a line to dry.

The next day, the scarf was clean and dry. It was not filthy anymore. It was bright and soft. Jill was happy. She had improved her scarf. She wrapped the scarf around her dad's neck. He smiled and hugged her. He said he loved her scarf. Jill felt warm and cozy. She loved her dad.

Once upon a time, there was a nice man who lived in the woods. He had a garden and a rake. Every day he would take his rake and tidy up his garden. He loved to look at the colourful flowers that grew in his garden because they were rare and very pretty. 

One day, the man heard a noise coming from outside his garden. He looked through the window and saw a little rabbit hopping around. The rabbit looked at the man and hopped close to him. It made a little noise and said "please".

The man was so happy to see the little rabbit. He opened the door and let the rabbit come into his garden. The man took out his rake and gave it to the rabbit. The rabbit was so excited. 

The man and the rabbit played together in the garden for the whole day. The man raked the garden and the rabbit hopped around him. When the sun went down, the man said goodbye to the rabbit and wished it good luck. 

The man and the rabbit will always remember their wonderful day together.

Once upon a time, there was a wise lady who lived in a small village by the sea. Every day, the lady would go for a walk by the beach and enjoy the sound of the waves rolling in. One day, a surprise arrived for the lady. It was a small fish in a bucket! The lady was so happy and she soon became known for being kind and wise in the village. 

From then on, whenever anyone had a problem, they would come to the wise lady for help. The lady always knew the best advice to give. 

One day, the village filled with happiness when a message arrived saying that a king was coming to visit. Everybody was excited, but the wise lady wasn't worried. She said it didn't matter who was coming, as long as they were kind.

The lady was right. When the king arrived, he was a kind and generous ruler who brought gifts for the people of the village. The wise lady was proud and everyone learned a valuable lesson from her wisdom: it's important to be kind to everyone no matter who they are.

It was a sunny day and Anna was visiting her grandmother. Anna's grandmother was very proud of her and said, "Anna, you are amazing! You will go to university soon, and it will be so much fun!" 

Anna nervously nodded and asked,"What is university, grandma?" 

Her grandmother smiled and said, "It's a place full of wonderful teachers who pour knowledge into your brain. It's amazing! They teach you so many things and you learn so much. That's why university is so special." 

Anna's eyes shined with excitement and she said, "Wow, that sounds amazing! I can't wait to go to university!"

One day, Rita wanted to go to the gym. She asked her mum if she could go. Her mum said it was ok and she could go as long as she promised to look after herself.

Rita was so excited! She put on her favourite purple t-shirt and her brightly coloured sneakers and then she took a taxi with her mum to the gym.

When they arrived, Rita's mum told her that she had to be careful and stay away from the heavy weights and machinery that the gym had. Rita promised to listen and her mum gave her permission to start.

Rita was very happy. She jumped, skipped and crawled all around the gym. Whenever she felt like it, she stopped to do some stretches or hop on the trampoline. Everyone at the gym was impressed with how well she was listening to her mum and staying away from the weights and machines.

After a few hours, Rita and her mum said goodbye to everyone at the gym and went home. Rita fell asleep on the taxi ride back and had lots of fun dreams. Every time she thought of the gym and all the fun she had, she smiled from ear to ear. It was a day to remember!

Once upon a time there was a very busy school. In the big room there was a blackboard.

The teacher looked around the room at all the students. She was very busy. She said to the students, "Let's all look at the blackboard".

The students looked at the blackboard and they saw lots of different colours and shapes. They were very curious.

The teacher said, "Let's draw some shapes on the blackboard to make it look nice".

So the students got out their pencils and they all started to draw on the blackboard. They were all very busy.

When they were finished, everyone looked at the blackboard and it was full of different colours and shapes. They all smiled because they had made a very colourful picture.

Once upon a time, there was a happy family. They went to a restaurant to eat some food. The waiter gave them a paper with pictures of food on it. This was called a menu. The family looked at the menu and chose what they wanted to eat. They then ordered their food from the waiter. 

The little girl in the family was very enthusiastic about her food. She loved the way it looked and smelled. When it arrived, she ate it all up and said it was delicious. The family finished their food and paid the bill. They left the restaurant feeling full and happy. The little girl asked her parents if they could come back to the restaurant again soon.

Once upon a time there was a clumsy bear. The clumsy bear wanted to travel and see the world. He had a special crib that he used for travelling. So the clumsy bear gathered up his crib, and he started to travel. He went far and wide - through forests, mountains, and deserts - and he saw lots of amazing things. He had lots of fun! Eventually, the clumsy bear came back to his crib and it was time to go home. He was tired from all of his travelling, so he snuggled into his crib and fell fast asleep. The end.

Mommy was at the store and she bought a very special dessert. Little Jake couldn't wait to have some of the dessert. When Mommy got home, he asked if he could have some. Mommy said, â€œYes, but you have to eat your dinner first.â€

Little Jake was so happy and he quickly finished eating his dinner. Then he asked, â€œCan I have the dessert now?â€

Mommy said, â€œYes, but only one bite.â€ Little Jake was very lucky and he quickly took a big bite of the dessert.

Then Mommy said, â€œStop! That's enough!â€ Little Jake stopped and smiled because he knew he had been lucky to get such a delicious dessert.

Once there was an ignorant boy. His name was Tim. All day long, Tim wanted someone to play with him, but no one wanted to.

One day he was walking by an old house. He heard a noise coming from inside. It sounded like someone was singing. Tim decided to kneel and peek through the window.

Inside the house, he saw an old woman. She was singing and stirring a pot of tea with a spoon. Tim felt so happy to find someone to talk to, he stopped wishing for a friend.

The old woman looked at Tim and realized that he was a very sad boy. She invited him in and they talked while they drank tea.

The old woman could see that Tim was feeling much better and she told him that he was never alone.

From that day on, whenever Tim felt lonely, he would kneel outside the old woman's house and she would invite him in for tea.

Once upon a time, there was a man who found an old rope. He wanted to use the rope to swing across a river and have fun. But when he grabbed the rope, he realised it was dead! The rope had been sitting in the sun for too long and it had all dried up and become dead.

This made the man very sad. He had been so excited to swing across the river and now he couldn't. He sat there and felt very disappointed and angry. 

But then he thought about something. He thought about how it was his own fault for not paying attention when he found the rope. He looked up at the sky, thanked the night and asked for forgiveness. 

Then, the man did something amazing! He picked up a long branch, made a new rope, and used it to swing across the river. When he reached the other side he shouted out with joy!

And the man learned a valuable lesson that dayâ€” always forgive someone if they make a mistake. Even if it feels hard.

Once upon a time there was a happy bear named Max. Max always tried to do what was right. One day he was walking in the forest, when he came to a dark and scary cave. Max wanted to go in, but he was a little afraid.

He paused for a moment and then decided to go inside. Inside the cave Max saw a fast, slimy snake. The snake told Max to come closer. Max thought this was a bad idea, but he was too slow and the snake caught him! He was having a nightmare.

Luckily for Max, he used his good sense and remembered to just say no! Max moved away from the snake and it was gone. Max decided that he had learned a lesson. If he ever came to a dark and scary place again, he would remember to be extra careful and never let anyone rush him. 

Max learned the important thing is to always use your good sense and take things slow.

Once upon a time, there was a hungry hunter. He had been walking in the woods for what felt like hours and it seemed like he had not seen any animals. He was so hungry that he decided to keep going and see if he could find something to eat.

The hunter kept walking until he reached a clearing. He saw lots of animals running around, but he didn't know how to catch them. He guessed that he could try and find something to hunt with.

He looked around and saw a big stick lying on the ground. He thought to himself that it was a perfect hunting tool. He quickly grabbed it and began stalking the animals.

Unfortunately, no matter how hard he tried, the hunter could not catch anything. He was so hungry that he felt like he was going to faint. In the end, he had to give up and go home with nothing.

Once there was a beautiful little girl called Lisa. She never stopped smiling and enjoyed the world around her. One day, while out in the garden she found a very special gem. It was so shiny and sparkly. Lisa was so excited and put the gem in her pocket. 

That night, when it was time for bed, Lisa heard a strange noise outside her window. She looked out and saw something magical. It was a big, green frog and it began to jump around. Suddenly the frog jumped up and down and Lisa saw that it had something small and sparkly in its mouth. It was her gem! 

The frog had found the gem and wanted to give it back to Lisa. Lisa thanked the frog and gave it a big hug. After the frog had gone, Lisa looked at the gem and saw that it was still twinkling in the moonlight. 

Lisa put the gem in her pocket and went to bed with a peaceful feeling. Every day she would go outside and enjoy the Spring weather, and she would think of the magical frog who gave her the special gem.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She was three years old and very curious. One day, Lily saw an elevator. She wanted to get inside so she could go up and look around. She asked her mom if she could get in and her mom said "yes".

Lily was so excited and she ordered the elevator to go up. The elevator went up slowly and Lily looked out the window to see the pretty view.

When the elevator got to the top, the door opened and Lily jumped out. But then the door closed and the elevator started to go down without Lily inside! She was so scared and started to cry.

Lily's mom heard her crying and ran to the elevator to open the door. When she opened the door, she said "I'm sorry Lily". Lily was very happy to be back with her mom.

Ben and Mia were friends who liked to play with paint. They had many colors of paint and brushes and paper. They liked to make pictures of animals and flowers and cars.

One day, they went to the park with their moms. They brought their paint and paper and brushes. They found a nice spot under a big tree and started to paint. Ben painted a lion with a big mane and Mia painted a butterfly with many dots.

"Look at my lion!" Ben said. "He is very strong and loud. He can scare anyone."

"Look at my butterfly!" Mia said. "She is very pretty and gentle. She can fly anywhere."

They showed their paintings to each other and smiled. They were proud of their work.

But then, a big wind came and blew their paintings away. They ran after them, but they were too fast. The wind carried them to a pond where some ducks were swimming. The ducks saw the paintings and thought they were food. They pecked at them and tore them apart.

Ben and Mia were very sad. They had worked hard on their paintings and now they were gone. They felt like crying.

Their moms came and saw what happened. They hugged them and said, "It's okay. It was an accident. You can make new paintings another day. Don't be embarrassed. The ducks didn't know any better. They were just hungry."

Ben and Mia nodded. They knew their moms were right. They wiped their tears and smiled. They still had their paint and brushes and paper. They could make new pictures of lions and butterflies and anything they wanted. They decided to paint something else. They looked around and saw an empty bench. They had an idea.

They ran to the bench and started to paint on it. They painted their names and hearts and stars and rainbows. They made the bench very colorful and bright. They were happy again.

They showed their bench to their moms and said, "Look at our bench! We made it beautiful. We are sorry we lost our paintings, but we made something new. Do you like it?"

Their moms looked at the bench and smiled. They said, "We love it. You are very creative and brave. You turned something sad into something happy. You are amazing."

Ben and Mia hugged their moms and said, "Thank you. You are amazing too. We love you."

They sat on their bench and enjoyed the sun and the breeze and the ducks. They were friends who liked to play with paint. They had many colors of paint and brushes and paper. And they had a bench that was theirs.

Once upon a time, there was a woman named Sue. She lived in a small house with her dog, Max. Max was an obedient dog. He always listened to Sue and did what she told him to do.

One day, Sue and Max went to the park. They saw a big, red ball. Sue kicked the ball and it started to rise high in the sky. Max was very happy and jumped to catch the ball. The sun was shining and the sky was blue.

Sue and Max played with the ball all day. They had a lot of fun. When the sun went down, they went back to their small house. They were tired but happy. Sue and Max were the best of friends.

Once upon a time, there was a clumsy bear. He loved going to the stream to play and splash. One day, he wanted to show his friends his swimming skills and stepped into the stream. He was clumsy, and soon lost his balance and fell into the water. 

Seeing this, his friends laughed, but the bear was sad that he couldn't show them his skills. His friends comforted him and said, "It's ok, bear. Do not worry."

The bear tried to take another step and suddenly remembered something. He said, "Wait, I remember now! I need to go on my tippy-toes when I go into the water. That way, I won't fall again." 

So the bear went on tiptoes, and he and his friends splashed around happily in the stream. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a naughty spirit who liked to steal things. He would sneak around and take things from other people. One day, he tried to steal some candy from a little girl. But just as he was about to grab the candy, he was stopped by a giant.

The giant was very angry and he shouted at the naughty spirit. The spirit was so scared that he ran away as fast as he could. But no matter where he went, the giant followed him. So, the naughty spirit had to give the candy back to the little girl.

The naughty spirit learned his lesson that day. He never stole anything again, and he always tried to be nice instead.

Once there was a bald man. He had no fur covering his head. He always felt sad and alone.

One day he heard something in the woods. He went to explore, and found a big, brown bear! The bear had soft, brown fur.

The man enjoyed looking at the bear's fur. He ran his hand over it, and it was so soft! He was delighted.

The bald man and the bear played in the woods together, and he really enjoyed it. The man was so happy, he started to smile and laugh with glee.

The man and the bear were now friends, and the man had the fur he was looking for â€” it was the bear's fur that made him so happy. Together, they played for hours until the sun set.

Little Maria was playing with her teddy bear in the park. She always made sure his buttons were secure. All of a sudden, one of them flew away! Maria looked around and panicked because she couldn't find the button. 

An old lady saw Maria and noticed her problem. She said, "Hello there, why are you so upset?"

Maria replied, "I've lost my button. I was playing and it flew away!"

The nosy old lady smiled and grabbed her walking stick. She said, "Let's look for it together, shall we?"

They searched around and soon enough, found the button! Maria hugged the old lady in excitement.

The old lady said, "Please don't forget to fasten it back to your teddy bear! And remember to never lose it again."

Maria said, "Thank you! I will never lose it again!"

The old lady waved goodbye as she left and Maria said goodbye too. She fastened the button back and thought that the nosy old lady was very nice. From then on, Maria was more careful not to lose her button.

One day, there was a little girl named Daisy. Daisy was three years old and loved exploring. 

She was playing in her garden one sunny day and she admired the beautiful flowers, the butterflies and the trees. As she walked around, she came to the stairs, which were colorful. Daisy thought they looked so fancy and she wanted to try walking up them. 

Daisy took her first step and admired how pretty the stairs were with all the colorful hues. Then she walked up one more step and admired how the steps changed color as she went. After Daisy went up a few more steps, she reached the top and felt very proud of herself. 

Daisy admired the stairs until she got to the end and wanted to go down again. Step by step, Daisy slowly but surely walked down the stairs, admiring the colors along the way. 

Once Daisy made it back to the bottom of the stairs, she appreciated how pretty and colorful the stairs were. She smiled with delight and went off on her next exploration.

Johnny was walking in the park and it was a very cold day. He felt the icy wind on his cheeks. He shivered and his teeth chattered. Johnny stopped and looked up. He saw a big tree with lots of peppers growing over it. They were a bright red color and hanging off the branches. Johnny smiled; he loved peppers.

He picked a pepper off the tree and put it in his pocket. Then he ran to the pond nearby. He saw lots of ducks swimming around and he smiled. Johnny dipped his finger in the pond and it was very, very cold - icy cold. He giggled and all the ducks started to quack. He put his hands in the icy cold water and gave the ducks a little splash.

Johnny was so happy and he laughed and smiled. He stayed for a bit more, watching the ducks swim around and around. Then he went home, with a big smile on his face, his pocket full of peppers.

Tom and Lily were playing in the living room. They saw a big vase on the table. It was shiny and blue. They wanted to touch it.

"Let's see the vase," Tom said.

"OK, but be careful," Lily said.

They climbed on the chairs and reached for the vase. But they were too small and clumsy. The vase fell off the table and broke into pieces. They heard a loud noise.

"Oh no!" Tom and Lily said.

They were scared. They saw their mom coming from the kitchen. She looked angry.

"What did you do?" she asked.

"We're sorry, mom. We wanted to see the vase. It was shiny and blue. But it fell and broke," Tom said.

Mom sighed. She was not happy. She picked up the pieces and threw them in the trash. She told Tom and Lily to go to their room.

Tom and Lily felt sad. They went to their room. They saw their snowman toy on the bed. It was white and soft. They liked it.

"Let's play with the snowman," Lily said.

"OK, but don't let it melt," Tom said.

They hugged the snowman and pretended it was winter. They forgot about the vase. They had fun.

One day, Jenny and her family went to the barn. When they arrived, Jenny's mom and dad smiled. Jenny saw a big fake cow. She laughed a lot.

Jenny's dad noticed the cow and said, "Let's laugh together for this funny cow."

Jenny agreed and laughed even more.

Then Jenny's family saw a fake sheep. Jenny loved it and started laughing again.

But when they noticed a fake pig, they all laughed together. Jenny giggled the loudest.

At the end of the day, Jenny, her mom and dad all laughed while they walked away from the barn.

Mum and Dad were in the kitchen cleaning up after dinner. The little boy was excited as he used his toy broom to help. After putting away the dishes, Mum closed the cupboard and sighed. 

"It's so quiet", she said. 

The little boy smiled. "Yes, complete silence!" he said. 

Mum suddenly looked sad. "Oh sweetheart, why don't you go and play outside now?" she asked. 

The little boy stopped smiling and hung his head. He looked ashamed. 

"But why, Mum?" 

Mum gently put her hand on his shoulder. "I just think it would make you happy, sweetheart. Plus, Dad and I need some time to ourselves." 

The little boy nodded and ran outside. He shut the door behind him and forced a big smile. He was a little bit ashamed, but glad he still had a chance to play outside. 

The silence in the kitchen felt even bigger without him, but Mum and Dad were happy, knowing the little boy was happy too.

Molly was a young girl who loved to write. One day she decided to write a story about a jellyfish. She grabbed a piece of paper and a gray crayon. She started writing about how the jellyfish sparkled in the sun. She drew pictures of it in the water with the gray crayon. Molly wanted to write more, so she added that the jellyfish had little tentacles that moved around. When she finished writing, Molly smiled because she had written a wonderful story about a jellyfish.

Once there was a lively girl named Lucy. She liked to throw things when she played. One day, Lucy wanted to try something different. She decided that she would throw hugs instead of balls. So she grabbed a big hug and threw it towards her brother.

Her brother was so surprised. He quickly caught the hug and hugged it back. He smiled at Lucy and laughed. Then they started to throw all kinds of hugs. They giggled and laughed while they tossed them around.

The game was so much fun, they kept going and going. Eventually, they got so tired from throwing hugs that they both decided to take a break. Lucy gave her brother a big hug and said, "I had so much fun!" Her brother hugged her back, and they both smiled happily.

Once upon a time, there was a blue bird named Bobby. Bobby liked to fly high in the sky. One day, while he was flying, he saw a big cloud. The cloud was white and fluffy, just like cotton.

Bobby wanted to play with the cloud, so he flew closer. As he got near, he saw a little girl named Lily. Lily was sitting on the cloud, laughing and clapping her hands. "Hi Bobby!" she said. "Do you want to play with me on the cloud?"

Bobby nodded his head and tried to land on the cloud. But it was so soft and slippery that he couldn't stay on it. Bobby started to slip and slide all over the cloud, and Lily laughed. "Don't worry, Bobby," she said. "I'll help you."

Lily held out her hand, and Bobby grabbed it. Together, they played on the cloud, laughing and having fun. After a while, the sun began to set, and Bobby had to fly home. He said goodbye to Lily, and they promised to play on the cloud again soon.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to draw and paint all day long. She was very creative and made beautiful pictures for her family and friends. 

One day, Lily's brother came into her room and started to tease her. He said her drawings were silly and not good enough. Lily felt very sad and didn't want to draw anymore. 

But then, her mom came in and saw what was happening. She told Lily that her drawings were amazing and that she should never let anyone make her feel bad about her art. She encouraged Lily to keep being creative and to never give up on her passion. 

From that day on, Lily made a loop of her drawings and hung them up in her room. She felt proud of her art and knew that she should never let anyone bring her down. The moral of the story is to always believe in yourself and never let anyone tease you into giving up on your dreams.

Once upon a time, there was a girl. She had the most reliable toy car in the world. One day, she decided to take it for a drive. She drove and drove until she saw a big blueberry bush. She knew she wanted to eat the blueberries, so she parked her car and went closer to have a look. Suddenly, something amazing happened. Hundreds of little blueberries were ripe, just waiting to be picked. She was so excited that she filled her pockets with the blueberries before getting back in her car and driving away. The girl was so happy with her reliable toy car for taking her to the special blueberry bush!

One day, Tim and Sam went to the park. It was a sunny day, but the wind was icy. They wore warm hats and big coats. Tim had a bag with him. In the bag was a jar of sweet red jam. Tim's mom made the jam for them.

At the park, they saw a little bird. The bird looked cold and hungry. Tim said, "We should care for the bird. Let's give it some jam." Sam agreed, "Yes, let's help the bird. It needs us."

They opened the jar of jam and put some on a small plate. The bird hopped closer and ate the jam. It looked happy now. Tim and Sam felt good because they cared for the little bird. They played in the park all day and went home with big smiles on their faces.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who wanted to explore the world. She wanted to see new places and meet new people.

One day, she decided to go on an adventure. She went to the airport, hopped on a plane, and flew away.

The little girl was so excited! She looked out of the window and saw all kinds of new things. The sky was so blue, and the clouds were soft and fluffy.

After a long time, the plane landed. The little girl realized that she had explored a whole new world. She was so excited.

The little girl thanked the plane for taking her on the adventure and headed back home. She knew that now she could explore the world and never stop dreaming.

Lily and Ben were playing with their toys in the living room. They had a lot of fun making noises and pretending to be animals. But after a while, they started to feel tired and bored.

"Can we watch TV?" Ben asked his mom, who was reading a book on the couch.

"No, TV is not good for you before bed. How about we read a story instead?" Mom said, putting down her book.

"Okay, what story?" Lily said, yawning.

Mom picked up a big book with colorful pictures. "How about this one? It's called The Empty Pot. It's about a boy who wants to grow a flower for the king."

Lily and Ben liked flowers, so they nodded and cuddled up to Mom. Mom opened the book and began to read.

The story was about a boy named Ping, who loved to plant seeds and watch them grow. One day, the king announced that he would give a seed to every child in the kingdom, and whoever grew the most beautiful flower would be the next king. Ping was very excited and took his seed home. He planted it in a pot and watered it every day. But nothing happened. The pot stayed empty.

Ping was sad and confused. He wondered why his seed did not grow. He tried different things, like changing the soil, moving the pot, and singing to the seed. But nothing worked. The pot was still empty.

Meanwhile, all the other children had beautiful flowers in their pots. They laughed at Ping and called him a failure. Ping felt ashamed and wanted to hide. He thought about throwing away his pot, but he decided to keep it. He had done his best, and he was not a liar.

The day came when the king asked all the children to bring their pots to the palace. Ping carried his empty pot, feeling very nervous. He saw the other children with their flowers, and he felt very small. He wondered what the king would say.

When he reached the palace, he saw the king sitting on a throne, surrounded by guards and advisors. The king looked at all the pots and smiled. He said, "I have a question for you, children. Do you know what kind of seed I gave you?"

The children looked at each other, puzzled. They did not know.

The king said, "I gave you all boiled seeds. They could not grow. I wanted to see who would be honest and brave enough to bring me an empty pot. And I see only one child who did that. Ping, you are the one I choose to be the next king. You have shown me that you have a good heart and a strong character. Come, sit by my side."

Ping was shocked and happy. He could not believe it. He walked up to the king and bowed. The king hugged him and put a crown on his head. The other children were amazed and ashamed. They realized that they had cheated and lied. They apologized to Ping and the king.

Ping forgave them and said, "Thank you, your majesty, for this honor. I will try to be a good king, like you. And I will always remember the lesson of the empty pot."

Mom closed the book and said, "The end. Did you like the story, children?"

Lily and Ben nodded and clapped. They said, "Yes, Mom, we liked it very much. It was a good story. We learned that honesty is the best policy."

Mom smiled and kissed them. She said, "I'm glad you liked it. And I'm proud of you for being honest and brave, too. Now, it's time for bed. Let's go brush your teeth and put on your pajamas."

Lily and Ben agreed and followed Mom to the bathroom. They brushed their teeth and put on their pajamas. Then they went to their bedroom and got into their beds. Mom tucked them in and turned off the light.

"Good night, Mom. We love you," Lily and Ben said.

"Good night, my sweeties. I love you, too," Mom said.

Lily and Ben closed their eyes and fell asleep, dreaming of flowers and kings.

Once upon a time, there were two friends called Mary and Bill. Mary and Bill both loved to rub. Every day they would rub together in rhythm. 

Soon, Mary and Bill became very popular. Everyone wanted to join in their rubs. They had so much fun rubbing together, and their rhythm was perfect! 

Their popularity soon spread across the town. People far and wide could hear Mary and Bill's rhythm. People from all around the world started coming to watch and rub with them. 

Mary and Bill were so happy that their rubs had made them so popular. They taught all the people who came to join them, and even taught them how to rub in rhythm. 

Mary and Bill's rubs were a hit and everyone loved it. Even to this day, people are still enjoying the fun rubs that these two friends started!

Once upon a time, there was a fat deer. He went to the park to play. He looked around and noticed a small pond. He wanted to take a closer look, so he walked over to it and started to poke the water with his hoof. Suddenly, a huge fish jumped out and splashed the deer. The deer was so scared that he ran away as fast as he could. He never went back to that pond again. He learned his lesson: never poke a pond!

Once upon a time, there was a brave knight. He had a shiny shield that he loved to show off. One day, the knight went on an adventure and his shield got broken. He felt sad and restless because he didn't know how to fix it. 

But then, he met a kind wizard who knew how to fix things. The wizard used his magic to fix the shield and make it shiny again. The knight was very happy and thanked the wizard. 

After that, the knight continued on his adventure with his newly fixed shield. He felt proud and strong with it by his side. And whenever he felt restless, he would just look at his shield and feel better. The end.

Once there was a jolly little girl named Lucy. She loved picking flowers in the garden. Every Sunday she would gather the prettiest poppies she could find. She admired their bright, happy colours and enjoyed giving them to her mum and dad.

One day Lucy was gathering so many poppies that a tiny rabbit appeared. Lucy was so happy and shouted, "Hello!" The little bunny hopped around Lucy's feet and asked if he could help her. Lucy invited the bunny to join her in gathering poppies. Together they filled Lucy's basket with flowers.

When the sun started to go down, Lucy and the bunny said their goodbyes and Lucy returned home with her basket of poppies. She gave them to her parents and showed them the bunny she had met. They were all very excited and said it had been a jolly adventure. Lucy gave the bunny a special poppy before saying goodbye and she promised to come back again soon.

Once upon a time there was a tall navy ship gliding gracefully through the sea. On board were two children, Pat and Chris. 

Pat said to Chris, "I want to spread my arms wide like a navy ship." 
Chris said, "Go ahead, Pat. It'll look cool." 

So, Pat spread his arms wide like a navy ship and he started spinning around and around the deck of the ship. He spun so fast that he felt like he was flying through the air! 

Chris laughed at Pat and said, "Stop spinning!" 
But Pat just smiled and said, "Spinning makes me feel so tall!" 

So Pat kept spinning around the deck of the ship and Chris kept laughing. Then the two children went inside with the sun setting in the background.

Once upon a time, there were two good friends, Ben and Sam. They loved to be together and often joined their two hands to make a frame. Ben and Sam felt the frame was very delicate, and only wanted to use it for special things.

One day, the friends decided to join the frame around a pretty flower in their garden. The flower looked beautiful inside the delicate frame and the friends decided to pick it and show it to everyone in the neighborhood.

Ben and Sam walked through the town holding the framed flower, and everyone they saw said it was the most beautiful flower they had ever seen. Pretty soon, the whole town was filled with framed flowers, and everyone was joining hands to create their own delicate frames. Ben and Sam smiled at each other, proud of what they had done.

Once there was a boy called Paul. Paul was three years old and had a very precious wallet. Every time Paul saw it he felt so grateful.

One day Paul decided to take his wallet to the store to buy an ice-cream. He was so excited but on arrival he realised he had left his wallet at home. He felt so disappointed and quickly realised he had to go home without his ice-cream.

When he arrived home he was very relieved to find his wallet on the kitchen table. He laughed and said out loud, "Phew, I was really missing my wallet!". 

Paul was very happy and grateful to have his wallet back, and from then onwards he was very careful with it.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his friends, but he was always afraid of new people. One day, Timmy's mother gave him a mask to wear. The mask made Timmy feel like a superhero, and he felt brave enough to talk to new people.

One day, Timmy met a new friend named Billy. Billy was very intelligent and knew a lot of things that Timmy didn't know. Timmy was amazed by how much Billy knew, and he wanted to be as smart as him. So, Timmy asked Billy to teach him new things.

Billy was happy to teach Timmy, and soon Timmy became very intelligent too. Timmy realized that wearing a mask made him feel brave, but being intelligent made him feel even better. Timmy learned that it's important to change how you feel, but it's even more important to change who you are on the inside.

Once upon a time, there was a scared squirrel. He was looking for a place to hide. He saw a tree and quickly scampered up it. But he was not alone, there were other squirrels there too! They were all part of a family. The scared squirrel felt safe and happy with the family of squirrels.

They played games and ate nuts together. Every morning the squirrels would part ways, each going off to do their own thing. But every evening, the squirrels always came back to the same tree.

The scared squirrel felt comfortable with the family. He was not so scared anymore. He was happy living with the squirrel family. The other squirrels never made him feel scared. He was glad to be a part of the family.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who was 3 years old. She had an aunt who always cared for her. Every day, her aunt would take her to the park, cuddle her and tell her stories.

One morning, Lily asked her aunt if she could go to the park. Her aunt said it was too cold to go outside, but they could play a funny game inside. Her aunt made a big surprise - she gave Lily a new teddy bear. Lily was very happy, she said thank you and hugged her aunt gratefully. 

The next day, Lily asked to go to the park again, but her aunt said it was still too cold to play outside. She had another surprise: a blanket that she made for Lily. Now Lily could cuddle with the teddy bear and keep warm. Lily hugged her aunt and thanked her again.

Lily learned that when things are difficult, her aunt cares. She was happy and grateful for her aunt's love and attention. Lily was sure that every day with her aunt would be filled with fun and surprises.

Lily and Sam liked to play a game with their white balloons. They would blow them up and then release them in the air. They would watch them fly and make funny noises. Sometimes they would try to catch them before they fell down.

One day, they went to the park with their mom and dad. They brought their white balloons and played their game. They had a lot of fun. But then, a big wind came and took their balloons away. They ran after them, but they were too fast.

"Mom, dad, help!" Lily cried. "Our balloons are gone!"

"Don't worry, sweetie," mom said. "We can get you new ones."

"But we liked those ones," Sam said. "They were our friends."

Dad hugged them and said, "I know, but sometimes things happen that we can't control. The balloons are free now. Maybe they will find new friends in the sky."

Lily and Sam looked up and saw their white balloons getting smaller and smaller. They waved goodbye and said, "We love you, balloons. Have fun."

Then they smiled and went back to play with their mom and dad. They knew they would always remember their white balloon game.

Tom and Mia like to play with their toys. They have many toys, but their favorite is the jet. The jet is big and red and makes a loud noise. They pretend to fly the jet around the room and go to different places.

One day, Tom and Mia find a seed in the garden. They wonder what it is. They ask their mom. She says it is a sunflower seed. She says if they plant it in a pot and water it, it will grow into a beautiful flower.

Tom and Mia are excited. They want to see the flower. They get a pot and some soil and plant the seed. They water it every day and put it near the window. They watch the seed every day, but nothing happens.

"Mom, why is the seed not growing?" Tom asks.

"It takes time, honey. You have to be patient. The seed needs sun and water and love to grow." Mom says.

Tom and Mia nod. They keep watering the seed and giving it love. They also play with their jet and have fun.

After many days, they see a small green thing coming out of the soil. They are happy. They see the seed is growing. They watch it grow bigger and bigger every day. They see it has a stem and leaves and a bud.

"Look, Mia, the seed is growing a flower!" Tom says.

"Yes, Tom, it is! I wonder what color it will be." Mia says.

They wait for the flower to open. They hope it will be red like their jet. They think red is the best color.

One morning, they see the flower is open. They run to the pot and look at it. They gasp. The flower is not red. It is yellow. It is big and bright and has many petals.

"Wow, the flower is different!" Tom says.

"Yes, it is. But it is still beautiful." Mia says.

They smile. They like the flower. They think it is special. They give it a hug and a kiss. They say thank you to the seed for growing into a flower. They say thank you to their mom for helping them. They say thank you to their jet for being their friend. They are happy. They have a jet and a flower and each other. They have everything they need.

Once upon a time, there was a little red bird. She wanted to go to the stage, so she flew to find it. 

She saw the stage and hopped on it. But she didn't know how to make it move.

Suddenly, she heard a voice behind her. "You need to lock the stage!" said the voice. The little red bird turned around and saw a blue bird.

The little red bird asked, "What do you mean?"
The blue bird said, "You have to press this button to lock the stage. Then, it will move." 

The little red bird was so happy and said, "Thank you!" She pressed the button, and the stage started to move. The little red bird had so much fun dancing and singing on the stage.
