The girl giggled and said, "Thank you, doggy, for understanding. There are plenty of other bones in this creek so you can come back and find another one." The doggy smiled and ran off to look for another juicy bone to chew!

Once upon a time there was a sweet little angel. Her name was Ella and she was the best angel ever. Every day, she would fly around and make the world a better place. One day, Ella was scared. She could feel something bad coming. She flew as fast as she could towards home, but something was in her way. It was a scary monster! But Ella was brave, and she decided to behave. She looked the monster in the eyes, and it flew away! Ella was so happy, she thanked God for helping her to behave. From that day on, Ella was the bravest little angel in the world.

It was a wild day on the beach. Mary and her mom were playing in the sand and decided to make a sandcastle.

Mary grabbed her bucket and said, "Let's mix sand, water and shells!"

Her mom replied, "Let's mix some of these pretty pebbles too!"

Mary clapped her hands and said, "Yes, and let's put these palm leaves on top!"

They each grabbed a scoop of sand and mixed it with water in their buckets. Mary poured in lots of shells and added a few pebbles. Then she carefully chose five long palm leaves and placed them on top.

When they were done, Mary's sandcastle was wild and wacky!

Once upon a time, there was a flower. It was a pretty flower with lots of colors. It grew in a garden and one day, it started to bloom. The flower opened up and showed all its petals. It looked so beautiful!

One day, a little girl went to the fridge to get a snack. She opened the door and saw some yummy fruits and vegetables. She picked an apple and closed the door. The fridge door was flexible, so it didn't make a loud noise.

The little girl went outside and saw the pretty flower blooming. She smiled and thought it was the most beautiful thing she had ever seen. She took a bite of her apple and sat down to enjoy the view. The end.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Sarah. She was very sad as she had not seen her friends for a long time.

One day, Sarah went for a walk in the park. As she walked, she saw a sweet on the ground. She picked it up and held it in her hand. She was about to eat it, when she heard a voice.

"Hello Sarah, don't eat that sweet!"

Sarah turned around and saw her best friend Maria. She ran towards her and hugged her tight. She felt so happy!

Maria asked why Sarah hasn't seen her for so long. Sarah told Maria about how sad she had been. Maria put her arm around Sarah's shoulder and said, "Let's cheer you up! Come with me."

They walked and talked until they reached a sweet shop. Maria took out some coins and bought them some sweets. They ate the sweets and tasted all the different flavours: strawberry, apple and lemon. 

When they had finished their sweets, Sarah felt much happier. "Now I don't feel so sad," she said.

Maria smiled. "I'm glad," she said.

Then they held hands and ran off to play, happy to be together again.

Sam and Lily were at the beach with their mom and dad. They liked to play in the sand and look for shells and rocks. Sometimes they found oysters, which were big and hard and had something shiny inside.

"Look, I found an oyster!" Lily said, holding up her find. "Can I open it, mom?"

Mom smiled and said, "Sure, but be careful. Oysters can be sharp and you might hurt your fingers. Here, use this knife and I'll help you."

Mom and Lily carefully opened the oyster and saw a pearl inside. It was round and white and sparkled in the sun.

"Wow, it's so pretty!" Lily said. "Can I keep it, mom?"

"Of course, you can, sweetie. It's a special gift from the sea. You can make a necklace or a bracelet with it."

Lily was very happy and hugged her mom. She thanked the oyster for giving her the pearl and put it in her pocket.

Sam was watching and said, "That's cool, Lily. Can I find an oyster too?"

"Sure, Sam. There are many oysters in the water. You just have to look for them."

Sam and Lily ran to the water and started to look for oysters. They had fun splashing and digging and finding more shells and rocks. They saw some fish and crabs and starfish too.

The beach was peaceful and sunny. The waves made a soft sound and the birds sang in the sky. Sam and Lily felt happy and lucky. They loved the beach and the sea and each other.

They found two more oysters and opened them with mom's help. They each got a pearl and showed them to dad. Dad was proud and said, "You are very good at finding oysters, Sam and Lily. You are like little explorers. You know what, you can bow to the sea and say thank you for the pearls. It's a nice way to show respect and gratitude."

Sam and Lily nodded and bowed to the sea. They said, "Thank you, sea, for the pearls. We will take good care of them and remember this day."

The sea seemed to smile and wink at them. It sent a gentle wave to touch their feet and make them giggle. Sam and Lily felt a warm feeling in their hearts. They knew the sea was their friend and they would come back again.

Sandy was a kind 3 year old girl. One day, she was in her bedroom playing. She wanted to make a surprise for her mom and dad. Sandy had an idea! She took off her pants and filled them with stuffing from her old pillow. After she was done, she put the pants on the floor. Then she clapped her hands and said 'rise!' Suddenly, the stuffed pants rose up. Sandy clapped and laughed. She knew that mom and dad would love her surprise. Sandy gave the stuffed pants a big hug. She was so happy that her special surprise was finished. 

Now, Sandy could show her parents her special surprise. She ran into the living room and said "Look mom and dad, I made something special". Mom and dad admired Sandy's surprise. They were so proud of her. Sandy smiled, she knew that she had made something special with her kind heart.

Once upon a time, there was a young boy who lived on a farm with his family. The boy often went outside to gaze out upon the fields, which were filled with animals and crops. He loved seeing the staff at work in the fields, navigating the land, and taking care of the animals and farms. One day, he heard a strange noise coming from a nearby bush. He decided to investigate and found a small, deaf rabbit hiding in the bush. He crouched down to get a closer look, and the rabbit's warm, sparkling eyes met his own. He felt a connection and from that day, he was determined to look after the rabbit. 

Months passed and the boy continued to visit the rabbit each day, sometimes bringing it food or playing gentle games with it. One day, the boy decided that he wanted to take the rabbit home with him, and this time he succeeded. He showed his family the rabbit and they were all delighted. The boy's parents told him the rabbit needed a special staff that was gentle around animals. With help from his parents, the boy found the perfect staff, and soon the rabbit was content in its new home and had a full, happy life. The boy always knew that with a loving gaze, he could see the potential and joy that the rabbit held.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a thick blanket that she loved to cuddle with at night. But one day, her blanket was gone. She looked everywhere for it, but it was nowhere to be found. This made her worry a lot.

Lily's mom told her not to worry and promised to find the blanket. But days passed and the blanket was still missing. Lily couldn't sleep without it. She tried to use other blankets, but they weren't as good as her thick one.

Finally, Lily's mom found the blanket. Lily was so happy and relieved. She hugged the blanket tightly and felt like everything was going to be okay. But then, just as quickly as she found it, the blanket caught on fire and burned to ashes. Lily was devastated. She cried and cried, knowing that her favorite blanket was gone forever. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a gentle reindeer. His name was Rudolph. He had a red nose that shone bright. One day, Rudolph wanted to run and play with his friends. So, he went to find them in the forest. 

When Rudolph found his friends, they were playing tag. Rudolph was it! He chased after his friends and they ran away. Rudolph was fast and he caught them all. They all laughed and had fun together.

After playing for a while, Rudolph and his friends got tired. They lay down in the grass and looked up at the sky. They saw the clouds and talked about what shapes they looked like. Rudolph was happy to be with his friends and he felt grateful for such a fun day.

Once upon a time, there lived a family. Dad and Mom, with their daughter, decided it was time to go on a trip. So they started packing up everything. 

"Let's make sure we pack the dishwasher too!" said Mom.

Dad and daughter gave Mom a puzzled look. "Why do we need to pack the dishwasher?" Dad asked. 

"It's a surprise!" said Mom. 

So they packed the dishwasher, and soon they were ready to go. On the way, Dad noticed something strange. The dishwasher they had packed seemed to be humming. 

"What's that noise?" Dad wondered. 

Mom just smiled and said, "It's a surprise!" 

The family finally arrived at their destination. And when they opened the dishwasher, they were amazed! Inside was an entire picnic set, complete with plates and utensils. 

"An amazing picnic set!" Dad exclaimed. 

And that's how Dad, Mom and their daughter enjoyed their amazing picnic using the dishwasher they had packed!

Sara and Tom are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big hole in the fence. They wonder what is behind the hole. They want to go and see.

They crawl through the hole. They find a big road with many cars. The cars are loud and fast. Sara and Tom are scared. They want to go back to the park. But they do not know how.

They try to cross the road. They wait for a quiet moment. They run as fast as they can. But a car does not see them. It hits them. Sara and Tom fall down. They do not get up. They do not play anymore.

Once upon a time there was a little boy called Joe. Joe was so worried because he had lost his favourite toy. He searched everywhere, in the living room, in his bedroom, even under the bed, but he couldn't find it anywhere.

He decided to take a look in the attic. He ran up the stairs, into the attic and heard a splash! Joe was so scared and worried that he hid behind a chair. 

Suddenly he heard a voice. "Hello Joe, why are you so worried? Come out and find me."

Joe slowly stepped out from behind the chair and saw a frog. "Are you swimming in the pool?" Joe asked.

"No, I'm diving" the frog replied. Joe and the frog started playing with his toy in the attic and they both had a lot of fun. 

In the end, Joe remembered to say thank you to the frog for finding his toy. Then, he hugged the frog and ran back downstairs to show his toy to his parents.

Lily was a little girl who loved to play in the garden. She liked to look at the flowers and the bugs and the birds. One day, she saw a butterfly with many colors on its wings. It was flying from one flower to another, and Lily wanted to catch it.

She ran after the butterfly, but it was too fast for her. She tried to reach it with her hands, but it flew away. She tried to jump and grab it, but it flew higher. She tried to call it, but it did not listen. She felt sad and angry. She wanted the butterfly for herself.

Then she saw a boy sitting on a bench. He had a butterfly net in his hand. He smiled at Lily and said, "Hello, do you like butterflies?"

Lily nodded and said, "Yes, I do. But I can't catch one. They are too quick and smart."

The boy said, "I can help you. I have a net. We can catch a butterfly together. Do you want to try?"

Lily said, "Yes, please. Thank you for helping me."

The boy and Lily walked to a flower bed where there were many butterflies. The boy said, "Look, there is a big one. It is yellow and black. Do you like it?"

Lily said, "Yes, I do. It is very pretty. Can we catch it?"

The boy said, "Yes, we can. But we have to be gentle and quiet. We don't want to scare it or hurt it. Are you ready?"

Lily said, "Yes, I am. Let's go."

The boy and Lily moved slowly and carefully. They got closer and closer to the butterfly. The boy lifted his net and said, "Now!"

He swung his net and caught the butterfly. Lily clapped her hands and said, "Yay! We did it! We caught the butterfly!"

The boy said, "Yes, we did. Let's see it."

He opened his net and showed Lily the butterfly. It was still and quiet. It did not move or flap its wings. It looked sad and scared.

Lily said, "Oh, poor butterfly. It is not happy. It wants to fly and be free."

The boy said, "You are right. It is not happy. It is not fair to keep it in the net. It is not a toy. It is a living thing. It has feelings and needs. We should let it go."

Lily said, "Yes, we should. But can we say goodbye to it first?"

The boy said, "Yes, we can. We can say thank you and sorry and wish it well."

Lily said, "Okay. Let's do that."

The boy and Lily held the net gently and opened it. The butterfly came out and fluttered its wings. It looked at them with its big eyes. It seemed to understand.

Lily said, "Bye bye, butterfly. Thank you for letting us see you. You are very beautiful and amazing. We are sorry for catching you. We did not mean to make you sad or scared. We hope you are happy and safe. We hope you find many flowers and friends."

The boy said, "Bye bye, butterfly. Thank you for teaching us a lesson. You are very brave and smart. We are sorry for being selfish. We did not think about your feelings or needs. We hope you are free and healthy. We hope you enjoy your life and your world."

The butterfly seemed to smile and nod. It flew around them and landed on Lily's nose. It gave her a little kiss. Then it flew away and disappeared in the sky.

Lily and the boy smiled and hugged. They felt happy and sorry and grateful. They learned to respect and care for the butterfly and all living things. They learned to share and be kind. They learned that sometimes the most ordinary things are the most extraordinary.

Once there was a boy. His name was Tom. Tom had a big wheel. He used it to go around the block. One day, Tom wanted to send his wheel to a friend. When he asked his mom, she said no. She said it was too rude to send his only wheel away. Tom was very sad but he respected his mom. So, instead of sending it, he gave his wheel to his friend as a present. His friend was so happy to get the wheel. They both played with it for hours and had a lot of fun.

Once there was a Little Kid. He liked to listen to music. He loved to play his favourite tunes on his toy piano. But one day when he was playing, his parents told him he was not behaving. He was very sad.

But then Little Kid had a brilliant idea! He decided to practice his music so he could play it perfectly. Then he would show his parents he could behave while he listened to music. So Little Kid practiced very hard.

After a few days, Little Kid's playing was perfect. His parents were so proud. When they heard his tunes, they said that it was wonderful. They told Little Kid he was behaving so well. Little Kid was so happy and he smiled a big smile.

Molly and her brother, John, loved playing together. One day, they decided to visit the nearby farm and look at the animals there.

Molly saw a goat standing in the field and exclaimed, "Wow, it's so beautiful!" She wanted to pet the goat.

John warned her, "We should be careful. Goats can be dangerous." But Molly wanted to pet the goat anyway.

John said, "If you want to pet the goat, you have to reverse slowly. Goats don't like it when people move quickly." Molly understood and started to reverse.

But then something unexpected happened. The goat charged and bucked Molly, sending her flying through the air. She cried as she hit the ground.

John rushed to help Molly and said, "See, I told you to be careful. Goats can be dangerous!" Molly was hurt and scared, but she knew John was right.

Once upon a time, there was a girl who loved to spin. Every day she would spin around and around in circles until she felt dizzy and fell down.

But one day, she found a jar of glue. She smiled when she saw how it looked. The glue was so attractive with its sparkly color.

So she decided to make something fun with her glue and spinning. She put the glue on the floor and started to spin around it. The glue made a beautiful pattern from her spinning.

The girl was very happy with the pattern. She wanted to make more and show it to her friends. So she gathered more glue and kept spinning and making pretty patterns on the floor.

Reckless she didn't stop until all the glue was finished. She made the most attractive patterns she had ever seen!

Once upon a time, there was a big blue ball. This blue ball was named Universe. Universe had many friends who lived on it. They were happy most of the time, but sometimes they would quarrel.

One day, two friends, Cat and Dog, had a quarrel. Cat said, "I am the best friend of Universe!" Dog said, "No, I am the best friend of Universe!" They could not agree, and their voices got louder and louder.

Universe heard the quarrel and came to them. Universe said, "Please stop fighting. You both are my best friends. I love you both the same." Cat and Dog felt bad for fighting. They said sorry to each other and to Universe. From that day on, they never had a quarrel again, and they all lived happily together on the big blue ball.

Once upon a time, there were two friends, Jack and Joe. They lived in a small house with a gloomy atmosphere.

One day, Jack decided to do something about the gloomy feeling in the house. He picked up a broom and started to sweep away all the dust. Joe looked on with shock as Jack worked with enthusiasm. 

"Why don't you accept the dust?" Joe asked.

"Because it's not nice," Jack replied. "The dust is making the house feel gloomy and I don't want to feel like that anymore."

Joe nodded in agreement and together they kept on sweeping the dust away until the house looked much brighter. After a few hours, the dust was all gone and the two friends sat back and admired the bright house they had created. 

From that day on, both of them agreed to keep the house clean and tidy so as to keep it bright. 

The End.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved going to school, but he had trouble behaving. He would often talk during class and not listen to his teacher.

One day, Timmy's teacher spoke to him about the importance of being honest and behaving in school. She told him that it was important to listen to the teacher and follow the rules.

Timmy realized that he needed to behave better in school. He started to listen to his teacher and follow the rules. He became a better student and even made some new friends.

The moral of the story is that it's important to be honest and behave in school. When you do, you can learn new things and make new friends.

Once upon a time, there was a birdie. The birdie had a feather on its head. The feather was so pretty! But one day, the birdie got some dirt on its feather. The birdie wanted to wipe the dirt off its feather. 

The birdie looked for something to wipe its feather with. It saw a leaf, but the leaf was too big. It saw a rock, but the rock was too hard. Then, the birdie saw a soft and modest flower. The flower was perfect for wiping the feather! 

The birdie used the flower to wipe the dirt off its feather. The feather was clean again! The birdie was so happy. It flew away, showing off its pretty feather to all its birdie friends. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She wanted to go to the park with her mommy. She was very happy because she loved playing on the swings and the slide. 

When they got to the park, Lily's mommy helped her start swinging. Lily went higher and higher, feeling the wind in her hair. Then, she went down the slide, laughing all the way. 

After playing for a while, Lily and her mommy went home. Lily was still happy and told her daddy all about her fun day at the park. She couldn't wait to go back and play again.

Anna and Ben were adventurous kids. They liked to explore new places and have fun. One day, they found a big balloon in their backyard. It was red and shiny and had a basket under it.

"Wow, look at this!" Anna said. "Do you think we can fly in it?"

"Maybe," Ben said. "But how do we make it go up?"

They looked around and saw a big tank next to the balloon. It had a hose and a valve. Ben read the label on the tank. It said "gas".

"I think this is how we make it go up," Ben said. "Gas makes the balloon big and light. Let's try it!"

He opened the valve and gas came out of the hose. He put the hose in the balloon and the balloon started to grow. Anna and Ben cheered and climbed into the basket.

"Are you ready?" Ben asked.

"Yes!" Anna said. "Let's go!"

They pulled a rope and the balloon lifted off the ground. They felt the wind in their hair and the sun on their faces. They saw their house, their street, their town, and more. They felt like they were in a dream.

"This is amazing!" Anna said. "We are flying!"

They did not know that the gas tank was almost empty. They did not know that the balloon would soon start to go down. They did not know that they were heading towards a big forest. They did not know that they were in for a big adventure.

Anna and Ben liked to play with blocks. They built many structures with different shapes and colors. Sometimes they made houses, sometimes towers, sometimes bridges. They had fun and learned a lot.

One day, they wanted to build a big castle. They used all their blocks and worked hard. They made walls, windows, doors, and a flag. They were proud of their structure. They showed it to their mom and dad.

"Wow, what a wonderful castle!" mom said. "You did a great job, Anna and Ben!"

"Thank you, mom!" Anna and Ben said.

"Can we go outside and play now?" Ben asked.

"Sure, but remember to clean up your blocks when you come back," dad said.

"OK, dad!" Anna and Ben said.

They put on their coats and shoes and ran outside. They played with their ball, their bike, and their swing. They had fun and forgot about their castle.

Then it started to rain. The rain was heavy and wet. It made everything wet and muddy. Anna and Ben ran back inside. They took off their coats and shoes and dried themselves with a towel.

They wanted to see their castle again. They went to their room and looked at their structure. But it was not the same. The rain had made the blocks wet and soft. The walls had fallen, the windows had broken, the doors had bent, and the flag had torn. Their structure was ruined.

"Oh no, our castle!" Anna cried.

"What happened?" Ben asked.

"The rain did this," mom said. "It made your blocks wet and weak. They could not hold your structure anymore."

"That's not fair!" Ben said.

"I'm sorry, Anna and Ben," mom said. "But you can learn from this. Next time, you should put your blocks away when you are done playing. Or you should build your structure somewhere dry, like under a table or a bed. Then the rain will not hurt it."

Anna and Ben felt sad and sorry. They realized they had made a mistake. They had not listened to their dad. They had not cleaned up their blocks. They had not protected their structure.

They hugged their mom and said, "We're sorry, mom. We will do better next time. We will improve our structure and our habits. We will listen to you and dad. We will put our blocks away when we are done playing. We will build our structure somewhere dry. We will be more careful and responsible."

Mom smiled and said, "That's good, Anna and Ben. I'm proud of you. You are growing up and learning. You can still have fun and be creative, but you also have to be mindful and respectful. That's how you can make good structures and good choices."

Anna and Ben nodded and said, "Thank you, mom. We love you."

They hugged their mom again and started to clean up their blocks. They decided to build a new castle tomorrow, somewhere dry and safe. They hoped the rain would stop and the sun would shine. They were happy and hopeful.

Once upon a time there was a factory that was purple. All the workers in the factory were so nice, but they were getting tired from working so hard. They needed help to make the factory run faster.

One day, a brave little girl came to the factory. She was only three years old, but she offered to help out. The workers were so happy.

The little girl was a big help. Every day she worked hard to make things move faster. She smiled a lot and was very friendly to everyone in the factory.

Soon, the factory was running fast and smooth. Everyone was so proud of the little girl and thanked her for her help. She was excited that she got to help out, and everyone was so happy that the factory was working again. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to draw with chalk on the sidewalk. He drew big circles and squares with all the colors of the rainbow. One day, Timmy's friend Billy came to play with him. Billy wanted to draw too, but he didn't have any chalk. 

Timmy said, "I have lots of chalk. Follow me!" Timmy led Billy to his house where he showed him his big box of chalk. Billy was happy because Timmy was a dependable friend who always helped him. They went back to the sidewalk and drew together until the sun went down. From that day on, they were the best of friends and always had fun drawing with chalk together.

Lily liked to play with her toy lion. She made him roar and run and jump on her bed. She pretended he was the king of the jungle and she was his friend.

One day, a big storm came. The sky was dark and loud. The wind blew hard and the rain fell fast. Lily was scared. She hugged her toy lion and ran to her mom.

Mom was in the kitchen. She saw Lily and smiled. She said, "Don't worry, sweetie. The storm will go away soon. It's just nature making noise. Come, let's make some cookies."

Lily and Mom went to the table. Mom gave Lily a bowl and a spoon. She said, "We need flour, sugar, butter, eggs, and vanilla. Can you help me mix them?"

Lily nodded. She liked to help Mom. She poured and stirred and tasted. She said, "Yum, yum, yum!"

Mom said, "Now we need some color. How about pink? Do you like pink?"

Lily said, "Yes, I love pink! Pink is pretty!"

Mom gave Lily a bottle of pink food coloring. She said, "Squeeze a little bit into the dough. Not too much, or it will be too bright."

Lily squeezed the bottle. She watched the dough turn pink. She said, "Wow, look! Pink cookies!"

Mom said, "Yes, pink cookies! Now we need to cut them into shapes. How about stars? Do you like stars?"

Lily said, "Yes, I love stars! Stars are shiny!"

Mom gave Lily a star-shaped cookie cutter. She said, "Press it into the dough. Then put the cookies on the tray."

Lily pressed and cut and placed. She said, "Look, Mom! Pink star cookies!"

Mom said, "Good job, Lily! You are a great baker! Now we need to bake them in the oven. Be careful, it's hot."

Mom put the tray in the oven. She said, "We have to wait for a few minutes. Then we can eat them. Do you want some milk?"

Lily said, "Yes, please. Milk is good!"

Mom poured some milk in a cup. She gave it to Lily. She said, "Let's sit on the couch and read a book. Do you have a favorite book?"

Lily said, "Yes, I do. It's the one with the lion and the mouse. Can you read it to me?"

Mom said, "Of course. I love that book too. It's about friendship and kindness. Come on, let's go."

Lily and Mom went to the couch. Lily brought her toy lion. She said, "He likes the book too. He likes to roar when the lion roars."

Mom said, "That's fine. He can roar with us. But not too loud, or we might scare the storm away."

Lily giggled. She said, "That's silly, Mom. The storm can't be scared. It's just nature making noise."

Mom said, "You're right, Lily. It's just nature making noise. And we're just having fun. We're making pink star cookies and reading a book and roaring with a toy lion. We're having a cozy day."

Lily smiled. She said, "I love you, Mom. You make me happy."

Mom hugged Lily. She said, "I love you too, Lily. You make me happy too."

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was an unusual cat named Fluffy. Fluffy was not like other cats because she could talk. One day, Fluffy met a little girl named Lucy. They became good friends and liked to play together.

One day, Fluffy said, "Lucy, let's plan a trip to see the veterinarian." Lucy was surprised, but she agreed. They both walked to the veterinarian's office, holding hands and talking about their day.

When they got to the veterinarian, Fluffy told the doctor, "I am an unusual cat who can talk." The veterinarian was amazed and said, "Wow, Fluffy! You are very special." Fluffy and Lucy were very happy and went home to play some more.

One day, there was a parrot in the tree. All the birds were different colors. The parrot was yellow and green. The parrot was very tired. He yawned. He had been very busy in the morning. Every morning, he liked to fly around and practice his singing. 

Later in the day, he flew over to a lake. He saw many different kinds of birds swimming in the lake. He watched them carefully and tried to learn some new things. He even saw a big fish swimming. 

He was very happy when he saw the fish. The parrot wanted to talk to the fish, but it was too far away. The parrot yawned again because he was getting tired. 

After a while, the parrot flew back to his tree. He was ready to take a nap. He said goodnight to all of the different birds and then he fell asleep. 

The end!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys all day long. One day, he ate too many candies and his stomach hurt. Timmy's mom told him that he needed to rest and drink water to feel better. She also gave him a useful pillow to support his head while he rested. 

Timmy was happy to have his pillow because it made him feel comfortable. He hugged it tightly and closed his eyes. He felt better and fell asleep. When he woke up, his stomach didn't hurt anymore. Timmy smiled and thanked his mom for the support and the useful pillow. From that day on, Timmy knew that he needed to take care of his stomach and not eat too many candies.

Once upon a time, there was a big sunflower in a field. It was amazing, with bright yellow petals and a brown center. A little girl saw the sunflower and wanted to pick it, but her mom said no. 

The little girl was sad, so she went back to the sunflower when her mom wasn't looking. She tried to pick it, but accidentally tore off some petals. The sunflower looked sad too. 

The little girl felt bad and tried to put the petals back on, but it was too late. The sunflower wilted away and died. The little girl learned that it's important to listen to her mom and not hurt beautiful things.

Amy loved her hair. Today it was extra special. She was going to dress up and she was so excited. She had a special dress that was pink and sparkly! She put it on and it fit just right.

Next, she brushed her long, brown hair. She brushed it very quickly, so it wouldnâ€™t take too long. When she was done, it shone like the sun. 

Finally, she was ready to go. She grabbed her bag and ran out the door. She felt so fast, like a cheetah! She was off to have a great day.

Once there was a knight who was very brave. He had a shield that shone in the sunlight. One day the knight was walking in the forest when he saw a creature dancing. The knight thought the creature looked very stupid but he was also curious. 

The knight called out to the creature, "What are you doing?" 

The creature smiled and said, "I am dancing!" 

The knight laughed and said, "That is ridiculous!" The knight drew his sword and held it up to the creature. He said, "Stop dancing or I will hurt you!" 

The creature quickly stopped dancing and cried out, "Please don't hurt me!" 
But the knight didn't listen. He slashed his sword at the creature and it hurt him very badly. The creature ran away into the trees and the knight laughed. 

The poor creature was very sad and he vowed to never dance again.

Once upon a time there was a little mouse who was very adventurous. He wanted to explore the world. So one day he set off on an adventure.
