There was once a girl called Summer who was very excited. She was excited because she was going to decorate her bedroom. She had been saving up her pocket money so she could buy all the decorations she wanted to. 

On the day she was due to decorate she began gathering the decorations together. She even found a bone, which she thought she would turn into a piece of art for her room. 

But as she was about to start decorating she heard a noise outside. Summer looked out of the window and saw a hungry dog. She felt worried, but at the same time she was pleased that the bone she had found might help the dog. She put down her decorations and ran outside.

Anna and Ben were very happy. Today, they would go to the market with Mom. They liked to see all the different things there. They wanted to buy some fruit for a snack.

They arrived at the market and saw many people. Mom gave them each a basket and said, "You can choose one fruit each, but not too expensive. I will meet you at the bread stall."

Anna and Ben ran to the fruit stall. They saw apples, bananas, oranges, grapes, and lemons. Anna liked apples, but they were too big for her basket. Ben liked bananas, but they were too yellow for him. They both liked oranges, but they were too round for their baskets. They saw some grapes, but they were too expensive. Mom said not too expensive.

They looked at the lemons. They were small and fit in their baskets. They were also cheap. Anna and Ben thought lemons were good. They took one each and went to the bread stall.

Mom saw them and smiled. She said, "You chose lemons? That's interesting. Do you know what they taste like?"

Anna and Ben shook their heads. They had never tasted lemons before. They were curious.

Mom said, "Let's find out. I will cut them for you. But be careful, they are very sour."

She cut the lemons and gave them a slice each. Anna and Ben put them in their mouths and made a funny face. They were very sour! They spit them out and said, "Yuck!"

Mom laughed and said, "I told you. Lemons are not good for eating. They are good for making juice or lemonade. Maybe next time, you can choose a different fruit."

Anna and Ben nodded. They learned something new. They still liked lemons, but not for a snack. They gave their lemons to Mom and asked for some bread instead. They ate their bread and went home. They had a fun day at the market.

Once there was a little boy whose name was Bob. Bob wanted to draw a picture. He went to his bedroom and found a black marker, some paper and a red crayon. Bob was excited to try and draw a picture.

Bob took the marker and started to draw a big black circle, then he started to draw lots of smaller black circles around it. He then tried to draw a big black tree with big green leaves and a black bird at the top.

Once upon a time, there was a big race. Many animals came to run in the race. They all wanted to win.

In the race, there was a fast dog, a slow turtle, and a little rabbit. They all had to run a long way. The dog was very fast, but he had a tight collar. The turtle was slow, but he never gave up. The rabbit was small, but he was very smart.

Lily and Tom are friends. They like to play in the park. They have a lot of fun on the swings, the slide and the seesaw. They also like to run and chase each other.

One day, Lily has to go to the doctor. She is sick and has a fever. She cannot play with Tom. Tom is sad. He misses Lily a lot. He does not want to play alone.

He goes to the park and sees a boy. The boy is bigger than Tom. He has a ball. Tom wants to play with the ball. He asks the boy, "Can I play with you?"

The boy says, "No, this is my ball. Go away." He kicks the ball hard. The ball flies in the air and lands on the roof of a house. The boy is angry. He says, "Now look what you did. You made me miss my ball. How will I get it back?"

Tom says, "I'm sorry. I did not mean to make you miss your ball. Maybe we can get it back. There is a ladder over there. We can climb it and reach the roof."

The boy says, "No, that is too hard. The ladder is very high. I am afraid of heights. You go and get it. You are smaller. You only need to climb an inch."

Tom says, "No, that is not fair. You are the one who kicked the ball. You should get it. It is not easy to climb a ladder. It is dangerous. We should ask for help."

The boy says, "No, I don't want to ask for help. I don't want anyone to know that I lost my ball. You have to do it. Or I will tell everyone that you are a baby and a coward."

Tom says, "No, you are the baby and the coward. You are mean and selfish. You don't know how to share or be nice. You are not a good friend. I don't want to play with you. I want to play with Lily. She is kind and fun. She knows how to miss someone. She is a good friend."

Tom leaves the boy and goes home. He hopes that Lily will get better soon. He wants to see her and play with her again. He learns that it is better to have a good friend than a bad one. He also learns that it is not good to miss something that you can't have. He is happy with what he has. He is happy with Lily.

Once there was a little girl named Lucy. She loved to use her creative imagination. Every day she would come up with new stories and adventures to go on. She especially liked to use lotion to make her skin feel soft.

The bear was very happy because he always knew that his special place was there for him if he ever needed it. He could go there and find comfort when he felt overwhelmed by the noise. Thanks to his special escape, the bear never had to feel alone or scared in the noisy forest.

Little Molly couldn't figure out why her toy bunny was so mysterious. She poked the button on its nose again and again, hoping it would do something special. But it was just silent.

Molly's mom came over and saw Molly pressing the button.
"What is that, my pumpkin?" she asked.
Molly stopped pressing the button and smiled.
"This is my bunny!" she said.
Molly's mom smiled and said, "Why don't you take your bunny to sleep?"

Molly nodded and put the bunny in her bed. When Molly went to sleep, the bunny suddenly started to glow. Molly opened her eyes and said, "Wow!" The bunny was glowing in the dark and it was so mysterious.

Molly giggled and nestled close to the bunny, knowing that it would protect her as she fell asleep. That night, Molly had the most magical dream.

One day, a cool cat named Tom went for a walk. He saw a big green thing with spikes. It was a cactus! Tom thought it was very cool. He wanted to play with it, but he did not want to get hurt by the spikes. So, he thought of a plan.

Tom found a long stick. He thought he could use the stick to play with the cactus. But then, he saw his friend, the dog named Max. Max wanted to play with Tom. Tom wanted to play with Max too, but he wanted to play with the cactus first. So, Tom told Max to wait. He said, "Max, I have to delay our play."

Tom used the stick to touch the cactus. It was fun! He did not get hurt. Then, he heard Max bark. Max was sad because he was waiting for a long time. Tom knew it was time to play with Max. He left the cactus and went to play with Max. They had a lot of fun together. Tom was happy he could play with the cactus and Max too.

One sunny day, a little girl named Lily was playing in her backyard. She saw colorful bubbles floating in the air and felt very happy. She tried to catch the bubbles but they kept popping before she could touch them.

Suddenly, she heard a loud noise and saw a big dog running towards her. She felt fearful and didn't know what to do. The dog came closer and closer, but then stopped and barked happily. "Don't be scared, little girl. I just want to play with you," said the dog.

Lily smiled, feeling relieved. "Do you want to catch bubbles with me?" she asked the dog. They both ran around, trying to catch the bubbles. They laughed and had so much fun. From that day on, the dog became Lily's best friend and they caught bubbles together every day.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy who loved pigeons. He liked to feed them and watch them fly around. 

One day, he found a really pretty pigeon. It was so beautiful he decided to keep it. He named it Bob and fed it every day. 

One day, Bob was playing in the yard when a fake pigeon landed nearby. It was made of metal and had pretty feathers. The boy was so captivated by it that he ran to touch it. Unfortunately, Bob flew away in fright. 

The little boy was very sad that he lost Bob and he cried and cried. Then his mom came and comforted him. She said, â€œBe careful what you bring into your life. Fake and real things can be mixed up and you could lose something precious.â€œ 

From that day on, the boy never forgot these wise words. He learned to value the things that were real and be careful with what he brought into his life.

Jimmy was a dependable 3 year old, who loved to wander on the road. One day, Jimmy was walking on the road near his house when he suddenly heard a loud noise coming from a way away. He stopped and was very scared.

Suddenly, a big truck came from down the road. Jimmy was frozen from fear. But then the truck slowly came to a stop in front of Jimmy.

The truck driver said "Hey little dude, what are you doing out here all alone?" 
Jimmy replied: "I'm just walking on the road." 
The truck driver said: "It's not safe for a little guy like you to be on the road all by yourself. You should always let your mom know if you're ever going out alone." Jimmy nodded his head.

The truck driver smiled and said: "You seem like a dependable kid. Be careful out there, OK?" 
Jimmy nodded and thanked the truck driver before walking back home. 

From then on, Jimmy remembered always to be dependable and to always let his mom know before he ever went out on the road alone.

Once upon a time, there was a nice cat named Whiskers. Whiskers liked to sleep a lot. One day, Whiskers went for a walk and saw a statue. The statue was very big and made of stone. Whiskers thought the statue was nice too.

But then, a dog came along and barked at Whiskers. Whiskers got scared and ran away. But when Whiskers looked back, he saw the dog was barking at the statue, not at him. Whiskers felt silly for being scared and decided to take a nap next to the nice statue.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his ball outside. One day, he was playing with his ball and he accidentally dropped it into a big puddle. The ball got all wet and Timmy was sad.

Timmy's mommy saw what happened and she went to get a towel to dry the ball. But when she picked up the ball, she saw that it had a little leak in it. Water was coming out of the ball! Timmy's mommy told him that the ball was broken and they couldn't play with it anymore.

Timmy was sad again, but his mommy gave him a big hug and said they could go inside and have some warm milk and cookies. Timmy loved warm milk and cookies, so he was happy again. Even though his ball was broken, Timmy knew that he had a mommy who loved him and that made him feel better. The end.

Once, there was a girl called Sarah. She was very sad because her pet rat had died. One day, Sarah asked her mum why her rat was dead. Her mum said that the rat had been in a fight and didn't win.

The next day, Sarah asked her dad if she could get another rat to replace the one that had died. Dad said that he didn't want Sarah to be sad and he promised to buy her a new rat.

Sarah was so excited! She asked her mum when she could get the rat, and mum said that they could go the very next day.

The next day, Sarah and her mum went to the pet shop. They bought a lovely rat and Sarah couldn't wait to take it home.

Sarah was so happy that she had a new friend! From that day on, she and her new rat were the best of friends, and they never had to worry about fights again!

Once upon a time, there was a clumsy little boy. He was sailing in a big, long boat. He was so proud of his boat! 

Suddenly, he felt a wave of tiredness and realized he had been sailing all day. He decided it was time for bed and made his way through the waves to the shore.

When he arrived, the little boy found a cozy little bed that looked just perfect. He got ready for bed and snuggled up to get some sleep. 

Just then, the little boy heard a voice. It said, "Hey, clumsy sailor - what are you doing in this bed?" 

He looked up to see a very, very old crab. The crab asked him why he was so clumsy. The little boy smiled and said, "I'm clumsy because I'm just a little boy learning how to sail!" 

The crab nodded and said, "Well, you'd better get off my bed now, little sailor!" 

The little boy laughed, said goodbye to the crab, and hopped off the bed. He went to find his boat, and was soon sailing away on the sea once again.

Once upon a time there was a baby, who was called Jake. Jake liked to explore and discover things around the garden.

One day, Jake was walking around the garden, listening to the birds and looking at the flowers, when suddenly he saw something small and shiny. He took a closer look and was so excited to find a bug!

"Wow," he shouted, bending down to take a closer look. The bug was gentle and stayed still as he looked.

At that moment, Jake's dad came to find him.

"What have you discovered?" his dad asked.

"A bug!" replied Jake.

His dad smiled and said, "That's great! Why not put it outside so it can fly away again?"

Jake smiled and nodded, gently placing the bug in a safe spot in the garden. He looked at the bug for a few moments before turning back to his dad, ready for his next discovery.

Lily and Max were playing in the park. They liked to pretend they were spies and look for clues. Lily had a magnifying glass and Max had a notebook. They saw a shiny thing in the grass. It was a diamond!

"Wow, look at this!" Max said. "It's so pretty and sparkly!"

"Let me see!" Lily said. She grabbed the diamond from Max. "It's mine now!"

"No, it's not!" Max said. "We found it together! You have to share!"

Lily was bossy. She did not like to share. She put the diamond in her pocket. "No, I don't! I'm the leader of the spies! You have to do what I say!"

Max was sad. He did not like Lily being bossy. He wanted to play fair. He had an idea. He took out his notebook and a pen. He wrote something on a page. He tore it out and gave it to Lily.

"What's this?" Lily asked.

"It's a sign," Max said. "It says that you have to give me the diamond or I will tell the teacher."

Lily looked at the sign. She could not read. She did not know what it said. She was scared. She did not want to get in trouble. She took out the diamond and gave it to Max.

"Here, take it!" she said. "But you have to be nice to me!"

"Okay, I will," Max said. He smiled. He was happy. He put the diamond in his notebook. He gave Lily the magnifying glass. "Do you want to look for more clues?"

Lily nodded. She was happy too. She took the magnifying glass. She said sorry to Max. They hugged. They went to look for more clues. They played nicely. They were friends.

One day, Ben and Mia were playing outside. They liked to pretend they were space explorers, and they had a big cardboard box as their rocket. They put on their helmets and gloves, and got ready to blast off.

"Five, four, three, two, one, go!" Ben shouted, and they pushed the box with their feet. They made zooming noises and imagined they were flying to the moon. They saw stars and planets and meteors in the sky.

"Look, there's a comet!" Mia said, pointing to a bright streak of light. "It's so pretty!"

"Let's follow it!" Ben said, and they steered their box towards the comet. They got closer and closer, and saw that the comet had a long tail of fire and ice.

"Wow, it's amazing!" Mia said, admiring the comet. "Can we touch it?"

"No, we can't!" Ben said, suddenly scared. "It's too hot and cold, and it might hurt us. It's bad to touch comets, they are not for playing. We have to stay away from it!"

He pulled the box back, and they moved away from the comet. They looked for a safer place to land, and saw a big green field. They decided to go there, and gently landed their box on the grass.

"Phew, that was close!" Ben said, wiping his forehead. "We almost got burned by the comet!"

"Good thing you stopped us, Ben!" Mia said, hugging him. "You are very smart and brave. You saved us from the bad comet!"

They smiled at each other, and got out of their box. They ran around the field, and played with some flowers and bugs. They had fun, and learned not to touch things that might hurt them.

The end.

Lily and Ben were playing in the living room with their toys. They had a lot of fun making noises and pretending to be animals. Lily had a soft blanket that she liked to cuddle with. She noticed that Ben did not have a blanket of his own.

"Ben, do you want to share my blanket?" Lily asked. "It is very cozy and warm."

Ben smiled and nodded. He took one end of the blanket and wrapped it around himself. He felt happy and snug. He thanked Lily for being so kind.

They continued to play with the blanket, making a tent, a cape, and a scarf. They laughed and giggled. They were having a great time.

But then, Lily saw something that made her sad. There was a small tear in her blanket. She did not know how it happened. Maybe it was from the toys, or the floor, or the couch. She felt a tear in her eye, too. She loved her blanket very much. It was fragile and precious to her.

"Ben, look what you did!" Lily cried. "You ruined my blanket! It has a hole in it! Give it back to me!"

Ben was shocked and scared. He did not mean to hurt the blanket. He did not know what to say. He let go of the blanket and ran away. He felt sorry and sad.

Lily hugged her blanket and sobbed. She wished she had not yelled at Ben. He was her friend and he did not deserve to be treated so badly. She realized that she had been selfish and mean. She wanted to say sorry to Ben and make up with him.

She got up and looked for Ben. She found him in his room, sitting on his bed. He looked lonely and hurt.

"Ben, I'm sorry," Lily said. "I was wrong to shout at you. You did not ruin my blanket. It was an accident. I should have been more careful and gentle with it. And I should have been more grateful and generous with you. You are more important than my blanket. Will you forgive me?"

Ben looked at Lily and saw that she was sincere and sorry. He felt a warm feeling in his heart. He nodded and smiled. He forgave Lily and hugged her.

They went back to the living room and mended the blanket together. They used some thread and a needle that their mom gave them. They made the hole smaller and stronger. They learned to be more careful and gentle with their things. And they learned to be more kind and loving with each other. They were happy and proud. They had a good lesson and a good day.

Once there was a dad, gingerly walking through his house carrying a drum. He had a special job to do - repair the rhythm of the drum.

"Daddy, can I help?" asked his three-year-old daughter. 

"Yes," he said, smiling.

He gave her a hammer and screwdriver and pointed to a loose screw on the side of the drum. She grabbed the tools and began the task, although it was a bit challenging for her tiny hands.

Her dad showed her again how to do it, and she was determined to try. She worked quickly and carefully, soon having the drum repaired.

"Great job!" said her dad, clapping his hands. His daughter smiled, quite pleased with herself.

Afterwards, she felt so happy and energized that she began to dance around the house. Her dad joined in and they both laughed as they moved to the rhythm of the repaired drum. 

The little girl was a natural. She was so quick and had a lazy way of moving that made it look effortless. She knew she had done a good job and her dad was so proud of her. She had repaired the rhythm of the drum!

One day, Matt went to the market with his mom. There were all sorts of things to see. Matt asked, "Can I buy something?"

His mom looked around, then smiled. "Let's see," she said. "Ah, there's something special."

The two of them went over to a display. There was a big fridge with a smooth, shining finish. Matt was so excited and yelled, "I want it!" 

The shopkeeper said, "That fridge will be perfect for you! I'll sell it to you for a good price." 

Matt's mom said, "It is a bit expensive, but I'm sure it will be worth it." She was right, of course. The smooth fridge was perfect for Matt's room. 

The family went home with the fridge and it was a great addition to the house. Matt and his family used it to store all the food and even keep the house cool. Now, Matt and his family see how worthwhile it was to buy the smooth fridge.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to draw circles. One day, she met a boy named Timmy who wanted to draw circles too, but he found it hard. 

Lily said, "Drawing circles is easy, I can show you!" 

Timmy said, "Thank you, Lily! You're so nice!" 

Lily showed Timmy how to draw circles and they became friends. They drew circles together every day. 

The moral of the story is, when someone needs help, it's always nice to welcome them and show them how to do something.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Tim and Pat. Pat was very lucky because he had a joke to tell Tim. They were sitting in the park when Pat said, "I've got a funny joke!"

Tim was very excited and could hardly wait. Pat told his joke and Tim started to laugh. He laughed so hard he had to yawn. Pat laughed too, and the two of them had a lot of fun together.

After that, Pat had to go home. He said goodbye to Tim and before he left he said, "You're so lucky to have such a funny joke." Then he waved to Tim and left. 

Tim smiled to himself. He was so lucky to have a friend like Pat and a funny joke to laugh at. Tim was a very happy little boy.

Cathy the bird was looking for her nest. It had been raining hard and her home was gone. "Where can I remain?" She asked herself.

Then she saw it. Far away and high up, she saw a nest in the tree branches. Cathy flew over to it. The nest was old and made of twigs.

"This will work," she thought and settled down in it.

Then something strange happened. A loud noise startled Cathy.

"What is that?" She asked.

Suddenly, a big and stupid bird flew in.

"What are you doing in my nest?" The bird asked.

Cathy was very frightened, but she stayed calm and answered. "I'm sorry. I was looking for a place to remain. I didn't know this nest was yours."

The big bird smiled. "It's ok. This nest is big enough for two birds. You can remain here with me."

Cathy was happy. She had found a place to feel safe and remain dry.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Lucy. She was only three years old and loved to play with her friends. One day, Lucy was running around on the playground when she suddenly twisted her ankle. She started to cry, and her friends were so worried about her. 

One of the friends ran over to a nearby hospital. The nurse at the hospital was very rude to Lucy and didn't bother to give her a smile. She just finished calling a doctor so they could check Lucy's ankle. 

Finally, the doctor came over and examined Lucy. He was much nicer than the nurse, and he asked her lots of questions about what happened. He told her that it was just a little twist and that she would be okay. 

Lucy was so relieved. Her friends all walked her home, and she was extra careful to not twist her ankle again!

Lily and Ben like to play with their toy cars. They have many cars of different colors and sizes. They race them on the floor and make loud noises. Sometimes, their cars crash and break.

One day, Lily's favorite car, a silver one, broke its wheel. Lily was sad and cried. She showed her car to Ben and said, "Look, my car is broken. It can't race anymore. What can I do?"

Ben looked at the car and said, "Don't cry, Lily. I can help you. I can repair your car. I have a tool box and some glue. Come with me."

Ben took Lily and her car to his room. He opened his tool box and took out a screwdriver, a hammer, and some glue. He found a spare wheel that fit the car. He used the screwdriver to remove the broken wheel. He used the hammer to straighten the axle. He used the glue to attach the new wheel. He waited for the glue to dry.

He gave the car back to Lily and said, "Here, your car is fixed. It has a new wheel. It can race again. See, it is smooth and shiny."

Lily smiled and hugged Ben. She said, "Thank you, Ben. You are a good brother. You are good at repairing things. Let's go and race our cars again."

They went back to the living room and raced their cars on the floor. They had fun and laughed. They were happy.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside and explore. One day, he found a cactus in his backyard. It was very interesting and had lots of prickly needles. 

Timmy's mom came outside and asked him what he found. "Mommy, look! I found an interesting cactus!" Timmy said. 

His mom was happy he found something new to explore. "That's very cool, Timmy. Why don't you give me the cactus so we can put it in a pot and take care of it?" she said. 

Timmy gave the cactus to his mom and they went inside to find a pot. They found a big pot and put the cactus inside. Timmy was happy he found something interesting and his mom was happy they could take care of it together. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little kitten. She was brilliant and loved to relax in the sunshine. Every day, she would close her eyes and feel the warm sun on her fur. She was so relaxed that she would drift off to sleep. 

Nearby, there was a 3 year old child. She loved to watch the kitten relax in the sun. She found it so amusing! Some days, she would lie down in the sun beside the kitten and try to relax too. 

The child and the kitten spent many happy days relaxing together in the sunshine. They would both close their eyes and dream wonderful dreams. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Julie. Julie loved having ideas. Every day, she got excited and had something new to share. One day, her Mommy urged her to come up with a creative idea. Julie thought and thought and then got a great idea.

Julie thought it would be fun to play a game. She asked her Mommy to play. Mommy agreed and the two of them had fun. They played for hours, laughing and smiling.

Finally, Julie had a new idea. She wanted to make her own pictures. With some help from Mommy, she used paint, markers and glue to make a picture. The picture looked great and everyone was so proud of Julie.

Mommy was so impressed with Julie's creative idea that she gave her a big hug. Later that day, Julie told her Mommy she wanted to make more pictures. Mommy knew it was a great idea and she urged Julie to make more.

And they lived happily ever after.

Once upon a Wednesday, there were two friends. One was playful, and the other was quiet. They decided to attach a string to a balloon and fly it in the sky. The playful one laughed and jumped around, while the quiet one enjoyed watching the smile and the color of the sky. They threw the string high up, and the playful one held onto the other end. It was so fun to watch the balloon fly in the air! The quiet one wanted to try too, so the playful one handed the string to the quiet one. Together, they watched the balloon fly in the sky until it disappeared from sight. They were both happy they were able to share that special moment together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Jane. Jane liked to go swimming at the pool. She went swimming with her mom every Saturday. 

One Saturday, Jane accidentally got her hair wet. Her mom said, "Oh no, we need to get shampoo and clean up that wet hair." 

Then, Jane and her mom went to the store and bought some shampoo. 

When they got home, Jane's mom filled the bathtub with warm water and bubbles. She gently put some shampoo in Jane's hair and started to massage her head. Jane felt so cozy and relaxed. 

After Jane's hair was nice and clean, she and her mom hugged. The hug was so comforting and warm. 

Jane said, "I love swimming, mom!" 

Her mom replied, "Me too, sweetheart!"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to dance and twirl around in circles. One day, her mommy bought a pretty ornament for their Christmas tree. It was shiny and sparkly, and Lily loved it.

But one night, as Lily was sleeping, she heard a noise coming from the living room. She tiptoed out of her room and saw that the ornament had fallen off the tree and was rolling around on the floor. Lily felt helpless, but then she had an idea. She started to dance around the ornament, twirling and spinning until she bumped it with her foot and it rolled back onto the tree.

Lily was so happy that she had helped the ornament get back where it belonged. From then on, every time she saw the ornament on the tree, she would do a little dance to show how proud she was of herself for being such a good helper. The end.

Once there was a ship named Little Birdy. Little Birdy was harmless and sailed through the ocean without causing any harm.

One day, Little Birdy met another ship in the middle of the ocean. The other ship was called Big Bob. Big Bob asked Little Birdy if he wanted to race. Little Birdy replied, "Yes I do!"

So the ships started their race. Little Birdy was very fast and soon caught up with Big Bob. Big Bob shouted, "Faster! Faster!" Little Birdy flew through the ocean faster and faster.

Soon, Little Birdy had passed Big Bob and won the race. Big Bob was so surprised that he yelled, "Will you teach me how you can go so fast in the ocean?"

Little Birdy smiled and said, "All you have to do is sail with a harmless heart!"

Jack and his mommy were walking down the street when Jack noticed something special. He ran ahead and saw a bright, shiny crib. It was big, sturdy and modern.

"Mommy, look! Can we get it?" asked Jack. "It looks so comfy."

Mommy smiled. "Yes, sweetheart. Let's take it home!"

They loaded the crib onto the truck and drove home. After they unloaded it, Jack eagerly hopped inside. He felt like this was his special spot. Mommy leaned down and gave him a warm hug.

"Now, this is your very own place!" she said.

Jack smiled and hugged her back. He knew this was the perfect spot for his nap every day. From now on, Jack loved to sleep in his crib. It was the most modern and cozy place ever.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny that wanted to make something special. The bunny hopped off to the kitchen to look for a mixer. He found a big, heavy mixer in the corner. He hopped over to it and turned it on. He poured in some milk, some eggs and some flour. He stirred it all around and around in the mixer until it was nice and thick.

The bunny hopped around the kitchen looking for something else to add. He found some blueberries and added them in and stirred some more. After stirring it all together, he hopped over to the oven and poured the mixture into a pan. He hopped back over to the mixer and wiped it clean.

The bunny popped the pan into the oven and hopped up and down. A few minutes later, he hopped back over to the oven and opened the door. Inside, he found a delicious blueberry cake! He hopped around the kitchen with delight and gave a piece to his friends. They all enjoyed the tasty cake and hopped away happy.

One day, Max and his family went to the park. Max saw a big square on the ground and he thought it was really cool. He wanted to play with it, but his mom said he had to wait until after lunch.

At lunch time, Max finally had the chance to play with the square. But when he got to it, he noticed that Bobby was there. Bobby was teasing him and would not let Max play with the square. Max started to get mad and he yelled at Bobby to go away. Bobby laughed and said no.

Max's mom heard the commotion and came over to see what was going on. She saw Bobby and got angry. Bobby's mom had forgotten to clean him up after lunch and he smelled really smelly.

Max's mom sent Bobby away and she told Max that he could play with the square. Max was really happy and jumped with joy. He had finally gotten to play with his favorite square!

One day, a little girl was playing hide and seek. She saw a couch and thought it would be a great place to hide. She stretched out on the couch and held still so that no one would find her. 

Then, something that she wasn't expecting happened. A big, scary monster came out from behind the couch! The little girl was so frightened that she began to cry. 

But the monster was friendly. He explained to the little girl that he was just playing hide and seek too, and he had been scared to find her already on the couch!

The monster and the little girl then became friends. They kept playing hide and seek every day. The little girl never was frightened when the monster popped up out of the couch; she knew that it was just part of the game.

Sara and Ben liked to build things with their blocks. They built houses, cars, castles, and more. One day, they decided to build a big bathtub for their dolls. They used all the blue blocks and some white ones for the bubbles. They were very proud of their bathtub.

But then, their baby brother Tom came into the room. He saw the bathtub and wanted to play with it. He crawled over and grabbed some blocks. He pulled and pushed and knocked down the bathtub. Sara and Ben were very sad and angry. They shouted at Tom and made him cry.

Mom heard the noise and came to see what was wrong. She saw the broken bathtub and the crying children. She hugged Tom and said, "He is too little to know how to play with blocks. He just wanted to join you. You should be nice to him and share your toys." She helped Sara and Ben rebuild their bathtub and gave them some extra blocks. She said, "You can make a smaller bathtub for Tom, too. Then he can play with you and not ruin your bathtub." Sara and Ben thought that was a good idea. They made a little bathtub for Tom and gave him a doll. Tom smiled and splashed with the doll. Sara and Ben smiled, too. They learned that being nice to their brother was better than being mad at him. They all had fun playing with their bathtubs.

Once upon a time there were two friends named Tom, and Lucy. They went to the theater together. Tom wanted to collect something popular. So they went to look around the theater. 

Tom saw a popular box! He was so excited and said to Lucy, "This box looks popular!" Lucy agreed and so Tom started to collect things from the theater. He found a toy car, some candy, and a special toy. 

Tom was so excited when he finished collecting all his things. Lucy was happy for her friend. They decided to go play with their new toys. They had lots of fun and laughed a lot! 

The two friends had a wonderful time collecting popular things from the theater.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to act like a superhero and save the day. He would put on his cape and fly around the house, pretending to rescue people.

One day, Timmy's dad was shaving with a razor. Timmy thought it looked cool, so he asked his dad if he could try. But his dad said no because the razor was sharp and could be dangerous.

Timmy was disappointed, but then he saw his dad's rough beard and thought it would be fun to act like a barber and give his dad a shave. He pretended to shave his dad with his toy razor and his dad pretended to fall asleep in the chair. Timmy was so happy that he could act like a grown-up and help his dad.

Ben and Lily were playing with their toys in the living room. They had cars, dolls, blocks and books. But they were bored. They had played with everything already.

"Let's do something else," Ben said. "This is boring."

"Like what?" Lily asked.

Ben looked around. He saw the door to the bathroom. He had an idea.

"Let's go to the bathroom and make bubbles!" he said.

Lily smiled. She liked bubbles. They were fun and pretty.

"OK, let's go!" she said.

They ran to the bathroom and closed the door. They turned on the faucet and filled the sink with water. They found some soap and poured it in. They stirred the water with their hands and made lots of bubbles.

"Wow, look at all the bubbles!" Ben said. "They are so big and white!"

He grabbed some bubbles and blew them in the air. Lily did the same. They laughed and clapped as the bubbles floated and popped.

They were having so much fun that they did not hear their mom calling them.

"Ben, Lily, where are you?" mom said. "It's time for lunch!"

She looked in the living room and saw their toys. She wondered where they were.

She walked to the bathroom and knocked on the door.

"Ben, Lily, are you in there?" she said.

Ben and Lily heard mom. They stopped playing and looked at each other.

"Uh-oh," Ben said. "We forgot to mention we were in the bathroom."

They opened the door and saw mom. She was not happy. She saw the water and the soap and the bubbles everywhere.

"Ben, Lily, what have you done?" she said. "This is a mess!"

Ben and Lily felt sorry. They did not mean to make a mess.

"We were just making bubbles, mom," Lily said. "We were bored."

Mom sighed. She knew they were bored, but they should have asked her first.

"Making bubbles is fun, but not in the bathroom," she said. "You could have made a mess in the bathtub or outside. And you should have told me where you were going."

She took them to the kitchen and gave them some towels.

She walked over to the plant and reached out her hand. But as soon as she touched it, she felt a sharp pain in her finger. She screamed and pulled back her hand. She saw a drop of blood on her finger, and a tiny thorn on the plant. She had touched a rose, and it had pricked her.

She ran to the house and cried for her mom. She felt very sorry and very scared. She had not been a very obedient girl.

One day, a prince came to visit her. He wanted to play with her, but he did not like to rock. He said, "Rocking is boring. Let's do something else. Let's run, or jump, or climb."

One day, Tom and his dog, Spot, went to the park. Tom was very excited because there was a big race happening. The winner of the race would get a prize. Tom wanted to win the prize, so he put on his fast shoes and got ready to run.

When the race started, Tom and Spot ran as fast as they could. They ran past trees and flowers, and they even saw a bird fly by. Tom knew he had to trust his legs and his dog, Spot, to help him win the race.

At the end of the race, Tom and Spot crossed the finish line first! They were so happy and excited. They won the prize, which was a big, shiny trophy. Tom and Spot took the prize home and showed it to their family. Everyone was proud of them for winning the race.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Jack. He was only three years old and he had a lot of questions about the world around him. One day he decided to go on an adventure and explore the city. 

Jack started walking down the street and soon he reached the subway. For Jack the subway was very busy, with people everywhere and the trains rushing by. He was very curious about all the activity and wondered why people were rushing so much. 

Jack asked an adult he saw nearby: "Why is this subway so busy?" The adult replied: "People here are always in a hurry because they want to reach their destination faster." 

Jack paused and thought about it. Then he smiled and said: "I think I understand, we should always take our time and enjoy life instead of always rushing!" 

The moral of this story is that it's important to find balance in life between rushing and slowing down. Taking the time to enjoy life will give us a better understanding of the world around us.

Sam and Max were brothers who lived on a big ranch with many animals. They liked to play with the horses, cows, and dogs, but they did not like to do their chores. One day, their mom told them to clean their room and help with the dishes, but they did not listen. They ran outside and played with the horses instead.

"Look, Max, I can ride this horse without a saddle!" Sam said, jumping on a brown horse.

"Wow, Sam, you are so brave!" Max said, clapping his hands.

But the horse did not like Sam. He bucked and kicked and threw Sam off his back. Sam landed on a pile of cow poop. He was dirty and smelly and hurt.

"Ow, ow, ow!" Sam cried.

Max laughed and pointed at Sam. "Ha, ha, ha! You are so silly, Sam! You look like a cow poop!"

But then, their mom came out and saw them. She was very angry. She scolded them for being naughty and lazy. She took them inside and made them take a bath and clean their room and do the dishes. She also said they could not play with the horses for a week. She punished them for being bad.

Sam and Max were very sad and embarrassed. They wished they had listened to their mom. They learned their lesson the hard way.

Mia was having a nice dream. She was flying like she was a butterfly. Suddenly the alarm rang. Mia woke up with a start. She remembered that today was an important day. It was the day of the big race. Mia had been practising for weeks and she was excited and a little scared.

Mia put on her running shoes and ran to the park. When she got there, Mia saw all of her friends and they started running together. Mia ran as fast as she could and soon she was crossing the finish line first.

The crowd cheered loudly and Mia was given the trophy. She held it in her hands and it glittered and shone in the sun. Mia was so happy.

"Well done Mia," said Mum. "You should be proud of yourself. You worked so hard to win this trophy".

Mia smiled and hugged her Mum tightly. She felt so brave and strong. Mia knew that nothing was too scary for her.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Lucy. She was three and liked to explore the world around her.

One day, Lucy was playing by the pond and she noticed something shining in the water. She decided to go and take a closer look. She stepped into the water, but as she moved, her foot struck against something hard. She bent down to see what it was and to Lucy's surprise, it was a bright, shiny coin.

The coin was fit perfectly in the palm of her hand. Lucy was so excited, she ran home to show her mum. Her mum was so proud that Lucy had found something so special in her adventures.

Every day, Lucy would go back to the pond and search for more treasures. She was always so happy to find things, proudly showing her mum all her discoveries.

Once there was an orange bear. He was very excited because he wanted to decorate. He went to the store to find something special. He saw oats and he thought they would be perfect. He bought a big bag of oats and went home.

Once upon a time, there was a tall giraffe named Gigi. Gigi loved to stand and look at the beautiful sky. One day, Gigi saw some clothes hanging on a tree.

Once upon a time, there were two furry friends - a lion and a tiger. The lion was a brave leader and he had a plan to go on a journey together.

They travelled for many days and on the final day, they reached a beautiful flowery meadow. The lion and tiger were so happy and hugged each other. Then, the lion leaned in and kissed the tiger on the cheek.

The tiger was so surprised and said, "What was that?"

The tiger felt special and the two furry friends hugged and promised to always stay friends and to keep going on new journeys.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy who was very eager. He wore his gear and went for a walk. He saw a big tree and decided to climb it.

Once there was a little girl called Julia. She was three years old and really loved to rock in her rocking chair. She would rock for hours and hours. Once upon a time, there was a small boy. He loved to go outside and explore. One day, he was walking through a field when he spotted a point. He was very curious, so he picked it up. Once upon a time, there was a fish named Nemo. Nemo loved to swim in the sea. One day, Nemo saw a shiny eraser on the ocean floor. He wanted to get it, so he dove down to pick it up.

Sam and Lily are friends. They like to play with blocks. They want to build a big tower with many blocks. They work hard to put the blocks on top of each other.

Once there was a little girl called Mira and she loved to play outside. One day, Mira spotted a net in the garden and she was super excited. She wanted to use it to play a game with her friends.

Once upon a time, there was a nice lady who always brought a yummy cake to the playground. All the kids loved to see her come. She was very patient with them and let them play with her cake before she ate it.

One day, one of the children noticed that the cake was starting to melt in the hot sun. He wanted to save it, so he ran to the lady and asked if he could help. She was very happy and said yes!

The little boy was so careful. He moved the cake to the shade and waited patiently for the lady to come back. When she returned, she was very pleased with his work and thanked him. She said he was very trustworthy.

The children played happily for the rest of the day and the cake was kept safe until it was time to eat. They all enjoyed it and the nice lady thanked the boy again for his help. 

From that day on, the children all trusted the boy to help them with important things. He was always so patient and they knew he would look after their yummy cake!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved playing outside in the sunshine, but sometimes her skin would get very dry. Her mommy would put lotion on her arms and legs to make them feel better.

One day, Lily was playing in the park when she saw a bottle of lotion on the ground. "Look, Mommy!" she exclaimed. "Lotion!" Her mommy warned her not to touch it because it might not be safe, but Lily didn't listen. She rubbed the lotion on her arms and legs and it felt very nice.

But then, something strange started to happen. Lily's skin turned red and itchy. She started to cry and her mommy rushed her to the hospital. The doctors said that the lotion was not harmless and had hurt her skin. Lily felt very sad and wished she had listened to her mommy's warning. From that day on, she always listened to her mommy and never touched anything that appeared to be dangerous.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved drinking juice, especially the fancy kind her mommy would make for her. One day, she asked her mommy for some juice but her mommy was busy on the phone. Lily waited patiently for her mommy to finish her call.

Finally, her mommy hung up the phone and turned to Lily. "What would you like, sweetie?" her mommy asked. "Juice please," Lily replied. Her mommy smiled and went to the kitchen to make her some fancy juice.

Lily was so happy to have her juice and she drank it all up. "Thank you, mommy," she said. Her mommy replied, "You're welcome, my dear. Anytime you want some juice, just let me know." Lily smiled and hugged her mommy. She loved her mommy's fancy juice and her mommy's love even more.

One day, a little girl named Lily went to visit her aunt. Her aunt had a wide, big house. Lily liked to play in the big house. She saw many toys and games. Lily was very happy.

In the afternoon, Lily felt tired. She lay down on a soft bed and fell asleep. She had a dream. In her dream, she was playing with her aunt in a wide, beautiful park. They were laughing and having fun.

Lily woke up from her dream and saw her aunt standing by the bed. "Did you have a good nap?" her aunt asked. "Yes," said Lily, "I had a nice dream. We were playing in a big park!" Her aunt smiled and said, "That sounds like a fun dream. Let's go to the park and play for real!" Lily was so excited, and they went to the park together.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named John. He was all alone in a big land. Everywhere he looked, there was nothing but trees, hills, and fields. John felt so lonely. 

He decided to explore and see if he could find someone or something to play with. He walked around for what seemed like forever, but there was no one around. He was so sad.

Suddenly, he saw a patch of bright colors! It was a meadow full of colorful flowers! John was so excited and started running around, picking the flowers and running in circles.

He stopped and saw something that made him even happier. A group of animals were playing around in the meadow! John was so happy. He joined the animals and started playing with them.

John had so much fun! He ran, laughed, and played with them for what seemed like hours. Finally, he said goodbye to the animals, and started walking home.

John was no longer lonely. He always remembered his day in the meadow and the animals he met, and he smiled.

Once upon a time, a boy called Bobby wanted to show everyone his favourite photo. He found the furry photo in a drawer and wanted to share it with the whole world. So, he decided to go outside and pull his furry photo around his neighbourhood. He was so proud to show everyone his special photo.

As Bobby walked around, he could see people's faces light up as he showed them his photo. Some were so happy, they clapped and cheered! Everyone seemed to love Bobby's furry photo.

But then, after some time, Bobby started to get tired. His arms were aching from pulling the photo around, so he decided to take a break. He sat down, resting in the sun with his furry photo, and had a little nap.

When he woke up, Bobby decided it was time to get going again. He put his furry photo back up and continued to pull it around the neighbourhood with a big smile on his face. Eventually, Bobby went home with a big happy feeling inside. He knew he had shared his favourite photo with the world!

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Jessie. She was 3 year old. One day she was feeling sad. Her parents asked her why she was feeling so blue.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He was a happy youth who loved to play outside. One morning, Timmy woke up early to go outside and play. But when he went to put on his shoes, he saw a disgusting spider on them!

Once upon a time, there was a country full of happy people. It was a peaceful place, where everyone smiled and acted nice to each other.

Lily and Ben were playing with blocks. They wanted to make a big tower. They put many blocks on top of each other. But the tower was not steady. It wobbled and shook.

"Be careful, Ben!" Lily said. "Don't put that block on the top. It will make the tower fall down."

But Ben did not listen. He liked the block. It was red and shiny. He wanted to put it on the top. He reached for the block and lifted it up.

"Ben, no!" Lily shouted. "Stop!"

But it was too late. Ben put the block on the top. The tower could not hold it. It toppled over and crashed to the floor. The blocks scattered everywhere.

Lily and Ben were shocked. They looked at the mess. They felt sad and angry. They blamed each other.

"It's your fault, Ben!" Lily said. "You made the tower fall down. You are a bad boy!"

"No, it's your fault, Lily!" Ben said. "You were bossy and mean. You are a bad girl!"

They started to cry. They did not want to play with each other anymore. They turned away and crossed their arms.

Mom heard the noise. She came to see what happened. She saw the blocks and the tears. She felt troubled. She wanted to help.

"What's wrong, Lily and Ben?" Mom asked. "Why are you crying?"

Lily and Ben told Mom what happened. They pointed at each other and said bad words. Mom listened and sighed.

"I see," Mom said. "You both wanted to make a big tower. But you did not work together. You did not listen to each other. You did not share. That's why the tower fell down. And that's why you are unhappy."

Lily and Ben looked at Mom. They knew she was right. They felt sorry. They wanted to say sorry.

"Mom, can we try again?" Lily asked. "Can we make a new tower?"

"Yes, you can," Mom said. "But you have to decide something first. Do you want to play alone or together?"

Lily and Ben thought for a moment. They looked at each other. They smiled.

"We want to play together, Mom," Ben said. "We are sorry. We are friends."

Mom smiled too. She hugged them and gave them a kiss.

"That's good," Mom said. "I'm proud of you. Now, go and have fun. And remember, be kind and gentle. And don't put too many blocks on the top."

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Annie. She was three years old and loved to play. One day she was playing in the garden with her pet dog. Suddenly, the pet dog jumped onto the grass and Annie heard a pop. When she looked around, she saw that her shoe was gone!
