The fight got worse, until finally, they both got hurt. Jack and Jill hadn't seen each other since.

Once upon a time there was a happy little girl. Her Mama and Papa loved her very much. 

Every day, the little girl and her Mama went to the park. She was so cheerful as she ran around playing with the other children. 

But the park started to get messy. The little girl saw a lot of waste lying around. She couldn't believe how messy it was! 

So her Mama gave her a special task. The little girl was to wash the park to make it look beautiful again. 

The little girl filled a bucket to the brim with soapy water and a sponge. She scrubbed and cleaned until the park was sparkly clean again. 

When she was done, the little girl beamed with pride. She had done a great job and the park looked wonderful. 

She ran back to her Mama, who praised her hard work with a big smile. The little girl was so cheerful and the park was clean again.

Once upon a time there was a Daddy and his little girl. The little girl loved spaghetti! Every day Daddy would make her a really nice and comfortable spaghetti dinner.

One day the little girl noticed something wrong with Daddy's spaghetti. It was all lumpy, and it didn't taste so good. The little girl asked Daddy what was wrong. He said he didn't know how to fix it.

The little girl thought hard and then she had an idea. She ran over to the kitchen drawer and took out a spoon. She showed Daddy how to stir the spaghetti and fix it so that it tasted nice again.

Daddy and the little girl ate the spaghetti and it was yummy! The little girl was so proud that she could help Daddy fix the spaghetti. Daddy was proud too, and gave the little girl a big hug. They both shared a happy spaghetti dinner and had a wonderful time.

Once upon a time, there was a big elephant named Ellie. Ellie was very upset because she couldn't find her favorite toy. She looked everywhere but couldn't find it.

Then she saw her friend, a little monkey named Max. Ellie asked Max, "Have you seen my toy?" Max said, "Yes, I grabbed it by mistake. I'm sorry."

Ellie was happy to hear that Max had her toy. Max gave it back to Ellie and they played together. They had so much fun that Ellie forgot she was upset earlier. From that day on, Ellie and Max played together every day.

Once there was a very proud little boy named Randy. He loved to play baseball every day, and his family was very proud of him. One day, Randy and a friend had a fight about who was the best baseball player. Randy thought he was the best, but his friend disagreed.

Randy's father watched the fight and he was very sad. He took Randy aside and said, "I want you to listen to me. It's not nice to fight with your friends. I want you to be a good example and show everyone that you can play baseball and be proud at the same time." 

Randy listened to his father and agreed to calm down and work things out with his friend. They made up, and Randy was happy. His father was proud. From then on, Randy played baseball with his friend, and they both were proud of the way they played. 

No more fights ever happened after that, and Randy and his friend had a ball playing baseball together. His father was proud of them for finding a better way to work out their differences.

Once there was a girl named Jess who loved to play. She liked to play in the park and on the swings. One day Jess was embarrased. Everyone was looking at her funny because she had shampoo in her hair.

She had been playing in the park and accidentally knocked over a bottle of shampoo. It spilled all over her. Her friends started to laugh and Jess felt embarrassed.

Jess started to cry because she felt embarrassed. Her mom came over and saw what had happened. She took her daughter back to the house and told her not to worry.

In the bathroom, Jess's mom put warm water in the tub and helped Jess wash the shampoo out. When Jess emerged from the bathroom, she felt much better. Her mom smiled and said, "You'll be okay, now."

One day, a little girl named Lily went to the park with her mom. She saw a big, scary dog and got scared. "Mommy, that dog is scary," she said. "Don't worry, Lily," her mom said, "just ignore the dog and it will go away." 

Lily and her mom walked around the park and saw some trees with peaches on them. "Look, Mommy, peaches!" Lily said. "Can we pick one?" "Sure, Lily," her mom said, "let's pick a peach and eat it." 

As they were eating the peach, Lily saw the scary dog again. "Mommy, the scary dog is back," she said. "Don't worry, Lily," her mom said, "just ignore it and keep eating your peach." 

Lily did as her mom said and soon the dog went away. "See, Lily," her mom said, "sometimes it's best to just ignore things that scare us." Lily nodded and took another bite of her juicy peach.

Mama was sitting on the porch, enjoying a mild day. She was sipping her drink when, suddenly, her three-year-old son ran out of the house. He had a smile on his face and a look of excitement in his eye.

"Mama, can I have a drink too?" he asked.

Mama smiled and nodded. She filled a cup with her drink and handed it to her son.

He took a sip and his face lit up. "Yum! This drink is so yummy!"

Mama's heart filled with love for her son. She gave him a big hug and kissed him on his head.

"I love you, my boy," she said.

He smiled and hugged her back. "I love you too, Mama."

One day, a little girl named Lily went to the park. She liked to play on the swings and slide. As she played, she saw a big dog. The dog was very friendly and came to say hello.

Lily said, "Hi dog! Do you want to play with me?" The dog wagged its tail, showing it was happy. They played together for a while, running and laughing. But then, Lily accidentally stepped on the dog's toe.

"Ouch!" cried the dog. Lily felt bad and said, "I'm sorry, dog. I didn't mean to hurt you." The dog looked at her and said, "It's okay, Lily. Just be careful next time."

Lily wanted to make the dog feel better, so she gave it a gentle slap on its back, like a pat. The dog wagged its tail and they continued to play. They played until the sun went down and it was time to go home. Lily knew she had made a new friend and they would play together whenever they were both available at the park.

One day, two friends went outside to play. They were very playful and ran around in the warm sunshine.

Suddenly they heard a sound! Something had split open. The sound had come from a tree, and the friends were curious to know what had happened. They went over and saw that an enormous orange fruit had split open and was now spilling out its juicy insides.

The friends laughed and smiled. This was such a special day! They ran over and picked up the pieces of the split fruit - it was so delicious!

The friends ate the fruit and their faces were covered in sticky juice. They laughed and played for the rest of the day until it was time for them to go home.

Once upon a time, there was a big village with lots of houses and people. The village was very beautiful with lots of trees and flowers everywhere. One day, a little girl wanted to borrow her friend's toy. She walked to her friend's house and knocked on the door. Her friend said yes and gave her the toy to play with. The little girl was very happy and played with the toy all day. When it was time to go home, she said thank you to her friend and returned the toy. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Eric. He wanted to go West, but he knew it was far away and it would take a long time to get there.

One day, Eric asked his mom, "Mom, how can I go West?"

His mom replied, "Eric, it's not easy. You'll have to walk and it will take a long time. But if you save up your money, you can buy a ticket on a plane."

So Eric saved up all the money he could. But when the day came for him to go West, he brought a heavy suitcase and when he got to the airport, he could not find a ticket he could afford.

He was feeling really sad until he saw a man with a ticket for West. He asked the man if he could buy the ticket and the man said, "Sorry, but I have a plane to catch and I need to go."

Eric begged the man three times, but he wouldn't give him the ticket. Eric was so disappointed. He felt like his hopes of going West had been dried up like a leaf in the sun. He could not go West.

Once upon a time there was a nice person. They went to the shop and wanted to buy something. They saw something funny and wanted to buy it. So, they gave the shopkeeper their money and they got the funny thing.

The person was so happy to have the funny thing. They looked at it and smiled. They showed it to everyone they saw. Everyone thought it was so funny. 

The person was so happy with their purchase. They decided to take it everywhere they went. Everyone thought it was funny.

The person continued to show their funny thing to their friends and family. Everywhere they went, people would smile and laugh when they saw it.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a very pale dancer. She loved to dance, but she was sad because she had a big problem to solve. The dancer thought and thought, but she could not think of a solution. She asked her friends for help, but none of them could solve it. She was starting to feel very sad.

Suddenly, the dancer had an idea. She went and told her friends the idea and they all clapped. The dancer felt so happy that she started to dance. As she danced, she seemed to find the answer to her problem. She smiled and clapped for herself.

The pale dancer had solved her problem! She was so excited and happy, she danced all day. The dancer invited all of her friends to celebrate. They all had a great time dancing and laughing together.

The pale dancer was so pleased that she had solved her problem. She smiled and danced, knowing that she had done something great.

Once upon a time there were two friends, John and Sally. John was very jealous of Sally because she had a shiny new fork. 

John said to Sally â€œthat is a very nice fork you have.â€

But Sally replied â€œyes it is. Do you want to hold it?â€

John was so jealous that he grabbed the fork and angrily threw it to the ground. It was destroyed!

Sally was very sad and started to cry. John felt bad for what he had done, he said â€œIâ€™m sorry. I was jealous of your fork. I will help you find a new one.â€ 

Sally smiled and said â€œthank you, John. That would be very nice of you.â€ 

John and Sally went off to look for a new fork and soon enough they found one. Sally was very happy and so was John. 

The end.

Lily and Ben are playing in the park. They see a big brown dog. The dog is friendly and wags its tail. Lily and Ben want to pet the dog.

"Hello, dog!" Lily says. She reaches out her arm to touch the dog's fur. The dog licks her hand and makes a happy sound.

"Can I pet him too?" Ben asks. He moves closer to the dog. The dog looks at him and blinks. Ben thinks the dog is cute and funny.

"Sure, you can pet him," Lily says. She smiles at Ben. They both stroke the dog's back and ears. The dog enjoys the attention and rolls over on the grass.

"Who are you, dog?" Ben wonders. He looks at the dog's collar. There is a tag with a name and a phone number. The name is Max.

"His name is Max," Lily reads. She can read some words. She points at the tag. "And this is his phone number. He has a home and a family."

"Maybe he got lost," Ben says. He feels sorry for Max. He hopes his family will find him soon.

"Let's call his family," Lily says. She has an idea. She runs to the bench where their mom is sitting. She asks for her mom's phone. She tells her mom about Max.

"Good idea, Lily," mom says. She is proud of Lily and Ben. She takes the phone and dials the number on the tag. She talks to someone on the phone. She tells them where they are and that they found Max.

Soon, a car arrives at the park. A man and a woman get out of the car. They look happy and relieved. They run to Max and hug him.

"Max, we missed you so much!" the woman says. She kisses Max on the nose. "Thank you for finding him," she says to Lily, Ben and mom.

"You're welcome," Lily, Ben and mom say. They are glad that Max is safe and reunited with his family.

"Can we play with Max again?" Lily asks.

"Of course, you can," the man says. He smiles at Lily and Ben. "Max loves to play with new friends. Maybe we can come to the park again sometime."

"That would be nice," Lily and Ben say. They wave goodbye to Max and his family. They watch them drive away. They are happy that they helped Max. They go back to playing in the park.

Once upon a time, there was a lovely car. The car was pink and shiny, and it made all the children smile when they saw it. 

Every day, the car would take a special little girl and her mommy for a ride. The little girl loved the car and enjoyed pointing out all the colors she saw and talking about the different places they could go.

One day, the little girl asked her mommy if they could share the car with someone else. The mommy said they sure could! So the little girl went around the neighborhood and asked if her friends would like to come and share the lovely car with her. 

Soon, all the little girl's friends were in the car and they took turns driving it around the block. All the children laughed and talked and waved at the people they passed. 

They had loads of fun and agreed that sharing the car was such a good idea! They were all so happy and thanked the little girl for sharing her lovely car. 

The end!

Anna and Ben were twins who liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a big dog with a bandage on his leg. The dog looked sad and lonely.

"Can we pet him?" Anna asked.

"I don't know. Maybe he is angry or scared," Ben said.

They went closer to the dog and saw a man sitting on a bench. He had a hat and a beard and a book.

"Hello, children. Do you like my dog?" the man said.

"Yes, he is very cute. What is his name?" Anna said.

"His name is Lucky. He hurt his leg in an accident, but he is getting better," the man said.

"Can we pet him?" Ben asked.

"Sure, he is very friendly. He likes children," the man said.

Anna and Ben petted Lucky and he wagged his tail. He licked their faces and made them laugh.

"You are very kind, children. Lucky is happy to meet you," the man said.

"Thank you, sir. You are very nice. Can we come back and see Lucky again?" Anna asked.

"Of course, you are welcome anytime. I come here every day to read and watch the birds. I like the park. It is peaceful and beautiful," the man said.

"You are very wise, sir. We like the park too. It is fun and colorful," Ben said.

The man smiled and gave them a candy. Anna and Ben thanked him and said goodbye to Lucky. They ran back to their mom, who was waiting for them.

"Mom, we met a wise man and a cute dog. The dog had a hurt leg, but he was happy. The man gave us candy and a book. He said we can come back and see them again," Anna said.

"That sounds wonderful, my dears. I'm glad you made new friends. What is the book about?" mom asked.

"It is about animals and plants and stars and things. The man said we can learn a lot from them. He said we should always believe in ourselves and be kind to others," Ben said.

"That is very good advice, my dears. I'm proud of you. You are very smart and sweet. Let's go home and read the book together," mom said.

Anna and Ben hugged their mom and walked home. They were happy and curious. They wanted to see Lucky and the wise man again. They wanted to learn more about the world. They believed they could do anything.

Patty was a happy little girl. She liked to play with her toys, but her favorite thing to do was to touch the string. It felt so nice!

One day, Patty was playing with the string when her mom said it was time to go. Patty was embarrassed. She didn't want to leave the string. She wanted to touch it more.

So, Patty's mom told her that she could take the string with her. Patty was so excited! She grabbed the string, gave it a big hug, and put it in her pocket.

Now, no matter where Patty went, she could touch the string whenever she wanted. It was so nice. Every time she felt embarrassed, she would just touch the string and it would make her feel better.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to draw with pastel colors. Her mommy bought her a big box of pastels for her birthday. Lily was so happy that she hugged her mommy and said "I love you!"

One day, Lily went to the park with her mommy. There were many children playing and it was very noisy. Lily didn't like the noisy sounds. She covered her ears and said "It's too noisy here!"

But then, Lily saw a little girl who was sad because she lost her toy. Lily wanted to help her. She gave the little girl her favorite pastel drawing and said "I love you, you can have this." The little girl smiled and hugged Lily. From that day on, Lily wasn't bothered by the noisy sounds anymore. She felt happy because she helped someone and she knew that love is more important than anything else.

Once upon a time, there lived an old man in a forest. Everyday, the old man would take long walks in the greenery. He admired the trees, the animals, and the birds. He was so happy and kind.

One day, the old man's little granddaughter came to visit the forest. She was so impressed with the greenery, she wanted to run and explore everywhere. The old man wanted to encourage his granddaughter, so he started running around with her. 

He taught her the names of the trees, and showed her where the birds sang. He even picked up some pretty flowers to give to his granddaughter. Together, they laughed and giggled.

The old man was so full of love for his granddaughter. He wanted to encourage her and make sure she felt special. Afterall, there is no place like a forest to feel the kindness and joy of nature.

Once upon a time there was a fit girl named Alice. She was very curious and always wanted to learn new things.

One day, she asked her dad to teach her something new. Her dad thought for a moment and then said "Let's start with counting." So they began to count numbers together, one, two, three.

Alice was so excited that she said "Can you teach me more? Can you teach me to read?" Her dad happily agreed and they started to read together.

Alice was a very fast learner and she was soon able to read all kinds of books. She was so proud of her new skill that she wanted to show everyone.

The next day, she went up to her mom and said "Look mom, I can read now, Dad taught me." Her mom was so impressed and gave her a big hug. From then on, Alice was the best reader in the family.

Once upon a time there was a family who liked to mail things. They found it very fun and exciting. One day the family decided to mail a package that was very heavy. They used lots of tape and added extra padding. 

When they went to the post office they were surprised by how much it cost to mail the package. They had to pay so much that they almost didn't want to do it. But they decided to mail it anyway.

A few days later the family received a letter in the mail. Inside the letter was bad news; the heavy package had broken in the mail! The family was very sad.

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Mary. Mary was a brave girl, and she loved adventures. One day, she went to a big forest. As she was walking, she noticed something red in the bushes. She was scared at first, but then she realized it was just a big red monster.

The monster wasn't scary after all. He was friendly and he wanted to be Mary's friend. She was very happy! The two played in the forest for one whole day. Mary laughed and smiled as the friendly monster showed her all kinds of fun things.

At the end of the day, Mary realized that the monster had to go. She waved goodbye and promised to come back and play with him again soon. Mary was sad, but she was also brave and happy. She had just made a new friend!

Once upon a time, a little girl named Lily went to visit her grandma's farm. There were many animals on the farm, like cows, pigs, and chickens. Lily loved to pet the animals, but she was scared of the cows because they were very big.

One day, Lily was playing in the hay when she saw a little mouse. She wanted to catch it, so she tried to be very quiet. But when she got close, the mouse ran away. Lily was sad, so she went to find her grandma.

Her grandma was in the garden picking vegetables. Lily told her about the mouse and how she wanted to catch it. Her grandma smiled and said, "Sometimes, things are too deep to catch. But you can always try to pinch them!" Lily didn't understand what her grandma meant, but she was happy to hear her grandma's kind words.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and her favorite was a fluffy teddy bear named Teddy. One day, Lily went to the park to play with her friends. While playing, she saw a man playing a beautiful flute. She thought it was adorable and wanted to learn how to play it.

Later that day, Lily went to her grandma's house for dinner. Her grandma made her favorite meal, spaghetti and meatballs. After dinner, Lily's grandma gave her a big hug and said, "I have a surprise for you!" Lily was excited to see what it was. Her grandma brought out a brand new flute for her to play! Lily was so happy and started to play it right away.

As she was playing, she noticed Teddy was looking a little sad. So, she decided to play a sweet melody for him. Suddenly, Teddy's paw started to move and he pinched her on the nose! Everyone laughed and Lily realized that Teddy loved the flute too. From that day on, Lily and Teddy played beautiful music together and they were the happiest friends in the world.

Once there was a boy called Henry. He loved animals and wanted to attach to them all the time. But he wasn't allowed. His mom told him it was against the law. Henry was very hurt about this. 

His mom told him that if he wanted to attach to animals, he had to do it in a safe way. So Henry made a plan. He decided to only attach to animals when he was outside with his mom. 

So every day when he went outside, he would check for animals. He would ask his mom if it was allowed and then attach to them if it was okay. 

Henry was very happy to be able to attach to animals again. He felt safe and secure, knowing that he was sticking to the law. Best of all, he wasn't hurt anymore!

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Lily. Lily was full of surprises. Every morning, she woke up feeling very lively.

One morning, Lily had an idea. She wanted to mix all her favourite ingredients together to make a special surprise. She eagerly ran to the kitchen and started to roll up her sleeves.

First, she took some flour, sugar and milk and put them in a bowl. Then, she added some blueberries and a pinch of cocoa powder. 

Lily started stirring her mixture, and very soon it smelt delicious. When it was ready she called out to her parents: "Mama, Papa! Come here! Look at my surprise!"

Her parents came into the kitchen, amazed by the delicious smell in the air. They tried some of Lily's mixture and they could not believe how good it tasted.

"Oh Lily, this is wonderful! What did you make?" her parents asked.

Lily looked up at them with a big smile and replied: "I made a tasty and lively surprise! I mixed everything together, just like you taught me".

Once upon a time there was a small girl who loved roses. She played in the garden every day, looking at the flowers. 

One day, she saw a beautiful rose and she wanted to pick it. She tried, but it was too high. She asked her mum for help.

Her mum nodded and smiled. She said it's easy, just watch. She raised her hand and the rose floated down to her. The small girl was so excited! She said thank you and hugged her mum.

The small girl then made a present for her mum with the rose. She gave it to her with a big hug and her mum smiled. She said it was the most beautiful gift she ever received. They both hugged and it was a happy day.

One day, a little boy named Tim found a colorful watch on the ground. It was very pretty with lots of colors. He picked it up and put it on his wrist. Tim liked the watch very much.

Tim showed the watch to his friend, Sally. "Look at my watch!" he said. Sally smiled and said, "It's so nice! I wish I had one too." Tim felt happy that Sally liked his watch. But he did not know that the watch could ring.

Later, while they were playing, the watch started to ring. Tim and Sally were surprised. They looked at the watch and saw a button. Tim pushed the button, and the ringing stopped. They laughed and played more.

The next day, Tim and Sally played again. The watch rang, and they knew what to do. They pushed the button and laughed. The colorful watch made their playtime more fun.

Edwin was a jolly boy who loved adventures. One summer day, he was walking through the meadow when he spotted something peculiar. He squinted his eyes to get a better look. On the grass was a spear, but it was so long that Edwin couldn't measure it with his arms! 

He decided to find something else he could use to measure it. After a while, he found a stick he could use to measure the length of the spear. He placed one end of the stick next to the spear, and then he stretched his arm out to the other end. The stick was just the right size! He marked the grass with a twig to remember the length of the spear and moved on.

The next day, Edwin had a jolly surprise. He walked back to the meadow, and the spear was still there. He measured it again with the stick and was glad that he had been accurate in his guess the day before.

He picked up the spear and said to himself, â€œThis spear is the perfect size for an adventure!â€ With that, Edwin ran all the way home, eager to start his next exciting adventure.

It was a long day for the three friends, Jamie, Steve and Jack. They were playing in the park. Suddenly, Jack saw a tall stand with an ice cream on top. He wanted it very badly.

Jack said, "Let's steal the ice cream!" Jamie said, "No, no! We cannot do that!" But Jack was determined. He slowly walked up to the stand and grabbed the ice cream.

Steve said, "Jack! You are going to get into trouble!" Jack started to cry.

But then a voice said, "What is going on here?" A tall man came out from behind the stand. "My son said he saw three boys trying to steal this ice cream. Is that true?"

Jack said, "Yes, sir. We did steal it." The man smiled. "Well, I was going to give my son this ice cream but since you have been so honest, you can have it!"

The boys cheered and they all ate the long, delicious ice cream together. They smiled and enjoyed the rest of the day in the park.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved to go on exciting adventures. She wanted to go everywhere she could and meet all kinds of new people.

One day, her parents told her it was time to pack for the most exciting of all adventures! She was excited and wanted to know where she was going. 

Her parents smiled and said, "We're going on a trip to find the most expensive bean! It's far away but we'll get there!"

The little girl couldn't believe it. She packed all her favorite things and set out on the hunt for the most expensive bean! 

One day, after their long and tiring search, they found the most expensive bean, just as her parents had promised. She had never seen anything so beautiful in all her life! 

The little girl held the bean close, feeling the excitement of discovering something so valuable. 

Her parents smiled and said, "We knew you could do it, now let's go home and celebrate your great find!"

Once upon a time there were two friends named Mary and Jack. Mary loved math and Jack was very fearful of it. Every day, Mary would keep asking Jack to try math with her. But every day, Jack said no. 

One day, Mary got an idea. She would keep trying to make math fun with Jack until he was ready to try it. She made math games and she kept explaining the math problems in a fun way. 

Little by little, Jack stopped being fearful of math and he started to have fun with it. He even kept practicing math with Mary! 

Now, Jack loves math and he and Mary are great math friends. They laugh and play and keep learning more math together.

Once upon a time there was a modest building. Inside the building lived a family of four. Mama, Papa, Nick and Nora. One day the family had an argument. Mama and Papa were shouting, and Nick and Nora became very scared. 

Nick and Nora felt that they needed to get out of the building. The two split up and ran out of the building. They found a big tree in a nearby park and Nick climbed it, hoping that he could get away from it all. Nora saw him and decided to join him so the two could talk. 

As Nick looked around from the tree he realised that the family's argument was like a tiny drop in the world. It seemed so small compared to everything else - the sky, the trees and the sun. He asked Nora, "How can the family's argument be so big and scary when everything else is so big and peaceful?". Nora thought for a moment and then said, "Maybe it's because we are too close to it, and it's hard to see the bigger picture". 

The two realised that sometimes it's better to take a few steps back and look at a situation from a broader perspective. This gave them the courage to go back inside the modest building and talk to their family.

Once upon a time, there was a boy who loved to pretend. He believed that the sky was green, and the trees could move. One day, he was pretending to be a superhero and he saw a trap.

The boy was a bit scared, but he was brave too. He knew he could use his pretending powers to help. He imagined that the trap was a way to help others.

So the boy opened the trap, and out came a friendly fox! The fox was very thankful, and gave the boy a big hug. The boy was so happy that he had been able to help. The fox ran off happily into the woods and the boy knew that he had done something good.

The boy continued to pretend, feeling more and more helpful each day. And the trap was never seen again.

Tom and Lily are playing in the park. They see a big tree with many birds. They want to look at the birds. They walk to the tree and are very quiet. They do not want to scare the birds.

They see a red bird, a blue bird, and a yellow bird. They are very pretty. Tom points to the red bird and says, "Look, Lily, a red bird!" Lily points to the blue bird and says, "Look, Tom, a blue bird!" They smile and clap.

But then they see a man under the tree. He is holding a note. He looks sad. He does not see Tom and Lily. Tom and Lily are curious. They want to know what the note says. They walk to the man and say, "Hello, mister, what is your note?"

The man looks up and sees Tom and Lily. He is surprised. He says, "Hello, kids, this is a note from my friend. He says he is sorry. He cannot play with me today. He is sick. I am sad."

Tom and Lily feel sorry for the man. They say, "We are sorry, mister. We hope your friend gets well soon. Do you want to play with us? We can show you the birds. They are very pretty."

The man smiles and says, "Thank you, kids. You are very kind. I would like to play with you. You can show me the birds. They are very pretty."

Tom and Lily are happy. They take the man's hand and lead him to the tree. They point to the birds and tell him their names. The man listens and laughs. He forgets his note and his sadness. He enjoys the birds and the kids. They have fun in the park.

Once upon a time there were two best friends named Tom and Belle. Tom was a kind and compassionate bear and Belle was an adorable little rabbit. 

Tom and Belle were always playing together. They liked to play hide-and-seek and hopscotch.

One day, Tom and Belle were a bit tired. So, Tom suggested they take a nap. Belle agreed and the two put their heads on a pot and fell asleep.

When they woke up, Belle smiled and said, "That was a great nap, wasn't it Tom?"

Tom smiled back and said, "Yes, it sure was. I felt so refreshed and relaxed."

Tom and Belle enjoyed napping together and stayed friends for a long time. The compassionate bear and the little rabbit were always there for each other.

It was a bright and sunny day. Jack was very excited. He wanted to go outside and have some fun. He put on his shoes, grabbed a toy and went outside.

Jack first went to the slide. He was so excited. He went up and down, up and down. It was so fun. He would laugh every time he slid down.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and make crafts with her mom. One day, she wanted to make a necklace with pretty beads. Once there was a berry who had a fit. He was feeling very sad so he decided to bury himself in the ground. He dug himself a nice, deep hole and hopped inside. But when he went to cover himself up, he heard voices. It was two children who were walking past the berry patch.

Once upon a time there were two friends. One was brave and the other was foolish. The brave friend said to the foolish one, "Let us try something new together, so we can be successful."

One night, Mike was in his bed. He had his blanket and he felt very cozy. Mike looked out the window and saw a big, white moon. He felt scared.

Once upon a time, there was a playful puppy named Max. Max loved to run and jump and play with his toys. One day, Max's owner, a kind girl named Lily, decided to teach Max a new trick.

"OK, Tom!" Lila said. "But we have to be back before lunch. Mommy said so."

They ran up the hill, holding hands. They felt the wind in their hair and the sun on their faces. They laughed and sang and talked. They did not see the dark clouds in the sky.

When they reached the top of the hill, they saw a big lake. It was blue and shiny and calm. They also saw a lot of mist. It was white and soft and cold. It covered the trees and the grass and the rocks. It made everything look like a fairy tale.

"Wow, Tom! Look at the mist! It's so pretty!" Lila said.

"Yes, Lila! It's like a cloud on the ground! Let's go inside!" Tom said.

They ran into the mist, feeling curious and excited. They thought they would see something amazing. But they did not. They only saw more mist. It was thick and wet and blurry. It made everything look the same. They could not see the lake or the hill or the park. They could not see each other.

"Tom, where are you?" Lila called.

"Lila, where are you?" Tom called.

They tried to find each other, but they could not. They tried to find the way back, but they could not. They felt scared and lost and alone. They wished they had not gone into the mist. They regretted leaving the park. They wanted to see their mommy.

Suddenly, they heard a loud roar. It was deep and angry and scary. It came from the mist. It sounded like a monster. It sounded like a dragon.

"Tom, help!" Lila screamed.

"Lila, run!" Tom shouted.

They ran as fast as they could, hoping to escape the roar. They did not know where they were going. They did not know what they would find. They only knew they had to get out of the mist.

They ran and ran, until they saw a bright light. It was the sun. It had come out from behind the clouds. It had chased away the mist. It had shown them the way.

They ran out of the mist, and saw the lake and the hill and the park. They also saw their mommy. She was waiting for them at the bottom of the hill. She looked worried and angry and relieved. She had heard their screams. She had come to find them.

"Lila, Tom, where have you been?" Mommy asked. "I've been looking for you everywhere. You're late for lunch. You're wet and dirty and cold. You're in big trouble."

Lila and Tom ran to their mommy, feeling sorry and happy and safe. They hugged her and kissed her and told her what had happened. They told her about the mist and the roar and the dragon.

Mommy listened and shook her head and smiled. She did not believe them. She thought they had made up a story. She thought they had a big imagination. She did not know they had seen an enormous dragon. It was hiding in the mist. It was watching them. It was waiting for another chance.

Once upon a time, there was a lazy cat named Mittens. Mittens liked to sleep all day on a soft velvet pillow. One day, Mittens went outside to play and found a shiny key. Mittens didn't know what the key was for, so he asked his friend, the dog. The dog told Mittens that the key was for a lock. 

Mittens went on an adventure to find the lock. He looked high and low until he found a big wooden box with a lock on it. Mittens tried the key and it worked! Inside the box was a beautiful velvet blanket. Mittens was so happy he found the lock and the velvet blanket. He took a nap on the blanket and dreamed of his next adventure. The end.

The night was quiet. Amy was 3 years old and was going to see a firework show for the first time. She was excited! Her mom looked down at her and smiled.

Amy and her mom walked to the park. There were lots of people and colourful lights in the sky. Amy paused and looked up - it was beautiful! Everywhere she looked, there were fireworksthat were sparkling and shining. It was like a dream!

Finally, the firework show started. Amy was so amazed! The colours were so pretty and the noise was very loud! When the show was over, Amy and her mom walked home. Amy paused one more time, and looked up at the sky. It was so quiet but she knew the colourful firework show would always stay in her memory.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to draw and always carried a pencil with her. One day, she went to a show where people sang and danced. When it was over, everyone clapped and Lily learned a new word - "applaud". She clapped too and felt happy.

But then, a boy pushed her and took her pencil. He was being rude. Lily felt sad and didn't know what to do. Suddenly, the people on stage saw what happened and they applauded Lily. They made her feel better and gave her a new pencil. Lily was happy again and learned that not everyone is rude.

One day, John's family got a dog. John was very excited. He loved his new dog and wanted to play with it all day. He ran to the dog and gave it a big hug. But the dog felt uncomfortable and started to bark.

John's dad stepped in. He told John, "We need to value this dog's feelings. He might be scared because he's new to the family." 

John thought about it and nodded. He said, "I understand. I'll be more careful and gentle the next time I play with him."

John's dad smiled and said, "That's my boy. You showed good understanding and empathy. Now why don't you two go for a walk together?"

John was happy. He grabbed the leash and ran out the door with the dog. He was careful to walk slowly so the dog felt safe. John knew he valued the dog's feelings, and this made him happy.

Once upon a time, there was a brown bear named Bobby. Bobby lived in a big forest with his friends, the squirrels and the rabbits. One day, Bobby was walking in the forest when he saw a needle on the ground. He picked it up and looked at it. "What is this?" he asked himself.

Just then, one of the squirrels came up to him and said, "That's a needle, Bobby. Be careful, it can snap if you're not careful." Bobby was scared, so he put the needle back on the ground and walked away.

Later that day, Bobby and the squirrels were playing hide and seek when they heard a loud snap. They looked around and saw that the needle had snapped in half! "I'm glad we didn't touch it again," said one of the rabbits. Bobby nodded his head in agreement. From that day on, they knew to be careful around sharp things like needles.

One day, a little girl was feeling very eager. She ran over to her special toy box and took out a plate. Then she placed it on the floor and began to roll it around. Each time it rolled, it made funny noises which made the little girl giggle. She kept rolling the plate around for a very long time. She was having so much fun! After a while, the little girl's mom came in and asked if she was ready for dinner. So the little girl put away her plate, and happily she went off to dinner with her mom.

Once there was an old man who was so restless he couldn't stay still. He wanted to go outside and do something new. So he asked his wife if he could go for a walk. But she refused. She said, "No, you need to stay inside and rest." He was sad, but he knew his wife was right. 

So he stayed inside and did some chores. He still felt restless though and all he could do was think about how he wanted to go outside. Then he had an idea! He got up and put on his coat. He was nearly out the door when his wife saw him. 

He asked again if he could go out. His wife refused again. She said, "No, stay inside and rest." The old man was disappointed, but he knew his wife was right. He was too old to go out anyway. So he went back to his chores and tried to be content.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. He loved to gaze at the sky and dream of finding great treasure. One day, he saw a big, shiny box under a tree.

Tim ran to his friend, Sam, and said, "I found a treasure! Let's open it together!" Sam looked at the box and said, "We should ask a grown-up first." But Tim did not listen. He wanted the treasure all for himself.

Tim opened the box, and out came a big, angry bee. It stung Tim on his nose. It hurt a lot, and Tim cried. Sam hugged Tim and said, "Next time, listen to your friends." The moral of the story is to always listen to your friends and ask for help before doing something you are not sure about.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Lily, and she loved to play outside. She found the most joy in chasing the sunset as it drifted across the sky. 

One day, her big brother asked her if she wanted to join him in playing a game of kick-ball. Lily was so excited! She had never kicked a ball before, but she was eager to try. 

They made their way to the grassy patch in the park, and Lily's brother showed her how to kick. It was so much fun! In no time, the sun began to fall, causing a beautiful sunset.

Lily and her brother were so grateful to be able to watch the sunset together. Suddenly, Lily remembered something and quickly ran off. 

Her brother asked, "Where are you going?"

Lily replied, "To catch the sunset!" And with a giggle she ran off laughing.

Once upon a time, there was a delicate barrel that hung from a big tree. It was quite high, but it stayed in place. A family had come to the tree and wanted to get the barrel. But it was so high that the family couldn't reach it.

They decided to get a ladder and use it to climb up to the barrel. They put the ladder against the tree and began to climb up. It was hard, but eventually they were able to get the barrel. They were very happy and put it on their wagon.

The delicate barrel was so light they barely noticed it on the wagon. They drove home and put the barrel in their house. Now they could keep lots of special things inside it.

The End.

Once there was a boy named Tom. Tom was an adventurous 3 year old. He liked to explore new places and find fun things to do. 

One day, Tom was walking through the woods, looking for something exciting. He kept walking until he came to a clearing. In the clearing was a big tree and under the tree was a shiny whistle. Tom was curious, so he kneeled down to take a closer look.

He could see that the whistle was made of metal and it had some writing on it. Tom picked up the whistle and smiled. He blew it and the sweetest sound filled the air.

Tom took the whistle with him. He went to all the places he liked best and played it for everyone he met. Everywhere he went, people wanted to listen to the sound of his whistle.

Tom was so happy that his whistle was available to everyone. He loved to make music and share it with the world. Whenever he had a chance, Tom kneeled down and blew the whistle for all to enjoy.

Lily loved to watch the sky when it was stormy. She liked to see the big clouds and hear the loud thunder. Sometimes, she saw bright flashes of lightning that made the sky look like a big firework. She thought lightning was very pretty and exciting.

One night, Lily was in her bed and heard a big boom outside. She ran to the window and saw a perfect lightning bolt. It was long and thin and zigzagged across the sky. It was white and yellow and purple and blue. Lily smiled and clapped her hands. She wanted to remember the perfect lightning bolt forever.

She ran to her desk and got a paper and a crayon. She tried to draw the lightning bolt on the paper. She made a line that went up and down and sideways. She colored it with different colors. She was very proud of her drawing. She showed it to her mom and dad and they said it was very good.

Lily put her drawing on the wall next to her bed. She looked at it every night before she went to sleep. She remembered the perfect lightning bolt and how it made her feel happy and amazed. She dreamed of more lightning bolts and more storms and more beautiful skies. She loved to watch the sky when it was stormy.

Once there was a little girl called Lily. She liked to dress nicely. One day, she decided to put on a special dress. It was different to her normal clothes. It had a colourful pattern of crosses all over it.

Lily twirled around and around in her dress. She felt so happy wearing it. She looked very pretty.

At bedtime she put on her normal clothes. But that didn't stop her from dreaming about her cross dress. She imagined wearing it to school and all her friends telling her how beautiful she looked!

That night, Lily went to bed with a big smile on her face.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Josh. He was three years old and he loved to crawl. He was very fast and he liked to stay on the ground so he could move quickly like a worm!

One day, Josh heard a yummy smell coming from his kitchen. He followed the smell to find a jar of butter on the counter. He wanted to touch it and taste the butter, so he started to crawl over.

Josh's mother saw him and said, "No, Josh! Don't touch that."

Josh looked up with big eyes and said, "Please?"

His mother smiled and said, "Okay, but just get a tiny bit of butter on your finger." She showed him how to lightly touch the butter and he smiled when he felt the light, creamy texture. He looked up and thanked her, then crawled away happily.

Once upon a time, there lived a little boy named John who liked to explore. He asked his mom if he could take a trip to the harbor, and she said yes.

John was so excited about his trip to the harbor! He put on his hat, his shoes, and got his bag ready.
John was almost ready to go, so he waved goodbye to his mom and marched off.

But when he got to the harbor, it seemed kinda fake. Some boats were moving, but it wasn't as exciting as he thought it would be.

Just then, John heard a voice call out, "Hey! Who is preparing this harbor?" It was a scary boat captain! He wanted to know who was ruining the harbor.

John was so scared, but then he remembered something. He knew that pretending to be brave helped him overcome his fears. So he stuck his chest out, looked the boat captain in the eye, and said, "I'm preparing this harbor for a fun adventure!"

The boat captain laughed, and said, "Well, that sounds like fun!" From that day onwards, John had lots of fun exploring the harbor with the boat captain and his friends.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys, especially his ball. One day, Timmy's friend Billy came over to play. Billy wanted to play with Timmy's ball, but Timmy didn't want to share. 

Timmy threw the ball at Billy, but Billy ducked and the ball hit Timmy's ear. Timmy's ear hurt really bad and he started to cry. Billy felt bad and wanted to make it better. 

Billy apologized and gave Timmy a hug. Timmy forgave Billy and they decided to play with the ball together. They had so much fun playing together that they forgot all about their argument. From that day on, Timmy and Billy always shared their toys and played together nicely. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. She was 3 years old. One day, she was at the store with her mom. Lucy was so excited to see all of the things to buy. She wanted to buy them all!

Lucy's mom looked at all of the prices. Some were too high and some were just right. They decided to get one special thing for Lucy. Mom showed her a pale pink dress. It was so pretty! Lucy couldn't wait to put it on.

Mom took the dress to the cashier and paid. She brought the package over to Lucy and said, "Let's unpack the dress when we get home." They went home and went to Lucy's room. Lucy helped mom unpack the dress out of the package. When she put it on, she looked so pretty!

The End.

Tom and Sue are friends. They like to play with blocks. They build a house with blocks. The house is humble. It has four walls, a roof, and a door.

"Look at our house!" Tom says. "It is nice and cozy."

"Yes, it is," Sue says. "But it needs something more. Let's add a window."

"Good idea!" Tom says. He takes a block and makes a hole in the wall. He puts the block on the side. "Now we have a window."

Sue smiles. She looks out the window. She sees a bird. The bird is blue and yellow. It sings a song.

"Hello, bird!" Sue says. "Do you like our house?"

The bird nods. It flies to the roof. It sits on the roof. It sings again.

"Wow, the bird likes our house too!" Tom says. "Now our house is humble and happy."

Once upon a time, there was a very small purple farm. Lisa and Shirley were the farmers, and they loved to organize things.

One hot summer day, Lisa said to Shirley: "Let's organize the purple farm!" Shirley agreed and they started to organize the farm.

First, they picked all the purple flowers. Then they harvested the fruits and vegetables. After that, they feed the animals and watered the plants. 

When they were finished, Shirley said to Lisa: "Look at our beautiful purple farm after organizing it!" Lisa said "Yes, it looks so much better now!" 

The farmers hugged each other and smiled with joy. From then on, they kept organizing their purple farm every day.

One morning, a family woke up early and took a drive to the park. It was a mild morning and the sun was up in the sky. Mommy ordered the kids to get their shoes on and they all jumped out of bed. 

When they arrived at the park, they ran and played together. They ran up and down the slide and slid down the swings. They watched as the birds flew around in the sky above them. 

When it was time to go, Mommy ordered them to get back in the car. On the way home, the sun was setting and the sky was filled with bright colors. They were so glad to have spent the mild morning together.

Lily and Tom are playing in the park. They see a big slide. They want to go on the slide. They run to the slide. But there is a problem. The slide is too high. They need to climb a ladder to reach the slide.

Lily is brave. She climbs the ladder. She holds on to the bars. She balances on the steps. She reaches the top of the slide. She looks down. She sees Tom. He is still on the ground. He is scared.

"Come on, Tom!" Lily says. "You can do it! It is fun!"

Tom shakes his head. He does not want to climb the ladder. He does not like heights. He thinks he will fall.

"No, Lily," Tom says. "I can't do it. It is too high. I want to go back."

Lily is sad. She wants to slide with Tom. She does not want to slide alone. She thinks of an idea.

"Look, Tom," Lily says. "There is another exit. You don't have to climb the ladder. You can go around the slide. There is a tunnel. You can crawl through the tunnel. You can meet me at the bottom of the slide."

Tom looks. He sees the tunnel. He likes tunnels. He thinks they are fun. He decides to try.

"Okay, Lily," Tom says. "I will go through the tunnel. You go on the slide. I will see you soon."

Lily smiles. She is happy. She slides down the slide. She feels the wind in her hair. She laughs. She reaches the bottom of the slide. She sees Tom. He is crawling out of the tunnel. He is smiling too.

"Hi, Lily," Tom says. "That was fun!"

"Hi, Tom," Lily says. "You did it! You are good!"

They hug. They are happy. They are friends. They play some more. They have a good time.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily had a doll that she loved very much. Her doll had a pretty dress and wide eyes. Every day, Lily would play with her doll under the big tree in her yard.

One sunny day, Lily and her doll were playing under the tree. Lily saw some leaves on the ground. She had an idea. "Let's scatter the leaves, doll!" she said. Lily and her doll picked up the leaves and threw them in the air. The leaves fell all around them, making them both very happy.

As they played, Lily's mom came outside. She saw the fun Lily and her doll were having. "What a fun game you two are playing!" she said. Lily smiled and said, "We love to scatter leaves, Mom!" They all played together until the sun went down, and they went inside to eat dinner.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Jack. He was very busy. Jack wanted to go to the beach to play in the sand. He also wanted to get some shrimp.

When Jack got to the beach, he was so excited. He started to make a sandcastle. He worked hard to make it perfect.

While Jack was busy building his sandcastle, he found some little shrimp. He picked one up to look at it. It was so funny! He needed to get more shrimp so that he could play with them.

Jack looked all around the beach for another shrimp. Finally, he found what he needed. He was so happy to have found two shrimp. He quickly put them in a bucket and ran off to have some fun.

Jack spent the whole day playing with his two shrimp. He had so much fun! He wasn't busy anymore. By the end of the day, Jack was tired but he was also very happy.

Tom and Anna liked to play near the river. The river was big and blue and made a nice sound. Sometimes they saw fish and ducks and frogs in the water. They also liked to pick flowers and stones and make things with them.

One day, Tom found a bright red ball near the river. He was very happy and wanted to play with it. He showed it to Anna and said, "Look, I have a ball! Let's play catch!"

Anna looked at the ball and said, "That's not a ball, Tom. That's a balloon. It has air inside and it can fly away. You have to be careful with it."

Tom did not believe Anna. He said, "No, it's a ball. It's round and it bounces. See?" He threw the ball in the air and caught it again. He said, "It's fun! Come on, Anna, play with me!"

Anna shook her head. She said, "No, Tom, I don't want to play with the balloon. It's not safe. The wind can blow it away or the river can take it. Then you will be sad. Let's play with something else."

Tom did not listen to Anna. He said, "You are silly, Anna. It's not a balloon, it's a ball. And it won't fly away or go in the river. I will hold it tight. I want to play with it. I insist!"

He said the word "insist" very loud and very hard. He thought it meant he could get what he wanted. But Anna did not like the word. She said, "You are being mean, Tom. You are not sharing. You are not being a good friend. I don't want to play with you."

She turned away and walked to the other side of the river. She found some nice flowers and stones and made a necklace with them. She was happy and proud of her necklace.

Tom was left alone with his ball. He tried to play with it, but it was not fun anymore. He missed Anna and wanted to say sorry. He looked at the river and saw how fast and strong it was. He felt scared and lonely.

He decided to go to Anna and give her the ball. He thought she would like it and forgive him. He crossed the river carefully and walked to Anna. He said, "Anna, I'm sorry. I was wrong. It is a balloon, not a ball. And it is yours, not mine. Here, you can have it. I want to be your friend again."

Anna looked at Tom and saw his sad face. She felt sorry for him too. She said, "Thank you, Tom. That's very nice of you. I'm sorry too. I was angry. You can have the balloon if you want. Or we can share it. I want to be your friend again too."

They smiled and hugged. They played with the balloon together. They were careful not to let it fly away or go in the river. They also played with the flowers and stones and made more things with them. They had fun and were happy. They learned to be kind and share. They were good friends.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play together in the park. One day, Lily has a big bag of cookies. She wants to share them with Ben.

"Ben, do you want a cookie?" Lily asks. "I have many. They are yummy."

"Yes, please!" Ben says. He likes cookies too. He runs to Lily and takes a cookie from her bag.

But then, a big boy comes. He is older and taller than Lily and Ben. He sees the cookies and wants them too.

"Hey, give me some cookies!" the big boy says. He is rude and ignorant. He does not ask nicely. He tries to grab the bag from Lily.

"No, these are mine and Ben's!" Lily says. She holds the bag tight. She is scared and angry.

"Go away, you are not invited!" Ben says. He stands in front of Lily. He tries to protect her and the cookies.

The big boy pushes Ben. Ben falls down. He hurts his knee. He cries.

Lily cries too. She does not like the big boy. He is mean and greedy.

"Stop it, you are bad!" Lily shouts. She throws a cookie at the big boy. It hits his face.

The big boy is surprised. He feels the cookie on his face. He tastes it. It is sweet and soft.

He thinks for a moment. He realizes he was wrong. He feels sorry.

"I'm sorry, I was ignorant," the big boy says. He wipes his face. He gives the bag back to Lily. He helps Ben up.

"Can I have a cookie too?" he asks. He asks nicely this time.

Lily and Ben look at him. They see he is sorry. They are kind and forgiving.

"Okay, you can have one," Lily says. She gives him a cookie.

"Thank you," the big boy says. He smiles. He eats the cookie.

They all sit together. They share the cookies. They become friends. They play in the park. They are happy.

Once upon a time, there were two kids named John and Lisa. John and Lisa were silly. They were playing together in the kitchen when Lisa found a dish. "Look at this, John!" said Lisa. John didn't know what it was. So he asked Lisa. â€œWhat is it?â€

Lisa smiled. â€œItâ€™s a dish,â€ she said.

Once upon a time there was an enormous sausage named Sausage. Sausage was the biggest sausage in the whole world. Everywhere he went, people trusted him.

One day, Sausage was walking near a pond when he saw a small frog. The frog said, "Hi Sausage, can I trust you?" 

Sausage thought it was a very good question and said, "Yes, you can trust me. I will always be your friend." 

The frog was very happy and hopped right onto Sausage's back. Together they played, laughed, and hopped all around the pond. They had so much fun that they became best friends.

Sausage was very happy because he knew the frog trusted him. From then on, Sausage was sure that he could always trust his new friend.

Once upon a time, there was a big store. In the store, there was a pretty velvet dress. It was very expensive. A little girl named Anna saw the dress and wanted to have it.

Anna asked her mom, "Mom, can I have this pretty velvet dress?" Her mom looked at the price and said, "Sorry, Anna. It is too expensive. We cannot spend that much money on a dress."

Anna was sad, but she understood. She and her mom went home. The next day, Anna's mom had a surprise for her. She made a dress that looked just like the expensive velvet dress. Anna was so happy and said, "Thank you, Mom! I love you!"

Mommy was very proud of her daughter. Every day she loved to watch her daughter study. Her daughter would always sit on the bright yellow chair with her bright yellow book. Every day she got smarter and smarter.

Sometimes her mommy would help her study. She would sit with her and ask her questions. She always knew the right answers. Mommy was so proud of how much her daughter was studying.

One day, mommy was so proud that she gave her daughter a big yellow balloon. Her daughter was so happy, she hugged the balloon and kept it close. She thought it was the most beautiful thing in the world.

As her daughter studied, she would watch the yellow balloon float around the room. Whenever she looked up from her book she would see the yellow balloon and it would remind her to keep studying.

Mommy was proud of her daughters hard work. She was learning a lot and she kept studying until she was done. Mommy and daughter had lots of happy times together, and the yellow balloon was always there with them.

Once upon a time, there was a rabbit named Jack. Jack liked to play. Every day, he would hop around and explore the world.

On one sunny day, Jack found a fragile flower in the meadow. He hopped around and over it, taking care not to break it. Suddenly, he heard a voice. 

It was his friend, Daisy the Deer. She said, "Come play with me, Jack." Jack agreed and they began playing tag. They ran around and around until they were both out of breath.

Jack said goodbye and hopped back over the fragile flower. He waved to Daisy, then went off to find more things to play with.

Once upon a time, there was a hairy cat. He was always getting into trouble. He would mess up the furniture and not listen to anyone.

One day, the cat's mom decided it was time to release him. He was given a basket and told to go find his own home. So, off he went, happily meowing away.
 
He wandered around all day, until he found a nice warm spot in the sun. He lay down and took a nap. After he was done napping, he realized he had a new home!

He went back to the cat's mom and told her the good news. She was so happy that he had found a new home. From then on, the cat was free from troubles and he lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time there was a little boy called Billy. He was a very honest boy who loved to explore. One day he was walking around his home when he found a carpet. He wanted to hide something so he decided to hide it under the carpet.

Billy went and found some of his treasure and put it under the carpet. He was very happy and felt proud of himself for being so honest.

Billy had so much fun playing hide and seek with his treasures under the carpet. He had lots of fun and became an expert at hiding things. Soon his mum found out about the treasures and was very proud of him for being so honest.

The End

Once upon a time, there was a little child who liked to explore. One day the child set off on an adventure. Suddenly, the child saw a huge, enormous thing. It was so huge that the child could barely see it! The child was curious, so it set off closer to the enormous thing. When the child got closer, it realized the enormous thing was a huge mountain! 

The child was so excited, it just had to climb the mountain. The child started climbing, but it was so hard. The child was determined and wouldn't give up. Finally, the child made it to the top! The child was so proud for achieving its goal.

The child looked around and noticed it was the highest mountain in the entire world! The child was amazed by the enormous mountain and just had to tell someone about their adventure. So the child set off back down the mountain and back to its home.

Mama was at the beach with her daughter. They were picking up shells. The shells were very beautiful and Mama was careful not to break them. Mama put the fragile shells in her bag so she could mail them to her grandma.

When Mama and her daughter got home, Mama took the shells out of the bag and put them in a box. She put the box in an envelope and wrote Grandmaâ€™s address on it. Then she took the envelope to the post office and mailed it.

The next day, Grandma received the envelope with the shells. She was so surprised and happy that she picked up the phone and called Mama. She thanked Mama for the beautiful shells and said she was going to put them on her shelves.

Once upon a time, there was a kind boy named Jack. He was very hungry, but he had no food.

Jack went to ask his mom for something to eat. She said, "I'm sorry Jack, but we don't have any food right now. I can get you something to drink." So Jack's mom gave him some special drink.

Jack drank the special drink, and he felt much better. He was still hungry, but his mom said he could have some food soon.

Jack's mom went to the store and brought back lots of yummy food. Jack was so happy! He ate the food and it was delicious.

Jack was very satisfied and content. He thanked his mom for the kind and tasty food.

Once upon a time, there was a big oasis. Every day, the oasis was very quiet and calm. But one day, it smelled something very smelly.

The smelly smell came from a big pot of food that someone was cooking. A boy from the village was cooking a meal for his family. Soon, the whole oasis smelled like the food he was cooking.

The village people were so excited about the food. Everyone wanted to try it. When it was ready, the boy shared his food with everyone in the oasis.

Everyone was so happy and ate the food with a big smile on their face. Everyone enjoyed the meal, and the oasis was very happy again.

Once upon a time, there were two friends in school, Dave and Sarah. They shared their lunch and drew together during recess.

One day, Sarah got a letter from the school. It said that she had to take an exam. Dave heard the news and asked Sarah if he could help her study for the exam.

Sarah was scared, but Dave said he would provide help. He gave her some books that were available from the school library. Sarah thanked Dave and they worked on her studies together.

When the time for the exam came, Sarah was very nervous. She put in a lot of effort but she still couldn't get all the answers right. In the end, she failed the exam. Sarah was really sad and she knew that Dave had done his best to provide her with help. But it still wasn't enough.

Once there was a little bear named Flora. Flora was very happy, but there was one thing she didn't like - rolling down hills. Whenever her friends asked her to join in, she would always say no. 

One day, Flora was out walking when she came across a hill. Her friends called out, "Let's roll down this hill together!"

Flora hesitated, not wanting to join in, but her friends talked her into it. She reluctantly went along and started rolling down, feeling uncomfortable.

Suddenly, Flora bumped her nose and it felt very uncomfortable. She started to cry and her friends quickly came to her side. They said, "We knew you were scared, but we didn't think it would be so bad! Maybe you should try it again, so it won't seem so scary next time."

Tentatively, Flora agreed. She slowly rolled down the hill and soon she was having fun. When she reached the bottom, her nose was now bumpy and everything was okay.

From that day on, Flora loved to roll down hills, as long as she was careful and stayed away from her nose!

Tommy was walking along the beach one sunny day. The sand was warm, and the waves were gentle. He saw a friendly little fish swimming near the shore. He smiled and said hello. The fish swam closer and he reached out his hand and tried to touch it. The fish darted away and then came back again. Tommy laughed. It seemed like the fish was teasing him.

Then, all of a sudden, a bigger fish came up and chased the little one away. But it didn't go far. It was hiding under a rock. Tommy bent down and looked at it. It was the same friendly little fish. He smiled and the fish swam away again.

After a while, the friendly little fish came back and they played together in the shallows. Tommy laughed and the fish seemed to enjoy it too. At the end of the day, they said goodbye. Tommy waved and watched the friendly little fish swim away.

One day there was a mighty post. Everyone in the village wanted to spend time with it. They wanted to spend every morning, afternoon, and evening with the post.

They would spend their mornings feasting around the post, their afternoons playing under the post, and their evenings dreaming by the post. 

Every morning they would all gather around the post. Someone would always climb the post and tell a story. Everyone loved listening to the stories. 

The village children would spend hours and hours running around, pretending to be mightier than the post. They would act out stories with imaginary friends and climb the post singing silly songs. 

Everyone spent happy times with the mighty post â€” from the youngest to the oldest!

Sara and Ben were playing in the garden. They liked to make shapes with the mud and the sticks. Sara made a star and Ben made a circle. They were very proud of their shapes.

"Look at my star!" Sara said. "It is very pretty!"

"Look at my circle!" Ben said. "It is very round!"

They showed each other their shapes and smiled.

But then they heard a loud noise. It was thunder. They looked at the sky and saw dark clouds. It was going to rain.

"Oh no!" Sara said. "Our shapes will get wet!"

"Let's take them inside!" Ben said. "Hurry!"

They picked up their shapes and ran to the house. But they were too late. The rain started to fall. It was enormous rain. It made big splashes on the ground. It washed away their shapes.

Sara and Ben were sad. They liked their shapes. They wanted to keep them.

"Mama!" Sara cried. "Our shapes are gone!"

"Papa!" Ben cried. "The rain took them!"

Mama and Papa came to the door. They saw Sara and Ben holding the mud and the sticks. They saw the rain pouring down.

"Oh, I'm sorry, my loves," Mama said. "The rain can do that sometimes."

"But don't worry," Papa said. "You can make new shapes tomorrow. Maybe the sun will come out and dry the mud."

Sara and Ben nodded. They were still sad, but they felt a little better. They hugged Mama and Papa and went inside. They hoped the rain would stop soon. They wanted to make more shapes.

Sara was walking down the street, admiring the pretty flowers by the sidewalk. Suddenly, she saw a carrot! She was so excited and reached out to grab it. But then Jimmy, the neighbor's little boy, came around the corner. He saw the carrot and ran over to get it before Sara.

Sara was angry with Jimmy for being so ignorant! She thought to herself that it was unfair that he got the carrot first. As she watched him take a big bite, she wished he would share a bit with her.

But then Jimmy surprised Sara by giving her a piece of the carrot. She was so happy, and she thanked him with a big hug. From that day on, Sara and Jimmy were the best of friends. Whenever they passed each other, they would both admire the carrot in the neighbor's garden, and share a happy smile.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and run around in the grass. One day, Lily saw a butterfly and she wanted to catch it. She ran after it, but she tripped and fell down.

Lily's mother saw her fall and ran over to help her up. "Are you okay, Lily?" her mother asked. Lily nodded her head, but she had a big scrape on her knee. Her mother picked her up and carried her inside to clean up the scrape.

As her mother cleaned her scrape, Lily watched her gracefully lean over to get the bandages. Lily smiled and said, "Mommy, you're so graceful!" Her mother smiled back and said, "Thank you, Lily. I try my best."

Later that day, Lily and her mother went back outside to play. This time, her mother held her hand so she wouldn't fall again. They saw the butterfly again and Lily tried to catch it, but it flew away. "Don't worry, Lily," her mother said. "We can try again tomorrow." And so, they went back inside, happy and content.

Once upon a time, there was a restless dove. She was always flying around, bouncing here and there. She never stayed in one place for too long.

One day, she came across a little girl. The girl was playing in the park and noticed the dove. She said to it, â€œHello little dove. Where are you going in such a hurry?â€

The dove stopped bouncing and said, â€œIâ€™m just looking for a good place to rest. Iâ€™m so restless.â€

The little girl smiled and said, â€œCome with me. I know a perfect spot for you.â€ She led the dove to a big tree and showed her a comfy nest in the branches. â€œSee?â€ she said. â€œThis is a nice, cozy place for you to rest.â€ 

The dove was very happy. She said to the girl, â€œThank you! Now I can bounce around without worrying.â€
