Once upon a time, in a small house on a hill, there lived a girl named Lily. She loved to talk to her friends and look at the pretty view from her window. Every day, she saw the sun, the sky, the trees, and the birds.

One day, Lily saw a fancy bird with big, colorful wings. The bird came to her window and they started to talk. The bird told Lily about the fun places it had been to and the things it had seen. Lily was very happy to have a new friend to talk to and share the view with.

As the days went by, Lily and the fancy bird talked and looked at the view together. They became best friends. The bird showed Lily how to dance, and they laughed and played together. Lily's days were full of fun and joy, all because of her new friend and the beautiful view they shared.

Once upon a time, there was a little bear. The bear lived in a big forest with his family. One day, the little bear went on an adventure and found a big log. He climbed on top of the log and it was very rough. The little bear liked how rough it felt under his paws.

Suddenly, it started to rain. The little bear wanted to stay dry, so he looked for a place to hide. He saw a big tree with a hole in it. The little bear climbed inside and waited for the rain to stop. When the rain stopped, the little bear climbed out of the tree and saw a big puddle.

The little bear wanted to play in the puddle, but he was too small to jump in. So, he found a cup and poured water into the puddle until it was big enough to splash in. The little bear had so much fun splashing in the puddle and he was very happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved to swing. She loved to swing so much that every day her mommy would take her to the nearby park and she would swing with all her might!

One day, while the little girl was swinging, she saw a bright yellow butterfly flutter to her shoulder. She was filled with excitement and began to swing even higher. 

The little girl asked the butterfly if it wanted to swing, too. The butterfly nodded its head and said, "Yes, I would love to!" 

The little girl and the butterfly began to swing together. It was lovely! They smiled and laughed as they flew higher and higher.

Eventually, the little girl had to say goodbye to the butterfly, so she gave it a hug and said, "Thanks for swinging with me. Bye-bye, lovely butterfly!" 

The little girl wished the butterfly luck before she went home, and they shared a special goodbye. 

The little girl was filled with joy and happiness, and she knew she'd swing again with her lovely butterfly friend.

Anna was a humble girl who liked to help her mom with the dishes. She did not lie or make a fuss. She was happy to wash and dry the plates and cups and spoons.

One day, her mom had to go out for a while and asked Anna to stay at home and finish the dishes. Anna said yes and kissed her mom goodbye. She went to the kitchen and saw a big pile of dishes in the sink. She rolled up her sleeves and started to work.

She was almost done when she heard a knock on the door. She wondered who it could be. She wiped her hands and went to see. She opened the door and saw a boy with a big smile. He had a bag of candy in his hand.

"Hi, I'm Tom. I live next door. Do you want to play with me?" he asked.

Anna looked at him and felt curious. She liked candy and she liked to play. But she remembered her mom's words and the dishes.

"Thank you, but I can't. I have to finish the dishes. My mom asked me to," she said.

Tom frowned and tried to persuade her. "Oh, come on. The dishes can wait. They won't run away. Just one game. It will be fun. I have a ball and a bike and a kite. You can have some candy too."

Anna felt tempted. She wanted to have fun too. But she knew it was not right to lie or disobey her mom. She shook her head and said no.

"Sorry, Tom. I can't. Maybe another time. Bye," she said and closed the door.

She went back to the kitchen and finished the dishes. She felt proud of herself for being humble and honest. She hoped her mom would be proud too. She put the dishes away and waited for her mom to come back. She smiled and hummed a song. She was happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she fell and hurt her knee. Her mommy took her to the doctor. The doctor was very kind and made Lily feel better. She put a bandage on Lily's knee and gave her a lollipop. 

Lily asked the doctor, "Why do you wear a mask?" The doctor replied, "I wear it to keep everyone safe." Lily thought the doctor looked mysterious with her mask on. 

As they were leaving, Lily said, "Thank you, doctor. You made my knee feel better." The doctor smiled and said, "You're welcome, Lily. Remember to be careful and not fall again." Before leaving, Lily blew a kiss to the doctor to say goodbye.

Once upon a time there was a mommy, who cared for her little girl. They played together every day. One day the mommy said, "Let's go to the park!" The little girl smiled, so excited.

At the park, the little girl saw a hot air balloon. It was so colorful! The balloon had reds, blues, greens and yellows. The little girl thought it was so pretty.

The mommy smiled and said, "Let's get in the balloon!" So they both climbed in, the mommy holding the little girl tight. Up up and away they went, way up in the sky.

The little girl laughed and shouted with joy, feeling the warm hot air around her. She looked at the mommy and said, "Thank you for caring for me and taking me on this special adventure." And the mommy smiled and hugged her.

Mommy said to Jack, "It's time to go to the park." Jack said, "Yeah!" He was so excited.

Mommy got his shoes and jacket ready, and then she handed Jack his bowl with his lunch. "Let's go!" said Jack, and he ran to the door.

At the park, Jack found lots of fun things to do. He went down the slide and then he ran around chasing the ducks. He even raced some of the other kids. After a while he was hungry.

Mommy said, "Are you ready for lunch?" She had put Jack's lunch in the bowl. Jack was happy; he said "Yes!" He quickly ate all the yummy food. Then he was ready to play again.

Once upon a time, there was a rabbit. He had always wanted to fly. One day, he decided to try. He spread his arms and jumped from the ground. He closed his eyes, expecting to soar. Instead, he fell to the ground. He was very sad.

Suddenly, a brush came tumbling down from the sky. The rabbit was curious so he grabbed it. He twirled it around and felt wonderful. With a smile, he lifted the brush up high. And then he started to fly!

He flew up and higher and higher. He flew fast over the trees. It was incredible! He was so happy that he laughed and shouted.

Suddenly, he heard a voice. It was a child!
"Woah! Look at him," the child said. "He's flying with a brush!"
The rabbit beamed. He flew up high, waving the brush in the air. He was so proud!

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to ride his scooter all around the park. One day, Timmy's mom said, "Timmy, we have to go home now." But Timmy was restless and didn't want to leave the park.

Timmy's mom said, "Timmy, do you want to rock on the swing before we go home?" Timmy said, "No, I want to ride my scooter more." Timmy's mom said, "Okay, but you have to promise to come back to the car when I call you."

Timmy rode his scooter all around the park. He went up and down hills, and even went over some bumps. Finally, Timmy's mom called him and he went back to the car. Timmy said, "Mom, can we come back to the park tomorrow?" His mom said, "Yes, we can come back tomorrow and you can ride your scooter again." Timmy was so happy and went to sleep dreaming of riding his scooter all day long.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the garden with her friends. One day, while they were playing, Lily saw a bee on a flower. She wanted to touch it, but her friend said "Don't touch it, it's dangerous!".

Lily asked "What does dangerous mean?" Her friend explained that it means something could hurt you. Lily understood and said "I will yield and not touch it". Her friend was proud of her for making a good choice.

Later that day, Lily's mom called her for dinner. She had made spaghetti and meatballs, which was Lily's favorite. Lily's dad asked her to pass the salt. Lily accidentally knocked over the salt shaker and got salt all over her thumb. She said "Ouch, my thumb hurts!" Her mom kissed her thumb to make it feel better.

Lily was happy because she learned a new word and made a good choice. She went to bed with a smile on her face, dreaming about playing with her friends in the garden again tomorrow.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a pretty aunt named Rose who always wore delicate dresses. Lily loved playing with her aunt, but sometimes she got mad and said she hated her. 

One day, Lily accidentally broke her aunt's favorite vase. She was scared to tell her aunt, but when she finally did, her aunt just smiled and said it was okay. Lily felt happy that her aunt wasn't mad at her anymore. 

From that day on, Lily learned that even if she got mad at her aunt sometimes, she still loved her very much. And her aunt always forgave her, even when she accidentally broke delicate things.

Once upon a time there was a girl who loved to travel. Every day she would go on a journey with her flute. The flute made beautiful music and it brought her joy. Everywhere she went, people would stop to listen.

One day, the girl came to a special place. She was so grateful to be there. She sat down and played her flute. Everyone who heard the music smiled and joined in the fun.

The girl and the people of this special place became friends. She was so happy spending her days with them. They named her the Flute Player and made her honorary mayor.

The girl was so grateful for the experience and the friends she had made. She promised to always remember that special place and the music she had made there.

Sam was walking in the park when he felt something buzz around his head. It was a mosquito! The mosquito flew away and Sam felt sorry he couldn't catch it.

Suddenly, he heard a noise and saw a bird in the sky. The bird was carrying something in its beak. It flew closer and Sam saw that the bird was carrying the mosquito he had seen before!

Just then, the mosquito bit the bird on its head and it let go of the mosquito. Sam watched as the mosquito flew away. He was sorry it had to go.

But then, something amazing happened. The mosquito flew back to Sam! It had returned and was now sitting on his shoulder. Sam was so happy. He said thank you to the mosquito and it flew away again.

Once upon a time there was a brave little girl named Ella. Ella wanted to prove to everyone that she could be brave and have success.

One night she found an old, smooth diamond in her backyard. She knew this would be the key to her success! She wanted to take the diamond and show it to the world.

So Ella packed her little bag and set off to find success. Ella ran and ran until she arrived at a big castle. She knocked on the big doors and waited.

Suddenly, a big, tall man with a pointy hat peered out from a window above the door.

"What do you want?" he asked Ella.

"I have a diamond!" said Ella proudly.

The man opened the door and let Ella in. Then he said, "You have succeeded! You can keep the diamond as your prize."

Ella was so happy she hugged the man. She had succeeded!

From that day forward, Ella was determined to succeed more and more. She kept the diamond with her as a reminder of her courage.

Once there was a little girl called Sarah. She was playing in her garden when she saw something very special - a violin! 

Sarah was so excited and wanted to play it right away. She picked it up and started to strum the strings. Suddenly, it made a loud sound and broke!

Sarah was so sad and she couldn't stop crying. Everything was so gloomy. Her mom could see how upset she was and came to comfort her. She told Sarah that things like that happen sometimes and together, they went to find another violin.

The next day, Sarah and her mom went to the music shop where they found some new violins. Sarah picked out the one she liked and they took it home.

Sarah was so happy that she could play the violin again. Now she could make beautiful music. Sarah never forgot the lesson - to be careful--and always look after her things.

Once upon a time, there was a little rabbit. He was so lonely living all by himself! He wanted to make some friends, but he wasn't sure how.

One day he had an idea. He saw a cable lying nearby and he thought he could use it to zip around and find some friends. So he grabbed the cable and zipped off.

Pretty soon the little rabbit found a group of other rabbits. They were so happy to meet him! They all talked and ran about, and had a great time.

The little rabbit was so happy now that he had friends. From that day on, he made sure to always keep his cable with him, just in case he ever felt lonely again.

Once there was a little bunny who loved to clap his paws. He would clap early in the morning and he would clap late at night. Every day he would go to his best friend, a loyal inchworm.

The inchworm would always be waiting for him and when the bunny showed up, the inchworm would smile and say, â€œHello, friend. Would you like to clap?â€ 

The bunny would always nod yes and the inchworm and the bunny would clap their hands together, the blueness of the sky their music.

But one day, the inchworm was not waiting when the bunny came hopping down the lane. He was not at their usual spot, so the bunny hopped and called out, "Where are you inchworm?" 

After a while, the bunny heard a little voice. The inchworm had moved and he was calling out, â€œIâ€™m over here, come find me! Letâ€™s clap!â€ 

The bunny hopped happy and determined until he found his loyal friend. And when the bunny saw the inchworm, the bunny and the inchworm clapped together and laughed with joy.

The moral of this tale is that even when your best friend moves somewhere new, loyalty will guide you and bring you back together. No matter how far away, friends that are true and loyal will always be able to find each other.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim liked to run and play with his friends. One day, Tim was playing with his friends when he started to fall. He fell down and hurt his leg.

Tim's mom came to help him. She looked at his leg and saw that it was not too bad. She put a bandage on it, and Tim felt better. Tim's mom told him to be careful when he played, so he wouldn't fall again.

Tim was grateful to his mom for making his leg feel better. He tried to be more careful when he played. Tim's friends were also grateful that Tim was okay. They knew that when they played, they needed to watch out for each other. And they all played happily ever after.

Once there was a girl named Jenny. She liked to go on long walks with her family. One day, she set out with them on an adventure.

Jenny wanted to reach the big hill at the end of the forest path and then go down the other side. That was her goal. Every now and then, her parents would stop to take a break and then keep going.

When they finally reached the hill, Jenny was so excited! She ran up the path, but it was a bit too steep for her. Jenny started to get tired and wanted to stop. Her parents told her that as long as she was fair and took little breaks, she could reach the top!

Jenny did just that, taking short stops now and then, until she reached the top of the hill. She was very proud of herself and so were her parents. They all hugged each other and celebrated the fact that Jenny had reached her goal. 

Eventually, they all went down the other side of the hill and continued their walk. Jenny was happy to have done such a big thing, and her parents were proud of her!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She went to school every day and loved to learn new things. One day, she woke up feeling very hungry and asked her mom for breakfast. 

Her mom said, "I'll make you some pancakes, but first you need to dress for school." Lily went to her room and put on her favorite dress. It was pink with flowers on it. 

When Lily got to school, she saw her friend Emma. Emma had a yummy apple in her lunchbox. Lily asked, "Can I have a bite?" Emma said no and Lily felt sad. 

During recess, Lily sat alone feeling hungry and sad. Emma saw Lily and asked, "What's wrong?" Lily said, "I'm hungry and I wanted a bite of your apple, but you said no." Emma felt bad and said, "I'm sorry. You can have the rest of my apple." Lily felt happy again and they played together. The end.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Lily went for a walk in the forest. She saw many animals like rabbits, squirrels, and birds. Suddenly, she heard a loud noise. It was a bear! The bear was very hungry and wanted to eat something.

Lily saw the bear and said, "Hello, Mr. Bear. Are you hungry?" The bear replied, "Yes, I am very hungry. I want to eat something." Lily thought for a moment and said, "I have an idea. Let's go snap some berries together. They are very delicious and will fill up your tummy."

The bear liked the idea and followed Lily to the berry bush. They picked many berries and ate them together. The bear was no longer hungry and said, "Thank you, Lily. You are a kind girl." Lily smiled and said, "You're welcome, Mr. Bear. I love animals and always want to help them."

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys and listen to his mom sing. One day, Timmy's dad took him on a big boat called a yacht. Timmy was so excited to see the big waves and the colorful fish. 

As they sailed, Timmy noticed a foolish seagull flying too close to the boat. Timmy's dad warned the seagull to be careful, but the seagull didn't listen. Suddenly, the seagull got caught in the ropes of the yacht and couldn't fly away. 

Timmy felt sad for the seagull and asked his dad to help. Together, they carefully untangled the seagull and set it free. Timmy learned that it's important to listen and be careful, even if you're having fun. And the seagull learned to be more careful around big boats like yachts. The end.

Once there was a boat called Sam. It was blue and had a big white sail. Sam sailed on the ocean every day.

One day, the boat was caught in a storm. The waves were so tall that Sam started to struggle. Very soon, Sam was a wreck.

The boat was sorry, but it could not sail anymore. It was broken and floating in the water.

The ocean was sad. It wanted to help the boat. So, the ocean sent a wind to carry Sam to the shore.

Finally, Sam reached the shore and it was safe. The boat was happy and so was the ocean.

Lila and Max were playing in the park. They liked to dig in the sand and look for treasures. Sometimes they found shells, rocks, or coins. But today they found something very special. It was a shiny, colorful jewel. It sparkled in the sun.

"Wow, look at this!" Lila said, holding the jewel in her hand. "It is so beautiful. I want to keep it."

"No, I want it!" Max said, grabbing the jewel from Lila. "I found it first. It is mine."

Lila and Max started to fight over the jewel. They pulled and pushed and shouted. They did not share or take turns. They only wanted the jewel for themselves.

"Stop it, you two!" their mom said, coming over to them. "What are you doing? Why are you fighting?"

Lila and Max both complained to their mom. They each said that the jewel was theirs and that the other one was not fair. They showed their mom the jewel and hoped that she would agree with them.

But their mom did not. She looked at the jewel and frowned. She said, "This is not a real jewel. It is a fake. It is made of plastic and glass. It is not worth anything. You should not fight over something like this. You should be kind and generous to each other. That is more valuable than any jewel."

Lila and Max felt ashamed. They realized that their mom was right. They had been selfish and rude. They said sorry to each other and hugged. They gave the jewel back to their mom and said that they did not want it anymore. They decided to play together and look for other treasures. They learned a lesson that day. They learned that being friends was more beautiful than any jewel.

Tom and Anna are friends who like to play with rockets. They have a big box full of rockets of different colors and sizes. They pretend that they are astronauts who go to space and explore new planets.

One day, they decide to bring their rockets to the park and launch them from the hill. They pack their box and their snacks and walk to the park with their moms. They find a good spot on the hill and set up their rockets.

"Are you ready, Anna?" Tom asks.

"Yes, I am, Tom. Let's go to space!" Anna says.

They count down from ten and press the buttons on their rockets. The rockets make a loud noise and fly up in the air. Tom and Anna watch them with wide eyes and cheer.

"Wow, look at them go!" Tom says.

"They are so fast and bright!" Anna says.

They imagine that their rockets are going to different planets with strange animals and plants. They make up stories about what they see and do in space.

But soon, the wind gets stronger and the sky gets darker. The rockets start to fall down and land on the ground. Some of them break and some of them get lost. Tom and Anna are sad and scared.

"Oh no, our rockets!" Tom says.

"What happened?" Anna says.

Their moms come to them and hug them.

"Don't worry, kids. It's just a harsh storm. It will pass soon. We have to go home now and be safe." One mom says.

"Can we bring our rockets home?" Tom asks.

"Of course, we can. We will help you find them and fix them. Maybe we can play with them again another day." The other mom says.

Tom and Anna nod and smile. They gather their rockets and their snacks and follow their moms. They still love their rockets and their space adventures. They hope that the storm will end soon and the sun will come out again.

One day, a little boy named Tim went to the park with his mom. They saw many kids playing and having fun. Tim wanted to show his mom how fast he could run. So, he started to run very, very fast. His mom was happy to see him run so fast.

Suddenly, a big, scary dog came running into the park. The dog was barking loudly and all the kids got scared. Tim's mom knew this was an emergency. She quickly picked up Tim and took him to a safe place.

After the scary dog left, Tim's mom told him that everything was okay now. Tim was happy that his mom was there to help him. They went back to playing in the park, and Tim showed his mom how high he could jump. They had a great day at the park together.

Once upon a time, there was an old rabbit who lived underground. He liked to sleep all day and all night. One day, a little mouse came to the rabbit's house and asked, "Can we play together?"

The old rabbit replied, "I'm too tired to play. I just want to sleep."

The little mouse felt sad and said, "But I want to play with you. Can't you please come outside?"

The old rabbit thought for a moment and said, "Okay, I will come outside, but we can't rush. I need to take my time."

The two friends went outside and played together. They had so much fun that the old rabbit forgot about being tired. From that day on, the old rabbit and the little mouse played together every day.

Once upon a time, there was a poor frog. He lived in a big pond with lots of other frogs. One day, he wanted to impress his friends by jumping really high. But when he tried to jump, he fell into the water and got all wet. His friends laughed at him and he felt embarrassed. 

The poor frog didn't want his friends to think he was bad at jumping. So, he practiced every day until he could jump higher than all the other frogs. When he showed off his new skills, his friends were amazed and no longer laughed at him. 

From that day on, the frog was no longer embarrassed and felt proud of himself. He realized that even if he was poor, he could still do great things. And his friends were happy for him too. The end.

One day, a little girl named Emma went to the park with her dad. She was so excited! As soon as she arrived, she looked around and saw a tall stand filled with delicious treats. Emma's dad told her she could pick one. She took her time, carefully observing all the options. Then, she chose a big, red lollipop. It looked so delicious! She enjoyed it as they watched the ducks swimming in the pond. It was a lovely day spent in the park.

It was Lucy's birthday. She felt so strong and was ready for all of her presents. As she walked outside, she heard a loud noise. It was a plane with wings soaring so high in the sky. She watched it, amazed by how it stayed in the air. 

Lucy wanted to be part of the plane's adventure. She imagined flying so far and feeling the wind rush against her skin. Suddenly she felt something tugging on her arm. It was her mom. She said, â€œLetâ€™s go to the park. Iâ€™m sure it will be fun!â€ 

Lucy was so excited to go. When they arrived, there was a big slide. It looked like the perfect plane! Lucy grabbed onto her mom and they climbed up together. As they reached the top, Lucy felt like she could soar. She stretched out her arms, took a deep breath and let go. 

Lucy felt so strong and free as the slide carried her down. When she was done, she felt like she had just been for a real flight! She knew that she would remember her birthday for a long time.

Once upon a time, there was a big mountain. It was so tall that it touched the sky. One day, a little birdie was flying around the mountain. The birdie saw a thick fog on the mountain. It was hard to see anything through the fog. Suddenly, the birdie blinked its eyes and the fog disappeared! The birdie was very happy and flew away. The mountain was clear again and everyone could see how beautiful it was.

Once upon a time, there was a kind girl named Lily. She had a friend named Max who was very nice to her. One day, Max shared his toys with Lily and she felt happy. "Thank you for being so generous, Max!" Lily said. Max smiled and replied, "You're my friend, Lily. I want to make you happy."

Later that day, they went to a show where a magician performed magic tricks. When the magician finished, everyone started to applaud. Lily turned to Max and said, "Let's applaud too! The magician was amazing!" Max agreed and they both clapped their hands together. They had a great time together and promised to always be kind to each other. The end.

Once there was a boy named Jack. He was a very curious three year old. One day he decided to go out and explore the big store. As soon as he opened the door of the store he was amazed by how big it was. He started to wander around and look at all the different things. 

Suddenly he heard somebody yell. He was so startled he jumped. He looked around to see who was yelling. It was an old man behind the counter. He was yelling at a squirrel who had snuck into the store and was stealing his candy. 

Jack wasn't scared anymore. He was glad the man was yelling to stop the squirrel. He waved goodbye to the old man and the squirrel then went back outside. He thought about the big store for the rest of the day. He was excited to come back and explore it again soon.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to go camping with her family. They would pack up their tent and go into the woods. One day, as they were setting up the tent, Lily's dad became grumpy. "I worry that we won't be able to set up the tent in time," he said. 

Lily's mom smiled and said, "Don't worry, we have plenty of time. Let's work together to get the tent up." So, they all worked together and soon the tent was up. Lily was so happy that she ran inside the tent and started jumping on her sleeping bag. 

Later that night, as they were all sitting around the campfire, Lily's dad said, "I'm sorry I was grumpy earlier. I just worry too much sometimes." Lily's mom put her hand on his shoulder and said, "It's okay to worry, but we can work together to figure things out." And with that, they all enjoyed their camping trip under the stars.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Mary. Mary was very enthusiastic and was always ready to play. One day, Mary decided to go out and explore the world. She started walking and soon reached a cell full of animals. She was so excited to see them!

Mary walked closer to see the animals and found a big brown bear. She was so proud of herself! She tried to strike the bear's paw, but the bear didn't move. Mary laughed and started to play with the other animals instead.

Then, one of the animals quickly jumped up and struck the cell wall. It startled Mary and she stepped back to take a closer look. It was a big gray elephant! Mary was amazed and delighted by the elephant's strength.

The enthusiastic little girl couldn't contain her joy and ran around the cell, saying hello to each of the animals. When she had explored them all, she knew she had experienced something extraordinary!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and have fun. One day, Lily's mom gave her some money and told her to go to the store to buy a pot for their dinner. Lily was excited to go on her own and pay for something.

As Lily walked to the store, she saw a mysterious man with a big hat. He looked at her and said, "Hello little girl, do you want to buy something special?" But Lily knew she had to buy the pot for her mom, so she said no thank you and kept walking.

When Lily got to the store, she saw a shiny pot that she really liked. But when she went to pay, she realized she didn't have enough money. She felt sad and didn't know what to do. Suddenly, the mysterious man appeared again and gave Lily the rest of the money she needed to buy the pot. Lily was surprised and grateful.

As Lily walked home with her new pot, she saw the mysterious man walking away. She realized he was a kind person who helped her when she needed it. From that day on, Lily always remembered to be kind to others, just like the mysterious man was kind to her.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who was only three years old. Her favorite thing to do was play games. One day, she went to the library and noticed something in the corner. It was a big, serious dictionary. She was very curious and went to take a look. Suddenly, she heard a loud noise that scared her. It was a mouse scurrying near the dictionary. She was so scared she quickly ran out of the library.

That night, she had a lot of fun playing different games and she wasn't scared anymore. She decided to go back to the library the next day and take a look at the scary dictionary, but this time she took her mother with her.

When they arrived at the library, her mother said "Don't worry, I will protect you". She felt more brave and they looked at the dictionary together. The words were strange and so big, but the little girl was excited. She looked through the pages of the big, serious dictionary and enjoyed spending time looking at all of the words. By the end of the day, the little girl found herself no longer scared of the big, serious dictionary.

Once upon a time there was a girl called Lucy. Lucy was 3 years old and loved to solve puzzles. One day, Lucy found a spade in the garden. It was orange and very shiny. Lucy was excited to solve the puzzle of what the shiny spade was for.

She took the spade and dug in the sand. She found lots of worms, but also something special. It was a orange toy buried in the sand! Lucy was so excited, she had solved the puzzle. She kept the toy as a prize for being so clever.

From that day, Lucy and her spade went on many adventures together. They dug for treasure and went on walks. Lucy was so proud of her orange spade and couldn't wait to see what puzzles she could solve next.

Peter was walking in the forest one day, looking for something special. Suddenly, he heard a noise. "Hello?" he said. "Who is there?"

From the trees, a tall figure appeared. He had a box in his hands.

"I'm here to deliver something special," the tall figure said. "It is a safe."

Peter was very excited. He asked, "What is inside?"

The figure replied, "It is something unknown. You will find out soon."

Then the figure handed Peter the box and disappeared into the forest. Peter opened the safe, and inside he found something wonderful. It was a mysterious surprise that made him feel very happy indeed.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Tim and a girl named Sue. They were brother and sister. They liked to play with their toys and watch television. But one day, the television was very boring. There was nothing fun to watch.

Tim and Sue started to quarrel because they were bored. Tim wanted to play with the toy car, but Sue wanted to play with the toy doll. They could not agree on what to play with. Their mom heard them quarrel and came into the room.

Mom told Tim and Sue to stop the quarrel. She said they could play with both the toy car and the toy doll. Tim and Sue stopped fighting and started to play together. They had fun and forgot about the boring television. They learned to share and be happy together.

Mummy was sad, so she sat down to have a cry. Little Jack saw Mummy, so he ran to her and said "Mummy, are you ok?".

Mummy said "I'm ok, come and give me a hug". Jack hugged Mummy and it made her feel better.

Then he said "Mummy, let's go outside and find a lizard". Mummy and Jack went outside and looked around the dry garden. Suddenly, they saw something moving in the grass. It was a little dry lizard!

Jack was scared, but Mummy was there to give him a big hug and comfort him. Together they watched and played with the lizard until Mummy made Jack go inside for dinner.

That night, when Jack fell asleep, he was thinking about the dry lizard and how Mummy was there to comfort him.

Once upon a time, there was a loyal dog. His name was Max and he lived on a farm with his family. One day, Max found a pipe leaking water in the garden. The water was soaking the ground, so Max started to lick the pipe. 

He licked and licked the pipe, until all the water was gone. Max licked so hard, he even fixed the pipe so it would not leak anymore. The family was so happy that Max was so loyal and found the leak.

From then on, Max was known as the loyal and strong dog who could fix anything that needed some help. He never gave up on helping out his family, and was famous for being the best pipe-fixer in the town!

Once there was a wise old bird. He liked to watch the world around him. One day, he noticed a squash in the garden. He had never seen such a thing before! So he got closer to take a look. He noticed a white skin with little green bumps, and a sweet smell. His eyes opened wide. He wanted to try the squash! He pecked at it and ate some of the soft, yellow inside. It was delicious! The wise old bird enjoyed the tasty squash and never forgot it. He was sure he would come back soon to try some more.

Lily liked to play with her toy tank. It was big and green and had a long gun. She made it go zoom and boom and crash on the floor. She pretended it was in a war with her dolls and stuffed animals. She had a lot of fun with her tank.

But one day, her tank stopped working. It did not go zoom or boom or crash anymore. It just sat there, silent and still. Lily was sad. She tried to push it and shake it and hit it, but nothing happened. She wondered what was wrong with her tank.

She took her tank to her dad, who was good at fixing things. He looked at her tank and smiled. He said, "Don't worry, Lily. Your tank is not broken. It just needs some rest. It has a battery inside that gives it power, but sometimes it runs out of power. Then you have to charge it with a special cord. See, like this." He showed her a cord that he plugged into the wall and into her tank.

Lily watched as her dad charged her tank. She saw a little light on the tank turn red, then orange, then green. Her dad said, "When the light is green, that means your tank is ready to play again. But you have to be careful not to use it too much, or it will run out of power again. You have to let it rest sometimes, just like you do."

Lily nodded. She understood. She thanked her dad and hugged him. She took her tank and went back to her room. She was happy that her tank was not broken. She decided to play with it for a little while, but not too long. She wanted to keep it warm and happy. She said to her tank, "I love you, tank. You are my best friend. Let's play and rest together." And they did.

Lily and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to run and jump and slide. They saw a big pile of leaves. They wanted to jump in it.

"Look, Ben, leaves!" Lily said. "Let's jump in them!"

"OK, Lily, let's go!" Ben said. They ran to the pile of leaves and jumped in. They laughed and threw leaves in the air.

But they did not see the fire. Someone had left a fire in the pile of leaves. The fire was small and hidden by the thick leaves. The fire was hot and angry.

The fire burned the leaves and made smoke. The smoke was thick and black. It hurt Lily and Ben's eyes and noses. They coughed and cried.

"Help, help!" Lily shouted. "Fire, fire!"

"Help, help!" Ben shouted. "Fire, fire!"

A man heard them. He ran to the pile of leaves. He saw the fire and the smoke. He saw Lily and Ben. He was scared and brave.

He grabbed Lily and Ben and pulled them out of the pile of leaves. He carried them to a safe place. He called for help.

"Lily, Ben, are you OK?" he asked. He hugged them and checked them for burns.

"We're OK, we're OK," Lily said. "Thank you, thank you."

"We're OK, we're OK," Ben said. "Thank you, thank you."

The man smiled and said, "You're welcome, you're welcome. But you have to be careful. Fire is dangerous. Don't play with fire. Don't jump in leaves that have fire."

Lily and Ben nodded and said, "We're sorry, we're sorry. We didn't know. We won't do it again. We'll be careful."

The man said, "That's good, that's good. Now let's go and find your parents. They must be worried."

Lily and Ben held the man's hand and walked with him. They were glad they were safe. They learned a lesson. They never jumped in leaves that had fire again.

One day a nice princess was walking in the forest. She noticed a big tree with lots of shiny apples. She wanted to pick the apples and add them to her basket.

The princess said to the tree, â€œPlease, may I add some of your apples to my basket?â€

The tree said, â€œYes, you may take five apples, but please do not take too many. Itâ€™s important to be nice to the trees!â€

So the princess only added five apples to her basket and thanked the tree. Then she went on her way, feeling nice and happy.

Once there was three friends, a dog, a frog and a mouse, who wanted to find a magical stand. So the three friends marched across the fields and forests, bravely looking for the stand. Suddenly, they heard a noise, and there in front of them was the stand. It was tall and mysterious and the three friends were so excited! 

But the stand refused to move no matter how hard they tried. It was very stubborn. The mouse pulled, the frog jumped and the dog barked, but the stand wouldn't budge. All their efforts had failed! 

At last, the brave three friends had an idea. They started to sing and dance around the stand and it began to move. It had finally worked! Together, the three friends marched around the stand and celebrated their success.

Mama and Papa were out walking when they saw a very tall tower. They thought it looked so tall that they couldn't even see the top. They asked a man who was bald to tell them how tall it was.

The man said, "My tower is so tall that it reaches the clouds, so no one can measure it."

Mama and Papa were amazed. Papa said, "I bet it must have taken a long time to build that tower!"

The man explained, "We worked very hard to build it. It took us many weeks."

Just then, a mailman came by and delivered a package to the bald man. Mama and Papa watched as he opened it. Inside was a shiny new hat.

The man was so happy to receive it. He put it on and said, "Now my head won't be so bald!" Mama and Papa laughed. Mama said, "There you go, now you have a hat to match the tower!"

Anna and Ben are playing in the sand. They have a big bucket and a small shovel. They want to make a sand castle.

"Can you supply me some sand, please?" Anna asks Ben politely.

"Sure, here you go." Ben scoops some sand with his shovel and pours it into the bucket. "Do you have enough?"

"Yes, thank you. Now we can make the tower." Anna flips the bucket over and taps it gently. A sand tower comes out.

"Wow, that looks great!" Ben says. "Can I make the door?"

"Of course, you can. Here, use this stick." Anna gives Ben a stick. He carves a door on the tower.

They are very happy with their sand castle. They smile at each other and high-five. They are good friends.

Once upon a time there was a purple mop. The mop lived in a big, pink room. Every morning the mop would wake up ready for the day! 

The mop would enjoy the bright sunshine that shone through the window and the birds chirping outside. Then, the mop would be ready to start its day.

Every morning it would go over to the floor and start to clean. It felt so nice having the floor all clean. After the mop had finished it would sit back,dance around and sing.

The purple mop was so happy and enjoyed its days, it wanted to help out around the house all the time. All the people in the house were so pleased they had the purple mop keeping their floors squeaky clean.

The days became so much fun for everyone and the purple mop loved being useful. It was a job it was perfect for! So, the purple mop kept waking up every morning to keep the house clean and everyone happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved yogurt, especially the tasty strawberry kind. One day, Timmy's mommy bought him a big container of strawberry yogurt.

Timmy was so excited to eat it, but his big sister Sally wanted some too. "Can I have some of your yogurt, Timmy?" Sally asked.

Timmy didn't want to share his yogurt, so he said no. Sally was sad and went to her room. Timmy felt bad, but he really wanted all the yogurt for himself.

Later that day, Timmy and Sally decided to race outside. Timmy was very fast, but Sally was faster. Suddenly, Timmy tripped and fell. Sally ran over to him and asked if he was okay. Timmy said he was fine, but he realized that sharing with his sister was more important than having all the yogurt to himself. So, he offered Sally some of his tasty yogurt and they both enjoyed it together.

Once upon a time there was a little boy, who was three years old. He was playing in his room when he saw something special. It was a colorful chair! It had all sorts of different colors on it, so it was very exciting for the boy. 

He ran over to the chair, but could not sit in it because it was too high. He started to complain to his mom that he wanted to sit in the chair, but it was too high. 

His mom said, â€œThatâ€™s okay, Iâ€™ll help you!â€ She took a step stool and put it in front of the chair. She said, â€œNow you can climb up and sit in the chair.â€ 

The little boy was so excited! He climbed up and was so happy to be sitting in the colorful chair. He was content and felt very special in the chair which was all his. 

The end!

Ben and Mia like to play with their toy cars. They have many cars of different colors and sizes. They pretend that they are drivers and go on adventures.

One day, they decide to make their own fuel for their cars. They find some empty bottles and fill them with water, juice, and soap. They shake the bottles and see the bubbles inside. They think that the bubbles are fuel.

They take their bottles and their cars to the backyard. They find a big cardboard box and cut a hole in it. They say that the box is their gas station. They take turns to fill their cars with their original fuel.

"Look, my car is so fast now!" Ben says as he pushes his red car on the grass.

"Mine too!" Mia says as she follows him with her yellow car.

They laugh and have fun with their original fuel. They do not know that their cars do not really need fuel. They just use their imagination.

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play outside. One day, they received a big red ball from their grandma. They were very happy and thanked her with hugs and kisses.

They decided to take the ball to the park and roll it down the hill. They ran after the ball and laughed as it bounced and rolled. They took turns throwing and catching the ball.

But then, the ball rolled too fast and went into a deep hole. Lily and Ben could not see it anymore. They were sad and scared. They did not know how to get the ball back.

They saw a man walking his dog near the hole. They asked him for help. "Excuse me, sir, can you help us? Our ball went into the deep hole and we can't reach it."

The man smiled and nodded. He tied a rope to his dog's collar and lowered him into the hole. The dog barked and wagged his tail. He found the ball and grabbed it with his mouth. The man pulled the rope and lifted the dog and the ball out of the hole.

Lily and Ben clapped and cheered. They thanked the man and his dog. They hugged their ball and each other. They learned to be more careful with their ball. They continued to play and have fun.

Once upon a time there was a magical place far away. In this magical place there was a crystal. It was so special, because it was the only crystal in the world that could make things happen. 

Every day the crystal would make clouds in the sky turn into rain. People would be so happy that the crystal made it rain. But one day the crystal started feeling a little sad. It didn't make rain anymore. 

In the magical place it started to become very dry. The grass looked like straw and the trees looked like sticks. Everyone was so sad. The crystal wanted to make it rain again but it was so unhappy.

Then one day, the crystal decided to think of something happy and soon it started to make rain again. Everyone was so happy to see the crystal making rain once more. The magical place became green again and the trees looked so happy. 

The crystal was so proud of itself and everyone thanked it for making the rain again. From that day on, everyone was happy and the crystal was so proud of itself.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Maggie. She was young, only 3 years old. Every day, Maggie went to the pool with her mom and dad. She was always so proud when she was there!

Today was no different, so Maggie and her mom and dad headed to the pool. All the other kids were diving and swimming, but Maggie just looked at the water. She was nervous like always.

Maggie's dad approached her, smiling. He said, "Don't be shy, Maggie. Let's show the other kids what we can do! Come on! Jump in the pool and dive!"

Maggie was scared, but she wanted to show everyone what she could do. So Maggie took a deep breath and stepped up on the pool side. She pushed off with her shoulder and she dove!

The water felt so cool and calm, and Maggie was so proud when she surfaced. Everyone was clapping and cheering for her. She had done it! Maggie smiled back at her mom and dad. They were so proud of her.

Lily and Max are twins. They like to play pretend. Today they pretend to be soldiers. They wear hats and boots and carry sticks. They march around the yard and say, "Left, right, left, right!"

"Where are we going, Max?" Lily asks.

"We are going to the restaurant, Lily," Max says. "We are hungry soldiers. We need food."

They march to the door and knock. Mom opens the door and smiles.

"Hello, soldiers," Mom says. "Are you here for lunch?"

"Yes, Mom," Lily and Max say. "We are very hungry."

Mom leads them to the kitchen. She has made sandwiches and soup. She gives them plates and spoons.

"Here you go, soldiers," Mom says. "Enjoy your lunch."

Lily and Max sit at the table and eat. They like the sandwiches and soup. They say, "Thank you, Mom."

Mom says, "You're welcome, soldiers. You are very good soldiers. And you are very fit, too. You march very well."

Lily and Max smile. They are happy. They like to play pretend. They like to march. And they like to eat at the restaurant.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved playing with her toys in the summer sun. One day, she found an ancient necklace in her backyard. It was shiny and pretty. 

Lily decided to wear the necklace to show her friends. As she walked to the park, she noticed something strange. Her necklace began to glow and shake. Suddenly, it attached itself to a nearby tree. 

Lily was scared but she remembered something her grandma had told her. She needed to be brave and say a magic word. She closed her eyes and said, "Abracadabra!" The necklace released from the tree and floated back to Lily's neck. From that day on, Lily always wore her magical necklace.

Tom was hungry. He wanted to buy a cookie from the store. But he had no money. He looked in his pockets. He found a penny. He was happy.

He ran to the store. He saw the cookies. They looked yummy. He gave the penny to the lady. She shook her head. She said, "Sorry, you need more money. A penny is not enough."

Tom was sad. He wanted a cookie so much. He walked away. He saw a man. The man was playing a guitar. He was singing a song. Tom liked the song. He stopped and listened.

The man saw Tom. He smiled. He said, "Hello, little boy. Do you like my song?" Tom nodded. He said, "Yes, I do. It is a nice song." The man said, "Thank you. You have a good ear. Do you want to try my guitar?" Tom nodded. He said, "Yes, please."

The man gave Tom his guitar. He showed him how to hold it. He said, "You can play any notes you want. Just have fun." Tom strummed the guitar. He made some sounds. He liked the sounds. He felt happy.

The man encouraged Tom. He said, "You are doing great. You have a talent. Keep playing. You will get better and better." Tom smiled. He played more. He felt proud.

Some people walked by. They heard Tom playing. They liked his music. They stopped and listened. They clapped and cheered. They gave Tom some money. Tom was surprised. He said, "Thank you. Thank you very much."

The man said, "You see, little boy. You have a gift. You can make people happy with your music. You can earn money with your music. You can buy anything you want with your money. Even a cookie."

Tom looked at the money. He had more than enough. He said, "Wow. You are right. I can buy a cookie. But I don't want to buy a cookie anymore. I want to buy something else."

The man said, "What do you want to buy, little boy?" Tom said, "I want to buy a guitar. Like yours. I want to play more music. Like you. I want to be like you."

The man was touched. He said, "You are a sweet boy. You have a big heart. You can be anything you want. You can be like me. Or better than me. I will help you. I will teach you. I will be your friend."

Tom was happy. He hugged the man. He said, "Thank you. Thank you very much. You are my friend. You are the best."

The end.

Once upon a time, there lived a little girl named Beth. Beth lived with her mommy in a very happy home.

One day, Beth's mommy went out to run some errands. As she was leaving, Mommy said, "I'll be back soon, sweetie. Be good while I'm gone!"

Beth nodded her head and watched her mommy drive away. She was so happy to have the whole house to herself for a while.

But then, something very sad happened. As Beth was playing in the living room, she accidentally stepped on her mommy's special cable. She gasped, and started to weep big tears.

Beth was so dizzy from all the crying that she decided to lay down on the floor and take a nap. As she drifted off to sleep, she heard her mommy's voice through the door. 

"Oh, Beth," said Mommy, see saw the cable. "It's ok, don't cry. I'm sure we can fix it!"

Beth was so relieved to hear her mommy's voice, and the tears stopped. Together, Mommy and Beth worked hard to fix the cable, and eventually their happy home was restored.

Once upon a time, there was a thoughtful little girl named Sue. She always wanted to help her mommy and daddy. One day, she saw her daddy trying to fix the door. The door was old and needed some help.

Sue wanted to show her daddy that she knew how to fix the door too. She picked up her toy hammer and started to tap on the door gently. Her daddy smiled and said, "Thank you, Sue, for being so thoughtful."

Together, Sue and her daddy fixed the door. They were both very happy. From that day on, Sue knew she could help her family with anything.

Once there was a little girl who really cared about gems. Whenever she found one, she'd keep it for her very own.

One day the girl went walking in a gloomy forest, and when she came across a special gem, she picked it up.

She was so excited and said, "I'm going to keep you so no one else can have you."

But then something bad happened. As she was looking at the gem, a mean giant grabbed it from her hands, yelling "You can't have this! It's mine!"

The giant kept the gem and the little girl couldn't get it back. She was so sad, and realised that she couldn't care for the gem anymore.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy who always wanted to have a special jewel. But he did not have enough money to buy one. He was so sad until one day, he had an idea. He decided to work very hard every day to earn money.

Soon, he started to work and as days passed by, his hard work increased and so did his earnings. He saved up all of the money until he had enough to buy the special jewel he wanted.

The boy was so happy when he finally got the jewel, but not everything turned out perfect. Unfortunately, the jewel was not reliable and it broke soon after he bought it.

The little boy was very sad but he realized an important thing. He learned that if he wanted something valuable and reliable, it was better to work hard and save money, rather than depend on luck.

The sun shining brightly and the wind blowing outside, it was the perfect day for a swim. Two people, Joe and Sara, went for a swim in the sea. They had so much fun splashing around in the cool water. When they were finished swimming, Joe and Sara dried off with a big, fluffy towel. 

They then saw a busy person walking along the beach. Joe and Sara stopped to watch as the busy person hurried along. After a few minutes, the person stopped and looked around. Joe and Sara were curious, so they walked up to the person to say hello.

Turns out, the busy person was looking for something. What could it be? Then, Joe smiled and pointed at a small sandcastle the two had made earlier. The person was so happy to find it and thanked Joe & Sara. 

Finally, Joe and Sara were all dry, so they said goodbye to the busy person and went on their way. The beach was nice and quiet again and the sun was setting. Joe and Sara had had a fun and busy day.

Once upon a time, there were two kids named Jane and Tom. Jane and Tom played together all the time. They dreamed of going somewhere luxurious.

One hot day, Tom said to Jane, "Let's guess where we can go for luxury." 

Jane thought for a minute. Then she said with a smile, "I think we can go to the beach for a luxury vacation. We can play in the sand and get hot there!"

Tom replied, "That won't be luxury! We need to stay in a big hotel with a pool. That is luxury!"

Jane had a different idea of luxury. She said, "No, the beach is more fun than a big hotel! We can go swimming in the ocean and find seashells too!" 

Tom and Jane looked at each other. They had to find a way to make both ideas become luxury. Then they both had the same idea at the same time. They said together, "Let's go to the beach and stay in a nice hotel too!" 

The two kids hugged each other and ran off to the beach. They had the most luxurious vacation ever!

Once upon a time, there was a boy called Jack. He was three years old and really liked to play outside.

One day, Jack looked out of the window. Outside he saw a lot of kids running and playing a sport. He wanted to do the same. So he opened the door and stepped outside. 

The other kids saw Jack and waved at him to come over. Jack smiled and went to join them. 

He walked up to a boy and said, "Hey! Can I play?"
The other boy frowned and said, "No! We don't want you here."

Jack felt very sad. He stood and gazed at them for a moment.

Suddenly, another boy stepped forward and said, "Of course you can join us! Here, you can have my ball!" He smiled at Jack.

Jack smiled back and happily joined the other kids. As they all laughed and played, they all forgot to be angry.

Anna likes to play dress-up with her clothes. She has a big box of clothes in her room. She can be a princess, a pirate, a doctor, or anything she wants. She likes to stand in front of the mirror and see how she looks.

One day, Anna finds a new dress in the box. It is red and shiny, with a big bow. She thinks it is very pretty. She puts it on and stands in the mirror. She feels like a star. She wants to show her mom and dad.

She runs to the living room, where her mom and dad are watching TV. She says, "Look at me! Look at me!" But they do not look at her. They are busy. They say, "Not now, Anna. We are watching something important."

Anna feels sad. She wants them to see her dress. She thinks of a way to make them look. She sees the door to the balcony. It is open. She has an idea.

She runs to the door and goes outside. She stands on the balcony and shouts, "Look at me! Look at me!" She waves her arms and spins around. She hopes her mom and dad will look.

But they do not look. They do not hear her. They are still watching TV. They do not know that Anna is on the balcony. They do not know that the balcony is very high. They do not know that the railing is loose. They do not know that Anna is in danger.

Once upon a time, there was a strange thing in the sky. It looked like a long line. Everyone was amazed and stared in wonder.

The line kept growing and growing. It was incredible! Everyone paused to take a closer look.

Suddenly the line started to move and changed shape. It started to look like a big butterfly flying in the sky. Everyone was so excited.

The big butterfly flew up high and started to dance in the sky. It was so beautiful. Everyone was in awe and clapped and cheered.

The big butterfly flew away and the line disappeared. Everyone was sad, but also happy because they had seen something so incredible. They all said goodbye and went home.

Once upon a time, there was a small blue bird. He was helpless without his mom. He wanted to meet her more than anything.

One day, he flew up high and saw his mom in the sky. The small bird flew as fast as he could and finally caught up to his mom.

He said, "Hi, Mom! It's been so long since I've seen you!" His mom said, "Hi there, my little one. I've missed you so much!"

The two birds hugged and chirped to each other. They had the best time playing games together.

They promised to meet again, and he flew away happy. He knew his mom was only a short flight away.

Once upon a time, there was an old man. He had a long white beard and a staff. Every morning he would wake up and bow to the sun.

He did this ritual day after day. He would take his staff and bow while the sun rose in the sky. The old man had been doing this for many years.

One day, a young girl saw the old man bowing and asked him why he did this everyday. He smiled and said it was a way he showed his respect for the sun and the world around him.

The little girl thanked the old man for showing her how to bow and went home. Everyday the girl would now bow to the sun just like her old friend and felt thankful for life every day.

Once upon a time there were two best friends, Danny and Bob. They were very excited one day as they were going to explore the new park they had found. It was a large, open space filled with trees and grass that they had never seen before. 

Bob said to Danny with a twinkle in his eye, "Let's show each other what we can find in this new yard!" 

Danny eagerly agreed and they ran off to explore their exciting discovery. As they ventured further into the park, they noticed that something wasn't quite right. Suddenly, the trees and grass had turned dull and lifeless. 

Danny and Bob knew that this was not the same park they had originally seen. The grass was overgrown and patches of mud had replaced once lush greenery. 

Danny looked to Bob with a heavy heart, "What happened to the beautiful yard?"

Bob sadly shook his head and both boys knew that something very bad had happened here. They had no other choice but to leave, feeling heartbroken and defeated. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy. He was only three. He was playing alone outside when he saw a cooler by the side of the road. He was very excited and ran over to open it. Inside was a big surprise! He found a big turtle. It was so cool. He wanted to take it home.

The turtle was troubled. It had been there for a long time and was very scared. The little boy tried to calm him, but it wouldn't snap out of it. He couldn't understand why the turtle was so scared.

Finally, the little boy came up with a plan. He took the cooler with the turtle inside and brought it home. He put it near the lake in his backyard. The lake was cool and peaceful.

The little boy watched over the cooler all day. By night, he noticed the turtle slowly coming out from the cooler. He was finally happy and safe. The turtle snapped around the lake and they became friends. 

The little boy and the turtle were very happy and the turtle never had to be troubled again.

Once upon a time there was a girl who loved wheels. She saw a big wheel in the park one day and said excitedly, â€œI want to go on the wheel!â€ 

So the girl went over to the wheel. It was dark outside and the wheel looked scary. 

The girl was nervous but she said, â€œI can do this!â€ She stepped onto the wheel and started turning it. As it spun around, she could feel the cool night air blowing against her face. 

The girl laughed and said, â€œThis is so much fun!â€ Then she started to go faster and faster and the wheel roared in the dark night. 

Soon the girl was spinning around so fast that it felt like she was flying. And even though it was dark outside, it felt like the brightest day. 

The girl smiled and said, â€œWheels are so cool!â€ 

The End.

Once upon a time, there was a chubby bunny. The bunny loved to eat lollipops. One day, the bunny went to the store to buy more lollipops. The bunny asked the storekeeper to load up a big bag with lollipops. The bunny was very happy with the big bag of lollipops and went home to eat them all.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to play with his red toy train. He would put the train on the rail and watch it go round and round.

One sunny day, Tim took his red train outside to play. He put the train on the rail in his backyard. His friend, Sam, came over and saw the train. Sam said, "Wow, your red train is so cool! Can I play with it too?"

Tim smiled and said, "Yes, you can play with my red train." So, Tim and Sam put the train on the rail and watched it go round and round. They laughed and had so much fun playing with the red train together.

As the sun began to set, Tim's mom called out, "Tim, it's time to come in!" Tim and Sam picked up the red train and the rail. They said goodbye and went inside.

That night, Tim put his red train on the rail by his bed. He smiled as he thought about the fun day he had with his friend, Sam. Tim knew that he would have many more happy days playing with his red train.

Lily and Tom are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big dog. The dog is black and white. The dog has a red collar. The dog is a guard. He works with a man. The man wears a blue suit.

"Hello, dog!" Lily says. She wants to pet the dog. Tom is scared. He hides behind Lily.

"Be careful, kids," the man says. "This dog is not for petting. He is a guard. He helps me catch bad people."

"Wow, really?" Lily says. She is not scared. She likes the dog. "What is his name?"

"His name is Spot," the man says. "He is a good dog. But he is also messy. He likes to dig holes and roll in the mud."

Lily and Tom laugh. They see the dog's paws. They are dirty. They see the dog's fur. It is muddy.

"Can we play with Spot?" Lily asks. "We don't mind if he is messy."

The man smiles. He likes the kids. He says yes. Lily and Tom are happy. They play with Spot. They throw a ball. They run and jump. They have fun.

The end.

Timmy had never seen a jungle before. He was leaning on his dad as he looked at the beautiful green leaves and tall trees. 

"We are going to explore the jungle together," his dad said. 

Timmy was excited and smiled. He couldn't wait to go on an adventure.

But then it started to rain. Timmy was upset. He wanted to stay and explore the jungle, but his dad said the rain was too strong and it was dangerous to stay.

The rain got stronger and stronger, and looking at the jungle made Timmy realize that maybe it was better to go home.

His dad took him back to their house, but Timmy couldn't help feeling like he was missing out. 

That night, after getting ready for bed, Timmy heard something outside. He opened his bedroom window to take a look. 

An elephant was leaning on the house and munching on some leaves nearby! Timmy shouted in surprise. 

His dad came running and they both watched in awe as the elephant finished its snack and returned to the jungle. 

Timmy realized that even though he hadn't been able to explore the jungle, the jungle had come to explore him.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who lived in a huge house in the woods. Every day, the little girl would explore the woods and measure the tall trees around her. On day the girl was measuring a very tall tree when she noticed something unusual; a huge vine growing on the tree. The little girl, who was full of curiosity, decided to get a closer look.

"Oh wow, this vine is so incredible!" the little girl thought.

She tugged on the huge vine, but it wouldn't move. No matter how hard she tried, the vine wouldn't budge. "I guess this vine is too big for me to move," she said with a sigh.

The girl went back to measuring the tree and eventually finishing her task. She noticed again the huge vine but this time she noticed something strange. There was a bright red apple growing on the vine.

The little girl was surprised but excited. She was determined to pick the apple off the vine. She tugged hard on the huge vine and with one last hearty pull, the apple came off the vine.

The little girl had a huge smile on face. She had learnt two valuable lessons; an amazing discovery can be found if you measure your surroundings and with determination and hard work, anything is possible.

Once upon a time, there was a small girl called Lucy. She was very lonely and often walked around the park by herself. One day, when Lucy was walking, she noticed an old man sitting on a bench. He had a kind face so Lucy went over to him and said hello.

The old man smiled and asked Lucy what she was doing by herself. Lucy told him that she was feeling lonely and just wanted a friend. The old man said he understood, and he suggested they play a game. He told Lucy they could play 'patty cake' on his knee.

Lucy clapped her hands together and laughed. She sat next to the old man and they started to play 'patty cake' on his knee. Lucy had lots of fun and soon she wasn't feeling lonely anymore. She thanked the old man and said goodbye. 

The old man smiled and waved as Lucy walked away. Lucy was very happy she had a fun time and found a friend. As she walked back home, she felt much less lonely than before.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved playing with her favorite toy, a shiny red ball. One day, Lily was playing with her ball outside when she accidentally threw it too hard and it broke into pieces. She was very sad.

Lily's mom saw how sad she was and gave her a big hug. She told Lily that sometimes things break, but that's okay because we can always fix them or get new ones. Lily felt a little better, but she still missed her ball.

The next day, Lily's mom took her to the park. They went on a big swing and Lily felt like she was flying. She took a big breath of air and her mom told her that she was breathing in oxygen. Lily didn't know what oxygen was, but it sounded important.

As they were leaving the park, Lily saw a boy playing with a shiny red ball just like hers. She ran over to him and asked if she could play too. The boy said yes and they had so much fun together. Lily realized that even though her ball broke, she could still have fun and be independent by making new friends.

Today was hot. Little Andy was very excited. He had to choose between two things to play with. First he thought about the red blocks. He could build something big with those. But then he remembered his dirt truck outside. Maybe he could do some digging with that truck. He thought and thought and finally made his choice. 

He quickly ran outside and got his truck. He could feel the hot sun on his face. He started digging in the dirt, pushing his truck to make big holes. He was having so much fun that he forgot all about the red blocks. He stayed outside until it was time for dinner. 

At the dinner table, Little Andy's mom asked him what he did that day. And with a big smile on his face, he said, "I chose to play with my dirt truck today."

John was a poor boy. He wanted to go to university, but he didn't know how he could ever get enough money. He asked his mom if she could help him, but she said she didn't know what to do.

John decided he would do it himself. So he started to look for a job. He didn't find one for a long time, but eventually he found one that paid enough money.

John worked hard and saved up all his money. After many months, he had enough to go to university. He was so excited, he ran to his mom and showed her all his money.

John's mom was so proud of him. She said "You have worked so hard and decided to do it all by yourself. Now you can go to university!"

John was really happy. He thanked his mom and went off to buy all the things he needed for university. He was on his way to make his dreams come true.

Mommy had a surprise for her daughter. She called out cheerily, "Come on out, I have something fun!" The little girl, who was only three years old, excitedly ran outside and saw that her mommy had a spade. It was thin and shining in the sunlight.

The little girl couldn't contain her joy and asked, "What is it?"

Mommy smiled and said, "This is a spade and it's for you! We're going to play in the garden and dig some holes with it! Will you help me?"

The little girl happily nodded and grabbed the spade from her mommy. She ran around the garden making big holes with it. She was so surprised when she found worms and other small creatures in her holes that she couldn't contain her excitement and kept digging for hours. Mommy was laughing and clapping at her daughter's enthusiasm.

Finally, when the sun started to set, Mommy took the spade from the little girl and said, "That was so much fun sweetheart, but it's time to come inside now. We'll come back tomorrow and make more discoveries in the garden."

The little girl happily skipped back to the house thinking about what other surprises the garden might have in store.

Once upon a time, there was a mommy and her little three-year-old girl. One day they were visiting the park together. 
The little girl was very happy and she wanted to play all day. But Mommy told her that it was time to go home.

The little girl was sad and asked: "Why do I have to go home?" 
Mommy smiled and said: "Let's have a little game before we go home. I have a surprise for you!". 

The little girl was very excited and asked: "What is it?". 
Mommy answered: "You will have to follow me and then I will reveal it to you". 

They went for a walk and eventually reached a small lake with many ducks and geese. The little girl was so happy and excited to see the animals. 

Mommy smiled and said: "Now I can reveal to you the surprise: nature is beautiful and it can make you happy". 

The little girl understood the lesson she learned today: happiness is all around us, if we just take notice and appreciate it. Then they went home very happy.

Once upon a time there was a bull. He was very selfish and liked to have everything for himself. One day, he was wandering in a field looking for food. Suddenly, he started to feel very silly and he stumbled and fell. He was so surprised and scared, but he couldn't find a way to get back up! He started to cry and the other animals in the field ran away. After a few minutes, a friendly cow came to help the bull get back on his feet. She was so kind and patient, and the bull was so thankful. From that day on, the bull decided to be less selfish and to think of others before himself. He learned an important lesson and was never selfish again. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat rice for dinner every night. One day, she went to the park to play on the swings. While she was swinging, she saw a boy who looked very serious.

Lily was curious, so she went to meet the boy. He told her his name was Tom and he was looking for his lost toy. Lily offered to help him find it. They looked under the slide, in the sandbox, and even in the bushes. 

Finally, they found the toy in the grass. Tom was so happy that he gave Lily a big hug. They became good friends and played together every day at the park. From that day on, Lily knew that sometimes when you meet someone new, it can lead to a wonderful friendship.

Once upon a time, there was a strong and fast racer. He loved to go fast, so he wanted to gain more speed. He practiced and practiced until one day he had an idea. Using a delicate touch he tweaked his car to gain more speed than he ever had before.

He raced with his new and improved car and flew across the race track faster than he ever had before! Everyone cheered as he flew over the finish line in record time. He had gained the speed he always dreamed of and was so proud of himself.

At the end, he won the race and was awarded a shiny trophy. He was so happy to have gained the speed he needed to win the race!

Once upon a time, there was a panda named Pandy. Pandy was very restless because he couldn't find his favorite toy. He searched everywhere but couldn't find it. 

One day, Pandy saw his friend, a little girl named Lily, passing by. Pandy asked Lily if she had seen his toy. "No, I haven't seen it," said Lily. "But I can help you look for it." 

So, Pandy and Lily searched together. They looked under the bed, in the closet, and even outside in the garden. Finally, they found Pandy's toy behind the couch. Pandy was so happy that he jumped up and down. "Thank you, Lily!" he said. "You are my best friend." 

From that day on, Pandy was no longer restless. He played with his toy all day and night. Every time he saw Lily passing by, he would wave and say, "Hi, Lily! Thanks for helping me find my toy!"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to play outside in the cold snow. One day, Lily went outside to play and forgot to wear her warm coat. She started to shiver and her teeth chattered. 

Lily's mom noticed she was shivering and asked, "Are you cold, Lily?" 

"Yes, mommy," Lily replied. 

Her mom quickly brought her inside and wrapped her in a warm blanket. "You silly girl, you forgot to wear your coat! Let's put a stitch in it so you don't forget next time," her mom said with a smile. 

Lily learned her lesson and always remembered to wear her coat when playing outside in the cold.

Once upon a time there lived a little girl called Jade. She was very pretty, with grey eyes and a bright smile. Every day Jade used to play in the park with her friends.

One day, when they were playing a game, a kitten suddenly ran across their path. All the children ran after it. But no one could manage to catch the naughty cat.

Jade however, did something very clever. She took out a bowl of milk, and patiently waited for the tiny tabby to come closer. Sure enough, the little cat smelled the milk and gingerly moved closer.

Once it was near, Jade carefully managed to grab the kitten and put it in her lap. She was so pleased.

So the moral of the story is, if you are patient and careful, you can manage to get the things that you want.

Little Betty hopped off her bed and put on her horseshoe shoes. She wanted to be brave and explore the world outside. She looked around and saw a spark in the garden. She was curious and carefully walked towards it.

When she got closer, she noticed it was a little firefly. Betty smiled and offered her hand softly. The firefly flew right onto it and landed gently. It seemed to say thank you with its shimmering wings.

The friendly firefly offered to take Betty on a journey. Little Betty was brave and said yes. She felt a little spark in her heart as the firefly gently scooped her up and flew away. Together, they saw many wonders. The world looked magical through the firefly's eyes.

Betty couldn't believe that this amazing adventure was her own. She was amazed and excited to see what the firefly would offer next. It was an experience she'd never forget!

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Joyce who wanted toast for a snack. She asked her mom for some, and her mom said, "okay".

Joyce was very excited about the toast. She ran to the kitchen to get it.

Mommy put two pieces of bread in the toaster and pressed the start button. Joyce waited and waited until the toaster made a ding sound.

The toast popped out of the toaster. Mommy spread some butter and honey on it and then gave it to Joyce.

Joyce was so happy with the toast. She took it to the table and started eating it.

As she finished the first piece, she saw the second one and said, "Mommy, I want more!"
 
Mommy said, "If you finish this piece and make the table tidy, I will make you more toast".

Joyce ate the toast very quickly and tidied the table. She was so proud of her work and felt very happy.

Mommy smiled and said, "Well done, Joyce! I'm really proud of you. Now, I'll make you more toast".

Joyce was so pleased and excited. She watched as her mom put two more pieces of bread in the toaster and the toast increased in size and smell. Soon enough, Joyce had two more pieces of delicious toast to enjoy.

One day, little Joe decided to wander around the house. He went up and down the stairs, looking at things. Eventually he made his way to the roof.

The roof was big and wide and Joe felt so happy. He could start to see things from a whole new perspective up there. He wanted to explore the roof, so he started to wander around.

Suddenly he heard a loud, rude voice. Joe turned around and was surprised to see a big, tall man. The man was not happy to see Joe and he demanded that he left immediately.

So Joe quickly ran back down the staircase and did not come back to the roof for a long time after that. The roof remained a mysterious place for him, but he wanted to explore it again one day.

Lily liked to play with her toy mouse. She named it Mimi and gave it a pink bow. She would pick it up and hug it and pretend it was her friend. She took it everywhere with her, even to bed.
