One day, Lily went to the park with her mom and dad. She brought Mimi with her and put it in her pocket. She wanted to show it to the other kids. She saw a big slide and wanted to try it. She ran to the slide and climbed up the ladder.

But when she reached the top, she felt something was wrong. She reached into her pocket and gasped. Mimi was gone! She looked down and saw her toy mouse on the ground, near the slide. She felt very anxious. What if someone took it or stepped on it?

She wanted to go down and get it, but she was scared of the slide. It was too high and too fast. She started to cry and called for her mom and dad. They heard her and came to help her. They saw Mimi on the ground and understood what happened.

They told Lily not to worry. They said they would get Mimi for her and that she was brave for trying the slide. They helped her go down the slide and hugged her. They picked up Mimi and gave it back to Lily. She was so happy and relieved. She thanked her mom and dad and hugged Mimi. She said she would never lose it again. She learned to be more careful with her toy mouse and to enjoy the slide.

One day, Tom and Jane went to the park. They brought a big sack with them. Tom said that he was going to build a fireplace. Jane thought it sounded exciting.

Tom took out some large stones and put them in a circle on the grass. Then he filled the sack with twigs and leaves and put them inside the circle. He lit the sack and a beautiful fire started. Jane thought it was very charming.

The two friends talked and laughed as the flames grew bigger. They roasted marshmallows and told stories. Jane even fell asleep by the fireplace.

After some time, Tom said they should leave. â€œBut where is the sack?â€ asked Jane. Tom smiled. â€œI put it in the fireplace,â€ he said. Jane smiled too. She thought the fireplace was so charming. They put out the fire and went home.

Johnny and his mom were playing in the park. His mom looked around and noticed a big bush near the playground.

"Let's go check out the bush, Johnny!" She said.

Johnny was excited, so he followed his mom over to the bush. When they got closer, they both noticed the bush was tough and prickly.

"Be careful, Johnny. That bush looks rough," his mom warned.

But Johnny was feeling overly brave and he stepped right into the bush. Instantly, Johnny fell and started to cry. His mom rushed over to find him with a cut and a deep scratch.

"Oh no, Johnny! That bush was too tough for you!" His mom exclaimed.

Johnny was in pain and his mom knew it was best to stay away from the tough bush from that point onwards.

One day, Timmy was very excited. He was helping his mom with making jam in the kitchen. His mom had gotten special purple fruit, and he couldn't wait to try the jam after they were done.

Timmy was carefully stirring the jam in the pot. It smelled sweet and yummy. All of a sudden, he felt the pot slip out of his hands. Timmy had lost his grip and now the jam was all over the floor! It was a huge mess.

He looked at his mom. She had a very harsh look on her face. He knew that he wasn't in trouble, but he felt very sad. He had lost the jam! He looked down at the purple puddle on the kitchen floor and started to cry.

His mom reached down and hugged him tight. She said, "It's okay Timmy. Even mistakes can turn into something good. Let's make more jam with the purple fruit and try it again." Timmy was so happy, and he was no longer sad. 

He smiled and helped his mom make more jam. Together, they mixed the ingredients and waited for it to get ready. Finally, the kitchen smelled delicious again. The jam was even better than the first one. Timmy was so happy that he hadn't lost the special fruit jam.

Once upon a time, there was a jolly little girl named Lily. She was very excited because her grandma was coming to visit her. Lily's mom told her to clean up her room before grandma arrived. But Lily didn't want to clean up her toys. She said, "I don't want to clean up. I want to play with my toys!" 

Lily's mom replied, "If you don't clean up, your toys will spoil and become dirty. Grandma won't like that." 

Lily thought about it for a moment and then said, "Okay, I will clean up my toys so grandma will be happy." 

When grandma arrived, Lily was so happy to see her. They hugged and talked about all the fun things they were going to do together. Grandma even brought some cookies for Lily. They sat down and enjoyed the cookies together. 

After the visit, Lily's mom said, "See, cleaning up wasn't so bad. Now you had a jolly time with grandma." Lily smiled and said, "Yes, I had a very jolly time!"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved to play in the snow. One day, she decided to go outside and take a look at the white, fluffy snow. Seeing the snow made her very excited, and she ran to the nearest hill to jump and play.

But as she did, she saw another little girl hiding in the snow. She could tell that the little girl was very sad. Being curious, the first little girl asked the other why she was so sad.

The next little girl said that she didn't want to talk about it. But the first little girl was very kind and kept asking her questions. After a few minutes, the second little girl finally opened up about why she was so sad. 

She had been playing in the snow when a rude older boy came and started throwing snowballs at her. He laughed and made fun of her, so she ran away and decided to hide.

The first little girl was very sorry to hear about this story and decided to show the other girl what a true friend can do. She gave her a hug and told her she could come play with her if she wanted. 

The second little girl smiled, happy to have a real friend, and the two of them went off to play in the snow.

Lily was a little girl who liked to play with her toys. She had many toys, but her favorite was a soft bunny that she called Floppy. She always took Floppy with her to bed and hugged him tight.

One day, Lily's mom told her to clean up her room and put her toys on the shelf. Lily did not want to do that. She wanted to keep playing with Floppy. She said, "No, Mom, I want to play more!"

Mom said, "Lily, you have to tidy up your room. It is almost time for your nap. You can play with Floppy after you wake up."

Lily pouted and said, "But I'm not sleepy, Mom. I want to stay up."

Mom said, "Lily, you are sleepy. I can see it in your eyes. You need to rest. Come on, let's go to your room and set Floppy on the shelf. He will be there when you wake up."

Lily followed Mom to her room. She was feeling a little sleepy, but she did not want to admit it. She set Floppy on the shelf and looked at him. He looked sleepy too. She said, "Bye, Floppy. I'll see you soon."

Mom tucked Lily in her bed and kissed her forehead. She said, "Good night, Lily. Have sweet dreams."

Lily closed her eyes and smiled. She said, "Good night, Mom. Good night, Floppy."

She fell asleep and dreamed of playing with Floppy.

Once upon a time, there were two close friends, Ben and Jerry. They always enjoyed spending time together, and never hesitated to mention each other's names when they got the chance.
One day, Ben and Jerry were playing a game where they had to combine different tokens. When Ben was done, he had put together a really nice bottle.
"Wow, that looks really cool! Can I have it?" Jerry asked Ben.
Ben thought for a moment and then said, "No, because this bottle was made with my original tokens. I don't want to share it - it's special to me."

Jerry got a bit sad. He looked at Ben and said, "I understand, I wouldn't want to share something that is special to me either." Ben smiled, understanding Jerry's feelings.

The moral of the story is that we should always respect the things that are special to others and never be selfish with them.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim had an incredible toy. It was a big red ball with a happy face on it. Tim loved to play with his ball all day.

One day, Tim's ball got lost. He looked for it everywhere, but he could not find it. Tim was very sad. He missed his ball so much. He told his mom about his lost ball. His mom had an idea. She said, "Let's mail a letter to find your ball."

Tim and his mom wrote a letter. They put it in an envelope and went to the mailbox. They put the letter in the mailbox and closed the door. Tim hoped that someone would find his ball and send it back to him.

A few days later, Tim got a big box in the mail. He opened the box and saw his incredible ball with the happy face! Tim was so happy to have his ball back. He thanked his mom for helping him. From that day on, Tim took very good care of his ball and never let it out of his sight.

Once upon a time, there was a furry mouse. His tummy was always empty and he was always so grumpy. One day, he decided to try and find some food. He began to shout out, "Food, food, please bring me some food!" 

Suddenly, he heard some rustling in the bushes. He quickly raced over to it, hoping it was food. But instead, he found a big furry bear. The bear was even hungrier than the mouse and it shouted out, "Food! Give me food!" 

The mouse was so afraid and he quickly ran away. But the bear was determined to get food and it started chasing him. The mouse ran and ran until he could not move anymore. His tummy felt so heavy and full, so he knew the bear was still behind him. 

The bear was almost upon him now, so the mouse quickly hid in a small hollow tree. But the bear sniffed out where he was hiding and with one last roar it shouted, "Food!" The mouse had no choice, so he threw his bread out of the tree. 

The bear gobbled up the bread and then roared with delight. The mouse had to stay in the tree all night until the bear was finally gone. From then on, the mouse knew never to shout for food again!

Ben and Lily were twins who loved to play outside. They enjoyed running, jumping, climbing and exploring. They had many friends in their street and they always had fun together. They were happy and healthy in their youth.

One day, they saw a big hill near their house. They wanted to see what was on the other side. They asked their mom if they could go. She said yes, but they had to be careful and come back before dark. She gave them a snack and a bottle of water and kissed them goodbye.

Ben and Lily started to climb the hill. It was hard and steep, but they did not give up. They helped each other and cheered each other on. They reached the top and saw a brilliant view. They saw fields, trees, flowers and animals. They felt proud and excited.

They decided to explore a bit more. They found a stream, a bridge, a cave and a swing. They played with the water, the rocks, the sticks and the rope. They had a lot of fun and forgot about the time.

Suddenly, they heard their mom calling them. They looked at the sky and saw that it was getting dark. They realized that they had stayed too long. They felt scared and sorry. They ran back to the hill and started to go down. But it was harder and steeper than before. They slipped, tripped, fell and hurt themselves. They cried and wished they had listened to their mom.

They finally reached the bottom and saw their mom waiting for them. She was worried and angry. She hugged them and scolded them. She told them that they had been very naughty and careless. They had to go home and clean their wounds and go to bed early. They had no dinner and no stories. They had to say sorry and promise to never do it again.

Ben and Lily learned their lesson. They realized that they had been foolish and selfish. They had wasted their time and missed their mom. They had spoiled their fun and their youth. They said sorry and promised to never do it again. They also thanked their mom for loving them and forgiving them. They hoped to enjoy their youth again, but in a better way.

Once upon a time there was a girl who loved to use her imagination. She wanted to think of the most wonderful things she could. So, one day she closed her eyes and imagined something really special.

She imagined that the ceiling of her room was changing. It was turning into a big, dirty beach. The girl was so excited! She laughed and danced as warm sand covered the floor of her room.

Soon, she was in a very special place. She splashed in the blue ocean and made sand castles with her friends. It was so much fun!

After a while, she opened her eyes and the beach was gone, but she could still feel the sand on her toes. She knew that one day, she would be able to imagine exciting places again and the sky was the limit!

Once upon a time, there was a little goat named Gertie. She was skipping and playing around in the meadow on a sunny day. Suddenly, she spotted a flame in the tall grass. She thought it was very mysterious, so she moved closer to have a better look.

Suddenly a voice spoke out. "Gertie, don't be foolish, stand back!" It was Gertie's mother and she was trying to keep Gertie away from the flame.

Gertie stepped back and looked up at her mother, a bit scared but also intrigued. "What is that?" she asked her mother.

Her mother smiled and said, "That is a flame. It is beautiful, but it can be dangerous, so it's best to stay away from it."

Gertie nodded, then she gave the flame a wide berth as she skipped back to her mother's side. From that day on, whenever Gertie saw a flame, she remembered her mother's warning and kept a safe distance.

Tom likes to count. He counts his fingers, his toes, his toys, his books. He counts everything he sees. He is very good at counting.

One day, Tom goes to the library with his mom. He sees many books with prints on them. Prints are pictures and words that tell stories. Tom wants to read the prints, but he does not know how.

He asks his mom to help him. His mom is happy. She picks a book with prints of animals. She points to each animal and says its name. Tom repeats the name and counts the animals. He counts one lion, two elephants, three monkeys, four zebras, five giraffes.

Tom likes the book. He wants to take it home. His mom says he can, but he has to be obedient. Obedient means to do what mom says. Mom says he has to give the book to the lady at the desk. The lady will scan the book and give him a card. The card tells him when to bring the book back.

Tom does what mom says. He gives the book to the lady. The lady scans the book and gives him a card. Tom says thank you. He puts the card in his pocket. He holds the book in his hands. He is happy. He can't wait to count the animals again at home.

Once upon a time, there was a little birdie named Tweety. Tweety loved to fly around and sing pretty songs. One day, Tweety saw a shiny triangle in the sky. It was so smooth and pretty, Tweety wanted to touch it.

But when Tweety got closer, a big, mean cat named Sylvester appeared. Sylvester wanted to catch Tweety and eat him for dinner. Tweety tried to fly away, but Sylvester was too fast. Tweety had to surrender and let Sylvester catch him.

Sylvester was very happy to have caught Tweety. He took Tweety home and was about to eat him when Tweety had an idea. He asked Sylvester to let him sing one last song before he was eaten. Sylvester agreed and Tweety sang the most beautiful song ever. Sylvester was so moved that he decided to let Tweety go free.

Tweety flew away, happy to be alive. But as he was flying, he accidentally flew into a window and hurt himself. Tweety was very sad and couldn't fly anymore. He wished he had never surrendered to Sylvester.

Once upon a time, there was a nice family who lived in the hills. One warm spring day, the Mum decided to make some tasty food for them all.

"Let's make some Pepper Soup," she said. "That sounds yummy!" said the Dad. 

So they all went outside to gather the ingredients. The Dad picked some red peppers in the garden, while the Mum began collecting some other things to add.

Soon they had all they needed and they took it back inside. They added the red peppers to the soup and put it on the stove. 

The smell of the Pepper Soup made everyone so happy, they couldn't wait to eat it! 

"It smells nice!" said the little boy. 

"It sure does," said the Dad. "Let's eat!" 

So they all enjoyed a yummy bowl of Pepper Soup on that nice spring day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Sue. Sue loved to dress up and was always searching for the prettiest clothes. One day, she was shopping with her mum and she found the perfect dress. It had a modern buckle that matched the ribbon around the waist. She asked her mum if she could buy the dress and her mum agreed.

Sue wore her dress every day until one day the buckle came undone. She cried, feeling like the dress was ruined. But her mum hugged her and told her not to worry. She said that it is important to value the things you have, even if they are not perfect.

So Sue's mum took her to get a new buckle. It was a modern buckle made from metal shiny like a mirror. Sue was so happy that she could wear her dress again. She hugged her mum and thanked her for teaching her the importance of valuing the things she had.

Once there was an old man who lived next to a big hedge. Every day he would sit by the hedge and explain things to the animals around him. He would explain about the world, about nature and he would tell stories.

One day, a 3 year old child came to visit the old man. When the child saw the man by the hedge, he asked the old man what he was doing. The old man explained to the child that he was talking to the animals and teaching them about the world. The curious child asked to join the old man, and so he did.

The old man explained to the child about how the hedge grows. He showed the child the different types of leaves, and where the roots go into the ground. The old man also explained how the hedge helps to keep the animals safe and how it provides shade during the hot summer days.

The old man and the 3 year old child spent the whole day by the hedge. The old man taught the child about the world around him, and the child asked many questions. Both the old man, and the child had a lovely day together, talking and learning about the old hedge.

Once upon a time, there was a very creative bunny named Bob. Bob was always looking for new and exciting things to do. 
One day, Bob decided to explore a part of the forest he had never been to before. He hopped and hopped until he came to a big open field where he found something very strange. It was a trap! Bob tried to hop away, but he couldn't because the trap was too strong. 
Bob struggled to free himself and he was getting tired. He called out, "Help! Is anyone there?"
A friendly squirrel ran over to Bob and said, "I can help! Just watch me be creative." 
The squirrel grabbed a branch and used it to open the trap. When the trap was finally open, Bob hopped away and thanked the squirrel. Bob never forgot what the squirrel had done and from then on, he was always more careful in his adventures.

A family was on board a warm yacht. The mother and father were supervising their three-year-old child. They were having a wonderful time, breathing in the fresh sea air and looking at the beautiful scenery.

The father asked the child, "Do you remember what we said about being safe on the yacht?"

The child nodded, "Yes, Daddy."

The mother smiled, "That's right. Now, don't forget."

The child looked concerned and asked, "What will happen if I forget?"

The father pointed to the side of the yacht, "If you forget, you will fall in the water and you won't be able to get back in. So always remember to stay safe on the yacht."

The child nodded and said, "I won't forget. I'll stay safe."

The mother and father smiled and hugged the child. They all settled down for a pleasant and warm sail around the bay.

Once upon a time, there was a huge musician. He wanted to take a walk in the park and play some music. He grabbed his guitar and headed off. As he walked, he saw lots of animals. He waved to a cow, high-fived a sheep and gave some breadcrumbs to a hungry duck. Soon he came to a big tree in the middle of the park. He decided to take a seat there and strum his guitar.

Before long, a group of children came to join him. They were very excited to hear the music. The musician strummed away and the children clapped along. It was so much fun! After a few songs, the children took out a jump rope and started to play. The huge musician jumped in and started to skip too. He was having a great time!

Soon all the animals gathered round to watch. The cow mooed, the sheep baaed and the duck quacked. The huge musician felt so happy. He was making lots of new friends. Everyone said goodbye to the musician as the sun began to set. He bid them all farewell and took his guitar off home.

Lily was a jolly three year old. She loved to jog around the park with her parents. But one day, she complained.

"Mommy, it's so terrible," she sighed. "I don't like jogging."

Her mom smiled and said, "Why don't you try singing while you jog? That might make it better."

Lily thought it was a good idea so she started singing. Sure enough, jogging wasn't so terrible after all. She hopped and jumped and sang her way through the park. She even turned jogging into a game.

While passing birds, she shouted, "I can hop faster than you!" And when passing bunnies, she said, "Let's race!"

It was the most fun Lily had ever had jogging and she never complained again.

Once upon a time, there was a playful dog named Spot. Spot loved to run and play in his room. One day, Spot found a big red ball in his room.

Spot tried to fit the ball in his mouth, but it was too big. He barked, "Woof! Woof!" Spot's friend, Kitty, heard him and came to see what was wrong. Kitty was a small, fluffy cat who lived next door.

Kitty said, "Meow! What's wrong, Spot?" Spot showed her the big red ball. Kitty had an idea. She pushed the ball with her paw, and it rolled across the room. Spot chased the ball and barked happily, "Woof! Woof!" They played with the ball all day long and had lots of fun.

John was a 3 year old boy who lived in a small town. He wanted to explore the world so one day he decided to get out of his home and take a walk. He said to his mom, "I want to get out in the world and find something lucky!"

His mom smiled and said, "Okay, be careful, but have fun too".

John put on his shoes and left. He spent the day walking and exploring. He saw so many animals and plants that he had never seen before. Then, suddenly, John got really lucky! He saw a little bird and it sang a beautiful song!

John was so happy that he was able to get out and hear the world's music. He knew he was lucky to have such an amazing experience. He waved goodbye to the bird, and smiled as he went back home to tell his mom about his adventures.

Once there was a little girl. She was three years old and her name was Lily. One day, Lily was playing outside. She saw an interesting thing on the ground.

It was very dry and it felt strange. She picked it up and looked at it. It was so interesting that she wanted to keep it. 

So, Lily took the thing and ran home. She put the thing in her pocket and went inside.

But when she took the thing out of her pocket later, it had gotten wet! She was very sad and started to cry.

Lily's mom tried to make her feel better, but she couldn't. It was too late. The thing was ruined. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a happy boy who loved to explore. One day, he was in his garden and noticed something strange. He saw a little fuzzy creature, and the creature's voice caught his attention. The boy was so eager that he wanted to get closer to it, so he took a few steps forward.

The creature noticed the boy and said in a little squeaky voice, "Hello! Who are you?". The little boy was so surprised, but he answered back, "My name is Jack!"

The creature smiled, and kindly said, "It is nice to meet you, Jack. Would you like to give me a squeeze?" The boy was astonished, and hesitated for a moment. But then he smiled and eagerly said, "Yes, please!"

So the creature let Jack give him a big, gentle squeeze. The boy felt so comfortable and loved, it was like a big hug. When the squeeze was over, the creature thanked Jack for the hug, and then said goodbye.

Jack waved goodbye to his new friend, as he watched the fuzzy creature disappear deep down into the garden.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She was very hungry and wanted to eat a cookie. But the cookie jar was locked and she couldn't open it. She asked her mom to help her unlock the jar. Her mom used a key to unlock the jar and Lily got her cookie.

After eating her cookie, Lily's face was messy with crumbs. Her mom gave her a napkin to wipe her face clean. Lily used the napkin to wipe her face and it became clear again.

Lily was happy that she got her cookie and her face was clean. She went to play with her toys and took a napkin with her in case she needed to wipe her face again. The end.

Once there was a boy named Jack. Jack loved to hold his mom's hand. Every day they would take a step together and go out to the park. It was the most popular park around and all the kids loved it.

Today was special. Jack's mom held his hand tightly and they walked to the park. When they got there, Jack saw that the park was full of friends. He saw all the swings, slides, and animals.

Jack and his mom went on an adventure all around the park. They held hands as they walked, jumped, and ran. Jack was so happy that he forgot all about his step.

At the end of the day, Jack and his mom went home, still holding hands. He was glad that the park was so popular because it made his day so much fun. From now on, Jack always wanted to go to the popular park with his mom and hold her hand.

Once upon a time, there was a little mouse named Timmy. Timmy liked to run around and play with his friends. One day, Timmy went on an adventure to find some cheese. He ran and ran until he found a big piece of cheese. But, the cheese was in a zigzag maze and it was very smelly. Timmy didn't want to go inside, but he really wanted the cheese.

So, Timmy took a deep breath and went inside the maze. He had to zigzag through the maze to find the cheese. It was hard work, but Timmy was determined to get it. Finally, he found the cheese and he was so happy! Timmy took the cheese and started to return home. He was so proud of himself for being brave and getting the cheese.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She loved to play with her doll. Every day she would grab her toy and go outside.

One day while she was playing, a pretty butterfly came near her. The little girl saw it and wanted to grab it. But the butterfly flew away before she could reach it.

The little girl's mom saw the butterfly too and said, "My lovely daughter, it's hard for us to grab the butterfly, but it's even harder for the butterfly to fly away from us. So let's not try to grab it. Nature is for us to love and admire, not to take away from."

The little girl listened to her mom and nodded. From that day onwards, she was more careful whenever she was playing outside. Even when she saw something beautiful, she did not try to grab it and instead watched it fly away with admiration.

The moral of the story is that nature is meant to be appreciated, not taken away from.

John and his mommy were walking through the store. He saw something he wanted and asked, "Mommy, can I have that yogurt?" His mommy said, "Let's discuss it". They went over to the refrigerator and looked at all the yogurt. Finally, John spotted a big strawberry yogurt. It looked so good and it was hot and gooey. He knew he had to try it. His mommy said, "Ok, since it's hot outside and this yogurt looks yummy, you can have one". He was so excited! He had the yogurt and it was the best snack ever. He thanked his mommy and they went home.

One day, a little girl named Lily went to visit her grandma. Grandma's house was big and yellow. Lily liked to play in the big yard with her dog, Spot. They loved to run and jump in the sun.

While playing, Lily saw a scary bug. She was scared and cried. Spot barked at the bug. Grandma heard them and came outside. "What's wrong, Lily?" asked Grandma. "There's a scary bug, Grandma!" said Lily.

Grandma smiled and said, "That bug may look scary, but it won't hurt you. It's just different, and that's okay. We should be kind to all creatures, big and small." Lily learned that even if something looks scary, it doesn't mean it's bad. She played with Spot and the bug, and they all had a fun day together.

Little Tom was walking around the garden and looking for something new. Suddenly, he saw a big mud puddle at the end of the garden. He was so excited and he wanted to soak himself in it. He carefully removed his collar and stepped into the mud. He tried to make lots of splashes.

Suddenly, he heard a noise. He was scared. He heard a voice. "Tom, why are you so dead in the mud?" asked a voice. It was his mom.

Tom smiled and said, "Mom, I'm just trying to have fun!"

Mom smiled. "Well, I guess it's ok as long as you don't get too soaked. Now, let's get you out of the mud and put your collar back on."

So, Tom got out of the mud and put his collar back on. He felt so good and excited. He now knew that it was ok to go and play in the mud every once in a while. He had so much fun and was so excited to show off his muddy collar to all his friends!

Once upon a time, there was an orange house in the middle of the woods. Inside the house lived a naughty cat. The cat liked to play around the house and have lots of fun.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toy cars and pretend she was driving a big vehicle. One day, her dad took her for a ride in his car. Lily was so excited to drive with her dad.

From that day on, Lily valued her shoes even more and never took them off at the park again.

Once there was a little girl. She was three years old. One day, she was feeling lucky. She wanted to find a way to make herself feel even more lucky. So she decided to go for a walk in the sunshine.

As she walked, she noticed a pond near her house. It was dry. She thought that if she could fill the pond with some water, it would make the pond come alive again. 

So she quickly ran home and grabbed a bucket and a hose. She attached the hose to a tap and began to fill up the bucket with water. Then she ran back to the pond and filled it up with the water. 

When the pond was full, the little girl felt very happy and lucky. She saw how the pond was alive again and had lots of little fishes swimming in the water. She was so pleased with her work and she was so proud! She thought that she had done a very good job.

Once upon a time there was a happy kid named Red. Red looked around and noticed how high the hill was. He thought to himself, "I wish I could climb that hill." Red decided to go find a way.

Once home, Red got out his file and started to work. He worked and worked, until finally he finished. Red was exhausted, but very proud of himself.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She was only three years old and very curious. She wanted to learn as much as she could about the world.

Once upon a time, there was a generous pirate. His name was Captain Bob. He was a tall, brave and strong pirate who sailed the seas in search of treasure. 

One day, Captain Bob spotted a tiny island in the middle of the ocean. He decided to explore it. When he got to the island, he was surprised by what he saw. There was a little boy, barely 3 years old, just sitting on the shore.

Captain Bob walked up to the little boy and said, "Hello there! What are you doing here all by yourself?"

The little boy looked up, smiled, and said, "Waiting for you!"

The pirate was confused, and asked, "What do you mean?" 

"I need you to take me back to my family," the little boy replied. 

Captain Bob smiled, and offered to hold the boy's hand and take him back. The little boy happily agreed, and they set sail together.

When they finally reached the little boy's home, his family was so grateful to generous Captain Bob for finding and returning their little boy safely. The little boy hugged the pirate and waved goodbye. 

And so, Captain Bob sailed off with a treasure more valuable than all the gold in the world: the trust of a little boy.

One day there was a tall cat. It lay in the grass, basking in the sun. It was soft and fluffy. Suddenly, the cat heard a noise. It was the sound of a small bird. The bird flew over and lay down next to the cat. They became the best of friends. The cat cuddled up with the bird. It closed its eyes and purred happily. The day ended and the cat lay down for a nap. The bird settled in a tree and watched over its friend. The cat and bird were always together from that day forward.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved ice-cream more than anything in the world. Every day, she asked her mom for ice-cream, but her mom said no because it was too close to dinner time.

One day, Lily's mom took her to the park to play. Lily saw an ice-cream truck and got very nervous. She wanted ice-cream, but she knew her mom would say no.

Lily's mom saw how nervous she was and asked her what was wrong. Lily told her about the ice-cream truck and how much she wanted some. Her mom said they could get some, but only if they ate their dinner first. This prevented Lily from being sad and made her very happy. She enjoyed her ice-cream with a big smile on her face.

Tim and his daddy were fishing together by the lake. He was so excited to be there with his daddy.

"What are you going to do, Timmy?" asked his daddy.

Tim smiled excitedly, "I'm going to put the hook in the water!" 

His daddy beamed, giving him a big hug and said, "That sounds great!"

Tim grabbed the hook and anxiously put it in the water. He peered over the edge, squinting his eyes, looking for the fish. Suddenly he felt something tug on the hook!

The two of them cheered as Tim pulled the fish out. He put the fish in the bucket, and thanked his dad for the wonderful day.

"You're welcome, Timmy," his dad said. "Let's do it again soon!"

Once upon a time there was a elderly beetle who lived in a big forest. Every day she would provide food and shelter for all the animals in the woods. One day she heard a noise coming from a nearby tree. She slowly crept up to the tree to see what was going on. When she arrived, she saw a small 3 year old boy picking apples and singing.

The beetle said, "Hello there! What are you doing in my woods?"

The little boy stopped singing and smiled. "I'm picking apples for my mommy! She said I could come here," he replied.

The beetle smiled and said, "What a kind thing to do! I'm an elderly beetle and I provide food for all the animals in the woods, would you like to help me?

The boy nodded eagerly, so the beetle and the boy worked together to provide food for all the animals. Afterward, the beetle thanked the boy for all his help. 

The little boy smiled and waved goodbye to the elderly beetle. From that day on, the beetle was happy knowing that she had a new friend who could help her provide for the animals in the woods.

Once upon a time there was a little puppy called Rosy. She loved to eat bones and spends her days running around and playing. One day, Rosy was out walking with her owner when they came across a pink bone. Rosy pounced on the bone and started to chew it. 

"Ah-ha!" She exclaimed. "This bone must have been left here just for me!"

Her owner looked down at her and said, "Not so fast Rosy, that bone could belong to someone else. We must find out."

They heard a distant bark, so Rosy and her owner followed the sound. They soon came across a big dog who was looking for something. 

"Is that pink bone yours?" asked Rosy's owner.

The big dog answered, "Yes it is! I was looking everywhere for it. Thank you so much for finding it!"

Rosy shouted, "You're welcome!"

So Rosy and her owner returned the bone to the big dog, and off he went, delighted now that he had his bone back. Rosy, however, was a bit sad she didn't get to keep the pink bone. 

But, Rosy's owner said with a smile, "Don't worry, I know just where to find you lots of bones!"

One day Timmy was walking in the park. He saw a big ball and he thought it looked fun. He decided to touch it but it was surprisingly harsh. He called out loudly for his mummy but no one answered. 

Timmy was getting scared so he started to walk faster. Then a big mean looking dog starting to chase him. Timmy shouted and ran but he couldn't get away from it. 

Suddenly the dog growled loudly and Timmy was very scared. The dog was about to bite when the park keeper arrived. The park keeper shouted and waved his stick at the dog and the dog ran away. 

Timmy was relieved but then he heard his mummy calling him. She looked angry and told him off for getting in trouble. Timmy felt bad and started to cry. His fun day had ended on a really harsh note.

Once upon a time there was a little boy called John. John wanted to find out the answer to a very important question - why was the sky blue?

John asked everybody he saw if they knew the answer but nobody knew. Everybody just shrugged and said they didn't know.

John was determined to discover the answer. So he asked his mum if she knew. His mum thought for a while and then she said, "Why don't you ask your grandma?"

John was thrilled. He already knew he could trust his grandma to give him the answer.

So John set off for Grandma's house. When he arrived, he was greeted with a big bowl of delicious steaming rice. Grandma smiled and asked why he had come to see her.

John told Grandma his question. Grandma thought for a moment and then she said, "Well, John, the sky is blue because of something called light reflecting off particles in the atmosphere. The particles are very small but they make the sky blue."

John thanked his grandma for being so persistent and helping him find out the answer. He gave her a big hug and then went home, happy and content that he knew the answer to his question.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She had a hanger in her hand. The hanger felt cold and distant. She looked far away, like she was looking for something special.

She finally found what she was looking for - a small door. It was far away, but the little girl knew it was the right one. She opened the door and found a secret room.

The secret room was dark, but she could see something shining in the corner. She went over to take a closer look and saw a beautiful diamond necklace. She grabbed it and put it around her neck.

She didn't want to leave the secret room, so she decided to close the door. She put the hanger on the door and it stayed shut. Now the secret room was locked up tight.

Once upon a time, there was a girl who had a purse that was very clean. The purse included many different treats, like candy, toys, and coins. Every Sunday, she went with her mommy to the store to pick new things to include in her purse.

The girl was really excited to see what was in her purse each time. She enjoyed playing with all the new toys and eating the candy. She even liked counting all the coins.

Today, the girl was extra excited because her mommy had given her an extra special treat to include in her purse. It was an ice cream cone for her to enjoy! 

The girl was so happy to have so many fun things in her purse. She couldn't wait to show her friends her new treasures.

Once upon a time, there was a big, red ball that loved to bounce. It lived in a hall with many different toys. One day, the ball heard a loud noise and saw a new toy coming into the hall. The new toy was a small, blue car. The red ball was very excited and wanted to play with the car.

The red ball and the blue car became very good friends. They played together every day in the hall. One day, they decided to play a game. The red ball would bounce high and the blue car would try to catch it. They had so much fun playing this game, but the red ball wanted to bounce even higher.

The red ball bounced higher and higher, trying to reach the sky. The blue car watched in amazement as the red ball went higher than ever before. Suddenly, the red ball bounced so high that it touched the ceiling of the hall. The ceiling opened up and the red ball bounced outside into the bright, sunny day. The blue car was so happy for its friend, the red ball, because it had finally bounced as high as it wanted to.

Lily and Tom were twins who liked to play in the park. One day, they saw a big truck with a picture of a cone and a scoop of cream on it. They ran to the truck and asked for some cream.

The man in the truck smiled and gave them each a cone with cream. Lily chose vanilla and Tom chose chocolate. They licked their cream and said thank you.

But then, a big dog came and jumped on Tom. He wanted to eat his cream. Tom was scared and dropped his cone. The dog ate it and ran away.

Tom was sad and cried. Lily saw him and felt sorry. She had an idea. She broke her cone in half and gave one half to Tom. She said, "Here, you can have some of my cream. We can share."

Tom smiled and took the half cone. He licked the cream and said thank you. He hugged Lily and said, "You are a good sister. You are wise and kind."

Lily hugged him back and said, "You are a good brother. You are brave and sweet."

They finished their cream and went to play on the swings. They were happy and had fun. The man in the truck saw them and smiled. He thought they were nice twins. He shouted, "Have a good day, Lily and Tom!"

Once there was a little boy who was very excited. He was so excited, he wanted to show everyone his new toy. Suddenly, a thief came and tried to take it away. The little boy was so embarrassed. He yelled for help, and soon his dad came running into the room. Dad saw the thief and quickly took the toy back. He scolded the thief and the thief ran away. 

The little boy felt so relieved and hugged his dad. Everyone else in the room was so proud of him, they clapped and cheered! The little boy was relieved and excited all over again. He knew he had done the right thing and felt much better.

Once upon a time, there was a cool lion who liked to swim. Every day, he would go to the lake near his home and splash around in the water.

One day, when the lion was swimming, he heard a something loud. He turned around, and saw giant dinosaur coming towards him! The dinosaur was roaring very loudly, and the lion was so scared!

He quickly swam away and the dinosaur followed him. The lion thought that he was done for, and he was even more scared.

But then, something unexpected happened. The little lion swam faster and faster, faster and faster than the dinosaur. The lion outswam the dinosaur and won the race!

With a sigh of relief, the lion returned to the shore and looked back at the distant figure of the dinosaur. The lion was so happy he had won, and he was very proud of himself. He felt so cool!

Anne was a three year old girl who loved people and loved to explore the world. She had an idea, to go on a tour around the world and do something powerful.

Anne asked her dad, "Daddy can I go on a tour around the world and do something powerful?", her dad said "yes, of course you can, if you sign this agreement first".
 
Anne was very excited, so she ran to get a pen and signed the agreement. Her dad smiled and said, "Good job! Now let's get ready for your tour".

Anne went to some amazing places, and did some very powerful things. She posed for pictures with important people, and made a lot of friends. 

When Anne got back home, she said goodbye to her friends, hugged her dad and said, "I had the most amazing time on my tour! I'll forever remember what I did because it was so powerful". Her dad smiled and said, "A big adventure awaits you, my dear".

Once upon a time, there was a little cat named Kitty. She lived in a small house with her family. One day, Kitty woke up and felt very hungry. She wanted to eat a good meal.

Kitty went to the kitchen and looked for some food. She opened the cupboard, but it was empty. Kitty sighed because she was very hungry and there was no food. She decided to go outside and look for something to eat.

Kitty walked around and found a big apple tree. She climbed the tree and picked some apples. Then, she went back home and shared the apples with her family. They all ate the apples and were happy. Kitty was glad she could find a meal for her family, and they all had full bellies.

Lily loves her new puppy. His name is Spot and he has black and white fur. Lily wants to teach Spot how to do tricks. She thinks it will be easy and fun.

She takes Spot to the backyard and shows him a ball. She says, "Spot, look at the ball. I will throw it and you will catch it. That is a trick. Can you do it?" She throws the ball and waits for Spot to run after it.

But Spot does not run after the ball. He runs after a butterfly instead. He jumps and barks and tries to catch the butterfly. Lily laughs and says, "Spot, that is not the ball. That is a butterfly. Come back here and try again."

She throws the ball again and this time Spot runs after it. He catches it in his mouth and brings it back to Lily. Lily claps and says, "Good boy, Spot! You did it! You learned a trick. I am proud of you." She gives him a hug and a treat.

Spot wags his tail and licks her face. He likes learning tricks with Lily. He thinks it is easy and fun. He hopes she will teach him more tricks later. He loves his new friend.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play with his toys and his favorite toy was a red car. One day, Timmy's friend came over to play. 

"Wow, I like your car! Can I play with it?" asked Timmy's friend.

"Yes, you can play with it. But please be careful with it because it's my own car," replied Timmy.

Timmy's friend was very happy and played with the car for a while. Suddenly, he saw a flag on the floor. "Look, Timmy! What is this flag for?" he asked.

"That's my dad's flag. He is a dependable soldier and he always carries it with him," Timmy explained.

Timmy and his friend played together for a long time and had a lot of fun. When it was time for his friend to go home, Timmy said, "Thank you for playing with me and taking care of my own car. Let's play again soon!"

Sara loved to play with her mom's purse. It had many things inside that seemed fun and pretty. She liked to take out the lipstick, the keys, the coins, and the sunglasses and pretend she was a grown-up lady.

One day, Sara saw her mom's purse on the table. She thought her mom was busy in the kitchen and would not mind if she played with it for a little while. She grabbed the purse and ran to her room. She opened the purse and started to take out the things inside.

She put on the lipstick and made a funny face in the mirror. She jingled the keys and imagined she was driving a car. She counted the coins and thought she was rich. She put on the sunglasses and felt very cool.

She was having so much fun that she did not hear her mom calling her name. She did not notice that one of the things she took out of the purse was a small envelope. She did not see that the envelope had a sticker that said "Do not open until your birthday".

Her mom came to her room and saw Sara playing with her purse. She was not angry, but she was surprised. She said, "Sara, what are you doing with my purse? You know you are not supposed to touch it without asking me."

Sara looked at her mom and smiled. She said, "I'm sorry, mom. I just wanted to play with your things. They are so charming. Look, I have lipstick, keys, coins, and sunglasses. And I have this envelope too. What is inside?"

Her mom gasped and took the envelope from Sara. She said, "Oh, Sara, this is a special envelope. It is a gift for you. But you are not supposed to open it until your birthday. It is a surprise."

Sara's eyes widened and she said, "A gift for me? A surprise? What is it, mom? Can I open it now? Please, please, please?"

Her mom shook her head and said, "No, Sara, you have to wait. It is only a few days until your birthday. Then you can open it and see what it is. I promise you, it is something very wonderful. Something you will love."

Sara pouted and said, "But I want to see it now. I can't wait. Please, mom, just a little peek."

Her mom hugged her and said, "No, Sara, you have to be patient. Trust me, it will be worth it. Now, let's put everything back in my purse and go to the kitchen. I have a treat for you. Some cookies and milk. How does that sound?"

Sara nodded and said, "OK, mom. I'm sorry I played with your purse. I love you. And I love your gift. Even if I don't know what it is."

Her mom smiled and said, "I love you too, Sara. And I'm glad you love your gift. But you have to wait until your birthday to open it. It is a secret. A very special secret."

Once there was a hot day in the garden and all the animals were looking for a cool place to rest. A butterfly fluttered past, looking for a tree with a shady spot. Suddenly, the butterfly spied an old oak tree, waving it's leafy branches in the gentle breeze. She fluttered over and landed on the tree with a sigh of relief.

The animal friends she had made in the garden were all gathered around the foot of the tree. They had been playing tag and were panting from the heat. The butterfly knew she had found the perfect spot to rest for the night. She settled down in a shady nook and waited for the sun to go down.

The animals around the tree taught the butterfly a valuable lesson. The butterfly realised that sometimes it can be better to find a quiet spot and rest than to tire yourself out with too much play. She thanked the animals for teaching her this important lesson and flew off towards home, feeling much cooler now that the sun went down.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Abby. She was three years old and she liked to play at night. One night, Abby wanted to go outside, so her mom gave her a flashlight. She was so excited! She held it tightly as she opened the door and stepped outside. 

Suddenly, it was very dark. Abby felt embarrassed and scared, but she held the flashlight up and shone it around. The light made everything better and much brighter. 

Abby began to explore. She found the furry cat hiding in the bushes, and the big bird sleeping in the tree. Everywhere she looked, the flashlight made things easier to see. 

Abby had so much fun exploring with her flashlight. It made her feel brave and not scared anymore. Later she went back inside, still holding the flashlight tightly. The end.

Lily and Tom were playing in the park. They saw a man with a cane. He walked very slowly and looked sad.

"Hello, sir," Lily said. "Do you want to play with us?"

The man smiled. "Thank you, little girl, but I can't play. My leg hurts and I need this cane to help me."

Tom had an idea. He ran to the sandbox and grabbed some sand and sticks. He started to build something.

"What are you building, Tom?" Lily asked.

"I'm building a new cane for the man. Maybe it will make him happy," Tom said.

He worked hard and made a cane out of sand and sticks. He put a flower on top. He brought it to the man.

"Here, sir, this is for you. A new cane. It has a flower, too," Tom said.

The man was surprised. He took the cane and held it gently.

"Wow, this is amazing. You are very kind, little boy. Thank you so much," the man said.

He tried to stand up with the cane, but it broke. The sand and sticks fell to the ground.

"Oh, no, I'm sorry. It was not strong enough," Tom said.

The man laughed. "Don't worry, it's okay. It was a beautiful gesture. You made my day. I'm very grateful to you and your friend," the man said.

He hugged Tom and Lily. They hugged him back.

They all smiled and felt happy.

Once upon a time, there was a rug. It was so soft and fluffy. It lived in a cozy house called David's. David was a very nice boy who was only three years old. 

David liked to play on the rug all day long. He loved to feel its softness against his skin. He often had very sweet dreams while he was laying on it. 

One day, he started talking to the rug. He asked it if it minded him playing on it all day. Surprisingly, the rug replied back to him! It said that it loved having David play on it and that it felt a special bond with him. 

David then thanked the rug and made a promise to play on it every day. He then hugged the rug and thanked it for taking care of him. 

From that day onwards, David and the rug were the best of friends. They played together all day long and shared many sweet moments. David was so glad that the rug didn't mind him playing on it.

Once upon a time, there were two best friends named Joe and Sam. After a long day of playing in the park, they were both tired and thirsty.

"Let's make something to drink," Joe said.

"I know!" Sam said. "We can make a hose!"

Joe and Sam took some soft pieces of cloth, and tied them together in a line. They found some sticks, and used those to join the cloth together.

Then, Joe put one end of the hose into a small bucket of water. Very quickly, water started to flow from the other end of the hose.

Joe and Sam were so happy! Now, they could both have some cool, refreshing water to drink.

"Wow!" Sam said. "This hose is really cool."

"Yep," Joe agreed. "It's a really soft and simple way to make some fun."

Tom is a fisherman. He likes to catch fish in the sea. He has a big boat and a net. Every morning, he wakes up early and goes to the sea.

One day, he sees a big fish in the water. He is very excited. He throws his net and tries to catch the fish. But the fish is too strong and fast. It pulls the net and the boat. Tom is scared. He shouts for help.

"Help! Help! There is a big fish in my net!"

Lily is a girl who lives near the sea. She hears Tom's shout. She runs to the shore and sees Tom's boat. She sees the big fish too. She has an idea. She takes a big stick and a rope. She runs to the end of the pier. She ties the rope to the stick. She throws the stick to Tom.

"Tom! Tom! Catch the stick!"

Tom catches the stick. He ties the stick to his boat. He lets go of the net. The fish swims away with the net. Tom is safe. He thanks Lily.

"Thank you, Lily! You are very brave and smart!"

Lily smiles. She is happy to help Tom. She likes Tom. She likes fish too. She asks Tom.

"Tom, can I go with you to the sea tomorrow? I want to see more fish."

Tom nods. He likes Lily too. He says.

"Of course, Lily. You can come with me. But we have to sleep early tonight. The sea is more beautiful in the morning."

Lily agrees. She says goodbye to Tom. She goes home and sleeps. Tom goes home and sleeps too. They both dream of fish and the sea. They are excited for tomorrow.

Once upon a time, there were two friends named Thomas and John. They loved to play together. The boys would often play chess to keep themselves entertained.

One day, Thomas wanted to play a different game, so he said to John, "Let's jump!" John was hesitant at first, but after much convincing from Thomas, John finally agreed.

John asked his friend, "How long should we jump for?" Thomas replied, "Let's jump for a long time!"

So, the boys jumped and jumped until they were both exhausted. After their fun, the boys agreed that it would be fun to play chess again soon. 

The moral of the story is that it's okay to try new things from time to time, but it's also good to come back to the things we enjoy.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to read books about history. One day, Tim went to the library with his mom. He wanted to find a new book to read. Tim was very excited.

At the library, Tim saw a big book with a crazy picture on the cover. He thought it looked fun. Tim requested his mom to help him get the book. His mom smiled and said, "Okay, let's see what this book is about."

They opened the book and found many stories about history. One story was about a king who had a crazy idea. The king wanted to make everyone in his kingdom wear a funny hat. Tim laughed and laughed. He knew that the crazy picture on the cover was a clue about the funny story inside. Tim and his mom took the book home and read it together. They had a great time reading about the king and his crazy idea.

Once upon a time there was a grumpy old man. He loved to store things.

One day, he went to the store and bought some milk. He was so excited to store it in his home.

The old man took the milk home and put it in the closet. He felt very proud of all the things he could store in his closet.

But the next day, something strange happened. When the old man went to get his milk from the closet, it was gone! He was so grumpy.

He searched everywhere for his milk, but he couldn't find it. It was a mystery!

Then one day, the old man found a small mouse in his closet. The mouse had been drinking the milk! He was so relieved that he'd gotten his milk back.

The old man was not so grumpy anymore. From then on, he was careful to store his milk safely. He never wanted to lose it again!

Once upon a time, there was a lady who was very confused. She didn't know where she was or what she was supposed to do. She walked around asking everyone she met for help.

One day, she met a little girl who asked her what was wrong. The lady said she was confused and didn't know what to do. The little girl said, "Don't worry, I can help you. Let's go to my house and we can figure it out together."

At the little girl's house, they sat down and talked. The little girl asked the lady what things she liked to do. The lady said she liked to read books and go for walks. The little girl said, "I have some books we can read and we can go for a walk in the park. That includes things you like to do!"

The lady was very happy and thanked the little girl for her help. They read books and went for a walk in the park together. The lady was no longer confused and felt very grateful for the little girl's kindness.

John was feeling sad one day, so he asked his mom for a hug. She smiled and said yes. She wrapped him up in her big, soft blanket. John felt warm and safe.

John asked his mom if he could go outside and play. She replied, â€œNo, Iâ€™m sorry. Itâ€™s too cold todayâ€. John sighed, it was boring inside.

John asked his mom if she could play with him. She smiled and said, â€œYes, I would love to!â€ They played with his toys and it was lots of fun.

John was happy and asked his mom if he could stay inside a little longer. She replied, â€œYes, but put your blanket back on to keep you warmâ€. John smiled and cuddled in his warm blanket.

Tom and Sam were best friends. They liked to play with cars, balls and blocks. One day, they found a big box in the park. They opened it and saw many shiny toys inside.

"Wow, look at these!" Tom said. He grabbed a red car and a blue truck. "These are mine!"

Sam looked at the toys too. He saw a yellow bike and a green plane. He wanted to play with them, but Tom did not let him.

"No, these are mine too!" Tom said. He pushed Sam away and put all the toys in his arms.

Sam felt sad and angry. He did not like Tom's behavior. He thought Tom was not a good friend. He said, "Tom, you are not fair. You should share the toys with me. We are friends, remember?"

Tom did not listen to Sam. He said, "No, I found them first. They are all mine. Go away!"

Sam was hurt by Tom's words. He decided to leave Tom alone. He walked away from the box and looked for another place to play.

As he walked, he saw a girl sitting on a bench. She had a big book in her lap. She smiled at Sam and said, "Hi, do you want to read with me? This is a fun book. It has many pictures and stories."

Sam was curious about the book. He said, "Yes, I want to read with you. What is your name?"

The girl said, "My name is Lily. What is yours?"

Sam said, "My name is Sam. Nice to meet you, Lily."

Lily and Sam became friends. They read the book together and had a good time. Lily showed Sam the pictures and told him the stories. Sam learned many new things from the book. He liked Lily's kindness and generosity. He said, "Lily, you are a good friend. Thank you for sharing your book with me."

Lily said, "You are welcome, Sam. You are a good friend too. Thank you for reading with me."

They hugged each other and smiled.

Meanwhile, Tom was still holding the toys in his arms. He felt lonely and bored. He realized that he had no one to play with. He looked around and saw Sam and Lily on the bench. They seemed happy and friendly. He felt sorry for what he had done. He wished he had shared the toys with Sam. He decided to go and apologize to Sam.

He walked towards the bench and said, "Sam, I am sorry. I was wrong. I should have shared the toys with you. You are my best friend. Can you forgive me?"

Sam looked at Tom and saw that he was sincere. He remembered that Tom was his best friend too. He said, "Tom, I forgive you. I am glad you came. You can play with us if you want."

Tom smiled and said, "Thank you, Sam. You are very kind. I want to play with you and Lily."

He put the toys on the ground and said, "These are for everyone. We can all play with them."

Sam and Lily accepted Tom's offer. They thanked him for the toys and invited him to join them. They picked up the toys and played together. They had fun and laughed a lot.

Tom learned a lesson that day. He learned that sharing is caring. He learned that being greedy is not good. He learned that being tough is not always right. He learned that being kind and generous is better. He learned that having friends is more important than having things.

He held Sam's and Lily's hands in his palms and said, "You are my best friends. I love you both."

They said, "We love you too, Tom. You are our best friend."

They hugged each other and smiled. They were happy.

Once there was a very smart bunny named Bun. He liked playing in the dark. One night, his mom told him it was bedtime, but Bun snuck out of bed. He grabbed his special toy, a little flashlight. He wanted to raise it up high and look around. He saw all kinds of things in the dark. He saw spiders and cats and he even saw a little mouse. Then he heard a noise. He was scared! He raiseed the flashlight up higher and saw it was his mom. She said "Bun, it's time to go to bed." Bun was so glad she was there. He raised the flashlight up to his face and smiled. And they both went back to bed.

Once upon a time, there lived a little girl who loved to go for walks. One day, she headed out with her stick and spotted a beautiful picture in the sky. She was mesmerized by the picture in the sky and decided to go closer.

As she walked, the ground started to get dizzy and she felt a bit scared. "Where am I going?" She thought to herself. She stopped and looked around and noticed a nice big tree with fruits. She picked a few of the fruits and was about to start her way back home. 

Suddenly, she heard a loud sound. There, she saw a big rabbit looking at her. "Hello there little one," said the rabbit. The little girl felt pleased. The rabbit offered her some more fruits from the tree. "These are magical fruits. If you eat them, you will have great strength and you will be able to yield more fruits from this tree!" exclaimed the rabbit. 

The little girl was excited. She thanked the rabbit and ate the fruits. To her surprise, she was able to touch the tree and the next thing she knew, fruits were falling from the tree. The little girl went home with her fresh bag of fruits. She was very happy.

Once upon a time there was a girl. She liked to do interesting things. She liked to run, jump and explore. One day she was feeling very curious. She decided to do something special. She wanted to see what a wink felt like.

So she winked with her eye. It felt funny and pleasing! She winked again and again. She found it to be so interesting. Then she started to do a little dance. She laughed and smiled with joy.

Soon the girl realized she had been winking for a very long time. She was thirsty and tired. So she stopped winking and ran home. From the window of her house she saw a butterfly. Its wings were sparkling in the sunlight.
