They start to climb the hill. They use their swords to help them. They stick their swords in the ground and pull themselves up. They have fun.

But when they get to the top of the hill, they see something scary. They see a big dog. The dog is barking and growling. The dog has sharp teeth and claws. The dog looks angry.

"Tom, look, a dog!" Sam says.

"Sam, run, a dog!" Tom says.

They are afraid of the dog. They do not want to play with the dog. They want to go back to their mommies. They turn around and run down the hill. They forget their swords. They drop their swords on the ground.

The dog sees their swords. The dog thinks they are sticks. The dog likes to play with sticks. The dog picks up their swords with his mouth. The dog runs after them. The dog wants to play with them.

"Tom, the dog has our swords!" Sam says.

"Sam, the dog is coming!" Tom says.

They run faster. They run to their mommies. They hug their mommies. They are safe.

"Mommy, there was a big dog on the hill!" Tom says.

"Mommy, the dog took our swords!" Sam says.

Their mommies look at the hill. They see the dog. The dog is wagging his tail. The dog is happy. The dog is not bad. The dog just wants to play.

"Boys, that is not a bad dog. That is a friendly dog. He likes your swords. He thinks they are toys. Maybe you can share your swords with him. Maybe you can be friends with him." Their mommies say.

Tom and Sam look at the dog. They look at their mommies. They look at each other. They are not afraid anymore. They are curious.

"Maybe we can, Mommy." Tom says.

"Maybe we can, Mommy." Sam says.

They go back to the hill. They go to the dog. They say hello to the dog. The dog says woof to them. They pet the dog. The dog licks them. They laugh.

They play with the dog. They play with their swords. They take turns throwing their swords and fetching them. They have fun.

They make a new friend. His name is Spot. He is a good dog. He likes to play with swords. He likes to play with Tom and Sam. They are happy.

Once there was a little girl named Sarah. She went to the store with her mom. Sarah's mom said, "Sarah, you can choose something for yourself." Sarah saw a pin that caught her eye. It had a spicy red color and looked magical.

Sarah said to her mom, "Can I please have the spicy pin?" Her mom said, "Yes, of course you can have the pin."

Sarah happily took the pin and put it in her pocket. She liked the pin because it was so spicy and made her feel special. She wanted to show her friends the pin, so she put it on her shirt.

Sarah loved her spicy pin and looked happy every time she saw it. She was proud that she chose something special all by herself.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Jack. Jack loved to play at the beach with his bucket and shovel. He would build sandcastles and collect seashells. 

One day, Jack saw a big wave coming towards him. The wave was so big, it looked like a mountain of water. Jack was scared, but he remembered what his mom had told him. She said that he should measure the waves with his eyes and wait for the right time to go in the water. 

Jack watched the wave carefully and noticed that it was getting smaller and smaller. Finally, it turned into a little white foam and gently touched his feet. Jack smiled and felt proud of himself for measuring the wave. From that day on, he knew how to stay safe at the beach.

Once upon a time, there were two birds. One bird was very brave, the other was very nervous.

One day the brave bird found a twig. She liked it so much that she decided to attach it to her nest. She worked very hard to make sure it was just right.

But the nervous bird was scared. He kept asking the brave bird if they should really attach the twig like that.

Eventually, the brave bird finished her work and the twig made the nest very strong. She looked at the nervous bird and said: "See, it is better to be brave and make the right choices, or else you'll never get things done!"

And the moral of this story is that you should be brave and make the right choices to get things done.

Timmy was playing in the sun when suddenly a nation of tall, colourful creatures appeared. Timmy had never seen anything like it before. They wore bright clothes, laughed loudly and stretched their long arms in the air!

Timmy asked the leader of the group, "Who are you?"

The leader replied, "We are called the Originals. We have come to bring joy and show you things you have never seen before. Would you like to join us?"

Timmy smiled and nodded eagerly in agreement. Then he stretched out his arm and joined hands with the Originals. He followed their instructions and stretched his body in weird and wonderful ways until the sun went down.

The Originals said goodbye to Timmy, telling him he was special, and then they vanished into the night.

As he walked home, Timmy smiled, feeling happy and more amazing than ever before.

Mommy was busy making dinner. She needed to mix some special ingredients together. She put them in a bowl. Then she stirred and stirred until everything was mixed up really well. 

When she was done, the bowl had a funny smell. Mommy tasted it and said "Mmm! Now that's a good mix!â€

But soon, Mommy felt a little bit of pain in her tummy. She forgot to add an important ingredient to her mix! She quickly got an apple and added it to the bowl. Now the smell was perfect! 

Mommy was happy with the mix, but she learned an important lesson: don't forget to add any ingredients when you mix!

Once upon a time, there was a boy. He wanted to go to the park. His mom said OK and off they went.

When they got to the park, they saw a big cut in the grass. It was dangerous and the boy was scared.

His mom told him to stand back and stay away from the cut. She said it looked like somebody had done it with a sharp tool.

So the boy listened to his mom and stayed away from the cut. He had lots of fun playing in the park and didn't get hurt.

He had a great day at the park and was glad he paid attention to his mom's warning. He knew that his mom was always looking out for him, and that made him feel safe.

Once upon a time there was a friendly deer. He was so thoughtful, he always wanted to share his special mushrooms with everyone he met. 
One day, the deer met a sly fox. The fox said he wanted to share the mushrooms too, but he had a sneaky plan. 
The deer agreed to share the mushrooms and the fox grabbed them all. As soon as the fox had the mushrooms, he ran away.
The deer was so sad. He had been so kind and thoughtful but the fox tricked him. The deer was sad and never shared his mushrooms again.

Once there was a beetle. He was a very unique beetle. He would fly through the meadow, zig zagging between the bright yellow flowers. But one day, the beetle was in a very sour mood. He couldn't find any happy smiles, as if his world had disappeared.

He decided to look for help and begged for it from every creature he ran into. His cries for help soon reached a butterfly's ears. She stopped to listen. The butterfly told him to forgive himself and forgive anyone who had ever hurt or upset him. She said forgiveness was the key to finding happiness again.

The beetle thought long and hard about what the butterfly had said. The more he thought, the brighter his world became and he found a special kind of peace within himself. 

The beetle felt like a new bug. He was happy again and ready to face the world with a forgiving heart. He thanked the butterfly for her kindness and flew joyfully through the meadow.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Bree wanted to build something. She found some pieces of wood and asked her Dad if she could make something with them. Dad said she could, so Bree started to build.

She built a big shield. It was so big that it would cover her whole body. She was very proud of her work and wanted to show it to everyone.

But then she walked into the sun and the shield started to melt. Bree was sad, but Dad said it was ok. He told her that if she wanted something to last, she had to build it with stronger materials.

Bree learned something very important, that if you want something to last you must make it strong. So she put aside the wooden shield and started to look for stronger material.

The moral of the story is that if you want something to last, you must build it with stronger materials. Even though it might be harder, doing it right will help it last longer.

Sara and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toys, but they do not like to share. One day, they find a big box in the living room. It is a gift from their grandma. They are very happy and run to open it.

Inside the box, there is a beautiful doll with long hair and a blue dress. Sara loves the doll and wants to keep it. Ben also likes the doll and wants to play with it. They start to fight over the doll. They pull and tug and yell. They disagree on who should have the doll.

Their mom hears the noise and comes to see what is wrong. She is very angry and sad. She tells them that the doll is for both of them, and they have to share and take turns. She says that is the fair thing to do. But Sara and Ben do not listen. They keep fighting and do not care about their mom.

Their mom gets very upset and decides to teach them a lesson. She takes the doll away from them and puts it back in the box. She says that they do not deserve the doll, and they will not get it back until they learn to share and be nice. She takes the box and leaves the room.

Sara and Ben are in shock. They cannot believe that their mom took away their doll. They start to cry and regret their actions. They wish they had listened to their mom and shared the doll. They realize that they were selfish and mean. They hug each other and say they are sorry. But it is too late. The doll is gone, and they do not know when they will see it again. They are very sad and unhappy. The end.

Once upon a time there was a bench. It was an unusual bench. Every night something special happened on the bench.

Every night, a big bear came to the bench and fell asleep. No one could believe it. Everyone was so curious.

One night, a brave little girl decided to take a closer look. She sneaked up to the bench, very quietly. To her surprise the bear wasn't asleep. He was wide awake and said, "Hi there! Would you like to be my friend?"

The little girl was so excited. She said, "Yes!" and stayed with the bear until morning. The bear taught her lots of things and they laughed and played.

Before the sun came up, the bear said it was time for him to sleep. He gave the little girl a big hug and a kiss before he curled up on the unusual bench and fell sound asleep. 

The little girl was very happy. She knew she had made a very special friend.

John had a broken toy. He was sad until his mom set him down and said she could fix it. She told John she had to find some hair first. John watched as his mom opened a drawer and set her hand inside. She pulled out a little box filled with colorful hairs. She took one and set it in the toy. 

John watched as his mom wiggled the hair around until the broken toy was fixed. John was so happy he clapped his hands and jumped. His mom laughed and gave him a big hug. 

John loves when his mom fixes his broken toys. He knows she can do anything with her special hair!

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Molly. She loved to sing and dance. She especially loved to perform on stage!

One day, Molly's parents took her to the theatre. She was so excited! There was a big stage and lots of people.

Molly's mom said, "Let's go get a microphone!" Molly smiled and ran to get one.

The microphone was big and it had lots of buttons. Molly was so excited to try it out. She turned it on and began to sing.

Suddenly, a voice came from the speakers: "Hey Molly, this is the theatre manager. You need to order the microphone from us before you can use it."

Molly's face turned sad. She wanted to use the microphone now. But her mom said, "It's okay, Molly. You can order the microphone and soon you can perform on the stage."

Molly smiled and ordered the microphone. Her dream of performing on stage was now a reality!

Alice was very creative. One day she had a great idea! She wanted to fly. She looked around and found a large piece of paper. 

Alice decided to use the paper to make wings. She sketched the wings and cut them out. She used the help of her parents to attach the wings to her back. 

Alice ran outside and urged her parents to watch. She tried to flap her wings, but she only moved an inch or two. Alice felt frustrated and sad. 

Alice tried again. This time she held her arms out and spread her wings wide. She urged herself to take a leap. She held her breath and jumped. To her amazement, she flew! 

Alice flew higher and higher. She looped and twirled in the sky. Her parents watched in astonished wonder. Alice had done it! She flew!

Lily was a princess who loved to play with her dolls. She had many dolls, but her favorite was a pink one with long hair and a shiny dress. She named her doll Rose and took her everywhere.

One day, Lily went to the park with her mom and Rose. She saw a big slide and wanted to try it. She ran to the slide, but she was careless. She forgot to hold Rose in her arms. She left her on the bench.

"Mom, look at me!" Lily shouted as she slid down. "I'm so fast!"

Mom smiled and clapped. "You're very brave, Lily. But where is Rose?"

Lily gasped. She looked around and saw a boy holding Rose. He was pulling her hair and ripping her dress.

"Hey, that's my doll!" Lily cried. She ran to the boy and tried to take Rose back.

"No, it's mine now!" the boy said. He pushed Lily away and ran.

Lily was sad and angry. She loved Rose and did not want to lose her. She followed the boy and shouted, "Give me back my doll!"

Mom saw what happened and followed Lily. She caught up with the boy and said, "Stop, young man. That's not your doll. That's Lily's doll. You should not take things that are not yours. That's not nice."

The boy looked scared. He saw Mom's stern face and heard Lily's sobbing. He felt sorry. He gave Rose back to Lily and said, "I'm sorry. I was careless. I just wanted to play with the doll. She's very pretty."

Lily took Rose and hugged her. She checked her hair and her dress. They were messy and torn. She felt sad, but also happy to have Rose back.

"Thank you for giving me back my doll," Lily said. "But you should not hurt her. She's very special to me. I love her."

The boy nodded. He said, "I'm sorry. I love dolls too. But I don't have any. Can I play with you and your doll?"

Lily thought for a moment. She saw the boy's hopeful eyes and remembered how she loved to play with her dolls. She said, "Okay. But you have to be gentle and careful. And you have to share."

The boy smiled. He said, "Okay. I will. Thank you."

Mom smiled too. She said, "That's very kind of you, Lily. You're a good princess. And you're a good friend."

Lily smiled. She said, "Thank you, Mom. I love you. And I love Rose. And I love playing with dolls."

The end.

Once there was a lonely foot. He didn't have any friends and he was very sad. Every day he went to the park but no one wanted to play with him.

One day, while he was in the park, he heard a voice. It said "I need help! Can you solve my problem?" The foot couldn't believe it, someone wanted his help! 

The foot looked around but he couldn't see anyone so he called out "Where are you?"

Then he looked up and saw a bird high up in the tree. The bird was stuck in some sticky sap and it couldn't get down.

The foot laughed and said "I know how to solve that problem!" He quickly ran and found some stones which he put around the tree. Then the foot climbed up the stones and rescued the bird.

The foot and the bird became good friends and now they go to the park together every day. The foot is no longer lonely, and he is so proud that he solved the bird's problem.

Timmy was playing with his toys in the living room when he heard a strange noise. It sounded like it was coming from the backyard. Curious, he opened the back door.

To his surprise, there was a racecar! It was made of red lego blocks and had a big engine sticking out of the back.

Timmy was so excited that he called for his brother, Bobby. Bobby came running outside and both of them looked at the racecar with awe.

"Who built this car?" They asked themselves.

Suddenly, a voice came from nowhere. "I built it," said the voice.

Timmy and Bobby looked around and saw a friendly looking man standing nearby. He smiled and said, "My name is Ted and I built this reliable racecar. Would you like to join me for a race around the garden?"

Timmy and Bobby looked at each other and jumped with joy. "Yes!" they shouted in unison. 

They all raced around the garden and had so much fun that day.

One day, John was in the kitchen next to his mother. He was hungry so he asked her for a snack. His mother gave him a bowl of icy cold ice cream with a long spoon beside it. John was excited and reached for the spoon to start eating. 

"Wait John," his mother said. She took the spoon from him and asked, "Can you reach it?" 
John nodded and stretched out his short arm to get the spoon. He was a determined three year old and tried to grab the spoon with his tiny hands. After a few tries, he finally got it and said, "I reached it!!". His mother smiled and patted him on the head. 

John was so proud of himself that he immediately started eating the icy cold ice cream. He said, "Yum! Delicious!" 

The End.

In the summer season, Mama and Baby were outside playing.

Mama said: "Let's design something fun."

Baby said: "Yes!"

Mama smiled and took Baby's hand. They walked around looking for something special.

They found a piece of wood, a hammer and some nails. Mama said: "Let's make something!"

They worked together to design a birdhouse. They hammered the nails, sawed the wood and painted it in a bright blue. The birdhouse was beautiful and very clean.

Mama said: "Look, Baby! We designed it together." Baby smiled. 

They stepped back to admire their birdhouse. It was perfect.

Sara and Ben are playing in the park. They see a big butterfly with many colors. They want to catch it and look at it.

"Come, butterfly, come!" Sara says. She runs after the butterfly. Ben follows her.

The butterfly flies away from them. It goes to a flower, then to a tree, then to a pond. Sara and Ben try to catch it, but it is too fast.

"Wait, butterfly, wait!" Ben says. He has a net in his hand. He swings the net at the butterfly.

But the butterfly is smart. It flies over the net and lands on Ben's shoe. Ben looks down and smiles.

"Hi, butterfly, hi!" he says. He bends down and tries to pick up the butterfly.

But the butterfly is tricky. It flies up and lands on Sara's hair. Sara feels something tickle her head. She reaches up and touches the butterfly.

"Wow, butterfly, wow!" she says. She holds the butterfly gently in her hand. She shows it to Ben.

"Look, butterfly, look!" she says. She brings the butterfly close to her face. The butterfly flaps its wings and tickles her nose.

Sara and Ben laugh. They think the butterfly is funny and pretty. They want to keep it as a friend.

But the butterfly wants to be free. It flies out of Sara's hand and goes back to the flowers. Sara and Ben watch it go.

"Bye, butterfly, bye!" they say. They wave to the butterfly.

They are not sad. They are happy. They had fun with the butterfly. They learned something new.

They decide to play something else. They see a swing and a slide. They run to them.

"Let's swing, let's slide!" they say. They have more fun in the park.

They remember to tie their shoes. They know how to tie. It is easy for them. They are big kids. They are proud of themselves.

Lily and Ben were at the park with their mom. They saw a big slide that looked like fun. Lily wanted to go first, but Ben was scared.

"Come on, Ben, it's easy. You just sit and slide down. Whee!" Lily said as she climbed the ladder.

Ben gazed at the slide. It was very high and shiny. He did not want to sit and slide down. He wanted to stay with mom.

"No, Lily, it's too hard. I don't like it. I want to play with the ball." Ben said as he hugged mom's leg.

Mom smiled and gave Ben a kiss. She said, "It's okay, Ben. You don't have to slide if you don't want to. But maybe you can watch Lily and cheer for her. She likes to slide a lot."

Ben nodded and watched Lily. She slid down fast and laughed. She looked happy and brave. Ben clapped his hands and said, "Good job, Lily! You are so fast!"

Lily ran back to Ben and mom. She said, "Thank you, Ben! That was fun! Do you want to try now?"

Ben shook his head. He said, "No, thank you, Lily. Maybe another day. I like to play with the ball. Do you want to play with me?"

Lily nodded. She said, "Yes, Ben, I want to play with you. You are good at the ball. Let's go!"

They took the ball and ran to the grass. Mom followed them with a smile. She said, "You are both good at different things. And you are both very kind. I love you, Lily and Ben."

They hugged mom and said, "We love you too, mom." They played with the ball and had a lot of fun. They were happy and gentle. They were good friends.

Mama and Baby were walking through the park. Baby saw a little tiger and cried out, "Look Mama!" Mama smiled, "Let's clap for the tiger!" 

Baby clapped her little hands together and the tiger jumped. Mama and Baby laughed. Baby asked, "Can I pat the tiger?" Mama said, "No, it's too wild".

Baby clapped again and the tiger hopped away. Mama and Baby watched as the tiger went further into the woods. Baby waved goodbye and said, "Bye, little tiger!" 

Mama and Baby kept walking, but Baby kept looking back at the tiger. With every glance, Baby clapped her hands and smiled.

One day, Peter and his Grandma decided to go on a walk in the park. It was a very sunny day and Peter was excited to explore all of the sights. 

As they made their way through the park, Peter noticed something unusual. He saw a large muscle on the ground. 

"What is that?" asked Peter. 

"I'm not sure," replied Grandma. "Let's go have a closer look."

When they approached the muscle, they noticed it was twitching. 

"I guess it's alive!" exclaimed Peter. 

Grandma smiled and nodded. "Let's move away and let it rest. It must be very tired."

They watched the muscle carefully until it disappeared in the distance. Peter had seen something unusual on his walk.

Once upon a time there was an embarrassed structure. It was all alone in the middle of a field. Every morning the structure wanted to spring, but it had never done it before. One day, it finally gathered all its courage and said "I'm going to spring!" It took a deep breath and jumped. Its jump was so high that it almost touched the sky. It was so excited that is was not embarrassed anymore. From then on, the structure loved to spring every day and it lived happily ever after!

Once upon a time, a little boy named Timmy went to the park with his mom. Timmy saw a big, juicy melon on the grass. He wanted to eat it, but his mom said they had to wait until they got home. 

Suddenly, a big dog came running towards them. Timmy was fearful and wanted to run away, but his mom told him to stay still. The dog came closer and closer, but then a man appeared and tied the dog to a tree. 

Timmy asked the man if he could have the melon, and the man said yes. Timmy was so happy and shared the melon with his mom. They sat on the grass and ate the melon while the dog watched them. Timmy wasn't afraid anymore because the dog was tied up.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play in the forest near her house. One day, she saw a big bear. The bear was very rude and growled at her. Lily was scared, but she remembered what her mommy told her. She said, "When you see a bear, you should yield and slowly walk away." So, Lily did just that. She yielded and walked away from the bear. 

After that, Lily was very careful when playing in the forest. She made sure to watch out for any rude animals. She also learned to yield when she saw them. Lily continued to play in the forest, but now she knew how to stay safe.

Once there was a little boy called Larry. Larry was only 3 years old and loved balancing things.

One day, Larry was playing in the kitchen. He saw a ticking sink and was determined to balance something on it. He quickly found an apple to balance on the sink.

"Look, I'm so clever, I can balance an apple!" said Larry proudly.

But Larry was too eager and soon lost his balance. The apple tipped off the sink and landed in the sink with a loud splash.

Larry was sad. He wanted to be grateful but he had made a big mess in the kitchen. What was he going to do?

Larry quickly ran away, leaving the mess in the sink. He was never seen in the kitchen again.

Sara and Tom were very happy. They were going to the festival with Mom and Dad. The festival had many things to see and do. There were balloons, games, music, and food.

Sara and Tom ran to the face painting booth. They wanted to have colorful designs on their cheeks. Sara chose a butterfly and Tom chose a tiger. The lady who painted their faces was very nice. She used a soft brush and some paint.

"Stay still, please," she said. "I will make you look very pretty and fierce."

Sara and Tom nodded. They felt the brush tickle their skin. They closed their eyes and smiled.

When the lady was done, she gave them a mirror. Sara and Tom looked at themselves. They were amazed. They had beautiful and scary faces.

"Wow, you are so good!" Sara said to the lady.

"Thank you, you are very sweet," the lady said.

"Can I rub your face?" Tom asked Sara.

"No, you can't!" Sara said. "You will ruin my butterfly!"

"Can I rub your face?" Sara asked Tom.

"No, you can't!" Tom said. "You will ruin my tiger!"

They laughed and hugged. They were very happy. They thanked the lady and ran to show Mom and Dad their faces. They were very enthusiastic. They wanted to see and do everything at the festival.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy had a big backyard with lots of trees and flowers. One day, Timmy saw an enormous bird in his backyard. He wanted to watch the bird, but it flew away. 

The next day, Timmy decided to peek through the bushes to see if the bird would come back. He waited and waited, and finally, the bird came back! Timmy was so happy to watch the bird for a long time. 

After that day, Timmy loved to peek through the bushes and watch the birds in his backyard. He saw many different kinds of birds, but the enormous bird was still his favorite. The end.

Lily and Tom were playing with their toy cars in the living room. They liked to make noises and pretend they were driving fast. Lily had a pink car and Tom had a blue car. They had fun racing each other and crashing into the sofa.

But then, Lily's car stopped moving. She tried to push it, but it did not go. She looked at the bottom and saw a small door. She opened it and saw a round thing inside. She took it out and showed it to Tom.

"What is this?" she asked.

"That is a battery," Tom said. "It makes your car go. Maybe it is empty. You need a new one."

"Where can I get a new one?" Lily asked.

Tom thought for a moment. He remembered that his dad had a box of batteries in his room. He had a big flashlight that used them. He had a plan.

"Come with me," he said. "I know where to find one."

He took Lily's hand and they ran to his dad's room. They opened the door and saw the box on the shelf. Tom climbed on a chair and reached for it. He opened it and took out a battery. He gave it to Lily and helped her put it in her car.

"There," he said. "Now your car will go again."

Lily smiled and turned on her car. It made a noise and moved. She was happy.

"Thank you, Tom," she said. "You are a good friend."

They hugged and ran back to the living room. They continued to play with their cars.

But they did not notice that something else had followed them. It was furry and had big ears and a long tail. It was Tom's dad's pet rabbit. It had escaped from its cage and was curious about the toys. It saw the box of batteries and decided to explore. It jumped on the shelf and knocked over the box. The batteries fell on the floor and rolled everywhere. The rabbit was scared and ran away.

Tom's dad heard the noise and came to see what was going on. He saw the mess and the rabbit hiding under the bed. He was not happy.

"Who did this?" he asked.

Lily and Tom looked at each other. They did not know what to say. They did not see the rabbit. They only saw the batteries.

They pointed at the batteries and said together:

"They did it!"

Tom and Sam are friends. They like to play with cars and balls. One day, they go to the park with their moms. There are many things to do in the park. They can slide, swing, climb, or run.

Tom says, "I want to slide. Sliding is fun. Come with me, Sam." Sam says, "No, I want to swing. Swinging is fun. You come with me, Tom." They do not agree. They choose different things.

Tom runs to the slide. He is careless. He does not look where he is going. He bumps into a girl. The girl falls down. She cries. Tom says, "Sorry, sorry. Are you okay?" The girl says, "No, you hurt me. You are bad." Tom feels sad. He says, "I did not mean to hurt you. I was not looking. I am sorry."

Sam runs to the swing. He is careless. He does not wait for his turn. He pushes a boy. The boy falls off the swing. He cries. Sam says, "Sorry, sorry. Are you okay?" The boy says, "No, you hurt me. You are bad." Sam feels sad. He says, "I did not mean to hurt you. I was in a hurry. I am sorry."

Their moms hear the cries. They come to see what is wrong. They see Tom and Sam with the girl and the boy. They are not happy. They say, "What did you do? Why did you hurt them? You were careless. You have to be careful. You have to say sorry and be nice."

Tom and Sam say sorry to the girl and the boy. They give them hugs. They say, "We are sorry. We were careless. We will be careful. We will be nice. Can we be friends?" The girl and the boy say, "Okay. We forgive you. We can be friends. Do you want to play with us?"

Tom and Sam are happy. They say, "Yes, we want to play with you. What do you want to play?" The girl says, "I want to climb. Climbing is fun. Come with me." The boy says, "I want to run. Running is fun. Come with me." They agree. They choose the same thing.

They all go to climb and run. They have fun. They are careful. They are nice. They are friends. Their moms are happy. They say, "That is good news. You are good friends. You are good kids." They smile. They are proud.

Once upon a time, there were two friends called Sam and Mia. Sam had a lucky number that he always kept in his pocket. 

One day when they were out having fun in the park, Sam said to Mia, "I have a plan to get a special prize. I have my lucky number in my pocket."

Mia was very curious. She asked, "What are you going to do with your lucky number?"

Sam replied, "There is a game at the fair next week. I am going to try and win the special prize with my lucky number!"

Mia was very impressed and nodded her head in agreement. She said, "Good luck with your plan, Sam. I hope your lucky number will help you win!"

The week had passed and the day of the fair arrived. Sam was so excited as he had found out his lucky number was the winning number.

He had won a special prize with his lucky number! Sam's plan had worked! 

Mia clapped in joy when Sam told her the news. She said, "Sam, that's wonderful! You are so lucky!" 

Sam smiled and replied, "Yes I am lucky! But I wouldn't have won without my plan and the luck of my lucky number."

"Yes! That's my spear, I found it yesterday. Do you want to play with it?"

Once there was a brown kid who was determined to succeed. He went up to his mom and said, "Mom, I want to succeed!" His mom smiled and said, "That's great! How can I help?" 
The brown kid thought for a bit, then replied, "I need to practice my numbers. Can you help me?" His mom gave him a big hug, and said, "Yes, I can help you." 
The brown kid sat down with his mom and she taught him how to say the numbers, one by one. After a few tries, the brown kid was able to count from 1 to 10, and he felt proud of himself.

The brown kid wanted to do even better. So every day after that he practiced counting to 30, and he started to get faster and faster. Eventually, the brown kid was able to count to 100 and he felt proud of his success. 

The brown kid smiled and said, "I did it! I succeeded!" His mom smiled and gave him a big hug, proud of her son.

Once upon a time, there was a little crab called Bobby. Bobby was very polite and always said please and thank you. One day Bobby was walking along the beach and found a beautiful bright shell. He thought it was so beautiful and he wanted to take it home with him.

Suddenly another crab came along and saw the shell. She said to Bobby: â€œThat shell looks very pretty! Can I please have it?â€ Bobby was so polite that he offered to give her the shell, but the second crab said: â€œNo, thatâ€™s ok. Why donâ€™t we share it? Letâ€™s each take turns with it.â€ Bobby thought this was a great idea and happily agreed.

Bobby and the second crab took turns with the shell. When it was Bobbyâ€™s turn he was always very polite and invited the other crab to have their turn first. Then it was the other crabâ€™s turn and she was also very polite and invited Bobby to have his turn first.

The moral of the story is that when we are polite, we can make friends and share things together.

Once upon a time there was a mighty hero named Bob. Bob loved to play. 
Every day, he put on his shiny helmet and went off to have an adventure. He was so brave that nobody ever dared to challenge him. 
One day, Bob went to a very far away place, and there he saw a magical spell. He was curious and decided to cast it, but little did he know it was a tricky one! Suddenly, Bob found himself flying high in the sky!

He was so brave and mighty that he didn't get scared. Instead, he laughed with joy and sang a happy song. 

After a while, the spell was gone and Bob came back, safe and sound. From then on, he put on his helmet whenever he wanted to play, reminding him of his magical adventure!

Lily and Ben were playing in the yard. They saw a big box under a tree. They ran to the box and opened it. Inside, they found many pretty things. There were dolls, cars, books, and hats.

"Wow, look at all these toys!" Lily said. "Can we play with them?"

"Sure, let's set them up and have fun!" Ben said. They took out the toys and set them on the grass. They made a tea party with the dolls, a race with the cars, a story with the books, and a fashion show with the hats.

They played for a long time, until they heard their mom calling them. "Lily, Ben, time for lunch!" Mom said.

"Okay, Mom, we're coming!" Lily and Ben said. They put the toys back in the box and closed it. They thanked the box for the pretty things and ran to the house.

"Did you have fun, kids?" Mom asked.

"Yes, Mom, we found a magic box with lots of pretty toys!" Lily and Ben said.

"A magic box? That sounds wonderful!" Mom said. She smiled and gave them a hug. She wondered who left the box under the tree.

The thin boy was always looking for an escape. He looked out the window and saw the changing season. The days were getting colder, so he knew he had to move quickly. He opened the door and started running. He ran faster and faster, until he felt the wind in his face. He was free! He didn't know where he was going, but he just wanted to keep running. He passed by trees and fields until he was so far away he couldn't remember where he had come from. He was feeling brave and happy as he stood in the middle of the tall grass. He knew his escape was complete.

Once upon a time, there was a big furry inchworm. He was a bit small, but he had big plans. He wanted to load up the biggest mountains in the land.

One day, the inchworm woke up feeling brave. He even told himself he was strong. He prompted himself by saying, "you can load the biggest mountain in the land!"

And so he started his journey. He crawled through the fields, over stones and twigs, until he came to a big mountain. He rested for a moment, and then he got to work. He loaded and loaded the mountain with dirt.

Finally, after many days of hard work, he made it to the top. He was so proud of himself he even smiled! He had loaded the biggest mountain in the land!

One day, Dad and Mom took their three-year-old son, Tim, to the hospital. He had been sick for a few days and Mom wanted to make sure Tim was feeling better. As they drove to the hospital, Dad told Tim that he was going to be OK.

Tim was nervous, but he was also excited to go to the hospital. He had never been before. Dad let Tim look out of the window to help pass the time.

When they arrived, the hospital looked very peaceful. Dad let Tim look around. Then they went inside and Dad showed Tim the nurses who were taking care of other children.

Mom and Dad let Tim sit with them in the waiting room. While they waited, Mom read stories to Tim. They also shared some snacks and talked about what they would do when they all left the hospital. 

Dad and Mom wanted Tim to be happy and peaceful. Thankfully, after a few more tests, the doctor said that Tim was healthy and could go home! Tim was so happy and relieved. Dad and Mom were happy too. 

They hugged Tim and thanked the doctor. Then Tim, Dad and Mom went home to rest.

Once upon a time, there was a mommy who had a new baby. The baby was very small and couldn't walk or talk yet. One day, the mommy was making soup for dinner. She left the soup on the stove and went to check on the baby. 

The baby was sleeping, but the mommy heard a loud noise from the kitchen. She ran to the kitchen and saw that the soup was boiling over! The mommy quickly turned off the stove and tried to fix the soup. 

But the soup was too hot and the mommy couldn't fix it. She was worried that the soup would burn the baby if she tried to feed it to him. So, the mommy had an idea. She put the soup outside to cool down and made a new batch of soup for dinner. 

Later that night, the mommy fed the baby the new soup and he loved it! The mommy was happy that she could fix the problem and keep the baby safe. From then on, the mommy always made sure to watch the stove and keep the baby away from hot things.

John was feeling very glad. He had a basket of apples and he wanted to rub them to make them shiny. He put one in his hand and started to rub it.

John's mum saw him and said, "John, what are you doing?"
John replied, "I'm rubbing this apple to make it shiny."
Mum said, "That's great John. You did a nice job."

John kept rubbing the apple. When he was finished, he put it back in the basket and grabbed another one. He was glad that he was making all the apples shiny.

He worked and worked until the basket was full of shiny apples. He was so proud of his work. Mum came back and said, "John, look at all the apples and how shiny they look! You did a great job!"

John was very glad. He knew that his basket of apples looked the best!

Sara and Ben are playing a game with cards. They have to match the cards with the same number or picture. Sara has a card with a big zero on it. She looks for another card with a zero, but she cannot find one.

"Where is the other zero?" Sara asks Ben. "Did you hide it?"

Ben shakes his head. "No, I did not hide it. Maybe it is under the pile."

Sara and Ben lift the pile of cards and look under it. They see the other card with a zero. It is stuck to the table with some sticky tape.

"Who did this?" Sara says. "This is not fair!"

Ben laughs. "It was me. I wanted to trick you. It was a joke."

Sara is not happy. She feels angry and sad. She does not like Ben's joke. She thinks it is mean.

"That is not a joke. That is cheating. You are a bad friend. I do not want to play with you anymore." Sara says. She takes her cards and runs away.

Ben feels sorry. He did not mean to hurt Sara. He wanted to make her laugh. He likes Sara. He wants to be her friend.

"Wait, Sara. Come back. I am sorry. Please forgive me." Ben says. He runs after Sara and tries to catch her.

Sara and Ben run around the room. They bump into the table and knock down the cards. They trip over the rug and fall on the floor. They look at each other and start to giggle.

They realize that running and falling was fun. They forget about the zero card and the sticky tape. They are not angry and sad anymore. They are happy and silly.

They hug each other and say sorry. They are friends again. They pick up the cards and start a new game. They match the cards with the same number or picture. They cheer and applaud when they find a pair. They play and laugh until it is time for a snack. They share a cookie and a glass of milk. They are glad they have each other. They are the best friends.

Once upon a time, there was a small boy named Tim. Tim was a good boy, but he had a bad habit. He did not like to clean his room. His room was always filthy. His toys were all over the floor.

One day, it was Tim's birthday. He was so happy because he would receive a big gift. His mom and dad told him, "Tim, if you want your gift, you must clean your room first." Tim didn't want to do it, but he wanted his gift, so he started to clean.

It took a long time, but Tim cleaned his whole room. When he was done, his mom and dad gave him the gift. It was a big toy car! Tim loved it. He played with it all year. He learned that if he kept his room clean, he could find his toys easily and have more fun. The moral of the story is: A clean room makes for a happy life.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and explore the world around her. One day, she saw an elderly lady struggling to carry her groceries. Lily wanted to help, but she didn't know the way.

Later that day, Lily's mom explained to her that sometimes people need help, especially when they're old. She showed Lily the way to be kind and helpful to others.

The next day, Lily saw the same elderly lady struggling again. This time, Lily knew the way and helped her carry her groceries. The lady was very grateful and thanked Lily for her kindness. 

From that day on, Lily always looked for ways to help others. She learned that being kind and helpful was the right way to be.

Once upon a time there was a clumsy bear. He was walking through the forest and he stumbled upon a gym. He was so excited! He wanted to go inside, but the door was locked. He knocked on the door and shouted "Let me in!"

Suddenly, a badger appeared at the door. He said to the bear, "Why do you want to enter?" The bear said, "I want to have a workout and have some fun." The badger said, "I'm sorry, but the gym is going to rot and you cannot come in." 

The clumsy bear was so worried. He mumbled to himself, "Now I'll never be able to have fun at the gym again." 

The next day, the bear looked for the gym but it was gone. The gym had rotted and there was nothing left.

The clumsy bear had no more fun at the gym ever again.

Once upon a time, there was a black armchair in a room. Every day, a little boy called Jack would love to shoot his toy cars on the armchair. He would make the loudest whoosh sound pretending they were racing cars.

One day, Jack saw something on the armchair. It was a black bug! He was so scared that he quickly grabbed his toy gun and started shooting at the bug! He was shooting and shooting until the bug was gone.

Jack was very proud of himself and he shouted, "I did it! I am so brave!"

The End.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy. He was very curious and liked to explore things. He was always looking for adventure.

One day, he went to his kitchen. He stood in front of the giant white box. It was the freezer! It was open and he looked inside. He saw some funny shapes in the ice. He wanted to touch them but he wasn't sure if he should. He became very confused.

Suddenly, the door to the freezer started to close. The little boy was scared and tried to open the door, but it wouldn't move. He was stuck in the freezer!

The little boy started to scream as loud as he could. Thankfully, his mama heard him. She quickly opened the door and the little boy was free! He was very happy and hugged his mama. He knew that she would always help him.

The long worm was crawling through the grass. It was looking for food and decided to go underneath the rock. Suddenly, it was disturbed by a loud noise. The noise had come from the sky, above the rock.
The worm was frightened and stopped moving. It tried to take cover under the rock but the noise was too loud. Then, the noise stopped and the worm was relieved. It slowly came out from under the rock and started looking for food again.
Soon it found some delicious leaves and began to eat. Undisturbed by the noise, the worm had a satisfying meal and then crawled away, back into the grass.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside and look at the cows. One day, she saw a big cow and said, "Hello, cow! You are so big and pretty." The cow said, "Moo!" and Lily giggled.

Lily's mom came outside and said, "Lily, it's time for lunch. Let's go inside and eat." Lily said, "Okay, but can we test the food first? I want to make sure it's tasty." Her mom smiled and said, "Of course, let's test it together."

When they got inside, Lily's little brother Jack was already eating. He said, "This food is yucky! I don't want to eat it." Lily's mom said, "Jack, you need to try it first before you say it's yucky. Let's all test it together." They all took a bite and Lily said, "Mmm, it's tasty!" Jack tried it again and said, "You're right, it's not yucky. It's tasty!"

From that day on, Lily and Jack always tested their food before saying if they liked it or not. And every time they saw the cow outside, they would say hello and the cow would say "Moo!" back.

One day, Johnny was very excited. He got a box with lots of colors inside. He took a brush and started to paint. Johnny painted a big zigzag in yellow and red. He was so proud of his painting.

Johnny was so happy and he wanted to show his painting to his mom. He ran to the kitchen, but she was busy cooking dinner. So, he ran to the living room to show his dad. But he was watching TV.

Johnny was a bit ashamed, but he continued to show his painting to the others that were in the house. His little sister showed lots of interest and smiled so BIG, that it made Johnny happy. He proudly showed her all the colors and the big zigzag. 

When dinner was ready, Johnny was still playing with colors and painting. His mom was so happy to see how much he was enjoying himself. She told him to clean up now before dinner. Johnny was a bit sad, but he said goodbye to all those colors and put them away in the box.

Mia and Toby were best friends. Today, Mia was feeling lucky. She had a special surprise to share with Toby. She showed Toby her new piano. Toby was so delighted, that he jumped up and down! Mia and Toby spent the whole day playing the piano and singing. They loved making music together. Mia was so glad that she could share her surprise with her best friend. Toby was the luckiest boy ever!

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play with a ball. They pass the ball to each other and laugh. They are good at passing the ball.

One day, a new girl comes to the park. Her name is Lily. She has a big smile and a red dress. She asks Anna and Ben if she can play with them. Anna and Ben say yes. They pass the ball to Lily and she passes it back. They have fun together.

Lily says, "You are very nice. I like you. Can I be your friend?" Anna and Ben say, "Of course. You are very nice too. We like you. You can be our friend." They hug Lily and say, "We are friends. We share our ball and our love." Lily hugs them back and says, "Thank you. You make me happy. I love you too." They are happy. They are good friends.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Sam and Izzy. Sam was a brave pirate and Izzy was a mysterious wizard. Sam and Izzy were best buddies, so when Sam demanded that Izzy help him to find a hidden treasure, Izzy agreed.

They set off on their adventure and searched all day. They looked inside caves and climbed trees, but they couldn't find the treasure.

Finally they reached a mysterious island. It was full of beautiful flowers and friendly animals.

As they explored the island, Sam suddenly demanded that Izzy used his magical powers to find the hidden treasure. Izzy nodded and used his wand to make a score appear in the sky.

The score drifted across the night sky, leading Sam and Izzy to the hidden treasure. As the friends cheered with excitement, they shared the treasure between them and went home with a huge smile on their faces.

Once upon a time there was a mighty bear. He was mighty brave and mighty strong. One day, he wanted to take a swim in the sink. He jumped in, but there was one problem: the sink was too small and the bear split it in half! 

The bear was very shocked and said, "Oh no, what happened? I didn't mean to split the sink."

Suddenly, a little mouse came out of the crack and said, "Don't worry bear, I have a plan. Let's get a bigger and better sink and use the old one to put in the garden. That way, you can enjoy a mighty big swim!"

The bear smiled. Together, he and the mouse got a new, more spacious sink and together they put the old sink in the garden. From then on, the bear had a wonderful place to take a mighty swim without splitting anything!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He went to the beach with his mommy and daddy. The beach was very big and had lots of sand.

Timmy saw a new friend playing in the sand. His name was Billy. Timmy's mommy and daddy introduced him to Billy. Billy was very charming and had a big smile.

Timmy and Billy played in the sand and built a big castle together. They had so much fun and became good friends. Timmy was happy that his mommy and daddy introduced him to Billy. They all had a great day at the beach.

Once upon a time, there was a pillow. Just like all other pillows, it was soft and fluffy. Every night it would be used by a little girl. She would take it to bed, hug it, and soon fall asleep. 

One night something strange happened. She woke up and saw something that scared her. It was a big, dark cloud standing next to her bed. She screamed and quickly ran to her mom.

Her mom comforted her and said, "Don't worry. It's just a dream. It's not real." Then she picked up the pillow and handed it to the little girl. The girl hugged the pillow with relief and soon felt safe again. She thanked her mom for being so fair. 

The little girl learned that night that sometimes scary things can seem real, but in the end, her mom was always there to take care of her. And the pillow was there to comfort her when she was afraid.

One day, a little girl named Amy was out on an adventure. She had brought her wagon with her and was on her way to the ancient temple. As she approached the temple, she noticed a big pile of stones and rocks on the path.

Amy stopped and said to herself, "I need to sort this mess out and make a path, or I'll never make it to the temple!" She got to work and started moving the rocks around.

After a few minutes, she had moved the stones to the side and made a path. Just then her wagon got stuck in the mud. She said, "What now?! How am I going to fix this?!"

Suddenly, a voice said, "Hello there. Let me help you out." Amy looked up and saw an old man. He said, "I can help you get your wagon out of the mud. It won't take long!"

The old man grabbed the wagon's handle and gave it a tug. The wagon came out of the mud with a big splash. Amy thanked him and said, "You're a real helper!" The old man smiled and said, "Just doing my part to keep the ancient temple safe."

Once upon a time, there was a little fish named Nemo. Nemo loved to swim in the ocean with his friends. One day, Nemo's friend Dory got lost in the ocean. Nemo wanted to help Dory, but he didn't know what to do. 

Suddenly, Nemo saw a big, red mailbox on the beach. He had an idea! Nemo swam to the mailbox and put a note inside. The note said, "Help! Dory is lost in the ocean. Please come and find her." 

The next day, a kind fish named Marlin saw the note in the mailbox. He was very alert and knew he had to help. Marlin found Dory and brought her back to Nemo. Nemo was so happy that he learned that it's important to ask for help when you need it.

Lily liked to observe things. She liked to look at the sky, the trees, the birds, and the bugs. She liked to learn new words and how to spell them. She had a book with pictures and letters that her mom read to her every night.

One day, Lily saw a big spider on the wall. She was frightened. She did not like spiders. They had too many legs and eyes. She ran to her mom and told her what she saw. Her mom came with a cup and a paper and caught the spider. She showed it to Lily and said, "This is a spider. It is not scary. It is just a bug. Can you spell spider?"

Lily looked at the spider in the cup. She saw that it was not moving or biting. She felt a little brave. She said, "S-P-I-D-E-R. Spider." Her mom smiled and said, "Very good, Lily. You are a smart girl. Do you want to observe the spider some more, or do you want me to let it go outside?"

Lily thought for a moment. She decided that she wanted to observe the spider some more. She said, "Can I hold the cup?" Her mom gave her the cup and said, "Be gentle and careful. The spider is a living thing. It does not want to be hurt." Lily nodded and held the cup. She looked at the spider and said, "Hello, spider. I am Lily. You are not scary. You are just a bug. I can spell your name. S-P-I-D-E-R. Spider."

The spider did not say anything. It just crawled around the cup. Lily felt curious and happy. She observed the spider until it was time for dinner. Then she said, "Bye, spider. Thank you for letting me observe you. You can go outside now." Her mom took the cup and the paper and let the spider go outside. Lily waved and said, "Have a good night, spider. Maybe I will see you again."

Mira was a good and obedient girl. She always listened to her mom and dad and did what they said. She liked to play with her dolls, read her books and draw with her crayons. She was happy and healthy.

But one day, Mira felt very sick. She had a fever and a sore throat. She could not eat or drink or smile. Her mom and dad were worried. They took her to the hospital. The hospital was a big and white place with many people and machines. Mira was scared. She did not like the hospital.

A nice doctor came to see Mira. He wore a blue coat and a mask. He checked her ears, her nose, her mouth and her chest. He said, "Mira, you have a bad infection. You need to take some medicine and stay here for a few days. The medicine will make you feel better. Don't worry, your mom and dad will be with you."

Mira nodded. She was a good and obedient girl. She took the medicine and stayed in the hospital. She missed her home and her toys, but she knew she had to get well. The doctor and the nurses were kind to her. They gave her stickers and books and puzzles. They made her laugh and feel less scared.

After a few days, Mira felt much better. Her fever was gone and her throat was not sore. She could eat and drink and smile again. The doctor said, "Mira, you are a brave and strong girl. You are ready to go home. You are well again."

Mira was so happy. She hugged her mom and dad and thanked the doctor and the nurses. She said, "Bye bye, hospital. Thank you for helping me." She went home with her mom and dad. They had a big cake and balloons and presents. They celebrated Mira's recovery. Mira was happy and healthy again. She played with her dolls, read her books and drew with her crayons. She was a good and obedient girl.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Sarah. She was only three years old and loved to explore her world. One day, Sarah noticed a small bell on a table. It was shiny and sparkly in the sunlight. She was very curious and wanted to try it out. 

Sarah picked up the bell and shook it, but nothing happened. She tried ringing it, but still, nothing happened. She was getting worried that it was broken and started to cry. 

Suddenly, a local shopkeeper noticed her distress and came to help. He asked Sarah to try ringing the bell one more time. This time, the bell made a beautiful noise! Sarah was so happy that it worked, and the shopkeeper was delighted too. 

The shopkeeper was very kind and said to Sarah to never be ignorant, because with patience and care, things can always work out in the end. Sarah said goodbye to the shopkeeper and went on her way, bells ringing in her ears.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside with her bucket. One day, her bucket was not available because her mom was using it to clean the house. Lily was sad because she couldn't play with her bucket. 

Later that day, Lily's mom gave her the bucket. Lily was so happy and she ran outside to play. She filled her bucket with pretty flowers and carried it carefully. Suddenly, she tripped and dropped the bucket. The flowers fell out and Lily was sad again. 

But then, her mom came outside and helped her pick up the flowers. Lily felt better and they put the flowers back in the bucket. They went inside and put the bucket on the table. Lily was happy because her bucket was available again. The end.

Tim and Lily were playing in the park with their ball. They liked to kick the ball to each other and run after it. Sometimes they missed the ball and it rolled away. Then they had to chase it before it got lost.

One time, the ball went too far and rolled down the hill. Tim and Lily ran after it, but they were too slow. The ball crossed the road and went into the yard of the big green church. The church had a tall tower and a big door. Tim and Lily had never been inside the church before.

"Let's go get the ball," Tim said.

"But we can't go inside the church," Lily said. "It's not our church. Maybe someone will be angry."

Tim looked around. He did not see anyone in the yard or on the road. He thought it was safe to go inside the church. He wanted his ball back.

"Come on, Lily," he said. "It will be quick. We'll just dive in and dive out."

He grabbed Lily's hand and ran towards the big door. He pushed it open and they went inside the church. It was dark and quiet. They saw many seats and a big cross. They also saw their ball. It was lying on the floor near the front of the church.

"Look, there's our ball!" Tim said. He let go of Lily's hand and ran towards the ball. He picked it up and smiled.

"Let's go, Tim," Lily said. She was scared. She did not like the dark and quiet church. She wanted to go back to the park.

But before they could leave, they heard a loud voice.

"Who are you? What are you doing here?" the voice said.

Tim and Lily turned around. They saw a man standing at the back of the church. He was wearing a black robe and a white collar. He looked angry.

Tim and Lily were very scared. They dropped the ball and ran towards the door. They did not say anything. They just wanted to get away.

They dove out of the church and ran across the road. They did not stop until they reached the park. They were out of breath and their hearts were beating fast.

"That was scary," Tim said.

"Let's never go inside the church again," Lily said.

They hugged each other and went back to playing with their ball. They hoped the man in the black robe would not follow them. They hoped he would not be angry. They hoped he would forgive them.

Once upon a time there were two sisters named Molly and Penny. Molly was the oldest, and she was very wise beyond her years. 

One day, Molly wanted to teach Penny a lesson about being kind, so she asked Penny if she wanted to marry a smooth stone. Penny thought this sounded like a strange idea, but wanted to be nice to her big sister, so she agreed. 

Molly took a smooth stone from the ground and held it in both hands. She told Penny to place her hands together over the top of the stone and say a special phrase. When Penny repeated the phrase, the stone became joined to her hands, just like a ring when two people get married. 

Penny smiled, feeling excited, and thanked Molly. Then Molly said, â€œThe lesson here is that when we are kind and understanding to one another, and treat each other with love and respect, then our bond will become even stronger and our relationship will be smooth like this stone.â€ 

Molly and Penny smiled happily and hugged each other tightly. From then on, they both remembered that no matter what, they would always have each otherâ€™s backs and show love and kindness.

Once upon a time there was a weak temple. The temple seemed to be fading away and everyone was worried. 
One day, a brave traveller came to the town and saw the temple. He knew he had to bring it back to life. So he went to the poorest people in the area and asked for their help. 
Together they went to the temple and brought it back to life. Everyone was amazed at how strong the temple was now. They thanked the brave traveller for bringing the temple back and celebrate. 

The end!

Lily hated her desk. It was too big and too hard and too boring. She wanted to play with her toys or draw with her crayons, but her mom said she had to do her homework. Lily did not like homework. It was too hard and too boring and too long.

One day, Lily saw a new desk in the store. It was small and soft and colorful. It had stickers and glitter and a lamp. Lily loved the new desk. She asked her mom if she could have it. Her mom said no. She said the new desk was too expensive and too messy and too silly. Lily was angry. She said the new desk was attractive and fun and smart.

Lily and her mom argued. Lily said she hated her old desk and she wanted the new one. Her mom said she had to be grateful for what she had and she did not need the new one. Lily cried. She said her mom was mean and unfair and did not love her. Her mom sighed. She said she loved Lily very much and she wanted her to be happy, but she also wanted her to be responsible and sensible.

Lily and her mom hugged. Lily said she was sorry for being rude and mean. Her mom said she was sorry for being harsh and strict. They agreed to compromise. Lily could keep her old desk, but she could decorate it with some stickers and glitter. Her mom could buy her a new lamp, but she had to do her homework. Lily smiled. She said she liked her desk a little bit more. Her mom smiled. She said she was proud of Lily for being mature and kind. They went home and had a nice dinner.

One day, there was a team of animals. They were all friends and they loved to play together. One of the animals was a big elephant. He was amazing because he could do tricks with his trunk. 

One day, the elephant wanted to show his friends how he could lean on one leg. He lifted his other leg up and leaned to the side. His friends were amazed! They had never seen an elephant do that before. 

The other animals on the team wanted to try leaning too. They all took turns leaning to the side and trying to balance on one leg. It was so much fun! The team of animals had a great day playing and trying new things together.

Sara and Ben are twins. They like to play outside in the field. The field has many flowers and trees and bugs. Sara and Ben have a game. They hide behind the trees and try to find each other. They call it hide and seek.

One day, Sara and Ben go to the field to play hide and seek. Sara says, "I will hide first. You count to ten and then look for me." Ben says, "OK." Sara runs behind a big tree. She thinks it is a good hiding spot. Ben counts to ten and then says, "Ready or not, here I come!"

Ben looks around the field. He does not see Sara. He walks to the tree where Sara is hiding. He says, "Sara, I found you!" But Sara does not answer. She stays quiet. She thinks Ben will go away and look somewhere else. Ben says, "Sara, I know you are here. Come out!" But Sara does not come out. She thinks it is fun to make Ben look for her more.

Ben gets angry. He says, "Sara, this is not fair. You are not playing right. You have to come out when I find you. That is the rule." But Sara does not listen. She thinks Ben is silly. She says, "No, you did not find me. I am hidden. You have to look harder."

Ben starts to cry. He says, "Sara, you are mean. You are not a good sister. You are not a good friend. You make me sad. I don't want to play with you anymore." He runs away from the tree. He goes to the other side of the field. He sits on the ground and cries.

Sara hears Ben cry. She feels bad. She says, "Ben, I am sorry. I was just joking. I did not mean to make you sad. Please come back. I want to play with you. You are a good brother. You are a good friend." She comes out from behind the tree. She runs to Ben. She hugs him and says, "I love you, Ben. Can we play again?"

Ben stops crying. He looks at Sara. He says, "I love you, too, Sara. Yes, we can play again. But you have to follow the rule. You have to come out when I find you. OK?" Sara says, "OK. I will follow the rule. I will not complain. You can hide first. I will count to ten and then look for you." Ben says, "OK. Thank you, Sara. You are a good sister. You are a good friend." He runs behind a small tree. He thinks it is a good hiding spot. Sara counts to ten and then says, "Ready or not, here I come!" They play hide and seek and have fun. They are happy.

Lily and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big hole in the ground. It is deep and dark.

"Wow, look at that hole!" Ben says. "I wonder what is inside."

"Maybe it is a secret tunnel," Lily says. "Or a cave with treasure."

"Let's go and see," Ben says. He runs to the hole.

"Wait, Ben!" Lily says. "It might be dangerous. What if you fall in?"

Ben stops at the edge of the hole. He looks down. He cannot see anything.

"It is okay, Lily," he says. "I will be careful. I will hold on to this branch."

He points to a branch that sticks out of the hole.

Lily is scared. She does not want Ben to go in the hole. She thinks it is too deep and too dark.

"Please, Ben, don't go," she says. "Let's play something else. Let's go on the swings or the slide."

Ben looks at Lily. He sees that she is worried. He does not want to make her sad.

He nods his head. He says, "Okay, Lily, you are right. The hole is too deep and too dark. Let's play something else."

He walks away from the hole. He takes Lily's hand. They go to the swings and the slide. They have fun.

They are happy. They are good friends.

Once upon a time, there was a pear that glowed. It was big and round, and glowed very brightly in the night. It was so special and expensive that all the animals gathered to look at it.

The rabbit was mesmerized by the glowing pear. He hopped closer and closer until he was face to face with it. His whiskers twitched with excitement.

The bear was so jealous. He wanted the glowing pear all for himself. He reached out with his giant paw to take it.

But the pear kept glowing and wouldn't let the bear take it. He kept trying, but he just couldn't get it. So he gave up, and all the animals went home.

The glowing pear is still there to this day. It is still very special and expensive.

Once upon a time there was a little boy who wanted a new toy. He asked his parents for a toy and his daddy said he had one for him. The little boy was so excited! He wanted to see his new toy.

They drove for a long time. Finally, they arrived at a big park. The little boy saw a tall statue and he said, "That's my toy!" His daddy laughed and said, "No, that's not your toy. Come, we'll find one."

They looked around and they found a spoiled toy. It was old and damaged, but the little boy loved it! His daddy said he could have it. He hugged the toy and said, "Thank you daddy!"

They drove home, and the little boy had his new toy with him. He was so happy and enjoyed playing with it all day long. The end.

Once upon a time there was a thin eye. Every day it looked around and observed the world. One day while it was observing, it saw a bird high in the sky. The bird had colourful feathers and the eye watched it in amazement.

Then the eye noticed something else â€“ a big and scary snake! It was slithering across the green grass and the eye was scared. But then it saw that the snake had gone away. The eye felt calm again and kept observing.

Soon the eye spotted a bright, shiny sun high in the sky. It was so beautiful! The eye watched it for a long time until it went to sleep. When it woke up, the sun was still there in the sky.

The eye had a lot of fun observing.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a big sister named Emily who liked to act silly. One day, Emily put on an ugly hat and pretended to be a silly monster. Lily laughed and covered her eyes with her hands. 

Emily asked, "Why are you covering your eyes, Lily?" 

Lily said, "Your hat is ugly and it hurts my eyes." 

Emily took off the hat and said sorry. She knew it was important to be kind and not hurt others' eyes. From then on, they played together without any ugly hats or silly monsters.

One day, a small boy and his mom were walking around the park when they saw a big tree. The boy wanted to throw something at the tree, so his mom gave him a wet rock. The boy was so excited that he threw the wet rock very hard. But when the rock hit the tree, the tree started to shake and then it fell over. Everyone in the park was so scared. The boy felt so sad because he caused the bad thing to happen. His mom was very mad at him and they had to go home. The boy never threw anything at a tree ever again.

Once there was a farmyard. In the farmyard lived a powerful rooster. Every morning, the rooster would rise up early to crow and announce the start of the day.

One day, a fox came to visit the farmyard. The fox told the rooster he had a secret truth. But the fox only wanted to tell the rooster if he agreed to not crow in the morning anymore.

The rooster thought and thought, "What should I do? It's always been my job to crow in the morning." Then the rooster said, "No thank you. I will not give up my job. Even if I don't hear the secret truth, I know it's more important to be true to yourself than to give up who you are."

The fox agreed and left the farmyard. The next morning the rooster rose up early and crowed, louder than ever before!

The moral of the story is that it is important to be true to yourself, and there is power in standing up for what you believe.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Bettie. She was very excited today because she was going to take a ride on a boat. As she got closer to the boat, she saw her friends already on board. They waved to her, and Bettie waved back with a smile on her face.

Once upon a time, there was a big rock. The rock had a message on it. The message was very sorry. The rock wanted to tell everyone the message, but it could not move.

One day, a little bird came to the rock. The bird saw the message and felt sad. The bird wanted to help the rock. So the bird flew away to find someone who could help the rock.

The bird found a kind girl. The girl came to the rock and read the message. She felt sorry too. The girl told everyone about the rock's message. The people came to the rock and read the message. They all felt sorry and wanted to help. They all became friends with the rock and the bird. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved going to the beach and swimming in the ocean. One day, she saw a dolphin jumping out of the water. Lily thought it was so cool!

Later that day, Lily's mom gave her a box of chocolates. Lily opened the box and tried one. It was bitter! She didn't like it very much.

The next day, Lily went back to the beach. She saw the dolphin again and remembered the bitter chocolate. She wondered if the dolphin liked bitter things too. Suddenly, the dolphin swam up to her and opened its mouth. Inside, Lily saw something shiny. It was a treasure! The dolphin had found it and wanted to share it with her. From that day on, Lily and the dolphin were the best of friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had many toys, but they were always in a big pile and hard to find. One day, Lily decided to organize her toys. She put all her dolls together and all her cars together. She even put her blocks in a neat stack. 

Lily's mom was so happy to see her daughter's toys all organized. She gave Lily a big hug and said, "You did a great job, sweetie!" 

Lily was so proud of herself. She decided to organize her clothes too. She put all her shirts in one pile and all her pants in another. She even hung up her dresses on hangers to make them look nice and clear. 

Lily's mom was so impressed with how well she organized her clothes. She said, "You look like a little princess in your pretty uniform!" Lily smiled and felt very happy. From that day on, Lily always kept her toys and clothes organized and clear.

Once upon a time there was a girl. She was very impatient. She wanted to write something, but she didn't have a pen. The girl saw a stick! She was so excited. She thought "This stick will do". Once there was a little girl named Jane. She was so excited because it was her birthday. She liked birthdays because it was a special day when everyone came to celebrate with her. 

When Jane woke up that morning, her mom had a special surprise. She gave Jane a special toy with a good battery. Jane was so happy and excited and hugged her mom. She knew it was going to be a good day.

Then all of Jane's family and friends came to celebrate. They all played games, ate cake and laughed together. Jane couldn't believe how many gifts she got. She was so happy.

At the end of the day, Jane and her family said goodbye and hugged each other. Jane thanked them all for coming to celebrate her special day. 

Jane went to bed feeling very happy and thankful. She said a silent thank you and smiled. She knew that today was a really good day.

Once there was a boy who loved tanks. He found a rare tank one day and it made him very excited. It was so exciting he couldn't wait to show it to his mom and dad. Once upon a time there was a little girl who loved to do lots of things. One day she wanted to play with her toys but she heard a loud rumbling. The little girl was scared and asked her mum, "what's happening?". Her mum said, "it's an earthquake sweetheart". The little girl was scared and started to cry. 

The ground started shaking and the little girl grabbed her mum's hand. The quake was getting worse, she needed help. Suddenly the little girl saw a big brown wall in front of her. She wanted to get away but she had no way out. 

The little girl was very scared, she didn't know what to do. But it was too late, the wall started to fall on top of her. She screamed and screamed until she was no more.

The little girl had no chance to escape the brown wall which crumbled due to the earthquake. She needed help but it was too late.

Anna and Ben are twins. They like to play together, but sometimes they are naughty. One day, they want to dress up like pirates. They find some old clothes and hats in the closet. They also find some scissors and glue.

"Let's cut the clothes and make them look like pirate clothes!" says Ben.

"OK, but don't cut too much. Mom will be angry," says Anna.

They start to cut and glue the clothes. They make holes and patches and stripes. They also cut the hats and glue some feathers. They think they look like real pirates.

But they do not hear Mom coming home. She opens the door and sees the mess. She sees the clothes and the scissors and the glue. She sees Anna and Ben in their pirate outfits.

"What have you done?" she asks. "You have ruined the clothes! You have been very naughty!"

Anna and Ben feel sorry. They did not mean to make Mom angry. They did not think about the clothes. They only wanted to have fun.

"Mom, we are sorry. We wanted to dress up like pirates. We did not worry about the clothes. Please don't be mad," says Anna.

Mom sighs. She is not happy, but she loves Anna and Ben. She knows they are good kids, but they need to learn.

"I love you, but you have to be careful. You have to ask before you use things. You have to respect the clothes. They are not toys. You have to help me clean up this mess. And you have to say sorry to Dad. Some of these clothes are his," she says.

Anna and Ben nod. They hug Mom and say sorry. They help her clean up the mess. They also say sorry to Dad when he comes home. They promise to be good and not be naughty again.

Mom and Dad forgive them. They know they are still learning. They also think they look cute in their pirate outfits. They take a picture of them and smile. They love their twins.

Once upon a time, there lived a famous fireman. No fire was too big for him to put out. He was known to everyone in his town, and everyone knew and respected him.

One day, something disturbing happened. A fire had started outside the city, and it was quickly getting bigger and bigger. The fireman was quick to rush to the scene. He worked hard to put out the flames, but it seemed like it was too much for him - the fire was just too big!

But then, his friends came to help. Working together, the fireman and his friends put out the fire. Everyone was very proud of him. They all learned a very important lesson that day - when something disturbs us, we must never give up, but ask our friends and family for help.

Once upon a time, a bear was walking through the forest alone. He was feeling lonely and decided to look for his friends. Suddenly, he saw a rabbit near a tree. The bear asked the rabbit where his friends were.

Once upon a time, there was a big blue ocean. The ocean was so big that you couldn't see where it ended. One day, a little girl went to the ocean to play. Once upon a time, there was a girl called Mary. Mary was very rich and very happy. She had lots of nice things, but sometimes she was sad because she was ill.

One day, Mary's mom said to her, "We need to go to the doctor and get you some medicine, Mary." Mary was scared but nodded her head. 

At the doctor's, Mary was given some medicine. She didn't like it very much because it tasted bad. But, the doctor said it was very important to take the medicine so she did. 

When she got home, Mary's mom hugged her and said, "See, dear? I told you the medicine would make you feel better."

Tommy was watching a video on the television. He smiled excitedly as his favourite TV show began.

Suddenly, a famous cartoon character appeared on the screen! He was giant, colourful and full of life. His voice boomed around the room and he said, "I have a special surprise for you, Tommy!"

The cartoon character smiled. "That's right, Tommy," he said with a wink. "You've gained a friend who will be with you forever."

Once there was a little girl named Janie. She went to the park to play on a sunny day. As Janie ran around, she heard a strange noise. It was someone whistling!

Janie looked around and spotted an old vendor at the end of the park. He had a very delicate cart filled with interesting things. Janie was very curious, so she ran closer to the vendor.
