Henry was very busy. He needed to manage his desk so he had enough room to work. Every day he moved flowers, pens, pencils and paper around on his desk. He liked to keep things neat and tidy. One day, he even stuck a sticker on the front of his desk to remind him to be organised.

As Henry got busier, he realised he had to manage his desk more carefully. He found a box and put all of his things inside it. Then he put the box on a shelf where he could reach it easily.

At the end of the day, Henry was happy with how he had managed his desk. He was so glad he had enough space for all his things. Now he could be busy without feeling cluttered.

Once there was a boy who loved to play. He had a special toy that could shoot. Every day the boy would go outside and shoot his toy. He had so much fun that he would play all day long!

The boy just kept shooting and shooting until it was time to go inside. He was so happy with his new seat, he had so much fun that day!

Lily liked to wander in the park with her mom. She saw many things that made her happy: flowers, birds, dogs, and swings. But her favorite thing was the pony. The pony was brown and soft, and it let Lily pet its nose and mane.

One day, Lily and her mom went to the park, and Lily ran to the pony. She said hello and gave it a carrot. The pony ate the carrot and nuzzled Lily's hand. Lily smiled and asked her mom, "Can I ride the pony, please?"

Her mom nodded and helped Lily climb on the pony's back. The pony walked slowly around the park, and Lily felt like a princess. She waved to the other children and sang a song. She was having so much fun, she did not notice the big cloud in the sky.

Suddenly, the cloud made a loud noise. It was thunder. The pony got scared and started to run. Lily got scared too and held on to the pony's mane. She cried, "Mommy, help me!"

Her mom ran after the pony and shouted, "Stop, pony, stop!" She caught up with the pony and grabbed its reins. She calmed the pony down and lifted Lily off its back. She hugged Lily and said, "It's okay, sweetie, you're safe. The thunder can't hurt you or the pony. It's just a noise."

Lily sniffled and said, "Thank you, mommy. I'm sorry, pony. I didn't mean to make you scared." She stroked the pony's nose and gave it another carrot. The pony licked Lily's cheek and made a soft noise. It was not scared anymore. Lily smiled and said, "I still like you, pony. You're my friend."

Once upon a time there was a brave girl who wanted to go explore the world. She asked her mum if she could and her mum said, "Yes, but don't go too far!" So she went on her way.

Sammy was a three year old boy who liked to play outside. One day, he went to the park with his parents. At the park, he saw an impressive swing. He ran to it and plopped into the seat.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Anna. She was three years old, and she loved to explore new places.

Once upon a time, there was a tiny mouse who wanted to find something new. So the mouse put on his best shoes and began to march. He marched through the grass and the trees, over hills and along streams until he came to a large chamber.

The chamber was dark and very big. He couldn't even see the roof! The mouse peered inside and it looked rather miserable. He couldn't tell what was in there, but it looked like a great adventure. 

So the mouse marched through the chamber, carefully stepping around piles of old things. He walked past cobwebs and saw bats flying in the darkness. Then, he stepped around a corner and right in the middle of the chamber he saw something amazing! It was a pile of cheese and it looked delicious!

The mouse was so excited that he quickly ran to the cheese and started to eat. He ate and ate until the little mouse was full. Then, he hurried out of the dark chamber, content and happy, but also a little bit miserable from all of the walking he had done.

Jill was playing in the garden one day. She loved to run in the grass and feel the sunshine on her face. Suddenly, she saw a way that she had not seen before. It was a clean way, surrounded by pretty flowers. She ran down the way - it made her very happy.

Jill smiled and started to run again. She knew that the clean way would be there if she ever wanted to take another magical trip again.

Once upon a time, there was an old man and he had a secret. He kept it hidden away in a box, but he was the only one who knew the special way to unlock it.

Once upon a time there was a bad man. He made other people very sad. He did not want to help people and only wanted things for himself.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy. He was walking through the woods and saw something shiny. He stepped closer and observed that it was an axe! The axe looked very powerful. He was amazed by it. He picked it up and pretended to chop like a lumberjack.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved to explore the forest. Every day she would go for a walk and marvel at all the trees, bushes, and wildlife.

John was an ordinary boy. He went out to play every day. One day, John wanted something special to do. He decided to push his red wagon at night.

Once upon a time there was a very careless fork. He wanted to serve his friends, but he was so careless that he always dropped the food on the floor. He was very sad, because he knew that his friends would feel bad if they didn't get their food.

Once upon a time there was a tree. It had a big trunk and lots of leafy branches. Its leaves were a very attractive green.

But then one day the tree began to rot. Its Greens turned brown and its branches started to fall off. All the people stopped admiring it and they started to feel sad.

The tree smiled, happy that its leaves found a new home. The little girl was delighted with the attractive leaves and soon she and the tree enjoyed the sound of the wind together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Amy. She was very independent and liked to do things on her own. One day, she went for a walk in the park and found a shiny mineral. It was round and sparkly, and Amy thought it was very pretty.

Amy picked up the mineral and showed it to her friend, Tom. "Look what I found!" she said. Tom looked at the mineral and thought it was pretty too. "Let's play a game with it," Tom suggested. "We can take turns to spin the mineral and see who can make it spin the longest."

Amy and Tom took turns spinning the shiny mineral. They laughed and cheered as they watched it spin round and round. They were having so much fun, they didn't notice the sun was setting. When they finally stopped playing, it was time to go home.

Amy and Tom said goodbye to each other and went back to their homes. Amy put the shiny mineral on her shelf so she could look at it every day. She was happy to have found such a special thing and to have shared a fun day with her friend Tom.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she went to the beach with her mommy and daddy. They played in the sand and swam in the water. Suddenly, Lily saw a dolphin swimming in the sea.

"Look, mommy! A dolphin!" Lily said.

"Yes, it's a dolphin. They are very smart animals," her mommy said.

"Can we go swim with the dolphin?" Lily asked.

"No, we can't. Dolphins like to be in the quiet water, and there are too many people here," her daddy said.

"I promise we will come back to the beach when it's quiet, and we can try to see the dolphin again," her mommy said.

Lily smiled and said, "Okay, I can't wait to see the quiet dolphin again!"

One day, Tom and Anna went to the forest with their dad. Dad wanted to chop some wood for the fire. He had a big axe that was very sharp. Tom and Anna liked to watch him swing the axe and make the wood fall.

"Can I try the axe, dad?" Tom asked. He wanted to be like his dad and chop wood too.

"No, Tom, the axe is too big and heavy for you. You could hurt yourself or someone else. You have to wait until you are older and stronger," dad said.

Tom was sad. He wanted to show dad that he could chop wood. He saw a small axe lying on the ground. It was old and rusty, but it looked like it could still cut. Tom picked it up and tried to swing it.

"Tom, what are you doing? Put that axe down!" dad shouted. He saw Tom holding the small axe and ran to him.

"But dad, I want to chop wood like you. This axe is not big and heavy. It is small and light. See?" Tom said. He swung the axe again, but he did not know how to hold it right. The axe slipped from his hand and flew in the air.

Anna saw the axe flying towards her. She was scared. She screamed and ducked. The axe missed her by a hair and landed on a tree. The tree had a hole in it. Out of the hole came a squirrel. The squirrel was holding a shiny thing in its mouth. It was a rare coin.

"Wow, look at that!" Anna said. She forgot about the axe and ran to the tree. She wanted to see the shiny thing.

"Anna, wait! Don't touch that!" dad said. He followed Anna to the tree. He saw the rare coin in the squirrel's mouth. He knew it was very old and valuable. He wanted to have it.

"Hello, little squirrel. Can I have that coin, please?" dad asked. He tried to be nice and friendly.

The squirrel looked at dad. It did not know what he was saying. It did not want to give up its shiny thing. It ran away with the coin.

"Come back, come back!" dad said. He chased the squirrel.

Tom and Anna watched dad run after the squirrel. They laughed. They thought it was funny.

The end.

Jane and her mom were having a picnic in the park. Jane's mom spread the red and white checked cloth napkin on the grass. Jane looked at her mom and said, "What should I do now?"

Her mom smiled and pointed to the sky. "Let's gaze up at the deep blue sky and look at the fluffy white clouds," she said. Jane looked up and saw many shapes in the clouds.

Then, she looked for a bird in a tree and noticed a big yellow feather floating on the ground. She picked it up and put it under the napkin to save it for later.

Jane looked back up and said, "Can we gaze at the clouds again?" Her mom smiled and said, "Yes, let's take a napkin break and gaze at the clouds."

They both laid back and watched the fluffy clouds float by above them. Jane smiled and said, "This gazing is so much fun!" Her mom agreed and said, "Yes, it is!"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily who loved to eat candy. Her favorite candy was sugar candy because it was so yummy. Every day, she would ask her mom for some sugar candy.

One day, Lily's mom gave her a big bag of sugar candy. Lily was so happy that she started to scream with joy. She ate one piece of candy after another until the bag was empty.

But later that night, Lily's tummy started to hurt. She felt sick and couldn't sleep. Her mom told her that eating too much sugar candy was not good for her. Lily learned her lesson and promised to only eat a little bit of candy at a time. From then on, she only had a few pieces of candy each day and her tummy felt much better.

Once upon a time, there was a curious cat named Tom. He liked to play and explore all day. One day, Tom went to the store with his mom. They wanted to buy something special.

At the store, Tom saw a green plant. It was called mint. He thought it was pretty and smelled nice. Tom asked his mom if they could buy the mint. She said yes, and they took it home.

Tom and his mom planted the mint in their garden. Every day, Tom would watch it grow. He loved his mint plant and was happy they bought it at the store. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a loyal dog named Max. Max loved to sit with Lily and play with her toys. One day, Lily's mom bought a new machine that could clean the house. Max was scared of the machine and ran away.

Lily was sad that Max left her alone. She remembered that Max was always loyal to her and never left her side. She knew that Max was scared of the machine and decided to turn it off. She called Max and he came back to her. Max was happy to see that the machine was off and sat next to Lily.

Lily learned that it's important to be loyal to your friends and family. Max showed her that he was loyal by coming back to her. Even though the machine was new and exciting, Lily knew that her friendship with Max was more important.

Mama had a surprise for the children. Today they were going to take a test. The children were excited to take the exam because they had been practicing hard.

Mama showed the children a special paper. On the paper, there were many questions. Some of the questions were easy but some were very hard. The children did their best to answer the questions.

When they were finished, Mama smiled. She said that everyone did a great job. She reminded them that it is important to always stay curious and practice to become better at something.

Mama said that those who are ignorant don't take the time to test themselves. She wanted the children to understand the importance of learning and growing. She told them to always take the time to test their skills.

The children thought about what Mama said and smiled. They were happy to have taken the exam because it was fun to learn.

This is the story of Mark and his family. Mark was a very active little boy and loved to explore the world around him. He had a big family and they were always available to help him when he needed it.

One day, Mark wanted to mark his family's door. He grabbed a pencil and scribbled happy drawings on the door. His family smiled when they saw the drawings and put their arms around him.

Mark was very proud of his work. He marked many things in the house and his family clapped and cheered for him each time. He continued to mark more things and made his family very happy.

So, no matter what, Mark's family will always be available to help him explore the world and mark things that make him happy.

Once there was a little girl named Jane. Jane liked to go outside and help her mom and dad, and one day she wanted to help them rake the leaves in the garden. So of course, her mom and dad gave her a rake, and she started to move it back and forth through the leaves. But then when she went to rake the leaves, the rake got stuck and it hurt her hands. Jane was sad, but her mom and dad told her that it was OK and showed her how to move the rake carefully so it didnâ€™t hurt her. After that Jane was able to rake the leaves without getting hurt, and she was so proud of herself. She was glad she was able to help her mom and dad with the leaves.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She liked to play with her ball outside in the sun. One day, she saw a big tree with a hole in its side. Lily thought a small animal might live inside.

Lily stood by the tree and called out, "Hello, who lives here?" A tiny bird came out of the hole and said, "Hi, I am Blue. I live in this tree. Do you want to be my friend?" Lily smiled and said, "Yes, I would love to be your friend, Blue."

Blue came out of the tight hole and stood on Lily's hand. They played with the ball all day long. Lily and Blue became best friends, and they always played together by the tree. And they lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her pink toy car and sing songs. One day, Lily's little brother came in and disturbed her quiet playtime. Lily got angry and told him to go away.

Later that day, Lily's mom came in and asked why she was so upset. Lily told her what happened and her mom explained that it's okay for someone to disturb us sometimes. We should be kind and patient with others, even when we want to be alone.

Lily felt bad for being mean to her brother and went to apologize. They played together with the pink toy car and sang songs, and Lily realized that it was more fun to share her playtime with someone else. From then on, Lily remembered to be patient and kind even when she wanted some quiet time.

Once upon a time, there was a lonely little boy named Tim. He had no friends to play with. One day, Tim went to the park to find a friend. He saw a big box and thought, "Maybe there is a friend inside."

Tim opened the box to reveal a funny toy. The toy had a big red nose, a silly hat, and long shoes. Tim was so happy to have a new friend. They played together all day.

But then, Tim tripped and fell on his knee. It hurt a lot. The toy just laughed at him. Tim was sad and still lonely. The toy was not a good friend after all.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who wanted to buy something very special. It was a cobweb. Every day, the girl went to the store and asked for the cobweb. The store owner shook his head and said no. "It is too expensive for you," he said.

The girl was sad. She felt bitter and she wished she had enough money to buy the cobweb.

Then one day, something special happened. The girl found a jar full of coins. She carefully counted them and found that she had enough to buy the cobweb.

The little girl excitedly ran to the store and bought the cobweb. It was the most beautiful cobweb she had ever seen. The girl was so happy! She was very careful to never let anyone touch the cobweb. It was precious to her and she put it somewhere safe where it would always be. The end.

Once upon a time there was a prince named Jack. He loved to play in the garden outside the castle. One day, he found something very special in the grass. It was a jewelry box and it was full of original jewels! Jack ran to show his mommy what he had found.

â€œMommy, look!â€

Jackâ€™s mommy was very amazed and said, â€œOh my! Where did you find this?â€

Jack said, â€œI found it in the garden!â€

Jessica noticed a beautiful freezer in the store. She wanted it so badly, so she asked her dad if she could have it. 

"No sweetie," said her dad. 

Jessica was disappointed but she decided to take matters into her own hands. She snuck into the store late at night when nobody was there. She opened up the freezer and grabbed it. 

However, the store keeper noticed that someone had broken into the store. He called the police and reported the crime.

The police were quick to arrive, and when they caught Jessica, she was really scared. They took her to the police station and put her in a cell.

Jessica was never able to get the beautiful freezer. She had to pay for her mistake and her dad was very disappointed.

Once there was a child who was very persistent. Everywhere she went she would try her best to make people laugh by telling jokes. One day she went to the park with her family and ran around telling jokes to anyone who would listen. 

The child never got tired of telling jokes. Even when people didnâ€™t laugh she kept trying to make them smile. Everyone she passed was happy to hear her jokes and even though sometimes it wasnâ€™t funny, they were impressed by her persistent nature. 

After a while, the child had gotten so good at telling jokes, that people were soon coming from other parts of the park to listen to her funny stories. People would smile and laugh and even the adults would be amazed by her ability to make them smile. 

By the end of the day, everyone in the park was happy and roaring with laughter, thanks to the child and her contagious jokes. She felt proud that her efforts had made so many people smile.

Once upon a time, there lived a young girl who wanted to understand the world. Every day she would explore the forests of her village, looking for new things to discover. One day, as she strolled onward, she came across a melon, warm to the touch. She was so excited to finally find a melon that she quickly picked it up and took it home.

That night, the girl proudly ate the melon for dinner. She was so shocked to find out it was vile and tasteless - a huge surprise to her. She had been so excited that she hadn't tasted it before eating it. 

The following morning, the girl was determined to find out why the melon she had eaten was inedible. She went back to the spot where she had found it and saw that the ground under the melon was much harder than the soil around it. That's when she realized that the melon had not been ripened on the vine; it had been rushed to the ground by nature. The girl learned that day that when something is not yet ready, it is not meant to be taken or understood before its time.

Moral: You must wait for the right opportunity to understand something and take advantage of it.

Once there was a poor man. He was walking along the road, feeling very sad. He had nothing to eat and no place to go. 

Suddenly, a kind lady allowed him to come into her house. She gave him a warm wrap to keep him comfortable, and warm food to eat. The man was so thankful. 

The kind lady allowed the poor man to stay with her, so he would no longer be hungry and cold. She even allowed him to stay in her house forever. 

The poor man was very happy, and he thanked the kind lady for allowing him to stay with her. He was very grateful for the warm wrap and the delicious food. To this day, he thanks the kind lady for allowing him to stay with her.

Once upon a time, there was a big swing in the park. It was so much fun! Everyone loved the swing. Johnny wanted to swing the highest, so he tried so hard!

He pumped his legs as hard as he could and soon he was so high. Johnny loved the feeling of being up in the air.

He kept going higher and higher until he stopped and just enjoyed the view. He could see trees, birds and houses for miles. It was so beautiful!

Then Johnny went even higher until he felt like he was flying. He was the happiest he had ever been. After all the swinging, Johnny was tired and felt sleepy. He said goodbye to the swing and went home. He couldn't wait to come back and love the swing again.

Once upon a time there was a zebra who lived in the African plains. All the other animals were very friendly with the zebra and greeted it when it passed. 

One day the zebra was feeling upset. It didn't understand why it wasn't like the other animals. It wanted to change to make all the other animals happy. 

So the zebra decided to try out different changes. First, it tried to change its colour. It tried every colour but all of them just faded away. 

Then it decided to change its stripes. It tried every pattern but nothing looked quite right. Nothing changed. 

The zebra was getting more and more upset until it realized that it didn't need to change to be accepted. All of the other animals still loved the zebra exactly the way it was and the zebra was relieved and happy. 

The zebra stayed the same and all the animals were pleased. They celebrated by having a big party and the zebra was the guest of honour. Everyone was happy and nobody ever wanted the zebra to change again!

Sara and Ben liked to play with water. They had a big tub in the garden where they filled it with water from the hose. They splashed and laughed and had fun. But one day, they forgot to turn off the hose. The water kept coming and coming. It spilled over the tub and spread on the grass. It made a big flood in the garden.

Mama saw the flood and was angry. She came out and turned off the hose. She scolded Sara and Ben for wasting water and making a mess. She told them to clean up the flood and dry the grass. Sara and Ben felt sorry. They said they were sorry and they did not mean to make a flood. They took buckets and towels and tried to clean up the water.

As they worked, they saw a bird in the tree. The bird was thirsty and looked for water. It saw the tub and flew down. It drank some water and splashed in the tub. It sang a happy song. Sara and Ben smiled. They saw that the water was not all bad. It gave life to the bird and made it happy. They decided to leave some water in the tub for the bird and other animals. They also decided to be more careful with the hose and not waste water.

Mama saw what they did and was pleased. She praised Sara and Ben for being kind and gentle to the bird and other animals. She told them that water was precious and they should use it wisely and share it with others. Sara and Ben learned a lesson. They agreed to use water wisely and share it with others. They also enjoyed watching the bird and other animals come to the tub and drink and splash. They felt happy and proud.

A boy and his dad were walking to the store when they saw a van blocking their way. The boy wanted to go around it, but the dad said that they must wait because the van was too big to go around. They called to the driver in the van to move, but the driver just ignored them. The dad got very mad and shouted at the driver but he stayed stubborn and still didn't move.

The dad picked up the boy and said: "Let's jump in the van and move it ourselves. We can hold it in place while I drive."
The boy was scared, but the dad was determined. He opened the van door, put the boy on the seat, and climbed in himself.

The dad put his hands on the wheel and started pushing the van. Suddenly something terrible happened. The engine suddenly roared and the van started rolling away with the boy still inside! The dad jumped out, but it was too late. The van rolled away quickly, leaving the dad and the boy behind.

The dad was heartbroken. He was so stubborn that he made a very bad decision that day. The van was never seen again.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Susie. She was three years old and she was always very curious. Susie wanted to find out what was behind the hill in her backyard. She decided to follow it and find out what was on the other side. 

When she got there, she was very surprised. She saw an unusual image on the ground. It was a beautiful picture of an owl and a bunny. Susie was so excited! She wanted to find out more about it, so she followed the image to the forest. 

In the forest, the image started to move and float around the trees. It was so exciting! Susie had never seen anything like it before. She followed the image until it stopped in front of a big, old tree. 

Then a big, magical owl flew out of the tree and started to talk to Susie. It said "thank you for following me Susie. This is my secret home!" Susie was amazed. The image that she followed brought her to a magical place. 

Susie thanked the owl and went back home to tell all of her friends about the unusual image she followed and the magical forest she discovered. She had the best adventure ever!

One day, a little boy named Tim went outside to play. The sun was shining and it was warm. Tim saw a ball and decided to kick it. He kicked the ball so hard that it flew far away.

As Tim ran to get the ball, he found a letter on the ground. He picked it up and looked at it. It had his name on it. Tim was very excited and ran back to his mom.

"Mom, look! I found a letter with my name on it!" Tim said. His mom smiled and helped him open the letter. Inside was a picture of a big, happy sun. Tim felt warm and happy, just like the sun in the picture.

Lily and Ben were friends. They liked to play in the park. One day, Lily's mom said, "We are going to see fireworks tonight. Do you want to invite Ben?"

Lily was happy. She ran to Ben's house and knocked on the door. Ben opened the door and smiled. "Hi, Lily. Do you want to play?"

Lily said, "No, I want to invite you. We are going to see fireworks tonight. Do you want to come?"

Ben said, "Yes, I want to come. Fireworks are pretty and loud. Let me ask my mom."

Ben's mom said, "Okay, you can go with Lily. But be careful and stay with them. Fireworks can be dangerous."

Lily and Ben thanked Ben's mom and ran to Lily's house. They got in the car with Lily's mom and dad. They drove to the big field where the fireworks were.

When they got there, they saw many people and lights. They heard music and laughter. They found a spot on the grass and sat down. They waited for the fireworks to start.

Soon, the sky was filled with colors and shapes. Lily and Ben clapped and cheered. They saw stars and flowers and hearts. They saw red and blue and green and yellow. They saw sparkles and flashes and bangs. They were amazed and happy.

But not everyone was happy. Some naughty kids were playing with firecrackers. They threw them at people and animals. They made loud noises and scared everyone. They were not careful and they hurt themselves.

Lily and Ben saw the naughty kids and felt sorry for them. They said, "That is not nice. That is not fun. That is dangerous. They should stop."

Lily's mom and dad agreed. They said, "You are right. They should stop. They are ruining the fireworks for everyone. They are hurting themselves and others. They are naughty and foolish."

Lily and Ben nodded. They said, "We are not like them. We are good and smart. We enjoy the fireworks and we are careful. We are happy and grateful."

Lily's mom and dad hugged them. They said, "We are proud of you. You are good and smart. You enjoy the fireworks and you are careful. You are happy and grateful. We love you."

Lily and Ben smiled. They said, "We love you too. And we love fireworks. They are pretty and loud. They are fun and amazing. They are a special treat."

They watched the fireworks until they ended. They clapped and cheered one last time. They said goodbye to the people and the lights. They got in the car and drove home. They were tired and sleepy. They had a wonderful night. They dreamed of fireworks.

Once upon a time, two friends, Billy and Kim, were playing together in the park. Billy was so excited to be at the park and he showed Kim how much fun it was. 

When they were playing, Kim noticed something strange - a small lock on a box in the middle of the play area. She asked Billy, "What is that lock? I want to know!" Billy said, "Let's find out!"

So they walked over to the box and Kim said, "Let me try my key and see if it fits." She put the key in the lock and it fit! They turned it and the lock opened. 

When the box opened, Kim and Billy were so surprised to see what was inside - a big, angry bear! The bear roared and it was so loud that Kim and Billy got scared and ran away as fast as they could. 

It wasn't until later that night when Kim and Billy realized the importance of the lock - it had kept the angry bear away from the park and protected everyone from getting hurt. They were so thankful for the lock that kept them safe!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy who wanted to see the world. He demanded that his parents take him to the mountains far away. So one day, they decided to take him on an exciting journey.

As they got closer to the mountains, they started to see snow and ice. The boy was overjoyed and couldn't wait to get there and explore. He ran around in the snow, making snowballs and exploring the sights. 

But then, a terrible thing happened. Suddenly the skies opened and dumped buckets of cold rain on him. He felt so miserable, and he shouted and demanded that the rain stop. But of course, it didn't. 

Raindrops started to fall faster and harder, and soon the little boy was drenched. He started to shiver from the cold and he knew he had to get inside and warm himself up. So his parents guided him inside, and made sure he was warm and comfortable again.

Even though the rain had made him so miserable, he knew that it was part of life and that it could always get better. So he accepted the situation and shrugged it off, eager to get out there and explore all the exciting wonders of the world.

Once there was a little girl called Emily. She was only three years old and was always very thin.

One day Emily was worried about something when she heard a loud noise outside her window. She saw a big monkey and it was trying to open the window.

Emily ran to her parent's room and told them about the monkey. Her parents were very scared and quickly locked the window.

The monkey couldn't get inside the house and Emily didn't have to worry anymore. Her parents hugged her and she felt safe inside the house.

The next day, Emily's parents added more locks to the window so that the monkey wouldn't be able to get in. Emily was happy that she didn't have to worry anymore.

Jill was hoping for a fun day at the park. She was excited to run around and play in the sunshine. 

She ran straight to the bubble machine at the park. It was a cool device that made big colorful bubbles. Jill loved to catch them, they were big and full of joy.

A few minutes later, a friend showed up. They both squealed in delight. 

"Let's play bubbles," Jill said. "Let's see who can catch more!" 

Her friend nodded eagerly. They got to work, chasing and popping bubbles. They both laughed and hoped for more bubbles so they could continue to play. 
 
Soon enough, a gentle wind came by and blew away all the bubbles. Jill looked disappointed. 

"Never mind," her friend said. "Maybe more bubbles will come soon." 

Jill smiled and nodded. "Let's hope so," she said.

Once there was a girl named Ruby. She loved to play in her back yard. She had a dog named Spot who followed her everywhere.

One day Ruby and Spot were playing outside. Ruby saw a gate in the back corner. She wanted to check out what was on the other side. She ran over and opened the gate.

When she opened the gate, she saw a big lemon tree. It had the yummiest looking lemons hanging on the branches. Ruby picked one and took a big bite! The lemon was so zesty and delicious!

Then, Spot started barking. He was so excited he started running around in circles. He spun in circles so quickly that he twisted around and bumped into the gate. Ruby laughed as she watched Spot twist and run.

Ruby and Spot had a great time playing and exploring.

Once upon a time there was a small boy named Joe. He was a very persistent person. He had a special crayon that he liked to use a lot. Every day, Joe would draw with his crayon and he was very proud of the pictures he made.

One day Joe wanted to see how high he could make the crayon rise. So he jumped as high as he could, held up his crayon, and tried to make it go higher and higher. He tried and tried, and was very persistent.

Finally, Joe's crayon made it so high that it rose above the clouds and kept going. Joe was very excited. He watched his crayon rise above the clouds until he could no longer see it. 

 Joe smiled. He knew he had done something special, something that nobody else could do. Joe was proud of his persistent effort and his amazing crayon.

Sarah and her mom were cooking dinner one evening. Sarah noticed that her mom was sad. Sarah asked her mom why. Her mom told her she was feeling competitive and couldn't escape the pressure. Sarah offered some advice to provide comfort. She suggested that she should do something to make herself feel better. Together, they went to the park and played tag. Sarah's mom was having so much fun that she forgot all about her worries. She smiled and thanked Sarah for providing her with a much needed escape from all the pressure. They had a great time and both went back home feeling better than before.

Bob was an attractive young boy. He loved to play with his dragon, which he had named Colin. 

Every day Bob and Colin would play together. They would run and laugh and sing songs. But one day, when Bob and Colin were playing, Bob got a little dirty.

Bob knew that he needed to clean up, so he took a wet wipe and wiped his hands, face, and arms clean.

He also wiped Colin's face and wings, so he could be clean and attractive too. Then Bob and Colin were ready to play again.

They ran through the park and laughed and sang until it was bedtime. Bob gave Colin a big hug and tucked him in for the night.

Bob had a wonderful day with his dragon friend, Colin. And they both looked attractive in the morning!

Once upon a time, there were two friends, Ben and Joe. They liked to play together all day long. One day, Joe wanted to play hide and seek. Ben wanted to play something else, but Joe kept repeating "Let's play hide and seek". Ben was tired of hearing Joe say the same thing, so he decided he would try to trick him. He told Joe that he was going to hide in the vegetable patch, so Joe should start counting.

Ben didn't go to the vegetable patch at all. He hide in the tree. When Joe couldn't find him, he became very angry. He was so mad that he started to pull up all the vegetables! Ben realised that it was a foolish thing to do so he made up a game to get Joe involved in something else. Joe couldn't resist playing the game and soon he was having so much fun that he forgot about his anger.

Once upon a time there was a fair hedge. It was a tall and strong hedge and it was well looked after. In the middle of the hedge was a big mix. 

Every day lots of animals would come to the big mix. They would eat the mix and have a lot of fun. The birds sang and the butterflies twirled around the mix. It was very lively in the fair hedge.

One day a little mouse ran around the base of the hedge. It jumped up and down and glanced across at the delicious mix.

The little mouse wanted to eat the mix. So it crept up the side of the hedge until it reached the top. The little mouse grabbed a hold of the mix and quickly ran back down the hedge. 

The little mouse was happy that it found the mix. It enjoyed the taste of the mix and it shared the mix with all the other animals too. Everyone was happy in the fair hedge.

Once upon a time there were two friends, a lion and a hare. One day, the two were talking about the land:

"I can see all this wonderful land around us," said the hare, "but how do we understand it?"

The lion thought for a moment before he answered, "We need to go explore and see what it has to offer, and listen to the stories people tell."

So they set off to explore the land. Everywhere they went they found something new to learn. In the far away meadows they found purple flowers, and in the mountains they found the bluest of waters.

The lion and the hare kept learning new and exciting things. As they explored, they realized understanding land comes from open eyes, an open heart, and realizing it's okay to ask questions.

At the end of their journey, they both learned an important lesson: understanding comes from exploration and curiosity. So they both decided they would always be curious and explore every piece of land they came across.

Once upon a time, there was a peanut. This peanut was smooth and brown. One day, the peanut got a wild idea. It wanted to race with something!

The peanut thought and thought until it came up with something. It decided to ask the rabbit. The rabbit was curious, "What do you want to race?" it asked. The peanut said, "I want to race with you!"

The rabbit agreed and the race began. The peanut raced as fast as it could. Its shell rolled and bumped on the ground. The peanut was getting tired, but the rabbit was still ahead.

Suddenly, the rabbit hopped onto the peanut's shell. The peanut was so happy and started to roll even faster. It caught up to the rabbit and together, they raced over the hill.

In the end, the peanut and the rabbit both crossed the finish line. The peanut was happy it had raced with the rabbit. From that day forward, they promised to remain friends!

Once upon a time, there was a cute little cat. Her fur was shiny and soft, and she always played with her best friends, a big elephant and a happy dog. 

One day, the cat went on a big adventure. She ran and ran until she came to a very strange place. There, the cat saw the most amazing thing: a mustache! The mustache was big and bushy and it made the cat excited.

The cat wanted to keep the mustache, but she knew that it didn't belong to her. So, she decided to return the mustache to its owner. She waved goodbye to her friends, and then she carried the mustache back home. 

When she arrived home, the cat's family was very happy! They had been looking for the mustache all day. They thanked the cat and said she had been very brave to return the mustache. 

The cat was glad she had done the right thing. And she learned that returning things to their owners is really the best way.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy who loved going to class. He always listened to his teacher and did his homework. One day, Timmy's friend Johnny came to class with a new toy. Timmy was envious of Johnny's toy and wanted to play with it.

During recess, Timmy asked Johnny if he could play with the toy. Johnny said yes, but only if Timmy could answer a question. The question was, "What is the opposite of hot?" Timmy thought for a moment and said, "Cold!" Johnny was impressed and let Timmy play with the toy.

Later in class, the teacher asked the students to examine a picture and find all the animals in it. Timmy remembered the question from earlier and knew the answer was hidden in the picture. He found a penguin, which was the opposite of hot, and raised his hand to answer. The teacher was proud of Timmy and gave him a gold star. Timmy learned that sometimes being envious can lead to learning something new.

Once upon a time, there was a big mall. It had lots of stores with toys, clothes, and food. One day, it started to rain really hard. The rain was so heavy that the mall started to flood. A kind man who worked at the mall warned everyone to leave quickly. 

The people ran out of the mall as fast as they could. They were wet and cold, but they were safe. The kind man was happy that he was able to help. The next day, the sun came out and the mall was dry again. The people went back to the mall to buy more toys, clothes, and food. They were grateful for the kind man who warned them and kept them safe.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play with toys. Today, they go to the mall with their moms. They see a big elevator. They want to ride it.

"Can we go in the elevator, Mom?" Anna asks.

"Sure, honey, but you have to share with Ben and other people," Mom says.

Anna and Ben run to the elevator. They push the button. The door opens. They see many people inside. They squeeze in. They are happy.

"Look, Ben, we are going up!" Anna says.

"Yes, Anna, this is fun!" Ben says.

They see the numbers change. They hear a ding. The door opens. Some people get out. Anna and Ben see a big teddy bear on the floor. They both want it.

"Mine!" Anna shouts.

"No, mine!" Ben shouts.

They pull the teddy bear. They do not share. They fight. The door closes. The elevator goes down. They are scared.

"Mom! Mom!" Anna cries.

"Help! Help!" Ben cries.

The people in the elevator are angry. They yell at Anna and Ben. They tell them to stop. They tell them to share. But Anna and Ben do not listen. They keep fighting.

The elevator stops. The door does not open. The lights go out. It is dark. It is quiet. Anna and Ben are alone. They are sorry. They are sad. They hug the teddy bear. They wish they had shared. They wish they had been successful.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tim. Tim was a poor bird who lived in a tiny nest on a tree. One day, dark clouds came, and Tim was scared. He saw lightning in the sky and heard loud thunder.

Tim wanted to return to his nest, but he could not find it. He flew around the tree, looking for his home. As he flew, the lightning made the sky bright. Tim was sad and tired, but he kept looking.

Finally, the lightning helped Tim see his nest. He returned to his home, safe and sound. The storm went away, and the sun came out. Tim was happy and thanked the lightning for helping him find his way back.

Bob was walking through the park, feeling bored. Then he heard something amazing - the sound of music! He went to investigate, and soon he saw a cell. The cell was very big and shiny. Inside was a man who was carrying a big stick and making the amazing music.

Bob was so excited. He wanted to carry the cell and make the music too. But it was too big for him. So he asked the man if he could help. The man smiled and gave Bob a small stick and showed him how to make the music.

Bob was so happy. He carried the stick and made the most amazing music. Everyone in the park stopped to listen and appreciate his music. Bob felt so proud of himself and his amazing music.

Once upon a time, there was a family that loved spaghetti. Every Sunday, they would settle down to have a delicious spaghetti dinner.

One Sunday, the family wanted to make an extra special spaghetti dinner. Papa and Mama stirred up a big pot of spaghetti, and everyone was excited for dinner. 

When Papa served the spaghetti, everyone took a bite - and it made them dizzy. Mama and Papa knew something was wrong and threw the spaghetti away. 

The family was so sad that their special dinner didn't work out. Mama quickly made another dinner, but they were disappointed that their special spaghetti was ruined. 

The End.

Once upon a time there was an old fox who had a fat tail. The fox was very proud of her tail and every day she would swish it from side to side. She wanted everyone to be able to see it and to appreciate its beauty.

One day, the fox came across a match and she thought it looked like the tip of her tail. She approached the match and tried to match her tail to the match. But no matter how hard she tried, her tail was not the same size as the match. 

The fox got very frustrated and yelled, "Why can't my tail be like the match?" 

An old rabbit hopped by and said, "It's ok to be different. Everyone is unique and that's what makes us special."

The fox thought about it and soon realized that the rabbit was right. She smiled and went on her way, happy with her fat tail. 

The moral of the story is that it's OK to be different. We all have our own strengths and weaknesses, and that's what makes us special.

One day, a little girl named Lily went for a walk in the forest. She saw a cute bunny hopping around. "Hello, little bunny!" said Lily. The bunny hopped closer and closer until it was right beside her. Suddenly, the bunny jumped up and surprised Lily! 

Lily laughed and said, "You gave me a surprise, little bunny!" The bunny hopped away, leaving Lily to continue her walk. She saw a big, green frog sitting on a lily pad in a pond. "Hello, Mr. Frog!" said Lily. 

The frog croaked and said, "Hello, little girl. I have a modest home here on my lily pad." Lily looked at the frog's home and saw that it was very small. "It's very cute!" said Lily. 

Just then, a porcupine with sharp spikes on its back walked by. "Hello, Mr. Porcupine!" said Lily. The porcupine said nothing and just kept walking. Lily continued her walk, feeling happy and surprised by all the animals she had met.

The elderly man wanted to paint. He took his paintbrush and colors and he went to a country. In the country, he saw a grassy field with a lot of flowers. The colors of the flowers were so bright that the elderly man was filled with joy. He began to paint.

When the elderly man started to paint, a small 3 year old boy came up to him. The boy had never seen someone paint before. He asked the elderly man what he was doing. The elderly man said, â€œIâ€™m painting the beauty of this country.â€

The 3 year old watched the elderly man paint and he was amazed. He said, â€œThis is so beautiful!â€

The elderly man smiled at the little boy and said, â€œI'm glad you like it! Maybe one day you'll paint a country too. 

The 3 year old smiled and nodded his head. Then, he ran off to tell all his friends about what the elderly man was doing.

Once, there was a little boy who liked to dream. Every night, he would close his eyes and dream of wide open spaces. One night, he dreamed of a big, wide cell. Inside the cell, he could see lots of people. But he noticed that they all seemed to be very sad.

The little boy asked one of the people, â€œWhy are you all so sad?â€

The man replied, â€œWe are stuck here and canâ€™t get out. Nobody wants to be here - it's no fun.â€

The little boy was very sad to hear this. He wanted to help the people in the cell. Then, he had an idea! He said, â€œLetâ€™s all close our eyes and dream of wide open spaces. At least that way, we wonâ€™t be so sad.â€

The man smiled and said, â€œYes, thatâ€™s a great idea!â€ So, the people in the cell all closed their eyes and dreamt of wide open spaces. Everyone was suddenly so much happier.

The moral of the story is that dreaming can help you feel better, even when youâ€™re in a difficult situation.

Tommy loves to watch videos on his tablet. He likes to see animals, cars, songs and stories. He always asks his mom or dad to load a new video for him when he finishes one.

One day, Tommy saw a video about a big truck that can load many things. It can load dirt, rocks, boxes and even cars. Tommy was very enthusiastic. He wanted to see how the truck works and what it can do.

He asked his mom to load the video for him. His mom said yes, but first he had to eat his lunch. Tommy was hungry, so he ate his sandwich, his apple and his yogurt. He drank his juice and said thank you.

Then, his mom gave him his tablet and loaded the video for him. Tommy was happy. He watched the video with big eyes and a big smile. He learned the names of the things the truck can load. He repeated them after the video. He said dirt, rocks, boxes and cars.

He liked the video so much that he asked his mom to load it again. His mom said yes, but first he had to take a nap. Tommy was tired, so he agreed. He put his tablet on his bed and cuddled with his teddy bear. He closed his eyes and dreamed of the big truck that can load many things.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. They have a stand with toys and books. They sell them to other kids for one coin each.

One day, a big dog comes to the park. He is brown and furry. He runs to the stand and barks. He wants to play with the toys and books. He grabs a ball and a book with his mouth. He runs away.

Anna and Ben are scared. They run after the dog. They shout, "Stop! Give us back our toys and books!"

The dog does not stop. He runs to the other side of the park. He sees a pond. He jumps in the pond. He splashes water. He drops the ball and the book in the pond.

Anna and Ben catch up with the dog. They are wet and angry. They say, "Bad dog! You ruined our toys and books! You owe us two coins!"

The dog looks at them. He wags his tail. He licks their faces. He says, "Woof! Woof! I'm sorry. I just wanted to play. I didn't mean to delay your stand. Can we be friends?"

Anna and Ben look at each other. They look at the dog. They look at the pond. They see their toys and books floating in the water. They sigh. They smile. They say, "OK, dog. We forgive you. But you have to help us get our toys and books out of the pond. And you have to share them with us. Deal?"

The dog nods. He says, "Woof! Woof! Deal! Let's play!" He jumps out of the pond. He helps Anna and Ben get their toys and books. They dry them with a towel. They play together. They have fun. They are friends.

Timmy was looking for something interesting to do. He asked his mom "Can I go outside?" But his mom said, "No Timmy, it's cold outside." 

Timmy was sad. He asked his mom "What can I do inside?" His mom said, "I recommend reading a book. You can learn a lot of new things!"

Timmy said, "That sounds boring!" He asked, "Is there anything else I can do?" His mom said, "You can also build a factory with your blocks."

Timmy was excited. "Yes! I will build a factory!" He quickly built the blocks into a big beautiful factory. 

When he was done, Timmy was very proud of his work. His mom said, "Great job Timmy. Building a factory is an enjoyable way to use your time and be creative!"

The moral of the story is that sometimes the best way to use our time is to be creative. Doing something fun and enjoyable instead of something boring is always recommended.

Once upon a time, there was a mystery that nobody could figure out. Everyone was so ignorant about it because no one had tested it before. So one day, a brave little three year old decided to try to uncover the mystery. He tested the mystery by looking at it, poking it, and shaking it. But no matter what he tried, he couldn't figure it out. In the end, he just gave up and went home, still entirely ignorant of the mystery's secret. Sadly, the mystery was never solved.

Once, there was a dependable clown. All the other clowns would always go to him to find help. One day, a group of clowns went to the dependable clown and asked him to explain something very complicated. The dependable clown thought for a moment and then said, "Let me put it this way. It is like when a 3 year old child learns something new. They practice it over and over until they understand it."

The younger clowns then thanked the dependable clown very much and said that this analogy made sense. With that, the dependable clown smiled, waved goodbye and went on his way.

One day, a little girl named Emma went to the circus with her family. She saw a cute white pony performing amazing tricks! The pony had a long, messy mane and it was very exciting for Emma to watch. She clapped and laughed each time the pony did something new.

After the show, Emma was determined to meet the pony. She tugged on her mom's hand and said, "Mommy, I need to see the pony!" Her mom smiled and said, "Okay, let's go find him."

They walked around the circus until they saw the pony eating some hay. Emma waved at him and he walked over and said, "Hello, little girl! I'm glad you liked my show." Emma giggled and said, "Yes, I did! I think you're the best pony here." The pony smiled and said, "Why thank you! Now why don't you give me a hug?" Emma happily ran over and hugged the pony, giving him a big kiss on the nose.

The two were very glad they had met each other. From that day on, Emma and the pony were very good friends.

Once there was a little boy who loved to play outside. He was always running around and having fun. One day, he wanted to do something different so he asked his mom if he could go to the park. His mom said no. The little boy didn't like that and he disagreed.

He then had an idea. He asked his mom if he could play at his friend's house instead. His mom thought about it for a moment and then said yes. The little boy hopped for joy and gave his mom a big hug.

The little boy was so excited to go and play at his friend's house. He had lots of fun running and playing tag. His mom even joined them for a while. They played so long that the little boy got a sore knee. His mom said it was time to go home and the little boy disagreed again.

But after a while his mom convinced him to go home. The little boy was sad but his mom made him a promise that if he was successful in being a good boy, then they could go to the park the next day. The little boy was so excited about the news that he forgot about his sore knee.

Once upon a time, there was a dog named Fuzzy. Fuzzy was very adventurous and liked to explore the world. One day, Fuzzy went on a journey and found himself in the middle of the woods. 

Fuzzy was feeling lost when he heard a voice. It was a friendly voice coming from a bird that was perched on a tree. 

The bird said, "Follow me! I know a way out of these woods." 

Fuzzy followed the bird and soon enough found himself back at home. The bird said goodbye and flew away.

Fuzzy felt grateful and never forgot how reliable his little friend had been. As a thank you to the bird, Fuzzy left a pill on a rock for the bird whenever he went out for a walk. 

The bird was very happy and from then on, the two were best friends. They continued to explore the world together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Emily. She was very creative, and loved to get her hands and feet messy with dough. Emily's mom had bought her a big tub of dough for her to play with.

Emily was very excited, and she immediately got to work on creating a wonderful sculpture. She patted, twisted and molded the dough together, squeezing it between her fingers until it formed the shape she wanted.

When Emily showed her mom her masterpiece, her mom was so happy that she offered to bake it in the oven. Emily eagerly said yes, and the dough was popped in the oven. 

As the minutes went by, Emily started to tremble in anticipation. She wanted to open the oven and see her sculpture. Finally, the oven timer went off, and her mom opened the oven. 

However, Emily's face fell! Her once beautiful sculpture had melted into a pile of dough! Emily started to cry, and her mom tried to comfort her. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a girl who loved her pretty dress. She wore it all the time. One day she came across a fake dress that was almost just like hers.

The girl looked at the fake dress and nodded. She wanted to take it home. So, she put on the fake dress and ran away.

Back home, the girl showed off the fake dress. Everyone laughed at the silly dress. Even though it was a fake dress, the girl loved it and kept it forever.

The End.

Once upon a time there was a poor little girl who lived in a small house by the sea. Every day, she would go down to the beach to look for shrimp. 

One day, when she was looking for shrimp, she found a big, shiny rock. She thought it was very exciting, and she picked it up and took it home to put in her room. 

The next day, a great storm was brewing in the sky, and the little girl was worried. She knew the storm would pour buckets of rain on her house. 

The little girl remembered the big, shiny rock, so she thought she should bring it outside to pour all hte rain from the storm away from her house. She ran outside, holding the rock in her hands, but it was too late. The storm was already pouring rain everywhere! 

Suddenly, the little girl had an idea. She put the rock in a big bowl, and then started pouring the shrimp from the beach into the big bowl. She had realized that the big, shiny rock was actually a stone bowl! 

The little girl was so proud of her clever idea. The poor little girl had used the stone bowl to save the day! 

The End.

Once upon a time, there was a store. It was very attractive and everyone liked to go there. One day, something went wrong. The store needed to be fixed. So the shop keeper called for help.

A kind man came and fixed the store. He knew just what to do. He fixed it up so it was even more attractive than before. Everyone cheered and thanked the kind man for his help.

Now, everyone can always go to the store and be happy. They know it will always look nice and it can be fixed if something ever goes wrong. That makes everyone smile. The end.

Joe was preparing for a fun day. He looked at his calendar and saw that it was a dull day. He wanted to sprinkle some happiness in his day so he decided to do some cooking. 

He prepared his ingredients: flour, sugar and eggs. He also got out some colorful sprinkles from the cupboard. He thought they would make his bake even more delicious. 

Joe carefully mixed the ingredients together and placed the mixture in the oven. When it was done baking, Joe took out his delicious creation and licked his lips with excitement. He topped it off with the colorful sprinkles. 

Joe smiled with delight. No more dull days anymore! He was already looking forward to the next fun day on his calendar.

Once there was a bee that was having a tough day. He struggled to find food and buzzed around trying to find something delicious. He flew past a stupid frog that was just sitting there not doing anything. 
The bee couldn't find anything to eat and so he felt very hungry and weak. He kept struggling to find food, but it seemed like nothing was around. 
He was so hungry and sad that he was about to give up when he saw a beautiful flower with lots of yummy nectar inside. He flew to the flower and started drinking the sweet nectar. He enjoyed it so much and felt so happy.

The bee was so thankful that he had struggled and eventually found something delicious to eat. He flew away feeling much better and full of energy.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy had a big sack that he took everywhere with him. One day, Timmy went to the park to play with his friends. But when he got there, his friends were not there. Timmy felt sad and gloomy because he wanted to play with his friends.

Timmy saw a man sitting on a bench and went to talk to him. The man asked Timmy why he looked so sad. Timmy told the man that he wanted to play with his friends but they were not there. The man said they might be at the store getting some snacks. Timmy thought it was a good idea and went to the store to find his friends.

When Timmy got to the store, he saw his friends and they were buying some snacks. They were happy to see Timmy and they all went back to the park to play. They discussed what games they wanted to play and had a great time together. Timmy was no longer sad and gloomy because he was with his friends.

Once upon a time, there was a brown bear called Bob. He was looking for a special something, but he didn't know what it was. So every day he would wander in the forest, looking high and low. 

One day, Bob saw a little rabbit. He waved at her, and she came over. 

Bob said, "Hello, rabbit. I'm looking for something special, but I don't know what it is."

The rabbit smiled. She said, "You should look for something that makes you happy and stops you feeling worried. Try looking at the sky!" 

Bob thanked the rabbit and said goodbye. He wandered around, looking up at the sky. It was so big and blue, and it made him feel so peaceful. Suddenly, he felt happy and his worries melted away. 

And from that day on, Bob never felt worried again.

Once upon a time, there was a restless pirate. He wanted to find victory. Everywhere he went he looked for treasure, but he couldn't find it.

The pirate sailed across the ocean and eventually came to shore. He was so tired from his journey that he lay down on the sand and fell asleep. While the pirate was sleeping, he had a dream about a big chest full of treasure.

The pirate woke up and began to look for the chest. He searched every beach, but he couldn't find it. He was about to give up, but then he saw something round and shiny lying in the sand. He looked closer and saw that it was the same big chest he had seen in his dream. The pirate filled the chest with the treasure and celebrated his victory.

The pirate was so happy that he could hardly contain his excitement. He had found his treasure, and now he could sleep peacefully!

Once there was a bear. He was very furry. He lived in a mill by the river. Every morning he would carry two big bags filled with flour. He would make sure to not drop any, as it was precious. 

Sometimes he would take a break. He'd sit on the edge of the mill and feel the sunshine on his back. He'd watch the river run, the birds fly and the children laughing on the meadows. Then, late in the day, he would take his last flour and carry it back to the mill. 

He enjoyed this life, and never wanted to leave his furry home. Even though it can get lonely, he knew that he had to carry the flour. He was so important for the village!

Once there was a little girl named Molly. She was three years old and very jolly. Every day she loved to go outside and play. Her favorite game was picking up a sharp stick and running around with it in circles.

One day, Molly asked her mom why she was running around with the stick. Her mom smiled and said, "That is the fencing style that I used to do when I was your age. It's lots of fun, so you should keep doing it!"

Molly was so excited. She ran around the yard sharpening her style with the stick. Her mom watched from the porch and smiled. After a while Molly asked her if she wanted to try it too. Her mom laughed and said, "Okay, let's do it together!"

So they both ran around the yard playing with their sharp sticks. It was so much fun that Molly started laughing and giggling. They laughed and played until the sun went down.

It was the best game ever - and they were both so jolly.

Once upon a time, there was a beautiful princess. One day, she went for a walk in the woods. Suddenly, the princess saw a weird veil. She went closer to have a look. As soon as she began to touch it, a loud noise came out of the veil. 

Startled, the princess quickly stepped back. But a strange creature popped out of the veil. The creature looked really weird. The princess was afraid and ran away.

The creature followed her. The princess looked around for help but there was nobody around. She was very scared. 

But then, a knight appeared and saw the strange creature. The knight defeated the creature and set the princess free. 

The princess was very thankful. The knight said that the creature was actually a spirit that tried to capture her in the weird veil. The two were very thankful that everything was now safe. 

The princess and the knight lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a poor little girl. She wanted a wagon more than anything, but she didn't have enough money to buy one. Every day she would look at the store window and wish for a wagon, but still she couldn't afford it.

One day, she had an idea. Day after day, she saved her pocket money until finally she had enough money to buy a wagon. She ran to the store and bought the wagon she'd seen in the window. 

She was so excited to have her own wagon! She started pushing it around the house and the garden, singing with joy. Everyone in the neighbourhood started to hear of the poor little girl who had gained a wagon. 

The little girl was happy with her wagon every day. She filled it with all her toys and even took it down the street with her. Everywhere she went, she could be seen pushing her wagon. 

The poor little girl who had gained a wagon was never seen without a smile.

Once upon a time, there was an old squash in the garden. It was big and round, and it made a loud noise when it moved. One day, a little mouse came to the garden. It was very curious, and so it decided to climb up the squash and have a look around.

The big squash was disturbed by the tiny mouse, and it started to shake. The noise it made was so loud that it woke up the other animals in the garden. The birds flew up into the sky and the bunnies hopped away in surprise.

The little mouse was scared and it ran away as fast as it could. The loud noise of the disturbed squash echoed throughout the garden and it was a long time before the animals all settled down. And the squash? It just sat there, big and round, making sure all the animals in the garden stayed safe.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Jack. Jack was very troubled. He wanted a juice to make him feel better.

One day, Jack saw a bright green bottle of juice on the ground. He jumped to pick it up and smiled as he tasted the sweet juice.

Suddenly, Jack saw something down the street. It was a man. He was waving at Jack!

Jack was so excited. He waved back and held up the bottle of juice. The man smiled and waved again. Jack was so happy that he waved back even harder!

The man continued to wave, and Jack continued to wave back. It was like a little dance between the two of them. Finally the man smiled, nodded and waved goodbye.

Jack watched as the man walked away. He was so happy that he held up his bottle of juice and waved goodbye too. He knew that his troubles were not so bad anymore.

Tommy saw a nice grill. It was red and shiny and he wanted to touch it. Mommy said no, so Tommy crossed his arms and stared at the grill. 

Then, he saw two people cooking on the grill. They had chicken and hotdogs and it smelled really good. Tommy's tummy rumbled and he wished he could taste the delicious food.

The people looked really happy and Tommy liked to watch them. He saw them laugh and smile as they cooked the food. It was so nice to see.

Then, Tommy waved at the people. They waved back and gave him a big smile. He was so happy, he almost forgot about the nice grill.

Lily loved her dog Spot. Spot was a good dog. He could sit, stay, and fetch. Lily liked to give Spot treats when he did a good thing. She owned a big box of treats for Spot.

One day, Lily and Spot went to the park. They saw other dogs and people there. Lily wanted to show how good Spot was. She said, "Spot, sit!" Spot sat. Lily said, "Good boy, Spot!" She gave him a treat. Spot wagged his tail.

Then, Lily saw a big dog. The big dog was black and white. He looked like Spot, but bigger. Lily said, "Hello, big dog. What is your name?" The big dog's owner said, "His name is Spot, too. He is a Dalmatian. He is very smart and fast." Lily said, "Wow, that is funny. My dog is also Spot. He is also smart and fast. Do you want to see?" The big dog's owner said, "Sure, let's see."

Lily said, "Spot, fetch!" She threw a stick. Spot ran after the stick. The big dog ran after the stick, too. They both reached the stick at the same time. They both grabbed the stick. They both pulled the stick. They both growled. Lily said, "Oh no, Spot, let go! That is not nice!" The big dog's owner said, "Spot, drop it! That is not yours!"

The big dog and the small dog did not listen. They kept pulling and growling. The stick broke in half. The big dog and the small dog each had a piece of stick. They looked at each other. They looked at the stick. They looked at their owners. They dropped the stick. They wagged their tails.

Lily and the big dog's owner laughed. They said, "Good dogs, Spot and Spot!" They gave them treats. They petted them. They said, "You are both smart and fast. You are both good dogs. We are proud of you." Spot and Spot licked their faces. They were happy. They were friends.

Once upon a time, there was a happy dog named Max. Max liked to play outside in the park. One day, Max saw a little boy with a big smile on his face. The boy was excited to see Max and wanted to pet him. Max was also excited and wagged his tail.

But suddenly, Max felt something bite his tail. He turned around and saw a small puppy trying to play with him. Max didn't like it when the puppy bit him, but he didn't want to hurt the puppy's feelings. So, Max just walked away and found a new friend to play with.

From that day on, Max learned to be careful around new puppies and always kept his face happy and friendly. The end.

John was feeling very sad. He had no furniture in his little home. He dreamed of having a warm, comfortable couch but he did not believe that his dreams would come true.

One morning, John was walking outside and he found a sofa sitting on the sidewalk. He touched it and it felt so soft! He looked around and saw nobody, so he decided to take it home.

John's mother was very surprised when she saw the couch! She asked John where he got it from. But John did not believe her when she told him he should return it to its rightful owner.

John's mother understood that John wanted to keep the furniture, so she decided to let him keep it. She said, "I believe you, John. You can keep the sofa."

John was filled with joy! He hugged his mother and said, "Thank you, mommy. This couch makes me so happy!"

John never stopped believing in himself. He continued to dream and those dreams soon came true.

John was very hungry. He had been playing all day, and his tummy was growling. He went to the kitchen to find something to eat. He saw a big bowl of salad on the counter. He grabbed a spoon and started to mark the salad onto his plate.

Suddenly, his mom walked in. She saw John making a big mess with the salad. She yelled, "John, how many times have I told you not to mark the salad!"

John said, "I was sure I was just supposed to mark something to eat when I was hungry." 

John's mom sighed and said, "you are not allowed to mark anything without permission. Now go to your room."
