"No, Mia. I do not like the slide. It is scary. I want to play with the swings." Tom says.

Mia sighs. She likes the slide. She thinks it is exciting. She wants Tom to try it.

"Please, Tom. Just one time. I will go with you. We will be safe. I will hold your hand." Mia says.

Tom looks at Mia. He sees that she is happy. He does not want to make her sad. He likes Mia. He trusts Mia.

"Okay, Mia. Just one time. But you have to hold my hand." Tom says.

Mia smiles. She is glad. She takes Tom's hand. They climb the stairs. They sit on the slide. They hold a note that says "friends". They slide down together. They laugh and scream.

"See, Tom. It is not scary. It is fun. You did it." Mia says.

Tom feels proud. He feels brave. He feels happy. He likes the slide. He likes Mia.

"You are right, Mia. It is fun. I did it. Thank you, Mia. You are a good friend." Tom says.

They hug. They are friends. They play in the park. They are safe. They are happy. The end.

Lily and Tom are twins. They like to play together. One day, they go to the shop with Mom. Mom says they can choose one toy each.

Lily sees a doll with long hair and a pink dress. She likes the doll very much. She says, "Mom, can I have this doll, please?"

Tom sees a truck with big wheels and a loud horn. He likes the truck very much. He says, "Mom, can I have this truck, please?"

Mom looks at the doll and the truck. She says, "They are both nice toys, but they are very high. They cost a lot of money. You can only have one toy each, and it has to be low. It has to cost a little money. Do you understand?"

Lily and Tom nod. They understand. They look around the shop for low toys. They see some books, some crayons, some balls, and some puzzles. They think hard. They want to choose a good toy.

Lily finds a book with pictures of animals. She likes animals. She says, "Mom, can I have this book, please? It is low. It costs a little money."

Tom finds a puzzle with cars and planes. He likes cars and planes. He says, "Mom, can I have this puzzle, please? It is low. It costs a little money."

Mom smiles. She says, "Yes, you can have the book and the puzzle. They are both good toys. They are low. They cost a little money. You are smart and kind. I am proud of you."

Lily and Tom hug Mom. They say, "Thank you, Mom. We love you."

Mom pays for the book and the puzzle. She gives them to Lily and Tom. They are happy. They go home to play with their new toys. They answer Mom when she asks them questions. They share and help each other. They have fun.

Lilly was walking in the field with her mom. She saw a large tree full of apples and tugged at her mom's hand while pointing excitedly. She asked, "Mama, can I pick apples?" Mom smiled and replied, "Of course, sweetheart. Be careful!"

Lilly was so eager to pick apples that she started running towards the tree. She grabbed the closest apple and quickly took a huge bite out of it. Mom said, "Lilly, why did you do that without asking?" Lilly replied, "I was so eager to try it!"

Mom laughed and said, "That's okay, sweetheart. Let me help you pick some apples to take home so you can have something healthy to eat too."

Lilly smiled, grabbed a few apples off the tree, and hurried back to her mom. They put the apples in a bag and started to walk away. Lilly had a look of satisfaction on her face as she said, "Thanks, mama!"

Sam and his mum were out at the park. Sam loved playing on the swings, so he had lots of fun! 

They stopped by the opera house and Sam looked up - it was so tall! He had never seen anything like it. Mum told him it was an opera house.

Sam had never seen an opera before, and he was curious. So they went inside and sat down in their seats. Everyone around was dressed all fancy and mum explained it was a special evening. 

The lights dimmed and the opera began. It was strange, but Sam slowly started to enjoy it. He listened to the music and singing and watched the people on the stage.

At the end of the night, Sam was amazed by the unknown sounds and sights of the opera. He and his mum enjoyed their evening out together and Sam couldnâ€™t wait to go back for another night.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she went to the park with her mom. She saw a big round thing that could spin. It was so much fun! She asked her mom if she could spin on it.

"Sure, you can spin on it, Lily," said her mom.

Lily spun and spun until she got dizzy. She felt like she was going to fall down. Her mom said, "Let's go sit down and watch the screen."

They sat on a bench and watched a movie on a big screen. But Lily didn't like the movie. She said, "Mom, this movie is smelly. Can we watch something else?"

Her mom smiled and said, "Of course, Lily. Let's find something else to watch." And they went to find another movie to watch.

Once upon a time, there was a girl who loved to eat fruit. Every day, she would go to the market and pick the sweetest and freshest fruit she could find. 

One day, when she went to the market, she couldn't find anything that looked yummy. She asked the farmer for help, and he gave her a big, juicy pear. She was so happy and took the pear home.

When she got home, she got ready to enjoy the delicious taste of the pear. But when she bit into it, it was sour and spoiled. She was so sad. She was sure it would taste so good.

The girl was determined to find something tasty, so she decided to go back to the market. This time, the farmer gave her a pineapple and a warning. He said, "Be careful! Eat it right away, or it might spoil too!"

The girl thanked him and quickly took the pineapple home. When she bit into it, the sweet and juicy taste filled her mouth. She was so happy. It was the yummiest fruit she ever tasted! From that day on, she always made sure to eat her fruit quickly, before it had a chance to spoil.

Tom was a very intelligent boy. He liked to read books and learn new things. He also liked to play with his dog, Spot. Spot was a good friend and a loyal pet.

One day, Tom and Spot went to the park. They saw many flowers and trees and birds. They also saw a big pond with ducks and frogs. Tom wanted to feed the ducks some bread. He took out a slice from his bag and tore it into pieces.

"Here, Spot, you can have some too," he said, and gave some bread to his dog.

Spot wagged his tail and ate the bread. He liked the taste and the smell. He saw more bread on the ground near the pond. He ran to get it, but he did not recognize the danger. There was a big sign that said "Do not feed the ducks. Bread is bad for them."

Tom saw Spot running and shouted, "Spot, come back! That bread is not good for you!"

But it was too late. Spot had already eaten some of the bread. He felt a strange itch in his mouth and throat. He started to cough and sneeze. He ran back to Tom, feeling sick and scared.

Tom saw that Spot was not well. He hugged him and said, "Don't worry, Spot. I will take you to the vet. He will make you better."

He picked up his bag and his dog and ran to the nearest bus stop. He hoped that Spot would be okay. He wished he had read the sign before giving him the bread. He learned a lesson that day. He learned to be more careful and to recognize the signs. He also learned to love his dog even more.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she went to the park with her mom. She saw a big slide and wanted to go down it, but it was too wide for her. She felt sad and started to complain to her mom.

Her mom tried to cheer her up by taking her to the swings. Lily saw a boy who was being mean to his sister. She thought it was stupid to be mean to someone, so she went over to them and asked if they wanted to play with her. They said yes, and they all had fun playing together.

Lily learned that complaining doesn't always make things better, but being kind to others can make everyone happy.

Once there were two friends. Wendy and Joe. They both wanted to change their world. 

One day, Wendy found an eraser and held it up to the light. It sparkled like a star! She knew it had the power to change things. 

So she and Joe got to work. They started erasing things that weren't happy, like bad thoughts and sad words. When they finished, their world was much brighter and happier.

But then, Joe decided to change something else too. He used the eraser to draw a big, light smile on Wendy's face. 

Now their world was perfect. They laughed and played all day long, spreading light and happiness everywhere they went. And the eraser became their best friend.

Nana and Grandpa were on a walk. Grandpa wanted to buy a gift for Nana from a special shop. But Nana disagreed. Grandpa thought the gifts from the shop were so charming that Nana would love them. But she still disagreed.

Grandpa asked Nana why she didn't like the shop. She said the prices were too high. Grandpa said the prices were really not that high and he asked her to just take a look at the shop.

But Nana said no. She said she thought it was better to buy gifts from another shop. Grandpa said, "But I think this shop has the best gifts in town!"

Nana smiled and said, "I know, but I still think the prices are too high. Maybe we can try another shop."

Grandpa thought for a moment and then said, "Ok, we can do that. Come on, let's go!"

And they went off in search of the perfect gift that they both agreed on.

Once upon a time, there was a cute little girl who wanted to do something special. One day, she heard a noise coming from behind the curtain. She peeked around the corner and saw a pretty butterfly. She wanted to catch it, but the butterfly was too quick. She tried to follow it, but the butterfly flew away.

The little girl kept trying though and she didn't want to give up. She put her hands up to the curtain and tried to grab the butterfly. She resisted, but the butterfly fluttered away again.

The girl kept trying to catch the butterfly until it landed on her shoulder. She was so happy she had finally caught it that she didn't even resist when it flew away one last time. She was content with the beautiful moment they shared.

Once upon a time there was a nice lady. She loved blowing bubbles. Every day she would blow bubbles and have loads of fun. One day she blew a very special bubble. It became bigger and bigger. It became bigger than her! Suddenly the bubble started moving and it grew fierce. The lady was scared but she followed the bubble.

The bubble floated over fields and through the countryside. The lady kept following it, but she soon became very tired. She tried to catch the bubble, but it was too fast. Eventually the bubble flew away and the lady stopped chasing.

She was sad that the bubble had gone. It had been so much fun watching it float away. But when she looked up, she saw lots of smaller bubbles. She smiled and started to blow some more. The fierce bubble was gone but she still had fun with the smaller ones.

Tom and Sam are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big truck with a sign. The sign says "Ice Cream". Tom and Sam love ice cream. They want to get a treat.

They run to the truck. They race each other. They want to be first. Tom is faster than Sam. He gets to the truck before Sam. He smiles. He thinks he is smart.

He asks for a cone with chocolate ice cream. The man in the truck gives him one. Tom pays with his money. He licks his ice cream. He is happy.

Sam gets to the truck after Tom. He is sad. He thinks he is slow. He asks for a cone with vanilla ice cream. The man in the truck says "Sorry, no more vanilla. Only chocolate left." Sam does not like chocolate. He makes a face. He is unhappy.

Tom sees Sam's face. He laughs. He thinks Sam is ignorant. He says "Chocolate is better than vanilla. You are silly. You should like chocolate." He licks his ice cream again. He is rude.

Sam feels angry. He does not like Tom's laugh. He does not like Tom's words. He says "Chocolate is not better than vanilla. You are mean. You should share your ice cream." He grabs Tom's cone. He is brave.

Tom and Sam fight over the cone. They pull and push. They yell and cry. The ice cream falls on the ground. The cone breaks. The man in the truck shakes his head. He is disappointed.

Tom and Sam look at the ice cream on the ground. They feel sorry. They wasted their treat. They wasted their money. They wasted their friendship. They are foolish.

Once upon a time, there was a big truck. The truck had a seat for the driver to sit on. The driver drove the truck through a rough road. The road was bumpy and the truck shook a lot. The landscape was beautiful with trees and flowers. The driver saw a bird flying in the sky. The truck finally reached its destination and the driver got out of the seat. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a shiny jewel necklace that she loved to wear. One day, she went to the park to play with her friends. She was having so much fun that she forgot to take off her necklace before playing. Suddenly, she felt the necklace slip off her neck and fall into the grass.

Lily's friends helped her search for the jewel, but they couldn't find it. Lily was sad and started to cry. But then, her mom came over and helped her settle down. She wiped away her tears and gave her a sour candy to make her feel better.

As they were walking home, Lily looked down and saw something shiny on the ground. It was her jewel! She was so happy that she hugged her mom and thanked her friends for helping her look. From then on, she made sure to always take off her necklace before playing.

Once upon a time there was an ordinary boy. His name was Jake and he loved to play in the pool. One day he saw an empty raft floating in the water. He went to get it before anyone else did.

He took the raft home with him and washed it with a sponge. The more he washed, the brighter the raft became. When he was finished the raft was sparkling clean!

Jake was so excited! He grabbed a towel and ran back to the pool with the raft in his hand. He was so happy to see that the pool was still empty.

He jumped onto the raft and paddled around the pool. He could feel the sun on his face and the wind in his hair. It was the best adventure ever!

Jake stayed until it was time to go home. He put the raft back into the pool and said a "goodbye" before getting in the car.

From that day onwards, Jake would wash the raft every time he went to the pool. He was so proud of his ordinary raft!

Once there was a boy named Chris. Chris liked to go to the shop. When Chris went to the shop, he liked to pick out healthy food. He went there with his mum and she always knew what to pick!

One day, Chris went to the shop with his mum and he picked out some healthy foods. He had apples, carrots and some yummy bananas. His mum was very happy and she said, "Chris, you know how to pick the healthy things!"

They went home with the food and Chris felt so happy. He knew he had chosen healthy and he wanted to come back to the shop again soon and pick out more healthy things.

So the next time Chris went to the shop, he was like a master shopper. He knew what things to pick and he knew being healthy was fun!

Once upon a time there was a lady who was very unusual. She liked to explore new places and try new things. One day, she decided to try something very special. Instead of walking, the lady ran!

At first, she was scared. Everything seemed so different when she was running. But then she felt something amazing. Someone was supporting her! It was like a secret friend.

The lady ran faster and faster. She ran faster than she ever had before. She ran until the world felt really big and really small at the same time.

When the lady finally stopped, she realised that her secret friend was still with her. Her secret friend was there to support her even when she was having fun. She was so happy that she spun around and around in joy!

The lady ran and explored every day, and every day, her secret friend supported her. She felt so lucky to have such a special friend.

Anna and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. They care for each other. They share their toys and snacks. They help each other when they fall or get hurt.

One day, they see a green bird in a tree. The bird is very pretty. It has a long tail and a yellow beak. It sings a sweet song. Anna and Ben want to see the bird closer. They walk to the tree and look up.

But the bird is scared. It does not like people. It flies away to another tree. Anna and Ben are sad. They want to hear the bird sing again. They want to make the bird happy.

They have an idea. They find some seeds and nuts on the ground. They put them in a small pile near the tree. They hope the bird will come and eat them. They hide behind a bush and wait.

Soon, the bird sees the food. It is hungry. It flies down and lands on the pile. It pecks at the seeds and nuts. It likes them. It feels safe. It sings a thank you song. Anna and Ben are happy. They smile and clap. They think the bird is great. They are glad they cared for the bird. They are good friends.

One day, a little boy named Tom was playing with his toy cars. He had many cars, but he loved his red car the most. It was a modern car, and it looked very cool. Tom wanted to make a line on the floor for his cars to follow. He used a long piece of string to make the line.

Tom's friend, Sam, came over to play. Sam saw the line and the cars. He liked the modern red car too. Sam wanted to play with it, but Tom did not want to share. Sam was sad and did not want to play anymore.

Tom's mom saw what happened and told Tom to think about how Sam felt. Tom thought about it and decided to share his red car with Sam. They both played with the cars on the line and had lots of fun. Tom learned that sharing is important, and it made both him and Sam happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He loved riding his bicycle around his neighborhood. One day, while he was riding his bike, he met a new friend named Sarah. Sarah was very enthusiastic about Timmy's bike and asked if she could ride it too.

Timmy said, "Sure! Let's ride together!" They rode their bikes around the block and had so much fun. Sarah said, "I love your bike, Timmy. It's so shiny and fast!" Timmy smiled and said, "Thanks! I got it for my birthday."

After they finished riding, Sarah said, "I hope we can meet again soon and ride together." Timmy replied, "Me too! I had so much fun with you." And with that, they said goodbye and went their separate ways. Timmy was happy to have made a new friend who loved his bicycle as much as he did.

Once upon a time, there was a kind and compassionate mom who had a little girl named Lucy. They lived in a small house with a big tree in the yard. Every morning, mom would make toast for Lucy's breakfast. Lucy loved her toast with butter and jam.

One day, mom put the bread in the toaster to make toast. But when she tried to snap the toaster down, it didn't work. The toaster was broken! Lucy was sad because she really wanted her toast. Mom knew she had to find a way to fix the toaster or get a new one.

Mom had an idea. She took Lucy to the store to buy a new toaster. When they got there, they found a big, shiny toaster that would snap down just right. They brought it home and mom made Lucy her favorite toast with butter and jam. Lucy was so happy and knew her compassionate mom would always find a way to make things better.

Once upon a time, there were two brothers called Steve and Dave. Steve was very intelligent and could do lots of clever things. Dave was not as smart, but he worked very hard.

One day, the brothers went into the fields to look for something special. Suddenly, they saw a shiny leather ball lying in the grass. They turned it over and saw that it had something written on it.

The brothers read it and it said: "Be intelligent and work hard." They knew that these words were important and really wise. 

The brothers realised that to be successful, they had to be both intelligent and work hard. They smiled and nodded their heads, happy to have learnt a valuable lesson. Steve and Dave went home, determined to use their brains and work hard in the future.

Once upon a time there were two best friends, Jack and Jill. They were very excited because it was a special day - they were going to get a surprise!

Jack and Jill looked around, but they could not find their surprise. So, they decided to look for clues. They searched all over, and then suddenly Jack yelled, â€œI see something!â€

Jill ran to where Jack was standing and saw a big box with a lock on it. Jack took out a key from his pocket and tried to unlock the box. But it wouldnâ€™t open! Jack tried again and again, but nothing worked.

Jill took out a big strong key from her palm and said, â€œLet me try this.â€ Jack and Jill worked together and finally the box opened.

They were so excited when they saw what was inside - a beautiful toy train! They played with it all day, and it was so much fun! They were so glad that Jillâ€™s strong key had unlocked their surprise.

Sam and Ben were brothers. They liked to play in the park with their ball. One day, they saw a big dog in the park. The dog was black and had sharp teeth. It looked hungry and angry.

"Let's go and pet the dog," Sam said. He was brave and curious.

"No, Sam, don't!" Ben said. He was scared and smart. "The dog might bite you. It wants meat, not friends."

But Sam did not listen to Ben. He ran towards the dog with his ball. He threw the ball and said, "Fetch, doggy, fetch!"

The dog did not fetch the ball. It growled and chased Sam. Sam was sorry he did not listen to Ben. He turned around and ran back to Ben.

"Hurry, Sam, hurry!" Ben shouted. He grabbed Sam's hand and pulled him away from the dog. They ran to the gate of the park and closed it behind them. The dog could not get out. It barked and scratched the gate.

Sam and Ben were safe. They hugged each other and breathed hard. They were glad they had each other.

"Thank you, Ben," Sam said. "You are a brilliant brother. You saved me from the dog."

"You're welcome, Sam," Ben said. "But next time, please listen to me. I don't want you to get hurt."

They smiled and walked home with their ball. They learned a lesson that day. They learned to be careful and to listen to each other. They also learned that some dogs are not friendly and that meat is not a good toy.

One morning a rat came to visit a house. The rat was very curious. The rat was wondering what it should perform. The rat looked around, and then it noticed that the house had a piano. So the rat decided to perform with the piano.

The rat looked at the piano keys then it started to play. It was difficult at first but as the rat kept playing, it began to get it right. It was amazing to watch the rat's performance.

People started to come and watch the rat's performance. They were clapping and cheering and the rat was so proud. It was so happy it jumped around and danced with joy.

The rat had performed so well that everyone in the house was so impressed. They all thanked the rat for the wonderful performance. Then the rat said goodbye and scampered away, leaving everyone behind in awe.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Jane. Jane was very excited because it was her birthday. She ran outside to find her mom having a picnic. 

On the picnic blanket there was a big pie covered with strawberries. Jane's eyes lit up and she ran over to the pie. She asked her mom, "What is this?"

"It's a birthday pie! How about it?" her mom said, smiling.

Jane clapped her hands and shouted, "Yes! I want some!"

Her mom took a big piece of pie and said, "This is a special pie. It's spicy!"

Jane was a bit scared at first, but she still wanted a taste. She took a small bite and found it to be delicious. She loved it so much that she started to scatter the pie all around. 

The pie scattered everywhere, but Jane was too busy eating and running around having fun. Eventually, she realized that the whole area was covered with crumbs. She started to clean it up and apologized to her mom.

Her mom smiled and said, "It's okay, birthday girl. You enjoyed your spicy pie."

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to wander around her garden and look at all the lovely flowers. One day, as she was walking, she saw a worm wriggling in the dirt. Lily thought the worm was very interesting and decided to pick it up gently. She held the worm in her hand and watched it move. The worm was very small and had a lovely brown color. After a few minutes, Lily put the worm back down in the dirt and continued to wander around her garden, feeling happy and content.

Once upon a time, in a land with many green trees, there lived a little girl named Lily. Lily loved to play with her fragile toys. One day, she broke her favorite toy, a green ball.

Lily was very sad and started to cry. Her mom came to see what was wrong. When she saw the broken green ball, she knew Lily had been too rough with her fragile toy.

Mom said, "Lily, you need to be more careful with your toys. I must punish you so you learn to be gentle." Lily's mom took away her toys for the rest of the day. Lily was sad but understood.

The next day, Lily got her toys back. She remembered her mom's words and played gently with her fragile toys. She never broke another toy again, and her mom was proud of her. From that day on, Lily took very good care of her toys, especially her new green ball.

One day, deep in the wild forest, a little girl came across a funny looking creature. She scratched her head and asked, "What's that?"

The creature said, "I'm a gorilla and I stretch all day long."

The little girl was amazed. She asked, "Will you show me how you stretch?"

The gorilla happily agreed and began stretching its arms and legs. The little girl laughed and clapped.

The gorilla said, "Let's stretch together!"

So, the little girl and the gorilla began to stretch until the sun started to set. 

As night began to fall, the little girl said goodbye to her new friend and went home. From then on, she would always remember the wild gorilla who loved to stretch.

Mommy was getting ready for the party. She was very excited because she had invited lots of friends over. She wanted to make sure it was a special day.

Mommy bought a lot of treats, like cake and candy. She also set up some activities for everyone to do. She decorated the room and put balloons on the walls.

When all the friends arrived, everyone was so happy. Everyone talked and laughed and they had a great time. At the end of the party, they all shared their opinion about how much fun they had.

Everyone was very quiet as they were leaving. Mommy thanked them for coming and invited them to come back soon. Everyone agreed it was a perfect day.

Once upon a time there was a small puppy called Spot. He had big, fluffy ears and a big, bushy tail. Spot was so excited when he heard there were going to be fireworks! He wanted to go and see them.

Spot's mommy said, "No Spot, you must keep safe inside while we watch the fireworks outside."

Spot didn't want to stay inside, he wanted to go out and see the loud fireworks. He whined and begged, trying to paw his mommy for her attention. She said firmly, "You must keep safe inside, Spot."

Spot was sad, but he stayed inside and kept safe. He waited at the window, watching the lights and loud noises from outside. Spot was a very good puppy and he was so proud of himself for keeping safe.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Grace. Grace loved going on adventures. One day, she decided to go on a walk through the forest.

As she was walking, she saw a big wet branch leaning against a tree.

Grace grinned and said, "I'm going to open it!" She squeezed her eyes shut and eagerly opened the branch.

Suddenly, a huge bird flew out from inside. Startled, Grace jumped back and then started to laugh.

The bird chirped and said, "You found my home! Thank you for being so brave and helping me out." Grace smiled and waved goodbye as the bird flew away.

Grace beamed with happiness. She danced away from the wet branch, never to forget her magical encounter.

Once upon a time there was a little girl who wanted to go on an adventure. She left her bedroom and started walking. After a while she came across an icy tunnel and knew she could explore it. She bravely stepped through the tunnel and clapped with delight.

The little girl's clapping echoed around the tunnel and suddenly she heard something else! It was a friendly voice from the other side of the icy walls. The voice said "Hello! Who's there?".

The girl was a little scared but then remembered she was on an adventure. She shouted back "It's me! I'm alone and I am exploring". The voice replied "I'm delighted that you are here! Would you like to come play with me?".

The girl was so happy and started clapping. She walked out of the icy tunnel and saw that the voice belonged to a friendly polar bear.

The little girl and the polar bear played together happily until it was time to go home. Before leaving, the girl gave the polar bear a big hug and promised they would play again soon.

Lily and Ben were very happy. They were going to drive with Mom and Dad to Grandma's house. Grandma always made yummy dessert for them. They liked cake and ice cream and cookies.

They got in the car and put on their seat belts. Mom drove and Dad sang songs with them. Lily and Ben laughed and clapped. They saw cows and horses and trees on the road. They were almost there.

But then, something bad happened. The car made a loud noise and stopped. Mom looked at Dad and said, "Oh no, we have a flat tire." Dad got out and looked at the tire. It was very flat and messy. He said, "We need to change it."

Lily and Ben were sad and scared. They did not like the loud noise and the flat tire. They wanted to go to Grandma's house and have dessert. They asked Mom, "Can we still go to Grandma's house? Can we still have dessert?"

Mom smiled and hugged them. She said, "Don't worry, we can still go to Grandma's house. We just need to wait a little bit. Dad will fix the tire. And Grandma will save some dessert for us. She loves us very much."

Lily and Ben felt better. They waited in the car and played with their toys. They saw a big truck come and help Dad. They waved at the truck driver. He was very nice and gave them stickers. Soon, the tire was fixed and the car was ready.

They got back in the car and drove to Grandma's house. Grandma was waiting for them. She was very happy to see them. She gave them big hugs and kisses. She said, "I'm so glad you're here. I have a surprise for you. I made your favorite dessert. Chocolate cake with rainbow sprinkles!"

Lily and Ben cheered and said, "Thank you, Grandma! We love you and we love chocolate cake!" They ate the cake and enjoyed it very much. It was very yummy and sweet. They did not mind that it was a little messy. They had a lot of fun with Grandma. They were very happy.

Once upon a time, in a big pond, there was a hippo named Hippy. Hippy was a selfish hippo. He did not like to share his toys with the other animals.

One day, Hippy got a big, yummy cake. All the animals wanted a piece, but Hippy said no. He wanted the whole cake for himself. The animals were sad and went away.

Later, Hippy felt bad. He knew he should not spoil the fun. So, he went to the other animals and shared his cake. They all had a big party and were happy. Hippy learned that sharing is more fun than being selfish.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside in the sunshine. One day, she went for a walk by a stream. The water was so clear and sparkly! But then she saw a little fish who was troubled. It was stuck in a rock! 

Lily wanted to help the fish. She tried to pull it out, but it was too slippery. Then she had an idea! She found a stick and carefully pushed the rock away. The fish was free! It swam happily in the stream, and Lily felt proud that she could help. From that day on, she visited the stream often to see her fish friend.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. He wanted to invite his friends to his house for a fun day. Tim was so excited that he put up a big, colorful flag in his yard to show his friends where the party was.

But then, a mean dog saw the flag and wanted it. The dog jumped and tried to take the flag away. Tim was scared and didn't know what to do. He tried to stop the dog, but the dog was too strong.

In the end, the dog took the flag, and Tim was very sad. His friends came, but they were all tired from playing outside. They didn't have any fun at the party because the flag was gone, and they all went home early.

Once upon a time, there was a bald man who lived in a little house. He wanted to go to the temple. So, he put on his shoes and went outside.

On his way, he met a little bird. The bird said, "Hi, bald man! Where are you going?" The bald man said, "I want to go to the temple. Do you want to come with me?" The bird said, "Yes, I want to go too!"

They walked to the temple together. When they got there, they saw a big tree. The bald man and the bird sat under the tree and talked. They were happy to be at the temple together. They had a fun day and went home with a big smile.

Tom and Lily were playing in the park. They liked to run and jump and slide. They saw a big bush with red berries. Tom was hungry and wanted to try them.

"Look, Lily, yummy berries!" he said. He picked one and put it in his mouth.

Lily was nosy and wanted to know what they tasted like. She picked one too and chewed it. But the berry was not yummy. It was sour and bitter and made her face twist.

"Yuck, Tom, this is bad!" she said. She spat out the berry and wiped her tongue.

Tom also spat out his berry. He did not like it either. He saw a sign next to the bush. It said: "Do not eat. These berries are not for people. They are for birds."

Tom and Lily felt silly. They should have read the sign first. They learned a lesson. They decided to play somewhere else and not to eat things they did not know. They ran to the swings and had fun. They forgot about the bad berries. They were happy.

The boy was very glad. He was going for a walk by the creek. He had his recorder with him. He was so excited!

He stopped in one spot and looked around. He heard the birds chirping in the trees and the water lapping against the creek's banks. He listened to the sounds and then started to record them.

He played back the recording to see how it sounded. He couldn't believe how it sounded; it was like he was really there! He recorded some more sounds, and then he decided to walk a little further. He was very glad.

As he walked, he recorded the sounds of the creek, the bird's chirps and the rustling of the leaves in the wind. He was so happy, he kept on recording until his recorder ran out of batteries.

But even after his recorder ran out of power, he still remembered the wonderful sounds of nature. He was so glad that he got to record it all.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Elsa. She lived on a small sailboat with her mom and dad. Every morning Elsa and her parents would sail to the market to buy food.

One day, Elsa's dad said, "Let's sail to the market!"

Elsa was so excited that she jumped up and down.

Once they arrived at the market, Elsa's dad said "Look around carefully. Always be alert in the market. There are a lot of people here, so be sure to stay close".

Elsa did exactly as her dad said and stayed close to her mom and dad. She walked alertly around the market, looking at all of the interesting things to buy.

After leaving the market, Elsa's dad said, "Remember, if you stay alert, you will always be safe".

Elsa understood the lesson and felt better knowing that she was always safe with her parents. From that day on, Elsa always remembered to stay alert whenever she went to the market.

Imagine there was a special candle. It was round and made of soft wax. It had a wick in the middle and it was dry.

One day a little boy found the candle. He thought it was special, so he took it home to show everyone.

When he got home he put the candle in his bedroom and he imagined what it could do. He dreamed of a room filled with light and warmth.

So he lit the special candle. He watched the flame dance and the light fill the room. Everything was feeling nice and warm and he was happy.

The candle burned for a long time and eventually it was used up. The room was still dry and dark but the boy knew the special candle was still in his heart.

One day, a boy named Sam went to the park with his mom. He liked to play on the swings, the slide and the sandbox. He was a jolly boy who always smiled and laughed.

As he was swinging, he noticed another boy sitting on a bench. The boy looked sad and lonely. He had no toys and no friends. Sam felt sorry for him and wanted to help.

He jumped off the swing and ran to the bench. He said, "Hi, I'm Sam. What's your name?"

The boy looked up and said, "I'm Ben. I'm new here. I don't know anyone."

Sam said, "That's okay. I can be your friend. Do you want to play with me?"

Ben nodded and smiled. He said, "Yes, please. That would be nice."

Sam took Ben's hand and led him to the swings. They took turns pushing each other and having fun. They also played on the slide and the sandbox. They shared their toys and stories. They became good friends.

Sam's mom noticed how happy they were. She said, "Sam, you are very kind and jolly. You made a new friend today. I'm proud of you."

Sam said, "Thank you, mom. Ben is very nice and jolly too. I'm glad I met him."

They hugged and smiled. They had a wonderful day at the park.

Once upon a time, there was a young pony who lived in the forest. He was very shy, and he always kept to himself. One day, he decided to go explore the woods. As he trotted through the woods, he found something amazing! It was a treasure chest, and it was full of wonderful things. 

The pony was very excited to open the chest. He opened it, and he was surprised to see a beautiful necklace! He picked it up and put it around his neck. Suddenly, the necklace began to sparkle and shine. It revealed a secret message!

The message said that the pony should go to a nearby field. He did, and there he found a big surprise. A group of other young ponies was there, waiting for him! The young pony was so happy! He had found new friends! They all played together for the rest of the day and had lots of fun. 

The young pony couldn't believe what had happened. On that day, he had revealed a secret message and made new friends!

Once there was a great boy named Bob. Bob was three years old, and he liked to play with his toys. One day Bob stood up and wanted to go to the toilet. He liked to flush the water and make bubbles.

Bob had a great idea! He opened the door and called his mom and dad. "Come and help me make the toilet bubbles!" His mom and dad stood up and helped him. They filled the toilet with soapy water and dropped a special bubble potion.

Suddenly, millions of bubbles appeared in the toilet. Bob laughed with delight as he watched the bubbles go up and down. When the bubbles had all gone down the drain they gave Bob a great big hug.

Bob had a lot of fun at the toilet that day. Even though he was only three years old, he was great at making bubbles!

Once upon a time, there was a happy dog named Max. Max loved to run and play in the park. One day, Max saw his friend, a little girl named Lily. Lily was very cheerful and always had a smile on her face. She waved at Max and he ran over to her. 

Lily had a pretty bow in her hair that Max thought was very nice. He wanted to play with it, but Lily said no. Instead, she threw a ball for Max to chase. Max ran after the ball and brought it back to Lily. She cheered for him and gave him a big hug. 

Max was so happy to see Lily and play with her. He didn't care that he couldn't play with the bow. Lily was his friend and that was all that mattered. They played together for a long time until it was time for Max to go home. He waved goodbye to Lily and ran home with a big smile on his face.

Once upon a time there was an adventurous bear. One day, the bear was walking through the forest when he came across a yummy treat. The treat looked tasty and the bear wanted to eat it. But then he realized that it was poison! The bear resisted the temptation to eat it.

The bear then heard a voice calling him. He looked up and saw a beautiful bird in a nearby tree. The bird asked the bear to follow her. She said that her name was Saila and she knew of a new and exciting adventure that was waiting for the bear.

The bear accepted the invitation and followed Saila to a secret place deep in the forest. As they went, they saw lots of fascinating things. They even made friends with some of the animals along the way. When they arrived at the secret place, the bear was so happy and excited to start the adventure!

Saila taught the bear lots of new things and together they went on many fun adventures. The bear was so glad that he had resisted the poison because the journey with Saila was much better than it would have been if he ate the treat. The adventures he had helped him to grow and learn in so many ways. The bear was so lucky and grateful for the amazing journey!

Once upon a time, there was a loyal tiger who lived in a temple. His name was Peter, and he was happy and content.

One day, a wizard appeared. He examined the temple and said, "This temple is too beautiful to be wasted. I must take it".

Peter the tiger was very afraid. He knew he could not fight the wizard, so he pleaded, "Please, sir, leave my temple be. I will guard it and be loyal".

The wizard looked at Peter coldly. He let out a deep laugh and said, "You are too loyal, tiger. I declare that you be frozen in time, so you can never leave this temple". 

And with a flash of lightning and a thunder of power, Peter was frozen in time. The wizard took the temple, leaving his loyal defender alone and helpless. Unfortunately, Peter could never leave the temple again.

One day, a little girl named Sue was playing in her room. She saw a big curtain near her bed. Sue felt comfortable sitting near the curtain. She liked how soft it was.

Sue's mom came into the room and said, "Sue, it's time to eat." But Sue did not want to eat. She refused to go to the table. Sue said, "No, I want to play with the curtain."

Sue's mom thought for a moment. Then she said, "How about we eat near the curtain? That way, you can still play after we eat." Sue liked the idea. So, they ate near the curtain, and Sue was happy.

Once there was a little girl who liked to collect things, especially napkins. Every day she was out gathering napkins, taking them back to her room to add to her growing collection.

One night, the little girl got an idea. She decided to collect as many napkins as she possibly could all in one place. So off she went, gathering every napkin she could find and stacking them in a large pile. 

Once she was done, the girl couldn't help but laugh. But then, her giggles were interrupted by a voice. 

"What do you think you're doing?" It was her mom.

The girl looked dizzy and confused. "I'm just collecting my napkins," she said.

Her mom just smiled. "Well, why don't you take a break and I'll help you?"

So, they both sat down and started folding the napkins into different shapes. Soon enough, they had made a huge castle out of the napkins.

The little girl was so excited, she jumped up and down with joy. That night, she realized there was more to having fun than just collecting napkins.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside with his friends. One day, Timmy's mom took him to the store to buy some candy. Timmy saw a toy he really wanted, but his mom said they didn't have enough money to pay for it. 

When they got home, Timmy's dad was doing his math homework. Timmy asked him what math was and his dad explained that it was like counting but with bigger numbers. Timmy thought it sounded hard, but his dad said he would help him learn.

Later that day, Timmy and his friends were playing in the park when they saw a big, dangerous dog. They were scared and didn't know what to do. Luckily, a kind neighbor came and chased the dog away. Timmy was grateful and thanked the neighbor for helping them.

Once there was a chubby bear who's name was Pick. Pick loved to explore his forest home, so every day he went on an adventure.

One day, he heard a loud noise coming from the south. Something about it gave Pick a strange feeling, so he decided to investigate.

When he arrived at the noise, he saw two chickens talking. Pick couldn't understand them at first, so he called out, "What's happening? What's going on?".

The chickens stopped and one answered, "We are looking for other chickens to play with. There's no one else around". 

Pick thought for a moment and said, "Well, why don't you come over and join me?". 

The chickens were delighted and they joined Pick on his adventures. Everywhere they went, Pick and the chickens had lots of fun. Pick even taught the chickens how to climb trees and catch bugs.

The chubby little bear and his new chicken friends spent every day together. They were the happiest group in the forest.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Jacky. She walked to the market on a very gloomy day. As she walked, she could hear people shouting and children laughing. At the market, Jacky saw a man selling toys. She wanted to buy one but didn't have enough money. Suddenly, the man reached out and slapped Jacky on the arm. She was so scared and started to cry. Then a kind lady saw what happened and came to help. She told the man off and gave Jacky her own toy. Jacky smiled and thanked the kind lady. She hugged the lovely toy and walked away happy.

Tom and Lily like to play in the park. They run and jump and slide and swing. One day, they see a pond with many green things in it. They go closer and look.

"Look, Lily, frogs!" Tom says. He points to the green things that hop and splash in the water.

"Wow, frogs!" Lily says. She wants to touch one. She reaches out her hand and grabs a frog. The frog is wet and rough and cold. It makes a loud sound: "Ribbit!"

"Ouch!" Lily says. She drops the frog. The frog hops away. Lily rubs her hand. "The frog is rough, Tom. It hurts my hand."

"I know, Lily. Frogs are rough. They have bumps on their skin. They are not soft like cats or dogs." Tom says. He picks up a stick and pokes a frog. The frog makes another sound: "Ribbit!"

"Listen, Tom, the frog is talking!" Lily says. She laughs. She picks up another stick and pokes another frog. The frog also says: "Ribbit!"

"Listen, Lily, they are all talking!" Tom says. He laughs too. They poke more frogs and listen to their sounds. They have fun with the frogs.

But the frogs do not have fun. They do not like to be poked. They are scared and angry. They jump out of the water and chase Tom and Lily. They make loud sounds: "Ribbit! Ribbit! Ribbit!"

"Help!" Tom and Lily say. They drop their sticks and run away. They run back to the slide and the swing. They do not play with the frogs anymore.

They learn a lesson: Frogs are rough and frogs do not like to be poked.

Once there was a girl named Lucy and she was three years old. Lucy had one rule in her house - 'No touching the refrigerator!' But one day, Lucy was very curious and she touched the refrigerator. Her mom saw her and she was very mad. 

She said, "Lucy! You know you are not supposed to touch the refrigerator!" Lucy said, "Sorry mommy!" Her mom said, "I am going to have to punish you for not following the rules." 

Lucy felt sad and started to cry. But then her dad came in. He saw the broken refrigerator and he said, "It looks like it was already broken. So I don't think Lucy needs to be punished." 

That made Lucy very happy. Her mom said, "I think you are right." Then they all hugged and Lucy was so happy that she got to stay out of trouble. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved playing outside in the sun. One day, he found a big, mighty palm tree. He climbed up the tree and sat on one of its branches. Suddenly, he saw a little bird fly out of a hole in the tree. It surprised him! 

Timmy decided to take care of the bird and made a little nest for it in the palm tree. Every day, he would bring the bird some seeds and water. The bird was happy and chirped all day long. Timmy was happy too.

But one day, a big storm came and the palm tree fell down. Timmy was so sad because the bird's nest was destroyed and the bird was nowhere to be found. Timmy learned that sometimes things can surprise you, but not always in a good way.

Once upon a time there was a strong bear who lived in a valley. Every day the bear would explore the valley and discover new things. One day the bear saw a fox, and he felt something inside his heart. It was an emotion he had never felt before - trust.

He wanted to build a friendship with the fox, so he approached it slowly with a big smile. The fox sniffed his nose and smiled too! From then on, they were the best of friends. They spent many hours playing games and exploring the valley - they were very happy together.

The bear was always very careful not to break the fox's trust. He shared his food and they both always stayed strong and stayed by each other's side. They kept their friendship strong and the valley was full of their adventure and laughter.

Mallory and her dad were sitting on the porch when a big, black beetle flew by. Dad said, "Look at that big, black beetle, Mallory!" Mallory asked, "What is a beetle? What does it do?" Dad said, "A beetle is a very special insect. It loves to eat and fly around." 

Mallory went inside to see if she could find something about beetles in a book. She picked one up and started to read. The book said that beetles come in many different shapes and sizes, and that some beetles are even brightly colored.

Mallory came back outside, excited to tell her dad what she had read. She said, "Dad, did you know that beetles can look different and some are even colorful?" Dad replied, "That's right, honey. That's why that black beetle was so special!" Mallory and her dad smiled at each other and enjoyed watching the black beetle fly around together.

Once upon a time, there was a nice hill. The hill was green and had flowers on it. A little girl named Lily liked to go to the hill and set up a picnic with her mommy. They would eat sandwiches and drink juice. 

One day, Lily and her mommy went to the hill and saw a big bird. The bird had a nest on the hill. Lily and her mommy were very happy to see the bird. They set down their picnic basket and watched the bird. 

After a while, the bird flew away. Lily and her mommy finished their picnic and went home. They had a nice day on the hill and were happy to see the bird's nest. From then on, they went back to the hill often to see the bird and have picnics.

Anna liked to number her toys. She had one doll, two cars, three balls, and four books. She put them in a line and counted them every day. She was happy with her toys.

One day, she saw a spider on the wall. It had eight legs and many eyes. Anna was not afraid of the spider. She wanted to make it her friend. She said, "Hello, spider. Do you want to play with me? I have many toys. You can be number five."

The spider did not answer. It moved away from Anna. It did not want to play with her. It wanted to be alone. Anna was sad. She did not understand why the spider did not like her. She said, "Please, spider. Don't go. I will be nice to you. I will share my toys with you. You can have my doll. She is very pretty."

The spider did not care. It crawled to the corner and spun a web. It did not need toys. It needed food. It waited for a fly to come. Anna was very sad. She cried. She felt lonely. She wished the spider would be her friend.

Her mom heard her cry. She came to her room. She saw the spider and the toys. She hugged Anna and said, "What's wrong, my dear? Why are you crying?"

Anna said, "Mom, I wanted to play with the spider. But the spider did not want to play with me. It ran away from me. It does not like me. It is not nice."

Her mom said, "Oh, Anna. The spider is not mean. It is just different. It does not play like you do. It has its own way of living. It does not need toys. It needs a web. It does not need friends. It needs food. It is not sad. It is happy in its corner."

Anna said, "But I am sad. I want a friend. I want someone to play with me. I want someone to like me."

Her mom said, "You have many friends, Anna. You have me and dad and grandma and grandpa. You have your toys and your books. You have your classmates and your teacher. You have the birds and the flowers and the sun. You have so much love, Anna. You are not alone. You are very lucky."

Anna smiled. She said, "You are right, mom. I have many friends. I love you and dad and grandma and grandpa. I love my toys and my books. I love my classmates and my teacher. I love the birds and the flowers and the sun. I am not sad. I am happy. Thank you, mom."

Her mom said, "You are welcome, Anna. I love you too. Now, why don't you put away your toys and get ready for dinner? We have your favorite soup and bread. And maybe we can read a story together later. How does that sound?"

Anna said, "That sounds great, mom. I will put away my toys. And I will say goodbye to the spider. Maybe it will find a fly soon. Goodbye, spider. Have a good day."

The spider did not hear her. It was busy spinning its web. It did not need words. It needed silence. It was not happy or sad. It was just a spider.

Once upon a time, there was a little bear named Benny. Benny was playing outside with his friends when he saw a muddy puddle. Benny loved to play in the mud, so he jumped right in! His fur got very dirty and his friends laughed.

Benny didn't like being dirty, so he went home to change. He put on a clean shirt and pants. Then, he went back outside to play. His friends were happy to see that he was clean again.

As the sun started to go down, Benny's mom called him inside for dinner. Before he went in, he gave all of his friends a big hug. Benny loved hugs and he loved playing with his friends, even if it meant getting a little dirty sometimes.

Lily and Tom were playing in the snow. They made a big snowman with a hat and a scarf. They gave him a carrot nose and two rocks for eyes. They were very happy.

"Look at our snowman!" Lily said. "He is so big and nice!"

"Yes, he is!" Tom said. "But he needs something more. He needs hair!"

Tom ran to the house and came back with a comb. He tried to make hair for the snowman with the comb. But the snow was too icy and hard. The comb did not work.

"Let me try!" Lily said. She took the comb from Tom and pushed it harder on the snowman's head. But the comb broke in half. Lily was sad.

"Sorry, Tom," she said. "I broke your comb."

Tom was angry. He stared at Lily with a mean face. He grabbed the carrot nose from the snowman and threw it at Lily. It hit her in the eye. Lily cried.

"Ow, Tom, that hurts!" she said. "Why did you do that?"

Tom did not say sorry. He ran away with the hat and the scarf. He left Lily and the snowman alone. Lily was cold and hurt. She wished she had a better friend. The snowman stared at her with his rock eyes. He did not help her. He did not care.

Once upon a time, a bunny named Benny went to the garden to find some yummy veggies. He saw a big, red radish and hopped over to it. He took a bite and it was so crunchy and tasty!

But then, Benny saw some other animals coming to the garden. They wanted to eat the radish too! Benny didn't want to share, so he tried to separate the radish into two pieces. But it was too hard and he couldn't do it.

Suddenly, Benny's friend, a soft and fluffy sheep named Sally, came to the garden. She saw Benny and asked what was wrong. Benny told her he wanted to separate the radish but it was too hard. Sally had an idea and used her soft wool to help Benny pull the radish apart.

Benny was happy to have two pieces of radish to eat and he shared one with Sally. They both enjoyed their yummy snack together in the garden. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a bird that wanted to fly to the moon. Every day the bird woke up early and tried to fly to the moon, but it was too far away to reach.

That's when the bird's friend, a little girl, came up with an idea. She offered the bird some lotion and said, â€œif you put this lotion on your wings, then maybe you can fly to the moon.â€

John was a very unique boy. He loved playing sports and running around. One day, he asked his mom, "Mommy, will I ever find something that I belong to?" His mom smiled at him and said, "John, of course you will! You just need to keep trying different sports until you find the one you like best."

John was excited, so he started trying out sports to see which one he liked. He tried baseball and soccer, but it wasn't quite what he was looking for. Finally, he tried bowling and fell in love with it. He was so good at it!

John was happy to find something that he belonged to, so he kept practicing bowling. He even joined a bowling team with his friends. Together, they had so much fun participating in tournaments. It was a special game, and John knew he belonged to it. He could remain unique in his own way, while also being part of a wonderful community and sport.

Once upon a time there was a big hairy monster. He was very sad because he had left his family and didn't know where to go. He was all alone, and he was scared.

As he walked through the woods, he came across a little house with a friendly old man inside. The old man was very kind, and he looked like he wanted to help. So the monster asked the old man where he should go.

The old man said, "You should go to the left. There, you will find the answer to your question."

So the monster thanked the old man and followed his advice. He went to the left, and soon he came across a big city. It was bustling with life and full of people laughing and talking and having fun.

The monster felt so happy to see all the people, and he really wished he could stay with them. But he knew he couldn't, so he turned around and went back the way he had come.

On the way back, he thought about how different his life could have been if he hadn't left his family. He even began to regret it.

But then he looked up and saw the kind old man again. He turned to the monster and said, "Don't regret what you left behind, because it's always in your heart."

The monster was filled with happiness and hope. He thanked the old man for all his help and left with

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside and run around with his friends. One day, Timmy's mom told him that they were going to go on a hike. Timmy was excited because he had never been on a hike before.

When they arrived at the trail, Timmy's mom told him that they were going to climb to the top of a mountain. Timmy was a bit scared because he didn't know if he was fit enough to climb a mountain. But his mom encouraged him and said, "I know you can do it, Timmy! Just take it one step at a time."

So, Timmy started climbing the mountain. It was hard work, but he kept going. Along the way, he met a friendly human who was also climbing the mountain. They chatted for a bit and the human told Timmy, "If you keep trying, you will succeed in reaching the top."

Finally, after a long and tiring climb, Timmy and his mom made it to the top of the mountain. Timmy was so proud of himself for succeeding in climbing the mountain. He turned to his mom and said, "I did it! I climbed the mountain!" His mom smiled and said, "Yes, you did, Timmy. You are a very fit and strong little boy."

Once upon a time, there was a little birdie named Blue. Blue loved to fly high up in the sky and feel the wind in his feathers. But one day, Blue flew too high and started to feel tired. He needed oxygen to breathe, but there was none up there!

Blue started to feel scared and knew he had to fly back down to the ground. As he flew down, he saw a big, dirty cloud coming towards him. Blue knew he had to fly fast to avoid the dirty cloud.

Finally, Blue made it back down to the ground safely. He learned his lesson and knew to be careful when he soared up high in the sky.

There were two brothers, Jack and Joe. Jack was a bit naughty so he always wanted to escape and have adventures. One day Jack decided to escape and went to the forest. Joe wanted to follow him, but Jack said no, so Joe stayed back. 

Jack walked and walked in the forest and soon he was very hungry. He saw lots and lots of food around, but it wasn't healthy food. Not like the ones at home, which were healthy and filled with vitamins.

Jack grabbed some food but it tasted really bad. He thought he would get sick, but he still ate the food. 

When Jack came back, Joe ran to him and hugged him. Joe asked Jack what he learnt from his adventure. Jack replied, "I learnt that healthy food is always the best!" 

The boys laughed, but their joy was not for long. Later that day, Jack got really sick because of the food he ate in the forest. 

The moral of the story is: Always choose healthy food!

Once upon a time, there were two best friends, Tommy and Joanna. They loved to do everything together, including riding their carts.

One day, Tommy decided to take his cart out for a drive. He shouted to his friend, "Hey Joanna, let's go for a drive!"

"Okay!" Joanna shouted back. She hopped on her cart and off they went.

Tommy and Joanna drove through the streets, feeling the wind in their hair. But suddenly, Tommy stopped.

"What's wrong, Tommy?" Joanna asked.

Tommy pointed ahead. "Do you see that cart?" he said. "It's so filthy!" 

Joanna peered over. She could see the cart was covered in dirt and mud. "Why don't we have a race?" she suggested. 

Tommy smiled and nodded. Then, they started racing towards the cart. They drove as fast as they could, until they skidded to a stop right next to it. 

Tommy and Joanna laughed. They had so much fun that day, driving their carts and racing each other.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy, named Joe. He loved to explore the wild outdoors. One day, Joe was running around in the meadow, when he stumbled across a shiny coin. He immediately stopped and picked it up. "A coin!" he exclaimed, looking at it in amazement.

Joe carefully balanced the coin on his finger, marveling at its beauty. "Hmm," he thought. "How can I use this coin?" Joe decided to put it in his pocket and save it for later.

The next day, Joe was in the backyard playing. He remembered the coin and decided to pull it out of his pocket. He tried to balance it on his nose while he walked, but it kept falling off. He laughed out loud and tried again. After several wobbly attempts, he finally managed to balance the coin on his nose and walk around the garden with it.

Joe loved the feeling of wildness that he felt while walking around with a coin on his nose. He kept practicing and eventually became quite good at balancing the coin. Joe was so excited that he had learned how to balance something so wild.

Once upon a time there lived a curious girl named Jo. She lived in a bright and happy kingdom with her mommy and daddy. One day, Jo found something that made her very surprised: It was a bottle with a purple liquid inside!

Mommy said it was poison and told Jo to stay away. Jo felt a bit ashamed because she shouldn't have touched it, so she quickly put it back where she found it.

But Jo was still curious, so she asked mommy what the poison in the bottle was used for. Mommy said it was used to keep the bad bugs away from the flowers. Jo was so surprised by this!

Soon afterwards, mommy took Jo to the gardens and taught her why poison was important. Jo now knew never to touch poison and she no longer felt ashamed.

The End.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. She was three years old and very happy. Every night, Lucy would look up to the stars and pray. She was special and believed in the power of prayer.

One day, Lucy went for a walk in the park. She saw a big wire on the ground and she wanted to pick it up. It glittered in the sunlight and made her very curious.

When Lucy picked up the wire, a spark shot out and a special light filled the sky. Everything ordinary became suddenly extraordinary. Lucy closed her eyes and silently thanked the stars for this special moment. She didn't know it, but her prayers had been answered.

Once upon a time, there was a little birdy. The birdy liked to fly high in the sky and see all the pretty things below. One day, the birdy flew too close to a cliff and almost fell off! But then, a gentle breeze came and helped the birdy fly away safely. 

The birdy was very happy and wanted to thank the breeze. So, the birdy decided to sing a beautiful song. But as the birdy was singing, a branch suddenly snapped! The birdy got scared and flew away quickly.

After a while, the birdy came back to the same spot near the cliff. The birdy realized that it was just a small branch that snapped and that everything was okay. From that day on, the birdy was more careful and always made sure to stay away from the edge of the cliff.

Once upon a time, there were two best friends. One of them was named Amy and the other one was named Tim. Amy had a special blanket that she loved very much. Every day, Amy and Tim would play together and Amy would bring her blanket with her. Tim wasn't jealous of the blanket, he was happy that Amy had such a sweet one to cuddle with.

One day, when playing tag, Tim tripped on a rock and scraped his knee. He was a bit scared, so he asked Amy if he could use her blanket to rest. Amy happily said yes and let Tim lay down on her special blanket. Tim felt so cozy and safe that he wanted to take a nap. "Do you mind if I take a nap here?" he asked. "No! That would be great!" Amy said, "you can have my blanket."

That night, Tim included his blanket in his bedtime routine. He laid it on the ground and laid right on it. He fell asleep so fast! He felt so loved and safe with the blanket and was so happy that he was able to share it with his best friend Amy. He knew they would stay best friends forever.

Once upon a time, in a small village, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim felt helpless because he could not run as fast as the other kids. One day, his big sister, Sue, saw Tim sitting on the ground, sad.

"Tim, let's play a game," Sue said. "I will encourage you, and we will win together!" Tim looked up at Sue and smiled. They started to play a running game with the other kids.

At first, Tim was slow, but Sue kept saying, "You can do it!" This made Tim feel strong. With each step, Tim ran faster and faster. In the end, they won the game! Tim and Sue jumped up and down, happy with their victory.

From that day on, Tim knew that with a little encouragement, he could do anything. He was no longer helpless. Tim and Sue played together all the time, and they always encouraged each other.

Once there was a turkey who was very frightened. She lived in a forest, and every day she had to struggle to find food. Each night she hid in a different bush, and she was always scared.

One day she had to find food near a pond. But when she arrived, she saw a big dog. The turkey was startled and very scared. She tried to be brave and not run away. So she slowly moved closer and closer to the pond.

The turkey wanted to find some food, but the big dog kept barking and chasing her away. She struggled to stay away from the dog and find food.

Finally, after a long struggle, the turkey found some food and quickly ran away. She was so relieved to get away safe and sound.

"Wow!", said Jack as he peered at a bright yellow raining cloud.
"What is it?", asked his mom.
"It's a balloon hanging from the sky!", said Jack eagerly.
"That looks wet!", said his mom.
Jack wanted to touch the balloon, but it was too high.
Luckily, his mom had an idea. She spread out a big sheet and put some delicious carrots on it for the balloon to hang on.
Jack smiled and waited for the balloon. 
The balloon floated down and landed softly on the sheet.
Jack beamed with happiness and hugged the balloon tight.
"We will take care of the balloon and keep it safe, won't we?", said his mom.
"Yes!", said Jack, before running off to show his friends his new balloon.

John wanted to organize his toys. He got out his big red truck and lined up all his stuffed animals in a neat row. He wanted to get his blocks too, but they were all the way in the bedroom. He was so small that he couldn't carry them, so he called for his mommy.

Mommy came in to help John. She lifted him up and they walked slowly to the bedroom. They found all the blocks in a big pile on the floor. Mommy helped John organize the blocks into color groups while he clapped with glee.

When they were done, John put the blocks in the truck. He was so happy that he drove it around the house - slow and steady. Suddenly, his mommy called from the kitchen, 'Time for lunch, John." So John left his truck by the toy box and ran off for lunch.

One day, Jimmy wanted to tell a joke. He got a big box, and put all his jokes inside it. He carefully picked out one and started to tell it.

His mom asked, "What's so funny, Jimmy?"

Jimmy laughed, "I'm telling a joke, Mommy!"

Jimmy did his best to tell the joke, but he couldn't remember how it went. It was too difficult.

His mom said, "Let me help you. I'll tell the joke, and you put in the funniest parts."

Jimmy smiled. "Okay."

So, Jimmy's mom told the joke and Jimmy put in the funny parts. Everyone laughed and Jimmy was very proud of his joke.
