Once upon a time, there lived an ancient panda. He was very old, but still had a lot of joy in life. Every day he would go for a walk and look for something fun. One day, he came across an old tree with a hollow that looked like a cozy spot to rest.

So the ancient panda climbed into the hollow and fell asleep. But he didn't stay asleep for long. Soon, he heard a delightful sound coming from nearby - it was laughter!

The panda peered out of the hollow and saw a group of children, who were laughing and playing games. They were having such a wonderful time! The panda couldn't help but smile and he even began to laugh too.

The ancient panda laughed and laughed with the children, until his tummy hurt. Then he thanked the children for the joy they had brought him, before continuing on with his walk. He was so happy, and he always remembered the special time he had spent with his new friends.

Once there was a bear who loved spicy food. He always used to pick the spiciest of all the food in the village. One day, he was making his usual rounds at the village market when he saw his friend, the rabbit. The bear waved and the rabbit bowed in response.

The bear asked the rabbit what he had in his basket and the rabbit replied, "I'm bringing yummy carrot cake to my grandmother. It's her favourite."

The bear immediately started drooling. He asked the rabbit if he could have some and the rabbit said, "Sure, but it's really spicy. Are you sure you can take such a pain?"

The bear was too excited to wait. He eagerly took the carrot cake and bit into it. Alas! The bear had never tasted such a spicy food before. Suddenly his mouth was on fire and he yelped in pain.

The bear learnt a lesson that day: when it comes to food, not everything that tastes fancy is necessarily best for you.

Once upon a time there was a scary skull. He was living in a dark cave and he wanted someone to play with. He was so lonely that he was getting very sad.

Then one day he heard a noise. He saw a little girl outside the cave. He was so excited that he came out of the cave. His eyes were shining with joy.

The little girl was scared when she saw the skull. She started running away but the scary skull was too fast for her. He caught her and demanded that she surrender to him.

The little girl was so scared and disgusted. But then she saw a bright light in the skull's eyes. She realised that the skull just wanted to be friends. So she said yes, and the two of them started to play together.

They were the best of friends and the little girl would often come to the dark cave to play with the scary skull. They enjoyed their special friendship until the little girl grew up.

Once there was a girl called Lucy. She was 3 years old and loved to explore. One day, while on an adventure, she came across a crack in the ground. She peered into the crack and saw something tasty. She tasted it, and it was so fine!

Lucy was so excited that she ran back to her house to find something to crack the tasty thing open. She found a big hammer and ran back to the crack. Lucy carefully tapped the hammer against the crack, and the tasty thing opened up.

The little girl then put her hand inside the crack and pulled out a yummy treat. She smiled from ear to ear as she took a bite. The taste was so fine that she knew she would never forget it.

Lucy never forgot about the tasty thing she found that day. From then on, she made sure to bring a hammer and look for cracks wherever she went, in hopes of finding something so fine.

Once upon a time, there was a humble girl named Sally. She had a small bottle of perfume. Sally liked to smell nice. She would nod and smile when her friends told her she smelled good.

One day, Sally went to the park. She saw a little dog. The dog was dirty and smelly. Sally felt sad for the dog. She wanted to help the dog smell nice too.

Sally took out her perfume and sprayed it on the dog. The dog wagged its tail and nodded. The dog smelled nice now. Sally and the dog played all day. They were both happy and smelled good.

Sam was very eager to get to the beach. He couldn't wait to feel the warm sand on his feet. He quickly grabbed his bucket, fishing rod and a small net and ran to the shore.

When he finally got there, the water was much colder than he expected. Sam shivered. He looked around and saw a little crab scurrying across the beach. With a big smile, he scooped it up with his net.

He took it to the wooden bench nearby. The crab poked its head out of the net and squeaked, "Help! What will happen to me?"

"Oh don't worry," Sam replied. "I'm just going to look at you and then put you back in the sea. I'm definitely not going to catch you."

The crab seemed relieved and thanked Sam before scampering away. Sam waved goodbye before running to the shore to put his feet in the cold water. For a moment he shivered, but he was eager to continue his adventures.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside, but it was very cold. Her mom said, "Lily, put on your jacket or you will suffer in the cold." Lily put on her jacket and went outside to play.

As she was playing, she saw an old man who was deaf. He was trying to cross the street, but nobody was helping him. Lily went up to him and said, "Do you need help crossing the street?" The old man smiled and nodded his head.

Lily helped the old man cross the street safely. Her mom saw what she did and told her, "Lily, you are a kind girl. You helped the old man who was suffering because he couldn't hear. Always help others who are in need."

From that day on, Lily always helped others who needed it. She learned that even small acts of kindness can make a big difference in someone's life.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Jack. Jack liked to watch the birds flying in the sky. He would sit on the grass and look up at them. One day, Jack's mom took him to a mill. Jack had never seen a mill before. The mill was big and had lots of wheels. Jack thought it was normal for a mill to have so many wheels.

Jack asked his mom, "What is this place?"

"This is a mill," his mom replied.

"What does a mill do?" Jack asked.

"A mill grinds wheat into flour," his mom explained.

Jack watched as the mill turned and the wheels spun around. He thought it was very interesting. When they left, Jack said, "I want to come back and watch the mill again."

Tommy was a polite three year-old. He loved to touch everything his hands could reach. One day, he came across a door knob. He was fascinated. He reached out and touched the knob with his little finger. "It is so shiny," said Tommy. Suddenly he heard an angry voice from behind the door. "Don't touch that knob!" yelled the voice. It was an old man. "That knob is very precious to me. Don't touch it," he said. 

Tommy was frightened. He quickly stepped away from the door and said, "I'm sorry, I didn't mean any harm." But the old man was still angry. He opened the door and grabbed Tommy's arm. "I don't want you touching anything that belongs to me!" he said. Tommy started to cry. The old man finally let go and Tommy ran away. He never touched any door knobs again.

Once there was an apple tree. It was a big, beautiful tree. It had lots of tasty apples. Everyone wanted to eat the tasty apples, but they had to obey the law. 

One day, a little girl came to the tree. She wanted to eat the tasty apples. She asked the tree if she could use the apples. The tree said yes and the little girl was very happy.

The girl started to pick the apples. She picked one red apple, then two yellow apples and finally three green apples. The girl put all the apples in her basket. 

Then she went home and ate the tasty apples. She was so happy that she used the law and enjoyed the tasty apples from the tree.

Once upon a time, there were two friends, Jeev and Sandy. They were walking together on the beach when they saw something sparkling in the sand. Jeev ran to pick it up and found a beautiful shell. They were delighted!

Suddenly, Sandy said, â€œOh! letâ€™s give it to the gifted girl who lives by the beachâ€. Jeev smiled and both of them ran to the house.

When they reached there, they saw the girl and her mom. Jeev shyly went to her and said â€œPlease take this shell. Itâ€™s a gift from us. We saw it and we thought you might like it.â€

The girl smiled with joy and said, â€œThank you so much! I love it!â€

Jeev and Sandy were very happy to give this present to the gifted girl. They hugged each other and thanked God for such a wonderful day at the beach.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Bob. Bob had a passport that was very helpful. The passport helped him go to new places and make lots of friends. One day, Bob left his passport on the table when he went out to play.

When he came back, his passport was gone! Bob looked everywhere, but he couldnâ€™t find it. He asked his mom and dad if they had seen it, but they hadnâ€™t. Bob was sad, because he had lost his helpful passport.

Bobâ€™s mom and dad took Bob on a walk around the town, to see if he could find his passport. They asked the neighbors if they had seen it and looked in the shops and parks, but it was nowhere to be found. Bobâ€™s passport had disappeared!

But then, one day, Bobâ€™s mom got a call from the post office. They said they had found Bobâ€™s passport! Bob was so happy to get his passport back. He thanked the post office for being so helpful and never again left his passport behind.

Once there was a little, graceful boy. He wanted to join in on a race, so he went to the track. It was so fun because there were other children there too, ready to join in the race.

The little boy was very excited. He stood at the starting line and waited for the whistle to blow. When it did, he began to run with all the other children. He looked so graceful as he dashed around the track, running as fast as he could.

As he rounded the corner, he started to feel tired. He kept going, knowing that he was close to crossing the finish line. Finally, he was the first one to reach it! He was so proud of himself and all of the other children who participated in the race too. They had all done so well.

The little boy smiled. He had joined in on a race, and finished it first! He was very happy with himself. He knew that he had done his best, and it had paid off in the end.

Once upon a time, there lived a chubby little girl. Every day, she would skip around the park and take a look at the fire. She was mesmerised by its beauty and warmth. 

One day, she got a little too close to the fire and started to fill with fear. "Don't be scared," said an old man. "The fire won't hurt you."

The little girl thanked the old man for his kindness and asked why she was not scared of the fire. "Well, I can fill your heart with courage", he said, "by showing you how one can use fire to make beautiful things".

The old man showed the little girl how he could use fire to make cookies and cakes. The little girl smiled and had so much fun. The old man filled her heart with joy and it made her feel safe. 

From that day, the chubby little girl wasn't scared of the fire anymore. She knew how to use it in a safe and fun way.

John wanted to do something special. He kneeled down on the ground in the bright sunshine and closed his eyes. He reached out to the ground and felt around until he found a smooth lemon. He held it carefully in his hand and was amazed by how heavy it was. He smelled it, feeling the sweet and tart scent enter his nose.

John wanted to share the lemon with his family and he ran inside to show them. Inside, he found his mom and dad. He offered his lemon to them with a big smile. They both laughed, but felt excited about what John had done. It was not normal for a three-year-old child to find a lemon in someone's backyard. 

John was happy he found the lemon and felt proud he could share it with his family. Everyone gathered around and they enjoyed the crunchy and juicy lemon.

Tom and Sam are friends. They like to play football in the park. They have a red football and they kick it to each other.

One day, a big boy comes to the park. He sees Tom and Sam's football and he wants it. He runs to them and says, "Give me your football. It is mine now."

Tom and Sam are scared. They say, "No, it is our football. We were playing with it. Go away."

The big boy is angry. He pushes Tom and Sam and takes their football. He laughs and runs away.

Tom and Sam are sad. They want their football back. They cry and say, "He is mean. He took our football. We have nothing to play with."

A lady sees them and hears them. She is kind. She goes to them and says, "What is wrong? Why are you crying?"

Tom and Sam tell her what happened. They point to the big boy who is far away.

The lady is angry. She says, "That is not nice. He should not take your football. He should share. I will help you get your football back."

She takes Tom and Sam by the hand and walks to the big boy. She says, "Excuse me, that is not your football. You took it from these boys. They were playing with it. You should give it back."

The big boy is scared. He sees the lady and he knows he did wrong. He says, "Sorry, I was just joking. Here is your football."

He gives the football back to Tom and Sam. They are happy. They say, "Thank you, lady. You are nice. You helped us."

The lady says, "You are welcome, boys. You are good. You should play nicely and have fun."

Tom and Sam smile and hug the lady. They say, "We will. We are friends."

They take their football and go back to the park. They kick it to each other and laugh. They have fun.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a favorite tree in her yard. One day, she saw a leaf on the tree. It was not a real leaf, it was a fake leaf. Lily was sad because she loved her tree and hoped it would be okay.

Lily asked her mom, "Why does my tree have a fake leaf?" Her mom said, "Sometimes trees get sick, and we hope they will get better." Lily wanted to help her tree, so she took care of it every day. She gave it water and talked to it.

But one day, the tree was very sick. All the leaves fell down. Lily was very sad. She tried to make it better, but the tree did not grow new leaves. The tree died. Lily learned that sometimes, even when we hope and try our best, things don't always go the way we want.

Once there was a bird. He was having a lot of fun rolling down the hill. Every time he rolled he laughed and it made the sun shine.

But then the bird heard a scary noise. It was a loud roar and it was coming from the mountain. The bird was scared! He didn't know what it was.

Suddenly the bird saw something coming closer. It was big and round and rolling down the mountain. It was rolling so fast that it scared the bird even more!

But then the bird saw it was just a big ball. It was rolling down the hill and it wasn't scary at all. The bird laughed and played with the ball and rolled it back up the hill.

It was fun to watch the ball roll back to the top of the mountain. The bird was happy and he learned that sometimes things that seem scary are really just fun.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny named Benny. Benny liked to hop around and eat carrots. One day, Benny saw a big fence. He tried to jump over it, but it was too high. So, he decided to chew on it instead. The fence tasted like wood and Benny liked the sound it made when he chewed it.

As he was chewing, Benny saw a humble little mouse. The mouse was very shy and didn't like to talk to anyone. Benny wanted to be friends with the mouse, so he hopped over to say hello. The mouse was surprised and a little scared, but Benny was very friendly. They talked and played together for a while, and Benny even shared some of his carrots with the mouse.

After a fun day, Benny went back to his burrow. He was happy to have made a new friend and to have chewed on the fence. He fell asleep with a smile on his face, dreaming of more adventures to come.

Once upon a time, there was a goose named Gigi. Gigi was very sweet and loved to eat bread. One day, Gigi got hurt and had a boo-boo on her wing. 

Gigi's friend, a little girl named Lily, saw that Gigi was hurt and asked, "What happened, Gigi? Are you okay?" 

Gigi replied, "No, I am hurt. My wing hurts." 

Lily knew how to heal Gigi's boo-boo. She got a band-aid and put it on Gigi's wing. Gigi felt better and said, "Thank you, Lily. You are my best friend." 

From that day on, Gigi and Lily shared sweet bread together and played in the park. They were happy and had fun every day.

One day, a strong little girl named Tucker was playing in the park. She found a pair of sunglasses and put them on. 

Tucker said, "I am a princess!" 

The girl then sat on a bench and imagined she was a queen. She looked at her new sunglasses and said, "I'm so strong with these on!" 

Suddenly, a friendly voice came from behind. It said, "Those sunglasses look really cool on you!" 

Tucker spun around to see a kind old woman. The woman said, "I see you have some strong sunglasses, would you like a crown to go with them?" 

Tucker smiled and said, "Yes please!" 

The old woman gave her a shiny, pink crown and said, "You look like a real princess now!"

Tucker thanked the kind old woman and sat back down on the park bench with her new crown and sunglasses. She closed her eyes and imagined she was a powerful queen ruling her very own kingdom.

Once upon a time, there was a small fish called Tiny. Tiny had a big dream; she wanted to dive deep into the big ocean. So one day, Tiny took a deep breath and swam down to the bottom of the sea.

When she reached the bottom, Tiny saw something sparkly. She opened her eyes wide and saw a beautiful pearl. She quickly opened her small lips and grabbed the pearl. Then she started to swim back to the top.

Suddenly, Tiny was confronted by a big fish. He said, â€œPlease give me back my pearl!â€
Tiny replied, â€œBut I found it first!â€
The big fish said, â€œYou can keep it, but I must have something in exchange.â€

Tiny thought for a moment. Then she said, â€œLetâ€™s dive together!â€
The big fish smiled. â€œThat sounds like so much fun! You have a deal!â€

So Tiny and the big fish dove deep into the ocean. As they dove, they found all kinds of beautiful things. In the end, they had a wonderful adventure and kept the pearl as a reminder of it. And they remained friends forever after.

Once there was an elderly couple who lived in a small house. They wanted to celebrate something special. So, they went to their closet and opened it. Inside was a big box filled with treats and toys. The elderly couple were so excited. 

They put on the music and started to dance. They ate the treats and played with the toys. They laughed and smiled as they celebrated their special day. 
 
The elderly couple spent the whole day playing together. When night came, they put the toys and treats back in the closet. They hugged and said goodnight, still smiling from their fun celebration.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to play outside with his friends. One day, Timmy's mom told him to be obedient and follow the rules when he went outside. Timmy promised to be obedient and do what his mom said.

As Timmy was playing with his friends, they saw a big, scary dog. Timmy's friends wanted to run away, but Timmy remembered his promise to his mom. He stayed calm and slowly walked away from the dog. His friends followed his lead and they all stayed safe.

Later that day, Timmy's mom asked him how he was able to be so brave. Timmy replied, "My brain told me to be obedient and follow the rules, so I did." His mom was proud of him for being so smart and brave. From that day on, Timmy always listened to his brain and followed the rules.

One day, a modern car drove down the street. Inside the car was a brother and sister. As they drove, they heard a strange sound. They looked out the window, and saw a little puppy in a tree. 

The brother said to the sister, "Let's help that puppy!" He opened the car door and started walking towards the tree. 

But before he could get to the tree, a big dog appeared and barked loudly at the brother. The brother started to scream. The sister started to cry and ran back to the car.

The big dog was not done yet. It started running towards the car. The brother was running after it, trying to help the puppy. 

The car drove away, leaving the brother and puppy behind. The sister looked back from the window, and saw the brother scaring the big dog away with sticks. 

The puppy raced to the brother's arms and the brother screamed happily. The modern car welcomed them inside, and drove away into the sunset. 

The next day, news spread of the brave brother and the sound of his cries for help.

Once upon a time there was a girl called Amy. She loved pizza! One day, she made a big pizza all by herself and she was very proud. It looked yummy and she couldn't wait to eat it.

When it was ready, she called her friends to come over. Everyone was so excited! As soon as everyone gathered around the table, Amy settled the pizza in the middle. They all admired it for a minute and then started to chow down.

The pizza tasted so good! Everyone gobbled it up quickly, leaving not a single crumb behind. When they were finished, they all had big smiles on their faces.

Amy felt proud that she made the pizza all by herself. She was glad that her friends liked it! From then on, pizza became her favourite food to make.

Once upon a time there was a powerful rainbow in the sky. It shone brightly and made the sky very pretty. All the animals in the forest stopped to look at it. The animals could recognize that it was special.

The rainbow stayed in the sky all day and twinkled and sparkled. The birds were happy because they knew that the rainbow meant special things were coming. After a while, the rain came and the rainbow started to fade away.

But the animals had recognized that the rainbow was magical. So they gathered under it and as it got lighter and lighter, they knew that it meant good luck was coming! They all cheered as the rainbow faded away and then disappeared.

And so the magical rainbow brought lots of happiness to the animals in the forest!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved going on holiday with her family. They would go to the beach and play in the sand. One day, Lily's favorite toy, a teddy bear, broke. She was very sad and didn't know what to do.

Lily's mom asked her, "What's wrong, sweetie?" Lily replied, "My teddy bear is broken." Her mom said, "Don't worry, we can fix it." But Lily was still sad. Later that day, they went for a walk and saw a magician performing tricks. The magician made things disappear and reappear.

Lily was amazed and asked her mom, "Can the magician fix my teddy bear?" Her mom smiled and said, "Let's ask." They went up to the magician and asked him. The magician said, "Of course, I can make your teddy bear disappear and then reappear all fixed." Lily was so happy and couldn't wait to see her teddy bear again. The magician did his trick and just like that, Lily's teddy bear was fixed!

Once upon a time, there was a boy. He was curious and wanted to learn about the world. 

One night, he looked at the stars and asked his dad, "What do I value?" His dad said, "What you value is up to you. Think about what is really important." 

The next day, the boy went to the store. He saw so many things, like jars of peanut butter and boxes of cereal. He wanted them, but he remembered what his dad said. Finally, he chose a yogurt because it was healthy and he valued that.

At home, he sat down to eat his yogurt. But it was dull. He tried adding honey, but it didn't make it any more exciting. The boy looked around and then he saw a spoon with a rainbow handle. He used the spoon to eat his yogurt and it made the yogurt special. 

He smiled and thought to himself, "This is what I value - the things that make life interesting."

Once there was a dependable parrot named Bob. Bob loved to fly around the house and say hello to everyone. One day, Bob met a new friend, a dog named Fido.

Bob asked Fido, "Do you value me?"
Fido shook his head and said, "I do not value you, Bob. I have a few other friends that are more fun. You're not as exciting."

Bob was upset, so he told Fido, "I may not be as fun as your other friends, but I am always dependable. I will never let you down!"

Fido thought about it for a moment and then said, "You are right, Bob. I need someone dependable like you in my life. I value you now."

Bob smiled and said, "Thank you! I will always be there when you need me."

From that day forward, Bob and Fido were the best of friends. They would play together and value each other very much.

Once, there was a girl named Lucy. She was very wealthy and had a lot of friends. One day, Lucy decided to go explore a new forest. After some time, she came across a small house in the forest. She knocked on the door and welcomed by an old lady. The old lady invited her inside.

The old lady said, "I have a special powder that will make you very strong. Do you want to try it?" Lucy was so excited to try the powder. She said "Sure!"

The old lady gave her a spoonful of the powder. Lucy swallowed it and suddenly started trembling. She felt odd and then turned into a giant bug! Lucy was so scared and ran out of the house screaming.

Even though the old lady warned her not to try the powder, Lucy was so wealthy that she thought nothing bad could happen to her. Sadly, she was wrong.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Lucy. She loved going for walks in the woods and looking for berries. One day when she was out walking, she saw a big bush with lots of tasty berries on it. She couldn't resist trying one and soon discovered it was the tastiest berry she had ever eaten!

Lucy was so surprised to find a berry that tasted so good that she filled her basket with them. She brought them home and showed her mum. Her mum recognized that they were special berries and said they must be wild blackberries.

Lucy was delighted and couldn't wait to share the tasty berries with her family. They ate them all up and everyone agreed that they had great flavour. From that day on, Lucy was always on the lookout for more wild blackberries when she was out in the woods.

Once there was a little girl called Daisy. She was three years old. One day, Daisy was looking around her house. She saw that everything was yellow. She looked at her walls, her toys, her clothes and even the curtains!

Suddenly, Daisy noticed something that was not yellow. It was a quiz. She was very excited and asked for help from her mum. Daisy's mum explained that it was a quiz and it had lots of questions on it.

Daisy was thrilled and started looking in all the boxes to find a pencil and paper so she could do the quiz. She got a yellow pencil and a yellow piece of paper and started the quiz.

It had lots of questions about animals, shapes, numbers and colours. Daisy answered all the questions really cleverly. When she was finished, Daisy ran to her mum to show her the quiz and show her how many questions she got right.

Her mum was very proud of her. Daisy was very happy and hugged her mum tight.

Mommy was making a delicious cake. She was very careful as she stirred the mixture together. When she was finished, she paused and licked her lips.

"Mmm, this tastes amazing," she said.

Suddenly the door opened and little Teddy walked in. He grabbed a spoon from the table and started to dip it in the cake mixture.

"Teddy, no!" Mommy shouted. "We don't eat things before they're finished cooking."

Teddy pouted and walked away, dragging his feet in a loop around the kitchen. Mommy watched him as he went, feeling frustrated.

She paused for a moment, and then had an idea. She grabbed a few spoonfuls of the mixture and gave them to Teddy. He smiled, happy to have been given the treat. As he ate, a bit of the mixture got on his face, and Mommy had to do her best to keep from smiling.

"Delicious," Teddy said, licking his lips.

Mommy smiled and hugged Teddy. "Yes, it is," she said.

Once upon a time there was a chubby little boy named Jack. He loved to play outside and play with his best friend, Bob. Every day they would meet in the backyard and make up games.

One day, Jack and Bob decided to put on a show. Jack got a big, iron bow and tried to pull it back. But he was a very chubby little boy, and the bow was too heavy. Bob laughed and said, "Come on, Jack! You can do it!" So Jack tried and tried, until he managed to pull the bow back.

Jack and Bob put on the show for their family and friends. Everyone laughed and clapped when Jack shot the bow and hit the target. He was so happy with himself!

The next day, Jack and Bob decided to build a fort in the yard. Jack found a big sheet of iron and started to hammer it into the ground. Bob smiled and said, "Jack, I think you are getting good at this!"

Although Jack was chubby, he was strong. With Bob's help, they were able to build the fort together. From then on, Jack and Bob's backyard was the most popular place in town!

Mandy was walking home from school when she heard a loud noise coming from the jail. She stopped and looked around, but she couldn't quite figure out what it was.

So she decided to investigate. She tip-toed closer to the jail and looked through the bars. She saw a big cat that had slipped inside!

Mandy was so scared. She wanted to help the cat, but she also knew that she wasn't allowed near the jail. She didn't know what to do.

Suddenly, Mandy heard the jail guard coming. She quickly grabbed a broom and started shooing the cat. With one last loud meow, the cat slipped back out of the jail and ran away.

Mandy was so relieved. She was glad that she had been brave enough to help the cat escape.

Once upon a time, there was a little cricket named Jiminy. Jiminy loved to sing and play all day long. One day, Jiminy saw a big, hard rock that he wanted to climb. He tried and tried, but he couldn't climb it by himself.

Then, Jiminy saw a little ant who was also trying to climb the rock. The ant asked Jiminy if they could work together to climb the rock. Jiminy agreed and they both attached themselves to each other's backs. Together, they climbed the rock and reached the top.

Jiminy realized that sometimes it's better to work together with friends instead of trying to do everything alone. From that day on, Jiminy and the ant became best friends and always helped each other out. The moral of the story is that working together can help you achieve great things.

Once there was a little girl. She loved to go outside and zoom around on her bike. One day, when she was riding around in the park, something shiny caught her eye. It was a rare chocolate coin! She quickly hopped off her bike, scooped it up, and put it in her pocket. Then she zoomed around the park, looking for more. 

Sure enough, after some time had passed, she came across another shiny coin! This time though, it was a different color. She grabbed it and held it up to look closer. It was a rare purple chocolate! She giggled excitedly and pocketed it away. 

The little girl spent the rest of the day zooming around the park, but unfortunately she didn't find any more rare chocolates. She was disappointed. She returned home, her bike zooming along the pavement. She had so much fun that day and was so happy to have found the two rare chocolates. She went to bed dreaming of going out again tomorrow and finding even more chocolates!

Freddy was independent. He could do all sorts of things. He could count, he could read and he could zip up his own coat. 
One day, Freddy wanted to finish a big task. So he got to work, counting, reading and finishing all of the pieces. Soon he was done. 
Freddy was very surprised when his mom came in and said, "Well done, Freddy! You finished all by yourself! That was very independent of you!" 
Freddy was so happy he jumped up and down and gave his mom a big hug. He couldn't wait to show her all the other things he could do.

Once upon a time there was a mommy and her little girl. The mommy was very excited. She said, "Let's go do an operation! It'll be so fun!" 

The little girl didn't know what an operation was, but she was very excited too. She said, "What is an operation? Is it fun?"

The mommy laughed and said, "Yes, it's very fun. Let's go!"

The mommy and her little girl went to the doctor's office. They opened the door and went inside. The little girl was so excited! She saw toys in the doctor's office and said, "This looks so funny!" The mommy smiled and said, "That it does! Now let's get ready for our operation."

The doctor explained what the operation was and what it would do. Then he opened the tools and the little girl watched. When the operation was finished, the little girl felt very brave. She was happy she was able to help her mommy! 

The mommy and her little girl left the doctor's office. The little girl said, "That was so fun! Can we do it again?" 

The mommy smiled and said, "Maybe someday. For now, let's go get some ice cream!"

Once upon a time there lived a curious turtle, Larry. He lived in a big pond all by himself, and he wanted to explore more of the world. 

One day, he decided to go on an adventure. He said goodbye to his pond, and zoomed off! Everywhere he went, Larry was amazed. He felt the warm sun on his shell, and touched the cool water.

As he kept zooming, he noticed an ugly bug on the side of the road. The bug said "Hello, Larry! Where are you going?"

"I'm going exploring!" said Larry.

"Oh, that sounds like fun!" the bug replied. "Would you like me to come with you?"

Larry didn't hesitate - he said yes!

Then the two friends zoomed off together, exploring the world and having fun.

One day, a magical yellow snow began to spread. It was so light and sparkly that it made everything look like a fairytale. The children in the neighborhood were especially excited when they saw the snow. They went outside to play with it and made a huge snowman in the garden.

The yellow snow was so special that it was like a gift from the sky. Everyone was so happy to see it that they spent all day playing in it. Everyone was making snow angels and having snowball fights, and the day was really fun.

As the sun set, the yellow snow began to melt away. Everyone was a little sad to see it go, but they knew it would come back soon. The snow was like a little reminder of how magical the world can be.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Molly who looked out to sea. "I want to sail away," she said. She saw a big boat with a sail in the distance and she looked up at her dad. "Can we sail away?" she asked. Her dad smiled. "We can't sail away today, Molly," he said. "But one day we can when we have more money."

Molly wondered what it would be like to sail away. When they went to the beach, she looked out to see and saw some palm trees. She imagined that if she sailed away, she could go and explore the palm trees. 

Suddenly, Molly's dad got an idea. "I know! We can sail away," he said. He had seen an advertisement for an expensive boat to rent. It wasn't far away either.

Molly was so excited and hugged her dad. They set off to the boat and Molly watched as the wind filled up the sail. They waved goodbye to the beach and sailed away to explore the palm trees. As they sailed, Molly felt so excited that she had managed to make her dream come true.

John and his dad were walking along the beach. John liked looking at the waves roaring onto the shore and the sand between his toes. He loved the feeling of the wind on his cheeks.

His dad stopped and looked around, then he said, "John, can you do something for me?".

John was curious, "What do you need me to do?".

His dad smiled and said, "I need you to go on a march and supply some things".

John was excited, "What kind of things?".

His dad gestured to a box he had been carrying. "This box is full of things that will help the people on the march, so I need you to carry it for me".

John was ready for the march. He started walking down the beach, with his dad close behind him. Soon the sand became rough, like small stones. The wind started to pick up, like it was warning John that something was coming. 

John's dad put his hand on his shoulder and said, "Remember what I told you, ok? You have to supply the things in the box to everyone on the march."

John nodded and kept walking. Little did John know, this march would be the most important of his life.

Ben is a dog. He likes to play with his bone. He has a big bone and a small bone. He likes the big bone more. He puts the big bone in his bed.

One day, Ben hears a loud ring. It is the door. Ben runs to the door. He barks. He wants to see who is there. He leaves his big bone in his bed.

Lily is a cat. She lives next door. She sees Ben run to the door. She is sneaky. She jumps over the fence. She goes to Ben's bed. She sees the big bone. She likes bones too. She takes the big bone in her mouth. She runs away.

Ben comes back from the door. He is sad. There is no one there. He goes to his bed. He wants his big bone. But his big bone is gone. He sees his small bone. He does not want his small bone. He wants his big bone. He smells the air. He smells Lily. He knows Lily took his big bone. He is angry. He barks loud. He chases Lily.

Lily hears Ben. She is scared. She runs fast. But Ben runs faster. He catches Lily. He takes his big bone back. He growls. Lily drops the big bone. She runs away. She does not like Ben.

Ben is happy. He has his big bone again. He goes to his bed. He puts his big bone in his bed. He lies down. He chews his big bone. He does not hear the loud ring anymore. He is a good dog.

Once upon a time, there was a cool car. It had a big motor. The car was red and shiny. It liked to go fast. The car had a friend, a little boy named Tim.

One day, Tim and the cool car went for a ride. They went to the park. Tim played with his ball. The cool car watched him. They had a lot of fun.

Suddenly, Tim had to sneeze. "Achoo!" he sneezed. The cool car giggled. They laughed together. Tim and the cool car were happy friends. They played in the park until it was time to go home.

Tom and Sam are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a pond with many fish. The fish are big and small, red and blue, yellow and green. Tom and Sam want to look at the fish.

"Can we go near the pond?" Tom asks Sam.

"Yes, but we have to be careful. The pond is deep and wet. We do not want to fall in." Sam says.

Tom and Sam walk to the pond. They sit on the grass and watch the fish. The fish swim and jump in the water. They make bubbles and splash. Tom and Sam laugh and clap.

"Look, that fish is funny. It has a long nose and a big mouth." Tom says.

"I know, it looks like a duck. Quack, quack!" Sam says.

They pretend to be fish and ducks. They make noises and faces. They have fun.

A man comes to the pond. He has a bucket and a net. He wants to catch some fish. He sees Tom and Sam.

"Hello, boys. Do you like fish?" He asks.

"Yes, we like fish. They are pretty and fun." Tom says.

"Would you like to help me catch some fish? You can take one home and keep it as a pet." He says.

Tom and Sam look at each other. They think about the fish. They like the fish, but they do not want to hurt them. They do not want to take them away from their home.

"No, thank you. We do not want to catch fish. We like to watch them in the pond. They are happy here." Sam says.

The man shrugs and walks away. He looks for another spot to fish. Tom and Sam stay by the pond. They are glad they did not catch fish. They are glad they let the fish be free. They are glad they are friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved flowers and had a big vase in her room. One day, her friend Timmy came to visit. "Look at my vase!" Lily said, pointing to the colorful flowers inside. "Wow, that's so pretty!" Timmy said, enthusiastic about the flowers.

Suddenly, there was a knock on the door. It was Lily's mom, who had arrived home from work. "Hi, Mom!" Lily said, running to give her a hug. "What a beautiful vase you have!" her mom exclaimed. "Thank you!" Lily said, beaming with pride.

Later that day, Lily and Timmy played outside. "I'm so happy you came to visit," Lily said. "Me too," Timmy replied, enthusiastic about spending time with his friend. As the sun began to set, Timmy's mom arrived to pick him up. "Goodbye, Lily!" Timmy said, waving goodbye. "Goodbye, Timmy!" Lily said, waving back. She couldn't wait to show him her vase again the next time he visited.

Tim and his mom went to the park. Tim liked to play with the swings and the slide. He saw a big dog with a leash. The dog was brown and had long hair. Tim thought the dog was ugly.

"Mom, can I pet the dog?" Tim asked.

"No, Tim, you don't know the dog. He might bite you," Mom said.

"But he looks nice. He has a leash. He can't run away," Tim said.

"That doesn't mean he is nice, Tim. The leash is for the owner to manage the dog, not for you to pet him. Come on, let's go to the sandbox," Mom said.

Tim was sad. He wanted to pet the dog. He followed Mom to the sandbox. He saw another dog there. The dog was small and white and had short hair. Tim thought the dog was cute.

"Mom, can I pet this dog?" Tim asked.

"Yes, Tim, you can. This dog belongs to our friend Lily. She is here with her dad. The dog is friendly and likes children. But you have to ask Lily first," Mom said.

Tim ran to Lily and her dad. He asked if he could pet the dog. Lily said yes. She gave Tim the leash. Tim petted the dog. The dog licked his face. Tim was happy. He liked the dog. He thanked Lily and gave her back the leash.

"See, Tim, not all dogs are the same. Some are ugly and some are cute. Some are nice and some are not. You have to be careful and ask before you pet them," Mom said.

"I understand, Mom. I like cute and nice dogs. I don't like ugly and not nice dogs," Tim said.

"Good, Tim. Now let's go have some ice cream," Mom said.

Tim and his mom left the park. They had a good day.

Once upon a time, there was a big, graceful cat. The cat had pretty, soft fur. One day, the cat saw a shiny copper toy. The cat wanted to play with the toy. But, the toy was in a small house.

The cat tried to enter the small house. But, the door was too little. The cat could not go in. The cat was sad. The cat wanted the copper toy so much.

Then, the cat saw a big dog. The dog was strong. The cat asked the dog for help. The dog pushed the small house. The house fell down. The cat got the shiny copper toy. The cat and the dog were happy. They played with the toy together.

Once upon a time, there was a fat bunny who loved to play in the garden. One day, he found a folder filled with colourful pieces of paper. He wanted to see what was inside. He hopped around the folder and tried to tear it open. 

Suddenly, he heard a voice. "Hey! Don't do that!" 

The bunny looked up and saw a big bear. He was holding a bunch of folders in his big, furry paws. "It's my work," said the bear. "Please don't tear it."

The bunny felt very sorry. He bowed his head and said, "I'm sorry. I'll put it back."

The bear smiled. "It's okay. Here, I'll give you one of my folders. You can open it without tearing it up."

The bunny was delighted! He held the folder carefully and took it home. He felt glad that he had been able to make the bear happy with his good behaviour.

Once upon a time there was a boy who had a friend. His friend was always very helpful. One day, the boy wanted to do something but didn't know how to do it. His friend said, "I can help you do it!" The boy was so happy and asked, "Will you allow me to try?" His friend said, "Yes, but only for one minute."

The boy was so excited and started doing what he wanted to do. He worked hard and used his minute to the best of his ability. At the end, the boy thanked his friend for being helpful and allowing him to try. Everyone was happy. 

The moral of the story is that it is always helpful to allow someone a chance to do something before judging them.

John and his mom were walking down the road. Suddenly, John started to jog, but his mom told him to stop.

John's mom said, "John, jogging isn't allowed here. You can get hurt!"

John replied, "But mom, it's so much fun! Let me just jog for a little bit!"

His mom thought for a moment and said, "Okay John, but we won't be jogging for long. It's too cold outside."

John and his mom started jogging. They both held hands and laughed. Suddenly, John saw something on the ground. He stopped to pick it up and found an eraser!

John smiled and said, "Mom, look at this! I can keep this and play with it later."

John's mom smiled and said, "That's great, John. Now, let's go jogging together one last time before we go inside."

So, John and his mom jogged one more time around the block with John holding his eraser. Then they said goodbye to the cold weather and ran inside.

Ben and Mia liked to play in the kitchen. They liked to open the drawers and look at the spoons and forks. They liked to open the fridge and smell the cheese and milk. But they did not like the big cupboard where Mom kept the cans and jars. Mom said it was dangerous and they should not touch it. She put a lock on it so they could not open it.

One day, Ben and Mia were very hungry. They wanted a snack. They looked in the fridge and saw an avocado. They liked avocado. It was green and soft and yummy. They took the avocado and a knife and went to the table. They tried to cut the avocado, but it was hard. They pushed and pushed, but the knife did not go in. They got angry and frustrated.

They decided to use the big cupboard. Maybe there was something in there that could help them. They looked at the lock. It was shiny and round. They wondered how it worked. They tried to twist it and pull it, but it did not move. They got more angry and frustrated.

They saw a hammer on the floor. It was heavy and metal. They thought it could break the lock. They picked up the hammer and swung it at the lock. But they were clumsy and missed. The hammer hit the cupboard door and made a loud bang. The door broke and fell off. The cans and jars fell out and rolled on the floor. Some of them broke and spilled. There was a big mess.

Mom heard the noise and came running. She saw Ben and Mia and the broken cupboard and the cans and jars and the avocado and the knife and the hammer. She was shocked and angry and scared. She yelled at Ben and Mia and told them to go to their room. She said they were naughty and careless and could have hurt themselves. She said they could not play in the kitchen anymore. She said they had to clean up the mess.

Ben and Mia felt sorry and sad. They did not mean to make a mess. They just wanted to eat the avocado. They said they were sorry and helped Mom clean up. They hugged Mom and said they loved her. Mom hugged them back and said she loved them too. She said they could have some avocado later, but only if she cut it for them. She said they should never touch the lock or the hammer or the knife again. They said they would not. They learned their lesson.

Once upon a time, there was a big, green field. On this field, there was a soft, yellow playground. Every day, many happy players would come to play. They would run, jump and act!

One day, a new player came to the playground. His name was Peter. Peter was a bit shy, so he watched all the other kids for a while. Eventually, he decided to join in the fun.

Peter started running around, jumping on the warm, soft grass. He watched the other kids play and laughed at their funny games. Soon enough, Peter joined the group and began acting in their play. 

The other kids were so glad that Peter was playing with them. They were always smiling and they accepted him with open arms. With all the kids together, the playground felt so full of joy and happiness. Peter had a great time playing with his new friends.

Once there was a girl named Lizzy and she hated nails. Every time she saw them she screamed and ran away. She liked all of the other things around her, but she just didn't like nails.

One day Lizzy and her mommy went to the store to buy some things. Suddenly she saw a big box of nails and she ran away and hid in the corner. Her mommy saw her and asked her why she was so scared.

Lizzy told her mommy that she hated nails and mommy laughed. She said that that was crazy because nails can actually be useful.

Lizzy didn't understand but she still didn't like them. Her mommy said that if Lizzy tried to like them and understand why they were useful, she could learn to like them and even use them for fun things. Lizzy thought about this, and decided to give it a try.

The next day, Lizzy and her mommy went to the store again, and this time Lizzy wasn't scared at all when she saw the box of nails. She even picked up some of them and tried to use them. Pretty soonLizzy was having lots of fun making her own projects with nails.

From then on, Lizzy no longer hated nails. She even loved them and thought they were so much fun!

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Daisy. Daisy loved to play in the rain. She always asked her mum if she could unlock the door to go outside, but her mum said no.

One day, Daisy's mum said that she could go out for a few minutes and play in the rain. Daisy was so excited! She put on her raincoat and opened the door.

When Daisy stepped outside, she saw a big, dark cloud. The wind was blowing hard, so Daisy had to close the door. She looked up and saw that the cloud was bringing rain.

Daisy was so polite and said thank you to the cloud. She watched as the rain hit the ground and heard the wonderful sound. Suddenly, Daisy realised that she had left the door unlocked and ran back inside. 

But it was too late. Daisy's mum was so angry and Daisy had been so naughty. Daisy had to stay inside for the rest of the day and she was not allowed to go out again. 

The end.

Once there was a tiny fish swimming in the sea. He was helpless, so he asked the other fish for help. One fish recommended that he get a spear. The fish was so grateful so he went to find a spear.

He eventually found one and it was bigger than he was! But he was determined, so he grabbed it with his fins and set off on an adventure.

He soon realized that the spear was actually helping him. He could use it to catch food and protect himself from predators. He felt so much more confident and safe.

The tiny fish was so happy with his spear, he thanked all the other fish for recommending it to him. He was no longer helpless, thanks to his spear.

Once upon a time, there was a deaf stitch. His name was Tony and he lived alone in a small house by a river. One day, he decided he wanted to go exploring. As he walked along the river, he heard some funny noises coming from the other side.

When he got there, he saw a group of birds, who were singing to each other. Every now and again, one of them would stop and keep talking. Tony thought it was very interesting.

He was so captivated by their sounds, he almost forgot why he came. Then he saw a large nest in the trees above. Sitting in the middle of it, was a small bird. Tony noticed it had a stitch in its wing.

He decided to try and help the small bird. He reached up, carefully pulled the stitch out and kept talking to the little bird. Tonyâ€™s soothing voice seemed to comfort the bird and soon it was calm enough for Tony to help it fly again. 

"Thank you!" the bird said, when Tony put it safely back in the nest. 

Tony smiled, happy to have helped. He watched as the bird flew away, then waved goodbye as he headed back home.

Lily liked to play in the garden. She liked to look for bugs and flowers. One day, she saw a cricket on a leaf. It was light green and had long legs. Lily wanted to catch it.

"Hello, cricket," she said. "Can I be your friend?"

The cricket did not answer. It made a loud noise with its wings. Lily reached out her hand to touch it, but the cricket jumped away.

"Wait, cricket, don't go!" Lily said. She ran after it, but the cricket was too fast. It jumped from leaf to leaf, and then it hid under a rock.

Lily was sad. She sat on the grass and sighed. She wished she had a friend to play with.

Then, she heard a voice behind her. It was Ben, her brother. He was holding a jar with some dirt and grass in it.

"Hi, Lily," he said. "What are you doing?"

"I was looking for a cricket, but it ran away," Lily said.

"Really? I have a cricket in my jar. Do you want to see it?"

Lily nodded. She got up and followed Ben to his jar. He opened the lid and showed her the cricket. It was brown and had short legs.

"This is my cricket," Ben said. "I found it in the woods. It likes to eat leaves and seeds. Do you want to hold it?"

Lily was curious. She reached out her hand and Ben gently put the cricket on her palm. It tickled her skin and made a soft noise.

"It's nice," Lily said. "Can I keep it?"

Ben smiled. He liked to share with his sister.

"Sure, you can keep it. But you have to take good care of it. You have to give it food and water and a place to sleep. And you have to let it grow."

Lily nodded. She was happy. She had a new friend to play with.

"Thank you, Ben," she said. "You are the best brother ever."

Ben hugged her. He was happy, too.

"You're welcome, Lily," he said. "You are the best sister ever."

Once upon a time, there was a little green jar. One day, the jar was sitting on a counter and thinking. All of a sudden, a little girl walked into the room.

"What are you doing?" the little girl asked the jar.

"I'm thinking," the jar said.

The little girl thought for a moment. "What do you think?" she asked.

The jar was silent for a moment, then said, "I think about the world and the things I can do to help it."

The little girl smiled. "That's so nice," she said. Then she hugged the jar and said, "Thank you for your kind thoughts."

The jar smiled and felt happy. From that day on, the little jar kept thinking and doing nice things in the world.

Once upon a time there lived a little monkey in a beautiful jungle. He was so excited to go outside and explore! But as he was taught by his parents, he needed to wait. He had to delay his adventure because his mom said it was not safe.

Soon, he was surrounded by other little animals in the jungle. There were rabbits, foxes, deer, and even bigger animals like tigers and elephants. The little monkey was so curious he just couldn't wait anymore! He wanted to see and explore the jungle.

The little monkey ventured out, hiding behind trees and bushes to avoid the big animals. The sun was shining and it was a beautiful day. He made friends with the animals and soon discovered wonderful things in the jungle. There were caves, fruit trees, and rippling streams, and it was all so exciting!

The little monkey stayed all day exploring the jungle. As the sun began to set and the sky became dark his mom called. She had been waiting for some time, but was very proud and happy to see the little monkey explore with the animals.

Bob looked up at the sky. The clouds were in the shape of animals and the sun was so bright and beautiful. Bob loved to look at the sky.

Bob and his dad drove to the mechanic's shop. His dad's car needed to get fixed. Bob loved going to the mechanic's shop. There were so many interesting looking things there.

The mechanic was very kind. He fixed the car quickly. When the mechanic told them how much it would cost, Bob's dad was very happy because he was very wealthy and could pay the mechanic easily.

When the car was fixed, Bob and his dad drove home. Bob was very happy they had the mechanic to fix the car. He was glad they could be home safe and sound.

One day, Jax wanted to go to the beach and have a great time. He was so excited and couldn't wait to get there.

When Jax arrived at the beach, he got all his stuff together. He went to the water and started playing in the waves. He had so much fun and splashed around for a long time.

Suddenly, Jax noticed he was all wet and covered in sand from head to toe. He felt embarrassed and didn't know what to do.

He called out to his mom, "Mom! I'm all wet and sandy!"

Her mom smiled and said kindly, "It's okay, Jax. Just come here and I'll help you wash off all this stuff."

Jax happily ran over and his mom helped him wash off all the sand and get cleaned up. After he was all clean and dry, he thanked his mom for helping him and ran off to have more fun at the beach.

Once upon a time there was an cool dragon. It loved to explore and fly around the world. One day it came across a peaceful village and decided to settle there. It made its home in a cave near the village. Everyone was very excited to have a dragon living close by!

The dragon was so friendly and kind, it helped the villagers with all sorts of tasks. It flew high up in the sky to collect clouds for rain, and loved playing hide and seek with the children. On hot days it cooled down the village by blowing a gentle breeze.

The villagers were so happy to have their dragon friend. They even threw a special party for it! The dragon had a wonderful time, and settled back in its cave when the night ended.

The dragon and the villagers became good friends. And to this day, he still visits the village, bringing cool winds and fun adventures.

Once upon a time there was a boy called Max. He was three years old and loved to explore his garden. 
One day, Max decided to take a trip. So he put on his walking boots and set off on an adventure. 
Max soon came across an oasis. It looked so cool and inviting, and he suddenly felt really thirsty. But when Max went closer, he saw something scary. Suddenly, he heard a low growling sound. Max was scared and quickly stepped back.

Turns out that the oasis was a home to a lion! The lion let out a big roar and Max lay on the ground, pretending to be asleep. The lion was actually just hungry and was looking for food. After a few minutes, the lion left and Max got up. 
He had learnt an important lesson - never believe a lie!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a pony named Sparky. Sparky was very tidy and always kept his mane and tail clean. 

One day, Lily and Sparky went for a walk in the forest. They saw a squirrel who was gathering nuts. Lily said, "Hello Mr. Squirrel, where are you going?" The squirrel replied, "I am going to my home in the tree, but it is messy and I cannot find my nuts." 

Lily said, "I can help you find your nuts, and we can tidy up your home too." So, they went to the squirrel's tree and found all the nuts. They also cleaned up the mess and made the tree very tidy. The squirrel was very happy and said, "Thank you so much, Lily and Sparky. You are very kind." 

Lily and Sparky went home feeling happy that they could help someone. They also learned that it is always good to help others and make things tidy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to eat candy and play outside. One day, she found a shiny penny on the ground. "Look, Mommy! I found a penny!" she said.

"That's great, Lily. Where did you find it?" her mommy asked.

"I found it by the tree," Lily replied. 

Suddenly, Lily slipped on a banana peel and fell down. "Ouch! That hurt," she said.

Her mommy helped her up and asked, "Are you okay, Lily?"

"Yes, I'm okay. But can we go home now? I want to eat some of that delicious candy you bought yesterday," Lily said with a smile.

Mia and Leo loved to play with their toy elephant. It was big and gray and soft, and it had a long nose that could make funny sounds. They liked to hug it and pretend it was their friend.

One day, they had a new idea. They tied a string around the elephant's nose and hung it from the ceiling. Then they took turns pulling the string and making the elephant spin. They laughed and clapped as they watched the elephant go round and round.

"Look, it's a brilliant elephant!" Mia said. "It's so shiny and sparkly!"

Leo agreed. He thought the elephant looked like a star. He pulled the string harder and faster, and the elephant spun faster and faster.

But then, something bad happened. The string broke and the elephant fell to the floor. Mia and Leo gasped and ran to the elephant. They were afraid it was hurt.

They picked up the elephant and checked it. It was still big and gray and soft, but its nose was bent and twisted. It could not make funny sounds anymore.

Mia and Leo felt sad and sorry. They hugged the elephant and said they were sorry. They wished they had not made it spin so fast.

They decided to take the elephant to their mom. Maybe she could fix it. They hoped she would not be mad at them. They learned their lesson. They would not play with the elephant like that again. They would be gentle and kind. They still loved their brilliant elephant.

One day, a hunter was walking through the forest. He was looking for something to bring back home. Suddenly, he heard a noise in the bushes. He stopped to listen. It sounded like something was in trouble.

The hunter saw a little bunny tangled in a bush. He carefully took the bunny out of the bush and held it in his hands. The bunny was embarrassed, but the hunter was very kind. He talked to the bunny and made it feel safe.

The hunter brought the bunny back home with him. He hugged the bunny tight and got it some food. He made sure it was happy and comfortable. The bunny was so grateful that the hunter came along and saved it. 

After that, the hunter and the bunny were best friends. The hunter would often bring food for the bunny and take long walks together. They were never embarrassed when they were together. They were happy to be friends forever.

Sara and Ben were playing in the park. They liked to run and jump and slide. They saw a big hill with a lot of trees. They wanted to go up and see what was there.

"Let's go, Sara!" Ben said. "Maybe we can find a secret cave or a treasure!"

"OK, Ben!" Sara said. "But we have to be back before dark. Mommy said so."

They ran up the hill, holding hands. They saw many flowers and birds and bugs. They heard a stream and followed it. They found a big rock with a hole in it.

"Look, Sara! A cave!" Ben said. "Let's go inside!"

Sara was scared. She saw a lot of mist coming out of the hole. She smelled something terrible. She heard a growl.

"Ben, I don't want to go in there!" Sara said. "It's too dark and scary! Maybe there is a monster!"

Ben laughed. He was not scared. He wanted to be brave and have fun. He let go of Sara's hand and ran into the hole.

"Ben, wait!" Sara cried. "Come back!"

But Ben did not come back. He went deeper into the cave. He saw a big shadow and two red eyes. He heard a loud roar. He felt a hot breath and sharp teeth.

He screamed. He was sorry. He regretted going into the cave. He wished he had listened to Sara.

Sara heard Ben scream. She was very worried. She wanted to help him. She ran into the hole. She saw the monster. It was a big bear. It was angry and hungry. It had Ben in its mouth.

Sara was brave. She picked up a stick and hit the bear. She yelled at it. She made it drop Ben. She grabbed Ben's hand and ran out of the cave.

They ran down the hill, back to the park. They were hurt and dirty and scared. They cried and hugged each other.

They saw Mommy waiting for them. She was angry and worried. She saw their wounds and clothes. She asked them what happened.

They told her everything. They said they were sorry. They said they regretted going into the cave. They said they learned their lesson.

Mommy was glad they were safe. She was proud they were brave. She hugged them and kissed them. She took them home. She cleaned their wounds and gave them cookies. She told them she loved them.

They said they loved her too. They said they would never go into a cave again. They said they would always listen to her and to each other. They said they were happy to be home.

Once upon a time there was a very colorful history book. It was filled with lots of stories about past events and people. John was a three year old boy who liked to poke the book with his fingers. Whenever he poked the book, colorful pictures and words would appear. 

John would poke near a picture of a historic building, and suddenly a drawing of the building in color would appear on the page. Then, he would poke near a sentence and it would suddenly gain colorful illustrations and words to help John understand the meaning.
 
John loved to poke the history book. It made regular words suddenly turn into colorful stories!

Once upon a time, there was a very special girl. She had a dream to find something special. So, one day she decided to go on a search. She picked up her pretty bag and set off into the distant fields.

As she walked, the girl looked around and picked the prettiest wildflowers. She strolled further, searching everywhere. Then, she spotted something sparkling in the grass!

She bent down and picked it up. It was a pretty butterfly! She watched it flutter around in the sunshine. After a few moments, it flew away into the distant sky.

The girl quickly put the butterfly back where she had found it and continued on her search. After a while, she eventually found what she had been looking for - a special, shiny stone.

The girl smiled and put the stone in her bag. She was very happy that she had found the stone and was so glad she had gone on her search. She skipped home singing a happy tune.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Emily. Emily was three years old, and she loved playing with her stuffed animals.

One day, Emily's mom asked her to go to the store to buy an egg. Emily was very excited! She grabbed her purse and wrapped it up tightly. 

On the way to the store, Emily saw a little bird sitting on a tree branch. The bird greeted Emily and said,"Hello Emily! I'll show you a secret if you come this way." 

Emily smiled and followed the little bird. As they continued walking, Emily noticed a basket of eggs on the grass. She picked one up and wrapped it up in her purse.

The little bird explained, "The egg you picked is a magical egg. Tonight, if you wrap it up tightly in a blanket, something wonderful will happen!" 

 Emily happily went home and specialy wrapped the egg in a blanket and placed it under her pillow. That night, Emily fell asleep and when she woke up, something amazing had happened! All of her stuffed animals had come to life and were dancing around her bedroom. 

Emily was so happy! She thanked the little bird for showing her the magical egg. From that day forward, Emily never went to the store without her magical egg by her side.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved going to the park with her mommy and daddy. One day, they went to the store to buy Lily a new toy. Her mommy found a cheap doll that she thought Lily would love. 

Lily played with her new doll all day long until it was time for bed. She hugged her doll tightly and fell asleep. The next day, Lily's mommy had to go to work, so Lily and her daddy went to the park. They played on the swings and slides until the day started to end. 

As the sun set and the day came to an end, Lily and her daddy headed back home. Lily was tired from playing and fell asleep on the way home, still holding her new doll. When they arrived home, Lily's daddy carried her to bed and tucked her in with her doll. She smiled and slept soundly, dreaming of the fun day she had with her daddy.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim was a very obedient boy. He always listened to his mom and dad. One day, Tim had a bad dream, also called a nightmare. He woke up feeling scared and sad.

Tim went to his mom and told her about the nightmare. His mom hugged him and said, "Don't worry, Tim. I will help you wipe away the bad dream." She took a soft cloth and gently wiped Tim's face, as if she was wiping away the bad dream.

After that, Tim felt much better. He knew that his mom would always be there to help him. So, he went back to bed and had a good night's sleep. From that day on, whenever Tim had a nightmare, he would remember his mom's words and feel safe and loved.

Once there was a little girl named Lucy who loved to explore and find new things. One day she was walking in the park when she saw a big box full of kittens. The kittens were so cute and Lucy felt so excited.

Once upon a time, there was a big, strong oak tree. It lived in a big forest with lots of other trees and animals. One day, a wild storm came and the wind blew very hard. Sam likes to create things with paper and glue. He makes cards, hats, and animals. One day, he wants to create a wallet for his dad. He finds some white paper and cuts it into a rectangle. He folds it and glues it together. He draws a picture of his dad and himself on the front.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny named Bounce. Bounce loved to hop and jump all around the meadow. One day, Bounce saw a big balloon floating in the sky. Once upon a time, there was a jolly little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to climb things. One day, he saw a big shelf in his room. It was very tall and had lots of toys on it. Timmy wanted to climb the shelf to get his favorite toy, a little red car.

Once upon a time, there was a grumpy bear who wanted to go on a trip. He packed his bag and set off into the woods. He walked for a long time until he found a nice spot to settle down and rest.
