One day, Bob saw some children playing in the snow. He wanted to join in. He quickly got ready to play.

But then, something strange happened. A gust of wind blew the snow away! Bob had to hurry to catch up with the children. He ran as fast as he could. But the wind blew faster than Bob.

The townspeople were sad. They were jealous of the wind for taking Bob away. It was too late; Bob was gone.

But when the snow came back, so did Bob! The townspeople were so happy! They hugged and cheered.

Bob had come back! They all played together in the snow. Hurray!

Once upon a time, there was a big tree in a garden. The tree had many branches and leaves. One day, a little girl came to the garden. She saw the big tree and wanted to climb it. But the branches were too high and she couldn't reach them. 

Then, an old man came and saw the little girl. He said, "I can lead you to a ladder so you can climb the tree." The little girl was happy and followed the old man. He showed her a ladder and helped her climb up. 

When the little girl reached the top of the tree, she saw some fruits. They were big and red. She wanted to eat them, but they were too high. The old man said, "I can prune the branches so the fruits will fall down." He took a big knife and cut the branches. The fruits fell down and the little girl was happy. She ate them all and laughed loud.

Once there was a little girl who loved purple. Everything she owned was purple - her dress, her shoes and even her oven. The oven was special because she used it to make all kinds of delicious treats.

One day, she decided to make a cake. She carefully placed the cake mix in the oven, closed the door and made a special request. â€œOven, bake me a delicious cake please!â€ she said.

The oven worked hard and heated up to an extra special temperature. As it baked the cake, it turned a lovely purple color. The little girl was so excited to see her cake that she opened the oven door before it was finished. â€œOh no!â€ she said when she saw the cake. But it still tasted delicious!

Lily liked to play with her dolls. She had many dolls, but her favorite was Anna. Anna had long hair, a pink dress, and a green hat. Lily believed that Anna was a real princess, and she liked to make up stories about her adventures.

One day, Lily and Anna went to the park with Mommy. Lily saw a big slide and wanted to try it. She asked Mommy to hold Anna while she climbed up the ladder. Mommy said yes, but she told Lily to be careful and not to let go of the bars.

Lily reached the top of the slide and looked down. It was very high and very fast. She felt scared, but she wanted to be brave like Anna. She said to herself, "Anna can do it, so can I." She put her finger on her nose and made a wish. She wished that Anna would be with her and help her slide down.

She let go of the bars and slid down the slide. She felt the wind in her hair and the sun on her face. She smiled and laughed. She did it! She was brave like Anna!

She reached the bottom of the slide and looked for Mommy and Anna. She saw Mommy, but she did not see Anna. She felt sad and worried. Where was Anna? She ran to Mommy and asked, "Mommy, where is Anna? I want Anna!"

Mommy smiled and pointed to her head. She said, "Lily, Anna is here. She is always with you. You just have to believe. She is your friend, and she loves you."

Lily touched her head and felt something soft and green. She pulled it out and saw Anna's hat. She gasped and smiled. She found Anna! She hugged the hat and said, "Thank you, Mommy! Thank you, Anna! I love you both!"

Mommy hugged Lily and said, "I love you too, Lily. You are my brave princess."

Jill and Jack were very excited. It was time to go on holiday. Jackie packed her bag with her toy animals and her favourite books. Jill packed her comfy blanket, a plastic bucket and spade and a cuddly toy.

Jackie was so eager to start their holiday that he couldn't stop jumping up and down. â€œAre we nearly there yet?â€ he asked.

â€œNo, not yet,â€ said Jill, â€œWe need to get on the plane first, but that wonâ€™t take long.â€

After a short flight, Jackie and Jill were soon in a new, exciting place. 

They stayed in a big, comfortable hotel and went out to explore. Everywhere they looked there were amazing sights and sounds.

At the end of the day, Jackie and Jill packed their suitcases and said goodbye to the hotel. They said goodbye to the new place and started their journey home.

Once upon a time, there were two good friends, a boy and a girl. They were best friends and were always supporting each other. 

One day, the girl wanted to climb the high tree in the garden. She was scared to climb on her own so she asked her friend to support her. The boy was happy to help her. He held her hands and said, "Don't be scared. I will support you."

The girl slowly began to climb the tree. But as she was climbing, she slipped and started to cry. Her friend said, "Don't worry, we will find a way to get you down." 

The boy then had an idea. He went inside and brought some vanilla ice cream. He put the ice cream on a plate with a spoon and showed it to the girl. She smiled, because it was her favorite flavor. 

The boy then asked the girl if she wanted him to help her descend the tree. She said yes, and he carefully held her and helped her get down from the tree. When she was safe on the ground, she hugged her friend and said, "Thank you for supporting me."

They both smiled and enjoyed the delicious ice cream together.

Tom and Mia were best friends. They liked to play in the park every day. They had a big red ball that they threw to each other. They also liked to look at the sky and see the sun, the clouds and the moon.

One night, they decided to stay up late and watch the moon. They put on their coats and hats and went outside. They saw the moon shining bright and white. They were happy and excited.

But then, they saw a big black dog running towards them. It was barking loud and scary. Tom and Mia were afraid. They hugged each other and ran back to the house. They knocked on the door and shouted for help.

Their mom opened the door and let them in. She saw the dog and yelled at it. The dog stopped and ran away. Their mom hugged them and said they were brave. She said the dog was not nice and wanted to take their ball.

Tom and Mia were glad they were safe. They thanked their mom and gave her a kiss. They said they were loyal to each other and would never surrender their ball. They looked out the window and saw the moon smiling at them. They smiled back and went to bed. They dreamed of playing in the park again.

One day, a little boy named Tim went to the park with his mom. Tim saw a big, light ball in the sky. He was so happy and started to laugh. He jumped and pointed at the ball. His mom smiled and said, "That's the sun, Tim!"

At the park, Tim saw a little girl named Sue. Sue was playing with a toy car. Tim wanted to play with the car too. But Sue didn't want to share. Tim felt sad and stopped laughing. He looked at his mom and she said, "It's okay, Tim. Let's find something else to play with."

Tim and his mom walked around the park. They found a big, red ball. Tim picked it up and threw it high in the air. The ball went up, up, up and then came back down. Tim laughed and clapped his hands. Sue saw Tim playing with the red ball and wanted to play too. Tim shared the ball with Sue and they both laughed and played together.

Once there was a little girl called Lucy. She was three years old and she saw a log by the river. It looked very gloomy. She wondered what it was.

As she got closer she saw a little mouse living inside. The mouse said hello and Lucy was so surprised. She smiled and waved at the little mouse. The mouse said it liked living in the log by the river.

Suddenly it started to rain. The log got darker and the mouse was getting wet. Lucy looked around and saw a big tree with lots of leaves. She asked the mouse to come and play under the tree and keep dry.

The mouse was very happy and they both ran over to the tree. The mouse was safe and dry and both of them were very happy. They laughed and played in the leaves until the rain stopped. Now, every day, they play together under the tree whenever it is gloomy outside.

Once there was a nurse who was very selfish. She never wanted to share anything with anyone. One day, the nurse had a delicious snack and it made her mouth water. She couldn't wait to taste it!

So, the nurse took a big bite, but it was too hot! She quickly grabbed a cup of cold water and gulped it down. That cooled it off just enough for her to enjoy the snack. But then another thought crossed her mind.

Suddenly, she realized that someone else might want to taste her snack. She thought about sharing it with others, but decided to keep it all for herself. She was too selfish to share.

Eventually, the nurse ate the entire snack and felt very content. But if only she had been willing to share, then she could have spread the joy. Oh well, the nurse learned her lesson - it's more fun when you share!

Tom is a brown dog. He likes to play with his ball. He knows how to fetch and roll and shake. He is a good dog.

One day, Tom sees a new thing in the yard. It is big and shiny and round. It has a hole on top. Tom is curious. He goes to the new thing and sniffs it. He hears a sound inside. He barks at the new thing.

"Hello, who are you?" a voice says from the new thing. Tom is surprised. He barks again.

"I am Sam, a tap. I live in the new thing. It is a barrel. It has water inside. Do you want some water?" the voice says.

Tom is thirsty. He nods his head. He likes water.

"OK, then. Come closer and I will give you some water. You have to push my nose. It is a button. Then water will come out of my mouth. It is a spout. Try it," the voice says.

Tom does what the voice says. He pushes the nose of the tap. Water comes out of the mouth of the tap. Tom drinks the water. It is cool and fresh. He likes it.

"Thank you, Sam. You are a nice tap. Can we be friends?" Tom says.

"Of course, Tom. You are a nice dog. We can be friends. Do you want to play with me?" Sam says.

"Yes, I do. How can we play?" Tom says.

"Well, you can push my nose and I will squirt water. You can catch it or dodge it. It is fun. Or you can roll your ball and I will watch. Or you can tell me stories. I like stories. What do you think?" Sam says.

Tom thinks. He likes all those things. He is happy. He has a new friend.

"Let's do all of them. You are a fun tap. I am glad I met you," Tom says.

"Me too, Tom. You are a fun dog. I am glad you came to the yard," Sam says.

They smile at each other. They start to play. They have a lot of fun. They are good friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who loved to tear things. One day she saw an envelope lying on the floor. She thought it was so fun to tear, so with a loud tear, she ripped it open. When she opened it, there were lots of colourful pieces of paper inside. She was so happy, that she started picking up the pieces and tearing them up until they were tiny. She kept tearing all the pieces until she could tear no more. Afterwards she felt all giggly and happy, so she laughed out loud. And they all lived happily ever after!

Lila and Sam were best friends. They liked to play in the garden and look at the flowers. One day, they saw a big, shiny book on the shelf. It had pictures of many things they did not know.

"What is this?" Lila asked, pointing to a round, blue thing.

"That is a planet," Sam said. He had heard his big sister say that word. "It is like a big ball in the sky. There are many planets, but we live on this one."

"Wow, it is so pretty," Lila said. "Can we go there?"

Sam shook his head. "No, we can't. It is too far away. We need a rocket to go there."

Lila felt upset. She wanted to see the planet. She wanted to see if it had flowers like their garden. She wanted to see if they could bloom there.

"Maybe we can make a rocket," she said. "We can use cardboard and tape and paint."

Sam smiled. He liked to make things. He agreed to help Lila. They got some cardboard and tape and paint from the garage. They cut and folded and stuck and painted. They made a big, colorful rocket.

They put the rocket in the garden. They climbed inside. They pretended to fly to the planet.

"Are we there yet?" Lila asked.

"Yes, we are," Sam said. He opened the door. He saw the flowers in the garden. He pretended they were on the planet. "Look, there are flowers here. They are blooming."

Lila looked out. She saw the flowers too. She pretended they were on the planet. She smiled. She was not upset anymore. She was happy.

They picked some flowers and put them in the rocket. They flew back to their home. They showed the flowers to their parents. They told them they went to the planet.

Their parents smiled. They hugged them. They said they were very clever and creative. They said they were proud of them.

Lila and Sam were happy. They had a fun adventure. They learned a new word. They saw the flowers bloom. They were best friends.

Once upon a time there was a gifted little boy named Mark. He was always exploring and stumbling around. One day he found a magical stick that had a sparkly star on it. Mark was so excited. He held it tightly and just knew it was special.

When Mark held it up, a fairy appeared. "Greetings Mark! I am your magical fairy. I can grant you a wish," she said with a sparkle in her eye.

Mark was excited but he wasn't sure what he wanted. He stammered, "Um, I don't know what to wish for?"

The magical fairy smiled and said, "You can wish for anything you want. What would make you happy?"

Mark thought long and hard and then wished to travel the world. Suddenly, his wish came true and he stumbled off on his magical adventure. He saw so many wonderful things and it was all thanks to his special gift and his magical wish.

One day, a boy named Ben was wearing his new copper hat. He thought it looked so cool and he wanted to show it off to all his friends. When he went to school, all the kids were so jealous of his hat.

On his way home, Ben saw an old man. The old man said to Ben, "That is a foolish thing to wear, copper isn't good for a young boy like you." Ben was surprised and embarrassed and he quickly ran away.

When he got home, he took off his copper hat and put it away. From then on, Ben was more careful in what he wore. He learned that being foolish can be a very bad thing!

Once upon a time there was a girl called Lucy. One day Lucy dared to go into her mum's office. When she saw it for the first time, it looked so big. But Lucy was brave and took a step inside. Everything in the office was so neat and tidy, it was like a palace. 

On the desk Lucy noticed a gentle brown bear. She was so excited and carefully hugged it. She was so gentle that the bear never moved. Lucy looked around the office and tried to find something else exciting to do. She saw a big chair and dared herself to sit on it. She closed her eyes and imagined it was a giant throne. 

She was feeling so brave that before she knew it, she had explored the whole office. Lucy was so proud of what she had done and so excited to tell everyone about her adventures in the office.

The sun was setting. Jack watched the last of its orange rays disappear over the horizon. He shivered as the wind blew around him, then made his way to his cozy little house. Inside, he found a warm blanket, some candy, and a cable. Jack smiled and grabbed the cable. He knew it would keep him busy.

Soon after, Jack was very sleepy. He curled up in his blanket and started to nod off. Suddenly, a wise old man appeared. He said to Jack, "You should not be playing with that cable. It is too dangerous!"

Jack ignored the man and continued to play. But before he knew it, he was fast asleep.

The next morning, the wise old man came back. He was upset to see the cable damaged. Jack was sad too. He realized that he should have listened to the wise man. 

The wise old man warned Jack again before he left. "Donâ€™t forgetâ€”it is very important to always listen to people who are wise."

Timmy was having a great day. He wanted to have a little fun outside in the sunshine. He saw a ball of yarn and had a great idea. He would join the yarn to make a big jump rope. He grabbed the soft yarn and got to work.

Timmy was very skilled at joining the yarn. He was quite modest about his work and didn't boast. After a few minutes, he had made a big jump rope. He picked it up and started to twirl it around in circles. The rope flew up in the air and landed neatly on the ground.

Timmy had done a great job. He was so proud that he had made the jump rope with yarn. He started to jump and soon was having a great time. His jump rope gave him many hours of fun and joy in the sunshine.

Once upon a time, there was a rabbit named Bun. Bun liked to jump and hop all around. One day, Bun saw a big salad on the table. Bun wanted to eat the salad, but it was too high to reach. 

Bun thought, "I can be independent and find a way to get the salad." So, Bun hopped on a chair and then jumped up to the table. Bun ate the salad and felt very happy.

From that day on, Bun knew that being independent was important. And whenever Bun saw a salad, Bun would jump up and get it all by themselves.

Once upon a time, there was a chubby cat named Tom. Tom liked to gaze at the birds outside his window. One day, he saw a quick bird and wanted to catch it.

Tom went outside and said, "Hey, quick bird, come here!" The bird looked at Tom and said, "No, I won't come to you, chubby cat!" Tom was sad, but he wanted to catch the bird, so he ran after it.

Tom chased the quick bird, but he was too chubby and slow. The bird flew away, and Tom could not catch it. Tom was very sad and went back home. He looked out the window and saw more birds, but he knew he could not catch them.

Once upon a time, there was a normal little pigeon. The pigeon liked to lean against the wall and look around. One sunny day, it even leaned on the door. Suddenly, the door opened and the pigeon flew right in!

Inside the house, there was a big surprise. A little girl was sitting at a table with a plate of cookies. She smiled and offered the pigeon a cookie.

The pigeon leaned forward and took the cookie. It leaned back and nibbled on the sweet treat. The little girl laughed as the pigeon crumbs fell all around.

When the pigeon was done eating, the little girl opened the door and showed it back outside. The pigeon thanked her with a special little chirp and then flew off into the sky. It was nice to be back out in the sunshine with the other birds.

The pigeon had a normal day after that. It leaned against the walls, looked around, and even enjoyed a cookie!

One morning, a hairy band arrived in town. The children were so excited they ran up to the band members to learn who they were.

A boy named Sam asked, "Why are you here?"

The lead singer of the band smiled and said, "We are here to teach you a lesson. You see, if you work hard and don't give up, you can do anything you set your mind to. We have worked hard over the years and now look at us, performing in your town." 

Sam was inspired and he asked, "Can I join your band too?"

The singer replied, "If you practice every day, one day you might join us!"

This is why it is important to never give up and always keep trying your best. With determination and hard work, everything is possible!

One day, a friendly child named Tim went to the park. He saw a big bell there. Tim wanted to make the bell ring.

Tim said to his friend, Sue, "Let's ring the bell together!" Sue smiled and said, "Yes, let's do it!" They both pushed the bell very hard. The bell made a loud "ring" sound.

All the other kids in the park heard the bell ring. They came running over to see what was happening. Tim and Sue were happy to make new friends. They all played together and had a fun day at the park.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a notebook that she loved to draw in. One day, her mom asked her to clean her room, but Lily was too busy drawing. Her mom insisted that she clean her room before she could play with her notebook.

Lily didn't want to stop drawing, but she knew she had to listen to her mom. So, she put down her notebook and started cleaning her room. It was hard work, but she did it quickly so she could go back to drawing.

When she was finished, her mom gave her a big hug and told her how proud she was. Lily smiled and went back to her notebook, feeling happy that she had listened to her mom.

Mommy was getting ready to decorate the house. She said, â€œLetâ€™s get started.â€

She brought out a pretty vest. She said, â€œWe can hang the vest on the wall. It will look attractive.â€

Mommy asked her daughter to help. She handed the little girl some tape, and then picked up some decorations. She put them on the vest.

The little girl asked, â€œWhat else?â€

Mommy said, â€œWe can string lights around the vest.â€

They worked together until the vest was decorate. It looked bright and cheerful and very attractive.

The little girl said, â€œI like it!â€

Mommy said, â€œMe too. We did a great job.â€

Once upon a time there was a patient dog named Fido. He always waited patiently for his owner to come home. One day, Fido noticed something different in the air. There was an event coming up and everyone was busy getting ready. 

Fido was very excited so he ran around looking for something to do. Suddenly he spotted an old stick lying on the ground. He picked up the stick with his teeth and started to play with it. He ran around with the stick, tapping it on the ground.

As Fido tapped the stick, he noticed the stick starting to rot. He quickly dropped it and stepped back. Fido looked around, feeling a bit confused. Then, he heard someone calling his name. He looked up and saw his owner in the distance.

Fido quickly ran over to his owner and barked. 

"Hey Fido, what were you doing?" His owner asked.

Fido wagged his tail eagerly and explained that he was playing with the old stick that was rotting in the grass. 

His owner smiled and said, "You're such a patient pup, waiting patiently while I was getting ready for the event. You're a good boy!" 

Fido's tail was wagging faster now and he was so happy that his owner was proud of him. He ran around in circles, enjoying the moment. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a man who lived in a valley with his family. He wanted to add something special to his family, so he decided to get a pet. The man and his family looked everywhere but they couldn't find a pet they wanted.

One day, the man walked through the valley and he saw a slow and gentle dog. The man and his family loved the dog and decided to add it to the family.

The dog was very slow and calm, but it loved playing with the man and the man's family in the valley. They played together in the sunshine at the weekends and during their holidays.

The dog fit perfectly into the man's family and made the valley feel even more special than it already was. The man and his family were so happy they'd added the gentle dog to their family.

One day, a big round ball went for a roll down a hill. On the way, it met a nosy cat. The cat said, "Where are you going, ball?"

The ball said, "I am going to find a friend to play with. Do you want to come?" The nosy cat said, "Yes, I want to come too!" So, they both went down the hill together.

As they rolled down, the nosy cat saw a big tree. The cat wanted to rub on the tree, but the ball wanted to keep rolling. The cat said, "I want to rub the tree, but you want to roll. We can't do both."

The ball said, "I don't want to stop. I want to keep rolling." The nosy cat got mad and said, "Fine, go roll by yourself!" The ball rolled away fast and got lost. The nosy cat stayed by the tree, sad and alone. They both lost their new friend.

Once upon a time there was a little boy named Sam, who was three years old. Sam loved learning about the world around him. One day, Sam heard something mysterious coming from his living room. Thinking it must be something exciting, he ran in to investigate.

Sam saw a man sitting in his favorite armchair. The man had bright, shining eyes hidden behind thick glasses. He looked very mysterious.

"Hello, my name is Mr. McQueen," said the man. "I've come all the way from a faraway place, and I'd like to teach you something very special."

Sam was excited. He had never heard of Mr. McQueen before and he just knew that learning something special had to be fun. 

"I'm a science teacher," the man said. "But what I want to teach you is something even more special, something that nobody else knows. I want to teach you the secrets of the human eye."

Sam wasn't sure what the man meant by this. But he couldn't help but be curious and he eagerly agreed to learn.

The man then explained to Sam that the eye has tiny parts called pupils which can see things that are unknown to most people. Sam was so interested, he couldn't wait to learn more. 

That evening, Sam learned that his pupils could help him see things his eyes normally wouldn't pick up - things that were happening in the world

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved animals very much. One day, she went to the zoo with her mom and dad. They saw many great animals like lions, tigers, and elephants. 

Lily was very brave and dared to pet a friendly goat. The goat was very soft and Lily was very happy. She also saw some monkeys who were playing and jumping around. 

At the end of the day, Lily was tired but very happy. She told her mom and dad that she had a great time at the zoo and couldn't wait to come back again.

Lily and Ben were playing with their toys in the living room. Lily had a yellow ball and Ben had a blue car. They were having fun, but they also wanted to see what the other had.

"Can I play with your ball?" Ben asked Lily.

"OK, but only for a little while. Then you have to give it back," Lily said.

She gave Ben her ball and took his car. She liked how the car could zoom and make noises. Ben liked how the ball could bounce and roll. They were happy for a few minutes, but then they started to miss their own toys.

"I want my car back," Lily said.

"I want my ball back," Ben said.

They both reached for their toys, but they were too far away. They had to get up and walk to get them. But as they did, they saw a dark figure in the corner of the room. It was a big dog, and it looked hungry. It saw the toys and wanted to play with them too. It ran towards the ball and the car, and grabbed them with its mouth.

"Hey, that's our toys!" Lily and Ben shouted.

They ran after the dog, but it was faster and stronger. It ran away with the toys, and they could not catch it. They were sad and angry. They had lost their toys because they did not share.

They learned a lesson that day. They learned that sharing is good, and that being greedy can prevent them from having fun. They also learned to be careful of big dogs. They wished they had been nicer to each other, and to their toys. They hoped they would find them again, or get new ones. They hugged and said sorry, and decided to play together with something else. They still liked the yellow ball and the blue car, but they liked each other more.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. He had a cane that he liked to use when he went for walks. Timmy thought his cane was very useful because it helped him walk better. 

One day, Timmy went for a walk in the woods. He heard some birds singing and he smiled. He walked deeper into the woods and suddenly, he heard a loud growling noise. He was scared and didn't know what to do. 

Suddenly, a big bear appeared! Timmy tried to use his cane to protect himself, but the bear was too strong. The bear took Timmy's cane and ran away. Poor Timmy was left alone in the woods without his useful cane.

Once upon a time, there was a young boy named Jake. He was three years old and he was always looking for something new to do and explore. 

One day, Jake wanted to find a new restaurant. He asked his mom and dad if he could go with them to one. They said yes and they drove away. 

When they got to the restaurant, Jake was so excited. He peeked through the windows and saw how clean it was. He wanted to go inside, but he had to wait until they were done eating. 

Finally, they were done, and they let Jake enter. He couldn't wait to explore. He peeked behind the counter and looked in the back rooms. He even peeked in the kitchen and saw the chefs cooking! 

Jake was so happy that he got to peek in the restaurant. He promised himself he would come back to peek again soon.

Lily and Sam were playing in the park with their mom. They liked to slide, swing, and run on the grass. It was a sunny day, but a little cold. Mom told them to wear their jackets.

"Look, Sam, a dog!" Lily said, pointing to a big brown dog that was walking with an elderly man. The dog had a red collar and a long tail. Lily loved dogs and wanted to pet it.

"Can we go, Mom?" she asked.

"Okay, but be careful and ask first," Mom said.

Lily and Sam ran to the dog and the man. The dog wagged its tail and licked their faces. The man smiled and said hello.

"What's his name?" Lily asked.

"His name is Rex. He's very friendly. Do you like dogs?" the man asked.

"Yes, we do. We hear them bark sometimes, but we don't have one," Sam said.

"Maybe you can have one when you grow up. Dogs are good friends. Rex and I go for walks every day. He keeps me company," the man said.

"He's very soft and warm. Can I hug him?" Lily asked.

"Sure, he likes hugs. You're very sweet, Lily," the man said.

Lily hugged Rex and felt his fur. Sam rubbed his ears and heard him make a happy sound. They thanked the man and said goodbye to Rex. They went back to their mom, who was waiting for them.

"Did you have fun?" Mom asked.

"Yes, Mom. We met Rex and his elderly man. They were very nice. We want a dog like Rex," Lily and Sam said.

"Maybe someday. But for now, let's go home and have some cookies. You must be hungry after playing so much," Mom said.

They put on their jackets and followed Mom to the car. They waved to Rex and the man, who waved back. They were happy and tired. They had a good day.

One day, two children were playing together in the park. They were playing tag and laughing. Suddenly, one of the children stopped in his tracks as something caught his eye. In front of them, he could see something hidden in the bushes. He ran over to take a closer look and saw that it was money.

He happily picked it up and ran over to show his friend. "Look what I found!" he exclaimed. His friend was very excited and said, "Let's take it to the pond, we can splash it in the water and make some wishes!"

The two friends ran down to the pond and started throwing the money into the water. They made a few wishes before they left, hopeful that the money would come true.

However, when they arrived back at the park, a large man was standing in the bushes where they had hidden the money. He asked, "Who put all this money here?"

The children looked at each other in fear and ran away as fast as they could. As they looked back, they saw the man taking all their hidden money away.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. She had a bright smile, but today she was feeling scared. 

She was looking at a beautiful vase that her mother had placed on the table. It was made out of glass, but Lucy was too scared to touch it. 

Suddenly, her mother came into the room and told Lucy that she had to serve the flowers in the vase. Lucy was so scared that she started to cry. 

But then, her mother told her that she did not have to serve the flowers alone. She said that if Lucy held her hand, they could do it together. 

Lucy stopped crying and smiled. She was so happy when she served the flowers with the help of her mother. Lucy knew that if she was ever scared again, her mother would always be there to help.

Once there were two bears, Bob and Sue. They both wanted to race to see who was the fastest, but Bob decided to ignore Sue's suggestion.

Bob thought he could easily win the race, but he was wrong. Sue had been very fast and modest, and she won the race by a lot!

First, Timmy glued the paper clown onto some cardboard. He painted the clown's face a bright red. He added a nose, eyes and a happy smile. Then he chose some colorful buttons to be the clown's nose. 

Next, Timmy decorated the clown's outfit. He added stripes and a big bow-tie. He glued on cheerful paper flowers and a jaunty hat. When it was finished, the clown certainly looked jolly! 

Timmy was very proud of his work. He showed his mom the clown and she smiled. Together, they hung the clown on the wall and it was just the thing to brighten up the room. 

Timmy was very pleased with his decorations. He had made the jolly clown all by himself.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Lucy. She was curious about the world around her. 

One day Lucy went for a walk with her mommy. As they walked, Lucy could feel the cool breeze in the air and the ground was wet. 

Mommy asked, "Do you feel the cool air, Lucy?"

Lucy said, "Yes, Mommy. I'm shivering!". 

Mommy smiled and said, "Oh look, there are some roots on the ground! Let's see what they look like!"

Mommy and Lucy knelt down and carefully inspected the roots. They were amazed by their shapes and textures. 

Mommy said, "Let's take some of these roots home so we can have a closer look!" 

So the two of them picked the roots up carefully and started walking home. 

Lucy was so excited and kept shivering in anticipation. 

Once they were home, Lucy was so curious to see what else was hidden in the roots they had found. She couldn't wait to explore!

One day, Timmy and his mommy went to the zoo. Timmy was so excited to see all the animals.

The first animal they saw was a lion. Timmy's mommy asked him to weigh the lion. He was not sure what she meant, but he pushed down on the lion's head to see how hard it felt. 

The next animal they saw was a monkey. Timmy was even more excited to see this one. His mommy again asked him to weigh the monkey, but Timmy locked her hand and said, "No, mommy! Monkey too fast!"

Timmy was so excited to explore the zoo, and he came up with lots of fun ways to weigh animals. He even pretended to weigh the birds every time they flew by! It was a very fun day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had long hair that was always tangled. One day, Lily's mom gave her a comb and told her to comb her hair. Lily tried, but it was hard. She asked her mom for help.

Her mom sat her down and began to comb her hair. Lily watched closely as her mom combed her hair. She wanted to examine how her mom did it so she could do it herself next time. After her mom was done, Lily looked in the mirror and saw that her hair was successful combed. She was very happy!

Once there was a brave little girl. She had to do something that was very difficult. She had to fill out a file. It was very long, with lots of confusing words.

The little girl struggled hard to finish it. She used her small fingers to write down her answers. But she found it very hard.

Suddenly she started to feel tired. She wanted to give up. But then she remembered that she was brave!

So she kept going, even though it was very harsh. She worked and worked until she finally finished her file.

When she was done, she looked around. She felt proud of herself for doing something so hard. Her parents were very proud of her too. She had finished her file!

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to look at the stars at night. One night, he saw a very bright star in the sky. He wanted to touch it, but he knew he couldn't because it was too far away.

Timmy's sister, Sarah, came outside and saw the star too. She said it was too hot to touch. Timmy didn't understand why it was hot, but he trusted his sister.

The next night, Timmy saw the star again. But this time, it looked like it was getting closer and closer. Timmy got scared and ran inside to tell his parents. They told him not to worry, it was just a shooting star passing by. Timmy felt better and went to bed, understanding that sometimes things can look scary, but they're really not.

Mum and Dad loved to talk about vacation. They would mention it all the time and their eyes would light up as they made their plans.

One day, Mum suggested a beach vacation and the whole family was excited. They packed their bags and pile into the car.

The beach was very pale. It had the softest white sand and glistening blue water. Dad spread the towel on the sand and the family spent the afternoon playing.

They built a sandcastle and splashed in the warm sea. At night, they roasted a hotdog over the campfire and made s'mores. Even in the dark, the sand was pale and beautiful.

When it was time to leave, the family was sad. Dad said he would mention vacation again soon and everyone cheered. They couldn't wait to plan their next adventure!

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tweety. Tweety was very tired and wanted to sleep. "I want to sleep," Tweety said to his friend, a little squirrel. "But I can't find a good place to sleep."

The little squirrel said, "You can sleep on the earth. It's soft and cozy." Tweety tried to sleep on the earth, but he felt sad. "I don't like sleeping on the earth. It's too sad," Tweety said.

The little squirrel said, "Don't be sad. You can sleep in my tree. It's very comfortable." Tweety tried to sleep in the tree and it was perfect. "Thank you, my friend. Now I can sleep peacefully," Tweety said. And with that, Tweety closed his eyes and fell fast asleep.

Once upon a time, there was a pretty girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and her friends. One day, she went to the park with her mommy and daddy. She saw a butterfly and tried to catch it, but it flew away. 

Suddenly, Lily started to feel sick and her tummy hurt. Her mommy and daddy took her to the hospital. The doctor said she had a fever and gave her medicine. Lily was scared but her mommy and daddy told her everything would be okay. 

After taking the medicine, Lily started to feel better. She looked at herself in the mirror and noticed she had shrunk! "Mommy, daddy, look at me! I'm so small!" she said. Her mommy and daddy laughed and said it was just her imagination. From that day on, Lily always remembered her adventure at the hospital.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She lived on a farm with her family. She loved to play with the animals on the farm, like the cows and chickens.

One day, Lily saw a big, scary snake in the grass. She was scared and didn't know what to do. Her dad came and told her not to be afraid because he didn't believe the snake was dangerous.

Lily's dad picked up the snake and showed her that it was just a harmless garter snake. From that day on, Lily knew that not everything that looked scary was actually dangerous.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Jane. Jane lived on a farm and her best friend was a mule. The mule's name was Joe. Jane and Joe had lots of fun together.

Every day, Jane and Joe would go for a walk in the open fields. They would enjoy the sunshine and play games. Sometimes they would play tag and hide and seek. Other times they would make believe they were knights and dragons.

When they would tire of pretending, they would go to the open barn and take a nap. They would snuggle up close together with the mule's warm fur tickling Jane's face.

Then Jane and Joe would go back to the open fields. They would run and laugh and giggle. Jane and Joe were the best of friends.

The end.

Sara liked to eat toast with jam for breakfast. She liked to spread the jam with her knife and make it cover the whole toast. She did not like to leave any white spots. She also liked to cut her toast into small pieces and eat them one by one.

One morning, Sara was making her toast when she heard a loud noise outside. She ran to the window and saw a big truck with a deep hole in the back. The truck was full of dirt and rocks. Sara wondered what the truck was doing. She asked her mom, who was in the kitchen.

"Mom, what is that truck for?" Sara said.

"That truck is for digging a new pool in our backyard, honey," Mom said. "Remember, we talked about it yesterday? We are going to have a lot of fun in the summer."

Sara nodded. She remembered that Mom and Dad had told her that they were going to build a pool for her and her brother. She was very excited. She wanted to swim and splash and play with her toys in the water.

Sara went back to her toast. She finished spreading the jam and cutting the pieces. She was about to take a bite when she heard another loud noise. She looked out the window again and saw the truck dumping the dirt and rocks into the hole. She gasped. She saw something shiny and red in the dirt. It looked like her favorite toy car. The one that Dad had given her for her birthday.

"Mom, Mom, look!" Sara cried. "My car, my car! It's in the dirt!"

Mom came to the window and saw the car too. She frowned. She remembered that Sara had left it outside yesterday and had forgotten to bring it in.

"Oh, Sara, I'm sorry," Mom said. "That was your car. It must have been in the grass and the truck picked it up. We can't get it back now. It's buried under the dirt."

Sara felt a big lump in her throat. She felt tears in her eyes. She loved her car. She did not want to lose it. She did not care about the pool anymore. She only wanted her car.

She dropped her toast on the plate and ran to her room. She threw herself on her bed and sobbed. She wished she had taken better care of her car. She wished she had not left it outside. She wished the truck had not taken it away.

She hugged her pillow and covered her face. She did not want to see anything. She did not want to hear anything. She did not want to eat anything. She only wanted her car.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and run around outside. One day, she saw a butterfly and tried to catch it, but it flew away. 

Lily's mom told her that sometimes we need to prevent things from happening, like getting hurt or losing our toys. Lily thought about this and decided to be more careful when playing outside.

As she grew older, Lily learned that being flexible in life is important too. Sometimes things don't go as planned, but if we are flexible, we can find new ways to solve problems and have fun. And that's just what Lily did, she learned to be careful and flexible, and had many happy adventures!

Lily liked to play with her dolls. She had many dolls, but her favorite was Anna. Anna had a pink dress and a yellow hat. Lily liked to dress Anna and comb her hair.

One day, Lily and her mom went to the park. Lily brought Anna with her. She saw a big slide and wanted to go on it. She asked her mom if she could go. Her mom said yes, but told her to hold Anna tight.

Lily climbed up the stairs and sat on the slide. She held Anna tight. She slid down fast and laughed. She liked the slide. She wanted to go again.

But when she got up, she saw a stranger. The stranger was a boy. He had a blue shirt and a green cap. He was holding Anna. He had taken Anna from Lily.

Lily was scared and angry. She ran to the boy and shouted, "Give me Anna! She is mine! You are a bad stranger!"

The boy looked at Lily and said, "No, she is mine! I like her! She is pretty!"

He tried to run away with Anna, but Lily was faster. She caught up with him and grabbed Anna. She pulled hard and got Anna back.

The boy cried and said, "That is not fair! You are mean!"

Lily hugged Anna and said, "No, you are mean! You took Anna from me! She does not fit you! She fits me!"

She ran to her mom and told her what happened. Her mom was proud of Lily. She said, "You are brave, Lily. You did the right thing. Anna is yours. You love her and take care of her. The stranger was wrong. He should not take things that are not his."

Lily smiled and said, "Thank you, mom. I love you and Anna. Can we go on the slide again?"

Her mom said, "Yes, we can. But be careful and watch out for strangers."

Lily nodded and said, "I will, mom. I will hold Anna tight."

They went on the slide again and had fun. Lily and Anna were happy.

Once there was a boy named John. He was three years old and loved to joke. He was always laughing and having fun.

One day it started to rain. The rain was cold and wet. John thought it would be funny to dance in it and he began to twirl and spin around.

His mother saw him and said, "John, the rain is useful. It helps make things grow." John listened and smiled.

The rain stopped soon after, and when it was over, John saw a beautiful rainbow in the sky. He laughed again and said, "Look, mom! A rainbow. We can joke about that."

His mother smiled and said, "Yes, we can! It's so special to see something so beautiful after the rain."

John smiled with joy and ran around the rainbow, laughing and joking again.

Jimmy wanted something special. It was his birthday and he wanted something special to put in his new room. His mom said she knew just the thing, so she led him to the cabinet. It was tall and expensive, and Jimmy couldn't help but feel excited. Jimmy's mom slowly opened the doors one by one, and there it was! A shiny red race car with bright yellow wheels. "Oh wow," Jimmy exclaimed. His mom smiled down at him and said, "Go ahead, give it a try."

So Jimmy hopped in the race car and zipped around the room. He raced everywhere, zooming past the windows, the doors and the walls. He felt so happy and free in his new car. The whole time, his mom just smiled and watched him have fun. 

Finally, it was time for bed. But before Jimmy could leave, his mom had one more surprise for him. She pulled out a brand new remote control and said, "This is for you, so you can zip around in your car even when I'm not here." Jimmy smiled and hugged his mom.

It had been the best birthday ever!

Once upon a time, there was a girl called Lucy. She was only three years old but she was very brave. One day, Lucy noticed a parade going past her house. She was very excited and wanted to join in.

When Lucy asked her mom if she could take part in the parade, her mom said, "No, it's too expensive. We can't afford it."

Lucy was very sad and she decided to hide so that she wouldnâ€™t be seen. She found a cheap box and got in it.

When the parade was over and Lucy returned home, she asked her mom, "Can I join the parade again next year?" Her mom laughed and said, "Yes, but only if you donâ€™t hide this time!"

Daddy and his daughter were playing together in their living room. She was so excited to see daddy, she just kept running and laughing. 

One day, Daddy said, "Hey! Listen to me!" His daughter stopped running around, and looked up at him. "You can hear my voice like a song," Daddy said. He started to sing a silly song. 

The little girl smiled and started to dance to the tune. She sang along with daddy. She thought it was so fun. 

"Whoa, that was a good song Daddy!" she said. Daddy smiled and said, "Yes it was! You have a very special voice, my little one!" 

The delighted girl hugged daddy tightly, as they both laughed. She said, "I'm so lucky to have a silly Daddy like you." 

They both enjoyed the moment, and Daddy said, "It's time to go! Let's listen to the birds outside and play some more."

One day, a little red automobile named Zoomy was fast asleep in the garage. The sun began to rise and the birds started to sing. The birds' songs were so loud that they made Zoomy wake up.

Zoomy decided to go for a drive to the park. On the way, he saw his friend, Sally the squirrel. "Hi Zoomy!" said Sally. "Where are you going?" Zoomy told her he was going to the park. Sally wanted to go too, so she jumped in and they went together.

At the park, they saw a spicy food stand. Zoomy and Sally tried some spicy food. "Wow, this is spicy!" said Zoomy. "Yes, it is!" agreed Sally. They laughed and had a fun day at the park. When it was time to go home, Zoomy took Sally back to her tree and then went back to the garage to sleep.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Lucy. She had a big playground in her garden and she loved to swing on her swing. She was swinging higher and higher and when she looked down, she saw an apple hanging from a tree.

Lucy wanted to try the apple, so she jumped off the swing and ran to the tree. She picked the apple and took a big bite. Oh, it was sour!

Lucy said, "Yuck!"

But then she smiled and said, "It's still fun to swing!" So she went back to the swing and started swinging again. She giggled as she went higher and higher. 

The End

One day, a little boy named Peter went out to the woods with his dad. Peter was very excited to go explore the trees and play with all the animals.

They walked through the woods together, and then his dad stopped. He had found a broken axe on the ground. Peter was curious so he asked his dad what it was. His dad told him it was an axe, and it had been broken.

Suddenly, they heard a loud sound! It was not a nice sound, and Peter felt uncomfortable. He looked around but couldn't see anything. His dad told him it was an animal and asked him to be quiet.

They continued walking until they came across a man with an axe. He was using the axe to chop down a tree. Peter was surprised, he had never seen this before. His dad told him the man was a lumberjack and he was breaking the tree apart so he could use the wood for something.

Peter and his dad watched the lumberjack for a little bit. Then, it was time to go home. As they walked, Peter thought about the broken axe and the lumberjack. He realized that wood can be broken, just like the axe, but he also realized that sometimes it can be uncomfortable to watch it happen.

Once upon a time there was a curious lizard. The lizard liked to wander around and explore the world. One day, the lizard found itself lost and alone.

"Where am I?" called the little lizard, now afraid. 

Suddenly it saw an old man who seemed kind and friendly. He said, "Let me help you, little one. We will look for your way back home." 

The old man and the lizard wandered around the woods looking for the lizard's home. But they never found it. At last, the old man said, "It's getting late now, so I have to leave." 

The little lizard was very sad. It had lost its way and had nowhere to go. It watched the old man walk away and soon it was alone once again.

Once there was a brown structure. Inside it were many different things. One day a special person came to the structure. She wanted to sort the things inside. She worked all day, putting the things in special piles.

When she was finished, the structure looked very neat. In one pile were toys, in the other were books. She kept going all day and soon everything was sorted.

When the sun set, she stepped back outside and looked at the structure. It was very neat and tidy. The special person had done a great job of sorting!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Daisy. She was very enthusiastic and wanted to improve herself. She wanted to be strong and fast like her brothers.

One day, Daisy heard her mommy and daddy talking about something called 'lungs'. They said that if Daisy practised hard, she could improve her lungs so she could run faster. 

In the morning, Daisy was so excited to try. She asked her mommy for help and her mommy smiled. Together, Daisy and her mommy practised running. Daisy also took quick breaths to help improve her lungs. 

After a few weeks, Daisy noticed that she was getting much better. She was able to run faster and further than before. She was so proud of herself and was still very enthusiastic about her running practise, Daisy just couldn't wait to show all of her brothers how fast she had become!

Once upon a time, there was a big dishwasher that lived in the kitchen. It was very powerful and could clean lots of dishes at once. One day, a little girl was helping her mom put dishes in the dishwasher when she accidentally dropped a plate. The plate made a loud noise and scared the little girl. She wanted the noise to stop, so she asked her mom to help her. Her mom told her to be careful and to not drop any more dishes. The little girl was very careful and the noise stopped. From that day on, the little girl loved helping her mom with the powerful dishwasher.

Once upon a time, there was a cool ranch. On the ranch, there lived a boy named Tom and his dog, Spot. They liked to watch the cows and horses play in the big field.

One day, Tom and Spot saw a new horse on the ranch. The horse was big and brown. Tom said, "Look, Spot! A new horse is here. Let's watch it play." Spot barked happily, and they went to see the new horse.

As they watched the horse, it ran fast and jumped high. Tom and Spot laughed and clapped. The horse came close and said, "Hi, I'm Brownie. Do you want to play with me?" Tom and Spot were so happy. They played with Brownie all day long on the cool ranch.

Once upon a time, there was a little duck named Ducky. Ducky loved to swim in the pond with her friends. One day, Ducky saw a big, graceful swan swimming in the pond. Ducky wanted to be as big and graceful as the swan, so she asked her mommy how she could grow big like the swan.

Mommy duck told Ducky that she needed to eat lots of healthy food and exercise every day. So, Ducky started eating lots of vegetables and swimming every day. But, there was a problem. The pond was getting too small for all the ducks and swans. They needed more space to swim.

One day, Ducky and her friends saw a big subway being built near the pond. They were worried that the subway would take up all the space and they wouldn't have anywhere to swim. Ducky went to talk to the construction workers and asked them if they could leave some space for the pond. The workers listened to Ducky and left a big space for the pond to grow.

Now, Ducky and her friends had more space to swim and grow big and strong. They were happy and grateful to the construction workers for listening to them. And Ducky kept eating healthy and exercising every day, growing bigger and more graceful, just like the swan. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a nice little boy named Tim. He loved to play with his toys all day long. One day, Tim met a quiet little girl named Sue. They decided to play together and became good friends.

While they were playing, Tim said, "Let's finish our game of blocks!" Sue nodded and they both started to build a big tower. They worked together and soon had a very tall tower. Tim and Sue were very happy with their tower.

As they played, Tim and Sue learned to share and be nice to each other. They had so much fun playing together that they didn't want the day to end. But when it was time to go home, they said goodbye and promised to play again soon.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy called James who liked to play every day. One day, he asked his mom if he could go outside to play, and his mom said yes. He was so happy, he ran to get his shoes on and opened the door. 

When he stepped outside, he saw that his friends were sat on the grass playing. He was so excited! He ran to join them. 

They were playing a game with a big ball, and they asked James to join in. He loved the game and they spent the day playing together. 

As the sun began to set, they all finished their game. James was a bit worried. The game was so much fun, why did he have to go home? Suddenly, his mom called from the door. She had prepared dinner for all of them, so if James and his friends wanted to keep playing, they just had to come and eat dinner first. 

The boys had a wonderful time. Every weekend, they would come and play their regular game. James was no longer worried, he knew he could see his friends and have fun every weekend.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. Lily had a cozy bed with a soft mattress. One day, Lily's friend Tom came to visit her. Tom said, "Lily, can I join you in your bed?" Lily replied, "Yes, you can join me."

Tom climbed into the bed and accidentally spilled his juice on the mattress. Lily looked at Tom and said, "Tom, you made a mess. You should feel guilty." Tom felt bad and said, "I'm sorry, Lily. I didn't mean to spill my juice."
