Once upon a time there was a happy family. Every week they would celebrate together by playing games, sharing a yummy dinner and singing songs.

One week the family decided to have a special celebration. They bought some tomatoes and made a delicious salad. Everyone was so excited to eat it!

But when the salad was served, the mum was upset. It had too much salt! Everyone was very disappointed. 

The family felt sad, but then the dad had an idea. He said â€œLet's make another salad. We can put tomatoes in it. Then we can celebrate with it.â€ 

So the family made a new salad. It had lots of tomatoes in it and just the right amount of salt. Everyone was so happy and they all celebrated with their delicious salad. 

The end!

One day, a fun dog named Spot wanted to perform a trick. He knew if he did a good trick, he would get a yummy snack. Spot was happy and excited to show his trick to his friends.

Spot saw his friends, a big cat and a small bird. He told them, "I will do a trick and you will like it!" The cat and the bird watched as Spot jumped high in the air. They clapped and smiled. Spot was very happy.

The cat and the bird gave Spot a snack. It was a big, tasty bone. Spot was grateful for the snack and his friends. He knew that doing a good trick would make his friends happy and give him a yummy snack.

Sara liked to write in her journal every night. She wrote about what she did, what she saw, and what she felt. She drew pictures of her family, her friends, and her toys. She used many colors and stickers to make her journal pretty.

One night, Sara was very sleepy. She had played a lot with her brother, read a book with her mom, and ate a big dinner. She wanted to write in her journal, but her eyes were heavy and her hand was slow. She yawned and rubbed her face.

"Are you ready for bed, Sara?" her dad asked. He came to her room and saw her journal on her lap. "You have a very nice journal. Can I see what you wrote today?"

Sara nodded and handed him her journal. She was proud of her work. Her dad smiled and looked at her pages. He read some of her words and praised her drawings. He asked her questions about her day and listened to her answers.

Sara realized that her dad liked her journal too. She felt happy and loved. She hugged her dad and said, "Thank you, dad. I love you. Can you read me a story?"

"Of course, sweetie. I love you too. Let's pick a story and then you can sleep." her dad said. He put her journal on her nightstand and helped her choose a book. He read to her in a soft voice until she fell asleep. He kissed her forehead and turned off the light. He whispered, "Good night, Sara. You are a wonderful writer."

Kathy and her friends were playing in the park. They were looking for adventure. Suddenly, they saw a big maze. It looked like a harmless puzzle.

"Let's dive in and explore the maze," Kathy said to her friends.

So they went in and were amazed by the many twists and turns. They laughed and ran and found lots of fun things.

After a while, they came to a clearing in the center of the maze. There, they found a sparkling pond. The pond was so inviting that they decided to dive in. 

The water was cool and refreshing. Kathy and her friends had so much fun diving and playing in the pond. They stayed in the pond until they got too tired.

"Let's go home now," Kathy said. 

So, they waved goodbye to the harmless maze and went home with happy memories.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Julie. She was three years old. One day, Julie was in school, playing with her friends. She was using her eraser to draw a picture. She needed more space, so she asked her friend for help.

She said to her friend, "Can I borrow your eraser? Mine is too little." Her friend smiled and said, "Yes, you can borrow my eraser." Julie took her friend's eraser and started to draw.

She had lots of fun drawing and coloring with the eraser. She thanked her friend for letting her borrow it. Then, when she was finished, she gave the eraser back to her friend. Julie's friend smiled and thanked her for taking care of it.

The end.

Once there was a car that went anywhere. Everywhere it went it made people happy. But one day the car began to make a disgusting noise. It wouldn't move and it was stuck.

The car's owner was sad, but he knew what he had to do. He called a mechanic. The mechanic examined the car and said it needed to sleep. So the owner put the car to bed and soon it was better. 

The owner was so happy he took the car for a drive. It ran just fine and everyone smiled. The car had woken up and was working again. It was great!

Once upon a time, there was a hairy cat named Fluffy. Fluffy liked to play with a long string. He would jump and run to catch the string. Fluffy was very happy when he played with the string.

One day, Fluffy saw a little mouse. The mouse liked to tease Fluffy. The mouse would run near Fluffy and then run away. Fluffy would chase the mouse, but the mouse was very fast.

Fluffy had an idea. He took his long string and put it on the ground. The mouse saw the string and wanted to play too. The mouse ran to the string, and Fluffy caught the mouse. Fluffy and the mouse became friends and played with the string together. They had lots of fun and were very happy.

Once upon a time there was a fox. He was very restless and kept moving all night long. He wanted to take a break so he decided to lie down under a tree and take a nap.

He laid down and started to yawn. The yawns were long and deep. He felt so relaxed that soon he was fast asleep.

But the fox couldn't stay still for long. He started to feel restless again and started running around in circles. He found it very hard to sleep for long.

He tried to take a nap many more times, but the same thing happened over and over. He would get very sleepy and yawn, but then he would get too restless and start jumping around again.

The fox knew he would be better off if he could just relax and stay still in one place. But it was hard!

Once upon a time, in a big forest, there lived a lazy deer named Dara. She liked to sleep all day under the tall trees. Dara had many friends, like birds and squirrels, who played around her.

One sunny day, Dara's friend, a bird named Chirpy, said, "Dara, let's gather food before it gets dark." Dara, being lazy, replied, "No, Chirpy, I want to sleep more. You go and gather food for us."

Chirpy flew away to gather food with the other animals. But Dara just kept sleeping. When night came, Chirpy and the other animals had lots of food, but Dara had none. She was very hungry and sad.

The next day, Dara learned her lesson. She decided not to be lazy anymore. So, she went with Chirpy and the other animals to gather food. They all had fun and worked together. From that day on, Dara was never lazy again, and they all lived happily in the big forest.

John and Sarah went to school together. John couldn't wait to unpack his bag and show off his new things to his class. 

At school, Sarah said to John, "How do you feel about your class?" 
John said, "It's gonna be so comfortable!" 
Sarah smiled and said, "Let's unpack." 

John and Sarah carried their bags to the classroom. They put their things away and John showed off his new bag to his friends. Everyone was really excited to see it! 

John and Sarah had a great day. At the end of the day, the teacher said, "Let's have a surprise in the morning. I'm sure you'll all be comfortable and you won't want to unpack!" 

John and Sarah couldn't wait for the morning. When everyone arrived it was time for the surprise. The teacher had brought hot chocolate for everyone and cozy blankets and pillows for them to sit on! John and Sarah were so happy and comfortable that they never wanted to leave. 

John and Sarah laughed and had a great time unpacking all of their things throughout the school year. They were comfortable in their class and with their new friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to run and play with his friends, but he would always get upset when he couldn't keep up with them. One day, Timmy's grandpa came to visit and saw how sad Timmy was. Grandpa told Timmy that it's not about how fast you go, but about having fun.

Grandpa took Timmy to the park and they played together. Grandpa showed Timmy how to count the ducks in the pond and they raced each other at a slow speed. Timmy had so much fun with his grandpa and realized that he didn't have to be the fastest to have a good time.

From that day on, Timmy didn't worry about being the fastest anymore. He enjoyed playing with his friends and having fun. Timmy learned that being old doesn't mean you can't have fun and that speed isn't everything.

Once there was a little girl named Lucy. She was three years old and loved to explore the world around her.

One day, Lucy went for a walk with her mom. She saw a big magazine shop and asked if she could go in and take a look. Her mom nodded and smiled, so Lucy opened the door. Inside, it was filled with colorful magazines that were stacked high!

Lucy was so excited. She picked one up and showed it to her mom. "Can I get one?" asked Lucy. Her mom said, "Let's see if we can manage it."

So, Lucy carefully chose the colorful magazine and showed it to her mom. Her mom smiled and said, "We managed it and now it's yours!"

Lucy was so happy. She grabbed the magazine and hugged it all the way home.

Once upon a time, there was a fearful little mouse. The mouse did not want anyone to steal her tea. Every time she had tea, she would be very careful.

One day, the mouse was sitting in her little house having tea when she heard a loud noise. She was very scared and rushed outside to see what was happening.

She saw a dog had come to steal her tea! The mouse was very frightened, but she was brave and didnâ€™t give up. She ran up to the dog and shouted at him. 

The dog was so scared that he ran away as fast as he could. The mouse was relieved, and she knew she had to keep an eye out for thieves.

Anna and Ben were playing in the park with their mom. They liked to run and jump and slide on the grass. They saw a big pond with ducks and fish. They wanted to go near the water and feed the ducks.

"Can we go, mom?" Anna asked.

"OK, but be careful. Don't go too close to the edge. And don't splash the water. The ducks don't like it," mom said.

Anna and Ben nodded and ran to the pond. They threw some bread crumbs to the ducks and watched them eat. They saw a big fish jump out of the water and splash back in. They laughed and clapped.

"Look, mom, look! A big fish!" Ben shouted.

Mom smiled and watched them. She smelled something strange in the air. She looked around and saw some smoke coming from behind the trees. It was gray and thick and smelled bad. She wondered what it was. She felt worried.

"Anna, Ben, come here. We have to go," mom said.

"Why, mom? What's wrong?" Anna asked.

"There's some smoke over there. It might be a fire. It's not safe. We have to leave," mom said.

Anna and Ben looked at the smoke. They felt scared. They didn't know what it was. It looked mysterious.

"OK, mom. Let's go," Ben said.

They ran to mom and held her hands. They left the park and went to the car. They hoped the ducks and the fish were OK. They hoped the smoke would go away. They hoped they could come back to the park another day.

Once upon a time there was a bossy puppy named Fluffy. Fluffy liked to kick everything he saw. One day, he saw a big ball on the ground and he kicked it. The ball flew to the top of a tree and got stuck! Fluffy felt so sad, he wanted his ball back. 

Suddenly, he heard a voice from the top of the tree, "Help me please! I'm stuck!" Fluffy was so surprised he barked back, "Who are you? How did you get up there?" 

The voice said, "I'm an itchy caterpillar. I was crawling around up here and the big ball bumped me and made me fall into the tree. Now I can't get out!" 

Fluffy said, "I will help you. I'm sorry I made you fall in the tree!" He ran and got a ladder and put it against the tree trunk. He climbed up the ladder and kicked the ball out of the tree. The itchy caterpillar crawled down the ladder and thanked Fluffy. 

Fluffy's ball was safe and the itchy caterpillar was happy. Fluffy and the caterpillar became the best of friends, and he never kicked anything ever again.

Jill was nervous. She was sitting in a room with a gray chair and taking a test. She had to choose the right answers. She had been studying hard and knew her facts, but she was still nervous. 

She looked around the room, counted the chair legs and took a deep breath. She saw the first question on the test and smiled. She knew this one! She picked up the pencil and chose the right answer. 

The next question was harder. She studied it carefully, thinking of all her facts. She decided what she thought was the right answer and chose it. 

Jill kept going until all the questions were finished and breathed a sigh of relief. She felt confident she had chosen the right answers and now all she had to do was wait for the results.

Once upon a time, there was a bear. He liked to spend his days playing in the woods. One day, he got very tired, so he decided to take a nap under a tree. Suddenly, he heard something terrible! He looked up in the sky and saw a huge dark cloud. It was very scary, and the bear wanted to go home! So he ran as fast as he could and quickly hid in his den. He spent the rest of the day there, waiting for the storm to pass. 

After a while, the sky became bright again. The bear could finally go out and play! But he was still very scared, so he decided to stay close to home. He spent the rest of the day exploring his little backyard, and he had a wonderful time. 

The next day, the bear did not hear anything terrible. The sun was shining, and he decided to enjoy his day out in the woods again. He ran and played with his friends, feeling safe and happy. 

The bear learned an important lesson that day. When things are terrible, it is always best to stay by yourself until it passes.

Anna and Ben were playing with paper and scissors. They wanted to make snowflakes and stars. Anna cut many shapes and showed them to Ben. "Look, I made a big snowflake! And a star with six points! And a heart!" she said.

Ben tried to cut his paper too, but it was hard. His scissors were dull and his hands were small. He could not make any shapes. He felt sad and angry. He looked at Anna's shapes and wanted them. He said to Anna, "Give me your shapes! They are mine!"

Anna was surprised and hurt. She said, "No, they are not yours! I made them with my scissors and my paper. You are selfish, Ben! You can't have everything you want!"

Ben did not listen. He grabbed Anna's shapes and ran away. Anna cried and chased him. She wanted her shapes back. They ran around the room, knocking over toys and books. Their mom heard the noise and came to see what was wrong.

She saw Anna and Ben fighting over the paper shapes. She was not happy. She said, "Stop, both of you! What are you doing? Why are you fighting over paper shapes?"

Anna and Ben stopped and looked at their mom. They both tried to explain. Anna said, "Ben took my shapes! He is selfish!" Ben said, "Anna has too many shapes! She won't share!"

Their mom shook her head. She said, "You are both wrong. Anna, you should share your shapes with Ben. He is your brother and he wants to play with you. Ben, you should not take Anna's shapes. She worked hard to make them. You should ask her nicely if you can have some. And you should use your own scissors and paper to make your own shapes. You can both succeed if you try."

Anna and Ben felt sorry. They said, "We are sorry, mom. We are sorry, Anna. We are sorry, Ben." They hugged each other and their mom. They gave back the shapes they took and shared them. They also used their own scissors and paper to make more shapes. They had fun and learned to be kind and fair.

Lily was sad. She wanted to draw a picture for her mom, but she did not have any crayons. She looked around the room, but she could not find any. She felt helpless. She did not know what to do.

She saw her brother Jake playing with his cars. She walked over to him and asked, "Jake, can I have some crayons, please?"

Jake looked at her and shook his head. "No, these are my crayons. You can't have them. Go away."

Lily felt hurt. She did not understand why Jake was so mean. She said, "But I want to draw a picture for mom. She will be happy if I give her a picture. Please, Jake, can I have some crayons?"

Jake did not care. He said, "No, no, no. These are my crayons. You can't have them. Go away."

Lily started to cry. She did not know what to do. She felt helpless.

Then she heard a voice. It was her dad. He came into the room and saw Lily crying and Jake playing. He asked, "What's wrong, Lily? Why are you crying?"

Lily ran to her dad and hugged him. She said, "Dad, I want to draw a picture for mom, but Jake won't give me any crayons. He is mean. He says they are his crayons. I don't have any crayons. I feel helpless."

Dad looked at Jake and said, "Jake, is that true? Did you not share your crayons with Lily?"

Jake looked down and said, "Yes, dad. I did not share. I wanted to keep them all for myself."

Dad said, "Jake, that is not nice. You should share your crayons with Lily. She is your sister. She wants to draw a picture for mom. That is a nice thing to do. Don't you want to make mom happy?"

Jake thought for a moment. He felt sorry. He said, "Yes, dad. I want to make mom happy. I'm sorry, Lily. I was mean. You can have some crayons. Here, take these."

He gave Lily some crayons. Lily smiled. She said, "Thank you, Jake. You are a good brother. I'm sorry I made you mad. Can I draw a picture with you?"

Jake smiled back. He said, "Yes, Lily. You can draw a picture with me. Let's draw a picture for mom together. She will love it."

Lily and Jake hugged. They took the crayons and some paper and started to draw. Dad watched them and smiled. He was proud of them. He said, "That's my kids. You are both very sweet. I love you."

Lily and Jake said, "We love you too, dad. And we love mom. And we love our crayons."

Once upon a time, there was a brave boy named Alex. He loved to try new things, so one day he decided to squeeze a hot pepper. He squeezed it and all of the sudden, it was too hot! He was so brave, though, that he didn't give up. He squeezed lemon on the pepper to make it more bearable. He cheered when he was successful! The pepper wasn't too hot anymore so Alex was able to enjoy it. From then on, Alex knew he could do anything as long as he was brave and kept trying.

Once upon a time, there was a regular TV in a special room. Every night, it would glow brightly. All the children loved playing in that room, because the TV made it so much fun.

One night, the TV was like magic. It started to move and dance! With a loud sound, it moved around the room, like it was playing with everyone.

The children were so happy. They laughed and danced around the TV. The TV glowed in the darkness and made the children feel even more excited.

When the night came to an end, the regular TV stopped glowing, and the children all said goodbye. But they knew that the same magical thing would happen again the next night.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. He loved candy very much and always wanted to eat more. One day, he went to the candy store and saw a long line of people waiting to buy candy. Timmy thought he could cut in line and get his candy faster, but that would not be nice.

Instead, Timmy decided to wait in line like everyone else. When he finally got to the front of the line, he saw that there was only one piece of his favorite candy left. But, he saw another boy who really wanted it too. Timmy decided to let the other boy have it and he felt happy that he did the right thing.

In the end, Timmy succeeded in being kind and patient. He learned that being nice to others is more important than getting what he wants. And, as a reward for his good behavior, he got a tasty lollipop from the store owner. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved playing in the snow and building snowmen. One day, Lily's mom took her to the park to play in the snow. Lily was having so much fun when she saw a big igloo in the distance. She ran towards it and was surprised to find a polar bear inside!

"Hello, Mr. Polar Bear!" Lily said.

The polar bear looked at her and smiled. "Hello, little girl. What brings you to my igloo?"

"I was just playing in the snow and saw your igloo. I wanted to say hi," Lily said.

The polar bear was heavy and Lily was scared. She tried to run away, but the polar bear grabbed her. Lily's mom heard her screaming and came running. She tried to save Lily, but the polar bear was too strong. Lily was never seen again.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. One day, Timmy went on an adventure to the underground. He wanted to see all the trains that went chugga-chugga-choo-choo underground. But when he got there, he saw that one of the trains was broken. 

Timmy felt sad because he couldn't ride on the broken train. But then, he had an idea! He wanted to pay the train driver to fix the broken train. So, Timmy went to the train driver and gave him some money. The train driver was very happy and used the money to fix the train. 

Now, Timmy could ride on the train that he helped fix. He went chugga-chugga-choo-choo all around the underground and had so much fun. When he got home, Timmy told his mommy and daddy all about his adventure and how he helped fix the broken train. They were very proud of him. The end.

Once upon a time there lived a brave elephant in the backyard. All the other animals admired her, but one day a big lion came to the backyard. The elephant was scared and knew she had to act quickly. She ran over to the sun and asked it to melt the lion away. To the elephant's surprise, the sun melted the lion right away! The brave elephant was so excited, she told all the other animals and they had a big party in the backyard. Everyone was so happy the elephant had been so brave and she was given a special treat as a reward. The brave elephant lived happily ever after in the backyard!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a very noisy dog named Max. Max loved to bark and play all day long. One day, Lily's mommy told her they needed to go get a license for Max. 

Lily and Max went for a walk to the license place. When they got there, the lady at the counter said they needed some papers. Lily's mommy had forgotten them at home. So, they went back home to get the papers. 

When they came back to the license place, Max was still very noisy. But, the lady gave them a license for Max anyways. Lily was very happy and she and Max went home to play some more. The end.

Once there was a boy named Bob. He was not very wealthy, but he was happy. One day Bob was walking in the park and he saw a big, fluffy cloud in the sky. He thought it looked so soft and snugly that he wanted to steal it! So Bob reached up high and tried to grab the cloud. But it was too far away.

Bob was sad and he thought he could never get the cloud. A kindly wealthy man saw Bob and said, "I can help you, Bob." The man pulled a long stick out of his coat and gave it to Bob. He said, "Now you can reach the cloud!"

Bob took the stick and swung it up to the sky. He had never seen anything so beautiful! He grabbed hold of the cloud and held tight. Before the man could say a word, Bob ran off with his stolen cloud.

Bob was so happy! He ran around, laughing and twirling all day with his new cloud close to him. He showed it to his friends, who all thought it was the best cloud ever. And Bob never felt so happy and wealthy.

Jimmy was a boy who was always obedient. His mum and dad had taught him to be well behaved. Every day, Jimmy's parents let Jimmy do something special. One day, they let him turn on the lamp in the living room. Jimmy was so excited! He grabbed the switch and clicked it. The lamp lit up and shone brightly. He was so happy. Jimmy's mum and dad smiled and said, "Good job, Jimmy! You are so obedient." Jimmy's cheeks turned pink with pride. From then on, Jimmy always made sure to turn on the lamp with a smile whenever he felt like playing in the living room.

Lily and Ben are twins. They like to play outside in the snow. They make snowmen and snowballs and snow angels. They have fun and laugh a lot.

One day, they see a big bus on the street. The bus is yellow and has many windows. The bus stops near their house and opens the door. Lily and Ben are curious. They want to see the bus.

"Let's go, Ben!" Lily says. "Maybe we can ride the bus!"

"OK, Lily!" Ben says. "But we have to be careful. Mommy said not to talk to strangers."

They run to the bus and peek inside. They see many children and a lady. The lady smiles at them and says hello.

"Hello, kids!" the lady says. "Do you want to join us? We are going to the library to read some books and have some snacks."

Lily and Ben are excited. They love books and snacks. They nod and smile.

"Sure!" Lily says. "Can we, please?"

The lady nods and smiles. She helps them get on the bus. She gives them a seat and a blanket. She tells them her name is Miss Rose and she is a teacher. She says the children on the bus are her students. She says they are poor and they live in a shelter. She says the library is a warm and happy place for them.

Lily and Ben feel sad for the poor children. They want to be their friends. They share their snowballs and snowmen with them. They talk and play and giggle. They forget about the cold and the snow.

The bus drives to the library. Lily and Ben see many books and toys and games. They see a big fireplace and a cozy sofa. They see a man who smiles and welcomes them. He says his name is Mr. Lee and he is a librarian. He says he has a special story for them.

Lily and Ben listen to the story. They like the story. It is about a snowman who comes to life and has adventures. They clap and cheer. They thank Mr. Lee and Miss Rose. They hug the poor children. They say they are their friends.

The bus drives back to their house. Lily and Ben wave goodbye to the bus and the children and the lady and the man. They run to their mommy and tell her everything. They say they had fun and learned a lot. They say they want to go to the library again.

Mommy hugs them and kisses them. She says she is proud of them. She says they are kind and generous. She says they are lucky and blessed. She says they should always help the poor and share their joy.

Lily and Ben agree. They say they love mommy and each other. They say they love the bus and the library and the snowman. They say they love their new friends.

They go inside and have some hot chocolate. They snuggle on the sofa and read a book. They feel warm and happy. They do not freeze.

Lily and Ben were twins who liked to play with their toys. They had a big box of blocks, cars, dolls and animals. They could build, drive, dress and feed them. They had a lot of fun together.

One day, their mom said they had to go to the doctor. She said it was to make sure they were healthy and strong. Lily and Ben did not like the doctor. They were scared of the needles and the cold stethoscope. They did not want to go.

Mom put them in the car and drove to the clinic. She gave them each a sticker and a book to read. She said they would be back soon. Lily and Ben looked at each other. They did not believe her.

They waited in a small room with other kids and parents. Some of the kids were crying. Some of the parents were smiling. Lily and Ben wondered what was going to happen. They held each other's hands.

A nurse came and called their names. She said they had to follow her. She took them to another room with a big chair and a table. She said they had to sit on the chair and roll up their sleeves. She said she was going to give them a tip. Lily and Ben did not know what that meant. They were very nervous.

The nurse took out a small bottle and a needle. She said it was a vaccine. She said it would protect them from getting sick. She said it would only hurt a little bit. She said they had to be brave. Lily and Ben did not want the vaccine. They wanted to run away.

The nurse gave Lily the tip first. She put the needle in her arm and pushed the plunger. Lily felt a sharp pain. She screamed and cried. She said it was not fair. She said she hated the nurse. She said she wanted her mom.

The nurse gave Ben the tip next. He saw the needle and heard his sister cry. He was terrified. He closed his eyes and clenched his teeth. He felt a dull ache. He whimpered and cried. He said it was too much. He said he hated the doctor. He said he wanted his dad.

The nurse put a band-aid on their arms and gave them a lollipop. She said they were done. She said they were very brave. She said they were healthy and strong. She said they could go back to their mom. Lily and Ben did not care. They still cried. They did not want the lollipop. They wanted to go home.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Emma. She was very excited because it was the fourth of July and that meant it was time to go out and see the fireworks. Her mommy and daddy took her to the park early in the evening. They all enjoyed watching the beautiful, colorful firework displays spark in the sky.

The next day, Emma was still talking about the firework show. She asked to hear the joke again and laughed like it was the first time she had heard it. Emma was happy and confused all at the same time.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Amy. She liked to help her mom cook food in the kitchen. One day, while her mom was away, Amy wanted to make a spicy soup for her family.

Amy went to the cabinet to find the spicy red pepper. She put a little bit in the soup, but she wanted the spicy taste to increase. So, she put more and more red pepper in the soup. The soup became very red and spicy.

When her mom came back, she saw the spicy soup and tasted it. "Wow, this is very spicy!" she said. Amy was happy that her mom liked the soup. From that day on, Amy always helped her mom in the kitchen and learned how to make many different kinds of food.

Once upon a time, there were two friends. One was named Tom and the other was named Jack. Tom and Jack were playing in the park when Jack found a long match. He thought it was extremely cool and he wanted to show Tom.
Tom said, "Cool! I want it!"
Jack said, "No, I found it. It's mine!"
Tom got angry and he said, "If you ignore me, I won't be your friend anymore!"

Once upon a time, there was a family. The family had a mom, a dad and a little girl. The little girl's name was Amy. Sometimes, Amy felt uncomfortable. That's when her parents were there to protect her.

One day, Amy wanted to eat something special. She wanted to eat jelly. Mommy and Daddy said she could have some of the jelly. They brought some jelly over and Amy ate it up! 

Amy felt so happy. She was so glad her parents were there to protect her and make her feel safe. Every time she felt uncomfortable, she knew that her parents were there to take care of her. That made her feel so much better.

Once upon a time, there was a big ranch. On this ranch, there were many animals. There were cows, horses, pigs, and chickens. They all lived together and played together.

One day, the sun was shining very bright. All the animals were happy and playing outside. But there was one little pig who felt ashamed. He thought he was not as good as the other animals. He wanted to shine like the sun, but he did not know how.

The little pig decided to ask his friends for help. The cow told the pig to be kind, the horse told him to be strong, and the chicken told him to be brave. The little pig listened to his friends and became kind, strong, and brave. Soon, the little pig felt like he was shining just like the sun. All the animals on the ranch were happy and proud of their friend, the little pig.

Once upon a time, there was a lazy dog named Mr. Fuzzy. Mr Fuzzy loved to sleep all day and he never did chores. One day, Mr Fuzzy's owner wanted to do a craft project with him. He showed Mr Fuzzy a pot of glue and asked him to help put together a picture. Even though he was lazy, Mr Fuzzy was very excited! He loved to use the glue and he ended up making the best picture ever. His owner was so proud of him! From that day on, he made sure to help with chores and crafts when they were asked of him. The end.

Mia and Sam liked to play on the beach. They liked to make sand castles and look for shells. One day, they saw something shiny and pink in the water. It looked like a flower.

"Look, Mia, a flower!" Sam said.

"Let's go see it!" Mia said.

They ran to the water and splashed in. They got closer and closer to the pink thing. But it was not a flower. It was a jellyfish.

"Ouch!" Sam cried. He felt a sting on his leg. He looked down and saw a red mark. He was scared and hurt.

"Sam, are you okay?" Mia asked. She saw the jellyfish and knew it was bad. She remembered what Mom had told them. "Don't touch the jellyfish, they can hurt you!"

She grabbed Sam's hand and pulled him out of the water. She ran to Mom and told her what happened.

Mom was worried and angry. She wrapped Sam's leg with a towel and put some cream on it. She hugged him and said, "I'm sorry, Sam. You'll be okay. But you have to be careful on the beach. Some things are not what they seem. Some things are beautiful but dangerous."

Mia nodded. She felt sorry for Sam. She looked at the jellyfish and thought, "You are not a flower. You are a mean jellyfish. I don't like you."

The enormous bird spread its wings happily. It soared up into the sky and over the trees. The bird passed a big field full of tall grass and then a small lake. It felt so good to be in the air. The bird was so hungry that he flew to the nearest tree. He was looking for a snack.

Suddenly, the bird spotted something delicious in the grass below. It was a piece of fruit! The bird flew down and gobbled it up in one bite. Now, he felt a little bit better.

The bird flew back up into the sky and felt the air rush through its feathers. He flew higher and higher until he found himself in the clouds. Here, he could soar and fly for as long as he wanted. Nothing felt better! The bird flew for hours and hours until the sun started to set and it finally decided to head back home. 

The enormous bird was feeling satisfied and happy. He had a snack and soared in the sky for most of the day! What a perfect day!

Once upon a time there was an elderly man. He liked nothing more than to go out and explore the world. So every morning, he would wake up extra early and start his day.

One morning, he decided to go for a walk. As he strolled along, he noticed a small child. The child was playing in the same spot, day after day. So the elderly man decided to stop and chat with the child. They talked for a while about different things, and then he said, "I always like to go exploring, it's so fun and exciting. Think about it - you never know what you'll find!"

The child smiled and said, "Maybe one day I'll do that too!"

The elderly man nodded and replied, "That's a great idea. Whenever you start to forget, I want you to remember what I said - every day is a new adventure, and it's good to explore!"

The child thanked him, and they said goodbye. The elderly man continued on his journey, while the child went back to playing. From that day on, the child never forgot to explore and have adventures. Whenever he started to forget, the elderly man's words would remind him.

Sam had a pocket. It was a useful pocket. Whenever Sam needed something, he would reach into his pocket and get it.

One day, Sam wanted to call his grandma. He reached into his pocket and pulled out a phone. He knew how to use it to call his grandma.

Sam looked at the number on the phone, then he pressed the buttons one by one. He heard a ringing sound. After a few seconds, his grandma answered.

He laughed and smiled as he ran, until finally he was all tuckered out and went back inside, safe and happy after his morning adventure in the mist.

Once upon a time, there lived a little girl. She was so excited because it was a sunny day. She raced outside to play in the sun.

Once upon a time, there were two best friends, Rob and Kim. They were both three years old. One day, Rob had an amazing idea. He wanted to play a game with Kim and make her laugh.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Jenny. She was three years old and lived with her mom, dad and dog named Poppy.

The next day, Jenny, her mom and Poppy went to the garden centre to buy some soil. When they got there, they chose the richest soil they could find. They brought it to their garden and spread it across the grass. 

Jenny, her mom and Poppy worked together to make the grass nice and soft. They trimmed the grass, watered it and covered it with fertilizer too.

Once upon a time, there was a little bunny named Benny. Benny loved to play outside in the garden. One day, Benny saw a little bird that was stuck in a tree. Benny wanted to help the bird, so he ran to get his dad.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a teddy bear named Teddy. One day, Teddy got lost and Lily was very sad. She cried and cried.

Once upon a time there was a little bear named Timmy. Timmy liked to lay in the sun and take naps. One day as he was laying in the sun, he heard a noise and he wondered what it was. He stood up alert, trying to find out where it was coming from.

Suddenly Timmy saw a squirrel sitting on the ground. The squirrel was shaking with fear and Timmy could see why. He had seen a big, scary bear nearby. Timmy quickly came to the rescue.

He walked up to the squirrel and put his shoulder under it, to show that he was a friendly bear. He said, â€œIt's okay, I'm here to help you.â€ The squirrel looked up at Timmy with relief and said, â€œThank you!â€

Timmy softly laid the squirrel down on the ground and it scampered away, happy and safe. Timmy felt proud of himself and puffed out his chest with pride, then laid back down in the sun to take a nap. The end.

Sara and Ben are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big basket of food on a bench. They are hungry, so they go to the basket.

"Look, Sara, there are apples and cheese and bread!" Ben says. "Let's eat some!"

"OK, Ben, but we have to be quick. Maybe someone will come back for the food," Sara says. She takes an apple and bites it. It is sweet and juicy.

Ben takes a piece of cheese and a slice of bread. He puts them together and makes a sandwich. He is happy. He sees a long green thing in the basket. He does not know what it is.

"What is this, Sara?" he asks, holding the green thing.

"That is celery, Ben. It is a vegetable. It is good for you," Sara says.

"Can I try it?" Ben asks.

"Sure, Ben. But be careful. It is crunchy and bitter," Sara says.

Ben takes a bite of the celery. He does not like it. It makes his mouth feel dry and sour. He spits it out.

"Yuck, Sara, this is bad! I don't like celery!" he says.

"Sorry, Ben. I like celery. It is fresh and healthy," Sara says.

They hear a loud voice behind them.

"Hey, you two! What are you doing with my food?" the voice says.

They turn around and see a big man. He is angry. He has a red face and a black hat. He is the owner of the basket.

"Uh-oh, Sara, we are in trouble!" Ben says.

They try to run away, but the man is faster. He grabs them by their arms and shakes them.

"How dare you steal my food, you little thieves! I work hard to buy this food for my family! You should be ashamed of yourselves!" the man says.

He takes the food from them and puts it back in the basket. He scolds them and tells them to go home. He says he will tell their parents what they did.

Sara and Ben are scared and sad. They cry and say they are sorry. They did not mean to steal the food. They were just hungry and curious.

The man does not listen. He is still angry. He pushes them away and leaves with his basket.

Sara and Ben walk home slowly. They are not friends anymore. They are mad at each other. Sara thinks Ben is silly and rude. Ben thinks Sara is mean and boring. They do not talk to each other.

They do not play in the park anymore. They do not eat celery anymore. They are not happy anymore.

Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to chew gum. He would buy gum from the store every day. But his mom told him that too much gum is not healthy for his teeth. So, Timmy decided to only chew one gum a day.

One day, Timmy went to the store to buy his gum. He saw a new kind of gum that was healthy. It had no sugar and was good for his teeth. Timmy was happy to find a gum that was good for him. He bought the healthy gum and went home to try it.

Timmy loved the healthy gum. He could chew it all day without worrying about his teeth. He was happy that he found a good gum at the store. From that day on, Timmy only bought the healthy gum and he had a big smile on his face. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. She had a friend named Olive. Olive was a kind and funny cat. They loved to play together every day.

One day, Lucy and Olive were playing with a ball. Lucy threw the ball very far and Olive ran to get it. But Olive accidentally broke a vase. Lucy's mom heard the noise and came to see what happened. "I'm sorry, Mom," said Olive. "I didn't mean to break it."

Lucy's mom was not happy, but she knew Olive was sorry. She said, "Olive, it's okay. Just try not to repeat it." Olive nodded and promised to be more careful.

From that day on, Olive always tried to be careful when playing with Lucy. They still had fun, but made sure not to break anything. And Lucy's mom was happy too.

The moral of the story is that it's okay to make mistakes, as long as we learn from them and try not to repeat them.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She loved going to the park with her mommy and daddy. One day, while at the park, she saw a little boy with a toy car. She asked him his name and he said it was Max.

One day, a boy named Tim had to unpack his toys. He had a big box full of them. Tim was very happy to see his toys again. He took them out one by one and put them on the floor. There were cars, dolls, and balls.

Once upon a time there was a grumpy girl called Lily. She was three years old and liked to complain about everything.

Once upon a time, there was a big, hairy bear who lived in the forest. He loved to play in the soil and dig holes with his paws. One day, he found a small, shiny rock and he wanted to keep it. Once upon a time, there was a mighty crib that rolled across the meadow. The rolling crib caught the attention of a little three year old girl and her puppy.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl called Mia. She was very impatient and wanted to find a dinosaur to wash. She looked all around but could not find one.

Once upon a time there was a girl called Sarah. She was very polite and always tried to act nicely. One day, Sarah's mum gave her a task to do. Once upon a time, there was a boy named Timmy. Timmy had big, thick sunglasses that he loved to wear. One sunny day, Timmy went outside to play with his friends. They decided to play tag and Timmy was "it". He ran around the yard, trying to tag his friends.

Tom and Anna were playing in the park. They liked to run and jump and slide. They saw a big hill with many trees. They wanted to see what was on the other side.

Timmy was happy again and continued to watch the trains go by. He couldn't wait to see the shiny red train again.

Once there was a little girl called Abi. She was 3 years old and loved to explore. One day, Abi spotted an aeroplane in the sky. She was so excited and said to her mum, "Mummy, mummy! An aeroplane! Can I go and explore it?".

Her mum said, "Be careful, Abi. You have to stay down here. We can't go up there in the sky. Let's just look at it from here." But Abi was curious and really wanted to explore the aeroplane. So, she started to climb a ladder to get closer to the aeroplane.

When she reached the top of the ladder, she saw that the aeroplane had lots of yummy treats. She was starving so she decided to take one. When she tasted the treat it was the most delicious thing she had ever tasted. 

Suddenly, Abi felt her eyes get heavy and realised that she was super tired. Moments later, she closed her eyes and fell off the ladder! Abi's mum was very worried when she didn't come home. 

The next day, Abi's mum went to the hospital and found out that Abi had eaten a bad treat that made her really ill and she was unable to wake up. Abi's mum was very sad, but she learnt a valuable lesson that day to always be careful, even when exploring.

Once upon a time, there was a big, brown bear. He had a thick, furry paw. It was his favourite part of him. 

One day, the bear went out for a walk. When he was in the woods, he couldn't find his paw. He had lost it! 

He looked for it for a long time, but it seemed like it had disappeared. He was so sad, he started to cry. 

Just then, a little bird came and said, "I saw something thick in the big tree over there - it might be your paw". 

The bear quickly ran to the tree, and sure enough, there was his thick, furry paw! He gave the bird his biggest and warmest bear hug and thanked her for finding his paw. 

The bear and his paw stayed in the forest, happy ever after.

Once, there were two friends called Mary and Ben. Mary had a big bowl of salad. It was red, green and yellow. She wanted Ben to help her sort it. Mary said to Ben, "Can you help me sort this salad?"

Ben said, "Sure!" and they started to sort the salad. They put the red tomatoes and lettuce in one big bowl and the green cucumbers and peppers in another bowl. Then, they put the yellow lemons in a small bowl.

When they finished sorting the salad, Mary smiled and said, "Thanks for helping me sort the salad, Ben!"

Ben smiled back and said, "You're welcome!" They both laughed and ate the salad. It tasted delicious.

Once upon a time, in a fair, sunny land, there was a big bear named Bob. Bob loved to eat honey. He would find honey in the trees and eat it all day. The sweet taste made him very happy.

One day, Bob met a small bee named Betty. Betty did not like Bob, because he ate all the honey. She would say, "I hate that you take our honey, Bob." But Bob did not care. He just wanted to eat more honey.

Betty wanted to teach Bob a lesson. She gathered all her bee friends and they made a plan. The next time Bob tried to eat honey, the bees buzzed and stung him. It hurt, and Bob ran away. He learned to share the honey with the bees and not be greedy. From that day on, Bob and Betty became friends, and they all lived happily in the fair, sunny land.

Once there was a little girl named Lucy. She loved to count. One day her mommy gave her a new shirt. It was a very fine shirt.

Lucy couldn't wait to try it on. She put on the shirt and it fit perfectly. Then Lucy started counting. She counted all the buttons on her new shirt. She counted one, two, three, four! She was so proud that she knew how to count.

After she finished counting the buttons, she went outside to show off her new shirt. She waved and smiled to all the people she saw. Everyone said that her shirt was very fine.

When she got back home, she looked in the mirror. She counted her toes, fingers and then the buttons on her shirt. She counted one, two, three, four. She was so happy that she could count.

Lucy now loves to count everything she sees. Every time she gets a new shirt, she counts the buttons and knows how to count them all. Counting makes her feel so proud.

One day, a little girl and her mum went to the park. The little girl was wearing a modest pink dress and a yellow helmet. As soon as they arrived, the little girl ran towards the slide. Before she could get to the bottom, her mum called her.

Mum: "Where do you want to hide?"

The little girl ran around the park, looking for a perfect spot to hide. She eventually found a bush and hid behind it. She quietly waited for her mum to find her. When her mum finally spotted her, the little girl laughed and jumped out from behind the bush.

Mum: "You did a great job at hiding! Let's do it again!"

The little girl smiled and ran off to find another hiding spot.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named John. John loved exploring and discovering new things. One day, he was walking through the park in his town. He noticed a strange bush he hadn't seen before. 

John was excited and decided to take a closer look. He reached out and touched the bush, and suddenly he discovered something special. It was a jar of sauce! 

John was delighted. He opened the jar to find a delicious red sauce. He tasted it and it was yummy! John was so happy he had discovered this amazing sauce. 

He ran home to tell his mom about the sauce. His mom was so thrilled, she said that now she had a special sauce available to make any food more tasty! 

John was proud of his discovery and was excited to use the sauce with all sorts of meals. He shared it with all his friends, so they could enjoy it too. 

The End.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl and her family. They decided to have a picnic in the park. The little girl was so excited and couldnâ€™t wait to go.

When the family arrived, the little girl saw a big hill, so she asked her dad, â€œCan we climb it, please?â€ Her dad said, â€œThatâ€™s a great idea! Letâ€™s go!â€

The little girl's dad was so generous that he said, â€œLetâ€™s have our picnic up here. That way we can enjoy the view.â€ The little girl smiled and agreed.

Once upon a time there was a beautiful lake. It sparkled in the sunshine and shimmered in the moonlight. Everyone who visited thought it was the most wonderful thing they had ever seen. 

One day, a group of animals decided to take a dip. The water was so calm and peaceful that they all quickly fell asleep. Suddenly, just as the birds were beginning to sing, something split the lake right in two. Steam rose up like a curtain, filling the sky with clouds.

The animals were very scared, so they started running. They wanted to get away from the steam as fast as they could. Sadly, the steam surrounded them and there was nowhere to go. The poor creatures were all split apart from each other, and in the end, the beautiful lake was no more.

Anna likes to help her mom in the kitchen. She puts on a pink apron and a big smile. She wants to make a cake for dad's birthday. Mom gives her a bowl and a spoon. She says, "Mix the flour, the sugar, and the eggs."

Anna tries to mix, but she is clumsy. She spills some flour on the floor. She drops some sugar on the table. She breaks an egg on her apron. She says, "Oops! Sorry, mom!"

Mom laughs and hugs her. She says, "It's okay, Anna. You are learning. Let me help you." She wipes the mess and adds some butter and milk. She pours the batter into a pan and puts it in the oven. She says, "Now we wait for the cake to bake."

Anna waits and smells the cake. It smells yummy. She says, "Can I eat some, mom?" Mom says, "Not yet, Anna. We have to wait for dad to come home. Then we can surprise him with the cake and sing happy birthday."

Anna nods and smiles. She loves her mom and dad. She loves to help in the kitchen. She loves to eat cake. She thinks, "Maybe next time I will be less clumsy."

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Timmy. Timmy loved to dream about flying in the sky. One day, Timmy woke up from a rare dream and went to his mom. "Mommy, can you answer a question for me?" Timmy asked. "Of course, sweetie," his mom replied. "In my dream, I was flying. Can people really fly like birds?" Timmy asked. His mom smiled and said, "No, people can't fly like birds, but you can use your imagination to fly in your dreams." Timmy was happy with his mom's answer and went back to bed to dream about flying again.

Sara and Ben are twins. They like to play with their toys and books. They have many toys and books, because their dad is rich. He works in a big building and wears a nice suit.

One day, Sara and Ben hear a knock on the door. They run to see who it is. It is their grandma. They love their grandma. She always brings them gifts and hugs. She arrives with a big smile and a big bag.

"Hello, my darlings!" she says. "I have something special for you today. Do you want to see?"

Sara and Ben nod and clap. They follow their grandma to the living room. She opens her bag and takes out two boxes. One is blue and one is pink. She gives the blue one to Ben and the pink one to Sara.

"What is it, grandma?" they ask.

"It is a surprise. You have to open it and see," she says. She winks at them.

Sara and Ben open their boxes. Inside, they find two dolls. They are not like their other dolls. They are soft and fluffy and have big eyes and ears. They are bunny dolls.

"Wow!" Sara and Ben say. "They are so cute! Thank you, grandma!"

They hug their grandma and their bunny dolls. They are very happy. They name their dolls Floppy and Hoppy. They play with them all day. They make them jump and dance and talk. They have a lot of fun.

Their grandma watches them and smiles. She is glad to see them so happy. She loves her grandchildren very much. She thinks they are the best gift in the world.

Once upon a time, there was a kind angel named Lily. She had fair wings and a shiny halo on her head. She lived in a big white cloud in the sky.

One day, Lily decided to serve the animals on Earth. She flew down to the forest and saw a little rabbit who was lost. Lily picked up the rabbit and brought it back to its family. The rabbit was very happy and thanked Lily.

Lily continued to serve the animals in the forest. She helped a bird build its nest and gave some water to a thirsty squirrel. All the animals were grateful to Lily for her kindness. From that day on, Lily became known as the angel who served all the creatures on Earth.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Amy. She was only three years old and felt very small compared to the adults around her.

One day Amy was feeling very worried. She had forgotten to use the toilet before leaving home, and now she really needed to go.

Amy asked her mum if they could hurry to the toilet. Her mum said yes, they could run as fast as they could.

Amy and her mum raced to the nearest toilet. As soon as they arrived, Amy used the toilet as fast as she could and felt much better.

This story shows us that it's ok to worry sometimes, especially when something important needs to be done. And it's always best to listen to your grown ups and do what they say!

Once there was a little girl named Jane. She loved to spend time outside looking at the world around her. Today, she was going to go down to the river to have a bath.

When she got there, Jane gasped with delight. The river was so beautiful, with sparkling water and colourful fish swimming around. She couldn't wait to jump in.

Jane took off her clothes and started to bathe in the river. All around her, the cool water tickled her skin and she felt so light and free. She laughed and splashed around, having the best time.

But then, the river got dull. The sparkles had gone and the fish began to swim away. Suddenly, Jane was scared and wanted to get out. She ran as fast back to the bank and got dressed.

When she was all done, Jane packed up her things and headed home. The river was still dull, but she promised to go back another day and try again.

Ben and Lily were playing in the park when it started to rain. They ran to find a shelter, but all the benches and trees were wet. They saw a big box near the trash can and decided to hide inside.

"Look, we have a shelter!" Lily said. "We are dry and warm!"

"Yes, we are!" Ben agreed. "But we are also hungry. Do you have any snacks?"

Lily checked her backpack and found a bottle of juice and a cookie. She shared them with Ben and they felt happy.

"Thank you, Lily!" Ben said. "You are a good friend!"

They heard the rain pour harder and harder on the box. They wondered when it would stop.

"Maybe we can make a game," Lily suggested. "Let's pretend we are on a boat and the rain is the sea. We can sing and tell stories!"

"Okay, that sounds fun!" Ben said. "What song do you want to sing?"

They started to sing their favorite nursery rhymes and made up stories about pirates and mermaids. They forgot about the rain and had a lot of fun. They were successful in making their own adventure.

Once there was a young girl named Sandy. She liked to go to the park every day and play with her friends. One day, when Sandy was playing in the park, she saw a man who was sleeping on a bench. She decided to be kind and make him a sandwich. 

Sandy made a sandwich and was about to give it to the man. But before she could do so, he woke up and began to yell and disturb everyone. He was very angry and started throwing things around. 

Sandy was scared and quickly ran away. Even though she had tried to do something nice for the man, he was so mad that he disturbed the peace. Sandy learned a valuable lesson that day: being too nice can sometimes get you into trouble.

Once upon a time, there was a little bear named Ben. Ben lived in a big forest with his friends. One day, Ben and his friends went to pick berries. They found a big barrel full of berries.

Ben said, "I want to take this barrel home."

His friend, Sally, said, "No, Ben. The barrel is too big. It won't fit in your house."

Ben felt sorry for asking. He said, "I didn't know. Thanks for telling me. What can I do?"

His friend, Timmy, said, "We can share the berries. We can each take some home."

Ben felt happy that his friends allowed him to share the berries. They each took some berries home and had a yummy snack.

One sunny day, a boy named Jack peeked out of his bedroom window. He saw the beautiful sky and it made him very happy. He quickly got dressed, grabbed a toy and ran outside.

Jack saw a cat hiding under the bush and thought it was so funny. He said to the cat, "Hi there! Come out, I won't hurt you!"

The cat didn't want to come out at first, so Jack waited patiently. Suddenly, the cat peeked out from the other side of the bush.

Jack was so happy that the cat came out to say hi. He reached down and patted the cat's back with his hand. The cat was happy too and curled up at Jack's feet.

Jack and the cat were fast friends and were happy to have each other for company. They spent the entire day playing together and had an amazing time. Jack knew he'd found a special friend that day, and he couldn't have been happier.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved going to the market with her mom. One day, Lily saw a toy she really wanted at the market. She asked her mom to buy it for her, but her mom said they didn't have enough money.

Lily felt sad and unhappy. But then, she saw a little boy who looked even sadder than her. He had lost his toy car and couldn't find it. Lily felt sorry for him and decided to give him her favorite toy. The little boy was so happy and gave Lily a big hug.

Even though Lily didn't get the toy she wanted, she felt happy because she made someone else happy. The moral of the story is that it's better to make others happy than to just think about ourselves. And sometimes, the best things in life can't be bought at the market.

Once there lived a loyal mouse. He had a mustache that was very long and fancy. Every day he ate yummies-- things like cheese, crumbs, and popcorn.

One day, he saw something very interesting. It looked like a bigger mustache than his! It twitched, like a tiny animal. He stepped closer and discovered it was in fact a caterpillar!

The mouse was very excited. He offered the caterpillar some of his cheese, and the caterpillar gladly accepted. They became fast friends.

Every day, the mouse shared his food with the caterpillar. The caterpillar was very loyal and thankful for the mouse's help.

Eventually, the caterpillar grew wings and flew away. But before he left, he showed the mouse how to make his mustache even longer and more fancy. The loyal mouse was very excited, and thanked his friend for the advice.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Max. Max was an enthusiastic dog who loved to play outside. One day, he saw dark clouds in the sky. Max knew a storm was coming, but he still wanted to play.

Max went to his friend, the big tree. The tree would bow when the wind blew. Max liked to watch the tree bow and play with its leaves. The storm came, and the wind blew strong. The tree bowed more and more, and Max was very excited.

After the storm, Max and the tree were happy. They played together in the sun. Max loved to play with his friend, the big tree. And they lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time there lived a friendly cat. The cat loved to work. Every day it worked to get food for itself, and then it would go for a walk in the garden.

One day, the cat was working in the garden when it heard a voice. 
"Mew! Mew!" said the voice. 
The cat looked up and saw a little girl. 
"Hi there!" said the girl. "What are you doing?"

The cat purred and said, "I'm working. I'm getting food." 
The little girl smiled and said, "That's cool. Can I help?" 

The cat nodded and said, "Sure! You can help me get food." They worked together, and the cat showed the little girl all the spots it liked to get food from. Soon enough, they had enough for a meal. 

The cat and the little girl were now good friends. They worked together every day in the garden, and the cat always showed the little girl where to get the best food. 

The end.

Once upon a time there was a graceful fisherman. He lived on the shore of a beautiful lake. Everyday he went to the lake to go fishing. One day he decided to go canoeing. He got into his canoe and paddled downstream. He felt the gentle breeze on his face and the sun warming his skin. He was so happy!

Suddenly he heard a splash in the water. He looked over and saw a big fish swimming in the lake. The fisherman had an idea. He decided to use his net to try and catch the fish. He cast the net out and the fish swam right into it. He pulled the net up and the fish landed in the boat. He was so excited! The fisherman had decided to catch a fish and he did it!

The fisherman took the fish home and cooked it for dinner. He shared the meal with his family and everyone enjoyed the delicious fish. Thanks to the fisherman's decision, they all had a wonderful dinner. His gracefullness had paid off!

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Lily. She liked to play in the garden. One day, when she was playing, her Dad called her, so she went inside to see what he wanted.

Dad said, "Lily, we're going on a journey! We have to pack our things and get in the van".

Lily was excited. She quickly grabbed her favourite toy, her teddy bear, and ran to the van. But before they could leave, Dad said, "Lily, we need to wake up early in the morning, ok?" 

Lily was scared. She didn't like getting up early, she was much more comfortable when she could sleep in. But Dad just told Lily not to worry, he said, "It'll be fun, I promise." 

The next morning they woke up bright and early and stepped into the van. They drove for a while until they arrived at a beach. Lily had never seen so much sand! She smiled and clapped her hands. Even though she had been scared of waking up early, it was all worth it.

Once upon a time there was a shy little girl named Amy. She liked to clean her room every day before she went to bed. One day, she was in her room and looked out the window - the view was breathtaking! But she was too shy to go outside.

Amy was feeling frustrated. She wanted to explore the outside view but she was scared of being seen by the neighbors. She didnâ€™t know what to do! She decided to clean her room harder to help her make up her mind.

After an hour of cleaning, Amy got a brilliant idea! She thought if she kept her room neat and tidy, the neighbors wouldnâ€™t be able to see her when she looked out the window. With a little courage, Amy finally went outside and enjoyed the beautiful view. 

The end.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Joe and Gina. Joe was brave and liked to do daring things. One day, he saw an old tree with thick branches. He asked Gina if she would dare to climb it. Gina was afraid and said no, but Joe kept asking her until she agreed. Joe started to climb first and Gina followed.

When Gina was almost at the top of the tree, it began to move and she started to feel scared. Joe told her to keep going and find the solution. Gina then looked up and saw that the old tree was shaking not because it was dangerous, but because a bird's nest was on the top of it. The bird was scared and tried to protect its nest.

Gina then understood that she should not be afraid anymore and she slowly stepped down from the tree. The bird was so happy and thankful that it sang very loudly. Joe was also happy and knew that he should learn to be quiet at certain times.

The moral of the story is that although it may be hard to be brave, it can also be important to be quiet.

Once upon a time, there was a friendly dog named Max. Max liked to play with his toys all day long. One day, Max's friend, a cat named Lily, came to visit him. Lily wanted to play with Max's toys too. Max thought about it and decided to share his toys with Lily. They played together and had so much fun!

Later that day, Max's owner took him to the vet for an operation. Max was a little scared, but he knew it was important to be healthy. The vet was very friendly and made Max feel comfortable. After the operation, Max felt much better and was happy to be back home with his toys and his friend Lily.

One day, Jimmy decided he wanted to try something new. He wanted to be special, to be gifted, so he went looking for a way to make that happen.

Jimmy found out that to be gifted, he had to learn to count. So, he began to demand numbers from the sky. First one, then two and three, and so on.

Surprisingly, he got an answer from the sky. It said that at the end of the numbers, he should reach zero. Zero was special and the most important number of all.

Jimmy was so excited. He started counting up again. When he got to zero, a sparkling light appeared.

The light started to spin around Jimmy and then, suddenly, he felt gifted. He had the power to do anything he wanted!

Jimmy was so happy! All thanks to zero!

Once upon a time, there was a dog who had a very keen eye. He wanted to listen to everything that was going on around him. He sat and watched the people walking in the street, carefully listening to the sounds they were making.

The dog heard a noise that was really tasty. He pricked up his ears and listened carefully. He heard a voice singing a beautiful song. He knew it was coming from an old house nearby.

The dog was so curious he walked over to the house and listened carefully. Through the window he heard a nice man singing and playing a guitar. The dog was so happy that he wagged his tail and tried to join in.

The nice man saw the dog and opened the door. The singing had made the dog very hungry so the man gave him something tasty. The dog thanked him with a big doggy hug, then he lay down by his side and listened to the beautiful music for the rest of the day.

Lizzie was a little girl who loved to play in her garden. One day, she saw a little wagon in the garden. It was so pretty! She figured out how to make it bounce. She hopped in the wagon and started bouncing. She laughed and laughed as she bounced around the garden.

Lizzie bounced higher and higher. She smiled as she felt the wind against her face. Lizzie bounced so high that she ended up in the air! She had never been so high before. 

When she finally came back to earth, her wagon had bounced away. She could see it moving further and further away. She ran after it as fast as she could. But she couldn't catch up!

Finally, Lizzie's parents saw her chasing the little wagon and ran to help her. Daddy caught the wagon and put it back in the garden. Lizzie hugged them and thanked them.

From that day forward, Lizzie and her parents enjoyed playing together in the garden, bouncing around in the little wagon.

Once upon a time, there was a group of friends. The friends were very enthusiastic about having fun. One day, they all decided to play a game. They were going to use lots of stamps and they wanted to unite them all together. So they took their stamps and put them into a pile.

The friends were so excited to put them all together to make something special. First, they put the red stamps. Then, they put the blue stamps. Finally, they put the yellow stamps. When the stamps were all together, it looked very pretty!

Everyone was so happy about it. The friends hugged each other and cheered for the pretty stamps that they united together. They all thought it was such a fun game and they wanted to do it again.

The End.

Once upon a time, there was a gifted little girl. Every day, she rose early and went to the fields to help harvest wheat. Her friends came along to help her, and they all had a lot of fun.

One day, when they were done gathering the wheat, the little girl called out to her friends, "Let's make a big tower out of the wheat!" Everyone cheered and said it was a great idea.

So they all worked together to build the tower. They rose one wheat stalk at a time until it was as tall as they were! They were so proud of their tower and they all cheered when it was done.

The little girl then smiled and said, "Together, we really can do anything!" Her friends agreed, and they laughed as they ran off to play.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a big bookshelf in her room that was always busy with books. One day, Lily's mom asked her to clean up her room. 

Lily said, "Mommy, I don't want to clean up my room. Can I do it later?" 

Mommy said, "No, Lily. You need to clean up now." 

Lily didn't want to, but she knew she had to accept her mommy's request. So, she cleaned up her room and put all the books back on the busy bookshelf. 

After she finished, she felt proud of herself and said, "Look, Mommy! My room is clean now." 

Mommy smiled and said, "Good job, Lily. Now, let's go play outside." 

Lily was happy and they went outside to play together. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a girl named Lily. She had a big red apple that she wanted to eat. She took a bite and it tasted very yummy. Then she cut the apple into small pieces with a sharp knife. She shared the apple with her friends and they all said thank you. Lily's mom said the knife was very useful for cutting the apple. The end.

Once upon a time there was a girl called Pippa. One day, Pippa's mommy gave her a piece of paper. Pippa was a bit nervous so she asked, "What for?"

Her mommy smiled and said, "Guess!" 

Pippa thought and thought, but she didn't know. She asked her mommy again, "But what is it?"

Her mommy just smiled and said, "You have to guess". 

Pippa was getting more and more nervous. She wasn't sure what was going on and she desperately wanted to know what was on the paper. 

Finally, her mommy said, "It's a surprise!" Pippa's eyes lit up. She was so excited that she couldn't wait any more. With a big smile she said, "Can I see it now?"

Her mommy said, "No. We have to wait for the surprise. Keep guessing and you'll find out soon". 

Pippa was so excited! She kept guessing and guessing what the surprise could be, until finally the day arrived. When her mommy opened up the paper, Pippa saw it was an invitation to her own birthday party!

Once upon a time, there were two best friends, Eric and Jane. They were the very best of friends, and they always had so much fun together.
One day, Eric invited Jane on an exciting adventure with him.
"Come with me," he said, "I have a surprise for you."
"Oh! What is it?" said Jane excitedly.

Eric took Jane up a big hill and showed her a long spool of red thread.
"This is the surprise!" Eric said. "Let's play a game with this thread. Follow the thread and see what surprise is at the end."
So Eric and Jane followed the red thread. It was difficult, because they had to jump over rocks and go through tall bushes. But eventually they got to the end of the thread, and there was a beautiful lake.
Eric and Jane were so happy that they had followed the thread, because now they could go swimming in the lake.
So Eric and Jane had lots of fun swimming in the lake. It was a great adventure that Eric had invited Jane on!

Toby was a little boy who wanted to play with the other children. However, all the children were too busy to remember to include Toby. Toby was getting very jealous.

Finally, when Toby was walking by, he saw the other children playing a game. He asked if he could join in, but all the kids just looked away. Toby was so sad.

Just then, Toby noticed that the other boys were pinching each other on their left arms. He ran up to them, and asked if he could join in too.

The other boys looked at each other. "You can join if you pinch the left arm of each of us," they said.

Toby smiled and said, "Yes!" He pinched each of the boys on the left arm and they all laughed. From then on, Toby was welcomed in the group and everyone was very happy.

Once there was a little girl named Mandy. She was three years old and she loved to explore the world around her. One day, Mandy got an idea. She wanted to test the creek near her house. 

Mandy went to the creek and compared it to other creeks she had seen. She noticed that this one was very colorful. There were beautiful stones in all different colors surrounding the creek. Mandy wanted to explore the creek, so she started to walk in.
 
Suddenly, Mandy's mom called out to her. She was giving Mandy a warning to stay away from the creek. Mandy was not allowed to go any further. Mandy was very disappointed, but she listened to her mother.

Mandy thought of another way to test the creek. She collected all kinds of colorful stones, twigs and leaves and threw them
into the creek to see what would happen. She was very curious to see if her experiment worked. 

The creek was still beautiful and colorful, but Mandy had to stay out of it. Still, she was happy that she was able to test it in a different way. She was sure to remember the colorful creek and all the fun she had that day.

One day, a boy named Josh went on a walk in his town. He was looking for an adventure. So he walked around until he found something special. He found a big tower with a big door. Josh thought it looked exciting. He knocked on the door but nobody answered.

Josh kept knocking until the door finally opened and he went inside. Inside the tower he found a lot of treasures. But then, he heard a sad voice coming from a corner. He turned around and saw a sad old man. 

Josh asked the old man why he was so sad. The man told Josh that he was sad because he had been locked inside the tower for a long time and he wanted to leave. Josh was so sorry to hear that. He told the old man he would help him, so he opened the door and carried the old man outside. 

Finally, the old man was free. He smiled, thanked Josh and started walking away. But as soon as he stepped out of the tower, the door slammed shut and Josh was stuck inside the tower forever. 

The old man never came back to help Josh. Josh was very sad and he never found his way out of the tower.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. One day, she went to the ice cream truck and received a cone with her favorite flavor, chocolate. She was so happy and ate it quickly.

Suddenly, the sky turned gloomy and it started to rain. Lily didn't like the rain because it made her wet and she couldn't play outside. She said to her mom, "Mommy, I don't like the rain. It's gloomy outside."

Her mom replied, "Don't worry, Lily. We can play inside and have fun. Maybe we can make some cookies together." Lily smiled and said, "Yay! I love cookies. Thank you, Mommy." And they spent the rest of the day baking and playing together.

One day, a boy named Tim and his dad wanted to build a big sand castle. It was a hot day at the beach. They took their shovels and started to dig. Tim's dad said, "We need to make the sand wet to build a strong castle." Tim nodded and went to get water from the sea.

As Tim walked to the sea, he saw a man with a long whip. The man was showing people how to make big, fun shapes with the whip. Tim watched and thought, "I want to try that too!" But he remembered the sand castle, so he filled his bucket with water and went back to his dad.

When they finished the sand castle, Tim told his dad about the man with the whip. They went to see him together. The man showed Tim how to use the whip. Tim made a big circle in the air and everyone clapped. At the end of the day, Tim and his dad went home, happy with their big sand castle and the fun they had with the whip.

Once upon a time, there was a happy figure called Little Red. Little Red was always looking around, hopping and nodding.

One day, she saw a secret place and wanted to go inside. She felt a little bit scared, but she decided to nod and go in.

Inside, she saw a happy surprise! It was her best friend, Big Bear. They hugged each other tightly and smiled.

Little Red and Big Bear had a lot of fun together. They played catch and giggled for a long time.

When it was time for Little Red to go home, she said goodbye and nodded at Big Bear. Little Red skipped all the way home, feeling very happy.

Once upon a time there was a boy. He was three years old and he wanted to go on a trip. He was so excited and couldn't wait.

So, his mummy and daddy packed a bag and they grabbed the car keys. Off they went on a wide, wide trip.

The boy saw so many things along the way. He saw farms with animals, and trees with big branches. He even saw a castle.

Then, mummy and daddy stopped the car and said, "Let's have a picnic!" They put down a blanket and the boy was allowed to hold a sandwich. He ate it slowly, with a smile on his face.

The trip was so fun and the boy was so happy, he didn't want it to end. So he held onto his mummy's hand and said, "Can we go again next week?"

Once there was a boy named Sam. He was three years old and loved to play.

One day, Sam saw a stack of blocks outside. They were quite unusual because they were covered in glitter. Sam wanted to find out what was underneath the sparkly cover.

He carefully started to take off the glitter. As he did, he found lots of soft toys! There were bears, birds and many more, all different colours and sizes. Sam started to play with them and was very happy. He stacked them up into a big pile and covered them with the glitter again.

Sam smiled and laughed; he had made an unusual stack of soft toys and covered them in sparkles!

One day, Spot and Sue went to the park. Spot had a kite, and was excited to try it out. They found the perfect place and began to fly the kite. Spot was so happy and grateful. They watched the kite fly in circles and zig zags in the sky.

Now it was time to put the kite away. Sue helped Spot bury it in the soft grass. When it was safe and buried, Spot said goodbye to the kite and thanked it for the fun. Then they went home, with an exciting memory of flying the kite.
