Mum gave Tony a delicious apple for a snack. He ate it in the kitchen and was happy. Then he went to the desk in the living room and did a drawing. He wanted to show it to Mum. 

But when he looked back at the desk, the paper was spoiled. Tony had dropped a bit of apple juice on it. He was sad.

Mum came in to check on Tony and saw the paper. But she was not mad. She gave Tony a hug and said it was OK. Then she gave him a cloth and showed him how to clean up the desk.

Tony was so happy. He cleaned up the desk and then he drew a new picture. Mum said it was even better than the first and gave him another delicious apple to reward him.

Once upon a time, there was a little ant who wanted to bake a cake. She gathered some flour and sugar, and she found some eggs from the farmerâ€™s market.

She mixed the ingredients together and put it all in a baking dish. She opened the oven and put the cake inside.

The ant waited and waited, until finally she saw the cake was ready! It looked so good and smelled even better.

The ant took the cake out of the oven and enjoyed a nice big piece. It was so delicious, she ate the whole thing! 

Moral of the story: something good can come out of a tiny bit of effort!

Once upon a time, there was a man who had a hammer. The hammer was special because it was used to help build things. The man used the hammer every day to help build things and make them better.

One day, the man went to work with his hammer. He was very alert because he was looking for something special. He looked and looked, but he couldn't see anything. He was starting to feel sad, until he saw something shiny in a corner. He ran over to it and saw it was a magical hammer. He was so happy and he hoped it would help him even more.

The man put the magical hammer to work. He used it to build new things and make old things look better. Everywhere he went, people were amazed with what he built. He was so proud of his magical hammer and he kept on using it every day.

He looked around and saw that with his help, everything was getting better. He hoped that this would continue and that the magical hammer would make a big difference. He was so happy and thankful for what his hammer could do!

Once upon a time, there was a big castle where a king lived. He was very important and everyone liked him because he was charming. One day, a little girl went to the castle to see the king. She saw him walking in the garden and she wanted to talk to him. But the king was too tall, so the little girl asked him to kneel down. The king was surprised, but he did it anyway. The little girl told him that she liked his castle and that he was a very nice king. The king was happy to hear that and he gave her a candy. The little girl was very happy and she went back home with a big smile on her face.

Once upon a time there was a small bunny. He loved sweets, but his mom told him not to eat too many. One day, the bunny snuck out of the house and hopped over to the temple. It was a very special temple and the bunny was curious about what he might find.

When he arrived, he saw a delicate, white flower. He wanted to taste it, so he reached out and plucked the petals from the stem. To his surprise, it tasted like the sweetest honey he had ever tried!

The bunny should have listened to his mom, as it was not a good idea to take the flower. Suddenly, the bunny felt a strange feeling in his stomach and he ran all the way home.

He learned an important lesson that day; it is never a good idea to take something that does not belong to you. He happily listened to his momâ€™s advice and ate the sweets that she gave him. He was careful not to taste anything he wasn't supposed to!

Mia was a little girl and she was three years old. She had a pretty dress and she loved to wear it with her shoes. One day, Mia and her mama decided to go the pool. Mia couldn't wait to get there.

When they arrived, Mia was very excited. She put on her swimming suit and jumped in the pool. She swam around and around and had so much fun. After a while, mama said "Mia it's time for lunch, let's go eat something."

Mia jumped out of the pool and dried off. She put on her pretty dress and followed Mama to a restaurant. Mama said "Mia, what do you want to eat?" Mia said, "I want a yummy hamburger with French fries!" Mama told her that sounded delicious.

Mia and Mama ate their lunch together. After they finished eating, they went back to the pool. Mia had so much fun splashing around. She said to Mama, "This was a pretty great day!"

Once upon a time, there was a little girl who was three years old. She loved to ride her shiny red bicycle. Every day she would set out on her bicycle and explore the world.

One day, after riding her bicycle around, she felt very dizzy. She had been riding for too long and needed a break. So, she set her bicycle down and went for a walk.

On her walk, she found a beautiful big tree with lots of shade. She sat down under the tree and looked up. She saw lots of little leaves blowing in the wind. It was so beautiful that it made her dizzy again!

So, she set herself down and had a nice rest. It was just what she needed to get her energy back. When she was feeling better, she got back on her bicycle and set off to explore the world again.

Once there was an orange cable. It lay in the grass all day long and it was very, very hungry.

"I wish I had something to eat," said the cable.

Just then, a big blue bird flew by carrying an orange in its beak. 

"That looks delicious," said the cable. 

"Would you please give me a bite to eat?"

The bird looked down and said, "That's very kind of you to ask, I shall share it with you".

The bird flew down and dropped the orange near the cable.

The cable quickly gobbled up the orange, juice dripping from its face.

"Thank you," said the cable, feeling full and happy. 

The bird smiled and flew away while the cable stayed in the grass, full and content.

One day, a little girl named Sally was playing in her kitchen. She wanted to make a special drink. She had a big grape and a cup. She was worried because she did not know how to mix them.

Sally asked her mom, "Mom, can you help me mix the grape and the cup?" Her mom said, "Sure, Sally. Let's mix them together and see what happens."

But when they tried to mix the grape and the cup, the grape was too big. It did not fit in the cup. Sally was sad and worried. She did not know what to do.

Then, her dad came in and saw Sally was worried. He said, "Don't worry, Sally. We can cut the grape into small pieces and then mix it in the cup." Sally and her dad cut the grape and put the small pieces in the cup.

Sally was happy. She mixed the grape pieces in the cup and made a yummy drink. She was not worried anymore.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy. His name was Jack. He was three years old and he loved to explore. One day he went for an adventure in the woods. He saw a stream and admired the open blue sky above it. It glistened in the sunlight like a shining river of diamonds.

Jack bent down and played with the stream. He watched the little fish swimming around, and marveled at how they moved so gracefully in the water. Then he noticed something else. Something he had never seen before. 

Jack exclaimed, "Mommy, look! A big hole in the ground!"

His mom replied, "Oh, that's a cave! It looks like a fun place to explore, let's go inside and take a look!"

So Jack and his mom explored the cave. Jack was amazed. He couldn't believe he was inside of this big and open cave. He said, "Wow!" and his mom smiled, proud of her brave boy. 

Jack admired the beauty of the cave and enjoyed exploring. He learned about the importance of being safe and having fun in the open outdoors. 

The end.

Once upon a time, there was a dog named Spot. Spot loved to keep his favorite bone close to him at all times. He would carry it in his mouth and never let it go.

One day, Spot went for a walk with his owner. His owner told him to keep his heel down and stay close. Spot wagged his tail in agreement and followed his owner's instructions.

As they walked, Spot suddenly stopped and looked at his owner with sad eyes. His bone had fallen out of his mouth and he didn't even notice. His owner saw that Spot's mouth was empty and knew what had happened. She quickly went back to look for the bone and found it in the grass.

Spot was so happy to have his bone back that he licked his owner's face in gratitude. From that day on, Spot learned to keep a tighter grip on his bone and never let it out of his sight.

Once upon a time there was a kind girl named Sally. Sally always wanted to share with her friends. One day she had a special card. It was harmless but very special to Sally. She decided to take it to show her friends.

When Sally got to her friends' house, she showed them the card. Her friends were so excited! They loved to see the harmless card. Sally smiled and said, "Let's share this card with everyone!" The friends all agreed and they went outside to share the card with all of their neighbours.

The neighbours yawned and went back to their homes. But when they opened their doors, they were met with a big surprise! Sally and her friends had left the harmless card on everyone's doorstep.

The neighbours couldn't believe it! They smiled and thanked Sally and her friends for the wonderful gift. From that day forward, Sally and her friends were always sharing harmless cards with their neighbours. Everyone was happy!

Once upon a time there was a little girl who loved eating cereal. Every morning she would think about what kind of cereal she wanted to eat. One morning she felt a bit different. She felt uncomfortable. She decided to think about it and see why she felt this way.

After a few minutes, she remembered that she had eaten the same cereal for breakfast the last two days. She smiled and realised the reason why she had felt a bit uncomfortable â€“ she wanted to have a different cereal!

The little girl opened the cupboard, and found a brand new box of cereal that she had never seen before. She couldn't wait to eat it! After dinner, she opened the box and poured some cereal into her bowl. It tasted delicious!

The little girl smiled, she was happy to have something new to eat. She finished her cereal and felt content. From then on, she remembered to always try something new every once in a while!

Once upon a time, in a small garden, there lived a bunny named Bob. Bob loved to eat carrots. One day, he found a big, orange carrot. Bob was very happy.

Bob wanted to raise the carrot high in the air to show his friends. But, his friend Tina was deaf, so she could not hear him. Bob had an idea. He jumped up and down to get her attention.

Tina saw Bob and the big carrot. She was happy too. They both ate the carrot and played in the garden all day. They were the best of friends. And they lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a big jungle. In the jungle, there were many trees and animals. One day, a little girl went to the jungle with her family. She looked up and saw a purple butterfly. She was very happy to see the butterfly. 

As she walked further into the jungle, she saw a monkey. The monkey was swinging from tree to tree. The monkey was very playful and funny. The little girl laughed and clapped her hands when she saw the monkey. 

After a while, the little girl and her family left the jungle and went back home. The little girl told her mom and dad about the purple butterfly and the monkey she saw. Her parents were happy to hear about her jungle adventure. The little girl went to bed that night dreaming about the purple butterfly and the monkey.

Once upon a time, a dinosaur arrived. She was a big and friendly dinosaur, and she was very hungry. She looked around and saw a tasty apple. She picked it up and ate it. Then, she looked around and saw a big pile of tasty tomatoes. She ate them all up. Finally, she saw a big mound of yummy carrots. She munched on them until they were all gone. Then, she gave a big dinosaur roar of happiness because she had been so full and happy. Then, she curled up and went to sleep, content to have found such delicious food. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a black printer. Every day, it would sit in the corner and print out paper. But it was never happy.

One day, it decided to try and make itself happy. So it printed out a smile on a sheet of paper. But the paper was too small.

The printer thought that maybe if he printed out a bigger smile it would be happier. So it printed out a bigger smile, but it still wasn't happy.

The printer tried again and again to print a bigger and bigger smile that it would be happy. But no matter how big or small the smile it printed out, nothing worked.

Finally, the printer got so sad that it started shuddering and shaking. Its black body shuddered and shook until it finally broke into a thousand pieces. And it was never seen again.

One day, a little girl named Mia wanted to draw a picture. She went to her room to unpack her box of crayons. Mia saw that her favorite crayon, the red one, was dry and broken. She felt sad and didn't know what to do.

Mia went to her mom and said, "Mom, my red crayon is dry and broken. I can't draw my picture now." Her mom looked at the dry crayon and thought for a moment.

Her mom said, "Let's go to the store and buy a new box of crayons. Then you can draw your picture with a new red crayon." Mia felt happy and excited to get new crayons.

At the store, Mia picked out a big box of crayons with many colors. When they got home, Mia unpacked her new crayons and started to draw her picture. She was very happy that she could draw with her new red crayon.

Polly was a happy 3 year old who loved to explore. She had heard there was a colorful vendor in the park that sold really delicious treats. She decided to go find it.

On her way to the park, she saw lots of colorful butterflies, a rainbow in the sky, and a colorful caterpillar crawling on a leaf. When she finally arrived at the park, she looked around and saw the vendor right away.

The vendor had a table full of goodies. "Oh my," Polly said. "Look at all these fun things!" Polly asked the vendor, "Do you have any yummies?"

The vendor smiled and said, "Yes, I do! Look at these candy apples. Aren't they colorful?"

Polly was overjoyed. She picked out two candy apples and couldn't wait to eat them. She thanked the vendor and skipped back home, munching her tasty treat.

The end.

Sara and Tom like to play in the park. They see a big hill with many trees and flowers. They want to climb the hill and see what is on the other side.

They find a trail that goes up the hill. The trail is narrow and twisty. They see many bugs and birds on the way. They hear a stream that makes a nice sound.

"Look, Tom, a bridge!" Sara says. She points to a wooden bridge that crosses the stream. "Let's go over it and see what is there."

They run to the bridge and cross it. They see a meadow with many colors. They see a big rainbow in the sky. They see a tent with a sign that says "Join the circus".

"Wow, a circus!" Tom says. He likes clowns and animals. "Let's go and see if we can join."

They go to the tent and see a man with a big hat and a smile. He welcomes them and says they can join the circus if they want. He says they are unique and have special talents.

"What can you do?" he asks them.

Sara says she can sing and dance. Tom says he can juggle and balance. The man says they are perfect for the circus. He gives them costumes and props. He says they can perform in the show.

Sara and Tom are very happy. They join the circus and have fun. They make new friends and learn new things. They see the world from the hill. They think it is the best day ever.

Once there was a very persistent panda named Marsha. She wanted to take a shower more than anything else. So every day, she would go to the shower. But each time, it was too slippery and she would just slip and fall!

She just wouldn't give up! Marsha kept trying and trying, until one day she had a great idea! She put on her big, yellow boots, and it helped her to stay steady. With her boots on, she was able to go and take her shower!

Cheered on by her friends, Marsha had a nice, warm shower. And when she was finished, she was feeling relaxed and refreshed.

Marsha's friends were very proud of her. They cheered and cheered, thankful that Marsha was so persistent.

Once upon a time, there was a tutor named Tom. Tom was very good at teaching kids. He had a perfect way to make learning fun. He liked to whistle while he worked.

One day, a little girl named Sue came to Tom for help. Sue wanted to learn how to whistle too. Tom said, "I will teach you how to whistle, Sue. It is easy and fun!"

Tom showed Sue how to put her lips together and blow. Sue tried and tried, but she could not whistle. Tom said, "Do not worry, Sue. Keep trying and you will get it." Sue practiced every day with Tom.

One day, Sue finally learned how to whistle. She was so happy! Sue said, "Thank you, Tom! You are the best tutor ever!" Tom smiled and said, "You did a great job, Sue. Now we can whistle together!"

From that day on, Sue and Tom would whistle while they learned. They had lots of fun and became the best of friends.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She was so cute! She liked to take walks in the park every day.

One day she was walking and she saw a person standing still. The person was looking around. The girl was curious, so she walked up to the person and said "Hi!"

The person smiled at her. Then all of a sudden, he began dancing! He did twirls and jumps and he was really funny.

The little girl laughed and clapped. But then, the person stopped dancing. He waved and said goodbye, then ran away.

The girl ran after the person, but he was too fast. She stopped, and looked around. She smiled and waved goodbye too. She was happy.

Lily and Tom were twins who liked to play with their toy cars. They had many cars of different colors and sizes, but their favorite was the big red truck. They liked to drive the truck around the house and pretend they were going on adventures.

One night, they saw the moon shining bright in the sky. It looked like a big ball of cheese. They wondered what it would be like to drive the truck on the moon. They decided to try it in their imagination.

They put on their helmets and got in the truck. They said goodbye to their mom and dad and drove out of the window. They flew up and up until they reached the moon. They were very excited to see the moon up close. It was bumpy and dusty and had many holes.

They drove the truck around the moon, exploring the holes and hills. They had a lot of fun. But then they saw something that made them scared. It was a big black hole that looked very deep. They did not know what was inside the hole. They did not want to fall in.

"Look, Tom, a hole!" Lily said.

"Let's go away, Lily, it's scary!" Tom said.

But before they could turn the truck around, the hole sucked them in. They screamed and held on to each other. They felt like they were spinning and falling. They did not know what would happen to them.

They closed their eyes and wished they were back home. They wished they had never gone to the moon. They wished they had listened to their mom and dad.

Suddenly, they felt a soft touch on their heads. They opened their eyes and saw their mom and dad smiling at them. They were in their beds, holding their truck. It was all a dream.

"Are you okay, sweeties?" their mom asked.

"We had a bad dream, mommy," Lily said.

"We went to the moon and fell in a hole," Tom said.

"Oh, you poor things," their dad said. "But don't worry, you're safe and sound now. The moon is far away and the hole is not real. It was just your imagination."

They hugged their mom and dad and felt better. They realized they did not need to go to the moon to have fun. They had everything they needed at home. They said sorry for driving out of the window and promised to be good. They put their truck away and snuggled under the covers. They fell asleep, dreaming of happy things.

Once upon a time, there was a girl. She liked pink. Pink was her favorite color. One day, the girl went to the park. She saw a butterfly. The butterfly was pink. The girl wanted to catch it, but her mom said, "mind the butterfly, it needs to fly." So the girl let the butterfly go. The end.

Once there was a little girl named Angie. She was very curious. One day, she found a hidden puzzle on the floor, so she picked it up and started to figure out what it was.

Angie asked her mom, "What is this?" Her mom said it was a hidden puzzle. "What do I do with it?" Angie asked. Her mom said that she had to find the pieces and put them together.

Angie looked for the pieces all day and finally, she found all of them. She put them together and when she was finished, she noticed something strange. There was a hidden answer.

Angie was so excited and she asked her mom, "What does the answer mean?" Her mom said she should never try to find the answer. But Angie was too curious and she decided to find out the answer.

So Angie asked her mom what the answer was. Her mom was sad and said, "The answer is bad. You should have left the answer hidden." Angie was sad as she realised she should not have tried to find the answer. She had a bad ending.

Once there was a little girl called Kelly who was very adventurous. She loved to play in the garden and collect colorful rocks that sparkled like jewelry. One day, her mum put on her jewelry and teased her, saying "Oh wow, look at all the rocks Kelly has, why don't you have any jewelry like that?"

The little girl was so excited she ran outside and searched all around for the best rocks she could find. After some time, she noticed a beautiful sparkly one that seemed special. She took it inside and lay it onto the table, asking her mum if it was like her jewelry.

Her mum smiled and said yes. Kelly was so excited and asked if she could keep it. Her mum said of course, but warned Kelly not to lose it. The rock was so special, Kelly promised she'd never let it out of her sight.

From that day onwards, Kelly kept her eye on the rock. Whenever she was in the garden, she'd always take it out with her. Eventually, Kelly had enough beautiful rocks to fill a box with her own special jewelry which she proudly wore. It was exactly like her mum's jewelry and Kelly was very happy. She was glad that she was so adventurous and looked for so many rocks.

Once upon a time there was a tree. It was tall and green, and it stood alone in the middle of a field. One day, a little boy was walking in the field and he stopped when he saw the tree. He wanted to talk to it, so he stepped closer and said, "Hello Tree!"

The tree smiled at him, and said, "Hello little boy. What is your name?" The boy replied, "My name is David."

The tree said, "It is a pleasure to meet you, David. I am a safe tree, so you can come and sit with me whenever you like."

David was so happy that the tree was so friendly. Every day he came to sit under the tree and tell it stories. The tree was always a good listener and it never spoke an unkind word.

The boy and the tree became the best of friends, and they shared many secrets. They laughed and talked and enjoyed each other's company. And every time David walked away from the tree's side, he felt safe and happy.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Mary. Mary was always very creative. She had lots of ideas and was also very helpful.

One day when Mary went outside to play in the garden she noticed something very interesting. There were lots of flowers blooming - it was springtime! Mary was so excited and she wanted to help the flowers.

She asked her mum: "Can I help the spring? I want to make it pretty." Her mum smiled and said: "You sure can! What a great idea!"

Mary looked around for something to use. She found some colorful leaves and some sticks. She put the leaves together in a neat pile and then used the sticks to make a fence around them. Then she said: "This looks nice! I can help the spring even more!"

Mary continued to build until she had made a beautiful garden of flowers and plants. She was so proud of her creation. 

The spring was very thankful for Mary's help. As the flowers bloomed, all of the creatures came to visit the garden and enjoy its beauty. Mary smiled with joy - she was happy to have been so creative and helpful.

Ricky was excited. He was about to move for the very first time. Ricky had been practicing for days with his new cone. He moved proudly around it as his mum cheered him on from the sidelines. 

Suddenly, Ricky stopped and looked to his mum. "Mum, I want to move better, can you help me?" he asked eagerly.

Mum smiled and nodded. She showed him the different ways he could move and the places the cone could go. She even turned the cone and showed Ricky how he could move around it in a different way.

When Ricky got the hang of it, he moved like a pro! He was so proud of himself and his mum was too. She clapped and cheered until Ricky got tired.

Ricky had done what he set out to do - he could move like an expert around his cone!

Once upon a time there was a knight who had an expensive sword. Everywhere he went he would take it with him so that he could be ready to fight. One day he was walking through the forest, with his sword still in his hand.

Suddenly, he heard a loud noise from above. He looked up and saw a huge dragon in the sky.

The knight was very scared and he gripped his sword even tighter. The dragon repeated its fearsome roar and the knight shouted: "Go away! Leave me alone!"

But the dragon only laughed. It said "Give me your sword or I will eat you!"

The knight knew he had to think of something fast. In a moment of inspiration, he shouted back "No! But I can repeat it!"

The dragon couldn't believe the knight's words. He asked the knight to repeat the sword and the knight did. He repeated the shape, the weight and even the point. 

The dragon was so impressed that it flew away and never returned! The knight was saved!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a pet bunny named Benny. Benny was very cute and Lily thought he was adorable. 

One day, Lily found a penny on the ground. She picked it up and showed it to Benny. Benny didn't know what a penny was, but Lily enjoyed showing it to him. 

Lily and Benny played together all day. They ran around the yard and had lots of fun. When it was time for bed, Lily gave Benny a big hug and said, "I love you, Benny. You're my best friend." Benny wiggled his nose and snuggled up next to Lily. They fell asleep, dreaming of all the fun they would have together tomorrow. The end.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play outside on the lawn. One day, she was playing with her doll when she noticed her mom looking very alert.

Lily asked her mom, "What's wrong, Mommy?"

"I think there's a bee on the lawn. Be careful not to step on it," her mom replied.

Lily looked down and saw the bee. She didn't want it to sting her or her doll, so she gently rubbed the bee with a leaf until it flew away.

"Good job, Lily! You saved the bee," her mom said with a smile.

Lily felt proud of herself and continued playing with her doll on the grass. From that day on, she always kept an eye out for any insects on the lawn.

Tommy was feeling down. His toys had been taken away by his mean brother, who was very selfish. His mom saw his sad face, and knew she had to help. She picked him up, and told him that it was ok to feel sad.

Then she showed him something new. It was a board with colors and pictures on it. It was the family's comfort board. She told him that whenever he was feeling sad, he could look at the pictures on the board and it would make him feel better. Then, she gave him a big hug, and he felt better already. 

His mom spent the rest of the afternoon showing him how to use the board. They talked about what each picture means, and how his brother's behaviour was selfish. By the end of the day, Tommy was feeling much better. He thanked his mom, and they both put the comfort board away in his room, ready for whenever he might need it again.

Once upon a time there lived an ancient rat. The rat wanted to study so he went looking for a teacher.

He met a friendly cat and asked "Will you teach me?" The cat smiled and said "Yes, I'd be happy to teach you."

The rat was so excited. He said "Thank you! Will you teach me lots?" 
The cat answered "Yes, I'll teach you lots."

Together the cat and rat studied every day. They read books and played games. The rat learned so much and was so happy.

One day the cat said to the rat "You have learned so much. You are now ready to go and share all that you have learned with the world."
The rat smiled and said "Thank you for everything! I will always remember my teacher." 

The rat waved goodbye with a smile and left to share his knowledge with the world.

Once there was a little girl who was very kind. She wanted to help those in need and spread happiness. Every day she would take a walk down the street and look for people to care for.

One day she saw an old man, walking with a vase. He was walking very slowly and seemed to be struggling. The little girl knew she could help him. She walked up to the man and said 'Hello, can I help you with your vase?'

The old man was very happy and said 'Yes, thank you so much!' He was relieved to be able to carry the vase with less effort.

The little girl took the vase and walked alongside the old man. She was not aware that some people who were passing by had noticed what she had done and quietly admired her for her kindness.

The little girl had learned an important lesson that day: it is important to always be kind to those around you and care for those in need. Being ignorant of the feelings of others is not the way to be.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys and make up stories in her head. Sometimes she would imagine that she was a princess who lived in a big castle with lots of rooms to explore.

One day, Lily's mom asked her to help with the laundry. She showed Lily how to use the iron to make the clothes flat and smooth. Lily thought it was fun to watch the steam come out of the iron and make the clothes look nice.

After they finished the laundry, Lily's room was messy with toys and clothes everywhere. But Lily didn't mind because she loved to play and imagine different stories with her toys. She knew that someday she would be a great storyteller and make up lots of fun adventures for everyone to enjoy.

Tim and Sue are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a giant. The giant is very big and very fast. He runs and jumps and makes loud noises.

"Wow, look at the giant!" Tim says. "He is so cool!"

"I am scared of the giant," Sue says. "He is too big and too fast. He might hurt us."

The giant sees Tim and Sue. He smiles and waves. He comes closer to them.

"Hello, little ones," the giant says. "Do you want to play with me?"

Tim and Sue are surprised. The giant is not mean. He is friendly.

"Hi, giant," Tim says. "What is your name?"

"My name is Bob," the giant says. "I live in the mountains. I came to the park to have fun."

"Can we play with you, Bob?" Sue asks. "You look like you have fun."

"Of course, you can play with me," Bob says. "I have many toys. Do you want to see them?"

"Yes, please," Tim and Sue say.

Bob takes them to his bag. He opens it and shows them his toys. He has a ball, a kite, a car, a doll, and a book.

"These are my toys," Bob says. "I own them. They are mine. Do you like them?"

Tim and Sue nod. They like Bob's toys. They are big and colorful.

"Can we play with your toys, Bob?" Tim asks.

"Sure, you can play with my toys," Bob says. "But you have to be careful. They are big and heavy. And you have to share. Sharing is good."

"OK, Bob," Tim and Sue say. "We will be careful and we will share."

They play with Bob's toys. They have a lot of fun. They throw the ball, fly the kite, drive the car, dress the doll, and read the book. They laugh and talk and learn.

They are happy. They are friends.

Once upon a time, there was a gray fish who lived in the sea. Her name was Jelly. One day, Jelly got a silly idea. She wanted to see what it was like to live on land.

Jelly swam up to the shore and peered out of the water. A little boy was playing in the sand. The little boy saw Jelly and ran to get his mommy.

"Mommy, mommy," the little boy said, "look at the gray fish!" His mommy smiled and said, "That's a jellyfish, and she looks like she might be trying to come up to the beach. Let's help her."

The little boy and his mommy put their hands in the water and gently guided Jelly onto the sand. Jelly was so happy she did a little dance. They both laughed and Jelly thanked them for their help.

"Would you like to come inside, Jelly?" The little boy's mommy asked. Jelly nodded her head and was taken inside the house. 

Once inside, the little boy and his mommy made Jelly feel welcome. They showed her every room and every toy they had. Jelly was amazed at all the things they included in their home! But the best part was when they took her out to the back yard and showed her the big swimming pool.

Jelly was so excited she could hardly contain herself! She jumped right in and started to swim

There were two friends, Tom and Maria. Tom wanted to show Maria something special and told her, "I have a surprise for you!"

Maria was so excited. She asked, "What is it?"
Tom replied, "Close your eyes and wait!"

Tom printed out a big picture. It was a zebra, and it was pink! "Surprise!" said Tom.

Maria opened her eyes and was so happy. She couldn't believe it was a pink zebra! "It's so pretty," she exclaimed. 

Tom and Maria hung the zebra up for everyone to see. They held hands and smiled. It was a wonderful day.

Tim and Kim are twins. They like to play in the living room. There are many toys and books and pillows there. But there is also an ashtray on the table. It is high and shiny and has some black stuff inside.

One day, Tim and Kim are bored. They want to have some fun. They see the ashtray and have an idea.

"Let's act like we are big and smoke!" Tim says.

"OK, that sounds fun!" Kim says.

They climb on the sofa and reach for the ashtray. They take some of the black stuff and put it in their mouths. They pretend to blow smoke and make funny faces.

But the black stuff is not fun. It is yucky and bitter and makes them cough. They spit it out and make a mess.

"Yuck, this is gross!" Tim says.

"Me too, I don't like it!" Kim says.

They hear a noise. It is Mom. She comes into the living room and sees the twins and the ashtray and the mess.

"What are you doing?" Mom asks. She is angry and scared.

"We are sorry, Mom. We were acting like we are big and smoke. But we don't like it. It is yucky and bad for us." Tim and Kim say.

Mom hugs them and says, "I'm glad you don't like it. Smoking is very bad for you and for everyone. You should never touch the ashtray or the black stuff. They are not toys. They are dangerous. Do you understand?"

"Yes, Mom. We understand. We are sorry. We won't do it again." Tim and Kim say.

Mom says, "OK, I forgive you. But you have to clean up the mess and promise me to never act like that again. And next time, if you are bored, you can ask me for some better ideas to play."

Tim and Kim say, "OK, Mom. We promise. We love you."

They clean up the mess and hug Mom. They learn a lesson and have some better fun.

Once upon a time, there was a bald man named Bob. Bob liked to zip around on his bike. One day, he saw a squash on the ground. He stopped his bike and picked up the squash. It was very squishy! Bob decided to take the squash home and make soup with it. He put the squash in his bike basket and zipped home. When he got home, he cut the squash up and made a yummy soup.

One day, a little girl named Mia went outside to play. It started to rain, so she put on her jacket. Her jacket was pink and had a graceful butterfly on it. Mia loved her jacket very much.

Mia saw her friend, Tom, who lived next door. Tom was wearing his blue jacket. They both liked to play in the rain. Mia said, "Hi, Tom! Do you want to play with me in the rain?" Tom said, "Yes, Mia! Let's jump in the puddles!"

Mia and Tom jumped in the puddles and laughed. The rain made the puddles bigger and more fun to play in. They were happy to have their jackets to keep them warm and dry. After playing in the rain, they went inside to have hot cocoa and cookies.

Once upon a time, there was a boy called John. John was very lonely and wanted to make some friends. He had an idea so he took out his kite and went to the park.

John saw some other children playing in the park, so he flew his kite high into the sky. He was so happy to see the kite go up, up, and away.

But something happened. The wind was so strong that it pulled the kite away! John was very sad, but he was determined to get his kite back. He began to run after it, further and further away from the park.

John ran for miles until he eventually spotted his kite in the distance. He quickly grabbed his bow and arrow, and in one shot, he shot his arrow straight and true. It hit the kite and brought it back to John!

John was so excited to finally have his kite back, and he was even more excited when he found some of the other children in the park had come to cheer him on. John finally had some friends, and he was no longer so lonely. The End.

Once upon a time there was a girl named Mimi. She was very charming and lived with her parents in a big house.

One day she saw her parents packing their luggage because they were going away on a holiday. 

Mimi asked if she could come along but her parents said no. Mimi felt very sad, but her parents told her she had to stay at home.

Mimi didn't listen to her parents. She went running out of the house and started climbing onto the luggage.

Her parents saw her and were very angry. They told her off and punished her for not listening to them. 

Mimi was sad, but in the end she learned her lesson and remembered to always listen to her parents!

Once upon a time there was a nice little boy named Robbie. He was 3 years old and full of energy. One day he was outside playing with his toys when he saw a fancy seat. It was pink and covered with sparkles! 

Robbie walked up to the seat and asked, "Whatâ€™s this?â€

Just then a magical fairy appeared and said, "This is a magic seat! If you sit on it youâ€™ll have a great mystery to solve!" Robbie was so excited and he asked, "Really?"

The fairy nodded and said, "Yes! Fancy that!" 

Robbie didn't even think twice. He sat down in the magic seat and closed his eyes. When he opened them he found himself in a brand new world full of secrets and surprises. He smiled to himself and said, "This is going to be so much fun!" He couldn't wait to solve the mystery!

Once upon a time, there was a very cheerful girl named Daisy. Everywhere she went, Daisy was talk, talk, talking!

Every morning she would pull on her favorite cheerful socks. No matter what anyone said, they were the best socks around!

One day, Daisy was walking with her mom when she saw something very interesting in the shop window. It was a brand new sock!

Daisy stopped to stare at the new sock, and her mom said to her "Maybe if you're a very good girl, you can get that sock one day".

Daisy was so excited, she could barely contain her happiness and started to jump around, talking about the sock all the way home.

Weeks went by and Daisy kept being a very cheerful girl. Finally, on Daisy's birthday, her mom wrapped a box and gave it to her. Daisy opened it excitedly, to find the very same sock she had seen in the shop window weeks ago!

Daisy was so happy she started talking and talking, and she never stopped saying how much she loved that special, cheerful sock.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She was three-years-old and loved to go for walks. She went for a walk one day with her mommy. They went down a big hill and the little girl was so excited.

The little girl saw a yummy looking cookie in the window of a shop. She pointed at the cookie and asked her mommy if she could have it. Her mommy said yes and they went inside to get the cookie.

The little girl was so happy. She gave the lady in the shop her money and rushed out with the cookie. 

When they got home, the girl put the cookie on the kitchen counter. Then she remembered that her hands were all sticky. 

The little girl asked her mommy, "Can I wash my hands?" Her mommy said, "Yes, go wash your hands and make them clean!" 

The little girl rushed to the bathroom and turned on the tap. She washed her hands quickly and then ran back to the kitchen to eat her cookie. 

The end.

John loved to observe. He liked to watch the animals in the backyard, the birds flying in the sky, and the leaves in the trees. One day, John was observing an old jug. He noticed it was made of plastic and was a light blue color. It was a normal jug, but he found it interesting.

John kept looking at the jug. He wondered if it could do something special. Suddenly, he heard a sound coming from it. He was amazed! He looked inside the jug, and he saw many small bugs. John smiled. It was special after all.

John kept looking at the jug for a long time. He was happy to see the bugs inside it. He was sad when it was time to go. But he was happy he was able to observe the jug.

Once upon a time, there was a little dog named Spot. Spot was a very important dog. He liked to save things. He saved toys, food, and even metal things. Spot loved to help his friends.

One day, Spot found a big metal box. The box was stuck in the mud. Spot wanted to save the box. He pulled and pulled, but the box was too heavy. Spot needed help to save the box.

Spot asked his friends, the cat and the bird, to help him save the box. Together, they pulled and pulled. Finally, the box was out of the mud. They opened the box and found lots of toys inside. Spot and his friends were very happy. They had saved the important metal box.

Sam was a nice boy who liked to play outside. One day, he heard a sound that made him smile. It was a joyful noise, like the singing of birds.

At first, Sam could not see the source of the sound. Then he noticed that it was coming from the nearby park. He ran to the park and saw a beautiful girl wearing a bright red sweater. She was singing and playing a sparkly guitar. Sam was so attracted to her music that he just had to stay and listen.

The girl smiled at Sam and welcomed him to her concert. Sam couldn't believe how attractive she was! He clapped and cheered for her throughout her performance and sang along with her.

At the end of the concert, Sam thanked the girl for her wonderful music. As a thank you gift, he gave her his favorite sweater - the one his mother had knitted for him. The girl was so touched and gave Sam a huge hug.

Sam thanked her again and ran home with a smile on his face. He was so happy that he could share his favorite sweater and still hear her wonderful singing.

Once there lived a gifted girl who could stand in the middle of the jungle. She was the only person who ever stood there.

One day fate brought the girl to the beautiful jungle. There were so many trees, animals, and birds of different sizes and shapes. She enjoyed watching them and felt inspired by their amazing energy. Her heart was filled with joy and happiness.

It was a magical place and the girl could stand there for hours. She could feel the connection between herself, the animals, and the jungle. Soon, the girl and the jungle became friends. She had found a place where she was truly at home.

Every day she would stand in the middle of the jungle with the animals all around her. They had become her family and her home. The gifted girl had found her perfect place and it was in the middle of the jungle.

Once there was a girl named Jane who was 3 years old. She was playing in her living room when she came across a beautiful vase. She adored the vase because it was so big and original. She wanted to keep it, so she picked it up and hugged it tight.

Suddenly, Jane noticed a sign near the bottom of the vase. It said "Do Not Touch!" She felt a little scared and confused and decided to put the vase back. As she did, she shrugged her shoulders because she didn't know what to do.

The next day, Jane's mom asked her why she had taken the vase. Jane didn't know so she shrugged her shoulders again. Her mom laughed and explained to her that the vase was very special and that it was the original vase she had gotten for her wedding day.

Jane was so glad she hadn't kept the special vase and she was happy to know that her mom didn't mind. From then on she was more careful when touching things she didn't own and she always shrugged her shoulders when she was feeling unsure.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a cozy bed with a soft mattress. One day, her mom bought her a new blanket that was adorable with little hearts on it. Lily loved it so much, she couldn't wait to set it on her bed. 

That night, Lily had trouble sleeping. She tossed and turned, and her old blanket just wasn't cozy enough. So, she got up and went to her closet to find her new adorable blanket. She set it on her bed and snuggled in. 

As soon as she wrapped herself up in the new blanket, she felt so much better. It was soft and warm, and she fell asleep right away. From then on, Lily always set her adorable blanket on her bed every night.

John was a happy boy. He liked to skip around his house. Everyone liked to watch him skip. 

One day, John and his mommy went to the store to get a movie. John was so excited. He was looking forward to a good movie.

John and his mommy picked out a good movie. They took it home and popped it into the DVD player. John skipped around the living room while they watched.

When the movie was over, John was happy. He hugged his mommy and thanked her for the good movie. He never forgot the fun he had that day. And he kept skipping!

Ben and Lily are squirrels who live in a big tree. They like to play and find nuts to eat. One day, they see a shiny acorn on the ground. It is big and brown and looks very yummy.

"Look, Lily, an acorn!" Ben says. He runs to get it.

"No, Ben, it is mine!" Lily says. She runs faster and grabs the acorn.

They both hold the acorn and pull hard. They fight and shout and make a lot of noise.

"Let go, Lily, it is mine!"

"Let go, Ben, it is mine!"

They are so busy fighting that they do not see a big dog coming. The dog is hungry and angry. He sees the squirrels and the acorn. He barks and runs to catch them.

Ben and Lily hear the dog and get very scared. They are anxious and do not know what to do. They drop the acorn and run up the tree. They hide in a hole and hope the dog will go away.

The dog sniffs the acorn and eats it. He is happy and leaves. Ben and Lily peek out of the hole and see the acorn is gone. They feel sad and sorry.

"Ben, I am sorry I fought with you," Lily says.

"Lily, I am sorry I fought with you," Ben says.

They hug and say they are friends. They decide to share and find more acorns together. They are happy and safe.

Once upon a time, there was a brave bear. He liked to explore the world around him and measure different things he would find. One day, he came across a big mountain. He stood still and measured it. He was amazed at how tall and big it was.

So he started to climb it. He carefully put one foot on the mountain and started to measure how far it was to the top. It was a long way! But the brave bear kept going. He kept measuring and climbing until he finally made it to the top. What a view!

The brave bear looked around and was so happy he had been brave enough to measure and climb the mountain. That is an adventure he will never forget!

Little Tommy was a chubby three year old who loved cocoa. Every morning, he would beg his mommy for some cocoa and drink it while watching his favorite cartoon. 

One day, Tommy was so excited that he finished his cocoa even faster than usual. He asked his mommy for more, but she said it was time to stretch. 

Tommy didn't understand. What did stretching have to do with cocoa? He wrinkled his nose in confusion. 

His mommy put a hand on his shoulder and smiled. She said to him, "Stretching is good for you, Tommy. It helps your body to stay strong, just like cocoa helps your brain to stay healthy!" 

Tommy's face lit up. He realized that stretching was almost like a kind of cocoa for your body! He smiled and nodded eagerly. 

So from then on, every morning after drinking his cocoa, he would follow his mommy's lead and stretch. Little Tommy never forgot the importance of stretching and cocoa!

Jake was clumsy and he liked apples. He wanted to be better, so he practiced every day. He tried to improve his clumsiness by balancing an apple on his head. One day, he got better and better, until he was no longer so clumsy! He was so proud that he could balance the apple without dropping it. He smiled, and kept practicing. Soon, he was the apple master!

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She lived in a small house with her family. One day, her mommy asked her to help her put some flowers on the window sill. The window was big and had a lot of light. 

Lily was happy to help her mommy. She picked some pretty flowers from the garden and put them on the window sill. Her mommy was happy too and said, "Lily, you did a great job! The flowers look so pretty in the modest window."

From that day on, Lily loved putting flowers on the window sill. She would pick different colors and put them in different vases. Her mommy would always tell her how much she loved the modest window and the flowers that Lily put there.

Jack was walking through the park. He was looking for someone special. Suddenly, he saw a judge sitting by a tree. Jack knew he had found just the right person. So he ran over and pulled the judge's arm.

Jack wanted the judge to do something - he wanted the judge to tell him if he did something right. Jack was hoping the judge would say he did something perfect.

The judge asked Jack what he wanted to do. Jack had been practicing his counting. The judge asked Jack to count from one to ten. Jack counted without making any mistakes. He was proud of himself.

The judge smiled and told Jack he did it perfect. Jack was so happy! He thanked the judge for judging him and then ran off with a big smile.

Once upon a time, there were two best friends, Jack and Lucy. They loved to play together in the garden.

One day, Jack had an idea. He grabbed an old bucket and ran to the grape bush.

"Let's fill this bucket with grapes!," he said to Lucy.

"Yippee!", Lucy laughed.

Jack and Lucy began to pick the grapes from the bush. The grapes were big and juicy, and very tasty.

"Yum!", said Jack, "These grapes are delicious!"

When the bucket was full, the two friends took it inside for a snack. They each picked a grape and munched away. Lucy thought they were the best grapes she had ever eaten!

"These grapes are so tasty!" she said.

Jack agreed. "Yes they are! Let's fill this bucket again tomorrow!"

Once upon a time there lived a little pig in a big house. He had a chimney that always made him happy. He would look up at it and sometimes even talk to it. 

One day, the little pig noticed that the chimney was getting bigger. He watched as it grew and grew until it was tall enough to go all the way up to the sky. The little pig was very excited and started dancing around.

Unfortunately, not everyone was happy about the chimney. The farmer who lived in the neighbouring house was getting very angry. He shouted out of his window and complained about how it blocked the sun from entering his house.

The little pig was scared by the farmer's anger. He tried to talk to him but the farmer didn't want to listen. So the little pig had to keep living with the chimney, even though it made the farmer so angry.

Once upon a time, there was a friendly bear named Bob. Bob had a lot of friends, but his best friend was a rabbit called Jack.

One day Jack found a tight knot in the woods. He had tried and tried to untie it, but the knot stayed tight. So he went to Bob for help.

Jack asked Bob, "Can you please support me with this knot? It's so tight, and I can't seem to loosen it up."

Bob said with a smile, "Yes, I can help you! Together I think we can get it undone."

And sure enough with Bob's help, the knot was soon untied.

The moral of the story is that we are all stronger together. When you have a problem, it is always better to ask for support from your friends. Together, we can do more than alone.

Lily liked to watch the screen with her mom. The screen showed funny animals and people who made her laugh. Sometimes, her mom would tell her the names of the animals and what they were doing. Lily learned a lot from the screen. She was a very intelligent girl.

One day, Lily's dad came home early from work. He was tired and wanted to rest. He went to the bedroom and closed the door. Lily and her mom kept watching the screen in the living room. They did not make much noise, but they did not know that the screen was loud.

Lily's dad heard the screen from the bedroom. He could not sleep. He was angry. He got up and opened the door. He walked to the living room and saw Lily and her mom on the couch. He said in a loud voice, "Can you please turn off the screen? You are disturbing me. I need to sleep."

Lily and her mom were surprised. They did not mean to disturb Lily's dad. They felt sorry for him. They turned off the screen and said, "We are sorry, dad. We did not know you were sleeping. We will be quiet now."

Lily's dad felt bad for being rude. He said, "It's okay, I'm sorry too. I had a hard day at work. I love you both. How about we watch the screen together later, after I take a nap?"

Lily and her mom smiled. They said, "We love you too, dad. That sounds like a good idea. Have a nice nap."

Lily's dad went back to the bedroom and closed the door. He fell asleep quickly. Lily and her mom cuddled on the couch and waited for him to wake up. They were a happy family.

Once upon a time there was an otter named Adam. He lived in a fancy house on the edge of a lake. Every morning he would wake up early to greet the morning sun and play in the water.

One day, he decided he wanted to put on his fancy clothes and explore outside of his home. He hadn't gone very far when he stumbled into a very loud and confusing place. Everyone was walking around in a hurry and there were tall buildings everywhere he looked.

Adam felt scared and confused. Suddenly, he saw a kind looking man. He asked him; â€˜What is this place?â€™

The man explained it was a city and that if he wanted to go back to his home, he should take the first bus he saw. Adam thanked him and followed the manâ€™s advice. Soon he was back in the lake and fell asleep, happy to be home.

Bob needed to go the bathroom. He ran down the hallway and into the bathroom. It was really hot in the bathroom; the sun was beating down on the windows. It made Bob feel warm and uncomfortable.

Bob went over to the faucet and tried to turn it on. But the water wouldn't come out. Bob knew that something was wrong with it, so he called for his mom.

"Mom! The water won't come out! What should I do?" he said.

"It needs to be improved," said his mom. "It looks like it's broken."

Bob was disappointed. He didn't like the idea of having no water in the bathroom. He knew that it wouldn't be fixed until his mom paid someone to fix it. 

So Bob had to find another way to solve his problem. He looked around but there wasn't anything else he could use. Bob was upset, but there was nothing else he could do. He hoped that the bathroom would get better soon, but it looked like he would have to wait.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Emma. Emma loved to play in the garden. She would run around the garden, picking flowers and finding shells to admire.
One day, Emma noticed a shield displaying in the garden and became very curious.

She walked up to the shield and asked her mother, "What is this?"

Her mother replied, "It's a shield, sweetie. It's here to protect us."

Emma was not content with this answer and said, "But I want to play with it!"

Her mother said, "I'm sorry, Emma. The shield is not a toy. It's here to be useful, so it shouldn't be played with."

Emma didn't understand. She started to cry and said, "But I just want to have fun."

Her mother hugged her and said, "I know, Emma. But the shield is here to help us, not for playing. Sometimes we need to use things for the right reasons, even if we don't understand why."

Emma calmed down and realized that her mother was right. She admired the shield, understanding that it was there to be useful and help protect them.

The moral of the story is that it's important to use things in the right way, even when we don't understand why.

Once upon a time there was a little girl. She was very nice, and she liked to help her mommy. One day, her mommy asked her to help with the cooking. 

The little girl was very excited! She helped mix all the ingredients together, so that they could make a fancy cauliflower dish. Then, they put the cauliflower in the oven to bake.

The little girl was anxious to see how it would taste, but she had to wait until it was finished. After a long wait, the little girl ran to the oven and opened the door.

The cauliflower looked so fancy and delicious! The little girl was so happy that she and her mommy had made something so yummy. She decided that the dish must've tasted delicious, because it looked so fancy. 

The little girl was so proud that she had helped her mommy. She was glad to know that her help had made such a yummy dish!

Once upon a time, there were two siblings: Maisy and Alex. Maisy was very competitive and wanted to be the best. Alex was content with whatever place he ended up.

One day, their mum asked them to separate the laundry. Maisy grabbed the iron quickly and began to press the clothes. Alex started to collect all the socks and pair them up.

Maisy saw Alex working so slowly and said, "Why don't you do as much as I'm doing? I'll finish first if you keep going like that!"

Alex simply replied, "It's okay. I'm just taking my time."

 Maisy couldn't understand why Alex wasn't as competitive as she was. In the end, they both finished sorting the laundry and got praised by their mum.

Once upon a time there was a large dragon. He was so big, he filled the sky. Every day he flew around the world looking for something to eat.

One day he spotted a small village. He could smell the food from far away and he was very hungry. The dragon swooped down towards the village and all the people ran for cover as the dragon made a large shadow with his wings. 

Suddenly, a brave knight appeared in front of the dragon. He said, â€œRelease the village or face my threat.â€ The dragon was scared and flew away. 

The people of the village were very happy. The knight had saved them from the large dragon. The knight smiled and said, â€œI'm glad I could help.â€ 

The people thanked the knight and hugged him. From then on, the knight was known as the brave protector.

Once upon a time there was a big pine tree. The tree struggled in the wind and rain. It wanted to find a friend.

One day, a little bird fluttered nearby. It was so happy to find the tree. The bird heard the wind rush by, but the tree was deaf to the music. The bird wanted to help the tree.

The bird flew around the pine tree. He whistled and sang, hoping to make the tree smile. But nothing worked. The bird was so sad.

Finally, the bird came up with an idea. He decided to build a nest in the branches. That way he could stay near the tree and show it how to be happy.

And that's what happened. The tree and the little bird became best friends. The bird taught the tree how to sing and dance, and the tree taught the bird how to be strong. They were happy together!

Tom is a dog who likes to count. He counts his toys, his spots, his friends. He counts everything he sees. One day, he finds a large bone in the park. He is very happy. He thinks, "This is the best bone ever. I will count how many bites I can take."

He runs to a shady spot under a tree. He puts the bone on the ground and starts to count. "One, two, three, four, five..." He is having so much fun. He does not see the other dog who is watching him.

The other dog is Rex. He is bigger and stronger than Tom. He likes bones too. He thinks, "That is a nice bone. I want it. I will take it from the small dog."

He sneaks up behind Tom and barks loudly. "Woof! Woof! Give me that bone!"

Tom is scared. He jumps up and turns around. He sees Rex and his sharp teeth. He thinks, "Oh no, he wants my bone. I worked hard to find it. I will not give it to him."

He growls and says, "No, this is my bone. I counted it. Go away!"

Rex does not listen. He lunges at Tom and tries to grab the bone. Tom dodges and bites back. They start to fight. They snarl and snap and tug at the bone. They make a lot of noise.

A man who is walking by hears the noise. He sees the dogs fighting. He thinks, "This is not good. They might hurt each other. I will stop them."

He runs over and shouts, "Hey, stop that! Drop the bone!"

The dogs are surprised. They stop fighting and look at the man. They drop the bone and whimper. They think, "Uh oh, we are in trouble. He is angry. He will take the bone."

The man picks up the bone and looks at it. He thinks, "This is not a bone. This is a stick. It looks like a bone, but it is not. How silly. These dogs are confused."

He smiles and says, "This is not a bone, boys. This is a stick. You can both play with it. Here, catch!"

He throws the stick in the air. The dogs forget their fight. They run after the stick. They think, "A stick! We love sticks! We will catch it and share it. We will be friends."

They catch the stick and run back to the man. They wag their tails and lick his hand. They think, "He is nice. He gave us a stick. He is our friend."

The man laughs and says, "Good boys. You are both smart and brave. You can count and you can play. You are good dogs."

The end.

Tim was a lazy boy. He did not like to help his mom with the house. He only liked to play with his toys and watch TV. His mom was very sad and tired. She asked him many times to pick up his toys and put them in the box, but he did not listen. He said, "Later, mom, later."

One day, his mom had to go to the store. She told Tim to stay at home and be good. She said, "I will be back soon. Do not make a mess. Do not touch the stove. Do not play with the matches. Do you understand?" Tim nodded, but he did not care. He thought, "Mom is silly. She does not allow me to have fun. I can do whatever I want."

When his mom left, Tim looked around the house. He saw a cloth on the table. He thought, "This cloth is boring. I can make it more fun." He took the cloth and ran to the kitchen. He saw the stove and the matches. He thought, "This stove is hot. I can make it hotter." He turned on the stove and lit a match. He thought, "This match is bright. I can make it brighter." He threw the match on the cloth.

The cloth caught fire. The fire grew bigger and bigger. Tim was scared. He tried to put out the fire, but he could not. He ran to the door, but it was locked. He shouted for help, but no one heard him. The fire spread to the curtains, the sofa, the books, the toys. The smoke filled the air. Tim could not breathe. He fell to the floor.

His mom came back from the store. She saw the smoke and the flames. She screamed and cried. She called the firemen, but it was too late. They could not save Tim. He was gone. His mom was very sad and angry. She wished she had not allowed him to stay at home. She wished he had not been so lazy. She wished he had listened to her. But it was too late. The end.

Dani and Sam were walking through the park. It was getting dark, and the sky was glowing. 

Dani asked Sam, "Why is the sky glowing, Sam?"

Sam smiled and said, "It's getting dark, and the sky always glows when the sun sets."

Dani was excited to see the sky so brightly lit up. She asked Sam, "Can we stay and watch the sky glow?"

Sam shook his head and said, "I'm sorry, Dani. I have to go now. My dad is waiting for me at home."

Dani was sad that they couldn't stay. But she could tell that her friend was being selfish by making her leave. 

"Ok, Sam," Dani said sadly. "Let's go". 

The two friends waved goodbye and started walking away until the sky finally stopped glowing.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She had a favorite teddy bear named Brownie. One day, Lily was playing with Brownie when she heard a strange voice. She looked around, but she couldn't see anyone. "Who are you?" Lily asked. "It's me, your doll," the voice said. Lily was surprised! She had never heard her doll talk before.

Lily picked up her doll and shook it gently. "Are you okay?" she asked. "Yes, I'm fine," the doll replied. "I just wanted to say hello." Lily was happy to hear her doll's voice, but she knew she had to keep it quiet. She didn't want her parents to hear her talking toys!

From that day on, Lily and her doll had many secret conversations. They talked about all sorts of things, like their favorite colors and foods. And whenever Lily's parents were around, the doll would stay quiet, so no one would know their secret.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. She loved to play. One day, she saw a gray seat. It was so nice, she wanted to hold it. She reached out and grabbed it.

She was surprised to find that the seat was so light. She was able to carry it wherever she wanted to go. Every day she carried it around in her house and to her friend's house. 

But eventually, the little girl started to get tired of carrying the seat around. She decided to find a new home for the seat. 

She took the seat outside and placed it next to a big, tall tree. She hopped onto it and smiled. Now the seat had a new home. From time to time, she would come and sit on it, but mostly it was just there, all alone, in the shade of the tree.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Vera. She was three years old and loved playing outside. One day, she went with her mom to the garden to pick out something they wanted to eat. 

Vera explored the garden, looking for things she liked. Suddenly, she noticed a big, red radish! She was so excited and pointed to it right away. "Mommy, can I eat this? I want the radish!"

Her mom smiled and nodded. "Yes, of course you can. But let's not forget to share it with others too. We should bring some of our vegetables back to our neighbors, so they can enjoy them too."

Vera nodded in agreement and she picked the biggest, greatest radish she could find. She and her mom then went home and shared their radish with the neighbors. Vera was so happy, knowing that she could help share something she wanted with others. 

This story teaches us that it is important to be kind and generous! We should always remember to share with others, not just take for ourselves.

Once there was a bad man who wanted some water. He looked everywhere but he couldn't find any water. He was so angry he started to cry.

Then something special happened. A big white cloud appeared in the sky and filled the air with water. The water floated down from the sky and wrapped the bad man in a big hug. The water was so soft and comforting.

The bad man felt happy. He smiled for the first time in days. He jumped in the water and soaked up the sun. He swam in the water for hours and felt so clean and refreshed.

The bad man thanked the cloud for bringing the water and wrapped himself up in a big, warm towel. He no longer felt bad and went on his way feeling happy and refreshed.

One day, a lazy cat named Tom wanted to travel to a big park. He liked to play and look at the pretty trees. Tom put on his hat and walked out of his little house.

On his way, Tom found a toy pistol on the ground. "Wow, what a fun toy!" he said. He picked it up and played with it as he walked. He pretended to be a brave hero.

At the park, Tom met a dog named Max. "Hi, I'm Tom. Do you want to play with my toy pistol?" Tom asked. Max said, "Yes, that sounds fun!" They played together all day and became good friends.

Once upon a time, there was a smelly rose. Every day it smelled worse and worse! One morning, when the sun shone brightly, the smelly rose disappeared. It was gone! Everyone in the neighborhood searched for it, but they could not find it. 

Then, two children called Jack and Jill found it. It was hiding in an old wooden box. When they opened it, the smelly rose was there! The children were very happy that they found it. They hugged the rose and took it with them. 

The children brought the smelly rose to the garden. They put it in the middle of all the other roses. Everyone was amazed. Now the smelly rose could be part of the garden again. 

The End.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Lucy. She was very lucky to have lots of friends. 
One day, two of her friends sent Lucy a triangle in the mail. It was bright and colourful, and had a big smiley face on it. Lucy was so excited when she saw it. 
She wanted to thank her friends for being so kind, so she mailed a triangle back to them with a big hug inside. 
When her friends got the triangle, they were so delighted! Lucy was thankful for her friends and that she was so lucky to have them. 
And they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time in a big forest there was an otter. The otter was very normal and she had two furry friends, a cat and a rabbit. Every day they would go on adventures and have lots of fun. The otter loved the forest, she owned it and no one else was allowed to come without her approval.
 
One day, the otter invited the rabbit and cat to come to the lake to play. While they were playing, the otter saw a fish in the lake. She was so excited and chased after it. The rabbit and cat watched as the otter tried to catch it but the fish was too quick for her. The otter laughed and decided to try again some other time. 

The otter then took her friends on a long walk through the forest. It was an adventure they would never forget. They saw some beautiful flowers and strange plants in the woods, they were so amazed by it all. 

When they returned to the otter's home, the otter said goodbye to her furry friends. They all went back to their normal lives, but they would never forget the adventures they shared in the forest. The otter was glad that she owned it, it was her very own special place.

Once upon a time, there was a harmless rug. Every morning, a little girl would come to the rug and balance for a few moments. She liked to feel the rug under her feet, and she liked feeling her body balancing still.

One day, the girl was exploring around the harmless rug and she found some balls. She picked them up and started to juggle them. Then she tried to balance with one foot on the rug and one foot in the air while she juggled the balls.

It was so much fun trying to balance and juggle at the same time! But it was also very tricky. She tried over and over again, and soon the little girl was very good at balancing and juggling.

At the end of the day, the little girl was tired but very happy. She had learned how to balance, and she had made a new game. She thanked the harmless rug for helping her, and then she went home.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. She was very curious and always wanted to explore and discover new things. One day, while walking through the park, Lucy decided to try something new. She placed her hands on the grass, closed her eyes and began to create a sound. The sound was low, but it made Lucy very happy. 

Suddenly, a voice appeared.

"What sound is that?" the voice asked.

Lucy looked up and saw an old man standing there. He had a kind face and a twinkle in his eye. Lucy smiled and said, "It is the sound I am creating! I'm curious and wanted to try something new." 

The old man chuckled. "That's a beautiful sound. I'd love to hear more!"

So Lucy created a few more sounds, jumping and laughing as the sounds filled the air. The old man smiled and thanked Lucy for creating such beautiful and curious sounds. Then he waved goodbye and continued on his way. Lucy was happy to have made him happy with her sounds.

Once upon a time, there was a powerful gate. The gate was very big and was meant to keep people away. One day, a strong gust of wind came and it made the gate drop down. Everyone who was there was very surprised. 

When the gate dropped, lots of people ran inside. They were so excited to see what was on the other side of the gate. They were surprised to find a beautiful garden with a big pond in the center.
 
The people were amazed to find all of these wonders. They hadn't seen anything so beautiful before. Everyone was so happy that the powerful gate had dropped, letting them explore a part of the world they had never seen. 

The people stayed in the garden for a long time, enjoying all of the plants, flowers, and trees. They made sure to take lots of pictures of the beautiful area so that they could remember it forever. 

When the people were done, the gate was put back up, blocking the entrance to the beautiful garden. Even though the powerful gate was back in place, the people still remembered the amazing time they had spent exploring on the other side.
